name: Goat Simulator 3
detailed_description: Pilgor's baaack! Take life by the horns in Goat Simulator 3 today! Gather your herd and venture forth into Goat Simulator 3; an all-new*, totally realistic**, sandbox farmyard*** experience that puts you back in the hooves of no one's favourite female protagonist. Join Pilgor and get ready to create your own whirlwind adventure on the island of San Angora. Lick, headbutt, and ruin your way through our open world in the biggest waste of your time since the original Goat Simulator! We won't tell you how to play (except in the tutorial), but merely provide the means to be the goats of your dreams. If your dreams contain more than one goat, that works for us! In Goat Simulator 3, you can invite up to three friends in local or online co-op to create carnage as a team, or compete in mini-games and then not be friends anymore. And don't worry, there are plenty of customisation options so you and your pals don't wear clashing outfits. Goat Simulator 3 first launched in November 2022, and since then our “game designers” have been hard at work adding even more weird and wondrous stuff. As well as all the original goat-y goodness, Steam players will be able to experience all content from the game’s post-launch updates; including the Mandatory Holiday Update, Operation Crackdown and the Shadiest Update, with more to come! KEY FEATURES: - You can be a goat - You can be a goat… on Steam! - Three of your friends can be goats too, and join you in local or online co-op - No really, there are so many goats. If you want to be fancy you can wear the skins of tall goats, stripey goats, and many more. There's a goat for everyone! - Dress up your goat in all kinds of nonsense, from toilet rolls to tea trays. Put on a jetpack for all we care - We have actual 'game designers' who have worked to create 'an okay amount of content'; including events, NPCs to mess with, physics, status effects, collectables, easter eggs, lies, betrayal, heartbreak - They've added mini-games too, lots of mini-games (seven is a lot, right?) - They’ve even added a bunch of extra content since the game first launched, aren’t you a bunch of lucky kids? DISCLAIMER: Since it launched in November 2022, Goat Simulator 3 has been a completely stupid game. It is still a completely stupid game today, except now it has more stuff! By this point if you're not sure what you're getting into, we can't help you. NOTES: * Goat Simulator 3 is technically not completely new, but it is new to Steam users! ** Our game is very realistic, if you happen to be a digital goat with a proclivity for ragdolling. *** False alarm, this one is actually true.

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone's away hammering the Helldivers 2 servers, or rearing third-party Pokemon in PalWorld, yet here's me running around aimlessly as a goat, licking pavements, people and stuff that's on fire.It's Goat Sim 3. If you know Goat Sim, you know you want to buy this - there's now a 3 at the end of the title, and your Goat can wear Crocs, which is all the upgrading that you need.

_childDocuments_.review: The Goat is GOAT, nobody should be surprised by this development.More seriously this is just a really fun game, can't really define it as anything other than just "FUN" all caps absolutely required. It's just the right amounts of silly, zany, wacky, crazy, silly, absurd, outrageous and all those other fun words. I'd say it's a great way to kill some time with random shenanigans but I literally blitzed the game in a few days without actually realizing how much time I had spent because I was having that much fun so I guess one bad thing I could say, if you are the type to consider it a bad thing, is that you will quickly find yourself spending a LOT more time than you realize just messing around with these ridiculous Goats trying to kill some time and wind down before heading to bed because you've got work/school in the morning only to find out it's 5am when you finally take a break to eat a snack or something and suddenly feel the exhaustion catch up to you as you stare uncomprehending at the clock that must be wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: The short answer: it's awesome. Super pretty world and plenty of mayhem to cause within it.I've got some more things to ramble about- here's the long version.Years ago, I played the original Goat Simulator and its various DLC packs. Hours upon hours. It might as well have been part of my childhood, so you could imagine how hyped I got when I saw there was a sequel coming up! I didn't preorder because the item offered really wasn't appealing to me, but I did buy the game on Epic as soon as I could- and more recently bought it again on Steam to move over to that. Compared to the OG, some features are a bit lacking, like a much smaller roster of creatures and mutators (though plenty of cosmetics and equipment). The music also falls short, at least in my opinion. The old soundtrack had a very defined 'identity' that the new game's tracks simply don't have. As for story, though? Daaamn!! It exists! It isn't very long, and any lore questions I had are still unanswered, but it was great. I thought the boss fight was quite creative. The visuals during the big escape sequence are fantastic. Love that stuff....With all that said, GS3 is absolutely worth giving a try. If at all possible, avoid spoilers, too! And if you read this far, thanks, I guess?

_childDocuments_.review: I was afraid this game wouldn't live up to the insanity and charm of the original, but surprisingly, I think it improves on the original by a long shot.First of all, the map is pretty huge. It's bigger than all of the Goat Simulator 1 maps together, but still manages to cram details and things to do into every nook and cranny. It's still easy to get around though, as there's vehicles, rails to grind along, fast travel, and even accessories to help you navigate the world.Then there's the events and instincts, which are basically small quests for you to do. There are so many sprinkled around the world, and some of them will take you a hot minute. Some even require that you do something else on a different part of the map before unlocking the next part of the quest. Everything has a reward attached to it.Just like the original, GS3 keeps a lot of the witty humor, references to other media, and chaos. There's a good chance you'll recognize at least a few of the references in the game, and they all add to the experience really well.Customization is great as well. There's plenty of accessories you can unlock through events and shopping, and as mentioned before, lots of them have special abilities. You can turn these abilities off if you just want the visual aspect, which is a nice touch especially if you're in multiplayer.Finally, the graphics are great. For a game as silly as this, they put some work into having nice graphics, which it really doesn't need. It strikes a good balance between realism and cartoony, which definitely works well for this game.Overall, I'd definitely recommend playing this, whether you've played the first one or not. There's loads of content, even if you don't wanna participate in the quests, there's still a massive sandbox for you to do whatever you'd like. There's an end goal as well which I love to see even though it's another thing this game didn't need to be fun. It's a shame this was an Epic exclusive for a while, I think that it hurt the sales, but this is still a really fun game worth the buy!

_childDocuments_.review: Unironically some of the most fun I've had in any game in the past 10 years. Crazy scenarios and endless silliness doesn't take away from the expertly designed quests, well hidden secrets, and levels that are a joy to traverse and discover. Played co-op with my daughter and loved every second of it. Pure FUN at it's best. You'll be laughing and having a good time for a solid 10-15 hours and there's nothing else quite like it. If you're on the fence, I whole-heartedly recommend you buy this game!

_childDocuments_.review: allows you to return playing as Pilgor the wacky and insanely powerful goat, wrecking havoc around the world of San Angora; and now can be done with friends. Explore a large map with a bounty of quests, unlockables, and items while you serve style of your choosing. Complete quests and rise the ranks of the goat tower to gain more benefits and quests as well as instincts to do for fun objectives. There are many different themes and areas from farmlands, to cemeteries, woodlands, vineyards, and city districts.- Great Graphics- Crazy Gameplay- Lots and Lots of Quests- Fun Instincts- Fun Abilities- Lots of Customisability- Drivable Vehicles- Co-op up to 4 Players- Lots of References and Easter Eggs- Lovely Soundtrack- In the first game abilities were an addition that could be stacked via mutators, and in this game it's tied to clothing items. Because abilities are tied to certain clothing items for the character, you're stuck with certain items if you want their utility. It's fine for certain things but there are lots of hats with cool abilities that you might not like the look of, or if you wanted to have two abilities that are cool but both of them occupy the same clothing slot or button, you have to switch between them.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure some people will hate this game because it's not exactly like the original, but it never could be and I love the direction they went with it. Overall a really fun game, a new game proper rather than a pile of shambling homages pretending to be a game (well, it kinda is that too but they're new memed homages or tasteful homages to the original game while still primarily relying on new goofs and mechanics). The physics and controls are the perfect ratio of good to garbage and they really put work into making the map as full and as silly as the original which is quite impressive. I definitely miss the original music, but I'm sure I'll live lol. Worth the money (to me) and I'm really hoping they plan to add more maps eventually (within an amount of time that is healthy and reasonable for the developers), I would absolutely pay for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Does this game need an explanation?I loved this game way more than the original, which already gets a pretty good score from me. There was a little more guidance in what to do to accomplish goals, without being handholdy. Still incredibly sandbox-ish, can go and do whatever you want at any time, but there is progression and technically, a 'story'. Which I found to be really fun and goofy.While it still has the fun bugs everyone loves in Goat Sim, there were a lot less of the bugs that made me so frustrated I wanted to close the game, such as being unable to do things with certain skins/items on, which in the original, you needed to return to the main menu to remove. While it's less of an issue in the first place, you can also now freely change items on the go! And the items are WAY MORE FUN.Honestly, there's not too much to say on this - it's fun, it's goofy, I feel like I more than got my money's worth already and I'm not done. While the story is complete, plenty left to discover and destroy! I haven't even touched the DLC yet.

I even bought it on Steam when it finally launched on here as I bought it on Epic originally hence why my playtime on here is only 14 hrs. The multiverse DLC is hilarious and very well put together. _childDocuments_.review: BETTER THAN ELDEN RING! Okay, okay, hear me out. I know Elden Ring is one of the greatest games ever made, however this game has so many positives that Elden Ring LACKS! First of all, Goat Simulator 3 is LOCAL co-op. This game brings back the good old couch video games of the past. Modern gamers often forget that video game systems like the NES, SNES, SEGA, N64, and the PS2 originated with MANY multiplayer titles that were designed to be enjoyed in the same room with your friends and family! I play this game with my two young kids and we have a BLAST. Did I enjoy playing through the Elden Ring DLC recently? Heck yeah. But would I pick that over an afternoon of laughs and fun with my kids? Not a chance.This brings me to benefit #2: Goat Simulator is HILARIOUS. I often genuinely laugh out loud while playing this game, and my kids? They often laugh so hard they have to pause to catch their breath! Even when I'm not belly-laughing like Santa Claus, I am still chuckling and guffawing every couple of minutes. The references and jokes are coming at you constantly and it's so much fun just to discover what silly thing the next quest or area has in store!Exploration and discovery is another great plus in this game. I won't say it's better than Elden Ring in this regard, however it is just as good in my opinion. In Elden Ring discovering items through exploration results in about 70% crafting materials, 20% armor, and 10% weapons. These things are nice, but other than the weapons, don't drastically change the experience of the game. In Goat Simulator, when you unlock rewards, you very often get wild new outfits (including some that actually completely replace your character model), and lots of crazy special abilities. Here are just a few examples: instead of being a goat, you can be a hammerhead shark rolling around on a skateboard; you can unlock the ability to attack people with giant Kraken tentacles; you can fire lasers out of your eyes; and you can wear gold shoes!Finally, this game is fun and accessible, in the same quality of a great PS2 era game. Some of the quests are challenging, but most of them are fairly easy. While Elden Ring is the type of game a gaming veteran wants to play, Goat Simulator is the type of game that MAKES gamers. My daughter is nine years old and my son is five, and they both can play and enjoy this game. I will always be grateful for that. you won't regret buying Goat Simulator 3!
_childDocuments_.name: Goat Simulator 3

_childDocuments_.review: Goat Simulator 3 is one of the all time great sequels to hit Steam.  From its benevolent baaaa’s to its special ed mammals, there is nothing that'll satisfy you more on God's green Earth.  As a former goat myself, there isn't a game that simulates goats quite like this one.  It honestly makes me question why I leave the house anymore, what's the point in going outside if I can just sit on my pc playing Goat Simulator for 18 hours of my day.  This game is by far the best game to have released in the past 66 years and it's not even close.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying that I have several hundred hours in the original Goat Simulator. While my Steam profile may say I have little over 100 hours, it was a game I regularly played in offline mode and introduced to many people.I fully expected (and was willing) to be paying for another Goat Simulator DLC.This is a fully-fledged game, online multiplayer (frequently teased about being missing in the previous installment) is present. The map is expanded and built out to be a full game, in a way that you would not expect from an otherwise joke series. I  goat simulator and all of its DLC. This is a game clearly made as a love letter to the original, with a map that is inspired by the locations in the original game and its DLC content, but built out to an extreme degree. I highly recommend this game as a fun way to kill time, especially to play and enjoy as a party game until other people show up to an event or game night. If you loved the first game, you'll love this one. If you  thought that the DLC was a bit much in the original, this is a great way middle ground, with less complication than the later DLC content. My only real complaint is I would have preferred to have the map still be separated into different areas, if it meant that we could have more chaos from intractable objects at a time, even if it meant that the game was less stable.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the first, buy this game. NOW. It's practically the original but better. Sure, they have 1 free map, but it's MASSIVE, it makes up for the cost of the game. _childDocuments_.review: In this game, you get to:- Cause millions of dollars worth of property damage with zero consequences- Reawaken and play as Jesus- Get sucked into a portal you make from IKEA furniture- Visit a church in the cemetery (that doubles as a fitness center)- Unleash an apocalypse of banana-human hybrid zombiesI haven't gotten to a point in the game where it's happened, but I wouldn't be surprised if I have to fight god.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted to be a goat with a rocket launcher? No? Well, too bad. Goat Simulator 3 lets you do that, and about 1,000 other things that make no sense. The developers woke up one day, looked at a goat, and said, “What if this thing could ride a bike and destroy civilization?” And here we are.Gameplay:You’re a goat. You lick things, headbutt people, and launch yourself across town like a furry wrecking ball. Want to ride a jet-powered shopping cart into a swimming pool? Done. Fancy summoning a tornado made of farm animals? Absolutely. Physics? Optional.Multiplayer:Up to four goats in one game. If you and your friends ever wanted to role-play as a goat biker gang terrorizing the suburbs, your dream has come true. There are no rules, just maximum goat chaos.Final Verdict:This game is a fever dream, and you’re the goat. 10/10, would headbutt a giraffe in

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best game ever created. It has references to almost anything you can imagine. From classic shows references to horror movies to FPS games to literally anything. Even the descriptions are funny and cute. And you're literally a goat who goes on an adventure licking and kicking things. You can go on top of skyscrapers and jump off. You can ride cars. You can go to slow motion and ride bicycles (goats can't ride bicycles in regular time speed ofc). You can wear lots of skins. It's my favorite game of all time. After a rough day, I'll just go into this game and roam around the city, wearing different skins each time and visiting some town and doing something random. It's almost better than real life. I really loved the yoga speech about goats.
_childDocuments_.name: Goat Simulator 3

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun exploration and climbing game where it seems like anything goes. I especially like the freedom of roaming an open world. If there is a challenge or collectible charm nearby you will hear a magic like sound. It helps if you have headphones to know which direction to look . You never know where something might be hidden in, on or around. Its especially fun to play with friends as you go around reaping havoc and destroying property. This is one of the most imaginative games I have ever encountered. I can only wonder what Goat Simulator 4 could have in store.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure what's missing here. It's not like I had high standards. We all bought this knowing that it is asset flip garbage with the sole purpose of being an anarchic playground. But, unlike the first entry in the series, it acts like it wants me to care, to achieve, to be something other than a vessel of wanton destruction and chaos. It's trying too hard to be funny (there are some legit laughs, though). It's trying too hard to be blase/cool/detached. It wants me to have goals. To uncover new goals. It loves parody ... so ... much. But it's still, at its core, a really terribly made game. Goofy controls, wonky physics, and a collision model that leaves you wandering under the world geometry after every third fall. It's not funny enough. It's not chaotic enough. And it's too goal oriented to be fun, given how badly it is made. I'm just trying to get a bit more out of it to justify the cost, but, at four hours, I'm rapidly running out of interest.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this because i remembered it being funny, and thought my kid (6) might enjoy. He does. He very much enjoys the chaos. I think its a lot like how it felt to play GTA3Me and him found secret after hilarious secret, each time we find anything conspicuous - which is everything - we poked around looking for the joke, and honestly i cant remember feeling like they didnt follow through on the punchline. If you think theres something funny going its because there is. You will always feel like this, and so you will be seeing a lot of funny stuff going on.We completed the entire base game, got everything but the giraffe and shark naturally, (you can buy almost anything, and by the end of the game we had like 800k points. Things cost maybe 3k, you will have more money than things to buy) and we have started the Multiverse DLC. I cannot stress enough just how thorough the worldbuilding is here. This team absolutely knocks it out of the park.Im almost 80 hours in and the game is still entirely enjoyable for myself and my kid. We love goat simulator, and so will you

_childDocuments_.review: Goat Simulator 3 is literally my dream GS game and it comes with a ♥♥♥♥-ton of improvements compared to it's predecessor simply titled Goat Simulator.Lets start with that has been changed/added:Mutators have been switched out for accessories Pilgor can wear, some of which give you abilities. To be honest, it's an alright change, and some of the abilities with certain items are pretty cool. Still, it takes a slight bit of charm away. You want to be a stinky, buff giraffe? Then you are playing the wrong game bucko, go play the original instead.The map is by far the biggest difference. The original's map(s) was quite alright, though it wasn't a fully-fledged open world like they did here. Still, San Angora is pretty big and well designed. This also goes for the DLC, Multiverse of Nonsense, which it's map isn't as big since it is DLC, but still well designed.The game-play still feels like Goat Simulator, not much to say here, except Pilgor has a new ability where you can charge your headbutt. This is a nice new addition. Also, driving cars isn't a paid feature now. If you know, you know.The visuals. I like and dislike this change at the same time. On one hand, everything looks much better and cleaner but on the other hand, the graphics in the original were sort of Glitchy and rough and that was what made them so charming. Here though, they went for a more cartoon-ish look and if i am being honest, It just doesn't fit the game for me.Oh boy, the physics. I am pretty conflicted on this to be honest. On one hand, they are greatly improved and some of the DNA from the original's physics still remain. On the other hand though, with there being new physics, they simply don't feel as buggy/out of control which should be a good thing, but this is Goat Simulator we are talking about here. Getting stuck in a wall was a common physics glitch in the original, but it contributed to the charm, just like the graphics and the Mutators did. Here though? It doesn't happen randomly and you have to actively try to make it happen.In general, It is a better game than the original, but in the process of making it's self better, it loses it's charm. Don't get me wrong, i'm not saying it doesn't have any charm, It certainly does, but the charm that is there isn't as unique and fresh as the Original's.Highly recommended :) 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Well made and long awaited sequel (triquel?) to the original Goat Simulator. You probably know what you're getting yourself into, if not, I'd recommend playing the first game and its DLCs, especially since the bundle with all the originals is 5 bucks on sale while this was 15.You run around on a sandbox GTA5-esque island and do various missions and quests across the map. It's a nice ambience, and the soundtrack isn't as catchy as in the old games, but it's nice. There's various gags, easter eggs and references everywhere, be it random props in the world or entire missions. These are the core of Goat Simulator, although I feel like the originals were slightly more authentic and funnier. The whole game being themed around this one map is a slight downside, as the different themes of the originals always kept it fresh and memorable.There's quite a lot of props and abilities to mess around with, younger me would've killed to play this for days. The controls, UI and everything feels betters than the originals, it's pretty smooth and nice to control. The gameplay is pretty solid for what you're doing, and there's a lot of various small fun surprises and interactions.It's not that deep, just some goofy fun and tasks to spend some time with quite a bit of content. Although, 30 bucks is kinda steep, especially since the first games are way cheaper, and are essentially the same but with slightly more oomph and different themes (although pretty old by now).

_childDocuments_.review: In Goat Simulator 3, you’re not just a goat; you’re a full-on chaos agent with a taste for mayhem. Picture this: you're prancing around a city, headbutting cars, launching yourself through the air, and causing delightful havoc. It's hilarious, ridiculous, and surprisingly addictive. Perfect for anyone who loves laughing at the sheer unpredictability of it all.

_childDocuments_.review: When i first booted this up i thought it was going to be a really obnoxious, reference filled, expensive piece of fan-service.The first elder scrolls joke was so "GET IT?? GET IT!? REMEMBER SKYRIM?!!" i kinda just gulped and expected the most obnoxious unfunny experience of my life.However, I am pleased to tell you that the first joke was probably the worst i encountered. The farmer remains extremely annoying all throughout his appearances but i guess that's kind of intentional since he ends up being the final boss.This game feels shockingly fresh and original for something i expected to be a milk of the original franchise. my only complaint is the lack of "goat" characters. There was no customisation in the original, you just went around unlocking more playables. The item shop feels like a pretty piss poor cheaper alternative to just letting you play as lots of different animals and joke creatures instead of just.. like.. being able to buy a new hat or shoes.The eleven pound DLC I've seen is obnoxiously expensive since it only realistically includes one more playable model (Pilgor). I would however buy a pack of just the original goats from every Goat sim game before Goat simulator 3.It takes place mainly in a city?? why cant i play as Old goat (Tyrannosaur) from Goat MMO??The price tag is pretty justified, its funny and very full feeling, Its a complete parody game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 98 year old father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Daughter, who is 57 now. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my daughter, as she is always out with her friends or just emptying her colostomy bag. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside her. I loaded into the game, picked my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Daughter for help and she hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Daughter since my hamster had died. This game has ever since brought me and my daughter closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the prison walls together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my daughter multiple happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played either Goat Simulator games and was surprised to notice right away that Goat Simulator 3 is a major downgrade from the 1st one, which I played immediately after. In 12 minutes, I immediately realized what was wrong. Goat Simulator 3 is in the process of adding too much realism despite the slight new cartoony aspects of the setting. While the original was a ironically unrealistic setting where absurd things happen due to physics, Goat Simulator 3 is a silly town with a lot of realistic elements. Goat Simulator 3 also makes less use of ironically good (bad) physics. In the original, you can tether objects a short distance and use that to do funny things like throwing people from a distance. You can also spin several times in the air before landing and skip over water long distances.Goat Simulator 3 thought letting you swim wouldn't be boring - which it is. Goat Simulator 3 at best lets you somersault once. You can barely tether things and the distance for grabbing objects with the tongue is sadly short. The strangest change of them all was the absence of the pointless scoring system. Goat Simulator satirizes the score system in series like Tony Hawk or just classical games in general where almost everything you do awards points and multiplies it. It ironically made doing random things entertaining to see if you gained points. Goat Simulator 3 instead has boring events like helping the town do things. I would rather just shove people off surfaces or find more things to blow up, which is now difficult to do except the gas station. Overall, it's a sad downgrade almost like playing GTA V with realism mods. Some minor QoL changes are there, but they were not a worthy tradeoff.P.S. It's now set in the late afternoon which is just moody and dull.

_childDocuments_.review: Goat Simulator 3 might be the perfect game, merely because it knows exactly what it is and doesn't try to be anything different: it sets out to be a silly game about goats and it is a silly game about goats, it succeeds at that immensely.Its a sandbox game where the goal isn't to win or lose, but to GOAT. Makes it perfect for those that might need a good foot forward when getting into video games, because the goal isn't about some concept of competition (there are mini-games, but they aren't meant to be balanced because of what your goat can equip) so the goat goal at the end of the day, is to have fun and GS3 does that well, because at the end of the day, isn't that why we play games? To have fun? Sure, winning and losing are fun in their own right, but if a person doesn't have a healthy competitive spirit, then winning is great but losing feels awful.If there's one thing this game can teach you, its to not take things too seriously. Keep it balanced. Be a little silly sometimes, especially when no one else is. The world needs more smiles, I'd love to see yours.

_childDocuments_.review: Goat Simulator 3 brings a very well-known game concept, one of open-world sandbox quest hunting, into its 3rd dimension. Now with the axis of being able to walk to the right, this game excels at being stupendous fun. It´s just what the two games before it were missing! So, before you have to read whatever else I have to say about it, this little intro should already tell you that I absolutely endorse this game for what it is right now.For those who have played the original Goat Simulator and have equally nostalgic feelings for it, this installation is simply a treat. Yes, the EpicGames Account link is a hoof-kick into the plump behind, but the general opening for multiplayer invites some interesting ideas. But as I see this still more as a singleplayer experience, I can assure you, the overall experience also works very well for those rather content with exploring on their own. The world is big, exciting, full of stuff and Pilgor has just been freshly styled at the barbershop around the corner. So let´s talk about the nitty, gritty and goaty.As you finally awake, this game opens its doors to you. Explore, create, destroy. Those 3 concepts alone made the very first version already a great game. Just that this time, there´s much more concept to the whole idea. While the very first game got famous for its ridiculous gameplay style and especially bugs, brought to you by the Machinima and Blooper Video era, this one has all hoofs to the ground. It feels less random in its controls and less “homey” in its world design, but not in a bad way. Everything comes together nicely in a world where there´s a lot of intent, but still also a lot of fun. The more “game like” structure of this simulation game’s world allowed the developers to create more distinct eastereggs, quests to fulfil and secrets to explore. There´s rarely a corner with nothing and even rarer nothing without a corner. The world is vivid, lived in and every action has feedback. Exploring is fun and small rewards, lots of collectibles and even events not explicitly pointed out to you are able to be found. The game gives you hints and most puzzles are easy to solve, some just fun challenges and some later ones can actually require a slight hint of problem-solving competency.As Pilgor comes to his senses, you feel the controls at your hands, electrifying your body. They´re still a bit wonky and floaty, but easy to get used to – especially if you played the former versions. The controls are not the type of floaty like ice physics in other games and easily modified with a plethora of different accessories and other clothing items that even allow you to fly, glide, dig, climb and more. So don´t worry about those.Yet the game didn´t just update the controls, but also the graphics. You now have a beautiful surrounding, sometimes with the same old over-the-top effects and visual “shortcuts” that, while obviously being cheap, feel like they belong – mostly due to the sarcastic undertone. There´s love in almost every detail and a lot of detail in the love given. The gameplay loop might not be for everyone. So be warned. This game requires a bit of a “brain off” kind of mindset to the playstyle. You absolutely have to love to explore an open world without a distinct goal… or at least without a distinct way to get to your goal. For those that played the newer open world Zelda games, this concept might be very understandable. Just that in this game there´s not required checkpoints. Your progress towards the finale is steady as long as you take action and fulfil quests of any kind. I completed everything there is to this game except for the last repetitive achievements and while I dragged my feet towards the end, I still didn´t get bored out too much – as I went in bored and just wanted to be somewhere else to start with. So to reiterate: This gameplay loop isn’t for everyone and you have to like “simply being in a crafted world”.The big reason this game is enjoyable is due to three main factors in my eyes:A) The enjoyable world design with all its silly meta comments, quests, love for detail and actual good world designB) The graphics and performance are on point and while this obviously isn´t the absolutely highest quality, you can see the competence and feel the attention. The style is less an issue of skill but more an intentional consideration and that feels just great.C) You´re left alone. Yes, I mean that. Other games take you at your hand, give you a lot of UI and bombard you with a To-Do-List. This one does as well, but there´s no rewards bigger or more important than the other, you don´t miss out by doing something else first and there´s no way to really “fail” a quest. It´s a To-Do-List, but if you can free you of the urge to complete everything right away, it becomes more of a completion log than that.Good question!I´d say this game isn´t for people that need directions or are easily bored by the simple act of exploring a world for what it is. You might feel like there´s no purpose to anything and no progress really made.This game also isn’t for any of the hardcore competitive gamers obviously. But I´d throw my hat into the ring and say “You can enjoy this too!”. You just have to like what it offers – not hate it for what it isn’t.Lastly, I´d say this might actually not be a good multiplayer game. Don`t get me wrong, there´s specific games ONLY for multiplayer and it’s indeed a lot of fun exploring together with your friends, but it’s not the type of game that you break out one evening and play for that purpose. At its heart it’s still mostly an exploration game with a limited world. So good enough for 4 people and a quick fun, but there’s no real tasks that are made for multiplayer except said games. Nothing feels like it needs any more goats to be around than it already has. But of course it’s nice that you don´t have to feel lonely when playing. So I can also definitely see this as a couples game to calm down and have some silly fun. Or a great game for streaming with some friends.I like this game. I like these types of games. And I like them when they´re done well.Between other good games like Alba, WiiSportsResorts Plane mode, A short hike and the original Goat Simulator, this integrates high in my list of these games. The developer already confirmed that they´re working on DLCs, there´s semi-regular updates and if all those things come and stay true, this game might get the same amazing community around it that the very first game had. A lot of mods, but also a lot of different ideas explored and other maps to explore. The creativity is high with this one and I can only see it age well into the future!

_childDocuments_.review: Title: A Gimmick That Lost Its CharmReview:I had high hopes for Goat Simulator given its quirky premise and the hype around it, but honestly, it didn’t live up to the hype for me. What started as a fun and absurd concept quickly wore thin.The gameplay is pretty shallow. The idea of controlling a goat and causing chaos sounds amusing in theory, but it gets old really fast. The novelty of headbutting objects and running amok wears off quickly when you realize there’s not much depth or variety to the activities. It feels like a one-trick pony that quickly loses its appeal.Graphically, the game isn’t anything to write home about. It’s clear that the focus was on the comedic aspect rather than creating a visually impressive experience. The world feels empty and lacking in detail, which makes the whole experience feel a bit dull.The bugs and glitches, which might have been funny at first, eventually become frustrating. They often interrupt the gameplay and take away from any potential enjoyment. It feels like the game’s charm is based on its flaws, but after a while, these quirks just start to seem like poor design choices rather than endearing features.The lack of a meaningful goal or progression system also detracts from the overall experience. Without any real objectives or challenges, it’s hard to stay engaged for long periods. It’s more of a time-waster than an actual game with depth.In summary, Goat Simulator might offer a few laughs and moments of absurdity, but it didn’t hold my attention for long. It feels like a gimmick that’s fun for a short burst but lacks the substance to keep you coming back. If you’re looking for a game with more depth and replayability, this one might not be for you. 20$ not worth it or even 30.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think you'd be able to improve peak simulator, but alas Peak Simulator 3 does just that! With three times the peak of the first entry, it's sure to get your peakometers overflowing. Coming off of the disappointment of Peak Simulator 2, often considered a "dud", Peak Simulator 3 brings itself back to tradition. Gone are the days of saving up your star tokens to afford a quazi-nuclear lithogram, now your QNLs are unlimited, and available right from the start. The Magicka system has also been overhauled, ensuring zorbles no longer impede your journey to excellency. Peak Simulator 2 was also very controversial for its often frustrating boss fights. While famous bosses from Peak Simulator returned, such as the Fallen Foreskin or the Glizzy Gobbler, they failed to live up to many people's expectations, and new bosses such as the Giant Evil Prolapsed Anus just didn't feel like they belonged in the game. While the Anus boss returns in Peak Sim 3, it has also been reworked, and now feels right at home alongside its eleventy-seventh fraternal great-granduncle, the Anal Ass-ass-in. New additions to Peak Sim only help improve its simulatorlike gameplay further. The Gussy Grappler, while seeming inconsequential on first look, is actually one of the best mechanics I've ever seen in a video game, allowing you to grapple that gussy with reckless abandon. Life just got a whole lot gussier. In totality, Peak Sim 3 marks the grand return of the Peak Sim franchise to its former peakiness. With statues marked to be erected to the developers in Fecal Frontiers, Montana, it's undeniable that this game will in fact have a significant impact on the United States election this year. Godspeed, Peak Simulator, and thank you for your service. I salute you.

name: PHOGS!
detailed_description: Play as Red and Blue, a duo of dogs on a captivating, puzzle-filled adventure for all ages! Stretch, bark and bounce your way through obstacles and challenges across three vibrant worlds, filled with hilarious physics-based gameplay and sneaky secrets. One Phog, Two Phog, Red Phog, Blue Phog Your faithful companions. Red and Blue are the goodest of doggos who will accompany you through your entire fun-filled adventure. Double-ended doggos. Linked by a stretchy belly, your Phogs are inseparable... for better or worse! Emotes at your fingertips. Pull cheeky faces at the touch of a button. Two heads are better than one! Co-operation is key. Put your heads together to solve taxing, teamwork-based puzzles. An epic journey. Explore 24 fantastical levels stuffed with exciting challenges and creatures to play with. Play YOUR way. Supporting single-player and shared-controller gameplay, plus local and online co-op, Red and Blue are always ready to play! Enter the Phoggyverse Nom Nom Nom. Forage through Food World, teeming with tasty treats. From hot buttered toast to chopped celery... even a river of chocolate! The dream team. Stroll through Sleep World, complete with teddy bears, cushions and quilts, all nestled in the glow of the soothing night-light. Fun in the sun. Pounce through the crazy toybox of Play World, exploring a beach amusement park, a retro arcade, and everything in between. Woof! A hat for every occasion. Customize your Phoggos! Find the Golden Bones hidden throughout every level to build your collection of adorable hats. And more to explore. The Phoggyverse contains a wealth of hidden secrets. Search far and wide to discover them all.

_childDocuments_.review: Phogs! is a cute physics puzzler game for 1-2 people. I played it on the same screen with my 4-year-old with each of us using Xbox S|X controllers to control one half of the phog.The main story will take you around 9-12 hours. The game is split into "hubs". There is a home hub that links to three thematic hubs. Each of those hubs has several levels, some space to goof off, and a few extra collectibles. You can collect golden bones and trade them in for silly hats.PROs - Great looking game. - The game design will give a nice tiny preview of a new mechanic before making it part of a puzzle. - Puzzles got more challenging over time. - Silly hats. - NPCs will pet the dogs. - bark bark bark bark bark.CONs - No ultrawide support as far as I could tell. - Got stuck in the floor a few times. You can click a "respawn" action in the menu to fix it and it'll drop you close by. - My kid wants a Phogs! shirt and they don't exist.If you're on the fence, give the demo a whirl. It's very representative of the game. It excludes the hubs and instead strings together a few parts of some of the levels in each hub.

_childDocuments_.review: PHOGS!~~~~~~~PHOGS is a family-friendly puzzle platformer. The game revolves around two attached dogs and their starchy adventures. Play and control both at the same time to traverse around the fun goofy world. Use both of your dog heads to control and manipulate items to solve puzzles and overcome platforms. Gameplay: PHOGS! Let's you play as two attached dogs and now you must help them throughout this goofy awkward world full of puzzles and platforms. PHOGS’s gameplay seems to be targeted towards every age; the game seems pretty childish and my initial impression was that it was for children. But no! The puzzles and platformer elements are intuitive enough for adults to enjoy as well. The gameplay is super-simplified with its WASD to control blue-collared dogs and Arrow keys for pink. Use space to interact items with the blue-collared dog and right control for pink. There are puzzles, platformers, and obstacles scattered around everywhere. And you will have to use a dog, or both at the same time, to interact with items to complete the puzzles or interact with a platform. The world revolves around these puzzles; each is well made and well placed, and all of them serve a purpose.  At no point did I feel that anything was out of place, or that the game’s target audience might not appreciate this. For an example: At the very beginning, you will need to raise four platforms from different floors of the beginning stage to be able to travel to different parts of the map. And in order to get to these platforms, you will have to go through a prescribed number of other platforms and puzzles. Some were as easy as placing a ball in a triggering switch, while a bit of a tricky one that requires you to use both of your dogs to reach a peak while strong winds are blowing.  Although there are a ton of puzzles and things to interact with, the good thing is they are very simple and tasteful. Even my 8-year-old cousin took a few moments to figure out the trickiest one, which is great! You don’t need stupid hard puzzles and platforms to enjoy a game; you need smart and well-placed ones. Another feature that is important and plays out quite well in a goofy way is stretching. By hitting Left and Right Shift, you can stretch the dogs and hit space/right control at the same time to grab on to items and switches to complete various tasks. For example, there are two switches far apart that you will have to interact with at the same time to start a function. Simply stretching the dogs and hitting grab at the same time will engage with the said switch. World design: Beautiful, colorful, and joyful is what my 8-year-old cousin said while playing, and I agree. There is a certain level of charm to this goofy cartoonish art style. And combined with its great visuals and relaxing environment, the game felt very good while playing. The only downside to PHOGS’ world design would be its awkward terrain and elements scattered along the pathways, which created quite a few minor annoyances throughout the game. Music and sound effects: Well-selected and implemented; fits the theme of the game just fine (but the music did get repetitive after a while). Puzzles: Easy, intuitive, and well designed. I’m saying this again . . . puzzles don’t need to be crazy hard or stupid, they need to be clever and well balanced. I must say PHOGS did a decent job at it. The puzzles didn’t hinder the flow of my gameplay. They were well integrated with the world design, easy enough for the kids to enjoy and clever enough to grab my attention.Considering all aspects of the game, PHOGS turned out to be a fun family-friendly platformer with a clever mixture of puzzles throughout its world. I played it with a young cousin of mine to get his perspective; it seems like the kid loved it, and rightfully so! A fun world design, goofy cartoonish art style, clever puzzles, and amazing visuals. Although a decently sized game, there is not much replay-ability which is something to consider as well. Positives: + Fun gameplay + Simple yet clever puzzles+ Unique art style + Fun and goofy gameplay machines + Decent music and sound effects + Collectables to find Negatives: - Few bugs here and there- Music got repetitive after a while - No replayability Dive into a fun goofy world with two cute dogs and their adventurous journey.  8/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: PHOGS! is exactly the game we need in 2020 – fun and violence-free title that is perfect to play with a friend and have some relaxing time together. Or alone if all of your friends got eaten by Cyberpunk 2077.🐾 Phogs themselves. No need for an explanation, just look at these cuties!🐾 Remote Play. You may ask, “Why is it a good thing?” Simple: this neat feature allows your friends to play with you even if they do not have the same game. I have already tried it in Tricky Towers, and the experience was 95% positive (except for some freezes, but these could have been caused by my friend’s slow internet connection). So, Remote Play can become very useful if your friends are not sure whether they want to buy the game or not, but want to it out;🐾 Lovely visuals! This is the best part – each world is full of lush colourful plants, cute creatures, bright backgrounds and various items. Not to mention that even separate levels within one world have their own unique differences and special elements;🐾 Smart puzzles. I cannot say that they were too difficult, but neither were they too easy or boring. Again, each level presents something new, which makes the gameplay fresh even withing one location. I think both children and adults can enjoy puzzles like these and solve them without guides – you just need common sense, some skills and a bit of creativity; 🐾 Nice music. Most tracks were relaxing, but there were also some more upbeat tunes that worked well with important scenes. In general, this kind of music works perfectly with puzzle games and makes them even more enjoyable;🐾 Various secrets and collectables, which include little green men that hide in the strangest places, golden bones and sweetest little hats for your Phogs. Each world has its own set of decorations, by the way.🐕Game physics. It can be both advantageous and very annoying at times. On the one hand, some glitches let you get through difficult parts without issue; but on the other hand, they can also turn out to be an obstacle. In particular, I can say this about Phogs themselves and their stretching ability – a very tricky thing indeed; 🐕Good length, but not that much replayability. I like completing the game once and enjoying it to the fullest while I am doing it, so for me this aspect of the game is not a con. One world with all its levels took me about 5 hours; also, I did not find all little green men, so we can add another half an hour (maybe even more) if I decide to look for them more carefully in the future. There are three words, so in total the game should last for at least 15 hours. Pretty good length for a puzzle game. Sadly, there is only one way to complete each level/world, so the replayability depends only on who you decide to play with, nothing else.🦴 KILL THE ALARM CLOCKS! With fire!!! OK, guys, let us be real: we all hate the sound of our alarm clock in the morning. Now, imagine that it also starts running away from you, screaming in the highest possible voice and ringing two bells in both of its tiny cute hands. And now imagine that there are three of them in the same room…If your imagination does not work well today, PHOGS! will be more than happy to show you the world with these “wonderful” creatures. God save us all…;🦴 Occasional bugs. I have encountered 2 of them within about 5 hours of playing; both were connected with textures – first, my doggos dropped behind one big construction and could not get out of it, so I had to restart the level. Second, the poor creatures got stuck inside a gear. The thing stretched them to an unbelievable condition, but, thankfully, I was able to catch the moon with one of the dog’s heads and get out of this trap. Such bugs are not really bad, but considering that all levels restart from the last worm , you can lose some sweet progress.Woof-woof! Oh, wait, you do not speak Phogian, right? Let me translate: “Should you buy and play PHOGS!?” - “Yes, without a doubt!”The store page does not lie: this is a game for all ages that will be neither too challenging for children, nor too simple for adults. It has its own unique puzzles and features, and all of them are well executed. Very rare bugs do not spoil the gameplay at all too. All in all, there is literally no reason to skip PHOGS! unless you have something against cute dogs with two heads and no tail.P.S. The cutest part is that Teddy Bears in the Sleep World can pet Phogs when you run past them. I love this small detail❣️

_childDocuments_.review: A recipe:One copy of PHOGS!One person you talk with on the regular. Solve puzzles, enjoy chaos, mash the "bark" button frantically.Right, so, the game itself?  You play one head of a two-headed dog-thing whose heads are linked by a stretchy doggy tube.  Somehow, each head can locomote on its own, and by virtue of being stuck together, each head influences movement of the unit as a whole.  So if you're not coordinated, it gets a bit chaotic.  I'm not saying we didn't get ourselves tangled on a post, because I'd be lying.  We totally did.Aaand together, you solve puzzles.  So far, they have not been really hard puzzles, they're just more challenging because both of you have to agree on the same general plan.  Since the game has hidden collectibles strewn about the map, your partner also has to want to go poking about looking for them as well.I don't think my wife stopped laughing the whole time we played.  2.2 thumbs up for that alone.  Worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're on the lookout for a game where you can be stuck—literally—with your partner but still manage to look cute and adorable, PHOGS is a must-try! If you're on the hunt for a cute and charming co-op game that will have you and your partner stuck together in the most adorable way, PHOGS is absolutely the game for you! This is the kind of game that’s perfect for easing into the co-op genre, with gameplay that's lighthearted, simple, and guaranteed to make you smile. Its difficulty is far more forgiving compared to some other co-op games out there, and the quirky physics add an extra layer of hilarity to the experience. The sight of two dogs joined together, navigating puzzles, is bound to keep things fun and stress-free.One of the things I absolutely adore about PHOGS is the dreamy world it creates. Each level feels like stepping into a different dreamland filled with vibrant colors and the most adorable creatures. It's like you’re traveling through a series of magical, otherworldly places that make you feel warm and fuzzy inside. As you and your partner explore, you'll solve fun and approachable puzzles that never feel overwhelming. It's the perfect mix of challenge and charm—just enough to keep you engaged, but not so tough that you'll want to give up or (even worse) end up frustrated with each other. It’s honestly the co-op game I’d recommend to anyone who wants a fun, easygoing time without risking any friendship drama!As for playtime, I feel like PHOGS offers a great balance. It’s not too long to the point of feeling exhausting, but it’s not so short that you’re left wanting more. The game is well worth its price, offering just enough gameplay to feel rewarding and satisfying without dragging on.However, like any game, PHOGS has a few glitches. Sometimes, player two might not be able to see all the hats in the hat shop, preventing you from unlocking some items. There are also occasional glitches during gameplay, but these often lead to hilarious moments with your partner, like when your dog body starts twisting and glitching nonstop.The most significant issue I encountered was trying to enter  and failing repeatedly. Thankfully, this problem was fixed by visiting another area first and then returning to .Despite these small issues, PHOGS is still a cozy, cute, and relationship-safe co-op game! If you're a fan of wholesome, adorable games and want a lighthearted experience with a friend or partner, this is definitely the game to try. It's charming, fun, and full of heartwarming moments!
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

However, this game has some issues when playing with a buddy which I will mention below after the pros.- If you're like me and play it online, I would recommend using something like Discord to talk with each other. Not necessary though if you want some chaos, which is the way we played, and we only used Steam chat if it was necessary. Good silent team bonding XD- Cute and quirky characters!- Puzzles are pretty straightforward but some can be aggravating.- Colorful worlds, very playful, makes you want to bite in everything which is unfortunately not always the case XD- Mechanics stays fresh in each world and isn't too overused.- HATS! FUN HATS!-While I was hosting, my friend had some animation issues with Play World's last level ("boss" level) where she was stuck in a loop during an animation and I suddenly was able to control both dogs while she was still connected. The issue is fixed when when she is the one hosting.- With that said, no matter who hosts, the other party cannot see every unlocked hat in the hat shop. Mind you, we haven't bought the hats, it is just empty for the one who is not hosting.- My keyboard settings gets reset each time I start up the game, I have to rebind it all again for both dogs which is annoying.All in all, it took us 13 hours to finish this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, with fun mechanics. I'd say grab a friend to play with if you can, it gets really fun when played in co-op, but playing it by yourself is very fun too! _childDocuments_.review: PHOGS!:After how good and fun A Way Out was me and my friend looked for a new game and since PHOGS! came out recently we wanted to check it out.The gameplay is simple, you are a dog with 2 faces and one person controls the other face so you solve puzzles and platform all over the place. The gameplay is fun engaging and unique, there is an arcade level where you get into the arcade machines and play them to get points in one level; in one level you are in a fruit factory trying to solve problems while squashing fruits and such, in one level you are in a stealth section and trying to protect the light ball. While I didn't even tell you some of the best levels the game offers, the consistency for level quality is mixed. There are 3 worlds and the best one is drastically better than the worst one its not even close. Also the game is fairly long so don't get scared when I told you there are only 3 worlds, there are bosses and such too.Aside from level consistency my biggest problem with the game is amount of bugs the game has. It messes you up a lot and me and my friend got frustrated a lot while playing the game. I honestly think you should be aware of these bugs.In conclusion this is a charming unique fun co-op game that has miserable bugs but still is a damn good time. I would've easily recommended you if there were no bugs and glitches but its up to you if you can suffer :D
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game of its own right but as far as games you can play cooperatively with a small child I think this might be, like, the best I've ever played. Was a little hesitant to pick this up at full release price but my daughter has been harping on me since we played the demo and I am happy with the decision. I have a 3 and 5 year old. Phogs's fun and bright art style gets them excited enough to talk about throughout the day, with puzzles and gameplay that challenges without frustrating. It's the nature of cooperative play which takes Phogs over the top for me. You can use a two controller scheme for couch-cooperative teamwork or a scheme where each controls both phogs, to help guide younger players. Either way you can help steer each other in the right direction while both are totally playing the game. Everything about it is executed well; controls, art, sound, music, gameplay. The devs definitely had a strong vision, with the talent and resources to execute it.

_childDocuments_.review: PHOGS! provided very enjoyable and creative puzzle-solving. As a Phog, I was able to explore colorful, uniquely designed levels by barking orders to guide the Phog herd. Each new area had its own charming aesthetic and obstacles to overcome. What really stood out was how varied each stage felt - one moment I was in a grassy meadow and the next a cryptic underwater zone. Beyond the charming visuals, the music fit every location perfectly with upbeat, playful tracks that kept me engaged throughout my time herding Phogs. While simple, using bark abilities on things like switches or to move platforms made for satisfying puzzles to work through. I can see kids especially having a blast playing this colourfully cute game together, cooperating to lead the Phogs to each level's exit. With enjoyable mechanics and adventures for all ages, PHOGS! seems like it will provide many fun family gaming sessions.

_childDocuments_.review: A great puzzle with an oddly-shaped protagonist that will take you on an adventure through colorful and happy world.What's hidden behind the silly name, I hear you ask? Why, it's the most adorable thing you've ever laid your eyes on in this crazy year of 2020. If by adorable you mean a legless stretchy body with two dog heads on each end, be my guest, I won't judge.The story's pretty much nonexistent. A phog dreams of his favorite things: a big mat to sleep on, a colorful ball to play with and a bowl with food. After waking up and realizing it has none of those things, the phog sets out on an adventure to find them. There's no talking or text; the little bits of information you do get are presented as slices of life throughout different worlds.The game's a physics puzzle. You're introduced to the mechanics right at the start in a tutorial level. You use left and right side of a gamepad to control each head; analog sticks to move, shoulder buttons to bark or grab things and trigger buttons to stretch the body. Keyboard can also be used, but it just doesn't work that well when you have to juggle with all those buttons and can quickly lead to frustration during some particularly hard puzzles. The game supports co-op where one of the heads can be controlled with a second gamepad, which is great if you have kids, or by finding someone online. I didn't try this because the game is definitely more enjoyable when you play it on your own. It's so easy to mess things up and you're bound to find someone online who'll just pull his head in the other direction or refuse to cooperate, which can lead to funny situations, but grows old quick if you actually want to finish a level. You'll also have trouble remembering which side controls which head; while phogs do wear a red and blue collar, I was never able to remember which is which. The worst was grabbing things. On several occasions I was rolling the ball up a slope with one head and tried to grab it with the other. But I pressed the wrong button and the ball rolled down. After completing the tutorial, you're free to choose one of the three worlds that represent phog's desires. Each world has a small hub with six levels that must be completed in order and the main event that opens after completing all puzzles. Hubs are pretty empty at the beginning, but become more populated the more levels you complete. Moving through the world is done by going into the mouth of a giant snake creatures (two-headed) that connects the islands. These same creatures also represent the goal of each level, the only difference is that you have to somehow force it to open its mouth (by offering food or ringing a bell). Each level is split into several little islands with puzzles that need to be solved by using stretch and mostly grab buttons. You'll have to move certain items into place, push levers, ride elevators, swing across chasms and even use phog as a hose to water plants. Don't ask how that works. Throughout the levels you'll also discover residents of this world. Each thematic world has its own and except for an occasional pat on the head, they don't interact with you. They're there just to make the world more alive and take part in slice of life scenes. "Sleep" world is pretty inactive because almost everyone is asleep, but "Play" and "Food" worlds really make the whole experience more colorful and ensure you don't get bored during problem-solving.Puzzles become progressively harder, but you're almost never stuck. You also don't die if you fall off the island; you're just returned to the very generous checkpoints or right next to the spot where you fell down. This way you never lose progress after solving harder parts of the puzzle. Gameplay might get repetitive after a while, but different worlds make things interesting. For example, the "Play" world contains mini-games, like golf and pinball, or "Sleep" world where you hide in shadows while avoiding lights with wings.The game also has collectibles in the shape of bones and little strange creatures hiding in secluded places. By pressing the "start" button, you can see how many bones there are in the level and whether or not you already found the hidden creature. While some bones are visible and require out-of-the-box thinking to reach them, others are hidden behind mini-quests you have to do for residents. These are very simple, like fetching a nearby object (displayed over their heads in speech bubble), making pizza, watering the plants, etc. The only problem is that you don't always get told what you need to do. Often, it's just experimenting with the stuff you see in a level or something not connected to the puzzle solution. And you have to do these tasks right away. If you move on to the next island, you can't go back and your only option is to restart the level. You can then use these bones to buy various hats in shops. Their only purpose is to customize the look of your phogs and don't offer special abilities or something like that.The game runs fine and I didn't encounter any bugs. There were some weird situations with physics where I got stuck behind some rock or thrown into the air, but nothing a quick restart from checkpoint couldn't solve. The game's also quite long for a puzzle, especially if you want to find all those collectibles, but it's not that difficult.  Rating: 6/10Reviewed by:

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:This is a very fun game to play with another person in co-op. There's a variety of worlds and levels and for me and a friend, one complete playthrough took us about 9 hours. The puzzles are fun and do not feel like they're too challenging, nor does it feel like the objective of the puzzle is hard to understand. I would not recommend playing solo as controlling both ends of the PHOG is a little tricky.The Bad:We ran into quite a bit of bugs while playing over online co-op with items not appearing or not showing that you're holding an item.There were also other bugs with some of the physics causing us to get lodged stuck into spots and needing to respawn.The controls are also really annoying to figure out. The game works best with a controller yes, but the devs could have also at least shown what the keyboard controls were in the settings. And with both controller and keyboard, I found that the controls would tell me one thing, but when I hit the button to do something in the settings, I wouldn't work. Like many games, PHOGs starts with volume levels at the highest, and we couldn't figure out how to do turn it down from the game's settings with keyboard. We were able to select what volume we wanted to change, but no keys would work to actually turn it down.The story is also rather vague.The game is also, in my opinion, a little highly priced at $25 USD. I felt like for that price, I would have expected more in terms of available levels and overall content. I feel like the game would be more fairly priced at $15 or $20 at the highest. This doesn't detract from the gameplay, but for the price I just wish there was more.

_childDocuments_.review: Phogs is an okay game in my opinion. It wasn't exactly exciting to play but I had a decently good time playing it. The premise of the game is that you and your co-op partner are dogs with 1 body so most of the puzzles revolve around that. This doesn't leave much room for creative puzzles and they can very quickly get boring or repetitive. None of them are really that complex either. They're mostly straight forward and easily done. In the final bits of the game  and I wish they introduced that idea much sooner. They could've made it so much more interested and included better puzzles but they kept it to till the end. There's collectibles throughout the maps such as bones that you unlock different hats with. There's another collectible but I don't think it does anything. There isn't much story. It's just the dogs trying to find their dog bowl I think? But that's all there was. The graphics are cute and well done. I didn't experience many bugs besides the fact that every once in awhile I would get stuck in the ground.Overall it's an alright game but as I said it's not too exciting. I dozed off a couple times while playing lol. I say give the game a chance but definitely wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The bad - It's a cute game and I enjoyed the demo before buying the full version, but the challenges are just way too simple (basically no challenge, it's pretty much just picking up an item and carrying it to a hole to drop it in). The only real challenge is trying not to yell at your partner bc the mechanics of moving as 2 dogs combined is INCREDIBLY frustrating, if the other person chooses to extend then you get slowed down or start swinging around or just bug out and crash into things, but if you don't extend then you end up just being extremely glued to your partner and it's feels like very slow and boring to get around the maps. I also really wish they didn't make the bite button the bark button at the same time, it gets a little tiring when you're barking 24/7.The good - It is cute and it would probably be entertaining enough if you have nothing else to play and just want something very simple and... gentle (slow) to play with a friend on a lazy day.Suggestions - I like the concept and I think it could be really fun if they reduced the amount of snap that the other player has on you (constantly pulling you to them, I know we're literally attached to each other but it just feels frustrating when you end up feeling like you're just dragging the other person's butt or they're dragging yours or you're swinging in circles trying to stop dragging each other), if they fixed some bugs, and if they made the challenges a little faster paced and actually challenging (Maybe add in some working together to swing across huge chasms or something, and make the movement speed much higher).Summary - It's cute, and I know lots of other people did enjoy it, so I wish there was a "meh" option instead of just yes or no for rating it, but I just have to say no, I don't recommend it, because in the end I just thought it felt like a 2 year old's playmat. No challenge, just moving balls into holes and sliding around like a worm......

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and goofy adventure, from start to end! I really enjoyed running around the themed worlds (Sleep, Play, Food) and seeing all the strange creatures that inhabit them. The bonus collectibles were also fun to hunt - especially because they unlocked wearable hats :] The puzzles aren't very difficult to solve, with the focus mostly on cooperation and mastering the movement of both dog heads. Phogs isn't here to challenge you: it's inviting you to laugh at some wacky antics.The physics were a little quirky sometimes, but the game is very generous with level checkpoints and an option to reset in the menu if you ever get stuck. As a result, I never felt truly frustrated when things went wrong. If you don't mind a relatively short game and find the visuals charming, then I'd absolutely recommend picking up this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I am only 1/3 done with this game and will update, but so far: IT IS ABSOLUTELY ADORABLE. Until now it also seems to be very child-safe.What is it about?You play as 1 very cute dog with two heads - so, every end of the dog has a head - and have to make your way through the levels by cooperating both heads independently. I assume playing the game with a friend is intended, but it seems to be possible to play it solo as well. I play with a friend and it is great fun.Levels:Three themed worlds - Sleep, Food and Play - with several levels in each of them. In the levels you have to solve puzzles - find your way trough a labyrinth, bring a tea service to a moth, wake up the sleepy dream aliens by freeing the alarm clock, turn on the lights for the sun and other. So far, I have not encountered any combat, and the worlds are very peaceful. You walk around and do things. Difficulty: it is not very difficult - neither in logic nor in skills (like timing or such)Aesthetics: But it is SO CUTE. OH MY GOD. IT IS ADORABLE. I have only played the dream world yet and it is extraordingly calming. I listen to the dream soundtrack outside of playing the game. The sleeping sun's sighs, the woken up aliens with bags under their eyes, the distressed teddy bears, the alarm clocks running around, the reading moths and tea drinking hedgehogs - they are all so unbelievably cute in their design. The game also seems to be very child-friendly. Up until now, I think I could play it with a 5 year old and they won't have any nightmares or stressful situations. The game does not hurry you. Basically, if you are old enough to coordinate your fingers to press buttons to go where your eyes want you to, and you are old enough to understand implicated causal relationships, you are old enough to play this game. The full price of 25€ MIGHT be a bit high depending on what you want out of the game - it is in no way 'challenging', but rather aesthetically pleasing and calming or just fun to play. I assume the total game hours to be...7,8 hours maybe? But 15 € does seem fair. This game is build with love and I'd want the developers to be paid for their work, be it 25 € or 15 €. You play this game and it brings peace to your heart. Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle platformer in which two people control a two-headed dog-creature crossing surreal landscapes.PHOGS! sees you take control of either head of what I can only describe as a dog-sausage hybrid, which allows you to move around expand/retract your body to get more distance between both Phog heads and bark to raise your head or grab objects. Using these minimal abilities, you’ll have to make your way through about 20 levels spread across “Food”, “Play” and “Sleep” themed worlds.This involves some basic platforming made difficult by your wobbly physics-based movement and the cooperation required from both heads. There are also some rather basic puzzles, which once again tend to become surprisingly challenging to navigate. Most level also include some unique mechanic, for example being able to shrink or grow your heads, luring NPCs using fruits or using light to remove shadowy blockades. Together, these mechanics make for quite a varied game which stays entertaining throughout its runtime, in lieu of the basic core premise.Spread throughout the levels are various collectibles which are either hidden or require you to complete certain bonus tasks. These give some nice incentive to engage more with the levels and can be exchanged for cosmetics ranging from adorable to dorky.The game can be played alone using a single controller to move both Phogs, though I would very much recommend playing with a friend for fooling around with the physics-based gameplay alone. PHOGS! presents well-balanced challenges, though coordination is always key in order to make it through with fun instead frustration.Complementing the enjoyable gameplay is a beautiful art style paired with a nice variety in level design and some decent background music. The game oozes charm, which is highlighted by many superfluous details spread throughout it, e.g. other creatures interacting with the Phogs when they’re close by. Given the nature of the gameplay, you’ll more than likely stumble across a few glitches related to the physics. While these are noticeable and can result in certain level gimmicks being a bit janky to use, they’re easy to remedy and never really managed to impact the fun me and my friend were having.PHOGS! was a blast to play and I urge you to give it a shot – it’s a wonderful couch (or online) coop experience.
