_childDocuments_.review: Do you like playing co-op games? Do you like co-op games where the two of you are attached? Do you like co-op games where the two of you have hit the bark button so many time that the number of barks is in the thousands?This is super cute. If you play co-op less for the challenge and more to have a good time with someone close to you, this is perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: My partner and I played this game together. It's a great time! The art style is serene, calming and cute. I never found the puzzles too challenging nor was I too confused to figure out where to go. The game has a great sense of humor and makes you feel like a kid again in the best way. If you're looking for a quiet, relaxing game to play with someone, I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: My friend gifted me this game for her and I to play together, and have gone as far as to get all the achievements. It's an incredibly fun, cutesy puzzle game for all types of audiences: best friends, roommates, couples, family members, you name it! Anyone, regardless of age and gaming experience, can pick up this game and make it worthwhile! It's also super easy to run on most computers (including my absolute toaster-oven of a laptop). The only bugs I've encountered were due to internet issues, and occasionally, your body spewing everywhere and bugging out would happen - still a funny thing to laugh at, and nothing a respawn/restart can't fix. Overall, definitely worth the buy as you'll get a lot of laughs and heartwarming moments out of it!
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. the Co-op can be a little off sometimes, but the game design and art style is so nice and cosy. it's great fun to play and can be challenging at times. there's one or two glithy parts where you can get stuck in the floor and the stretch is a little off, and we've had trouble where only one of us can see the hats available, but overall I would highly recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game to play with your special one :) ( I would not recommend it for playing alone) It is not hard but also not easy, it has some surprises at the end. There are some bugs, we could not buy anything in the shop while in multiplayer because the second player could not see the items and the net code is not perfect but just provide some funny moments and not a disconnect.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: Funny, cute, co-operative experience! The level designs and visuals are great and the puzzles are on the simple side so it's perfect for when you want to relax and have a good time with a friend. I appreciate that the movement/input demands for puzzles are generous and forgiving.I would also like to thank the developers for making a demo because I would have passed on buying this game if there wasn't one.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: After writing my initial review, we figured out that just respawning often fixes bug issues, and it doesn't reset you far at all (if you ever lose progress, its like maybe 1-2 minutes tops). Makes the game really enjoyable, so I would like to recommend this game, and if you have bug issues respawn frequently! -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Previous review: Although I will still continue to play it now as I have it, I can't really recommend anyone to buy this game, even on sale. Every time I have played online coop, it is extremely buggy. It often gets worse the longer we play, which becomes a real annoyance when we are so close to clearing a level but literally can't get to the finish line because the game is bugging out so bad on us. Today it also messed up my sound somehow, making everything really robotic and strange. It might be worth it for local multiplayer, and it might be easier with someone with closer proximity (I'm quite global), but there's a definite issue with bugs in this game that really robs a lot of the enjoyment of this game. I adore the cute aesthetic and the funny sounds in the game, and the levels are always fun, but I wish that fun wasn't inhibited by the constant lag and bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: The main puzzles are pretty simple, and the gameplay is relatively limited. The fact that it's a 2-player co-op which can also be played by a single person with 1 controller is a good indicator of the simplicity of it all. It has some charm and can provide some good light-hearted fun with a friend. However, it's not going to be intellectually stimulating like a heavier puzzle game would be, and the platforming is very basic. So yes, it's a puzzle platformer, but it's not heavy hitting on the puzzles or the platforming. The challenge of hunting down all the little secrets can pass the time and force you to replay a few levels to figure them out, but mostly this is a chill game to play with a friend. Nothing transcendent here.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: What a game. Simple, cute art with basically satisfying puzzles. It's a game I'd call 'conductive'.Lemme explain what I mean by that. 'Conductive' in this context, means that something provides something extremely easy for two people to connect through. Just as metals 'conduct' electricity between two or more points, you'll find that this game is more about who you're playing with, rather than the game itself.I know for some of us, it's important that we remember that. So stay inseparable, like the Phogs :)
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: There's currently no online co-op, just remote play, which can take some of the fun away. Being on the remote play end, I found sometimes it got lower quality or lagged a bit. That said, overall was a very cute game with fun themes and an engaging end. Had a lot more content than I initially expected. Considering only one person needs to buy + the amount of content, it's a pretty worthwhile game. If you're able to play in the same physical space or don't mind remote play then 10/10 recommend
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: My 5 year old son and I play this together local coop with two Xbox controllers and we absolutely love it!! Super fun puzzle adventure that is low stress (no timers, no bad guys). All of the characters are so quirky and amusing, and my son finds it hilarious when we get all tangled or get whipped around really fast.TLDR; Relaxing and fun adventure/puzzle game to play with the kiddies (if you have two controllers, I used two Xbox ones)
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute, the puzzles are tricky but none so far are impossible. The worlds are pretty large and steam remote play works great. Great fun with a friend, tho probably ho-hum single player.Edit: Around 10 hours of play to the end, the coop is great. Highly recommended if you're looking for fun nonviolent coop! Super cute ending.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game by chance on some unknown youtube channel and as soon as I saw the footage I knew I had to buy it. I don't understand why this game isn't more known? it's honestly some of the most fun I've had for a while. It's funny, relaxing and cute. This is a really good COOP experience and I've been enjoying a lot with my girlfriend.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS SO CUTE AND IS NEARLY PERFECT IN EVERY WAY. Phogs is a puzzle platformer with an emphasis on "puzzle", yet the game feels EFFORTLESS to play. The puzzles are so well ingrained in the environment that it just feels like natural progression and exploration. The game provides at least 10 hours of gameplay and I highly recommend co-op mode. If you were to play solo, a controller would be the best fit (KBM was difficult solo). The worlds were MAGICAL and soothing. The Phogs were buggy sometimes over online co-op but like charmingly so and just quickly reload if for some reason you're stuck. Clearly so much imagination, love, and care went into this game. The art style and settings had me pogging (or should I say *phogging*) constantly. You literally cannot play Phogs without smiling. Also a very fun and easy achievement completion (I got them all within my 14 hours of play time). 10/10 HIGHLY recommend. Get it full price or on sale it is so worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: Grab your bestie cause this is the chance for you and your buddy to be connected at the hips to solve puzzles - literally. Is very cute game - would recommend for those who enjoy adorable simple co-op. The puzzles are VERY simple - but my friend and I enjoy it anyways! Gotta love the glitches in the game - nothing like flying spaghetti phoggies! Just a warning - desyncs do happen from time to time and hilarity ensues.11/10 for the adorkable confused phog emote alone.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: PHOGS! is a very wholesome and goofy 2-player puzzle-platformer that makes up for some of its online jank with funny creatures, beautiful locales, and simple-yet-rewarding problem solving with the help of your butt-buddy.You may find some sections vaguely reminiscent of games long past, such as Sonic Adventures, Sly Cooper, Super Mario Sunshine/Mario Party, to name a few. There are three worlds to explore that evolve the further you go. To not spoil anything, we all were surprised and loved when we realized what our final goals actually were at the end of these worlds. Each world has some very clever ideas and sound game design that come together to put your barking skills to the test in the final fourth world!I'm not sure if there is any intended path, but we felt that the Fruit Kingdom -> Beach -> Dream World path was a perfect build up to the end, with each world getting better and more complex.There are a couple of different kind of collectibles to encourage you to explore and think outside the box to obtain, and interact with other characters and items that don't distract you from your main quest. Getting these lets you unlock new hats which is always great. Why wouldn't you want to put a cool new hat on your good doggie?My friend and I played through it together in its entirety, and it took us about 10 hrs to complete it. I myself only got around half the achievements and didn't find all the collectibles yet. We did encounter some issues like the hat shop not showing any items for player 2, some interactable objects not entirely synced up between us, and some general physics goofiness. The movement in this game is a little floaty as well (no, it's nothing like Human: Fall Flat), but I wonder how many of these issues were just because we had a large amount of ping between us specifically (maybe 250-300 ms ping) or are just common problems for everyone. I can count on one hand the amount of times we had to force-respawn ourselves or restart the game to fix an issue. That might be a big nope for some, but it didn't sour our experience, because everything else about the game was so sweet.If you and your bestie are looking for an easy puzzle-platformer to goof around in for a couple game nights, I highly recommend. You may also like Knights & Bikes, another best-friend co-op game about exploring a quirky island that's being invaded by your childhood imagination, that one is a little more like an arcadey action game.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: Great, relaxing and funny co-op game for two players.The entire game is cute in a way that both kids and adults can enjoy.It is also rather easy so that it is definitely more for kids, those looking to relax (or just straight bad at gaming ;) ).Despite this, the level design is incredibly creative - you'll be surprised how many mechanics (usually tied to different levels) can be packed into what seems to be a very simple idea.My only real gripes (beyond the lack on Linux support) are that you cannot go back to specific parts of a level (e.g. to look for a bone) and have to do the entire level again up until the point you actually want to repeat.Also, that it is often very hard to tell where you are in relation to the level if your phogs are in the air - the shadow is just not clear enough.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only two hours in, online with a friend, but this game is adorable and a lot of fun.You don't need a controller, but it doesn't accept mouse input at all, not even on menus. WASD and space to navigate the menus.Local co-op can likewise be done with the ancient one keyboard two players system of WASD and arrow keys.If you've played Snake Pass and are expecting this to be like that, it isn't. There's no slithering and no climbing. Grab and stretch are the only control mechanics you need to worry about. And the game does a lot with those.Update: Apart from an annoying issue with the hat shop in multiplayer, I have no complaints. I love this game.It's really easy to break in harmless ways: You can abuse the physics to take contraband into or out of levels, or get to places you aren't supposed to (yet).
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: PHOGS! has become one of my favorite platformer/puzzle games. My girlfriend and I played through the game and we really had a great time playing it. There's three themed worlds, food, sleep and playing, each with their own levels full of fun puzzles to play through. The visuals, sound design and characters are all very charming. If you're looking for a fun game to play, alone or with a friend, PHOGS! is worth the price
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute, relaxing co-op game. The puzzles weren't too difficult (took a couple minutes at most to solve), and the introduction of new mechanics kept the game fresh and interesting. Music, graphics, and overall concept were well done. Only issues are the glitches and de-sync. We occasionally experienced glitches where one of us would get stuck underneath a platform. Thankfully, there's a reset button if you can't get loose. The de-sync created situations where my co-op partner saw that we could unlock new hats, but since they weren't showing up on my end, we couldn't unlock them and a few times it looked like I was doing something on his end, even though I wasn't. The Corsair iCue Integration seems to be a little bit borked (it messed with my keyboard's basic settings after leaving the game. I ended up disconnecting my keyboard and reconnecting it). I didn't try the single-player mode, so I can't comment on it. Despite these issues, I would definitely play this again.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely need to have somebody to co-op this with, but that being said the game is fun.The puzzles are clever enough and have a cute design to them. Environments are designed to reflect the specific mechanics you are using in the level. Charming aesthetics with a goofy attitude. Music is aight too. The kind of game you can play at the end of the day to just chill and have a good time with whoever you are playing with.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game, that has continued to surprise with each new level.The game only has 3 "worlds", but each one of those concept is explored SO thoroughly! I really love that approach. And each new level within those worlds has some new twist, mechanic, or fun new way of playing. I'm maybe 1/3rd of the way through, and it's been a blast!Definitely play co-op if you can. We've had some pretty odd and intense glitches playing online, but nothing game breaking so far.
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best co-op games I have played and well worth the price tag in case it was making you hesitate. For full disclosure, my boyfriend and I were able to 100% the game in about fifteen hours with a decent amount of goofing off, but we had a ton of fun (and borking) along the way. Each level has a variety of puzzles, and there's some degree of freedom in how you solve the puzzles (mostly by manipulating the physics to jump up/over a gap). We found them to strike a good balance of not difficult/frustrating but not boringly straightforward. The game does a good job of hinting at what the solution to a given puzzle is without beating you over the head with it.The level design is amazing and each level will tend to repeat a mechanic thematic to the world but have their own twists on it. Each level looks beautiful and the music/sound design makes each one unique and a blast to play through. The arcade level is my favorite because there's like 7 mini-games you can play in the level and it makes me miss going to an actual arcade as a kid. There were very few bugs we ran into while playing the game and they were mostly related to stretching. They were almost all either minor inconveniences or hilarious, and nothing a respawn couldn't fix. (Also, the respawn mechanic is pretty generous, there's frequent checkpoints if you do happen to get stuck).tl;dr: 10/10, would bork again
_childDocuments_.name: PHOGS!

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is exactly what it promises on the cover. It had me and my friend grinning and laughing constantly as we  completed its little mini-challenges that make creative use of the games mechanics. Its also really freakin cute, and there are tons of HATS and adorable interactions with the characters. Great wholesome game to play with a friend, your SO, or kids. Delivers hard on the game play promised in the promotional materials.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is in need of a bit of polish: a lot puzzles can be easily bypassed, some parts are a tad buggy (non-jumping jump platforms, I'm looking at you), the level design could be better; BUT, that doesn't stop the charm of the game from getting through, especially if you play this with another person. So, if you want a fun, if somewhat buggy, experience with a cute atmosphere, this is a game I can recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute little game. Definitely best played in co-op, but it has online support (which I haven't tested as of this review, only local play). It's a little bit janky at times (as it's physics-based) and I had a few frustrating glitches, but the generous respawns and checkpointing made it less of an issue. Overall it's a fantastically cute game in what has otherwise been an extremely dreary year. If you have someone to play it with, I really recommend it.

name: MindSeize
detailed_description: MindSeize is a single player 2D Metroidvania game set in a sci-fi universe. Explore untamed planets and stop the mysterious organization that stole the mind of your daughter. You play as the private investigator M.C. Fox , who is chasing a dangerous criminal organization ' The Ascended ' across the universe. The first confrontation between M.C. and the leader of The Ascended severely injured M.C. and left him crippled. They also managed to seize the mind of his daughter Taryn . This left only one choice for our protagonist: hire a crew, connect his consciousness into a robotic body called MAG and continue the chase! Classic 2D-action with a modern twist - Smooth and fast-paced action with beautiful hand-drawn 16-bit pixel graphics, mixed with atmospheric music and hard hitting sound effects Explore mysterious planets - Travel to 4 different and unique planets, unravel their secrets and fight the dangers within. Remember to take a break once in a while on your ship and talk with your crew Upgrade your MAG - Buy and find different mods, weapons and abilities that bring versatility to your MAG's combat capability Delve in to the world of MindSeize - Follow the story written by a professional script writer with comic book style cutscenes, read the log about planets and their fauna, experience the heart-rending twists

_childDocuments_.review: is a classic side-scrolling metroidvania set in the far future. Players impersonate Mordred Chad, a soldier that suffered permanent injury and is now bound to a wheelchair. One fateful day, mysterious entities known as The Ascended seize his daughter's mind, claiming her to be the key for the success of their experiments. After that, Mordred embarks on a great quest to find his daughter, with the aid of an advanced remotely controlled combat armor. 🟩 🟥 On the good side, the visuals of MindSeize are more than decent, even if they use a purposefully low-res style to resemble the old school games, they still manage to deliver very good environments, animations and effects - which also are consistent in quality from start to end. Level design is surely commendable, as each stage has a multitude of secret paths to uncover, hidden behind the classic "cracked walls" or in some cases difficult jumps. Exploring each level is not only interesting but also rewarding, as eventually you will rack up many potent character upgrades.Boss fights are no trivial affair, as each of them is markedly distinct from the common foes and features multiple attacks that evolve as the fight goes on, becoming more rapid, dense as the boss takes damage. The challenge of these bosses is always high and each needs a unique approach to be defeated. Combat features melee, ranged weapons and is built around precision control of your character, as well as timing of execution. Reckless moves and button mashing are often punished. The biggest issue in the core gameplay is to be found in the design of a few bosses that result very sub par and unfair, since they rely on spamming additional mobs to create challenge instead of having better design onto themselves. Balance of weapons needs to be reworked, as there is one specific ranged weapon that is better than any other for sheer damage, while some melee weapons are simply not worth using. The fact progress-critical elements are in no way highlighted and confuse with the background, can be very frustrating - as well the fact discovered obstacles' locations are not saved on your map.🎮 Gameplay is divided into Exploration, Character Management and Combat.Is performed on foot across various environments, ranging from lush forests to post-apocalyptic cities. As in any metroidvania, there is an heavy emphasis on platforming at all times, so you'll have to jump, vault and climb your way across maps, with more or less difficult platforming challenges depending on the location. Across each map there are Landing Pads and Save Points where you can save your progress, the first one is a more "complete" variant that also allows you to access the upgrade shop and fast-travel, while the second is only used to regenerate your HP and save.Finding secrets is an integral part of exploration, and they are everywhere in the forms of cracked walls, hidden buttons or difficult jumps. They often contain upgrades to your Max HP or unique passive abilities, while often plenty of Credits to purchase more upgrades with at the shop. It is almost mandatory to find at least some of these secret upgrades, as bosses further down the road will be extremely hard without them. A global map marks your progress and indicates save points or other important quest locations - though not everything important is indicated.Is done at a save point of any kind, where you can change your current ranged and melee weapons choosing among those you found so far. Some bosses or enemies will be better faced with a specific weapon, but anything goes really. The upgrade shop can be only accessed at Landing points and can be used to acquire major passive abilities, if you have the money for it. Healing charges can also be refilled for a small credits cost. Weapons however cannot be upgraded.Plays out in melee or ranged fashions depending on the situation. Melee weapons usually deal better damage but are also riskier, while ranged ones pack less punch but have a range advantage. Each weapon has a unique special ability that can be used if you have enough Energy, built up from hitting enemies. Often this attack is very powerful but has long execution times. Normal enemies are never overly challenging or numerous especially later on, while bosses are instead very though to crack and the true apex of MindSeize's combat.Using your attacks with the right timing, and also jumping, sliding and using Shadowing (become invincible for a short time, consume energy) with perfect timing are all mechanics to consider when facing a boss fight. The game is designed to punish reckless tactics and reward accurate timing. You can heal during a fight of course but unless upgraded this process results slow and limited in effect, becomes much better with the upgrades if you find them. None. Resource usage is within expected values. No issues. Runs without issues in 1440p, 85hz. No major bugs to report. Some minor bugs are present at times. None.MindSeize is a solid metroidvania that however has some flaws preventing it from being truly great. It remains a solid title for the genre that fans will appreciate thanks to an original setting and challenging combat mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Mindseize is a game I really want to love. But I can't. Here's the thing; I love hard metroidvanias. I loved Hollow Knight, Guacamelee 2 and others. But this game is just frustrating, and not in a way that feels earned or good. The biggest issues stem from the controls and combat, but there're a lot of problems with level design that make those issues pop out. Level design-wise, checkpoints and particularly fast travel points are few and far between, and often in odd places. It's really annoying in a game this backtrack heavy to have so few options for getting back to points of interest fast. Checkpoint placement is just weird sometimes, especially on the space station level, where I found myself stumbling into several minibosses/midbosses without a checkpoint in the same *timezone* as the boss, leading to frustrating runs of shame back to the boss for round 2, 3, 4.... and so on. Another issue re: backtracking in level design is that the map has annoyingly few markers and no way to mark points of interest to make up for it. This is a game that loves to, starting from the first map, put bomb/fire/shock blocks everywhere, and it's a pain to remember them for backtracks. Games like Hollow Knight and Timespinner solved this by letting you mark these points; this game instead turns it into a "ugh, better redo this whole level because I forgot where all the shock walls were." Finally, the game loves to throw low visibility environments at you throughout most of the game, and while it's atmospheric and moody and all that rot, it's just a pain to navigate, especially when there's enemies about. Eyestrain ain't good world design, and the darkness just feels like it's there to frustrate you since your fire, shock, and other attacks don't cast light, and neither does your drone.Control-wise, the game oscillates between handling alright and being a total clunkfest, but much moreso the latter. The game has the classic "only one jump height" type jump physics, which isn't a problem until you start needing to do complicated stuff like intentionally hang from a ledge to do a climb dash, and you can't because you have no way to shorthop up to the ledge without passing it. An occasion of this actually resulted in a friggin' softlock on the fungus planet, where I sat there growing more and more frustrated at being stuck in a pit with only two exits, both of which required climb dashing, and neither of which would take airdashes or let me ledge hang because all my jumps just wall stick instead. The wallstick and ledge hang play really, really badly with each other in this game. There are times, once you have the dash, shadow dash, and double jump/airdash that the game feels really good, but the often-frustrating level design really hampers any of that acrobatic enjoyment.Combat, too, is often unsatisfying and clunky. This game is often compared to Megaman X, but the difference here is that enemies take a huge amount of punishment to actually kill, making your character feel like a total wuss for most of the game. Seriously, even the saber often takes 4-5 swings to kill basic enemies in the midgame. And enemies in this game don't flinch, so often you're stuck doing slow, annoying dash in-dash out tactics to avoid getting point-blank grenaded to death. Ranged weapons tend to do mediocre damage, which also doesn't help. It's like the game wants you to rely on the "super" moves to do a lot of your damage, but energy regens so slowly that it's hard to have enough energy for that and the shadow dashes you need to be spamming to stay alive in pitched fights. So you're stuck doing piddly damage from range just to play "optimally." It's not great. To continue the MMX comparison, imagine if suddenly every enemy required you to stop the high-speed action to stand there and plink away with the weakest buster imaginable. The second gun you get is actually solid-damage wise, it should be noted, and if you stick to the default saber and it your damage is respectable enough, though enemies are still a little too tanky and a lot too damaging for how the game seems to want you to play. Something else that doesn't help the game is that it wants you to have every important attack skill available at once, so it uses a shoulder button as a sort of toggle; you have to hold it to shadow dash/jump, use weapon supers, and access your fire and shock abilities. It's not great, and it contributes to the clunky, overly complicated feel of your moveset.I do have to give credit where credit is due; the graphics are lovely, the music is atmospheric and eerie as a Metroid soundtrack, and the writing and presentation *of* said writing are well done. But this game often felt like a struggle to sit and keep playing, and more than once, I found myself thinking "Why the heck am I still playing this? Am I really still playing this?" And so on. The game has good ideas, and there's fun to be had here every now and then. But it's bogged down by bad decisions, clunky controls, combat that wants to be like Megaman Zero but doesn't really get how to make it work, and fails at elements of level design and quality of life that have become more and more commonplace in metroidvanias.TL;DR: The game is frustrating. Controls overcomplicated. Bad checkpoint placement and QOL. Combat feels clunky and weak. Tiring to play.

_childDocuments_.review: is a great game so far for what it offers. It does have a lot of reminiscent elements with metroidvanias of old. I really liked playing it, but there wasn’t much need to customize for given situations as I’d have liked. The laboratory map was a bit weird and disproportionate too for me, so it made certain areas tough to figure out how to get into, without careful investigation.I would have liked to see more crazy abilities, but what was offered was pretty useful as far as the automatic and passive stuff. Some was not quite as necessary as others. Some balance could be employed on some fights. Some were extremely difficult, and some were easy to avoid all or most damage without a ton of skill. I prefer it too easy, rather than too hard though. Also, lots of small glitches, as it’s very new out of the gates. The development is great in putting together some constant fixes and patches to make it run better as more is offered up. Super NES vibes, very reminiscent of Samus-style Super Metroid. Super Metroid is a better overall game - perhaps I am biased. It still has some setting and feeling and music that reminds me of this genre/era of gamingFairly easy to play with controller. Good responsiveness with movement. I had problems with button function a few times and would get “stuck” here and there, leading to deaths.Story is pretty decent for a shorter game. I say short, but I still got around 15 hours out of the game total.  Developer was very passionate about learning about bugs and trying to emply fixes at a steady rate.  More than I can say for most. Always glad to find one that has integrity, and isn’t just selling “half-assed” products on Steam, doing as little work as possible just for sales.Lots of things needing fixes along the way. From invincible enemies, to ledges that are hard to hop onto while hanging, to falling through surfaces after getting hit, to getting stuck with no abilities to leave areas when I went there before I was supposed to - also some sequence breaking made me wonder if I missed something a couple of times. Hell, armed with my map, I love exploring!Games like this are always hard to remember what abilities later do what for things passed, so that can be an issue. So, it is difficult to find everything without a detailed guide.No need to change weapons really for the most part. When you got an upgraded version, the older ones were obsolete for the most part, unfortunately.The sequence-breaking factor messed with me, as mentioned. I had a few odd occurances due to this.  Making some routes impossible or less viable than they were to the explorer like myself would help this.I wish the map had more detail on which map areas had what on them. If a door was impassable before I got certain abilities, it’d be nice to have them color-coded or something to that effect, for instance.While it’s a bit short for the price, it’s still a nice addition to anyone who is a fan of metroidvania games. I feel it could go a bit further, but it’s a nice ode and tribute to the past. Recommended highly, even now! It should only get better in time.Special thanks to  for their support!

_childDocuments_.review: The map in this game is beyond atrocious. Having giant blocks for one area is just awful, look at how other metroidvanias use the block style map. In Sotn for example you know the staircase area just by looking at the map because of the way its shaped. In this everything is just a huge block with sometimes some elevators in between. The entire map system needs scrapping and total rework. Make each area have a distinct shape not just huge square blocks. This would make moving thru the levels so much more intuitive and make the map actually helpful. The combat could also use some reworking. Why give me a downward jump thrust if i'am going to just take damage when i land on the enemy? That move is totally useless. Why are some of the enemies so tiny? Why are the projectiles so tiny? I have no answers and all i can guess is maybe this is the first game by this studio.The art, story and music are all quite good but man that map just totally makes this game a total chore. I noticed it almost right out the gate and thought maybe after going to the next planet it would get better.     It did not.I made it to the 4th planet and by then i was just done. You have no idea where you are going, where maybe that cool thing you saw earlier is hidden among the endless squares. I may come back to this if they completely scrap the map and rework it to a proper map. Until then i doubt i will ever play this again.

_childDocuments_.review: is a new 2D metroidvania that has recently been available on Steam. It features a interesting story with a good amount of background lore, a decent set of interesting enemies, a variety of bosses, and a progressive series of upgrades that allows for backtracking and further exploration.Despite its appearances and claims though, the game's fairly linear and not wide open like other metroidvania games. There are certain sequences that you must go through to progress the story and to reach new heights, often literally, so that you can move to the next section of the game. (Difficulty setting added for an easier mode.)You have both melee and ranged weapons for your action sequences and you will see a lot of combat amid your attempt to explore. As many such games go, enemies respawn upon reentering a room, save select enemies and bosses, such that it becomes difficult often to try to move around quickly. Sometimes this may be welcome so that you can collect enough currency to then purchase the next upgrade available, but a lot of times I find the repetitions a bit tedious and unnecessary. With more discovery of newer movement abilities, this becomes less of a nuisance. And sometimes it feels good to find a new and better way to deal with a particular type of enemy so that you can get better at moving through their ranks without suffering damage.The bosses are hard in this game, There are some glitches in the game as well-- (Some have been fixed, though others remain.) While not major mostly, such as getting your character to be stuck in a particular type of terrain shape or to accidentally pushed between floor levels for not good reason, a simple reset (hopefully your last visit to the save point wasn't too long ago) takes care of it. But I had an issue with my buttons all of a sudden becoming unresponsive on my controller mid-level or sometimes while fighting a boss, especially the latter was a serious detriment to enjoyment. There are a decent amount of upgrades to your character throughout the game, and a good number of weapon choices, to somewhat tailor the game to you as you play. The upgrades are often crucial for progression, but also allows you to discover some secret areas that can make you feel pretty smug about yourself. I do think that this game could use some touching up, some improvements such as  glitch and bug repairs.  There is a demo available, so at least you can try that out.Controller and Keyboard control layouts. Game had issues with some input with the DS4 controller, but the XBox1 controller seems to work fine. Controller definitely recommended.Retro-style 2D pixel art that works well with this type of game.Soundtrack is pretty nice, the sound effects work well.With the newly introduced difficulty settings, I think any platforming metroidvania fan can potentially enjoy this game.For what someone can get out of this game, if this is what you are looking for, then it's worth it. On the fence? Try the demo first.+Good variety of combat with progressive upgrades+Tying things together with a story and the lore+Good artwork+Fitting and nice soundtrack+Plenty of things to discover+Decent variety of regular enemies, and the bosses are well-designed+You can pet the dog- (Easier difficulty setting added.)-Hefty log of glitches that I personally encountered in 9+ hours, I imagine most other players have seen similar issues. (Some glitches still remain.)-Can only switch weapon loadouts at save points. Why not allow switching at will?-Your game might freeze if you pet the dog (Did for me once, my character sprite disappeared from the screen. Had to force quit.)>The progression of the story and bottlenecks designed to be in place makes the game progress more linear than open and exploratory in a lot of places. Once you are able to explore more, the remainder of the zones after initial exploration is fairly small in comparison. is a pretty accomplished indie game. There's no doubt that it will make it to someone's top indie lists because of its many strong points. [/strike]For me, I can see where the game has value, but I also experience the personal frustrations at being completely unable to progress because I am just not good enough. I might come back to this game in the future to see about improvements, but I will have to put it down for something else at this time.[/strike] (With available easier difficulty, I am able to enjoy the game better now. I am glad that the developers have modified the game to make it more enjoyable for the players.)(Updated score 7.5/10 for the improved difficulty settings to make it more enjoyable for more audience members, for continued work to fix glitches, and for attentive and receptive developer of this fairly large undertaking in an indie project. Currently waiting for controls to be fixed to be able to play again. PS4 Controller--Shadow Dash doesn't work, XB1 controller--both triggers seem to only do the Shadow Dash, normal Dash not available.)

_childDocuments_.review: It might not be the Metroidvania you still dream about 15 years from now, but MindSeize grew on me the more I played it. The world is large and offers a lot to explore, there are diverse enemy types and unique bosses, a motivating upgrade system for your character - the basics of a satisfying representative of the genre are here. The most important thing are the controls, and they are old-school but as tight as they should be. The sci-fi story centers around a father trying to save his daughter (or better - her mind) and take revenge for his own crippledness. With a remote controlled robot, he fights his way through the ranks of the evil organization that seized his daughter's mind, visiting 4 planets on the way.The game is broken in ultrawidescreen, but works fine with FullHD or 4K. Retro-styled graphics like on a Sega Megadrive, an above average story, an easy mode (for people like me), perfect gamepad support and developers that put their heart behind the game (and fixed a ton of minor inconveniences during the last weeks) let me wholeheartedly recommend this game to all fans of Metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: MindSeize

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to lie, this game has its flaws. Some of the boss battles are not very imaginative, they rely on cheap punches/shots. Also the map system leaves a lot to be desired. But I loved this game. It quenched my thirst for exploration and adventure and I couldn't stop playing until I've finished it and unlocked all its achievements. There's plenty secrets to be found and powers to unlock.It has a simple sci-fi story about a private investigator whose daughters mind has been seized (hence the title) by the evil robot organization called The Ascended. He's been left crippled after the confrontation, but his crew connects his consciousness into MAG body and now he's back on track to rescue his daughters mind and end The Ascended once and for all. There are some comic book style cutscenes, but personaly I liked the pixel art of the game more. I also liked the soundtrack.Overall this game was a fun experinence for me and that's why I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: MindSeize

_childDocuments_.review: A very well executed hommage to the metroidvania games of the 90ies era.Music and art style are awesome and the upgrade system is motivating.The resolution, especially of the texts, is a little to blocky for my taste and there are a few minor problems with controls in the menues. Jumping and shooting is old-school and you need a few minutes to get used to it. Even the smaller enemies in the beginning have quite the amount of health and different attack patterns you need to remember, so it's more of a tactical approach than simple run and gun.I had some major issues with the ledge-grabbing system and had to try some platforming sections dozends of times until I finally understood how it's supposed to work and that the game wants you to practise those to get the controls right. Once I got the hang of it, I could manage those sections every time.Despite some minor issues, it's definitely one of the best of its class.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid Sci-fi metroidvania, with a few problems, the main one being it's very hard to figure out where to go after each item/boss, so if you hate not knowing where to go next, this is not the game for you, I still liked the overall level design, just wish their was a bit more direction to it, occasional hit detection issues are a pain, especially with boss's, in general an okay game, just doesn't really impress much.

_childDocuments_.review: Back in March, I was desperately looking for a Metroidvania game on Steam as I wanted something both to enjoy casually and to learn to speedrun. I found MindSeize and decided to give it a chance, and I could not have made a better decision.The game starts you off slow, introducing you to the mechanics, and then almost immediately it opens you up to multiple paths, giving you a surprisingly number of places to explore right off the bat. At first, I found that generally the game was guiding me towards getting a certain ability or doing a certain thing before being able to make progress elsewhere, and then later it definitely feels like there are multiple things you can do out of order, whether it's finding extra abilities, acquiring new optional weapons, or doing one of many different things needed in order to progress with the main storyline.In a nutshell, the game consists of Metroidvania-like exploration and fun, creative boss battles, and I enjoyed the heck out of all of it. I even found myself discovering developer-intended shortcuts allowing me to go through areas just a little bit faster, skip some hazards, enter a room via a different door, etc. Although the bosses at times felt difficult, they never really felt unfair, as there was always room for me to improve.Back in March there were a few bugs I discovered casually, one or two of them game-breaking, but the developers have been extremely hard at work to fix any of these and they have been nothing but supportive and understanding in fixing things. They have a Discord server and have been really down-to-earth, having conversations with me about why various things might be happening, why something has to remain as it is, etc, and it's a real pleasure to keep returning there to participate in their--for now, small--community.On a separate note, I took the time to create a speedrun route for this game and I've been enjoying speedrunning it so much that I wanted to add auto-splitting to LiveSplit so that I could track my times accurately, as well as allow others who want to speedrun the game to do the same. The developers have actually worked so hard on this with me and have gone as far as to add new data to the game and even modify the way things work in order to enable me to make auto-splitting work properly.Conclusion:I very highly recommend this game if you enjoy the 2D Metroid games, Axiom Verge, Hollow Knight, etc. The game is getting better all the time and the developers have fixed so many bugs since I started playing less than a month ago.In its current state, I would give this game an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sat on my wishlist for years while I decided if I wanted to get it. The other reviews for it where mixed at best, citing all manner of bugs and overall game play issues. Well: there was a sale, I wasn't interested in most of the other games on my wishlist right now, and MindSeize was one of the cheapest games on my list, so I decided to give it a try. Is it good?...it has its moments. I didn't find any glaring bugs at least. That's the kind thing to say. It's essentially a Mega Man Zero fan-game. You collect the standard assortment of movement and path-opening abilities that are common to most Metroid-style games, but most of the things this game does are almost a 1:1 copy of Mega Man Zero. Mega Man Zero asked this question: "How far can the Mega Man formula be stretched across a semi-open-world map and not be broken?" Rather than spawn at the start of a purely linear level and move mostly from left to right to get to a clearly-marked boss room, players had to navigate to different points in a single map to complete different objectives and fight different bosses. This game does have different maps, but that's basically what this game does, on a larger scale.MMZ had a dual weapon system. Zero used both a buster (gun) and his Z-Saber, and later gets two other weapons. This game gives the player a choice of one gun and one melee weapon, with the selection slowly expanding throughout the game. The first two MMZ games had level-grinding for skills. This game just gives you an in-game currency to buy those things.They even have a sequence towards the end where your ship gets attacked and there's a boss you have to fight. You get what is basically Leviathan's spear just in time to go to a planet of "water" and ice. One of the skins you can get for your drone is an off-brand version of Zero's helmet. Those things are straight out of MMZ.That may sound fine if you liked the MMZ games, but I haven't talked about the problems. To break it down:-The game defaults to using the arrow keys for controlling the player character. Unfortunately, with arrow keys active, the player character constantly ran left at the start of the game. This caused him to run straight off the cliff you start on and kill himself. I initially thought I was still watching an opening cutscene until the game respawned the main character back on the ledge and I held the right arrow to stop him from running off the edge again. I thought this might just be an issue with my main keyboard, so I tried a different one, but the same thing happened. I tried switching the direction keys to wasd and back. Same problem. So right at the start I'm switching from arrow keys to wasd and remapping all the other keys to go with it (I went with: JKL; for jump, dash, melee, and heal, UI for diagonal aim and ranged, Q for specials, H for grenades, and C for drone control. It sort of worked for me). Not a great start.-Next, on the very first map, I was herded straight to an optional fight, with no indication that it *was* an optional fight, or that the actual correct path to take involves heading back in the direction I came from. I eventually looked it up in the Steam discussions. I am not the first person to have this problem. On the second map, I did absolutely everything I could find to do, and had to look up a YouTube playthrough to find the one spot I hadn't been to. I'm not asking for giant neon signs (I'm pretty observant and well-versed in the typical ways game devs lead players along), but the game's most open maps hide where you're supposed to go just a *bit* too well. -Most of the save and fast travel locations are in weird places that make you do a lot of backtracking for no good reason. -I often lost boss fights over and over again, not from lack of skill or because I couldn't figure out the bosses patterns, but because of bad controls. Another thing worth noting is that if you get hit by a bosses' attack after you kill it, you'll have to redo the whole fight. That happened a lot more often than it should have. Also, the "tentacle fish" boss had me wishing pain on the developers. I'm not sure how they play tested the game and thought it was okay to subject people to *that* fight, with *these* clunky controls. -They claimed they didn't add downward aiming as balance thing, but require players to cheese every enemy possible to avoid taking at least one hit of damage per enemy, and the levels offer just enough places where downward aiming would be helpful to make it a QoL thing to be able to do it. But they also said they lost their animator in the same explanation, and *that* was the actual reason. Pick a reason. It was a stupid decision either way.-Healing is limited, and it is never enough to properly compensate for the hits enemies all but force players to take.-There's a hacking mechanic in the game where you hold down a button to switch to controlling a drone, then navigate to objects or enemies with a little icon over them that shows that they are hackable, and then they get disabled. That's just fine outside of a boss fight, but multiple boss fights implement this mechanic. That brought me to an obvious realization which I'm surprised the devs didn't consider: moving the drone to hack things adds *nothing* to the experience. You can't even move the drone to hack something unless you're near enough to the thing in question to do it. Players should just be able to hold down the hack button to hack something when they're near enough to something to hack it. Maybe flash a "circle of influence" around the drone if the player isn't close enough to anything hackable and they press the button for it.Nitpicks:-English is not the native language of the devs. If I were paid an hours' wages, I could fix all the issues with the games' dialogue and lore. That's how little time it would've taken. Yet they didn't get anybody to edit the text in the game. -I saw a review of this game on YouTube where the reviewer said the music is amazing. It is not. It is passable. I'm not going to look back on this game and think, "I'm really glad I played this game because of such-and-such track that I wouldn't have heard if I hadn't played it." So do I recommend this game? Not unless you've already exhausted all the other Mega Man or Metroid-like games you've already heard of.

_childDocuments_.review: this game kinda sucksthe premise was really cool and i dig the artstyle in a lot of waysbut jesus christ is it unfair. it seems to be gong for the souls like approach but instead of being hard because it's hard, it's just obtusei was determined to finish it because i was past the point of a refund and decided that i'd at least get my money's worthbut almost every single death left me wondering what i had done wrong. it was never clear why i died, the bosses were just absurd. the only way i beat any of them was sheer dumb luck and cheese strats. i tried turning it down to easy mode but that seemed to change dying in 4 hits for dying in 5 hits rather than anything at all usefuladditionally, lag, animation errors, and the game just deciding it didn't want to register my inputs more and more as the game progressed made me rage quitthat was the point i realised i couldn't recommend this game in the state it is in and that is a shame because i enjoyed the premise and visuals. it's just not fun to play

_childDocuments_.review: Started off somewhat strong, particularly the first two worlds.At first glance, it's a non-linear type of exploration metroidvania, but it is very linear. You progress from one area to the next typically and can't do bosses out of order. In fact, if you're where a boss should be, it just won't spawn.I had a lot of fun with the game in the few few hours, until I got to a point on the 2nd world I ran around for literally 2-3 hours not knowing where to go and have explored every speck of the map. Until I realized the elevator I took was broken and the game wanted me to go down the elevator from the top again... and some monster that sends boxes across the map spawns only after this event. After that, I was super frustrated and just rushed through the game, but even then finding every secret wasn't hard after you find a certain upgrade, which I got because I was at a loss where to go and got every secret possible. While the mechanics of the metroidvania was interesting - i.e. cut scene triggers or specific event triggers cause stuff to spawn in other parts of the same map without much indicator can be very frustrating if you don't figure it out.The platforming was clunky and combine with the giant hitboxes made platforming and combat a pain in the ass. The boss design started out ok. Then I don't know, the bosses started getting lamer in my eyes. I started winning on the first try often.I don't know what the other reviewers are talking about though how bosses use cheap tricks? I didn't see any cheap tricks. In fact, the player can employ some cheap tricks... I thought I could have some fun getting the boss rush achievement at least, until it randomly rewarded me the achievement when I was practicing the bosses one by one by optimization time efficient strategies. Got all of them nailed down and then went to the last one. First clear on the last boss in practice mode, I was rewarded the achievement. Pff. Now all that practice gone to waste and I didn't even need to earn the achievement.Most bosses in the game, it's actually better to face tank everything and do maximum dps. Because you have heals, you have some error. I was able to find all the optimum facetank max dps strategies in practice boss rush mode.Final words. ♥♥♥♥ linear metroidvania, ♥♥♥♥ platforming, bad combat, bad game design with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ elevator I wasted so many hours and it was so unintuitive.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★☆☆(3½ stars if half-stars were possible - it's a good metroidvania platformer)============Review:If you've played metroidvania games before, you know the drill. You explore areas, beat bosses, get new parts and moves and revisit old areas with the new stuff to unlock more stuff.. yeah there's a lot of backtracking if you want to collect everything.I really like the art style of the game, it's very well made pixel art with good animations.The sounds do their job just fine, and the music is generally quite good. It didn't get annoying at any point of the game which is a plus in my book.============Ok so the technical side is good, what about the gameplay itself?It's a quite typical metroidvania - the controls aren't as crisp as in some other platformers of recent years, but other than some fairly early wall jumping sections I didn't have much problems.Honestly I think the game is sort of a slow starter - it's worst at the very beginning (usually many games are better early and get worse), but it gets better later.Early game is kind of clunky, especially the wall jumping part. But once you get them double jumps and dashes and stuff it gets way better and very enjoyable to play in my opinion.The story is pretty meh, but I didn't really mind. Games like these don't need awesome stories anyway.One thing I disliked was that the game doesn't mark stuff on your map - like if there was a specific thing blocking your path before and you saw an item behind, it doesn't mark that. You just have to remember it yourself. The game does give you tools to find the items later, but it was a bit frustrating early game.They nailed the game's difficulty in my opinion - it's not too easy but it's not hard either. Generally I had to try each boss a few of times before beating them - which is kind of optimal in my opinion.And the game's length is very good in my opinion - it's not too short but it doesn't drag on forever either so you can play it even if you have little gaming time.============Overall, I think MindSeize is a good game. If you want something fairly short and light to play, MindSeize does that job nicely. Apart from the clunky start, it is a enjoyble metroidvania game.Technically I could have given it a four star rating - I think after you get past the clunky start it is a four star game - but I did take the poor start into consideration and dropped the rating accordingly.It's definitely worth it if you can get it cheap - so get it from a sale when you can.============Summary:The Good 👍+ Good pixel art+ Well balanced difficulty+ Good game lengthThe Bad 👎- Clunky early game- Would be nicer if the game marked items on map
_childDocuments_.name: MindSeize

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like Early Access title.First things first, why I recommend it? Because gameplay loop feels real nice, with smooth animations, nice mobility and very satisfying combat (for metroidvania).But, there is a lot of buts:- Many bugs, like getting stuck in terrain, invincible enemies, music stopping, etc.- Visuals are subjective, but I didn't like everything except actual gameplay art. Looks like cheap deviantart.- Pretty short, took me about 7-8 hours for 96% on first playthrough. Maps 1-2 seems huge, but 3-4-5 are tiny in comparisson.- No indicators on the map except savepoints, so you gotta memorize all the spots for future upgrade use. I have a bad memory for these things and I don't want to comb through all levels for that 100%. Although secret beeper upgrade is real nice.- Lots of annoying stuff on big maps, like loops for the sake of loops. You finally find flamethrower, you go back a couple of levels to find some secret but no, it's just a corridor that loops around to a room I found hours ago.- Story is bland and fizzles out quickly.- Unskippable credits with hundreds of backers, nice.Overall pretty solid game, but in the end feels too small. Good for sale price.
_childDocuments_.name: MindSeize

_childDocuments_.review: **Since this review, devs have fixed some bugs I mentiond and added some features that address my complaints.  Plz check the game's update news**So much potential.  Game still seems to need some work, but thankfully the devs are still actively involved.Pros- Strong metroidvania elements.  Tho it's not a single large sprawing map.  But rather, smaller worlds.  However, each map is heavy in MV (or at least the first one was).- Music is really good.  Great at some parts.- Story starts off fairly straight forward, but also interesting enough to see where it goes.  Lots of effort in the history and lore of the game w/ a deep index of characters/enemies.- I really like the graphics style, the sorta high "32-bit" pixel sprites all look really nice.- Devs are continuously supporting the game.  Cons- Still lots of bugs.  Can get stuck while walking up a diagonal platform.  I had a massive screen glitching on first boss.  UI doesn't reflect changes to keybindings.  After beating the final boss at the end of the first map, went to the central hub, checked the travel computer, hit cancel to back out, and a **GAMEBREAKING BUG** caused game to softlock, making me to have to restart over from my previous save right before a boss (there is no autosave after maps and apparently not saving at the central hub).  After re-beating the boss and given the option to stay on the map (in order to save) or go to the central hub, selecting the stay on map option did nothing.  I was forced to go to the central hub...  So, go to central hub, try to re-create the bug again and...did.  Game softlocked again after accessing the travel computer w/o me ever saving my progress.- There is no autosave after maps and apparently no saving at the central hub.  **Repeated intentionally**- Ledge/wall grabbing feels so inconsistent.  The mechanic is you have to hold forward while jumping in order to ledge/wall grab, but it still seems to not always work.  I think b/c you need a hard confirm that you grabbed, which is frustrating for a faster-paced MV like this.  - Inconsistently designed enemies.  Some are just ranged bullet sponges you shoot for 10 seconds.  Other are easy 1 melee hit kills.  It's like the game wants to be a fast-paced action MV, but then at times you're sitting there just standing still for 10 seconds shooting things.- Combat is unsatisfying and stiff.  Game doesn't know its identity as a shooting MV or a melee MV.  Constantly doing both attacks sounds fun in theory, but isn't in practice.  Especially given the design of some enemies.  Melee and shooting are both stiff and somewhat slow, no dash/jump cancelling out of animation.  Forgivable in general, but not for a more faster-paced MV like this.  This is just my preference.  I think the game tries to do too much w/ both melee and shooting, while making neither feel really significant. Neutral- This is just a preference thing, but I do not like the platforming at all.  The hard confirms into grabbing ledges/walls breaks the flow of platforming for me.  Also, Jump is what pulls you up from ledges, but down/duck is what makes you fall.  Doesn't feel right.  Defintely not intuitive.  Up button should bring you up, if down drops you down.  And I greatly prefer auto-grab for ledges.  But again, this is just my preferences.  Devs maybe have their own preference or vision in mind for the game.This game has a lot of potential.  I can get over the platforming mechanics/inputs.  I can even get over the lack of combat identity the game seems to have.  But the bugs...losing my save progress...can't recommend this game right now.  Mostly b/c I don't even feel I can play it.  Not if I risk losing my progress due to the softlocking.  Thankfully the devs are active.  I'll probably continue at a later date.

_childDocuments_.review: If you find this review to be helpful, my curators page is here: As a parent your worst nightmare has come true. That moment you hoped would never happen, and yet here you are: a group of cyber-evolutionary-terrorists have stolen your beloved daughters brain!!And to make rescuing her brain even more difficult, you are in a wheelchair. Under normal circumstances this need not be a problem, but when there's an army of killer robots between you and rescuing her, well, you need a helping hand. Or, more specifically, a helping...uh...leg, or two, for extra mobility.Which is where plonking you in a mechanised assault suit comes into effect. Now you can walk, run, slide, tap-dance, jump, double-jump, and wall-jump with the best of them, and you''ll need to if you're going to have any chance of rescuing your daughters brain. Except for the tap-dancing, you won't actually have to do that. What follows is a metroid-vania, with more of the metroid and less of the vania. There is a modest level of upgrading to abilities that you have, but this aspect isn't particularly deep or make much of a difference overall to how you play. The main emphasis is on combat and platforming, with a modest element of exploration, and it's as an action title that it succeeds.Basic combat is relatively simple. You have a melee and ranged weapon, and whilst you find extra weapons as the game goes on, you can only take one of each into battle. There's  a small melee combo, a vertical strike, a jumping downward strike, and then you have power moves for both types. Sliding exists to avoid obstacles, and you can wall-jump, as well as cling to walls.The fighting and shooting may not be the most expansive of this kind of game, but it is fluid, responsive, challenging and enjoyable. Varied enemy types, and ways in which they attack, keep you on your toes, and the difficulty is pretty well judged. Bosses are either impressive in scale, or tricky to face, or both, and generally have nicely worked out attack patterns.It's pretty decent graphically, with colourful, well animated sprites, and extra oomph added from particle effects and lighting. Sound effects are all quite chunky, with fairly stirring music. Story-wise it's passable stuff, but speaking bluntly: the writing won't win any awards for being quality dialogue. Having said that: cut-scenes aren't very lengthy, or hard to follow, and can be skipped.When all is said and done, the level of execution is high, and there's a lot of fun to be had from it. Could it be better executed or more spectacular? I think it could be, yet off of the top of my head I can't really think of a shooty metroid-vania that's significantly better. As a run-and-gunner, Blazing Chrome is tighter on the action, and a smidge more intense, but it's also kind of bite-sized in it's approach. Mindseize is a meatier experience, with somewhat more depth due to being non-linear in it's level design, and being able to backtrack with new abilities to access boosts and upgrades for your character. These boosts don't necessarily change how you play, but the overall difficulty is high enough that they are worth finding. It's nothing revolutionary, and there's games that maybe do it's elements better (Iconoclasts as an example), yet taken as a whole, with it's excellent boss-battles, it's well worth checking out.For reviews of other titles in this genre, and more, my curators page is here:

_childDocuments_.review: An ambitious but ultimately unremarkable and deeply flawed metroidvania. Somewhere in this mess bloated by kickstarter backing and delusions of grandeur is an okay video game and a rather nice book, but they mesh with absolutely no congruity and it's clear that by the end the devs were out of ideas and probably money as well. Map design is amateurish and powerups are metered out seeming at random meaning there is no feeling of progression or structure. Enemies fire tracking projectiles that pierce through walls, bosses move erratically with high damage spikes, there's a completely unnecessary currency system that just serves to add tedium when restoring health packs, the problems are all far from backbreaking but together they just create a game that has nothing to recommend it. The writing and worldbuilding was given entirely too much focus by the devs compared to the gameplay, and yet what writing there is comes across as rushed and lopsided. Someone watched Firefly one too many times while writing this game and forgot that there's a reason why Samus is usually alone.I can applaud the devs for trying to make something that's more elaborate than "super metroid but you have a sword" but unless you are absolutely jonesing for metroidvanias and scraping the absolute bottom of the barrel, you can give this a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I am EXTREMELY glad I didn't pay attention to the negative reviews and tried this game for myself instead. When I game it a first run I will admit that I started and stopped immediately because I thought the somewhat stiff movements were signs of an indie game from a team that's still learning...I'm also guilty of judging the quality of the game based on the artwork used in the opening cutscenes and technically that's not only petty, it's unfair. I was DEAD wrong about this game. First off I had to wipe Axiom Verge 1 & 2 and AM2R off my plate and forget the control and move set I was used to and most metroidvanias play it safe because they may lose persons who can't let go of Metroid or the Castlevania games...look, LET THOSE GAMES GO and try other things. MIND SEIZE is one of the easiest Metroidvanias to get a fully 101% completion during your first run through, this isn't due to the developers being afraid to give the player a challenge it's because the team that made this game CLEARLY knew that as soon as you get the hang of how it's played you're going to reward yourself with the exploration side of things. Here's one of the main critiques I read in negative reviews...MOBILITY, but what I've found is every upgrade you collect makes the game more familiar to long time fans of the genre then all of a sudden you instinctively collect everything without a guide or faq. There is absolutely no way this game was this good/simple because I'm skilled but I haven't realized it as yet lol.THE GAME REQUIRES PATIENCE in the beginning not because it's bad and you have to let it grow on you, it's like that because the moment you start collecting UPGRADES for the MAG suit I kid you not, you will be ZIPPING all over the dam map. The Story May be it's weakest area, there a beginning, middle and a coherent end, there were tons of great themes and philosophical ideas that could have happened (Think Deus Ex Human Revolution) so I think that was a missed opportunity, at one point there's a . But it was at least satisfying and to the point.As far as a rank is concerned, I'd say its like a 7 because I think with more time and money there are somethings on the cutting room floor they wanted to add but couldn't. The weapons you collect and movement upgrades shows are sure signs of player preference and fighting style they wanted to add more complexity to but couldn't so I'd like to see that in a sequel. I had a weapon load out of choice not because one weapon was better than the next, it was based on how I wanted to play the game.Play the game, stick around, it's not a hard as a Soulslike, but you will die a few times and it's not a run and gun, you have to consider your enemies before you fight and you have bars to manage, those upgrade frequently as well.P.S. You're gonna find the sprite bits on the main ship charming and you're gonna wish the game had a few other populated hubs on other planets for the main character to wheel around in, explore and talk to more npc's.  You'll see,,,

_childDocuments_.review: I truly hate this game.Let me start of with the good things about this game. The metroidvania elements are done well, when you land on a new planet you usually can explore multiple directions and you can do something regardless where you go. The items and powerups are hidden well and the game often gives you ways to obtain items early through backdoors. The abilities and powerups you find are interesting and varied. I also like the general enemy design however their placement is often annoying as the game loves to put annoying enemies between the checkpoint and the boss. The general movement, the platforming and the puzzles are all acceptable. The backtracking is kept to a minimum with a lot of well placed teleporters, this could have been a really good game.So why do i hate this game?First of all it has way too many bugs and there is a huge missmatch of abilities and general design and almost all the bosses are poorly designed.Lets start with the bugs, at least 5 of the bosses can glitch out and often times leave you softlocked which is especially terrible if it happens to you in the bossrush. Bosses that can glitch out are: Illuminator: If you hit the boss during the wrong time when he comes down he can glitch out and move off the screen leaving you softlocked.Duke Atlas: The boss sometimes disappears in the transition to phase 2, the game usually hands you the win if it happens but not always. Also after getting grabbed you sometimes cannot move after landing.Thyr: Sometimes he is invincible at the start of the fight, usually hitting him with grenades gets him out of it.Assassin: If you juke him too much he starts moonwalking, if he teleports during a moonwalk he sometimes teleports to nowhere and you are softlocked.Mimir: I got softlocked once on Mimir as well, he was dead but the doors didn't open thus softlocking me.Valkyrie: If you kill him in the wrong spot, the killing animation can glitch out leaving you softlocked.Bad boss designs:The Duo: Problem is the Attack the Lancer does once he gets to half HP, i spent over an hour trying to figure out why it would randomly kill me and i couldn't so eventually i started to just jump off the platform to get i-frames to not die to it. I still don't know what you are actually supposed to do?Parasite: I suspect the Boss only exists for the Laser weapon to be useful, just plain awful design. Raining random enemies on the player and basically forcing wait time for the Parasite to spawn in a favourable location is just not fun.Drifter Hanu: Just awful design again, why is he invulnerable during most of stage 1? Stage 2 is a nightmare unless you just kill him before he moves at all which makes stage 2 really just a knowledge check.Sea Monster: You really just need to get lucky with tentacle spawns as there are no safe-zones if you get unlucky. Feels extremly cheap and unfair.And the worst Boss in probably any game i have ever played: MIMIRMy goodness, i wish i could know what went on in the designers head when they made this boss, i really do. This boss requires you to know what he does at every point, if you don't you will just lose. There are a lot of hitboxes that make no sense and in the wrong spots on this fight, when and where the fists hurt you is just trial and error. The only reliable way to kill him in the bossrush is to pace your damage, get him to half hp and then burst him down from half by sequence breaking him. If you damage him too fast you will get overwhelmed as he can spawn 4 waves at once, if you aren't sequence breaking him the fight takes forever and you will likely get whittled down.Missmatch of abilities and design:The game wants you to be fast and agile, swing with your sword and dash in and back out basically you are supposed to be a ninja but you really can't play that way. I eventually ended up mostly playing ranged for the entire game, jump around the bosses while slowly killing them with my gun. The reason is just that every melee attack is a huge commitment, you can't cancel your attacks and once you swing you are a sitting duck. The only ability that gets canceled that you never wanna cancel is your heal... Also almost all of the bosses spam projectiles and your dash doesn't have any iframes, only if you spend energy and don't forget about using it can you negate attacks. It is just not feasible.Most of the weapons in this game feel bad, for the majority of the game the only gun worth using is the stranger pistol. The rocket launcher has some uses but the base gun and the laser are mostly worthless baring some very specific situations. I feel the same way about most melee weapons. The base sword feels best for most of the game, i do realize that the quad cutters can deal insane amounts of damage but they are very unsafe to use. The huge sword is too slow to be useful, however the finisher is quite strong on some bosses. The spear comes to late but is good for sea monster and that is about it i think.In conclusion it could be a good game if the combat/bosses weren't so bad.
