_childDocuments_.review: I love metroidvanias. Super Metroid and Metroid Fusion, not to mention indies such as Hollow Knight and Iconoclasts, are some of my favourite games ever. For years, I've made it my personal goal to play at least the most interesting ones in the genre. Thus I was super excited about MindSeize when it was announced on Kickstarter. I played the alpha demo and generally liked it despite the bugs and problems I had with the movement. Of course, the game has come a long way since then, and after finishing the game, I'm glad that it lived up to my expectations.The premise of MindSeize is quite simple. Player controls M.C. who is using a robotic body to hunt the villains who stole his daughter's mind and also crippled him during the same incident. M.C. is travelling with a bunch of other people, trying to take down the organization called the Ascended. I'm not going to spoil anything here, but I found the story descent enough without it ever taking the focus of the game. However, I think MindSeize shines brightest during gameplay.The most important part about any metroidvania is world design and the inclusion of different power-ups that gradually open the world. This is where MindSeize shines, as each of the four planets in the game are huge maps filled with secrets. What really surprised me was the amount of variety in them. For example, in Verdant Gamma, the player starts in the mountains, descends to the jungle and plains, and finally goes through a complex cave system filled with enemies. So each of the planets are divided into multiple sections, forming a convincing world. Each of the planets offer quite different experiences, as they have different obstacles and different enemies. Nonetheless, each of them are quite open, even though the first planet might seem a bit linear during the first minutes. Keep on playing, it gets better as it goes!MindSeize has a ton of different upgrades, ranging from different melee and ranged weapons to new movement abilities or improvements to the drone accompanying M.C. New attacks and upgrades can also be bought with the scrap collected from enemies. As is often the case in metroidvanias, new abilities unlock new areas in each of the planets. This generates a really engaging gameplay loop that I've always liked. In MindSeize there are also lots of shortcuts and secrets to uncover, which could lead to some interesting speedruns in the future. Who knows, maybe this game will be the next hit in the speedrunning community? I sure hope so.The combat of MindSeize feels like a mix of Castlevania and Super Metroid, not too far from from something like Dead Cells or Axiom Verge either. You have both melee attacks and ranged attacks, and you get multiple different weapons to choose from later in the game. Using dash and jumping around is necessary to avoid enemy attacks, as battles are quite fast-paced. Especially melee combos are satisfying to use, as the hits have just right amount of power behind them. What makes these battles more interesting is the inclusion of different special attacks. Each weapon has their own, powerful special attack that use energy, and you get some other energy-consuming equipment to your arsenal too as you progress. Nano bots are used for healing, but you can only carry a few of them at the same time. Similar to Hollow Knight, healing is a risk, as it takes a small eternity. However, this is only a positive thing, as it adds some strategy to the challenging boss battles. Finding a moment's rest to heal is easier said than done.I think the pixel art in this game is definitely worth mentioning. The backgrounds look beautiful and the tiles have just enough detail while still maintaining that low-res style that should please anyone with a sense of nostalgia towards retro games. However, I think parts of the visuals are a bit incoherent. During story segments, the detailed character portraits stick like a sore thumb from the pixelated backgrounds, even though the art itself is fine. The choice of font might also divide opinions. It's easy enough to read, but looks weirdly low-resolution considering how big it is on screen.Reading some of these Steam reviews gives a good idea on the biggest issue currently on MindSeize. Yes, it has quite a good collection of bugs in it. Some of these are completely harmless, while some of them might produce small softlocks or make the character get stuck on the ground without any apparent reason. However, the developers have given their best to fix every single bug that has been reported. One day I reported a bug and found that they fixed it in just a matter of hours through a patch. Now that's dedication! It's also worth mentioning that the game has already gotten a couple of patches that have fixed the most pressing issues. I have faith that the developers will continue to push forward and make this game even better in the future.As a conclusion, I really enjoyed MindSeize. It has been really enjoyable game with fantastic world design, entertaining upgrades and challenging boss fights. The biggest problems with the game are some bugs and balance issues, but they'll surely be taken care of soon enough. For anyone looking for a new metroidvania to play, don't look further. MindSeize is definitely worth every penny, but at this point, you should expect to encounter some glitches during the journey.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a good game, that slowly starts to fall apart in the later stages. The first world was amazing, with my only complaint being that the game coaxes you in the opposite direction of progress after the elevator. The optional boss was also a bit frustrating, since I didn't figure out that I could kill his drone to prevent him from healing. The second world was, for the most part, fantastic. Again, I only really had one complaint, and that was that the endboss of the area didn't show up until his fight, unlike the endbosses of the other areas. The 3rd world was just as great as the last one, but I had a few more complaints than the first 2. First, the section where you descended to the planet itself was rather frustrating, since the boss there was difficult with my Current upgrades, and you can't leave until you've completed the quest. Secondly, the first boss you fight on the station seemed like there should have been dialogue, but they just showed up and died. And the Heavy Assult mech boss felt unfair, with attacks often hitting me without any chance to dodge them from my current position. Also, it was a bit unclear where I should go next at several points, requiring a lot of map-checking, which considering that the map isn't the best, wasn't too fun.The scene between the 3rd and 4th worlds was great. Best scene in the game, but I can't really talk about it because of spoilers. Needless to say, its fantastic.The 4th world is where most of my problems come up, and it seems like the game could have used a little more time in the oven. The 4th world is very linear and straight, with only 1 Deviation for an optional boss. This is fine for the first area, as its supposed to be a bit of time for quiet reflection on the game (Though there are just a tad too many enemies to make that really work), but the final headquarters was just so bland and linear it left me disappointed. And the final boss feels very rushed, with a very cliche First phase fakeout. But even in the second phase she just spams the same attack over and over, save for a couple Bullet hell segments. I might have had too many upgrades for her to be actually difficult, but she just felt so boring. The game certainly needs some more work, and from what I've seen, the developers agree with me. I'd say that the final area needs a full makeover, and a couple of the bosses could use a bit more love. Other than that, the game is great, and I had a lot of fun with it. The soundtrack is amazing save for one track (I felt that Thyr's theme was just a little too similar to the Ascended theme), the worlds look gorgeous, the Characters that do have fleshing out are well written and unique. The plot was overall great, but a few characters just seemed a little unfinished, like the developers didn't have time to program in a conclusion for them. Thyr just disappears, the hermit stays in one spot past the first world, and Shiva just doesn't have enough time to shine.Overall, its a great game that just needs some more work on the end, and on the whole was a joy to play, despite a couple rough edges. I'm excited what they will do in the future, and Definitely going to keep an eye on Kamina Dimension for their next game.

The developers at Kamina Dimension have managed to put out a very solid and worthy entry to the genre...and truth be told, the game actually  like it was made by fellow gamers that grew up loving the 16-bit era of video games. _childDocuments_.review: Mindseize is a solid 8/10 game, but has some notable weaknesses that hold it back from being an unconditional recommend. The art direction and animation is probably the game's strongest aspect, not to mention what attracted me to the game in the first place. The music and gameplay are solid, enjoyable but not outstanding in any particular way. The writing is the game's weakest point. Most of the dialogue is written in a stilted, awkward way, and the story is pretty cliche overall without much unique/novel to offer. It takes a stab at exploring transhumanism, but only at a surface-level understanding of the ideas without a whole lot to say about the subject. Let's be real though. You don't remember Super Metroid for its deep and touching story. You remember it because you had fun exploring an alien planet, powering up over the course of your journey and fighting crazy bosses along the way. Critiquing a self-proclaimed metroidvania, one that hews close to the genre's roots, for a weak story feels a bit disingenuous. It's got kickass pixel art and solid gameplay. That should be good enough for a lot of people who got recommended Mindseize after playing similar games.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this project on Kickstarter and the devs have really delivered pretty close to the announced deadline … what a welcome surprise and professionalism! At least half of the game projects I backed, going as far back as 2013, still haven't seen the light of day and/or will probably never be released :PSo kudos for that, and after having played MindSeize for about 90 minutes, I can really reccomend it! Nice pixel art, large and varied maps and so far, I've collected two new moves that allow me to explore further and I completed two boss battles. My only complaint so far is that having to fire diagonally using a button feels counter-intuitive, especially if you shoot up by pressing up+fire :P Also, I really hate the "hornet"-type enemies, but we wouldn't want the game to be too easy, right? :DThe devs have already released a big patch pretty much right after release, so I hope they'll keep on supporting the game in such a professional way and hope game will be the success it deserved to be!

_childDocuments_.review: Update 2: Pretty much all the issues I had were fixed in patches. The devs are doing a great job, and I'm now about 10 hours in and the game is still superb.Update: Still loving it! And the devs have released another patch fixing more stuff.You can tell a lot of care went into this game. It's like a love letter to Super Metroid, but adds elements of its own as well, including sword attacks (in addition to shooting, and both are useful in different situations), and buying/crafting upgrades (in addition to finding other upgrades in the world). The world is non-linear but you won't be able to get everywhere until you get the various abilities. The amount of choices about where or how far to go, while not getting so far off the path to the next upgrade, seems just right so far, as does the amount of stuff you can see but not reach yet.I've only played the start of the game, which only came out yesterday, but since it's great so far and doesn't have many reviews yet, I thought it deserved a boost. I love the metroidvania genre, but don't love every game in it. This is one of the great ones, based on what I've seen so far. Exploration and ability gating seem well done. Pixel-art graphics are great. You can do a bunch of different moves, even early on, but the controls aren't overly complex or confusing. The sound and music fit in perfectly with the 16-bit/SNES-era graphics.I did run into some bugs, which other reviews have touched on. I still highly recommend the game. The developer has already released one update (edit: now two, a day later), fixing several reported issues less than a day after release, and is working on more fixes. I reported a couple of issues I noticed and they were friendly and responsive, and you can tell they care about this game (I've been following its progress for a while now).Obviously, if you don't like 2D metroidvanias and hated Super Metroid then this game is not going to change your mind, and I don't know why you'd even be here. But if you like the genre, then I don't think you'll be disappointed spending your money and time on this gem.

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Overall Gameplay:The first hour or two of gameplay felt a little slow, as is common with other metroidvania titles where your character starts out with limited equipment/move set. However, the game quickly builds pace as you acquire upgrades, and the bosses/NPCs also become progressively more difficult in a way that remains challenging but achievable. Overall I think the difficulty scales well, provided you take the time to go back, explore, and use your newly acquired equipment to access rooms in previous areas to find additional upgrades. Some of the later bosses would be quite difficult if you're going quickly and not looking for more advanced upgrades.Music:REALLY enjoyed the OST with this. Fit the atmosphere splendidly. Highly recommend you consider buying the OST with the game. "Iron Will" - the factory track - is my favourite piece, though all the music is fantastic. Story:The story paced itself well. I tend to prefer metroidvanias that minimize dialogue and friendly NPCs in order to:1. Provide a smoother, more immersive exploration experience, and2. Make you more reliant on finding upgrades/exploring without NPCs providing scripted adviceThat said, MindSeize's characters did not insert themselves in a way that took away from immersion. I appreciated the story for what it was and how it provided a purposeful metanarrative and explained the universe's context. Also, as someone who likes to find all the upgrades and achieve 100% completion,  Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a decent challenge, great soundtrack, and satisfying upgrades. Found myself saying, "Oh, nice!" upon getting some of the mid to late-level equipment upgrades - MindSeize kept the exploration and upgrade process really enjoyable, and the boss fights were also fun to figure out. At just under $12 (for game + OST/artbook) during the summer sale, MindSeize was absolutely worth it. Thanks for a great game, Kamina Dimension!

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Mindseize is a bit rough around the edges, but makes up for it with engaging combat, dynamic bosses, and a unique world that pulls inspiration from Super Metroid.  It ends a bit abruptly, but offers a fun 10-15 experience that metroidvania fans are likely to enjoy.What's Good:-I love the pixel art.  The character designs are excellent and full of detail.  All of the worlds are unique and brimming w/ different colors and textures. -The boss fights are awesome.  They range from giant mech-like enemies that take up most of the screen to invisible ninjas that attack w/ cat like speed.  It's a lot of fun, and there are plenty of them.-The combat and progression are some of the highlights of Mindseize.  Once you discover some unique guns and melee weapons, you start to feel really powerful.  There are also a whole bunch of powerups to discover which range from double jumps, health upgrades, enhanced dash, etc.  -Tons of powerups to explore.  There are well over 25-30 powerups to either find or purchase which really incentivizes players to explore every area thoroughly.-Gives a solid 12+ hr gaming experience.  I actually hit about 15, but I tend to take my time more than the average player.  I was really happy w/ the game length and never felt burnt out.Could Use a Few Changes:-Movement and combat never feels as fluid as top tier metroidvania's.  It takes some getting used to and can feel a bit clunky.-Big difficulty spikes can be pretty frustrating.  There are some clear pacing issues.-Big drop off in worlds 4 and 5 in overall world design.  I read somewhere that the devs ran out of time/resources near the end of the game and had to make big cuts to world 5 which is a bummer.  I really loved world 1-3, hated 4, and felt like 5 had the potential but left a lot to be desired.-I ran into a few bugs.  The devs have done a great job cleaning up this game since launch, but it still isn't perfect, so keep that in mind.  Nothing was game breaking and they didn't happen that frequently at least.Thoughts:-Mindseize does a lot of things right.  I found the first few hours a bit slow, but really enjoyed most of the rest of my 15 hr experience.  This is a good choice for those that have already played the big guns of the genre and are looking for something new to tackle.  It's unfortunate that the final act isn't as engaging as the rest of the game, but even w/ that shortcoming, this is still a worthy challenge for fans of the genre.Consensus:-Middle of the Road Game (Tier 4 and makes up 25% of my reviews).  I love metroidvania's and Mindseize is another fun option for those itching for a game to sink their teeth into.  It takes a lot of inspiration from Super Metroid and Mega Man X, so those that grew up playing those gems, will likely feel right at home here.  Pick it up when on sale and don't look back.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:The visuals look cool and the game-play "feel" is satisfying to me, especially wrt melee attacks. Different enemy types, especially bosses, encourage the player to diversify tactics and use everything at one's disposal. So far I've really enjoyed meeting the different characters and getting to know what they're about as the story unfolds. Level design is particularly impressive, and I thought it was an interesting choice in terms of representation to have the main character be in a wheelchair.Negatives:Some minor bugs, mostly with UI; haven't run into anything that would hinder my progress. If you don't have a controller to play with, you'll probably want to remap the default key bindings to something more natural and instinctive.Your Mileage May Vary:The boss fights are very challenging, and, at times, bullet-hell-esque. If you're a f'n scrub like me, you'll spend hours on each boss, but if you're already very familiar with the genre and/or looking for a challenge, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Review Update: 1st May 2020At the time of this update, the game is in a good place. Map and controls work well. Combat feels a bit stiff but perfectly serviceable. Movement and traversal feels fluid. Huge amounts of bugs have been fixed and the developer continues to impress with their dedication to a polished product. Achievements have been added, including one for 100% collection rate which is perfect for a completionist and map creator like myself. Definitely recommend in this current state.Original Review: 22nd February 2020Let's get this out of the way: at the time of writing the game is buggy. Really buggy. Controls randomly stop responding, there are softlocks in various key places, and the map doesn't always display properly. I had a weird issue where upgrades I'd bought for my MAG were also unlocked for a separate playfile, and the map showed up for that fresh file too.That being said, the actual game is a lot of fun when it works. The map is impressive, the upgrades are well worth seeking out, and the fights offer just the right kind of challenge. Once the bugs get fixed, this will be a good metroidvania experience. As it is, it's still in the better half of the genre right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignored the bad review comments to give this game a shot, and wholly regretted it. Everything about this game is full of jank. The movement is clunky, and while functional at the start of the game, become a battle to fight against once the enemies and bosses start opening up new angles of attack. It honestly feels like you're piloting Robocop against Armored Core bosses, and you will die a lot without learning anything new about their attack patterns, just the bitter growing dissatisfaction in your choice of game.The thing is, boss battles look like they could have been fun to fight, which is a pity because half the time you'll be trying to even get within range of the boss to deal damage. Switch to a ranged weapon? The thing feels like a BB gun shooting a string of pathetic 1 point hits. And the diagonal aim requires pressing 2 different buttons (not even counting the normal movement buttons mind you), which is frankly absurd. In the world 1 monkey end boss fight, just getting into position to shoot it diagonally is a chore, and it's probably gone by the time you get there. This could have been mitigated by a halfway decent healing system, but healing takes too long to apply and too long to regenerate over time for it to be viable in a boss fight.The game kinda *works*, but with the proliferation of excellent metroidvanias at good prices, simply *working* just doesn't cut it anymore. There are far better games to spend your time and money on.
_childDocuments_.name: MindSeize

_childDocuments_.review: The review scores are certainly a little low for this game. We have a really solid Super Metroid clone here that probably launched in a rough state and starts a little slow, but steadily builds momentum over the course of an entertaining if familiar 12-15 hours. The dialogue is tropey and clumsy, the cutscene art style a bit amateurish, and the bestiary cannot keep up with the ever-more-powerful Player Character during the second half of the game -- but everything else is a good time. The upgrades are a highlight: plentiful, meaningful, sometimes even inventive. The pixel art is good and the music sets a mood. I like most of the bosses. Mindseize ultimately falls short of the classics, but it's a strong genre piece and real showcase of aesthetics and mechanical character progression. Recommended for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: I am editing my recommendation on this game, based on the support I am receiving and the demonstrated history of supporting this game with almost-daily or -weekly patches.The good: this is a Metroidvania that has a very similar smell to Ghost 1.0. This is very high praise. While it does not thus far seem as brutally-calculating as the also-excellent Axiom Verge, it controls and plays very well.I'm only on the second planet, about 25% complete, but there are some curious things happening here. I hope the story-arc fleshes out some of the trans-human questions and constructs: Ghost 1.0 did an excellent job of this. I fear that the story-arc will end with an obvious, "and now you're going to fight ... YOUR DAUGHTER," but this is par for the course and not really this game's fault if it comes to pass.Controls are very tight; this game feels a bit like The Messenger in places where you just flow through rooms. The wall-jump mechanics are spot-on, and jumping lands you pretty much where you would imagine it should. Again, high praise as many games get these items totally and completely wrong.Hopefully (my) crashing issue gets resolved!Original Review: Game crashes to desktop with plenty of computing resources available.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game but it joins the majority of other let downs that come through Steam. The platforming in this game is just atrocious. The upgrades you get could have been easily just been a double jump that would have been the correct move in this type of game. The thing that really just made me despise this game is fighting The Stranger. I know exactly what he does yet no matter how much I hit him he just heals through it even when using the power up when he gets low...I ended up saying screw it and killed the leader of the area to see if I got anything that would help with the fight. _childDocuments_.review: First impression after playing for a little bit over an hour: MindSeize seems to be exactly what I had hoped for. Atmospheric Metroidvania-fun with a good gameplay-feel and lots of secrets behind walls :) I see a couple of people running into bugs - that's unfortunate, but the devs seem to be on it already. I personally didn't encounter any and the overall impression of the game is anything but buggy. So I wouldn't let that discourage me from giving this game a go. Defeated two bosses already and have a blast exploring the planet and finding out where to go next. The pixelart is beautiful, btw.And there seems to be more story here than most games like this have to offer. Can't really comment on this yet, though.If there's anything I'd wish for, it's some way to tell what percentage of the map I've uncovered. But who knows: Just now I found some kind of radar that hints towards nearby upgrades. So maybe there will eventually be an item that gives you more details for the map.I really like how you don't get spoonfed all of the game's options and secrets. This can be quite demanding, but also very rewarding if you take your time. Hope there's a lot more to discover - once I've done so I'll surely update this review. Until then, all I can say to the action-platforming- and most of all the Super Metroid/Metroid Fusion-fans out there:Go for it! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Do NOT buy this, not matter what the positive reviews are saying.The dev is hopelessly overburdened with this game, it has the most atrocious controls of any metroidvania I ever played, which are also glitching out quite regularly. Especially in boss fights, wich are either cheap or boring. I bought this game for 9 bucks and I'd still refund it on the spot if I could. The game tries desperately to emulate too many games at once, but changes how certain aspects are handled from respective games to the worst possible combination I have seen. It ends up being a clusterf*ck of bad design choices with dumb mechanics and frustrating controls which are in itself the entire difficulty of the game. And I f*cking mean it. No, this is not "Hollow Knight, git gud!" kind of tight platforming or the likes, it is more along the lines "why the f*ck is this ledge all of a sudden so hard to grasp when your character clings onto everything else by himself, no problem?"The way certain things are handles are just mindboggingly stupid, e.g. how certain projectiles have a certain quality, while the samey projectiles from another enemy do not. Or blind drops, you know? Not once do I recall anyone saying "yeah, blind drops, this game has it, awesome!", and for a reason. Just one of the many mechanics that are utter sh*t, yet entirely avoidable.The platforming is inconsistent and again, the only difficulty here is the bad controls which are so f*cking infuriating, they belong to "getting over it" and not in a metroidvania.The dev at least goes to the motions of "listening to feedback", or at least so they keep saying, but there is no excuse for the state this game is. None. Graphic glitches, a death loop where FPS keep tanking to sub 20 fps levels for no reason (while the hardware of my PC registered no high demand from the game or any other software), etc. just to top off an experience that could easily be pretty good. Gameplay influencing glitches are in here as well. Getting glue-stuck to enemies, taking randomly double damage, hits not registering although your enemy is clearly within your melee animation graphic, your drone glitching out and getting stuck, mid bossfight, etc. If you collect really unnecessary and infuriating/gamebreaking glitches, this, however IS for you. What the dev apparently is not willing to fix is the utterly broken POS that is the core gameplay, along with its mechanics. Calling this game metroidvania is more a technicality than anything else at this point. I have played better games of this genre, when it was still young and devs had virtually no concrete idea what works and what not, but the way this game handles A LOT of the core mechanics is just... this game would have been utter dogsh*t on SNES, or any other platform for that matter, 20 years ago, and it is today. There is a reason some things are handled by most games of a genre the same or similar, it's called "standards" and this game has none, it is all over the place. And I had this on my wishlist for a long time, so if THIS constitutes a largely finished and polished product, I suggest the devs get their head out of their *ss and start looking why other metroidvanias are actually considered good games by a few more people than this. Sadly, similar to the rogue-like genre, metroidvania has become so mainstreamed and oversaturated, that no matter how utter sh*t a game is, you'll find enough people that'll still love it, because they crave something new. This game isn't it. The game HAS vision, and certainly good aspects, I am not trying to deny that, they are just too little, too few, and too inconsequential to offset the huge, steaming pile of horsesh*t the core gameplay is. Like the melee system. Boy, first I thought it was really amazing, only to find out that a huge majority of bosses essentially have to be beaten "mega man style" unless you want to drag them out for ages, for no reason. What good is something if you are supposed not to use it in most instances?Another thing is, that you can review almost any upgrade or action you have acquired. Except, weapons. WTF!? If you want to know what a weapon can do as special atk and how much dmg it deals with different atks (yeah, for some reason, different melee atks deal different dmg, even base atks), they are the only thing you have to equip, find a mob, and hit it/use your special to see what they do. How does that even make remotely sense? Maybe you should have spent your time more on doing something useful, instead of writing an enemy log for *every* f*cking creature in the game. Like, you know, fixing your ridiculous amount of glitches. If you want metroidvania, play something else. Anything, really, there'll be not a lot which control worse, I can almost guarantee you that.As somebody with friends who are indie devs and somebody who knows people that are developing games, from one-man productions, to little studios, I can only say: Everyone I know who develops games for a living would be ashamed to ship a game in this state. Until the core gameplay changes drastically in terms of cleanliness, accuracy and the majority of the glitches and bugs are sorted out, I can't and won't recommend this game to anyone, even for half price off. If you absolutely HAVE to see for yourself how atrocious this game is, wait at the very least for -75%, and even that I wouldn't recommend.I hate nothing more to be hard on an indie dev, but this game is horrible for no reason other than you made sh*tty design choices, just so you can pretend the game is different which somehow translates to it being good. It isn't. It *could* be. But it isn't. Why you would release a game that requires precision and has such abhorrent, garbage hitboxes, hitreg, glitches and inconsistency in its controls is beyond me.Also dev: Writes a litany with a bunch of BS excuses and then later changes it to "cheers!". So you just not only are bad at making games, but literally owning your mistakes too. Why am I not surprised at all. Cheers to you mate!

_childDocuments_.review: This game scratched an itch that some other really good MV games have not reached: the mega man element. At first this game feels 100% metroid but as it opens up the mega man elements really come out. There are some rough edges, like having to replay complete boss dialogues on subsequent attempts, but overall this has been one of the most enjoyable MV games I've played this year.  I had heard it came out buggy but as of now (Dec 2020), it ran really smoothly for me on a fairly basic laptop.There is also this great lean into exploration as the game gives very little guidance so a lot of the time I ended up checking the map for unfinished room walls and poking around. That visual cue proved to be enough to get me to the right places without endless hours of wandering hitting walls. I only checked online once for clues which did turn out to me just being impatient.If you liked mega man and need a good sci fi delve, I feel like this is a good bet.

_childDocuments_.review: Add this game to your collection.  I purchased recently and didn't experience any of the glitches I saw mentioned months ago.  When they say old school, they mean it.  This game reminds me of Genesis classics like X-men clone wars, so you really can't compare it to Hollow Knight, it's not meant to be the same type of experience.  Your character is highly mobile and the controls are awesome.  The enemy characters are unforgiving and sometimes cheap, but this is the challenge right?  I've changed my play style a few times as the difficulty increased.  Each new weapons had advantages and drawbacks.  The powerups are plentiful, though rarely easy to reach.  If you like the vibe of this game and appreciate great pixel art then do yourself the favor and get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the 1st planet, Verdant Gamma, bought all available upgrades. Just started on planet #2. This is a very enjoyable game! Is it still a little rough around the edges? Yes, but by and large it works and it's fun. My only gripe is the MAG's goofy crossfit pull-up on ledges. It flings itself up and forward slightly and on skinny platforms I've watched it launch itself up and over into a pit. I'm talking specifically about the hanging chains area underneath the crashed ship, for reference. Maybe it's some twitch of my hand on the controller? I don't know. The melee and gun play are good and the boss fights I've done have been fair in that Mega Man way. I really enjoyed figuring out the strategies to beat them. On one pistol slinging boss in particular, the game really clicked together for me and it was a very satisfying mollywhomping I dished out. The graphics are unique, I can't say I've played anything that really reminds me of MindSeize. The environments are unique and the enemies fit their setting. The story at first seems a little melodramatic, but it's caught my interest and I am excited to find out more. It's a more traditional way of telling a story in-game, and since I've been playing a lot of games full of cryptic lore it's nice to just be told a story. For me, MindSeize has been a good change of pace from all the dark fantasy Metroidvanias and Souls-like games I've been playing. That's it from me, back to exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks great and the sound is awesome, but as a metroidvania fan there were simply too many things that, on first impression, this game got wrong. Maybe they resolve, but honestly it's too frustrating to give it a few more hours of play just to find out. The map in this game is just boxes, which wouldn't be that big of an offense save for the fact that the maps and intuitiveness of progress are designed poorly. Very cumbersome and awkward. It is almost like it tries to get that "open world" feel but really just stumbles and makes it awkward instead. For as awkward and out of the way the progress is, you can't even mark your map with markers which would be a huge help. Just squares and relying purely on photographic memory while you progress endlessly through annoying enemies that damage unfairly. The second point is combat. It is so clunky and choppy it is a shame for such a beautiful looking game. It takes a while to get used to the awkward button arrangements, and certain mechanics make it just overall awkward to fight melee, even though that's where your damage is. Moves feel heavy and choppy, and your ability to heal is extremely limited. When you combine these two things, it makes this game a real grind and that's unfortunate.

_childDocuments_.review: Ho boy does this game have some issues... The 2nd planet is soooooo ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dark, most times I had no idea I could jump up through the ceiling to another room because it was so dark that the ceilings nearly blended in with the black void-space where the ceiling is missing and these were areas of just normal progression not like secret areas! BAD! VERY bad!     The jumps in this game? I would have more luck standing on a pogo stick blindfolded, doing a backflip and landing on a balance beam. The jumps in this game are just absolutely disgusting. Seriously. They went so overboard on some of the difficulty of the jumps it's absurd. It makes me actually hate the game and start to feel like I'm just pushing through it. Combine that with, the nearest I can figure, input lag and it makes for an experience that takes the game from Metroidvania to Ragegame. Maybe it's different on KB I don't know; it's selectively lagged though. Analog stick directions seem fine, but button presses are definitely lagged behind (maybe I need to turn on vsync... still don't see howdirectional presses would be ok though as all input should be lagged then, not just button presses). I also just ran into a glitch (that pushed me over the edge to write this review) whereby I literally kept swinging at these robots (2nd planet -- after the elevator falls and I have to find a way back up) and the animation clearly showed me as swiping RIGHT THROUGH them but no damage was registered on them, yet the enemies hit me just fine. I must've swiped at them 30 times or more (just out of disbelief). There were two of them, and BOTH acted that way... ♥♥♥♥ me.... stay away from this game until it gets some updates lol

_childDocuments_.review: Normally when playing a game like this: If the controls are buggy it's something I'm willing to over look. Although when I swing my melee weapon and I slide in the direction I'm facing slightly I drop the game immediately. There are other ways to make a game frustratingly challenging. This is the first (and probably only) game I'm making an exception for because so far everything else about it is pretty [explative] cool! So far I'm enjoying it, Haven't finished it yet. I'd put it on par with Blasphemous or Axiom Verge. The story's premise makes sense and the atmosphere is great. What really changed my mind and had me willing to put up with the earlier gripes is the music. Great job to whoever made that!Don't even know what happens at the end but a sequel is merited

_childDocuments_.review: Review 3. Fittingly 3 months after initial release.the controls are still weird. They are buggy too. The first half hour only the dpad worked and the analog was dead. It started working after I got my first pickup (which displayed a hint box that I could only dismiss by clicking the right mouse button)The difficulty ranges between git gud and punishing. The jump and run and exploration scenes are ok. pixel perfect jumps and good timing are required.Where it falls apart is the boss fights. The are not ashamed to stunlock you, take huge amounts of damage and have multiple phases. However each following phase is far more punishing than the last and they don't get interesting, just more of the same. Sometimes there are save spots right in front of the boss. Sometimes they are placed so you miss them and have to replay a large chunk of the map because checkpoints are so casual.Surprise! The first few patches rolled in and they fixed a few of my gripes. Why do developers think its a good a idea to rush things out the door a few days early?Health packs can no longer be cheesed and I haven't had a ledge quit on me yet. So far so goodYet by their own admission there is still content missing (like a boss fight) which makes it early access.1. review belowwait for the first few patches- overhangs and ledges regularly become non-grabable- either buy health packs for (a small amount of) coins... just die and enjoy a free refill- a lot of expo text with a noticeable amount of typoseven if all of those re fixed, I can already hear every second review rant about the weird/bad control scheme (x=fire, up+x=fire up, x+lb=diagonal fire)even if you accept that the weird scheme somehow works you end up with a weird combination of too much expo text about the backstory and not enough clue about whats going on in your immediate surroundings. If the bugs were fixed, I wouldn't be as salty about the rest

_childDocuments_.review: MindSeize - A "Wanna be Metroid"-gameSpoiler: "Something ain't right with this one..."The designers of MindSeize really seem to strive to recreate the classic Metroid of old but in my opinion they have failed. Hard.So much to get through, and I barely played 30 minutes... barely.======== Enemies =======Lets start with enemies because... why not?Many of the archtypes of enemies you see in a regular Metroidvania are there. Wallcrawlers, fliers, jumpers, big slow hunks.The ones I encountered in the first half hour proved too easy and too difficult at the same time. They resulted in no deaths but this inconsistency is prevalent in enemy design.My problem with the enemies stem from the way they break the Metroidvania-mold. - Note: Breaking the mold is not bad if you do it well, MindSeize doesn't.A good enemy in this genre will clearly choreograph that it's going to do something, enemy timings are rarely random and neither are movement patterns for the indicated action.Good enemies are by design built to be watched, understood and countered so mastering the game becomes an enjoyable experience and not an exercise in futility.In MindSeize this is not the case.The choreography is unclear and inconsistent across most of the enemies you encounter (except maybe the wallcrawlers though that's not saying much).Attack timings are weird and inconsistent.Enemies fail to adhere to the movement rule-set they communicate (I'm looking at you "alien hornets").****** SPOILER AHEAD ******The one "miniboss" you get to fight this early on is even worse but for a different reason.At one point an alien rhino chases you which sets you up a for a miniboss fight.The rhino is an unbeatable enemy, of course, and chases you through a standard platformer-style chase with pillar obstacles that get destroyed behind you and everything. Dandy!You would imagine that this is a setup for epic miniboss fight with said rhino right? WRONG. You get to fight a hornets nest... Yepp, a hornets nest.Oh and what does the alien rhino do?It sticks around to block you from getting out and randomly throws dirt at you too keep you from just killing "the boss" by holding 2 buttons. Why does it do this? Why doesn't it just charge you and kill you like it was doing a few seconds ago? This not explained. Smells like stinky stinky designer cheese to me.After you kill the epic (not) alien beehive the rhino simply disappears... At this point I'm baffled.WHY AM I DOING ANY OF THIS?WHY A HORNETS NEST!?Surely this whole ridiculous scenario could work though, if only it was imagined and presented with some humour yes?Nope, not single comedic bounce, not single quip or funny sound.It's "You'd find more cheer at a graveyard"-serious.****** SPOILER OVER ******======== Screen space =======Next on the list. Screen space.As of October 2020 66% of steam players run a 1080p screen setup (Source: Steam Hardware Survey).I'm one of those players.On my 1080p screen the player character takes up a wooping large part of the screen's height.Much larger than I've seen in most other platformers.Other parts of the game are of course balanced against this which means you as a player end up with this cramped feeling, even in outdoor areas. Like you can't see. You can pan the camera around a little bit but it still feels like the camera is stuck too close to the player at all times.Here there's also definite lack of camera work to help provide a better experience.Ori and the Blind Forest is an excellent counter-comparison for usage of camera control to deliver the desired feelings while not cramping the player's style too much.======= Player control =======My main gripe though is player movement. Spoiler: It feels feels clunky and mechanical.Let me give you an example.The "jump" button makes your character go up and then down and from a technical perspective it looks like he's jumping.The issue is that it doesn't feel like a jump.I'm not sure why, maybe it's animation timing or the mechanical attributes of the jump or something else.Whatever the reason it doesn't feel as satisfying and responsive as any good platformer should.It's hard for me to get more concrete than "It doesn't feel right" but it really doesn't feel right.This clunky movement is a big minus for game with such a lackluster story and is what ultimately made me quit just shy of the 30 minute mark.======= Story =======Speaking of the story... there's not much to say cause there's not much of it this early on.The intro to the story did nothing to entice me into learning more and the whole thing is really abruptly pushed on you.The problems of the protagonist are heaped on you within a cut-scene with a manuscript no longer than this review.There is no sense of storytelling and world-building before you are introduced to a host of characters all of which seem, on the surface at least, extremely stereotypical and dull.After the really short introduction the protagonist is dropped on an alien world to rescue his daughter from the evil "Ascended".This is where you get to start playing, let loose on a world you have little knowledge of and where only your wits will save you. EXACTLY LIKE THE START OF SUPER METROID.Except, of course, in Super Metroid you have at this point already had the backstory explained, played through a level that forces you to learn the basic controls and you even had to fight your first boss. COOL!Super Metroid for the SNES that is... Not MindSeize.====== Verdict ======I love the Metroidvania-genre. For me to stop playing MindSeize and refunding after 30 minutes says more than the fact I arsed myself to take 2-3 hours to write this stupid review.MindSeize has some good concepts and the possibilty of some cool takes on the SciFi-side of the genre but the execution is lackluster and the game feels... plain.My rating: 2.5/5 - Less exciting than stale bread and a glas of water.

_childDocuments_.review: The controls are absolutely terrible. I don't think using a controller instead of a keyboard would help. There's nothing crisp about movement so platforming is met with lots of frustration. It does have the Metroidvania feel to it. And you are punished for dying without saving (that's good, adds a layer of challenge). However, the amount of damage you can take but with so little health, you quickly die. Unlike older Castlevania games, there's no real way to swing your sword in all sorts of different directions to kill the annoyingly placed enemies all over the game world. There's also a delay in swinging your sword in some directions which makes it even more frustrating. The controls, lack of health (would be awesome if you could find health tanks which added 100 more health instead of just 10 health). And the enemies have far too much health. Also, the world does not naturally push you to upgrade your abilities like a polished Metroidvania game does. It feels more off the rails and more "just go everywhere with no real purpose and perhaps you'll find stuff and progress." Clearing rooms doesn't always work. Want to platform across a large room to make progress? Too bad: enemies respawn that you just cleared out in the same room. Make pretty far in a platforming puzzle? Too bad, random enemy spawned on a tiny platform and you must restart the entire sequence after touching it.Wall jumping? Don't know how. Maybe it is an ability you unlock later but wall jumping doesn't work. The game doesn't make it obvious you unlock wall jumping with an ability, alter. It might help if I could see all possible upgrades, their costs, and then grind like a madman to progress - then I might be more interested in playing more. But you only have a very small handful of upgrades available. Maybe I don't want to use the clunky sword for killing enemies and I'd like to upgrade my gun and kill everything from a distance? Charge gun? No, it uses an energy system that is not intuitive at all. It doesn't help that I cannot find any information on this game. Also, I don't like the blocky nearly unreadable text. I'd also like to see the 16-bit visual design of games go away. Give me a 2D Metroidvania without throwback graphics. Make it in high detail with beautiful textures and surfaces. Some games of done this and they get awards and accolades for their art. Still, keep my money. I want more games like this and this seems like a great attempt at a real and high quality Metroidvania game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a... standard Metroidvania experience.  If you're looking for one and stumbled across this, you may as well go for it!  It was a passable experience all around!  No major flaws, though a glaring (minor) oversight was quite annoying.  It has enough polish for fans of the genre.Getting 100% of the items wound up being a 10-hour experience, and only one of the bosses felt a bit unfair to me.  (My reaction speed was not fast enough to adapt to his otherwise simple pattern, but he shows up in two spots, and they are next to save points.)  Considering I beat the final boss in my first attempt, (maxed healing upgrades is sure handy,) it sure made that particularly tough boss stand out as an outlier.  So long as you try and keep collecting the various upgrades, you'll do fine throughout the adventure... with some pattern learning.  The melee weapons seam all fairly well balanced, so you're not forced into using one you don't like.  The guns, however, aren't quite as polished.  Though you could still ignore a gun if you don't mesh with it well... assuming it isn't gun 4.  That one is just better. (But not by numbers, just effect.)The largest glaring oversight was the controller cannot dismiss the 'obtained upgrade' menu at all.  CANNOT. AT. ALL.  Randomly halts things until I get over to my keyboard and press spacebar every time I collect an upgrade.  The controller's menu button (or activate, or any other button really,) dismissing this menu would be an easy workaround.  You are invincible during it, (along with any other situation that locks out your controls,) so I can't get randomly murdered from it.  My only complaints after that are little things: Not able to complete the map, map itself makes sizing a room hard as the black line defining the end of a room is a bit too thin, (missed a gun until after I reached the final area due to that,) no ability to fire down-diagonally forward, forward momentum in air is reduced at a certain distance that feels really random... small things.  Wall-jump inputs feel strange initially, but still easier to get down then Super Metroid's wall jumps.  All in all a very small list.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty dang good!The writing is bad and some of the art, in particular the cutscene art, is challenging let's say. The actual gameplay is really fun though!The traversal tools are fun, the weapons are fun. Combat in general feels more involved than most metroidvanias. You can't just ram your head into things or unload a dozen missiles in everything. The areas are also more interesting than your average metroidvania area. There are actual level gimmicks and involved platforming. Often it feels more like a level-based platformer than a metroidvania, which to me is a good thing.Bosses are also good; quite involved with a lot of attack patterns.As for the exploration itself it's not hand-holdy, yet it only happened once that I didn't know immediately where to go next. The map could've perhaps used a few extra features, but it's standard fare and works.Just an enjoyable time overall.

_childDocuments_.review: OK, so I initially reviewed this negatively. It just felt difficult and unfair in all the wrong ways. However, for some weird reason, I felt like revisiting it several months later, and I have changed my mind for the time being. I've actually been having fun with it now, and wanted to update my review to match. Stuff I like: - The presentation is pretty good, with good art and music direction, with decent writing as well. - Combat is primarily melee based, but you have a ranged weapon as well. The interplay is interesting, in that melee attacks charge your energy meter, which in turn fuels your gun. The gun feels less like a "sub-weapon" and more part of your main arsenal, albeit one you can't over-rely on.  - There are non-mandatory upgrades hidden around the levels. This is pretty cool, as you can get powers that are super helpful, but not required to proceed. It encourages exploration for more than just health or ammo increases. - The traversal powers are useful in various situations, not just to open the next area. - You get a regenerating shield, which is pretty rare outside of FPS games. It stops very little damage and takes forever to recharge, but it's still nice to have a little buffer. - There are refillable emergency health kits, which can come through in a pinch.Stuff I'm neutral on: - The default difficulty is really hard, and I've beaten La-Mulana and Blasphemous. Thankfully, Easy feels like just the right level of challenge for me. - Some of the boss fights feel really unbalanced or require some level of trial and error, but are mostly still doable. - There is a currency system that mostly feels unnecessary. There are some upgrades you can buy with it, so it partly serves as a way to let you get a bit stronger even if you can't make regular progress. It also lets you refill your emergency health kits at a save point, which again feels unnecessary.Stuff I don't like: - The controls take a little getting used to, as the jumping feels a little floaty and the ledge-grab is kind of wonky. Everything feels just a little too stiff. - You have a sliding "dodge" move, but unless you have a specific upgrade and energy to use it, it doesn't have any i-frames. And triggering that in the midst of combat can be tricky. - It's not always clear when you are in an area with bottomless pits, or if falling will just drop you down a screen. Luckily, falling into one just damages you, and doesn't kill you outright.I got this game for a song, and I'm glad I came back to give it a second chance. I haven't finished it yet, but if the rest of it changes my opinion again, I'll update my review.

_childDocuments_.review: Its an okay metroidvania.Some of the new weapons you get doesnt feel better than the ones you start with, and the upgrades you buy/find doesnt enhance you that much, specially not offensively.  So while the enemies gets harder, you dont get much stronger to compensate.Your healing is also frustratingly poor.  It takes a long time to activate, it heals over time rather than instantly, and it heals for around 1/4 of your health, which doesnt help a lot when you often end up having to take hits trying to activate it, specially on boss fights.I enjoyed it enough to 100% it, but its not a great game, just a decent one.

_childDocuments_.review: Sigh. This game.... with a smooth performance and sharp controls you would think this is going to be a great metroid-like. The problem is, the dev has neglected to include so many modern QoL features and managed to make a map WORSE than the one in super metroid, a 30 year old game. There's also quite a few really nasty bugs that occur if you do things a bit too unusual from what the dev expects. a very notable one is the game hardlocking if you save at the very start of the game and  exit after the old map runs away from you but before you catch up to him.A final issue is that the dev abandoned the game and only came back to do one thing: Increase the price of the game by 57% which is just utterly hilarious and this alone makes a recommendation impossible now.

_childDocuments_.review: I just started getting into Metroidvanias again, and this is the first one I got into. I also have Blasphemous and tried it, but I was completely confused on where to start after that first boss fight. I didn't feel that with Mindseize.You basically start out on a planet and work on that one planet, before going to the next one. This works out for me, since I'm just starting to get into these types of games again; I don't have to worry about trying to figure out where to go on a huge map like other Metroidvanias. You travel to other planets as the story progresses, and you can always go back to previous planets to go search out upgrades once you receive certain upgrades from defeated bosses. I love the art style as well, although I can care less about the story...not very engaging, at least not yet. I'm still playing the game and only have about 12 hours in.As far as the cons: I'm NOT a fan of the healing animation...AT ALL. I don't know how many times I've died from boss fights because I was in the middle of healing myself. Folks that made the game: please fix this. Also, I'm not too big of a fan of the map, as it doesn't really give you any type of markers so you know where to go back to to try to go back and get those upgrades you couldn't get because you didn't have the right ability at the time. You basically have to guess where those power ups are and search through areas you've already traversed all over again. Enemies can also take you out pretty quick if you're not careful....or even if you are careful. The later areas have some brutal enemies, but this just my opinion and my combat skills probably just suck. Results may vary. There's also some glitchiness in the game: There's been a few instances where the character froze after getting hit by a boss or regular enemy, while the rest of the game keep running.I hope the developers have been reading these comments and make the necessary changes. I actually still enjoy the game, but fixing a few of these issues would make the playing experience ten times better.

_childDocuments_.review: MARVELLOUS MODERNISED METROIDALIKEThis summer I took a trip down memory lane and completed Super Metroid again- it really is still a great game, so I went looking for something to replicate that hit.  Axiom Verge was a letdown for me - boring, and "A Robot Named Fight" is a bit meh, but this one came out of leftfield and really hit the spot! I really think the game deserves more credit: it has much of what Hollow Knight had, yet in that good old Metroid sci-fi territory of alien planets infested with weird creatures.  There's all the backtracking you'd expect, looking for a previously inaccessible area you can open up with a newfound power: what this game nails is making backtracking through the map FUN, because the combat is so good, and the platforming is pretty decent too.  There's an excellent variety of enemies to tackle, each needing different approaches with the sword/gun/grenades and dash at your disposal, and it's balanced such that you can't get complacent when heading from A to B: you need to stay on your toes or death and a trip back to the last save station beckons.There aren't too many surprises in the powers you gain- without wanting to give too much away, they're pretty much everything you'd expect in a modern Metroidvania- y'know, a dash, wall-jump, sword-dive etc.  Some abilities can be purchased but you get most of your gear by searching for it, and I did appreciate the sheer amount of stuff you can find.  Not all of it is spectacular, much of it involves tweaks to your abilities, but in this challenging enviroment all upgrades were welcome.The boss fights are fine- not as spectacular as those of Hollow Knight, but generally they provide the right level of seemingly-insurmountable challenge until you work out the right tactics.  There's an extra boss-rush mode which I didn't try.Storyline?  It's pretty straightforward, whisks along quickly, and there is an emotional motivation for your quest.  All good things in my view.  The traditional Metroidvania solitude is broken up with occasional visits to your team in an orbiting spaceship, which I thought was rather nice and added to the heart and soul evident in the game.Complaints?  Well, a way of placing markers on the map certainly wouldn't go amiss.  The music, though praised by many, didn't do much for me- in fact I found one of the first tunes infuriatingly repetitive; fortunately the rest of it was inoffensive.  Though the animation and character design is great, the backgrounds are somewhat bland.  They're more conservative than some of the weird stuff seen in Super Metroid.  I encountered about 3 bugs in my 21 hour playthrough, but it's good to see that at the time of writing a programmer is still working on fixes and providing updates.Well done to the devs- I really enjoyed your work!(I bought this game in a sale at the ridiculously low price of £0.89)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. VERY heavily inspired by the Mega Man Zero and the X series from what I can tell. Also, there may have been some bugs when it was first released, but I just finished my play-through with no issues at all. Difficulty was challenging but never unfair, the upgrades were unique and interesting, and while the dialogue is pretty bad at times, the story is just fine with a few bright spots here and there. Movement in this game feels really nice, especially towards the end where you are using abilities on top of abilities. Biggest downside would be the map and its lack of waypoints/defining markers as it gets a little confusing at times.Overall, definitely one of the better Metroidvania that flood Steam. Worth a shot.

I don't know what was wrong that it couldn't manage to detect controller nor keyboard to try to play, but it works now.Positive review thus far just for a dev that actually took efforts to fix things.  Will leave further review when I've had a chance to play more.Further review- A few iffy parts, a couple early bosses needed more playtesting I think, and there was a point in the game where I seemed to skip a very large zone (research lab) to go straight down to the planet accidentally, and later found the electric gun before fighting the boss that gives you the tool to reach the electric gun, and a slew of other odd things.Little hiccups aside, the gameplay is generally solid and the bosses well built. _childDocuments_.review: I find the game to be a mixed bag, but more good than bad, and is a decent addition to anyone who likes 2d Metroidvanias.It's not a Metroid-like. It's an equal mix of Metroid/Igavanias/Mega Man Z games.IMOGreat:- A great collectibles system. Instead of just finding 50 missile packs and a few major upgrades, you find very many little upgrades that tweak your abilities in interesting ways. You don't need any of them, but each time you find one it's very meaningful.- The main music track of the 2nd world. <3Good:- The pixel art style- Some of the boss fights- Movement control- No hand holding- Unique story with okay charactersMeh:- Enemy behavior becomes too predictable and stale- Most boss fights lack polish- The close-ups on the characters, also the change in pixel size just doesn't look nice.- Title screen- Not enough enemy varietyBad:- The map provides far too little feedback. Try Rainworld, Out Buddies or so many others for an example of how to provide useful info via the map. It lacks terrain details, is misshaped and doesn't show collectible or just about anything.- Finding hidden stuff usually amounts to bashing every wall.- Weapons control. SOOOO stiff. Cant shoot diagonally in the air, attack animations are so long and uninteruptable. This x3- A lot of the platforming feels like filler. Stage design is uninteresting, especially mid game.- Some boss fights are garbo. (a few are decent)Overall, I'm glad I stuck with it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has some shortcomings but some strong points that make up for it. First and foremost, the gameplay is solid, tight, and very satisfying. Movement is a bit odd at first (the ledge/wall grabbing) but you quickly get used to it. The combat is very fun. The different weapons are good, but I wish there were more! The soundtrack is excellent, and really helps drive the action.Now for the shortcomings: the story is a bit lackluster, told mostly through somewhat clunky and derivative dialog. Maybe I'm expecting too much but other similar games do a much better job of world building (Axiom Verge and Hyper Light Drifter come to mind). Perhaps Mindseize would have done better with a bit LESS story, letting the world come to life through incidental/environmental discovery. Also, I would have preferred if the cutscenes just took place in the game, foregoing the jarring animations.However, my biggest gripe is with length and pacing. The first three acts are excellent, but the fourth and final completely fails. Just when I was really getting into the game it suddenly ends. The final level is so short, so devoid of life and seeming effort that it mars an otherwise excellent game. It just feels like the developer ran out of time/money/inspiration/♥♥♥♥♥ to give and just needed to wrap up the game.Having said that, I do recommend it if you can get it on sale under 10 bucks. I had a great time playing the game for 12 hours or so (100% completion, 19/20 achievements). I just wish it could have lasted another 12 hours though.

_childDocuments_.review: Short: Good metroidvania with emphasis on graphics, especially environmental and sprite detail. If you want a solid mteroidvania title, this will work. Good: beautiful art direction, sprite and backgrounds are given great detail; solid mechanics once you get used to them; Bad: gamepad support can be weird (no joystick support on DS4); the story thins out past the halfway point and does not exploit its own potential; fairly little is done with the characters that we are introduced, even though its obvious some effort of depth is given them;Meh: the chase scene in the beginning was weird; the ending was too simple; difficulty curve with bosses can be uneven, I found the Abyssal Monster tougher to beat than the final boss; Undecided: I feel that the game is cut-down, the first three worlds are much bigger and more expansive than the last two; Overall, I do not regret buying and playing this game but I feel that it sets itself up for stuff that it then doesn't use. The ending in particular felt rushed and overly simple.

_childDocuments_.review: I found the general atmosphere of the game very enjoyable. The sci-fi theme was well executed and tightly connected to the plot. The attack and movement animations are also very on point. Movement feels smooth and controls are tight. Level design was also pretty solid, I felt encouraged to explore without getting lost too often.  I did encounter a few issues during my playthrough, but none that were in fact detrimental to my experience, also the developers were very quick to reply on discord and get things fixed. Respect.

_childDocuments_.review: Best thing that has happened since Super Metroid. This game offers the sense of adventure and exploration that we seek from metroidvania games, and while it has relatively user friendly level and progression design, it does not hold your hand or point straight to the next step. Freedom to do certain things in your own order and pace gives you the feeling that you are in control and making the decisions and advancing the your mission. It looks good, sounds good and feels good. Yes, there are some occasional (rare), benign glitches, but they do not really impede your experience in any way. I loved this game and hope that there will be more content in form of DLC or sequel. This was just amazing!

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the Metroid games as much as I did, this is an easy recommendation for the price. The thrill of exploration and discovery is there, as well as a somewhat clunky but ultimately badass combat system. A lot of thought seems to have been put into the alien worlds, and the different distinct biomes within each, such as a crashed ship on a forest world or devastated war-torn housing units surrounding a decidedly OSHA non-compliant factory.  It's still a little rough around the edges, as other reviewers have mentioned, but by the time of my purchase the devs seemed to have fixed any major bugs and remain active in fine-tuning the game. This should be a strong contender for an Indie Gems list, if they don't already have too many Metroidvania's in there.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game, absolutely. A tad tough at time, no doubt about it, but absolutely worth the time. I suppose I sorta wish there were even more upgrades, possibly a DLC expansion or perhaps even, after completing the final boss, a way to open up map markers for missed upgrades. As it is, I'm probably just going to consider myself retired from the game after my successful run, delete, and move onto other titles. Map reveal would certainly give me a guided reason to dive back into the world and spend a bit more time there, Buuuuuuut 17 hours for the cost I paid (granted, probably 2 of those hours were probably spent afk) for the price I paid; certainly already worth it. I'm definitely not claiming that I didn't get enough bang for my buck. As far as Steam is concerned, You've got your Hollowknight, Ori, Bloodstained, Shadow Complex, Shantae & I reckon you could include this MindSeize within the top metroidvania style titles available (yeah, I dug this more than Axiom Verge)[edit] - It may be important to note that I specifically waited to play the game AFTER achievements were patched in (to be more specific, I began my game run yesterday 4-4-20). I only state this in order to supply the statement that my run had very few bugs. None that were game breaking.Some examples: 1. Sometimes while wall jumping not being able to spring from left to right & just jumping and inexplicably being forced up one side of a wall. 2. character freezing temporarily. 3. character only facing one direction temporarily. 4. while fighting an enemy too close to the side of a screen that transitions to a new screen, I might occasionally/rarely get stuck (I died only once due to this).Really, honestly, the bugs were pretty rare & I wouldn't say they ruined my experience, Not by a long shot. & I'll again state, I'd love for the developers to do more with this engine/world/characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very nice Metroid-vania experience. The music fits the mood well and graphics look nice. Some sprites do look off like they don't fit to the overall style, but that's not an issue. The diagonal aim might be hard to get used to unless you have played GBA Metroids (Fusion or Zero Mission). Though, oddly you can't aim diagonally down and diagonal aim doesn't work mid air.On release the game did have a fair amount of bugs (which could be reason for some negative reviews), but the developers have already released several patches to fix them. I can usually ignore small bugs that are not bothering gameplay.The difficulty is fine, aside two bosses. The Monkey boss moves a bit too fast to reliably predict what the boss is about to do in time. The boss in the research facility that gives you the flamethrower (iirc) has sometimes a bit too much happening at once. One issue is that the boss fires grenades too often, sometimes over 5 times in a row, which makes avoiding them very difficult. Unfortunately I had to resort to cheating to get past these two bosses, so I hope they'll be balanced a bit in a future patch.

_childDocuments_.review: This metroidvania gets a lot of things right but unfortunately it is a buggy and glitchy mess. The combat is very fun, if not a bit irritating with the enemy attacks. Every set of enemies you run into requires a bit of strategic approach which keeps it fresh, but with it being a metroidvania requiring you to revisit many areas multiple times, running into these sets of enemies over and over when trying to advance the storyline or find progressive items can feel tedious at times. The game follows the traditional progression of finding the next ability that will let you access the next area, and some might find it bearable, I had a lot of issues with areas being forced to search every nook and cranny to find that next item only to be greeted with minor upgrades that don't help at all. There is literally an ability you find that moves your character a few pixels forward when attacking. This is totally unnecessary. You will be searching  for the one item that will get you into one smaller area to advance the game and it never felt rewarding at all. Sound effects are good, music is ok but would be much better without the tracks ending then starting back over again, no proper looping for this type of game is slightly jarring but not the worst thing.The upgrades and abilities you get are typical metroidvania attire, if not a bit predictable, but the dashing movement you unlocked felt really fun traversing through areas you've already explored. Having both a gun and melee attacks helps shake things up when approaching different sets of enemies keeping you on your toes.The graphics are pretty good, I really enjoyed the pixel art style and the scenic backgrounds.Unfortunately what really turned me off this game, with it's numerous bugs and glitches, was that on Day 1 this game was  unfinishable. It has since been patched and fixed, but during a fight with a certain boss on the second planet, the boss would glitch into the floor and fly away if it did a certain attack, leaving you stuck in a room softlocked with nowhere to go and the only solution was to reset the game. Only problem is it did it every single time for me, completely unable to advance the game and actually finish it. If this was in EA, it would be easy to pass over this and accept that it happened, however the developers decided to release this game  that it had a myriad of issues with promises to release upcoming patches, with I just find unacceptable. As much as I enjoyed a lot about this game, I expected a finished product on Day 1, and it wasn't, and the result is that I have no motivation or interest in going back to finish this game.If you want to enjoy a finished product of this game, wait for numerous patches and keep tabs on the community hub, but as of right now I cannot recommend this game until it gets fixed, and even then I don't see myself coming to finish this one.
