_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I haven't had time to really give a deep dive, but extensive patches (and a bit of testing since then) have shown consistent and massive improvement in both the feeling of gameplay and the issues I encountered. I can't attest that all the bugs are gone because I haven't had a chance to play all the way through again, but the most critical issues I faced are fixed and since I was already barely not recommending the game that's definitely enough to sway it. Kudos to the developer for continuing to support and update the game past release! Most of the original review is below, but it is definitely out of date thanks to the persistent efforts of the developer.I don't dislike MindSieze, but I can't recommend it right now. There are several issues that are simply frustrating and seem to be the consequence of a lack of polish/QA/testing. While the story, music, and gameplay are good, there are many issues that make it impossible MindSieze in its current state, which is a shame. Even just two hours in, there are already some pretty annoying issues.The most devastating is a control lockup issue when using the second ranged weapon. Every once in a while, I simply freeze up after using this weapon and cannot do anything. I am playing on keyboard (arrow key layout). Once this happens, I have to quit the game or let enemies kill me to reset controls, meaning that I lose all progress to the last save point. This is not a huge deal, since the first ranged weapon is a bit better in my opinion (mostly because of movement) but it's still annoying for when I do want to use the second weapon (more damage per shot means that it can deal with flying or enemies a bit more easily). Generally, controls seem a bit unresponsive at times. I know a controller is recommended, but I suspect that some of my issues, such as dropped attacks, seemingly unresponsive frames around attacks, and some difficulty with timing may be either design or bug induced. It also seems like inputs can freeze or queue in ways that make the character just kind of move wrong, which is frustrating in a platforming segment, though fortunately almost all of these tie into attacks, so precision jumping is typically fine. I also once encountered an enemy on the second planet that I just couldn't hit with anything (attacks just passed through), though I don't know what the culprit was there.There are also some platforming issues, which is kind of odd. In one area on the second planet, there are pods moving on an assembly line, and if you try to climb onto them towards the direction they're coming from, you'll launch past them. On the first planet, before entering the abandoned ship above the forest, I had issues clambering up onto suspended blocks. Dying and returning to the save point fixed this issue, and I'm not sure why. Generally, there seems to be some glitches with how the character climbs and perhaps other movement options. Additionally, readability for environmental objects is a bit dicey. I believe there are some objects that can be broken by power attacks. I say I believe, because they only actually seem to break rarely. I'm pretty sure the blue crates with the star looking icon are supposed to break to sword power attacks, since one or two of these were effectively destroyed by this, but I'm starting to suspect that there's some issues with either that only happening because the attack clipped through and activated a hidden trigger item or that I'm completely mistaken. Now, the game doesn't need to hand hold players on that, but it feels really inconsistent. Perhaps there's a detail I'm missing, but since I think my progress is gated behind these kinds of gates (either fire icon gates or star icon containers), it's frustrating to know that I've sometimes, but not always, gotten those to open, and the reason may or may not be apparent. That said, this is very narrowly a not recommended. I like the music. I like the designs. I like the platforming. When the controls are responsive, I like the combat. The environments are, for the most part, solid, though some of the areas have issues with lighting and readability in my opinion. However, it's frustrating to lose ten minutes of progress to an issue such as freezing, to not know how to proceed because I can't tell why things happen, or bugged enemies who spawn invincible. However, the moment I see a patch, I'm definitely giving this another go. There's a lot of great potential here. For some reason the game wasn't launched in Early Access, which unfortunately is what this game feels like at the moment. However, the developer has acknowledged that there are still some things left to finish and polish, though, so I hope it will be fixed up soon and ready to really clear through.

name: DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition The Deluxe Edition includes the game, a Cooking Item that gives your character permanent Ki-ATK and HP Stat boosts, and the Season Pass. The Season Pass adds 2 original episodes and a new story. LEGENDARY EDITION The Legendary Edition includes: • Full game • Season Pass (2 original episodes and a new story arc) • Season Pass 2 (3 new story arcs) • 2 Cooking Items that give your character temporary and permanent Stat boosts • Tao Pai Pai Pillar About the Game The Dragon Ball RPG of your dreams! For the first time, you can play the rest of the story. Step into the universe of Dragon Ball Z in all its iconic glory and become the hero you were always meant to be! Experience the legendary Dragon Ball Z story with total immersion! A hero on an unending quest to become the greatest warrior in the universe. The son training to live up to his father’s epic legacy. In DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT , you’ll live through every moment in breathtaking clarity. You’ll meet the people who shape the story, take on a would-be hero’s life, and learn firsthand exactly what’s worth fighting for! Fight, Fish, Fly, Eat, Explore, and so much more! Life on Earth has so much to offer a Saiyan hero, and you can try it all! Go fishing to relax after a big battle, eat a hero-sized meal with your Z Fighter friends, explore the city, or take off and fly to the farthest horizon. You can also complete unique side Story Quests to help out the people of the Cities and Villages. Living these peaceful, fulfilling moments in the world of Dragon Ball brings you closer to the characters than ever before. Relive the most iconic arcs through epic fights! Now that you’ve tasted everything this bustling planet has to offer, there’s even more on the line when opponents come looking to tear it all down. When the worst of the worst show up with their schemes, you’ll be waiting to take them down as your favorite characters!

You’ll meet the people who shape the story, take on a would-be hero’s life, and learn firsthand exactly what’s worth fighting for! Fight, Fish, Fly, Eat, Explore, and so much more! Life on Earth has so much to offer a Saiyan hero, and you can try it all! Go fishing to relax after a big battle, eat a hero-sized meal with your Z Fighter friends, explore the city, or take off and fly to the farthest horizon. You can also complete unique side Story Quests to help out the people of the Cities and Villages. Living these peaceful, fulfilling moments in the world of Dragon Ball brings you closer to the characters than ever before. Relive the most iconic arcs through epic fights! Now that you’ve tasted everything this bustling planet has to offer, there’s even more on the line when opponents come looking to tear it all down. When the worst of the worst show up with their schemes, you’ll be waiting to take them down as your favorite characters!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a well designed arena fighter, jumping around from 1v1 to 3v6 battles.  The controls feel tight & responsive.  Techniques are easy to use, as are the transformations.  Everything is unlocked through an upgrade menu skill tree, using orbs to make the way down to the bottom, with some techniques hidden behind training battles.  The visuals & soundtrack all pop, using many tracks from the show itself, though missing the insert songs.  As for the story, it's exactly what you expect from a Dragon Ball game.  The side quests, though, provide additional content, attempting to explain both what was going on during major events, as well as showing off some characters that borderline disappeared in the second half of the series. This is an RPG at heart, & as a result, the endgame is loaded with grind.  Although the core game gives plenty of opportunities to gather orbs & provides you with plenty, a fair amount of the endgame requires an insane amount of them.  The higher level challenges can also feel incredible cheap to attempt to playthrough.  It also feels like the game has a lot of bloated downtime between the chapters, with some side missions & challenges feeling rather unrewarding (though admittedly it is amusing having Son Goku cruising about in a car).  A fairly big miss, however, is the lack of the entire first half of the story, with the game kicking in at Raditz's arrival.  Finally, there's the oddly detailed free card game DLC.  This is entirely dependent on the user playing, but it feels like a cheaper version of Magic the Gathering.  Personally, I didn't enjoy it, but I could understand someone putting more hours into that instead of the main game. The achievement list is actually very simple.  Though it's varied & may seem like a challenge, the majority of them will actually be completed just playing through the story & completing side quests.  The only one that will provide some challenge is the battle with Mira.  My recommendation is to actually boot up the first DLC as soon as you can.  The rewards make leveling up very simple, & should not be passed on until the endgame. This is actually a well designed arena RPG that has enough content to pull you through to the end of the game.  Though it feels a bit laggy in content from time to time, & the lack of the first half of Dragon Ball is missed, the positives outweigh the negatives.  Definitely worth a look, & not only just for Dragon Ball fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Though I'm only a few hours in as of writing this, Kakarot has been an awesome experience so far. It's been giving a very close look at the original story (I've been told it follows the manga, not the anime? Citation needed), but also takes some tiny liberties for the sake of gameplay.The gameplay aspects are tons of fun. Word of warning for Xenoverse fans. THIS IS NOT A FIGHTING GAME. I REPEAT, THIS IS NOT A FIGHTING GAME. This is an RPG. There are no combos, no light/heavy attacks, and some of the special attacks can be... difficult to use strategically. The combat is much more about the flashy fun. It is not as technical or precise as a fighting game would be, and it feels very.... video game-y, if that makes sense? But it also FEELS like DBZ. No stamina management but a somewhat small dodge window means you can vanish step all over the place and feel awesome, but still get hit if you aren't paying attention and looking for the right timing. Ki recharges fast, so you can use your abilities when you want to, and properly stringing your abilities together seems to be the way to win fights, so there is definitely some skill/learning involved. I was surprised at the difficulty of some fights, but I'm admittedly not the best at the game. With some refinement, this system would be amazing for Xenoverse 3.If you love DBZ, get this and enjoy the nostalgia. Classic DBZ story without much alteration, the ability to explore some open areas and see cities and combat areas from the anime from new angles, Japanese version  music, and a great visual style.

_childDocuments_.review: The base game is good up to the Cell Saga. Afterwards, there's a huge dip in quality and story-telling. It genuinely feels like development was rushed near the latter half of the game. Battle of Gods is a separate expansion that you can play during the main story or after. Problem with this is that it gives you a stupid amount of EXP and early transformations that aren't referenced in the base story. So you can literally walk into the Raditz fight as SSG Goku and one-shot the rest of the base game. Other than a fight with Beerus, you don't get much else.Resurrection of F actually is locked to the Post-Game, and you unlock Blue right out the gate. Horde battles are introduced, but they're EXTREMELY boring to do, resulting in you mashing the attack button and spamming team attacks for 15-20 minutes for ludicrous EXP. Most of the dialogue is text driven, without any voice-acting whatsoever. You fight Frieza, beat him, then revive him in a side mission to fight him over and over again. That's it. Overall time to do all of this, probably about and hour or two, if you're taking your time. My opinion of the DLC for Battle of Gods and Resurrection of F do not make the game any better... The only thing you really get from it is an updated combo-system, SSG and SSB transformations for Goku and Vegeta, and subpar story with hardly any voiced character dialogue. I would strongly recommend avoiding these DLCs as they actually worsen the experience. They're built as blatant cash-grabs that add nothing new to the game and are not worth more than a buck or two. I've seen free updates with more content than these two paid DLCs.

Bad, however it is not what it claims to be, this isn't an rpg where you get to train people up. it's possible but not attainable reasonably.what I mean is grinding is not needed Good right? but this goes against the random encounters which suddenly have no point.the reason grinding isnt needed is because large amounts of exp are given as the story moves on to keep the characters as powerful as they need to be in that part of the story.in the Saiyan sagathe average random encounter gives 100 exp, when it takes 9000ish to level up, not horrible but already very grindy per level, but like a good JRPG player I did a little grinding, got a good pile of exp from side quests which gave 10000+, then when Goku comes back from King Kais he is suddenly given over one hundred thousand exp.The same thing happened when he arrived on Namek, Over Six Hundred Fifty thousand exp for arriving on Namek.it is a great way to show the growth of these characters. but YOU do not make that growth. it feels hollow and by the android arc you know very well that there is ZERO point to engage in random encounters. the only way to gain good EXP is side quests and main missions. which is fine. but it isn't what was advertized.why does fighting 5 saibamen give 200 exp when giving random tourists a rock give several thousand? because it's an easy way to balance the fights by forcing you to be at or around a certain level.that being said, the combat is flashy and honestly very fun it just rubbed me the wrong way to have the illusion of RPG mechanics.Would I recommend it? yes, sure. but only if you're looking for a flashier but less deep budokai. not if you're looking for a Legacy of Goku or Xenoverse.

_childDocuments_.review: The cutscenes are pretty, I have to admit it for the least, but it is just barely enough to overcome the flat open world and underwhelming mission design.Censorship is also a huge part in this game since there is no blood, certain scenes are removed or altered and it just feels awkward.For some reason, changes to the graphics settings are very limited.Many visual aspects bothered me at first, including abusing lens flares, bloom, chromatic aberration and so on. But after a while, I had come to think that it fits the general appearance so I pretty much got over it.The game hits you with lots of nostalgia but falls flat when it comes to having substantial gameplay. The fighting aspect feels dull, you can probably start every fight the same way against any opponent and flying around the world is very clunky, especially while collecting orbs.It tries to be an RPG but lacks so many aspects of the genre that it immediately becomes very trivial. I personally don't use food since fights couldn't be easier.I didn't mention the difficulty since it's an RPG and that it can quickly become very easy as you level up.It mostly delivers original compositions but some of the Dragon Ball Z anime soundtracks are included and I couldn't have asked for more. Oh, yes, original voice-overs are a real treat.Some parts of the game are strangely mixed and make most story scenes not as intense as it should be ().Other than that, I don't have much to say about the sound effects, given that most of the sounds used are from the anime.Dragon Ball Z Kakarot could have been a worthy RPG for fans such as me, but the game ultimately underperforms in too many aspects and no matter how strange it sounds, it’s at the same time very close and very far from being the best Dragon Ball game out there.Honestly, if it had been any other franchise with this gameplay and storytelling, I couldn't have cared less about it.So, should I recommend this ? Yes, but only to people familiar with the anime at best.Am I disappointed ? Of course, I am.Then  would I let someone play a game I didn't really enjoy in its entirety ? Simple. Because objectively, the game still delivers a lot of good things and even subjectively, I enjoyed many things from it, mainly the voice acting. But the cutscenes are what made me change my mind. It is satisfying to play through the story and get a beautiful cutscene during and after intense fights and these things as well as nostalgia, did nonetheless, make me play the game for approximately 40 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: How does this game not have basic features like a "restart fight" mid boss? Why do bosses suddenly change the rules of the game mid fight? Why does blocking certain moves sometimes work and other times not? Its because this game lacks polish. The games idea of difficulty is enemies magically get hyper armor out of nowhere. Cant even tell whats happening when using Ki attacks, if the enemy starts casting an uninterruptible move and it doesn't show up under their name displaying that they are in fact casting, that's bad polish and that's what the downfall of this game is, bad polish. I feel like this stuff would be common sense in another game. Enemy moves should ALWAYS be displayed somehow. Blocking should be consistent as its one of the two defensive options you have, dodging being the riskier one. Not to mention the lack of a tutorial explaining core mechanics like being able to cancel your channeling moves. Its the frustrating little things that add up due to the lack of polish and yet the game has $160 worth of DLC.Not to mention how BS certain characters are to play, let alone fight. Piccolo is broken compared to every other character. Just spam Explosive wave and with Solar flare supports and win. Radditz and Nappa are more annoying to fight then any other character in the game, quite literally spamming the same two moves repeatedly like a 5 year old. You can fight characters 10 levels above you but every move they spam, hit stuns you into the next spam. Any solution to the games BS difficulty can also be solved buy buying a ♥♥♥♥ ton of healing items which is boring as ♥♥♥♥

_childDocuments_.review: A fun nostalgia trip for fans of the series. The fact that this game is an RPG is what sets it apart from other DBZ games. A lot of the mechanics feel unnecessary and cluttered but it seems like you can mostly ignore the parts you don't like and still progress through the game. One of my favorite parts of this game is that you can have fights with more than 2 fighters at once. The battle against Raditz is actually a 2v1 and I can't think of another DBZ game that lets Goku and Piccolo fight side by side. It also adds a bit to the narrative like with more detail about the Red Ribbon Army between OG Dragon Ball and the Android Saga. Hard to recommend this game to those that aren't fans of the manga or anime but some good fun for true fans. Only thing that would make it better is a versus mode but thankfully we have every other DBZ game ever made to fit that purpose.

The special effects are out of this world.14 - While we wait for the great Sparking Zero, enjoy this magnificent game.This game gets a 9/10 with a banging Kamehameha...

_childDocuments_.review: If for some reason you want to play this game but havent watched the anime or read the manga there will be SPOILERSI decided to write this review after finishing the main story twice, all sub stories, every revived enemy with the Dragon Balls and all villanous enemies. The game is pretty good and has alot of pros. But it would be a long review to cover them all in more detail so im going to sum the pros up and give a more detailed review about the cons. But I do think that the pros heavily outweight the cons and I definetly recommend this game if you are a Dragon Ball fan. Since the games selling point is that its a very immersive DBZ game and its basically made to capture a nostaliga feeling in DBZ fans and filling alot of plot holes I suggest that you watch the anime before playing this game. However this game is also a great introduction for those that are newcomers to Dragon Ball.   Pros: Overall fun gameplayLeveling is addictingGood Boss fightsGreat additions to the original storyThe Map gives a great perspective of Earth in Dragon ballAlot of things to doGreat animationsSoundtrackNostalgiaGreat mini stories Many contradicting things in the lore has been retconned to actually make senseCool Minigames like Racing and BaseballGreat animations and cutscenes made from scratchGood graphics that stay true to the "anime look"Cons: Great powerup moments which were the coolest in the anime/manga doesnt exist in the game while some pretty forgetable moments were included. For example when vegeta kills Jeice and Burter was included but Vegetas final flash vs Cell wasnt. Or another one which really bothered me was Gokus kaioken powerup in front of Captain Ginyu wasnt included. Some crucial moments in the story were very undramatic/underwhelming for some reason. One example beeing when Piccolo sacrifised himself to save Gohan. Goku becoming a super sayian for the first time. Trunks getting killed by Cell. It just doesnt manage to capture the same feeling that the anime does.In combat you wont get any cool animations unless you break the enemies guard which very rarely happens.Alot of the side quests are just fetch missions which you have to do if you want to level up and get crucial rewards before the story ends, which is needed for learning new moves and they are very tedious. Like relying on RnG to capture 2 "blue fish" which took me more than 20 minutes. Combat is mostly very easy since you can literally spam super attacks in most fights. Even on "hard" difficulty.No new game+ and the game has almost 0 replayability.Alot of arcs are locked behind expensive dlc which are pretty important for the overall story. Like Bardock and futute Trunks DLC.Dodoria was literally the hardest boss fight lol.  The only relevant characters are Vegeta, Goku, Gohan and Piccolo until his fight with Android 17, while the other Z fighters are just support characters (I get that its basically staying true to the anime but you can almost never play as them unless its an intermission)Very little variety in standard enemies were the only ones beeing: Pirate robots, Freeza Soldiers, Saibamen, Babidis Lackeys and R.R Army robots.FINAL VERDICTIts definetly one of the best Dragon Ball games that there is. It just falls a bit short in some areas being mostly repetitive combat/enemies and some very booring long tedious sidemissions. But if youre a Dragon Ball fan this game is definetly a must play in my opinion, but due note that some great moments in the Anime arent in the game, while moments that are - will leave you pretty dissapointed, which atleast made me feel that I would have rathered watched the anime instead.Sometimes through the story I actually watched the moments on youtube instead of the game to capture that feeling that was missing from the game. This was in my opinion the biggest flaw in the game.7/10 Non Dragon Ball fan8/10 If you are a Dragon Ball fan

_childDocuments_.review: The best Dragon Ball game so far, but if it weren't a "Dragon Ball" game I think people would call it average. Personally, I'd be happy with a 2D turn-based RPG like Attack of the Saiyans, but I'm a lame old man. *Minor spoilers*Pros-Exploring the Dragon World is loads of fun-Ability to wish back villains is a nice touch-Minor world-building-You can buy a car -Improvement from Xenoverse graphics/mechanicsCons-The random battles are annoying/tedious and have verrry little EXP payoff-Game isn't really an RPG, there are limited ways to earn worthwhile EXP-Story has a few changes, for the really BIG Dragon Balls fans it could be fun, but I found myself skipping the cutscenes-The gore with the Raditz, Frieza (vs Goku and Trunks), and Cell battles has been removed-Lazy animation in a lot of parts-Missed story opportunities (King Kai's place, Yardrat, general side stories, etc)For DBZ fans, I'd recommend, but anyone "Eh" on the series should pass. I loved it for the first two days of playing before realizing if it were called anything else, I wouldn't bother with it.For those who experience crashing, update your drivers. _childDocuments_.review: The combat is wonky and awkward; the camera angling is awkward, the fighting feels unconventional. Games like Raging Blast and Bodukai Tenkaichi nailed 3D DBZ combat, while this game tries to fuse Ultimate Ninja Storm and Raging Blast. Separately, both games are great. Fused, it feels unnatural. The game succeeds, however, in building cinematic moments, however fleeting moments in which the best reaction garnered is "huh, cool" doesn't make this game more interesting. The open world element to this game looks intriguing, but is just so damn tedious; there's a side mission to everything that you do. Overall if you're expecting a classical DBZ fighting experience, don't get this game. If you want cinematic moments and don't mind the tedious gameplay within combat and otherwise, by all means give it a try.The developers have definitely made better games and are capable of much more than this. 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: This was basically my teen-self dream game. I wish they had made this game back then. :GIf you grew up watching Dragon Ball, then this is a must buy. Rushing back from school just to catch the newest episode on TV, and then discussing that episode with all the other kids the next day at school is for sure one of the fondest memories I have of that period.This is by far the best retelling of DBZ in videogame format. The developers really took care in trying to perfectly recreate the most important moments of the story as accurately as possible, down to all the countless outfits each character wears in the different story arcs. The high-budget cutscenes are lit as ♥♥♥♥ and some of them are even better than the TV series counterparts. They even remade some classic tracks of the TV series' soundtrack, and all the iconic DB sound effects are all there. The combat, even if super simple, gives the perfect Dragon Ball (Z) feeling, and that is really all you could ask for.If you are not a fan of Dragon Ball though, you should skip this game, since it has (objectively) too many faults: it is repetitive, the areas are kind of empty, the sidequests are all the same, and in general the game tries to bite off more than it can chew. Many of these faults are due to the ambition of the game (retelling the whole DBZ saga) while working on a limited budget, but I'm glad they tried anyway.Btw the game should have been called  "Dragon Ball Z: Gohan" since you play as Gohan a good 60-70% of the entire playtime. :ptl;dr A fantastic game for the fans, everyone else should just ignore it.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game worried that it would be boring as I have seen the dbz story a hundred times. I will say that I am overall enjoying the game and am satisfied with it. 8/10. If this game had a slightly deeper combat system it would be a real 10/10 dbz game. COMBAT: Your options aren't as deep as xenoverse, which isn't that deep in the first place, HOWEVER most of the enemies I fight so far have different attack patterns and you must attack and defend differently on said enemies otherwise you are gonna take a lot of damage and risk losing. I don't like making this analogy as I have played Dark Souls and cringe whenever I see people use it as a weak comparison, but there is a very similar comparison I can draw to give you an idea of the combat. Dark Souls boss battles are hard, with that said, if you just dodge all the attacks and attack when it is safe you will win, which is how any game is, but this game is closer to the difficulty of dark souls then xenoverse in the difficulty of doing so (but it's not as hard as dark souls don't get the wrong idea). This makes the combat feel really satisfying as you try to figure out how to get around opponents. Although this challenge can be circumvented by just stocking up on healing items and using them midbattle, making it so you can just keep attacking and not worry about strategy, I choose to not do that.STORY: Even though I am burnt out on the same dbz story I find myself enjoying the game and wanting to continue it, although as of now I am reaching the Android saga and am just now feeling the onset of burnout, I still wanna keep at it. If you haven't watched all of dbz or played it in story format this is the game to play. It feels like they didn't miss a single cannon fight that took place. You fight everyone that the main cast fought in the anime, even the smaller baddies. Dialogue in many past dbz games have been bad, in this game it is good and there is a lot of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is to help you deciding whether you are going to buy the game or not. Please be aware that part of this review can or not include spoilers but I feel every detail should be considered. I have completed 100% of the game.Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot is an open world RPG game where you can explore most of Earth while using most of characters. Exploring experience is decent, with high quality visuals and details. Levelling system is acceptable, but it for sure is grindy. While travelling around, you can fight some enemies that give you EXP and Orbs which is most of you need to level up. There is no PVE mode like Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 and there is no training mode. The "training" mode is only used to get more super attacks for your characters, and those can be very challenging if you do not meet level requirements. Story line/Main missions are VERY good, no questioning, If you are a Dragon Ball fan you will be very proud of this game, I almost felt like watching the Dragon Ball movie, so Unreal Engine 5 is a must from now on.Overall Dragon Ball: Kakarot does offer a great experience, it is a game to be played patiently, to enjoy the whole experience of Dragon Ball. If you like to rush, then you will miss most of the precious details. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a long time Dragon Ball fan - I've played and watched the anime. The game does a lot of things from the anime, be it filler or throughout all of Super, justice. It's fantastic because it actually makes you feel like you're in the Dragon Ball world. A lot of funny things like Vegeta having maximum Cooking because he had to cook for Whis as well as the reason of the Potara earrings having a time limit unless Kais are involved, which are all "end of DBS" things is fantastic. I am simply amazed beyond comprehension as a fan of the franchise.That being said, there are a couple bits of issues.Awareness is very important in this game - red unflinchable strong attacks are something that players have to keep track of, and if you don't avoid it, you get stunlocked. Sometimes, the game feels like it's very unresponsive to your command inputs and your opponents can't be knocked back even when you blast a full power Kamehameha/Final Flash/Special Beam Cannon.Lastly, leveling. The biggest thing in an RPG style game is "over leveling." When you're overleveled here, the game really makes it known because the stat differences are insane. I felt too powerful starting from Cell to the end, even through the final secret boss, Mira. Vegito, which is unlocked through a substory, is also overwhelming stronger than his level states, which fulfills the fantasy note of how strong he truly is.The story also diverges in a weird way - you are unable to access Super Vegeta and Super Trunks (Grade 3 Super Saiyan), however you can play as Super Vegeta 1 time AND you face him in training grounds combat. This bothered me because even though Super Vegeta isn't efficient compared to Super Saiyan 2, the level should be in between. If I can access Kaioken, I should have access to this, too, it's only fair.Post-game content is also very weird - we don't get to fight Spopovich, Yamu, or King Cold, we just kill henchmen, which is nothing but cakewalk at that point in the game.Otherwise, I loved the game and the post-game content was cool.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun. But, it has its caveats. To sum up my experience:Dragon Ball Z focused on both the story and the filler. Dragon Ball Z Kai focused on more of the story, less of the filler. Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot focused less on the story, more on the filler.DBZ offered a very balanced experienced and is the original after all. Would recommend watching. DBZ Kai still solid offered a solid experience with the voice acting and animation being a lot more refined than Z. Would recommend watching still. DBZ: Kakarot on the other hand still delivers the full story, but tends to skim on some of the details. If you've watched DBZ, then you will still enjoy this game as you get to play through the original story since it stays mostly true to the original. However, a good chunk of the details are omitted or skimmed over when it comes to delivery of the main story. I can't move with WASD *AND* hold the 'q' key *AND* press the '1' key all at the same time with my left hand, it's impossible.The obvious fix would be to move the modifier keys to the mouse, but lazy programming PURPOSELY blocks us from using any additional mouse keys such as mousebutton1, etc. I don't know how to compensate for all the dual-button presses on the left hand when you can't use ctrl, alt, or shift for them. This game was designed for a controller. If you don't have bumpers 1 and 2 on both left and right, using modifier keys on a keyboard isn't actually a functional design. They built it, but it's not actually functional... more like a fakearoo designed to trick Steam into thinking the game is actually keyboard compatable when it is in reality no such thing. EDIT: bought a freaking keyboard... and now this: 127 Hours in, and an update wiped my save files. Now some sync problem between Steam Cloud and my Local files mean that I have NO saves whatsoever and have to start from scratch. NEW EDIT, some 120 hours later and like a year later after a fresh install.Somehow the whole steam cloud sync thing wiped my Kakarot saves AGAIN. so... now I have to restart for a third time? Y'all really need to fix this.I will NOT be starting from scratch. FFFFFFFFFFF this freaking game to heck.

_childDocuments_.review: Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot revisits the main story from the Dragon Ball Z series. If you already know the main story from the show or manga, then most of the story will be familiar to you. There are substories present, but many of the ones I did were not interesting. There were some good ones though and there might be better ones that I have not done yet. The combat system felt a bit basic first, but as I gained more abilities, it became more fun. Moving around during combat also felt great. The random battles during exploration got in the way at times, especially when I was trying to complete objectives for a substory or when I was gathering materials. You can tackle enemies and auto complete battles if you are at least five levels higher than the enemy, but the battles still got in the way at times.Overall, if you are a fan of the Dragon Ball Z series or are familiar with the series, I recommend checking this game out. If you are unfamiliar with the series, you may want to watch the show or read the manga first. However, playing Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot can also be a good introduction to the series. However, just be aware some scenes have been cut out, which is more noticeable in the Android Saga and is very noticeable during the Buu Saga. I recommend getting the deluxe edition since it comes with the three major DLCs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fun, but not in an awe inspiring way. It was the generic dbz rpg fans had been requesting for a while, including side quests and main story and after story (with little side tracking for fishing, cooking and other activities) the gameplay has somewhere in 30-40 hrs of content. In some ways the combat is very punishing, in others it's very easy. WIth the later parts of the game becoming childishly easy. The combat is in the middlegrounds of simplistic and giving that tenkaichi or budokai feel. The combo remains the same, but you have some flexibility between surge mode, your skills, using support skills and support combo move, and dash, or combo and ki blast moves, but not a whole lot of variation. The enemies can become tedious, since they litter the map and will endlessly attack you, unless you overlevel them greatly and gain the ability to dash through them. The lack of variety in enemies is somewhat disappointing as well. With many assets reused, and instead of fighting certain characters, they just spawn in enemies that litter the map with no special mechanics for a very disappointing fight. I also had a feeling like later parts in the game (specifically the Buu saga) the cutscenes in "DBZ Kakarot the movie, the game" were a bit rushed or underdeveloped. Overall the game was enjoyable, but not something I would play a second time without another arc added in.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I’d like to say that I’m only at the Frieza saga, but so far, it is turning out to be amazing! I’ve been wanting a DBZ game just like this. No hate to the Xenoverse series, but it wasn’t exactly what I wanted out of a DBZ game. It’s awesome to relive my childhood by playing this game. Brings back so many memories, and instead of watching the episodes, I get to be a part of it.Okay..now to my thoughts on the game itself:• Graphics are great for what this game is, it’s like an actual episode of DBZ!•The voice acting is on point!•The fighting in the game seemed complicated at first, but just like every other fighting game, once you get used to the buttons and combos, you’ll be kicking butt like a true Saiyan!•The open world is exactly what I was looking for, especially when I’m cruising around on the flying nimbus.•Side quests are a plus too, I’m actually glad it’s not just a straightforward, main missions only game.That’s all I can really say about the game so far (work life gets in the way of game time, lol).I did have one frustration early on, and it happened when you fight your first “boss” if that’s what that fight was. My fighting was decent, but I was still getting the hang of the game itself. So, not knowing what certain things are meant for (menu stuff: orbs, community, etc.) It wasn’t until after the fight I realized that the orbs I gathered while flying around could be used to upgrade powers. Now I know, so my next fight were way better.In conclusion, DBZ Kakarot is a great game to start the year off with. If you are a fan of DBZ, any and all, I believe this game is worth the pick up. Buy it now, or wait till it’s on sale, in either case, get this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it during the summer sale. Glad I didn't buy it at full price.First off, I will say that I am one of the biggest Dragon Ball fans that you will meet. I collect the figures, actually read and own all the manga, seen the anime a stupid number of times, etc. All that said, I can not recommend this game, even after beating all the subquests and main game. I wanted to like this game, tried to go into it with as few expectations as possible, and tried to keep an open mind. - The cinematics  are redone versions of the anime with 3D graphics with much and reworded voice tracks; it is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cringy and frustrating to listen to. Eventually I ended up skipping through every single main quest video. Honestly would have been better just to splice in bits of the anime or at least kept the same voice tracks. - The subquests are ridiculously stupid and time consuming/tedious; a lot of it is item finding/fetch quests (not just the dragon balls, but stupid ♥♥♥♥ like minerals) and going from point A ---> point B ---> point A over and over again. It's like this game was designed to merely eat time rather than provide engaging entertainment. -The RPG aspects and levelling system is laughable. Not sure why this game has been so well received, it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ take on the franchise. -For a game called , the time spent playing as Goku is very minimal. Yes, I get that in the Buu saga playing as Gohan makes sense. However, there were several missed opportunities/glossed over points in the story which would have yielded very fun gameplay as Goku. The fact that they didn't do any missions/objectives related to the time training on King Kai's planet was a big oof. - The only redeemable aspects are the fighting mechanics; honestly just play xenoverse or DB FighterZ.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually?  Amazing.  Can look even better than some of the more recent episodes of the anime, and at times I swear I'm watching an anime and not playing a video game.  The nostalgia is strong, and I like how they brought back a lot of the older/forgotten characters.Otherwise?  Bad.  Suffers from the ol' 'tries to do too many RPG-ish things and as a result all the RPG-ish elements are borderline useless.'  IE Food-eating getting you permanent and temporary boosts is a really good idea, and totally fitting into the DBZ world.  However, am I going to waste time taking the 15 seconds to talk to ChiChi and cook each individual dish for a +1500 hp boost from a main course when I already have 20 million health?  The answer is no.The combat can be annoying as balls, too.  Some fights are ridiculous without healing (most prominently is fighting high-powered versions of Vegeta/Nappa/Raditz, who have ridiculous 'everywhere attacks' as a team).  And if you use healing, of course you're going to win.  No cooldowns on healing items, you can just spam yourself up to full everytime you need to since it's instantaneous. Dragon Balls can easily net you 30k money which will easily buy many of the best healing items.  Even without them, you end up picking up so many items you can sell to easily buy a ton of healing, and if you have enough you can get through any fight.There's also no way to tell for sure if leveling up is even worth it.  Your character undergoes so many power ups (as is typical and expected from this) that it seems like if I had waited to level up before a big power boost, perhaps I would've had even more stats upon leveling up after said power boost.  No way to know for sure by just playing the game.

This is easily the BEST game if you want to really feel that power rush of dropping a Big Bang Attack on a group of Frieza Soldiers. _childDocuments_.review: A complete re-telling of the events of DBZ all the way up to the end. It's mostly done true to the original story, with some things changed to fit in with the game in terms of fillers and how drawn out it is. There's a couple of iconic things missing like the "over 9000" line from Vegeta and some other bits here and there, and it would be nice if those were in but doesn't really change much in the end. However, the game often skips over pretty major things like Goku getting Instant Transmission and nothing being done with it in terms of combat. Vegeta and Trunks becoming Super Saiyan (2) are just glossed over. And then on the other end of the spectrum they added Goku getting his driver's license, down to the same color of the cars.The combat is fine and isn't anything groundbreaking. Some of the bosses really mash out their supers quite a bit and it looks like they have hyper armor pretty much the whole time. This can get annoying and shoehorns you into mashing the same moves to stun them as well. Overall, the combat does the trick and most of the iconic moves and scenes are included.The bigger issue are the ridiculously large amount of script errors. Subs that don't even match up with the english lines, a plethora of grammatical and spelling errors, and some bugs with duplicate voice lines or characters having the wrong voice/line. For example, Recoome has Jeice's voice (and the subs say "Guys!") when they introduce themselves. Shortly after Recoome's line, Jeice says the same line. The game should not have been released with the script in this state. This was clearly a rush job, since CC2's prior games were polished.Overall? A mediocre game suffering from some bugs and a lot of translation/script issues. Play this if you want to relive the whole DBZ story through a bunch of pre-rendered cutscenes and some okay fighting. Do not play this if you're looking for involved and technical combat in a DBZ game, or if you're a newcomer to the franchise.EDIT: Revised review to reflect my gameplay past the Frieza saga. Changed from okay game to mediocre game. Still recommend it since it's overall enjoyable, but only for true fans. Best to wait after the bugs are fixed and maybe they do a proper QA on the translation.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the late Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball, Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot is an excellent open-world format game where you can play as Goku, Gohan, Piccolo, Vegeta, and Future Trunks, sadly the other characters are support only, so you are unable to directly play as Krillin or Yamcha. This game was fantastic, but there were a few inaccuracies to the story, but besides that, I have no problems with this game. The DLCs are also a lot of fun. I highly recommend this game to fans of Dragon Ball and/or anime. Rest easy, Toriyama-Sensei!

_childDocuments_.review: Embodies the anime visually and thematically. Battles are stunning and fought with a staggering sense of scale, a frenetic pace and techniques that let you feel as powerful as Goku, Vegeta and Gohan ought to feel. Limited RPG mechanics, clumsy camera control while free-roaming, uninspired side quests and lack of end game content detract from an otherwise spectacular experience. The enjoyment of this game stems largely from the nostalgia DBZ: Kakarot exudes as it beautifully captures the most iconic battles and transformation from the show.As a pure game, 7.5/10. As a nostalgia boner for DBZ fans, especially those who grew up on Toonami, this game is a 9/10 and will only improve with DLC addition of the time machine to replay old battles/side missions.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks and sounds good, for the most part, but that's all I can really say about it 13 hours in. The gameplay itself is very shallow, with one button for basic attacks, another for ki attacks, and then hold buttons for supers, supports, and transformations. Gathering materials for cooking is uninteresting grind, and travel feels slow and clunky. I honestly hoped for more out of this.If you really want to play this, at least wait for a sale. There's no point to paying top dollar for this.

_childDocuments_.review: I've got a couple hours in. I am farther along on PS4, but let's be real....PC is home. The game is a great play for anyone into the DBZ universe. Is the game overly complicated? No. Is it going to win game of the decade? Nope. Is this game a fun way to interact with a fan-loved franchise in a different way? Yes.The graphics are subtle but still awesome to look at (let's be honest, a realistic looking Goku may just be too weird). The combat is really simple, but I find the longer I play to more ways I find to mix up the style. The game contains basic rpg elements which isn't a bad thing. Having said how fun the game can be, I don't see the full price tag as being justified. Keep in mind I'm only a few hours in, so read other reviews about end game thoughts. This is a must grab if it's on sale; especially if you are looking to just turn off and relax with the Z warriors.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a solid Dreamcast title. I mean that in the best way possible.So many game mechanics. There's combat, flying/running around, car customization and racing, cooking, a card game, a skill system, a board system, and more I'm forgetting. It has so many things in. Most of is good, and everything that's kind of okay is optional. All that's missing is a Chao Garden minigame.The combat is competent. It's lots of fun 1v1, group-vs-group, or you and friends vs a single enemy. Fighting by yourself against multiple enemies sort falls apart into frustrating chaos. Fortunately, it's not often or it's tied to an optional training (which you can level up and do later more easily). If I had to complain, I'd say the boss fights up to Frieza are more challenging and have fun gimmicks to deal with. They taper off after that. The combat lets you do all the classic fight abilities. I keep thinking "This game would have been ahead of its time if it were made in 1999."I never did the car customization or racing (outside of a required story mission) - and even then, it's a decent racing mini-game. The game is not challenging (most of the time), so I never dabbled with eating.The upgrades are fun, especially the forms (Super Saiyain, etc). The story is DBZ. If you're looking to play through the story of the show, this game delivers. There are a lot of optional side quests that bring back characters from the original Dragon Ball show too. The voice acting is great, but the sound effects undercut the scenes sometimes. All the new music feels true to the show. I just wish they broke up the cutscenes into smaller chunks. I'll be watching a boring scene, skip, and next thing I know, I've begun fighting a Saga-ending villain. I'm super glad I can skip scenes though, but I'd be pulling my hair out of I had to watch it all each playthrough.It looks like the show. It's not the most technically impressive game, but because of that, it doesn't run like garbage (*cough GTA Definitive Edition cough*). It runs as well as you'd expect Half-Life (1999) to run on a modern PC.It's not perfect, but I recommend anyone who is a fan of the show to try it.

_childDocuments_.review: More like "Dragon Ball Z : Gohan" for obvious reason.Overall a pretty good DBZ game for both old fans and casual newcomers as it tells the story from the beginning of Saiyan Saga till the end of Majin Buu saga. But not only that , it's open-world element also allows player to explore the world of Dragon Ball , visiting iconic locations as well as interacting with familiar faces from the original series before Z and help them out in sub stories which give this game some laid back adventure element that Z was missing.Combat is simplified compare to Xenoverse and most story related fights won't be too hard unless you are severely underleveled. Completing Sub stories give you a lot of EXP and therefore you won't have to grind for EXP with mobs in the open world.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy JRPG mini games (fishing, fetch quests, "relationship management", alot of text collectibles) and want to do those in the DBZ universe this is definitely the game to play.If you like RPGs, open world, and action there was none of that in the time I played it.Pros:- It seems like they got the original voice actors for the english voices. Good voice acting- Nice soundtrack- The art style is very DBZ- The fighting system seems fairly easy and visually impressive. There are a few button combinations to remember but in the two fights I had it did not matter how much I just tested out the controls and still easily won.Cons:- Tutorials are  "here's a list of things you can do" without any progression or helping you getting used to them. E.g. the tutorial fight a minute into the game is "this is the list of buttons you have during fighting. Now beat Picolo". - Not open world! The first quest in this game is you having to follow Gohan around collecting apples. You cannot leave a small designated area.- Boring and annoying quests. The second quest in the game after collecting the apples with Gohan is to follow Gohan to a fishing spot. While Gohan walks VERY slowly to the quest marker, you cannot leave his side or he will stop and start crying.- Not every conversation is voice acted (e.g. the first side-quest). These conversations are only done in speach bubbles, and to make that worse the characters have short voice clips at the start of every line that get repeated seemingly at random.- Bad character animations outside of combat. Any conversation is only done in pretty much speach bubbles with the characters just standing next to each other.- I did not even get to the end of the first Anime episode after 1,3 hrs because of constant interruption of gameplay by introducing (as far as I played) useless game elements.

_childDocuments_.review: It's high time players played the anime...oh, well. DBZ: Kakarot does what the name suggests; an expansive story, straight from the anime, RPG gameplay with battle elements, U4 engine graphics and remixed anime music (the Japanese one, mind you). Playing the game has so far made me walking down the memory lane - and that feels great. About 2 hours in the game, looking forward to spending more.For some reason, the game did not allow me to change to the highest resolution, something that forced me to go to the -ini file and tamper the settings. However, apart from that, everything is optimal. There is keyboard/mouse support as well, one of the pluses. The control system might seem  a bit off at first, but eventually players can get used to it. Characters, lore, series encyclopedia are among the positives as well. If only we didn't have these horrible orbs, everything else would have been much better.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game, I've been playing it for weeks now trying to get 100% achievements. Slow process for me since I really only get an hour here and there if I get any time after work at all.Pros:- I like the simple combat system, since I play after work I am typically too tired to figure out too many button combos and what not- I am just a fan of the old school DBZ story, this reminds me of playing Legacy Of Goku I and II and Buu's Fury for the GBA, except its the higher graphic 3D version 12-14 year old me had dreamed of- I liked the soul emblem system for gaining extra bonuses, I may be weird because I know others hated it, but I liked messing with stuff to improve my set up- The extra sub stories added a certain freshness to the overall story, however (see the mehs)The mehs- Some of the sub stories get stale, IE some dude is clearly bad, summon robots to fight off, they are surprised you beat the robots and run away- They missed an opportunity to have more movie content (I want my Gogeta Janemba fight!)- Z Orbs after a point didn't feel like they mattered because I was getting so many nothing was stopping me from progressing through the skill treeCons- NO.... POST GAME... FUSION. Look I don't know how, and I don't care how, but I want to be able to pointlessly fuse into Vegito/Gogeta/Gotenks to destroy random overworld mobsEDIT: - Only a con if you don't like the combat to feel too easy, but I highly recommend you finish everything in the base game and the deluxe content (Bonyu and training room stuff) before you start any DLC. You gain so many levels doing that stuff, going back and finishing up stuff in the base game is just... mind numbing and boring. This might not bother you though

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best Dragon Ball games I've played to date. The storyline starts off a little before the actual anime story on DBZ and contains more scenes than the anime also.A lot of the main storyline isn't dragged out like it was in the series and some of the main storyline is just different compared to the series. One example is when Goku reaches King Kai's, the monkey and cricket are no where to be found (until later in CS's), Goku stands perfect upright and doesn't mention the gravity difference between there and Earth. Aside from the small differences, the storyline is just as great as the series.The voice actors are pretty similar to the original ones, but a few of our favorite characters seem to be a little different. The main characters seem to be the same, but some of the villains are different, but it's not a big deal breaker.I really like the layout and the fighting techniques. It's more RPG layed out than a fighter game. The open world experience and the side quests, along with many other things to do in the game, make this game that much funner imo.If you enjoyed the anime series, you'll enjoy this game just as much. _childDocuments_.review: If you are a Dragon Ball fan you may have played through the Saiyan sage through to Buu a fair few times already, but I would say this is the best way to play that journey again. If you've ever played the Legacy of Goku trilogy then you can recognise this as the ultimate remake of those games.While I can see why some people would find it tedious, I've actually really enjoyed flying around the overworld collecting the orbs you need to level/rank up your abilities. Whether this will change or not as I rack up the hours in this game is to be seen, at 10 hours I am not fed up yet.While the models for the characters are great, the overworld can look a bit lacklustre up close. The attacks are beautifully done but they can overwhelm the screen some what. As an epileptic I need to highly recommend to the devs to have an option to disable bloom because I've had to walk away for a bit after a longer fight where big effects are tossed around.The combat is simple and fun but can have a bit of depth, the thing that will disappoint some people however is that the depth is entirely unnecessary. Once you've levelled up to be just slightly above the enemy you can just mash the melee button and launch the occasional super attack.Overall, if you are a Dragon Ball fan I would call this game a must play. Seeing some of the side arcs get some love brings back some happy memories of Saturday mornings watching Goku and Piccolo learning to drive cars. Seeing some of the most iconic scenes in all of anime beautifully rendered in HD is also a real joy that I imagine most fans will not be able to stop themselves smiling at.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 2 hours in and after looking at other reviews I can see the complaint about the fighting mechanics, however on the flip side I think people expected a different type of game than what I believe the game claimed to be. Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot is not a strictly centered fighting game, even though it has elements similar to it's arena brothers. What Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot is in actuality much closer to a 3D version of the Legacy of Goku games with it's simple fighting mechanics, exp grinding, item collecting, quest and world exploration. The game is a completely different beast from the Xenoverse and Tenkaichi games. The game at it's heart is an open world JRPG, so if you enjoy playing through the story of Dragon Ball Z as a JRPG rather than a fighting game then I believe you will be content with it. However if you are buying it in hopes of holding you over for Xenoverse 3 then you will very likely be disappointed by the fighting aspect of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I liked the game a lot. It's not perfect by any means. That said, I thoroughly enjoyed myself for the entirety of the game. The combat system can be a bit off at first, but soon enough you learn how to counter enemies attacks with specific ones of your own, and it actually becomes really fun. Now, this isn't like a triple A title, mind you. The systems in the game can be a bit janky, and I got some slowdown at points running on a Ryzen 5 with an RTX 2080. Why? I have no clue. This isn't the most visually complex game, so I think parts of it may have been a bit rushed. You will get tired of fetch quests, but you will have to do them because they are almost guaranteed to level up your character when a million fights against random baddies give you dirt XP. In spite of all this, the game's strength is that the story of Dragonball Z shines through it all. The world and the events feel dead on, with proper weight and significance given to almost every important moment in the series. I have been a fan since I was in junior high, watching the Saiyan Saga and half the Frieza saga on repeat for years before we got the rest of the series in the states. I am now 35 years old, and this game really just takes me back to all the amazing excitement I felt when I was a kid. It highlights not only the cool stuff, but also the heartfelt moments of Dragonball that made you feel as if the stakes couldn't get any higher. If you are like me, and just have a soft spot in your heart for DBZ, you will grumble a bit but ultimately walk away feeling as if you had a blast with the game. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT

_childDocuments_.review: Great if you want to relive classic dragon ball z moments and you want to skip all the anime filler, so don't expect entire dragon ball episode cut scenes, all the important stuff is there and you can skip the cringy bits if you want to. For me the open world filler was a bit tedious but necessary to level up each characters progression tree, I don't care much for crafting and resource collection. It took me 35 hours to finish the main story, I don't bother with 100% completion so there could be somethings I missed after completing the story. To scratch my dragon ball itch I finished the Buu saga, and then watched Dragon Ball Super and the 2 recent anime films.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for people who love the grinding aspect of a true RPG. It is still a new game so all of the minor bugs are to be expected early on and it seems the developers are doing a great job at listening to reports and addressing those issues with patch updates. The only issue I have is a very tiny technical oversight that is more of a personal wishlist so it would not affect my overall 1-10 rating. I wish they could add the ability to somehow pause and access the main menu when you initially start a new game. There are several times I have accidentally hit new game and then have to either force shut the program down or have to play through the tutorial battle just to be able to access the main menu and get back to the title screen.
_childDocuments_.name: DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid, I loved the Legacy of Goku trilogy (well, first one not as much). So when I heard about this game, I was hyped but never found the time to get it. Now that I have, I can say it met my expectations and then some. Lot of stuff to do, skills to acquire, quests to fulfill, plus it encapsulates the entirety of the series in a good 30-40 hour run. Only downside is the final saga is a bit linear at times and that kind of is where the main game starts to wear its welcome a tad, but thankfully not by much. The combat also can be a bit annoying in terms of whether to dodge/block or use specials, but it's not very difficult at all if you come prepared. I spent about 2-3 hours doing previous quests I missed out on before I got to work on endgame and realized I had played for five hours in one sitting. I guess that's an indication of how addicting this game is.If you're a die hard Dragon Ball fan, or want to learn about it in video game format, this is a perfect way to (re)experience it. Strong recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot is an incredible game because while it certainly has its issues, it's pure flipping fun for any DBZ fan.It's not going to win any awards for its graphics, combat system, RPGness, or storytelling.   Graphically they rely quite a bit on shiny lighting and there's some oddities like how character auras don't change to fit their transformations.  The combat system does have a bit of depth to it, including some bits they don't really tell you, but overall it's focused more on making fights look/feel good rather than trying to be something with a competitive skill curve.  The RPG elements are kind of light in nature - except for possibly the post-game, grinding really isn't necessary nor is it wise to waste time on, but there's enough there to have some degree of depth to dig into with the Community Board system and learning/upgrading skills.  Story-wise the game is comprehensive for sure, doing a great job of covering all the key story moments in DBZ, but it's done in an abridged manner and they definitely take shortcuts when they can (i.e. no "over nine thousand" scene since that just eats up time).   What this game really shines at though is encapsulating the whimsical fun nature of the Dragon Ball franchise while still capturing the tension and serious moments throughout DBZ's story.  Also fanservice.  Lots, and lots, of fanservice.  From collecting memory items that reminisce back to Dragon Ball days to seeing folks like Eighter and Raditz commenting on Goku's resemblance to Bardock, this game feels like THE singleplayer story-based game for fans of the series.  Running around in the world environments is fun, and something that really hadn't been done in a DBZ game quite this way.  Between the main story moments you get side quests here and there, often bringing back old characters or attempting to fill in details on questions folks might have.  The stuff to do in the game isn't enormous, but there's enough of it to keep you busy if you choose to pursue that stuff.  Intermissions give you time to kind of just breathe and have some fun flying around/doing side-content before moving onto the next saga.  Xenoverse players might also raise an eyebrow with a certain type of side content, aka 'Villainous' enemies appear in the game after a point.  Let's just say that the game doesn't completely end with Buu.  All-in-all this is a game that's been much-needed for awhile now - one that just oozes with fanservice and bringing folks into the world of Dragon Ball's Z era without trying to have a competitive multiplayer component.  It certainly has some rough spots, and it's likely not going to convince non-DBZ fans to buy into it, but it's such a wonderful joyride for anyone who loves Dragon Ball.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:  The game is fun, if you don't care about the story you can speed through dialogue and skip cutscenes to get to the gameplay faster.My full thoughts.In my opinion the good far outweighs the bad, and I use the term "bad" loosely.  There's nothing explicitly bad only things that could've been done better.  There's a lot to do without it feeling bloated.  The game isn't stingy with the "rare" items.  They're JUST rare enough to make you not want to waste them, but still common enough to where you don't feel like you have to farm areas for an hour just to see 1 or 2 items.  The gameplay is smooth if somewhat basic.  However, in the case of this game, basic works in its favor since you don't have to remember combos to pull off special moves, you don't have to be at full power to trigger Super Saiyan so you can then go into SS2.  The story itself is a complete retelling of DBZ.  That's it.The stuff that could've been done better.  You know how annoying it was when bosses could give themselves super armor was in Xenoverse?  Apply that to this game AND throw in basic trash mobs being able to do it.  They can unstun themselves while in the middle of your attack and knock you out of your attack.  Some attacks have quick cutscene animations that trigger when you perform them, time for you doesn't stop this happens meaning you'll come out of that cutscene to find the mob up in your face already pounding on you.  Worst case you come out of it, and have already been interrupted out of the attack.  Bosses also have cutscene attacks and time DOES stop for them, and it will automatically stop your current attack when they pull it off.  It can be really annoying when they spam these attacks.  For a game named after Kakarot, you don't actually play as him very often.  You'll spend the bulk of your time as Gohan, Piccolo, or Vegeta.  The Namek Saga feels empty as there's not much to do besides the main story, and this saga is extremely linear with the way it railroads you into each mission.  The Buu Saga is EXTREMELY cutscene heavy.  I'm talking about going into a 20 minute cutscene, come out for a 3 minute fight to right back into another 3 minute fight and back into a 20-25 minute cutscene.  I'm not being hyperbolic at one point I actually paid attention.Some final thoughts.Always use Consecutive Energy Blast over Rapid Fire Ki-wave.  On paper they do the same thing.  But they function differently, CEB is better in every aspect.Vegeta is the best character to play as.  His Big Bang Attack comes out faster than Goku's Spirit Bomb making it more versitile in combat as Spirit Bomb needs a 2 or 3 second animation first.  Though Spirit Bomb EX can hit enemies multiple times as it seems to do damage every few frames.Gohan is boring to play as.  He has no unique skills, and doesn't get access to Consescutive Energy Blast.

_childDocuments_.review: 30hrs of game play to complete entire game.No tournaments to continue fighting in? Idk one of the major features the genre had to offer and no where to be found. Disappointing.Theres a bunch of mini games that are great for children. For people who grew up with DBZ... they take 2 brain cells to complete. Just created to waste your time.4 arcs: vs Vegeta. vs Frieza vs Cell and vs Buu. Wow that sounds familiar, almost like this is just a remaster and not a new game sold as "kakarot"Speaking of that, for a game that advertises its all about Goku. You dont play him very much. I actually had Gohan 15lvls higher than goku/vegeta by end game. Glitches... for a game thats a remaster or close enough. There are far to many glitches in this game.Open world, mostly useless. 3 things total. Annoying npcs that dont pertain anything to the plot (they literally let you run over them and count it as a win after your high enough lvl, this shows they know their garbage adds.)Finding dragon balls, which are pointed out to you pin point plots. So you literally dont look for them u just grab them..And collecting orbs. Which at first you may think "oh cool a decent feature that I need to attend." - No. By frieza saga they are useless. USELESS. By end game I had 100k extra of each one just from completing fights. I literally couldnt get rid of them fast enough no matter how hard I tried.My personal favorite to show they didnt care much about the game. During the buu saga they show dende grown up, like 5ft tall. And during the last cinematic they reverted him back to a kid from frieza saga... If that doesnt say this game is a joke idk what does. The only thing it had banking for it was cinematics and it literally messed up the last one due to them rushing it. Theres plenty of stuff like this throughout the game.Lastly no challenge. The lvling system messed the game up so hard. If you take on a lvl to high u only do 1 damage to the npc  and if your to high you one shot things. If your the same lvl you only take a small amount of dmg. Unless of course you use a special talent that gives you 40% dmg increase but "decreases health slowly" - Biggest joke in the game. It was literally doing more damage to me than npcs by about 3-5x as much. The only challenge was when you had 3-5 npcs higher lvl than you spamming attacks all at once non stop, which isnt a challenge but rather just poorly designed fight mechanics... because you cant react, your character just takes all the damage if you get caught once.This game is created as a nice relaxing time waster. People are trying to highlight the RPG side but its ♥♥♥♥. Theyre just complacent because its better than nothing. Its been awhile since we had a legitimate DBZ story arc campaign game. The previous game before this did an amazing job for its genre. Why did they drop the ball so hard on this one? I will never understand it.

_childDocuments_.review: What is a ? An RPG. One that faithfully recreates the story of Dragon Ball Z, in the most pleasant of ways, but isn't without its faults. In-depth storytelling and cutscene direction that's actually worth a buck. Kakaroto's take on each and every saga, & some of their most iconic beats, have been, for the most past, faithfully recreated alongside a soundtrack that's been lifted straight from the show.Visuals be no slouch either (albeit some "engine.ini" tweaking was required to tone down the crappy bloom), attention to detail is abundant throughout, and the sheer amount of love and care put onto some of the most iconic landmarks is tangible.Speaking of maps, the game's been divided into a dozen or so explorable area's, and they've been sized just right. Not one is either too big and empty or too little and claustrophobic. Traveling from one side to the other is often a quick affair.Character modeling is on another level though. Each boasting crazy high polys and all intricately detailed.The more you progress through the story, train, and attain new moves & transformations, the greater, more impactful your actions will be. Some to the point of brokenness, like the maxed out versions Vegie's Big Bang Attack, Goku's Spirit Bomb. It's amusing.There are two distinct types of "currency" (kind of), and each serves its distinct purpose.Zeni (money). You earn it by farming for ingredients (meat, fish, spices, vegetables, fruit...), minerals, mechanical parts, even gifts (which can be used to upgrade your community boards), and all can be sold for prices of the variable type.Z balls (of which there are 6 types in total), easy to come by, they're scattered everywhere & can be used to upgrade your skill trees.With that said, there's one set of special balls to collect, 7 of them actually, and these are of the wish guaranteeing type. They allow you to ask for severe amounts of all of the above. Or you can wish your enemies back to life. Like Rasditz and Napa. King Cold and The Gunyu Force. ...and so on. These "what ifs" are the best kind of side mission you can get.Skill trees too. Unlocking more and new upgradable slots/techniques (ones specifically marked by an icon), requires the beating of training sessions. But to beat each training course, one must be at a similar level as of the required. Which wouldn't be too much to ask.Problem is, reaching higher levels, needs story progression, and even though farming's a bit of a requirement (but not overly imposed), what comes out of it the most, is Z Balls, maybe some items, but not much else. Generic battle encounters, other than Vilaneus Enemies (and even those), barely give any meaningful amount of XP, making all of the leveling process, feel not only a tad little bit on-rails, but never truly satisfying.Speaking of battles. The game's severely lacking in enemy variety. Each random encounter (can usually be avoided) consists of the same 2 or 3 types of robots, a drone or two, and colour swapped Frieza soldiers. Not fun. Combat in of itself, ain't anything to write home about... It's fluid and does the job, but is simple and button mashy, which leaves a lot to be desired given the game's colossal size.Sub Stories, aka, side missions. They serve their purpose and earn the player decent amounts of XP. At their best, they give insight on the littlest of details, raging from early Dragon Ball to later Z, even some the most obscure facts are thrown around.But they're just not fun, and can be divided into 2 types. It's either, go there and fight the same random enemies over and over. Or... go there and collect some rare items. Maybe a mix of both if lucky.It's a bore fest, really.Menus, menus, and more menus! Oh man... There's a butt load of them and they never go away. The more you play, the more chapters you beat, the more menus you get introduced to!It got odd, fast... and for each one, a pop-up tutorial or two. Speaking of tutorials, they're everywhere, for everything you do, for everything you earn, for everything you unlock, you get a random tutorial pop-up for it, constantly breaking the flow of the game.Making Kakaroto's all the more confusing, a lot of it overlaps after a while, making it hard to keep up.What about battle buffs? Oh my... You can get some characters to make you the most delightful meals, and each meal earns you exclusive buffs of variable stats and duration. But the problem stems from the fact that there's just too many, each requiring all sorts of ingredients, some more common than others.Some cutscenes suffer from pre-render syndrome, and their resolution was capped at 1080p & rendered at the lowest possible bitrate imaginable.Kakaroto's a long, long game, that tells the story of DBZ exceptionally well, and is fully loaded with fan service, but falls short of being truly great.Therefore earning a rEvo's rating of 6/10.
