_childDocuments_.review: I've gotten to the beginning of the Android/Cell Arc. 9/10The Good: Incredible game. This is everything childhood/teenage me has wanted from a Dragon Ball Z game. Sure it's fun having a fighting game with a huge roster, but this is a lovingly created adaption of the anime, does away with filler content and adapts the material to justify the shorter charge times for attacks with a notoriously long charging time such as spirit bomb. The game itself is fun, and has enough systems and content to keep you busy and entertained for hours on end. The scenes are lovingly adapted and are both humorous and contain an emotional punch that I dare say the anime never quite did.The Bad:So my first critique is simply because I enjoy the game so much that i wish there were more of it. I would have loved to see more side quests, the ones they have are great, but they don't have much punch to them. I think they would've done very well adapting content from the DBZ films and featuring villains from those films such as Garlic Jr., Bojack, or Android 13. The of the main story of the game would have been well served if it included film characters such as Cooler or Broly.Really I could settle for just Broly. I feel he is an essential part of the Saiyan mythos and always makes an incredible secret boss, or a great opponent to face at the end of a side-quest chain. I feel Cooler is also important to the Frieza, King-Cold Mythos however I understand his omission as a writer myself.Next, we get to the numbers. Many developers have become acutely aware of the absurdly high numbers involved in many video game RPG systems. Unfortunately this is not a strong point, while the numbers in regards to experience and such start out in the hundreds they quickly spiral out of control and you will find yourself recieving 10's and then 100's of 1000's of EXP early on. A number squish would serve this well, though I will cede that it is a thematically appropriate choice to allow your characters to recieive millions of experience points. Simply put it quickly becomes difficult to calculate how long you have until your next level because they are flashing massive numbers on your screen for short periods of time and you will often jump several levels in over the course of a single story battle.Z-Orbs, while an interesting element, become quickly irrelevant. If you spend a moderate amount of time grinding, you will quickly find yourself with more Z-orbs than you can spend.IN CONCLUSION:Amazing Game, 9/10 I would pay good money for DLC that incorporates classic DBZ film characters, i'd pay double for a DLC that incorporates Cooler and Broly into the main story.  I definitely got a little emotional when Frieza murdered Krillin.

_childDocuments_.review: I have experienced countless games that have tried to capture the essence of their source material, but none have quite reached the pinnacle of perfection like Dragon Ball Z Kakarot. This title not only pays homage to the beloved series but also delivers a gaming experience that is both innovative and thrilling. It is a true testament to the developers' understanding of what makes Dragon Ball Z so special.The game's astonishing graphics are a sight to behold. The characters are rendered with an exceptional level of detail, and their movements are fluid and true to the anime. Even the most intricate of battle sequences are brought to life with such precision that one cannot help but marvel at the visual spectacle. The game's environments are equally stunning, providing a vibrant and immersive backdrop that transports players to the Dragon Ball Z universe.But the true genius of Dragon Ball Z lies in its gameplay. The developers have crafted an intricate and rewarding combat system that caters to both newcomers and seasoned fans alike. Players can execute a variety of moves, including combos, special attacks, and transformations, allowing them to fully embody their favorite characters. The game also boasts an impressive roster of fighters.The story mode, however, is where the game truly shines even more! The developers have managed to distill the essence of the anime's epic narrative into an interactive experience that is both engaging and emotionally resonant. The pacing is expertly crafted, and the game's story arcs are faithful to the source material. Each pivotal moment is presented with a cinematic flair that rivals even the best adaptations in the industry. This game allows players to relive their cherished memories of the series while forging new ones within its digital realm.In conclusion, Dragon Ball Z Kakarot is an absolute masterpiece, earning a well-deserved 5/5 rating. Its captivating gameplay, breathtaking graphics, and enthralling storyline make it a must-play for fans and newcomers alike. The developers have not only paid tribute to the iconic series, but they have also elevated the gaming experience to a whole new level. Dragon Ball Z is, without a doubt, the perfect way to relive old memories and create new ones in the process.I paid $14.99 on a flash sale... looks like you can purchase it for $21.24 at the time of this review. _childDocuments_.review: Nostalgia tells me thumbs up and 4/5Sadly, it's barely worthy of 3/5I enjoyed the first half of the game with as much enthusiasm as the anime. It's incredibly fun to relive the DBZ sagas with your own hands. The open world exploration is simple, but just fun enough to push you to want to 100% the game. I have yet to get in vehicle building or the dlc, but have completed the main game with a few achievements to go, all in all, around 50 hours.I purchased this game on Steam instead of Xbox thinking I would have better video and optimization options. I was sorely mistaken. This game is a bad console port, with minimal settings and horrible mouse and keyboard optimization. There's a constant glow coming from the sun that washes out the game. There are ways to fix that in the .ini file, but how many kids are looking that up. One thing that hindered the immersion was the lack of voice acting at times. Even the main characters have many instances where they're grunting at each other as you click through reading their dialogue. I was still interested in the game going into the Buu Saga. There seemed to be a sudden increase in cut scenes, most of which you have to click through the dialogue yourself (sounds insignificant, but it gets extremely annoying). Cut scene, fight, cut scene, fight, cut scene, fight. This switch to a more cinematic theme, with minimal story explanation eradicated the small amount of RPG that was left in the game. I understand there's post game content and endless training, but I missed the open world freedom I had in the beginning, and felt rushed through the end of the game.A fun, nostalgic experience that I will complete soon. Just extremely let down by the lack of customization options, poor graphic quality for pc, and the lack of voice acting throughout. Could have been done better, but I loved replaying my favorite childhood anime; so there's that.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I have only finished the Cell saga, but I have played ~35 hours. With Buu's saga I could imagine playing for another 15-35 hours.If you're a DBZ fan, this game is fantastic. I haven't played a DBZ game since Budokai Tenkaichi, but this is by far the closest a video game has come to replicating the experience of watching the anime for me. In some cases, it even enhances the experience. However, if you're not a DBZ fan, the game does suffer in a few aspects. Pros:1) Combat is great, but simple. 2) Story and cutscenes are beautiful when playing through the main quests. 3) Developers stayed true to the source material and even included photographs to recall events that occurred in Dragonball. This made me so happy to see. It warms my heart whenever I find these.4) Great character customization.5) Absolutely LOVE the community system. It's my favorite new RPG element. The community system allows you to link together character emblems based on their prior lore interactions. (For example Goku and Gohan can link because they are father and son). This system makes you think about character relationships and lets play a unique board game to gain bonuses. Cons (I'll try to be unbiased here):1) Too many enemies floating around each area. Gets annoying, kinda like Zubats from Pokemon inside of Mt. Moon. Would be less annoying if there were more enemy variation from the beginning. (Plenty of enemy variety by the time you get to the Cell saga). You can insta-kill enemies by charging at them, but you need to be 5-7 levels above them.2) Combat is simple. This is only an issue because of #1 on this list. There are constant battles, so it would have been nice to see more complexity. 3) Side quests are kind of boring at times, but I feel obligated to complete them because they provide emblems for the community. The main thing that makes them boring is that they often are defaulted to fighting the same 3 robots that you encounter endlessly while flying through the early-game areas. Would have been nice to see more variety. 4) Levels matter, but grinding for them is pointless. The main story quests level you up to whatever level the game needs you to be. This gives the game a "pseudo-RPG" feel because normal RPG elements don't really apply. I don't personally mind this leveling system, but because the game sold itself on being an RPG experience, I'll include this as a con. Regardless of the negatives I mentioned, I have not been able to put this game down since I got it. If that doesn't tell you what you need to know, then I don't know what will. Get the game if you're a fan. This is a game for the fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Gosh, where to begin. Thought Kakarot for sure couldnt top Xenoverse 2 but damn it does.If you thought this was just another game to play through the dbz storyline, you are partly correct.But this game is so much more. Being semi-open world gives rise to unique and nostalgic conversations.Graphics are top-notch, combat feels fun and your connection to characters for some reason feels much better than you would expect.Played the future trunks DLC too, dreat job by the devs there. The extra parts after the android saga (not shown in the anime) is a treat and hits hard. Going through the DBS arcs now and might/might not change this review.Overall- Fantastic and well developed/directed. Cant wait to play more
_childDocuments_.name: DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! Finally a proper DBZ RPG game like I have always wanted. For the small amount I've already played I'm really enjoying it. It's more focused on the story and rpg elements than the combat which I think is a nice change. Although the combat is still great and everything looks stunning! Being a huge DB fan it's a great game to experience it all again while being able to actually play it. Sure it's not perfect but it's a great stepping stone to future possibilities we could have!Recommend it for old and new fans. Explains a lot of the story so great to play even if you haven't seen the anime/manga

_childDocuments_.review: Best Dragonball game so far, by a large margin. This is a great way to experience the Dragonball Z story and play through it as if you were watching the tv show. The open world and lite RPG mechanics make for some easy going fun gameplay in between the cinematics and fights. I haven't finished the main storyline, but seeing all the Dragonball pick ups that fill you in on some of the backstory from the original show, makes me really wish they'd do this same game for Dragonball so you could play through that story and then into Dragonball Z. I agree that combat isn't the most amazing, but as someone who wanted to play more for the strict story adherence campaign, it has just enough depth and forgiveness to make some fights challenging enough to feel rewarding but easy enough to just breeze through when just wanting to enjoy the story.
_childDocuments_.name: DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is in my opinion one of the best games ive played. Each time i start this game up i get hyped!It follows the story of our childhood hero Kakarot.It goes from the Saiyan saga all the way to the Buu saga! (without 10.000 hours in the Namek saga) (God i hated those fillers)If you are a fan of the series, its Definitely worth your money and time.Im 31 hours in and im at the Buu saga. There is loads to do in this game like Fishing with a strap-on tail, Punching animals to get meat. Shooting Ki blasts on dinosaurs so they cant hit you.During your way through the game you can find some photos of the old dragonball series which i think is awesome addition to the game since i enjoyed Dragonball as well!Thank you for making this game, and i cant wait to see the DLC'S!!TLDR; Buy this game if you wanne relive your childhood

_childDocuments_.review: Akira Toriyama (1955-2024). Known most especially for the Dragon Ball Franchise, he brought such laughter and excitement to so many people through his work, not only in Dragon Ball (1984-2024), but also in: Dr. Slump (1980-1984), Dragon Quest (1986-2024), Chrono Trigger (1995), Blue Dragon (2006-2007), Kajika (1998), Cowa! (1997-1998), and Sandland (2000, 2024). His work has endured for over 40 years, and has been produced as graphic novels, television series, films, and video games. He was an integral part in bringing the literary genres of Anime/Manga to western audiences. His work is just as loved today as it was all those years ago. An author and artist, fully worthy of those distinctions and titles.Thank you for 44 years of laughs and adventures, Akira Toriyama, rest in peace!

_childDocuments_.review: An RPG style Dragonball game has already been somewhat explored in the likes of Xenoverse. _childDocuments_.review: Good fun, simple gameplay. If you like DBZ, it's a solid nostalgia trip and the graphics are pretty nice in combat. (the open world is pretty boring looking but still has a decent DBZ look and feel to it. The character cut scenes are total crap. Basically just characters standing still talking to eachother for long amounts of time. I think all but the most die hard BDZ fans will skip 95% of the dialogue in this game. Another downside is the combat doesn't really evolve at all. New attacks are just more powerful versions of old attacks. Nothing interesting to unlock. Good if you're ok with simple fun combat for a little BDZ nostalgia. Not good if you want depth.

_childDocuments_.review: Portrays itself as a basic fighter game with rpg elements when in fact it is a rage game in disguise, nothing is consistent or reliable and none of the enemies follow any of the rules you do. None of the difficulty in this game is real and the most effective mechanic is to spam and give zero though to what your doing.Furthermore, the quality of the graphics are comical at best. The textures were obviously thrown together for free and appear to have been designed by a 1st year student. I dont blame the devs though, this is a painfully obvious cash grab and a death howl of a dying industry.It could theoretically have been fun, but someone forgot to schedule that phase of development.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably the best DBZ game I've played. If you focus on the main story stuff it is an absolute blast, and the cut scenes are so incredibly animated. So beautiful. Its the rest of the game that suffers IMO. The free roaming is fun for the first hand full of hours, then becomes tedious as there really isnt that much to do. Most of the collectible things in the free roam enviroment are mostly pointless to collect, especially Orbs. The side quests 80% of the time are " Fly Here, grab thing, Fly back," Or "Someone needs help, Fight Robots, Done" There were a handfull of the side quests that did at least have some good dialogue. You can level your characters up to like level 200, but I cannot fathom why anyone would want to do that with how little there is to do after the game is done. My highest level after i finished the game was less than 80. But even though the RPG side of the game is really lacking, this is easily the best and most enjoyable way to play through the DBZ story, and highly recommend it for that reason alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I am going to be brutally honest; this game is a great nostalgia trip. It would also be great for anyone wanting to learn about the old shows, without having to watch over 9000 hours across several series worth of anime. The combat is absolutely horrible. The controls are abysmal, as is per usual with most Dragon Ball games. There is nothing original about this game, and most of the things it copies from other franchises, it does not do as well. Animations (including talking, running, various NPC's) can be ridiculously bad. Multiple times I have had an NPC i was speaking with slide off the screen never to return. The unscripted battles, are pretty dang lackluster. Camera angles in combat with large enemies, terrible. Bandai apparently thought that starting the game off with a fetch/ gather quest, followed by an escort mission of a crying Gohan was a good idea. All that being said, the game can be fun. I like flashing bright lights, nostalgia, and punching things while screaming for 8 episodes without any plot advancements. Is it worth the price? Probably not. Is it worth your time? If you are a fan of Akira Toriyama's work, I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: I like Dragon ball z a lot, So I'm going to keep playing this and my review might end up changing but, early impressions:In fights the core buttons are; Ki blast, Guard, and the combat system is pretty terrible. Press fight, spam Body Blow and step dodge. I haven't touched any difficulties below Hard mode, but the AI is bad so I assume its just Get-Hit-Harder Mode."But it's an action RPG not a fighting game so it's not fair to say the combat is bad!!!"except, yknow, it's very much an integral component of the game.Flying around in the overworld is cool, but, collecting orbs is just repetitive game lengthening that doesn't feel good. Particularly when you re-enter a zone slightly later in the story and all the orbs you grabbed are just back. Ontop of that, You receive orbs from combat which is neat, except, the combat isn't great- and you'll just be getting jumped by (the same singular model of) RR skull robots and Saibamen every 45 seconds if you aren't boosting around grabbing orbs or B-lining to your story mission.The cinematics are cool, the voicing is cool, the story is cool. It's just DBZ so all of that is great.Collectibles are neat, Old pictures and captions about the older Dragonball (z) stuff is very nice. Hunting deer and dinosaurs and collecting materials is much less cool and feels pretty pointless so far.If I bought this game for its full price I would be botheredI bought this 67% off and that feels less bad - but if it wasn't a DBZ title I would have refunded it based on the gameplay.I still get to play as Goku and the boys, but I can't recommend this game at full price based on how it feels.If you like Dragonball alot, Play the demo and then consider buying it when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of Dragon Ball, this game will hit your sense of nostalgia. All the important parts of the story are either animated or playable. This feels like a spiritual successor to the Legacy of Goku series from the GBA era. If you are a fan pf DB this is a game you will love. For newcomers to the series, this game will be a great way in.
_childDocuments_.name: DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a DBZ action RPG. Eh... I'd give this game about a 5/10. (The RPG elements do not feel impactful at all, you can completely ignore them and play the game).If you want a DBZ fighting game. Eh... I'd give this game about a 5/10. (The combat system is very simplistic, either spam melee attack, spam energy blast, transform, charge energy, do a super, dodge or block. Each character feels about the same and every enemy is capable of doing this red charge up attack where you need to press block or dodge and then repeat spam attacks. The combat pattern is heavily repetitive, some enemies have custom super attacks, but many just copy the other enemies super attacks or have ones that are so similar they might as well be the same. Pretty lack luster).If you want the best retelling of the DBZ story in a video game form I'd give this a 9/10. But since I have heard the original DBZ story sooo many times by now, I struggle to give this a 6 or 7/10.Basically, this is more of a fairly accurate t.v. show or movie simulator rather than a game. The cut scenes and text boxes are by far the best part of this game. If you are the kind of person that skips game text or movies, it'd be pretty hard to recommend this game, since that is the only reason I'd recommend playing this since the story is pretty well done. The problems comes in that most of us have already went through this story a dozen times.Anyway, for me personally 6/10. I've been playing it slowly and only play it when I want to watch some dbz movies or tv shows. Don't ever really crave the game play. I can't say I regret purchasing it, since at this rate I will eventually beat the game (cell saga currently), but I can't really recommend it to people that were hoping for a good action RPG in the dragon ball universe.

_childDocuments_.review: After having just beaten the game, I must say that it was an amazing experience. Overall the game's story and the story of the original DBZ anime are almost the same, cutting out a couple fights like Super Saiyan 1.5 Trunks vs. Perfect Cell, but it also adds some new story and a brand new character.The gameplay is fantastic, and battles actually feel like you're controlling Goku, Gohan, Vegeta, Etc. Ki Blast shots (at least to me) are fairly useless because of the low damage and high chance of the enemy moving slightly to avoid it.The graphics, in my opinion, are for the most part great. There is however some laziness with a large amount of the story being told with text boxes instead of animated cutscenes, but it isn't that big of a deal. The cinematic cutscenes look astounding, the major events of each saga being reborn with 3D look astonishing, Vegeta and Nappa arriving on earth, Piccolo's sacrifice, Father-Son Kamehameha, and more are recreated.Overall I'd give this game a 9/10, but only because they're taking so long with the final dlc, but I can be patient and wait.

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the main story, it took around 45 hours. The game is just great if you are a dragon ball fan. It has standard jRPG elements: random combat encounters, items that can boost your stats or heal you, character skill based progression. On the bad side - it gets kinda repetitive. At some point you will do what you can to avoid the random henchmen enemies because fighting them is just too tedious, especially while doing sidequests. As for the optional missions, most of them are standard go from point A to point B and listen to some character exposition. For example Master Roshi wants to do something so you go to certain character, speak with them, go to another place, have a generic fight, come back, get some more exposition, get rewards. That said, the rewards are sufficient. To my surprise the game has no grind. Main story gives you enough XP to beat it just by doing main missions. I've beaten it on hard difficulty and it was perfect mix between challenge and fun. If you dont care for the story you might as well skip all sidequests and cutscenes and beat the game in about half the time. The cutscenes are plenty and sometimes its a string of cutscenes without end. If you are okay long cutscenes revisiting story of your childhood then its great, but if you prefer constant action, you might be bored to death. Fighting is okay. Like I said, it gets repetitive while exploring but boy, is it spectacular to dash around avoiding danger just to pick the right moment and fire kamehameha at your enemies. The boss fights have some original element to them, boss characters can initiate special sequences where you have to dodge their beams and attacks for a while until they are finished. It is very visually appealing how all the light beams look in cell shading world. As you unlock more powerful (and ki consuming) moves, you get access to some cool looking abilities like genki dama, dragon fist, makkan...special beam cannon. The combat is probably not xenoverse level but it has a charm to it. Just try not to fight too many random enemies or else it gets a tad boring.The soundtrack is incredible. A lot of original Japanese tracks, were re-created as orchestra version of them and it is truly epic, especially in the decisive moments of main plot. I had shivers down my spine just because of the ost. Again, this will be a good thing if you are a dragon ball fan in the first place. The game adds a lot to 'slice of life' side of dragon ball. You meet old friends from OG dragonball like Lunch, Nam, Pilaf gang, Andoid 8, Upa and his father etc. If you liked filer episode with Goku and Piccolo getting their driver license, you are for a treat as the hover car is there and you can use it anytime to drive around the world in a bit slower pace instead of flying everywhere. This is adds more into immersion of the world. By all means, this isn't GTA style sandbox world but I am pretty sure its the best 'open world' DB game ever. Cities do not look that big from above but you can step down and take a walk on the street and really feel like you're in dragon ball world (Im not being paid by IGN). The game is a love letter to all the dragon ball fans who wants to feel like a child watching the anime after coming back from school again. It's not just a fighting game like many before it, but a dragon ball world simulator with open world that you can explore and be a part of. There is a reason why this has 'overwhelmingly positive' reviews. tl;dr if you love dragon ball - this is a must. If you never watched it or aren't that into it - you might want to wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: DRAGON BALL Z: KAKAROT

_childDocuments_.review: If Dragon Ball FighterZ is, in my opinion, the BEST DB game in the "Versus Fighting" genre, Kakarot is the BEST DB game in the "Adventure / RPG" genre :)So respectful of the manga / anime in the slightest details, it's like "playing" the anime on steroids.The "simplistic" fighting gameplay gain in depth during the game and feel very good in hands.The cinematics are very cool, i feel like when i was young in the 90s watching them.The big + for me is the encyclopedia that is VERY big and while maybe not complete, still HUGE for newcomers or old fans wanting to perfect their knowledge. You can learn about hundreds (yeah) of characters, places, rewatch every cinematics, genealogic trees, and more !The open world is not that good in the sense of it's deja vu and kinda boring / empty, but i just started the game and i'm only 6h into it.But the main story, of boy... you know it by heart and still get thrilled :D

Play wise, very simplistic; was not very hard to pick up and is welcoming to new players.I only wish you could choose to navigate the open-world with the fusion characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Updating my review since it's been a while (like, since launch) and I'm finally doing another playthrough including all DLC released so far. It's incredible. Not perfect, targeting can be annoying, combat isn't incredibly deep (imagine if it had Sparking Zero combat), I'd like some more OG Dragonball representation but at least we got the incredible 23rd World Tournament arc. Overall a very worthwhile package, especially on sale. Watching the anime would still be better for newbies to the series, but if you're like me and almost never watch anything and would rather play it, this is the only DBZ game that I feel like is a worthy "play it for the story" rating. The cutscenes are great, it's awesome to see the story in between arcs, lots of references to things that we never got to see in the anime after OG, it's just an awesome experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy hell. After going and playing both Xenoverse and FighterZ after completing this, I now have a new appreciation for it. It's so smooth and handles fantastically compared to especially Xenoverse, even if all the playable characters are same-y__________________________At completion of the main game, Lv300 Beerus defeated, Lv300 Golden Frieza defeated, History of Trunks complete, Lv115 Dabura defeated, Goku and Vegeta at level 300, everyone's skill trees maxed, and all side-quests complete, it's clear I enjoyed this game. Very repetitive. Very samey all the way through, but still fun enough . My negative review still stands though __________________________original review: - Numbers mean nothing. When your health is 345276 and you level up and it goes to 356842, where's the feeling of becoming more powerful? They're just a slew of numbers with no meaning or commas. When you're dealing 89482 damage and you level up once and it goes to 94362 it means nothing. (I bet you didn't even read those numbers properly and just skimmed them, and that's my point!) My level 32 Vegeta has 1,533,474 HP and I have no idea if that's good or not. When you take damage, all you're looking at is how much green was taken from your health bar. The slew of 5-digit numbers thrown at you are meaningless. It's solely so you can say "Well my power-level is 1 million" like that means anything. Toriyama introduced scouters so power-levels would become meaningless. This is an RPG at heart with stats and levels but it doesn't act like one. In Final Fantasy 10 for example, increasing your Strength by 4 early on makes a big difference. When you hit for 500 damage instead of 200 for the first time, you really go "Wow!" because it's noticeable when you one-shot enemies that were giving you grief. Or in Final Fantasy 7 when you briefly have Sephiroth in your party, the damage he's dealing at that point in the game makes you go "Damn! He's strong!". There's no sense of progression/increase here. - Why can't I fly with the right stick!! like every other game with flight controls!?- Levels are way off balance. The whole point of DBZ is beating someone far stronger than you. Here, even if you're only 2 to 3 levels under the recommended level, you're getting your ass whooped! You have to come back once you're over-levelled and slap them around in an anti-climactic way. But once you're at the recommended level, it's too easy. There's no in-between happy-medium. It's too hard or too easy. I'm yet to lose a story-related fight. Only time I've lost is in the optional training with 3 vs 1 and I'm only 2 levels under the recommended level.  - The problem with so many characters is they all end up very same-y. Bosses and enemies in general all have the same moves so they can all be beaten the same. Go in for a combo, send them flying, then hit them with a long-range attack and repeat, with a dodge or block here and there. All bosses have the exact same dash move, charged stun-lock, and charged shield-breaker and they all telegraph them exactly the same way which means you know what's coming and how to avoid it even if you're facing them for the first time. All playable characters are the same with different skins and attack names. They all move the same, handle the same, have the same speed in battle, and have the same controls. There's no difference between Goku, Vegeta, or Piccolo (which saying that to a Vegeta fanboy is sure to hurt their Saiyan pride!) Why would Vegeta fight like Goku? He wouldn't! Any playable bosses as well suffer from the Chrono Trigger "Magus syndrome"; when you get a boss as a playable character, they don't have the moves they did in battle. - Padded to buggery. In-between sagas and fetch quests are a slog with unnecessary, poorly designed content that is laughably unimaginative. "Go get me this thing, fast travel there and it's where you spawn, collect it, then fast travel back to the quest-giver and receive your useless item" (usually cooking ingredients). All it does it add to the Steam timer so you can say "I played it for 80 hours" by the end, when most of it was waiting for loading screens. - Even though they're easy, beam struggles don't happen naturally. You have to go out of your way to force them. This should happen very often. The enemy should counter-attack at random times whenever they're open to an attack and going to e hit anyway just for the real feel.- Much like the show, the game starts with a reliance on getting good with working out timing and combos (like Dragon Ball. By the end it's all about keeping your distance and spamming beam attacks (unlike the show)- The new English dub's voices are terrible. Not once in my entire 33-year life have I ever found Gohan annoying in any way. Not in the original Japanese dub, the Ocean dub, or the original Funimation dub with Stephanie Nadolny. This new Gohan voice however is insufferable. She yells every line of dialogue and is way too high-pitched, especially for an action game. I ended up playing the Gohan sections either on mute or swapped to the Japanese dub. I'd rather suffer through Granny-Goku's voice than listen to her. Monica Rial as Bulma is just as bad for the same reasons. Tiffany Vollmer was way better

_childDocuments_.review: The best Dragon Ball game I have ever played. You play through the Saiyan Saga where Vegata and Nappa invade earth all the way to the Majin Buu Saga. There are "intermissions" between sagas allowing you to choose from several different characters as you explore earth and the several huge open world maps it provides completing side quests.There's cooking giving you buffs to HP, Ki, Attack, Defense, and EXP. You need recipes to make dishes along with ingredients. Chi-Chi can make full course meals requiring three dishes you made to be combined into one making the bonuses even greater than before. Time Trials with cars and bipedal walkers. Baseball, fishing, and I think a couple of other "minigames". If you're a Dragon Ball fan this game is for you no doubt about it. There's "photos" you can find and pick up describing old episodes of Goku when he was a kid. You can collect and use the dragon balls as many times as you tediously want to collect them. HOWEVER the wishes you can wish HELP SO MUCH. Especially when it comes to wishing for money, z orbs, or rare materials. Greatly reducing the collections and time needed to advance quickly. The combat and leveling is somewhat simple yet still enjoyable and requires you to be able to read the enemy's attack and react accordingly. My only complaint would be, where this rarely happens, but the AI would spam the same super attack over and over again forcing me to dodge relentlessly or making me use a lot of healing items. I did not die once in any fight in this game but I have gotten very close. It's not a walk in the park but at the same time not extremely hard. Skill is required but not extreme amounts.Overall it took me 27 hours to complete the main stories. I completed I would say 85% of the sidequests with several unlocking after you complete the final saga. Looking forward to DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Short review, if you grew up watching the DBZ series on Cartoon Network or anywhere else, this game does a great job of telling the story of Adult Goku and Son Gohan through the fighting of Saiyans Vegeta and Kappa, all the way to Frieza and beyond. Some minor repetitive quirks, but overall the experience of playing the game is fun. Also the game is BEST played with a controller, it can be a pain with KB+M, but it's still manageable. The overall combat is great! I am not even close to being done with finishing the game yet. Game is a solid 8 out of 10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The formula for this game is as follows:1: Watch a cutscene2: have a battle3: Fly around the map until next cutscene4: have a battleThis would be fine as it's the basic formula that allot of Dragonball Z games have followed but this one somehow manages to screw it up by having a very basic and boring combat system. You will spend allot of time playing characters such as Gohan, Piccolo, Vegeta and Goku but they all control the same, there is slight variation in their special moves but there is no difference in them beyond animations. There is almost zero strategy to combat encounters as they can be won by mashing the melee button and spamming the dodge button to create space. Every single major combat encounter I had in the game (up to frieza final form) played out exactly the same as the last.. spam B, launch a beam, dodge dodge dodge, spam b (sprinkle in a super that isnt the beam) rinse and repeat. It's mind numbing how repetitive this game is.As for what you do outside of combat the fully realized world of Dragonball Z is pretty cool, this is probably one of the only games that really lets you get a good 3d look at the locations from the show so I will credit it with that. The flight controls are a bit wonky with RB making you go up and RT making you go down but it's not that bad. The music and graphics are pretty awesome, the music is lifted from the original Japanese OST and the graphics while not quite as cool as something like FighterZ are a step up for sure over Xenoverse 2. Outside of the sites and sounds however the world is devoid of any fun offerings, there are mini games like fishing and mindless MMORPG styled side quests (with plenty of pointless fetch and combat missions) but none of them are fun and end up feeling like an afterthought.The game makes an attempt to be systems heavy almost as if the developers kept remembering they were making an RPG but none of it really comes together in any way that makes it fun or meaningful to engage with. The Emblem system for instance lets you collect tokens of characters from the world and create communities on a board with them which will then grant you little bonuses such as 5% to melee power. This system is fine but allot of it will require you to engage with the mind numbing side quests and the bonuses aren't anything great so it's not worth your time. Likewise every character in the game has a skill tree but the game locks you out of progressing into newer cooler skills because it just wouldn't be right to have Vegeta using the final flash on first form Frieza. There is also a cooking system in the game in which Chi Chi will make dishes for you and your party which can heal you and sometimes grant permanent stat bonuses but again.. it's nothing noticeable or complimentary to the feel of the gameplay so I don't feel compelled to engage with it.Coming from Xenoverse 2 to this I am fairly disappointed, the combat in Xenoverse was much better than this and featured plenty of variety and skill ceiling. Kakarot would get a pass on it's combat if it wasn't 90% of the game.. sorry to say this one is a bit of a stinker outside of cool cutscenes and music. A definite pass for all but the most die hard of fans.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Dragon Ball you'll forgive it enough to like it but if you're not the repetitive combat and boring side quests will have this game often feeling like a chore to play. You're going to get tired of facing the same 4 enemies for almost every side quest, it feels like a complete waste when you think about how they could've included some of the movie villains in as side quests between arcs. Having characters like Lord Slug, Broly, and Janemba would've been a good change of pace instead of facing robots and saibamen over and over again. The progression system works well but I wish they would've involved the community board a little bit more as you don't even really need to use it to get through the game. Plus I wished it could've done more with customization to where you can use your zeni to buy alternate customs for characters. But for all the bad points I still had fun playing this game. I've been watching Dragon Ball since I was 5 and I'm 27 now plus I've played almost every game between Budokai and this game. This is not your typical RPG game but instead something for the fans.Graphics: 8/10 (Had it's rough spots, but the cell shading was on point)Gameplay: 5/10 (Very repetitive, wished they would've looked at Budokai 3 or Raging Blast 2 as a template)Sound: 8/10 (I'm being picky but I would've loved ad least a DLC option for the Funimation Dub OST)Story: 7/10 (Everyone knows the DBZ story and they do it well but not including the movie villains hurts it)Customization: 6/10 (Skill progression and upgrading skills are good but the community board definitely lacks)Overall: 7/10 (Buy if you're a fan, buy on sale if you're trying to become a fan)

_childDocuments_.review: Let me get this out of the way to start: If you are not already a DBZ fan, save your time and spend your money on something else, because this game won't convince you. If you *are* a DBZ fan, go ahead and read on.So, welcome fellow DBZ fans. I know, our standards are pretty low these days because of the quality of the average DBZ game, but here's the thing: for a fan, this game is actually pretty great. Don't expect a 10/10 of course, but if you like the Tenkaichi games, this game will fill a void FighterZ doesn't (amazing as FighterZ is).There's something special about being able to freely fly around and explore fairly large and lovingly recreated Dragon Ball settings, and they are fantastic settings. They look great, they feel great, they sound great, and they're packed with references and easter eggs from the shows and manga. The non-combat activities aren't mindblowing, but they're enough to keep you exploring and flying around, and that's good.The combat is about equal to Tenkaichi but a bit better. Play around with it and you'll have fun and feel really cool. The enemy types can get repetitive on the open world but I still found it enjoyable. The story fights and boss battles are where it can get really good.Speaking of the story - once again this is a retelling of DBZ, but it's a very good one and unlike most, there's a lot of care taken to add memorable scenes, characters and missions that keep it more fresh than usual. There's some cool surprises in there.This is a very chill game, great to spend time relaxing in. Leveling up can get grindy, especially post-game, but if you're just chilling out with it that's a good thing, like for me. If you're a DBZ fan and you don't mind a game being kinda repetitive then this is a solid purchase you won't regret.

_childDocuments_.review: So I am a massive DBZ fan, grew up watching it and have continued to rewatch and keep up with the Anime. Played most of the games so I have a lot of comparison material.So, First Question. Should you buy the game? And I have to answer No. Not unless games £20 or less.There is such laziness with the game it down right peeves me off. Following Xenoverse's "Hard" Enemies where attacks don't effect, this game follows the "Damage doesn't do nothing to stop me" game style that has been adopted into the games for whatever reason. This was never in Budokai to me recolllection so why in the hell is it now a thing boggles the mind. An example of this is the mission I was just on as Vegeta on Namek fight Dodoria. No matter what super attack i did, i could not stop him charging his Ki or Attack with his supers. This is INCREDIBLY FRUSTRATING as at this part of the story, Vegeta is suppose to be STRONGER than Dodoria so why is it that he can just charge me directly through a Galick Gun and deal mass damage to me.Moving onto the combat system itself is just pure garbage IMO. Mash B, dash to enemy, mash B, Dash and so on. You can dash to your hearts content so you can really take the p with melee. Hit 3 times dash to side hit 3 times dash to side. It makes fighting cringe-+worthingly boring and repetative. Sure you get up to 4 skills to use like Xenoverse and a buddy fighting system giving you up to 8 moves if 2 buddies are fighting with you but its still a really boring mechanic.Another issue I have with the game is the voice's, Now flying around in freemode is fine, BUT EVERY TIME YOUR NEAR AN ENEMY DOES THE SAME 2 LINES OF VOICE GET PLAYED. STFU GOHAN IDGAF THAT YOU CAN TAKE THEM -.- Also, cutscenes are bad, there such a long pause between character conversations. Example - Krillin and Gohan save dende and krillin just solar flared Dodoria, In this TIME CRUTIAL MOMENT it takes Gohan a good few seconds to respond to Krillin saying 'Let's Hide' with OK. Im guessing this is to allow different Language's to be implemented but ♥♥♥♥ ME is it irritating.If i had to compare the fighting in this game to another, i would say it is similar to Jump Force, which i refunded, cause it sucked.Missions - Plentiful to do outside the story line. That's fine. BUT IT SHOULDN'T TAKE AN HOUR TO FIND A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ TOMATO (turtle side mission)All in all, another poor show for a much loved franchise. I will continue to play and if things get better, i'll update my review, BUT i am NOT holding my breath.TLDR; Games bad and Devs should feel bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! Just fantastic!I haven't played a Dad Simulator like this since Fallout 4. Cant believe I slept on it.Even tho it is strictly an Asian dad simulator (for Anime dads to practice fatherhood) and the culture differences are rather stark, I was still able to enjoy my time as a virtual dad in this unfamiliar space.As per usual, when I find a gem like this boy, I neglected my irl family and played thousands of hours offline, so my displayed playtime in no way reflects actual time spent engaging in the advanced father simulations.Ruminating on the moments I mentally highlighted as a physic anchor, for when my irl family disappoints me and it cant be overstated how often they disappoint me, I couldn't help but notice that there was a slight problem with the boy-son-child of the game.It might be my lack of a frame of reference regarding raising an Anime child, but what troubled me the most was my inability to control the types of people my Anime child was permitted to interact with. This Kame Roshi man was clearly a molester. I know it was implemented in the game to warn of the dangers, however, I felt a dialogue option to confront Mr. Roshi or alert the authorities of him would of been realistic to the simulation. If this had of been developed by Bethesda we could of expected such options. I would like to speculate that they would of scripted an event whereby you attend Mr. Kame Roshi's trial and  give a witness statement in the dock, you and then your boy-son-child. I digress.It is because of this that I unfortunately cannot recommend this game as there are many fantastic Father Simulators on the market these days.This is is still a great game. Please don't let my 'one thing that annoys me' deter you. It is a fantastic way to get an insight into raising an Anime child from the perspective of an Asian father.I almost forgot to mention one of the most important features this Dad Quest game has that so many others forget to include. This is the fishing mechanic. No Dad Quest Father Simulation game can boast the full robust experience of operating a virtual father if they lack this key component.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: With 3 hours played at the time of this review, I can easily recommend it for DBZ fans despite some imperfections. Combat isn't that deep but it's a fun system with a couple of interesting layers. Side quests are kind of weak in terms of gameplay but the dialogue is good. The graphics aren't quite as crisp as FighterZ but are a very close 2nd, especially considering how recognizable the settings are. The main cutscenes (which are numerous) include solid voice acting from many of the original actors. The RPG elements aren't fleshed out but there are tons of characters. Overall, very good game. I haven't watched the series since middle school so playing through it is a lot of fun, like a trip down memory lane. Easily worth the $60 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game was made to empty the wallets of nostalgic 90's kids.-> I am a 90's kid.-> You know I'm gonna call this a masterpiece. Full stop.If you've ever played any of the Naruto Storm games by Cyberconnect2 you are gonna find the combat in this game very familiar, the simple B button smash combos and fast dashes still remain and, when powered up, super attacks trigger cutscenes too. So overall a familiar feel to the combat, but in general Kakarot is its own beast.Definitely the best thing about it is the amazing attention to detail from both manga and anime, I'll name a few of them:-Power levels rise along with the story progression and are accurate in every event of the anime.-Transforming strenghtens Saiyans ridiculously and makes other characters useless, just like in the anime.-Stuffing your face with food before a battle is OP, just like in the anime.-You go faster by flying. But you still use Nimbus. Because you know it's fun. Just like in the anime.-You can race cars and ask Bulma for parts in her workshop, just like in the anime.-Yes, you can properly collect Dragon Balls and spam Shenron wishes, just like in the anime.-Korin gives you free Senzu beans overtime. Yes they are OP as they should, just like in the anime.-The end game Super Spirit Bomb is so huge it's rendered out of the frame, just like in the anime.-The cutscenes are... you know it. Just like the anime.I could go on and on about every tiny detail there is, only noticed if you are a fan and care to look deeper, but it would be a long post. Hopefully these few things I mentioned are enough to make you buy the game and get immersed in what I think it's the best DBZ universe experience ever made. Go feed your inner kid some happiness, and it starts with that opening.

_childDocuments_.review: *RECOMMENDED ONLY FOR DRAGON BALL (Z) FANS*I have played many Dragon Ball, Dragon Ball Z, Dragon Ball GT, you name it... games. From Dragon Ball Advanced Adventure to Dragon Ball Origins, GT: Transformation, Supersonic Warriors, Budokai Tenkaichi Tag Team, Budokai to Budokai Tenkaichi, Battle of Z, Xenoverse, etc... I'll keep it short, this is not a great game, but it is not bad either, as a fan of Dragon Ball, i like the game but the game still needs lot of work.It is better than One Piece: World Seeker though, it has more playable characters even though not all of them are playable even though they should be, Krillin and Tien for example. Fortunately there's a mod which makes them playable which i also recommend with the versus mod for the endgame.Better gameplay, gameplay is actually enjoyable.At first the map is enjoyable to roam but it gets repetitive and boring real quick. It could use better and more maps. If this would be released by an actually competent developer, it would be ten times better but we're talking about Bandai Namco so it's no wonder but they actually made a better job on this game than most of the others games but it still is way too lacking in many departments. The graphics and the effects are good, no complaints in that part. Also, common enemies are generic and boring, i was expecting more variety, also dinosaurs to fight but in that department it is plain boring.Also, first-person mode Ki is kinda clunky, when you're on ground, even if you aim a bit above, it will touch the ground right away. One more thing, you can't change costumes during the game, it should be possible during endgame but it is not.This game could use of many quality of life changes.Now that was all about the game but i'd still like to see more of this, having a Dragon Ball: Goku game would be pretty neat, which would be about the original story from the beginning all to the end.One of Dragon Ball: Super would be neat too, i'd say even one of GT would be cool but not the coolest.I do not expect much from Bandai Namco though as they barely can get anything done right with only one game so my hopes aren't high.Get this game if you love Dragon Ball (Z), otherwise make your way and forget about it as you may not really like it.If you are a fan of Dragon Ball (Z), you'll be playing the same story once again, huh, but this time it will be a bit different unlike from getting from Xenoverse to Xenoverse 2. But get on heavy sale only, -85% or better.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, this is a game that does what its predecessors did and little else, but it's fair to say that all of those predecessors, in telling the story of DBZ, failed to capture the same essence of the story due to their focus on other themes, like Xenoverse's time travel, budokai's moveset customization, or tenkaichi's intricate fighting system. Kakarot is actually the first game to do what it attempts to do with a significant degree of success, and wins its own merit in execution. I simultaneously began rewatching dbz Kai with a friend whom has never seen anything about dragon ball other than the Broly movie when this game came out, and I can seriously say, if you use some quick youtube searches to watch some more iconic scenes like the ssj3 transformation or the father-son kamehameha to supplement this game's slightly brisk pace, it is absolutely a legitimate alternative to the anime. But that's a review for players who haven't watched dragon ball or haven't gone through the same story as many times as other die-hard fans like me. And for those people, they probably care more about the gameplay if anything. The gameplay is an absolutely standard, quaint RPG system with a very nicely streamlined, xenoverse style combat system. There is no pvp or online functionality, which for me personally, does not matter, but if it matters to you, you may find little replayability. However, if you're someone who, in addition to being interested in Dragon ball Z, is a fan of RPGs and JRPG pseudo-open world exploration, story driven games, this is absolutely for you, and I totally recommend it. In terms of performance and polish, it's just shy of exceptional. There were 2 instances where an NPC floated away from their spawn point, soft locking me from the quest until I restarted the game, the factory settings are set to 1080, and you can't change them until after you've seen the (great) opening to the game, which isnt a big deal, but also, all of the major cutscenes are pre-rendered in 1080 60fps, and it may be jarring at times seeing your crisp, 2k, 4k, 75hz, 144hz or whatever higher spec monitor you have, suddenly lose a good bit of clarity for the sake of file compression. This is honestly my biggest complaint with the game at large, but is it a deal breaker? absolutely not, even in 1080, the graphical fidelity and quality of animation are super cutting edge, and you can tell that the artists of this game really give a ♥♥♥♥, although I feel they kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up base goku's hair.TL;DR: The new standard in streamlining new fans into the series.|Rating: 8.5/10 worth 60$

_childDocuments_.review: Resembles an Open-World DBZ game. Pro's:Fun, the way you get around the world and the way it controls is just fun.The fight's can be very fulfilling and satisfying.It portrays the story in a unique way not seen before by previous games.It has skill tree's and customizable skills and powers. The power progression is balanced and satisfying.Cons:Some of the fight can be down-right annoying, unhittable enemies who hit you back with a 50k damage kick out of nowhere isn't fun. It doesn't tell you when they are un stunnable and you going in for a hit when they're in this state can mean life or death, and you will have to restart the whole fight.The items are WAY too easy to mis click on PC. You can accidentally pop a really expensive 100k health heal because C is right next to V and in the middle of battle you spam a little.The talking mid-fight like it's so easy as Goku or Vegeta when the enemies kicking your ass is very annoying. "You're no match for me! This is too easy!" as you're 1 health and they're at 200k launching a beam that deals 50k your way and your guards broken lolIt's fun, I'd say it's worth it if you're into Dragon Ball or fighting games!

_childDocuments_.review: Hour after hour I keep playing this game. I think just to justify my purchase. Its just not good. Yes it is a nostalgia run. But the fights are beyond annoying. You are either fighting cookie cutter mobs that run you down in the open world or bosses that have no limit to the abilities they can cast as well as extra moves that assist them further. Your only option is to overlevel your character and slap them around. Which is kind of a boring grind to do. The bosses will "little brother" you. By that, I mean they will use their same couple moves over and over and over again. Stunning or guard breaking you. The dodge system is what is cool but either it doesnt work or my brain doesnt. You will also get 3v1d constantly in training and 5-8 v 1 a lot in the open world. This game should be good. The graphics are cool and the effects when fighting are sweet. I dont even mind the empty open world littered with repetitive mobs that much. In all honesty if they made the AI a bit more unique in its fighting style it would be more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game to anyone who is fan of DBZ.The reason this game interested me was because many years ago on the Game Boy Advanced they had "The Legacy Of Goku II" and that game was one of the only RPG DBZ games around(Atleast the only good one).This game has a lot in common with that game so if you were looking for a more modern take on it then look no further.The fighting is pretty decent and it feels good progressing your characters skills.The cutscenes in this game are glorious. Sometimes even beating the actual anime itself.The aspects I didn't like are the amount of Orbs and medals you need in order to unlock skills. Orbs are actually not a huge problem but D medals are going to start holding you back from learning your skills. Its not a huge problem but it definitely became annoying to have to try search for D medals in the world in order to train and learn new skills.The two Dragon Ball Super DLCs are not that great but the latest Trunks DLC is excellent. That Trunks DLC has a lot of heart and emotion put into it so its a great addition to the game.Overall its a fun game to play through.

_childDocuments_.review: Its one of the best retellings of DBZ story-wise and graphically.But man. The combat sucks ass. Instead of relying on intelligent enemy AI, Bandai has enemies over-use hyper armor to prevent you from winning too easily. In certain fights, the AI will spam hyper-armor moves back-to-back and you will never be able to combo them. Just super attack, dodge, charge, and repeat. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to any FAN who enjoys the Dragon Ball universe and would like to play a more immersive experience. I am around six hours in and I have only played two separate sessions. Again, as a FAN I totally recommend this game because it's engaging and full of things to do. However, as a gamer, there are issues with the game:Controls and keybindings aren't the most streamlined, especially for keyboard. Combat is much easier with a controller. I wouldn't recommend a Steam controller, but a USB Xbox controller should work just fine. The amount of tutorial pop-ups is tiresome, yet will net you very little help in figuring out the game mechanics. I have had to explore the menus a fair amount in order to get a grasp on what is going on. Lastly, there are small differences between the subtitles and the English dialogue that - to me - show evidence of some corners being cut. All-in-all, buy the game, but if you're more in it for the gaming experience, don't expect this game to win "Game of the Year" and your expectations won't be let down.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Having just completed the story mode, I'm left with both awe and disappointment.I've played Budokai 1,2, and 3, budokai tenkaichi 1,2, and 3 and Xenoverse 1 and 2, battle of z and utlimate tenkaichidespite my criticism the game is worth buying and playing if you've been playing DBZ as much, if not more than I have.Pros- Combat mechanics are great; no cool combos like you had in the Budokai series; but perhaps the better battle mechanics than the Tenkaichi lineup- In fight transformations (I very much disliked the games that did not have this)- the open world concept is better than Budokai 3- the resource gathering is mostly for side quests and replenishing health between skirmishes and is a refreshing new concept to the DBZ game family, beyond just collecting dragon balls, skills, and outfits.- story line removed useless fillers and still stays true to the story including the always neglected pui pui and yakon fight, and the fight with freeza looks down right better than the show itself.- the after image illusion from the faster pace combat (in supercharged ssj mode) really give the feeling that you are in a high speed combat that mere mortal eyes cannot follow. Sometimes it's so fast pace I rely on sounds to predict their next move, which should be part of the gaming experience. I think Xenoverse 2 accomplished this as well.-the battles were a bit like soul games where there is a discernable combat pattern you need to predict, dodge, defend, and retaliate accordingly.cons- My biggest gripe was the handfull of fights by the time you reach the cell games where the difficulty is purposely set so you need health repleneshing items on you. To me, that defeats the purpose of these games. These fights are no longer challenging since you end up getting frustrated enough to have to buy a bunch of health restore and just keep using that. They gave the enemy an unfair advantage that prevents them from getting stunned and is really good at stunning you and preventing you from being able to even recover from non-stop barrage of attacks. you can lose up to half of your health if you let them break your defence just once. There is no need for this.- it strictly is about the Z story from Raditz to Buu (with dlc for golden freeza and beerus fingers crossed for broly); references from the original Dragon Ball can be found when gathering in the open world.- The filler that got cut out got replaced with side quests. Some might like this, and though I certainly don't mind filtering filler content, I think intermissions should have included the movies as well, even if its only 1-3 fight scenes at least, I would hope to see all the movies added on into a dlc/seasons pass. no dead zone, no lord slug, no cooler, no wrath of the dragon, none of it. I can understand not including DBGT, but still. even if they didn't include the previous broly movies and opted, instead for the new one, that would be great.- as a result, the main story line is rather short, so don't do like me and rush through the story line, enjoy the side quests as they appear on the map, or you will end up finishing the main story within 30hrs or so with only half of z souls and techniques unlocked. apart from side quests and villains, and using the time machine to get "S" scores on each battle, there isn't much else to do that is supper exciting. - I think there was a missed opportunity to add more distraction and diversion; for example, there could have been a non combat game feature for when goku was training in 100x gravity that combined reflex and puzzle solving.I hope one day, they will take all the best parts of the Kakarot, Tenkaichi 3, and Xenoverse and make a thorough game in story, originality, open world/universe, and game mechanics

_childDocuments_.review: Overall 6/10(Keyboard/Mouse Player)KB/Mouse Is surprisingly comfortable but you have to look up how to get to the controls and also change the game in the graphics settings to reference KB/Mouse instead of controller buttons to make it playable.First Impressions Playing up to just after Goku Vs RaditzPro'sAs someone who grew up enjoying the original Dragon Ball series I was really hoping the story would start out from the beginning instead of just referencing the places with pictures and short snippet stories, but what is there is good.  Story starts from the beginning of Dragon Ball Z, but the nostalgia is still strong.Game play is Okay, Fighting mechanics are 8/10 even with KB/Mouse It becomes very comfortable-----Con's 90% of the fighting and materials grinding is insanely painfully repetitive with literally the same enemy being the only thing you fight in the same group of 1-2.  You'll avoid grinding fights not because they are tough but because you cba to push 3 buttons to grind the fight or deal with the 15 seconds of cut scene getting into each one.  Gathering mats is even worse, it isn't tedious, it's dreadfully simple. The open world game play reminds me of Spyro level cringe friendliness even though The DragonBall story and DragonBall Z stories are NOT overtly kid friendly, and it's referenced that they aren't very early on with reminders of Master Roshi's pervy old man role coming up a few minutes in.First mission of walking Gohan to a fishing spot will make you want to become an actually abusive father immediately, on top of it is also immediately buggy with Gohan potentially getting stuck on and inside of map objects forcing you to restart the "mission" of escorting him the most painful 100 meters of your life.Besides that, I ran into game breaking bugs twice after beating Raditz of the post cut scene, in game cut scene having potential for perpetual sliding off characters who move, and possibly taking place inside of map objects, all of which will freeze it because they never reach their marks to trigger it to end, forcing you to restart from the last save, which is Stage 2 of the Raditz fight.   Other reviews have mentioned that this bug exists in future scenes as well, so it's a constant gamble throughout the game.------ConclusionI want so much to enjoy the game, and I will finish it, but with this many bugs and the painful open world content I can't recommend anyone pay more than $30 USD at the high end for fans of the series.  In 2020 and with this amount of money on the line, this level of simple bugs they had to ignore from start to finish.   It's pretty bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Loading...Loading...Loading Screen ZZZZZZZZ!All joking aside, Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot is one of, if not the best DBZ RPG games ever. Starting at the beginning of Z and going through the entire series, if you remember the old Legacy of Goku games, this is basically a HD version. Or if you want to get a little more obscure and oldschool, it's a HD Remake of Legend of the Super Saiyan from the Super Famicon.CyberConnect2 could have went with the easy route and just retold the DBZ story with an RPG bent and it still would probably have been okay. However, they decided instead to RPGify the story. All the staples; levels, random encounters, skill trees, party members, NPCs, side quests, collectables, TCG minigame, color-swapped enemies, all here for your enjoyment. Not an open world per say, the areas are divided into large, open sections for you to explore. You can explore famous landmarks; West City, Kame House, The Lookout, King Kai's Planet, and the areas around them. You can interact with the cast and the people of Dragon World.For the purist out there though, you may not like all the 'filler' and 'nonsense' included. The game goes to great lengths to showcase the world, from stories and quests in between the Sagas, to just little things to help flesh out the characters. One example is Goku feels far less like a forgetful, deadbeat Dad in this game than in the Manga/Anime. The game does included the Japanese Dub if you prefer that over the English Dub. It even includes the original opening, CHA-LA HEAD CHA-LA. From the way the game looks, to the sounds and music, to just flying around, they did an amazing job of capturing the Dragon World. You feel like you are in the Anime. I just have a blast flying around, seeing the world, collecting things. One thing the series is known for is powerful fighting and not all DBZ games have managed to capture that feeling. I feel like Kakarot does. Each punch has a nice feeling of power to them, the blasts explode in brilliant color and the transformations are strong but also drain your KI. So you have to manage that along with health as you dart around the arena. Praising the story in a DBZ game is something I never thought I'd do. We all know how the story goes; Saiyans, Namek, Android, Buu. However it's not just how they handle the story, with accurate-to-the-source scenes, but also how they expand upon that story. Side quests about getting Bubbles some unique bananas, how Puar misses Yamcha after his death, to even more unexpected ones like helping some Space Tourists visiting Namek during Frieza's invasion. After all, isn't that what we all want? To spend more time with these characters? Not only when they smashing in faces but also when they are relaxing? I would say the game is 90% voice acted. I haven't tested to see if the Japanese Dub is 100% but some of the side quests are not voice acted. Some are also weird too. Like part of it will be voice acted but as you play through it, the quest will suddenly not be? All the important moments are voice acted though! By the original cast (which was already mostly Christopher Sabat anyway) at least the English side. A nice addition is the fact that this isn't just the Goku & Vegeta Show. You do get to play as other characters, like Gohan, Piccolo, Krillin and if you can't play as them, they get to be in your party; like Yamcha and Tien. While the fights are flashy and a sight to watch as you punch, blast, and warp around the open map, they all boil down to just mashing the attack button. Your character will do a series of combos but you can only watch Goku kick or Vegeta blast someone so many times before it becomes boring. So a long time ago, in the ancient era of the PS2, games were designed to hide their loading times/screens in unique ways. PC games often had a big loading screen in the beginning. I know as games have become bigger, loading takes longer. My issue comes from when the loading screens appear. They often appear in the middle of a cinematic, when the scene is changing. It only lasts a second or two but for whatever reason, that rips me out of the immersion. The screen could have just stayed black for a few seconds longer and I would have been perfectly okay. So this CON depends on your commitment to the original source material. With the expanded storyline and the gameplay in between the Sagas, I would have liked the Movie Storylines to fit in. Sure, the movies themselves don't fit except for a couple, but it would be easy to fit Cooler, Android 13, Broly, Bojack into the story. Maybe through the Dragon Balls?I cannot express how much I have enjoyed this game. When I was younger, watching the show, playing the games, all I ever wanted was a big, RPG-type adventure through the series and now we have it. The game isn't just good for fans of the series though. I believe anyone who enjoys fast-pace action RPGs or JRPGs in general would enjoy this game. The DLC is also not necessary for your enjoyment. There is an online aspect with the card game, called Dragon Ball Card Warriors but I have never tried it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Dragon Ball Z Kakarot is an enjoyable light RPG which re-tells the story of the Dragon Ball Z from the beginning of the series, through to the end of the Majin Buu Saga. Whilst the dredge of playing through another game which re-tells the almost thousandth times told Dragon Ball story has been told. It remains to be a enjoyable and albeit pretty experience thus far. The story is split into pseudo-chapters in which you play from different characters perspectives as the game progresses, with significant portions of the story split and title carded to make you feel as if you are directly watching an episode from the TV show, which is a nice touch. In the sections of down time you are given between completing the story you are able to freely fly around the areas of the game collecting orbs which can be used to train the characters abilities, uncover secret areas, complete side stories which give insights into where characters from the previous Dragon Ball series are during the unfolding events of the story and fill small plot holes left over from the show itself, and change party members out at will once you've progressed far enough through the game.The combat feels solid enough for an action RPG, being able to swap out a characters special abilities and changing party members which allow better combo chaining or suiting your play-style more accurately, with certain characters focusing mainly on defending you from large scale attacks, or being frontal attackers allowing you to inflict more damage in one swoop. Although I find myself hardly using the movement controls during the game random encounters, a large amount of fights thus far have mostly consisted of me using the dash button to close in on enemies, combining melee attacks and finishing with a special ability and holding the block button after in case they retaliate with a heavy damaging attack. This isn't the case for the Boss battles however, where movement can prove to be a useful asset in dodging and weaving through the enemies attacks. I feel as if a bit more solid variety in the random encounters would flesh out the open world a bit further and make fights feel a bit more rewarding.From an audio standpoint the game gets a perfect 10, everything is here, all the original voices for the characters and even the soundtrack. Major scenes in the story are lovingly re-created in 3D with the music from the series syncing to the scenes perfectly

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'd like to start by saying that, in general, I'm a big fan of DBZ games. I played most of the Budokai/Tenkaichi games, both of the Xenoverse games, and have been an avid DBZ fan for most of my life. So, going into this game, I'll admit that I didn't have high expectations. I expected an experience similar to Dragon Ball: Xenoverse, where you rehash all of the key battles from the Dragon Ball Z series with some running around in between and a couple of role-play elements. Man, was I wrong. This game is a MUST HAVE for any DBZ fan. While it is true that you engage in all the key battles from the DBZ series, such as Goku and Piccolo taking down Raditz and Gohan turning Super Saiyan 2 and wiping out Cell, there is so much that happens in between these battles. You get to train, learn new attacks, do cool side quests (called sub-stories) where you help the Ox King find the perfect gift for Master Roshi (hint: It's a Girly Mag) and save a wayward chef from vicious robots, and monsters, and whatever else (poor girl gets attacked a lot...). There is also a really interesting meal system, and for anyone who loves DBZ, you know how much our resident Saiyans love good food. Or okay food. Or any food. Also, the "Community Board" system is really interesting too. It revolves around you collecting character emblems and applying them to different boards to boost your stats in game. There are also a lot of throwbacks to Dragonball. Eighter (Android 8) shows up quite often, and you can collect pictures, which are scenes from Dragon Ball with a little description of what's happening.Overall, I give this game a 9.5 out of 10. Almost perfect, and the things that bug me are so small that it's really just nitpicking. If you're a fan of the Dragon Ball Z series, you definitely need to get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It started out great. Interesting fights, vast world, lots of little things to do and collect, pretty graphics and the guide book that holds information about characters, animals, vehicles and other stuff. Additionally you can replay past cut-scenes which look remarkable. You can collect dragon balls to revive old opponents (to fight them again for additional rewards) or gain resources.The problem is that sometimes "less is more." There is too much meaningless filler in this game. I don't have problem with the game having filler but i have a problem with it being of a low quality. Majority of the sidequests are fetch-quests with uninteresting story. Items that are sprinkled over the open-world are just glowing points of light of different colours that you touch to collect or colorful orbs that you press "B" to collect. The worst part is that you're just mindlessly flying towards the next point on the map, trying to avoid enemies on the way (because the fights become a chore after a while), you collect the item and then hope the quest automagically teleports you back to the questgiver to finish that quest.Basically, there is too much downtime, where you are not engaged in any interesting way. Envoirments are pretty but uninteresting. There is no exploration or unique locations that would make you stop to look at them. There are some caves to open up that hold two or three resources. There are Z-orbs which ahng in the air and which you collect to level up your skills. It feels like those elements were added to artificially inflate the playing time.The guide book, while having some good content, also has plenty of entries that are short descriptions that don't bring any interesting knowledge - the majority of the animal section is like that. I would throw all that out or condense those pages into a single page (really, there is no point in having a description for every fish in the game, when for the most part the're just a recolour or a modification of an existing model).There is a (dead) online card game here as well. I think it would have been more interesting if it were part of the main game (KotOR did this well).I don't want to go into detail about the fighting system - plenty of other reviewers did that, plus, there are youtube videos. The main fights are great. All the other stuff becomes a chore. Especially when you have to fight 1 vs 5. I'm not talking about difficulty here. I'm talking about more mindless filler. The spectacle fights look great, the mechanics though detract from the fun.I think the game was spread too thin. It would have been better if it focused only on one saga but with more detail put into the environments, mechanics (both mini-games and fights) and side-quests.The first two dlc's are said to be bad but the third one is supposedly much better than the main game. At this point though, after the Cell Saga, I'm burned out.
