_childDocuments_.review: This was a very pleasant surprise for a DBZ game in my opinion. I know most DBZ games before this were their own re-telling of the story, but having a world to interact with during the story made it so much more enjoyable to me. I had a genuine blast playing through the story, I played on Hard only encountering some issues during the earlier sagas. I was doing all of the sub-stories that I could alongside the main story, which did unfortunately make some of the later fights a fair bit easier. So if you decide to pick up this game and want have a better challenge, I would highly recommend saving sub-stories for the "post" games (finish Buu saga).While I do have a fair bit of genuine praise for this game, I would like to mention that some of my complaints stand out a good bit, as few as they may be.Gathering, while not an issue to me because I passively did it while doing quests, hunting dragon balls, being out and about in the world, etc, getting ***any*** "higher" quality item will have your character making a comment about it. Every time. Back to back. This complaint isn't only limited to gathering items. Passing enemies of weaker, stronger, whatever variety, they will also comment about that. It becomes a thing so frequent that if I wasn't exclusively doing the main story missions, I would turn the voice settings off while playing.This one is potentially a personal issue, I was never able to find a solution for it though, but I did encounter some frequent audio fluctuation. I had most settings pretty low (4-8 "ticks" in the settings), I thought things were a decent level that nothing was overbearing to the other, but sometimes at random, the general sound effects (Ki blasts, specials, hits taken/given, flying, entering a new zone) would be SIGNIFICANTLY louder for just a moment, then go back to normal.Overall, I would say this game is like a 7.5-8/10. It's really consistent throughout the playthrough, and it really scratched my nostalgia itch for the DBZ sagas.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are expecting this game to be anything like a remaster of Legacy of Goku II overhauled to over 9000, you will NOT be disappointed. The map is huge with pretty much every location featured in the manga/anime present in the game including the iconic Korin Tower, King Kai's Planet and a small portion of Snake Way, Kame Island/House, Grandpa Gohan/Goku's house, all of East City, and the entirety of Namek just to barely scratch the surface. You will not get burned out on exploring quickly.  Throughout the course of the game you will get to play as several of your favorite characters including but not limited to; Goku, Gohan, Vegeta, Piccolo, and Trunks to name a few. Each character can be leveled up and enhanced so you can pour your time into your favorites to make them all powerful and most of the other anime/manga characters major and minor can be unlocked as community members with each one giving you unique bonuses that change depending on where and how you use them. You play through pretty much the entire DBZ timeline starting with the Raditz saga on through past the Cell saga. It's not canonically accurate as there are several changes in the dialog and order of events with some being more subtle than others; but overall this is still possibly the best DBZ game ever made. The graphics are beautiful and the boss fights are fun and diverse with 360 degree fighting action and a skill tree that lets you power up iconic moves such as Piccalo's Special Beam Cannon or Vegeta's Galick Gun. The fishing and mining elements grow stale after a while and you will get sick of the random battles that happen when you're flying around. (Seriously its like fly ten feet, fight some robots, fly another ten feet, fight some saibamen; it wears thin quick) but other than this the game is overall exciting and refreshing. The key mapping can be a little annoying if you don't have a controller but I am proof that with a little patience you CAN figure it out (I made a cheat sheet). Also they could have put a little more effort into giving unique icons for the individual items but that is just me being nitpicky. At the end of the day DBZ Kakarot is beautiful and loads of fun to play and one of the most well developed games to come out in the past few years. This is one of only a handful of times this year that I feel like I actually got my money's worth out of a game. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: DBZ: Kakarot is just fine. I think that's what makes me not want to recommend it. In a sea of exciting DBZ games and adaptations (not even to mention the oceans of good action/adventure games) this game just really treads water and makes me yearn to play something with more robust implementations of it's core elements. Let me state the obvious: If you're a fan of DBZ looking for an engaging way to relive your favorite moments from the series, this is for you (maybe not at full price, but on sale or something). If you're new to DBZ and want to "relatively quickly" go through the series and engage with some of the best parts, this is for you too (again, not at full price). However, as a longtime fan of DBZ and action adventure and the like (some dare to call this an RPG, I wouldn't go so far), whenever I'm not in those moments, I just find myself wanting for more and wondering why they made the choices they did. Again, nothing egregiously terrible, more like...outdated and surface level. THE VERDICT: If you're a massive/new DBZ Fan who wants to experience the hits: get the base game on sale (DLC 3 and on are the only story additions, but imo none are really worth the price of admission). If you're someone looking for a good action/adventure game with fighting and RPG elements. There are far better out there.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10, for a game called DBZ: KAKAROT you spend an great part of the game playing as everyone else, which puts Goku's entire role in DBZ into perspective.Anyway, this game is a great RPG game with a very dynamic fighting system. The quests can get a bit boring as it's mostly go here then go there then go back there, then again most RPG games follow the same dynamic.What impressed me most were the fields and maps, they really did an OUTSTANDING job with them, fights could go all over the place, you could be fighting i the mountains then in the ocean the back in the open sky, it doesn't restrict you with fake barriers or at least I've never into one (and I play really chaotically). One very small downside to that is that some major scenes seem small or not as powerful because in the anime it focuses on the area affected but in this game you could see the vast lands even beyond the battle, which is a nice way to show how big actually the earth is and still base Vegeta from Saiyan saga could blow it with a relatively small attack.As I said the fighting system is dynamic, it allows you to move swiftly as you attack and dodge and keep safe distance if you plan only on hitting and blocking then oh well... but movement is a huge part of it. There are combo variations too but I still can't figure them out.SOME scenes are not in the game, which may disappoint some people, but the rest of them make up for that lacking.Overall, and as I said,  a very solid RPG game with very dynamic and enjoyable combat mechanics. Would recommend it to Dragon ball fans because this game actually tries to fill in a lot of the wholes from the original story and would even Recommend it to someone new to dragon ball and willing to explore the universe.oh and there's a gacha game too. as an advice: stay away from gacha kids.

_childDocuments_.review: Dragon Ball Z: Kakarot genre: fighting rpgdeveloper: Cyber Connect2 Co. Ltd.publisher: BANDAI NAMCO EntertainmentTHE BASE GAME:We follow the story of Dragon Ball Z without a lot of the filler episode stuff, but the game is long enough as it is. Soundtrack-wise, you will find a lot of the old classics from the anime, but also new versions and the whole soundtrack is perfect. The graphics are amazing and the animations are even better. The game is optimized really well. So, with a good enough computer, you get stable frames and can enjoy the main part of the game - the combat. You get put in a big arena, where you can move freely and it consists of standard punches/kicks with which you make combos, but you can also fire ki blasts. You have the ability to supercharge, but you can also break your opponent causing them to freeze and allowing you to hit them freely with all your attacks. In combat, you can use super attacks like Kamehameha, Super Beam Cannon or Gallick Gun to name a few, that help you take down your opponent, but you can only use them, if you have enough ki, which you get by standing in place and charging. In some quests or while freeroaming, you have up to two additional characters in your party that help you in combat, where they beat up the enemies and charge their supers, that you can use for them. A massive part of the Dragon Ball franchise is transforming and this game doesnt lack that. You will find every transformation you can remember and they will offer you boosts in combat at a small cost. The combat was done perfectly and the only thing I would say is bad about it is the balance of some enemies according to the manga/anime. Out of combat, you can explore the vast open world filled with sidequests, orbs and collectibles with which you fill your encyclopedia. While exploring, you may come across campfires or special chef NPC's, with which you can cook special meals from gathered ingredients that give you temporary or permanent buffs. You get a lot of the cooking materials just by roaming the wild and capturing animals, but also by playing a fun fishing minigame, that will make all the og fans feel true dejavu from the very first episode of the original Dragon Ball manga/anime. Aside from cooking materials, you can also come across caves filled with various ores and rare items, with which you build and upgrade cars and other robots. After getting enough orbs, you can upgrade your characters or unlock their new abilities. If you choose to do the main story, you will be happily suprised with dejavu filled voice lines and cutscenes. Every important aspect of the Dragon Ball Z story is included, so don't be afraid of the game missing something. Have you finished the main story? Dont worry! You still have a lot of stuff to do. Some recommendations would be getting all the steam achievments, completing the encyclopedia or upgrading everything to the maximum. Overall, I haven't enjoyed a game this much in a pretty long time, so I would recommend it, and if you're a fan of the series, make sure you get the DLC's for more content. A NEW POWER AWAKENS DLC SET:This set of two DLC's brings the Dragon Ball Super series into the game and I've got to say that after the main game, I expected a little bit more. The first DLC consists of getting put on Beerus' planet as Goku and Vegeta and training with him/Whis. Here, you unlock god ki along with god transformations and new abilities. This was a fine catchup for the second DLC, but it got repetitive really fast and only really helped you improve your gameplay. The second DLC covers the "Ressurection F" movie/saga and it brings back the action from the main game. You get some new side quests, but also a cool main quest line with Frieza filled with cutscenes. As a set, I would recommend it, but be prepared to grind. It will come with a prize of course, the Frieza part.TRUNKS - THE WARRIOR OF HOPE DLC:In this DLC, you get put into the life of future Trunks during the Android Saga and a part of the Buu Saga and experience the world as it was for him and his friends. As a massive fan of Trunks as a whole, this was a treat to play for me.Trunks starts off young and weak, but by losing almost everything and everyone dear to him, he transforms into a powerful warrior. After losing his sensei, future Gohan, he achieves super-saiyan and starts training on his own until his mum, Bulma makes a time machine. Using it, he travels to the normal timeline, which he helps save and trains with the other heroes. After getting a massive power boost in the present, he comes back and destroys the Androids in his timeline, avenging everyone. After that comes the future Buu Saga, where the Kais train him with the Z-Sword and he defeats Buu, Babidi and Dabura.This DLC was, for me, the best thing about the whole game and I loved every single moment of it. I just wish that it was longer, but even as it is, it contained some stuff, that we've never seen before! If you enjoy the main game, do not even think about buying this and start playing it as soon as you can!

In a nutshell, I would recomend this game to people that are fans of DB series, and people that want to get into DB series, otherwise I wouldn't. One of the reasons is price. In my opinion the game is overpriced for what you get. Standard edition is like 60 € and Ultimate edition is like 90 €. In standard edition you only get game itself. In Ultimate edition you get game, tao pai pai pillar that is like 1 € dlc which I acctually never used because you can fly much faster, you also get one cooking dish which is absolutely useless because, if you cook dishes you will probably  be making full course meals because dishes gives you patetic boost, like 2 HP or 1 DMG. You get also music pack, and you get season pass. Season pass is the only good thing in Ultimate edition, because you get 2 new "little" stories (so far only one, but other will come out soon i hope) which are probably DBZ films and one new story arc (as I said only one thing came out). Story is DBZ story so I have nothing to tell there, it is good. Last cutscene is absolutely fantastic, and I see that they put so much effort into that part of the game. On the other hand, animations in cutscenes are to stiff. Idk how to describe it, they just dont look right. _childDocuments_.review: It's not a perfect DBZ game. There are flaws. But it's an insanely enjoyable DBZ game with a lot of love for the source material. It is by far the best way to experience the story in a video game and offers more things to do, the further you progress. Pros:Play as multiple characters and use support characters that travel and fight with youBest story adaption in a DBZ video game and offers tons of playtime in the main story aloneBuild a hover car and robo walker at Capsule Corp and level them up with materialsYour support characters eat meals with you and travel in your hover car's passenger seatGohan and Goku can ride the nimbus all over the world (Including Namek and Supreme Kai Planet)Plenty of opportunities to find fights even in the post-gameCollecting Dragon Balls is very quick and intuitiveThere are several large zones to exploreSwimming underwater is a featureTons of OG Dragon Ball characters and references returnOriginal Japanese music included in the sound trackMini games such as hover car time trials, robo walker time trials, fishing and baseball battingCons:English lip sync is horribleQuality of cutscenes is often inconsistentGame design seems to cut corners a lotToo many fetch questsToo many loading screens in between fast traveling to different zonesNo combos or grapple attackNo difficulty optionsYou can infinitely use healing items in fights and never loseNo NG+ Not enough Post-Game content

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:   Amazing visuals and animation.           Smooth gameplay.           Quest hunting is actually fun.           Entertaining gameplay mechanics.Cons:  Repetitive music.           Extremely easy and no challenge.           Absurd DLC that breaks the game.           Unnecessary RPG elements. This game is a thumbs sideways for me. Its fun but does a lot of things wrong. My most frustrating problem with the game is that it presents RPG elements like a level up system but completely undermines them. In pokemon you had to grind quite a lot to fight a boss in the game, sure it was time consuming but it was very rewarding once you beat it. In this game when you complete a mission you earn a bunch of EXP causing you to level up multiple times and when you finish a chapter you gain 15+ levels. This shouldn't be bad given the fact that you don't have to grind but its not satisfying at all. Enemies in the overworld are pretty much meaningless and you can just ignore them, so why add them at all? It bums me out when i proceed to the next saga and my Goku (level 30) goes to level 60 in a matter of seconds. Its disappointing and dull. Don't even get me started with the music. You hear 1 track, 1 TRACK, in the overworld, that's it. After 20 repeats you'll want to mute the music and it'll be much better. The music pack DLC isn't worth it either. They're the same tracks from FighterZ and Xenoverse and it should be free because they're practically milking it. The DLC story is garbage and lazy. You can access the DLC at any time and what it does is basically give you a major boost at the beginning of the game. in 10 minutes your Goku goes from level 1 to level 40, Gives you super sayian 1, 2 and 3. So if you want to have an easy experience and break the game's point of getting stronger as the story goes on, go ahead but it will be very boring. The games combat system is simple but fun, mostly because of the combos and the visuals, but there is literally no challenge at all. It is so easy, i just wish it didn't have a set difficulty. I wish the game had options to make the game harder, like in dragon quest. For example, the game doesn't let you cook or doesn't let you buy anything, things like that. Overall its an OK game, every fan of the show will love this because of nostalgia and because its "Dragon Ball". I don't think its worth full price, maybe $40 but not $60. Its a pretty good experience but not the best. I'll give this game a 6/10. It could've been so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Dragon Ball game, but a "so-so" RPG. Definitely the best Dragon Ball game I've ever played, and I'm excitedly looking forward to some hopeful DLC where they continue to add stuff from the anime/manga past the end of Z (ie: DB Super.) There were some bugs around, several obnoxious ones (such as where you'd leave a cave and be completely unable to fly until you left the zone and came back. Not even saving/reloading would fix it) and many amusing bugs, including NPCs spinning around in place during cutscenes, items not being used from my inventory when I went to use them (leading to infinite items until I saved/reloaded/restarted the game), to the Dragon Balls being instantly gatherable again after making a wish (it's supposed to take 20 irl minutes, but one day during playing they just instantly reset. The downside to that is Bulma kept telling me the balls were available to collect every time I changed zones... but that was a minor annoyance towards my goal of getting all the sidequests done)Overall, definitely worth playing if you're a Dragon Ball fan. I got ~52 hours out of it so far, but I spent a lot of time doing side stuff that wasn't really necessary (such as clearing a few zones making sure I got all the orbs... I wasn't aware at the time that the orbs respawned if you leave the zone and come back, but that was a good 5+ hours wasted there)I really, REAAAAAALLY wish there could be some kind of collaboration done with the DBZ Abridged guys... I'd pay full price for this game (again!) if there was an option to have either the story changed to match what was done in DBZA or to have the DBZA crew do full voice work for the story in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the best way I can start this review is by saying that the game is good - it's another run through of the same story we all know, and that's about it. For the game to become an open world JRPG is great, don't get me wrong, it's a concept I've wanted for a while and it works... alright... but I think there's a lot that could be done to make it better, the open world aspect becomes a bit mundane once you repeat the same things over and over, within the first couple of sagas at least. I feel that story wise, there didn't have to be many cut outs that there has been, personally I feel like having a longer story would have been great, because with the time it had taken me to complete each saga, it felt like it took no time at all, and that's a small issue for me, I would have preferred depth instead of sub stories that feel like filler... but... useless filler. Stringing on from sub stories, filler and the mundane tasks, the sub stories are basically just the same thing, but with different characters, and that's literally it unfortunately. Gameplay wise, it plays great-ish, if you've played any of the other previous Dragon Ball releases you will be able to get easily acquainted with the controls. The overall sense of the way the game played out, was pretty good if I'm honest, big attacks during different moments made everything seem explosive (no pun intended) although after a long time fighting would become just quite repetitive, do A,B,C to attack get hit, A,B,C again, etc etc. The last thing I wanted to talk about is the "Dragon Ball Experience", and how well the game makes you feel like a Z fighter when playing. It doesn't. But. Does. During the Frieza saga and Goku obtains the infamous Super Saiyan form, I expected to be more, blown away (still no pun intended). Super Saiyan was a rocking point in DBZ and it honestly just felt like "oh. okay. this is cool", I just expected more from it. When you get to fighting, it just... doesn't feel like "Super Saiyan" and the way it's painted out to be, you don't feel powerful at all (and if I'm honest it feels the same at all of the "great" moments). However I also said it does and honestly there was only one point during the game when that happened - the cell Saga when Gohan get's Super Saiyan 2. During that moment you do feel powerful, you actually feel like you've got SOME sort of power, but that's literally it.All I can really say in short is that the game is good - some moments are made more captivating than others (story wise) and gameplay is a 6/10 at best.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:  -DualShock 4 support-Graphics are pretty much on par with the anime.  It literally feels like I am watching the DBZ.-They did a great job with the fightingCons:-Running/Jumping/Flying.  It doesn't feel or look right.  It doesn't feel DBZ.  Seriously, there's 100+ episodes to reference from.  How did they get this wrong?-Enemies variation.  You're literally fighting the same robot over and over again.  I knew this before buying but i didn't think it was going to be this bad.  This was really sugar coated when I was doing my research.  Be prepare to fight these guys every 30 seconds or less.  If you ever watch DB, the Red Ribbon Army consist of more than just this robots.-Skill leveling.  You need these dumb orbs, a certain level, to pass a certain story check point and more of these dumb orbs.  Had to give stuff to Chi-Chi, nope she can wait because you're collecting these dumb orbs.  You don't know what they're used for yet but you collect them because they're all around the place and it's probably important.  Had to go check out the place where Raditz landed BUT wait, there's all these orbs you should probably collect because you found out they level up your skills.  You collect more orbs.  Need to go rescue Gohan from Raditz so you level up your skills but you notice all the orbs you collected so far, was not enough and you need to collect more of these dumb orbs.  Who thought of these dumb orbs!!! The worst part is, running, jumping, flying and that stupid robot isn't your friend.  This game should have been titled, DBZ: Pirate Robot and the Orb collector.  Spoiler Alert!! In case you don't know who the orb collector is, that's YOU!  You're the master orb collector!Other Thoughts:I seriously don't recommend this game but at the same time I did not ask for a refund.  Not because I couldn't ask for a refund during my orb collecting time but because I am hoping BANDAI does a better job on the next one.  You can't have a sequel if the game flops or if no one is going to supports the game.  I just hope they make a better DBZ action RPG.  I'll give this game another go when I feel like fighting the same robot over and over again or if i feel like i want to become a master orb collector like all the other positive reviews.  If you like DBZ and collecting stuff, this game is for you.  (orbs is the main collectible but there's other stuff to collect also)

_childDocuments_.review: KAKAROOOOOOOOOOTTT!Is how i feel when ever i play this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. Now dnt get me wrong, the DBZ vibe is here in full force with flying around the world and powering up each character... but so much of the vibe is lost when you discover combat is very repetitive and super spammy. Whats worse is that the bosses ONLY spam super moves. They never try and just melee attack you or try combo's, but rather sit in the back and rotate super moves. Plus when you do get close to stun or combo them, you get countered but an unblock-able stun counter. So you have only two real choices, try and keep at range and spam supers or try and close the gap but get very limited damage through and then get stunned. _childDocuments_.review: Really, really great game for Dragon Ball fans. Personally, it's my favorite combat system out of any of the 3D dbz fighting games. Xenoverse 2 is close, but this game has a sense of weight, power, speed, and visuals that really separate it from DBXV2. As for depth, DBXV2 has an objectively deeper system. I also believe this game has the best graphics out of any dbz game, or anime games in general. It feels like Dragon Ball, which very few anime games can say about their respective show. Furthermore, the animations and voice acting feel less like the VAs were forced into doing the lines and more like they gave it the same amount of attention as the anime and movies.The story is great, as is it is a retelling of the original DBZ storyline, from the Saiyan Saga to the Buu Saga. One of my personal favorite fillers from dbz is also included as a side mission: the driving lesson with Piccolo and Goku. The combat and abilities progress very well with the story, as transformations, ki super attacks, melee super attacks, etc. unlock with mostly the skill tree, and some with the story. The leveling system is well done, but some skills are locked behind a specific story event even if you reach the required level, which makes sense as Goku would unlock super saiyan in the fight with Frieza and not before it. The visual effects are done really well. I'd liken it more to DB FighterZ than DBXV2.Where the game suffers is the open world exploration. Although easter eggs and the collectible photographs/polaroids are cool for DB fans, it suffers for a non-DB fan. I'd still say the exploration is enjoyable. Also, the game rarely tells you where to find specific items for certain side quests. I can't remember the exact name, but there was this one type of fish I spent ages looking for and couldn't find. Then I looked up on Google where the fish can be found, and I found the amount I needed tenfold. Though, mini-games such as fishing and hunting are nice. The open world exploration is more of a feature you won't think much about instead of actively disliking.The DLC is decent. The later DLC are definitely the best. The first two, the BoG and RoF ones are just for level farming and DBS abilities and transformations. But, I do like how although there is no new game plus, you can unlock all abilities (even super saiyan) before you even reach Namek. I bought the legendary edition on sale, so I recieved all DLC. The price for each pack individually is not worth it, so I'd recommend to buy the season passes if you want the DLC. The following DLCs are good, but not great. They are enjoyable, but short and don't provide enough content. All in all, the DLC do not compare to the original game, in quantity and quality. The best DLC are either the 23rd World Tournament or the newest one with Uub, in my opinion. tl;dr: great combat, great story, great skill tree, great graphics, good open world, decent exploration, decent DLC, mixed side quests (some really good, some worse)

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is an honest review because well, I wasn't the biggest fan of DragonBall Z Growing up I was a bigger fan of Guyver, Vampire Hunter D, Street Fighter etc. anime styles than DBZ, so I didn't really start watching the series until I was much older. Being said, I finished up series about a year ago, and had been looking at this game with all seriousness just because it looked fun, and had that RPG Feel, but I'm cheap and wanted to wait for it to go on sale, glad I caught it on the most recent sale (Last sale I saw it was 5 or 6 months ago) so I made out. Now if you're a fan of the series of fighting games, this ones a bit different. It's an RPG with some fighting features at it's core, but nothing really extensive as far as controls & moves like previous fighting games. The whole game is built on the unreal engine so the graphics are really nice and the animations aren't too bad. But to sum it up you're playing from Goku & Friends perspective of what seems to be the storyline of DBZ so far, and I'm not trying to do any spoilers on myself, just a normal play through just to see how close it is to the TV series, as it feels like that's the route the story lines go. Now onto some more of the good stuff before we go onto the stuff I feel is a bit muddled. The controls are easy to learn, take about 10 minutes or so to adjust to, you can customize them, my X-Box controller works perfectly for almost every bit of the menu stuff I've encountered so far. The fighting sequences although flashy have really odd camera angles and the flying on the Nimbus or just regular character flight take some real getting used to, I don't feel that by default they are measured correctly, so you may need to tune them as I will get around to that myself. Gameplay is open world, there seems to be alot of content & subcontent, side quests, mini games, and other things to keep you occupied if you're stuck on a boss. Raditz was fun and a bit challenging and also a good push to begin the game with so that you understand how everything works together. So I think a lot of folks will be very satisfied with the way the open world game play works. You can farm items, if you're that person, you can grind out XP for levels by killing zone mobs. So there's a ton to do and the learning curve really isn't bad. The Bad: I really don't have much bad to say about the game, I've noticed some minor things, that aren't gamebreaking in design like background changes aren't exact during battles, just some small things, nothing that breaks the game or makes it unplayable. Just minor stuff, and again I've only been at it for about 4 hours, and I'm sure I'll update this more and more as time goes on, but so far, I would definitely recommend this game to most people who are fans of the series, and want to just play through as your favorite heroes the storyline.

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game! Yes it is yet another retelling of the same story. However I would say this is the best telling of that story in video games that I have played thus far. They stuck pretty close to the Kai show and hit all the important notes expertly. The cut scene animations were top notch, sound track was excellent, and graphics were great. The final fight with Buu with out giving to much away damn near brought a tear to the eye with the way they did it. Very well done in my opinion.As far as actual game play goes I thought it was a very fun game to play. The combat admittedly was pretty simplistic and straight forward. So if you are looking for a complex fighting game this isn't the one for you. But it was fluid and satisfying to me. The boss fights added some cool mechanics in the form of their special moves. I LOVED the surge system (I called it full power mode). In most dragon ball games when you power up you never really feel stronger. The dmg you do goes up but your character doesn't feel different at all. But when you activated the surge mechanic all your hits became more dramatic and felt heavier. It really made me feel like my character was more powerful during that time frame and I loved it.The RPG elements were decent enough, though a bit to simple if I am being perfectly fair. The community board was a fun little side distraction. But past boosting your characters stats with meals you really couldn't do to much. I would have liked to be able to change out fits or something but that is not possible. So sadly the RPG elements could have used a bit more fleshing out. But the map itself and travel within the world felt really good to me and I enjoyed flying around to the various places. The side quests (quests not involving the main story) were pretty lack luster if I'm honest. They were mostly just fetch quests and none of them were voice acted which was lame. But if you are a hard core Dragon Ball fan the side quests add a lot of nice nods to OG Dragon Ball and some more obscure lore things that I appreciated a lot. But they would admittedly be lost on the average person. There were some other side activities such as random world encounters, villainous fights, racing, and the training chamber. - The random world encounters could get repetitive after a while but they were easy enough to avoid so they didn't bother me to much. - Villainous fights were really fun and a challenge if you didn't just save them to the end (which I recommend not doing). Try them out as they come up, it was great fun and provided a decent challenge.- Racing was fun enough but it was ultimately a time challenge style race. So not the best thing in the world but I wouldn't say they were bad. Building up your car and stuff was fun enough and provided something at least mildly entertaining to do. - The training room was interesting, I liked the power ups it gave you and the fights were similar to the villainous encounters so I enjoyed them. Though they were kind of a one and done thing so not much replay ability there. All in all I thought the game had a lot of great content, some admittedly pretty lack luster content as well. But honestly I have a real hard time giving this game any less than an 8/10. The story was done beautifully, combat was fluid and fun (again surge mechanic was AMAZING), side activities were interesting enough for me to 100% them. Honestly I think this is my favorite DBZ game thus far (I have not yet played FighterZ). Highly recommended to any DBZ fan. For those of you who are not fans this is a good game to get the major plot points of the story but some of the nuances of the side quests will likely be lost on you.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s so cute! I love it! Full of wonderfully weird and whimsy creature designs, all with their own little personality quirks, Penko Park is an on-rails photography collecting game with light puzzle elements. You start out with basically nothing, just a cart that you can’t control but as you take more unique photos and better quality photos you gain experience which unlock stamps to access new areas and gain new abilities (such as the ability to pause the cart or grab items in the distance).Creatures are very easy to miss, some blend in with the environment, others require you to do things before they will appear. You have to do similar things to other creatures making to them react and have certain poses to complete their index. Each level has multiple routes so it’s not possible to photograph every creature on a single level playthrough. It took me approximately 2 hours to get enough experience to make it through all four levels and reach the boss but there is plenty of replayability in seeking all the creatures and unravelling their mysteries. It can be difficult to figure out where to find missed creatures in the end game as the photo album gives no hint about their whereabouts other than the level they are in and even when you do find them - a couple of times I found it was deceptive as for some creatures spawns it's impossible to get three stars photographs however that is just end game, for most of the game finding the creatures is entirely fair and finally completing the photo album was very satisfying. For completionists - there is one annoying luck-based achievement (What are the odds?) and although it is possible I didn’t get it through natural playing of the game. Fortunately for me it only took about 15 minutes of replaying meet the requirements. All in all, Penko Park is a rather short game but an absolute joy that I highly recommend. Simple, creative and full of little surprises.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever seen an idea so niche you never even considered others could possibly attempt it? For me, that was the idea behind Pokémon Snap: repeating stages over and over, on rails, manipulating the environment around you and unlocking new paths with the goal of taking the best possible pictures of the wildlife around you. For a long time, I associated that idea to that specific game. I never even thought anyone would attempt to follow on those footsteps… until I saw, and played, Penko Park. And I can safely say: I am really happy I did!------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- You are a visitor who arrives at Penko Park, an abandoned wildlife park. As soon as you get there, you are greeted by a cute little creature called Penki, who serves as your guide through the different trails and stages in the game. It gives you your “complimentary Penko Snap-A-Lot 9000™”, which you use to take pictures, tells you to hold on to your seat, and off you go on leisure cart rides through different stages. The game is, after all, set in a wildlife park, and it does a good job of emulating that. Penkos run past your cart, others observe you from afar, and some even interact with each other.  How, you may ask? Well, they make it so a Penko’s expression changes, and as you will see in the photograph below, each emotion is a different picture for you to take. Be careful, though! There is a limit of 35 pictures you can take every time you go on a track - though admittedly, I never hit that limit. And you can increase it eventually.One thing you’ll quickly find out, however, is that a lot of these expressions and events are unavailable at first.  At the end of a run (which usually lasts around 5 minutes at default cart speed), you get given access to your picture album, where you can paste your new pictures, and replace old ones, should you happen to get a better version of it. The album is divided by stages, with each stage containing pages that cover all the Penkos and their respective possible poses.  - it may seem like a chore, but it certainly didn’t feel that way (and getting 100% is not needed to beat the game). When you originally start the game, you begin with barely anything: just a camera, a cart and a dream. But as you unlock upgrades, you gain access to things such as a grappling claw that allows you to grab things in the tracks. This, in turn, allows you to trigger switches, which opens up new pathways for your cart; allows you to grab Penko collectibles for your album and even unlocks new Penkos and expressions (as some are not very happy when you try to grab them or their possessions). Not all upgrades are this substantial, but there are a few that do unlock loads of new possibilities in your cart rides - which is good! It helps the repetition feel… less repetitive.Now I know you may be wondering about the repetition above, which I have yet to explain, so here it goes:  In fact, the game “only” has 3 large maps and 1 small map. Most of your time will be spent going back on the same tracks over and over, seeing lots of the same sights, chasing new and better pictures.  Your upgrades are well spaced unlocks, meaning that throughout most of the playthrough (about 4 hours for 100%), you will be getting new tools, which will allow you to see new sights (whether new paths or just new expressions/penkos) in old maps. Don’t get me wrong: eventually, you will run out of new things to do and just have to re-run the maps over and over trying to figure out how to get one creature to show up or do a certain expression. But some late game upgrades also help make that process faster.Now, the gameplay may be the crown jewel of the game, but what about the other elements? Story, art style, audio design… they’re also important parts of the experience, and the game thankfully delivers on them. Well, kinda on the first one.  As you progress through the levels, Penki may make observations about the Park, which give you some of the story and lore of the game (and they’re often… not happy in their nature). Furthermore, you will find buttons on the track. Pressing them will give you the lore of some Penkos (which work as hints on how to get them to change expressions), or tell you the story of the park itself. That’s not all, but I’ll leave the rest for you to find. Throughout your journey, you will find lemons with wings, spiders holding pieces of ores and even sentient lava blobs. Even the most complex ones - such as the giant creatures seen off in the distance - are still pretty simple in their design and concept.   While it isn’t anything impressive, they do use it really well. Oftentimes, you will only be dealing with ambient noises (which can be creepy on its own - like hearing a bush rustle as your cart goes past it), but as you enter certain areas, you will also get actual atmospheric tracks that really help set the mood. With all these combined, the game does manage to hit the atmosphere they were going for. It’s not scary, mind you. Not even close. It’s just cute and, at times, slightly creepy. And it is great. - though not with performance, it ran great here (rtx 2060, i7 8700, 16gb ram, 144fps). There are moments when you simply won’t know which creature you’re missing in a stage, or how to get another creature to do a certain expression. And sometimes, it feels like not much is offered in terms of guidance, in some cases. While I didn’t get stuck, I acknowledge that some expressions I only got because I accidentally looked at the right place at the right time. And to some, this might not even be an issue, but rather a characteristic of the genre - but still one I would be remiss not to mention. The game is also short, and slow paced (especially in the beginning), which will turn some people off. But none of these were a detriment to my enjoyment. Bottom line is: , and if you enjoy exploration and/or loved pokémon snap, this game will also probably be right up your alley!

_childDocuments_.review: Have you played Pokemon Snap and just want more? Or maybe you just don’t have a Switch and want a Pokemon Snap-esque game? Well, Penko Park has your back. Penko Park actually came out before New Pokemon Snap, and fun fact on my birthday too (!), but I had no idea it released until I finally played Wunderdoktor, looked into the developer’s other games, and saw this one. And it was finally time to play it.Welcome to Penko Park and I hope you don’t have anywhere you have to go for the next couple hours. This takes place at a mysterious and abandoned wildlife park named Penko Park. For most of the game, you’ll be riding on a cute little kart, making this an on rails photography game, and guided by the cute Penki. As you’re riding along, you have a camera which you can use to take pictures of any of the creatures you see. As long as the creature is properly in frame, the camera will recognize it and once you take a picture, you’ll automatically get rated and see the name of the creature. You’ll also see how many different poses you can get the creature to do and which ones you already did or ones that you need to get a better score on, which is so helpful if you’re aiming to do everything. Based on what the games tells you, and from playing, your score is based on how in frame the creature is in, and you’ll naturally get a lower score if there are flora in the way or if they’re too far away. Anyway, you’ll continue down the path being able to take pictures of any creatures that you happen to pass before you arrive at the end.And that’s the core of Penko Park. You’ll be riding along, enjoying the scenery, and taking pictures of the many creatures that live here as well as different poses that they do.At the end of each area, you’ll be able to select which picture you want to put in your little photo book, though it will default to the higher scored photos. The photo book also gives you a quick line bit telling you a fact about the creature or maybe what someone said about them. You also get to see all of the creatures in the area on the first page, which acts as a way for you to enter it as well, and which ones you fully completed.You’ll start with only one location starting out, as well as just the camera and the normal kart, but you’ll be unlocking more as you take more pictures. You see, with every picture you attach to your photo book you gain experience. This will eventually unlock a stamp which you’ll use to get further along the (sort of) level up path to unlock areas and things. You get to unlock four other areas (though the last one is more story-related than anything) making it a total of five areas you get to ride through and upgrades for you kart, like giving you an option to give it a boost or stop, and your camera so you can zoom in more. Though, more importantly, you can unlock more tools which will help you in taking photos and generally to get everything. There’s a grappling hand so you can grab artifacts or cute hats for Penki to wear, pull levers, destroy fragile fauna/rocks, and to hit info signs if you want to know more information about the area. You can unlock the ability to have a turn signal which lets you go down paths you unlocked by the means of your other tools and an upgrade which can perhaps let you see into the spirit realm. There’s also Penko Balls which seem to kinda be a treat, which can get creatures to change their pose, though some won’t like it (and I may have accidently pushed a creature off a cliff while they were sleeping, don’t tell anyone). And lastly, a Penko Wand which lets you play a song that you can find on signs in each area and this will let you get a pose from creatures (which are marked by the sign somewhere around them) and the rocks with those symbols on them actually correlate with the Penko Wand songs and playing the corresponding song will cause it to lower revealing something.With every upgrade and tool at your disposal, getting pictures for every creature and all the poses, as well as all artifacts and hats if you want to go even further, is difficult. Getting the basic picture is easy, but some creatures are hidden pretty well (and the way to unlock an alternate path can be hidden well too) and it can be difficult to figure out what you need to do to get that pose you’re missing or maybe figure out where else they appear as that pose might only be able to happen in the right environment. Not to mention that the artifacts and hat boxes hide pretty well behind other flora or objects and can easily blend in (especially the artifacts).The only thing I would say I wanted was the ability to save your photos as screenshots.Penko Park was quite fun, though I don’t think I’ll be able to find everything. While the game does feel boring starting out, it did quickly grow on me as I got to see the park and the unique creatures that inhabit it. What I planned to be maybe an hour turned into several as I couldn’t stop until I unlocked every location, tool, and upgrade as I wanted to see the other areas of the park and what other creatures (and designs) the game had in store. I’d definitely recommend picking up Penko Park if you’re interested in photography games, and especially if you want a Pokemon Snap-esque one.
