_childDocuments_.review: Thanks to Special Offers section in Steam I got to discover and play this game!A bit surprised about how good this game is, because it had better mechanics than the New Pokemon Snap. Yeah, the main game is a bit short (less than 3 hours), but I enjoy every minutes of it, and gonna try to complete the collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: PROF. OAK: Wonderful!The best Snap-inspired game I've played thus far with branching paths, reactive creatures, secrets, and everything you'd expect if you've played either of the Pokemon Snap games. This game doesn't have as much content as New Pokemon Snap on the Switch, but for the price ($12.99 USD normally or $3.89 USD on the current 2022 winter sale, which is what I paid) you get more out of it than you paid in my opinion. Penko took me about 5 hours to 100% with a little help from guides, but it was for leftover artifacts that I couldn't find for the life of me. The little monsters are adorable, sometimes spooky (in a cute way, not scary), and worth exploring this cute little world for.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: It's Pokemon Snap on Steam. So, I really liked Pokemon Snap on N64. I know, I know, it's a game for five-year-olds, but it was so much fun - travel around different locations, keep your eyes peeled, take some good pictures. Well, that's what this game is... just with the random monsters of a different imagination. It's kinda weird - this game is quite a bit simpler than Snap, and yet... I think I liked this one more. Heck, the graphics aren't even up to the Snap level (Snap was 3D, super animated, blah blah blah... This one is hand-drawn-y, simple animations, etc) - and I still think I like this one better. My ONLY disappointment was how quickly I "beat" the game - I'm showing 4.2 hours logged as of writing this, and that was with trying to take my time to enjoy (rather than trying to "steamroll" the game).Don't get me wrong.. as soon as I fire this review off I'll be headed back to try to get better pictures and collect the rest of the artifacts, search out the missing monsters, etc. I just... wish there were more, because this was really fun.So you've got your scrapbook, your camera, and you're ready to roll. You go out, ride in a little cart (looks like a witch's cauldron with wheels lol), and you go through the different environments. You unlock things along the way - like the grappling arm, or the penko ball, etc. Most of the game is just careful watching - looking around, trying to sniff out the creatures. You throw Penko balls to get a reaction out of the creatures, or you use your grappling arm to pick up artifacts. You add the pictures and artifacts to your scrapbook.. and I really like that you keep the pictures and can view them later. If you end up getting a better picture... great, update your scrapbook!What's really great about this game is that you actually WANT to find all the creatures. Maybe people who enjoyed the old Pokemon games know what I'm talking about - sometimes, when you play one of these "gotta catch 'em all/tons of creatures" games, you find yourself... unimpressed with the creature collection. Feels like a cheap rip-off. You don't get that feel with this one - I really was motivated to find each completely unique creature and get the best pictures possible. Yeah. It was fun.They're so varied. Some of them seem perpetually terrified. Some of them are goofy. Some of them are creepy, some of them are angry... Some of them have completely unexpected surprises waiting! "Oh, how cu-WHOA!!! DUDE!!" I don't know. Overall, it's a pretty silly game. I paid the full price, but in the end I felt it was worth it, despite how quickly I "beat" it. And like I said... I'm about to hit "post review" and go back to take some more pictures (haven't quite finished the collection yet!!). So if you were in any way, shape, or form involved in the Snap game or Pokemon in general.. I think you'll really enjoy this one....And the art just makes it all the more enjoyable. Developers did a GREAT job making their art come to life. Just thought I'd throw that in
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I discovered this game today, on its release, via twitter and was immediately pulled in by the art style and concept. I decided to buy it and play on stream and it was an absolute blast for me and everyone watching! The game is well written and witty, the pacing is just right in terms of unlocking things, and the story is great! The story is told through the descriptions of creatures you find, as well as signs throughout Penko Park, and through other little secrets. Absolutely worth purchasing, and if the devs ever release DLC I plan on being the first to buy it! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, fun, fun! Very reminiscent of Pokemon Snap, the only difference is that it's better.So yes, it's an indie version of Pokemon Snap but without the Pokemon; and for those of you unfamiliar with Pokemon Snap, both it and Penko Park are railshooters where the only thing you "shoot" are the pictures you take with your camera. Instead, the developers have created a very rich and diverse world of creatures for you to explore through four detailed levels. As you go, you level up  and unlock abilities and perks to help you snap pictures of these exotic creatures. Overall the amount of interactability and the various paths you can take keeps you engaged with the level beyond just taking pictures of all the creatures.All of these elements keep the game fresh as you run through the same levels multiple times to tease out all the various poses and moods you can find the creatures in that need to be photographed (for example, a few creatures only have one standard pose, where as others have several poses/moods that each require its own picture). Rerunning through levels is standard in these games, and it's the sign of a game well made when the developers make this prospect both appealing and rewarding.Admittedly if you are going for every single achievement you  get a little irritated on hunting down some of the sneakiest creatures in some of their rare poses, at least if you don't use guides to do so. I never quite reached this point, so my only personal criticism of the game is that the rating system (your pictures are rated on a scale of 1-3 stars) is very simplistic, it's based entirely on zoom and doesn't take into account focus, background, other creatures being in the shot, etc.Otherwise, all other elements of this game, be it sound effects or visuals, are well-crafted and really work together to give the game a unique and special charm. Everything comes to life, both the environment and the creatures you are tasked to photograph. I can't recommend this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Is it horror? No. Is it horror adjacent? Kinda. Penko Park is a spooky cute version of Pokemon Snap with it's own unique visual style and a flair for the absurd. You ride a cart through a long abandoned wildlife park and take pictures of the creatures that have taken back said park. This will take you through lush forests, underground tunnels, magma rich volcanoes, and even underwater. There are no scares here, no adult scares anyway. Sometimes an area can feel foreboding, but it's quickly offset by a goofy little creature doing a goofy little thing. The controls are tight and the progression system is fun and rewarding. The real challenge is completely filling your scrapbook with perfect pictures and artifacts...and of course hats for your tour guide. Definitely buy this game if you like taking pictures of weird creatures in weird places with a weird little feller that rides in your mine cart with you.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Slightly embarrassing, but this game is the reason I finally made a steam account and bought my first PC game ever (never formed the habit growing up, fully an adult). I saw someone playing it, and HAD to try taking the controls myself. Extremely worth it. It's like a quirky, slightly sinister national park full of endearing art, fascinating critters, and clever tricks to get the perfect pic. Not being a 'gamer' by nature, I tend to balk at needing fast button dexterity to move on, and this game starts challenging, but pretty quickly lets you unlock the ability to slow down and really linger everywhere. It's a really charming little slice of wilderness with a satisfying little ending, to boot.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: (This review was written before the Shivering Crypts free update, which added content to the game.)A rail shooter with the genetics of Pokemon Snap.  Its biggest differences are that it eschews the grading period and each creature has to be photographed in multiple poses.  While the lack of major grading makes repeating stages less fun (even if there are multiple paths one can drive), it keeps the pace fast.Its story is underdeveloped.  I kept expecting it to turn creepy, but it never does, it's just playfully morose.The game is short and easy, around 2.5 hours to get to the ending which is probably not too variable because stage progression only requires collecting stars from photos and you hardly need many to continue.  Extra abilities are also unlocked through collecting stars from photos.  Thankfully a boost function is unlocked early to reduce repetition and make it easier to hunt for extra creature poses and artifacts after finishing the game.It's cute, fun, and snappy in a fairly rare genre which makes it pretty easy to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly the best "pokemon snap" style game I have ever played. The weird creatures are delightful, the power-ups are well paced, the lore is darkly humorous. I also appreciate that while getting 100% isn't too impossible, the game only requires about 60% completion to see the end level. For me, after using the unlimited pause power-up to have a really, really good search - I still had to use a guide to get about 5 last tricky poses. 10/10 keep resetting my save file and coming back to this.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Calling this game "horror" is a real stretch. It's cute as heck. You are guided through an old wildlife park with weird fantasy creatures in some kind of photo safari, and can work on completing your album with pictures of the "animals" in different poses/moods. There are "artifacts" to collect, info posters with lore, abilities and new areas to gradually unlock with a kind of XP/level system. The creatures are a lot more funny and adorable than spooky, unless you're five years old or something? The most "horror" thing I've noticed is the questionable ethics of the park's founder that shine through in some of the info and notes. It certainly seems like a rather light-hearted family-friendly game, but I've had lots of fun with it. * * * I collect chill and story-driven games in my curator .
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy little game in which you traverse 4 levels repeatedly while trying to snap a picture of every  Penki in each of their poses. Collecting more (and better) pictures grants you abilities such as throwing something at Penki for a reaction or playing a tune for them to dance to. Cute. Also consider  if you want more of the such.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up loving Pokemon Snap, I absolutely adored Penko Park! An incredibly detailed, relaxing photography game, with many secrets to uncover and cute Penkos to meet. Environment: 10/10. For me the sounds make the game. Each Penko has its own voice, each level has its own distinct mood due to the sound design. But it doesn't hurt that the art is also adorable and whimsical.Gameplay: 9/10. The pacing felt perfect for me, though some may find it too slow. I deeply appreciated the helpful mechanics you earn as you progress. The only thing I would say is maybe a mini game or a challenge mode could add some variety (but the Achievements do a pretty good job of challenging). Story: 8/10. Lovely design, with character info written in for many of the Penkos in a nature park/safari style. I like the humor as well. Lighthearted, not terribly deep, but fun.I want to add a note about accessibility and the UI/HUD as well, because these were game changers for me. The ability to  (a feature you earn later on) made me so happy, because after a certain point I could take the game at my own pace without feeling rushed. Additionally, certain HUD features that allowed progress tracking mid-level made it so I didn't have to run a level over and over again while trying for 100%. HUGE stress relief. Lastly, the sound cues for certain collectibles are an excellent touch, so it's not solely an "I spy" mission for the toughest secrets.Overall I highly recommend this game if you're looking for something peaceful, whimsical, not too challenging, and you like nature and/or photography games!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: EXACTLY what I wanted. Pokemon Snap was easily a top-five game of my childhood, and I feel like this game hits that particular nostalgia synapse in a way that a straight up remake never could. I'm also a sucker for a combination of cute and creepy, and Penko Park NAILS that aesthetic. I think it's a better game in many ways than Snap, or the recent sequel, especially because its environments are truly beautiful, and its creatures are all pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ weird and fun. It's goofy, it's compelling (game-play wise), and it's easy to learn. Each new ability requires no more than one run to get the hang of. I'm trying to think of a down-side and all I can say is that (2 hours in) I can tell it's going to be over quickly, and I'll want more. That said, the ability progression and the wide variety of ways to interact with the world make it so that I'm (so far) always happy to return to past levels. I don't know what the end-game content is for this game, as I've done my best to avoid spoilers, but I'm pretty sure you could power through this game quickly. I recommend taking your time, and not stressing if you miss a photo or item on a run. That just means you have motivation to go through the level again, and you can spend more time enjoying the art and weird little dudes all around you. This world feels very full and fun. 10/10. Please make a sequel. (But I'll be following whatever these devs want to do down the road.)
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: As a Pokémon Snap fan who is eagerly awaiting the new game, Penko Park is a great taster for the time being. It's not very long (neither was the original Pokémon Snap) but the beautiful art style and the Snap-esque gameplay make it worth the price. It really does nail the Snap feel! Genuinely, if you liked Pokémon Snap then you'll like this, it's very close.On its own merits, this is a lovely little on-rails-photographer game. If you like games that have an aesthetic or a unique feeling as their base selling point, Penko Park's slightly eery, but lush and vibrant setting and the unique animals will be enjoyable for you. It's satisfying to take photos of the animals and drag them into your photo album, discover artefacts in the wild, and unlock new ways to manipulate your environment - keeping every level fresh as you replay them to complete your album.Even though I recommend the game, there are a few things that make it feel a little less complete than the game its based on, I think the biggest thing is that the point-based system which you are evaluated on in Pokémon Snap is absent from this game. It would have been nice to get a better score on a photo by having a group of the same animal in one photo, but as it stands in Penko Park the other animals of the same species are pretty much just an extra opportunity to get a decent photo of the animal by itself.The other thing that's missing from Penko Park is interactions between two different animals, resulting in new photo opportunities. This was a big part of Pokémon Snap, as you would make one Pokémon do something which would have a knock-on effect, and lead to unique photos worth a lot of points or photos of new Pokémon altogether. I understand that Penko Park has a small team though, so I get why that sort of thing is missing.On the whole, considering the price, Penko Park is a fun little collecting game where you take adorable photos of weird animals. If you like cute games, games with fantastic art, or... Pokémon Snap, then you'll find something worth your time and money here.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a rail-shooting game where you ride on a trolley and have to shoot all the targets on your way, it looks the same, only you take pictures, but you will not be able to click all of them, and also open all the secret passages at a time, since your cart goes non-stop, and you will have to dive into this chic atmosphere of an unusual abandoned park again and again in order to farm photos for your research album.You can collect collectibles or activate something with your unusual extending hand, similar to a special tool from the video game "Poppy Playtime". You will also have Penko® balls, by throwing which you can excite the monsters, thereby opening up new emotions from them for capturing on film, as well as a musical stick.The idea of ​​the game is just awesome, it captivates and relaxes you with unpretentious gameplay in a good concept, collecting new shots, you upgrade new skills, no one forces you to farm everything at 100%, you will collect a full skill line in 4-5 hours, but on the other hand game practically does not get bored, it is exactly as much as needed, there is even a well thought out final boss.Although, of course, after the first location, the rest are not so atmospheric, and the lore of the park is not something outstanding, rather childish, although in some places you can catch some serious jokes) The game cannot be called something incredibly outstanding for the gaming industry, not even 8/10, but this is such a typical "local masterpiece", an example of a good "farming game", which will leave a lot of positive impressions for connoisseurs of unusual indie-games.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: According to Bartle's Gamer Test I'm 93% Explorer, so I guess the game hit my soft spot.  You're being taken on a ride through an abandoned monster safari park, and your quest is to take photos of the different life forms in their different conditions. The (monster) design is unique, the names are creative, the animation super cute and the environment beautiful, the underwater section is my favorite. It's a cute and relaxing game that made me want to return and explore more. Thumb up.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly a passion project from people who loved the Pokemon Snap games growing up, but updated very intelligently for modern audiences. The slightly spooky aesthetic meshes really well with the uncanny nature of it all, but the monster designs keep them feeling cute. I only wish that the spirit dimension could have be integrated in a more interesting way in terms of gameplay. For what seemed like a really interesting mechanic while you worked towards unlocking it, all the spirit dimension really acts as a sort of bonus "secret" collectible, instead of really adding a sense of verticality to the world. A very well paced game that refuses to waste your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Want to go on a weird safari? well then heres a game for you!Penko park is an exploration game in the vein of Pokemon snap, you sit in a cart and are driven on a tour of the abandoned Penko wildlife park, as you travel through the park you take snapshots of the various animals that inhabit the place, in many ways its like a rail shooter.Of course theres more to it that simply riding passively through the park, there are numerous collectables to find and alternate paths to open up. And simply finding the various animals isn't all there is either most will have multiple poses to collect so you have to figure out how to get them in addition to just finding the animal, for the most part this is fairly easy as the interactions involve only the target animal itself, but there are a few situations where things get complex (like using one creature to scare another) its just a shame that there aren't more of these in the game (like scaring away a predator causing a new creature to come out or something) but I can see how that would be alot more work for such a small team.Overall Penko park with its charming artstyle and atmosphere is a short but highly enjoyable experience and one that fills a niche that is somewhat lacking here on steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazingly cute.  It is about 4 hours till credits, but you won't have found everything if you finish that quickly, so you can go back in and keep taking pictures to find everything.There are a lot of mechanics similar to Pokemon Snap but they feel more useful and less fiddly, and there are a few new ways to unlock areas and fun pictures too.  Almost anything you could complain about not having at the beginning you will have after unlocking everything, so you can eventually line up your perfect shots with ease.I like how you know what pictures you still need once you focus on a Penki and you can tell if you've taking a 3 star shot right away.If you are looking for something with a kind of creepy feel but not flat out scary this Halloween, consider picking up this game!The areas feel big especially as you unlock new abilities and find the hidden paths.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: A really delightful game. Obviously very reminiscent of the OG Pokemon Snap, but with better QoL (you can charge your throw, late game you get an unlimited stop ability). The creatures are interesting and creative, and the game in general is also great to look at. The text is enlightening and bizarre, though I will say, I was not expecting the amount of dark humor. The pacing of getting new unlocks wasn't bad either. Like, I didn't have to go back to perfect each level and get tired of them.Took me about 2 hours to 'complete' the story, and then 2 more hours to get all the achievements. But somehow it felt a lot longer than that (in a good way). The levels have just the right amount of creatures, secrets and story, so they don't feel empty, but they weren't too crowded either. Just a fun, charming experience. Also, there are hats. Definitely recommended. 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game. Similar to Pokemon Snap, as others have mentioned. However, I'd say this one is more fun. The way the unlocks are spread out gives each zone tons of replayability. The quality of life upgrades you can earn for your treks make the game even more enjoyable, and feel earned, without making the game too easy. The star-rating system for the pictures actually makes sense, and I can usually tell why I got 1 or 2 instead of 3 (not close enough, not enough of the critter in the picture, etc) instead of the random crapshoot that is in Pokemon Snap. Very worth the price, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: It’s difficult to not compare Penko Park to Pokemon Snap and even harder to judge the two without nostalgia getting in the way. However, what Penko Park excels at is replayability. You will have to complete the stages multiple times to progress through the story, but the unlockable tools and features are interesting enough to keep things fresh. I am also impressed with the overall quality of this game, especially when you take into account that the developers didn’t have an established IP to center the game around.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: : its very charming!! you should play it if you want a short game about finding cute spooky critters that features exploration and a tad of mystery. definitely play if you like pokémon snap.(i realize this review is very long and that my english is somewhat broken. i'm just a brazilian guy who wanted to leave my thoughts here for whom it may concern)pokemon snap is a game that resides very close to my heart, but that for decades hasn't received any love from nintendo or game freak. although penko park was launched after "new pokemon snap" was announced, i'm pretty sure that its development started before the announcement happened, in the timeline where we didn't know if there would ever be another official pokémon snap. as someone who also lived in that timeline, i feel great empathy for this game.penko park keeps both the game flow and core mechanics of pokémon snap. in both games you stay inside a little car that goes through a level, and you take pictures of the animals, trying to frame them so they don't look like crap. once in a while you need to interact with the creatures to shoot a rare photograph, and after you've taken enough photos, the next level is unlocked. and because you usually can't take enough pictures in just one run, the intended flow of the game includes replaying the same levels again and again.the DNA of the games might be the same, but like dizygotic twins, they don't feel the same way.first of all, the aesthetics of penko park are totally different. the game is set in an abandoned park, so everything is ~spooky~ and mysterious, and there's a mood of mystery and fear as you reveal more and more details about the true nature of the park. on one hand this mystery corroborates the feeling of exploration created by the game's mechanics (you never know the next critter yuo might find), and on the other hand it thematically unites the levels in a way that snap never could (with its videogamey adjacencies of "water level" and "lava level"). the "abandoned park" theme also provides a decent explanation for the "700 species in a space of 3 feet", something that snap also couldn't explain very well.the aesthetics is also what helps penko park face its biggest challenge: the fact that it isn't a pokémon game. in a game about taking pictures and finding new critters, the player needs to actually care about the critters, or else everything is going to feel forced or bland. snap took advantage of the fact that every kid already liked pokémon, but penko park can't pull the same trick. the challenge then is to create 100+ critter designs that are both captivating and different enough from each other to capture the player's interest. luckily, penko park handles that without much stress, thanks to its phenomenal art direction. the artists managed to make tons of simple but expressive designs: this is the creature that sleeps but it's angry; that is the tree that camuflates; and that one is the dung beetle that dances. they are instantly memorable and interesting, which urges the player to keep playing the game and finding new ones.there's another system in the game that help makes the critters memorable: the scrapbook. in the original pokémon snap, you just gave your pictures to professor oak and received a generic congratulation, but in penko park this whole process is much more elaborate. first of all, you are responsible for pasting the pictures in the scrapbook, and everytime you do that you receive a funny little flaovr text that provides some insight about the nature of that critter. this not only makes them feel more alive and interesting, but also frequently reinforces the ~spooky~ vibes of the game. these texts are so well-written that they became to me a true reward, as big as finding the critters themselves. not only that, but in your scrapbook you not only put the photos of the creatures but also some objects related to them that you find scattered around the levels: bones, eggs, poop. these objects really act like "special stamps", such that finding one is more rewarding than usual; this whole object system didn't exist in the original pokémon snap and is a very refreshing improvement. also it's pretty funny because i didn't have the slightest idea of what the object was until i read its description in the scrapbook (is this some kind of egg? a skull??? oh its poop)the pacing also deserves praise. just like in snap, to unlock the next level you must reach a minimum score that practically requires that you repeat the previous level at least 3 times. i remember it being kind of boring in snap, but here it rarely becomes a chore because you're always unlocking new stuff, be it a new way of interacting with the environment or a new upgrade for your trolley. this continuous chain of unlockables, together with the existence of multiple paths in the levels, makes the level-replaying process much less "aurghh i don't wanna replay this just for that one critter" and more "what can i discover now?"my main criticism of penko park is that it ocasionally betrays its own mystery theme. it all stars with how it simplifies the scoring system from pokémon snap: the numeric scoring was transformed in a 3-star system, and you always know how many stars a photo is worth immediately after shooting it. i don't have any gripes about these 2 decisions, but this one really fingles my jingles: every time you point a camera to a critter, the game tells you exactly how many pictures that critter has, and which ones have you taken. on one hand this makes the game easier for players who want to "complete the levels", but on the other hand it makes the gameplay resemble a checklist: you completed 73% of the level, X Y and Z still remain, good luck. it feels like the game is encouraging a 100%-completion mindset. this reduced a lot of the "exploration" feeling for me, and i don't know if i'm a fan. other minor mechanics also reduce exploration, for example the fact that the camera's crosshair turns red everytime you point it to a creature - that means you don't need to actually pay attention to the environment to find the creatures, you just need to shake the camera randomly and wait for it to detect something.related to that, penko park's biggest problem is the absence of secrets. in the game's first level there's a rare picture that you can only take if you throw a critter over a waterfall and then take a specific path thorugh the level that takes you to the end of that waterfall (you need to make the mental connection and realize that the lake is the end of the waterfall). it was a pretty magical moment for me, because it's basically a puzzle that tests your knowledge about the geography of the level and about the creatures themselves. sadly, it's also the only example of its kind in the gmae that I could find. this kind of stuff wasn't that rare in snap (e.g.: finding gyarados, magneton, charizard, slowbro etc), and it made the game so much more mysterious and interesting to explore. also, in penko park there are very few creatures that interact with each other, which also hurts the immersion since although they're in the same environment, they basically always ignore each other. i missed that.but these are all nitpicks of someone who played, loved it and wanted it to be slightly different. even the way it is, penko park is a joyful experience that I would recommend even to people who haven't played Pokémon Snap. I wouldn't be surprised if Penko Park is actually better than "New Pokémon Snap". we shall see...

_childDocuments_.review: Such a spooky-cute hidden gem! I truly cherish this game ♥ The atmosphere is so chill and the art style is unique and wonderful. The goal is to explore locations taking photos of unique creatures with quirky names. You need to catch adorable monsters on camera in different states, collect items related to them and also find hats for your cute little companion, Penki, who is telling you its story through the game. Penko Park never bores you, because the more you play the more you unlock different perks and abilities to interact with surroundings and creatures. If you want to complete the whole collection and on 3 star rating you will always find something new in your adventures and have thoughts like "Oh how could i miss that!" And it was so fun to find all those secrets and complete the game on 100%!Big thank you to the developers for this game, it was such a delightful adventure ♥ Would pet Smoll one million times!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I've played it to "completion" and had a lot of fun..... but now it doesn't feel fun anymore. And I feel really bad about that because it's a genuinely good game. But now that my first experience with it is over, I don't think I'll ever be able to feel that same excitement that I did the first time I played it. _childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Packed full of surprises and replayable levels- trying to get better pics on one animal and BOOM theres one you never saw- getting different paths and figuring out the "puzzle" aspect of getting the best shot is def gonna keep you moving through this cute and kinda creepy game 10/10 would erase my memory to play fresh again and again- ALSO!  with a 5 Hour complete time for those puzzle savvy people its a GREAT GAME TO STREAM!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I loved my time in Penko Park. It was short, sweet, and worth every penny.First off, the game is just so incredibly charming. Everything from music and sound effects to character(s) and creature design feels like it was made with love and care. The 2D-cutout look works really well and makes all of the different elements stand out from each other (but not too much).Controls are simple and snappy, and the upgrades provided by the leveling system often builds on existing controls while also making it even easier to capture the exotic wildlife. Apart from the main photography-mechanic, the game includes collectibles and a very straight-forward leveling system, which adds a nice incentive to explore the maps and get better pictures.The subtle story is endearing and well-tied together, and made me want to know more about the Penko universe and its inhabitants.I would absolutely love to see more from this game, and I do wish there were even more parts of the park to explore. For what it is though, Penko Park delivers a relaxing on-rails scavenger hunt, which feels incredibly well tied together.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. Not only does Penko Park make for an amazing indie successor to Pokemon Snap, but it puts its own uniquely mysterious spin on it. The journey was surprisingly well polished as well, with excellent pacing, and lasting exactly as long as it should. This is easily one of my favorite games to release this year, and I encourage everyone to check it out and refer it to a friend as well, it deserves much more attention than it seems to have gotten so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Yep, it's Pokemon Snap, but it's also every bit as good, branding aside. You'll know what you're getting into, but the mechanics here are arguably a slight improvement from its inspiration overall, and though there are only three proper levels (though it seems more will be added in the near future), they are a VERY expansive, critter-packed, and secret-stuffed three levels (seriously, you'll be impressed by how much they managed to squeeze into THREE levels). If you're a fan of Snap and the aesthetic here works for you, this is simply a must play. Good stuff, excited for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: One hell of a ride!Definitely was not sure if I would enjoy it, however if you like cozy and somewhat silly games, this is a great one. _childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: What a cute little game. Absolutely charming and very hard to put down until you find all these magnificent critters. _childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: This is the EXACT definition of "A cozy game that isn't about farming for once"It's got cute creatures that are a little messed up! It's got surprises around every corner! It's got a lot of little power-ups that can overwhelm you at first, but they are given with the promise that you can always go back again and again at your own controllable pace!This is the game for people who don't want to miss anything- people who want to explore every little bit as slowly as they want, without ever having to start from scratch to achieve that. You constantly build on progress and lore, learning as you go without being punished for mistakes or wrong turns.The art style is unique and whimsical, the lore dystopian with a satisfying ending, and most importantly?THERE ARE HATS! HATS FOR A CUTE LITTLE GUY!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: A whimsical entry in the sub-genre of animal/creature collection games, where you are sent through various biomes/regions in an abandoned theme park, attempting to take pictures of all the bizarre fauna that dwell within and along the way try to figure out the (sorta dark/unhappy) story of the park and its shuttering.The art style is like pale construction paper cut-outs, similar to a faded National Film Board of Canada vignette from the late 70's/early 80's (if you know what I mean), which lends it an exaggerated, somewhat grotesque children's book atmosphere.Overall the game is quite enjoyable, but I do have some quibbles....Positives:*Art Style*  I dig it, but not everyone will.*Gameplay*  Mostly fun and entertaining, with that vague undercurrent of grim unease running through the game, but the gameplay is also a negative feature (see below).  Snapping pictures of the various beasties in assorted poses (yes, in order to get 100% completion, multiple creatures must be captured in multiple poses, such as growling, smiling, flying away, etc etc) is enjoyable, up to a point....Meh:  The music is a little meh, and while the art style is generally appealing to me, after awhile the faded out colour scheme does get a little too drab for the game's own good.Negatives:*Gameplay*  You are literally on rails (running on a theme park/zoological attraction train ride) and even though new discoveries will unlock new abilities which enable you to find new branching paths and new creatures, over the course of the game (if you want to 100% it) you will see the same trails/tracks many, many, many, many, many, many times.  So, what began as enjoyable fun, slowly but surely becomes drudgery by the last couple hours of the game.  Whether that's enough to turn you off of the game is up to you.So, a largely entertaining game with some pleasing attributes, hampered by the eventually repetitive (to put it mildly...) nature of its level design/gameplay.  I did have fun, so I'm absolutely going to recommend it, but it's not a flawless game by any stretch of the imagination.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and relaxing game. You can finish pretty quickly, but if you want to collect all the things, it will take a bit more time. I enjoyed it so much I went for 100%. Well made, I ran into zero bugs. The creatures are cute and wild at the same time. Would highly recommend. Hope more is added in the future, either through updates, or I would be more then willing to buy a expansion to continue the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I love all the different areas, critters, and details hidden in this game! The lore and story is really intriguing, and I'm looking forward to going back to 100% everything! I did receive the game for free, but I was NOT paid to leave a review. I just really enjoyed it that much.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Pokemon Snap, but available now! Travel through several levels, collecting pictures of creatures, manipulating their poses, and grabbing items. As you level up (by getting points for good pictures) you gain abilities such as being able to grab things, throwing items at the creatures, choosing different paths to take, and changing the speed of your cart. It's very charming and, while the mechanics seem very similar to Pokemon Snap, all the new creatures are fun to learn about. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: 💡 Pokémon Snap lovers pick it up now!The goal is to capture the best photo you can of each creature. Also, you'll want to catch their different states. No, I'm not getting existential on you. For example, a sleeping animal vs an awake one. Taking the perfect photo is a little tricky, the game doesn't explicitly explain how to do it. But they do tell you immediately when you have the shot which I appreciate. In fact, the game tells you a lot of information on the camera. The information includes a little red dot when you're over an animal, the state of the animal, and your previous grade on the photo. A great set of features which removes the guesswork and makes the game more friendly.After you finish the level it's time for some scrapbooking. You go through the photos you've taken and selected which ones are added to the book. It's pretty simple and you're able to choose the one you like the most but you'll always want to save the photo with the higher score. As you level up your scrapbook you gain stamps which are used to unlock more features of the game. The first item you get is a hand grabber. Used to touch many things throughout the level but not the animals directly.You are going to be playing the same zones over and over but it's not a problem. First, it's interesting to scour very little corner of the level trying to see everything. I've done each zone at least five times and I still haven't seen all the animals. Second, one of the unlocks allows your cart to change directions and there are multiple paths through a zone. The game is a lot bigger than I imagined. The point is the game keeps adding new content quickly.Overall, Penko Park is definitely worth your time. The developers knew exactly what they were doing to make a fun safari. I finished the game and I'm still tempted to go back through and find every one of their creations. The ending was nice as well and brings some closure the park's history.I make legit video reviews,

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:  Penko Park is great, and well worth your time if you like these sorts of games.  No more caveats.  Basically everything that I wished would be expanded on in the original game got polished up in the update and I couldnt be happier with how the game is now.  I think its a testament to its quality that since I got a new computer, and the game doesnt have cloud saves, I didnt mind just replaying it again so I could see the new stuff.  To summerize what I think they improved upon, you have a new versatile tool to play with, more secretive poses and creatures, and a new area with some of the coolest designs in the game (with a few new ones sprinkled in elsewhere).  Feel free to read my original review below if you want more details about what I was hoping for, and what they ended up delivering on almost to a T, but honestly the update kind of invalidated the need for it.  So just give the game a try instead.Penko Park set out to add one more game into the "on-rails wacky wildlife photography" style, making the genre two games big now, and while I think it certainly accomplishes its goal, I cant help but want more.  Dont get me wrong, what Ghostbutter has released here is absolutely worth the 12 dollar asking price.  I had an immensely good time filing out my photo album over my ~5 hours.  That being said, Id still like to offer my unsolicited and likely unwanted thoughts on how the game could be expanded if the devs' "exciting news next year" is a DLC or a sequel.  1.  Larger secrets.  If you are going for 100%, finding all of the creatures is a great time, especially some of the more hidden or obscure ones.  Turning around at just the right time to see something for a flash before you can take a good picture of it is a hell of a dopamine rush, along with scouring the level for the right sequence in order to properly photograph something.  My only wish is there were larger secrets waiting to be found.  Maybe after you do several actions throughout a level, a secret path opens up at the end or something like that.  The game has a great atmosphere for stuff like that already, and I dont think it really capitalizes on it as well as it could.  2.  More tools.  Manipulating the environment is always fun to do in these types of games, but there are not a ton of options here.  I wonder if thats because the expected audience for this game doesnt have any prior knowledge about the creatures theyll be photographing?  Still, even just splitting up the all-purpose penko ball into lets say, a water one, a fire one, and an nature one could result in a lot more critical thinking.  Im not saying this is a good idea, but maybe a burrowed creature will only rise for you if you throw a water ball at it, or perhaps fire will always agitate the creatures, while nature one could put them to sleep.  Adding any more depth to the game is welcome in my book.  3.  Lean in harder on the theme.  The themeing, that being a "spooky-cute" game, is super cool and serves to make the game pretty unique and enjoyable to play.  I had never considered a fully committed horror game in this genre, but man, how cool would that be?  Youre being jump scared left and right trying to snap good shots of the thing you actively dont want to look at?  Id say it would have to be more arcady maybe?  As the scares would naturally lose there punch and you would be left where you started.  The artstyle might not work for a legitimately scary game either, but honestly, I cant help but just want a game like that anyways.  Even if they dont try anything more scary than where they are at now, some of the creatures still felt a little samey.  Roundish body, some limbs, a face, and a pair of wings describes at least three creatures.  Theres a few too many 'orbs with eyes" too. Go cuter!  Go spookier!  There are a lot of really neat designs, so its not like they cant do it.    I know its always easy to ask for MORE MORE MORE, especially when I dont actually have to do anything, but I feel like Ghostbutter is on the verge of greatness here.  I absolutely love all of the little tweaks they made to the standard formula, and with just a little more I think they will have something really special on their hands.

_childDocuments_.review: A little pokemon snap-like that i had a good time with. _childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I love this weird little game and all its quirky little creatures. Adorable and occasionally eerie, Penko Park was simply a joy to play. Having never played Snap before, the whole photography rail-shooter thing was a pretty fresh experience to me. I definitely needed an easygoing distraction today and Penko Park fit the bill nicely.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Penko Park because the art looked fun and charming. I love collection games and trying to complete tasks/badges to the best of my ability, so this type of game seemed to be a decent choice for me. I'm so glad that I got it; the concept is simple, but not boring, and there's an element of challenge despite how easy completion seems. The mechanics are simple and easy to understand; my only complaint is the lack of a feature to change bindings for keyboards and controllers. When playing with a controller, I often mixed up the joysticks and their functions. I feel that the left joystick should be used to move the camera around, and the right should act as a speed control, while this is the opposite (can't remember if that's right, please correct me if I'm wrong).Overall, Penko Park is a very fun and cute game, and it's obvious a great amount of time and effort went into creating it. It's not the shortest game I've played, but it's also not outrageously long and drawn out. It's a good time-killer. I highly recommend purchasing this game if it catches your interest or is on your wishlist.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: In some ways i've enjoyed this even more than new pokemon snap, there is a real sense of progression as you keep unlocking alternate paths, finding hats for your penki partner and learning new songs, the monsters are both creepy and yet cute, loved every second of this game, If you like pokemon snap, do yourself a favor and check this one out
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Good gravy, I can't believe I didn't get this sooner. An absolute delight to play, and it makes me want to go find and play a copy of its Pokemon inspiration. _childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Played this during this year's Extra Life and it was my surprise favorite of the whole day. The gameplay is a relaxing photo safari with light puzzle elements. Wildlife in the park is endlessly entertaining, from their unpredictable antics to the often-disturbing journal notes. There's lots of incentive to keep revisiting areas of the park, whether it's to explore alternate paths, to spot a creature doing a different activity, or just to take a better photo for your album. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Had a craving to play Pokemon Snap, didn't want to buy a switch, so I found Penko Park. Best fallback plan ever! It's adorable and unsettling and I love it. _childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: A blatant rip.. inspired by Pokémon Snap game.But sort of creepy/spooky in a Addams Family or Nightmare Before Christmas way.The gameplay is basically a rail shooter where instead of shooting a weapon, you're shooting pictures.As the game goes on you'll unlock several methods of influencing the world around you in order to make the creatures behave in certain ways that you'll need to capture on film or unlock new routes through the levels.Capture all the creatures in all of their different poses/situations and that's basically the game.The graphics are quite simple, but highly stylized and good.It's very much like a children's cartoon or pop-up book.The sounds are good, although sparsely used and there is no music as far as I know.Now as to would I recommend it?Yes, it's a fun quirky relaxed game with no risk to failure except for having to do a level again.It can be finished in a couple of hours, but 100% completion will take some time.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love Penko Park! If you are a lover of Pokemon Snap you will love this. _childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

The bits and pieces of the lore are definitely some of my favourite things about this game! Even if it's simple I liked it a lot, and some of the picture/artefact comments got a good chuckle outta me lol

_childDocuments_.review: Penko Park, with Player and Penki!While walking through the woods one dayPlayer and Penki saw something strange,a little sleeping Dubbel who liked to dance and playthey followed their dancing friend,not knowing where this adventure would end.The penkos were headed just around the bendWhere are they going?I don't knowHow do we get there?In Penko Park!Me, and you and Penki!!Come along and see whats newWe are seeing the thing the penkos do!New penkos friends to seePenkos park's the place to be!Smoll are charging, acos are leapingNippers are running and nobody's sleeping!me, and you and PenkI!Come along and see whats new!We are seeing the things penkos do!me, and you and PenkI!Come along and see whats new!at Penko Park we're waiting for you!Penko Park!Yes, i loved this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and simple game about collecting pictures. _childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: While the Pokemon Snap influence is obvious, I enjoyed my time with Penko Park much more than the new Pokemon Snap. Each area has multiple paths to explore, and you unlock a handful of different ways to interact with the creatures and environment. _childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: A super cozy, super cute, slightly creepy and slightly surreal picture taking game. I love the designs of the various Penko and it's super fun to see them do a little dance if you give them a penko ball or play the right tune. Collecting hats to make your little companion Penko dress up in them is very fun.A comparison to Pokemon Snap is inevitable, as it shares many of the same gameplay features. While it doesn't have the big name power of the Pokemon series or the sheer amount of content of the New Pokemon Snap, it has its own charm and atmosphere that set it apart reasonably well.All in all I had a blast and it was a perfect game for a nice cozy Halloween.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: First saw this game on a Secret Sleepover Society stream but only just tried it out myself. So fun! I love the artwork, the sound design, and especially the little blurbs about each creature. I love all the little guys so much! I've played for about five hours now, and I'm like 80% done. _childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only other game that scratches the itch that Pokemon Snap does, it is a criminally underused genre and I wish more games were like it. _childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for more of the Pokemon Snap gameplay loop, this is your game. Ride a cart through the different areas of the park and take pictures of the various creatures to put into your album. New creatures and better photos give you points to unlock new areas and new abilities. You have a sticky hand for picking things up and pressing levers, a ball you can throw at things and a flute that plays 5 different songs that you have to manually input every single time. For whatever reason, the game didn't quite click with me. All of the creatures are rather forgettable and have names that all sound alike and it gets a bit tedious going through the same level a dozen times hunting down the last few alternate photo poses and I gave up on 100%. It's not a bad game, but I'd wait for a sale if it's something that interests you. 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is lovely. The descriptions of the creatures and such are often very funny. The animations and interactions with the creatures is often very entertaining, such as when they get angry at you or start singing (some real bops, there!). Overall it was a very cute and pleasant game to play. I got about 90-95% done before I decided I needed a guide to find the rest of the photos/artifacts, though half way through getting the rest I gave up because I realised I wasn't really having fun any more. I still did enjoy the first 5 hours or so, and would say the game is worth it.I think it would have been cool to have a "backwards/rewind" stamp unlock at the end of the game, to make 100%'ing the game a bit faster/easier. I feel that the link between the required actions from the player and the symbol/emoji next to the creature's missing photo could be a bit clearer, for example sometimes they had sparkle/diamond symbols but required certain music to be played, and other times you'd play music but you'd get something else when taking the photo. Mainly it was the sparkle/music note symbols that didn't seem to line up every time. Sometimes you'd see a snowflake/teardrop etc. sign saying what song you needed to play, but then you'd need to be in a certain position or had to hit them with a penko ball first in order for it to do anything. Aside from that though the game was great.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing study in creature design and world building! Get lost in the world of the rundown park, take snapshots of some adorable, creepy and bizarre creatures, and see how the wildlife of this world have overtaken the ruins left by others. I felt like   an urban explorer in the best way! It also really rewards replaying each level so you can uncover even more to see! I entirely recommend you go explore for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game with some decent complexity for those final snaps. Pretty low stakes but that just makes it feel like very high stakes! Extra points for an excellent range of hats for the lil Penki tour guide. Remember - scan every blade of grass - it might be a Turfo. And ABC - Always Be Checking behind you
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Cursed Pokémon Snap with a few improvements for a much cheaper alternative. Art style allows for creatures to be more expressive and because everything is unfamiliar you’ll be frequently surprised. The cart has a much faster boost, a stopping option and clearer turning points. Abilities and scoring are streamlined for the better. Only a two hours base game but a very enticing 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: A nice lil picture-taker : ) It should keep you decently entertained for at least 3 hours or so! Some of these beasts are so, so good..... Clenches my fist. The game's entirely on rails, as you're in a sort of safari ride, but it works really well! I love the vibe. You'll be going back to areas repeatedly, but the game does a very nice job of keeping things interesting regardless
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing little photography game with some great mechanics including both interesting methods of interacting with the creatures in the game and great quality-of-life mechanics for when you're looking for just a handful of specific shots. Creatures and setting are unique - simultaneously a bit bizarre/unsettling and cute. Great bite-sized gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I always say that there really need to be more photography-based video games, so seeing this game recommended to me on Steam was super exciting. If you've played Pokemon Snap, then you already know the basic gist of the gameplay, but it also adds a lot. A Spooky Realm, a grabber tool to collect artifacts, a cute little tour guide you can gather hats for, and more branching paths. I also really appreciate the unique artstyle. I haven't even finished the game yet but I can already say I love it, even before starting I was just glad to find another photography game! And now that it's on Switch I can tell all my friends to get it >:)
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely adorable and the game pacing is just right - there's a lot of things to interact with to unlock new places and even while replaying a level you can always find something newif it was up to me there would be a lot more levels because i'm addicted to snapping pictures of silly little monsters now (/slightly spoiler but the guide commentaries makes me feel like the "are we the baddies" meme so much lol)
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: its a somewhat short game could probably finish it in one sitting if you get to go undisturbed but imo well worth it if you enjoyed the pkmn snap games or like the concept of taking photos of cute, weird and spooky lil creatures while on safari through a zoo that has seen better days. had a great time going on the rides taking photos of all the weird penkos, not a bad game to spend an afternoon or two with. grab some friends to watch with if you can for extra fun
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game quite yet but I love this game! I love the creatures and how they are creepy but cute! The game is amazing in many aspects such as the urge to finish the collectors guide and the different tools to make the penkos do different things. This game is amazing and I love it !Edit: I have now fully completed the game and my opinion is still the same! The game is some fun and cute. Completing the game was tons of fun and i hope to find more games like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Its a lovely game, I have never played the Pokemon snap game before so I have no nostalgic ties to the photo? game genre.The game has a lot of cute and creepy creatures to discover with fun little hidden details to help tell the story of the park. The game has a lot of replay value if you're into completing games. I was very pleasantly surprised and  found myself almost addicted at times to keep going and find all the hidden poses/creatures. I would highly recommend this people who have enjoyed similar games in the past, or individuals looking for a causal title that is visually interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable! You travel around the park on rails and take pictures of spooky ooky creatures. Taking quality photos unlocks items that let you interact further with the creatures, and functions like being able to stop or speed up your cart for example. This game is best played in short bursts imo, or it'll feel a tad repetitive. A very good 'palate cleanser' game if you've played something really intense and just need a brain break. The fact the devs included a whole expansion for free is a testament to how much care went into this game. Wish it was more popular because I'd love to see a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little game that is heavily inspired by Pokemon Snap, specifically the one for the Nintendo 64. The creatures you take pictures are adorable and creepy all at the same time. I was definitely able to pick my favorites out and it was so funny to watch them do silly dances or otherwise. I took my time to relax, enjoy the entire game in its full and 100% it. Delightful little experience that for any that enjoy casual and stylized games this is for you... 9 out of 10 Silly Dancing Monsters
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Penko Park's spooky-cute creatures make for a really fun photography game. Each critter has its own personality and actions, which are fun to discover and capture on film. Each individual ride (~level) is short enough for a 15min break, making it easy to fit into your day when you need a little boost. The game has a smooth progression and reaches a satisfying conclusion, but there's also a whole album to fill with photos of critters in funny situations, if you feel like coming back. So hop on and get cataloguing!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the Pokemon Snap.If you haven't played that - it's like a chill on-rails shooter where you take pictures instead of blast things to smithereens.It has a strong art style that gives the game a unique atmosphere, and it's fun to see all the "creepy-cute" monster-things sleeping, sitting, runnin' around, etc.Relaxing and fun to get 3 star photos.  Overall, I enjoyed it a lot. I wish there were more take-picture-on-rails-games. It's fairly short - so, you know, if you hate that, then keep that in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I love this game WAY too much. The art style is amazing and cute! The game play is nice and simple with being a snap-based game, but offers many fun varieties of tools and things to do. Plus with recent updates, I find myself always returning to play more and get everything offered. There is even an underlying story to this too! There is so much to do and look at that I find myself just playing more and more to pick up on details I haven't before. 10/10 would obviously play again!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: This hidden gem of a game combines a beautiful art style with a simple gameplay mechanics that makes for an addicting and entrancing experience. The highlight for me has to be the variety of creatures alongside with the character design, it truly is a treasure.  I really hope this game comes out with a sequel or has further updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: (EDIT:  This is just an additional note since I played the content update.  They added controller support, and it works.  The new island is just as great as the rest of it and I appreciate the free content.  Game still good.  Maybe a few of the requirements for 100% are a touch esoteric when there are multiple paths to consider, but that's a minor quibble.)The first of a wave of Pokemon Snap-likes that I've gotten to, I enjoyed this very much.  The basic upgrade system gives me exactly what I want in a photo safari game when I want it.  The creatures are cute and memorable and nothing overstays its welcome.Foolishly I assumed this had controller support, since the inspiration came from console, so I had to use a 3rd party program in order to play it the way I wanted.  Having that might be nice for anybody else who wants it to feel like Pokemon Snap.Overall excellent work.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful game for playing with the kids, they loved it and I loved it. It's a sort of play on the Pokemon Snap game style, being a non-violent rail shooter where the objective is to take good pictures of every animal in the park in each of their behaviors and collect related artifacts. There is plenty of replayability, given the different paths through each habitat, and the number of secrets to find.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Pokemon Snap for the PC, Penko Park is everything you could ask for in a safari game. Cute animals. Variety of locations. Different poses/actions. A casual playthru may be quick (not a bad thing), but there is *so much* to discover here. It's charming, yet with the right amount of dark. Can't recommend enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: this is a hidden gem! play this if you like slime rancher or katamari, with those cute but weird creatures,you have to take photos for them with different behaviors, and finding the artifact about themits casual but challenging at the same timeits very family friendly, while i take the picture and my daughter control the kart and stick the journal photo for meit worth every cent even with it full price. hoping for DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable, entrancing game that goes beyond its homage to Pokemon Snap to introduction of compelling and refined mechanics, fantastically designed and animated creatures, and a pleasing variety of goals and upgrades.  Even after 100%ing it, I noticed additional subtle touches in the levels while watching friends play through and I'm excited to get deeper into its speedrunning!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Penko Park is beautiful.Look. At. It. Look at Penki, wearing his little hat (that you can change!). This game just oozes charm out of every possible corner. There is so much to see an explore. The lore, the fantastical creatures, the environment, the puzzles and interactions, the features you unlock while progressing through the levels.It just brings so much fun in a unique chilled out way.I can wholeheartedly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly cute title. Very short, but effective. The definition of quality over quantity. It captures the charm of Pokemon Snap without relying on Pokemon to generate that charm. I'd really enjoy speedrunning this game, I feel like there are a lot of interesting categories that could be done.I keep editing this review. make more DLC >:)
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty short, but the "genre" of rail-shooter-but-actually-photography is extremely niche. The price tag is fair, and the game is extremely comfortable to play. You're never really pressured (unless you're trying to get the best picture you can get) and every map has multiple routes and secrets you can take. Simply put, it's a cute, humble game. If you can't deal with the short length (You can get all the achievements fairly quickly) it might not be for you. If that's not a big deal? I'd try it out. It's a fun little adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Penko Park is a short, cute/creepy, "Pokemon Snap." The game only takes a few hours to beat and a couple more to complete. The world is enjoyable and interesting. The world is unsettling with its lore but cute in design. My main issue is that there comes a point where there is nothing more to do. Unlike Pokemon Snap, where perfecting a photo was quite difficult and getting those few extra points for a slightly better picture was exciting. In Penko Park, it uses a star system. Once you get a Three-star on a pose, there is no reason to go for it again. It makes certain levels feel barren once you have three stars for most of the creatures. With that said, I would love DLC for this game. It was fun while it lasted and made me feel what I felt when I first picked up Pokemon Snap.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Penko Park is a photography-based adventure I had an amazing time with! I had fun exploring the different worlds and hunting out the cute and spoopy creatures contained within them.The progression system is really nicely done, as you level up with the more 3 stars photos you snap. The gameplay loop is nice and snappy and you feel like you're back in the action straight away.Penko Park controls beautifully and feels nice to play. I can definitely recommend it for anyone who wants a cute, relaxing time. I look forward to future updates from the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: What a charming experience this game is! Every mechanic is very well considered and integrated, and there's a lot more little secrets to find than I expected going in. All of the design work is clean, cohesive, and especially adorable (occasionally in a spooky way.) I've already played it twice, and I'm very much looking forward to 100%ing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Pokemon Snap who cannot wait for the new instalment that was announced earlier this year then Penko Park will definitely fill satisfy your craving for a photography adventure filled with weird and wonderful creatures! I've played the first two areas of the park so far & it's a nostalgic joy to unlock additional features & work out the right way to interact with the creatures to get the perfect picture. Great fun, very addicting & a genuinely wholesome game for all ages.An extended look at some gameplay -
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: The Ghostbutter team took the general mechanic of Pokemon Snap and improved in many ways such as a simplified rating system, adding collectible artifacts for many of the creatures and using the multiple expressions/poses of the creatures as a way to fully complete your album.Aside from that, Penko Park has so much charm and whimsy that every area and creature is such a delight to find and interact with.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is way way good! It's Pokemon Snap but with cryptids, and it's absolutely brimming with charm. It's not too hard or long to complete, but it's a joy all the way through (aside from one VERY TRICKY picture). I can't recommend this game enough if you just want to lose a few hours existing inside a colorful, vibrant world of weird monsters and adorable tour guides
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I came for the cute and stayed for the feels.The way the history of the park is told through descriptions is super well done, you can infer a lot of things as you have fun trying to get 3 star pictures of these adorable monsters. Plus, it feels like you see new things every time you go through a level!Also I would give my life for Penki in a heartbeat
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully cute, majestic and even sometimes a lil spoopy Pokemon snap style game! I thourougly enjoyed my play through of it, and even had a some feels towards the end. There are multiple areas to go through with multiple ways to go and lots of creatures to take photos of! I did the main "story" in about 2.5 hours but I have not 100% it yet, which requires multiple run throughs of each zone to get the perfect photoWorth every penny though <3
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: Nice adventure & exploration game with a unique art style and an enigmatic/mysterious feel. One travels through different parts of the park on a rail and tries to take pictures of small and big creatures along the way. During the game you can unlock more and more skills to e.g. access hidden routes in the levels or to interact with many creatures to take special pictures of them, so that each progressive run is different to the last, and much new is to be seen. Anyone who liked Pokemon Snap will love this!
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I had never been to Penko Park before and yet visiting it feels like coming home.Perhaps it's the art style, perfectly balanced between creepy and cute, just like the developer's previous game, Wunderdoktor, which I quite enjoyed (and played through at least four times). It marries itself perfectly with the poignant yet sweet setting of an abandoned wildlife park. Unlike Wunderdoktor, where the story is the main drive, here in Penko Park, the story takes a step back to allow the wildlife to take center stage (as it should).Wonder, more than anything else, is what drives Penko Park. And is what will have me returning to this game every once in a while. Just for another sample of that awe that comes with visiting a beautiful place such as this.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game for less than a full day and have already spent over 6 hours. This game feels very reminiscent of Pokemon Snap with artwork inspired by Where the Wild Things Are. I played it for about 3 hours on Twitch and the Dev team came in to chat and watch - it was SUCH an honor!! The game is well worth the money and has lots of hidden things that keep the game intriguing and interactive. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: I adored everything about this game. If you want Pokemon Snap but more polished with a slightly spooky aesthetic, this is perfect. Even if you've never played Pokemon Snap, give this a try! The Puzzles are challenging and can give you a run for your money, but the game does give you hints in the environment and your in-game album.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real gem. The gameplay is simple: Sit down, relax and take fotos of the creepy and cute wildlife.At first you only have a camera but the more you play the more skills you unlock. These skills allow you to unlockmore and more routes and secrets and make you want to revisit places you have already explored. The graphics are super unique and the quirky dialogues (lots of puns and fun references) make for a great time. Definitely enjoyedthe game so far and plan on finding out more about the intriguing history of penko park. Also what is up with this Penkiguy and his haircut? xD
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: You probably played Pokemon Snap, thought "dang, that game looks like Pokemon Snap, and I love Pokemon Snap", and are now looking at the reviews. Cool, because if you liked Pokemon Snap, then you will also love this game.For real, while this game shares the camera system, where it's most similar is the hardest part of making a "Pokemon Snap" like game— making evolving content that keeps each run fun and interesting, even after going through the same stage 3 or 4 times. There are multiple unlocks, stages, and various photo types to take of each resident.I dig it, and I think you will too.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: The game play is simple yet there's more to it than you might think. Snap photos of cute monsters in different poses and try to get quality (3 star) shots. Find hidden artifacts and open new pathways throughout the park. There are upgrades which you'll earn rather quickly but each one helps you to get a little further in the game and to take better pictures. You can rush to the "end" but the fun is in hunting down those perfect shots and hidden items.Wonderfully quirky art style and relaxed but engaging game play. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: A bit under two hours in and very happy with my purchase. I love chill exploration games and walking simulators, and this is much in that kind of vein, with added guiding goals and unlockable mechanics to pace your progress. Some of the mechanics could use a little more in-game explanation, but nothing's too obscure. Excellent art and animations; enjoyable cute and (very vaguely) sinister tone. Glad to get to explore this world.
_childDocuments_.name: Penko Park

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Bought today and beat it (100% completion) same day because I couldn't step away from it. I've always wanted to play Pokemon Snap and never got to, and this absolutely scratched that itch. It's a wholesome game with some mildly darker components to it. Excellent for people who want no combat and enjoy exploration. Despite the fact that the game moves on a linear track, there are multiple paths that can be unlocked, each with different animals, items, and poses to uncover. A few stumped me so much that I decided to search up how to get them. Then I realized that the game only came out yesterday! So I went back and tried again, and with some creative thinking, figured it out. It was rewarding being able to figure it out on my own, and I suggest others do the same. I wouldn't have the same sense of satisfaction if I had been able to look up the answers.I hope the developer will create DLC or a sequel.
