name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale
detailed_description: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale is an exciting spaghetti-western stealth game, in which you guide a 6-year-old boy on his quest to find his mother. As a six-year-old, 'El Hijo' must always sneak past the dangers of his world. As he overcomes his challenges, he gains self-confidence and cunning and with it more schemes to get past his foes. On his journey, he will find himself in a remote monastery, a harsh and unforgiving stretch of desert and a frontier town rife with crime and villainy. The journey begins when a farmer and her son El Hijo are attacked by bandits who raze their farm to the ground. The mother decides to leave 'El Hijo' at a secluded monastery in order to protect him. However, El Hijo decides that the monastic life is not for him and decides to escape. 'El Hijo - A Wild West Tale' is a non-violent stealth game. Violence is instead exchanged with the mischievous, playfulness of a young child. Shadowplay is in the core of the game and 'El Hijo' will often have to hide. Without needlessly adding new mechanics, the gameplay is extended naturally, as variations of existing mechanics are gradually introduced and then combined with each other to increase the challenge. These twists on familiar mechanics are often a product of the varied, increasingly dangerous environments that 'El Hijo' must traverse to reach his ultimate goal. Features: Survive the Wild West with the cleverness of a young hero Explore dark monasteries, deserts and boomtowns in a spaghetti-western world Merge with the shadows to hide from the lawless Solve playfully tricky environmental puzzles Use a playful arsenal of tactical toys to bypass and distract diverse desperadoes Inspire other children towards the path to freedom Enjoy the gripping storyline of a brave son searching for his mother

_childDocuments_.review: El Hijo is an interesting puzzle game about innocent mischief where you as a child have to get past supervisors and other adults unseen.A level has a certain pattern that you have to figure out and follow to complete the escape, some levels also have 2 or more patterns that you can follow to complete the level.When you are caught by the elderly you sometimes still have the chance to escape and hide, but this does not always work.Moving in the shade or hiding in cupboards or pitchers are very useful options to avoid being seen and often required.You will also be able to use certain items during the game to temporarily distract the adults so you can pass them when it doesn't seem possible otherwise.Also, you will have to look out for other kids in the levels, they will perform different domestic tasks or take lessons, if you find them you will have to find your way to them, while also remaining unseen, with the task of motivating them.Once you have motivated all the children in the level, the exit is open and you can escape.Levels 1 - 6:
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A very casual, charming, non-violent stealth game about a young boy, El Hijo, trying to find his mother after their farm gets torched by outlaws and she leaves him in the monastery. In a true mischevious spirit, and probably fed up with the monks, El Hijo decides to bust out and go look for her. But he seems to have bonked his head on a candelabra in the monastery and is a bit woozy for the rest of the game, with the controls aptly simulating that.It's an undoubtedly beautiful game. Honig Studios crafted a visually arresting Wild West, borrowing liberally from spaghetti westerns. From austere monastery walls to the drunken saloons, you'll feel the essence of the West. But, instead of guns and dollars, you get a fistful of rocks and fireworks. Lovely Morricone inspired soundtrack will follow your wanderings and chases through all the locations.The story is heartwarming, but very sparse, simple and not especially emotional. There are no high risks, hazards and gambles here. It's told through a few cutscenes where the terrific art style takes over in showing the relationship between mother and son.The main gameplay of El Hijo is stealth from a locked isometric perspective. And it's very easy going and forgiveable. As long as you're in shadows, you can stand inches from someone and he won't spot you. There are no direct combat options, you don't get to shoot or punch anybody. Your arsenal is a mixture of children's toys and nature's bounties in the form of pollen sacks. There are no shoot outs or teleportation powers if you mess up, you just get sent back to the last checkpoint. There is a cardboard box though, taking the form of a giant sombrero hat you can use to hide in plain sight.There are 29 levels of slinking and tiptoeing past monks, bandits, soldiers and coyotes by using shadows, hiding in pots, coffins and using all your distraction tools. The levels are puzzles more than free stealth environments, and there's usually only one "right" path. It's not that you can't take different paths, it's just that they're much harder and usually annoyingly so. And this game's grim collectibles, enslaved children that you can inspire and rouse from their fate in chains, are usually at the ends of those other paths. You can use a small bird to zoom out your vision and check your surroundings better, but it's not enough to form a clear path to the end of the level. Enemies can't be incapacitated, only distracted and temporarily stunned in later levels. You can also see the precise sightlines of the enemies, removing some of the guesswork. The levels are still a matter of trial and error. The enemy AI also seems slightly inconsistent, sometimes following you for a long time, sometimes forgetting about you the instant they spot you.Controls and the responsiveness are the biggest pitfalls here. They're very imprecise and occasionally just don't work. I've had El Hijo stuck on scenery numerous times, got him in a weird ladder loop animation, and managed to get out of bounds on one map and had to restart the entire level. Crouch controls are the worst. At best, they take a few seconds to register, at worst, they don't register at all, button prompts just not appearing. Aiming is also wide of the mark, at times taking a few seconds to trigger and having problems properly showing you where you're aiming. I've thrown pollen sacks and shot rocks at chandeliers and barrels, and yet, the game was telling me I was aiming where I wanted to.All those hiccups weaken the entire game since they're often the only reason you'll get caught. You could argue that the game compensates for that by being forgiving, but that does not in any way diminish the poor controls and the annoyance of having to restart a checkpoint for the umpteenth time because the button prompts failed to appear or register. All those issues can probably be patched, but for now they're a flaw.El Hijo has a lot of heart and warmth, there's no confusion there. Enslaved children seem like a miss, not because that shouldn't be shown, but because it comes off as tacky and a bit distasteful, passing them off as collectibles, in a mostly cheerful game. The poor controls and the 19,99€ price tag for a 6 hour game with no need for replayability don't help much in recommending it. Wait for a sale if you're interested in some non violent sneaking and don't mind the control issues.: Mostly easy achievements. You can select levels from the main menu when you finish them and the game keeps track of everything. One collectible, the grim enslaved children. And there's an achievement for finishing the entire game without getting caught. With the poor controls, that sounds rather tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: 🔸What comes to your mind when you hear Spaghetti Western? Saloons filled with cowboys breaking their necks while drinking? Dramatic horseback ridings? Tense shootouts between lawmen and bandits? Well,  is none of them. Instead, it tells the revenge tale of a six-year-old boy, mischievously and swiftly sneaking past monks, bandits, and lawmen. Separated from his mother, the unnamed son escapes the monastery he unwillingly lives in and set out on a pacific stealth journey across the wild west. consists of 29 levels that follow a quiet and wordless yet engaging narrative in a locked isometric perspective. The son starts his escape from the monastery and makes his way through many dangers of lawless locations. Levels are sprawling multi-layered maps that get progressively more difficult by introducing more guards and obstacles. They are often huge but there's only one optimal route through them and the game forces you to set foot in it. Being pushed down that route not only makes me reluctant to explore more but also cuts back on the challenges higher levels are offering.The game's brand of stealth is slightly fast and more trial-and-error based. Early on, the son must use shadows to sneak past the guards and throw stones to create distractions. A slingshot, wind-up toys, fume bombs, and fireworks are introduced later in the game to make a more diverse playstyle. He can also take advantage of numerous organic and ambient elements as noise-making hazards like shooing animals, breaking pots, or lanterns.I enjoyed figuring out the precise timing and combination of what items to interact with, albeit too linear, solving small puzzles and sneaking past guards is fun and a bit brain-tickling at times. However, I wished it felt more alive. My chief complaint here is how trivial the AI is. As long as the son is in the shadows, he can stand literally inches in front of guards without getting busted. For the most part, guards give up the chase rather easily, forgetting they were chasing someone moments ago. Their cones of visions also don't work quite well as the son might get past a chasing guard unnoticed if he's hugging an obstacle. makes up for some of those shortcomings by a simple yet top-notch presentation. The fantastic art does an excellent job of conveying the emotions between the mom and son. While most Locations and environments have a brownish tone to them, they are vivid and cheerful. The soundtrack also wonderfully backs the gameplay as the son navigates rugged cliffsides and goes through drunken saloons. It perfectly represents how he sees and hears the world around him.🔸🔸The game uses about 40% of VRAM at 1680x1050 60 FPS.🔸🔸🔸 is simple and gorgeous. However, it stumbles when it comes to the essence of the stealth core; The decisiveness of action that makes you feel as if you've outsmarted the AI. I don't expect in-depth mechanics from a cheerful non-violent stealth game, though, it's only fair to say the gameplay left important bits to be desired.🔸Each level can be replayed without being seen, granting you tokens to unlock the concept arts but that's as far the replayability goes. The other form of collectibles is inspiring enslaved children, albeit not pictured distastefully, it feels out of place given the colorful soul of the game. Short playtime, poor controls, and AI forces me to recommend it only at a discounted price.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: An innocent little stealth puzzler set in The Wild West (Mexico). You play a six year old boy who was brought to a monastery by his desperate mother. Your task is to escape the monastery and find your mother. To do so, you have to sneak past all adults and reach the level exit. On your way, you can find other kids and play with them. You can hide in many places (behind wall-curtains, inside vases, and especially in the shadows), climb ledders, push chests or ladders, and you can distract the adults in various ways. When you get caught, you just respawn at the last waypoint, and there are many in each level. The difficulty starts very low, but the levels grow larger later on, and there are around 70 levels. The game is playable in a screen resolution of 3440x1440@100Hz. My XBOX 360 and One controllers were recognized without any problems, cloud save works fine. Is it a masterpiece? No, while it is a polished game, it lacks a bit in diversification. Even when you obtain more items to distract the adults or reach new locations, the core gameplay stays the same.Cute, textless, nonviolent, stealth puzzler for people who love to play hide and seek.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: So I think this might be my first ever review:I'm moved to write it by the pleasure of playing this game for a couple of hours. The art, level design, art direction, and music are exceptional. There's a consistent visual and auditory aesthetic which really works to tell the story through the characters, and the game oozes atmosphere. It's gorgeous.Gameplay wise it's an excellent combination of simple and complex: the premise is fairly straightforward; sneak around obstacles (monks in the first few levels as you escape a monastery). The way it's executed is intuitive and gradually adds layers of complexity and interest: you sneak around monks reading, doing washing, cleaning, cooking, and learn more and more ways to interact with the environment as you go. I'm a couple hours in, and it gets more challenging without getting frustrating.I'd recommend it to anyone who feels like being transported to the Old West with tasteful art direction, music, engaging level design, and gameplay that is fun and challenging (and without having to murder everything you see; despite the clear inspiration from Jodorowsky's El Topo this is a refreshingly non-violent game).
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The seemingly simplistic nature of this game wears off quick, and this game ends up lasting far longer than it needs to  be.  It's okay for a short while, but gets boring quick and hardly attempts to stay exciting.  The worst part is how finicky the controls can be.  Lots of times you'll find yourself trying to duck down behind cover and your character simply won't respond to the control.  Also, aiming the slingshot can be very problematic at times, and the game fails to teach you that shooting your slingshot as a distraction only works when you're in the light.  The game started off great, but got boring quick and easily forgettable.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Really strong aesthetic, but the AI and "game feel" isn't there. 30 minutes in and the gameplay is already incredibly repetitive and mundane. Also, as the other reviews have mentioned there are bugs for sure even early on. I got softlocked twice in my short playtime. Once while opening a hatch on the first level, and then again after talking to the first child.For 20$ you could also get "Metal Gear Solid V - Phantom Pain" or "Ground Zero", as well as "Inside", And I would suggest you do that instead if you are looking for a great game with stealth elements.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This really is the type of game I love, but this is just so full of bugs, that it is unplayable. First bug I encountered was when I needed to crouch at the scare crows. It just did not want to crouch. Then, after a restart it worked. Second bug was when I needed to open the hatch to go to the second level. It opened, but the character did not go in. I was stuck there and pressing "E" just resulted in a sigh from the character. Another restart. The third bug, in level 2, was when I inspired the child. The game went in "movie" mode, but just did not come out of that anymore. That was when I decided to quit. It needs more bugfixing.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A nice attempt at a smaller scale stealth experience....marred by clunky controls and finicky precision issues.  The visuals are lovely and I enjoyed the wild west setting.  But, there were issues with unresponsive controls and with aiming the slingshot.  There is really only one path through each level, which makes it fruitless to try and use your limited weapons in creative ways.  Additionally, while I won't spoil the last level, the gameplay deviates tremendously from the preceding 28 levels and I found it to be obnoxious.Try Hitman Go, which is a far more polished (and far cheaper) experience in the same genre.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks completely fine at first glance - alright art and presentation, stealth elements look fine etc. But when you actually playing it - unresponsive controls ruining all the fun. In a stealth game where all decided by seconds when you move from cover to cover, your hero will likely stuck on a ladder a dozen of times or move in different direction that you intented. So you get caught and getting sent to checkpoint and you get caught again because controls are still terrible and again and again... In a current state this game is just annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: 15h 5/10 1, but I did replay all the levels for the achievement to not get caught. There is level selection in the main menu No You don't need a guide 2 on Astats No No No No No No No difficulty option NoIn this stealth adventure game you play as a young boy who is separated from his mom. During this journey you'll try to find her and be reunited with her, but along the way you'll see a lot of injustice while trying to inspire the children around you and not get caught by all the bad guys (and beasts).The game mechanics are simple. You can't be seen while in the shadows as long as you don't touch an enemy. In my mind, this felt sometimes weird because I was standing so close that I got the feeling they should almost be able to hear my character breathe. You will also be able to hide behind obstacles and sometimes even hide in or under them. The controls for hiding around objects felt a bit clunky, the animation starts a bit late which caused that I wasn't always sure if I would be in a hiding spot on time. In my experience, the game acts like you're already hidden while the animation is starting to show you going into that spot, but it just felt a bit clunky. Later in the game, you will get some tools to influence the bad guys in all different kinds of ways. I enjoyed the game a lot but was only able to play it in short bursts. I'm not sure why but the game felt like it was draining my focus. Luckily the levels aren't too big and you can easily stop playing after a few and come back later for more, so that's what I did. For the achievements, you have to beat every level while not being caught (or reset to an earlier point for any other reason in the few non-stealth levels) and inspire all the children. I played every level twice, the first time to inspire all the children and learn the layout of each level and directly after beating it I played them again without getting caught because at that moment I know the way how to beat that specific level. You can see in the main menu on which level you need to inspire children and on which you got caught, so you can go back later and replay those. For all the children to count you have to inspire them all at once, not a few in one playthrough of a level and another kid in another playthrough, you need them all at once. There are a few other achievements like shooting all lamps in a specific level or hide in a coffin for 3 minutes, but you can easily go back later and get those.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, I recommend this game, but with some caveats.I learned about this game in the desperados III discord, but gameplay-wise, those two don't have much in common. Somewhat easy stealth game (took me about 6 hours to clear it while inspiring all the children) with a handful more difficult spots. You'll rarely have to worry about finding a spot to hide or wondering how to get through a corridor that has 5 patrolling bandits with intersecting routes. All levels are about getting to the end of the level, and although you may sometimes wonder WHERE the end of the level it, you're usually steered in the correct direction, and there are usually multiple paths you can take to get there. The game's cute, the art style is agreeable, the music has a nice heavy Morricone vibe.Whatever gripes I have with the game can probably be patched out as most of them are about the controls; crouching is often a pain in the ass and is not as snappy as one would hope (there seems to be a delay of quite a few seconds after standing (after a crouch) before you can crouch again, how close you need to be in order to properly crouch seems to change all the time, sometimes you can't even tell if you're crouching and hit spacebar again only to stand up and get detected), the toggled aiming is really a preference thing, but I've always preferred "hold to aim" control schemes and having to learn how to deal with a different mode on the fly lead to some frustration (and ignore the in-game tips saying that you can hold Q to aim, it's really a "hold Q to toggle aim until you fire, but if you don't want to fire after all, you need to toggle out manually" kind of thing). On multiple occasions, I clicked out of the fullscreened game WHILE trying to aim and shoot. Outside of the controls, there are some things that have annoyed me that seem to be bugs more than anything else, such as enemies occasionally not going through their pathing/viewcone routine until I'd reloaded the game (via getting caught) a number of times, or when I noticed that I'd lost some ammunition for my rockets 'cause I hit the checkpoint spot, but the thing I'd destroyed with my last rocket didn't stay destroyed through a reload, so I had to come up with a new strat to get through a bandit.So like I said, I ultimately recommend this game, but maybe wait a bit for the first couple of patches to come out.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: El Hijo is a top-down stealth game that sees you playing as a young boy set upon reuniting with his mother. Taking place in the wild west, you must sneak your way past bandits and survive the harshness of your environment. That, and tackle with the game's many technical issues.The biggest problem with El Hijo is that it feels like a constant battle to play. Its controls are wonky and unresponsive, which is not exactly good when you need to react to situations quickly. Its stealth mechanics are poorly refined, coupled with AI that is just downright unfair. It gets to a point where playing it feels like a chore, and it doesn't take long for this to set in.The game does have merit, though. A good story married with stunning presentation and a charming visual style give it a definitive edge. The level design is expansive, with each one feeling alive. There's always lots of things going on, and some set pieces really do catch the eye.Unfortunately, I don't think all of that is enough for me to be able to recommend El Hijo, simply because it fails at what it sets out to be: a stealth game. If your a die hard fan of stealth games, or wild west settings, maybe get this on a heavy discount. Otherwise, I struggle to find reasons to purchase it.If you would like to see a slightly more detailed version of this review, as well as reviews for other free to play indie games, be sure to check out my video for them here:
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I bought El Hijo for the amazing art style and found the gameplay to be really enjoyable as well. It's rather on the easy side but you'll encounter new obstacles and gadgets quite regularly and getting to switch to another character every once in a while also helps keeping the gameplay fresh. Also loved the music, it really helps bringing the western setting to life. The non-violent gameplay approach was a nice touch and works well in the story.Only complaints I have are the controls which can be a bit unresponsive and I had two bugs where I had to restart the level due to the character being stuck. While it's not a big deal since the levels are quite short, it would have been nice to have the options to go back to the last save point instead.Nonetheless, I really enjoyed playing El Hijo and recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. It's pretty low-key and looks amazing. It's a great premise storywise, and the gameplay is right up my alley too. _childDocuments_.review: Yet another one of those games where I wish we had a neutral rating, or informational like curators have. The game idea and gameplay loop are awesome, the problem comes with technical stuff, it's unpolished, janky and straight up broken at times. My game broke on the very first level with enemies first time I played it, then it kept happening pretty frequently throughout with other levels as well. There's an issue when you complete a level, your character just stands at the exit and the prompt is gone, as you already pressed it to "complete" it. So you can now restart the whole level, enemies will also not see you in this state so you can't go back to a checkpoint either, as you have to "die" in order to do that. Enemies have preset routes they follow, or certain angles they turn, which will randomly change for whatever reason when you get caught and get sent back to a checkpoint, making some parts virtually impossible to do without again,  restarting the level. This soon becomes very tedious, especially as it wipes all of the level progress, even "collectibles". This also makes some of the achievements, like finish the whole game without being seen, way more difficult, because you cannot affect how enemy AI will react and if they will break or not at some point.The game usually follows the very reasonable learning curve where it gives you a new item or a tool and then teaches you how to use it on the most basic setups as it ramps up to more difficult ones. Problem is, sometimes a certain setup is encountered only once in the entire game, so you'll most likely not know what the game wants you to do, there are also enemies immune to getting stunned or moved by noise, so you'll have to learn a lot on your own without any hints or tips. Some personal things that bother me is not being able to use crouch anywhere, but only when against a wall or inside tall grass and with all the jank going on, you'll sometimes get spotted because character isn't pixel perfectly aligned to said wall so you can't engage "crouch".Final escape sequence was also very bad, you're supposed to ride a cart through swirly railway while being chased by enemies, so you can't slow down, but also having rocks drop on top of you, for which you sometimes have to slow down. This was never used in the game before, but now it does and it's absolutely horrible. You get sent back to a checkpoint in the beginning of all of this so you have to do it all over again even if you fail at the very end of the sequence.A cherry on top is achievements are not working as they should, either they pop in game and not on Steam, until you turn the game off, or they pop in game and never on Steam, even after turning the game off.For these reasons I'd rather give give it a neutral rating until and if they fix it, in the contrary I'd just not recommend it at all, but since that's not the case, I'll give it a positive rating with a warning that you should only buy it on steep discount and not expect much from it, unless they do intend to fix some of these fundamental issues.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend this game to anyone who just wants something to I guess relax in, this game was very much worth the purchase and it was really fun to complete :), I really enjoyed the puzzle solving and trying to figure out how to use the very few items they give you to avoid being seen, I really enjoyed the game :D
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game very much.It looked beautiful and had a simple and fun story. You are playing a little boy in the wild west who is trying to reach his mother who went to fight off bandits. The whole game is sneaking around with a different twist and a little bit of thinking.Like shooting a stone with your slingshot in one direction to make the guard look around in a different direction, blowing of the lamp lights to make it movable in the dark and unseen, hanging underneath a moving Bison's belly. Or moving behind a moving rail cart.As you move on in the game, the sneaking around will become a bit more complicated and you will need new tools to move from one direction to the other like a moving toy soldier to make the guards go check it out, or fireworks to stun them, or smoke bombs to hide from them.Throughout the game(with the exception of some creative special levels and 2 levels where you will play the boy's mother)  you will also have the option of trying to inspire imprisoned children to act in rebellion by reaching them in harder to sneak to areas and interacting with them. Sometimes they will even give you depletable items that you are low on or even help you out a bit. This is some kind of extra fun for those who want to get the most out of the game and you will even get to see something special at the end if you mange to inspire all the children in the game.I got to say, this was not a very hard game and besides some very small bugs that almost never happen it was overall very enjoyable. It felt like a breath of fresh air from the usual action filled violent games that I usually play all the time. Also, the price was very decent for the value I got from the game.I will defiantly recommend this to anyone that wants a fun little game that feels like you are watching a family friendly animated movie.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I played about an hour last night and had a lot of fun. The art style is really impressive and the stealth so far has been challenging while also remaining low stress (lots of places to hide and plan your next move, as opposed to the sort of stealth game where you're never "safe"). Looking forward to see how it develops as levels progress, but already enjoying my time enough to give it a solid recommendation!
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: El Hijo is a nice little stealth game. It falls into the same territory as Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3, though given a more charming facade and a more casual friendly difficulty.The game has 69 levels, starting out short and getting longer and more involved as you progress. Levels usually give you multiple options to progress through them, but were also space efficient and felt generally interesting to navigate.They also did a good job of making sure all of the tools are not only useful, but they also give you situations in which you even have to figure out effective combinations of items to bypass obstacles.The game has fairly few bugs, I only ran into one the entire time and it was of the more amusing variety. Controls can be a tad too sensitive in snapping you to things like ladders as you navigate around, and the slingshot can be a little unresponsive at times when using mouse and keyboard (most notable when trying to reduce shot distance from max.)The game uses a show-not-tell approach to the story, which has thus far worked out well and leads you to wonder more about the world you're in as mysteries slowly unravel through the levels. It rewards paying attention to environmental details, but might lead to a lack of interest for those who prefer dialogue and exposition based story telling.I don't really have an n/10 to give the game as I'm not a fan of that kind of rating system, but I have enjoyed the game thus far and think it's definitely worth a look for those who like stealth games and don't mind a somewhat less difficult experience.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: El Hijo is a beautiful, quirky, and immersive stealthy puzzle adventure game. The story was clever and engaging, with the puzzles ranging from simple to quite challenging. I got stuck in a few places, due to my own inability to solve the puzzles as opposed to being any issue with the game. The game was far larger than I expected, having come in to the game expecting a short story, I was pleasantly surprised to see just how many levels there were to be played through.

_childDocuments_.review: El Hijo is a breath of fresh air when it comes to wanting a puzzle stealth/escape chill adventure.  What caught my eye were the beautiful stylistic graphics.  I particularly love the way you can control your character in a detailed overtop terrain with a lot of detail and things to explore. _childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in 9 hours. Overall enjoyed this game and I think it totally worth the time I put in. It does a nice job of introducing new mechanics in a fair pace.The progression of difficulty is okay, could be improved as I think the later levels are too simple. The devs seem to increase the difficulties by putting the save points further apart, but I think the puzzles should designed to be harder instead.Regarding the negative reviews, I personally haven't encountered any game breaking bugs so I guess the devs must have fixed a lot of those since the game launched. I've only encountered 2 bugs that requires me to restart a level, both pretty minor as I wasn't that far into the level so I'm not loosing tons of progress.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I was worried that I would encounter bugs like others, but I was fortunate enough to be able to enjoy the game without it breaking.Overall, I enjoyed the game very much. Each level has its own little mechanics that you would need to learn with the overarching theme of stealth, and that made me wonder what's next at the start of each level with some excitement. Sometimes some of the puzzles can be solved in multiple ways, or be cheesed, which is pretty cool.The only con I saw in the game is how some mechanics were not explicitly explained, and that meant some minutes of staring at the screen and enemy movement in confusion and debating about whether it's time to look up a YouTube video. In exchange for the frustration, there is that "Aha!" moment I suppose.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A cute stealth puzzler with a well rendered theme, this is right up my alley.It's a competent enough one, with above average level design. The guard system is about as basic as can be, very predictable and without actual purpose, they're very much obstacles rather than NPCs. Still, there is something to be said for clear, predictable gameplay, especially on a puzzler that's a tad on the light side. You won't mistake this for any complex, top shelf stealth games (the most recent Hitman series this is certainly not), but it's quite endearing, and one I'd gladly recommend for an introduction to the genre.The game is a bit janky; the controls don't feel precise and predictable (trying to crouch next to a wall is very finicky, for example). There are also a few bugs, notably when inspiring children or getting captured, twice forcing me to restart a level entirely. Ideally these would be fixed, but a stopgap measure would be at least to allow the player to go back to the last checkpoint rather than the start of the level.Still, the good outweighs the bad, and if it seems like it's up your alley, give this a try. I played on a keyboard, but a controller would've done the trick just as well. I'm a PC guy through and through, but this seems tailor made for the Switch.
_childDocuments_.name: El Hijo - A Wild West Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not done yet, but this game is fantastic. The artstyle is beautiful and you don't even need any words to understand the story or what is going on.The puzzles are not too hard, but still challenging in some parts. I would definetly say it's more based for younger adults but not for kids, since they won't understand the puzzlemechanics most probably.What is really good, you don't need to solve the puzzles in a specific way. You can choose if you want to run, hide or distract enemies. You have a choice and this is really impressive and for me personally new in a stealth/puzzler like this.8/10. The only thing that could be a bit improved is the birds sight. Sometimes you run into an enemy because you are not careful enough, but the birds sight could cover a bit more of the map to make things a little easier. But other than that, a fantastic game, totally worth the price!

_childDocuments_.review: Good game.As it stands, it's a fun, kiddie Western game. Since I'd partial to the Wild West, having been born and raised in it, it reminds me of my own childhood as a Mexican anime child.The art style is great and there's a surprising amount of effort put in the animation quality, the environments and the setting. But therein lies the conundrum for buying this game right now.The price is simply too steep for something that you'd probably play once on a relaxing weekend. And it's painful to write this as I bet the studio hired a lot of expensive and great artists to make this and will have to make money off it, but considering the game only has about 30 reviews right now, it's fair to say the price hasn't attracted too many people.If the game was 5-6 euro, I'd say buy it on the spot.

I have only played 90 minutes in over a month and can't muster the will to try again until i get a controller. I will update as time goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: El Hijo is a well designed and adequately themed Indie stealth title that relies a lot on its lost longing and emotional story. Its core mechanics are driven by stealth and large maps that often seem like a maze but with a purpose and idea behind them. The entire game brings many positive vibes; that’s also because its story is quite purposeful, and there is no violence in the whole game. name: Ikenfell
detailed_description: A turn based-tactical RPG about a group of troublesome magic students. Use timing mechanics to power your spells and block attacks, explore the twisted halls of a vast magic school, fight challenging monsters and bosses, find tons of hidden treasure, and uncover dark secrets never meant to be found. A heartwarming and twist-filled story about friendship, trust, love and loss 3 students in battle, from a total of 6, each with unique powers and strengths 48 unique spells: blast your enemies, knock them back, poison them, or heal and buff your allies. There is no 'MP'... spells are about skill and strategy! Each with its own timing to master 100+ enemies to battle: spirits, myths, monsters... even students and teachers! Learn their tricks and traps, and master the timing of their attacks to overcome them 22 challenging bosses who will push your strategy and timing to the limit Hundreds of items to discover: wands, hats, cloaks, rings, and magical artifacts. Secret treasure is hidden everywhere, and every item you find helps you fight against the powers threatening you. Explore a vast school of magic: the dorms, alchemy labs, astronomy tower, twilight yard, and a dozen more mysterious and magical locations Beautiful soundtrack from the composers behind Steven Universe Cats. Everywhere.

_childDocuments_.review: By all accounts I should absolutely love this game. And I try really hard to. But I just... can't. I don't want to spend a lot of time tearing into this game, because a ton of heart was poured into it and I don't think it deserves nearly as much hate as it might seem I'm giving it. But the further I've gotten into it the less fun I find myself having and the more frustrated I've grown playing it.The game's story is charming on the surface, and the characters are fun, but it quickly devolves into a series of roadblocks where the party is constantly bouncing back and forth to track down the next work-around with very little payoff and no real sense of progression. Which kinda becomes a drag, but wouldn't be as big an issue if it wasn't for the battles.The marriage of a tactical battle system and timed hits seems like a good idea on paper, but the timed hits only serve to drag the battles on ever longer. And the hits themselves don't give great feedback on why you're missing them. There's not a visible "reaction" the characters take to avoid hits, so the timing is difficult to understand. You'll swear you've got it perfect but you'll get an "oops" instead of a "nice" or "great", even if it seems like your timing matched the way you did it just one turn before.And speaking of "oops", "nice", and "great", the further you get into the game the more important it is you get those "great" hits. You only output a pittance of damage at "oops", and an "oops" on the defense will likely get you killed, especially when you're swarmed by enemies. Even "nice" hardly gets the job done the closer you get to the game's end. It gets to the points where if you get "nice" instead of "great" you might as well exit out of the game and restart the battle instead of wasting your time trying to salvage what can't be saved.And the boss battles go on *forever*. Especially the late game bosses who spam minions and get multiple moves for each of their turns. There's nothing like playing through a boss fight where there are so many enemies whose speed outclasses your own to the point where there isn't a single one of your characters showing up in the turn order roster at the top of the screen.The game gets frustrating quickly, and that frustration just as quickly grows to monotony. I'm near the game's end and at this point I'm practically forcing myself to finish it. There is feature to disable "oops" misses so that you always at least get "nice", and another that makes all button events automatically complete as "great". It's a really cool addition but this switches the game from frustrating to outright dull. There's likewise an outright "auto-win" button you can enable in battles, which is a nice gesture and one that more RPGs really need to have, but it seems like such a needless band-aid for a game that I shouldn't want to skip through as much as I find myself wanting to.At this point I'm at what appears to be the final dungeon (I hope), and the only thing keeping me going is the music. Because goodness knows you can't say enough good about this game's soundtrack! Coming across it was what got me really interested in the game to begin with, and it's absolutely incredible. I just wish the game lived up to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is simply put, a masterpiece.  Easiest summary, a beautiful blend of Paper Mario, Steven Universe, and Carry On.  If you want a lovingly crafted turn-based game set in a magical school, Ikenfell is the game for you.The gameplay shows a mindfulness to design and attention to detail you rarely ever see in games.  Blending a simple systems like Paper Mario-esque timing with a simple grid system produces an RPG experience with incredible depth.  Enemy variety is astounding; playful and readable, a perfect blend of enemy design, encounter design, and a really strong AI.  The stat system and gear systems are incredibly simple, but pair in a fantastic way to actually give the player a lot of meaningful agency over your gear and out of combat decisions.  The difficulty feels spot-on, though it does slant towards being quite challenging -- with numerous options to make the game feel easier in the options, if you'd like!The characters and world are just DRIPPING with charm.  Everyone feels so deliberate, so delightful -- punchy, distinct, flawed and relatable.  There are tons of small details that really enhance the feel of the game, and breath life into the world.  Exploring feels incredibly rewarding, treasure chests feel varied and meaningful.  Environments are delightful and playful.I could ramble forever; I wanted to really hammer on how phenomenal the design is because that's what personally hooks me on a game.  But guess what?  This game is also absurdly cute, has a charming pixel art style with impressive animation, an unbelievable and robust sound track, exquisite SFX work, and a spectrum of beautiful representation that'll make you feel at home.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone that read Harry Potter as they were growing up, I won’t be surprised if you wished that you could go to a magical school and have the ability to wield magic or be proficient in something like potions. I know I sure did (and still do). Though, there is still a factor that you wouldn’t be capable of performing magic in the first place in this situation. And let’s be honest, us hopefuls will probably land in that category.Ikenfell has you play as a teenage girl named Maritte who lives in a world where magic is a real thing. In fact, she’s heading to a magic school just as we join her. However, she isn’t going there as a student at the start of a new school year. Maritte is an Ordinary, or someone that can’t perform magic, and she’s traveling to Ikenfell to find her sister Safina, who is a witch there. Safina didn’t return home when she normally did and she was worried that something happened. On her way there, she learns that Ikenfell is in lockdown for some mysterious reason and suddenly develops her own magic as a pyromancer. Once you get into Ikenfell, the majority of this game is exploring the different areas of the school, finding out what happened to Safina and where she is, and working with and getting to know Safina’s friends (or those that just know her).While you’re exploring Ikenfell, you’ll come across some puzzles that will block your progress until you solve them. Most of these are pretty basic and easy, even the ice sliding puzzle section. There was only one puzzle halfway-ish that was difficult to figure out, but once you realize the fireflies will point your way it’s smooth sailing from there. Enemies also roam the grounds and once they see you, they’ll try to engage in combat. You can try to dodge them, but sometimes you just can’t.It’s combat time! Combat happens in its own little area that acts like a 12x3 grid with your team starting on one side with your enemies starting on the other. From here, it acts like a tactical turn-based game. Everyone on the grid has a certain amount of steps they can take and attacks have a certain range. Some attacks/buffs will just target a couple grids in a row or a column or two in front of the caster, or even mix it to where it can hit in a plus. While you won’t know the range until you click it to see what squares it highlights, movement isn’t locked in. Though, your teammates and enemies will block your way if you don’t think ahead about your positioning. Once you choose what to do, they’ll do a special animation where you have to time a button press to just as the indicator reaches your target. Depending on your score (from a totally missed “Oops” to a perfect “Great”) it will determine how much damage was dealt and if the status effect the attack may have takes effect. It’s the same with enemy attacks, except this time you time your press to just when the enemy’s attack would hit you to minimize damage.I quite enjoyed battles. It was pretty fun and most of the attacks enemies will throw at you are easy to pick up on. Especially when enemies will roughly share the same animation if they share the same attack. It was also pretty weird not having MP or any weaknesses, but I don’t really mind at the end. After all, your teammates only have magic spells to attack with, there is a limitation put in place where some spells need a couple turns to recharge, and it allows you to have anyone you want on your team. No need to switch someone out or just struggle through if a current teammate is weak to the current enemies. You can choose your team based on their skills (and if you like their character in my case with Gilda) especially since unused teammates will still get EXP.Though this grid system does have a problem with big enemies blocking the grids behind them so it looks like an enemy isn’t there or it looks like the enemy is on the square you’re aiming for when they’re not. And towards the end of the game, the boss battles do become longer due to the difficulty being raised with the help of multiple phases and the ability to summon a couple minions.One question that I’m guessing some people are asking, and what I try to find out when browsing RPGs, is if Ikenfell requires you to do some grinding to continue. Well, as long as you are fighting enemies on the regular as you’re going through new areas, you don’t have to grind out levels. Unless, of course, you want to. You don’t even necessarily have to grind for money. Bosses, one of Rook’s abilities, and certain situations will give you a coin item that you can sell for a nice stack of coins so you can buy new equipment or healing/buffing items.There are accessibility options for those that have a hard time with timing or just don’t want it to be a factor during battles. While manual timing is the default, you can switch to have it semi-automated where the default rating is a “Nice” leaving only a “Great” as a manual attempt, or have it fully automated if you would rather just have standard RPG battles. In addition, you can activate an automatic victory option. If this is on, you’ll have an additional option during battles that, when chosen, will end the battle right there. Your team members won’t lose any health, you still get the experience points, and the achievements that are associated with bosses will still unlock. I can see an argument here that it makes the combat system pointless, but at the same time this is completely optional even when it’s on, you can quickly complete battles if you’re going back into previous areas, will let you continue with the story if you come across a hard battle, or let you skip boss phases so you don’t have to spend the time it took you again. Personally, I mainly used this option when I was going through previous areas to find secrets and it was very helpful in that regard.So does Ikenfell have extra content to do? Yep! While there are no side quests (or not what I’d call side quests), there are a decent amount of secret and optional stuff to do and find. There are chests that are hidden, sparkling spots indicating an item (which if you listen closely gives off a little twinkle sound), three kinds of gems to find that you can trade for special accessories, and five secret bosses. There isn’t a point of no return so you can go back and explore areas at any time.After 2 years of waiting and looking forward to Ikenfell, I have to admit I was a little scared that this would turn out to be a disappointment. Thankfully, my worries didn’t have any grounds and this turned out to be an amazing game. I’m a sucker for the writing style, I loved the characters and how they grew as you got to know more about them, the music definitely fits as it has a magical tone to it (which isn’t surprising since I learned the composers worked on Steven Universe), and it has a fun tactical timing combat system. If you don’t mind the pixel graphics, I recommend picking this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: 23.6h (100% achievement, finished the game) No. Yes (20 achievements). No. is a turn-based RPG game with tactic elements. Despite the grid-based combat, it heavily relies on QTE rather than strategy, which can be turned off anytime outside the battle.- A lot of accessibility options to tweak your gameplay- Optional boss fights to challenge yourself- Inactive party members got exp, making it easy to change your party- Unable to see enemies' stat and movement range in battle- No restart battle buttonIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650I liked how the game uses a different color palette for every area to make them distinguishable from each other. Characters' sprites are also varied; in addition to movement, it also has others to make them look more lively whenever they are doing something in the story. The only gripe that I had for the sprites is the nodding animation. It seems that the height of each pixel is slightly bigger than the width, giving a strange visual whenever a character nods.The game sets in a universe where LGBTQ+ is the common norm. There is a diverse cast of characters, with their gender and preferred pronouns - there is even someone with ze/zir pronouns, which took me some time to get used to since it's the first time I heard about it. Character pronouns' are also being written on the menu page to make it easier to refer to. However, their pronoun usually doesn't reflect their gender, although luckily, you won't need to know it to understand the story - only their pronoun and sex preferences matter. Speaking of preferences, there isn't any NSFW content in the game; the most that you'll get is a kiss from two pixelated characters that can be hard to see.The story is... alright. The dialogue feels bland, though. There is this conflict that is happening in the town, and you need to go back and forth between places to find more info that amounts to nothing - the lore that you get tends to be too little compared to what you are going through. Moreover, the "bad guy" that became the threat becomes too pathetic with all that happened. It seems that the game wants to give a reason for why they are doing the things that they did, but it makes the whole story feels pointless as a result.  Those words stuck in my mind when I was watching the finale. Well, at least the music is nice. I wonder why they didn't sell the soundtrack yet. The game is very straightforward: you'll explore dungeons upon dungeons, defeating bosses on your way. Despite the numerous dungeons, most of them are usually small-sized. It's also easy to figure out where you have to go next by just looking at the map. Some dungeons will also have puzzles in them, although they are usually easy to solve.Combat is touch-based. Enemies won't spawn until you exit the area (not the screen), making it easy to explore everything. It starts by placing your active party members on the right side of the screen and your enemies on the other side. The grid-based terrain makes movement similar to tactic games, although the mechanic is way simpler than that: there is no backstabbing, no height advantage, and no terrain - all you need to do is move your character to another spot and attack if you are able. Attacks have different ranges and effects depending on the character, and with 6 party members to choose from, you can change your party based on your playstyle.Despite having 3 active party members in a fight, your inactive party members will also receive some exp. Their exp gains might be slightly reduced compared to the active members, but they are small enough to notice - inactive party members will mostly be 1-2 levels lower than your active members, and leveling is easy to do. Combat heavily relies on QTE. You need to press the A button in your controller at the right time whenever you are attacking or attacked to either increase damage or reduce damage taken. Timing it correctly will net you a better effect, although failing it will result in a worse outcome. If you hate QTE, you can always turn it off or activate it partially through the options. There isn't a way to train your QTE timings except by trying it in the actual battle, though. Some skills might take several tries to figure out and it can ruin the battle because of it.Although it's fun to figure out the QTE timings at first, it can be exhausting in the long run. Sometimes, playing the game feels like a chore since it feels too redundant. Battles take a long time to finish, and dialogues only serve as a way to move to the next objectives. Sure, you can skip the dialogues and disable the QTEs, but I think I'm going to miss a lot of things if I did so - those are the main meat of the game, after all. I finished the game in 23.6h. The game wasn't hard, but some fights can be annoying or almost impossible to beat without items. It has a lot of accessibility options that you can take: there is an option to either disable or prevent the worst result of QTE, and an instant victory option in the battle to automatically kill all enemies on the screen. Battles can take a long time to finish so I was grateful for this option. It removes the grindy part of the game when you need to gather some gold for equipment. I usually use it for enemies that I have beaten before, although you can also use it on a boss to skip the fight.That being said, money is scarce. You won't be able to upgrade your gear every time it's available without grinding, even with an accessory that increases the gold gain. Luckily, the instant victory option can help to some extent if you need easy money. You still need to wait until your turn is up though, meaning that enemies can still hit you if they go first. tries to combine tactics and RPG in its combat, although the capability is too basic. Accessibility options are also available to make it easier for casual players, but there are no options to make it harder for veteran players. Despite the unique combat, the game doesn't feel that memorable to me, although I admit that I still had some fun from the battles. That being said, I feel that the game is best to be played for those who like RPG and QTE, especially since QTE plays a huge part in the game - you'll miss a lot if you hate it.

_childDocuments_.review: Witches. Magic. Ghosts. Queer af characters. And cats – lots of cats.The story starts out with the protagonist looking for her sister at the witchy school of Ikenfell. Her sister always comes home for summer break, so when she doesn’t, the protagonist feels something is very wrong. Upon her arrival, she discovers she has powers, even though it was believed she was an “ordinary”. While searching for her sister, she uncovers secrets about the school and befriends several people along the way. •	Turn-based battle system. On a grid, but isn’t actually strategy. •	Even though magic is used, there isn’t an MP measurement. However, some spells do have a cooldown period.•	Only 3 characters in active party. 6 party members to choose from all together.•	Each character has completely unique magic and abilities. •	No characters use weapons,  some characters can conjure a weapon for it to fly into enemies.•	For me, it took about 29 hours to finish this game, but I actually watched/read all the story parts. I also fought optional bosses. •	For those just wanting to enjoy the story and aren’t fans of fighting, there is a Victory Option, in which the battle menu has an option for an instant win. Also, as far as I can tell, the player can run from all non-story battles. •	Keyboard settings can’t be changed in options. As a left-handed player, that’s super annoying, so I definitely utilized the controller.•	The game crashed a few times, even though my computer has absolutely no issue running the game? Thankfully, auto-save kept me from having to redo much.•	Typos here and there.•	Some areas could’ve used more save points, or “save cats”, if you will.•	Just about everyone in the story is queer af. •	Several nonbinary characters. F*ck yeah!•	Excellent ethnic/racial diversity.•	There are lots of cats and they’re save points! You  the cat, their purring  you, then you get to !•	An optional boss is the Allcat, in which you get to engage in the most adorable battle, . The cats don’t get vanquished like regular enemies; instead, they just trot away once you’ve “defeated” them. There’s a move the Allcat does called “Stampede” in which a bunch of cats charge onto the battle grid and it is the  move in the game. :3•	The characters are really well-developed and written. Each have their own personal issues to work through, as well as the protagonist.•	Promotes self-care and acceptance. •	The Epilogue actually tells you what everyone does after the main story. I also feel like there’s an opening for a sequel, but perhaps I’m looking into it too much.•	Puzzles throughout the game are well-designed and not too difficult, and this is coming from someone who feels they’re not that great at puzzles, honestly.•	Photosensitive Mode, Content Warnings, & Timing Mode options available for ensuring more availability to players. Photosensitive Mode is for those who could possibly experience seizures from flashes of light or those who have sensory issues. Content Warnings can be enabled for those who want to be warned about disturbing content. Timing Mode is basically a way to enable “easy mode” for some of the battle mechanics, as regular gameplay involves timed key/button presses.In conclusion, this game is really for anyone who enjoys a good story and characters, as actual battling is optional. Be gay, do magic.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a must-play for any fan of quirky RPGs like Paper Mario. The characters are diverse and fun, the environments are full of secrets to find, and the battles are challenging without being unfair. Not to mention the soundtrack, which is phenomenal!I've seen criticism of how attack timing is handled in this game. At first, I agreed with it. I thought it was confusing how there was no clear visual indicator to tell you when to time your attacks correctly. However, after a while I realized that the game wants you to practice your spells as if you were a real student learning magic for the first time. The game gives you opportunities to practice your timing during random enemy fights, which will help you prepare for the more difficult boss fights. The game lets you suffer a bit so you can learn to grow and overcome challenges. I appreciate that detail, and I prefer it over the game holding your hand.Also, if you don't want to take the time to practice spells, there's an option that lets all your spells land with perfect timing automatically. It's good that the game devs considered an easier option for people who need it.The story is where most of my personal criticism comes from. It's not a bad story at all, but it is very slow in the beginning. It takes a while of playtime before the plot really kicks in.TL;DR : Please play Ikenfell! 8/10! Very worth your time and money!

_childDocuments_.review: A very charming, almost even relaxing game. The combat incorporates a lot of simple concepts in a way that makes it all come together into a fun system with a lot of options, with a cast of 6 unique characters who all bring a ton of different spells to the table. That being said, the timing based block and attack system, akin to Paper Mario or the Mario & Luigi series, can sometimes feel a bit too punishing (although the game has a handy option to prevent complete misses, or even circumvent the timing system entirely, if needed), while the position-dependent grid system, almost like a trpg, can sometimes feel a bit sluggish.The characters are diverse and interact in fun ways, while not lacking in depth, and the story is charming and interesting, although it doesn't do anything particularly special or unique.The soundtrack is fantastic, with track after track of beautiful atmospheric music, although I found the few songs with vocals to be bothersome to the point where I almost wanted to mute them entirely, despite the fantastic backing tracks. Luckily, there weren't too many of these all-in-all.The art is a bit weird - the expressions are very detailed and the overworld looks gorgeous, without sacrificing the ability to tell what is what, but the battle art and animations can looks a bit wonky and take some getting used to, and some character's faces are a bit off as well. Over-all, it's a very solid game and a definite recommendation if you want to play something not too active, but that wont bore you either.

_childDocuments_.review: This one was really disappointing for me. The graphics are charming. The game looks great. The music is excellent. I appreciate that it has diverse characters. But the combat gets tedious quickly, the story is boring, and the characters are incredibly shallow. It feels like each character is nothing but a sexuality and/or a gender identity and/or a personality quirk. I am on board for an RPG full of queer characters but it felt to me more like they just went down a checklist of queer identities and then called it a day. I certainly didn't hate this game, but I got bored with it. For me an RPG has to have more substance to its gameplay, more substance to its story/characters, or a shorter length.

*prrrrr*CONS:- Unable to see Enemies hp without selecting it.- No restart battle option.- Long boss battle fights.VERDICT:We've stumbled onto a hidden gem guys! It has everything an turn-based game should have, minus the cons I threw in, which can easily be overlooked from how in-depth the attack moves each character has, some battle scenes are pretty darn long, having a checkpoint helps but even with the help of that, can still feel long. With that said, if you're still struggling with these bosses and just want to be done with the battle, there is a choice to auto win, which is deemed as cheating but if you want to enjoy the story then I see no shame in using this option.The characters are all likeable and fit in so well with the plot, this can be a make or break moment but with the creative battle scenes to back up the characters, I can't find a single negative point with any of the main characters. If you've got the spare cash, I'd pick this game up without a second thought, it's the perfect turn-based game and very easy to pick up where you've left off. In the story, the player initially controls Maritte Hildegaard, a non-magical teenage girl who journeys to the titular magical school Ikenfell, in an attempt to investigate the disappearance of her witch sister Safina. _childDocuments_.review: The good:- A colorful cast of queer characters of all sorts!- An engaging, well-designed battle system!- A lovely soundtrack by aivi & surasshu, of Steven Universe fame.- Well-animated pixel art style visuals that fit into the overall feel of the game quite well.- Emotions! And singing!The not-so-good:- There are some issues with pacing. Parts of the story feel a bit taped together, as if they were ideas that were came up separately and then shoehorned together later. - The battles can drag on a little bit, making it feel repetitive at times, especially with some of the later boss battles, which can be quite long.- I'm on the fence about the high level of emotionality in the game. I'm a sucker for queer content, absolutely, and this game has a TON of it. But, the writing leaves a little bit to be desired - Some of the crises feel a bit phoned in. It's not bad, it's just a little hammy. If you're into that, then this game is absolutely for you. It's certainly a game that wears its heart on its sleeve!All in all, this was a worthwhile experience, and I definitely recommend this game, especially at its $20 price point. It made me feel warm and fuzzy inside.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;drPositives:Earlier spells are just as good as later spells.Game is ver tactical.The pixel art is great.The ui and controls are simple.Has full controller support (i used a ps3 controller and it worked fine).Puzzles are pretty fun.Negatives:Only the first 8 hours i was truly having fun.The setting was basically Harry Potter but not interesting.The characters an d writing are fanficy.Story isn't interesting enough to be in a game this long.Combat doesn't have enough depth to for the length of the game.Conclusion: This game is too long for its own good.I suggest playing until it's not fun anymore and then just quitting.Non tl;drThe Story:Story just spins it's wheels for the most part. The objective is to find the main characters siter and find out what happened to the schhol but it's very obvious that all will be explained in the ending so the whole game you are just waiting for the game to end. What makes it worse is that you can look at the map and count how many levels are left which makes it even more excruciating because every level is basically: go to building, fight your way through building doing okay puzzles until you reach a boss, beat boss, get told to go to a diffrent building. This becomes very repetitive very fast.Characters are very stock. There is a positive proactive character, there is a shy scared character, there is a bookworm character. there is an edgy character who is actually sensitive on the inside . there is a rival character who doesn't like the main characters sister but the main characters sister actually likes the rival when they are in disquise. Every character can either be linked to a harry potter character or to a fanfiction cliche.The combat:Initial reaction was postive. Combat is turn/grid based whith paper mario style timing minigames.In the beginning this was fun but as the game went on the cracks in the design became gaping holes.For staerters the RPG mechanics are way too simplistic to the point that if you are slightly underleveled your attacks start doing 1 damage no matter wether you got a oops or great timing. Damge calculation seems to be damage - defence and since a single levelup can add +3 to your attack means that wether you win or loose is based heavily on your level.At one point i got a new character on my team who was 2 levels higher and had a better weapon by default and was doing up to 18! damage per attck while the rest were doing 1 to 3 damage per attack.Secondly the grid just helps your enemies than it helps you. enemies especially bosses have better area of effect spells than you, they have better movement and even get multiple attcks per turn. Meanwhile your area of effect attacks can hit teammates, they are weak and have limited range, teammates often get in the way as you are trying to move into the perfect position to attack. Enemies are just better at exploiting the games mechanics.What really was the final straw for me was the boss in spooky forest.The boss starts out as three guys which aren't so hard but when you defeat them one of them turns into a big ghost that attacks and moves twice per turn and has area of effect spells that super hard in an area of 3X3 or a straight line across the entire field which means that you can't stay near or even in the same line as teammates without getting hit hard and of course in order for character to help each other they need tobe close together. A catch 22 basically.So after a very tough battle i defeat him only for him to split into 2 more big ghosts both of which still had a lot of health and could move twice per turn again. Which basiacally meant i was now in a 3 v 4 even though the last form was difficult enough.At that point i just selected the win instantly option because i just didn't have the power to win.Now maybe i could have gone back and grinded a bunch but at that point why even play if the only way to beat bosses like that is to just have higher numbers than them why even bother with an rpg system at all.At that point i had already given up on the story and now that the combat had lost its luster i basically ragequit.Luckily i do think the cobat can be salvaged with only a few simple changes:1. Make traps and poison do percentage based damage. this way high health enemies can be dealth with even if you have low power.2. Add an extra accesory slot specifacilly for the pins you buy with gems as using these now prevent you from using the stat increase accesories that you need to keep your power up.3. Make it so getting a Great timing on a spell has it do at least 3 damage. Because who cares if i'm underleveled. If my timing is really good i should be rewarded for it.4. Consider just removing the stats from the game and just have each spell do a set amount of damage. Because right now you've got all the skinner box mechanics whitout the satisfaction of hitting an enemy and seeing a big number above their heads while they die.Even though ive been really negative on the game, i don't hate it. I just don't want to play it.I can forgive a meh story if the game is good and i might even forive a meh game if the story is good but neiher is really up to par even compared to other indie games. I do think that the game can be improved and i do think the beginning of the game is solid enough to be enjoyable.I'm really hoping the developers can get the chance to make a sequal would like to see more grid based rpgs.

_childDocuments_.review: I was REALLY looking forward to getting this game for a long while, but I ended up being *extremely* disappointed, to the point I’m actually bothering to write a review.The art direction is definitely one of this game’s strongest areas, along with the music; the animations in particular seriously impressed me. That’s already about where the good tapers off for me, though, because immediately after that is the gameplay, and I did NOT enjoy the battle gameplay as much as I was hoping to.The idea behind the combat was like half the reason I bought the game, but in practice…GOD, was everything slow.Having not been an issue at first, the length of battles VERY quickly began to spiral out of control. Almost every time I entered a new area, all of my attacks would be doing 1-3 damage to enemies with 20-30 health, and I’d be lucky to be doing more than 5 without constant buffs by each area’s end. Many battles have 3-4 enemies, which all take up a pretty decent chunk of time doing stuff, but when enemies start getting really fast, and when they get to set traps without wasting their turn, AND when some of them have really slow animations, you end up taking anywhere from 5 to TWENTY MINUTES on a single battle. And that’s just a *regular* battle; bosses are WAY worse in this regard, as multiple of them have multiple turns, set traps often, and summon MULTIPLE enemies with full health, repeatedly. Expect to spend up to 90 straight minutes on some of the worst cases.This doesn’t even take YOUR moves into account, which can ALSO be rather lengthy but feel extremely uncommon because everything in this game will outspeed you in spades; you spend more time blocking attacks with minimal feedback than actually attacking. That reminds me: for all the amazing animation this game had, I was surprised to not see ANY animations for characters REACTING to damage at all, whether you block or not. That, and some moves’ sound effects not feeling very punchy, noticeably detract from the experience for me.The battles are definitely my biggest complaint, but something I’m also not the biggest fan of is the amount of item clutter and how quickly new equipment becomes obsolete. I kept blowing a ton of cash on strong-looking equipment, only to get a LOT of new items within half an hour. Things ranged from being pretty decent items that I equipped right away, to having been obsolete before I could even get to them because of all the better stuff I had access to before then. Some of the item stats still really confuse me, but more than anything, it was annoying to have to keep opening the equipment menu every 5 minutes because “oh hey I found another yet hat.” The same goes to the standard consumable items, but MUCH less so, as stat scaling was small enough to let me make use of weaker items later on. Overall, battle-related content just felt like a massive chore, more than a fun time.Now, the characters are a weird one for me. I generally like the character designs, and I like what personality I can glean off of them, but they come off as pretty basic when it comes to writing. I feel like we don’t get to actually KNOW them all that much, besides being fed their personal issues and sexual orientations, and a few moments with them were jarring or just straight-up confusing. It feels like only the bare minimum was done to make these characters work.…Actually, this isn’t even just an issue with the characters: you don’t get to know much about ANYthing in the game’s world outside of the mystery you’re looking into, unless it’s directly plot-related. It just feels really shallow overall, which is a shame, because, again, I really like the character designs. ESPECIALLY (Spoiler)*.…It’s also a shame because this means I didn’t like anything outside of the art and music. And the sheer sluggishness of battles made me start to get sick of their music and spritework, so I actually have to say that I didn’t like this game that much as a whole.*Eoc; dude is my favorite character.
