_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, I loved the story and couldn't wait to see what was gonna happen next. Although I will say that this game bounces you around EVERYWHERE, you will explore the entirety of the campus, normally I would be happy but you don't go up and then gradually unlock everything going down or some variation, you go VERY far back, and then you go VERY far forward, repeat for majority of the game. Bosses are okay, most just do the same thing of "spawn minions wait for all of them to die then spawn more after 3 turns", my main issue with them is the multiple turns per turn, YOU JUST SPAWNED MINIONS WHY DO YOU ALSO GET TO ATTACK ME??? Lastly, I feel that your characters are too fast, making the enemy turns a huge drag, you have to wait for 6 different enemies to use there turn and attack you, all that so you can spend 20 seconds attacking the enemy and maybe kill 2 of them. As much as I don't enjoy the gameplay for long periods of time, this game's music and story make up for it in the entirety, and despite what I said, you should still buy the game, if you believe what I said here, and feel that the gameplay won't be fun, the game has an auto-win feature in the options, switch it on and enjoy the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a game with the music and energy of Undertale, the combat styling of the DS Paper Mario games, and everyone is is a gay wizard, or witch, or whatever floats their respective pyromancing boats. They also manage to do a not ♥♥♥♥ job of representing the LGBT community. In 2021. Crazy, I know.gameplay-wise, every character that you unlock, from the primary protagonist to the last character (no spoilers!) feels viable for combat. some are much better at certain jobs than others (for example, one or two characters have strong healing moves, while others have moves that trap spaces and do hefty damage if you or an enemy trods on one of those traps), but all of them have their niches and i thoroughly enjoyed building one character as a tank with another being a glass cannon, which I played through much of the game with. The story, for the most part, makes crystal-clear sense and is decently fun to follow, but if you are playing for the story primarily do NOT make the mistake of skipping a custscene. I did that once early on and lost quite a bit of context for one of the party member's actions (though this was later rectified). It also does a great job of conveying tension, especially for the style in which the game is in. There were a few moments that had me genuinely laughing or disturbed or even a bit freaked out, and sometimes all three at once. my only actual gripe with the game is that the final boss (or bosses, depending on what you consider a boss) took me FOREVER, not because I failed multiple times, but because the bosses had massive-ass health pools that took me ages to put a dent in, supplemented with dozens upon dozens of annoying little guys who were fully capable of ganging up on one of your party members and taking them from full to no health in a single turn, even if you perfect-blocked every attack. as a result, half of my turns were spent downing healing items and revives rather than actually attacking the boss (granted, I didn't bring a dedicated healer into the last fight, which may have contributed to this).Overall, do yourself a favor and play this game through. I was lucky to win it from a raffle on discord, since I don't think I'd have heard of it otherwise, but it was really a treat to play through, and I think I'll be going back to 100% it later on if I've the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I really liked the animations and general vibe, unfortunately the actual gameplay brings about the games eventual downfall in my opinion.While the timing mechanic starts out nice, it becomes sort of stale and more stamina based really after the first third. Especially the last few bosses, where I used one of the "cheats" to don't worry about inputs, it became absolutely horrendous. Once you figured out the best loop, it was just repetition until the next phase.  I shouldn't have to deal with a boss phase for 30 minutes. You can imagine how the last 1/2? bosses with 6 phases in total must feel, if you had to perfect probably hundreds of QT events.I really liked the first 3-4 chapters though, the story was low key mystery, the characters although predictable also cute.

_childDocuments_.review: Campaign and 100% completion can be done in about 18 hours. (Why i have 20 hours explained below)Its a Turn Based JRPG using Grid Battle System. Closest game i can recall is like Rhapsody PS1 version. It also has something like FF8 Squalls Gunblade or Legend of Dragoon type of timed attacks to deal critical damage or lesser damage per action.First and foremost majority of the complaints is its characters are mostly LGBT+, it was not forced but nearly every character seem to have lines specifically mentioning that they are(not forced but still unnecessary to always bring up). If you have problems with it then skip this aside from that the story\adventure though contained in plot, was engaging enough for me to want to know the ending.   Battle System as first mentioned is QTE in a way. Good thing though the game has built in cheats to remove it completely or even instant win. As much as you really don't need to use the Instant win, it was VERY USEFUL for me since i forgot to backup my save when i reformatted by SSD. The 2 hours of game I played was redone in about 20 minutes. Battle System it self though is sometimes difficult to time and thus increases its difficulty specially for new enemies that have different timings.Pros- Decent Adventure- Good soundtrack as Store Page has stated- Part of currentl Humble Choice- Useful cheats to modify your gameplay style- AND SAVE YOU FROM REPEATING but it shouldn't be a problem ifNeeds improvement- They enabled Steam Cloud saves- Maybe they timed this due to LGBT+ month and it does promote them but i felt that shoehorning nearly every person as one and repeating it for nearly each character is not a good story idea. The story already flows enough that you should understand some characters are LGBT

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplaywise, I'd sum this up as similar to Paper Mario or Megaman Battle Network; turn based grid combat with action commands (although these can be switched off in the accessibility options). It features an impressive array of accessibility options (including the ability to switch on content warnings, and skip irritating fights), but also combines this with smart design (bossfights have their own leitmotif just before save points, and you always get one before cutscenes for example). This makes for an experience very similar to early JRPGs without any of the frustrating parts.Storywise; All the best parts of a certain wizard franchised patched over with Steven Universe DNA (I wasn't surprised to learn that the music was done by some of the same people who worked on the latter!). Some top notch spritework and animation, catchy music, and just the right line between building on and deconstructing the genre without getting too cynical.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics and sound design are endearing, but I just don't enjoy the gameplay. Both the riff-raff and boss fights drag on for too long. I don't mind long fights if the strategy is interesting, but it's just standard fare here. I absolutely do not enjoy the implementation of the timing system. Rather than a smallish bonus for getting timing right, the difference is frequently 1x/2x/3x, which makes getting the timing correct crucial. However, the cues for many attacks are not obvious, and the timing is frequently a narrow window before or after you'd normally expect from other games with similar mechanics. There are options to turn the system off, but the slow and awkward animations are just that much more grating when you aren't engaged in trying to press the button.The storyline and charm of the game just isn't enough to justify continuing when I'm not having fun from moment to moment and I've got so many other games to play/books to read. That said, if you're not opposed to a slower pace in battles and aren't prone to getting annoyed by some weird/janky timings, and you think the game looks charming, I'd say it's still worth giving a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful gem of an RPG.  Artwork is simple but highly effective.  Characters display a lot of emotion and the writing is decent.  The game is extremely welcoming, with the ability to fine tune the challenge to just where you want it.  None of this "easy mode" just reducing hitpoints, you can reduce the difficulty of mechanics directly.Combat system has a timing component reminiscent of Mario RPG (or Paper Mario, etc.) which provides a little more spice to combo-ing powers.  Items are handed out with frequency and grinding is unnecessary but rewarding.  Several optional puzzles and search elements add some more to do.Bonus: save games are in plain text and easy to edit for those of us who enjoy that sort of thing!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: A monotonously unimaginative narrative, strung along by an upsettingly tedious and shallow combat system.The novelty of the colourful pixel world and tile-based combat system are fine at first, but only get worse as the game rolls out more content to reveal there's no more depth to the experience than that. The combat system is not very tactical at all. Every single combat encounter the map is the exact same three by twelve grid with no obstacles or hazards or anything. Every single map is just that. All the player does is move the characters in range of the enemies on this confined, barren grid and then chunk out the same damage skills over and over again. To artificially make the experience more engaging players need to perform a quick time event every single time they use an ability or are attacked. These quick time events drastically impact the outcome of each turn and encounter as a whole. Missing the quick time will generally result in an enemy attack dealing triple damage compared to pressing at the very last moment for the most reduction. Same goes for when the player controlled characters attack, it will be anything from a fraction to full damage based on the quick time event. Players have to do this quick time event for every single action in every single combat encounter throughout what is probably a fifteen or more hour campaign. And every single new enemy attack and new character ability has a completely different timing, sometimes it's about when the hit lands other times it's a fraction of a second after the hit lands other times it's not the hit at all it's based on some random other part of the animation.At first it's not so bad but after over ten hours of combat which is only engaging because quick time events force the player to pay attention, it's exhausting and unfun. The map layout is the same every fight, there's barely even any room to move around in, there's no dynamic strategies or synergies between items and abilities, players have minimal access to buffs or control affects that allow for actually strategy, there's little players can do to tactically respond or counter or account for enemy actions at all in any way, and players have to take up a whole turn if they want to use an item so items are a waste of time outside of higher difficulty fights. If players don't waste time fighting against anything other than the boss, then players end up being underpowered for the boss fight and have to waste ridiculous amounts of time chipping the boss down; which negates all the time the player saved from skipping the previous fights. There doesn't seem to be much variety in gearing for statistics either since players can't really focus anything enough to make a huge difference, although without speed enemies will start taking multiple turns before the player gets to. Admittedly the game does actually give players a toggle in the settings menu to allow for instantly winning combat and, I think, bypassing the quick time events as well. But if entire core mechanics of the game need to be removed just to make it less unfun then that's a problem.Similarly to the combat, at first the story is also decent if not especially exciting. But it doesn't get anymore exciting as it advances. The world is just a bunch of bland, unimaginative copy paste magic whatever. Nothing special, nothing unique or creative about any of it. The lore of how the world was created gets even worse. Arbitrarily large whale, mammoths and a raven who for some reason have the ability and desire to create things; created things. That's it that's the universe lore. Same with the plot, it does try to at least do something different yet it's still just a vague asinine problem that has a vague asinine solution and overtime it just becomes less vague. None of the twists the plot provides in twelve hours are actually exciting, especially because most of the specific details that the plot revolves around are arbitrarily thrown at the player out of nowhere; and the player just has to nod along.The characters are about the same. Not awful, but not unique or interesting either. Very copy paste predictable personality categories without much depth beyond that initial category. Half of the characters either don't have any major drama problems but also supply absolutely no reason for the player to be interested or intrigued by their existence at all; while the other characters do have drama problems but it's all petty obnoxious issues that make zero sense to be showing up in the middle of such a drastic world saving whatever plot.The most consistently fresh aspect of the game is simply just running around the world collecting items and advancing from room to room while solving mild puzzles. The game has decent pixel graphics and fairly diverse, if not still uninspired, environments along with a solid amount of nice music. The select few songs that actually have sung lyrics tend to be shallowly written and extremely out of place though. Ironically the least music variety appears to be in combat. Players get to listen to the same song for the fiftieth time while performing the same quick time event for the two hundredth time.As referenced I was genuinely fine with the game at first. But after twelve hours of the same quick time events, the same empty maps; the only reason combat even started becoming especially difficult was because the characters had become underpowered due to me desperately avoiding enemy encounters to save time, and I actually started missing quick time events more often because of how tired I got of doing them. Meanwhile the story just keeps going on with the same inane fantasy save the world discover the boring details of the predictable secrets and now one of the characters is having a tantrum again so time to stop everything for them before immediately resuming once the petty social crisis is over.There's just nothing new about this in terms of gameplay or story. Yet it's over twelve hours long and demands constant attention from the player the whole way despite not providing anything of genuine intrigue. This game actually would of benefited from being much, much shorter.If you're interested in finding some games that I do positively recommend they can be found on my curator page .
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I was referred to this game because it has witches and fire magic.  I bought this game because it promised music by the Steven Universe composers, and Cats Everywhere.I promise, there is no shortage of cats.  Cats everywhere, and I adore them.  Witches everywhere!  Awesome magic!  And this game is so LGBT+ positive it's incredible.  Everyone is a little queer, in some way, and I love them all.  And not in a "And that's the source of all their interpersonal drama," just in a casual way that reminds you that who you love and what gender you are doesn't define you.  I want all the characters in my party, all the time.  Having to pick 3 of them is the hardest part!I did find the timing part of combat a little annoying.  You can turn off the timing component easily enough, but it has the side effect of making combat feel trivialized, unfortunately.   Which is a alright if you just want a great little story and some casual gameplay, but I would have loved a couple more settings between "All greats" and "do this timing trick or you'll find combat extremely difficult."There's also no option to change the keybindings or use a mouse, which is unfortunate from an accessibility angle.  The controls are a little strange and atypical, which left me struggling just to open the menu in the early stages. (What sort of game doesn't open the menu/settings with esc?)  It would likely make more sense with a controller, but with a keyboard, I found myself very confused in the beginning, with no way to change how I played.Overall, a great game, but could probably use a couple more customization options.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate the games attempt at accessability, but unfortunately it doesn't fix the games awful pacing. The combat is incredibly slow. That, and compared to most RPG's, the character and story are extremely bland. A lot of the characters are one-tone personality traits with one defining characteristic that becomes their whole personality. There's never any cute quirks or remarks you get from the characters outside scripted cutscenes to help make the characters feel more dynamic and alive, no charming mid-gameplay conversations that add nuance and subtlty to the characters... The bosses are all very similar as well. While some may have more phases or different aesthetics rarely do they have you do anything other than just hit attack and time your attacks and defense well. There's puzzles in this game that range from infuriatingly difficult to brain dead easy with no progression. It's very easy for the player to assume one thing, with things like enemies being misinterprated as clues for a puzzle, and no puzzle solving in fights themselves. There's a *lot* of running back and forth for no reason. Even with the fast travel trees.Bosses have too much health and outstay their welcome even with the highest attack I could have at the time.There's... just so much about this game that's annoying. With more side content it might help with the pacing of the game but as it is now I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, except without all that TERF nonsense and weird incredibly racist implications. What's not to love?In more seriousness, my review can be summed up as follows. The Pros of this game:- Great combat system. Little tricky to get the hang of, but once you do you really feel your team's power. On top of that, while my team was night unstoppable, I got the feeling that everyone has their uses; there's no "this one squad is a million times better than any".- Good story line! The plot is great and funny when it needs to be, and sad and deep when it needs to be. It handles trauma very well, things like apologies and the feelings of characters are not brushed aside, and it even has content warnings for scenes if you wish!- Which brings me to the accessibility settings: they rule. Skip combat if you want, make combat easier, make  scenes skippable after warning you about the content warnings, reduce flashing lights... they thought of everything :). It's always very nice to see.- It's like, SUPER gay. Which frankly is a major plus in a game these days. Handles pronouns expertly too! There's a nonbinary he/him character, another who uses they/them, and one of the frankly best characters in the game uses ze/zir. It's INCREDIBLY refreshing.- The music. Especially the four that contain lyrics! Phenomenal stuff.The cons:- Its absolute obsession with the Oops/Nice/Great system. Basically you want to time your hits like paper mario jumps; time just before you land a blow and just before one hits you. But this is taken to the Nth degree. Every move requires this timing. Every heal requires this timing. Every defense? That timing. Giving a speed boost to teammates? You better believe you need a timing. You can set this to auto nice or auto great but good god, it's still way too much. I would definitely recommend reigning this in if they ever make a sequel or some other similar game.- It also suffers from what I refer to as "ending fatigue". This is that thing you see in games, ESPECIALLY RPGs, where the last like 6~ hours (maybe more) absolutely feels like it could've just been 2, maybe even 1. But I might just be being cynical! Your mileage absolutely may very in this situation.- Some characters felt a little shallow. The last character added to your team is one I had been waiting to get for so long, and was like "YES" when it happened....... and then her character just doesn't go anywhere. It's very disappointing in that sense. Also, Ima absolutely deserved more charactertization.Regardless: I highly recommend this game. If you like RPGs, if you like plots about love and about forgiveness, stories about pain and loss and overcoming these things, and of course stories that don't shy away from the fact gays exist? This is for you.Pick it up!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and cute rpg with a nice story, great LGBTQ representation, and colorful ideas and strategy mechanics. I enjoy the positional strategy and action-command style of combat, but once there are more than maybe two or three opponents battles becomes quite tedious and boring to engage with due to how slow it becomes. Worse, while battles can get pretty long, if you are underleveled (which *will* happen if you just follow the plot) you will start wanting to skip battles entirely. Thankfully, there's an auto-win button option so you can just... not deal with the grinding. That's really my main issue; it's just a bit too slow and leveling is too slow too. Almost feels like padding but this game is a decent enough length without it regardless so I'm not sure why it was designed this way. It's a 7/10 to me, but it's an enjoyable romp throughout even with the minor hiccups. Recommended on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The best word I can use to describe Ikenfell is delightful. A delightful game about delightful characters in a delightfully charming world.The visuals are understated, but clean and the animation is very impressive in battles. The soundtrack is wonderful with a predominately chiptune style with orchestral elements weaved. And when they bust out the vocal performances, it becomes incredibly catchy.The battle system is what truly sets Ikenfell apart, using the grid system movement and attack ranges of games like Fire Emblem pushes through the filter of a turn-based RPG. Lining up enemies perfectly and busting out a spell to wipe them all out in one attack is a beautiful feeling. The fact that the game foregoes MP was strange at first, but the different ranges and applications of spells as a counterbalance meant I wasn’t missing it.I can’t say I’ve finished the story yet (though I feel I am quite close), but the characters encountered thus far are great. Each one a flawed, but brave young person assisting each other to overcome their weaknesses. It’s a story of emotions and control that’s not afraid to lighten the mood either (usually whenever Gilda’s on screen who is a treasure).I wouldn’t say the game’s perfect. The formula of ‘go to place, solve puzzle, fight boss, repeat’ can be repetitive and gives little incentive to return to old areas. The game’s first half is also a little on the easy side. Not a complete pushover, but I didn’t suffer a single character KO until about 7 hours in.But does any of that ruin the game? Of course not. Ikenfell is still an excellent RPG with exceptional aesthetics and a charming cast that I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game !A 2D RPG,  : each character has his own set of magical skills. Combats are tactics, on a map like a long 3-cells wide hall. You start with the main character alone, and you'll get new recruits in the first chapters of your story (I have 6 now, but you have to chose 3 of them for combat).You need to be well synchronised with the animation of your skills in combat (like Mario RPG) to get the most of them, so it's like a turn-based/tactics with action game.The pixels graphics are very good, the story is well crafted, and the music is awesome for some special combats or cute scenes.The game became a little difficult for me at the end of chapter 4, so I had to grind a little to gain some XP and levels. You can only save by petting sleeping cats, but there are almost everywhere you need them, so it's just cute.It seems linear and probably has not much replayability as it is, but for this price, it's really something you need to add to your steam library for hours of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fine title if you're a really big fan of turn-based tactical combat, but the only 2 possible selling points - combat and story - leave some MAJOR holes.Combat-It's slow. Tedious and repetitive. Part of this is because of the "combat timing" interaction, where abilities have a slightly randomized pattern to make it harder to get perfect defense, but that really doesn't excuse it when increasing combat speed isn't an option. Some enemy attack animations (paper airplanes) can make a single instance of combat last for more than 15 seconds before you have the *option* to cheat for instant victory. Buffs and debuffs typically last 3 turns, and you're expected to use them a lot for any hard combat. Bosses almost always spawn adds to slow you down, have tons of health, and usually don't hurt. In some cases, they also have several dull phases. Further, characters can't aim sideways. There's no explanation given, but you're on a 3x12 or so board, and being next to a target is generally a problem. In the end, the combat isn't really difficult and doesn't require a lot of thinking. You keep up your buffs, debuffs, and wail on the enemy for as long as it takes to make combat end. Most items are prohibitively expensive to use outside of hard combat situations, and the only remedy for this status is copious amounts of stealing - which, again, extends each and every combat, and can only be done by 1 character.The story:Apart from major gaps in the story, minor characters steal the spotlight at the end for no apparent reason, few of the characters are actually likable, and there's a weird disconnect between how the avatars are presented in game and the apparent ages and actions of the characters themselves. The ending scenes don't even seem to relate to the events that occur during the game.The secrets in the game, after a ton of hunting, will lead you to secret bosses! These, like the others, generally aren't hard, but expect to take 20-45 minutes *each* to defeat. They will not offer additional story content or any fun lore/interactions.Negative ranting aside, the music in the game is genuinely incredible and worth listening to without playing the game itself. It might be the only reason I felt compelled to finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give a mixed review since this game has some decent features and actually made me sit through itself, but it has many flaws. In the end, I don't recommend  purchasing this game, but I would only really recommend it to die-hard classic 16-bit RPG fans who ran out of things to play (like me). It's a turn-based RPG where you need to use timing mechanics in order to make your attacks stronger or defend from enemy attacks, sort of like the Mario & Luigi series. Unlike Mario & Luigi it also has grid-based movement in battles, and positioning matters for landing your attacks. There are six characters you collect throughout the game, each with their own role and arsenal of unique spells. The spells don't become obsolete with unlocking new ones, almost every spell has its uses and that really makes you excited for level ups so you can play with new spells. So that's good. There is however a big flaw with the combat system. It's super slow. Between moving around, playing animations and waiting for your inputs, random battles can last over 5 minutes each. Boss battles with multiple phases can last half an hour. The less is said about the final boss, the better. It gets kind of annoying. So it's kind of fun for the first few hours but once you've collected most of the characters and the novelty wears off it doesn't really hold a candle to Mario & Luigi, Megaman Battle Network and other similar games. There's a lot of equipment to try on your characters, but most of it just increases stats with no interesting side effects. If you read the description and expected some kind of a magical school simulation... You'll be in for a disappointment. The game is conveniently set during the summer break, so the school is pretty much empty with about a dozen characters in the entire game, with nothing going on aside from your quest. No classes, no students aside from your party, nothing. It's not a magical school game, it's a standard RPG where you go from dungeon to dungeon, but set in an empty magical school. Games like Hourai High for the SNES, Magical Vacation for GBA and the Harry Potter hand held RPGs do a much better job in creating a magical school experience. If you don't care about that, it's just an OK dungeon diving JRPG, kind of linear. There isn't too much in the way of optional exploration except looking for currency that can be exchanged for special items (that become obsolete very quickly) and a pixel-hunting quest you get 3/4 of the way through the game. Everyone is gay. This isn't an exaggeration!  character in the game is some fashion of LGBT except maybe 1-2 characters who are too minor for us to know the details anyway. Now, I normally really don't mind stuff like this, but Ikenfell has the subtlety of a sledgehammer to the face in this regard. Early into the game you meet a duo of comic relief villains who are gay for each other. Alright, I thought that was kind of cute. Then your rival shows up, who is gay. (She literally says "I'M SO GAY!" How's THAT for subtle characterization?) Ok... Then it turns out that , literally everyone is either gay or at least has specified pronouns like "they" or "zir". Your sister is gay. You are gay, for a character who is also gay. The main antagonist is gay. There is one playable male character out of six and it eventually turns out they are actually nonbinary. So what gives? Is Ikenfell an LGBT-only school? That is never explained or explored. It honestly feels like a self-parody, "what if Tumblr wrote a game".I wouldn't have even minded that much if the writing itself was good, but it ranges from ok to pretty bad. The characters are pretty cute and endearing, but also kind of stereotypical and bland. I didn't really feel like I was rooting for anyone throughout the game. People compare this to Undertale, but in my opinion UT had much better characters. Story beats are predictable and bring nothing new to the table. There is some interesting worldbuilding like the creation myth, but it's entirely drowned out by characters talking about their feelings and relationships. The ending is pretty bad.  Basically, the story isn't anything new or special. Fine I guess? Average pixel graphics, nothing in particular to criticize or salivate over. The character art style is kind of cute. Enemy sprites are probably the best part of it, well-animated, juicy and characterful. It's alright, but it doesn't stand out. The only part where I have no complaints at all, the OST is pretty great and memorable. There are even a couple vocal pieces, which was surprising.  Easily the upside of the entire game. 5/10, an okay little game that can make you sit through it, but except for music it fails to live up to the games and cartoons it sets out to emulate, and refuses to play up to its strengths. The combat system comes with a downside of being sluggish, the school setting is underutilized, and the writing is overly focused on character relationships where the characters aren't super interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a good time with this one! The combat system shines to me, it felt refreshing and more engaging than the usual turn-based battles.The game is filled to the brim with tiny details, many things are well planned like the characters, the atmosphere, the story, the gameplay. The music too was awesome, a song for any playable character is an original idea if you aim to give personality (Gilda's song is a banger, the other ones I'm unsure). Graphically is very appealing. Now, to the complaint. I've read the game's tags before beginning it, I felt slightly dubious if I would have liked it or not. If there's something characteristic of the LGBT[...]+ community, is their obsession about representation, inclusion and the emphasis they put on accepting any person under the many umbrellas people can have. It's actually a nice thought if you put it like that, but as I feared they overdone it. Nothing wrong with adding groups of people with different gender identities and sexualities, just it has to fit well. Personally I found it weird, every character we got had to specify how they were part the LGBT community and with that some dialogues were forced to show it off.What it really put me off for a while was when  It kinda ruined the mood.Aside from that, I'm still suggesting Ikenfell as it's very polished and an interesting take of an overused genre.

_childDocuments_.review: A masterclass of game design.It may take a few levels to really get into the battle system, but this is game of the year material.The pixel art is lovely, the characters are all dorky and lovable, and the story has a great momentum to it.If you are a fan of RPGS like "Mario & Luigi Superstar Saga" or "Paper Mario" this is for you. It feels like all the best pieces of past RPGs all patched together into one big delicious video game stew. I cannot tell you how happy I was when I saw that all Companions get XP after a battle, not just the ones you use in combat. That alone probably cut down of 50% of the grinding i usually have to do, and it didn't make me feel guilty for not using specific companions. They level up with the main party and I felt super encouraged to use different combinations not because they had good stats, but because each character was fun to play as. I don't feel like I am being hyperbolic when I say this game earns a 10/10 for me. It has the craft and care put into it that the high score feels more than earned.Also there are basically no walkthroughs, reviews or even discussions of this game as of right now. I feel like this needs to be on the level of popularity Celeste, Stardew Valley and Undertale got, it has that level of charm and it needs more attention.

_childDocuments_.review: TL; DR: Everything's great except the battling in mid-to-late-game, but the story and music easily make up for it.This game has some incredible music and some of the best writing I've seen in a game in a long while. A lot of the plot in the early game is character-driven, but it feels very natural and always works along with the main plot without feeling like filler or side-story. The initial plot point is a missing sister, and the search for her reveals plots and conflicts very smoothly. It's very text-heavy, but doesn't feel like a cutscene. The ending has a few plot-bumps, but the final boss is handled with such care and dignity that it's very satisfying.The music and art are both very well done. The art is, obviously, pixelated and so there isn't much to say if you have strong feelings about pixel art, but it's all technically competent. The characters are given both musical themes (several with great vocals) and unique designs and silhouettes, ensuring they always stand out. The music is catchy and the composer has done some incredible work matching the emotions of the locations and scenes. Dark places sound dark and unsettling. Sad moments are given the space they need to let the player feel it along with the characters. The world and level design are more average than outstanding, with a few interesting puzzles and plenty of rewards for exploration. The use of cats as save points is thematic, and is utilized very well at one point in the late game, but can make it a bit annoying to save-and-quit. Fortunately, the map contains an indicator of where to go and there is a fast-travel system to reduce running around (and dealing with low-level enemies). That brings us to the battles, which is my main annoyance. Before you start, look at the options window and note that there is a setting for "Manual, Semi-Auto, and Auto". The battle system here uses a timed-hit system, similar to the Mario RPG series, but with three levels of success/failure: Great, Nice, and Oops. It seems that, roughly, a success deals double (receives half) damage and a failure deals half (and receives double) damage. Attacks in battle have specific attack ranges and moving about and positioning your characters is very important. This is a great system, no notes except I wish I was better at using traps. The timed hits system, however, gave me a lot of frustration. In the early game, the timings all make sense (except Nel's). Around mid-game, however, a lot of your attacks and enemies use a timing that is a bit early compared with what you'd expect based on the animation. Ima's regen spell was vital for my play-through, but the timing took ages to get consistent. Nel should be a great healer, but they lack damage and their timing doesn't make sense for me. I didn't use most of the late-game spells because I didn't have the patience to figure out their timings. This is where I suggest you go back and look at the options menu. I was trying to tough it out on Manual (gotta Get Gud) and I should have switched to Semi-Auto ages ago. That removes the failure penalties (which get very steep late-game) while still letting you try for successes. Which brings me to the other issue with the battles.Battle difficulties scale with area but do not scale with your power level. It's an RPG, so of course your stats go up and you can buy better equipment with time, but this ends up being required to survive late-game. Fights can quickly overwhelm you if there are more than three enemies. One mistake on timing and you're in trouble. Initially I tried to specialize characters to stats, but that doesn't work. Having a high speed didn't give my characters more turns, but a low speed makes them act much less often (and a lot of enemies get bonus actions). Your main defenses are your defensive timings and HP, not your defense stat. Some battles would adjust their difficulty by spawning fewer enemies, but I'd much rather the difficulty either reduce enemy attack power, or be more generous in the defense timings. I can't do rhythm games precisely enough to be amazing at them, and I avoid souls-likes because the dodging systems are way too tight for me. It was really frustrating to feel like I was keeping up with enemies rather than surpassing them, and many of the late-game spells weren't strong enough to be worth learning the timings for. Oddly, I think one extra equipment slot might have helped with that as it would let you equip one accessory for stats and one for special effects instead of choosing between them. But for all my gripes there, I think there are solutions in the game, and the final boss was, again, handled so well. Great writing. But I'm not doing the optional boss. Nope.Overall, this is a great game and you can tell the creators put a lot of work into it. I definitely recommend it, with maybe suggesting you consider the battle style options if you're getting frustrated. But the story and music are really good and if those are things you look for in a game, then you'll love Ikenfell.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an interesting mashup of the tactical RPG with QTE elements interwoven in combat. On attack (and defense) you need to time button presses with the animation to maximize/mitigate damage dealt and received by your character. The story is really engaging and follows a non magical girl ("ordinary" in this universe) as she goes looking for her sister.Pros:- Engaging story with diverse cast of characters.- Characters have very distinct move sets which differentiate them in combat.- Varied accessibility options for combat.- Excellent music- No technical issues, and due to low performance bar it will run on a potato.Cons:- The QTE system in combat can get frustrating in later encounters.+/-:- Simple Pixel Art graphics, I enjoyed it but YMMV.All in all I enjoyed this game quite a bit and I'd recommend it if you're looking for a (relatively) short pixel art RPG with endearing characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game just now & wanted to put down a couple words about it. It seems this was made by a very small team, I feel they deserve a recommendation & some props.Overall, I think I would recommend this game, but not to everyone. I do have conflicting feelings about the game as a whole.- At first, I found a lot of enjoyment in the combat system. Learning attack timings, Paper Mario style, was enjoyable! The animations were for the most part well telegraphed.- I liked how stats were kept low throughout the game. Most often, JRPG stats become exaggerated as the game progresses, making it hard to estimate exactly how each minute change to your stats will impact your combat performance. In Ikenfell, I never felt like I lost the ability to estimate damage values - which made me actually use the stat-boosting consumables that I usually completely disregard in other games of this genre. - However, as the game went on, and on, and on - seriously, this game felt *tediously long* towards the end - the act of learning combat timings became a chore. The overabundance of bosses means that you have a lot of learning to do if you want to play the game as it was intended...   Thanks to the amazing accessibility settings, I was able to simply turn off attack timings. I was able to power through the last few bosses thanks to this option. If you find yourself frustrated, I definitely recommend doing the same.The art was stellar. I can't believe how many character portrait variations there are in this game, each and every one of them granted each character such personality! It allowed the emotion to really come across in some of those scenes. Seriously, the pixel art in this game was in a league of its own.I also loved most of the character designs, except maybe the main character who felt very basic, and the janitor guy who was an absolute mess (seriously my guy looks like a 2000s l'Oréal commercial).I'm a bit mixed on the story. The world of Ikenfell is super convincing and I could see it get expanded further. Its jabs at expanding its own deep lore were a welcome surprise. However, without spoiling, the story does feel a bit shallow and lacks subtlety in its approach to complicated human situations. In the end, it read like Tumblr fanfiction - a feeling that was reinforced by the very on-the-nose-at-times dialogues. But hey, teenager me would have probably adored this style of delivery; to each their own :)Spoilers below.The music was pretty stellar. From the moment I heard that very first battle theme, I knew I was in for a treat. The sound design was incredible too, especially on the monsters. THE CHICKENS ARE VOICE ACTED. Spotless work.All in all, you should play this game. But if you're a jaded, tired gamer like me, I strongly recommend giving in to the accessibility options at the slightest hint of fatigue.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just lovely. The plot can feel a little disjointed at times, but the characters keep things grounded. That and the story's heartfelt delivery make it hard not to love. I personally really enjoyed the turn-based combat with its timed button-press mechanics, though I could see some people finding it tedious. Luckily, you can make the timings easier, turn off the timing mechanics, or even skip the battles entirely if you want to. The options for this game are actually pretty comprehensive, more so than I've seen from many larger games. You can even ensure pixel-perfect scaling, which I love. And on top of all that, the pixel art and the soundtrack are both delightful. An all around amazing game.Also, you can pet the cats 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell has potential but squanders a lot of it through a lot of small issues that end up building into one massive frustration.The core gameplay of this game is similar to the Mario and Luigi RPG games from the Nintendo GBA and DS days. Its a turn based RPG that requires you to learn the impact point of moves so you can hit the action button at the right time to either muliply the damage you give or reduce damage taken. The system works competently enough in this game and isn't all that hard to get to grasp with. Even then there are accessibility options in the game that allow the player to automate these if they struggle with their reactions. In my opinion accessibility options are always worthy of praise.However battles feel like they take an age. Not that they are difficult or challenging but they all start to feel like they drag after a while. Maybe the designers were trying to go for the same sort of experience you get in the Persona games where even an encounter with even the simplest of enemies could expand into explosive clashes but it kind of just falls flat here. Unlike Persona this game lacks the masterful presentation those games have which make those long battles interesting to play and engaging to take part in.The snails pace of the battle also starts to bleed into other areas of the game after a while. The story is glacial at revealing further plot twists and developments. With no sub plots or side activities that support the main story I honestly started to physically feel the passing of time. Either the main plot needed more to happen, move at a much faster pace or be supplemented by other side stories to keep itself interesting.The final straw for myself came when I had to find several keys to enter a location. To do so you have to wander a small but very bland map in what I can only describe as a pixel hunt. Nothing is more infuriating than when I start to feel I am wasting time without fun in a video game.With that said I don't recommend Ikenfell but I do hope the developers do carry on with their work. I feel there is a good game almost ready to be made here and just falters in too many areas for it to be truly enjoyed. I'd like to imagine with some time they will be able to make more cohesive and engaging stories and gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to have a monster of a review for this game, but now all I have to say is that my top gaming experience of all time was when I played this game for 10 hours straight after getting to chapter 4 because I was so invested in the story and characters that I had to get to the end and see how it all turned out. Ikenfell is a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a huge fan of most encounter-based RPGs because I find them to be repetitive and not engaging. Pressing the A button until the enemy falls over and then doing the same thing over and over to be on par with a boss doesn't sound like fun to me. What Ikenfell does with its battles is both innovative and engaging. It takes the positioning and turn system of a TRPG and combines it with timing for attacks and defending a-la Paper Mario or Mario & Luigi. To win battles you need to learn the timing of enemies' attacks and your own. I didn't find myself bored during any of the fights, and many of them are very challenging.There are no random encounters in the game. All enemies in an area will stay defeated unless you leave and return to that area, so there is very much so an intended difficulty/level you are expected to be at. Each level you gain is very important, so not fighting a few enemies in each area might leave you underleveled later on. While I did have to go back to fight an extra enemy or two to level up my party, it's a very small gripe considering what other games might have you do. My advice for anyone playing the game is to just fight every enemy you come across. (There are only about 6-7 enemies in each area.)The story is probably the part I liked the least about the game, simply because it takes a bit to get going. Once it does, though, the story is very interesting, as it focuses on its characters, their interactions and their experiences. The story does get very cheesy at times, but the when it wasn't, it was very enjoyable. Unrelated to everything good or bad, but I'm pretty sure every character in the game is either gay or non-binary, if that interests you.The last thing I want to touch on is the visuals and music. There are many catchy songs that I've found myself humming to, especially the main theme and its variations. The pixel art style is fantastic and the colors used fit the themes perfectly. A specific scenario comes from one of the last areas of the game, where the music and visuals gave me a huge amount of tension leading up to, and surprisingly, during the boss fight.I was expecting an interesting game when I came into it, but what I got was much more. It isn't flawless, and falls behind mostly in the story department, but the entire experience was very enjoyable. I wouldn't replay the game but it's worth the price for the gameplay you get out of it. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: SUMMARY: A charming, fun JRPG-style adventure at a magical school in a state of crisis.   Characters have unique traits, there's plenty of skills and equipment to use, treasures to find, and you pet cats to save the game.  The centerpiece of the game is the combat, which mixes turn-based grid positioning and twitch reactions.  A well-designed game for someone craving that JRPG twitch-itch, combined with a fun plot that takes a standard story and takes it farther.(Note I did Kickstart this game).Ikenfell is a game that knows exactly what it wants to be: A JRPG-type game with a retro look, tactics-mixed-with-twitch combat, and a plot about various colorful personalities on an adventure.  Does it pull it off?  Well, yes, so let's look at the game!PLOT: The plot starts standard - your sister went to a magical school that then went into lockdown.  However you quickly find a school in chaos, and you don't have all the story.  It's done with broad strokes, but each character has a backstory, and there's some surprises and questions that are interesting.CHARACTERS: Each character is individual in their skills and abilities.  There's no complex skill trees - leveling brings new attributes and occasional new abilities.  The challenge to the game is figuring out the skills and using them.  Characters have their own character and backstory, and the game's cast is happily inclusive - there are gay characters, an intellectual who's a badass not a weakling, emotional vulnerability in supposed villains, and so on.COMBAT: Combat is a big part of the game, and it has strategy and real-time components.  Characters and enemies navigate a grid, and activate abilities - where timed button-pushes can increase attack or defense.  Character abilities are all different, have different "twitch" elements, and work in different positions.  Combat is thus always interesting as you have to interact.ENEMIES: There's all sorts of enemies to fight, with very different attacks and surprises.  Each combat requires you to know what they do and deal with it.  Boss fights often are multistage and require planning.EQUIPMENT: There's the usual festival of equipment to use, and choices do alter the game.  Speed?  Defense?  Special recovery?CHALLENGE: The game's not overly challenging at the start as long as you pay attention to the twitch elements and skills.  It does ramp up about 1/3 a way through, and you'll need to keep up with how character abilities, equipment, and position work.GRAPHICS AND MUSIC: The game has a great retro aesthetic and musical score, and some characters and bosses have their own tunes.Overall the game is a well-polished JRPG style game that knows exactly what it wants to deliver and does so.As a game, it's pitched at a specific audience that wants this kind of game - strategy-twitch, equipment-planning, some grinding, and exploring.  If this is your thing, then the game is your thing.Who is it for?* People that want a JRPG type game.  Period.* If you have some JRPG experience and want an RPG, it's mix of engaging tactics and straightforward play may be your thing.I kickstarted it, and enjoyed it.  If this is your thing, you will too.

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute, it's fun, it's well-written, but it has some curious pacing issues.Pros:- I was skeptical at first that the Paper Mario-style action commands *and* a grid-based system would be way too cumbersome, but Ikenfell manages throughout to make it click. It rewards planning and positioning without feeling unnatural.- Every character feels like they can both fill their niche and do good damage. Everyone has support moves alongside damage output, so you can reasonably use whichever party you want.- Great music, which should be a given with aivi & surasshu on it.- Relatively diverse characters, definitely in terms of gender & sexuality. There's clearly a lot of care taken to present the characters well.- A moderate set of accessibility options, including the ability to skip battles entirely.Cons:- A bit too long for my taste. It's comfortably 20ish hours with extra goodies if you want them, so compared to other RPGs it's short, but it drags a bit in a few spots.- The pacing is weird? I like to keep a bit under the level curve generally in RPGs, and Ikenfell is one where it's a real slog if you skip a few too many battles between bosses. For a good chunk of the midgame, half of my party did 1 damage with every attack. Some items and attacks scale linearly while others seem to scale logarithmically, etc.- Consequently, while the boss fights are largely excellent, some can take almost an hour if you aren't set up correctly.- The story's fairly middling, constructed to give the characters a reason to visit each location and not much else, with some lore thrown in for no particular gain.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most charming games I have played in years. The characters are wonderful and I love them all. There's some good character growth and twists a long the journey that were impactful and memorable.The combat is a joy to experience if you like tactical rpg gameplay! There's a lot of fun experimenting with the different characters and moves. Enemies and bosses mix things up and keep things fresh through out the whole game. There's some fun side / hidden bosses that can offer some nice challenge as well. If that's not enough to win you over, the soundtrack is an absolute gem. Go pick this game up!

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game. Reminds me of Super Mario RPG a lot with it’s timing battles, while the grid adds an extra layer of complexity. Not having mana or some kind of magic points means the spell you use depends entirely on the position of your team and the enemies. My only complaint is the music with lyrics for certain fights is extremely distracting and keeps repeating. Makes it hard to focus. For Ikenfell 2 (and I hope there will be one!) I’d suggest keeping lyrics songs to either an intro or credits scene.I’m over 15 hours in, will update when I finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I had a lot of fun with this game.  I love the modern-pixelated feel to it. However, there were still a few things still bothered me a little.PROS- Cute artstyle, modern-pixelated feel- No loading screen at all. Accessing to the menus, changing areas all loads instantly- Funny moments, some have some undertale tone to them- Interesting story and characters- Every character has their own battle skills and moves, it was fun to discover them all- The music is incredible!- Original battle style- Cool battle animations- Fun engame battles and secrets to discoverCONS- The game is extremely linear. By this I mean although you have access to a big map, you cannot explore anything that doesn't follow the story (everthing else is blocked off). - The battles can get repetitive. It was very fun to discover them, but eventually I felt I wanted to skip them. Luckily, the dev added an option to automatically win battles, so people that want to skip battles can do so.- Although there a plenty of places to visit, their structure are pretty much the same, which gives a repetitive feel to them. By this I mean the story brings you to a dungeon, you explore and beat the monsters in there, beat the boss, then on to the next dungeon. Repeat this around 10 times, that's pretty much the whole game.I finished it in roughly 25hrs. I'd say half way though I kept playing because I wanted to know how the story ended and because I wanted to find all the secrets. I'd still recommend it because it was a fun experience, but keep in mind this game isn't really replayable, you play mostly for discovering new places and for the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Majority of this game is good, and I would say the gameplay to gameplay moments are great. However I do have some general gripes with the game.Combat is similar to "South Park Fractured But Whole" as the closes comparison. Other example would be a mix of Megaman Battle network series + Timed hits from early Paper Mario. Missing these timed hits can be very punishing, but there is an accessibility function to make the combat easier for yourself if you're struggling.One of my general grips comes into character selection, it feels as though later characters are for more powerful/useful then the first half. I do think all character are usable, but the amount of options some characters have over others doesn't feel perfectly balanced. Another gripe is character stats and boosts, it's hard to tell how much advantage they are generally giving you, especially speed, when it comes to turn order.Story is quite interesting, and kept me hooked through most of the game. I would also mention that there quite a bit of LGBTQA+ characters, and certain story moments can feel contrived from their inclusion, but overall handled well.Only other gripe I had is with a gem collecting side quest, there isn't a in game hint system on where any of these 40 gems can be, so if you missed one and you're at the end of the game, it can be very tiresome to find which one you missed.I still think the game is worth playing despite all my minor gripes with, it's around 20-25 hours to 100% complete the game.. probably less with a walk through, and generally fun throughout
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I found Ikenfell to be well balanced gameplay-wise and charming in its writing. It uses a manaless ability-based combat system with attack/block timing as you'll see in some JRPGs. The combat feels good, and it's cool how many distinct abilities/attack patterns there are. The cast is diverse without using token characters or tediously acting woke about things, instead creating developed characters from diverse backgrounds that seem to fit naturally, which is great. Overall, I'd highly recommned Ikenfell for people who like turn-based RPGs with charming writing.

_childDocuments_.review: Handful of hours in.Art style is extremely pleasant; wonderful choice of color palettes and saturation.Soundtrack is very well produced, one of my favorites from recent times.Battles have a cool sense of depth.Options for an easier play experience are very considerate to more casual types.Only complaint is the "phone vibration" that plays at the end of the victory fanfare, as if I didn't unhealthily check my phone often enough, but that is more of a personal fault considering I've conditioned myself into the longing for and anticipation of phone notifications to make it feel like someone was just thinking me even though it ends up being an advertisement for the travis scott burger via mcdonalds app, but just like the travis scott burger this game is lit.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell started off strong with engaging combat and interesting story arch (at the beginning anyway). However, you experience pretty much all the game has to offer in the first hour. If you're looking for new mechanics beyond that, you won't find anything more.The main combat mechanic is actually really fun and engaging: You move freely from tile to tile and when you're in range of an enemy you select a spell and cast it, but you have to time your attack input well in order for the spell to really get any value. Each spell has a different animation and timing, but ultimately the combat comes down to timing alone.I'm a really big advocate for representation of all minorities/marginalized groups including LGBTQ+, however the representation in this game felt like an after thought and tacked on. There was a review that I read that expressed it perfectly by saying that it seemed like they went down a checklist of Sexual Orientations and Gender Identities and slapped them each on a character.The characters themselves are very two dimensional (no pun intended) and have little to no personality other than their assigned orientation or identity; This resulted in me losing interest in the story and ultimately the game itself.For the record I kickstarted this game and so I had a lot of hope invested in it, so I felt really let down when I eventually felt it necessary to uninstall.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely game that scratches an RPG itch without having to dive into a 100 hour JRPG, featuring a diverse and likeable cast adventuring through a pixelly not-Hogwarts finding magic powers and friends along the way, what's there not to like.As another review mentioned they "didn't shoehorn in any straight CIS relationships" (nb: I am CIS + straight) which makes an excellent change from the usual paint-by-numbers videogame character 'relationships' hurpy durp. Some effort has been made to give most characters a bit of depth, including flaws, not too bad an effort considering the linear game time is probably about 15 hours without mucking about. Hopefully you'll love some peeps, hate some, and maybe even change your mind about some. The characters are all fun and quirky, even when they stray into serious topics, with a fair amount of side characters and animals/creatures to uncover. At the end of the day you're in Ikenfell to pat cats, and find photos for a grumpy wall, and you're going to do both.It's all pulled off with cute simplistic art style that only adds to the experience, with well suited music. Though some of the characters get banging vocal tracks for specific bits (otherwise the game is unvoiced) which leave the other songs in the dust.The combat system kept me on edge for a lot of the fights, and the early game fights are varied enough, with a solid pace of tricky boss fights. There is a timing mechanic that some people may find frustrating, but this can be disabled in the menu. I found it rewarding to persevere with, it being very satisfying to start pulling off critical hits and saves consistently, and adjust for new enemies. The 'hit' box for some attacks wasn't worth the trouble of figuring out (or perhaps was too tight) to the point where I just ended up not using those characters at all, so it's not perfect by any means. Though I found the battles a solid challenge, as soon as I held back for even a bit to grab some extra XP I was quickly able to push my way through the bosses (or by using items), which seems like a great balance. Needless to say, if you are looking for a tough-as-nails hardcore experience you wont find it here, but those looking for a relaxing walk in the park should also visit the menu and play with some settings so they can enjoy the game.The late game can get a bit slow, and some of the puzzle sections are a bit of a drag, but nothing too dire, and if you've made it up to there I'm sure you'll be playing through for the ending anyway. Plus by then you'll be keeping an eye out for all the secrets which is the best part... all in all, an excellent package, good length, good balance, memorable cast, and a very enjoyable time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell took a little while to grow on me.  The combat timing is unforgiving and takes some experimentation to figure out, the battle difficulty is tuned hard enough that I felt like I had to run back to the free healing after almost every encounter for a while, and the first two people who join your party are fairly uninteresting.  But the game's good at drip feeding you a compelling mystery, combat gets better as your characters get more options, and the rest of your party is great. _childDocuments_.review: A very solid JRPG style game. I very much enjoyed the combat system, which reminded me a lot of Super Mario RPG in how good timing could increase the effect of you abilities. I did find it frustrating at times that all attacks and defense relied on pressing the button at the right time to be effective. In a game that focuses so much on diversity (delightfully so), it was a weird move to have a core mechanic that would make it almost impossible for players with hand slowing disabilities to play it. For me, though, it was an intensely enjoyable experience
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Rating : 6/ 10 (Good enough to play through)Decent enough game with a few annoyances that hold it back. Combat starts fresh but quickly becomes a chore.Characters are interesting and absolutely adorable but some lines about gender/sexual identity feel awkward and forced.I wanted to fall in love with Ikenfell. The art style, quirky characters, decent sound track and interesting story and setting seemed right up my alley. The first hour or so hit every box on my list even, and I had a blast. Somewhere around Chapter 2 I started feeling like the appeal was slowly waning. By Chapter 3 I was having an okay time and really just want to see where the story goes.The game play itself is solid enough, with an interesting mix of classic RPG, a bit of tactics, and a unique timing based combat mechanic. The first hour or two, I dove into each combat and boss battle excited to tackle the challenges thrown at me and come out with that sweet, sweet exp. After the fourth hour, I was almost dreading combat, wanting to just get the loot and hurry on with things. The mechanics I loved at first just served to slow the game down, with some of the boss fights and even normal foes dragging on for many turns. The mechanics are fun and new at first but quickly become a burden, to me at least.Exploration is relatively straight forward, with most puzzles and hidden loot fairly easy to find. I never found myself really wanting to check every nook and cranny of the maps though, mostly due to the fact that loot was fairly obviously marked and "hidden" passageways were easily spotted with even a brief glance. A lot of back tracking through the same areas for the story also took the magic out of this magical academy fairly quickly.Sound is hit or miss. The standard tunes are good enough and don't feel out of place. The sound effects for the attacks all make sense and sound good. My only real complain is with the special Boss Fight songs, where there is singing involved. The lyrics are... cringe worthy and really took me out of the game. I found myself straight up muting the game whenever the came on, which is a shame because the game overall sounds good. That's not to say they're *bad* really, just not my cup of tea I suppose. Your thoughts may differ.Graphically, the game is excellent. The character designs are adorable and the world looks great. The combat animations are well done and the character animations are a perfect fit for the style. Absolutely no complaints here.The story is decent and has a few twists that I've seen so far (haven't finished yet so this may change). Everything fits together well up to where I'm at and it's the story that's keeping me invested in the game, despite my growing dislike of the combat.The characters, on the other hand, are a mixed bag for me. I love the diverse cast and especially the gender and sexuality representation. This, unfortunately, is also a downside for the game. I believe in the show, don't tell, school of design. The two adorable coven mages making hearts at each other and blushing behind the other's back? Perfect. Loved it. The witch calling the MC cute and going beet red? Wonderful! The lines "I'm so gay" and "Excuses you I'm non-binary!", however... felt a bit forced and in your face. These kinds of in your face lines just broke it for me. Again, this is a personal pet peeve and one I'm sure some won't share, but it really just took me out of the story and into the identity of the characters. It really just felt clumsy and a bit awkward, sadly.Overall, I'm enjoying myself well enough and will definitely see the game through to the end. I'm excited to see where the story goes from here and how these adorable characters end up. Just a few things that are making it a bit more of a slog than I would have liked, sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: First off let me start by saying this. Ikenfell is to games what Oscar Schindler is to the Jews back in Nazi Germany. It is a beacon of hope, a revered masterpiece. With the production value I would have expected this to be a $99.95 game (and I would have gladly paid that price). My only regret in playing this game is that I know its story will one day end and I will lose the experience of experiencing this game again. The gameplay mechanics of this game are unparalleled, unprecedented and unrivalled. If you are on the fence about this game buy it and and DO NOT REFUND!!!!!! <3 XOXOXOP.S. I love this game

_childDocuments_.review: I’m actually kinda surprised that it had as much playtime in it as it did (20~ hours in my case) but honestly none of that time was ever wasted or spent on padding. _childDocuments_.review: This game is brimming with the love of its developers from every possible angle.- Nifty and quirky combat mechanics that are neatly scaled- Character arcs that pull at the heartstrings- Audio/Visual/World design working together beautifully- Accessibility options to ensure as many people as possible can experience the storyI'm tempted to say something like "Original Paper Mario, but with tactics based combat, and character interiority on the level of Night in the Woods." _childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Your beloved sister went missing in the famous Ikenfell school for witches. You, as any good magicless, defenceless and powerless sister, go in an adventure to figure out what happened to her. The game plays like an old-school pixelated JPRG. You form a team of 3 (out of 6) chars, each with 8 pretty unique skills in terms of area, damage and effects. Each skill can be "comboed" if you press a button at the right time, matching the animations - kinda like The Legend of the Dragoon, but way less cool. There are lots of equipment and usables, and the game reproduces an atmosphere pretty loyal to the classic pixel-RPGs.I liked the story, but not the characters. None of them are very likeable, and even the comic relief was not comic. The leveling system is super simple (disappooooointed!) and the battles do get repetitive. The combo-ing thing was pretty poorly developed and laggy, it was VERY hard to time it. There is an "auto-complete the combos" option and even an option to automatically win any fights though. No Linux port, but worked flawlessly via Steam Proton - thanks Valve, you guys are awesome! Achievements are quite well developed, but were kept kinda on the easy side.The richness of the skills of the characters almost makes up for the flaws, but since combat gets boring so quickly, it doesn't make up for the rest. Get only if there is a huge discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell, the conflict of the game is caused by poor communication, leading to people who should be on the same side working against each other and almost dooming the world. One character in particular, Safina, ends up alienating many of her friends because she keeps too many secrets from them, regardless of her intentions, and much of the character interaction in the game is about trying to heal from these wounds.Although the game is about going to a magic school, the school itself is in a state of emergencies and classes are suspended, so you the player aren't really introduced to magic concepts in a well-paced manner. Instead, the game is about exploring the mostly empty school as if it's a huge dungeon crawler with secrets and shortcuts to unlock.There are some interesting character interactions here and there, but the pacing of the game makes it so that actual dialogue and character development are very sparse in comparison to the task of dungeon-crawling through the school. The writing is at its peak during the final boss events and you feel good for the characters when they finally get their happy ending, but the ending and epilogue feel like they skip a lot of important character development, like how Maritte progressed her relationships with Gilda and Pertisia. It feels like there's a skeleton of a good script in the game that just never got fully completed.The game has a grid-based system where you have to position your characters and use AOEs efficiently, but the grid itself is a very narrow 3-tile tall corridor. Additionally, characters can only face left and right, which can affect how the AOE and range of your skills work. Additionally, player characters cannot move past each other, which means your own positioning can screw you over if you're not careful. While early enemies face this same restriction, later ones tend to fly and teleport, giving them an advanatage over player characters in terms of positioning.The game also has a timed hit system where you have to press the confirm key/button when an attack lands, allowing you to maximize your damage while reducing damage from the enemy. There are 3 levels of hits: oops, nice, and great, and you obviously don't want to see the former. Fortunately, the game's difficulty setting allows you to guarantee nice or great hits if timing is too difficult. I personally went with the middle difficulty because I wanted to be rewarded for good timing without being too punished for bad timing. The game's damage overall feels balanced with the expectation that you're getting mostly nice hits, so the middle difficulty will still require you to be decent at the grid/tile system.7/10The gameplay is creative and well-balanced, but I personally thought the pacing of the story was off and that the game was too minimalistic with dialogue. It's a shame, since the story has a lot of potential and teaches an important lesson.
