_childDocuments_.review: Aside from some cringe shoehorned pronoun stuff (and everyone's gay, WE GET IT, SHEESH), the game on it's own is very good. I don't remember how much I paid for it, but if you spend $20 you'll definitely feel like you got your money's worth. There's a good amount of optional things to do, and the game map is compact and has teleport spots so you'll never have to run for very long to get where you're going. The game also points to your next objective, which is a nice addition. Speaking of nice additions, there is quite a lot of polish in this game, there's all kinds of little touches that they could've just not done and no one would've cared, but the extra time and attention was spent. The pixel sprite animations are quite good, and there are very few palette swapped enemies.The story was also pretty good. I'm not usually a story guy but this game's story had you putting pieces together and figuring out what happened prior to your arrival in a way that kept me curious about what was gonna happen next. I also thought it was interesting how the characters don't always get along, despite cooperating, there's tension beneath the surface that they spend the game trying to work through.Most of the music is pretty good, with a few standout songs, but there's also one song that I heard a lot that sounds like the intro to a song but it doesn't go anywhere cos that's the actual song. I thought that the sound effects of some of Petronella's moves, the sound of the cap being taken off the bottle and the bubbly sounds, are very tasty.The items are impressive, there is a pretty large variety of items with a large variety of effects. Each item (and gear) has it's own sprite as well. Speaking of items, there is a steal ability that ALWAYS WORKS, A GODSEND. Many of the items you can steal are quite good and worth getting as many of as you can (you can even steal gear or two items at once sometimes), and even when an enemy has "nothing" you still get a consolation item to sell for extra gold.And finally on to gameplay. I thought it was very interesting. There's no straight-up attack button, so you always have to use one of your abilities. There's no MP to worry about, which I thought was good, and all of the abilities except for a few can be used every turn. Because of the grid-based battles, you always have to keep positioning in mind, and you won't always be able to use the attack or ability you want to so you'll often have to improvise and do the best you can each turn. The six playable characters each bring a unique skillset to the table, and the blending of different combinations gives a lot of options of flexibility for different playstyles. There are very few status ailments, but status ailments ALWAYS WORK, EVEN ON BOSSES, ANOTHER GODSEND (assuming you hit the timing correctly). Speaking of timed attacks, you definitely have to get most of the timed hits or else your party can go from full heath to completely dead real quick (no checking your phone during the enemy's turn!). There's two levels, nice - where you sorta got it, and great - where you did it correctly (and oops is a miss). The difference in damage between a great, a nice, and an oops is quite large, and a few oopses in a row can put you in a tough spot real quick. Same goes for your attacks, oopses will deal a pitiful amount of damage and even a nice will leaving you feeling like you left a lot of damage on the table (because you did). Btw, that one negative review where the guy was complaining about getting oopses all the time was just pressing the button too late and somehow never figured it out. Many of the timings are later than you might think, but if you press too late it's an automatic oops, too early is likely to get you a nice, so if your timing isn't super great you're better off erring on the early side so that you at least get a nice, but unfortunately he never realized it and it soured his entire experience with the game. Oh I almost forgot, there are two characters with a regen spell, one stronger than the other, and you can STACK THE TWO REGENS. Freaking awesome : D The boss fights were a bit on the longer side, but that just made it more satisfying when you finally beat it. They go to the well too many times with the "when hp reaches a certain point, summon minions, when hp reaches another point, summon more minions", but once you kill the minions they don't summon any more until their hp drops to the next threshold. The one boss I didn't really like was the final boss, it was too easy, I had a much easier time with that one that I had with some of the previous bosses, so I felt kinda let down since I was hoping for a more satisfying win, but ultimately relieved that it wasn't that hard, so I guess I'm okay with an easy final boss after all haha. There's also a lot of little secrets sprinkled throughout the game, there are lots that are obviously placed, but there's also several that you're likely to overlook altogether, and a good amount of the time you're rewarded with a new piece of gear for your trouble. Weapons are pretty basic, just buy the new one cos it's always better, but with the other armor slots you're constantly making trade-offs (is it worth losing 4 attack to gain 2 defense and 5 speed? ect.) You can go for a defense build or a speed build, if you go all defense, the enemies will get more turns since your speed is lower, so you're gonna need the extra defense (and good timing on the blocks) to withstand all the extra attacks that you wouldn't have to worry about if you went with the speed build.All in all I had a great time with this game. Recommended as long as you can withstand some occasional inserted pronoun stuff that doesn't contribute to the game at all, it's well worth putting up with cos the game is so enjoyable. Thanks for reading : D

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 8/10. Great story, visuals, and music let down by a truly frustrating combat system.I want to recommend this game. I really really do. The game is a masterwork of representation, and there's little bits of humor and quirkiness tucked away everywhere. 90% of this game I would recomend in a heartbeat.But that combat... oof. It's a paper mario TTYD style system, but the timing is either buggy or stupidly precise. "SCREW YOU GAME I HIT THAT." is in full effect here. _childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun and unique experience that has a few quirks that prevent it from being a masterpiece. Ikenfell was overall a very pleasant surprise. The only things I knew going into it was the game was some how described as both ridiculously hard by some, and shallow and boring by others. I thought that was quite the odd dynamic, and truthfully as responsible for making me check out the game as what little screenshot and video game play I decided to watch. Ikenfell plays a bit like a Harry Potter game meets Paper Mario, with a dash more tactical strategy than you'd typically find in either of those games. Overall? Not a bad combination. The game certainly is difficult at times, but I think it's more an issue with an inconsistent difficulty curve. The beginning of the game is rather unforgiving with your lack of personal experience, lack of levels and spells and characters. Then the good middle half of the game is considerably more manageable - bordering on easy - only for the last bits of the game to become challenging again- bordering on cheap. Suffice it to say, it's a roller coaster of difficulty. Never so steep as to become unmanageable, but it certainly could use some more fine tuning from the developers. The characters are over all pretty enjoyable too. They each have their own personalities and quirks that make them unique, and you can believe they would all work together towards a common goal without seeming like "generic band of adventurers" who would otherwise never be seen together in the real world. That said, I have to address the game's need to start pushing it's socio-political ideology and agenda, and that's a big no-no. It's not done as brashly and harshly as some other games, but I never appreciate it any video game. Video games are not an appropriate medium in which to push your views onto others and that includes transgender rights. You are certainly allowed to have opinions on the matter - and you have the right to feel strongly - but keep it out of the avenue in which many of us use as an escape from the rigors of reality. Overall, the game toes the line and is rarely in your face on it's stances, but it does get a bit too close to the line for comfort at times. All-in-all a very good game that is pockmarked by a view odd design choices that keep it from being elevated to super stardom.

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is one of literally thousands of 2D JRPG ripoffs infesting Steam, although at least this one was "genuinely" made instead of being asset flipped from the godawful RPG Maker construction kit.  That doesn't mean, by a long shot, that this lazy, badly done console port is the kind of game any self respecting PC gamer would touch with a 10' pole. From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.There's no options to change the resolution for the game or customise the graphics settings.  There's no way for gamers to ensure this is running at the native resolution of their displays... there's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.  There's no way for gamers to try improve the low quality graphics. PC gamers will be insulted by the presence of console peasant children's toy controller prompts, despite this being on PC.  Developers should try to be aware which platform they're developing for.  Because this is a console game, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Ikenfell has a truly insulting price of $20 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games (with 3D graphics instead of pixelcrap!), let alone the sheer number of free games available on Steam.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, and the questionable ethical nature of the developer and/or their associates (as outlined above), this is impossible to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't even finished this game and it's probably going to be one of my favorite games for a while.This game does extremely well at creating a story full of compelling and complex characters, I don't think there's any characters I don't like, even down to the random characters with 3-4 lines of dialogue. It has a refreshingly welcoming and colorful (literal and more figurative) world, too, especially for a video game. As for the gameplay, it succeeds in its strategy system (positioning plays a big role if you can figure out the placement of enemy attacks and the trap system is great because of that) and its timing system is weird. It isn't bad, per say, just different: you will probably not succeed the first time you use a spell, but I've heard someone compare that to learning to cast and perfect spells, and I like that. It also adds a bit more to the gameplay that might otherwise feel simple, and while it is annoying I kind of like the unique style of timing. Items also are around, which is good, plus extra equipment that grants passive benefits you'll be able to obtain if you look for secrets. Most of the out-of-combat time is spent running around grabbing things, but I have run into some good puzzles, too (not horribly hard, but not easy either). In terms of difficulty, the game lets you take your own route a bit. You aren't punished for saving between every single combat, and you can easily run around a lot of the enemies. If you do end up in a fight you don't want to be in, you can always flee. The combat, however, can be reasonably challenging but I doubt the average person will need to retry it too often.If you want an earnest RPG with good representation and a pretty fun combat system, this one's for you!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Great game, with lots of quirky character. Would recommend for sure.The good: Cool story, not breaking any new ground or anything but it was funny, cute, and intriguing. Cozy pixel graphics are always a nostalgic win. The music was very good throughout the game. There weren't any areas where the music didn't fit the mood or fell in quality.  It was fun to interact with the kooky NPC's. Nice side quests and side goals. Very creative and inventive gameplay. The timing system was both the best and worst thing about the game, but first let me talk about why it's cool: having to keep a close eye on the timing of my attacks (as well as the enemy's) kept me engaged throughout each battle and it was cool to learn each enemy's unique attacks. Each time I learned a new spell there was also a learning curve for the timing. Also, the boss fights were inventive and challenging. ALMOST no grinding required. I think most players hate grinding and this game has almost none required, until the endgame but we'll talk about that later.The Bad but not really all that bad, just kinda: These are things that don't really bother me too much, but I do feel the need to be nit-picky about them. The game dragged on for too long. The story isn't deep enough and the gameplay isn't diverse enough for how long this game is. I was ready for it to end halfway through the game. The soundtrack was great, but I think it would have been more impactful if there were themes for each character, and an overall game theme. You reach the end of the game and out of nowhere, every item costs thousands of dollars, and the money that enemies give you doesn't keep up with inflation. You would have to grind for a long time just to buy the last sets of armor and weapons for all six characters.The Actually Bad: As good as the battle system is, it's way too punishing. It wears me out fast. The margin of error is so small that you are forced to be frame perfect with your inputs. It feels like I'm trying to Perfect Parry in Street Fighter 6 or Dark Souls for every single thing that happens. Attacking an enemy? Gotta get it perfect or there is a huge damage nerf as punishment. Getting hit by a monster? Gotta time it perfect or there will be a huge damage multiplier applied to the attack on my character. Missing just one perfect timed move can ruin a battle. You won't notice it TOO much in the fist half of the game, but in the second half, it's brutal! You'll spend 30 minutes in a Boss fight only to miss ONE block or spell attack and it's over. Your character dies in one hit and it starts a downward spiral from there. I couldn't tell if the window of opportunity for the endgame enemies was getting shorter, or if my attention span was too fried from having to pay such close attention ALL. THE. DAMNED. TIME.All in all, I loved the game. If there a sequel I would definitely buy it, but I hope the battle system is a little more forgiving.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This game had been on my radar for a while after stumbling across it in store. I'm glad I kept tabs on it and ultimately made the purchase when it came up in a solid Humble Bundle deal late last year.I finally got around to playing it after chipping away at my personal queue, and I couldn't put it down! It had a nice blend of turn-based combat and side content (non-grindy collectibles) wrapped up perfectly into the story, all while running perfectly on my Deck.With getting 100% completion in 23.5 hours, it passed my $1/hr "value test", even at full price - would be a great deal on the current Steam Summer sale 2024 price and others that pop up with somewhat regularity from SteamDB's history.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is a game with a wonderful cast of characters.  I really love cozy character driven stories, and on that front, Ikenfell is one of the greats, alongside similar cozy stories like Celeste, Wandersong, Chicory, etc.  Mechanically, I love a lot of what the game does, but it definitely felt like a singular vision for what the designer loved in a game, and so whether it matches your taste is going to vary person to person.Overall a solid A-, extremely gay, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adored this game. My ADHD ass struggles to get through games that feel repetitive, but this game had a compelling storyline with lots of well-placed foreshadowing, lore that is delivered in small, plot-relevant chunks so I rarely felt like the game's worldbuilding turned into a lecture, and satisfying character arcs. I could not put it down until the end. The timing-based combat may not be for everyone, but I enjoyed it, it added enough action to the turn based elements that it felt far more interactive than "pick move, watch move, move on" like you get in turn based games like Pokemon or Fire Emblem. And if it isn't for you, you can turn the timing aspect off and still enjoy the story and characters with lower difficulty.The story is unapologetically queer, and delves into some pretty heavy feelings around grief and trauma in a way that's relatable and cathartic, and the game does a wonderful job of developing a pretty wide cast of characters to the point where I adored them all. And then of course the music was absolutely phenomenal, and the sound design was top-tier. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept with great characters and a fun (albeit tedious) combat system, held back by poor prioritisation.This game features little-to-no story and what story is does have is all written around the gameplay, not  the other way around. It's honestly disappointing how little time you spend in the school doing school things, I expected something like Persona but instead got the shell of a promising game made by people who very obviously care.I honestly hope that someone else enjoys this game, but I truly didn't.(Also, the game's levelling is ♥♥♥♥♥♥, there's a lot of grinding and new party members never match the level of your party)
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely cute! All the characters are lovely and their queerness is apparent without overshadowing the rest of their personalities. The story is very interesting and has strong emotional beats, though the plotting is occasionally a little messy. The high points more than balance out the low ones though and the game's conclusion and character arcs were very satisfying.I enjoyed the battle system, which was a mix of grid-based tactical RPG party combat and Paper Mario-style action commands. Each party member has their own move set with unique timings, range, and area of effect.  Figuring out who to bring and how to use them effectively in each fight is very satisfying. The game has a bit of a steep difficulty curve as enemies (especially bosses) ramp up their damage very fast if you can't do blocks with good timing, but healing is plentiful and the ability to restart a fight immediately after losing helps to make re-doing tough fights less frustrating. Since enemies can be encountered (or avoided) in the overworld to start battles, I was hoping to have some sort of first-strike system to get an edge going into a fight, but that didn't seem to be available.Overall, I had a great time with this game, both in the main story and in the handful of secret side trips lurking around. Highly recommend to anyone who is a fan of action-command RPGs and queer witches.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: My god, where do I begin? Ikenfell does so many things right. It is a turn-based Paper Mario style video game with many queer characters. You could essentially call it a gay Harry Potter, but that would do it injustice in many ways. We follow Maritte as she tries to find her sister, Safina, in Ikenfell and end up meeting a host of wonderful characters. The combat is extremely tight and janky in some parts - if you're bad at timing-related action sequences, you will probably burn yourself out in the middle of one of the fights, which, mind you, can take over 1-1.5 hours if you're not buffed right (also, there is no pause button while you're in a fight!). As challenging as these fights are, you do feel hella satisfied beating the crap out of many fun bosses, all of whom have their own unique weakness patterns.The story of Ikenfell is well-done. I particularly enjoyed the ending and the journey throughout and watching some characters step up to the plate (although they're all predictable in most ways) was very heartfelt. Now, the best thing about Ikenfell is its brilliant sound design. The boss battles, character themes (some with vocals) are very upbeat and fun to listen to. I highly recommend playing Ikenfell, but keep taking breaks, lest you develop a grudge against this game simply because you end up dying after a half-hour's worth of efforts in a fight sequence.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe it took me so long to get around to this game! At first I was intimidated because I'm not great with timed key presses, but I got the hang of enough moves to beat the game. It had good enemy diversity, didn't feel super grindy, and the dungeons weren't overly long or confusing. The last bosses did drag on a bit (mainly the secret ones), so I'm really glad I looked up a guide to make sure I didn't miss anything and have to do them again. It was really satisfying when I beat them though! The epilogue made my gay little heart very happy :3
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the combat. Initially, it felt like the game had a low margin for error, and I suppose that's still somewhat maintained, but, as late game approached and XP started pouring in - the boosted levels made the difficulty start to back down. Story also started out interesting and mysterious, but as the mystery was revealed, it turned into a drama with everyone hugging and crying. Not that drama can't be interesting, but so much of it felt predicated on a "whoops, I forgot to mention that". The game is so focused on pairing everyone up for its Happily Ever After ending, but here I'm rolling my eyes on how irresponsible this all feels. Meh. That combat was good, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: A story we found endearing, paired with a quite engaging tactical turn-based combat system with timing elements. The visual and sound design were excellent throughout (we even still have some of the songs stuck in our head), and the puzzles the game offered were generally simple but enjoyable. And every single character was delightful, or at worst compelling, in their own ways.Overall, a fun game, and the way it treats queer identities and relationships as normal really helped make it also quite the cozy experience for us.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who barely ever plays JRPGs, Ikenfell is uniquely interesting and was a really fun play for me. I love the characters, I think there is a lot of fun to be had and while generally I'm terrible at fighting, the implementation of the auto-timer and the option to win every battle were both incredibly helpful to me. After I turned the auto-timer on, I won pretty much every battle first try.The music is also really cool - I like that some of the characters had themes with singing in! Ima and Rook were personal favourites, but Gilda is an obvious love of mine.The epilogue does make me desperately want to see a sequel. While I'm not sure how likely it is to happen, I think it would be even more fun to play as long as they keep all of the features they had in this game (auto-timer, insta win, etc.)The only gripes I had:- Sometimes, as many other reviewers have said, the battles can get a little boring. In several instances, the boss or their minions would have several turns, while your player characters only get one turn per person, so you have to spend a few minutes just watching your characters lose health. Even if the boss and the minions already outnumber your party. So it can be rage-inducing, as well.- I would've liked to have more than 3 people in my party at any given time. I thought the game would lead up to the final battle allowing me to use all 6 characters, but I ended up levelling up and spending money on three characters I never even used. My final party was Gilda, Ima and Rook, but tbh I never gave Nel anything more because I just found them completely useless.I did use a walkthrough for the majority of it (bc im usually just bad at video games anyway lol) and of course auto-timing so I can't speak that much for the difficulty of the game. However, the environments, music and overall aesthetic was nothing but charming.If there was to be no sequel, I would be morose. But, I do hope to see content of these characters and their story if not through video game. I'll miss them a lot. I hope to see them again some time!!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: So charming and finely crafted! I was worried re-trying a JRPG after remembering the random-battle repeat-the-same-attack grind so common in games of my youth (that I otherwise treasured), but this has re-vitalized my perspective on the genre. If I pick up more modern RPGs (Sea of Stars, looking at you) in the future it's thanks to this game.Oh, and to clarify the gameplay evolutions I found here that I liked -- there's an added dexterity element to attack and defense that makes fighting fun. Also other good trends (some pretty old) like roaming, defeatable mobs rather than the random swirl into battle that punches your flow-state in the gut. That and just good craftsmanship - the player moves are balanced enough that you won't have exclusive favorites you spam. The dungeons are rewarding one-sitting experiences, each with a unique twist and fun secrets. The world unfolds well - the map makes promises about future exploration that get fulfilled and fast travel pops up once you need it. Also, lol, there's at least one boss battle where your opponent sings the boss theme. This and Baldur's Gate. Let the trend continue.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: cute graphics, cute story, cute characters, absolutely fantastic accessibility options. i recommend turning the timed hits system off in the options, and turn on the ability to win any battle by pushing a button in combat, this makes combat a lot more enjoyable, and makes its so that backtracking through previous areas is less of hassle, this game for sure isn't for everyone but its certainly for me and anyone who likes cute rpg maker / pixel art style games with a lot of heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE THIS GAME SM!! The battles are challenging, but not too challenging if you have the right strategy, and I just have to say that I have had to restart this game several times, and I did not mind that because the ikenfell is just that fun. Also, most of the music was made by the same people who made the soundtrack (like backround music) for Steven Universe, so if you are a fan of Steven Universe backround music, you should check this game out, it is really well made!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I'm typically not really a fan of these turn-based tactical combat systems, but was really engaged by the refreshing and approachable active-time elements which gave the combat a natural and compelling flow. Additionally, the spells themselves are a wide variety of effects, feel good, and rarely was there any one I wasn't using often. I also ended up really enjoying the story. Though the quest design and plot is pretty simple and formulaic, the character storytelling is really the driving force and hits pretty dang well. Definite recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, the game has cute artwork and a nice setting and a pretty decent plot, but, for me, the most engaging feature was the turn-based, grid-based battle gameplay. A *huge* variety of moves and strategic interactions opens up a variety of tactics and play styles to experiment with and optimize by the lategame. The game rewards exploration and risk-taking with a wide variety of loot, and the special items open up further options when it comes to the battles. I finished the story, now I want more fun fights!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Great storyGreat settingGreat charactersInteresting and dynamic combat that offers a lot of options for how to build your teamPHENOMENAL MUSIC - This isn't an exaggeration. The music for this game is incredible with several original, voiced tracks unique to each character. It's so charming, it makes up for the game's one massive, major con...Cons:Near the end game, I could not get my damage to scale appropriately to handle the bosses the game threw at me. This led to a string of extremely tedious boss fights that weren't challenging, just time consuming as I whittled down bloated health pool after bloated health pool. Every boss summons minions and there will be times when you feel like the enemy has done 10 things since the last time you got to act.I still recommend this game because the vast majority of the game is a delight, including the combat for the first ~75 to 80% of the game.But, when it comes to Chapter 8 (and secret bosses if you're going for achievements), just turn on the instant victory button and skip these boss battles. There's nothing enjoyable or gratifying about them.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: The battle system and gameplay was unique, if sometimes a little frustrating to learn. However, story was a really great YA-style focused adventure, and the music... oh my God the music. It's worth it for the music alone. Just enjoy the adventure, have some fun battles along the way, and save the school.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Relatively small beautiful game with awesome music. Most of the gameplay is taken up by timing and turn-based battles (i love the animations so much), but accessibility settings do allow you to semi- or even fully automate the timing so you can focus on the strategy. You can also enable an autowin option with is pretty handy and definitely reduces stress. You can also skip a lot of smaller battles by just avoiding the enemies, but that will make the boss battles harder.There's a lot of characters in the story, and though i do find that their development is evenly distributed, there's also a small and limited amount for everyone and i do with i could've seen more. They're indearing and i will miss seeing them, especially a certain two coven mages :') The story has a bit of a stronger focus, it's decently paced. Though most of it is spent trying to get an item/get into a certain location, it's part of the gameplay which i don't mind.I also absolutely love how queer this game is, it's heartwarming to see people just existing so casually and comfortably in their identities. Overall, i had a great time playing this and was looking forward to seeing more every time. Still listening to the OST on loop.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I've absolutely adored Ikenfell. It is a beautiful play on the magic school genre that gives me warm Undertale vibes with it's playful array of enemies, friends, and everything in between. And that's not even starting on the music, including a beautiful vocal piece. Please don't hesitate to give this game a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: It's very cute, very gay, very retro. Works for me. :) Story's nice, music is great (some of the vocal songs have awkward lyrics but it's fine) , and the tactical combat is fun. It blends a kind of quicktime system where you can block or increase damage by pressing the action key at the moment of impact. Sort of like FF8's gunblade.Level scaling can be a little extreme. One level makes a pretty huge difference, so you kinda do have to go around grinding sometimes... unless you're just REALLY good at this kind of tactical turn-based combat, and have quick reaction time. And you'll want to anyway, to have the kind of money you'll want. That said, it's not THAT much grinding. It's just an occasional 'eh, i better go spend 15-25 minutes before i continue'. Could be worse, but it'd be nice if it was more of something that happens along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice turn-based RPG with a wonderful story, pretty good as a casual game if you just want to relax and enjoy the story (options menu even has accommodations for such things) for those looking for a challenge in the combat i'd recommend either no grinding encounters and/or no battle items, both of which i did on my playthrough and had a fairly challenging, but rewarding experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly standard old-school style RPG, if this is your type of game then you'll probably enjoy it. Don't expect AAA level production values, but do expect fun. The focus is on the story and characters, and it's good. The battles use a turn based tactical combat system, but with a button press timing based component that is probably my least favorite aspect. It is meant to keep you engaged, but ends up meaning you cannot go through even the lowest stakes battles without a level of focus you may not want to give the game, i.e. no multitasking while playing this game despite being turn based. If this sort of game is your jam though, don't let that discourage you, pick it up. Especially if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: The little spin to the solid turn-base grid combat gives it unique flavors. The soundtrack is nice, and the story, while set in a fantasy world, is relatable. The game's inclusiveness also extends to people who prefer story over gameplay.By all means, It's not perfect, and there are details that can be improved, but you can tell it's made with love and care.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: At the end, its fine. I don't personally find the story or characters interesting enough to want to replay, and the gameplay is, at best, annoying. I still think its okay, worth a play if a story about gay witches trying to stop the world from ending, but the twists aren't very fulfilling and I feel like most of the actual answers land with a bit of a wet squib rather than any level of intensity. If you like the idea of games made for LGBT and POC by LGBT and POC, give it a play... if only to give you an idea of how high the bar for such things is.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS AMAZING!!!!The graphics are nostalgic. They remind me of all NES graphics and the story was surprising good! The character development was fun! . The battle system is what really blew me away. I lioved that I could hit buttons at the right time to increase duration, attack, etc! It gets complex which makes it more enjoyable and not boring! Really, really amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid RPG exploration game in a partially abandoned fantasy magic school setting. The characters, game mechanics, setting, music, art, and overall plot are pretty solid! Also characters get actual character development and pretty decent dialog, although I wish there was a little more of it to see. The battle system lets you switch up your party a lot, they all gain exp so you don't have to worry about leveling up anyone if you wanna rotate them into your party and see how they fight. You also have a partial parry/timing system where your attacks must be timed to work, but if you time a parry to your enemies' attacks you get reduced damage, it works pretty well! The only real cons that I have are1. I felt like the game rushes the last like 1/3 of the game and the plot suffers a bit as a result2.  you can't really get any flavor text when exploring rooms. There's so many neat little baubles or features in so many rooms, and trying to interact with like 95% of them gives you nothing. Only items you're supposed to pick up get any reaction. Your party will also not interact with each other unless in a cutscene. And this isn't like, a game breaker, but it does make the game feel a little emptier
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I start a lot of games, but barely finish them. This is an exception. I played through it in three sessions, and loved every minute of it. It feels like a modern interpretation of Harry Potter, with a gameplay loop inspired by Paper Mario (the good one), and visuals that remind of the SNES.It has an interesting story, interesting characters that are all essentially are trying to do the best they can, a combat system that's just challenging enough and interesting enough to be engaging without being overwhelming, and it doesn't overstay its welcome. It also runs great on pretty much any PC, including handhelds, even if they aren't of the latest generation.This is, quite simply, the most fun I've had with a game in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: My little gay heart is completely in love with this game.For starters the soundtrack is AMAZING, not only it fits with the game, but the songs are complete bangers.Then the game play is really well crafted. It's hard and feels challenging but the learning curve is well adjusted not for it to feel impossible. The final battles all tie really well with the plot and the combat itself adds to it. The optional bosses are just another level.And the plot is SO good. I loved every single character and I cried more than once with the story. Feels, just a lot of feels.Ikenfell is a really solid game that I want everybody to play just because this world deserves to be a little bit more happy
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: When I first booted up this game, my main thought was, "Uh oh, is this going to be really boring?" The opening was... underwhelming. Everything felt very basic... the dialogue was bland, so was the music, and the story... well, it didn't exactly start with a bang. The opening hook, I suppose, is that your main character is an "ordinary," someone with no magic--who now suddenly has magic, and would like to know why. Also she's looking for her sister. Somehow neither of these things, off the bat, hooked me at all. But it didn't take remotely long for me to start getting into it. The gameplay, at first, was the main thing that drew me in--it's got a very Paper Mario-esque battle system that I find super fun, and the longer you play, the more party members you amass... the more complex and interesting the battles get. Then the story starts to pick up too. The characters get more interesting, the stakes get higher, more is revealed about the world, you start to genuinely wonder what's going on... sure some characters don't get nearly as much development as they deserve, but enough do that after a while I realized I was genuinely, properly invested. And the gameplay kept being great too--often in RPGs, you run the risk of battles getting samey and boring, but Ikenfell manages to avoid this, thanks to how many unique characters and enemies you can play as and fight against, respectively. Plus some special items that really can massively change how you approach battles... meanwhile your characters are slowly unlocking new abilities, and those also can change how you approach stuff... yeah. Just a lot of really great detail and diversity to work with in the gameplay. And then the story reached a point that was just... SO good... it abruptly cemented itself as one of my favorite video game stories of all time (yes, despite all its character development flaws). At that point, the gameplay and the story finally merged for me--now I felt the  I was playing as in the battle--my motivation for winning the battle was more than it just being fun, it was to protect the characters and help them carry out  motivations. Might sound sappy, but honestly that's the level of investment I want in my story heavy games.At this point, I think it should come as no surprise for me to say that this is one of my new favorite games. Celeste is still my #1 no question, but if I were to pick a #2... Ikenfell would be in the running. I just wish  character in the party was given enough development to be really compelling...
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the battle system, story, secrets, and the overall challenge.  Grinding wasn't necessary, but the option was always there, and exploration was rewarding .  The last several battles are tough, especially the optional content, but with proper inventory management and getting the timings right, you can do it.  If there's a sequel, I'd look forward to continuing to follow the same characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I know a lot of folks like to compare charming and quirky games to Earthbound on SNES, but Ikenfell is doing the most. In many aspects it reminds me of Mario RPG on the SNES as well. Not to mention a diverse cast of characters with representation for people of color, women, and LGBTQIA identifying folks. There are so many details about this game to praise, but instead of listing them here, It is best that other players experience them first hand without spoilers. I wish I could play Ikenfell for the first time again myself.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: The story, the gameplay, the music, and the fact that there is not a single cishet character are all amazing elements of this game. It's really fun in every way, and an amazing game that everyone should play. This is one of the few video game stories that have invoked real emotions in me. This game is truly a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: The save points are cats. Automatic thumbs up for me.The combat is always just difficult enough to be engaging, while not necessarily being unfair. Except for the secret superboss after you find all of the things. I was pulling my hair out over that one.Also, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ everyone is gay. They're all gay. Even the characters you think might be straight--nope, actually gay.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about Ikenfell. I appreciate it for what it is, and I applaud the effort that went into it. That's why my review is positive, but unfortunately it has some flaws that made it tough for me to get through.I don't like the combat timing system, so I greatly appreciate the option to bypass it. The difficulty settings are quite generous. Ikenfell is terribly cute, and overflowing with charm. I really liked most of the characters. I got a few different vibes while playing, including Earthbound and classic Legend of Zelda. The dungeon puzzles were a lot of fun. I really hate how enemies are loot pinatas - they drop coins all over the place after combat. Wish I could have just been given the money at the end of battle.The combat system is where it all falls apart for me. Combat is a grid based tactical system, and the fundamentals are sound. I think it could have done so much better with a bit more work on the combat system. In general, most abilities are extremely restrictive about your positioning and where you can target. Most enemies are much more free than you are to move around the battlefield and use abilities with less restrictions. Most enemies are extremely fast to the point that they get 2 or 3 turns to my 1. Most combat abilities are slow to give time for the timing mechanic. These effects combine to make combat feel extremely slow and tedius, as I spend a lot of time just sitting and watching the enemies dance circles around my characters. Most boss battles are the same - they lay a trap, immediately take a second turn to attack, and sometimes a third, and they summon waves of buddies. I found the lategame boss battles to be a real slog. (Tedium, not difficulty) I think it would have been better to have a slightly bigger battlefield, allow the characters to walk through the spot where allies are standing, have less restrictive attack positioning, make enemies have approximately the same number of turns as the player, and make the enemies play by the same rules as the player in regards to setting a trap (enemies get free turns after setting traps, the player does not).
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly warm hearted and inclusive queer adventure. Searching for your missing sister you go to the school of magic that she attends and meet a wacky cast of characters who join you along the way. With a turn based battle system that is on a grid you have to strategically place your characters to best use their skills. Can you discover why your sister has gone missing and what terrible secrets she may have uncovered in the past? Charming pixel graphics and a score by the composers to Steven Universe (Aivi & Surasshu) give this quirky and fun RPG a lot of character.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Solid little Indie RPG with a timing-based light-tactics combat system and a fun little Harry Potter-esque save the magic school storyline.The combat *can* get a little frustrating toward the endgame as timing windows on attacks can be a little inconsistent, some having a sweet spot shortly after the impact, while others come before it, and the difference between a hit and a miss can be the difference between a glancing blow and half of your health, but the characters you have access to have varied enough movesets that if you hit a roadblock chances are you can pick a party that is better suited to the specific challenge, and thanks to the even experience distribution among your party members you don't have to worry about anybody falling behind.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR if you like turn based RPGS, especially old school ones with action commands, give the game a shot. Good story, good gameplay, good balance. I normally don't leave steam reviews, I'm pretty sure I have around 600 games and have probably left around 6 reviews, if you think you'll like it, check it out, truly a diamond in the rough.This game is not only fun to play but is a work of art. If you don't like turn based RPGs this game probably won't be for you, maybe even newer turn based RPG players, but I would still at least recomend trying it out for the 2 hours that Steam will let you refund it for. It has beautiful pixel art and a well thought out story, as well as engaging gameplay. Where some most turn based RPGs fall short, in my opinion, this game keeps you engaged with action commands. I could make a whole rant about how action commands can make you feel engaged in a turn based RPG but I feel like if you've ever played some classics like the older paper mario games you'll know what I mean, and if you;re a fan of turn based RPGs and haven;t played those either check them out their a joy. However, back to this game the story, the music, the art, and the gameplay all come together to create a turn based RPG like the games that made me fall in love with the series. Many Turn based RPGs are kind of cookie cutter now a days in my feeling but this one isn't, however that being said if you aren;t a fan of so called "woke culture" don't try this game out. I personally don't think it's a problem and in fact adds to the game as it's one of the few games that has nonbinary pronouns and even in the party selcet screen includes pronouns, but if that bothers you enough to truly miss what is a phenomenal game then just move on, don't buy it and leave a negative review due to it being "woke". Honestly though just check it out, it's a well balanced turn based RPG that gripped me story and gameplay wise, I also feel it's really well balanced as it even had me, a person who plays a lot of turnbased RPGs and is the classic hoarder of "I don't want to use a consumable what if I need it later" using consumables much more often because I felt I had to. Not in a bad way like the game is too hard, just I didn't wind up with 99 potions in my bag at the end of the last boss fight, more like 5 or 6, which was still more than enough. It's engaging both gameplay wise and story wise, and I would highly recomend playing at least til the refund timer of 2 hours, I started to really enjoy the game then, but I stopped playing, came back later and played further recently. IT has essentially been my obsession since then, taking all my free hours because I wanted to know what happens to the characters, and what has happened to the characters before I played.

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is a tidy tactics RPG with timing mechanics. I was heartened to see accessibility options for removing them, though, as they are absolutely required. Still, I enjoyed getting used to the various abilities and learning enemy patterns. And boy does every battle tend to test you. You really have to learn how to adapt, how to utilize each character to the best of your ability, and how to build in ways conducive to their skills.The story is heartwarming, the characters engaging, and the lessons on point. I enjoyed the writing greatly and honestly could not find an excuse to put the game down lest I delay finding out more. The game is genuinely unsettling when it wants to be, mysterious at other times, and warm and bright in others.There is one legitimate criticism and one utterly absurd criticism. The legitimate criticism is that the game can get slow. Enemies are not chumps to defeat unless you've outleveled the area greatly, and your item management and care well be put to the test. Even with optimal play, encounters can take a while, and bosses are true feats of endurance on occasion. I don't personally see this as a bad thing, as the gameplay was fun for me throughout.The illegitimate criticism is that this game is "too Tumblr". By which I presume to mean "ew, diverse cast and non-binary pronouns". This is far more a plus, and they handle the inclusion tastefully and without going hamfisted. Quite honestly, every person complaining about this is giving a positive review of the game and a negative review for themselves.The only negative I truly found in this game...was that I genuinely hated one song. I ADORE the soundtrack for every single other track; the music is wonderfully evocative and catchy. But...geez, that one song is painful. Still, I'd gladly play through this game again even if I had to hear it five times as much as I did.Absolutely worth your time and money to experience. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Really lovely little RPG, had a lot of fun and it's a solid little play. Story has a lot of nice little twists and revelations, for both characters and the overall plot. Characters are all largely likable and party members useful, equipment is mostly 'better number = better' but it does have a nice balance of choosing between some stats like stacking more defense or speed. Combat system is quite decent, though the ranges on abilities can be a little annoying at times and it gets a bit punishing later on, I ended up just turning off the button timing in combat (though you can leave it at 'everything is minimum good' for an okay challenge) Bosses can be a bit brutal with extra phases or they summon extra minions or a lot of enemies have multi hit abilities. Climax falls a little flat with an extra twist/revelation I don't think was explicitly needed and kind of takes away from the big fight before it. Final fight just feels kind of anticlimatic. Wonderful looking graphics, everything looks made with care and character and level design are well done. Wears it's queerness on it's sleeve, happy for the representation and treats everything as normal. Was a delight to see. Really hope to see more from this developer, this was an excellent little game and shows a lot of potential for more. Solid B+

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't have the biggest expectations going into this game because I had only heard from it once before in an off-hand comment from a Youtuber. After finishing the main story, and soon to be going back to get the last few achievements, I will say that I really came to love this game, and I don't think I've gotten bored in the approximately 17 hours it took me to complete the main story. --Story, Characters, and World--The story of Ikenfell starts out pretty simply. The main protagonist comes to Ikenfell in search of her sister and ends up getting involved in a situation that will have you exploring every corner of Ikenfell, making new friends and learning more about Ikenfell and magic.  The characters of Ikenfell are very charming and there is more depth to their characters than what might be on the surface. The playable cast are fun and you are introduced to them nicely over the course of the main story. The world itself is also very interesting and uses it's magical world well, creating one that feels as if it goes far beyond the school in more ways than one.--Gameplay--Gameplay is a very straight-forward RPG with a deceptive amount of depth, especially when you start getting later in the game. Items, equipment, and skills are pretty easy to manage early on, but as you get further into the game you have to consider what stats are most important for each character. You also get a wide variety of skills that are unique to each playable character which helps cement a unique identity for each of them, and later on you might come to consider some characters more useful than others depending on your own strategy. I have found a few tier lists for Ikenfell and it seems like anyone's placement can vary wildly based on the player. Try to experiment and see which characters work best for you.The actual combat of the game is straight-forward. In a Paper-Mario-like fashion almost every skill in the game utilizes some form of timing in order to influence it's effectiveness, including enemy attacks. With proper timing you can drastically increase the amount of damage/healing/effect a skill does, and when a foe uses a skill on you almost every single one can have their effects mitigated with proper timing as well. This becomes ESSENTIAL late in the game, but for those who are worried about their own skills there are accessibility options that allow you to make all timings manual, make all timings "nice" with the ability to make them "great!" with timing, and automatically making all timings "great!" by default. --Presentation--The game looks very good. UI elements are very clean, the soundtrack is incredibly solid with a handful of "special" tracks that you will know when you get to them the first time. There are many nice quality of life features that allow players to receive content warnings, as well as options for those who may be photosensitive in some fashion. The entire game utilizes pixel artwork both in and out of battle, with battle itself having a wide variety of different animations for playable characters and enemies. --Misc--This game has a lot of quirky aspects to it. The save points you utilize throughout the entire game are cats, and there are a wide variety of cats. You may also become addicted to the purring sound they make when used, like I was. This game is also unapologetically queer and has a focus on representation that, in my opinion, is done very respectfully. The plot of the game does not hinge on these themes, but they are present and are important to the backstories and development of most of the cast. I went into this game knowing it was going to be extremely queer, and I surely did not leave disappointed. --Overall--Overall, I really, really enjoyed my time with Ikenfell and want to recommend it to anyone who is looking for a fun RPG with a fun magical world. The characters are fun and there is a surprising amount of room to experiment and see what strategies work best for you. Easily one of my favorite queer-friendly games that I would love to come back to again in the future and will definitely share with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game!  Explore a school of magic with eccentric characters as you search for your missing sister.  I will say that this game is LBGTQ friendly.  You'll have a variety of pronouns and relationships within the game....so if that is the kind of thing that will bug you, then this game isn't for you.   And also, **** you.  As with most RPGs, you will find yourself exploring "dungeons" with monsters, solving puzzles, and gathering gear.  You'll also find yourself collecting some collectibles and perhaps exploring extra side content.The combat involves some minor placement strategy.  You and three of your potentially six characters will navigate a small battlefield to get the best placement for the attack you want to do.  In order to really become successful, you need to time the attacks with a button press.  I was worried this would add extra stress to the game, whereas I wanted a casual destressing game.  However, I found the timing involved isn't very difficult...although there are settings that let you modify this feature in various ways (such as always giving you the "good" or "great" setting).I don't normally focus on music unless it is a mechanic of the game, but there are a couple of songs with vocals that are really good.  I still have one stuck in my head as I'm typing this.  I thought it was a cool addition to the game.I would've loved to have played this with voiced lines, but I understand that this is not always do-able (especially for a smaller team).  Hopefully they will one day add an extended version with voiced lines...but even if they don't, it was still a good game.If I could make one recommendation to people playing for the first time...after you clear an area for the first time, look up a walkthrough for JUST THAT AREA and make sure you collected all the gems.  I ended the game one short.  I guess I could go back through every single area looking for them via a walkthrough...but it just seems like so much effort.Also, stay tuned after the credits for a short epilogue!  :-D

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing I should mention is that this is a very LGBT-friendly game. So for those who are uncomfortable about such things, you have been warned.- Let me start by saying that I had fun with the game. It is a pixel game, so don't expect amazing graphics, but it is pretty impressive with what it has.-The game is an RPG, but doesn't play with the simple turn-based type of battles. It's more strategic because it allows you to position your characters, before you choose an attack. Not only that, but there is variety in the types of attack, here's a quick list: single target, multiple targets, traps, decoy, buffs, debuffs, healing, and repositioning. However, when it comes to buffs and debuffs, there were times when it felt that they had no real impact in battle.-The story is actually interesting, with plenty of plot twists, and a wonderful ending. The characters are diverse, but it felt pretty similar to your typical anime. One example would be a character that is very shy, and one that is energetic.- Loved the soundtrack, especially the songs with vocals.- Important problem, as you can tell by the amount of time I have played the game, its not a very long game. Most of the time I spent playing it, was to grind for EXP points until I maxed out their levels.Overall, even though it had problems, they were very small, and the price felt fair for what I got. Therefore, I would recommend the game to any RPG lover.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a tough call... The story about a mystery in a magic school for wizards is quite interesting (J.K made millions off that idea so there is certainly something appealing about it.) The writing and the graphics are charming enough, the design of the school is interesting to explore and the UI and controls do the job but your best playing with a controller like most RPGmaker..ish games there is no mouse support.  However its not all good; the combat arguably boils down to a mini game quick time event where you need to press the A button at the crucial moment in order to buff your attack or your defense (and you really need to do this as some battles get extremely long and difficult otherwise, especially the boss battles.) The closer to perfect the better the buff. Its engaging at first but it quickly becomes tedious and annoying. Now luckily you can disable this mechanic so that all of your attacks are full strength but then consequently the combat becomes kinda boring so its a real catch 22 situation. Maybe you could argue there is another dimension to the combat is in terms of positioning since some moves have areas of effect but this really just boils down to avoiding grouping your units to close together or having them all in the same row etc,The other big issue I have is that the loot/gear/equipment whatever you want to call it is very underwhelming. For example a lot of items just increase a single stat by a point or two at most but then at the same time will decrease another stat by the same amount. So they are not really upgrades. True upgrades seem few and far between so progression is slow and not very fun.I guess if you like RPGmaker style of games and stories about magic schools for children or you have a masochistic predilection for quick time events then I do recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really hard to recommend, even though I really wanted to like it. You can clearly tell a lot of love and work went into this game. I wasn't sure whether to give this a positive review or a negative one, but ultimately decided on the latter despite my feelings. I completed the game. Not 100%, but I finished the story and have no desire to go back.It's very inventive. You have to position yourself to use abilities and then press buttons in time with animations to do/take less damage. At first this feels fun, but as time goes on it becomes absolutely tedious as combat gets longer and longer.I kept up with gearing my characters with the best gear. I fought every single battle I could, I sold every item I didn't think I would use. Towards the middle of the game I almost had more money than I could spend, but towards the beginning and end it was all I could do to scrape together what I needed for gear. And you NEED that gear as much as you need the levels.Each new area the stats of your enemies skyrocket and you barely ever feel like you're getting stronger when you manage to keep up on gear. If you don't keep up on gear enemies will often go twice before you characters get turns, and your low damage will make your turns feel meaningless. I feel like the game wants you to experiment and find the best combination of speed, power, and defense out of the gear to best tackle individual challenges, but it gives you nowhere near enough money to do this. I only had the money to keep myself geared because I exploited the hell of out a character's "steal" spell that replicates expensive boss loot and got lucky.I think the problem with boss battles is that they're basically normal battles but worse in every way. Bosses have erratic or tricky button-mashing patterns you have to press to avoid damage. They have enormous health pools. But the most egregious sin of all is that almost all of them spawn normal enemies onto the field to fight alongside them.Normal enemies already feel like collective mini-bosses on their own. Imagine fighting a boss who fills the playing field with them. Some bosses will only do this once, but others will disgorge new ones when you wipe the board, or just keep sending them out regardless of whether you defeated the last ones.If it gets frustrating the menu has "auto-win" and "auto-QTE success" features you can enable to make battles a cakewalk, but that feels like giving up. And if I didn't know any better, it feels like a sign that the devs gave up on balancing the game in favor of just giving players a cop out feature for when it got too tedious.It's passable. A young girl without magic journeys to a magic school to find her lost sister and gets magic powers and friends along the way. The story is shallow and focuses entirely on the conflict and drama at hand; the worldbuilding is nonexistant. We're constantly told that this or that thing is  or  in the realm of magic but given no reason or context as to why. You find almost nothing out about the school, it's curriculum, or the wider world. If I was ever told what the name of the region we're in, the continent we're on, or what the name of the world was it flew completely by me. Even the main conflict at the end of the game is largely unexplained. The world is doomed because...because it is. Because the "natural order isn't being obeyed" I guess? Even that's me trying to fill in the blanks.The story largely is centralized around its characters. They're all LGBT and they have a lot of the traumas that come with being LGBT. They're all serviceable if kind of shallow. I didn't really feel much of anything for any of them.I don't really understand the main drama with the main character and her sister. The main character is upset because her sister never told any of her friends she had a sister? Which is...normal? I mean I don't talk about my family at work or school, or even with my friends. It just never comes up. We're all focused on getting stuff done or having fun with each other. I mean, literally none of the characters mentioned anything about their families if it wasn't immediately plot-related. Get over yourself Maritte.I also don't understand Maritte's...relationship choice? Maritte spent all game defusing that person. They had like, two friendly interactions all game. I don't understand how that somehow blossomed into love? I'm not arguing a case for her other love interest either, that was just flirty and fun and not the basis for a loving relationship either. Love requires time and intimacy that doesn't involve changing someone's emotional diapers.Ima feels out of place. Ze's one of the main characters and uses the very awkward ze/zir enby pronouns(even mentally pronouncing them gets tiresome, and I still cannot get behind them at all). Ze has no trauma, no baggage, and almost no use in the plot. Everything ze contributes could easily have been done by other characters. I guess ze acts as a temporary leader at one point? But I feel even there another character could have benefited from that spotlight and potential growth moment. Ze almost feels like a self-insert character, in a weird way.This one baffled me the most. There was some great music in this game and I loved most of it. But my god was it poorly utilized in some places.Towards the middle of the game you get your final party member and Ima's theme song becomes the main battle song for the next arc. It's a cool song, but the following arc takes place somewhere unsettling and creepy, and having the ambiance go from dark to overly cheerful in battle is jarring. Especially because all the enemies and surroundings in battle are still creepy.Also this is another reason I think Ima was a self-insert. Ze gets zir own theme song with vocals. There are, to my knowledge, four theme songs with vocals in the game. Three of them are for main characters and one is for an important NPC's backstory. Ima adds almost nothing to the game. Why the heck was ze given one when Maritte, the  doesn't even have their own personal voiced theme song?Gilda gets one, and it gets used in mostly appropriate moments. Rook gets one...that you hear once and only once towards the end of the game if you happen to do a specific trial to get his ultimate weapon. That feels like such a late and weird place to unveil that? And that's it. Nobody else.To be honest, even with the lackluster plot. world-building, and characters, this is still salvageable. Not the plot, world-building and characters, that's beyond saving. The game-play though. I made no mention of it, but the out-of-combat puzzles were really good. That was fine.If the stats of the monsters were fine-tuned so that most monsters went down in a hit or two so combat breezed by, it wouldn't feel insufferable. You might argue that this would invalidate the spells that were clearly tailored for the more long-form combat, but that's why the boss battles exist!If normal combat was a breeze then it would actually leave people thirsting for longer combat to get more use out of the buff spells. As it stands, boss battles stand out for being just "more of the same, but even more insufferable" compared to battles against normal enemies. This could make them stand out as challenges to be overcome, turning something insufferable into a treat to look forwards to.Gear needs to be better fine-tuned. As it stands its too expensive and the sheer variety seems to beg for experimentation to find the right combination of stats. Even at the end of the game, I had no idea how to balance speed, defense, and power at all because grinding for money was literal torture and it was all I could do to get everyone kitted out to make combat slightly bearable.Get it on sale if you have to.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked:* The world, story, and characters. Like when I first read the books by the author-who-must-not-be-named, I wanted to see the next area, the next chapter, and discover new parts of the world.* The music and sound design are instrumental (pun intended) in bringing the world to life* The exploration and puzzles (for the most part; less trial-and-error in the Stacks and less hiding things behind other things, please)* The adorable style (cats are save points and restore your HP!)* Accessibility options (otherwise I would have stopped playing, see below)I didn't like:* The combat: While there is a large variety of enemies and enemy moves, the enemies functionally fall into a few categories, and so combat has no tactical depth, which makes them slow and boring unless you really like action timing. _childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give a game a thumbs-sideways if one aspect is bad but the rest is good. Because the combat system in this game has some frustrating flaws, but every other aspect is great.So first the good: The plot, characters and setting are extremely good. The visuals and music are great. Dungeon design and puzzles are good. You get a variety of swappable party members by the end whose abilities each feel different. As an RPG, this game checks every box except one.Also, the combat isn't all bad. It takes place on a grid and each character and enemy has a vareity of moves which can target different tiles or AoEs for different damage levels, or cause status effects. Each character feels different and in the right circumstances it is fun. Thy certainly tried.The bad: Sadly some fundamental bad decisions ruin the combat.First of all, the timed hits. It seems balanced on the assumption that you'll be getting "Great" on 3/4 of all attacks and "Ok" on the rest, punishes you severely if you ever get a "Miss". Enemy attacks are mostly well telegraphed, but the player's attacks aren't. Every move has a different animation with its own timing that must be learned. And a LOT of them (including and especially the main character's main attack) make it almost impossible to tell what the moment is that you're supposed to hit the button. Failing a QTE because your reflexes are bad is one thing, but failing because you couldn't guess when you're supposed to hit the button sucks. If you flub it, you generally do exactly 1 damage and basically waste your turn.Fortunately there's an option to automatically land the timing on every move, and after a certain point I just turned it on and left it there. That laves it feeling like it's missing some features (ie nothing deals status effects), but it's the only way to enjoy the game.Second, the stat balancing is just... bad. Damage seems to be calculated by just subtracting defense from damage, but the numbers are so low that a single point makes too much difference. If you do anything except stack attack buffs in ever inventory slot you'll be doing 1 or 2 damage with every attack, and a single level up sometimes doubles the damage you're dealing to a foe. Of course there's not enough attack up items to go around so usually at least one person will be doing no damage. Maybe level grinding would reduce this a little, but it goes both ways--if you're scoring "Great"s most enemy attacks do 1-4 damage, or multiple hits of those numbers, and a defense buff will reduce them to exactly 1.Overall, if you're willing to play an RPG with a flawed combat system if the rest of the RPG is really good, this is a good pick.

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is an earnest, charming RPG with a tactics twist to its combat. The story isn't life changing, but it's an inclusive tale with a lot of heart that's worth seeing through to the end. Each of the characters are interesting and have personal troubles and interesting arcs.To put it succinctly, if you enjoy classic RPG's and a little bit of Paper Mario-esque timing in combat, you owe it to yourself to give this a try! At a generous 15-ish hours to complete the story it's a perfect length to enjoy.
