_childDocuments_.review: Cute magic school game with a colourful artstyle and catchy music. The battle system has a 'timed hit' system like Paper Mario, but it was optional... so I turned it off. I greatly appreciated the option as someone who sucks at those types of mechanics. The pace felt just right for the length of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell tells a wonderful story with many twists and turns, using a wide cast of colorful characters, each feeling unique. The battle mechanics are fun at first, with grid-, turn-, and rhythm-based attacks, however after some time the battles, especially boss ones, tend to drag on for much longer than is interesting. The different environments are all especially unique, and they all have nice soundtracks (except I personally can't stand the library one). I had to stop before I was able to beat the game, as whatever boss I was on was just too difficult, and I wouldn't stand having to grind for levels. Overall not bad, especially if you're into/have the stamina for RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: First found the soundtrack on Spotify by listening to Aivi and Surasshu, and I just had to check it out. It's so cute! It immediately made me feel good that there are such diverse characters, and that there's use of so many different personal pronouns. I give it bonus points just because of how comforting it was to see nonbinary representation and feel the lgbt voices that went into the story.Some have said it's slow and I like that about it, it lets me relax. There's settings to make it as easy as possible, so you can go through the places and the story quicker, in case timing attacks isn't your strong suit. So: cute, comforting, lgbt positive, good music. Will continue recommending it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: At the beginning I was honestly skeptical and the game was stuck in my library for a long time. In the beginning, it briefly felt like a more colorful, pixelated Harry Potter version. But not everything that has to do with magic is Harry Potter, so I took a look. And: That was by far one of the most beautiful games I've played so far. It looks simple, but it's not. I was able to completely lose myself in the gaming world. From the beautiful music and the sound, to deeper insights into the stories of individual characters, the special combat system which challenged me just right, a well thought-out story thread, to an absolutely great queer design. This game made me so happy. It's nice to play a game with queer characters without that being the focus. For example, the use of various pronouns without making a big fuss about it. Thank you for this game <3
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Shortly before buying this game, I bought Bug Fables to try and fill the Paper Mario void in my heart. Sadly, it didn't manage to do so. I bought this game cuz a dev i like (Greg Lobanov) reccomended it on his twitter, and was shocked to discover it filled that hole a million time better than the actual Paper Mario clone did. If you're looking for a hard game, this ain't it. If your looking for a game where you go to wizard school and use awesome wizard attacks to feel cool, this is it. Seriously, perfectly timing button presses to do max damage to your enemies is my jam, and this game does that very well. I especially love the different themes for each character, who all specialize in various fields of magic.There are options to skip battles, cutscenes, as well as potentially upsetting content. It really feels like the devs wanted this to be a game anyone could enjoy.Half your party is non-binary, which is certainly a welcome inclusion considering another wizard-school series that turned out to not be so friendly to the trans community.The graphics are charming and the soundtrack is phenominal. The only real weakness is the story which, while engaing for the first half, gets quite bloated later on. The second half (maybe last third?) focuses more on maximizing drama, and unneccesary plot twists (only a few of which are good) that are obviously meant to shock the audience and not to tell a good story.Not a deal-breaker, though, and I'd definately reccomend this game if you're trying to fill the Paper Mario void or need a new series about kids at a wizarding school
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I loved everything about Ikenfell and can strongly recommend it.The story has a somewhat slow start, but it's engaging enough and after a couple hours, you really get hooked and want to get to know all the story arcs of the endearing and profound characters, and the mysteries of Ikenfell. I finished the game yesterday and I'm still left thinking about the last few chapters, the ending and the moving personalities of this ensemble cast.And then the gameplay was also a big hook for me. Each area/"dungeon" has cleverly designed puzzles, which are fairly simple yet very fulfilling to resolve, while also enjoying the beautiful artwork and level design.And battles are a mix of tactical RPG (you move characters on a grid and take actions such as using a spell or an item) and timing-based action as each skill you use or are subjected to requires a precise timing to maximize its effect (or defend yourself for enemy skills). This was a lot of fun for me, but I understand that it can be off-putting and difficult for others - but the game provides accessibility options so that you can reduce the stakes (no possibility to fail timing) or even guarantee a perfect ("GREAT") action (so no timing involved at all).Added to all this, the sound design and soundtrack are top notch, even featuring vocals for the theme songs of some of the main characters, which give them a lot of personality.Overall, it's one of the best games I've played in recent years. It did start a bit slow so keep going for a couple hours if you're not hooked in right away by the story, it gets really interesting after the initial setup.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: What a good gosh darn GAME! Loved the music, the characters, the lore of the world, and how it handled topics that generally would be difficult to deal with. _childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, this is a great game and I highly recommend playing it. I originally bought it because the music is by the legendary Aivi & Surashu (Steven Universe composers), but the combat, the story, and the characters are all fantastic. This is one of the few games I've had the urge to replay.That being said, it does have its faults:1. My main issue is with the story pacing. The early part of the game has you going after objective A, which requires objective B, which requires objective C, which requires objective D. It makes it feel like you aren't making any progress for a while. Thankfully, it is less of an issue in the late-game.2. The combat often feels like it drags on for a long time. If that's an issue, however, there is an accessibility option to immediately end combat encounters. 3. The music tracks with lyrics are a bit too short, so they feel very repetitive in longer battle, e.g., fighting Gilda. Also, Ima's track, "Paint the Future" (used in the trailer) refers to "Martin Luther King Jr." as "Martin Luther" who is a DIFFERENT PERSON. I love that track and the rest of Sammus' music, but that will never *not* bother me.Also, this game also features a lot of LGBTQ+ representation which I really appreciate. From my understanding of the game's development, the story was completely rewritten to have a pro-LGBTQ+ narrative, and I can only applaud the developers for this endeavor. Unfortunately, the representation does feel a bit forced at times which takes you out of the immersion.All in all, I would highly recommend picking this game up.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed making my way through this game.Mechanically, the combat was enjoyable enough at first, but the mobs got boring rather quickly for me. There is absolutely no variation in what you do to get the good/great bonuses from turns/defense in combat, something that games that this takes a page from in that regard have done better since Super Mario RPG. I definitely utilized skipping a few fights so that I wasn't too fatigued. It seems charming enough at first but really drags the game down. Considering I started this game because I decided to try what I thought would be a quick RPG (which it is as far as RPG's go), it was a disappointment here. Fortunately, the accessibility features are things I wouldn't mind seeing in more games just on principle, and using them also let me focus more on the good parts of the game. I felt the non-combat gameplay puzzles and gimmicks had a good balance of being something to think about, but not too hard, and without overstaying its welcome.Seeing as I picked the game up thinking about "RPG", I definitely did notice later on the game that I wasn't the target audience. Considering that being the case for 95%+ of games and characters, it was noticeable but is  a complaint. It's great that games like this can exist, and it is close-minded to believe anything otherwise. Besides that, I feel like it handles sensitive topics such as trauma very well.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This game... is **really** worth the playthrough if you enjoy RPGs with an interesting story. Granted, the combat did get kinda tedious at certain points, the fact they just built in an "instant victory" button in case you just want to play the story is really rad. The music combined with the charm of the characters, is also really well done. I found myself tearing up a little at certain points. Overall, very much worth the time I put into it. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Generally a good game all around. The combat is easy to understand and so is the story. The music of this game is in all honesty beautiful and doesn't reuse the same battle music each and every battle. The story however is a bit underwhelming, and loses focus around the point you get your 6th and final party member. There is a HUGE amount of representation in this game though, in all honesty I was kinda shocked seeing how much there was, there was even an ace character! There isn't a lot of representation for a lot of shows/games but Ikenfell went above and beyond to try and include a ton of representation. Sadly though, there isn't a lot of replayability, but for a game that costs 20 bucks, and could easily take several days to complete, I say Ikenfell is a perfect game for anybody that loves a turn based tactics game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Great story, and I was never bored. Starting this game will make you want to see things through. The writing is simple, but it gets the job done and then some.- Characters are likable enough- Soundtrack is great. I was really surprised by it.- Plays a lot like the Mario & Luigi series, for other nostalgic fans of that. This is a good thing.- Entirely pixel art, yet I was really impressed by it.- Everything you could possibly dislike is skippable (more below)- No money troubles and you always afford everything you need throughout.- Photosensitive mode. Thank you. (This one is minor)Cons (mostly combat):- Combat is really slow. Nearly every encounter you face multiple enemies, and waiting for all of them to go is painfully bland. Encounters feel pointless except you need to increase your stats in order to stand a chance against bosses (there is an option to skip fights altogether, which I began using for every minor encounter halfway through.)- Some combat timings are a lot harder than others (there is an option to disable timings.)- Bosses take forever to beat without even being difficult. They all rely on summoning to which just draws out fights.- Bonus content, like finding gems and such, is so obscure that I completed the game without even finding where to use them. (Minor)- Character development is spread far apart, maybe a minute every hour so of gameplay in the form of memory shards. My favorite chapter to experience was the epilogue (which is just story, goes to show how combat dulls things). You don't find out anything outside of personalities about most of the main cast. There is one single interaction between the main character and her sister, despite this relationship being the one of the main aspects of the story- Lyrics in certain songs (usually major boss battles) are out of place at best.Other thoughts:I don't want to comment on the LGBTQ tropes, of which there are many, due to the debate's controversial nature. It's great that there are games dedicated to representation but those elements are there just to be there, and do not contribute to the plot itself much. It doesn't really matter. In other words, you need to be an extremist to dislike the game just for those elements.So overall:Story 9/10Art/Soundtrack 10/10Gameplay 6/10Definitely worth it for the price asked, and I would play it again if I happened to forget the story overnight.

The battle begins.Okay really, the timings are a lot in this game, and it sure loves to dump one dungeon after the next. But there are really sweet moments in the game, the characters are all interesting, makes you feel like a real gaymer. Keep your expectations in check and you'll be alright.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some cute character art, but besides that, the world is incredibly bland and repetitive, the characters are completely one-dimensional caricatures of themselves, the story (up until now) feels very cliché and old, and the combat is quite slow and very unsatisfying.I wouldn't have a problem with slow combat if it actually felt tactical, but this weird combination of slow animations, turn-based combat and accurate timing just doesn't work for me.I bought this game thinking it might be a cute and fun experience portraying different types of people, with a diverse cast of characters and feeling very inclusive...but instead I couldn't find a single character worth sympathizing with. The writing is really poor and the characters feel like someone came up with three adjectives, some pixel artwork for their face and called it a day. There's absolutely no investment on any of the characters' sides (not even "I'm looking for my lost sister and am very sad about her disappearance"), so I don't think this game will ever get any more investment from me.Honestly, don't get this game if you're looking for a wholesome story with cute and quirky characters. Just get A Hat In Time instead and it'll definitely be worth your while.

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell stands out for being the first turn-based RPG in years to really hold my attention. Active blocking and attacking does wonders for keeping you engaged during battles. It also adds a little controllable randomness which can spice up the predictability of an encounter. Using a turn-timeline and grid-based positioning further differentiates the game from blander turn-based systems. The game is paced well and offers new mechanics and foes regularly throughout each chapter. I thoroughly enjoyed the diversity, music, story, sprite work, character designs, environments, and most everything else Ikenfell had to offer. I was not prepared to become so fond of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is a very sweet RPG combining grid-based action-command combat, memorable characters and a magical school setting. Mechanically there's plenty to sink your teeth into, and switching up your party and their equipment lets you try different approaches, which keeps things interesting as you go through the game. Watching the characters grow together is lovely, and they work well as an ensemble cast (although I will always have a soft spot for Ima!) If you're looking for a satisfying 20-30 hour RPG, I definitely recommend Ikenfell!

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is the gayest game you're going to find in a long time, and if you can't handle that, then you might want to try somewhere else. Moving past that, I'd say its an extremely polished and competent turn based game, with little secrets and optional things to do sprinkled everywhere. The accessibility options are also great, and surprised me with an option to just skip the battle if I so chose. I can understand that now however, after playing the game. This game is a challenge the whole way through, with a difficulty so fine tuned that it nearly completely eliminated my hoarders mentality that I had developed from other games. You will NEED to use items to survive some battles. This, combined with the game's interesting and varied combat range system, makes for very good gameplay. I was repeatedly challenged throughout my playthrough despite finding many secrets. In regards to the story, my feelings are a little more mixed. The reasons the characters have for doing things are always explained eventually, but sometimes the explanation can be a little lacking and shoehorned IMO. Despite this, the overarching story (when not getting sidetracked) is good. The ending is satisfying, and when paired with everything else the game has to offer, no one should really be complaining about the story. It does its job just fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: A great combination of turn-based tactics and whatever Paper Mario RPG has going on, tied together with an interesting story and plenty of secrets. I also like that the game gives you the option to pause when it's in the background (which I used extensively), skip cutscenes (which I used after forgetting to save), and even auto-win battles for accessibility (which I never used). With good action commands and strategy, you never have to grind, and I ended up only very rarely having to use items mid-battle. Attacks are, with a couple of exceptions, pretty easy to see where to hit the button, making it entirely your own fault if you take much damage at all from them. just git gud lmaoA lot of the music is, well, background, but I love Gilda's, Ima's, and Rook's themes (they have lyrics).Without spoilers, the last fight in the main story is incredible.Also, I think there are a grand total of zero straight cis men (though the groundskeeper and tavern owner might be, idk), which I find mildly amusing.

The timing mechanic was well designed and quite fun to me, though I'm biased as a huge fan of rhythm games.

_childDocuments_.review: paper mario crossed over with little witch academia and found a whole lot of LGBT rep along the way, what????it is very solid all around with cute pixel art, some absolute banger songs, a wholesome and well-written story. the combat-- i feel like in order for a turn based RPG to be interesting enough to play it really only needs action buttons -or- grid system, but this game has both. it also helps that most areas are short and sweet, taking you to the next of many bosses before they wear out their welcome.also for a game this cutesy, this has some surprisingly horrifying bosses wth?????this game's biggest weakness is that the equipment/store menus are not quite as convenient as they could be, and that is a very small nitpick. i was struggling to think of any particular weakness tbh. i guess sometimes areas and fights feel like they exist for the sake of content, but the content is still fun, so who cares.multiple non-binary characters, multiple gay characters and aro rep are all huge pluses. also the entire party is quite likable, and while i had a few favorites i stuck with, i appreciated that it was easy to rotate folks in even if you haven't been using them. one more shout out for the vocal tracks. well worth the time and price, also a steal on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is a lovely and charming game from start to finish. Each of the characters is charming, the story is well paced and well thought out. Any twist it has was well earned and not a "Gotcha" twist. And all of the gameplay mechanics are intensely enjoyable. The only negative things I have to say about this game is its so close to being 12/10 amazing all that the odd quirks it has just stand out to me. But overall I'd give this a 8.5 or 9 out of 10. A simple joy to play from start to finish.The good: - Turn based RPG on a tactical grid. It adds just that little bit of extra depth to the standard RPG game that kept it from getting horribly repetitive. - Every character's abilities felt truly unique and fun - The sound track is wonderful - Story pacing is very well done - Story is very well written and while keeping a charming and relaxing atmosphere still manages to tug on your heart strings - Game didn't get lost in the grind, combat doesn't overstay its welcome and doesn't overburden you with an encounter every 12 steps for artifical paddingThe Meh - The puzzles. They were there, there were alright. Nothing I haven't seen before and nothing I couldn't solve in 2 minutes.The Bad/Odd choices they made - Can only switch party at save points. I personally like hot swapping party, I think it makes a game more fun and typically leads to more interesting encounters when you can bring our your specialists as needed - Lack of player inflictable status effects. Positioning was key in this game, buffs were important, it made for a good play style. However the solution to every enemy was get the biggest nuke, maybe add a turn delay. Everything else just didn't do enough to justify it. - Fall prey to the healer problem. Nel has a unique spell list, and in theory it is fun. I enjoyed it at the beginning of the game. But they just don't do enough at the end. Poison is too weak, and healing alone wont win you a combat. I just used Ima's Regen and it was better than Nel's Aura. Very few RPGs succeed at making the healer feel useful all game, and unfortunately Ikenfell is not one of them. - Menus information. You just get a basic overview of what your spells do, no information on them. Not even how the duration of your buff works. You can figure it out, it isn't hard. But it would be nice to be able to read everything your spell can do. - Item info. Why can't I see the stats on my item? Why do I have to play the game of mathematics? This was just a poor decision. - Lack of unique items. Weapons just made your attack go up. Most items outside of the gem shop just did stat stuff. I liked the special accessories, and wish more items had cool effects.So yeah, there it is. I feel like all my critiques are pretty nit picky at this point. Everything is just almost there, almost to being absolutely wonderful in every way they just stick out. But none the less I highly recommend it, its a comfortable touching story, with fun gameplay mechanics that can help amplify the notes the story is going for.

_childDocuments_.review: this is one of the best games i've ever played. it wont be perfect (no games will), but it was an incredible experience and it's one of my all time favorites now. every time i played it'd be hard for me to stop playing because i was so interested in the story! it was very fun to see how it developed, and as i found out more and more i became more invested.the combat system was also really nice! if i had to describe it, it'd be like a fire emblem and super mario rpg crossover. it was very fun to play with and find strategies for. i admit, at first the timing was a little hard to get down but i got much better at it after playing more. there's also options in the menu for if you want to "turn off" the timing.i heavily enjoy the accessibility/quality of life options, such as content warnings and photosensitive mode. i did not use them myself, but it's very pleasing to see settings like those for the people who want or need something like that.the soundtrack was wonderful, the people who worked on it are fantastic. aivi and surasshu have done a great job as per usual, i'd really recommend buying it on bandcamp if you'd like to listen to it on your own. listening to one of the songs as i write this as a matter of fact.i would say more, but i've gone on long enough already. everything about this game was so pleasing and it was great experiencing every bit of it. absolutely recommended if you're a fan of this type of stuff!

_childDocuments_.review: A niche game for a niche audience, but oh, what a treat Ikenfell is if it's your kind of thing. A cute, heartwarming story with interesting characters, fascinating locales and creatures, and supported by a beautiful chiptune soundtrack. Plenty of clever puzzles, and turn-based battles that reward clever tactics over grinding.There were a few instances where I found myself clicking all over a room trying to find a way to progress and I'm unsure whether that was intentional, my fault for missing a clue, or just an issue with my colorblindness rendering an otherwise obvious button invisible, but that aside, Ikenfell was damn near perfect for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good old-school-style RPG, with one big issues: you hit buttons during attack and defense animations to deal more or receive less damage, but the game's calibrated where you need to have perfect timing for these. Miss a button press and your attacks are almost useless and one attack could knock off a third of your HP. Hit the buttons perfectly (or just turn on the option to make all button presses perfect automatically) and the game's really easy. Miss a few and fights become a long slog.If you can get over that, it's a solid game with an interesting plot, one that gets into some surprisingly dark territory for a game with such cutesy design, and that doesn't outstay its welcome much, finishing in about 20 hours of play.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: As I'm sure others have noted, this is a indie game with 16-ish bit graphics. The gameplay is a mix of Paper Mario and turn based tactics. The story is incredibly compelling, and will resonate with fans of games such as Celeste or Wandersong. Also, the representation is really fantastic. My favourite part about this game is that because everyone is a magic user, there are no mana bars to speak of. The most limited your attacks can get are just simple cooldowns. Overall, I definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Yo why does the book keep murdering me?(In all seriousness it is a very good game, has a sort of young adult fantasy feel for the story and despite being a tile based strategy game the timed blocking and attacks bring to mind Paper Mario or Super Mario Bros battle-wise. At least they do for me.)A very fun game, if you think you might like it, check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: My god, these witches gay! Good for them, good for them.Ikenfell is an excellent game. It has great pixelart style. It has a loveable cast of relatable characters. Its plot, while heavy on the themes, is fun to interact with. It has music which quite honestly slaps. The mechanics are also mostly good; while late-game fights have the kind of difficulty curve that mostly boils down to "more things on screen to worry about", the overall premise of putting a Paper Mario-style timing-based turn RPG onto a tactical grid is great, and the need for button presses keep fights engaging. It is also really nice when the game clicks with you once you find your favorite squad to fight with.The game is also relatively easy and pleasant to 100%, especially with the guides available on Steam (and I'd also recommend going for 100% since it's more of a good game, and also having a level or two on the final boss can make a significant difference).Overall, I wish more games had so much fun simply existing as Ikenfell does. A recommend for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a really solid game. Way better then I thought it would be. Theres some nick picks here and there like some of the bosses being slogs near the end of the game or the sub-par writing when it comes to everyone not being straight. Writing is good for the story and characters mostly. However the LGBTQ stuff isnt written very well into the story and took me a little out of it whenever it comes up. Music and sound is top notch. _childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game enough to anyone in the LGBTAIQ+ community! The entire cast of characters is queer, the story will keep you on the edge of your seat, the music is wonderful, and the aesthetic is absolutely precious. It's like Legend of Zelda, Chrono Trigger, and the Harry Potter series came together an had one big gay baby. The story also addresses mental health in an incredibly constructive way. _childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell. Let me first address that the game does include some heavy handed LGBTQ insertions that had my eyes rolling and despite being a magic school for mage users from all around, it seems most of the straight students have gone home for summer vacation. Even the title itself is colored to a gender neutral yellow and purple, coincidence? Perhaps, but not likely due to the direction the game takes.Enough about tags, what is Ikenfell?You play as Maritte, a girl with no magic powers at all who has come to the magical school of Ikenfell in search of her sister Safina who hasn't come home for summer vacation. Along the way you meet Safinas friends and they join you as you puzzle your way through the school, fighting against ghosts, angry birds, magic books...evil denim pants...?Ikenfell is a turn based pixel RPG very reminiscent of Earthbound and not just with its strange enemies. Two party members follow the a main leader, however once more members join your party you can bench other characters to make better synergies; not even Maritte, the main lead of the game, is safe from being sidelined which is nice that you are not forced to use her if you find someone else you want in your party.The combat field is a three long twelve wide grid where your characters hop around trying their hardest not to get in each others way in order to preform attacks and skills. The combat relies on a timing mechanic where pressing a button at the right time can prevent damage, status effects, and even death; a precise button press could turn the tide of a battle in your favor. Though a neat mechanic that always keeps you on your button pushing toes you can actually toggle this in the options menu to automatic or semi-auto if you want to try for maximum damage but don't want to miss. If you are just interested in the story or perhaps don't have time to fight every battle, there is also an instant victory condition in the options menu as well.The story itself is good but the beginning was like someone turning a light switch on and off, saying to myself "I like this." then "I don't like this." then "I like this." I really hate to bring up the LGBTQ tag again, but its like that old vegan joke, "How do you know someone is vegan? They'll tell you". It's the same here. Some characters are offenders of this or have an excessive flamboyant nature (looking at you Oxley) that seem unrealistic, but there are some relationships in game that show great interactions instead, the headmistress of the school being just one of them. Albeit being cliché at points with some rare spelling errors, the middle and ending of Ikenfell kept the ball rolling and had me invested with it's narrative and characters' progression and personalities, even having an affinity to characters i didn't initially like. That is until the next person tells me their sexual preference.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Great turn-based rpg with timed mechanics. Played through this back when it was on gamepass and am happy to be able to own it on Steam since it is on sale right now. Has a great soundtrack, story is good and the characters even more so. Worth at least one playthrough, definitely scratches that Mother 3 itch for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is difficult to *just* give a thumbs up or down to, since I love the game but there are aspects of the gameplay that drive me up the wall. Lets start with the big con: This game is *SLOW* - the combat, the cut scenes, the animations, and everything else move very slowly. It can be supremely tedious at times. This could easily be fixed by the developers adding in a 2x feature or something in the settings, which is amazing they do not since the settings are super robust.Pros: Great story, inclusive and interesting characters, interesting combat (that would be more interesting if a bit faster). Settings allow you to completely ignore combat (or at least "instant win" it) which is great when you're tired of the tediousness. All in all, I keep playing it because it has a lovely story and good music. But it puts me to sleep sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing! The combat has a unique mechanic where timing is very important and timing is something I very much struggle with in games. This meant this game was quite difficult to me however the game is prepared for that where you can adjust how much importance is done on the timing!! Whilst I didn't remove the timing completely I did adjust it so if I messed up the timing it wasn't super bad for me. Another thing about the combat is when going from one section to another you find the jump in the monsters to be quite high. This put me off fighting the monsters so I'd try to avoid instead however my recommendation is to not to do this as the XP you get from them means you'll often be leveling up and those few stats increase you get per level help you out loads!! The story was beautiful! This game has kept me gripped for weeks as I've been playing it and having just finished it I have to say I'm in tears over how beautiful it was.There were a few things that annoyed me, specifically with the equipment management. When equipping something you choose the character you want then the item to equip however I think it would have been better the to do it the other way around as I would often be cycling through multiple characters to find out if this new thing I found was an upgrade!And the map also annoyed me to, sometimes I would forget where a certain building was and it wasn't clear to me from looking at the map where things were. To be fair this is a minor one as the map does tell you where to go next and the way the game is designed you do learn things quickly and the Traveller Oaks are a godsend! Overall I loved it and recommend you give it a go if your interested in a magic school stories!!

_childDocuments_.review: really lovely game! _childDocuments_.review: The game starts off deceptively simple, by Chapter 4 it is quite complex. I love the story, of a "normie" searching for her talented sister only to find she has talents too! _childDocuments_.review: This game is a nice surprise, and if you are looking for a good story about magic and friendship while you are waiting for your Howwards's letter, Ikenfell is the perfect candidate. _childDocuments_.review: The good and middle good points first: the game has a nice story, if you are a little tired of plot twist every time and just want to play with a not that simple but by far not a complex story.Second: I love RPGS and tactical RPGS, Final Fantasy Tactics, Disgaea, that type of games and jet, there's a point where the combat stops being challenging to become frustrating, even if I hate cheating, first I turned on the auto success to avoid the timing system to be a drag to plainly activating the option to pass every combat since a combat of more than 10 minutes thanks to the grunts spawning and the boss huge amount of HP is something that really makes the combat system frustrating at the very end, jet the atempt to innovate in the matter is something that I should give credit to the developing team, it just needed a better balancing.Third: the puzzles are not that challenging but they really need to be able to observe really well the area and some trial and error to find out what you are supposed to do.The not so tolerant part: I'm not against LGBT, actually I support every equal rights movement and jet, if one of the issues in the media is the lack of representation ob the LGBT community, it's also true that in this game they are over represented, all the characters that have any weight in the story is either homosexual or bisexual (except petronella but they never mention her likes in terms of sexuality in the whole game), the point is; I don't condemn gay characters in any form of media, but it's also true that a lot of times seeing this and not have a warning will bring people who is completely intolerant and try to bring a issue in a game where the sexuality of the characters doesn't affect the story, my only suggestion to the creators is; if you will bring this kind of relationships, don't forget straight relationships or people will start demanding you to  put a LGBT label to the game, even if it's not that important.The bad part: The game feels a little unpolished in terms of power growth with the items and the challenges, as stated before, this makes the last part instead to feel challenging to start to feel annoying, even if the characters are charming, there's no so much introspection to the core problems of most of the main cast, and if you need a finish battle button (you can activate it from the option menu) to enjoy the game again, (even if that's good for the people who only wants to read the story) that's a call for saying that the battle system is not that good.Long story short: if you want to play a simple but entertaining story, with a somehow decent level of challenges and you don't mind using the same strategy many times in a very long boss fight (for around ten bosses) chances are, you will enjoy the game.

You have a super interesting set of characters you can have in your team, I honestly just love them all.  The story is really interesting too, I cant say ive ever been bored in this game. _childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This very much a "get it on sale" sort of game. The characters are cute and their interactions are interesting, and it's nice to have some LGBTQ+ representation. The overall story was interesting, though had implications that I feel weren't fully explored, a sequel in this setting would definitely go a ways towards fleshing out how magic works in this setting. The game does a lot to make it accessible as possible, with content warnings, reaction difficulty, the ability to skip combats to just experience the story, and so on all being available. That's kinda where my praise for the game ends, unfortunately. Combat is kind of tedious, with the furthest extent of tactics being huddling your characters together to utilize a buff better. Beyond that, all you're doing is meandering into the right spot to hit an enemy and timing your hits to maximize damage. Honestly, you can just turn on the instant-win button in options and skip all of the fights and you won't miss out on anything, and I'm saying this as someone who normally like RPG combat. On top of that, your attacks, even when you get the best timing for them, always feel impotent, which for a game where you play a new generation of witches summoning phenomenally powerful elemental magic is a bad sign.Overall, I wouldn't say the game is bad, especially since this is this studio's first game, but I can't endorse it at full price. Pick it up on sale, and maybe skip all the combats and just enjoy the characters.Also Gilda is the best character in this and she is criminally underutilized c'mon I need more Gilda in my life she's awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is an absolute delight from start to finish. the story is compelling and the characters are fleshed out, there is good representation across the board, both in terms of race and sexuality.It has a neat battle mechanic that lets you boost your attack or defence against one with timing. What's that? you don't do well with rhythm or have chronic finger pain? NO PROBLEM! this game is inclusive and has different settings for accessibility. You can set the battle mechanic from manual to semi automatic or automatic! It's friendly to those with photo-sensitivity too, with a setting to turn of flashes and NO complicated buttons! A,S and enter with the directional buttons are all you need!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy this game - It was fun, compelling and surprising (three times I rolled my eyes at the story and said "Oh it's so obvious where this is going" and not once was I right), and adorable visually. I know some people have written negatively about the characters, but I disagree. They might not be the most developed characters, but I still found myself very much so caring for them and their struggles and the story as a whole.I think one of the biggest strengths about the game mechanics is that skill trees aren't permanent. Because it's based on equipment you can buy, sell, equip, un-equip and pass around, you could completely change your strategy half way through the game if you feel like it (although, you can't always buy back what you sell).There are a couple of issues, though most can be summed up as "stats displays." Not only is enemy hp not displayed during battle (but you can check it), there's no way to look at their defense, power, or speed (also, your own speed is confusing - the stat is never defined and I had to look it up online). Also, equipment doesn't say what effect it has on you, but rather the net change of putting it on - which includes what happens when you take off what you already have. This made it confusing and difficult to make decisions. Lastly, while everything is skippable for repeat play throughs, there can be some very long cut scenes and very much dialogue to click through. Despite this issue, the game is still great - lots of hidden things like optional bosses, collect-a-thons, and side quests. Plus, the many many accessibility features is a huge huge plus (including content warnings, sensory overload protection settings, and gameplay changes)I bought the game on sale, but it would have been worth it at full price too
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: An RPG seemingly inspired by games like Earthbound and Undertale, and similar to those games, Ikenfell has a colorful comic strip art style and some comical, yet sincerely heartfelt writing.  Because of that, as well as its indie origins, the queer characters throughout also feel like their inclusion comes from a genuine place, and that they weren't just shoehorned in at the demand of a marketing committee to increase sales because their company's highly conservative board of directors needs a few more easy dollars to throw at the next election.  Gameplay is also inspired by another classic in Super Mario RPG/Paper Mario, with mastery of timed hits and blocks essential to surviving combat.  However, combat also takes place on a wide grid (3x12) and each characters' spells will only strike tiles within specific ranges, so positioning them carefully to deal damage, stay out of enemy attack range and within reach of one another's healing abilities is another major component of the game's strategy.  One can also set traps on panels to harm foes, create/destroy obstacles that impede movement, and knock targets around with certain moves, so there's a pretty significant tactical element on top too.  Ikenfell may not be flawless or the most groundbreaking of games, but it never pretends to be, either; it's clearly a work of passion from a few gamers who wanted to tell a fun story while entertaining you with familiar, yet creatively remixed gameplay, a high level of polish and a reasonable runtime, and that gives it way more mileage with me than some overstuffed multi-million-dollar release that takes itself way too damn seriously while giving you nothing to see or do that's actually entertaining (but which has plenty of fanboys/paid marketeers who insist that its uninventive, disingenuous 'message' is too important to not slog through 90+ hours of tedious busywork for).  So, for being a well-made and entertaining passion project, yet humble enough that it doesn't have to stop every 8 seconds to milk every last brownie point out of its woke element, I say Ikenfell is worthy of a purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This game did something for me that I don't encounter very often. As I was approaching the end, I got a sad sense of melancholy because I realized I'll only get to experience it for the first time once. Major props for that. All in all, the game is an absolutely lovely experience. The cast is charming, the soundtrack is (almost entirely) fantastic, the animations are cute, and the accessibility settings are a great touch. And, even the story was varied enough to have had my attention throughout the game. It's not quite an ideal experience, as in a few places, it feels like things were left on the cutting room floor. Presumably due to deadlines. And, having tons of great accessories but only one slot did get a tad frustrating. On the whole, though? It's a wonderful experience. Oh, and best of all? You save the game by petting kitties.Aspects of game design are smartly done and make it a point to avoid wasting your time. Fast travel points are plentiful. The secrets are hidden without being obtuse, giving you a solid chance of finding them first time around if you're paying attention. The combat feels varied with every character having a unique skillset that has its own usage cases, which is terrific. And, the enemy roster is surprisingly varied. Save points always heal you. You're approaching a dungeon? Have a save point. You're making your way through a dungeon, have a shortcut to the start and access to a save point. You have an upcoming boss fight? Have a save point. You just finished a boss fight? Have a save point. It's so nice. And, funnily enough, having access to button timing window length and skip combat actually led me to be interested in doing *more* combat. That's just good design.I did see some complaints about the combat system, which confused me. So, I replayed the optional bosses and last boss a few times in different party configurations, attempting not using items, and avoiding buffs/debuffs. Ah. I understand. A few tips:-One, gain a level or two. There's a reason why it's so quick and easy. A level or two makes a big difference. Especially if you just gained a new party member.-Two, do enough combat to get the hang of button press timings. Make sure your controller is charged or run it wired. And, don't hesitate to switch the accessibility settings to like...Semi-Auto. There's no shame in using those. -Three, party configuration matters. It's tempting to just use the characters you like the most, but having damage output AND support matters in boss fights. Having distance heals and buffs can really help turn the tide of battle. And, so can having a dedicated character whose job is to constantly smack the boss.-Four, don't stockpile your items. Use them to fill whatever you're missing. Damage output, defense, regen...it makes a big difference. There's no reason to turn things into a slog.-Five, unless the boss is close to death, deal with the adds. That'll make traversal and setting up for attacks easier. And, it will let you focus down the boss or give you time to recover from a bad situation.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay wise, incorporating timing is used to make players get more involved with the combat system. How engaging it is varies from person to person, though the pitfall of "losing a match because you mistime a single action" ala Virgo vs the Zodiacs is not present, which should give you a glimpse of the overall difficulty. Personally, I recommend new players to turn on semi-auto for the first few chapters to get a sense of the timing without trivializing everything.  Though be warned that once you master the rhythm part, most boss fights become cakewalks. The boss fights are also pitfalls of the game: Because of the 3xN nature of the grid, a single enemy will be severely restricted mobility wise, which, combined with traps, allow for the players to pummel bosses relentlessly. There is also no mana, so resource management isn't a concern.  This means that bosses are difficult not because of their own patterns or gimmicks, but mostly because they throw a bunch of minions at you, sometimes to the point of blocking movement altogether, though I guess that's the point. Of course, at any time players can press the "I win" button, which I applaud for inclusivity - video games are for everyone after all. Speaking of inclusivity, the story absolutely does that theme justice. So as to not get into spoiler territories, I'll just say that you have representation of all sexual orientation and genders: from lesbians, gay, straight, to  enbies and genderqueer... It shows a more realistic representation of life, that your identities matter, and most importantly, that people can accomplish great things regardless of background. Though I do wish that their identities factor into the plot or their character arc a bit more, but it's within the developers' imperative to create a fully tolerant world free of bigotry, and I respect that.Edit: apparently you can buy the entire game's OST on bandcamp, so I retract that part of my review.

It's also a stress-free game, where you can save your game easily, and if you lose a battle the game just let you restart the last battle. It's highly playable, enjoyable game, totally recommended! _childDocuments_.review: An rpg with a lot of heart for the shes, gays, and theys. I have a couple frustrations. While animations look nice, they can be lengthy and draw out fights. The story can have some rough pacing at points. But I do think this game is worth your while and you will find a lot to love about Ikenfell and its characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Just, like, in summary - the game is good. You should buy it. It exemplifies all of the best parts of the games as a creative works, instead of vehicles for large companies to make lots of money. If that's even vaguely something you're interested in, the game is worth your time.Ikenfell is very well written and the characters are well-developed. The soundtrack - by the same people who composed the soundtrack for Steven Universe - is incredible, and the pixel art is gorgeous.The game play is mostly good. The dungeon / area puzzles are very enjoyable, and combat progression feels very well balanced. The only downside is that the combat itself - in my opinion - does feel repetitive. This is especially noticeable for boss battles, which almost always have the same structure - one main boss that summons minions, which you can mostly ignore in favor of chipping away at the boss. It's only the hidden bosses at the end of the game that fundamentally shake up that pattern. It's also a point in the game's favor that there are in-game options to significantly reduce how much combat you need to do, if you want to get back to the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: The amazing pixel art drew me in and I'm glad I played it! I love RPGs and this is now one of my favourites. It's fun, I love the characters (Perty and Gilda) and setting, the music, and there are save cats! I also enjoyed progressing through the different areas and discovering what's next. The only thing is that this game could use some quality of life features, like quitting the game in-battle (quick reset?) and skipping/speeding up enemy movement animations, and maybe accessibility options for the time-based combat. Despite that, I was sucked into this game and staying up late to just get a bit further xD
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is basically if the creators of Steven Universe decided to take a stab at making a Harry Potter RPG for the gameboy color. There's a magic school, lots of kooky memorable characters, mischief, a somewhat challenging battle system, and lots of exploration. The cast of Ikenfell is extremely diverse and represents the LGBTQIA+ community well, although sometimes it feels a bit heavy handed and you get whiffs of tokenism. The art and music for this game is top notch. The music sets the tone and atmosphere of each area perfectly and lets you immerse yourself in the experience while the art is cute and unique and surprisingly diverse, ranging from adorable to horrifying depending on the need. My only gripe with the music would be Ima's theme which was a bit cringe but that's just me. The battle system is a mixture of a tactical grid and timed attacks. I really appreciated that the battle system wasn't overly complex but challenging enough that it wasn't just mashing the A button. The enemies you encounter also have a lots of interesting attacks and abilities that keep you on your toes. That being said I do wish the difficulty was set a bit higher. Mobs were easy to kill and the only thing that made the bosses difficult was their HP pool. At no point while playing the game did I feel like I would die or lose. Exploration in Ikenfell is very linear. You go from point A to point B and then to point C and so on as the plot unfolds. There are one or two optional dungeons and bosses, as well as secrets that require a bit of backtracking, but overall there is very little deviation. However each area feels distinct and creates a different vibe so it never felt off putting or tiresome. The biggest downfall of Ikenfell is with the characters. It becomes very obvious very quickly that some characters are way more powerful and useful compared to the rest and so you end up only using three of them the entire story. A re-balancing of skills is definitely needed to incentivize players to swap out and use all of the characters. The ability to swap in characters during battle like FFX would be great as well. Ikenfell is an adorable game that almost anyone can pick up casually and enjoy. The message is heartwarming and the plot surprisingly full. The game is not without its flaws but if you love gameboy color era RPG's you will love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: turns out you only realize how much you needed a game where queerness overtly and subtly pervades the world and narrative when you find yourself playing one.EDIT: after having 100%ed this game i feel like i can offer a deeper review. creating narrative tension without a designated antagonist is a challenging thing for a writer, but chevy manages to pull it off convincingly in the end. some of the side conflicts and mid-bosses are only set up as obstacles by miscommunication between characters, which i found a bit frustrating at times. But the main plot - the search for safina - is propelled along by a breadcrumb trail that cleverly turns the characters' and player's understanding of the situation on its head with every new reveal.if this game can be said to have a villain at all, that villain is trauma, and the arc of the story is ultimately about healing from emotional scars. in that way, it touched me deeply.fans of tactical rpgs are likely to love this game, though they might, like me, be irritated at the inability to pause combat or give up and retry a doomed battle. the timing mechanic adds a fun twist on classic grid tactics, but if you don't love it you can always turn it off in the settings!the accessibility options here are great as well. there are options for photosensitivity, content warnings, adjusting the consequences for timing misses or removing them altogether, even automatically winning fights if you just want the story.this is a game i haven't been able to get out of my head for days after finishing it. the epilogue is one of the most emotionally satisfying denouements to a story i've seen in a really long time. i cannot recommend ikenfell highly enough!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this review short with a list of pro's and con'spro's- great soundtrack- combat is fun with lots of different abilities. The ability to pick who i want in combat is a fun way to mix up the combat. With lots of different types of enemies combat stays fresh-  really good characters with a compelling story- the world is nice but a bit smallcon's- only one con, it is very common to have bosses spawn mobs in combat which is fine however i feel like it was an over done ability, it is also an ability i personally didn't like. _childDocuments_.review: The story is so good, so so good. If you turned off all combat and puzzles and just watched the game, it would be worth it. Compelling narrative, great cast of characters, this is why you buy this game.The combat was less good. I personally hate the timing-based attacks, but there is an option to turn that off. Even then, the non-boss fights felt like they took too long, between the animations, fairly low damage relative to enemy HP, and however turn order is calculated. The boss fights were better, and the more chaotic ones were strategic and fun. Some of the bosses would probably be more fun with the timing mechanic enabled, but oh well. The last 1/3 or so of the game has the most interesting combat.Music is great overall. More vocals would have been cool, but I get it $$$. Some of the non-boss fight music got old, but I think that's minor.Puzzles were pretty good, some better than others. Nice variety over the course of the game.Lots of secret passages and secret bosses, but I didn't find myself struggling to 100% in 23 hours. You might have to spam A on every bookshelf in the game... but the secret bosses were very fun to beat.TL;DR buy it for the story, customize combat to not be annoying for you
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I entered this game with low expectations but I was really charmed. While the game is linear and the main plot relatively cliché and he character development of each party member is simple, all the elements have the merit of being effective.Mechanically, the game works well, the puzzles are simple to figure, the combat is good if once again mechanically simple.Also there are features to make the game easier or less grindy (qte always succeed and insta-win the fight by selecting an option in the fight menu)I used the latest extensively to cut down on repetitive grindy fight (because lets be honest, most rpg feature those as grind mechanics to level up)This game has a small scale, didn't try to be too deep, too edgy, and too convoluted. It's set to do what it promises without outstaying it's welcome.So it's a big thumb up for a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Music and sound design are excellent, the timing mechanics can be challenging at times but make combat engaging, vibrant characters, engaging story with themes that really resonate with me (even as a mid-20s cishet male). If you like turn-based tactics games and/or story-driven games with magic/fantasy themes, then you'll love Ikenfell.While the tracks in game were quite strong, when the vocal versions appeared I found the lyrics to be pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ compared to the instrumentals and sound production overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes heaps of inspiration from other games and executes them all extremely well. The influences are clear but they come together to make an RPG greater than the sum of its parts.You have a battle system that's a mix of megaman battle network and Super Mario RPG,An overworld reminiscent of earthbound, with plenty of things to find and puzzles to solve, (think Golden Sun without the powers)A group of refreshing, likeable characters,Excellent music. Lots of fun, bouncy chiptunes backed by sampled instruments.Things I liked:- It was always worth solving that one extra puzzle for a chest. Found items never felt throwaway.- The sheer amount of "juice" in the battle system, and how smooth the UI is. - Enemy designs, in particular the bosses, were always fun.- About 13-14 hours in, and probably nearing the final 5th of the game. A nice length that doesn't overstay its welcome.Things I didn't like as much:- MSI Afterburner overlay crashes the game on launch.- It felt like the timing was very slightly later than it should be on some attacks. A few frames after the moment of "contact" in the animation.- The party lineup felt unbalanced. I had the 1st, 2nd, and final party members in the main group. The others failed to carve a niche.- Checking health on enemies took longer than it should, I'd prefer a keybind to show health bars on hold.I'll be keeping an eye on if there's a sequel to this, I feel like the dev has only just touched on what can be done with the systems they've made. Would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I rarely give reviews but this game deserves it. In short it is a beautiful game and you should definitely buy it.The simple but detailed pixel art is extremely eye catching, and is done incredibly well. The characters are designed so damn well, each character feels like an actual person, and believe me I got very attached to them. And they're all unique which is good, not flat. Some of the dialogue is odd at times, sometimes forced, but overall it's done very well. Storywise is pretty straightford, so not many side quests, but it is an interesting story to follow as you figure out what happened to Ikenfell. The turn based fighting seems straightford, but as you progress you get new abilities and equipment to better aid and personalise your fighting style. I love the grid based fighting, and each character has unique fighting styles that you can experiment with. The music, oh my god it is amazing. I would buy this game for the music alone. It switches between old school game music to pop to soft piano so well, and each character has their own theme which is done so damn well, just saying. Not giving anything away, but it has a scene where a character is having a panic attack, and I've gotta say it's the first one I've seen in a game before. It was done very well, without being "Oh they're having a panic attack". Don't wanna go into detail about it, but as a person who has panic attacks frequently it was good to see it represented in a realistic way. Overall I fell in love with this game very quickly, and I hope you do to.Chevy Ray, thank you so much for giving me this experience, I hope it gets as much love as it deserves

_childDocuments_.review: What a phenomenal game. I love the characters and absolutely love the story. The worldbuilding is also amazing, and I loved every minute that I played. It's games like these that remind me just why video games are such a good medium for storytelling. This tale is about love, healing, recovery, and support. If you liked Undertale, you'll absolutely love this - the soundtrack is also great. I only regret that I can't play it for the first time again, but I will likely come back to this game again in the future.
