_childDocuments_.review: ikenfell is lovely (I'm not capitalizing it because it's not capitalized in the logos and I like how it looks).I think the story progression is a real highlight. It's not a complicated story, but it's delivered well with charming characters. There's a lot of seemingly unrelated plot points and locations, but I was surprised how cohesive it all felt at the end. It covers a lot of emotional ground: triumph, loss, fear, uncertainty, glee, etc. The principal and supporting cast is packed with diverse queer folk, so if you're looking for magic school fix without transphobic and racist baggage, this is a great pick.The game's visuals are clear and effective, especially the higher-res character portraits that appear in cutscenes. This also translates to the battle system, full of unique animations (more on this later). You could describe the overall visual aesthetic as expressive, alternating between cute and dark. The soundtrack is eclectic and fantastic. Aivi Tran and Surasshu do a wonderful job blending live instruments and synthetic beats, and yes I was reminded of Steven Universe (which is certainly not a bad thing). The soundtrack is bolstered by instrumentalists like Jeff Ball and some great vocal contributions from artists like Sammus. The vocals are not ubiquitous, which makes their inclusion feel welcome instead of rote.The battle system and combat progression are more great parts of ikenfell. While it does start out a bit slow, you wind up accumulating several abilities, some of which are always handy and others that can be more situational. The battles feel like Paper Mario mixed with a light tactics game. All attacks, support moves, and even your party's defense can be strengthened with well-timed button presses. Thankfully these never require tricky or repetitive inputs. The attacks and support moves feature a variety of different effects and ranges, so positioning is key. It never felt like I needed to plan more than a couple moves in advance, though I'm reasonably confident there are optimal strategies to be found. There are no random encounters, you only initiate battles by encountering enemies in the maps or by triggering cutscenes with an ensuing boss battle. No grinding is necessary, though I did refight a couple of encounters accidentally. The equipment system leaves something to be desired, unfortunately. Though there is some fun in menuing through different gear combinations to get good stats, I would have preferred finding items that boosted your stats coupled with special effects. There are a handful of special items you can purchase with well-hidden collectibles, but these items won't affect your stats. I wound up ignoring them for most of my playthrough. It's also rarely encouraged to create specialized builds for characters, with balance taking priority.ikenfell also hosts an impressive suite of accessibility features, including options to: reduce flashing lights and other potentially triggering effects, enable a content warning system, disable text sounds, automate or semi-automate timed button presses, enable an instant victory option in the battle menu, enable auto-run, and disable camera shaking. Also of note is that there is no penalty for running from a battle with regular enemies (you cannot run away from boss battles). I never used these, so I cannot comment much on them. I will say I've seen that the instant victory option will still give you XP and enemy drops, so you're not losing anything in the progression by using this. These are great features, but it is unfortunate that there is no in-game controller or keyboard remapping. I hope such options can be added in the future.Overall, ikenfell is a great, just challenging enough RPG with a great story, wonderful music, and fantastic inclusivity and accessibility.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty nice mix of JRPG and SRPG mechanics.  I had a few sessions where I just didn't feel like doing the button-hit mechanics during the fights, and luckily this game has nice options for auto-succeeding or partially auto-succeeding which made that a lot less stressful. I also enjoyed the story, all of the characters had good and believable motivations (no one was just out trying to kill everyone because that's what evil people do). People in the LGBTQ+ community who want representation, this game has plenty of it.  There were definitely a lot of character traits that would have to be 'overcome' in other games, but really they're fine and I thought that this game handled them well.As a fan of sprite graphics, I thought that this game looked great.The music was overall good in my opinion.  There was one song that made reference to real life people, that really drew me out of the experience. It was even an alright song, I just wish those lyrics had been different, because the fights can be long so you wind up hearing them a fair amount.  But I was on board for all of the other music.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start with the negative. I am not a fan of adding quick-time triggers to RPG combat. I think that actively makes this game worse. You can turn off that gimic, but that basically puts the game in easy mode, which is a bit sad. Everything else, however, is terrific. The pixel art graphics work perfectly to tell this story and the soundtrack is just outstanding. The story took some time to grow on me, but it's amazing once it gets going. It's a perfect dark fairy tale with compelling characters and events that are serious and leave scars but never quite extinguish hope. Probably the best story I've played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful music (same artists who wrote Steven Universe background music!), intricate characters and lore, fantastically rewarding but challenging game-play, battles that encourage strategy over brute strength, and so much LGBT+ representation. A brilliant, touching, stunning game. It took me 26 hours to get through my very first run-thru, so with THAT MUCH content it is definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of older rpgs such as Phantasy Star, Shining Force and Final Fantasy and I totally loved Ikenfell! The story is lovely, the characters feel real and the combat system is quite unique. The game is neither too complicated or too simple, which makes it very engaging for casual gamers. You go through it never having to overthink about complicated inventory or equipment management but still having to make decisions about character stats that depend on their equipments. Each character has unique spells that are quite diverses, which gives a lot of possibilities toward strategies you can adopt in battle.In the end, it comes off a little bit easy, but still very, very entertaining. I had long been waiting for a rpg I would love as much as Ikenfell.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell reminds me of the RPGs I used to play when I was a kid, the kind of games where I'd stay up all night playing because I just had to know what was going to happen. The story, the characters, the lore. . . its all very captivating. I enjoyed it very much!I found the timed input attacks difficult for me to get right, so I switched the timing to auto in the options menu and  that made the game much more enjoyable for me because it became a traditional turn based strategy RPG then, without having to worry about timing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game and I am proud to have been a backer during the Kickstarter campaign. It was made with much love and brings back all the good memories from turn based RPG games in the 90s, with a bit of timing twist in the battle. The characters are all very nicely created, memorable and develop during the story of the game. All of them have unique magic powers and there is always a trio chosen for the combat that can satisfy the skills of any player.Music is fantastic, it never becomes repetitive or boring. Anyone will notice straightaway how much effort and energy was put to create a great music score.And last but not least: the story, one of the most important parts of a RPG, is great. Every chapter reveals new secrets, the memory crystals found throughout the course of the game are a nice touch to explore past happenings and in general I always wanted to play a bit more, to uncover the next plot part in this amazing story.I would easily give this game a 9/10, it may not be Breath Of Fire 2 or Chronotrigger, but it does not have much to envy from JRPG classics, it is an excellent game in its own and will definetely offer you an unforgettable 20-hour-ish gaming experience.Our duty as gamers: support the (indie) creators and make a beautiful (Christmas?) gift to your friends or yourselves :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and engaging story! Gameplay is turn-based RPG on a grid with timed hits. Accessibility features are great for when you want a break from getting perfect timing all the time or want to skip obviously winnable encounters. Took about 18 in-game hours to clear the story and get every achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Ikenfell. The strategic battle system is engaging and presented some real challenge. Even basic mobs will take your party members out quickly if your timing is off, as both offense and defense are heavily affected by a keypress-on-hit system. Note that this game does contain options to make this system more forgiving or bypass battle entirely.The story moves from beat to beat pretty well without any fetch quests or necessary grinding. "Dungeon" puzzles were not too hard and their mechanics will be familiar to players of JRPG/Zelda style games.The game has a lot of heart and likable characters. You have good flexibility to use the set of characters that you like the most. It is noteworthy that this game is inclusive in showing characters of differing sexualities and gender identities. I did not find it to be pedantic/soapboxy and it was a nice touch.Overall I liked it a lot and am looking forward to the next project by this developer!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to compare the story and tone to something, I'd say it's a bit like Steven Universe. If you like Steven Universe you'll probably like this. Personally I hate that show, but this isn't nearly as bad so if you aren't a fan you might at least be lukeworm on Ikenfell's story. The characters are overly empathetic and understanding to the point of being a bit saccharine.Gameplay-wise Ikenfell nails it. I usually don't play RPGs but this one had me hooked from start to finish. Really does something interesting by applying paper mario combat to an SRPG structure. I don't regret backing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely my favorite game since Celeste. Plays like a hybrid of the original Paper Mario/TTYD with either Into the Breach or Radiant Historia: turn-based combat with movement and timing-based abilities to choose from for the current state of the battle grid. Everything is done with only arrow keys and A/B equivalents. Unfortunate that very few player abilities (and only slightly more enemy abilities) involve forcibly moving combatants around, though. In the harder boss fights, you're practically required to use one of the characters than can heal, but aside from that and some story restrictions I appreciate the ability to mix and match your 3-man party as you please. M and G were definitely my favorites. XDSimple, evocative graphical style with a whole lot of charm to it. The sprites' nodding animation threw me off the first couple times, but that's literally the only visual quibble I have.The story really hits home in a lot of different ways. Pretty much all the characters are relatable, sympathetic, and multifaceted. Be forewarned: at some points, it gets quite dark and disturbing in some relatively abrupt and very unexpected ways. Ikenfell is not a world of sunshine and rainbows... although it does have quite a few rainbows.Absolute banger of a soundtrack, too. One of the few games I've bought the OST for instantly upon beating the game.11/10, would risk magical calamities for a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is incredibly charming and a lot of fun. The unique battle system keeps the game fresh with some decent puzzles along the way. The pixel art is a pleasure to look at and the soundtrack absolutely slaps. The story manages to be both lighthearted and deep, and there are just enough extras to keep things interesting without sidetracking the plot.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This game nails all of the feel of an old NES game but with the added benefit of decades of polish. Every attack, menu, movement, sound effect, everything adds to that polished nostalgia feel. The optional of timed attacks during a typical JRPG style combat action reminds me of Final Fantasy games of old. The soundtrack also hits all the right notes.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I paid full price for this game, and I don't regret it one bit. I am close to the end of the story, have not found all the secrets, and still have gotten over 20 hours in so far. The story is engaging, and the combat is fun and rewarding once you get the timing and strategy down. All in all, Ikenfell is a good quality indie game and worth a try for those who enjoy turn-based RPGs. It won't be everyone's cup of tea, particularly since the combat takes some trial and error in order to get used to the timing of moves, but you still just might find the story and characters as charming as I do. It's also nice to get casual LGBT+ representation in a magical setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: My game of the year. An incredibly heartfelt Super Mario RPG-like game with a ton of queer relationships that are all written extremely well, really emotive graphics (especially in the style of the game), and characters you just want to root for. The perfect salve to having to stay inside for months. ... I want to play it again. Astoundingly good.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Here's a quick Pro / Con list from what I played:Pros:Great enemy variationFun and varying abilitiesWell written characters and plotUnique level design and accompanying soundtrackOverall a feel-good gameCons:Spites feel like they could've been more detailedCombat relies on timing your attacks and defensive actions; this timing mechanic can make combat either a walk in the park, or an instant loss. HOWEVER their is an "instant-great" option so you don't have to deal with this.Overall I feel that Ikenfell is a great game, supported by it's evolving gameplay and interesting cast & story; the only thing it could've done better imo was maybe some higher detail pixel work.8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosur: I was a Kickstarter contributor for this game.After several years of sporadic updates about this game in my inbox, I was really excited to finally play it.The art is very old style pixel-y, but every character has a unique design that makes it easy to tell them apart, and every playable character has unique abilities that makes it fun to find your own favorite team composition - the only complaint I had was you're more or less forced to include either Ima or Petronella in any team configuration for the sweet sweet heals. Even so, it was neat that my husband i playing on separate save files ended up with completely different teams - I ran Gilda, Petronella and Pertisia, while he had Ima, Maritte and Rook. According to dev comments, the intention is for you to fight every mob once to be the approximate necessary level as you progress linearly. If you're struggling, a single level up will make the difference. I did find this to be very true, providing a challenging but not often tedious combat experience throughout, completing the game at around level 24 (level 25 is where the level up boosts start to decline and level 30 is the maximum.) There are enough collectable secrets and optional bosses to provide some more fun after finishing the main storyline - searching for the missed gems (rare, shiny, sparkly) and cat doors is a fun way to revisit all the games locations. The Allcat boss is a truly brutal experience - I nearly beat it at level 24 while exhausting my entire item supply but died with 40 hp to go, my husband had his level 30 team steamrolled. Running away from encounters when you're not interested in extra grinding is simple with fast run and the Run Away combat option (there is no failure to this option.)I liked the accessibility options for the QTE fight system. We both played with auto-Nice and it felt like a good balance for fairly-causual game players. We played on PC using an xbox controller (I absolutely could not figure out the keyboard controls)The music is delightful especially the final boss motif and variations. It was a very different twist including the lyrics and very refreshing. The composers were Aivi and Surrasshu of Steven Universe fame.I personally loved the inclusivity of the characters - I have many loved ones who are LGBTQ, and I'm always trying to do better to make sure I use correct pronouns and this game was actually a great way to practice using pronouns I may not use as commonly as others. I played this game with my 3.5 yr old son at my side, so I was reading the dialogue (and doing voices, naturally) and it makes me happy that there is media like this that helps him experience a wider world than I did at his age. On the same topic, the relationships and messages of this game are more of the stuff I like to see and share with my child - love of all different shapes and sizes, including loving and being kind to yourself. I have to admit I teared up at the end - Aeldra's story hits home, and the relationship between Bax and Ibn  also ended up being much more powerful than I expected from their goofy start! Due to corona virus we are homeschooling and it just happened that one of our homeschooling themes the week we finished this game was the emotion "heartbroken" so I was pleased to tie in the concept of how different characters being "heartbroken", why, and how it affected their friends and people around them.This is a fairly short game, we both have around 40-50 hrs on our saves, and that's with taking our time and exploring plenty (not to mention getting lost as hell in the Stacks, which let me tell you, is exactly as creepy and spooky as it needs to be, yeeeeesh.)All in all, a lovely little game, a delightful diversion and very wholesome.If you're the kind of sensitive person who reacts with fear to non-binary pronouns, cute gays, and feels your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clench whenever you conjure the specter of "PC Culture" you should definitely avoid this game until you can toughen up your delicate, fragile heart.As for me, I really hope this game will become popular enough for DLC! I also really hope that the Game Grumps play it! I think they'd love this game and I'd love to hear their take on the character voices!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful, heartfelt modern take on classic Japanese RPGs. Amazing pixel art, animation and soundtrack, lovable and diverse cast of characters. Also, cats. The game will take around 15 to 20 hours to beat. The battle system is fun and interesting, but if it's not your thing there are ways to ignore that part of the game. The story on it own is well worth it the journey. Highly recommend. :)(for full disclosure: I got the game as a reward from backing its crowdfunding campaign at the time)
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game overall 8.5/10.  Challenging fight mechanic with pattern-based real-time elements.  I didn't use everyone super heavily, but all the characters have interesting move sets to choose from.  Some of the puzzles were a little easy, and the story could use a tweak or two, but all minor stuff really.  The best part is the diverse music score; that really seals the deal for me personally.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: A cute pixel RPG with a clever little battle system. It's easy on my 10-year old iMac too, the fans don't whirr when I play this. I like the inclusion of several queer characters. I like that the save points are cats. Difficulty level/complexity is good for kids, or for an adult looking for a sweet breezy game. It'd be nice if it was on mobile so I could play it on the go. I like all the little secrets, like hidden paths and rare gems to find. I don't like that I cannot quickly exit to my desktop, I wish I could just hit ESC and quit. The battle system includes this time-based aspect I like, that keeps me engaged, makes me feel I'm more in control.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little tactical turn-based RPG with surprising depth and a heck of a lot of charm. Don't go into this expecting XCOM levels of complexity, but I had a great time figuring out how to best position my party based on the targeting range of their spells. The battles also have a timing-based element during attacking and defending, much like the Mario RPG franchise. That adds a nice layer of immediacy to the battles. The quality of life features are welcome, too and prove that the developer loves classic RPGs but knows they can be better. The characters are well-rounded and the story is snappy and twisty enough to keep me interested. Definitely pick this up if you're a fan of old-school JRPGs with modern touches.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Summary: A charming game with fun characters and an enjoyable story, but not the most engaging gameplay.Graphics: 10/10. Charming, colorful, and fun! The graphics team got basically everything right with this game.Music: 9/10. The songs are catchy and enjoyable; it's not quite up there with Bastion in terms of music, but it's still great.Sound Effects: 7/10. Competent, most of the ambient sounds didn't really stand out much. There's only one sound effect in the game that I specifically dislike, that being the one associated with one of the characters' buff spells.Overall Story: 8/10. I'll give this one points for doing something extremely unique for RPG games, although I don't want to spoil things. The story seems to take cues from Harry Potter on the surface, but it quickly becomes clear that it's its own thing with its own world and characters. The Harry Potter comparisons are mostly just little Easter Eggs, and a tool to help set up your expectations in a certain way.Character Interactions: 10/10. The characters feel realistic, including their faults, and they play off each-other extremely well.Gameplay (Combat): 5/10. This is where I have to hit the game a bit hard. While the gameplay had a lot of good ideas, the execution is a bit lacking. While the developers tried to implement something similar to the action commands in the Mario RPG games, they made the mistake of making a lot of the attack sequences overly complex, and including too many enemies per battle. Both of those together result in the battles being extremely slow-paced. Additionally, while the attempt to balance a battle system without any MP meter was pretty interesting, it takes away a lot of the actual decision-making, resulting in battles often boiling down to timing the action commands and little else. The equipment in the game is pretty generic; it's mostly just collections of stat boosts. While there are a small number of gear pieces with special effects, they're all acquired from a single shop, and have no stat-boosts of their own. As a result, those pieces of gear tends to feel like they're not worth it compared to the stats you're losing out on.As a quick side-note, the developers seem to be at least somewhat aware of these issues, and have added options within the settings to skip over battles entirely.Gameplay (Exploration): 7/10. On a bit of a higher note, exploring Ikenfell itself was quite fun. The puzzles added into the exploration weren't anything special, but they were solid and charming. Overall thoughts: 8/10. Despite the lacking combat mechanics, I still enjoyed playing Ikenfell, and would very much recommend it if you're interested in the story! It's not quite a masterpiece, but it has a vibrant world and charming characters. I'm currently very much looking forward to seeing what Happy Ray makes next!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is a very cool game about witches trying to figure out the misteries of the Magic School they are in. The game features really cool pixelart, incredible music, engaging combat and a heartfelt story.The game is also very accessible, with differing difficulty options and even trigger warnings. The cast is some of the most diverse Ive ever seen, and while it can be a bit jarring for some, it is a welcome addition in the effort to normalize treating others with respect.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been made with love, and it shows.A cute and relatable story with some great fighting mechanics, many characters you want to protect at all costs, and a beautiful music work. This game also makes an excellent job at being one of the most inclusive games I've seen in decades in so many ways, and at exposing a lot of personal social issues we are experiencing in our daily lives but that we often keep to ourselves. It's a game about understanding yourself and learning to love yourself.Ikenfell is definitely going in my favorite indie games list, and I will keep warm and strong memories of it. I am sure gonna miss all the wonderful people of this world.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun JRPG. The combat requires a bit more strategy than many other JRPGs which means that it doesn't get boring and grindy, which can sometimes be an issue with JRPGs for me. The timing mechanic really required me to be on my toes which was fun -- but it can be turned off with no penalty which I did a few times when I just wanted to relax. The story was engaging and the characters were interesting, and the music was really good. I played through the story in just over 20 hours. Totally recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Kickstarted this game several years ago, glad that it finally came out. I've quite enjoyed it so far.Pro:- A solid homage to colorful, 16-bit JRPG, if that's what you're looking for.- Story is sincere without being too saccharine.- Excellent soundtrack. A nice blend of knowing when to chiptune and when to not.- Good variety of environments and unique visual design for each.- Pretty good pacing - each environment feels like it has room to breathe, but doesn't overstay its welcome. - Environmental puzzles are kinda RPG-standard, but they give a good bit of variety.Con:- Combat can be a bit simple. Small battlefield, most of the time positioning is a minor consideration. There's no elemental considerations, so spell choice is typically just "what has the most appropriate targeting area, AoE, or does the most damage".- The hit-timer mechanic, while it does add some juice to combat, can be pretty strict about giving a 'great', and can be pretty punishing if you screw up a few turns in a row. I've found it a bit easier with controller instead of keyboard.- Minor balance considerations. There were some ranges of levels where it felt like some party members carried while others couldn't really contribute - particularly, the more support-oriented characters.- There's a surprisingly large wardrobe of equipment, but it pretty much boils down to "Am I focusing this character on defense or offense"?note: The game has accessibility options to disable the hit-timer mechanic, or to bypass combat altogether.if you're looking for a fun bit of entertainment, I'd recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell is an RPG that has nothing new, but that has an amazing combination of elements. Game mechanics are fun, with a system that rewards a good timing to get the most of th juice in your spells, but also punish you if you fail. Developers added options to make gameplay easier if you want, but I had no issues finishing the game without help. Itemization is quite important, since it really impacts the final stats of each character. It was fun to have a glass cannon, a tanky healer and a versatile rogue in the party.Storywise, the game has a lot to offer, it is a linear story, nothing complicated, but it feels fresh and deep enough. After finishing one part you want to know more and more.Soundtrack is amazing, with some vocals in parts where the game wants to focus, making some parts really touching (it seems is raining again).In resume, if you like old-school RPG, this is your game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little indie RPG thats all about wizards and witches having feelings. It blends its lore within the game excellently and you really get to feel for the main character. The few issues I had were mainly that I feel that the original party members start falling off into the background as far as development goes, and that while the lyrical songs were nice, I think having more of them would have been much better.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game It's basically paper mario meets a stradegy rpg. Now before going into this there are lots of gay refrences here and there sprinkled in so if you're not into that it will probebly be a turn off for you. Pass all that what you have here is a decent rpg with a timed battle system much like as i mentioned above paper mario. However you have to be really good at these as the timing for most of the attacks at best require seconds after the animations about to finish.This doesn't becoming a problem later on however as it's pretty easy to tell with a lot of the attacks having visual aids when to press the button and i've noticed no delay in do so. You can also set it in the options to do it auto or semi autoYou can do everything this game has to offer in one run which will last around 25 - 28 hours. All of the side stuff requires you to find everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: All the best parts of Super Mario RPG in a TBS game that can appeal to all kinds of players. The option to instant win the mob encounters takes away the slog and keeps the story going. Something about young adults solving a mystery at a magic academy will always be an endearing story. Ikenfell has a lot of heart, and I found myself coming back to play every day without realizing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I backed the game and at first the story seems to be very cheesy, but it gets better and you start getting invested into it. the same goes with the fights, which start very low, but the timing concept feels very rewarding. there are some game design decision, when changed would improve the game  a lot, but you can ignore them after a while. the game is actually more console driven, but is not a real breaker. all in all, I can recommend it, when you are into a different version of harry potter final fantasy based game
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: A charming turn based tactical RPG with a great story, wonderful characters you'll love and a fantastical world to discover. I'm still playing but I've been really taken aback by this game. Keep in mind that I actively dislike a low pixel sprite art style; despite going for an aesthetic I really don't like, Ikenfell won me over. It looks spectacular: this is a world I've been getting lost in since I picked the game up, and am sure I will continue to for a while to come. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely lovely game. I originally really wanted to play it because of the magic school setting and I was unsure if I would like the battle system, but it turned out to be fun and easily adaptable for my playstyle.The game has a lot of accessibility options, I turned on the photosensitivity mode immediately cause I get headaches easily. I also used the auto-timing mode, as I found the timing based stuff to be a bit frustrating. Towards the end, I occasionally used the instant victory option, because I was getting a bit fatigued with the battles, but so sucked into the story that I didn't want to quit the game. I'm a very story-focused player and not used to turn-based combat and I thought it was nice that there was an option for players like me.I really enjoyed the mystery elements in the story and finding out bit by bit what happened in Ikenfell and why Safina went missing. It just makes the whole framing of the story so engaging and I really wanted to find out what happens next.I also really enjoyed the character writing. I ended up caring a lot about the main cast. Every issue they were going through seemed so tangible and real and in the end I was empathising with all of them.Also being able to pet cats in the game made me irrationally happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Played it. Loved it. Wrote a guide for how to beat one of the bosses in it. It's wonderful. Very fun combat, very tricky if you want it to be, but can be made far easier in the options, to the point where you can have the game just win you a fight for free if it's really giving you trouble. Very paper mario-esk combat too, with timing giving you better damage, but again, you can have the game fix the odds for you so you always ace it, or art least never get a bad outcome.I like it's sense of humour, and I like it's more serious side as well. Not many games can pull off both. The game has an option to have content warnings before traumatic scenes, which I had turned on before I got very far. I recommend having it on regardless of whether you personally need it, because it can help explain the subtext behind certain scenes.It's got a lot of LGBT representation, with many gay, bi and lesbian characters. There are even a few straights, as a treat! How novel!It's got collectables, if you're that 100%'er type of player. Several types of gem scattered hither and thither that can be traded in for strong (ish) items. You don't need to go crazy looking for them though; you'll find enough to get by if you just pick up the odd shiny here and there.All in all, good fun and well worth the asking price!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful, with an amazing soundtrack! And while I love how gay the story is, it really looses its character focus as the story goes on. Gilda kinda just exists after a certain point as a hype man and Ima just gets some moments out of nowhere. The character arcs felt a little all over the place. I enjoyed a lot of the puzzles except for the Twilight Courtyard and Archive puzzles, which could have been clarified more, the game sometimes needs to be a bit more clear about where things are. Combat was probably the weakest part of the game, if it weren't for the win button I would avoid every single fight. Some boss fights are extremely long (such as the final boss fight with 6 FORMS) the timing just doesn't feel right for a lot of attacks and defending moves, its sometimes really hard to get "greats" unless you play around with it a lot. I'm very mixed on the final product but when it's good it's good.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. A mixture of the quirkiness of undertale, the semi-precise timing of Paper Mario and lots of fun, if a bit stereotypical, characters. The battles are a bit tougher than you might think, but they very generous healing cats help balance that out. A bit stale until you unlock a few characters, but once you fill in the roster a bit, you will have a pretty wide variety of attacks and defenses that add a much needed spice to the overall game. Have not finished, but the story so far is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: So far I've played two hours and reached chapter 2, and fittingly I have two thoughts on this game so far. First is that I'm having fun. I'm a fan of pixel art and this game does it well, the music is very fun and the battles are fun. I grew up playing the mario and luigi games so the times button presses add both skill to combat. My second thought is that I think I know who the villian is already. The story has been good thus far but I think it's been going heavy on the foreshadowing. So far, even from my brief playing of the game I'd still recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game, even though i found most of the fights towards the end of the game a bit too easy (though there are secret bosses to make up for it). The combat system is easy to learn, if you've ever played any (Paper) Mario RPG and even though the game itself is linear, there are enough secrets to discover (i'm not fully done, yet).Some skills feature brief screen flashes, which may cause issues for some people, but the game features an option to (i guess) disable them. I didn't try it out, because i don't have a problem with flashes, but that could be something to keep in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Fluffy game with a fairly unique story. Has some music from the guys who did Steven Universe and there are a couple parts where it makes the scene. Gilda is my favorite boss so far, with the adorable kitten being a close second.Tips: (Marked as spoilers, but these don't spoil story, promise.)Timing System:Astronomy Tower:

_childDocuments_.review: characters are cute!!!! combat is fun!!! kitties are save points!!edit: now that i've finished the game and played through most of its extra content, i guess i'll write an actual spoiler free review. normally i'm not one to talk about things like "pacing," since most of the time i have no idea what that means, but for this game especially the story has pacing problems. the real meat of it doesn't really kick in until about 8 hours of gameplay, so you really have to like the combat and the characters in order to make it that far. a major story detail is revealed and then immediately subverted within like three lines of dialogue, which i wasn't a huge fan of. sometimes story beats feels contrived and treated like a big deal even though they barely come up again. some things seem arbitrarily put into the game just for the sake of making it longer, especially in the first eight hours.none of the character writing is groundbreaking persay, but it has a lot of heart put into it.. my favorite is gilda (which seems to be a popular opinion).in the latter quarter of the game, the pattern seems to be 1) enter new area, 2) fight through encounters, 3) beat a boss, 4) find out new information telling you to go to another place, 5) repeat. if the story isn't engaging you and you don't like the combat, then it gets dry really quickly.in terms of combat, you can probably find more detailed reviews on it by people far more knowledgable about game design than i. i had fun with strategizing which characters to take into which battles, and timing defense and attacks has the right amount of difficulty. sometimes the animations for attacks really slow down combat, and the music can be jarring.all of the above being said? i really like this game. i think the combat is super fun. when the story did kick in, i was interested in seeing how it would unfold. i'm a fan of the soundtrack (though some lyrics in paint the future kinda pulled me out of the immersion because it alluded to real world events). lgbt cast, pretty art, and there are still kitties! i do realize this review sounded mostly negative but i hope seeing my 30 ish hours in this game is a testament in of itself. i would personally wait for a sale to snag this game, but i promise that if youre a sucker for lgbt shenanigans, character development, and an engaging story with fun combat, you'll have fun with this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: (will hopefully update once I beat the game, but indies need reviews for exposure!)Ikenfell is a very, very pretty game. It doesn't put its best foot forward, though: the beginning is both too hard and too slow, and for a moment I thought it'd be another bad western developed game imitating the JRPG aesthetic. Push through that, because once you get to a full party the game owns.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first time I felt such a strong need to write a review :DIkenfell is just an enjoyable experience in all the ways, has cute retro visuals, fun gameplay, amazing (as always) music by aivi & surasshu and a pretty interesting story (even if the dialogue mentions "weird magic" definitely way too often ;p).A nice feature that while I haven't used so far, but is very good to see is being able to simplify timing for attacks to personal needs/preferences, letting more people enjoy the game without having to worry :DUltimately, if you like this kind of retro rpgs, you're going to have a great time ;)P.S.: I almost forgot to mention, you pet cats to save the game OwO - instant 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to wait a bit longer before writing a review for this game, but honestly it's great and deserves all the attention it can get. Obvious Harry Potter influences aside, the narrative in Ikenfell is genuinely interesting and has a great hook to draw the player in. The music so far is fantastic, and the characters are memorable. Even though I only played an hour yesterday I keep looking forward to getting to play more.The battle system is finicky, and I'm still too early to really be able to draw conclusions on it. I've heard that speed is probably the strongest stat in the game in terms of actually being able to act in battle, but also there are accessibility options that can help if you are having trouble. From what I've played it's great, but these are just things I've heard.Honestly I think this game's quality is high enough to warrant a higher price tag, so getting it at the launch price of $17.99 USD is a steal. If the game remotely intrigues you, or you like RPG's I definitely recommend getting this game. It's well made and has a lot of charm.
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: Ikenfell takes a little bit to ramp up, especially to some of the more powerful party members you'll get later on, but it definitely is a cute and fun quirky game. There's plenty of little offshoots to grab hidden collectibles (some really cleverly hidden that reward you looking around) and it feels great when you get the timing down on some of your favorite moves. I'm excited to continue forward to find new party members and interesting boss fight mechanics for quite a few hours more. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ikenfell

_childDocuments_.review: A turn-based tactical RPG about a group of troublesome magic students. Use timing mechanics to power your spells and block attacks, explore the twisted halls of a vast magic school, fight challenging monsters and bosses, and uncover dark secrets never meant to be found.

name: Paranoia: Happiness is Mandatory
detailed_description: Paranoia is a CRPG that takes place in humanity's last idyllic refuge, Alpha Complex, which is controlled by Friend Computer. All citizens enjoy a life of joy, cheerfulness and cleanliness. Questioning the benevolence of Friend Computer is an act of treason. Having access to information beyond your security clearance is an act of treason. Refusing to drink your daily dose of Bouncy Bubble Beverage is an act of treason. Treason is punishable by summary execution. Stay alert! Trust no one! Traitors are everywhere, plotting to destroy The Computer, Alpha Complex itself, and our precious way of life. Identify them, report them – or eliminate them as the treasonous scum they are. Keep your laser handy! You lead a team of Troubleshooters with RED security clearance. Your job is to find trouble – and shoot it. Friend Computer monitors your every move, alert for any sign of treason, and will undoubtedly reward you for prompt and heroic action in defence of Alpha Complex – or punish treasonable acts, possibly by assigning you to be used as reactor shielding. A retro-futuristic world filled with technologies as wondrous as they are deadly Create and lead a team of four Troubleshooters working for Friend Computer Choose your specialisations from 9 available skills Unique character progression through cloning (if you die, you progress!) Real time tactical combat system with active pause, inspired by classic CRPG games Original enemies, including malfunctioning robots, aggressive drinks dispensers and defective clones

_childDocuments_.review: Settings menu offers only 2 low resolutions. If you keep any dropdown open in the settings you will be unable to leave the page. One of the player character animations failed to start along with the robot it needed to sync up with. This was all before I had gotten out of the tutorial.I think this game could be a fun one at 5EUR at some later point in time, but it feels barely complete as it stands.The world deserves a great PARANOIA game, but this isn't it. Which is sort of sad, as the game clearly has a lot of time and effort put into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paranoia: Happiness is Mandatory

_childDocuments_.review: So after all this time this game finally came out and honestly, it sucks.  I played about an hour of it, being a fan of Paranoia RPG, and this thing is just boring.  The music is very bland, the characters look cheap and have no real variety in appearance, the combat is sub par with poor AI for the player characters, and it just isn't fun at all to play.  I refunded the game.  If this is the kind of junk Nacon has to steal to make money, they have really low standards.  I will not purchase anything by Nacon again as they are known thieves in the industry.  Really, just avoid this game.  It is not worth the price so save your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Paranoia: Happiness is Mandatory

_childDocuments_.review: They massacred my boy.You'd think three years of litigation would have been ample opportunity to fix things. The project feels barebones. My character did not seem to have a sitting animation for the insertion of the cerebral coretech so he stood there while the robot and furniture clipped through him. This is within 5 minutes of starting the game.Let's back up. Paranoia: Happiness is Mandatory appeared for a glorious month as an epic game store exclusive before promptly vanishing in a storm of legal filings. The developers were unhappy because the distributor published a blatantly unfinished product, the rights holders were unhappy because it was a blatantly unfinished product. Suddenly, without warning, it appears on Steam. I bought it not wanting it to vanish just as quickly and with the vain hope that maybe they'd fixed it.It does not appear that they have.The Alpha Complex of the game is bright and colorful. The aesthetic is right. But it feels empty. The partial voice acting really drives home how incomplete the game feels. It's missing several features that were standard to the kind of game it's trying to be: holding tab to highlight interactable objects, being able to save anywhere and run multiple saves etc. Combat is dull. You point and click. There doesn't seem to be any point to cover as it hinders you as much as the opposition. It's a game of attrition: Who will run out of HP first?An isometric CRPG is also just the worst possible choice for Paranoia. I'm a huge fan of the Paranoia TTRPG. More than most, it relies on player interactions and fast-paced hijinks. Paranoia would have made a great basis for a zany arena shooter. It's just not good for a CRPG. It also doesn't give you the obvious options. In the tutorial your team leader hands you a mini and tells you to hide in your safe storage. Why are you not able to immediately go and report him for this clear contraband? And worst of all? The game's boring. The music is lifeless. The combat is dull. The jokes need life support. It's appalling for a TTRPG that frequently tells you to 'Entertain or Die.' Because it's a single player RPG you're also kinda stuck playing in a boring manner. I pick boring dialog options because I don't want treason points. I can't be funny. It's a comedy game that actively steers you away from the funny! Make it make sense.It hurts because it's not like the developers didn't care. There is some genuine love that bleeds through in what was released and it's a shame they don't seem to have been able to massage this in to something playable.Update:Got in to the second mission. The hacking minigame is absurd. There is essentially a zero-tolerance for any mistakes making it nearly impossible to pull off. The worst is if you die. It takes you back to the tutorial room, where the game begins. It doesn't make you replay the tutorial but getting back to the mission is going to take several minutes as you have to manually run back to the location site. This is something the TTRPG solves handily. New clones are deposited with the party pretty quickly after the old one falls. You have to keep things moving. And I just can't. I think I'm going to request a refund. Maybe I'll buy the game again if it goes on sale for $5 but it is simply not worth its current asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Paranoia: Happiness is Mandatory

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not certain if it's a release issue, but the textures in game are aggressively low textured, even on the "ultra" settings. I'm not certain if it's a bug, or just as normal.That's the stuff I'm not certain on. The rest...Combat is automatic. There's no cover system outside of just line of sight and your team mates are just as likely to shoot the box they're hiding behind as well as the thing attacking them. The only mission I did, I literally just walked through it, mind.  There's a bunch of Animation breaks, and you can walk through static objects. The forced camera angle means doors are impossible to spot. Out of dialog chat messages are obnoxiously large, and can appear off screen meaning you miss "important" updates. And while there's certainly an effort to the setting and tone of the game's setting, the rest of the game seems to be an afterthought.It's a shame, given the hell that this has gone through since it's release, and I knew going in it wasn't going to be a stellar outing. But I think after about an hour, I don't think I need continue. Happiness might be Mandatory, but clearly it's not to be found here. Sorry guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Paranoia: Happiness is Mandatory

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I had fun with this. I went in with really low expectations after knowing it got shut down years ago, hearing that there were bad bugs, hearing it was a poor game from when people originally played it, and just knowing that Paranoia is not overly popular as a TTRPG. If you're a big time Paranoia fan, I do recommend giving it a try. My playthrough took a total of 9 and a half hours to beat the game in its entirety, and that was on top of doing any optional objectives I was presented as well. So, it may be worth waiting for a sale just because the shortness of the game may not feel worth the price. During my playthrough, I only experienced one major bug, where I was told to report to Friend Computer for debriefing and when arriving, the debriefing wouldn't start and I was unable to continue the mission. I was able to fix the bug by self terminating at a termination booth, which sucked because it meant losing a clone, but I was doing well enough in the game and was able to purchase extra clones that it didn't bother me too much. One thing that did turn me off a bit was towards the end it became mostly long missions of going room to room dealing with combat after combat. It reminded me of playing Vampire: the Masquerade - Bloodlines, where the developers were rushed towards the end and so just made a bunch of combat to extend time and wrap the game up. That being said, I went in with low expectations and was surprised at the amount of personality and interactions your teammates are given within missions. Where bringing certain teammates can activate unique interactions and even side missions. I'm considering another playthrough to switch around which teammates I bring along to see what I may have missed. As far I noticed, I only saw two secret societies you can join within my playthrough, unless joining a secret society locks you out of seeing more, as I joined the second one that asked me. I didn't find the two that I saw overly exciting, but it was cool that they approached me for a mission along with the members of the secret society and being part of them unlocked a unique ending.Tl;dr - while a rather short game that could definitely use a lot more, was pleasantly surprised and enjoyed it. Buy on sale if you're interested and like Paranoia.
_childDocuments_.name: Paranoia: Happiness is Mandatory

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth $30 USD in this state.I finished this game.It's pretty buggy and some of the bugs are really frustrating.  I ran into one several times were the game somehow forgot what crafting options are supposed to be available and I could only craft the very low tier gear most of the time.   Because of it's checkered past, I doubt any patches are forthcoming.The opening was good.  Some youtuber playing the first mission is what got me interested in the first place.The mid game section  was mostly just a big tedious dungeon crawl.  It's bad.  A lot of the core things that make the setting good are just totally absent here.  The system of infractions, backstabbing NPCs, vending machines, and experimental gadgets and all that.  It's just go from room to room and shoot things.  The combat system just isn't really the game's strength.The last mission was better, but not super great.  It's another shoot-em up but there's some more amusing bits and it's not as massively long as the mid game was and some of game's flavor returned.The endgame, in terms of gameplay, was terrible.  Just completely terrible.  There's a super easy one  but the rest are total BS.  You go into the computer in a sort of tron like virtual reality and you have to do this big puzzle fight.  It's easy enough to cheese to a large degree, but even doing that there's still a metric tonne of RNG to deal with here and it's very easy to lose through no fault of your own.  Repeatedly.Once you finish this big BS combat puzzle, you're presented with a set of options that determine what ending you get.  Some will only be available if you joined the right secret society or whatever.The ending cinematics were amusing though.  The text is so dang fast it's hard to read it all.As far as I can tell, there's 5 or maybe 6 endings.  Possibly a few more.Overall, I would say it's a C-.  Potentially a B- if they ever do fix some of the bugs.  I really don't think it's worth the current asking price.  Maybe $10 USD would be fair in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: The  treason of the tabletop was short and punchy allowing for everyone at the table to laugh. This is all snapped away when you find out how limited you are on clones. Being punished for things outside of your control no longer makes you laugh but makes you want to go "Why? This isn't funny. This is just mean/unfair." Case in point when  You are punished for 13 points of treason at the mission debriefing cause  . If you argue that is unfair, you punished with more treason (which IS in line with the humor/theme of Paranoia but the amount is just mean). I laughed as my clone yelled FREEDOM before being zapped on the spot. One screen later, I see a clone count and all that "I can do silly treason things for fun" went right out the window. Now the game changes into  instead of The UI's font/size/tootips are all lackluster as the font is too small. There is a lot of unused UI space that could allow for easier to read font/size. Right-clicking items doesn't always brings up a menu in the inventory menu. No Map (Only mini-map). No UI resize. Limited screen sizes. No Borderless Window.The hacking mini-game is...  Limited by time, you have to swiftly click the letter when it appears in the box at the right time. If it passes by you have to wait till it comes around, costing you more time. Sound is alright, nothing to really write much about. My only complaint is that all audio stops when the game is defocused. Which feels very archaic and out of place with modern game streaming.Over all, I feel very disappointed in a game that could be very fun and funny that punishes you for the very reason it is fun and funny. The substandard UI, setting, and lack of gaming standards is just saddening. I will be waiting for patches to help clean up this game before I return to it.

_childDocuments_.review: The core of the Paranoia experience is there, but the presentation is very bland. I'd say it would be acceptable if you buy it on sale but I experienced a game breaking bug that has stopped me playing so I cannot recommend:I was doing a mission and used a terminal to open a door. Because this game doesn't allow multiple saves I have no way to load back to before the bug so I'd have to start all over again.I don't recommend buying this in its current buggy state.

_childDocuments_.review: Stop whining. Happiness is Mandatory! _childDocuments_.review: Paranoia is one of my favorite games and I was excited to see a CRPG version, even if only single-player.I gave this a thumbs-up mainly for that.  If you are, like me, a super fan of the game.. pick it up and enjoy.   If not, but a fan of isometric CRPG, wait for a sale.  Otherwise, don't waste your money.The initial mission is from the quick-start and matched exactly as I remember it.However, HareBrained Schemes released ShadowRun Returns in 2012, a CRPG adaption that set the bar for isometric game play and character interaction. In comparison to that decade old game, this one looks to be a quick cash grab.Game play isn't horrible, I did the best Troubleshooter approach and didn't use any tutorials.There is no voice acting, lots of 'continue' bar on the narration, and each clone is a completely new character. {reskill, new mutant ability, etc..}, very little in the way of communication options { only one mission in...} , and treasonous people just hanging out in the cafe.What is horrible, your clone is decanted in the same place with the same non-skippable cut-scene ..*and you have to walk back to the mission after re-equiping*Also, you are recanted in /shudder/ a white jumpsuit.At least the marketing is spot on. This is the first official adaptation of the cult-classic, not a faithful adaptation.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game... I have been waiting for sooo long and I'm happy with the outcome. I love seeing the TTRPG in game form. Alpha Complex looks amazing and seeing Friend Computer realized in game is great. Cant wait to get back to playing the TTRPG with my friends after I'm done being a good citizen.
_childDocuments_.name: Paranoia: Happiness is Mandatory

_childDocuments_.review: I have 100's of hours on this game in the EPIC version.I have a long history with PARANOIA in both the TTRPG format as well as this game, when it was previously released.This game went through a legal gauntlet years ago and was only made available for a very brief period of time. Since this was taking place while I was actively playing, I tried contacting the developers, publisher, original creators of the TTRPG, and basically anyone that had something to do with the game. They all, essentially, said they were under NDA.I love it. If you have familiarity with the TTRPG then you understand the "every choice is the wrong choice" concept behind the design. The game is meant to be narrative driven and humorous. Still, I recommend it for the good time factor alone. It's a feels good title that has a LOT of scenarios that are conditional on dialogue decisions.Do not expect Baldur's Gate 3. Remember, this game  came out YEARS ago.That being said... This game has a lot going on under the hood in terms of mechanics and routing. A lot of items have useful interactions with other items and if you bring certain items/teammates/skill points with you then you will encounter a lot of different situations because of it.All in all, I feel like the length of the game, amount of dialogue, and it's infamous history make it a really intriguing title to add to your library - especially if it disappears again!

_childDocuments_.review: Lead a team of four Troubleshooters of dubious loyalty, who (mostly) obey orders from Friend Computer, a paranoid and irrational artificial intelligence. Inspired by the classic games of the CRPG genre, experience the first official adaptation of the cult role-playing game.

name: Tribes of Midgard
detailed_description: ULTIMATE EDITION CONTENT JOIN OUR DISCORD About the Game Join the celebrations for Tribes of Midgard's 3 Year Anniversary with a new Festive Event! The Valhalla Menu, the Sanctuary, the Village, and even the Goblins will be showing off their festive spirit. From June 27th to July 18th, enjoy the themed Main Menu music, complete 3 weekly challenges, and claim the adorable Sóleyra and Mániklo cat portraits. Gear up, journey across Midgard (and beyond!) in this epic Survival ARPG adventure. Build, craft, explore, and fight creatures of legend to discover the secrets of the Sanctuary stones. Valhalla awaits, Einherjar! Save The Day, Your Way: Travel across procedurally generated worlds to harvest resources, gather loot, craft powerful Weapons, level up, and chase chickens in the most colorful Ragnarök you’ve ever seen! Survival Mode: Explore at your own pace and build your perfect Viking home! Choose among 90 skills as you progress and fight your way through towering Jötnar until you can face off against the all-powerful Ancients. Discover what awaits you at the end of your epic journey.  Saga Mode: Challenge yourself in this fast-paced adventure to face the forces of Ragnarök before the endless winter. Unlock and specialize among 8 Classes to defend your Village for as long as you can. The greater the feat, the greater the reward when you take the Bifröst! Face Colossal Threats: The bigger they are, the harder they’ll fall! And trust us—they’re pretty big!   Descending from Valhalla, your Einherjar starts with nothing but a loincloth and a save the world attitude. Stand against the ever-looming threat of the gigantic Jötnar, and the even more threatening Ancients that command them. Unleash mighty Spells contained within your Weapons, block incoming attacks with your trusty Shield, and time your evades in this action-packed gameplay against these screen-filling baddies! Forge Your Viking Legend: You are in control of your own destiny, Einherjar! Create unique character builds by leveling up and choosing game-changing abilities from the Norse gods. Hunt rare resources and loot powerful Runes that will modify your playstyle in surprising ways. Complete in-game events, sail boats across the oceans, take on NPC quests, and raid dungeons to grow your legend further! Or simply fish! Not only are you up for the challenge, this is what you were chosen to do. Rally The Tribe: You don’t have to do it alone, save some glory for the rest of us! Adventure solo or form a tribe of up to 10 players in online PvE co-op. Play together to build a functioning village, complete with formidable defenses, towering structures and top-of-the-line crafting stations! Or just an aesthetically pleasing Viking homestead with some well-earned decorations! The game difficulty adapts to the amount of players in a world. Note that we recommend taking on Ragnarök with a tribe of four or more. Keep Up the Fight: Never has the end of the world been so bright and fun! Continuous free updates and limited time Festive Events bring even mightier treasures to the endgame. Play to accumulate Golden Horns and redeem them to unlock a myriad of recipes, including Starter Kits, Runes and Equipment, to make each new session more rewarding. Progress through Valhalla Levels and complete hundreds of challenges for even more. Make each saga your own by wearing your best costumes and bringing your cutest pets along!

_childDocuments_.review: "The Giants are coming! Form a tribe with up to 10 players to defend your village from the relentless onslaught of deadly spirits and gigantic brutes hel-bent on bringing on the end of the world in this game with a unique blend of action, survival, and roguelite elements."Tribes of Midgard comes across as decent and appears to tick all the boxes. It sets out to incorporate elements of a survival roguelite game with the semblance of tower defense mechanics.But ultimately at its core lies a plain, unsatisfying gameplay loop that DOESN'T warrant the grinding involved in completing any of the modes, which is further exacerbated when attempting to play the game solo.---------------THE GOOD---------------- The art style is decent and brings a charming vibe to the game.- The sound track is not bad.- Playing with friends can be fun. Voice chat and coordination rewards teamwork, and all of you grouping together to take down a tough foe is often a swell time.- The controls are fairly responsive, none of that janky hitbox issues that some games have (I tried controller and KB+M, ultimately went with KB+M but controller works well).- The game is fast paced due to the day-night cycle that constantly pushes you to do something before night falls.- The periodic arrivals of Jotunns (with different elements) helps to inject a change of pace into the tedium of the grind for resources.- The game is challenging enough that a run ending is always a possibility, which is what you'd like to see in a roguelite.- There are a few biomes (e.g. snow, fire) that offer some variety in terrain.--------------THE BAD--------------- Online lobby experience leaves a lot to be desired. There's very little teamwork, so it plays more as solo-play with an easier traverse of the map.- The map generation, while procedural, is by all measures a broadly similar experience with very little variety and poor use of verticality.- Awkward placement of ramps to engage with the vertical elements also meant my character might just get blocked by my own ramp.- The soundtrack gets repetitive quite easily - there's limited variety that's easily exhausted within ONE run.- As a roguelite, it completely neglects the notion of player progression after a run ends. Every run you begin as the same basic -- weak -- character and you go through the tedium of trying to progress to the point where you have the necessary equipment to engage with the world proper.-- The 'rewards' from each run are purely cosmetic and there's an absurd 'freenium' cash shop inside with a season pass that's more cosmetic rewards. If the publishers wanted to run with the freemium model, they shouldn't have made this a paid game.- The classes feel severely gimped due to the horrible implementation of durability. It's basically divided into playing as the 'Warden' (no durability issues) and every other class. There's little reason as to why you'd choose a different class from a quality of life perspective, as the trade off from being shoehorned into a gimped durability experience is too great.- The enemy variety is lacking. Once you've seen the same few enemies from your first 1-2 runs, you've seen everything the game has to offer.- The bosses are basically meatsinks where you just wail on them with your weapons and dodge the odd attack. There's very little skill involved and you don't feel like you 'grow' as a player. The mechanics are trivial.- While I don't advocate handholding in games, the game does a poor job from its short tutorial at telling you what you need to be doing in game, and the in-game hints are sorely lacking. You need to constantly refer to the journal and/or internet posts to make sense of where you should find the material you need to make a particular item. In that sense, the experience and/or immersion is marred by the constant disconnect at trying to figure out what you should be doing next.- The experience is fairly standard across runs. There's little to distinguish one run from the next once you've experienced a complete run (EDIT: which IS possible on solo, just extremely painful), and as a result there's no real reason from a gameplay point of view to replay the game, past a certain point.- Considering how the core gameplay loop is to grind for resources and essentially to tick off a list of chores (e.g. getting the right armour sets before temperature becomes a problem), the lack of variety in game means that the overall experience leaves much to be desired in terms of functioning as a roguelite.-- I will concede that I would consider going on to play with my friends if they were on, but I think that's more of for playing  game with friends rather than playing  game with friends.- The runs are surprisingly LENGTHY (2-3 hours) despite the pace of the game, which makes coordinating a multiplayer game troublesome (contrary to many other roguelites). It's true that the roguelite/roguelike genre has had roguelikes* with considerable run times, but those incorporated an ironman save feature -- one autosave that can be loaded --so it would be possible to play the game at their own pace. This is just neither feasible nor desirable with the way multiplayer works now.- Resource gathering is as monotonous as it gets and effectively goes towards better weapons, which could still salvage this aspect of the game...-- EXCEPT the better weapons are just bigger numbers and handle the SAME mechanically. There's little change to the player experience in terms of using weapons. Again, there's a lack of variety and if there is variety, the depth is lacking altogether.- Speaking of weapons, the combat in this game is unsatisfying. The game encourages LMB spam and there's very little depth to the combat. Dodging is ineffective and once you've got the enemy/boss mechanics memorised, there's little more to it.- Speaking of dodging, there's no strategic 'poking' like in dark souls as there's a lack of animation cancel. This further reduces the already shallow approach to combat.- Construction is of limited value. They provide little value, compete with limited resources. and the most valuable product is the buggy ramp.- Endboss's moveset lacks depth - it gets stale after 1-2 runs max.-----------------THE HORRID------------------ Scaling for the number of players in game is completely botched. A solo run is just terrible - the map size remains the same so while the resources required are reduced, it's just borderline frustrating to keep pace with the day-night system (which doesn't change).-- It also appears as though the enemy spawns are not tied to player count, just their HP (so the total damage decreases in a linear manner, despite the exponential benefits one gets when playing with more players).- The day-night system as a solo player makes the process incredibly frustrating as you're forced to break your grind to defend your base, but given how the combat is not satisfying (it's literally LMB + space and the occasional RMB/E/R skills) it comes across as a distraction in the earlier stages and then as a punishment in the later stages.-------------------CONCLUSION-------------------This game needs more time in the oven.There are a lot of elements that could make for an enjoyable experience if executed well, but the released product fails to deliver on multiple levels.A bland, unsatisfying and uninspired experience, that's *heavily* reliant on the multiplayer aspect *with people you know* to transform it into something passable.I could only recommend it if it was fairly discounted, but even then there are other great games in 2021 that by any yardstick offer more value for money.Only get this if you're scraping the bottom of the barrel with co-ops.Solo experience: 3/10Public lobby experience: 4/10Playing with friends: can be fun, but again I stress it's fun from playing  game with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very rough start game but once you learn what youre doing and get  your first win under your belt it becomes butter every round you play. I still may not be able to solo it but Between 3 people we can do it in 8 in game days. At first the rounds are really long because you usually push the 15 day limit, but you can always purchase more cosmetics for golden horns you win in game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fairly decent so far, BUT... There are some glaring issues:-Jotuuns need a perpetual marker on the map, they will ruin entire hours of work if you don't locate them fairly soon after they spawn in. You already mark event areas, mark the Jotuuns.-Player tuning solo and in multiplayer needs some adjusting. Playing solo feels extremely punishing given the short days and Jotuun's health.-NPCs feel almost useless most of the time. If they even try to fight more than 1 decent sized mob, they die (even after upgrading).-Implement block and dodge attack animation canceling. With as many high hitting hits from Jotuuns and other mobs and near instant AOE's, let me get the heck out of the way as soon as I want to. Using longer animation weapons feels punishing with the current system.-Archer towers barely do anything for the amount of resources you pool into them (solo play).-Allow us to repair gates.-Allow a "deposit all" function for upgrading NPC's / objects.Other than those things, the game has some good bones.

_childDocuments_.review: Run around and gather stuff for the early game with very awkward contols and no real focused direction. Then around early mid game, play a diablo light style game that still has those crafting elements and requires you to hunt down your next major boss across the map. A lot of the actions do not have any feedback so it feels lifeless and souless doing certain things like mounting and teleporting. Orientation change often causes more problems than not in co-op, but it at least has co-op.Trash, I don't even know what it is, and their presentation leaves me not wanting to find out. They somehow managed beat WoW in the most uninteresting way to display a quest or dialogue. The game looks like it could have had more going for it in the story sense, but it is quite litterally the most tacked on excuse to justify you killing a boss. You will find nothing engaging here.Here there are mixed feelings. The visuals look both great and awful at the same time. Their use of colors are done often in a way that is unappealing because things are either very busy or boring. The models and detail of the enviorment and characters/enemies is actually pretty well done. Animations for combat are pretty solid, but animations for almost anything else are your typical early access low effort - non-existent gathering etc.The Sound  is probably the best part of the game. They have ASMR level boat wood creaking noises, combat noises have acceptable and heavy feedback sounds. The music is solid, with nothing that makes it stand out as amazing but nothing offensive. It's one of the things that kept me from immediately hating the experience.The early game of this game is honestly one of the most boring I've played. I litterally dozed off with the partner I was playing with cause I was having such a lack of fun from the game itself. Thankfully things changed once I was able to get some decent weapons and armor giving it an almost Diablo style experience. I almost - almost had a full 180 about how I felt about the game. However there are a lot of clunky controls, features and just an overall feel of an unfinished, unpolished game that they spent instead on making a micro transaction storefront. It could be better, I doubt it will ever truly be.
_childDocuments_.name: Tribes of Midgard

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

If you're a fan of Norse mythology, cooperative survival games, and unforgettable journeys that never cease to amaze, then Tribes of Midgard on Steam is an absolute must-play.
