_childDocuments_.review: As a solo player the game is disappointing at best. I cannot comment on multiplayer at this time. The game is repetitive and has no real components for how they marketed it. The game mechanics force you to stay near your base at all times to defend against the nightly raids only to die when the first Jotuun shows up and kills you, over and over again. They are completely unbalanced. When you are a new character with basic level 2-3 weapons and level 1 armor you have about 3300 health and do about 90 damage. The Jotuun has 36,000 health and does about 3,000 damage per small hit. If you enjoy wasting your time in a world you cannot go back too, a world where everything you crafted and built is destroyed, then sure the game might be enjoyable. Just keep in mind you rinse and repeat every 10-15 minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: So what is Tribes of Midgard?the tags have it as a tower defense and roguelite.Roguelike/roguelite games are about RNG so each run is different. This game does not do that. As soon as you load in you do the same thing every game regardless of the worlds layout or runes you collect. FInd and break barricades then build quarry so you dont have to worry about the tedious farm for those materials. holding down button to upgrade/ hand in materials. Why not just make it instant? who decided that?spam clicking interact button to pick up items individually in a game that has you farm 100's of materials. Also excellent. Auto collect maybe?Now lets get to the shop. why have a timer for a rotation on recipes? that is content that adds FUN to the game and you have it rotate on a 24hr cycle (down from 48hr at launch). Have cosmetics rotate and a separate tab for recipes, so that we can access the ones we want to unlock and play within our games. Tower defense is literally building a gate and a archer tower at each section of the village. The archer towers barely do anything so you have to come back and defend it anyway. Crafting ramps and floors are to be done by an npc at town? so if you come across high terrain you have to teleport back and craft it at the npc in town. Why not just craft on the spot if you have the materials?This game has a massive identity crisis and has added survival, tower defense, RPG, rogue like and done them all at an average/ below average level. Basic quality of life upgrades and a change to earning resources instead of hitting barricade simulator would do wonders for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately this game was completey mis-marketed and is therefore going to receive a lot of flak for players expecting something that this game isn't. _childDocuments_.review: Tribes of Midgard tries to fuse light tower defense (can only make walls / one kind of archer turret with 4 types of arrows it can shoot) + light arpg (multiple classes but all with tiny passive-only skill trees, only two actual skills per weapon) + light survival (heat and cold but not food) + light crafting that is more akin to dauntless (enemies don't really drop loot, they drop the components to make the weapon that makes killing them again a little easier) + light rogue-like mechanics (runes are random-ish and can provide, guess what, MORE PASSIVES) + light base building (you can make ramps..and fences...and a couple of other things). It doesn't do any of them particularly well. Did I mention buggy? Boss mobs frequently get stuck on the all-too-jagged edges of your base and glitch into an attack animation that isn't actually doing any damage. With all the things/genres it tries to pull off coming out mediocre (at BEST) I really don't see much of a future for it. Maybe it gets better with updates but I don't really see that happening. I could see it being a bit of a spectacle with 8+ players, but at the end of the day, it's slightly better looking Muck. If you live for chopping down trees and mindlessly crafting smaller things into bigger things, there are better games out there.Oh also, it's the kind of game that doesn't really give you the information, gear, or power to actually beat the game until about 4-5 deaths in. Making those first runs feel absolutely pointless. The tools and information and power are literally given to you after death in a battle-pass style progression system. So there is cross-game progression but it's metered out in such a way that it feels like "why the ♥♥♥♥ don't we just start with this" (looking at YOU Villager Starter kit) and less like progressing: more like asking for gruel in an orphanage. You ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ need that gruel to survive but they say "after you die a couple of times we'll let you eat the gruel".it's a sad example of modern game design where developers think adding steps is adding complexity and therefore good. It's not. It just giving the player the run around and forcing them to do all the same ♥♥♥♥ over and over.Imagine if a mario game, every time you got to a new level: it made you redo all the previous levels before it. Not so bad at lvls 1-3. Maybe even you'll improve your time or get a better score. But then you get to level 10 and you realize you now need to do levels 1-9 again, for the umpteenth time. You'd ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ go crazyImagine playing dark souls and you're about to fight a boss, and you realize you only have one copy of the weapon you're using and you know you're going to break at least 2 copies getting the boss below half health, so you have to go back and grind and craft extras because YOU KNOW going into a boss fight with one copy of a weapon simply won't get you anywhere no matter how skilled you are at dodging and parrying. That's what it felt like in Tribes of Midgard.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay now that the first couple waves of crappy comments are gone. I want to put a realistic review.First my rating of this game 7.5/10This game was marketed to be kinda like a ARPG i.e Diablo, Path of Exile (PoE), etc.However although it does have ARPG elements, many people fail to recognize the other elements this game offers.To review, this game is a Rouge-like, "Survival", TOWER DEFENSE, Co-op, ARPG. Those would be the tags that I would classify this game as. It offers many hours of play, with each run feeling slightly different than the last. Hence the nature of Rouge-like. The game does offer "survival" mechanics, but as you would notice from the quotations...not many. The only "true" survival mechanic that the game offers is a temperature system which depending on the class can be completely negated. Now come the MEAT of the game the TOWER DEFENSE, this game IMO at it's core is a tower defense game. You spend your days gathering material upgrading yourself and your base. Then at night monster called "Helthings" try to destroy your base and chop down your cherry tree (Yggdrasil). Your main goal is to defend this tree by fortifying your defenses via archer towers or upgrading your walls/gate. There is co-op, pretty self explanatory, and there is ARPG elements via dungeons and SAGA BOSS. However I believe this element of the game was poorly executed because there are just not enough dungeons/caves/hideouts. Hopefully more will be introduce in later patches. Pros:- Despite what people say I believe the combat feels really nice, I will say that the bow can use a bit more attention.- Game can be difficult (This allow room for defeat and reputability)- RougeLike, the nature of RL games is that you trial and test different items and build.   (There are many different weapons, playstyle, and classes to try)Cons:- Game can feel repetitive once you discover the main strategy- Has exploit and bugs (of course)- Could use more content. I personally feel that the game has a good amount, but could've used a bit more like caves/dungeons.- Scaling may feel difficult for some.A lot of people keep screaming that the game is too hard for duo or trio party, I've beaten the SAGA BOSS multiple times in party of 2-3. Its not that hard once you play a few rounds and begin to understand and prioritize certain objectives.- Long patch window. (There's already a roadmap for the game out, for those that has already checked it the gap in between updates seems long. This is not completely a bad thing, but there are bugs and quality of life things that many players including myself wish they would fix already.) Although there are more Cons vs. Pros. I believe that if you like Rougelike games, into Norse mythos, and don't mind the Tower Defense idea of the game I think it is a pretty solid game. Also it goes without saying that the devs will be adding much more content as the game goes on so even this review is subject to change. Hope this review help sorry if it was long, and I will be updating this later on!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start this review by saying: If you found this game hoping for a fun survival-type game to play with your friends, then keep looking. This ain't it, Chief.However, if you and your friends have dabbled in Survival-Games and you just finished your newest Character on your preferred Dungeon-Crawling game, while saying "Oh man, wouldn't it be cool if we had an upgradeable base for our Characters and every time we start a new run we can redo the whole base thing?" Then stop right there, Criminal Scum. You have found your game.In it's essence Tribes of Midgard follows a very simple Gameplay loop: Start naked, get gear, beat Saga-Boss while defending your village against Monsters at Night and Jotuns throughout the playthrough.That is if you're playing Saga-Mode, I haven't tried survival mode so I won't get into that. You have 13 days before the eternal Night drops, which is your soft-cap to finish the map, since Helthings will endlessly besiege your village at that point, making it hard to finish the rest of the objectives you need to complete the map.As a side-note I should tell you that while solo-play can be fun, this game seems to be definitely developed around groups playing together. Exploring the whole map and finishing all the objectives in time can definitely be done, but it's so much more fun with friends who share the workload with you.Since you have a time-limit it very much becomes a game about finding and playing out the optimal strategy to finish the run. This does not mean that you'll leave all rounds empty-handed however. For every Jotun you kill, you get one golden horn when you leave the map through the bifrost. Which leads me to the next topic:Horns are what it's all about baby, you use those bad boys to buy yourself recipes and cosmetics in the Shop, or craft legendary gear inside of a run. It might seem like they're hard to get, but since they can also drop randomly from any mob in the game, you can end up with a surplus pretty quickly.The dreaded topic, in-game transactions for the elongation of microgenitals, or something like that. Well in all honesty, there's a premium currency and you can use that to buy cosmetic gear or use your horns to buy different cosmetic gear, but it's all meh at best (At least for now, who knows what devious plans the future holds).For challenges, battlepass levels and through the shop you get cosmetic gear. I've used that word a lot now, but what exactly is cosmetic gear? Well, all the gear you get in a run is actually shown on your character! Don't you love it when a game does that? But if you put on cosmetic gear before a run starts, all the gear you get in a run will look like that cosmetic gear, while having the stats of the original piece... of gear.I personally am not much of a fan of that, since I enjoy seeing my character look cooler by getting better gear, but I might change my mind after hundreds of runs, looking at the same gear progression.Onwards to the most exciting feature of the game though:I am completely joking. Turns out, quests give you quest fragments which you need to open up the boss lair. Why they give you rewards that would be good for early game, while sometimes having requirements that are more mid-late game is beyond me, however.So yeah, Quests are kinda big doodoo water.If you got the cash for the base game (deluxe really isn't worth it), and some friends who enjoy grinding with you, go for it dude.

_childDocuments_.review: As a life long fan of aarpgs and maybe a year as a fan of rogue-likes, this game is alright.  The game launched using a battlepass system similar to games like fall guys, but instead of doing runs for crowns, you do them for golden horns.  You start a world and can only exit (and "win") by killing a jotunn (giant boss creature that spawns far away and slowly walks toward your base).  You can leave as soon as you kill the boss, or stay in the game and wait for another to spawn (and the longer you stay, the more the difficulty scales).  The gameplay loop works well enough if you realize that this is not a creative/survival/builder but more of an aarpg with some tower defense aspects thrown in. _childDocuments_.review: Great game, with a lot of fixes needed.The bad review are coming from people who expected something different from the game or doesn't understand how to play the game. This is a high focus, high strategy game that will keep you on your toes for at least 2 hours per run.Every. Second. Matters. The moment you're spawned in the game, actually, before you even spawn in game you need to know what you're going for. Immediately go for those objectives, never stay in base, never stop moving, never stop thinking what to do next, the day cycle goes by fast. Have a plan, where to go, what to craft. If you're spending 30 seconds in the base, that's too long.The souls economy is fine as long as you KEEP MOVING. I usually end up with thousands extra soul by the end of the run.THE GOOD:-. It's fun if you like strategy, especially with friends. Planning what each other are doing is key.-. Doesn't really get boring mid-game since there's so much going on.THE BAD:-. The combat's pretty terrible. Compared to something like DST, this is so far away from being "tight".-. Bug fest, but that's almost always expected from games these days.-. Missing some QoL and important hotkeys that makes certain things take unnecessarily long.-. It's exhausting to do a single full run.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't understand the negative reviews of this game. I have owned the game since Season 1 and have played for almost 40 hours - most if it in Saga mode - without ever experiencing a bug that was notable, let alone game-breaking. Not saying they don't exist, or people's experiences are invalid, but it's just strange to me to see some calling it unplayable.I also typically only play the game with 3-5 people, so have not attempted to max it out at 10 players. I could see where if the host was located far away or didn't have an excellent connection that it could be a problem. Also, not being able to join mid-match could potentially cause an issue if someone does experience a disconnect (not sure if they would be able to rejoin?), but again, these are not issues that are so prominent that they have affected me personally. I have played with people ~2,000 miles away without a problem.From what I'm reading, it seems that some people potentially are not understanding the play-style, so perhaps I can shed some light on that for potential buyers.It's obvious both by the name ( of Midgard) and the play style that this game is designed as a multiplayer game. I think it  be fun to play solo (in Survival mode perhaps), but the game in general is tailored to, and will most definitely be more enjoyable for, groups of friends. If you are trying to solo Saga especially, it's just not going to be as fun in my opinion. I also don't think you will find yourself very happy playing with randoms as this game takes coordination and some level of trust among a tribe, and people can be ... well, people.Tribes is also potentially not a game you are going to play for two months non-stop, but it's a game definitely worth returning to from time to time. My friends and I will usually play it intensely for a a week or so, kill the boss(es), complete some challenges, and then move on to different games and return when there is a new update/season. Perhaps there are people who play it more regularly and that's awesome! I think Survival mode tries to put in a bit more longevity as well.I think it's important to note that if you are looking to play the "main" mode (the Saga mode) that it indeed  the first couple of times you play it. That's the point. You really aren't  to get it on the first attempt, or even necessarily the fifth attempt, and it's supposed to feel a bit overwhelming until you figure things out and start to understand your priorities/goals. - You'll learn what's important, what's not, and will continue to progress further and further each run.Your first couple attempts will likely only last a few game days (and thus be shorter games) until your tree collapses . Once you start figuring things out and start getting closer to defeating the season boss, each run will take you just over two hours  - because by that point you will likely be overwhelmed if you haven't already won, and eventually you may become skilled enough to do it in much less time.Ultimately, when starting out and progressing, be prepared for around two hours of moderately-paced game play with basically "zero chill" while you explore, gather, gear, build, defend, and do other tasks to complete your Saga goal(s). Take your potty breaks in advance people.The last thing I want to mention is the Survival mode because some friends and I just started playing this mode recently and so far I really enjoy it. I look forward to logging many additional hours in this mode and would definitely recommend it for those looking to experiment a bit more with various builds for gear and armor, master the structure building (like ramps), focus more on gathering and exploration, and just generally "exist" without the wild hustle and bustle of Saga.

_childDocuments_.review: 🎮From the onset, Tribes of Midgard does not hold your hand but throws you into this large undiscovered map with a very vague guideline in terms of what you are here to accomplish. From crafting a simple Villager Sword to protect yourself from Helthings come nightfall or finding branches and flint deposits to craft the basic flint-ax to aid in deforestation or the basic flint-pickaxe to relinquish stone, iron ore, and many other materials to aid you in your crafting journey in the midst of the Jotun and Ragnarok threat.There is a big emphasis on exploration within the game since you only find certain crafting materials once you reach certain areas in and around the map, the caveat here is that each area has its own power level. So if you decided to venture into Ash Beach with a power level below 180, needless to say, you’d have a difficult time trying to accomplish anything. Whilst power level is of great importance, focusing on the biomes you are moving into is also something to keep your eye on because if you move into an area that is either too hot or too cold they can both negatively affect your character and eventually begin draining your HP.Aside from environmental effects throwing you for a loop, you also need to keep your eyes peeled for different enemy types who all have their own elemental traits. From wolves to trolls to serpents, Midgard has the majority of what you’d expect from a fantasy roleplaying game and we are all for it. Taking this into account, the wisest course of action is to ensure you have a weapon of each element on you at all times whilst you traverse the world that is Midgard.👾🔥🧊🔮🗲Enemies are plentiful in the land of Midgard and they are placed all around the map, from the early on level 20 Bright Forest enemies that can basically be blown over with the least amount of exertion to the level 200 and above enemies that can be found in high-level areas that require the right attire to deter the harsh conditions and also requires elemental effect imbued weaponry.From the Dokkalfar to the Brennalfar, From the Blue Goblin to the White Goblin, From the Unsunken to the Unfrozen, and everything in between there is enough opposition for you to sink your proverbial teeth into and a sizable meaty challenge to every encounter, as long as you are correctly equipped and tenacious enough in the face of adversity.But, in this land unfortunately it’s not “one size fits all”, since all enemy types have their own elemental preference you need to learn what to use to counteract. Luckily, there are only 4 elements you need to memorize which is about as simple as a match 3 puzzle. These elements are Fire, Ice, Dark, and Thunder(Lightning). As you could probably deduce on your own Fire and Ice are each other’s weaknesses and, Dark and Thunder are in the same boat. 🔧When launching into a fresh world of Midgard you will be required to craft the most basic of essentials such as an axe and a pickaxe and at least a Villagers Sword just so you and The Seed of Yggdrasil are able to survive your first night. Once you have fended off the residents of Hel , you can then start planning out what is most needed to upgrade whether it be the farm, quarry, or the lumberyard. Each with its own set of advantages. Once you have begun venturing in and around your Homebase, you will come across shrines which you should definitely activate as these are used as fast travel points because you will notice that walking around Midgard under-equipped will be met with a quick and swift demise.Once you’ve exposed a decent amount of Midgards land, you would have come across various enemies and resources that would aid you in your crafting journey. Plenty of trees, various mineral deposits, wolves, Dokkalfar warriors/witches, a troll or 2, and definitely at least one Jotun. Now, you can begin working towards creating a decent armor set. At the time of writing, there are currently 10 armor sets you can craft, all with their own elemental advantages and stats.🎬Tribes of Midgard is such a visually pleasing game to experience because it’s a game that just goes to show you that you don’t need hyper-realistic graphics or a massive budget to make a good game. There are vibrant colors used just about everywhere which is so refreshing in comparison to the dull and dreary colors of today’s “realistic games”. Games are games, if I wanted to go outside I would so keep it that way.🎵I enjoyed the atmospheric background music as I became invested in the lore as well as the many mechanics in the game, it’s great because it’s not so much as to distract you from what your goals are but it’s also not less enough to not make some kind of impact. So to me, it’s perfectly balanced so far as sound and music go.📃●	Tons of replayability●	Bunch of armor and weapon sets●	Good atmosphere●	Runs exceptionally well●	Introduces you to a hint of Norse mythology which I rather enjoyed❖	Level 10 cap for character☁If you are looking for a new multiplayer experience that you can jump into with a bunch of your friends or maybe even just a bunch of randoms that has a good amount of replayability as well as a simple introduction into Norse mythology you should definitely pick up Tribes of Midgard for your Steam library. Rating: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Tribes of Midgard is a co-op survival game with RPG and base building elements. Developed by Norsfell and published by Gearbox in 2021, it draws inspiration from Norse mythology, placing players as a Viking warrior tasked with defending the Seed of Yggdrasil from endless waves of invading spirits and monsters.Gameplay revolves around gathering resources during the day to build up your village and defenses, including walls, archer towers, and traps. At night, increasingly difficult hordes attack, requiring coordination with your teammates to defend key points. There's a real-time strategy element to designing your village layout for optimal protection.Between attack waves, you explore the procedurally generated worlds around you or venture into other realms via the Bifrost. Here you gather better gear and special items to aid your survival efforts. There's a crafting system for weapons and armor, allowing considerable customization of your playstyle.The RPG mechanics provide a good sense of progression as you gain experience, unlock new godly powers related to Norse figures like Loki and Odin, and enhance your combat abilities. There's a large tech tree for further village enhancements.Visually, it nails the Vikings meets fantasy aesthetic. Bright, colorful worlds filled with magic contrast with the gory combat and enemy design, which pulls from Norse legend. The music is suitably epic and dramatic when in combat.For replay value, the randomized worlds, loot grind, and multiple difficulty settings make each playthrough unique. Both solo and co-op modes means you can fight alone or with up to 9 other players. While combat grows repetitive over time, the base building and progression elements keep things interesting.Tribes of Midgard skillfully blends survival, base building, and ARPG elements into one package. Despite some repetitive combat, its charm, magical worlds, and addictive growth mechanics make for an enjoyable co-op experience.

_childDocuments_.review: My first steam review so here you go. 6/10My thoughts on this game are that it has potential but right now its a bit of a shell of a game. The crafting/town upgrading mechanics are super shallow. After the 20th run this stuff starts to get boring, especially considering the time it takes to dump souls in the upper levels of the merchants.I tried every weapon, and they were fun, but like most things with this game because of the repetitiveness it became old very fast (most weapons share the same 2-3 skills/animations effects there is not much depth. Some fully upgraded weapons dont even get a new skill)This game doesnt have the same randomness as other ARPGS and you find yourself going cutter-cutter builds doing the exact same attacks over and over and over without your damage or anything else getting higher/harder. More enemies dont spawn, after a certain point they stop getting more difficult, and yeah it can be annoying to defend your town solo but its still pretty easy honestly.  It has less variety than Minecraft Dungeons. This is also by far one of the most buggy games I have played on the PC, with lots of getting trapped between constructions, falling into the water for no reason, and other optimization issues. The game feels like an Early Access. I'm happy with the 20 bucks I spent and think its worth it, just think it has a long way to go before being something you don't get bored of in a couple of days. It's like a mix of a survival/gather game, a tower defense game mixed with an ARPG.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE April 11th: When our group first complained about the Abandon button behavior, we were told that the next version of the game will have a fix for this. Well, that version is now out and the Abandon button still exists. The fix? The devs merely moved the button down a bit and made it red.Destructive UX that doesn't need to exist shouldn't exist.If destructive UX needs to exist, it should be least destructive.If a player that abandons by accident could still rejoin the multiplayer session as invited by their friends, it would be an annoyance at most. But as it stands, the Abandon button is the single easiest way to ruin an otherwise decent game by allowing users to destructively ruin their own experience by accident without recourse to recover.Another review by our group called it a "ban me" button. In effect, that's what it is and that's what it remains...--After spending a considerable amount of time playing this game with my friends, I find myself compelled to share my thoughts on an aspect that has thoroughly soured my multiplayer experience: the ill-conceived "abandon" option.At first glance, the game boasts an impressive lineup of features, immersive gameplay, and a beautifully crafted world. However, the excitement of exploring and conquering challenges with my friends was quickly overshadowed by the game's crippling "abandon" mechanic.This option, presumably meant to provide players with a clean slate, actually serves as a one-way ticket to a realm of frustration. Once you abandon a world, there's no way to rejoin it, which is a huge oversight by the developers. This mechanic not only hinders the multiplayer experience but also completely undermines the progress made by the affected player and their friends.Imagine spending countless hours grinding, exploring, and building together, only for one accidental click to throw it all away. The feeling of loss and wasted time is gut-wrenching. With no option to reverse the action, the motivation to continue playing the game rapidly dwindles.Furthermore, this harsh mechanic has created a negative atmosphere within the community. Players are hesitant to invite new members to their world, fearing an accidental abandonment could jeopardize the entire group's progress. This has led to a fractured player base, where trust and collaboration are overshadowed by the constant threat of an irreversible mistake.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game would be great if the devs fixed some major flaws that really hurt the player experience.1. The combat would be a lot better if blocking was actually beneficial. The animation for blocking with a shield cannot start right after you attack, therefore enemies will strike back and hit you. Given that you don't move/roll away. So the fact that blocking is pretty much useless aside the guardian class blocking (because you taunt enemies), really makes the combat feel clunky to me.2. The amount of time you have to collect resources before night arrives only gets shorter and shorter the more you progress because nights get longer. This is really annoying especially while playing solo or with one other friend because you have to take care of jotunns and night defenses, which leaves little time for exploring and doing side quests.3. Strong viking dies instantly to water, apparently. (No joke, if you roll in the water you die and lose all the souls you racked up)Those are my biggest gripes with this game at the moment, but I will admit it's a great looking game that can be fun with a group of at least 4 friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This game suffers from lack of some real quality of life/ substance/ fun issues. For instance when you get close to a boss (Jotunn) the camera zooms out to give you more of a full view of how large it is. Great...but because im playing an archer, if i'm safely away shooting, sometimes the camera zooms in and out repeatedly, which is really disorienting and not great for overall enjoyment.Also as an archer, I cannot gain certain achievements like my friends can. Example: you get a cosmetic armor set for last hitting each type of Jotunn. So all of my friends got the last hits and the entire time I just thought I was unlucky or not doing damage. In fact they even kindly backed off to let me get the last hit, and each time it would go to someone else and we were not able to find out why. Until it dawned on me...what if I walked up and meleed the damned thing? And yup..that was it. So because I chose an archer class and have no interest in playing a warrior while everyone else did, I was being made to feel punished. The other classes are basically walled off to me, and I'll explain why later...I'd also like to describe the frustration of playing with only two players. The hubby and I love playing with friends, but the ones that do play with us have been busy and our other friends (understandibly) did not want to purchase the game because of the whole false advertisement thing. We were all siked to play a certain game and that game did not come out. But the hubby and I decided to try the game anyway despite this. So because its basically just us, we have to play as 2. We are actually pretty good at clearing and harvesting the map and getting back before dark when the waves of enemies come in, hell we even usually get the first boss down. but as 2 players thats about all you will ever be able to feasibly do. It is literally impossible to level up your entire base, level up the npcs who you use to make you strong enough to go against the later bosses, level up your gear and tools, and harvest enough stuff on the map so you can upgrade stuff, explore and gain more powers and level up, and all the while keeping the damned tree alive every night and keeping the Jotunn's at bay. Oh and dont even think about doing fun events, unless they are in your path you will not get them without sacrificing valuable base building/harvesting time that will ultimately cost you the ability of being able to kill the first Jotunn and gain the ability to port out and 'win' instead of getting a game over. So basically the devs have said they did scale the game appropriately depending on the amount of players, but I can tell you with all honesty that they definitely did not. It doesnt feel scaled at all, and in fact if the two of us werent so organized, strategic, and goal driven we probably wouldn't even get the first boss down. Thank goodness we make a great team or there'd be no progression at all for us...We have played for about 15 hours now, and for a 20 dollar game thats not too bad I'd argue, but the issue I'm having after playing so long is that the game feels...off.I told the hubby that if I were to describe this game as a food dish, it would be bland boiled white rice. No salt, no butter, no spices. Just bland hospital food. There's no awe inspiring views, no details that make you go "oh wow thats kinda cool" and no real immersion here. And because of how they built the game, even when there a lot of you and your friends playing there is never any time to stop and enjoy the world itself even if they had built one. Youre always rushing, running around, trying to build the next thing before the proverbial ♥♥♥♥♥ hits the fan so to speak. I would have liked to be able to hang out in the base, maybe do some simple quests for the farmers station and quarry, but no...if I do that im wasting time...time that costs us the game. Time that costs our characters overall progression towards well...cosmetics and nothing really that good I guess?And lets talk about quests. Why bother having them? I mean none of my friends and I ever have the same ones, so in a game about trying to work together and win together, in a game about time constraints and going fast, we have to stop and go "ok who has what" and try to figure out of we can even do the same quests. Because anything past easy requires more people which is a waste of time if only one of you has it. So we never really do the quests, because they reward one of us and the ends never justify going through that much trouble.The quests that actually DO matter are the ones that unlock other classes. But those are locked off to us as I have stated above, because of the same reason that 2 people cannot properly enjoy this game and get past the first and sometimes second boss. You might be able to get a Seer after some time of farming one boss and leaving but the rest of the challenges will never happen with just 2 people playing cooperatively. Every part of the game just ramps up the difficulty way too quickly for that to even be an option.Besides the game being so obviously flawed, the shop itself its incredibly expensive. Probably because it has a cash shop and they want to pressure people into buying into their 2 different types of currency? I get that everything in the shop is cosmetic. But I have played for 15 hours. FIFTEEN....and guys, I can almost afford 1 single item. So 15 hours of gameplay, do you want pants or shoes? and the shop is like fall guys, so it changes thru inventory every 24 hours and also a second bar changes every idk 15 hours or something like that. But unlike fall guys (whereas the ever changing shop is cute and fun...) because the currency is a literal hell grind, I dont know if something better will come along in a few hours and ill regret my purchase. And again, I can only afford 1 thing right now, so even if I am going for a set, I cannot save for one, or I can but It will probably take a good few months or something by the time I complete one.In the big wide world of vidya games, Tribes of Midgard is the color snot green. It could have been a cool color, one that is nicer to look at. it could have been jade, or jungle, or hell I'd even take a nice pine. But it's snot green and if you dont like snot green...youll have to like it because there is nothing else to enjoy here.You dont like tower defense?You dont like being rushed in your games?You dont like being punished if you try to set foot outside of the box that the devs think you should be in?You dont like having to say no to exploring because if you dont head to the boss fight and kill it before it gets to your base or youll almost certainly lose?You dont like rng deciding whether or not you 'do well' on a certain play through with materials and routes on the map?If you agree with any of these, this game is not for you. It's not the worst game...it's just..'okay'....but in a world where there are quite literally 30-50 awesome games coming out every month, ones that are more fun and nicer to look at. Ones where the devs seem to really put a lot of thought and detail into their game, or even ones that you can actually finish the quests in if you pick a diff class than the devs clearly play on the regular....well then I ask you...is just 'okay' enough?If I could go back in time I might not have bought this game. But now we own it and we have 2 other friends who bought it because we did. Maybe theyll make it better, maybe they wont. My friends and I will make it fun because that's the kind of group we are, but the game should have been better... I hope this long ass rant did you some good. Because now that I've been playing it, I can tell you from experience that 'just okay' is not enough for me. =/

_childDocuments_.review: Like Terraria and Valheim combined, however survival is a questionable design. There is little to no point of the structure crafting, you can't build anything out in the world that is of use, the walls are entirely pointless.Basically the only reason and way you build is if you are the warden b/c it's free and infinite.There are little things like this scattered around the game, just really weird questionable design choices, however a lot of this could be contingent on how each saga (aka seasons) will change the game; whether it be drastic changes or minor tweaks, this game has great potential.The combat feels good other than the fact that blocks and dodges don't break animation making the damage mitigation abilities feel very clunky.The XP needed for the season pass needs to be looked at. You don't get far enough for a reasonable amount of time; for example, I currently have ~85 hours played and am only level 42 on the season and that's with doing a day 100 survival, and every other achievement and earnable rewards other than season pass rewards and the max level season achievement.Saga mode and survival are the only two modes in the game, saga typically takes about an hour to complete through matchmaking ( which can be done as fast as 10-20 minutes if you have a group in communication knowing what to do) and survival mode which is made to go as long as you possibly can.The problem with survival is that after some time you get to a point where you have nothing to do, you can be full build easily in 12-17 days without coms or really trying that hard, and then after that it's extremely boring.Each 24-hours cycle is 10 minutes long so doing 100 days is 1000 minutes which is 16.7 hours. I completed this over the course of 2 days and let me tell you all after day 30 we all had our frost armor and maxed weapons we wanted, we had the entire map unlocked. We decided to work on the Spend 1 million souls achievment by buying souls potions and popping them which took about 60 days, even then after spending 1 million souls we were at a point where we were just waiting in our village for 10 days to roll over.TLDR; The game plateaus out very heavily in survival since the goal is to survive as long as possible, but as long as possible is really really really really really easy, the only difficult thing is not falling asleep after that long duration.It would be nice to have something to do for a long survival run, but there currently isn't anything.Saga mode is the "quick" mode, but still match-made groups typically are going to take an hour to complete a mode, I think the devs need to take some hints from league of legends and do things to make the "quick" gamemode a lot faster.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game but I can't. It feels like a phone game that was rushed to be released. It's trying to be a hybrid of a tower defense/survival crafting/exploration game but it does none of those things particularly well. There's very little depth in the game and each game feels exactly the same as the last game and the only progress made in the game is trying to last a little longer than the last game which would be fine if there was a reason to do so. In each game, you have to do the same specific things in the same order each time otherwise you lose when the first winter comes. And if you're playing in a pub game this will rarely ever happen. The combat is clunky, the weapons are bland and many of the class attributes are entirely useless such as a 10% damage increase with 1 weapon type which you can't tell the difference with or taking reduced fall damage when there's barely any fall damage in the game to begin with. If you dodge roll, it doesn't even block damage unless you have the attribute from the warrior class that lets you block damage when dodging. When you die in the game, you lose all your souls and if you're playing a pub multiplayer game, souls are so slow to accumulate and repair costs are so steep that people just quit the game after they die once. The only chance you have of surviving at all in the game is if you have a private party of people who put all their materials into the war chest and let a Warden craft and delegate gear to everyone. In a pub game, this will rarely happen unless you get people who are actively cooperating over voice comms.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like it should be in early access, not recommended at the moment.* Movement is terribly janky, you get stuck in small details in the environment.* Moving around ledges and building platforms don't snap so you can get stuck in terrain very easily, and you automatically die when touching a bit of water which is an issue when dodging or monster hitboxes push you around.* Movement and attacks are animation locked which makes dodging feel sluggish and unresponsive.* Boss targeting and telegraphing is broken. The boss can start his telegraph and you dodge out behind him, and the he flips 180 degrees and slams his sword in your back. Or the boss might just shoot the attack out his "behind" while looking at some other player.* Menus and interface is also janky. No proper feedback when inputing materials in buildings, not sure if you actually pressed the icon or what's happening. You can input materials into a slot and the UI shows green, only to escape out and then notice that the game dumped your stuff into the void and the slot is still missing. This is EXTREMELY satisfying when inputing the last dungeon fragment only to notice that you actually just wasted all that time.Incredibly frustrating overall, it's only friends playing that's keeping me in the game.Edit: The jank killed this game for me, no more play.

_childDocuments_.review: God awful in every way that counts - the game play. The aesthetics are pretty great. Cell shading looks nice, and animations look fine. Sounds is ok. I like the gibberish of the voice over. (Maybe it's a real language, I dunno.) Combat is generic. Super generic. Left click, right click when bar is charged. Maybe dodge. Maybe block. Dodge doesn't have i-frames unless you spec into it. Block works. Mostly. When attacks don't phase through.The economy is absolutely borked. You will not get enough souls to keep the tree alive and repair your gear. In one night of the attacks from the mobs, your weapon will be nearly destroyed. You will get enough souls to repair it...if you're lucky. But the constant drain on the tree makes it so you cannot even repair plus get the tree back to what it was prior to the night beginning. Wanna do some upgrades? You can. Too bad your tree won't actually stay alive as a result.Seems to be some bugs. There are "Global Events" that seem to be the only decent way to keep your soul economy up. HOWEVER, in 4 runs with my buddy, we got the stag twice. Worked fine. The third event we saw was the prisoner. He wasn't there. He was on the map, but not actually there. Roamed around the area. Nope. Buddy checked. Nope. Next event was Roosters of Ragnarok. Same story. If the global events are the only way to keep things moving forward...they should work.I've never hated a game so much I've left a bad review. 2.5 hours was enough to put this at the top of my "nice idea, terribly implemented" list.

_childDocuments_.review: A very weird, unfortunate game. It plays essentially like every standard phone survival game, sans micro-transactions. In that the survival / gathering aspect is just a artificial time extender without any significance or gameplay. Combat is extremely simplistic and essentially consists of spam attack and abilities and only bother dodging for telegraphed attacks. It's sad because in terms of quality and the world you can see the developers definitely had a lot of passion for the game, but aside from very casual players, the gameplay loop is about as enticing as Candy Crush Saga or so, and after upgrading my crafts people to the 4th tier (before servers crashed), It felt more like just grinding for the sake of grinding then to achieve anything. So take into account, I am not sure what far-end gameplay is like, but mechanically it seems simplistic. I can't see any major sort of skill/knowledge curve to the game.Also be aware it is a pseudo-roguelike, in which you'll be joining sessions and reverting world progress often, just make sure to factor that in, as this game is quite a nice mash of different genres that makes it hard to peg into one category easily.I'd say in the game, there lies a lot of potential, especially with the quality of the actual game. I'd be keen to see what these devs bring next to the table, but personally I just feel like the game is a bad recipe made by a expert chef. Some people may still find alot of fun in this with friends, or just a casual side game, but if you were looking for a sort of ARPG with challenges or complexity, then there are greener pastures. But for a more chill just grinding time, then it might be for you.I personally am likely not to be playing this game, but if you know what the gameplay cycle is and are curious on quality, then I whole heatedly recommend it. The game definitely comes across as one of the more polished and passionately developed games, unfortunately I just think it's too niche/casual for what I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: This is essentially all the base elements of a survival, MMORPG and hack'n'slash game thoughtlessly mixed together with no understanding for what makes any of it satisfying.It is immediately noticeable how weightless the combat is. Players press, or hold down, the attack button to repeat the same combo over and over. The screen maybe jiggles a bit, smaller enemies slide backwards with no animation, but otherwise that's it. You just hold the button down until the enemy goes away. There's no sensation of impact or meaning or investment to attacks, it's just the rigid animation that plays when you hold a button down to lower the enemy healthbar. A lot of the animations look like animations, characters and enemies appear like puppets being strung about.The default sword attack combination forces players to constantly keep stepping forward as they attack. So if players are fighting an enemy that takes many attacks to knock out, players will constantly keep walking into them then sliding past. This forces you to constantly reposition yourself because your own attack combination is relentlessly displacing you, yet basic enemies have enough health that you'll have to put up with this everytime you fight them. Instead of worrying about stamina or danger, your biggest worry is over your own attack moving you away from what you're trying to attack; thus lowering your damage per second and making this pointless fight last longer. It looks terrible, it feels terrible, it feels like playing a hack and slash project some game development student made for a class.The crafting and survival elements are just the most basic crafting and survival mechanics copy pasted into place for no reason other than wasting time. Players are expected to run around the map clicking a button to immediately chop down trees and gather rocks. There's nothing satisfying or immersive about it; you just press a button to instantly topple a tree and get wood. You can barely even keep track of all the things you're gathering because it's just such a frantic rush of collection. Then players need to take all that random stuff, bring it to specific characters in town and have them turn it into gear. There's a different character for each type of thing so you have to run all around town for each individual need, plus you need to refine resources into other resources just to then build basic things, and your gear degrades so you have to go to a specific crafting station in town just do repair it all every single time it breaks.There's zero sensation of progression or collection or creation it's just a pointless slog players will constantly need to go through just to get and maintain equipment or upgrades. No satisfaction or sensation of meaning, it's just a chore.The game also has a noticeboard of fetch quests or something. So you're not even encouraged to just openly explore, if you want structured rewards you need to go to the noticeboard to get a quest then go to that specific place to do X thing. And you can only get one quest at a time, because the developers really need you to waste that extra time going back to the noticeboard after you finish every single quest. Apparently this game has a class system too, but the tutorial doesn't mention it and it's kind of just a part of the user interface you have to wander into. From what I saw the perks aren't very interesting. The starting perk for the default melee class is every third attack triggers twice, or something. So it's a passive damage increase that adds nothing to the actual experience; this is the first thing you unlock. This is the defining introduction to your class.I was holding out hope that the game would be less of a mindless button pressing simulation when the difficulty ramped up. So I found a mini-boss encounter while exploring in the starter area. This is one of those games where players are expected to relentlessly spam their attack if they want to actually deal decent damage to remotely significant threats, but you're also punished for spamming your attack because you can't properly avoid the abrupt enemy attacks. So you have to choose between hitting the enemy for a half percentage of health then backing away so you can dodge their next attack, or actually attacking more than once but then getting hit because you're animation locked. There's no back and forth flow to fighting, no last moment dodges right before an attack hits. It's simply; if the enemy abruptly decides to attack you at the same time as you attack then you get hit. Now attack them a hundred times to whittle their healthbar down and if you get knocked out by the constant damage trades then restart. Receiving damage is barely even noticeable, because this game has no sense of impact.Everything is just happening. Damage just happens, there's no character animation for it; the healthbar just goes down. Dealing damage just happens, the attack animation plays and the enemy healthbar goes down then maybe they slide backwards a little without actually moving their legs. And enemies just decide to deal damage, a rigid attack animation immediately plays and if players aren't already blocking or preparing a dodge then it lands. You're encouraged to spam because there's nothing else to do but spam yet you're punished for spamming because you constantly step forward and displace yourself while getting hit because of animation lock. This is all just in the immediate early game and already the most basic enemy encounters are unsatisfying damage races. It feels like this was designed to be played by mindless swarms of players mashing threats down amidst an nonsensical flurry of puppet-on-string animations.This doesn't feel like a paid product. The rigid animations, lack of any impact or satisfaction to combat, the spammy flow of combat, untelegraphed enemy attacks that simply just happen, can easily not even notice yourself getting hurt because the only visual indication is the healthbar going down, pointless copy pasted survival mechanics that add nothing but tedium, very unexciting introduction to what looks like a shallow class system, arbitrary noticeboard quests. It's like the game is just trying to tick as many boxes for genre mechanics as possible simply for the sake of it.Spammy damage race animation lock combat? Hack and slash game check.Run around pressing buttons to gather resources then run around town refining them?Survival game check.Class system with such exciting starter perks as ten percent more sword damage? Role playing game check.One-at-a-time noticeboard quests that want you run across the map because reasons? MMO game check.Just the most shallow, thoughtless emulation of stock gameplay mechanics all mashed together.If you're interested in finding some games that I do positively recommend they can be found on my curator page .

_childDocuments_.review: At the core there is some good ideas here and some potentially fun gameplay.And it is a lot of fun for a handful of games, while you die a lot and figure out how to play.Once you do figure out how to play however, it becomes quite tedious as each runthrough is basically the same, the map is random but what you need to do and the order to do it in is always more or less the same. There is literally nothing to do once you have beaten the game once, apart from grinding the season ranks, which unlock some rewards that in my opinion are not very interesting, certainly not interesting enough to warrant grinding the same game loop over and over again with zero variation.With some more content added, more game modes and more stuff to do and better balancing, sure it could be an awesome game, but for now this is not worth it in my opinion.* Combat, while initially it seems reasonably entertaining, is really just holding down the mouse button and then spamming your abilities when mana is full. This is very pronounced on later state bosses where they have a lot of hp and it is merely a matter of holding down your mouse button for long enough to kill them (and constantly repairing your weapon, seriously some fights will have you going back to town to repair 3-4 times during a single fight), while dodging very predictable routines.Shield is basically useless as it is always better to spam attacks because its just a damage race, and bows are even more so useless because other weapons are far better in terms of DPS and range is rarely any advantage.* Gear is quite unbalanced, this leads to almost always using the same gear loadouts and everyone usually uses the same, so you rarely see any variance here cause there is no point.* Same goes for classes, current implementation feels like it was just slapped on in order to say "we have classes". In reality it is a selection of mostly meaningless perks, where 2 classes just soar above the rest in power because of a few perks that actually do something, hence everyone plays those 2 classes.* "Tower Defense" When sometimes referred to as partly a TD game, this is not true. You can build the gate and 2 archers towers at each entrance to the town, then upgrade them a few times with the same materials. Thats it, they help a bit in town defense but there is no TD gameplay here per say, and it mostly feels like a chore to defend the town that actually detracts from the fun parts of the game, exploring.* There is a building system in the game, which again feels like an afterthought, because it has absolutely no damn meaning in the game, apart from building ramps to reach some treasure chests on cliffs. You can build walls and stuff but there is never any point in doing this as there is always something better to be doing with the limited time available.* Which leads to the next point, the Saga mode is very time constrained, day/night cycle is short and there is very little time to explore/build/craft, you need to be collecting specific materials and doing specific things in the same order every game in order to win, and there is no freedom to vary this by much. For some this gameplay might be fun but for me personally it makes it very tedious because there is not much strategy involved, there is only one right way to go about it.* While the game has not been out for very long yet, the first couple of patches are not very promising, they are not adding anything new, merely tweaking some stats here and there with a few bug fixes, if this is indicative of future improvements, i am not holding my breath.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve never wrote a review before but I think that such a great and promising game receiving the reviews it is deserves a comprehensive review as compared to bad reviews like “game doesn’t let you join midway through saga” or good reviews like “The game is good”. There is a tl;dr at the bottom.This is all from my point of view, but I’ve almost 100% (all but level 50, 85/100 days in Survival, and 1M souls spent) all the challenges for season one. I’ve played both modes, solo, with friends, and with randoms. Other Reviews: -	The bulk of the negative reviews that I’ve seen are stating that the game is too grindy, that the combat is boring, and that saga mode is too hard/too fast paced. They don’t specify how the game is grindy, but I’m going to assume the battlepass which is grindy UNTIL you start winning in Saga, as I stated earlier, each saga win is a level basically. Saga is fast paced, but it matches the story of the game; weren’t people just complaining about how slow paced Cyberpunk2077 was when the story was so frantic? I will concede though that combat against run of the mill enemies is boring, but against the jotunn, saga boss, and giants it’s a lot of fun. Which facing off against a giant lava giant should be more entertaining than kicking a goblin if you ask me.-	The bulk of the positive reviews that I’ve seen state that the game is fun to play with friends, the battlepass system, and that it has a lot of potential. The game is a lot of fun with friends, but what game isn’t? It’s also a lot of fun solo and the couple of games I did with randoms were great. The battlepass system is included with the game and changes each season, you cannot buy levels and it gives you items that effect gameplay which is a great way to reward and motivate players and they plan to roll out seasons every couple of months. The game has enormous potential and I really hope that Norsfell don’t let the mixed reviews on steam deter them, the game is already great and I really look forward to them doing more with it.Saga: -	The “main” game mode is saga; you earn golden horns by killing jotunn (1 per) and killing the saga boss (5). You need to leave/extract from Midgard via the Bifrost to collect your golden horns (a currency that is earned through play and cannot be purchased). If you’re getting close to a defeat and are worried you can extract via the Bifrost at any time and collect the horn(s) you’ve earned. You use golden horns in game and in the shop. In game to craft legendary items and in shop to buy recipes or cosmetics. Saga is timed, anything past 15-16 in-game days and you’re gonna have a bad time. It is fast paced and challenging, at first, but once you’ve learned a bit and gotten used to the game you really start thriving in the game mode.Survival: -	If the main game mode is too fast paced or challenging for you than this is for you. You can set the parameters of the world a few examples are world size, resource abundance, and enemy difficulty. As you change the parameters making the game easier or harder you also adjust how much battlepass experience you earn. If you run everything down then you earn less, but if you’re worried about experience then use the easier settings to learn the game and then jump into saga to earn horns and exp (each win is about 28k exp which is a level and some change). There’s no time limit here like in Saga and everything respawns so you don’t need to worry about running out of resources.Currency: There’s golden horns (that were covered in the Saga overview above) and there are coins. The coins are a microtransaction, but they are only able to be used on cosmetics ONLY. You cant use them to buy golden horns or to buy the recipes that show up in the shop occasionally.The Good: -	The game is extremely fun solo, with friends, or with randoms. If you are worried it won’t be fun solo, then hop into some random worlds with matchmaking. There are emotes, voicelines, a text chat, and you can talk with mics to communicate. Maybe you’ll make some friends there that you can regularly play with.-	I love that the battlepass system and the shop are setup to reward you for playing and playing consistently. (A complaint I have about WoW is that the catch-up mechanics for returning players feel like they punish active players; why grind something for a year when I can come in towards the end and do everything in a month?)-	The graphics and sound are absolutely beautiful. I can tell which jotunn I am about to fight before I see them by the sound of their footsteps, or I know a goblin is off screen cause I hear them skittering around.-	Runes are a lot of fun and create strong synergies with different classes. A friend of mine craves “Nothing to hide runes” that make you do more damage per empty armor slot. They then pick berserker and run around with a hammer doing crazy damage, truly the viking we should aspire to be.The Bad:-	Combat can be frustrating. Attacks hitboxes don’t line up for some enemies (looking at you trolls) and blocking is only useful very early in the game and niche at best later.-	The environment is working with your enemies. I can not tell you how many times the water’s gravitational pull has coaxed my body through earth to drown me. A few time’s I’ve gotten stuck on a rock and been faced with the option to kill myself (luckily there’s an option if you’re stuck) or have a lone goblin chuck rocks at my head until death’s sweet embrace took me.TL;DR:-	It’s a great game with it’s share of bugs and jank, not game breaking, but frustrating at times and you can learn to avoid them. Saga is a race and is difficult (at first) but as you learn and get better at the game it becomes more enjoyable. If that sounds scary, try Survival where you can adjust settings and play/learn at your own pace. The game is great solo, with randoms, and with friends (I’ve experienced each and have had a great time each time). Microtransactions are cosmetic only and battlepass/seasons are included with the game and give you premium currency among other cosmetics and items that effect gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say this feels like the early days of Don't Starve Together, before you get good at that game. The difference is Don't Starve at its heart is a survival game, you are tasked with surviving but all obstacles you face, can and eventually will, be beaten. Runs go from lasting minuets, to hours, to days and beyond. Somewhere in that the games stops feeling like a rogue-like, and more like a base builder. Tribes of Midgard feels like a rogue like at its heart. The game starts off as a challenge, and only gets harder. The game becomes easier at higher player counts, but if everyone is not pulling their weight, death is sure to come. At day 15 night becomes endless, and the base never stops being attacked. They're are only so many upgrades to be done to the base, and the final boss of the run is only ever a few hours away. When you add all of that up, you get a game that, with a few friends, leads to a few hours of great challenging fun, that has left me and my group of friends saying, lets have another run. From run to run you will be sure to be thinking on how to optimize gathering, resources and builds. Depth that is much appreciated for the flavor it adds to the core game-play loop. Progression with unlocking classes, and through the free battle pass is also a very nice touch.  Are there drawbacks sure, if you don't like rogue-likes the game is probably not for you. You will lose a lot. Matchmaking and difficulty scaling could be much improved on. I would love to have a friends only mode that did not just cap my party size at what ever my party size is going into the game so friends could join late. But it is 1.0, and for a 1.0, I could not be happier with the game. A big group rogue-like

_childDocuments_.review: Summary/Update III: It's been months and the devs haven't addressed the issues plaguing this game. The playerbase has dwindled, gameplay is still stale, and we've received more microtranscations and cosmetics than we have meaningful improvements, additions, or changes.Stay far, far away from this one.Update II: Patch 1.10 just launched, about a month after the previous patch. Bug fixes are great, but the only notable gameplay changes made the game more tedious by making Jotunns even more powerful (They already had some absurd exponential ehp scaling & one shot you about an hour and a half into a run) as well as making it impossible to leave your base after day 15 in Saga mode without the town being overwhelmed. For those running the meta classes, builds, runes, and strat with speedrunning, nothing changes. For those that like to take the game slow, try for longer Saga runs, or use off meta gear, the game just got more difficult, tedious, or outright impossible. Really strange direction for balance changes; instead of rebalancing the game so that most players don't use the exact same overpowered things and are instead encouraged to find their own enjoyable playstyle, they instead nerfed the options that weren't overpowered while trimming away at ways to play the game. Update I: As a note, we've got a patch about a week and a half after the game's launch that was very promising - many community complaints are being addressed, quality of life improvements, and bug fixes. The developer's grasp of the game, community feedback, and how to handle it moving forward appears to be very promising, although the game is still a rough experience overall. I'm doubling down on this review; it's currently rough, but I expect this game to be a gem after a few months of patches, possibly a season or two out.Tribes of Midgard has many problems. It's a promising, gorgeous game and can be fun, but at the moment it's buggy, frustrating, and extremely punishing. Overall, I'd suggest waiting for a few months and then checking back in to see where the game is at. For a more detailed look into the game;Gameplay wise, Tribes of Midgard is very similar to Don't Starve - featuring day/night cycles, seasons, and resource gathering - with Diablo styled hack n' slash combat. Exploration is pretty satisfying. Biomes are diverse and interesting and the game captures a fun gameplay loop, although the first hour of every game is always slow and repetitive as players scramble to mine enough stone, wood, & ore to build a quarry. Combat is a basic hack and slash. Actions are queued up and most attacks animations are fairly lengthy, so dodging and blocking are massively unreliable, it's always more consistent to just eat hits and spam potions. At least, that's the case until enemies start one shotting you. Abilities are tied to weapons, with higher tier weapons having access to more abilities, and different weapons typically having different abilities with some overlap. Classes are honestly a joke. Warden and Seer are the two best by far largely for their quality of life and strong support abilities, Warrior is moderate for having extra mana to boost their most powerful attacks, and everything else is lackluster. Skill trees are also almost all filler - +10% damage with swords, +25% durability with shields, +20% thunder efficiency, etc. It's a total miss, as are the game's secondary build system, runes. You literally just run the strongest damage boosting ones you can find because they're random drops, otherwise you pick up ones that increase resource gain or provide hp regen. Many are borderline useless; increasing damage explosive jars deal by 50% when jars are already a bigger threat to you than to enemies, making you move 20% faster while overheating even though you should be circumventing overheating, exploding when you die, etc. This is the most rogue-like element we have, with runes functioning similar to items, but it's still not very close thanks to their rarity and 5 (or 6 on warden) rune cap per player.Weaponry is wildly unbalanced. Bows are clunky, hammers are unwieldy, and shields are too slow to use. This leaves swords and axes which is what nearly everyone uses. There are also five damage types - physical, ice, fire, void, and thunder. Thunder is the best by far though - it does more damage to the creatures that attack your camp every night, the most dangerous of the Jotunns, and most generic bandits while very few enemies resist it - so everyone just uses thunder axes & swords. These weapons also generally scale better with the more powerful damage boosting runes anyway, so even less reason to try using off meta weapons.Scaling is an issue. Every night you defend your base. In solo play, you can ignore this except for bloodmoons, and things are generally not too difficult. However, this game has a tradeoff; fewer people makes combat easier in exchange for increasing the amount of gathering that needs to be done by any individual person. In multiplayer, you have to fight tooth and nail to survive. Enemy hp & spawnrates scale with players, so night quickly becomes difficult with higher player counts, shaving away the limited time you have to complete the game. Jotunns also have scaling hp & armor, meaning by the 4th or 5th Jotunn in saga mode, they're going to take 10+ minutes of constant hitting to kill it. Also, they'll one shot you even with the best armor, so have fun with that.Bugs abound. Interactions randomly getting stuck, WASD keys no longer working, block no longer working, items being unrepairable even with the correct amount of souls, invincible enemies, attack hitboxes that don't look like they'd hit but they do anyway, random pieces of geometry in the terrain like a tiny board on the ground hindering movement, maps not rendering, the list goes on. Many of these massively interrupt the flow of gameplay, and from my experience, I regularly see multiple of these every run.Quality of life. Gear breaks quickly, and you'll need to stop mid boss fight multiple times to repair gear. Yggdrasil's health  slowly drains slows over time, for some reason. Enemies can hit you from off the screen, some of which attacks deal massive damage. You can't animation cancel your attacks, making dodging or blocking difficult if not impossible for faster attacks. Water instantly kills you, even if you can see it's literally only a few inches deep. Building is a clunky nightmare and everybody avoids using it at every chance they can. UI is clearly made for console, doesn't use space efficiently, lacks hotkeys, and has a painful ~0.5 second delay between inputs. Broken items won't be manually requipped after repairing them, even if the slot they fit into is empty. The Bifrost encourages players to bail on their team instead of fighting difficult battles. Achievements in the game encourage randoms to essentially grief by bailing from the game early, stealing from resource chests, etc. Do you see a pattern?The game has plenty of issues to iron out. It's still a blast, but many of the design choices or lack thereof so far massively hinder the experience. It's a shame - this game has some very interesting boss designs, a gorgeous art style, and is genuinely fun when the game hits its stride. Unfortunately, it fumbles along the way.

The game is easy with just basic communication, but nearly impossible without game knowledge and organization. Matchmaking was incredibly frustrating after launch, but now the meta has stabilized and it's a much more consistent experience. A lot of people make comparisons to Dark Souls or Valheim, but I think it actually feels more like FTL: Faster than Light or XCOM: Enemy Unknown weird as that sounds. Won't click with everyone but it's relatively cheap and well worth a look. Better with controller.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this is not a game you buy to play by yourself. It only costs $20 because to truly enjoy the game you and 3-4 other friends are going to buy it. The tutorial is a little... okay?? There are very important aspects of the game that the tutorial does not encourage you to do. Pros:1. Playing with a dedicated group for the 2+ hour experience is great, communication is key and with it defeating the saga boss proves to be much easier than just matchmaking into 10 randos who want to farm Jotunn last-hits for the achievement. 2. Resources. Crafting everything requires you to go to increasingly difficult areas to farm for the mats you need. Building everything requires easily wasted materials, which adds a level of thinking to the game. 3. Jars. Almost every treasure camp is littered with jars that make it so any player with a tier 1 sword can walk in swinging and walk away with whatever was in the chest. 4. Runes. Nott for Speed go BrrrrrrCons:1. Ever played Halo? Ever gotten your character a little wet. Enough said.2. Knockback. So you need a resource next to said water. Dodge roll incorrectly away from an enemy, Halo. Enemy hits you, Halo. You try to walk and sometimes bug into sliding near infinitely along an edge and into water, Halo.3. The weapons. Every weapon type has a clear pick for what is the best. Hammer = Fire, Axe = Thunder, so on. 4. Ice. The frozen gear is by far the hardest to obtain, and unless you're playing for fun in the forever siege, not worth it. The mountain area is an easier clear, less temp. threat, and the avenue to get crucial materials for end game, such as gold and hideout fragments. 5. Animations. The jotunn are honestly less threatening than a pack of wolves to a player with the bow starting kit 5 minutes in. This however, does not mean that you can time them like darksouls bosses. The chaos jotunn has a special move that makes 3 Aoe's. Don't let yourself be fooled, the circle does not need to be visible at first for it to damage you, and depending on the amount of players, kill you. Assuming this is a bug, this probably isn't final game design. But yeah, the game is very fun, I've played quite a bit of it in my free time. The shop is okay, golden horns are a weird currency, but use them right and you'll always end a game with more than when you started. I'd recommend this game to people, and have gotten a few people to buy into it as well. Will you play it for months, maybe? Will you regret your purchase, certainly not.

There's an almost none existent active skill system as there's only 1 per weapon. The skills are bland.Classes: Just your standard classes with a small passive tree that simply does +x% to this and that. Its mediocreProcedural maps: the map generated by placing linking RNG generated zone tiles together. But its mediocre, every map is the same thing but just in a slight different layout.Multiplayer is just a go off on your own experience, slay a big guy that does a couple AoE's and defend the village at night.Tower defense: Just in the bare minimum. Build couple gates, couple towers, maybe a funnel. that's it.Also: In game real currency item shop.This game feels like a pile of systems thrown together that one way or another many systems are just parasitic game design to another system. _childDocuments_.review: A fantastic co-op game if you don't expect it to be the same as Diablo or something like that. It is really a challenging game with resource management and IMPORTANTLY require all players need to communicate. Therefore, I think that the problem of the game is the lack of tutorial and the matchmaking system. The tutorial do not provide you enough information to really understand what you really need to do in the game to achieve the goal since it only show you the basic movement and how to interact with the environment of the game. Otherwise, if players are familiar with survival game such as Don't Starve, the tutorial literally do not help you at all. For the game with so many activities that are mandantory to engage in such as quest, building construction, limited-time events, explore hideouts, fighting bosses and creatures at night, gathering, etc.. they really need to make the tutorial LONGER and MORE INFORMATIVE. For the matchmaking system, personally I think that it can't provide players a good experience with other players when playing the game. Literally it is 10 random people without clear purpose like end the saga mode, go to bilfrost as fast as possible, surviving to 15 days,... and due to that the players in matchmaking could never enjoy and explore the game until the last moment or going in the intended way of this game is to COOPERATE WITH OTHER PEOPLE AS A TRIBE. Simply, the matchmaking is bad because people don't understand what they REALLY need to do which come from the tutorial at the first place when they get in the game didn't give them ENOUGH INFORMATION TO KNOW WHAT TO DO! Well, those are the 2 points that make me think that could heavily affect the experience of players at first try. But thanks to Discord, players can find other people to play with in there and communicate through voice chat and guide each other to fulfill the purpose of the game. And when  you can overcome the 2 big-ass obstacles that stop you from enjoying the game. Then, this is a wonderful roguelike survival/ tower defense game with Viking concept where you can have fun with friends/family. DEFINITELY WORTH A TRY AND FOR THE PRICE IF THEY ARE GOING TO UPDATE AND TACKLE THE PROBLEMS OF THE GAME
