_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. Another Viking Survival game to occupy my time while I'm perpetually waiting for Valheim updates to finally arrive? What could possibly go wrong?* Little continuity - you die and start from scratch over and over and over, at least on single player.* There is a "real money" shop in the game that has a mix of cosmetic and pay-to-win items in it - you can get sparse amounts of the currency without paying* The store has a rotating limited selection of items that are fairly important - meaning you need to log on a bunch to catch the item you want...* Last point on the store - it feels like a watered down version of the horrendously unfair pricing schemes phone games use. You probably won't bankrupt yourself on this game, but if you think you will get far with just the $20 you spent up front, think again.* Your character can literally drown in a puddle.* Upgrading building seems like an afterthought. Maybe later in the game it's easier to get resources, but in all of my attempts I rare got enough resources to upgrade more than one building before I was overwhelmed by enemies and died.* The day/night cycle seems superficial at best. Most games I barely survive til the 4th day, which doesn't allow for much exploration during the day or much novelty to the tower defense mode that occurs at night. * The game would be better without the tower defense mode at night - it happens too often, is predictable and repetitive, and interrupts the best aspects of the game (exploring, gearing up, fighting giants, etc.).* You have to build platforms, ramps, etc. to reach certain areas... what is this, Fortnite? * There are too many mechanics squeezed into one game without enough polish on any one of them. This game is like a mix of Diablo, Fortnite, Valheim, Tower Defense, and some crappy freemium phone game, all rolled up into a confusing mess.Bottom Line: 5/10 - While the game is generally free of bugs and supported by the developer, it is fundamentally flawed in its design and would need a major rework to feel remotely rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is packed full of potential, and very close to being great.  BUT.. right now it's "Don't Starve meets a hardcore MMO raid".  The 'pioneers' will die a lot while finding tactics which work. Later, players will have difficulty unless they spend a long time to learn tactics and roles. Ultimately, successful runs will rarely be achieved by pickup groups, far more by pre-organised teams.  With some re-balancing, I think the game could be great.  At the moment, the balancing makes the game feel as esoteric and time-pressured as Don't Starve.  Each run takes maybe 2.5 hours, max 10 people per run.  If enough of them don't know what to do, the run will fail.  There is no mechanic for replacing those who drop out.  With that said, the game is very enjoyable to play, and there is a lot of re-playability.  If the balancing were changed from "hardcore MMO raid" difficulty to "casual pickups can do it most times but might miss some rewards" difficulty I would be really enjoying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore all these negative comments about the "fortnight like battle pass" and "crappy servers." This game is solid and fun in groups. The servers are fine for a game that has only been out for less than a week, and the so called battle pass is a season based level system not a pass. You do NOT have to pay for the pass and you do NOT have to pay for premium currency. There are legendary skins in the store that you can grab with a premium currency, but they effect nothing about the game and the premium currency is not used on recipes that effect the game. The store itself, for the most part,  uses a currency called golden horns. These horns are earned by completing games and extracting and can be spent on recipes for new weapons as well as top tier items while playing games. YOU CANNOT BUY THIS CURRENCY. you have to earn it. As for the game play, it is a fairly unique game. It combines aspects of survival games (Such as having to run around and gather resources to build better items to be able to do more stuff) with almost tower defense style games (since ultimately you are attempting to defend the world tree from enemies hell bent on destroying it.) while also trying to attack and kill bosses while exploring a randomly generated map.  My only real complaint about this game is that, as of writing, there is not a whole lot of unique items that you can build. there is only a few sets of armor and maybe 5 types of each weapon. It has hours of game play in it, but after you find your favorite weapon type the game becomes a little redundant. Overall the game is a lot of fun if you are playing with a group of friends, but hard if you play by yourself.  Outside of wanting unique items and more build paths than it has, this game is solid and promises to update every two months. I don't think it's exactly an award winning game yet, but I am also yet to find any game like it, and I honestly believe that in time, and with additional game modes added, this game will be one that I could sink hundreds of hours into. Until that time, I think that this game is loads of fun and feels satisfying to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Review might contain minor spoilers!!I will first start by saying that my review isn't a straight no. I am though heavily plunging to the no each time i play this game. I have 8 hours in this game and i am already bored. I find absolutely no reason to continue playing the game as it is.My experience came strictly from solo play-through. This game feels like a roguelite base defence survival game with no actual progression that will make each run easier. You are forced in a loop with the upper limit the 16th day which then you are forced to start anew. Each time you finish a run you are rewarded xp that unlock things in a free battle-pass. Unlocks are cosmetics, premium, runes and the semi premium currency which is Golden Horns.Runes are in game drops considered as perks that help your run. (you can have up to 4 in a run).Cosmetics have absolutely no use apart from making your character look more shiny.Game-play wise the game offer no excitement. Each run is the same. EACH run. You drop in the world, during the day you farm resources to craft a pick-axe and an axe and then farm some more to build better weapons. and then farm some more to build better armour and then you farm some more to build better weapons and armour. Defend the occasional Jotun that arrives.At night you have to defend your village from Helthings which can be handled by ncp's during the first nights if you spend some souls to upgrade them.Now comes the issue. As the game progresses and the Endless Winter approaches the weather gets colder days become smaller and nights become longer making a solo player's life miserable. You have so much little time to do anything before the Helthings arrive and eventually have to restart.They have to at least include some form of progression. Something that makes your runs easier. Increase the Day/Night cycle the lower number of players you have and decrease the resources needed to build defences and the various mines.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A fun game for casual gamers that dont want to spend much time or dollar on games like Valheim and / or only plan on playing this as a group of friends.We bought this game with a group of 6 people for our annual LAN. We were specifically looking for cheap, easy to learn, coop/ PVE style games. We really enjoyed the Genre of RPG Tower Defense (like Dungeon Defenders or the good old WC3 mods), so we went for Tribes and Midgard - and got exactly what we were looking for. This game does not require any skill whatsoever. You'll learn what your class can do, which weapon to use and strengths & weaknesses of the bosses during your first run. And without looking up strategies online, you'll need like 3-4 runs before figuring out how to beat the first boss easily (if you are an experienced group, maybe earlier). After that, the game lacks another level of challenge, as the other bosses are quite similar once you know what to do in Midgard.Positive:- easy accessible: this game is cheap (in sale!) and you can play it on any kind of computer, so even your reallife friends with their office laptops will be able to join your party.- easy to learn: no depth means you'll learn this game in no time and even the noobiest reallife mate will be able to have fun and feel like he is contributing to beating the game.- fun game mode: it's the classic "gather a group of friends and beat the evil boss while hordes of monsters try to destroy your base" type of game and those just always work.- classic theme: while going with the frequently used theme of nordic mythology isn't that creative, it is still fun to choose your favorite class, craft medival weapons and beat up monsters Negative:- as mentioned, this game has no depth. Once you know how to reach and beat the bosses, you'll never have a hard time doing so again. Also, lots of stuff added to the game (items, food, many weapons) are not at all necessary to win.- few updates: we played the game in March/ April and recently looked what's changed til then - not one single update in almost a year.-graphics, gameplay, UI... this game feels more like a mobile game than a title you'd be willing to pay 20€ for.Do I recommend it? Not to everyone. If you wanna dive deep into a world, if you are looking for solo player action, if you have an expensive rig you wanna use to the limit or if you wanna challenge yourself - this game is not for you.But if you have a group of friends that is not necessarily great at videogames, but wants to spend an hour or five having fun with friends while during holiday season, you will not regret spending 6-7€ for a game like this.

The community have given the devs alot of help and ideas to save the game but they don't seem to take it in and actually use the information properly. Instead they throwing out the updates in almost a naked condition and focuses on the in game shop alongside with very little new content from time to time. Also a little bird showed me some internal talks about the build limits and it seems its a techical issue from the dev side so i guess they don't know how to fix?[ORIGINAL FENRIR/SERPENT SAGA]You can complete the game in 30 minutes or less. Most people done at 10 hours.Its good but would not recommend to buy until the game gets more overall content. At its current state it just doesn't deliver. On top of that its very hard to say what the game IS since its a weird mix of basic boring tower defense, basic speedrunning and boss battles. You can choose to play survival or saga mode and i will explain more in detail about these and why you should avoid buying it so you don't have to suffer bad decisions like i did!Lets clear up Saga mode wich is about speedrunning to kill several bosses in its current state.1. Most equipment, gear and items are worthless because you only need few early game items.2. You get to play around 2 hours until the world you joined or created becomes endless "tower defense"3. Low player count for multiplayer makes it hard to find decent lobbies.4. Building basically pointless since you can progress completly without it.5. Classes are boring. Sure they add to the game but need big overhaul. Lets clear up Survival mode (if we can call it that) wich is about building, progress and endless fighting.1. Building system is meh and you can't place how many pieces you like since there is a limit. (really low limit)2. Late game bosses doesn't respawn. (they now do and scale from lvl 1-10)3. Not real survival. Hunger doesn't exist, Nothing will attack your starting area. 4. This mode is basically just grind simulator that lets you kill 4 bosses with same animations and attack patterns that offers no real challenge.5. When you reach late game there is NOTHING to do except grinding and waiting for bosses to respawn. (you can now build a farm but it costs building pieces so no lmao. Also you can defend a few areas every 15 minutes but actually never have seen more dull invasion event in my life).Overall problems with the modes and game.1. Communication is hard because the game does not deliver a polished communication system. Only basic voice chat and text. Emotes don't really matter since nobody will look at the chat anyway.2. Inventory and chest systems is tedious and slow.3. A whole lot of bugs to be found everywhere! (Now with graphical issues!)4. AI is not great wich makes combat somewhat boring. Just attack, dodge repeat. Mostly click and tank repeat.5. In game challenges are not very great and for the most part too easy.I played this game in closed beta and later i bought it after the official release. I noticed not much been added and mostly cosmetics and some bosses you don't even need to do. Now that i have 100 hours + i regret buying it.Short said: Don't buy unless its sale and you happen to be very bored cause all your friends went out to drink and you have to be home sick.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game but missing some things to hit its potential. It has two gameplay modes; Saga & Survival.Saga has a somewhat tight time constraint -- Days last ~10 minutes including nighttime, when you have to play defense for a tree. If the tree dies, game ends and you're penalized on rewards. At first it's a balancing act between gathering materials for gear/grinding levels and nighttime defense. Eventually, though, bosses spawn somewhere on the map and slowly make their way towards your tree. Then you add dealing with the boss before it becomes an issue to the balancing act. On top of this, nights get progressively longer, taking more of the 10 minutes, until around day 14, where it is always nighttime.It gets frantic when you try to do the "Saga Quest" on top of all of this, which are the world bosses that require other prep to attempt (the frost wolf, the world worm -- featured on the art).The other gamemode is Survival which is getting reworked to be more of your typical open world survival craft on August 16. Currently it's just like Saga mode but sometime after day 14, it stops being night all the time. The rework to this mode is a welcome change.Anyway, there's just some questionable design decisions that hold the game back. Some classes are vastly underpowered or so specific in their use it's hard to justify their existence. Or, like the Berserker, their entire identity is their starting skill (+weapon speed) with largely useless fluff around it, and even detrimental fluff that actively reduces the class effectiveness. More synergy between skills in a class would be nice as some skills just do not make sense.The tutorial is pretty ass, though it's not hard to get how the game works if you've played a video game in the last 20 years.Still a fun enough game, I'd probably never play it solo, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Tribes of Midgard

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun with some interesting mechanics but...As a team based game that relies on communication and coordination to succeed this doesn't work. The premise is simple enough, each day you set out to gather supplies to prepare for the onslaught at night, when night falls you return to base to protect it. Explore the map, find valuable resources, bring them back to the base and share them with your tribe. It sounds great, and it is... if you are playing in a group with your friends. With up to a lobby of 10 people you can get the whole gang together.However, when it comes to public lobbies it all falls apart. People horde the supplies, don't come back at night and rarely group up to fight the wave bosses. This may improve as more people learn the basics (which the tutorial only scratches the surface of.) But as of now, I would say get it if you've got at least three other people to play it with.P.S.The tutorial doesn't teach you about selecting a class. Did you know that you can push B in order get there quickly? Alternatively it is found in your inventory window ( i ) by default. It doesn't teach you about building the town gates, or preparing for Fenrir. Nor does it teach you about repairing the Quary, Farm, or Lumber Mill - all of which are necessary for the end game and keeping your base alive.

_childDocuments_.review: I've preordered Tribes of Midgard two years ago, only to request a refund upon its atrocious launch. The marketing team, in an attempt to ride the Valheim hype, tried to brand the game as a survival, which it was not. Instead, what we got was a lackluster roguelike tower defense game, leading to everyone being disappointed. The joke "Tribes of Mid" became so prevalent that people adopted the name unironically in the forums for a while.That said, the developers have somehow fixed this mess to an extent. The inclusion of a genuine survival mode encouraged me into repurchasing the game. The game is still very far from perfect. The UI remains abysmal, like a bad mobile game, and the overall game design feels convoluted and directionless. It's as if they spent their entire budget on the cool animations and misguided marketing efforts. However, the game now finally delivers on its original promise: being a mid Valheim clone. And an enjoyable one.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely repetitive and lacking content, should be F2P, not 20 bucks. It has Micro transactions too. It looks, feels. plays, and markets as a free to play game. It takes more than 2 hours to really get a feel of how the game progression and reward systems work. The actual game itself - music, artwork, combat, items, etc. Really isn't BAD. Just has no real depth. Kinda feels like you are playing an open beta. After you finish playing it a few times, you are left wanting more. But there is nothing more except cosmetic micro transactions and "Sagas" (Seasons that will add content-another live service)Public games can be hosted or joined in matchmaking. Very minimal bugs from what I've seen. (Once, a boss launched right when a day changed and it was bugged, just standing there so I punched it till it died. lol)Can be very enjoyable with friends, but the pub matches are just like any other game, most people do their own thing and it hinders your group.Over all, I'd say 6/10. If it was F2P I'd probably go 8/10. Just not worth 20 bucks. Maybe 10 or 15....I've taken poops with more content than this game.

That's not really a pro or a con.Attacking is left click then a few right clicks when you have left clicked enough to get your weapons ability. There seems to only be one per weapon with slight variances depending on the tier of weapon. IE: Going from ground smash to ground smash that sends out shock wave. Basically, the fighting is boring and uninspired. Face-tanking and swinging.,Now you may ask why I haven't refunded, and the answer is because my girlfriend likes this game. _childDocuments_.review: There are other reviews that explains the whole deal, for me the lack of depth in the combat is the main reason I asked for a refund.Here's some other frustrating parts:- Equipment breaks very quickly, forcing you to travel back to town to repair them, and it costs a lot of souls(main resource), the problem here is the combat is heavily depending on your gear, you better wish there is a travel point near by to get you back to town asap, or your damage just drops completely.- There is a rune item to travel back to town wherever you are, you most likely would use this when the mobs attack on night time.  However, the cooldown for the rune is too long, or I should say the day/night cycle time is too short, you can only use this rune once in 2 days, but going back and forth from the town is a constant thing, this makes exploring the world extremely frustrating, as you often have to make sure you have a travel point near by, or just waste all the precious time on walking back.- The pacing is bad, you barely have enough time to finish anything in a day.  If you're wondering around figuring out what you should do, you already are losing since the difficulty is always scaling up.  You need to speedrun the game to survive, but it's not like Risk or Rain where speedrunning is a tradeoff between difficulty and better gear.- It's heavily coop based.  The game is designed to be played by multiplayer, the resources needed to survive through the early game is just too much for one person.This game definitely has potential, but the current state is just not enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this.  I really did.  It's a gorgeous game, the artwork and setting is superb.  The music and sound effects are on point.  The controls are very, very responsive.  It runs very well, even in Linux+Proton.But after 45 minutes I found myself going, "meh, what next?"I'm sure there's more to the game, but it felt like just a chore to run the shallow loop of "gather/craft/repair" and "fight bad guys at night trying to shoot the tree."  And then a Jotunn arrives, which is basically a big and slow high-hp damage soak that spawns mobs and does AoE attacks.  Again, absolutely great artwork and design, but mechanically it felt sterile and basic.  It felt like the Kingdom games a little except here you do the fighting and you have to repair your gear (every five seconds) on top of managing your defenses.It felt like they spent the most time coming up with the gathering/harvesting/crafting dynamic and let slide combat.  The overarching mechanics of the game just felt too basic and rushed to me.  If someone told me this was a mobile game ported to PC, I'd believe it.  It lacked dynamism and literally everything in it made me ask myself, "Why am I doing this?  Why am I still playing this?  Why does everything feel like it's all just busywork?"Refund requested.

_childDocuments_.review: At this time I do not recommend this for most people... The reason is this following issues, ALL affecting how well you can travel, and how smooth/immersive your gameplay is. Clipping/Movement/Map hitboxes:- It seems like at least after 11 hours of straight survival mode the map has a lot of spots where you will get stuck, slowed, bumped, or staggered on. This happens mostly on wooden objects in camps, diving down the hillsides, and other areas of land with any extra texture to them. Honestly this seems like an issue with the objects they made for the map and their hitboxes, I could be wrong, but it is very present, for most people it will be a game killer. - The ocean is no exception to movement problems, your boat will clip on nothing, the rocks and land her actually is not a problem. Your boat will have a lot of issues turning in certain parts of the map, very similar to what you would see if this was clipping on land, but in the ocean you cannot see what you are catching on. The land its very clear that some of the wood plank objects etc are just poorly made, its always the same ones. So yes on land and on sea you are sort of screwed here a bit with movement which will kill the game for a lot of people who might already be struggling with the other glaring issue of solo play. In my opinion the solo mode is not a problem, I have done just fine solo in survival, but Saga it is still a big problem and you likely need NPCs, more traps, or your pet to be able to fight. I will keep playing the game for now, but I hope to see some improvements which likely will involved a big overhaul of how they are creating maps. There is a lot to like about the game:- The performance is solid with uncapped frames on Ultra settings.- The progression feels pretty good until about the 2nd or 3rd boss where I feel like the extra travel starts killing the steady progress, and you start to see the map become more an more repetitive.- The idea behind the game is solid, lore is basic, but there. - For weaponsl; so far I have tested swords, axes, and bows, all work well. The main issue is again maybe a map issue many enemies, and your own weapons can cross multiple levels. Example: I can swing my sword and hit a giant 2 platform heights above me. They can also hit you through the floor. Seems like a map issue again. If the devs commit and follow through on fixing the core issues with the map and hitboxes of objects would definitely want to support the game more through their shop which is not overbearing. Thumbs down until we see some changes or a good plan/response.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game, I really do. There is a great game with potential. But there are quite a few systems that make it horrible to play with randoms and sometimes friends. The inability to drop runes only destroy them is high up there, nodes that drop an exclusive night mat which often encourages people to not help defend the base at night. The ability to clean out the communal storage and sell all of it for souls. Systems like this encourage people often to play selfishly they are more reluctant to put stuff in the communal storage or defend the base at night or just ignore a good rune cause it doesn't fit their build and accidentally pick it up cause most players spam pickup to pick up mats.The quest system is rough. Odd that you take a quest to go to a remote quest giver to get the quest. Y cant the quest giver be in town. Or you start the main part of the quest from town. Several times i have traveled to a quest giver to get a quest to kill wolves and realize i killed the majority of the wolves on the map getting to the quest giver. The durability of the bow is pitiful what bow breaks in less than 100 shots? ranged combat is also odd and often doesn't shoot where you are aiming with aim assist on or off. These are minor issues but having an in-game store with weapon recipes behind a rotating store is also a negative although i appreciate that you cant get the recipes with cash. This game feels early access and has a $20 box price with an in-game store with cosmetics which is a shame cause i would love more gear in the base game and especially if some looked like the cosmetics also only one legendary of each weapon type is a very limited selection.I see the potential of this game an arpg where a group of people pursue own goals and defend a common base and aid each other is a great idea. The cell shading artstyle is a timeless asthetic. But playing with randoms is often a negative experience and several game systems are detrimental to cooperative play.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent quite a few hours playing this game, but overall I wouldn't recommend it in its current form. It's just majorly flawed in its multiplayer design:- Why is there a Solo mode if even when doing everything "right" you are just gonna get stomped and swarmed anyway and finishing this game in Solo is virtually impossible. (Mind you I am experienced player and a very efficient too when it comes to getting gear upgrades and scavenging biomes). It just doesn't matter because the 4th Jotun will have so much HP you will need to spend literally DAYS in game to beat it before it reaches your settlement, while also having to complete events, defend base at night, perform upgrades and repairs. Just impossible to juggle all these activities for a single player so why is there a Solo mode?- Completely unbalanced for 2 people. I wanted to play the game with just my GF and not with some randoms. We are virtually unable to get past the 4th jotun while constantly juggling tasks and defending base. In rare case you are able to make a super effective weapons for the 4th jotun, it might be possible without as much of a hassle but then again: Why bother.- Game difficulty simply doesn't scale well with the amount of players. Too few players and you won't be able to even reach fenrir - but on the other hand have a 9 people team with 3 people who know what they are doing? You can just sit back and relax because they can just play the game for you - it's that easy- Game lacks balance when it comes to weapons, classes and skills. Two handed hammers are far inferior to one handed weapons that tend to have more powerful mana abilities anyway. Seer and Warder are head and shoulders above all the other classes. Extremely hard to unlock berserker is absolute total garbage of a class compared to what it requires to get it. Generally any class without some form of a heal is weaker and every game you basically have to rush Norn Axe just because it's that good and provides decent healing- Bows feel bad to use and lack the impact of arrows.- Walking away from an attack is literally better than trying to dodge it. Dodging is clunky and just feels awful and most of the time you can react quicker and cover more ground just by walking away- Gameplay loop is boring and lack of enemy variations is disgusting. Once you fight the jotuns and fenrir at least once you basically know their moveset by heart and only way for you to die in that fight is because of poor dodge mechanics or simply due to enemy glitching out and suddenly spinning in your direction to somehow catch you in the aoe but overall the combat is just boring. You hit the boss or bigger enemy few times and you walk away for its super slow and super telegraphed attacked that it does every 5 seconds by the clock.- Level 10 is max character level despite it being achieved long before even reaching fenrir portal. Why is it max 10. If I am able to gather more experience due to my efficiency, let me spend more skillpoints which usually just give you a little more versatility like shock damage + or dark damage +- Bugs bugs bugs. Game crashed several times for me. And about 3 times my character animation just froze and I couldn't attack - i could just switch weapons. Had to leave the world and reenter.- Leaving the world and re-entering basically acts like a recall but is free. You get thrown next to your settlement.- People afking in worlds just to unlock seer.- I killed fenrir few times now and tried every class. I don't feel there is any reason for me to continue playing. Every match looks virtually the same: Quickly get a little better weapon. Kill some Linorms. Craft a weapon with means of healing. blah blah blah. Game might have randomized world but overall it's pretty much always the same and the events are always the same and there is nothing that can surprise you anymore after you played it a couple of times. I know there's a meta progression, but do you really think I wanna spend several hours per run doing everything almost exactly the same just to unlock a cosmetic or a rune I will never use?I would hold of with buying this game - it REALLY needs better balance and more content.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game. Overall it's similar to "Don't starve together", but less mature at the moment. I like the combination of tower defense, crafting, camp and dungeon raiding on top of the rogue-like mechanic. I also like that the weapon is not universal and you can't craft something useful in any situation till the end of game. Also the limit of the character level is great thing, since you need to combine your skills with the weapon and runes.But there are points that can be improved to unlock the potential of the game advantages:- Mobs and bosses currently are covered by two weapon tipes: lightning and void. Other types are not so useful. So the camp spawn could be more varied from the elemental PoV.- BOSS attacks and timings a pretty similar, so this also may have some diversity to make the game less straight forward- Mob spawn usually is too limited to grind and craft enough armor the big squad- After began to experience a shortage of new weapons and items. And again variety  of weapons are not coherent to mobs much.- Lot of issues related to glitchy controls and lose of controls completely- Why the hell does a treasure map need to be added to inventory and not just read upon activation?- Survival is nice, but useless, the only reason to play it are few achievements that player needs to open a weapon. Why don't you combine it with something else?Just an idea that comes from one of my friends:Use survival mode to grind building resources that afterwards can be used in Saga mode. For now it only makes sense to play the survival mode once and forget about it forever.- Finally: Game becomes boring after 2 days of playing the fresh update.- A lot problems with control, that simply ruins the gameplace.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, kinda mediocre. It's just BARELY serviceable. My problem is I played V-Rising before this which by comparison has such super fluid gameplay and actually challenging bosses that this game just sorta... Feels flat. It's bosses are far too easy (You can just stand in front of them and smash away without a brain cell) its combat feels hyper clunky because every attack either moves you slightly forward or slightly backward in a weird jutter-like way. And the base building is absolutely terrible. The UI for it barely works and small things like if you want to dismantle a crafting station you also dismantle the wall and the floor beneath it. Oh, and a consistent bug means walls roofs doors and windows constantly vanish from the game only to re-appear when you travel away and back again. Meaning your bases walls and defenses can sometimes just not be there. This game is V-Rising, the exact same gameplay. Except significantly worse. It's a "fine" game on its own, but I would have a far cleaner and more interesting gameplay experience just going back to V-rising. At least midguard's color pallet is nice though, V-rising is pretty much permanently GREY.

_childDocuments_.review: This game should still be early access, it has a REALLY long way to go. It's also deceptively shallow. It's actually fun for roughly 3 hours until it's too late to do a Steam refund, so be prepared for that. This feels like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mobile game ported to console and then re-ported to PC. And there's nothing roguelike about it, you can loot and craft the same ♥♥♥♥ every single game. The only random thing about it is which jotun you'll get, and honestly that barely matters either.Here is a short list of things I hate about this game:Item durability has no warning, your weapon just breaks and then you're punching things like an idiot. It needs a repair all button. Bow durability in particular is comically low, it feels like it breaks every five minutes. These are the simplest mechanics that could have been ripped off straight from Diablo 1 from TWENTYFIVE YEARS AGO, that had a better town experience than this. Honestly just scrap the durability system at this point, it just sucks some fun out of the game. This game also needs an in-game clock and better notifications for events. For Pete's sake PLEASE ADD SOME SOUND NOTIFICATIONS! If a jotun is like a minute from walking into the base, you better be putting up giant flashy things on the screen and blowing war horns and ♥♥♥♥, because those dudes will just walk right in there and kill your tree in like 12 seconds and you barely even get a text popup about it. Tell me that nighttime attacks start at 9PM and show me a clock and I'll be there on time, but otherwise I'm busy doing these lame quests and looting.And another thing! This game is incredibly shallow. It's easy to believe there's more to it at first, you can get a little lost in all the mechanics, but once you figure that out, almost every game will play out exactly the same way and it's not difficult. People are already speed running it in 3 days game time. Combat is clunky, bows are stupid and only shoot half a screen, you have to zoom the camera out like 5% for some reason every time you start the game!? Just make it a fixed camera at that point, that amount of zoom is worthless. Go to the Land of Pools zone first, kill/loot some stuff and craft a lightning axe on day one, and the game is pretty much over already.Oh and how about not letting monsters camp the shrines? Nobody needs a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dragon thing just hanging out at the fast travel portals. Monster spawning / leashing zones are busted. You can fall into the water SO UNBELIEVABLY EASILY it's crazy. Water is an instant kill. Sometimes you'll even die when you're standing on the shore next to some water. There's no real way to tell how dangerous a monster is until they're killing you, sometimes some really deadly dudes will be right by your starting point. Playing this game feels like work and I hate it. It's such a half assed hack and slash game with poor combat mechanics. It absolutely blows at being a base building and/or tower defense game. RPG elements? Yeah okay buddy! My friends all seem to like it though. So there's that I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: This game shows alot of promise. However since it is out and not EA i kind of have to judge it as a full experience. Now out of my 25 hours of gametime i would say the first 15 was enjoyable and me and some friends managed to beat the game a few times. However after beating this game once you kind of know what to do and beating it again is much much easier. All the rougelite elements kind of die down since you just craft whatever gear you need no problem. The only difficulty is if your seed is bad and thus don't find certain biomes fast enough. Now with their season system and updates i had hoped they could add more to the core experience of the game and expand on the rougelike feelings, maybe add some stuff that might be present on the map or might not be, make certain gear only obtainable through unique materials beyond just completing the bare minimul requirements for unlocking the protal to the final boss anyways. There is just too much repetition in a game that should have a different feel every time you play it. Also survival mode could be cool if more items were present and you could scale further than in the regular mode. But no, you cap out in survival around day 15 if you play decently and from there you will not get stronger at all. Getting to day 100 for the achievment was pain and no fun. and kind of killed my last enjoyment of the game. Maybe next season will bring changes that make this game worth it, but this mid season update does not seem to change anything that impacts the core gameplay loop at all and thus you'll be doing pretty much the exact same thing you've been doing so far except the final boss is different. I would wait for a while and see if the devs add any meaningful content to the game or if they imagine the current gameplay loop is just fine. Either way, if you think beating the game once (taking about the 15 hours atleast for me and my group) is worth 20 dollars, then that first time through is really enjoyable. But you'll soon after find yourself very bored at even the idea of playing it again.

_childDocuments_.review: I played only 8 hours, I didn't feel like going further, here's why :Good looking, the ambiance and design are quite nice, but each run felt too repetitive and grindy for my liking. The same upgrades must be done to maximise efficiency, so each run follow the same pattern even if the map is randomly generated. The thrill is in finding the right places to collect and upgrade the Tinker for your tools, the Smith to rush for Nornir Axe and the Quarry for sustain and upgrade the village. Then you can do the rest, meaning grinding to craft the same stuff that do the same thing while the clock is ticking. The only change is your class, that didn't feel that different when you craft the same gear for everyone.Instead of putting a peon at task like in Warcraft 3, so you can enjoy other aspect of the game, here you actually play the peon for quite some time in each run. The first 30 minutes of each run feels awkwardly the same and make the experience tedious.If a run was about 60-90 minutes max, with a lot of different weapons and changing situations/strat, it could be good. In this actual state, I suggest a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm trying really hard to like this game, but it's just not sticking with me. My major issues are:1. Saga mode feels like you're trying to speedrun a game. If you load into the map, explore for a little bit and don't find the biome you need, it's better to just reset your map than to explore and find it. Additionally, dying after spending 15-20 minutes gathering souls can just kill a run.2. Combat feels clunky. The delay after swing/shooting your weapon feels weird, not sure how better to describe it. Rolling/Dodging, doesn't actually dodge attacks, that's only a skill for the Warrior class. With how slow you are after rolling to get back up to full speed, I've learnt it's better to just run and strafe enemy attacks. Bows are extremely underpowered. A T4 Light bow will deal only a quarter of the damage of the T3 Hesir sword.3. The early gameplay loop is the exact same. Scavenging for resources, upgrading your village, etc. It's not entirely bad, but doing the same thing every single time you play really starts to wear you down.4. Matchmaking and multiplayer. Matchmaking is pretty bad at the moment. My friend and I playing together will get matched with someone and have very high ping. Players can't join midgame and when you get a leaver you feel it. Mobs in multiplayer also have far too much health in the early game. We've noticed that with just two people mobs have twice as much HP. One could argue this is fine, but resources are not doubled so pacing gets staggered a bit and if one person doesn't pull their weight for a little bit, the group starts to feel it.What I do like about the game:1. The concept is amazing. Dropping into a randomly generated map, scavenging for resources, and building up a base is fun. I hope the construction side of the game adds to this, there is a ton of potential here.2. Heroes are vastly different which gives a great sense of individuality. There does need to be some tuning done, but unlocking and playing a new class feels rewarding.3. The art style and music are great. With how much time each run takes, it doesn't feel bland and worn out to listen to, even after a few hours.Overall, this game has a ton of great potential, but the gameplay loop is starting to wear me down and with how punishing the game can be at times, it has me in a much more hardcore mindset which is just what I don't want this early in a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Tribes of Midgard is a mix of action RPG and tower defense with a little bit of exploration and roguelike.It's co-op with 1-10 players (yes, it scales the difficulty and you can play solo)It got it's mixed review score from the "the game is not exactly what I wanted it to be, the devs lied to me" crowd.What you get is a light action RPG by day - 8 classes, skill trees, abilities, equipment, dodge rolland a tower defense by night - build gates, towers, resource buildings, upgrade all of them, defend your tree.What you get the whole time is a giant random generated map with different biomes and enemies, filled with dungeons, quests and monster camps (and the big Jötnar)Overall it feels like an oldschool Warcraft 3 custom map.Yes - there is an ingame cash shop for cosmetics and a !free! season pass.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. Chat box: Needs to last longer than a moment so you can read what the person has written. There should be a chat log accessible when you press enter so you can read the last 30 or so player typed comments, but really it should keep a detailed chat log for referencing information. 2. Colour blind options for colour blind players, especially with the cursor.3. Fall damage is insane. You can roll down a ramp from the side and still lose a few hundred HP on the smallest incline. There's a perk to minimise it in atleast the Warrior class but I just don't like overly dramatic fall damage at all so it depends on your preference. 4. Falling into water. Now walking along water edges is awkward and blocky, so that's a reason to avoid it, but the worst part is sometimes you just slide in and instantly die. It happens when you roll near cliff edges too. It is just awkward, not to mention annoying.5. You should be earning more souls.  You should be able to reclaim lost souls ala Dark Souls method.  Actually the whole soul economy just needs a revamp so that you get slightly more. You should not be rolling in souls, but sometimes there's almost no souls to use because you've died and they're gone and if this happens to multiple players well the game gets a little wonky and everyone falls behind. 5.1. Helthings should drop more souls and consistently. It is SO frustrating when the few souls the Helthings drop become stuck above the gate too. Souls should just vacuum to you on their own once they're earned. 6. Enemies are just bloated HP mobs. I'd rather vs extra enemies with normal health than needing 20-40+ clicks on one enemy. It isn't that enjoyable and it makes exploring alone, especially at the start, more a game of ignore enemies than fight them. You can have purple weapons and stacks of health pots and still lose to enemies, which is kinda not fun.7. People leave way too often and way too early, especially with the annoying leave via 10 bifrost challenge. Why would they encourage players to leave early is beyond me. 8. The ability to mute people who do not know how to turn their mics off, have horrible mics, horrible background noise etc.9. Players should be able to join empty slots in all days and be auto levelled to everyone elses average level for the sake of the health and longevity of this games life. People leave and the game is basically ruined.10. I know it is challenging but missing out on trophies where you didn't get the very last hit make no sense because you still could have been there fighting the Jotun/saga boss and doing alot of damage so maybe instead the game should record your % of damage and reward you with a trophy when you do technically help kill it. _childDocuments_.review: It has potential, but the game is really grindy...At first, it is quite enjoyable, but the novelty soon wears off, you cannot jump in the game, only roll, and most of the areas have low ledges that which if you could jump would be better to traverse the map on, but you have to run all the way around to find a ramp and it takes foreverThe things i liked about it:Quirky characters that are quite coolThe nordic theme is really goodThe combat isn't bad, it's actually quite enjoyableThe things i didn't like about it:Healing is very awkward to do in that game, and bases itself on potions mainly, which you can only hold 3 of, each oh which only provides a 3rd of your HP bar, so bosses become a bit tedious to fight solo.The death mechanic is similar to that of Dark Souls, in the sense that when you die, it leaves a recoverable grave for you to loot again (which has a percentage of souls and materials, i think, it isn't quite clear), however, if you fall off an edge, the grave doesnt appear (or appears in the hole in which you fell) and is essentially lost.The game also uses ships, which is quite cool, however, you get a recall stone that lets you return to a sanctuary, and when you travel to another island, you have to leave your boat on a shore and then explore (which is fine), but if you accidentally tap T (the recall stone activation button) after 3 seconds you teleport back to sanctuary... but your boat remains at the other island, thereby forcing you to craft another, and then there are two boats at the island when you travel back (so accidentally tap T, you in essence lose your boat)And finally, there isn't really any good places to build a base in the game... enemies spawn in weird places (more at night too) and will just randomly attack, which i wouldn't mind too much if I could pick a place that is accommodating for different base ideas, and while there is "room" for the bases of choice to be built, there is nothing interesting or cool about the areas that could add flavour to a base (like a cove, rock formations, etc.)The game is certainly well made with the mix of genres and things and it is good to see a game try a different approach than the copy-and-paste things you see these days, but it feels like the game is very inhospitable to solo play.Death in the game isn't too much of an issue, it is just the right amount of penalising that it needs to be, but i feel it severely disadvantages solo players and they could work on their healing mechanics (because I don't want to stand still for a long time trying to recover HP with rune effects, you can't do that in combat), but if that is where they want the challenge element of their game to be, then fair enough, but I wouldn't be recommending it for solo playI got this game on a fairly reasonable discount (costing around £5 at the time) and I've played 6 hours and got bored of it, but for a £ and hour, it certainly isn't bad - But i wouldn't go so far as to recommend it (especially at full price)

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool concept and art-style. The game seems to be great with a premade, and I would definitely recommend it if you have a group or want to use LFG discords and such. Unfortunately I’m not really in this camp. I don’t want to waste 45 minutes to find a group in discord every time I want to play.Solo is too fast paced and unbalanced, but this should be easily fixed by the devs.Matchmaking sucks: screeching monkeys with open mic making dumb noises (thanks to default mic settings), 50%-80% of people leave during the first few minutes, 350 (xi xin) ping players, body blocking, no chatbox history (is this 2001?) and hoarders/quitters/lootstealers.The idea that you can put up to 10 random people (without regional matchmaking) in the same game and expect them to communicate, plan, and most importantly SHARE NON-INSTANCED RESOURCES AND LOOT for over 2 hours is wishful thinking. This will simply not work with randoms. Yes I am aware there is a town chest. Shared loot only works in games where people are supposed to compete. This is not the case here, there is ZERO need for competition between players, yet the game gives anyone the power to ruin the game and leave with half the map resources or simply waste/hoard them.There are currently too many design issues and missing QoL features to make this game playable with randoms. In some aspects the game feels like it was designed as a battle royal but then switched to coop. I have no doubt matchmaking will get better as the game stabilizes and the majority of people give up playing with randoms.“Battlepass” is free, stop complaining about it. Store is absolutely not pay-to-win (for now), unless you consider getting pink hair is a massive advantage. Everything is obtainable for free by playing the game.8/10 with a premade5/10 solo, needs rebalancing but this is clearly not what the game was made for2/10 with randoms

Now you put all that learned and you get a run that is +15 days, you get all the fragments to unlock the lair to fight fenrir, you fight and defeat fenrir finally ! Now you’re sitting around debating if you want to keep playing, and the answer is NO. The game lacks any form of fun RNG to keep you interested, once you figure out the game every run is trivial, your team is running around collect all forms of resources, cutting down thousands of trees and picking up thousands of rocks, you have your team of farmers and your team of defenders, and then your team of boss killers, every merchant supplies you with the same items every match, with the same stats, there’s nothing different, all the classes feel the same and they play the same, generic talent trees with stuff like “increase fire damage” or “increase ice damage” you play a hunter and they have no access to a pet, like what ??? There’s a big problem with replay ability here, everything will soon feel the same, there isn’t enough RNG, yea sure you get runes, but you will never get runes that make you feel stronger, if I’m playing an axe warrior build, you best believe I’ll get “increase range arrow damage” runes, or you’ll get “keep 20% of ingredients when you die” but wait, I don’t want to die and that rune only works when you die, what a waste ! Overall, if the games classes actually felt different, and played differently from eachother and had very unique abilities that only their class has access too, it would be more fun, if every chest you looted actually gave you fun loot for once instead of “potions” and “traps” or “floor and ramp” it would keep you interested, if the actual loot that was equipable had different stats or abilities it would keep the game fresh, and if runes actually improved the gameplay, this would be a very fun game, I personally didn’t mind the farming and collecting all the wood and stone, but outside of that nothing was fun.This games main problem is it’s fun factor, once you’ve experienced everything it all feels the same, there’s no new combination of loot and runes or abilities to make you want to keep playing, there’s nothing to farm for that’s new, or to discover, you already know what equipment is in the match, and what that equipment does, like imagine looting a chest and you get really good weapon, and in the past you’ve been losing, but with this rng weapon drop you’ve gone further than ever, now your future matches you know that weapon can drop randomly and you’re excitedly opening every chest in hopes you see that weapon or a weapon just as strong to drop, and you start yelling to all your friends about your new item, but right now, the only communication is “I’ve cut down my 300th, I’m coming to deposit the wood in the chest”The game is not bad, but it is not fun, and that’s easily reflected in the $20 price it has, make the game have more RNG, so people can say “this is a good run” or “this was bad run” and not say “this is the same run over and over” make chests have actual loot and not floors and ramps and weird trap bombs that no one uses, make the classes feel special and have unique abilities, if I’m playing a hunter I better have a pet that fights with me, make equipable gear more fun with different stat values, like you want people to continue playing your game and buying your in game currency to purchase cosmetics ? We’ll make the game more fun and not bland, after playing it for two days around a total of 20 hours or so and killing fenrir, I believe I’ve seen and done everything the game has to offer, so for that I will not recommend this game for people to play, it’s simply just not fun after a few matches

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't go through the effort of posting reviews, be it positive or negative, but for this game I have to.The gameplay itself isn't terrible. It's decent. However, the game suffers from many major issues.The game only lasts for 3 hours (saga) or 4-5 hours (survival) and has absolutely no replayability.The core gameplay in saga mode is to complete the 3 sagas as quickly as possible as the longer you take the harder it gets, and restart and go again. This may sound enticing, as you can try new classes/builds and try to beat the game differently/quicker, but the game falls flat. The classes don't feel unique, a few of them actively do nothing (guardian, gimmick is to taunt ads but any ad you'd ever want or need to taunt ignores it) so once you've played one class you've pretty much played them all.Then there are the weapons and armor. This game has the worst armor/weapon balance in any game I have ever played. You have absolutely NO options for weapons. If you want to beat the game, you get the easiest legendary weapon you can get, which changes every game because of RNG with Jotunn spawns....but because of terrible balancing some of the legendaries are extremely easy to craft so you'll make them and just ignore all other weapons every single playthrough. 9 times out of 10, by the time you can craft the legendary you WANT to craft, you'll already have crafted a different legendary 30-90 minutes prior and can't/dont want to waste the resources to craft a new one. This is most prominent with spears, which have only one choice for an endgame weapon. How do you craft said spear? By using the drops from the minions right before the final boss. That's right, the ONLY endgame spear you'll use to kill one enemy and then restart the game, if you can even be bothered to waste your time leaving, crafting the spear, then going back to kill the boss with an at best, sidegrade, instead of just killing the boss with whatever legendary you already had.Then there is survival mode.Survival mode is terrible. Plain and simple. It is saga mode, but slower. You also no longer have a class, you just have a huge skill tree that incorporates skills from every class, this is a positive or a negative based on preference, I personally don't like it. The enemies are more difficult EARLY but the game remains the same. You go through, beat all of the jotunns and bosses, then you'll be on day ~18 after beating the game if you took your time and crafted the specific armor/weapons you wanted to, since on survival you can take your time to craft the specific legendaries you wanted, except the spear. The spear is still acquired right before the final boss.But it is survival, so surely you can go and do stuff after you "beat" it, right?No. The main three bosses never respawn, so you just go through and kill the four mini-bosses when they spawn every few hours, which takes about two minutes to kill all four. Between that time, there is nothing to do. There's no town threat so you don't have to defend your town, you already crafted your armor/weapons so there's no need to keep farming, and the worst offender:YOU CAN'T BUILD. A survival game where you are limited to placing ~200 tiles. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I can't even explain how terrible this is. I have three tiny shacks and I am at the build limit.All of this and not even mentioning the devs way of trying to get you to play the game is by making achievements that take arbitrarily long and are timegated. There is an achievement on survival for playing to day 100. Keep in mind that I already said you'll have beat the game if you took your time, with nothing else to do as you can't even build, around day 20.And finally, the bugs.When you kill an enemy or deplete a resource, it drops multiple loot piles. Your pet is supposed to auto-loot for you. There is a bug in saga where 90% of the time, it doesn't work. To fix it, you have to restart your game, un-equip and re-equip your pet, join back and hope it works. If that already sounds annoying, now just remember you're also on a time limit in saga, making the problem that much worse.In survival mode, every 30 minutes you'll randomly fall through the world your camera position will lock into place, and your screen will rapidly zoom in and out of the ground. To fix it, you have to either use a shrine (which is borderline impossible because your camera is locked in place) or relog anywhere between 1-10 times.To recap:Okay combatOkay resource gatheringLittle to no replayabilityPoorly, no, terribly balanced crafting systemGamebreaking bugsTimegated achievements disguised as contentBUILD LIMIT IN SURVIVALNo difficulty modifiers, making the game incredibly easy after you beat saga mode for the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's a fun game, though not without it's issues. Let's run the pros and cons shall we?Pros:* It's Co-op ... YAY* It's stable. I play this with my friend and neither of us have crashed or experienced any noticeable bugs.* Nice looking graphics, a combination of cell shaded and animation that comes together well.* The combat can feel a little loosie goosie at first, but once you get the hang of it it's fine. Nothing ground breaking or amazing but it's perfectly serviceable. * I've seen the Devs post in the forums and they seem to take an active interest. Thus the game should only continue to improve.Cons:Some systems feel like they need some tweaking* The day/night cycle feels really fast. The entire game rotates around this cycle so solo or small groups can have a hard time getting things done. The game keeps your back to the wall constantly. I never feel like i have a chance to relax and just enjoy the game. Though i understand some people will like the frantic pace you have to maintain, i and my friend are not among them. I would like to see this changed or altered somehow as i feel it detracts from the game.* The repair costs and durability are out of wack. Your weapons degrade very quickly and require large amounts of souls to repair. But you lose all your souls when you die, and since your weapons degrade while fighting... and fighting is when you die... this leads to failure spirals where you can't repair your weapons to defend your base or finish off what killed you.* This ties into my first con. Because of the hectic pace of the game you don't get to fiddle with things. No browsing through the vendors to compare weapons or armor. No running off to gather rare mats you need to maybe try different weapons unless they are along the path you're taking to achieve your next goal. There's a building system in the game that i haven't even touched. Not because i'm not interested in it, but because i can't imagine wasting the amount of time it would take to stand there and fiddle with placing pieces.Final thoughts:This is neither a pro or a con, but this game was initially called a survival mixed with Diablo (ARPG).  It is neither of those things. There is a temperature system that comes into play in certain areas, but that's about as close to a survival game as it comes. There's no food/drink to manage, which i'm thankful for TBH. While there's building (see above) it's nothing like you'd find in an actual survival game. You cannot build and decorate your own base, just upgrade the existing premade one.It's not really an ARPG either. The core of that genre is that you kill mobs to get loot (weapons and armor). Here the mobs only drop souls and crafting mats that you can use to make gear yourself. In ARPGs you farm mobs to lvl and get stronger. there's no time in this game to farm anything.What this game is, is a Roguelike. Each play through is only supposed to last aprox 2-4 hours. You pretty much start over each time. Don't get this expecting a long term game that you keep coming back to like a survival or ARPG. Which is fine, the tags have since changed, but just know what you're buying.As i opened with, Overall the game is fun. With a few changes it would be even better. We are both enjoying it, so as long as you know what you're getting into and are ok with that, i give it a solid thumbs up!

_childDocuments_.review: Tribes of Midgard is a fine game with very minimal gameplay intrigue. I don’t have a problem with the game as a whole, provided you just put blinders on and ignore all the microtransactions and habitual daily quest bullshittary. The problem comes that there isn’t much else to the game. What you can do is super low level with no real gameplay beyond the intrigue of the initial discovery.Combat is very samey and boring. Different weapon classes act a little differently but how you use them is pretty much hold left click, occasionally press right click. There's not much in the way of nuance or fun to be had overall.The world is large but made super small by teleporters. You explore an area once, plop down a teleporter near anything important and, whenever the little wait to respawn timer goes away, you just plop back for a quick murder before heading home. Unlike games like Valheim where teleporters are a thing but are difficult to make, maintain a hub and have restrictions to keep the world feeling large, Tribes crushes itself down to a list of grindy points to interact with.Base construction is pretty awful. The system itself isn’t terrible other than being unable to remove a single piece of an area, you have to dismantle the entire vertical stack but its hyper limited in what you can actually create (there's a friggen 'complexity' meter that tells you if you've built too much stuff; wtf?). Using what you've built is also really bad if you want to add a roof or second story. We found just sticking everything nearby the dump chests to be way less frustrating than trying to have things sensically added to a multi-story home.The farming system is pretty meh. You click once to dig a hole, click once to plant a thing and, after a while click it again to collect your prize. It and the fishing thing seem like they were added soley to tick off the mandatory 'survival' game requirements more than anything.Mentioned the microtransaction and dark pattern habits the game tries to get its players into but worth mentioning again.There's, unfortunately, little reason to play the game and after, like, 5 hours I was already bored. Stuck with it to play with friends until they got bored too so now we're all quitting.Spend your money elsewhere :)

One of the blue runes that spawns projectiles is insanely good and basically everything else is hot garbageDeath - Why make souls vanish upon death? Why can a gentle tail swipe from a giant lizard shoot me directly into water that again- One shots the player? Why is this a thing? Just get rid of it or let me vibe in the water, literally the most obnoxious thing I've ever experienced in a video game is accidentally rolling to my demise in some 2 inch deep pond that apparently sucks me straight to hell.Day/Night cycle - Make days longer, give us more nights beyond the (((blood moon after party))) night where we can explore and grab ♥♥♥♥ since you decided you wanted materials to be exclusively harvestable at night.Invasions - Have them drop more ♥♥♥♥, souls, items, anything. Feels horrible getting invaded, breaking both of my weapons via durability loss, and then having jack to show for it. After a few rounds (and especially so after you beat a "Saga Boss" once) the previous charm of this game is pretty obviously broken down to it's components.This game doesn't actually do anything very well.   -  the combat is a clunky mess with long delays on blocks or dodges        -  equips where you're either OP or useless        -  bosses(jotun/saga boss) are just easy but time consuming giant damage sponges        -  the bow and arrow has to be a joke   -  gathering resources is a chore that you need to do every single run , where some are overly plentiful and others overly scarce   -  a huuge amount of content is blocked behind them following that stupid "season rewards" trend, they're really trying to make free-to-play bux while not even being a free game   -  this isn't an early access game even though it doesn't seem finished at all   - survival mode has no purpose, if you can do everything the game has to offer in a little over 10 days(in-game time), why would you stay for 100 days? there's not any more content or anything   - roguelike, except every run feels pretty much exactly the same, not nearly enough randomization for runs to feel different, gets old real quick

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great. This makes you play on edge and careful. -Water. It's fine as is. I'm not sure why people keep rolling into and dying then complaining about it. Just don't roll into it. What needs to be changed IMO:-Bifrost needs a serious rework. Game punishes you for trying to make it to the endgame (which requires you to play a 3.5hour session) , yet rewards players that dip out early and play 1,maybe 2 hrs. -Should have it's pace slowed down, but without slowing down the actual game play. Game play wise, you will do tedious tasks like facing off against monsters with ridiculously high HP, which is cool. What's bad is that you're rushed to do everything as soon as your spawned in the world and the game doesn't give you time to prep what you need such as giving you time to explore class abilities or taking time to craft. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. The gameplay loop is interesting, but the combat is just not there. There is a huge delay between when you attack and when you can block, which makes it feel worthless, especially since the large enemy attack rotations, which seem like they need to be blocked/dodged, don't line up smoothly with any attack combos. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but it unfortunately feels like a big disappointment. The game's mechanics prioritize efficiency and time management, at the expense of exploration, experimentation, and play. I've only had a one truly successful run in my 20+ hours, and I haven't unlocked every class, but I till feel like I've seen just about everything the game has to offer. Each run feels just like the last one, with the repetition extending to your weapon and armor options.I really hoped that this game would be more like a traditional ARPG, which my wife and I could explore and enjoy, but the game's mechanics make that essentially impossible, since the act of enjoying the game is antithetical to the urgent race which this game presents. Every choice & every battle you fight in this game is really just a distraction. Sure, you COULD clear out that camp of baddies, but if you don't need any more of the resources they drop, then you've just wasted time and energy you should have spent on more pressing matters. If you are trying to fully explore a biome, then you're doing it wrong. If you are looking for interesting secret stuff, you're not gonna find it. The extent of this game is very limited, and the gameplay is pretty disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, what a rollercoaster of emotions I'm experiencing with this game.I've never felt this much stress playing a video game. Well, maybe some competitive games do make you go crazy, but definitely not a pve one. I couldn't drink a glass of water without worrying that I waste time in the game for nothing, because "OH NO, THE NIGHT IS COMING-- THE BOSS IS COMING-- I NEED TO DO THIS AND THIS AND THAT--". I imagine it gets better the more people you have in the game, but seriously, who expects an average gamer to have ~10 friends... The game doesn't want you to progress far since there's not much in it overall, and-- every playthough is going to be exactly the same, unless you plan to use different classes\weapons. Some of the mechanics are absolutely unusable, like building. But then again, I didn't have much time to build, so-- there's that. The bosses are easy (most of them have only a few attacks), they just have a lot of health. And the quests are bad. Again, take too long for barely any reward.There's a lot more things I could comment on, but-- I don't want to make it look like I hated the game, it's actually the opposite. The game is still fun, but it could be so much better. I'm looking forward to its future updates and (hopefully?) some changes to the gameplay and whatnot.

Weapons break so fast, and if you build to make your weapons last 50% more in a class like Ranger for example, your build becomes ♥♥♥♥ !By the way, this game is like GTA Vice City. You hit a pool of water, you die instantly. Overall it's a good game, but these problems are too annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: Lot of problems with this game.Combat very unsatisfying, just hold left click.  A few classes have some ways to make it more interactive, but largely it's hp attrition.Loss of souls on death is a stupid design.  I had a weapon break, died because of it, then had no souls to repair the weapon with - I'm supposed to go whack trees until I can?  It also punishes players...for what?  The ideal way to win the game is paint-by-numbers - rush as fast as possible, have certain things built by certain days.  You want to hurt the non-ideal players further?  Just make repair free or scrap durability.Quest implementation is not good, at all.  'Easy' quests have me running to the literal opposite end of the world, and there's no clear indicator on the map where I'm supposed to go.Weapon variety at a given tier doesn't exist.  You get the weapon you can make, then you go whack things you can kill to make the next weapon.  At at given tier there are maybe 2 choices, most there are 1.  It's possible to skip tiers but pretty unlikely.  Most weapon skills are not impactful or interesting.The skill trees are largely very boring and do little to change gameplay.  If a skill tree doesn't make me feel powerfully distinct from another class, or make the playstyle unique and fun, then it needs a redesign.  Skill trees are about making interesting choices - these don't.  Likewise, classes do not feel distinct or interesting.Microtransaction cosmetics should not be in a game you pay for, full stop.  Zero variety between runs - no interesting randomized events, world generation is dull and same-y, no interesting monster variety.After seeing their first major patch adding a boss and -more- cosmetics, I have to say the dev team's priorities feel very off.  A lot of people are telling you your game needs fundamental changes.  Doubt I'll come back to this one ever.

_childDocuments_.review: I really REALLY wanted to love the game.My biggest gripe, and really what killed it for me, is that the tutorial is almost useless.In the tutorial you learn how to gather resources, craft an axe, pickaxe, and sword, and do a little fighting. After you've crafted your tools (not even armor yet) they hand you a bunch of gear and teleport you to fight a giant, which is gonna be one of the big parts of the game loop. Super cool, super fun, feeling awesome taking down the giant. But then that's it. That's the tutorial.I don't necessarily expect them to spoon feed all the info and run through absolutely everything, but the amount of information that you're given in what's supposed to be where you learn how to play is just not enough to get started at all.The gameplay itself feels fine and I can imagine would be really fun, but if you don't already know how everything works in the game, or have someone to tell you how it all works, it's not gonna be a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I give my negative criticisms, I'll say that the game has a great concept and with a few tweaks I could see this game having amazing longevity.  On the first month of its release it was one of the top played games on steam and because of that I hope developers give it a lot of attention so it will stay near the top without it fading out into obscurity.Now my biggest gripe is that I wish the classes had more identity.  The warrior plays like the seer, the seer plays like the hunter, the hunter plays like the beserker...ect...  The differences between these classes are minimal +10-20% stat boosts to a weapon or element.  Some of these stat boosts are also confusing, as the ranger has +20% to dark element but has no dark bow besides an endgame legendary that will take too long to get to 90% of games.  There are some classes that have more unique differences, such as the seers healing or the hunters increase in gathering; but these are such minimal abilities they hardly make any difference.  The seers sprout heals for so little it's not noticeable, the hunters extra gathering only affects certain non essential resources, ect...Balance is another one of my gripes, especially on gear.  There are weapons/armor sets in the game that are 'the best', and the only real reason to pick another set is to avoid the rat race with 9 other people trying to also get 'the best' set and fighting for the same resources.  I have yet to play survival mode, but in saga mode (normal mode) the days become progressively shorter and nights longer.  With the night also comes the cold, meaning that mid-late game the cold armor set gets more value than the others.Blocking and dodging feels a bit clunky to me.  Your character has to completely finish an attack animation before you can dodge/block instead of a dodge/block canceling out your attack to feel more dynamic.  Now this is probably a personal gripe because I have seen a lot of popular games use this clunkier dodge/block mechanic; and the bosses in Tribes of Midgard also have extremely telegraphed attacks to likely make up for this.And finally...onto my last gripe...resources.  In the basic 10 man quickplay games with randoms there is not enough of certain resources for multiple people to have the same armor sets/weapons.  An example would be: I frequently try to craft the lightning axe...about half the games I play I am able to find the resources for this naturally (without buying)...now also take into consideration this axe can be upgraded which costs more of that resource...AND...there's a 5 piece lightning armor set that also takes these resources per piece.  If I am struggling to even craft a single lvl1 lightning axe, then how about the other 9 players in the lobby some of whom also want the lightning axe and to upgrade it or even the full 5 piece set.  Now there are ways to obtain some of these resources through merchants, however they are expensive and will funnel resources into buying these things instead of upgrading the base/gates/towers/buildings.A lot of these issues are fixed or alleviated if you are playing lobbies with friends only.  Classes like the warden who got limited value from crafting his gear cheaper now can get massive value because you can coordinate crafting ALL your teams gear.  Friends can coordinate who will be using what weapons and armor so resources aren't fought over.  And while playing with friends does help these downfalls, I would argue that the game should be balanced around quickplay lobbies instead of min/maxed private lobbies because quickplay lobbies is where most people will be playing.Anyway...I hope my review helped.  Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I love this game. Norse mythology, Refreshing graphics style & a decent combat system. However! Be Warned - New players will likely go through an exciting 'Love it' Phase, followed by growing frustration and maybe even a brief 'hate it' phase. Trust me. Push through this frustration phase. Watch video's, group with friends or join pick up games to learn the extremely important basic steps through the game needed to survive the constant onslaught. You Will not regret it!  Do the tutorial (It doesn't show enough) and keep in mind the saga mode is far more time stressed than the more open ended Survival mode. Treat your first dozen attempts as tutorials and keep in mind that even brief games reward you XP and progress in your start game menu achievement unlocks. These unlock valuable items like starter kits that give you a solid half day or more head start ... Stick to it to get the basics down to get to the super fun parts of the game. it is really Quite good. To help new players, My YT should have a simple guide up in the next day or 2:  "How to survive the first 3 days in Tribes"  :)  Good Hunting! Karandar
