_childDocuments_.review: The game is overall good 8,0/10Here are the PROS and CONS in my perspective:PROS:-Maps are randomly generated each time you play-You get EXP regardless if you loose or not, so trying your best gives you rewards regardless:)-Classes have their unique-ness, and though some specialize in different weapons, it is never a bad thing to choose a tank or healer to go full dps in a game, choose your path to your liking. -The game difficulty scales with people, it is solo able, but more fun with people-Items can be crafted by anyone, and if you play with a group, you can harvest resources and put it in the war chest where everyone can enjoy the materials.-They have a discord server. People will help you on what you need and normal runs etc, just fallow the rules and info, you get the hang of it fast;) Search: Tribe of midgard discord of google or any search platform and wala!-Rush mode or Long mode, these are just words we came up with, but as the name suggests, either rush the final boss in a Saga mode, or play as long as you are able to. The rush mode is for those who only go for dailies for example and long mode for those who wants to accumulate a lot of exp for the seasonal reward and achievements etc, and to give them a sense of a challenge.-So far the best thing is that they are updating the game with new content, and what i like the most. Well like the first season, "Fenrir" was the end boss, second season "Jörmungandr" the sea serpent is the nest big boss to join the stage. Now the thing is, looks like every season new big named bosses will appear as the game expands, who knows what more there is in the future! :DCONS:-Game length, well for 1 day in game, thats 10 mins in real life time. So for people who wants to play a short game, well you could end it as soon as the 1st Jotun/giant is killed (day 2 or 3) to bifrost out (to end the game and get rewards/Early quit the game), but that means you will get less rewards, as the more days you survive the more rewards and exp you will get.-If you cant defend the "tree" and it dies, you wont get "Horns" (in game premium currency, only found and rewarded through bifrosting or lucky drops from killing NPC, or opening chests)-The game can get repetitive, since the runs never differ (the same principle is applied every run, you need to do this and that to either survive long or ending it as fast as possible) , but as long as you choose different roles it might give you some other options to run your runs, but not much.-Random ques. Randomly queue up can either ruin your run or you will have a good run, the thing is, most people dont know what to do, so your expected session/run wont turn out to be the way you want sometimes. So i recommend either run a private group or join the discord server that Tribes of Midgard have made, to find active people in joining you on your run. Everything is up to you, but if you want to experience the game to its fullest, you run with people that knows what to doThis is only applicable to season 1, since a lot might change in the future, but regardless, the game is fun and i see even more positive things to come in the future:)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a ton of fun, both solo and with friends. Haven't played Survival mode yet, but I'm already going to leave a thumbs up for Saga mode. Every survival/crafting game should have the equivalent of Saga mode, in my opinion. Don't get me wrong, I love long, ongoing games like Valheim, Ark, The Forest, etc. But it's really nice and refreshing to have a one-sitting game mode, especially with friends who may not be able to make a regular commitment to the larger game mode. It's fun, fast-paced, and addicting. I'd imagine the Survival mode is slower paced, for those looking for the more traditional survival/crafting experience. There's something for everyone. Even though I got it half off, I would say that the $20 price is definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with friends, has amazing potential and will require very little work from developers to turn into a great game. I will list needed changes agreed upon by me and all my friends who played the game:- Slight reduction in souls cost of repairing gear (mainly weapons);- Possible upgrade of repair building (to mitigate repair cost);- Slightly better biome frequency (sometimes fire biome is extremely rare, or the resources within are);- Attack moving you forward with animation lock could be removed or reduced (able to dodge faster after attacking);- World tree should not degen (invasions and giants should be the threat, or it should only degen when already below 50% hp to reward soul investment);- Remove ability to dodge into water (leads into instant death from a wrong key press? why? Also lizard tail swipe might make you fall in it and die);- Nerf building costs (actual building parts like walls and corners etc not village buildings) no-one will spend wood building those even with quarry/lumberyard rebuilt;- Days need to be longer (time to explore and gather is basically non-existant);- Quest UI on objectives needs reword, objective needs to be seen at all times;- Bow attacks should stay in place or kite only after movement command has been pressed (sometimes you want to stay in the same place);- Recipes can be traded for Golden Horns, but not on a rotating shop, that's unecessarily punishing;- Opening the map should NOT stop your movement inputs (I just want to double check the map , tap in tap out and keep moving in the overall direction);- There NEEDS TO BE a way to play several worlds at once, sometimes I have a group of 4 friends, sometimes just 2;Will update the review later based on more feedback. Overall, it is a good game with a potential to be great, even amazing. Just push a little bit more devs, you're on the path!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that this game is good. not great but a solid 7/10the game is a rouge like with game mechanics like diablo and the exploring and feeling of a open world tower defence game if that makes any sense. you explore the world collecting materials that you can either use to build defences for your base or to upgrade vendors in your base to get better gear. you can also spend said materials on a farm, lumberyard, or quarry to do the work for you.every night there are creatures that attack your base and try to destroy the tree in the middle of your base. it is your responsibility to protect the tree because if it dies your run is over and that's not fun. there are also these bosses that start coming to your village every three days or so (three days after you kill the first one). you can find these bosses and kill them before they get to your village so you don't have to worry about them completely destroying you village. if you manage to kill these bosses you get parts from them which you can use to make legendary weapons. which are op by the way.unlike other rouge likes though, it's more of a grind to get upgrades outside of each and every run. so that being said if you want to beat the final boss you kinda just have to know how to manage your time and make sure you go back to your base every night to protect the tree.you can play this game with up to 10 people but i have only played by myself because i have no friends. i don't know what the multiplayer experience is like but i know the game gets harder and harder the more people you have in your party. solo being the most easy while with 10 people being really hard. i think the more amount of people do only change the health of bosses and maybe making things more expensive.so all in all the game isn't bad for it's price tag so if you have the money i say give it a shot.but don't hold it against me if you don't like it

_childDocuments_.review: I played Tribes of Midgard with 2 players and 3 players and I can say that you are able to go quite far and win, although having more players allows you to complete more tasks and go even further. It was fun to play for the 9 hours I did but I think that it lacks content or good replayability. My friends and I don't really feel like doing more rounds as we basically already saw everything in the game and don't feel like replaying it.The combat doesn't feel good. My problem is that you can't block or dodge fast enough after attacking. There is a huge delay when you attack and you are basically better off just face tanking the enemy. You don't get rewarded for fast reactions and the dodge roll doesn't even have i-frames to begin with, only when you got the warrior skill. The Jötner are disappointing as well. They each have only about 3 attacks and you learn them very fast, making the boss fights trivial. The only reason the Jötner are a threat is because of the bloated amount of hp they get after every level. I hope they improve the combat system and rework the bosses (and add new ones)!Again, the game was still fun for a bit but I hope they improve the game a lot more. So if you are looking for a fun little co-op game to play for a few rounds, you can pick this up but I can't recommend Tribes of Midgard at full price, you should grab it at a good discount.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Works well and quite fun once you give it a chance and learn a bit outside of the tutorial, see it as don't starve but with vikings is my best way to describe it but without the fear of food. 50/50 review it needs work but has its fun parts as well.I went into this worried due to reviews, I will admit it was not what I was expecting but I am enjoying it after giving it a chance. I enjoyed it a lot more thanks to a player in survival named "Thuse" who was patient with me being new and telling me things here and there instead of getting mad which was nice, thanks dude your one of the great players online needs more of.More could be in the tutorial as it doesn't tell you much about what else to do outside of a few things but I see this as Don't Starve where you make errors and learn from your mistakes to be better next time. But this is why I can see not many having the patience with the game.It is a rough start but once you get a good team mate or two it gets easier and then more free time for yourself to go explore or kill stuff instead of rushing around for things.Match making needs work, you cannot select the lobby but survival lets you pick from a list, why not matchmaking also? It is also not much matchmaking as you can be put in with complete new players when you played over 40 hours. This is annoying when half the lobby leaves/afk or just plain rude when you ask them to help with the objective acting like matchmaking is unlimited survival time (heads up IT IS NOT) often making you waste 1-2 hours of playtime because only 1-3 other players cared to learn, listen and help. Matchmaking is fun when you do get a good team but you will 50/50 get a bad bunch of players too who won't even listen on how to play the mode they are even in and this can ruin it for many.Survival is ok, good for exp if you survive long enough but you need to be level 2 on your account just to play it, so if you don't want to go into match making off the bat have fun in your solo world where it is not scaled to one player, making it stressful the first few times just to open a mode. But once you max everything all you can do is go out and collect more stuff or kill enemies to occupy your time though this is more fun with friends on mic-chat I am sure but is often boring when you have sweep the map clean.Yes there is a "cash shop" but so far, I see nothing wrong with it, it is just cosmetics and items needed for it you can get from season pass or from playing the game and getting horns so I have no issue with them having it. If you spend real money on it, that is on you, not them. they gave you a way to earn stuff in-game for it. Have more will power people.Now the online does need work, firstly the chat box disappears too quickly and you cannot bring up messages again, so if you miss that message you need to hope the person repeats it. Why is this not a chat box we can scroll and re-look through? If you have one lag spike you will no longer be able to read other players chat until you relog.Secondly people can grief and take everything from your shared chest and log off with it, why not just make it where logging off auto-puts it back in the chest or in a chest where they logged off so someone can go get it? put a safe option in the world creation to stop people taking everything!Thirdly, items you can pick up including souls often get stuck on the gates or other high end areas you cannot even reach, please fix this.

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, saw a lot of questions in the discussion forum about players that are unsure if this game is a good fit for solo or with a group of friend. The simple answer is both. Here is a quick run down:, go into saga or survival mode and its going to be a good adventure. Lots of monsters to hunt, resources to gather and tools to craft your way into 20+ hours of play. Saga mode offers a quick and fast game play that is sure to keep entertained as your team tries to defend a base with a 15 day timer before a non-stop enemy attack. Also, survival mode maps saves at all times making it ideal to hop in at any given time with or without friends. The world will update for everyone which is good if you can't sinc everyone's schedule.Now for  you could think of this as a souls like game with lots of dodging, healing and leaping your way through both modes as it is harder to go after big bosses with little to no help. Going solo is the ideal path if you wish to unlock every item in the game as resources and experience are focused only on you. Hope this review helps and I hope to see you around!

_childDocuments_.review: Tribes of Midgard is a diablo style game with light survival elements played with 10 players in 2 hour chunks. (when you are winning) If that interests you and you can accept that the overall package is kind of light in terms of time and depth, go ahead and get it.It is somewhat like a roguelike in that you start from level one every game, though there are starter packs you unlock and some items that you can find that you could not before after every run.Although I had a good time with it, I see a few technical and gameplay problems that worry me.Gameplay problems: The starter packs are being handed out very slowly, the fighting is not responsive, and the game will quickly become repetitive once you beat it a couple times, yet they expect you to beat it 10 times to gain certain rewards. They need more modifiers to the base game, more reasons to keep playing, and they need to change the nature of why you must return to base. Having to stand in one spot and fighting the same enemies while managing gates is boring. The game ends up feeling like the final level of a game, instead of the whole game.Technical problems: When a game lasts 2 hours you expect it to work every time. Having a game drop in the middle is a severe loss of time. They do have a system in place to rejoin if you get disconnected, but I have had it fail to reconnect permanently. They have a system in place that gives you better rewards for leaving before your base is destroyed, but this requires you are in game to leave through a specific spot and if the game booted you, you are now getting diminished (possibly even no?) reward. After 2 hours of play that is just unacceptable.This game has an interesting idea that I would love to see get more attention, but it is not the best version of itself. I can see a world in which this is done better, and I look forward to that game.Ways I think it could be better. -More starter packs that allow for more play styles. These are by far the most interesting aspect of the game, but I am about 10 hours in and the 'right' one at the moment is clear. I think they should have perk sets similar to the call of duty series. I think unlocking those would be a good fit for this game.-Run modifiers randomly selected at the start of the match. Once you know the game, you can just kind of autopilot through it and the only factor that matters is does your team have microphones and do they know how to play the game. If yes, you win, if no, you don't. Changing the nature of the game, your goals, or what is available to you could really mix it up and keep it fresh. Like what if everyone does 5x damage, but also has 1 hp? Only ranged weapons. Every zone is cold and requires building fires to explore else needing cold immune potions. Stuff like that. You could even chain this together with the starter packs and allow people to choose their starter pack after they know the modifier. Allowing them to customize their character for the challenge.-Get rid of the town and night time defense or change it. It sucks.The worst part of the game is having to return to town to run around in circles killing enemies. It is very rote and really is more determined by your stats than your ability to defend the town well. The game shines when trying to coordinate a team exploring a map at high speed while juggling varying objectives. There still needs to be a thing you are gathering resources for, and you need a fail state, but it could be something better than the town as it currently exists. A tower defense game in town would be better.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably fabulous for people with lots of time.  I understand the episodic nature of saga mode is supposed to allow short installments of game play, but even those short installments, for anyone remotely progression oriented, constitute a nearly knife's edge technical grind, where failure awards you with... the same grind again, and success rewards you with... the same grind again.  In short, if you're casually playing this game you are not actually playing this game, and if you're actively grinding that is accurate.  You are grinding. And grinding.  Or, you get into a team who has "solved" saga mode to get... what exactly?  Literally no part of this game is compelling to me EXCEPT the capacity to allow 10 players Co-op.  This is a fabulous redeemer which may keep me playing semi-casually (as much as is allowed) until I can't take the repetition anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'm obsessed. I think i worked it out to be about 1 hour of real time per 6 days in-game (Saga Mode). As most (successful) games end between Day 13 - Day 15, I think it's safe to say that you should plan to be in a game for close to 3 hours if you're trying to beat the Saga Boss. That being said... the game is challenging, mostly because it was made to be challenging. It's also challenging due to the lack of cohesion in majority of the games as well as bugs. More often than not, I am placed in an already dying world or a world where everyone on the "team" is playing by themselves. Matchmaking requires a lot of working together to be adequately prepared and most of the players I have come across fail to realize that. As for the bugs, i've experienced a bunch. Item glitching all over the place where you can't reach or that you just can't pick up at all. Runes glitching/bugging out and not knowing if they're even active. Once i started a game and I was stuck there at the beginning just dead. Another game, i was carrying a bunch of souls and suddenly i started randomly getting hit constantly by something invisible? I tried teleporting to town but it was chipping away at my health in town as well and ultimately I just had to die I guess. The most frustrating is when you're fighting a challenging enemy in order to get a specific loot, on your last sliver of health and then you finally kill it and manage to survive... but then the loot gets stuck under ground, under platforms, on a tree you cant get to, etc. I give a "recommend" for this game with the understanding that it's a new game and that the bug and glitches (which are annoying enough to make me not want to play sometimes) will eventually be ironed out and fixed. Also in the hopes that the player community will eventually be more balanced between those who know what they're doing and new players.I hope something is done in the future to promote more teamwork in matchmaking. As it stand right now, leaving the game early is rewarded with golden horns which leaves those who want to beat the final boss struggling to do too many things at once in a world with a difficulty scaled based on a number of players who are no longer there.

_childDocuments_.review: Dont really understand all the negative reviews, sure it has some bugs lol i dead on my last run under the gate in the village and my gear/mat box land ontop of the gate and was irretrievable. Yes i play with drop everything on death, if you have any skill with any souls-like, rogue-like, ect its not hard. Well its not hard unless you set everything to hard and put your resources to hard aswell( this can only be done in survival, saga mode is on its own difficultly track i.e day 1-15). Ive finished the saga now solo and with a group(4 other homies i always play with) before day 10 with a maxed tree, t5 everything and thousands of souls in my pockets. the game is fun and has some challenge but the call for balancing is a joke, if anything we need an option to make the saga mode more challenging. As for survival, normal setting has some challenge but similar to the saga you can advance to fast and by day 12 you're maxed and now you have a very boring 88 days ahead of you.  i have had attempted multiple runs with the difficulty set to max, large world, no giant warning, scarce resources( mainly applies to souls, you really have to choose what to upgrade and whether its better to make a new weapon or repair your current ect. Currently we keep wiping on the first blood moon after the first giant is killed, you end up with multiple boss mobs on each gate and we haven't had the damage ability to get past that, YET.Positives: Its fun, it works, it costs 20 bucks, good loop, appeals to those that dont like wasting time, fast paced. no commitment, rewarded whether you win or lose with account exp.Negatives: Not meant for those that are looking for a relaxing survival experience, days are short nights are getting longer and winter is coming no time to spend 10 minutes figuring out what weapon you want to use. It does have some bugs, only run killer ive experienced was my loot box falling onto an unreachable area. All in all if your looking to another Valheim keep looking, but if youre looking for say a roguelite(ish) with punishing combat, a large random gen map, that can be played with up to 10 of your friends then this is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend the game, its fun. However I would pay more in the area of 10 euro's for it and play it with friends.The game is fun, plays well and monsters can be quite though. Its a challenge to collect the highest tier weapons and some campsites can be quite hard. Multiplayer is fun, even with people you dont know as the game has a shared storage. This shared storage works really well and it gives the feeling you are truly working together building up the camp, collecting your gear and protecting your tree. Another big plus for me is the short tutorial that does not make you feel like an idiot.I do think it has a content issue, there is not enough for it. By the 3rd game it started feeling repetitive for me, which is not something I expect for a 20 euro game.The classes feel lacking as they mostly add passive bonuses. This is because the skills are bound to your weapon and the amount of skills you can use are bound to weapon tier. This makes the classes feel quite empty. The classes also do not go in depth as much as I feel like they should. I would expect a more in depth customization of classes and gear depending on the situation of the game.Fun game to play with friends

You need to explore, read and do quests, study the game, learn items and so on, but you are on a tight timer of "almost every night your city is attacked". This ruins 90% of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Unlike most others in the reviews, I knew this was a roguelike going in.What I didn't know is that the combat is absolutely terrible. And melee combat is unsatisfying, because even though you're given a dodge roll and shield, enemies attack so quickly and with little to no telegraphing that it's basically impossible to avoid taking hits from anything but the bosses.Movement is also fairly clunky, and I managed to get my character stuck in terrain by literally just walking into it.Also, the one whole match of this I played ended with some giant dude who was basically invincible absolutely destroying the life tree. _childDocuments_.review: Not sure what all the crying is about. I haven't seen this game described well so here's my take:It's a tower defense. There's a tree in your base, you must feed it souls. Enemies come at night and try to hurt the tree - this takes away souls. Get souls by killing enemies, gathering stuff, doing various things around the world map. It's hard. Actually really hard. Managing where to spend your souls (upgrading the base, upgrading weapons, or replenishing the tree, etc) appears to be the crux. Not much is hand-fed to you. I'm playing it with a duo partner and yeah, it's tough. When you (inevitably) "lose" a match, you gain experience towards unlocking recipes and stuff that can make you more powerful on your next go-round. I'm hooked for the near future, at least, plenty to explore and see what's next. Seems like I will easily get my $20 worth out of this.

_childDocuments_.review: By combining many different game mechanics, the game looks as if it has created a new genre. While doing Tower Defence, you are trying to survive in Midgard.To counter the dark forces that waves to the tree of life in your town at night, you must take advantage of the resources that Odin has bestowed upon you, and you can choose classes with multiple different and innovative abilities, and craft your armours and weapons according to your playing style. You want to think of it as a survival game in many ways, but that's not the case. Hunger is a factor in a classic survival game, and sometimes, even thirst. In the Tribes of Midgard, you won't get hungry or thirsty, you just have to put on a weapon, armour and fend off the dark forces that waves to your town at night and protect the tree of life. At the same time, you must expel the Jötunn who are travelling to Midgard to fulfil the Ragnarök prophecy. The Jötunn approaching your town at night may cause you to shed some sweat. Because dealing with the dark forces that waves to your town at night and dealing with Jötunn can be a bit tiring. However, since up to 10 co-op is supported, this defence is very comfortable if 10 of your friends are in the same game. You can even improve the 3 gates that lead to your town and build archer towers on your walls.To survive in the game and become a true Viking legend, you must go into the wild to harvest resources that we see in classic survival games during the day. You have to do this quickly, for the dark forces and the Jötunn are not waiting. There are many types of armour and weapons that you can craft and acquire in the game. You can find NPC around the world, too, which offering good deals and mythical creatures that give you gifts. There are also 8 classes and you have to unlock each of these classes by playing the game. While you can only be Ranger and Warrior at the beginning, you can also play with that class after completing the requirements of the classes. I liked the variety of classes and the skills they had. Because it gives the impression that you are playing a role-playing game and then you realize that you are playing the game which is a combination of survival and tower-defence genre with a little bit of role-playing content. Fantastic!If you think you have completed a world, you can return to Valhalla through Bifröst. But for this, you have to kill the first Jötunn at Midgard when he or she arrives. It's not very difficult. However, if the tree of life in your town is destroyed, the world is also destroyed with your character. However, your account has progress. So your hero in the world can be thought of as a consumable object. Your account is not. You can level up and complete a process with different rewards each Season. You can think of it as a Battle Pass.There are also many cosmetics, runes and starter kits in the game. You can use them for your hero, whether you're playing a game in Survival or Saga Mode, Solo Play or Matchmaking. So, if you get a rune that gives a 20% bonus while collecting materials, this rune will be active in the game. If you have the Gatherer Starter Kit (which is obtained by completing the second level in the first season), you can activate it for your hero before they start. You can start the game with an axe and pickaxe in hand.However, the fact that the gameplay of the game appears to be innovative and a combination of several good genres does not mean that the marketing strategy is right. I think they mislead some gamers with their marketing strategy. So, it was a bit of distrust that they initially presented the game as a pure survival game and continued to introduce it as tower-defence when the game was released. And the latency is a real issue by the way.Still, I think you should play the game and start enjoying the game after your account reaches 5-10 level at least. You can play with your friends in Survival Mode and save this world and exit the game. However, if the tree of life here is destroyed while you are in the game, unfortunately, that world also disappears. Protect the Tree of Life no matter what!

Even if it is only for cosmetics, it shouldn't be there, you should be able to get everything just by playing, unlock things, or even maybe release a DLC with more stuff;- Some things in the shop are completely nonsense, like a robot bird and some costumes that don't fit with the Viking fantasy.Even if it seems that I wrote more cons than pros, I like the game, it's just some details that I would like to see in the game to make it even better.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: The "no" recommendation is with the current state of the game. That said, I do enjoy the game, but it needs a handful of changes and refining before I can actually suggest people spend money.The absolute biggest issues are the flow of combat, and most importantly, the length of the day cycle. You are constantly babysitting your town, as every night you have to protect it, and days are only 10 minutes long. You have almost no time to collect resources, and even less time if you plan to explore. IMO both of those issues - and a further issue that that these changes would make - can be fixed with a couple simple modifications.First, the day cycle needs to be longer; and with these changes probably shorter nights at least at first. I suggest the day cycle be increased to at least 15 minutes, instead of 10, and community feedback and testing can decide if 15 minutes is long enough/too long/ect. But 10 minutes is short, every day feels like it ends immediately and you had no time to do much.Second, for combat, I would make 3 changes. Firstly, the dodge roll cool down needs to be MUCH shorter. Cooldowns on skills also need to be much shorter, or at the very least, skills should trigger faster. The bow shotgun blast, for example, has a weird, slow, clunky wind up. It should fire the instant you press the button, as should other skills that aren't specifically meant to be changed. As it stands, combat flows very awkwardly because you're forced to either just stand there and chug health potions, or constantly back away. Now, obviously, with shorter cooldowns and longer days, the game suddenly becomes too easy, which comes to my last suggestion. A lot more enemies around the map during the day, and a bit more at night; and if Joutunn are found to be too easy, then boost their HP/Damage as necessary, I'd suggest about 25% more of each for the start.Just a few simple changes and I think that would dramatically improve the game's flow.Also, is it just me, or does the fact that you instantly break rocks and trees feel really weird to anyone else? I get the reason - it's to keep game flow because days are so short - but it feels WEIRD.Edit: I should also point out that I do agree with most of the other reviews that combat in general lacks any kind of "weight" to it, and just feels awkward, but it's passable if you are ok with a weird mix of diablo and zelda.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think the marketing for this game was the most well done. I was expecting more of an ARPG with MMOy towns and house building, instead of a Tower Defence/Wave suvival game. But I think it is pretty fun overall and I love the art style. I enjoy pushing out in a direction and exploring, gearing up my guy and fighting big norse baddies, defending the town and throwing up defenses. Also there are no survival mechanics, its take damage, do damage, die, retrieve your lootbox before it disappears. You don't eat, sleep, or drink so don't worry about that.As far as some of the other reviews complaints, I only had connection problems very briefly this morning after launch and its been gone all day now -- I've been online matchmaking, no solo. Also there is a free-form build mode, its not just the gates and towers, but it is a bit lackluster. You press C by default and it consists of walls and fences for extra defense/pulling enemy aggro, "ground" for making bridges across rivers or ravines, and ramps for climbing up to shrines or buildables (quarry, lumberyard),I think the game really could have benefited from something to flesh out your character/playstyle outside of the match besides just the cosmetics. The problem is, I don't really know what they should or could have used to do so given the format of the game. I think Red Solstice 2 did that part well though. There's a pretty nice skill tree and loadout system built in for customizing your character and tailoring your playstyle outside of matches, then all the random items you find in game. I think pulling the classes out of the realtime gameplay into the menus, making it something you spec out before you join maybe along with starting weapons, might possibly help a lot with replayability. RS2 also has map modifiers, more enemies, less random items, etc. for more XP/more risk or less XP/less risk, another idea for ToM considering in 6-7 games I have yet to even repair the bridge and I got bifrosted twice.Also, the tutorial sucks. It does not explain that freeform building even exists and make sure you pay attention to the multiple tabs at vendors (took me almost 2 full rounds before I realized the tool vendor is where you process raw material for building supplies, its not just the random barricades you find). Finally, it might be better to play with a controller, only because the controls aren't very "tight" anyway and combat feels very floaty -- I think the controller vibration might really help it suck less :D Also as far as mouse precision, good luck to all ranged characters anyway lmao

_childDocuments_.review: Tribes of Midgard : By Triple F"Tribes of Midgard" by Norsfell Games is a unique blend of action-RPG and survival mechanics that plunges players into a vibrant, Norse-inspired world where the primary objective is to defend a village against ever-encroaching threats. With a mix of crafting, combat, and cooperative play, the game challenges players to gather resources, fortify defenses, and battle waves of mythological creatures, all while preparing for the impending doom of Ragnarok. Offering both solo and multiplayer modes, "Tribes of Midgard" delivers a fast-paced survival experience that is accessible to newcomers but also provides enough depth to keep seasoned players engaged.The game’s world, Midgard, is a procedurally generated environment that combines lush forests, icy mountains, and sprawling plains, populated with diverse wildlife and enemies inspired by Norse mythology. This dynamic setting encourages exploration and rewards players with resources necessary for survival and crafting. As players venture out, they’ll encounter camps, rare resources, and increasingly dangerous foes that challenge their ability to survive. Each session feels distinct, thanks to the procedural generation and day-night cycles that influence enemy behaviors, giving players a reason to explore different strategies and adapt to new challenges with each playthrough.At the core of "Tribes of Midgard" is its cycle-based structure, with each day requiring players to gather materials and upgrade their village defenses before nightfall, when waves of Helthings, giants, and other enemies attack. This cycle adds urgency to each action, as players must balance their time between exploration, gathering resources, and defending the Seed of Yggdrasil, the village’s lifeline. The looming threat of Jotnar, massive giants that spawn periodically, requires teamwork and strategic preparation to fend off successfully. This daily pressure keeps gameplay focused and intense, and the unpredictability of giant attacks adds a thrilling layer to the cycle.Combat in "Tribes of Midgard" is fast-paced and responsive, with a variety of weapons and abilities that allow players to customize their playstyle. Players can choose from different classes, each with unique skills and perks that suit various roles, such as tanking, healing, or dealing high damage. The game’s class system is well-designed, allowing players to mix and match weapons and abilities to find their ideal setup. Weapons range from swords and hammers to bows and staffs, and each has its own combat feel and upgrade path. Combat is straightforward but requires timing and precision, especially during larger encounters with elite enemies or bosses, which demand teamwork and coordination.Resource management and crafting are integral to the "Tribes of Midgard" experience. The game places heavy emphasis on gathering resources to upgrade village defenses, craft new gear, and build structures. As players progress, they unlock new recipes and structures that aid in both offense and defense, from upgraded walls to weapon forges. Managing resources efficiently is crucial to success, especially during later stages when resources become scarce, and enemies grow more powerful. This system encourages players to strategize and plan ahead, balancing the need for immediate upgrades with long-term survival. However, the reliance on resource gathering can feel repetitive, especially in solo play, where the workload is significant.One of the highlights of "Tribes of Midgard" is its co-op mode, which allows up to 10 players to join forces and protect their village together. The game truly shines in this multiplayer environment, as players can divide roles, tackle larger threats, and pool resources more effectively. Communication and teamwork are vital, especially when facing Jotnar or higher-level enemies, as each player’s class and resources contribute to the group’s success. Multiplayer mode also helps alleviate the resource grind, as tasks are spread across team members, making for a more balanced and enjoyable experience. However, solo players may find the difficulty spikes more challenging, as the game’s design leans heavily on teamwork and cooperation.Visually speaking, "Tribes of Midgard" employs a stylized, colorful art style that brings the Norse world to life in a way that feels both mythic and approachable. The art direction is charming, with vibrant landscapes and unique character designs that give the game a distinct, storybook-like aesthetic. The creatures and bosses are particularly impressive, with giants towering over the landscape, and each enemy type has distinct visual cues that make them memorable and easy to identify in the heat of battle. Paired with a lively soundtrack that features Nordic-inspired tunes, the game creates an engaging atmosphere that complements the fast-paced gameplay.To summarize, "Tribes of Midgard" is an ambitious title that successfully combines survival mechanics with action RPG elements and a touch of Norse mythology. It delivers an experience that’s both accessible and challenging, with mechanics that encourage exploration, cooperation, and strategic planning. While solo play may feel repetitive and unforgiving at times, the game’s cooperative mode offers a rewarding experience for players who enjoy teamwork and dynamic challenges. For fans of survival games who want a fresh twist with a strong cooperative element, "Tribes of Midgard" is a creative and exciting journey through a beautifully crafted world on the brink of Ragnarok.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally followed this game in it's alpha test a couple of years ago, it looked like it had a bright future ahead of it. Sadly not much has changed from its original concept since then. Now I'm not to angry about how it changed from what was advertised   to being a roguelike how it is now, because one I really like rogue like games. Risk of rain 1 and 2 and other in the genre have held my attention for many hours before. This on the other hand feels like a poorly designed tower defense game with very minimal effort in its roguelike features. It has some kind of identity crisis that has been holding it back. I played through it a couple of times and I didn't feel the want or need to try another run which never happens for me in roguelikes specially since I'm the kind of person to keep playing them until I unlock most everything. * Pros: Beautiful graphics, great concept, amazing world lore, and over all strong core.* Cons: Lack of content, terrible pacing(the day night cycle is so fast that it feels like I'm always rushing when I want to be able to explore the world a little bit spend my time in a dungeon or two, it makes the game feel awful when the world looks so good.) , lack of roguelike elements( The dying and restarting rewards with nothing other than a couple of cosmetics and maybe a new rune which you most likely wont use), Poor tower defense mechanics (the upgrades consist of upgrading walls towers and merchants which can get expensive, this is slightly alleviated by the use of sawmills and other resource producing building there aren't really any options so customizing your base to deal with different types of enemies is non existent and in the end doesn't even matter once a giant comes knocking at the door.) Clunky combat mechanics for blocking and dodging (personally I prefer if I have the option of animation cancelling or stopping a combo midway through in these types of games but even without that I still find myself never blocking because dodging and being slow paced is more worth while than blocking with a shield or other weapon.) There's other things I could go into but if you aren't discouraged yet than you could see for yourself. I really hope that maybe they come out with more game modes in their "seasons" that they are doing that add some of the features I was hoping for because I was really hoping for this game to be all that it promised. Sadly this is a pass for me.

_childDocuments_.review: By the bearded beard of Odin, "Tribes of Midgard" is as dull as watching ice melt in the eternal winter of Niflheim! This game, if it can even be called that, is a yawning chasm of tedium, a mind-numbing endeavor that would make even the most stoic of dwarves fall into a deep slumber.In this sorry excuse for an adventure through the realms of Norse mythology, one can expect no grand epic, no heroic quests, and certainly no exhilarating battles. Instead, we are burdened with the soul-sucking chore of ceaseless resource gathering and defending a village that is as lifeless as the roots of Yggdrasil.The visuals are as uninspiring as a gloomy day in Helheim. Midgard, the jewel of the Nine Realms, is rendered with all the splendor of a mud puddle. The characters are as lively as a pile of rocks, lacking any spark of vitality or charisma.The gameplay is as monotonous as an endless recitation of Eddic poems. The controls are as clunky as the giants of Jotunheim, and the combat system feels as engaging as a debate with Mimir's severed head. One is condemned to an unending cycle of fetch quests and tedious crafting, with no sense of accomplishment to be found.In summary, "Tribes of Midgard" is a bleak mockery of our Norse heritage, a pitiful attempt to capture the grandeur of our sagas. It is a game that would send Tyr to sleep, one-handed or not, and make Frigg question the value of creation. I would sooner endure the endless winter of Fimbulvetr than subject myself to the numbing boredom of this wretched offering. May the Aesir and Vanir alike shield us from such tedious trials in the future. Skål to those brave souls who managed to endure this insufferable borefest – they truly deserve a place in the halls of Valhalla.

_childDocuments_.review: It definitely needs a lot of work.The combat is very floaty and definitely needs to be tighter. There needs to be some QoL improvements, like a Repair all Equipped Items button at the blacksmith, a better designed mini-map that shows nearby downed teammates, important loot, etc, a better crafting UI perhaps allowing you to craft mats wherever instead of only at the vendor, more information on the UI like your Tool durability. Classes also need to be reworked a bit to feel more meaningful, currently the differences feel too minor but there's also classes that feel just bad, like Guardian is all about blocking but blocking in this game is awful. First off you can't attack while blocking, 2nd off there are fairly quick attacks that can't be blocked and the attacks that can be blocked still deal damage to you, so it's actually better for your own survival + speed to just spam attack everything, dodge when needed and chug health pots if you're getting low. The roguelite system only unlocks different starting Gear for the most part which only changes the first 5-10 minutes of a game that can take hours, you can also unlock new runes that you can randomly find when playing but you don't find so many that you can actually create the build you want with them very easily. The runes are also no incredibly game changing, usually just being a "oh that's cool I guess" when you read their description.There's also a lot of mechanics at war with each other. Like pooling resources is how you get everything built, but if someone dies a lot they won't be able to pool Souls for upgrades/repairs/crafting as you lose all your souls on death. It forces you into a pretty boring "i don't want to die" gameplay style, which leads to farming easy combat encounters. The resources you gather on the map aren't per player as if someone else gathers it before you, you have to wait for those resources to respawn if you want to gather them. There's items like from chests/bosses/destroying walls that are given to everyone, but they're not marked on the map very well when they exist so people have to call them out. There's also no auto-loot system, you have to press F to pick up everything rather than just vacuuming them up. There's also the problem of selfishness involved, as each player can choose whether to put what they farmed into the community chest, the easiest way to win is be totally communist about it and share everything but sadly, not all players are going to have that mindset. Probably would be a better idea to just share all loot equally by default. IDK it's just weird.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 423 year old shoe-repair gnome and shopkeep.  I am a single father to my son, who is a two-week-old kitten. My son was begging for this game, so we bought it and installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 36 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always playing with his kitten friends or rolling around cutely on the floor. So I decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my son for help and he taught me how to click the mouse buttons and hit the keys on my keyboard and how to roll around cutely on the floor. Me and my son's favorite gamemode is survival, as we can leave the game alone for awhile and do cute kitten things together, and get screamed at by other players for not actually surviving.  This game has ever since brought me and my kitten-son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my son many happy memories.------------------Okay, snark aside, I've only played the survival mode with my wife, as we have a collective taste for craft-and-survival games.  And it's broadly fine, it'll pass the time for a dozen hours or so.  She's partial to Norse mythology though I'm not sure it had faerie cats per se.  Regardless!  It's fine.  You can build a base, they've added "plants" of a sort, the crafting benches have a radius where it can access chests, so there's some nice touches.Now, it bears the stink of potential microtransactions, but they've been ignored so far.  I guess you can buy spangly things for your character if you want, but I gotta be honest, I'm playing as an archer and my screen is max-zoomed-out, I won't see your precious pixels that well, not sure what the point is.And there's this annoying quirk where the game is hosted on their servers, and if the server decides to go down (which it did several times when we first played the game) you've lost the whole "day" of progress.  It also means if Gearbox tires of hosting the game, you're outta luck.There's this whole other "Saga" game mode, which might suit you if you're into a PvE-sort of MOBA-like affair with Ragnarok trappings.  But all of this is going to be exactly as good as the other players are, so... you know, I guess it's fine.And as a 423 year old shoe-repair gnome, I can say I bought it discounted and I'll get my money's worth over one or two playthroughs.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I'm going to share some pros and cons, although starting out I want to say definitely don't pay full price for this game, there are too many cons to be worth it. I paid $6.79 and honestly I would say it's only worth maybe $3.99. The videos and screenshots on the store page make it look way better than it actually is. Pros:- Art style is neat.- The ancient boss battles do feel epic and are very cool, although I've only seen Fenrir because none of my maps ever get to the other ones.Cons:- Tutorial is hidden and does a bad job of explaining game mechanics.- For multiplayer mode, you can have 10 people per map but the most I have seen is 3-4. Not busy enough to really get any objectives done, as Jotunn health and damage scales up hugely after day 15.- Chat box is hard to distinguish player chat from leveling spam and does not appear to have filter options. - Saga quests should be progressed map wide, without individual options. It is too hard to tell which objectives others are going for after the Jotunn is dead. - The amount of time to mount is a bit much, and should be shortened.- Some classes seem less balanced than others.- Class skills and attacks should have a bar placement mode- not being able to change keybinds or mouse buttons is restricting. - There is hardly any premium currency earned by weekly quests, so if you want an item costing silver in the cosmetics shop, you would basically be forced to buy microtransactions. Not a fan of this. The other currency you can earn in game, but is slow going and also if your map wipes you lose all horn currency you earned in that game.I think there is overall a lot of room for improvement in this game, it has potential but I wouldn't go crazy in time played in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... meh. Not really worth your time.I'll point out one thing i liked: combat. Pretty well-done and engaging when you unlock weapons with 3 abilities.Everything else is either mediocre or bad."Survival" part is non-existent, you don't really risk anything when dying apart from your stash with materials which is really easy to get. There is no hunger or thrist, too. There is temperature hazards but they are easily countered."Building" part is really bad too. It requires tinkering with camera for proper placement, you can't upgrade structures, each demolish comes with animation and it's easier to just build new house instead of upgrading your OG one unless you want to spend hours.The worst part, IMO, is that you need to play Saga to unlock top weapons. I came for your usual survival game, and in theory i can play it, but to unlock endgame armor and weapons i'm forced into saga mode. And multiple times, too, because challenges are "kill same boss X times".In-game skin shop uses predatory mechanics straight from mobile games - ie skin pack costs 2300, but you can only buy 2200, 1050 or 500. I also wanted to play that on steam deck while offline, but turns out even single-player mode runs on their servers. Meaning always online requirement.There is also really annoying challenges to unlock certain items, like fish 100 times or spend 1 million souls.It's pretty cool for first couple of hours, then it starts getting dull and boring.

_childDocuments_.review: First 10-15 hours of the game were enjoyable, the recent serpent update gave me about 4 more hours of enjoyable content, but it gets boring very quickly, and here's why.The first few hours, you'll likely spend learning the game, not knowing what to do at all, and this is enjoyable. After this phase, after you've killed the saga bosses a few times, it gets extremely repetitive, with the only real difference between each game being the map. The main problem is that most of the things that you could do in this game just aren't worth doing. Bows are one of these things, trust me, I've tried for hours to make bows work, even with full ranged runes, you'll still be under-performing, even against single targets. The only decent thing about bows is that you can change which arrows you use to deal different damage types (good luck finding these arrows early game.) Furthermore, none of the bow abilities do significant damage at all, even the legendary bow's third ability is pretty bad. The fact that bows can't deal significant damage makes the ranger, and hunter classes significantly weaker. As it stands, hunter and ranger are only good for exploration which is sad because firstly, exploration isn't really that useful now that maps are extremely easy to get, and secondly, seer and warden are actually  at exploration than the ranger or hunter. There are many more things in this game that just aren't worth using, such as the guardian/sentinel classes, most of the starter kits, frost weapons (their abilities suck, and frost weapons are extremely hard to get for what they do,) and more. All this combined means that you usually only really see the same 3-4 builds in every single game, and if you try to deviate, you'll have a pretty rough time compared to everyone else.Mind you, most of these things can be fixed, but until they are, I have to give this game a negative review. The only reason I'll be playing this game is to max out my season level, but even that's not really worth it anymore since you can now just buy stuff from previous seasons.

_childDocuments_.review: Tribes of Midgard saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: Review is based solely on the story mode, I haven't played Saga mode but I don't know if I want to.1. Fun first half, second half gets very repetitive very fast.When everything was new, it felt great to explore and craft... but once you got a feel for the game, you realize how repetitive and tedious it is. As your character gets stronger, enemies become nuisances and dungeons/enemy camps become chores.2. Unnecessarily big maps.There's 4 biomes in the game spread out randomly according to your generation but they always just have the same few things. If you've seen the biomes on your starting island, you've seen the biomes on the far edge of the map, making exploration beyond the 4 biomes you found earliest to be redundant. There's also nothing to do while sailing beyond dodging the occasional obstacles and stupid sea serpent you can't even attack. It's honestly god-awful spending close to 15 minutes sailing and dodging other islands just to get to the far off quest mark.3. Lack of build diversityThe biggest sin in my opinion. With the way runes stack and having different weapons and elements in the game, it opened up potential to so much they can do with the gameplay... but in the end you're just going to either stack the naked rune together (give damage if you're not wearing armor) or the fenrir runes together (give 2x damage if you're below 50% health) in late game... and all you're doing is mostly just spamming attack. Other runes pale heavily in comparison.THE SKILLS ARE USELESS.They're slow and doesn't do as much damage as your regular attacks when you have the level 1 berserk stacked up. And if you're like me, you'll realize only the bow is really worth investing into... other weapons put you in harm's way without much option of self-preservation (that the bow doesn't have) and doesn't deal nearly as much damage to make up for it as the bow can oneshot regular enemies anyway. An exception is the axe for late game bosses but all it does is save you a bit of time.4. Constant CrashesI don't know if it's just me, but I've had the game crash several times on several occasions. To the point that, get this, it saved my first save in a spot where I just crash when loading in... (outside some dungeon) and I had to redo my game. TBH it's not that big of a deal... WHEN THE AUTOSAVE WORKS. But sometimes I get a game crash and when I load back in, the last autosave was maybe 30 minutes to 1 hour prior to the crash and that's just disheartening.I had high hopes for this game when I started, when it's at its peak, the game's fun and simple... eventually, I just end up feeling like it's not worth to even play to completion. I bought this on sale and it was still a bit disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't know what it wants to be, and it doesn't even try to explain itself. You've got tower defense elements, adventure RPG elements, survival crafting elements, and even an overarching story. Yet...there are so many things wrong with it that I've failed to even SUMMARIZE them here without writing a 5-page essay on it all. Several times I've just cleared it out because I want to keep this concise.The TD elements exist, but it's unclear as to whether it's even worth using them, because as a whole, they suck. Utilizing them requires sacrificing resources that could be used elsewhere.The RPG elements exist, but they require doing quests, which are often nonsense. You run halfway across the map for an NPC to tell you "you know what to do" - without an explanation, btw, literally nothing - and the only goal of the quest is on the MAP page. It's often terrifically vague, like "kill an elite monster" - but to this day, I still don't even know what an "elite" monster IS or where they live. Even if you do do them though, the rewards typically suck, but you actually NEED to do them to beat the game - not that it tells you that anywhere.Doing anything requires gathering resources, which basically boils down to pressing "F" on trees, bushes, rocks, grass, and flowers. You want to hit everything you run into. Literally everything. Note that if you don't run into silver, then your tools will break and you will be left at the base tier, forced to sacrifice resources just to keep the things working.There's a map, and a legend on the map, but all the stuff that really matters isn't even mentioned on the legend.The guides online are pretty terrible, and the tutorial in the game doesn't cover half of it. It doesn't feel like it, but it is fast-paced; you can't dawdle reading item descriptions in your base. You will have to do that to learn the game, but doing so basically means throwing your run away. At the same time, you have to survive until later to learn the later stuff, which means sacrificing further runs. There is no pausing, and you cannot revert to a save point; it autosaves at the start of each day and at undefined "checkpoints" that aren't announced or explained.Learning it requires starting runs, doing well, stopping to learn/experiment, losing, then trying again. It's frustrating and, frankly, boring. Never once have I felt excited about anything. The talent trees are boring as hell, and so are the items. There are other classes, but they're really not that different from the main two you start with. It's a bad game.However: If you and friends have played through other multiplayer coop games and can't find anything else good, this will probably satisfy the craving for a few hours. So, it's still a bad game, but you can still enjoy a bad game with friends, so...yeah.

_childDocuments_.review: 12h mark review:Some of the solo mode issues were addressed in a patch and playing a bit more definitely helps with getting used to the commands and flow of combat. From my current perspective, the previous review was rushed and doesn't do it justice. It's really a different experience now and I can definitely recommend it. Solo mode is challenging at times, but as you get a better idea of what you need to do (and what you need to avoid doing) it turn into a pleasurable "hunt", for those few resources/drops that you need for your next weapon/armor/upgrade. I have only scratched the surface of what the game has to offer.4h mark review:Not a complete review, by any measure, but it's what I got out of my first 4 hours of (solo) play.I got the impression that it takes too much resources to re-build things, for a solo player. I'm barely able to gather enough iron and stone for a single gate, let alone think about archer towers or re-building the lumber camp, quarry or farm.Even then, the gate gets destroyed and needs to be re-build from scratch. Maybe a different repair system can be introduced at that point. Something that needs less resources to repair, that it took to re-build it.The archer class could also probably use some more powerful weapon options that don't require high-level crafting materials, and the tutorial needs some additional chapters, like building, reaching cliffs, leveling up your class i.e. distributing skill points. I did my first two playthroughs waiting for a class system to show itself.The fact that it's primarily meant for console players (controls are a bit clunky and unintuitive on K&M) also doesn't help. Click to walk&attack would be a must-have for a PC version. The attack is there, but the controls would be better if the click allows you to do do different things in different situations, perhaps even gather resources when the character is out of combat and the location clicked has a harvestable resource.I also noticed an issue with the combat when you have the shield out. As long as you're just attacking, the character attacks in the direction of the mouse pointer. Press Shift to hold the shield and the character is locked towards the WASD movement directions, even when you're simultaneously trying to block and attack i.e. hold Shift and Left Click.I think the game has huge potential, but it does need some additional work. Also, the RM-Shop is completely unnecessary, in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for January 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before January 3th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A fun survival game with a focus on battle. Tribes of Midgard does a lot to let people get into the survival genre.  Looting of items is extremely fast, players can level up and build up their base and character as they want.  The entire game is based on trying to survive, as long as the player can, against an onslaught of enemies, including impressive giant Jotuns, and if players fail the game resets and has the player start over on a different map to make different choices.The other side is while the tutorial is good, there’s a lot to understand, to the point I would say most players are going to have to spend 5-10 hours just to understand the proper flow of the game or read a guide.  But there’s a bigger problem.  There is a cash shop, which appears to be limited to cosmetic items, and a battle pass, with daily or weekly quests, that’s something I always call out.  With Ubisoft and Gearbox Publishing involved with the game’s launch, I worry. Pick this up if you like survival games, especially if you want to partner up with a few people and play a game.  This has a 10-player online multiplayer which is unique, and while there’s only a horde mode and a survival mode, it does feel like there’s a decent amount of content here to keep you entertained. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

Sitting there for 45 seconds holding the mouse button down to donate materials is ridiculous. Overwhelmingly, what you want as a player is to donate all materials necessary. _childDocuments_.review: Despite not recommending the game, I am going to continue playing it. So what's my issue?Combat: The combat is really unresponsive. If your character is in a move, you have no control over him until he finishes said move. It is indeed annoying being unable to dodge while attacking, but just git gud, right? Indeed you start playing around this handicap, but where you really feel the weight is with shields. I really like shields in any game, but here it feels like a handicap to even consider using it. Staggering the opponent with such an unresponsive combat system is hard enough (at least against faster opponents, not those slow mofos), but even if you stagger, the gain is low (not to forget you still take damage when you block normally).Season Experience: In this game, you have no real level, but you can farm exp for the season to unlock rewards. This includes starter kits, cashshop currency, decoration or golden horns for other shop items. The problem is, that this is the only feeling of progression you get and for that it is really slow. A Saga mode to day 15 nets you more or less than 30.000 exp. Level ups after the very first few start costing 22.000 exp however. Doesn't sound bad, right? But those 15 days take quite a long time and they take quite some time irl. The amount of time you have to invest feels too steep. I did several runs so far, killed the saga boss 5 times and I'm still around level 15 of 50. When you know what to do the game loop isn't interesting enough to invest hours of your time for the seasonal experience.Shop: I was quite surprised seeing a cash shop in a buy title. After Skyrim selling horse armor as a DLC, it shouldn't be that surprising, but it still leaves a bad aftertaste to see it. At least you get some coins from the season progress and everything you can buy with those coins is only decorational, so don't deter from the game because of this. What bothers me more is the items for the golden horns. The shop shows you 3 items every rotation you can buy with those golden horns, which you can randomly find in your playthrough, get 1 per Jotunn you slay and another 5 for defeating the saga boss. Meaning you can get all golden horn items by playing 1-2 games (if you can slay the saga boss, otherwise those 1-2 turn into 4-6 runs). However I am strongly repelled by blueprints needing to be bought. As a new player you jump into the game, want to make a Raider Axe III (as an example), just to see you don't have the blueprint to even try it out. So you have to wait until a part of the game appears in the shop. This really shouldn't be a thing.EDIT: It is funny watching the buggy physics to sometimes sling enemies or trees at mach 3 speeds through the world. It is less funny if you place a Jar and you are stuck inside it.EDIT EDIT: It seems they fixed shields. Pressing the shielding button now instantly puts it up if you aren't performing a move instead of waiting for the animation to finish. They also block more of the damage. Makes shields good enough to be used again.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Tribes of Midgard gets its priorities wrong and, thanks to the overall jank and seriously awful design decisions, makes for a grindy, quickly repetetive slog that is only really fun with friends (which really shouldn't be a good argument or selling point for any game, since that applies to every single game in existence)It's definitely a Co-op game at heart, but unfortunately the devs failed to balance the game around that idea, especially when it comes to matchmaking. They somehow managed to make it Co-op UNfriendly, with mechanics that actively encourage abandoning your party, splitting up, getting annoyed at each other, or Soloing.There's also a very strange and unfitting Fortnite influence that was clearly tacked on later in development (an awful building system and actual fortnite skins).Highly not recommended unless the devs completely change their approach to balancing and game design... or you already have a friends group to play with.---------------------------------------------This showed a lot of potential in the early Beta release. I really wanted to like it too, but some of the design decisions are extremely worrying.Unfortunately, the game really hasn't changed much at all since then, and it remains a good IDEA with mediocre to completely awful execution. What SHOULD be a fun time in theory turns out to be a frustrating slog and grind for the most part, especially when it comes to the most critical, game-defining aspect of it all: Co-op.Here's the most critical issues in the current (release, 08/2021) state of the game:-The game balances heavily around playercount. The more players (up to 10) there are in a match, the more enemies will spawn and the harder they will be to kill, and the less materials and souls each player will get. Scaling is nothing new, not a bad idea right? But oh boy, the devs sure managed to make it an awful idea:-Players are not really encouraged to work together, but to split up and go off on their own. Gathering nodes are first come first serve, so players are COMPETING for space on the map, which can leave some players void of resources if the other players don't share what they gather. Since the entire game is also a ticking timebomb that never stops ramping up in difficulty, players are further encouraged to split up to find all the hideouts, world merchants, camps, Jotunn spawns, biomes, Waypoints... and on and on.-Players can leave midgame, and take anything they want with them, including everything in the shared storage. There is no way to get those things back for the other players.-If players leave via the Bifrost (a "get me out of here" portal that takes that player out of the game along with all their stuff) they get REWARDED with the shop currency. Players that stay in the game and possibly fail do NOT get that currency. Wew. But wait, it gets worse:-One of the class unlocks ENCOURAGES people to abandon matches the moment they kill the first Jötunn (which is basically a tutorial boss, and at which point no further, new players can join)... TEN TIMES!Another class unlock encourages players to discover the entirety of the map, which is a waste of effort and manpower if new players don't know wtf they're doing.this is honestly one of the strangest and most worrying design decision in the history of gaming, and does not exactly instill much confidence in the competence of the devs.What this creates is an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of matchmaking where randoms are encouraged to leave early and take their scrap winnings rather than stick around and actually finish a match. And no, this isn't just an issue in earlygame, the whole Bifrost "get me out of here" mechanics ENCOURAGES people to abandon their party for their own gain at the slightest sight of trouble, or even just for efficiency. For a supposed Co-op game, this is literally the worst possible thing to implement.-Instadeaths, difficulty spikes: Apparently, Vikings can't swim. When you roll into a puddle of water, you instantly die and lose all your souls and half your materials. Enemies can also knock you into those instant death traps. every enemy has some sort of knockback attack. Oh, also falling a couple of feet instakills you. Fall-damage is %-based and almost everything is covered in randomly generated mountain patches. Better not roll the wrong way, or you're instantly dead. -The "souls"-like system: Yes, they even called it souls. When you die, you instantly lose all of them, with no way to get them back. Souls are required for upgrading a bunch of town stuff, repairing your gear, buying things, keeping the world tree alive... basically the main currency. When you run out, you can't repair any of your gear, so you better hope it's not broken when you die. Also better hope your teammates didn't die with a bunch of souls on them, and that they actually SPEND them (and hopefully on the right stuff)-The game is actually easier to play solo (if a bit more stressful). From actually visible attacks with no micrustutter or lag, to no resource competition, to easier mobs in general. Again, an impressive feat from the devs, for a supposed Co-op game.-Exploration and knowledge about the game is handled in a strange way. New players start out utterly confused and lost in the world with basically an ingame wikipedia to read through for information, while the doomsday clock is ticking nonstop. There is no random generation in anything but the terrain: Biomes will always be the same, with the same materials and enemies in them. Gear always requires the same region-specific materials to craft. -Knowledge of how to get those things is required to actually craft your items in the first place. Some resources only spawn at night for example, in certain biomes, so you have to know that beforehand or figure out through trial and error. Which leads to: New players don't know wtf they're looking for, how to get it, or how to progress or contribute. Players who do know speedrun through their pre-planned strategy, since everything is the same progression path every time. -It's basically a steep, stressful learning curve that immediately flattens out and flatlines once you understand how the game works. There's nothing new to learn or explore once you know where to get everything and how to progress, and very little variation in approach and gameplay for veterans.-There's also a lack of interesting progression in any of the RPG systems. Classes are very barebones with only 10 points to spend in a skilltree of 14 points total. There's very few weapons that all play fairly similarly (4 moveset archetypes with 1-3 active skills locked to weapon) And once again the ridiculous design decisions marr the experience, with things like ingame crafting unlocks or starter kits locked behind *random daily rotating Shop offers* (a selection of 5 items that change every day, and another 5 that change ONCE A WEEK. good luck, and better log in every day to potentially get that unlock you need :)-Lastly, in case you were confused from the tl;dr: Yes. There's also a definite Fortnite influence with most of the shop items being ridiculously unfitting colour-explosion skins ripped straight out of fortnite, which... make of that what you will. (one of the first pets on offer was a dancing pink rainbow bear, the first weapon set was sparkly Rainbow-coloured, and the first armor set was a purple sumo/boxer outfit, for some godforsaken reason, with likely more random quirkiness to come, rather than anything fitting the setting)
