_childDocuments_.review: A game that threw a few too many systems into the mix for me to find fun.GatheringCraftingExplorationBoss BattlesBase Defense...This all may work better in multiplayer when you have friends to help, but in solo, your attention just gets split up too much for you to focus.The combat is ok, if stiff, where you are a slave to the animation locking you in place while you attack, which means you can't click spam, as then you are stuck when the bosses attack lands.But between the game wanting you at the far reaches exploring, and back at the base defending almost every single night, I just did not have fun playing this on my own.  Sure, upgrading your weapons to do more damage seems fun, but it's less fun when you were just out in the wilderness, and had to either burn your teleport stone or find a portal to come all the way back, chop up some bad guys for the night and then finally get to talk to someone and wade through menus to find the right thing that is the upgrade to whatever you have.Then there's the construction...  Which seems to be in the game to justify the horrible terrain generation, which makes anything of a different level just separated by a sheer cliff...  It was 4 hours of game before I realized that i was supposed to build my own ramps instead of just use the terrain like every other diablo like game ever has taught me to do.  I still couldn't figure out how to build down (maybe that's what the invert incline button is supposed to be for), and the whole building system is just so slow and clunky I don't know who it's supposed to be fore except to be a cross between fortnight and diablo...

_childDocuments_.review: A good surprise !I would describe this game as being an action RPG, putting the emphasis on exploration (on foot, on horse or even with a drakkar !) and fighting with a good part of crafting and building.You are left almost free in a sort of sandbox world, starting naked like in many games of this type, but with a story ! It is yours to build up your character and your wares, there is a questline to follow, with objectives and boss to fight, as well as side missions with various rewards and things to accomplish, all that in the order you desire.On your path you will unlock better equipements and progress throught a skill three offering varied capacity, but you are also free to build a home, an outpost or whatever you desire, harvesting threes and rock, hunting animals, fishing like you would expect in a survival game.There are many hours awaiting you to beat the game, solo or co-op with friends, and after that you can play endlessly in saga mode, trying to fight against time and waves of ennemies to save the Yggdrasil tree, co-operating with up to 10 players !This is definitly a game to own and to give a chance, you will certainly enjoy, especially with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Due to poor marketing, this game just really isn't what I thought it would be.The closest comparison I could draw would be Risk of Rain, where the core gameplay loop is trying to grow your power enough to beat a boss/get as far as you can before you're overwhelmed.I was expecting it to be more of an ARPG/survival game, but those aspects are secondary and not the focus.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain meets Don't Starve Together.A lot of the complaints I have seen in this game are time based to cost based. This honestly comes from lack of experience. After a few games you get in your groove of what to do and when. Once you learn what you SHOULD be doing at any given time you begin to walk through the games. Until then though, the learning curve feels stressful with how fast you need to move and progress. This game is NOT solo only friendly. Not by any means. Matchmaking however. Amazing and simple and well done. Join a local game, get partied with a few randoms and go from there. Generally great experiences with this. SO to buy or not to buy-BUY IF:-You enjoy Temp gameplay with overall account progression-Working with others-JRPG combat-Weird conversations with strangers-Base Defense-Enjoy difficult gamesDON'T BUY IF:-You give up easily-Don't handle learning curves well-Don't play well with others-Difficult games arent your forte-Dont like Nords

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tentative yes.Solo mode is pretty great. Game is toxic with only two people. I don't like playing with random people, I don't want to have to play with random people, and if you want to beat this game you have to play with random people.So if you like randoms or have a boat load of friends, absolutely get it. IF you like solo roguelikes then go ahead and give it a go. But when they scale enemies in online mode to not only having higher health but higher resistances as if there were more than two of you that gets out of hand IMO. I only want to play games with people I know, I like to coordinate with people I know, and I don't want to deal with randoms. So this game is a no for me.The only saving grace is that the game cost $20 bucks and I have spent much more on much worse, so while I am disappointed it isn't like I am going to go off and scream for a refund. Solo mode is fun but I'll never see anything but the first 3 classes playing that way, so there isn't really much else to try and accomplish in this game. Wish they had scaled it to party size, but whatever

_childDocuments_.review: If you take even a step out of the village its too late the Jotunn is already kicking your ♥♥♥♥ in.Seems like it could be fun after some major changes but it seriously needs some changes to economy of materials, durability of items & time per day and many more elements.Matchmaking is a complete mess as soon as you join all the trees, rocks, flint & branches needed to craft basic tools are gone so you are genuinely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ from the get-go, when you hit account level 3 you get an item that lets you start with those tools to actually be able to do anything but you have to suffer until you get there, why? is that the 'roguelike' part of the game? I'm not a fan of wasting time just to get an arbitrary few levels up just to actually be able to properly play.Solo play is tough, if you're not well equipped enough by day 3-4 you're going to have a bad time as there will already be a Jotunn slowly making its way to 1-shot your village as its extremely unlikely you'll have the defences to deal with it.Every day that goes by will just be a mad rush to get resources and quests completed to deal with the next night-time pillaging by enemies that arrive at nightfall so you really can't explore at your own pace.If you're expecting a survival game this isn't it and it honestly feels like this game hasn't marketed itself properly as the game feels more like base defence battle-royale with the seed of yggdrasil you defend being the entire lobby's only life.I'm going to hold off on playing more of this until the early game is bettered as it is far too punishing and rush resources reliant to be worth your time and this is coming from someone who thoroughly enjoys both grind & difficulty in many games.

_childDocuments_.review: Tribes of Midgard is a fun survival game both solo and with friends. You start off in a small village which you need to defend against "Hellthings" (at night) and "Jotuns" (Giants). In order to protect your village you can upgrade it by building and upgrading walls and archer towers. Any player can choose a class they want to play. Each class offers different perks that can help you / your group defend your village. Pros:+ Fluid combat + Randomly generated maps+ Rewards that can help you in future runs+ Classes with different perks. It makes sense to pick different classes in group play. + The developers are going the release future updates for the game each season. + You gain access to different skills depending on the weapon you are using. Cons:- The game has a couple bugs that should be fixed rather sooner than later. Most of them aren't game breaking tho. - Dodge rolling allows players to cover height (only downhill). However it can also lead to death if you accidently roll into water. This may not sound like a big deal, but it is super annoying in my opinion. - The game starts getting less interesting once you get better. As of now the game offers about 20-50 hours of content. A single run (saga mode) usually takes between 1.5 - 3 hours. - Building in this game is pretty much inexistant. All you can build yourself are ramps. Anything else is pretty much useless.

_childDocuments_.review: inb4 "what about bugs? what about the marketing? the steam tags?"- if you don't watch gameplay videos before buying a product, sucks to suck, especially after what we received from Biomutant and Cyberpunk.- As for bugs, the game just released. We also only spent a grand total of 30 bucks for this game. So, I'll be reviewing it as a slightly pricey indie game.TLDR; an amazing $20 game that I would've happily forked more money for. a welcome surprise after the disappointing releases of recent triple A titles. simple roguelite survival fitted over gearing up for later runs- akin to RoR2.Pros:- Vikings.- An excellent art direction, similar to BOTW.- Combat feels nice, customization feels great.- Free "battle pass" where you level up just by actually playing the game, you don't need to buy anything.- Cosmetics that you can earn, or buy, but earning isn't as grindy as other games.- Solo play is tweaked to be easier.- Multiplayer still feels difficult, not everything is handed to you on a platter.- Builds matter. You can't just hack and slash everything.Cons:- Various bugs. I can get stuck, or sometimes when I go to level up it'll use 2 points. Nothing actually game breaking though.- Cap out at level 10, leaving you to have to be very selective over abilities.- Resources feel too scarce for the amount that you have to use.- Some classes feel just naturally better. Needs some balancing.- Solo play is inherently more difficult regardless of tweaks. Resources need balancing, as well as time restraints.- Quests feel unrewarding. Most of the time I have higher tier gear before I'm able to finish a quest that would give me a low tier item.Tribes of Midgard is a roguelite style game where you're dropped into a vast world filled with demons, bandits, and various enemies. Your goal? Keep a tree alive, and manage your small village. This means collecting resources, absorbing souls from enemies, and doing quests. Explore a large scale map, craft gear, upgrade your village and survive nights where demons come to try to destroy your tree. Every few days, a large elemental giant will spawn in. You must take down this formidable foe to activate a portal that allows you to escape and end the game, thus collecting experience for cosmetics, as well as in game currency, and bonus experience to grant you items and boosts to assist in other runs. Complete tasks to unlock classes to suit your play style, and spend skill points to tailor your ability set to how you want to play the game. Rinse, repeat, simple.Failure to protect your tree will result in game over, where your character dies, and you lose a significant amount of gained experience- as well as no in game currency.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I have changed my mind on this game. The pro's and Cons are still valid I feel but the game has grown on me since I wrote this review and now I understand how it all works I am finally enjoying the game.The game has a pretty sharp learning curve and that took me some getting used too. Nothing is explained properly.  You have to read EVERYTHING every tool tip every thing you pick up. That is how I finally understood how important some items are. There are no help guides around to guide you, they all go on about weapons and armour. The most important item to CRAFT yourself in this game is the GATHERING TOOLS. You need RARE or above to get resources quickly Silver being the most important early on. Once you get the hang of that, and upgrade The tinker to level 3 you can start to build defences (most important early on) then move onto the quarry, farm and lumber mill resources. The game is still stupidly hard and even now I am enjoying it, I do not think this game is for every fan of ARPG out there.The waves are still dumb, and the bosses have way too much hp. The blood moons are broken and you 100% cannot solo this game without tons of luck on the map or resources. Even small groups is still impossible to get past day 4/8 unless you have a constant group of people on the server who know what they are doing.PROS:* Nice graphics* Norse Mythology* Good sound design* Randomly generated maps* RNG loot generation* Action RPG Combat is fun and simple* Easy to pick up and play* Fun with friends just as enjoyable with randoms (so far)CONS- Game play is not explained well and is a steep learning curve- Game difficulty is way too hard as single player or in a small group- Game play is repetitive and gets old pretty quickly- Useless classes. The only good one for damage is warrior. Ranger has gathering benefits. Hunter needs work. Guardian is boring and just buffs shield and is a tank that does no damage. The rest are still locked.- Has a In game store that is basically a pay to win for those that want to unlock in game progression quicker than farming the golden horns. I.E paying for Raider axe 3 unlock (which is daft why it is in here) with golden horns to get it faster than farming for it (like i did)- Music is drab and not epic enough- The waves are way to unbalanced during blood moon. You get a blood moon at wave 3/4 (usually) it is impossible to survive unless you got super lucky with resources.- Giant enemies have way to much hp and do too much damage to the tree (if they get to it) it is game over if they get past your walls / defences- Broken Physics leads to hilarious things flying out of the sky. Like trees and enemies getting stuck on your head as you move around.- You can only have one saved multiplayer game and one saved single player game. Why? Makes no sense to do this. Considering you can pick different classes?It is somewhat Overpriced for what you get and should not be a full release however the game is enjoyable if you can get past the steep learning curve and have friends to play with. As a solo ARPG avoid until it is balanced for single player. Or wait for mods to come out or even cheat engine to work on it if you expect single player progression. As it stands right now it is a fun game, but it is tedious and annoying most of the time. It has that "one more run" itch but it really does need balancing and improving. Once they do this, the game will be extremely enjoyable.Overall: 6 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: Get this game if you enjoy games like Diablo and tower defense games. At first I didn't know if I would keep playing it ...then I kept going back more and more. There is some strategy to consider in approaching base defense so it's not a brain dead experience. There is loot, crafting, and carnage. There is replay value due to some of the solo difficulty and the cosmetics. Hopefully they add more content as the seasons progress beyond cosmetics but for the cost of the game this is completely fine so far.*Edit: I have put in roughly another 20 hours..I see people saying that public games are full of chaos and people leaving. _childDocuments_.review: Game is legit fun but not perfect. Short answer is you should buy it if you have fun. Its good fun time. You won't be playing this very long way like you do with RDR2 or GTA5. This is 20 dollar game and it delivers that 20 dollars 6.8/10. it's good playing with peepal.One major grip i have with the game is its Animation.. from cutting wood, mining... to fights, blocking and hit registration.. animations lack a lot of weight. For a lot of effort i see in Art-style in this game but animation department is really not catching up. I hope they can improve everything in a big patch.. the whole experience could have been great but cut short by almost half due to floaty animations.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Those looking for the game to be easier, survival mode lets you change the game settings to do just that (or the opposite) which can make it much more enjoyable to the casual player.This game is such a nice experience with some roguelike elements. It's almost reminiscent of Don't Starve in which if you die, you're gunna have to start from the beginning in a new world BUT you get xp and unlock stuff depending on your progress.The combat reminds me a bit of diablo and games similar to that. You have your usual hold left click and attack whatever your mouse is over and then you have your ability keys. It's a great time with friends and if you're on the edge of whether or not you want it - get it and play it with some people. It's a fun and challenging game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tribes of Midgard

_childDocuments_.review: Tribes of Midgard is a beautiful game to interact within, and it definitely is something that could develop into an even better game than it is currently.  The tutorial needs a bit of work on teaching the player more about the world they will be engaging in as I could see newer players racing straight into the multiplayer experience. When you have a solid group to play alongside the game goes smoothly and you can make it to the higher days. However with the matchmaking of multiplayer needing a complete repair, this game will be rough for those seeking out other players. Most matches you will join, within the first three days players will join and leave, or they will leave the second the first Jotunn has been slain. Thats just my take of the game though, try it out yourself or watch someone play it to really see if this is something you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Tribes of Midgard

_childDocuments_.review: In Tribes of Midgard players can play solo or co-op with a team of up to 10 players to resist the oncoming invasion of giants during Ragnarök. Set in worlds full of dark creatures, hidden gods, and abundant materials to be uncovered, players begin the game as a Viking living in a village that houses the Seed of Yggdrasil, which is the last bastion that protects the gods from the other realms.  Fans will need to explore the wilderness to craft new weapons and be prepared to defend the sacred center of your village from the grim shadows from Helheim that prey upon its power. All the while, giants stalk ever closer to the village, seeking to destroy Midgard and fulfill the prophecy of the end of the world.

name: Little Nightmares II
detailed_description: PC Enhanced Edition ✨ Dive into an unsettling adventure that you'll never forget, now enhanced in mesmerizing 4K at uncapped FPS. Little Nightmares II owners also get access for free to Little Nightmares II Enhanced Edition upgrades. The Enhanced version visual upgrade includes Ray-traced reflections, improved volumetric shadows, and increased game details such as interactive particles. A new immersive 3D soundscape mix will also be accessible in 5.1 and 7.1. to make your Little Nightmares II even more immersive. For optimal Enhanced experience: OPERATING SYSTEM: Windows 10 PROCESSOR: Intel Core i5-8400 | AMD Ryzen 5 1600 MEMORY: 8 GB RAM GRAPHICS: Nvidia GeForce RTX 2080, 8 GB | AMD RX 6800 Digital Deluxe Edition Purchase the Deluxe Edition and receive the following digital content: Little Nightmares II Full Game The Nomes’ Attic DLC Follow the Nomes to find this special in-game puzzle and unlock the Nomes’ hat as a reward upon completion. Full Digital Soundtrack Enjoy the full Little Nightmares II soundtrack, composed by Tobias Lilja from Tarsier Studios. “The Art of Little Nightmares II” Digital Artbook Dive into the making of Little Nightmares II with this 56-page artbook full of sketches, artwork and design decisions by the Tarsier Studios art team. A Wallpaper Set Mono & Six avatars About the Game A boy wakes up alone in the woods surrounded by the husks of burnt-out televisions. After stumbling through traps and pitfalls in the wilderness, he finds a girl locked in the basement of a dark and terrible house with only a music box to keep her company. This is their story. WORK TOGETHER OR DIE ALONE You play as Mono, the boy traveling with Six, his enigmatic companion. Although they never knew each other before their story began, they must find a way to cooperate as they try to survive the terrors and secrets of the Pale City. Mono can call Six to summon her, but she is also quite independent and observant. Pay attention to her cues and work together to open hidden trapdoors, climb giant furniture, and, if you’re feeling a little scared, hold hands as you both navigate a world never meant for children. STAY HIDDEN TO STAY ALIVE The Residents of the Nowhere are enormous, implacable adults like the Teacher or the Hunter who stalk any child Visitor foolish enough to catch their attention. When they’re around, it’s vital to remain quiet and out of sight, or your end will be quick and unpleasant. RUN FOR YOUR LIFE At times, hiding won’t be enough. If a Resident is chasing you, you’ll have to run as fast as you can, clambering over any obstacles in your way. Maybe you’ll be able to stay alive long enough to find a place where the danger can’t reach you… for now . IF YOU CAN’T RUN AND YOU CAN’T HIDE, YOU HAVE TO FIGHT Mono is strong-willed when he has to be. If you’re trapped with an enemy, look for something you can swing to fend them off. It’s tough work for a such a little kid, so time your attacks carefully. You won’t get a chance to make the same mistake twice… FIND THE SIGNAL Mono is the only one who can stop the ominous Thin Man, the Resident who seems to be the source of the Signal luring him into the heart of the city. Find the courage to confront your nightmares and just maybe both Mono and Six can get out of this alive. Good luck, little ones.

_childDocuments_.review: The game keeps its mix of nostalgic and creepy visuals. It combines with music and sound effect to truly hammer down the oppressive atmosphere of horror and decay. The puzzles were good, blending well with the environment. I have not been stuck anywhere to the point of frustration. The combat is hampered by somewhat clumsy controls, but this is at least partially a design decision. The weapons used are supposed to be hard to wield. Still, aiming and timing issues made me repeat these sequences several times. The running sequences are maybe a bit too tight in some places, but since I managed to get through them eventually, they cannot be too bad.  A worthy successor to the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow that was WILD. I have some GRIPES with this one, namely the addition of combat (it's not very good) and the game's absolute insistence that you play sequences exactly right, since a lot of sections are set up to be you scraping by by the skin of your teeth. This lead to MANY scenarios where my thought was W0W THAT IS CREEPY followed by "ok now i'm pissed" after having to redo the section over and over. Maybe I'm getting old and I'm bad at videogames now idk. Either way, I feel like the devs knew this too since the game is practically auto-saving every 3 seconds.But I digress, very fun and creepy ride and a neat ending. Not too long, not too short. Doesn't outstay it's welcome, though I'm looking forward to any more content they give us. Also due to the story tie-in , it's effectively a must-play if you liked the first one.

Whack-a-mole and hide-and-seek and a bootleg of Red Light, Green Light are all mandatory and the controls for them are abysmal. _childDocuments_.review: A very creepy atmospheric game that really is the stuff of nightmares. Unlike Little Nightmares I, you are going through it with an AI companion for a lot of it, which I personally liked.   The characters that you have to avoid and run from are uncomfortable and unsettling, which is how it should be. The puzzles aren't too easy, but not so hard that they're impossible. I however did find the controls a little clunky and executing things quickly was a challenge, particularly the torch levels as I'm over 30, so keeping a torch shone in several directions was a real challenge. I managed to overcome it though, but I imagine it's harder the older you are. The game isn't too long and it is even shorter than the first game, but I still think it has replay-ability. The music is nice and creepy and the art style reminds me of Tim Burton. I played I and II over a few days. I personally prefer II, but this game is really good and I definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares 2, more of the same, still a good buy.I was fascinated with the original, this dark silent storytelling using subtle clues as you play. The world was mysterious and drew you in for more, but the gameplay felt lacking at times. Once the game started introducing a new concept, they use it once and never again, and for the length of the games, that feels a little disappointing. Unfortunately this game does the same, while the new gameplay features are fascinating, they don't always live up to their greatest potential, although some feel a little dragged on. I can't say I'm disappointed with the game as a whole, it was a thrilling ride that did improve upon the original, but I think it could have been a lot more once it got the attention that it did.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares 2 is the kind of sequel that not only lives up to the high expectations set by its predecessor but manages to elevate the entire gaming experience to a whole new level of spine-tingling horror and surreal brilliance.From the moment you dive into this nightmarish world, you can't help but be captivated by the stunning visuals. Little Nightmares 2 maintains the dark and atmospheric art style of the original, but somehow manages to make it even more haunting and visually arresting. The environments are meticulously crafted, each room telling a story of its own, and the attention to detail is jaw-dropping.The introduction of a new playable character, Mono, adds a fresh layer to the gameplay dynamics. The partnership between Mono and Six creates an emotional connection that adds a new dimension to the narrative. The puzzles are cleverly designed, requiring teamwork and coordination between the two characters, making the gameplay even more engaging and challenging.What really stands out in Little Nightmares 2 is the expansion of the game world. The developers have taken the nightmare to new heights (or depths), introducing new, grotesque enemies and environments that will leave you in awe and terror simultaneously. The level design is a masterclass in atmospheric storytelling, and the variety of settings keeps the gameplay experience consistently thrilling.Sound design continues to be a standout feature, with the unsettling ambiance and subtle cues heightening the suspense. The absence of a traditional spoken narrative is a bold choice, yet it works wonders, allowing the player to immerse themselves in the nightmarish world without distractions.Little Nightmares 2, like its predecessor, excels in telling a story without holding your hand. The narrative unfolds organically, leaving you with a sense of unease and curiosity about the dark mysteries of the world you're navigating.In conclusion, Little Nightmares 2 isn't just a sequel; it's a masterclass in horror gaming. It manages to retain the essence of the original while introducing new elements that make it a standout title in its own right. If you have a penchant for atmospheric horror and enjoy a good psychological twist, Little Nightmares 2 is an absolute must-play. Consider me thoroughly captivated and slightly traumatized in the best possible way.

Highly recommend playing this game, it's an absolute blast, each stage is super unique and it's all the same mechanics without feeling monotonous in any way.

_childDocuments_.review: It's easy to tell from the trailer alone that this game will be stunning and will get you completely absorbed in its universe. The visuals, the concept, and the music are all solid and as a follow-up to the original Little Nightmares, you expect no less. It almost felt like you wanted to screenshot every single frame of the game. Eyecandy. The dynamic between Mono and Six in this game adds A LOT in comparison to the first game. It's a richer experience. Your drive is not only to just escape, you want to escape together! And that opens up a lot of possibilities for interesting game mechanics. The horror is doubled, the excitement is doubled, and the puzzles are absolute genius. This time, they give the music a bigger role in the storytelling, which is always a huge plus! If you're going in this game with any hopes for a sunshine-and-rainbows ending, I'm not sure what to tell you....it's just hard to expect an ending with any kind of true relief from such a horrific adventure. This is a game that leaves you with many unanswered questions, wanting more. The thrill ride is always worth it though. A definite recommendation!!

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Well, that was disappointing....wait, I spent $25 on this??Note: Having 100% the game after 26 hours, I wanted to update my thoughts. Each update will begin with EDIT.Where do I even begin? The fact that enemies can clip through objects sometimes? That issues that plagued the first game carry to the second? The ever-mounting frustration that comes when getting killed because for some reason Mono won't grab the damn ledge? Or maybe the fact that THE ENDING KIND OF SUCKS?EDIT: Just ignore this for now...or don't, if you want ¯\_(ツ)_/¯Tell you what, I'll just jump in with the COLLECTIBLES - in the first game, they were just a little extra thing you could do for some achievements, and if you couldn't grab them all the first go-around, you at least had a good idea of where they were (basically, they were fun tidbits that weren't a chore to find). In this game, you're about need to be Sherlock Holmes for the first or second playthrough, because they REALLY hid these things - these are,of course, only for achievements so it's not really something to get worked up about, it's just that it didn't feel as fine to do as it did in the first game.EDIT: Having found them all, I still think it's a bit of a chore, but really, the issue here is the lack of a permanent light source to use in dark spaces (something I'll expand on later).In terms of PLAYTIME, despite having spent 8 hours on the game, most of that was making mistakes and taking everything in. Realistically, you could easily beat the game in two hours, maybe one if you git gud. The irksome thing is the pricing is way too high for something this short. The other irksome thing is they did the exact same thing with the first game, meaning I fell for it TWICE.EDIT: Nothing new, just edited the paragraph to be less wordy. My stance is still the same.ENEMIES are a total letdown - Interactions with the major enemies play out mostly like the first game, but the larger level layouts and longer chase sequences, which just bogs the whole experience down.Dealing with lesser foes boil down to find the conveniently placed object on the floor and swing. The attack animation is slow and clunky while hit detection is extremely finicky, meaning you have to be slow AND precise when fighting against enemies who are fast AND can clip through your attack animation sometimes to kill you, so even if you timed it right, there's a high chance you still get screwed.EDIT: I discovered a couple of things that made combat a bit easier: A) holding the run button with a weapon moves you slightly faster, and B) you can swivel during the attack animation, allowing to correct your aim. However, this does not mitigate the issues with the attack animation or BS enemy grab range. Boss fights in this game are a bit lackluster in comparison to the original, though there a few dramatic moments in the final chapters that bring it back.EDIT TO THE EDIT: Not having played it for a while and looking back, I realize that most of the issues in combat - particularly those animations I mentioned - were technical problems caused by my potato computer.The ENVIRONMENTS are mostly solid, though there are some things I have to gripe about here as well. The worst offender is the lighting - it's atrocious. Now, don't get me wrong, I understand and enjoy the dark, ambient atmosphere the studio wanted to create with this game, but did they have to take the "dark" part of it so seriously? There are huge segments of the game that are in almost total darkness, and others that are so dim you'd need a flashlight to see. Talking of flashlights, you get one!...3 chapters into the game, where it becomes the core mechanic of that chapter and then lose it permanently in the next one. This is a problem (and my second issue with the environments) because, in all 5 chapters ( there's plenty of moments where a flashlight would be really handy, especially when hunting for collectibles. Hell, even the first game did this right - at least Six got to keep her lighter the whole time! EDIT: Really, this and the collectibles problem would be solved if they just let you have the flashlight at the beginning of the game and let you keep it all the way through - even on full brightness, most of the game was just about too dark to see around in without it. Perhaps it was to help build the ambiance of the game or something, but when I'm spending over 18 hours trying to find a "cleverly hidden hat" in a spot where I can barely see in front of my face, then screw ambiance, give me the friggin' hat!Changing gears, the PUZZLES are great! Each chapter has more or less unique puzzles and mechanics to keep things fresh. My personal favorites are the last two chapters; NO SPOILERS, but the way they play with physical space is both intriguing and entertaining. Overall, the puzzles are a nice challenge that's not easy enough to make you roll your eyes and scoff, but they're not so hard that you wanna throw your controller at the wall.EDIT: No changes here, but I thought I should also mention that the  AI companion works well for its intended purpose. Now, would I call Six a great AI character? No, she just kinda stands there being useless when she doesn't have a scripted task to do. However, when she does something she's supposed to, she does it well, and having played other games with AI driven companions that are less than stellar, I can really appreciate that. Oh, and the soundtrack is also well-done, just like in the first game.That said, despite some praiseworthy puzzles and some other minor things, Little Nightmares 2 is neither the sequel I wanted or hoped for. An ending that ultimately answers nothing and doesn't serve much outside of shock value, cumbersome controls, environments more style than substance, middling enemy design, and bad personal moments (some minor jank and getting softlocked TWICE) are enough to leave me dissatisfied, which really bums me out.In my heart of hearts, I knew that Little Nightmares 2 would expand on the concepts and themes explored in the first game, as well as answering some of the more mind-boggling aspects of the overall story -- yet, that's not what happened. Instead, I got a game that, to me, felt more like a redo, or some weird prequel to the first game, that exists in it's own continuity, and does nothing in service to the first or the greater story being told. Whatever the case, it just doesn't do any justice to what came before.EDIT: A lot of what I said here I still believe. Yeah, the controls were wonky at times, and yeah, my game both soft locked twice AND crashed twice, and yeah, I thought that ending was a subpar payoff to a narrative that didn't really engage me. HOWEVER, these were my personal experiences with Little Nightmares 2, and not all of them were bad. I still found plenty to enjoy, and I know most of you who read this enjoyed it too. I don't want to take that from you, so please feel free to ignore this review if it leaves a sour taste in your mouth and, if anyone from Tarsier Studios reads this, I truly enjoy what you've done here, and I can't wait for what comes next.EDIT TO THE EDIT: As I mentioned in an earlier segment, I was playing on a potato pc at the time, and a lot of my frustrations in the technical department were misplaced - I apologize profusely.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fantastic look-up-the-solution-because-I-have-no-clue-what-the-♥♥♥♥-I'm-supposed-to-be-doing simulator. But as a puzzle game, it's terrible.Expect no hints about what you're supposed to be doing. Also expect to die suddenly and seemingly randomly, which becomes even more frustrating when coupled with no hints. _childDocuments_.review: To sum up all of my mixed up feelings about Little Nightmares 2:the game is technically amazing. Controls are a little tighter than game 1, musical score is somehow atmospheric  thematic at the same time, graphics are wonderful, sets and every one of the monsters are wonderfully creepy...it is a beautifully dark game.The story, however, ends up going only where we've been before. It's too Rogue One for my tastes. Not only that, but it feels like the writers refused to give any lore about the world or any sort of explanation for anything happening in Pale City, or even why Six showed up in the first place! The plot was unsatisfying to me when it seemed to hinge around an understanding of the world they lived in, except the players never got the chance to understand anything about it. I think the game would have been exactly the same if, instead of Six, Mono dragged a Nome around with him.I still hold a candle for the girl in the yellow raincoat, because monsters lurk inside all of us. The only difference is if we accept them as a part of ourselves or pretend like it doesn't exist. I seriously hope there is a third installment of Little Nightmares, because even though part 2 was frustrating to me, now I feel like there's so much more I want to know.P.S. - the first time I played through, the Teacher terrified me. _childDocuments_.review: Firstly I want to say congratulations to the developers, this game has a clear artistic vision and they deliver exceptionally well on that. However, if you are looking to purchase an enjoyable single player horror game, this is not it. Unbelievably tedious. I had to force myself to finish this game as the game is reliant on tried and tested formulas that it never shakes itself from (until the final 5 minutes). Mostly every time I could predict how the encounter or puzzle was going to go (lock with a key missing, electric plug missing fuse) because the game paints by numbers in this area to a maddening degree. As well as the repetition, too many times I had to do a section over because my character clipped a door frame, did an animation for it and was subsequently caught. These are things polish and playtesting should have got rid of because it seriously drags down the game and led to me essentially speed running the last third just to see the end. In a game like this, you never want to notice the controls, and the fact I was constantly aware of them reminded me that I playing a game and this really damaged my enjoyment of the game.On the subject of enjoyment, this game has serious issues with bloat and inconsistency in its content. In a game like  the player was shown huge, expansive locals that you wanted to explore yet you knew the side scrolling nature of the game  meant that you couldn't veer off the path, and this kept with a laser focus on your task - an extraordinary way of marrying narrative and gameplay elements. The opposite is true of Little Nightmares.Too many times I would be drawn to explore these amazing locals that the game provided (a wave battered beach, a street that was twisting in on itself etc.) and I would find they were completely empty, devoid of content and worst of all, inconsistent in their interactivity. This last point especially hurts the game, as the game has rooms filled with interactable objects (child's room, etc) yet there is never any logic as to which ones can be interacted with and which ones can't. This again takes you out of the game as you realise you are operating on an extremely strict railroad that leaves the player incredibly powerless and it ultimately left me bored with the lack of ingenuity or autonomy that the game allowed me. If I were making this game again, I would edit down so many of these empty spaces in the game or, as previously seen in the masterful Inside, actively reward the player for pushing against the game with unique settings and meaningful collectibles. I understand this game has collectibles but every time I explored this game and I didn't find one, I lost the motivation to search anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Hard for me to place a rating on this one. There's a lot I like here with the atmosphere and world design being at the top of the list, but I also have gripes. It's a beautifully creepy world to explore with a very cool art direction.A lot of people seem to hold this game as the better Little Nightmares game. Maybe in gameplay that's true, but in world building and story I think I much preferred the first entry. The first game had a lot of unknowns and part of the fun for me was trying to learn more about the world and what was going on as you proceeded through. The subtle storytelling from just paying attention to the background was great and it felt like each section linked together nicely.I didn't feel that as much this game, the backdrops were interesting but I never felt like I was venturing forward to find out more about the world. It just felt like I was moving from one set piece to the next with little to no meaning between them.The game suffers for me in a few areas, mainly, the control you have over the gameplay. A Lack of depth perception in many areas can make it hard to tell when you're running towards an object or the space next to it.The combat sections give you a very short time to land a precise hit but the controls often make lining up that hit difficult and it can be frustrating to replay those sections when you know how to proceed but miss by a small margin. (skill issue.. I know).I encountered a few bugs, mainly with Six not being where she was meant to be to allow me to progress. One section she decided to not climb into a building with me which meant a re-load of the chapter to allow me to proceed.I think I maybe put a bit of extra pressure on myself during high tension sections or puzzles because I was streaming this and perhaps I would have enjoyed this a little more taking my time with it off stream. Who knows?Overall, it's a good short game with fantastic atmosphere and a few issues. If you liked the first you'll enjoy your time here too.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, if you haven't played the demo yet, do it, you won't regret those ~45 minutes.But to put it simply, this is probably the best game I've played in my life. I could go on about things like the beautifully rendered stylised dark game art, or the complex story that is told without the use of any words, or how the game is paced very well between different types of gameplay so that I never get permanently stuck, or how the audio and soundtrack add so much to the immersion and cinematic flair of the game. The game is also plenty long for a single-player story, with my play-through taking a total of 22 hours, plenty of content for the price.If you're looking for a really scary game and you're an experienced horror consumer you may be slightly disappointed as the tension wore off for me after about two-thirds of the game although it may have been because I played the game over several months and it's still definitely not bad enough to pass on the game. It's definitely still a scary game though as some of my friends and family can attest to.TLDR - A no-brainer purchase if it's on sale and the best game I've ever played. Please play the demo if you haven't already.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Well made game. Some of the scenes and monster designs are so well crafted, it's awesome and creepy. The general atmosphere, music and scenery work well together. The puzzles are pretty simple, but engaging and keep a good flow to the game. There's a few frustration with this game though. Because of the perspective in the game, sometimes I found it awkward to try line up jumps to grab onto things, often completely missing them because I can't really tell what line or angle to jump at because of the perspective. The section with the flashlight was an awesome idea, but control wise was also rather awkward. I also found the game has a little bit too much of an obsession with sections and sequences that you couldn't possibly do first try. Needing to learn what to do and where to go is often a die and restart cycle because to complete them you have to be moving and doing everything correctly right from the get go.Overall though, this game was a well crafted experience. The design and atmosphere are fantastic and so if you liked the first game, you'll like this one too.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: After having completed LM1 a few years back, LM2 certainly doesn't disappoint. Here are some of my few takeaways.Pros:1) The lighting and environment, sound is INSANELY dark and creepy. The reflections on the water, mood, and music is just perfect. Major props to the team for making the game look and sound so good.2) There are many puzzles which don't require you to think that much, depending on how smart you are. Nothing that hinders the game too much or is too complicated if that makes sense.3) The twist at the end!!! (Watch YouTube vids to get a better understanding)Cons:1) The game is pretty short, around 7-8 hours (5 chapters) which I feel it could be be longer. However you can certainly replay the stages and find all the collectables but I just wish there was like 10 chapters or something. (However I understand that this is tying up with the storyline nicely)2) Most of the chase sequences are trial & error, if you mess up with the timing you'll have to try again and again. So if you keep failing the suspense is gone and it can get annoying.Overall it's a fantastic platformer with an INCREDIBLE STORYLINE and I can't wait to see what else this studio produces. Please buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares 2 aims to become a scarier and better experience by offering a bigger world than the first version and adding various new features. But is it successful?All in all, Little Nightmares 2 is one of those games that you can easily recommend to everyone when you are tasked with reviewing it! Yes, it is true that the game is still a bit short and after its 3-4 hour experience, it is not worth repeating much, but to be honest, in this relatively short time, it fulfills its mission to entertain the audience in an almost ideal way.Little Nightmares 2, on the one hand, has a really good story, and by depicting the relationship between Mono and Six, as well as using valuable references and concepts, it narrates it very well, and in terms of gameplay, we see a scary experience with mostly well-designed puzzles. They have and you can enjoy the platformer aspects and even the fights and chases a lot.Even the existing problems of the game are not so big and impressive that they hit it much. As a result, I suggest that if the things I mentioned are important to you in a game, don't miss the Little Nightmares 2 experience.Strengths+ Narrating a deep and meaningful story using smart references.+ Very attractive and riveting ending.+ Creative design of most game puzzles.+ The charm of fighting, stealth and escape parts.+ Appropriate induction of effective fear.+ Great atmosphere thanks to sound and visual effects.weak points- Providing a relatively short experience without much replay value- The controls are a bit dry and clumsy.- The strange things that happen in the cooperation of Six and Mono.Score: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, Little Nightmares II, the game that made me feel like I was in a horror movie marathon! From the graphics to the sound, this game had me shaking in my boots - and I loved every moment of it!Let's start with the graphics. They may be simplistic, but they're also dark and eerie, just like the monsters that haunt you in this game. The ray tracing may be limited, but who needs fancy shadows when you've got terrifying creatures lurking around every corner? The graphics are so stylized that I felt like I was playing a nightmare rather than a game!Moving on to the controls, I have to give kudos to the developers - they're responsive, simple, and easy to learn. But don't let that fool you, dear player, because the monsters will still be chasing you down like a pack of hungry wolves.Now, let's talk about the sound. I'm pretty sure I need therapy after playing this game, thanks to the tense, psychological, and downright creepy sounds that made my skin crawl. From the sound of the creatures' footsteps to the eerie music that played in the background, every sound effect in this game was designed to scare the living daylights out of you.And last but not least, the gameplay. Let me tell you, dear player, the creatures in this game are not to be messed with. They're scary, creepy, and downright frightening. You'll spend most of your time hiding, sneaking, and running away from them. But hey, that's all part of the fun, right?In conclusion, Little Nightmares II is a horror lover's dream come true. The graphics may be simple, but they're also dark and stylized. The controls are responsive and easy to learn, but that won't save you from the terrifying creatures. The sound is so tense and creepy that it'll give you nightmares. And the gameplay? Well, let's just say that you'll need a change of underwear after playing this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: I want to highly recommend this title and it is a good game worth its purchase but it has its flaw's for the few frugal customers who might want to wait for a sale. _childDocuments_.review: Decided to buy this game after having a great experience with the first game in the series. This game basically does everything the first game did but improved upon it and added some stuff. The game is very charming and the monsters are also charming in their own way as well. The game was just about as long as the first game however I will most likely be going back to it to get the collectibles. The atmosphere was even more intense and creepy than the first one. The music was great as expected and kept me on edge. The story is one which you might need to do some thinking as the game doesnt have any narrative storytelling but is told through world building. The characters (mono and six) work in tandem together and it was cool to see the backstory and some questions I had about the first game. I personally loved the ending as it followed the same structure as the first game sorta. Highly recommend purchasing. If you loved the first one you will love this one and if you havent played the first one, you will still enjoy it though I strongly encourage to play the first one.

_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: An artistic masterpiece. Excellent atmosphere and definitely delivers on the creepiness.That said, there isn't enough game in here, both in terms of gameplay and length.It's so weird how a studio tries their hardest to make an exceptionally good looking environment, and even invests in being able to interact with so many things in the world but then completely neglects the actual game design. Why take the same puzzle solution and then force the player to redo it again... and again.. and again..? How is that fun?All LN2 does is crouch from point a to point b, jump to get the item, throw item on switch, get key, put key in lock, run away while something chases you, rinse and repeat. This is supposed to be a puzzle game but there are really 2-3 actual puzzles at most in the entire ~5-6 hours game.Get this on a steep sale and just expect some cool, pretty, and creepy environments to walk through.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: The game and story itself are amazing, the atmosphere and overall feel is very well made. However the performance is clunky and the controls are atrocious, especially when it comes to using the flashlight. The graphics are well made. Performance wise the game is not that good but story and graphics wise it is. Do what you will with that info. Overall the game is a 6/10, deducting 4 points due to performance being quite clunky.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games I've ever played. I will be putting up a picture of this game in my room. I loved the story, although it made me sad. I loved the hats. I loved that you could hold hands with six. I thought the challenging parts were not annoying, but just the right amount of challenging. I think the soundtrack is beautiful and the overall sound production is fantastic. I learned the controls pretty quickly and thought they were quite easy to remember. It is not the longest game I've ever played, but considering the production of it and the storyline, I can see why it's not as long as some other games. I enjoyed going back for all of the achievements and the secret ending and I'm looking forward to if they add any more DLCs. I will definitely be there if a Little Nightmares III comes out and look forward to any other projects associated with the name. Amazing game! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game right after it's predecessor, which i would've liked if not for the janky controls, hoping this one would not make the same pitfalls. Sadly this game makes the same mistakes and even adds to them with actual game breaking bugs that REALLY hamper the experience. There was a certain bug involving an item that didn't spawn for me, even after resetting to the last checkpoint, making me have to restart the entire chapter and go through 15 minutes of gameplay to get back there. Even doing this it took me more than 3 full chapter restarts to get this item to spawn, i did everything as intended but it still didn't work until the one time that it eventually did. This all added up to an HOUR of wasted time trying to get the game to work. Not only was this incredibly frustrating but it also made me worried with the rest of the game that i'd run into similar issues (which indeed happened later, but there a checkpoint restart was enough to fix the issue). The worst thing about all of this is that the bug in encountered has been a KNOWN ISSUE since 2021... These developers don't care to fix this issue that has plagued dozens of people but instead worked on little nightmares 3 coming up later. I don't care how loved the series is, this single fact will make me not play the last entry as the devs simply don't care either. The game also just isn't fun at many moments, from janky controls to unforgiving sections and the same poor depth perception of the previous title, this game feels like a slog to play through. The addition of combat, while visceral at times, made the game feel even clunkier. These issues take all of the wind out of little nightmares 2's sails. No amount of amazing visuals or great sound design can make up for this. The game is also just waaay overpriced for the amount of content on offer. Had i not been stuck for an hour i could've beat this game in 6 hours and i took my sweet time with it. A regular gamer that isn't looking to thoroughly explore every nook and cranny will probably clear it in 4 hours, which is too short for this price unless the game is of exceptional quality. This game isn't and therefore isn't worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked games by David Cage and are here for a horror game, then I recommend this game. David cage tells a decent narrative at times. But where you get narrative and aesthetic, you lose out polish and fun game play. I like this game, but I also liked Heavy Rain, and I feel they both have a good idea executed via frustrating game play.This game is honestly getting a harder review because this isn't their first game. This is at least their second game, and I am a fan of LN1. I enjoy the characters and the story and the lore; the fun little details. But that game had very annoying aspects. I died more often due to unfair game play killing me (getting stuck on everything, wall running when nowhere near a wall, etc). When I saw the trailers for LN2, the first comments my family said was "I really hope they fix how the game feels". And this is why I don't recommend it. They didn't fix the issues that make the game unfun. The game is fun, but dying over and over because the game is working against you, watching your death play out, reloading, then getting back to where you died and hoping the game lets you win this time. There are ways of working around the game, and working with it, factoring in all the issues. But more often than not this is also fraught with frustration. And I honestly feel like recommending a game that didn't fix the problems of the first game is the same as supporting companies like Bethesda who never fix the bugs in their games. That is the problem here. Some of these issues aren't just fun breaking, they are game breaking. Enemies reaching through and clipping through walls. Physics often breaking. Sprites just disappearing. These aren't things you will experience every minute, but I would be surprised to believe you left one chapter without experiencing something like that. I have seen reviews that said the puzzles are hard. This is false for the most part. The puzzles are almost insultingly easy, for the most part. I did get stuck on a couple for a couple minutes, but nothing close to something like Braid. Closer to Thomas was alone in terms of difficulty. Most often Six is there to tell you literally what you have to do, either with a clue or just literally going where you need to go. If you are here for puzzles, complex and fun ones, this is not it.I will recommend the game if they ever fix the issues with it. Anyone who plays the game can feel the issues, and that end boss fight is the worst thing ever. This isn't a spoiler, but the worst final boss in this game is an axe. The velcro physics are spot on, but is sucks when you are trying to drop something, or touch anything like a wall. The esthetic and sound are great, and the lore and story are engaging. The ending is brutal. It is good, but I wouldn't recommend it to my friend's because I don't think they would enjoy the frustrating parts.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick and short - if you liked the first game, Little Nightmares 2 is just more of the same formula, but somehow even better.DISCLAIMER - you do not need to have played the first game to play this, though it does add some nice to have context to the game.The good:*The story is very enticing, very different (to other games of the genre) and very interesting.The first little nightmares game was already a great example of good storytelling and the sequel/prequel is very much more of the same.*The graphics, whilst somewhat cartoonish at times are very appropriate and look great in the context of the story.*The audio work is well executed and fitting.*The puzzles are quite fun and quick and add a bit of charm to the gameplay without overcomplicating it (and messing up the pacing of the game).The meh:*The gameplay is overall easy to understand and doesn't get in the way, however, occasionally can be a bit tedious.This comes in the form of awkward delays of movement compared to inputs, or just parts of the game that can only be completed in one "specific" way (which means you will have to die multiple times before you figure it out).*The length of the game is quite short. For a game that lasts only about 4-5 hours, $30 is potentially a bit of a steep asking price (through I have to admit I personally much prefer a short and concentrated game than a long diluted one)*The deluxe edition shouldn't exist. I don't know if this is just a way for the developers to try and recoup some more of the cost to develop the game, but with how little the deluxe edition adds to the table, I think it should exist and rather the extra area should just be part of the base game (and then make the OST and art book a separate add-on you can buy).Overall, an amazing game and a great sequel (or rather prequel) to the original game. At the price of £25, this might be a steep ask for only 4-5 hours of gameplay, but I think this game is very much worth that price. Give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: This review is as much relevant to the first game as it is for this one. The story, atmosphere and overall character design are great, absolutely flawless and really create a world which can exist on its own two feet. As a self-contained story, this game does great. However, it does remain a game, not a book or a movie, but a game. And in games gameplay matters a lot. The things mentioned above are important, no doubt, but in a GAME, GAMEplay is also an essential component. I am not exaggerating when I say, out of all the games I've played, some good, some mediocre, this game I truly disliked playing. It is the jankiest, most badly-tested and executed game I have ever tried. My playtime is well over the 2 hours shown as I was playing offline the past two weeks. I am around the bit with the shopping cart and the electrified water and I intend to finish the game, once I find the strength to get through its horrible gameplay. However, I've already experienced enough to be able to say, I do not enjoy playing this game. I enjoy its story, its lore, its world, but not its gameplay. And that is why I cannot recommend you buy it, but rather watch a non-commentary youtube walkthrough of it. Often times you can make jumps because the story demands it, others not, sometimes you grab onto stuff, others not, sometimes you run fast enough, others, you don't, sometimes the bosses' reach is enough to catch you, others not, sometimes Six will block your path, other times no, sometimes you will stumble onto stuff, others you will move flawlessly. And allow me to NOT elaborate on the HOSPITAL FLASHLIGHT section. It is all so arbitrary, so all over the place, and when a game doesn't follow its own rules, it is no longer fun. Like chess, if the bishop could suddenly teleport to the other side's king and take him out. The gameplay (I played with a controller), is very often unresponsive, janky, and downright unfun, and the worst part is that the horribly placed checkpoints often force you to go through it all over again. It would have been fine if the gameplay was enjoyable, but it most certainly isn't! Games and developers shouldn't get away with disguising bad gameplay as difficulty. This game is not difficult because it's difficult (at least not in most parts), it's difficult because it is janky as hell (AGAIN: Hospital. Flashlight.). I can guarantee you that at least 90% of the positive reviews for this game are for the things I mentioned initially, the things I also loved: the story, the characters, the atmosphere, the lore. We're just forced to slog through the horrible gameplay to enjoy those other parts. Buy this game only on a severe discount or watch a youtube walkthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game due to the first game being fantastic in almost everyway yet this one is nearly close to it but falls short due to the gameplay and how repetitive it is. The atmosphere, story,graphics, character designs, bosses, enemies etc are all fantastic and follows the same style as Little Nightmares 1 the only thing that doesn't work would be the gameplay. Gameplay ends up feeling like a tough as nails platformer where you end up dying in a section over and over again because 1 simple mistake will outright kill you and i feel that's not what Little Nightmares is going for, even the first game had those moments but due to the excellent pacing and controls, you end up easily escaping without a death. During gameplay such as the chase sequences, it gives you no room to breathe or even think during the situation as it all relies on you dying then figuring out what went wrong to avoid it which isn't bad at all just again, this game has more chase sequences and combat so you start noticing it even more compared to the first game where both were few and far between mixed in with stealth sections and great pacing that if it did have that, was able to hide it really well.The games pacing also really isn't good, as it gives you little time to take in what the world has to offer and throws you into a chase sequence or combat sections where any and all immersion goes away as death after death just feels cheap due to the controls and bugs. The controls for this game is almost identical to the first game but due to having even more chase sequences and combat sections, you start to notice the flaws as the controls weren't really made for them since your character fails to climb up ladders/areas properly, doesn't face the enemies even though it looks like it on screen so it misses, character getting stuck on small geometry that's basically 1 pixel leading to death as the geometry is what kills you 90% of the time, character fails to pick up a weapon despite being right infront of it and holding the button to do so etc. First Little Nightmares never had any of these issues as the controls felt really tight and responsive which made chase sections no problem.Little Nightmares II feels more trial and error which is a shame since everything else is fantastic, you can see the love and passion put into the art direction, music, character designs and even the gameplay at times isn't bad at all, it's just mainly the controls and your character getting stuck or failing to pick up an item in time during sections where doing so would be your death over and over again as deaths should be the players fault not the poor controls or buggy environments that leads to it.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- State of art visuals with impressive 3d graphics and lighting. You'll find yourself pressing the screenshot button very often.- Awesome world designed with tons of imagination. It's like an interactive surrealistic painting where only crazy things happen. All these changes of scale are impressive. It takes you from dinner tables and claustrophobic air ducts to open roads and big sceneries and all this zoon in-out happens in a magical, seamless way.- Strong, rotten, dark atmosphere that is combined perfectly with some emotional moments creating a great mix.- Unique creatures and enemies. They're so imaginative and horrifying that you cannot forget them.- Smooth, detailed animations with great clothes' and soft bodies' movement. This realism makes the enemy creatures even more creepy.- Great sound design. They keep it simple using mainly ambient and environmental sounds, but the final result is pretty dark and imposing. Enemies' sounds are awesome and will give some extra chills too.- Cool, mostly ambient music. The main theme sticks in your mind.- Stunning direction and cinematography. Especially camera's movement and the seamless transition between cut scenes and actual gameplay is amazing. Sometimes you're not even sure whether you are in control or not and this creates a unique, continuous, uninterrupted experience.- Deep enough lore with many locations, events, creatures and scattered clues around the world. It's pretty abstract but if you're observational it can be interesting. - Some chasing sequences look like great executed choreographies with good pace and pleasant synchronization between your characters' and enemies' movements.- It doesn't want to mess with you. Constant checkpoints won't let you lose a lot of progress when dying. The bad- Problematic gameplay with unresponsive controls. I don't know if this is an issue caused by the overpolished animations, but you can never be really precise and you never feel like having the full control. It's hard to anticipate depth and you'll find youself bumping on random objects or jumping to your death because you were not at the correct place. Maybe a wider lens could be helpful. Also, you character often fails to grab ledges after jumping and hitting enemies with a hammer can be pretty slow and inaccurate. All these manage to ruin the game's rhythm and fluidity and make the game much less enjoyable.- It gets repetitive after a while. Solve a puzzle, confront some minor enemies, hide initially from the big boss before escaping in a chasing sequence and all over again. We've seen this recipe at the first game of the series too.- The lore is deep but the main story is so fragmented and abstract that makes it too easy for the developers to include whatever they want. Especially the last part of the game (with the TVs) is so extravagant that feels like being there not exactly to serve the plot, but just to impress the player and give the game a blockbuster tone.- It has small duration and offers no challenge at all. Puzzles are childish and on top of that sometimes your companion (Six) initially gives away the solution. If they wanted to make an interactive movie they could avoid including any puzzles at all.

_childDocuments_.review: As I previously played Little Nightmares and thoroughly enjoyed it, I had high hopes for the sequel. I had already seen a brief gameplay clip but aimed to stay away from spoilers as I wanted to go into the game as blind as possible. Therefore, I purchased the game with the digital content bundle.Firstly, I noticed that the game looked a lot better than the previous game. I assume that this was due to a larger team working on the game; it really shows. The updated graphics helped to create the spooky atmosphere needed. This along with the ambient sound and soundtrack worked perfectly together. I found that due to these reasons alone that I felt on edge when the music suddenly changed or faded away.With the new graphics, came some new hostile characters. Each one of these scared me in another way. Every character had a different attribute to them which changed the way Mono, who is the playable character, had to traverse around them to progress. This kept the gameplay fresh and introduced new skills throughout the game. The developers did a great job in making the characters come to life and move is a strange but natural way. I can see that this was well thought about in development.In the first game, Six would carry a lighter around with them to light the way. However, Mono could use multiple different items. This started as a torch. The game did well in making climatic events that caused Mono's items to become broken. For example, there would be a section where the scenery is collapsing around you and Mono would only just escape. The torch would be lying on the ground broken. The other items that you would collect would impact the gameplay greatly.In conclusion, I loved this game. With the updated graphics and the amazing soundtrack, this game did not disappoint. I had around five hours of fun and fear. This game, along with Little Nightmares, takes a fresh idea and runs with it. I have never seen a game that has a cute art style but strikes fear into me. I would highly recommend Little Nightmares Two.

_childDocuments_.review: "Little Nightmares 2" is a visually stunning and atmospheric horror adventure game that successfully builds on the eerie world introduced in the first installment. The game maintains a sense of suspense and unease throughout, offering a captivating and immersive experience. The level design is creatively crafted, filled with intricate details that contribute to the overall sense of dread. The narrative unfolds in a mysterious and intriguing manner, keeping players engaged as they navigate through unsettling environments.The character design and animation are exceptional, enhancing the overall unsettling atmosphere. The puzzles are cleverly integrated into the gameplay, providing a good balance between challenge and progression. The sound design is hauntingly effective, further intensifying the eerie ambiance.While the game maintains the spirit of its predecessor, it also introduces new elements that keep the experience fresh and unpredictable. The cooperative gameplay mechanics add an interesting layer to the overall experience, creating opportunities for teamwork and strategic thinking."Little Nightmares 2" successfully delivers a captivating and unsettling journey that will leave players with lingering thoughts and a desire for exploration. It's a worthy successor that builds upon the strengths of the original, offering a memorable and chilling gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: ‣ 9/10 – A very strong ending.‣ Game Audio / Soundtrack - 10/10‣ Graphics – 10/10‣ Atmosphere – 10/10‣ Main Story / Characters – 10/10‣ AI – 10/10‣ Ragdolls / Physics – 10/10‣ Movement – 8/10‣ Combat – 6/10‣ Final notes: I played Little nightmares 1 and 2 back to back, so my knowledge of the story is very recent and fresh, however I will not deny I got some questions on what the hell is happening here. Luckly with a few youtube videos I managed to fully understand the story. Everything in this game is the same as it was in the first, but there are more combat episodes and of course the puzzles are new and unique like in the first one. _childDocuments_.review: The original Little Nightmares is great, but this game improves on its predecessor in several ways. The creep factor has been dialed up a few notches: Monsters are scarier, more creative, and better at searching for you; spooky sound effects in the next room put you on edge; and there are some dark rooms only navigable by flashlight. The flashlight is properly utilized, whereas it was completely optional to use in the first game.  The story is intriguing and artsy. They don't hold your hand, but let you develop your own interpretation of what happens. The huge monster city is absolutely gorgeous, almost breathtakingly so. The devs did a fantastic job on this game's aesthetics. I also enjoyed the puzzles and time-based challenges a lot, although those things sometimes frustrated me.Here are some issues I had with the game (which I think are outweighed by the good things about it):1. The puzzles are generally pretty well-designed, but occasionally they're difficult to figure out and can be frustrating. Not sure if that's a me problem or a game problem though.2. The last puzzles of the game with the doors are unintuitive and frustrating. I had to use a walkthrough multiple times to figure out how to get through them, and I still don't understand how I was supposed to figure that out.3. The time-based challenges can be fun, but also annoying and tedious if you have slow reflexes. I found myself going through many of them over and over and over again, although that made it feel even better when I finally succeeded. I think this game should have an option to lower the difficulty for time-based combat specifically.4. This game can be a real struggle to play without a controller. I won't knock them too much for this though, because they specifically say at the beginning that it's highly recommended you use a controller.Tldr: If you're looking for a challenging, scary puzzle game with a solid story and beautiful scenery, check this game out. It is a great improvement on the already good Little Nightmares. I would highly, highly recommend you play with a controller, and if you have slow reflexes like me, be prepared to play some scenes over and over until you get them right. However, this is still a fabulous game, all things considered.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to write a bad review about this game. First of all I LOVE the art work, design, sound and story. The gameplay.There are two things, first of all the bugs, you can stand infront of an item you want to pick up but the character doesnt pick it up and you try moving back and forth aso but sometimes it takes 10 minutes to pick up a simple item which caused alot of frustration especially when youre being hunted. So the game is ALOT of trial and error and as the game is time pressured enough, at some points you have to be 0,00001 seconds right or you have to do it again, and again, and again... The second thing is that you cant point your flashlight in the direction you want and I saw many others had the same problem. Which is a shame beacause you cant continue the game if you cant point it.However if these things were fixed I would love this game aswell even tho its not at much puzzles like the first game. I enjoyed meeting Six again and the teacher is so unique, loved that chapter.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game with a really thought provoking ending. The first game was good, but this game is just amazing-- It's in atleast my top 10, maybe even top 5. It's strangely emotional, and the scares were much better excecuted this time around. I've heard that the company that owns the Little Nightmares series won't make any more games- but I wish they would. Or atleast make something, like more comics or a book. I'm so interested by all of the environmental storytelling. Now, even if I adore this game, It does have some issues. Some encounters are a guess-and-check or do not have a very obvious answer. Similarly to Little Nightmares I, the movement can be janky (though it is MUCH more bearable than the first game's). My last complaint is that its too short!! I would have loved to have maybe one or two more chapters worth of Mono and Six's relationship growing, I think it would have made the ending feel much more impactful. Anyways-- you should get this game. It's only a few hours long, and its well worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not worth it's current price. It's pretty and the first act is really good but then it feels like more of the same stuff but done worse. If you remember the awesome chase scene in the first game in the "feeding room" and how cool that was. This game tried to imitate that but did it worse every time by making it extremely easy to die by either not sprinting as soon as the chase starts or by clipping into the damn wall and getting stuck. Now getting into mild spoiler territory... the ending was lame, I wanted to like it but i thought it was pretty predictable and contrived at the end. I wanted to love this entire game I'm a big fan of the first one along with limbo and inside. But this didn't feel like those games, the puzzles were lame. Half of the gameplay involved chase sequences or badly designed combat, and they missed base with the companion system on account of her not being around for more than half the game. And with a 6 hour run time this game is not worth the $30 and I wish I could refund.
