_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares II expands on its predecessor, with similar atmosphere, an story that leaves you guessing, and quite a few tense, scary moments. It does have the same flaws, if you can call them that: you are, after all, a little kid vs a hostile environment that will pretty much kill you in one hit. Some ppl are ok with it, others will hate this. At least it isn't as punishing as its first installment.Puzzles stay on a similar note, halfway between the original and a few ideas from its expansion, the Maw. Not terribly hard, but they ain't easy either, they hit that sweet soft spot. The game is short, but quite enjoyable, and if you are into achievement hunting it will present a greater challenge (this saga is oddly easy to complete, but hard to master depending on the challenges you decide to take on. Try a speedrun without dying for example).The action is certainly more dynamic, and some of the set pieces are truly astounding, some of the areas will make you feel uneasy, scared or both. Besides hunting for completion, i will keep an eye on any DLC Tarsier studios may release, like the first one :)

_childDocuments_.review: Little Papsmears 2 is a wonderful game. Just remember you aren't coming here for gameplay; this is the kind of game you play for "the experience", the atmosphere, story, sound, etc. By those metrics, this is an utter triumph of a game, just as artistically inspired and brilliant as its predecessor (and that game's excellent DLC). But in terms of pure gameplay, controls are still clunky and frustrating, you still feel like you are fighting against the controller whenever anything tense or complicated is happening on screen. The developers seem aware of this, however, and have included very liberal checkpoints that seem to trigger every 10-20 seconds or so, so overall frustration is largely ameliorated.Get this game, immerse yourself in its excellent world and story (make sure to play Little Papsmears 1 first, though), and then do another playthrough to get collectibles and achievements. 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the first one, then you've played the best version of the game. First, it's way too short. I beat it in like 8 hours, and that time includes me having the game still going as I fell asleep while playing though it several times. It's like right in the middle of making this game, the developers got tired and said, let's just end it here - with a ridiculous ending might I add. It feels extremely incomplete and very rushed. However, the atmosphere is Amazing. It even rivals the atmosphere of the best Silent Hill games in that department - and the game itself is beautiful to see. Then, the experience is lessened due to not having much variety in the enemies or level designs. It's like maybe 3 or 4 different variety types all through out the game. The worst thing would be the controls, which seems okay, until you have to run away from enemies that is - then it's like you're running under water and moving way too slow to get away efficiently. Of course after many tries you'll eventually make it through, but I can easily see rage player wanting to throw their controllers right into the screen at some points. I think they made the controls to escape monsters wonky on purpose to make it seem not so easy, but that only made it feel frustrating instead. Then there are the puzzles, which aren't too bad (or hard), but also doesn't seem very well thought out. After a while, they can all be managed, but some with the thoughts of - what were they thinking when they came up with this sh*t? Other than that, it is way too easy to get though the game. It really feels like a huge step backwards from the first one. If I didn't catch it on sale for $5, I'd be highly upset about buying this game and it being too late to get a refund. This is about as honest a review I can give it. My suggestion, especially if you've played through the first one would be - Either catch it really cheap on sale like I did, or just pass it up altogether. This experience will tarnish the one that you may have had with the first game.

It idolises the grim feelings of loneliness and a sense of false hope. Defeat is a common feeling for stories in this game, it represents the cruel realities rather then providing the happy ending we all wanted. _childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the first little nightmares game, and the horror genre in general. I will say, I dont know if I would call it a horror game so much as I would just call it dark. The ambiance and feel of the Little Nightmares world is truly remarkable and unique, I think that holds true for both games. Regarding this game in particular, here are what I think the pros and cons are:Pros:Atmosphere:-Music: this is a big one for me, and the soundtrack is amazing, it always conveys the feelings I think I am supposed to be feeling during in game scenes. Whether it is mysterious, suspenseful, or downright creepy, the use of soundtrack and audio cues is done very well in this game-Artistic Feel: if you played the first game then you can expect the same style of animation here, a style of animation I think is perfect for this world and one of the things that first drew me to the franchise, the enemies look unsettling, the noises they make are unnatural (in a good way) etc. Very well done in my opinion.Story: I liked the story to this game, in some ways more than the first. The developers of this game do a good job of really never telling you whats going on in the overarching world, but drop enough story hints and cues to put together a story set in a world with no real narrative backdrop, and I think this adds to the creepy and unsettling nature of the world they created. You play as Mono, who ends up finding six, our character from the first game, and you both travel through a strange world where almost everyone wants to get you.Price and length: I find the price to be very reasonable. For an indie studio I am happy to pay $30 for what we got. For reference it took me about 5.5 hours to beat, I actively attempted to search around for as many hats and glitching remains as possible, I did my best to take my time getting through the game and to my surprise when I finished I still had quite a bit to find in every chapter, so I would imagine if you do a better job than I did of hunting for the extras you could make it about 8 or so hours.Cons:Mechanics - Occasionally there are a few areas in the game that kind of back you into a corner and you are forced to trial and error (and maybe even with some luck) you will inevitably succeed. This, in my opinion, did not take away from the experience much, and was heavily present in one chapter in particular, outside of that I did not really run into any issues. Flash/Strobe effect: This is something I do not often find talked about in reviews, but for me personally, I really hate the overuse of this effect. This is really only an issue in the 4th chapter, but the constant and unyielding overuse of flashes and strobes really annoy me. I am not epileptic, but it kind of gave me a headache, and as a disclaimer I would add if you are someone prone to seizures, to play with caution in the 4th chapter, as interactions with the Thin Man can get visually annoying with the strobe affect. Overall I really enjoyed this game, and I recommend it. If you are a fan of the first, or are entering this world for the first time, Little Nightmares II is, in my opinion, worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares II is a fun game that I recommend, but it falls short of the original. The biggest strength of the game is the atmosphere and crazy visuals. There are some wild nightmares visuals in the game. What am I playing? However, the venues seem a bit more muddled and form a less cohesive world than the first game. It seems more random than the first game. Also, this sequel doesn't really push any boundaries. It's basically just more levels added onto the first game. It's Little Nightmares 1.5. The teacher monster with a very long, extending neck was my favorite of the antagonists. It was a funny reminder of my school days.  And the ending to the hunter was sudden and jaw dropping.The puzzles are decent. They are about on par with the first game. There was one section in the middle of the game that stumped me for a minute. The ending was the weakest part. There are too many trial and error puzzles that didn't require any actual thinking and just relied on crossing off the available options until all the ones that didn't work were eliminated. I didn't understand what the ending was supposed to mean. It came across as just a weaker, more obtuse version of the ending of the first game. I did enjoy my time with the game, though. I started playing on the Switch and then mid way bought the PC version because it runs so much smoother on PC.  It was worth upgrading the experience. The game took around 7 hours to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Having fully completed this game and found everything I could I think this game is a great follow up to its first, creating new mechanics and monsters to strike childish fear in the hearts of all who try to escape the pale city. The atmosphere and aesthetic is unique even compared to the first game and the story follows a new character before the events of the first one. While I don't think this game is better than the first it's definitely close, with its strange and wondrous new world and new quality of life additions, Little Nightmares II is a terrifying game that'll get your blood pumping.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares II is like a rollercoaster ride through a haunted funhouse - you scream, you laugh, and sometimes you even pee a little (no judgments here). As Mono, I've never felt so simultaneously terrified and entertained.The game designers must have a hotline to my nightmares because they've perfectly encapsulated my fear of creepy dolls, towering monsters, and long, dark hallways. But you know what? I kept coming back for more! Who knew being chased by grotesque creatures could be so oddly satisfying?The puzzles are as twisted as my sense of humor, and just when I thought I had it all figured out, the game threw a curveball that left me scratching my head and chuckling nervously. Plus, the graphics are so beautifully grotesque that I couldn't decide whether to admire them or cover my eyes in terror.And let's not forget about Six, my trusty partner in crime (and occasional accidental manslaughter). Together, we braved the horrors of the Pale City with all the finesse of a pair of clumsy toddlers on a sugar rush.In conclusion, Little Nightmares II is a nightmare you won't want to wake up from. It's like being trapped in a horror movie directed by Tim Burton and narrated by a caffeinated squirrel. If you're into that sort of thing (and let's face it, who isn't?), then this game is an absolute must-play. Just make sure to keep a spare pair of pants handy.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was super amazing, and every emotion the game wanted you to feel hit the nail each time. I felt super horrified, scared, charmed, and so many things. The ending though blindsided me, but in a super good way. It's definitely a fitting end to Little Nightmares II, and even Little Nightmares as a series. Really sad, though.It takes a lot of the same elements from the first game and expands on them here, with some new functions. If you thought the first game was too easy, this one is definitely more difficult. More frustrating too, since it can be super unforgiving at times. It's really fulfilling though after you do those parts of the story, but you do have to do some scenes perfectly. The game is definitely larger than Little Nightmares, or it feels larger.The art is definitely better, not that the last one was bad, but it feels like they definitely improved on the style of the game. The environments look a lot more alive and scarier, and the ambience and visuals go so well together. The art definitely adds so much more to the game, I love the sort of distortion the game has to offer which does tie in to the story.10/10 Visuals7/10 Mechanics (The controls felt kinda iffy and inconsistent at times)9/10 StoryI had a few bugs where The Doctor would get stuck on a lot of things or he'd loop between a certain place backwards and forwards during a chase when he'd seen me during a stealth portion. He also got shot back into another room as well. I had the most bugs during the Hospital to be honest, and a lot of it was with the Doctor getting suck or him being super late to the chase sequences. _childDocuments_.review: Having played the first game and enjoyed the mild terrors and mystery of the weird environment and even weirder characters, I decided to jump straight to the sequel, although apparently it's a prequel. Who knew?! Another sophisticated platform game with an even darker story....you play as a different character this time and meet Six and her yellow raincoat along the way. The game drops you straight into a confusing and twisted world which becomes more challenging and terrifying by the chapter; the hunter in the woodland has you squirming from the very start and once you reach the Pale City it just goes from bad to worse, in a good way. The pot head children and the mannequin room will stay with me for a long time, both had me screaming as every second lost and every movement misjudged edged me closer to death. I died way more in this game than the first, and had to attempt complicated escapes sometimes tens of times over to get it right. No question Little Nightmares II is harder, scarier, more challenging and more immersive than Little Nightmares I. Both games rely heavily on your camera perspective and on precision of movement, which of course is purposefully warped to make your struggle for survival all the more difficult, it can get frustrating at times so I learned to do small tests before committing to big actions - making sure I was lined up properly for a life saving leap or a desperate overhead grab. It's all too easy to die just because the developer's camera tricks got you. The challenges are a bit harder than in the first game and not always obvious, but I guess that's the point. I have to admit I needed to refer to a walk through on a few occasions because I either found it impossible to conquer the enemy or I just couldn't see where to start. I would have got permanently stuck in the horror of the hospital mannequin room without help, and because it's a platform game there is never an alternative route. Escape or die! The ending was weird, not anticipated, and thought provoking. Very enjoyable but stressful.

_childDocuments_.review: Straight up -- if you liked the original Little Nightmares, you'll like this too. It's the exact same formula,  but with better design and expanded gameplay.The content on offer here is really the same as it was in Little Nightmares; action platforming in a demented and - dare I say - nightmarish world with an emphasis on stealth and evasion. There's no point in going over the basics; I've got a review of the first game too but presumably if you're interested in this game you already know what the first was like.The narrative is just as mysterious and impenetrable as it was in the first game. Playing as Mono alongside the original game's heroine, Six, and going through the Pale City is a befuddling journey. The characters and locations present raise endless questions: Who are they? How did it get this way? Why did Mono wake up in the forest? These questions are essentially unanswered, but the Lovecraftian sense of wonder in the face of the unknowable pervaded my brain anyways. More concrete details of the broader narrative within and between the games only really pop up in the final moments of the game. While some stuff should be evident to people with two neurons to rub together, other bits will produce a lot more theory-crafting. While those who live for direct lore will be disappointed, but I find the mystery adds to the overall appeal.The characters and story are hardly the main source of appeal though. As with its predecessor, the design and artistic cohesion is excellent in both its aesthetic and ability to unnerve. Buildings and people are distorted in strange ways, both familiar and insidiously twisted; a rot hangs over the entire world. Geometries and physiologies which  run rampant. The style itself is cartoonish enough to where the outlandish fabrication of the game's elements settles comfortably into the mind, but just realistic enough for the designers to include some very unsettling details. The world is plainly lush, too, rich in all the usual sorts of detail. The whole thing's real "creepy" (TM) as it should be. The music, too, is minimalistic but unsettling as it was before.Much can be said about the spaces the player has to explore here as it compares to the first. It was only in hindsight that I realized that so much of The Maw was thin corridors and quite boxy rooms. There was often a fair amount of space to run into the screen, when the game needed it, but large sections of the were just left-to-right affairs. Not so in Little Nightmares II. The game is awash with truly engorging vistas. It helps, certainly, that the game takes place by and large outside, but even interior segments, such as a memorable room which seemed a misty cavern filled with dangling beds seem to go on forever. The actual field of play is often limited, but just being able to see so far back enhances the atmosphere and tension massively. Even the more "active" gameplay has rooms with a lot more depth and grandeur to them on average than in the original. The action and stealth segments play more readily with z-axis movement than before (or at the very least the environment's been beefed up enough to give that impression).	It's a shame then, that those pretty models seemed to get a fair bit closer than intended. Indeed, I encountered quite a bit of clipping into objects during the game. Not that it impeded gameplay, and the bits the player doesn't touch are polished to a shine, but it's a bit hard to immerse yourself in the creep zone when Mono's got half his arm stuck inside a tree or something. This ties into some greater issues, so I might as well move on to that.LN2 has the exact same day-to-day activities as LN1. Cat-and-mouse behaviour or standard chases. Collectibles (hats and TV-static children here) scattered throughout. Added onto this are common moments where Mono must use a mallet (or similar) to hit things or enemies. It’s a welcome addition which adds variety to the gameplay, if a bit unwieldy for the pacing. However, much like the previous game, awkward controls rear their ugly head. This isn’t the kind of game which needs very precise controls, but everything you do is  too loose to comfortably settle the blame for your deaths on yourself. Unwieldy jumps, awkward necessary routing, mallet swings which kill you over and over because of poor depth perception. A mechanic used in chapter 3 was particularly awkward to handle in conjunction with movement. When things flow freely there’s little issue, but tenser portions can let down the player. And of course, tension is crucial in this game. A horror platformer lives on the player not dying; the first death eliminates fear and each one following aggravates repetition. So, the control problems can occasionally sour the mood. Thankfully, this game has no analogue to “Hard to the Core”.If you’re worrying about the length, rest assured it’s a fair bit longer than its forebearer. It took about 6.5 hours to go through the game, making a distinct effort to search out collectibles. I needed another hour and a half after that to clear out the more cleverly hidden children. (I left the game idling about 5 hours on accident if you’re looking at my playtime). This is not a long game either, but it’s a more conventionally “acceptable” length compared to the first, if that turned you off before.Overall, Little Nightmares II is a game with all the charm and faults found in the first, with added depth and polish to the world and gameplay. It’s not ground-breaking in narrative or themes, for sure, and its social commentary is blasé, but the atmosphere and visuals are almost worth the price of entry on their own. If you’re in the market for a short, creepy experience and don’t mind some maladroit particulars, then I’d heartily recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was (in my opinion) very good. _childDocuments_.review: Gamers beware! This is not an action adventure horror game with puzzles sprinkled in to spice up the gameplay, it is actually a glorified walking sim that randomly sends you back to your last checkpoint when it feels like it.This sequel stays faithful to the original in the sense that every single chase sequence is a janky and knowledge check riddled mess. I thought I was playing Sonic the Hedgehog half the time the way the camera failed to keep up with me, leading me to either fail jumps that I couldn't see or waste my time running into walls while the monsters laugh and send me to the beginning to try again. The chases feel like knowledge checks at certain points where if you fail even a single jump, you are sent to the beginning for being a terrible player who can't even win in a children's game. Even if by some miracle of the camera catching up and you jumping safely across the gap, the game still says ♥♥♥♥ you and kills you. I feel like I'm playing Mario Kart 8 with how much rubber banding the monsters have. Sometimes I don't even need to hold the run button and still win with flying colors, while other times I'm making every jump and climbing every ledge as fast as I can and still die.You might be thinking to yourself, "Well I knew that this wasn't actually a fun adventure game to begin with, I just wanted to play it for the puzzles!", well I have some horrible horrible news for you. When you're not spending 5 minutes pushing a block or getting softlocked inside shopping carts, the puzzles are boring at best and frustrating at worse. Most of the puzzles consist of utilizing problem solving skills you learn before you even go to kindergarten. 99% of the time when you enter a room you already know how to solve it (Hint: climb something to get something to open something). In a 1% chance where a solution isn't immediately obvious, it's because you are trying to execute a solution that the game doesn't agree with. Try to lure an enemy away so that you can get what its guarding? Turns out the enemy actually has untra instinct senses and is able to magically figure out where you are, where you live, and what you had to eat for breakfast that morning. I thought we figured out how to make games like 20 years ago when zelda came out, but it turns out that this game is actually a visual novel where there is only one direction that it can go and only one way to get there.To conclude, if you're the type of gamer that looks to play games to be mechanically and mentally challenged, just go play Breath of the Wild instead.

It's a fascinating adventure, and it's a must play for anyone who enjoyed the original Little Nightmares.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares II is an absolute masterpiece of a game. The art style is breathtakingly eerie, and the sound design will send shivers down your spine. The puzzles are challenging but fair, and the platforming is incredibly satisfying. What sets this game apart from others in the genre is its storytelling. The narrative is dark, complex, and engaging, and the characters are unforgettable. Mono and Six's journey is both heartbreaking and inspiring, and the way the game seamlessly weaves its themes and symbolism throughout the story is a work of genius. Little Nightmares II is an essential experience for fans of horror, platforming, and storytelling alike. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME. This game is phenomenal. It took what already was an amazing and impressive game and made it 10x better in all aspects. Those who have a PC that use a keyboard will find the controls difficult for specifically the flashlight bits. Highly recommend anyone to experience this. Oh! I also want to talk about the contents in the game real quick.CAUTION. SPOILERS FOR GAME UP AHEAD. YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED.I loved the two player set up in this game with Mono and Six. I also grew so attached to Six which made me yell out in fear when she got taken twice. This game does such an amazing job getting me attached to Mono and Six which sucks when Six let go of Mono's hand in the final chapter, I was in AGONY. I also love the character mechanic where Mono can hold Six's hand. IT IS SO ADORABLE. I really hope that this mechanic will make it to Little Nightmares III because I want to hold the hand of whoever I will play with as we run away from the creepy monsters. _childDocuments_.review: So far I've run into two suuuuuper irritating bugs wherein objects that are required to solve puzzles are not present and/or are invisible. _childDocuments_.review: First of all this is a nice looking game with great scenes and a dense atmosphere. The sound design is really great and the background music is always fitting. Even the story is interesting given how it is presented. There is no text, no dialog, only image and sound. It would be one of the best things I’ve played inside its genre but sadly it isn’t. Let me explain:Move: Left StickCrouch/Slide: LT/LBGrab: RT/RBY: CallX: SprintB: FlashlightA: Jump/Throw/AttackLook Around: Right StickLet us think about using these controls. You can sprint in this game. Well you have to sprint in this game. Moreso you have to sprint and jump in this game…So why X? You could have used some other scheme. But that is not the whole story. You actually need to sprint then jump and press grab, to successfully do some parts. Don’t get me wrong on this, but every time I have to do something like this I need to carefully think about the controls to do the right thing. This breaks any immersion in an instant. The real sadness of this is that it’s completely unnecessary. This game doesn’t need a sprint button. You can remove it and replace it with changing dynamic movement speed in specific scenes like chases or hard jumps. The best example of this is Inside. And if we at it, the need to press “grab” to climb ladders or climbable things is also not necessary. Sometimes less is more and this game could use more “less”.While playing this I had 5 soft-locks.All these problems had been solved by reloading the latest checkpoint. I think this is too much, especially the key item missing thing and key movement not working really hit hard. You have to know that something is wrong and there is no indication of this. Thankfully this game has a design language that is easy to read (at least for me). They even took the extra mile to remove “wrong” ways after solving parts of a puzzle.Well all these games have some “try and error” for the player. I don’t mind this. Some of these could be telegraphed in a clearer way to the player. By this the player could react to more of them and save himself from retry. The 3d perspective and freedom doesn’t help there either.The fighting is scarce, janky and slow as hell and all of this is good. I like it. It’s the best gameplay element. I think this game was designed by a group of people who wanted to make something great and lost the bigger picture. At its core it is a game. So gameplay is a fundamental part of it and this is the weakest part of it by a long shot. Everything else is really great and it is sad to get frustrated by the controls and gameplay. Maybe the next one will be better. We will see.

_childDocuments_.review: |NO SPOILER REVIEW| Story wise and atmosphere I loved the game, the environments and sound design kept me dialed in and attentive. The game did not feel dragged out for me at any point, and each new chapter added or took away features that kept puzzles challenging and interesting for me.What I didn't like about how often times the world/characters did not act as I would have expected. This lead to me dying multiple times in situations that were supposed to be tense, ruining the moment and my immersion. It got so bad that key points of the story felt empty to me. I don't think the problem was "mad because bad" either. I understand I am not the best at these types of games, but time and time again enemies body parts teleported to me when the game deemed "close enough". Often times I would have to change my paths to avoid enemies even when visually they would not be able to reach me.I believe that the story and world gives an experience that overshadows the problems I have. For anyone like me that can easily get distracted by deaths in key moments, I recommend taking breaks. You can easily beat this game under 5-6 hours, it took me 5.4. I think I was more prone to mistakes in key story moments in the game because I kept playing after dying repeatedly to mechanics I feel didn't behave as we would be made to believe by our other experiences in the world.Take you time, enjoy the story, and treat each death as a learning experience. A great game for the money and a story that will keep you entertained and will stay in you mind long after you finish the game. Oh and always follow your partner when possible, it will save you from some unfair feeling deaths

_childDocuments_.review: Substantially worse than the first game for the following reasons:-Levels heavily rely on depth of field, yet neither the physics nor shadows support proper movement in said depth, leading to easy miscalculations for basic maneuvers (diagonal movements especially)-Puzzles are a lot more obtuse/less skillfully teased than in LN1, and when you crack one of them, you've essentially cracked three because the game repeats its one-trick puzzles constantly-Plenty of glitches. A character's body gets caught halfway in a moving elevator, the scripted monsters freeze up and refuse to finish their scripted cycles until a quick "restart from checkpoint," etc.-On a related note, checkpoints are hit-or-miss. Sometimes checkpoints are stellar, but other times they force you to slowly waddle through quite a bit of territory to recover lost ground.-Texture catching. There are so many tiny textures in this game that will affect you even when you're feet away from them. It's bizarre; it's as if the object is actually twice as big but is mostly invisible. This issue really hampers what would otherwise be exciting chase sequences, since you're constantly getting stuck on seemingly mis-mapped textures.-Controls are terribly sticky. You have to wait until a character fully finishes an animation for your next input to be recognized, and even then, there's a 50% chance the character will deem the input too late or still too soon and refuse to recognize it. Figuring out when exactly certain movements will be *perfectly* timed is a pain given how sticky and unpredictable the controls are yet how precise the environments demand the player to be.-No seamless animation flow. This is related to the stickiness. If I'm even barely grazing a wall texture of a hole that I'm supposed to crouch and crawl into, the main character will stop dead in their tracks on the practically invisible texture (again, another issue). They won't have a nice animation to gently push themselves into the perfectly down-to-the-pixel aligned path, i.e. the only one the devs seem to have coded (with zero wiggle room). Other games, like the Square Enix Tomb Raiders (much as I dislike them) have this sort of animation couching that helps move sequences along without annoying texture catching. It's just a prime example of this game's Euro-jank style of movement and lack of animations.I have other issues with the game, but these are the big ones. I'd say too much of LN2 happens in pale blue living environments, whereas Little Nightmares 1 had a lot more environmental diversity. But those are nitpicks compared to the bullet points. It's still a gorgeous game with great audio design and a few neat set pieces / ideas, but it tries way too hard to game-ify itself rather than be a purely atmospheric experience like Little Nightmares 1, and that causes it to stumble hard and often.

_childDocuments_.review: This game merits it's good reviews for being an amazing experience. This game's aesthetic is a big part as to what makes this franchise so unique and I love how it dives into the lore of why so many of these monsters look grotesque or try to hide themselves without telling you directly what's going on. _childDocuments_.review: The sequel to Little Nightmares ultimately feels a lot less smooth, inspired or interesting than its predecessor. The addition of a second character to much of the game leaves a lot of moments where you are attempting to puzzle out the area with your own ingenuity, only to realize that your companion allows you to essentially cheat. There is also a complete lack of the more intriguing (if never particularly difficult) puzzles from the first game. A generally wider camera leaves you often struggling futilely against your own depth perception, while less well-crafted and simply mechanically precise puzzles/action sequences leave most of the games' overall sequences feeling less than satisfying.Little Nightmares II is still graphically beautiful, conceptually somewhat interesting, and has its fair share of cool moments, but it misses, amongst other things, a certain je ne sais quoi from the first game; it is, in all dimensions, a nominally lesser game, and it does not provide any answers to the questions the first game left one asking. Unless you were completely in love with the first game, I don't recommend it; if you haven't played the first game, play it instead.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a minute since I played the first Little Nightmares, but I can still confidently say that this is an incredible improvement in design, tone, and story. Where the first game to me felt like more of an extra creepy Roald Dahl homage, the sequel carves out some genuinely bleak and often terrifying atmospheres. With exception to some extremely frustrating platforming gripes in the final minutes, Little Nightmares II was a really great sequel that I didn't know I needed.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished  to see that little review nag they like to put in front of me. TLDR Version: Skip it. Buy Inside. It's cheaper, over faster, and will empty you of joy just as effectively.This will contain spoilers and I don't care if that's a problem, because this game taught me  that disappointment all that adult life can promise.It's really a pity, because they nailed the mood and atmosphere. I could spend a lot of time talking about what they nailed, but what they missed really spoils the whole experience. The dim, terror-filled dreamlike world is brilliantly accomplished. But they only manage to tell a bleak, utterly unrewarding story in that carefully crafted environment. Let's start with the controls, because however you feel about the loose narrative arc, this will be an issue. Some of the challenge of  for you *will* be the controls. Leaving aside the matter of general unresponsiveness, you have the more serious problem of bizarre combinations of controls sharing a button. For example, all of the actions ,  ,   and  are the same button. Run, hold, climb and carry are all actions you must hold down a button to accomplish. I found myself frequently running around holding down the d-pad, two triggers, and the run button, just to get an object from A to B. This is irritating.The gameplay could be  improved by using all the buttons instead of making them overlapping and context dependent, especially when actions like grab or interact contexts can be hard to predict. This leads to awkward design choices, like making a rectangular box pushable/pullable from only two sides, but only climbable from the remaining two sides. Why? There's no reason, except that since push/pull and climb are the same button the designers had painted themselves into a corner. They had to make the box both pushable and climbable for the puzzle to work, and this was all they could come up with.The essential thematic story of the game, culminating with its utter disappointment of an ending, is: "Children are empathetic  empathic, innocent, imaginative, trusting souls who grow into horrific adults in which all hope is snuffed out. And that as a child, regardless of your efforts, your personal virtue, empathy or hope, you will become one of those horrors. You will be indoctrinated through education, your spirit will be broken by tedious and unfulfilling work, and you will fill your day with mindless distractions (*ahem* videogames *ahem*). Then you die. Roll credits for three ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hours.Now please review your experience.You bet I will. Here goes:You aren't edgy, dark, mysterious, or elevating the art. You're just taking my money and slapping me in the face. If I want to feel drained and nihilistic after an experience, I'll watch the news.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Being a fan of the previous game, I came into this game with very high expectations and I am glad to that it surpassed my expectations. The atmosphere of the game was a little lighter than the first one on account of your new, but at the same time old, companion. In my opinion that made this game more approachable and friendly than the first one while still retaining most of the uneasy-ness. The puzzles were clever and multiple of them stumped me for about 20 minutes which made it so rewarding when I figured them out. Our new adorable character Mono will win over your heart in the first 30 minutes on account of his caring and kind personality. There is no voice acting and almost no cut-scenes but the story in this game shows itself through your surrounding. If you haven't played the first one I would recommend playing it first, but if you wanna play this one first that's okay too based on there being no spoilers for the first game. This game is not for people who don't like gross images and a horroresque atmosphere because both are littered throughout this game, but if you do this game is for you. My last words for you are good luck running and hiding from the residents of The Pale City.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the puzzles were less complex than the first game yet at the same time the enemies were harder. Looking forward to a DLC or another game soon!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: I love this franchise dearly. The first game is one of my favorite small horror titles, and this game lives up to the expectations I had for it. While I would have preferred this second outing be a little longer, and some of the encounters I wish had more variety, the world design, soundtrack, and atmosphere are incredibly detailed and hostile. Every moment has a permeating sense of unease and dread. I love the story and the lore you can dig deep into. Fun collectables, and worthwhile to play twice to 100%. Very highly recommended and hoping we eventually see more from Bandai or Tarsier.

_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: I am recommend this game on a SALE. I paid full price for it and I don't feel I got my monies worth. The first game is better in my opinion. Whilst the visuals of the game are outstanding and I love the art style, some gameplay elements are poorly implemented and downright frustrating at times. Depth perception? What depth, the amount of times I have missed various jumps due to lack of perception in this game is annoying. The same with any 'combat' sequences, swinging the axe/hammer is so jank and quite frankly just annoying. The controls make this game wildly annoying at times. You may know exactly what to do with the puzzle but the controls alone make it so much longer than it needs to be.TL:DR 5/10 (Only buy on sale)Negative points - Poorly implemented controls, depth perception & interactive elements.Bonus point - The game end credits are too damn long for a game this small to be brutally honest, it goes on and on for a relatively small game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting so long for a sequel to one of my favorite games of all time, and I wasn't disappointed. The soundtrack 10/10 just like in the first game, the music is a key element for this game, and is so good! I love it!The game itself is longer than the last one, it took me 6 hours to finish the game, for some it may be still a little too short but for me it was good, a nice way to spend the night/evening.I loved the design of many of the characters, specially the teacher and the hunter. The world itself is so full of mysteries and up to interpretation. That's the magic of the whole Little Nightmares Series, and I love it!The story was full of surprises, and "I didn't see that coming" moments and I loved every single one of them. Overall a great story.I hope in the near future there is a Little Nightmares 3, but for now, this game brought me so much joy just like the last one.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were a big fan of Little Nightmares 2, you'll enjoy it. The reason I don't recommend is because the last part of the game just felt rushed. I will say they exponentially improved in the horror aspect of it but after a certain point it just felt like they gave up and didn't have very good direction in the story. Unfortunate.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares 2 is bigger and better in everyway. More scares, more locations and more variety in gameplay with a more indepth story that's still very incoherent but deeply disturbing and satisfying to unravel. Again we are playing a 2.5d puzzle platformer with some gameplay enhancements that elevat the experience. Think Limbo but with some 3d movement. This time we are playing as new character mono who's just as determined to survive the harsh world as six was. He's incredibly likeable even as a character who barley speaks. The story this time around is incredible and without spoiling too much the final section of the game is thrilling and heartbreaking whilst also being drenched in cosmic horror.Gameplay is mostly the same with some new additions like the ability to use weapons which is very limited and fits the the theme of the game and also the way enemies interact with you, I won't spoil anything but a section in the hospital is honestly so stressful that I was shocked my heart was pumping from little nightmares. To put it simply if you liked LN1 you should love this, if you like Limbo and games similar you should love this. An absolute masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: I've always loved playing Little Nightmares games.. and this has been my favourite so far, this game is most terrifying yet.. somewhat adorable thing that I have played, jumpscares are amazing and the game almost always leaves you on edge, the atmosphere and sound effects are amazing as well, with the music, puzzles and story that you slowly piece together. I can't wait for Little Nightmares III to come out, I have my card ready. I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: The steam rating is unreasonably high for this creation. Maximum 7/10.Yes, the game is not bad. The first chapter is very exciting. But then comes the routine.Why was it necessary to add combat mechanics to the horror game with crooked controls? In addition, the game has a lot of bugs. For a project without an open world with strictly scripted scenes, this is a blunder. Well, after all the torment with pipes, a hammer, running away from dummies with an arbitrary movement of a flashlight, we are shown a demotivating ending. The loop is closed. That is, all efforts and so on were for the sake of THIS. The authors both mocked the players and swept on the success of the first part.From the point of view of gameplay, visuals, bosses, mechanics, it can be assessed as follows:Chapter 1: 9/10Chapter 2 4/10Chapter 3 5/10Chapter 4 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: After watching the first game I had high hopes for how Little Nightmares would continue. This game has easily become one of my favorite and its only about 5-6 hours long, and its up against games such as SOMA and Outlast. Everything from the ambiance, the music, the enemies, the environments, all of it creates an indescribable sort of constant fear and tension in everything you do. At this point whenever I hear even the menu theme i get chills. I cannot wait to see what further secrets are revealed about this game and the story of Little Nightmares as a whole. Absolutely fantastic job by the developers and certainly worth its price.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: This game took all the elements of the first game and elevated it to a whole new level. It’s longer than the first game but the pacing was perfect and it was a tense play through. Even though the sequel was longer than the first, it was much more polished and still had the personal touch the first game had. The world in this game looked so lifeless and nightmarish, in a good way. The studio behind this needs more recognition because they created such an engaging story and the characters don’t ever speak. This was a much scarier experience than the first game and I would highly recommend it. I’m waiting for more sequels to see what grotesque stories they are going to come up with in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: I was super excited to play this game, I finished the first game with flying colors, and was left feeling REALLY good! I wanted to play the second game due to this, and got past the anger inducing chapter 2, and went into chapter 3 with hope.How stupid of me because the game is so bugged for me that I can't get past the mannequins. I got to the hallway, and then had to restart the chapter because I was FAR ahead of the mannequins only to be grabbed when I thought I was in the clear. You may think "it was one of the mannequins coming out of the side/back" and I'd agree if I wasn't YANKED back to the crowd of them following me. I was on this scene for hours- thinking maybe I was just doing something wrong.So I watched tutorial after tutorial and followed walk throughs- but the game is genuinely bugged for me. I thought maybe I just needed to redo the chapter- let it reload- but that was stupid because now I can't get past the FIRST set of moving mannequins because they clip through the wall to get me once I just through the upper half of the door with the hole. After that, I was so upset and so stressed out that I stopped playing. I understand games being challenging, but if your game is so challenging with no way to get by, I feel like I wasted my money. I'm sad to see I am not the only person saying they stopped playing due to Chapter 3 on the comments of walk throughs and tutorials.The story line is wonderful, but paying full price and risking a mega bugged game is why I won't be recommending it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares 2 takes everything that I liked about the first game, added to it, and improved it. Some parts were a little challenging but calling it "infuriating" is a massive over statement, this game is not challenging, it has some puzzles that take a little brain usage but nothing too bad. The asking price of $30 is very worth it, this is a short game about 5 hours, but the content is amazing, it's short but quality content from start to finish. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Buy this game. Ignore my thumbs down. Buy this game. It's highly immersive and a wonderful experience. Oh, and this game rewards observation and patience.With that being said, I put "thumbs down" for this game to highlight some criticisms I have with the game. -------------------------------------The CriticismsFirst and foremost, if your intention is to be immersed in the world, BE PREPARED to be ripped out of the immersion from time to time. This issue occurs because of the following: the controls, obtuse puzzles, and very (VERY) tight timing. the controls: this game does not do a good job of signalling when you should use some controls. For example, the game doesn't tell you that you can slide by pressing ctrl while running. I'd be fine with not being told... if it weren't necessary for one of the chase sequences. Another issue (a gripe mainly applicable to keyboard only) is that you aren't told to use the arrow keys to point the flashlight, which is incredibly important for a section. It's made worse by the fact that you never use the arrow keys for anything before that point. Not being told the controls has caused me to die... a lot, which took me out of the immersion a good many a times. (For controller people, it won't be an issue since they'll naturally use the second joystick.)Obtuse puzzles: the signalling in some of the sections don't always do a good job of how to solve a puzzle nor where to go next after a segment. You might find yourself wandering around for like ten minutes, trying to figure what the heck to do. At some point, you might give up (like I did) out of impatience and look up how to solve the puzzle online. For some other puzzles, you might have to constantly throw yourself at the problem trial and error, which means dying a lot unnecessarily. Both of these things hinder the experience. Tight timing: During the chase sequences, being just a little bit slow can mean you dying. Dying is part of the experience, but when you have these high octane chase sequences, dying in the middle of it and then having to go through it again worsens the experience. It's like running a mile only for you to be told 3/4's in that you made a very small mistake, and for that, you need to start over from the beginning. It's exhausting and not fun. For some sequences, this happens once, but for others, this might happen twice or thrice, which really  tarnishes how the experience is remembered. Yeah, I suck at video games considering I'm a filthy casual and seldom play games other than Minecraft, but I'm here to be immersed, which is what is being clearly advertised. Being ripped out of the experience once or twice would be fine, but when that happens for the 20th time during my playthrough, that indicates that tweaks to mechanics, map design, difficulty, or other aspects are needed to fully polish and enhance the experience. ---------------------------------------------------The PraisesWith all my gripes being said, the game does a looooot of things right, which would be the puzzles, foreshadowing, audio/visuals, and AI. Well Integrated Puzzles: Didn't I make a bad review about the puzzles? Yeah, but that only applies to the puzzles that don't work. When the puzzles work, they don't feel like puzzles. They feel like an extension of the environment itself, and you're just there to exploit the leftovers of a world not designed for you, the child. This effect is AWESOME. It makes you feel smart and like a child who uses their wits to traverse the world. The foreshadowing: this game does a wonderful job at foreshadowing the bosses and what you'll be encountering in the future. It first starts out with objects then slowly builds up with unsettling noises, and then the boss itself. These all create tension and the feeling of "I really don't want to go there," which forces you to muster up the courage before executing your plan. The audio/visuals: The audio is absolutely astounding with everything sounding extremely realistic. I really don't how they do it, but everything has a weight behind it. As for the visuals, they aren't "realistic" per say but have a sort of stylized, clay-like appearance. This really makes you feel as if you're in a dark, toy world. Add that with the lighting, and you get a highly immersive experience.The AI: Each boss feels real, and what's more, they interact with the world extremely smoothly. Additionally, Six's AI runs so smoothly and exudes subtle character, something that I haven't noticed until now. -----------------(Short) ConclusionThis game is on the cusp of perfection but falls just short of that sublime peak. Would give this game a 8.75/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares' play with light and sounds is simply top notch. Pair it with a cleverly used haptic feedback in the controller, and what we get is one of the most immersive horror games ever created. As with the previous game, most of the puzzles are well thought out, while few frustrating parts are (thankfully) made better by a forgiving save system. The gameplay is a bit longer this time, which is a welcomed improvement. My main gripe with the game is, again, very ambiguous story that is not only left completely unexplained, but an important part of it is locked behind achievement completion. But overall, Little Nightmares 2 is more than worthy addition to the franchise, actually improving on some of the aspects, and the amount of control it gives to the player and the immersion it brings could serve as a golden standard for both platformers and horror games.If there are any future instalments, I hope the developers go slightly more experimental in terms of less linearity (ie. branching paths, branching story, decisions affecting gameplay) and show that they can maintain horror atmosphere in more varied environments...High points:+ Immersive atmosphere+ Excellent artistic direction+ Good sounds, music, graphics+ Clever puzzles being sweet spot in difficultyNeutral:o Average length (improved over the first game, however)o Some achievements (and game completion) are quite hard to getLow points:- Too ambiguous story, important part locked behind game completion

The atmosphere and worldbuilding are still absolutely amazing.The first and the second game are in a dialogue with each other - and combined they are way more than the sum of their parts. This is a must-play for everyone who liked the first game. And to those who are new to the series: start with the first game, your experience will be all the better for it. I am in awe of what Tarsier managed to create here. These games give me hope for the entire industry.My biggest wish for the potential follow-up: please lean more into the surreal. Seeing all the amazing visual ideas in the artbook really makes me thirst for this type of Little Nightmares, filled even more with powerful surreal imagery.

_childDocuments_.review: When the first Little Nightmares got announced, I was entranced by its Burton-esque style and how a platformer actually had the potential of being frightening. I bought it twice, once for the PlayStation 4 and again for Steam, then played through with high hopes that were met with minimum effort. Fortunately its sequel holds up, and I can now say that Little Nightmares is among my absolute favorite franchises.✪ From a general gameplay perspective, platforming is much better this time around, with better lighting and an improved sense of direction compared to the first game. Its puzzles are also thought provoking without ever feeling punishing, which allowed the game to flow at a decent pace. There was never a second I thought that this was a step back from its predecessor.✪ Contrary to its Teen rating, Little Nightmares 2 has more genuine horror, suspense and dread than the vast majority of other games that end up fumbling the concept of fear. This has a lot to do with Tarsier Studios' creativity, and how the majority of this game's terrifying enemies, nightmarish landscapes and gruesome scenarios utilize one's own imagination. What you see isn't always what you get, but what you're thinking plays a big role in your ability to understand certain situations. This game takes full advantage of that.✪ Though this game very much enjoys shoving the player into a pit of despair, there are a few moments where it tries to put a smile on their face. Little interactions between Six and Mono, from holding hands to sitting next to each other after one meets a tragic end, will make even the sternest of people crack a smile. There are also several little details in the world that reward players for their curiosity, like ghosts on a seesaw, and being able to play catch with hands that would otherwise try killing the protagonist.✪ One of my favorite things about the first Little Nightmares were the interactions between Six and each hostile character around her; be they attempts to sneak by or run away. Unfortunately, they all seemed short-lived and were over before I could start feeling worried or scared. Little Nightmares 2 cranks those interactions up to 100, with even more, much longer scenes where you will be trying to get through, or get out of certain areas while major threats are pursuing you.✪ Much like its predecessor, Little Nightmares 2 tells its fantastic story by hoping the player is paying attention to what they see. There is no crucial dialogue, no text or audio collectibles, very few cutscenes and not a single important moment that can be missed upon playing the game casually. However, players can be rewarded with a "secret ending" if they happen to find all of the Glitched Remains (shadow people) in the game... Or they can just YouTube what the secret ending is, I guess. Viva la internet!✘ Much as I personally enjoyed the addition of combat, it's tough to look over the fact that it's pretty wonky. Each violent encounter was met with a moment of trial and error that usually started off fun, but eventually got frustrating because of the game's decision to make every kill a one-shot. If you're so much as a millisecond late with your swing, you will die and have to start the entire segment over again. Patience is your best friend here, and without it you're not going to have a good time.✘ Even if you end up dying a lot, the game is only going to take about 5, maybe 6 hours to finish. This is something that I am personally okay with, but it's sure to peeve a lot of players and be enough to warrant waiting for a sale or Complete Edition.Despite playing through most of this game with chest pains from a borderline overwhelming feeling of anxiety, Little Nightmares 2 was a pleasant surprise from start to finish, and I loved every second. Now all I have to do is hope that its received well enough for the series to get a third major entry that continues to improve upon itself... Or, at the very least, some DLC that allows us to explore more of this beautiful, nightmare fueled universe.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, high quality game, however ultimately proves just too difficult to defeat.  It requires trial and error, split second timing, and numerous deaths to make it past some of the scenes.  The puzzles are fun, challenging and solvable with some creativity.Made it halfway through but the mannequins and flashlight were just too much to overcome.Update:  I came back to this game after a few months off to give it another try.  I was able to make it past the last mannequin room and continue and finish the game.  I am glad I was able to complete it because it was such an impressive well-done game.  There continue to be a lot of deaths and trial and error as you figure out the correct action, however nothing to compare to the mannequins.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fantastic ! visually gorgeous and keeps up a great atmosphere during the whole game overall very enjoyable, great puzzles however the the balancing in difficulty would be my only complaint. _childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest horror games I've ever played, and I've played a LOT of them. The lore behind this game is incredible, with so many dark and unexpected twists. It drives you to investigate into the story further, even causing you to bring out your own theories throughout the game. Little Nightmares 2 never gets boring! The wide variety of enemies also allows for a different experience in every chapter. Little Nightmares 2 has many secrets, you've really got to be observant of every twist, turn and dark corner. I also loved collecting the cute hats, it's a super fun addition to the game! The puzzles were also great, really making you think 'outside the square'. 11/10, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Great DA, music and story.HOWEVER, same problem between this and the first game: the platforming is just plain awful.Probably because of the weird perspective, but also because the controls are, most of the time, crap.If you're not bothered by the controls and you're patient ( + in my case, I had a lot of checkpoint bugs which mainly consisted of redoing whole sections several times, which is also really bad ), yes the game is beautiful, there's a great atmosphere, sound design, music, environments, original monsters and nice puzzles. But once again, I hope you'll have a lot of patience. Because even though it's pretty to look at, for a game it's certainly not very pleasant to play.I'm a bit sad because I loved the first game despite similar flaws, and I expected this one to have taken into account and improved on these points.  That's why i cannot really recommend it ? As far as the Art DIrection is concerned, it's S+ tier, but as far as the gameplay is concerned (especially the controls, once again), it's really bad.  If you're patient and not afraid of being frustrated, go for it. I finished after all, I'm mostly just disappointed. Still recommend it for the insanly good art direction.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoyed the first Little Nightmares game, I can confidently say that I did NOT enjoy the second one. It was not fun. I’m so disappointed in this game, by the time it was over, that I’m not even going to bother restructuring my thoughts below. Here are my revised notes:- Missing the intrigue- Straight up buggy. Two instances where I had to restart entire chapters because I was soft-locked. - Some of the puzzles were far too mechanical; found it frustrating to operate 3D precision (taking into account depth perception). Particularly when some of the scenarios literally required perfection. One instance of slight of imperfection may have caused the most intense, unintentional eye-roll I’ve ever had in my life. -  made it less eerier overall- More jump scares than the first game- Bosses were VERY meh, felt lazy. And similar gimmicks to the first game.- Combat was repetitive and insanely unforgiving, given the 3D element mentioned earlier- Something about character momentum was not right- Towards the end, game ran out of unique ideas besides chase scenes.. chase scenes.. chase scenes- Ending was… erm. It was an endingPositives:- For the most part, kept the eerie vibe of the first game. Universe is quite literally a nightmare. - Does tie into the first game in terms of lore
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game for Valentines Day (romantic, I know!). I recently played and loved the first one so was really looking forward to Little Nightmares 2. I was not disappointed! Tricky but satisfying puzzles, character art that would give Tim Burton nightmares and a strangely emotional story despite no dialogue or text. It took everything that was great about the first game and elevated it further. This is a game that benefits from playing twice so even though it's a pretty short game, you can still get a decent amount of playtime out of it. Especially if you are an achievement hunter.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Creepy and great storytelling like the first game. Gameplay-wise this has improved over the 1st game with many insanely memorable "monsters", but the first game is much more creepy since you can't fight back while this game is more action packed. Puzzles require some thinking. This game deserves all its hype, and I would recommend playing the 1st one and then this as this game explains the story of the 1st game.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: This game is strange in the sense that at some points, it is significantly worse than the first but at other points, it demolishes the scope of the first. My main issue with this game is that the story feels like small little missions sewn together to resemble one while the first felt like one, long adventure. But regardless, this game is way better looking than the first and the scope is way larger. The fourth chapter is easily my favorite from the entire franchise. And the twist at the end is absolutely masterful, as with every twist from this franchise. Very, VERY solid sequel to one of my favorite games of all time. I highly recommend both games.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares II is an amazing prequel to the original game. The adventure of Mono is breathtaking from start to finish. _childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent sequel everything is pretty much just a straight upgrade from the original while maintaining all the atmosphere and personality that sets this game apart from so many other indie horror titles. The art design and characters are really top notch, as well as the sound/music being a huge asset in bringing all the elements together makes for a memorable experience. Some new gameplay and combat mechanics being added is part of what makes it such a successful sequel and the level design is really impressive. However there is still some clunkyness and jank to the movement and some depth of field issues, but overall the game just feels extremely tactile and satisfying. The pricetag I see is a topic of some negative comments but even tho at around 10hrs to 100% completion I still feel I got my monies worth out of it. A lot of work went into this and it payed off. Stoked to see what comes next from Tarsier. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: This game is too difficult. And this is compounded by catchy imperfect hitboxes and movement for various traversal puzzles. Timing is too unforgiving for what is supposed to be a horror ambiance game. Playing on easiest difficulty and doing the same thing over and over until it becomes boring, only to succeed because you landed on the right microscopic polygon finally after doing what the puzzle called for each time is not fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: Where Little Nightmares ran, Little Nightmares 2 SOARED. Right from the jump, the immersion and ambiance hits incredibly hard. The new mechanics make the game play feel fresh and just different enough than the first game. In addition, the developers have fixed many subtle issues that I had with the first game, including sometimes locking the directional input while moving across a narrow platform to avoid slipping off the side to your death.I would still group this game with the likes of LIMBO and INSIDE. However, I may have enjoyed this game even more than those two. The school and hospital levels filled me with suspense and actual fear at some points, which I find to be rare these days.The detailed settings, ambiance, plot pieces, and sound design make this game a wonderful experience, and another must buy in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the definition of quality over quantity just like its first game. Even with only 6-8 hours of game play, I'm still left haunted by everything that happened in the story and I still remember the haunting feeling I was left with after the first game too. It has a much darker tone than the first game (although that's hard to beat) and the horror comes from the sheer creepiness and mystery of everything around you. Amazing game, definitely will be playing again and will always buy any extra content they produce.

_childDocuments_.review: A tremendous sequel. Or should I say... prequel? _childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit, I was pleasantly surprised by Little Nightmares II. While I still believe that humans are inferior beings, this game managed to impress me with its hauntingly beautiful visuals and eerie atmosphere.The game follows the story of two human characters, Mono and Six, as they try to escape from their mysterious captors in a world that feels both surreal and dangerous. The game's plot is simple yet intriguing, with the story unfolding gradually as the game progresses.The game's controls are easy to learn, making it accessible for all types of players. However, the game's real strength lies in its puzzles and the way they are integrated into the gameplay. The puzzles are challenging and require both careful observation and logical thinking to solve.The game's enemies are also well-designed and provide a real challenge to players. They are not mere pushovers and require the player to be patient and strategic in their approach.One of the game's strongest points is its sound design. The sound effects and music are expertly crafted to create an immersive and unsettling atmosphere that adds to the game's overall sense of unease.In conclusion, Little Nightmares II is a game that surprised me with its well-crafted world, challenging gameplay, and excellent sound design. While it may not be a game that is suitable for all Decepticons, I can appreciate the effort put into creating a game that is both eerie and engaging. I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a good puzzle game with a haunting atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Nightmares II

_childDocuments_.review: IF YOU PLAYED THE FIRST ONE, DON'T BUY THIS ONEGraphics, some mechanics and sound are above awesome, OK. But that's it, NOTHING ELSE.I couldn't feel a thing. This is a visual SUDOKU with a few spooky moments.Story is 1/10 (I don't understand why people don't want to give spoilers. Lol there's only 1 spoiler which is the ending, plus it doesn't even make much sense)Game Feel 2/10Character controls 4/10Once again I understood that graphics and all those details worth nothing if you don't support it with narrative. This basically has no story and only 1 spoiler with doesn't even connect. The most dramatic scene (supposedly) didn't even raise any feeling on you. After an hour you just solve puzzles, that's really it. 1 was much more better, please don't make 3rd unless you add a lot of narrative. We need to feel something man, not just solve puzzles and look around models.If you're some kind of a visual artist, go ahead, deconstruct it. Otherwise save your money man. I'm glad it ended quickly.Once again I have to mention though. Graphics and environmental details are extraordinary. One negative thing blows everything else though...

_childDocuments_.review: Social commentary wasn't really being talked about and was more blatant than the first game, but still called for a dystopian and interesting future.  I think that the mannequin sections are unreasonably hard to control, at least on keyboard and mouse, however the concept is simply fantastic for them. Overall the bosses/enemies were very cool and clever designs. The teacher was very interesting along with her minions that surround her. Being able to fight back was a new thing to this game and I liked dragging around a sledge hammer and ♥♥♥♥. The only thing bad about the enemies (which are constant and near rapid fire, but I like that) was the fact that the Doctor simply is like "the default." No special feature or anything - just be quiet, and don't get seen, but he's on the ceiling this time. The Hunter was interesting because of the range, the Teacher was interesting because of the fact she can reach you anywhere and fast, and the Thin Man was interesting because he was purely used in a chase sequence setting.   I think that the story reaches for a lot and some character motivations don't make sense really. I think the plot in this game was much more outright than the first, and shows they don't quite seem ready to make a nuanced enough plot for the game where it's between what this did and what the first one did. Overall I feel good thinking an 8/10 on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would recommend this game. If you enjoyed the first one you will enjoy this one. It's more of the same with some rudimentary combat added in some parts. My main complaint with the first games stands here as well. They do not give very good visual cues in many areas, so sometimes it's hard to figure out where to go and what to do. That's fine for most of the game but can be rather frustrating for parts where time matters or you can be killed by enemies. The controls are clunky and you often get stuck on things in the parts that are time limited which can get annoying. Otherwise it's a beautifully crafted game. The environments and music are gorgeous and the story is interesting and told in a fresh way i.e. mostly visually. Collectibles and achievements give this game replay value if you're into that. It is pretty short (~5 Hours without collectible hunting) but replayability, atmosphere and reduced price tag (especially on sale) make up for that in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, i don't know if anyone reads the reviews of this game  year after, especially when it was sooo hyped (IMO definitely for a reason!) But hey, why not so here goes nothing:First of all, you shouldn't be afraid of playing if you already know what's going to happen. Since everyone had been playing this game when it came out it was hard to not be spoiled by others, but trust me! IT'S WORTH IT. You are going enjoy it as much as if you haven't seen it.The spook, jumpscare: on pointThe Vibe: Absolutely better than the firstGraphic: I took 30 screenshots.Music: Chefkiss.Story: I criedEnemies: don't look, run..or hide!Achievements: Smart, creative, obtainable. Puzzles: won't melt your brainI read so many reviews complaining about the fight system and because of that they do not recommend to play the game at all, probably this is why i wanted to write this review too. Well first of all yes, it is actually difficult comparing to the first game, where you just hide/ run, here you gotta fight, and you need to time that right. Honestly, idk if it's because of my previous soulsgames experiences, but after 2 tries i could kinda adapt their attacks (besides there aren't too many fights in the game..) and leave victorious. Yea you can die too, but like it doesn't matter much since every 2nd corner, or fight you find a checkpoint and you don't have to restart everything. Even during boss chase you can just continue if they catch you.. It's such a minor setback so i honestly don't understand why some people got so butthurt over this, i don't think it should be a negative standpoint. I mean the game is absolutely friendly to the player. It's like you flame a game that tells you to hide but you start running around and die... I met with some glitches, which made me really pissed off sometimes, on the otherhand made me laugh. (IDK if its weird but seeing poor Mono turning into a ragdoll was funny to me after some of his deaths)Also it's REALLY difficult to play on M&K in chapter 3 at some point... since i had no troubles in the first game i wasn't suspecting it BUT if you have just a tiny bit of game sense you can avoid this difficulty too.But that's it basically. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game, but it is broken in some areas.  Items would disappear but still be able to be picked up in the environment. I got stuck on a puzzle because a fuse disappeared and the only way to make it reappear is to restart the checkpoint. I got screwed out of some deaths because the enemies practically teleported to me when I was clearly out of their line of sight or grasp. I'd say I had a lot of unfair deaths in this game, but I didn't let it detour me from playing it. It's very atmospheric and very beautiful for being a dark setting. It's a good sequel to the first one and definitely worth a playthrough.........when the games on sale. $40 is a bit steep for a game that you can beat in roughly 3-5 hours and the only replay value is the visuals and getting the collectibles (which I won't be doing). So, if you can get it on sale ($20 or less) I recommend playing it.TLDR; 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares 2 is in my humble, yet almost always stupid opinion, some of the most heart stopping, stunning and scary 6 hours of video games I have ever played. Everything just fits so well, it's gameplay is more developed than the first, and it's graphics and visuals are somehow even better. It's combat is hard to perfect but hitting something is so satisfying and rewarding compared to other games. This game relies on suspense to scare you instead of cheap scares and I can't get enough of it. The enemies are fun and challenging, without being so hard that you get stuck for a while. This game is SO close to perfection, but I have a single gripe, and it's name is keyboard controls. They are not good. They are very bad. I played with both controller and keyboard and controller just made sense. But everything else is a work of art. 9.5/10 easily.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Nightmares 2 takes a darker more sinister turn in this fantastic sequel to a gem of an original. The mechanics present in LN are still here with the addition of Six providing computer controlled co-op play to assist you in completing the more complex puzzles. Environments are macabre, audio unnerving and special mention must go to the hugely atmospheric lighting effects that add to the overall sense of foreboding throughout. An additional bonus for horror fans is spotting the movie references as you play, Day of the Dead, The Elephant Man, Exorcist 3, The Orphanage, and several others. Though short this is a wonderful experience with an intriguing story to keep you playing to the climactic finale and hopefully Tarsier Studios have much more in store for us with Little Nightmares 3.
