_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight was such a phenomenal game that I was willing to eat up anything else helmed by Yacht Club Games. Then they announced they were publishing Cyber-Shadow, and after going through The Messenger, aka my favorite indie game up until Ultrakill, I was incredibly pumped for this game, ignoring the fact that this was the developer's first game. Still, not even Yacht Club could save us from a rookie's first game.Much like The Messenger, and the upcoming Bushiden, Cyber-Shadow takes heavy inspiration from the NES Ninja Gaiden, with a lot less unfair difficulty and a lot more cool additions, although the former is certainly not a feature here. Unlike the other games I mentioned, Cyber-Shadow keeps its mechanics simple: you start off with a jump and a horizontal attack and that's it. It can feel pretty slow and basic early into the game. However, those two functions are pretty snappy and feel great to use. Eventually you unlock more abilities like being able to throw shuriken and shoot fire balls upwards, both at the cost of MP. There's no shop to use your currency on, and all of your upgrades are progression-based. You can also upgrade your health by defeating bosses or finding secrets, and you can also upgrade your MP by searching for secrets. You'll also run into power-ups that affect your attacks, such as making your swings longer, giving you a shield, and so on. Aside from the sword extension, they're all super helpful.The boss fights are usually simple but still enjoyable, save for a couple, including the ones I mentioned earlier and two particular bosses on Level 5. I would also like to praise this game's intelligent checkpointing system, where every action is constantly being saved even if you don't necessarily get to the next checkpoint. For instance, let's say you defeat a boss, then go to the left to open a lock in order to open a door to the right, but you die before you reach the next checkpoint. When you revive, the boss will still be defeated and the lock on that door will still be gone.I think the mana system is pretty weak. Your special moves are already very basic and yet they cost so much mana. The game is already designed in a way for you to play through its entirety without ever having to rely on moves that require mana, so it feels very obnoxious to have a system that's this restrictive over moves that are only slightly helpful. The only move I use consistently is the upwards fireball, but even that I barely ever use. I also heavily dislike how currency is only used to upgrade your individual checkpoints so that you can make them heal you completely, replenish your mana or dispense an item that adds an effect to your attacks. Mana is already not that useful, and the most common item that alters your attacks is the one that extends your blade and it's the most useless one.Now for the big downside that has a significant negative impact on this game. Remember when I said the controls feel snappy and responsive? That only applies for the moves I mentioned previously; every other upgrade you get past that point just feels awful. For starters, you get a Shovel Knight style pogo jump with your sword which you can use to bounce off of enemies, but in order to use it, you need to hold down in mid-air and then press X, and then you have to press those buttons again so you can keep the combo going. It's really ironic how the developers who perfected the pogo jump published a game that kinda botched it. The next thing I noticed was the wall jump, which games like Guacamelee and Spark the Electric Jester figured out by just making the player jump automatically away from the wall regardless of the direction they held the button in (and if you held it towards the wall, you will keep jumping up the same wall). Here, you must keep holding towards the wall otherwise you will fall, which makes it incredibly awkward if you're trying to jump towards the opposite wall.That's not even the big elephants in the room; those are the parrying and sprinting/dashing. In order to parry, you must quickly tap towards the projectile coming towards you at the correct timing to stop it in mid-air, then you hit it with your sword to send it back. It's an incredibly unnecessary two-step process that's quite difficult to nail down consistently, where sometimes you'll feel like you should have parried a projectile but you just end up running into it and eating it. Was it really that difficult to just hit a projectile in mid-air with the right timing to send it back? If the developers were so worried about it being broken or busted, they should have just made the bullets fly faster. I ran into two boss fights that heavily relied on you parrying and got stuck at them both because I was constantly struggling and fighting the controls instead of the boss, and it didn't help that that's the point when the game decided out of nowhere that you should take two pips of damage (and sometimes three) from enemy attacks. It's not like I'm not good at timing stuff; I play fighting games and games like Devil May Cry consistently, where perfectly timing everything is super important and I'm actually quite good at it. When someone like me is complaining about it here, something is definitely wrong.When it comes to sprinting, you need to hold down the RB button and move. Your momentum will still carry even when you jump. In order to dash, you need to be sprinting (even if mid-air) and then attack. The issue is that it's incredibly inconsistent to do because of some finnicky controls, and you might even get stuck for a while on the level that requires you to take advantage of dashing. You can't start sprinting while in mid-air; you must be on solid ground first. You also can't hold the sprint button while stationary and then attack to dash. Sometimes, fulfilling the arbitrary criteria the game sets out for dashing doesn't even work, and you'll end up falling into spikes and dying. I've held down sprint, moved, and jumped but for some reason attacking only did a regular attack instead of just making me dash. I've never felt this lack of confidence in a game's platforming mechanics in such a long time. I feel like I am at the mercy of the game's arbitrary decisions rather than a set list of rules or even the limitations of my own skills. Also, your pogo jump and dash use up MP if there's any available, adding even more stress to your stingant mana system.The levels were pretty good up until the second half of the game, where the experience becomes downright miserable. Lots of hazard placements mixed in with some terrible enemies that can track you multiple screens or have inconsistent movement patterns. Some of these hazards and enemies are placed in a way where you can't see them in advance enough to react to them so you just take damage from off-screen. The game also has a habit of eating your inputs, taking away your momentum from a sprint, and so many different inconsistencies that further make the experience that more unfair. On top of that, there are very long stretches between checkpoints at times and it's always at the absolute worst areas in the level. Admittedly, the last level was excellent up until the end where you have to fight three bosses in a row with no healing in-between, adding to the frustration of the third boss being quite disappointing.I initially liked this game and even recommended it, but after having spent more time with it, I have to take all of those good words back. Cyber-Shadow is absolutely a rookie's first game; the terrible controls, the annoying enemies combined with the dreadful later levels that essentially recreate a cheap sense of challenge that the NES Ninja Gaiden games were notorious for. This one is definitely a skip.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the folks saying this is too hard, or the controls are clunky, the games perfectly fine. By far the worst aspect of this game is how short it is, it'll only take you about a day or two to beat this 100%. Still, I'd highly recommend buying this, though I wouldn't blame you if you waited for it to go on sale. What's here is honestly quite good, and the combat is quite nice. Also, to parry, once you actually get the ability, just tap forward towards the bullet once its fairly close. You'll see a blue orb in front of you if you did it right. You can easily parry multiple bullets and even stationary orbs if you time it right. So yeah, go get it, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to love this game.  Would have gladly paid $60 for a game that captured the feel of oldschool NES Ninja Gaiden with upgraded sensibilities.  The level design, however, makes even the cheapest parts from NG1 feel fair, fast, and fluid by comparison.  If I'm playing a ninja, I want to have the best part of my playtime be fighting against actual -enemies- (jump, attack, dodge, etc.) and not have most of my time spent fighting inanimate level progression timing puzzles, and insta-death jump challenges (think the disappearing block climbing segments from the old mega man games, but less intuitive and more infuriating)."Super House of Dead Ninjas" and "Pixel Shinobi" are both far more satisfying ninja action games.  The level design for this game, however, just feels low-effort.  As if the enemies were added to the levels more like an afterthought because they're expected to be there, rather than being the main appeal for the game's action.  Maybe it will get better later on in the game, one can only hope...
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent tough-as-nails platformer with an engaging story and plenty of amazing sprite work / music. Controls felt mostly tight, but I did have quite a bit of trouble getting the dash slash to work reliably in the middle of boss fights.  Though part of that was maybe my problem.Would love to see some updates in the future.Oh and if you're having a hard time choosing between this and the Messenger, they're different enough that you'd probably enjoy both.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is an amazing action platformer oozing style and solid game design. Much like Shovel Knight, it takes clear inspiration from the golden NES/SNES era while standing out on its own with satisfying gameplay and a surprisingly touching, if simple, story. Unlike Shovel Knight, however, Cyber Shadow is less afraid to reference and tribute the classics that inspired it; if you're a retro gamer, you'll find plenty of small references and tributes all around. The difficulty curve is a bit sharp, but smooth, and the plethora of tools at your disposal make seemingly overwhelming screens turn into challenging yet fair sections with many options as to how to face them. A very interesting checkpoint upgrade system makes wonders for the game's accessibility, and with little to no penalties for dying this game always steers clear from becoming frustrating. I highly recommend this game for everyone, specially fans of Shovel Knight and/or old school platformers. But if you like the original Ninja Gaiden games, this game is a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best retro games to come out in a very long time. Its Yacht Club Games so you already know they know what they're doing. The music deserves a special mention, I have not heard such great music in a retro game in a long time, I'd put it up there with Chrono Trigger, Batman for Sega CD, and Waterworld. Its a synthwave style soundtrack made with chiptune, many of the numbers are catchy enough I listen to them outside the game.The combat is fast and fun, you start out fairly weak and simplistic, by the end of the game you're bouncing off walls, double jumping, and cutting a path through enemies, they really pay off that fantasy of being a ninja, just stick with it. The aesthetic is perfect 80s style futurism. Took me back to the golden age of genesis games. If you like excellent retro music, pixel graphics, Ninjas, or 80s gaming nostalgia, you've found the perfect game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: It's almost great. Theres some really cool ideas and elements in the game, but they are inter-spaced between large amounts of less inspiring or outright frustrating content. Like for example, you encounter an enemy that feels like a Pong Paddle. It hovers there tracking your vertical or horizontal position. You kill it easily and move on with your life. Later, you encounter a laser enemy that fires a bullet, which will deflect when it hits this pong platform. Due to its position its usually above or to the side of you and causes the attack to be quite dangerous. Really interesting idea... shows up like twice, never spoken of again.Or the Swag Blade. A spinner weapon that will swing around you, get knocked away by your sword, and make use of your momentum. Easily the coolest platform game weapon I've ever seen. Encountered it like once or twice in ten hours, and instead get various lame guns.In between these cool elements there are endless mazes populated with a hell of a lot of instadeath spikes, or annoying enemies that suddenly fly on and can only be defeated by memorizing their locations. Overall, found it mostly between average and frustrating as opposed to enjoyable. If they implemented some of their ideas more I'd definitely give it a thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: If you plan on playing this game, duct-tape your controller to your hands before you do so. This game holds nothing back and has no shred of mercy for the easily discouraged.Spike hell, Bullet hell, These are merely words; The reality is much worse. The cheap deaths this game will throw at you will enrage even the most seasoned platforming veterans. That said, the controls are tight and responsive and the game, while unrelenting in wanting to turn you into a pile of ninja scrap, isn't unfair.10/10 would ninja throw my controller at a wall again.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: very goodi finished this ♥♥♥♥ two times and im gonna say that this game is good as hellobviously mostly i liked the music, every song in this game is a damn banger, i wish they would add it on spotifythis game isn't so hard and i finished it in under a five hours, would be better if there was a NG+ mode
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid action game. The art and animations are excellent and I get some serious Natsume vibes from the color choices and overall look of this game. One of the later stages in the game has a song that sounds like a callback to the stage one track from Shadow of the Ninja.The controls are pretty damn tight, moving and slashing all feels great, though I never got a feel for the parry move seeing as there's no real feedback if you're doing the input correctly other than you reflect the shot or eat some damage. The other upgrades are all fun, with the exception of the LV 2 sword, more range is good but I'm a little disappointed from the damage increase, seeing as it means enemies past that point have inflated HP pools to make it so you don't one-shot them, so nothing really changes other than going back to previous levels to clean house. HP inflation in general is a little aggravating seeing as enemies start doing progressively more damage to keep up with the player's HP going up, so again it's essentially unchanged from the start, you could go without the HP upgrades but then a stiff breeze would kill you in the later levels, this complaint is pretty petty honestly and a personal gripe.Most of the subweapons you can find are fantastic though, the swag blade is incredibly fun to play around with, though the charge blaster and the free aim cannon are a little underwhelming. I'm a little disappointed at the lack of extra content after 100%-ing the game with that big EXTRAS option on the title screen and nothing else other than the feats list, maybe the team has plans for more stuff in the future?My own gripes aside, I've enjoyed my time with Cyber Shadow and if you're looking for a tight and difficult ninja game to cut your teeth on, you've found it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks really good, but there are lot of weird design quirks and frustrating levels that just bring this down for me. For example, it's a game where getting hit knocks you back, which is fine on its own, but getting knocked back into spikes is an instant death (your i-frames don't save you like in Mega Man). Also, there are lots of long stretches with death pits, so again getting knocked back is an instant death. And the length between checkpoints gets obnoxious.So yeah, it's a hard game and normally I'd be able to power through and try to master the thing, but the way the game controls became so frustrating after a while that I had to put this down, and I'm not sure if I'm going to pick it up again. You eventually get a "run" button and from then on, the level design pretty much requires that you use the run->teleport slash attack. I'm going to try to explain why this is so frustrating: Once you start running, any slash you do becomes a teleport slash. This slash goes a set distance, but only if there's nothing in front of you. If there's an enemy in front of you, the game sometimes tries to move you more or less depending on the distance you started the teleport. I swear to god I tried to figure this out, but it just feels like I have no control over the distance I travel. Sometimes I don't go far enough and I just run into the enemy. Sometimes I hit the enemy which brings me TOO far and I fall to my death. Other times, I feel like I've got the perfect spacing and the presence of an enemy causes my overall dash to shorten by half and I fall to my death. I cannot figure it out. I swear they put sections that look like the PERFECT opportunity to use this ability and have the game flow really well, but as far as I can tell, if you do the intuitive teleport you just get spaced wrong and you die.Not to mention if there's a single pixel of collision wrong with the teleport you collide and your movement gets cut short. Sometimes your run gets cut off at the last second (by any pixel) and you do a normal slash and fall to your death. Sometimes you WANT to stop running and do a normal slash, but you have to let go of Forward to do this, so it's easy to mess up and just get a teleport by mistake.And all of this is happening while hopping around above instant death pits, hordes of tanky enemies, and long stretches between checkpoints with very little healing.It's also frustrating that every time you use an ability for any reason you drain special ability points. This is offset by an incredibly inexpensive SP recovery option that is available at most checkpoints.It's a strange dichotomy though, because a lot of the bosses can be destroyed in one rotation by parrying and throwing fireballs in their face. But this is only after you practice that opening a couple times getting destroyed without even scratching the boss. If this sounds like it's for you, then it's a pretty nice looking game, but in my opinion it lacks polish in the control and level design department.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is a good game. Not a great game, just a good game. It has a lot of ways that it inflates its difficulty that are really annoying, very Mega Man 1 style. But besides that gripe that really only affects the second half of the game, the art direction, music, etc., is absolutely phenomenal. I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: To answer the most important question first: Would i recommend this game without restrictions to my friends? No, I wouldn't. Play The Messenger instead.Let me explain why. The biggest enemy in this game is gonna be the controls itself. I am not quite sure what they were thinking when they designed the blocking mechanic (tapping the dpad once in the direction of the incoming projectile). If you design a game arount this, then it has to be reliable, and this mechanic is the opposite of that. Most of the time, you just end up running into the projectile by trying to block it, completely defeating the purpose. So you rather opt in to try dodging, since this actually works most of the time.The button layout itself is also not quite as good as it could be. Most buttons on the Gamepad aren't used at all. Throwing shurikens for example is bound on up+attack. Trying to do this while steering your way through tight platforming sections is impossible, since you cannot press 2 opposite directions on the dpad at the same time.The difficulty curve is quite steep, and you end up playing the same sections over and over and over again, since savepoints are as rare as health refills in the later stages.The story is meh, i didn't perceive it as very interesting yet it also isn't bad. I just didn't feel i build a connection with any character at all.The replayability is also not there for me. Rather than cheering for yourself for beating another stage after hours of trying, you end up just being relieved that it's finally over.There is a lot more to say, yet i try to keep it short and focused on the (for me) most important points.So IF you like difficult games, you have a high frustration tolerance and a GOOD controller (like a ds4), you can give it a try. If you just look for a fun platformer, with matured and responsive controls, try The Messenger instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: I was at first skeptical about buying this game. Lots of people  talking about how difficult it is and how it is just frustratingly tough. As someone who doesn't like difficult games, I was feeling this wasn't for me.However, the game is not really tough. I mean its hard, but every section can be beaten in 4-5 tries. Same for the bosses. Also the controls are fine. You get more abilities as the game progresses, once you are well versed with the basic abilities. Please don't quit it in the first 2 hours. The game gets really cool as you progress.Highly enjoyable game!
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game. Feels great to control; there's lots of enemy variety; love the music and graphics. The boss fights imo were definitely this game's greatest strength if you want to compare it to other games like The Messenger.The level design forces you to play very deliberately, and make the best use out of all your abilities. I found it very satisfying maybe 70% of the time, and the other 30% I'd consider ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enemy spam. I'm a bit of a masochist when it comes to these things so it didn't ruin the game for me, but I expect it will for others.The story is a cute, simplistic NES-style narrative. I enjoyed all the little cutscenes, although I think the lore tablets could've been done better, as most of them didn't contain very interesting information.The feat system is very cool, it gives a secondary way to fight each boss upon a second playthrough (like fighting the water boss without touching water).I like this game, and would recommend it to those interested, although I wouldn't recommend it to Shovel Knight fans who are expecting something remotely similar.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is a great game. At first playing it, it can be frustrating but it's all around pretty fun. I went for all feats and they weren't too bad with a little practice and patience. I personally think it has a lot of replay value. Though, there's no new game + I've had fun starting over and going through it multiple times doing 100% runs. Once you get it down, they don't even take that long. I am in no way a speed runner and I just did an 100% run in under 3 hours. Fun game to play over and over again. Pick it up and play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!Not understanding the negative reviews, rather confusing. Once you've obtained all the abilities (about half way in) the game starts to become much more fast paced, which to me is great! But it seems most players find this too challenging, and are complaining about the difficultly. Honestly, I feel the game is on the easy side, but whatever.I suppose once an Easy mode is added there will be less negative reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: The production value of Cyber Shadow is very high. Gorgeous pixel art, animation and design. The sound and music are also great. The only problem, and it's a potentially huge one, is the game play. As you can see from most other negative reviews, the trailer and press for the game (even if inadvertently) create the impression this will play similarly to classic NES games, especially the Ninja Gaiden series, but it does not. Though being a cyborg ninja you spend the first half of the game feeling very un-agile and amazingly, even though it would have been very useful to have the ability to duck, roll, or slide, you never get such abilities, even when several boss fight mechanics seemed to be copied from games where you did control an agile character who could slide.Here is a video review my friend and I made:
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Basically abuses the worst traits of the old days and tries to pass it off as a good idea. not a hard game but a exercise in intentional frustration. people still think this is a good idea so xXbaitmasterXx can talk about having beaten it while not mentioning or greatly downplaying how annoyed they were during it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is a nice addition from Yacht Club Games to the 8-bit platform new wave. They did a good job. The pixel art is great, levels feel progressively difficult, soundtrack is on point and the character abilities are interesting and develop through the game. I really like the Cyberpunk genre but the story here is nothing extraordinary. It's just fine and the characters are ok. Gameplay is good but I feel the controls are a bit janky at times. There are checkpoints through the levels but that doesn't diminish the frustration. So this is my main issue with this game. I found myself dying countless times just to move foward through certain level areas. If you don't have much patience you'll lose interest because it will break the progression and gameflow. Now, if you have patience it's a nice rewarding feeling once you beat it. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Every time this game showed up for me, be it a trailer or someone playing, I saw them dashing and killing enemies in awesome ways. The first hour of this game is absolutely none of that. It is a frustrating experience with absolutely brutal platforming sections that are super unforgiving. When comparing it to other platformer games, this one is just unnecessarily outdated.This game reminded me a lot of The Messenger. That game had engaging platforming mechanics from the very start, and while enemy variety was lacking, all enemies made the levels feel like you had so many approaches to beating it.Cyber Shadow, however, has the player move in an incredibly slow paced manner in tight platforms with a myriad of objects that can damage the player from all angles. While the checkpoints were forgiving, having to do the same section over and over again felt like they were miles away. It becomes an anxiety simulator, with every death having me question if my meds are actually working as I juggle between throwing my controller out of my window or at the screen of my PC.With a limited amount of time in my hands, I can only play so much of one game and feel like I accomplished so little. If you have a lot of time and patience for this game, give it a try. The soundtrack sounded really good, and the pixelart is also on point with the theme.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Side scrolling action that starts fun but simple before giving you double and wall jumps, parry, a downward strike to bounce off enemies, sprints with a lunging invulnerable slash all leading to more interesting movement. Boss fights are varied in style with good looking enemies, though are pretty easy to beat (even when going for each of their achievement challenges). Good art though not that unique as the future dystopia setting and level backgrounds is fairly common, great soundtrack. There are more hidden pickups that will increase your health or SP for your special attacks but your health mostly increases automatically from beating mid level bosses so you aren't overly punished for not finding every hidden thing like you would be in most games that do that. The only more difficult parts tend to come from some of the SP increasing items you need to backtrack for.The game controls well but the sprint attack is likely going to be fairly unwieldy outside of the better players, but the game doesn't overly force the move onto you as you can almost always get through sections without it. It tends to be pretty easy outside of knockback pushing you into instant kill pits and those deaths can always be annoying but they start to get mitigated quite a bit once you gain the option to double jump and can angle yourself out of some of them. Even as someone saying the game is easy, I am not good at using the sprint attack at all. The pickups for currency to power the save machines for additional functions is just pointless as I never came close to running out and even if you did you could just grind them doing nothing for the game but adding a potential layer of tedium.Very solid game, complaints don't really amount to much, though all the skills are rarely used together to create more interesting stage design (probably not helped by giving some of the abilities so far into the game). Not at the level of excellence that I would find the Shovel Knight games but still an easy recommendation.First playthrough with 100% item collection and all but four achievements, took about 4 hours and 20 minutes with 66 deaths (with a good number of them being from trying to beat a boss without touching water and trying not to get hit on the motorcycle section).Screenshots:
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Every cool thing this game does feels like an accident. It has perhaps the worst first two levels conceivable in an action-platformer. After those, the game gets progressively more tolerable, but it consistently feels like a worse version of The Messenger. Just play that instead.It's a bummer too. I was looking forward to this game because Shovel Knight is on my all-time GOAT list, and I was hoping for Yacht Club publishing to be a little better. Oh well.

_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: I really dont get what all the fuss is about with this game. It starts of kinda meh, the intro levels are all fun but the story is lackluster at best until the later chapters. And when you reach the later chapters the difficulty ramps up to a point where it becomes a slug fest. Maybe im just not the type for this game, but dying 40+ times to get from checkpoint to checkpoint because I "havent found the flow of the level" where it all makes perfect sense yet is a terrible excuse for lackluster game design. I really wanted to like this game, coming from the messenger i was hoping for another great and fun platformer, but for me this misses the mark completly, it's way too intense for my casual skills and i dont see the point in frustrating myself for an hour until i give up every day after work. _childDocuments_.review: Fun game, good visuals, but ♥♥♥♥ all moths, bats, and bat adjacent thingsKilling things is fun, boss fights are fun, platforming controls well but the levels are designed like absolute garbage. I'm running into way too many situations where the game mechanics doesn't support the level design (ie. stuck in a vertical corridor with spikes underneath with an enemy coming down from above, and no means of attacking up while in the air), platforming where the next landing is hit by constant pink flames, narrow horizontal sword swings where the stupid moths fly in anything other than in front,Too many stupid instadeaths because of dumb bat-adjacent things-- it's like the designer/playtester took all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ spots where the character happens to drop and places dumb spikes RIGHT in that location, completely unrelated to the platforming itself. Also, there's a bunch of ledges guarded by these laser spear things that just stunlock you to death? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid. The boss fights take like 2-3 tries, the vast majority of the deaths are from the spikes.Also, what's with the stupid cyber core boss, with the last phase having constant bullets shooting out of it and spikes underneath? I just got stuck countering 50 of them, if I jump I get hit or knocked to the spikes. What a dumb sequence.♥♥♥♥ bats, and ♥♥♥♥ spikes. What a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ relic of old school gaming that should've stayed dead, without any real modern day qol improvements. Just because you force a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of deaths doesn't make it good, old school difficulty. Maybe sometimes it's just ♥♥♥♥♥♥ design.===edit: Stepped away, took a nap, came back and beat the game. After slogging through levels 7-8 or so, the platforming is a lot more doable and even fun near the end. Having the endgame moveset helps with the platforming a whole bunch (especially with recovery), even though dealing with enemies directly above you while midair is still a pain, and facing some annoying death situations (getting hit/shot by enemies offscreen, recovery jumping into a floating enemy for repeated damage). Maybe the early game is just a pain in the ass? I still think that the moth sacs early on are the most frustrating/hardest enemies in the game, bar none. (Then again, getting max health near the end probably helped a bunch too)Similar to other reviews, I also wished that you could somehow toggle the use of essence with your special moves? I end up spending all my essence with recovery dairs (when the extra damage isn't really necessary) and being unable to use any ranged attacks where it would've definitely helped. Think I spent most of the playthrough with zero essence.The parry mechanic helped make getting around enemies a lot more doable/fun. A lot of the issues with low essence/ranged options and annoying AI (flying drones always staying just out of sword reach) were mitigated through liberal use of the parry-- which works on most if not all forms of enemy attacks.Random notes on boss fights:- Cyberspace boss I mentioned earlier: jump over the boss and the endless stream, hit it in the back a few times, rinse and repeat. - For the floating skull with the surrounding orbs, you can clear out the orbs guarding the platforms by either parrying their electric fields and killing them, or killing them with magic- downward stab works well due to the aoe. Somehow I thought that the electric orb things were invincible and you had to fight around them.- After the first phase of the last boss, attack the corpse for health drops-- you can save the health drops until you need it

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow ReviewMy disappointment is immeasurable, and my day is ruined. Okay, maybe not that bad, however so far, I am disappointed in this game. The standard jump and slash feel like you don’t have many options mainly because you can’t attack upwards or crouch to attack below which makes small enemies a pain to deal with. Also, it feels restrictive but that’s okay as long as the game is still fun. However, the fun factor gets taken down heavily by these annoying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ flies that get in the way and getting pushed into instant death spikes/pits. My problem is that when I get stuck in one spot and I die (which happens quickly because of insta death traps) I have to do parts of the game over again which after two or three times doesn’t make me feel like a master but instead grinds the gameplay to a halt and I have to do stuff I already know how to get by easily over and over again without any purpose. I will play more because I believe that the parry and dash will make the game much better but so far, I think the game suffers from expectations that were set too high by having to live up to being “the next Shovel Knight” and presenting gameplay in the trailer that you will only get to experience once you get through the slog that have been my 2 hours with the game so far. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start this off by saying that I love Yacht Club Games, but jeez this is what it must have felt like to wait for Cyberpunk only for it to come out and not be good.  I'm at the last level of the game and, sadly, I won't finish this. It's beyond me what kind of level designer made the game. I've been killed more than 100 times by things that are above me/ below me and I can't see.You know, "The Messenger" had a great feature where you can recover from being hit with the press of a button. If only this game had that.Pros:- Pixel Art is great. "Cutscenes" have a great look to them. Really enjoyed them visually.- The Dash ability, when it works, is a lot of fun.- Most boss battles are really fun.Cons: - Levels are too long for a single track to loop over and over. Levels being too long is not a con, the single 2-3 minute loop is.- Abilities legit don't work sometimes. I can't tell you how many times I've died due to the dash ability just deciding to not let me dash more than once.- The enemy placement is made just so the game can be hard. There is a distinction between smartly placed enemies which have interesting patterns that you have to learn, and just placing 4 flying bots which fly from every direction of the screen and follow you while you're trying to pixel perfect jump gaps, avoid the flying bots, and trying to parry other flying bots which shoot.- The "get hit 3 times and you lose your ability" is a miss for me.- The above point is a miss for me because you can get hit, have no invincibility frames, get hit again, from the same enemy, just as you recover and then get pushed off of the platform.Here's a real example:There is a mechanic in the game where if you go through a certain point in a level, you will get chased by a wall of flesh (that's what it looks like to me). That's cool, okay. You have to use what you've learned to get away as fast as you can. The problem is, at one point, you're being chased while climbing a wall, you get to the top of the wall and there's always an enemy that has a move pattern that always meets you on the ledge and his attacks cannot be parried because he's shooting straight lasers not bullets or pellets or whatever. And even if you get hit a single time, even if you touch him, you're sent flying back down and you're likely to get killed by the wall of flesh.- The last stretch of the game is devoid of checkpoints.The biggest gripe I have with this game is the enemy placement. They are placed the way they are placed just so it can be a hard game. There's nothing smart about it. But ,hey, maybe it's just me. I dunno.4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Shocked by how great this is.  As the "Ninja Gaiden" breed of indie platformers goes, this is probably the best one I've played.  Controls are air-tight, level design is superb, combat is as simple and satisfying as you'd hope for.  It's also got a really high skill ceiling.  The abilities at your disposal are a lot of fun to use, but they really require skill.  Once you master all of the abilities, it practically becomes a whole different game as you start employing more high-risk-high-reward maneuvers, and the game always makes sure to reward you for playing this way.  I also appreciate this for resisting the temptation to be meta.  I don't have a problem with games being self aware and having some meta humor and 4th wall breaks, but it also feels like every indie game of this type does that now, so it's refreshing to play a game and have it just tell its story.  I don't really have many complaints.  Difficulty borders on cruel at times, and the checkpoints are all placed pretty far from one another.  This does make for a few sections which are more frustrating than fun.  But most of the time, this is an absolute joy to play, and I can't recommend it enough.  It almost completely flew under my radar, and I'm so glad I discovered it.

_childDocuments_.review: ***SPOILERS AHEAD*** This game is frustratingly annoying. Enemies often shoot projectiles so fast that you get caught in a corner and then you're dead. It wants you to go fast but if you do and miss a jump or land in the wrong spot, there are so many enemies or spikes or electrified floors that you will die. There are so many traps to fall in that you cannot get out of, you just die. It seems that for any given situation they have an intended mechanic you are supposed to use or you will simply not get through the area. Health is very scarce, the game starts off giving you more health after you defeat a boss and then it just stops that, some boss fights give you nothing, and it is made worse by the fact that every hit from an enemy takes 2 HP, sometimes more depending on the enemy. They give you a dash late in the game that does allow you to dash in the air but only if you were running on the ground first. This leads to a lot of mistakes in platforming which usually leads to a bottomless pit or insta-kill spikes or being trapped and just having your HP get depleted. The air dash is also an attack but sometimes does not hit the enemy at all and the i-frames from getting hit are non-existent. I air dashed through an enemy and landed on the same very small platform that it was on but its hit box was on its head, which I couldn't hit from the platform, but its tail was on the only spot I could stand on. If I stayed there I kept taking damage from the tail, if I jumped there was another enemy out of reach shooting loads of projectiles that will hit me mid-air causing me to fall in electrified water that I couldn't jump out of because another projectile would hit me causing me to fall back in the electrified water. There is even a motorcycle stage that has enemies floating above you so you can't jump and then enemies coming from behind you and you can't shoot backwards. In this case if you didn't manage to kill the enemies above you before the enemies behind you show up you have no choice but to take damage and when you only have 10 HP and each hit takes at least 2 with no i-frames in between, your HP goes down very fast. Once I unlocked all the abilities and got them buffed I wanted to go back to previous stages to see if I could get more health. However, you are only able to go back via a certain terminal that does not show up again for a very long time. Not to mention stage hazards, like spikes, that only pop out when you are close enough to them and sometimes are hidden in the background by something in the foreground. It was really frustrating getting hit by something that I couldn't see. The game does have a fun aspect to it but it is constantly undermined by the horrible stage design, enemy placement and enemies constantly shooting you without pause. The parry system is a joke. You have to move toward the projectile at the right time and then press attack to fire the parry back at the enemy. This should have been assigned to one of the many buttons that are not used and the projectile should fire back immediately. Even with parrying being what it is, it only stops one projectile. If an enemy shoots you at an angle, you can parry the attack but it will not hit them as the parry only moves either left or right depending on how you're facing it. Combine this with the huge amount of projectiles on screen plus the enemies that come straight at you and you can get stuck in a situation where all you can do is parry but not hit anything and you can't move because the enemies never stop shooting. The checkpoints are also pretty far apart in late game so going through a very difficult part just to get to another difficult part only to find yet another frustratingly difficult part with no checkpoints in between makes you just want to play something else. A lot of abilities only work if you have SP and are very weak so even when you do have SP the abilities are not much help and some checkpoints do not refill it. Overall the game has a cool concept but is executed very poorly and relies on your memory of the stage in order for you to proceed. Which means you will die a lot before getting to the next area where you will also die a lot until you remember the stage and this only gets worse as the game goes on. I like challenging games but the challenge needs to be fun, not frustrating, and often times the game feels like you fail because the game is programmed for you to fail. Which wasn't OK when the games were made to eat your quarters and it isn't OK now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gives me all the awesome feels of an old Ninja Gaiden game with a sweet mix of Metroid! It brings back the feelings I had as a child sitting in the floor with a controller in my hands and bowl of Fruity Pebbles at my side ready to get my game on! This retro-styled action platformer developed by Mechanical Head Studios and published by Shovel Knight developer Yacht Club Game is a truly rad kick in the face take on the 2D Ninja Gaiden formula! I could have left it with that but it gets even better because it constantly changes and bodaciously adds new gameplay and level design challenges with every new upgrade that it gives you! It goes from a simple yet fun action platformer to an absolutely brutally difficult one that surpasses its inspiration in every way. The pixel graphics are beautiful and fits to the "cybernetic" theme very well and the story which is told through both in-game dialogue boxes and nostalgic 8-bit cutscenes with large, detailed, but still very low-res sprites, much like the NES days just drove it home even more! The game has a ton of nostalgic personality which throws you back into those glorious 80's gaming days. Another sector where the game hypes it up even more is the gameplay! It really hits on all fronts: level design, enemy design, music, enemy variety, character progression, boss battles – it’s all top notch! I highly recommend purchasing this masterpiece and playing it until you beat it because the game is well worth your full attention!

_childDocuments_.review: No. Just no.If your attention was grabbed by the YACHT GAMES (same people from the fantastic Shovel Knight), then lemme tell you that this game IS NOT from Yacht Games. This time they acted as a publisher, not as developers.But that's not the real issue (I mean... It was, at parts. Because you may expect a game as good as Shovel Knight).The issue is that this is just another "Not Ninja Gaiden" game.At first I thought that it was a Metroidvania, but it also is not. You CAN backtrack after you get some upgrades, but the things you get are extra HP and SP. The important upgrades you get simply by playing the game. It's linear.More or less like the Mega Man X series.The game starts off very easy, letting you get a feel of the controls and mechanics, which is nice. Also when you get a new upgrade, the stages are designed in way where you have to use that new upgrade. That's good game design.Bosses fights are also interesting and can be challenging.You have infinite lives, when you die (quite a lot) you restart very fast and there are a fair amount of save/checkpoints. So, with so many positive things, and things done right, why wouldn't I recommend the game?For starters, there's nothing that stands out, really. It's just a Ninja Gaiden'esque done well, with nothing else to offer.It's kinda.... Generic.Also, as the game progresses the difficulty increases in an annoying, almost unfair way. You know, those cheap deaths where enemies are positioned so you can get hit and fall on an insta-death spikes.(yeah, insta-death spikes are everywhere on later stages!)To make matters worse, the stages get bigger and checkpoints more spaced.Then you find yourself in a position where "Is it difficult? Yes. Can I git gud and best that stage? Yes! But.. DO I WANT to git gud and keep playing? Hhmm.... Maybe... No?"That's my overall feeling. Other than the feeling of "I've beaten the game" there's nothing making me want to keep playing.If you want a better Ninja Gaiden clone, The Messenger is definitely a better game.If you already have played and beaten The Messenger and are craving for more Ninja Gaiden clone... Sure, go for it. It's not a bad game. And if you are a skilled player, you may even beat it in a couple of hours (there's an achievement for under 3h) and have a little fun.Just a little. Don't expect too much.

Like threading a needle during an earthquake.🎵 Soundtrack: Imagine a chiptune DJ battling a boss on a turntable. The beats hit harder than a shuriken to the face.🤖 Enemies: Malfunctioning robots with more attitude than a rebellious Roomba. And those toaster bots? They’re toastier than a fresh bagel.🌆 Story: Our silent ninja wakes up, squints at the neon city, and mutters, “Guess I’ll save the world. But first, let me sharpen my kunai.”🎨 Graphics: Pixel art so sharp, it could slice through code bugs. And our ninja’s pixelated butt? It’s surprisingly aerodynamic.🕹️ Overall: Grab your katana, channel your inner ninja, and dance through cybernetic chaos. Bonus points if you stealth-kill enemies to the rhythm.Remember, if you die, blame it on lag, blame it on the respawn timer, or blame it on that one glitchy pixel that distracted you. Keep slicing, dicing, and pixel-parkouring!

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, I won't be finishing this game and here's why.-There's just too much I don't like about how certain combat techniques work.1) Parrying SUCKS in Cyber Shadow big time! Why the F do you want me to press two effin  buttons to parry bullets? It does not work 50% of time and just infuriating. Who thought this was a great idea? Well, he should be fired. In Capcom's Strider you can parry bullets by just hitting them with the sword but no, apparently for Cyber Shadow devs that's too damn convenient and cool, so they much rather complicate things and make them worse. Well F this.2) Wall jumps SUCK especially in sections where you need to wall jump, not get hit by one-hit kill spikes and kill flying enemies at the same time. Plus wall jumps just flat out don't work sometimes and I can't tell you how many times I died cuz of this effin BS.3) Why do I need to press 2 buttons to use special abilities etc.? There's 4 effin additional buttons (R1-2, L1-2) on my controller, why can't I use them? For the love of god, WHY?!-I don't like enemy placement in later stages at all. To say it is bad, horrible, terrible etc. is to say nothing. They are deliberately placed that way just to infuriate you and create false sense of challenge. Challenge should be fair and fun at the same time, but it's not about Cyber Shadow, not even close.-Too effin many one-hit kill spikes everywhere like in Super Meat Boy. WTF? Not to mention electric floors and platforms in later stages, 99% of which you can't avoid without getting hit and you can't stop it from happening cuz turrets that shoot electric bolts are on the top or the bottom of the room so you can't destroy them. There's just overall too much stuff on the screen and too much stuff you need to handle at any given time in later stages. It's just not fun whatsoever.-Why can't I crouch? WHY?! Have you ever played games like this on NES/SNES etc.? It's just absolutely buffeling to me.-Why can't I recover from enemy hits? Or better question yet, who thought that adding Castlevania / Ninja Gaiden level knock back after enemy hits will make the game better? Whoever it was, he should be fired.-Very few checkpoints in later stages which forces you to replay frustrating parts over and over and over and over and over and over and over again if you can't play absolutely perfectly and nail everything with 1000% accuracy.-Who's idea was it to take sub weapons away from you after 3 hits? WHO? Again, have you ever played games like this on NES/SNES etc.? Even effin Castlevania and Ninja Gaiden games do not allow themselves to be so cruel and punishing, and they are not easy games by any means btw, Ninja Gaiden games especially.I like some parts of this game - story, pixel art, some of the level designs and music is great, but there's also so many parts of this game I don't like at all and this ultimately kills it for me. _childDocuments_.review: Steam doesn't allow for a "Meh" category, so thumbs down is what I would lean more toward. _childDocuments_.review: Unlike some crybabies complaining this game is too hard for their weak minded personalities, Cyber Shadow has everything an 80s platformer had in the golden decade of Nintendo NES. Obviously, this game was made with old players like me in mind. Platformers were extremely popular and the NES had an impressive selection of fantastic titles. Even the most obscure Nintendo platformers were fun and challenging to play. Cyber Shadow has done some research, and it shows. From the futuristic aesthetics inspired by some of the coolest NES titles (Ninja Gaiden, Batman, Power Blade, Metal Storm, Street Fighter 2010 among others) to playing with one of the most popular characters from the decade: a Ninja! a cyborg ninja! against a bunch of his own kind. The soundtrack is pretty accurate for the time it wants to take you back.Playability is great, don't believe idiots that can't play with "How to" tutorials. The difficulty level may seem hard but, like most of the old games this one wants to pay homage, platformers are all about patterns, and once you get them, you'll discover it isn't an impossible to beat game. Controls work perfect. I play it with my beloved Xbox controller and so far, and as long as you know what you're doing, the controls are  responsive. HOWEVER, the dash feature doesn't work all the time and believe you me, it's necessary for certain areas. Also, when reflecting projectiles, especially when there are mini bosses at a distance, it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pain in the ass to get it to work. These two details may be extremely frustrating at specific areas. I doubt they will ever be fixed since the game was made by one person only.What are you wating for? go buy this game now!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Cyber Shadow is a game that tries to recreate the magic of old-school tough-as-nails platformers like Ninja Gaiden, but fails because it also carries over all the frustrating aspects of those games without trying to modernize them. If you're looking for a platformer that captures that magic without being annoying, I would recommend Shovel Knight, or The Messenger, if you want to scratch that Ninja platformer itch.I was really excited for Cyber Shadow because Yacht Club Games was publishing it but it turned out to be a big disappointment in a lot of aspects, to the point where I quit halfway through(after Stage 4).The game gets noticeably more difficult after Stage 1, however not in a fun, challenging way, but a frustrating one: Checkpoints and health pickups are very rare, so you often find yourself replaying the segments, which gets more and more annoying over time because the levels themselves are very long and there's not much variety within levels, so playing through them starts to feel like a slog. I would've preferred it if there were more but shorter levels with more variety instead.The trailers promised fast-paced ninja action but the actual gameplay is very bland, slow and clunky and is coupled with frustrating enemy design. At the beginning you're restricted to only jumping and slashing, crouching is not possible, so small opponents are really difficult to hit. Basic techniques like upwards-slashing or a downwards-stab attack have to be unlocked later down the line. Most enemies use long-range attacks, while you're restricted to close combat, so you often find yourself bombarded by projectiles, unable to retaliate. The option to deflect projectiles is only added halfway through the game, after Stage 4. In addition to that, a lot of enemies are very annoying to deal with, most notably the flies in Stage 2, who chase you and are very hard to hit because of their size.I might consider resuming my playthrough if they update the game to fix some of these annoyances, for example through re-balancing or an Easy Mode.

_childDocuments_.review: this game could have been another phenomenon like the messenger. instead it's modern spiritual successor of ninja gaiden. if you think that is a good thing, then 1) you've lost your mind and 2) good for you, you can stop reading now... you will like this game. i would give 'neutral' score if i could and the only reason i can't recommend the game is its price, which i don't think is justified. first of all: graphics are top, music is great, controls are tight. however, the difficulty is quite high and for 20 euros/dollars i would expect at least something as basic as three difficulty levels. you won't get that. you won't get other game modes either. there's no new game+, no dlc... nothing. besides that it's fair to say cyber shadow is remarkable piece of art. but certainly not for everyone, even if you like platformers. the fact boss fights feel like you've finally got some time to rest says a lot about the level design. be prepared for: tons of death pits, plethora of enemies shooting from all directions and kicking you down from platforms into said death pits, demanding sequences you are expected to execute almost flawlessly with no or very little room for mistakes. even though you have unlimited amount of lives, the progress can be pretty slow at times. every upgrade serves only as an excuse to ramp up the difficulty and throw you into another hellish nightmare level. you will never feel overpowered and when you get the "overpowered" uprade, you can only laugh at such a bad joke. the fact the character is barely up to the task the whole time might make sense as a part of the story, but from the gameplay perspective it's not much fun. so, all in all, if you're looking for a challenge, buy cyber shadow on sale. but if you're not super-fast-twitch-reactions-i-drink-a-lot-of-energy-drinks-hardcore-gamer™ then well... maybe look for something else.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an unfortunate one as it makes you wonder if the publisher's previously well-received efforts where less planned and more happy luck. The levels themselves feel less inspired by their obvious 8-bit influences and more direct clones, happily wearing all the warts brought along with them.The difficulty is moderate, but feels less like "I was punished for making a mistake" and more "I hit bad RNG," which feels awful and makes paying through the game a chore. In the same way some NES games would it gives you a feeling like you should be able to go fast but is crushingly punishing if you do instead requiring laboring efforts to ensure you are on just the right cycle, just the right frame rules. Many large enemies take several hits with a cooldown between them to defeat, making it more advantageous to stand waiting for an opening to avoid them than to fight. The levels themselves aren't fun, with enemy placement feeling just "off" in a indescribable way. Many enemies due to the lack of a means to attack directionally other than using a singular downward-thrust that requires depleting your skill points to use even though you don't need (or honestly, want) the "empowered" version of it take most if not all of your too-limited pool of skill charges making the already spartan combat feel even more hamstrung. The powers, for as few charges as you have, feel too weak to be satisfying to use, and instead become largely ignorable to just directly attacking with your standard sword swipe.Exploration feels punished instead of encouraged. In a game like this, finding a quicker or hidden path should feel rewarding, but instead feels largely like like the developer intended it as the singular "correct" path but left too few clues to lead to it. One area in the 4th stage comes immediately to mind, where a path was hidden-yet-obvious leading to a challenge for a new skill. Finding this could have felt rewarding and been a interesting bonus; instead the clue leading to it was just out-of-the-way enough to not be worth grabbing until already leaving on your way out after completing the area, and you then discover the skill is a required one to proceed. What could have been a interesting off shoot offering a interesting reward instead feels like the game is robbing you.The bones for a good game are here, but it feels too much like a cheep Unity cash grab rather than a pleasant modern rework of a ancient idea. Unlike Shovel Knight, which felt largely reminiscent of older games "done right" for a modern age, this game instead reminds you of other games like the Messanger, which appeared to be going for the same goal and attempting to hit the same notes but where far more successful at reaching it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those "retro" games that misses the point. Most of them understand that the idea is to take old school gameplay and ideas, and marry them with modern concepts, and give us what was promised on the box in those old games rather than what was limited by engines and technology.Cyber Shadow, on the other hand, acts like an arcade machine, like someone gets another quarter every time you eat dirt. Which is a shame, because it sounds and looks absolutely amazing, but when just about every screen has some instant kill spikes or instant kill pits, and enemies(which come from all angles, while you only have a scalpel-precise flat attack forwards or backwards) throw you about half a screen on contact, then just restart me at the edge of the screen or the edge of the pit when I hit them, with a health penalty, don't throw me back two screens to a save point and waste my time.It feels weird that this is a game published by Yacht Club when Shovel Knight was a generally pretty perfect understanding of what we *didn't* want to keep from the old games and only really had one area throughout the whole game where I was swearing about the dearth of save points.Plus it also looks like this game expects me to backtrack and revisit old areas with upgrades? At least that's what I assume from these unopenable boxes and doors? I believe my response to that is "lol. lmao even." You'd have to bribe me to go *forwards* through one of Cyber Shadow's levels, with the badly dated level design, going backwards through one of them or redoing them for extra bonuses is a hard sell.

_childDocuments_.review: Light game play SpoilersI will re-review this when I complete the game, but currently on level 7 out of 10. I have gotten all the upgrades, which started out pretty cool but have gotten pretty meh. This is game is overall a nice game, and is so sooooo close to being really really great. But it's not. It is riddled with so many choices that I leave me baffled wondering if the devs even played their own game, or any other modern retro throwback, cause they seem to have an idea of what they want but no idea how to execute it.First off weird control design. There is no duck/crouch, something even the original Ninja Gaiden had. It has only a horizontal basic attack. No swinging sword up or doing and cool aerial up down sword swipes. There are only two action buttons (technically three). Now you do unlock extra attacks. All of these new attacks are gotten by pressing a direction while attacking. Up and attack is shuriken, down and attack on ground is upward flame attack, down and attack in air is a drop attack. This is an incredibly dumb decision. Now there is a reason it's like this. Because they are trying to push the boundaries of "two button" gaming. But why? Because the original Ninja Gaiden only had to buttons? Because old 8-bit games in general only had two buttons? Why limit the mechanics to two buttons and not other things. This game obviously couldn't run on any actual 8-bit hardware, so why this specific limitation. It doesn't add anything to the game that's for sure. But it DOES take away.  Having to use D pad for extra inputs while already using it for movement is something Ninja Gaiden did because it had to. This makes moving while doing quite clunky. Sure you can get used to it but it always retains a bit of annoyance, and having separate buttons for this would be objectively better for the game feel.The special moves have other issues as well. There is a mana bar needed to do special moves. But some special moves you have to be able to do, like the drop attack and dash attack. So these moves are still possible with no mana, just now as powerful. The problem is, what if I need drop attack to destroy something to progress but I don't want to use mana. I know it's possible to use it without mana when it runs out, but I can't use the mana-less version when I'm just destroying blocks to save it for something actually useful? Nope that is not an option. This also applies to the dash attack. Speaking of which dashing is problematic as well. Remember how there's only two buttons? Nope there's a third, which is entirely dedicated to sprinting. There is another way, by double tapping a direction, so why include other button as well. The devs probably realized how clunky it was (and that it interfered with the parry mechanic when you're doing many parry's in a row). But if they gave us an extra button for this why not for our other abilities? Even still there is more clunkiness. You have to start moving before you can push the sprint version. If you press it then move, nothing will happen. If you are already running, you cannot stop by letting go of said sprint button, or by pushing it again, you have to stop moving. This makes trying to speed run through an area by sprinting very clunky. Every time you get to a new "level" there is not a save to start of, only at end of last, So if you die before you get to the next one, rather than respawn at start of new area, you start at end of last, which sometimes is one screen away, but not always. Each level also has a teleporter at the end of the level which I simply don't see the purpose of. Why not just let me fast travel between saves? Most stages have some secrets (though they are never exciting and feel mostly feel like a waste).In spite of all of this.. if you are a fan of the original Ninja Gaiden games I have to recommend this to you. I like Ninja Gaiden quite a bit, and this IS better. Any one of the issues on their own would just be s nitpick, it's just that there are so many issues that are in the core game play mechanics so they are prevalent throughout the entire play through. If you're a big retro fan but not so much of Ninja Gaiden specifically, I'd recommend looking elsewhere. I will edit this review to add the positives and praise what the game does good when I finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: [Introduction]When I got this, I expected something in the same vein as Shadow Of The Ninja and Ninja Gaiden, what I got however.. was... very different.[Graphics]Definitely amazing stuff, the cutscenes, the environments, the animations are all just top notch. The art in this game is incredible to say the least.[Sound]Really good tracks that make you feel like you're definitely playing a ninja game. They're driving, energetic when required,  and tranquil and serene in other places. Beautiful range and composition. Sound effects are crisp as hell.[Gameplay]This is where the game really falls apart. Because unfortunately the dev clearly made a conscious choice to make this game hard as diamond. And not in the good way either. No, they chose to emulate the absolutely worst parts of NES era difficulty which are still joked about today. Now, difficulty in these kinds of games usually just boils down to two things: Muscle memory and pattern memorization. You repeat the level over and over until you figure out the bosses pattern or where the enemies are located and when they shoot, what their timing is etc.And you've all the bad parts of NES era difficulty things represented here. Instadeath spikes put into places where you land? check, enemies positioned so they can hit you easily but you can't hit them easily because of your limited movement? Yep. Bosses that do ridiculous damage and kill you in three hits? Oh yes, we've got those too. And don't forget enemies outside of your screen that you only see when you run into them. But again, if you've played NES, you can just use the above tactic of repetition to figure it out. Unfortunately, this is not a NES era game, because the controls are very poorly designed. Inputs are ignored about 10% of the time and trying to invoke some of the powers usually ends up with you getting killed instead. The parry system is even worse because there, even if you have perfect timing, half the time your parry doesn't connect and you get hit. And again, you don't want to get hit because three hits means you're dead. Then you have the dodge system which is even worse because it requires you to have a running start which .. drumroll, is ignored approximately 10% of the time. So instead of doing a running start to dash over to the other side of a chasm, you jump right into the chasm. If you combine all of this together with enemies that are ridiculously aggressive, take many hits to kill, dish out lots of damage, you can see how it's frustrating. But, there's also the fact that the game has save points which are spaced so far between that the levels become gigantic chores to beat as a result.I gave up on the game after I got the dodge mechanic because it reminded me of another game called Hyper Light Drifter where the dodge mechanic just works so damn well. And while I was trying to get through an annoying sequence that required pixel perfect jumping and parrying, I actually found myself daydreaming about the other game instead. So yeah, when a game annoys me to the point where I start daydreaming about replaying other games, that's when I throw in the towel.[Story/World]The reason I didn't throw in the towel after the first few levels was honestly the story. It's engaging and develops fairly well throughout the game. The game world itself is beautiful and really paints a great picture of the kind of world you're in now versus how it used to be. The characters are really interesting and your own motivations are a good point as well.But again, keep in mind that I haven't seen the ending yet, I'll look that up online later, which irks me to no end. [Summary]This is a game that has amazing art and music and story, but even though they're all stellar, they can't fix the gameplay which is incredibly tedious and frustratingly hard, in the worst kind of way.

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of a shame, that the Game isn't more popular. Someone compared it with "The Messenger" and that this took away the popularity. But the Games couldn't be more different. So the level design is made that you can mostly do it with your regular moveset, that doesn't use up your SP.In the Messenger, the leveldesign changes with the Powers you get and it turns into a Precision Platformer like Celeste.So for the people who seek a more classic NES/Sega Genesis (Mega Drive) type of Ninja Game, then this is the right one.It is difficult and some checkpoints are pretty far from each other, but it's still fair. _childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this is a good game and I played to the end of it for a reason. But unfortunately there was a deal breaker for me despite everything else.Pros:-Overall artwork and music were great, I enjoy both pixel and platforming games and it did not disappoint-Item synthesis, I liked all of the item synthesis options in both function and creativity, even the simpler ones-Progression, they did a good job keeping the game interesting but not overwhelming in both story and player strengthCons:-Skill mechanics, while I love how most of the skills worked, they would sometimes act a bit buggy and off even after I learned them, this may just be on my end but I felt that the parry and airstrike in particular just didn't work properly at times-Increased difficulty in the wrong way, couple reasons for this, for one having the enemies simply do more damage as the game progresses isn't very enjoyable, I'd much rather them be harder to dodge and the player being more likely to lose their item synthesis as a result. The second reason ties back to skill mechanics where a lot of the times that I died it felt like it was due to a skill malfunction instead of the enemies themselves. I want to die to an enemy and slowly learn how they work in order to defeat them, not wondering if my parry will work the way I want it to this time.Overall, I think I had too high of hopes for this game due to it being published by Yacht Club games, which is a bit unfair. It's a good and enjoyable game if you can look past the sometimes malfunctioning mechanics, but don't compare it to Shovel Knight or you will likely be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I made it further than I thought I would in this game, but frankly it is too hard (look, I suck at platformers, I get it).  Sadly I am unable to request a refund because out of pure stubbornness I played past the two hour mark.  The developers did a good job on this game, there are a few things they could do to maybe allow folks with less prowess at video games complete this game so I thought I'd at least give them kudos for what they did right and feedback on what didn't work for me.This game at release does not have an adjustable difficulty.  I was drawn in by the cyberpunk story and the graphics are quite nice, the audio has some surprisingly good tunes too - there are moments of silence, allowing quiet contemplation and reflection on the story, which is a wonderful touch and done right.  But after many, many deaths and some flow issues with the gameplay this game is just not there for me.Why is this game too hard for me?  Well - this game is a lot like the original Ninja Gaiden for the NES.  Instant death drops + lots of knock back when hit = falling into pits.  There is a serious lack of ranged weapons, and those there (a throwing star that costs one energy on a meter that had 7 points on it where I stopped) have an expensive cost to them with no guaranteed enemy drops of the ammo type.  The power ups are mods of sorts that give you shields (with a projectile), charge guns, a cool gravity glaive-like thing... they are nice but they break after you have been hit three times.The level that killed me - that made me give up.  The level right after the reactor.  No. Just no more.  Getting knocked around by numerous enemies that have projectiles while the level is literally growing behind me to kill me AND instant death things AND not enough health... Why?  What purpose does this level of difficulty serve?  I wanted to like this game, I really did - it hits so many things that I want in a game but in the end I am unable to play further because my skill is insufficient.  I want to see the end of this story, but, frankly, I can save myself broken controllers and the high blood pressure by choosing not to play this game.  So, I will not.  This game did do another thing positive - it got my attention to this developer.  Please put out more games, you've got a good product here, I just wish I could actually finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically like one of the NES Ninja Gaiden games, polished with current standards of game design for a modern audience. You run. You jump. You have a katana and you know how to use it. There are animated cutscenes in that same original-Ninja Gaiden style that are triggered at certain points in the game. The game is divided into levels, and there's a boss at the end of each level. There is a tale, and ninjas are heavily involved. I'd say that Cyber Shadow also kind of reminds me of a Metroid game in the way the game gives the player new abilities, but since the game is completely linear, it's really more of a way for the devs to ease players into the full range of abilities that Shadow eventually has.Overall, the game is really well-made, and really fun, but there were at least 4-5 places in the game where I almost gave up and quit playing out of frustration (MekaDragon, Spiderail, the boat ride, and the final boss gauntlet (Yes gauntlet. It might be a very minor spoiler to say that, but it's the final bosses, so it's not like you couldn't have guessed. Also, the story's not that deep)). I highly recommend the game, but needless to say: beginner's need not apply.
