_childDocuments_.review: My problems with this game:1) The game DELIBERATELY gives you WAY TOO LITTLE moveset to start with in the earlier levels of the game to make you FEEL LIKE TRASH by not being able properly react to enemies due to limited moveset (ESPECIALLY early bosses) in the name of "making you feel more powerful and accomplished" once you FINALLY expand your moveset with new abilities later on, but AT WHAT COST? DELIBERATELY killing you over and over early on and FORCING you to "learn boss patterns" to overcome your abilities limitations?! As someone who ALWAYS strives to beat a game with AS LESS of deaths as possible (as well as beating bosses FIRST TRY), this game's design choices are UNACCEPTABLE to me whatsoever (and no, I don't get "a sense of accomplishment" when beating a boss after dying so many times due to deliberate limited moveset).2) In conjunction with the first point, I DON'T LIKE the fact that the game doesn't give you BASIC abilities like "parry" or "dash" until very later on into the game (THESE should have been available from the get-go to help you against early bosses as well as general platforming).3) And the sad part is, both the "parry/dash" mechanics are FLAWED in this game too. To be more specific, the parry requires you to "push the forward button" at the right time to parry an incoming projectile, but the PROBLEM is that when you are standing on small platform which is over a MILLION INSTANT DEATH SPIKES, unless you time your parries right 100% of the time against the ENDLESS barrage of projectiles coming your way, you will likely press the forward button too early or too late and fall to your death. As for the dash, you have to FIRST trigger the "run animation" before being able to dash past enemies and the problem with that is it can lead to UNINTENTIONAL/ACCIDENTAL dashes (especially in the air) as sometimes I just wanted to "normally slash" an enemy in the air but then the dash ability AUTOMATICALLY TRIGGERS, causing me to drop to my death into those LOVELY "instant death spikes". In short, 4) This game has SO MANY CHEAP "instant death" traps/spikes/flames. Like.... WHO ever thinks that putting so many "instant death" traps in his game is gonna be a "fun thing to deal with" for the players and absolutely not an INFURIATING experience 99.9% of the time?5) The "checkpoints" are TOO DISTANCED from each other (especially later levels) and it is even worse that you have to "pay" for EACH SINGLE CHECKPOINT to get the "SP recharge" or "usable item". There were SO MANY TIMES where I just had to do the BORING TASK of "going back and forth" to collect those glowing orb things just to accumulate enough of them to BE ABLE TO recharge myself and continue my progress. (This is EVEN WORSE given the fact that dying does NOT automatically recharge your "SP", so you will be FORCED to do this garbage "pay to recharge" chore especially if it was before a boss or a tough incoming portion of the level).6) WHY can't I "turn off" the equipped items when I need to?! Because during the "monkey race climbing" bit, I had the "spinning shuriken" equipped and it was MESSING ME UP as it kept breaking stuff in front of my character which I was supposed to "bounce off" using my down sword attack and there was nothing I can do about it because I couldn't turn off the equipped item when I didn't need it or when it was messing me up.7) Forgettable story.Overall, this game was an  rather than a "fun challenging experience." If you want a "retro-style 2D Platformer", then go play  because THAT GAME had the  while also giving you new abilities AT THE RIGHT TIME without making you feel like total trash for the majority of the game. (And the "2" is entirely for the retro music, nothing else).

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is a perfectly OK game.It is never outstandingly fantastic nor is it ever really bad. And this "middle of the road" stance runs through this game's veins:When everything works out, you're dashing and slashing through the stage in style and grace.If not, it changes from resembling Ninja Gaiden to resembling Super Meat Boy instead.Extremely short invincibility times after getting hit + a decent knockback on hit + a plethora of instant-death traps that don't even respect what little invincibility you have, and you have parts of the game that feel more like a puzzle than anything else.It's a pendulum between great and meh parts, between fluent and fast action and slow and frustrating platforming, between spot-on controls and moves that often defy muscle-memory.The games story is also perfectly servicable.It's a "save the girl, avenge the clan/family" kind adeal. Perfectly OK, but not particularly intriguing.The de-facto highlights are the graphics and sound department.If you like pixelart, you're gonna love this! It's authentic without being overly obsessed with sticking to atrtificial limitations. The soundtrack is absolutely solid as well. Plenty of tracks that got stuck in my head or where i unavoidedly started humming along while playing. And here as well, it sounds authentic without limiting itself too much. Overall, Cyber Shadow is a solid recommendation. The game's biggest fault is just how "OK" it is. Its great and not so great moments are kept in balance, creating a perfectly fine game that may not survive the test of time, but right now, is absolutely worth playing!

_childDocuments_.review: Truly an innovative game - I never would have thought of creating skills that SOMETIMES work. There is nothing I love more after a hard day at the office than coming home and hoping that dash and deflect decide they feel like doing their jobs too...or that dash slash doesn't get cheeky and decide to ram me into a spike wall. You know why people love Shovel Knight and The Messenger? It's not (only) because of what they look and sound like - it's because they offer tight gameplay that rewards considerably more than it punishes, and because they always keep the enjoyment of the player in mind. There are a lot of things that Cyber Shadow gets right, but that isn't one of them: it takes so many lessons from the older titles it seeks to emulate but doesn't recognize why we've moved on from doing things that way. There's not a particularly good reason to pick this instead of just doing another playthrough of SK or TM.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd been looking forward to this game ever since I saw the trailer for it last year, and the prospect of some Ninja Gaiden-esque fun with a rocking soundtrack appealed, and I was stoked to finally get my hands on it and play it.In practice, ultimately, it looks great, sounds great, but it's brutally un-fun. One would think that the main character would control fast and fluidly with the touch of a button, but in practice, feels very clumsy to control and your attack options in the game are pretty limited early on (supposedly you get more stuff the further you play, but I haven't found anything) and enemies are very skilled in getting in close right where your attacks won't hit them.I realize some of that's by design--it's meant to evoke the challenge of old Nintendo games, but having played a lot of them back in the day, this feels artificially difficult for its own sake and doesn't really encourage me to play further the way I remember the best of those titles doing. Plodding along inch by agonizing inch isn't really very much fun, and with all the stuff that might make it fun not available or accessible, it's more chore than diversion.It's a shame, because I really liked this visually and was eager to play it and recapture the fun of the old ninja games, but there's nothing that makes me want to play it further and it's a purchase I regret.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really hyped for this one. Sadly it's just too frustrating to recommend. It has beautiful pixel art, seemingly great music from the little I heard and responsive controls. It's also an homage to old school NES platformers, and it's great at that, but at the same time it comes with some of the faults those games had that should be left buried with the 80's.Cyber Shadow is just not that fun and borderline infuriating at times. At least in the beginning of the game. The thing that made me quit was getting to a boss that seemed pretty unfair when considering the limited gameplay options I had at that point. The boss had incredibly fast startup animations on attacks that made it pretty much impossible to react to while trying to deal damage up close. You get a ranged attack but you never get ammo for it in the fight so it's useless. You have no way to dodge so if you get pinned in a corner you're just ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and tanking damage until the boss decides to jump so you can go under him. If the invincibility frames on getting hit was a bit more lenient this problem could be avoided. The whole fight just felt really unfair to me, and if that early boss indicates how the game is gonna treat the player later on I would rather spend my time on something else.I also wanna add that getting knocked back from damage is such a dumb game mechanic in a game like this. Even games that try to emulate old school games should just leave this out because it was never fun in the first place. It's a relic of the past. Combine this knockback with instant death spikes/pits and small enemies that are flying from directions you can't hit and you got yourself a game that is so rooted in the past it becomes unfun. I wanted an homage to Ninja Gaiden etc. with some quality of life improvements and modernizations, isn't that kind of what this game should be? Make it hard but not for the wrong, outdated and frustrating reasons. If this game tries so hard to copy even the stupid parts of those old games, why not just boot up my NES? Maybe all these things are what the target audience for this game wants, but I sure as hell don't want it.I'm sure you get more mobility and defensive/offensive options as the game goes, but the game didn't persuade me to get that far, or to improve or to analyze the boss pattern. I just slammed my controller in my desk and quit, because I don't like games that are hard for the wrong reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start by saying i truly feel for the developers, I really do. However, this game is hot garbage. It starts off pretty strong but slow since you get most of the abilities you saw in the trailer as you progress. The problem is with retro platformers such as this the level design needs to compliment the skills you obtain but that concept was clearly lost on the developers of Cybershadow my main case being the "Dash" ability you obtain has no actual uses to what's presented in front of you in the level and is rather a gimmick you can use to kill a few enemies, it's not totally useless rather unnecessary considering you can kill those enemies without using the "Dash" ability. The controls feel clunky on an Xbox Series X controller due to the button mapping being mapped for an NES controller. If you were hoping for a cool story here might as well skip this one because the story is nonexistent and the boss fights vary from too easy to totally unfair with no middle ground. If you want to smash your controllers over and over again this is the game for you! If you want a cool retro platformer transitioned into modern day game desing, this ain't it man.

_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow has got to be one of the best Ninja Gaiden inspired games I have played in years. At its core Cyber Shadow is an action adventure game with some light metroidvenia elements added in to the mix, which results in a smooth learning curve of the various skills as you go through this 6-8 hours long game.In short I highly recommend this game to anyone that is a fan of the old Ninja Gaiden series or Yacht Club Games previous title: Shovel Knight.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of potential, but seems to lack the missing "it" factor that would make it truly great. Lots of neat little ideas, but nothing truly surprising.  One of the better NES-style retro games, but I was still expecting a little more.Positives:- Art direction is great. Awesome NES-style graphics and cutscenes- Some interesting boss battles like the mechanical dragon- Lots of fun little ideas like the alerts in the factory level- Varied enemies with fun designs - The docks level is a nice homage to Shadow of the ninjaNegatives:- Lots of emphasis on the story, which would have been okay if it had kept my interest- Soundtrack has some memorable tracks, but for the most part it doesn't really catch your attention
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine only being able to attck in one vertical axis and ♥♥♥♥ flying at you from every direction and even though you hit it the hitboxes are so tiny that you miss and die. _childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10. Game is good but be prepared for some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ difficulty spikes and table slamming.If you like instant death hazards, annoying enemy placements, and checkpoints that are stationed far from where you died, then give this game a try. Jokes aside, I thought Cyber Shadow was a good game with a few flaws that made it very frustrating to play. The game looks beautiful and your character's moveset is really fun to control, even if the controls are very, VERY outdated (why can't the parry be set to a button??). I honestly didn't care for the story, so I barely remembered anything throughout the journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game: Tough as nails, but really enjoyable. I've seen a lot of people complain about level design, but I disagree. You are expected to memorize the layout and enemy spawn points as well as fully utilizing your power-ups to maneuver. Some have complained about RNG, which I don't understand at all, everything can be mastered (with the exception of the dragon boss, which is the only time I felt I was taking cheap hits). My only real criticism, which is in nearly all the reviews, is that some of the checkpoints are too far apart. I'm a pretty mid-tier gamer, and I beat the game in a little less than 11 hours with 425 deaths: It's not easy, but it is fair. I wish it had been discounted a bit since it came out 3 years ago, but even at 20 bucks, it's definitely worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:- Great pixel art- Added a nice touch with scan lines "bad wires" making it feel like a retro game- Excellent music- Weapon system and power ups- No required back tracking- Reasonably challenging- Fun boss fightsNeutral:- The story / plotThe Bad:- The controls, inputs don't register fairly frequently- Sometimes the knock back doesn't provide enough time to move away from the current attackThe controls are really the biggest issue, the dash mechanic was more difficult to perform with the double tap and I even tried using the other approach, but still found it didn't work as well as needed.Overall:Fun game to play if you get it on sale. I think if the controls could be fixed, this would easily be one of the best games I've played in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is a really cool retro-style ninja-like with great level design and a surprisingly intriguing story. I don't have a lot of experience with this sub-genre of platformer so my initial playthru was a bit challenging but all of it was enjoyable. My favorite part of the game is how crazy the movement and navigation options become as you unlock more abilities--it feels like you are playing an almost completely different game by the end. I also really liked finding secrets and fighting the bosses, though the final boss felt a little anticlimactic.From what I understand this was a project largely by a solo dev and it's absolutely amazing considering that. Not as robust in content as something like Shovel Knight (but which game is?) and maybe a little more sharp around the edges, but I enjoyed it infinitely more than my time with The Messenger. The Messenger's platforming/level design was very binary with little room for player expression, whereas in Cyber Shadow you can clear a room in a variety of ways depending on your skill and comfort level with your abilities.A great game I would heavily recommend playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: In the end this game's to difficult to be fun and I guess that counts for most people who will play it. I really liked The Messenger so I gave this one a shot. It has some nice art style and cool music, smooth gameplay and good level design but this game get's frustrating really quick. I eventually got in chapter 8 now and I probably wil finish it but man, this game's a pain in the ass!
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Pixel platformer game contrary to popular metroidvania genre belief. Or better we say it is relatable with metroidvania elements..Often compared to The Messenger, which is why I bought it due to its similarity. However, even though the taste it left on the palate was not as qualified as The Messenger, it is still a good and tougher game. The Messenger executed metroidvania elements perfectly, and its story, humor, and the transition from 8-bit to 16-bit were original and these are what made The Messenger better.Other than that, Cyber Shadow's bosses, monsters, and level designs are varied and force you to use different tactics provided by the game throughout the chapters. The story didn't attract me. For negative criticism, I would say the absence of NG+ is weird. Moreover, many people believed that NG+ would be added as DLC, but there is no news from the dev for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool ninja game. At first I was worried it was going to be another retro-styled game that doesn't really have retro challenge, but it gets nice and tricky in the later parts of the game, especially if you aim for collecting some of the hidden powerups. Biggest complaint would be that it starts off slow and doesn't really pick up until you're fully powered up. Despite surface-level comparisons to Ninja Gaiden or Shadow of the Ninja, felt a bit more Megaman X-ish in terms of the platforming. Story is not that interesting but it's never outright bad.Never had any issues with the controls at all, don't know if the game was patched or what but the negative reviews complaining about the controls felt very misleading. Never had any trouble with the parrying and thought it was one of the best/most unique parts of the game.Overall it's a pretty good platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some extremely good ideas, but also some big flaws. TLDR is I still recommend this game as it was very fun and was rewarding to master. I can't wait to see MekaSkull's next game as it will no doubt be excellent. The Good:-1st half is a fun Ninja Gaiden like game-2nd half is a good bit different and is excellent-Enemy designs are interesting with and there are many different enemies-Music is very good, not chart topping like a zero ranger, but very solid/catchy-Cool and fun boss battles-The final move-set you unlock around the halfway point is simply sublime. It is easily the best thing in this game-Lovely little cinematics (I wish there were more of them)-Enemy attacks are well telegraphed and feel very fair-Beautiful visuals/sprite workThe Bad:-I get it, it is an NES inspired platformer it needs to have instant kill spike traps and I am fine with it. I think we went just a little bit overboard with it. I would have preferred if we removed some of the difficulty from the platforming parts and relocated said difficulty to the stage enemies and or bosses -With how insanely good the movement on the full kit feels it is a crime that you only get it half way through the game. I would have preferred if you got the movement related stuff much faster as this is when the game is at it's finest.-The second half of the game is very light on the number of bosses compared to the first half and that is a real shame with how good the bosses that  are here are.The Ugly:-The parry requires double tapping the dpad in the bullet's direction, making it super hard to do while trying to maneuver through the air. I just wish you could bind it to a button.-The story has the kernel of something great, but is a little too underdeveloped/doesn't have enough screen time to truly be an important part of the game. Which is a shame because I can see what the dev was going for in his head (so much potential in this area).

And you will realize how much you miss ducking relatively quickly.Other than that problem..its a really fun ride. _childDocuments_.review: An excellent loveletter to the retro titles that advertised themselves based off difficulty, most notable Ninja Gaiden and Contra. The game controls extremely tight, has generally good level design with probably more enemy variety than was really necessary but makes every stage fresh, and tons of variety in the stages themselves. Every new stage will introduce different mechanics incentivizing you to use your most recently unlocked ability, and as you complete your moveset it becomes extremely fluid and feels natural to control due to the gradual introduction of your moveset. There are tons of bosses and mini-bosses as well which will test your use of your various abilities, and most of them are very memorable. The game provides a solid challenge overall, and while it doesn't shy away from instant-kill spikes/pits or killing you in a few hits towards the end of the game the lack of lives and fairly spaced checkpoints keep a solid balance between challenge and frustration. I actually found the game was a bit easier than I expected, but this might just be me having played a lot of challenging games and platformers.The soundtrack is also absolutely fantastic and always fittingly sets the mood. The song heard in the trailer is one of the best but there are plenty of other great tracks all throughout the game, and tons of tracks in general. Most stages have mutliple tracks for different sections, and every single mini-boss and boss have their own theme. Combined with the other tracks from cutscenes and the odd calmer area there are almost 70 tracks in the whole game. I saw another review mention it's the best non-memorable soundtrack they've heard, and I think the one downside of this huge musical variety is that on a single playthrough you won't be hearing any track for more than 15 minutes once and then never again for the rest of the game unless you backtrack. The soundtrack is excellent, you just will be hard pressed to recall it due to not hearing any single track for very long.I think the game's main flaw is that despite how long it was in development, it still seems a bit unfinished and it feels like there should have been more. It's already great, but it could have been an absolute masterpiece had it been given more time or it had more than a single developer. For starters, the story is good for a platformer but apparently only about 25% of the whole written story was used in the full game. There are also elements of backtracking with some barriers and hidden passages you need abilities unlocked later to reach. There are very few of these however, and they only open up side paths leading to a mini-boss  guarding an upgrade to your health or SP. This ends up making the backtracking feel a bit pointless as you're taking the time to go back only for a teeny bit of extra content and nothing as interesting as the main path through the game. The main path also feels quite short. 6 hours is not a bad runtime for a retro platformer like this which focuses on quality over quantity, but the real issue is by the time you've unlocked your full moveset you're already 2/3 of the way through the whole game and only have a few stages left. There are also the Ethos dojo stages which seem like they would be fun challenges that deviate from the main gameplay loop, but the last 2 are essentially just cutscenes where there should have been room for more challenges and a boss fight. It feels like just when the game is getting good, it's over. If there were a few more stages, and maybe the unlocked abilities were introduced a bit faster, it would feel much more satisfying.Despite the flaws, Cyber Shadow is still an excellent game and absolutely worth a purchase. The core of my complaints are just that it feels like the game had the potential to be something truly special, and while it's a great game that I would highly recommend it fell short of being an indie game that blows up and has a lasting legacy like Cave Story, Shovel Knight or Hollow Knight. It's still absolutely worth a purchase, at the very least wait for a sale, especially if you're a fan of platformers. I would love if we ever got a DLC or sequel to the game with more developers to help it reach its full potential, though that seems unlikely with how long the solo dev already worked on the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is a 2D plateformer designed to feel as retro as possible, while still being modern in some respects. Don't be too afraid of the challenge, as the game is usually generous enough with checkpoints and you have infinite lives.Be aware, however, that this is indeed a tough game that will expect you to exploit all its mechanics to succeed. Personally though, I found that the abilities were spread out well enough throughout the game to give you enough time to master them.I remember being put off initially by some of the negative reviews the game received, but when I got to try it out for myself, I was hooked. It's a really charming game, with fun but challenging gameplay and an enticing somber atmosphere too.

_childDocuments_.review: It is ultimately a good game, but its pacing is a bit lacking.While it's normal for games like this to give you more tools as you progress, your initial toolset is extremely limited (melee attack and jump) and the first half of upgrades don't improve your situation all that much, and with how extremely limiting the ammo/mana system is, those tools will be near-useless in combat and only good for puzzles for at least 60% of the game. Of course, this also translates into the level design.Which is most likely why they give you gimmick weapons that you lose after 3 hits, to sorta spice up your combat until then,One aspect that I do find completely negative is the lack of control input customization, I should not be forced to be limited to NES-like 2 button inputs just because the game is retro-inspired, especially the shuriken should have had its own button input, there were countless times where the shuriken didn't register because of this,So... Why am I saying this is a good game then? Well first, the early game never gets actually boring, the game doesn't lack challenge either, it's just that the mechanics are very limiting early on. And the late game is excellent, especially the last few bosses actually make you use your full skillset.While the asking price is not too steep, it might be more worth it for you at a small discount, but I feel I got my money's worth; it took me 20 hours to finish with 100% of the collectible life and mana upgrades.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Cyber Shadow is the newest throwback ninja game published by Yacht Club Games.  This was by far my most anticipated game of 2021 and I am very happy that I finally got to experience this brutally challenging love letter to the NES glory days of gaming.  It's not as good as The Messenger, but it's still a fantastic experience that every fan of the genre should experience.  What's Good:-This game looks incredible visually!  This is a true love letter to the very best bosh rush games of the NES and SNES era.  Similar to The Messenger, this game is a perfect blend of retro nostalgia and modern visual styles.  This game is a top notch example of 8 bit pixel art.-This game really hits it's stride about half way through as your character becomes an extremely agile, gravity defying, badass ninja.  It's such a great feeling as you get better at dashing in mid air, chaining attacks, and dicing through enemies like swish cheese.  It's take a few hrs to really get going, but once it does, this game never takes it's foot off the gas.-The learning curve is quite steep, but the skill ceiling is also extremely high.  It's a really rewarding feeling as you master the mechanics.  As you get better at the game, you will touch the ground less frequently and stay airborn for longer periods of time.  It's so cool!  -The bosses are smart, tactical, and very challenging.  The environmental hazards are arguably the most challenging parts of the game, but the bosses are the most fun imo.  I loved almost every boss fight, which is pretty rare for a game in this genre.-Although this game is very challenging, there are quite of few modern accessibility options that make the experience more manageable.  First off, there are checkpoints, which is great.  There isn't a live system, so you can die a thousand times if that's what you need to beat the game.  There are also both permanent upgrades that you can find, and temporary upgrades that you can purchase to give yourself every opportunity to succeed.  Could Use Some Changes:-This is a challenging game.  I don't think it's that crazy difficult, but I do think that the learning curve is steeper than the average game.  Platforming is a massive part of this game, which is probably why I didn't struggle as much as most ppl (I play tons of precision platformers).  So, if you really don't enjoy challenging platforming sections, this game may not be for you.  There are lots of spikes or electricity that instantly kill you.  These are probably the most challenging moments in the game.-The only downside to being fully upgraded and being able to dash through the air like a ninja, is that it makes it easier to avoid enemies in order to clear tough sections.  I prefer to really take my time and defeat every single enemy, and that becomes really tedious late game.-My last gripe is that the game ends a bit too early imo.  The problem is that it takes 3-4 hrs to get a few upgrades and master the mechanics.  By hour 6-7, you are already taking on the most challenging sections.  Then by 8-9, the game is over.  I think the pacing could use a few slight tweaks, but that's just my personal opinion.Consensus:-Solid Game (Tier 3 and makes up 35% of my reviews).  Cyber Shadow is a love letter to the glory days of gaming.  To those that grew up playing Ninja Gaiden, Contra, or Shinobi, you'll feel right at home w/ Cyber Shadow.  I don't think this game is as good as The Messenger, but I still think it's an easy recommendation.  I enjoyed almost every minute of my experience, and wish that there were a few more hours of it!  If you haven't played this yet, pick it up and have a blast slicing and dicing baddies to bits.

_childDocuments_.review: A good mix of Shadow of the ninja (Kage) and Shatterhand (Solbrain).The ramp up in the difficulty in the second half of the game can take you by surprise with it's ninja gaiden like tight timing and platforming and challenging bosses. But I'd say that the first half is just too easy.Checkpoints are plenty. Mastering the skillset and levels make you feel like a true ninja.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: A relatively simple and short 2D side scrolling action platformer, Cyber Shadow does a competent job at delivering on the standards and expectations of the genre.  With design that borrows from both Ninja Gaiden and Mega Man wrapped up in a modern package, you could do much worse on Steam.The controls are all 'correct'.  There are options for a few of the few UX-y things that bugged me, and the 'rules' of this genre are all adhered to with delightful precision.  This is clearly built by someone who understands what works in this genre, and what makes it tick.All that said, it's definitely a relatively safe game and doesn't do much to challenge the status quo of the genre too much with the exception of a slash/dash you get later that lets a skilled player zip through sections like a badass.  This also serves as a great entry point into the genre if you didn't grow up with the NES games this takes inspiration from.The game is somewhat simple and short compared to some of it's contemporaries such as The Messenger, or Katana Zero, but I definitely enjoyed my time with it and would happily recommend it to both fans of the genre and those looking to explore it for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is an excellent adrenaline pumping platformer that gives the player a lot of options in how they take on the game's waves of enemies and bosses. You have ninja attack dash, shurikens, fire magic and charge attacks to name a few). It's a tough game but the controls are perfectly tuned for ground and midair combat, you have just the right amount of floating to out maneuver your opponents. Fans of The Messenger and Shovel Knight will likely love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is best described as a tough platformer with NES-like aesthetics and a few trackback elements. The various boss battles are doable, but prepare to die a lot from the tough ass level design. Especially the secret areas. The music is fitting and good, if at times a bit subdued. Some achievements are pretty tough to get. I do love the many easter eggs in the game, not least of which is Optimus Prime's truck mode parked in the ruined city. The final boss btw is nasty since you need to go 3 rounds with 2 lifebars each...
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not only aesthetically pleasing, it also plays beautifully.  I really love my classic Ninja Gaiden games and this really scratches that itch for another game like it.  It also has elements of Shatterhand, Shadow of the Ninja, and even some Megaman X/Zero.  At first you probably feel like the game feels limited.  You have a jump and a slash button and that is all.  You don't even have a wall cling, a secondary weapon, or even a crouch.  However you start unlocking skills after each major segment of the game and they change the game slowly.  It starts as a standard Ninja Gaiden type romp, but by the end it does feel a bit like a very very difficult Megaman X game.  Each new move obtained is followed by a lengthy section that trains you to use that new tool to succeed.  As soon as you get the shuriken throw there is a stage with buttons to hit from a distance.  As soon as you get the downward pogo, you have sections where you can bounce on enemies to progress.  At first I thought it'd be nice having all these tools at the beginning of the game, but I think the nuances of each skill is too much to take in all at once.  As you reach the end of the game, all the tools are required at once traverse areas more easily.  With that said, most areas can be completed without masterful use of the new moves, but the path is often slower and more treacherous.  Speeding through areas is the reward for mastering the skill set as you learn to string the movement options together.  It feels satisfying to zip through a line of enemies using the dash attack, and chaining pogo bounces for distance and height.  Attempting such stunts often leads to countless deaths, but the times it all works out flawlessly feels magical.    The game might seem impossibly hard, but if you come from the NES Ninja Gaiden games and still have them fairly fresh in your mind and want a new challenge, this game is right up your alley.  If you are acclimated to the old Ninja Gaiden game, the game probably doesn't feel very difficult until you reach the outskirts in chapter 7.  Even then, I don't think this game is ever as punishing as trying to play through the first Ninja Gaiden for the first time.List of Pros and Cons Time!Pros:-Graphically stunning game, the pixel art is gorgeous to look at and the animations are really beautiful.  They capture that retro aesthetic while doing things that the devs of the olden days can only dream of doing.-Most of the soundtrack is bloody amazing.  It might not be the most amazing music in a retro style game, but there are a bunch of bangers that will get you bobbing your head.-Controls are pretty stellar.  You have directional input while jumping.  If you get used to all the moves, you can really do some pretty amazing ninja-like parkour.  Dash jump and zip through a line of enemies, double jump and pogo off another, bounce off a wall and parry something mid jump.  It's very satisfying when it works out.  Most of the time it doesn't work out, but when it does... -Difficulty is amazing.  It's a very tough but fair game.  It's not unfair like Ninja Gaiden with their enemies that spawn at the very edge of the screen scrolling.  If you take it slow in Cyber Shadow, very little should take you by surprise.  But you still need twitch reactions to get by.  Game demands a lot out of you, and you would either love or hate it.Cons:-There really needs to be a way to turn off double tap to dash, or at least a way to make it so the dash slash doesn't come out when you don't want it to.  It's very easy to forget that you are building a charge or something or to accidentally dash slash off a cliff or into some death spikes.  I'm sure you can get used to it, and I think the controls are great.  It's just not something I got used to even after beating the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is a love letter to the 8-bit NES games of old. You can feel the influence of Ninja Gaiden, Shadow of the Ninja, Power Blade and Mega Man. It's a challenging game but not TOO challenging and when you die, it mostly feels fair and you learn to get better. There will be plenty of obscenity shouting when you don't quite make it to the next check point but that also makes it fun and you want to keep trying unless you master it.The game has a very lite Metroidvania aspect to it where you can use your new upgrades to go back into previous levels to find power ups but it isn't required but gives you something a little extra to do if you'd like.The controls are good but if I'm nitpicking, I do think they feel not quite as tight or fast as I'd like them to be. The immediate comparison is Ninja Gaiden but rather than the quick and snappy controls, it feels a little slower paced and closer to Power Blade or Shadow of the Ninja. You also can't duck which will really throw old school players. There were plenty of times early in the game where I would get hit because I would want to duck and slash an enemy and instead, I'm just normal slashing. While the game doesn't need it, I do miss ducking. It's just instinct.As for the music, it's fantastic and you'll be humming the melodies long after you've ended the game.If you like challenging action platformers, this is absolutely one of the best games in the genre and would be hailed as an all time classic if it was released during the NES era.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: It's great, really. Perhaps almost as good as The Messenger & Shovel Knight. Definitely recommend it at its current discounted price of 13.99 but it's honestly worth full price as well. Combat is fluid, movement is spot on (not floaty at all) and power ups are great. Graphics-wise the game is exactly what you'd expect from a modern day 8-bit classic - easy on the eyes and allows you to navigate through the world without confusing you if whether a platform can be jumped on or not etc. Enjoy! :) P.S: definitely better played with a KB rather than a controller but I'm not sure if this is entirely true for this specific game or it's just my preference as I always find it 100x easier to play 2D platformer games with a keyboard.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful homage to the late NES era platformer.  It recreates how those games  without all the drawbacks of late 80s / early 90s game design.You can tell this game was made by NES fans.  The attention to the retro detail is just wonderful.Edit:  I've been reading some other reviews and would like to clarify something.  This is not a metroidvania.  This game is quite linear, but it does allow you to backtrack in order to find *optional* items.  The people calling this a love letter to Metroid must have only played Metroid Fusion :)Also, the difficulty level of this game is high, but fair.  If you want to see extreme and unfair difficulty just try the original Ninja Gaidens!Oh, and use a D-Pad.  This type of game is made for digital input.  You're only making your life harder by using analogue.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun little retro-style action platformer. The biggest blemish on the game is that the inputs for some of the advanced moves feel kind of inconsistent, in part because the game doesn't really explain how they work, at least to my knowledge.Other than that it's challenging and quite fun. Not peak of the genre fun or anything, but it's a solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. Blew through it this week. It's squarely in the NES-homage action platformer genre, similar to shovel knight. Very fun gameplay, you start out with a basic set of attacks and moves that grow with each level. In a lot of games like this I usually only like one or two of the special moves that I got and ignore the rest, but I found myself using everything that was given to me pretty consistently. And there's a few sneaky combos with the moves that you can figure out. You ever see that thing in an anime where a character runs back and forth doing a ton of attacks in the blink of an eye? With enough button mashing and the dash attack move you can actually do that in Cyber Shadow! Very cool.Story was fine, I honestly didn't follow the events or characters super well, but I got the gist of it. I could just be dumb though. The cutscenes and characters designs are very pleasant to look at though. If you're happy with vibes and don't need a super concrete story, you won't have a problem.Only thing that was a bit annoying was that the map system for the game is a little weird. You're encouraged to go back to old levels to pick up previously inaccessible items, but navigation can get very confusing. You can fast travel between points that roughly correspond to the start of each level, and there's a stylized map that gives you an idea of where to go, but after that you've got no reference points. The levels connect at certain weird points and you can get off track, some of them are also changed permanently after you go through them once which can make it tough to figure out where to go. It would have been nice to have some kind of mini-map. Otherwise, no complaints, great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore all the people crying that this game is unbalanced or broken, this game is old school difficulty. I had my moments of hating this game but I know it was just the building frustration of being stuck on certain parts for an hour+, this is a great game that provides a wide variety of abilities and gadgets to help you progress its surprising length of levels.  Typically when I get games similar looking to this I expect 6-8 hours of content but Cyber Shadow shocked me with almost 14 hours from start to finish, all being quality content. All in all just know what you're getting into, it's a really solid retro platformer with a good (not too complex) cyberpunk story and a pleasing aesthetic but damn does it get hard.  Originally I thought 20$ was a bit steep but content-wise I think it's fair, Cyber Shadow really impressed me with it's true old school gameplay, witty crossovers, dystopian cyberpunk aesthetic, and wide variety of play mechanics. Buy it, have fun, punch walls, have more fun
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow joins the ranks of other retro-style games like Shovel Knight. Published by the same Yacht Games, but developed by a different person, it not only delivers the aesthetic and killer 8-bit music, but also a series of well designed levels, abilities, and ever-increasing difficulty. There are game that have the look, but fall flat on the retro platformer gameplay. Cyber Shadow is NOT one of those games. If you like NES games with hard but fair levels and bosses, then this is a game you cannot miss. I recommend playing with a friend, passing the controller, and shouting together in frustration  as that ONE TINY FLYING DUDE KILLS YOU AGAIN, then in joy when the next checkpoint arrives.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: I tried a few  times to like and get into this game but i can't. While other challenging platformers are also fun while challenging does this game oberall just feel tedious. You can't crouch or attack in different directions, so for being able to hit certain enemies you have to position yourself just right. The stages are designed that there are hazards everywhere, so working on a concept getting through a stage rarely if ever gets you in this kind of flow you know from other games where the game just clicks and it's fun. I know you'll later get some upgrades etc, but in the beginning your character can't do ♥♥♥♥ and it's just boring and bland. I've waited so long for this and its just disappointing.I can recommend Shovle Knight or the Messenger if you're looking for something similar but really well made.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, enjoyed it. Good platforming that ramps up in difficulty after a while where you need to deal with moving enemies alongside moving platforms mixed in with the additional abilities you get along the way. Good variety of enemies each with different attack patterns. Some parts at the end can be a little frustrating at times, but with the checkpoint system, it doesn't feel too punishing.  The powerup system isn't too amazing, you can basically purchase an ability at each checkpoint, or the rare powerup in the wall secrets, to help if you're having issues with a particular segment.  These can include reusable projectiles, temporary shield, or extra sword range. Otherwise, you're using just your sword, dash, and basic shuriken projectile about 90% of the time. Which didn't bother me too much since the enemy level design, platforming, and general feel of the game is top notch. Music is well done with the futuristic setting.  You can definitely tell the game draws inspiration from some NES games like Batman and Ninja Gaiden from the NES with its early level color palette, enemies design, and platforming segments alongside with some Easter eggs which, for me, is a good thing.  Story-wise, up until a bit more than halfway, you just kind of go "whatever" since you just get little snippets of dialog and the random computer logs you come across.  But eventually the story ramps up enough to make it have enough oomph to get a bit invested and ends satisfactory enough unlike most other games. 3/4
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet retro style game. The gameplay mechanics are all very solid and it just feels better and better as you get powerups. The difficulty feels fair and there are a good number of checkpoints. You can take your time if you like to play casually but speedrunners will enjoy exploring the mechanics to see how to breeze through bosses and levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: o_0This game is simply frecking "AMAZING" and any fans of 8-Bit NES/FAMICOM will deffo lose they minds. It's basically the Natsume game KAGE (Shadow of the Ninja) meets Strider Hiryu on crack but very much it's own game as well. Stellar soundtrack and great execution of the genre. My only gripe is that I keep wanting to crouch and Shadow doesn't seem to be able to do that. BUY THIS GAME!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: I have really mixed feeling of this game. I'm gonna still gice it a thumbs up because I initially really enjoyed this game and got many hours of fun from it. It's just towards the end as the difficulty ramps up it stops being enjoyable. Cyber Shadow is worth a play but it is not great.I love the retro feel, I love the ninja-gaiden vibes. It hit all the awesome nostalgia points for me. The game is not doing anything transformative, it's not really adding anything super modern twist on this formula but it is doing what it is doing well and it was totally all I needed. I really liked that it gives you some control over the difficulty: at check points you get to use points you earn in gameplay to buy health/energy/weapon re-fills so that if you die at the section, you start the next try with full energy or a weapon. You could try to beat the section with pure skill and if you failed you could buy the weapon and then quickly realize that "oh, this is totally designed around this ability" and usually beat it quite fast after this. It stayed challengin but fun.Then towards the end the game seems to take this away from you. You hit check point after checkpoint where all you get restored is your health and everythin else is puposely disabled. Suddenly you are just grinding the same sections over and over and over again because you are forced to play them without any upgrades and every corner is filled with instant deaths. If you play well and can hold on to the abilites/weapons without dying, thing are extra easy because you are way more powerful with them. If you happen to die then the game feels like it is slapping you in the face and saying "you suck" and try it now without any upgrades and then you are in the grind. And it stops being enjoyable wheares the earlier part of the game was both challenging and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. I am a huge sucker for retro style games and this one nails every aspect of the platformer genre. It takes obvious inspiration from Ninja Gaiden but it has elements mixed in from other 2D platformers of the era as well. Especially the Mega Man X series. The game has a flow to it that makes it impossible to put down. Give this one a shot, especially if you love the genre. It's published by Yacht Club Games after all, what do you expect?
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the platforming sections feel like BS, but the game can fairly consistently "get away" with it due to the lack of a lives system, and you feel like a badass when you do pull it off. And that IMO is where I think the game excels at most, even beyond its solid gameplay foundation, poignant story, and pulse-pounding earworm soundtrack. It does a good job of making you feel like a badass ninja robot kicking all kinds of ass, especially numerous spoiler segments in the late game. I say give it a shot, though its most certainly for experienced platformer veterans.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: While not made by the same people as Shovel Knight, it does bear their stamp of approval as publisher, and Cyber Shadow is something of a kindred spirit to that game. While Shovel Knight borrowed from Mega Man and Castlevania (with a dash of DuckTales), Cyber Shadow feels tied very closely to Ninja Gaiden. That's not just the esthetic and the gameplay, but also the feeling of difficulty. You will die often, but Cyber Shadow lacks a lives system so it's very easy to jump back in and try again. Cyber Shadow also aspires to Ninja Gaiden-style storytelling, but I never cared at all about what was going on there. Perhaps the less-is-more approach of its inspiration would have served the game better.This is a tough, occasionally frustrating but often clever and stylish game. Exploration is rewarded, as is sharp play. This won't be to everyone's taste but I give it a solid recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm gonna be 100% forward about my attitude towards this game: I was excited the moment it was announced. Being a massive fan of Ninja Gaiden, Strider, Shinobi, and generally any game that lets me Zip-Around as a Ninja/Martial Artist/Assassin, I was hyped for this from Day One. I've had a lot of disappointments in games I've been hyped up for and this was not one of them. In fact, I couldn't put this game down when I started playing it.So, the visuals: Expect detailed and gorgeous pixel-art. In terms of visual design, you won't find any lazy efforts. From the cherry-blossom leaves, to the various bosses and enemies, everything seems to have been paid good attention to.Gameplay: Fast paced Arcade-y action with challenges that are built into the level designs themselves (think Ninja Gaiden on the NES and how some the level designs were made to test the skills you learned along the way). I can't find any fault with the gameplay whatsoever. In fact, I'll infer that I prefer this game to Shovel-Knight. While Shovel-Knight is amazing (especially the Treasure Trove edition), this game simply has the aesthetic and gameplay I'm obsessed with.Music: Great. Chiptune but it's obvious that whoever wrote the music has both a talent and a knack when it comes to making music that sounds good in 8-Bit (this is something that's important when it comes to music and sound design in Retro-Style games. You can't just plop a Midi or Music file into a game and expect it to set the mood. You have to know what mood you're going for and what notes compliment the atmosphere you're going for).Sound Design: Can't find anything to complain about. Generally reminds me of old-er games (which is the point). So, good stuff.Level Design: Challenging but also fun as heck, especially if you're trying to do runs where you don't take any damage.Overall 5/5. I can't recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of the greatest retro 2d action platformers to date, touting lush pixel art mixed with responsive, precision based gameplay.  If you loved "the Messenger" as heralding the torch of the NES era Ninja Gaiden, this game continues the marathon.  Mixing feudal Japanese iconography and ninja mythology with modernized cypberpunk themes and elements in it's world design, enemies and story.   You get to seemlessly traverse retro futurist settings and environs as you uncover the mystery of "the essence".  Each upgrade allows you more abilities to zip around and dispatch enemies more effectively.  Unforgiving difficulty will feel nostalgic for those who cut their teeth on the tough games of the 8bit era, and this delivers in spades.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Ninja Gaiden 1/Strider-like platformer published by the creators of Shovel Knight. It's a highly polished & well crafted experience with excellent music.You control a member of a ninja clan dedicated to eliminating rogue synthetics on behalf their creator, Dr. Progen. But something went horrible wrong and now Dr. Progen seeks to siphon the power of his previous allies and dominate the world with his robot army. You're Shadow, the last survivor, and you must stop Progen at all cost.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like Ninja Gaiden and Shatterhand for NES had a lovechild, and I mean that in the best way possible. This game is really fun and fairly challenging, with a surprisingly deep and heartbreaking story. I loved it and recommend it to anyone, regardless if you think you're an expert at platformers. The difficulty ramp is so smooth, I'm sure anyone can have a shot at beating it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: First try, sub 12 hours... Where do I even start?Let's just say, you pick Ninja Gaiden, Metroid, Megaman, Shadow of the Ninja, Shatterhand/Tokkyuu Shirei - Solbrain, smash them together, put the result in a post apocalyptic city of Mekacity, spice it up with an interesting story and you get Cyber Shadow.The beginnings can be a bit tricky, with no special abilities, but the game doesn't ramp up the difficulty because of that instantly. Once you have the abilities, that's a WHOLE DIFFERENT CLUSTERF*CK, but it's really challenging... Sometimes maybe TOO challenging. The controls are responsive, the mechanics work as intended (except for the knock-back when you get hit...) like a well polished NES game. Once you get the "dash slash", that's where the real stylish swag moves hide. You've gotta go fast... really fast!There is a huge variety of awesome bosses too!All in all I'm super impressed with Cyber Shadow, it's a master-class in game design, especially in the music department. The tunes are out of this world, honestly!This game is not for weaklings and It needs more attention!
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Shovel Knight you will like this.  It's more NES-style platforming, but very refined and with the life-system edge taken off.There were a few sections where I felt cheated that I was killed by something I couldn't see coming, but that is to be expected from the style of games this is trying to emulate.  The penalty for death is never high enough for me to not give it another try.Difficulty is hard, just hard enough to make you feel accomplished when you finally overcome, but not hard enough to make you ragequit if you've played an older platformer before.  Treat death as a learning experience and take it slow.The presentation, both art and music, is amazing, nothing else to say for that area.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! This game brings me so much nostalgia to Saturdays trying to clock the Ninja Gaiden games. This game is incredible and very faithful to those type of games. Its challenging but not impossible. Im thankful for save areas and love all the different upgrades and extra gadgets you collect. The pixel art is great as well as the 8 bit soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid platformer for platformer fans. Technically it's a metroidvania, but the main path is so linear (and backtrarcking so rare) that it's effectively just a platformer with hidden side-rooms and periodic new moves. Instead, almost all the focus is on delivering the best platforming and combat that it can.Level design is creative, varied and well-paced. Enemy design is also quite good. Music and visuals are great while sticking to the low-bit aesthetic. Bosses are pretty good. Controls are great EXCEPT for the dash move.Negatives... some of the later areas are a bit all-or-nothing, in that you either make a perfect series of jumps and dash-strikes or you make one mistake and eat a ton of damage because you lost your momentum or activated a security system. And if you prefer using the dedicated button rather than double-tap dash, the dash sometimes doesn't work when you expect since it doesn't activate if you weren't moving before hitting the shift button (this almost always results in immediate death). But both of those gripes only apply to later levels, and only occasionally.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is good bloody 2D fun. The controls are tight (for most parts), the level design flows just great with shades of its forefathers echoed in every layer and pixel, and the platforming combat mix is brutal yet fair.Yacht Club and Mechanical Head have clearly made a title for acquired tastes, specifically the masochistic kind, but they at least had the decency to be generous with its continue system and new-age game design nuances like refillable energy for your skills. All in all, highly recommended if you think these past few indie games of yesteryear are a bit too tame for your liking.Full review:
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: More than anything else, I am happy that developers are realizing that these kinds of games can tell a far more in-depth story than most games do, and this game has a very well done story, complete with lore and details in a satisfying quantity. While I may not like the ending, the story was well made.However, while the beginning of the game is great, the second half is plagued by tedious sections of the levels that do not have any way of moving through quickly, which is a huge problem if you die after that point. The special abilities are great, but I ended up not using the second to last upgrade because it didn't work half the time.Overall, though, not a bad game. Not a great one, but not bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is quickly becoming my favorite 2D ninja platformer ever.  The game can be tough to learn and master but it is very rewarding to level up on and the story plot, setting and gameplay are what I had been waiting for ever since I heard the publishers of Shovel Knight were making a ninja game. The music is also fantastic and fits perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Considering how much hours I played Showel Knight, I was ecstatic when I seen new game from Yacht Club Games and scared....So far I played  game for not even two hours and already I started using some curses I did not know I known. I did not get in "breaking controler mode" but game is not easy, but I would not said it is extra hard...... I would go challenging.Graphic and music I do not think there is need to explain it is 8 bit style pixel graphic with synthetic music.Just do play this with controller if you wanna save nerves. _childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: ooohhh boy this game was alot of fun playing i tell ya start off being ninja gaiden with support assists weapons like shuriken or katana enhances attacks then becomes more metroid view world exploring then start out like playing strider hiryu/metroid decent story telling only thing personally wish it was more snes style & kinda wish they stop relying on metroid exploring linear if there spin off going on im interested & recommend worth game of the year thumbs up

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of old school Ninja Gaiden and of course Shovel Knight i purchased this because Yacht Club Games   did such an amazing job with Shovel Knight that i would support any game they release because they are beyond talented and Cyber Shadow is so far really awesome not that i expected any less. I look forward to anything they make and so far this game has been Amazing! Challenging but yet i keep trying and an interesting story i cant wait to put some serious time in on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Take the mediocre reviews with a HUGE grain of salt, the game is more than worth it! Best experience on STEAM close to the real NES games. An amazing game, can't wait for Cyber Shadow II. I'm hoping for MORE Feats and more content for this game, it deservers so much more content!I love the difficulty of it, yet so fluent in pacing!
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Challenging, gorgeous, and it even comes with a well-presented story, Cyber Shadow is the kind of platformer I love. The controls are solid, the upgrades are satisfying, and overall, I find the experience of mastering the game's mechanics, platforming sequences, and boss strats extremely gratifying. And the music? Stellar, top notch chiptune goodness. At the price point, I'm thrilled with the purchase.Update!Having now played The Messenger, I'd like to address the comparisons being made between that game and this one. At best, this is a false equivalency and at worst it's lazy: both games have ninjas, duh?!Cyber Shadow and The Messenger are two completely different experiences. The Messenger is a good game, but it doesn't take itself seriously and it borrows more heavily from classic ninja games, while Cyber Shadow simply pays its dues and moves on to do its own thing. The gameplay and the exploration are different enough that making direct comparisons between the two just doesn't hold water for me.If you liked The Messenger, that's no guarantee that you'll like Cyber Shadow and vice versa. If you want to play a fun game with tight controls, they both have that in common. If you want great music, again, both games have that in common. If you want unfunny jokes and a lazy story (the writing's in the same vein as UnEpic if that is somehow your thing) go play The Messenger. If you actually want atmosphere and a surprisingly well-told story to go with your challenging gameplay then play Cyber Shadow.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Oh Cyber Shadow, how were you so much fun to play?  Easy exactly.  This game had the right amount of difficulty, mixed with challenging levels, and an awesome soundtrack.  This is your typical platformer with all the random platforms and flying enemies, but this game has something different.  The special items were fun to play with and mixed perfectly with the level design.  Hats off to everybody on this team that made this game.  I hope that there is another Cyber Shadow game and it stays in this 8it-ish design.  This game is worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Really incredible gem, I can't believe I postponed buying it for so long because of some of the negative reviews. It's hard, sure, but not insanely hard, every death I felt I deserved, checkpoints are plentiful, you get to learn patterns and feel like you're improving. _childDocuments_.review: First off, after reading some of the reviews I think people miss this key point: because the latter one is a modern game with pixelated graphics, and with CS it feels like the devs actually took NES (Nintendo Entertainment System) engine and made some improvements to it. Don't believe me? Just take a look at the requirements, this game runs on Windows XP and takes 250 MB of disk space. What I'm trying to say here is that the target audience for CS is primarily those who played NES games (tbh we can narrow it down to NG (Ninja Gaiden), not really all platform players. Now, if you haven't lost interest, let's talk about the game.–  I really loved the level design in CS, you get to see all the classic attributes of NES levels like turbines, broken pipes, laser beams etc. accompanied by juicy 8-bit sound effects.–  Do you remember the cool fire ring in NG which lasted for like 10 seconds?  What if I told you that you can have it indefinitely in this game? (well, technically until you get hit 3 times, but still) Or maybe you remember a typical boss attack where they fire a wave at you with their weapon swing – in CS you get to feel how to be the boss and destroy pathetic robots in ranged combat with such waves. And there are more! (yes, your classic extended blade is also there) The weapons add some fluidity to the gameplay and I really enjoyed killing stuff without even touching it in a melee-based game.–  As soon as you get all movement abilities the game starts feeling differently: I could get to any visible point on the screen or I could speed up and dash through levels ignoring most of the enemies. In short, you get the control of the map and total flexibility. Sounds awesome, however this only happens somewhere in the second half of the game and I would love to play more levels with maxed out mobility skills.–  You can’t squat in this game, which at first was extremely underwhelming to notice. This means that you can’t miss hitting an enemy or projectile as long as you are facing them no matter how small or close to the ground they are and as a result you expect some simplifications to the gameplay. Actually, I stopped noticing this limitation quite soon and didn’t feel much inconvenience about it. Another thing to mention is button combinations, which aren’t just complementary abilities that add gameplay variety, but sometimes are crucial to your level progression. Playing on gamepad I was mostly OK with them, but they may be trickier to exercise on a keyboard.–  There are 2 types of bosses in CS: human-like cyborgs and immobile security systems (actually there is one more but he’s quite unique). Regardless of the boss type, most of the time you get to fight in trivial arenas with walls being your only recourse to maneuver and dodge stuff. No platforms, spike sections or just anything to make them look less boring. Speaking of boredom, the way human-like bosses rotate around you is so simple that you rarely need more than 1 or 2 attempts to kill them. Not to mention that they look pretty much alike.–  There are special items hidden across the game in some challenging areas that increase your HP/SP. As soon as I got maxed out HP I felt too OP for that level of difficulty, because now I could simply facetank bosses attacks and burst them down fast enough before my health runs out. I’m glad that the game rewards me for my curiosity but such large HP bar was overkill. You could say that I should change difficulty level, but I absolutely hate being forced to unlock it by finishing the game on the easier one!–  The plot constantly revolves around this Master-of-the-clan-girl, who is obviously much stronger than you and could solve any problem in no time it’s just too bad that she’s ill right now and you are left to cure her (and clear all the mess by the way). Our character doesn’t have a single line throughout the game, so I’m not even sure whether he actually has human will or was just a dummy following orders. Then, you get a scripted scene where he gets beaten up to 1 HP and hurled like a tin can. Of course we take revenge later, but don’t see his reaction to defeating the foe as if it was just another random boss. Finally, the ending – I don’t know whether he had actual intentions and achieved his goal, but in general just feel kinda sorry for this guy…Overall, I think this game is a great tribute to NG and I can definitely recommend it to all retro gamers out there. From this POV I would rate CS at , it’s really a great nostalgic game. For the rest, well, this is a project of smaller scale than the Messenger and can appear to have more trivial gameplay, so I’ll lower my grade to .

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of 2D platformers like Ninja Gaiden and Shovel Knight, I feel that you will like this game.The asthetic is well done and I love the chiptune soundtrack and 8-bit look. However, I think the designers may want to revisit the basics of the gameplay. The checkpoint system doesn't really make sense and somehow comes off as less fair than the classic 8-bit games of yesteryear. I feel that they could have at least let you die a certain amount of times before being forced back to a checkpoint. That, or making the checkpoints less far apart. There doesn't feel to be a good merihari between sections of a level so it lowers the overall cohesiveness of the experience.In addition, the gameplay mechanics lack a lot of functionality that you would expect from a game like this such as ducking and faster movement. The mechanics that it does have going for it are introduced too slowly and have the opposite effective of making you question why they weren't accessible from the outset of the game. Add to that, that some of the ways to use said skills seems very counter-intuitive and annoying to pull off, which wouldn't be as bad if you weren't constantly tested on working out the annoying control mechanics.Overall, this game as more of a real game of the area aesthetic and gameplay feeling than the Messenger in my opinion. However, the Messenger perhaps outshines this in the long game with more variety and progression towards the end.On my scale of :(1)   Garbage     (2)  Bare playable      (3) Fun time-waster      (4)  Great fun    (5) MasterpieceI rate it a 3 out of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow joins Axiom Verge in the unique realm of indie games that are a retread that offers nothing new, but a very high-quality retread. Albeit with a few asterisks.As far as the basics go, the game is flawless. The movement is fast and snappy, whilst stil evoking the NES-era heft. The combat starts out simplistic, but gets very complex and fluid as you go through the game, with excellent feedback to punctuate successful hits. Enemies are well-designed and varied, especially the bossfights. Levels with good gimmicks, catchy music - basically all of it...Except for the many, many little nitpicks. Most of which stem from the game trying too hard to be an NES game. Insta-kill spikes, an insistence on doing everything with 2 buttons, powerups that break when you get damaged, long segments over deathpits with sparse checkpoints in between. Basically, all of the old design tropes that no one misses. At times, their prevalence can add up to being quite annoying, so steel your patience when you play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is in many ways a true homage to the NES classics of old.That is to say: This game is hard as hell if you're not used to the genre. I've never been great at platformers but I thought this one looked neat so I gave it a try. What came next was 12 and a half hours of pain. At the end I felt really satisfied as I watched the final cutscenes play out.Luckily, unlike it's NES inspirations, this game has no life system and has checkpoints that kind of double as shops. These quality of life improvements definitely help make the game's difficulty managable. Though, it's worth mentioning that the checkpoints have spacing issues at times, especially around the halfway point in the game.Difficulty aside, this game's controls are incredibly smooth and fun to play with, especially once you've unlocked all of the attacks and movement options. Pogo-ing off of enemies or dashing through a full room without touching the floor is insanely fun and satisfying to pull off. Getting to those badass moments of ninja awesomeness made the frustrating, NES style difficulty worth the struggle.The pixel art and music are also really well made. Each level looks amazing and is accompanied by a fantastic selection of music. The Apparitor and Subject Alpha boss themes are definitely highlights of the soundtrack in my opinion. I'd definitely buy the soundtrack if they put it up for sale.As for the story, it's kind of basic. The sales pitch/description here on Steam is more or less what you get. It's nothing genre defining or mind blowing. I feel like the narrative definitely suffers from the game's length. There's only 10-11 levels and it can be beaten in 7 hours or so on your first run if you're good at the game. The characters didn't get a lot of development and some are introduced randomly in one chapter and dropped the next (I'm looking at you, motorcycle lady). I didn't mind it, but if you're looking for a rich, narrative driven experience then this probably isn't for you.The worst part of this game, in my opinion, is probably the enemy design. The visual designs are fine and the bosses are pretty good, but I hate those stupid green and purple robots that fly off screen and then swoop back in and try to knock you into an instant death spike pit (I have no problem with the instant death spike pits on their own, but the knockback from the enemies sucks). It doesn't help that as the game goes on they not only appear more and more frequently, but their damage is also tripled by the end so their projectiles deal 3 points of damage per hit.Overall, I'd rate Cyber Shadow a solid 8/10. It was definitely an enjoyable and challenging experience that's only slightly held back by questionable enemy/level design and pacing issues. It was well worth the 20 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Long back, I saw this guy making a post on Twitter about making this game. Just to imagine all this was mostly done by one guy, is nuts. Nicely done Aarne "Mekaskull" Hunziker.Cyber Shadow is another throwback to Ninja Platformers on NES. This game starts slowly with a basic jump and attack. As you tread ahead, the player is rewarded with abilities that makes the game more accessible and difficult. The game throws nicely crafted levels that encourages the use of the recently granted ability. Once all the abilities are collected, the game amplifies the difficulty to a point, it feels like a decent challenge. Since, being a homage to NES, the game functions only on 2 buttons along with the navigation keys(d-pad/wasd). Sadly, the story was not well written/executed to have a proper emotional impact the way it intended to.   The style of the game is frantic, with various enemy units having varied weakness/patterns and gauntlet like levels for platforming. The pixel art is very well done, you'll notice great use of distinct palettes through the levels. I personally like the transitions of indoor areas to open areas, like from cool animated Background tiles to multiple parallax Background accompanied by lightning strikes, It sets a great narrative and technical tone to it. The music artist Pentadrangle (Enrique Martin) along with some assistance by Virt (Jake Kaufmann) made a kickass Medley for the game, which I'm still waiting for public release. I am a big fan of Ninja Gaiden series, and the way Temco parted from the game was pretty sad as a legacy. And then, I get to witness games like Cyber Shadow that proves, there is still a huge space for these abandoned ideas and styles/aesthetics to be discovered/re-imagined. There are 11 levels and a fair amount of secrets to keep you engaged after completion, and with nicely crafted mechanics it has a great take on speedrunning too. I give this game a 4/5.
