_childDocuments_.review: Its been a little over a week since release and even though i beat it the weekend of the release I just wanted to give it sometime before I touched up on my review. Some key points you should know going into this game especially if you aren't super familiar with a lot of platformers in general.This game is advertised as being fairly fast paced it isn't. Unless you are a pro with these kinds of games, its fairly slow and methodical taking your time in various unfamiliar segments is definitely the better option. There are a lot of lazy (cheap) deaths that really just involve you getting knocked into a bottomless pit and falling to your death especially if you are playing the game too fast. The controls are fairly simple but a little frustrating to master. The game uses this archaic method of combining single button presses with directional button presses. Probably fine if you are used to this or are playing on a keyboard but can be frustrating with an Xbox controller or any controller with a joystick for that matter. Nothing seems to be more frustrating then falling to your death because you didn't properly execute a move you swear up and down that you did.Being a fan of the Mega man X series and never actually playing Ninja Gaiden, I would say this game plays more similar to Mega Man x or Mega Man x2. It actually felt like I was playing as zero most of the time from said series. In terms of difficulty I would say it is definitely on par with Mega Man styled games. I feel like the game feels more difficult from the beginning and feels like it gets easier the more upgrades and moves you get even if some are difficult to get the hang of at first.The music and visuals are great, I love the way the game looks and sounds, I love the story even if it consists mainly of reading. I think the only thing that might deter anyone from finishing or even playing this game is the difficulty. I wouldn't recommend jumping into this if you've only ever played something like Super Mario world because it will definitely put your skills to the test. As far as the length of the game goes. It took me about 17 hours to beat it and I pretty much combed through every nook and cranny I could and I died 655 times. So not really a game I'm used to so realistically this game could be beat well under 7 hours which makes it fairly short. But I think it's well worth the price especially if anymore content comes out of this.

_childDocuments_.review: <SPOILERS AHEAD>So after beating the game for the first time I can say this is 100% worth your money. There were plenty of emotion in this story like in the motorbike level where you have to ride a sentient motorbike that turns out later to be a friend that you knew before you died in the beginning of the game. Then they die to the appirrator who they were also friends with. The ending is also bittersweet with shadow, the player character, joining the master in the ethos, the games afterlife, and the world being safe.  My only gripe with this game is after you get the sprint mechanic. It suffers from what I call, Mighty Number 9 Syndrome, essential after the sprint/sprint dash you become an incredibly fast and lethal machine (pun intended) but the levels sometimes demand slow platforming making some abilities useless. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Beautiful graphics, great music, responsive controls and amazing game play with some small quirks.Although some people seem to think that the game is too difficult, I disagree. I did find it challenging at times but never unfair. What helps is to take your time learning how to use your abilities properly and having some patience. While it's an action game the trick is often to go a bit slower and navigate the levels carefully instead of just rushing into things and end up getting overwhelmed.The graphics and music in the game are just outstanding and the sound effects are great too. Each level has its own theme and atmosphere with new enemies to fight and you regularly get new abilities and items that change up the way the game plays. Those all make for a varied game that never gets boring. Sometimes after having cleared an area of enemies I even end up lingering for a while before moving on, just to admire the beautiful pixel graphics and listen to the catchy chiptunes.The difficulty generally ramps up at a good pace and while there are some spikes (literally and figuratively) including certain areas where save points are a bit far apart, with additional tries you quickly improve and soon breeze through parts which may have seemed almost impossible at first. The bosses in the game are varied and really fun to fight. Some of them are challenging for sure, but every time one kicks my butt I can't wait to have another go and try a new slightly improved strategy. You never have to run far to get back to the boss after dying, which takes away a lot of the frustration it might have caused otherwise.The controls are super simple and responsive, you can do everything in the game with just the d-pad and two buttons. This doesn't mean that the moveset is limited though, just implemented in an effective way. By pressing certain directions in combination with the attack button or by double tapping you can unleash a bunch of special attacks and moves. The smooth controls make it a real joy to run, jump, wall climb and dash through the levels. I noticed that every time I died it was because I did something wrong and not due to the controls failing me.The story can be a bit confusing and information is sparse in general, especially when it comes to the new skills and abilities you acquire throughout the game. I do appreciate not having to read through a lot of text (heh, ironic) and it can be rewarding to get to experiment and find out things by yourself, but I would appreciate a bit more information about pickups and upgrades when you get them.Outside of speed running, finding 100% of the items and getting all the feats, replayability is a bit lacking. But this is mostly just a comment on how much fun the game is and that I wish there was more of it. Hopefully some additional modes like new game+, boss rush etc will be added in the future.Yacht Club Games had already proven themselves as great developers and with Cyber Shadow they've shown that they're excellent at finding great games to publish as well. I can't wait to see what they and MekaSkull will come up with next!In conclusion, although it's a bit early to say, this might very well end up being the best game of the year for me. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game after having owned it for a few days and after playing The Messenger, it was nice to get another classic Ninja Gaiden-ish kind of platformer to enjoy. The story and setting is rather interesting if a bit light but that is hardly a problem when the focus of the game was readily to give the player a challenging ninja platformer. The ending, without spoiling anything, makes me think that perhaps we will have a sequel or perhaps DLC episodes using other characters, much like how Shovel Knight gave you the chance to play as some of the boss characters.The Feats grants replayability as you need to complete specific actions in the game either against bosses or pulling off some specific action at one point or another. The difficulty overall felt right as you can technically control it with the check points usually granting you a full health recovery but an optionnal, purchaseable SP and special item to help you out. Speaking of special items, I like that they are semi-permanent as they are only lost when you take 3 hits after collecting them so playing well means you keep your powerup longer.Graphically, the game definitively has a NES feel to it with the options even allowing to simulate CRT and even the "ghosting" effect from bad wiring. There was never any confusion as to what could be interacted with or stood upon as well as clear indications of enemy projectiles and such.Control wise, it may feel a bit stiff at first but as you progress, your expanding arsenal of abilities and weapons makes the whole of it much more enjoyable. The option to allow a double tap dash is welcome althought it can be a bit tricky to enable if you are going to use the later deflection skill that requires you to tap towards a projectile as it comes close to you and accidentally send you into a sprint.I finished the game in about 6 hours and one of the feats is to finish it under 3 but that would mean skipping most hidden paths and powerups that you can come back for in earlier levels. I intend to replay it to finish collecting all powerups in my finished file but perhaps attempt that 3 hour run.In short, a very good game for its price, especially if you have played such titles as Ninja Gaiden on the NES or, more recently, The Messenger.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorta has the feel of those older Nintendo Natsume platformers... it's more Batman than Ninja Gaiden, but that's fine, controls are very tight and you've gotta worry about your hitbox more since you can't just kill everything in one swing.  Music is a bit of a rollercoaster, I've gone from not liking several tracks to enjoying them a lot on repeated listens.  At the end of the day, at worst it fits the aesthetic most of the time, and at best there's some bangers on the tracks for sure.Once your big dumb brain simmers down, honestly a lot of the boss encounters are maybe a bit too easy, but the platforming is solid.  Probably my biggest gripe is the last powerup you get, feeling like it should have been given a LOT earlier because it makes the game a LOT more fun to play around with.  But I'll leave it at that.  Good game!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a well-made game. A real nostalgia trip.It's also mostly a rhythm game where you memorize everything and then breeze through. After getting the Dash Slash you skip as much of the levels as possible, then memorize the boss pattern and repeat until you're done.I would wait for a steep sale to purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Ninja Gaiden + Hagane + Shadow of the Ninja. The creators of this game knew what they were doing, and they did it majestically. There's nothing more satisfying than powering up your character and using his abilities in battle while unveiling the story of this game delivered through a compelling narrative at every step of the journey. If you liked any of the games above, finished The Messenger and got left craving for more ninja action, this is a definitive grab.Beware though, as this game is as challenging as its inspiration. You will die. A lot. And you need to learn from your mistakes in order to get through. But once you do, the game rewards you in spades.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing.Great platforming, amazing pixel art, ambience and a cool soundtrack that fit the game.  Do not expect another Shovel Knight (only share publisher) or a new Ninja Gaiden (only share some inspiration and the way that cutscenes are presented). This game has its own identity. I played on linux (Pop_OS)  and with a Logitech pad.

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is a game that takes inspirations from the 8 bit nes era classics. A few of the games people have drawn comparisons from include the likes of Castlevania Mega Man Ninja Gaiden  shadow of the ninja while having the esthetics of the nes batman game. While the game does draw most of it's inspirations from the games mentioned above i have also found that the developer Mechanical head has also payed homage to games such as Ducktales in particular the level in which the player chases the games villains Magica and Glomgold  up a mountain to retrieve scrooges treasure in this case however the 2 baddies are replaced by a monkey who rewards you with one of your ninja abilities. Now that we've got all the  nostalgia out of the way some of the the more modern touchs that have been addedi include checkpoints which save your game when touched and can also allow you to purchase helpful items with the essence currency that you pick up and there is also some very nice modern graphical enhancements that the nes was not capable ofback in the day. Having played this game for a few days now i  have to say i am impressed with what i have played so far and felt i had played enough to warent giveing this review. For my final thoughts I can't recommend this enough as I am so happy to see that  although older in style these games still have a place in 2020 and are recieving much love in the way of modern enhancements. I would also like to give a shoutout to Yacht club games for picking this up and allowing this one man dev team to realize his vision and  get his work out on more platforms. I can't recommend this nough if you like old school 8 buit games pick this up
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Cyber Shadow is a hard but fun game. A lot of negative reviews say it's too hard, which I think is a bit unfair. It is a challenging game for sure, but defeating a boss you're stuck on for several attempts is very rewarding. The story and lore are also great, and give character to the world. Overall, It's great fun, as long as you are accustomed to the combat difficulty of metroidvanias like Hollow Knight, and the platforming difficulty of games like Celeste.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend, but with qualifications. It's a 5-10 hour game depending on your skill level, and if you're looking for something ninja gaiden like and a mix of shovel knight (even though not the same developer, just publisher) this is an excellent choice. Keep in mind it's more on the ninja gaiden side than it is on the shovel knight side.Less platforming compared to shovel knight. 8-8.5/10. Anything below are just my thoughts on some aspects of the game after finishing it. Controls: Extremely tight and it feels great to move around 10/10. Never got annoyed by wonky physics or strange hitboxes. You mess up it's on you. Only nitpick is parrying (acquired later). The timing feels a bit inconsistent for the faster projectiles. It's hard to explain until you actually try it.Level design: Had a blast playing through the game, but there was enough odd design (aesthetic/gameplay) choices for the levels that they stick out. You'll have dead ends and empty ledges placed conspicuously that don't lead to any secrets, and often breakable walls are underwhelming. Imagine breaking a wall in castlevania only to find not a pork chop, not a powerup, but a single small heart. To be fair it can be a powerup or secret room, but more commonly than not you'll get that heart. Also the game doesn't challenge you to fully utilize enough of your movement abilities. I.E you get the sword bounce relatively early, introduce some things, and then they kind of forget about making you use most of it in platforming until the last level.Bosses and enemies: Difficulty is good, not too hard where I felt the game was cheating me, and not too easy where I could just attack without caution. Enemy design is mostly great, but I gotta dock points for 'annoying' enemies which mess up the flow up the game, namely the ones that fly in and out of the screen, and the ones that try to stay outside the reach of your sword. The way they sap the pacing is frustrating. Strangely enough the medusa head equivalent in this game was slow enough that it didn't bother me.Powerups and abilities: 2 things here.-Kudos on the abilities and powerups. Both powerups and abilities were all varied enough where I saw use for most of them in combat and bosses. Wish there were more platforming parts that took advantage of the sword bounce and cross slash. Instead cross slash seemed like it was designed for speedrunning. - Head scratcher on special meter usage. Most abilities will burn an SP bar automatically for a stronger version. This would normally be fine, but this includes the sword bounce and upward slash. That means anytime you want to sword bounce or upward slash, you burn an SP bar. You can still use either after running of of SP (they just become weaker), but that means  it discourages you from using those abilities cause other abilities need SP to use (shurikens, cross slash). Should be an option to turn toggle off SP version of upward slash and sword bounce.

_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: I never played Ninja Gaiden but this was a pretty fun game and I enjoyed it! The art-style looks great! The music was pretty banging (I personally never felt it got repetitive unlike a few other reviews have mentioned)! The bosses were fun to learn and destroy (that last boss, WOW)! The movement felt fluid and well paced with increasing mobility through learnt skills throughout the game! Difficulty really spikes towards the end with some punishing checkpoint sections!A few nitpicking things that I would have preferred to be different were mainly in the control scheme.-Double tapping forward to sprint is one. However, there was an option to hold another button while running so I binded it to LB and it made it much better. Although, you have to be moving first before pushing the sprint button which just felt weird. I would have liked being able to hold sprint so whenever I moved I was always running like most games where you have two movement speeds.-Parrying projectiles with the directionals is another. This, AFAIK, could not be rebinded. Using the same button to move also to parry was awful and awkward especially when trying to parry in the air while moving. This easily could have been fixed assigning parry to a bumper or trigger or even just using the attack button on the projectiles at the right timing.-There were maybe just a tad too many sections in the platforming that fell to "Shovel Knight Syndrome" where there was tight platforming mixed with the crazy knockback over pits of insta-death. Therefore, a lot of times when an enemy shoots or flies into you, you most likely will fall and die meanwhile you're at full health. Doing this often in a game to make it more difficult, I don't really agree with. It makes it more annoying and frustrating rather than rewarding and enjoyable especially during the longer checkpoints.Like I said though that's some small nitpicking; other players may have felt these weren't issues but it made a fun game only slightly little less enjoyable for me!Overall Cyber Shadow is a well-done and solid game! If you don't want to pay full price, it'd be a fine grab when it goes on sale! But I feel like I got $20 worth out of it so thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: Cyber Shadow

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting a long while for this game to be released, and it did not disappoint. Rather it blew my expectations!where to begin..  Rock solid - as is a requirement for action platformers. Pacing and ramp up hits the sweet spot and goes from easy-going to almost-frustrating at the end. They all have their own move sets and strategies to defeat. Besides maybe one or two tracks, the music is spot on, and really help enhance the retro feel. beautiful pixel art, the environment needs a special shout out, they really made every level feel unique. It's there, it's alright. I loved it, every second. Though I wish it would've been longer, I think the length of the game works very well, the game sets a fine pace in difficulty and ramp up as mentioned above, and making it longer runs the risk of making areas feel like 'filler'. Hard mode? Yes, please.Sequel? HELL YES! (I'm a huge fan of this genre and retro games in general)

name: Session: Skate Sim
detailed_description: EDITIONS About the Game With the dual stick controls, each stick represents one of your feet. You will need to learn how to control them and transfer weight, just like on a real skateboard. The physics have been developed with a focus on realism, smoothness and immersion. Just like in real life for a new skateboarder, the first hours can seem challenging, but once you have mastered the technique, you will feel the unrivalled thrill of pulling off your very first kickflip! Session: Skate Sim also includes full options customisation, so you can enjoy the perfect experience tailored to you. A full tutorial provides all the help you need to get started, and you can choose from four difficulty levels! Inspired by the golden age of street skating – the 1990s – Session: Skate Sim lets you experience true skateboarding and its culture: no scoring system; just you, your spot and your imagination! There's no need for judges to tell you that your noseslide or varial heelflip are perfect for this spot. And because certain locations are iconic, the developers have added several of them to the game for you to skate in and express your creativity, including Black Hubbas (New York City), Brooklyn banks (New York City), FDR Park (Philadelphia) and many other spots. Skating and pulling off the best lines in the best spots is one thing, but if no one is there to film it, it didn't really happen… In Session: Skate Sim, you can film with a 1990s filter or fisheye lens, and you can use the video editor to create your clips and share them. You can play with multiple options, including changing the field of view, time of day, filters, and different camera views (tripod, orbit, etc.). Session: Skate Sim also offers the chance to go from skater to filmmaker: pull off your moves then go into film mode to experience the action from the point of view of your camera operator and create the best clip. Show off your style with an extensive customisation system for your skater and skateboard. By completing challenges, you earn money to spend in skate shops. You can find nearly 200 items (hoodies, shoes, caps, T-shirts, trousers, etc.) from top brands, such as Fallen, Zero, GrindKing, Thankyou, HIJINX Net, Antilanta, Roger Skate CO, No-Comply, iDabble and others. You can also customise your skateboard with over 250 parts, such as wheels, trucks and many other components from famous brands like, No-Comply, GindKing, Thankyou and many others. In addition to the design aspect, the components (trucks, riser pads, wheels…) impact the way you skate. Find the right ones for your style and shred the most iconic spots!

_childDocuments_.review: As far as skating goes, this is the most realistic simulation I've ever played. The sound design is absolutely solid, and the controls are incredibly immersive. You'll quickly go from having two left feet to performing extreme flips in quick succession by muscle memory alone. I've only skated casually IRL, but Session feels like the real thing more than any other game I've played, despite still being in its early stages. Devs regularly improve physics and add new maps, and the modding scene has even imported some iconic venues from across the world and SLS. If you want a wild and extreme skateboarding game, you won't find it in Session. But if you want to kick back to some lofi tunes, plan some lines, practice, and really earn every trick you land, then Session is worth your attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Session: Skate Sim

_childDocuments_.review: When Session was announced as a "Skateboarding Sim" I was hoping that's what I would be getting. I love EA Skate. Those games are awesome. My issue was always that everything always felt too easy and I didn't have to try very hard. As someone who's been skating for 20 years, this is what I've always wanted. The controls are difficult but once you spend the time learning them, so satisfying. The game looks great (thanks Unreal 4.0) and the animations are most of the way there. Can't wait to see what this game grows into.
_childDocuments_.name: Session: Skate Sim

_childDocuments_.review: Yes! The controls feel true to the experiencing of skateboarding. This is the kind of game I would dream up in my mind as I played THPS or Thrasher as a kid, wishing there was something more 'realistic' to play. It can be challenging, but that's what's fun about the game; you find a skate spot, you have a trick in mind, and you either land it or fail and try again. Once you land it, it feels satisfying in a way similar to how it feels when you skate in real life. That's pretty cool to pull off in a video game. Recommended to skaters or people who want experience the 'feeling' of skating!
_childDocuments_.name: Session: Skate Sim

_childDocuments_.review: This might be THE BEST skateboarding game in existence. If wanted to fill the skate 3 void, HERE IT IS. If you aren't into skateboarding be forewarned: this game has no obligation to make sense to you, you're likely missing some important ♥♥♥♥ that makes this experience as good as it is for someone like myself. I'm sorry but there are other more deserving games that could be dragged down with your complaints (gta V won labour of love ffs).-anyway-Early access and pretty rough around the edges, riddled with glitches but its still THE BOMB. Asking price is easily justified by the playable map alone.Fleshed out city area complete with pretty much every spot you could want (broolyn banks, yo).No bowl or vert but its not like any of the skate 3 crowd could USE them anyway.. lol.you can customzie clothes, board, change stance, change gender.This game has come far since the early prototype. Controls are insanely detailed compared to Ea's skate series (you will need a controller). In regular stance, one stick controls left/front foot and the other controls right/back foot. triggers to lean on heels or toes and turn. its got everything from 'hold to mutli-flip' (cough 540 flip cough), right down to a manual 'catching' function (which I have yet to try as of writing), even has scoop sensitivity settings.If you don't skate in real life you probably wont understand any of it, it will probably seem really obtuse and counter intuitive with convoluted controls.  IDK what to tell you, trying picking up a board irl? The best I do to explain it is:"This game presents a deeper skating experience grounded in realism rather than the obnoxious parodies of skateboarding presented in pretty much any other videgame you'd care to mention (i can think of 2 that aren't)".  There's some ♥♥♥♥♥ who left a review complaining because the controls are "aweful".. if there is ONE idiot who just doesn't get it, its THAT moron. Now go Switch crook that police set, ♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The foot and board control is challenging at first but amazing once you get used to it. It really feels like you’re street skating. The challenges are also quite fun to do. The game is well optimized and the physics are really good. For example ollie’ing onto rails feels really realistic.The game lacks slightly in the transition and ramp riding area. For example you can’t really pump transitions easily or hit vert and do grabs and that sort of thing. Please give us a mega ramp! :)That being said it’s a great game. If you just want something that feels like real skateboarding and is challenging this is a solid choice.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterpiece for anyone who loves the thrill of skateboarding! This game perfectly captures the essence of skate culture, offering an incredibly realistic and immersive experience. The physics are spot on, making every trick feel rewarding and authentic. The attention to detail in the skate spots, from the gritty urban landscapes to the iconic landmarks, is impressive.What sets Session apart is its deep learning curve, which mirrors the real-life progression of becoming a skilled skater. It's challenging yet immensely satisfying as you gradually master the controls and land that perfect trick. The game doesn’t just hand you success—you have to earn it, which makes every accomplishment feel that much more meaningful.The developers have clearly put their heart and soul into creating a game that honors the spirit of skateboarding. Whether you're a seasoned skater or new to the sport, Session: Skate Sim offers endless hours of fun and creativity. It's not just a game; it's a love letter to skateboarding culture. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a true-to-life skateboarding experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Successfully funded on Kickstarter back in 2017, and is being called the predecessor of Skate 3, Session is an open world skateboarding simulator set in the picturesque city of New York. Explore some of the most iconic places that formed skateboarding in the city, whilst performing various tricks on loads of objects in the world, such as ramps, chairs and pillars When not skating why not chill out at your apartment and watch the best lines you've completed and get a new changes of clothes with a couple of board modifications, thanks to Session vast character customization options. So if your waiting for Skate 4 or just want to ride along and listen to the sound of bricks as your wheels ride over Session is a great pickup!

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a departure from Tony Hawk in an attempt to make a more realistic skate game (and it totally is).  But, lets be honest, the reason we love games like TH is that they are fun.  The real world learning curve to skateboarding is huge, and this game, whilst obviously easier than real life, is still painfully tricky and often quite annoying.  They need to increase the assisted modes further, disable bails, speed up getting back on the board if you bail, make switch simpler, make locomotion and turning better.  Take away all the annoying tedious mechanics, which make things like having to spend 3 attempts to ollie up a pavement, and allow the focus on real tricks to be the fun whilst also embedded in reality, like realistic gravity and realworld combos.

_childDocuments_.review: The game really changed after a couple of years. A couple of years ago I tried this game and it was very unstable. Now after some big updates the game became more solid. Npc's have been added (can be enabled via the pause-gameplay menu). Skate-like inputs are available and you can tweak the difficulty like you want it.  They really went far with this. All we just need is a bit more stability, grabs and multiplayer... and perhaps more skateparks.

_childDocuments_.review: EARLY ACCESS REVIEWLittle bit over 15 hours into the game now, and I'm loving it, and kind of hating it at the same time. I'll start with the parts I'm loving so far. The controls are pretty weird to get used to at first, but after playing with them for a while, I'm really enjoying them. The fact that going into switch ACTUALLY switches your footing controls is pretty wicked! (They're honestly so much better than Skate 3's controls in my opinion)The sound effects are BEAUTIFUL in this, along with the visuals, especially at night. The map is a bit limiting as of the moment, but you can still find some pretty sweet spots to do some skate lines around.Although there's not too much customization as of the moment, one thing that they brought to the table are custom griptapes, which honestly look AMAZING! Why they never bought that to Skate 3, I'll never know.Now to the parts that have been a bit irritating. The skater seems to be EXTREMELY fragile to pretty much anything you tend to even slightly nudge into. Almost anything sends you flying off your board, and even then (from time to time), I'll just randomly fall off my board for no good reason, mainly during a grind that looks PERFECT, I just randomly fall, but I'll go back through and do that same grind the same exact way, and I'll be fine. Ragdoll animations will crack you up at first, but then you just get tired of seeing your skater fall for no valuable reason what so ever.Reverts seem to work a solid 50% of the time. (at least in my experience so far) Sometimes I'll be doing slight adjustments to where I'm going, and BOOM! Instant revert that I never wanted to do, but if I'm trying to do a revert during a trick or manual (I mainly have this happen during manuals), the skater just wants to adjust his board a million times, but no revert. They should maybe change the input for reverts to maybe doing a half circle on the sticks or something instead of having them with the directional inputs of the board? Just so the controls don't mix up the fact that you want a revert and not just minor adjustments to your skateboard's direction. Just a thought.Now this last issue has honestly been drawing me AWAY from the game, and honestly makes me want to drop it until this gets fixed. There's currently a bug in-game that messes up your camera angle to where the camera is pretty much only showing your feet (unless you jump, but reverts back to showing your feet), and makes it to where you can't do anything but run around with the worse camera angle in existence. Can't skateboard or anything, and the only way to fix it is to return to your apartment. I know it's not too major, but it's honestly really annoying when you're trying to record something for said game, and you encounter this so many times (I've had this happen 12 times in the matter of 25 minutes if that tells you how many times this can occur), it makes you not want to continue playing the game. Now if I could at LEAST keep my waypoint to where it was when I returned to the apartment to fix this stupid bug, I'd have no issues, I could INSTANTLY go back to the spot and resume what I was doing before the bug happened, but it's the sad fact that that's not the case. You have to return to the apartment, exit, then go ALL THE WAY BACK to where you were to continue what you were doing, and like I said, this could happen again 5 seconds after you resume what you're doing. I know the game is in Early Access, so it's going to have bugs, I get it, but to release a game with a bug like this is honestly pretty irresponsible on the side of Crea-Ture Studios, especially seeing as to how it literally prevents you from playing the game from time to time.EARLY ACCESS REVIEW CONCLUSIONOverall, I sadly can't recommend this game to anyone while it's in Early Access. Although I love the game for what it is, it's issues hold it back too much as of this time, especially when there's a bug that LITERALLY prevents you from playing the game repetitively, which Crea-Ture Studios definitely NEEDS to patch ASAP!Still excited to see what the future brings to this game.

_childDocuments_.review: What a dissapointment.Bought Session when it was still early access because it showed promise and the Devs seemed to be motivated moving forward, this was in 2021. 1.0 was announced shortly after, which seemed exciting at first...Fast forward to now and to be honest, it's pathetic...- Vert/Transition is basically nonexistent, nice touch adding FDR Park in Philly that you can't do anything with.- Goofy isn't done properly.- Grabs used to be possible, removed on 1.0, never returned.- Every time there is any update, it's a DLC and maybe, if you're lucky, some minor bugfixes- Playing S.K.A.T.E (local Multiplayer) was removed for 1.0- Even though i don't care, Multiplayer will never be a thing...- etc, etcThe point is:They used to have steady updates in EA that were actual improvements, ever since Nacon got involved the Game is basically stagnant and is miles away from being anywhere near complete. Once SkaterXL went downhill i got behind session as the Devs seemed motivated and got burned again. great.Asking 40 bucks (as of right now) for this game is just insane, you may want to get it on sale.Communication with the community seized to be a thing and if you want to get a sense of how mad people are at how the game progressed, take a look at the comments of the developer blogs.if have no idea where the good reviews come from.Even though there is promise in the base system, it won't ever be what was promised nor close to what would be worth 40 bucks.Side Note: Pet peeve of mine and session does it too: Spins accelerate mid air, how/why? that's not how it works.Anyway, if you like Transition/Vert... stay away.If you're into street skating you may have fun with this one but it ain't a finished product and if you see angry comments: Those people waited for certain features for years -as there are no real alternatives at the moment it's frustrating and how they deal with their communityis the cherry on top.The fact that i only clocked in 90 hours in a skateboarding game is a telltale sign that it ain't what it should be, sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good, but it's obviously unfinished. I love the gameplay and it actually feels like skateboarding. My biggest issue with this game is the camera, I haven't seen anyone talk about the problem with the camera. I understand that the game is going for a cool skate filmer style, but it makes gameplay really difficult. The camera needs to be above the character and centered so we can see what's in front of him rather than a side view. The low angle side view has issues with the character literally blocking the view of certain obstacles. I've played around with all the camera settings and the highest angle you can get still isn't good enough. There should be an option to have a camera angle similar to the far angle in skate 3. There are a lot of other issues with this game especially ramp tricks and map design. The ramp physics just don't work and it's really really hard to figure out how to maintain speed by pumping. I've spent a lot of time trying to figure it out, but I just can't get it. The map design is really frustrating as well. There are so many spots that would be really fun to skate, but there's either zero run up so you can't get enough speed to skate it, and some of the spots that are skate-able, there's usually something in the way right as you land so you can't roll away from the trick for more than 2 seconds. I really like this game and I think it has some serious potential and I think fixing these issues will make it much more enjoyable. I don't know if I'm the only one having these issues, but I think it would fix the game. I'm kind of shocked that there's no animation for throwing the board down, you press the button and the board just teleports under his feet? I understand that this an indie game, but this should have been one of the first things they would make. The developers clearly have an understanding of skateboarding and what it should look like, so it's odd they don't have something as basic as that in this game. Overall this game could be the best skate game if some of these fixes are made as well as new additions like multiplayer and custom maps / parks.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest. The reason i bought this game was because I miss the skate franchise and was itching for the feeling that game gave me all those years ago. Unfortunately this just isn't it. The big glaring frustration is the controls. If you don't know, the left stick controls your front foot and the right stick controls your back foot. On paper this doesn't sound too bad but if you played the skate series for hundreds of hours like I have your muscle memory gets in the way of even doing an ollie. Landing any trick was unbelievably frustrating to wrap my head around at first. After about 40 mins into the game I got a better hang of it and was able to make some tricks with ease. Another big issue is the world is empty. No cars. No people. Even the pros you are sent to, to do challenges for don't have a voice actor, so you have to read dialog... The more I played, it seemed the sole satisfaction out of playing the game was the mechanics. But personally for me I didn't get the game because I wanted to play a challenging skateboarding game. I just want to chill and get immersed in a world of skateboarding. Unfortunately this doesn't even come close to scratching that itch.

There are a couple minor bugs here & there & a couple animation details to be filled in as well but nothing I notice too much at all. Oh & yes it is really hard & imagine if you don't have any interest in street skateboarding this game is not for you but to everyone else with the slightest interest, pick it up! _childDocuments_.review: It's almost like the DCS of skateboarding games. MASSIVE learning curve after almost twenty #$#&!!@ years of steering with left stick, ollie/trick with buttons or left stick. However it is proportionally as rewarding as it is challenging. Once you get the hang of it it's not so bad. I feel like any reviews talking about how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the controls are just couldn't wrap their brains around input layout changes and having to form new memory pathways. Also, my money is on them playing with the default settings and *still* complaining about it. Try it on manual board catch, endless spin/scoop. It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HARD yeah, but omg is it fun and rewarding when you get it. It's just like skateboarding. People aren't pulling off 540 body varial laser flips into backside noseblunts on the regular. That is going to take you try after try after try to land. I'll find myself skating around - and there's a TON of maps to choose from included (DLC is okay - nothing spectacular but I got it anyway bc maps.) and finding a rail, ledge, gap, stair set, or line I want to do and try for the silkiest kickflip to bs tailside or just one stylish af crooked grind down an impressive feature. It's just relaxing and fun. It can be frustrating, but only if you let your emotions control you. The story is.... a feature. I guess. It's not bad per se. But it's not great, either. It does however alleviate the itch when you need something defined to be completed. It will also open up new cosmetics and props as you gain xp and skrilla. Which is nice.The tutorial I found to be tedious and too slow. I made it as far as the fifth lesson maybe before I exited and said "I got the basics. I'll figure the rest out." Aaaaand I did. But it was A LOT of failure until I could do things somewhat competently. Flip tricks are easy to get the hang of. Catching the board can be hard to learn but man is it great! Grinds are taking me longer to learn. I have everything on the higher difficulty/manual settings so that's part of it, but even before turning those on I was still floundering for the first hour or two. There's some glitches here and there. You'll go all limp sometimes like one of those toys where you press the underside of the platform and the figurine collapses because you put slack into the strings holding the pieces tight and keeping it upright. Some minor clipping here and there. Nothing that makes it unplayable. I can't imagine the coding that had to go into all this so I'm more than willing to overlook some imperfections; especially with only six devs. Even the most polished AAA games will have their bugs and glitches so don't hold this to some unreasonable standard there as bleed-over rage from your brain too fried from low nutritional value, fast-food gaming to learn something new and that offers a sizeable challenge.I read somewhere where someone called "The Dark Souls of skateboarding games" and that's pretty accurate.This game is a delayed gratification type of game.If you put the time into learning things, you'll be rewarded for it.

_childDocuments_.review: 1.0 Review:This feels like an alpha or a beta, not a full release. The Bad (Controls):- There are bugs that cause your skater to randomly bail, like pushing and trying to turn at the same time.- Random bails happens frequently enough to stop being funny and start being annoying.- Turning the skater feels bad. The triggers are either too responsive, or not responsive enough. Tried both on steam controller and XBox SS controller.- Because turning is bad, aligning for grinds/manuals is really annoying, and extremely challenging.- Popping 0.1s after your front wheels leave the ground causes your skater to bail mid air. This results in many attempts down stairs resulting in your skater rag dolling immediately after takeoff.The Bad (Story)- The story has no voice acting- The objectives sometimes bug out and don't detect when you do the trick, or pass you during a bail.- The story objectives aren't visible during game play, even if you activated a new mission, instead you must pause the game and check your skate log. - City is lifelessThe Bad (Everything Else)- The camera makes it hard to align for grinds. Changing the settings barely helps. It looks good while skating but it's not functional to help you gauge distance.- You get to listen to elevator music while skating. - There is no vert, only street, meaning no grab tricks, or physically flipping the skater.- Impossible (flip trick) doesn't wrap around your foot and instead looks like a 360 shuv.- Game runs worse than BF1 or BF5 on my system yet the graphics are nowhere near as good.- Off board animations look very incomplete and look wonky, like jumping back on board your board literally just spawns underneath your feet regardless of what you were doing- Because running off board makes you immune to obstacle cipping bails (e.g. your skater brushes their knee on a bench and crashes) it's often faster and less annoying to traverse the city on foot as opposed to on-board. In a skating game this is a big red flag!The Good- Most flip tricks and grinds are in the game and their animations are pretty nice- Each trick looks distinct due to skate sim engine- Checkpoint system like in EA Skate is great for sessioning a spot- Character customization is adequate - Novel flip trick controls feel fun and rewarding when things work correctlySummary:Wait for significant sale, and for significant updates. The current game is okay at best when everything works out, and you're spamming a trick you want to land at a spot until it works and you feel good about it. However everything outside of that gameplay loop is severely underdeveloped and it shows. The potential is there but this is far from a 1.0 release in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I really like this game and understand that it is still very much so a work in progress however very much still playable and for this reason I would most likely recommend this game. That being said, the current version of this game is pretty rough around the edges.The biggest problem with this game currently is the fail physics. They are so sensitive to the point where the character will seemingly randomly fall even on a simple ollie on flat ground which in theory, you shouldn't be able to fail. This becomes very jarring to the natural dynamic of the game especially in combination with many ridiculous corpse launches and poorly placed obstacles. When the game will recover you from the fail if you were say attempting a grind, it will spawn you on the ground almost immediately next to where you fell facing the obstacle as well as being unreasonably close to it to the point that even turning the board will make fall again, forcing you to get off the board to continue without having set a waypoint and resetting. Often when grinding, the character will start off grinding as intended and then flip to the side and grind parallel with the grind, obviously resulting in yet another corpse launch. The waypoint mechanic is pretty similar to that of skate 3 which I like as it was well designed, however, resetting will absolutely make my game drop frames which if you set off again pretty much guarantees a random corpse launch. Also, interacting with quarter pipes is pretty grizzly, just not really enjoyable at all. The game doesn't know what to do with the character and pretty much the only thing you can do successfully just rolling into one head on without falling is a flat spin and it will kill all of your momentum as you roll back down which is a bit counter intuitive.The next and really only other big problem I have with the game is the level design, not that it is bad because it looks great and there are definitely good spots littered around the place to skte. There are a lot of spots that look like great spots to skate and otherwise would be but are a constant fight with the collision mechanic and impossible to gain momentum because it's either at a weird angle, in or leads directly to a corner, or is just simply over crowded with decorations and ledges. The maps that aren't the main one you spawn in can feel pretty barren to skate and like a big missed opportunity, they look great but spots never really line up again and they can be pretty small or empty in parts.This more feed back to the devs than a review but if you have a bit of patience, this game is a great little time waster to fill in gaps between games or if you're waiting on something.

_childDocuments_.review: Session can be as frustrating as skating in real life. Sometimes tricks come quick and easy, other times it takes a lot of tries and emotion. Session can also be very rewarding as skating can be in real life. It is a sim, and it is a very good one. Controls take time to get used to (especially using triggers to turn), but once you figure it out this how the game is supposed to be played it all clicks and works. The amount of changeable gameplay settings is really amazing, you can fine tune so many aspects to tailor how it is you want to experience the game. The maps are awesome with classic golden east coast skate spots. Good game so far and each update improves the quality. Definately worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Session: Skate Sim

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down the best skateboarding game (sim). Easily. I can’t believe it was made by only a handful of people. The amount of care and love put into is unmatched, and you can tell us made for skaters by skaters. Be been replaying skate and skate 3 for like a decade now and now I finally have a new game that I think I’ll be replaying into the next 10 years. They continue to support the game and listen to the community. You can talk to the devs in the discord and actually get insight into why the mechanics are the way they are and sometimes even insight into what’s coming next. The dual stick controls are hands down a must for any realistic skate game going forward imo. That’s just the start those. Mechanics like side pop, board to body distance, flip/scoop desync , board pitch , ect are just not going to be found anywhere else. This level of customization makes the game for me and it’s why it takes the cake for me. Loving the transitions mechanics they just added and can’t wait to see what’s added next. Don’t get me started on the replay editor. It’s just godly. The graphics are already amazing but man does it shine with the right filmer. I’ve been addicted to making edits for years now, way before 1.0 and I don’t see it stopping anytime soon. My edits   Does the game have some rough around the edges? Sure , without a doubt but you can’t tell me the devs don’t improve more and more update after update. They haven’t missed yet imo . I put a thousand hours into the game long before 1.0 and long before console release. I gotta be sitting close to 3k now if I combine my pc , Xbox and ps fine. That’s more than I could have asked for. Way more than my moneys worth. Imo this game is 9.5/10 as is. Anything they add , any bugs they fix that’s just extra. This game is top tier and as a skater who started skating in 2000 (I know it’s “set” in the 90’s) this game hit home and captured a HUUUGE part of my life perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Before being acquired by Nacon this looked like a promising successor to the skate series, or something close. Now it seems they have severely limited the scope of this project in order to reach a release date, which is reasonable considering they had piss poor update pacing and community interaction throughout the early access period. This being a niche title you'll find a ton of ardent defenders on the boards telling you how they haven't scrapped much if anything, and that you just don't get it. I enjoyed this title for maybe one hour of playtime, the rest was dealing with bugs and immersion breaking physics problems. I want this title to succeed, but it is looking like another early access title that will go from positively reviewed to mixed or negative at launch because of the disillusionment many will experience when the devs announce they are done supporting the project.Edit: As of 5/30 the devs have stated that they are cutting grabs and vert, both meant to be ready for June, from the final version of the game. They also implied that post launch support and the addition of these core features will be conditional to sales, But the suits deciding to cut features instead of themselves like to skate so they are super cool dudes.Edit 5/10/22 :Another year, and there has been exactly one post release hot-fix, and cosmetic DLC. Nacon can't even support developers that hold on to lucrative license deals like Warhammer or WRC, all because of their parasitic treatment of developers where development time is always conditional on income from monetization schemes that are equal parts aggressive and lazy. This game had potential, and the developers struck a deal with the devil. Its an easy filter for me now to just avoid anything that has the misfortune of being published by these leeches.

_childDocuments_.review: So after 2 hours of playtime, this is what I've thought about Session. (My views could change over time, but I'm pretty solid in how I feel about this).Session is a skater's dream sim, but it could use a little work in a few areas. One thing I noticed through my play through was that my skater seemed to be pretty slow, especially when on a flat surface just pushing the board. Even going downhill, I still feel a little sluggish, but that's all my complaint on the speed and what-not. Next thing is the turning, which is the one thing I can say I don't really like. I played on a Nintendo Switch Pro Controller, so I should've seen this coming. My issue (along with other reviewers from what I've seen) is that the trigger turning is too sensitive, no matter what setting I put it to. I constantly revert and it ruins a lot of the lines I try to skate.Now onto the actual stick controls, I've been actually slowly falling in love with them. I played the Skate franchise since 2010, and it was a struggle at first to get used to two sticks instead of one. After my first hour or so, I was starting to get used to it. Map is nice, music is pretty alright too, just not my cup of tea.So in the end, if you're looking for a game like Skate 3, DO NOT LOOK HERE. If you wanna just have a nice, realistic skate sesh, this is the one for youBiggest Complaints from me: Player speed, trigger turning

_childDocuments_.review: This is not Tony Hawk Pro Skater or Skate 3. But a new type of skate sim that can be very fun if you give it some time. Like real skateboarding it will be hard at first, but very rewarding when mastered. Watch a few Youtube tutorials to learn the basics mechanics. First few hours just cruise the streets and do simple ollies nothing more. The fancy looking tricks aren't hard at all to learn. Its the timing and ability to judge distance and speed while riding. That will help you progress the fastest. The down sides are the game as of version 1.0 is still incomplete. But its much further along in development. And you can tell the developers really care and want to support the game for a long time. If you are unsure or little intimidated by the learning curve maybe wait for a sale. Then give it a try. I think this game is going to be future  of modern twin stick skateboarding games.

_childDocuments_.review: Sesion is an early access skateboarding game being developed by Creature studio, much in the same vein as the EA skate series. Currently a section of New York is playable, with a few skate-parks included with some notable landmarks; such as the Brooklyn banks. Music Stations are also available in game, which adds some great ambience, all that is missing is pedestrians and traffic to make the world feel more alive.Moving on to the gameplay, the game requires a controller to play, with multiple control schemes available to the player, such as those similar to the skate series. The player can make a variety of tricks including pop-shuv-its, heelflips, and grinds such as salads and five-o’s. The map is big enough at the moment, some of the content is a bit bare bones at this current time, however the developers have stated they plan on implementing new features over time, hopefully making the game more complete.There are many character customisation options, such as clothing, boards and decks, even including a few pro-skaters and ribs-man. Session is becoming a fine title every update, I would recommend it if you are a fan of skateboarding. I would suggest waiting if you are not a huge fan, depending on how the development turns out. Session is current available for £15.49/$20 on steam.Rating: 8/10 (If a skateboarding fan) ; 6/7 (if not a fan)

_childDocuments_.review: i played a bit of skater xl and was unimpressed. tricks felt kinda floaty and unsatisfying, but i came to the conclusion that the lack of controller rumble is what gave skate 3 the extra weight that made it feel so much better, so i expected session to be the same.my friend who loves this game gifted it to me and now i know that rumble had nothing to do with it, sxl just doesn't feel great imo. tricks in session are just as satisfying and weighty as skate 3. and you can't just fling the sticks around haphazardly to flip the board all over the place like in sxl, you really gotta focus to land a trick.biggest cons for me rn are player animations and the tiniest bump flinging you off the board, sometimes at the same time, especially in grinds. i'll enter what looks like a solid grind and then suddenly my board and skater start flying in opposite directions, making it hard to tell what exactly went wrong. it also seems like the board needs to stop flipping an unnecessarily long distance from the rail for the grind to stick, but maybe that's a camera perspective issue. overall i'm impressed how polished this game is considering luckily most of my gripes seem to be improved in the upcoming update, along with a whole lot of other improvements and new features, so i'm pumped for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Creature's still gotta iron out some bugs. More come with every update, but this game has a BIG future as the skateboarding game for skateboarders. The animations look great, the maps are nostalgic and super fun to skate, and the overall aesthetic of Session makes the other skateboarding games look corny.At first, I had my troubles with the control scheme, but when I locked that muscle memory in, i realized how much skill expression is possible. Your inputs determine EXACTLY how your board flips, how its caught, where your trucks land on the ledge, how you spin and revert out. I have spent hours grinding the same couple ledges because (aside from the bugs) it gives me the same feeling as irl skateboarding.At $40 though? I would hold off. I picked it up for a lot less when it was in early access. Either wait for it to be polished or wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to love and little to hate. For me at least. Of course a lot of people want grab moves added from what i hear, i'm sure it's a future plan for them. Skating vert in this game is difficult for me, but i can agree it seems lack luster. I'm assuming it only gets better though from here. I mostly enjoy street skating so this game really fills that description for me. At first the learning curve made things pretty dang tough. Steering with the triggers was just the most awkward thing i've done haha, but l after a while i got the hang of it and things smoothed out. Though i still catch myself trying to steer with the stick sometimes*EA Skate brain*, there are control settings that make the gameplay more like skate, but i dug the challenge and stuck with original settings. With the added "manual catch" option on it makes landing tricks that much more rewarding. That's a big part that I love about this game, the difficulty can get to you at times, but landing tricks is a very rewarding payout. Landing them clean? Oh man!There is a storyline that you can follow to gain EXP and Cash rewards* or you can just be free and go skate the streets or a few skateparks**. There are also challenges you can complete while skating around. I honestly haven't paid attention to the reasoning for the EXP but I'm assuming it's probably to unlock more gear or maybe it goes towards growing sponsors? idk. You do get alright cash payouts to go purchase gear and even purchase drop items. Drop items being ramps/rail/etc that you can just plop down and make your own skate spot. Very nice feature.    *So before the board breaking update, getting a ton of cash together was ALMOST pointless. ALMOST. Obviously there is tons of gear to buy, but now cash management almost plays a role in the game, which is sort of cool. Your board after a while of skating around gets inherently weaker, depending on how hard you skate, and will eventually snap. That board and grip are gone, your trucks and wheels you had on that board are not. You'll need to go back to a shop or your apartment to get a new board. You can buy a stock of boards to keep at your apartment, and you can just fast travel back there to get a new complete together or you can just hold the respective button to instantly get a blank deck/grip (with your trucks and wheels from the broken board). THIS to me makes for an almost cash management aspect and why i say cash seemed almost worthless to me before. Idk if that point will hit everyone, but I mean c'mon, real life right there lol. All-in-all i love this feature, because it adds to the Sim. There are a ton of settings and even "experimental" settings to mess around with to absolutely tweak the gameplay. You could make it super arcade-like or make it even more Simulation-like increasing the difficulty and ultimately getting that sweet sweet "i f***ing landing it!" payout.   **It would be awesome to see more of these, i'm sure it's in the works. More than likely will be DLC stuff. Maybe, maybe not. I'm fairly happy with what i already got in front of me lolThere is tons i could probably drone on about. A big thing i would love to see is to be able to skate with some friends or maybe have a lobby to where you can skate with others. I think that would really add a huge level of fun and obviously still add a lot to the Sim aspect of this. These are things they more than likely think about as a dev team. If we show a ton of love and support to them what do you think we will get in return dudes? Yep, this awesome game and tons of future improvements <3All together i absolutely love this game and hope to only see it grow immensely in features and detail! Enough of this, let's go SKATE!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a skateboarder for about 16 years now. I've been playing skateboard games for just as long. Big THPS fan and later on down the road I picked up EA Skate for the realism "simulation" aspect of those games. When Skater XL came out I quickly turned to that and started filming videos using the in game video replay editor. Skater XL allowed me to let my imagination go wild and create the skate videos of my dreams. Any video editing skills I have to this day are purely because of that game and I am thankful for all the fun it has given me. I purchased Session the day it was launched on Steam and immediately saw all the potential it had. While I have to admit the learning curve of this game really did turn me off, over 40 hours of this game (which really isn't a lot) has showed me what this game really is... a true skateboarding simulation. Us OG Skater XL fans tend to forget that the game we are playing is nothing like the REAL game itself. I watch videos people on consoles make vs what we make on PC and cringe often forgetting that they are using what they are given whereas we have awesome people in the community creating features just to make the game what it should've be in the first place. What blows my mind is that Session has not only given most of these features to console and PC players, but they have also given us things we didn't even know we wanted like more customisation options and screen filters that are just awesome. I plan on sinking many more hours into this game and am excited to figure out more of what it has to offer. Thank you crea-ture Studios for not only making a game for some of the community, but for the whole community. Good luck on future updates and keep on doing what you're doing. We appreciate your passion. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a fun skating game that will make you feel like you've actually learned to play the game, then this game is for you!There is a fairly steep learning curve at the beginning. The mechanics may be a little frustrating or confusing at first until you do them over and over again and find the logic in them. Once you've mastered them, you feel so good! You start nailing tricks and lines better than you ever thought possible. The game truly rewards you for sticking with it.The maps are fun to skate with a plethora of different rails, stairs, gaps, ramps, etc to test your skill. While I wouldn't consider the maps gigantic, I'm still finding little things tucked away in corners I never explored which helps keeps things interesting. It all feels nice and cohesive to skate which makes the world feel like an empty canvas that you get to be creative with.Another great thing is the how you can customize your experience. You can adjust your turn speed, flip speed, pop height, push speed etc to really tailor your experience to what you want. Or if you're having trouble in a mission and just need some help, the options come in handy. I would also imagine you can get really crazy with the settings and have some not so realistic fun with them!Although, there are a few negatives. As previously mentioned, the mechanics can be pretty frustrating at first. Another negative can sometimes be the missions. There's been quite a few missions that won't register what you're doing unless you land them or complete them in a very specific way that the game doesn't show or tell. So you end up just doing the same thing over and over again trying to get the game to register that you did what it asked. Most missions aren't like this, but when it does happen, it can be really frustrating.Overall, this game has been a blast to learn and play. I love cruising around looking for spots I haven't skating and trying to come up with new things to try! There are some parts of the game that maybe could be polished more or improved, but I don't find those ruining the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: *2023 UpdateThis is actually really awesome now that the missions are fully structured, even if they  can be ridiculously difficult. The flexibility you have with fine-tuning how difficult/realistic you want your experience to be is really neat. The three areas in the game, even though they are devoid of life, still feel incredibly real and it's fun to just cruise or walk around and find new spots. The recent addition of the experimental board breaking also is still really neat when it happens and gives the wear and tear on the board a lot more importance. If you're into a sim skateboarding game and you have a controller, this is definitely worth checking out finally. It still has a ways to go, but it's pretty neat as-is. I'm hoping vert/transition skating gets a bit more love at some point, but this is still really cool*Updated Review*I'm kind of annoyed with the number of games that have a date set for version 1.0 but it feels like they still have a lot of work to do. This was cool in early access, even if the updates were so sparse, but it's hard to justify calling this "done" considering it feels like there are a lot of missing animations and features you'd expect for a retail product. I prefer the feel of this game over SkaterXL, but both games feel like they're just...not fully baked. It's extra disappointing here because the fundamental gameplay is great when it works, but it sure is annoying trying to nollie down a stair set and for some reason, your skater bails before you even get a chance to because of a clipping issue or getting stuck on geometry. If I could, I'd give this game a mixed review, but because I can't, I'm going to give it a thumbs down. My suggestion is make sure you look into what the game is and watch some videos before picking this up. It's literally a skateboarding sim with a lot of rough edges, but it can still be a lot of fun if you're alright with that.*Original super early access review*A friend sent this to me earlier and I am already in love with this game. I had tried out the early demo and pre-alphas and they seemed neat but like they needed a bit of work in terms of animations and features. Holy Toledo. This totally blew away my expectations for a skateboard sim and it's only in early access! The controls are great once you adjust to them and allow you to do exactly what you want when you want. It looks absolutely beautiful with incredible animations, textures, lighting, etc. The map is HUGE compared to what I was expecting. Yes, it's just this one city, but it's pretty big with a lot of variety, feels like an actual city, everything is scaled appropriately, and you can drop in a few custom pieces here or there to give you even more options. The customization stuff for as early as it is features tons of options, same with the replay editor. Yes, you will still fall over whenever you make contact with anything on your skateboard, and not everything is perfect, but this is a fantastic product with a ton of promise. I really wish the replay editor was explained though, but I'm sure that will happen in the future. In the meantime, if you love skateboard and are interested in a skateboarding sim that is definitely more hardcore, realistic, and rewarding than Skate, you need this in your life.

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive fan of the Tony Hawk franchise and the Skate trilogy, I gotta say this game (along with Skater XL) are slowly making Skateboarding genre within the video game market back to square one. Surely both Session and Skater XL are still Early Access titles for Steam and STILL need updates and new content in order to be allowed on consoles and such, but i gotta say what i've seen from both titles really gets me excited for whats to come next (hopefully a unrealistic skating game like the Tony Hawk games will be next in the future)tho one complaint i'd say from both is how different the controls are compared to the Skate trilogy. like with Session the only time you need to use the left stick is when you wanna do a trick and can only use the back buttons to move around your skater. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game, definitely recommend. Worth $20 even in this earliest state of Early Access. I wish that they would introduce a casual mode that played closer to a Skate game than what it is now. I know the goal was to make this game more of a sim than a casual game, but I feel like there is a massive audience for a game like Skate on PC whereas there is only a small audience for people who want a game that makes it feel like the real difficulty of skating.Skating is one of those things where it takes the best of the best 20-50 attempts and hours upon hours to really hit a perfect line... I don't have time for that. And while I love setting a session marker and trying a line over and over, I'd rather be spending my time trying different tricks to see what looks and flows best through that line than trying 100 times to nail even a short line.Anyway, still highly recommend, but hopefully the devs listen to many of us on the more casual side of the community eventually and create a control scheme where you can use an analog stick to move your skater and the other to do tricks with one hand. Sure, they didn't want to just copy Skate, but Skate did SO MUCH right that it would be no shame to copy a lot of the groundwork they laid.Sorry if this review sucks, drunk af over here my fellow gamerzzzzzz!

_childDocuments_.review: I reviewed this game a couple years ago and gave it a fairly glowing review. Now though? I can't really recommend it anymore. I'll explain why below.I'll break it down to three main reasons: 1. the development team at Creature2. An absolute heaping pile of missing features3. Multiplayer? Never coming. 1. Creature has spent the better of part of two years after their official 1.0 "launch" releasing paid DLC maps and barely noticeable bug fixes for minor issues. In that same time they announced an UE5 re-work (and promptly cancelled it 6 months later), disabled the General chat on their discord to avoid criticism, announced plans to start work on a *different game*, and refuse to produce an actual timeline for basic features that were promised upon launch (transition skating, grabs, plant tricks, throwing board down animation, fixing goofy stance, etc etc etc.) These features have almost been ignored for 15 straight dev updates (minus a vague promise for fixing goofy in the latest one). 2. As alluded to in the first point, FEATURES. This game feels like a development project, not a full-fledged skateboarding game. There's no grabs, no plants, barely functional transition physics, no vert physics at all, no no-complys, (feels like I'm reading the rules to a game of Berric's SKATE). The maps are lifeless and empty, and a decent number of tricks and features have been stuck in "experimental" for over 2 years. It does two things well and that's grinds and flip tricks. That's it. If you only enjoy that aspect of skating then it's not terrible, but if you enjoy the other 70% of skateboarding then this game will feel desperately hollow. 3. Multiplayer? Yeah right. It's never coming, so don't expect it. Feels like a huge swing & miss to not have any plans for a multiplayer mode in 2024, but considering they can't even get the basics right maybe it's for the best. Long story short, don't buy this game. The dev team is just milking it dry with DLC maps until Skate 4 comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: The more i play this the less interested i am in other skating games. I enjoy how realistic Session is. There is no point system, there is no stringing together 20 different moves. Nothing that flashes on your screen telling you you're awesome, its just super chill and rewarding. I'll try something 20 times, and when i finally get it, there is a personal satisfaction - "cool i finally landed that, now to try the next thing."Controls are weird at first, but give it a day and once it makes sense you'll never want to go back to any other skate controls. You'll go thru a phase where you try to figure every trick out, and then a phase where you'll try to do each trick on command. The controls for the item dropper are a little rough but manageable.Graphics are really good. I'd like to see the character textures improved - the diffuse maps are decent, but the normal maps seem really non-existent. The city textures however are insanely good quality in my opinion. Overall the graphics are better than Skater XL's. Sounds are also really good. Again, better sounds than Skater XL hands down. Everything sounds very realistic and true to life.Great game all around and i was looking forward to more updates, but after the 1.0 release, the devs just totally clocked out. Every update after the 1.0 has been WEAK. They do like 1-2 bug fixes, and spend the rest of the time making DLC, using the DLC money to fund this other new game of theirs. Its sad to see that this game has no real future, no roadmap, nothing to get excited over.
