_childDocuments_.review: Wow, Session seems to have the potential to become an outstanding Skateboarding SIMULATION Game.Why uppercase simulation. Because it tries to get really close to simulate how you have to use your two feet to skate, and that is really impressing me after only 20 min. The other 20 min I spent on figuring out how to play it with a PS4 controller (Simply check your settings for controllers!), but its early access so I don't mind.Back to the game, and I don't wanna focus on graphics and performance too much: Runs smooth on an i5 8400, 16 GB RAM and a MSI GTX 970 so far. Graphics look also nice, but there is room for improvement.What impresses me more are the controls, especially when right and left foot are locked (don't change this setting, it's like cheating) and you really need to switch what your left foot/thumb and rigth foot/thumb is doin. I'm skateboarding for over 20 years now and thats closest feeling of skateboarding ever experienced on a contoller so far. It's definitely not easy (as skateboarding isn't for most people, me included ;) ) , it's very different to the EA series, but I think it's a blessing that EA didn't continue Skate and by this opened up the market for some indy dev companies like crea-ture!After getting a bit used to the controls if figured out how to set my stance to goofy, because I simply ride goofy, and then tried tricks I like to do in reality. After getting used to kick and heelflips reg and switch, I got to fs flips reg and switch, and I first really stuggled to get them right. I always turned more than 180. But then it clicked in my head and I figured out you need to catch and stop the rotation to get them clean. [Edit: And you get them really clean when you only press the rotation button smoothly half way down. What a game!] Doin this also switch took me another 3 min, but it was really satisfying. And now I want more - nollie bs flip and fakie fs flip are the next ones.I didn't try Skater XL so far, so I don't wanna compare which game the better skateboarding simulation is. But after the 20 min I can tell you Session ain't easy like the Tony Hawk series or the EA games, and that's what makes it really interesting for me. It's more fun to me to try and learn tricks I want to do instead of clicking buttons and flicking sticks to see my board flip around crazy into the next bs noseblunt slide without effort.So when you love skateboarding and you aren't afraid of having to learn and remember tricks, definitely try Session. I thought it will be more expensive, but 17€ is a real bargain. And when you love skateboarding and want to do tricks very easy, maybe better wait, read some other comments and maybe buy another skateboarding game, because then Sessions simply migth be not the right one for you.Thumbs up to crea-ture, really like what you released as cheap early access game, and hope for more in the next months!

Needless to say you´ll only get wind of it because others are reading their SM channels...they haven´t said a word around STEAM...such a joke of a company...DO NOT BUY!Edit 10292023: set to "not recommended" due to four "updates" and no meaningful progressI deleted my early access review, just so you know I have been playing this game for quite some time and versions.I still think it´s a good game, although it needs improvement in many fields, so don´t expect a fully fleshed out game...it´ll take time.Positives:- new sounds, quite realistic now- new map/city, although I haven´t played that very much at this point...not as optimized as the older maps- highly detailed- historical spots = who did what at these and it´s up to you to redo them - for skatevideo-nerds mostly- unique control scheme, hard to master...and I mean HARD... - clip editor with tons of options concerning "looks" in case you like the corny look of older skating footageNegatives:(no particular order)- very floaty with vanilly settings now, but can be adjusted (mandatory imho)- tricks often do not register on obstacles you need to perform them on for daily/weekly/story challenges- this leads to the player doing the same trick on the same obstacle over and over again until perhaps it registers, hasn´t been that bad in prior versions- mission descriptions are unclear, leaving anyone without intermediate knowledge about skating in the dark, and once you´ve clicked the texts (yes text!) away, there´s no means of looking them up again- a lot of the music got removed without any notice given as to why, not that I miss the screaming noise called punk rock...but still - _childDocuments_.review: LIKE: Difficulty, I do not want to play an easy game, the controls and the requirements to land a trick successfully make it very satisfying when you nail a clean trick. Once you play for some time you will find certain tricks as your go do. If you master a trick, going switch makes it like learning all over again. This is by far one of the most realistic skate games that have ever existed, and you can tell the creators actually care about that. Map, if you are a skate fan, look up these areas and you will see that this game is pretty much dead on when it comes to the layout and feel of the actual locations that exist and existed. Historical trick list is awesome.DISLIKE: I am going to refrain from ranting about mechanics of the game because it is pre release and crea-ture Studios is doing a great job at tuning the issues. Overall the physics and mechanics are pretty good and I am excited to see where the game improves. Some of the grinds get funky, you land tricks going at insane speeds and you get way too much air on ramps sometimes. It is way too easy to manual and when you do a trick and try to manual after there is a disconnect that is obvious. Vert just doesn't even exist, I hope to see that added in, right now you are just bound to slam every time you try to hit a quarter pipe. The music is okay but the variety is limited and it gets old really fast. I am sure there are thousands of musicians and bands that would love to have their music featured in a game. Smaller labels would probably allow rights to usage.character customization is very weak, board and person.The recording option is a cool idea but it is just a chore to mess with and is way too glitchy, the videos don't save and it just feels like a waste of time until they improve it.The map gets oldMY PERSONAL BIGGEST COMPLAINT:There is no story, stats, or progression. You have really no purpose in this game. That is cool sometimes but being able to just skate should be an option not a demand. Adding interaction would be fun, maybe traffic, pedestrians, other skaters. mini games. That is one area that THPS really takes the cake versus this game. WHAT I WOULD ADD:STORYINTERACTIONSMUSICVIDEOS OF REAL SKATERS (maybe after you do one of the historical tricks a video of it unlocks if the footage is out there)MORE MAPS

_childDocuments_.review: It's.... okay.It's nice that some games are trying to fill the void that the Skate series left when it was killed by EA, but none of them quite get there. While it's not really fair to compare low budget indie games to ones published by one of the richest game companies out there, it's genuinely surprising at how close they get to replicating that experience.... and then they try to put their own spin on it and unfortunately it's not for the better.First of all the controls are extremely difficult for most people to transition into, using the triggers to steer completely messes with the muscle memory you have likely been building up with the Skate series over the years.Secondly, it feels pointless. The lack of a score system might be fine for some people but for me personally, I want gamified  features because... I am playing a video game.I want the feedback so I can learn how well I am doing and what I can do to beat my previous score. I want to set high scores and beat them. I want to see leaderboards and attempt to beat those. I can walk outside and skate with a real board any time I want, and if I want that experience, that's exactly what I would do. I play games, because they are games. They let me do things I wouldn't necessarily do in real life. In real life you don't get helpful system on your UI to give you feedback on how well you are doing and other things to work towards.Unfortunately until this game starts embracing the fact that it's a video game, I wouldn't necessarily recommend this, but it's got a solid foundation with the potential to be a great game someday, and if you are willing to put up with it's biggest issues then it's probably worth checking out on a sale.As of right now I'd give it a 5/10. It's good enough to give a thumbs up, but no where near good enough to fill the void that Skate left.... yet.

They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. _childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of skateboarding games in my life. Session (and more recently Skater XL) distinguishes itself from the rest by foregoing all "hand-holding" and focusing instead on granular control. Initially, I hated the controls and preferred Skater XL's approach - I retracted that statement pretty quickly. Some of the controls in Session seem perplexing at first, but only until you play for a while and get that "ah-ha!" moment. Although still lacking in content and features, the core gameplay is immensely fun. I've spent hours skating the same spot over and over. The feeling of sticking a landing after attempting a particular line a 100x times is pure bliss. For such a low price, you really can't go wrong - this is probably as good as it's going to get for a skateboarding sims on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: First of: THIS GAME IS NOT SUPPOSED TO BE SKATE 4, a lot of negatives reviews are from people who were expecting a Skate 3 spiritual sucessor, with similar controls and what not. SESSION IS NOT THAT GAME. Session is a new kind of skateboarding game, alongside Skater XL. After that, how is the game?The game is good, but there is MUCH room for improvement, and the developers know that, this early access is a taste of what we can expect from this game and these devs.The control scheme is very different from what people are used to in skateboarding games, and a little bit  similar to Skater XL, but they behave very differently from each other. At this point I think that Skater XL is more fluid and dynamic than Session, specially when it comes to spins and grinds. But the overall experience of Session is elevated by it's instant replay, customization and object dropper mechanics. Also you have different options for inputs in spins, fliptricks and scoops, but at this moment it's unclear what is the actual difference is between those. You can also enable manual catch, but there's no instruction of HOW to actually catch the board, what makes playing with that option enabled very inconsistent and frustrating, so for now I would recommend leaving auto catch and continuous flip on. The game presents a very big map to skate on, and some customization of your character and board, including graphic, griptape, size, wheels, wheels size and trucks. The audio design is very good, so are the graphics of the game, but the performance can be very inconsistent and bugs exist. If you're in doubt, you should wait and see how the devs handle updates, like if they update the game in a regular basis  and if those updates are signficant. For $20 bucks it's worth it if you liked Skater XL and wanna try something different, or if you just want to play a new skateboarding game that you have been desperately waiting for since Skate 3, but remember, it WILL BE DIFFERENT from Skate, THPS and even Skater XL. The roadmap of updates looks promising, and the game will progressively get more expansive, so if you plan to play this game in the future, it might just be worth it to save some bucks by buying it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: There's no way of explaining just how poor the current early-access development of this game is. A lot of false hope, lack of communication, and broken promises from the developers. Best way to explain it is what I've listed below.- implement new physics animations BEFORE fully fixing grabs and vert as that now sabotages any plans for putting transitions into the game without having to rebuild the ENTIRE physics literally from the ground up. (they were really putting the cart before the horse on this one)Like HOW were they going to introduce half of the tricks like primos, darkslides, grabs, stalls, reverts, etc. into the storyline when half of those tricks don't even work in-game. That limits the story progression to nothing more than doing the same common tricks but at different spots... which sounds really familiar because it's pretty much what Historical Challenges ALREADY achieves minus animated cutscenes with pro's)- having a more fleshed-out game before partnering with NACON (because when they introduced investors and they put money into a product they want to see profitable returns by a date specified and Crea-ture no longer get to take their time on improving things because it becomes a race to money)Getting a fully-fleshed out character creator would have done that job on its own as the community would have literally created pro-skaters in their likeness FOR YOU, CREA-TURE. Modding communities have literally made Tyler The Creator, Spiderman, and freaking GOKU playable in Session. Taking a page out of WWE2K22's book, their online creation community were given character creation tools and have literally created half of the people in existence with their character creator. As the old saying goes, "If you give kids LEGOs they'll build their own toys."The order that things should have went: Physics/Animations, Storyboarding, Features, Level Design, Mission Structure, TESTING AND BUG-FIXING, and then when you have a solid basis THEN you begin adding Signature Assets and Cosmetics. (the two excerpts below are literally taken verbatim from the developer's last update post)"As skaters, and gamers, we know what’s expected and we hold ourselves to a high level of quality. The current improvements in the game show great promise, but the need to further improve quality and cement the best skate experience for V1..."The following features have been “cut” from V1 for quality reasons, however they are on the list for our possible post launch production plans:On Foot navigation improvements have been CUTLegacy controls have been CUTGrabs & Vert have been CUTParty Games have been CUT

_childDocuments_.review: I'll come back to check for updates. For now, the learning curve is way too steep, but mostly it is temperamental. I thought XL was hard, but this is even harder to just aim at something. I think this is because the ollie takes a long time to setup...even for smaller things, like benches. I prefer the XL controls for pointing the rear foot direction left, or right for shuvits and forward for flips. I still can't figure out what sets off my shuvits, in this game. XL has lethargic gravity/ physics, but amazing controls. In XL, the gravity behaves similar to how it would be on Mars...but without the jump height benefits. Session nails the physics, to earthlike levels, but the controls are not as intuitive as XL. At least not in the sense of what separates flips from...not flips. Both XL and Session do suffer from one thing, however, incredibly frail skaters. That you could just coast into a sidewalk or bench and fall into an awkward, boneless collapse. Even if a skater doesn't land a trick, the most that will happen, in most cases, is he stumbles. Maybe catches himself on a wall, or rail.  I can tell you right now that I can run into a sidewalk at probably approaching 5 mph and not fall. I think  both games need to do one of two things; Put in some sort of stumble mechanic, or just allow some acceptable bump padding. Meaning, coasting into a curb or concrete bench isn't going to make you fall. You'd just simply bump into it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a skateboarding game that's more grounded this is the game for you.  The learning curve isn't too difficult for the flip tricks, but the grinds do take a little time to get used to.  Just like in real life its all about how you approach the obstacles and the angle to get that sweet backside noseblunt or fakie fs180 nosegrind.  The physics are what really draw me coming back to this game and when you get a certain trick you've been working on it is very satisfying.  Overall I highly recommend this game for those that don't want that "floaty" style of gameplay and want something a bit more realistic.

_childDocuments_.review: Read about the control scheme before you purchase. If you purchase, make up your mind very quickly if you can live with it, and if not ask for a refund right away.I really wanted to like this game. I simply cannot get used to the control scheme - using triggers to steer. Despite giving you a few options for how the triggers react either pressure, time, or speed, I simply can not get used to it. It feels completely unnatural even after several hours of trying. I could get a bit of flow going but I just can't get any precision in the steering which makes lining up tricks not just difficult but near impossible (for me). The only way I got any meaningful game play so far was to very painstakingly align a trick to an obstacle, and then drop a session marker so that I could reset easily. Even still, it just feels completely cumbersome and awkward. If you look in the forums, you'll see a lot of haters hating on people for saying they don't like the game or won't play it until they offer another control scheme. I won't say I don't like it because It "feels" like it could be awesome, but I won't be playing it. I understand others may have no issue at all getting used it the controls but for me , it's just not enjoyable. Being such a dramatically different control scheme and with so much being written about it,  I do wish they had offered a demo or something because I really tried to like this but basically wasted my money.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a massive EA Skate fan back in the day and needed to scratch the itch of spending hours trying to perfect a line and the overall dopamine rush of getting something down. This game firmly scratches that itch. I've read a variety of negative reviews of the transition from early access to 1.0 and can't disagree more.While it lacks the content that is present in Skater XL, this game shines out as a modern successor to Skate.My main feeling, having put in a few hours before the full release, is that the game feels and has an animation system to match. Go look at clips of skate 4 to understand the finesse that is present in the animation system. Grinds feel hard earned, 180s and follow on tricks require thought, tricks can be styled and tweaked, and while the bail system can feel a little overzealous, the overall experience draws you in for more.Things didn't make so much sense in the early access release, with trick failing feeling more like a punishment than a mistiming or a slight miscalculation of distance. Yet, I get a strong sense of smoothness in this release. Yes, there are aspects which could be further improved, such as improving the  run-on mechanic so that you get a consistent amount of speed in a run up, but for an "initial release", i.e. this is v 1.0 and will receive further updates, It really makes Skate - which felt like  a massive advancement of THPS - feel like an arcade game.If you're concerned about the "nonsensical" input system, put a few hours in - like with any other game - and you'll get your head around it and recognise that this makes a ton of sense. I would highly recommend getting it now and I can't wait to see where it goes in the future! Well done guys!

_childDocuments_.review: Session is hands down the best skateboarding game I've ever played. The ability to pick up your board and move freely through the map can't be overstated - this is a game that just lets you skate - whether you work a particular rail or obstacle until you get the trick right - or just want to freestyle around the map. I was never a great street skater IRL (when I was younger and less blubberish ;-) but i remember enough to appreciate what this game offers - And that is the  of just skateboarding. In game terms - no checkpoints, limitations or any crap like that - just grab your board and skate, which is what street skating is. A lot of talk in the reviews and forum have been about the controls - and while they're kind of funky when you first start - after several days playing, they just click. Session makes you  to learn the moves - they're not handed to you on a platter. I've spent a while now trying to learn tricks in both stances and when you get to the point where can confidently land a certain trick at will - it feels incredibly satisfying. For sure.I'm looking forward to more skate spots in the future (which I think is on the roadmap) and I can say I've EASILY gotten my $ worth of enjoyment from this title. My only criticism is that there could be more explanation of the features - ie: I didn't know I could place objects like ramps and rails until I watched a YT video. But this is still early access so the gripe is very minor.Overall this is a fantastic skateboarding experience as long as you don't expect to master it in 20 minutes. And street skaters who skate/have skated will appreciate the feel this game has for the freedom of that style. Looking forward to more content and the future of this title. Cheers ;-)

_childDocuments_.review: so, I still have trouble getting consistent lines and techie tricks for the most part but this game is incredible if you are willing to put the time in to get better. The most important thing about this game that translates pretty well to real life is that ( Timing is EVERYTHING ), to get better at this game your timing on landing a trick to a grind has to be perfect. Once you figure out the timing the game gets so much easier. I started playing this game on the hardest setting almost instantly, as I found the game so much more rewarding and fun doing so. I really only began getting better after 100 hours.I enjoy playing Session while I have youtube or something playing in the background, especially when I am trying to perfect a trick or line. If you have a low to mid tier pc anything GTX 1650 4 gig or better you can run Session and have youtube running on second monitor with a pretty consistent 60 fps and temps under 65 degree C, 149 F in my experience.Only thing I don't like about Session is the lack of grab tricks, only street, I was ok with this when I bought the game about 8 months ago but after 200 hours I feel like having grab tricks would make the game feel more complete. still for all the time I put into the game and enjoyed it I would say, if you are a skateboarder or use to be or you want to try something more challenging than skate 2 and 3 this game will have you covered.

_childDocuments_.review: My hours will build because I will conquer the controls :)Word to the wise! It will challenge you even if you've played SKATE before. It feels like I'm trying to solve a mathematical equation with how in-depth it is with foot placement, flick movement, and the whole ordeal. I guess what I am trying to say is if you want to know how to play this game, watch Nyjah Houston. LOL SCIENCE IS AWESOME!Even when you feel like saying "ugh, these controls suck or need to be fixed," just know that it's your brain wanting to give up. Stick with it and take your time moving your control toggles to see how each foot placement connects, whether you are hitting a rail or about to nollie up a 3-set of stairs – it's all about timing. Once you get used to the controls, you will get smoother. I realized I found myself getting extremely frustrated when I bumped and fell on the floor countless times. Then it hit me, would this happen in real life if I tried to go over a crack in the ground, or should I ollie over it? You'd jump over it. So, good work to the developers for making my favorite game of the year. While yes, I do skate, it's so rewarding when you can just begin to flow with a couple of tricks and then have to go back over and over to get the foot placement and flick just right, and even the landing... starting to see what I mean? It's real, so enjoy the process and keep struggling.Love this game :)Get it! WORTH EVERY PENNY :)

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of the EA skate series, I would definitely recommend this game. This game has the learning curve that I had missed in skate sequels. _childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a skateboard simulator, look no further. This game will provide you with that hard-earned satisfaction of landing the perfect trick to finish off the line you've been working on, and allow you to make a sick replay of it to share later. Twin-stick controls give you total control over your skater, even if it feels pretty awkward at first, the depth of things you can do is seemingly endless. If you can imagine a line, you can make it.And it does all of this while still being in alpha, blowing the competition out of the water. Sure, it feels harder to get into, but the controls just make sense after you learn them. Many features that are only still planned or only available through mods on the *other game* are basic features well implemented here. Stats menu, time of day, soundtrack control, board wear, classic camera filters for replay editor... More tricks and possibilities. All things that are excellently implemented here. Darkslides, Primos, Late tricks. These, even in an experimental stage are already quite satisfactory to pull off.The only thing I have to say is not very good in this game is skater and baord customization, as the variety of clothes and board graphics is a little bit lacking. But it already shows promise in possibilities, such as differently sized or shaped boards, wheels, deck rails. Another point that still needs work is the skater animations to make them feel a tad more natural and fluid, but honestly I trust these devs to keep pouring in love and work into this game.

Looks great, feels great, the NYC map feels sprawling and connected though other maps feel more segmented. Not much of a main story but plenty of missions to keep you busy and moving through different tricks, grinds, manny pad challenges etc. Drops off mission-wise pretty sharply once you've finished the main line, but by then you're probably doing your own thing anyway,Main issue/complaint is that there are a couple bugged missions, and mission descriptions that aren't clear enough/use confusing or conflicting trick names. Had to visit reddit countless times and found answers from 2 years ago - so these issues have been around awhile. The game also puts a lot of strain on the PC, even with low quality settings, so be wary.Otherwise, had a load of fun, has a good sense of weight if you get the settings right, great to get the thrill of landing a trick if you're not skilled or brave enough yet. Recommended

_childDocuments_.review: I finally got 20+ hours in this game, so I think I can offer somewhat of a review. Hands down, this is one of the best skating games I've ever played in a while due to its innovation and realism. While I believe this game is great, it's definitely not for everyone; it requires a lot of patience and does not hold your hand at all, after the tutorial you're left alone to explore the city and discover new tricks to perform. If you're expecting a game more like Skate this may not be your cup of tea, but if you want a more realistic experience for a skating game, you will definitely fall in love with this game. The maps alone have really nice spots to perform tricks and are beautiful to just go around to skate and explore plus it feels really satisfying when you get a clean line. _childDocuments_.review: Session is a great skating game. For casual fans of the Tony Hawk games Session's gameplay might feel largely confusing and/or frustrating but I highly recommend it to dedicated Skate fans who are looking for an extra challenge.It's really cool how in the first 30 minutes or so of gameplay even the simplest trick seems like a difficult task and just a couple of hours later you can do all sorts of cool lines and combos. That feeling of progress you achieve is one of the best things about Session. You definitely need some patience to get to a point where you can do most tricks without much effort but considering it's supposed to be an authentic experience it should be expected.For an Early Access game, Session definitely has its bugs, mainly in the form of collision detection issues and (most notably) how easy it is for your skater to fall over even with the slightest bumps into objects. The ragdoll physics is definitely something that needs refinement.Overall, I can say Session is definitely worth checking out if you're a fan of the genre. Very challenging but also very fun :)

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from the Skate franchise, the controls are an absolute head ♥♥♥♥. It is completely understandable that they are going for a realistic type of game, as stated in the description, but when it gets in the way of playing the actual game (control turning with triggers, which is either too sensitive or not sensitive at all), it just isn't fun. The actual skating itself is clunky; grinds are either completely sideways or dead straight. There is no positioning of the feet in a way that matters. The ollie-ing and mechanics like that are so flawed that half the time you pull off something completely random and just have to roll your eyes. Just trying to ollie down two stairs into a kickflip ends in three ways: 1. you succeed, 2. you end up being sent flying and ragdolling from the 10th of a second you missed your ollie, or 3. you get pulled into the stairs with the gravitational force of the sun and don't stack it somehow. The game feels like all attention has gone to the wrong places, and I would say that it is barely worth the 17 AUD I paid, let alone the nearly full $60. It definitely has potential, but for a game that has been out for nearly five years (including early access), I don't think we are getting that any time soon. It does seem enjoyable if you can work past those flaws... and i will give it some time and might amend my review, but I highly doubt it.Edit: After playing some more, I can definitely stand by what I've written. Attention is all in the wrong places. There is a lot of customisation, specifically the board decks, trucks, and wheels, but most of the clothing options are generic reskins of each other. The only saving grace of this game is the soundtrack (which is essentially all just free-use music from a couple of different chillhop playlists) and the replay feature, which is disgustingly polished and fun to manipulate and use since you will always be stacking. The map choices consist of one main free roam area in each city, and then a bunch of random self-contained areas only accessible through bus stops (completely unnecessary considering you can just use the map in the pause menu). Only two or three of those self-contained maps have any potential for anything fun and the first free roam area is by far the best one. Still, give this a go if it seems like something you would enjoy, since I may just be spoiled from Skate. Overall, $60 is still too much for this game, but due to the effort put in the wrong areas, I'd still only say 25 AUD at max.

The grinding does need a bit of work, and you can sometimes get stuck in the level, but these things will probably be ironed out and improved upon in the future. At this point, I can definitely recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of Skate.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game way back in EA and just picked it back up to see if its progressed much since then and, unfortunately, it hasn't. As far as I can tell, all of the jankiness and issues that were there in EA are still there in release as of the time of this review. The camera seems to fight you, bails will happen randomly and recovery from bails feels like it takes eons, the ragdolls are straight out of 2004, and completing missions often feels like an impossible chore where even clear successes won't register until they randomly do. The worst part is the crashes. So many crashes. It usually takes me at least three attempts to even get the game started and god forbid you alt tab. Half the time when I do get into the game there's no sound and I've got to restart it again. Its extremely frustrating to say the least. Its such a bummer. I really like the way they do the skate sim controls/physics and sticking a cool line feels great. The maps are fantastic. The feel of the game when its on is really really good. I just can't recommend anyone spend money on this game in the state that its in. Its also missing things you would want to have in a modern game like this like an actual character creator, customizable music playlist, and, while I personally don't care about it, the lack of multiplayer seems like a huge missed opportunity. Maybe pick it up on a deep discount if you want the bones of a great skate sim and have a high tolerance for jank. Def don't pay full price.

If you're looking for a Tony Hawk esque game this is not going to be your cup of tea, it's not a tricklining game. There's various control options where you can turn on Skate like controls however I haven't experimented with that. Day and night settings can create some beautiful shots/video clips. Map is based off of real locations and the attention to detail is astonishing. I bought SkaterXL and Session at the same time and ended up returning SkaterXL, I can't stress enough that the difficulty is what makes the game worthwhile. If you've skated before or want the closet thing to Skating VIA a video game pick this up boyos the community is fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game and i recommend that people stick through the initial hard phase because it's so fun when it flows. Sadly though it's riddled with little bugs here and there. One that plagues me is the analog on my controller not responding the way it should have responded. For example, when I pull down my left analog straight to the bottom, the skater should've "crouch" to prepare and do an ollie, however my skater does a manual instead. This really sucks since if you have the unique pop height thing on, your pop height wouldn't be as high as it should've been because the skater decided to do a manual instead of preparing to do the trick. Can't tell you how many times i tried to prepare to do a grind on a handrail but failed to do a high kickflip or ollie just because my skater wants to do manual instead of preparing to jump and ♥♥♥♥.Customising stuff in this game is fun. You can pretty much change how the game plays in the advanced settings. You also can change pretty much everything about your board. Trucks, wheels, graphics and the tape is customisable. Your skater can be customised as well with various clothes to choose from. Although i would love a bit more variety in the type of clothing like cz all the t-shirts and hoodies r getting old, the pants needs more variety (there's like only cargo and baggy pants in the game).Outside of that, solid game. Fun when it gets flowing and when you hit the line you've been trying over and over to do, it made me came a bit.6/10 prolly an 7 if it wasn't for that analog thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to pick up, but entirely worth it. I love skateboarding, I love this game, I'll literally worship it if it one day gets more varied tricks (impossible, strawberry milkshake, etc) and multiplayer. This is the spiritual successor to the skating genre of old.EDIT:I'm dying over the number of people bashing this game because they think skating for 10+ years in real life entitles you to becoming a pro in this game in 30 minutes. I've had trouble landing grinds, yes, but I didn't complain about it, I kept trying until I landed it lmaoIt's called effort, and at first I sucked insanely bad at grinds, now I can land smith and feeble grinds fairly easily because I did this rare thing called "practice"Devs, if you see this, you have a wonderful game that just needs more content and polish, and it'll be fantastic. People who complain, I fear you'd HATE real life skateboarding.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! The controls are amazing, I am really glad they stuck with their control scheme even though a lot of people were complaining it is too hard. _childDocuments_.review: Considering that this game is in early access, the gameplay is pretty solid. For me it took about an hour to get into the controls (meaning that I was able to do more than just kickflips and ollies). Here's a few pros and cons after a few hours of gameplay:Pros:+Fairly solid gameplay for an early access title+Controlling one foot per stick is a great idea, so far working pretty well+Gameplay and controls can be modified (e.g. how the board flips, auto-catch and much more)+The game world is pretty big even at this stage of developmentCons:-At times the physics and gameplay can be a bit wonky-Grinds seem to be a bit tricky (at least for me the player might just suddenly bounce in the air for no reason whilst in a grind, grinds don't lock on that well etc., might also be that I just need more practice)-Three crashes occured during two hours of gameplay (well, this is still an early access title)About the performance, the game seems to run pretty smoothly on my PC @ 1080p (i7 8700K, GTX 1080 Ti, 16Gb DDR4), around 60-120fps varying on the location. Some hickups here and there, but I would assume that the devs will address the game performance during development as well. TL;DR - Solid early access title, especially for fans of the original Skate-series

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this on the steam deck is just great, some text can be a little small however. _childDocuments_.review: If you played Skate 3 on "hardcore" mode because it was "more realistic" then this game is 100% for you. On day 1 of playing Session, I upped the difficulty to the hardest setting to make it the most realistic. In session, you control different feet with different joysticks, turn with triggers, you have to catch flip tricks, and you have to gracefully land when dropping down a gap/ stair set/ coming off of a rail down a stair set. If you thought Rob Dyrdek's challenge to get a 360 flip crooked grind on the hubba was a annoyingly awesome, this game is for you. Props if you get the reference.

_childDocuments_.review: I got session yesterday, and i've already played the game for 12 hours. So far this is all of my thoughts, with the pros, and cons.Pros:-I have the same feeling of desire to do a nice trick that i'd have skating irl.-No Critical gameplay causing issues or bugs, Game works more than fine.-The most in depth skating game that i've seen so far.-A game that you can easily play, and lose track of time trying to do one trick over a gap.-The hardcore mode allowing individual control of each foot is an amazing Touch.-Extremely indepth control scheme-Alot of various controllable options for video, audio, ETC.-Easy to understand Learning curve that feels rewarding.Cons:-Early access-Replays and montages can be saved, but not viewed if you close out of the editor.-opening up a montage from your apartment crashes your game.-No current multiplayer-When loading into the game, you will always load into a regular stance, even if you switched your preference to goofy.Things i've noticed:-The game will sometimes cause full loss of controller input, and you'll have to unplug your controller and plug it back in or close the game and re open it. (atleast this was happening to me but then later stopped.)-The game does have slight issues where you clip through your skateboard, but if you are Trying to do certain tricks, and not spazing your board around hoping to pull something crazy off, then you can make it look smooth and there wont be any clipping.All and all, if you're looking for a pc skateboarding game experience, i'd highly recommend this game, and if you're looking for a simulation game with a fun and interesting learning curve, i'd also recommend this game.Solid rating of an 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: So the game is pretty great so far! By far, the best overall animations in a skateboarding game so far! There's a lot of content here for an early access game. I just have a few criticisms that could make the game even greater: 1: For the love of god, let me remap reverts! I've gotten to the point where I don't do it super often, but every so often I'll do it by accident and it's really frustrating! Either R1/L1 or R3/L3 would be nice.2: Allow me to turn off wind up. I really wish I could have more control steering while crouched down for a trick. Also, the windup doesn't seem to make me spin faster, and it doesn't look that unrealistic without them, so even for 360s I just never do it. 3: Allow me to invert the direction when skating switch like Skater XL. This is an area where I think the SXL control scheme makes way more sense. When you're riding fakie, you do your tricks the same way you do regular, and switch is the same as nollie but rolling the other direction in real life, so why do I flick my feet in the opposite direction? I got used to all the other changes, but this one I just can't get used to. 4: Let me push faster more immediately, or at least let me do this when already up to speed. I really like skating fast and aggressive, and it's really annoying when I lose my speed just a little bit, and have to push like 5 times just to get back to the speed I was at a second ago. If I'm already going 3/4 of full push speed I shouldn't have to push more than once to get back up to speed. 5: Slopes. They don't add enough to your speed when you roll down them, and banks are basically unskateable. I'm assuming this will be part of the transition update whenever that comes?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is in a league of it's own. By far the best skateboarding game that's ever been made, in terms of the level of realism, compared to any other skateboarding game on the market. Seriously. It has some minor bugs here and there, but overall it already feels pretty polished in it's own right. Every physics setting is fully customizable allowing for anyone to pick it up, and tweak it to their preferences. Controls admittedly do take some time to get used to, especially if you're coming from one of the "Skate" series games, as this game has more controls, complex combinations and sequences of inputs than just about any other skateboarding game, but that's what allows for such a high level of realism. Just like real-life skating, learning the mechanics of the game are equal parts challenging, and rewarding. The game also has a robust replay editor system that allows you to make really cool videos from game-play. All-in-all, this probably the best, and definitely the most realistic skateboarding game I've played, if you love realism in skating games, it doesn't get better than this. Can't wait to see what the devs have planned for this in the future, but even as it is today, it's a must-have for any skater's library.

Soon after I turned on unique pop height and bigdrop landing, then adding more manual control as i got more comfortable. After landing tres off of things I probably shouldn't have, i finally recently decided to switch to full manual catch mode. Genuinely gave me a whole new appreciation for how the system works.If you aren't into street skating and the creativity involved in making spots from the infrastructure around you, you might not like this game as much as others. _childDocuments_.review: At the moment, it is a matter of getting used to the controls, the problem is how early access this game is. It's too janky, sometimes my player won't position for a trick and will just continue to roll forward until i get off the board which ruins the flow/speed. I love the options they give you like being able to catch the board manually as you would in real life, but if you time it wrong, the player will float upward, stopping in their tracks before floating back down. The option to choose a goofy stance and to switch the analogs between front/back foot and left/foot is great, I feel awkward when my skaters push/ride regular. Which does make things slightly easier. Also the customization seems promising, especially changing trucks/boards/wheels. Plus the ability to change the time of day is nice, plus being able to get off the board to run makes traversal and catching speed easier. So far, Session wins in terms of environment and music, setting the mood, you've got a large map. It's pretty cool. As far as animations and polish goes, Skater XL feels cleaner but almost too sterile in comparison, even though the control schemes are greatly similar with each using both analog sticks to position and complete tricks. It's too bad these two development teams can't team up. I'm gonna remain hopefully and hold on to both games. I can't say whether I'd recommend either right now unless you really want to get that itch out and are willing to devote the time to practicing. I bought both and I will keep playing both through their early access. I know this is a review for Session, but being one of two possible Skate successors, it's impossible to not compare them.UPDATE: Upon further hours playing both, the controls do get much better and feel right and proper. Just need to get the grind bugs out of the way. Definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an early access review, so I'll probably end up changing it once the full game hits.I backed Session on Kickstarter. When the game hit Early Access, I wondered where my key was. I emailed the devs, and was informed that the tier I backed entitled me to a Steam key when the game left Early Access, and that it was only the higher tiers got Early Access. That was entirely my fault for not properly reading the tier descriptions before emailing, but a few days later the devs messaged everyone and said due to a number of people asking the same thing, they were giving everyone Early Access keys. That's some great customer relations right there!So on to the game. The intro screen says to judge this game on it's potential, not it's current state, which I'll be doing here. Yes the game is missing some features, and some polish, and the physics mean that your perfect ledge grind will catch and you'll get flung half a dozen feet into the air, but it's Early Access from a small team, so things like that are to be expected.The game itself looks amazing and plays quite well. There's a full day / night cycle with dynamic lighting, a decently sized, realistic map, a replay editor, an object dropper (that saves the position of the objects even after you quit the game!), some challenges to complete, and a whole bunch of input customization options that can make the game easier or harder.Skating feels natural and realistic. If you want to 360 a trick, you have to set up the spin before you pop, none of this leap off a ledge and decide in mid-air to squeeze in a 900 before landing crap. If you want to grind, you have to line up perfectly, as by default the game is rather unforgiving about grinds. I think even the wheels are taken into consideration on grinds, so if you nose slide, but you're too far over and your wheels touch the lip, they may catch and throw you off, just as you'd expect when doing an actual noseslide.On to the controls. This is where the game gets realistic and to some, frustrating. Turning is done via the triggers which simulates leaning left and right on the board, and your feet map to the analogue sticks. By default it's left foot / left stick and right foot / right stickIn the settings menu there's a few input things you can customize to make the game easier or harder. By default the game auto-catches flips for you, but you can ramp up the realism by turning on manual catching so you have to tap the stick at the right time to catch a flip. It's frustrating, but satisfying when you do get it.You can also change how the triggers work. As mentioned, by default they act like leaning on the board. The further down you press, the further you lean. But there's a few other modes you can set it to, such as speed-based (so the faster you press down, the faster you'll turn) and timing based, where how long it takes from the time you started pressing to when the trigger was fully depressed determines how fast you turn.As mentioned, by default the game uses a left stick / left foot, right stick / right foot mode. You can change that to left stick / back foot, right stick / front foot mode, which makes skating switch easier because you don't need to be aware of how you're skating (and when double tapping the triggers reverts, it's easy to forget!)So overall, it's a good game. There's still plenty to be done, and some things I'd like to see added, such as wallrides, hippy jumps, being able to turn when sliding to a halt, a music selector and other stuff, but it's a ton of fun so far, and I can definitely see myself sinking a LOT of hours into this, like I did with Skate.

_childDocuments_.review: While the core mechanics of this game are enjoyable up to a point, it's important to note that this is far from a complete product. The controls are responsive when they work, but the character is plagued with bugs. It's not uncommon for the character to inexplicably fall while riding in a straight line, pop out of a grind only to faceplant onto the ground, or experience other equally frustrating glitches.The trick system is heavily skewed towards street skating, so if you're looking to perform lip tricks, grabs, or anything more aligned with vert/park skating, you'll be disappointed. The developers have made it clear that their focus is on selling overpriced DLCs with shallow maps, while features that should have been included before the game left beta are relegated to an "experimental" tab. And by "experimental," they truly mean it—these are essentially unfinished mechanics that were added over two years ago with promises of improvement post-release, but have since been neglected, leaving a menu cluttered with half-baked features.The story mode is not worth your time; the missions are simplistic and poorly explained, offering little guidance on how to complete them. In essence, this is an unfinished sandbox skate simulation priced at $40. I can only recommend it if you find it on sale and have no interest in the other mechanics I've mentioned.
_childDocuments_.name: Session: Skate Sim

_childDocuments_.review: Looking at game-play footage of this game, I was given hella "EA Skate" vibes, and that enticed me to buy it. I went in thinking I'd be playing it casually, however, after playing it for as long as I did, the best way I can describe it accurately is if Skate wanted to be the next Dark Souls and wanted to kick you in the nuts repeatedly while it was at it. It even makes it clear upon launching that the game will be unforgiving, which disappointed me on a casual level. The controls are off-putting--triggers to steer/turn your skater in the air, left stick to control front foot and right stick to control back, etc--and customization--in its current form--is hideously limited as it gives you a generic Skater to play as. Until this game gives you the option to have Skate-like controls--which I prefer over this clunky mess--I won't be picking this up again anytime soon. I'd gotten a refund after playing the game for 83 minutes, 20 or so of which were most likely after I'd finished the tedious, bone-grinding difficult tutorial.As it stands, I wouldn't get Session right now. First impressions are everything, and I was left with a bit of a sour taste just seconds into playing. I'd say give it a few months or so. If the game still isn't accessible for a casual audience by then, steer clear unless you want your face to meet with the pavement and run up that hospital bill.I cannot recommend this game to the casual gamer, such as myself. That's not to say I didn't have fun with it. On the contrary. I got used to the controls, but I could not grind to save my life. That said, only the hardcore will flourish in this love letter "to the golden era of Skateboarding".

_childDocuments_.review: I remember the Kickstarter trailer for Session, being stoked and then...kinda forgetting about it until I began playing Session in 2020 via Xbox Game Preview. I loved it despite the (very) rough edges and put in around 200 hours. Since the early access hardly any of the aforementioned rough edges have been smoothed out. Instead of improving and polishing the game's core they instead release DLC and actively refuse to work on the games issues. I do not think this is entirely on CREA-TURE. Nacon have proven themselves to be a thoroughly untrustworthy publisher in the past. It's just a shame, I think Session *IS* good. But the price, lack of polish and overall unfinished feeling really makes it hard to recommend. Don't buy it at full, or even half price.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game a couple years back and I got to say, I'm glad they followed through on making a challenging skate sim. Before I got any further, I have to say this, this game is NOT like SKATE or THPS. Please do not buy this game expecting something similar because, that would lead to a negative review with the topic being "This isn't SKATE4!!!" Tbh, that's one of the reasons why I like this game. Its wanting to be its own thing and I can appreciate that very much. One of the cool things about Session is that it has so much potential. They're still in earlier access, meaning that they have some time to put more polish into the game before releasing it fully.  I do have some pros/cons for anyone still looking at the game and debating on whether to pull the trigger or not...CONS:-The character has some stiffness here and there and can really show depending on the trick you do. -The skater can ragdoll hard as heck if you even touch the pixel above your board, meaning you have to ollie alot and be careful around those ledges.-There isnt much going on in terms of music. You get a few tracks which are nice to hear at first but can get tiresome after the 5th go around. -There are occasional bugs that can throw the game into a frenzy of lag, even when you're running the game at the best settings for your pc. But, they are working on that so this con isnt going to stay much longer. -The controls are a pain at times, meaning that is not like SKATE or THPS.PROS:-Very nice visuals and location, the devs really wanted to make a good first impression and they sure did in my books.-The sounds are crisp and authentic when your board lands on a railing or when you're riding over tile and getting that nice sound effect. -The fact that you can customize is always a plus in any game. Plus, there will be more clothes and decks coming out soon.-The controls a pain to learn, but once you nail that trick, it feels good and almost fluid, as if it was second nature.I hope that helps and also hope you'll enjoy the game that the devs have worked hard on!

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot in good conscience recommend this game in its current state (V1.0), especially for the price being asked.I've followed the progress of this game all the way through Early Access, and all the way through I've been waiting for the update that would finally make this skating tech demo feel like a game, with a purpose, but well... the game is now officially out of Early Access and I'm still waiting.The only structured content you're given in the game is to explore the map to find random skaters that are standing at skate spots. You'll then see a short 10 second clip of them doing something and then you'll be given a list of tricks to do. The thing is, the game is really inconsistent at telling you what it actually wants you to do and is really bad at detecting when you've successfully done it. An early mission had me doing flip tricks down a staircase and I was told to "BS Pop Shuvit". I did the trick about 15 times down this set of stairs and the game would just not register it. Bizarrely, the game actually has a Trick Display that will tell you what trick you did, making it easier to confirm that you're not the one at fault, but it is turned off by default (Options > Display > Trick Display). The point is though, the one form of structured content you get in this game is bad.Now, you could say that this game is really aimed at just being a sandbox for you to skate around in, finding cool lines and filming cool stuff, and I mean sure, I'd be fine with that, but then, the price should really reflect this. Also, if the devs haven't been spending all of this time creating meaningful structured content for us to experience, why is the core skating experience so far behind where it should be?Originally, the intention was for V1.0 of Session to include:- Improvements to on foot navigation- Legacy controls- Grabs and Vert- Party GamesThe intention is for these to be added to the game down the road but then, why leave Early Access if the game isn't yet done? And the game really feels like it isn't done.Currently:- You cannot customise your character's features - hair, eyes, nose, mouth etc.- The transition from skating/standing is instantaneous, your character effectively teleports from one to the other- Your character cannot get up from bails. You fall over, the camera remains where you fell from, your body ragdolls away and then a second or two later, you're teleported back onto your board- Grinding is really inconsistent. You will land in a grind, slide along the rail for a second or two and then your character will randomly pass out. It's funny but definitely brokenAlso, did they lose the rights to the old songs or something? I've been flicking through the different radio stations in game but it seems like all of the rap music is gone, now your choices are Reggae or Chillhop.But yeah, for the price you're not getting much. Three lifeless cities to skate around in and some painfully unfun missions that you need to complete (at least 5 to 10 of) if you want to customise your character and board beyond the starting gear.

_childDocuments_.review: I just 100%ed the game (all achievements and challenges including DLC content) and in my opinion it's one of the best skateboarding games out there. As the name suggests it's a simulator game,so if you expect arcade gameplay like in THPS, then this game is not for you...If you like a more realistic approach - especially if you skate or used to skate in real life - then go for it.I played a ton of skateboarding games. I was pretty good at all the THPS games - especially THPS3 online multiplayer, platinumed all the 'Skate' series games on ps3 and played a bunch of skateboarding games on handhelds and the smartphone.None of these games really compare with Session. If it comes to controls, the 'Skate' series is probably the closest one, but Session takes it to a whole other level when it comes to realism.At first there is a steep learning curve and people might already give up before the game really started, but if you learned the controls it's a ton of fun.It's basically the 'Dark Souls' of skateboarding games.I played in hardcore mode and it's really fulfilling to land tricks with 'manual catch' enabled - comes close to skating in real life.Unfortunately there are still annoying bugs like getting stuck in the ground or turning around while using Session markers (saved places you can jump back to) and some tricks and lines don't register well during challenges.But, all in all the good outweighs the bad by far and I can really recommend the game. Skater XL might be a bit smoother, but Session has way more functions and possibilities ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I would definitely recommend Session to anyone looking for a true Skateboarding Sim. If you love a game that can actually give you a challenge, you'll find plenty here. It's controls are different than any Skate game or Tony Hawk game.What I love most about Session is that just like skating in real life, when you finally land a trick you actually feel rewarded. You have plenty of options to tweak the game to your preferred style, and you have the option to turn all auto settings off. Meaning that you actually have to watch the board rotate back around, or actually having to be mindful on how you approach a ledge for a grind.I wouldn't say you have to know about real skating to enjoy the game, but if you do really skate or have an understanding of real skating, you'll enjoy it even more.Keep in mind that it's still in Early Access, which means you will encounter some bugs and glitches (obviously). But if you can look pass the minor stuff, you're in for a treat with this one!

I was lucky I was able to get it during refund season since currently I've been on a Skate fever, watching videos on the game and wanting to get the game again on PS3 but unable to find any copies. I searched and saw this game, then I did a little digging around and saw that it was hailed as a spiritual successor to Skate, even though it's not made by the same devs.I have to give credit where it's due, the environment is visually appealing, it looks like I downloaded a really good shader for MIncecraft, only a lot more realistic. The controls are interesting, having to control each leg and foot with the joysticks. It is built like a Skate rip-off, but a good Skate rip-off of course, with the building of obstacles, ramps, and rails to be put into the map, as well as the camera, simulating a more realistic Skate experience. I can tell that making a game of such high caliber took work and time and I am grateful that the game was made by dedicated people that know what it is to be a skater.But I have to admit, my expectations fell within 15 minutes for when I played the game, sadly. The controls are extremely hard to learn and perhaps easy to master, players perhaps getting confused depending on their stance on their board. The environment feels empty, with no people or fellow skaters to skate with, which made me feel lonelier than I should've been. There's also not much to do, aside from the challenges, which you could perhaps do pretty quickly if you got the hang of the controls. There are glitches and problems within the game, such as when I fell off my board and I was caught in an infinite falling loop until I changed location to get out of it. It is also very hard to pull off tricks aside from your kickflips, heelflips, and ollies; it's a hassle to grind/slide without the assist, hard to gain enough speed to, per se, jump a small gap, and not to say the terrible falling physics of the game, in real life you do not fall off your board if you hit a small curb.I know this game is a work in progress, but if you think about getting this game, wait a little bit more, I'm sure the devs are dedicated and will fix the glitches and issues within the game soon. Maybe not wait until the game is officially out, but wait until enough updates have come out, I know I will. _childDocuments_.review: Final Review Update for Session 1.0:Pros: Grinds are nearly perfect, Has a stats menu, Sounds are good, Music is good, Has an experimental physics animation setting that helps a lot to adding a sense of steeze/flow, I feel more inclined to skate the smaller objects in the world because of how the pacing is. I spent a lot of time grinding on a slide and stuff like that is where this game shines best. It's the little things that grab my attention.Cons: The internal control scheme is bad. Having to pop an ollie by using the front foot input annoys me. It should be 1 stick pop off of the back foot for low pop then level out with the other stick after you get air. Also we should be able to hold down both sticks to pop medium and high. I don't like how the game turns your skater for you when you pop out of a grind. I'd like to control as much as possible when it comes to my skater. I don't want the game doing anything automatically for me.Correct me if I'm wrong but it feels like the board doesn't react to the environment but rather the environment reacts to the board or more so, my inputs. I don't like this because it makes it feel like the board isn't its own entity in the session world. It seems only my inputs are being responded to by the objects in the world, rather than the board itself reacting properly to its surfaces and environment. I've been thinking ever since the primo was added into the menu as an option that the board itself is not physics based because why else can't we just catch the board sideways by chance due to physics? same with darkslide. Another 2 things I'll never get over is having to turn with the triggers and catching with flick inputs. Turning with triggers feels perfect and innovative when manualing and nose manualing. Trigger turning outside of that feels clunky and unnatural and I'll never get over it. As for catching with flicking the sticks. I don't like this and never have, which is why I strictly use auto catch. Catching with flicking feels pointless for the majority of the time anyway, considering the fact that you auto catch when you move the stick sideways for a tail slide, for example. I want to be able to catch by clicking the sticks in then do the grind. It feels way more involved and I feel more in control over everything.Final note: If the devs want more realism but want people to still enjoy the game. Implement a more complex and more involved catching system and move the pressure/pocket pops to LB and RB, implement turning with the left stick. Also allow the feet to be used when grinding to shimmy on a grind with the front or back foot. Having to use triggers to turn into another grind after the initial grind is not good because the sticks are suppose to be my feet. I should ALWAYS be able to use at least 1 of my feet to do certain things in some scenarios. With all that being said, I can't recommend the game yet until pocket pops get moved to LB and RB or a different control scheme like that gets added. Popping medium and high but only holding down 1 stick for both also is a big issue for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is still very broken years after development. When it works, it's very fun and easy to relax and just hit a rail for half an hour like you would in real life. Here's a few of the issues that have never been fixed:-Look up the quest "Philly's Finest" online and you'll see that quest has had the same issue with the grind hitbox being messed up for over TWO YEARS, and the devs have not fixed this simple mistake. -Mongo pushing (pushing with your skaters front foot) does not work unless you are turning, else they trip over their own leg, causing an immediate bail and subsequent frustration if you're going too fast and respawn in the opposite stance. -Respawns at session markers often break, causing your skater to go into an infinite falling loop where the only way to fix it is to either pause/teleport or try and get off your board as soon as you spawn. -Grinds often don't connect or cause you to instantly bail despite hitting them perfectly because the hitbox for the ledge/rail doesn't work right. -Oftentimes, slides or grinds will have this strange oscillation that you simply cannot control with any stick input even when you landed the grind perfectly so it looks incredibly ugly. Most of these are very simple fixes, yet the devs would rather spend their time pushing out microtransactions.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Skateboarding game ever......if you like realism and are not afraid to learn.Just like in real life skating you will be frustrated in the first hours learning the controlscheme. But after you get your head around to control each foot with a stick and turn with the triggers everything will feel natural and intuitive (if you skate in real life or have skated in real life even more)That feeling you get when you land a trick after trying for minutes (sometimes hours) is just like in real life.And most times when you bail you know that it was your fault and not some bug (most times).BUT there are some bugs. This game is in early access so there will be some bugs. I haven´t had any gamebreaking bugs but i´ve heard of gamebreaking bugs. Also you should have a xbox or ps4 controller. I´ve heard of some third party controllers that wont work. Aaaand you need a good PC. The game is pretty demanding and is in its current state not very optimized.BUT (again) all these negatives above will propably be fixed untill the game gets out of early access.Content: untill now there isnt any content or story in the game. You can do some trick challenges but mostly you can explore the map and most importantly: have a nice session. Just like in real life skating there is only you, the board, the spot and the trick you have in mind. The replay editor is right now in a buggy state but that will change over time.In the future the developers want to implement a money system, a skateshop, vert skating and multiplayer.Coming back to the most important part and selling point in my opinon: the controls.You may have seen people be frustrated after 5 minutes, leaving a bad review, saying the game and the controls suck and refunding the game. I say ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.You need to invest some time but after that it´s the closest you can get to real life skating.To all the people who say the game is unplayable: just check out some of the session montages on youtube, or the youtuber JLNightmare. That doesn´t look that unplayable don´t you think?You can make the game easier for example turning the auto catch mode on or making it easier to lock into a grind. Thats pretty good for learning the controls, just like training wheels on a bicycle. But unfortunately the developers implemented the legacy control scheme. Thats basically the skate3 controls.And i hate that they implemented that. Because now a lot of players will chose out of convenience the legacy controls over the original controls and they will all miss out the best part of the game.So If you read this review before buying the game be sure what you want:Do you liked the realism that the skateseries had and you like more of that realism? You are not afraid to learn? You have no problem supporting a small developer by buying an early access game and don´t mind a few bugs? => What are you waiting for? Buy it, Now!!!Do you like the Tony Hawk games and are more the arcade type player? You hate unfinished games and if there is just one bug you will personally kill the entire development team in the slowest way possible?=> maybe you shouldn´t by this game.If none of these descriptions above fit => just try the game. And please try the original controls. If you don´t like it you can still refund it if you haven´t played for longer than 2 hours. Or you can wait untill the game is finally released.Written after playing for 130 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a fan of the EA Skate series, and have hoped for some time to see the return of that genre to the game market, and the idea of Session certainly piqued my interest for this reason. Unfortunately, the game in it's current state certainly doesn't satisfy that itch, and it's release in this state has me doubting that it ever will.One thing you should know going into it, is that the control scheme is actually quite different than in the EA Skate series, and if you remember having a hard time learning the skill required to play those games effectively, buckle up for a whole new level of foreign and unintuitive controls, the likes of which I don't think befit a mainstream game. You turn by using the triggers of your controller, which sounds like the control scheme for an Octodad sequel, but this is a game in which precision is extremely important if you're going to accomplish anything that will give you a feeling of satisfaction.This is exacerbated by many issues with this build of the game, but most prominent to me is that you can't easily build up the speed needed to pull off many of the things you would expect to, such as grinding the majority of rails, which always seem just out of reach. You can spam push for as long as you like, but your skater quickly reaches a max speed which, besides being unrealistically limited, is not fast enough to get on top of many rails, unless perhaps you can align it near pixel perfectly, but that's an insane ask in a game with foreign controls in which nothing short of accomplishing that feels satisfying. The only way I could find to build a reasonable amount of speed was to roll down hills, but even if you're pushing the whole way, shortly after you leave the slope of the hill your speed will throttle back into that annoying rut.I really wanted to enjoy the game, so I thought hey, maybe I should just find a great 'spot' to practice, maybe one with a hill before a short rail. Unfortunately, from what I've explored -which is admittedly not a lot before I realized this was something I was going to refund- a lot of the terrain is flat, and nothing stood out and said "Hey, you can see how to skate this, right?" Exacerbating this issue is that I don't think there's a map. If there is, you'd have to navigate the terrible menu interface, that one can only hope will see dramatic revision.There are a lot of core features that are missing in this build of the game: such as the ability to do manuals, pump your legs; which might have helped with speed, or do grabs. Apparently grabs are an "experimental" option you can enable, but there's no explanation of how to do them. Perhaps what this game needs most, though, is the waypoint system from EA Skate, which would be a huge quality of life improvement, so you could keep trying the same trick over and over from the same position and angle, the latter of which will be nigh on impossible for you to replicate with this game's controls. It feels like a total crapshoot whether you'll pull off a grind, or manage to clear a gap, and that's the only compelling promise this game offers. You can do flip tricks on flatland easily enough, but nothing about that feels dynamic, since you can't chain them with manuals, and again going over a gap or trying to position yourself to grind is nearly impossible.The game is also a far cry from what you might expect from an EA Skate game in terms of customization options, with no real brand licences shown, and pitifully scant and inconsistent options to choose from. I can only presume this aspect of the game is nowhere near the intended target for 1.0 release, and this is something I can easily forgive of a game in early access, but sadly, there's so little to show in the rest of the game, that this point does seem important as it illustrates just how very far behind the mark this game is.In short, I think the game is in no shape to enjoy, and after how long the game has been in development, and the deal they've made with Microsoft, it's troubling to see them trying to sell this extremely, extremely incomplete build of the game. It feels like a very ambitious project developed from the top down by an amateur studio who are failing to contend with fundamental flaws in their core idea. I'd love to be proven wrong, and see this become a great game, but I don't think that's a reasonable expectation, and cannot recommend you spend your money on this mess. You won't be missing out.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for a good skateboarding game for some time now.
