_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 2: Finally. This game has finally reached a stage in its development and how it feels to play where I can recommend it. Don't get me wrong, it still has bugs and a long road of work ahead to tweak and add features, but it finally feels good. I still think that modded Skater XL is the far superior game in terms of flow, style, feel, and I desperately wish that Session would add a control setting that copies how SXL does fakie/switch controls (Session's fakie/switch controls still make no sense to me), but now when I play Session I don't close it after 10 minutes and think "god this sucks", I close it after an hour and think "that was fun, now I'm gonna go play SXL for 2 hours".EDIT: The game was pretty bad at the time that I initially reviewed this. There have since been numerous improvements, but many of the points I made here still apply. The controls still feel far inferior and less responsive than Skater XL. I like that the dev team for Session is far more communicative than Easy Day, but I still thoroughly believe that SXL is a far superior game, especially with mods. There's a reason I only have 10 hours in Session and around 300 hours in SXL. I will reiterate my previous position that if you HAVE to play a skateboarding game on PC right NOW, I would recommend Skater XL over Session by a large margin. If you're wary of giving Easy Day money, that is totally valid. However, I don't think the solution is to buy a game like Session that simply feels much worse to play.First I'll say that I've been wanting a PC skateboarding game for many years, and when Session was advertised more as a skateboarding sim rather than a casual game, I was pretty jazzed about that. I remember playing the tech demo and...well I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hated it. It controlled absolutely horribly, nothing looked natural, nothing felt intuitive, and even doing relatively simple things felt...wrong. Sad to say that many of those problems are still there.My biggest problem right now is that revert being on triggers means that I keep doing reverts by accident when trying to fine tune my approach to a ledge or rail. Triggers are WAY too sensitive for turning so it's easier to tap them a little bit, but then you just revert and it screws your whole approach up.It seems that a lot of people are complaining about having to control each foot independently rather than like in the Skate series where flip tricks are all controlled with the right stick. I think that's pretty silly, Skate's control scheme was viewed as a novelty at first as well, and look where that series went. Y'all got used to it. The problem with Session isn't exactly the control scheme, it's just that Session feels clunky and artificially difficult. The independent control of feet works fine (great even) in Skater XL, as does trigger turning and spinning, but pretty much none of the controls FEEL right in Session. Body rotation is extremely hard to control the speed on, no matter what body rotation setting I use or how slowly or how far I push the triggers. Sometimes I can get a slower rotation, but it feels like something the game decided to do, not something that I made the game do. Also SXL's switch/fakie controls make way more sense to me. I had to switch to front foot/back foot because left foot/right foot didn't feel good at all, but even that doesn't feel right compared to SXL's foot controls. Also styling your tricks in SXL is very simple and rewarding. And don't even get me started on grinds in Session. They're just...I feel really bad saying that they're terrible, but they really don't feel good at all. Holding the sticks in certain directions to do grinds feels less like you're getting into position to grind and more like you're holding the triangle button in Tony Hawk, whereas in SXL, grinds are driven by physics. Your angle of approach matters just as much, if not more, than what direction you're holding on the stick to do a specific grind. It just makes sense.Session has potential, but it feels extremely clunky and the controls feel like a worse version of SXL. It might be a good idea to either wait for some more polish after some updates before you pick up Session. My faith that the devs could deliver a polished and good feeling game weren't super high when I played the initial tech demo, and they went down when I started to see how janky the raw footage clips were leading up to release. I really hope I'm wrong and they clean this game up down the line.If you absolutely NEED a PC skateboarding game in your life RIGHT NOW, honestly go pick up Skater XL. It currently has much less content, (only one official map) but will be getting a pretty big patch soon that will not only add a new location, but actually clean up the animations a ton and smooth out much of its jank. There's also a decent sized modding community making maps all the time. That said, I'd also consider waiting to pick SXL up until that big update drops, despite how much I love it even in it's current state.I would at least just check back on Session in about 6 months and see what has changed in that time before buying it.Sorry devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Having grown up playing all skateboard games available, this game certainly is not like any of them. I mean that in a good way of course! The problem with most skateboard games is that they become quite easy very fast.Session goes as far as to allow you to adjust every single aspect of the physics from the speed gained from every push to the height you can pop your board. Being a lover of skateboarding and video games, this is the perfect mix. You can make it as realistic or as simple as you want (to an extent).The only downside to this game is that there is no voice acting and the bit of text dialogue is pretty silly, but it works I suppose. If the developers added a little bit more depth into the story, this game would be even better! Simply said, if you love the art of skateboarding (including the coordination and difficulty) this game is for you! If you want a THPS or a SKATE clone, this is not for you as it is very much as simulation as you can get! If you're on the fence, wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very, very realistic.  If you are expecting Tony Hawk Pro Skater, this is not for you!!!  This game is an amazing game, if you appreciate skateboarding as a sport.  It takes some time to get used to the controls, but once you do, you'll realize why it is set up the way it is.  There are a bunch of maps, very life like city skate spots with all sorts of rails, ledges, handrails, and launches.  I would say it takes about 4-5 hours of consistent play for you to really get the controls down, but you'll be hooked once you do.    This game is very good on the Steam Deck, especially.  I prefer to play it on the Steam Deck over the PC.  It plays really well even with lower settings and at 40fps mode on the Steam Deck (to save battery life) but you can crank it up to high settings and 60fps as well, if you don't mind charging your deck a bunch.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels weird giving, what is effectively the best skate sim available, a thumb down. Lip tricks are not fun. The game doesn't even tell you how to do them so i cant tell you if the feature is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or if i am just an idiot. From what i understand you use the command for a powerslide which also has what seems like a 50/50 chance of being a kickflip. Lets say you achieve a powerslide, if you are turning at all while you do so you instead do a revert. The powerslide mechanic is just too finicky to feel good in motion so to speak. The new bails and slams really help cover up the early access jank. And just as there is a positive there is negative. Prepare to bail for no reason, like on flat, like while you are on flat and just pushing, like you just got headshoted in cod out of literally no where just instant ragdoll. Side note about missions. The objectives in the corner don't stay visible for long enough and in some cases lack critical information to be completed. Example, early on you have to do a bunch of bs and fs 180 and 360 tricks down stairs. you do this because the objective is something like "fs 180" and there is a visual prompt by some stairs. When you get to the "fs 360" objective, even though the visual prompt still shows by the stairs, the game expects you to do it on flat. Had to make a new character to re experience a one time dialogue that implied i needed to do the trick on flat and not on the stairs.All the gear is locked now, it doesn't make much sense to me. The game throws currency at you but gives you nothing to buy with it. This however is not the greatest sin here. I have purchased both the "Brandalised" and "Supporter" pack and while the gear appears in the skate shops its, you guessed it, locked.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, To start with this review I would like to say that this game is NOT like the Skate series and the Tony hawk series where it is really easy to get going. This game is instead just like learning to skate in real life, the controls are hard to get used to but once you get used to them they give lots of possibilities.I really like how rewarding it is to hit a trick, I sometimes spend tens of minutes on trying this one trick and it gives an amazing feeling when I hit it (partly because it is so hard)The world is big with lots of places to skate The world does have some pro's and cons for example you can skate on almost every object in the game, this gives lots of variety in doing tricks. There is also the option to place objects in to the map (which I really like for when you want to add things to your route.) One Negative thing that I have to say is that the world feels a bit to empty kinda like skating in an empty city, would have loved for there to be an option to chose how many people and cars that there are on the road to make the world feel a bit more alive.One thing to not forget is that this game is still in early access(you can clearly see how somethings are still really buggy.)This game definitely has a lot of potential to be one of the best skating games out there(in my opinion) and I can't wait for the full release!

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I have to give this game a negative review. I've supported this game since the kick-starter and was extremely impressed by the level of detail in the physics during development, all up until they got bought by Nacon. Every update before they sold out was all about improving mechanics and making the game feel DEEP and unique (manual catch with your feet, customise every aspect of how your character moves the skateboard, it was GLORIOUS especially when they figured out vert/lip tricks and although it was very janky to start, but based on previous updates it was going to get polished and improved based on our feedback). Then they sold out to Nacon, got pushed hard to release on console and everything they had been working on seemed to get pushed aside and left as-is. The "story" that they added is shallow, awkward and feels cheaply made despite having big name pros. Every update since 1.0 has been cosmetics, maps or additional items to place in the world (something modders would have added because the people who love this game really love this game) instead of listening to the majority of the playerbase who are begging them to finish making their game. Just look at ANY of the updates and what they say (adding more payed content) and the comments therein. It's clear as day that the devs are only trying to please the publisher and not the people who are trying to enjoy their game.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to skate so I thought this game would be fun but I think a sense of realism made the experience with controller kinda counter intuitive and there are certain elements of realism that either arent there or I simply didnt even get far enough to see them.Firstly whilst having the two sticks as your left and right leg (or forward and back depending on settings) is a cool idea for realism its EXTREMELY counter intuitive to the actual design of a controller. the sticks are for fine adjustment (as good as can be on a controller) and the triggers are not. So not only does it result in the movement being inaccurate as all hell but the amount of times I accidentally kick flipped because literally EVERY GAME uses the left stick for movement meant for a frustrating time. I feel like adding this was an idea anyone could have come up with and is more of a question of SHOULD you do this in your game rather than COULD you... and in my opinion the answer is no. either make it an option to turn on or use the controller how it was DESIGNED to be used.Secondly the animations are horrible, getting on and off your board and even a lot of the movement other than the tricks literally looks and feels like a joke. Your skateboard teleports into your hands and to the floor, theres no real system for falling off you just simply ragdoll which looks really really stupid... no trying to save yourself with your arms. nothing. just a basic ragdoll. You could hit something slightly off the side of the board and simply just faceplant into the floor it looks incredibly stupid. and for what is meant to be a sim... this is a pretty poor effort to have such little decent animation.The graphics are meh. Honestly, they look like 2010 graphics. Playing on highest settings in 2k looks below average for 2023, again in a sim the graphics are kinda important. Tying into this even with pedestrians on the world feels so dead its not even funny but I do appreciate you can turn the pedestrians on or offLastly there is just such a lack of polish from lackluster and missing sound effects (like when you pick up your board not only is there no animation but there isnt even a sound that plays for popping the board up or anything).Look all in all I am sure some people will like this but for the price and for me this just doesnt cut it. It is meant to be a Sim but its not really an all inclusive one, it scratches the surface, maybe? at best? which leaves it kinda dull and frustrating at times. No ability to adjust your trucks or your bearings, next to no customisation for your skating position other than standard and goofy. The only real sim part here really is the tricks to a certain degree but thats just NOT the whole picture thats just a part of it and to charge $56.95 at full price for that.... well... lets just say I am going to wait for Skate 4 when it comes out later this year.

_childDocuments_.review: Session is a great game for fans of skateboarding and skateboarding simulators because it thrives on realism. The game may be very difficult at first but after some time and practice it becomes easier and easier (much like real skateboarding.) It's the most realistic skateboarding simulator in the video game market at the moment, from the controls, the difficulty, and even the feeling of repeating the same trick attempt to nail it perfectly. It also includes many challenges that incentivize players to find new spots and re-create famous skateboarding tricks landed in those spots in real life over the years, which is rewarding to long-term fans of skateboarding, and educating to new fans of the sport.  A downside is that it is still in early access, so there are a lot of bugs. Certain grinds are very choppy and jarring, the camera replay system is very basic, the animations can be glitchy. However, because the game is still in very early access, it shows promise for something much better coming in the future as the developers continue to work on the game.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Skater (in the past) this game is awesome! BUT... play the game without the music.The game is going to be brilliant when it is completed, there is so much to do in this little section that you get from the beta purchase. It actually feels like i'm skating again as age caught up with me and this is the next best thing.The controls took a little getting used to after playing skate 3 for many years and being able to do all tricks from one stick, you now have two sticks which act as each foot. There is even an option in the menu to catch your own board after tricks instead of you catching it automatically, which gives it even more of a realistic feel. If your a fan of skate then i highly recommend this.The replay editor is very good and easy to use and the object dropper during game is a nice touch that i really enjoyed from skate 3. I have spend hours making my own lines up and trying to perfect them. Even when you fall of (which you will A LOT) there is a sense of accomplishment when you land the tricks you planned out. The game makes you think of your next trick instead of knowing you can land basically anything like you can in other skateboarding games.The only bad thing about the game is the soundtrack, i have been playing it for hours with the music off, By far to many swear words on every single song and I dont see the point in it to be honest, where is the rock and punk music that many skaters listen to also as this seems to be all rap type music.....Play the game with the music off as it spoils the experience hugely.

_childDocuments_.review: Session: Skate Sim is an amazing skateboarding simulator. It's very easy to get lost in the world and just play for hours. It's easy to play, graphically stunning and an amazing skating journey awaits with this game!✅ Amazing story✅ A variety of difficulties✅ Simple Controls ✅ Fun gameplay✅ Moddable ✅ Amazing Replay mode⛔️ There are some bugs and glitches but they don't happen a lot.The gameplay involves a lot of different elements. Skating, Walking and Replay Mode are three of the major elements in there.The skating is quite easy to pick up and has many ways to customise how easy it is or how realistic it is. Sometimes you may encounter a bug or two but the majority of the time you will be completely fine. There is a whole load of tricks you can do in this game and so many different ways to do them fakie, switch, nollie etc. Theres an advanced options section where you can control gravity, push speed, low pop hight, high pop hight, max speed, flip speed, scoop speed and much more.There's not too much to do in off board mode, you can walk run jump and use the object mode. You can get on and off your skateboard by pressing Y on xbox or triangle on playstation. You can use object mode by pressing LB (left button) but you have to be off your board to do so. There's more about object mode below.You can use object mode by pressing LB (left button) but you have to be off your board to do so. There's tons of Objects you can buy at the skate shops (more info on skate shops below). You can place rotate and edit Misc items, Ramps and rails. There's tons of cool spots you can make with just the object mode and I can't wait to see what you guys come up with.There is 3 skate shops in session 1 in each city. You can buy many decks, board rails, riser pads, trucks, wheels, ramps, rails and clothing items. There's many actual skate brands like santa cruz, welcome etc.The music playlist is amazing. Board Sounds, rail sounds and all the different surfaces have different sounds. You can tell the developers care about the sound in the game because it is just amazing.The game does have a  bugs and glitches but so does every game. The main bugs are some story mode missions need you to switch stance to goofy or regular. Sometimes you'll need to go to your marker twice as the first time your player is bugged and cant move. But really these are small inconveniences that wont really affect the whole gameplay.Session: Skate Sim is a overall good game with a nice community and I think you should just  If you end up not liking it (I'm 99% sure you will), Give it a review on steam and say why you don't like it. But what I can say is I've enjoyed it and I think you will too! Unless your not into skateboarding simulators? Which is weird because your reading this review on a skating game.

_childDocuments_.review: SESSION is the skateboarding game for folks who want a mechanically rich and challenging but ultimately rewarding virtual skateboarding experience. In Session every flip trick, every manual, every grind is performed almost exactly as it would be in real life with your thumbs and two joysticks filling in for the part of your legs and two feet. This means you'll probably spent your first hour bailing and crashing into every rail, ledge and stair set in NYC but if you choose to persist and put in the practice, working on your flip tricks, understanding which stick is which foot and how your stance can effect the way in which you control your board at any given moment you'll find one of the most satisfying and skill based experiences in video games. The moment it all starts to click and 45mins of slams pays off with that super crispy Heelflip to Tailslide down a handrail I can guarantee you'll be hooked and looking for that next trick, that next line and find yourself diving deeper into Session's board control mechanics to get more technical and go bigger than you did before.Even in it's early access state I cannot recommend Session enough to fans of the genre, IRL skaters, and even newcomers looking for something that is 100% committed to delivering a unique and deep experience like no other. It can only get bigger and better from here so why not support a great small development team and join in on the fun now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: : This game is better than ever. It's tough to master, but very rewarding. The visuals, controls, and customizations are . Session is easily the best skateboarding game, and perhaps the most important title since the original THPS. You may see frustrated reviews about certain aspects, but I suspect much of it is exacerbated by the relatively steep learning curve. I implore you to try it for yourself and give it some time to familiarize yourself with the controls. The career mode does a decent job introducing different concepts at a reasonable pace (the skate shop meetup being a possible exception--feel free to pm if you need help here). I was fortunate to get it at a lower pre-1.0 price, but this game is worth every cent of its full cost and more. (I will note that I'm on PC, which seems to be the best-optimized platform. So, that may affect your experience.)----(Edit: I've read some harsh reviews and I gotta say, I think they're unwarranted. (Part of me thinks some reviewers have a personal vendetta because the game is harder than they expected.) It's not a perfect game, but it is damn good. Also, calling the devs "money grubbers" is disingenuous. What Crea-ture is trying to accomplish is immensely complicated and time-consuming--read: expensive. Of course they're looking to make money. Plus, it's still in early access; I expect a lot of complaints to be addressed when we get 1.0. I wouldn't recommend waiting until the full release when you can get it for cheaper now. It's still an amazing game as it is, so why not get it when it's half the price of the competition. You can get used to the controls and enjoy the updated/fixed version when it finally comes out and you've already paid for it.)Having recently gotten back into gaming, I started playing remakes of the old THPS series. While fun, the over-the-top arcade style doesn't have as much replayability for me. I went looking to see if someone had made a more realistic sim-type skate game by now, and came across Session and XL.After researching both titles and watching many gameplay vids, I decided to try Session first. And I'll just say, I'm positive it was the right choice. I'll be honest, this game was hard for me to pick up--almost too much. I'm still far from the skill level I want to be, but I also haven't played nearly as much as some people (started toward the end of August 2022). The learning curve is steeper than I usually tolerate, but the reward is commensurately satisfying. My first ollie was a moment of pride; my first grind, a veritable triumph. Aside from the odd glitch, the level of realism is wild. The graphics are excellent and getting better each update. Some have poked fun at the story/career, but I see it as a clever way of introducing new tricks/techniques at a manageable pace. CONS: There are definitely boundary glitches from time to time, but not anything close to deal breaking. Linking manuals together is currently 100% impossible for me. I've given up at this point. You don't fall/bail/crash as much as you probably should. And there is no animation for picking up or getting on your board. However, I'm positive all of these issues and more will be addressed eventually, imminently even, for many of them.Session is not only a better game than the competition; it also costs considerably less. I found it on sale via an external outlet for $16. But it's well worth the 24.99 Steam price. I recommend getting it now if you're on the fence. Expect the price to go up when the full release launches end of September.In short, Session is more realistic, more rewarding, and has better graphics than any skateboarding game I've ever seen. It's a much better game than its biggest "competitor" for (currently) ~half the price.

_childDocuments_.review: TO GET A FULL SENSE READ THE WHOLE REVIEW:Ok so I've played this game for a few hours and I can tell you its pretty fun. The skateboarding itself is very satisfying and the tricks are smooth and feel awesome to land. Grinds are pretty hard though, still haven't gotten the hang of them yet. If you've read a bunch of reviews saying the controls are sh*t, I'll tell you right now those people have never skated in their lives. This appeals to a true skater, or a person who is willing to take 30 mins to get the hang of the controls. Turning seems a bit weird at first but I got the hang of it after 5 mins of just cruising around. The fact that joysticks represent different legs is also weird at first, and if you've played Skate 3 then they will seem very unnatural, but, again, the controls take at most 15 mins to get the feel of and then they seem very natural and if you've skated irl you get the hang of it faster as the control of the legs is meant to represent real life. I'll list a few pros and cons about the game if you're still not sure:PROS:- As a skater, I find the skating in the game very realistic and satisfying, just like real life.- Cruising and trick controls seem incredibly weird at first, but takes very little time to get used to them, and even less time if you've skated irl.- Good deck and character customisation. I find the 'OG' character incredibly hilarious due to his unfinished model and the funky physics of the hair when doing tricks (ik this game is still in early access).- Found that the tutorial dialogue is quite funny and adds a nice touch to the game, like making fun of pushing mongo.- Map is absolutely massive for an early access game. Very big map with tons of ramps and rails and ledges to grind on.- Replay editor is very nice, even though it seems a little unfinished but at the stage it is at right now it is very impressive.- Quite a big variety of tricks right now, but hope to see more in the future.- Pretty cheap price for such a big and well developed (for early access) game.CONS:- Controls can be funky and weird to get used to.- Not as big a variety of tricks as I'd like to see.- No NPC's or moving cars (yet).- Grinds and slides can be very hard and takes some time to get used to, but it's just like real life.- Quality of game decreases MASSIVELY when going from high to medium to low.- No multiplayer (yet).- Small variety of in-game music, and only one artist.WHAT I'D LIKE TO SEE:- More tricks and harder tricks that require combinations of joystick movements, like casper stalls, dark slides, nollie late flip, late flips...- Fixing the 'OG' character, as hilarious as it is.- More customisation for deck and character would be nice.- NPC's.- Campaign.- Multiplayer, battles against other skaters (like pros).- More music or the ability to add own music to the game.- Maybe make it so that the character doesn't ragdoll when he hits small things like curbs or cones, and maybe he like jumps of his board and stumbles but doesn't ragdoll.If you're still not sure whether to buy the game, watch some game play.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels great. After you get down turning and lock down how your feet behave, it's pretty fluid and feels very true to skating. The aiming grinds is great, as well as most flip tricks. Those aspects work together great and feel like they should. Your character has weight and doesn't feel overly arcade-esc. Camera editor is a neat add. And to why the thumbs down: Tutorial needs a bit of work, but i guess that's because beyond the flipping and turning... there's not anything else to the game. The spin tricks are near impossible to understand. I'm mostly guessing on any of the ways to spin when i jump down stuff. You CAN'T grab [yes i know it's an experimental, but it's useless]. Character is very alien looking regardless of what you do in the editor. The city feels cool and is fun for about ten hours. Then you've tricked on almost every edge in the city... and heard your same 5 songs thousand times. There are no moving cars, npc's of any kind... or any life to the game. It's missing a lot of skate aspects:There is no boneless/no comply system.There is no wall ride system/ There is no vert system AT ALLThere is no footplant system. There is no hippy jumps.There is no freestyle tricks. Manuals work.... sometimes. There is no forward flips, impossibles, late tricks of any kind, noseblunt/blunt powerslides, primo, no real darkslide/casper. Quite frankly, this feels early alpha. With the amount of work this game needs and the rate they've put out content [oh wait, none since i've bought the game in almost 4 months] it won't ever be completed. This game NEEDS to be on the steam workshop and have a true park editor so users can download fanmade stuff if devs are this slow to add new things... "Freedom of expression" right?

_childDocuments_.review: There are two recently released or yet-to-be-released games which claim to be Tony Hawk's Pro Skater with actual physics, where you control each foot individually rather than relying on button mashing or combos. They are Session and SkaterXL.I chose Session because I heard complaints that SkaterXL was lacking in content, and was essentially more tech demo than game. Unfortunately, Session isn't much better. While it is in Early Access and more content may be coming, for now there are only four maps and no clear goal. It's basically a very limited sandbox mode and little else.But that isn't my main gripe with the game. The "realistic" physics based controls which sounded so interesting are such a pain, for example every time you change stance (which often happens for seemingly no reason) the thumbstick controls swap over to reflect this, making muscle memory and remembering techniques damn near impossible.The camera is in the most godawful position, making it difficult to see upcoming obstacles, especially grinds and especially as you turn. And on top of all this, respawning is broken. If you bail out trying to grind on, say, a park bench, chances are you will respawn , where the mere act of pushing yourself forward will get your foot stuck and you will crash again.Tl;dr: good idea, really badly executed. Maybe see how it is once it's out of Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: Non-IRL-skater review:Most reviews boil down to "game is good if you add mods"  but I wanted to test the opposite. I have only played vanilla thus far, as you can see about 50h. There's a lot of content, some is filler other teaches you core mechanics (every mechanic is unlocked by default). In this perioid I finished all the missions, story or otherwise save from the hidden ones and phone ones (did a few of them). I had a good amount of fun, some frustration and definitely looked up fakie full cab flips on youtube twice. Skateboarding isn't easy and this game let's you know about it in intimate detail. Review will start with the bad stuff cause I want them seen and ideally addressed by the developers.Negatives / Constructive Criticism:- Game is officioally past 1.0 stage of development but feels unpolished mechanic, cosmetic, goal tracking and animation wise. It's usually fun to play but you're definitely not getting too immersed, a bug is waiting around the corner be it invisible rocks, weird collisions with your feet, board, walls, ground etc. This is about 10% of all gameplay. Too much for a 1.0 release imho. Oh and sometimes landing a trick required even when the game registers it, won't trigger the mission checkpoint. - DLCs are short on content / value for the money, means that someone from the team is a little too hungry for profit, which is fine as long as the value is delivered.- Few more animations need to be mo-capped, like running off your board, throwing down your board to ride it, rolling away from a bail parkour style... Like does my guy really have to fall face first into the sidewalk when I'm rolling with brisk walking pace into it? Or when I hit the imaginary rocks? At a certain speed it might be the case but that's 1% of the cases. - Rethink manuals,they might work with a perfect stick controller (ps5 maybe), but I for example have MSI GC30s which are kinda some of the best you can get and yet they're not sensitive enough to pick up what I am doing. I had a really hard time with the Daewon missions and still can't pull off cool looking fluent manual combos. - Models are very lame / cloned - none of the pro skaters look like themselves, some are downright funny. You can't stick a jpg over the same polygons we have much better technology available in 2023. My friend that's making a 3d fighting game for the first time has added himself and his gf as test players and their faces look super similar to real life. Ijs. Clothes clip through other clothes more often than not. - Controls are a bit difficult to "get" first time around, you might need 5-15 h to "land more than you bail" depending on your skill level and experience with this genre. This is slightly offset by the fact you can literally affect the gameplay and physics via sliders from the in-game menu, making a varying degree of difficulty and removing crutch by crutch until you become an independent skater controlling both feet, rotation, pivot and catching each trick manually. It can get as realistic as you want to make it, but there are ways to make it arcadey too.- Add a face editor, add beards, add shorts. These things are QOL and need to be in the base game.Now for some of the positives, as I am ultimately recommending this game:- Fully customizable physics and gameplay. It can be as hands-on or as automated as you like. You won't be able to get THPS' arcade level of ease but it's still miles above manual catch hell.- You can change weather, day/night, add pedestrians, edit their density etc.- 3 big maps-with many locations- Skate shops sell cool merch, and you get enough money to buy all you need and want after a few days of playing and mission progress.- Your board gets wear and tear and can even break, then you only keep the trucks and wheels.- Graphics are descent but I wish for better fps optimization.- Plenty of content- Mod community is alive and well but it's not really on Nexus, you gotta download some mod editor first, JL Nightmare on youtube has the scoop on that. I'll be dipping my toes in modded Session soon enough and might update this review then. EDIT: Had to come tell y'all the mods are cool and all but definitely set up the Physics Menu that right there is a life changer, you can select faces, gender, new clothes, backpack, haircuts etc with actual physics seemlessly as you play. There's also an autoload feature so that your custom character stays the same when you load another map. I had my guy riding in Timbs holding a glizzy in his hand with an MF DOOM mask on and dreads with his cap backwards and shirt open going crazy bumping Cooking Soul in his airpods. Oh and his backpack had on all kids of cans, tools, a gameboy and YOU GET THE PICTURE this stuff is fun!- Ultimately, the game is fun and rewarding as it is, as you can see by my play time. It's not an ideal example of good execution but it's not a buggy mess either. What made me buy it is the devs clearly working on it and updating it as they go. Last year I've bootlegged a copy and played around 10ish hours so I can see and tell big improvements since that version, a much more playable game. It's pretty much the best looking and most easily customizable skating simulation we got at the moment. Pick it up on sale and have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh hell yeah, this is the best skater game right now (even tho it's in early access) and definitely worth the price. I've never played the Skate franchise, so I needed time to get comfortable with the controls, but when you'll learn how to play the game it becomes an incredible experience. (There's also controller layout for those who have played Skate, but it is highly recommended to use the game's default settings). You get a big chunk of New York as you playground and you get access to a prop dropper, to insert a kicker, rail or some lamps for better lighting if needed. The game is focused on street skating, so you got flips, grinds/slides and basic manuals. No grabs or Mullen's kinda freestyle here! It's essentially a free skate mode, no objectives, no story. You don't skate to win a competition, or to progress a story. You skate here for the experience of skating. You'll need to use your surroundings and creativity to creat a line, which you'll fail hundreds of time, but when you nail it, you'll get a feeling of pride and accomplishement that surpasses every lootbox opening.  You can customize your character, however since that is not the main feature it is in an early state. You get daily, weekly and historic challenges to earn ingame money (right now this is useless, but later they add more customization items and you can buy those for ingame currency). Daily and weekly is quite self explanatory, Do X amount of trick type at a certain spot. Historic challenges are much more tricky. If you want to do it on your own, watch a bunch of old skater videos which were filmed in NYC, find the spot and replicate the tricks! Just amazing. There's also a game of SKATE mode, still in beta (and only local game), but it's fun anyway.  The controls in depth are simple but incredibly tight. The speed of you flicking the stick determines the speed of the flip, you can turn on the manual catch, so you'll be able to do double-triple flips. The left stick is your left foot, the right stick is your right foot. I don't know what would be more simple than that and this helps you visualize what you need to do, to do a certain trick.  If you want to share your best tricks/lines you can, because there’s an ingame replay system which lets you just simply record and save what you just did, or you can set up camera angles and edit a montage on spot, without leaving the game.  So what's the catch? Well, since this game is still in Early Access, you'll experience plenty bugs. "Broken" ankles, clipping, tricks not registering/goofy trick names are still buggy, random bails. Also i've got a now quite old pc and i needed to lower the quality to maintain a stabil 60 FPS, but this is a problem on my side, not the game's fault. If you already know that you'll only care about the gameplay (as i said earlier play this game for the pure experience of skating and using your creativity), then you'll dismiss the bugs, and have a wonderful experience.PS: yeah, there's Skater XL, a similar skating game, but so far i enjoyed Session more, but I'm keeping an eye on that one aswell. Debating these games are like comparing BF to CoD. Same genre, different style. Find the one that suits you better and enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of Session since the day I first heard of it and the proposed unique controls. I couldn't contribute to the Kickstarter, but I joined Early Access back in 2020. I'm stating this so it's clear why I'm no longer a fan of Crea-ture as a dev company: They didn't communicate well with their supporters all throughout early access, and once they were picked up by Nacon, they rushed a still very incomplete game to launch on consoles. They put focus on cosmetic things that no one asked for (like shades, full body costumes, etc.) and never fixed longstanding gameplay issues that remain unaddressed to this day-literally YEARS into this game. Session has had incredible potential to be one of the greatest skateboarding sims ever (if not the greatest), but it has been plagued by ham-handed dev team management, a lack of listening to the fans, and honestly really bad marketing (sorry Donovan, but a competent social media manager you are not, though you've improved marginally since launch).The core gameplay was based on a cavalier control system wherein each stick on a controller corresponds to a foot, but I don't think many people play it that way from what I can tell. The theme is 90s golden age skateboarding, and I think the game does a great job of representing that by being raw and unpolished, unfortunately. Animations are glitchy STILL, some don't exist at all (goofy stance, grabs, the majority of lip tricks, even just throwing down and picking up your board, etc.), and there is no multiplayer support whatsoever, so you just skate in a vacuum with zombie pedestrians who populate annoyingly right where you are constantly.I hardly play now, and it looks like there's no endgame in sight as always. They've been dropping dlc of maps and things that honestly could've waited until they got the core gameplay experience locked in, and those wear out quickly as you can't really skate them the way you'd like to with all the glitches and experimental features that remain unaddressed. Ultimately, Session has just become tired. Wait for Skate. (Skate 4) It's already shaping up to be a FAR superior skateboarding experience.EDIT: Checking in in July 2024, and now the devs are saying they're moving to Unreal Engine 5, something they told us they couldn't do in the past. Supposedly, that'll make multiplayer a potentially accessible feature. As it stands, the game is still pretty much the same as when I originally left this review. Only time will tell if it gets better.

There are places for Arcade style games and they are a blast, but sometimes you want more of a challenge. Session offers that realistic challenge. It isn't uncommon to sit at a spot in session for a few Hours trying to perfect the line or the single trick you have been attempting all Session. But for me that is the fun! Once you land that trick it is a similar feeling to real life! Now that is to me, my taste isn't everyones taste, so take that for what it's worth.I will say, the learning curve is very steep. When I first started playing Session I was going to quit because I couldn't get the controls down. But once I was able to wrap my mind around the controls, I was off to the races and haven't looked back since. This game is tough, but super fun and rewarding. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool skateboarding sim. Very innovating in the controls department. The sticks serve as your feet, and you turn using the triggers. Definitely a big learning curve, and if you're coming from the skate franchise it's gonna take you a while to get used to, but once you get the basics down and start to improve you'll start to understand the level of reward that comes from knowing how to play this game. It becomes very satisfying to learn new tricks and land them, although it can be a pretty painful process. Visually the game is stunning. Having visited some of the real life locations that are in the game, the map design is pretty accurate to their real life counterparts. The game still is early access, and this can be quite clear at times. I've ran into a few small bugs here and there, but nothing game breaking. In terms of content the game is lacking. I'm not quite sure of the direction the developer has in mind for this game, but as of right now this is a barebones skateboarding simulator and that's it. No story, very little dialogue, and not much in terms of customization when comparing it to other skateboarding games. There is no multiplayer, however there is quite an active community of people who enjoy this game and the developers seem to be pretty transparent about future updates and content coming to the game. This has all the potential in the world to be a fantastic skating game. With continued support from the developers and an active community of players, this is a game I can see myself coming back to for quite a while and I am very excited to see what the future has in store for Session.

With it being up there with some of my favorites such as Skate 3 or the Tony Hawk's Underground series. From the lovely modern settings you play around in, and the more diverse options for things to do. Session is setting itself as a sandbox skating game all about getting from it as much as you put in.Freeroam in the game is fluid, with you being able to find most areas that lead to other levels. These said levels ranging from being quite expansive such as the starting level. Or more compact ones like the skate parks. NPCs can be found and will have jobs you can do. While you're also given challenges as well to break up any monotony. Or feel free to go around as you please and just do tricks until you're satisfied with the solid controls. With several available levels, character customization and board customization. Session offers a decent amount of options, although some aspects can feel like they could use some more attention in the future.All the skating in-game is done on controller, with Skate series style dual-stick layout. With you using the thumbsticks on your controller to map out how you move your feet. Some moves are still in development such as grab moves, but with a large amount of flip tricks, great gaps to cover, grinds and manuals.. Session allows you to pursue the gaps you want to make. Especially with the item placement menu. Where you can add ramps, tables, and rails around your levels (to a certain amount) and be able to sync up crazy combos. All throughout the game feels like the skateboarding game PC has needed for a while. And with all the updates the devs keep adding, bringing in new settings, tweaks to recording your skater, new levels and just more things to do. Session might just be what we've needed with Skate 4 not coming out for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: First I want to say - this is ultimately a good game. But it has major flaws, which may or may not ruin the experience completely. For me personally, they are not bad enough to ruin the game and I often play this to relax with a cup of coffee. This game is not a game where you try to get best scores and do some crazy stunts, this is a skateboarding simulator.It tries and mostly succeeds to capture the feeling of skateboarding. The control scheme is great, I really like the dual stick approach, the maps are OK, especially the new schoolyard DLC map. Some really iconic spots. Graphics are good and the game can be quite beautiful at times. It also runs very smoothly, atleast on my PC (i5-11400, RTX 3080 and 32GB DDR4 RAM). I can easily get 120 frames per second on highest graphical settings on 2560x1440 so no complaints there. There is a lot of customization in options to make this game feel more or less realistic, to your own liking.The replay editor which lets you save your lines and edit them is good, a little bit hard to get into but it is possible to create very realistic looking videos using it. The career mode, if you can call it that, is OK. The missions the pro skaters give you are usually good and fun to make. The pro skaters character models look like terrible though, but this does not matter to me personally.Animations are really lacking. Skateboarding itself looks quite good most of the time, tricks look natural and quite realistic but most everything else is just janky. When you bail, the skater goes full ragdoll, like they died mid-air or something. Compare this to for example Skate 3, which is nearly 14 year old game, it's not just anything like it.There is no animation getting on and off your board, period. Again, Skate 3 and even Skate 2 had this. It's a huge miss, especially if you are into making your own skate videos in-game. There is no real transistion or vert skating. There are no grab tricks. I get it, it's a street skating game but could we atleast have some basic grabs?There are a lot of weird bugs or the physics engine behaving weirdly. When you land, especially a bigger trick, your board kind of bounces around below your feet. If you ride down a 5cm drop, like a curb, often times your skater just bails. Also nollie and fakie tricks especially have to be done very far from the edge of whatever you are jumping off from, or it will result a ragdoll death. Then there is some QoL missing. Like, you can set your board to break which is cool but why must I go to apartment everytime to get a new board, other than one with blank graphics. Why can't it just replace the board with same or one of the random decks I've bought?Sometimes the session quick markers behave weirdly and you spawn and instantly bail and then spawn again. No big deal really but it makes the game look really unpolished. Which, of course, it is.If you liked EA Skate series back in the day, you might like Session. At the time of writing this review, the game is quite unpolished. It almost feels like a tech demo. For fans of skateboarding, I can give this a mild recommendation. Still, it is the best skateboarding game we have on PC currently.

_childDocuments_.review: 1.0 review here. Take this with a grain of salt if you're from the future.Basically  skateboarding sim. If a realistic skateboarding sim is what you're looking for, this is absolutely it. It's extremely addicting, and putting down lines and filming clips of them is really, really satisfying. The replay editor is really robust, too. Transition isn't there yet, but they're close, and they've made it clear in their dev timeline that it'll be coming further down the line.The mission mode is  It feels like the game's ability to determine what trick you've landed for missions has somehow gotten  in 1.0. Expect to have to redo lines that you absolutely nailed just because the game inexplicably doesn't understand that you've landed exactly what it's asked for. Also, it feels like the QA on the new missions is even worse. Misnamed missions ("Philly Truck Line" on a ledge grind/manual mission?), the second "jam" mission, you're told it's a "best trick competition" but it's programmed identically to the first jam - instead of it counting your best trick, it wants you to do as many tricks as possible, in half the time and half the space! Skill issue? Yeah absolutely. But it's still a pain. This game is really,  good at what it's good at. Meanwhile, all the afterthought stuff like the story missions are busted to hell. But still. The core gameplay genuinely, 100% makes up for it, if you're looking for a challenging skate sim that makes landing a FS bigspin lipslide down a handrail actually feel dope, Session is definitely it.

Cool intuitive way to add style to your tricks.  I found the default setting  for body rotation which is pressure too easy to over rotate. Opted for timed, now i am throwing smooth 180's variations into lines.  The catch mode I wish worked as simply as Skater XL where you click in the thumb stick and the corresponding foot catches the board. Can't seem to do flip tricks and land catching with the font foot in manual catch mode, or it's just less exaggerated compared to Skater XL. Where you can catch the board and spin with it stuck to one foot dangling. Overall having a lot of fun. As for visuals it is quite polished and looks good in it's current state. _childDocuments_.review:
Inspired by the golden era of skateboarding, Session's primary goal is to make you experience what skateboarding really is; an incredible culture where there are no other goals other than expressing your creativity and achieving success through hard work, perseverance and bits of madness for no one else other than yourself.

Be ready to play the most authentic and grounded skateboarding experience in the most legendary spots on earth, film and make the gnarliest skate parts out there.

Don't be fooled by copycats and experience the real pioneering dual stick board control feature! Session offers for the first time a per foot stick control giving you the full power in your hands where each stick represents a foot. Careful though, skating switch now has a real meaning.

Filming has always been a big part of the skateboarding culture. With Session's video editor players can perform their tricks; edit, and create a montage in-game.

Explore the best and most iconic skate spots, starting with New-York which helped shape what street skating is today. Recreated on a 1:1 scale and supported by grounded and realistic skate physics, get the feel of what it is to skate the infamous Brooklyn Banks and our fresh twist of the surrounding financial district of Manhattan."

name: Tails Noir
detailed_description: You’re not special. You’re not a hero. Thrust into unfortunate circumstances, you find yourself with no other option than to unravel what might be your biggest case yet. There is no choice. We change, but we change nothing. Get to work, detective. Tails Noir is a post-noir narrative adventure. Become raccoon private eye Howard Lotor and explore dystopian Vancouver inhabited by animals as you uncover a deeply personal story of change and transformation. Tails Noir is inspired by film noir, weird sci-fi, post-soviet aesthetics, modern political regimes, the works of Lynch and Kaufman, and existential philosophy of Sartre. It is a linear, cinematic narrative experience that subverts genre and challenges your perception of what it means to be a person. Tails Noir’s gameplay is focused on storytelling and emotional expression, featuring rich and elaborate dialogues inspired by old school CRPGs, as well as exploration of the lush environments. The end of all things is inevitable, but defining which version of Howard Lotor reaches the conclusion is up to you. As Howard, you will: • Make meaningful connections with a diverse cast of characters in pursuit of truth • Shape and express your identity through dialogue choices - decide what kind of person you want to be • Explore and experience both downtrodden and flourishing districts of a strange, yet familiar version of Vancouver • Come to terms with the universal pain of existence and loss • Be a raccoon Post-noir dystopia Tails Noir's Vancouver is a dangerous place, bleak and dreary, but not entirely without hope. It’s a tale of a cold and uncaring world, interspersed with genuine connections and a bruised but undying drive to make a difference. Everyone wants to change the world, but not always for the better. Stunning visuals The breathtaking combination of high-resolution pixel art and 3D effects like dynamic lighting, pouring rain, volumetric fog and neon lights bring the sprawling City to life. Visit iconic Vancouver locations like Gastown, Granville and Fairmont Hotel, reimagined in a world now inhabited by anthropomorphic animals. Evocative and unforgettable soundtrack Original doom jazz soundtrack by Danshin and Arooj Aftab features an innovative combination of classic jazz and electronic music. Tails Noir’s OST is expertly crafted to create a cinematic, atmospheric, and simply jaw-dropping soundscape that serves and enhances storytelling.

There weren't much gimicks or puzzle because all in all, it feel like all i had to do is make sure I click on everything and go through everything. Things like having an inventory tab and picking up item feels bit redundant to the gameplay if all the player had to do is just walk left and right and go through dialgogue. Still Im actually quite hooked in the story and all the mystery. But i feel that the ending really left me feeling that: IS THAT REALLY THE END? Because there wasnt any conclusion towards anything at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I was patiently waiting for this game for what felt like forever, and I can say now that I've completed a playthrough of the story, Backbone has successfully delivered on some of my expectations and been upsetting at others. Backbone is built on a strong noir story and memorable and likable characters. I think if you enjoyed the demo like I did, there's some more of that in the full game, and I would even say its worth experiencing for the characters, music, and art style, as they are probably the strongest parts of this game. I think for what I expected out of the game, Backbone is good, but not quite great.I do agree that one thing that was missed from the prologue was more active participation in what Howard actually does on screen. Following the prologue, there is only one other stealth section, and both of them are pretty short. I think people who are coming into this game expecting to sneak around and solve the mystery single-handedly are going to be dissapointed by what the game actually offers. Even though there is only one ending to the game, so your actions and dialogue choices really only matter within the scope of the conversation, the dialogue is all that players have to keep them engaged with the story.If you buy this game, you should go into it understanding that you aren't playing it so much as a hero of the story, but more a surveyor of the plot as it unfolds and reveals its different twists. I get that a lot of people would rather be more active in the game and how the story unfolds, and so I understand that this game really isn't for everyone. And even for those who do want that more passive experience, the story has struggles of its own, namely the strange sci-fi elements, and how short the final two acts of the game are. The final act especially feels very detached from the rest of the story, and goes in a direction that makes me wish the story had been a bit simpler and stuck very closely to the original premise of the prologue.Despite some gripes, this game is well written and a great story experience overall, highlights for me being Acts 1, 3, and 4.  And the developers have stated there will be more from this universe coming out, so there's promise of more of the characters and story. I think if you had any interest in this game, whether playing the prologue or just checking out the trailers. It's an experience worth having as long as you understand it's more like experiencing a book or show than a more traditional game. Definitely would recommend this game to anyone interested, just maybe wait until it goes on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: a hard game to review, everything's there depends on your point of view for life.it shows itself reservedly, although one playthrough last from 3 to 6 hours.relationship between Howard the Detective and Renee depends on your choice - trust her or not.there's only One ending, and it tells a little more than nothing, so give it a try and figure it out for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: great art, great writing, great music, great vibes, doesnt over stay its welcome. i loved this, i can only assume the negative reviews for this game is because some people are upset it wasnt exactly what they wanted, instead of appreciating what it does bring to the table, sad i slept on it for so long, give it a try
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: A very linear narrative game with no puzzles. While the graphics and "noir" ambiance are great, the dialogues are often short and contrived. The story isn't particularly innovative or well delivered : the final twist is overall a very common science fiction trope, and not particularly explored either.The ending is cut short and clearly done either to launch a sequel, or because of a lack of ideas/time...Overall quite disappointed : not a point & click (no difficulty at all), and the story isn't developed or compelling enough to make it a good narrative game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Good Game and amazing narrative written and told. Loved the story, characters and pixel art all the way through the game. Noted a few bugs:1. _childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Almost great. The art, some of the music, most of the characterization, and half of the narrative were delightful. Sometimes it felt like my decisions made a difference in the game and playstyle, other times it felt railroaded. The story jumped the shark and went into Evangelion-eqc wannabe psychology suddenly. It pushed some well made arcs together a little quickly and once the character does the stupid thing to enable the 2nd half it's mostly downhill. Ending on sequel bait is also not satisfying. I enjoyed much of it, but can't give a recommendation with the narrative spoiled when it's the backbone of the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say I don't recommend Backbone. The story is rich and the characters engaging. I feel most of the mixed reviews arrived from mixed expectations from the games early release material. The game itself has a rich vibrant story and narrative, helping to set a setting and feel that is unique. I remember my first play though (and only play through) as enjoyable and I ended up sitting through it almost in one sitting. It was truly engaging. That said the game leaves you with the same feeling as Omensight at its ending, which without spoilers, is a let down to a overall engaging and thematic setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone has an interesting premise and stunning visuals. The visuals alone can easily sell the game.But you spend most of the game in dialogues. Even the inventory items can't be used directly, they just add options to dialogues. Is that a problem? Well.In Disco Elysium, dialogues are a fun game mechanics, you have to think what to say to whom. In The Banner Saga, one wrong choice can lead to a death of a key character. In Ace Attorney, the dialogues contain info that you need to solve puzzles and find contraindications. In all the above the dialogues are exceptionally well written.Backbone has none of that.The detective part of the story is interesting to follow. The second part (whatever that was) is just weird. The twist in the end comes out of nowhere, changes the whole narrative and tries to be a social commentary on themes that were barely explored during the game. On top of that, the game has technical issues. Some of them block progression. And you can lose your saves.I would definitely buy another game with a similar art style. But I would hesitate to buy games from this studio again.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I truly adore this game. This is the first game, i have ever finished. The art style, the music and the overall atmosphere of Backbone is perfect. The amount of times i got goosebumps from moments, were insane. The storyline was very unexpected, i went into this blind and unaware of what would happen, this made the experience SO much better. Backbone deserves ALL the hype, and i wish it was more popular, The ending did seem a bit rushed and it would have been better if it gave a *tiny* bit more information of clue as to what happened, what might happen etc. HOWEVER, this does leave room for a sequel, prequel or whatever it may be. and it gives room for the player to speculate for themselves. I really do recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like the writing team was fired and replaced half way through the game.First half is a fun film noir story with so much potential.Second half is a rushed mess which needlessly jumps the shark into a different genre and fails to address the mystery of the first half of the game.Don't expect to find a satisfying story here.Visuals are nice. Music is fine.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was decent, nothing too amazing. I agree that the story was maybe a little hit or miss. But what I think really gets this game a good review is the visuals and the music.Both of these things are spectacular and really make the game for me personally. And the writing early on is also very good, for example the demo. That was a good trip.The best analogy I can make for this game is like comparing a Steven Moffat episode to a Steven Moffat season. For example The empty child is one of the best episodes of all time while series 7 was extremely ehhIn the end I still would recommend a playthrough but maybe not much more than that.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I was severely upset to learn this game had a linear path and contained such a lack of lore. As you start the game and throughout the first half many things ramp up, you learn cool puzzles and have plenty of interesting choices as well as more than one way to approach an obstacle, but you are soon severely let down as soon as you learn through an evenly paced middle that the third section is underwhelming and utilizes none of what it has used before. The ending is depressing - which is not a necessarily bad thing - but moreover leaves many unanswered questions, more than just being let to one's imagination.Overall I'm genuinely sad. The art direction is beautiful, the characters make themselves known and make you feel a good connection with them, and so many concepts had such great potential, but this game feels extremely unfinished. I'm left craving but in the end I'm given just as much an injustice as the main character.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Here is the deal, I really like this game, and got very into it's characters. but there were several times that I wanted more control, I wanted the way I played to have a bigger impact on the outcome, this seems to get worse the closer to the end of the game you get, sure the game offers you options but in the end maybe some dialog changed. I can forgive most of this railroading because it is such a great game and you should play it, (even if some of the messages are almost comically shoved into dialog out of nowhere). just know going in that no matter what you say or do the same sad sucky ending will play out and you will have ZERO resolution.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: This game had so much potential in the beginning. A great setting, good characters, good direction, and a stunning art style. Yet the devs decide to throw it all away in the name of "pseudo-depth" and a plot-twist, I suppose. You start the game finding the answers to some questions and in the end, none of the questions are answered, yet you are left with even greater questions with no answers to anything in sight.I wouldn't recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: As has been said before, this game could've done with a bit more of the polishing that the Prologue got. The messages of class conciousness and the evils of the rich were heavy-handed, yes, but honestly it doesn't really detract and it's not like the prologue didn't make it clear that the game would deal with that, so for those of you surprised by this, well. Perhaps you should engage in some reading comprehension courses. At risk of spoiling, there were some existential bits at the end that were eh, so-so. They make you think or they make you scoff, either way you acknowledge them. I would've liked for your choices to have made more of an impact. They make an impact to some degree such as the dialogue paths or little interactions here and there, but that's about it. I wasn't disappointed by this, just intrigued by the direction it took. I'll replay it for sure. Could've used a chapter select feature, some more puzzles or ability to interact with NPCs in a meaningful way.This game feels like it'll have a sequel and i'll probably buy and play it too.The world building was great! As was the art! The city and the world felt real and living and vivid and should be commended!

_childDocuments_.review: It's stylish. It's beautiful. The music is amazing. It sets a great mood. The prologue was amazing.What went wrong?I had been looking forward to this for years now, and it feels like the game just tripped over itself. There are serious hallmarks that the game was rushed to completion. The game that had been promised at the beginning is not the game we got later. I'll do my best to be brief.One big problem is that there are multiple mechanics that are irrelevant past the beginning (the prologue). The game tutorializes concepts like your inventory and the ability to examine objects, moving things around on a table. This is used a bit later to solve a small puzzle to figure out a passcode. Neither of these appear anywhere later in the game. At no point do you ever examine objects, nor do you have any need for an inventory. On the rare instances where you do pick up items, they're only used that exact location and automatically used. The trailer also showed combat that does not appear in the game. Another example is that the game has a map, but that's meaningless because at no point can you choose where to go. You're shuttled from location to location with no input from the player.Given that the game basically throws away all semblance of "gameplay" away, that means it has to rely wholly on its narrative to carry it, and it falls apart there as well. The game has a nasty tendency to take current events and use them to "bridge" to a larger situation, but then it just ignores what came before it. The multiple mysteries we're looking into never get resolved. We start looking for multiple missing girls, one character says he knows what happened to them and that's the last we talk about that. Even the central gambit is handwaved away during a conversation in the last act.Everyone talks about the 3rd to 4th act transition, and it's a big one. The game takes a hard, hard left turn into sci-fi at that point and it, unfortunately, also goes nowhere. A main character is killed and this is given very, very little attention whereupon we transition to a location and meet a whole lot of characters who mean nothing to the plot (a common problem). It's all wrapped up in this vague non-explanation for why it matters and after a perspective shift we listen to a conversation where the villain insists that what they did was for a good cause, but none of this ever comes to fruition. Then we're left with an ending that's like the one to Inside but without having deserved it.The characters? Some are interesting for sure, but unfortunately conversations are very "utilitarian." The prologue has some depth to the characters, but once you leave the first location that dries up rapidly. Conversations proceed with only what's necessary to move the plot forward and don't spend much time on development. The exception is the aforementioned location where everyone is given the beginnings of personality and mini-arcs, complete with little conflicts between them, but that's immediately cast aside when we get taken to the next location. Never brought up again. The final act (titled "Epilogue" for absolutely no reason because the plot hadn't concluded yet), launches us into a discussion between the villain and our partner that, apropos of nothing at all, transitions into gender politics and larger social issues. This hadn't been brought up prior, and doesn't have anything to actually say. They're just thrown in there to give the appearance of depth when the game has none.Backbone is a game that is amazing at setting a mood and laying down a premise, but absolutely failed at exploring it. The locations appear rich and full of life, but you're allowed to interact with exceptionally little of it. Characters seem like they're fleshed out, but don't offer anything past your initial conversation with them. On multiple occasions someone seems critical to the plot and there's a dramatic scene with them and then they're never mentioned again. To put it simple, the game broke my heart a little. I'd been waiting so long for it, bought it the minute it went live, and less than four hours later I was wildly, wildly disappointed.If you want a game that has a similar aesthetic but much stronger writing and gameplay, pick up Chicken Police.

There were many points where it felt like the story had either stalled or skipped over itself in a way that legt the narrative choppy and the “twist” felt belated and half baked in how it tied into the conclusion.
