_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game, some of the best pixel art I've seen, in a nice parallax enabled 2.5D environment. Great music. Unfortunately the story goes from a classic tension filled noir to grinding to an absolute halt about midway. It then gets so tedious I was literally checking my watch as the story crawled on and everything ends unresolved. The half baked mechanics also suggest it was meant to be a different game where that actually matters, and the sneak function isn't just used for 2 sections that can't fail.I wouldn't even recommend this on sale. Enjoy the pixel art in pictures instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game from the moment the prologue came out. This game looks beautiful, and I enjoyed the experience, now having played through the game.That being said though, I have to admit it's a bit of a disappointment. It's awfully short at around 5 hrs of gameplay, and unfortunately the prologue ended up being the best and most interesting part of the game.I feel as if none of the story that we were introduced to in the prologue was sufficiently solved, or brought to a satisfying conclusion.This isn't an LA Noire style game with different cases and investigations as I might have been hoping, but a borderline visual novel with one singular investigation that's never really finished.I hate to not recommend this game, because I was ecstatic that it had finally come out. Unfortunately though, I think it's best to maybe just watch a playthrough online and see the outcome for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game since finishing the prologue. It had me intrigued from the start with its fantastic graphics and well-written neo-noir dialogues. The art style blends modern lighting with a 2D side scroller and it's gorgeous to look at. There’s a lot more detail than you’d likely see in a regular pixel art game, with windows populated by people going about their business. It’s a pretty nice-looking title overall, with the world being the real star here. Every character is thought out well, unique and has its own distinct personality. This accompanied by a great jazz soundtrack is a must-play for me. And don't get me wrong: noir titles featuring anthropomorphic animals are often a hit or miss. I disliked 'Chicken Police' so much I couldn't play more than 30 minutes of it. Blacksad is alright, but I should get back to playing it again sometime. So it's pretty clear that while Backbone fits into the same genre, it's a completely different game. In a good way, like The Wolf Among Us. The gameplay isn't difficult at all. Everything you can interact with is guided by an icon, so it's hard to get stuck. You may 'get caught' in certain stealth levels. They could've used some more work in my opinion, but that could be featured in a future patch. Even if you did get caught, you have a checkpoint right at the start of the stealth section. It isn't that big of a deal. The game could've benefited greatly from a bit of dialogue, ambient sounds, just anything. Right now you're spending quite a bit of the game in silence, listening to your computer fans whizzing while you're trying to read a great piece of conversation. That's a bummer, but again, that's something that hopefully will be added in the near future.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most intriguing games I have ever played, played it first when the prologue demo initially came out. After waiting patiently for the full release of the game I can truly say it was worth the wait, without spoilers it does get dark and existential towards the end but in personal opinion one of the best stories that I have read in quite some time!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only really recommending because I think it's worth the experience. Soundtrack, the atmosphere, and characters have a unique touch to them.From midpoint onwards tho, it does feel like the game was rushed because there were a lot of gaps in the story that doesn't really get answered and just kinda confused me for the most part. There's a lot of tension throughout the game, but most of it ends up being unsatisfying - it doesn't feel like it's completely resolved. The game has decent replayability, but it doesn't feel like you're finding something new every single playthrough.Again, unique experience just that it could've been executed a lot better.

_childDocuments_.review: it is a very good game with quite an interesting story but i do wish that you'd have more control over the story itself and that your choices affected it in some way. the only reason im not recommending the game is because of the price and if you're interested by this game, i definitely recommend checking it out but i would also recommend waiting for it to be on sale to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is kinda janky, pretty short, and I'm not sure how the branching paths work. There isn't much gameplay, and the walking sequences aren't really my jam. _childDocuments_.review: Now, I have never done a review but I guess i'll give it a go for this game since I have a few things to say and the game just recently released.(see my recommendation at the bottom of post, the rest is critique and opinions)I was first introduced to backbone around 2020 to 2019 when it's first demo chapter came out. I loved this demo and I recommend it to anybody just for the visual experience. Backbone is certainly an interesting game. It has its up and its downs. First I'll talk about its downs.Backbone's first chapter is a little deceiving. It was at least for me. The first chapter is a noir puzzle adventure type game with some stunning art direction and nice storytelling. It gave you multiple options to solve certain puzzles which gave it some replay value. But compared to the rest of the chapters it kinda seems outta line. The rest of the game is a walking and talking type game. You don't get a lot of puzzles and when you do they're quite simple and easy to solve. The story completely derails from chapter one and instead of turning into a dark noir game turns into a- i suppose it turns into a more sci-fi alien apocalypse game? With probable inspiration of venom. It completely shifts gears into something you wouldn't expect. Which surprised me since it felt like the game was advertised as a noir game instead of a more sci-fi future-esc game. It also kinda starts to turn into a classism thing? It starts talking about revolution and freedom which sorta feels outta line. The villains in the story are kinda iffy. One gets completely abandon (atleast what it felt like to me) and there are alot of lose plot threads in their story. Another does get mention and seems important to the story but honestly isn't. They're just sorta teased to be the big bad guy without showing it to us directly. There is no clear bad guy in the story which on its own isn't a bad thing perse but there is a clear setup for two of the characters and yet the writers didn't take it. Opting to not fully develop those plotlines further. It's honestly kinda disappointing if that was the story you were looking for.Now the story overall. I don't hate it honestly. I think the game plays with some interesting concepts and ideas. It just didn't develop those ideas and concepts fully. It leaves alot to be desired. Which sucks because the game could've had such an amazing story if it did so. Unfortunately that isn't the case and it feels like the writers abandoned the main story to develop a side story. Which inevitable became the main quest. I also feel like most of the characters were underutilized. Many of them had interesting relationships with the main character. They had interesting stories that I wish we could've seen. Yet the game has only about 4 to 5 hours of gameplay which doesn't allow the characters to really grow on you or time to develop. The only character I personally was able to connect with was a goose and the main character. Which should say quite a bit. And I wanted to be attached to these characters. I really tried but there just wasn't enough time and there was alot happening. Now, with all that negative talk do I dislike backbone? No, I don't, I like backbone quite a bit. Like I said it has compelling ideas it plays with. Which i really hope that later on maybe those concepts could be explored further. I like the art design, most of the game play elements even though some are very underutilized. I like the characters even if I couldn't get attached to them. I just wish the game could've been longer. Because it would've been an amazing slowburn story. I liked the sections when you weren't actively participating in the main quest and just learning about some of the characters.  I like that you had to pick with who you wanted to hang out with so you can choose who you get to know better. I just wanted those types of sections lasted longer than they did.The music in Backbone is also great. I wish they had more atmosphere music though. Many of the sections I played were very silent and I often thought my sound was off. There were some minor spelling errors every so often but they weren't distracting from the main events. I feel like some of the dialog options really didn't matter in certain moments which really devalued the whole "pick your own narrative" type game this seemed to be. Of course I get this. This isn't a big studio type game but I want it to improve because I like the idea that they had. I just wish the game had been longer and that the plot and characters got more development. So would i recommend this game? That depends. If you're expecting a full noir experience then no. If you just want a fun casual story with some neat ideas, sure! Go right ahead and support this game. For price recommendations you shouldn't look at my review. I have no idea what kind of price this game would be good at. Anyway, have a nice day :)! And hopefully you get to enjoy the game if you buy it! (Also excuse my english)
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I will start this review by stating that I never played the original prologue demo for the game. I will also say that I have never made a game myself so I do not know what this team went through to get this out the door. What I will say is that there were great gameplay mechanics (puzzles, stealth, multiple paths) introduced at the start that get discarded quickly. At the end of the day, I could forgive the game for all of those great mechanics disappearing. What I really dislike about this game is the way it handles it's pacing and story. The story was both a crime thriller and a sci-fi psychological horror; each of which felt very incomplete and disconnected from one-another. In my opinion. there was a great story to be told on the crime thriller side if the last quarter was rewritten to fit the rest of the story.What I will tell you is that the musical score and pixel are in this game is to die for. I am constantly listening to the soundtrack at work and it is some seriously excellent noir music! The pixel art is wonderful with lighting being used in full affect here. Also, the use of animal humanoids instead of regular humans allows the game to tell a mature and dark story without being hopelessly depressing.There are very good things about this game but don't expect perfection.Please note:I WILL HELP PAY TO GIVE THIS GAME A DIRECTORS CUT/REWORK!

_childDocuments_.review: Upon reading a lot of these comments, I couldn't help but feel compelled to provide my own perspective on the game itself, and perhaps address a few trends I'm noticing among said comments... Not necessarily to justify anything, but at the very least to counterbalance a lot of the more negative reviews... Generally I don't leave reviews for games.. But this one is very much deserving.To begin, It might be beneficial to understand what exactly it means for a piece of media to be classified as "Noir" before diving in... A quick google search will give you that much, for sure... Defining it now would ruin a lot of the experience if you were to purchase a copy. But for simplicity: Noir genres address the more serious nature of, at the very least in Backbone's case, a fictional sci-fi setting (which doesn't get brought up too much until the end of the game... more on pacing later). These worlds and settings are cruel and unforgiving... And no doubt it's that unforgiving nature that can leave a bitter taste in the players mouth upon completion.With that said, I think that disappointment MEANS the game was successful. I cried, myself. That's exactly what a game like this is supposed to do. When I finished it, I scoured the achievements list to see if there was any kind of alternative paths similar to games like Undertale way back when... But I discovered that a more accurate comparison would be to that of Night in the Woods, where your dialogue choices merely influence your own individual character's thoughts or interactions later on. This change isn't much... But in a world like this where everyone is enduring hardship and is openly defensive and hostile, it might soothe you to know that you can risk pissing off a fellow here or there to get more information that you otherwise wouldn't have gotten by trying to tread on sticks. Upon having made this discovery, I felt... Somewhat soothed that this was the intent of the game. That everything you played was intended to amount to one particular ending... So then I started to question why? What was the goal here? I knew the game MEANT something... Because if it didn't mean anything I wouldn't have felt so moved, I wouldn't have grieved an anthropomorphic raccoon and his foxy equivalent from a video game lmao. I felt attached to these characters, and I could relate to their hardships... Especially in a setting like this where individuals seemed confined and limited by the society or environment in which they were born into. I wanted an underdog story. I wanted Mr. Lotor to succeed... But I think it's obvious if you've read other reviews or even if you're capable of making inferences on mine that this didn't exactly happen. And that heartbreak was deliberate.So then I started to analyze the societal dynamic... The rich eating the poor, medication isn't free, racism, sexism, class-ism... the whole nine yards. I think it's rather obvious that these things aren't exactly new to many of us, and are particularly prominent in first world society as well, which is to say that they are exactly that: present. And they're things we're familiar with and can relate to... Which brings me to problem number two: the execution of these concepts... I understand that this is long as it is... So to keep this review easier on the eyes, I'll spoiler areas such as the following ones that are not nearly as condensed or summarized.But after having thoroughly looked over the state of this city, I wanted to know  it had come to be this way... Even just a  would've sufficed... But we're left guessing... Even here... Not only was I left dissatisfied with the story, But I was inevitably dissatisfied with the lack of elaboration or understanding of the history of this world... The specifics of how it functions... And in a variety of ways I just felt... Ultimately Betrayed... It was like my grandfather had died but I wasn't invited to the funeral... I didn't have any kind of closure, and I was forced to accept the loss of something great. I couldn't fall asleep after having completed it at 3 am... My mouth was agape for five hours trying to cope with the loss of a story so powerful. But then I realized: I can play it again!!! I can choose different dialogue options and learn more the second time... Experience it similarly, though not the same admittedly... And I can cherish every moment the second time.I mean it when I say it.. This game is just an absolute experience... I didn't even touch on the Soundtrack OR the art direction. If you've watched the game trailer you'd know just how good both are. The prologue portion of the game is absolutely charming, debatably more interactive than other portions of the game... sort of. But it shifts and changes into something more peculiar, albeit.  But with the knowledge that a second game in this world of Backbone is in the works, I like to believe that most of my curiosity will be quenched. But as it stands they seem to be able to tug at my heart strings rather effectively, so perhaps I'll have to break up with this game all over again... Please have mercy lmao.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Pretty good, nice art and sound; minor complaints, a little rough but awesome buildup from Chpts. 1-2, but from 3 on sucked monkeybutt.           I first saw this game as a demo around a year back, and I've finally gotten around to finishing it, and boy, it was a doozy. I've never been fond of the 'dystopian' genre, but the premise of this game was at least intriguing enough to give it a chance, but generally the dystopian stories I've read, and now played, go from pandering, to interesting, to intriguing, to pandering. But I wanted to go through this game and see what it had to offer.      Visuals - 8.5/10 (Astounding!) | Overall, this game has impressive visuals, from character art, animation, and weight, as well as color, scale, detail, and Character from the simple background object, to the overarching environments utilizing both 2d and 3d Rendering techniques makes for a visually impressive game, despite a few oddities coming from the clash of its color palette and discerning important objects from the un-interactable environment.     Sound and Music - 7/10 (Mostly Great.) | The Music in this game is awesome; the noir, jazz, and synth blend give this dark and abrasive blend something that parallels the game wonderfully. Sometimes the music can be TOO abrasive, with some synths overpowering the rest of the mix, and being a little too adventurous for what the general theme is to be for a certain area. I.e. A bridge full of homeless people should not have a calm track interrupted with an ear-piercing synth.   Gameplay 5/10 (It's a story game, this isn't even its focus) | This rating is just a neutral way to say "you could've done this differently. It isn't bad, but it isn't unique." In other words, a story-based game like Night In The Woods still includes more platforming to differentiate segments of talking, world-building, and interacting with the environment in a simple yet fulfilling way. But the 'Sneaky' sequences are a dime-a-dozen and are rarely seen after being in The Bite.      I Can't give a specific #/10 for this part, but if I could choose a range, I'd say 3-7/10. The first chapters of this game, it was an awe-inspiring introduction to a wide world with a thick backstory, and a few ways to indulge in it if you took the time to [literally] listen. But the main character (although being a good option for players to imprint themselves) seems to have a mixed-bag of dialogue choices ranging from; Neutral, Forward, '♥♥♥♥ you!', and a jokey other response that contrasts with the story's tone. The best example is when you first get to The Bite in the prologue when you go from friendly or pushy [as the player decides] to "Oh ♥♥♥♥, ♥♥♥♥, ♥♥♥♥, ♥♥♥♥!" These seem to clash with what the story is trying to tell: a moving, or at least intriguing story about control, class, or society, all juxtaposed with talking to a 'geezer' that gives you seemingly pivotal information, only to affirm a character's feelings later in the Epilogue. Things like this show, at least to me, writing that is trying to make a wide world, but focusing and tripping on itself when trying to do it.      Stepping back for a second, the dialogue options make you think your choices affect how you go to the next point, which, after getting in the Bite, are more or less giving you fewer dialogue options to play with before transitioning to the next section. Like getting information out of the Scientist, or finding the Artifact, certain scenes are just checkpoints to go to the next act that lose their perceived agency or weight as the player realizes: "Oh, my choices don't matter as much as I thought, huh?" It's not a new problem; a developer can only do so much in one game or account for so many possibilities, but even the slightest choices like, 'I have to choose how to go through with this.' or, 'I have to decide who to be with today.' with a certain gameplay loop can lessen this disappointing feeling, but in this game, a distinctive gameplay loop other than 'explore>talk' can't give this kind of effect. 	In short, the story after Act 1 and most of Act 2, seems rough to a degree that, it was not thought out as much as it needed, rushed to meet a deadline, or fumbled to make the impact it wanted to with the story and gameplay beats it had. But, with the new Backbone sequel-prequel-sequel thing, I just hope it not only explores the great world they could've had, while still remaining true to its attempted themes and tone while remaining self-contained -- Not relying on it being a sequel-prequel thing, or whatever will come of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone is a classic noir experience that innovates by introducing aspects rarely seen in noir. It has fascinating characters and an intriguing story; both of these aspects being expertly woven into a solid game. The most immediate aspect of Backbone is its excellently written dialogue. While it does occasionally suffer from interrogation-itis, the dialogue flows naturally and can leave you wishing you said something else. There are times that it’s clear that all options would lead to the same answer, but most of those cases are well reasoned within context. The characters are well defined through the dialogue, and the responses available allow for a wide range of ways for the player to react to the fascinating characters. I can personally say that I have not found another game that recreates conversations so naturally as Backbone.The gameplay of Backbone shines as a refined and modern interpretation of point and click adventure games. While the interaction that the player can exercise on the world is streamlined, it helps bring focus to the dialogue and the story. A hangover of the adventure game basis is a mostly useless inventory. While items in your inventory do contribute to moments in the story, it serves more of a purpose as static flavour text. What puzzles there are in the game makes the rest of the experience feel severely lacking. A mechanic that is introduced fairly early in the game is to be able to closely inspect certain areas and be able to move around the items in frame. There is only one puzzle throughout the entire game that utilizes this, and it is never used again in depth. Overall, the base mechanics in Backbone is a natural evolution in adventure games, paving the way for future titles.From this point on there will be spoilers. If you don’t want the story spoiled for you, just know that it is amazing and worth the price alone. You have been warned. Backbone made bold decisions when it comes to what is to be expected from a traditional noir setting, namely the inclusion of sci-fi elements. That might be a bit too far ahead, so let’s roll back to the fundamentals. The story of Backbone has a near direct adherence to the themes and customs of noir, making this game an absolute joy for any noir enthusiast. However, some expecting a more rigid approach to following the conventions of noir will be disappointed with the story delving into the previously mentioned sci-fi aspects. The pacing of the overall plot is very well structured but begins to break down near the end as the story delves into more philosophical elements. The point at which this becomes the case is when the main character Howard is taken prisoner, not only by greater enemies but also his mind. From there the story branches off into different perspectives, a difficult task to do with such a well-established point of view. But these changes in perspective are handled well enough to enhance the story instead of it being dragged down by it. As the story progresses, the world around it is built up expertly, leaving the player wanting more and speculating as to the true nature of the world. However, some of the questions raised seem rather too important and instead of leaving the player satisfied with a seemingly large and fleshed out world, it leaves them thinking that some plot threads might have been dropped during production. At the end of the game the story leaves three questions unanswered to such a degree that only a sequel could amend their prominence. What is the whole deal with the Apes, how did the world come into the state that it is, and why do people want to go out into the wasteland? It leaves the story in the odd middle ground where less would have been more yet doing so would compromise the plot. It makes you wish that the studio had more money to flesh out the story further and tell the world of Backbone’s entire story.Should you buy this game? Absolutely. It is a great and emotional experience, despite its flaws. Also it’s another furry noir game to add to my list of favourite games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone is a short, short game with some pretty wonderful moments, some very underwhelming ones, and definitely a controversial game when it comes to the question "is it good?"First of all: the presentation is gorgeous. Audio and graphics are amazing, the atmosphere is pretty involving and the love for the source material (ahem, Vancouver BC) really shows. The pixel art is spot-on, the ambients are lively and detailed and the music, oh gosh it's good.In terms of gameplay, unfortunately, the game felt very underwhelming to me. If you've played the Prologue, you might remember it had segments with a bit of puzzle action, some stealth, even multiple choices in how to approach a challenge.  From that point on, that simply doesn't happen anymore. You do get to choose the order in which you might do a thing or two (literally, a thing or two), but the rest of the game is very, very linear in how you navigate and explore the space around you. No puzzles, no tinkering. Just walk left and right towards the next dialogue. The structure is more akin to a visual novel than to a detective/adventure game.If you can look past that, you'll see some moments in which the writing is great, and the game does tackle some issues that, on their own, are worth those 5 hours of gameplay alone. I did _not_ enjoy the overall plot, but there are some special moments in the game that truly felt inspiring, sincere, and more humane than many games with, well, humans. I chose to recomment the game for those moments alone and I think you should definitely experience them, but be mindful that the overarching story and the gameplay might be a huge turn-off to many players.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in good faith suggest this game to Point and Click fans :(I backed this game on Kickstarter because at the time, I was going out of my way to pursue and support games doing full releases on GOG, but what really caught my attention is that it was a Point and Click game. One look at my profile, and it’s easy to tell that I’m insane for point and clicks.Awhile after the Kickstarter, a demo version of the game came out, labelled Prologue. One of the features showcased here were puzzles for the player to solve. The puzzle mechanic is absent from the final retail version of the game, barring one or two things to solve. For this reason, I think the demo is superior to the release game. Additionally, one the features funded via Kickstarter but absent in the final game is any voice acting.  This is extremely disappointing.  The developers also backed out of their Kickstarter promise of selling a version for those running Linux operating systems without notice. Now, spoilers below, be warned!The story of the final game starts out as advertised. You’re a raccoon detective named Howard who solves routine and mundane mysteries. When one day you get a phone call, regarding disappearances of people and a request to look into it. So, your task is to talk to people who may know about it and explore a fictionalized version of Vancouver. The music and visuals of the game really help to set the tone of Backbone, and I believe is the strongest part of the game. The gameplay is also unfortunately almost fully linear, leading to the few choices you make ultimately not mattering much. The storyline on the other hand is easily what makes this a bad game. For the first and second acts, the story stays consistent within itself and reality slowly sinks in that people are being butchered for meat to be eaten by the affluent of the city for pleasure. The story after you get found out for snooping is where things go off the rails and fall apart. Not only is there a butchering murderer, but for some reason that’s also a secret laboratory with an alien symbiote in it! One thing leads to another, and it’s attached itself to Howard and you’re taken captive to prevent it from getting out. This is the point where all the plot development and atmosphere of the game goes out of the window. It’s one thing to have a giant twist late in a story, it’s another to essentially start telling a completely different story in the middle of telling another. At this point the symbiote has begun consuming and transforming you, leading to Howard trying to make an escape from the laboratory, later waking up in a rebel commune without memory of how he got there. From here on out, the game focuses on the alien sci-fi story and pretty much discards the Noir story that was happening before, all amounting to an end screen where Howard just collapses and dies, the main story AND this alien story unresolved. Upon release, I had a viewing party with a friend of mine as he played through the game. We had both been excited for years for the game to be released, so we played the game the first chance we got. This ending took all our excitement away the moment the alien laboratory appeared. We were pulled out of this murder mystery we’d been tasked with and essentially played for fools. The developers have been adamant that all this was their intention, but that still doesn’t justify the ending clashing with the rest of the story, and it ending in a disappointing fashion. I’m gonna side with the reviews on the Prologue and agree that you should skip the full game and go with just the Prologue. Also for some reason the game asks for Firewall access and I’m not sure why. On that note, the developer’s behaviors toward players asking them questions has been really poor. Case in point, a fan and player of the game simply asked the developer why Howard’s ear was damaged in the final game, when there’s scenes in the Prologue where this isn’t so. Instead of being kind to the person, the development staff and fans of the game proceeded to mock the person who asked openly, both within the game’s community discord and on the game’s official Twitter. So, in writing this review I’ve taken it upon myself to scope out why this person may have been confused, and I found my answer; the visuals for Howard are inconsistent, as seen here. These screenshots are from the Prologue version of the game, but I confirmed the frames are identical in the release version as well. Just by looking at these screenshots, you can understand why somebody would be confused as to why the ear was injured and suddenly not harmed in the next scene. As a disabled person that misses subtle details, I understand why the person that asked this question was confused, and the developers should be ashamed for helping to enable the mistreatment of this person. For the privacy of the person, I won’t be posting screenshots regarding them, they’ve had enough happen to them already. This toxic behavior from social media teams for brands has been normalized by brands like Wendy’s, and to some it’s amusing, but in my opinion the person in charge of social media for Backbone acted in bad faith toward the person that asked about Howard’s ear for clout and relevancy. In closing, just because video games are art, doesn’t mean they’re immune to criticism. An artist’s vision is imperfect, and by putting an artistic work out into the world you open yourself (and those who worked with you) to criticism for that work. For these reasons, I cannot recommend this game, and am disappointed the game turned out way different than what I bought into.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not a lot I can add to what people are already saying about the game. This is definitely a game that felt very rushed and focused more to detail on the aesthetic than the gameplay and plot themselves. I was really bummed to find out about this, especially from how good the prologue was. The story in the prologue seemed very well thought out and the idea of having to solve puzzles and sneak around areas made the game seem very intriguing. Also, the ending left me jaw-dropped in pure shock and left me sitting back trying to process everything that had happened in the hour I played.Before I talk about what I dislike, I do want to say that this game does have a good storyline. The story on it's own always left me wanting to find out what exactly was going to happen next. Of course, the art is absolutely gorgeous and the pixelated, noir aesthetic with the dystopian setting works so well together. Also, god that soundtrack is beautiful. Each song fits the emotion of the scenes so well and adds both so much intensity and so much relief as well. I was absolutely driven by this soundtrack.However, it hurts to say that I wouldn't recommend this game to people. I was so excited for this to release, but $25 for something the prologue did better than the main game is not something I would gladly praise to friends. The main game takes away all the fun puzzle components and doesn't incorporate much gameplay wise. One thing I'm very disappointed about is even with the gameplay removal, your responses do not really affect the game in the slightest. Yeah, you can get some cool achievements if you answer in different ways, but they all lead to the same events and there are no consequences to any of your actions. While I complimented the story, the plot itself leaves practically every question unanswered and feels very rushed. The last two acts on their own don't provide any answers and add on more to the plot that just never gets explained. In fact, stuff like  are completely brushed over. It feels like acts 1-3 and 4-5 are their own plotlines and that I'm playing a whole new game. Even if they were planning on having a shocking ending like in the prologue, I felt very confused and wanting more clarity since the ending itself is a beautiful and heart-wrenching scene on its own. There is just no proper conclusion and nothing to tie the game together as a whole.I'm really hoping to either see a revision of this game or even a new game with the same style by EggNut. There's a lot going for this style of game, but I think there just needs to be more focus on the gameplay and plot more than the aesthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on .Despite its advertising, the game is a linear visual novel. Your path is set from the start. Choices that you make only change the resulting flavor text, but the same events happen. There are no alternative routes, alternative paths, or real alternative choices.Linearity isn't a problem in of itself.  does well with many things. I love the world - besides being visually striking the hints of lore and avenues for expansion are tantalizing. The character interactions are endearing and memorable. It's all executed very well. Despite this, I'm disappointed. is a game that could have done with more game. We're given a great cast of characters, but their interactions aren't utilized often enough. We are introduced to new environments that could potentially serve as an introspective moment, but they fade too quickly. The world seems rife with potential for complexity and a long history, but this is only hinted at. The main story is rushed at the end, with exposition dumps serving to make clear character motivations.I'm not sure why this is the case. It's clear the developers have talent. Initial execution of everything is just so good, but it ends up falling flat. isn't a bad game. There's some room for a sequel, and I hope that one is made. This world and cast have so much potential, but for now it feels half baked. Great crust, but a sour doughy middle.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really disappointed me. After the prologue was released several months back, the game seemed very promising. The chance to be a detective thrown into a case much larger than they intended, along with the art style and overall ambiance made me wishlist the game and I looked forward to it's full release. However the game that came out was nothing like what seemed to be built up.-Spoilers Ahead-Admittedly, I'm willing to look past the abandonment of the puzzle solving that the 0451 door code that is present in the prologue alluded to, as I don't think puzzle solving is necessary to tell a compelling narrative in a linear game (though it is honestly a strange choice in a game about a detective). Furthermore, I think that the first 2 acts really start building up a good solid story that seemed like it was going to focus on modern societal issues like classism, poverty, and race.What we ended up with is a story that builds up for 3 acts, just for the finale of the 3rd act to introduce a symbiote MacGuffin and completely abandon any notion of what the story was even about. The game changes from an interesting dive into real issues, only to become an extremely worse and honestly cringey version of Disco Elysium (an amazing game by the way). It abandons it's own narrative for seemingly no reason whatsoever to instead bring up concepts like the definition of who we are and identity and existence, but it does it very, very poorly. It's so upsetting because the game literally didn't need any of this to happen. It could have just focused it's narrative on the topics it started with and told a very compelling story about the upper classes' abuse of the lower class (to the extreme point that they are literally eating them) and how the current society of The City struggles under serious racism (for instance, entire species are looked down upon and even forbidden from taking up certain jobs). It is almost as if the developers felt they were not fully capable of handling such a serious or divisive narrative and so they hand-waved it to try and seem deep and thoughtful with existential nonsense. Which if anything just confuses the whole point of the game. Even now I can't even begin to understand what the game was trying to say, because it didn't go anywhere.The game has no resolution, there is no conclusion of any of the threads brought up throughout the game save for the symbiote eventually killing your character. Renee maybe works with Clarissa to bring down "The Wall" and The Apes and quits writing her book, but that isn't something you end up actually getting to see. The high society that is consuming the flesh of the lower class narrative is never brought to a head. Anatoly gets killed for what seems to be absolutely no reason other than to make the player feel bad because "oh no you killed your best friend while basically being mind controlled." The missing girls from The Bite are just outside the wall living... somewhere. There is just no real ending and then you just die and the credits roll.The game is a disappointment, and it hurts to see that such promising concept was completely abandoned. Stories about racism and classism have real value and should be explored and to see a game pretend to be about them so heavily just to whiplash the player into trying to be existential feels tone deaf and ignorant of such serious issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I give it a negative rating, but really it's floating on the borderline.  The game has some good things going for it and some bad things going for it.Plus- The graphics look very nice.  The character sprites and backgrounds both.- The worldbuilding is very well done also.  You get spoonfed drips throughout the whole game, and there is no exposition dump or info menu that explains everything.  Just the way I like it.- The atmosphere is on point.  The music supports it well.Minus- There's very little gameplay, honestly.  You get choices of what to say constantly but the invisible hand can clearly be felt railroading you towards the same outcome.  Almost the entire game is walking and talking to people.  There's a grand total of one puzzle, and a couple half baked stealth sequences.  It needed a lot more.- The entire game was done within a mere 3 hours.  That's REALLY short.- The story is...disappointing.  This is the second "Private Eye Animals Detective Game" I've played recently, the other being Chicken Police, and that game went over the top to stick to the whole noir shtick, while this one starts off that way and then veers wildly into the bizarre and overly....let's say....artistic? about two thirds of the way through.  It's not to say it's uninteresting but it's quite weird.  It's offputting, but that's the not the real issue.  The real issue is the ending of the game is monstrously unsatisfying.  Since there's no gameplay - the game experience is completely held up by the story and at the end the story does not tie up and is left open ended.  It doesn't feel like you're getting a complete experience - it feels like the story just stopped.If you didn't have to pay for it, this would be 3 hours of decent entertainment for most.  But it's a video game, as a game, it's just not quite cutting it.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: This review was made before the game's name was changed, when this game used to be referred to as "Backbone" I still stand by my opinion here, for this is a bad game.If you thought Backbone would be a point & click style, narrative-driven detective/adventure game, you are mistaken.Backbone looks wonderful and has a good soundtrack, but everything else is awful. The "game" barely features enough gameplay to be considered a video game, as it is too restrictively linear and non-dynamic for a "game" of it's genre. There is puzzle solving, but it rarely appears outside of the intro chapter and while the game also has a menu for objectives and inventory, it is underutilised and a pointless mechanic to have.The story itself is a massive and messy disappointment. A "game" that grows into a mess with more plot threads established, barely linking to the original case shown in Backbone: Prologue. Your dialogue choices do not effect the storytelling and outcomes of a situation, and later features a shocking and insulting genre-changing twist caused by the protagonist's nonsensical action that you cannot control.I wanted to like this "game", the presentation of the "game" and it's prologue demo enticed me into it's world and characters, but after the twist happened, I've lost all care and respect for the overall story. I simply cannot continue and finish the game after it suddenly threw a curve ball into a story that did not need to over-complicate a detective story with social messages and shallowly explored plot threads.Backbone is not a good "game." Go play the free Prologue instead and that will be enough.3/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this game, because I think people should play it. The gameplay changes part way through, as others have said. But, while that was a part of what drew me in, it isn't lacking in other equally important places by a long shot. The atmosphere doesn't stop. They maintained their original commitment to give us a story and a sense of place and mood, front to back. What some would call jumping the shark, writing wise, I'm gonna call, in the case of this games narrative arc, a constant escalation of stakes. With EggNut closing it's doors, I'm especially recommending this game. It does end on a cliffhanger, and we're probably not getting a sequel. They may not be able to fully wrap up this story. But I don't want Tails to fall by the wayside because of that. This team made something truly unique imo. They made something that inspired me personally and creatively. And I think that that is as important, if not more so, than getting every bit of it perfect. New, cool things are often rough around the edges and should be appreciated for what they are. I think that if you look at the promotional materials, and like what you see, you'll have a good time with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone is a masterpiece in storytelling, as seen from the perspective of the lower-class Private Investigator Howard Lotor, and a glimpse into a life filled with struggles based on class or societal status.  Accompanied by a calm but prominent jazz soundtrack, and hands down some of the best pixel art and scene building I have ever seen, Backbone is a ride which you will not want to get off.Watch my 8 minute review here: Now I know a slower-paced, conversational game might not fit everyone’s preferences, but if you are ever going to take a chance on one, this is it.  With such a well-written and poignant story, and clever conversational choices, there is so much to unfold through personal interactions and meetings in The City.  The world-building and art is sublime, and I would rank it in my top pixel-art games I’ve ever played.  Backbone has been built up for years as a game to look forward to, and it is such a relief to be able to recommend this as an adventure that you should not miss.

_childDocuments_.review: I played and finished this some time back but needed time to fully process what I enjoyed and didn't. Lets get the big positives out of the way first+Art Style+Music+Writing+Big Set PiecesI really can't compliment the devs enough on those things and I don't feel as though I would be able to properly explain how well they were done.Now, the biggest issue with the game is that it was very clearly missing two or three more acts that would tie everything together. I would say that there's three separate plotlines going on and only one gets a conclusion. The first two work together but are left completely unresolved in order to do a rather sudden and dramatic tonal and plot shift.  The final plot could work, but it needed more time to be built up, instead it's very rushed, which makes me feel as though several acts were cut that would've fleshed all of this out.If you can look past the poor payoff and enjoy the parts of this that work, then I would greatly recommend it. However if you're looking for a complete narrative that flows properly to the next point, you will be disappointed, and I wouldn't blame you.

_childDocuments_.review: If a game was done right, it would be Backbone.The story is implemented to gameplay with heavenly smoothness. It all adds up to a breathtaking scenery. The depiction of nightlife in the city felt so real, I felt inside that world. I took the time to inspect the backgrounds, notice how my shadow reacted with the environment and spent minutes just staring at it moving from wall to wall and object to object. That water sequence after you *spoiler* was the real ♥♥♥♥. The twists and turns of the plot kept me on my toes. _childDocuments_.review: Backbone was a game I really wanted to love. I backed it on kickstarter and even beta tested the prologue via my backer access on the discord. I can only assume that somewhere during the development cycle things changed a ton, and that's fine in my opinion if you stay true to the original concept. Backbone's kickstarter trailer (outside of maybe 2 scenes) might as well be a different game because much of it is not shown in game. Ever. Seriously, you should go watch the kickstarter trailer.On the positive side though, I did enjoy the game for the most part. The environments are stunning, the music is fantastic, and there are branching dialogue options that other characters seem to react to properly, instead of having a blanket reaction to all the statements with one. The game really catches that noir vibe and doesn't let it go for much of it's duration. When you are actually engrossed in the game and it's good, it's a fun time. My biggest gripe that I need to get out of the way is . Like, crazy short for the price tag. I will give the caveat that I knew what I was doing throughout the prologue, because I had played it before. But everything else was new to me and I still managed to finish in just over 4 hours. And probably less than that cause I do recall stepping away form my PC a few times. Because this game is so short I feel like there's some pacing issues that need to be mentioned.  There is one particular moment where a song is playing and the entire song plays through. But you can't seem to do anything during that moment. I didn't time it but it was at least 1 minute+ of gameplay that was just you staring at the screen. I thought perhaps I had missed some interactivity during the moment, but really it was just downtime where I  you were supposed to watch a character "sing" along to the song. I feel like some dialogue happening or some extra animations would have made it more interesting.Another big gripe is that the gameplay is eventually reduced to a dialogue simulator. The game is saying it's a point-and-click adventure with stealth and puzzles but the stealth segments and puzzles are very rare. I understand the main character is a PI but it didn't seem like many of the dialogue options actually had a fail option, so you always got the information you needed regardless of what you said. I don't think the lack of a failing option is a bad thing, the game definitely lacked challenge though since it's very linear in many ways. Even the dialogue options have no real effect on story.Now this is where I'm going to get very vaguely spoilery.  It just feels like everything was very rushed, especially when the game was initially supposed to be a 2019 release. I'm not happy that I have to mark this game as not recommended, I wanted it to be so much more. I'm hoping maybe with time that will change. i won't say don't play it if your heart is set on it, but I'd say wait for a sale or grab gamepass for a month to check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Review-Readers, y'all probably know it already: The game gets more & more linear and philosophical towards the end and then kind of cuts you off while you weren't looking. Roll credits. I still think the sheer amount of negative reviews is NOT what this game deserves. Why, you ask? The amount of detail is amazing, I still think much work was put into every chapter, character and location and it shows. I didn't know it at first, but I quickly fell for this corrupted and dark world and its numerous struggling characters. While there's not much to be done other than talking and walking and looking at things, it still feels as if you would do stuff all the time, just because there are these tiny little side things to discover. So when I saw the kind of rushed ending I wasn't mad or confused - I was just sad. Because the developers made me care for that Raccoon guy in his trench coat and I just wanted to go out on the streets with him again, ask Anatoly about his 12 or what kids, before strolling down to the back alley to meet up with Larry. Also, I can live with unanswered questions and kind of liked where this was going with Renee, but that's probably, or hopefully, stuff for a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: It's tough to review this one.I'll start out with the most obvious thing first: The ending is incredibly rushed. There are lots of people in the reviews who interpret this as some sort of commentary on The Human Condition, or that it's intentionally absurdist, or that if you didn't Get It you shouldn't have gone in expecting an RPG with Multiple Endings or whatever. I think these are all pretty pretentious excuses for a half baked plot. There's room for logic, and for at least some of the plot threads to be developed on, but the game never delivers. It will ask you to forgive people for doing unforgivable things, without giving you a good reason. It has themes of "getting in over your head," and I don't really expect it to spoonfeed me every last detail, but with the little information given, there's simply not enough to go off of to reach a satisfying conclusion. If you're someone who values a strong, meaningful ending above all else, this simply isn't the game for you.However! There's a lot else going for this game. The visuals are gorgeous in a way that you just won't understand from looking at a few short clips. Locations are beautifully rancid, and disgustingly opulent, all wrapped into one. I've never felt more at home at homeless camp, and more perturbed at a cozy suburb. Even the characters with only a dozen words to their name feel full of life, and really sell the setting. And before the story ran out of stops to pull, I really was hooked. I do desperately want to learn more about all these characters and their lives.So considering all that, I can't *not* recommend it. I feel disappointed, having played it. It had so much of what I wanted, but failed to stick the landing. But knowing this going in, I hope maybe you'll be able to appreciate what's there.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is... not what i expected. don't get me wrong, it wasn't bad at all! but if you're like me and played the prologue back when this was still called backbone, you might have been expecting a tale of intrigue and mystery, delving into a conspiracy and searching for answers in a dark gritty setting, and... while yes, you do get that, it doesn't exactly stay that way. a good bit into the game, suddenly the story takes a bit of a drastic turn, and if you're not expecting it, it can feel a little like it came out of nowhere. i'll admit i was even a bit disappointed by it, since the mystery we're following takes a bit of a back seat to this new plotline, and it unfortunately sort of lost me after a bit (through no fault of its own, i was simply thrown off). while the biggest questions are given answers by the end, they feel like an afterthought to me. haven't played preludes yet, so it might have a little more of what i was hoping to see in this setting, but i'll review that separately if i play it.i would definitely recommend this game; it's got a gorgeous style and an intriguing setting and pretty good characters to boot! but if you're hoping for a long-earned, satisfying conclusion to the mystery, prepare to be left hanging. gameplay also didn't last as long as i had hoped, with my playthrough clocking in at around three hours. still worth playing, though, especially if you get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing I want to get out of the way -- yes, this game looks good, as you can tell from the screenshots. It is consistently detailed, fluid, moodily-lit, and gorgeous. Moving on...I can't say that I was satisfied by this game. It was fun, and I felt like there was depth there, but it was overshadowed by a sense of disjointedness. The overall plot is easy to follow, but a significant portion of the dialogues took some jarring twists and sudden shifts -- even before the events of the final chapter (no spoilers). The sense I was left with was one of having listened to about an hour of something between beat poetry and jazz scat, played in a dimly-lit bar, air hazy with smoke, with a couple glasses of whiskey having passed my lips. Atmospheric, yes. Pretty, yes. Conclusive, no. But maybe that's what was intended, with its noir influences dressed up and paraded, stage front and center. It's a love letter to the genre, with the last paragraph made up of newspaper and magazine clippings.(Side note: At the time I played this, I had some trouble dragging-and-dropping some items using a controller. Hoping that gets fixed.)

_childDocuments_.review: Some spoilers contained ahead.I only became familiar with Backbone about a week prior to the game's release. So it's fair to say I did not have a lot of accumulated expectations. I found the artwork, environment, sound effects, music and overall mood of the world comprehensive and captivating. I can honestly say I have not come across a game of this genre that's looked this good in a long time. World building is important and I'd say this team nailed that. The puzzle solving and challenges posed in the Prologue were spot on - I really felt the sense of urgency and curiosity as I got Lotor into The Bite. I can't think of too many titles that actually got me to care about the plight of the protagonists this early in the game.Unfortunately this style of problem solving gameplay ends with the Prologue and the rest of the game becomes fairly linear storytelling from there. Now the linearity is hidden pretty well with number of side characters the player can interact with and the amount of response options given, which can change the tone of any conversation - but ultimately there are no actual options other than the one conclusion the story is destined for. Now that's not to say the story isn't any good. I thought it was pretty captivating initially. I found most of the main characters and side NPCs multi-dimensional and interesting enough to go out of my way to talk to. The plot driver with the underground cannibal cult and its deep ties to city politics was gripping and I had hoped this would have unraveled as the game progressed. However, towards the middle of the game this plot point stops developing and gets dropped almost entirely for what is, in my opinion, and far less riveting sci-fi oriented plot device that carries the story to its conclusion. Maybe it's my personal tastes, but I just did not care for the sci-fi turn the story took. Probably because it's a trope that's been done to death in film and other works of fiction, but I digress. I appreciated the more risky decision to have a tragic ending rather than a happy-go-lucky-hero-saves-the-day ending, as I found it appropriate for the noir genre Backbone is harkening to. It left the ending just ambiguous enough for a sequel, as Lotor's fate wasn't entirely clear to me and there were so many loose ends left untied.Lastly, there is quite a bit of low-key ideological messaging that has little to directly do with the story and gets more insistent by Act 4. This could be off-putting if you're not into that sort of thing. On as side note, a character belonging to a known real-life politically charged figure also makes a cameo in Act 4 - if you know who she is, you'll know her when you see her.  I won't go into details, because I think it's all a matter of personal opinion anyway.I would still recommend this game, because it's downright beautiful and the story is -interesting enough-. I'm honestly quite amazed what such a small development team managed to create. I hope to see bigger and better projects from EggNut in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: First 2/3 of the game is traditional neo noir and it does a great job of telling that story. Visually its beautiful, the pixle art, animations and the lighting is done very well.  The world is also incredibly fleshed out, you really get the impression that it is a living and breathing city.  In the last third it takes a hard left into science fiction which was honestly unexpected.  The ending of the game leaves you with a want for more and I see other reviews bashing the writing for it but in honesty it follows the traditional arc of a neo noir story and I don't know if I can really blame it for that. The ending is inconclusive, neither a good ending or a bad one its just the way things kind of went for protagonist.  As a piece of story telling it can be dissected, examined and interpreted a million different ways and I feel that a part of it value as a story is in it's ability to provoke thought in the player. My advise is to get the game on sale.  Its good storytelling yes and its pretty to look at but I wouldn't pay 30 loonies for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am so torn about this game. First, without spoiling, I wish for optional endings. _childDocuments_.review: Objectively there is no way this game should be $25. A 3 to 6 hour game that has no branching paths and very little replay value should never cost this much. Liking a game is of course subjective. I really wanted to like this game. It has a great sound track and the first 2.5 Acts are a masterpiece. The first 2.5 Acts are just a fun detective romp and then the wheels just fall off. The game abandons the great story that it had been building and turns into a disappointing slog until its end. While I have many issues with the numerous unresolved plot lines and awful story shift halfway through; The biggest problem for me is cost and length. It would be one thing if a single play through of this game took 3 to 6 hours but there were also different endings you could get. The ending of act 2 for instance would be a great point to split the story into different paths. But this game only has the one short linear path. It is highway robbery that this game costs as much as it does. If you choose to buy this game wait until it either: A. has steep discount or B. Has additional story added.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a cute little game that is very aesthetic. I had a lot of fun playing through it but it does have its faultsThe ending left me with a sense of dread and it didn't really help anything when i learned that there were no other endings. I feel like they game was leading up to something bigger but ultimately kinda fell off after Howard had came into contact with the artifact. I feel like there was suppose to be multiple endings but it was never implemented. This game had a lot of potential and in the end, kinda let me down.Despite its flaws, i truly do think this is an outstanding game that just needed a little more time to develop. The characters were so engaging and they felt real. They all had their personalities and wasn't bound to the main plot of the story. The settings blew me away. This is kinda rare for me in a pixelated game but it accomplished it. Every new place was so different from the others and there was so much to look at. There were points in the game that actually made me tear up. The music was impactfull and evoked the right emotion for what was going on. If this game had more time to develop, i truly believe it could be something better but unfortunately the game is over 4 years old now so there's no chance it will ever be updated. _childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, it's pretty and the first few chapters are intriguing, but... then it just switches the story half way through, leaving the main investigation unsolved and the implications of the 'twist' are completely ignored for the greater world because it just... ends.The villains are never defeated or ousted, what happens to your principle ally is never developed or mentioned again and there are no puzzles, no consequences and just... nothing. Which was a shame as it was really engrossing up until it just 'stopped', half done. Your choices don't matter and nothing has any effect. Maybe that was the point. _childDocuments_.review: The story is interesting, immersive and sometimes fun. _childDocuments_.review: Don't be discouraged by the mixed reviews - if you enjoy noir and point & Click adventures, you will get a lot out of this game. While the execution of its story and gameplay elements falters at times, this is a game with a lot of thought, polish, and a solid "backbone" to it. Definitely worth a try if this type of game is up your alley, particularly if you don't mind it leaning more towards "visual novel" than puzzle-based adventure. Pros+Gorgeous, creative art style (both background and characters design)+Good dialogue options+Likeable characters+Great word building+Story is solid and has a lot of potential for future chapters, which I think is their plan. Subverts expectations in the latter half of the game.Cons-Act 1 (which was the demo) promised multiple pathways to complete objectives. The rest of the game is quite linear.-Act 1 also involved some puzzle elements, which are notably absent from the rest of the game-Did not focus enough on building chemistry between the main character (Howard) and his supposed Partner (Renee)-Latter half of the game (particularly the end) felt a bit rushed and unsatisfying. They could have spent a little more time fleshing some story elements out, but this may have been deliberate choice to keep things ambiguous. This game, as a first installment, shows a lot of promise for a potential series, especially if the developers take the criticism above (which has been repeated by other reviewers) and implement some changes to make the multiple choices/puzzles more consistent throughout future games. However, if viewed as a completely stand-alone game, the latter half does feel unsatisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: Original review - 28th November 2022 - Game was Called BackboneMy review after one play thought it only takes about 2-3 hours to complete but I went AFK for a bit.I'll be honest act one is a compelling start for the game. The plot for act one is finding a person and photographing them but they turn up dead. The start was great would recommend it. Also, the jazz in the bar is just 10/10.In act two we have introduced some new characters and some more fun. the music is also just really awesome. Partway through act two leaning towards the end, it starts to drop off a lot. At the start of act three, the stories make a little less sense.That's right you're not playing a detective murder game. I can't describe it but the story and telling start to become weird and misshaped. It hints at the butterfly effect (The butterfly effect is the idea of changing small things that can lead to having an impact on a system) but it doesn't feel like one of these games. Like the choices are there but you are almost always funneled into them. You have no  There are long walking scenes that drag on and characters that you will only see once and never again. By act four this game is a shell of what it was in act one. The story has been a curve ball to something totally out of conception. It feels very out of place and in your face.By act five  what you've just played is a fever dream and makes almost no sense like a fever dream. From where we started to where we came the story lost its way and became deteriorated almost like paper soaked in water. The music and SFX stayed awesome throughout. Characters I enjoyed but there isn't much depth to them. The story seems like a work in progress. They try to incorporate what Guy Ritchie does in his movies with multiple story lines but it's far too late unless the game is part of an overarching story. I also did play the demo a few years ago on a friends account and did thoroughly enjoy it.I will be replaying this game again to try and understand more and get achievements. My ratings are below (first run through):Characters 8/10SFX 6/10Score/music 9/10Replay ability 5/10 Story WTFAct one 8/10Act two 7/10Act three 5/10Act four 3/10Act five 2/10Review Made 23/09/2023 * The game had a name change to Tails NoirMuch of my analysis and thought are mostly the same. Ok so I've played this game extensively since the last review and can honestly say that I enjoyed this game overall. The music is just awesome and the sfx are pretty damn good. The art is just interesting to me being a dystopia story with a dark and almost creepy setting. The story makes much more sense and the characters are dynamic and full of witty banter and cheeky little remarks. Replay-ability 9/10Story - 9/10Sound -8/10Music - 10/10Acts:1 - 10/10 Great introduction to the story, characters and setting2 - 9/10 Gives us a bit more backbone to the story and the setting of the world3 - 9/10 The real meat and fat to the game, characters are getting stories webbed out and the story is progressing.4 - 6/10 The progress kinda slows down a lot here and all the momentum is kind of lost. till expands on the story but not as good as other acts.5 - 7/10 The Game kinda finishes poorly for what was anticipated and what we were led to believe. It makes you feel like you've been robbed of a good ending. Although the Ending of this game sets up for the next it does seem strange that the next release was a predecessor to the story not a successor. Having this game rely more on flashbacks to event that weren't playable in the current game but in the next which was still in development and unreleased.Overall though I absolutely love this game and do think that it is important to the story like how some people like myself Jojo's Bizarre Adventure Part 1. Doesn't have as much flashiness or appeal as the other parts/ However, it has importance for setting up the story. I rate this game overall a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with immersive music. Love the vibe. Fun and simple gameplay, good writing. I had no idea where the story was it was going which was quite intriguing. I'm impressed with how they manage to show so much detail with so few pixels. However, I found the last act to be a bit too jarring compared to the rest of the game, and the ending was somewhat anticlimactic, at least to me. _childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to recommend this game. I personally got it for free and as such, it was a pretty good experience. The atmosphere is on point, the stylized 2D graphics are gorgeous, the sound design is really good, the characters are endearing and the writing is (mostly) really competent.I enjoyed playing through the first three chapters a lot, classic point & click gameplay with good dialogue and story buildup ? Who could ask for more ?However the writing really falls short at the end. I feel like the writers wanted to make their ending very existential and deep, but it didn't fit the vibe previously established at all. It just felt kinda confusing, out of theme and underwhelming. That would've been totally fine if there had been several endings, but no. Your choices in paths and dialogue don't impact the story in the slightest, which sucks. Gotta hate illusion of choice.To sum up, if you like this style of game, give it a try. It's not a bad time and has some great stuff in it here and there, which is why it's so frustrating that it doesn't fully meet it's potential.

_childDocuments_.review: This is literally one of those games that you HAVE to think like a Noir detective to get the right answers and progress the story in a more positive light.  There were times I was the nice detective, got me blocked from certain areas hence doing more to achieve the goal.  There were times I was the hard-ass detective and it got me through without a problem.  Here's the things, the scenarios are vice-versa depending on the situation.  This is definitely a game you have to "read the room".  Multiple ways to go about interviewing and progressing the path of the story.  The game play is short, roughly 5-7 hours depending.  The music is on par with the style and atmosphere.  The characters are gripping and really make you immerse in the world.  20/10 would recommend.**About to start my second run to make different choices.UPDATEDon't get this game. Even with additional dialogue, there's no escaping how sideways this game turned from the middle to the end.  Highly disappointed, a waste of kickstarter money, years waiting, and for what? _childDocuments_.review: //SPOILER REVIEW//I have been looking forward to this game for around half a year when my friends and I stumbled across the prologue. As soon as a completed the prologue I fell in love with the game and was intrigued by the story. I kept up with the development and played the prologue several times as I could not contain my excitement. When the release date was announced I was thrilled and my excitement was overflowing.That takes us to the release date. I bought the Artifact Edition and have yet to read the script but plan to. Gameplay wise I wish there was more puzzles, the only one I can think of is the code puzzle towards the start of the game but since I played the prologue so many times I already knew the code so I got through it pretty quickly. Other than puzzles the gameplay is quite plain but there is nothing wrong with that, it is more of a story driven game so gameplay isn't at the forefront and there is not much to talk about, but story wise there is  far more to talk about.I personally loved the story and loved the conversations between characters, Renee is my personal favourite character and I loved her relationship with Howard especially towards at the end when she says that she misses him and talks about how relationships like theirs are few and far between my only wish is that it would last longer (maybe could be done through a DLC that I would 100% buy). Anatoly and Howard's relationship was also special, I just felt like they worked well together and was horrified when Howard killed him against his own will. I wish the lore was explored a bit more as I was intrigued about what was outside the wall and what happened before the present time in game. The story itself was great although I wish it lasted longer. Towards the end when it gets trippy and when Howard is talking to the artifact really reminded me of Disco Elysium and when you talk to your mind which I love. I also love the end where you play as both Clarissa and Renee for a short time and propose to team up to find Howard. My favourite part has to be when your vibing under the bridge with all the streeties and when your vibing playing the harmonica and it's just all ruined by Sooz plus the music when your all sitting around the fire vibing to the song "The Warmth of Parents' Hands" which is a great segue to music.The music in this game is superb, I'm not a professional music critic nor do I play any instrument but to me the music is absolutely perfect I listened to the music in the prologue far too many times and "Abode" is one of my favourite songs of all time but the full soundtrack is even better. Nikita and Arooj Aftab did a fantastic job on this soundtrack and I will be listening it for the next few weeks.In conclusion the game is great and the music is too. Although my only wish is that they continue the story whether it be through DLC or a free update. Anyway game's great, go play it now or I'll get Sooz on you.

_childDocuments_.review: (Spoiler Heavy Review!!!)I wish I could recommend this game, it's a beautiful art style and started off really strong story-wise. The beginning to the middle of the game was really strong because of how fun and engaging the story was. Solving puzzles, engaging in investigative dialogue, being a DETECTIVE. It all just gets thrown away. I've given it multiple play-throughs and thought I'd eventually understand the ending.But there's no understanding it, it's just plain bad. The first half of the game was really well done, up until the point where Howard gets infected by the Artifact. At this point, the story just completely goes downhill, as if it were some pretentious attempt to add a twist to the story.There is no proper payoff to finishing the game. If there wasn't this bad of a cliffhanger and we got to play the rest of the game as Renee, maybe I'd be a bit more forgiving. There are so many loose ends, all of which were brought on from the introduction of the Artifact. - Anatoly's death; unexpected, and quite frankly, unnecessary.- Harry's involvement with helping Howard; seems like they just brought him back because they didn't know how to segue to the laboratory beyond the Wall and just came up with the bridge community.- Renee and Clarissa's negotiation.- Finally, and the most damning, the final scene itself.Elaborating more on the final scene, Howard just dies there? Really? All of that character building and getting us attached to him all to end in a pile of raccoon goop?? To clarify, I don't mind that Howard was killed off, but it's the way that he was killed off that was poorly written. It's clear that they tried to do some philosophical Blade Runner type melancholic ending, what with all the dialogue with the Artifact and such. But I think the writers got far too ambitious, and ended up writing some absolute garbage that surpassed their own ability. Again, I don't mind that Howard died, and I don't mind that we got a cliffhanger, but it was just very poorly written. Frankly, Howard getting shot to death would've been a much more profitable ending to his character, then the game could've transitioned to playing as Renee and could've been left off at her talk with Clarissa. But instead we got a prolonged Howard death scene that lasted for basically two whole story acts.It's a very nice game, visually and soundtrack wise. The prequel game is definitely really good too, as it is mainly an anthology with only the writing and the mechanics of the first half of this game. If there's a sequel coming I'm still interested to see the direction it'll take. Also, do not pay full price for this game, you can get it off of other websites for literally less than a dollar, which is what this game is worth because of the poorly written second half. All in all, the game is a 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I've noticed their are a lot of negative reviews for this game but I believe it's because people are used to being fed 18+ hours of endless gaming content rather than enjoying a genuine story-telling experience.
