_childDocuments_.review: So for full disclosure, I backed this game on Kickstarter and had been eagerly looking forward to it since It had first been announced. So I took awhile to gather my thoughts and feelings on the game and my experience with it before I decided to eventually leave this review. So, overall I really liked the game but it does have some pretty big issues, mostly in the last hour or so of game play and story. First it has some beautiful and well made pixel art, both in character design and background work. The music and sound effects work perfectly to create what feels like the perfect atmosphere as you explore and encounter what the game's setting has to offer. I also really enjoyed the characters and the main narrative story for how they were presented for the most part. However, as I mentioned before, the story and characters take a rather unfortunate direction at the end of Act 3 and it only continues to fracture through Acts 4 and 5.For the First two thirds of the game, you are presented with a very interesting story about a missing person's case that leads to uncovering a horrible secret and how it's connected to the rest of setting's society in this dystopian future version of Furry Vancouver.  I was actually really invested in this narrative and seeing how the characters were reacting to it just made me even more engaged, though, I admit, it was moving a bit fast paced for my taste, but I think that is mostly because EggNut were doing the best they could to try and weave in all the elements of their setting as they could. Still, I was very invested.It's when you essentially get into the last third that the game starts to fall apart. The kind of sci-fi dystopian noir story you're been following takes a sharp and steep turn into philosophical and existentialism with very little build up or set up. You could be lenient and say that they had hinted at it throughout the earlier Acts, but I feel that may be too generous, since it is a very abrupt change in tone and pacing and if I'm being honest...it does feel like they took a little heavy handed inspiration from Disco Elysium with the integration. Though, if it had been worked in better and given more time to develop, I think it might've fit in great. As it is, the tonal change in story isn't all of it. Certain characters are presented in entirely new directions with no prior set up for it. Mostly one of the main antagonists. I get the feeling EggNut wanted them to be more morally grey, but a single scene that doesn't have that effect, especially after the game's story has rushed as fast as it has. The ending does feel very unsatisfying, though, not because of it's bleak nature for the game's main protagonist, but because it doesn't make any effort to tie any of the game's story threads together. I wouldn't call it a cliffhanger, so much as a...weirdly intentional title drop. Despite my negative feelings with the game's pacing, and narrative and character developments, I did honestly and sincerely enjoy my time with the game and while I wouldn't give it super high praise, I would for sure recommend it for it's atmosphere and setting. Backbone has a lot of potential inside it and I hope that EggNut continues to make more games with it's world and setting.

_childDocuments_.review: In conclusion, Backbone is a banger of a game that could have been even better. In all honesty, if you see this game in action for a few seconds, I don’t think an empty stealth segment or two alongside a patchy narrative will sway your interest enough not to give it a go.Reviewed by Austin Ernst. _childDocuments_.review: Went into this hoping for a fun detective game with a story I could seriously invest myself in, and came out of it with merely a point and click adventure with dialogue options which unfortunately all culminate to the same, disappointing ending.While the gameplay is pretty boring on it's own, probably largely due to me expecting to be more involved in the mystery rather than just watching it unfold, the story is interesting enough that it kept me entertained throughout. There's some great characters which manage to be memorable through their design and writing. There's fun interactions that made me smile and Howard's inner dialogues with himself portrayed through the choice system made me love him even more than I already did. I ended up really caring for the cast and was eager to see what would happen to them all the way up until the epilogue, when it dawned on me what the writers had done. If you beat the game too, then you are probably just as upset as I am right now.I must applaud Backbone for taking the story in an unexpected direction, but Overall I did enjoy my time with Backbone. Though the gameplay was lacking, it makes up for it as its story, characters and world are fun. I would like to commemorate the devs for all the work they put into this project! It's just unfortunate that I'm so pissed, cause, y'know... Obviously the devs have more planned for the future, so I'll be sure to keep an eye out. :)

I really want to recommend this game, because the atmosphere and story telling is really great for 80% of the story, but fumbling that last 20% is rough.

_childDocuments_.review: Art and music are stellar.Setting is interesting.Themes are neat and inspired by modern topics.Story fell off a bit, but was by no means not engaging. I wish we had more time with the characters, I felt like the game was just getting started by the time it ended. The prologue section was the strongest, after ACT III it kinda started to lose me, but I still had a blast.Would have enjoyed more of it had we got more character build up, more plot build up, and a bit more character drama than one off conversations and implied backstories. Also some mechanics made 1-3 appearances throughout the entirety of the game, and could have been used more to engage the audience or even diversify the gameplay.The original feel of the game is gone by the end of ACT II, and it's sad. The Backbone: Prologue was one of the best games I had played in years, I had been eagerly awaiting the game for over a year, but while I felt something for the characters, by the end I was left wanting ACTUAL resolution.The ending just appears and everything that was built up with other plot points is left up in the air. A game with a good soul, but inconsistent execution of the threads it wants us to follow. As a game designer everything except the execution of the narrative is spectacular. As a player everything but the story (excluding the characters until they're forgotten about) is amazing. As someone who is both however, the pros just barely outweighed the cons, and that's only because ACTs I, II, and III carried the old feel for as long as they could. I got this game the hour it came out and expected greatness, I got something good but not what was showcased in the prologue.Good game. But fell short of the phenomenal prologue that came before it. Overall a 7/10 for me, but with the potential to have been a 9 or 10 if more was done with the amazing premise they had. Try it for yourself if not for the story then for the music and art, but don't go into it expecting the same level of quality as the prologue, it will let you down as it did many. But if you just go into it for the experience, I think you'll enjoy it as much as you possibly can.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an awful game. The graphics are well-stylised, the writing, at least in the first half or so is pretty good, and the character design is well-done. The ending in particular I want to talk about, with spoiler tagsOverall,  I think this is a well-made game, but the main drawing point, which really is the narrative, declines in quality to such an extent that I can't recommend it. It's such a shame to see such potential missed.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot in good conscience recommend this game to someone at full price, despite my positive review for the game. However, I would highly recommend this game to someone when this game is on sale. For the record, I have put two full play through's of this game before the writing of this review, and I absolutely love the game. Even with it's flaws. The game, although lacking in some areas, mainly being the writing in the latter half of the story, and the sometimes very linear and boring game play. Always manages to make up for it's short-comings with very impactful characters, dialogue and visual storytelling. The setting of post nuclear Vancouver is bustling with city life, and Eggnut did a very good job of nailing the Dystopian yet 40's esque style. Complete with rusty old cars, and the future 1984 police boxes. Giving you the impression, from Act one of the Game that something is not alright. The characters, Howard, Renee, and even the side characters all felt very, very real. I would find myself, often times getting choked up during the my play sessions. The Devs clearly had an eye for detail when making the set drops, there was clearly much passion put into this project. The music is masterful, as well as the greater sound design as a whole. I find myself unironically listening to the sound track of this game for a relaxing setting. The sound design as a whole for backbone was very great, from the foot steps on different types of material, to the city scape and such. The game gets A's for me.Where the game lacks, as many other people have stated. Was the games latter half- to the ending. I just feel, that some of the passion died. I feel, personally. The stuff with the artifact should have never been. I feel that Eggnut really shot themselves in the foot by killing Howard off in such a way that they did. The ending was bitter, and left many questions unanswered.Because Aliens.

The music is also another strong point.Then right at the very end, when you felt like you were still at the beginning of your journey, they explain the plot twist and it ends... It is hugely narrower, more linear than I would normally like (at all),  but I was swept up in it and enjoyed every minute. Superb.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine you are out for dinner at a new expensive restaurant you been waiting to open for ages.Super excited.You walk thru the door, looks nice, atmospheric, stuck in time, interesting, almost asking to be explored.You have to pay upfront.The place is packed but its very silent in hereThe waiter pops out of nowhere "do you want stake freak?"No matter whats on the menu your dialog options to his question are "Yes", "Yes if you have chips too", "♥♥♥♥ you I want stake".There's bread and drinks on the table, but you can't pick them up. They're just clever images on the table cloth. As you get closer the illusion is broken.Your date for the night turns up. Here we go. Her conversation keeps you at arms length whilst hinting you might have a chance.The food arrives but rather than being served it pops out of thin air.  It looks great.  Hmmmm I'm hungry.You eat the stake left to right. Starts of meaty enough.  As you move on, you notice gaps like bits have been cut out or somehow the meat has holes in.Your date spends more time in the bathroom than with you.60% of the way in, you realise the rest of the meal is just coloured cardboard and grease.Your date vanishes off with your nemesis.What food you have eaten was poison and rot.  It mutates you so that a spider arm will one time and one time only, pop out and stab your best friend.You roll to the floor groaning.The waiter pops back and urinates on you.Everything goes black and you are left with you schizophrenic mind chattering.♥♥♥♥ you devs. You promised me an adventure game. _childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: This game blends 2 of my absolute top games in the genre-- Gemini Rue, and Night in the Woods. That could not be higher praise. A part Noir, part Sci-fi detective thriller dotted with thoughtful characters, witty dialogue, and masterfully crafted setting. The environments are top notch, mixing real life Vancouver with creative 20s flair and a dash of post apocalyptic. The music is tense and ominous, helping remind you the severity of the narrative amongst a distractingly beautiful game.I love seeing the classic point and click/puzzle adventure game get it's due, and all the better when it's done faithfully with pixel art. With Backbone, modern lighting and reflection techniques have been worked in to elevate the art style and to distinguish Backbone from it's contemporaries (The Last Night technically showed off a lot of this style years ago but has still yet to manifest, so Backbone gets first to the punch bragging rights.)A short experience with somewhat limited variety in the outcomes, but all-in-all a wonderfully crafted game with a lot of heart and a satisfying world of story. Hope to see DLC that expands the world of Backbone and gives us a chance to see some new avenues of the city.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid indie game player, I was compelled by Backbone overall. The pixel graphics are intricate and nostalgic, the choice-dialogue allows players to converse as witty or as serious as they would like, and ultimately, this is the type of narrative game I will think about for a long time after playing. To the people deciding whether or not to buy, know this:1. Many of the negative reviews point out that the demo sets up the expectation for stealth and puzzles throughout the game that goes unfulfilled. While I agree with this, I also think that the game is excellent regardless. Just go into it with an open mind, expecting it to be more like an interactive graphic novel.2. The final two acts do take quite a turn from the rest of the game, which is also another point of contention for some players. All I can advise is to fully embrace the story. After finishing the game, it's clear that the story was never about the mystery at all - it was about the personal, moral, and mental transformation of the main character. Just know that you aren't buying a "detective" game, you're purchasing a very raw, painful, and breathtaking story about a raccoon trying to find himself in a very demented world. What's happening around Howard is entirely beside the point. I respect the developers for sticking to their guns despite some of the negative responses. Love it or hate it, they told the story they wanted to tell. I really do think this game is worth experiencing. Merely adjust your expectations before playing, and you will not be disappointed. I would honestly classify this game as more of a work of art than a video game, but that makes it even more meaningful to me personally. If you're into philosophical, thought provoking, and ambiguous stories that have applications to real world issues, I would highly recommend. If you're merely looking for a clean-cut detective game, this may not be the one for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: as many have said: the potential is endless but the execution was lacking (specifically towards the end). _childDocuments_.review: Deep and complex, hinting at a rich history and complex society. It is a classic detective noir tale that takes some pretty big twists that keep it from getting complacent. It could have just stayed as a typical private detective story but it takes a lot of artistic risks.It is short, it is less of a complete story end-to-end and more of a vignette, an intersection of people who decide to "show some backbone" if you will. It leaves you with a lot of unanswered questions, some in a good way and some in a not so good way but overall the characters are story and setting are worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone is a linear story driven game with many dialogue choices. While it does feel like you have control over the relationships of the characters, ultimately this game has one path and one ending no matter what. The story is very unique and interesting, and in many ways this game feels like it was intended to be a visual novel. There are a couple moments where you have to figure out puzzles, but overall it's a straight forward story. You play as a detective tasked with finding a woman's husband who she suspects is cheating among other things. This leads you to a club which leads you down a long rabbit hole of crazy endeavors. The plot reminds me of famous movies like Donnie Darko or Akira. I can understand why certain plot twists would be a turn off for some people, but personally I found this story fascinating. And if it were simply the plot of a film I don't think people would question it as much. Also they're furries. There is a bit of world building on that, I guess. With Apes being the world leaders, and then other carnivorous animals like lions, bears, and wolves are deemed a part of higher society. It's a cool premise. Definitely a unique experience. If you enjoy an immersive story game, similar to a film, and can go in with an open mind, than you'll enjoy this. If you expect anything else you will be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to love this game. And I did! Beautiful visuals, insanely good music, charming storytelling- For three acts, likely my favorite mystery-adventure of all time. The tonal shift in act 4+ and turn in what seemed like a plot reaching it's conclusion and it's abrupt ending and genre swap out of nowhere- I can't recommend this game unfortunately, especially at it's current price for how short it is. It's a shame too, I really really hope the devs continue working on games because they have amazing potential!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Writing a bad review is nothing I enjoy, but I fear, Backbone deserves it.tl;dr: Excellent graphics, horrible story, bad writing, no riddles (beyong prologue), short (~3h)First the good:The cinematic art is really awesome. Whoever created the graphics and animations, kudos to you, and I hope, we will see more or again from you. The music/sound is also quite good. But that's kinda it.First of all, there is barely a game. After the prologue, the demo, that was used to advertise the game, there is no game anymore. It is just an interactive story. Choices and dialogs don't matter at all. In my opinion, this is blatant false advertising. The prologue does not reflect what you get in the full game.Secondly, for good or bad, it's short. I mean, if you are a thorough reader, you might be able to extend it to four hours.Which brings me to the writing and the story. The writing is done as if there were choices, but since nothing matters, the writing fails completely in that regard. The characters stay flat and meaningless, while they try to give them a bit of "humanity" and a background, it simply doesn't work.The story starts really well, with a noir vibe, with a hero that isn't a detached, hard-boiled cynic like Sam Spade but gets downhill pretty fast. Several parts of the story don't work out and do not make sense. And I am not talking about the weird stuff that happens later on, I am talking about the interactions of the characters. I feels like the developers threw all ideas they had in a chamber pot and then used a sledgehammer to fit them together (pot included).Also, nothing is completed in a satisfactory way. I mean, a good short story with an open ending can be quite fulfilling. But if nothing makes sense, only anger remains. The ending makes no sense at all, neither the ending of Howard nor of Renee. Honestly, an open ending would have been better than what we got.The open letter of the developers was for me kinda the icing on the cake that made me write this review. I would have accepted an honest apology but telling us, that "art is subjective" and the game is actually what they wanted to create? Puh, either they are in denial or they are blatantly lying to our faces.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: The devs advertise that the game is 7-8 hours long, which is not true unless you go take a walk irl during one of the "exploration" moments in the game. I was going back and forth, to find easter eggs, secrets etc. I still managed to finish the game fairly under 4 hours. I wouldnt mind it being 4 hours long if it felt complete and finished, the only part that felt finished in this game is the audio-visuals, music, character design, everything mentioned is well done and polished. Well... Unfortunately that isnt what the game is about, is it.. Story feels split in half, by that i mean that we get only the half of the story. Everything ends opened, the only thing closed is the case with the otter you get at the start. Character development is great, but given the ending we get nothing back, like no redemption, i wouldn't mind Howard dying, but i am pissed that we dont know whats next, what about René and Bloodworth, what about the Apes, what about the mutation of Howard, the girls beyond the Wall, Howard's death, Anatoly's family, there is a LOT of stuff they could be expanding on, especially for 20€, i feel robbed tbh, i wouldnt mind paying them  +/- 20€, even if the ending was bitter-sweet, i mind that we dont get the escalation of all the stuff we develop through the gameplay and story development, at this state this game should have been around 10-15€ max. For those who played it, i think we can all agree on that they cut us off like Howard when he tells the Otter woman about her husband being dead and then hanging up basically. Huge potential, i hope the devs will wake up, because this might be one of their greatest opportunites to break through in the gaming industry. 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game, with a very intriguing storyline. The setting is something new and fresh to me, and if this was a book series or a comic I would be pretty hooked! And that is part of my problem. The creators of this game have come up with a rich story world, but the game is much too linear and short to really delve into anything. We keep scratching the surface but never delve deeper. I played this game at a casual pace and finished the story in about 5 hours. Maybe that's not bad for an indie game, but this kind of plot and world the developers have built up really deserves more! If this is all we'll ever get from the "Backbone Universe" then I shall be very disappointed. So much potential! What really cements this sense of hopelessness is the ending. I won't spoil the ending, but I can tell you that there is only one way to finish the game, and it is not a happy ending. It is not a very open ending, either. Which makes this feel like a one-off game. In fact, if it hadn't been for the ending, this would be a thumbs up review, but the ending really ruins the rest of the game for me. I will never collect all the Steam achievements, because I will never play this game again. There is really no reason to play this more than once, and that is kinda bad for a video game. If you suffer from a depression, or you are a highly sensitive person, don't play this game. It will only make things worse. I'm all for games and art making an impression on me, but had I known it would bum me out this much then I would've avoided it. So yeah, I love the concept, love the characters, love the aesthetic. Too bad it all ends where it ends, though.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - I loved it personally, ... it  feel kind of like a 1.0 release at the moment.I'll first start out by saying I haven't been invested in this game as long as some have - I wasn't a Kickstarter backer, and I only found out about it in early May.  I actually logged into Steam for the first time in 10 years to be able to play the demo, as I don't have Gamepass or other options.  The last game I played on Steam was Portal 2 :)  For what I wanted out of it, it worked for  personally - the visuals are awesome (I love the raindrops hitting the lens, nice little added touch!), the sound design is awesome ( the use of "I Wonder" in Act II - I think that's my personal favorite "noir" moment), and bonus - raccoon detective!  The "gaming" aspect worked for me, there weren't a cavalcade of detective or stealth segments in it as some have mentioned in other reviews, but I personally wasn't let down by that.  I'm more of a casual gamer, and I was more interested in seeing how the story has progressed since the prologue demo than the gaming aspects of it.  The story... ehh... well, it does kind of fall off about 2/3 of the way through it IMO.  It's not that it's bad, as I'm also a fan of David Lynch-esque things, which it does eventually become, it just seems a little thin - like it's not 100% there just yet.  There are a lot of loose ends and background set pieces that I'd really like to see tied up or fleshed out somehow, either through some sort of additional content, or a possible sequel/prequel kind of situation down the road.  There is a  of good in Backbone, I just hope there  hope in the future for more  it - hopefully the book isn't closed on it just yet.  Definitely voice acting as well, if it can be arranged - the lack of VAs didn't really put me off, but it would be a lot more immersive with them.  So, would I recommend it?  As a hard-core game with lots of stealthy MGS-style gameplay, probably not... but as a visual novel with scattered detective and stealth elements, definitely.

_childDocuments_.review: I really struggled with how to judge Tails Noir (formerly Backbone).On one hand, I feel like the story really gets muddled and the ending felt pretty unsatisfying. However, the mood and the atmosphere and the art are SIMPLY WONDERFUL. I get the impression that this project was a labor of love that faced a lot of difficulties during development. (Also, from what I understand, this is Eggnut's first game?? Which is really impressive.)My verdict: give it a try, knowing it's imperfect. The good bits are really good. _childDocuments_.review: I hate to say it, but I only recommend this game if there is at least a 50% discount, don't pay anything close to the full price because, again I hate to say it, it's not worth it. I'm not the first and nor the last to be disappointed by this game and many others have already talked about it in reviews and forums. There's a lot you could criticize, but I think overall it's a great game, if only it were a complete game. It feels exactly as others have described, like production of the game was rushed and then cut short for whatever reasons be it personal, financial, I don't know. It certainly does not feel like a finished game, in the sense that the story ends without having developed any of the storylines or characters. It's like they started writing a really great book and stopped after 2 chapters but still published. It's incredibly frustrating. The best part is by far the free-to-play prologue which I still highly recommend. I love the concept, the look, everything about it was executed to really high quality, and as a visual style and a concept it is beautiful and unique. I hate to be so negative about a game which had a lot of great qualities especially when this game has just been released. I was so excited for this game after playing the demo a year ago. It had so much potential but was not executed to its full potential and I think this is the most disappointing thing for players. Even though there's no going back and changing the story, in my opinion, if Backbone were cheaper and a sequel were made, it could be redeemed. Not recommended at full price. Recommended if it's at least half price (full price is just over $30 AUD at the time of this review), you loved the demo, and you're prepared to be disappointed and frustrated at its abrupt ending. But otherwise still a good game overall and beautifully made. I will probably change to 'recommended' eventually because I enjoyed the game until I was disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I love the dark and melancholy dystopian strangeness of the story. Its like a cross between Soylent green and Planet of the Apes. The hand drawn graphics are beautiful enough to stop and admire---even worth looking at all the animal "People" in the shop windows and apartments going about their lives.  However, it has an awful "one game only" save system and some people have lost their save file accidentally. So if you play, please don't start a new game until you you are finished. And most certainly don't let a cat walk across your keyboard while you are on the menu screen or you might lose all your progress! Fortunately the game has an interesting story and good replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: I love video games but some genres are indigestible to me. Point-and-click adventures have always been hostile to me because of their style of play. Puzzles do not amuse me and destroy my suspension of disbelief, as many do with songs in musicals.I was intrigued by the mixed reviews, even though I knew the risk of the game boring me was high. Many complained that the story takes an unexpected turn halfway through the game, then spirals completely out of control. And while I don't like point-and-click adventures, I do love wacky stories. So I decided to play it. Do I regret it? No. Is it a masterpiece? No. Is it a game I found enjoyable? Yes.Can I explain the disappointment of so many players? Yes.In short, if what you expect is a classic-style point-and-click adventure in a pure noir setting, prepare to be disappointed, unless you decide to play only the first two acts, leaving out the rest.The game is an extremely linear adventure, where the player's only task is to follow the story and enjoy it. The end. I loathe games without gameplay and freedom like this one, they bore me to death (I find it more enjoyable to watch a movie at this point), yet Backbone has features that made me come to the end, satisfied: it has a short duration that prevented me from being bored to death (and paradoxically, the part I found most boring was the initial part that underlies the enthusiasm and subsequent disappointment of so many), it has well-written characters, a story that all in all stands up despite being very ambitious, and above all (the game's strong point for me) fantastic atmospheres supported by a sound that is really convincing in translating the feelings of the moment into music. In conclusion, if you can get rid of the expectations of having a game with puzzles, with a narrative in full noir style, or that has particularly original traits, perhaps this game will be able to give you a few hours of pleasure and some nice emotions.My favourite Howard will always be the duck, but to the raccoon goes a remarkable second place: it was a short but intense ride, PI.

_childDocuments_.review: Going into the game, I never knew... How amazing it would be. The twists it hits you with every single act, how likeable the characters are, how charming the whole atmosphere is, so I'll make sure to say things like they are in this review.Tails: Noir puts you in the shoes of Private Investigator Howard Lotor... a Raccoon! Yup, you heard right, the world of Tails: Noir is one where the only remotely human figure is the Shepherd, the God people worship in this universe. There are many kinds in this society; rats who tend to make deals in the shadows, mice, beavers who work as taxi drivers, and other shady looking mammals... Like a NOIR version of London, there is a lot going on with the people, ahem or should I say the animals of this game. Howard, who starts off by simply taking a case to stalk and take pictures of a cheating husband, ends up in one of the most cryptic vortexes ever... He'll find himself entangled in a story about a cannibalistic cult, and an alien being simply refered to as The Artifact.The game is very well animated and all that pixel goodness is just very well done to the most minor of details. While reading through the many layers of dialogue, you get to pick choices that would reflect on the outcome of an act, although most choices would lead to the same thing in the end, it's just that the scene would be different with each different choice that you make. Moreover, you'd sympathize with Howard, being the loner that he is, especially what happens to him towards the end of the story. All in all, Tails: Noir is an amazing pixel master piece. In my book, this is a  but only because it lacks the more occasional voice-acting here and there. As I was reading loudly through the dialogues, one of my cousins who was in my house at the moment came up to me, sat down and started paying very close attention to how I interpreted each dialogue... That's when I realised that this game would catch anyone's attention with its amazing post-modern writing, its mysterious scenery and its exceptionally written characters... Also, mistrusting individuals on the street of Gastown is really the only way to go, I mean I wouldn't trust someone with my real name too if I were investigating their druglord lol

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love it, it was rad and weird and definitely not what I expected even though I follow the development of the game real close It was worth it for me and the art with the music was so cool and rawyes I get why some people are angry about it or displeased, but I think we haven't seen it all and even if it's like this the "ending" I thought it was entertaining and intriguing

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone is a sidescrolling point & click game where you play as a raccoon detective named Howard in post noir Vancouver. In a world filled with Anthropomorphic animals, citizens come to you for help with such matters like finding evidence of infidelity. Though the story is very linear and is a bit short with a slightly rushed ending, it was still quite enjoyable for the interactions, worldbuilding and visual aesthetics. There is plenty of dialogue to undertake with the residents in order to find clues and uncover problems and mysteries. A lot of the choices do not matter much and are just for idle chit chat, but that is fine since they are still fun to read and keeps the game a bit more casual at times.Visuals and graphics are the selling point to me in this game. The pixel graphics are well drawn/animated with lots of vibrant colours and detailed backgrounds which makes the areas feel lively. This is enforced with aspects like the rain which even drips onto your screen. The backgrounds are eventful with a lot of things happening like the residents chilling at the bar, people waiting in line for the theatre or at food stands, and people just loitering and walking about. Music is another solid point with the jazzy and electronic soundtrack that plays in the background. Adding to both the story and visuals that you see on screen; the soundtrack creates an atmospheric and cinematic experience which feels immersive as you become more connected with the world.Being a simple point & click game, the controls are easy to play with, with only a few various buttons to use for things such as movement and interactions. Though, the price is a bit steep for a typical indie game. However, it is published by Raw Fury so I can see it being bundled sometime in the future. I would say to pick it up during a sale or if you are a patientgamer, can wait for it to be bundled.The game did have a kickstarter campaign which ended a few years ago, and then took the developers another couple of years to deliver the keys. I read that this has caused a stir with the backers understandably, though I can’t comment on that since I am not one of them. Overall, it is a story rich game with a wonderful and vibrant world full of life. If you want to play an absorbing point & click game where you meet and converse with a lot of the townsfolk, then this is one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: After avoiding Tails Noir (formerly known as Backbone) for years due to its mixed reception, I find the game has been unfairly judged. While I can't speak to any technical issues upon its release, my personal experience was a smooth and bug-free playthrough of the entire game.The primary critique often leveled against Tails Noir pertains to its narrative departure from the Detective/Noir theme, evolving into something perceived as 'weird' or 'bizarre.' Interestingly, this shift is what captivated me the most. From the fourth act onward, the game exudes a palpable sense of hopelessness, reminiscent of the common tone found in Eastern European writing. It defies categorization as a romance, a Noir tale, or even a character-driven narrative. Instead, it unfolds as a tragedy, its core purpose being to illustrate how an oppressive and powerful regime can distort people's perception of reality. The concept of what lies beyond the city's walls drives individuals to commit horrific acts in pursuit of freedom. Irony abounds as the unknown beyond the wall (represented by the Artifact) proves to be even more menacing than the city's oppressive regime. The protagonist serves as a mere observer, a pair of eyes witnessing the horrors within the city, outside it, and the monstrous act people commit in their pursuit of elusive goals. The ending, far from a happy resolution, leaves no relevant loose ends, effectively concluding the observer's role and planting the seeds of revolution.The overarching idea behind Tails Noir is commendable and even remind me a tiny bit of Stalker. However, its execution falls short. It could have become one of my favorite short stories if it had fully committed to its grimdark themes and spent less time on surface-level comedy and Twitter-like political commentary (which feels heavy-handed and out of place). It appears as if there were brilliant people in the team with great ideas, but alongside writers who just wanted to get their rocks off. Additionally, the story is entirely linear, which is fine, but I understand people who might feel misled by the presence of dialogue choices that, in reality, only serve as mere conduits for Steam achievements.In conclusion, Tails Noir deserves a purchase and playthrough, provided one approaches it with an open mind and hold no expectations of a conventional detective story. Fans of 'Eastern European-like' narratives and horror stories akin to those of H.P. Lovecraft may find this game more appealing than the average player. However, it's essential to acknowledge its imperfections, especially where writing is concerned.

_childDocuments_.review: 4/10. A really interesting, vibey story that will get you in the first half, ngl. I loved it. Then the plot changes, and while it does keep you engaged wanting to piece it together, it kind of just falls into an unsatisfying ending that feels forced on the player. Wouldn't be so bad except that there are no branching paths or alternate endings. I want to love it, but it doesn't really let you walk away with anything but confusion and sadness. Maybe Preludes will be better. Honestly, these guys write great characters and atmosphere, so I'd be willing to give it a shot, depending how reviews go. _childDocuments_.review: Like you I saw the little mixed review flag on the top and came down here to the reviews to figure out what's up. Having played it let me assure you, this game is absolutely worth your time. It's beautiful, well written, enthralling and so deliciously noir it might as well be vanta black with a splash of scifi. There are few games that can even come close to the quality this game has when it's at its best.The biggest criticism I can level at the game, which I think is also the source of the mixed reviews, is the fact that the game feels jarringly unfinished. You can practically feel the seems where content was cut (Similar to cyberpunk 2077 weirdly enough). The final chapters feel like they're setting up a grand new act of the story only to grind to a halt before the fireworks start. There are entire areas of the game discussed at length like you might visit them but they never materialize and when the game just ends there's a very strong sense of bittersweet anticlimax that I think a lot of people take with them to the reviews.The ending is kinda lame but I mean that's just tradition for PC adventure games at this point right? Don't let the reviews fool you; this game is an beautiful, black, gritty gem and I can't wait to see what the developers make next. The pixel animation is flowing and gorgeous, ingeniously lit with modern rendering techniques with lovingly made scenes and environments. The story is well written and the characters are deep. If you love narrative games and noir then this game is a must have.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Yes and No Review.everything from presentation and Music is epic! I felt like the story was going more towards the city corruption and the politics surrounding crime. maybe it had something to say about its setting of vancouver but no this story could have taken place in any other "distopian version of a modern city"Gameplay wise. i did enjoy aspects of how it was noir. you often were given the choice of 2 lesser evil in a way. like you had to get your hands dirty to progress further into the case.some of the puzzles gave me no clue what to do. wish i could have spent more time in the world and meeting the people of the city. that was the fun part.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no "game play" after the first 30 mins. Everything beyond Act I is an uninteresting script that you click through via dialogue boxes. The game had a unique visual style, cool noir vibe and music, but nothing else redeeming. I constantly added things to my inventory (mugs, books, etc.) that had no purposes. I was really hoping for a game that would  involve legitimate detective work - collecting clues, putting theories together. Perhaps GameDec later this year will scratch that itch - this game certainly did not.

_childDocuments_.review: If you do not like walking simulators, this game is not for you. This game has two core mechanics: walk and ask questions. _childDocuments_.review: is a strange one, and after finishing the game, I now understand the "mixed" reviews. About , there is a major shift in the story. Initially, while surprising, I felt it was handled quite well. The developers blend genre while maintaining, and continuing to build, an intriguing narrative. The writing shifts as well, introducing abstract stream of consciousness interjections, a la . Unfortunately, this doesn't persist, and we're fairly quickly thrown into a confusing transitionary section followed by an anti-climactic epilogue. In a way, I understand what they were going for, given the story beats presented prior. Ultimately, however, it doesn't stick the landing and it's completely justifiable that some folks were disappointed.That being said, the rest of the experience is great.  pixel art, a compelling mystery to solve, and an appropriate noir soundtrack make for a fantastic start to this game. I'd still recommend it, for the pixel art alone honestly, but be wary that the ending and  leave something to be desired.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay. People are being way too emotional, dramatic and even disrespectful in the discussions. The game is exactly what is meant to be. _childDocuments_.review: Wow, I really loved this game and the vibes it gave off. The story really goes in some unexpected directions after those initial couple chapters, but they still nail the underlying noir story telling it was trying to channel. It's not just your traditional noir mid-30s to 50s either, it takes steps to expand on that and reflect on how this atmosphere can apply outside of those times, without of course going full Blade Runner. Try to take a moment as you play and really savor the visuals too, this has some of the most beautiful artwork you could hope for. Cannot recommend enough, give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: So much potential, such a disappointing conclusion. Still a worthwhile experience.I agree with most people that this game feels unfinished. The world-building and plot are incredibly intriguing and rich until about the 3/4 point when everything takes a hard left turn. The entire post noir detective story the game has been building up to this point goes completely out the window and it rushes to a non-sensical, underwhelming ending. It appears like the devs either completely ran out of time or had no idea how to finish their story.But somehow I still enjoyed this game thoroughly. It's offensively gorgeous, it oozes atmosphere and the dialogue options are consistently enjoyable. It kept me engaged with its well fleshed out and eclectic characters and left me wanting more until the end.That being said, the demo is false advertising. After the Prologue there are no more puzzles or alternate ways to approach any obstacle - the game becomes strictly linear and ends on a disappointing cliffhanger that resolves none of the major questions the story built up over its short 5 hour runtime.This game may not be for everyone. But it spurred my imagination. And that made the disappointment at the end worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Really love this game, absolutely well written, with deep themes and occasional references to works like Blade Runner. Despite the ending not being everyone's cup of tea, I actually enjoyed it, and the writing in the game's final acts was some of my favourite. The loss of player agency actually fits very well into the themes of the game, as well as of the works it's clearly inspired by, and allows the player to get "lost" into the deepest reflections concerning our own existence - something that I personally love, but that some people find "unsatisfying". But as in life, some questions simply don't have direct, palatable answers, and some problems simply don't have solutions within our reach. I believe this is also why the game doesn't really have "choice", the player choices don't really affect the ending. But in this case, I'd say it's worth going on the developers' journey and embracing it to best appreciate it. I wouldn't go into this game expecting it to be a choice-based game, or a linear, superficial narrative. I'd go into it focused on the journey, with humility to forget I'm the player, and rather embrace the fact that I'm an "interactive reader" of the journey.It's a short one, but at the same time, it's just the right length for the story and themes it communicates.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale, which I think is the best way to buy Tails Noir/Backbone (which, after finishing the game, is a much better name). I was not familiar with this game during its Kickstarter or demo days, but was lured in by the graphics. This game is not at all what I expected, and the ending left a little to be desired, but nonetheless I enojoyed my experience. I see this less as a game, but more as a piece of art. I wish the devs had taken a different turn, yeah, and I wish there were maybe another act or 2, but I did really appreciate the time I spent with this game. If you're a fan of Gris and/or Life is Strange 2, I think you'd enjoy this game. Most of these sour reviews are valid, and I think make excellent points, but I think a lot of them are marred by an expectation they had way before playing the game. While it wasn't the story I would write, I can see the value in what was trying to be said. And to understand the story, it's important to read the dialogue (AKA... if you don't like reading/skip over paragraphs.... seek another game) and interact with as much as you can. I loved this world, and I wish there was a sequel or some kind of update so I could explore it further. Really the only true disservice was not making this game longer, especially for a 25 dollar price point.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I've been anticipating this game for awhile since I played the prologue, and I have to say, I really enjoyed it. It's less of a traditional point-and-click adventure and more of a Disco Elysium, dialogue-heavy narrative game but that didn't bother me. I thought the dialogue was really well done - other reviews have said it's clear the creators' main language isn't English but I didn't get that feeling at all. I felt the characters all used very modern English that made sense to me.While I did enjoy the story, it's very clear where this game stands out is in the visuals. They're stunning. The lighting is a big part of that obviously, but even in areas where the lighting wasn't so focused - when I came onto an apartment block I'd never seen before that was packed with life and detail I audibly gasped. EggNut has done a fantastic job selling this as a real world that characters actually engage with that I think helps set the mood of the story.===SPOILERS: The end of this review contains a spoiler for some end-game features, read on at your own risk===The game is definitely on the short side, and that would be my only real complaint, if you can call it that. It took me under four hours to complete. I don't think every game needs to be a Final Fantasy or a Death Stranding, but I do tend to prefer longer games and the ending came sooner than I expected. I wouldn't call the ending quite so much of a "cliffhanger" as I would a clear setup for a sequel, and I don't mind that,  I've played plenty of games set up that way and enjoyed them, but tonally the shift to playing other characters with different knowledge, goals, and morals than Howard, the character I'd been playing and rooting for the whole game, was odd. I didn't really know what dialogue options to choose because I'd only seen these characters through the lens of Howard before, and getting into their heads was an abrupt shift the game does nothing to prepare you for.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a mystery game, this probably isn't it.But, if you are looking for a game about ethical choices, humanity, mindfulness, ambiguity, social justice, character interactions, and purpose, this is a great game. It's one that's going to stick with me for a while.I was skeptical after seeing mixed reviews about how it ends, but was pleasantly surprised. It's ambiguous, yes, but thought-provoking. The characters, music, and scenery are really great throughout. It has good replay-ability too as there are so many different choices in dialogue to make.
