_childDocuments_.review: The game is stunning, it's cleverly made and the story is intriguing. My only problem is that the game feels cut off, the ending is abrupt and leaves you wondering. Without spoiling the ending, it just seems abrupt and out of nowhere. The game was a blur towards the end and seems like they ran out of ideas. Another thing is that the game is short, only about 4-5 hours of playtime depending on how much you explore and how good you are at puzzle solving.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: First, one , . there are none in the maingame, thats so dissapointing... i cant see a reason why they did that.Since the day the Prologue came out I was looking forward so much to this awesome game. I love the art, the gameplay, the story in the prologue. But honestly, the Prologue is better then the maingame. The maingame is very short (5 hours if you play slow, includes the Prologue), but thats not the problem, there are some ways to play different some parts so you can play it a second time. . While the prologue sets the tone for a epic masterpiece it really is the first 3 chapters of the game, of those 3, the prologe is the best chapter by far. its the only chapter with a puzzle AND with a different choice how to enter a building. After Act 2 it starts all of a sudden to turn into a mess, and even after the Epilogue chapter (where you for no reason all of a sudden control a different character) it makes no sense at all. Its so sad, because without that weird turnaround the story was really set to be great.In the end it didnt even matter at all what happened in the Prologue, they switched the story at one point to a different story and both storys did not finish, so you are just left with questions. A bad outcome for a short singleplayer game. It is really sad it turned out like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Game is beautiful. I enjoyed it's story. Dialogues we often bad. It certanly has it's moments (first computer, unexpected visit and celebration to name a few). In my humble opinion, ending is complete BS(!).I don't play too many adventure games, but I think this one doesn't deserve a recommendation. However I see great potential in studio and their idea, so this review is positive. I had fun.Now let's hope Tails will be as good as they presented it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: First 3 chapters were pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good, but then it just ended out of nowhere. No mysteries were solved, too many loose ends left untied. No character development. Builds up all this intrigue about the origins of the city and all these conspiracies and things, then just drops it. Same with the characters - they build up these plotlines about how the characters could do epic things (won't spoil) that would change the entire fate of the city once and for all, and then they just... drop it. WTF? There's a scene where the main character has to struggle through captivity for days on end, and once he finally escapes... the game ends. Where is the character development? Where is the conclusion? Super disappointing, underwhelming and unsatisfying ending, can't believe I waited like a year for this game to come out.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: My second time playing this game. I think it's misunderstood. Some players may have expected a detective adventure, yet this is a game about life and all its intricacies. The writing is superb, oftentimes hilarious. It's obvious the authors are very intelligent people.I find myself thinking about this game year after having finished it. It's an experience that lingers. Especially recommended, if you are a fan of games like Disco Elysium or Night in the Woods
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: The Yes or No system really doesn't fit for this game.It's got a fantastic atmosphere, the music is perfect, the art style good for its purpose, the characters seem interesting and plot points start seeming like they're going somewhere.But they all lead to nothing. The story is very straightforward, which is fine if it's meaty and develops everything. But there's a trillion loose ends and that can be cool sometimes, but so little gets explained it just kind of gets... annoying? A straightline story that's thinner than you want for the dev time and not really an ending to fulfil expectation either. It almost hurts the promise this art piece had for it to just end up how it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: A game that gave me mixed feelings, and for which I've waited for since 2019.Backbone has a SUPERB prologue that unfortunately is better thant the whole product. Backbone presents itself as a noir story,so we must analyse it as one.Right in the begining we're shown a map with diverse neighborhoods of the game city, and a brief description of each. Each level is set in one of these neighborhoods. Until West End,the game follow a traditional - and very effective - noir story. Soon we're presented to the main investigation, and to our partner. The following chapters involve mainly investigations, inquiries, typical detective stuff. No point to bother about until then - except the lack of puzzles. For a story that could easily bring point and click elements, Backbone depends wholly on dialogues. At certain point, however - doing my best to not spoil anything -, the narrative crearly becomes lost. The initial mistery is throw away and a series of sudden and poorly impactful events are  mixed in the plot with no real effect or meaning. I think the narrative tried to grasp too much for a short story to handle, and in the middle of that, forgot to accomplish the basics of noir, that were so well established in the first chapters. The bigger themes are not well done, the late game characters are so briefly shown that the player can't feel emotionally attached by them, as clearly was intended to be.I know how difficult can be for an indie dev to put a project like this foward, and I hope Eggnut can take the criticism this game deserves and make a more coherent product next time - as I've said before, the first chapters prove that they're completely capable of that, they just got lost in the middle. I still look foward to their next projects.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: The only good thing about this game is the music by Arooj Aftab. Do yourself a massive favor and just look her up on Spotify. Don't buy the game. The first chapter shows what the developers wanted to do, then it's just a sad and dismaying progression downhill as you feel like the only story you're experiencing is their approaching deadline and leaking funds.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: In spite of some of the best pixel art I've seen in ages, it's pretty short and the story falls into massive disrepair very quickly with some of the oddest choices in narrative material I've seen in a while. It's a total mess and I have to wonder if there were more than one person writing this thing for it to go so pear-shaped after a strong start. The devs seem to have imploded and the Tails Noir universe is now being appropriated into weird unaffiliated spinoffs by other people. A very strange and unfortunate state of affairs for what could have been a really promising series.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone takes incredible swings at being exactly what it wants to be.I get the mixed reviews. If you go in for the mystery, you'll be disappointed. However, if you buy into the incredible characters, gorgeous world, and amazing atmosphere, you'll have an amazing time. Backbone isn't a mystery, it's a narrative about living. I'm super happy I played it and can't wait to play the prelude. Would love to see other stories set in this incredible world.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I love the neo-noir genre and after playing the prologue of Backbone, buying the game for me was a no-brainer.- Incredible pixel art, very eye candy atmosphere. - Music was charming and well used.- Fascinating storyline (ACT 1-3, at least)- Certain levels were simply devoid of the music which kind of spoiled my immersion.- Clear lack of character development and the ending was extremely underwhelming. A lot of plots were left unanswered which is why I'm certain it'll be getting a sequel or a DLC sooner or later.- Only one ending no matter what decisions you take.- A very short story (3.5-4hours)This game had so much potential from the prologue but Backbone simply couldn't follow-up on the story. For the price I bought the game at (about 4-5$) I would probably say it was worth it. I wouldn't recommend spending more than $10 on the game - only buy it during the sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Backbones tells the story of , a dystopian (god forgive) city through the lens of protagonist raccoon Howard Lotor. Beginning the journey small and with a missing persons case, the story evolves into… a mess? Nonetheless the outstanding levels and the gorgeous soundtrack compliment this game beautifully. That is as much good it has though.As already stated the story is awkward to say the least. Putting it into words is hard. I don’t understand what the writers of  were thinking. The story starts off grounded with a great premise and with an instant hook. Definitely, the best act is the first act, and that one is free. You get dragged into this missing person case only to find the target dead and being part of a plot involving a crime lord and the bureaucrats of the city. The other parts continue strong with pacing issues and somewhat stale, but plot wise, strong. Until you come across with the “Artifact”. From that point the plot devolves into a complete mess. It’s overwhelming and not in a good way. Where noir works do so to hook, this one just messes you up. What’s the point of this in the plan of the city’s ministers and the criminals? What does it do? Why is it secret? Why is it so important? What is the connection between chopping people off into flesh plus eating them, and this thing? Why is this tumor in the back ask so many existential question? What is its purpose? You better off not asking these questions and more cause the cracks begin to appear. Albeit, there is no way in not asking them, the “Artifact” is the sole purpose this is a game! I take great care in story writing and more so in games where they want to tell a story like Backbone. But this game fails to deliver such, it is very convoluted. Not to mention the sound design leaves much more to be desired. At the end of the day Backbone is a lackluster post-noir detective Visually stunning and with a memorable cast of characters, the expansive world of Backbone and the story of Howard Lotor leaves much to be desired. A promising game, with a disappointing story.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like this game.  I want to support furry games.  I enjoyed the start a lot and where it was heading.And then it got super surreal super quickly, I was left with a lot of ??? and then it ended.  The last frame was,  I'm pretty sure,  pretty much my most hated trope of furry games, too.  Given the price, the part of it that I enjoyed I'd say was worth it, but with the note that it's because effort went into this and it's a furry game :P  If it was another genre I'd probably not recommend it.Still, for the parts I liked, they did them well.  Good environments (mostly)  Good soundtracks (mostly)  Good dialog (mostly).  I just wish it didn't leave me feeling like I'm walking away from a helicopter crash.  Good, good, good, spinning in circles and then exploding.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone was a wonderful experience. Not having any expectations going in (and not knowing about the aspects of the game that were initially promised in the kickstarter), I just found it to be a wonderfully paced and engaging narrative. I was really impressed with the artistic vision of this, whether or not it was what was expected during its creation. Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I got this for the art and music and was not disappointed. I will try to say whatever I can without story spoilers(I will discuss lore however).Dialogue choices are sometimes childishly edgy and force you pick an option that paints Howard as a person who doesn't know much, which was annoying to me. It forces the game to explain things to you like you're a new born. I loved the cheeky pop culture references throughout the game( my favourites were american psycho and the canines playing poker).Character work is quite cool and has some interesting NPCs(Clarissa and Renee are especially well written), it also does really well to make you trust or doubt characters whenever the plot needs it.The game explores some sort of animal class system where apes are revered, canines are treated as royalty and our protagonist(A Raccoon) is constantly harassed for being a 'striper'. They also seem to have a deity called 'The Shepard' but I could not find much lore that digs deeper into this. The suggestions of this societal structure was great for world building and they give us some more info in the final chapter.The story picks up very quickly and shows promise as a gritty crime noir but turns into a strange investigation into existentialism in the final few chapters making it feel like a detour from the original story. I do not know how I feel about the ending to be honest, I hope there's a part 2 that builds on the lore and characters. Shout out to my homie Anatoly the beaver.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: "Backbone" has a beautiful art style, awesome soundtrack, and a gripping story so far. If you're a fan of hard-boiled detective stories I'd definitely recommend it! If you're not, you might like it too so give it a shot.Post-game edit: Having now completed the game I still stand by everything I said previously, however it's worth noting that the game does have a turning point where it steps on the gas and does not stop and at that moment player choice starts to feel more and more like an illusion. I still recommend the game, but if you were captivated by the prologue and the actual detective aspects (as I was) you might walk away disappointed by the time the credits roll.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't been this let down by a game that had so much potential in a long time. I'll be pointing out the positives and negatives of the bullet points as follows. (go to point 5 for a TL:DR)1. The artwork: Extremely well done in both visual and style all throughout the game. Every scene, both big and large, is so crisp and enjoyable to look at. Whomever did this work deserve more work opportunities and the highest praise (That parade scene with the water, WOW!).2. The music: Great quality and really sets the tone and mood for the intended time period and setting. Really gives that noir flavor that you'd expect from what this game is going for....most of the time. There are a few spots in the game that have oddly placed pieces and really leaves one head scratching at times3. The characters: Really interesting and engrossing characters that leaves one chomping at the bit for more backstory and information about them. That said, the biggest let down is the wasted potential they had for literally all of the main characters. So many loose ends, and odd decisions for a few characters as well. Super disappointing in the end.4. The plot: Ohhhhh boy is this one a doozey. This game leads you on right off the bat as a noir style detective style game trying to do good by folks needing your help as you play Howard. It gets really interesting as you progress and uncover the truths. Unfortunately, the plot "peaks" too early in excitement and enjoyment. The plot starts flying off the rails at break neck speeds and jumps the shark with sudden plot points that really left me blinking on their choice and method of segway into such plot points. By the end, it left me wondering what the hell was really going on and what the point of many plot points were. Considering that there were so many loose ends left open (Would be a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing if they decided to do a cliffhanger route with DLC/ sequel for such points).5. TL:DR: Very interesting story (at first) with great art and music that brings you in, but hugely wasted potential in characters, plot, and generally overall. Not worth the money paid. If you're interested in this game, wait for a sale. Huge let down and largely wasted potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems to be tragically misunderstood. I get that people didn't get what they were expecting, and I get that this is all subjective in nature, but I think more people need to realize that the ending is bitter on purpose. This game was the developers' passion project; they wouldn't have made the choices they did without any thought.I think with different marketing and release tactics,  would have left less of a sour taste in players' mouths. And I think that this cold, disappointed feeling so many felt as the narrative concluded was exactly what was intended in setting the experience up with false promises.  lulls the player into a sense of comfort with its (initial) standard narrative beats, but then swiftly breaks down that wall of comfort and expectations, and fills its hole with something raw and disorienting. Comparing this game to , both works set up and knock down these same assumptions, and both of their conclusions disorient you in the same way. Looking at it through this lens, the narrative choices make much more sense. I think they did a fantastic job with this game, personally.The critique I have here is that the game's marketing wasn't indicative of any of this in the slightest. I think  tried to lull their audience into a false sense of security too hard and too early on, which ruined the experience for many people, unfortunately. If you don't mind a non-traditional narrative, then I highly recommend this game. If you do mind, or if you're looking for a cool detective mystery game and only that, look somewhere else.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game and I don't recommend this game. Read for the nuanced take.This is a fantastic game with an ending cut short. Seriously, you will not see it coming.I've seen criticisms against the abrupt shift in story after ACT III and personally, while it was startling and outright boring initially, I grew to appreciate the sharp left turn in the plot. It was unexpected and interesting. I read online that when the game was being crowd-funded on Patreon the devs had told their supporters that the ending given to us in the final release of the game was supposed to be the prologue, and that there was more of the story to tell. I haven't verified if this is true but after playing the game, observing the distinct change in tone after ACT III, and finally with the abrupt ending, it does seem like there was a lot more to explain and that the developers either ran out of time, money, or interest in this title. Either way it's a shame as the story, setting, and it's combination with the noire-crime framework made for a truly unique experience.If for nothing else this game is beautiful to look at. And not with just stunning art, or lighting, but with it's presentation of objects in the foreground and background. Thing reveal themselves slowly as you walk left and right of the screen and it makes for a very visually appealing and interesting look. The soundtrack is incredible. It strikes all the tones of a noire-backdrop but with hints of modern muscle-tensing action beats. It's a sound I don't know how to describe but you'll recognize, and trust me it works well with the jazzy noire sounds.I have one final criticism mostly aimed at the developers, should they actually read my random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ review. This one contains story spoilers. Seriously if you have even a slight wanting to play the game, do not read on.Anyways, my criticism is directed at you, developers because I feel you guys are extremely talented, and that I would love to see more from you guys. I think that this game was ultimately a great experience but fell flat at the ending. It's a small but big mistake, and one that is easy to learn from, I think. Please like this review if you think it helped you decide. Take care out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay, It really pulled me in. The prologue was fantastic, but the rest of the game suffered from a lack of mechanics from the prologue and poor worldbuilding. Backbone needed more time in the oven to fully flesh out the story and world it wanted to explore. With a bit of extra cleaning up and some work on the pacing it could easily be a 5/5. The Dev's letter says more to come for Backbone and I am excited, hopefully the next Game we get will be even better than the first.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone is definitely worth experiencing, but as for whether it's worth buying, I recommend playing the free Prologue and then asking yourself how much you would pay to play a few more hours of a much more linear version of that. I enjoy Backbone, but there are several caveats that prospective buyers must consider or else risk heavy disappointment (hence the Mixed overall rating at the time of this writing). TLDR: Unless you're a furry with leftist ideologies, you will be disappointed with how little Backbone there is for the price until it goes on sale for <$10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I am sad to say that I cannot recommend this game in good conscience. While the music and art style are both beautiful and works of art in and of itself, the drastic shift in gameplay from the first hour or so to the rest of the game was too jarring and ended up ruining my experience with the game. Backbone starts out with a simple task, investigate an otter under suspicion of adultery. Howard Lotor is an interesting character that the player wants to know more about, and talking with the people of the different districts within the walls really fleshes out the world and the connections between people. The first major twist of the game really has Backbone hit the ground running. I was immediately sucked into the story and wanted to know more. The puzzle aspect also gave me more to do than just walk about and inspect items or talk to various differing characters. Unfortunately this doesn't last, the latter acts of the game ditching the puzzles more in favor of exploring the environment and the characters inhabiting it.I have nothing against games that have the sole purpose of portraying a story. I've played plenty of visual novels and enjoy the interactive fiction genre. My problem with Backbone is that the game begins as something more than that. Interacting with the environment and the player deducing things too, not just Howard. The puzzle present in the beginning of the game was pleasant, it was a nice diversion from just letting the character put everything together for the player. Backbone introduces the mechanic of being able to move objects around when Howard inspects certain areas, but the  times the player utilizes this mechanic are during the tutorial and during the puzzle. Every time I found myself inspecting something up close I found myself looking for objects to move around. Trying to connect more things to find more clues, but it never happened after the first real utilization of the mechanic.  This is the main source of my disappointment with Backbone. The jarring change from a world I felt I could really interact with and the narrative experience of the latter portion of the game left me dissatisfied. Now, if the story aspect that Backbone decided to pivot to over the gameplay was done in a more satisfactory manner, the change from gameplay to story wouldn't have been as much of a problem.The game began by setting the bar high, but then shoves the player off that bar into a murky, confusing narrative that leaves the player with too many questions. The first thing I did after completing the game was look up to see if the game had multiple endings. My first thought after finishing the game was, "Did I get the bad ending? Is that why the ending felt so bad and unsatisfying?" I was unfortunately met with the reality that none of the choices you make in the game matter, and the ending I got was simply just... the ending. TL;DRBeautiful art and music, disappointing story after gameplay being reduced from detective/puzzle game to interactive fiction.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Anticipation and disappointment would best describe how i feel about this.The game starts out really good and from act I to act III, it feels like you're actually making progress uncovering the case.Then suddenly the bad writing comes in; Main plot is dropped (unfinished of course), Story-arcs go unfinished and Characters starts behaving differently.Then out of nowhere, the game introduces completely new plot-points before dropping the last remnants of the original story. And from here, the game goes to absolute sh*t.Luring you in with the well-made prologue demo seems like the developer's way of compensating for the garbage writing in the latter part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: After about Chapter 1 and midway through 2 the story felt hollow like it was fine just being a "lets bust the higher ups of society" story! But then it devolved into just madness and Howard breaking character for the sake of the plot NUMEROUS times as well as just numerous turns for the sake of shock value and nothing more. The beginning was excellent but it just sputtered out and crushed it self by not even bothering to elaborate or take its time. Plus its very very very short even if you investigate everything in the game it feels way way way too short.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write many reviews, mostly because my opinion's fall on deaf ears. But, this game really inspired me to do so.Backbone is a Detective-isk game, I say that because the game mostly tackles conversations with other characters to push a narrative. That narrative more or less is a jumble of cases which affect the main story line. I’m not gonna get into the nitty-gritty because it’d be far too spoiler heavy.  But to put it bluntly, don’t go into this playing a puzzle game. I more or less thought of it as a “controllable” visual novel that you (the player) pick the outcome to (kinda like telltale). I haven’t gone down maybe “bad” dialogue branches because I played the game as if I were the main character. But it’s something you can do, and characters react human with your responses. PS, learned after that no matter the dialogue  options the outcome is always the same, besides certain achievements. You'll get different things said to you but the end of the encounter is always the same.The visuals are some of the best I’ve ever seen, the game gave me an intianal Beastars vibe but as it went on the universe has its own independent feeling that makes it stray away from other worlds that have antratomorpic animals. Or, just human animals. The artstyle (pixel-art) makes it so characters are mostly distinguished through clothing rather than personal differences. Although certain characters, such as one of the main characters' friends (another raccoon) , have a different facial structure which sets him apart in a nice and familiar way. Now the characters are something I really wanna touch one. Renee being one of the main characters really made me happy she is a main character, she brings a weird sense of sweet sternness that I really like in her character, it even makes her a contender for my all time best girl! (sorry penny..). Also the main character is excellently written. All Howard’s character dialogue feels within the characters realm of personality, a nice man that does unreasonable things. Not to mention a lot of the side characters are also well knitted. You’ll only see them once per area. Not including Po, Mo, and something else I can't remember. But they all seem like actual people that live in this sad yet realistic version of a future Vancouver.Now for some of my gripes with the game. Around the late part of the 3rd chapter the story takes an unexpected turn… It caught me by complete surprise and to be honest I wasn't a big fan of that direction of the game. But I did still very much enjoy it. I do hope they make a sequel to Backbone because it deserves one, not only because of how the games ended but because of all of the potential. They talk about the outside world near the end (semi-spoilers) and revolution. I think if they go for a tlou2 approach where you play as the last games “side character”-Renee it could be very very interesting, or not even playing as her full time but playing as her more frequently than in this game. The inside and outside world have so much potential along with grand world building. But to conclude this review. I would personally advise someone who's into world builders to purchase this game. It delivers a very new and unique experience that not alot of detective/mystery games bring to the table. I think the game can be considered a bust because it doesn’t feel the same after the first 3-4 hours of the game. It’s still enjoyable but the same sparke is there. I hope anyone reading this has a decent grasp on the game, and I hope I didn't confuse the reader too much with the jumping around. This is my first review and I’m doing it because I'm genuinely passionate about this game. I think it could’ve been better but it still kept me on the edge of my seat wanting to play more. Thank you for reading my first review. -Buster

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a good noir detective game with antropomorphic animals play something like Chicken Police. This is essentially a glorified visual novel which just happens to have a detective as the main character.(minor spoilers)It's also not really a mystery game either. While the main character is presented with a case to solve, it never really does get solved in a fulfilling fashion. I didn't mind that at all but I can defiinitely see why people are disappointed by the final chapter of the game. I would even say it does feel a bit underbaked when compared to the rest of the game. However, I do not believe it is a reason to just disregard the game as a whole. The story takes a turn in Chapter 3 (out of five), so by the time it reaches conclusion the player should already embrace that the conclusion might not be what they initially anticipated.A lot of the criticism also comes from the fact that the relationship between Howard (the main character) and Renee (side character) which begins to form at the end chapter 1 just kind of stops existing after chapter 3. Funnily enough the writers of the game kind of dug themselves into a hole in that aspect. Some of the dialogue options seem to assume that you will like Renee right after the first conversation with her (there is even an achievement for "trusting her right away") and the character is definitely written in a way to make it the case for many of the players. Howard frequently mentions her in his thoughts as well, which sort of gives the impression the writers REALLY want you to connect with that characters for ultimately little to no payoff. I personally didn't fall for it, as aside from a common goal I didn't really see a reason to fully trust her, which I guess influenced my view of the entire game as well.(major spoilers) Also the pixelart in this game is gorgeous. The water reflections, the sun setting down - just beautiful stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: On its own the game's... okay, but not great. With the added context of broken promises and disingenuous advertising, it's a disaster.After a great start that was the prologue, the developers swiftly discard all the introduced mechanics in favour of a fairly linear narrative game, that becomes less and less coherent as the time goes on. The genre keeps shifting, the plot threads get cut off without a satisfying resolution and the characters make uncharacteristically dumb decisions, just so the story can have turn.I do love purely narrative games, visual novels, walking sims or simple adventure games. But even assuming that's what Backbone was always supposed to be, the final deal - aside from the fantastic visual style - is just not all that good.However, the game had a promise of being much more complex deal, even based on its demo alone. And looking at the Kickstarter page makes it quite clear, that what we got in the end was a bare minimum for this title to function.And don't even get me started on the queerbaiting they did with hyping a "bisexual raccoon detective", or the lousy excuses the devs were making when people called them out about having absolutely no indication of that in the actual game. It leaves a bad taste in my mouth, considering they've already started marketing the next game with claims of it being "more gay" and retweeting fanart with queer themes.

_childDocuments_.review: After a long time in development, and a Prologue available on Steam for over a year, Backbone finally makes its way to the PC and Xbox this week. It’s neo-noir piece of interactive fiction, set in a dystopian world of anthropomorphic animals, most of which are up to some form of shady dealings.You take control of private eye Howard Lotor, a flawed, lonely racoon, clearly modelled off hard-boiled detectives such as Raymond Chandler’s Philip Marlowe. The story begins in typical Chandler-esque fashion. Lotor interviews a distressed wife adamant that her husband is adulterous. What starts off a simple case of marital infidelity, soon reveals something much more sinister, and exposes widespread corruption across the city, covering all strata of life.Based on the strength of the Prologue, and first act, it’s easy to how Backbone become many people’s most wanted indie of the year. The script is excellent, totally believable, and feels like something from a classic novel. Finding your way in to the local club, come brothel, The Bite, is an early highlight, with nothing preparing you for what Howard finds in the basement. The later parts of the game, perhaps, don’t quite sustain the quality of the first acts, but don’t let that put you off this thoroughly engaging 5 - 8 hour story.Backbone’s art-style is truly wonderful, with the 2.5D pixel art aesthetic breath-taking on a high-resolution screen. The level of intricate details given to characters, buildings and backgrounds is impressive with dynamic lighting, rain effects and volumetric fog further helping to bring the dystopian Vancouver to life.The developers claim Backbone to be the modern evolution in the point and click genre. Howard can be controlled with either a controller, or mouse and keyboard, with the former working surprisingly well. Gameplay is primarily taken up with interrogative work and there are vast number of memorable characters to interact with. Once in conversation, you are able to choose responses from a list. Your decision can often change the tone and direction of the dialogue; although sometimes, even different responses lead to the same outcome – suggesting choice is more illusory than it appears. In typical point and click fashion, you have an inventory, and can pick objects up to give to characters, but primarily the narrative is driven by dialogue choices.The game also features some quite creative puzzles. One of the earliest ones involves moving around a series of documents on a cork board to reveal a key code. The ability to move whilst crouched, allows for some interesting stealth mechanics; you can hide in the shadows or create a distraction to pass foes. It’s all rather simple stuff but it does mix up the gameplay.Rather than a grandiose, 1940s style jazz soundtrack, as you may expect with a noir title like this, the soundtrack is subtle, and actually a little underwhelming. It’s not always present, and sound effects are kept to a minimum, even on busy streets.Like its protagonist, Backbone has its flaws. It’s by no means perfect, and may disappoint some, which is inevitable given the weight of expectation. Yet, for me, the script, the beautiful pixel art and the intriguing protagonist make this an easy recommendation.My video of the review features here:

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone! What can I say? I really enjoyed this game. It might not be the puzzle-solving noir game people were expecting, but it's highly enjoyable thanks to it's dialogues, the beautifully made pixel-art/3D elements, and characters such as Howard Lotor, the main character. Soundtrack is also really amazing, and I recommend you give it a listen, it's on Spotify. You can also buy it as a DLC! Perhaps one of the flaws I can see with this game is by how fast the plot shifts during act 3, without saying anything to not spoil you the surprise, but I think it's a twist well done but that needed more time to develop, there was a lot of potential with it but it wasn't fully fleshed out. Also, the game gives you lots of choices for dialogues but the game is linear af and the events will always be the same, there's only one ending. A bit more of freedom would've been cool but I take it more as the developers wanting to give you the freedom on how you want Howard Lotor to be by your choice of dialogue, which is fine.Despite flaws and some potential that wasn't fleshed out completely, I think Backbone is a cool and enjoyable adventure, but not exactly for everyone. I give it an 8.5 to a 9 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Labelled as a "post-noir narrative adventure" and a point and click, the atrocious thing Backbone grows and morphs into resembles some of the worst nonsensical, new age, post-hipsterism I have ever seen. Criminally mangled and misunderstood or just badly interpreted philosophies mesh with some of the most second-rate, shoddy and apathetic existentialist nonsense written by first year philosophy freshers that picked up some rudimentary knowledge off the back of a cereal box.The only redeeming quality and a good firm step is the "noir" epithet, but even that only applies to visuals, music and ambience, not writing or themes. Some really incredible and stunning scenery and backdrops from a dystopian, walled, apocalyptic Vancouver will follow your ailing and struggling brain trying to comprehend the ridiculousness of the story. At least your eyes and ears will have something to feast upon, with gorgeous parallax cityscapes of different districts filled with details to the brim and some amazing lighting washing over the city at all times, accompanied by some, as the developers call it, doom jazz, that just pulls at the strings of your soul.Having played the free prologue after finishing the game, I can see the terrific detective premise EggNut cooked up when it came out, but ultimately wasted with a horrendous hodgepodge of poorly thought out ideas. The first chapter and the prologue are the same, mechanically and gameplay-wise. Some smidgen of gameplay, like sneaking and a few puzzles, and multiple choices of progress sheepishly peek out under a lice-ridden blanket of black hole sized illusions of choice, rotten stereotypes, needless story fillers, introduced and then squandered plot points that all feel rushed and a mysterious wrapping that feels like a cop out for writing flaws and misused metaphors. All that neatly packaged into anthropomorphic animals does not make it redeemable in any way. Orwell's Animal Farm or Sartre's Existentialism is a Humanism this isn't.And it becomes worse the further you go. A badly written, ludicrous and presumptuous visual novel, devoid of any gameplay it advertised through Kickstarter and the prologue, that will fly over the top of many people's heads. It's also fond of pulling large words from a dictionary, like apoptosis and vellication, presumably to make it even more pretentious. An open letter from the developers framing the failure that is Backbone as an artistic, subjective spilling of their souls doesn't help the game's case much. But, kudos to them for sticking to their guns.There's no backbone in Backbone's story or a challenge to your perception, of any kind. Whatever is written about it on the store page is not there. It's a farcical caricature of everything it's purportedly inspired by, from existentialism, modern political regimes and class struggles to Lynch and Kaufman. It feels empty, pointless and tiring, just like your finger will feel after clicking through uninspired dialogues and dichotomies between character motivations and the information you're provided with, which is particularly egregious in the epilogue. And if those dialogues were inspired by old school CRPGs, someone definitely wasn't paying attention. It's a 4 hour slog through a bad cinematographer's mushroom induced fever dream that they had the nerve to charge 25€ for.Playing on an i7-7700, RTX2070, 32GB of RAM, and an SSD didn't cause any technical issues but also didn't make suffering through this shoddy theatre of the absurd any easier.

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone is a short but lovely (and dark) narrative-based game that subverted my expectations and left me wanting more. If you're expecting a game with heavy emphasis on puzzles and stealth mechanics, those things are fairly sparse here. Where it really shines and spends the majority of its time is in the development of the plot through your choices and dialogue.Top-notch story-telling.Wonderful visuals all-around. Character designs, pixel art, animation, and lighting are beautiful.Wonderful music.Solid mechanics (which I would have loved to see featured more)Speech in Backbone is a bit odd, in that it includes a lot of modern phraseology in a world where it feels out of place. I got used to it after awhile, but it did remove me from the experience a bit when it popped up, which was frequently. But I also get the sense of humor, which is great! There are also a number of moments throughout that were genuinely heartfelt and refreshing to see/be a part of. It is a game that's played as a linear experience rather than an open-world where you can freely travel between areas. It does feel limiting in that sense, but the bottom line for me is that it was a good experience, and I'm happy with what I got for the money that was spent on it. While the length of Backbone feels disappointing, the fact that I did want more is telling of the quality of their work, and I look forward to more games from Egg Nut in the future! (Would totally be up for a Backbone 2, or even DLC stories, if that's an available route - just sayin!)

_childDocuments_.review: All I'm going to say about the game is simple, I was excited because I thought it would be like a good version of LA Noir without the cheesy dialogues, the janky car driving, the glitches, and the amateur-ish voice acting... Hell it has furries even! Not to mention the nice retro graphics that bring me back to better gaming timesI thought that the first chapter was a good beginning, a random lad who returns late at night, & abuses his wife... and we're sent to follow him and see what's he up to? I was smiling when I entered the Bite a second time! I thought it was all good! We would find him, shoot a few pictures and case closed before moving onto the next case, eventually working our way to biggest and more ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up cases.And then there was the otter filets, the club is used to turn people that wouldn't be missed into filets to be eaten by apes. I was surprised as we kept digging and finding more powerful people involved, but then? I thought that Howard was going to become the bad detective and tighten everyone's nuts until they spill the beans, eventually bringing everything to light and cause a huge societal collapse or a revolution that results in your death by the powerful people.But nah, it all devolved into the protein thing, maybe it was related with the meat they were sending in the first place? Maybe, that could have been good… but then the game's writing crashed and burnt the moment they involved this “alien” thing nonsense and directed the game into existential nihilism which climaxes with... Howard just getting out of the City into the nothingness beyond the walls, he then ends up dying eaten by the parasite on his back only leaving his backbone (wasn’t the parasite supposed to CHANGE the individual instead of KILLING it?) The fragment with Renee and Clarisse? It didn't contribute anything else to the story apart from a “possible fight” We don't get even a post credit scene, we don't even know about Howard's mom or why he hates her, why the alien even killed him off or where Larry went to.Honestly, I'm glad I got the game for free… Because if I had bought the game and received this sh*t writing and end… I would have made sure the writing dept of this game properly learned how to develop a story, TLDR: Beginning is good, but then the game devolves into nihilism and alien nonsense and after it kills the main character for no apparent reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I absolutely loved this game. I even liked the weird twist that seems to be a point of contention in other reviews.I love the characters, top to bottom. From what we see of the baddies (you barely scratch the surface in this game), the supporting cast and random passers by, and the goodies helping you along.However, the themes in this game honestly kinda messed me up. I've been in a funk all week after I watched the credits roll. It's not so much the themes that affected my in this way, but more the way it was portrayed, and how you experienced it through the player.Spoilers below.The game's protagonist, Howard, dies in the end of the game. The horrific, tragic way that he died wasn't pleasant to experience. Having been infected by a symbiote of unknown origin, Howard slowly loses himself as the symbiote gradually consumes him. You converse with this entity a couple of times, having a sort of fever-dream argument. You can choose to hang onto Howard, or affirm the change. For me, choosing the dialogue option that read, "I am afraid" was less of a character choice, and more of a confession from myself.You watch [what was once] Howard walking through a desolate wasteland after escaping confinement and the city. As the sun rises, you see the remnants of human civilization break through the haze - a crumbling city and infrastructure. Howard's beaten, bruised, tumor-infested body gives up.As fantastical as death-by-symbiote is, it felt incredibly real. I had experienced, in a way, a very similar fate through my father. For him, it was COVID-19. Just like Howard, he died alone. He was hypoxic and afraid.This is the worst that I've ever felt after finishing a piece or media. Yet, I'm grateful. It made me address problems that I didn't know I had. As it turns out, it's gonna take a lot of work. I'll probably revisit this game when I get better.

_childDocuments_.review: What positive I can say about this game is that it's definitely absolutely gorgeous. However, unfortunately it's really let down by the writing. And when that's what 95% of the game is, that's a huge problem. It starts off well enough and really got its hooks into me and I was curious where it would go. Unfortunately, where it goes is nowhere particularly interesting. Plot threads introduced early on are completely dropped, new ones are introduced seemingly out of nowhere, characters behave strangely for no reason other than to move the plot along, and character motivations and actions just outright make no sense and are even outright contradictory by the end. Add on to that further disappointment that at first this seemed like a game where choices would matter, as in, if you're kind or rude to people or perhaps who you're kind/rude to, stuff like that, but as far as I can tell, none of that makes a difference at all. I really wanted to like this game, especially since it starts off so strong and looks so great aesthetically. But unfortunately, with those kind of flaws, I can't really recommend this. Like, ideas are definitely present in this game. But that's all they are: ideas. And they just come together into an incoherent contradictory mess that doesn't seem to have any clue of what it wants to be, what it's trying to say, if it wants to say anything at all, and just feels very unsatisfactory in those regards so unless you're nonetheless hurting for a visual novel and enjoy the aesthetic, I'd recommend looking elsewhere, unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: "its so f#$@ing sneaky that the game is GOOD for the first 2 hours then falls apart"The noir elements in the prologue (as in the demo) are excellent, and I was super hyped for this game. It stuck to them for a while, got a bit repetitive and overly expository, and laid out some interesting threads to follow. I think the meat of the 'hard-boiled private investigator' trope is in struggling against odds to achieve some minor, intractable change in an unforgiving (and ultimately largely unchanged) world. At the outset, it really looked like it was going to achieve this.  it undertook some curious genre-defying pivots that I do not believe worked well for it, left several plot elements off hooks, and attempted to stoke interest in secondary characters that I do not believe were ever sufficiently established. I feel like a presumed interest in secondary characters is something the game took for granted. A love interest and an established friendship aren't developed or conveyed as easily as the game desires; the former is particularly jarring given established conventions of femme fatales in the derivative genres. I felt the most connection to a charming cabbie, and for all they used the character, the developers abandoned them in a hurry.I did not experience any game-breaking bugs, but I don't believe there was enough content to really see the world shatter. A couple of clipping issues undermined immersion, but little else. Only a few spelling/grammar mistakes throughout. There were a number of weird cuts in the action, despite all the exposition, to different scenes - I felt at least twice in my four hours of playtime that I had missed something. It has the achievement issue of linear progression peppered with missable distractions, so if you're looking to 100% the cute furry game you're best off following a walkthrough. It has strong Night in the Woods vibes, but I'd probably recommend a few other titles before saying it deserves this likeness. I'll probably flick through others' reviews to see if I missed something - because I really feel like I did - and I feel that compulsion is a little telling.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I will recommend this game despite the fact that it left me disappointed. Here's why: it had a beautiful style and dark atmosphere. The characters were written in a unique way which made me like them even though I wasn't given the chance to speak to them a lot. Backbone really is a special game with a ton of potential and the 5-6 hour playthrough is worth it just for the cool ideas alone. BUT as many others pointed out, it just leaves a lot to be desired. The story is short, feels rushed and moves away from the detective aspect pretty quickly. If you are a fan of Blacksad or similar games this might not be for you. If you like stylish pixel games as well as artsy and philosophical twists to things, this might just spark your interest.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great story and commentary on existence and society. Plus it has some of the most breath-taking pixel visuals that I've seen! Yes, it's a short experience, yes it leaves a lot of cliffhangers, BUT I don't think it needs to have the pay off of wrapping up the ends on screen. There is the implication that it happens  And sometimes that's all a story needs to address the endings. We know what happens to the major players, we have an idea of the reasoning. It might be unsatisfying and I'm okay with that.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: This game was bummer for me. It really had very little anything with puzzles. In fact all the puzzle elements are in the introduction which you can play for free in the demo. As for the story it was interesting to the point but then takes a wile U-turn and completely changes genres. Goes from noir to scifi abruptly. Im not necessarily against scifi as I love scifi, but this game just sort of ends and i feel like so many loose ends, doesn't feel like a complete story and writing feels rushed at the second half of the game, and like i said no puzzles except for the start. I felt i only played half a game at best. Feels disappointing honestly. That being said I guess they are working on a sequel but as someone who was part of the kickstart, i feel like I was bamboozled a bit.Now Graphic/Art and Soundtrack is really good. I give them credit for doing a great job visually and audibly. Really liked the design of the characters and city.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Please do not listen to the negative reviews. I almost didn't buy it because of "Mixed Reviews" but the game sounded so good I decided to play it anyways and I'm so glad I did. There are so many criticisms - mainly of the final 3rd of the game - which, honestly, is the part that sells this game for me. Yes, the graphics are beautiful and the music is absolutely captivating which most people seem to agree on. I have become a better, cooler person just by throwing a few of these tracks on during road trips, like no lie. BUT what I love most about this game is the story and its world-building. Many people don't love the story or the fact that this is not a game where dialogue choices give you much variety in the endings of the stories, but that's the point. It literally says in the game description "There is no choice. We change, but we change nothing." And I don't understand why people would not recommend this game because it delivered on it's thematic promise in a dozen different ways. This game is daring and that means some people aren't going to like the strong choices it's making, but that doesn't mean it isn't an experience worth having. Also, somehow this game had the balls to  There's no option to skip it. And I legitimately cried.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I had a fantastic time playing Backbone. I'm surprised at the number of negative reviews, and would be very sad to see this game slip through the cracks - it is deeply atmospheric, thoughtful, and compelling, and the craftsmanship is obvious. Would I have been happy if there were more puzzles? Sure. Would I have left the game more satisfied if its resolution was neat and tidy? By definition.But who are players to criticize a game for something like that? Those things were not part of the developers' vision. They made the game they wanted to make, and it was a beautiful game. Sure, some of it was a bit janky or uninspired, and those are fair grounds for criticism, but I think it's weird how many reviewers are judging Backbone harshly on the basis of what they expected it to be, rather than what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: this is rather a novel than a game. your choice doesn't change the results. sometimes even the logic of the dialogues seems not fluent, as you can tell that the authors want to force the dialogues to a certain ending.  however, I would not say it has a bad ending. Actually I really love the ending, it feels like there is hope raise from the foggy and painful world.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Completely craps the bed in the last hour. To quote Eurogamer, this is "a moody narrative noir spoiled by absurdity" and "undercut by a non sequitur of an ending." I was really excited to play this, really invested and enjoying the first half, and then... the game takes a sudden turn that just completely killed all of my interest and enjoyment, and ended out of nowhere having told me nothing. All the plot threads set up in the first half go nowhere, and the insane ending comes out of nowhere and expects to be taken seriously only to just stop suddenly without the faintest hint of cohesion. I am legitimately angry and heartbroken. I can recommend the soundtrack, but unfortunately not the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this as I thought it would be a adventure/noir game. It is that for about 1.5 acts then drops all pretense and becomes a linear game where what you do doesn't really matter. While the story was okay, the first act sets this game up as a puzzle/noir game then it becomes something else entirely. I don't really even think the story was completely closed. Overall this was pretty disappointing, and I don't think its worth the price I paid for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: story isnt as good as it should be, the ending is left open and closed at the same time, its pretty short (I have 7 hours but thats because I walked away to do stuff for 2-3 hours), and generally its not a detective mystery game, it loses that after the prologue and youre honestly better off playing that for free and coming to your own conclusion of how things end, not to mention this game gets political about systemic sexism when most of the cast are women who are powerful, smart, or rich. A dialog line that was really horrible was when I was talking to a child and they remarked that they had a doll or something and they didnt like it and i had the choice to say "yea me too, I dont like gender sterotyping" as a detective raccoon tryna solve a case of cult like cannibalism which doesnt end up being anything interesting cause it gets redhairing into TL DR "I cannibalised these people to goverment officals so I can blackmail them and overthrow the goverment cause sexism". not a joke at all, play the prologue if you dont understand how let down I am with the full release of this game after TWO YEARS, $25, and 4 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a more philosophical gain rather than the more traditional narrative satisfaction that we would like to derive from it, and because of such, is more difficult to appreciate conventionally. This game does not stick the landing in a conventional way, and it hurts it heavily. It is harder to appreciate because of that, and if it'd manage to do both, that would be great, but sadly it doesn't. It is great visually and has an amazing soundtrack, yet the lack of a decent conclusion makes it difficult to recommend and enjoy. I hope there are other stories in this world that are as thoughtful and satisfactory.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cool little story. It's more of a talking simulator than a detective game. It doesn't really have many puzzles or deduction requirements; pretty linear. But, the story itself is cool. Good characters and conversational writing. It's the right length to not overstay its welcome. It's all pixel art, so if you're playing for the furry characters, you'll have to enjoy their fuzzy faces pixelated.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really cool. I played the demo and was pretty hyped for it. I was expecting a long, slow-burning game full of branching paths, intrigue, and impactful choices. I didn't get a long game, as you can tell by my hours played. I didn't get any branching paths. I got mere crumbs of intrigue, and I don't think any of the choices I made actually made any difference to the game's story. Two things might explain this failure to live up to the expectations set by the demo. One, the devs rushed the game out and simply didn't finish it. Two, the devs literally only had 4 hours worth of story to tell. For some games, 4 hours is fine. For a game about immersing yourself in a whole world, steeping down in to the nitty-gritty of it all, it's no where near enough. You're a private eye investigating a huge conspiracy that could topple the very foundations of an entire society. The story does not do enough to fulfill that pitch, and suddenly and randomly decides to completely change the direction of the narrative and make everything you thought was important entirely irrelevant. It's utterly mind-boggling. Game has incredible atmosphere, art direction and animations, and overall world-building. Unfortunately it is under-developed, full of weird, quirky dialogue that often takes you out of the moment, and possibly up its own ass a little too much. Hopefully whatever they decide to do next will at least feel like a complete experience, if nothing else.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone’s a good game, but it’s better if you know what you’re getting into before you play it.The prologue is not a good indicator of what the actual gameplay is like. The detective gameplay quickly takes a backseat in favor of a story that starts off very strong, but doesn’t quite stick the landing. It gets increasingly linear, to the point of reading more like a noir visual novel, so be prepared for that switch. I was disappointed at first, but the artstyle and dialogue options in the game are excellent, and carried my interest through to the end. There is some seriously gripping imagery in this game.It’s a short game, but a very memorable one and I’ll be replaying it again soon. Eager to see what else EggNut makes!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: The game is so anti-climactic. So Kafkaesque. It takes a U-turn midway so fast you'd splat across the windshield as if you were a bug.I've been eyeing the game since 2019, and I remember being blown away by the mysterious air surrounding it. I mean, c'mon: A detective noir game with anthropomorphic animals, pleasant jazz (as if jazz isn't pleasant but whatever), mature themes, interesting dialogue, and impeccably  pixel art? I SIGNED UP IMMEDIATELY!The prologue showed the crux of what the game was supposed to be: Full of interesting characters, brim with good puzzle design (with a touch of backtracking, but I think it was fine), and shocking discoveries that led me further down the dark rabbit hole. It was all sublime.I don't care much for the choice-based dialogue elements in games because I know first-hand how painfully DIFFICULT it is to design — let alone develop — a similar system; it's not worth what little it provides. Besides, it's a detective game anyway... linearity is doable, and still enjoyable. Always is. Always will be. But if you are a sucker for that kind of thing, you should know they are weak; inconsequential to your progress as both character and player. At best, it plays towards your headcanon about the personality you want for the protagonist.But the rest of the game was diluted down to nothing more than a walking simulator that seldom had anything interesting for you to do. The entire game, though essentially a point-and-click adventure, instils the need for keyboard inputs. I felt that decision made no sense since the game's nature is PERFECT for a point-and-click game.Additionally, there wasn't a lot that took me out of the main story's focus. The rest of the game lacked the challenge of puzzles and 'greasing palms', so to speak, that I found in the prologue. No tinier game elements with which I could play around with. No consequences to the actions I upheld.So all the while, I was 'strolling along' with the narrative. A quick visit here, a bit of small talk there, but that's about it. Nothing that encouraged me to do or explore more. Nothing that helped me dive deeper into the game's world. Nothing to do with all the lore I could gather, if at all. Even with all that visual beauty, any implicit value I expected to find in the game was entirely absent.Characters were an afterthought. Some of them were too controlling, or rather the protagonist gave up control too easily; take your pick. While some were likeable, characters were quickly sidelined by the  direction of the plot. Their motives, purpose, interests, vision, roles, personalities... including those of the protagonist... didn't matter.It was devastating for me to witness how the thrill of the hunt for the ANSWERS to my questions, the KEY to the mystery, the END of the LINE... was forcefully shut down for the sake of catering to an absolutely  genre-changing decision that was made midway.Since that point to the end credits, I was left with one final thought: 'What the ♥♥♥♥ did I play?' And it's a valid question. What was the game about? Was it ever about the murders? Was it ever about the rabbit's foot? Was it ever about showing how curiosity can kill the cat?You will not find agency here. Only questions. Questions that you started the game with but were left unanswered anyway. Questions that leave you completely speechless and baffled. Questions that make you think in introspection what the flabbergasting  was happening in the writer's room for these decisions to have been made during development.I was looking forward to enjoying this game. Damn. Is this what being cheated on feels like?
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: What caught my eye initially was the art. I didn't think it would have a lot of ambiance~ but the great soundtrack, the small details in the environments and the plot.. it was a great game to play. Not sure if its worth 20 dollars but I definitely enjoyed the experience. I liked being able to decide most of the dialogue but it doesn't seem to be a multi ending type of game. I think it would've been better if there was a directory on different endings or different significant changes in the plot. 10/10 highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me, you checked out this game, became interested, read the very mixed reviews, and decided to skip on this one. I'm here to tell you to give it a chance.First of all, the art style of this game is amazing. Every new level gave me much joy just from looking at the world it portrayed. Honestly, this alone is worth buying this game (when it's on sale) and playing it. Then we have the story. It starts out how you would expect it to do in this genre. Then just a bit over the middle of the story it kind of shifts. This is what most of the negative reviews talk about. It goes from your typical 'noir' genre to a more  themed story. Another thing a lot of people did not like was the way the story ended.Personally I did not mind the shift in the story. It did feel a bit weird, but it did not stop being interesting or fun. The ending, while a bit unsatisfying isn't terrible either. It doesn't go the way you'd expect, but that doesn't mean it's bad per se. The only thing I would say is that I feel it ended too fast. I recommend this game if you love the art style and if you like a mysterious story and don't mind if it gets a little wonky. I wouldn't buy it for its original price, it's a bit too short for that in my opinion. But when it's on sale and you feel intrigued: try it!
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts off so strong with a compelling murder plot, gorgeous artwork and gritty atmosphere. For the first half of the game, stealth and item use mechanics hold enough interest to carry the plot along. However, the second half of this game feels incredibly rushed, and said mechanics are nowhere to be found. Essentially, the game devolves into a visual novel in the second half, and in my opinion, the overarching story is not fleshed out enough to maintain the compelling gameplay the first half offered. The second half of the game, I felt as though I was going through the motions in hopes that the part I was playing was just a lull in the story. However, after slogging through the dialogue, the game just ended in a way that felt incredibly unceremonious. With all of the potential and intrigue of the first half, I was left feeling as though I had just played an unfinished game. This game is gorgeous. The atmosphere is amazing. You can tell that so much effort went into the visual aspects and character creation. I wish they could have delayed the release and provided a story that was more than just surface level sci-fi horror. So disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I expected a bit different story from what I had chance to play thought the prologue.But well, it was not that bad how many say here.First, the art is delightful, as the world is. It's total masterpiece.Characters are amazing, deep, beautiful and intense.But it's an linear story, none consequences, even the tiniest one.The story is short, I imagine the game could be twice as long.Soundtrack is cool, but plays almost never.Only one puzzle or miny game.Long story short, it had bigger potential. But it can be a great start for future of epic Backbone world.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only starting with act II but I thought I would give this a bit of a write-up so far.In short, I am having a lot of fun, the story is intriguing and the game is quite unique with enough familiarity that I feel a degree of nostalgia while maintaining a sense of newness to the experience. The music and the sounds are something that I am enjoying in particular.I adore animals so I think that gives me a soft-spot for games with anthropomorphized animals as characters, and I truly love pixel art games especially the point-and-click variety... so I jumped at the opportunity to try out Backbone when it popped up on Steam. The feel of the game is good, which allows me to get drawn into the story and I've already had a mix of emotions notably from one "ohhhh, crap" moment; to others where I felt invested in a character, and due to my decisions, I have been left wonder if there is now a missed an opportunity as well as a dejected and disappointed character I might have to face in the near future. I am excited to get more into the story, and definitely makes me want to play for just "one more hour". It also feels like the creators are using the nature of having animals as characters to more gently touch on some sensitive topics, so I would wager that a lot of effort and thought has gone into the dialogue and characters that you meet along the way.To the devs:Loving your game, really well done. One or two minor tweaks might be needed with the speech overlay and potentially walking past interactable items, which catches me out quite frequently. Also reading the note in the minor in the changing room in act I while stood to the right of the note caused a second main character sprite to render an idle animation until I started moving again.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Great visuals, art style, and music, but some of the story beats felt unearned, like I was watching a movie that was skipping several scenes so that things aren't making sense anymore. I hope the devs release an extended version that ties together all the unfinished storylines and does justice to its (pretty amazing) characters.Still, I would recommend this game because I loved it despite its flaws, and I would play the hell out of a sequel. Don't let the other commenters dissuade you from buying and playing it. I still had a lot of fun and it it made me think.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: It's not quite the game I expected. The actual detecting is somewhat limited and the plot and gameplay is very linear. You can make some choices along the way that come back at later points in the game, but none, as far as I can tell, alter the actual progression of the storyThe game is short-ish, with a story that can be completed over a few hours, but for the price it currently sells at, I think that's an appropriate amount of time.The story overall is well thought out, and quite dark. The game goes for lo-fi pixel aesthetics of old-school adventure games, but manages to still look pretty stunning mostly thanks to the level of detail put into backgrounds.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I had a really good time playing this game.7 hours without rushing nor being that slow, so I'd say it's acceptable for the price and considering the fun I had discovering this strange and immersive story.Beware it is not a game with puzzles to solve or requiring deductive skills, it is more of an interactive novel in a dystopian world, really well presented with stunning pixel art and really good music.It's sad there are so many negative reviews because I think this game doesn't deserve that kind of bashing.I can understand that some people who had played the free prologue felt disappointed that the full game orientation is not all focused on a classic noir detective story as they could have expected, but for me, having played the game as a whole, everything wraps up smoothly, even if the ending felt a little bit abrupt.I would be glad to discover more about Backbone universe in the future.Well done to the dev team.

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful game, gorgeous, also the response options can be hilarious as u can choose to senselessly flirt or be a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at times.
