_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: So, I’m going to start this review off by saying a few things, first this review will contain major spoilers for the game and second, I really wish I could leave a mixed review, but I choose to leave a positive review because I am very interested in what will come next with this universe that Backbone sets up.      Let’s get into some of the meat and potatoes, first of all is Backbone anything like the prologue that was released in 2019? Yes and no, something I was really bummed out about is that unlike the prologue, Backbone doesn’t have any puzzles or complex sneaking sections outside of the prologue and what felt like a throwaway section in the factory. Now when it comes to the soundtrack and art style, I felt that Backbone majorly out preformed the prologue, I thought the game looked and sounded better than the prologue did.   To talk about the dialogue system in Backbone I found it unique yet slightly restricted. It felt like Backbone does a great job at providing the illusion of choice with a lot of its dialogue systems, this illusion being no matter what you pick you tend to end up exactly where you need to be for the story to progress. I don’t mind this style of dialogue I just found it interesting.   As for characters, Backbone does have a very interesting cast that I found myself enjoying the company of. I thought Howard and Renee are a fantastic duo as well as Howard and Anatoly plus who can forget Howard and Larry? All the character interactions were really good, and I enjoyed watching their character development play out. I wish that the game was longer honestly so that I could see more interactions playout. I did absolutely love the Epilogue section, I thought that and all of Howards one on one’s with Renee were probably some of the best interactions in the game.  As for the story itself, it’s good but a little confusing? I was following along great and was super invested until the end of Act III. It just felt out of character for how I played Howard’s dialogue for him to make it all the way to the Artifact, get told not to touch it, and then instantly touch it and have it become part of him. I guess to its credit the game was taken in a direction I could have never expected and I’m excited to see where it goes, but I felt like it was trying to avoid playing it safe a little too hard. Honestly, I would have been perfectly okay if the Artifact didn’t infect anybody, and it was still contained in that room. There could have been more set up of the tension between Howard, Renee, Bloodworth, and The Apes in Act IIII and maybe consequences for Howard’s meddling and then switch the Epilogue around to be something related to the Artifact that sets up a sequel. Because I think the part that is drawing the most negative feedback to this game is the ending of Act III. Even as Act IIII stands I really enjoyed it, I really like establishing the Under the Bridge section of people, I think it does a great job at deepening the depth of the world. I get killing Anatoly to establish that the Artifact isn’t controllable by Howard and that we should be worried about it doing something horrible during Act IIII, but it never does which threw me off a bit. The suspension of something happening just kind of faded away halfway through Act IIII, I just felt that there was nothing to be worried about until the dinner scene with the guitar playing, that’s where I was at the most vulnerable for something to happen with the Artifact but instead Howard is kidnapped which I felt worked too. This is a little bit more gameplay sided but I really liked how there was no way to undo any choices that you made; it gave a sense of permeance to how you treated people and the choices that you made.  Artistically and musically Backbone is a very easy 10/10, I could have never asked for a prettier game that sounded as wonderful as it did in my entire life. Honestly, I think this is the strongest element of Backbone and frankly part of the reason I was so easily able to play the game and never felt like I had to trudge through it. Really, I could go on all day about how wonderful the soundtrack is and how pretty the game is but frankly I don’t think I could give it justice in words, you just have to go watch and listen for yourself.  Overall, I think the only way I could score this game accurately due to all the ups and downs I felt it had, is a scale of 1-100. I would say that Backbone was a solid 75/100 which for Eggnut, a brand-new studios first project I don’t think is too shabby at all. I enjoyed Backbone, I finished it right before writing this review and honestly, I want to play it again because of how I regret some of the choices I made. I really feel had this game been given some more time to focus on some gameplay elements, stealth sections, and maybe a little more work on laying some more foreshadowing and foundations for transitioning from detective in over their head to alien tumor it would have worked better. It’s not that I didn’t like the idea or concept of the transition, it just felt a little bit forced and slightly confused on what it wanted to be. I wish the Howard and Artifact sections had a bit more dialogue choices for Howard fighting the Artifact and trying to not conform into it. In conclusion, I personally enjoyed playing Backbone and intend to play it again, but I couldn’t blindly recommend it to anybody, I would have to prep them alongside my recommendation. A few simple things like, there is no gameplay outside of the prologue and it takes a weird turn you might not enjoy but stick it through to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love noir titles and the way the writers made this game was very true to the genre.... up until about the 3rd act. I'd been following this game's development for a couple years which makes it a bit more disappointing. I didn't quite enjoy what seemed like a sudden shift to a sci-fi genre (the prometheus liquid was too much imo), but still finished the game for the mystery aspect. I would have loved if Backbone didnt incorporate so much of the sci-fi and stuck to just mystery/crime drama etc. Aside from that though still glad to have played it - finished it in about 6 hours total, wish it was longer.To be candid, play the prologue - it's the best part of the game and has all the excitement built in. I don't feel like the $22-$26 tag is worth it for the full game unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics, but too expensive for five hours of gameplay that goes nowhere. At first I was curious to see if future instalments would complement the story, but going by the open letter the game devs published, they have learned nothing and future games will just be more of the same disappointment.I can’t recommend this game and will not be playing future entries. (I recommend Disco Elysium, though! If you're looking for a brilliant detective game where your choices actually matter)
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: people complaining about the lack of choices missed the point of the game heehee but ill admit i just bought it for furry animals but the story is quite an interesting look on humanity and existential dread i havent kept up with any marketing prior but yeah if u just wanna walk around, read and get hit in the feels its good
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: The noir and pessimistic environment were engraved with faded colors, well-prepared dialogues, and the people who never cast their eyes on you with any good intentions. This game is for people who are looking for a companion to their loneliness and feel the struggle of fighting against windmills with the very hope of changing the corrupted status quo.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: So I didn't play the prologue when it was first out. I thought this looked so spectacular that I waited until the full release to get the game. The prologue WAS INDEED spectacular! The style and music is fantastic. I was so stoked for the rest of the game and when I completed it today (total of three hours of playtime) I can honestly say I feel swindled. I am not the kind of person who needs neat and tidy endings but this was on another level. About a little more than a third of the way through, this stopped being a detective game and turned into a boring, freshman-level philosophy conversation clicker in which the choices you make don't actually do anything. The dialogue itself feels unedited and stiff. I genuinely feel like all the effort was put into making the prologue and the rest was cobbled together a week before release.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game to completion on XBOX Game PassDefinitely mostly just a walking simulator. Walk here, talk to people, walk there, you get it. But it's cozy with a Noir aesthetic I personally appreciate. I enjoyed meeting these characters and following through the story. My only issue is that it's far too short for what I'd like. The Acts of the game couldve been more, and the ending leaves me wanting more as well. The transition between two of the acts was incredibly jarring and went more along what i had thought might happen than I expected, honestly. Also, I do enjoy that there's hints of world building that aren't fully explored, though part of me wishes there were a book follow up to the game to really dig into it. Overall 5/7 perfect game

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRGraphic novel with extra steps. Nono.DESPITE this being a negative rewview over all, I recommend people still play this game because it really is intrigueing. I think many people can enjoy it despite its flaws. Now, that being said: *SPOILERS AHEAD*You were warned.I liked this game, especially the characters and music. Sadly I can not give a neutral rating, so I have to give it a negative one. Let me elaborate:The characters and art are great, the music is wonderful and the visuals really give you a feel for the different situations.What I didn't like was how the story progressed. I feel like there was no proper conclusion, no real explanation. A bit like in "Under the Dome" where *SPOILER ALERT* they just say "oh yeah it's magic btw" *END OF SPOILER* at the end.It just feels so incomplete. Clarissa was made out to be evil and in cahoots with the apes, but somehow at the very end the dialogue options push towards her just being a very angry woman who hates men. Men, specifically. Not the apes per se, just men. Howard going beyond the wall and literally just dying is such a bad ending in my opinion. I'd rather have been left not knowing what became of him and instead see what becomes of everyone else.Especially Anatoly. I refuse to believe he's dead. All in all, yes, good game, I enjoyed playing it and I enjoyed all the characters. But the story itself was... lacking.Lastly: there is only one ending. So none of your actions have any impact on how the game ends. You could be rude to Renee the whole time and then tell her you love her at the end. The only thing that different dialogue options get you is certain achievements. Which means you can't get all the achievements in one play through, despite there being literally no reason to play it again.This is probably my first negative review on steam and I am kind of sad it's for this game, because it genuinely had amazing potential. But a story-based game with a lacking story can't really get a good rating for it...

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone. Or "Tails Noir" as it has been renamed. It's a game that I did not expect anything from. I launched it and let it prove itself. ...and what a beautiful performance it turned out to be.First of all the pixel art style is incredible. It's used competently and everywhere in the game, there is attention to detail. The colors, shadows, clothing, palettes...etc. Everything looks stunning in the pixelated style used. It's one of the many things that add to the beauty of the game.The soundtrack is truly unique. It's not trying to fill blank parts with mindless background music or use sound effects where they are not needed. Every single sound you hear seems to serve one purpose; to make the world you're in come alive. It's captivating, refreshing and immersive.When it comes to gameplay, it's simplicity. Nothing mindblowing, nothing mindnumbing. It's exactly where it needs to be at, for the game to tell the story it's trying to tell. You move left and right, you interact with objects and you read the text bubbles from interactions. In conversations with characters, you read it and click whichever response you feel is in line with the values of your character.The plot itself is engaging and makes you feel like you're right in the middle of it. It twists where you don't expect it to as well as being wholesome and entertaining at other times. You are made to feel that what you choose to say has an impact and carries weight. All in all, Backbone (or "Tails Noir") was not the game I thought it would be. However it's the game I am glad I played and would regret to never have experienced. It takes about 3 to 4 hours if you take it all in and is well worth your time. Make some coffee, kick back, relax and enjoy the story.

_childDocuments_.review: *No Spoilers*Backbone is a very stylish game with a well-set mood and a story that is well-scoped to its world. The game peaks in the first chapter and then again in Act IV but is engaging and moody throughout. As a visual, musical, and narrative experience, Bakcbone really knocks it out of the park. It's combination of pixel-art and 3D effects had me genuinely engaged with my screen from minute one. Shadows, lights, and water some together beautifully, especially when you crank the graphics settings up to the top. Further, the soundtrack (which I found regrettably absent at times in excess of what the noir genre demands) was haunting, atmospheric, and slammed straight into my music library.That all said, Backbone is a game held back by many of its game-play elements, such as the player's minimal ability to interact with the world and short stealth segments that are, at best, Barebone. Further, the game's often profound and funny dialogue is sometimes held hostage by a conversation system that feels both a little too gamey and inconsequential at the same time. Backbone's handful of puzzles are its saving grace on this front and, while not complicated, they put a nostalgic, point-and-click smile on my face.In all, if you want to love this game, you will. There's a lot of good stuff, I'd even say brilliant stuff, to be found in the game's world. Part of me wishes it was longer but another part of me had to grit my teeth to get through the middle bit of the game (if you do play it, make sure you get to Act IV because it honestly changed my whole view of the game for the better). Backbone is a 4-7 hour masterclass in worldbuilding with hit-or-miss presentation. I recommend this title wholeheartedly if you love noir vibes and are looking for your next game-novella. I don't recommend this title if you're looking for your next stealth game or if you are expecting an intricate social system. Enjoy the game and cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR It's a fantastic environment and world, but it ends too soon. If you love the Noir style/genre, it's worth it. If not, maybe wait for a sale.It's rare I include a review on a game, but this one left me feeling really conflicted. I picked up the Prologue shortly after it came out and was drawn in to a very interesting (and disturbing) world. I'm a big fan of these games and I think they have some of the best story telling out there.This game both exemplifies that and fails it. Some parts of the story feel intricate and deep, with your dialogue choices (which as far as I can tell do not affect anything in game) emphasizing the serious or humorous parts of the story. Other parts feel incredibly rushed. At one point I had to check and make sure I hadn't accidentally skipped a huge amount of content, as it felt like their was no way it ended so quickly. I don't want to give any examples especially since many would include heavy spoilers, but just know if you want a fully fleshed out story, this might fall a little short.Overall the game was under 4 hours (closer to 3 without checking for every possible interaction and a restart). It's a shame there isn't a mixed rating on Steam as I'd put the game closer to that. It draws you in really well at times, falls short at others, and definitely ends in a way some people will like, and some will hate.Overall: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's weird to not recommend a game on the basis of an ending. I think Mass Effect is one of the greatest games of all time, but it does have a really lack lustre ending. Does an unsatisfying conclusion mean that you can't love or recommend something? Backbone is a detective noir game which introduces you to a struggling private detective in the beautiful backdrop that is downtown Vancouver. There is genuine charm in the pixel art, and really sharp 'human' dialogue that helps to set up an incredible world of class structures, and the struggle between the have's and the have-not's. The conversations and personalities you interact with are really superbly written, and may be the best part of this game.Like many others, I think the first 3 acts of the game are absolutely stellar. There's a real mystery you're slowly unfolding, and I appreciate that the choices you make which seem inconsequential and bitty come back in the dialogue later on. Despite the linear nature of the story, there's definitely room for a personality to emerge which really fleshes out the character and their relationship with everyone else. The last two acts of the game feel like 'jumping the shark'. It feels out of place, and almost as if someone else came in to write the ending in a way that the player wouldn't see coming. Like someone who really wanted to make you go 'what a twist!', even though it's so tonally inconsistent with the front half of the game.One criticism I've read and kinda agree with is that the game is somewhat unforgiving in how you move the narrative. If the trigger for the end of the scene is 'read the newspaper on the table', there isn't much of a clue that maybe you should check the rest of the room first. Sometimes it's obvious ('Leave the room to progress the plot!'), but sometimes it catches you by surprise when you poke one element of an otherwise really interesting scene, and you're whisked away to the next scene. Combine this with a very rudimentary save feature that only saves at the start of the scene (which means you can very easily get pushed into the next scene and overwrite your only save slot) and it can be an exercise in frustration to think 'wait, I really wanted to engage with X and didn't get to'. To that criticism, I will say that I didn't really mind it as much. It keeps your choices tense and when it's done well, it really shines. As an example, one time I thought I'd try to get smart with one of the characters before I'd really checked out the room, and it turns out that character was in charge of the place and had me thrown out of the location. It's unfortunate that I didn't get to talk to everyone, but that felt organic and real that I'd tripped into pissing off the wrong person, and as a result I was thrown out of the scene. That's a neat evocative feeling of actually feeling like I'd been ejected from a room because of a choice I'd made, and I'm down with that. It is less forgiving when it's something like 'oh, I can sit here and read the newspaper' only to advance the scene when I thought I was just doing something inconsequential. All in all, I really like a lot of the setting, the dialogue, and the relationships; but it's ultimately a dissatisfying experience and given how short it is; you could probably just go watch someone else play it to get the same sensations.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is worth the purchase. Despite the flaws, it was an experience that I enjoyed. I think it's well worth the purchase. That being said, I have a couple gripes with the game:This game is interesting. Its biggest problem isn't really its pacing, as some reviews have claimed. Instead, I think it's the way it chooses to conclude its story. Without getting too spoilery: nothing really feels satisfying about it. Not saying it has to conclusively explain every detail and leave nothing up to interpretation. It's really just that it neither feels like a satisfying conclusion to Howard's journey nor a logical conclusion of and statement on the themes that the story has been building up to. It sort of just feels like an . It left me with a sort of "that's really the end?" feeling instead of a "that was a good place to stop" feeling. Perhaps I just need to sit on it, but it really just didn't feel like a meaningful way to end a story with this much narrative potential.Tldr; This game does not really live up to the hype. Do not play it based on that. I'm going to recommend it, but on sale. I'm not sure I can really recommend it at its current price. A decent amount of it feels a little half-baked. If you want a stylish detective story with a decent amount of intrigue, encourage you to pick this one up.

And now, having finished it for the first time, was it worth the wait?...I can't say for sure. This game is...frustrating.I did enjoy my time with it, some may say that it was too short but I try not to judge a game based on that metric as I believe it's not an accurate reflection of the quality of a game (for instance, how many AAA open world games are filled with meaningless "content" just to pad out the runtime?). _childDocuments_.review: I had the pleasure of playing the prologue for Backbone back in 2019 and I absolutely adored it. I was immediately intrigued by the story that they set up with it. It was an incredibly interesting, soulful first chapter in what I hoped to be an incredible story.After playing the full game I'm kind of left with the same feeling. That this is an incredibly interesting setup for a grander story. Everything that's here is full of personality. These characters are relateable, they feel real, their reactions to the world around them is real. The story that's being told has so many angles that it's hard not to become invested in it immediately. The problem that I'm left with is that, for a first outing, I feel like there just isn't enough. I think the ambition to leave so many plot threads open for sequels or spin-offs or whatever they have planned is an incredibly risky move that I hope pays off in the end. But I think it's clear the reason we're seeing such a "mixed" response is because most people, myself included were expecting more. It feels like a second prologue, rather than the full version of the story that was previewed to me two years ago. This is clearly chapter one in a much bigger story and unfortunately it's a very short chapter that asks for a pretty hefty price tag considering the amount of content. I'm happy to pay it, I don't feel like my money was wasted, and I believe in this team's ability to expand on this world in a meaningful way, but I understand why so many people are left unsatisfied. People were hoping for a more conclusive and hefty experience given it's 5 year development time. And unfortunately my experience with the Steam userbase is that a lot of these people are incredibly harsh and judgemental, and they tend to be very eager to tell you so when they feel personally wronged by something (Which happens a lot, because they seem to take EVERYTHING personally, but that's neither here nor there).I would strongly recommend that people play this game despite the general response. Play it knowing that it's open ended, play it in hopes that this series will be expanded on in the future. As someone who genuinely loved this experience I would hate to see this story's future shattered by people who didn't understand it. I believe in this team and I believe in the story that's being told, I just wish there was more of it on day one.

The cityscapes are gorgeous, and combined with the music, the atmosphere of this game is top notch.I enjoyed the dialogue too - I haven't played a second time (my long playtime is from me accidentally leaving the game running when going to do something else) so I can't speak for how linear vs branching the conversations are, but every character, even just inconsequential ones on the street, had personality and flavour, and I didn't tire of stopping to talk to everyone I could.I do agree with the other reviews here that the game might have benefited from more puzzles and explicit opportunities for player choice and agency, and a more conclusive ending, but I still found it a great and worthwhile experience - there was just potential for it to be even better. I'm definitely still excited to see what the developer has in store next.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game in under 5 hours, I can safely say that the game itself felt incomplete. However, it feels like the story tries to go off into too many directions at once and then fails to give any conclusions or real meaning to your actions. Without giving too much away: obvious that the ending was meant to be a cliffhanger for either a sequel or to give a feeling of "what if?" but it really only left me feeling empty and disappointed.Overall, what this game does well is an absolutely gorgeous setting and music/sound design, but it really doesn't make up for the lack of content. _childDocuments_.review: Although I have mixed feeling about the game, I do recommend it overall, so long as you don't expect it to be like the Prologue.Backbone starts off like a detective noir for the first 2/3  of the game, an intensely enjoyable narrative rollercoaster. The traditional puzzles of the Prologue are never to be seen again, but that's not to say that what replaces it is somehow lacking - just different. The characters are likeable, and there are plenty of tense moments. The jeopardy ticks up and up over time, resulting in tense moments, followed by occasional comic relief to offset the mystery turning increasingly grim.However.The final 1/3 of the game is... uhhh... head-scratching. A twist changes the tone, pacing, and well - everything about how the game feels. It's mostly weird, it's unexpected, and eventually leads to a deeply unsatisfying end. It's as if Backbone started as a game and but increasingly lost the desire to be a game, to be for the player, and became more and more its own thing, living for itself despite the player. Perhaps, on some meta level, this is quite poetic.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Unfinished and unsatisfying.The gameplay is nothing to write home about, and there doesn't seem to be any change in outcome based on the decisions you make.And that's fine, the story, atmosphere, and world-building are superb. The stakes keep escalating and you constantly have to adjust your brain to what kind of story you're really in....But then it just stops. So many concepts and plot threads keep building up your expectations and suddenly the game is over. There isn't any clear answers, catharsis, or satisfaction to be found. All the vibrant character work fizzles out, and you're left unfulfilled.I understand running out of resources and having to roll out what you have, but I was so invested that I would have preferred a "to be continued in part 2", even if part 2 only took the form of an ebook. Very disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game. A true testament to my stubbornness and curiosity more than anything.I did not expect this game to be even 5% as good as Grim Fandango or any other of the classic adventure games.But playing this just stirred up emotions of bitterness, anger, hopelessness. Not from anything the writer intended, quite the opposite. How could I be so gullible to finance such ill hidden political statements. I should have known better, small signs were already in the free prolog and I should have read the reviews before buying.There is no way around it in 2021 but usually the agenda is embedded in an actual game, not just packaged in a closed ended and witless dialog that does not affect anything.I guess all the right checkboxes were ticked to fit the present day.* Humorless* Close ended dialog* Shallow and self-righteous* Embrace and mutilate a classic and beloved genres (Noir and adventure games in this case)The OK:* graphics* sound design* prolog musicThe not OK* Story* Dialog* Characters (or dept of)* Marketing it as "Noir"* Marketing it as a game
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: The game has an amazing art style that brings so much life and charm, but sadly that's where the positives really end. The story was compelling in the first couple acts, but starts to get messy, loses direction and leaves more questions than answers in a bad way. Dialogue choices in the game were also weird, some choices that felt like big forks or allowed for different outcomes didn't feel meaningful or impactful, meanwhile some other dialogue choices that didn't feel important turned out to change the direction immensely with no warning. Characters also felt like they had little time to develop and really didn't stick with me long. Puzzle mechanics that were introduced in the beginning were not really used later in the game as well. tl;dr: Beautiful looking noir-style game with lots of wasted potential in mechanics, dialogue and story. Hopefully they can redeem this game in the upcoming prequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: It really is a shame how severely underrated this game is, and I honestly can't understand why it's rated to negatively. The music, art style and characters are all great and well made. I understand the story gets very weird out of left field and ends so abruptly, but I found my self engaged with Howard's journey the entire time. Maybe people went in expecting something completely different than what was here and that's why. By no means a masterpiece of a game, It still deserving of a positive rating in my books. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: I'm reviewing this as a kickstarter backer. Spoilers ahead. This game is beautiful to look at and oozes a very unique, fascinating atmosphere that really brings the world of the City to life. It reminds me a lot of Blacksad mixed with some futuristic elements. The story premise is gripping, interesting and the introductory part of the game is extremely well done.The gameplay is pretty good for a kind of 'adventure-lite' game, though the absence of any challenging puzzles makes it a little boring at times. The stakes are very low in each section, you will generally not experience any challenge and the game will be relatively straightforward, unless you spend the time to discover all the hidden moments.My main gripes are with the story after the initial couple of acts. The premise of accidentally uncovering a cannibalism ring and it quickly spiraling into a far-reaching conspiracy is engrossing, but it is not followed through on AT ALL and ends at roughly where the mid-point of the story is, with the main character lost in the wasteland. It falls apart completely after the character is exposed to an alien artifact that can over-write his DNA and it is so abrupt that you'll probably get whiplash. The mood and tone change so completely that it's almost a different game past that point.There are few satisfying explanations as to why there is cannibalism, why the characters are involved in this plot, or why they act the way they act - it seems as if decadence is a reason in and of itself. When it comes towards the end, you take control of the secondary antagonist Clarissa who apparently wants to create a revolution, but her reasoning for it is borderline nonsensical as nothing that she talks about was clearly illustrated in the game. Indeed, in my opinion, there's a lot of tell and not enough show. There is also a lot of bloat - unnecessary characters, unnecessary locations and the entire section towards the end where the main character lives at a commune of the poor feels pointless. The addition of these elements and omitting additional sections where we could explore more about the plot and the characters makes the game's pacing feel either breakneck or slow and it is extremely difficult to reconcile.The game is *severely* hampered by its dialog, which feels written in a Russian speaking pattern that doesn't quite sound natural in English and contains a lot of swearing. It makes the conversations difficult to follow and understand unless you're vaguely familiar with the mannerisms of this type of dialog, and even then it is very odd in English - a few more passes to put it in more 'flowing' English would have benefited the game a great deal.Finally, once the 'artifact' comes into play, there is a lot of philosophizing about inevitability, death and what it means to be a person - but this feels, again, tacked on and difficult to reconcile with the character because the game is too short to meaningfully explore him or his relationships to the other characters.It's a shame, because this game has moments in it that are jaw-dropping or downright inspired - such as the parade scene after the discovery of the artifact, or the story of girls in love trying to escape the City for the world beyond, or meeting the mother of one of the missing girls. Overall, if you're interested in spectacle over substance, this is a good candidate - the art is amazing, and there are truly fantastic scenes. If you're interested in a solid story, I would recommend looking for other adventure games or waiting until there's a follow-up.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so disappointed with this game... First of all, it's a really short game for the price. I was so into the story, it was well written, and I really enjoyed the ambiance.But the end ... Omg. I was so disappointed. It just leaves you with the feeling of rushed ending, no conclusion, nothing. It doesn't make any sence. It really is a disappointment considering what they could have done with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME, I´m being dead serious here, and I higly dislike giving bad reviews to any game, specially to PnC adventures because as long as the puzzles are not super tedious or the story extremelly poorly written, I tend to enjoy all of them.Backbone though... You can already see the mixxed reviews mentioning the ending, but that´s hardly the problem here. The issues with the narrative come way before the ending because mid game suddenly the entire plot and focus is shifted drastically. The game makes a 180º degrees turn from a detective story to a "space horror" non conclusive short tale, and all your detective work is set aside by a single conversation with an NPC with no connection to the story simply telling you "nah, it was all good, don´t worry about it". So yeah, the ending sucks, but only because the story you started with it´s dropped and the second story you are presented comes out of nowhere, takes control over the narrative, and presents you with a straight line to a definitive ending that leaves more questions than answers in the air... no more puzzles, no more clues, just 2 more acts of dragging your character until the game decides it´s enough.So for your own shake, STAY AWAY FROM THIS GAME, I know you are looking at the trailer and thinking "come on how bad cold it be?, I have played games with bad endings before", but you never played two different games that don´t gel together and you only get to experience the first part of one and the second part of another (and the second one it´s just bad). Sure, art direction and ambiance look astonishing, and that´s the only thing providing this game with the few positive reviews it has, but it won´t be enough to wash away the bad taste of a good first 2 acts being made pointless.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I'm close to finishing the game, and I thought I'd better throw my hat in the ring because I've seen many mixed/bad reviews for this game. First of all, you'll enjoy the ♥♥♥♥ out of it, as I did. It's funny, visually appealing and the music is fantastic. That being said, yes, the ending is a bit underwhelming and sudden. But, as an avid player of adventure games, this is often the case. (Hello, Fran Bow, Beneath a Steel Sky, Cathy Rain & more). I think this game was fantastic, if a bit simplistic. (Not a whole lot to figure out puzzle-wise.)It scratched the itch for something akin to Disco Elysium (not the same level of art, obviously). It's a fun and thought-provoking little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: On the one hand, it's a beautifully made game visually with a really compelling story. I was sucked into the pretty quickly. But the downside is that the game feels very short, like it's only half of the game. I am very stoked to see what other games the developers release, but I would perhaps urge them to try expanding future games. But that said, one of the oldest rules in show business is "always leave them wanting more".
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to make a negative review as the game is stunning in some aspects (atmosphere, sound design and of course visuals).But narration is problematic. Choices have no concequence. Dialogs feels incoherent. Story starts to get exciting but the game suddently ends.Backbone left me with a bitter feeling of a game that could have been incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Would-be masterpiece (Amazing Artstyle, Amazing Soundtrack, A great (Minor Spoiler) Noir World) if not held back by the two major flaws of: linear storytelling (your choices will not matter and bad/good choices are just delaying the inevitable actions taken), and the story spinning around trying to find a way to connect the dots. The game will not explain everything, that is not what the game is meant to do and not what I wanted it to do too. You're part of the system and it will remind you of it.. That is not the main issue either. It just abruptly... ends,... almost as if they had to cut it short. It leaves a story that has a giant chunk missing.But, the story is far from bad. They're trying something great in concept, and I hope a (possible) sequel could finally tie this story up. There were some unexplained tidbits explained in Prequels which I did like but it feels like theres so much more unexplained and unfinished plotpoints waiting to be tied up. I wish EGGNUT the best in developing. They have made fantastic artistic games so far and there is only up.(Also, spoilers but )
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: ☆☆☆This is a complicated game that leaves you wanting in both good and bad ways.  The world building was fantastic. I was invested throughout and well after the credits rolled, theorizing about the structure of the setting and how a bigger story fit within it.  However, there is a stunning lack of delivery on ANY resolution to the numerous story lines presented.In terms of visuals and mood, this game has some of the most stunning graphics I have come across, with an attention to detail that is really breathtaking.  For game play, the first Act has quite a few semi-challenging puzzles that were really enjoyable, while the rest of the game has very little in terms of engagement past text options.In the end though, I truly recommend Backbone.  This game has really stuck with me and in some ways it's shortcomings add to an experience that is, in my opinion at least, well worth the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves playing games, especially Visual Novels, I do adore this game. The graphics, the music, and a lil bit point-n-click here and there. The story itself is quite fine, I find it intriguing tbh. I can see how most of people are going to "kinda hate" this game. The cliff hanging story, the gameplay, and all those stuffs. You can say i'm a bit biased to the characters as well. Howard, Renee, even Bo have their own things to make the story quite rich. For the main story, since it's a kinda detective/mystery driven theme, I'll say the unfinished story (as what most of people say) fits well with the concept. As for myself, I'd prefer the story to be ended that way, even the feeling to know what's coming up next is through the roof for sure. I have to admit that I haven't finished this game yet, but because I'm used to play some VNs with heartbreaking endings, I'm pretty sure I'll be fine with whatever the story try to deliver.The gameplay, as I refer this game to be a Visual Novel (even the developers don't say so), is quite alright. I'm not used to a point-n-click games, but some VNs do have this feature as their main sell point and I'm fine with it. Overall, I'll give it 7/10. Great visuals, great musics, the story is quite fine since I heard there are very few endings, and the gameplay didn't do much since it's a story-driven game. I did buy this game by the Bundle Artifact Edition and tbh I thought I'll regret my decision for buying this for like 10 bucks. So i set my expectation low and hey, this game is kinda refreshing and charming. Maybe I'll give an update to this review later on, if I find something else.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: The game shines in the prologue, using puzzle mechanics and offering different paths and choices to do things.Sadly, that's the only time you see diverging paths or puzzles in the game. It becomes very linear.I'd have been OK with that, given the gorgeous graphics, but then the game pulls a genre-changing twist, offers not really much in the way of explanation as to why, and turns into some kind of existential-crisis simulator in which the player has pretty much no influence on the story.The game's ending also feels.. incomplete. I am not sure if they intended a cliffhanger, or if they just thought this is a good place to end the game. I get it.. not every story has to provide all the answers, but I couldn't help but find the ending very unsatisfying and inconclusive.Still, you can play it for the chance to commandeer a witty raccoon around the well done pixel graphics, but don't expect much from the story or hope for clever puzzle mechanics.I'm actually sad writing this.. I really wanted this game to be awesome, but as it stands now, whoever runs their Twitter account is better at engaging with players than the game is, by a long mile.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: This is a though one. I'm not sure if the game really deserves a thumbs-down, because it has a couple of merits. Above all it is visually stunning and as good as pixel graphics get. Honestly it's a lot of fun to simply walk through the town and look at all the cool backgrounds and details. It definitely has a lot of atmosphere.Unfortunately this is where the positive aspects end for me. My main complaint is that the game is boring. It is really boring for a crime story. It feels mostly uninspired; just the same tropes that you see in every Noir genre game. I never cared for the fate of the protagonist and most of the characters are very bland and 2-dimensional. Without giving anything away I must also add that it has an extremely unsatisfying ending.There also really is no gameplay to speak of. You just walk through the background pieces, click every dialogue option and advance with the story. Nothing you do matters, it could just as well be a virtual novel. No puzzles, no anything.Overall I would say it's one of those games I would recommend during a sale for 5 bucks, but apart from the visuals it's really nothing special sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Man oh man, I wish I could recommend this game. I love detective stories, especially ones with a great noir atmosphere. This game has basically everything to make it a fantastic, memorable detective game. The art is stunning, and the story and characters are great as well... Until you get near the end. I had a really fun time playing until like the last act or two. The mystery that we were solving almost feels like it was put on the back burner, and we are playing a different game entirely. I'm fine with games having twists, but the way this game ended was so jarring and inorganic in my opinion. And not only that, this game (which took me around 4 hours) basically has no replay value either. The lead up was great, but the follow through... not so much unfortunately. Great potential, just not what I thought I was signing up for. It could be your cup of tea still, but not mine.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a few chapters in and I find Backbone very enjoyable. It's much like an interactive novel. There isn't as much detective work (only a couple puzzles so far) as I had hoped, but the story, art, and music are enjoyable. Most of the game is talking to people (hence the interactive novel comment). You choose the MC's responses and I found it fun to roleplay the character. I'd recommend it to people who would be interested in reading a story more than heavy gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone is a game made with good intentions first and foremost, The plot and story is intended to be great, and for the first 3 or so acts, up until a certain spoiler element happens, the plot is superb. Among some of the best noir plots I've read, its about a complex power struggle between the ultra-rich and ultra-powerfull, an underground market for cannibals, a missing group of girls from the west end, and their relations with each other in the world and within the story. However this game isn't great all the time: The ending, and the 4th and 5th act all seem both rushed and un-thoughtout, and decrease the enjoyability of the narrative and of the game. without going in to spoilers all I can say is that there is a MAJOR tonal shift after act three and a MAJOR change of pacing, suddenly instead of the contemplative and brooding atmosphere of a noir the air changes to that of a sci-fi thriller with no happy or cathartic ending. If you are thinking that this is possibly a good thing you'd be wrong, in this circumstance the ending is abrupt and sudden, the character you have been playing as up and vanishes and you are railroaded through cutscenes that do nothing more than tie up loose ends left in the story and set up for a possible sequel. To be entirely honest, if the story had just stopped at act 3s end with a "To be Continued in Backbone 2" I would have been more happy with the result. You could honestly cut the game off right after the parade scene (because that scene was beautiful) as long as you can fix the plot holes with how that scene ends up happening and still reach the same outcome. The long and the sort of it is that Backbone is a good game yes, but not for its entire runtime and the ending leaves a sower taste in your mouth as if you bit into a lemon, The missed execution of the finale makes the entire story feel worse and worth less as a whole than the sum of its excellent parts.
_childDocuments_.name: Tails Noir

_childDocuments_.review: Backbone is a post-noir roleplaying detective adventure. Become raccoon private eye Howard Lotor as you interrogate a diverse cast of characters, collect evidence, and explore dystopian Vancouver, BC inhabited by animals.

name: The Eternal Cylinder
detailed_description: You were born on a dangerous planet. Surreal and fantastical environments, teeming with exotic creatures that defy description. This world is both terrifying and awe-inspiring, as full of wonder and mystery as it is dangerous. But whatever dangers can be found pale in comparison to this world’s biggest threat: The Cylinder. This gargantuan, ancient rolling structure crushes everything in its path. But where did it come from? And how can it be stopped? In this place, you are but a tiny creature called a Trebhum. While you may not be the fastest or the strongest, you have the most powerful ability of all: adaptation. Trebhum can mutate and evolve new physical attributes and abilities that can help them defend themselves against predators and navigate through this perilous world; what you lack in size, you’ll need to make up for in improvisation and resourcefulness. So, prepare yourself, little Trebhum. Gather your family for the dangerous journey ahead and save your world from The Eternal Cylinder. An unforgettable alien world to explore… A vast, open world that contains four unique biomes, each filled with extraordinary flora and strange fauna. What wonders, or horrors, lie ahead will surely be unforgettable. …with real-time world destruction. Every time The Cylinder roars to life, more of your beautiful planet is crushed under the weight of the ancient destroyer. Trees fall creating obstacles to escape while hills and mountains are flattened leaving nowhere to hide. Your only chance of survival is to run! Build Your Own Alien Family Each Trebhum can choose from 50+ mutations that give them the ability to grow spikes, shoot tornadoes, fly, and more! This allows Trebhum various methods to overcome any obstacle they face! Additionally, each mutation gives Trebhum unique appearances, meaning Trebhum herds become a diverse cast of lovable creatures customized for ultimate survivability. Solve Ancient Mysteries In hidden sanctuaries, built by generations past and protected by complex puzzles, is the ancient knowledge passed down from generation to generation of Trebhum. Seek these sanctuaries out for they house the only hope your world has left. Watch out for The Cylinder’s servants Servants are abominations created by The Cylinder; infesting, destroying, and consuming every natural thing on the planet, leaving nothing behind. Stay as far away from these monsters as you can! *ANNIVERSARY UPDATE - NEW CONTENT* New Creatures to Discover! 2 new creatures now roam the world - Approach at your own risk! - The Buddugh Gropp is a highly aggressive herbivore found in tundra biomes. - The Gharukuk is a large tripodal omnivore found in the desert. A new mutation! Trebhum have developed a new, fiery mutation allowing them to shoot jets of flame from their trunks. The ability makes sure that any would-be predator knows that Trebhum may be too spicy for food (especially for those with fur!) New graphics options! The Eternal Cylinder now supports 4K AND ray tracing make your journey to salvation the most vivid and immersive ever! Enjoy this gorgeous world the way it was meant to be seen, even more vividly!

_childDocuments_.review: I played The Eternal Cylinder when it was released on the Epic Games Store in 2021, going through the entire campaign in . And now that I've played through the Steam version with the Anniversary Patch, I can conclusively state that my opinion remains the same:The Eternal Cylinder is , and one of my personal gaming highlights of 2021 (and now 2022 as well).By ‘mature’ I mean that The Eternal Cylinder far exceeds what you may be expecting from a small studio like ACE Team. We all know that they excel at crafting  that have no equal. But I think we can also agree that these unique worlds have sometimes been paired with gameplay of the ‘serviceable but nothing special’ variety, or plots that are interesting but may have occasional storytelling hiccups. Or just a general feeling of ‘not-quite-as-polished-as-it-could-have-been'.You’ll find none of these flaws here, as the world of The Eternal Cylinder is , the storytelling is  and the gameplay is .The Eternal Cylinder plays like a  in which you gather additional characters (the ‘Trebhum’) to add to your party (or ‘family’), as well as edible items that provide the Trebhum with various mutations. In that way, the game actually , as you shape your Trebhum family to deal with specific situations. Like having a long-legged Trebhum that can jump high and glide through the air to reach faraway places, or one that’s particularly good at shooting water from its trunk to knock fruit from trees. There are also a few unique interactions with objects and creatures in the environment that you’ll have to figure out yourself.That being said, I feel like . That’s not a problem, since you could always just apply another mutation or switch to another Trebhum to actively control, keeping the ones with highly situational mutations for when you need them (that’s why you have multiple Trebhum, after all). But I think the developers could probably have come up with a few more uses for things like the cuboid body mutation, which (AFAIK) only serves to turn your Trebhum into a ‘key’ for opening specific cube-shaped locks.The gameplay is wrapped up in a  as you unearth the knowledge of an advanced ancient civilization, trying to figure out where this giant cylinder that’s crushing the planet’s surface has come from – and what the intentions of its masters may be. At the same time, , facing the imminent annihilation of an entire world. Add to that the  and you’ve got yourself a game that’s not just fun to play, but also immerses you deeply in a  and the mysteries buried there.One piece of advice for first-timers: Don’t get too attached to specific mutations you’ve found. And if you’ve found a mutation you feel like you can’t do without, make sure you always carry around a few spares of the corresponding mutagenic substance, just in case.

_childDocuments_.review: i bought this thinking it was going to be a fun game about little alien dudes having a good time running around a mildly sus planet solving puzzles & being cute together - instead i got the most intense 2 hours ive had in weeks fighting for my life with danger at every turn. when i awoken the first servant, he killed one of my trebhum & my party of trebhum made an expression so painfully sad ill never recover from the depression

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, Salvador Dali painting: the game.Huh Q*bert sure is looking different.Acid trippers were like:"Dude, wanna like... make a game?"Man, Snuffleupagus’s origin story sure looks crazy. This is like something out of my nightmares. It reminds me of a reoccurring nightmare I had as a kid. It's one of the trippiest games I've ever played. Also Hands-down one of the most interesting games I've ever played! It was like the Codex Seraphinianus was a game; the feeling of opening an encyclopedia before being able to read and marveling at all the truly alien wonders just out of reach (and later in reach). Not perfect, but worth my time a hundred percent. Such creativity and some incredibly memorable moments.It seems like such a criminally underrated game, but it's honestly unlike any game I've played before. It’s so original and the art style is really striking and unique. Such a refreshing experience with a lot of polish and charm and an almost constant sense of dread. You take over the role of a 'Trebhum' on an unknown planet. Even though the Trebhums are the lower end of the food chain, they have special instant mutation abilities when they eat items. E.g. eating the fruit of a special tree makes you float in the air or eating eggs of an grashopper-like creature makes you jump higher. Now you may be easy prey to any other bizarre creature on this world but thanks to this amazing tree of abilities that your people have you’re able to take materials from the environment and adapt yourself to the different challenges, environments, and puzzles all while uncovering your peoples past of prosperity and peace and being constantly perused by a massive rolling cylinder that wants nothing more than to... I almost spoiled part of the story. Let that just be a testament to how good the story is, there's just so much of it that it’s hard to talk about this game without saying spoilers. So you play as these creatures who can mutate to solve puzzles, whilst being chased by an unending steam cylinder. Seeing the size of the cylinder at first gave me the same anxiety that the camera flipped levels of Crash Bandicoot did as a kid. Your goal is to survive, find a way to stop the destructive rampage of the cylinder and discover the truth about your people’s history. It's nightmarish, but there are moments of solace. I genuinely cried after seeing the images of your characters peoples past, its just so hard not to shed a tear after seeing all the prosperity that these creatures went through.Some things were a bit tedious at the beginning but I loved the game by the end. The controls, specifically the camera and jumping, are slightly into the territory of being annoying. The art, audio, and creativity put into the game are all top notch though, and make the few negatives worth dealing with. I was devastated to find that there was no new game plus where you can play again with all of your mutations saved. I would pay money for that. I give this game a 10/10 it’s just too amazing not to play and would recommend to anyone who’s into speculative evolution, bizarre lifeforms or acid trips.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most unique games you can play. The art-style alone is gorgeous, even more so combined with the soundtrack and graphics. The story was extremely intriguing and kept me motivated to see the ending. I would recommend this game for these reasons alone.However, I have trouble recommending this game from a game-play perspective. I didn't play on easy mode (I'm stubborn) and I regret it. Consider the following:- Unstoppable enemies will often attack you if you try to explore. They don't de-aggro easily. This leads into:- Your squad-members dying easily from things out of your control. It's taxing to revive your members and you don't always have the option to bring them back. Because of this I guarantee you will re-load a previous save. This leads to:- The game taking a lot longer than it should. I spent a long time with inventory management (your characters only have 3 inventory slots and there's a lot of items), checking the map, saving the game, and re-loading.- The hunger and water mechanics are a chore. You need to always be at full water and hunger or else you have low stamina.- You're going to get some (or all) of you powers taken away from you and it's frustrating.Despite this, I played The Eternal Cylinder to discover a completely unique world and my expectations were met and exceeded. I hope the developers continue to create such creative stories!
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: I love me an intriguing, high quality, weird ass game that takes itself seriously. You control a tribe of charming little aliens called Trebhum, which are blessed with the ability to mutate based upon what they consume. As you set out on your quest to survive and put a stop to The Eternal Cylinder, you'll have to outrun Tonglegrops, hunt Glickbol, avoid Zooshgarg, sing to Trewaalha, and evade the servants of The Cylinder. Most of that probably made no sense. That's the best part.The game gives you PLENTY of Trebhum to work with, as well as the ability to revive any that die. So, more likely than be short on teammates, you'll find yourself unable to recruit/save more. That's something I think the game should add. Recruit and auto-send to "The Cloud" where you can keep Trebhum in reserve. Also, this game would be fire with multiplayer.The only issues I ran into were a few crashes, but the game does have autosaves, checkpoints, and allows manual saves as well; so no progress was ever really lost.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to recommend this game, but I just can't. The first chapter is great, it has nice pacing, great starting mystery and atmosphere. Chapters 2-4 are tedious. They basically have the same gameplay as chapter 1, with no changes, barely any puzzles or anything, just randomly generated biomes with some monsters. Randomized progression that you can actually lose also does not feel good, and discourages exploring. The plot of the last 2 chapters is also not great, it majorly fails to deliver on such a nice mystery.This game is 3-4 hours of content and story stretched over 12 hours of extremely tedious gameplay with janky (but fun at times) controls and major "Fatal error!" crashes. The game should have been 3-5 hours long, not 12.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: The Eternal Cylinder is at its best when it is not a survival game, and it is most of the time. After a bunch of hours gathering food and water gets tedious and the escapes from the cylinder lose their charm.Nonetheless, there is so much good in this game. The sweet score, the great philosophical story, and the art direction that is just nuts in the best way possible. The gameplay is pretty unique and fun, too......but like I said, without the survival part.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for this game ever since the devs posted a video clip of the prototype years and years ago.  I remember posting suggestions and theories on ACE Team's official forum alongside a whole bunch of other excited fans about this game (a common question we had was "what's behind the cylinder?" which ended up being a driving question in Act One, so you have us to thank for that teehee).  I broke my anti-EGS vow for this game.  I played through it beginning to end twice over there.  I bought it on Steam as soon as I could.  The Eternal Cylinder is the best game to come out of 2021, ACE Team's best work since the original Zeno Clash, and one of the greatest exploration games ever made.The utterly alien world is so beautiful.  The Trebhum are charming protagonists with a neat adaptation mechanic that helps them survive wherever they may end up.  Creature design for both the native species and the cyborg antagonists are surreal and amazing.  The cylinder itself is a dominating and threatening force from the very first moment of the game; its constant presence a reminder that you are not safe.  The music helps enhance the beauty and danger of the setting.  The story is full of dread and full of hope, with some cosmic horror tidbits to put Sovereign's speech is ME1 to shame.Altogether, it creates a unique and memorable experience.  Fans of alien worlds, exploration, and surrealism need to jump in on this one.  Thank you for funding this game, Tim Sweeny.  That is a sentence I will never utter again.Now if you excuse me, I need to play it through yet again.

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Cylinder is a great game. It is unlike anything that you’ve played before. Even though I found the start of the game a little frustrating, the artstyle, storytelling, and it just being a unique game, helped in keeping me playing.The GoodThe artstyle is very good. Reminds me a little of spore, but also of this old book from I think the 70’s, that was made to be just pure nonsense but had a lot of art of alien plants and creatures. Also, reminds me of that 70’s animated film with blue people. Maybe even a little bit of Zoombinis for me, especially with the sounds of the creatures.The story is alright. I don’t really understand what is happened. There was a lot of words and the guy didn’t explain anything. Also, my mind is kind of busy thinking about stuff. I have some kind of idea about it but I don’t understand why the cylinder was created or why the things look the way they do.The music is really good. I loved it.The animations are really good.The game runs really good.The game instantly loads which I find kind of crazy cause the world of the game feels large an there’s a lot going on and that cylinder is huge and endless.There are many types of ways of changing your creatures appearance and their effects.There’s a couple of options to change some settings to easy mode.The world of the game is beautiful.The sound effects are great! Creatures sound cute.The cylinder is scary when you are trying to escape it and you can hear stuff exploding behind you, even though you aren’t close to it.Everything gets crushed, killed, or destroyed by the cylinder. You can save pretty much whenever you want.Controls are ok when you don’t have the balloon mutation. Otherwise, it’s good controls. Except for the platforming parts. Sometimes it wants to perfect pixel jump and that stinks.I like rolling and going fast.The BadThe beginning part when you have to go around the long neck creature was frustrating. Once you get around, you have to jump into poison. The ai isn’t that great so they are taking their time to get to you while you die. Only way to try and do it a little faster is to switch to them but when you do, all of them will now start to go to your new guy.The switching characters is the worst design decision. It could have been a simple switch your character by cycling them but it isn’t. Like it works that way when you tap it but it doesn’t cycle through all of them, only the ones close to you! Imagine constantly switching between 2 creatures when there’s a couple around you and you want a specific one so you have to do it the other way but even that way sucks.When switching your characters, there is another way to do it and that is holding down on it. And you still can’t switch to everyone, only the ones close to you. Some creatures may actually be missing sometimes and you can’t switch to them to find out where they are.I was pretty frustrated when I first experienced the electrical storm. You can’t go far away from the storm because the game won’t allow you; even though the area that you were trying to go through looked fine, but with just a couple of lightning strikes that totally didn’t hurt you. The game then force kills you if you go too far. You have to stay close to the cylinder.The menu where you can see all the plants sucks. It takes forever to scroll down that long singled line list. Using a mouse helps but it really needs to be organized by category. The plants in the menu don’t tell you what they turn you into.No way to change the horizontal or vertical speed of the camera. It only works for the mouse.The game crashed a couple times for me stating a “Fatal Crash Error” message.I don’t think the game tells you that the blue light above the pillar guides you to locations that you have to go to. I felt like I was exploring a lot of the world when I didn’t need to.A lot of fetch-like quests. Pacing of the story could have totally been shorter.I spent a lot of time looking for plants and stuff for upgrades that could never be found. Personally felt like I wasted my time doing that, when I should have just been going for the blue locations and progressing the story. Cause getting a lot of mutations doesn’t actually matter.When I tried to store a creature in the cloud, and then bringing them back, they lost all their items.The game tries to force kill your creatures in many ways. So, imagine having items that were super hard and took a lot of time to find, and then they just get killed. It’s not fun. And when you lose powers that were hard to find like the 3rd eye, it makes it even worse.Game kind of bugs out. In a white block section of the game, when I was brought in, my creature was stuck in the sky. I had to jump. I went through the entire level of that white place and nothing happened or progressed. I looked up on youtube, and the game basically didn’t register that my character was there, because I didn’t drop within a certain time limit because I was stuck. Had to load the autosave.The above kind of thing happened again but in another section of the game.ConclusionI originally bought it because of the artstyle alone, but I enjoyed my time playing the game and it was fantastic. A good one of a kind game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a tough game to recommend.+ On one hand, it's rather unique (especially if you haven't played Spore, Creatures and Evolva from '00s). It tells a tale unusual in the time where everything is generic fantasy, and most happy tales are about spending days on a farm. If you're tired of standardized game genres, settings and plots - this one is a must!+ It is visually interesting, and interesting to explore. Figuring out a whole new world, with its own rules and dangers - a novel experience.+ Easy settings allow to play it without much challenge (though some boss fights and "runs" were hard).+ Lot of rolling (if you didn't get enough in Rock of Ages series by same devs).+ Trebnums! Yoohoo!On the other hand, I felt like for bigger half of the game, I was struggling against game mechanics to have fun.- Lots of rolling. Not a fan of this, tbh.- Fighting against UI/UX all the way- Core mechanics like jumping and aiming felt very clunky on kb+m- Semi-automatic save system, only available during "calm" periods outside- Inventory management makes any interactions there an extreme chore - check- A mandatory temple with timed platforming puzzles - check- Enemies taking away your powers (and a long, grindy hunt to "keep" them permanently) - check- Sequences where you're forced to almost WALK for a while (or get killed by purple lighting) - check- I also got a rare bug that somehow sent me back in progress, so I completed first chapter almost twice - hence 24h mark.All in all, I give this game thumbs up and recommend it for being something unique and bold.This, it accomplished, and I am thankful to the dev team (as long-time fan of Zeno Clash series, too).But I sighed in relief once the end titles rolled, and rather than playing a minute more, would rather remember this one fondly :)So go on with very moderated expectations and healthy curiosity!
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start... The Eternal Cylinder is a logical-exploration-adventure game where you control rather humble and funny looking creatures called "Trebhum". You collect mutations and upgrades for them as they journey through hostile environments while being chased by the titular "The Eternal Cyliner". The gameplay has more intricacies than what I've explained but treat it as a very, very general abstract. I won't get much into details regarding graphics. They're stylized, cute and pleasing.Now, mechanics of the game is just a one side of it. The other, I believe, much more important is the amount of symbolism and philosophical backbone presented in the game. The idea of a cylinder causing a mass extiction event is an unprecedented idea that I've never seen before. Nevertheless, its symbolism rooted in the idea of reducing everything to the primordial chaos and negating all forms and disparities is very much inspiring. On the one hand we have a representation of pure, utter nihilism in the form of The Eternal Cylinder and its servants, on the other, there are trebhum – small and fragile but diverse and adaptable nonetheless. It is the battle between nihilsm and vitalism that compels a player to push forward, not only to save the Trebhum but also unravel the mysteries of The Eternal Cylinder.That being said, the game suffers from a set of drawbacks that I'm afraid I can't overlook.- Trebhums are sometimes clunky, and while it is merely an issue that stems from the physics engine, your creatures being stuck on some small, irrelevant objects brings about only frustration, especially during tense situations.- Trebhum are getting lost at times. It's annoying and breaks the gameplay because they die idiotically.- Lack of replayability. Sure, you can collect all the other mutations that you haven't collected before, try to secure them all within the mutation tree, level up the Trebhums to ease the journey. But that is merely a completionist approach and not the actual endgame content that would prompt me to play the game after finishing the main story. Not unless I feel merry about reliving the experience again.- Lackluster of puzzles compared to the amount of mutations. The mutation tree is big. You can mutate Trebhums' body, legs and trunks and there are so many different forms, upgrades and possibilities that it is a pity that I didn't feel the necessity to invest more into fine-tuning my Trebhum team to make things as fitting as possible. One could say the game is then too easy.- The difficulty is, at times, frustrating. Not because of the puzzles, these aren't very difficult. It's more related to various interruptions that you face during the gameplay. Mobs running around you, stalling your progress by a few minutes and such. These are all small things but they are frustrating.- Some mutations are practically useless. In theory, there are offensive mutations, which seems like a cool option given that you're bound to play with these fragile, little creatures. But then it turns out that instead of scaring the hostile creatures, it is better to simply run away from them.By and large, the game delivers a very inspiring, profound and poignant at times experience. The soundtrack hits nicely having mixes of horroresque, brave and peaceful tones that follow the circumstances fittingly. In short, if you like artistic adventure games with lots of symbolism and philosophical backbone, then give The Eternal Cylinder a chance. A slightly flawed gem is still a gem and it'd be a shame not to give it a look.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: The Eternal Cylinder is a unique and charming game that has you play as the Trebhum, a weird and small little creature that has the power to mutate and evolve itself to gain new attributes and abilities.The planet you are born on is dangerous, beautiful, and surreal.You don't get the time to appreciate your new existence in the world for long, however, for The Eternal Cylinder is not far behind you, and it's out to crush your whole planet and everything in its way..The Eternal Cylinder is relentless and indestructible. It will consume everything in its path. It can be delayed, but it cannot be stopped.Newly hatched, you will have to set out on a journey to save your planet, building a family of Trebhum along the way.The story has themes of hope and family, with plenty of mystery and emotion. It has a compelling story with a lot of heart put into it.I love the entries in the Compendium. The descriptions of creatures and various foods and mutations help to make the world feel more alive and fleshed out. The creature and enemy designs in the game feel super original, and there's a great variety.The Trebhum are SO CUTE AND ADORABLE, and they have idle animations with each other.. ah, my heart..!Also.. the Glickbol?? I want to hug them???? Please?? Let me pet them???The movement is fun, and I liked exploring the world. A lot of rolling around, honking at enemies and spraying them with water!Vacuuming up items in the environment is oddly satisfying, as are the sounds that go along with it. The sound design in general is honestly really good, and the soundtrack was a pleasant surprise.You will have to manage food and water to keep your stamina up, but it's a forgiving and not very difficult system to manage. The game auto-saves but you can also manually save at most points. There are options in the settings to make the game easier if you feel in need of it.There are over 50 mutations to be found, though there are a few of them that barely have a use. You'll be giving your family of Trebhum different roles to help you survive, and you'll be introduced to and find new mutations at a nice pace that isn't overwhelming.Depending on your spook-factor, there can be a few scary elements in the game. Some of the hostile creatures can be a bit frightening when they come at you, and the atmosphere at certain points can feel a bit disturbing. The Cylinder approaching at a rapid pace right behind you might also get your heart beating fast.The non-leading Trebhum tend to jump and bounce around all over the place, sometimes right into danger, which can be quite frustrating. I wish there was a way to direct them without having to switch to them, or a way to tell them to stay put for a bit. Thankfully, they will always teleport offscreen to your leader.I had a few performance issues, and I also had the game crash on me two times, but it ran fine for me the majority of the time.A thing I ran into a few times was that the Trebhum I was controlling would get stuck in the ceiling upon entering a structure. Switching to another Trebhum would make the stuck Trebhum unstuck itself though, and so it was more of a small annoyance.Unique, charming, and strange. A wonderful experience, worth every penny.If you're on the fence about the game, I recommend checking out some videos to see if it looks like something you'd enjoy.We need more of this type of game! Highly recommended. ♥
