_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed playing this game, and considering the game-play loop, I'd say the length (16.4 hours in my case) is just perfect. It's a pretty unique and original game, set in a unique and original world. The creatures have funny names and you play as a funny little things called Trebhums. I was entertained throughout the game. You evolve your Trebhum as it fits your needs to complete puzzles, fend off things that are trying to kill you, and survive the elements; you do this all while trying to outrun The Eternal Cylinder, which crushes everything in front of it and leaves a desolate land in its wake.Its not an especially difficult game though it can get spicy sometimes if you don't fuel up before a long leg between towers, it has light survival aspects with different biomes where you can freeze or burn to death, etc. You can starve, etc. but its not too hardcore about it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game, even at full price. You likely have never played anything like it and never will again.The basic premise is there is a massive cylinder (like a rolling pin) rolling across the world and destroying everything so you have to keep ahead of it. A lot of the game is running frantically. It's really impressive to watch it crush things though.The other aspect of the game is that you are a little alien creature that can mutate by eating things. You can gather other aliens and there are puzzle dungeons to unlock new abilities and learn more about why there is a cylinder rolling across the world and how to stop it.There are also lots of huge and dangerous monsters roaming the world trying to kill you. You die very easily.After a number of hours, the gameplay starts to feel a little repetitive and there are bugs that will get you stuck or make your camera float off. Still completely worth it for the trippy experience and unique gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game has been an absolute blast, the environments feel alien due to their surreal nature, and the wildlife that inhabits the world have to be some of the most unique creatures I've seen in a game in a long time. The music, the graphics, the story are all great. My only complaint is that platforming is a bit wonky because the critters you play as are a bit bouncy, and i feel like there could be some platforming improvements, but other than that the game is incredibly interesting. I dont want to spoil too much, but the game features a combination of both wonder and relaxing  moments, to terrifying and intense as you watch in horror as the cylinder crushes everything and lights up the sky with fire and lightning. I have not finished the game, but the inventory and item collection and survival systems are unique, there are only a few major biomes, but each ecosystem is incredibly diverse with life and every environment has its own cast of creatures with interesting behaviors. Overall ive enjoyed this game so far, and my only complaints are im regards to platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a linear crafting survival game with AI-controlled companions. I wish I knew this before playing this game.The main gameplay loop is that you move from one area to another and each area is its own small open location where you need to search for water and food and avoid numerous predators. In regards to crafting, you don't really craft any equipment, but instead search for ingredients to get permanent mutations So, basically, more streamlined crafting where you "craft" your own body.Survival elements are good though. Further and further into the game you encounter more and more dangerous predators to the point of almost breaking (it's stressful being at the bottom of food chain) and then you become powerful enough to tear everyone apart with bombs and become the hunter. This survival part is really well done here.Now, here is the reason why I am giving Eternal Cylinder a negative review : AI-controlled companions. They are obnoxious. They get in my way, they die way too easily, they are simply morons. And the worst part is that I need to keep a lot of them to be able to carry all my stuff since inventory space is very limited. Example of where companions die easily : when they fall into cold water or lava, they don't understand that they are slowly dying (or quickly in case of lava) and don't even try to jump out. It was very frustrating considering that I needed them to carry my items.Game does allow you to stash away your companions, but only in specific rare locations and not at any moment. If I could stash them at any moment or if there was a limitless shared inventory, a lot of frustration could have been avoided. And that is the reason why I am giving this game a negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, i beat it in under 7 hours its pretty fast paced and fun puzzles cool mutations and overall amazing graphics might be my favorite game. Does it need work? Yes it does need work, like a sandbox mode or a endless mode. I love that each mutation blends with the other ones like fat body and spikes all that stuff is amazing. I love this game, I played it during the demo in 2021, and revisiting it a lot has changed and its by far better that the demo (i did still love the demo).  And Problems with the game, about none. There are a few like no save games and no sandbox mode after you beat the game. But not including that stuff its amazing. Thanks The Eternal Cylinder. -ArgoFlex
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an unforgettable experience. I never thought I'd find myself so pulled in by a game where you're running from a giant cylinder while half man, half machine beasts hunt you down, but here we are.I bought this game last year, played through it somewhat clumsily, and ended up getting all but about five achievements. I struggled with the desert segment, but overall, I still had a lot of fun. I was satisfied with where I left it. Then, this week, I decided to pick it back up and get the last achievements. A let me tell you, it was even better the second time.I feel like I got the proper experience this time around. Starting from the beginning, taking my time looking for every last mutation and creature to add to the compendium. (The last one I needed was the final boss itself, go figure.) The permanent upgrade system is REALLY useful. Don't ignore it like I did on my first playthrough. Also, I CLOWNED on that Exonerator for that one achievement. It landed, and I just PUMMELED it with projectiles and killed it instantly. Lol.Overall, this game is just gorgeous. The narration is brilliant. The story is well-crafted. The environments and level design are superb, and the creatures fit perfectly into it. It really does feel like a totally alien world. And the SOUNDTRACK. This soundtrack is one of the most beautiful I've ever heard. Seriously, it is expertly composed. I've listened to it many times. The cave theme in particular is my favorite. I love the echoey droplet sounding effects. They fit into the score perfectly, making you feel like you're really in a dazzling cave filled with pretty gems and glistening water. 10/10 score.I love this game so much, and getting the rest of the achievements was an incredibly fulfilling experience. I got to re-enjoy the beauty of the world and narrative all over again, and really appreciate it for the work of art that it is. Props to the developers, you did good with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: The Eternal Cylinder was a very unique game. There are a lot of games where the world is ending but never quite like this. You are a small creature known as a Trebhum that can transform to get new abilities (e.g. Long legs for Jumping, A Big body to hold more items, a trunk that can spit fire...) to survive the Alien World filled with unique creatures.Now what i think what makes this world ending scenario unique is that youre always running from the eternal cylinder. you Can always see it, it can only be paused by special towers but it can never be stopped, so all the time you can see the world ending entity rolling towards you, youre just running away from it, you know it is always there.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: As the name implies, eternal cylinder is chasing and you have to survive. Even the concept of this is so weird, but after playing it through, I must say, it's very fun game.First of all, game is not perfect technical-wise. I did get some crashing now and then, but after I applied couple lines in engine.ini and one other file, it fixed it all for me. Look for steam discussions for more info about that.Soundtrack is very good. Epic as it can get.Graphics are nice. Nothing superb but it fits the game well. Creature models are very alien, so realism is subjective thing, but I personally liked them. Gameplay can be a hit or miss for many I think. Core concept is fun but if you're perfectionist, it can stress you if you lose a mutation and don't have idea if you can get them back easily. Or when biome changes and you lose access to some incredients or etc. But I assure, you can get most of them all the way to the end, and rest you can get from cylinder servants.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Although the game has a slow start, it's definitely worth playing It has a wholesome & cute vibe, alongside sinister and creepyThe creatures you encounter are incredible! They are very unique and well designed, some even made me gasp a couple timesThe level design was so huge, it seemed procedurally generated but it turned out to be hand-made!Special effects were also very impressive and I can tell the devs spent a long time on itSound design and music are very good, I love the cute sounds and small interactions Trebum haveCons (outweighed by the pros):The movement in the game relies heavily on the physics engine which can become frustrating at timesAlthough providing additional game-play, the mutation tree turned out to not be necessary as most of the mutations you need to progress quests/puzzles are always close-by. This also made losing abilities have less of an impactMost important con perhaps is the save system, being way too overpowered and making a serious consequence turn into a minor inconvenienceIt feels like some sound effects are missing (mostly footsteps & ambience), and the exploration theme didn't feel fitting in the final chapters(personal preference) I felt like the narration removed a bit of immersion from the game-play at times
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: It is unfortunate that this game hasn't received the attention on Steam that it deserves. The artwork and trailers really hyped me up for a unique experience and the game certainly delivered. I am only on chapter two but so far it has been a lot like Spore mixed with puzzles that are simple yet provide a sense of accomplishment and a good ole drip of endorphins. There is also a nice sense of progression as your herd grows and collects a wide variety of mutations/evolutions. You certainly begin to care for the little buggers. I have gorwn fond of them to the point of restoring saved games whenever I lose one of them.If the trailers or artwork intrigued you at all then I wholly recommend this game. It has unfolded to be exactly what I was expecting it to be and so far has scratched that Spore itch that never got satisfactorily taken care of many years ago.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Another excellent work by ACE team. While I was hoping for The Eternal Cylinder to be an open world game that took place inside a gigantic cylinder habitat, the actual story and gameplay has kept me engrossed regardless. I'm still sore that this game wasn't released on Steam right away, but that's okay, since I have it now. Not being at the top of the food chain is a nice break from playing some lone star hero, as you have friends along for the ride who engage with each other in an amusing manner whenever you get a chance to sit and rest. The recipes for making mutations permanent are something you have to figure out on your own (or use the wiki), which is rather irksome, and the Cylinder's servants are absolutely horrible to contend with, but besides that, The Eternal Cylinder is worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: The Eternal Cylinder mixes Spore to Zeldaesque features and delivers a surprisingly rich experience. Of course, the phenomenal soundtrack, creature/environment designs, and storytelling (thrilling without being unclear) are a big part of it, but the gameplay itself is fun. Neither too simple nor too complex. Discovering new mutations (even though you don't need all of them to progress) keeps things fresh even when the narrative's pacing slows down, and experimenting around leads to entertaining discoveries. That's part of what turns the game into a compelling journey that has you do much more than just run away from a giant cylinder.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO UNDERRATED. I'm not even finished with the main story line yet, and I'm having a blast! This game gives you 30+ hours of playtime, an open world, incredible narrator, cute main characters, an detailed and mysterious story, lots of crazy creative creatures, 221,347,488,284,231,041,398,408,534,792 different combinations for mutations, a great soundtrack,  and just a really fun overall experience. I couldn't have expected better from this game. This is not to say that it does not have it's fair share of bugs and glitches, but nothing I have found game-breaking. I really hope this company makes more games like this in the future, because I'm excited for more. People need to discover this hidden masterpiece. Seriously,  buy it, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok...  it takes a lot for me to get into a game.  This one looked interesting, so I gave it a try.  It is a masterpiece.  The idea of your little Trebum family, the idea of growing and keeping your family safe offered a beautiful, societal and emotional aspect to the gameplay.  Graphically, you are in a strange alien world all beautiful-rendered.  Yes, there is a linear path to this game, but also open world while you search areas to mutate and build your family, and grasp and maneuver the terrain.  It is a dangerous world you must traverse, and I found myself mostly avoiding conflict and using the mutated defenses to scare away the threats.  The game is simple, but complex with its depth.  It is different and unique, so I loved the game and its dynamics.

_childDocuments_.review: In this day and age where there are a billion options for the same genre with a slightly different skin, I found The Eternal Cylinder to be such a refreshing, unique and beautiful experience. Definitely my top game of 2022, hands down. Sure, we have our shooters, our RPG’s, our MMO’s and what not, and I love all of these, but I have never played a game like this, and I think that’s one of the biggest compliments I can give an experience. If I had to describe it, I suppose it would be an action adventure game with survival elements but that doesn’t really do it justice. The Eternal Cylinder is a game oozing with charm at every moment, it’s story is interesting, wacky, scary, and despite playing as these adorable, silly little blob creatures, surprisingly mature in it’s themes and presentation. However, in spite of this, it doesn’t forget that you are playing as silly little adorable blob creatures, and has plenty of levity to balance it all out. The world itself is graphically beautiful. It's funky, unique, charming, and has a good bit of variety as you go through the game. Even the music and sound design is great, the music is fantastic and the sound design fits the wacky world and adds a lot of character to the Trebhum and other creatures that inhabit it. The gameplay is fantastic too, it has a lot of emphasis on creating your family of Trebhum and building them out as you want, for example, maybe you need some more storage so you forage for the materials to mutate a Trebhum into a big-boi blob. Maybe you’re like “man, crossing water is slow” - well you’re in luck, go and find some mutagens to adapt a Trebhum to be an olympic swimmer! There are also lots of different designs of Trebhum to collect, so I quite enjoyed swapping them in and out to get the prettiest squad of fluff-balls that I could! As for moment-to-moment gameplay, I found for the 29 hours I played, I wasn’t getting bored one bit, and I usually find myself getting bored with games far before that. I found the pacing was pretty well done, I didn’t feel rushed through nor did I feel it dragged on longer that it needed to. If anything I would’ve liked to be able to play after the credits rolled though, if for no other reason than to say goodbye to my squad of Trebhums that I had become VERY attached to. Speaking of the Trebhum, so much love went into making these little creatures believable and lovable. Honestly, you can kill off a main character in a game and I’ll be like “oh that’s sad” but if anything so much as looking at one of my beautiful my Trebhum funny then HOO BOY, YOU ARE DEAD. I only really have a couple criticisms with this game, firstly, sometimes having a big squad of Trebhums can be a little bit of a liability in the harder segments as they get in the way a bit and end up getting quite spread out. Now you could of course just not have the full amount, but I love my little fluff-balls so there’s no way I’m not having as many as I can. Secondly, there are a few points in the game where you will lose a great deal of your mutations - now the game is paced with this in mind, so don’t let it turn you off too much, but it did frustrate me a little bit. Lastly, and probably my biggest gripe, UNSKIPPABLE CUTSCENES BEFORE FIGHTS. For the love of all that is holy I thought the gaming industry learned this lesson about a decade ago?! Still, given I only have three criticisms, that’s quite amazing really - I feel a game like this could’ve been very frustrating if they didn’t make a number of smart design decisions which cut down on micromanagement, because having 14 (I think) Trebhum by the end of the game would be a nightmare if you had to feed each one individually, because let me tell you these little buggers can eat. I could sing the praises of The Eternal Cylinder all day, but honestly, I went into this game pretty blind, having watched a YouTube video of the first 30 minutes of gameplay like a year ago. I think this is a game that the less you know, the more you’ll enjoy it. So, stop reading reviews! Go and play this game, it is so absolutely worth it!

Is it evil? Is it GOOD? or perhaps something much more?Surrounded in all this majestic nature divine beyond the limited control of the unnatural you shall find others of your kind who such as yourself have the ability to evolve and transform into greater forms of being when feeding and ingesting the cuisine feast all around you enhancing your abilities to survive in this carnal and spiritually nourishing environment teaching countless moral lessons on the importance of family,friendship, of never giving up, of when to fight and when to flee etc.In the midst of all this pagentry of beauty and learning you shall hear the magnificense of.. _childDocuments_.review: So good I bought it twice. First on the Epic games store, then on Steam. I'm just playing through it again now; a very good game with a beautiful world, plus awesome creature and character designs. As a person interested in character design, along with zoology, the ecology and interactions between creatures was really something. Seeing a Tonglegrop killing something in the distance, watching a Great Gaaarh swallowing up sand, spotting a Frozen Sklaa out in the wild, or witnessing a Witness examine anything that moves, that really made the game for me. And of course, the Mathematician was a highlight. His animations, sound design, music, and most importantly of all, character design, really made him an intriguing antagonist. Truthfully, I couldn't keep my eyes off him, his anatomy and movements were so realistic. Great work ACE team, I'll be checking out more of your games in the future, that's for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: The Eternal Cylinder is a very interesting game that kept me captivated throughout the adventure.The story centers on these tiny creatures called Trebhum, the mysterious majestic space creatures called the Trewhaala, and the titular deadly cylinder called The Eternal Cylinder that is destroying the planet. Your first Trebhum was born in a wrong place at the wrong time just when the Cylinder is already next to you. You must keep moving forward to avoid being crushed to death by the cylinder and survive, but that doesn't mean you're safe from the many hostile creatures you may come across. The goal of our young Trebhum is to find a way to escape this harsh planet with a help from these Trewhaala, but for some reason they're hostile to you. Along the way you will discover the truth behind the Eternal Cylinder and its monstrosities of servants.The gameplay is pretty simple with satisfying controls; You can jump, you can vacuum and shoot stuff with your snout, store foodstuff in your tiny inventory, and you can roll-up into a ball for faster movement. But the main mechanic of this game is that the Trebhum has the ability to absorb upgrades from the food they eat, and you can use these upgrades to adapt to the environment. You can't stack specific upgrades over the same body parts and actually replaces it, but if you increase your herd by adding more Trebhum you can distribute these upgrades to each one for more variety.The Eternal Cylinder itself is scary; At first it advances slowly and gets a little bit faster the longer it rolls. But it can be stopped temporarily by activating the towers. Activated, the towers turn blue and will stop the cylinder from advancing. Around the towers will cast a barrier, and while you're inside this the cylinder will remain dormant indefinitely and you can explore the area at your own leisure. If you leave the barrier the cylinder will awaken and destroys the towers that hold it. You must then activate the next towers to stop it, but failing to activate one as the cylinder crushes it it's game over.Thirst and hunger play a role in this game that'll affect your Trebhum's survival and movement. This can be remedied by stocking up on water and food. You can also improve your stats by finding these upgrade shrines that you can enter. Here you can increase each of your stats by spending minerals you find along the way (those glittery crystal things).I don't think I need to explain how pretty the graphics are. It's otherworldly pretty and very imaginative that is quite refreshing. Destruction is also beautiful once the Eternal Cylinder starts rolling and crushes anything in its path.Story-wise, it's very interesting to learn about the Trebhum's history, their relationship with the Trewhaala, and the Eternal Cylinder's existence. I will not spoil the story, but all I can say is that the writing is okay. Every creature speaks in alien language, so there's a narrator that tells the story for us. He sounds fine, since he's well-known in other games.It's a short game, though I admit I spent my time exploring the area so it took me longer to finish it. The biome and the fauna in each area are cool! My only wish is that they could've added something more to keep the theme of exploration and survival more exciting.While the game is nice, my only complaint is that there's one chase section that is impossible for me to outrun the Eternal Cylinder. I repeated this section for Gawd-knows how many times. I tried different tactics, but no matter what I always end up getting crushed by the cylinder. It got me to a point that I had to use the accessibility option to slow down the aggressive cylinder only just to finish that one annoying part before setting it back to normal.Another thing is the boss fights, especially the final one. If you get the right power-up some of the boss fight became trivial, and the final boss fight is kinda anticlimactic in that you just have to tank it through.All in all, it's a pretty neat game! I recommend this if you want a simple and enjoyable experience set in a wondrously strange world. The Trebhum might be small and fragile, but together they are strong.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunningly beautiful game. The alien and strange world of "the eternal cylinder" is full of interesting mechanics and interactions. The world building and story telling are simply breathtaking.There's little to no fighting in this game, but you have a lot of abilities to choose from to deal with all the different dangers of the world.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really thinking this would be a mix of spore and pikmin with a really surreal vibe. A game where you simply play as an animal trying to survive in a world where the apocalypse is here and its a planet-sized rolling pin. No real goal outside of survival, and a world that feels like it would move on even without you. Where the threats to your survival, be it the Cylinder or the predators, would live their lives and try to escape death even if you weren't there.Well i definetly got the surreal vibes. But I ended up with a heavily story-driven game where the dangers don't move unless you do. Even the "predators" or just generally agressive creatures can be avoided easily. There's really not much danger when YOU say when the Cylinder moves. And it seems that every time it moves its not for a long distance, making it less of a threat and more of an annoyance. And what I've seen from the story was mainly fetch quests. All of this made me drop the game very fast.The fact that it doesn't work well on my end didn't help either. I crashed twice before being able to enter the cave where you can upgrade your Trebums. And entering one of the ancient temples put me under the map and crashed again.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: An alien-looking adventure game about tribe of creatures called Trebhum that try to overcome a calamity by recovering their race's memories. Game is interesting mainly due to it's oddness, but with never evolving it's gameplay it can grow a bit stale.A story-oriented adventure game about a tribe of creatures called Trebhum and you guiding their attempt at overcoming the calamity known as The Cylinder. There are two quirks about them - first one being that their body can be modified if they eat an item counting as "mutagenic" (indicated by green lightning icon). Each Trebhum can mutate it's legs, eyes, trunk, body and skin to make your whole tribe prepared for different situations you'll run into on your mission. The second quirk is that their memory is genetic. But for some reason this generation of Trebhum can't remember anything from previous times, and so while trying to find a way how to stop The Cylinder you're also attemting to recover the race's memories.The gameplay itself consists of two parts. First part has you wandering around an area enclosed by a force field. During that time you scrounge around for food and ways to get water (Trebhum can eat a lot of things that either beat hunger, thirst or heal the whole tribe so it's not too difficult to manage), avoid predators and possibly Cylinder's servants, find some new mutagens and perhaps find a shrine (which allows you to upgrade your tribe) or a temple, which contains some environmental puzzles and at the end of which an elder awaits, talking to which pushes the story forward.When you've done all you wanted in the area, you have to cross the force field and the game moves to the second part. Leaving safety area of the tower causes it to lose power, and so The Cylinder awakens and starts rolling across the landscape crushing everything in it's way. Now your tribe has to run away towards the next closest visible tower before The Cylinder catches up with you. Your tribe's water level influences how high your stamina can recover and satiety is directly turned into energy for sprinting, meaning if you start the run sequence unprepared it's likely your tribe isn't gonna make it.The main pull of the game for me was semi-realistic graphics representing a world that is completely alien to ours. That augmented by grandiose music gives a sense of wonder when we explore that world.However it didn't take long to get used to all it, as the game doesn't alternate the environment a lot (there's only savanna, "the cold climate", "the hot climate" etc).The controls are a bit janky, you can hit Q to change which Trebhum you control at the moment while the rest of the tribe do their best to follow you around, teleporting to you if needed. The bigger your tribe is the more difficult it gets to account for all Trebhum and not have them get stuck somewhere while they follow you. Additionally enemies considered servants of the Cylinder have a beam of yellow light which they shine in the direction they look, which gradually burns mutations off all Trebhums caught in it effectively stunlocking them, which not only makes it more difficult to not get them killed, but also costs you your tribe's improvements.Other than that, the controls include basic things like jumping, rolling (which is a spring), sucking items in and spitting them back out which is on a bit of delay (so it's always difficult to spit only one item out) and using special ability related to mutations (like hover eyes, suction legs etc).Overall the game varied it's events a decent bit and it kept me interested enough to keep going. I loved the alien environments, creatures and names (like Tonglegrop), but considering it's rather slow paced and gameplay itself is never really varied in any way aside from having to find a specific new mutations to handle a specific problem I'd understand if people grew bored of it halfway through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game expecting spore honestly. I was disappointed at first, but what I got return was a different kind of great. You go through a cute and sad story of adventure as a little creature just trying to survive at first. I loved experiencing everything for the first time and listening to the narration build the world around me as I played. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and uglycute game with some interesting mechanics. Basic gameplay loop is, you are in an area of the world. It has clear boundaries defined by a shimmering wall. Inside that area, which can be quite large, you get to avoid enemies, gobble up resources, collect mutations (happen when you eat some resources) and go to special structures like temples, that serve as progressors of the story. As soon as you cross the mentioned wall, the cylinder starts moving and you better haul ass to the next tower to activate it before the rollypoly runs over you. Rinse repeat.Areas differ from jungle, to desert, to lava land, to ice, to.. It has a few biomes.The survival aspecs, as in eating and drinking, are quite toned down so if you don't like that you don't have to worry, you can even make themless potent in the options, which I liked.The gameplay is actually rather monotonous to be honest, but I enjoyed it.Most negative things I could say about this game is that it wastes potential in nearly everything.The story it set up is interesting, but is so little explored that in the end it feels like reading a blurb from a backcover.The various mutations are all interesting and most have their unique uses - in more way than one, there were several where there was like one or two puzzle you ever needed a mutation for. They really should have put in more temples, some with nothing but maybe a rare mutation indegrient at the end, that made usage of the mutations you may have picked up and or were provided in that same temple.You can "master" mutations so you can mutate them whenever you want without an indegrient, but you aren't able to master all of them no matter how much you try by the end. You don't learn enough "recipes" and some you learn later on need indegrients only found in earlier areas. To make the previous point worse, there is no new game plus or endless mode despite mutation mastery basically begging for it.You can defeat some enemies and get mutation indegrients from them, but besides pure luck, you need one of two special mutations to defeat any enemy and they're very rare. There should really be a way to defeat some without extra mutations.In the end, nice game, I enjoyed it, but it has it's imperfections.Note that for some reason, beside the wiki you can't find any help on the internet. No matter what question, the first 8 results are youtube vdeos, the rest not from the game. Nothing to blame the game for, just curious. I never saw so many videos on the front page with any search before.Also note that it was put in epic store embargo, so only buy if it's on sale, such anticonsumer moves shouldn't be rewarded
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every thing. The originality, the story and storytelling, the mechanics, and the music is a banger.The oddness of the world but also the incommensurable, unchanging and uncaring cylinder. It's the story of an alien world, that doesn't seem to make sense but is so original and wonderful to discover, and annihilation by something that also doesn't make sense, but is still even more odd, out of the already weird world. Nothing gave me the feeling of it being illogical though, just things that we have yet to discover fully. Things that are made by aliens could theoretically not be understood immediately, and this game is only showing things through the eyes of the Narrator and the Trebhums.Remember SPORE? It's a bit similar but focused on the creature stage and with a storyline. The savannah gave me a nostalgic feeling of my time playing spore as a kid.One annoying thing, and pretty much the only one. When I jump to get some minerals to process through my trebhum's body, I tend to hid the cave surface and be sent backward, so climbing those are annoying.I would strongly advocate for a new game + that increases difficulty while keeping the mutations you've unlocked. And also the ability to choose the colors of the trebhums
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the earlier version of this I played somewhere else, but the full game is just a wee bit tedious. Abilities and requirements are not spelled out, making some of the puzzles bothersome only because you have not been told a basic mechanic. Remember when most games were like that?Then there's the way you can lose abilities when trebums (your wee guys) are killed, so good luck with building a core of different guys.Also, the basic mechanic of the cylinder rolling only when you are ready is at times interrupted, leaving you struggling to get to the next safe zone in time, with purple lightning behaving one way on one of these forced rolls and another way on another forced roll.At least 50% of the game mechanic here is figuring out what the game mechanic is, and most of the other half is trying to keep your guys alive. There's little or no sense of progression, of overcoming the mechanics of the game, of controlling your destiny.It got so bad that I started ignoring all the opportunities to get new trebums, because they were just more trouble than they were worth.The game is quite beautiful to look at, and the whole scenario holds great promise. Let down by deliberate obfuscation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: an absolute tour de force masterpiece. this game is severely underrated and that on itself is a crime. I played this game expected a spore clone, what I got was an absolutely stunning story, amazing abstract imagery, and a wonderful soundtrack. do not miss out on this game.my only criticism is that this game has a bit of latency issues with the controls, such as the game not responding to me "sucking" sometimes. I recommend patching that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game inspires exploration without feeling overwhelmed by too much travel. Every time you survive, you live to find something new and mysterious. It's very imaginative. Creatures will leave you just observing them from a distance, noticing their similarities with Earth's creatures, while being unable to ignore their massive differences. The Narration is very well written and well read. Close to Stanley Parable levels. Not just because of the accent. It's a thought provoking game, that adults can enjoy. But offers a family friendly dialogue and atmosphere. Which is good, because we are family. And to survive we must embrace everyone of us.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: A really charming indie game that will take roughly a dozen hours to complete. Was pretty fascinating to see such a unique premise and environment, with lots of truly alien creatures. My only wish was for the Amber eyes to be a little more easy to find, but overall I can't recommend this enough for a general audience. (Also thanks to Jerma for exposing me to this game!)
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little game with a novel concept and unique gameplay, as well as creative design.Unfortunately I cannot recommend it as the game design itself is rather poor and feels janky or disrespects the players time (perhaps deliberately to pad game length).- The game initially teaches you to avoid hostile creatures. Aside from a boss fight with an ice creature (which feels half-baked), the game does not indicate that you can actually kill some hostiles (and in fact, need to in order to get some recipes)- Upgrade shrines always contain upgrade materials in the walls. Every time I saw an upgrade shrine, I groaned, knowing I'd have to spend 5-10 minutes collecting rocks off of the wall and feeding them to my mineral processor trebhum. Same for holes. These seemed to be the game's way of padding for time, because othewise it would be a <6 hour game.- There's no way to control your squad of trebhum. Their bad AI often gets them killed in BS unfair feeling ways (wait till you watch your mineral processor guy walk into lava and die). I save scum BS deaths, but sometimes it's hard to even know how they died -- sometimes it's mysteriously offscreen.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing setup, mediocre execution.Survival chores only further bog it down for me.The world is threatened by an incomprehensible unstoppable cylinder that destroys everything in its path. You're a small useless creature that can eat stuff to mutate. Mutations to the same part override each other. You can also have a crew and build a team. This is the perfect pitch for me, except this game doesn't really do anything interesting with either of those things and takes the most generic approach. I wanted to give it a chance (maybe it gets good), but then it brought the hunger meter that takes a while to fill and I mentally tuned out.The squad can die of-screen and you lose any powers that those members had unless you can resurrect them (not a problem IF you notice them die) or find the powers again. At least early crew members and some mutations are finite so... save scumming?The powers are keys to progress the story and not tools to diversify gameplay. Examples:  Jumpy Legs (higher jump), hair that attracts healing, passive conversion of materials into other things (like water which you can spray, or resource you use to resurrect allies). The concept is amazing, but this game simply doesn't do anything worth seeing with this concept.Finally hunger meter. It's not difficult to fill, but it takes a while because food barely does anything. It took me like 3-5 minutes - it's just a massive chore.On top of that controls are somewhat clunky as you perform SOME actions in direction character is facing and some in direction camera is facing.You can explore 1 small area at a time. The moment you leave it is the moment cylinder starts rolling and locks you into next small area.I love the idea of unstoppable natural force leading you towards extinction. It's an almost  Lovecraftian story where you face a threat you can't comprehend. It's a natural force you can outrun, but the planet will eventually be crossed and you'll end up on barren side with no life on it and no way to survive.Then the game says "Watch out for the agents of the cylinder" and ruins the setting in that 1 sentence. It takes this intangible natural force and attaches it into a tangible (meaning destructible) villain. It's like going for Lovecraft story and saying you can just shoot the monster to avoid the crisis.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Most games are a variation of some game that has come before with copy paste systems you've seen before. Which is perfectly fine, some of those systems are popular for a reason.Eternal Cylinder could have used some polish, and maybe a little more depth, but despite that it's quirky and unique and interesting. The game is longer than you might expect with more depth than you would think, and it develops gradually and delightfully at the pace you set.If you want to try a solid title that breaks the mold a bit, definitely give this one a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game: great story, ingenious game design, and powerful message delivered by a team of adorable protagonists. While the game does have some unclear or flawed mechanics, these are easily overlooked in the overall success of the storytelling and the world building. Well done team, this is a big win in my view.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, the story, the characters, including the enemies, the whole world. It is definitely different, which is what I was looking for. It is also perfectly playable, I have found one only bug but it was nothing important. One thing I miss is that the narrator gives you lots of clues to solve the scenarios and it makes it quite easy. It is not a hard game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: My personal Game of The Year 2023.It is a third person exploration/runner/shooter/puzzler with extraordinary survival mechanics and tribe management. I would say this is a worthy spiritual successor of "Spore".The graphics are out of this world, absolutely breathtaking on max settings. Animations: flawless. Gameplay: simple yet deep and constantly morphing/evolving. Never a dull moment. And, contrary to previous ACE Team's games, this time, music is absolutely fantastic.It is very demanding though: I had to upgrade to RTX4060Ti to max it out on 1080p.Can't recommend this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Difficult to articulate why I love this game so much. It reminds me of a more welcoming version of Rain World. Cute little weirdos running around an alien world with all sort of things for you to discover and a surprisingly thoughtful and at times even philosophical plot. A hearty recommend if you would like to try something different from the 10000 other games full of recycled mechanics and generic worlds.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a great experience! A plot that makes you think about the world. Creatures I'd never think of. A narrator and music, that creates a great atmosphere.The gameplay is great, even if it takes some time to get used to the controls. It took me 15 hours to end the game, however, you can invest even more hours if you want to achieve everything.You don't have to worry about loosing or aquiring skills. Everything follows a storyline, every step is well thought out and, ultimately, solving a small puzzle is part of every section.I can highly recommend the game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Leaving a positive review for this gem. Simply put, there's nothing else quite like this on the market. It's weird, unique, beautiful and mesmerizing. The premise itself is very strange, but that's a part of the appeal, along with the really weird creature designs. Just give it a shot, you'll know if it's your kinda thing within two hours.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Just beat the game and honestly I loved it. The world feels so nice, the Trebhum are adorable, I got so attached to all my lil dudes. Gameplay wise its alright, there are very stressful times during the game and unfortunatley as others stated, it can get repetetive, but other than that its pretty good.Overall this game has such a unique feel to it and I just love it, this feels like playing through a dream 6 year old me would have had. I give it a solid 8.5/10, I love this game .
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing game with a charming atmosphere.The alien ecosystem you explore is unique and complex and the mutations you get are a great character customisation tool for your little crew. The story is well told and interesting, and I had a lot of fun with it.The visuals and the soundscape are great, maybe the strongest points of an already well made game.My one small gripe is the puzzles: they are overly simplistic and the game often spoils them by straight up showering you with the tools you need or even telling you the solution before you ever begin.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: although my game has crashed once (from the time of this review) don't let the few overly negative reviews stop you from buying this game. I feel like Eternal Cylinder is sort of the closest thing to playing a scene from the Never Ending story (take that with a pinch of salt) my playtime has been short, but i cannot deny this game is incredibly charming.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: The art direction is phenomenal (and might be worth buying the game at $5 to experience it), but the gameplay is mediocre. Most disappointingly, the game's length is extremely padded via pseudo-open world sections which aren't interesting after the first few times.If you can resist the game's temptation to waste your time, however, the game might be great, so consider rushing through only what's required if you do buy the game. I wish I'd been able to enjoy most of my time with it, but I couldn't.I also didn't like the storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most detailed games I have played in the last years.. so I really loved  the music in every map/mini boss/ new area/ fights etc I freaking loved the variety and the creatures were so original that it reminded of my Subnatica gameplay.. thanks for putting this much effort and as a Chilean I had my hopes up for you since the first trailer and you didn't dissapoint. Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: I love absolutely everything about this game except for the gameplay. The controls are janky, there is a lack of direct guidance, the narrator only hints you at what needs to be done, your trebhum will die randomly and unfairly to enemies you didn't know existed, there's all sorts of problems with this one which makes it tedious and generally irritating to play.The best way to experience The Eternal Cylinder is to watch you friend or a streamer play it so that you can get the full experience without actually having to play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: was kinda a cool game, until they decided they wanted to be a platformer. platforming in this is just random chance and there are so many situations where you are just screwed and have to redo some tedious series of jumps. platforms move randomly and you can fall back to the beginning in many areas, there just isnt enough fun here to validate such inconvenience
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game but with flaws. The game has exploration, survival and platforming tasks. There are couple of puzzles. But at first it is story-driven, and all other aspects are nominal. There are not a lot of things to explore, not a lot of puzzles, not a lot of survival things. Unique game world is a big plus, but you should try to pass the game faster as otherwise you'll be disappointed by poor content as it was with me.1) Control. Imho, it would be much better to have option control trebnum from 1st person view. In game you have some platforming moments and they made bad as trebnum bounces from other trebnums, walls, etc. It irritates a lot. The same with boss battles. There is no aim icon in game, but you have to shoot by water or stones. How? Why not to add an aim?2) Lack of unique content. I've passed game for 27 hours, trying to investigate each place I stay. Now I think it was a mistake. Thought I've got more mutations, I have lost a lot of time looking at the same places, same shrines, same creatures. It could be possible to make more biomes. It could be possible to add some unique places that is cool to find. It would be really cool to have different shrines as all shrines are the same. Yes, they have small differences like additional trampoline or bonus. But when you visit 10th such shrine it is very disappointing.3) Optimisation. I played Witcher 3 on my PC and did not have any issues. This game lagged and my only explanation is bad optimisation. Also I had 1 crash and once a game has been frozen. Probably for 27 hours of game it is fine. At least compared to New Vegas. :)Also I should tell about strange mix of game appearance and atmosphere. I play funny creatures with funny voices. I see quite funny animals. But on the other hand I see cylinder minions looking like monsters from body horror movie, I see the apocalyptical story and in general the story is not fun but sad. I don't know whether it is okay or not. There is some charm in it, but I feel like something else should be added or rebalanced to make the store 10 out of 10.My final score is 6,5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: MEGA game I love the narrator and the story is also mega good The absurd way of playing the game at the beginning is a sweet absence and always a wow momentI hope the ACE Team take this crazy and very beautiful, impressive game design for the following games and continue to come up with such unique/crazy creatures 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: My god, what an experience. This game was incredible from start to finish, and I found myself absolutely enthralled in the story. Admittedly the gameplay is quite repetitive but there was enough to shake it up throughout that I really didn't mind, and the design of the world and its inhabitants made for a captivating journey throughout the game. I highly recommend this game to anyone who's interested.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every second of this game. Even some of the frustrating parts. The story is beautifully presented, the creatures are adorably weird, and the monsters are imaginatively grotesque. I wasn't sure whether to buy the game when I stumbled across it on the day of its release. At first I thought it was a cousin to Spore but with a story, which it kind of is, but it's way better than that. I just wish I could continue the lives of my little family after the story ends, but that's a me preference and doesn't at all change the gameplay qualities. Whoever reads this please play this game; you will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: More than "weird", The Eternal Cylinder feels really alien, from the world to its inhabitants, and the cylinder is the most alien entity of it all.There is something very compelling about it, like its sheer size or the way it seemingly extends infinitely on both sides, crushing everything on its path... its a very great hook for a game and probably one of my favourite antagonistsI liked how this game managed to explore its themes through the gameplay, encouraging you to have many trebhums to  have access to a good variety of mutations so you can overcome obstacles easily. Sometimes they die, sometimes its not even your fault but such is the world they live in.I also loved the narration and how it gave life to the world, describing the trebhums struggles and emotions through their adventure.I was very pleasantly surprised by The Eternal cylinder and strongly recommend it !
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: You know, this is one of those games where cute graphics won't save it.The control of the trebhum is so bad that I started getting nightmares. And if you begin to look too closely (namely spend more than 5 minutes in each "level") you will see how terribly repetitive those level elements actually are. I am not joking, I'm really glad it's over - and I very, very rarely say that because making unique games is definetly not easy. But I NEVER got nightmares from a game like this before. A mechanic that absolutely killed my patience in the end was to have a ball of soft flesh bounce back (or rather rag doll back) ~ 5m or more because there was a fruit in the way, a relative height distance of ~ 10cm, or an invisible wall out of nowhere. The same physics even apply when you fly as a balloon, making the harvest of items that are higher up a "15-minute-game of patience" as well. With super repetitive sounds as well.Not to mention that there are several spots where necessary resources are *inside* the walls or piles of stone, the animals pass right through the cylinder, you get the occasional "flying object" and after a while you'll get glitchy light effects that made me worry about the health of my graphic card. Luckily this really was just a programming issue, but to have this happen at all is a very bad thing.Which is a terrible shame. I like the trebhum. The trebhum are cute and the worlds design is interesting. Although not all mutations seem to have that much of a usage, they are quite funny too. In the end, they could have done quite a bit with it. But they didn't and I can't change my feeling of dread now.---Oh, and by the way: reloading right after collecting stuff will reset and respawn those in most cases as well. Do with this info as you like, maybe it will help you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Another masterpiece from ACE team.You play as a family of Trebhum, little creatures that can absorb powers and mutate from things that they eat. your goal is to keep your little herd from dying of thirst or hunger and search for the reason for the downfall of your race's civilisation. all whilst being chased across the world by the rolling megastructure that the game is named after, crushing everything in it's path.The soundtrack is incredible, the creature designs are super alien and unique and the gameplay, whilst not super challenging, is engaging enough to keep you from getting too relaxed/bored.There really aren't many similar games to compare it to. There is Spore, but it reminded me more of a much more forgiving version of Rain World. Creatures in the environment seek out food and hunt one-another in a believable ecosystem, meanwhile you're just another small scavenger animal trying to get by in a world full of large carnivores. If you're on the fence about getting it I would highly recommend that you take the plunge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: It is rare to get to play unique games these days. Reminiscent of the styles from early 2000, when people were just trying new ideas and had a cool vision. The Eternal Cylinder is that type of game and it deserves your support. I wouldn't thumbs it up however it was not a good game. I went into it blind with little knowledge of it except there exists some eldritch-like Cylinder that smashes everything. I think that's mostly all you need to know in regards to the plot. There's a certain joy in being dumped into an entirely alien world, what you are and with no clue what's going on and what's dangerous and learning to survive in it. Too bad you happened to hatch in the middle of some kind of armageddon extinction event. Roll along now!
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game. I am currently halfway through the game (in this playthrough at least. I got the game back when it released on the epic store and played through it) and it is once again a wonderful experience.The real drive for the game is the story and the mysterious world. The world is just wonderful and wonderfully alien.The game does have a few rough edges, but nothing that really kills the experience. Some are even rather quirks of the game than rough edges., like the wonky ballon physics when floating into a wall.All in all I can't not recommend the game. It is the only game in well over ten years that made me feel that sense of wonder at exploring a new game world I had as a child in the late 90s and early 2000s.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: First off I love the game/premise, but there are several things that bother me.collision: constantly running into your trebhum herd. bump bump bump. now everyone is dead because you couldn't get away from the aggressive monster(tonglegrops).monsters: there's nearly always some big beasty that pops up when you have no resources or combat ability. the one trebhum with the mutation you need always dies to it.towers: unclear, do I just walk over the light or do I need to stay on it? I have had trebhum run into the cylinder seemingly on purpose. usually the ones with the resources I need to unlock mutation tree upgrades. Having to go across multiple biomes in order to collect each resource for one skill makes it difficult to unlock anything.respawn area needs to have a bank for resources, at least for us low skill players.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Eternal Cylinder is an amazing game. The story could be a contender for a Locus/Hugo/Clarke award!But the story is not the whole game, only a part of the game. Neither is it the best thing in the game. To me, Eternal Cylinder is foremost a great environment and a truly alien world. An alienness captured and depicted much better than any other games (unlike for story, the bar is set high here!) This is due to the amazing soundtrack, sound design, monster design, graphic programming and the .You are a little creature called Trebhum. You are a small weak thing in this world in a scale far beyond yours, completely alien and unpredictable.It's terrifying. You are always watching out for danger, fearful of your blind spots, listening attentively to make sure you are not running straight into the maw of danger. Even plant life can be dangerous.But maybe this is not the game for you. I found the controls very limited, specifically, if you try to jump up a ledge, you are usually pushed away from it. And generally, your input more often feel like a suggestion, there is always half a second of delay between you pressing left and the Trebhum going left. Also the Trebhums are quite happy to act like lemmings and jump to their death even if your party leader is in a safe place.Also, even if excellent, the soundtrack and sound effects are poorly balanced, resulting in VERY LOUD bits at times.Finally, props for integrating AMD FSR2, the game looks amazing on my 4K display, and I can run it at good frame rate thanks to upscaling, FSR2 makes upscaling actually difficult to distinguish from native resolution.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: So you start out as a Little Guy. You're not very good anything in particular. However this little guy is functionally an alien Kirby with a trunk (elephant, not car). Right away the game introduces you to it's namesake, The Eternal Cylinder. It is quite literally a Very Large Tube that just steam rolls the landscape. And it is chasing you. Thankfully there just happen to be mysterious towers placed exactly where you need them to temporarily hold back your tubular pursuer. Each time the Cylinder takes a break, you get a defined area to forage and explore. Foraging is where things get interesting. Not only are you looking around for water and food to drive your biological meat sack, you will also find certain food items that will give your Little Guy a special trait! There are a few 'slots' that can be changed on any given dude you have. And you will have a whole family! Each one you can specialize what they do, and you collect this dust that you can use to level up your general stats like health, stamina, the number of creatures you can bring around at any one time, etc. So that's the basic loop. You run from the cylinder, you look for food, find new abilities, find new family members, level up, and become more and more comfortable surviving with your family in this otherwise harsh world. All of this is narrated by a wonderfully delicious VA, and interweaved with surreal mystery that still has me scratching my head. Highly, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: For some reason my playtime is at 0.7 hrs, but I think that's glitched. I'd say i've played closer to 15.The Eternal Cylinder is a great game. Super weird and charming, with some rogue-like vibes (but not too much). The creature and enemy design in this game is some of the best I've ever seen. I appreciate the open exploration coming in little chunks at a time. The story is great as well. Even though i've beat the story, I'll probably come back to the game to try and unlock all the mutations.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: This one snuck up on me.   I hadn't even heard of this game.  Practically zero hype surrounding it.  The trailer looked great and unique so I took a chance.  I am glad I did.  This game has heart.  The game play is a nice blend of frantic chases followed by gather and collect yourself survival moments.  Intriguing and mysterious story line.  Visually it is looks great and is really psycedelic, the soundtrack is really chill but ads the right amount of anticipation and anxiety when needed.  Solid well done game design.  It doesn't seem grindy and yet you need to prepare for the next stage.  Its just a perfectly balanced game with a unique play style and artwork.  We need more games like this.  Not sure why this one fell off the radar.  I highly recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Played through this in the beta 2 years ago, finally got it on steam and got to playing it, and MY GOODNESS. There is so much more to it that I though.The Eternal Cylinder, now complete, remains among the best games I've ever played. The little creatures you control are certainly silly looking but it's such a gorgeous, wholesome, and fascinating game (though a little tough at times for my non-epic-gamer self). There's never a boring moment in the Eternal Cylinder (even me as an explorer who scours every inch of an area) a lot of super strange alien creatures and interesting lore with a little reminder and a cute ending scene to meet you when you finish.10/10, you should absolutely buy if you want a good game to get through in a break or something.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's kind of like Pikmin meets Spore, but scaled down a bit.Add some rpg and some survival elements and you've got The Eternal Cycinder.You adopt or hatch, and evolve your little round guys with abilities to help to traverse the world and solve puzzles to figure out why your world is being destroyed by a giant cylinder.The cylinder does stop, so it's not a constant mad dash. You activate towers that make a safe zone until you leave the area to progress, then the cylinder starts again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: The world of this game is amazing. Everything is weird and crazy. The whole cylinder thing is extremely interesing. You wonder what's up with all of this and want to explore the world and find out and then ... you get a narrator. Just some third person narrator throwing exposition at you at every corner. NO! You ar enot allowed to wonder what that weird creature is. The narrator just tells you. Period. Move on. It's the exact opposite of "Show, not tell." The game tells you all the time. And it's this tiny problem which seriously hurts the entire experience to an extreme extent. Had they designed it around environmental storytelling instead of a narrator that thing would be a no brainer. But as the story depends on the narrator simply telling you everything, I can't really recommend it. You might have fun with the game. But all the while you will be just sitting there, feeling spoiled and thinking about what could've been.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointment. The premise looks cool af, I was so curious to find out what is the giant cylinder, why is is there, and so on.. but the gameplay loop.. ew.it's like they took the worst aspect of Spore creature stage, added unintuitive puzzles to the mix, a LOT of different items and interactions between each items to remember and account for, plus you have your party following you without being self sufficient (so you have to check that they don't starve themselves despite walking tru plenty of food) and die by random enemies that unless you watch a video you'll never have guessed how to counter-attack them. maybe I'm missing the point, the narrator seems interesting but doesn't help much (I don't want to be handheld but after 1 hour of gameplay I'm still clueless on even the most basics gameplay aspect)

_childDocuments_.review: Normally, I'd write a thoughtful, detailed review to provide as much information about a game as possible... The Eternal Cylinder? I think "what the f*ck" suffices. It's what you'd get if Spore was turned into a survival RPG: fantastic visuals with a very wide variety of extraterrestrial locations, beings, and items; a great soundtrack; an "antagonist" in the form of an endlessly-rolling cylinder that made me sh*t myself several times; a somewhat linear progression system with decent puzzles and bosses.Story-wise? I ended up finishing the game with more questions than I started with, if that tells you anything. It might've been due to the fact that I was faded for ~10 of the 11 hours I played, but I think the game is just so wonderfully weird and outlandish that you end up not really thinking about the "what" or "why" and end up just "doing".Pro-tip: don't name your Trebhum after your friends; your friends will hate you for letting them die, and they  die. _childDocuments_.review: for the first 2 chapters i thought this game was going to end up my goty right before 2023 but they got in their own way from the middle to the end. This game has a lot of gameplay decisions that detract from the experience rather than add to it. The further into the game you are the worse it gets.VIDEO GAMEIn the beginning you run from the cylinder. Each section where the cylinder stops has a temple or 2 to visit and loot. These temples can upgrade you, they can have puzzles, or platforming sections. The reason i dont like these is because it feels like the overworld mechanics were already fine. These added gameplay sections take away from the feeling of being a prey animal trying to survive in the wild. Trying to survive, finding weird mutations and aliens, trying to run away from predators, thats where this game shines.The magic in this game in the beginning was also fantastic. It was the addition of a page of lore for every animal, mutation, and plant in the game that made that magic slowly disappear. The story also has this problem of over explaining the events where strange magical events happen. The narrator is not the problem, i love the nature doc tone, the problem is that he gives so much information that theres barely any time to wonder.VEGEL: LEGEND OF THE ONE AND ONLYThe point of this game is your GANG your GUYS the BOYS your PEOPLE and they just LOVE jumping into poison and lava and dying leaving all your resources behind resetting your progress on unlocks. TOO MUCH TROUBLE! ALL YOU NEED IS ONE GUY!Vegel was that guy for me...He was born into this world a sickly yellow color and he was very fat. A cruel existence for sure. One day the cylinder had taken all his comrades. Vegel knew he had to finish the mission.HARD WORK AND DETERMINATION led Vegel to a max level stamina. Cant kill what you cant catch. He could turn food into water so he never needed to stop for a drink. He smelled HORRIBLE (actual mutation) so he could eat in peace knowing none would want to eat him. FOUR SPRINTING LEGSUNLIMITED STAMINANEVER STOPSA DEADLY ODORNONE MORE WERE NEEDED BUT VEGELThe game continued talking about "us" but it was only Vegel. The final boss gave me a warning that my current group would be all i could take with me. Vegel handled it just fine.I dont regret playing and finishing it but with the flaws it has i wouldnt recommend anyone else spend money on it unless it was discounted.

_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game asks you to lead a group of incompetent morons around the most dangerous planet I've ever seen, and then kills your AI companions than have vital tools you need to continue playing. It was very promising, but poorly executed. The world is interesting, and the gameplay concepts were fun, but losing significant progress in a way you can't control makes this game unplayable. Save scumming didn't make the experience any less frustrating, because sometimes the last save was when you were in peril, and there's not an easy way out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: . .  Cant really recommend..   Basically one big escort quest, with random stuff, that you dont see killing your dudes. Technically there is a setting that means that enemies only target the controlled Trebhum. But since all your guys are always right behind you, and all damage is AOE, then you will constantly, be reloading and trying again,, or just leaving the guys dead, which wont quite work, since you need a certain nr. of guys for certain triggers..Additionally, calling this game openworld, is sort of misleading, since you are confined to a small'ish area at alle times, and if you leave the area, you are forced to quickly move to the next confined area, to survive.On top of that the gameplay, is not really that interesting..
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game with lovely design and story.Pretty much everything in there is just neat.However I won't give positive review to this.There are two major issues inside the game.First one is the fatal error / crash to desktop.Almost every loading screen results in crash.Sometimes that even softlocks the save file.It is a very frequent issue throughout game.And sometimes it blocks off the shrines too.Some achievements therefore unobtainable.Many people voiced this issue in the forums.Last update was in 2022 though, so it is oof.Second issue is the lack of a new game plus.If you miss a collectible and beat this game:You gotta start from zero and try that again.But since it crashes a lot, it's a painful grind.And from what I can see it is impossible too.Since some shrines just always like to crash.Until the issues are fixed I can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: My equipment:OS: Windows 10 (64 bit)Proc.: AMD Ryzen 7 4800HVideo: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060RAM: 16 GBSolid-state drive.An entertaining mixture of such ancient games as Evolva, Sacrifice and Spore. Character development in the form of mutations, terry cannibalism, team building and team management. There is a certain plot-story that develops as you progress through the game and is voiced by the narrator. And, of course, there is a well known game design from the ACE team. These are pluses. I have not played in such projects for 10 years.BUUUUUUUUUUUUUuuuuuttt....The game is very poorly optimized. With my hardware I play without ray tracing and on the lowest requirements with a resolution of 1080р. 25-35 (!) FPS guys. This is a total fiasco. I have been a huge fan of ACE team since 2011, I love all your games very much. But now, unfortunately, I can not recommend this product for purchase.Update: There is an uneven load on the CPU cores. One core is loaded by 90-95%, the second by 40-50%, the rest are not used at all. I think this is the source of the friezes of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: 7\10 but i wish it was a 10a bealtiful well crafted story about diversity and the bealty of being a stubborn kind, the true strenght of humanity is our differences and our abbility to cooperate with each other and create bonds, and in that premise, TeC excells, however, it gets sabotaged by its own desire to be a video game, and thus falls into the traps of having the little quirks and annoyances of a mid title.many people don't know but using the inventory map (press i, the game doesn't tell you that, i know) you can find exactly how to progress to the next tower, otherwise it becomes a frustrating game of guessing, while many games with multiple characters have the decency of making non controled characters take care of themselves, in this game you will find yourself babysitting most of your family because if left to their devices, they will drown without getting out of the water, be attacked by creatures, turn on traps that remove the items you deposit on their inventory, it ends up making this bealtiful tale be accompany by the world's longest bodyguarding quest in gaming, it seems to be a trend with ace team to make bealtiful games brough down by their own need to be mid to average games, to your next title, focus on being fun please.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a dev actually thinking about the gameplay aspect first, nailing it and then building a story around it. Really well executed gameplayloop that drifts into the repetitve once in a while without being overly obnoxious. There were some frustrating parts: The food mechanic just does not make any sense. It drained more than your thirst meter. Also, personally, I do not like the "take away your powers" mechanic. You invest so much time building up these cutsie, little monsters, getting used to their look and imbuing them with character, only for it to be taken away due to the slightest mistake (which might not even be your fault - the game has a couple of janks and glitches).Overall it's an endearing experience, clad in an enourmous effort on the musical ambience front. No, really - check out the soundtrack. This is "Ori Blind Forest" levels of orchestral accompaniment.I had a great time, despite a lot of frustrating parts that kept me from continuing sometimes.  I hope for a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: There's is a certain unspoken rule when it comes to developing and releasing a video game, and that is to not create software that damages your player's computers. sadly, this game poses a great risk to your computer's health, especially if you have amd hardware apparently. My experience with the game after playing for several hours ended with the game hard crashing to desktop, my entire save becomes corrupted, and my graphics driver suffers a very bizarre malfunction. Doing some research i found this is a pretty common problem. Some people experience their entire computers blue screen while playing this game long enough. You should play this game at your own risk. _childDocuments_.review: This might be the best game I've ever played and definitely the most unique and amazing. Every new area ( which there are a ton of) introduces at least a few new things, and they are always totally crazy and unexpected not only in design but in the ways they behave and the uses they have. The level design is genius. You get to spend some time in each open area exploring, adapting, fleeing from creatures and finding secret areas before rolling off as fast as possible across a just as detailed landscape as the cylinder crushes it all. Having multiple little guys in your party that can evolve separately gives you more ways to solve things and because they can die it really makes you feel that you are fighting extinction for your species and how much you'll be losing. When one of them dies or just you alone scrapes by it gives the stakes some emotional weight. You can still bring them back later though so it never feels hopeless. When I was looking at the store page for this game I couldn't quite figure it out but I knew I had to play it right that second, and I hope you do to. If I could recommend just one game to anybody, it would be this one.
