_childDocuments_.review: Ive been a huge fan of ACE team and their insanely cool projects since the day I picked up Zeno clash 1 on xbox 360 when I was probably 12. The worlds these devs create, the psychadelic, insanely unique vision most of their games possess, captivates me unlike anything else. I was given the opportunity by the devs to showcase this game to my very small audience of close friends and acquaintences. Not the first time its happened but never from a company Ive loved and respected for over half my life. Most of the time Ill give the games a good hour, give an out of ten review of what I played and submit to devs for approval. This time I couldnt stop myself from playing even when it got so late my eyes burned. I blasted through this game with a smile on my face (almost) the entire time. Theres excitement and curiosity in every new mutation to discover, there are abilities to make the game completely open up to you in ways you would never expect. Mechanical depth mixed with a wonder and an atmosphere means there isnt a single chance the game will ever give you to get bored. This game has more than enough content to give completionists and fans of collectathons something to really bite into. But something again has to be said about the atmosphere, art direction, storytelling, and pacing which I think ACE team is getting closer and closer to making perfect with every subsequent project. I am baffled I got this game for free, I beg you to experience it for yourself. One small gripe but it is important to share, this game has a bug where occasionally after adding a new Trebhum to your party, you will simply lose control over your main trebhum completely. The fix for this is to simply save and load into that save to regain control. It happened maybe 3 times in my playthrough but knowing the fix made it much much less of an issue than it couldve been. Thank you ACE team for giving us another weird and wacky work of art to experience, and thank you so much for the opportunity. Everyone I showed it to loved it immensely and I think a few might be writing reviews of their own for this game pretty soon
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: The Eternal Cylinder is a sublime game which transported me far and which moved me greatly. An open world that doesn't insult the player's intelligence. Regardless of the bugs and AI issues, it didn't steal its 9/10 in the French reference magazine Canard PC. The soundtrack is fantastic, my respects to Patricio Meneses.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rare gem of a game that really is unique. It's the sort of game that would have stayed with me for life if I'd played it as a kid. It feels like a true struggle for the survival of your funny little guys, it's artsy, it's weird, it's meaningful, it's a story about the strength of diversity and hope, and it's just a great game. It's not perfect, it wont be for everyone, but I'm really glad this sort of game is still being made. Do yourself a favour and give it try!

_childDocuments_.review: The game punishes you for not hoarding materials from earlier biomes when you have no incentive to do so, and when you do, it's too late to go back and collect the materials and you're stuck scavenging the small patches of early-game biome that appear sometimes later on, often with little success. This is unbelievably tedious and has you fretting over the fact that you didn't hold on to that one item just a little longer. I was willing to put up with it but due to a breaking bug that sometimes crashed my game when I entered an upgrade shrine, I had to put an end to it. _childDocuments_.review: It's kind of hard to recommend this game to people, and it's a difficult game to even describe since the core gameplay is getting a little herd of Scrimblos and feeding them different kinds of mushrooms to give them stinky feet or whatever.But I think if you can get behind playing a peaceful and positive game that often slows things down a bit, there's a lot to enjoy here. It's easy to get lost in the details of fiddling with your boys and trying to make the best team possible, although ultimately the game was easy enough I was able to get by with basically whatever. Also obviously the world is beautiful and full of incredible creatures, whoever does the monster designs for ACE Team is doing top-notch work.SLIGHT QUIBBLES:I do think the yellow light stealing your powers is not a greatly implemented mechanic though, it REALLY pisses the player off for no real reason. I'd probably just signpost it more? Like as it is now the game just sweeps a light over your scrungus horde and you hear a series of pops and you're aware you just lost like 12 powers but you don't know WHAT or on WHO. I think the game could have benefited from 1) a menu you could pull up that immediately showed what powers everyone had at a quick glance and a way to rapidly select the right guy and 2) more info being given to the player about what the light was doing. as it is now, if I want to find my Third Eye guy I have to physically move the camera around and look at them all one by one to sight-check which of them has it and then slowly switch through the entire group to get to him.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a fantastic surreal experience. To me, this is the spiritual successor of Cubivore. There are few higher praises in my book. The Ai on the Companions isnt as bad some make it out to be. They are very simple FOLLOWERS. They do what you do. If you vacuum or spit water they do the same. They path a little oddly sometimes though. The mutations are a fun unique system to get new abilities, again a la Cubivore. This was wonderful and immediately gave me vibes / experiences i havent had since, again, cubivore.Only real negative i have is it crashed about 3 or 4 times over my playtime. It autosaves pretty regularly so it wasnt much of a setback.
_childDocuments_.name: The Eternal Cylinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is not one of those typical joke reviews on Steam. I am dead serious when I say that The Eternal Cylinder and the ever-evolving story of the Trebhum has touched my heart in a way no other person, piece of media or simply anything in this realm of existence ever has. The profound impact on my life and future that has been caused by this game is one not to be underestimated; by playing this game, and committing real time, emotion, thought and love to it, you are signing a contract with The Lord Above (Amen) to spend the rest of your days with the beautiful exclamations of a Trebhum echoing in the back of your mind, their resounding efforts against the cylinder pushing you forward, motivating you to push for greater heights in all areas of your own life. The Eternal Cylinder and its masterfully crafted storytelling have left me touched on the deepest level by the sheer spectacle that is the life cycle of a Trebhum. I can assure you wholeheartedly that you will not regret following this experience of a lifetime.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very original game design that's worth checking out if you don't mind the unsettling aesthetics. The developers have managed to take the very strange Zeno Clash world and bring it to life in a new experience where you control a group of adaptable creatures in a way that feels like a more serious version of the Creature mode from Spore. The gameplay shifts with discovering new abilities that allow you to progress to new zones, or gather new materials, or otherwise deal with new situations. The controls & squad management largely work against you, but I found the story to be pretty engaging, and the systems expand enough as you progress to keep things interesting. As difficult as the controls & squad mechanic was to deal with, I think the game was done really well overall and the experience is pretty memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a surprise for me. I wasn't expecting much and I had a lot of fun with it. It's like if Spore and the Oddworld franchise had a baby, with Crash Bandicoot there acting as the midwife. If you're the type who enjoys systems-based mechanics in games, this is definitely up your alley. It's not the deepest in that regard, but what's available is interesting and fun to play around with. There's definitely some design oversights that are surprising for a developer who's released so many games, but the game-play loop, story, and world/creature design was enough to keep me interested. Start to finish, I'd say it's worth the price, even more so on sale.

_childDocuments_.review:
In The Eternal Cylinder, players control a herd of adorable creatures called Trebhums and must explore a strange alien world filled with exotic lifeforms, surreal environments, and the constant threat of the Cylinder, a gargantuan rolling structure of ancient origin which crushes everything in its path. This unique ecosystem is a massive, procedurally generated land with unique animal AI, real-time world destruction, and organic exploration and puzzle design to create emergent gameplay that ensures no two playthroughs are ever the same.
Your Trebhums begin at the bottom of the natural food chain but can mutate and evolve with new physical attributes and abilities by eating a variety of flora and fauna. Discover and adapt dozens of mutations, including new traversal skills like flying and swimming to reach new areas, and new senses to help overcome puzzles, challenges and dangers. Your many Trebhums can each have different mutations, and new mutations don't replace ones you already have, letting you stack ability sets in dynamic ways. Each mutation will also change the physical look of a Trebhum and stacking these will generate near countless surprising new creature designs which players will be able to organically discover as they explore this unique alien ecosystem. 

Game Features:

* Unforgettable Alien World to explore: Players must explore a gorgeous procedurally generated world which is populated with unforgettable vistas and unique landscapes which have something new to discover around every corner. The Eternal Cylinder features an open-world which allows players to reach and explore any areas which they can see on the horizon. This encourages constant exploration and ensures that there's always something new to see. 

* Real-Time World Destruction: Everything in the world can be destroyed in real-time by The Eternal Cylinder, so players must continuously evade its destructive path in order to survive whilst marveling at the visual splendor of its godlike power.
Story Driven Open-World Survival: Unlike many open-world survival titles, The Eternal Cylinder features a deep and engrossing story for players to uncover as they continue to explore the vast world. The game explores themes of family and heritage, and the lasting power of knowledge.

* Build Your Own Alien Family: Unlike standard survival games where you have a main shelter that you can build or improve, in Eternal Cylinder players develop a nomadic herd of unique alien creatures called Trebhums. Players control one Trebhum from the herd at a time and the rest follow (Al controlled) but players can switch to any individual member of their herd at will. Explore the world to rescue more of your brethren and continuously expand your family. Control a herd which can grow to more than 20 members at any given time and imbue each of your Trebhums with their own unique mutations and skill sets. Players can create a custom name for each of their Trebhum, increasing the emotional bond between player and their Trebhum family. 

* Unique Mutation System: Although Trebhum's are generally frail and start their lives at the very bottom of the world's food chain, they have the unique ability to mutate and unlock new skills by consuming natural edibles which populate the game world. So, players must explore and experiment with a vast array of fruits, flora and alien creatures to unlock new powers and gameplay options. 

* 50+ Mutations to discover: Players can unlock more than 50+ unique mutations as they explore the world, each one of which enable new gameplay options. These include new traversal options such as the ability to fly and swim, but also new offensive moves like the ability to spit fire and create loud warning noises. New mutations allow players to explore new areas and each mutation stacks thus creating a truly expansive skill set which is constantly evolving. 

* A Trebhum for everyone: Enjoy a virtually endless visual variety of Trebhum designs, as each mutation combine with one another to create surprising new creatures. This allows your herd to continue to evolve as players explore new areas and players can share the unique look of their Trebhum family with the rest of the world online. 

* Layered Survival: Players need to manage multiple layers of resources in order to be able to survive. These include hydration level, various temperatures each with their own impact and stamina. 

* Living and Breathing Ecosystems: The world of The Eternal Cylinder is populated with more than 30 memorable handcrafted alien creatures. These creatures vary greatly in size and range from those smaller than a Trebhum, all the way to skyscraper sized leviathans who dominate the horizon. Each of these creatures feature their own dedicated Al and behave in natural ways. Players must learn their unique behaviors and discover surprising ways to utilize the natural food chain to their advantage and interact with every creature. 

* Organic Puzzle Solving and Progression: The world of the Eternal Cylinder has been designed to empower players to organically solve its mysteries and progress without the need for obvious prompts and mission logs. This allows for fully immersive exploration which rewards players of every skill level, as the greater majority of the puzzles are not required for progression but do provide unique experiences. 

* 4 Unique Biodomes lo Discover ond Explore: Players can explore 4 unique biodomes including alien savannas and infected habitats, each with their own dedicated ecosystems and unique creatures to discover. 

* Truly Emergent Gameplay: The Eternal Cylinder's lush procedurally generated world, vast number of mutations to discover and unlock, unique creature Al system, living natural ecosystem, real-time world destruction and organically placed puzzles combine to create near endless possibilities for emergent gameplay and help to ensure that no two playthroughs will ever be there same.

name: Arise: A Simple Story
detailed_description: Arise is an emotional journey through the bittersweet lives of two people where memories come alive and time bends to your will. Lose yourself in moments of happiness and overcome every hardship as you relive your life’s story. A story of joy and sorrow. A simple story. YOUR ADVENTURE OF LOVE AND LOSS Set out on an adventure through the changing landscapes of memories lush with feelings of love and loss. Every moment of this rollercoaster ride is a new challenge and a chance to see your life in a different light. INSPIRED ARTSTYLE Enter the wonderful world of memories and feelings brought to life by the talented artists from Piccolo Studio. Discover the heartfelt magic in your personal, everyday struggles thanks to the game’s soulful music and beautiful art direction. MASTERY OVER TIME Control the flow of time and change your surroundings from the shifting of seconds to entire seasons. Fast forward, move back or pause time to relive your memories and overcome every obstacle on your journey. PLAYING TOGETHER Invite a second player to help you control time and enjoy the journey together. The easy to pick-up nature of Arise keeps everyone engaged and lets them experience the emotional story to its fullest.

Manipulate time, solve puzzles, reshape surroundings as you push forward into the bittersweet recollections of a past life. This is a story about happiness and hardship, joy and sorrow. _childDocuments_.review: This is a game that deals with the emotions of a loss. I will share that I lost my wife. She was my other half and my best friend. Every day that goes by I feel empty yet I try to be happy as she would want me to be. Playing this game brought so much emotion out of me, both devastation but the happiest of memories as well. To anyone suffering with a loss of any kind, please play this game. You will feel those memories you cherish so deeply but also that feeling of being alone without your loved one(s). To the developers, I just wanted to say thank you for giving me a few hours to feel again and allow me to escape the world for a bit. I want to give this game a 11/10 and I hope anyone that reads this review can understand that through loss you will gain strength. Even though you feel alone you are never truly alone. Arise, as the game's title says.

_childDocuments_.review: Ironic, this game is called Arise yet you’re always falling.Just played this game for the first time not too long ago and finished it a day later. Been listening to the soundtrack a lot since, and I think about this game often. My grandpa died of covid back in November 2020, and I often dwell on what his entire life and memories must have entailed. I miss him a lot, and this game certainly makes me feel that loss, but also lifts me up when I play it. This was one of the most beautiful heartfelt emotional games l've ever played. So deeply touching for me and so delightfully creative. It’s an absolutely beautiful game artistically and story wise. I loved how it dealt with life, first love, happiness, disappointment, finding your own path, loss of loved ones, falling apart but coming back together and in the end the hope that we are reunited in an afterlife. Reminded me of journey a lot but maybe even better. It is fairly hard to describe, but I have not felt so many emotions playing a game in a long time. The only accurate description that comes to mind is the intro sequence to Pixar's "Up". That's how good this game is.The game is roughly 4 hours long. It is a narrative game, but the gameplay mechanics are really neat. You pretty much go through the memories of a man who just died, from his childhood to his death, mostly centered around his love life and hardships. Each level is a stage of his life, where you platform through his memories, while manipulating time and space to platform around the memories.The score is also top notch. The music was just so beautiful.  When they gave you the cartoon drawings that showed his life I could easily just leave it on that screen and listen to the music while admiring the art.When you play coop you have to trust your partner to time the memories just right, otherwise you will fail, especially in sections when you are on a timer. A complete different challenge. The local coop is on purpose, because you have to plan, speak and decide together to succeed. Simple at core, sure but there are layers to it. It feels rare to play a game that really touches you and moves you like this game did.  This game made me want to cherish time with loved ones more because we're all just going through this life and it's not going to last forever.  One day we'll be very old and grey like the main character in this game looking back on our life.  So make the most of your life, live and love as much as you can. It's so nice when a game can really make you feel something and strays away from the typical game models.  Those can be fun too but it’s games like this that really move you and stick with you.tldr: It's one of the most touching games I've ever played. It makes you cherish the people and time you have now.  It's so fu*king beautiful and sad, and beautiful... Everyone who is thinking about buying it... DO IT. It's so pretty, so sad, so amazing... The ending is just chef's kiss... I can't... It's amazing. I highly recommend it for anyone that enjoys a relaxing paced story about love and loss.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to swim against the current here and say that, despite a lovely story, beautiful  artwork, and a compelling soundtrack, I have very mixed feelings about this game, There are some truly magical moments. Most reviews focus on the emotional depth of the narrative (which is powerful) but make little mention of the game-play itself.This is where I have my issue. Arise is not a 'simple story.' It is a precision platformer with some incredibly creative mechanics. You change the environment (winding it forward and backwards) to build pathways. It is a complicated and shadowy landscape with many twists and turns. There is a lot of puzzling your way through, especially if you are looking for memory collectibles. These are often on side paths and are not obvious. I used a controller (the keyboard was not manageable for me) and the right stick shifts the physical landscape. This is quite a departure from other games that use the right stick for scanning or changing direction and it took me awhile to adjust. There is nothing like having a cliff collapse when I hit the stick, thinking I was turning my head! The camera angles are fixed and it is often hard to tell if you are positioned correctly. This resulted in me sending my character leaping to his death more times than I can count. If you do die, the game usually respawns you close to your point of departure.However, there is no save on exit so you are likely to return to a much earlier position than you had hoped for. I ended up playing more hours than I wanted to in order to avoid potentially repeating tricky segments. I am still not sure when the game saves during a chapter.Achievements are by chapter: (1) completion, (2) finding all collectibles, and (3) performing some task (touching things, avoiding things, not dying, etc.). I've already abandoned the idea that 100% is even a possibility for me, as I have died far too many times!I spent hours getting through the first 3 chapters, with success. Then, I hit Chapter 4 which adds running gauntlets of dark sorrows that swarm and kill you. Given the weird camera angle, it was difficult (for me) to run a straight path through them and I got a bit overwhelmed. Later chapters add fire that burns you, cold that freezes you to death if you don't move fast enough, and darkness that overwhelms you. Yikes!I recommend this to those with strong platforming skills and good coordination (using multiple keys or buttons/sticks in concert to perform tricky maneuvers). Most of all, you need more patience than I have. If you are looking for an emotional game to just chill and enjoy, then this may not be the adventure for you.  But, if you are willing to trudge through the hard parts, then Arise is quite a ride!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest, I wasn't sure about Arise in the beginning. I had mixed feelings on if I would like it and the story but I am very happy to announce how wrong I was about Arise. I let it sit in my game library for way longer than I should have. I was pulled into the world of Arise about 4 or 5 chapters in, but even the first few before I was hooked were compelling and interesting to get me to keep playing (I am SO glad I did keep playing). Originally I had some issues with keyboard and mouse, I was struggling to control the character as much as I wanted and figure it out to work smoothly but once I switched to controller, it was peak. Idk if I was just stoned and couldn't make my hands work on a keyboard or what but I would recommend controller for this game!The game pulled at my heart strings, I sobbed twice during this game and I'm not someone who cries very easy. The devs portrayed the story of love and loss so beautifully that I'm in awe of how they accomplished it with no dialogue. Telling a story entirely through music and gameplay is hard but they did it exceptionally well. If you wanna cry and feel like you need to have an existential crisis on true love: play Arise, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Arise: A Simple Story~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Arise is a simple yet clever puzzle-platformer that pushes the puzzle-platformer genre in the right direction. Arise is a soulful, relaxing game that revolves around a man’s journey of reliving his bittersweet memories with his partner. It’s sweet, it’s simple and it’s truly emotionally driven. And combined with its beautiful world and enjoyable gameplay, we have an all-rounder on our hands. Plot: A simple silent man’s journey after his death. Faith has given him another chance of reliving and rediscovering his bittersweet memories. Memories of his life, childhood, his hardships, and most importantly the one person who meant the world to him. The journey won’t be easy; the path will be long, but getting to relive your intimate moments one more time is a blessing that none should refuse. Gameplay: As the title suggests, it’s a simple story of a simple man. But although the gameplay looks and plays out simply, it’s nothing short of a masterpiece. The whole puzzle platformer aspect of the game is presented right from the very beginning, but the gameplay starts out in such a  slow and relaxing way that it took me a while to realize, “Oh! The Game has been going for a while, and I have already walked so far and completed quite a few puzzles without even realizing it”. I had already been enjoying the game, and then realizing how far I’d come blew me away. The gameplay for the most part went about as a simple top-down, side-scrolling platformer, with its basic WASD movement, and space to jump and climb. Everything ran smoothly and efficiently. The star feature of Arise would be its Scrub and Freeze time feature. Scrubbing or freezing time in a game is nothing new and many games over the years have done it right, but Arise just nailed it and took it to a newer level. Scrubbing time; lets you scrub through a limited time period in the game. This can be done everywhere, which works very well with Arise’s puzzles and also its platformer elements. As you progress further and further into the game, you will face new and complex challenges; challenges that consist of creating a new path for yourself, of finding objects that you need in order to progress, of manipulating elements of your will with limited outcomes, etc. By hitting the Arrow key left and right, you can easily manipulate elements around you and create new possibilities for yourself. The game doesn’t have any unnecessary challenges or puzzles; your journey is the puzzles itself, and the way in which you go about using your manipulative powers is the solution. Freezing time; as you progress through the journey, you will be greeted with a new power to aid in your journey; the power to manipulate time. By simply pressing the Arrow up and down keys, you will be able to go back/forth, speed up, slow-down, and freeze time for a limited period in every scenario. This will help you cross more complex challenges as you progress. As you progress many sudden events will take place, which will require you to either slow down or freeze time. The further out you venture, the more you will have to use both of these powers, scrubbing and freezing time to progress and solve all these simple yet clever puzzles.Climbing and grappling; nothing much to say about these two. Both worked as named and both play important roles through the game, both separately and together combined with your powers. Puzzles: I am thoroughly impressed with Arise’s implementation of environmental puzzles and challenges. Each puzzle and challenge played out very well; nothing too taxing on the brain, yet they force you to think outside the box for a little while. Most of the puzzles along your journey consist of figuring out how to create a path, remove or overcome obstacles, and manipulate time in order to interact with elements and solve issues, etc.For someone like me who doesn’t enjoy complex puzzles, this game brought just the right amount of complexity and brainstorming to the table, which I very much appreciated. World design: Cute, colorful, relaxing, and family-friendly. Very well designed and detailed. Although the lighting at places was either a bit dull or too bright, which detracted from a sense of immersion, it was nothing serious. As the game progressed and I was pushed into newer locations, I started to appreciate the level of dedication it takes to make the locations stand out from each other. From snowy mountains to colorful sunflower forests, it was amazing work that brought an enjoyable flair to the game. Music: Brilliant music selection. Relaxing and immersive, it suits the game as a whole, as well as the tone of each scenario very well. Performance: Constant 60 fps without facing any sort of bug, glitch or issue. The only minor complaint that I have with the game is that with certain scenarios while jumping, the camera angles and jump machines don’t work that well with each other. Considering all aspects of the game, Arise turned out to be a great family-friendly platformer. A great combination of silent story, well put-together puzzles and good music selection, making for an enjoyable gameplay. Positives: + Amazing story + Family friendly + Enjoyable gameplay machines+ Good music selection + Simple yet clever puzzles + Beautiful world design + Time manipulation features + Good pricing Negatives: - Awkward camera angles at places - Minor lighting issues at places Faith has given you another opportunity to relive your memories, don’t waste it. Relive your memories with your loved ones one last time. An amazing combination or story, gameplay, feature machines, music and visuals. 9/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: The theme of remembrance is often associated with the idea of being in control of time. One of Kurt Vonnegut’s best-known novels, , is an example of this: it tells the story of Billy Pilgrim remembering his life, and also grants him the power to time travel within the confines of said life, revisiting any of its events, at will.  follows almost exactly the same design document: it has the same central theme and also uses a time manipulation mechanic to deploy it.The game tells the story of an old man at the end of his life, looking back at the most important events that shaped it and himself, and the first thing you’ll notice, mechanics-wise, will be that the right stick, which usually controls perspective, has been repurposed to time manipulation. This means that in this game will be more important to orient yourself in time than in space, which you’ll find quite fitting with the game’s message.Furthermore, the story  tells is said to be “simple” because it is highly symbolical. We know almost nothing about the old man we play as, we don’t know his name, we don’t know when he lived or where, we don’t know what his trade was, we don’t even have proper access to his memories, we only guide him through these highly allegorical representations of key events in his life, each one a level in the game and each described by a single word, a word that may not even denote an event, but, sometimes, ineffably, a “simple” feeling. And in reproducing these feelings lies the true strength of the game: its levels are so well-crafted, so fresh and different from one another, so consistently effective in conveying the symbolism attached to them, that you’ll often feel that you are in the presence of superior videogame craftsmanship.Therefore, the game’s narrative isn’t a novel, or a (short) story, as is usually the case in videogames, but, with the high levels of symbolism it involves, it's actually, more appropriately, a poem. A poem about memory, about how remembering the events of your life, no matter how world-shattering they may have been at the time, can make you discover new meanings for them, truer and more fulfilling. And, in that,  may very well be one of the greatest examples of poetry conveyed with videogame means of expression.

_childDocuments_.review: I generally loathe platformers, even while I love exploration games, and ARISE: A Simple Story is very much both. As such, ARISE: A Simple Story offers something both interesting and challenging, although many of the challenges are indeed the unfortunate result of playing three dimensionally within a two-dimensional game concept.The idea behind the gaming concept / genre of “platformers” is an old one, almost certainly derived from the limitations of early computers: actions take place on the X and Y axes (left/right and up/down), with the Z axis (front/back) disregarded as legitimately being non-existent in the gaming technology of the time. But how long would platformer-playing gamers be satisfied to play based on technology limits largely overcome almost 30 years ago? ARISE: A Simple Story says you can already begin playing a platformer fully with three-dimensional graphics dimensions, even if new limitations and issues arise (since no game is “true” 3D at all as long as it's being viewed on a flat screen)A little background on this beautiful, yet ofttimes maddeningly frustrating game. You are an old man who has died, and in order to proceed, you must collect memories of your life by traversing very beautiful natural landscapes (and beyond. I’m only as far as the fifth level, so I acknowledge my limited exposure.) Each level (so far) uses time manipulation, but in varying ways. In one level, the time manipulated is a single day. On another, time is measured in planetary climate change over millennia. In another, the passage of time measures continental drift over eons. On a new level I've reached, the character traverses giant earthworms...I think. (As a general rule, this concept of time manipulation works better than it likely sounds, but does generally involve manipulating time shifts almost constantly in order to discover one’s options for movement.) By collecting memories, one learns about both the happiness and heartache of life and love. For the most part, once a memory is “discovered” it’s pretty easy to get to. But many of them are very cleverly well hidden in plain sight. And that is a wonderful, usually very effective aspect of ARISE, and possibly reason enough for many of you to wish to invest of yourself in this game, as has been the case for me. (Will the gorgeous settings and fun exploration aspects be reason enough to deal with the many issues, and even finish ARISE? "Time" will tell…)Therein lies one of my biggest issues with ARISE. There is a known quantity of memories on each level, and most of them are found on side paths. Yet it can be frustratingly easy to miss a memory because there is nothing to designate a side path over the main path. Yes, you can reverse your journey to find all side paths, but once you realize you’ve come to the end of the main quest for each level, return seems to no longer be possible. Unfortunately, there is no way to differentiate memories found in the current game vs. earlier games (both simply being shown as found.) As such, there’s no way to be sure how many new memories are left to encounter on a given level without have taken written notes and comparing, and how many are truly newly discovered memories in the currently played game as opposed to previous ones found a second time.Obviously, the very concept of escaping inescapable limitations weighs heavy in ARISE. I can’t begin to count how many dozens (or more likely hundreds) of times I’ve missed a jump simply because it wasn’t strictly “X and Y”, and there is little or no perspective-based information to assist in a safe jump. (After all, nature supposedly has no straight lines, and platformers are based on straight lines determining pretty much every action.) While ARISE presents as three-dimensional, in truth the right stick is exclusively for time manipulation and is absolutely useless for aiding in 3D perspective or to alter camera angle or POV to any degree.(The only exception I've encountered is rare occasions when the suggestion to move the right stick up or down is offered for a slight change in the viewing angle to aid in necessary game progression, but still only X and Y.) As well, you can only see in one direction: straight ahead. So, if you want to look at something you’ve passed, your only option to reverse your POV is to reverse your travels. Not overwhelming once you get used to it, but still very frustrating at times in a game that has such breathtaking graphics and a large degree of originality.Another issue that is very “platformer” is that of checkpoints (which you will need because of the many deaths ARISE’s limited perspective will generate.) Often checkpoints are very reasonable and frequent. Others far less so. (“You listening, lily pads?”) Yes, I have exited out of frustration more than once specifically due to this issue. But you can also use death to your advantage. Since many memories are literally on side treks, it's very often possible to obtain a memory, then die to return to the checkpoint at the start of the divergence from the main path more quickly, and at no apparent price.In summary, this reviewer feels that ARISE: A Simple Story offers enough really good gaming to offer significant respite from what is so bad. Will this be how platformers will be designed from now on? I certainly hope not. Still, it’s enough fun, and original and creative enough that I hope many of its successes will become part of gaming into the future.Thank you and enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this 3-D mostly isometric platformer game is good. It has the potential to be much better, perhaps a sequel. However, its isometric approach to platforming, faux color illusions of 3-D perspectives, and lack of 3-D user-control moved the game from fun to frustration. You will fall many MANY times playing this game. There will be times when you will be guessing which direction to jump - repetitive trials and errors are never fun. Its non-verbal communication storyline was great and should be able to be understood universally -- minimum localization needed. There were many good game mechanics nicely integrated into the story. However, the designers committed overkill with the length of each phase; thus, minimizing the effectiveness of the good game mechanics. For example, in the Fruit game phase, It could have easily been cut in half.  I had enough of jumping after a while. I was thinking to myself, "when will this frik'n phase ever end!?!"A GOOD 3-D platformer is hard to find. Either that, I am just too picky. I would pay over $20 if these designs were remedied.

_childDocuments_.review: You play as an unnamed Old Man who passes away, and in his afterlife, he relives his youngest to most recent memories. What makes this game unique and special is the ability to rewind, fast forward, and stop time at any given moment, allowing you to manipulate landscapes and move from the beginning to the end of each level. Throughout the levels, there are a few collectibles that I recommend checking before you venture into each level, so you don't miss out.It's a simple puzzle-adventure platformer game, but time manipulation is what makes all the difference. The game was a total blast. It's very easy to pick up, gives me a very relaxed and smooth experience with beautiful places to see and experience. Although, sad, it's worth experiencing blindly.   This game features incredibly easy-to-understand visuals that are aesthetically pleasing. The cutscenes are fairly simple and voiceless, yet full of character.Each level feels special, unique, and distinct from the others, while still maintaining a good consistency between them. Lighting also plays a significant role, breathing life into some incredible moments.Every moment I spent in the game was worth taking a screenshot of. It's truly gorgeous.   The sound effects are great. Despite the fact that the character doesn't talk, you can hear him groaning when jumping or during cutscenes, and it's more than enough to understand the feeling behind each moment. Every grab, fall, or moment of effort feels impactful and on point.   The story is rather simple, hence the name, but don't be deceived, as it tells a very touching and sad tale about an old man who passes away and revisits his oldest to most recent memories in the afterlife.Each level shares a compelling moment and piece of information to the story through statues of himself and his wife that he discovers along the way.The old man feels incredibly rich with character and personality even without a voice. It's amazing how the developers managed to convey even the slightest facial animations. Hats off to that performance.   The game is fairly short and unless you miss out some memories collectibles you're basically gonna be able to finish this game between 5 to maybe 10 or 15 hours as I did. It's not difficult, but requires you to think at times and play with the time. The most difficult levels are the last ones where you have to be careful not to die if you want 100% completion. Arise tells an incredible story that will forever remain in my heart. Its art design, incredible songs, and moment-to-moment cutscenes are worth cherishing and experiencing for yourself. It's an amazing game that doesn't demand too much of your time and delivers an incredible puzzle-platformer experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I would really like to recommend this game, as there is certainly a lot of attention to detail in the development. The design and lighting of the levels and the music are beautiful. However, the controls react very slowly and unreliably. The keyboard layout is very unusual and unfortunately cannot be adjusted. In addition, the camera rotation and thus the viewing angle cannot be influenced. For this reason I fell down several times, as it is very difficult to walk precisely in a certain direction with the keyboard, e.g. diagonally down to the left. In the second level I finally got no further because the throwing hook did not trigger, although the target was marked yellow and the instruction "Hold ALT" was displayed. I don't recommend it, because for me it is unplayable with keyboard.

_childDocuments_.review: Piccolo Studio created a visual masterpiece with Arise: A Simple Story and they should be proud of themselves. Just like its name, gameplay and longevity is simple and short. You may get a little bit teary eyed while playing because the game's gist is so sweet. Also, original soundtrack composed by David Garcia Diaz (Rime; Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice) and it's definitely spectacular. Along with the visuals, it's one of the most crucial elements of the game and it's indisputable that I will listen it all the time.If you like Limbo, Ori Franchise, Gris or similar artys games with wonderful soundtrack, please don't miss it. It also looks and plays very well on Ultrawide with a community update. Made the game ten times better.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I wanna say that this is a BEAUTIFUL game. It is very charming, the gameplay is very smooth and there are a lot of unique ideas that makes this an experience worth having. That being said, I just simply cannot recommend this game. This review is written for people who play games with the intention of getting 100% of the collectibles.In this game the main collectibles are memories you can find in the form of pictures that create a slightly more detailed narrative of why you are in the scenario you are, and to find most of these you simply have to follow the level and poke around a corner or 2. However, there are a few that exist seemingly out of laziness, and just simply waste the player's time. Most notably in the first 2 levels: I understand adventure games, or puzzle games, or games similar to those expecting the player to do stuff like this, but I feel like this game is more intended to give the player an emotional experience, and take in some beautiful scenery. I also understand their intention with these placements may have been a reward to people who want to see all of the scenery from all angles, but I just feel like for this style of game that it really falls short, and just really feels like a time-waste. I am already someone who likes to over-explore things. Though I tend to get bored of games really quickly, because I will explore their world instead of actually playing the game, and then decide the game isn't fun. Maybe their thought was to put stuff in these places so players like me feel rewarded for doing that, but in practice it just feels like an obligation. It removes my ability to pick and choose when I want to explore, and when I want to follow the intended flow of the story.Like I said, the game has some unique mechanics, but at it's core it's essentially a walking simulator, with neat mechanics to fill in the space between. They then place some of the memories in places that force the player to have to spend more time just walking, and less time exploring their neat mechanics. This feels very boring, and heavily slows down the pace of the game.If you are someone who just wants to play the game and doesn't care about collecting everything, you will most likely really enjoy this and I would recommend it to you. However, like I said, this review is for people who would start up this game, see there are collectible memories, and feel like they have to find them all. Unless you are someone who has experience with video games and can easily spot when a game is trying to force you away from something, you will most likely end up wasting some time and replaying some of these levels to find all the memories. Replaying levels of a narrative game, with no real reason to replay other than to collect the things you missed because the developers wanted to pad their average play-time.Hide a memory in a cool looking formation, inside a little crevice carved into the side of a wall that most people will not notice, in a section where . Hide a memory in a spot where the game tries to get you to pan the camera, and reward players who look in other directions, hide a memory behind a rock wall in the middle of the level that some players might not look for (this actually does happen). But why, dear god why would anyone think it's a good idea to hide a collectible  Just seems like they ran out of places to put them, and it's really a huge pain in the behind.

_childDocuments_.review: Arise: a simple story is a very soothing and beautiful game where the journey is about an old man reliving his memories at the time of his death and recalling his memories with his childhood friend, lover and wife; and how they have lived with various ups and downs throughout their lives.It's an emotional journey, and how every chapter is dedicated to an emotion that the old man had faced during that years of his life adds a very sweet touch to the game. The main mechanism of the game if time forward and reversing, where you have the control of how time flows and affects the environment around you and using it to solve puzzles. Its very fun and joyful when the puzzles vary wit h each level and how time impacts those of the surroundings as well as the old man's feeling itself.I recommend this game to someone who wants a cozy, pleasing and peaceful game, and wants a simple yet loving tale of a friend, lover and husband and how him and his wife grow through the duration of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm bored.  I typically love many puzzle platformers with such beautiful art and a nice story.  However, I'm not even 2 hours in and it's difficult for me to want to go back and press on.  I'll start with some positives:+Beautiful graphics+Beautiful music+I like the game play here where you can manipulate the environment to progress or solve puzzles (Seasons After Fall comes to mind).  As an example, you can control time in the game and many of the puzzles are quite fun+Many points in the game are, what I would consider to be, cuteThe negatives:-The story is VERY simple.  Now, I understand the name of the game but I didn't realize it would be so literal.  I'm losing interest. -Inability to freely pan the camera to move and look around.  This drives me crazy as you can't really turn your head to look in different directions, rather, you walk there at random often with no real incentive to do so.  It results in awkward game play at a top down 3rd person perspective.  Camera mechanic will often fight against you rather than with you.-Related to above is the memories you collect.  They are often hard to see or find due to the above mechanic.  You can't actively look for them and they are often hidden in areas you'd have no reason to go to for a "core" story moment.  It isn't intuitive at all.-Speaking of memories, currently they are a single fogged out picture.  Would've much preferred a fleshed out animation of the memory to bring a deeper meaning to the story as you play along.  Maybe they "come to life" at the end of the game but I need to be interested enough to get there.  I'll find the belief, within myself, that I will continue this journey as dead Santa and make it to the end to perhaps find something more meaningful in and for this game.  I just wish it wasn't so uninteresting and awkward to play at times.  It is still quite beautiful.  5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Since purchasing this game, I had really only thought that it was a game about the process of grieving and remembering a loved one.  It looked like a cute game with a lot of potential, though I never knew just how wonderful of a game this could be.  Not only does this game explore the grandeur of living life with another person, but it also highlights the hardships that a couple can run into during their lives.  Every moment of this game was thought out and executed very well in my opinion, and I am so glad to have played this game.When I initially purchased the game, I thought this would be a short game that could be finished within a few hours.  This game very well could be finished within a few hours, but that doesn't add in the time needed to gather the memories of the main character's life.  There are 10 chapters in total for this game, and the story literally accounts for every moment of his life from when he meets his significant other, down to his last moments with her.  Every chapter explores a different section of their life, and with it comes the wonders and tribulations of those.  Relationships are something that a lot of people romanticize, and while this game does a little of this, it is nothing but honest about all the emotions people can feel.  Each and every chapter was well-written and flows from start to finish too, so there were no unanswered questions at any point during the play through.The music was beautifully composed for this game, every composition matching the theme of the chapter.  Some of it was gentle, some of it was anxiety-inducing, and other bits were so heart-wrenching.  Of course, there were moments where the music would pause or go into a brief remission, but not once did it get tiresome or irritating because it looped.  This is something that I would absolutely listen to over and over because of how wonderful it was.The achievements were very balanced for the game.  There were the story achievements you got for just finishing the chapter, then you had the memory collecting achievements, and then you had level-specific achievements where you had to complete a task.  Each of these grew in difficulty so there were variation.  This game made it very easy to retry levels to get achievements or to replay the level entirely.  I will say, I would have appreciated a tutorial or a hint saying that I could replay a level by praying at the statue (just like building them) but it was something a quick search found.  I otherwise have no issues.Overall, this is a game that has had so much love, time, and effort put into it, and you can tell that when you play.  Games like these tend to be smaller, but it's worth so much to experience.  Not once were the emotions made out to feel like a burden or made light of, and were given proper tribute to.  I got so much more than I bargained for when I purchased this game, and I'm so glad to have had the chance to play it, especially with how much we are given.  There are some heavy topics that are discussed in the game, so play at your own risk, but I absolutely recommend playing it on your own.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a "yes, but" or a "kind of" option for recommendations. I picked yes because it's quite apparent the developers and artists put in a ton of work on this game and it shows. The story is beautiful, it's anything but simple, and if this doesn't make you cry then I dunno what will. The idea of tying time manipulation into a puzzle platformer was really neat, the puzzles are not difficult. The music as you progress through transition scenes was breathtaking. Little weirded out by the decision to use this guy's sperm as as a platform, if you don't get the connection you're basically platforming in his wife's womb for a level.Why wouldn't I recommend this? The actual game play mechanics leave so many things to be desired, most of all a functioning camera view. The locked camera made some jumps impossible, also the jumps seem predetermined so if you fight the mechanics at all to try and do your own thing you're going to yeet yourself off every cliff and rockface in the game. Not a big deal but a content warning on episode 6 would have been nice, it's only because I usually employ Game of Thrones rules when it comes to happy endings that I already knew how that was going to end (There's your content warning). I also hated level 4, I don't really do well with horror aspects.I had to put the game down several times due to the rage-inducing problem that was the inconsistent fall damage. It's for this reason I would never replay this game or attempt any of the "don't die" achievements. I would never pay $20 for this, but if you can get it on sale it is a pretty game.

_childDocuments_.review: What cannot be written can only be felt.Depending on personal experience, this game can hit like a meteorite upon your earthly heart, killing all the little dinosaurs of your past… and not with malice either; after all, those dinosaurs were relics and memories, people and experiences in your life.Loss is a funny thing because in order to feel it, you must have something originally. You cannot lose what you don’t have. You can close up your heart and not let anyone in and, sure - you won’t suffer as much but also you won’t live at all. So much of popular media focuses on the haves especially when discussing matters of the heart, but they don’t tell you the whole story: they don’t tell how much it hurts to lose those you love, how inevitable it is and how seldom pain of such magnitude can be mended.The silent protagonist is a man stuck in limbo portrayed as a snowy mountain peak of memories. Traverse through his life, his romance and heartbreaks in a poignant tale of loss and hope. Watch him Arise, guided by the soul of his love… and hopefully it’ll make you think of and appreciate those that keep you whole.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding story. Beautiful graphics and chapter locations - I was in awe at the scenery and the creative ideas on how to get around; from jumping on flowers, to spider webs, to flying through fireflies. The story was heartbreaking but very bittersweet. I definitely got teary eyed. One thing I will critique is the lack of room you get after falling down or into water - I wish there was an option to be able to jump out of water before drowning instantly. Same with falls, I seemed to have died in very silly locations from heights that were very small. Other than that, the game was magical. I really liked that it wasn't easy either - the 9th level (the ice I think) was actually very hard to navigate through, but fun nonetheless. If you like games with no dialogue (speaking or text), beautiful ambience, inventive controls and a lovely story; this is definitely the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: It is a short, simple but heartfelt story tugging at your emotions.While from time to time I felt like the game was lacking something or could have been more expressive, the visuals convey the feelings nicely and have some really unique moments and clever usage of its medium. I especially liked how in level seven 7, you move back and forth time as you try to evade both fire and darkness, which conveys that state of being stuck in an emotional rut.It was also extremely buggy for me, and it's hard to immerse yourself in the solemn melancholy of the scene when you're respawning for the dozen's time because the character can't seem to jump over a ten pixel wide gap...All together, while it has its shortcomings it was worth experiencing, and I'm intrested in what the the developers will make next.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does so many things very well. You're going through the memories of the character's life, from birth to death.The themes are mortality and grief, developed in a deep yet hopeful and poetic way.Graphics are great and well-optimized.The gameplay is also well developed as you have control of a window of time back and forth (like Braid for ex.)Do yourself a favor though, play it with a controller and with a 27' monitor at least, the photography of the game is very cinematic, and many times the camera is very far from the character so that the player can better appreciate the environment, but on a small monitor or laptop it's hard to see where you're going.All in all a solid indie game that is worth picking up on sales.7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most gorgeous narrative games I've played. The story is about love, loss and life, it's really emotional and very moving. It's about 5 hours long for the main story, but there are artwork memories to find too, so you can go back and repeat levels to find them if you want to. It's a puzzle platforming game, you manipulate time to change the environment in order to move forward in your journey. There are many checkpoints so if you fail you never go back too far which I liked. The soundtrack and artwork are amazing. Overall, a super beautiful game. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty story-telling game that doesn't rely on dialogue to paint the narrative -  similar to the likes of Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons. The game mechanics are interesting, but also easy enough that you'll be able to navigate most levels quickly and focus on the story elements. Would recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Devs managed to create a game where you become attached to the character. The bond grows stronger with each well placed gesture, change of music and escalating narration. They show, they don't tell. Loved the levels! Each one is a different adventure, set in a unique landscape. You control the environment - fast forward fire to burn the forest and make the road clear, rewind the fire to climb the said trees. Rewind to form snow patches or move insects, then fast forward to ride a log in now melted snow or access a different sunflower with the bumblebee. Got the idea? It gets crazier with gravity affected maps, or with rolling boulders and with so many more episodes!The game has lots of checkpoints, death doesn't slow down progression at all. Maps aren't long either i.e. take about 15mins to complete. Well, longer if you search for the secrets. Some of them are tricky to get and require the said rewind mechanic!The whole style is very cute and colourful, Arise masterfully utilizes graphics all game along. The ice caves, romantic flowers whirls, the thunderstorm chase... great!
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Just like I felt after playing Journey, this is a game that can give you a lot in only a few hours and without any spoken word. The only downside is platforming, which is not that great and can lead to countless jumps into the pit that might break the flow of a really nice story. However, the game generously provides checkpoints and unlimited lives, so you never suffer too greatly from a missed jump. The music (David Garcia) and art style are simply stunning, a real work of art. I can recommend this beautiful game without the slightest hesitation. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays a lot like Journey, but the story and the way it is told really sets it apart. It is both heartwarming and heart wrenching as you relive the memories of the old man you play. Through simple yet elegant visuals and memories collected as photographs, Arise demonstrates that a picture (and an incredible soundtrack) really is worth a thousand words.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: It was a touching and emotional journey. It's a simple story but told powerfully through stunning visuals and sound, with no voice-over. _childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: The music is great and the graphics are stunning, the puzzles are good and involve some fun and original mechanics, the story is pretty good, following a man reliving his life in the limbo and covering some good themes, though unfortunately the platforming gets janky sometimes, and the last levels seem to drag on for a bit too long.Overall a pretty good and underrated game, definitely worth picking up when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice and friendly game that anyone of any age can enjoy. No hard puzzles, no weapons, no grind. One player can play with an X-Box controller, and a second player can join on the keyboard. The one downside, if you want to find one, is the inability to rotate the player view so that you can see behind stuff. The rule is, though, if you can't see it, you can't go there.The concept is innovative, in that you control time to affect getting from place to place. The cut scenes are emotional and sweet. Is it worth $20? Compared with a lot of garbage out there, it is definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: First 7 levels or so, were interesting and fairly enjoyable, but after that it quickly degenerates into an annoying and frustrating experience. Almost gave up with it towards the end. By which point I realised I was forcing myself to keep playing, I was not still playing because I wanted to. The core concept of manipulating time, in order to alter the level, and proceed, doesn't ever get utilised in any particularly interesting way, You mostly move two platforms closer together to be able to jump between them, and that's it. This quickly becomes repetitive and dull. To be fair there are occasions when the time manipulation mechanic, is used in other ways, than bringing two platforms closer together, but not many, and the later examples are just frustrating and annoying. A running theme for this game sadly.  Lining up jumps is often tricky, and judging whether or not a drop is to high and will kill you, is pure trial and error. This starts out mildly annoying in the very easy, first 6 or 7 levels, but then becomes rage inducing during the last levels.With a lot of the trial and error deaths removed, a second playthrough would probably be a more enjoyable experience, but even with collectibles to find, i don't personally think either the gameplay or the story is enough to get me to play a second time. Lastly, be aware that whilst theoretically, this game can be played with a keyboard, I would imagine that it would be an even more frustrating and annoying experience. So the reality is, this is a game you can only play with a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: When I first looked at this I thought it seemed like it had very little gameplay, maybe a go-left game like Inside/Limbo etc and so I didn't buy it.Then I looked at it again and realised it actually does have gameplay so I bought it.Launched it, started the first level and immediately see one of the most innovative and interesting gameplay mechanics I have ever seen in my life and what turned out to be one of the best games I've ever played.You control time within short memories, manipulating it to create a path through the level in various ways. There are only 10 levels but it's made up for by how incredibly unique each one is and on each level you are able to control different aspects of the world by moving back and forth in time - making snow fall in winter to create mounds or water rise in spring to reach higher places, freezing time when lightning strikes to create light, or moving lilypads as they float over the water. The story is told purely through the level design and small cutscenes with the only written words in the game being the names of the levels, a single word each related to what they represent. It's a very sad story but done extremely well and with a good pace. The soundtrack is great as well and really adds to the story told in each level.A Simple Story is a fitting subtitle but not in a bad way. I was able to get this for only £3 because it was on sale in a bundle in the past week, but I would 100% recommend it for more than that, possibly even full price even if it is a bit steep.The uniqueness of the game's design and core gameplay is enough on its own, combined with a really nice story and a satisfying ending it's amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: I'd echo what others have said prior, it's a beautifully done game and one I won't ever forget. A simple story, with simple mechanics, simple visuals, and it comes together perfectly. The soundtrack fits every moment in the game, and yes it's on music platforms to enjoy later (as I have done, and will do). If the chapters in the game don't strike a chord and have you thinking about your own life while playing, they will, at some point. If I could sum up the games message; appreciate the people you have in your life, the moments you share with them, as everything is finite.

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice little game. Controls are really responsive and the game runs and looks great. The music is nice but not memorable. The platforming "puzzles" are simple to solve but still creatively designed and satisfying to get through. I have a few complaints though. Fall damage in this game is absurdly short. Also, when taking most jumps that are more than a hop the character will land and do a little animation like straining to get up or stretching his back. During these couple of seconds the game takes away control from you until the animation plays out. I get why they did it, the character is an old man and its supposed to be cute or something. But it gets old extremely fast and it gets a little annoying because control is constantly taken from the player and no gamer likes that. I still enjoyed the game and recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: All stories don't need words to be impactful,  is a perfect example of that. _childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game. In 5 hours, it treats you to a decent platforming challenge through an engaging story about the life of the old protagonist and his love. The animations are great, the music wonderful, the visuals are truly gorgeous, level design is interesting and with the execption of the first world also nicely related to the story. The game really gave a Pixar vibe everywhere.The puzzels mostly revolve around the ability to influence time. While interesting, I absolutely loved together mode! It allows a second person to take over control over time, which allowed my girlfriend to help me through the story while also keeping her engaged. This made a fun story into an adventure for two. It works perfectly and she loved it as much as I do, especially because she's pretty poor with a controller but this was exactly right for any non-gamer like her. Of course, it also caused the occasional laugh when she moved a platform the wrong way causing me to fall into the void/water/fire/ghosts again. PERFECT addition, that I really recommend to any developer to add. I imagine it can work really well with your kid as well.TLDR: Great game that you should play for the visuals, music and the story. If available, get an SO to control time and have a lot of fun together, especially if they aren't a gamer. At +- 5 hours it is perfect for a lazy Saturday!
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Arise is an amazingly well done game. I'm even more amazed by the fact that it was done by a Polish studio, Techland. Makes me so proud!+ The game has simple yet beautiful graphics. As soon as I watched the trailer I had to add it to my wishlist. I knew I wouldn't be disappointed!+ Very atmospheric, followed by dreamy puzzly stages and a touching story between the couple.+ Soundtrack and sound effects are phenomenal, and add even more feel to the story.+ The concept of rotating the environment by playing with the physics, controlling time and changing seasons, in order for the old man to get from one place to another, is so fun. Love all the particle effects too. Depending on the choices you make, the environment will react to each action differently uncovering new areas to explore.+ Lots of challenging achievements to unlock.- The camera may annoy at first, when you can't zoom in/out to see where your character is heading, but it's something you quickly get used to.The game is worth every penny, so get grab it. If you played games such as Journey or Lost Ember, you will definitely enjoy this one!

_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A deep, emotional journey trhought the life of a man and his family. Arise - A Simple Story is a delicate and yet powerful narrative. Its themes are universal: love, loss, death, and going forward despite the pain that life might bring to you. When the end comes, the only thing you can do is revisiting your memories and be joyful for having them. Life is imperfect, diffucult and sometimes painful, but also full of joy, happyness and people to care for. This game is a celebration of all of this. Gameplay wise, this game is simple but elegant. Everything is well thought and even the collectibles aren't too scattered around the landscape, and add new shades to the protagonist's story, becoming way more than a distraction. Some sections would have benefit a better use of camera and a different palette to improve the platforming experience, but for the rest the game goes smooth as it comes and delivers on many levels. The artistic direction is eye-candy and the soundtrack does an incredible job to accompany the player through various stages of life, loss and hope. You can finish this one in less than 5 hours, but I strongly raccomend the experience. Its themes, visuals and simple but powerful story might be cathartic for many poeple.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A story of one man's life that's anything but simple, told without words, except for the titles of individual chapters. Main mechanic is manipulation of time, not of your actions but in world around you, to open new paths.It is a wonderfully directed journey, at times deeply touching, at times strikingly beautiful, but what makes it special is reflection of man's inner emotions in appearance of outer world, and how well Piccolo Studio managed to interpret those emotions through visualization and music.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Every now and then a game comes along and humbles the hell out you. For someone who enjoys fast paced gaming like Call of Duty it's a breath of fresh air to come back to the basics of what great gaming is, what it looks like, and how it makes you feel. _childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a beautiful game. Lovely art style, nice music, sweet & sad story. However, it definitely has some game play flaws. No way to change your camera view (really needed in a lot of instances).  Collectibles are at times, simply not possible to collect (there was one in particular that was supposed to have had a ledge to access above and no matter which way I manipulated time there was no ledge). At points, you are being overwhelmed by shadow creatures or fire or you are going to freeze to death and there is no way to go off looking for memories, real bummer. That being said, it is still definitely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Arise is a game that tells the life story of the protagonist without a spoken narrative (other then „arise“ being whispered). The story is told by you progressing through 10 levels in total, while being accompanied by really fantastic top notch music (I can‘t stress this enough!). You start with the death of the main character and play through the main events of his former life.To me, it is somewhat of a 3D platformer that does not take a lot of time to play through. You can finish it in one evening, if you don‘t go hunting for each „memory“ of his. While the art style and level design feel childish sometimes (which might have been the intention by the developers here and there), the story and emotions (especially the sadness) expressed in the game are far from being „childish“ and present a view on how troublesome life can really be. Still, some levels are super creative and can offer very unique and satisfying experiences.Sometimes I got a little annoyed. There are very repetitive levels and the magic is gone quickly. Personally, I was longing for at least some narration that is spoken here and there. That is especially true in one particular level where there is a lot of almost meditative moaing and groaing from the main character. It was just too much for my taste and it came across like a meditative asmr audio porn (lol). Furthermore, I had trouble estimating distances, depths etc. leading to failed jumps quite often. The camera movement got a little bit in the way at some points.In the end I still highly recommend playing Arise. It is a quite unique and wounderful experience, holistically speaking. If you enjoy game music a lot, you will definately have a wonderful time with Arise. I only may play it once more with a friend (one using a controller, the other using the keyboard) but I am looking forward to listen to the album over and over again!
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: a story-driven puzzle platformer in which time manipulation is the main mechanic.The soundtrack and graphics are absolutely first class, they do such a good job setting the mood of each level and the overall theme of the game. The story is - as it suggests - very simple, but extremely well told and very affecting, especially as a (relatively) new father. And the way it is told through the mechanics and the levels makes it much more satisfying and immersive. I don't play many platformers so as such I found it to be pitched at a good level - the controls arent very precise and I can imagine a more experienced platform gamer being frustrated by how simplistic it is - but the manual difficulty of the platforming isn't the point, its more about solving a puzzle of how each section works and then actually doing it once you know is very easy. My one major criticism is the "bonus content" - unlockable memories hidden in each level are very fun as puzzles - where they might be hidden, how to reach them etc. - but the actual reward is just a single watercolour picture for each, which made me not really bother with the added difficulty. Overall a beautiful, deeply satisfying game that you can finish in under 5 hours. I couldn't ask for much more.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Arise is an excericise in what it means to live a life.The key feature of the game is the ability to use time as a means to transform the levels. It is a constant back and forth. You make one step after the other to get through the terrain of each level. Each of them has a theme, most of the time revealed at the beginning of the level.Those themes set the mood for the underlying story of each level, while always thinking about the overarching portrayel of the path the chararcter has gone thoughout his life.All levels are distinct from one another, yet share enough similarities, so you have a constant feeling of achieving something with the toolkit you are given throughout the game.The lighting of the levels, the staging of the themes, makes Arise a trinket in it's genre which has many gems.There will be moments, where you will curse the controls, but such is life. Nothing works the way you want it to, almost always. Thats the beauty of games: They don't always move forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is again a case where I wish there was an option to give a neutral review.The game is beautiful and is a work of art.BUT, there is no option to chance controls which is a big problem.And there is no real camera control which is also a problem because perspectives are not always clear.beside that it is also short and pretty easy.I'd suggest buying it on sale only.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, moving, narrative led story with outstanding art direction and a memorable score. As you play Arise, you'll accompany a recently deceased man as he wanders through his life story and journey through past experiences of love, loss, and hope. Mostly told through flashbacks and without dialogue, this is a tight adventure that one could finish in one or several play session. There are a few sections with somewhat tricky platforming, but it will not be very frustrating to a majority of players. If you're a fan of Journey, Gris, or Abzu this game should be a must play!
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story
