_childDocuments_.review: I'm sad I couldn't get into this game. I got as far as Level 2 and then just gave up. Though I didn't play much, I could see myself liking the story. The style of the storytelling worked for me and the orchestral music was particularly beautiful. (Even looking at a full gameplay video right now, I think the music throughout is sublime.)My main impression of Level 1, however, was "boy, these controls feel clunky." Especially jumping. Then I got to the end of the level and realised I had missed out on some collectible memories.Ah, so there's hidden areas to find.When the controls aren't tight, you don't want to explore - why prolong that experience? The movement just isn't natural. It feels like a slog, and I didn't even play it for that long! The world feels too big to walk around.I thought to myself "okay, just get used to it. You'll become more familiar as time passes by."But then in Level 2 the grappling hook control started failing. While it was fiddly before, now it simply didn't work.Okay, okay, fine. Switch to keyboard controls.It was successful for one grappling hook and then it failed again. That's where I gave up.I'll hold my hands up and say that it was probably an issue on my end. Yet the thought of continuing the game even if I fixed the problem was unappealing. I couldn't be bothered to work with the mechanics and extend my playtime to get all the memories.It doesn't seem right to leave a negative review. My experience wasn't great, so I can't recommend Arise based on that. The gameplay just doesn't cut it for what you're expected to do, in my opinion.But I suppose if you can quickly adjust to the controls and you don't care about 100%, you will like it. The story and music do stand out.

_childDocuments_.review: Arise is a game I wish there was a "Maybe" rating for. Arise's gameplay has some undeniably unique and fun platforming with time manipulation mechanics where you can reverse or fast forward time, most strikingly during sequences with a wildfire spreading back and forth, pausing time when lightning is flashing in order to nullify creeping ghosts surrounding you, and arranging a crumbling mountain canyon to be able to platform through the environment amid the floating, locked-in-place pieces.The part of the game I found quite lackluster and frankly annoying by its conclusion was the delivery of its story. Although some sequences are more subtle and metaphorically presented visually (the conception / birth sequence comes to mind..) other moments are so glibly presented they come off as "baby's first college research paper" as you watch the character chortle incessantly while jumping on platforms made of spiderwebs and flowers, hang his head, slump his shoulders and sigh for the fifteenth time, or spin through the air while holding his love's hands as a sweeping, over-the-top soundtrack blares in your ears for far too long. The story does take a surprisingly dark turn I was not expecting that I give it credit for, and its explorations of grief, loss, hope, love, and perseverance are subjects I think more games should address, but something about the delivery here is far less profound and insightful than the game keeps patting itself on the back for as it drags on and on, beating you over the head opining that it  is that deep before taking a pretentious bow expecting to be showered in roses and uproarious applause.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: It looks nice.It plays *very slow*.It's basically a walking simulator but in which you can miss a jump and have to do a bit again.The beginning is weird (I saw another review where someone had just given up at this screen) in that the "tutorial" icons show "press left arrow and right arrow alternately at about 0.5 second intervals" and if you do that it's not at all obvious that they're doing anything - what you actually have to do is press and hold right arrow for like 5 seconds to make anything significant happen.The fact that the game has to constantly prompt you throughout about what keys to press and when is a good indicator that the controls and actions aren't intuitive or meaningful.The title of the game does make it reasonably clear ("a simple story") that you're not really going to be playing a game, but as someone who likes to be playing a game, I'm giving up on this after one-and-a-half sections, it's clearly not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game excellently masters its storytelling with its in-game graphics. The parts that are joyful are beautiful, brightly colored, and all-around fun to navigate. The parts that are deep and dark feel nerve-wracking and as though death was one jump away. I want to compliment this game on how well you get sucked into what the character would actually be feeling at that exact moment. You’re struggling through this… emotionally and mentally challenging experience, right alongside him, and with every failed attempt, you get back up and try again. I honestly felt eager to get to the end. Not because I wanted it to be over, but by the fifth chapter in the game I was so invested that I needed to know how it ended. I will say that you pretty much know how it ends around 2/3rds of the way through, but, it was still a great experience nonetheless. Every part of this game was fun, mentally engaging and sometimes a little challenging. You’re not only controlling your little person and moving about the world, you’re also controlling the time. While I didn’t find it incredibly difficult to get the hang of, it did take a bit of getting used to to get the controls down, and there were still plenty of times that they were the death of me. I want to give this game props because while the gameplay stayed similar in each chapter, they were all so drastically different graphically and in how they traversed and navigated. It was incredibly fun and kept me from growing bored with it. Another gorgeous aspect about this game is the music. You’ll go from dark drum beats to dancing violins, to sad piano and everything in between. Sometimes games have those soundtracks that you get sick of half-way through the game but this one made me want to turn it up. It does a great job of translating the mood of the chapter and bringing you that much deeper into it. Honestly, I’d rate this game pretty high. It only took me about 4 hours to beat and that’s not incredibly long but the depth and detail at which they suck you into it was great. I got this game on sale, packaged alongside another game by the same publishers, and I definitely consider it a great buy. I adore story-led games with puzzling gameplay that challenges the brain… and this delivered. It made me giggle, gasp, and screech in misery at the saddest of moments. Any game that can give you that sense of childlike wander is money well spent in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: Arise tells a very beautiful and emotional story about the life of an old man and his wife, throughout a short 4 hour campaign, and it does this very well. Not only is there a lot of emotional impact for each story beat, but the gameplay isn't half bad either. While similar games that focus on emotional storytelling might fall short in terms of satisfying or fun gameplay, Arise manages to avoid this pitfall. This game offers an interesting time manipulation mechanic, in which you can move time forward and backward to do things such as melt snow in order to raise the water level, which makes this a quite competent puzzle platformer. The game also has a beautiful soundtrack which serves to enhance the story telling and gameplay in interesting ways, without the need to say a word. Over all, I highly recommend this game, both to those who want a story that will make them cry a little, and to those interested in playing a simple, but interesting puzzle platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: Arise: A Simple Story is a slow 3D-platformer with a very nice low-poly aesthetics where you go through the memories of a dead man experiencing his greatest joys and darkest times before he passes on to the afterlife. The main gimmick of the game is the ability to affect time to a limited extend; having it go faster, go backwards and stop it completely. You must use these abilities to get to the end of each stage of the man's life.The game holds some replayability in the form of collectible memories and certain achievements requiring you to interact with things in the levels a lot or completing some levels without dying once.Overall I'd say the emotional journey you go with the main character is the game's strong suit with the gameplay being a bit eh sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute graphics and it sounds like there's a great soundtrack. I would not recommend playing with a keyboard. The game does not allow you to rotate the camera, it does it for you. This causes a problem because the platforms you have to jump on to are not pure north, south, etc; most of them are a little off. Pressing a combination of the WASD keys while jumping does not work as well as some of the other games I've played that have similar key controls, and I ended up missing most of my jumps, falling into the water, and being forced to start again from a checkpoint. It also "allows" you to move the camera angle to above your character to see the platform puzzle, but it only gives you like five seconds before automatically readjusting to the normal angle, then you have to readjust it again. I probably could've probably stuck around to figure it out better, but it annoyed me too much. If you have a controller it will most likely work better (if the game supports controllers, I didn't check). I'd recommend getting it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to put into words how this game has made me feel. It only has titles and imagery throughout, no dialogue, and yet I'm so mesmerized by it. It has uplifting moments that are filled with hope and curiosity, combined with one of the most intense, but simple stories. This game is now and will always be one of my favorites. The soundtrack is the voice of this game that helps to progress and express with divine instrumentals. I have played this game with my love and it's been an incredible experience. The co-op gameplay is extremely unique and executed well. We're able to play our parts at the same time and the game flows seamlessly. If you have problems with not being able to control where your screen is looking, consider playing an FPS or any game with free-roaming capabilities. Having a fixed screen isn't a new concept and I would encourage you to look past that to give yourself the chance to experience this game at least once. Arise is very special to me and I highly recommend it to any and everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: As the title says, this is a simple story.A story about love, loss and coming home.Told through memories, wich come in hand drawn pictures to collect.The music is soft and orchestral, sometimes even reminding me at the Harry Potter soundtrack.One thing I had problems with was the detection of the player inputs.With them sometimes not, or not precisely working, it got a bit frustrating for me.Also that our guy is dying by falling from quite little heights sometimes felt a bit strange, as I guess he was something of a viking or northman. Though I guess it makes sense narratively, as this is all a dream.-The owls simply approve.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly unsure what to say about this game. Despite it being labelled as a "Simple Story" practically every little detail in the game, from the music to the visual design is overflowing with the theme and symbolism of the level you're playing. While the story itself is a fairly straight forward tale, its told in a way that makes is very easy to relate to what the player character is experiencing. 10/10 would bawl my eyes out at this game again.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A simple story. That's about right. Relive the life of the protagonist as he revisits the key moments of his story before passing on to the great beyond. Sweet, heartbreaking, emotional, brief, and well done. Depending on where you are in your life and how you might relate, expect to shed some tears.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: I would always recommend these kind of good narrative games with cute art design and great soundtracks.The twist here is that the right stick controls time (to put it simply), which creates a lot of original and creative ideas. The cameras being uncontrollable make some of the platforming experience a bit annoying but nothing terrible.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful little game. Not too difficult, but really inventive mechanics and fantastic synergy of graphics and music. At first I thought the local coop was a bit forced, but I soon discovered it was actually really fun to play together, with one person controlling the main character and the other the flow of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Experience a haunting journey through life and beyond in this emotionally gripping video game. As you navigate the memories of a man, you're drawn deeper into his story, only to realize the profound truth awaiting at journey's end. In the final scene The main character finds solace and is a poignant reminder of love, and loss. Prepare to be moved.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Great game but with game breaking bug (spider web jump). Tried methods from official forums and non of them helped. I know that it`s working on some systems and isn`t on others, but I have this problem and it isn`t fixed and developers says that they do not know how to fix it. I will gladly change my review to positive when the problem will be solved.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a blessing, truly a gem among all the endless cutscene, gore and violence games. It was absolutely beautiful and I loved the new bits of mechanics you'd develop over time. The idea of time-control is well done and reminded me of Life is Strange but in a way better and more complex way. I loved being able to play a game again which is about gameplay rather than text after text after text. Without a word, I could follow the whole amazing but sad story. Every level fascinated me and made me cry from time to time. I wish to see more games like this one in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Its a cute game, certainly worth the $4 I gave for it, and I do recommend it. You can tell it was created with a lot of passion. A short but sweet title, and yes, emotional. I do have one nitpick that should be addressed though... The majority of the story should not be told through memories that you have to search for, rather than find along the way. The story will lose a lot of magic if you play like me and don't search hard for them. The only way to get most of these memories (aka the story!)  is completing puzzles that are off the beaten trail and are easy to miss. Therefore I cannot recommend this game for $20, its just not a great game-model for storytelling if you're not told upfront about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Basically what it says on the tin. This is a fantastically artful game that will make you happy to have working eyes and ears.It is technically multiplayer, but the other player plays as the other half of the single player mechanics. By yourself, you run and jump and control time, in 2 player, you run and jump and your friend controls time.Based on it's release date, if I had to guess, this game was originally going to be longer. The entire story focuses on the Old Man's relationship with his SO - which is fine, and very beautiful. Though I did find myself wondering if there was going to be more at one point when it didn't really get explained how he found himself in a community of people towards the end.Really, a forgettable hiccup that's mostly subjective.Very well made. Worth your money.I bought this at a discount for 3$ and I feel thoroughly guilty for doing so.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful story, with new puzzle mechanics added on to each level and then wonderfully intertwines them along later levels. It has some curve balls to throw you off here and there and some portions that take 2-3 tries before understanding what to do. It had great artwork and music and I'd recommend this to any kind of gamer out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me cry, think of my past relationship, kept me completely occupied for the time that I played it, and genuinely left me speechless. I was gripped by the story and amazed by the beautiful graphics (not to mention the fantastic soundtrack). I thought that the ending in particular was an amazing way to end things off; it really was a short story with an opening that garnered curiosity and an ending that left you fulfilled. If I could, I would play it for the first time again. TLDR:10/10 story telling10/10 graphicsBuy it
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: With over 100 games in my library this is the first time i felt compelled to write a review. What a great game, clever mechanics, emotional story complete with perfect orchestral music bringing story and game play together. It may be short to many other games {completed in just under 5 hrs) but so worth it and a huge recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: This has got to be the best $3.99 I ever spent on a game. The scenes are beautifully done, the soundtrack is mesmerizing, the gameplay itself is smooth. I don't understand why it's only $3.99. For that price, I didn't expect much going in, but I am quite literally blown away by it. This game is HIGHLY recommended!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Big maybe. First, use a controller. It's fine, just some choices they made (I'll get into below because spoilers) I felt were hindrances.  Also some of these achievements are just time-wasters, they are just "do stuff 50 times" "do more stuff 100 times". Really dev? I'll get into some spoilers blow later once I updated this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Arise: A Simple Story is just that. A simple but good story. I had some fun playing this game, but I did have a few complaints. My complains lie within the camera control and fall damage. As a 3D platformer, you should have a good amount of control of the camera, but this game lacked that in many cases, making some jumps and movements horrible becasue I couldn't tell where I actually needed to move. The fall damage/death was also annoying in several instances.But besides those two issues, the game was still pretty good. The art style was it's largest strength, as it's just so beautiful. The soundtrack was also very enjoyable. The game's story was pretty simple and easy to understand, and I think it did a great way of telling it.Overall a 7/10, not the best game ever, but certainly not a bad one.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Beat it in this time^ with about half of the collectibles. WOW. It is a beautiful story telling experience. Very innovated method of navigating the levels, has the right amount of tension in some places, invokes feelings, and makes you WANT to find the collectibles when possible because of what they reveal. Story is simple, and makes you feel things. Artwork is beautiful and the use of light in this game is superb. 12/5.Would recommend to everyone. If you are a streamer looking for a nice one-shot game or to break it up in two streams, this game work nice for that. Soundtrack is on my spotify playlist now. Thanks for that guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. The orchestration is great. The time dilation mechanics are used in a variety of ways and are smooth and easy to figure out. I did start with keyboard and mouse but i switched to controller, as I found some angles easier to navigate with the joystick. It is a very pretty game that evokes feelings appropriate to the level's theme. There was a lot of time, love, and thought put into this game. It is not a lengthy game. You can expect to spend between 4.5 and 7 hours in game, though it could be longer if you want to touch every corner. Many 'memories' are easily in hand, while others are in classic video game misdirection, hidden corners, etc. TLDR: beautiful, short in a good way, natural progression, and a genuinely great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game about the life of a man with a great mechanic of time alteration. The musical score carries the game far as does it's exceptional lighting. It does suffer from some clunky jumping mechanic and sometime difficult camera angle making the platforming experience frustrating at time at least on a keyboard. I could not try it with a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: It's gorgeous, like playing through a Dreamworks movie! Using time to solve the puzzles in the levels is pretty cool, and the challange is most of the time figuring out how to do it. There are a few slight elements of time critical moves sometimes that are a bit stressfull. And honestly sometimes dying was annoying. Still, beautifuly made.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A game that focus on delivering a great story, unfortunately, the story peaks mid game but you will start losing interest right after that. gameplay is average and movement fells clunky sometimes.But the music on the other hand, is top notch and touching. as will as the level designs that are refreshing and colorful. Achievements are easy if you follow a guide. and the game is always on huge discounts.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A really beautiful game. It has a wonderful story. Simple, yes, but relatable, and altogether human. It hit wonderful emotional beats as you progress through, and you can see the love, grief, and hope despite the relatively simple figures and visuals. I loved it, thank you to the developers!If I were to critique the game, it would be on control and camera positioning. Playing on a keyboard I was moving the character primarily in the 4 cardinal directions and their diagonals, but the camera often made it difficult to understand if a platform was positioned directly next to the character or diagonal from him, so I ended up jumping into the abyss somewhat frequently. Maybe if I could nudge the camera a bit manually I could have better understood the 3d positioning. Being a completionist/collector, I played most of the early levels trying to search out the hidden Memories, but I found that was actually detracting from feeling connected to the story. So I stopped searching so hard for the memories and I feel like that's the better way to play your first time through, then you can go back and get the memories on a second play.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Arise is not only a simple story... but a beautiful one at that. Love, struggle, grief are themes in this story that we can all relate too. This game has such a unique mechanic of time manipulating objects and environment to help you progress through the journey. The graphics are STUNNING! This is a game that will make you go WOW! If you're looking for an easy, relaxing yet heartwarming puzzle adventure, do not hesitate! The game does go on sale quite a bit so look out for that too.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Extraordinary! Beautiful, beautiful couch co-op game with high art 3D graphics, flawless animation and cinematic music score. One player controls the character in third person while the other player controls the flow of time, and thus, the scenery. Flawless co-operation is the key, but even failures are fun. Lighthearted and romantic. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful visuals, audio and story. My only complaint would be the controls if you're using keyboard. Sometimes there's some nice challenge stemming from the dexterity required from manipulating key combinations, similar to Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons, but other times gameplay greatly suffers from the limitations of keyboard controls in a 3D environment. Especially when the automatic camera movements suddenly changes the trajectory of the key you're pressing. So yeah, I'd play it with a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Wow was I not expecting this game to be the experience that is was! At base level, this is a story driven traversal game with a few "puzzles" along the way. I will give you a fair warning: this is an emotional one. Follow the path of a man who has lived a long life and is now traversing the after life to be reunited with his family. Experience all the ups and downs that life can bring as he re-encounters all the different chapters in his life. There isn't anything too difficult about this game other than getting used to the mechanics. I did really enjoy the time manipulation mechanic in this - this is what creates 'puzzles' through out the game. The art is beautiful. The music is an integral voice in this game. There isn't any dialogue, which makes this journey hit even harder sometimes. Overall - 10/10. I truly and deeply loved this game. It may be 'a simple story' but it was a beautiful and heartfelt one. I will be achievement hunting in this one for awhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is a moderately challenging platformer with time manipulation as its main mechanic for solving puzzles. The art style is pleasant with its soft edges and dreamy lighting. The soundtrack is equal parts beautiful and sentimental, which works in a game like this. I highly recommend this game for people who are looking for a short, relatively easy, and kind of touching experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: If you think the movie UP for the first 10 minutes will make you cry - try again... This game will make you cry regardless of how the ending goes. If you don't cry then you don't have a heart LOLThe game has an amazing sound track, wonderful art and great mechanics. This game deserves a 10/10 stars for sure and would highly recommend it to all my friends.As one of my friends would say, this game is definitely "emotional damage" for your heart and soul.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted this game for a while before I eventually bought it and I was not disappointed. The art style is beautiful, the soundtrack really sets the mood, and the core mechanic, though it is used throughout the game, has enough variation that it never gets boring or tedious.You essentially get control of a slice of time and moving it forwards and backwards alters the environment to create a path forward. There are a few different creative uses of the same mechanic, from moving platforms to changing the weather and another level where you need to stay within a light that's guiding you through the dark. The hidden memories give you reason to explore paths that are not the obvious way forward though I'm not a completionist so I won't be going back for them all.I would definitely recommend Arise for anyone that enjoyed games such as Gris where the art and creative use of the environments make up a huge chunk of the experience. The puzzle and platforming element is satisfying and the story is simple and short but engaging. It's difficult to fault this game. Being picky I didn't like the ice sections as much but it's all part of the challenge. I also wouldn't say the game has much replayability either apart from trying to get all of the collectibles.If in doubt get it on sale but if you like arty puzzle platformers you are going to love Arise.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Good ideas, fantastic score, but faulty gameplay (atleast on PC). Thelast level is particularly terrible with it's "follow-the-light" mechanic which prevents you from collecting memories and the restarts after dying makes it almost impossible to folow.The auto-orienting camera makes it hard to estimate where and how far objects are. A short hike made it really good imo.Overall, an amazing game with little frustrations here and there.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Arise: A Simple Story is a beautiful, heartwarming, and thought-provoking game that will stay with you long after you finish playing it. The game tells the story of a man who travels through different stages of his life, from childhood to old age, using the power of time to overcome obstacles and reach his goals. Along the way, he reminisces about family, friendship, and love.The game is visually stunning, with a minimalist art style that perfectly captures the beauty of the natural world. The music is also beautiful and atmospheric, perfectly setting the tone for each scene. The gameplay is simple but engaging, and the time-manipulation mechanic is used in clever and creative ways to solve puzzles and progress through the game.But what really sets Arise: A Simple Story apart is its story. The game is full of heartwarming moments, but it also deals with some difficult themes, such as loss, grief, and death. The game never shies away from these difficult topics, but it always does so with a sense of hope and optimism.Arise: A Simple Story is a truly special game that will stay with you long after you finish playing it. If you are looking for a game that will touch your heart, then Arise: A Simple Story is a must-play.If you are looking for a game that will touch your heart, then I highly recommend Arise: A Simple Story.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Really loved how the 3d puzzle/platformer mechanics fit so well with the narrative of this bittersweet story, enhancing the power of the tale been told. Some moments have been really exhilarating (when you get to the end of the Romance chapter you will know what I mean) and others have definitely made me shed a tear. The sweet and melancholic mood is consistent all throughout the game, with the up and down story beats just where they had to be, and the beautiful art and soundtrack really helped at that. The mechanical peculiarity of each level made it so that the game was never boring, and made the experience engaging all along.I just wish the studio had been a bit more brave with the kind of story they wanted to tell, but... after all, it's a simple story, and perhaps that's exactly what makes it so powerful. Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: "We are made of memories"And as you go through the game story you can experience grief itself even by not losing anyone yet. Grief is way beyond a human being but any type of loss. The game story is awesome and character helps on feeling like in his shoes despite of not having any dialogue. At some point his tiredness became mine as I walked through the different episodes. Graphic design is simple yet vibrant and alive. Not much content is required and it achieves the expected environment. Music and sound effects are thrilling and touching. I can say that, from a UX experience the game is surrounding and immersive.Yet, from as game play experience I do have some details I would change to make the game even better:- Once you finish a chapter there is no way to turn back.   This means that, from a collector's perspective and kind of the point of the game of gathering memories if you didn't find all memories in a chapter you're done. This is slightly frustrating and some chapters are really challenging and all you want is to get through it. IF you are an experienced gamer this may not sound too biggie but still, it would be awesome to get back after you pass the chapter and search for the remaining memories not found at once.- Camera rotation:  Camera rotates automatically as the character walks but based on above mentioned if you can't go back on searching it would be awesome to look your surroundings and catch those hidden memories. Enjoy the game, give it a try and good luck!

_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Arise: A Simple Story is a beautiful game that manages to tell the story of a man's life using only pictures and metaphors. The puzzles aren't too challenging, but are still enjoyable enough. I personally couldn't continue past the 7th level because it hit too close to home, but I will say if anything that it depicted the experience of grief and moving through it very well. _childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game- very artistic in both the looks and story telling. It hits a lot of boxes for me, in that the visuals, and music, and themes of the levels set a mood, and tell a story the puzzles bring you through. I really enjoy visually beautiful and stylistic games that have a melancholy or emotional story with game-play that is interesting and plays into that. The time mechanic was really neat- it did a really good job starting off really simple and got more complicated. Not dropping you in the deep end but building in a way that felt pretty natural and adding more complicated ways of using it. Lighter emotional levels had more simple uses of it, and more emotionally turbulent-themed levels had a more complicated use. The first level was pretty dull, but when you consider it is both a learning level and that its symbolically simpler cause hes a kid, it bothers me less now looking back. My only real complaint is that the controls can occasionally be a bit wonky, in that you can sometimes hit a button and keep going in the same direction following a path and then it will decide it doesn't follow the path automatically and jump off whatever object you were on. Also there were a few times the camera angle was annoying and there is not many ways to adjust it to be better that I found in the moment (I only found a vertical adjustment and it snapped back in place after a tad, no promises I didn't just miss something though). Also a few times where the field of view made jumps unclear if they were possible or not.Over-all, I really loved the game and am very happy I got it. It was a really fun and whimsical journey of love and loss with an interesting game mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, sweet little game to waste an afternoon with. Nothing groundbreaking but pretty good for what it is. Keep in mind that it's still mostly a walking sim with a couple of cool mechanics and very simple puzzles. Even if you love these types of games, I don't think anything here will blow you away so manage your expectations accordingly.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A short and beautiful adventure that albeit cliche in it's story can still move you with it's beautiful music and environments. For a puzzle platformer the way forward is in most cases relatively straightforward, so it doesn't require too much thinking, however the mechanics of the game are still interesting enough to keep you engaged. Each level is visually distinct, and although the mechanic is the same throughout, the gameplay is unique to each level. Sometimes you manipulate the seasons, sometimes floating lillypads and other times a sea of fire. Although you press the same buttons it feels refreshing each time. What does not feel as good however is the poor depth perception that sometimes makes you under/overshoot a platform, leading to you falling to death. Luckily respawns are generous but it happened so often that it kinda worsened the experience. Performance and polish are great though, so apart from the platforming the game plays very well. It's a nice relaxing experience for those seaking one. It's pretty short though so the game is best purchased on a sale. Along with it's soundtrack, as that together with the visuals is this games biggest strenght.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a phenomenal work of art. The silent story telling, the beautiful art style, the fun puzzles, the gorgeous environments and ambiance. Every level is a level deeper into knowing the main character and his love for his wife. The ups and downs of their lives together. I smiled and cried so much while playing this. I cannot recommend this game enough. The character's love for eachother is unmatched and the devs really encaptured their love across this entire game. Got it as a gift and I more than loved it!! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: A really well thought out and well designed platform game. It has a different mechanical style from other games. It's confusing at times and can be really frustrating. The atmosphere of the game is beyond great. The story is beautiful and at the same time very sad. Some of the achievements are very challenging. You have to play the episodes over and over and it can get nauseous after a while. Whether it's the music, the game design, the visuals, the story, they're all beautiful. If you buy the game on sale, I recommend it to everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Do you ever get stuck feeling lost, numb, and jaded to everything? Feel like your empathy- your ability to feel SOMETHING has left you forever? Play this. Pick a day when you don't have much to do and play this. I felt so empty and devoid of anything. Yet somehow Arise: A Simple story manage to yank the feels choking and sobbing right out of me. It's time. You've earned the right to feel something <3
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful visuals, a even more beautiful soundtrack and a story that will leave you crying at the very end. What more could you ask for?Again the visuals are so beautiful the story telling done by just visuals alone and then you have the musical tracks that add so much to what is happening and are more then a joy to listen to!
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: an arty, story-driven, combat-free 3D puzzle-platformer in the vein of games like Journey and GRIS, with its central gimmick being the use of the right analog stick to rewind and advance time. not at the top of its class in a subgenre I'm quite fond of (the platforming doesn't feel as tight as it should, and the fixed camera angle makes it more difficult than it should be to gauge distance when platforming), but the time-manipulation puzzles are generally pretty fun and the story, while not terribly original (the "simple story" part of the title isn't an exaggeration), is fairly well-told through gameplay, with a genuinely touching ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from some technicalities such as difficulty to grasp some climbing paths or placement of some collectibles on some levels, I would say this is a sublime atmospheric story-driven experience. The scenery, the colours, the sound all converge to form a deeply moving interaction and I strongly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Arise is a puzzle platformer that utilizes a time mechanic for each of its ten levels. You manually rewind and/or fastforward time for various different reasons to interact and progress with the levels, each in their own unique way. The soundtrack is gorgeous and compliments the levels and events that take place, reacting to the actions that take place dynamically. Each level displays wonderful visuals through the game's art style, and many of them have details in the animation that meld with the story and character. The game features an optional mode called "Together Mode." This feature allows two players to play the game; one player controls the main character and traverses the level as normal, while the other focuses on manipulating time to help their partner with the level. A habit players who are at all familiar with platforming will already have the habit of waiting to jump until they're at the very edge of a platform. Due to the game's short delay between jumps, this will usually lead to death. Most jumps are distanced to reach gaps normally though. Regular playthrough may give you 3-4 hours, while focusing on the collectibles or going for the game's achievements may net another two or three hours. A wonderful experience for a relaxed state of mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Havent finished it but the ambience sounds, music, animations, coloring, all absolutely perfect, the story is  simple but engaging and beautiful. The only thing I would change is the unlocked memories that had their own background music which is messes with the mood of the actual music happening before the memory.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really nice little game. It's a simple story, but effectively told. There is ten levels, each with a different style, which made it interesting from beginning to end. The gameplay loop is engaging enough that it doesn't become boring and the soundtrack was really good too. It's a perfect game for the Steam Deck!
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game with a bundle, without thinking anything of it.  Decided to play it to de-stress and see if it was worth buying.  My gawd, I experienced the roller coaster of emotions:  From curiosity to joy to sadness.  I really recommend playing this game, can play this in less than 5 hours.  Controls can be a little janky, but the artwork and how the story is told is just amazing.  8/10, definitely recommend playing
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a work of art. The story ending hit me hard. I sobbed and cried. I few minutes later trying to explain the story to my husband i burst out in tears again. the game play is fun and engaging, nothing repeats and there are puzzles to tickle your noodle , yet very relaxing. The music is fantastic. The message is powerful.Took about 6 hours to play through. Very impressed with the level of emotion and game play put into this . _childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: I was absolutely hooked from beginning to end. The graphics are absolutely stunning, the music is beautiful, the story is emotional, gorgeous and engaging. The levels are well designed, interesting and challenging, sometimes a little fiddly but not impossible – the checkpoint placement and frequency is great for times when you need to make a few attempts. Hoping to try co-op with friends.The only drawback for me was the limited camera manoeuvrability which was a little frustrating at times but understandably done to add to the challenge of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Short but really pretty, and a pretty relaxed experience (except for the one mildly spoopy level).  The time mechanic is neat and used well in level design.  Music is lovely.  Took around 4 hours to complete my first playthrough, without going after all the extras.  Not sure I'll bother to go get all those extras, but I enjoyed it.  Worth the price on sale, but I would have been a bit disappointed at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I hated this game the entire time I played it, but I have to recommend it on principle: it works, it is what it says it is, supports Steam Cloud, controller, multiple languages, co-op with Remote Play, Steam Deck, you name it, it's got it.But aside from checking all the boxes, this game actively fought me from enjoying it beginning to end. You play as an old man with incredibly weak ankles for a guy who can jump his own height, because your character will die constantly by falling off off low ledges and venturing too near shallow water. But that's cool because you can rewind time! Except you can't when you're dead, which is a cardinal sin in time manipulation games. Because I am alive, the player, and replaying the same sequence over and over again just to miss the same jump because of questionable level design SUCKS.There are two EASY ways at ready to solve this problem: 1) let me rewind the mistake, or 2) immediately respawn me where I last had solid footing. Nobody's got time for a slow death animation.Despite what the reviews say ( of players have bothered to finish the game), I found the game with a collectible run far too long at just under eight hours. Not a single one of the game's 10 levels felt fun owing to the sheer amount of dying I had to do to complete each one. Cue achievement to beat a crap level without dying! Oh, I see you also have a bunch of achievements to do X thing Y times? Do not pass go; GO DIRECTLY TO HELL.If you're a fan of time manipulation platformers, whatever. You'll be happy this is in your collection in that it's a good looking game worth its market price. You're supporting an indie developer, so good on you because you are the ones I am recommending the game to. For everyone else? 4/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The end of a life is not necessarily the end.  Waking up from what you assumed was your last moments you find yourself going back through your life; from your youth to your old age alongside the woman that you love.  Here you remember your journey and make sense of life before the final goodbye.Arise A Simple Story is a narrative third-person platforming game which focuses on a very human story.  You play as an old man who dies and finds himself in Limbo where he goes back through his life chapter by chapter.  You follow his memories of his one true love, his triumphs, his sadness, and the eventual end of his life in a fantastically powerful game that tugs at the heartstrings.Games can be art and Arise A Simple Story is a great example of this idea.  The world is beautiful and done is a stunning art style that is both angular and soft.  Throughout the game you will find Memories that tell the story within each chapter and expound upon the tale.  Each level is a look back on the protagonist’s life, starting from early childhood to old age and are brilliantly themed, colorful, and emotive.  Additionally, the soundtrack throughout the entire journey is impactful and works well with the story presented.  These items, in conjunction with the wordless story, make Arise a true work of art and one that will stay with you for quite some time.The main game mechanic of Arise is the ability to move time forward or backward and each level has its own reason to do so.  For example, progressing time forward in one chapter changes the season from winter to spring and opens paths that might not normally be accessible while in another chapter time forward or backwards controls a raging fire that devours all within its path.  Coupled with simple platforming; the game becomes a little more intricate as well as interesting as your progress through the story.If one negative thing can be said about Arise A Simple Story it would be the platforming.  Arise is a beautiful game to look at but it can be a chore to play.  While the main game mechanic is exciting and feels fresh, the platforming mechanic is frustrating and feels rushed.  With the fixed camera system, and a camera that sometimes moves while you are leaping, you end up dying a lot while jumping from area to area which slows down the game as well as the story of the game.The achievements are not only challenging but fun to get as well.  While there are achievements for completing each chapter; the vast bulk of achievements will be attained by finding all the memories as well as completing certain tasks in each level.  These special tasks range from jumping a hundred times or collecting dew drops to not freezing to death or touching fire.  All the achievements in Arise feel as if they are a part of the story and not just something thrown in there…a definite bonus especially for achievement hunters.Arise was a wonderful and heartfelt story from its grand opening to the moving final credits and an experience that I am sure to remember for quite some time.  From the epic environments to the sweeping musical score; Arise offered a beautiful story told without words in which you can take part and experience alongside the protagonist.  I wholeheartedly recommend this game to everyone, no matter what genre or style game that you may play.  Arise is a simple story well told and one that should be experienced.

_childDocuments_.review: Get the tissues!An extremely beautifully told story following the love and loss through this characters life.You really do get immersed in his journey and feel his joy and pain throughout. Stunning visuals and the music is excellent (i listen the album quite abit!) it brings each section of the game to life and suits the changing moods perfectly.As i said, get the tissues, I smiled, i cried, it really is a heart wrenching game and super wholesome.

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful story-driven game (and all that without speaking a single word). The main gameplay mechanic (manipulating time) is nicely implemented is various ways and makes for some interesting puzzlesolving. Reaching the end of each level is not that difficult, finding all the collectibles is the main challenge.But not everything was fine though... While looking for collectibles I frequently got my character stuck (especially in chapter Ashes), but loading a safe point could easily solve that.Often I would come across what looked like a hidden pathway, thinking it would lead me to a collectible, only to find out it was the main route after all and I couldn't get back anymore for the collectible on the other route. In these cases using the latest safe point was often also not helpful , so I had to replay the level again from the start in order to get the collectibles I missed.And finally, in one of the later levels you have to bounce from cloud to cloud and I would quite often missjudge the distance only top fall to my death again. Luckily respawns are quick and usually just a few seconds have to be replayed.In all, this game was a very nice experience and is highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Arise: A Simple Story is a gorgeous tale about a man looking back on his life. It has instantly become a favorite of mine and I would absolutely recommend it to anyone that enjoys story driven games and doesn't mind having no dialogue.The story is wonderful and sad, beautiful and real. The tale follows the life of a man, as he grows up, as he finds love, and as he grows old. There are 10 chapters, each tied to a time in the man's life, and each with a vastly different environment and theme. Emotion plays a key part in this game, and this game decides to focus this emotion into the art styles and the environments of the chapter rather than focusing on facial expressions. This clearly pays off, as the game absolutely succeeds in invoking the changing emotions throughout the game.The gameplay in Arise is well polished and seamless, and is a perfectly crafted medium for the story Arise tells. The story plays a pivotal importance in the gameplay, enabled by the fact that the player has very minimal control over the camera. While this concerned me at first in a 3D platformer, I quickly grew to love the game's camera, and the control it gave to the game's director over my experience. You are tasked with following a path through each chapter, manipulating the environment through your control over time, to solve puzzles and experience the story. Most puzzles range from very easy to mild thinking required, but shouldn't ever take too much time.Arise took me roughly 4 hours to complete, with another 3 hours to replay and hunt achievements. I was more than happy to replay Arise, and am very glad I did, as I missed many details that I was unable to appreciate in my first playthrough.Overall, if you enjoy story driven games at all, I would absolutely recommend Arise to you, and think it is worth the price, even when not on sale. My only note: play solo, while this game does support co-op, it was definitely designed for single-player.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

The game looks amazing and while I was playing for some reason I thought about It Takes Two which is a much larger game compared to this but it's very similar. Arise does have co-op but I have not tried it just yet to see how it works but I can see it being fun.If you are interested in a relaxing game look no further!

_childDocuments_.review: ProsStrong Visual DesignBeautiful MusicInventive Time PuzzlesCons3 Hours Long for $20Slow Movement (Jumping is faster for some reason)Getting Down When Climbing is VexingAs the title conveys, Arise: A Simple Story is a simple story. An old man revisits the memories of his life at the end of his existence. You'll travel through 10 incredibly designed worlds solving time manipulation puzzles and collecting memories that flesh out the narrative. The presentation is fantastic and the musical score is breathtaking. Even though I got a review copy the game is a hard sell for $20, $15 would've been a better asking price.I would recommend this journey for those who enjoy games like Journey, Sea of Solitude, or GRIS. It has system emotional tones to those titles. With the focus here being the importance of time and being with those you love. Overall, great game and one I would recommend.

An emotional yet simple story that draws you in, and new game mechanics in each chapter to keep you entertained.[+] Immersive story[+] Inventive game mechanics[+] Variety in the game play[+] Great soundtrack[+] Lovely animation[-] Control seem to have been designed for a controller - balancing over things with keyboard can be an annoying challengeDuration: I've seen people finish it in 2.5 hrs, but depending on style it can take 4-5 hrs. _childDocuments_.review: Absolute one of my all time favorite games.I had the chance to play this for free once before but there was no way i would ignore supporting the developers, who made such a touching, and beautiful game. There was no doubt i had to get it for myself. Without any offense i really want to say, if this game won't make you feel anything, then you might as well try to find a therapist. Just a little tale of an old man's life, that most of us can relate to in one way or an other.There is not a single negative thing i could say about the game. It's pure joy and tranquility.  It made me smile and tear up a lot and it also made me drop my jaw with the beautiful scenes for each memory, not to mention the in game music is just so meaningful. The symbolism in this game is just indescribably creative. Either you like puzzles or not, they are also fun and it won't melt your brain to figure it out. And most importantly....it's just a simple story...with so much love of course.

I'm 32 years old grown man, and by the end of this game, I was bursting into tears like a baby and I'm not ashamed of that. Thank you developers for proving that games can be much more than mere entertainment. Thank you for creating this magnificent story, that reminds us of what is important in our lives. Thank you dev team for this masterpiece, which is so rare nowadays. I wish you and your families all the best. With love and respect from Ukraine.
_childDocuments_.name: Arise: A Simple Story

_childDocuments_.review: Glad I found this- it does a lot with a little and it's very underrated imo.Top notch art/lighting with great color choices and cinematic shots to help tell the story, great OST that felt similar to 90s film scores, great sound design and implementation, and simple/effective mechanics that you can pick up easily but that stay fresh and don't lose their touch after while. The time freeze mechanic was especially fun. Lots of polish all over the game.The story is also great. It feels a lot more authentic than a lot of the stories in indies. It's also told very well- the story is built into the design of the game rather than just force feeding you additional plot points.Great to see the devs escape the 9-5 ad work and make something like this.

name: Songs of Conquest
detailed_description: Songs of Conquest is a turn-based strategy game where you lead powerful magicians called Wielders and venture to lands unknown. Wage battles against armies that dare oppose you, hunt for powerful artifacts and expand your territory. The world is ripe for the taking – seize it! Adventure Awaits Explore a wide variety of maps with diverse enemies and valuable loot. Delve into contrasting biomes with unique factions, environments and battlefields. Build an Empire Manage resources, research new advancements and expand your kingdom. Plan your towns to match your playstyle – Will you enlist every archer you can to rain death from their bows, or will the eternal legions of Aurelia march to war beneath your banners? Wage War Dive into a deep combat system using troop abilities and powerful magic. Combine troops to maximize available spells and damage potential. March into epic siege battles and determine which faction matches your playstyle and strategy. There are many ways to conquer! Play Your Way Handcrafted maps for the curious adventurer, or randomized maps for endless replayability. Conquest maps allow head-to-head battles, while Challenge maps offer strategic puzzles to hone your tactical thinking. Find a plethora of maps created by the Lavapotion team as well as our mod community. Alone or Together Venture into the world of Aerbor on your own, team up with a friend, or enlist AI allies and enemies - the choice is yours. The majority of maps are playable in single player, co-op, or multiplayer through local hotseat or online. Four Factions Four factions are locked in an epic conflict. Arleon, knights of old battling each other for dominance. Rana, ancient tribes fighting for survival in the swamp. Loth, necromancers raising the dead to create a glorious future. Barya, bold mercenaries and inventors dedicated to coin, gunpowder and independence. Four Choral Campaigns Listen to the bards as they celebrate your path to victory. Each campaign comes with a unique song that tells the tale of your rise and ruin. Unlock new verses as you complete missions, enjoying the full track at the end of the journey. In-game Map Editor The in-game map editor allows you to create your own adventures using the same tools the developers use to create campaign and skirmish maps. Script in-game events, control the soundtrack, write dialogue and share your creations with others!

_childDocuments_.review: What I can say about this game is "Song of conquest 2 would be a very great game."The reason for this is that while this game is heavily inspired by HoMM 3 I can't say that is game is better, or even on par with it. The game is different that's for sure but some of the system in this game just doesn't go well together and was, perhaps, overlooked in the development cycle.For example, this game have really low readability. What I mean by this is that It's hard to tell what's going on sometime. The art style in this game makes it hard to tell which building is which or even the creature suffers the same problem. The UI here is also to blame. I wonder why we can't view t total creature in a dwellings just by hover your mouse over it.Another problem is the overall core game loop itself. While trying to give the players more freedom, it end up making the game itself somewhat more restricted. The town building are meant to make it so that players have to decide which building to build and which to leave out. How ever, you also have to build resource building. This leads to not having to depend on the world for too much. This makes most of your turn are spent building resource and in the end, not much of it is planning at all. I another thing that might be a problem is that wielders are really powerful in this game. Each wielders (or heroes) have command limit meaning that they can only have only certain number of creature stack according to the skills they have. They also limit the number of creature per stack, meaning no matter how powerful your army is you can only bring 3 stack if your wielder is brand new. Number of stack will also affect the numbers of essences that you gain per round meaning more stack will let your wielder cast more spell which by the way, you can cast any number of spell per turn as long as you have the essences. All of this makes wielder too powerful. If they have one great wielder and you don't you will get snowball really easily even if your army outnumbers them.The list of the problem goes on but in end, I think this game have a lot of potential. I still recommend this game. I mean if you compare this to the top of the genre like HoMM 3 it gonna lose. This game has good direction. With more polishing and revising some the questionable system in the game, this might become a spiritual successor to the beloved HoMM 3 one day.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent HOM3 clone with some basic improvements and some annoying issues, but overall fun.What you need to know:1. There is four kingdoms in this game. One is humans/elves if elves were all ugly goat men. Another is undead and smelly hobos. The third is a bunch of minorities with guns. And the forth is a bunch of frog people.  It all seems... balanced. There really is nothing extreme game breakers like massive ghost armies/etc. 2. The auto battle option still remains worthless garbage that will have your ten thousand knights all die to a single peasant. Why? Who knows.3. The game is horribly not optimized. Despite the loads and odd slow now and then, it looks great.4. It is pretty much a better looking heroes 3 with a unit cap so you can't stack 10000000 bowmen and instead have to tier up. This is a good thing! 5. The music is pretty decent.So far for an EA game, it's not bad. I'll update this in the future, but if you are looking for a decent heroes 3 like game, this ain't too bad.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy the Heroes of Might and Magic series you'll definitely find more to love in this game than the most recent two games released from Ubisoft...While still in Early Access, the game feels complete and having just finished one of the campaigns, only came across one minor text bug in the description of a site I could visit, otherwise no issues, crashes or similar. The songs between missions, at least for the Stoutheart campaign are great, think 'Throw A Coin To Your Witcher' style.
_childDocuments_.name: Songs of Conquest

_childDocuments_.review: The game follows the rules of Heroes of Might and Magic but less with the problems it had. Such as teleporting around with a town portal or "poor man's town portal", or having a high-speed unit on your army and waiting until you rush the enemy with Mass Haste.Or having or needing a limitless doom stack to kill your foes.Songs of Conquest is Homm-like. So, it's taking some elements and making their own thing with the elements.Heroes are wielders. There is no mana like in heroes however there is essence. Essences are gained from your units and with them, you can cast spells. You gain more unit slots from level-ups. No complex movement formula like in the Heroes series is based on unit movement and terrain. There are only three ways terrains either hinder or improve your movement.In battle, Units can buff themselves either by ability or passives. There are no more hit-and-run tactics. However, you could always plan and use a secondary wielder (or hero) to weaken the foe's main army. Losing your main wielder in some maps is never the end if you can create a secondary wielder. Units have stack limits. Hiring wielders requires you to have towns upgraded and to control wielders. As well as an option for what wielder you want to hire.There will be some familiar things from Heroes in Songs of Conquest. I have been enjoying this game and have over 1400 hours in the game. I'm eager to see more content now that everything is set up.There is also a map editor and I had fun making maps. I spent way too much time on it than I expected. Made a couple of maps, a custom campaign which I am still working on. They may not be the best but was fun making them.Currently, there are 4 maps for each faction. All have 4 maps each of a total of 12 maps. They all are good at storytelling in my opinion. It's rather similar to Heroes where you get a text about what is happening but done way better.Each campaign explains how the faction was formed or how they came to be where they are now. What was the cause of it? Why are they doing what they are doing and their point of view? What is next?My critique of the campaign is the lack of info being given on what's being carried over. Which can be a turn-off for some people. Some of these are big and some are low impact on your playthrough.I will keep this short as I don't look into graphics in games. I barely take notice. However the pixel art is amazing! It's top notch and love every second of it. I only wish I was able to slow down the animations in battle.They (the devs) listen to feedback and do check what people say. So don't feel discouraged to give your feedback and one more last thing. If you do encounter a bug in the game. Use the in-game bug report tool or press b three times. Helps the devs more than saying what happened on Steam forums or in the discord. That is if you can report it. If the game crashes it's worth telling what happened.Last but not least.Songs of Conquest has been delightful and fun. I enjoyed seeing the game developed over the 2 years and I hope it continues. The devs are amazing people and I only wish them the best. To me it is inspiring. I was a tester for over 2 years. There is more to come from the game. I have high hopes.

_childDocuments_.review: Very similar to previous HoMM games while being different enough to be unique. It hits the spot since Ubisoft killed the HoMM series. So if you liked HoMM like I did, you will probably like this as well.My main issues with the early release: - There are four factions. And while it somewhat feels like 8 since each kind of splits in two paths, I would still appreciate more choices. - The AI is . . . lacking. That's about as nice as I can be, lol - Only two campaigns with 4 missions each. You can go through them fairly easily. - I know a lot of people love the magic system. I'm not entirely sold. It's just a bit much having to keep track of all the essences and which unit brings what and think about what your opponent might be able to use. Maybe with time I'll get used to it. I'm not saying we should go back to HoMM "only one spell per round" as that was stale, but I'm also not sold on this either. Not sure what my solution would be or if this is even up for change. I'm guessing this sticks, oh well. - Would appreciate more variety with unit upgrades rather than the fairly bland "defensive units get 10 defense", "offensive units get 10 offense", etc.. Also unit abilities from upgraded units would be nice to have additional variety. - The graphics aren't exactly ground breaking, yet it stutters when moving around portions of the map quickly or when AI takes their turns. My rig isn't really old, but a 1070 ti for these sort of games should be more than enough. Hopefully that can be sorted out and optimized.Some of those might be addressed by release. Some not. Either way it's a fun HoMM style game that I'll gladly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Making this review because the announcement that the game is about to be full release popped up, and in no way would I have expected that this soon; the base game is fine but there's SO much left wanting. The map design feels like a placeholder where they've made sure the basic idea is in place but haven't actually done the design work to make it feel immersive rather than 'you are at objective A, move to objective B and capture it'.Visuals are nice, combat is fun. The magic system based on army composition is interesting, the combat system works well enough.- the mechanics of the game are all present and correct, but there are only 4 factions with a small unit pool for each. Either each faction needs more variety or you need more factions, every game becomes extremely samey because of this.- the maps are incredibly 'game'y, there are very few included with the game, the majority of which are 'pvp' maps (meaning designed for 1v1 balance and tournament standard rather than immersion, now referred to as 'balanced' maps). After that you have player created maps, which seem to work strangely with the AI sometimes, and the quality of them is super varied as you'd expect, and the random map generator.The random maps (and a good portion of the included maps) are designed like a MOBA; there are home bases for each player with 'lanes' to each of the other bases, with smaller towns to capture along the routes, so push outwards capturing the points until you arrive at the enemy base. This again leads to every map feeling similar like a different colour version of the last.There's clearly a love for the game in the development, and a lot of it is good; the feel of exploring the map is nice, the sound effects and visuals of the hero walking about collecting stuff is nice and satisfying, the music is good for what it is, the battles are engaging. There's just not enough of any of it: The battles are engaging but you quickly see every permutation of them and start to just wish for a good autoresolve. The exploration is fun but you run out of space to explore very fast, seems to be the ethos is more 'push the lanes take the towers kill the ancient' then 'every map is a story'. The contents of the map just aren't that interesting: resources, xp boost, units. 1 or 2 things are like creature banks from HOMM3 but for the most part its just those, and there's little 'flavour' to any of it. Artifacts are pretty plain stat boosts, rarely you might get a more indepth buff but anything like angel wings, tomes of magic, or any of the more interesting artifacts from HOMM3, forget it. The game also doesn't seem to care much when you get one, it just makes a little sound and its in your inventory, with the 'best' gear autoequipped if you dont touch it (reducing another aspect of the game to a routine autohandled thing with no flavour or depth)I really want to like the game, and previously thought 'oh its still early access theres more content coming' but with 1.0 being around the corner, not so sure. I want to explore the maps more but the design discourages it, and limits the enjoyment of it. I want to like the factions but they're so shallow it's like a container for a faction rather than a faction itself. There's difference between them but functionally none of them are particularly unique, for fantasy theyre pretty generic, and other than the swamp frog people it feels like the same faction had 3 offshoots (theyre all human + something else, the units are different but something just makes them all feel samey - imagine if in say a new command and conquer the GDI had a split and now theyre GDI North, East and West, and those are the 3 options you can pick)I do still enjoy the game somewhat so i cant say 'not recommended', if I didnt know the devs were considering this the full release state I'd say go for it 100% it can only get better, however seeing as this is it, I'd advise keeping expectations in check.

_childDocuments_.review: I play HoMM3 yearly, and recommend SoC.Many things are different from HoMM, but the core is there. You choose level-up bonuses for your Hero (Wielder),  visit points of interest (strategically), claiming mines, and building your towns to generate creatures for battle. In battle you cast spells, move and attack with creatures, and the end result can be drastically different based on your choices.A lot is different also, but in good new ways. Town building comes down to level and how and what size plots are available for buildings.  Magic is used by points in different schools that can be gained by simply doing something in battle or visiting buff locations before. Troop size is limited, and you have to take skills to allow more troop slots.It's just fun with a depth of strategy that isn't immediately apparent. Highly recommended if you loved HoMM 2/3 and even King's Bounty.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a Heroes of Might and Magic III killer for me, but still a good game. TL;DR: Songs of Conquest provides a good gameplay flow, some useful innovations and nostalgic pixel graphics. Nevertheless, in my opinion there is a reason why the number of active players is currently around a third (approx. 1200 to 400) of the HD version of HoMM III.Notes after 12 hours in:- Tactical combat feeling is similar to the HoMM series. The heroes - called Wielders - all have their own specializations, level up and receive new skills and artifacts. At the same time, there are some cautious changes and new tactical options.- Through the deployment phase before the manual battles, it is possible to specifically exploit the height differences of the various battlefields or to position yourself closer or further away depending on your own and enemy troop types (ranged or fast units, etc.). - Unit staples are capped now. So no more doom stacks. This keeps encounters more balanced throughout the game. Even though some players might miss the charm of steamrolling enemies late game.- Defeating a staple of units grants a small, stackable momentum buff, further refining the battle dynamic.- The magic system, in which a certain amount of essences are generated each round turns out to be an interesting innovation. Which essences (chaos, order, destruction, etc.) are added depends on the troops used, but also on artifacts and other factors. Your own army composition and the magic system are therefore intertwined. One can choose to spend your essences quickly or save or combine them for more powerful spells.- The maximum number of different unit staples a wielder can bring along - and thus to a certain extent the amount of essences generated - depends on his command points.- No city screen or faction specific music while managing your settlements, which I personally don't like at all. The buildings are placed on the world map. Space is a limited resource. You have to decide which unit, resource or upgrade building suits you best. Planing your cities therefore feels impactful, but without the typical HoMM III flair. So, in my opinion, immersion and identification with the respective faction doesn't work so well. - Only four playable factions. Not much compared to HoMM or games like Age of Wonders.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been testing and playing SoC since closed Alpha days and got game for free as a gift from devs like all other tester. During those 2,5 half years game changed in many ways. Devs were always kind, open and responsive. We often could directly talk with them and exchange ideas, suggestions and feedback. I know they made many choices and sacrificed some ideas and planned systems to focus on other  the end we got charming turn based strategy game that takes inspiration from many of its predescesors and gives its own spin on things. From building on the map to magic system. While gameplay may seem simple there is depth in army buidling and magic system that is directly connected to it. However there are aspect that are a bit bland/lacking which can be upgraded.I know that things like more factions or more neutral units are planned so I won't be bothering with them.What I love about game:1) Beautiful pixel graphics - handcrafted pixelt art take a lot of time to make and it can be seen in SoC. Game looks amazing and has a lot of details. From simple things as rocks to 2) Music - I can listen to it for hours. Its great. Simple as that3) Town building - I love that I can buildings on adventure map. With one glance you can see what was build and upgraded. It also makes map a bit more alive4) Factions - while only 4(more coming after 1.0) they are rather diverse, with unique looks and feelWhat I would like to be added/changed, things I feel that games is lacking:1) Faction mechanics - some special, unique things for each faction to spice things up on adventure map.2) Special terrain for battle maps - things that would give troops standing in it some buffs or debuffs. From something simple like mud or tall grass to shrines, runic stones3) Unique faction talents - I would love to see some faction specific talents that would give me ability to use specific units/army composition even more.4) Mechanic that uses musician units - I know that it was planned and that is why each faction has some sort of musician in its lineup. I know it was sacrificed for other things. I want it in game. Thats it.
