_childDocuments_.review: Note: I refunded this and bought the Switch version because it comes with special Digimon promo TCG cards. Only available for both pre-orders and early purchases of the physical copy.Oh man, what a time to be a Digimon fan. Over the past several years, we Digimon fans have been living out the celebration for the 20th anniversary of Digimon with the Tri. movies and the 2022 Digimon Adventure anime remake. It's now the 2nd half of 2022 - AND WE'RE STILL CELEBRATING! With this wonderful love letter to the fans of the original 1999 Digimon Adventure anime.And that's something important to note: it's a tribute to fans of the anime, not so much a Digimon game. While it contains tactical RPG elements, it's first and foremost a visual novel. That isn't an issue for me since I love visual novels, but I do understand why certain people are annoyed and disappointed. However, for us fans of the 1999 anime, this could easily be the perfect Digimon game we've always dreamed of, going on a dangerous adventure like Taichi/Tai and the gang, but only this time, it's a much darker, more tragic survival adventure meant for us Digimon fans who have now grown older and seeking more mature content. It contains similar "Lord of the Flies" drama and conflict just like the anime, the same cathartic "all hope is lost!" moment that leads to the salvation of evolution (minus the "Brave Heart" theme song that would've made the moment perfect), and it has characters that easily remind us of the original eight children from Digimon Adventure (especially Shuuji Kayama, the Joe Kido counterpart). Just about everything in the game and storyline feels like a tribute to the anime's first season.Best of all, your Digimon's evolution is determined by your choices in the game, so your adventure feels personal, like you're growing alongside your Digimon. Just the same way Taichi and the others did on File Island two decades ago on their adventure as they question their moral values, you'll have to do the same too. This is easily the best and most crucial part of the game, and it greatly enhances replayability as you seek out alternate endings and evolutions you might have missed.And the main title music theme... god, that is freaking beautiful. It easily conveys the tragic tone that's to come in the game, and I literally started crying when I entered the main menu when the game hasn't even started. It's not some bubbly, exciting theme song like Butterfly or "Gotta Catch 'em All!". The thing people tend to forget when they watch the Digimon anime is that these are literally children forced into life-or-death scenarios, and I think both the songwriters and writers of Digimon Survive understood that, and so the song fitted with that idea, the idea of innocent children forced into a tragic situation of survival and regretting not cherishing their life. I remember a line in the trailer, when one of the characters said something along the lines of, "We never really thought about the preciousness of life." That line hooked me to the game because it might as well have been telling me, "People are gonna die, and we'll regret it."While this might be the dream game that Digimon Adventure fans could get, is it really a perfect game? Not really, since the plot does drag a bit like many JRPGs. The way the game gets you to move forward in plot by talking to essential NPCs (marked with an exclamation mark no less) is also detrimental to the mystery of the plot since you already know where to look for certain missing characters everyone's trying to find, whom to talk to to progress the plot, etc. It's not a great feature and it does drag the story down a little bit.The "auto" function of the game that moves forward the dialogue is also a bit annoying. Because the voice acting is in Japanese, I sometimes accidentally skip over voiced lines, thus ruining the immersion of the story, which is why I put it in "auto mode" when the characters' lines are voiced. However, unlike most visual novels, the speed of the text in this one isn't balanced enough that it hits the right speed; it's either moving too fast when you adjust the Text Speed to "Fast," or it's moving too slow in "Normal" speed. The problem becomes obvious when you get Takuma's non-voiced thoughts mixed into the voiced lines. For example, when I played the voiced dialogue in auto mode, I'm allowed to see the full text of what the character's gonna say immediately when I press "A" on my Switch, and it doesn't skip the line after that even if you keep pressing A until the voice performance is fully played out. However, you WILL accidentally skip Takuma's thoughts if you do this, and because the text is either playing too slow or too fast, you either get annoyed that Takuma's thoughts are being displayed at such a slow speed, or get annoyed that they're being skipped ahead way too fast during auto mode. The auto mode speed isn't balanced.But aside from those gripes, I love this game for what it is, for what it offers us Digimon fans who are still around in a Pokémon-dominated world. I love the tribute, and I love the tragedy. If you love Digimon Adventure the anime, then this is a MUST-BUY for all of you Chosen Children/Digidestineds out there. Believe in your brave heart! :D

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in my review is Spoiler FreeAs a long time Digimon fan, and having followed this game's rocky release from being delayed multiple years, so far would say it's worth the wait. It's not a game for everyone, as it is essentially a visual novel with some point and click elements and TBS battles inbetween, but for those who do enjoy the visual novel format and enjoy Digimon it is an engaging enough game to sink some time into.That said, there are some obvious corners cut at times, and I'll list a few here:- The map is confusingly low quality, it looks like it wasn't finished honestly and probably the most irking graphical choice.- Moral choices are clearly marked, both by the options being in the same spots, but they're also colour coded when you hover over them. The game clearly lets you know what outcome you will get from each choice, this may be a pro or a con for people depending on your preferences. - While most of the story is voice acted, it will randomly without warning stop, even on the linear sections that are required to progress the plot. Not sure if they just forgot to voice those parts or what, but it's a little jarring.- The animations on sprites is not AAA standard, as each fade transition allows you to see the objects that make up the sprite. As an animator, this can be avoided by simply not using fade transitions, or setting the linked layers to be registered as one flat object so each part isn't transitioned separately. It's just a bit amateurish.- While you can use a mouse, some parts are more tricky than others and clearly still intended for a controller. After the 5th time of accidentally clicking the wrong direction for my Digimon to defend after I was clearly covering over the correct direction, I just gave up and started using the keyboard.- Though I haven't finished the story, I would say it's a little cliche and if you do watch a lot of anime or know anything about Japanese folklore, you'll probably know where things are going pretty quickly initially. All that said, I am still enjoying the game, but if you're not a hardcore Digimon fan you may want to wait for a sale. For those of us who are hardcore fans, show the series some love, this game went through hell to get here, so it sure needs it.

_childDocuments_.review: Se: Jag behöver inte begå självmord eftersom det här spelet redan har dödat mig inuti.EN: Play this game, it changed my life. Do it now, this is a threat.In all seriousness Digimon Survive is many things. It's strange. It's amazing. It's also horrific and beautiful. In my 20+ years of being on and off with the franchise I've seen games of wildly varying quality. This game to me isn't just special as a long time digimon fan, but is among my very favourite video games.It's a visual novel with strategy RPG combat. I've heard people whine about the latter. I don't get that. I especially don't get it because the level of polish in the visuals, for a VN, is top notch. The game IS more story-focused for what that's worth. However it's by far the best game out there to best capture the tone of early Digimon media like Digimon Adventure and Digimon Tamers and I doubt it will be surpassed anytime soon, if ever.I love the game and for that reason I have to discuss it's flaws. The translation isn't great. If anything the bad translation is entirely carried by the voice acting, which is frankly amazing and carries the tone on its back. One of the most egregious issues with the translation is the translators themselves having no idea how pronouns work. No, this isn't what some of you think I might say, its just genuinely bad. I like it using male and female pronouns as opposed to many digimon games which are strictly "it" by default with the occasional "him" added. This is normally as it should be more in line with the anime, but characters, more specifically the digimon themselves, are misgendered constantly. This gets really noticable when you have casses like Labramon who is very frequently. Or R**amon who is like 3 times in the same cutscene. It'd dumb and the translation honestly is one of the weakest parts of the game. I also want to say that while I like most of the endings and the tone each carry, the fact that things don't really change until around the 8th chapter and that's kinda dumb. Also once you learn how the endings work it becomes a little too simple. Though I do like how choices in the game impact you and your Agumon mechanically, I like that a lot. Though there are some story bits at odds with each depending on how you play the game. By this I mean, and no major spoilers but, there's a moment in the game where two characters argue after a bad thing happened. This makes perfect sense in every ending except one. In that one it feels really, really dumb and honestly should have been cut from that path entirely.Though like I said the fact that the game can still convey it's tone and emotional weight so well is a testament to both the game's writing and voice acting which are on point. The sprites are CUTE! They also have a surprising variety of animations included tired animations for every single Digimon in the game. The variety of Digimon is rather limited compared to some games. This is mostly since the roster offered is like 80% digimon that are either story-related or random enemies througout the story and about 20% bonus critters. This is somewhat balanced out by the choice of Digimon for the main characters. Yeah you get 3 popular digimon as the main character's partners, but the others really stand out for the better speaking as a fan of the series. While there are certain digimon I wished could have been in the game and the limited roster does dumb down some evolution lines I struggle to call this a flaw. I love this game. There's a reason why I have some many hours and why it happens to be among the few games I decided to go all out and get 100% of the achievements for.It's presentation, writing, music and voice acting make an incredible experience. There are little bits all around the game that should appease fans like me, but the story itself, for those that have the patience, is absolutely worth trying even to outsiders.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon Survive is.. plainly put a bad game. A poor melding of concepts. Nowhere near enough of a game to warrant a high tier price tag. It is carried by the fact that it is Digimon and, despite Digimon being a strange illogical hodgepodge powered by friendship and adding metal to make things cooler, it is at its core lovable and filled with goofballs like Agumon. It survives by having pleasant art, bonds of companions new and old, and at the very least being generally free of bugs.Exploration is slow and inconvenient. Scanning an area for interactables, scanning again with your phone, talking to the character you are in that location for, then immediately returning to that area to scan again in case anything new has been added. Bonus treat, return and scan again again after moving to another area and talking to a character there. Repeat after every interaction to make sure you don't miss anything. This alone pads the gameplay to double its size if you manage to put up with it. Not every item is valuable, many are small consumables. Some of course are not, and a few are special diary entries or rarer Digimon encounters. The phone scanning is extra weird given most of your time is spent in the Digital World where things should.. already be visible? It might be more interesting if one were noticing oddities in the Human World, but in general extra vision modes like this, even when stylised and well attached to a story, just obstacles.The combat side of the game is.. fine? It's functional. It's difficult to claim that it adds much of value, and even has auto-battle system to help skip it entirely. Which perhaps enforces the idea that is not particularly good. Another inconvenience, this too is where the game likes to litter its items. While it is understandable to try give some exploration item gathering to the game, both of the ways mentioned are terribly inconvenient and it is a little more natural when given by characters or as plain combat rewards.Which would finally leave the story and visual novel aspects. The story and characters are exactly enough for a Digimon story. There are familiar aspects in a number of them, reminiscent of the originals like Tai, Joe, Mimi, but they all have their own thing going too. Friendship is the heart of the cards and all that. Some, you want to throw into the river as soon as you meet them for how stubborn or extreme they act. By the end, of course, they grow on you. That being said, the end you can reach is limited by not actually being allowed to reach certain good outcomes on your first playthrough.Some interactions are voiced, some are not. While this can be understandable when picking up random items, it is often jarring when games pick and choose how much to bother voicing. Which cutscenes are important enough. Some super weird noises chosen for some of the Digimon. Dialogue is often fairly slow paced, and leaving the dialogue to play automatically would take half your lifespan. To add to this, a lot of the events in the game are cut up into moving to a different location, returning to locations, selecting through characters, and a lot of ideas get repeated multiple times. Many of your dialogue choices feel arbitrary and just for the karma system that determines what kind of character you are rather than having any meaning in the actual words.All this brought to you while auto-battling through the final battles and cutscenes.

_childDocuments_.review: Intriguing and mostly engaging new experience for Digimon with notable flaws.----------------+ Key character design is very good. They fit in well with the scenes with the lighting properly reflecting on them, and they even went the extra length of having variations of how shadows are casting from their bodies depending on the location and time of day.+ Story is arguably the "darkest" in the Digimon franchise, making for a solid mystery and some fairly unexpected moments.+ Relationships between the tamers and their Digimon are interesting and reflect each other well, which is important for a story-focused game like this.+ Solid voice acting+/- Combat is very hit or miss. While it is definitely serviceable at worst, it leaves a lot to be desired. Digimon are limited to a basic attack and one special move unless using their 2 equipment slots to add more.Playing on 3x game speed is essentially a must. You can't skip battle animations unless you turn them off, and there's no instant movement. I don't believe you can turn off evolution animations, which is something you will be doing a lot with your main Digimon. Digimon jumping up and down elevated ground is annoyingly long.Speaking of terrain, there isn't really much to go for it. The most variation you see is elevation which has some attack modifications and which angle you attack from (front, sides or back). There are some maps with gaps that only Digimon that are capable of flight movement can cross.The character affinity and team backup system is mildy interesting but sometimes feel a bit too random. Some Digimon that have AoE attacks can also discourage the player from trying to position for this.+/- Soundtrack is mostly good, but the selection does feel small and there are some forgettable tracks. The main theme is good and I like the different renditions of it you can hear throughout the game.- Enemy AI is weird as hell and will sometimes actively go out of their to avoid fighting you and prolong their own life. This is most notable experienced in one of the earlier chapters with Meramon, who will run away to the edges of the map and defend every turn. Reiterating why playing on 3x game speed is a must.- Pacing can be very bad in some parts of the game. Something will happen in the story and every character will basically exist just to reaffirm what has happened. Something will happen and characters can become stupid just for the sake of something happening, which you then have to do with multiple characters to solve a problem that almost feels copy-pasted.- Partner Digimon evolutions are tied to character affinity. You increase character affinity during free time segments when interacting with characters and responding properly to the situation. Because of this, it's possible for certain partner Digimon to fall behind in their evolution line, which can be a detriment in story battles where you are forced to use them. However, you can pause and save at any time during the story segments and can essentially just save scum until you get the right answer.- English script is not the best at times. Too much Americanized slang and lingo that doesn't even properly match with what is actually being said and feels out of place. Even if you are fluent in Japanese, you can't play the game in Japanese because Bamco decided not to include a Japanese text option in the international version.- Definitely priced too high for a game that is mostly a visual novel. $80 Canadian is very high but I managed to get it for just $53. It is decently long but I don't think price = playtime is a fair view to look at it from.----------------Despite my gripes with the game and the multiple times I considered dropping the game entirely, I still thoroughly enjoyed it because of the relationship between the partners and Digimon and the story. The combat, while half-baked, can still be enjoyable especially during some of the pivotal story moments. I haven't finished the game in it's entirety (got the Wrathful ending, and there are 4 endings total, 3 for each part of the moral compass and a true ending unlocked after completing at least one of those endings), but I do plan on coming back to it eventually and finish up at least the true ending if not the other 2 routes with it. If you like visual novels/story-driven games and Digimon I would recommend the game, preferably below it's current price. I would be highly interested in a sequel or successor that has more consistent writing and pacing, a better balance of VN and SRPG segments, and refine upon the SRPG part of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: An atmospheric and immersive horror visual novels, with some fun strategy rpg elements here and there.The art direction of this game is amazing, it not only feels like watching an interactive anime, but the character designs, background art, sprites, and even menu UIs are gorgeous. The characters are complex and full of depth, allowing you to feel deeply for them as you get to know them through the story. The digimon available might be limited in number, but there's enough for what this game is. Each character feels purposeful in their inclusion.Though this is a darker retelling of an adventure like premise, the story has clearly been crafted with love and an understanding of what made the original Digimon Adventure anime so special and enduring in the hearts of fans. A welcome return to nostalgia for an older audience, and a good gateway for players unfamiliar with the world of Digimon looking for a less childish entry to the franchise.Also I would die for Miyuki.

_childDocuments_.review: Loving it currently, although I do love Digimon and a good visual novel. That said, I don't think liking VN's is necessarily a requirement- just be prepared for a fair amount of reading and dialogue choices in between battles for some points in the journey. Art is gorgeous and expressive, mainly on the visual novel side, but the in-battle sprites are still a joy to look at and animate smoothly. The music thus far is pretty good at capturing emotion, especially the main theme which they use fairly liberally in other tracks. I think I'm still pretty early on, but the story, setting and characters so far have gripped me and I'm definitely interested in seeing how/ if different decisions on a second play-through will change the narrative. On the combat side, it has kept me entertained and the recent boss battles have been quite close shaves on the hard difficulty.  As a tactics game it hasn't felt especially tactical thus far which is a bit of a shame for me. Picking the right monsters for the job and giving them the right equipment beforehand makes the most difference which isn't necessarily a bad thing. I feel a game like Devil Survivor (which this game is pretty similar to) managed to hit a more ideal balance between rpg elements and tactical decision making. Hopefully more interesting maps, map objectives and enemy layouts show up later in the game to really put me to the test. My only other real issues are pretty minor: I feel some of the dialogue choices are a bit misleading in communicating what your character is going to say. For example the option to say 'Phones don't work' ended up translating to praising a character for noticing his phone isn't working. I've been trying to stick to my choices as much as possible, but in situations like that where I would/ wouldn't have picked the option if it was clearer what I was going to say, I would just reload. There's a not unnoticeable amount of awkward translations that probably needed another round of editing, not at all as bad as Digimon Cyber Sleuth in this respect though. Also, for a game with a lot of reading, some of the fonts stick out to me as a bit out of place but that could just be me. The skip function doesn't seem to work well either as even if I hold it down I keep having to press it again after every dialogue box. If I'm going to be especially nit-picky, then the cursor that you can freely search the screen is sluggish when locking on to things and feels a bit redundant given you can just cycle through points of interest on the screen with Q and E; not sure why it's there (unless there are secret points I've been missing, but I have been looking and found none so far that pressing Q and E didn't find). Finally, as a long time Digimon fan, some of the evolution chains stick out to me as odd, (e.g. why doesn't Dokugumon get to digivolve to Arukenimon?) but I am excited to fill out the roster. Will update this review on completion, or maybe after completing a few routes so I can comment on the impact your choices make and how well the game holds up after multiple play-throughs. So far though, I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly Recommend As a Fan of Digimon, buuuuuuut this game is a huuuuge departure from the Monster Training Sims before. What I likeNumber 1- It's Mega-Depressing like a proper Horror Visual Novel; and the game lets you know when something will happen.... but it's waaaay worse than what you expect. The dialogue is realistic to a fault. Honestly this game could have an F-Bomb Dialogue Edit and It would feel exactly the same. I'm not a fan of VNs but the ones I have played have been the same level of Suuuuuper Depressing 70%/ and 30% UWU for the rest. Number 2 - The TRPG elements are super basic; but that's kinda the good/bad thing that will keep you. The combat is closer to Pokemon Conquest than something like Tactics Ogre. Simple and bare bones. You will get the hang of combat quickly by watching the AI get more consecutive Crits on your mons the first few battles. I honestly liked the combat once I started to use Item moves, but the game can easily be cheesed by Stat Items. Personally; I liked that there is an Auto battle feature so I could just let my mons go and I would always be ahead of the curve. Except for the second boss, I found the bosses are all really threatening, Even if you are Gigachadmon.Number 3 - The Post-Game is something I look forward to doing. Extra challenges and more Items mean more combats. Number 4 - This is a self contained story that could easily have been a Digimon Story game. Self Contained, yet enough references to the Anime to make me happy. You'll appreciate it if you are into stuff like Fatal Frame. The No Bueno Number 1 - This game is kinda Rough, I get they reused game illustrations, but I can see the Pixels in the mini-cutscenes.  I don't like to bash on game assets since I will get a hard on for anything with Pixel Art, but this game needed some more time to cook.Number 2 - This game needs more Mons. I would have been fine with reuse of Existing Digimon Assets. If I have to fight another Etemon I'm going to punch my screen. Number 3- There should have been an Item shop. Like for real. Status attacks are like 100% guaranteed to give you status effects and you get status heals after the midpoint of the game. Number 4 - The combat might be too simple. Like I could have used at least one more attack per Mon, The game rains Ribs everywhere so i could have used more incentive to use them. Number 5 - The Percentage for recruitment makes no sense.  Make it easier. 6% means nothing, And the penalty is worse for failures by forcing me to lose End Battle EXP/Items. Honestly 8/10. If you can look past the roughness of combat, It's a good book game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll try to explain without spoilers. I was expecting choices to matter more since it is a visual novel of sorts made by a large publisher. But they don't branch out as much as you would hope.Your choices effect how Agumon evolves. They also effect your Affinity with companions. Having high affinity with companions trivializes the game in later stages, where as having low affinity makes the game impossible to beat without lowering the difficulty.The turn based tactical game play is average, but about half way through the game it stops giving you unique battles with unique win conditions. There aren't many Digimon to choose from, only around 100. There are a number of typos and bad translations the further into the game you get. The story can be dark, but isn't very good and drags on for too long. The game takes around 42 hours to beat, less if you use the auto-battle mechanic but that defeats the purpose of the game. It also expects you to replay the game all over again after beating it because of .Play Digimon Cyber Sleuth instead. If you get bored of that game and don't beat it, I wouldn't bother trying this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not even into visual novels but this game is a masterpiece. The beauty of digimon games is they are so slept on that the developers can't afford to not make a good game. And I assure you this game is a modern classic.Digimon Survive makes up for all the times we've been CyberPunk'd. This game was made with real passion and love (I heard that they may have had to stop development a few years ago). It would be really sad if something this beautiful was slept on so I will try to give an overview of exactly what this game is.Yes, Digimon Survive is in fact at it's roots a visual novel. BUT (and this is so important!) it is so unique, fresh, and clean that once begin you honestly do not feel as though you are playing a visual novel. IMO Digimon Survive is more akin to those 'choices matter' games. It is difficult for me to explain, all I can say is if you are worried about the game being boring and cringe you are completely wrong.-----BREAKDOWN STARTS HERE-----Art is absolutely gorgeous, it looks exactly as though I am watching an episode of an anime. Everything is animated so well, even backgrounds have life. Definitely doesn't feel 2D. And something about the art is both dark and comforting at the same time... think almost Higurashi. Did I mention the Digimon sprites?? Incredible quality! 11/10Music is superb. Same quality you would expect from a theatrical movie release. There is music for every single event so it never feels empty. And there are no annoying tracks. 11/10Sound Design is amazing as well. Sound effects in battles are very well made. 10/10Voice Acting is phenomenal!! Definitely one of the highlights! 11/10User Interface is fantastic. Menu is easily navigated, and text is easy to read. Autosaving after almost everything you do. Plenty of options to tune the experience to fit your taste. And the tutorials do an excellent job of making you get the idea of what to do. I have read of people experiencing crashing? I haven't in over 20 hours. 10/10Gameplay is addicting like Pokemon Sapphire was and that says alot!! The game has a few very different portions to offer; however, transitioning between feels very natural and seamless. Very rewarding gameplay loop! Not to mention you can free battle almost anytime, and damn are they addicting. It's actually like Final Fantasy Tactics and Pokemon on crack. You can even have enemy Digimon join you. And so far the... um, ..pokedex? (digidex??? idk.) has something like 120 entries to discover. There are lots and lots of choices you need to make which impact many things, including evolutions, and the visual novel plays alot like an exploration/detective style game. It actually feels like an RPG due to the fluidity in the game. For some reason I get big Final Fantasy X vibes off this game even though they are not similar at all lol. Also the game does not feel stale. Always something new to do but you are never rushed. Very satisfying experience! 11/10And I believe lastly I'll share my thoughts on the Story and Writing. For me this is another highlight. Digimon has been reimagined into a new story line so if you don't know anything about Digimon this game will still play out as intended. They took a stereotypical anime plotline but accompanied it with very mature themes and very down to earth, realistic, dialogue. It's not cringey anime. Plot gives me the same disturbing tense vibes that the Higurashi series has (minus all the crazy ♥♥♥♥). Characters are fantastic - there's plenty of them and all have their own flaws. Everything is just over all well written and oozes maturity and class. I have already put in over 20 hours and I am still getting tutorials here and there. To me this is a good sign as I can tell this is going to be a wonderfully long experience.One thing I would like to see addressed is the spelling/grammar errors. There are not many but for $90 CAD I think it's not very professional in that regard.Overall this game is to Digimon what Final Fantasy 7 Remake was to the Final Fantasy series. I sense nothing but love and dedication from the folks who created this masterpiece. It may not be for everyone but for that reason this game is even more special. I wouldn't say that the Visual Novel genre is particularly lucrative when it comes to a paycheck and yet you can tell the devs were trying to create something to stand tall and proud next to the giants of the video game world.Unfortunately I believe that many people will misunderstand what this game is and unfairly judge. But if you are open-minded and are searching for a good story driven, party based game then I have a feeling this game will not let you down. Oh and if you are a Digimon fan then what are you waiting for?

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't finish the game, some of this probably improves later.Most of the early game is just spent listening to kids whine about the situation which is realistic but isn't fun to read and isn't good story material. This would be fine if you only had to listen to a few of them but you end up listening to it 7 times over. On top of that any time something happens you have to hear all 7 of them and their partner digimon chime in on it which just made it feel like things dragged on alot longer than it should and made it feels so tedious.The VN side felt weird, constantly bouncing you back to menus instead of continuing the story, felt like the developers had no clue how a VN should flow. There were times that there was only 1 way forward but for some reason they decided to send you to the area select screen just so you could re-enter the scene you were just in. To many dialogues that only seemed to exist to give you another chance to score Karma points. Choices also didn't really matter much, your Karma score was pretty much the only decision you made which only influenced a few events that don't happen till late in the story. If they cut the cast down to the 3 main friends or alteast didn't have the other 4 be in everything and got over their whining faster this could've been a decent game.The devs made some changes from how I've seen VNs work and honestly the changes seemed to be worse than the standard, either slow and tedious or just disrupted the flow of events.Combat worked fine but I question why there is a level system for something with so little focus on combat, usually a level system would be for something with more of a grinding focus and if they were having trouble beating a section they can just decrease the difficulty rather than grinding since you can set the difficulty at the start of every fight. Combat could slow down sometimes due to the movement, at times I spent several rounds in a row doing nothing but move because enemies were so far away.The controls were a little weird playing on PC but they worked, worst thing I had to deal with there was having to hit some keys twice before they registered which for a slow game like this doesn't matter.The karma system seemed a little to simple, the options are always in the same positions and 2 out of the 3 seemed pretty similar to me. It also determined to much, put to much points in one of them and certain events are impossible to avoid which is weird when the other non-wrathful option is so close in what it is to the correct one.Endings: Minor spoiler?Havent actually got there but read ahead and this killed my motivation to finish. TLDR: To much whining from to many people makes the game slow and tedious. Combat is alright but can be slow at times. PC port parts work but are a different from what I'd expect.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this game, but I couldn't.Aesthetically, it's beautiful. I've never seen a visual novel polished to such extents, beautiful backgrounds that are not static images, shadows over character images, the smooth transitions between places and in-between characters, well done particle effects, an awesome UI, and even animations for the eye and mouth movements that don't look unnatural. The art style is good, but I feel like the poor character design makes it look worse than it actually is.Sadly, that's the only good point I found about this game.The beautiful animations are nice but they easily become annoying when you have to constantly switch between locations or things of interest to investigate. The gameplay loop involves A LOT of this, so it really ruins the experience.The story is extremely boring and the characters even more, I really tried but I couldn't like any of them. I was actually starting to like Koromon, until a few minutes later it evolved and never saw it again during my playtime. The translation is also awful and extremely stupid, which makes everything even worse, I can guarantee a team of unpaid fans can easily do a better work.Battle-wise, it wasn't so bad. I liked the idea of talking to Digimon to try to befriend them and be able to invite them to your party, but the dialogues to do so were so silly and boring that it loses all charm.Does the game gets better a few more hours in? Maybe, I don't know, but I cannot continue to force myself to waste any more time in an overpriced visual novel. There are way better ones out there and even if this game was free, I would've dropped it anyways. I cannot recommend it.tl;drOverpriced visual novel that looks good, but it's extremely boring.Gameplay loop gets annoying really quick.I can't recommend it neither as a fan of digimon, nor as a fan of visual novels.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon Survive blends the unique gaming experiences of a visual novel (80%) and a SRPG (20%), telling the story of 7 teenagers ranging from the age of 12 to 15 that end up in another world during a camping trip (or during the events of said trip) and have to fight for their survival in unforgiving and foreign surroundings. Longtime Digimon fans have probably already discovered the resemblance with the events of Digimon Adventure 1 in regards of the story's rough outline. Digimon Survive, however, takes a much darker, much more mature approach towards its storytelling and introduces a gameplay system that emphasizes the importance of keeping a level head, making decisions, and knowing what to say and do in various situations, leading to interconnected karma and affinity points, which, moreover, have both an impact on the partner digimon's evolution line and the story's ultimate conclusion (such as who gets to live, and who will die). Digimon Survive has great soundtrack and a pretty solid story that keeps the reader hooked, although it cannot compare to the beautifully written Digimon Adventure 1. Most of the characters are easy to emphathize with, considering they are youths spirited away into a hostile realm with seemingly no way back. It goes without saying, however, that some (other) characters are, more often than not, ruining the reading experience with their extreme and needlessly annoying personalities, complexes, and their need to start fights about one and the same thing over and over again. It gets old with time. The boss battles are well made (especially the OST), but free battle encounters and monster negotiations that were seemingly modeled after the successful Persona series, paired with the selectable auto fight function, end up becoming repetitive very soon. You spend your free-time between major battles exploring the area and interacting with your team, learning more about the unfortunate situation you are in, slowly unmasking each character's backstory, forming bonds with your teammates (if you know what to say in each respective situation), or finding valuable items that can be used for digimon training or battle. All things considered, I would recommend this game - although primarily to those who don't mind reading and who are veteran followers of the Digimon franchise. Digimon Survive was a nice experiment and a fresh and welcome approach towards gaming experiences within the Digimon franchise. However, personally, I would like to see another Digimon World Game (such as DM World 1 or Next Order) in the future, with a more balanced approach towards storytelling and gameplay/progression.

_childDocuments_.review: So, given we just had a reboot of the Digimon Adventure 01 Anime, that did not only basically throw away almost all of it's origin story/core concepts for success, this one could have rather been the one that should have gotten an Anime adaptation (with a few minor additions to the characters).I'm still on my 1st playthrough, but given the time I already spent and the slow progress, I would assume, I can recommend this to anybody interested.This is essentially a VN at core and a FF Tactics/Tactics Ogre RPG-styled game in the battles/equipment part, and has not gameplay you might hope for - like e.g. Digimon World 1.I think this style really fit's the bill for Digimon Games the most, though, if not in DW1 style (Remaster pls?).You might rather distantly compare this one with the Digimon Adventure 01 (JPN-only(?)) Sony PSP Game.I think it's a well made game for a rather mature audience, though development time did take it's sweet time.. not sure how much is C19 dependent, though.Anyway, playing this is time well spent, so far.Having said that: For me, some of the characters do feel fleshed out allright-ish, all in all... but in other occasions they just act plain / dumb - kinda sad.More dialogue/chances to talk would have probably fixed that problem.Most annoying Bugs encountered:- You cannot move back to your original position after e.g. "talking" / evolving in battle... just do these things always first, before moving your Digimon.- The englisch translation... and some of the labels... not really happy about the way it is and how it was implemented.Both can be argued against, though, I bet.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics quality is good on the overall, albeit the level of care for details is slightly heterogeneous.Despite the incipit being very good, the narrative is unfortunately peppered with incoherences and several purely specious lengthinesses. The software isn't well optimized: everytime a new area is loaded, the fps fluctuate for a few dozens of seconds before stabilizing. This happens on a machine that has a way more powerful hardware than the one recommended by the developers. During the fights, it's possible to let the artificial intelligence play in your place; howewer it doesn't use items or abilities that heal when needed, it doesn't evolve the digimons (unless a specific strategy is selected) and it often doesn't efficiently uses the resources. The difficulty level is, on the overall, coherent with its description. Often the software doens't correctly detect the position the cursor clicked at, resulting in selecting the option below the desired one. During the fights it's not possible to calibrate the camera rotation, which sometimes makes it difficult to see beyond some obstacles. Good quality on the overall, with a convincing voice acting. Good quality on the overall; the tracks are coherent with the circumstances they are played in. On the overall, I don't recommend this game because, despite the idea to keep the Digimon brand alive through a visual novel is indeed very good, the narrative of this game is seriously damaged by many incoherences and specious lengthinesses.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoys the genre and the IP I did want to like this. But it's half-formed as both a strategic RPG and a visual novel. On the combat side, there's potential in the idea of switching forms back and forth to manage your MP-analogue resource, but there is no urgency to the battles, so you can easily optimize the fun out by just waiting to recover your resources. That is, if you even had to considering that several hours in I'm still waiting for the combat to have any level of challenge. It's also missing basic srpg things like terrain details (there's an elevation mechanic but you can't be sure what elevation something is until you try to go up or down it) and combat objectives. On the VN side, the moment-to-moment decisions fail. There's a part early on where you decide as a team whether to move out and explore or hole up and stay put, and the group takes some time to cool down and reconvene to decide later. During this time, some of your group just moves out to explore, which would be an interesting thing to have character conflict over--except when you get back together the argument starts again as though nothing happened. There are free time mechanics, but at least twice in my experience there were exactly as many time-spending options as I had units of time to spend. There are some good points--some of the character work is competent and the aesthetic as a whole is incredibly crafted. I know it sounds simple but I'm constantly impressed by the sense of scale that was able to be implied by characters that each take up only one unit on the combat grid. But those aren't nearly enough for me to recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played a visual novel-style game before but watched a review beforehand so I knew what I was getting into. This game's biggest weakness is its style - because it's not for everyone - yet, if you give it a chance, I think it'll surprise you; as it did with me.The story is classic Digimon. A bunch of kids get ripped into a different world, meet their partners, and save the world. I've played these games since the first Digimon World, and from memory, I gotta say - this is the darkest, most gut-wrenching one.Your actions have real consequences on the outcomes, and any character (just about) can be a bad decision or two away from death. The characters are believable, entertaining and grow throughout the story. It's very character driven at the beginning, with the real plot only showing itself towards the end (but you do get some crumbs here and there that'll tip it off early on). Loved the game, and if you're a fan of the series I'd say grab it with some tempered expectation that you're not getting a Digimon World or Cyber Sleuth-style game. With all that said, I do just have one grievance. ******Spoilers ahead*******I was not a fan of the true ending being locked behind New Game+. _childDocuments_.review: I was really quite excited to play this game. I thought it would be akin to a Devil Survivor-esque game with a Digimon reskin, but it is much shallower than that, with less interesting gameplay mechanics, and a poorly written story that could have done with a few more QC and editing passes. Overall, I would not recommend this game to anyone, as there is little to be found here that can't be found elsewhere, done better. A shame, as my two favourite genres in interactive media are visual novels and strategy RPGs, but this game provides no satisfaction in either aspect.I will start with my main gripe: the story is atrociously written. Much of the drama that arises happens due to convenient circumstance or because the characters are actively too stupid to figure out a better course of action. Characters will take turns holding the idiot ball for extended periods of time just to make stupid decisions that make things worse for everyone and cause unnecessary drama. Sure, some of the plot beats have a cool resolution or callback to the animated show of my childhood, but relying on nostalgia to carry weak writing only can go so far before patience wears thin. One strength of the game, at least, is its ability to generate emotion from me. Specifically, the emotions of utter disgust and hatred. I absolutely detested most of the cast in this game. I found it almost impressive how they managed to hand craft a cast of such intensely unlikable characters. Even the main character is a spineless simpleton who never says anything meaningful due to the game's unwillingness to hand over the reins and allow us to make decisions that matter. Our dialogue choices range from milquetoast to outright meaningless at worst. So often in my playthrough I chose a dialogue option that was promptly skimmed over by the cast, then disregarded in favour of something else. Why even present the illusion of choice, if only to shatter it seconds later?The rebuttal to my above point is that those dialogue choices affect the karma system of the game. However, the only things that karma affects are the evolution line that Agumon takes, and the final route that the story goes with. I have even heard that it doesn't even do that competently either, as some have reported that you can just choose whatever ending you want to get when prompted at the relevant story decision, regardless of karma. If that is the case, then why even have a karma mechanic at all? It just seems like something shoehorned in for the sake of having that illusion of choice.The tactics RPG gameplay is pretty bad as well. It somehow manages to land in the sweet spot of being hilariously easy, while being infuriating and time-wasting. There were so many moments where I found myself questioning the necessity of even having gameplay, as all it seemed designed to do was pad out an otherwise mediocre visual novel. I distinctly recall a map where all the enemies just ran away from me and guarded, seemingly for no purpose other than to waste my time. If the gameplay is so uninteresting that it adds nothing to the experience of the game, again, I find myself asking, what is the point?If you've read up until now, you might have noticed a common thread in my criticisms of this game. There is just no reason for this game to exist. The story is mediocre at best, bogged down by one of the worst main casts I have ever had to suffer through. Both core mechanics of the game present no meaningful contributions to the game as a whole. I believe that this game was made for those who are really down bad for Digimon content, but even if that's you, you should honestly skip this title. It doesn't respect your time nor your intelligence, and the highlights of the game are carried hard by nostalgia, not good writing, nor good gameplay. Especially at this price point, you'd think they even bothered to proofread their script. If you're interested in this game, don't be. Go play one of the Devil Survivor games instead. Those games achieve nearly everything this game set out to do, but with generally likeable casts, a competent story, and much more interesting gameplay. Or if you haven't already, check out the Utawarerumono trilogy. Either of those series will provide you with a much better experience than anything that can be found here, while still roughly aligning in the same genre of game.

_childDocuments_.review: A disclaimer for potential buyers, if large amounts of dialogue and reading aren't your thing, back out now. This game is a visual novel first and a tactical rpg second.With that out of the way, this game really captures the essence of the original Digimon Adventures television series, both in it's characters and story. I honestly found myself thoroughly enjoying it despite a predictable story and character tropes. That being said, the story can get pretty dark, and is clearly targeting a very specific audience of fans: specifically, those of us who have been with the franchise since the beginning who crave the nostalgia of Isekai-style Digimon storytelling who are now quite a bit older and can also be confronted with more adult topics such as death. I do find myself wishing the tactical rpg portion of the game was more prominent. It's a good system, allowing you to equip items to your digimon, recruit wild Digimon through talking (giving me Shin Megami Tensei Vibes, honestly) and digivolve along any number of lines to your favorite monsters. Honestly, the two sides of the game could have easily become two entirely separate games and lost very little in terms of substance. All in all, a pretty great game with decent replay ability. If you're new to the Digimon Franchise, I'd much rather recommend Digimon World: New Order, or one from the Cyber Sleuth series - but if you're looking for a solid Digimon Title to fuel your need for nostalgia, this is the one for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing!  After 8+ hours with the game, I'm completely enthralled to see what happens nerxt. It's not going to be for everyone, though. It is a visual novel style game, which I had no idea when I first downloaded it. I knew there was a tactical grid-based battle system and I just assumed it would be a traditional RPG surrounding that, Instead its got a visual novel surrounding that which is really unique and different but in a good way it somehow works. There are choices along the way and an affinity system that dictates the direction of the story and how characters react to you. This may be common to the visual novel genre, but having never played one, I wasn't sure if branching stories and characters are a standard thing.The story, to avoid any spoilers, is very standard Digimon in the beginning. A bunch of kids end up in the digital world after a series of mysterious events. Then they meet their Digimon and begin to realize they aren't in their homeworld any more and then all the traditional Digimon weirdness starts to happen (pieces of other dimensions showing up, etc). Only, this game doesn't seem to be "digital" but some sort of world that predates Digimon. I'm sure the world will reveal itself more later but as of now there are no digivices, no real digital intervention other than the kids receiving weird encoded text messages, and no reference to the word Digimon or Digivolution at all. The story is unique and familiar. The characters are interesting and all unique to this game so far, however they follow similar archetypes to some of the classic characters from the show (the nerdy guy, the brooding guy, the studious guy, the beautiful girl, etc.) But they aren't straight rips in any way which would have turned me off if they had done so.It is literally like watching the anime. Most everything is fully voiced - of note that you HAVE to have Japanese voices and English subtitles, no English dub - and the graphics are BEAUTIFUL. It's truly like watching a top-tier anime with portraits that move and blink, animations, 3D set pieces mixed with anime backgrounds. The game is truly beautiful and looks just like you are watching the show. In fact, my only complaint with the game so far is that with all the visual production that was spent on this game, it is shocking that the awesome and classic Digi-volution scenes from the anime, with the bright colors and streams of DNA, awesome pumping music, panning on the new character, etc. is completely absent and not only that, made very ho-hum and not exciting where that should be a very important and celebrated event. Instead, the Digi-volution plays some sleepy piano music while your static Digimon sprite moves into a bright light and then moves out of the light as the a static sprite of its Digivolution. No streams of color, no cool music, no animations, nothing. It's completely shocking to me. I can understand that people would not want to watch them over and over (not me, but probably most normal people), but I would think they would have made them more "special". Even if there was the same variety of camera angles used for every Digimon, I wish they had done more for that sequence.Battles are not too challenging and so far are easy to master. You have a deck stacked in your favor and you can also adjust the difficulty down two steps from Normal if you are facing a challenge. In so doing, you receive a handicap for less damage, and the enemies receive a handycap for more damage. On the lowest difficulty all my Digimon earned one hit KOs while it would have taken an NPC 4-5 hits to defeat one of my Digimon, and you are allowed 6 of them to start with, and the largest enemy party I've seen was 2. In addition to handicaps, you also have the option to talk to opposing Digimon, and upon success you can instantly remove it from the field which would be another way to cull numbers in facing a lot of foes. So suffice it to say, Normal mode is not super challenging, but exactly what I had hoped for as someone who does not generally like Tactical Battle Systems like Fire Emblem or Final Fantasy Tactics. I just came here for the story, man.Overall, I'm really happy and pleasantly surprised by this game. When they announced it I was stoked, being a huge fan of Digimon, but when I saw tactical battle system I scratched my head and resolved it wasn't going to be for me. Upon learning it was completely not what I thought it was, I was prompted to try it, and to write this review for people who are also on the fence or who are big Digimon fans and not sure if they'd like the game.Its oozing with charm and really brings me back to those times I first watched Digimon Adventures way back in the day. It's like experiencing it anew for the first time but with a completely different lovable cast and in a video game format where I can make some direction to the story. What more could you ask for the Digimon anniversary?

_childDocuments_.review: Know what you are getting into.  The latest trailer before release was a bit misleading, pretty much only showcasing the battle system in the game.  Make no mistake, this game is 98% visual novel, and only 2% Grid-based Tactical JRPG (similar to Fire Emblem, or even more closely to the old "Digimon Adventure Cathode/Anode Tamer" games for the Bandai Wonderswan).As someone who typically doesn't play visual novels ever (in fact I think this is my very first one), I had a very hard time getting into the story at first.  I'd say the first 3-4 hours were honestly pretty boring and lack luster.  Being a digimon fan, it seems they wanted Digimon Survive to just be a greatest hits mashup or past digimon partners, human partners, and story beats that are time and again retold in digimon media.  The later parts of the story get far more interesting, right up until the end and ending, which it becomes a lazy trope that can honestly make or break the entire game for a lot of people.  I myself really didn't like the Moral or the Truthful (ending only possible on New Game+) Ending.  I'm not interested enough to try the other two, at least at this time.You have your typical male leader of the group, Takuma, who sports the classic leader goggles which enables him to have an Agumon / Dinosaur partner.  You get the girly-girl who gets a plant digimon Floramon as her partner, etc.  At least most of the partner digimon shown in the game have been partners of kids in other digimon media, whether they were characters more explored in the manga, anime, or other games.The game sports a mediocre choice system, which you pick between the Moral, Wrath, or Harmony.  These options, whichever is highest at the time, is what dictates Agumon's next evolution.  For example, Agumon's Champion/Adult evolution choices are Greymon (Moral), Tuskmon (Wrath) and Tyrannomon (Harmony).  It also effects at the end of chapter 8, which ending path you are going to go for.  Choices for which path to go will only appear if one of the three options is at 25 or above.  The game does let you save before you make your choice, which makes it easier to go right back to after you complete a path.  If you reload to do a new path however, it will be using your stats and items from where you saved at that point.  However, once you get into new game plus, another problem arises which I'll explain a little later.  Other than that, the choice system doesn't seem really story relevant or all that important outside of a single choice on New Game Plus, but that is super spoiler territory so I won't go into it just yet.The battle system is simple, but pretty fun.  It uses a rock-paper-scissors style of combat to determine weakness and resistance.  It also further stacks on Elemental weakness/resistance, and the position your character is to the enemy.  Side attacking an enemies nullifies an enemy's guard and makes them take slightly more damage too, and doing an attack from the back does double damage. It's not very complex though, and got pretty boring by the end.  I mostly just turned on auto battle and waited for a battle to end. It's pretty easy on the normal difficulty, but on a per battle basis you can at any time, lower or increase the difficulty.  The main content of the game is the Visual Novel, so honestly save yourself some headache, and throw the game onto Very Easy, and turn on auto battling.  You get no increased or decreased benefit from the difficulty like more/less EXP or different item drops.  My largest complaint is the Part 8 save spot, where it 'generously' lets you save before you pick your ending path.  There's a huge issue with this.  Once you complete a path and get one of the 3 normal endings, you are then prompted to make a CLEARED data save, which you can then load into another play through.  This is necessary to get the TRUE ending, which requires (SPOILER WARNING) .  So you have to play the entire game back up to the Chapter 8 split, where you again choose your path.  At this point though, it doesn't seem your choice path matters, because you'll get put onto the TRUE path regardless.  Now, there are 2 endings I still haven't got, The Wrath and Harmony ones.  On my New Game+ playthrough, I chose the Harmony path option, but it funneled me into the TRUE path anyway, so now at this Chapter 8 save point, It's impossible for me to do the other 2 normal endings, without intentionally , thus I would have to replay the entire game again to get to that Chapter 8 save point, it's really annoying.  There is a skip feature for dialogue you've already seen before, but even with that, it still takes HOURS to get up to the point...All in all.  I DO NOT recommend this game at $60, which is really unfortunate that for the content I played, that the price is the most damning thing about it.  If you can pick it up for maybe $20 USD, and you enjoy visual novels, it might be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Its dramatic, intense and immersive. Its definitely not perfect, but it just hit me the right way, i suppose.STORY & CHARACTERSThe characters are amazing, there is so much thought put into them. Even though there is 50+ hours of dialogue between them, i never got the feeling that they acted out-of-character. None of them are perfect and sometimes straight up annoying, but in the end this makes them even more interesting. And in the end they all grow from their mistakes. Its just great.They managed to do the same with the Digimon. They feel as alive as the human characters. But by the way, they are called "Kemonogami" and dont really have anything to do with "digital". They made their own idea of a Digimon-world and its awesome. There are several different paths. I "only" experienced two out of four. But what i have experienced i do not regret. Or do I?COMBAT/GAMEPLAYOh well... it feels like a huge incomplete idea of an interesting system. While i did play the whole game on hard (and regret that a few times, actually) i did get some strategic moments out of it. The best moment was when i realised the importance of speed buffs/debuffs and taunts. But in the end it just feels incomplete and i have more than a dozen of ideas how to improve the combat and the RPG elements. For example two different kind of equipment, one for additional skills for more combat diversity and one purely for stat improvements. But thats not so important for a review i guess.MUSIC & ARTThe game is quite long (one playthrough takes around 60-80 hours i think) and there isnt THAT much variety after a few hours. Especially music will start to repeat itself quickly. I still enjoyed everything. Especially some battle themes were really awesome.I think the developers didnt have that much time/resources and put almost all of it into the story and characters. At least thats how it feels for me.Overall i wouldnt suggest this game to everyone. If you like nice stories with nice characters this might be for you. If you like the old Digimon series, even better. But be aware that this game has mostly just dialogue/story, not much gameplay, which is sad... I would love to see a second game of this, with more focus on the gameplay!

_childDocuments_.review: A few things first:- I am a Digimon fan, the kind that fights tears as an adult when hearing Butterfly or Brave Heart- I haven't finished the game yet- I have extensive experience with Digimon games, monster taming games, and rpg games in generalTL;DR: This is a good to great Digimon game that will hit the right notes for fans.I wanted to write this review because i felt many reviews tackled this solely on how it feels as a game. I want to add my thoughts on how it feels like a Digimon game, and why I think that, despite a stormy development process, it's shaping out to be a Digimon game I am really satisfied with (I didnt like Cyber Sleuth that much, I will also tell you why).Nostalgia factor: the first Digimon anime had a few key elements for me that made it stick for decades:- exploring an unknown world that was an eerie reproduction of the real world- the feeling of dread the protagonists faced as they tried to find each other, survive and find a way home- the colorful cast, which was well rounded and grew a lot over the course of the story (i know a lot were tropes but it's a kids show)- the bond between tamer and partner, which, along with the before mentioned growth, were key elements to the plot and led to extremely cool digivolutions.So far, the game managed to nail each one of these. The story  hits the same beats of exploring, surviving, colorful cast, and growth.I've seen people complain about the amount of text and low amount of digimon, but hear me out: Your complaint is valid if you're looking for a regular monster collecting game. However, for a Digimon game I don't think being able to collect many monsters is the main drive, but the bond between tamer and mon. I played Cyber Sleuth extensively, and I was let down a bit by how collecting digimon and their evolutions felt shallow. Most mons got one specific attack, a chosen few got 2. the rest of the skills were generic with poor animation and almost no gameplay impact. Even evolutions felt unsatisfying to me, because there was no tie in to the story, the bond was reduced to a friendship meter.What Survive does right, However, is that partner mons have few evolutions (making them stand out as individuals) and participate in the story, with full blown personalities, and they grow more attached to you as it progresses. again, this is a good thing, because it evokes the feeling of the anime. Agumon also unlocks evolutions based on your VN dialogue choices, and him reflecting your personality also feels great and accurate (almost like a throwback to digimon evolving into violent, horrific forms if their trainers had an impure heart)Long story short, the VN part does an amazing job in turning your digimon into real characters and making them matter to you, and as such the low amount of Digivolutions doesnt feel like a detriment.Gameplay wise, what I feel was done accurately was the digivolutions and party support. Instead of being permanent forms, Digivolutions are now a powerup ability where you select which form you want to digivolve to, and it's done dynamically in combat, as a free action. you can choose which form you want to choose, and higher level ones will offer more stats and better abilities, but will have a higher upkeep cost in terms of SP, your skill resource. As you go along, this will be a question of wether you go all in with a mega form, or use something slightly less powerful but easier to maintain.Shortly put, either stay in rookie for low stats, but SP regen at the end of every round, or lose the SP upkeep cost at end, but have way more survivability and powerful attacks. It's really fun, and again, accurate to the anime.Support actions are something that happens automatically, based on your affinity to each character and map positioning. when you attack, a partner might cheer you and increase your damage, or cheer you up and recover your HP/SP/both. it sells the feeling of bonding and growing as a team.To add to the feeling even further, there is a talk function where tamers can cheer for the Digimon, providing super powerful stat boosts, just like in the show.the VN part was something that worried me for a while. despite all i said positively about it, it takes a while before the game 'opens up' (as much as a VN can open up), and I was worried that the digimon partners wont get much variety, and that the '30% combat' part meant that I would have to wait for when the VN threw a combat scene at me.both these fears were, i'm happy to say, unfounded. You can befriend Digimon in fights and use them as party members! you can also use the 'free battle' function to farm items, digimon and xp to your heart's content, and its usage isn't gated at all.Progression is not overtly complex, but a nice touch nonetheless. you can feed items to permanently power up your digimon, equip up to two items which provide many stats or skills, which satisfies the customisation itch for me. Digimon also have traditional levels, and leveling up gives you a ton of stats. It's not all that exciting, except for the fact that SP also grows. this might be a very dumb thing for you to see argued, but since the digivolution upkeep is a flat value, leveling up allows you to maintain a digivolved state for longer times, which again reminded me of how it became easier for the digimon to maintain them as they moved forward through the story.Outside the Digimon lens, I think the VN is beautifully drawn and richly animated. The tactics RPG side for me worked very well and is satisfying, but I don't know if it will satisfy fans of the genre, as I'm not knowledgeable enough.I hope this rambling review helped a bit in making up your mind as a fan. I didnt want to diss other people, sorry if I did, but a lot seemed to focus on the unimportant, while most fans are searching for a nostalgic high that this franchise gave them as kids, and hopefully wrapped up in a game that's decent or great. I'm happy to say that I feel Survive is such a game, and will go down as one of the better Digimon games.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon Survive is a visual novel/tactics RPG fusion. The visual novel aspect plays a much larger role than the the RPG part of the game, so do keep that in mind if purchasing this game.If you're good with that, and you're a Digimon fan, you're in for a treat. The story takes dark turns that are completely unexpected for a piece of Digimon media and they leave a lasting impact. It's a bit refreshing, actually, and the true route is a proper Digimon story through and through.The game itself isn't that hard, even on the harder difficulties. I found myself only needing to swap out crystals on a handful of fights. But if you don't take the time to level up and train your Digimon, you'll find yourself vastly underleveled and needing to rely on tactics.The game won't be for everyone, but it's worth going through, especially if you're a Digimon and/or visual novel fan!My biggest gripe has got to be the localization. Some naming choices were odd, and there some choices that make you scratch you heard in confusion. Truth be told, there weren't THAT many mistakes, but when you come across them, they stick out very noticeably.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon is a franchise full of potential, but sadly it just keeps on getting mishandled. When are we gonna get a genuinely great Digimon game?(funnily enough Digimon aren't even treated as Digimon in this game).Digimon Survive is truly terrible. The gameplay, graphics and combat being atrocious is one thing, it's not the focus of the game (this is a Visual Novel); but even the story and the characters, supposedly praised by some as"mature", "dark" and "serious"; are actually insultingly trash. This game treats the player like an idiot and forces you on a loser MC, obvious plot points either get ignored or repeated over and over, characters keep saying the dumbest things and making the dumbest decisions, etc. The game's art design and music are very good but I can't get ever get immersed in the world and the story when it keeps insulting my intelligence.  The game starts off decent but slowly gets to the point of being truly insufferable by the end of the playthrough. Maybe the True Ending route is better? Even if it is, it still doesn't matter since the devs completely locked the True Ending behind NG+ like the dumbasses they are - with how irritating the game has become for me I won't even finish the 1st playthrough, let alone starting a 2nd.Edit: This is my review of this game even after I have installed a bunch of mods to make it better before playing - Improved Translation mod, Better Free Battles mod, Affinity mod, 100% Recruitment mod; and the game still ended up being an awful experience for me.
