_childDocuments_.review: The game is a visual novel with tactical, grid & turn based combat. The visual novel aspect takes the vast majority of the game. There's also a good bit of 2d area exploration like an old pc adventure puzzle game. This allows you to explore the environment, gather extra items, do extra battles and discover different story options. The game can be fairly slow and tedious. Even the battle areas are very vast. It's not uncommon for the first round of a battle to be just movement.The story is the strongest aspect of the game, but it's also quite different than a traditional digimon story. It's a tad bit more dark and mature, but honestly just a bit. The game also leans into the horror genre with the environment/background art, but never really plays into jump scare/horror beyond that. The horror-esque environment is vastly different than your traditional digimon world as well. The music/sfx are incredibly bland and repetitive. They're probably the weakest aspect of the game.Overall, I'd give the game a 78/100. I honestly think it would've made a better anime than a game.Would recommend: The game having more soundtracks for different areas. Smaller battlefields. A faster way for searching environments, both with and without the phone. Clearing understanding of affection levels, nature of choices, routes, which answers to give digimon for befriending, etc. I know it's somewhat traditional for visual novels to be very open, branchy, and push players into using a guide/multiple replays, but it also pushes away players who aren't hardcore VN fans just here for Digimon.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon Survive

_childDocuments_.review: THIS IS A VISUAL NOVEL.YOU WILL BE READING A LOT.90% OF THE GAME IS READING STORY AND PLOT.DO NOT BUY IF YOU HATE READING.Got that out of the way? Good!----Digimon Survive is incredible. To sum it up, you've been isekai'd into a world full of dangers where Digimon sacrifice human kids for nefarious reasons. With your ragtag group of friends and Digimon companions, you're forced to fight to survive and try and make it home in one piece.  Or...can you...?Some pros:  -Art is incredible. The sprites have a lot of character to them and the battle sprites are lively. There's some weird issues with some of the character's faces whenever they blink and you can tell they used Live2D to make the models as whenever they leave, the bodies despawn in 'layers'.-Combat is shockingly difficult. If you don't angle your Digimon just right, bring the right team, or have a healer you're probably in trouble. I recommend looking at the WHOLE map as sometimes Digimon spawn behind you and you have no idea.-The story is DARK.  I haven't beaten it yet but so far we're dealing with suicidal thoughts, death, implied sexual assault, nihilism, depression, mental illnesses, and the like. The game might seem cheerful but there's a lot of things that make it feel a lot more mature than other games.Some cons:-It wasn't beta read. There's a LOT of grammatical errors and in a visual novel where reading is 90% of the gameplay, that's an issue.--Some characters are just awful. You understand where they're coming from but it's just annoying dealing with them. Yes, you're upset you're stuck here but please get your head out of your ass.--♥♥♥♥ Shuuji, he sucks.--A lot of the dialogue...doesn't make sense. And I don't mean that in a 'this was translated wrong'. I mean either the MC Takuma is an idiot or they just rinse and repeat.  For example, Takuma will ask 'what do you think?' and a character will answer, to which they ask HIm what HE thinks and he's like 'hmm, idk, what do YOU think?" over and over.-The game HEAVILY implies that your choices matter but I've save scummed live on stream and chose a different answer and got a similar outcome. As a spoiler, there's a part where you can leave a character behind by themself, with help, or bring them with you.  No matter what you choose, said character goes with you.  So don't feel like your choices ARE set in stone.Now, again, this is a visual novel and the story is compelling but you might find yourself very bored at times.  However, when you get to the meat of it, the story is incredibly deep and fulfilling, but it can be a bit of a slog to get through. If you're a fan of Digimon or visual novels, this game is well worth the price and has a ton of replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon Survive

_childDocuments_.review: I waited a loooong time for this one, and for the most part I enjoyed what we got, but I definitely have my share of critiques. Let's start with the good. Compared to past Digimon games, the story in Digimon Survive is actually interesting and engaging through and through. If you loved the Adventure series as a kid there's a good chance you'll like Survive since it quite resembles it in some few aspects - kids getting isekai'd into a different world during summer camp, partner digimons bonding (or not) with their partner humans and becoming developed characters in their own right (or not), etc. Maybe it's my nostalgia kicking in, but I genuinely think Survive's story is really good, the Digimon team should start turning such concepts into anime instead of VNs because people hate VNs and I'm afraid such a story won't be available for a wider audience. Now the bad. Sadly the game was made on a very low budget and it shows. The SRPG aspect is barebones and while the VN segments are probably the best part, it still has some pacing issues, most notably near the end. Pretty clear there is some cut content, like the SkullGreymon evolution; and there are way too few Digimons and that's probably my main issue with the game, like, only one hundred and something Digimon? Come on, Bamco. In fairness, Survive was always meant to be a side thing and as it stands is a decent game, good if you're a Digimon fan like me, but it really shouldn't have been 60 bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon Survive

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game if you enjoy visual novels and games like fire emblem.The story was very nice and there were moments I was surprised with how grim this game could be, there were moments were I found myself semi-skipping the story since they sometimes talked for a LONG time about the same point, but this was only for a few minutes max.  I really enjoyed myself playing this game and trying to befriend a ton of Digimon. I currently have 1 route completed and will edit this review once I've done the other 2 routes and the true ending---Well, I've finally done it. Did the 2 other routes and the true ending. Now I have to say that getting the 2 other routes wasn't the most fun, a few things are different but not enough to keep my attention going sometimes. The True ending was the most interesting to me and i found myself paying attention to the story again. Now getting 100% achievements was frustrating, the "encounter all digimon" should be "obtain all digimon" since I did all of the stories, saw all the digimon and the achievement didn't pop. After a bit or research, I found out that you need to obtain them all; causing me to have to go through one more route up to part 10 to get the last digimon I needed.Overal I did enjoy my time playing it but having to go through the story at least 4 times for 100% wasn't the most fun. So I would give this game a 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The 'talk' system sucks. No depth; you just memorize answers.Your actions literally have no effect on the story;  no matter what. (You can't pester him or do anything that might change that no matter what) A Telltale game even feels like you might be changing something even if it's intended for a forced outcome to happen.Not everything is voiced, but there's no consistency as to what is and isn't; even some main story bits are unvoiced."Free time" is linear; the passage of time is kinda pointless since in chronological means, it's probably an hour, but in the end you're still funnelled to certain choices or a certain path and can still exhaust all dialog within that time "limit".Digivolution felt like an anime gimmick (like in the literal sense where you're in the shoes of the characters using it willy-nilly) - You run up as Rookies then Digivolve.The only "choice" you make is a variant in tone about certain events, which increase Wraith, Moral and Harmony (which are three stats that only affect how easily you can get certain types of side characters )They seriously over-hyped this game.If you were just here for a run-of-the-mill Digimon anime in game form, well, you got it. But for what they promised... Not so much.If this was an anime, it would be an instant recommend... But because it's a game, well, there's the problem. I think the visual novel is great, not so much the execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This is a visual novel which I did not realize upon purchasing. I went into this title expecting similar game play to other major Digmon titles such as the Digimon World series or Cyber Sleuth which this game is not anything like. But that was my own fault for not looking at the tags or doing research prior to purchasing.One other note: THIS VISUAL NOVEL IS NOT WORTH THE $60 PRICE POINT UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCES! Please wait until a sale prior to purchasing this title. I would recommend $30 at the highest and aiming for a sale with a $20 price point. Also the first month bonus is nice, but not nice enough to make up the difference in value I personally find in this title.Ok with that out of the way here are some bullet points:Pros:- Riveting story line if you make it through the first hour slog.- Artwork is well done and fun to look at- The character designs really suck you in. Some characters you fall in love with, others... well lets say I dont like them. But it means they were designed fairly well.Cons:- The actual story beat tactical battles are few and far between- None of the battles are difficult even on the hardest settings- No additional awards for beating battles at higher difficulties- All the fights can be brute forced with minimal tactical thought- Very repetitive character interactions with choices that dont seem to have any effect on anything other than your main mon.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon Survive

_childDocuments_.review: If you are or ever were a fan of the Digimon anime and ever wanted to play a video game that was basically that, this is the game for you. There's so much about this game that reminds me of Adventure 01, especially, in a "yeah, I could see them turning this into an actual TV series" without feeling like they actually copied any of the preexisting anime (the similarities between this game and Adventure 01 are largely superficial). That being said, once it's lulled you into a sense of familiarity, making you think "I've see both Digimon Adventure anime, Tamers, Frontier, etc, I bet I know what's going to happen or how this situation will turn out," it's going to go in a completely different direction and make you think "Oh wow, they really went there!"Disclaimer that, while I compared this to the Digimon anime, Adenture 01 in particular, the demographic for this game is *not* the same as the demographic for the anime. This game made me sit back and consider the fact that Digimon may have been a horror series this entire time, except unlike the anime, this game doesn't hold back on it and really leans into the darker, more horrific aspects of the franchise, while openly dealing with some really dark themes (abuse, suicide, death, etc).
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon Survive

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great game especially for old school Digimon fans, the VN style is surely not for everybody, but aside from that, the graphic is beautiful, the characters are great, and the Shin Magami Tensei style monster recruitment stuff is tough but very cool. _childDocuments_.review: First things first. If you want to play this game, you should know that this is a visual novel. That means the fighting aspect is actually really small, 80% is a full on novel. The point is interacting and feeling with the characters.And it is a damn good story. It's kinda like Season 1, at least it makes a few callbacks, but it's much darker. You will grow on some characters, while you start to dislike others. And then you will reach the point, where you wish you acted differently.I don't want to spoil anything for the story, because it spun a few twists on me I did not see coming in the slightest.From standard-heroic moments to a bit comedy to lighten the mood, everything is included. Even moments, that made me feel genuinely heartbroken, which I did not expect at all. And this did not happen only once.So you should defintely enjoy playing VN or readings books. Otherwise, this game might not be your cup of tea.But if you can get into a story and want a different Digimon experience, this is a must have!

_childDocuments_.review: Finally finished the game. I rather this game than replaying Cybersleuth again lolFirst off I have to claim that I hate Visual Novels, its a genre that I have a hard time liking. I was skeptical at first to get this game but as it is a Digimon game I just didnt mind too much as I love Digimon. Dont get this game at full price unless you really like Visual Novel or Digimon. This game should be 30% or 40% off.So lets discuss what makes a Digimon game, well Digimon. The best part about Digimon is that you are not limited to a single tree of evolution for the Digimons, for example my Agumon can turn to Greymon, but yours might be Tyranomon. Fortunately, this is implemented in the game for almost all Digimon and best part is that your main Digimon will evolve based on your choices in the game which is Moral, Wrathfullness and Harmony. However, Free Digimon(Digimon that you befriend) Digivolution does not need any required stats but instead needs some sort of evolution items that looks like SD card, Floppy disk and Hard Disk. This is ultimately a cons for a Digimon game as there is little requirement to train the Digimon with stat boosting items aside from making them stronger.Tactics battle is a welcome change and makes you wish it is the main core of the game albeit this is not the case. The tactics part of the game is basic and does not require that much strategical confrontation unlike other tactics game like Final Fantasy Tactics. However, what they did right is the Visual Novel aspects as unlike any other VN that I gave up on are very slow and annoying to navigate, this game however the UI feels very snappy and is easy to navigate from one point to another. There are some bugs tho like Agumon will phrase my lines instead and etc but happens when you progress or read too fast that the game fails to keep pace.The narrative is what you would appreciate from Digimon franchise. Its kind of decent and mature. The game is not afraid to show you what failure bonding or training does to your Digimon and I appreciate it. From what I think, this game is for the Digimon Anime fans. If you love the Anime you will find your home here.Is this a good game? No. Not by a longshot. Is this a good anime? yes. Very good anime. Is this a good Digimon game? Depends, it stays true in making the narrative similar to the anime except much more mature.To be frankly honest I'd say this fails to recapture what makes a Digimon game be Digimon. But succeeds in recapturing the Digimon Adventure anime.|The game's soundtrack is very good tho, the boss battle particularly is my favourite soundtrack.tldr;-Tactics is basic-Digivolution doesnt have stat requirements like other Digimon games-Narrative is pretty good, Takuma the main protagonist is really good at reading the room-Plot twists are pretty good-good OSTs-Snappy navigation2/5. Decent. Playing this game makes me want to play other Digimon games but not CybersleuthALSO HABU PLEASE FOR THE LOVE OF GOD PORT NEXT ORDER TO STEAM

_childDocuments_.review: I know a lot of people are upset about the game, but I'm a firm believer that this product is doing what it set out to do. If you'd been following the updates on this game from the beginning, then you should know that the game is pretty much exactly as the developers advertised: it is a visual novel. While it does have some tactics style elements to it, the game is a VISUAL NOVEL. If you're a fan of the Digimon anime because of its story, themes, and characters, you probably will like this game. If you're a fan of tactics games, you might not (there are few battle opportunities). That said, the battles themselves are decent and not as bare bones as I would have expected from a title like this.As a visual novel this is probably one of the better titles I've played in a long time even with the Digimon skin attached. It's got a pretty cool branching system of morals and interesting characters. Everything you do / say does effect the game and your ability to digivolve into certain lines. There aren't that many Digimon available in the game itself (only 113 at release). There's an in-game recruitment system so you can have multiple Digimon in your party outside of the one assigned to you (Agumon) and your friends (Falcomon, Kunemon, Labramon, etc).There's some horror elements so be warned if you dont like that kind of stuff. There was one jump scare in chapter one that was pretty jarring. The game has a very somber/suspenseful feel to it and they don't shy away from heavy themes / character death.Beyond that, Minoru is the best boy. I don't make the rules I just write them.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon Survive

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely yes! My expectations weren't as high despite the full price.. and I'd like to think that overall  isn't all terrible. My first walkthrough was Moral route, took like 70 hours due to afk and unnecessary grinds, and only came back to continue all other routes + 100% at 6 months later.Yes and no. While the game may have marketed as hybrid Visual novel + tactical RPG, don't let that trick you into thinking  is sRPG with a little mix of VN, because it isn't exactly like what many people have expected before buying. It turns out more of a VN instead, there are loads of text to be read than going into adventure to befriend Digimons, exploring places and fighting baddies etc.. hence the disappointment in some fans. Characters' dialogues are not fully-voiced, only partial. There is some other interactions such as using phone camera to discover hidden items and shadow battles. If you've watched the classic  anime, you'd find some of the characters here have slight resemblance to them, while there were also a moment that reminds of . Story-wise is much more matured. So if you're into Digimon but also enjoys VN too and/or simply likes reading, then yes. If you are expecting for more actions, highly immersive gameplay, wide variety of monster collections and explorations here.. I'd suggest to avoid this. I personally haven't played enough Digimon games to recommend any other than this for better gameplay, but the one title I've truly enjoyed was  on Story were mysteriously dark and nicely written, albeit some parts of the text seemed to be quite a mess to read. Filled with quite the number of grammatical errors. Translation seemed awful, it almost felt like they are entirely machine translated. The story in the beginning is very slow-paced, but engaging enough to keep the readers intrigued. There are 4 Routes to be experienced;  and  Truthful Route will only be unlocked in NG+ with the right requirements. There's a Bad Ending at specific chapter but it does not unlock any achievement by doing so. Each route will take in between 30-40 hours on average, depending on player's reading speed, activity etc. Meanwhile Digimon list in this game isn't as huge, there's only 117 in total  Some Digimons are highly missable from Shadow Battles and Story, so keep that in mind if you are trying to collect all for the achievement. Some characters can appear to be very unlikeable, but each has their own background story, some will be explained later in the same route or another. Affinity-related choices matter but somehow not in every situation, pretty much scripted on each route, though having high affinity would still help greatly in most battles. I find a few sound designs to be rather odd, while the OSTs were really good. Gorgeous arts, not to mention the main theme sounds amazing, I can almost never get tired of hearing it! There's one weird little thing that kinda bugs me in a way was that.. they shorten "Free Battle" as "Free Bat." for some reason, which can be confusing for first time players. Then there's one issue I often have to deal was that, since I have multiple monitors, when I switch to other tabs, the game will suddenly render incredibly high FPS  that caused my GPU's temperature to rise so much despite having V-Sync ON in settings. "Skip" function don't always work either. Combat gameplay is pretty fun, although it can be rather repetitive over time and the viewing angles might need a bit of improvement.The game sure has their flaws, but that didn't stop me from loving the game still, and I'd only  recommend to get it on sale if you are practically into VN and doesn't mind some of their tedious dialogues with grammatical errors. Also if you do play the game, perhaps could give it a try at going for Truthful Route in NG+ some time even if you don't feel like spending more time for other routes or 100%, the story just gets better there (or at least satisfying) and worth it imo.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played games like Danganronpa then this might interest you as 'choices' will definitely affect how you progress in the game. Being a Digimon fan myself I expected something similar to what I've played with the other digimon titles, but sadly I was mistaken as the title having 'survive' made more sense as I play it longer. This is 'NOT' a game for people who wants more gameplay though as it is more story-rich with lengthy chapters and repetitive battles to grind for loot. However, the main story is 'voiced' which makes it more tolerable than other visual novel games. The game devs applied a 'skip' and 'auto' which saves you from stress or smashing that next button as you can play the game in windowed mode to also multitask like read the walkthrough while you progress. Overall, having played this more than once to get all achievements, I do recommend using a walkthrough for this game as it becomes really tedious and in fact you get more from of the story with a walkthrough than scum saving on each choices (although I do recommend just playing your first playthrough blindly if you want the game to be more of a challenge). Definitely not a recommended game for people who are not Digimon fans, but definitely something people might buy if they are a fan of the series and having alot of time on their hands as this game kinda shows an understanding the lore how Digimon got digitalized.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the 'Digimon' franchise, I would like share my experience with this game.Pros:+ Amazing visuals: One of the best looking sprites and animations I have seen in a visual novel. The user interface is also really good.+ Darker tone: As a game targeted toward the original fans, I really love how they took a more mature approach to the story.+ Music: The background music in this game is very atmospheric and really matches the situation.+ Voice segments: The voice actors' performances are really good. The way each character conveys different emotions is amazing.+ Choice system: Game has branching paths. Each dialogue effects your digimon's evolution path, as well as story scenarios.Cons:- Pacing issues: Beginning can be slow and some chapters have been padded to just to make them unnecessarily longer.- Lackluster battle system: The SRPG section, despite being passable, is not really good compared to standard SRPGs and lacks variation. - Translation errors: A lot of translation feels rushed, has a lot of grammatical errors and bad sentence construction. There are also lots of typos.- True route required: As others have stated, having to replay the game to get the true ending is kind of hassle and may cause fatigue in players. Overall, I really enjoyed the game and appreciate this more mature storytelling for the franchise. I would rate the game 7.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Over an hour into the game and you only see Digimon in the opening scene.This is NOT a Digimon game. It is a Visual Novel with the skin and name of Digimon. So stay away if you liked any previous Digimon game and are looking for a similar experience.Ill preface this by saying that I like VN and choice based only story driven games such as The Quarry, Doki Doki, As Dusk Falls, and Heavy Rain.  You're introduced to a bunch of dull characters that have little to no substance aside from the tropes their role is supposed to fill. MC brought from another world who lost his family.The cute nice girl you just met.The happy go lucky "best friend".The rude popular boy.The popular girl who follows the rude boy around.The annoying class president.The local guy.I do not doubt that the characters get more development and actual character as the game progresses. But they expect you to slog though at least 2 hours of the same old anime trope story with lackluster characters before you get to any of that or gameplay.When you have a game that is comprised of different genres(Visual Novel, Tactical RPG, JRPG) you should spend time making sure all of those elements are present in the game and not just focus on one element making the game completely devoid of the others for long stretches of time. You start off with a combat tutorial immediately, but then do nothing aside from VN for the next ~2 hours (based on my experience and other reviews).I have refunded the game and do not recommend anybody buy this game at its current price point. Instead wait for it to go on sale if you're a really big fan of Digimon or Visual Novels. I may pick it back up again for a 50% off or more sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing a review as someone who hasn't beaten the game quite yet but has played more than enough to know how I feel about it.This game isn't like Cyber Sleuth. But that's not a bad thing. This game puts the story first and does so very well in one of the most visually interesting visual novels I've played. It's not your average, 2 or 3 characters on either side of the static png background. It does a good job of using the VN aspects to flesh out the area you're in.The tactical RPG mechanics are pretty basic. As far as I've played, it doesn't do more than it needs to in terms of complexity. As a fan of tactical RPGs I was initially upset that the game didn't center around the combat, but I'm glad it didn't forget about it either. It's fun enough that I enjoy the battles when I get to them.Honestly the strength of this game. The story unfolds in a way I can easily see being a more serious themed digimon show. It starts off slow but has you invested when you reach part 2. There isn't much to say without spoiling it, but fans of a good narrative and digimon will appreciate the lengths the team has gone through to provide us with a story worth seeing through. I have no idea what's going to happen, but I've enjoyed every step of the way.My main gripes would have to be mostly on what I expected. Up until a couple days before release, I was under the impression that this would be primarily an RPG. Personally I would have enjoyed more emphasis on that. The combat is rather shallow without too much opportunity for much variation. Although that could change in the later parts of the game.The controls for the game feel a bit weird initially. Using mostly the letter keys on the left side of the keyboard leaves your hand hovering in an awkward position as you hit "confirm" or "cancel" and accidentally hit the "Fast Forward" button and miss some dialogue.--------------------------------------------------------------------------Digimon Survive is a great Visual Novel first and an okay Tactical RPG second. If you're a fan of a compelling story that puts you in a darker themed digimon adventure, you'll enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say this is probably the best Digimon game I've ever played. The music, the art, the characters, the story, it's all utterly fantastic to my eyes. Feels like a hearty blend of Digimon Adventure and Digimon Tamers that I am all about.The digivolution mechanics are very nice and have a much better flow compared to other digimon games I've played, and the overall combat feels very good. The visual novel segments also feel quite nice, though I sometimes wish the dialog options would give the first sentence to let me know exactly what I'm saying, as there has been one or two times it felt off. Not nearly as much as Fallout 4's dialog wheel, but still.Overall, if you enjoy tactic RPGs, Digimon or both, I highly recommend Digimon Survive.

_childDocuments_.review: As a digimon fan I'm down for almost anything related, digimon world on the PS1 to Cyber Sleuth (skipping DS) and this puts a spin on things. This is a VNRPG, VISUAL NOVEL basically lots of pictures and short clips, lots of gameplay but you'll mostly be reading. VNs are not for everyone but certain VNs peak peoples interests so if you dont like VNs period you may not want to take this up, but if you like some VNs or havent touched a VN I implore you, play another VN and keep trying and see if you find one you like.1. GAMEPLAY/STORY I'm putting these 2 together because its a bit different then your standard T game. Its a Tactical VNRPG. The game is EXTREMELY long, like VERY VERY long, its a VN, VNs take story and put it to the extreme focusing on voice acting and pictures. Its a tactical RPG, positioning, weaknesses, attributes, you need to know what gives you an advantage, I was playing on normal because I usually like playing on normal for the most neutral experience but it was actually getting kinda easy so I switched to hard and holy hell I got smacked around a lot, I had to be 10 levels higher to make things easier, and that was at level 5. Literally got a new character to join my team mid fight (a part of story in mid-late) and the boss straight up 1 shotted him so hard mode is no joke. It does get better as you progress, i'd say around 2-5 levels above is standard for hard mode when your in the 30-40s. For me personally the story is definitely a plus, its just different from what we would usually see, its waaaay darker then any other game from this series. Its like when you watch TV and you see the rating TV14, its more like on the edge of M, but you just add anime. Very typical anime story line (which is completely fine) about bonds, and friendship blah blah blah, but still very nice. 2. GRAPHICS The Graphics on the game isnt your typical 3D model (except for DS ver.) turn based move game as some previous titles. The digimon are a flat 2D seemingly 3D image across a 2.5D plane which is actually really cool, the quality of the graphics are really crisp and nice, the digimon and characters arent defined like what you would normally see but the 2D smol look of them dont look that bad.3. Anything BAD? For me personally, the only thing I would have liked to see is a more defined roster, I do like how they give lots of digimon that arent that well known lots of spot light but at the same time I really wish we had gotten some more in here. Hopefully we either get some really good artists, animators, and modders, or we get some updates.

That being said, the game is genuinely one of the best digimon games I've played in a while. The story can get INCREDIBLY dark, but it makes everything stand out and shows that your decisions are actually important. There are several ways the story can go, plus a new game plus route. _childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this game is a Visual Novel, not an SRPG.Second, as a longtime Digimon fan I can safely say that unless you're a fan of the franchise, you won't be getting a lot of enjoyment out of this game.Third, temper your expectations. This game went through development hell but don't let the delays trick you into thinking the game is a massive, ambitious project where every choice you make affects the story in a meaningful way. For the most part, they don't. The only choice you have is the route you end up on, and even then the game lets you know how to make the right decisions to end up on those routes, so the feeling of being unsure of your decisions and not knowing what effect they'll have is never there. That being said, there are very little surprises in the story, especially for someone familiar with Digimon. Despite all that, I can't truly say that I did not enjoy this game for what it is. It's a nice little treat for Digimon fans even if it isn't up there with some of the best that this franchise has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: As the show case for survive showed it's a visual novel game first and forth most. The game is a story about people and Digimon Surviving through a situation.Honestly being a few hours into the game now I know I'll love it myself. I'm a fan of digimon and JRPG's. Just like Cyber Sleuth we get a ton of talking to help build characters and the world. It's great for that. I think right away the translating is obviously better. Hackers Memory had better translating then normal Cyber, but this one does it better probably because a more straight laced visual novel.Like many visual novels though this has some other gameplay within it. Using vtuber like 2d character models, the characters have some movement and talk as well. They are not just crusty 3D models, or png's. Honestly I find it pretty neat that the exploring section of the game is more like a Phoenix Wright game. You interact with the back drop and move around it to try and solve basic puzzles. But this having a form of combat you also find digimon to fight against or items to help you in battle.Now onto the combat- I am actually surprised how much you can battle. At first I thought it would be like 80% visual novel. But you can battle a bunch pretty quickly. Capturing different digimon and leveling already feels a bit addicting to me. The back drops for battle really does remind me of a combo of xcom and Disgaea... Probably lean more toward Disgaea where positioning can matter for what direction you face. But you also get team abilities and can deploy so and so many units to a battle field. And some battle fields have terrain blocks or elevated platforms etc. Like for anyone who may play this game and complain it's a visual novel when it says it's a visual novel and the producer said it was mostly a visual novel- is odd. Meanwhile I am over here surprised how much combat it has haha. One thing people may or may not mention is it has a base area you could call it where you can free battle digimon without even having to find them through exploring. You could over level, capture a ton of digimon, get a bunch of items. From free battling a bunch if you really wanted to. Honestly the game is more like it is a visual novel, and you can battle as much as you actually want to. You don't need to battle a bunch, but you can if you like that side of the game more. If you wanna capture the mon, train the mon, get items from the mons. You can totally do that. I suppose if you ignore the tutorial and don't know how to read you could skip over such functions. But if you want a visual novel with some detective/exploring, that's there. If you want battling and training making number go up. That's there. If you want both together, that's there. If you rather focus on one or the other. Ya can.If you like digimon. You get to hear the required "Agumon!" and have your life enriched.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll probably try to finish this game at some point, but as far as I'm concerned, it's very, VERY boring. I should start by saying that I actually don't have a problem with the idea of this game, but rather, the execution of it. I'm of the opinion that this game could basically be divided into two sections (although acting as though it's a 50/50 split would be a bit disingenuous). Story=======================It should be noted that Digimon Survive is primarily a Visual Novel, and it's basically a retelling of Season 1 of Digimon with different characters and a mildly different, albeit more detailed, plot than the anime. That in and of itself isn't a bad thing, as I feel that the story of kids going on a school retreat, and then being whisked away into the Digital World to be a cool concept that's rife with potential, you can go in several directions with it, so even if it's a premise that the franchise itself has already used, that doesn't mean that it's going to be a bad game because of it. However, my problem with it, is that the story's writing-- whether it's because of a mediocre localization, or the story itself is just that poorly told, results in an incredibly unfulfilling plot. I haven't played more than about 6 hours of it, but I can guarantee that most of the story has been reading. That's fine, but it's very slow and boring. "What should we do?" "We should go explore!" "Do you think exploring is such a good idea?" "Well if we do not explore, we will not find out what we are going to do!" "But if we explore we could die!" "But if we don't explore, we will die as well." These aren't exact quotes from the game, but you get my point, the game has a tendency to have very slow repetitive dialogue for no real reason. I don't mind dialogue having slow moments in a story-- especially if the setup pays off, but so far, none of it has. Combine that with the gameplay of having to constantly talk to everyone in a room to "hear what they have to say," and everyone splitting off in various directions and adding "gameplay" of sifting through menus to have to talk to all of them, makes for a very tedious experience from a narrative perspective. The game even has an affection system within the game that seems to have some effect on your partner's evolutions, but NOT in the way that you'd think. IE, it's not that being mean to someone can cause them to have one branch of evolution while being nice to them causes them to have another path (this would have been kinda cool to be honest, they could have had say, a person you were mean to get devimon lines but if you were nice they get angemon or something). Instead, the only thing that it does is make for a moment where you're probably going to want to have a guide because not having the right amount of affection simply means that you don't get their Mega forms for that playthrough. Speaking of different playthroughs, you'll probably have to play through this game more times than just once, as the game doesn't let you see the "True" ending on your first playthrough, and without playing NG+, you'll be missing pieces of the story and dealing with different paths which -- while they could be potentially interesting, don't mean much in the grand scheme of things because they decided to go with true route / not true route style paths with one of them obviously being canon and the other ones not. Can't say I'm a fan of games that have branching paths that have a canon path like this, because it just makes it feel like they should have just had the canon path be the only route and fleshed it out more instead of having 4 underdeveloped ones. Granted you DO get some character insights on different paths that you wouldn't beforehand, but that requires you to be invested in these rather drab characters to care enough. If you are, that's fantastic, and I could see you enjoying the game, but if you find the poor localization and repetitive dialogue annoying to sift through, you aren't going to find this as a positive. The story needs massive work in my eyes if it's going to be the main draw of the game. At least with other games in the franchise, even when they had mediocre stories, the gameplay was at least passable at worst. Here? I'm not so sure. Gameplay===============To be quite frank? It's awful. It does almost nothing interesting or right about it for me to really compliment. First of all, you have a very small number of mons that you can deploy, and with non-storyline monsters that you recruit, you can't even do all of the mechanics with them-- such as using the tamers to talk to said monsters and giving them various buffs based off of the tamer (would have been cool if different forms were based off of which monsters you let be trained by other units). So instead, you're probably going to want to use the storyline characters for the most part-- besides maybe the free Guilmon you get, because there's no reason to use randoms that don't have nearly as many resources on their side... Not that you'd need to, because the gameplay is incredibly shallow and easy even with it being in "hard mode." Digimon can basically only have 2 moves naturally, and perhaps a couple of more depending on the accessories that you have equipped. I'm sorry, but 2 moves is simply not enough to do anything interesting. So you have a tank digimon, and it has an attack move that's single target, and then an attack move that's AoE. That's it. Nothing really interesting with status effects, nothing interesting about positioning really, just... Attack and attack. And even if they were, the interesting things are like "Megadramon's special attack let's him/her use an attack that has a low chance of raising their physical attack or special attack one rank." In this day in age, and we still have games that aren't telling you the percentages of "low, medium, high" chances? At least outline what those translate to in a tutorial within the game. Considering how little depth there is to battles, that's the least they could do. Positioning hardly matters because most enemies simply stand there and wait for you to arrive in their range, which means that at many moments, the sheer enemy numbers aren't even pressuring because you will never be swarmed, and you have no reason to rush into danger where you can get ganged up on. But just to make it matter, it's basically: if you attack from front, less damage and less accuracy, attacking from the side gives a slight bonus to both, and attacking from the back gives the largest bonus. That's about the most depth you'll get from it in terms of things. Sure, there's a damage triangle of Virus > Data > Vaccine > Virus, but even THAT isn't enough to add depth to this rather barebones system. It honestly feels as though the battles are tacked on rather than a feature that got an equal amount of weight. I'm not going to complain about recruitment, as the Shin Megami method was never my favorite way, but it's also not the worst, so I'll let it slide, but I definitely can say I preferred Digimon Dusk / Dawn or Cyber Sleuth's method of recruiting where encountering the digimon allowed you to build up percentage and then eventually create one based off of gathered data. That was pretty nifty. I suppose it's not ALL bad though, as the graphics are very pretty, and it's probably one of the best looking visual novels I've ever seen, and the animators did a very good job with making the scenes coming alive. The character designs are pretty nice too. I think most of them look pretty varied and I don't think I particularly disliked anyone based on their looks. And environments are surprisingly interactive even if most of the interactions are pointless. It's easily one of the highest production values I've seen for any recent Visual Novel. All in all, I can't say this is worth the purchase, as the story is definitely the only thing that's worth playing it for, and I think it's kind of bland.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start by saying that even though I never was interested in the "Visual Novel" gaming genre, being a longtime Digimon fan since the PS1 era (and also a big fan of "grid-based combat" gaming genre), Digimon Survive turned out to be a great Digimon game for me as I enjoyed both its main story (one of the best Digimon stories btw) AND the occasional grid-based combat throughout the game.Having said that, I would like to point out a few areas that can be improved either in a future update (or most likely a "sequel" if that is ever considered). These are as follows along with a suggested solutions for each point:1)  There are only 4  camera angle options during combat which really was an annoying thing to deal with, especially when I was trying to get an overview of the battlefield and strategize based on all units locations. Add both "vertical" and "top-down" as extra viewing angles and that should really help in giving players a better look at the battlefield during battles. 2)  Currently, there is no option to "view" max enemy movement/attack range and that has led to many frustrating moments where I had to MANUALLY go back and forth between my units and enemy units to estimate their max attack range. Implement an "area highlighter" (like in ) where if you press on any enemy unit, you can permanently keep their max movement + attack ranged highlighted on the battlefield WITHOUT needing to go back and forth and hovering over enemy units to estimate their movement/attack range.3)  These two aspects felt missing from the combat in this game and that's one of main reasons why other reviewers feel that the combat in this game was "basic" and not as strategic as it should be. Add more dynamic mechanics like powering-up attacks on certain terrains that match the attack type, moving terrain (like bridges opening/closing) and appropriate stage hazards (e.g. lava, poisonous lakes, falling debris) and that should reward smart decisions based on terrains.4)  Currently, there is no way to view your Digimon partner's evolved form stats/attacks when selecting units before the battle starts and that was such a hindering aspect when selecting my units at the start of battles. Also, even after the battle starts, you CAN'T see the "attacks/abilities" of unlocked evolutions only until you digivolve into them later on. Simply have all evolution infos (stats, abilities, attack, etc...) available at all times as soon as a battle is initiated so that we can make better strategic decisions in a strategic game such as this game.5)  Currently, the only way to evolve wild Digimon that you befriended is through "evolution slabs" and my biggest issue with that is, I ended-up with MANY "Rookie level" Digimon that I NEVER used because either I didn't have enough slabs, missed-out on Digimon who give you those items like Leomon or having already met the "evolved form" of these Rookie level Digimon shortly afterwards and thus making it USELESS to evolve them when I already met and befriended their evolved form later in the story. Have AT LEAST  with the other evolution method being  and that should at least reward those who train their unevolved Digimon rather instead of punishing them for not having enough evolution slabs.6)  Currently, you have to refresh the "Free Battle" location by battling the Digimon currently appearing there or progressing the story to see if there are any other "new" Digimon appearing in the current chapter you are playing in. THIS has led me to "miss out" on many Digimon (ESPECIALLY important ones like Leomon who give evolution slabs). Furthermore, I noticed that some Digimon are "exclusive" to those "Shadow Encounters" which is another point that I didn't like because it forces you to "over-battle" just to make sure that you didn't miss out on any new Digimon as you progress in the story. There should be an  page that you can click on when hovering over the "Free Battle" area which shows ALL the Digimon that could show-up during this segment/chapter of the story (could be in the form of "black silhouettes" to avoid spoilers). Additionally, I feel that "Shadow Encounter" Digimon should also be possible to catch in "Free Battle" areas and not just be exclusive to those kinds of battle encounters.7)  While I didn't feel that the  in this game was too small in my 1st playthrough, it definitely was the case when I started doing "New Game+". This especially hurts when you learn that older Digimon games had a bigger Digimon roster (e.g. Digimon World 2 for the PS1 which had  back in the day). Increase the Digimon roster to AT LEAST 200+ playable Digimon. Also, increase the number of signature moves for each Digimon (or AT LEAST "fully evolved" Digimon) to 2-3 signature moves along with appropriate  for all moves as was the case in older Digimon games like Digimon World 2 (another idea is to record these voice-overs once and then  in future games. This is much better than having "generic voices" for attacks as was the case in this game and other recent Digimon games).8)  While the "colored" karma choices do impact your partner Digimon's future evolutions and story path when you reach chapter 8, my biggest issue with this system is that it does NOT have any  on the situation other than a slight change in the dialogue for each choice (Example: When choosing between "Hide", "Run" or "Confront Enemy", no matter what you choose, the situation will progress at a certain path, so if a battle "has to happen" at this point in the story, EVEN if you choose "Hide" or "Run", you will end-up "Confronting the Enemy" anyway and thus making it feel USELESS to decide between those 3 decisions in the first place). Implement the  video game where EVERY CHOICE you make will  lead to a tangible different outcome and that should make deciding between those 3 choices 9)  I have noticed many spelling errors throughout the story, but most notably, many Digimon partners were referred to by the WRONG pronoun (e.g.  who's ALWAYS been depicted as a  and has a female voice-over and yet was referred to as a "He" throughout the game). Hire a better localization team who are not only competent, but also understand the Digimon lore/characters being presented in the game that they are working on.10)  While the game gives you "Learning Crystals" to increase Exp gained, grinding in this game can STILL be a pain, so I would've appreciated other methods to speed-up leveling, especially during end game. Add Exp. multipliers or Digimon that have exp-gaining abilities (like PlatinumNumemon in Digimon Cyber Sleuth) to help with leveling multiple Digimon as you reach the end game.Overall, despite the above points, this game was a very enjoyable experience and I look forward to what's next for the Digimon franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon Survive is a pretty solid visual novel for both Digimon and non-Digimon fans.. I went through the effort to get every ending and achievement in the game, so I put in the effort to fully experience the game. The strongest part about Digimon Survive is that the story is pretty entertaining and that the characters are well made. The characters are well made and feel like actual kids with believable personalities. I quite liked that Digimon Survive was pretty mature/dark for being a Digimon title. The game technically has 5 endings, but only 4 of them are actual endings. I appreciated that the protagonists in the story felt like actual kids trying to figure out what to do now that they've been sucked into a dangerous world with seemingly no escape. The 4 endings are pretty distinct from each other, with a few obviously similar aspects to them. I personally found the story to be an 8/10, but in lamest terms, it was a pretty good story that kept me entertained all of the way through.The soundtrack was decent enough to not annoy me, but it wasn't anything special. The voice acting in Digimon Survive is top notch. Now, let's get onto my one and only complaint about the game, which is that the combat eventually becomes just plain tedious. I've played a couple of tactical rpgs in my life, and this is the worst of them all. Now, it has some promise to it, but you can tell that it was more of a low-mid effort thing done just to keep the game from being purely story and decision making, which I would've been fine with. The fact that every Digimon only gets 2 moves, with the 1st move just being a standard attack, is just plain lazy and dumb. Yes, I know that there are equipable moves, but taking up 1 or 2 of your slots for a pointless attack, when you can slap on a damage booster or something better, is ridiculous. The only tactics in the "tactical RPG" part of this game, is the placement of your Digimon to get side-attacks, back-attacks, ally attacks, or higher crit chances. These mechanics are good building blocks, but when these are the only things you have to think about when making a move, then it really quickly becomes boring. What the combat part of this game needs is for the Digimon to actually LEARN MOVES, in order to get legitimate movesets. Like, what's the point of the "attack" stat when you'll basically only be spamming your special move since your basic attack will be LEAGUES worse? All they had to do was incorporate the RPG elements from their other games, like Digimon World, into the combat, and that would've been great! The combat is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lazily done and bare-bones that it shouldn't have even been included in the game. The developers almost certainly know that the combat is ♥♥♥♥ since you can swap to the very easy difficulty setting and just blast through the mandatory combat scenes with auto battlers. I didn't do that, because I ain't no ♥♥♥♥♥ that'll lower the difficulty and have a game play itself for me. Final Thoughts: Digimon Survive is a well-made 8/10 visual novel game that even non-Digimon fans can enjoy. However, the combat should've either been excluded from the game due to lack of effort put into it, or they should've actually put in the effort to flesh it out. Don't get this game expecting a tactical RPG, because it's just a VISUAL NOVEL with some foundational level tactical RPG elements thrown in for ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles.

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of people complaining that this game is too story dense and not very gameplay dense, but what little advertising I saw put the story content up front and center and made it very clear that this would be a primarily visual novel experience. If you're a first timer who just wants a JRPG I'd say yes, listen to the reviews that tell you to go play Cyber Sleuth, but comparing the two games is a fallacy because they're two very different beasts. If you're searching for a more story driven Digimon game then Survive is likely a good choice. If you want more gameplay focus, then go for Cyber Sleuth. I personally think that this is a worthy addition to the roster of Digimon games out there and hope to see more games that aren't afraid to experiment with the format like this one.Also my one negative thing to say about other reviews: C'mon now, holding the game's roster against it? You've been warnedI love this game, the art is always so vibrant, the game play is fun, the story was both dark as hell, funny and wholesome, this coupled with (mostly) enjoyable main characters make it all better. The game hosts a variety of difficulties and challenges and allows you to play the game in almost any way you would want. The only downside to this game was that not only did it feel like the choices didn't matter in the first run, they just straight up didn't. The first run is mostly a set up of the story before trying to throw you down another, the only "real" choice you make in the first run is which of the three main paths you'll go down (which determines who dies and how agumon evolves). _childDocuments_.review: Oof, not a fun or enjoyable experience. The concept suckered me in, I mean Digimon with a dark twist and choices that actually mattered, sprinkled with some good old fashioned tactical RPG elements? I jumped at the chance. I should have saved my money. The story started with promise, and if handled differently I feel it could have carried the experience for me, however it was bogged down with characters that I honestly couldn't wait to see the back of. Some of the characters were well presented and interesting, but there are a few that grated on my nerves so badly that I just wanted to shut off the game. They didn't mesh with the rest of the cast or present a meaningful counter-balance, they just pissed me off. The story itself was intriguing and had a good dose of mystery paired with discovery, the dark elements where death could strike from anywhere was a nice touch and I really wish it could have gripped me more to offset the negatives.The gameplay aspect is a fairly generic visual novel style with occasional breaks for a bit of rudimentary combat that offered little in the way of challenge and felt very bare bones, like it was tacked on at the end, or an afterthought. Not really much else to say about it.I LOVED the art style, very well drawn and a lot of care and attention went into the making of the sprites and environments. It really shined through and brought life to the screen.The music was brilliant, the minute I booted up the game and was hit by the menu music I melted a little in my seat, and that quality kept up for the majority of what I played.Overall I just can't recommend this game, which is unfortunate, because there's a lot of potential in here, and who knows, maybe later into the game it grows into it's own and flourishes, but I couldn't get that far. Nearly 15 hours in, most of which I was telling myself that it'll pick up and hit it's stride soon, and I packed it in. The character interactions, a couple of the characters themselves and the bare bones gameplay just killed the experience for me, so much so that this is literally the only game I have ever permanently removed from my Steam library as I could no longer get a refund.This one just wasn't for me.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR, try it if you like VN. Don't try it if you like SRPG. Don't expect good combat from it.Play it for the story.As everyone else says it, probably wouldn't be everyone's cup of tea.I enjoy it quite a lot. Without analyzing anything I will give it a 7.5/10.Being a visual novel game, the presentation is very good. Crisp graphics and UI.Each character has around a dozen of portrait switching around. There are parts where you explore a part of the map where the scene isn't locked to a small background. You can pan and slightly explore.Music is very good for building the tension, but it somehow get repetitive over time.IDK. maybe it could be bugged for me, but till the end game I am still hearing the same set of music. Would have helped if there was more variety.Probably due to development hell they went through, the combat is pretty shallow. Digimon only has access to 2 combat skill, normal attack and unique attack. You can equip addition skills up to 4 skills but they use the same slot as equipment. It will be state below but just these 2 skills is more than enough, thus making it quite mundane unless you try to make it more 'creative' by trying out skills rather than pure equipment stats boost.Digimon has their attribute just like in Digimon Story Cybersleuth, but it hardly matters. Each digimon has "elements affinity" from the list of Fire, Water, Wind, Earth, Light and Dark. High affinity gives damage boost and resistance, negative means you give less damage and take more from this element. It doesn't give 1.5x or 2.0x damage boost/reduction. Probably between 0.75 to 1.25. You can deal more damage by attack from the side or from behind, you also have higher change of crit/dodge attacking from higher elevation. This boost/reduce more damage. I might as well just rant it here but some Bosses and map are so stupid. Some map are ridiculously HUGE and took me 12 turns to reach the boss; and the boss did nothing but standing still waiting for me to reach 10ish square from it before moving. If you have many characters on the map then it become a chore just move all these slowpokes across it.StoryIt's not as bad everyone else make it to be, but could be much better if we had 10~20 more of solid dialogs / exposition per scene.Just like how each Digimon series tells its own story of the Digital World and Digimon, this game also has its own tales. It is a very interesting take. Don't go to Wikipedia as they put up the interview which spoils this. Now for the story and the character, it is pretty good. Not gonna type to much as I don't want to spoil. But it is a tale of teenages trying to survive. Dark and gruesome, yet also relatable. The game has its own chapters called "Part" and they have their own focus. Early game was pretty smooth but late game feels slightly rushed.Rant

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon Survive is about 75% visual novel, and 25% tactics battle game (in a similar style to Final Fantasy Tactics or the like). This game is not a kiddy game; this is the Doki Doki Literature Club of Digimon. You will have people - human people - die during your first playthrough, minimum.The core of this game is character. Each of the children involved has their own 3-dimensional character, as well as one or more particular psychological demons they are dealing with. While the main character is still designed largely as a player insert vehicle, even he isn't lifeless and has his own personality, even if it's a bit generic anime protagonist.The other focus of this game is on exploring an alternate origin of Digimon (the word "digimon" isn't even used throughout the game!). Instead, this setting is based far more around traditional Japanese mythology, presenting a world entirely separate from the computers or digital information that is usually the core of the franchise, yet while maintaining the Isekai spirit of the original series.Overall, this is an amazing game, and one that has good, engaging playtime. A typical playthrough is said to be about 20-25 hours, though that's with a minimal level of farming and poking around. My first playthrough was around 95 hours as I hunted down 'mons to collect, with subsequent playthroughs for the multiple endings and 100% completion effectively doubling that.Pros:++ Great soundtrack++ Great characters and immersive dialogue++ Good tactical battle system, simple but engaging enough to require strategyCons: (spoilers contain spoilers, and may impact your enjoyment of first playthrough - you've been warned!)-- Little direct control over character deaths: -- Plot branching: -- Mandatory new game+:

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Digimon Story: Cyber Sleuth – Hacker's Memory before, and I really enjoy tactical RPGs. The visual novel aspect is interesting; some of your choices affect Takuma's (main character) Affinity with the other human characters which can help randomly in battle. Other choices may increase Karma (Wrath, Moral, or Harmony) which effect what Agumon evolves into (I got Tyrannomon) as well as how the story plays out. Not sure if it only effects the ending or other story-related parts. You can also save pretty much anywhere, even before making choices, to make sure you pick the choice you want. Recruiting Digimon can be a hassle, but rather simple. During battle, you can "Talk" to an enemy Digimon, it will say or do something, and you respond back between 4 different answers. A 6-segmented bar appears above the Digimon that will increase or decrease based on your decisions. Two will decrease the bar, and the other two will increase it by one or two. Once it gets halfway, you have the choice of either asking for an item or recruiting it, but attempting to recruit has a percentage. Some will have a higher chance than others (some as low as 16%), but you can retry the battle over and over. Depending on luck, it may take some time to recruit some Champion or higher evolutions. Overall, the game is not perfect, but if you enjoy tactical RPGs, you may enjoy this game, even if you're not a fan of Digimon and find visual novels boring. If reading is not your "cup of tea", then this may not be the title for you.EDIT: There are a few things that I forgot to mention. The voice-over language is only Japanese, however the text is in English. I have noticed quite a few typos/errors early on as well. Not sure if they have patched them out yet, though. And, definitely the most important thing I left out, are the more mature themes. The most constant themes are fear and death. There is also constant swearing throughout, though it is mostly the "D"-word. There's also an occasional "A"-word, and, at least once, the "S"-word. So, if you're an adult getting this for your kid thinking this is another Pokemon kid-friendly game, it is not. I know this is a lot to read, but thanks for taking the time to read my whole review on this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible, in my opinion out of all the digimon games I've ever played this one is one of the best.But lets start from saying this: it's mostly a light novel, its around 70% light novel and 30% battles. It's always been advertised to be a light novel first and an rpg second so I don't understand all the negative reviews about it. It's like buying a pokemon game and expecting a first person shooter.Now let's start with the positives:-The story of the game is amazing, it's full of emotions, plot twists and memorable moments.-Most of the cast is really likable (aside from maybe 2 people), especially if you talk with them a lot and get their affinity up. So when they die it's even more of a tragic moment.-The battle system is great, it's really fun and there's clearly been a lot of thought put into it.-The sprites and animations look really great.-The game is long (around 30 hours for a single playthrough) so you'll really get your money's worth.-The soundtrack although really small had some great themes.-And I think what was the most important for me in this game: The Choices.When the game came out I was afraid that our choices wouldn't really matter that much but I was completelywrong. Your choices are incredibly important and if you aren't careful with what route you take you can get a lot of characters dead or take the story in a completely diffrent direction. Pretty much every character can die at some point of the game aside from the main character. I myself had some bad decision during my playthrough and got a ♥♥♥♥ ton of characters dead. Only 4 of my characters survived in the end. And by the end of the game my story turned out pretty tragic even tho I got a pretty "Good Ending".Now for some negatives:-The soundtrack even tho great was really small so through out the 30 hour game you'll be hearing the same 10+ or so tracks.-The first two deaths are unavoidable on a first playthrough which is just a weird choice in my opinion. It's like the game telling you your decision don't matter even tho they really do.-The battles are too easy.  The first couple of fights are pretty "challenging" but once evolutions come in play it's basically a cake walk.And that's basically Digimon Survive, it's definitely not a perfect game, it has many issues but overall I think it's an amazing entry into the Digimon Games franchise. I will probably do more playthroughs in the future as the game is extremely replayable, especially after a first playthrough.I'd give it an 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll put my two cents in. I love the Digimon franchise. I've seen most of the shows and loved Cyber Sleuth. This is a hard game to rate because it's definitely a visual novel first; so if you're looking for compelling gameplay like Cyber Sleuth, this isn't the game for you. In terms of story, I compare it to a darker version of the Digi-Destined from the first season. It's really compelling with great replay value based on your choices and really dire consequences. I love the darker tone of this story so it was right in my wheel house. The characters I also found really enjoyable to know and to mold in someway. As for the gameplay, it's mediocre at best. In terms of fun, it's a very plain SRPG. Fire Emblem and XCOM do far better jobs of making that type of gameplay more fun and engaging. There is absolutely nothing special in the strategy of it. Also speaking technically, while I haven't ran into any glitches, it's feels a bit rough around the edges for mouse and keyboard. You can't place your units easily, movement feels clunky, it's very bad at conveying enemy information, and the searching feature in the visual novel is a bit clunky as well. I respect games that are not smooth but innovative or games that aren't necessarily innovative, but have really easy and smooth gameplay. This game fails on both of those fronts.While the game is enjoyable, it's very dependent on the story to keep it upright. So if that's your cup of tea and you can deal with a good amount of reading, this game is fun. If you want strong gameplay, you may want to find another game or at least wait until it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: I have received this game as the Month One Edition due to a friend of mine having gifted me the game within that time frame of the initial launch of this game. As a result, I myself did not pay for this game, and thus I cannot reliably say whether this game is worth your money or not with what I have to say otherwise below.The visual novel aspects of the game can be quite lengthy, but the character building, setting, story, lore, choices and consequences can more than make up for how lengthy the mandatory scenes can be. Especially helping matters is that performing actions during this in important moments will ultimately allow you to unlock specific Digivolutions for your partner Digimon, and also allow the other characters to unlock their own Digivolutions as well. At virtually all times, every Partner Digimon is only given the freebie of having their Champion Level form unlocked via the storyline progression alone; Agumon will be able to go into Mega Level by the end of the game regardless of the outcome, but the player's choices they make have a karma meter which is not only important for determining the possible ending you get, but also directly factor in to which form Agumon will Digivolve to dependent on what your highest karma related value you'll have.The visuals, gameplay, and overall narrative and direction of the game is very good overall, and as a word of advice for first time players of this game that won't spoil anything directly? Agumon will flat out be the only partner Digimon you can always rely on; sometimes certain characters will be inaccessible for you to use for one reason or another, and you can only have six Digimon on the field at a time when beginning a battle. Pick your teams carefully, and don't feel afraid to try and talk with the Digimon you encounter in battle in hopes of either befriending them and recruiting them, or asking for an item in exchange for the conversation you have with them if your responses appeal to them enough.

_childDocuments_.review: A grim Digimon Visual Novel, with turn based tactical rpg style combat.+ Great visuals, several different styles for different aspects of the game. + Great music.+ The darker tone is neat.+ Nice story.+ You need to have a dialogue with digimon to recruit them, which is interesting, gives off a small Undertale vibe. - The game is a bit slow in all aspects, especially the grind. RNG have mercy on recruiting digimon.- Low amount of digimon variety. (Understandable why, but that doesn't change the fact.)- You are locked out of the good/true ending on your first playthrough, which means that trying your best to save everyone is futile until you start NG+. (Tip; replay the game a year later for other endings if you care, don't force yourself to replay the same starting segment multiple times so quickly.)Overall the game offers a niche experience, you need to be into that niche if you want to gain optimal enjoyment out of the game. I rate this game a 7/10, taking into account how niche the game is.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not succeed either as a tactical RPG or as a visual novel. I purchased it already aware of its shortcomings in the combat sections, but what I did not expect was that the RPG element would slow this game down to a crawl. Not just because of the speed of combat itself, but because you often engaged in pointless repetitive battles against the same enemies.I also found the story telling to fall short of expectations. In the beginning it has a strong world building and strong characters, but towards halfway through the story the supporting cast just keeps overcoming the same character flaws over and over again. There is also some repetitiveness as in some sequences, all characters are having a crisis all at the same time, and you have to one by one support them in the same repetitive way. The story also foreshadows too much, so halfway through the game you already have an idea of everything that is going on, making the rest of the game tedious and slow to play through

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - Art (the character designs and backgrounds are gorgeous)- Voice acting (I know it being in Japanese is a turn-off for some people, but the voice-acting was amazing and each voice unique and fitting for the character)- Adult themes (some pretty dark stuff touched on in here)- Characters (each one is unique and interesting with their own personalities, flaws, and quirks)Cons: - Pacing (The game moves too slow at times. It'll seem like it's picking up and running, but then it slows back down to a crawl. Can't seem to choose what momentum it wants and the result is a flash of tension before it backtracks and you find yourself back at the school going over what you're going to eat for breakfast again)- Story (Where it's good, it's good, but it never quite GETS there. The ending of the main route kind of never reached that THIS IS THE BIG END feel and then when it did end, it ended ABRUPTLY with everyone seemingly okay with the decision reached. It never felt like it actually ended.)- Choices (Characters will ask your opinion on something, but it won't matter because whatever you choose, if it doesn't follow the story, they'll disagree with you and choose to do something else, so it's like, WHY ASK IN THE FIRST PLACE).- Endings (The other endings aside from the main one felt convoluted and shoved in there- Battles (Too easy and felt pushed in here. By the end you want to further the story, but you're stuck battling over and over again.)Overall, a good game. Maybe get it on sale. I have no major complaints and I enjoyed the time I spent in it. I would die for Agumon.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR section for people allergic to reading: It's a typical grid-battler RPG with a far more serious and/or desperate tone in it's plot than most Digimon games.Avoiding spoilers (let's just say story is definitely the best/most worked on feature of this game), It's a grid-system RPG much like the Fire Emblem or Advance Wars series. It's pretty typical of it's genre mechanics-wise. What sets it apart from most Digimon games I've seen over the years is that much like the title implies, the main characters are actually trying to survive, and can even die outright with actual narrative consequences to the plot. No respawns, no quest to beat the baddies and save the world, no "captured so let's go rescue that defeated teammate before they die which they never do" mechanic. they face actual, real deaths and it shocks and terrifies the surviving cast if it happens. The cast doesn't know why they're there, and they're not pointed at an evil digimon and set loose with their partners like (and i say this jokingly) a little kiddie hit-squad armed with sentient murder-mons. It's a pretty substantial change from the franchise's usual plot formula. The cast is lost, scared, and for the majority of the game I've played up to (chapter/part 7), they stay that way, just trying to figure out WTF is going on with no information being handed to them like in other stories. If you're looking for a different take on the usual digital adventures, this one will fit the bill.
