_childDocuments_.review: Digimon Survive is a VISUAL NOVEL. Keep that in mind when you decide to buy and play it. Otherwise when you write a bad review on it complaining about its gameplay style you'll just sound like someone who are coming into a bakery and complaining that they're selling bread.However, for a VN it's very interactive. Minus the turn-based battles, I'd say the gameplay reminds me of DanganRonpa. It's also not as text-heavy because it doesn't have narration, only dialogues. Now, something that might not please everyone but is also very, very common in VN's gameplays: there are multiple endings and in order to unlock what is called the True Route that will guide you to the True Ending, you must finish the game once and get one of the "normal" endings. The endings, as well as the way your Agumon evolves, will be chosen according to your highest attribute out of three: Moral, Wrathfulness and Harmony. Also, as in many VNs, each ending has a different vibe, so you could divide them between Good, Neutral and Bad endings (I'm not telling which is which tho). So, yeah, the true ending of the game is hidden behind New Game+.Now that we're done with this, let's talk about the game itself.Your main character, Takuma, and a bunch of other kids need to survive in this weird, wild world where there are monsters, while trying to solve its mystery and to find a way to go back home. The game's story and characters are all new, but if you're familiar with the original Digimon Adventure anime you might notice some shoutouts to its story. Digimon Survive can get quite dark at times. And while the exploration of death as a theme is not new for the Digimon franchise, I'd say this game went deeper in it than any of the anime series and the other Digimon games I've played.I won't get into too much detail to not spoil anyone about the story.The gameplay.Things I liked (and consider pros):- Turn-based battles where you can use from 1 to 6 (and in rarer cases 8) mons at once.- The system to "catch" mons is similar to the one in Persona 2 (or Persona 5) where you need to talk to them, answer their questions and them ask them to join you. I find this fun, but admitedly it can be frustrating at times.- Interacting with characters to get higher affinity with them (which influences in battles).- Multiple endings. I love having different versions of how a story can go depending on the player's decisions.- Atmosphere. As I said it can get quite dark. Things get really tense sometimes. I appreciate that.- There are also light-hearted, cute and fun moments as well, and I love those too.- The way the game introduces the monsters not as "digimon" but as "kemonogami" and has a very different worldbuilding than what I'm used to with the franchise is very interesting.Things I didn't like (and consider cons):- Only 117 playable mons? In a franchise that has over 1000 different creatures? C'mon Bandai, you made we wait so much for this game, you could have done better than this. Many of my favorite mons are not in this game and that makes me sad.- The evolution system is quite meh. Other than the kids' mons, who are going to evolve according to how the story goes, you can evolve your "free" mons to any available form as long as you have the one item that is necessary for evolutions. The level they are doesn't matter. I guess this works well considering the rest of the gameplay but I've played Digimon games with cooler evolution systems.- Each mon having only one attack move besides the physical attack is very lame. You can add attacks with equipments but they will be in place of equipments you could use to make your mons stronger or more resistent instead.Right now I've reached all the common endings and am on Chapter 10 of the True Route. If I find necessary I might edit this review after I'm done with it. But one thing I know I won't change my mind about: this game is good and worth playing! If you like Digimon and visual novels, go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: First of all you have to understand that this game is a visual novel and not a strategy RPG. Once you've got that figured out we can get into this review. If you like the Digimon Animes and want to experience yourself playing as a lead character and making choices that impact the storyline you are in the right place. The games unique story content is amazing, based on your choices you will feel all sorts of emotions as you progress. The story keeps all of the main elements that your typical Digimon anime / story - manga would have with a dark twist. Gameplay wise the tactical element is fun, I played through the story on Normal which is a decent challenge based on your characters Afinities and what choices you make in the story. The tactics based gameplay which resembles a Fire Emblem / Final Fantasy Tatics esque style is fun for what it is. The movements with the different digimon characters are fun, the evolutions during the fights are unique (for the story characters and partners). If there was on thing I think was lacking a bit, it would be the ability for the digimon to have multiple attacks without having to equip something to give them an extra. There's only two slots available so managing stat increasing boosts versus giving another attack is a little lackluster (I think another slot could have helped). Otherwise i've got no complaints.The visuals are awesome, i love the art in this game. The art flows so well from scene to scene and the characters and digimon are very well represented. (I really like collecting the TCG) The art is very similar to to an anime style while keeping some of the trading card elements. This game also has a great soundtrack, really sets the tone and emotion of the entire story... you'll feel the impending doom and you'll feel refreshed when you've won. (the only negative thing I have in terms of the audio and visuals would perhaps be on the scenes where the main characters hit there evolutions - they need a little more pep lol, kinda like what we felt in the 2020 Adventure reboot - This is just an opinion)The New Game + works well giving you the option to skip past old cutscenes and tutorials (I don't want to mention more so that you can experience it your selves).If you love the Digimon stories / animes / manga's and enjoy reading a lot then you'll absolutely love this game! I sure am having fun with it, still trying to complete different endings and to acquire new Digimon and items. Hope this review helps! (thanks for taking time to read it and remember, only you are the best judge)Cheers Everyone!

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily my favorite Digimon game. And possibly one of the best as well. I just finished my first play through. It took my roughly 35 hours, I didn't grind very much and kept the difficulty at default.To give you an idea of what to expect, this game is mostly a visual novel with some turn based combat similar to games like Final Fantasy Tactics. Most of your time is spent going to locations to talk to people or to look for clues. The beginning of the game is slow. It takes a while to set everything up with foreshadowing and establish each character's personality. The game naturally takes a slow pace because most of it is talking. But it does get better after getting into the digital world where the talking is broken up by combat and managing your digimon.I think one of the best qualities about this game is how your choices do matter a lot. You are constantly making choices throughout the game. Some choices matter more individually, such as saying the right thing to build a relationship with a character. Others matter more in the long run, adding up to make out your personality that later on will have massive effects on the story and game play. This all gives the game massive replay value.The story in this game is better than most Digimon games. The characters are well written. I have not noticed any major plot holes, and plot contrivance is not as bad as others in the franchise. This game so far has held up my suspension of disbelief more than any other Digimon story. Which is one area I often find Digimon struggling. One of my favorite things about the story is that it is by far the most mature Digimon game I've played. It may be a kid's series, but this one goes to some dark places and touches on subjects like survivor's guilt. It's not all good though. Sometimes characters are kind of dumb and it takes them a long time to figure things out that you the player have pieced together for a while. Sometimes it is really clearly spelled out and characters don't get it for a while. And there are times in which should be saying a lot about something but your character doesn't and it can be very annoying. Or someone will be making irrational decisions and your character won't say anything about it.As for combat, it is ok. A little bare bones in comparison to similar combat systems like the previously mentioned FFT. I found combat to be very easy though. I never lost a battle. Only came kind of close a handful of times. I will try harder difficulties on subsequent play throughs. The main change I would expect from that would be needing to use type advantages. I almost never had to worry about type advantage and by the end game I had almost all virus digimon on my team still absolutely railing other viruses and even vaccines. Although my one vaccine digimon kind of carried the final battle.Overall fantastic game. Highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, This game is lucky that I enjoy playing visual novel type games like Ace Attorney and Danganronpa.  If I didn't, I would be pretty disappointed in my purchase.  This game is a Visual Novel Game first then a JRPG second.  You will spend a majority of your time reading dialogue and going through the story.  The tactical rpg gameplay is a break from the story.  So if you were expecting be mostly fighting monsters, befriending them, and evolving them, you will be disappointed.  But personally, I am enjoying the game. I am interested in the story and the gameplay is a little bit above average to keep me playing.On the STEAM DECK, this game will not be able to get past any in game movies. The game also hides a majority of the button prompts behind a blank white box because it seems the game can't recognize what the inputs are for the Steam Deck.  But the controls are very simple so it isn't too much of an issue.  I prefer to play this game on the Steam Deck, and even though it crashes as the end of the in game movies.  I am able to progress on the game on the Steam Deck by using my PC to create a save spot after the in game movie and continue on my Steam Deck from there.  So hopefully that gets figured out.  This is a pretty poor PC port. The game is just frustrating to play without a controller.TLDR: This is a Visual Novel Game with Tactical RPG as a break from the story.  Buy only if you enjoy Digimon and Visual Novel Games.  To all the Digimon fans that wanted to just fight and evolve your monster, this game is not for you.  Hopefully the next one they make would be like Monster Hunter Stories 2. Steam Deck plays well. Button prompts are replaced by white boxes. You will crash at the end of the in game movies since it is some sort of codec problem with the videos.   You can bypass those in game movies by creating a save point on your PC after the movie then continue on the Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, while it has many flaws, is still a great little spinoff and an interesting take on Digimon. It feels a lot like an interactive homage to the older anime seasons, such as Adventure and Tamers, so if you enjoyed those, I highly recommend giving it a try.Since it's primarily a visual novel, the focus is on the story and characters while the gameplay takes a backseat for the most part. The SRPG combat is pretty barebones and not very challenging aside from a few specific fights, but it's decently polished and not overly clunky or frustrating.For me, the biggest upside of Survive, and the main reason for my positive review, is the fact that it treats the partner Digimon as actual characters, which is something that always felt like an afterthought in previous games. There is still some room for improvement in that regard, but it does a good enough job of making the titular creatures feel like companions who would be fun to hang out with, as opposed to generic interchangeable JRPG monsters. It is a welcome change that I hope will be utilized more in future games.The voice acting is another highlight – if you’re an anime enthusiast or play many Japanese games, you will most likely encounter some familiar voices. The story has some interesting elements, with a fairly dark tone involving some scenarios that haven’t really been explored much in the series before.The VN segments are nicely presented, with high-quality artwork, while the combat segments (as well as certain cutscenes) use a more stylized approach. The combat sprites of the Digimon, while simplified and more „chibi”-looking, still have some nice little details, such as Wargreymon taking off his shield from his back or Lopmon hiding behind his ears while defending. The soundtrack is… alright, but nothing special. I didn’t find it particularly memorable, aside from the main theme, which has a rather nice vocal version as well.I personally haven’t encountered any technical issues such as bugs or crashes during any of my playthroughs, and as far as I know, the few problems that were present at launch have since been patched.As for the downsides – I think most people can agree that the pacing is all over the place, with plenty of redundant and repetitive dialogue that causes some scenes to drag out far longer than they should. I’m inclined to agree that the story would’ve felt a lot more solid without the unnecessary padding.The English translation/localization is nowhere near perfect, which is unfortunately a common problem with Digimon games and media, but I still found it much more serviceable than Cyber Sleuth’s localization.Another common complaint is about the lack of variation between the different routes, and that many of your choices don’t have enough of an impact on the direction of the story. This is partially due to the way the branching paths are implemented in Survive, and I can’t disagree that it could have been done a lot better. As it stands, doing more than one playthrough (which is required for the true ending) is only really recommended if you absolutely loved the game, and going for 100% completion will feel like a slog even then.Overall, Digimon Survive is kind of a mixed bag, which clearly had plenty of love put into it, but the budget constraints and the signs of its troubled development are noticeable in many places. Whether you’ll like it or not greatly depends on what you want from a Digimon game, and what you like about the franchise as a whole. If you’re a diehard fan of the World-type games, or just want a regular JRPG like Cyber Sleuth, it may not be for you. If you have a soft spot for the anime and want a more narrative and character-driven experience, you are more likely to have a good time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about this game, particularly in the story homages and what is done to emulate but "enhance" a genuine Digimon Adventure 1 experience. But, to me, the flaws of this game heavily outweigh those benefits to the point where I find it an absolute slog to get through this game. The battling gameplay takes inspiration from SMT/Persona, but the experience leaves a lot to be asked for, and I cannot imagine spending hours farming or grinding to "get my favorites" with this system. My recommendation is only doing the mandatory fights, and even skipping Camera investigation fights where possible. I find doing those voluntary battles drains my battery to continue playing the game in a given session. You will miss out on recruitable digimon this way, but that's more grind than this battle system is worth. Auto battle is surprisingly competent, so it may be better to just use that outside of some manual to pick up items when you can.The story is painfully shounen, but you will get what you ask for when you play this game. I did not enjoy how little my VN choices up to Part 6 have influence on how the story events progress. From the sounds of it, NG+ is a requirement for some story elements to go your way, and you don't actually choose a route until later on in the game. I may or may not be able to sit through until that point. I recognize that you play as "the main character", but in actuality, you are playing as a kid with leader archetypal potential among a group of other kids. So, what you say has some effect on the group dynamics, but ultimately, the group decides what the group decides, and the story will follow suit. Building Affinity with other characters matters but does not pull as much weight in controlling the story direction as I wanted. The above is also painfully made aware to you when key decisions in the story are performed by other characters when your MC could have easily done the same but chooses not to.I also wish they sampled Butterfly when it came to the music choices in this game. As a fan of the original, the music tied to digivolution and the heroic moments where overcoming personal adversity with your Digimon partner really really stand out to me. I got these story elements when playing the story, but the music choices are not there, and it hurts. I haven't found a single track yet that compares to say the Royal Knights theme from Cyber Sleuth. Maybe a possibility in a sequel of this genre? I don't want this genre to go away for Digimon games because I definitely think they have something special here. Visual Novel format for Digimon definitely works. But, the pros in this game do not outweigh the cons for me, which sucks because the pros are unique to this game as compared to other Digimon games right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon Survive is a visual novel first, and a video game second. 70% VN and 30% video game. Which I'd say if you don't like VN's then you won't like this. However, the reason I like the VN part of it is that characters are explored rather than constant fighting. Digimon Tamers was different from other digimon series since it focused on 3 characters and had more screen time for them figuring themselves out. This game reminds me of that, although it's probably more like adventure 1 and 2 since it's hard to juggle this many characters and digimon.I wish I could say more in the review but I honestly like the combat the least in this game. The four direction system doesn't work well, since it's you either move just out of range of the opponent and they defend instead of moving, or they can easily manuever to hit your weak spot, then you do the same to them. I feel like if the direction system was taken out this would have been fine, but the directions don't work well as they are. Melee digimon get shafted while digimon with ranged attacks can easily make use of shooting a weak spot from a distance. There's also an element system I think since I see weak and strong, but it never matters enough for me to strategize around it.Also more games should include Guilmon. All of them, in fact. Give me more Guilmon.

_childDocuments_.review: Taking what is usually a lighthearted and oftentimes shallow monster collector series and shaping it into a narrative that is surprisingly heartfelt (and dark) is quite a unique, welcome step in an interesting direction for Digimon. _childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, especially if you like Digimon. Very much captures that feeling of nostalgia watching Digimon Adventure, and clearly models a lot of its characters and plot off of it. Basically the original Digimon show, but a lot darker. Multiple routes and New Game+ carrying forward a lot of your prior collections mean it has a lot of replay-ability, as the story does change depending on your choices.That said, it is mostly visual novel, so if you are looking for something fast-paced or combat-heavy this is not your game. The game can't seem to decide if it wants to be a visual novel or a tactical RPG and ends up failing to really commit to either. The combat mechanic only happens a few times per chapter, unless you choose to Free Battle monsters, and recruiting additional monsters is pretty tedious. Grinding will definitely be necessary at least on your first play-through in order to beat some of the end-game bosses.Still not a bad game if you like visual novels or tactical RPG's, and definitely worth it if you like Digimon. But maybe wait for it to go on sale, as it's probably not worth its $60 value.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is hard for me to review. Clearly I like it - as of writing I have almost 38 hours in-game. Are you new to the franchise?  Just looking for a good visual novel? Well stop right there, I don't recommend this game in that case. Go play Cyber Sleuth (or a different VN) and then come back.This game falls short in a few ways. The English translations were very clearly not proofread or play-tested. Part 4 has multiple pronoun issues making it confusing about who the text is talking about. They literally left in "Takuma's portrait and name are not shown for this line". Also "Start Bat.". Why not just say "Start Battle"? The game also takes forever to wind up and get going. The cheery victory screens also totally take me out of the immersion. The combat system also is not great. Battles are slow even at max speed. Due to the forced low angle prospective, it can be hard to see parts of the map. Requiring digimon to evolve from rookie each time a battle starts is tedious (at least, I feel like this could be made better while keeping the interesting evolution mechanic). But the artwork is pronominal! The music is great! The story concludes well (depending on what you choose, of course)! And the community has made mods that fix both the bad translations and the broken button prompts (The images are missing on the Steam Deck!?) But these mods shouldn't be required for a $60 game!Anyway...Recommended if you've played previous Digimon games, can install a few mods to fix errors, can put up with slow story, and can get it on sale.Not recommended otherwise. Since I feel this applies to more people, I'll use that for my review.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s like Pokemon if Nintendo had balls.Pokemon could never give me depression like this game does though.Dude, hear me out… there’s *gulp* girls in this game!!!!This game is extremely Japanese, like more Japanese than a samurai driving a Toyota Camry in the middle of Tokyo. Survive is one hell of a game, and definitely worth it. It’s about 70% Visual Novel and 30% gameplay but I really loved it. I've beaten it multiple times, seen all the endings and pretty much done everything there is to do. The story hit on a completely new level... Digimon has definitely grown with its fanbase. It also is my favorite Digimon game now. It was such a love letter to the original adventure, and it's only one more reason to love the game. It gave me some of my favorite characters in the entire franchise.This game is essentially a video game adaptation of a would-be anime series with unique tamers partnered with their sole partner Digimon as opposed to nearly every other game prior that which was essentially monster collecting/ raising like Pokemon with focus primarily on a single protagonist. As such the VN approach is appropriate to help develop this cast of interesting characters. Even more similar to the anime are the earlier story-scripted battles which have specific partner Digimon evolving to their new form for the first time very much like it was on an episode. The overall dark, J-Horror inspired narrative is amazing. It's not like super grim dark - but it has its unsettling moments but is ultimately about the teens, lost in a world, scared and building relationships with their Digimon. It's a far more realistic take on it compared to the kids show.What's interesting about Survive is that I started playing it and thought l'd like it better as a regular Anime season, but towards the end I realized it worked better as a game. If it had been an Anime, I could only see it being one that showed the true route where nobody died. The story's unique identity is in the very real danger that you could lose someone, especially since the game forces you to lose characters your first go round.I enjoyed the combat. Even though it's simple/ shallow doesn't make it bad. I enjoyed it more than the combat in Cyber Sleuth. Music is amazing, and the game is a good experience. My biggest gripes so far is that I do wish that load times into battle would be faster such as restarting the battle to reattempt recruitment of a particular Digimon again-and-again. Also I’d wish that the combat were more difficult. The tension never comes from battles just from the choices you make in the visual novel part. There are a lot of battles where enemy Digimons attack you in very predictable pattern and 1 at a time that makes it even more easier. Yes they hit like a tank but because you almost always outnumber them they are easy to beat.I think it’s great if you want to get into the theme of what Digimon is. Especially this story is basically a more mature retelling of its most popular piece of media - the first season of the anime. What I'm getting at - is if you are after what Digimon as a concept and a piece of media invokes to fans such as myself. This story is probably the closest in terms of retelling it with the utmost care - for a more mature audience of course. The game is basically an origin point for the lore so you can jump in without prior knowledge.What an amazing game. If you want a great story it's perfect for you. It’s dark and has a lot of horror themes in Tamers and Ghost Story style. This game though is clearly not for everyone. It's 70% visual novel 30% combat. The combat already is for a specific taste, long story short, do your homework and you won't regret your choice. It's also a very mature story so if you come expecting the happy go lucky world like Pokémon don't even bother looking this way. Now if Pokémon had the guts to go this dark with their stories Nintendo could have something. Really hope Digimon Survive can survive for a sequel.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon Survive is a very beautiful Visual Novel/TRPG Lite game, the start is a little slow but once the plot kicked in, its certainly got me hooked. The TRPG game play reminds me of Final Fantasy tactics where back/side attacks deal extra damage and allies can give buffs if positioned close together. The Karma system is fairly intuitive (Red options increase Moral, Yellow increases Wrathful and Green increases Harmony) and depending on how you play it determines which Digivolutions you have access to as well as has effects on the story as it unfolds.Other Digimon other than the main cast partners can be recruited via a Talking system similar to the Shin Megami Tensei series where you talk to a Digimon and give it certain responses in order to gain it's favour. The music is beautiful and the art and animations for the characters in the visual novel mode is certainly one of the best I've ever seen. Overall if your a fan of Digimon and are looking for an interesting tale set in that universe i'd certainly recommend picking it up. Just be warned this is a very dialogue heavy game and if your expecting lots of TRPG game play from the get go you will probably be disappointed. The Japanese voice acting is well done and what TRPG game play is there however is solid and certainly fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal.  I'm still barely out of the prologue, and loving it.  If you like Digimon, any facet of the series at all, definitely give this a play at some point.  If you like the Shin Megami Tensei series, or the Persona series, definitely give this a play at some point.  If you enjoyed The World Ends With You on 3DS, definitely give this a play at some point.  (I haven't played the sequel/update/remake on the PC yet, I assume the same applies.)  Oddly enough, if you like Danganronpa, give this a play.  That is not something I thought I'd be comparing a Digimon game to.  Similarly, if you enjoyed Yuki Yuna Is A Hero, or Madoka Magica.  Just the vibes, not necessarily plot elements.  Maybe.  No spoilers here.  Graphics: Top notch visuals in the visual novel portions, adorable as hell sprites in the battle portions.  Sound:  Sound should have a separate channel for dialog voice, and whatever weird sound call sound effects happen when choosing Digimon recruiting options.  I have to keep increasing and lowering my volume.  Controls: Says to use mouse, mouse doesn't seem to do anything, but using J K I L, it's like the right handed version of WASD for 'camera' control.  Gameplay: I'm barely even into anything one would consider gameplay at this point, for me at least.  It has been mostly visual novel + adventure game.  I did recently unlock a free-battle mode, and it's reminiscent of some earlier grid-based tactics games.  Maybe not FFT or FE, at least not yet, but it's solid.  Maybe once I start exploring evolutions, and whatever else the game has in store, the combats will become more tactical and have a more vast web of strategies to consider.  For right now, it's basically: move to a side angle, attack for boosted damage, do it again next turn, fight is over.  Of course, I'm the type of powergamer to grind until I'm one-shotting or two-shotting things, so that may just be a *Me* problem.  Story: Not going to spoil anything, plus, other than passing out for a bit with the computer on (tired, not bored), I've barely experienced a fraction of the story, but what I'm guessing is the length.  I'm still in a Chapter 1 section, the prologue took plenty of time since I wanted to experience everything.  Like in most good adventure games, interacting with something multiple times can give multiple responses, as well as interacting with everything/everyone else, whenever you've interacted with something new.  I basically kept going through every possible dialog/response every time something new happened.  Solid voicework in the jp voices, not sure if I can switch to an English dub somehow, as I prefer to go with that, but I've learned enough japanese over the years through anime watching that I recognize a lot of the phrases when they're spoken, and show up in text.  Translations seem on point for those ones at least.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, after four years' worth of delays, shifting devs and engine changes, the Digimon franchise's take on the turn-based strategy genre is here. It's certainly worth getting excited about to be sure, however, development issues like these often reflect badly on the final product, so how does Digimon Survive stack up?Gameplay-wise, Survive is a mixture of Visual Novel and SRPG elements, with the focus leaning heavily on the VN side of things. On the combat front, it's essentially just a mixture of classic Final Fantasy Tactics-style strategic movement and team-building with the multi-faceted weakness system from the Cyber Sleuth games thrown in. units generally have both a Pokemon-esque elemental weakness as well as an attribute weakness, not too dissimilar to the Zodiac weakness system found in FF tactics. The key to victory thus lies in having a team composition that can take advantage of both of these weaknesses with a single attack to deal even greater damage than if you simply targeted each weakness individually (in other words, have a unit of the Vaccine attribute attack a Virus attribute, fire-type unit with a water elemental strike to deal maximum damage). Add on the damage bonuses that you get from advantageous positioning (like attacks from behind or from higher ground) and you'll be able to deal positively stupendous amounts of damage. While this greatly encourages a varied team composition, it does unfortunately result in a battle system that's heavily stacked in favor of a savvy player, even on the highest difficulty. Luckily, the game does give you the ability to play on hard mode from the get-go, which I'd very much recommend if you're at all familiar with these kinds of titles.On the VN side of things, Survive is generally good. Hard-hitting moments carry an appropriate amount of impact and your choices feel like they have significant weight to them due to the lethal danger that surrounds the characters. There are some rather bothersome shortcomings in the characterization aspect, however. While the original anime made waves for its bold decision to give its characters deliberately unlikable character traits in order to give them room for growth, Survive unfortunately struggles to find a balance in its characterization. Certain characters are so exceedingly unreasonable from the moment they first appear that the idea of them developing past their flaws seem nearly impossible. Meanwhile, others are so pleasant that the moment where they start to crack feel too sudden even if the situation they're in would have more than justified their wavering if it had happened more gradually. Nonetheless, seeing the characters finally pull themselves back from the brink is still immensely satisfying since the story makes it abundantly clear that them overcoming their flaws is very much not a guarantee in this darker setting. Admittedly, the seeming lack of nuanced character development might simply come down to the rather inconsistent translation. Like the Cyber Sleuth duology, Survive's English translation runs the entire gamut from typos, misgendering of characters, inconsistent speech patterns, dialogue boxes being attributed to the wrong characters and so on. It's not consistent enough to ruin the intended experience, but it certainly gives the game a rather rushed feel. It's worth noting that while most of this game's language options had on average four main translators, the bulk of the English translation was seemingly a two-man show, which certainly excuses the rougher edges to some degree.On the whole, Digimon Survive is a perfectly pleasant time. The SRPG aspects aren't anything groundbreaking, but neither do they falter in any way and does do an especially good job at encouraging solid team composition (even if it comes at the expense of the difficulty). The translation may be rougher than one would have hoped, but your personal choices do nonetheless still carry the appropriate amount of weight in this do-or-die setting, which makes the triumphant and heartfelt moments feel that much more significant. Digimon Survive isn't going to change your impression of SRPGs, but it is a good time nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: I would strongly recommend buying the game when it goes on sale as i do not feel that its worth its current price (£40/$60 Game).The advertising is a bit of bamboozle but the game is truly a Visual Novel. 10% of it is actual combat and this can be simply be removed if you turn on Auto-Battle, this works 9/10 times since the fights are relatively easy and straight forward and this is on normal mode.StoryWon't go into details but definitely your typical Shounen along with very dark elements which is unusual for Digimon including some very surprising routes/endings. My only complaint was that there was lots of transparent padding here and there. The beginning was also very slow to start and if you haven't played a Visual Novel before this may turn you off really quickly.CharactersThey are somewhat likeable until you reach life/death situations which impact certain characters heavily by giving them a "shock". You may be able to tolerate it or not but this becomes an occurring theme.GameplayMechanically for a Visual Novel i think its mediocre, i personally wasn't a fan of how you have to achieve certain routes. The game is also very slow paced so you will need a lot of patience especially if you want to replay it. The free-action/investigation sections also felt unnecessary at times and would have preferred mashing enter for text honestly.Battle SystemHorrible, its fun for the first few battles then you start to realise its very bare bones in what you can do and feels as if you are playing a poorly made mobile game. Even on fast mode + animations off its still very slow to go through. 90% of the fights i left it on Auto-Battle as i lost interest in it very quickly and only cared for the story afterwards. Graphics / Art / MusicOverall the game is aesthetically pleasing, UI's are about passable although bit mobile like and low effort in some areas. Animated characters is always a plus to have in Visual Novels and contrast well with the background. The sound track was also well made, really fits theme of the situations that happen in the story, especially the melodramatic ones. Only complaint was that theres very little music to hear so it got quite repetitive very quickly. Positives- A lot darker than i anticipated- Visually pleasing art- Plot is just about passableNegatives- Very little Digimons - Not worth the price- Little music- Combat feels repetitive and unengaging- Lots of unnecessary padding and slow pacing

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon Survive is a tactical rpg visual novel. It's not bad, but it's not good and that's coming from a hardcore Digimon fan. The story is alright i guess, nice and dark, how I like my digimon stories but it was hard to keep me interested. The game was advertised with choices that could mean life or death for the children in the game game, which is kind of true. Your first playthrough you can get 1 of 3 endings, from the good to bad 1 and bad 2. Endings Bad 1 and 2 kills an extra already decided 2 kids on top on the minatory 2 kids deaths during first playthrough. So really you're deciding the story outcome and not character deaths, which are two different things. And I HATE that to get the true ending I MUST play the New Game+, eventhough I did everything in my power to keep one of the children live, nope story death no choice.... in a game about choices! Second, the gameplay is boring and repetitive, but that might be because I'm not really into tactical RPGs. I loved Cyber Sleuth cause it reminded me of Persona. Also a weird option I have, is that they should have made you use the children's digimon and not be able to recruit random digimon. I mainly used all random digimon and just agumon throughout the game, and could have cared less about the story digimon at all. The children get little if at all character development. I love Digimon so much, and I really wanted to like this, but the more i write and think about it, I can't.

_childDocuments_.review: Most people are salty that this is a visual novel first, and an RPG second, but that is what was advertised.To give my thoughts on it, I think that this is a great game. A uniquely grim and dark story filled with strange creatures, decent combat, and great characters. Multiple plays are needed to get the true ending, and I'd recommend playing blind first to fully experience it. Many people consider this game to be the reboot of the Digimon Adventure series, and I can see where this comes from, but my personal enjoyment comes from this game being a spiritual successor to one of my favorite games of all time: Devil Survivor 2 Record Breaker, a visual novel tactical rpg where your choices determine who lives and who dies on a charming but dark adventure. If you don't mind visual novels and the occasional grind, I wholeheartedly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:the tactical portion of the game is wonderful. Art style is gorgeous and all the characters stand on their own. I can admire both the background, & character animation. The story is great too! the Horror element really adds to digimon whose never been to shy to talk about heavy subjects. If your a Digimon fan this game is very much a double edge sword but, if this is your introduction to digimon this game is great fun,even with the Visual novel portion of the game. I also love he fact that the main digimon in this series are Digimon that are usually in the background.The Bad:The price tag! They had 5 years to develop this game and only gave us 100+ mon's out of the 1000+. Pokemon has done this recently but its because their models are 3d scaled from scratch. They didn't even bother to place in the filler recolored versions of Agumon(black, white, toy), or characters with counterparts like Ladydevimon, and Terriormon.  on top of that there are probably like 6 maps to play on. Post game content is basically new-game plus without a good skip option for evens your already did. I want this game to succeed with DLC but conflicted that we would have to pay extra when this game should of been $30 at launch for its lack of content. you get more out of a random indy game at this point. I'm disappointed with Bandai but I am not surprised. at this point just port or remaster Digimon Dawn and Dusk. Honestly the gameplay is cool and fun but not enough for the pricetag.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: A patch was released which fixed the video freezing issue[ACTUAL REVIEW AFTER 30 Hours]I do highly recommend this game if you are looking for a great Digimon story, however if you are not a fan of Visual Novels then do not get this or wait for a sale. It is a VN first and foremost and your first run of the game will take about 25-30 hours. Not to say there aren't any battles, you can actually do those pretty much whenever, but it's just not the main focus of the game. I would also say for pretty much everyone to bump the difficulty up to hard, it's just too easy at the start; however I would like to add the last half of the game has some really REALLY fun combat. You also get access to Mugen battles on NG+ which are some of the best combat the game has and are VERY fun. Also for those worried that additional runs will take up a lot of time, there is a skip option in the game (right on the D-Pad for controller) and it will only skip dialogue you've already seen and stop for any NEW dialogue a character has, so getting all the new story bits for a new run is very easy and wayyyyy faster than you would think. This is just a great QoL feature for doing the different routes. 8.5/10 from me!

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr, game's nothing special, pick it up for like 20 bucksnot a bad game by any means, but man, i gotta say i'm disappointed. the story is a mixed bag - the dark tone and a certain mystery throughout the game are both done pretty well and i quite liked them, but the characters just feel dumb for the sake of the plot a lot of the time. conflict can feel forced, characters can be totally oblivious to an obvious plot point right in front of them, and they keep feeling like they're regressing in their one character trait/arc for the sake of personal growth that we've already seen them go through, like, 3 times by now. the tactics gameplay is just alright, too. not bad, not great. i really only had to strategize well in the last few fights, and some of the fights that did hit that sweet spot of challenging but fair were spoiled because they story decided it was time for a new digivolution which is statted to steamroll whatever's in front of you. anything that wasn't set up to be a major boss fight was just a tedious waste of time. I'm a huge fan of tactical rpgs, and i can get really into a good, suspenseful, and well-written visual novel from time to time as well, but this game just took me so long to beat because i felt like i was slogging through it once i got back the initial hook of, "oh, hang on, this game's not afraid to be really dark, is it?". really disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon Survive

_childDocuments_.review: While visual novels aren't for everyone, I highly recommend this if you enjoy digimon. It's a breath of fresh air to the series, adding in actual risks with your actions. The characters each fulfill a role, making you either hate them or love them... And of course how your choices play out will determine what happens to them. The name of the game is Digimon Survive... Meaning you need to choose the right things if you want to survive. There are a few mishaps in the game, spelling mistakes or even moved around names, but that doesn't take away from the immersion of playing. The game is more than long enough to have you spending 50+ hours trying to get the game 100% completed. The rpg battling experience is not bad either. They make it understandable and when you are allowed to fight you can change difficulties to match how you feel at the moment, making it very forgiving. I'll go ahead and give what I've liked so far about the game and what I've disliked...Positives:-Beautiful Visuals: The game has been years into development and it payed off, the visuals, background, even the characters+digimon are all drawn so beautifully-Voice Acting: Each and every VA did such an amazing job with the roles they were given. There hasn't been a time where I did not think the lines they said didn't match the character-Battling: The battling mechanic is not bad at all, being a table top turn based battle system. The gimmicks they introduced work well and very easy to understand. Being able to change the difficulty and retry battles at any point during the battle is a big plus-OST: The ost, music and all, were beautifully done. Throughout the game it'll change depending on the situations you're in and it doesn't overwhelm the player, matching the scenes perfectly with whatever tone is set-Interface: Menus and all that are not at all hard to understand as well as navigate. The controls chosen are easy and always on the screen to show you what you would need to press to do what you want. The game even allows controller support and even then it still has the buttons mapped. Each screen is perfectly sized and sectioned off to do exactly what it's meant to doNow, Negatives:-Bugs: Every game has them, though I never encountered many besides one major one... And that is that during a game mechanic known as "Free Time" I was unable to progress into the story due to doing certain things which in turn locked me out of progressing. Saving before you do major choices is key-Grammar: Of course translation from one language to the other is never perfect, some things not easily told, but there have been a few instances in the game where... How do it put it... it didn't make sense? Things weren't spelt how they should've been and even one point in the story a digimon had a completely wrong name. But it didn't affect the story or my enjoyment reallyIt's not much of a review, but I will say if you enjoy visual novels as well as a battling mechanic, then this game is a perfect fit for you. Just don't expect the game to be mostly battles. After all, it was promoted as a visual novel more than it was a battler.

_childDocuments_.review: It's anime virtual novel style interaction mixed with Final Fantasy Tactics gameplay. It's definitely great for those who love Digimon, and turn-based tactical strategy as both worlds collide and the combat is fun. The virtual novel is pretty lengthy between combat segments though, so if you're not interested in the story be prepared to hit the skip button quite a bit. It's a Bandai Digimon game so you'll be in for a grind to reach the conclusion, even if you streamline the story tailor your expectations to this being a long haul. I've enjoyed it, not sure if it's worth the full pricetag, but you won't be unsatisfied if the elements I wrote about above are down your alley.P.S. I've been playing on the hardest difficulty and haven't found anything challenging thus far, so it's not the most difficult game if you're familiar with the genre, also not as kid-friendly as I expected storywise. Post-Game PS: Just completed new game+ and I really enjoyed this game. The story is great, and the combat is strategically stimulating. I don't regret paying full price, and honestly can't wait for the next installment.

_childDocuments_.name: Digimon Survive

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty average game, both as a VN and a Digimon game. It honestly doesn't even feel like a Digimon game aside from the notable monsters and evolutions being there. There is nothing fundamentally "digital" about them or the world. You could have thrown any random off-brand monster collector franchise in the game and it would have been the same. It sure as hell was no DMW3 or Digimon Story Cyber Sleuth, which were both incredible games (DMW3 being the best obviously). The gameplay was a slightly better than originally expected, but still pretty subpar. The only nice thing was not really needing to grind to get evolutions or progress the battles, which I usually enjoy doing in other Digimon games, but the pacing of this game really needed quick and easy collection and evolution. I would have gotten bored and not completed it if the game required real grinding with the way this one was structured. On hard difficulty you do need to grind levels slightly to avoid getting one shotted in a couple main battles. Other than this, the battles are clearly an afterthought. The game is a VN first and foremost with battles tacked on just to offset the drawn out dialogue. Go into it expecting a pure VN experience and not a Digimon game and you'll probably get some enjoyment out of it. Unfortunately the story was pretty cliche and weak with little desire for replayability, so I will likely just look up the other endings on Youtube. This is the only Digimon game that I've played and did not even bother trying to get all the evolutions. Every moment playing I just wanted to reach the end, which was very abrupt and lackluster as well. Maybe some of the other endings are better, but as I said before, I have no desire to sit through all that mundane dialogue again. Don't mistake the 65 hours of play either. I literally fell asleep every time I played which racked up more time than actually playing, probably more like half that. At normal difficulty, it could probably be finished in about 20 hours.It really deserves a neutral rating, but I still recommended as I did play it all the way through despite it feeling very mediocre. Overall 5/10 game.Also, don't pay full price for this. I still over payed at $40. This is a $25 game at best.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon Survive is an incredible game that offers a unique blend of tactical battles and visual novel elements that truly make it stand out from other games in the genre. The storyline is captivating, with a great mix of action, adventure, and drama that will keep you engaged from beginning to end.One of the things that really stands out about this game is the way it seamlessly combines tactical battles with visual novel storytelling. The battles are intense and require strategic planning, while the visual novel elements provide a deeper understanding of the characters and the world they inhabit.The art style is beautiful, and the music is top-notch, creating an immersive experience that will keep you hooked for hours. The Digimon themselves are a joy to watch, with each one displaying unique skills and abilities that make battles exciting and challenging.Overall, I highly recommend Digimon Survive to anyone who is a fan of tactical games or visual novels. It's a fantastic combination of the two that creates an unforgettable experience that you won't want to miss, especially if you're a Digimon fan.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a love and hate for this game...I love the story, the characters, it has the nostalgic of Digimon Adventure feel, but dialed the serious tone from 0 to 100.What I didn't like is the visual novel part, not that I don't like that this Digimon game is a visual novel, I KNOW this is a visual novel, I played visual novels, Digimon games has always been like this, trying new stuff, and not just stick with one type of game, so this doesn't surprise me.What I hate about is about visual novel in general...that you will NEVER, get the real ending in the first play through, they advertise how your choices matter, but it doesn't. (for the most 90% of the time)I know, that they want to tell a story, and show the gruesomeness, and want us to feel all that in the first play through, and THEN let us play again, and let us play the real ending. in a way, forcing you to play again, not because you want to, but you're being forced, because they didn't gave you the choices in the first play through to get to the "real" ending. like that one person, no matter how many times you try, the event will happen, you can't avoid it, unless you play the game again."Oh, visual novels has always been like this" you might say...WHO!? WHO wrote this the constitution, bible, or ten commandments, that visual novels, HAS to be like this!? IF your game is good, your story is good, people will play it again!I hate the part when they gave me, 1 2 3 options, but hide the 4th option, only available when you play it again!....Over all, I like this game, I like the characters, the story, the part I hate is that they keep saying "your choices matter" when it really doesn't!I don't like visual novels force you to play a game over and over, and not give you the mechanics you need from the first play through. Forcing people to play it again, just to see the "real" ending, is not good mechanics imo! especially don't advertise it as "your choice matter" because it doesn't! (for the most part)

_childDocuments_.review: Early on, I had the impression that digimon survive was a tactics game, but it became clear pretty quickly that digimon survive was both a visual novel and a tactical RPG. While I do think I'd prefer a bit more emphasis on the tactics side, this game is really fun. I think the first chapter is a bit slow, but it also has some genuine horror ♥♥♥♥ in it, like straight up "the ring" stuff. The original series, with characters like Devimon and Myotismon, was always a lot more mature (not just in content, but in themes) than a lot of its shounen anime contemporaries, and I think Survive does this well.But also... there are some traits that make something 'digimon,' and I feel like a lot of newer digimon tv series don't get it.1) weather anomalies leading people into the digital world (in tamers, it was fog, in adventure, it started with snow, etc)2) leomon always dies (i haven't met him yet but I am hopeful)3) big bug type (usually kuwagamon, but sometimes dokugumon) that causes problems for the kids and spurs their digimon to evolveThis game has all of that.I'm not sure how I feel about the game's kinda slow "let's look for food" story elements; I get why it's happening and all, but I do think the pacing could be tightened up a bunch.If you're looking for a cool twist on tactics (your digimon use SP to stay evolved in combat, which isn't something I can recall seeing in other tactical rpgs) with a story that's super interesting (so far, I'm about 6 hours in), Digimon Survive is really cool.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely unique and it could go either way. I'm predicting some superfans and some big haters, and honestly, both groups would have valid points!THE GOOD PARTS:* The art is really good, along with the music and voice acting* It has a good cast of memorable heroes and villains* The core design is solid and does what you'd expect, and it has some good replayability (so I'm told.)* The aesthetic is cool and so are the concepts. It's another of those alternate-world Digimon things that I never get sick of.* It has difficulty settings! Normal mode is really easy.THE BAD PARTS:* It's incredibly SLOW. Every time there's a conversation, characters will repeat themselves 3-5 times, talking in circles. "Are you scared?" "Yes, I'm scared" "Aren't we all so scared right now?" "I think everyone is scared..." "Yes, I'm scared, too!" "It only makes sense that everyone is scared." "I think what I'm feeling is... scared." LIKE WE GET IT.  MOVE ON. You'll find yourself button mashing like crazy just to get to a scene that matters.* Similarly, the characters  are written way too dumb. Someone has to outright say the solution to a mystery at least twice out loud before any characters acknowledge it. Even if all the clues are there and you, the player, have solved this in the first hour of gameplay, it will take 10+ hours before your characters figure out the obvious connections. It will hammer you over the head with the answers until you're sick of how obtuse everyone is being. It's like playing Blue's Clue's with a 2 year old but Steve is like "Where's the clue?" and instead of waiting 30 seconds for your kid to respond, he waits 12 hours with no commercial breaks.* The pacing is just plain bad. It takes a really long time to start getting fun Digimon, but then as soon as you do, the game gets way too easy even on harder modes. You barely get time to enjoy using the most cool Digimon because by the time you get them, you're at the end of the game with only like 5 real fights left.* Evolution items are super aggravating to get and training your dream team doesn't end up being super important. You'll want to spend a lot of time getting your favorite Digimon, because that's what every Digimon fan does. But don't do that. I mean, if you want to, go for it, but in the long run, you really need to be focusing on keeping all the party members' Digimon in play basically the entire time, otherwise you'll get whooped near the end of the game when it starts narrowing how many of your non-face character digimon you can put on the field. It's a little bit of a slap in the face since the amount of grinding and luck it takes to get evolution items is pretty high.* They get really sparing and repetitive with the art assets as the game goes on. There's lots of artificial exploration where you're just clicking into identical rooms and passageways and fighting the same boss over and over because he has clones of himself, or is an illusion being cast in multiple places, or because each group of characters is facing him at the same time in different locations. it's a cool concept, but ultimately just means you often have to do the same boss battle 3-4 times in a row against the same background and like... it gets old. * Not collector-friendly! It doesn't warn you about this, but once you progress the story, some areas will never be able to be visited again, or if they are, they won't contain the same monsters. So if you are in an area that has Free battles with characters you like, do NOT move forward with the assumption you can get them later. In a lot of cases, you can't! TIPS:* Go Moral your first time playing. I did Harmony without planning to (just by picking the most natural responses) and was getting really bummed with Agumon's evolutions, so switched to Moral about halfway through. This made a BIG difference in how fun battles were and I think this ending is probably the best for a first or only playthrough.* Slabs will dry up, so when you have a source for them, exploit the hell out of it before moving to the next area or else you'll be annoyed and not get to switch up your team for a long time. They don't become plentiful until very late in the game.Overall, I liked this game, but I think Digimon Cyber Sleuth is still my favorite Digimon game. I might play this one more time to see the true route  (there are 4) if I think I can bear to speed through the ridiculous amounts of dialogue again, but I am on the fence. If there's an anime adaptation someday, I'll definitely watch, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I kept saying, "maybe I'll start enjoying it soon".Little things were bugging me: There feels like there is a small delay between each line of dialogue after pressing A(Space,X, whatever)Opening up the map and it having to tell you, for two seconds, that you did In fact open the map... every time.Feeling the need to check every select-able thing on the screen, and opening up the phone to search for things to scan; the game states there's items hidden everywhere, and who wants to miss finding anything? Combat also felt very delayed - even with auto battle on, usually you would expect an auto battle to speed through, but there's still like a second or two between each action. This is even with text speed fast and battle speed x3 - maybe I'm impatient, or maybe it's ADHD, I don't know, but it was getting on my nerves.Then I found myself losing interest and just trying to get to the next interesting thing, ignoring as much dialogue as I could, and eventually I thought "What am I doing, I'm wasting my free time doing something I'm not enjoying because I think I might EVENTUALLY enjoy it." that's not a way to live.It's a real grind getting through all the dialogue. There turns out to not be a lot of typical engaging gameplay, and when there is I found myself just selecting "Auto-Battle". It may get more enjoyable eventually, but even though I am a Digimon fan, I just don't enjoy the grind to potentially get to that point. Honestly, I wish they allowed for refunds with longer play times; at least for games like this, where it takes way longer than a couple of hours to get to a point where you would truly know if you are going to enjoy it or not... especially at £40.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally feel this is the best Digimon game in years, and I'm talking as someone who played some of the really old games like Digimon World.I'll start with story gameplay and exploration etc:I've always been okay with Visual Novel style games, and appreciate that it isn't for everyone, but I think it's a really great form of story telling for the vibe this game is going for. Animations and art are beautiful, and it really gives the characters a chance to react to the world and situation around them. The exploration is not as limited as one might expect from a VN, and if you spend some time to go back and forth between places, talking to your friends and Digimon, you gain a lot more lore as well as items. You can essentially do as much or as little as you like, though I feel it is rewarding to explore every option that I can.Thankfully as well, there is a save at any time option which you can even do on choices. So for those who worry about the decisions they make, that's a nice safety blanket.Choices influence your own personality to a small degree which in turns influences your own Digimon's potential Digivolution paths. The other aspect of choices is affinity with other characters which has impact on how they support you in battle. While so far it doesn't seem to be the most impacting choices in terms of "changing the world", the choices do at least not feel empty because of how they effect your party.While there is sadly no English dub for those who want it, the Japanese voices are on point, and for those used to watching subtitled anime, you won't have any issues here.Story (NO SPOILERS):I will quickly add that as an old hardcore Digimon fan of the original anime series and games etc, there are a lot of great throwbacks and story beats that people will appreciate and get some mega nostalgia for. Though new fans will still be able to enjoy the game without that older history - you can definitely feel that this is a love letter to the origins of Digimon.The premise of the game when announced was "a Digimon story for older fans" and you do truly get that vibe. They did think of how old fans will appreciate these moments, but also it is a story that does have a much darker tone and feel to it. Nothing overwhelming, but it plays on this "survival and danger to your own lives" aspect more than the Kid shows did back in the day. Which in a lot of ways adds a depth of realism (yeah, I know... realism in a game with transforming monsters, but hey) that helps ground the player and makes you remember that these are just kids who are initially way out of their depth in a world they don't understand.Speaking of the kids, I find the cast of characters to be fairly appealing. They hit some of the common tropes, but it is a fairly diverse cast of personalities that gives enough of a variety that anyone should be able to find a character they can vibe with.Battle:This is in a lot of ways Final Fantasy Tactics-esque, but would be comparable as well to Disgaea/Fire Emblem. Again, battle visuals are crisp and pretty. Strategy elements seem to be growing more as I progress, as well as unlocking Digivolutions and new Digimon friends to round out the party (though the story Mons are very appealing in their own right).Those used to the Shin Megami Tensei/Persona games etc will feel a familiarity in the recruitment system of wild Digimon as there is a talk option where you have to choose the right options to then get a chance of having that Digimon join you, or give you items. There are also talk options where you talk to your own Digimon as the Tamers, and that gives them temporary buffs and boosts in battle. There are a lot of options and I'm looking forward to uncovering more.Anyway...I hope this at least somewhat helps people on the fence. I will say that a lot of people do seem to be giving it a hard time, but I do think it's because a lot of people aren't used to the Visual Novel style of play. Again, it's not for everyone, but hey. I can only speak from my own experience. I really hope this game sees the success it deserves so Bandai can keep investing in Digimon in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon Survive

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to recommend this game but I can't, especially at full price. With a title Digimon Survive I think most people were expecting something darker even more intense...but they slapped a Teen rating and held back on a lot more of what It could of been. Lets get into it.Gameplay/battle/taming: This is not as fun as FF Tactics and shouldn't be compared to a legendary tactics game as FFT. The maps have little to none interplay which is a shame. You'll get a diamond that heals or damages anyone nearby sometimes. You level up decently and thankfully they do let you re-move if you clicked somewhere wrong by mistake. Taming wild Digimon is a nightmare. They asked super random questions and you have to give them dumb answers. Example.(not a real in game question) "Which is your favorite fruit?" Correct answer is something like "I drive a racecar." Yes, you have three questions like that. After all that dosn't mean you will get the Digimon. It grants you a % so good luck. Digivolution is fine they did good with that.Story/Artwork/OST: Ok. I understand it's a visual novel, sure that doesn't mean it automatically gets a pass for a good game. It does touch on the classic story from the show and that's fine but everything starts to become typical and the characters all get easy predictable labels. You have to survive some of the game's dialogue it gets so repetitive and boring. We get it, you all are scared, this is strange world with mons but shadows and evaporating doesn't strike fear into the reader or looker w/e you call the person playing this. The bond you create with your Digimon is stale and friends are what you make of it with the choices. The overall story really is nothing special typical bottom line destroy the world. Final boss battle for me was super lame and I'll have a photo uploaded on why. Everything looks and sounds great can't complain about the artists.Improvements: Tough to make a better story with a Teen rating but not impossible. More map interaction would of been nice. This is still sold and labeled as a tactics game so don't ignore it. I'm not going into the characters because they are molded to your answers but I don't care if any of them survive...that's the impression they left on me.I give them credit for going for something different and I've always been a big Digimon fan/supporter and will continue to do so. But I will not tell people this is a great game. Get it on sale if your on the fence. Go ahead have at me in the comments I've spoken.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I, like many others have been waiting on this game for 4 years, and my expectations have been met.In previous interviews the producer said the game is roughly 70% VN and 30% TRPG and so far that seems to be the case, the game is a Visual Novel with TRPG elements, and the VN part is the largest and main part of the game, so if you wished for a pure TRPG Digimon you may be disappointed, but so far I'm loving the story, the mystery and the characters. The game has 113 Digimon to find, 117 if you get Guilmon which we don't know if it will be obtainable later(Bandai has already offered bonuses for early sales that never came back so be warned if you want Guilmon). Cyber Sleuth had over 300 Digimon so it definitely feels lacking in comparison, but most fan-favorites and many other cool unknown Digimon to the larger audience are featured in the game so that's a huge plus.The combat so far sometimes seems optional, and it might as well be since the game even included a Auto feature and a option to speed up combat up to 3x, I enjoy doing only the story necessary battles and leave the Farming to the bots, It's very easy to over-level in this game so try to avoid doing too many free battles if you want to keep some degree of a challenge.As I stated previously I've been truly enjoying the story so far (avoiding major spoilers like the plague tho!), the beginning of the game got me hooked to find out the rest of the story. I've been playing on my mother language so I wouldn't know how the translation is in english but so far I'm enjoying the translation(not a 100% but good enough). It's nice to see a few tidbits of a character come out in some of your choices and their own dialogue, the oldest one among the group tries to force himself to be seem as a reliable leader(like Joe from the original anime) for example.This game was designed with replayability in mind, in previous interviews it was already stated that to get the true ending it is necessary to play at least twice, the Karma system of the game defines Agumons digivolution path and the game is hard locked on a Karma story path around chapter 8 depending on your choices so far.If you hover over the dialogue options they will show a color that indicates which Karma they influence and they are always the same position(< for moral, ^ for wrathful and > for harmonious). If you press R1 and L1 on the Dualshock you cycle through available spots to investigate, so don't worry about pointing the ingame camera at everything to find hidden items and just cycle through the options. The prologue is roughly an hour so get ready for that.tl;dr it's a VN game so if you don't have the patience or the will to sit and read A LOT of text then you're probably better off waiting for the next Digimon Story game (that they are already working on!!), but if you hunger for a Digimon game with a unique flavor to the story, with beatiful art and superb music definitely buy it when you can!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon Survive

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon Survive is a mixture of Visual Novel and Tactical RPG (Think Fire Emblem). It's a very different beast to more upbeat games like Cyber Sleuth or the World Series, and in a way that can be off putting, it's a very dark game at times and I found that very refreshing.It's a horror game through and through, something I doubted you could do in a Digimon Setting, where your partner Digimon are, by and large, super powered dinosaurs that can obliterate threats by sneezing on them. It's got fantastic writing, sound design and atmosphere. The Characters, while grating early, quickly grow on you as talk to them more and more and understand who they are more and more.Overall, while the games not perfect, it's good enough that I came into it only having played Cyber Slueth and Rumble Arena 2 and still compelled me to do *5* seperate run throughs of the game. While some things are samey on multiple run throughs, I was surprised by how much wasnt and the True Ending TM is absurdly different.I've never really given thought for Numerical Scores or what have you, but I'd give it 9/10 or 4.5/5. It was a good, solid story that kept me on the edge of my seat for the whole way through and genuinely hurt at times watching the consequences of my actions.I can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon survive is decent overall, a 7/10 for me. If you're not a digimon fan, there are countless better options out there. Digimon fans would probably like this game though, especially old school fans like myself. Survive is very similar to danganronpa in terms of its design. However, danganronpa is a much better game overall for many reasons. Many of the issues with Survive are very simple and it's very puzzling as to why they are even there. I won't cover the good aspects of this game much, as they are plain to see and very subjective. Here's my critique bomb:STORYSurvive's writing, while competent overall, lacks a certain target audience. The dialogue is clearly written for young teenagers, but the game is also clearly made for old school digimon fans, whom are all 18+ today. The dialogue is sometimes so overwhelmingly kid friendly at times, I can't help but cringe. The main character is a stereotypical and clichéd shounen protag who fits so badly into the plot that other characters even make fun of his "perfect" characteristics. VISUALSSurvive's visuals are clearly designed for a handheld. The visuals are so similar to danganronpa's, It wouldn't surprise me if they share the same engine and framework. Danganronpa was made for the PSvita, a 1-decade old handheld that is weaker than a ps3. Luckily, the devs knew this and put a super heavy depth of field effect that obscures the background. Frankly put, the 3D visuals look like dogsh!t whilst the 2D sprites look quite nice. SOUNDTRACKThe soundtrack is insanely limited in terms of quantity. I think there are less than 10 songs in the entire game. Hearing the same 5 songs or so playing on repeat for 40 hours is unprecedented. This is by far the greatest weakness of the game overall. The individual songs are good though, so it's not a complete dumpster fire. GAMEPLAYThe gameplay is good and addicting enough, but it lacks a connection with the story. It's like the team was split into 2 different teams - one responsible for the gameplay, one responsible for the story. One of these teams were clearly put on the dark side of the moon encased in a lead dome, because there are is no way they knew what the other was doing. Right before release they regrouped and jumbled the story and gameplay together. The character's lines barely make any sense before, in, and after combat in terms of context. The gameplay team also thinks the player has all the time in the world, as interacting with anything takes 2-3 clicks to affect the game. It feels incredibly unresponsive and slow and it pisses me off.

_childDocuments_.review: It's refreshing to see a tactical rpg with such a strong narrative focus. The characters feel really believable, with plenty of effort going into making the player experience what it might feel like if such a far-fetched situation actually occurred. There are a couple cringy dialogue choices like too many 'ai'nts' being thrown around, particularly for characters like Aoi. Also, it takes awhile for them to mention that they haven't eaten in like 24 hours in the first part, etc. But I was pretty drawn in otherwise. The early tactical battles are a bit simplistic, but I'm excited to see how it evolves over the course of my playthrough. One thing I would have liked to see is an option to scroll through all of the findable items in a map; it's just too tempting not to use it when it's on, but it kinda defeats the purpose of searching when you can just scroll. It's slightly immersion breaking, even though it is terribly convenient. Overall, though, definitely the best Digimon game I've played; and I was an OG playing Digimon World on the Playstation when it first came out.

Minoru and Falcomon having to work on themselves to become better partners is a rewritten version of the anime pendeant and so on. Combat is nothing worth mentioning either. Its not meaty enough. _childDocuments_.review: I want to make this very very clear for anyone wanting to buy this game.  This digimon game is a visual novel.  Yes, it has a tactical rpg battle system, but trust me when I say it feels like a complete afterthought.  It's as if they focused on the story and visual novel portion and then right before release thought, "oh crap, this is a digimon game, we gotta have them battle, right?" and then they came up with this system that I wouldn't even consider worthy of having in the game to begin with.  I'm really really sad, because visual novels really aren't my thing.  I play digimon to grow and train a team of badass partners that I trash bad guys with, but in this game, how strong your digimon has literally 0 effect on the story.  Not only that, but it's even so loosely tied to the actual meaning of the game, that they let you change the difficulty of EACH individual battle.So, while visual novels aren't my cup of tea, I can see other people who like visual novels really liking this digimon game.  The story isn't bad, in fact, it's rather engaging.  I can understand the gripe of not having english voice acting, but let's be honest, this game had a history of complications and i'm honestly surprised it even came out.  That said... Please come out with a proper digimon game...  Look at pokemon and its transition to a more open world environment with really nice movement systems and a brand new, yet refreshing battle system.  Digimon has always been about taking your tiny little partners and growing and training them to become forces not to be reckoned with.  It's about saving the world(s) from bad actors and bad digimon alike with your friends.  I'd say if you just take a tiny look at Pokemon Arceus and its success, you could easily see how you create a digimon game in the same vein and be wildly successful.  Stop screwing with the digimon ip and come out with something ground breaking, or at the very least, follow in the steps of Pokemon so we can get some decent modern digimon games for the love of all that is digital in this world.
