_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly really well done, the writing is the best part, though the ending can come off a bit campy and over the top if you're sensitive to that kind of thing. The characters were very recognizable and distinct. Biggest issue is that the game is very clumsy in execution a lot of the time, the voice acting is very hit or miss, the graphics are both beautiful and bad depending on what you're paying attention to, and there are a ton of questionable design decisions like the inventory system and the lack of a comprehensive information log of what the player learns over time. Still its a very good game overall, the writing really carries this
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: A deeply thoughtful game that takes the 'bones' of Bethesda exploration games like Fallout or Skyrim and uses it to be squarely focused on ancient history, branching story-lines, and a well executed time-loop mechanic. It has a lot of things to say about sin, law, and ethics. Smartly written and a compact narrative, it's a great game for the price. This is one of those few games that you are really rewarded for picking the right dialogue at the right time, and it never feels forced. Well done, and looking forward to their next game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I played my friend's copy of the game originally, and so I actually have around 10 hours in it and already experienced all 4 endings. However, I decided to buy my own copy to support the devs.This game is one of the best I've played in years. The final ending had me both wholly satisfied and wanting more selfishly. It was satisfying in that the ending was suitable to the game and the characters; I want more because the game was so good!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: A 10/10 game in my opinion ,engaging story ,great characters ,amazing concept ,an underrated game imo,a friend recommended it and i had such a great experience ! ,give it a try if you are into story heavy games and have a keen eye for the dialogue,as the developers said "dont brute force it",Enjoy it .i wish to see more of their work in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Great adventure game. Very interesting story and writing. It is a little janky, but because the platforming is limited this is not really a problem. There are a couple of extended action sequences that were not so good because of the jankiness and I think could have been left out in favor of a totally story driven experience. Not recommended if you are really disinterested in classical history or don't want to read a lot, or if time loops annoy you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing and deeply emotional adventure. You'll explore Greek and Roman history, dabble in philosophy and morality, always surrounded by a cast of lovable characters that are not always what you think them to be. Enough surprises and twists to keep you invested and entertained up to the very end. I had tears in my eyes seeing the ending. Well done, Modern Storyteller. You've done so much with so little, this is game design at its finest.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely story piece. If you like mystery or investigation this is a title I would not miss. Not the longest title, but the multiple angles of approaching the story do make it very enjoyable. The "Groundhog Day" game loop doesn't get very repetitive either given how the game handles the start of the cycle and your progress through the lives of the inhabitants of The Forgotten City.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Keeping in mind that this was made by, like, three people, Forgotten City is a fantastic mystery/adventure game. The world that it builds reminds me a lot of the Myst games in a way. But, this game is less about puzzles and more about exploring and communicating. Unfortunately, I can't say much about the story because of how spoiler prone it is. The best way to play the game is knowing as little as possible about it. Just note that there are some horror elements in the game (some of which are optional). That said, it kept me hooked until I got all the endings. There are a few cons with the game: the combat feels pretty shoe-horned in, the NPCs seem a bit robotic, and one particular quest seems to drag on longer than I'd like. But, those are all pretty minor complaints. Totally would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: A fun mystery with surprising moments, neat twists and turns and interesting historical details that nerds can appreciate.Overall gameplay was around 6 hours, where I hunted down all endings. Might take another hour or so for me to get the last achievements.I enjoyed my time with the game but felt it would have been great if there was... just a bit more. More side stories? More mysteries? Not sure and this definitely isn't the type of story you can make DLC for, so I suppose I'll hope the next game by the Devs will be just as interesting.The gameplay loop (haha) was enjoyable and the few moments of platforming and action were surprising, with certain story moments catching me off guard as a fan of the original mod.Highly recommended, but make sure you know what you are getting into. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Really worth the experience of playing.Minor negatives tho;The rare but possible character model clipping.Incredibly linear in regards to exploration and story line.The primary situation is incredibly obvious, especially if you know a hint of mythology.The positives.None of the minor negatives ruin the gameplay, at all, and it remains a worthwhile enjoyable experience.The backdrop scenery is absolutely breathtaking.Despite some story linearity, there are multiple paths to take once you find them.I genuinely wish there was more exploration and puzzle solving to it, if only to add a way of solving mysteries without character interaction, but that's more of a desire than a critique.Sufficed to say, get this game, it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games of the year and a crowning example of what a high quality Indie game can look like. The game is short and loses its unique appeal once you know the story already, so normally I'd recommend picking up on sale for around $10-15. In this case though, buying it for full price is something the few developers of this game richly deserve. Something everyone should play!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: A Mod's Story to A Game and Success of This MasterpieceThis is a game which started as a Skyrim and the developer was a guy who really wanted to do games and create something which we could enjoy. Well, here it is. Different from all the games we see on the market right now which does not have any guns, battles or mature content but pure history and mythology adapted into a game where you talk and learn about other people from scratch to save a city. Graphics-wise we can see the Unreal Engine did its job great and it's a fine example of new generation games in terms of graphics. When we look at story and gameplay as I mentioned this game is one of its kind where it makes you think of elements from some games like Disco Elysium and Paradise Killer and more but it does not look like any of them at all. Story has its distinct points and raveling as you progress through the game and talk to people in this city. Gameplay is rather simple but subtle in which you have to talk to right people at the right times for your quests to complete and progress within the game. Using 2 history professors to fact check and create the historical and mythological side of this game highly paid off as the player will feel familiar as we hear the names of the gods from our mythologies and their story told correctly which keeps the game as a whole and no blank spaces in both the storytelling and the informational side in it. The characters on the other hand are written fully and they feel like not NPC's but citizens of 2000 years ago walking around the city alive and making you feel like you are not playing a game but you are really there 2000 years ago. The games events are linked to each other which means that one lead can discover more leads and solve many things at once. By this, you never end in a loop or a dead end you always follow a lead and go on through the story. The game also resurfaces a phisolophical question asked by thousands of years about ethics and sins of one person and the innocence of the society. This moral question is there to be talked about, answered by you and you the player only since there is only the game and you to think about it. This is just not a game but a tool to think and a canvas to apply your thoughts.The game by all its component are one piece of art and its a great product of 3 hardworking people along with support. Thank you Nick Pierce, Alex Goss and John Eyre and if you read this you product here really had an effect on my life and my history love. Thank you for this masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I didn’t like the game, but determined to finish the game and I did complete 1 ending.  I found myself running all over the place, constantly talking to the all the games characters.  I didn’t come across any clear indicating factor (guidance) of what character I should approach or what I should do.  I managed to collect all 4 tablets, but my game ended before I could get to the temple.  The game lasted far too long for me (13 hours) but I got bored repeating the same thing and 'character talks' over and over again.  I printed-off an online walk-through for guidance, but the game took a different direction.  I really did not enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This games got it all - Great story, great voice-acting, great atmosphere and graphics, great, not too complicated mechanics - and it was such a great mystery to solve! The world just feels alive (sometimes a bit too much, creeped me out at times.) and you can tell a lot of love went into this game. You could feel the skyrim-roots in the basic mechanics, but that just made me feel at home while navigating the world - beyond that, the games goes above and beyond in terms of bringing mechanics and narrative together with the use of the time loop. They also help you, juuuust enough - It's so much fun piecing the story together and navigating the world, without being pushed too much into any direction. Please, don't watch a playthrough - play it yourself. It's worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. The time looping was done in an interesting way, the characters were well-written, and the overall plot was engaging.My biggest gripe is that the facial animations were not very good. The faces of NPCs visually looked very good, but the lip-sync didn't match the audio very well. In addition, there were a few times where the animations just felt really out of place (two that come to mind, without major spoilers: the way one onlooker reacts after a suicide, and one person's facial expression when you walk in on them crying).I also once hit a bug where two characters kept repeating a conversation constantly, and some other NPCs wouldn't let me talk to them while these two were chatting. This effectively locked me out of being able to talk to those characters, meaning I had to go break some Rules to progress.I did just about everything you can do (though I'm sure I haven't seen every single interaction between characters). It took around 10 hours. I only used a guide for one achievement. This isn't a long game, but my time with it was very enjoyable.I'd probably give it a 9/10. The graphics look really good (a few animations aside), I had a nearly bug-free experience, and I really liked trying to puzzle out what everyone in the city was up to. Solving their problems, and figuring out how to do so such that those problems were easy to solve at the start of a new loop, felt rewarding. And the way your character goes from one time loop to the next means there are some cool ways to obtain items or progress that wouldn't be available in some other time-loop games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic storytelling and mystery. It takes about an hour or so to really get into the game, but the writing is top-notch and the "mechanics" (no spoilers) are executed very well. I ended up grabbing all four endings, which only took around 7-8 hours, but still felt absolutely worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of the original Skyrim mod, and with the story fully realized as a standalone game it's even better. Unlike most whodunnit games, no single bad decision has to affect the outcome. You can always just steal something to trigger the Golden Rule, then sprint back to the portal to restart the day Groundhog Day style. Piss off a character and now they won't speak to you? Once time resets, they will have forgotten everything. All the items you've acquired and knowledge you've gained remains with you in the next time loop, consequence free. There are a couple parts in the game where you do have to fight, but this game is by no means a shooter, and acts of violence won't get you very far because attacking people triggers the Golden Rule and resets the day.  The combat isn't terribly difficult and is definitely geared more towards telling the story than actually trying to kill you. And lastly, the way they tied the narrative in to actual religious mythology was very well done. They definitely did their homework on Roman, Greek, Egyptian, and Sumerian religions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I'll purposely keep this short, so not to spoiler - please buy this game at full price to help the Devs to make more good game's like these! Honestly one of the best games I have played in a while - intriguing story that captivated me from start to finish and that actually managed to make one think about profound themes and maybe even realize a few things you did not before. Thank you to the whole Team!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: George R. R. Martin discourages writers from writing stories in an already established world or setting, warning that said writers will never have that creative spark necessary to discern themselves by taking 'the lazy way out.'However, The Forgotten City, originally a Skyrim mod, completely disproves that view.With easily likeable characters, interwoven side quests and countless memorable plot twists, The Forgotten City easily stands out from it's humble beginnings.However, do not go in expecting an action packed thriller. Your job here is to do some talking, convincing and  investigating, and you don't need a gun for that.The game might give you one anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: A++ Recommendation, would love more games like thisI'm an avid timeloop story fan anyway, but this is beautifully crafted.  The story is good, the twists are great, the mechanics are interesting, the openness of it feels good and unconstrictive, the scenery is beautiful, the writing is funny, it's just ticking a lot of boxes honestly.Plays a lot like Elsinore meets Eastshade, with a spritz of Outer Wilds, you're stuck looping in time in a lost Roman-esque city and information is your greatest weapon. There's well over 20 good characters to get to know and learn the secrets of, and some really fun dives into the history and architecture of it all while trying to unravel the mystery of why you're here, what's keeping you all here, and how you can escapeIt's just clever, that's the first thing that comes to mind when trying to describe it, the dialogue is simple but witty, the twists and turns got some great gasps out of me which I didn't expect, and sometimes the options that open up just made me grin like a giddy child with a new toy.  It's very polished.   I spotted one or two continuity errors - knowledge I shouldn't have had just yet - but nothing that really took away from anything.Someone could make a lil' diorama of the city and I'm buying one, no question.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This game has become very special in the short time that I've played it. Never before had I heard of this title until it came up in a search for immersive open world adventures and found this gem. This incredible adventure is accompanied by one of the most amazing OSTs I've ever heard and is an instant classic for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful puzzle/mystery solving game. If you like finding clever solutions to problems and/or unraveling ancient mysteries, this game is for you.There are multiple endings, but it's not a particularly long game. If you want to achievement hunt or play a new game for each ending, it'll last a bit longer, but I was able to finish all the endings in about 8 hours by reloading old saves. I played the original Skyrim mod, which was itself a masterpiece, and this is much better IMO. I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys mysteries, exploration, and a good story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. I've been anxiously awaiting it's release since the original Skyrim mod and I wasn't disappointed! I could not put it down once I started and when I finished it I was filled with a deep sense of sadness. I was hoping there would be some form of romance (to over complicate the time loop and potentially cause us to hesitate when using it), but I understand those kinds of mechanics are hard to incorporate into a game not focused around it. All the same, it was an amazing game and I would 10/10 play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: For having such a small team, this game is so much better than it has any right to be. It seamlessly integrates aspects of multiple genres into a cohesive romp through time and space in pursuit of answers to a mystery. I wholeheartedly enjoyed the journey and LOVED the quality of life improvement of being able to ask NPCs to run errands for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game - albeit a quick play as I completed it (apparently with the optimal "Canon" ending) in 5 hours. However, I believe it is worth investing in a developer putting out solid content even if it is a quick play. I like that it was more casual and story-focused, but included a handful of action elements giving it a nice mix of game play. Game was fairly seamless - with only the occasional loading screen when moving between lower and upper levels.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: The Forgotten City offers a compelling world with many compelling mysteries to explore, and scratching away at all those various mysterious is consisting rewarding. The game is at its weakest in its few barely serviceable combat sections, and it has a fair amount of jank, but you'll be spending most of your time talking to the varied, well-defined characters populating this isolated town and finding ways to help them out. Oftentimes, there's fun to be had in just arguing philosophy with these characters.Regardless, this is an excellent game that is well worth playing, preferably without getting spoiled beforehand,
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent one. It is much deeper than I expected, and putting together all the information needed to complete the game was an absolute blast. Its short and sweet, but that is perfect for what it is. It doesn't overstay it's welcome, and I'm sure Ill return to it soon to complete the other endings. Support this developer so they can make more awesome games like this one!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is amazing and I cannot recommend it enough. Without spoiling anything, the Story had me glued to the screen from start to finish, the Characters you meet are all interesting and mostly sympathetic (I especially like Vergil), you learn a bunch about history and ancient legends and the dialogues are well made and often funny (You can explain memes to a roman priestess). Plus, there is 4 endings, 2 which I have unlocked by now, so there is some replayability even after you know most of the twists and turns of the Story. I can only recommend it to anyone interested in good stories and history.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This game drove me insane. If you don't like repeating your steps all over again over and over and over again don't get this game. I really wanted to like it, I really did but I couldn't handle it. It's exactly like ground hog day in the movies. If you have seen Happy Death Day it's just like that were you repeat everything and you get a tiny bit ahead then the last time you did it or sometimes you don't. You are also timed as in you have to figure how to save everyone and solve the puzzles before someone get hurts. Oh and you don't know how much time you have ever. So you might be close but then have to start the game over again. No joke it gave me a head ache and I played this for a few days. Just be warned if you play this game of the never ending repetition.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Forgotten City is a creative and engaging game. I played without quest markers, which I definitely recommend. I stumbled upon one of the endings quite early, but was able to backtrack and continue playing for a while afterward. Total playing time for me was 12 hours. Great game, especially if you enjoy ancient history and have a basic idea of Roman culture.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! Love how in depth the story is with different solutions to tasks and different endings. It's detective story urges you to dig deeper into the lives of The Forgotten City residence whilst trying to unravel what you are doing there, who you can trust and how you can influence everything around you.Fantastic work from the creators! I first got ending 1 to which I then changed some decisions and got ending 4. (What an ending - so happy!) Would defiantly recommend this game! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: The Forgotten City is a super engaging mystery game. It's a solid unique and worthwhile adventure you can easily get lost in. I can't really add much without spoiling it, you'll have to dive in.In terms of gameplay, it's very simplistic. Pretty much paint by numbers, meaning you'll hardly miss anything.A+ for the voice acting, which greatly contributes to making this a solid recommendation as dialogues are a major part of the game.If you're not into walking-talking games, then this really won't be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, philosophical mystery. Honestly, solving the puzzle of the game is probably more fun than the relatively elementary philosophy, but there are still some lingering things to think about once you learn the main thrust of the game. Overall a brief, but enjoyable, whodunit with a fantastical twist.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: The Forgotten City is so much more than just a Skyrim mod turned standalone indie game — it’s a truly enthralling piece of storytelling with a beautifully realized world, but features some platforming and combat that isn't as polished as I'd like. Despite its few flaws it’s still incredibly special and a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I have completed a few of the endings but still have some to go. Don't worry no spoilers here! The game itself is incredible. The map is small but it feels like it fits so well that one doesn't mind it. The real incredible part of this game is the story. The story is incredible and goes to show how a small dev team can out-write triple A studios.  Hats off to the team that put this together.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Some might see that summery and think 'Outer Wilds'. Understandable, but its different enough and doesn't make you use as much brain power as the other. There is a quest journal and quest marker system that pretty heavily guides you around, but you still have to figure some things out, and in different ways, ex. Deus Ex.I like it though. For a game made by a few dudes its pretty fantastic work. If they don't keep their own company I hope they get hired into some high positions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Well structured, well written, story that gives the player freedom to explore a beautiful ancient world (the only first person game in existence IMO that lets you explore and interact with Ancient Roman culture). Beautiful visuals, atmosphere and attention to historical accuracy. The game both intrigued and motivated me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I don't remember the last time I binged a game so quickly. The story is captivating and the gameplay is more akin to that of a detective story, almost like a 3D, modern point-and-click. My biggest, biggest draw for this game is how quickly you make progress, and how earned it feels. Yahtzee, the game critic, sometimes talks about the ability for a game to make you feel smart for figuring things out, even if they are not objectively difficult things to figure out. This game does that really well.Some flaws:- Janky character animation.- Grating music.- Weird combat. It's not difficult, just...feels tacked on.- The game is quite pricey for what it offers. I got it on 50% off and still only managed to get around 6 hours out of it. Caveat is, the quality of those 6 hours was very good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: At 7.3 hours, I've gotten all 4 endings(discounting minor variations on how). The writing is amazing, and it carries the entire game. The city looks great, and from what I can tell it's a very thoroughly researched scale model of a roman city. Only one bug, and I just reloaded the last auto-save from a minute earlier, as-well as frame rate drop in some areas. They even found a way to get around making the player redo everything when they reset the day. This game is very nearly flawless, and I can't wait to play the next game from these devs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game because some people say it is comparable to Outer Wilds, but it is nothing of the sort. Regardless, I tried to give this game a fair chance but it is absolutely packed full of quirky attempts to be funny, pop-culture references (in a game about a 2 thousand year old city) and modern day Western political undertones shoehorned into the dialogue. Stopped playing early on because of these reasons so I won't speak on the actual story or gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This just gets on the right side of the thumb scale. A diverting (f short, 10 hours to do all four endings) mystery constructed by Classical Antiquity nerds. Starts off well enough, you (a person of one of four particular backgrounds, although it scarcely seems to matter which one you choose) wash up on a river bank, where a woman directs you to a set of ruins where some other person has disappeared into. You head in and stumble into an underground city populated by extras from the cast of the HBO series Rome, only if Rome was under a curse where everyone would die if one person committed a sin and was also combined with the movie Groundhog Day. And there are ziplines for some reason.This is all as intriguing as it sounds, and the game starts off pretty well. You chat with people and discover more about your environment and the fact that there's a girl who got poisoned, another one is missing, yet another one has barricaded herself in a temple at the top of a hill, there's some drama about an upcoming election, and a mysterious stranger in town is looking for a guy with different-colored eyes, and doesn't this all sound really cool. My favorite part of the early game was working out with one of the NPCs about how you (and everyone else) actually came to this place, which is the best moment in the game, where I may have actually exclaimed, "oh, neat!"Unfortunately, once you get past the promising start, the game loses steam. All these interesting things happening get resolved quickly and anticlimactically, usually after a conversation or two. How will you get the evil moneylender to drop out of the election? Pretty easily, as it happens! How will we get into the temple with the crazy lady? By accident! What secrets are hidden underneath the city? Not much!You run around, you talk to people, you complete a series of what feel like side quests that aren't really "side" because they need to be done in order to progress the main plot for the "proper" ending. The proper ending is pants, by the way. a novel that abruptly cuts off so you can have a philosophical debate with the author about how he's as much of a ponce as any of his characters. It all feels very abrupt and rushed (like the second season of the HBO series Rome).And yet this is still a thumbs up review, partially considering the degree of difficulty about how this game was designed by like four people using a Commodore 64 and a roll of duct tape or whatever (and the Unreal Engine, because if you're masochists, there are no sense in half-measures) and partially because what is there in the game is actually pretty well done. The dialogue is well-written, there's some humor sprinkled in without things getting overly silly. I wound up liking many of the characters even if I barely got to know them. When your biggest gripe about the game is "I wanted more of what you were offering" that's really not so bad.Anyway, these are developers who I'm going to keep an eye on, because an expanded version of The Forgotten City would be a really terrific game that I would enjoy diving into. Even the cut-rate version is worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely interesting approach to storytelling in games.The baseline plot is not particularly interesting, but is well presented.The movement and gameplay systems are no innovation, but are well implemented and fluidly put together (particularly the shifts between dialogue and general gameplay).The game truly shines in the way it melds the historical and philosophical elements in a coherent fashion. These themes are all presented with a pace that allows the game to be a decent introductions to a variety of topics in history, philosophy and even theology.This is a decent game for the general audience, but it is outstanding for people looking for interesting approaches to present difficult "academic" topics in a palatable way for general audiences. I wouldn't even be surprised if somewhere down the line this game is suggested as a possible "motivator" source for high school or undergraduate courses.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original Skyrim mod, I can say this tale has always been my favorite creation to come from that community.  So years ago, I was elated to hear that the team was working to turn their creation into its very own game.  And, after years of waiting, I am soo happy to say that it has been everything I could hope for and more!  There have been plenty of changes since the original, mostly in aligning the narrative to make sense to players not within the Elder Scrolls universe.  But there are plenty of elements from the original mod that return, and it has been so nice to play through this and relive them all in this *immaculate* ;) recreation.Even if you have never played the mod, I strongly recommend giving this game a chance.  And if you have, I can only encourage you to do so even more strongly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I've played just two hours of the game, and I can confidently state that I'm already completely engrossed! This game has surpassed my expectations. I came across an online article mentioning that it originated as a Skyrim mod, and that piqued my interest to give it a try. The modding community consists of incredibly creative individuals who have contributed to its excellence.All in all, the game is fantastic, boasting a profoundly intricate story to delve into. Without a doubt, I wholeheartedly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly my favorite game from 2021. An excellent, engaging mystery with smart writing and many twists and turns. The city is beautiful, highly detailed, and the characters feel real. All of it ties together with an effective musical score, and a clever use of the time-looping mechanic that makes it stand out from other games. Once I started playing, I didn't want to stop until it was over.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Forgotten City is certainly a pretty fun, short game. My experience left me a bit overwhelmed by all the options at the start, but very often a solution to one quest leads to resolving another - you'll promptly check all of the required boxes! You can't softblock yourself in any way and you can even avoid doing certain actions over and over again by havign someone else do them for you instead. The game has a great atmosphere, dubbing is well done, characters are well written - both those likeable and less friendly - and the mystery beats can certainly suprise the player! The Forgotten City also offers also some completely optional exploration and finding treasures - while simple, can offer you that 'yes!' moments. I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Simply awesome,I was surprised at every turn.The mechanics make you really - and easily, i usually can't b e bothered - invested in every character's life,I actually learned stuff, we think we now about the romans and others ancient civilisations because we watch Gladiator or Moon Knight and expect them to be a documentaries,That game got me thinking, debating with myself and the characters - WITHOUT BORING ME, granted i'm a nerd for ethics, but easily distracted - about both what was happening in  the context of the plot as well as some big stuff like morality, personal responsability, community... Exploring many different points of view of many cultures as they interact with each other at a time we think barbaric because they didn't know stars are made of gas but who cares. What are right and wrong? Does it depend on personal or historical context? Are they absolutes? A form of spectrum? Should an answer to that should be personnal or a communal consensus?Reminded me a bit of The Good Place, presenting you with a good mysterious plot, but tricking you in studying a syllabus about the many forms of ethics proposed by many philosophers by making understanding ethics part of the plot and important to figure out what's going on.Emmotional as well, the different endings each commented on my actions and left me thinking on them. Was not kidding about caring about the characters. I didn't come to love them, I've only known them for a few in game days, real world hours. yet as their fate rest in their own hands, as I could influence them i could influence their fate for the best, so by causality of responsability, I was responsible in part for all their fate.I obviously wanted to help those I liked, those I deemed worthy, those of compassion, intelligence. But what of the others? Should I save abnoxious, hateful, manipulative or selfish people, just because I have the means? Not doing so would be wrong now wouldn't it?I can only babble about ethics for so long without straying off topic or spoiling the game.JUST PLAY IT.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the setting of this game, we don't have many games devoted to Roman culture and their lifestyle, rise of different religions and historical events and figures included with this game. Also some of the music in this game reminds of Carl Sagan's Cosmos, especially the ambiance and the music featured in the ship of the imagination parts. Fantastic game with many different endings, well worth getting, although it is not as open world but still a great setting and storyline.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Not a game that requires much thinking or gives many choices. You can waste time talking to every NPC with the exact same dialogue options or just do the very obvious thing to help them. There is very little to find by exploring and no room for player expression. I accidentally sequence broke the game and bugged several NPCs into not speaking to me until I looped again. The best thing about the game is that it's very short and didn't waste too much of my time
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: #SPOILER FREE#Before you purchase or play this game: - The game is primarily based around dialog and dialog choices (all of which are well written) with a selection of memorable characters, the stories are interwoven and result in the game having multiple endings; there are also a couple of very simple combat encounters, but the meat and potatoes of the game is exploring the forgotten city, talking to the residence, and trying to piece together whats happening and how to solve the games underlying problem- highly suggest not reading anything more than you need to about this game, most of the fun is uncovering the story yourself, and some things are easy to spoil if you read the wrong thing!- When you start the game, HIGHLY RECOMMEND you turn OFF the quest notifications and quest markers; I found some of the notifications gave away clues in their wording which i had yet to pick up myself.- Remember this is a game made by a small handful of people, there is some very minor jank and bugs, but nothing to tarnish the overall experience or take away from the fantastic writing and story telling.My thoughts:Never played the original Skyrim mod but decided to give this a try based on a recommendation; this being the first steam game I've cared enough about to finish every ending and 100% all the achievements for should say enough about my experience. You can tell a lot of effort and attention has been given to the story and characters and its very well paced.ON the technical side I encountered a few minor bugs, inconsistencies and interesting pieces of terrain to get stuck on, but when you consider the story behind the guy who came up with this and the eventual size of the team that mulled it together it is truly a masterpiece worthwhile experiencing, just for the story and historically accurate world alone
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished playing the game and wanted to really thank the creators!They made a great game with a very interesting story despite their limited resources compared to the big gaming companies, you really notice how much time and effort the team spent on this project.Many thanks for this amazing video game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a huge fan of historical fiction, but this game really engaged me. You get trapped in a city full of romans and have to discover how to stop a curse that results in the residents getting turned to gold and you stuck repeating the same day over and over. The characters were all well fleshed out and voiced, and there's some absolutely killer dialogue, some very meta and funny, a lot of it touching, and some philosophical. There are some amazing set pieces, and the environment itself has a great natural feeling inter-sectional design so you can always easily get to where you need to go.Really enjoyed it, and hope the devs make another game soon!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy mystery time loop games like Outer Wilds, only with a skyrim instead of a oddworld flare, then you will both enjoy and blitz through this game. Its also a long time since I had to memorise a map, even a small one, instead of having a mini or pause menus (not a bad thing or a good things just an observation)So get it, or if you're on the fence get it on sale, or don't.I have no power over you. But not playing it would violate the golden rule, just fyi.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: An intriguing question turned into an elaborate murder mystery with a little bit of the horror of civilization built on civilization. Forgotten City is very compelling, its many puzzles are delightful to parse out and its loop mechanic much more fun than frustrating thanks to Gularius' whole deal. While some of the choices late game kinda feel a little weaker, personally never a fan of  as a plot twist however ending the game on a Socratic dialogue did hit. The weakiness that struck me the most is the models are a little... well not nearly as good looking as the rest of the game which is what makes them feel so uncanny. Sparse criticism from someone who hates looping games, and hates timed segments in games though. Ultimately I just couldn't resist the charm of the character driven puzzles, the world, honestly being a historical game genuinely wanting to interface with the history of its world. The best Karen joke in history. I just really felt charmed. I also really loved that the endings dont feel like "choices" and more pushing the limits of the scenario  with different ideas. When I learned the other endings it felt more "Oh so Yeah that would cause that and so forth." Its all just genuinely engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This thing is like a wild blend between an elder scrolls game and loz majora's mask with improvements to the formula of both. A touching story, with great characters, and some thought provoking tomfoolery to boot. Also if ur an archaeology nerd it has some fun tidbits. Honestly one of my favorite games of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:+ Amazing time loop story+ Great characters+ Overall experience - Only the slightest non-issuesLong version: [No spoilers]This game has probably near perfected the time loop gimmick in video games and that is a praise all on it's own, The devs really did damn near nail everything with this one. There literally is nothing else to say but to encourage you to stop this review and play the game.All right, there has to be some negative - the only criticism would be that there are a few achievements (other than the "speedrun" ones) that you can miss out on. Some make sense, but one in particular is locked if you don't choose X dialogue on first contact and it's impossible to choose said dialogue on subsequent loops. There may be other such issues, but I only ran into one that slightly bothered me.Other than that there are a few places where very minimal social commentary about [CURRENT EVENTS] is thrown in, which might irk some people, but it never felt forced and in terms of dialogue options was I think always optional.Overall 6/5 Time loop game, takes less than a working day so just buy and enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite a fun mystery to solve. :)It does start a bit slow, but it's something many mystery games struggle with. You spend quite a bit of time just wandering around and talking to everyone, and asking about their stories and their concerns. Fortunately, after that, you'll probably have all the story hooks you need to start making progress and discovering all the different content this game has to offer. I especially appreciated all the effort that the developers put into the epilogue of the 'canon ending'. I won't go into details to avoid spoilers, but the fact that every single person has different responses to you based on  how exactly you went through the game is delightful. :) It shows the amount of effort and care the developers put in, and really made the ending feel like 'mine'. I played it twice, just to see different dialogue the second time!I recommend this game for anyone looking for a mystery. If you're looking for action... It's probably not for you,  though there are a few action themed sections. The facial expressions can also be a bit weird sometimes, but that doesn't bother me. I'm a bit autistic, so all faces look weird to me anyway. :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with a captivating story and a well-rounded puzzles. When I was stuck, the game would give small hints to nudge me to the solution without giving the answer away, and when a particular quest line ran out of leads, the others filled them in. A simple game that'll take about one or two afternoons to complete. Please play this game before it gets spoiled!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I've been eyeing this game off and on since STEAM announced it. All I can say is don't judge this game by comments.  Play it for yourself then decide.  The developers requested for no spoilers, so there will not be any here! After hours of playing this, I can say there is a lot to this game. The graphics are wonderful, the story is intriguing, well thought out and put together. The NPCs are fully voiced.  This is a game about the decisions you make and it makes you think about the consequences of those choices. (Like I stated you must play it for yourself to experience the game fully.)  Make sure to talk to every NPC, do the quests they give you, explore everything and everywhere, read everything, investigate (look) at the items, etc. Remember, there are consequences for breaking the "golden rule".  I made one by walking away from the game to long and letting it run, I came back to find my character dead. LOL   SO DON'T LEAVE YOU'RE GAME RUNNING...SAVE AND LOG OUT IF YOU PLAN ON BEING GONE TO LONG!  Make sure to save often while playing. By saving often you save a lot time have to repeat yourself if you happen to die. Yes, you can multiples of the same game.  That way if you don't like a decision you made you can go back to a previous save and redo it.UPDATE:  I completed my first play through. (There are 4 different endings.) What an excellent, well thought out game. The story is very intriguing.  I can say how some of the things mentioned about human nature through our history is so true! And the developers know there history very well.  I cannot wait to see what this team of 3 does in the future. I know they have me wanting more of this kind of gaming genre.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: The Forgotten City is an amazing detective game, filled to the brim with surprises and plot-twists. It also helps a lot that the roman setting and the visuals are simply said: "cool as hell" and that the characters have a lot of nuances and interactions with each other. Even though the action sequences are a bit janky they can be skipped for the most part and sometimes characters seem a bit weird with their dialogues, overall it is a very good game anyone that likes to rumble their brains about should at least try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting game who's premise is doing all the work as an incompetent writer just ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed every once in a while so hard that it undermines all the hard work that is making the game great. The player character is a potato of the grandest kind. _childDocuments_.review: The Forgotten City is a wonderful little adventure about the consequences of the ethical Golden Rule (Do unto others as you would have them do unto you) taken to its extremes. The game might look a little dated but is full of witty writing and genuinely heartfelt moments. Without spoiling anything: the central mystery of the game is impossible not to solve if you go at it for long enough, exploring new options of dialogue or taking new actions. There are some minor combat encounters which are generally optional. I played through them on my first attempt and can pretty safely say that they are not great, but they're still serviceable. The characters are charming, some major reveals had me audibly gasp and the ending even brought a little tear to my eye. An overall lovely experience that I would advise anyone to play but especially so if you played games like Outer Wilds or The Sexy Brutale ;) iykyk

_childDocuments_.review: Very impressive coming from a 3 person team. A Herculean task ;)Why a negative then? Main point: If the reviews overall here were more lukewarm I'd be giving a thumbs up. This game is perfectly enjoyable, if pedestrian. I think some may be lured in by the tags and review %, only to be disappointed. Given the price tag (for a ~6 hour experience), it's a buyer beware situation. Read some positive and negative reviews before purchasing. If you're the type of person who will regret buying this game, I 100% guarantee you'll know it when you read the negatives. For an actual review of the game: It's disappointing when a story loses steam from start to finish. This is one of those. Instead of a build up, conflict, resolution kind of thing, it sets up an actually pretty compelling mystery in the first hour that just slowly deflates as you pull back each curtain. With some structural/storyboard changes, there could have been interesting developments and reveals as time went on, instead of it dumping all of the mystery on your head before minute 30. For example, you'll be aware of the time loop well before you have to encounter it, just because of a basic exposition dump. Likewise, the nature of the golden statues is immediately apparent. And I'm not sure what the angle was with Al, either, since you instantly find him. These could have been interesting things to discover.   Or, to extract from the dialog trees of characters that otherwise don't have meaningful ones. Imagine if For a game with very little gameplay outside of walking & talking, it really needed the walking & talking to be good. Both fell short at different times for different reasons, and the nature of the 'canon' ending (to put it diplomatically) risks alienating the audience and souring the whole experience. Since there's no real gameplay to offset this, you may very well take nothing meaningful away from this game.  If you're looking for 6-10 hours to kill, you could do worse. I could name a few other similar titles on Steam that are cheaper or better for the time investment. Read up on the reviews before you decide to buy!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing gem to play!I played the Skyrim mod a few years ago and have been eagerly awaiting this full release version. I was not disappointed! Some things may be similar, albeit very minor, but it isn't enough to warrant the thought of "I've played this before, I know what to expect". The writing is great, the characters each have their own personalities to love or hate, and overall I enjoyed my time with it. _childDocuments_.review: Emotional:You know how some games just make you feel profoundly good? Well, this is one of those games. A tremendously well-made piece of digital art form, which challenges and engages you while being little more than a walking/talking simulator. A game that you just wanna go and show to everyone and make them play until they reach the Canon Ending (which might be one of the most satisfying endings in gaming, period).And to top all that - and I am not kidding here - it will stir your interest in the Classical History and teach you stuff better than any Assassin's Creed game. It will probably also make you a kinder, more empathic person.Rational:Over this 6-10 hour first-person adventure you will be doing a variety of quests, most of which are structured like in a classic RPG - talk to this person, find an item, talk to another, make a decision, do some investigating, come back later etc., albeit without combat (mostly). All NPCs in this game play a crucial part in the story and narrative, and absolutely no part of the world feels like filler. In fact, the game is chock-full of revelations, a-ha! moments and meaningful discoveries. But please don't expect action setpieces or fast gameplay: this is a very methodical experience, which rewards patience, curiosity and attentive play. Forgotten City will be especially fun for those who enjoy learning about ancient cultures like Rome and Greece. There is a time loop mechanic here, which is interwoven into the narrative brilliantly. Saying anything more would be a major spoiler, so I definetely recommend going in blind. However, it speaks volumes about the quality of the game's writing, because despite the fact that I accidentally managed to spoil one of its biggest surprises, it didn't affect my perception of the game at all due to the sheer amount of other, even more interesting secrets to uncover and mysteries to solve.There are multiple endings, and you, as a player, have total agency in how things play out.The visuals are nice, and there are a lot of cool details for history buffs. The characters are convincing and endearing despite modest facial animations. The voice-acting and music are top-notch. Go play Forgotten City, support its developers. I highly recommend it. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Unearthing the Mysteries of a Bygone Era - "The Forgotten City" ReviewRating: 9/10"The Forgotten City," developed by Modern Storyteller and published by Dear Villagers, is a time-looping adventure that masterfully blends intricate storytelling, moral dilemmas, and a deep sense of mystery. Originally a mod for Skyrim, this standalone release expands on its predecessor, delivering a captivating and thought-provoking experience.Storyline : 10/10The narrative of "The Forgotten City" is the shining jewel in its crown. Set in an ancient Roman city trapped in a time loop, players unravel a complex web of secrets, morality, and consequences. Every decision made has far-reaching implications, and the game weaves a tale that is as intellectually stimulating as it is emotionally resonant. The characters are well-crafted, each with their own motivations, adding layers of intrigue to the unfolding mystery.Gameplay and Exploration : 8/10The gameplay revolves around exploration, dialogue, and solving intricate puzzles. The city itself is a marvel of design, with attention to detail that makes each location feel both historically authentic and fantastical. The time-looping mechanic adds depth to the exploration, encouraging players to experiment with choices and observe the consequences.Graphics and Atmosphere : 8/10While not a graphical powerhouse, "The Forgotten City" boasts an art style that immerses players in its ancient world. The atmospheric design, coupled with a haunting and evocative soundtrack, creates an ambiance that is both enchanting and eerie. The aesthetic choices contribute significantly to the overall experience.Moral Dilemmas and Choices : 10/10Central to the game's allure is the emphasis on moral dilemmas and choices. Every decision made impacts the narrative, and the game doesn't shy away from exploring complex ethical questions. The interconnectedness of characters and events ensures that each playthrough unveils new layers of the story.Voice Acting : 8/10The voice acting in "The Forgotten City" is commendable, with performances that bring the characters to life. While some moments might lack the polish of AAA titles, the overall quality of voice work adds depth to the narrative and enhances the emotional impact of key moments.Replayability : 10/10One of the game's strengths is its replayability. Multiple endings and branching narratives encourage players to revisit the time loop, making different choices and uncovering alternative paths. The depth of the narrative ensures that subsequent playthroughs reveal new layers of the story.Conclusion : 9/10"The Forgotten City" stands as a testament to the narrative potential of video games. Its intricate storytelling, moral complexities, and the interplay of choices create an experience that transcends the boundaries of traditional gaming. For those who appreciate a thinking person's adventure, where the story is the true star, "The Forgotten City" is a must-play. It not only pays homage to its mod origins but elevates itself to a position among the finest narrative-driven games, offering an experience that lingers in the mind long after the final time loop concludes.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no question The Forgotten City a very well-made game, both visually and technically. The dialogue is well-written,. The NPCs are interesting, and the game is charged with mystery from the get-go, although it is debatable whether it succeeds in mainlining player interest to the end.One thing needs to be said clearly, and that is The Forgotten City is not a Skyrim game and has little to do with Skyrim. It may have started out as a Skyrim mod, and an excellent one at that, but apart from some of the visual similarities, the comparison stops there. Players looking for a Skyrim-type RPG will be disappointed. This is a dialogue-driven puzzle loop - a visual novel, if this is your sort of thing. Some reviewers have called it a walking simulator. It is more than that because it sends you back to the beginning every time you fail - minus being dead, unless you keep on failing. Each repeat brings with it new revelations and information, but if you are averse to repeating yourself (without cheating), then this game probably isn't for you. In order to give this game justice, one has to approach it without preconceptions. Forget Skyrim. Forget RPGs, and approach The Forgotten City as a sleuthing game. If you're not into mystery, the game is not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game that you should buy at full price if you can. Support these developers.In The Forgotten City, you’re an archaeologist or explorer or British colonist or whatever you choose, who stumbles upon a trapped floor while exploring Roman ruines that leads you to an underground city still in Ancient Rome. Its occupants, you now included, are trapped in an authoritarian nightmare where all of them will die if even one person commits a “sin” - be it murder, theft or, uh, attempting to escape. As if they have some sort of right to freedom. Y’know, the real heavy-hitters. This is called “The Golden Rule” and as you might expect, it’s completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dysfunctional. Your job is to figure out how to fix it with the help of the city’s magistrate who will open a portal to send you back in time if-slash-when whoever’s in charge goes goblin mode and tries to kill everyone. I could rant about how much it’s lifting from Bioshock, what with the isolated “utopia” falling victim to human flaws and descending into authoritarianism to keep it running, but I’m a busy man so let’s just say that the setting is still extremely creative, well-executed and lives up to the potential of its mysteries.It’s gratifying the sheer amount of thought put into every angle of this premise. Most of the questions you might have, from how specifically the rules work to how to change the very toxic beliefs of people from the Roman Empire, are almost all addressed in some way - in so much detail that conversation is the main gameplay loop.There are a few short-lived action segments but dialogue puzzles are the main way you progress in the game - for the most part they’re pretty good, but it can occasionally grind gears with the time loop mechanic. You always have options to give the more terrible characters a well-deserved scolding, which is satisfying, but that often locks you out of further discussion for that loop. And since half the time you need something from them, you’re forced to take a more manipulative or empathetic route, and in doing so might actually start to empathise with them. Maybe you’ll need to lie, maybe you’ll need to be brutally honest, maybe you’ll need to do something they’ll hate you for because it’s still the right thing to do. It’s great. These are balanced out with more laidback philosophical discussions with no stakes, which were just as enjoyable. I like when the discussion is itself the exercise and there’s no pressure to prove anything if you don’t want there to be, which goes for the writers as well. It’s a confident game, but rarely feels pretentious.That’s not to say it doesn’t resolve its own questions. A lot of stories like to dump philosophical treatises on the floor for you to pick through while it hedonistically lowers grapes into its mouth. The Forgotten City follows things through, even for the simplest ideas. For example, collective punishment: the argument in favour of The Golden Rule is that it really encourages people to spy on their neighbours to avoid being punished. And while technically it works in Roman armies (as decemation), the cost is due process and value of life. It’s obviously abhorrent but to prove that, there are quests based around characters that plot around the rule in the shadows so that they can’t be monitored. Decemation might work when you sleep three feet away from your sweaty, handsome soldier mates, not so much when the dangerous ones hide in villas you can’t enter without vandalism or stealing a key (which will both get everyone killed). Without wishing to spoil, the way you get around those sins is nothing short of absurd and not something possible in real life.Every quest has some sort of thematic resolution like this, and they’re all interconnected, too. Whether a life is ruined or repaired, events ripple all the way down the social ladder. It really helps the city feel like a place rather than a series of lectures on politics from the writer. Fractal objectives might not be great in a mostly linear game like Bioshock, but it works with the tight setting of The Forgotten City. It’s like a giant societal Heath Robinson machine.In retrospect, describing these as “puzzles” might not be accurate. You only need to succeed once to learn that it pays to play nice with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ people, after which you start doing it all the time. And it can be overt what choices you should make simply by the detail of one option compared to the rest. I’m not saying there are no genuine puzzles, there are, just not as many as I would like. Ultimately I think I admire the game more for its content and room for agency than its actual challenge.Being locked out of conversations is also pretty annoying sometimes, too, to bring it back to the time loop mechanic. I like that characters can have realistic boundaries without ruining the story, but… Some selections of answers can seem pretty interchangeable even though only one progresses things, like with the gold digger chick, or if you’re in one of those Mousetrap quests and have all the solutions but need to restart because of a single misclick, those cases are very trial and error and resetting the loop becomes a chore. This also kinda discourages experimentation. To be honest, I’d rather go the point-and-click adventure game route of a Men-In-Black mind-wipe between every attempt.Another issue with the dialogue system is a common pitfall of a lot of choices-matter games, that being that its moral dilemmas are always filtered through the perspectives of the writer, who will always have a limited perspective. It’s in line with the setting, I guess - everyone having limited perspectives on morality is the whole conceit of The Golden Rule - but it’s not great for immersion if you’re ahead of the discussion with no way to express yourself. For example, one of the common counter-arguments characters make against your points about ethics is that you or other cultures do the same bad thing in a different way. And every time that came up I immediately thought of that line from The Big Short: “That doesn’t make me wrong.” “No, it just makes you a hypocrite.” I was crying out for some sort of option to say, like, “if you’re right, then neither of us can excuse our unethical behaviour and we both deserve a clip around the ear.”As for being behind the discussion, I actually think that can be pretty fun. When arguments sprout fully formed from the dialogue box for you to click on - on paper it might seem dumb, like it’s sucking all the challenge out of the game, but if even you listen to a particular opinion and instinctively recoil, you might not have an instinctual counter-argument or the the patience or concentration to piece one together. So when an argument would appear that put the pieces together, I would cry “exactly!” and eagerly choose it. On the flipside, there were a few conversations where I had a limited or wrong opinion that the puzzles made me reflect on, like some of the more authoritarian laws of Sentius, the city’s magistrate, that are mostly necessary to keep everyone alive, where the fault was with whatever dumbass made the Golden Rule and less with him. He’s far from perfect, of course, but I felt bad for reflexively getting angry when I would have to make the exact same decisions in his position and would also want a little sympathy for my trouble. (That’s another idea that evolves over the game.)The game itself is janky as hell and I had a few bugs, but as the twists and turns went on I found it more endearing than frustrating. Like the developers had a certain vision of graphics and atmosphere in mind they didn’t want to compromise on, so they pushed as hard as they could to just get it over the line. The grandiose scenery a title like “The Forgotten City” would imply gets the visual detail that it deserves. It’s absolutely dripping with passion and I love that. It’s even made in Australia. Go team. Hearty recommendation. Get it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: I'm a huge fan of exploration mystery games, and this game, with its unique mechanics, offers a refreshing take on that genre. It's definitely story-rich, and its lore--based in real ancient mythologies--raises many philosophical questions that stick with the player past the credits. I first heard about this game while it was early in development after its first life as a Skyrim mod, and I'm happy to say it lived up to my hopes for it.Cons: there are a few bugs here and there, though nothing game-breaking so far. Considering this was developed by a very small team of talented individuals, I can excuse them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I really feel you can't say much about this game specifically without ruining it, so I will say this:I nearly gave up at a couple points, because things didn't add up the way I wanted them to. I am glad I didn't give up. It's a really cool game with sensible paths and a wild amount of depth for a relatively tiny world. I also might not have even gotten through the first little bit, because it was pretty slow to get started. I hope this encourages you to get past that slow opening: once I got hooked, I couldn't stop playing until I got an ending I was satisfied with.Also, they do time travel pretty damn well, and that is *not* easy. 9.5 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I got this 2 days ago and I completed all the endings, by far the best narrative game I've played. The entire plot is so elegantly done with genuinely good plot twists and changes. All the characters are well done, nothing is cringy. If you are into mythology, thats an added bonus, tons of references and allusions to various legends. Amazing world building, you can discover things about characters by seeing where they live n such. The mechanics and lore are all consistent and make sense within the world.It feels satisfying to figure things out but nothing feels hard.And I can't say anything more because figuring out everything yourself is the best part. This game is worth every penny. Do me and yourself a favor and play it.10/10Literally the only thing negative thing I can think of was that the combat (what little there is) wasn't amazing, however I played exclusively with a controller and can imagine it being far easier and better with mouse and keyboard.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: I'd just come off a renewed binge of Outer Wilds so this time loop mystery was definitely my jam. The story is great and the many mysteries always felt enticing rather than tedious details to figure out. The shortcuts that open up over time are also a great bonus.Normally, I'm the type that often needs to consult a walk-through because I'm stuck on some excessively-clever solution or been forced to stare at it for too long, and miss something obvious. With this game, everything flowed so well and had multiple ways to find a solution, without anything feeling patronizingly easy.That said, the minor combat feels tacked on, the levels had lots of weird invisible walls, and oddly I was able to get the final ending without even touching what seemed to be an integral mystery/reveal. Insignificant gripes honestly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent indie adventure games where you loop through time to uncover the intertwined mysteries of an ancient roman city under the thumb of an omniscient law, The Golden Rule. If you like the looping (and spooky) aspects of Majora's Mask, you will definitely enjoy this. There is a system to let you streamline previously completed tasks.Some of you may remember this as the title of an outstanding Skyrim mod. The creators did fully flesh out their vision and create a full game more than distinct from the mod. And their dev name, Modern Storytelling, ridiculously undersells the incredible talent and writing put into this game. I fell in love with all the characters and the city, which is full of history, intrigue, some open philosophy about morality,  and plenty of interesting nooks & crannies. This game has 4 endings, the true ending being one of the most satisfying conclusions I've gotten to experience from a video game. I also believe there is some great speed running/ optimization potential to be had after the first full playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: A great little adventure game with some light combat thrown in. An interesting story with plenty of twists to discover and some simple puzzles to solve. A bit on the short and easy side but it makes up for it with an interesting story and compelling characters.I only really have two complaints. The first is that the combat feels out of place and I think the game could be improved by either removing all combat completely or by removing all weapons and making avoiding enemies a puzzle like everything else. My second complaint is the size and scope of the game. I usually prefer shorter games but in this case I think some additional complexity around the story and puzzles using the time loop mechanism could have improved the game greatly. It is a good 10 hour game but I think it could have been a much better 15 hour game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful! It somehow made me feel more human, and everyone on earth should play this. I have a profound sense of "novel hangover" after the intense emotions and connections I formed with the characters and the world - seeing all that end because I finished the game is almost depressing. I wish it had gone on forever. Thankfully, the canon ending is breathtaking and makes it all worth it. Buy it! Play it. Buy it for your friends! Talk about it. Hype it up! This game is so good it might just make you a better person.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Originally a Skyrim mod, so the developers had plenty of time to polish up the experience when translating it from mod to a full video game, and what a lovely and unique experience it turned out to be. The story is very well thought out, the choices are excellent with twists and turns around every corner, the puzzles are fun and there is a good balance of the game letting you figuring them out by yourself and guiding you so you don't get overly frustrated. If any of that sounds good to you then you should absolutely grab this gem!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, yes yes. This game is a masterpiece - I love how the time loop premise allows you to experiment with different paths and actions, and how the game respects your time by allowing you to catch NPCs up to speed with what you've already discussed. In addition, I really enjoyed the philosophical debates around morality that pop up around the core premise of the game: The Golden Rule.For such a contained/condensed experience, I was also pleasantly surprised with just how much there was to discover as well. Even though I completed the game within a few hours, I decided to go back and keep exploring (man, I missed a ton of stuff that first playthrough - including some NPCs I didn't even meet!)If you're interested in picking this game up, I recommend going in as blind as possible. Also the devs added an option in the settings to turn off "Hints" which is a godsend for players who like to really chew on the puzzles in the game before looking for help.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forgotten City
