_childDocuments_.review: is a side-scrolling, action-adventure game with a comic book style of gameplay and storytelling. An anti-government group, who call themselves the , aim to free the people from the shackles and restraint of government’s control, by uncovering the shocking truth of what they tried to hide from them. ✔️  The story is fine, not great. There is some good writing here and there, and the characters are okay, I guess.✔️  The story unfolds across the pages of a comic book, the tone and dark comic style are very impressive.✔️  The voice acting was believable and managed to keep me interested till the end.❌  Dumb events and moments that are beyond logic and left unanswered. Also, all the choices don’t really matter; they just extend the game a few scenes/extra dialogue and that’s all, no branching paths or anything.❌  The story ended with an unsatisfying cliffhanger,❌  It’s a cakewalk, no challenge or anything. You just headshot people or stealth kill them (at a VERY slow pace), do a few easy puzzles, kill a few drones, do boring QTEs and run from one place to another. You also have unlimited ammo, so you can just go guns blazing and ignore stealth.❌  Couldn’t hit an enemy, some had infinite health, couldn't aim my gun a few times and certain enemies disappeared after I respawned. It is understandable, since It’s a Unity-engine game. ❌  Just ambient songs that play in the background, nothing special.It took me about 3.5 hours to finish the game and the 2 free DLC. I don’t mind a game having very little gameplay (Telltale’s  is one of my favorite games), but the story was not great, the gameplay wasn’t really fun, the songs were bland and the ending left me unsatisfied. In my opinion, it’s not worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: LIBERATED

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine yourself living in a world totally digitised.A World where the Government controlls everything you do, for your own safety.A World controlled by modern Technology.A World …..with Resistance.Welcome to LIBERATED.LIBERATED is an extraordinary Game in many ways.At first we have the amazing Noir Graphic Style. A World covered in Black and White, dirty, rough but very detailed  and alive. The Game is presented like a  Comic Book. Picture after Picture, Page after Page you follow the exciting Story, which is represented from different views.  4 Comic Books + 2 more DLC`s are waiting to be played by you.From time to time the Comic goes into Action Scenes.That feels like diving into ANOTHER WORLD and i do not mean only this World, i mean the Classic Game. Like in ANOTHER WORLD or FLASHBACK you take control of a Character to lead him through Sidescrolling Action Szenes.  Here you have to fight against enemys, solve puzzles, master Quick Time Scenes  and find your way. Mostly armed with a weapon, you can also go stealth and overcome your Foes out of nowhere. Believe me, you will die many Times, because there are challenging Passages, but you will be returned to the last scene unlimited times and can go on. So, don`t worry. The Sounds and Voice Acting are great and are fitting very good into the Game. So what do i think about this game?I tell you.LIBERATED is really, really amazing.I love the hand drawn Noir World. That was Love at first sight.I also love how the whole game got liquid from scene to scene, from just Pictures into the Action Scenes. The Animations of the characters and the whole World, that makes it so alive. What i also like is the Story, because it is shown from different sides. In the first Comic Book you take control of a young man, hunted by the Government, getting help from the Resistance called LIBERATED. In the second Comic Book you take control of a police Captain who is hunting the Resistance.  Book after Book the Story will be revealed while the Storylines of the factions come together. There is no good and no bad, because the Game will show you each side to understand their behaviors. As said before, the Voice acting is really great and i also like the Music, that also fits very good in every scene of the Book.Well, this game is really special and will not hit everyones Taste. For me it feels like a game you can only hate or only love, nothing between.One thing i don`t like are the Quick Time Events, that sometimes are so fast, you can`t press the Button in Time and die instantly. Maybe i´m too old and slow for it, i dont know.Many Elements in this Game feels like hommages. V FOR VENDETTA, MATRIX, ANOTHER WORLD, FLASHBACK, THIS WORLD OF MINE and not to forget the NOIR Movies.Thanks to the Developer for this really unique Game, that i really enjoyed. It was an amazing experience for me.So, if you like the unique Graphicstyle and also like great Storytelling combined with good sidescrolling Action Scenes this is for you.  If you want to get it, the Price for what you get is really fair in my eyes. Enjoy.Thanks for Reading.
_childDocuments_.name: LIBERATED

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry I have to leave this review but this game just made me feel empty.For starters, the art style is amazing, I've never seen anything like it and the concept of a playable comic makes it even more intriguing. But it doesn't carry the game through its multiple problems.I purchased this game on a 70% off sale and I would say the $8.70 price tag was only barely worth it for the content I got. The characters you're given control of have OK ish depth *cough* except the police captain *cough* and the story they are a part of has the most nothing ending I've ever read.I will be going to the story a bit so spoilers ahead from here.The game's story starts so well, Barry's story and personality are top notch and the increased control he has with the player being able to choose how he responds to things makes him feel more real, his introduction into the Liberated and first mission is decently thrilling and his chemistry between the other members of the group is quite good. The first issue ends with a really difficult set of skill checks compared to the ones that occur in the rest of the game that actually determines whether or not Barry dies for real. No respawns, no retry's. If you kill him accidentally you have to restart the issue to save him, which is something I actually did because I liked his character, I can't say the same for everyone else.The other members of Liberated that you get to play as are decent but aren't really given enough screentime to fully flesh out their characters, Meg is the best out of all of them but doesn't really fit into any sort of archetype after the first issue. Now the police captain, he has a name, but I honestly don't remember it because he's that forgettable. Even though he's playable in two of the issues pretty much cover to cover and renowned as a hero in the second DLC. He barely talks and whenever he does he's just calling someone a piece of ♥♥♥♥ for shooting one person in a non lethal area, his morals are also unclear due to the fact that if you went to the effort to save Barry he just appears in the captains storyline and dies to the captains gun. There's no inner remorse or consideration for bringing him to jail, he just calls him a piece of ♥♥♥♥ and shoots him in the face. The reasons they state in game, like Barry killed his friend, is just not justifiable because there's barely anything in game that lets players believe that. The second DLC even admits he's just a random corrupt officer and doesn't deserve anything, but I guess he deserves two whole issues to flesh out his character over others, even then they barely take the chance to do it.Last negative point, the ending sucks, after the gruelling issues playing as the police captain the 4th issues seems to pick up the pace switching you between the characters of Liberated who all have separate jobs in a high stakes situation. Those stakes I talked about disappear real quick though, as the characters die without really doing anything for the story. The undercover cop gets called a piece of ♥♥♥♥ by the police captain, and dies. Meg's friend (forgot his name as well) dies off screen at the end, and in the end nothing is solved. The ending of Liberated is pretty much the exact same as the beginning, and if that's the message Atomic Wolf is trying to push, that revolution is bad. It's just a massive swing and miss. As that excuse just doesn't solve the myriad of other problems.The DLC's make no effort to fix the awful ending either, DLC #1 is just about screwing over an old man as a pointless side character, and DLC #2 reveals that the guy in the chair for Liberated has been out to betray them this whole time and just ends. There are some events with Meg that makes you think playing through this slog of a story was actually worth something, but nope, she just gets arrested and the story ends. For good this time.I don't recommend this game, especially when this current sale period ends. It's barely worth 9 bucks and 100% not worth 30. I really wish I could say something different for a game that has so much potential and looks so good at first glance.But a story driven game can't be carried by OK ish gameplay and amazing art because in the end, it's story driven. So it needs a good story.TLDR: Story is really lacking, which makes the game not as good as it could be. 4.5 out of 10 for me simply because of the unique artstyle and decent gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: is a stylish platformer with shooting, stealth mechanics and QTEs. + Engaging story told from different perspectives+ Very stylish look+ Replay ability provided with achievements and story decisions- Animations are poor and buggy- QTEs will catch you by surprise- Gameplay feels too repetitive on second playthrough The game is set in a dystopian world, the kind where big brother is watching you all the time. So, the story follows a group of freedom fighters called the Liberated, who got fed up with all the surveillance and want to overthrow the government. You play as Barry Edwards, a newly recruited hacker on the run from police. It’s kind of an overused setup, but it works. The game has a couple of interesting twists, that you probably won’t predict right away. And the fast pace of the story helps it feel engaging as well, even though it’s the same story you’ve seen multiple times. Even though you play as a hacker, you get to shoot a lot in this game. The stealth mechanics are basic, you can walk slowly and hide in the background to silently take out enemies. But it takes so much times and there are so many enemies, so you’d be better off just shooting them. Shooting isn’t particularly complicated either, you get your standard shooter weapons: pistol, sub-machine gun, shotgun and that’s it. Most of the fights happen in corridors, so it’s easy to just hold your aim on the same level as enemies’ heads. Between the fights there are a couple of simple puzzles and platforming sections thrown in. They are simple, but platforming controls feel a bit stiff, so you will most definitely fail a few tries before getting them right. Another part of the game, that feels very frustrating is QTE, they happen very spontaneously and it’s hard to recognize which button to press, because they don’t match to your character usual actions. For example, when shooting enemies in gameplay you press RT to shoot, but when the QTE starts, you character shoots when you press , ,  or  chosen at random. Due the game’s style (everything’s done in black and white), those QTE buttons use the same color, so it’s harder to recognize them if you’re not experienced with a controller. The variety is great, but different playstyles aren’t evenly spaced throughout the game and shooting part takes up most of the time. It might get boring towards the end, but the game has just the right length, so it doesn’t. Unless you try to get all the achievements, which is a bit boring, because you can’t start a level from any point, you can only replay it completely, there are 4 levels and each of them is around 40-60 minutes long.As mentioned earlier, the game’s visuals are completely black and white. During gameplay it looks like a noir movie. Between that it takes the form of an animated comic. It looks stylish and the animation makes it more appealing than reading the usual printed comic book and, by the way, they are fully voiced. During gameplay, though, the models look very low on polygons, especially when they are shown up close. Animation in gameplay segments looks poor too and has some bugs with transitions. On the audio side, everything seems ok, the music isn’t memorable, but it manages to create an immersive atmosphere. Voice acting is good, performances are believable enough and characters sound distinct from each other.Specs: Intel Core i5-7300HQ, 12GB RAM, NVIDIA GTX 1050 4GB.The game runs at steady 60 FPS at 1080p resolution. Didn’t notice any drops or crashes. Sometimes the character animation bugs out, like he instantly goes from running to standing still or a gun disconnects from the hand and flies around you. There wasn’t any other technical problems apart from that.If you’re looking for a short adventure with an engaging story and varied gameplay, then it’s the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Liberated is a combination neo-noir dystopian visual novel combined with 2D sidescroller sections that have action, stealth, and some puzzle elements. On a level of recommend and do not recommend, I'm going to recommend it with some caveats. This won't be for everyone, but there's some interesting themes, and if you're in the mood for a dark graphic novel then this may be for you. First to get out of the way, I really liked the music - lots of heavy synth, and industrial sound. The rest of the audio was hit and miss: voice acting (and yes it's all voice acted which is an achievement in itself) is mostly okay, some of it falls flat. The gunfire or fires are kind of lame ducks, but other effects are okay like rain for example. Something is off with the sound effects, but I can't put my finger on what it is. Visually it was good, not exceptional but it maintains its theme throughout. I think having some splashes of colour - a la Sin City or Schindler's List where they used a single colour to highlight story or emotional elements in certain scenes - could have been effective.Last is the actual action and controls. They were at times clumsy (specifically when jumping was involved), and sections that asked for stealth quickly felt unnecessary because there didn't appear to be any consequences. The QTEs require random keys (W, A, S, D) so be prepared. Gunplay was very simple which is fine, and the puzzle sections were actually nice. Overall these sections seemed to mainly serve a purpose of pushing the story forward, and providing the player with more interactivity and immersion in the story than clicking "next".  To that end they fulfilled their purpose.

_childDocuments_.review: How can it be that I never ever heard of this game until now? When I saw this in the steam store by luck, I immediately purchased it!Liberated is a 2D interactive side-scroller telling a very well written story about a over-surveillant state. The liberated are a group of resistants fighting against the government. The story is overall great and includes nice plot twist. I absolutely enjoyed it!The whole game is a playable comic and uses black & grey visuals, which are really well done, to fit the story. This unique art style is incredibly impressive and is well animated. You play in a comic bubble and click to the next one. The pages turn and you get the feeling to reading a comic that came to life. There should be more developers creating such innovative games.Concerning the gameplay: Apart from clicking through the story and enjoying the visuals, you will also walk around, shoot, do parkour, have quick-time-events and solve some short but nice puzzles. The game isn’t perfectly fluent, especially when jumping, but some really nice little details can be found in the gameplay design: your aim is straight, when you stand still. If you move, it slightly wobbles, and you lose precision. Also, walking backwards while aiming, makes you slower than walking forwards while aiming. Furthermore, headshots kill instantly, while it takes two or three shots on the body to kill non-armoured enemies (it will take 2 headshots and about 5-7 body shots for armoured enemies). These are some nice and realistic details, that I appreciated a lot.I must also recognize how well done the sound effects are. The sound design is brilliant, which is indeed extremely important for such a game.In addition to the main campaign, which consists of 4 comics and a total of 3 hours gameplay, there are 2 free DLCs. Each one takes about 15 minutes to beat. I am grateful for those short (but free) DLCs as they added good input to the main story.Overall an amazing game. This is definitely a hidden gem and I wish that Atomic Wolf would develop more games of this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start my review by saying I think there is a good concept here but it just isn't executed as well it could of been. I did really like the art style and it being told within panels of a comic book. Each chapter represents the next issue in the story. I did like the story they were telling which I won't spoil but I think if a it were tackled by another studio the result could of been better. The first issue I had with the game is the AI. It is pretty poor. I was able to choke out an enemy while another guy was easily within site of me but did not react to me at all. Enemies also won't react to any dead bodies that they may come across before you either step out of cover to sneak past or shoot at them. The second issue is there were  times enemies spawn behind me after I just cleared a room and moved onto the next. I survived those instances but it is certainly an odd design choice. There is also no way to remap the controls if you would like to. I didn't personally have an issue with them but still having that choice for those who may want to. The game is quite short at around 4 hours and the 2 free dlc's are short as well and add a bit more onto the end of the story that was told in the first 4 chapters.In conclusion Liberated is game with an interesting story but is let down by poor AI and if another studio tackles this same idea I think we'll get a better game as a result.

Tyrants will always use fear and the regular people love to be afraid. Pretty bleak but also true.The 2 FREE DLC "For the Homeland" and "Glory to the Heroes" are very short chapters 5 and 6.They too have something to say, criticizing the workers that gladly partake in an evil system thinking themselves heroes.Or questioning the convictions of the rebels, even founding members who were ride or die from the very start.Our societies are slowly moving towards such a Dystopian future.China, North Korea and all the other pathetic little dictatorships out there are already living like that.But what do regular people care, it is somewhere out there but not here. Our future children's problems, who cares.Dismiss everything, conform and enjoy the warm and comfortable chains of corrupt tyrants.Once the issue hits you personally or worse, your children, then you will cry out.But everyone is like you were, meaning nobody cares. _childDocuments_.review: I like to think Liberated was inspired by these old animated shorts such as The Sad Reality Of This World animation and IN-SHADOW - A Modern Odyssey - An animated Short Film that was popular back in my day, (man I'm old, not that old btw). This game is oozing with style from the use of detailed lighting effects and subtle hue shades of black and white, emphasising the grimness of a noir dystopian world told in comic panels with the addition of onomatopoeias. I love how everyone just looks so miserable and edgy, I thought this was a utopia and everyone wouldn't mind having all their activity recorded and having their life affected by their activity, but apparently not of course. These are the reason I'm recommending this game as I'm still mixed on this game mainly due to the gameplay and the objective being repetitive and a lot of the enemy's AI not thinking outside of the box and just being predictable even after they spotted you, taking away the immersion.The story is interesting, especially that little 'twist' before the halfway point which made the game more realistic, maybe too realistic as things just sort of end without a satisfying conclusion, but I suppose that's activism for you and things didn't get sorted as quickly as we like it to be. Still, I would only recommend this game, not for the gameplay in itself but for admiring the comic book art as well as the extra free DLC like soundtracks, and wallpapers, and other more, making it worth a little less than the full price if you're planning on purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: This review contains major spoilers. Be warned and proceed at your discretion.LIBERATED is one of the games that you're not meant to have fun with. It tells a dark story about dystopian future, where the government controls every aspect of human lives. Don't purchase or gain enough via wire? Don't post enough photos on social media? You're under suspicion. Maybe you post an online comment doubting the current government? You're asking to be arrested, discredited, pretty much erased.There's a group of people in that world. They call themselves The Liberated. Throughout the game they hunt for the proof that the government is corrupt, and ultimately, that it was behind the big terrorist attack on the school, which they needed to justify building this strict regime, where privacy is a crime.It starts like you'd expect such a story to start: after initial success The Liberated broadcast a message where the masked person announces their movement and urges people "to think for themselves". The story seems predefined by then, right? With every major step forward a new video is released, more and more people start to doubt the government, the riot arises...Except it's not the case. Unexpectedly, after the first issue the story shifts to the other side, and for the better part of the game you play as a villain: the police captain who's deeply convinced that all he and government do is the right thing, and The Liberated are no one but bunch of terrorists.It's quite a refreshing feeling: to play for someone you don't want to succeed.But ultimately, The Liberated manage to receive the crucial evidence they were looking for. It was the government who orchestrated that story-bending terrorist attack. They took lives of dozens of innocent children just so the people would give away their freedom willingly. It's all here in these files, just take a look.And guess what... Nobody gave a sНit. Some would claim it was a forgery; others said, "Oh well, another political bunch of crap, I best go watch a movie or something". Few of those who actually expressed doubt and were willing to even consider that the files were truth were harshly prosecuted and removed from the society. So the good guys failed. To no surprise, actually. Government has all the cards, it can and will do whatever it wants, for the rest of times.Visual part of the game leaves mixed feeling. The story part is told in comic strips, which look stylish and tell the story perfectly. The interactive part, well, it's way weaker. Character models look dull and out of the place, bodies ragdoll all around at the slightest touch. Though some inspiration is there as well: I like how the gunshots are accompanied by comic-styled BANGs, and the interiors are actually great and detailed. But it can't go unnoticed how clunky the gameplay is.But despite of all that, I can't help but recommend this game. It mirrors my fears over where my country is going nowadays; it's quite possible that The Liberated scenario can unfold here. And this game dares to show something rarely shown in this kind of stories: when it comes to the government atrocities, the good guys are not some shadow almighty warriors, but a sad bunch of outnumbered, outpowerered and outlawed renegades. Only miracle can help them win... And miracles are prohibited by law.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly surprised by how many positive reviews this game has. I got it for 75% off on the Steam Winter Sale and even then, I feel like I wasted four hours.Pros:-Very cool noire comic book art style.-Neat initial premise about a dystopian surveillance state and a group fighting back against it.-Music is pretty good.Cons:-Boring, predictable story that ultimately ends with nothing of note progressing or changing.-Weak writing.-Mediocre voice acting.-None of the characters are likable and you'll spend so little time getting to know them, you can't develop a connection anyway.-Mostly (admittedly very nice looking) cutscenes. What interactive segments there are involve basic platforming with frustrating, simplistic combat and the occasional puzzle thrown in.-No sense of pacing at all. You'll go from high intensity combat to having the brakes suddenly slammed on to solve a puzzle that takes way too long.-One of the two free DLC episodes is literally just cutscene.-Hitches and stutters, even on my beast of a PC. Unity Engine, common optimization issues.There was a really cool kernel of a game here but it feels like it either had to be rushed out or the developers just didn't know how to make it into something cohesive. If you're really intrigued by the style, I recommend getting it for $10 at the absolute most.

It touches some deeper subjects but never loses FUN from its sight.For me it's like an 80s action movie, and not done in an ironic way.

_childDocuments_.review: The beginning was very promising, but, after first several minutes the game quickly began going down.The gameplay is bad. The AI is dumb and just goes blindly towards you in 50% cases. Very quickly enemies start using bulletproof vests and helmets. What's the problem? The experienced veteran of the police (that's you) is too dumb to pick them up from the ground and use them. So you fight enemies who sometimes need whole clip to die, while you die from 3 hits. There are three weapons - pistol, SMG and shotgun. Pistol is the best cause it's the most accurate, SMG is weak and have high spread and shotgun... I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate shotgun in this game. It's slow and strong only against enemies without protection. And the worst part is - if enemy manage to hit you first, you get stun-locked and won't be able to shoot back. The sequence with shotgun in 3rd chapter was the most infuriating. Stealth is ♥♥♥♥. Plain and simple. You move VERY slowly and, because of the camera, usually get spotted even before you notice the enemy yourself. The camera is, by the way, garbage in shooting sequences too. Also, the game sometimes just spawns enemies behind you as well as before you. Sometimes immediately. Cool, right? But the main problem is - there's too much of it, the gameplay. Unfortunately, there is no "reading" mode, that would remove all those gameplay sequences, making the game a comic book. Although that probably wouldn't be such a good idea too, because...The story is bad. There will be SPOILERS next so be warned. The game creates nice beginning with supposed main hero. It starts giving us more information about him, the organisation he joined and his new comrades... Just to kill him. Yes, our MC - the character we begin the game with is not actualy main chararcter. Actually, there is no main character in the game. Barry? Dies either in the end of 1st act or in the end of the 3rd. Chief of police? Sure, we're playing as him most of the time - 2nd and 3rd acts, but he's closer to be an antagonist. He does not give any reason to fell sympathetic towards him and he constantly tries to stop our "freedom group". He could've realised the truth at the end of the game and become a good guy, but nope, he just dies. The woman (Meg, I think) and black guy?  Too litle information about them for me to actualy feel something towards them. So, I guess we don't have a protagonist. Cool, I guess?Ok, but what about the actual story? Eh, if I had to describe it in one word, I'd choose "s h i t t у". The world is ♥♥♥♥♥♥, the people are ♥♥♥♥♥♥, the events are ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Almost every character in the game is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and those who aren't just die. Barry dies, the brother of black dude (who was a teacher before school explosion) dies... And those are the only two "good" people in the game. Meg and her afro friend leave Barry to die at the end of the first act if you ♥♥♥♥ up the QTE, chief is a dumb moron who doesn't care about the corruption and surveillance (and who also protected the alcoholic police officer that raped the girl in the past), the father of Barry is the corrupt politician, etc. Hell, even people on background are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. At the end of the game, we manage to leak the truth about terrorist attack (that it was actualy made by government) and what do people of society do? The game specifically shows us that 90% of people laugh and don't believe this. And, in 5th act, that comes after story we see that nothing changed, the system still works and we even see how it destroys lives of people who dared to say something bad about it. The story "pays homage to tv shows like Black Mirror or Mr. Robot and 90’s cult movies such as Matrix and Fight Club" according to Steam page. In Fight Club there was a good ending, in Matrix there was a good ending. So what, they decided to follow Black Mirror where every episode is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥, depressive future in vacuum that lives by it's own rules, created to conveniently plug the holes in plot? Nice decision.At the end, I definitely can't recommend the game because, at the end of the day, what emotions do I have now, after finishing it in one take? Anger from ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gameplay mechanics and disappointment from the story that shows us the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ world where nothing changed.

_childDocuments_.review: 6h 2/10 for most of the game, 8/10 for the achievement "Barry" 1, there is chapter selection, but each chapter takes around 50 to 60 minutes to play through No There is a guide in Russian , if you struggle with an achievement it can help, but most achievements are easy to figure out 3 on Astats  No  Yes, but there is chapter selection. The achievement "Hacker" is one to focus on from the beginning, that one is hard to track where you did go wrong. I'll explain more below. No Yes, but the achievements for Issue 5 and Issue 6 you can get with the 2 free DLC (For the Homeland & Glory to the Heroes) No Yes, I would call Barry a RNG-achievement because of the absurd timer on the 4th QTE event No, you can play on the easiest difficulty No  This is an amazing 2D Shooter/Action game. The story is very immersive and after each chapter in the main game, I needed a little bit of breathing time before I could continue, it is so heavy but in a good way.  The world in this game is very dark and all the chapters in the main game end on a very intense cliff-hanger.   I had a lot of fun playing Liberated, even when it was so intense. I would rate it very high but 1 achievement is very annoying and so, for me, that knocks it down a little bit. The achievement; "Barry" asks you to complete the QTE at the end of chapter 1 without making any mistake, while the timer to push the correct button is insanely crazy. To make things worse is that it directly affects the game saves and if you don't want to use the trick to copy and paste your save file before you begin this event, you'll have to play chapter 1 from the beginning to have a new chance at it.  I may suck at this type of mini-game but I needed around 30 tries before I was able to get the achievement, you can imagine how worse it would be if I had to replay all of chapter 1 (which takes around 30 to 40 minutes to replay when skipping all the scenes as quickly as possible) all that time. The length of time the logos of the developer and publisher are on screen when starting the game already drove me a bit insane, when trying to get this last achievement. The cutscene after you finally do win this QTE mini-game, makes it even worse.  Another achievement that would be wise to keep an eye out for is the one in which you have to finish all 7 mini-games in the main story in under 90 seconds. Most of the time I took my time trying to understand it and get as close as possible to the solutions before resetting to the last save point to be able to do it in time. This doesn't work with the "mastermind" mini-game, which is more based on how quickly you find the right numbers.  Perhaps this sounds more like a rant, which isn't meant to come across that way. I did really enjoy Liberated a lot and didn't have any problems with the hacker achievements, it is just that I did go for that "Barry" achievement as my last achievement, which turned out to be so horrible to obtain. It tastes a bit sour to have that as an ending to what is essentially, such a great game otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok first the good stuff:- The story is interesting, I like dystopian-related stuff, and this one is a simple but good story. Characters all have their reasons to behave like they do- It was pretty easy to get used to the gameplay, shooting in the head is a damn good feel- The graphics are reaally cool, I love how this B&W design mixed with a XIII-like cartoon is done.- A lot of the story isn't directly told to the player, even if it is kind of obvious is left me with a feeling of open ending (I''m not sure if this is how english people say it?)- No bug at all, and BTW I was playing on Linux and no problem at all but a little bit of FPS loss sometimeThe bad stuff:- The game is very short and very easy, too easy (headshot-ed 90% of the ennemies). I died a few times, but never got near from stuck because of difficulty, this may not be a cons for who are reading this, as the game focuses on story and not difficulty, but I was looking for more- Hiding isn't useful at all, just like slow walking. I always run and shoot. Maybe that is why it took me only a few hours to finish the game?- Why do I feel that the shotgun and the rifle are less powerful than the handgun? With the latter, I could headshot everyone and even enemies that weren't yet on the screen, but shotgun felt bad to use, sadly :(Random stuff and SPOILER:- The ending is pretty cool, finishing the game with the people's reaction on Twitter was a funny way to say tell the end of the story- I would love more episodes talking about the world and character, like following the life of some of the people that are talking on Twitter and how they live with the CCSFinally, I think that Atomic Wolf has made a good job on this, I enjoyed playing this game and would definitely recommend it, but you can feel that this is one of their first game, everything could be "more/better" (characters more deeply defined, a story less common as a dystopian universe, etc...). Anyway, If you people at Atomic Wolf are going to do another game, I will surely buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun short story with an inventive style, I'd echo what other reviews say that the gameplay is perhaps a little basic, but the story was fun enough to make me compelled to finish it in one sitting.My main question of the gameplay is the stealth mechanic. As far as I can tell there's really no reason to waste your time hiding in a alcove to get a sneak attack when most enemies die with 1 or 2 well placed headshots, and as far as I can tell gunshots don't attract any significant attention from other enemies, so using a run and gun tactic is just way faster. Theres even a part of the game where it attempts to railroad you into using sneak attacks by giving a few enemies 5x Health, but since the player can shoot from further than the AI can, you can just back up and land a couple headshots, making stealth still not really required.Anyway, despite that the game is clearly well put together and is a fun couple hours, would definitely recommenced,  especially if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: From the first day I’ve seen some early footage I was hyped for this. Black & White aesthetics, cyberpunk / dystopian themes, surveillance and rebellion - that’s definitely my thing. Then I realized that it’s actually a comic book you can play so I was completely hooked-in. And luckily, the game fulfilled most of its promises.It is a comic book you can play although it resembles me more serious graphic novels from Alan Moore or Frank Miller. It has some wonderful art-style, a dark setting and a story which feels like it could really happen in a few years time or maybe even today. Especially after the covid thing resulting of more authoritarian policies in many countries, surveillance apps and stuff like this.I’ve written ‘most of its promises’ because I don’t quite like the sneaking parts. I expected something a bit deeper here but I guess you just shouldn’t expect another Metal Gear Solid 😉. That doesn’t change the fact the game is entertaining. The entire gameplay feels balanced, the puzzles even if not too diverse, are a good interlude and  those headshots are… well, headshots. Meaning: pure fun 🙂

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game but should be picked up only on sale. _childDocuments_.review: Liberated's story is mostly a comic book. The game is presented as though you're reading through four volumes of a graphic novel of the same name. As you pass over panel after panel, you'll occasionally pause on one that becomes a playable side-scrolling level, where you're generally tasked with shooting a lot of enemies, or hiding from them and breaking their necks as they pass by.Liberated attempts to be something else, and these moments are equally clumsy. Often, this comes in the form of puzzles that are little more than connecting wires or playing the board game Mastermind. There are quick-time event segments, none of which are particularly great.Its a simple straight forward 2D platformer, has a solid story and visually its great. The voice acting just makes this game better. Feel free to watch the extended game play, where I play 3 of the 6 issues.     Its not a bad game nor a good game, I would rate it 3 out of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: A slight yes. This game could have been much more than what is offered.On a personal level, I'm not fond of how the story is delivered. It stills would have been in better use for the gameplay. This is where the game "Framed" did brilliantly in contrast.Here, we have good ideas which are really limited. Recommending this is my way to support the work and the execution of this refreshing idea. _childDocuments_.review: I have very mixed feelings about this game. From the start I loved the game but slowly as I went through it that changed. The art and style of this game is fantastic, voice acting is great and the story at first is interesting. The actual moving around gameplay was fun throughout although very simple and in the end you really don't need stealth. But by the end I was left disappointed by the story and I wasn't quite sure of what side to be on, the liberated or the police. I think there should be more added to this story wise just to flesh out the world and individual story some more because it just felt too quick.The DLCs is where ♥♥♥♥ gets bad, with the main 4 "issues" it is an overall good experience, it just doesn't have a great ending (in my opinion). The DLCs seem less refined than the main gameplay, there is no "fail" screen so the game seemingly stops working but its actually just reloading the last checkpoint and again it feels too quick.I'll just go through pros and cons so I don't ramble on too much more.Pros:+ Great style throughout whole game+ Good voice acting even though sometimes there isn't enough or the right type of emotion put into it+ Interesting story even though it falls short+ Fun gunplay with very satisfying headshots+ Simple puzzles+ Good use of lightingCons:- No need for stealth for the most part- no proper fail screen for DLCs- Story falls short and doesn't end well- No indication of how many bullets are in your gun- Certain animations like walking cancel reload or at least seem too- I feel like there needs to be some kind of autoplay option for the comic storyFirst Look Review: Steam Curator Page:

_childDocuments_.review: You can play as a 60 year old Chief of Police who despite his old age, runs jumps and falls his way through an enemy base, the later chapters in this game and their "difficulty", will give you grey hairs too so, Look forward to that.Chapter/book/issue 4 of game is absolutely feels against the player in terms of level design.Sure, you get a shotgun. But enemies suddenly are placed in areas obstructed by the foreground, explodey drones (that do half your health and if more than 1 hits you it's insta death) are suddenly in abundance and flock together like kamikazes. Multiple elevators where you have to go up, but there are enemies on both sides of the shaft with a slanted platform protecting 2/3rds of their bodies, leaving your head exposed as it nonconsensually ascends the elevator, ripe for penetration of the lead variety. Forcing you to die over and over until you get that perfect shotgun shot.Did I Mention that there's some segments with enemies that can shoot you from off screen, because the camera pans only when you enter the door but they're on the other side of said door?Stealth game this is not, I know it doesn't say it on the "box" but early on the game teaches you to stealth but you can almost run and gun this entire game. If it wasn't for the artificial feeling slowdown.Also game makes Steam Deck sound like it's gonna take off while DMC 5, and No Mans Sky actually have a longer projected battery life than this game.. for some reason..TLDR:All this rant aside though, the style, vibe, aesthetic and environment of this game are awesome and it's a shame I can't say the same about its gameplay.Get it on sale if it still interests you. _childDocuments_.review: The date is March 12th 2024, in this near future cyberpunk dystopia where all aspects of always online social media is controlled by the government in the name of safety. Technology rules the roost in this world, social media, facial recognition, fake news, citizen credit systems. Everything is available to the government who use these measures to control the population. While most people submit their lives every day for scrutiny, there are some who fight the system, an insurgent group known as Liberated.  Starting a new game, you will have the choice of two game modes, Player and Reader. Player mode will give you more of a challenge along with the story, Reader will focus more on the story, challenges will be easier, aim assist is turned on and you’ll do more and take less damage. After deciding which mode to play the game will start, displaying the cover of Liberated Issue 01.  Issue 01 will then open and the story will start taking place in each of the comic style windows. Cameras using facial recognition scan the people waiting for the next train to pull into the station. One of these persons is expressing his French at realising that he better get his botty moving otherwise he’s going to miss the train. From here you will start to take control of the character and you will be instructed on which keys do what depending on whether you’re using keyboard and mouse or gamepad.  You make your way onto the train where you get scanned, Barry Edwards, Age 25, Male, Heterosexual, Bank Balance and No Activities on Social Media. After scanning a few others, you leave the train with the objective of exiting the Metro station. A message comes over the tannoy system about the St. Martha’s School Tragedy anniversary this Saturday. Those in attendance will receive complimentary citizen credits. It’s then that your phone receives an alert message, your citizen credit system account has been flagged for Social Non-Compliance. You have failed to attend your Scheduled Citizenship Training and now there’s a warranty out for you and you must return back to your place and wait for the authorities. You must now make your way home before the coppers do, so that you can scrub your computer's hard drive. As you make your way hope you’ll have to hide from enemies, where you can hide are indicated by a “Y” (gamepad) or “Q” (Keyboard). Don’t let the enemies see you go into hiding as they will come to you and start attacking you. However, if you hide and they walk past you, then you can come up behind and choke them. Later you will have a gun (Pistol, Uzi and Shotgun) to help you get by enemies. Sneaking rather than running will make less noise when you’re moving about so you may be able to sneak up on your enemy. Once you have a gun you can go for headshots, one shot on most enemies will drop them quicker than a lady of the night’s knickers on happy hour. As you make your way through the game you will come across puzzles in which you must complete so as you can proceed forward. The types of puzzles you’ll find are Cracking Codes, Fixing Circuits or Supplying Power to receivers. You will play as various characters throughout the game; this will give you the point of view for each character in the story.  The options in Settings consist of Brightness, Sound, Music and Dialogue Sliders, Resolution, Bubble Size, Language (English, Spanish, Polish, Russian, French, German, Chinese and Brazilian Portuguese) and Game Mode (Player and Reader). I have enjoyed playing Liberated, I think the living graphics looks fantastic, the story is good and the game isn’t hard to play. There is some language which some might offend some folks but the “French” isn’t too bad really. The game isn’t as long as I hoped for, four to five hours it took me taking my time playing the four comic issues of the game. There are a couple Downloadable Content which are free on Steam. I hope that some more content comes out at a later time. Positives + Looks fantastic + Good story + Two game modes + Has achievements Negatives - Couple times had me  - No cards currently Will you comply or will you become “Liberated” and free yourself and others from the constant monitoring of Big Brother. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Liberated is a great comic book. It has excellent art with distinctive, grim style and - more importantly - it tells captivating story, . What it takes to turn our modern world, where everything is connected through Google or social media, into some kind of cybertotalitarianism? And what is the society willing to do about it? Those are the questions Liberated is centered around.Unfortunately, in addition to comic book Liberated tries to be an action game at the same time. Well... it could be much worse, to put things gently. At least gameplay mechanics are diverse, including some nice puzzles. And before you get bored to death with running through monotonous grey levels and shooting in the head three types of enemies with non-existent AI, there usually comes another cutscene and things get interesting again.So if you're considering whether to buy Liberated or not, you must ask yourself: how much are you willing to forgive the game which can offer you ? I've forgiven it enough to finish this review with thumbs up after all :)

If you are a fan of comic books, you've got growing hunger of everything that's noir and cyberpunkish and you're an indie game lover - absolutely.Liberated is by no means a perfect game. It has it's fair share of problems - be it slightly naive narrative, bugs popping here and there, or kind of dragging stealth sections of the game. But it's also a fresh concept done bravely, if not daringly. It's a beautiful art style, a cool to explore concept of comic book coming to life, and a story with few bits that hit way too close to home. Try it out for yourself; I'm sure it will give you few hours of fun and will find a spot in your heart for quite a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Those that know the Black Mirror episode about the social credit score and read or watched V for Vendetta know what they’re in for. Liberated’s story is yet another dystopian story where the good guy resistance rises against a controlling and manipulative government. Drawing further comparison to V for Vendetta, the good guys all wear white masks. The game even has a plot device about a bombed school called St Martha’s, immediately reminiscent of the movie’s St Mary’s. While this is not a downright accusation of anything, the game sure wears its influences on its sleeve.Ironically enough, Liberated doesn’t even do a good job with the already cliché plot. The story is filled with constant time skips and plot holes which lead to an ultimately disappointing ending.  Adding to this, its characters are completely flat and uninteresting, basically cardboard cutouts. Each of them gets a few lines of dialogue that barely develop their personality or makes the player bond in any way with them. Liberated’s graphics are a beast of their own, divided in two completely different parts. On the one hand we have the comic sequences. These have great illustrations, though the character designs have the same problem they do in the story, they’re basically stereotypes. On the other hand we have the gameplay sections, made up by simple low poly 3D models. While the backgrounds and areas tend to be unique, the same can’t be said about the characters. While the playable ones are kind of unique, the enemies are identical to others of their type.  As a fun note, the devs didn’t deactivate the rigidbodies, the skeleton of a 3D model, for dead enemies. This means the player can strut through corpses making them ragdoll around, which looks quite goofy in a game that takes itself so seriously.The game’s sound design is alright, the soundtrack is mostly made up by “tense moment” tracks and the SFX are simple but work. A highlight is the voice acting though, which is included for all dialogues both in the comic and gameplay sections. While sometimes the delivery is not the best, the actors nonetheless do a good job.As mentioned in the introduction, the gameplay in Liberated is a mix between VN and side scrolling shooter. Sadly, it takes the worst of both worlds, leaving it as a very bland experience. The VN sections include a very low amount of choices which only add a pair of lines or a sequence that ultimately leads to the same point. Meanwhile, the pitfall for the shooter parts is its difficulty, the player is armed with unlimited ammunition and enemies die in two headshots at most. Despite the attempts at making stealth interesting, it is way easier to go in all guns blazing than to wait for a full guard cycle to stealth kill.Both types of gameplay also include a mechanic all players love, QTEs. These quick time events generally result in outright death on failure, though most are very simple and give the player loads of time. An outlier for these was mentioned with some spoilers during the Story section, so refer to that if interested.To add to the simplicity of the shooter parts, the player picks up a pair of new weapons on the different chapters. These substitute the default gun, without option to go back to it but do a much worse job. Both of these weapons are extremely inaccurate and have long reload times, which only make clutch sections a slog. As another fun note including another developer oversight, one of the achievements, supposedly getting the shotgun, is triggered when the player receives a machine gun.The game also includes some puzzle sections, though these are quite easy, further proven by the achievement for solving each of them in under 90 seconds. Most are based on line connection, with a few number guessing ones. It is a shame how few of these are included, seeing as they add some much needed variation.Liberated is a very bland game with a poorly handled story and simple gameplay. On a different kind of game it would be easy to excuse a simple story, but seeing as it’s a comic it becomes pretty hard to do so. The incredible short length, around 3 hours or so, does it no favors either. At a price point of 16,79€/$14,99 it is definitely not a worthy game, seeing how little it includes.

_childDocuments_.review: While the art style is fantastic, the gameplay itself is lackluster to the point I couldn't even force myself to play through it.  Some key points that turned me off and eventually convinced me to just refund it.From what I played, there's nothing really that makes it stand out.  Just another dystopian uprising story.For all the hype that the devs have been toting on their "excellent voiceovers", I found it rather flat and bland.  The lines sound forced and not well played to be honest.  There's no real emotion behind them, just "here's the line from the paper in front of me".  On top of that, if you happen to die a bit just after a VO (whether learning the next panel or ♥♥♥♥ controls), you get to listen to the line over and over and over and over and over and over and over again.The control scheme is minimal and not very in depth which is to be expected as it's a rather simplistic game overall.  I started playing on K+M but couldn't reliably aim since there is no cursor and the line is useless when you can't reliably see where you're pointing.  On top of that, I'm an ESDF player and there is no option to change the keybindings.  So I switched to controller (which also has no option to change keybinds, big shocker there) and it was better, but still a mess.  I'd aim to the right the first time, it'd aim straight right.  Next time I aim, it's aiming at their legs.  Checked the controller calibration and it's spot on, so it's not an issue with that.  More deaths are credited to "poor aim" than anything.For the most part, stealth is a waste of time.  There are too many moments where your carefully planned stealth kill from cover goes to ♥♥♥♥, whether it's from the guard deciding to check the spot your hiding to enemies magically appearing out of nowhere behind you (AFTER you've killed everyone behind you no less!).  You're better off just headshotting your way through the levels to save yourself time and effort.... if you can get the game to actually aim as discussed before.

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of playing a comic book is pretty awesome. Games are about interaction and this one makes it possible to interact with and be a part of another format of stories, and generally, stuff around us in the world instead of just witnessing their progress. The gameplay tho could be to some extent more challenging throughout the whole game and not just in some parts. Also, it probably offers enough hours of gameplay for its price. However, it could be to some extent less repetitive and present even more niches with hidden stuff. The stealth gameplay option is acceptable. The characters are complicated enough; however, I wish the devs raised the price and extended the lore and the characters with it.  The theme of the story is typical, but the mechanisms of the groups it displays have been illustrated well- not as flat, but with their complexities laid out. And the turn the "revolution" the game's promo discusses has been taken out of the fairytale atmosphere of such stories and viewed realistically.

_childDocuments_.review: Liberated is a bold and innovative experiment that merges the visual charm of comic books and graphic novels with the interactivity of video games. It boasts of a short yet fantastic story that talks about the world we live in – the perils of losing democracy and the pitfalls of absolute surveillance. _childDocuments_.review: Turned comments off, as people fail to grasp the complex concept of playing the Switch version well before the PC port was finished.Sorry about that.  -Liberated is in interactive Comic-book styled game where you control the pages and the story.The art style is simply perfect, black and white with only red added for blood - it's a very gritty Film Noire effect, I dig it.You start each comic out, learnign the sotry and playing the parts as you go along.Sometimes this involves some QTE events, usually you're doing the sidescrolling stealth/shooting thing. It feels a lot games such as Limbo, you're on a fixed plane of travel - you can interact with objects and hide for stealth, and jump ( also QTE events interspersed throughout ) The story is pretty interesting, Technology rules the people, right down to monitoring and regulating everythign they do, say, speak and feel.Dissention from this results in Legal action - and plenty of cover up scandals to hide the truth also occur.You start off controlling the son  of the ministry of defense - you get entangled with the group known as " the liberated " and your story begins to unfold, page by page.I enjoy the game so far, the graphical settings is obviously the highlight.The main difference between this and the Switch version, better resolution, better framerates, and fully voice-acted lines - nice touch from the devs.Performance is pretty good, it runs at 144 fps for me usually, but the farther you get on the panels in the pages, the more it drops - usually settling for a crisp 72, which isn't entirely awful.But, I ended up locking my pc to 60 fps, just so I didn't have to go through this dimishinng framerate. Pretty sure it's not a memory leak, it stayed at 60 virtually the entire time ( excpet for when itloads a new pages, which is acceptable ) the controls are fine, but with a mouse - you are not getting any favors in aiming your gun - no pointer I could see beyond the main menu and pause screen. But it's fine, as controller feels tight as responsive.Pretty sure your choices have actual consequences, as the very last page in Comic 1 ended in a way I didn't expect ( honestly thought they were going to make me redo the chapter ) but nope! Page closed, volume 2 is now open. I dig that if this is the case, perhaps it was a scripted event and I only slightly changed how it goes down by flubbing the final QTE.) If you're into the themes of this game ( dystopian future, rebellion to a totalitarian govt , freedom seeking ) then you're gonna enjoy the ride. The writing is done well, the visuals back it up - and the gameplay is solid to boot. You can stealth kill enemies, or just shoot em all. I ended up going for the gun route, as you can't see an area you can hide in until you're ON the area, so it makes setting up a stealth kill a bit of a pain.Solid 7/10 more if you're digging the visual style.Volume 1 gameplay here ↓

_childDocuments_.review: Liberated is a visually striking indie game that blends comic book aesthetics with platforming and puzzle elements.Pros:- Unique Art Style: The hand-drawn, comic book visuals create an immersive and distinctive atmosphere.- Engaging Narrative: The story tackles themes of surveillance and freedom, drawing players into a thought-provoking experience.- Innovative Gameplay Mechanics: The game effectively combines platforming with puzzle-solving, utilizing comic panels as interactive environments.Cons:- Short Playtime: The game can be completed in a few hours, which may leave some players wanting more content.- Pacing Issues: Certain sections may feel slow or drawn out, disrupting the overall flow of the gameplay.- Limited Replay Value: Once completed, the linear nature of the story and puzzles might not encourage multiple playthroughs.Overall, Liberated is a captivating experience with a strong visual style and narrative, though its brevity and pacing could be points of contention for some players.

_childDocuments_.review: Nicely animared graphic novel with simple sidescrolling action and some puzzle games in between.This game is to relax for half an hour and read/play through one of four short comic books. really cool american graphic style in the novel sections. the 3D graphics could have been more adaptive to that, but works all right and has its own style. Dubbing was quite ok, a bit lifeless at times.the controls are easy and the level design is as simple as it can get, there is not much variation of enemy types, its all pretty straight forward and easy to handle.would not say that this was a grand journey, but i enjoyed the time i had with it and would like to see more of the story evolving. until the end, the story stays pretty much in the cliche of a "V for Vendetta" in the digitalized world, seen from different characters perspectives. There are storys of betrayal and relations between characters, but the game fails to give more insight into them, to make them believeable or even understandable. I liked the fact that you actively play on both sides of the dilemma. The Story has potential, but didnt quite got out of its baby shoes within those 4 chapters. It stays a vague mix between V for Vendetta, Sin City and mission impossible.Nonetheless, the world is pictured detailed enough, its kinda fun to just read and play the passages in between. nothing too complex, and thats actually how it should be.All in all its totally worth the 3,50€ that it paid, but i would probably be a bit disappointed if i paid 17€

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very unique game playing experience . The comic book asthetetic brings me back to the 80’s-90’s when I would read comic books.  The game provides for two types of experiences 1) interactive play mode and 2) story only mode. In the interactive mode you get to play out some of the story whereas story mode is more like following along with a digital comic book. The entire game is voice acted which creates an immersive experience.If you are looking for an action packed platformer or shooter, then this probably isn’t the game for you. But if you are looking for an interactive experience with a good story to just relax and play, say on your Steam Deck, then I recommend this game.  In terms of gameplay, think games like Inside and Limbo. Liberated is not as deeply rooted in problem solving or puzzles as those two games are, but it has the same dark feel to it. Additionally it is that 2D style of game where your movements are restricted to left and right, jump and climb over things. It also has a twin stick shooter type of gun mechanic. Overall this has been a fun experience and I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, while the graphic novel structure is interesting, it isn't unique to this game alone. _childDocuments_.review: --Story spoilers ahead--Dropped this game and returned it. Amongst other things, the story is profoundly meh. The story starts in a very standard way (liberation front trying to uncover a government conspiracy), but no time is spent on developing the characters and their motivations. As a result, the liberation front ironically look like the bad guys for a moment. I got halfway through Issue 2 when I stopped playing. At that point I felt the story wasn't gonna be worth it, but I wanted to see the ending anyways and turned to walkthroughs. Reading the ending and DLC, I think the story was approached in a wrong way. Amongst stories about government coverups, this was one of the more straightforward ones - to me, it had nothing unique to offer in that aspect. But what was more interesting was the government workers' naivety about the government, seemingly unaware that the government would want to spy on citizens for purposes other than safety. With the ending and DLC content, I feel it would have been much more interesting if the game focused on the creation and maintenance of propaganda. Those were the more chilling parts for me personally. The premise of playing a comic book game is very cool, but it wasn't executed as well as I had anticipated. There was not a single moment where the player gets to admire the environment and see, for themselves, the effect of the mass surveillance. Instead, information about the world and the effects of the surveillance are dumped on you, which at some point feels like unreliable narration from both sides. The dialogue is not that compelling, and at times feels very corny/stereotypical. Of course the liberation front people will say stuff about freedom, but I know nothing about how they got to that point. That personal layer is missing in all characters.  I know the point this game is trying to make, but the execution was rather amateurish. The story would have been better in the hands of a better writing team. Gameplay was entertaining enough (the switch in quality is jarring at first), but not being interested in the story depleted my motivation to play.

Aiming at enemies, traversing the 2D corridors, jumpíng, the puzzles. Everything felt stiff, badly executed. I honestly didn't had fun going through the game. _childDocuments_.review: Exciting and fulfilling!When I finished Liberated, I felt that I experienced something meaningful. Not only because the conclusion is far from your Hollywood affair, but also because this was a legit new thing.I think what they did with the game-inside-a-comic concept deserves MUCH more praise than it gets. It's not just icing on the cake. They went full in and made the game PLAY like you READ. There are no 'levels', there are panels, short bursts of action that intertwines with dialogue etc.The 'game' part is a side-scroller, but not like a skill based platformer, but more like Shadow Complex (minus the Metroidvania part for obvious reasons). It was very solid, not groundbreaking but it perfectly served its purpose as the interactive part of the comic. The story was very cool and engaging, even though I wouldn't mind going deeper into the world.Bottom line, Liberated was refreshing to play. It reminded me of Deadlight, another rather short side-scroller that I love, stylish and engaging. It knows what it wants to be, and it does it perfectly.I see that many reviews scoff at the game not for what it is, but rather for what it isn't. Well, for me 'what is' is great already. I learned to appreciate ideas and effort instead of soulless craftsmanship.

_childDocuments_.review: More than the sum of its partsIf you deconstruct Liberated and examine each element, each will be serviceable, good. But together, they form a truly great whole.I'm a gamer that gets bored with any game that makes me do the same thing over and over again. I dislike most open worlds because they feel like checking marks off some list. Liberated managed to keep me engaged from start to finish, despite every element of it seeming simple at the first glance.Take action, for example. You go right and shoot, sometimes hide or swim. The story is reading panel after panel about an unveiling conspiracy. But these have been served in rather unique proportions, where you move from story to action set piece to story to set piece in a manner that stays fresh. Having different characters helps keep this freshness until the very end, even though mechanically, it doesn't change much.I'd say Liberated isn't about the graphics, the gameplay, the story etc. It's about how it all works together. The whole is much, much bigger than each of the parts, and this is the staple of clever design, if you ask me.

name: Shenmue III
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition The Digital Deluxe Edition includes the full game and DLC Season Pass (the complete post-launch DLC content and the “Burning Sandstorm” Advanced Technique Scroll) and the legendary Ryo’s Flight Jacket. DLC1 Story Quest Pack One day, Ryo encounters Zhang Shuqin - a subordinate of Zhu Yuanda, who had helped Ryo out in the past. Just as Ryo thinks that he's renewed an old friendship, he learns that Zhang has been kidnapped. But by whom - and why? DLC2 Big Merry Cruise A new cruise ship has arrived in the Niaowu harbor. Various types of entertainment can be enjoyed aboard the ship, as well as challenge missions which can only be played here. Also, new outfits for Ryo can be obtained by clearing mini-quests encountered onboard. DLC3 Battle Rally A battle race set in Bailu is about to begin! The three contestants engage in battle while racing their way through the course. Reach the finish line in first place to acquire awesome items. About the Game The brainchild of award-winning game director, Yu Suzuki, Shenmue is commonly known as one of the most ambitious game projects in history, which captured the imagination of players from around the world. Shenmue established the open-world format for action RPG games. An awe-inspiring world with an immersive story, featuring cinematic sequences, a realistic fighting system, and entertaining mini-games, Shenmue garnered acclaim and adoration all over the world. Play as Ryo Hazuki, an 18-year-old Japanese martial artist hellbent on avenging his father’s death. In this third installment of the epic Shenmue series, Ryo seeks to solve the mystery behind the Phoenix Mirror, an artifact sought after by his father’s killer. His journey takes him to an immersive representation of rural China, brimming with activity and surrounded by beautiful landscapes. Ryo’s adventure leads him to towns and mountain villages where he can further his training, try his hand at gambling, play arcade games, and work part-time jobs while investigating those who know truth behind the Phoenix Mirror.

_childDocuments_.review: What they did to PC backers by not giving them Steam keys for over a year, already makes this game worth the negative review, but lets talk about the game itself.The fact that it came out with a 66% discount should give you a tip about the quality of it.Shenmue III came out exactly one year ago for PC (Epic Store exclusive) and PS4, which is the version I bought and finished.The game was a colossal bomb commercially, it was destroyed by reviews, and even the most hardcore fans considered it a massive dissapointment.Now, does Shenmue III deserves all the trash it got? yes.This game looks like an early PS3 game, and it play like a PS1 game...no, not even a Dreamcast game.Its controls, pacing, voice acting, graphics, and level design are even more dated than those of the original two games (released 20 years ago), there is absolutely no excuse for a game which got $7M dollars from backers and a big chunk of money from both Sony and Deep Silver to look and play like this.I remember a year ago I kept playing because of the story...there is no story, literally. As Super Eyepatch Wolf said, "we waited 18 years for a Shenmue filler episode".There is literally no positive aspect I cant find in this game, and the story (or lack of) feels like a spit in the face.This game is an insult to fans, its own legacy, and Yu Suzuki's reputation, but at this point is pretty clear Yu Suzuki decided to sell any prestige he had left the moment he took the money from fans/Sony/Deep Silver and made what it feels like a budget fan game.The only reason why I bought this game (I sold my PS4 copy a long time ago) is because of the 66% discount, the fact that is dirty cheap in my country, and because I want this game to serve as a reminder, that no matter how much you liked something 20 freaking years ago, it comes a point in life when you have to let go.Shenmue III was a mistake.

_childDocuments_.review: A huge disappointmentI was a fan of the original Shenmue games all those years ago. I owned both games on DC and even bought an Xbox to play Shenmue 2 on it. Bought some merchandise and signed up to the ShenmueDojo, etc, etc. I enjoyed the, at the time, revolutionary world that Yu Suzuki and his team crafted - and while the game wasn't perfect, it was groundbreaking and memorable (in a good way). The story (of both games), well let's just say it wasn't one of the games' strong-points, but it was enjoyable if you didn't overthink it. Fast-forward nearly 2 decades, to this.Let me be clear, Shenmue 3 is not a terrible game in itself - it's simply mediocre. But it's a bewildering disappointment, it's crazy to think that in the near two decades since Shemue 2 was released on Xbox that this Shenmue 3 would be the result. A game delayed 3 times due to development issues and delayed on Steam due to the publishers having so little confidence in the game to sell in sufficient quantity (on PC) that they took a money-hat from Epic rather than sell it on the biggest PC gaming platform. The good (in no particular order): It's Shenmue 3 - the game does feel like a Shenmue game (strange that, right?) - but those games were released decades ago and the world has moved on since then.The world itself - though this has to be qualified, the environments are quality and the game, if you don't focus on the npcs, can look good - but the details, of Shenmue 1 & 2's worlds are missing. The audio - though plenty of the music is reused. Fishing - is not a bad addition to the mini-games. The nostalgia - and a few surprise returns. Forklifts - enough said. The bad (in no particular order):The story/plot - more on that below.The grind - much (maybe even most) of the time you spend playing Shenmue 3 will be grinding.The stamina system - whoever dreamt it up needs firing and banning from having any creative input in any game for all eternity - in a game that already moves at a snail's pace, Ryo even has to grind for food to even be able to run. The combat system - because who wants throws, right? Combat is a massive step back.The inconsistency of the art direction - from realistic cartoony muscle men to more realistic looking NPCs  - it's a stretch to believe that Shenmue 3 had an actual art director, and if they did, that person also needs banning.The lack of diversity in the mini-games - though tbf, this was presumably due to licensing issues.The ending - yes, I know I mentioned story/plot but the ending really is terrible.The wafer-thin characters - yes, Shenmue has never had the greatest character development - but wow, the new characters in Shenmue 3 are so instantly forgettable that you'll pine for characters like Yuan, Tom or Goro.  The cuts - of course, these were presumably beyond the control of YS Net, but in the last act the cut content becomes fairly obvious as you're tasked with a completely incongruous side-mission that makes little sense right before for the final battle.  The lack of set-pieces - yes there are QTEs but they are fewer and less memorable.The broken dialogue/terrible localisation - crap translations might have been hilarious and forgivable 20 years ago, they're less so now.So back to the story/plot. Wow, it's a mess. There's really no other way to describe it. It's as if Shenmue 3 was written by someone who had only a passing knowledge of Shenmue 1 & 2 - perhaps they'd read the synopsis on Wikipedia. As a result, lore is forgotten about, retconned, or simply ignored (even within the same game). If you exclude the final act, the game can be summed up as simply the quest to learn a move and its reverse form. No joke. This slog, which will entail you playing countless minigames with unskippable animations, is even thrown right back at you too. Because you know how enjoyable it is to have hours and hours of boring gridning rewarded by being slapped in the face metaphorically. I don't want to go into too much depth, because of spoilers and I risk boring myself, let alone anyone else. But the game's one big plot twist is meh (and that's kind), and Ryo - wow, this game just destroys him as a character. The writers must truly hate Ryo. Anything he might have learned about the Wude, and from the many people who helped him along the way in Shenmue 1 & 2, is just completely disregarded in one of the most unintentionally hilarious climaxes I can remember - you'll find yourself laughing AT Ryo, not empathising with him.EDIT: wow, check out those achievements - imagine the hours of graft that went into those 3 - yes THREE - icons used repeatedly for all 64 achievements. In a way, it's fitting, for Shenmue 3, that such little effort was put into the achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played shenmue before, you will hate it!The controls are not modern, you will get frustrated.You will often have to go home and go to sleep because some event you're about to take part in hits 3 pm and ryo will say "Guess i'll come back tomorrow".You will have to go on fetch quest after fetch quest.But if you've already played shenmue, and actually liked it, you will enjoy this game.After 15 hours, it starts feeling very familiar. Mechanics from previous games really kicks in after a while.People have much mkore to say this time, i used to run into the occasional "I'm too tired to talk now" but now, everyone has something interesting to say, and some of the dialog is pretty funny, not as funny as the "shut the hell up" guy, but funny.The combat is absolute trash, and i get that Yu wasn't able to stick his world leading Virtua fighter fighting engine into the game, like past titles have had. But this is inexcusable.When i got this game a few months ago, it looked super janky, but the team has been putting out tweaks and improvements, and its really starting to look more professional. Ryo's face has been fixed, but you still find faces that really don't fit into the game, and look pretty cartoonish.The arcade games... Well, you already know they aren't his past games.
