_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral "meh"  review rating option, as this game falls into that category for me.  I got Noita as I was looking for a magic-based game with plenty of replayability, while also influenced by all the positive reviews.  I fully understand the appeal.  Individual pixel physics, unique spell and wand combinations, and challenging, increasing difficulty per level that make it exciting!  However, after that initial noob hurdling of constant absurd deaths, I quickly realized this was not the replayability I was looking for.  Players start out with very little, and hope they don't die in level 1 or 2 while searching for decent spells, wands, and items.  As someone still learning, I rarely make it to the point where replayability truly kicks in.  Before that, it starts to feel like a painful grind.  The first levels are all very similar, first level spells seem to sample from a limited subset and the touted RNG, which can be fun, also causes frustrating deaths (getting shot while stuck on a few difficult to see pixels, shot at from off-screen, very unforgiving environment, etc).  Simply put, the player must get through an initial grind every run to get to the actual replayability part, i.e. I have to play through a required, increasingly not fun portion of the game each run for the potential of fun (which at my current skill can be fleeting).  My definition of a fun game is one that is fun throughout.  Even when the player is gradually getting better at it.  And this game is not quite that, hence: meh.  Not necessarily bad, but not really good either (at least to me).Other suggestions that may have improved my experience:-optional tutorial: For items/potions, environment, etc.,  I frustratingly had to learn through dozens of deaths, or discovering on the forums.  I understand how the "classical" players like this style of learning, but an optional tutorial would be very beneficial to newbies.-Additional game modes/settings/starting:  For those like me who'd prefer, especially starting out, an easier and more interesting start.  I imagine there's mods for what I'm talking about, but it feels like this should be in the base game to start with.-Legacy option/mode:  Even something simple like carrying over a previous spell/wand/buff, that would make each run feel more significant. Again, there's probably a mod and "classic" players wouldn't like it, but still.Meh, I'll probably still occasionally play Noita when bored, but I don't see my opinion changing with more play time.

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt one of the most entertaining games I've ever played.I already thought this game was ambitious by simply making every pixel interactable, yet it surprised me even more as I played. The map is always random, making a lot of room for replayability, I've been playing for hours and there always seem to be more and more stuff I hadn't encountered before.There are many, many, manyyy spells in the game, I'm always finding new ones after 24+ hours of gameplay, every spell is different/unique from the other, there are also variants from those. Not only there are spells, as there are potions, weird rocks, eggs (spawn allies), and even abilities, making combos a very interesting option for a run.There are many mechanics that look simple on the surface, yet very well designed, like the ability to eat, that can be used for consuming liquids of the ground, drinking blood to regain health (Vampirism ability), trying some odd mushroom you found, only to later realize you are now on drugs, etc. Kicking also helps in many situations where you are either stuck, or want to move an explosive barrel to a wooden wall.Overall, I'm absolutely loving this game, this is for sure a great recommendation from me, I doubt you'll dislike it.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, incredibly chaotic and thus frustrating if you aren't ready for the chaos.There's a very deep wand crafting system, and TONS and TONS of secrets to be found.This is like a roguelike, but if you just turn left and walk the other way, or find a way to scale the cliff in front of you, it's just a massive world of mystery to be explored.Certainly nothing like this has been made before.I heavily suggest looking up some beginners tips for this game.My play time says 74 hours as of this review, but chop that down to 50 hours due to AFK time - I just got my first win in, beat the final boss with one hp to spare...11/10 would blow myself up again.PS THE STREAMER MODE IS SO MUCH FUN GET A FEW FRIENDS TOGETHER ENABLE STREAMER MODE ITS A GOOD TIME

_childDocuments_.review: rng: the gameYou spawn in with 2 random wands that can either be super good, or so bad that you might as well reset on the spot.Then, you go down and there could either be no enemies and super good wands everywhere, or there could be no wands and so many enemies that you couldnt possible kill them all and survive.Did i mention that there's no health regen? Yeah, good luck getting past the first 2 levels if you dont get an upgrade like vampirism or a wand that has healing on it.And enemies will constantly set fire to everything around you, and spawn so much acid it fills the cave up and you cant go anywhere.You also only have so many spells on certain wands and can only refill them after completing a level, so good luck if you get stuck in some falling soil with no bomb spells.Speaking of spells, the game wants you to try and tinker with them, but doesn't really give any tips on how to not insta kill yourself if you get the explosion spells. Not to mention the fact that half of them damage you as well when you use them.Other than that awesome game, but I guess I just have a skill issue lmfao. Honestly if it weren't for the fact that there's no health regen, it would probably be one of my favorite games.Edit: right after making this review, the portal to the 3rd level was covered in lava and i died instantly trying to get to the next level. That is not a skill issue ;-;

_childDocuments_.review: The first time I played Noita I blinked and 2 hours had passed. This time it was 5 hours, I've reached the final level a couple of times now but I've still only scratched the surface. I've only discovered 25% of perks, 17% of spells and 40% of enemies. Very few times do you find a game that surprises you like Noita.Noita is a roguelike that can be quite unforgiving, however half the enjoyment of Noita comes from it's growing modding community. With workshop support you can play Noita how you want! Want a tough challenge? add more unique monsters and bosses! Want to play around building different wand combinations, sure! Hey, you can even change some of the roguelike elements and make the game a much more forgiving one and a great entry into roguelikes with the use of checkpoints.You enter the game as a small yet mighty pixel mage. You seem quite underwhelming at first, floating around and killing a few weak enemies. You stumble upon a new wand that doesn't have a great attack spell on it but has a few modifiers, now you can save this till you get to the holy mountain at the end of each level and move the modifiers onto your own wand. This wand system is core to what makes Noita special, you practically craft your own attacks, will you be a water mage that can swim really quickly but also flood an entire level? Maybe you want to rain down hellfire as a pyromancer? All is possible in Noita.Play it now and you definitely will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun physics based game. I know, yeah, that's it's main appeal. Still feel like it needs saying.  If you've played around in Powder Toy at any point in your life, and enjoyed it - this will absolutely feel like your type of game.  It's a rougelike (Rougelite maybe? Unsure if there's perma-upgrades) about a wizard.  Now, I would've said "about a wizard trying to reach the bottom of the cave\mines\whatever" but as it turns out - there's WAY more things going on than just the bottom of the cave.  The game has ridiculously cool details and I keep finding out new things in my consequent playthroughs.  I'll go and try and sell it to you via some events that happened in my sessions.There's an explosion spell. If you put it right on your want, it'll explode in your face and do some damage to you.  But if you combine it with a spell that makes long-distance spell shots, you can have a large explosion which  explode in your face.  Found a homing projectile modifier? Tack it onto the wand with the long-distance explosion.  Whoops, you've accidentally created heat seeking mini-nukes.  You inevitably kill yourself because a barrel of oil flew into your face just as you were trigger happy with nukes.You restart.You find a wand which has a triple-shot. Three triple shots. And a triple shot modifier.  You've accidentally found a trench gun.  The next store over you find acid trail projectile modifiers, so you tack those on your trench gun and completely violate the wizard world Geneva convention equivalent. At this point it's a suggestion and not a convention. You've become a lawless god, above anyone else, you shoot a shotgun which ruins not just your enemies but the land around you. You go insane, you start modifying the landscape, you ruin the poor randomly generated scenes.  Up until you anger the gods. What happened there? What does that mean? The game doesn't explain in text, but you're sure to find out soon.It's just another secret in the game, completely activated by your own hubris, which leads to your demise.It keeps you exploring, it keeps you testing, using new items\spells\perks, just combinations in general.If there's one thing I will fault the game for, and  - it's the spell system.  Not as a whole. It'd be really weird if one of the main aspects of the game doesn't work.  No, just a couple of quality of life features are necessary I feel. At some point you'll have 4 wands and a bunch of spells.You can't quickly remove or add spells, but rather you have to slowly hold and drag them across your entire screen.  The game would get such a QoL buff in my eyes if they added some form of shift clicking, à la Minecraft.It is SO close to perfection in my eyes and I'm barely scratching the surface of it with my measly 12+ hours.  Check it out. It's fun.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR An esoteric physics simulator beautifully integrated with an "anything goes" weapon programming module. With mod support.Noita is an excellent time sink that, despite losing everything on death, will keep you returning to constantly try something new. You are a faceless wizard or witch, seeking to attain to the highest practice of alchemical knowledge with nothing but your own curiosity as the limiting factor. There is basically no tutorial and NOTHING is spoon fed to you, but the world is completely open before you to explore every place in it, limited only by your skill. There is no explicit story in Noita. There is no dialogue. There are no quests. There is just you and the world. If anything you are learning how the devs operate their world and what they have hidden for the curious adventurer to discover. Much like an alchemist who puts together pieces of the world to meditate on the meaning revealed through their interaction. The "plot" and environment are full of connections to hermeticism and alchemy, with hidden knowledge being one of the key mechanics that keeps the Noita community so engaged .The physics and materials environment is reminiscent of The Powder Game remixed with esoteric alchemical recipes. Even at this time of writing there are still known mysteries within the game that have yet to be solved. However, there is enough challenge and content with the main quest line that you could spend hundreds of hours on it while being completely ignorant of the myriads of side challenges within the world. Aside from the environment, the spell crafting mechanic is masterfully done. Anybody familiar with the basic concepts of programming should be able to seamlessly transition that understanding into making powerful wands with the right ingredients. There are some hidden spell mechanics that I wish the devs included in the stats, but most community tutorials will tell you what those are.That being said there are plenty of tutorials and 'spoilers' online. I use spoilers loosely because it's not like a normal spoiler that will ruin a plot or story. Personally, I've already looked up most of the spoilers and still want to keep playing the game. But for some, this is not like a typical game, even typical rogue-lites, and they won't enjoy it. It's refreshing to know that every player, from the most to least experienced all start their runs with exactly the same opportunity. That being said, the mod support is very well integrated and online tools exist to help the player with their individual seed. I use some mods to help learn the mechanics with a little more forgiveness, but look forward to completing a run unmodified. All in all, for $20 you get a stellar game, for $10 it's a stellar steal.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: I accidentally got turned into a giant worm and burrowed rapidly through snow until I then got turned into a beholder and got sniped by a lightning skeleton. I died.I haven't been this entertained by a roguelite in quite some time. It's a fun time.To be honest, I think this straight up might be one of the best roguelites ever made. I'm talking up there with the greats like Gungeon, Isaac, FTL, Dead Cells etc.For starters, the pixel art is obviously great. The custom engine they made for Noita is stellar. The whole "every pixel is simulated" is really cool and is executed really well. Especially when it comes to things like fire. And everything having physics in a game like this is really unique.The moment-to-moment combat is super satisfying and the constant danger you're in means playing recklessly can quickly result in your demise. The wands and all the different spells associated with them are cool and help keep combat fresh. The customization you can do with the spells can help you succeed at a higher level as well.The enemy variety, biome variety, and spell variety is already pretty darn good considering this just launched in early access.And of course, the difficulty of this game is very much apparent. There's a lot more floors than I originally expected, and they get immensely dangerous. It's hard and you will perish a lot, sometimes in hilarious ways. It's a stellar game already and honestly already feels like it could be complete. So the fact that there's more to be added is very cool. Also, as a roguelite I like the fact that there's no "progression system" to make runs stronger like so many other roguelites have... I prefer it that way. Though maybe some sort of unlock system would be nice.Again, it's good. If you like roguelites at all, I highly recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game I spend my time on from time to time, kind of puts me off how much your start depends on RNG with wands (of course it can be fixed by mods). Something I'd like fixed is basically a small tutorial so understanding things like mana, spells etc doesn't have to come from external sources. Small issues, but generally a great game to play. Excellent sounds, visuals are something unique, and amazing in their own right. Definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: The roguelite gameplay directly conflicts with this game's origins, a literal sandbox game. I don't understand the dev's decision to make it a roguelite at all, as this type of game would benefit immensely from a large persistent world to explore, and the ability to freely experiment without consequence. Whenever you die, which will happen a lot, you will spend about 10 minutes navigating the first cave with a 2-shot laser that can barely interact with the environment at all. You have to pray to RNGesus to get a decent wand, and focus all your attention on scraping together a little bit of gold so you can buy a wand at the next stage. The novelty wears off fast and I found myself immediately seeking mods to make the game tolerable.Persistence is a great mod that adds the meta-progression that this game desperately needs.

_childDocuments_.review: Very glad I pulled the trigger on this game! It’s been in my wishlist for a few sales now and I finally got it simply because the pixel art etc was so beautiful. _childDocuments_.review: I'd had no internet for a few months, and when I get it back the first game that catches my attention on the steam store is Noita. the ability to Destroy Everything, and the way that fluids moved in the images and gifs and videos on the page made me want this game. the next day a friend in a discord server asks if anyone wants a game for about $20. I end up getting this game gifted to me. let me tell you something: There has never been a game this difficult, and this unfair, that I found fun. That doesn't mean this game isn't difficult and unfair. It can be downright cruel. The coolest spells in this game so far that i've had the chance to use are a lightning bolt wand. Very nice. good kickback, lethal to almost anything I got to at that point, arcs a little messing with accuracy but still nice. It killed me. if your spell can kill other things with ease, it can kill you with ease too. Chainsaw: like 8 different chainsaw spells with some fire trail spells and stuff, good for digging through ice/snow, probably good for digging through most other things, and DEFINITELY good for digging through enemies! Accidentally hit an explosive barrel and got left with 6 health. I died just before I could get to the portalBlack holes. shoot a black hole that eats through stuff, but you only get 3. I don't know if it does damage but even the if it doesn't the sound it makes as it digs through stuff makes up for itAnd finally the EXPLOSIONS in this game... the sound reminds of some of the cooler explosions from Mythbusters, and you feel it in your chest, the reverb and it just fills me with joy. Not a single game, with amazing 3d graphics or hundreds of dudes developing it have made an explosion that felt so real! This is a 2d game! Tips for people who get this game: things like oil field tend to make the thing on top of you, and with exception of the crummiest spells everything is gonna be bigger than you expect when you first get to it. Experimentation WILL be lethal, so if you get real far and find a cool wand with spells you've never got before: BE CAREFUL! it might be a game changer that lets you breeze on through! It might cause ungodly lag and set you and the entire level on fire! either way it'll look bloody cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: not very well balanced, basically everything is strong except you and it is very hard to change that. This makes it feel very unfair and frustrating. This game is just trying to be hard by making enemies overpowered, you take damage from everything and there are basically no opportunites to heal. It breaks the experience for me.+ you actually have to think about your actions+ high replayability because of random maps and many wand/spell combinations+ per pixel physics!- rpg mechanics lacking (not that many items, equipments, few ways to heal)- level based (imo a con, I would like it to be open world)- badly balanced, little healing options, you deal little damage but every little thing hurts a lot- most potions are completely useless and useful ones are extremely rare. _childDocuments_.review: Hard, each run you learn something new.- If you add water to slime it turns the slime to water.- Edit your wands- Explore the levels, power up your wands early- Know when to run away- Don't get cornered in the ice cave by 5 guys with jet packs.- DON'T THROW YOUR VIALS. You can also empty them between levels and fill with water- DON'T USE A WAND WITH A NEW ABILITY WHEN YOU ARE LOW ON HEALTH. IT'LL USUALLY KILL YOU.

You`ll encounter many obstacles, which you must overcome (mainly by shooting in their general direction) with your fully customisable magic wands. It strikes the perfect balance between total rage and god runs, but you still have to be good to get a god run. Or, at least know what you're doing. I wouldn't recommend it to anyone with a short attention span or a short temper, but if you think you can handle it, Noita is a great game.Gaming is intense..But Noita is SERIOUSLY intense.*goes super saiyan for literally no reason*

Playing Terraria in high school was a gateway drug for the black tar of Noita; boiled until it's reduced from a wine to a glaze, sickly sweet with emergent simulation interactions and an unflinching demand for player math.I am terrifically bad at it.But! _childDocuments_.review: There is a lot more content than most people realize. So much so that almost nobody who plays this game will find any of what this game has to offer. Get this game if you know what you're getting into. It's unlikely you'll be getting far in 98% of the runs, but that's not what makes the game fun. What DOES make the game fun is finding all the secrets, completing the list of stuff to find, customizing wands and exploring. I don't play this game expecting to win, and by doing so, you have a lot more fun. Sure, sometimes there are deaths that feel unfair, but that's customary of all roguelikes. Fighting many enemies acts more iike a puzzle, figuring out the right spells and ways to handle it. And while you won't get the spells you need every time, you don't have to for a lot of the part if you learn the enemy's movement and how they act. It's a complicated game, but if you're willing to put in the time to enjoy it, it's worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: Despite not playing that long of the game, I got to say it's one of the most fun yet rage inducing games I've played in a long time. If you enjoy a game that requires you to constantly learn, evolve your game style and also have hidden treasures to find then this is the game for you. Please note, you will die... A LOT!!! Also something to keep in note about the game play that I've noticed is that there is a small amount of luck required during your runs. Some runs you may have better or earlier access to better equipment or potions while others will force you to grind and explore more to expand your arsenal. All in all great game and defs recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: Came for a physics-based magic roguelikeStayed for the insane rabbit hole that is every other interaction in this game.Seriously, if you see a machine, or weird table, or weird writing on a wall somewhere,  you VERY likely can cast a spell, bring an object, spray a potion onto it to make *something* weird happen. Playing this game just to win a run is barely scratching the surface.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: Experience the magic and mystery of Noita. Discover interesting new ways of accidentally killing yourself. Figure out which perks and spells exist purely to disappoint you. Go new places, get eviscerated by new things. Become an unstoppable killing machine immune to most forms of damage, then step in two pixels of glitched acid to die instantly. Have fun. Stop having fun. Become frustrated. Become hollow and bitter. Start having fun again. 9/10 game, I hate it and the next one hundred hours I'm going to spend playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, 36 hours in, and i have to say I love it. Absolutely fantastic. This beautiful game combines chemistry, physics, and Finnish lore in a way that is surprisingly realistic and immersive for a 2d platform. _childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: (1) Visually appealing gameCons: (1) Lack of difficulty scaling (easy/beginner) mode, (2) No ability to save a game/progress. (3) You die easily/often and then have to start over from the beginning. (4) The game boasts about giving you the ability to create your own spells, but in reality, the majority of the spells are hard to use and inflict more damage on the caster, rather than the target. (5) Instead of supplying you with new/useful spells, the game provides vast amounts of duplicates of the worthless spells. (6) too many broken or unusable wands. (7) perks that are basically useless/irrelevant. (8) Little to no guidance/information within the game.CONCLUSION: Play it for free or don't play it at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: The environment simulation is just as good as it looks in the trailers. The roguelike aspect is also very well designed, after each stage or level you get healed and are allowed to purchase new wands/spells as well as swap/combine the spells your current wands use. There's no healing in the levels themselves so you are tempted to reach the shop as fast as possible, but the prices for new spells increase quickly so there's also an incentive to explore the level for longer. Without purchasing or finding powerful spells survival becomes impossible anyway as enemies become more dangerous. Also, the enemies and perks are really creative. Almost all of them interact with the simulated environment in some way (creating puddles of toxic slime, blowing holes in the walls etc). There's lots of cool ways all these things can interact! If you like roguelikes that allow you to experiment with weird abilities and strategies each time you should definitely check this game out. The closest comparison I could make would be Unexplored, but this game is much prettier.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: You get wands, they have spells slots, you can transfer spells between wands at will: create your super wand. Also, become a blood sucker vampire and grow spider legs!Note that this is a rogue-like game: as it happen, combining "gun-powder trail" and "explode at impact" spells on the same wand lead to serious back fire. You have been warned!
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: The detail put into every pixel of this game is impressive. You're given more power than you can handle in the form of highly destructive spells, and set loose on a volatile world. More often than not you will die consumed by the very chain reaction you set off, but it never makes the chaos any less delightful It reminds me of one of those old browser explosive powder games with a little wizard running around inside killing monsters, and I would recommend it to everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: The process of acquiring new wands and spells and refining them into more powerful weapons is incredibly satisfying, even as your experimentation with them gets you repeatedly killed in embarrassingly preventable fashion. No matter how frustrating any previous death may have been you'll find yourself diving right back in to craft another glorious spell combination on the perfect wand.   The enemies you utilize your wands against are numerous, dangerous, and varying but manageable with smart tactics or a little forethought. Even after fighting the same few enemies for hours, they do not feel repetitive or annoying beyond the threats they pose. Each enemy type feels unique and interesting, with new creatures appearing here and there to intrigue. More than fifteen hours in and apparently I've only discovered about 27% of all the different kinds of enemies.   The dungeon feels alive, as though it exists beyond your immediate presence. It's not unusual to stumble across enemies killing one another or accidentally burning half the dungeon down. Explosions can be heard in the distance and you may never know where or why. Danger is constant and certainly where and when you least expect it. Maybe some dynamite-wielding nutjob just blew up some vat above you in a futile attempted to kill another enemy, and flooded you with toxic sludge. Only the temple is (usually) safe.   The most dangerous thing you'll face? Your own personal OSHA violations. I have killed myself  - Touching the electric sparks wand to the water I'm standing in (to see what'd happen)  - Attempting to use a black hole spell on a wand (don't cast it next to yourself)  - Standing in front of my own mining laser (spells effects do not always move with you)  - Underestimating the death power of lava or acid (just another fluid, right?)   There are so many cool interactions, with so much variety, sneaky secrets, and everything about this game encourages you to find and enjoy them. I cannot recommend this game enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: This game has TONS of replayability. Not only is it a normal roguelike, you can also explore the surface a bit more if you're clever enough to find out how. This game has lots of hidden lore, making for an interesting story to this world you play in. The developers are supporting modding which will allow this game to become better. This is my new favorite game, I hope you enjoy it too!
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: Fun to play occasionally even when limited time. When I know i have 10-30 min time to play, I always start this game. At first it seems frustrating when you die all the time but when you get used to it and just have fun trying different setups it gets more enjoyable and actual good fun! Good way to relax between competitive games too (like CS:GO)!
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: Tentative recommend after all these hours. This game has a lot of interesting stuff going on but I feel like there's a few things holding it back. 1. The alchemy system is very complex, but the game never teaches you about any of it, and you have no real way to interact with it beyond pouring stuff on the ground like a dope. Why can't I pour from one flask into the other? 2. I'm a big roguelike fan and I would say this is not a great roguelike. Pro-tip: difficulty in a roguelike shouldn't come from the enemies having perfect tracking on every shot and no cooldown on their melee attacks. There should be information about enemies that can help you against them, but Noita doesn't do that. Instead it says "hurr just try to dodge their projectiles what's the problem bro it's just five hiisi all spamming explosive bolts at you" (again, with perfect aim). 3. For a game with such an expansive world it sure as hell hates letting you interact with any of it! The whole world is gated behind finding a teleport wand and a digging wand and if you don't find those you're basically ♥♥♥♥♥♥ out of luck. 4. For all the cool spell combinations there are, the game sure as hell doesn't tutorialise any of that system. 5. Way too much hidden instakill ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in some levels. "Here's an insta-kill explosive prop, it's the same colour as everything else in this level, good luuuuck" like okay thanks. The game itself is fun but there's a lot of room for improvement. Actually teaching the player about the spell and alchemy system instead of just expecting them to Google it would be cool. Enemies on the first floor can just erase half your health with two attacks which is ROUGH for a freaking roguelike where you have to start all the way over every time. And it seems like there's kind of some cool story and lore and hidden stuff going on when you first start playing but it quickly turns out all of it is just meant for you to Google. Lame. So yeah. I dunno. I guess I recommend it, kinda. We need a Noita 2.0 with a better alchemy system and less "hurr more difficult more good" mentality. ♥♥♥♥ hiisi and ♥♥♥♥ urkos. That's all.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible.On the surface its a solid 2D roguelike physics sandbox. But then there's a moment where certain mechanics click, you start to discover just how deep and extensive certain mechanics are, learn the Art and truly begin to see just how  far and extensive the overall scale of the game is. It truly is a unique piece of game design and I am very excited to see what potential this game can really do and how far the devs take it.You'll also die. A LOT.Play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate rougelikes, but for some reason this game is super addicting and a ton of fun. It's probably because the physics adds a whole new dimension to gameplay, as you don't just have to worry about the RNG of the mobs, wands/spells, and map layout, but also all of the chemical reactions.I also appreciate being able to save mid run. Too many rougelikes make you finish a run, which can add to the stress and ruin the experience. Being able to play in short bursts allows you to take your time with each run, but also not feel as disappointed when you die, because it doesn't feel like you dedicated hours of your life in one sitting just to die from something dumb.The RNG in this game is rough, though. Most runs are honestly just not possible. It's not easy to beat the game when you get essentially 0 spells, crappy base wands, and the shop is full of garbage. That alone kinda sucks, and becomes extra upsetting when you finally get decent RNG to make winning possible, and then you die, knowing you may not get another chance for a while.Overall great game. If you  like roguelikes, you may like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite challenging permadeath 2d game with beautiful physics with gas, smoke & fire, also explosives to destroy through objects of certain densities. You start up on a mountain cavern entrance, approaching a shaft. As you advance through the first level fighting mobs & picking up different wands, finding what one seems best for you. Each level fully progressed you enter a shop where you can re stock health & buy upgrades. Each level you complete into the abyss gets harder. Enemies get more aggressive. Learn your playstyle & focus on a good build. Otherwise great little game. Hope this sums it up :)

_childDocuments_.review: It's...Strange, with a capital 'S'. It's a very hard game and utterly unfair and arbitrary at times, sometimes hilariously so. You're an alchemist or aspiring to be from what I can tell. The environment is a fully destructible playground, sometimes a peaceful area that you deliberately destroy, other times a chaotic hellscape constantly exploding into whiskey, lava, steam, water, toxic sludge, gold, mana, polymorphine and literally a dozen or two other liquids. I once stumbled onto a lab filled with potions, except enemies were there and they were killing each other and then trying to kill me. I threw a bomb into the lab, this detonated a dozen potions. It just sprayed every liquid everywhere which sloshed straight down through the level. This had unpredictable results on creatures and the environment below.You get wands, they are like guns except you can kill yourself by pointing it at enemies. Going in blind and ignorant you'll probably have a good run, then make a spell that fires eggs that spawn explosive crates that blow up and catch you in the radius. Some basic varieties I've encountered; machine gun wands, mining lasers, bombs, rain cloud generators. Some more advanced types I've made; fan shape shotgun blasts filled with exploding gunpowder, a sniper round that fires a cutting laser on impact, a rain cloud of self lighting oil that rains hellfire below.The enemies can be tough, sometimes it's better to just blow them up with excessive explosives. Other times just pour water on them. Most of the time going a few floors down it's more about watching how you're going to get blown up or shot this time. If you can laugh the quite literally 300th time you've died barely making progress watching your corpse bounce around spurting blood everywhere, it might be the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start: Noita is an absolute, but very rough gem of a game. The only reason it warrants a review this long is for I'm really taken with it. For a price of less than 20USD you should pick it up without hesitation.Personally I hate describing things through its potential - but in case of Noita it is unavoidable. The most prominent selling point; namely the fully destructible terrain with realistically simulated interactions between materials, in conjunction with the freedom of crafting your own spells allows for unparalleled freedom. This is where Noita shines: not only is it near limitless in player freedom, it also achieves this through enticingly imposing means. Noita is without a doubt, especially on first sight, a contender for the title "modern day classic" - and one of the most noteworthy indie games in a long time.The amount of content that the game sports, be it hostiles, spells wands or hidden mechanics and secrets, is gigantic. Yet the game willingly limits you to a very small cut of it all unless you are willing to withstand severe hardship(not nearly as melodramatic as it sounds - more on that later). The graphics fall somewhere in the spectrum of "OK" - which is easily forgiven considering the technical limitations that come with a fully physically simulated world. The gameplay is very basic. Even though most individual enemies do have a particular weakness, or do require some unique approach - pretty much all of them are disposed of easily if you find a sufficiently powerful combination of spells. The real threat comes from facing larger groups of enemies or environmental hazards. Describing the difficult of Noita is on its own a challenge; but if you wish to express it in the odds of you "completing"(the ultimate goal) a run the word would be "extreme". This brings us to Noita's darker side. The game is draconically unforgiving. Some of the difficulty stems from unintended interaction, but most of it comes from either deliberate design choices or consequences of the latter. You will find yourself dying to a scenario that seemed completely unavoidable time after time again. Noita will flail you for every single minuscule misstep you make. RNG will ruin your chances of winning regularly, even if you did try to obey the game's extremely extensive list of willy-nilly demands. And it will keep happening again, and again and again. I found the main reason to continue trying is the promise of reward, and the reason I stopped playing because the risk-reward ratio is one that would keep Satan up at night. This has many negative implications which will all start bothering you the more you get slapped across the face with them:And these are just a bunch of negative points I could come up with from the top of my head. My main gripe with the game stems from how impressively hard it tries to make your time miserable: the game punishes you for going right, then punishes you for going left. It wants you to move fast, but wants you to move slow too. It will give you something, and then proceed to starve you of any reward for the rest of your attempt to journey downwards. The never ending annoyances eventually manifest themselves in a brick wall of frustration you will probably hit sooner or later. For people who don't dearly love the concept this won't be a big issue, but for people like me it is.

_childDocuments_.review: If it won't f*** up your mood, then this one is a great little fun game. It is absolutely not supposed to get you into rage-mode and go all ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-crazy on that poor little bottle of water right next to you, nor the innocent-looking sheet of paper that accidentally slipped right next under your mouse while you tried to murder that sorry excuse of an ice-bastard-mage who froze you on the spot and takes its time to slowly squeeze the life out of your damn accident you had 5 seconds prior to this one with your new wand you quickly wanted to test out and it and everything around you exploded in a fire-lightning storm and blew you right in front of said mage. You enter ruins of some type, head down through mines, ice caves, underground jungles, temples, and more.It adds on alchemy and spells, and has a bunch of alternate/hidden objectives that you can discover.Pros: Cons:
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: Most runs tend to peter out early on simply because no good spells drop, so you're stuck facing continually improving enemies with a stagnating set of tools. You can play flawlessly, but still struggle, flounder, and eventually die an unsatisfying death simply due to sheer luck. In many games where death is frequent, the levels are so short that it doesn't matter, however Noita is a rogue-like, and a very long one at that if you want to do any of the interesting things anyway. Spending hours and hours hunting for spells that might let you stand a chance against the next onslaught only to die from a random explosion is incredibly frustrating. Worse yet are the many, many times where you slowly bleed to death because all of the randomized drops are garbage. Noita can be exceptionally fun when it works, but it rarely does. There are a lot of incredible ideas here, but it is impossible to really explore those ideas. The spell programming gameplay is innovative and fun, but held back severely by the randomized drops that often give you the same boring, useless garbage.  A world of secrets and intense challenges would be fun to explore, but spending hours and hours and hours repeating the same 4-5 stages just to get there is too tedious to justify. Ultimately, Noita does things that I wish more games did, but not all at once.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where absolutely absurd stuff can happen. You can find a wand that fires nukes. An enemy can find a wand that fires nukes. You can build an entire run around a wand you find on the second floor, or go from level to level by the skin of your teeth. You can lose half your health at the first part of a floor then never get hit again. Lava can just happen. I now consider any sort of absurd misfortune "Getting Noita'd."

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent so far! The physics and material interaction is amazing and can create some fascinating results and situations. The random effects on wands and the ability to mix and match effects can create some amazing combinations and I've only scratched the surface. _childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: Beginning can be difficult as you learn the mechanics and parts of the game (i.e. not knowing an orb is electric and then using the wand in water thus killing yourself). It then grows into something you can play in many different styles. Fast paced, exploring, experimental, or just plain goofing around. In the first 3 hours of playing I have realized just how much more this game has waiting for me around the corner and I look forward to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Noita

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Spelunky, instead of ending on level 7-99, actually continued until 30-5 with a bunch more bosses with hundreds of different items and modifiers and perks. And if you figure out the trick, you could pickaxe between the levels, revisit them - dive under olmec's lair, past the lava, wind your way back up through the intermission screen, and use your jetpack to finally hop that cliff off to the side of the intro screen because there's a whole other game over there now.  Noita invites you to break the game mechanics, even encourages it, and hides the bulk of its content behind these opaque goals that aren't made evident, only discovered out of your pure curiosity of seeing what lies over the horizon. I beat the main boss after 50 hours but there is 80% more left for me to discover. I try not to read the spoilers in the wiki but apparently there's an entire alchemy system that I've never discovered for starters.There's hundreds of different spells and modifiers and perks. They combine in different ways that will kill you as easily as the enemy. Sometimes the game gives you a wand with a spell or configuration you've never seen before and it's a trap - it spawns an explosion right in your face, or electrocutes you, or opens a portal to the tentacle-realm and beats you senseless. You ded. Next time read the spell descriptions more carefully! But take those wands to the intermission stages, the refuge between the levels and you get a chance to reprogram your wands. Take the spells from wand #1, combine them with some modifiers from wand #2, and stick them on a wand #3 with a huge mana pool and rapid fire capabilities. Create all new spells of mass destruction. And as you learn the mechanics over an excrutiatigly long time, spells and perks that initially seem worthless, become tremendously powerful when combined with others. For example, a spell to surround yourself in clouds of Whiskey is worthless. But wait, what if you modify it so that the whiskey cloud spawns at the end of a short-range projectile. And what if we attach a fire trail to the projectile and cause it to move in spiral pattern. Now you have a remotely detonated fire cloud that spins around the map widly setting everything on fire, including yourself. Then you remember you once saw a perk that gave you fire immunity. Aha. Spotting those amazing, absolutely game-breaking synergies is what keeps you retrying death after death.Another example: I found a spell modifier that causes projectiles to spawn more copies of itself. So if I shot a fireball off to the left, it would spray more fireballs as it soared across the screen. Nice. Instead of the obvious application, I applied the spawning modifier to a TNT crate. TNT crates just kind of plop out of your wand and sit there. They don't despawn after impacting a wall. Therefore, combined with this modifier they just keep spawning more copies of themselves infinitely, filling up the level with dynamite like a virus. This wasn't an obvious combination at first, but it absolutely deletes an entire level and anything contained within it. Drop a crate out of the entrance hatch, wait 30 seconds and drop a match. The CPU pegs at 100% for a moment, you deal 500,000 explosive damage to anything below. It's a world ender. Also I blew myself up. Restart. Next time I'll modify it so it safely shoots crates from a projectile, and add tentacles for good measure.Every time you die, your carefully engineered wands are thrown into a graveyard, some data file tucked away in the game's folder. The next time you play through, there's a % chance that your ghost will spawn wielding one of them. It's a mixed bag, on one hand you get an opportunity to reclaim a favorite wand. On the other hand, your ghost is using it against you. I did eventually run into my 'world ender' wand again and barely managed to get it off my ghost before everything went up in smoke, but there's been plenty of other times I've run into a ghost of a past run and recognized all too well the wand they were wielding.Noita is fun. Not everyone will like Noita, it's pretty unforgiving and even flat out unfair at times. The first level becomes a chore. You can rush through it, the really interesting spells don't start in until snowland anyway. Enemies will snipe you from some darkened corner of the screen. Enemies will *steal* wands from their pedestals and use them against you. The game will hand you a wand sabotaged to blow your face off. A worm will anger the 'shopkeeper' out of your control, before you have any weapons capable of surviving the encounter.  And you will end many promising runs by building weapons that are too simply too powerful and dangerous to exist in this world.  You don't really start to feel like you have a handle on spellcrafting until dozens of hours in and many players will rightfully give up before then. But each run I see new spells or see new things. And the hope that, next run, I'll finally get a chance to try out a build I've been working up in my mind keeps me coming back.4.3 out of -13e^2 stars

_childDocuments_.review: Me and this game have had an interesting relationship. At first I only played it for ~30 minutes and then refunden it because I thought it was an exhausting game for sure. But after getting into some of the theory of this game I started to love it. Don't get me wrong, however - this game is incredibly unforgiving and requires a decent amount of time to get down the basics. You might get put off by this, but trust me: once you get over the hurdle of learning the basics the game becomes incredibly fun and addictive as hell. Learning about all the interactions spells can have, learning more about the layout of the game, interacting with other players to find the MANY MANY secrets is a very enjoyable process. So if you are looking for a game with an enormous learning curve - which will pay off your know-how - and an enormous map filled with lots of elements - then Noita is definitely your game. There is honestly just one flaw that I find annoying - this game is filled to the brim with secrets (and I understand that you have to look out for them) but some of the secrets are way to complex. Fortunately, the developers added little hints in the beta branch of the game so you can find out about some of them, so that is honestly a pretty good direction. I haven't even talked about the beauty of the developers' investment into the next update, the fantastic soundtrack, the great sound- and level design, the community and the storytelling. I highly recommend the game! And whatever you do - stay away from Polymorphine.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even start? The visual fidelity? The simulated love and care for each moving pixel to make a finely tuned rogue-lite machine? The fact that each run truly feels the same and different in the best possible ways? The feeling of power when you can melt entire floors under you with acid? Or maybe the fun of summoning an army of baddies to defend your honor as you run like Hell through mining tunnels, icy caves, and a Hellish, nightmare-fueled temple. Of course that's not every biome or area available, but the game's secrets and lore are hidden behind a beautifully formed wall of skill-based aristocracy that only makes you want more. Even when I'm fuming from dying for the 80th time that day, I still just keep wanting more. Death feels like a punishment made to help you, rather than harm you. This game will teach you patience, and it will make more of a man out of you than Li Shang in Mulan.Good luck, Noita.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate this game.Its true. I absolutely hate this game. This game has the worst that roguelike/roguelite/rogueadjacent games have to offer. You can build your arsenal on a run that you have invested a good amount of time in only for the game to flip a switch and immediately kill you. Its one of the most frustrating games I've ever played in 36 years of playing videogames.Its also an absolutely brilliant game with incredible mechanics that is deeply satisfying on a moment to moment level. Kicking a box into an enemies face as he jumps at you will never stop being badass. One-shotting the enemy that normally screws up your runs. Figuring out how wands work, how to read a wand's sheet quickly to determine how promising it is, different types of wand styles and even unlocking nuclear options that make end up slicing enemies in half.I had been waiting for this game for a long time. I discovered the tech demo for the Falling Everything Engine, it was very cool to screw around with for a few minutes. That feels like it was before 2010. It was always known that there was a game on the way, but when it was announced it would be a witch game based on Finnish folklore I became less interested - magic and potions aren't really my jam. Still, I'd keep an eye out for it.Years after release, I finally bought it and got immediately hooked. 66 hours later and I've finally (FINALLY) beaten it with the help of online guides and mental health resources. This game drove me crazy and I absolutely hate it. But its wonderful and I also love it and you probably will too.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up for the steam deck, and it works just fine, it's better / easier on a proper PC with a mouse and keyboard though - so big thumbs up there works great.Not recommending this, the game is just too random and rough around the edges, at times it's blatantly unfair - which I'm actually fine with - but stuff happens that I honestly don't think the developers intended to happen, and if they did, I'd question why the hell they allowed it because it spoils the fun.I gave it a good few days of on and off playing, actually quite enjoyed my runs, picking up some new wand and seeing what it can do, occasionally it'd just blow me up or do something I didn't expect which resulted in my demise. Then I started to get the hang of the first few areas... some sense to the game was arriving.What took the biscuit after it'd happened a few times was when a super lich wandered into the "safe zone" between levels whilst I was swapping about things in my wands and 1 shot me back to the menu, I was like, really... that's a thing in this game?There's a lot of that in Noita, just random slapdash events that'll end your run, sometimes it'll be you've messed up, sometimes it'll be blind luck, like I've had a dynamite stick shot out my hands as it left my wand, I've had water fall on me the moment I use my shock wand - ultimately I stopped having fun when these weird broken events came along.Many love the game and will tell you it's part of the experience, or deal with it and get good, so certainly if you like this kind of thing, take my un-recommendation as a recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, addicting, and unbelievably deep in it's mechanics. The game is unforgivingly difficult, and some runs, you're just going to be boned from RNG, but anyone who complains the game is PURE RNG is just salt posting cause they aren't taking time to learn the mechanics of the game. In the same way you're encouraged to explore the world of Noita on each run, players must explore the mechanics of the game. The game's wand modification system can be daunting at first, with little to no hand holding from the game, but after much experimenting (and many failures), players naturally and organically learn what to look for in wands. The same goes for potions! There's a whole range of mixing players can do! For instance, did you know mixing unstable teleportatium and slime makes regular teleportatium?The game is brutal. Easily the most difficult rouge-like I've played, but the pixelated physics and diverse world of Noita provides not only quantity in content, but quality too. This game being $20 is an absolute steal. It's amazing how games will be sold 3 times the price of Noita with only a fraction of the quality it provides.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a fun game under there, somewhere. Maybe it can be unearthed with mods, maybe it requires an overhaul of stats+perks re-balancing, but the game engine you could definitely make a good game out of. The first thing you'll notice when starting of Noita is your movements feel akin to a plastic bag twisting in the wind down a city street; some hits knock you all around the level, other less forceful hits drop you like a rock and can lead to getting combo'd by a base mob (especially if it's a melee one), and your character always feels like it has a speed debuff relative to every other character. On sharp odd ends of the terrain you can get stuck for what feels like no reason at all, and unless you have one of a few digging wand spells you can't get out quickly (and if there's mobs around you're SOL). The camera should be fixed centered on the character, currently the "chasing cam" only accentuates how awful the movement system feels. Health is a chore to maintain (not unique trait to this game of course) which could feel engaging if your movements more appropriately matched your keystrokes and there was some common way to replenish your health besides between levels. Weird RNG is the central tenet of roguelikes and leads to dynamic stories, but some of the wands you can grab throughout the levels generating with mana caps unable to fire the spells within them seems like a massive oversight (might literally be a bug? disregard if so). Further, limiting your ability to swap out the spells to the hub zone between levels leads to less experimentation, and just makes you feel bad. The rare time when you get served a good digging wand you can collect pockets of gold from the first two levels and actually buy wands/spells from the shop, and digging for that gold with one wand while managing killing mobs with another is actually really fun juggle that I wish was more common.

_childDocuments_.review: Noita is a very lonesome game. That is for certain. I got it, played it for a while, but then got refunded it because of it. There is so much unknown, and you are all alone. But in my experience with it, it got so lonely that I just didn’t have the heart to play on any further.But I have to give credit where credit is due, and that is the physics for the ground in the caverns. They market it so that every single pixel crumbles, burns, shatters, etc. and they are correct. They made this aspect of the game really cool.There are also some other very innovative ideas, I think the idea of splashing your enemies with potions is cool as well, or buying new spells for your wands.There is one other problem I had, and that is with the combat. It became a bit tedious over time, because all you can really do is hide behind a wall and shoot occasionally. And even when the enemy dies, it spreads some poison, acid or lava so you can’t get to the loot it drops. That just became annoying as time went on.I think that there is a certain group of people that will like this game, and another that don’t. For this reason, I would recommend it, but be prepared to fell alone in the Noita world should you choose to pay for a ticket to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I will be honest: this game is pretty damn confusing if you don't use the wiki, but I think that the joy of discovery and experimentation is part of the experience Noita offers that is kinda hard to find elsewhere (at least to this degree). Also, don't write this game off for its pixel graphics! The developers really embrace the pixels and actually use them to their advantage in  ways you might not have expected. In this way, it uses the ambiguity of pixels to actually show *more* detail, not less.Noita is a real charmer in many more ways than what I've listed here, and I think it is worth its price tag, especially if you enjoy rogue-lites/rogue-likes.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish you could give a positive and negative review at the same time, because this game is a masterpiece and unplayable at the same time. Sometimes you can blow up the entire level, and sometimes you get instakilled by a stealth propane tank. Sometimes you're solving huge mysteries that unfold into a game around ten times bigger than what you think you're getting, and sometimes you're walking for 10 minutes through a completely empty desert just to get a little more health. Sometimes you're using the game's ridiculously deep wandbuilding system to create a wand from hell that does 5 *quintillion* damage per second (yes, and without any glitches), and sometimes you're crawling through midgame levels with your starter wand because you never found any good wands.This is a game only for people who are mentally prepared for it. If you like putting yourself through pain to succeed, you'll love this game. Even if you don't, you might still like it. You can tune the game to your liking if you're not so masochistic. Unless you eat nails for breakfast, I'd recommend playing with the "Peace With Gods" mod, to avoid getting endgame enemies shoved in your face on the first floor to punish you for something you didn't even do (damn worms). Just don't be one of those people who uses seed tool to find their lively concoction and alchemic precursor recipes and acts like it's not cheating. Most people won't be able to solve most of the game's puzzles alone, but playing this game with no guide is an experience you can't get from anything else these days. This game is like what you thought videogames were when you were a kid, like using strength on the truck to find Mew.Final review: Sit against a wall as long as you can. If you physically fell over instead of giving up from pain, buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Noita is a difficult game to review. Not because its bad. Its actually a very good game. The main reason is that i've spent very little of my 17 hours to date playing the game as it was intended by the developers.Why? Because the developers have made it very easy to mod. Even for someone like myself who finds the intricate folders within folders of games quite confusing, ive been playing with mods non stop.To put it simply, Noita in its vanilla state is a hardcore rogue-lite experience. You start on a mostly randomly generated world (key locations and landmarks are always generated in the same place, and biomes always fit the same areas) with the goal of exploring down through increasingly challenging dungeons. Your health is restored at safe zones between each biome. If you die, your run ends, and your progress is lost, starting you from the start. Unlike alot of Rouge-lites, there is no mechanic for getting stronger each play through. You dont gain any permanent bonus each game. What you do gain however is experience. Each time ive played, ive got further down and over time found the game full of more complexity than I could have imagined.I strongly recommend the game. Its detailed and challenging if you like that sort of thing. If not, then there are plenty of mods to ease the difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: The basis of this game promises endless fun - a procedural generated, completely destructible environment where every pixel has its own physics,  elemental or magical attributes and interactions.  On that level alone, the novelty of playing in the sandbox and the interesting, unexpected effects of various spells, along with the impact of the destructive force you can unleash, means the combat is never unsatisfying.I think this game would have benefited from being less rogue-like.  there doesn't seem to be any permanent progression that accumulates over time, and every death has you start back at zero.  Some weapons/spells are way better than others, so many runs are doomed from the beginning if you don't have a high damage/accuracy wand by level 2.  Speaking of accuracy, the enemies' aim is impeccable.  If your dodge and weave game is weak, you will get picked apart if there are more than 2 enemies with ranged attacks on the screen.  Also, enemies get tough fast, with some creatures able to 2 hit-kill you by level 3, even with extra HP.  This encourages a hit-and-run style of play with tougher enemies - you simply don't have defensive options to withstand more than a couple of big hits.  It can get very frustrating when you get bulls-eyed by a goon that isn't even on screen.I think I would have loved this game if there was the ability to start runs at later levels or have more powerful gear appear more frequently as you got more experience or something.  As it is, I can only get so good at the mechanics that whether I make it past the Ice Caves (level 3) completely depends on how lucky I was with the weapon lotto.  3 out of 5 times, I feel like the game is just not giving me the tools I need to stand a chance.My recommendations without overhauling the game design would be to balance the attack spells better so there wan't such a huge gap between the strong options and seemingly useless ones.  Maybe offer a slightly lower difficulty level, or provide an option to decrease the accuracy of the AI's ranged attacks, or give the character a defensive tactic other than zig-zagging through the air - maybe a consumable deflection move or shield.Excited to see how this property develops.

_childDocuments_.review: If you used to enjoy those falling sand flash games that were really just a sandbox you should really consider checking this game out. I will say as someone with a pretty unimpressive pc I do get a lot of slowdown, which I bothers a lot of people. _childDocuments_.review: Terraria - But not complete Not a game for people who like to accomplish things.The wand and potion system seems really cool. And the lore seems like it would be super cool too. That being said, you can't really play it. You will die from off screen projectiles. You will die from picking up a new item. You will die, simply for being next to something that wasn't hurting you before but now it is. You will die so often you will forget what the point of a game is. It is not that the game is difficult, it is that the game is unbalanced and unfinished. There are key features of gameplay missing and mechanics that should be in the game just not there. If the game was 10% the length it is now and relied on quarters to keep going, it would make sense that this would be an arcade game. It is not an arcade game. You can get hours into a run, and just randomly die. You will lose all your progress. You will start from the beginning having become no better or better off because of it. You will simply learn that everything kills you, and there is no point in exploring or playing. The story or tiny enjoyment you get from starting a run is absolutely not worth dying every 12 minutes and becoming more defensive to what the game wants you to do. Some people may find randomness fun. The difficulty in the game not telling you how anything works can become overcome with a little bit of common sense and reading. A bit of problem solving and pattern recognition will get you through the most cleaver parts of the game. But you will be immediately punished for enjoying the game by being absolutely gang banged by a bunch of random enemies that just spawned in, have perfect aim, and resistance to whatever wands you have built. Honestly this game is so close to being playable too. Just add in healing items, a regeneration after combats, increase health pools, armors, check points, and just a touch of dialog even exposition just to make sense of the randomness in the game. It is literally right there and this game would be great.Don't waste your money on this game as it will only frustrate you rather than provide joy like a video game is suppose to.

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent a long time looking for a true "you're op but that's ok because the game itself is op" experience for a long time. That is not to say that you will experience its thrilling glory straight away (if at all, unless you look up guides to regain at least some of your sanity), simply because the developers genuinely don't want you to. There are hints scattered around the map, but who cares, I just want to build cool wands damn it!On that note, when you play the game for a bit, you begin to understand what the devs had envisioned for this game, because it is honestly one of the greatest games I've ever played. _childDocuments_.review: There's so much sandboxy experimental fun to be had in this game.  I've won a few runs but I haven't even scratched the surface of optional areas and bosses.+ An incredibly complex wand-building system that lets you mix and match spells to create different styles of wands; you can create a wand that drops a bomb then teleports you; that homes in on an enemy and spawns a black hole on them; that places down an egg and turns nearby water to acid when it is broken.  You can also make wands that kill you through collateral damage quite easily, lol, so take some time when looking at new wands.+ A perk system that fundamentally changes your gameplay style as you traverse the dungeon.  The perks tend to grant powerful changes - like automatically freezing all liquids you are nearby, or running an electrical current along anything you touch.  These perks aren't always pure benefits and cause certain situations to be more dangerous or wand configurations to be more or less valuable.  Some perks cause total chaos, like teleporting whenever you take damage.+ A physics engine that ties all the sandbox elements together well and makes navigating the dungeon much more interactive.+ A good variety of dungeon areas that present significantly different challenges from each other and force you to either adapt your build or use caution going through an area for which you're not suited.+ A good general sense of risk/reward where you're basically always chasing more gold but the risk of death becomes more imminent.  I have lost so many runs to thinking I'm just going to grab one more piece of gold.- The sound design needs some touches, as you will hear chaos and destruction going on about you with not a lot of rhyme or reason as to where it's coming from.  Maybe a visual highlighting of the screen edge based on the direction of the source would be good.  This is information that can help save a run.- Some spells and perks will require you to go to the wiki to fully understand their basic function.  This is not good because you only get one choice on perks, and experimenting in this way can immediately destroy your build.- Some moments of unavoidable death, for example when certain enemy types get ahold of wands while they are off-screen below you, they can target you before they appear on-screen.  Runs are a dime a dozen so it doesn't feel like an imminent loss, but I have lost a few promising runs to a pin-point accurate instant destruction wand from an enemy I didn't even know existed.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that is wholly unique with its magic and physics systems. This will make it worth a try alone if you’ve ever wanted something with this level of experimentation. The core gameplay loop of killing things with magic might be eclipsed by choices that make the game tedious to play through; but luckily can all be fixed with mods. Compared to most other roguelikes, in which players expect to start over a lot, this game offers literally nothing to mix it up: choose from a selection or random starting wand, modifiers, faster movement, no early shortcuts, and just growing tired of the first two areas. This is compounded by starting over so much more than any rogue-like I’ve played, so this gets old really fast. Luckily there is a mod that can make it more enjoyable here: . Something like this should be in the base game.It’s amazing both in terms of how well the physics run, in the amount of different elemental interactions with the enemies, and level geometry without slowing your computer down. In most roguelikes I've played procedural level design isn't an issue. In Noita, the layout is very maze like, which made exploring tedious. Especially early on, as it's a chore because you're slow, lots of dead ends and without early ways to blow up walls, and you don't know where to go to find wands and chests, so you backtrack alot because of this. A few fixes could be: make the player base speed 50% faster, always start with like 10 bombs, or a . The more I played it, the more clearly the issue became annoying to me. But thankfully the exit is always at the bottom and not random, so you know what direction to always head in. The magic in this game is one of the best; you have literally hundreds of spells and modifiers that you can combine in any way within the game’s logic, not literal spell creation, more like change the properties of wands with any combo of spells and modifiers: spawning, teleporting, bouncy, fast, duplicate, explode on contact, damage on element doused enemy, add shields, or one of my favorites, spawn TNT that explodes instantly while immune to explosive and fire, to point blank kill everything. The list goes on and on and I cannot state how cool this magic experimentation is. It took me 17 hours to beat the final boss with only seeing 60% of the spells, bosses and secrets. I modded the game which quickened it. Without modding, it will average 40+ hours to do the same. This is where I think the game commits the biggest sin to game design, let me start by saying you pick up wands through the level and sometimes you want the whole wand, or just the spells in it, or test out some combo on the spot. This is limited to only within the shops where you buy with gold collected through killing enemies and opening chests: either prebuilt wands or modifiers and also buy one of 3 perks that offer more power not always pertained to magic. Some examples are: higher jumps, suck up gold, element immunity, passive shields and even unlimited spells. You cannot modify wands outside of these shops and this alone made me stop and pray for a mod to save this game and did: ,a sin that this isn’t a main feature.If you are a masochist, or want a game to literally take forever to finish, this game will be amazing. But I think Noita is one of the most unfair games in terms of challenge. Balance is thrown out the window in many ways, first you die so easily, so randomly, it’s fun for the first dozen deaths, then it gets old to die to a random explosion, getting poisoned, one shot, or just not getting any good spells and wands and are below the difficulty curve. People call this a death simulator and sure, it’s a meme, but not great game design. Similarly many rogue-likes this seems to be an issue for those devs that think their game works better in a rogue-like shell vs other genres. But that’s a whole different topic for another day. If you don’t like to have a lot of runs end from getting one shot by many things in the game; I would say skip. Some examples are: most new encounters, traps, or a few pixels of land that your fireball hits. Here are mods that helped fix that issue:  why isn’t this a thing either, , one safety net feels so nice, should be standard.This is the hardest game to discuss out of the 400+ games I’ve reviewed. I went from dislike, to love to thinking the developers made a good starting off point of a game, similar to how I think Minecraft is a bad game but mods make it great. If the only way a game is enjoyable is by modding its major flaws, that the devs didn’t think should be in the game, then I have to not recommend it for now. All the mods I linked here don’t break the fun, they make it fun. Most have over 100,000 downloads, so  I don’t  feel alone saying that most can’t be bothered with the base game, it’s too time consuming and tedious to enjoy, even though I loved it towards the end with some even better mods that kind of break the balance: , ,  To end on something positive, this game has great variety of enemies and secrets. Once you get past the starting zone and keep going deeper, the enemies get more creative, weird, deadly, cooler, and more unique in their attacks and can get chaotic, if it doesn’t kill you. There are many secrets, many I didn’t find that lead to most of the bosses. I think most will be hard to find without 100+ hours of knowledge and practice, or mods. But when you defeat one, usually it means avoiding their one hit attacks, bosses drop game changing spells, I only got a meteor shower that was EPIC and was worth the effort. Hopefully you can see the confusion I have:  the core game is great, but too much outside the magic simulator gets in the way of having fun. I’m glad it has a passionate community to mod it so I could enjoy it instead of giving up.Here is a video of just the first 11 runs and I slowly starting adding mods towards the end:

_childDocuments_.review: This review isn't needed, but Im going to do it anyways.  This game deserves as much attention as it can get.  Noita.  An indie game thats more deserving of the AAA tag than any "real AAA" game that has been released this year.  What is noita, in short?  A procedurally genareated action/adventure rougelike where EVERY. PIXEL. has its own physics.  Its also a game thats worth far more than its $18 pricetag.Where do I start?  Lets just start as every round of Noita starts, with your character, near an abandoned mine.  A hooded,  nameless wizard, searching.  for what?  ♥♥♥♥, even i dont know that.  Your first few runs will be met with almost immediate death once you delve into the mines, and thats okay.  Your main goal is to survive as long as possible and learn the mechanics.  once you get the hang of levitating around projectiles, avoiding world hazards and seperating enemies to make the challenge easier, youll start exploring the caves and surface in more detail.  youll learn what the basic spells do, and what wands fit each spell combo the best.  youll learn to dilute the toxic sludge with water to reach otherwise impassible areas, to carefully kick a lantern towards a wooden wall to burn it down and engulf the nearby enemies in flames, thats when youve started tinkering with the real meat of this game: alchemy.   should you buy this game?  yes.  a million times yes.  if i could give it 2 thumbs up I WOULDplus, with modding support, this game has literally infinite potenial.  Well done Nolla Games,  youve done it.  I sincerely applaud you, and look forward to whatever projects you make in the future!
