_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica has shown us just how compelling deep dives into mysterious oceans can be, and it wasn’t even the first to explore those depths. Despite its runaway success and the more modest successes of titles like Endless Ocean, diving games are few and far between. That makes the appearance of something like Beyond Blue a cause for celebration, even if it’s not quite the scope or scale we’re looking for. I could certainly complain about the small dive locations or short campaign, but honestly I’ve just been so content swimming around and scanning different fish and jellies that it hardly bothers me.Meet Mirai, a young diver sent to the bottom of the sea in a high-tech one-woman sub. She’s working with OceanX to produce educational livestreams about life beneath the surface, and also complete research projects for her benefactors. Mirai’s real passion, though, is a pod of sperm whales she’s been following for years, which has a new addition to the group. Her efforts to catalog the undersea world will lead her to some of the deepest places people can dive, on the trail of mysteries that could mean disaster for the fragile aquatic ecosystems. And life back on dry land has its own twists and turns, as Mirai deals with her sister Ren and their sick aunt as best she can while thousands of miles away.There’s a fair bit of story woven through Beyond Blue, all told through radio chatter as you reach dive checkpoints and use downtime on your sub to make some long-distance calls. You’ll have several threads to keep track of, between the sperm whales, Mirai’s family, the friction between her teammates Andre and Irina, and a number of deep-sea mysteries, and they never really come together to form a cohesive narrative. It’s messy in the way real life is, but not in a gratifying way that games need to be, and ends on an emotional twist that I don’t feel is well-executed or earned. Ultimately all the story bits give you something to stay plugged into as you swim from one sonar buoy to the next.Beyond Blue consists of eight dives across six different locations, from shallow atolls to deep-sea vents, and even one out in the vast, bottomless open ocean. Your objectives are fed to you by Andre, and usually involve reaching a sonar buoy, scanning for important sounds like whale pods or sensor alerts, and checking them out. While the gameplay itself isn’t much more than following objective markers, the aforementioned radio dialogue and events they trigger make for some pretty engrossing moments of natural marvel. Watching a pod of whales awaken or orcas corral and feed on huge schools of fish are magical experiences to experience even in a simulation, and the detailed creature models and attention to scientific details really help sell it.You won’t just find whales down in the depths, either. Loads of aquatic life have been modeled for Beyond Blue, from tiny moon jellies to massive sun fish. You’ll find all manner of sharks, crabs, rays, and tentacled critters, too. The one thing that really helps broaden the gameplay experience is that you can scan things with your high-tech suit, adding them to an index of creatures encountered. You’ll get more info about them as you scan more of the same type, including where they’re found and their common behaviors. There are hundreds of fish and animals to scan, with some being rarer than others and occasionally surprising you with how they show up. In addition to these bits of sea life trivia, you’ll unlock clips from the documentary Blue Planet 2 as you complete story objectives, which was very openly a major inspiration for the developers.Still, even between revisiting the different dive sites and scanning all the critters of the sea, I saw everything Beyond Blue has to offer in less than five hours. Make no mistake, this is not an open-ocean odyssey like Subnautica. Those eight dives will pass very quickly, and as relaxing and marvelous as they are, it’s still a very concise experience. I wouldn’t show up for the story, either, with its many loose threads and scattershot execution. But man, there’s just not that many opportunities to swim with whales on Steam, are there? For as limited an experience as this is, I thoroughly enjoyed discovering the exotic locales and creatures of the deep ocean. Until we have a more robust diving simulator to excite and educate us, Beyond Blue will fill a very important niche.Did you enjoy this review? I certainly hope so, and I certainly hope you'll check out more of them at  or on my !

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond blue is an exploration and documentary-based game set deep into the ocean. Play as Mirai, a deep-sea explorer and scientist part of a newly-formed research team with Irina and Andre. Follow, document, track, and take samples of whales, dolphins, fish, turtles, and more in this informative and fun 3-5hr adventure! I had a ton of fun playing, I love these types of games and it was a real treat to see all the behind the scene videos and listen to whale calls. My favorite thing though, was that despite going into deep,  sea there were  I am wholeheartedly a coward and I freely admit that.Beyond Blue is more than just a documentary though, there is real story going on and it really makes you wanna keep pushing forward further down into the heart of the ocean. I loved the voice acting, I didn’t experience any problems (Except, for some reason one fish was invisible. I found him on accident though.) and I wholeheartedly recommend Beyond Blue to literally anyone, even if this isn’t the genre they usually go for.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Great overall experience! This is of course NOT a SCUBA diving simulator or a freediving simulator. It's an educational adventure to marine biodiversity and its threats. There's solid scientific revision and it shows. Species names are correct, their positions in terms of depth ranges and habitats make sense. Also, a realistic depiction of sharks as calm, passive predators that are just doing their thing and don't want to mindlessly attack humans for sport. Very refreshing.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game for about a year now, ever since I first caught wind it was coming out. I really wanted something to bring back the love and joy I had for Endless Oceans many years ago when the original Wii was still a big thing. Sadly, I wasn't able to play this game for longer than an hour without getting incredibly bored. Artistically, it's incredible -- the graphics, sounds and amount of ocean life are really well done, but it's easily drowned out by the constant repetitive gameplay of buoy>scan>buoy>scan>∞I made a short list within the hour of me playing of pros and cons; they're as follows:Pros:-Gorgeous Graphics-Voice Acting-Very Realistic-Creative Characters and Storyline-Diverse SealifeCons:-Incredibly Repetitive-No concrete tutorial past your first dive-Controls feel bulky and weird-Not enough interaction with the sea creatures-Whales and biometric scanners are the prime objective-Sub interactions and controls-No character customizationOverall, I don't think this game was ready to be released. Though the idea is there, it doesn't seem fully fleshed out - more like a trial for a bigger and better thing to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Good things: Music used in the sub of the game is very lovely. I like the videos, but some are repetitive with the clips. Seeing some of the advancements in our underwater tech is something that I was happy to see. I liked a lot of the behaviors they let us see with the whales in an up close nature, and the focus on the destruction of the ocean.Graphics are nice and seeing the movements up close is interesting.Cons: The story is very empty. You go into the water, do what they ask and leave. The story with her sister is dead ended, and there is a lot of drama between characters that just has no place in the game. Feels like a last minute addition or a half added thought. You never really follow the whales or get any results from what you're actually doing in game. Also a lot of things you can look at on the sub that never really do anything. You just glace at them....for some unknown reason? I was hoping for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this one as really like ocean based games. At first glance it looks nice, the graphics are not overwhelming but pretty solid. It does not come close to a real diving experience where there is a great variation in underwater clarity. In this game there is always an optimal clarity so finding your way is pretty easy. To  make things even easier you are guided to objectives by search icons provided in each section by a 'minigame' where you 'discover' your waypoints. A sense of achievement in discovering things for yourself is totally ruined. Swimming to a designated point brings you to the animals (usually whales) that need to be examined to achieve a msission target. Again, the animals are nicely rendered. I stayed with them for a while to observe them ... only to discover they are 'fish on rails' ... the animations are looped .. there is no reason to stick around after fulfilling the mission purpose, nothing else to wonder about after the first animation.Killing the experience completely are the submarine sections which feature robotic animations by our antagnosist, totally useless objects to interact with in said submarine and a totally irrelevant narrative about 'research' and private conversations  (with soulles voiceacting) between sisters about a grandmother suffering from dementia. Only nice feature here are the background videos that can be played explaining more about ocean wildlife.Usaually I only refund if a game crashes on me (2x in first hour is a sure refund for me), this time I refund because the game does not live up to the experience I had expected from the previews.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game.The story of this game is okay, but it's not the main thing about the game. The game is for people who are very interested in the underwater world and want to learn more about the sea. Personally, I'm very interested in this and already knew a lot about it so I'm probably an exception, but it was still a very nice experience with a great atmosphere and I think anyone who is in any way interested or looking for a relaxing game will like this game.The gameplay reminds me a bit of "Pokemon Snap", you move through the sea and scan everything you find to learn more about some creatures while following the story and experiencing really nice moments.In line with some of the scenarios you experience ingame, a real-life video is unlocked to give you more information.Even though the game is not particularly long with 3 hours, this game gets a clear recommendation from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is a narrative game where you play a diver who belongs to a group that studies sperm whales in particular.The story is quite interesting because it tells real facts about the dangers threatening this species. The gameplay is quite relaxing and very easy and what's more is accompanied by beautiful graphics ! You will have the opportunity to unlock small documentaries on a lot of things mentioned in the story and a catalog of fish with rather interesting data (once these have been scanned).Unfortunately the game has certain weak points including the impossibility of completely removing the HUD from the game, the sound (excluding music) which is not excellent, the character being quite slow in the submarine or even some bugs like the "Continue" button which does not work ! (You have to manualy load your previous save)No achievements are missable, you can clearly do the story and then do the rest of themYou will need do some actions on the submarine and scan every creatures and items (all of them are marked on the map, difficult to see them on some maps, you had to zoom or put the cursor on the edges of the map)Just launched into the game, the  swimming peacefully above the reef as well as , make the game magnificent to look at ! With that, you will have a scanning function that will allow you to discover little by little all the creatures in the game !, swimming can be done slowly or faster depending on your choice and  : you can very well spend 2 hours searching and wander around the area without advancing the story ! I have to say that I really appreciated this detail.Speaking of the story, the latter surprised me quite a bit because I was not at all expecting . It goes so far as to tell some quite  while remaining soft, which is quite pleasant.Linked to the story, . The discussions are not useless and even if at times the details can be complicated, most of the data received is very interesting! To this we can also add the documentaries unlocked as the adventure progresses, as well as quotes and references to research related to this game. to know where the last scans to be done are located, which is very practical, but which also hides sad management...The first thing that frustrated me quite a bit was ... No color blindness or gamma options, no adjustment for the HUD and to remove it, no switch camera in first person (which would have been excellent in this game) and no way to remove the interface in the cockpit of the submarine when you are seated, even after the game ends ! I find these features quite important in a game of this magnitude and especially for such a recent game... This didn't stop me from taking a lot of screenshots but I must say that the compass is really frustrating ! I must admit that I removed the music very quickly, not that it was poorly done, but I wanted to enjoy the sounds of the ocean, swimming, whales, etc. Except that the latter are not all very successful... Swimming makes practically no noise in general, some fish no longer have even if they can pass by you quite quickly or even some elements of the scenery which don't make any noise more than a few meters away (volcanic explosions must still make quite a bit of noise at a few dozen meters right?! haha). It's quite disappointing on this point.Some bugs in the call, notably the bug not corrected for more than 2 years :  You should know that at present, if you want to continue a game you must not load the save game. This isn't the end of the mode but it's still annoying, knowing that a lot of people have reported it ! is also excessively low, it feels like he is moving through water... Which is quite ironic x) : this is what made me waste hours looking for the last specimens missing in my register... How did I not see them? Because of their very pale color on the fairly white and bright maps... Which requires putting the cursor in the possible ends of the map to really see them, or really zooming in! It was a frustrating discovery I must say (5 hours wasted looking for a jellyfish haha)Finally, we can talk about . The game will only last a few hours, between 4 to 5 hours (unless you don't use the scan benchmarks, that's another story), which is quite short for a price of this magnitude but is quite made up for by the content of the game: documentaries, educational facts, interesting data and a constructive and touching story!Certainly I was quite disappointed with the lack of functionality or the rather short lifespan but being amazed by this underwater world,  ❤️
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game of a beautiful world that is unfortunately under attack... This game is a relaxing "finish in one sitting" kind of game that you would enjoy if you like watching things like Blue Planet in the evening. Beyond Blue is about the same length of a full length film (unless you look to grab all the achievements which will take 4-5 hours casually). It's centered around marine life in the west pacific and a pod of whales you follow throughout the story - but instead of watching the movie - you get to play through it. One of the primary reasons i love and play video games.Being a recreational diver myself - i thoroughly enjoyed the play through. Its compelling, educational, I didn't experience any bugs, and honestly was pleased to see how they worked the story into the different dives/settings and how the collectibles "unlocked" different things back on the sub. The only "negative" to the game I could point out is that it implies to someone who wouldn't know better that a human could dive to a depth of 4000+ meters and not be crushed. Developmentally it's easier to call the suit "high tech" than it would have been to try and develop a completely different mechanic to control a submersible... and honestly it works just as is. Being in a dive suit brings you much "closer to nature" than you would be behind several inches of glass - and for those complaining -its a game :)No - its not "Subnautica" (although i love that game too) - and honestly, other than a couple of game mechanics i think its stupid to compare the two. This is meant to be more than just "a game" and comparing this to a game like that is like saying that Nat Geo TV show series are a waste of time because they lack good comedy or drama. *Insert face palm here*Big thanks to the Dev's & all involved in putting this experience together - well done and very impactful!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly engaging and atmospheric. It's clearly a love project of the developer. I thought it would be boring at first, but although there is no action, it's still very intriguing to play. At its core it's a narrative adventure in which we follow the main characters in her dives, which are guided by two other scientists and focus on the whale family the MC is following. The game sucked me right in with the second dive. Very immersive. The main story is very short though, but you can repeat all the dives and explore to your liking.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: what a AMAZING game ! PLEASE buy this game ! support the developers and safe the ocean and the creatures who are living in it. don't rush ingame, just enjoy the environment of the ocean and explore and scan all the creatures in it (tip : check your map). i took my time and explored the oceans and got all the 30 achievements in a bit more then 4 hours.don't hessitate, buy it
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This year has been really rough for me, and a lot of other people too of course.. With the continuing spread of COVID-19, I can't travel to the ocean, and I've really been missing the ocean. Yesterday night I even had a dream where I was swimming with dolphins.. today I decided to look up underwater games, and stumbled upon Beyond Blue. After finishing the first mission, you're loaded into your sub, and as the music started playing on the cute little 'jukebox', I started crying. I couldn't stop! Outside the windows of the sub, I see whales and schools of fish swimming by to the tunes of well selected music. Needless to say, I think I found the underwater game I was looking for.The gameplay leaves little to be desired. What I do miss is to scan corals, or talking more about the trash you can find on the sea floor (maybe it comes into play later in the game?). The gameplay that is there, is relaxing, but still keeps you on your toes. Swimming alongside with a Sperm whale is simply breathtaking and amazing! I've only played about 1,5 hours but I've learned so much. This game made me love the ocean even more, if that's even possible. It's vast and filled with life!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved ocean life ever since I was small. I've even considered a career in Marine Biology myself.Having said that, I think this game is beautiful. The graphics are amazing, and so are the creatures themselves. While I wish there was more variety, the different sea animals we got were good choices. The animations are both smooth and realistic, and the models are stunning. The different area's you visit throughout the main story campaign are stunning in their own ways as well. From the shallows of the coast and a small atoll filled with wildlife, to the large and mysterious brine pools in the midnight zone near the boiling sea vents. One of my favorite aspects was scanning wildlife as you go on throughout the game and coming back to look at fully animated, 3D models of the different creatures you have found. You can look at different animations of behaviors specific to that animal as well. Another feature is looking at the depth at which they are found, listening to audio of the whales and dolphins you have recorded, etc. However, this game is not without it's cons. The main narrative of the game feels extremely weak and very short, only taking about 3 hours to complete. I found myself slightly disappointed by it. The tensions between the main protagonist and her sister felt forced, as well as other dynamics between different characters. I just wish there was more story to this game.I have also found myself many times throughout my playthrough wishing for more wildlife and behaviors. While you do get to see some cool behaviors, such as a Leatherback Sea Turtle eating Jellyfish, they don't feel as if they are happening naturally. The behaviors feel artificial, as you only see the behaviors on story missions. It would have been really nice to see randomized AI with randomized behaviors. All in all, this game was really beautiful. I've found myself always wanting to come back and complete scanning all of the creatures to unlock different behaviors, information, etc. As well as to fulfill my life-long dream of swimming up close in personal with a Bottlenose Dolphin pod. I really do hope the Developer team adds more to the story, maybe some DLC with new areas, creatures, etc? That would be amazing to see!!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautiful game, no doubt. There is a linear story which takes about 3-4 hours if you take your time. However, you are limited to the exploration of the map sizes. If you hope that this game is an open world exploration game then do not buy this. It has a story mode and yes you can explore the maps after you've done the full story. Most of the time you are scanning the marine life around you. You go from one way-point to the other and that's about it.This game is highly educational with all the information you get per species and you also get the additional Blue Planet video's in your sub. If you don't care about the game time then buy it. You will learn something. Just be warned, no open world. The marine life is well made, the animations are well made, graphics are perfect, story is so so. I wish I could recommend this game, but I was expecting a way bigger game then what it is. I hope the developer sees these remarks because the game is beautiful and well made but it lacks in size. If they update the game with about twice the size of the maps then I will change to recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is a beautiful interactive documentary. Raising awareness to protect the world's oceans is worthy cause. That said, If the developers want to appeal to the gaming community, they're going to have to step up their game a bit with larger environments, more locations, greater diversity of life, SOME element of danger and more than 5 hours of game play.Oh yea, almost forgot... There's a slight glitch, nothing too serious but if you don't finish the game the first time you play it, use the "LOAD" option in the main menu. Using the "CONTINUE" option crashed my game every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is a linear story-based game and not really open-world. There are objectives in each "Dive" (8 chapters). During each Dive, you can take your time and explore the level, plus scan all the sea creatures you can find. There is no combat and no danger at all. The story mainly follows a family of whales, and also has some character backstory. The voice acting and actual gameplay are really nice. Very chill atmosphere + great score/soundtrack.I finished the whole game + all achievements in about 5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: If like me you you liked Subnautica but you found it a bit "meh" that all the data you collect on the alien creatures are just fake, then probably it's a game for you too. There are so many wonders down there... and you can do it from the comfort of your home!Everything is real and that's what make it stand out. Only the characters and the narrative in the game are invented but they allow you to actually feel what real scientists feel themselves when they're away from their family, when the creature they got attached to die, when they discover something huge, ... idk, it's magical!The base of the gameplay is that you have to scan animals. More scans you do of the same animal and more information you unlock on that specific animal (not much tbh). Then you go back to the sub and you follow the rest of the story. These interludes are very suiting because it brings some variation in the gameplay. As you progress you also unlock short documentaries (<5 min) which are amazing and also help understand the whole deal better.Also the sound is fantastic. These whales make such a beautiful sound. It's like they're singing. I digress... well... ok. You need to either turn up the volume or make sure your installation is very good because it's incredible to hear. I think people got turned off by the fact that you can "collect" all the scans of all the animals and they start perceiving this as a chore. When I started to play I didn't realize that the map was showing location of animals I have not yet scanned. So I just ventured and scanned randomly and it was the nicest experience of all. When I realized the map could be useful to "collect" the scans (which also unlock some of the achievements), I started to enjoy the game less. I think the discovery is VERY important and you should not try to collect things. Imagine trying to get a picture of all the fish in the oceans? It's ridiculous.So,  in my opinion you should not use the map and not try to get 100% scans. Just go with the flow and feel free to explore randomly. Follow the fishes! And don't worry about the achievements because when you reach the end of the game you will be able to navigate to all the areas and make all the scans to collect things if you want. But first, please focus on the first part of the game that is the discovery. This is the best.The real voyage of discovery.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely do reviews.But iamma just write my thoughts.beautiful.playing this is  almost like i'm actually free diving.all the animations were so well done and it doesn't feel like the fish is just simply going circles.every detail, every rock, every piece of weed feels real.also, when i actually went on diving, i had this weird feeling when i look into the depth of the sea.i feel terrified, like something is gonna come up and eat me.but in this game, i don't have that feeling.in general, I love this game.But i wish there's more to it.the story is great and all, but i'd want bigger maps to explore.more stuff to do ingame.also, the submarine was a nice touch, but there ain't much to do inside besides sitting in the chair and read message and play through dialogues.Also, if u made a sub with that much detail, why not let us ride it and pick our locations to go?

_childDocuments_.review: It reminds me of Endless Ocean, that old game on the Wii.  You're a scuba diver uncovering secrets of the ocean with a big focus on accurate ecosystems.  There's no combat or violence (towards the player, anyway; there's some circle-of-life stuff amongst the critters).  There's also a big focus on narrative with characters that are quite likable.  Most importantly is the educational aspect about ocean science and conservation; its very well done through the game itself, the scannable entries, and the unlockable documentary clips.If you're looking for chill scuba exploration game or to scratch that nostalgic Endless Ocean itch, try Beyond Blue.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game! If you are looking for a challenge then this is not the one for you, but if you are looking to experience the ocean and it's wild life under a few different conditions, and especially if you are interested in learning more about the ocean and the research that is being done in recent times, I can definitely recommend this game for you. There is a story about the ocean the game tells, as well as a story about the character you play as, both are short but sweet. I had a lot of fun with it and would love to see more games like this!

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews for the games I play, but for some reason this game has just moved me to the point of me needing to leave a review.I can't even put into words how this game moved me, it really does show off just how beautiful the sea is. The sounds while diving are so mesmerising and somehow even when you are just inside the sub talking to your peers, the atmosphere and music really makes you feel like you are 10,000 leagues under the sea.I have a real pure bred passion for the sea and just how little we know about it, if you love a story that is simple yet moving please play this game. It does everything it needs to, and the sheer amount of educated information they have on each creature you scan is just amazing, I am in true awe of this game.The best part about this game is the behaviour you track between the Sperm whales I would scan a whale and sit there and just watch them. _childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue struggles as a narrative adventure game but shines as an educational tool that brings awareness and reveals some of the ocean’s secrets. Its few characters don’t quite stand out and the simple core gameplay loop of swimming, scanning and following waypoints comes off as rather bland. While there’s not much excitement in the actions that you perform, the way they’re contextualized pulls the experience up significantly. Different moments during exploration and the short documentary-style videos featuring real-life experts ensure that by the time you’re done with it, you’ll have learned at least a handful of new and fascinating things about the ocean and its inhabitants. .
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I wish that I had this game back when I was a kid, however, I enjoyed it immensely as an adult. Yes, it does have an educational aspect to it, and is reminiscent of being inside a National Geographic documentary at times. However, I feel as though the educational aspects of this game are very tastefully implemented. It doesn't shove information down your throat constantly. Instead, it tries to blend immersive underwater swimming gameplay with a bit of an educational twist. That being said, the swimming mechanics are phenomenal. One of the best I've seen of any underwater game. The whole experience is very realistic and true to the diving experience. The sub-plot is a bit shallow and irrelevant. I forgave this, though, because I feel as though the sub-plot was perhaps meant to take a backseat. It did feel like an afterthought, however, I feel as though they tried to use it subtly as an interlude to drive some sort of narrative forward. Otherwise, it would literally just be an educational diving game, with not much substance. However, it definitely did have a bit more substance than it would have had if it solely was a diving and educational game, but it definitely wasn't anything too profound. However, the soundtrack is amazing! Between dives, you have an underwater abode where you have access to a really cool playlist. I added all the songs from this game to my personal playlist because they're all so good. Swimming with sea creatures has always been a fantasy of mine. I loved exploring the sea and swimming with all the animals. I really can't complain much about anything. It was a very good game and I highly enjoyed it. I wish there were more underwater games that executed the water and swimming mechanics as seamlessly as this one does. My one and only critique, as I've stated, is that I feel as though the plot was a bit thin. Still, the star of the show was the diving, and I do wonder if a heavier plot would have taken away from that.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing casual game focusing on exploration (Scan all the fishies!) and education (includes a documentary, delivered via byte-sized video clips that unlock as the game progresses). It's rather short with ~5 hours needed to see everything and reach 100% completion.You also get to spend some time on your sub between dives, though there isn't much to do besides listening to your music playlist, looking at all the sea creatures you've unlocked so far and eventually making a few calls to colleagues / family. I thought Mirai's banter with her science peers was done well enough, but the family stuff felt a bit tacked on and unfinished. Apart from that, everything is delivered with superb voice acting - if you don't look at the cast, you might even get flashbacks to a certain space station.i didn't encounter any bugs while playing besides Mirai clipping into her seat on the sub at one time. Played with Proton 7.x (GE-Version) on LInux, no performance issues or video playback problems.

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond blue is an interesting game if you are interested in Marine Biology and the real-world work of biologists. While the number of specimens of each species (and their proximity to one another) is grossly exaggerated, This is a video game and thus is allowed to make such creative liberties. I enjoyed the game, all in all, but I'm left feeling almost cheated. I put 2.3 hours into this game and I completed the story-line and All I have left is achievement hunting by scanning various species. I understand that this game is trying desperately hard to be a real-world depiction of marine biology and Marine ecosystems, this is still a video game. One where I feel like 2.3 hours of gameplay isn't enough and where the climax of the story still feels like the building up to it. This is a game that feels like it was created by marine biologists, but game developers. Great for realism, not so great for a consumer. *Spoiler Alert*I would have loved to have seen more in the way of painting the ominous nature of the open ocean, the mysteries of the deep. I would have liked to have seen longer story-lines with satisfying answers and endings. This game feels like it sets up some over-arching mystery as to why a healthy whale passed and what's going on with the miners, but it basically cuts there. I feel like this was supposed to be a set-up for something bigger, but it wasn't. Like someone quit halfway through. As a result I'm left feeling like i've been cheated out of a complete story and enough game-play time for my money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue captures the beauty and majesty of the sea, playing like an ocean documentary that you and your crew are able to live inside.As someone who loved the surreal side of Abzu and the survival aspects of Subnautica, I wasn't sure where this game would land for me, but the grounded approach to gamifying the experience of learning about the ocean and its creatures created a meditative experience for me that I can't wait to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really beautiful underwater game, that could have done with some more time in QA-testing. There are bugs, and obvious UI problems/errors that should have been fixed months before release.Let's start with the biggest: After having finished the game, there was a trio of Remora that I hadn't scanned. but I could not find them on ANY of the maps.. so I start a new game, to see if there was a new game plus mode, where the game would remember what you'd scanned and what you hadn't. No such luck. you start over from scratch when it comes to both the story and the scanning.but more importantly... the game deleted 5-6 of my last savegames. Two hours of playtime, just gone. and it replaced the autosave with one created by the new playthrough.Some UI parts of the game will let you use the D-pad on a controller, others wont. some will let you use a mouse, others wont. some parts of a menu can be clicked by the mouse cursor, some can't (on the same page!)... you have several ways to see a list of all the animals that are in the game (after you've scanned at least one specimen of the species), but only one of those lists will show you how many more of that species you need to scan. The player model while swimming is flawless. The player model while walking on the sub is liable to give you nightmares.Every time you enter the sub, the music player will start playing. Regardless of whether you paused it or muted it last time you were on the sub, and it's full of copyrighted music. Only stream this game with the music silenced in the settings menu... though that will also remove the background music while you're diving, which is quite soothing and nice.Every mission you finish will unlock a small documentary that you can watch. The UI for play, pause, forward, back and exit... will show over the subtitles, and only disappear if you pause the video.. defeating the purpose.but other than that, it's beautiful, short and soothing as all heck. and I really liked the voice acting as well. Mira Furlan (Delenn from Babylon 5/Danielle Rousseau from Lost) knocks it out of the water park.If it gets a patch, I'll change my recommendation to "yes".Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most beautiful games I've played. A shorter game, but packs so much emotion and enjoyment. _childDocuments_.review: From about the age of five, whenever I was asked what I wanted to be when I grew up, I would always respond, “marine biologist”. I didn’t much know what a marine biologist , mind; I had no real aptitude for the sciences. All I knew is that it meant exploring the ocean, and to me the ocean was a world as extraordinary and mysterious as any found in the fantasy and science-fiction novels I was gorging myself on at the time.I was enticed by the ocean and afraid of it in equal measure, fixated on that mesmerising blue-green sheen – sometimes serene, other times turbulent – that served as a veil separating the world below from our own. I loved the water. I loved to swim. I loved  in that fantastical world, so teeming with exotic beauty, strange life, and dangers both visible and hidden.I still do; that childhood reverence has never left me. If anything, it’s only grown – in tandem with my understanding of the ocean as an essential element of our life here on Earth. And just like all those fantasy books of mine and the myriad threats their worlds faced, our ocean was under siege from threats of its own.Only those threats? Each and every one was a consequence of human activity. I love the ocean, but apparently we as a species don’t love it enough.So whenever a game like  pops up, I’m right there. The video-game is an ideal medium for ocean exploration, capable of creating the illusion of a vast expanse of blue and its uncharted depths and evoking feelings of utter isolation, which can be considered either peaceful or terrifying, depending on your inclinations.For me, it’s often both., released for PlayStation in 1997 by Black Ops Entertainment, was my first taste of such an experience. The game punished players for killing harmless wildlife, inducing a welcome level of respect for the ethereal environment you had the privilege of inhabiting. There was a baddie, too, whose actions were wholly detrimental to the ocean. Simon Black, I think his name was. Totally a baddie.Conversely, I was also playing  at the time, which in one inventive level dropped Lara 40 fathoms below the ocean surface, pitch black in every direction and surrounded by sharks. Wildlife was never kind to Lara, but can you blame them? She lays waste to every ecosystem she finds herself in.The ocean game, then, was a system – or simulation – that could test our relationship to it, and the ways we might interact with its inhabitants, be that for good or ill. As the medium has moved forward we’ve seen some exemplary additions to the sub-genre, from the incredible  to the effervescent, damn near poetic . takes a different approach to the above titles, to varying levels of success.Its development is associated with BBC Studios’  series and exploratory ocean initiative Ocean X, alongside a host of pioneering oceanographers and marine biologists who make an appearance in a series of unlockable mini-documentaries. Their inclusion elevates  into something of an educational simulation, the necessity of which couldn’t be more pressing as we hurtle heedlessly towards climate catastrophe. Bleak? Yep, and  knows it.You play as Mirai, a young woman who unlike me followed through on her dream to become a marine biologist.  is a little way into the future and you’re investigating a pod of sperm whales – Mirai’s particular fascination – in a region in the Pacific. In your ears are your two colleagues, André and Irina, both specialists in their respective fields with their own scientific objectives they seek to accomplish during Mirai’s dives.The presence of these characters and their in-level banter was one of my favourite aspect of the game. Scientist-types are a regular staple in the medium, but these guys are the real deal. Their authentic dialogue makes it feel as if you’re truly part of an expeditionary force driven by the benevolent passions of its members. You’re able to successfully follow the thread of the story being told, what’s at stake and why these dives – of which there are eight in total – matter by inculcating you into Mirai’s field of expertise.So, what about the game bit, then? I think it's here  is at its weakest, although that feels unfair given the game’s openly simple (but never simplistic) intentions. It’s just that there’s actually very little to it in terms of engagement.With each dive you’ll make your way to a buoy, identify the location of the sperm whales, glide effortlessly towards them – a sublime piece of animation – through a series of diverse biomes, and then scan the whales once you’ve found them. Sure, there’s plenty other aquatic lifeforms inhabiting the reefs and dark depths of the ocean floor, and swimming alongside them is pure joy, but that’s roughly it as far as the gameplay goes.The mini-documentaries you unlock showcase a staggering variety of technological apparatus for studying the ocean, but I found myself wanting to see more of that in the game itself; as it is, it’s mostly alluded to in text from your colleagues. Similarly, I felt the documentation of the aquatic life you discover was way too thin, revealing little beyond their genus.I'm also of the opinion that the game struggles to intertwine the two narratives it has in play. The central focus is the pod of sperm whales Mirai is tracking, which elicited all kinds of complex emotions in me – a reverence, melancholia, even a touch of love – and then there’s the interpersonal drama of Mirai’s colleagues and her sister, Ren. The friction between the two siblings is mostly fluff, adding little of value or interest.If Ren was on the line during the inter-level sub breaks, I was invariably at risk of tuning out. It’s low-level, uninspired drama, and the writer in me wanted more. That’s a shame: the voice cast is impeccable. is not like . There is no Simon Black. It's also not like  (oh, really?). There are sharks – lots of ‘em – but they’ve no interest in taking a bite out of you. Lara was lost, trapped and afraid in the ocean depths, but Mirai is at home – a place she wants to be, as often as she can. It’s always the next dive.To round off I’ll go with an anecdote. In one of the later missions, I was swimming through the twilight zone – beyond the reach of sunlight – investigating vents on behalf of Irina. We’d known something was wrong in the region for awhile, and we were trying to piece it together.As I approached my goal, I swam into a spacious cavern, where just above me glided a sleeper shark. I didn’t have to panic; he was perfectly comfortable with my presence, so I relaxed, and we swam together, me towards the object of my study, he simply through his home. Soon enough we emerged from that tunnel, and before me lay debris from the deep-sea mining we’d suspected had been taking place.And as my new friend glided on, disappearing into the perpetual dark it called home, I felt a pang of sadness and guilt, but he was gone before I could utter a meaningless, unintelligible apology. The problem was me and where I was from – that above world – but he wouldn’t know that.I love the ocean. It’s why I’m able to be so shamelessly sentimental. But time is running out.  is far from the most sophisticated of ocean sims, but it’s worth the dive, if only for the reminder that there’s a great deal of beauty we can yet save, both for the extraordinary diversity of life beneath those waves, and for ourselves as well.Originally published on

_childDocuments_.review: A friend of mine recommended I play this game since I couldn't decide what to play next, and I am so glad they did.  This was a revolutionary game that shows you the wonder and magic of deep-sea exploration in addition to the dangers and terrors of the same space.  It is not a romanticized game in any way, and stays true to what we know of ocean exploration.The design of this game is absolutely breathtaking, the 3D art style immersing players into a world they otherwise wouldn't have known existed.  It's so realistic it gives people a chance to learn about sea life without having to really leave their homes or do extensive research.  The depths are impressive, and the way all the sea life interacts with one another is true to their behaviors.The music also was very gentle and added to the game without being overpowering.  Sure the music gave suspense or added wonder to the game, but you also had a choice as to what you could listen to while back in the Pod.  I enjoyed the subtleness of the music itself and really enjoyed being able to listen to it while I explored around.  My favorite part of the game are the videos that are added in giving real-life stories about the same things we are exploring  in-game.  Learning about the teams that do the same things makes a more personal connection and brings the actual research closer to home.  This game is a marvel with how much research and information went into creating it.  From the information about each species of animal in the game to the videos, to the environment everything lives in...  It's crafted so well that it makes you feel like you are the one doing the research and swimming around.  It was such a convincing and wonderful game that it has absolutely made me wonder if I want to get more involved in more things like this.Even though I have finished the game, I do plan on keeping this installed simply so I can do more exploring and so that I can use the information table in-game as a way to do art studies on sea life.  This is such a wonderful resource that I can't help but take advantage of something so masterfully created.Please, I highly recommend playing this game if only to see the sea creatures and how well they are created to work here.  It was worth every penny that I had spent to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say this enough - We really need more games like Beyond Blue! Not only is it very educational (I've learned loads), the game is absolutely breathtaking to behold! From the incredibly detailed sea creatures to the well-sculpted coral reefs, it's very obvious that this game is a labour of love. Plus, you can swim alongside some of the coolest and most majestic sea creatures around - my favourite is definitely the orcas (and yes, I was influenced by Free Willy). Seriously, what's not to love? The story here is pretty decent too. Besides the main storyline that's linked to the family of sperm whales the protagonist, Mirai, is tracking, the game also lets you explore the relationship between Mirai and her sister, Ren, as well as the pain of slowly losing someone she looked up to and loved to . Full playthroughP/S: The crackling sound at the beginning isn't a fluke. You'll quickly find out what it actually is :)+ Gorgeous graphics, excellent voice acting, and most importantly authentic sounds and animations of various undersea creatures. Several of the OSTs are truly fantastic too, including the demo track. Though, I'd like to point out that only certain creatures will react more noticeably to your presence... mostly fishes. There were times when I basically swam right into a dolphin and the dolphin didn't even veer away from me :P+ Educational. Lots of detailed info about each species you encounter that you can read all about when you're back in the sub. The game even includes clips from the Blue Planet 2 documentary by BBC+ Free roam mode. Will be unlocked after you've completed the game once.+ Lots of stuff to scan and lots to explore. This aspect of the game strongly reminds me of . + Characters are well-fleshed out and they feel relatable.+ No hardcore puzzles that impede the story. It's basically a walking... ahem, diving simulator with some relatively easy "find stuff to scan or put a tracker on"-style mini-puzzles.+ Great story, plus there are some dialogue choices that you can make, but I'm not sure if these choices "matter", as in will alter what sort of ending you get.+ Smooth controls+ Great for kids! After all, gamifying education is the way to go! + Bonus point for having an achievement that gives a nod to Douglas Adams :)- Not sure if the story's different depending on my choices, but it seems like the game simply shrugs off the (no spoilers) "other option" after you picked one incident to focus on. - If you look at the playtime-vs-cost ratio, even if you're the sort to 100% any game, this game is still a bit more on the expensive side. - There's a typo (the text is slightly mismatched with the audio); and a bugged quest that was auto-completed but the quest marker was still there.- Please add more places/scenarios for us to play and explore? They can be added as a paid or free DLC.I went into the game expecting a -level (story-wise) narrative-driven diving simulator and I wasn't disappointed. Besides having smooth controls, the storytelling is amazing here and it's well-fleshed out by quality voice acting, graphics, and actual (and educational) facts. The game is perfect for kids to play too! In fact, I honestly think that Beyond Blue is the sort of game that'll inspire a whole new generation of marine biologists, conservation scientists, and other related professions if more kids/teens are encouraged to play this game. But of course, for the rest of us, we can take this game as an inspiration to start/continue to do our parts, and take heart that there are incredible people out there doing great work to help preserve the world for our future generations.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is a sandbox game on the smaller side, closer to an educational tool more than a game. There is, of course, a story mode included: it's pretty short, but provides an overall touching experience in the end. After the completion of the story mode, all the areas previously featured will become once more available to freely explore for either enjoyment or achievements. Even at the very end, the game never becomes boring, just extremely relaxing. The gameplay is smooth and very simple, while animations, models and environments are realistic and very well made. It additionally provides a great photo mode, and bunch of short extra documentaries that, as someone with a deep fascination for the ocean, I personally found very interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually review games but here goes!I'd like to start with the fact I haven't finished the game yet but I'm a decent amount in to say some thoughts on it; I may update this once I do if I have more to add.I'll start off by saying I adore the cutscenes in this game the way they're styled is beautiful and they really get you into the mood to explore. Not only that, but they do bring out a few emotions which is probably helped by the great voice acting and music. I also enjoy the way the characters act with eachother it gives they some clear dimension and feels like they do actually know eachother.The gameplay itself is about what I expected. My interest in this game spurred from the fact I was a big fan of the wii game endless ocean and really wanted something that captured that same feeling. Traversing in this game is pleasant (I am using mouse and keyboard) one tap of the shift key and you're off at a nice pace while still being able to turn easily with the mouse, there's also a convenient quickturn (s), and you can seamlessly switch between scan mode mid swim without any slow down. When playing, you have a sizable set area (on of 8 I believe) to explore with some goals to complete which you can do straight away or explore a bit first. Though, you cannot backtrack until you finish story mode.My highlights of the game so far would have to be the creature interactions, the environmental story telling and the music. I also like some of the little touches like the suit lighting changing to match which light type you are using. The creatures are also very nicely animated.A few things I personally had a few issues with would be there's a school of fish in the third dive I believe which is super glitchy but I expect they'll patch that out you can still scan them they just act and look a bit funky and some of the menus would be easier to navigate if you could also use the mouse to navigate them but that's about it really.I will also note it doesn't seem to be the longest game (again I haven't finished it yet just noting from how far I'm in and what the game page itself says about the amount of dives) and I think most of the gametime comes from finding the creatures but if that's what you get the game for that's not really a problem it's a pretty cheap game and it's clearly had a lot of effort put into it and I personally think it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly amazing experience. The game is relatively short (got all the achievements in less than 5 hours) but quite unlike anything I've seen, especially considering the mix of exploration gameplay and documentary approach. _childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is a gorgeous game that extends more than just a diving simulator. The characters are surprisingly human and in-depth for a game where the main draw is the diving, I found myself getting emotional not only because of the beautiful visuals but because of the characters as well. This game scratches the itch I had for a game that was educational and touched on environmental issues, a very niche type of game that Beyond Blue delivered on perfectly. There's a 'theatre' that has interviews with marine biologists that you can watch which gives you more context on what is going on within the game which I recommend checking out, not only for the achievement but also to learn some more about what Beyond Blue is telling you. If you love the ocean and want to enjoy an amazing atmosphere this is the game for you. While I found the story engaging I can understand those who did not, don't worry even when in areas where you have an objective you are completely free to swim around and enjoy the reef without the game nagging you to continue the story besides to unlock new areas.This is not only a game, it's an experience. Also I want to live in that sub that Mirai lives in please make that real
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Short and bittersweet, with a greater focus on education than plot. Don't go into this one expecting an engaging game so much as an atmospheric documentary. If all you're looking for is to chill with marine life and learn a bit along with it, I'd say the $20 isn't that bad, but if you're on the fence or hoping for something more, then wait for discounts.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game. Besides the fact that you get to dive with large, wonderful cetaceans and giant squid, it's also good to see a game related to ocean exploration that isn't technically a horror game. My only problems with this game are that it didn't run very well on the computer I played it on and it is very short, the only thing one can really do after beating the game is try to scan more fauna, not there's anything wrong with that.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing and visually pleasing. You spend most of the time just scanning animals and exploring their habitats. The videos that are unlocked are great introductions to topics about the ocean, and watching them and having my character swim to/around the areas described only made my love for nature grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game has similar vibes to the endless ocean games, but it doesn't quite reach that yet. I feel like if the actors weren't so cheesy, (or if the characters had more time to develop!) it'd be an even better game. But yeah, this game makes my little marine biologist heart happy :) I also love that it is so scientifically accurate.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: if you're looking for an INCREDIBLE ocean game, then this is for you. its a short game but trust me, it's worth playing! the storyline is amazing, the mechanics are excellent, the graphics are exquisite and after you finish the story, you can still choose to explore different maps! the meaning behind it is gorgeous and really tells you the ocean is important. It's also informative and teaches you new things. i've already finished the game but trust me again, it's worth your while.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:I was after some Endless Ocean nostalgia, and this game did a really good job in that regard.Visually beautiful and atmospheric, the artists clearly paid a lot of attention to the 3D models.Cons:It's a very short game, could complete in a couple of hours. Limited replayability. Story feels a bit rushed and unclear.There's a very limited number of things to do compared to something like Endless Ocean. _childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful experience of the ocean and its life. The story around the sperm whales and Mirai's connection to them was very touching, especially towards the end. The graphics are stunning, as well as the soundtrack. Just a little heads up: turn down the sub music in the options or it'll blow your ear.All in all, a very enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to play this game since it’s been uploaded to Steam. I saw it in my recommendations list “similar to Subnautica”, but I would prefer not to compare them, as Subnatica has different goals, graphics, etc.As for the positive aspects of the game – there are quite a lot of them. Firstly, the knowledge about the ocean you receive during playing #BeyondBlue game is amazing. There are some videos uploaded, which tell about the discovery of the #Pacific and show marvelous video pieces of #underwater wildlife. People, who worked on the discovery projects, also tell the players about their progress in these video interviews. It is very convenient that the videos become available only after passing particular missions, so you are not able to make a spoiler for yourself. It is obvious that the game has a lot of educational materials in it and you should definitely try it if you want to discover the ocean to yourself. ;)Secondly, the whole game is based on the realistic exploration of the rich underwater flora and fauna. The graphic designers definitely did their best.  It is very interesting to swim for the Marai character, who has cool gear, and scan objects, which surround you. There are plenty of different fish or animals, which don’t scare you, so you can enjoy their presence peacefully swimming around. As for the characters: as I got the game, they have their real life prototypes and they are shown to us in the videos (but I can be mistaken for sure).Thirdly, the game brings up such a serious problem as the #pollution of the ocean. I personally think, that it is a really enormous problem of the world and humanity on the whole, and this is very appreciative that the game developers try to show this, using plastic litter left in particular parts of the bottom. A little spoiler alert: in the end of the game its creators give us the information on the #OceanX development and progress and offer the players to join this amazing and very useful project.But nothing is perfect, so here are some negative things :-	For me particularly the translation is important, because I don’t know some of the words divers use, but the translation does not work properly all the time.-	It is a pity, that the territory of exploration is strictly limited and you can’t even peak out of the water. The range of the fish is impressive, but still, there are not so many of them.-	The whole story is quite short. I managed to pass it playing slowly and detecting everything and watching all the videos in only 4 hours. It would be better if it was longer or there was some of them.-	You can’t experience the #oceanlife for real, because nothing harms you at all.-	There are only three locations available to swim in. I guess, it would be better, if we had an opportunity to swim around the certain part of an ocean, rather than 3 small areas, right?Whatever, I really recommend the game and believe, that the work of the developers won’t be to no purpose and many people will #getinvolved in cleaning the ocean to help it survive.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Max. 2 hours of gameplay, consisting of looking at some fish/whales and swimming to objective markers, accompanied by a boring story that just ends without a resolve. The environments are very restricted with barely any interactivity.Technical issues - Some fish appear invisible, and trying to view the insight videos crashes the game and makes PC slow.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: It is one of those rare gems which you can play after a long day at work with your legs outstretched. Serene underwater environments with soothing ambient music fill the room you are playing in. Top notch vice acting with some human drama sprinkled like salt on dish, makes it worth playing, even though the objectives are a quite repetitive. But the end of the game, you'll regret completing it because there's a message this game tells us, of the damage we humans do to our oceans.To see my detailed review follow this link
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed every single minute of this game. It's a shame it's so short but in my opinion it is worth the money. The gameplay itself is amazing. I would've loved to learn more about the ocean in this game. The little cutscenes and the videos you can watch about the scientists are so interesting. _childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful and informative game. I love how it has mini documentaries between each story chapter. There was so much love put into this game. And the geological formations and activity were stunning to look at.Sadly, it left me wanting more. With only a select number of ocean creature to scan and with the main character able to maintain a constant fast swimming speed, it felt like a just a cup of the ocean. I can only hope this game inspires a more fleshed out experience as it inspires a more consciences society.

_childDocuments_.review: hm... not sure. its a console port and you feel it a lot.there is literally no gameplay after 3 hours, expect of "scanning" and a bit collecting.like a swimming simulator. but why rate it good, cause it has awesome graphics and a pretty nice atmosphere.the animals and animations are well done. the felling is great, so i cant give it a bad rating.but think twice before you get it. its just enjoy graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I was really digging this game. Swimming around scanning fish in beautiful environments is fun, and I liked the characterization through dialog and personal effects in the sub. And I loved the short videos you unlock; they genuinely got me thinking about things, and that's great.But as a game, it's pretty lackluster. It reminds me most of that game about Disneyland, where you're running around taking pictures and getting autographs. It's a fun activity, as far as that goes, and your mileage will depend on how compelling you find the setting. But Beyond Blue ground to a broken halt with a level where you're scanning hydrothermal vents with no map and very little direction. I ended up just swimming in circles through the most godawful boring environment in the whole game. There are next to no animals, it's just a rock maze, and everywhere I went, I'd already been there I tried to make a paper map, but I still got lost. You may play this and luck right through it, but woe betide the player who misses one in some corner.After coming back to the same broken drone a dozen times, I gave up. And since this is a linear experience, that means the whole game is hosed.This could be an amazing experience for what it is, but for me it was absolutely broken by terrible level design.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: The story line is not finished.It just abruptly ends. Like, maybe 2 hours of gameplay.It just feels like there was so much left out. I really believe this should have been put out as an early access game where they could have developed each dive episode further and put out one at a time as they were completed.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it! _childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Had it been a $80 game. I'd be upset. But for $22, it's wonderful. Scanning all the life is a bit tedious but this game is an educational joy ride, along with some of the best soundtrack in a game. It's not as well put as something like Endless Ocean but again, that's a full retail game. Really happy with it so far and I am looking forward to the deep sea elements. Throw on some headphones and explore the ocean! Huge ups to the developers for not making an action packed ocean game that will scare the life out of kids but a game to scratch the curiosity itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games of all time was Endless Ocean - and this game comes close to that experience! It took me about 3 hours to complete the main story - but a "free dive" mode unlocks after the story ends which enables the player to revisit the locales to study the marine life further.  I spent $20 on the game and felt it was definitely worth that!  There are no timers, no damage - just diving and exploring  - learning about marine life as well as the characters in the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely won't appeal to everyone but I very much enjoyed my time with it. It's definitely more about capturing the awe and experience of being in these underwater locations rather than the gameplay itself. That may sound lame to some, but to others this is will be a very refreshing gaming experience. $20 is a reasonable price for what's on offer here, though I admit I would have loved to see what a completely fleshed out $60 version of this concept would have been like.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Informative : 100% in 4.5h, taking time to read and learn. This is what this game is about : educate. A pragmatic experience with facts and knowledge.  It won't fit gamers who search a open-world or an abstract experience. If you rushed the "campaign" in less than 2 hours and de-installed Beyond Blue, then you completely missed the point of this game.As far as I'm concerned, I was standing in awe about all that was provided during the playthrough. It has everything an ocean lover can ask : details on the ecosystem, short documentaries and, mostly, Dr. Sylvia Earle.Still hesitate about this game ? Just ask yourself one question : Do you think you know everything about the ocean ?
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure if I can even call this a game, as it's more an interactive short film. It's incredibly short, only taking 2 hours for me to play through entirely (not completing all the scans).The 'gameplay' of going around and scanning everything is fine, not terribly interesting or bad. It gets bad once you have to zoom scan and use those atrocious controls. What really kills this game for me is that inbetween already short dives, you spend about 5-10 minutes just listening to characters you don't give two ♥♥♥♥♥ about talk. The story is unengaging and has little to do with what you do in the game, your conversation options don't appear to impact the story at all, and the story just seems to be there to keep you away from swimming around. The one redeeming factor is that you can skip all the dialogue by spamming 'f'.Don't buy this game, 17 euros is FAR too much for what this is. If you can get it in a bundle or with some insane discount, it won't hurt to try as it's incredibly short.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Dude I've only played this game for half an hour and I'm enthralled. If you love the ocean, buy this game. If you like to learn, buy this game and watch the insights. If you love beautiful atmospheric games, buy this game. _childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not what I normally play but I would be lying if I said that i regret installing and playing it. This is an emotional rollercoaster of two stories combined into a game with beautiful graphics and sound that left me speechless at the end of it. It takes roundabout two hours if you focus mainly on the story, however there is a free dive mode so you can explore the beautiful underwater world. _childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a good experience marred by a few missed opportunities. My praise is as follows:1. Beautiful graphics, especially wildlife models and animations. 2. Intuitive gameplay, I never forgot how to control the game3. Clever, believable writing. Many games fall down in this area. 4. Good, thematically appropriate conservation message5. Many welcome video extras, cataloguing feature, bonus songs, etc.Now, the downsides:1. You cannot drive the sub. It's just a mission hub/3d menu basically, and it's cramped for that.2. No habitat. This might make for a cool DLC or sequel feature in partnership with Fabien Cousteau's Proteus project and would alleviate the cramped feeling of using the sub as the between-level hub area3. Repetitive, simple gameplay loop which is only expanded upon twice in the game (zoom scanning, UV/red lights)4. Inaccuracies in an otherwise scientifically focused game, like the deep water ADS looking identical to the normal wetsuit and no nitrogen saturation mechanic, which would have been a good opportunity to teach players about dive tablesHow to improve for a DLC or sequel:Let us drive the sub. Let us dock the sub to a habitat where the wet lab and menu items are. Greater mission variety like scanning seafloor to make maps, setting up biorock accretion structures, building artificial reefs from debris, retrieving lost artifacts from shipwrecks, possibly flooded cities in a post sea rise world, etc. If there is deep water diving please use an actual atmospheric diving exoskeleton. Also please include a first person mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adored this experience. As a Marine Biology graduate I knew i was going to feel passionate about this from an admitted bias, however i didnt fully expect this to be a gripping experience as it was.  Exploring the world beneath the surface is breathtaking enough but its captured so masterfully by development team that it truly feels alive. The story is loose but it does show the obsession and attachment that researchers have for the animals they are studying. The educational videos are eccentric and needed to educate the players on the conservation of our oceans and wildlife. Absolutely surreal experience. Only con i could make is the price tag does not match the game length if that is something thats important to you.  If you price off the experience, the tag is worth it.  If you also look at this from the charity aspect, as i assume the proceeds benefit the research in the game, it is also worth it.Overall: solid 9/10 would recommend

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely not for everyone however I really enjoyed the whole experience.The story is on the short side however the presentation is fantastic. Voice Acting, Sounds, Music, Graphics, they all add up to a very believable diving simulation. I wish the play area was larger and there was more to discover under the water but I cant fault any of what is already here. I can see myself returning to this just to swim with dolphins or simply as a chilled out experience. There is also an educational side to the experience including a number of documentaries that cover the discoveries during the story.I honestly feel like we need more calm experiences like this and I am grateful to the developer for what they tried to do with this title.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: As someone currently studying marine life, I was impressed with the use of UV and red lights during dives along with some relevant scientific details of the animals. Another great aspect are the models of the organisms which are detailed and animated beautifully! However, I was a little disappointed with the amount of species present in the game and the size of each location. Bottom line, if you're looking for something akin to the endless ocean games, this isn't quite it, but may be worth a few hours of enjoyment if on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Allow me to brief you before you purchase this game. You shouldn't expect Endless Ocean levels of freedom. With that being said, let us carry on to the meat of the game.Now I have only played a few hours of it thus far, taking my time from navigating towards the Cetacean calls in order to fully maximize what is essentially your oceanic Pokedex, and by god it's relaxing.You shouldn't expect in-depth gameplay when it comes to this game, but it is an enjoyable experience, especially if you have an affinity towards the ocean. The amount of research that this team has gone through is insane, from realistic movement and behavior of fish and mammals to even normal ocean physics and the like. It is a game that is short, yes, I would compare it to what I have heard about "Firewatch," so please keep that in mind.Now I will admit, I have a hard-on for marine inverts, so only seeing Octopus, Squid, and Jellyfish be represented here was a bit of a letdown. Hell, even taking water samples and bringing them back to the submarine to analyze on a microscope would have been a cool and unforseen addition in which the player could go as far to examine phyto- and zooplankton, or even larval forms of larger sea creatures. There is so much untapped potential in an oceanic exploratory game that the team can totally capitalize upon with either paid-DLC or free content updates in the future with minor story additions to a very developed set of characters. And by God, this is only scraping the surface. The music in this game is phenomenal and adds so much to the atmosphere. Diving in the ocean and having mellow tones fading in and out is beautifully idyllic, and when you're back on the sub jamming out to licensed songs, it's a fun time and a half with that. ♥♥♥♥ man, this game isn't for everyone. If you're expecting to relive your days of Endless Ocean, you can go back to that. But if you're looking for a new, surreal experience, if you're looking for something to let you learn even more about the ocean that goes as far to show you what developments have happened in the world of marine research since that time, or even if you're looking for a game you can kick back and down within a few hours, and feel refreshed and fulfilled, this is your game right here. I highly recommend getting this game to anyone who wants something new and unexpected.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

As a scientist with deep concerns about environmental issues, this quite is really powerful to me: “The science has always lagged behind the industrialization. I would like, for once, to see the science ahead of the industrialization, and have the science define the limits of the industrialization.”

_childDocuments_.review: I myself don't have a strong personal connection to the ocean. However when I saw this game after getting it from Jingle Jam 2023 I knew I had to play this. The game itself looks absolutely beautiful and lets you explore many fascinating areas of the ocean. The amount of different areas and living creatures that you can explore and find in the game is quite good, but I would always love to see more. The story of the game is quite short but you can explore freely afterwards so if you think you missed something you can always go back and explore some more. And that is what the game is mostly about, exploring the ocean and learning about it. And if you want to learn even more the game provides you with short documentary videos about the ocean and how it affects us. One small issue I have with the game is the controls, they are a bit strange but easy to get used to as they aren't too complicated. Over all a 9.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

Then there's the completely unnecessary depressing melodrama of a story that involves you listening to unskippable phone calls with characters you don't know or care about. This is followed by the love it or hate it music, I personally hate the trying too hard to be indy music style. I was really looking forward to this game based on the trailer but it's a let down for me.

I would absolutely pay for a DLC for this game.  Like there are so many more oceanic biomes to explore!  Please Please Please, More DLC! I love this game and I can't wait to see it grow!

The story was sweet and at times heart warming and wrenching. Was this |_| close to tears near the end haha! The models are fantastic and the videos were very interesting to watch and added to the story. The soundtrack is GREAT and I added it to my playlist to listen to.
