_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive fan of Endless Ocean, I saw this game and immediately knew I needed to play it. 10hrs later I have 100%'d the game and starting a new one. It's a smaller game, but the story is compelling (I cried) and the graphics are stunning. I adored the 'science' aspect, the videos and codex's they included. _childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I wish there was a neutral option for recommending. It's an easy 6hr or less game, it's very chill, it's very pretty, the controls are smooth, music was beautiful (soundtrack on the sub was hit and miss), however I wish there was just something... *more* to it. Just a little something more. There's no repercussions for anything, there's no danger anywhere. I wish the developers had delved more into ocean mining both in game and in video explanation, included more impactful and environmental issues/awareness in videos about what humans are doing to the planet. I also miss all the in-depth animal facts and information that I remember seeing in the PAX demos. Overall: There was a lot in this game that I liked, a lot of little issues or things I wish were included, but weren't, and I wish there was more to do. I've been excited for Beyond Blue to be released since PAX West 2019, I'm happy it's out, I'm happy I have it, but it really is a one and done game. I've played it 100% in one sitting and there's kind of no reason to go back.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t enjoy being harsh with indie games, but here I will have to offer up criticism I wish I had read before purchasing this game. I had been hoping for something along the lines of ABZÛ (which is a fantastic game), but that’s not what I found here. This game doesn’t have a full story, it doesn’t have a well-written plot, it doesn’t have very likable characters (mostly because they aren’t given the chance to really develop), it doesn’t have any interesting mechanics, and it doesn’t have a stellar soundtrack (though some of the tracks are astonishingly good, the soundtrack as a whole is a mixed bag). Where the game shines is in the visual department: it can be gorgeous. Unfortunately, it doesn’t exploit this; the play area for each chapter (or “dive”) is so small or sparse that exploration is short-lived. Some of the monologue/dialogue rubbed me the wrong way. The zoom-scan controls were the only part of the gameplay I found frustrating: they are inexcusably bad. The game itself was shorter than I was expecting (and I took my sweet time with it), but by the end I was relieved it was over with. Even setting aside the bugs I encountered in my short time with it (including an odd infinite loading screen error when attempting to ‘continue’ my game), it provided an unsatisfying experience. It didn’t feel like art for art’s sake – it felt distinctly preachy in its tone and presentation. There’s nothing wrong with preaching, of course, but there’s a reason the Lord of the Rings will always be better than The Chronicles of Narnia, and I’m convinced the writers behind this game don’t appreciate the distinction.My overall impression is that this game was a missed opportunity. If this game had cost below $5.00 all of the elements I just criticized would have been much more excusable, but at the listed price I cannot recommend this game to anybody.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: I cried at least 3 times during during my play through. It's a beautiful story that will pull on your heartstrings in several ways. The visuals are stunning, and as someone who really doesn't and probably never will have the opportunity to dive with them, getting to spend some time underwater with these magnificent creatures was surreal. The theme also moved me to adopt a whale, so I'll be doing that. :D

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! Highly recommend for anyone that loves and/or is curious about the ocean. - Peaceful. There are no dangers. _childDocuments_.review: At its core, Beyond Blue is an educational tool. However, by hiding the obvious learning material behind a more human narrative, these teaching moments are made to be sought out instead of forced on its audience. The story being told to distract from the sea life lessons waiting under its surface is strangely insignificant and complex at the same time. You play as a diver with a clear backstory, an equally clear motivation, and more complicated trouble in her life outside of the ocean. Her two colleagues butt heads for reasons that do get spelled out by the end, but are only resolved as much as you would expect to be in the span of a single research project. And yet, even with the personalized playlist and all the small trinkets scattered around the sub changing between missions, the characters remain perfectly ignorable. Beyond Blue keeps the focus where it should be, what the field it's trying to portray is about, exploration. Everything, including the information the game hopes to teach, is up to you to discover.

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite simply a game that is forced to live up to the expectations of another earlier game (Abzu), and while it clearly has a lot of work put into it; it fundamentally falls flat for a number of reasons.Chief of which to me is simple pacing. In Abzu, the game takes its time. The first level doesn't have any big animals, the biggest is a grouper about the same size as your diver. It doesn't start throwing whales at you until about the middle of the game; and in the late game there's a level that's an absolute curveball which simply should not be spoiled. Here, it goes straight for sperm whales. After that, what is really left to wow a player? What else am I going to find? Megalodon? Given the eco-documentary-inspired plot, I think that's going to be highly unlikely. So basically, if you've played the first level you've played the game. It's about whales. You follow whales to various locations full of fish. That's it as far as presentation goes, and it could have easily been avoided by making the whales something you're tracking but never quite find until the late game; so by the time you see them then they can really be impressive.Worse is the gameplay. This game bills itself as an 'underwater exploration game'. It's not, it's a scavenger hunt game. You go around the map scanning various species. One after another, until there is no more left to scan. That's the gameplay loop. And the animals themselves are pretty passive. They don't hunt one another, like in Abzu, and you can't ride them, like in Abzu. Sometimes there are scripted "scan this creature extra hard" sequences, but that's actually more boring than scanning them normally. It took only five minutes in the first level before I stopped caring about anything around me and just scanned it as I passed without a thought. My experience in Abzu was filled with far more wonder and watching, because there was activity to actually watch and I wasn't encouraged to only care about scanning for data.If Abzu hadn't given me various preconceptions, this wouldn't feel like ash in my mouth. The visuals are stunning. While some other reviews complain the levels are too small, I think they're about the right size. If you liked Endless Ocean and Abzu, and absolutely must have new content - sure, buy this when it's on sale. But you could just play Abzu...I think this is a good first run for the developers. If they want to go back and add more interactivity - both from the player and between animals in the environment - I think this game would shift to a recommend. It's not the worst thing in the world - a sold 6/10 - but I've played so much better and was hoping this game would have learned from its predecessor rather than started from square one.

_childDocuments_.review: So, back during the Wii days, there were this game called Endless Ocean. It didn't really get that much reception, but I quite liked the idea behind it. It's a scuba adventure game where the emphasis is on exploration and interacting with sea life, rather than the adrenaline rush that most games tend to go for. Well, here we are today with another game that tries to do exactly that, but this time I can actually play it on PC.This game was inspired by the BBC's award-winning Blue Planet II nature doc series, so if it wasn't already obvious, the focus is on giving players a realistic look at the ocean and the life that can be found within it. Although you certainly can find potentially dangerous species like sharks, they do not pose a threat, the game is purely exploration-based and you are never in any danger. I can see this turning away many players, but for this type of game it didn't really bother me.You're simply tasked with swimming around, scanning different species, and collecting samples, all while following a light narrative — it's a pretty relaxing experience overall. This is aided in part by the intuitive controls, I had absolute no issues getting right into the game and swimming around with ease, without even needing a tutorial. You're given a very brief tutorial on how to scan ocean life, but once that's done you're pretty much set loose.I immediately went about scanning everything I could see, with the game recording new species to my science log as I scanned them. In-between dives, you're able to use this science log to look at 3D models of any species that you've scanned, along with looking at their different animations depending on how many unique specimens you've found for each species. I was a bit disappointed to find that there's little in the way of actual info about each species outside of a few tidbits unlocked by playing. It would have been cool to see additional info regarding habitats, hunting patterns, rarity, etc. without having to hop outside of the game to google them. Outside of the science log, you also unlock mini documentaries called "insights", which aim to provide just a bit more info on certain topics relevant to the game.So the overall gameplay may be simple, but it isn't without cause — there is a narrative in place that drives the experience. You play as a diver in a small research team and the gameplay objectives reflect that. Whether that be placing a tracker on a group of whales or investigating a strange noise, there is at least some direction to the gameplay outside of just exploration. I won't say that the story is the highlight of the experience, but it's definitely not bad and it does a great job linking together the different dives without feeling like an interference.On the topic of the graphics, I gotta say I was actually pretty surprised. This game was originally developed for the Apple Arcade, so I was half-expecting some dumbed-down graphics as a result, only to find that that is not the case with Beyond Blue. The graphics are not mind-blowing by any means, but they're much better than what I was expecting. I didn't know what to expect with regards to the soundtrack, but they did a good job there as well, making the perfect complement to the relaxed gameplay.While the game may be a short experience at around 2 hours long, it's definitely worth the look, especially if you can catch it on sale. I had fun swimming around, scanning different species, and taking in the game's narrative, it was quite the relaxing experience if anything. And considering that it was developed for Apple Arcade, it doesn't even look that bad. If you're a fan of games like Endless Ocean or ABZÛ, it's a pretty easy recommendation.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is this: You dive around a small area and try to scan every animal around, working through the markings on a map, in order to complete your collection. Or you follow the apparently quite short story (usually takes 2h judging from playthrough-videos), doing the exact same thing except with pre-indicated animals and occasionally you press F to "interact" with something, while listening to poorly written dialogue.The graphics are fine but nothing special, I played ABZU earlier today and liked its stylised graphics far better. Certainly not "breathtaking" as some reviews suggest. Sound design is horrible, there is shallow music in the background and no ambient sound whatsoever. Very rarely you can hear some animal sounds (like clicking sounds from sperm whales or whale songs) but 99% of the time you swim around in utter silence.I don't agree with other reviewers saying the controls suck, I played with mouse and keyboard just fine.The overall quality-of-life in terms of HUD, menus and menu controls however is absolute garbage. There's no way to check your objectives, which led to me swimming up and down the area for a good twenty minutes while looking for a dolphin I thought I hadn't scanned until realising I had to swim to the dolphin marker and pick up a stick rather than search for dolphins like the marker would usually indicate. Controls inside the extremely unpolished, not to say disgustingly ugly, menus are counterintuitive and just a general pain in the ass.After just over 2h, I couldn't get myself to continue playing. I would have refunded far earlier, but I got the game through humble bundle, so no money wasted. I think my displayed game time is 0,1h though, which is probably because of the crashes I encountered which made the session not count into play-time. Which brings me to the next point:When I first started Beyond Blue, I started a new game, found myself in the starting position and looked around with the mouse for a few seconds. Then I pressed W to start swimming, which led to the game freezing and me back on the desktop. So I started it up again, pressed continue in the main menu and ... the menu disappeared, the menu background stayed, but nothing loaded. After 20sec I Alt-F4-ed, started the game again and pressed New Game, after which everything worked fine until I completed the first chapter and found myself in the submarine. After a bit of clicking around I figured out that the Log-thingies in the menu are supposed to be videoclips, so I pressed enter after clicking on it (why doesn't clicking on it start the video???), which should have started the clip, but really just froze the game and crashed it. At which point I uninstalled it and came here to leave a review.TLDR: Very shallow, bad menus, likes to crash - flabbergasted how it has "Very Positive" overall reviews!

_childDocuments_.review: The idea is awesome. Unfortunately, quoting one of the scientists from the included videos, it was made by old world apes who could never understand the ocean, so the execution is... Cringeworthy on EVERY SINGLE COUNT.I'll outline just a few here. Believe me, it's that bad on EVERYTHING ELSE, too:* The ocean in this game is not just dead. It is doubly dead, at the very least. Anyone who dived even once knows that both the euphotic and dysphotic zones are EXTREMELY alive. In this game, even subsurface is barren. The "population density" is about 1% of what it is for real. It's like running the Epic Battle Simulator with just one unit on each side.* It is doubly dead because NONE of the animals in it feel alive. Interaction? Forget it, they are just mechanical dolls, moving in a looped path, not reacting to anything. Even in the scripted sequences they don't feel any more alive.* The UI and controls have definitely been made not just by an old world ape, but by a wheelchair bound one, too. The map is strictly 2d no depth indicators, neither for the environment, nor for markers. The controls are at best 2.5 DoF. You can't roll over, you can't flip over, you can't do anything you do in the water.* The story is sprinkled with an abhorrent and totally unnecessary amount of personal and interpersonal drama. No, it does not make the characters feel more human or more alive. It could have worked in a different kind of a game, and in a different kind of a story, but here, it just makes you wanna puke.* The "livestream" facet (the team is livestreaming the dives in the plot) is done just as poorly. While in-game info hypes the stream as getting a million views early in, to a person who saw, or especially cast, any actual streams it feels more like it failed to take off the ground having just a few occasional stragglers at best.So yeah, it is a great Could Have Been.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a weak positive, but with some reservations. It kind of hurts I can't rave about this game as it should be right up my alley, but there's a few things about it which just didn't quite gel for me. Graphics: On the whole it's reasonably nice. The rendering could be better as they do have that plasticy 3D render look about them, but overall ok The movement of the diver is also pretty good.  Interactivity and reality: It's sad there's little interaction in this though. You just get bumped out of the way if you get too close to any of the creatures. Few things appear to react to your presence at all which really breaks the immersion for me. I'd expect fish to scatter, larger animals to move towards/away from you when noticed, jelly fish/particles in the water to get brushed out of the way etc.The animals don't react to each other either unless it's a "story mode" point. You have orcas peacefully swimming along side sharks and dolphins with zero reaction, predators swimming through schools of fish that just slide past each other. Turtles sitting in a static swarm of jelly fish etc.The "story" parts of the game in the water tend to be mini movie scenes where you watch what's happening rather than interact. Otherwise you kind of just place markers, collect samples (but don't actually test/investigate anything yourself) and scan. Having to repeat scan so many animals to get their info unlocked gets kind of annoying as it's not really interesting to do. Even in the sub, you can zoom in on books, notes etc, but you can't pick them up, make entries, read them etc. It's "just a game" but I kind of did a double take at the diver in a wetsuit, freediving fins, and no back up equipment swimming around on a rebreather at over 400m below the surface by themselves. (Nitpicky I know as it's just a story, but it is meant to be a reality type educational one. Just have to roll with it.) There were other little nit picks like comments about white tip reef sharks needng to remember that the player's character isn't on their dinner menu. (That species doesn't eat people, for an educational game it'd kind of be better not to reinforce the jaws stereotypes.) Or being surprised that a reef shark might try to make an opportunistic meal of an octopus (which they will.)Storyline and educational potential (they kind of go hand in hand in this game): The livestream aspect is a kind of nice touch as to why you're swimming about recording and talking to yourself.  Bit of a over obsession with cetaceans going on (which I understand, but can we also have some big reactions to other cool stuff like the sharks, sunfish, etc turning up? It's like, oh yeah, big school of hammerheads swimming past... and over there a whale shark... and a huge school of barracoota just cruised+... but I don't need to comment on any of that  at all... said no diver ever.)It has a conservation message which I can 100% support, but it hasn't done a great job at getting people invested. This game is likely preaching to the choir on this one, and we've all heard the (I'm assuming as I haven't finished the game yet) now cliched story of the nameless evil corporations plundering the seas for their greed before. (Yes I definitely know it happens, there's one they keep trying to put into place near me right now I'm really upset about (it'll almost certainly result in a major environmental disaster to an area that includes a whale nursery ground if they ever do it due to the conditions and remoteness), but most people will probably shrug it off as a "too big an issue for me".)  People know its bad. Most people are going to think it's too big an issue for them to do anything about (unless the devs are actively promoting where users of this game can find info on how to petition, donate to causes, buoycott companies etc that are pushing for drilling in sensitive areas. I mean how much more impact would this game have been if they focused on something like one of the animals we've been following being injured and having to be rescued or dying as a result of entanglement in plastic? (You see some of it littered in the game- reduce, reuse, recycle guys!) Or at least make some smaller but important and easily actionable on the part of the individual causes part of the thing they're talking about.  Anyway, I guess that part of the story is ok, but I also think it was a missed opportunity. Onto the less great. I have no idea why so many devs seem to think they need to shoehorn in totally unrelated family drama. Honestly, if I wanted to play a game that pulls me back into the real world where people I care about aren't getting along, are unwell, having personal life issues etc, I would do that.... Or just not log into a game and remain in the real world. I don't need someone else's imaginary life dramas on to of my own. This is a chance for me to check out for a while. This was sold as a game where you get to explore the amazing ocean. Why am I constantly discussing the medical trials my relatives are in, that the character's mother is dead (or moved out? Can't remember, didn't really care as I have no idea who she even is so no emotional investment there,) that my kid sister seems to be failing university, or any number of other dramas the peripheral characters seem to be having amongst themselves or their own families?There also needs to be a skip on some of the conversations. Some of them do drag a bit more than I'd like and you have to wait till they're done. There seems to be some docos in there that might be worth looking at. (Only seen one of them so far.)Sound: Voice acting is good. (I have no idea how they got the actress who played Delenn on this project, but it was nice to hear her voice acting in this.)Sounds in the ocean sequences are reasonable and not intrusive. I agree with one of the characters that I wasn't a fan of the music available in the sub which gets old quickly. You can mute it in the menu though thankfully if you just want quiet to hang out with the fish. Controls: I was using keyboard/mouse. It's ok if you're used to using WASD. Particularly when the drone is in action it can be annoying trying to get it to swing to exactly the right angle to scan a specific part of the animal it wants you to. Overall servicable. Bugs: Seem to have one where can't progress due to the UV light not turning off. If this can't be resolved it'll swing this review from a positive to negative as a game breaking bug. Edit: Game is actually a bit buggy in places. Had a load up and a continue bug that caused the game to freeze multiple times today, and seems like I'm not the only one. Only way around it is to get it to load to the main menu and then select an earlier save- so if you play this game, do save at least once per level if you don't want to be kicked back to the beginning if decides to bug out.Non-story mode? I don't know if you can unlock one, but this game desperately needs it. Just swim around the different environments, exploring the sites. Allow a single scan to bring up info on animal on command as you scan it if you like. No chatter with the other characters in the background. Overall?If you like ocean exploration games with an educational bent, you might ike this one, but it's kind of let down by some of the above issues. Might be still worth checking out, but wasn't what I was expecting to be honest. Some other recommendations for people who are playing this game:If you want pure education and spectacle- I'd sit down and watch BBC's blue planet which this game was apparently inspired by. If you want a (short) but very cool underwater VR experience I'd go with TheBlu.If you want to see an imaginary underwater world of wonder where you swim around and be amazed by all the creatures I'd look at Abzu. And you know, just get out there in the water if you're able to with a snorkle, take a freediving or scuba course and look around for real.

And this is the game i was looking for, A Quality story mode that does not make you feel restrained like idk, let s say Uncharted 4, while this being much much little in comparison to other underwater exploration games i played, it nailed exactly the points that i wanted to see. The story was super okay i didnt had nothing to complain about, and i loved the fact that i there was a radio and i could change the songs when i wanted to. The devs really thought every aspect of the game and it showed, They really built like they knew the mind of the player.  Other cool aspects: Real life underwater specimens, bonus educative videos, and also the fact that everything was built to suit the theme of the game. Astounding. 9.5/10 from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: It's a charming game with beautiful areas to explore. The animals are beautifully rendered and there's quite a bit of information given on the animals and biomes you get to visit. Three hours was plenty of time to finish the entire story, and while I enjoy swimming around in the biomes, I could understand that other people might feel left wanting. I know that I too would have really enjoyed more story and more exploration. I really liked the game, so I wish there was more of it. The conclusion to the story felt a little rushed. I enjoyed every bit of the story while it was going. The characters are well developed and it is nice to play a story that isn't incredibly dramatic. I think this game is also a great way for people who suffer from thalassophobia to try to face their fears if they want. Unlike games like Soma or Subnautica, you won't be jumpscared by anything. I don't have that phobia, but I can understand how the environment can feel frightening. I think this would be a good way to get some exposure if someone wants to do that, plus you get to learn some cool whale facts along the way. This game reminded me how much I wanted, and still want, to become a marine biologist.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is a beautiful game showing the beauty of the ocean and its inhabitants. It also reminds us, how important it is to protect the ocean from damaging human influence like plastic pollution. It is a love letter not only to the blue lung of our planet but also to scientists who devote their time and energy to the study of the sea in an effort to preserve this unique habitat.The game is not without its flaws. I couldn't get any of my controllers to work with the game and despite this issue being known for quite some time, it has not been fixed. One of the game's mechanics is controlling a drone to take samples from animals and the controls are a bit tricky to get used to. On top of that, some quality-of-life features are missing like the ability to re-bind controls.If you are willing to look past those flaws however, you will be able to experience the beauty of maritime life, listen to good voice acting and even learn interesting facts about various aspects of the ocean by unlocking short video clips featuring interviews with scientists. I'd definitely recommend this game to anybody who likes the ocean and/or wants to learn more about it.Getting all achievements wasn't hard, the only one that's a little tedious is to scan everything in the game but there is a hint system on the map, so it's not too hard to get it. I achieved 100 % completion in roughly 5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: It's clear that a lot of love and passion went into the development of this game. I just wish that it wasn't so short. There's so much more content that could have been squeezed out of this concept and the story. It feels unfinished. But it's also beautiful and enjoyable. I wouldn't get it if it isn't on sale, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game was awesome, 100% recommend!Pros:- Great voice acting that gets you engaged- Beautiful graphics- Had suspense to it and what felt like threats but turned out to be a risk free game which meant my 5 year old could play it and not be scared- Made for a great cause/very educationalCons- Too short of story play, I beat it and got all achievements in 5 hours, so I hope they do DLC for more game play and more educational material
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This was a beautiful game!! After experiencing some Subnautica and getting a bit afraid of the open waters, this game made me rethink how we should see the Oceans. Everybody that made this game, i am glad you did and that you spread out awareness and information about the oceans and the life that is in there.I suggest you play this, story is interesting, bioms are looking great and the immersion gives you what you would expect :D !
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: As my wife and I are both (cold water) divers (Advanced and Instructor) who dive around the globe to sooth our minds to be one with the ocean, this game sooth the mind with its atmospheric visuals and sounds. Although there is a little reverb missing, it does make you relaxed.This game is also in Dutch (text and subtitles) so it was easy for my wife to follow up on the story. (thank you devs for this)If you're looking for a relaxing game, want to learn a thing or two and want to love the ocean as we do, this game is for you.And remember,
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting this game to be a huge open world ocean game with a large main story then you're not gonna get what you're expecting. Beyond Blue is a beautiful and immersive ocean game with a small story that you could probably tackle in two hours. The soundtrack is heavily underrated and has many good songs like Only In My Dreams, Love That Never, and Tangaroa Whakamautai! The game is a mix of a cozy, relaxing ocean game, but also an educational video game too! If you want to learn more about our planet's ocean and the creatures that inhabit it, then Beyond Blue is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up I used to play a game called Endless Ocean on the Wii which feels similar to this short scuba game where you swim around in ocean environments scanning creatures, such a nostalgia trip.The big issues I had is controls for keyboard is horrible so highly recommend you play using a controller. I played it on the steam deck and it works fine but the ocean insight videos don’t work with Linux. You can just watch them all later by opening up your save on PC when you finish the game, the video cutscenes are just a repeat of the in game cutscene you saw on your dive so don’t think your missing something important.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Best game ever! 'Beyond Blue' is insane, perfectly blending entertainment with education. The graphics are stunning, and the soundtrack is wonderfully immersive, enhancing the overall experience. I especially appreciate the educational aspect of the game, which provides accurate and fascinating information about whales and other marine life. The game makes you appreciate the beauty of our oceans even more. I need 'Beyond Blue 2', please make it happen !!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! It had amazing humor and was very informational and even tugged at your heartstrings in the story. I highly recommend! _childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. As many reviews have said, go into this with proper expectations: this ins't intensive from the gaming perspective but it is a love letter to oceans and whales. But obviously a labor of love for the subject.I found this game when I started to take scuba classes and wanted to see if there was anything in the same vein. _childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Although Beyond Blue’s ocean doesn’t compare to the real thing, the instances it does try to emulate for our enjoyment are truly fascinating. The team would have had an uphill climb trying to program a perfect emulation of the vast ocean and all the life beneath the waves. However, the focus on the whales and the few shark species that acted realistically was breathtaking.It may have been on a small “unrealistic” scale but realistically the developers focused on delivering the best moments possible with the whales and other encounters that fit with the narrative, over focusing on the whole wide ocean. I think this made the game feel a lot more personal. Mirai was hyper focused on the whales and that’s what we saw the majority of. I like to think that we just saw the ocean through Mirai’s view. Also, I just love ocean wildlife so any game that can emulate that ecosystem, even in just a small way, will always have my attention.Overall Rating: 8 – Very Good!Platform Played On: Steam DeckRecommendation: YesFull Review -
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I think it's very important to know what to expect heading into Beyond Blue. It is very much a game designed around educating the player in marine life and how scientists study and learn about the ocean and the wildlife that call it home. It's not a survival game, or even an exploration game really. Yes there are open areas to explore, but that is not where this game really shines, or what the main focus of the game is. If you go into the game expecting it to be an educational tool, with simplistic but relaxing gameplay that rewards the player for taking the time to engage with all aspects of the game, then you will enjoy your time with Beyond Blue and learn a lot. If you go into it expecting it to be a game with a super engaging or thought provoking story, or with super big open areas to explore, you will be disappointed. Beyond Blue features a "campaign" of sorts consisting of 8 dives. Each one only takes about 10-15 minutes long and are connected by a story. This story is fine for what the game is trying to be, and the ending of it was actually a little bit emotional. Throughout these dives you explore a few different ocean environments, all of which felt surprisingly unique which I wasn't expecting. The types of fish you can scan and encounter vary slightly from region to region.The swimming controls worked really well I think. I didn't feel myself struggling against them at all, and they were really easy to learn. It's also easy to switch between scan mode and regular mode. Scan mode just allows you to scan a fish you're looking at which worked super well with no issues for me. Scanning fish unlocks additional  information about them that you can read on your sub which acts as the hub for in between dives. The sub is actually super cool. There's big open windows where you can see the fish swimming by, and there's a really cool soundtrack that you can listen to and pick your favorite songs to play. I found myself spending a surprising amount of time just relaxing here between dives, reading about the fish, and watching the mini documentary style videos that you unlock. These provide a really cool insight to the world of marine biology that I found genuinely interesting. When you finish the 8 dives, you unlock a free roam mode which allows you to clean up scanning any fish you might have missed, as well as just further exploring the environments. I found this to be really cool, and a nice way to get some more playtime from the game. The campaign only takes 2-3 hours to finish depending on how long you take. This makes justifying buying the game at full price a little difficult but I think getting it on sale if you like what you've read so far is fair. Overall, I really enjoyed my time with Beyond Blue. I think it's not only a really relaxing game, but one that you can genuinely learn something from, which is always cool. For more reviews, follow my

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet. Not really a game, more an interactive experience. You can tell this was made on a budget, as some little things here and there are a bit rough around the edges. On the other hand, the animations and visuals in general are well done, and the diving gameplay feels fluid enough. Be aware though that if you have Thalassophobia this game is likely going to trigger it.It's also fairly short. Grab it on a sale to get your money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: In a world where Subnautica didn't exist, this game might have been massive. Unfortunately, Subnautica does exist, and seems to do almost everything this game does, plus an absurd amount more.I completed the 1st dive (of 8), and the only gameplay was swimming to areas and pressing "A" or scanning fish. No challenge, no excitement, just meandering around scanning fish. I tried headbutting a shark to no avail.This game is evidently more story driven than other sea games, but the story elements are completely disjointed from the gameplay. Whilst the dive is mostly alone, with occasional voice comms, once it's over you end up in a tiny submarine, with a few voice calls to work through.Beyond Blue seems to emphasise conservationism, containing various interviews with real world ocean experts. It also has a bizarrely high profile voice cast:> Experience an evocative narrative with full voice cast - Anna Akana (YouTube), Mira Furlan (Lost, Babylon 5), Hakeem Kae-Kazim (Black Sails, Hotel Rwanda), and Ally Maki (Toy Story 4)The swimming movement is somewhat smooth, although navigating through tight spaces can be a little frustrating. I'd really recommend Subnautica instead, sorry!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely, science inspired journey throughout the ocean. The gameplay is simple and relaxing and the story well written, carrying a distinctly human touch whilst also shedding a light on the horrors humanity is imposing upon our world. Inspired by and including actual clips from Blue Planet II, it's a lovely way to consume this kind of media in a more engaging fashion.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. The controls were fluid and the environment was gorgeous! I hope we get suits like this in the future, would love to try them out.The banter between the characters was refreshing and felt quite realistic! _childDocuments_.review: This is a very relaxing exploration and mostly educational game. It has no violence or whatsoever, it is purely made to educate and spread awareness about our oceans and underwater life. It also brings the insight of the life of the scientist who risk their lives and also live two separate lives (family and undersea) which takes it's toll. Very emotional and realistic. Would be really awesome if all the books and things in the pod could be more interactive, like you could get a link to the book or smth? _childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is a visually stunning underwater adventure that combines breathtaking graphics, educational content, and a captivating narrative. Explore the depths of the ocean, encounter mesmerizing marine life, and learn about conservation efforts. Though it may be a bit short, the immersive gameplay make it a must-play. Prepare to be amazed by the beauty of the deep blue sea. 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Swimming around the different scenes and interacting with some of the animals is fun, but that's about where the fun stops. It seems like they ran out of budget or gave up on this game just when it was starting. Your character just gives up out of nowhere and it's not satisfying at all. It feels like all your hard work in the game leads up to absolutely nothing. Also, it's reaaaally slow-paced.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: First things first... if you are looking for action, shark attacks or any scary stuff, you'll be disappointed. It's completely absent in this game. What you are getting is more of an educational experience. You are following a quest-line that sends you to several dive spots where you observe and scan animals. The more animals you scan the more information you will get. This info can be viewed in the sub along with short videos of people who are actually in this field of work.Central to the story is a whale family and it's an amazing experience to swim alongside them. But the makers don't shy away from the fact that life is very harsh for them and the ocean needs to be protected.All in all you can tell that a lot of love went into game. I would certainly recommend it for anyone who is interested in swimming around in this beautiful environment and learning something along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: It is educational, but for that purpose watching an actual documentary would be both more effective and more engaging.There's barely any gameplay mechanics in Beyond Blue, but it consists of the following: you start a dive. The game gives you markers. You swim to them, then point your scanner to the required sea creature (whale, shark, etc.) and scan it by pressing and holding a button. That gives you some context + dialogue and let's you advance. The game, then, gives you new markers, and once you complete the mandatory scans the dive is over. You can explore each location and scan other animals, but there's no incentive to do that other than to appreciate the view.In-between dives, you can watch some mini-documentaries you unlocked. There are 16 of them, ranging from 1min30s to 2min30s each. I enjoyed them and recommend to check them out as you play as the game's plot draws some parallels to the real people that inspired it.Completing all 8 dives and watching all documentary pieces takes between 3h and 5h depending on how much you rush it. After completing the dives/story, you can return to the previous locations and explore some more, if you'd like.Beyond Blue looks nice and can be relaxing, but there's so little gameplay it can also feel like a chore.Play this if you can't get enough of underwater games and you don't dislike walking simulators in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to say whether Beyond Blue is a "game" in the traditional sense or not, but it's definitely an incredible experience. You can explore the ocean and scan the life around you at your leisure, basking in the calm of the sea and listening to a pretty chill soundtrack. No, there is not much action, and you get your hand held pretty much throughout the game (except for one section in the deep sea) but not every game out there needs action sequences. Like so much media centering around the sea, it puts heavy emphasis on whales - sperm and humpback whales, to be exact - which is a bit of a thorn in my side, but swimming around everywhere feels so smooth, fluid and fun, I can forgive it. There is a bit of a story with our main character Mirai, zold entirely through dialogue sequences with your coworkers and your sister Ren, but thd main focus is on making swimming in the sea as enjoyable and chill as it should be. If you're in any way into marine biology or have a love for the ocean in general, you should definitely get this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game as a part of the Humble Bundle last summer, looking for something atmospheric and water-related to get in the summer mood. If you like sea creatures, conservation, and collection-based games (and I do!) this one is for you. TLDR: Beautiful game, zen ocean vibes, fabulous message and educational payout, but shorter than expected. Get it when it's on sale.PROs: - Beautiful, diverse, atmospheric environments and accurate, well-styled animations. You see coastal, open ocean, and deep ocean biomes and the animal animations feel really authentic. - Simple mechanics and easy-to-follow story--great when you're craving some zen or winding down. - Conservation-focused. There are excerpts from the Blue Planet II documentary that are both informative and a nice break from the "scan all the things" gameplay. The story also provides valuable insight to how scientists observe, track, and measure the health of the ocean. This would be a fabulous choice for any young ocean lovers in your family (or part time mermaids like me). CONS: - Short! I finished this game in about 4 hours--I was expecting a little more from the gameplay and story, which I didn't get, but given what this game ended up being, this was the right length. Any more and I think it would have been too repetitive to finish. - Some small rendering issues, mainly some groups of animals being stuck in terrain. - "Biodiversity." I expected to see more animals. We get a good smattering of fish, mammals, and sharks, but I found myself wishing there were more unique finds, and a more robust library of critters to scan.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game because I love Endless Ocean. So there I am poking some fish and next thing I know I'm in a sub looking at the legal papers of what I am assuming is a child custody battle and hitting on my boss in the middle of a zoom call. I... just wanted to float with the whales, guys. Thankfully you can actually turn the chattering California voices droning out of your radio off and do exactly that, so on that front the game is good and I'm recommending it because diving games are rarer than hen's teeth, but what a strange, jarring experience nonetheless. I've never been happier to see an audio slider. I want a diving game, not a midlife crisis simulator.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the main game and I would say overall, it is pretty decent. The storyline is about 3-5 hours depending on how quickly you make it through each of the 8 dives. The personal storyline for the protagonist is a bit... stilted, but that's not the true focus of the game. I love the storyline for the whales, and the graphics are fantastic. The little documentaries also really help you learn more. Overall, a relaxing, chill game, albeit short. I think it has fantastic potential for further development, such as expansions with more dive locations and storylines similar to that of the whales. Voice acting is pretty good but the sound went funky after I played awhile. Might have been my mid-tier gaming laptop getting too hot though, not the game's fault.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a nice, short game to play between longer titles or a good choice for something to play to relax. I love that the fish and other ocean life looks really good in the game making it feel more realistic and immersive to me, though I didn't always love the visibility especially in the open ocean where I got lost a few times in free play because I didn't have anything to help me figure out where I was in location to what I was looking for as far as whether I needed to swim higher or lower so that was a little frustrating, otherwise the game is very easy especially if you don't care about scanning everything and only care about completing the story. I was surprised to find the characters were realistic. While I didn't personally care about anything other than exploring the ocean and helping the ocean life, the character's personal lives in the story did add depth to the game. One of my favorite things though is the photo mode. I do animal and nature photography in real life so I love any chance I can get to use a "real" camera and photograph my environment and the creatures in it. I loved getting the chance to live my fantasy of photographing ocean life through this game as it's unlikely something I will ever have the opportunity to do in real life. I might actually return to this game in the future just to do some simulated ocean photography.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I must say, this beautiful game really suprised me in a very positive way! I didn't expect to learn so much about the ocean while having fun diving and seeing all the marine animals in such a good quality. They really put a lot of effort into this game - the very realistic background story, the diving experience (it is as if you're really out there!) and you still have some freedom to choose what the character is saying to its co-workers / what you want to do next. If you ever wanted to dive with wales, dolphins or wanted to work as a marine biologist, this game is made for you! PS: Please, after playing this game, make sure to tell as many people as possible how important it is to save our ocean.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This was an incredible experience to play it didn't feel like a game it felt like a journey through a different world a must have for any ocean lover. _childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting walking, or rather diving, simulator.Beautiful sceneries, great soundtrack, freedom to explore the ocean.Story is there, but it doesn't rush you in any way to progress, nor does it feel like it's forcing some stance upon the player. Instead it tries to educate. It feels more as if it was part of a documentary movie.Great way to mix educational aspects in and keep a charming and relaxing atmosphere.Cons:I can''t really think of any serious ones. The few minor ones- you can literally get blocked by even a tiny fish. It won't escape nor can you push it aside. They're like a concrete wall- drone controls could be improved a bit- some sharks temporary swim outside of accessible area in one zone while the game actually encourages to scan everything- not for people looking for action. You simply can't get hurt, nor have to worry about time. For me it wasn't a problem, but I assume some people may find it discouragingTo sum up a very pleasant experience. You explore the ocean at your own pace, learning some facts about it alongside the journey. Has some drawbacks, but they are all rather minor hindrances and have minimal effect on the overall feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game worth buying it?10/10 if you just like to dive around.09/10 for the story. It is a good, but short one. Kept straight forward/linear allthough this topic has some good potential for side quests.12/10 if you are a scuba diver and could not dive the past two years due to the pandemic.12/10 if you are looking for lightweight educational content08/10 for the graphics -> they are quite good nevertheless
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Truly breath taking, it feels like a real immersion in amazing locations of the sea. The animals in they're enviroment, playing, socializing... it's something hard to describe with words. Amazing job. I wish they are gonna make a sequel where we can discover more animals or some expansions to this one. Worth all the money! Truly amazing
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really short, and really relaxing. Has a lot of accurate depictions of different aquatic animals in their natural habitats :) Overall I really like it. Reminds me a lot of Endless Ocean, however it's not nearly as big and long as that game. I recommend getting this game while it's on offer.This next part of the review has slight spoilers, so if you want to go in blind then don't read on!This game also has some issues. The overworlds are absolutely beautiful and do a great job of depicting the species they have, however they at times feel very dull and empty. The very small amount of species actually in this game doesn't help with this at all, it would've been nice to be able to visit areas that have animals such as seals, eels, etc, as well as depicting more species of dolphins, sea turtles, rays, etc. In addition, the open ocean should've had birds that can swoop in the water near the surface imo. Of course geographical location should be taken into account with these things though, and what was actually added to the game isn't bad at all.I appreciate that they tried to cover serious topics in the main story, such as ocean pollution and species going extinct in specific areas because of it, however the cheesy dialogue and mediocre voice acting makes it hard to take it seriously at times. I do enjoy the format of them explaining things because they're making a podcast though!The side story with Mirai's family, and honestly all the phone calls in general, felt very unnecessary and didn't add anything to the game. Again, the dialogue and voice acting are very cheesy and although not bad by any means, it's not really great either.The game is also far too short for the emotional parts to have any actual impact, as by the time I felt I was getting to know the characters the game was already over.Overall, this game is very beautiful and does a good enough job at depicting ocean habitats and problems in preserving them, however it doesn't go that extra mile like the Endless Ocean games did to truly make it special.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game to any, ocean lovers, or just general nature. It is one of those stories that you want more of in life that warm your heart while silently breaking it, the only thing this game lacks of, for me is a DLC, or sequel. Even considering that it is short compared to games similar to it, it still makes for an amazing time playing. It has one of the best story lines that i have seen, and doesn't lack in any category that affects game-play. I truly hope that the game continues in some form one day but i don't think I've played a better game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This Game was recommended to me by a coworker and I really appreciate that!This Game is very beautiful and you get to swim with all Kinds of Ocean Life, I love the exploration in it and there is no jump scares. Its really hard to find an underwater game that doesnt include jump scares or scary things! The Graphics are beautiful the atmosphere is amazing and the Soundtrack is lovely. Overall this game is very relaxing and informative, so I can recommend it to anybody that loves animals and is somewhat eco orientated.However since this game is roughly 4 Hours long I recommend getting it on Sale!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first review I have ever written for anything. lol This game is just simply fun and makes learning fun. More games should bring this perfect amount of energy. I used to love the ocean growing up then I watched Jaws in 6th grade.However this game has changed my point of view on the ocean for a more positive outlook, whilst giving me MoH Frontline feel with the actual documentary clips in between segments. Already 4 hrs in and I've learned a ton about ocean.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing learning experience. Well-crafted dives with interesting information about ocean live and amazing ecosystems we just begin to understand. The scenario composition and free roaming gives peace of mind while the destiny of the observed species lets you think about how ignorant humans are. An interesting feeling to be floating peacefully through calm waters, while starting to worry about how we (mankind) are systematically destroying our oceans.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: There should be more games that educate people about nature, in this case the ocean. I have been watching documentaries my whole life so I knew what to expect. This game is beautiful and it does what it is supposed to do and that is to educate.Beautiful and  a sad game at the same time but everything in this game is well done. The story is interesting, the voice acting is solid, soundtrack is ok , good graphics (sometimes they are a little bit meh but doesn't really matter) .I would just like to say that the we (humans) are acting like we are god given , like we own this beautiful planet. Our obligation was to live in sync with our planet and we are destroying it and I really don't see if there is a way to save this planet when the global corporations own everything and everyone. To finish on a positive note, all these things don't mean that we should sit down and stop fighting for our planet, everyone can help in their own way.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game turned out really good. I got it in an Earth Day bundle and because the graphics looked amazing, I tried it. It did start out really slow and I wasn't really into it at first, but then decided to give it another try and immerse myself in the ocean. And what can I say! It turned out to be a lot of fun and I actually learned a lot of new things that I didn't know before. I loved the idea with the "Ocean Inside" videos that you unlock with every dive and can watch to get a more detailed insight. And the story actually became interesting. I could have done without the side story with Mirai's sister Ren though. It is still unclear to me what the purpose of that was. It feels unfinished. Like they were trying to go somewhere, but then decided otherwise halfthrough. The dialogues with her colleagues felt alright and in place, but the story with her sister and their grandmother felt forced and superficial, mainly because it served no purpose with regards to the actual story, or the theme of the game. Overall though, I definitely recommend playing it. The visuals alone are worth it and if you're into swimming, diving or ocean live, this game is definitely for you. It is a bit on the shorter side though. I explored and scanned everything and the game took me about 7 hours to 100% completion.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: A touching story, though lacking in some areas. The way characters were introduced and related their conflicts and backstories was interesting, and the story of the whales was well told. All that being said, I kind of wanted an Endless Ocean 3 and this isn't it. I think it was worth the money (on a 30% sale) but I came into it with the wrong mindset.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with Beyond Blue - I got it in the Humble Bundle - but here's what you should know.1. This is a gorgeous, relaxing diving game. But pretty much a walking simulator.2. The main point is education and awareness raising.3. The main mechanic of the game is scanning animals ala No Man's Sky. You follow markers, you scan.4. There is a story, but it's not that compelling. You follow a group of whales and there are a few minor complications. The two other characters disagree a bit. You have a sister taking care of an aging grandmother with dementia.5. Voice acting is fine.6. I finished the game in 3.8 hours.7. Worth it on sale if you're interested in marine biology or just want a stress free narrative experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is a very polished, very beautiful game where you learn more about underwater creatures and the impact humanity is having on them. If you like to nerd out about the ocean and all the creatures who live in it, this game is for you! learning about the ocean, learning about marine biology, Subnautica educational
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Are you looking to relax? Explore the ocean but you're poor like me? Well this is the game for you! Its BEAUTIFUL. The details are stunning and I learned way more about the ocean from this game than Animal Planet. My only complaint is that its pretty short. I wish the story for Mirai was more in depth.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this underwater experience. It's a mix between a documentary and a walking sim (only you're swimming). This is a great tool to share awareness of the changes happening in our oceans RIGHT NOW. I'm a bit sad to see some of the negative reviews here of people complaining there wasn't enough in this game. Maybe I came in knowing Beyond Blue was inspired by documentaries about our planet and it's an educational/awareness tool. I definitely wasn't disappointed. There are some very memorable moments in this game; not every game needs to be a survival or violent show.The designers did a fantastic job on every creature animation and model. Everything looks alive in the game. The different ecosystems/environments were fantastic to explore. You can view the in-game's iPad and watch the animations. There's real interviews you can watch about a handful of scientists trying to save our oceans. I do wish there was more information about each creature in the game. Maybe how they live and how they're affected by the climate.I would like to see more call-to-action in the game. You can visit the game's official website and visit their partners page. But I would like to have see something in the game about what can we do in our daily lives or what some of these organizations do to help.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and relaxing walking (actually swimming) simulator that lets you explore the ocean and deep sea. Lots of interesting animals to find and scan with some educational aspect to it like learning how they live and some other background. There are also some interesting real-life documentations in the game that are gradually unlocked while progressing through the story. Highly recommended if you are interested in the ocean or just a relaxing experience with beautiful graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is a Exploration, Documentary-based game where youswim aimlessly into nothing more beautiful than the ocean-it-selfand scan endlessly whilst swimming and breathing in a rebreatherthe surrounding sushi fauna.While I'm not gonna tell the entirety of the game without spoilingthe story, I can already spoil you one teeny-tiny bit of it:It is hard to really get into the story with the voice actors spittingout facts and theories about certain species of whales.I'm not so sure what's more annoying, the fact that the voiceacting is odd, or to deal with the drama andpersonal struggle within certain scenes.They both suck to be honest, it didn't hook me at all...Bad start I know, but:- was the feeling of literally swimming(and scanning) the surrounding beauties of the ocean.- are nice and all, not too much,not too much in your face but that's alright.Too much immersion can hurt the eyes after a while.- are whacky at first but you'll get used to it.Although now that I come to think of it...Nah, never mind, you'll do fine!- is not bad, but the interaction is not really there,just pretend, but I know from experience some just can't.- is very hard to get into like I said. It has itsmoments especially near the end, but yet again, I'm not spoiling.- is not what I expected in a good way.The main theme is fitting and my favorite, the music that's beingplayed in the submarine is a mixed bag. Most of them are bangers;, , , etcand others like  a nuisance,but do not let my matter of music taste be a judgement, othersmight have a different platter filled with their tasty riffs and beats.Overall very entertaining experience,very little care about the backstory of the characters,there's also photo mode which I haven't tried out yetmaybe i will in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Short game, finished in just over 2 hours. I'm a big ocean lover and conservation advocate so I had to play the game.Pros: great music, informative, nice story, visually pleasing.Cons: Drone is a bit clunky sometimes, some dialogue is snooze and seems irrelevant.Overall, nice short game. I got it in a humble bundle so it was worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Part game and part documentary, this is a must for any lovers of the ocean or marine biology. What an amazing experience. Educational and entertaining - a peek into the life of research on the sea. Great graphics, accurate models and entertaining to boot. I really appreciate the effort they took to maintain accuracy in all the marine life. A very well put-together project that I would highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Just like Never Alone, Beyond Blue has some opportunities to learn things about the real world. It's a super relaxing game with an interesting story. It's not very long but I had a great time. It's super easy to 100% if you want to take the time to going back and forth with the map to find all the scannable objects.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This two to four hour game has a lot of heart, but may be more or less enjoyable depending on how you play.  If you are interested in achievements, you'll find yourself swimming all over the map to scan the same fish over and over again.  I would've loved more narration during the fish scanning...maybe the voice actors stating facts about those fish as part of a conversation r something.  Speaking of voice acting...I thought it was excellent!  The music too!  In fact, this game has a lot of heart (and a definite message).  It is very pro-environment, but I did find it interesting to note the variation in the REASONS why the three main researchers were involved in the dives.  Lots of reasons to protect our oceans, I suspect.I got this as part of a bundle, and would have been disappointed at the current $20 price point.  However, depending on how much you think you'll enjoy poking around the ocean (while either pursuing a story, going from one spot to the next scanning fish, or just enjoying the scenery), you may find yourself willing to dish out $5-10.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly ran great. Very pretty and nice that there is no chance of danger.I didn't even use the map until after I beat the game. Would have saved a lot of scanning time, had I know the map primary purpose is to show unscanned animals. I scanned everything to find one glitched and unscannable fish. _childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Not as viscerally entertaining as Never Alone, this game is a relaxed exploration of the beauty of the ocean. The story is not really important, but swimming with the fishies is touching in a way. I encountered a few glitches I hope will be fixed soon (Continue crashing the game, models in the ocean not loading in...)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I've only just bought Beyond Blue and have not played it for very long, but my first impressions are very positive, it reminds me a little of World of Diving, or that should be, it reminds me of what WoD could have been if it wasn't abandoned several years ago in early-access. If you're looking for a fast-paced, action-packed game, this is probably not for you, but if you just want to relax, swim around and explore a beautiful underwater world for a few hours, then this is great. I will possibly edit this review in due course as I play more of the story and explore more of the dive sites but so far so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I know I haven't exactly lived in Game but I couldn't wait to recommend This one.
