_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever longed for something akin to Endless Ocean on the Wii and really like the science behind oceanography and marine life, this is definitely the game for you. Very calm and chill, with no time limits or suchlike (although there is story, you are allowed to wander where you wish, even in the more...corridor-esque areas), and you will not get hurt by anything (although I was jumpscared by a shark suddenly appearing right behind me at one point).If you're only here for the story, it's a very short affair, only about 4 hours, if that. The real meat of the game is honestly chilling in your environment and scanning the local wildlife (and occasionally other things) - the game wears its partnerships and science lean proudly on its sleeve, and whilst it's easy just to roll your eyes and ignore the little Insight video clips, I'd thoroughly recommend them. They're very information and interesting, and tie in very well with the technology and issues that are raised by the game - one of which, of course, is the effect of humans on our environment. There's a couple of issues with the game for me: Mirai (the character you will inhabit) controls a bit awkwardly inside the sub, and you can clearly see that time was more spent on her movements in water than in the sub (understandably). Her facial reactions to certain events can be...a little flat. There were also beautiful moments in which the immersion was jarred by models clipping into one another, which was a shame. Also, whilst the map does display where creatures are that haven't been scanned, the lack of a Z-axis can make finding little critters like comb jellyfish and especially spider crabs very annoying.Yet all in all, this game was lovely, scratching an itch I'd had for a very long time, and, well - I've perfected this game. I hope that stands as a testament to how much i love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond blue is a beautiful game where you swim amongst the fishes, dolphins and whales. The visuals are really beautiful and relatively lifelike, the general feeling of peace and quiet is real and intense. Even if there is this sort of meshing on the sides that makes you feel that you are, in fact, in VR. lol. I played with the joystick and it was smooth, and I did not get any crash at all. The gameplay is simple and smooth also. The story is not earth breaking or even original, but it does it's job, meaning, it transports you in this magic world of beauty and quiet. You get attached to the characters, humans or whales, and you swim along the storyline toward the ineluctable end. The game also wants to awake your awareness on how fragile this wet giant is. The ocean is a huge ecosystem that has been exploited for ressources for many centuries, each of us believing is bounty boundless, but it is just not the case. And every one of our actions impact on the life of this giant. With several comments and many videos of scientists interviews, you can learn more about all this. The way the game informs you, is not dogmatic or boring, but every bits are incorporated inside the game and are quite seamless. For those of us collectors addicts, there are many animals to collect et many achievements to reach. All in all, it is a very nice game, Thanks to the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game, I was actually hoping for some more exploration and game play. I  thought it was going to be similar game play like Endless Ocean (Nintendo Wii) with more treasures to be found and such, but over all it was a beautiful game. The story line lasts less than 10 hours depending on how you play.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I very much recommend this game, just finished it. It's graphics is absolutely breathtaking and it takes you about 3 hours to finish the game. It makes you know a lot about the animals and makes it feel like you're actually there. If you don't know, in Beyond Blue you're playing as Mirai, a Marine Biologist documenting a Sperm Whale family, and you watch a calf go through it's entire life. Again, I very much recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Educational, magnificent & eye opening. I wasn't sure what to expect with this game to be honest. I was initially drawn to it as it reminded me of abzu but with an educational twist. Seeing as I like Marine life this had my attention. I was blown away by just how educational this game actually is. The insights (mini documentaries) also add a lot to the game. In fact, calling this a game is a stretch, it is an educational experience with a slight game attached (which is great). First game in a while that I feel I have learnt a decent amount from and it was presented perfectly. Highly recommend for everyone, even those that are not overly enthusiastic about marine life, there is a lot to learn even for the average person.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This is a swimming simulator with a nice touch of deep sea documentation. The story is linear, but satisfying and the atmosphere of just swimming in the ocean without the fear of being swallowed whole is quite relaxing. I liked it. Not sure it's worth the full price, as length-wise there's not much there after a few hours. Sure you can go back and scan every fish and watch the documentary pieces (which are interesting and informative, but not very long), but that's pushing the amount of content to maybe 4-5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Received for free: I obtained this as a Christmas gift from a friend.I feel like this is a very calming and relaxing game.  I well enjoyed it and it allowed me to sort of let my mind calm as I explore the beautiful ocean.It does seem a bit short to me and I was able to fully complete it in 7-8 hours (could've been shorter if I wasn't taking my super sweet time and if I realized sooner I could track down animals I didn't scan).I do feel as if there's a bit lack of content and there could be a bit more to it for more playtime, but otherwise I feel this is a good relaxing ocean game.  I always enjoyed these types of games where I can explore an ocean, scan and learn about the types of fish in the area.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely beautiful.  You almost feel fully immersed into the realm of the deep blue ocean.  The story is somewhat educational and follow along with the main character as she explores what lies below.  I will say, that it has no "end game"  it is just about exploration.  I loved a lot about this game, but I will say it was short.  Personally, kids who love things about aquatic life would LOVE this.  No real "scary" jump out at you danger.  It's what I would consider family friendly.  I have yet to try this camera mode, definitely something to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly well-done and well-researched. I'm a biology major taking an ecology class right now, and so many of the topics we covered in class were also touched on in this game. It was a great reinforcement for me! It's also a fun game; you can just swim around and interact with the environment and wildlife and experience the characters' stories. My only issue so far is that the scanning mechanic can be a little unwieldy at times, but it's only an occasional annoyance. If you're a science fanatic or love the ocean, you'll love this game!Edit: the map indicator for scans is very difficult to see (so much so that I had to read a guide to know it exists). I'd love to see this fixed
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic is great, the graphics are nice. The story is a littlebit sloppy, and the movement can be a littlebit better, but it doesn't affect the experiance that much.Personally I learnt a few things about the sea life. I got the game during a discount, and in the end, I think its worth it.I can recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: A calm and informative game about the oceans, Beyond Blue was made together with marine biologists and includes several mini-documentaries as unlockables. Gameplay consists of swimming around and scanning things--don't expect monsters or combat. The story is quite thin, but the characters are fun. Needs a mermaid skin/mod.If you love the ocean and/or animals, this game gets an 8/10.If you are looking for an action or survival game, I must sadly tell you to keep looking, because you won't find it here.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves Marine documentaries but has mild Thalassophobia I had a mixed experience. The game is absolutely beautiful and with it's great soundtracking it has a fantastic atmosphere. You do Deep Dives which were terrifying at first but I can say that it helped me understand the ocean a lot. The game gives you a ton of insight in the work of Marine Biologist both in the game and in the additional Videos you can watch. The graphics are amazing as well and you can go back to every zone after the story ended although I didn't had the urge to do it.I can 100% recommend it though. I would have been satisfied with far less for 16€ and I had a great experience with it
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice visuals, the music is also nice! It's a shame you can't listen to it when you're diving though. Story is good, but not something to write home about. It definitely puts into perspective the diversity of life in the ocean and how beautiful but fragile the ecosystems are. Great game, hopefully in the future there is more content because I would love to see what is coming next!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game, if you can call it as such, is relaxing and educating. It reminds me why I went to school to protect the natural environment and gives me strength to continue towards a better tomorrow. My only complaint would be that there was not more. More creatures (plant and animal), more quests, more areas, and it felt like it sort of ended without tying the loose ends, but maybe it was meant to be that way. Either way, I would definantly purchase and support more content like this. Education + Games = Fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game was more of a work of art, and thank you for letting us experience it. Very few times have I been this touched by a video game, it gave me goosebumps. Listening to Marine Biologists talk about the ocean, conservation and how fragile life is on our planet was fascinating, and knowing how we all individually have a responsibility to do what we can  to protect life, because this is our only home, left me with a profound affect on my own behaviour that only Blue Planet 2 has elicited in me before. If you like Blue Planet 2, play this game. I think if Sir Attenborough was narrating I'd have been fully gone.Also my autistic ass loves scanning literally everything to completion so, win-win.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is a beatiful underwater game.It is perfect for those who like to explore, especially the oean. but that is basicly all you can do.I had a Great time exploring the ocean and smimmming next whales and sharks. to summ it up you should play this game if you like the ocean and its Habitants. If that is not the case you will prably be bored by this game,I Love it!!<§
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: From a purely gaming standpoint, Beyond Blue is... not much of a game, really. Its mechanics are really barebones, and although you can technically roam freely, there's nothing to do outside of the main story's objectives, besides just scanning specimens to fill in the sliders.No, Beyond Blue's appeal is something else entirely: it's the experience. It's hard to describe (also because my brain sucks at translating feelings into words), but it's deeply relaxing and, despite the lack of action, not boring at all (at least for me). The voice acting is believable, and a good commentary on what happens on screen; the plot is... honestly what you could expect from that kind of environment, nothing groundbreaking but a nice story to follow, and the voicecalls between dives are a nice little touch.Just don't expect it to be Subnautica with better graphics, it's nothing like that. It's more along the lines of an interactive documentary, but an actually engaging one.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game to relax, a way to explore to incredible wonders of the ocean, this definitely does the job. It's been a while since I've been diving. This game kinda scratches that itch. The graphics are simply amazing. It's also a gentle way to introduce the players to the significant impact of how we lead our lives on the health of the ocean. You definitely can finish the game in a few hours. However, the true value of this game lies after you're done with the game. You essentially get to just roam freely and explore the various dive sites. As you play along, you unlock several short documentary videos, which I find interesting. However, these are only a few minutes long. I wish they were more extensive, and were taken in HD.I have an extra wide monitor, and viewing the game using this monitor is zen-like. I get an incredible immersive experience. In short, this is an exploration game, more focused on education, rather than gaming. It also introduces the beauty of the ocean, and its endless habitats. I see why some people end up being marine biologists. The ocean is a fascinating world that most people are just aware of. I would certainly buy this game again, more as an escape from the stressful reality of work and family.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: The magic of the sea has no words to describe its reality, unless you are there. Now, I can describe it, because I am there! For as many hours as my heart desires. I am in awe and disbelief of the incredible comparison to real life, this game holds. I can almost ride the whales, pet the fish play with the dolphins. This, is life on earth, at its best!! I can never thank you enough for designing this much life giving energy, and never having to leave my home to share in it.  This game is a gift from my daughter, that will keep on giving, for the rest of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great visuals and if you love sea life I can truly recommend the game but unfortunately the personal stories of the characters are uninteresting. we come here for the ocean not some random people. power through this 2ish hour story and you unlock freedive. allowing you to explore and relax at you whim, with no annoying characters
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Like most have said in a nutshell - Pro's: spectacular graphics, environments, ocean life - Cons: boring and uninteresting personal story. Gameplay is swimming around to various waypoints and scanning things, rinse and repeat.I loved the visual experience, but just swam to the waypoints clicking skip past the story audio I fast as I could.On balance still recommended for a single playthrough for anyone remotely interested in the oceans. Also props to the dev/publisher for coming out with something unique. This game would be a great candidate for a DLC or story remaster, as the visuals are really stunning.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is a fantastic and immersive ocean exploration game that is casually fun and educational.The overall gameplay is very easy and it didn't take long at all to get all of the achievements. Visually, the game is stunning and looks amazing on the highest settings and really brings the ocean to life. I only wish that the maps were bigger and there was more coral as well to really give the reefs that vibrant feel, but I suppose realistically, with the addition of plastic in the ocean it shows the effects of human activity in the water, which is perhaps why some areas aren't as populated with coral. And the models of sea-life are so realistic, it truly does make you feel as though you're there.The ambient music was superb when exploring, trying to find all the different types of aquatic life, and definitely had a sea-feel to it; that sense of vastness and freedom. However I wasn't a fan of the submarine music, but that's just personal taste!Superb voice acting throughout and I loved the addition of the documentary videos as well as the model viewer for all the sea-life you find, accompanied with facts and information!Overall, I highly recommend this game for a casual afternoon game and it was well worth the money in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Endless Ocean, i've been craving for a similar diving game for years. I've also been looking for a game that was calming and less chaotic to play after work and this definitely ticked the boxes. This brought me joy as i dived about discovering sealife and learning about new technologies that are used to discover dangers and new life. Unfortunately it ended so quick and i wish i could discover more species with more maps and information. But this has definitely made me empathise with marine biologists and researchers who are looking to discover, find cures and protect our sealife, and I have full respect for them. I wish them best of luck to making the sea and the world a better place.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game. I'm a sucker for ocean games anyway, so I'm usually not too picky. But even so, this one stands out from some of the others.It's very similar to Abzu in the way it plays, but also has some Subnautica vibes when you dive deep. It's relaxing, fun, and full of educational quips about ocean life. I learned some interesting facts from this game. (Immortal moon jellyfish intensifies) Overall, I loved it. The missions are very smooth and I liked the conversations you have with other people you work with on the campaign's expedition. The soundtrack is peaceful, the animal behavior is fun to watch.The only 2 things that I think could add even more to this game are:A: More campaign missions. I didn't want the exploration to end. Maybe there are DLCs in the works for this game? One can dream...B: It'd be nice to interact with the animals. I was hoping to be able to ride around on the big fish like you can in Abzu.But those 2 possible add-ons don't take away from the experience. This is a labor of love, and a very well put-together game.I got it on sale cause I heard the campaign was short, but if you're the kind of gamer who doesn't mind trading 20 bucks for 3 - 5 hours of relaxing swimming, then definitely go for it.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Well to start this game is amazing. Sure the scanning and all feels repetitive but the graphics are pretty and the whole thing just looks great. Can't really say there's a "game" but if you just kinda wanna swim around and watch fish and other things do their thing then this would be it. Does tend to make me a little said thinking about just how much humans have trashed the world playing this but meh. This sure isn't for everyone but for those that might like it I'm pretty sure you'll find this a big gem/
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: A cool concept, and the first hour or so is enjoyable, but the game is over in 2 hours and there's a lot of personal dialogue about characters that aren't really developed. In the second half of the game (the second hour) it's mostly moody voice acting while you complete the same tasks again. I found myself just rolling my eyes when I was forced to make personal calls between stages. I understand it's a narrative indie title but a bit more focus on animals and learning with a little less angsty family problems would have left me with a better taste in my mouth. A great idea but would have been better serviced with a longer story and maybe some more creatures, locales and character development. Probably not worth full price of $23 CAD that I paid. Maybe pick it up on sale if you're looking for a casual narrative experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: The ocean is so fascinating and also terrifying I always loved watching Blue Planet and PVR'ing shark week ect so I'm interested in games like this. Calling it a game tho feels kinda off yes it is a game but it's more about the message and raising awareness. I found it too be pretty immersive and a decent looking game however the sound mixing was all over the place I was adjusting volumes constantly. There is a lot of species variety but the missions are too simple and the mechanics are dull. My biggest complain however is the lack of content and length of the game, it is poor value. I  appreciate what projects like this are trying to achieve we need to take better care of our oceans this is the only reason I gave this a thumbs up because as a video game it's not great. There is so little content that they put like 20 little BBC videos in the game and even with watching this videos in between mission it's like a 2 hour game with very little gameplay. The voice acting is well done and thankfully they put abit of a story line in there otherwise you might as well just watch a documentary you'll get better use of your time. On sale if you like me just enjoy spending time in a virtual ocean it's worth picking up but at full price it's not worth it. 6.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game, I felt the environments and sea life was well realized, and the basic hook of the game was engaging enough to keep me plowing forward through the levels.  You are prodded along with some basic objectives to follow and there is a light story that I felt served its purpose well enough.I enjoyed the game so much that I went back to 100% the achievements, which brought my total playtime to 6 hours.  I paid full price and I feel that my short experience was very much worth what I spent.  If you are at all curious about the ocean and its creatures, I would implore you to enjoy this game.  I expect to visit it again in the near future myself.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: A quite fun little experience of swimming in the ocean, scanning sea creatures and working your way through a short story. Enjoyable, calm, relaxing and beautiful. Recommended to people that generally like relaxing, easy and/or short games. Achievements take about 3-4 hours to get with minimal effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is an absolutely amazing title you must play.I found this game relaxing, engaging, and very easy to be immersed into the world.The Visuals and the sounds are just phenomenal.The soundtrack to this game is also really good.My only issue with the game, is the story.Not that the story was bad or anything, it's just very very short.The game only took me 3hrs to complete but I enjoyed every second of it.My next task for the game is to speedrun it and try get PB's.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. It's absolutely relaxing, with a nice story to go with it (not too deep, but you don't need super deep) and a beautiful soundtrack. if you want to relax for a while and swim in a beautiful environment, and - forbid - learn something while doing so :)  - go get this. No fights, no hurry, just relax and enjoy this beautiful and well-done game. I enjoyed it!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I'd had this game on my wishlist for a long time after finishing Subnautica because I desperately wanted another game like that to scratch my itch for underwater exploration. Sadly, this isn't that game, but I feel like it's not fair to leave a bad review because of my own expectations. It's an interesting little experience, but it's all scripted and very short. I think a lot of the content was supposed to come from reading and watching videos to learn about the different sea creatures, and trying to tag all the different creatures in each zone, but I personally have no interest in that sort of thing. I also found myself skipping through all the story dialogue near the end because you are forced converse with people over the phone between each mission and that's not really what I wanted from the game. The storyline seems fine I guess, it's just that it's only told through characters speaking and is kind of irrelevant to the gameplay. It's quite heartfelt but it I found myself not even caring about it towards the end. Also because the game is quite short, it gives the player even less incentive to want to care about the narrative.Overall Beyond Blue is certainly not a bad game. There are beautiful, almost scary, sights of whales and other sea life peacefully swimming in a seemingly endless void of ocean. That combined with other dives exploring the dark depths of the sea floor and its creatures and there's something of an experience to be had here. There was clearly a lot of passion that went into creating this game.Just to echo some of the other comments, if you come in expecting a successor to Subnautica, or you want an autonomous exploration game, you aren't going to have those expectations met. That's just not what this game aims to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet. Gives off good old Endless Ocean vibes, and drops in some really neat marine life and environment facts in between all the chill experiences. The environments are stunning and animals are modeled with great detail and a myriad of behaviors. Especially swimming through a feeding ball of small fish was awesome. :)May not be many hours of gametime, but feels like a game that will stay with you for a while after you've finished it. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Simple controls. It's short, only 2 hours, but there's a free dive mode so you can explore some more on your own. The music in and out of the sub is nice. The dialogue can get quiet at times, so having subtitles on is a good idea if you don't want to miss any of the story. I feel they could have made this game longer by adding more to the dives and the story... I think there's one or two spots where a different decision could impact what dialogue options you get, but I have yet to test that out.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This is a relatively short game with a small amount of plot that hits home right where it needs to. It's happy and sad in shares, and the gameplay is more akin to the walkabout style see in things like Gone Home or Whatever Happened to Edith Finch, but the topic at hand is marine biology and ocean conservation instead. There's not a strict path to follow to each objective, but the only other things to do are to investigate other fish, mollusks, sharks, and so on. I do wish that a positional/depth gauge was on display in a corner, or could be pulled up as an action on our fancy watch, because I did occasionally find myself going in the same circle while trying to track creatures, but beyond that there's not many gripes. The sub base is delightfully futuristic and it makes me want to live there, the soundtrack and voice acting are both well done, and even the character's design looks cool--really dig that tattoo! The only other thing that irks are the story beats with the sister, mostly due to lack of communication to the player what happened before, which isn't strictly important, but with everything else being so excellent it just comes up like a single spot where content was cut to make room elsewhere--which is fine, given the rest of the content. All in all, this will pass a few hours, and you'll probably enjoy yourself through both the delight and the pathos. Highly recommended, if a low key underwater exploration game sounds like your jam. There's no threats, no attacks, no danger of running out of air a la Subnautica or its kin, but this still invokes the same kind of awe of exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful. Just beautiful. As well as exploring the ocean and learning about the species living in multiple types of habitat, the story allows you to fully immerse yourself in the role of the marine biologist/ diver. A must for anyone who enjoys the ocean, and to be honest, who doesn't?!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: tough one this one. don't get me wrong. The game is astonishing and wonderful for playing just to chill a bit.However it is horribly short. It ends before you know it. you can still pass some time scanning missing stuff but that is all that remains shortly after. despite the longevity I have nothing of much to point out so...TO be Honest I recommend the game, but wait for a sale or a discount of sorts because It maybe more worthy concerning its lenght. It is basically a one day pplay this game and you won't touch it again in a while
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue captures the feeling of exploring the ocean quite well. The only downsides to this game are that it gets quickly repetetive, scan life form, go to buoy, scan lifeform, go to buoy etc. and it is relatively short compared to its price (it can be easily finished in around 4.5 hours, exploring everything and obtaining all achievements). Other than that I greatly enjoyed looking for unique creatures and following the narrative of the story, the insight shorts were well done and informative. I can recommend this game to people who like exploring nature and simply enjoy the aesthetics of the game. If you expect something more than that I wouldn't buy it for its price.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly not what I expected, or maybe I've put my hopes up too much. - Especially after Abzu-I hoped to have more interaction with the animals, but sadly it's almost as if you don't exist when you swim by or even bump into them. The story looks a bit on the depressing side as well.. Perhaps that clears up in a while, but I didn't want to stick around to find out. Requested a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: this was... such an amazing and moving experience, i litterally cried both because of the emotions this game procured but also because of the way things are written in it, the different videos, the breathtaking images and sceneries, the deeep meaning behind this whole game. Thank you to everyone who has crated this game, it is a masterpiece and a must have!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with a great atmosphere. You can feel the ocean and alive envoirment. Eventhough i have thalassophobia (fear of ocean) it was fun to explore ocean and be close to gentle giants. This game also lead me to make some research on marine life and sustainable way of life. I greatly recommend you to experience it. It's almost like an documentary rather than a game. I'm sure you will love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Animals, the Ocean or exploration games then this is a perfect combination of all three. While this is an educational game, there is a bit of story there are you follow a pod of Sperm whales. Its very documentation style with you exploring and scanning the animals in the reef.Game took me roughly 4 hours to play through and complete the achievements 100%. I would recommend this short but charming game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: it is a beautiful game. relaxing. i love the charectors and the story. only thing is tha tit is to short! i want waaay more! crossing my fingers for exspantions or something of the kind. the ocean is very big. lots of places to go. and may i say. i was crying for two reasons, the beautiful game and the ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely spectacular! The art is fantastic and really pulls you into the atmosphere. Some of the volume levels are a bit unbalanced, but you can mostly fix that once you're in game through the settings menu. Being able to learn more about ocean science and the animals they are studying is such a wonderful experience. The 'real life' videos you unlock along the way is a great touch! Getting to hear from the real scientists who are studying these animals and learning how to help them is a really powerful thing. Vod available here:  if you want to see some of the gameplay. Also, I met the guys from E-Line Media at Pax last year and they are wonderful people! You could just tell how very passionate they are about this game and it's message.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I know some people went in expecting something very different, which affected their opinion, but it's great for what it is. If you're looking for something like subnautica, this isn't the same. If you've ever wished an ocean documentary or an aquarium was truly interactive, then this is a game for you.The story wasn't overly groundbreaking, but was engaging, as were the characters. I enjoyed the little hints in the environment of the sub that took that further. The visuals are beautiful and there's a good amount of exploration to enjoy (especially in free dive). It's short, but I definitely enjoyed the evening I spent playing it. I plan to watch all the educational clips next.I did notice a few glitches (some fish stuck in places, one of which might be preventing me from getting the full scan achievement), but there weren't many. There's also a lot to learn, even in just the game itself. I especially enjoy the work that was put into making the game both accurate and educational.It's basically a relaxing and educational walking (swimming?) simulator, but I also don't think there's anything wrong with that.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: It's weird to review a game like this, it dosn't have action, it dosn't have huge dramatic moments, it dosn't have fun gameplay or a great story, it barely has any mechanics... but if you are in the right mood for it, it can be a relaxing experience. It's pretty short, i got all achievements in 5 hours, it really is just a game to chill out for a moment and watch some fishes, don't expect anything more than that. But for what it is, i enjoyed it, wish it was bigger in every way, but i got it for very cheap so i don't mind, i just wanted to look at fish.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Very quality over quantity game. Beautiful graphics and relaxing gameplay but not exactly the sequel to Endless Ocean 2 that I was hoping for. It would have been nice to interact with more objects while diving and be able to zoom in to see the tiny items in the sub. There's new things lying around after every dive but it's hard to see what they say. I'd also love to play the sub music during the dives, there isn't much to do in the sub with the music playing. There are still a few bugs, Mirai doesn't blink and the zoom drone often goes inside the whale models, but they're minor.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue - What for a game! I wished it would be longer because it was awesome!A game without violance and fighting, with exploring the wonderful world of the ocean and learning about it... a beautiful conzept!I really hope there will be some DLC for this game and other games like this (maybe a "Beyond Green" about the rainforests or something like that).Our planet and it's nature is so beautiful and unique... we should take care of our earth as if it where our very best friend. I wished I had a diving suit like that in the game. _childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! Great storyline, nice graphics. I only wish it was longer! The whole game took me less than 3 hours to complete. Worth it, though. I'd love a sequel. Something in Endless Ocean style with more story and more opportunity to explore would be so amazing. I'll be looking out for Beyond Blue 2!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: The story is a little janky, with some interesting interpersonal events and other events that were brought up as a big deal, but never got closure or an explanation. Along the lines of 'bad emotions happen, never get expanded on, but at the end we just skip to everything is okay now.' There were some gameplay aspects that were interesting, but didn't get used enough, like the different light sources, (red light, UV light, white light), but you only had to use UV once, and red light just existed but didn't really make any impact. Would have been nice to be able to customize keybinds, as well.However, it's a really peaceful game. Great for spending time on to relax and learn, and it certainly gives you a good sense of just how important the ocean is and the life within it. 9/10 from me. The informative videos that you unlock, and the wildlife data were really cool to sift through.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I played this in a single sitting and really enjoyed it. If you have even a passing interest in shows like Blue Planet or in marine biology in general you should definitely play this game. I really felt a strong recognition and appreciation of the hard work that goes into the kind of research displayed, and made me think about how a finding can go from a researcher's notebook to the big screen. Really cool!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game a little longer is still think it's beautiful and well designed for a relatively small production like this. There are a few downsides for me though. I don't like the voice acting for the main protagonist. It does not fit the mood of the rest of the game in my opinion. Also the fact that you can move around the sub does not make a lot of sense. There is almost nothing to do and having a character model to move around does not serve any purpose. But again, i still like the game regardless.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: It is a great experience if you go in primarily to learn about the creatures of the deep, or if you are interested in biology in general.  If you come expecting rich game'ish systems, then you might find it a bit lacking. The creatures are wonderfully detailed, and you can learn about the creatures and organisms of the sea by playing through the story of watching the unlockable mini-documentaries. There is also a nice 3D model viewer to get closer up on the creatures, and some slides for each scannable organism. It is a great way of learning and I am really enjoying my time with it. I wish games like this existed when I was younger. I can just imaging the impact it would've had on me growing up.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: It's an ocean exploration game where you scan various aquatic wildlife.  There's not much more to it.  You can finish it in less than 2 hours.That being said, if you're looking for a casual relaxed aquatic exploration game, this might scratch that itch.  The environments are smaller than you'd expect, but are detailed enough to make the environment beautiful.  Swimming is easy, and scanning the various fish, whales, squid, etc. are pretty easy to do.  The story feels unfinished, as if there was originally something bigger here that got cut somewhere through production.  This leaves you with a feeling of always wanting more.  There's a bit of a subplot with deep sea divers that seems like it'll be the one of the main focuses.  Unfortunately it never comes to fruition.  The main focus is on following a pod of whales and researching them, which at least stays fairly consistent.Gameplay wise, there isn't much here.  You scan sea life.  There's no real tangible reward for doing so, which hampers any desire to scan 30 dolphins or 20 hammerheads.  However, swimming alongside the various creatures does have it's moments of tranquility.  And really, that's what this game is about.  Relaxing in the ocean while seeing various sea life.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game captivated me with it's visuals and atmosphere as well as it sounds and narrative. I thoroughly enjoyed the non linear experience that let you explore yourself in an open world style, without being pushed to follow the mission objective immediately, with some of the objectives cropping up after swimming for a while, it made for a really relaxing experience. These are my experiences after playing around 40-50 minutes from the introduction to the end of the first level sequence until the sub base.Positives from my experience:- The graphics are beautiful and modern (not sure which engine it's running, Unreal? Or Unity?- The Wildlife have realistic animation, comparable to real counterparts I've personally seen in aquariums- After the narrative mode, you can continue to explore freely in the free mode exploration stage after the story- The controls are simple and easy to use and navigate around with in the ocean, great for beginners or younger players- The mini documentaries offered give further insight into ocean life and the ecosystems- Realistically portrays eco system by showing littering of the ocean's seafloor with scattered debris / shipping containers- The ocean life species catalogue lets you expand your collection by scanning and discovering new species per ecosystem- There is an ocean hub which is your sub marine that's fully interactable (music player/tablets/3D Fish model viewer)- The 3D Model viewer on the submarine lets you play animations for each fish and is great for screenshots tooWhat could have been improved upon:- Some wildlife is static such as the clams and cannot be scanned, although this is a minor thing- Some more seabed creatures like shellfish, and plant life could be added and be scannableI would recommend this game as my first experience with it was positive, I usually don't make an effort to review a game unless I thoroughly enjoy it or dislike it and this was one of the good ones for me so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with some nice graphics & atmosphere but there are absolutely zero interractions with the animals which makes it very frustrating since you have the feeling to be invisible for them. It miss an A.I. so the creatures can reacts to you. Also the moves of your characters are very limited, it would have been more fun if you could do more moves & touch the animals with one hand (with vibrations in the gamepad when you touch one).

_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed this game. I've been looking for a newer version of Endless Ocean 2 for years and this fits the bill! I found it really immersive and relaxing, as well as informative and awe inspiring.The models are really well detailed and the environment is really well designed too.I just really wish there was at least one end game feature, like an aquarium zone or something to do with the fish you have scanned; apart from scanning all the animals. I also wish this game was longer, I didn't want the story to end, I wanted to keep exploring and finding new animals and places. On the whole, I really love this game. It's a solid 9/10 from me, I would want to see more fish and an end game feature to bump it up to a 10. The atmosphere is spot on, the soundtrack is fabulous, and the visuals are crisp and realistic. Well done to the developers of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue is an experience that is beyond words.  It’s not quite a game, but it is.  It’s not edutainment but you learn stuff.  It’s the best possible mix of going to the aquarium and actually learning to scuba dive, but unless you have a few hundred million in high tech gear and mini-subs or work for OceanX you’re not likely to experience anything like this in your lifetime short of playing this game.Full review at 4K/UHD 60fps Gameplay Impressions at
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a simple - short game then this is for you.I completed this game in 6 hours over two days so you can tell from that alone that it is a short game.Eventhough it may be extremely short for some people - myself included - worry not! After you've completed the game you can access free roam mode which is exactly as it sounds you can go to all the places you visited during the game and scan all those fishes that you may have missed when going through the storyline. This game also includes insight videos from highly qualified researchers, scientists and conservationists. They give their insight into certain whales or fishes to how we can help to keep our oceans healthy. I personally found this extremely interesting to watch.Even though the game may not have the desired ending you may wish and may leave you with more questions than answers - like it did for me - but I think that's the beauty of the game it is based more on real life people and problems that we face today and overall I thought that the game was fantastic for the style of game it is. Overall I give this game a 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Enchanting, educational and enlightening game about ocean exploration and conservation. The behaviours of each of the sea creatures you encounter are authentic and realistic. There's something so peaceful about swimming along side some of our earths most majestic animals. The Maps are fairly large and enjoyable to swim around. But most of all the message behind this game is an important one, about saving our oceans and the beautiful creatures that inhabit them.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a (short) beautiful linear narrative driven game (very much like some of the "walking simulator" games) in which you discover some of the wonders of our beautiful oceans, a world mostly undiscovered, even today we know very little about our oceans and you could say we know more about space than what lives right below us in our deep, vast oceans.While the main story focuses on a mother whale and her newborn it also touches on the destructive nature of mankind and the effects our way of life has on the oceans and the importance of the oceans to (all) life on earth.As i said the game was quite short, it probably took me around 5 hours to go through the story, and i took my time taking in the sights and scanning whatever came across my path (you can probably do it way faster if you just go from waypoint to waypoint), after the main story ends the game will open up and let you go back to all the areas you dived before and explore for as long as you want. It took me probably around 6,5 hours to completely finish everything that you can do (which is mostly just scanning all the fish and mammals) and get all the achievements.As a big fan of ocean exploration i really enjoyed the game but wished it was way longer, the story was over before i knew it and felt like it was mostly just briefly touching on most of the subjects. After finishing the story there is not really much left to do other than swim around and enjoy the scenery but i feel the game was definitely worth it's price and very enjoyable. Overall i would say it's more of an ocean awareness/educational tool than an exploration type of game, so if you are going into this thinking you are going to do some (unlimited) open world ocean exploring, you are going to be dissapointed."If we wipe out the fish, the oceans are going to die. If the oceans die, we die. We can't live on this planet with a dead ocean."- Paul Watson“No water, no life, no blue, no green”– Sylvia Earle
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a love affair with the ocean since I was a little kid, and this game is the love letter my heart would write. The visuals are beautiful and the music sounds like the most solid Spotify group playlist ever. The cinematography is, of course, fantastic.The game is similar to what Endless Ocean tried to do on the Wii, but a thousand times better. It's not the whole package--it's an educational game, so of course it's pretty light on the "game" part--but it's really enjoyable. Definitely worth the full retail price for me since all I want to do is swim around, watch the wildlife, collect things, and watch nature documentary-style programming when I'm not quite sober enough to play video games, but I recognize that that's not gonna be everyone's jam. Features that are notably absent:- Photo mode- VR modeBut holy cow, if there were a subscription option that included periodic updates on the research and cinematography being done, I would save up and shell out the money for the lifetime plan.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty much a slightly interactive documentary. But it is very well made. The graphics are beautiful and you can learn a lot about fish and the ocean and the problems it has.I would recommend this for families with kids and for nature fans. It doesn't have much playing as you pretty much just swim around and watch the different underwater landscapes and the fish that live in each. There is no survival, no horror (unless you count the deep sea fish), no fighting or anything. Gameplay style is more or less a walking simulator. But I think it is worth it. It's calm, relaxing, beautiful and informative.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: I always had a weird interest to explore deep-sea creatures so when I first saw the premise of this game, it was like a dream come true. Beyond Blue mostly delivers what it promises it is mostly an educational game where you encounter all kinds of sea creatures. You do this by simply scanning the creatures, which then unlocks some interesting facts. Unfortunately, this is all there is to the game, there are no survival or crafting mechanics, there is no real way to interact with the creatures and there aren't any puzzles. The game does have a story but it isn't all that interesting, it's just about a diver who live streams her sessions in the sea while doing some tasks for scientists. She also can't shut up about whales... The story is also fairly short I completed it in 2 hours. Even though the game doesn't have a lot of content, it's still a fun experience to explore the sea fauna. The models of the sea creatures all look great and it's a great touch that they added a realistic sound design for the animals. I must admit however that I'm a little bit disappointed that there weren't any real surprises. Not adding easter eggs like the bloop or some Cthulhu like monster is a missed opportunity. If you accept the game for what it is and don't set your expectations too high it will be well worth your money!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Blue

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Blue takes players into the near future, where they will have the opportunity to explore the mysteries of our ocean through the eyes of Mirai, a deep-sea explorer and scientist. She and her newly-formed research team will use groundbreaking technologies to see, hear, and interact with the ocean in a more meaningful way than has ever been attempted. The game features an evocative narrative and exploration of an untouched world. Embracing the same inclusive development process that was used to create Never Alone (Kisima Ingitchuna), E-Line’s BAFTA award-winning game about Alaska Native culture, the company partnered with BBC Studios (developers of the acclaimed Blue Planet II), OceanX Media, world-class game makers, and some of science’s leading ocean experts to craft an experience that reflects the awesome wonder and unbounded mystery that infuses our planet’s beating blue heart.

name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED
detailed_description: ROME REMASTERED includes the Alexander and Barbarian Invasion DLCs, as well as a copy of the original ROME: Total War Collection* if you don’t already own it.   Improved Visuals ROME REMASTERED brings the classic Rome visuals up to date, with 4K optimization**, ultra-widescreen and native UHD resolution** support. This visual upgrade extends across a multitude of features, including re-modelled buildings and objects, and environmental effects like dust clouds and heat haze. The refreshed campaign maps also boast new high-resolution models, and units have been remodelled and retextured to look their very best on the battlefield. Modern Features ROME REMASTERED includes a host of modern features and improvements to existing mechanics. The in-game camera has been enhanced, including map rotation and wider zoom level in Campaign mode. Heat maps and new icon overlays have been added for gameplay mechanics such as diplomacy and security. In Battle, the new tactical map, unit displays and range markers give you greater command over Rome’s battlefields. Enhanced Game Mechanics Players can now expand their armies and experience 16 additional factions that were previously locked, giving a grand total of 38 playable factions. In a first for Total War, you can now take your favourite faction to battle against friends in cross-platform multiplayer between Windows, macOS and Linux. A whole new agent type has also been added to the fray; Merchants can be sent all over the world to create trade links, access resources and buy out rivals to increase your income and assert your faction’s economic power. *Please note, ROME: Total War Collection is only playable on Windows. **4K enhancements unlocked by downloading Enhanced Graphics Pack

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, I am a huge fan of the original RTW, it's my most played game on Steam at nearly 700 hours. If you go into this game knowing the remaster is definitely not a complete remake/fundamental change of the original 2004 game, you will definitely not be as disappointed as some of the negative reviews that some people have. Most of the changes that have been made were mostly optimization/quality of life changes rather than fundamentally reworking the game, and i think there were nice details added that make it anything but a lazy cash grab as some might claim. Also I'm writing this long review because I appreciate the work put in and hope this is a sign of M2TW Remastered.The graphical improvement is naturally going to be a big improvement from the 2004 textures, with individual units as well as building textures being much more detailed and realistic looking, all of this being enhanced by the native 4k resolution. However, due to the way lighting and ground textures work in this 2004 engine/game, obviously the game will look flatter and not as good as something beautiful like Shogun 2. Additionally, the layouts of settlements in RTW has always been simple, and graphical changes just won't do anything about that. The visual changes to the campaign map were very much welcome ones, and the campaign map overall just looks better, and i appreciate the little detail of the edges of the map being blocked by stone walls and each corner having a mosaic of the faction that lives closest to that corner. I have also been playing on the new highest unit count which is an "experimental" Extreme setting (200 soldiers in an average infantry unit card), which really allows for an even greater sense of scale of battles. With the generally improved optimization its now actually possible to have a battle with nearly 50 THOUSAND troops (though you might need to tone the graphical settings wayyyyy down) but the highest troop count I have been able to actually play at maximum 4k settings at a reasonable frame rate is about 24000.The overhaul of the camera controls in the battle and campaign map are very welcome changes that help RTW catch up to the modern total wars, and are pretty similar to Three Kingdom's controls now. Previously the battlemap camera was fixed angle depending on your zoom level, and was generally unideal for the Epic battle size because the zoom levels were way too low and forced too much camera movement, which was on controlled by using your mouse. In the battle map the range of being able to zoom in and out has been massively increased. You are now able to zoom all the way to eye level with your units and unit fade allows you to zoom into the unit as opposed to being stuck above them if you zoom too close, and you can zoom a ridiculously high level away even before you get to the "Tactical view", I was able to completely see/control a nearly full army at the "Extreme" battle size (approx. 3200 troops) without having to adjust my camera once. The camera controls are also not limited to the mouse and full keyboard control of the camera is pretty straight forward (WASD for general movement, C/V for up/down looking, E/Q for pivoting/rotating).  The campaign camera has now been given the ability to rotate, which while completely unnecessary this was one of the random quality of life changes that was a sign of the effort the studio had put in to generally improve/help RTW catch up. Just like the other modern total wars I rarely use Tactical Map, which is present in both battle and campaign maps. It is nice zooming out to see the little icons representing units on the map though, and it reminds me of historical videos about battles the YouTube channels make.A lot of the complaints about UI I feel are somewhat understandable, but mostly just people being disgruntled with having to relearn a UI. Similar to as if I was playing a true sequel game, I accepted the idea of relearning an UI, which I think is necessary to help keep an open mind about the UI. Overall the UI has beenimproved in terms of functionality, though I can see why people may have some complaints about the aesthetics. In battle UI, I am one of the people who really enjoyed the way RTW and M2TW had the unit card/abilities displayed, and aesthetically the orignal UI is definitely more pleasing to me as well. However in terms of functionality this UI is definitely an improvement. The improvements are as follows: 1-allowing the overhead map to be dropped down or hidden2-in addition to all the other things the original RTW unit card tells you it now tells you the fatigue status without having to hover over it3-a side menu that allows additional controls over what you see in the battle, with 3 toggle settings (always off, always on, only on when your cursor is over it) these things that you can toggle are unit flags, a status wheel which displays the same information as your unit cards (but appears for the enemy as well), pathfinding trails, range, and vegetation. This menu also allows for some controls like setting default movement speed and whether or not units start off with guard mode.The Campaign UI has also made a major improvement, although may also seem a bit clunky and aesthetically unpleasing at first. The Campaign UI took me an hour or so to get used to and while the original UI was much more straightforward and simple for the things like construction and recruitment, there were a lot of other details that I would routinely forget about because of the original UI's simplicity and focus on the two main aspects of armies and buildings. In the new UI there was definitely improvement in terms of allowing you to easily keep track of every aspect of the campaign, however this somewhat came at a sacrifice to being able to glance at the main 2 focuses of the game and know what is happening. While there is a lot more going on in your screen, this means that nearly every sort of information is at least 1 mouse click away and multiple htings can be viewed at once, whereas in the original UI you might have to go through an addiitonal 1 or 2 layers of searching to find the same information. One of the best examples of this is how prominent army, fleet, agent, and settlement tabs are now right at the bottom middle of your screen. Additionally agents now have a small pop up menu on the bottom right when you select them that has a list of actions they will try to complete without you actually clicking on where you want them to go (Ex: Spy on Mogontiacum). There is now a next turn system similar to Civ 5 where before you officially end turn they remind you of units that have remained inactive or had their path blocked, however you can just ignore these and continue to the turn if you do not want to do anything about it yet. The diplomacy UI has also been improved and allows you to much better see the mentality/reasoning behind the AI, however as always the AI itself is not exactly the brightest at times.There have been complaints about bugs/lack of optimization/AI issues, but a lot of these issues are fundamental to the engine/system that the original RTW was built on and it may not have been feasible to actually make some of these changes. AI in total war has never been too bright, and RTW was definitely no exception, considering its the oldest 3D total war. Working on AI in a 2004 designed game no matter what you do will will not result in a miracle, and AI behavior even in the most recent Three Kingdoms has some horribly braindead moments. Aside from the massive file size, the game has been pretty well optimized and I have experienced 0 performance issues running it on 4k maximum graphical settings over 7 hours of gameplay and 0 crashes. I have not run into many bugs/pathfinding issues, but if I have they were typically involving siege battles but this may be due to the extreme unit size that the game was not designed around, but RTW has always had pathfinding issues anyway

_childDocuments_.review: In my view the game delivers what was promised. It's still Rome Total War with minor and optional changes. I only played Campaign for the base game so far. Started with short campaign as Scipii on hardest difficulty.The campaign UI is quite different, but I like it after getting used to it. You can navigate your empire quite fast using shortcuts. Without using shortcuts it's pretty tedious, as buttons are placed oddly imo. I think it's also much clearer how new buildings will affect your city's mood, growth and income. Moving followers between characters is much easier now as well; you simply pick the character you want to move a follower to and use the "move follower" button. Then it takes X turns for the follower to arrive (depending on where it is).AI is notably improved, but nothing groundbreaking. I've seen it at least tries to withdraw when defeat is inevitable rather than wait to get routed and slaughtered. I did notice that Julii struggle with Gaul, though. Haven't captured any of Gaul's cities in 45 turns in my campaign. Brutii aren't doing much better either. Might have always been like this and Romans only pick up after Marian Reforms, though.That said, there are still bugs (the game crashed for me once when merging troops, nothing major outside of that), but frequent auto-saves don't make it a huge loss of time. The game seems to save before battles and at the start/end of turns. I've played and enjoyed much more unstable games.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I probably have played original Rome for well over a 1000 hours over the years, as I first bought it when Barbarian Invasion hit the shelves. I would consider changes made by Feral either positive, or neutral. I think that the new UI makes it easier to navigate the empire, as it grows, but I'm not a fan of it's visual design. Same goes for battle UI. It's helfpul (unit morale, ammo, health), but I just think it looks kind of ugly. The reason I'm not recommending it, is due to completely broken unit path finding in narrow streets and on bridges. It's definitely worse than in original Rome, as I put another 50 hours, or so into it a few months ago, so my memory is quite fresh. Tactical movement through bridges and narrow city streets in the Remaster is pretty much impossible, as the units completely break formation while moving through them and start running in wide circles for a while after leaving them, to reform, so you can't order them to pour out of the street and form a line, when the enemy is near. As both sieges and bridge battles are happening very often, the game is simply not enjoyable in this state.Edit: Feral has improved the game a lot with recent patches. You still can't move the units through bridges in formation, as the game considers it the same as swimming through water, but otherwise the units tend to keep their formations, even on extreme unit scale. The UI looks quite nice in the current version as well. Overall very good job done by Feral.

_childDocuments_.review: The correct way to do a remaster. Leave the core game alone for the most part and give players the option to disable the any new additions or enhancements that you do add.Total War Rome is one of the greatest PC strategy games of all time and I spent thousands of hours in it when it first released. When I repurchased the game on steam it disappointed me how the game ran so poorly on modern PC's. This remaster fixes that and for that reason alone it's a thumbs up for me. Some people will complain about changes the developer didn't make. For example the unit AI and pathfinding in siege battles appears to be unchanged and is as bad as it ever was. But that's just what TW: Rome was like. While many of us Total War fans complain about the new games; going back a couple decades can be a reminder as to how many things really have improved. For me though, it's perfect and exactly what I was looking for. I personally turn all the new enhancements off. The addition of merchants in particular kind of irks me because I never liked that mechanic in Medieval 2 but once again, I'm free to turn it off which I do. I'll probably play around with them in the future but Rome TW in it's original form is that comfy blanket that has holes in it but you still love, warts and all.A++ work, Feral Interactive. Looking forward to a Medieval 2 remaster.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original on CD as a kid and i have hundreds of hours in it.This remaster is everything I wanted it to be, and I really don't understand the negative reviews.If you think the original UI is better I don't know what to tell you, other than to get your eyes checked.A lot of these people saying it falls short of the original release must not have actually played it in the past ten years, because rose tinted glasses is my only explanation for how they can feel this release is somehow worse.This is classic total war at its best, its janky, its brutal, and it wont hold your hand like the new ones do, but if you have patience, it will reward you with one of the best experiences in the franchise.Don't like the colors? turn them to realistic in the settings.Don't like the vibrancy of the campaign map? turn it to 0% in the settings.Dont like the path finding issues?  ...that's valid actually. Half the complaints I have seen are more a matter of personal taste than an actual problem and even then you can change it if you just take 5 seconds and look at the options menu.Yes this game has flaws, and i'm not going to lie and pretend its perfect, but basically every problem was also in the original, and if the devs had changed it people would complain that they weren't faithful.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this game for about 400 hours since it was released, I can confidently say that this game is a must-have for fans of the beloved classic as well as for fans of the newer Total War titles. I admit that the user interface is very different and it took some getting used to, but in the end, I believe that Feral Interactive did a wonderful job in remastering this beloved game.Please keep in mind that this is a remaster, not a remake, and so, some of the issues that are present in the original game, such as pathfinding in cities, are still present, unfortunately. On the other hand, the visuals are wonderful. The new and improved textures in the campaign map as well as the units on the battle map are gorgeous, and the gameplay itself is solid.In my opinion, if you loved the original Rome, you will love the Remaster. _childDocuments_.review: Processor: Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700 CPU @ 3.40GHz   3.40 GHzMemory: 32 GB DDR4 @ 2400MHzGPU: GTX Nvidia 980 TIOS: Win10 64xI got Total War: Rome in 2004/2005ish back when you had to have a physical CD to install/play it. One of my all time absolute favorite games. Which is why with a heavy heart I can't recommend the Remastered version.Quick explanation:- AI pathing is somehow significantly worse than the original.- The game crashes often.- You need to manually save often as the crashes corrupt the current turn you are in.- Auto resolve battle ends in defeat most of the time regardless of force superiority.- New UI is clunky.For those who want more of an explanation I will elaborate.The original Total War: Rome (released 2004) had a fairly simple AI pathing system, however it worked fairly well and usually didn't cause stress. In the original Rome from almost 20 years ago ( I really want to stress this) you were able to position your troops tightly in city streets. The formation selector simply just showed red if the placement was invalid and yellow if you were good to go. You could tweak formations in order to get them just right.The new remaster that released in May of 2021 has 'updated' the formation selection tool to where it now auto-snaps. If you try and place units in a precarious alley it won't let you at all. (This becomes insanely annoying when working with war dogs)  The War dog unit does not have a 'formation' they form as a gaggle, this makes them unable to be placed anywhere besides dangerously far from the city square near an opening.Fighting in small towns near the city square. If you have been playing Total War for a while you already know how sometimes you are just going to be severely outnumbered. In the original this wasn't an issue due to the forgiving unit formation placement. Once the battle got going repositioning units wasn't going to cost you the battle.Unfortunately in the 'improved' Remastered the AI doesn't seem to recognize they are in a city square, in fact it seems that the AI doesn't really know what's going on at all. Most of the time engagements requiring reinforcements from units within the square will have them path back to the flag and than out to the side. This obviously takes a significant amount of time. Unsurprisingly having units completely expose their back to reposition just a few feet away will end up costing close to have your unit.Specifically spear men, in the original they would remain in their Phalanx formation with spears down forward. In the Remastered version the AI more often than not will switch to their secondary which will cost the battle especially when playing as one of the Barbarian factions.Another thing that has to be micromanaged like crazy is all of the units are set to auto run EVERYWHERE. So if you give a command they are running. I am used to the original where you would need to double click to make your units run. I found out vary fast after getting into a few battles where all of my units were exhausted before the fighting even occurred. Another issue with the AI pathing is just battles in general. For example in the original telling your cavalry to charge ahead of them would result in the cavalry charging directly in front of them.... you know like how you ordered.  In the new Remaster if you position the cavalry to the side of say ... a Phalanx formation and tell them to assault their very vulnerable side there is a very good chance the cavalry will get close to the side, come almost to a stop and reposition in front of the phalanxes and then proceed to attack... This is incredibly frustrating.The new 'optimized' AI pathing is just really bad.Another big negative is this game crashes a decent amount. This wouldn't be so much of an issue if it didn't corrupt that turn. Not sure what sets it off. It is usually when ending a turn and when the enemy AI tries to break a siege. Manually fighting the battle will end in my game hard freezing at first contact with the enemy. I can consistently reproduce this.The only fix is to break the siege and then try again next turn (pretty frustrating). Or reload from a previous save from a few turns ago.Merchants? Why? They don't add anything. Should of focused on not absolutely destroying the AI.My last gripe which is just a minor inconvenience is the auto-resolve battle function is now completely useless. Sometimes I do not want to waste time taking my army of Gothic cavalry and spearbands to fight 3 rebel peasants manually. However auto-resolve will just say it was a defeat most of the time. Or a 'Close Victory' where my army of 1500 troops vs 400 will absolutely get decimated. I absolutely love Total War: Rome. At the time of writing this I have just shy of 60 hours sunk into the Remastered version. I really, really, wanted to like this but the AI and crashing issue makes it hard to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Having recently purchased Rome Remastered with high hopes of a graphical and system upgrade, I was eager to dive back into the world of ancient warfare. However, my experience with the game left much to be desired.Gameplay and Mechanics:Rome Remastered's gameplay mechanics felt like a step backward compared to the original and its sequel, Rome 2. While I expected smoother gameplay and more intuitive controls, I found myself grappling with a less user-friendly interface and cumbersome systems. From managing resources to commanding armies, the game lacked the depth and polish that made its predecessors so compelling. Battles, once the heart of the Total War experience, felt lackluster. The absence of diverse formations and unlockable abilities stripped away layers of strategy, leaving engagements feeling shallow and predictable.Visuals and Graphics:The promise of improved graphics in Rome Remastered was enticing, but unfortunately, it fell short of expectations. Rather than a visually stunning update, the game's aesthetic veered towards a cartoonish style reminiscent of lesser-known titles like Evony. While some may appreciate this artistic choice, it felt out of place in a series known for its historical authenticity. Additionally, the stylized approach to presenting game information further detracted from the immersive experience that fans of the series crave, breaking the immersion and disconnecting players from the rich world of ancient Rome.Performance and Stability:One of the most glaring issues with Rome Remastered is its performance and stability. Reports of frequent lags, game freezes, and crashes have plagued the experience for many players, even without the use of mods. These technical shortcomings not only hinder gameplay but also erode confidence in the overall quality of the game. As someone who values a smooth and uninterrupted gaming experience, these issues were particularly frustrating and ultimately soured my impression of Rome Remastered.Recommendation:While Rome Remastered may evoke nostalgia for those fond of the original game, I cannot wholeheartedly recommend it to players seeking an enjoyable Total War experience centered in antiquity. For a more immersive and well-rounded gaming experience, I urge players to consider Total War Rome 2. With its superior gameplay mechanics, visually appealing graphics, and greater stability, Rome 2 offers a more satisfying journey into the ancient world of warfare.Conclusion:In summary, Rome Remastered falls short of its promise to enhance the classic Total War experience. With lackluster gameplay mechanics, unappealing visuals, and significant performance issues, the game fails to capture the magic of its predecessors. For those seeking a truly satisfying dive into ancient warfare, Total War Rome 2 remains the better choice.Recommendation:While Rome Remastered may evoke nostalgia for those fond of the original game, I cannot wholeheartedly recommend it to players seeking an enjoyable Total War experience centered in antiquity. For a more immersive and well-rounded gaming experience, I urge players to consider Total War Rome 2. With its superior gameplay mechanics, visually appealing graphics, and greater stability, Rome 2 offers a more satisfying journey into the ancient world of warfare.

_childDocuments_.review: Total War: Rome (the original) is possibly my favourite game of all time. Unfortunately the advent of Windows 10 made it (along with most of the rest of my games on disc) difficult, if not impossible to play. The Steam version worked, but lagged badly, which took away a lot of the enjoyment that this game once gave me. Needless to say, I was ecstatic to learn that there would be a remastered version. I made my pre-ordered purchase and waited eagerly for the day that I could once again lead the Julii to their rightful domination of the known world!Unfortunately, the remastered version has been pretty disappointing. The colour of the maps is nice, but putting all the pop-up screens in beige (I know, it's supposed to be "marble") with faint gray letters are a major strain on these old eyes. The ease of access that was so appreciated in the original version is also gone. I now find myself flipping through multiple pop-ups to find the simplist of information that I need. Adding merchants (which I've never liked) was another fail. Merchants were a poor addition to Total War: Medieval 2 (where the AI always seems to have merchants that can easily destroy the player's ones) and a very unnecessary addition to the remastered version. Overall, the remastered Rome is a bust.The good news for the Total War franchise is that the majority of the fixes are simple. Change the colour schemes back to the original palettes. Make the lettering darker and easier to read. Keep the merchants or not. They're mostly a distraction, but you might as well leave them in unless their removal is also a simple fix. If possible, change the access screens back to the original version's. The beauty of the original game lies in it's simplicity. "If it ain't broken, don't fix it!" Maybe TW can make an updated version patch that fixes and restores the glory that was once Total War: Rome.Until then, I'd wait for a heavy discount on the purchase price, or hope that your original version doesn't lag.Now about Total War: Medieval...I'd love a "remastered" version of the original. Make it playable without crashes and change nothing. :)
