_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished the Scipii long campaign I thought it high time to write my first ever steam review.Some backgroundI am what is sometimes referred to as a Total War Boomer. I mainly played Rome and Medieval 2, and I know and love the mechanics of these games.Total War (and gaming in general) has made a lot of progress since Rome was first released, most of these changes are good, however I do not have the time and energy to invest in learning the mechanics of newer Total War games, the new games therefore have little appeal to me. I also play a little guitar, and the first song I learned to play in full was Transilvanian Hunger by Darkthrone.The pro's* I can play Rome Total War again!* I can play a Total War game of which the mechanics I understand.* The graphics update is really good, it may not be as detailed as some of the modern Total War games, yet it manages to look fresh and familiar.* The updated campaign map gets some criticism, yet I really like the bright and living colours of this map.* Some slight improvements were made, making the barbarian factions better playable at the endgame and the AI a bit smarter.* Diplomacy can actually work now.* Steam achievements were added including one named Transilvanian Hunger, which I like since I can play that song!The cons* The new UI is horrible and counterintuitive, even once you get used to it, it just is not good.* Pathfinding is still bad, especially during sieges. During normal battle's I prefer the pathfinding to the newer Total War, because I know how it works, I understand this can be a real turn off if you play newer Total War games.Conclusion* Buy this if you are a Total War boomer who wants to play a Total War game you know , love and understand.* Buy this if you like Total War in general and it is on sale.* Don't buy this if you don't like playing outdated games.Now I'm off to start a short Dacia campaign to get that Transilvanian Hunger achievement.

_childDocuments_.review: There are many different types of Total War fans, so when I look at the reviews it makes me really sad. Rome Remastered is beautiful. They overhauled all the graphics, UI, as well as many other quality of life improvements. There are small changes here or there that need improvements, but Rome Remastered is truly faithful to the original game.  The reality is over the last 15 years the Total War Franchise has changed drastically and created a wide variety of fans with a wide variety of tastes.  The largest split I feel exists, as I am part of it, is between the Fantasy/Historical Drama lovers who love the Individual story arcs of the new games and those who do not like the direction the new games face.  Personally I absolutely abhor most of the new game mechanics implemented in the new games. The 3 Warhammer games with the fantasy element have completely alienated me. I have no desire to take dragons and orcs into battle with me. I also have no desire to watch Heroes literally tear holes through entire units in Troy and Three Kingdoms the few times I play out a battle. The older Total War games like Rome were great to me because I was able to min-max an economy and in Rome abuse growth rates to hit the Marian Reforms quickly. It may have been simple but at the time there was no other mainstream game like that. The 3D battles were great, but honestly outside of the first campaign battle, I would seldom choose to fight out a battle unless I had to cheese it. I played the early Total Wars because you got to paint a campaign map with semi-historical overtones that the newer games don't necessarily lack, but there now there far better alternatives in the Paradox Games. Do not get me wrong, Total War's battles are what makes the series unique, but for many it was just a part of the game and enjoyed it because of the historical realism of their sims. Over the 6 years the Paradox Games have become a fringe franchise only few die hard strategy gamers have heard of to mainstream. I believe it has been helped along by Paradox capturing this type of demographic. Sure its not 1 for 1 people are complicated. The Game of Thrones mod is one of the best mods for CK2, but for some people it was less about the battles and literally painting your color on the map. Which leads me back to the negative reviews. Please stop bombing an older title because it does not have the same feel as a newer Total War, especially when Creative Assembly did its very best to integrate old and new TW players with so many different settings options. When I hear comments like , "It's AI is bad" what does it matter to you if they AI is bad when Hero's basically act like an army of Bezerkers in every battle. At least Bezerkers are a unit rather than 1 individual. I totally get why many people find that feature awesome. I am not trying to throw shade at you. It clearly works monetarily for CA!Many older Total War players liked the franchise for a different reasons and a REMASTER should not get review bombed, "because I don't like it". And there is a huge difference between "I don't like it because it doesn't play like a modern total war" and I don't like it because "They ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up the remaster and it is no longer faithful to the original title".

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful and respectful remaster of the original with some marginal issues.The UI is... Not great, unfortunately. Not awful, but definitely more designed for aesthetics than functionality. It definitely takes some getting useful.Graphics are solid, and keep very close to the original game's style. The option to switch between the bright colours of the classic game's units and a slightly more realistic darker hue is a welcome feature, as well.Gameplay changes are almost universally improvements over the original, and the ability to toggle individual elements between the classic and modern functionality allows you to pick and choose which changes you want to keep.Mod support is even better than the original, though we'll have to wait and see whether anything is made to match the heights of Europa Barbarorum or Roma Surrecta.All in all, a solid remaster that you should definitely play if you enjoy classic Total War. HOWEVER, the price is definitely excessive, especially if you don't get the loyalty discount from owning the original. In that case, or if you pick it up after the discount ends, I would strongly suggest waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, this is a remaster, I was not expecting a remake, LOL'ing at all the people dismissing legitimate criticisms of the remaster by saying people were expecting a remake. A remasters job should be to give it a fresh look and (in theory) make it the superior version to play. Many remasters have accomplished this, both on PC and console, it's not rocket science, and I was excited that Feral was also putting a bunch of QoL improvements in as well. I was excited to play it.The problem it seems is that Feral massively overstepped what they needed to do. All they needed to do was improve the graphics and just release it. All they had to do.There are certainly some improvements over the original here. I like the new diplomacy insights you can get, as well as both the battle and campaign map overlays. Merchants are a fine inclusion, doesn't really change the game much, but still. Night battles in vanilla are cool, as are the variation between individual soldiers (and horses!). There are some minor improvements to the campaign and battle AI, but I didn't really notice a big difference, and I also played a siege battle and the pathfinding is basically the same as before, there are minor balancing tweaks but nothing major. The battle camera is much better in the remaster.I am not a fan of the graphics. Sure, the armor and buildings look objectively better, but Feral has tacked on so many lighting effects that watching battles looks like you're playing in 720p, not 1080 or 4K, like someone smeared vaseline all over your screen, and this was after I turned off distortion effects and bloom and such, do not even attempt to play with those on because it makes battles unplayable. I also turned down the saturation completely as it looks like complete garbage turned up, like a cartoon basically. The water definitely looks better, but I'm not a fan of the overall style, I prefer the originals.And none of these minor changes make a difference when the UI makes the campaign almost unplayable. Prepare to dig through many menus before finding what you want to do, and also prepare to squint whenever you're on the campaign map because unit and building cards and information are much too small. Yes, it is only the UI, but especially in battles, where you need to be micromanaging all of your units and mere seconds between orders can mean victory or defeat, having a spread out and unintuitive UI makes, you know, real-time battles, a chore and nearly unplayable. I dreaded having to manage my empire in the campaign, why the ♥♥♥♥ did they think it was okay to put the notifications behind several different menus for you to even access? In the original you could quickly click through them and also remove them by right clicking in a matter of seconds, there was absolutely nothing wrong with it. Nor was there any issues with the UI really, all they had to was upscale the images and textures and boom, done, all you had to do. It looks identical to the mobile port of Rome and that absolutely is why the UI looks the way it does, in the year 2021 we still have major gaming companies compromising PC releases of games for mobile because they don't feel like making two separate versions. There's also many bugs too. I had a crash within the first hour of playing, the game is poorly optimized (seriously, it doesn't even look that good and has trouble running on my PC which isn't the best but can play modern strategy games no problem on Ultra at 60 FPS), load times are horrendous, even with an SSD, and the pre-battle speeches have a delay between the commanders final statement and the cheering, which obviously isn't a big issue but completely ruins the impact of the speeches. You also cannot click space once on the campaign map to have the units move quickly, you have left click after order, every single time, why did they change this??? I seriously don't understand.Theoretically, these issues can be fixed in a patch, which is what I'm currently waiting for. If they aren't fixed, or there isn't a mod that fixes the godawful UI within 2 weeks, I will be refunding this and just sticking to the original. I was also excited about the steam mod support, because I'm too lazy to mod Rome myself, but the ease of modding is certainly not worth all the negative changes made to this game. I honestly cannot believe they're charging people $15, let alone $30 for this.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not perfect, but it's got the under-the-hood changes that will serve to make this game the heart of a vibrant modding community for another two decades.The UI isn't great, but it isn't bad.  It just needs polished up and it'll be fine.  That said, like a lot of modern games, the UI focuses on using pseudo-windows, which wastes a tremendous amount of space.  I'm fine with it not being the old UI, but you shouldn't be squinting at 1080p like this.Here's some small gripes:They added arrow trails because you physically cannot see arrows anymore.The escape key is really clunky now.The message center is a neat idea, but it shouldn't replace start-of-turn popups entirely.  Give me both.  I shouldn't need to go to it to see that I have a Man of the Hour prompt, which most players are now going to miss out on.The in-game wiki is currently borked on linux.There are a lot of pathing issues with cities now, and you can't issue multiple units onto walls or bridges.As for the good?Performance is great, and the game only chugged at 3x game speed with nearly 12,000 men on the battlemap, with the new graphics.The balance changes have introduced more challenge into the game, and it's good that cavalry isn't impossibly overpowered now.Managing the large amount of characters and settlements late game is far easier than in the original, and once they sort out the agent UI I'm sure that will be great,

Some of the gameplay changes do help like the squalor fix and the various small tweaks to the gameplay like night time battles, better diplomacy, better AI and merchants are good too so they did make some positive changes.Overall I think almost everything good about this game is directly because of the original and a lot of the changes they made are unnecessary and just hinder the experience. All they had to do was make it look good and make the small gameplay fixes, that's it. Why couldn't they just do that without butchering the UI and messing up the controls?

_childDocuments_.review: After quite a while getting used to the new UI which is not hugely intuitive I have started to really enjoy playing this game. The battles are so much better than later iterations of Total War with a proper morale mechanic that rewards tactical gameplay as well as proper formations and damage that makes it feel much more like a tactical battle than the arcadey feel of the later games. On the campaign map too I'm really enjoying the depth of the strategic gameplay with a traits and ancillaries system which again hugely outdoes the later versions, senate missions, detachable units, freedom to build and upgrade all cities as well as towers and forts. Plus a diplomacy system that actually makes sense, with factions accepting ceasefires when they're losing a war. The graphical enhancements as well with unit variation adds just a little bit more realism for extra immersion although Egypt is still hugely anachronistic. All in all it feels like a proper Total War game and I'm starting to remember how I felt when the original Rome came out when I was young! I would definitely recommend this game. The only drawback is I'm a mac user and so cannot use any mods but I'm enjoying vanilla so much at the moment it doesn't seem too bad although I'm looking forward to getting a PC in the future and playing some of the mods such as Imperium Surrectum.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this review by saying that my recommendation is not permanent, and may change over time. I will explain why in the paragraphs below.The game has great potential. Building upon the mighty RTS that is Rome: Total War, the Remastered edition brings with it updated graphics, new campaign features (including merchants!), Steam workshop support, a modern RTS camera, 4K support, as well as included remasters of the Barbarian Invasion and Alexander expansions. Units are much more detailed and have variation in how they look, adding to the immersion of the game. The legendary soundtrack of the original game was even kept, adding to the already-existing nostalgia.However, the game has quite a bit of bugs, the worst in my 1 hour of playtime being the absolutely horrendous path-finding. AI units will often take long routes to where you want them to go, often going in the complete opposite direction, or even refusing to move entirely. This, inevitably, leads to frustration as you see your men getting massacred as they run through enemy units when you told them to run away from the enemy. This is a game-breaking bug for me, and I will be waiting until patches to play again.All-in-all, I'd say wait until these issues are resolved before picking this up. The bugs are too much right now to be enjoyable, at least for me. That being said, the game has incredible potential to be a faithful remaster of the original, with many welcomed quality-of-life and gameplay improvements. Please fix the bugs, CA!

_childDocuments_.review: Here is what you really need to know if you're still on the fence;1) The game is about 50GB with the optional HD texture pack, without it it's about half that size. I would recommend the HD texture pack if you have the space. My specs are a 1070, i7-10700K and 64GB of RAM for comparison. I have zero issues or lag even with everything maxed out and on highest resolution and settings. So if you meet or exceed my specs, then you can just max it all out and have no problems. If not, no worries because it didn't break 37% of my cpu capacity and even with like 50 tabs of chrome open at the same time, my RAM usage didn't break 26% and 25% is where it sits with all the other programs I have open currently. GPU sat at about 63% at max load. Nothing was running full tilt so don't be scared off if you have an older computer. 2) It's almost exactly like the original Rome Total War. If you want a modern Rome Total War experience then buy this. If you want this game to play exactly like a carbon copy of the original, then just play the original. What does modern mean? Better camera and controls just like Rome 2, Attilla, Warhammer, etc... Don't like that? Then play some Bye Bye Bye and boot up the 2004 version. 3) AI. As usual, it can be bad but not game breaking. The AI will sometimes make laps during sieges no matter how much damage they take. They also won't sally forth (at least so far during my couple dozen or so sieges) so currently if you break down a wall or gate the enemy will just chill and patiently wait for your assault. Sometimes units will break formation but not that often and not in a way that will destroy your lines. From what I've seen if your units are in guard mode and beat back an attack, sometimes one unit will move forward or back slightly from the others. Last issue is sometimes the pathfinding is not great so double check the paths to make sure no one goes where they aren't supposed to. Aside from these issues it plays just fine. 4) Graphics. The textures are good, but some of the units have a very pale, almost zucc-like skin tone. Aside from that the developer was honest in all promotional pictures, so if you can run it on max settings expect gameplay just like in the promotional pictures and videos. You can also enable unit variation to give the units a similar appearance to the ones in Attila and Rome 2. If you don't like that, you can turn that off. 5) Expect the original Rome Total War units, campaign, etc... with the functions of Atilla and Warhammer in this game. If that doesn't sound good to you, then this game isn't for you. If you want to relive the days of Rome Total War without having to finding install disks then this is it. You can even view your towns develop in first person and use the old school cheats. It's exactly what they promised, an updated Rome Total War.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'm someone who didn't play the original Rome: Total War. I was four years old when that game released, so there is no nostalgia factor involved in my review.I'm someone who's played most of the prime Total War titles and really enjoyed Rome 2, Empire, and Medieval 2. Out of the first 4 hours that I've played of this game, it definitely holds up with the latest TW titles as long as you come with reasonable expectations.This game is a remaster, not a whole new game. If you thought you were getting Troy campaign maps and Warhammer level cinematic battles, I don't know what planet you're on. This is a game that came out 17 years ago. If they wanted to make Rome 3, they would have done so instead of releasing this. Either way, here's why I believe this game is a really solid title to play:- The campaign is simply deeper than many of the newer total war games, especially Rome 2. There's a lot more strategy involved in Rome 1. You don't feel like the overpowered monster you were in Rome 2 while playing as Rome, at least in the early game. The Gauls have given me plenty of trouble so far. In Rome 2, they were basically a rag tag group of small stack armies that didn't put up much of a fight.- For being 17 years old, the remaster pulls off battles well. I won't call them amazing. I would much rather play Rome 2 battles in all honesty, but once again, this game is 17 years old. The fact that it even looks as good as it does is astounding and lots of props to Feral for redeveloping the textures. Battling with your generals and faction leaders also makes battles feel noticeably heavier. You don't want them to die. There's an attachment to them that you never really feel in Rome 2. It's also fun to keep track of their traits and stats. This is common in Total War but the added emotional attachment makes them more Crusader Kings-like. - There's a confidence in this game that radiates. It feels polished, as if it's had 17 years to craft its identity. Playing this as a newcomer, I can tell how strong this game was back in its hay day. While it isn't a revolutionary game compared to its modern counterparts, it's the type of game that you know can stand the test of time — as it has. You don't feel this in many of the newer titles. Most of the new ones, besides Warhammer, have been these one-off games like Brittania, Three Kingdoms, or Troy. Total War is starving for a landmark historical series.- This game has limitless potential. As of this review, we're only on the second day of this game being out and a mod that enables naval combat has already been released. Like what? For anyone who thinks the game lacks depth and needs some of the more modern Total War extras, I'm sure a mod will cover you sometime soon. It's absolutely insane how modders have already released stuff on the Workshop. I can't wait to see what gets added.There are definitely issues with the game. Some of which will probably be fixed in future patches. But I can see how someone might be turned off by the classical nature of Rome 1. It's not a streamlined experience, it's not a battle-focused game, battle AI isn't incredible, and sometimes units break for like absolutely no reason. But beyond those issues, most of which modders will probably take care of. This is a deep, fun, and classic Total War experience. It challenges you, it forces you to think, to weigh options, and to make sacrifices. I've been playing TW for a long time. This game is really good.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could redirect half of what I paid for this game to the Imperium Surrectum team. With that mod, this game is for me the best Total War experience I've ever had. The large, but detailed map really is a gamechanger. Every part of your empire feels alive, planning a military campaign takes time and effort, recruiting soldiers from all over your cities feels like your whole society is involved in the effort. Mountains and the sea are actual natural barriers. The interaction with neighbor  states is intense because of the many settlements, but at the same time it takes some time to come into contact with civilizations further away. Which at first seems boring, but the immersion is fantastic. Imagine playing Rome, slowly grinding your way through Italy, consolidating at the bottom of the Alps..Finally crossing them and then finding out there are hordes and hordes of Gauls ready to slaughter you. I've seen people complain about the difficulty of the mod, but honestly if you find some guide / video about how to survive the early game (mostly cleaning up financially), after that it really gets fun. And I'm saying that as a very casual player.

_childDocuments_.review: I first played Rome: Total War sometime in the mid 2000s in middle school. I was a big history nerd(still am lol) and i was just looking around at a small table of games at the book fair at school one day when i spotted this. I very much enjoyed ancient history and this game to a middle schooler was just perfect. I didn't know the treat i was in for when i paid for the box collection of Rome: Total War with all it's DLCs. I can say i enjoy this game. Do i have some complaints about the remastered edition? Well, yes. It's not perfect, but i can say it runs much better on a modern machine and has allowed me to enjoy the game from my middle school years that made me fall in love with total war games. This has been a treat and i very much plan to play more. Pros:-----------AI has been improved, britons actually use boats and pose a real threat in numbers with late game units, all the factions actually use their late game units and aren't bumbling around using militia and garbage tier units all day. You will be posed with a better challenge, though maybe not to the same extent to later games like the warhammer and shogun era stuff.-The graphics, while more colorful and not exactly true to the original, are an upgrade(of sorts) and feel pretty sleek and like it will age better than the original graphics thus preserving the game. -All factions(besides SPQR) have been added to the playable game without modding the files, which is nice. -Loads of achievements to unlock, giving you small semi goals. -Lots of graphical options to tune to your playstyle, including the "unit size" option that people love to tune up to huge/experimentally large(yourself included)Cons:------------UI does feel a bit meh?-Some annimations have a huge pause on the map screen where you're waiting for something to happen even when the animations have all been sped up you'll stare at an army who you know is going to attack your city and it takes a solid 5 to 10 seconds before the animation actually happens, which is annoying-The AI, while improved have taken to walking around your army to attack a city, which may have happened in the original(been a while since i've played the OG copy) but it's quite annoying to chase an army down and it just walks around you to annoyingly attack a city. -Some of the new balancing(which you can switch to the original) feels like an improvement in some ways and a huge nerf to units that didn't need to be nerfed in other ways. Overall, i do recommend this remaster pack especially since it includes the great DLC(even if alexander is not anyone's favorite, i enjoy it for what it is). If you enjoyed the original or are looking to try out the total war games, i highly recommend buying this - especially if you can catch it on a sale. I wish i still had my box set, i didn't know at the time that box sets of games would become rare and it'd be nice to look at the cover of it one more time.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited when I saw we are getting a remastered version of RTW. Sadly the curse that follows the Rome games is present in this one too. The UI feels like it was ported from a bad mobile game (in fact I prefer the old one much more). The pathfinding frequently gets your units stuck in cities to a point city battles are annoying. Phalanxes are broken, cavalry charges into the back of a phalanx has the units suddenly turn around - with the same phalanxes untouched from the cavalry charge. And speaking of cavalry charges, they're not as powerful as they were in old Rome. Confusing Battle AI decisions across the board (it takes you out of the game, what even are formations?) To elaborate the AI breaks its own formation to a point you can send a few cavalry units and kill the entire enemy army while the bugged pathfinding tries to sort itself out. Confusing Campaign AI decisions - the AI will send 6 javelin units to a fortified city, or a lone general unit will siege a city with walls.Diplomacy is a meme, but it was in the old one so they get a pass on this one.Audio issues across the board, music clipping and certain sounds not playing in combat, etc. For instance the Barbarian Warband has a sound you can hear from afar when they start to run/walk. Roman Melee units appear to not play any of these sounds. There's also an absence of actual fighting sounds and instances where one side will play their fighting sounds, the other won't.All in all a very disappointing remaster without a patch one month after release.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite not being a fully new experience, Rome Remastered achieves the feeling, play style, and the fun of Rome Total War, Original. If you were expecting a classic game updated for modern hardware and graphics, Rome Remastered is the game for you. In terms of gameplay and authenticity to the Ancient World, Rome Remastered does well and continues the themes of Rome 1. If you're coming into this looking for an authentic Antiquity warfare experience, I'd recommend Rome 2 with the Divide et Impera mods over this, however, Rome Remastered nails the classic Total War ambiance, experience, and units. In addition, in terms of visuals, Rome Remastered with the "Realistic" unit option does an excellent job of representing the units of Antiquity in a true to life form.Some people may say that the game is just the same old Rome and not enough was done to it, but this is exactly what I wanted from a Remaster of my favorite game. I'm glad they kept the scope of the project to revitalizing the game and modernizing it, avoiding the pitfall of a far too ambitious remake instead of remaster. If you loved the original Rome Total War, then this remaster is for you. If you're expecting a brand new game, this is not for you, and would not be a remaster if it were so.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played almost every Total War title (except non historical one), spent hundreds of hours between them. This new remaster, is a great one (at least for me). It doesn't change much except for the graphics and a few tweaks (sadly the UI is worse than the original). The only negative aspect is the game arbitrarily need Windows 10 even though the game run perfectly with DirectX 11 (do they have a deal with Microsoft or is this just a lazy effort from Feral were went unanswered)If you are fans of the original and willing to look past it's worse UI, then you will enjoy this game, definitely, afterall the old Total War players are the main target of this remaster. It stills, in my opinion, far above later Total War titles including ROME II.

_childDocuments_.review: Calling this is a  is insulting when it's released in a sloppy and broken state.The game has 2 launchers you have to go through, with one being pointless, and the other having options that should have been left in the game itself. Before it lets you play it then stops you with a prompt requesting you to send them crash reports. It gives you 2 more prompts on the menu about the campaign, which they should have put in the campaign menu.There's 2 idents that both feel like jumpscares as the volume is so high and their sounds suddenly kick in. The intro of the original remains better even as a low resolution 4:3 video, as the intro to this one was clearly thrown together. The menu backgrounds look like they were done with the simple brush tool in MSPaint and have awkward animations - far worse than the original backgrounds (that were subtle). They added (useless) tips to loading screens (that already had a quote in them) which feel like trying to listen to 2 songs at the same time, as the attention should have been focused on just one.Where the original had decent optimisation to bring so many soldiers onto the screen, which seemed groundbreaking at the time, this remake 17 years later suffers with a poor framerate. By default you're only able to use a few factions. The campaign tutorial dragged on for about an hour, I was still confused about several mechanics that aren't explained, and the game wouldn't even let me save the campaign when the tutorial was finished. It  let me save my progress awhile later, but the unit size was then stuck on small - the scale of the game felt underwhelming.The campaign objective was to hold 15 provinces, but a notification said that Egypt was suddenly close to that, but I couldn't even see them on the map so it felt disconnected, if not just metagaming to react to. They're so far away that it was irrelevant, why would I try to rush forces all the way across the Mediterranean when so many factions randomly attack the armies and navies around Italy itself? Wasn't the game supposed to be about having fun playing as Rome? Why would you want that stopped just because of what some uncontacted faction was doing?Certain mechanics didn't have to be in the game, I can only give you my perspective on things that frustrated me. Like the fog of war existing in your own lands which makes "controlling" a province meaningless - yet it's a campaign victory condition. It left me wishing the objective of the game was more tangible. Regiments spread out when moving, which can make them unintentionally bump into enemy regiments. I was 5 hours in when I found the replenishment mechanic, so it ought to be reworked (or just explained clearly).You have to poke around the map to find cities. It's not clear if there's a construction limit to the number of different things you can build in a city, so planning is hopeless. I only got one regiment of archers and couldn't train more, so it felt a bit silly that the entire Roman army could only fire a few arrows per battle, assuming the battle even involved that one archer regiment.The AI puts units among trees, so your enemy has an artificial advantage because your camera view being blocked by the trees isn't something that stops AI from micromanaging its own units. There's so few points on the campaign map that units can stand on that it gets cluttered. Sometimes you can't move a unit where you want without having to collide with another, making unwanted interaction menus come up.The new graphics are pretty flat - not really appealing, and not charming like the original. There's quality of life issues like not being able to sort battle statistics by regiment kills, unit cards not being arranged by type, and the savegames being hidden in C:\Users\name\AppData\Local\Feral Interactive\Total War ROME REMASTERED\VFS\Local\RomeYou can't play naval battles. Trade isn't explained or shown in any depth, even in negotiation windows. The training queue doesn't show how many turns all the regiments will be ready by. Troops like Hastati are so slow to throw their missiles that they often get attacked without doing it. Cavalry often charge into friendly soldiers. I couldn't see any option for a multiplayer campaign.Nearly all the achievements are nonsense and have cringey names. The amount of friendly fire is shocking, forcing you have to constantly babysit your ranged units. There's a bizarre change from spacebar to right click to speed up campaign animations, and you can't toggle it off, so every time you want to move something you have to left click, then right click. I can't find an option to lower the campaign map scroll speed which is frustratingly high.Rebels randomly spawn for no reason and do nothing, and can disappear (rebellions can be fun if implemented well). Clicking on an enemy army to attack it on the campaign map sometimes just sends your army somewhere else. It's difficult to tell how much ammunition a regiment has at a glance, which was not a problem in the original.In  when AI tried to break a siege they'd just trigger a battle but then do nothing. If  try to break a siege in this game then the AI still does nothing. No matter which of the two you point to as having the fault, they should have fixed it. Potentially you can just go up to them and shoot them with archers (if the game let you train any), and they still won't do anything.Ranged units fire arrows after  is toggled off. Units can take up formations you didn't pick. I got night battle achievements despite the battle happening in daylight. Only 2 of 120 soldiers might actually fight when ordered to attack, but awkwardly the whole regiment gets "exhausted" by that. To move a few feet forward sometimes units often go on a long diversion during siege battles, which makes their journey longer and often causes them to unintentionally bump into the enemy getting themselves killed - wasting the interactivity of the game.It was nice to have a visualisation of the ranged units range, and for the game to be made with 16:9 screens in mind. For £24.99 I think it's terrible value considering all they really did was add a sloppy coat of paint to the original. They should have put some effort in, especially if they wanted people to pre-order it and outrageously then release it in a broken state. But their lack of care isn't surprising after they left previous titles in a bad way (like  with gamebreaking memory leaks). These kind of shoddy remakes often feel like cashgrabs that just split the playerbase if anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: After the June patch (2.0.1) the game is constantly crashing for me, and others (check discussions) after roughly 20 minutes or so. Doesn't matter if it is in battle, campaign, or menu. After contacting SEGA support and trying various fixes, they are no longer replying to my emails. I would not recommend this game until this issue is fixed. Crashing was not an issue before the June patch (only one crash in roughly 30 hours) but since the patch the game has crashed probably 30-40 times in 10 hours.---Original reviewIt's a really great remaster. One of the top complaints is about the UI, but once I was used to it, I prefer it to the original. The addition of a summery overlay is really helpful and makes for some good eye candy once you get a large enough empire built up. AI is somehow worse than the original, and I have extremely long load times with sieges (which is what a majority of your battles will be), despite having the game installed on my SSD and having more than enough capability on my hardware.One thing to keep in mind is any mods installed will disabled achievements, which is unfortunate. Most of them are fairly benign in nature (such as replacing unit cards with upscaled original) and don't change the gameplay at all.Overall though, I enjoy the remaster and would give it a 8/10. Would happily see a remaster of the other older Total War games, especially Med 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the old Rome total war, and played it A LOT back in the day. It's needless to say I was excited when the remastered version came out.The price was so high that I didn't feel it would be justified to pay that much for an old game. Finally I saw it on sale, and purchased it.Now to the review itself:To start things off I need to mention that I do not enjoy Rome 2. I feel like it doesn't have the familiar Total War feeling, the graphics are better but still in a way a lot worse. The game also has too much everyghint.IMO Rome remastered is basically the same game, with Rome 2's negative aspects. Literally, it feels like playing Rome 2.Rome 1 had an amazing feeling, just like Medieval 2, but this remastered version has taken it away completely, and just kind of mashed it together with Rome 2.To me these aspects from Rome 2 are just the things I dislike in the game, so the remastered version was basically a ruined version of a good old game.So TLDR of the negatives-They basically tried making it into Rome2. They added all the crappy things from Rome 2, but not the good things-Expensive-The feeling is NOTHING like the good old games had (Rome, Medieval 2 etc)-The catapults SUCK. How bad you ask? I've never seen anything like that before. They will miss 9/10 shots from a good range. They are terrible.Positives:None. You're better off just playing Rome 2, or the old Rome Total War.

_childDocuments_.review: Caveat Emptor. The OG Rome Total War worked great on my PC but i knew when I saw this I had to get it. Got it 50% off as part of the loyalty scheme. All the cheesey strats you know and love from the original remain but with much better performance and graphics.Many reviews on here are true, it is the same game and has some of the same weird quirks from the original, some can be frustrating, but, you cant not love them, good or bad. Performance issues, I havent had any, throughout all my hours on this. It is never going to compete on the level of a new release game. To hold it to that standard is to lose sight of what is to love about Rome TW. Truely a classic and hopefully thanks to this remaster, will have an extended life for years to come. One that I will always return to and probably never uninstall. Plus, achievements for gameplay now, satisfaction is immeasurable. To bastardise a quote from 'Kingdom of Heaven.' "What are achievements worth?" "Nothing" .... "Everything"

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played it for an hour and a half in both MP and SP. Thus far: * Zero crashes* Great performance @ 1440p* No major bugs noticed* Graphics are vastly superior to the original; people complaining it doesn't have the same graphics fidelity as the new games are brain dead. This game came out in 2004, and have you seen the original? Surprised they even got it to this level. * Overall, the game is faithful to the original. The toggles for the features are excellent - it allows people to avoid the new features if they so wish. That should be the standard across remakes; this sets the bar high. * Battle AI is still bad, but the AI is bad in every TW. Further, anyone expecting major improvement here was just fooling themselves. Again, this engine is ancient - there is only so much you can do!* UI is a little odd, but I am getting used to it. It is overall better than the original's UI on an objective level. * Faction cap increased to 31 (original was 21). This makes the modding potential huge. In the end, this is a remaster, NOT a remake. All of the wrinkles of the old game will remain present... but also all of the gems. RTW remains the standard to which I compare all TW games, and the remaster does exactly what it set out to do: improve the game in small ways, especially in the graphics dept (and make it much more optimized for modern PCs compared to the original), and STAY FAITHFUL to the original product. It accomplished that. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Strikes a good medium of being "new" and being old at the same time, while improvements such as combat AI are still missing the remaster cleans up a lot of old lingering problems that plagued the tail of the old Rome. In comparison to other remaster titles such as Age Of Empires II, Rome only falls short by not cleaning up lingering combat AI issues such as path finding and targeting. Changes to the UI can be toggled for the most part with other additional game elements like tracers for arrows can also be toggled. The Graphics can look jarring at times but it stays authentic to the original art asset by up-resing textures and adding additional poly counts. The price is pretty subjective as to what you value 15~30 USD I'd argue 15 is worth the price to simply have the game run on modern systems and the addition of Steam Workshop + increased modding capabilities will make this game will get better with ageIf you are worried and don't wanna take the risk wait to pick up in the future but its worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Total War: Rome Demastered is an attempt to remaster a beloved 2004 game that falls pretty much flat on its face in a number of ways. Simply put: the AI is still eligible to park in disabled spaces, diplomacy is only 'better' in that it shows more clearly how the useless diplomacy system is useless, still crashes as often as Richard Hammond, squalor feels worse than it did originally, mods get deleted sometimes, Senate missions are dafter than before and so onWorst of all: it hasn't the soul of the original. If somehow the mythical 'future update' that people allude to actually even attempts to fix some of these issues, I might recommend it. Otherwise, honestly, only buy this if you really want the originalEdit (since I'm still playing this game):Barbarian Invasion is now actually a lot more fun than the base game, back in the day it was a lot more unstable than the base game, now it's about on par, hence why I've doubled my playtime since originally reviewing this.

_childDocuments_.review: The new UI is designed entirely for form over function. It's like stripping the nutrition facts from the can to make it look sleeker, and then putting all that info in a smaller, harder-to-read format. Now I don't have any information to make snap decisions on.  Here are just some problems I've had so far:Can't tell how many soldiers are left in a unit without breaking focus and squinting at the unit card because now everything is in a smaller, more cluttered cardCan't tell the status/morale of a unit without doing the sameBecause they're smaller, unit cards are harder to tell apart and have less information presented in a harder-to-read format.The arrows showing future unit location are lower-contrast and difficult to see on some maps, especially at night. The orignal brighter, “clunkier” colors contrasted against everything.Have to wait a moment after hovering over a unit to see their infoHave to press an extra button just to get groups to lock formationFor some reason the camera scrolls more slowly than the 18 year old version. The original camera snapped right where you want it. It was very satisfying. _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: The game runs on modern machines, and allows cross-platform play, so get it if that's what you want. The graphics and UI are fine. Some control tweaks could be better. Of note, the battle control of units is slow and buggy at times for me, and occasionally worse than the original.I wanted to recommend this, and expected to from pre-launch videos and reviews, but the first hour or so of gameplay (on a 2016 Macbook Pro) had significant bugs. After a longer play session I feel more neutral about it, and at least don't think it deserves a negative review.Issues I found to be significant:-units, particularly ranged units, will spontaneously rearrange their formation against orders, sometimes pushing the front of the unit into combat or through the front of units in front of them. This appears to be a change from the original with the intent to improve city pathfinding, as the units reform to better fit the action ordered, but while this might improve movement when not at risk of battle, it can destroy command during battle.-units will fail to attack enemies with entirely overlapping formations, particularly if the enemy is routing: an issue when attacking, but even worse when my entire army (particularly 2 generals' cavalry) was incapable of running down any soldier in four almost full warband across a chase from the map corner reinforcement point to a siege gate, when none of the units started close to the settlement. It feels like an import of the Shogun 2 system, where units spent so much time trying to maintain formation that sometimes the best way to kill routing units was just to order the formation to stand still in the path the routing unit was heading.-the game runs slowly enough that command lag can be an issue even on the lowest settings, for a macbook pro. It also crashes semi-frequently, but the auto-save feature helps ameliorate this.Minor issues:-lack of hotkeys for some useful actions, like settlement details, or a lack of tooltips on hotkeys for the same, like locking groups-units occasionally refuse to disengage or cease firing, sometimes leaving a unit stuck for 30 ish seconds unresponsive. Luckily this happens rarely for me.-trees flicker constantly on the campaign map-even on low, the graphics run inconsistently and sometimes pixelated on a 2016 macbook pro; Shogun 2 however still runs like butter on medium, and looks better to boot-the steam achievements are very uninspired, it's discouraging that some basic skill achievements like win a heroic victory or beat a (non-alexander) campaign on VH/VH are missing. There are way too many achievements that feel gated by playtime and willingness to repeat campaigns, it takes some of the motivating fun out of the achievement idea.Neutral:-campaign AI seems to sped longer building armies and keeps them as one force more often, and seems more willing to let . This makes campaigns less war-focused and allows more of a turtle. Mostly, just an interesting difference.-some of the soldiers seem deathly pale or sickly. I find that hilariousPositive:-It works on Mac/Linux and cross platform play is feasible!-the graphics look like they could be pretty, if they fit the machine they were running on.-night battles and merchants are fun additions(edit: wish there was a neutral review option still. After more playtime, the issues I came across originally were less game-breakingly frequent, and considering it still managed to hold my attention well and I'll keep playing it, I don't think it deserves a negative review anymore)

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this remastered version of Rome: Total War. But I have to wonder if it really gave much added value over the original game. Yes you can play all the factions here - but with simple modding you could do that in the base game. Yes it has better gameplay - but the AI is still seemingly suffering in executing amphibious attacks or finding a path around in the steppes. This isn't to say there isn't some nice stuff here though. The camera improvements are certainly nice and being able to see information on an icon above ones troops when in battle is certainly convenient. I also like some of the little tweeks that enable changes to the gameplay - that you can turn on and off as you please; so horray, I can turn off those stupid Merchants, but leave the rest in!But is it worth the price? I can't say it really felt like it was worth the value in comparison to having already owned the previous game. Those with newer computers might not be able to run the original game though, so that might be a consideration for picking up this game; that and never having actually 'played' the original.I will note that in playing this game that I didn't experience any real issues. I had a rare crash here and there - but after 200+ hours of game time, I can't actually say it was worse then the original, which also tended to crash here and there.

_childDocuments_.review: Having put several dozen hours into the game at this point, I can say this is a pretty good remaster. Is it perfect? No, and nothing is or ever will be.Simply put if you wish to play Rome on a modern OS this is the way to go. I've played the original on and off over the years and yes it works okay on Windows 7, getting it to work on Windows 10 is nearly impossible and I even have the CD version. But besides that this version has so many quality of life improvements (quick saves during end turn battles, projectile range cones, tactical map, campaign map rotation, diplomatic success chance, etc.) that to list them all would be staggering. I cannot and would not take anyone who says "the original is better!" seriously, especially when virtually everything new can be toggled on/off.That said there are some downsides. The new Campaign Map UI is functional, but seems cumbersome and poorly laid out in some regards (recruitment & construction). Frankly this is one area where the original may be better. City pathfinding seems worse, but honestly it's always been bad so hard to definitively say if it's better or worse. Also there are some new bugs - for me audio from the campaign map playing while in battle. But other then that I've only had one CTD.I'm sure I could write a small essay here on Rome Remastered, but suffice to say it's worth playing. Whether you're nostalgic for the old game or have never played it before - it's worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Total War: Rome's remaster is in most ways superior to the original. Units have many more distinctive characteristics, such as the ability to alter their appearance depending on the area where they were recruited. The AI for the battle and campaign maps has been enhanced to be more difficult. The addition of Steam Workshop functionality in the remastered version makes a significant improvement. Most of the original game's active modders have either switched to the remastered version or had their creations move over. Mods like Mundus Magnus and Roma Surrectum, as well as others, are included in this. With the Steam Workshop, there is no need to use zip files or search through fan sites for different installers and patches.The campaign's and the fights' user interfaces have improved from the original as well. A bit of comedy has also been implemented in the game, making you chuckle or shake your head in amazement. Despite its many positive aspects, Total War: Rome Remastered does have some annoying elements. Sometimes the game will crash out of nowhere for seemingly for no reason, and you would lose your progress on that turn, may it be a battle or fixing up your settlements. However, overall, if you like the previous installment of this game (TW: Rome), this game might reignite your liking of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mess with very little improvements over the original and arguably even worse. The UI is dull, unimaginative, lacks color, doesn't scale well, text doesn't scale, unit cards are small and ugly even at 120% scaling. Menus are behind menus. Family tree is still buried and portraits are unfinished, notifications are behind a hidden menu, diplomacy screen isn't modernized,  I play on very hard because that's how I played the original and because the enemy will insta-rout on easier settings, battles are over in 5 mins or less. Battles and sieges are terrible because pathing wasn't fixed, animations are terrible and sped up, and units rout too fast and often don't even have to be touched before running away. Units will refuse to form a line and lose formation, units get stuck on walls, trees, rocks, and sometimes on nothing at all. Your units will do a little dance in a circle instead of listening to orders. Units fail to skirmish properly, phalanxes fail to form, and units take nonsensical routes to their destination. Units aren't balanced, enemy cavalry are ridiculously overpowered even versus spear units. A triarii should hold up for a little while to a cavalry unit but the horses melts one of the strongest early game units just the same as if they were peasants. Ironically attacking a phalanx in the rear with cavalry destroys your horsemen instantly, obviously bugged or broken. The mass that units have are all off, the push effect is way too strong and unnatural.So, really the only thing that they truly remastered in a good way was the graphics. They are much better than the original but honestly that's a very low bar. The units look better, the vegetation looks better, the cities and buildings are better... the background and sky box however are blurry smudged up images. The campaign map is improved but yet feels like it's not as detailed as it could be and loses it's luster when you zoom in. There's many discussions on what a "remaster" really means vs a remake. Honestly, it doesn't matter. Either the final product is good or it's bad and it will be judged on those merits alone. This is still a bad game and there was very little effort into making the gameplay, the battles, the pathing, and the unit balancing better than the original. This isn't a re-master, it's a re-mediocre. I can't recommend this product because it's just not that much better than the original that was made 17 years ago. I feel like nothing was learned by the developer given there's 17 years of improvements and balancing modders have fixed within those years. The only shining light at the end of the tunnel here is that this version is easier to mod and once again CA will push for their game to be saved by the modding community.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the first thing I want to point out is don't buy or play this game if you want to feel nostalgic. If you are a true Total War fan and would like to have Total War: Rome REMASTERED in your library, you can buy it and play it. However, this game is a Remaster, not an entirely Remake. By knowing this, buy and play the game. Otherwise, you will be grievously disappointed.Although there are new elements and improvements, naturally, there are mostly improvements without going beyond graphic enhancement. However, I prefer the AI ​​of Rome: Total War to the AI ​​of Total War: Rome REMASTERED. In the REMASTERED version, both the campaign map and battle AI are disgraceful; at least that's how I experienced it. Units change formations just randomly. Sometimes they are acting like I'm not giving the order them to do something. The only bad thing about the REMASTERED version is the AI, and it is bad, really bad. I mean it!However, the game has its advantages, too. Total War: Rome REMASTERED appears to be a completely new game that was not released as an improvement over the original Rome: Total War. This is the point that makes me worried. So, it also means they're changing artificial intelligence. If only they hadn't... From the graphics improvements to the game's REMASTERED version, there are more user-friendly elements in the game, also new contents that we haven't seen in the original Rome: Total War. The game supports ultra HD resolution. There's also amazing updated 3D unit models and textures, widescreen and ultra-wide monitor support. Not to mention the new agent Merchant, of course. The atmosphere of war, campaign map and visual effects are also included in the graphic development. The new pieces of information and lines on the faction, trade, summary, etc. screen and unit information screens on the campaign map of the game have also been improved. In addition, improved camera and control settings have been added to the game. In addition to these, there are also quick access lists to facilitate access.Overall, it is a good game to experience Rome: Total War with good graphics and atmosphere, but as I said before; "...don't buy or play this game if you want to feel nostalgic. If you are a true Total War fan and would like to have Total War: Rome REMASTERED in your library, you can buy it and play it. However, I would like to point out that the game is Remaster, not Remake. By knowing this, buy and play the game. Otherwise, you will be grievously disappointed."By the way, I started with Julii, and defeated the Gauls, fought with Britannia and Spain to the death, did Marian Reforms, conquered half of Europe, hit to top on the economy; that was a good experience. But, I'm not talking about AI.

_childDocuments_.review: "Rome: Total War Remastered" revitalizes a classic of the strategy game genre, enhancing its visuals and mechanics while preserving the depth that made the original a landmark. This remastered version breathes new life into the grand campaigns of ancient empires, offering sharper graphics, improved interfaces, and modernized features that make the intricate gameplay more accessible to both returning fans and newcomers.One of the highlights of the remastered edition is its inclusion of the iconic expansions: "Barbarian Invasion" and "Alexander." "Barbarian Invasion" thrusts players into the tumultuous period of Rome’s decline, allowing them to either fight to preserve the crumbling empire or lead the barbarian hordes to carve out kingdoms of their own. This expansion enriches the narrative with a dramatic, dark-age backdrop and challenges players with complex new scenarios that test their strategic prowess in entirely different ways.The "Alexander" campaign, on the other hand, offers a more focused narrative, detailing the ambitious conquests of Alexander the Great. This campaign is notably challenging, as players must replicate Alexander’s rapid expansion across an enormous map, from Greece to the fringes of India. The campaign's tight timeline and massive battles capture the relentless drive and strategic genius of one of history’s most legendary conquerors.Both expansions benefit greatly from the remastered version’s enhanced visuals and streamlined gameplay. The improved UI and AI make for a smoother strategic experience, while the graphical upgrades bring battles to life with stunning detail, from the clash of swords to the dramatic landscapes over which these epic wars are fought."Rome: Total War Remastered" is not just a nostalgia trip; it's a comprehensive upgrade that makes an already great game even better. With its engaging blend of deep strategy, sprawling campaigns, and historical immersion, this remaster is a must-play for strategy enthusiasts eager to experience one of the genre's best in modern glory. Whether defending the glory of Rome, riding with the barbarian hordes, or marching across Asia with Alexander, this game delivers a robust and thrilling historical strategy experience.

_childDocuments_.review: While the reviews are a mixed, I feel that is from how it was marketed. The AI is just as terrible as it was during the original release. While having glaring issues if you are an fan of the original game you will love this game just as much. The camera is a million times better than it used to be and the new features add a little spice to the mix. Another added benefit is the modding community that will be coming to this game, I feel the real fun will start in a few weeks. Hope Medieval 2 is next!

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommended. Flaws of this remaster are obvious from the start:- Horrible pathfinding especially in siege battles. Units take strange detours, sometimes freeze in place for several seconds and often break formation for no reason (usually during forementioned detours). I played original Rome TW couple of weeks ago and don't remember pathfinding being this bad. It seems the problem has emerged (or at least worsened) during remastering process.- New and "improved" UI is a mess. For example, in the original we had one simple settlement panel from which we could manage everything about the settlement: Governor, auto-manage options, taxes, building and recruiting. In remaster, instead of one menu to rule them all, the same information and functionality is scattered between three separate menus/panels for you to jump between. Extremely bad UI design and I cannot fathom how anyone could call this an improvement upon original. Changes are pointless and only serve to make stuff you need harder to find.- This last complaint is pretty nitpicky, but it was the final deal breaker for me: Speaking of bad UI design, for some unknown reason developers have bundled save and load menus into one. It's kinda obvious why this is a bad idea: At the end of my last session I navigated to this menu to save my progress. Routinely I double-clicked my saved game only to find out that double-click doesn't actually save your game; it loads it. Thus I lost all progress made during my last turn. So be extra careful to always use mouse over buttons for saving and loading as otherwise mistakes are prone to happen. Fortunately the game auto saves often so not much progress was lost, but after all the other annoyances, this was the last straw for me.I will probably refund the game if it doesn't get some major  during the next couple of weeks. Honestly, a simple stability and compatibility update for the original would have made me so much happier. Improvements here are hit-and-miss... but mostly miss.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a remaster with some great features. Nothing is made significantly worse, but many things are made slightly to significantly better.GOOD: 1) the strategic view on the campaign map with the Public Order overlay makes it easy to see when corners of your empire are getting angry at your leadership; Very helpful2) when you hit end turn, the game pops up a message about idle armies, navies, agents, settlements, etc. This is very helpful to avoid forgetting about distant armies. You can ignore it if you want, but it's helpful when you need it.3) After you hit end turn and the game is doing all your queued multi-turn moves, the game allows you to update orders if a path gets blockedBAD: 1) There is no way to speed up movement on the campaign map by default. You must always click twice or tap R after telling an army/agent/etc to move. How could they overlook something this basic?2) Armies look blurry at a distance. Honestly when zoomed out, Medieval 2 has better graphics. Units turn into a semi-unintelligible blob when the camera is far away3) The construction and recruitment systems are kind of wonky. It would be nice if they were always there when a city is selected, but they are not. There's no need to make me click an extra button when I just want at a glance information.4) I wish I could see what buildings are in a settlement and what armies are in it at the same time. This was a problem in the original, so it isn't like this is worse, but it isn't better either... And I think they could have fixed this.

_childDocuments_.review: not a true remaster.  In truth this is more of a unit reskin than a proper remaster.  The overall quality of the game is severely lacking, poor amateurish school kid level artwork,  limited repetitive loading screens, ugly truly hideous cumbersome UI (a real tedious clickfest) and a garish fluorescent toxic waste effect campaign map.  The original UI was fluid and intuitive this is like wading through mud.  It's vastly inferior to the classic UI, it's obviously designed for touchscreens and not the pc mouse.  Not only is the UI vandalised but the wonder and agent videos have also been discarded,  it's very much a "streamlined" version of Rome.Gone are the iconic abstract soldier silhouettes replaced by low quality primitive cartoon loading screens. The general art style and aesthetic of the game is now a triumph of bad taste. The game now has a very trashy low brow look and feel. The overall effect is to give a cheap low budget, poor quality feeling to the game like a cheap knock off copy rather than an authentic faithful remaster.I have thousands of hours on the original dvd version and I can say this MOBILE PORT is actually worse in many areas than the old classic.  It's a cold dry mechanical, soulless update, devoid of the artistic style and charm that marked the original, it just feels wrong and off.  The character and ambience of the original has been stripped away.  In conclusion Feral like a mangy cat has delivered a stream of hot cat piss in this so called remaster, a shoddy update with all the quality and finesse of used cat litter.  Feral keep your damned dirty paws off Medieval II.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one, because my review would normally be a "meh."  On the plus side, the improved graphics are a plus.  The tooltips to help you manage your empire by locating people, agents, and armies are 100% a useful feature and make managing an empire so much easier than the original game.  You can also get more information about factions as you are negotiating with them.On the other hand, it doesn't really go far enough.  Do your armies automatically recruit from surrounding settlements to replace losses, like in Shogun 2?  No.  We don't want the game to be too realistic, now do we?  Did they solve the bug where certain naval units won't group with others because the other unit is more experienced, a different type, or is missing a sailor?  Nope.  Did they solve the issue where siege towers refuse to unload their units?  Can't say yet, but probably not!I also had two major bugs in the tutorial- one where it refused to progress me to the next tip, which meant I couldn't continue the campaign, because features in it are unlocked gradually.  God forbid a player actually say midway through "nope, I'm good, I don't need help anymore!"  And the second bug was my ship insisting "it couldn't sail there" through a green area of water.  I'm not asking it to sail to the New World or on land!  Just go the nearby island!  So they clearly haven't fixed naval navigation completely, either, though it's better than the base game.All in all, I'll probably continue playing it, but it's really not worth the cost I paid.  This should be worth 10 bucks max.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original game when I was about 7 years old, and have been revisiting this game ever since. The major issue was how badly the original title aged; choppy framerate, outdated GUI, even the visuals felt odd after so many years - at least for me.AND THE REMASTER TOOK CARE OF THE EXACT ISSUES.Battles are much more enjoyable thanks to the performance and controls fixes. No more 15 FPS 3000 vs 3000 men battles. The menus need some time to get used to, but they're an upgrade for sure. The soundtrack is the same with some additions, and it sound better than ever.I should mention that there are some minor gameplay elements added but worry not - If you'd like to have a completely authentic experience you can toggle them all off. But even if you decide to keep them, I can assure you that the game feels 99% the same!I personally experience unusually long loading times and I've heard of a few bugs, but I'm sure they will be taken care of in the long run.PS -  Notice that most of the negative reviewers spent no more than an hour playing this. If you really loved the original title, this remaster might as well be your new favorite addition to the series!

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to complete a full campaign before writing a review, to avoid knee jerk reactions on things - As the original RTW was my go to game for years and years, despite it showing minimal hours on steam for me, I played the CD version for 1000s of hours, so I had high expectations for this remaster.The good- The visuals are a huge step up, I'm actually amazed at the level of detail that was able to be brought to such an old game, though soldiers can appear too skinny sometimes.- All the new features are fairly decent, aside from a few things that need improvement. The ability to be able to turn off new improvements at your will and customize between old and new is very nice.- The AI appears to be a tiny bit better in field battles(though sieges is another story)- The new camera and controls are amazing. The old control set is just really outdated and bad - But for those that like it, you can set the default classic controls if you wish.- Being able to scale UI is god sent, though it would be better if we could select what is able to be scaled.- The affects of buildings, traits etc are made much more clear and understandable, a big improvement compared to the original.- For the most part the new UI isn't too bad, it takes a while to get used to, but a lot of it makes sense. It could be streamlined a little more, as certain things can take a few too many clicks and are positioned in odd places.- New unit balance is fairly decent(aside from archer balance)- The map overlay system is awesome!- Merchants originally felt a little weird being added, but after playing with them it makes map resources more useful, it needs some balancing though.- It's a lot rarer to have many small armies being sent at you by the AI, now there's multiple large stacks! :P- Squalor isn't as severe in the remaster, but can still be a pain in the butt if you don't control it.- Steam workshop support straight off the bat! Already a tone of mods!- Performance on my build is buttery smooth for the most part!The bad- Battle AI can be ♥♥♥♥♥, especially in siege battles. The pathing appears to be worse than the original, AI patrolling back and forth on roads dying to your towers, your own units stop chasing enemy units near walls. Enemy sending 1 - 2 units at a time into your whole army defending. AI committing to utilizing their 5 siege rams, 3 siege towers, despite there being holes in the walls made previously by their artillery.- While the AI appears to merge armies better in the remaster, but it doesn't exactly know what to do with them. The AI rarely attacked my field armies, or armies inside forts....but would constantly sent 2 - 3 stacks to siege a settlement(On very hard difficulty). 90% of my battles were sieges. I've seen instances of AI loading onto boats, sailing a little and dropping back off where they were just picked up from in the same turn lol- Diplomacy AI isn't much improved - AI will do some weird stuff like offer an alliance, then on the same exact turn attack you. End game becomes a breeze with the "bribe" option. Just pay off large enemy armies coming to attack you!- As stated above, the UI isn't overly bad, but could use some refinement as it can make somethings more tedious than need be.- Campaign map appears too vibrant, even though there is a slider in settings to adjust, even at lowest it doesn't seem right.- While above I said the merchant was a good add, it really needs balancing. Once I reached mid game on long campaign, I just spammed out merchants, sent them to the East and South, each merchant was pulling 1000 - 3500 per turn with the highest tier resources. Made me rich, too fast.- The UI can lag out randomly sometimes on campaign map. ConclusionIf you're expecting a "remake" then you probably will be disappointed. If you understand what a remaster is, then you'll be surprised at the improvements! Work is needed to be done, but for the most part it lives up to the hype. Worth the 50% off price!

_childDocuments_.review: Rome Remastered didn't have a perfect release. A year and several patches later, however, I think it can stand as an example of a remaster done right. Much has been left the same, like the factions and their rosters (save for minor balance changes). Some things have gotten big improvements, like the graphics and the battle controls. Only a couple things count as downgrades in my opinion, namely the UI and some tweaks to agents. Plus you're getting RTW, BI, and Alexander all together. Overall, I think the good pretty heavily outweighs the bad.The game wasn't as moddable at launch as Feral had indicated, which was a big point against it and them. Those issues have been fixed, however. There are now truly no faction, unit, or culture/religion limits, which opens up tons of modding potential which could give the game a very long lifespan. If you're a fan of classic Total War, I think Rome Remastered has earned it's price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: First: I wish we could give a more nuanced Feedback than Yes/No because this is very very much on the Edge for me.I do recommend this game, this is easily the best Total war out there. The changes they made from the original game are disappointing but at least it wont crash every 5 minutes.The Bad:-WHAT IS THIS UI?? at least give us a CHOICE!!!!!-Most changes they made are very questionable...-What is this new AI? "More aggressive" its just erratic and acts against its own interest a lot.-Ai is still kinda bad at developing -The movement and positioning sometimes is off, it way to often just ignores the formation you wanted and just registers a click, also i wish they upgraded the pathing a little, Units still take too long to actually get into formation after moving.The Good:-While its still an easy game it is a little more challenging than most Total wars-Old Rome Total war was my favorite game and this is not only about nostalgia, i played more Rome 1 Total war than any other total war and thats with it crashing.-City Management actually matters, developing your economy feels good-Loosing troops actually matters, every soldier you recruit will be deducted to the Town.-The animations in the new Total war games look amazing but not having those animations actually makes the Battle more fluent.-Most countries actually play out very differently.-NOSTALGIA-glad they upgraded the Graphics a little.-I kinda like new Merchants-You can choose what changes you want to use (mostly)Verdict:I stay positive and hope they address some of the issues since this is a 35$ pricetag and deserves some love, I will keep it at recommended for now and might change it later if they don't patch the issues, it's still my favorite Total war on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, great remaster, no performance issues as long as you remember to turn off the V-Sync interval and the FPS limit, which is what I'm assuming most people with FPS issues are not doing. The V-Sync Interval defaulting to 2, making the FPS very limited on 60Hz monitors is terrible and should not be the default option.The UI is a hit and miss though, with major issues with city UI especially with visibility of settlement details, unit information, building effects, and the recruitment and construction windows. This can and probably will be fixed with mods in the future but you really shouldn't have your UI be this hard to parse. Detailed options can also be hard to find, with the button looking more like an icon for the window rather than a separate menu.The new balance changes are great, with the exception of the Population Cost Balancing making recruiting a ton of units not wreck your economy as much as it used to in Rome: Total War, luckily, like every change, you can turn off the remastered changes if you so wish, and enjoy the game unchanged mechanically.The campaign map vibrancy and the unit vibrancy being changeable via the options is also very nice, as much as I like the look of the new map, it can be a little too cartoony at times.The "new" playable factions being available from the get-go instead of needing to go into an INI file to change is a welcome addition as well, I just wish some of the other options, like infinite ammunition for everyone on the field, and disabling the Marian reforms, were available.I highly recommend this remaster, and so far I think it's shaping up to be the best Total War game on the market.  Also if you're looking for a youtube series on this game to see how it plays, I recommend  as an introduction to beginners as well as just a very enjoyable series I've watched many times.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Rome 1 which still has amazing battles that are actual battles and not blob fights like in new TW games. Brings great fun to this day, but the remaster made some things wrong. It's a good remaster, but not a perfect one. Could use another update to polish the game and make it a perfect TW-modding platform.. There are some issues that should have been ironed out with one more update, but Feral was a 3rd developer hired by CA to to this remaster and they won't update this game any more.It offers unlimited modding possibilities, but still can be glitchy at times. Pathfinding has been noticeably improved, but of course it's still not perfect, especially around bridge ends. Game is very heavy and too bad there is no "light" install version that wouldn't clog up too much of your SSD, for example to use for mods.When it comes to UI, it actually isn't bad. It's completely different from R1/M2 so muscle memory from those games is useless here, but I got used to it after 10-15 hours of gameplay. It's pretty reasonable and everything is doable with the new UI, but it has one huge problem: scale. And the text scale. Buttons and text are way too small. They tried to make everything look roman-style, but that meant they traded visibility for visuals. But other than that it's fine in my opinion. "Tactical map" from R2 comes here, but it's actually useable. Unit cards were completely changed rather than upscaled (there is a mod for it), also unit orders in battle are still "laggy" as in the original. Difficulty combat modifiers are still very punishing. And a lot of other things, good and bad, that I can't fit in the review word limit. If you have too much time and want to read everything (good and bad) that I noticed in this game when playing it, you can have a look: Overall if you want a modern Rome 1 experience, it's a good game, albeit not perfect. Definitely look up some mods to improve the experience.
