_childDocuments_.review: I was introduced to the Total War series with Rome, needless to say I have certain dose of nostalgia with this game (I'll let you decide if it's a healthy dose or not).First playing this remaster took me a bit to get used to the new look and UI, had to adjust the gamma, brightness and saturation until I found something suitable, also I had to disable that ugly unit detail wheel on top of the unit banner.Fortunately the game is full of customization features so you should find something to please you.Once past the initial hurdles the game clicked for me, it's Rome Total War like I remembered it, but with a fresh coat of paint, some small bonus features and improvements like better battle controls and camera.It has my favorite TW battles to date due to the engine, individual unit physics is still the best here, with units pushing each other as the battle rages on and charges fell meaty and brutal. Also it runs with more than 15 fps on modern systems...Sadly it does not do much else to improve the base game. The AI is trippy as ever, if you get your army close to the AI chances are its gonna panic and scramble their whole formation for no reason, bridge battles are still an AI meat grinder, during siege battles the AI does not know how to deal with missiles and the pathfinding is terrible in siege battles as well, needing constant babysitting to make sure your units don't climb down the whole city hill to get a little to the left.The UI is functional but I would't say it's improved, really this is a simple game in the campaign map and you only need to pay attention to what buildings and units you build. Besides that you just need to check which financial buildings are going to bring in more profit and change taxes occasionally for bonus public order and growth, sadly I still have to open an extra tab to do that just like the original, even though there is more than enough space to show that now.So I'd say the UI accomplishes the same, it's just different (and smaller I guess..) but not improved for gameplay really.If you're wondering why I'm giving this a thumbs up: 1- Because Valve does not give me more options.2- Mod support which may very well save this game and improve it's value.3- For all it's faults I don't feel this is a cash grab, effort was clearly put into this, even if it didn't reach it's full potential.So would I recommend this game?If you played the original, if you want to play it again with a decent framerate AND have the 50% loyalty discount, sure I'd say it's a fair buy.Just make sure to adjust your expectations.For full price I can't really recommend it unless they really improve the AI, wait for a sale.(Honestly 15€ should have been the base price)

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT:Looks like only my first battle was messed up. Subsequent battles went alright and troops responded to commands properly. I still don't like the UI but I enjoy the game even more than the original (due to upgraded resolution, graphics and framerates). If you enjoyed the original Rome Total War, you might enjoy this one.ORIGINAL REVIEW:It's a solid "No" from me just with an hour of playtime. The first hour pretty much says how this game is going to be. I love the original Rome Total War, the first Total War game that I played, even though it has a lot of faults and buggy mechanics. I've played it for hundreds of hours, more than any other Total War game. I was hoping that this game would be an improvement over the original but it's not. It is an improvement over the graphics and nothing else. Everything else is even more broken than the original.The UI is atrocious and worse than the original, though I can get used to it. The worst part is the buggy and broken units and AI.  In my first battle in Segesta, I asked the velites (javelin units) to fire at the enemy Barbarian Peasants. Instead of stopping and firing, the idiots ran right into the enemy and suffered casualties as a result. The hastati units also mostly don't bother using their pilums when you ask them to attack. They just run right at the enemy and engage in melee combat. The units also sometimes refuse to respond to attack commands and just sit in one place unless I right-click repeatedly and even when they move, they were blocked by some building and refused to try going around it. This basic thing worked fine in the original Rome Total War released so many years ago. It baffles me how CA could make a remastered version even more broken than the old original.Running is now the default mode instead of walking. I couldn't find an option to turn that off. In the original game, it used to be single right-click for walk and double right-click to run but now units run by default so whenever I give a move command I have to also make sure to switch the unit back to walk mode since I don't want them to run all the time and become tired.Creative Assembly have changed nothing in their base mechanics since Rome Total War. Every Total War game since Rome Total War has the same broken mechanics and bugs and frustrations. They are so lazy that they have just reused the base code for the past 2 decades and just added a different skin to each game and selling it for $60. I am sick of their laziness and attitude of SEGA which keeps selling pathetic DLCs which contain "features" that barely add anything and should have been part of the base game anyway. I'm not going to waste my money on another Total War game.

At the very least, I was hoping for the "large battles" from newer titles, but you're still limited to 1 army while the computer is not.I will say this is by far the best Total War game; Medieval 2 comes very close, but the original is still the best.  If you don't already have the original Rome, then this is a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Total War Rome has always been one of my favourite TW games, especially its Barbarian Invasion dlc, and this remastered edition is glorious. The campaign map is beautiful enough and during battles it's a pleasure to watch my soldiers go at it in such amazing detail. There's also some new artwork and voice acting. The new UI is pretty okay although the unit pics on the sidebar are a bit too small for me.Playable emerging factions are now a thing and I'm looking forward to play as one; after I've finished humiliating Rome as the Franks that is. With Steam Workshop support and an already active community there'll be plenty of mods and overhauls in the future.I played for a few hours and experienced no hiccups or crashes. The game needs optimization though, including loading times, and some people have mentioned blurry graphics or flickering (things I've not encountered personally). There are also bugs that need fixing and unit handling needs improvement.On the whole I think Feral Interactive has done an excellent job with their remaster of this 17 year old game, extending its lifetime by another decade.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this title as a first time player of Total War: Rome. I had heard good things and went into this game blind with zero nostalgia of this particular sub-franchise in the Total War series. Its really hard to explain, but this game just *feels* like a (((true))) total war game. I have had experience with almost all of the modern Total War games (ex. Warhammer, Warhammer 2, Troy, Rome 2, Shogun 2, Three Kingdoms, Atilla) and have liked each to varying degrees. None of those titles felt as good to play then Rome Remastered. The game is dated by comparason with my previous experienced Total War titles, but alot of that can be mitigated by just getting used to it (time) and some helpful graphical mods. Because I have never had such fun from any battle in a Total War game, as I have had playing just a few hours of Rome Remastered. Here is just a few things I have noticed that really change the way I enjoyed the battles in Rome Remastered. (Also this is just anecdotal, I have not verified if any of the things that I noticed are objectively in the game [The wiki is kinda ♥♥♥♥]):COLLISION:This is perhaps the biggest factor in this game *feeling* much more like a Total War game. AFAIK the collision in modern TW games use a soft collision, or atleast something very different then what Rome Remastered uses. This is easily apparent by just the positioning of units, they feel like they actually have weight. When I am moving and ordering my heavy infantry togeather, It actually feels like I have a mass of flesh to throw around. AND THE BEST PART: Cavalry actually feels useful, and trampling is a viable and extreamely fun way to rack up 300+ kills in a single charge! Excluding the obvious limitations of the engine and the reality of TW games, Rome Remastered has really excelled in making these units feel real and impactful on the map I am manipulating them on.MAPS:From my experience the battle maps are either very numerous or that the maps are psudo-generated, because every battle map has been based on my army placement in the campaign. And Im not saying its like how modern Total War games do it (i.e roll a dice to pick through 4 premade grasslands maps), the maps actually feel really close to the layout of the campaign at that point. I had a battle in the entrance of a mountain pass, and my placement on the map corresponded to a battle map where my army was in the mountains approaching from a plain while my enemy was approaching from a mountainous corridor. I have no clue how they made this happen, but along with the collision I just felt immersed in a Total War game for the first time! Honestly, I would buy the game just to play the battles, because they are much more enjoyable then any other Total War game I have played.There are a few other things to cover that I felt was an amazing experience as a new Rome player.Diplomats:They seemed gimmicky at first (Essentially turning the diplomacy tab into an agent). But I felt myself pleasantly enjoying having to plan out my diplomatic logistics on top of my army logistics. Its a really minor addition on to my campaign thought processes, but it really added to the experience of being a faction leader. It allowed me to feel more involved in diplomacy now that it wasnt some aetheral plane that appears in front of me where I can instantly communicate across the known world and manage to bring my entire treasury with me. Also it really isnt too much of a hassle as any unit that a faction owns (settlement, agent, or army) can be interacted with by a diplomat to deal with said faction. I think its a pleasant addition to my Total War experience.Bribing:Any unit on the battlefield is a character with a family! The ability for me to walk up to the governor of a local settlement and pay for a settlement is a neat way to go about things and comes in very handy when completing missions against factions you arnt ready to full take on yet. The AI doesnt really do it to the human player as far as I have experienced if you were worried about AI spam. I neat option that was a welcome addition.The Senate Missions:Playing as Rome, as you will probably do atleast once, involves 3 families that fight for dominance over Rome's enemies. The Senate (that controls Rome) gives you a constant cycle of missions that ask you to do a specific task in accordance to the senates will (Which will usually involve killing people around you, with occasional "go make make peace" missions). You can ignore these AFAIK, but they do provide little mini goals that can really make a campaign unique and fun to play as you are presented with options for a minor reward, that is almost like a mini-game that makes you do things you wouldnt normally go. If you ever get bored of of playing Total War the *same* way, then this will be a neat way to allow you to spice up every campaign. Plus the added strategic options based of of your Allies "campaigns" that allow you to occupy yourself on the downtimes in some campaigns.Population:While not as complex as the system in the Rome 2 DEI mod, its still a system I wish Total War wouldnt just throw out. Having the included incentive to do well during battles, by trying not to lose people who are literally the basis of your economy and settlement progression. It also allows a minor balancing act where you recruit from a bunch of settlements rather then one main one (like what would be common in modern Total Wars). While minor, it atleast makes the recruiting not completely mindless.Spys can open the gates for you:This is just cool, want this more.You get the originals:Pretty value if you just want them, while having the ability to taste a more modern control scheme. You are gonna play it either way regardless of what version you are yearning to play.The remaster covers all the expansions:Both Barbarian invasion and Alexander are included within the Rome Remastered Launcher.The options:They really allow you to mix and match to really customizing your particular Rome experience.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Downsides:- Pathfinding in settlements can be VERY BAD at times, This may seem like a deal breaker but it can be worked around and it seems like Feral is continuing to work on the issues with that system. Its also not a constant and is more intermittent, yet infuriating.- It is very dated graphically, but this can be rectified through mods and a generous eye.- The roster for the game seems a little small compared to modern Total War games. You will likely have almost all the units in your faction in your army by the end of the game. Dont go into this expecting Warhammer, or even Troy. Its small but it has enough to play with that it becomes more of a personal preference.- The wiki is really lacking. Its a nice reference... kinda. Expect to be using trial and error, combing over the tutorial, and trusty Google to assist you when you are stuck. They should really look into Paradox's new Tooltip system for I:R and CK3.-------------------------------------------I really recommend this game, if nothing but to atleast try it. It really has alot of what I have been wanting CA to add to new Total War games. Its just sad that in an attempt to reach a wider audience, they threw out some real great mechanics and ideas that Rome Remastered still includes. If you are a fan of modern Total Wars, then I will bet you will enjoy this games battles once you give it a chance. Shouldnt need more then the hours I have at posting this to understand what I say when I say that this game ***FEELS*** like a TRUE Total War game.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I love Total War, hell I love the bad Total Wars... I played the hell out of Rome 2 on launch and had a GREAT time. Rome 2 is still my favorite (3K is slowing creeping up on it though)..... and I still cannot recommend this to anyone for any reason.And that's unfortunate, that's HELLA unfortunate. I wanted to LOVE this, it's the first TRUE historical Total War game since ATTILA! Like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! But this falters in every way, for me personally at least. They made it very clear that it was JUST a remaster from the start, I get that, I do, but holy damn, they left the AI as it was SIXTEEN YEARS AGO, the pathfinding is still TERRIBLE, the updated UI not only looks like a mobile game, but is EXTREMELY confusing and impossible to get used to. This game, remaster, cash grab, whatever you want to call it is literally, LITERALLY just a fresh coat of paint on a 16 year old game. It's crazy to me, and I don't know if it's because Feral didn't want to do more, or if CA wouldn't allow them to do more than they did, but this is absolutely ridiculous. I think I could've lived with everything else, the bad pathfinding, whacky UI, the lack of any improvement whatsoever, IF they improved the AI in the slightest. For example, I'm the Julii, cool, basic faction to get back in the grove of Rome 1, I love Rome, let's do it. Take out the rebels at the start, okay, cool. Decide to go after Gaul, great, let's stay on history's path. Beat. The. ♥♥♥♥. out of them, 20+ turns, army after army falls to 2 of my armies, I reform and retrain, more come, they die. And let me preface this in saying, the AI has always been dumb, even in the newer games, but for the most part, they know when they've lost. TURN AFTER TURN I TRY FOR PEACE, no, destroy another full stack, march further into their land, taking settlements, no. Like NOTHING I did made them surrender. Finally, after 4 or so hours and over 100 turns and every faction I had alliances with, trade agreements with, etc. etc. DECLARING WAR ON ME OUT OF NOWHERE, I gave in.The AI is horrible, there's no diplomacy, your allies will betray you within a turns notice, no faction will surrender no matter what, even if you offer INSANE amounts of gold, like it's just so off putting. Like why would you release 3K, with the BEST diplomacy we've seen in YEARS, then chose to remaster one of the GREATEST Total War games EVER made and chose to just make graphical improvements and some slight QOL improvements and just call it there? It blows my mind. I know some people are going to BIG disagree with this, because they've become accustomed to eating all of the ♥♥♥♥ that CA puts out, which, I'm guilty of as well, with 3K and even Rome 2, but there comes a point where you HAVE to notice what's going on and stand up and say "♥♥♥♥ THAT!" and now is that time...The saddest part about ALL of this is; this was the chance, this was the BIG chance to get historical Total War back on the map, the chance for a Shogun 3, Rome 3, Medieval 3, and I don't know if they purposefully ♥♥♥♥♥♥ it, so they could continue to stray away from historical TW or what, but this was IT, it needed the sales, it needed the reviews, it needed the love, and anyone with half a brain WON'T give in to it. That's the worst part, it further hinders historical Total War, and that hurts. That's my review, love it, hate it, I don't care, it's the truth.EDIT:I like to continue my reviews, especially if a game gives me a knee jerk reaction to immediately write a review, and even more so if it's a BAD one. With that being said, I've put about 12 more hours into the game, restarting the Julii campaign to give the game another good, solid try. I lowered the difficultly to see if that would impact anything at all, turns out, it does. The AI on *yes, laugh, it's for science* easy difficulty actually acts like it's not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ braindead, making agreements, suing for peace when they know they've been beaten, even forming very well put together armies. What the AI on normal or hard has done in my experience on most of the Total War games I've played since Rome 2. The battles are still immensely fun, but only out of siege battles, the siege battles on this are horrible, the pathing as mentioned in my initial knee jerk review is TERRIBLE in siege battles, so avoid them at ALL costs. But in the open, they're fun, REALLY fun, like taking me back to when tactics actually meant something FUN! So for about the first 80 or so turns in this new campaign, I was having a considerable amount more fun than I had in my first.... that's when it went downhill. It really comes down to being able to see how little work was put into this remaster and how the "Quality of Life" changes were only surface level and barely, if at all, help the mid to late game. For example, because if you've read this review through, you know I love my examples. The Roman reforms happen around 225 to 222 BC. While I actually LOVE the retraining aspect of Rome TW, having to have the correct buildings for the specific units and have them garrisoned to actually replenish, one of my pet peeves of the game was always the reforms. When it hit that point, if you were in any wars, especially on multiple fronts, you were ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and I mean ♥♥♥♥♥♥ HARD. Because, after the reforms you can't retrain any pre-reform units, so every army you have is ONE and DONE. You can't retrain or reform any of your pre-existing units into the newer Cohorts or even just the upgraded Roman archers, or whatever the post reform calls them. Also, don't forget, settlements only recruit 1 unit per-turn... So, and for my example I had 3 armies near Rome, because I focused West, South West, and North to North West and the Greek Cities managed to become a power house, I had 5, count them FIVE SPARTAN ARMIES AT MY DOOR STEP... "Hey, enjoy the reforms ♥♥♥♥♥♥!" so turn after turn, I'm throwing armies to the meat grinder, recruiting units one at a time, this that and the other, the Spanish and Brits decide to throw our peace, trade deals, and everything else out the window and declare war on me in the same turn, while I'm trying to reform my armies on that front... Can you see?? In a good story, there's a beginning, middle and an end, and with that comes rising action. Rising action is basically the tension of the story, something happens to kick off the rising action, that leads to event after even continuing the rising action, eventually leading to the climax, falling action and resolution. The rising action in this case is of course, war, that leads to conquering, which leads to more war, which eventually leads to victory or defeat, in the case of victory, that leads to quelling rebellions, which leads to the resolution, which is of course, peace. The rising action of the story that I was creating was hailed to a completely stop, due to aged and dated game mechanics, that of which could have been fixed VERY easily and probably will be fixed by modders, VERY quickly. The "remaster" and "quality of life" changes for this game feel purely, PURELY surface level. Enough for someone to say "Oh that looks cool! I'll try it!" after seeing maybe, MAYBE an hour or 2 of gameplay. After that it falls to ♥♥♥♥. That's the major problem as well, unless you're playing short victory games 24/7, the "quality of life" changes only affect you for a short amount of time, because most of us play the LONG games, take over the ♥♥♥♥♥♥' world games. I'm still not done with my campaign of course, armies are reformed, working on taking the rest of Spain and finally moving into Greek lands, I'll probably, MAYBE update once I'm finished and give an overall summary, TL;DR, something like that.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played TW: Rome. I played a lot of it. I found it to be intriguing, fun, challenging … but there were things that bothered me. I was not a fan of the political system, which was nearly entirely abstract and really added nothing to the game play, it really just got in the way most of the time. The way a general's retinue worked always bothered me, and it really was just a complicated back-end making both army and settlement management way more cumbersome than it should have been, but improperly managing it could significantly impact any campaign's outcome for the worse. Army management otherwise was fun and interesting but some … let's say questionable … unit types, mostly either anachronistic or outright non-existent historically (Arcani, I am looking at you).  It got stale.Then I got TW:Rome 2 (Emperor Edition, which apparently fixed many earlier problems that I did not know about), and thoroughly enjoyed playing that. Really, the only thing about Rome 2 that I missed from Rome 1 was the ability for individual cohorts (basically) to march out on their own; all armies had to be led by a general. That was a minor quibble really. The naval combat was interesting a couple of times, but once the novelty wore off it was quickly evident that auto-resolving naval battles was a better use of time even if it was a less effective method to prosecute naval campaigning. The general's retinue system worked much more logically to me, and the political system was still reasonably abstract but I had a lot more input on it, so it was far more interesting. The intrigue units (spy, champion, dignitary) were similar to the original, but added depth to the game in a more natural way.CA, Feral, et cetera, they remastered the wrong game. They tout the 4K graphics, but running it on a 4K monitor at 4K is actually too much for the engine to handle, and crashes it. Officially, support said to instead run it at 1080 resolutions, at which I raise a skeptical eyebrow. The "refinements to gameplay" seems to basically just be the addition of the "merchant" unit to the intrigue spy, assassin, and diplomat cache, and if there are some underneath improvements they are not at all obvious.If you absolutely loved TW: Rome, did not like TW: Rome 2, don't mind that the game doesn't really run that well at high resolutions, and absolutely have to have a TW: Rome game, then you might get your money's worth out of TW: Rome Remastered.If you are not in that camp, you will be wasting your money.CA and Feral should have been working on remastering TW: Rome 2, instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll get the bad stuff out of the way first. Maybe I'm just used to the origianal, but the UI seems more convoluted, especially with agents (just let me right click a target for my assassin, not choose a mission from a dropdown in the corner of the screen). At least diplomats can still right click on their targets. The family tree is still there, but not an actual graphical tree which I liked from the original. The diplomacy seems better, but I don't understand what influences reputation (why do I only have 70 when I've never broken any treaties?), and the AI still does counterintuitive stuff (if my relationship with parthia is 100, why don't they want an alliance? I suspect it's because I'm at war with their ally, but in that case WHY is our relationship at 100??). I've also noticed a bug where it only shows half your holdings in the Territorial Ranking graph.The good stuff: I love the strategic campaign map view, but I'm a sucker for maps. Visuals are much improved, and while that's to be expected (and perhaps not quite as improved as they really should be 15 years later), it runs MUCH smoother on my machine than the original ever did even with the better graphics. Battle and campaign AI is still lacking but much better than before, and I love that you gave options for remaster balance/feature changes or to keep the original stuff.I'm very glad it's still got the music and feel of the original, and for $15 it's a steal. The puzzling diplomacy and strange new UI are what's holding it back for me -- 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a great remaster, very modular, mainly focused on quality of life changes to the classic Rome TW UI that were confusing and/or clunky, and modernising the game a bit with a few unobtrusive changes. They added the merchants mechanic from Medieval 2 (except the ones in this game are actually useful), which I think was a nice touch. Diplomacy also seems to be a lot less... weird, than in classic RTW; i.e, I haven't gotten a single "please do not attack, accept or we will attack" request yet, in nearly 150 hours of gameplay. Protectorates are now somewhat more viable, with factions you are dominating more willing to make a deal with you rather than face extinction. Roman factions are still backstabbing A-holes, but hey, I'm chalking that one up to historical accuracy.What I can't chalk up to historical accuracy is that (at least on hard and very hard, can't speak for the lower difficulties as I haven't tried them yet) the AI seems waaaay too hyperfocused on attacking the player, like, even more so than in classic RTW. You'll have the Julii completely ignoring or even forging alliances with the Gauls, and the Scipiones ignoring the Carthaginians for the sole purpose of dog-piling the player faction, regardless of how impractical a target your faction currently is. Playing as Carthage in particular is a bit of a slog, as you're spread thin from the very beginning, and, quite literally, the whole world is out to get you. If your faction starts with territory in the north or northwest, be prepared to fight full stacks of Hastati and basic Warbands ad nauseam in the early game. I don't typically mod TW games, but I'm fervently praying for a mod for this game that makes AI factions behave more naturally. If you've read this far and know of any mods that do so, please leave me a comment. I'll love you forever.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a GREAT remaster of my favorite total war game of all time. _childDocuments_.review: Is this a good remaster? For the most part yes, you can play in the classic original mode or with the new updates. Sieges are a buggy nightmare where most of the issues come up with pathfinding. Troops will get stuck on walls, going through streets, trying to leave or enter settlements etc. Its a damn shame since many of these battles would've been much more interesting if the players and AI's troops didn't crap the bed. Having this happen on one siege would be fine but when it happens in every single siege and results in you losing your men because they can't recapture gates and towers it frankly gets infuriating. _childDocuments_.review: This is not a new game, nor is it a remake of Total War Rome. It's the good old 2004 Rome with enhanced graphics, UI and some quality of life improvements. That means that some of the bad old stuff from 2004 are still in the game, namely, pathing. You'll have to micromanage the way your troops and agents are going to go, which is not particularly bad except in city sieges.From my point of view, the price is quite adequate. You're getting the vanilla Rome Total War with both DLC, which means you get the original campaing and starting date, the Barbarian Invasions starting date, and the Alexander campaing, with 38 playable factions. You'd need to buy a bunch of DLC to get all the factions available in modern Total War titles, not to mention Attila was released as a separate game, not a DLC for Rome II.The game runs pretty good on my system (Ubuntu, GTX 1080), my GPU is working ok and I get a very good FPS (locked at 60 fps). I know that some players have had technical issues, but I haven't had a single crash, or glitching, in 17 hours of play. I haven't tried the free HD textures DLC nor am inclined to download 20 GB for it.I've read that some people hate the GUI, I find it acceptable, then again, I've been playing Medieval II, which has a hideously dated UI, so maybe my bar is too low. The GUI in Total War Three Kingdoms or Attila is way more streamlined and modern, so gamers coming from that might find it awkward.Feral, thanks for a great game, and for consistently supporting Mac and Linux gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: I think most people here misunderstand what a remaster means.Most expected loads of "improvements", where the goal was simply to make the game playable natively on newer system.Now you can play RTW for the rest of Windows 10's life (which should be eternal according to MS).It's 15-30€, for 3 legendary games. For first timers it's a great fun game, not the most challenging but a good bit of fun.Anyone with basic knowledge of strategy will overcome the game. But I think it also makes irrelevant cheesing tactics that so many streamers/players have to resort to to beat newer Total War games in the hardest difficulty, because they think it proves something. Games are games.If you want a whole new, serious experience with more challenging and balanced aspects, go buy 3 Kingdoms or so.Personally I still remember the day I bought RTW 15 years ago. I had really great memories, but in recent years I was sad it wouldn't run well on newer PCs. It took a lot to make it work, and even with mods it struggled. OK, on to the review :In terms of performance :The game works very well, I average 110 FPS with a current generation card and a 4 years old CPU. You can run it in Windowed Borderless and chill watching stuff on your second screen, the pinnacle of RTW experience!I agree it is too heavy, 67GB with HD textures instead of 9GB for the Gold edition. Clearly missing some optimizationUI :The UI is a change, took some adapting, some things like the lack of success rate on agents' actions directly in the map preview sucks I'll admit. But after 18 hours I'm 100% accustomed to it and it works well. The one tiresome thing for me is that Escape does not always exit an UI, some things like army merges lack a "CONFIRM" button instead of clicking an annoyingly small button.Mixed opinion on the UI. If you recruit in half the provinces at  the same time, opening the recruitment message is laggy. AI :The AI hasn't changed much. It's more aggressive, yes, but it's still very easy to cheese, and to get a challenging experience you'll probably have to cheat to give the AI extra resources. Rome is still busted OP.Diplomacy is still messy, it feels like every action you take will deteriorate your reputation forever. Allies still backstab you all the time for no reason, diplomats still interact with your cities / armies only to do nothing. But there are no "regressions" compared to the base game. You get what's expected.Graphics :The map looks pretty, textures are smooth and pretty. Feels well polished, the battles look great.You can choose the map's vibrance if you prefer more tame colors.In the end, for the price of 6 subs to hot tub streams or 3 MOBA skins, it's a great value.

_childDocuments_.review: I've deleted my initial review I made after a few hours of frustration. Now that I've put some 130 hours into this, and completed 2 VH/VH long campaigns, I can at last make my final, comprehensive judgement. Unfortunately, I still cannot recommend it. In fact, I don't think I'll ever come back to it. Next time I have a craving for some good old fashioned RTW action, I'll just boot up the EB2 mod for M2TW.Now, just to be clear on a few things:1, Yes, I absolutely have pink tinted glasses for the original game. That's why I bought the remaster, like 90% of people.2, It still IS Rome: Total War. Even if they changed up the title. It's an incredibly fun game for oldschool TW fans, or strategy fans in general. And it works. It has some bugs here and there, but they are not game breaking. I had like 2 CTDs in all this time. It's just not justifiable to sell this for 30 EURs in 2021.3, The developers (Feral Interactive) seem like nice guys by the current standards of the gaming industry. They keep supporting the game after the release, fixing and improving a lot of stuff. The mod support they added in the latest patch looks awesome, too bad I'm not sure if there's gonna be a community to take advantage of it. And the way they made it possible to turn all the new features on/off individually is absolutely the right way to create a remaster.So why don't I recommend it? Here are some of my biggest gripes:1, It looks awfully outdated. Like something from 2008. I don't usually care much about graphics, but when your whole pitch for reselling a 20 years old game is updated graphics, then maybe, you know... update the graphics? The campaing map somehow looks worse than in the original. And the biggest crime: unit armor/clothing is still completely the same on all individuals. It's not an engine limitation, M2TW already had this 15 years ago with an updated Rome engine. The only reason I can think of is that they didn't want to invest the time and money to create new texture variations, which is completely unacceptable when free mods with far larger unit counts have this.2, The UI changes are hit and miss. Some quality of live improvements are very welcome, but some are clear regressions that also impact the gameplay in a major way. Eg. the new follower transfer screen is the worst UX mess I've ever seen. I keep triggering night battles as the attacker and I still don't know how (I don't check the box, at least not on purpose,) and the red line signaling the border of the battlefield is not visible unless you zoom way in. Also, they removed flavor text from the unit cards, followers etc. Not cool.3, They completely kneecapped the campaing AI. I think it's related to the fact that now the AI can go bankrupt too, it doesn't just get free money. (I can't find any references to it online now, but I remember people mentioned it in YT reviews...) This sounds good on paper, except they neglected to also update the AI so it can actually manage its economy. Even on VH campaign difficulty you'll often see it disband half its army just before a critical battle. Some factions have especially weird behaviors, like the Julii and Gaul keep spamming navies until they can't afford any armies at all, the Brutii not building even basic ports in their starting cities etc.Conclusion: if you are fan of the original, and can't resist the temptation, don't worry too much. You'll still get your money's worth out of it in terms of hours played. But be prepared to spend those hours with a nagging feeling of disappointment in the back of your mind.If you haven't played the original: don't buy this. Get M2:TW instead. It's a better game, especially with mods, and works just fine on modern systems.

_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: A great face-lift on one of the greatest strategy games (and certainly the best total war game) of all time. New graphics are great to introduce younger players to an all time classic. Definitely worth it for new players, and even if you still have the original it is worth revisiting  (although get it with the introductory offer or on sale). Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: OK, I will say I am a TW fan from the get go, but this doesn't feel like one. There are a couple of things that I don't like about it from the beginning:Voice acting - while its ok for any other title not in the TW stable, the American accent is a real put off. UI - Yes, TW:RR is a remaster (I didn't play the original), the UI feels confused, unintuitive and bland. I ran it in 1440 and it still looked like a 15 year old game.Battle - Roman units don't seem to be cohesive and ordered when advancing and engaging enemy. A disciplined unit of Hastatii or Triarii should hold formation when in contact. Archers seem more like a nuisance, rather than a serious threat. As far as I am concerned, this isn't a CA game. It doesn't have their stamp of quality. It has the hallmarks of complete outsourcing to Feral Int. Unfortunately, this is the first negative review I have given a CA title. If you haven't played any Total War games before, then by all mean, give it a go. You may enjoy it.I, however, did not.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: As a girl who's been playing RTW since she was 6, when I heard the game was getting remastered, I was thrilled. My dad was a huge nerd, so growing up RTW was a huge part of my childhood. I absolutely adore horses which meant Armenia just had to be my favorite faction lmao. I did take a forced hiatus when I started drawing battles with dead soldiers, Mom wasn't too happy about that... anyway:I'd say counting back the past 16 years, I have about 6-7k hours total on RTW. I've played it to death. I have roughly 100 hours on this game, and in my opinion, it simply cannot compare to the original. You know what they say, "If it ain't broke, don't fix it". The graphics irk me and are a major turn off. It's nice to see the soldiers looking different, but the horses are.....squiggly. Their eyes scare me! They look like someone tried to draw them from memory.  Also, the cataphracts were NERFED. Major L. :(They really dropped the ball with path finding when taking settlements. Granted, it wasn't that great in the original either, but there's no improvement at all. The battle map drives me nuts too. Just show me the damn map. I don't need to see it from a satellite view. I miss having the option to see where everyone is. Speaking of where everyone is: they did not need to change the family tree. It was fine the way it was. It's hard to find some people sometimes, lol. You also have units in battle that won't do as told and suddenly become sentient or something. Like, I'm calling the shots here. Why aren't they listening? :PThe merchants were a nice detail, and to be frank, I still really don't know how to utilize them. I can figure that out with time, sure. It's also nice that you can have a definitive set tax rate in each settlement without requiring a governor. They really made an effort to revamp the game. But I'd give it a 6/10. Like I said, it can't compare. Alright, I'm done D riding the original. That's all for now!-C
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: When I first bought this, I didnt give it much of a chance. I played Rome 1 most of my life. The UI changes and things were a turn off. However, after messing with a few options like the brightness of the campaign map.. now that I am use to the UI and things, I am SO happy I stuck with it. So many little quality of life improvements on top of the graphical. It is def an actual remaster and not just a skin slap. Also having the workshop, is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: Even nowadays this game is king, or Imperator, or even Emperor among its kind, its still a classic but yet flexible, its just a better version of the OG game and for what you get its worth it, it doesn't force huge changes but rather offers them whilst offering the original experience but better, perfect remaster.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: Rome Remastered has proven to be an excellent game in all regards. The graphical overhauls are absolutely incredible, making the game look as gorgeous as one made near a decade letter. Things such as battle controls and the camera have been brought to the standards of 2021 seamlessly and flawlessly. Nearly every aspect they've changed for the remaster is toggleable before starting a campaign, ensuring that even if you're just here for the graphics change and don't otherwise like what they've done (though almost all of it has been an improvement in my opinion) you can enjoy that experience.If you loved the original you'll find that it's just as incredible an experience with a newfound splendor in appearance. If you've largely played the newer games and haven't picked up Medieval 2 or Rome 1, you should be able to learn fairly quickly and will find much of intuitive or well explained. And considering the immense modability of the game you'll find that it will only increase in value and replayability. I cannot say that I have had this much fun with a game since picking up Divide and Conquer for Medieval 2. It is incredible and has been without performance issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: For a remaster, this game is really weak in my opinion. It's more of a QoL update for the original game and, with that being said, some of the updates make the game worse; especially the UI. The UI is a total mess and, even though the original wasn't perfect either, they could have done an overhaul and made it akin to the newer titles; more clean and easier to navigate, but nope, two steps backward. The graphics look pretty in the screenshots and trailers but in-game it's very disappointing and I did download the 30GB "Enhanced Graphics" add on, which changed nothing lol. Ultimately such a shame.HOWEVER, at it's core it still is Total War: Rome and if you have never played it, it's worth giving it a go on sale. My not recommended is merely due to having played and loved the original for CA to give us a half-arsed "remaster" when they could have done SO MUCH MORE to bring the og back to life. I really wanted to like this...
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this game for a modern audience but like you get more enjoyment if you played the first Rome Total War. This game is a remaster to the core and at times to a fault. In a modern light with all of the improvements I would say the game is a solid average experience. If you like Total War games or style of games you will likely have a lot of fun playing this.The game still does a lot of great things. How Rome plays and is broken in 3 factions, how certain units feel like pikes, a ton of character in generals and their speeches, and interesting city management once you learn how it all works.  The biggest issue the game still has it the AI, it just isn't great. Often doesn't attack in formation and sends 1-2 units to attack at a time, and re-position so much you often will catch them out of formation.I would give this game a 3\5 at the end of the day. A fun experience, and if it gets mod support like the first Rome it can easily have near endless replaybility.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: Great Remastered. UI can at times be a little confusing, but its not that bad. You can turn off all the changes and play the original game with better graphics on a modern operating system, unlike the original game where you need to do workarounds. The changes of the remastered are not bad and actually improve the game. Still one of the best Total War Games.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: I really dig the fact I can play all the factions I had to destroy and move files for back in the day, good additions but not too many, runs smooth. I was iffy about the price point but worth it overall, do wish it came with barbarian invasion and alexander but I expected nothing less from total war.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: Scrolling around on the battle map makes the game stutter just like in the original. They have done a good job of improving and preserving the charm of the original battle map but the foliage and lighting in battles is worse. Performance is not acceptable for this level of appearance and graphics.Whereas in the original units moved flexibly and in a controlled manner, possibly an attempt to bring the movement up to par or to make it more "realistic" has given us slow and buggy unit pathing. A simple formation order will lead to troops spinning around in a circle continually.
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: If u play Rome 2 you'll find it takes forever to build up an army. 1 trooper per city, per turn.  This need to move faster. Most building complete in 2 maybe 3 turns, this isn't so bad. In the 3 hours I've played I only managed to build 3 particial armies so I have not had to deal with food or squalor. It's not fair to compare remastered to anything else cause it's an animal unto itself.  It plays like an older game cause it is. It looks better than the first version. I'll have more to say when I learn more about the game.    Later  K-9
_childDocuments_.name: Total War: ROME REMASTERED

_childDocuments_.review: Total War: ROME REMASTERED lets you relive the legacy that defined the award-winning strategy game series. Remastered to 4K with multiple improvements to visuals as well as refinements to gameplay, it’s time to revisit a true classic. Not everyone gets a second chance to conquer the Roman Empire.

name: Redout: Space Assault
detailed_description: THE NEXT GENERATION OF ARCADE SPACE SHOOTERS IS HERE Redout: Space Assault puts you in control of a Super Orbital Recon Fighter during the 2395 Colonization of Mars: dive in the fastest, most epic and exciting arcade space battle you can experience. Outsmart, outmaneuver, overpower, outclass your opponents in lightning-fast, adrenaline-inducing single-player space combat. You play as Leon Barret, ace fighter pilot of the Poseidon Security Forces. Here at Poseidon Corp., we are trying to pave the way for the colonization of Mars, as mankind is struggling for survival, split between a depleted hot Earth and a cold, claustrophobic Lunar colony. Your job is to maintain order by eradicating rebels and space pirates, facilitate our scientists' research while keeping them safe, and protect all our personnel from the numerous external threats. Dive down into gigantic asteroid mining plants, shoot down Rebel drones and fighters, roll left and right avoiding enemy fire, unleash impossibly powerful missile volleys, but also race against stray pilots and space scavengers at breakneck speed for the sheer thrill of it. By completing missions you will unlock Cards and Tokens to upgrade your fighter's Hull, Shields, Energy Weapons and Missiles until you are able to go up against massive Capital Ships and single-handedly shift the tide of the war. In an interplanetary struggle where nobody is good or bad, you will experience Leon rising through the ranks, the meaning of “necessary evil”, the cost of integrity and ultimately, what it means to take a stand. FEATURES Career mode - learn every skill you need to survive and triumph in the Redout Universe. Many Thriving Worlds - exotic locations, grandiose events and epic battles beyond every frontier. Deep Gameplay - manifest your tactical superiority by putting your dexterity, quick thinking and adaptability to the test. Bigger, Badder Weapons - From Plasma Cannons to Shock Rays, Railguns, Scattershot, Air-To-Air Missiles, and Loadup Gatlings, a vast array of weapons is at your disposal. Choose, upgrade, and even install multiple instances on your ship. Pimp my Ride - upgrade your spaceship to scale it up: let them come by the dozens, or single-handedly take on a Destroyer Warship! Drop and swap Cards to improve single aspects of your ship and better fit your style. Music for your ears - An entirely dynamic soundtrack that will drop sicker and sicker beats the tougher the experience gets! LOTS TO DO IN SPACE Fight enemy Drones, Fighters and all sorts of enemy ships in rail shooter sections: avoid missiles and buckets of bullets while you take them down one by one. Explore Iridium mines and abandoned space structures in search of hideouts, resources, and Rebels: enjoy the freedom of movement, cut your engine power to squeeze through narrow passages, but be careful not to scratch your paintwork. Race through enemy installations, behind enemy lines, through gigantic space battles, or against space pirates for a quick buck. Assault Capital Ships in specially designed missions that pit you against gigantic vessels: each with unique strengths, weaknesses and special attacks, each a turning point in the narrative of the game! FAST-PACED SPACE ACTION Redout: Space Assault comes with the Redout Adrenaline seal-of-quality. Every ship movement, from rolling to avoid missiles to pushing the limits of your ship via the enhanced boost, will make you feel like you are actually driving a space-capable fighter jet, on the brink of control. You will not need to instantly become a top gun in order to enjoy the game, but you will definitely need some skill if you want to achieve all bonus objectives and max out your fighter stats!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't waste your money. Get Everspace 1 if you're short on money and want the best space shooter roguelike out there, or 2 if you want an incredibly amazing game, currently under development.------------------------------------------------------------------Don't be fooled by its looks: THIS IS A MOBILE GAME PORTED FROM APPLE ARCADE TO STEAM.What does that mean? You can't move freely around space and explore, instead the game takes you where it wants your ship to be, not the other way around. Perfect if you love ultra-slow rollercoasters in space (yes, it's really slow). There are a few levels that have some freedom but there's no point in it as controls get magically inverted for those levels, making it a pain for you to control. And the sole goal in those levels seem to be collecting coins and some flying giant translucid holographic ♥♥♥♥ that they like to call blueprints. Thanks devs! I love games that play themselves for me! Press ENTER to shoot auto targeting missiles. ENTER, lol, why not just go for F7 to make it even less comfortable while you're at it. Almost as if they were designed to be TOUCHED BY THE HUMAN FINGER. HOW CURIOUS, RIGHT???????????? Oh, and cards that give you +x% shields, damage, hp... that do not stack. You get to pick one, the other 2 are converted into currency. Don't misclick or say bye bye to that sweet 5% in54n3 missile damage boost! HOOT HOOT! Textures take some time to load properly, even on high end rigs: Dual SSD's running in raid0, game isn't even reaching 40% cpu load. Still textures need a 2nd pass in order to render in decent quality. This happens while playing, therefore becoming noticeable when a giant rock right in front of you looks alll blurred out - then all of a sudden the "nice" textures kick in. Because F U, immersion! AHAHAHA. No, seriously. It's worse than that. You'll find yourself pressing Enter ASAP just to skip it. Uninteresting. Bland. Mediocre. Cliché. Has no hook. It's just a mobile game with some text that SCREAMS for skipping. I'd rather have no text than such a low key effort (if there was any) of a story. It was just crammed in to give the feeling of being a "full game". Just like mobile games do, surprise surprise! Mission 5 for example. Hover for 1:40 minutes. End. OPTIONALLY ADDED DIFFICULTY - USE ONLY IF YOU CAN PARRY AT LEAST 5 CONSECUTIVE TIMES IN DARK SOULS: Press up arrow for boosting. Did I mention i LOVE when my games play themselves without human interaction? gReAt iDeA d3v5!1! That pretty much sums it up. HOWEVER, That wouldn't be so bad, BUT it has the REDOUT brand on it. And this goes for the rest of the game. If you, 34BigThings, would have named this piss poor R-Type malformed clone something like "Generic Mobile Nonsense Space Shooter", it'd be more fitting, and we would be more forgiving. You're ruining the only good thing you've released as a studio.I can't believe it. 34BigThings had SO MUCH potential on their hands.Wasted. 100% wasted. But not unintentionally wasted: This is what we get to experience when greed takes over a dev company.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn’t Star Fox. Redout: Space Assault may vaguely resemble it on the surface, but it’s not. Your ship even has a similar profile to an Arwing from the rear. Yet it lacks most of the qualities that make a game like Star Fox good. What’s especially disappointing about this is that it seems to be piggybacking off of the “Redout” name without having any of the polish or quality from that game. If it wasn’t from the same developer, I would assume it was just some blatant infringement with a pending lawsuit. What the game is, outside of that disappointment, is thorough mediocrity brought even lower by game-breaking bugs.Abbreviated Review: Space games kind of get a step up on other games in terms of visuals because they get to avoid a lot of things. Most people haven’t been to space, so they have free creativity. They also can get away with single bright lighting sources with hard shadows because there’s no atmosphere, as well as minimal terrain. So if they have decent textures and plenty of lasers and explosions, things always look decent. Redout: Space Assault delivers pretty much just that. It looks decent when compared to most indie space games for the past five years or more. Notably, however, it doesn’t look anywhere near as good as the original Redout game, but I suppose the fact that this was originally a mobile game makes that make a little more sense.Redout: Space Assault seems to be heavily influenced by Star Fox, but it doesn’t deliver that experience. The only thing it shares is that most of the game takes place on rails with some fully 3D sections sprinkled throughout. Mechanically, it plays more like Rez, however, even there you get to aim. Redout: Space Assault doesn’t give you that option. To use your main weapon, you just line up your ship and fire in a straight line. You never aim at an angle, you don’t have to lead targets, you just put yourself in front of it and shoot. Rather, you let the game shoot since it’s set to auto-fire from the beginning. You can turn it off, but pressing the trigger to shoot in a straight line at a reticle you can barely see doesn’t add anything to the game.The bulk of what you do is spamming the other trigger to lock and fire missiles. You don’t aim to do this either. It just locks whatever is on the screen. This accounts for the bulk of the damage you do in the game. In part, because it’s the best way to consistently hit targets, but also because it’s the only way to fire without just parking your ship directly in line with the on-screen enemies. By the time you’re a third of the way through the game, you have to dodge and roll constantly to stay alive.For some reason, you unlock several different types of main weapons in the game even though most are nearly indistinguishable and mostly ineffective. One “chain lightning” weapon seemed most effective for the times I could actually use it, but the vast majority of damage I caused in the game was from spamming missiles dozens of times each mission.Even at its bargain bin price, Redout: Space Assault doesn’t feel like it’s worth it. It has nine chapters with between four and seven missions each. These missions range from 2-4 minutes outside of the ones that put you on a horrible scavenger hunt in the open 3D realm of an infinitely brown asteroid field. Except I couldn’t actually finish this relatively short boring experience because halfway through, a bug had me flying off into oblivion at the same spot in a mission every single time. I had this happen before, but restarting the mission fixed it. This time around, however, I restarted four times and it bugged out every time.What makes this more disappointing is that Redout was such an enjoyable game and I assumed this developer was going to bring similar quality to a new title. Seeing it originally release on Apple Arcade and look and feel like a coin collecting marathon of auto-shooting was disappointing. It took so long to come to PC though that I assumed it would be significantly upgraded. If it was, it doesn’t show. It’s still full of subpar-to-terrible voice acting, awkward coin collecting, and one of the blandest upgrade systems I’ve ever seen. 34BigThings did an excellent job filling the void of Wipeout-styled games with Redout, but Redout: Space Assault isn’t going to be “Star Fox on PC.” It’s just another indie space game that will be forgotten as soon as its released.

_childDocuments_.review: Some reviewers here don't understand that some people - me included - ACTUALLY WANT RAIL SHOOTERS. I find open all-axis games disorienting, daunting and boring, while rail shooters, due to their linear nature, can be faster, focused and more action-oriented (and are less time-consuming). Giving this game a bad review because its a rail shooter is like complaining a racing game is bad because you don't like racing - brilliant. This genre of games unfortunately, comprise a very small minority of modern games.This games has some great features: it's exhilarating in a sense that it manages to convey a feeling of epic engagement with its great audio and visuals (don't be fooled by some reviews - THIS IS NOT A MOBILE GAMES!, not even close).For me, it would be nicer to have more constant flow of enemies with diverse attacks (a great example of this is the arcade classic "solar assault" by old KONAMI), where you constantly need to evade linear attacks, not just homing ones. Also, your attacks should be a bit less automated (as some reviewers pointed), and more skill based.That said, it's a good rail shooter - recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is tailor made for someone like me, who is an arcade gamer from way back. Especially considering the low cost, I find the negative reviews on this to be quite surprising to be honest.There really isn't too much to say here.. if you like the feel of Space Harrier style gameplay with spectacular modern graphics, then you will enjoy this. If you want a space sim with depth of any kind, you will despise this. It's that simple really.It's an arcade shooter in space. Think starfox, space harrier as mentioned above, along those lines. If you want simple action that looks pretty and is set in space, you'll love it.I am really enjoying it so far :) I am having FUN, and that's all that matters :)

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of the most pleasant surprise purchases I made. From what I read in the forums, this is apparently an Apple Arcade title that got then released on PC, set in the same universe as the Redout racing game. I come totally blind and not too knowledgeable of the development on Redout: Space Assault but I love arcade on-rails shooters like Panzer Dragoon, Star Fox, Rez, Omega Boost and many others so I felt right at home with the focus being heavily set on lock-on guided missiles, which is a primary element of the scoring in such games and a homage to the famous Itano Circus, the majestic missile dodging and soaring acrobatics that was polished with Super Dimensional Fortress Macross. And any title that tries to recreate that obviously has my attention!Graphics wise, this game looks amazing with extremely colorful and pretty space vistas and fairly decent ship design. It's a shame the main character ship doesn't have one or two trails to further increase the sense of velocity, perhaps they can add it in a future update. There was a bug with HDR, along a lot of other issues that were fixed on a quick patch released shortly after launch so, using the latest version as the basis and having 100% cleared it, the game seems to perform mostly well now.So, with that aside, let’s focus on the campaign, which is divided in several chapters each one containing a set of missions. This approach of quantity over quantity is what hurts the game the most. Unlike a majority of shmups or on rails shooters, which have 5-7 stages tightly designed for scoring with a distinct and "huge battleship approaching fast" at the end, you get defense, escort missions, some item hunting and others that kind of break the pace in favor of more story building within the missions. There are actually some cool capital ships you take on (in a rather odd change of controls that removes inverted axis flight in favor of arcade directions) and a big "shoot the core" moment but they get spread away due to the chapter structure. To make matters worse there are two missions that I take were added to harken to the original Redout where you “race” against the enemies and they are probably my least favorite and what may put some people off for sure even though they are (thankfully!) very short. I could do without those!As an experiment to fuse genres I think it does fairly well, but that conflict of identity may end up being a deal braker for those looking for a full fledged space shooter or those looking for a pure arcade on-rails shmup with no filler, falling straight in the middle of both fields. The music is pretty good and it sounds great outside of the game too, although some of the tunes (like the menu one) are less than stellar. Would've loved something packing an extra punch since music tends to elevate shooters to greater heights.With the amount of space sims around it's a breath of fresh air to have an arcade title that only has a few minor key upgrades (and you should probably just pump it all on lock-on missiles and the guns anyway) and focuses a bit more on enemy and bullet patterns. There are even are a few instances of small bullet hell! I wouldn't mind if they double down on all those elements and keep most of the story sections on cutscenes (or briefings/debriefings in the vein of those cool Ace Combat 7/Armored Core 4-5 ones) for a potential sequel.In short, when the game clicks, it's great and it's a very nice surprise too considering how much I like on rails shooters. It’s also appreciated that it won’t demand much of your time either so that’s another plus in these busy days.(Note: the game was played entirely using an Xbox One wired controller, which quickly loaded an official configuration.)
_childDocuments_.name: Redout: Space Assault

_childDocuments_.review: Was pretty excited for this, as I'm a fan of arcade style space combat games but wound up really disappointed. It feels slow and floaty while the shooting isn't fun since it's so automated, which is really bad for a (mostly) on rails space shooter. The way the levels feel like they just loop you around the same area over and over is boring, so you don't feel like you're on a daring attack like you would in a Star Fox level. Upgrading your ship just doesn't feel significant or engaging. I went in hoping for star fox, and I left feeling like I was playing a bad mobile game, which it is.The Gummy ship missions in Kingdom Hearts 3, and even the ones in KH2 feel better than this. Don't waste your time with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is hard.I really wish there was a more nuanced rating system on Steam.That said, I'm going to have to give this game a negative rating, even though it breaks my heart to do so.If you were a fan of Redout, or interested in RSA because you like space combat games in general, I would not recommend this title.Redout Space Assault, very much retains the feeling of its mobile roots, it's not terrible, but also suffers from the diminished scale required for mobile games.Control:The combat levels take place in a rail shooter format, it's not bad, but control of the ship is limited.  Exploration levels, allow for more free movement, but in general it feels underwhelming.Graphics: RSA looks like a well-made mobile game, that's as honest as I can be... space does not seem immersive or believable, and if you were to spend money on a space combat game,  there are many other options on Steam which would be a better choice.Progression/Upgrades:The skill and progression systems very much feel like the free-to-play mobile games they were adapted from, obviously they've changed the drop mechanic, and there is no premium currency, so you will progress fine with minimum grinding, but there doesn't seem to be any in-depth customization possible.The developers addressed the fact that they made an intentional choice on the next thing I'm talking about, but the UI, still looks exactly like a mobile UI, at no point in the game are you able to get away from the feeling that you are playing a game meant for a phone.The story:There's nothing to care about, you spend the beginnings of levels hearing communication between characters which you will never find interesting, relating details of the story, which fails to display any imagination or draw you in whatsoever.  It feels pointless, and makes me wonder whether or not 34BT has any idea who actually comprises either their audience, or the audience for this type of game.Even without ANY story content, Redout managed to be more engaging than RSA.  Everything else being as it is, this is a glaring mistake, there are many areas of mobile game cannot hope to compete with a game made for computers, but a well written story, compelling characters, or excellent storyboard art, would have been one way the title could have sought Redemption.Price: At $10, the game is a good value, the game has a star Fox kind of vibe, and enough content to more than justify that price. I'm not sure what led the developer to the point that they're at, but it is indeed unfortunate.  REDOUT is one of my FAVORITE games, I'm going to guess that it might not have been sold as well as I'd hoped, especially since I always see it on deep discounts on third-party websites.  Between releasing the game on Apple arcade, scaling it back over all, I have to guess that the developer was having money troubles, and did what they had to do to adapt.It's a shame this happened, because after their previous game I would have happily paid full price for the game I had hoped they were making.Finally, I have to say that it's hard for me to leave a negative review on this game, because I'm so grateful to the Developers for their previous work.I WANT them to succeed, I want to see REDOUT 2 or RSA as it was intended.I also, can't turn a blind eye and pretend that the game is something is not.I hope that something changes in the future, and that becomes possible, nothing is sadder than seeing a promising Indie developer fail at their ambitions.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm genuinely pretty upset about Space Assault.  Redout is one of my all-time favorite games but Space Assault does not live up to the original.  It gives me a feeling that there is very little control over my ship and my aiming, and the weapons auto shoot and auto aim, although I expected somewhat strange controls since this was ported from mobile.  In addition, what I do have little control over does not feel so satisfying, since the game-play is so simplified.  There's almost no back story, and it was hard to tell what was going on, or who the main character was.  The voice acting felt very unnatural and out of place.  The difficulty spiked at times, and I found myself clearing some missions with ease while others I had to focus extra hard on (while trying to hassle with the lack of control over my ship).On the plus side, the visuals are stunning, just like the original game.  The music is great as well, although music transitions felt very abrupt at times.In short: Redout Space Assault could have been amazing if a few things were changed.  34BigThings struck gold with the first game but this one has too many shortcomings to be enjoyable.  It's really rather unfortunate.  However, I do still highly recommend the original Redout racing title released in 2016.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 85% rail shooter, 15% free flight in short mission sequences. Its shining moments are in large scale dogfights, occasional fast-action sequences, and bullet-hell dodge & weave combat, but the design of some levels and mechanics doesn't bring out those moments effectively enough. It certainly has enjoyable gameplay for the price point, but currently there are bugs and other design issues that hold it back just barely enough to not recommend it currently. The rail shooter segments have you traveling very slowly while battle drones appear in front of you in challenging patterns while you fire homing missiles at them and fire directly forwards with your armaments. In lieu of aiming, you use twin-stick controls for additional dodging and some degree of speed control. At first, slow movement seems inappropriate for a series known for its speed, but when it throws enemies at you like a proper bullet hell or when the speed picks up as you race past turrets it can be quite satisfying. These rail sections require a balance of dodging and offense because you cannot aim your regular weapons, only your ship. To this end, the game offers 4 different subsystems of your fighter to upgrade: Hull, Shields, Weapons, and Missiles, so you can customize those upgrades according to your favored playstyle: Do you go aggressive with your weapons and take a few extra hits, or play it safe and focus on dodging while you let your missiles clean up?Unfortunately, this dynamic is challenged by level design where enemies leave almost as fast as they appear, which makes the rail segments feel less like a bullet-hell and more like a DPS check. On certain levels some or even a majority of enemies remain on the edges of your view and cannot even be targeted by your weapons due to your ship's very constrained firing angles, so unless you invest heavily into missiles you will struggle. To make matters worse certain secondary or even primary objectives require eliminating as many as 90% of enemies. The game will sometimes toss you between free movement and "locked" strafing movement when fighting large ships. While this should be a convenient mechanic, it doesn't always work properly and the transition can leave you unable to dodge incoming fire and even missiles.Finally, the story is an interesting bit of Redout lore but only a little gets conveyed in the short dialogue sequences during missions so it feels less like a complete story and more like snapshots taken from one. The game isn't bad, but it would be best suited to at least 2 of the following: the thrilling speed of Redout, the intensity of a proper bullet hell, or the polish of a good space dogfighter, and it usually it has only 1 of them at a time.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, where to start.  This is one of those games where it really doesn't take much time to see how poor it is, that said, consider this my first impressions.  This game has less mechanical depth than star fox 64, horribly unreadable combat, and extremely simplistic physics that lack a satisfying sense of momentum when you move around the screen.  The story might as well not exist since no effort is made to ground the player in the lore.  I've played through the first 2 missions, and the only word that comes to mind to describe this is "uninspired", which is fairly ironic considering the star fox inspiration is obvious from the trailers.In some ways, I could see this coming, in hindsight at least.  The original Redout is truly a great game, at least in the design of the moment to moment gameplay.  It's one of my favorite AG racers after all.  That said, the substance for the backing systems (progression, powers, and the career mode) was extremely poor.  This game follows in Redout's footsteps in this way, but now lacks the satisfying gameplay that can make you overlook it.  I was eager to support whatever this studio put out next, and as a big star fox fan myself, I was optimistic about this game, but it fails to even meet the standard set in 1997, and I'd even say that star fox zero on the wii u is a significantly better game.I'm going to give it a bit more of a chance before refunding, but I fully expect my opinion to stay the same.  This review will be updated should my opinion change.EDIT: Gave it a few more missions, and yeah this is gonna be a refund.  0 of the "flavors" this game throws at the player are fun, imo of course.  I don't know if there's anybody I'd recommend this game to.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that could do with a neutral option.For those that loved Redout and considered it as a spiritual successor to Wipeout, and heard about this game 2 years ago, and assumed this would be the equivalent of Colony Wars, then think again.Unfortunately this is nothing more than a very simplistic Mobile on-rail shooter. It does look beautiful and like mobile games, this can be fun for an hour or so to pass a bit of time, but really nothing more.The gameplay is bland and dull. That's not because its on-rails - more that this is nothing more than a port of a mobile game. Alright for a few pounds to pass an hour, but really an hour was enough. Real shame, I was hoping that this would obliterate Everspace 2 as the latest space shooter. A missed opportunity! I think this games perhaps once had a much grander vision and as a result I expect this game will get bad reviews. If it was always marketed as a simple on-rails shooter then I think review would be more favourable.As it stands, if you fancy a fairly repetitive on-rails shooter to pass a few hours of time then this game does have merits. If you are after something more, then maybe everspace 2 is a preferred option.After another hour with the game I'd say this game is a recommended if you are into on-rails shooters, as its pretty good for short bursts. If you're hoping for something with free roam and advanced gameplay then I wouldn't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Many of the severe bugs were patched within a week of launch and I now have 100% completion in the game. The game is merely fine still but it is no longer broken beyond completion. The game looks alright and occasionally fulfills its space sim fantasy.1: There are a bevy of bugs and glitches in the game. There are currently objectives that are impossible to complete and an achievement that will not unlock. (I am a completionist and this is a big knock.)2: There were about 8 different ways I got soft locked in the game and had to restart missions. They were either easily reproducible or just an issue with the game at its core, leading me to believe it was known to be busted but the game had to come out.3: HDR is default on and the game has far too much glow most of the time. It is insanely easy to lose your aiming reticle and the solar flares are INTENSE. (The triple laser attachment is an instant headache)4. The game attempts to do  rail shooting and open world within single stages but does so in a really really rough way. You can be doing a rail portion then suddenly it is open arena. I like inverse controls and they switch settings depending on which you're in (no idea why) so in rail up is up then in open for me up is down and I just slam into the terrain or things. The overall experience is really disorienting in a way games like Star Fox 64 and Panzer Dragoon never were.5. The story feels incomplete and the voice acting is so bad it turns comical.6. The weapon system seems like it should give you a lot of options but really with objectives requiring X amount of kills or avoiding hull damage you end up forced to use the strongest ones stacked together to just get through things quickly.7. The upgrade system is very unclear. I have finished the game and I still don't know if you get stronger per point or is it only at the level up. The hull upgrade is also completely useless as you get hit with don't take hull damage objectives all the time so its just better to learn how to keep your shield up.8. There is a card boost system but for the life of me I can't see a reason to use anything other than weapon upgrades.9. You have to grind if you upgrade in a balanced way. I ended up going 9 and 9 in weapons and had half the levels in shields and hull because enemies reach a weird bullet sponge level and one mission in particular asks you to kill a % of them and through normal play I don't think you can reasonably do it.TL;DRGame is buggy and needs patches and then even so I think the game wouldn't be better than Afterburner, Panzer Dragoon, or Star Fox 64. It lacks the boss battle umph a rail shooter requires and the scripting is often broken or boring.
