_childDocuments_.review: 100% Worth the buy. This is what a video game should be. FUN. It isn't as polished as a triple A title but the soul and character that make a game great is there. It's a fantastic game to just blow off steam and have a cheap laugh here and there. It's a solid mix of Mario Odyssey and platformers of the N64 and PS2 Era. Think Spyro, Jak & Daxter, Conker, and Banjo. I would love to see bigger and better from this developer as well as an industry wide recognition that modern gaming has strayed too far from what makes an experience exceptional like this one. I hope I can encourage a purchase or two to support this studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Hell Pie

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, Creampie!It was really nice to play a game starring a demon where the demon actually looks like a demon and not a human with wings and horns. A wholesome Christian Game. It honestly makes hell look more fun to go to.This is Banjo Kazooie for big kids. Instead of a bird, you’ve got a pudgy, joyful cherub on a chain.My wife says it’s like A Hat in Time mixed with Conker and Doom.My wife’s boyfriend says it’s like if GOAT Simulator and DOOM had a baby and that baby smoked drugs with Conker.Hell Pie isn't a game, it's a litmus test for early identification of children who will grow up to be on law enforcement watchlists.Hell Pie is a 3D platformer with gameplay reminiscent of A Hat in Time. Unlike A Hat in Time, Hell Pie contains a large dose of not-safe-for-work humor, which usually hits the mark. Humor is obviously juvenile, but I loved it. The level designs are interesting and the controls intuitive, though maybe a bit less polished-feeling than some others in the genre. The areas themselves are fun to navigate with a lot of knooks to find collectables tucked away in. Some of the areas are very intriguing and unpredictable and considering how the entire premise and tone is unusual you never know what's gonna happen next... it kept me glued to the screen til the end. It really does feel like playing those old classics like Psychonauts, Ratchet, etc, but with some perfect modern mechanics. I really quite liked it. One thing it nails is the movement. It gives you an incredible amount of options from getting from point to point. Much of the movement involves swinging through the air from a chain, which you can anchor in space through the use of your flying cherub, Nugget.  The thing that most impressed though was that all platforming challenges seem designed for the standard default moveset, but through upgrades you can vastly increase your movement options such that you can pretty much ignore platforms and reach far away ledges just by yourself. Once fully upgraded, this allows for an absolutely absurd air distance traversal. A double jump, a dash, 5 spiderman swings and a really long glide. But it doesn't make the game too easy because there is a certain level of mastery required with the game's swinging mechanic and chaining together movement actions to reach far off ledges that would otherwise take longer to get to. It rewards player creativity, it rewards mastery of the game's systems and rewards collection if you found enough upgrade items to unlock those moves. And I think that shows a lot of confidence in the game's own systems and in players choosing how to use them. I feel like you don't see that too often in platformers, other games will design a jumping challenge to require you to use certain moves or have certain upgrades so the whole game feels more linear and you're just jumping through hoops the dev pre-made for you. It is a joy for any old school platforming enthusiast.Combats an afterthought but traversal is as good as any in the genre. I expected to enjoy it, as I do pretty much every 3D Platformer (I’m easily pleased), but godd**n this was much better than expected. I fu**king loved it. The mechanics, environments, characters, art style, & humor. All top notch! I'd say it's well priced for what it is; a well made 3D platformer with a smattering of toilet humour. Fairly short overall, Hell Pie just gets on with what it wants to show you and then leaves before it outstays it's welcome.I seriously hope it blows up or achieves a solid cult following, because it's the best 3D platformer I've played in ages. Humor is wonderfully juvenile, it's challenging, movement is fun, unique, and is pretty indepth. After just a couple nights with it, this quickly became one of my favorite games of the year, and possibly in my top 10 for the genre. Overall, I had a lot of fun, and would recommend the game to anyone who enjoys 3D platformers.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Beating the game and getting 90% of everything, I have to say it's a hit and miss experience.People who are already fans of platformers will probably enjoy Hell Pie quite a lot. It's unique setting, great/crude sense of humor, and an absolutely adorable protagonist have a lot of charm and will most likely be the reasons why you stick with it like me.Moreover the movement mechanics in the game are spot on and polished to a mirror's edge, the game absolutely nails the platforming of well... platforming. It's an absolute blast to be swinging around through the levels, collecting new outfits and seeing what new things come when you gather enough collectibles.Having said that, the game feels unfinished. There are many aspects of the game that feel rushed or like they have not been playtested, resulting in greatly lacking polish. I am mainly referring to:-lack of consistency (objects may appear in cutscenes, then disappear once the game shifts back to gameplay)-stuttering animations (there's seemingly little in between animations, the characters snap from one state to another)-carryable objects can easily become stuck in walls and become irretrievable, making you backtrack to start their carrying process over from the beginning-overall low quality of world 3-npc dialogue being incredibly easy to miss (the range in which you can listen to npcs talk is very small, combined with the high speed you're usually moving at you will constantly skip dialogue boxes)-the abrupt ending, I won't spoil it, I'll just say it's incredibly short and disappointingIn addition the game has two other major things that hold it back outside of lack of polish, that being repetitiveness and lack of challenge. Around world 3 the game becomes less and less fun the more you play it, as the way you deal with all your problems never changes apart from when the games gives you a gun, or when you unlock the final set of horns, both of which had great gameplay segments.As for the difficulty, it's a cakewalk (HA!), the game never poses any challenge making you at most repeat a segment once or twice. It is a real shame.All in all Hell Pie is a decent game, Nate being adorable, the movement mechanics being incredible and the humor making you smile all contribute to making it a good game. However all the shortcomings heavily detract from the experience and often made me groan with disappointment, lamenting that this beautiful little gem has an awful amount of blemishes.I really hope the devs will update the game and work out the kinks.
_childDocuments_.name: Hell Pie

_childDocuments_.review: Oh wow- I almost forgot what it felt like to play something crafted with love and different with no compromises on the original vision. I love the setting of the game, it being in hell is perfect and the characters that you meet along the way are ridiculous and entertaining. I love the adult themed entertainment that I haven't seen a platformer since Conker's Bad Furr Day. I don't throw that comparison around willy nilly by the way. It's as refreshing as it is disgusting. The most important thing, platforming, is rock SOLID. Like, it's good, really, really good. It makes exploring the hub worlds and getting around extremely fun and easy to do once you quickly get the hang of it. There's also a lot to collect and unlock along the way in terms of abilities and outfits so while being fun to play it gives you a reason to explore. I applaud the developers for being fearless and making a game that feels like a game they always wanted to play as well as make. TDLR; If you like platforming collectathons and adult humor akin to Conker's Bad Fur Day, for $25 dollars, this is more than worth it's weight in gold.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm definitely not going to go crazy, Hell Pie is a great 3D platformer with both nostalgic and funny gameplay!One day you get a phone call from Satan instructing you to ask the chef about his special cake. It's Satan's birthday and the cook has totally forgotten about it. What follows is a crazy story.Check out some great gameplay from the game here: Hell Pie is a 3D platformer that in our eyes focuses on adult gamers, especially with humor and bloody scenes.But let's face it, this is a teen game anyway, I would definitely play this when I was younger and today I played it too and later I'll turn it on again to continue playing!It's a pleasant title that keeps you sweet through four different worlds.The visual style fits perfectly with the setting that the developer wants to create and here too it is not really taken seriously, because that way you get styes as enemies or real plants in the form of genitals. There are some bugs here and there, but they can of course be fixed with an update.Through the four different worlds you will search for a number of unique ingredients that the cook needs to bake his cake.Of course, you are not alone, as you get help from a captive angel, Nugget.Nugget corpse reminds me a bit of Eric Cartman, I can't give a good explanation for this either, see for yourself:You can use it to fight enemies, but also as a grappling hook to get to higher or further positions. The open world also allows this, but of course you will experience a linear progression with which you can only travel to the next world when you have collected enough ingredients.A 3D platformer is of course nothing without collectables and we can reassure you that there are enough in Hell Pie. You have cans of food that you can collect, with which you can upgrade Nugget and, for example, unlock an extra swing. You will find small creatures with a horn hidden, with which you can give Nate an upgrade.Throughout the levels you will find teleporters. These are devices that serve as checkpoints and fast travel, while also saving your progress.The enemies also seem to be placed very statically in the levels, which makes for a stable challenge, but not impossible either.The game works great on steam decks as well: The game also has good support for ultra-wide resolutions, you can see an example of gameplay at 3480*1080 here:

_childDocuments_.review: + Extremely well crafted platformer and collectathon game with very responsive controls. Movement feels fluid and seamless, barring some very occasional glitches or hiccups. You have plenty of tools to unlock that make that responsiveness even more rewarding - direct upgrades that allow you to do more moves, horns that give you unique abilities you can combo into movement or use to open new paths.+ Goofy, gross, and slightly twisted writing and humor that often hits the mark and had me laughing pretty consistently. It doesn't try too hard, which makes it hit that sweet spot that is hilarious and endearing.+ Art style that is grungy, flubby, and really vividly... 'ugly'. But, designed to look that way, and combined with bright and cheery environments, some cutesy enemies here or there, and a lovable protagonist duo, the visual style strikes a pretty good balance that you'll find enjoyable. It retains some of the cute energy of its platforming predecessors for sure.+ Unlocks aplenty to reward you for exploration, with what has to be over 20(?) costumes for both you and your companion nugget. The system reminded me quite a bit of Mario Odyssey, with collecting a currency to purchase outfits (granted, no hat/costume seperation). Combine this with abilities, horn abilities, and side areas with challenging platforming, and you're looking at quite a bit of enjoyable rewards to pursue.+ Short and sweet - after collecting almost every reward and beating the game, I'm at a solid ~14 hours. I will probably spend some time to unlock every cosmetic and find every collectible, which could bump it up to around ~15-16 hours, maybe more depending on how long it takes me to earn the currency.- There is an overwhelming feeling that this game might've been rushed. There are loads of blocked elevator doors that seem to hint at a far larger scope at one point in development, and another sign of this is the circular demons of hell room seems to imply that at one point we encountered every deadly sin because some of the doors open. Also, the final zones and encounters felt... odd. The final level only has one sublevel, the final scenes have numerous spelling errors and borderline filler text in dialogue boxes, and you're left feeling kinda weird about the way it all ended because the ending happens suddenly and without any sort of... climax. - There are a handful of collectibles that I am missing that, in trying to find them, I found significant frustration and came up empty handed. They were all in hub worlds, which are simply too big! A post-game reward that upgrades your now-useless starter horns to give rough AOEs of where collectibles are would be a huge help, and a worthwhile reward for beating the game.- Nugget repeats his lines far far too much. His text bubbles often got in the way of my vision, and his babbling sound got a bit annoying when trying to find collectibles.  I would recommend an option to disable nugget repeating any lines, or at least make it to where he only repeats a line on the first load into a level.I love the everliving ♥♥♥♥ out of this game. Yes, it might've been shorter than I'd hoped, and it isn't perfect, but the gameplay loop is satisfying, and the entire game is endearing and entertaining, and for an indie game priced at the extremely low price of $22, this game is a steal and a real treat to experience. It's unlike any other game in the market right now. It's very fun! I want to see a Hell Pie 2 that is more ambitious and longer. I want to see more from this developer and their stupid crude sense of humor. Please, buy this game. They absolutely deserve your money!

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who says presentation is 100% unimportant in a videogame should play Hell Pie.ORA monkey’s paw wish for complaining modern platformers are too milquetoast.Hell Pie’s a competent collectathon at its core, really. Basic movement is silky smooth. The main gimmick of swinging around with your cherub is unique and a bit overpowered, but who doesn’t like flying over things when applying a bit of physics knowledge? Level design isn’t remarkable, but it does it’s job. There’s a good mix of open-ended explorable hubs and linear obstacle course style levels, the game also introduces new elements and stage gimmicks regularly enough to keep things from getting stale. Collectibles are all around, there’s a decent variety and they all have specific uses like buying new costumes (always a plus). The game’s a bit simple overall, but usually all this would be enough to give me a decent time. Too bad the game’s constantly farting in its hand and forcing me to smell it.It’s not that the game has edgy humor, or has immature humor, it’s that the game barely has humor to begin with. The dialogue’s generally witless and full of typos. I go into a sewer full of ♥♥♥♥, and there’s turds in S.S. uniforms executing ugly big nippled blob monsters who clearly eat ♥♥♥♥ by the brown stains on their hands and mouths. Definitely crass, but what’s the joke? It’s funny because it’s disgusting? Everything in the game is disgusting, that’s not novel or a joke that can last for a few minutes, let alone an entire game. I’m not laughing or even offended, I just go “Ew.” and then I have to spend the next 10 minutes looking at ♥♥♥♥ and blob monster gore before going to the next batch of pointlessly ugly things. It may give you some nostalgia for early internet shock humor at first, but that wanes quickly and the game never really gets more clever than “that enemy has a vagina for a mouth”. Don’t think you can just skip all the dialogue and focus on the gameplay alone because so much of the humor is visual, good luck ignoring that the power star you picked up is some jizz! Hahahaha! That’s all it comes down to. It’s a decent platformer but the gameplay’s not good enough to be worth putting up with the rest of the game. Any fun I got from swinging around was usually canceled out soon after by some obnoxious dialogue or picking up a half-digested human as a collectible. This game is usually compared to Conker’s Bad Fur Day, but Conker is much more clever (it has some actual jokes), and that’s saying a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Never have I thought that the metaphorical phrase “Don’t judge a book by its cover” could be taken more seriously when it comes to describing what Hell Pie is like. Stating this title as a kid-friendly game based on its appearance is the equivalent of saying the movie “Team America: World Police” being suitable for a family night watch because of its puppet characters. If you aren’t shy from these themes, you’re in for a wacky trip.Let us grab the horns of Nate, the cute little Demon of Bad Taste, the 8th Sin in Hell, as you are tasked with finding the most unimaginable, disgusting, foul ingredients from the upper worlds. All of that to conjure up the ultimate grotesque, Dark Souls-like monster of a birthday cake you ever bake to celebrate Satan’s birthday. Accompanied by Nugget the Cherub, the tiny naked angel who assists you with combat and swings you around to overcome the increasing obstacles.Exploration is mainly on foot, enhanced with the speed boosting or gliding horns once you acquire them by naturally progressing. There are many hidden and locked away areas which unlock only after you finish certain levels, or own the right skills (or horns). Backtracking every now and then is particularly necessary if you care about getting your hands on 100% collectibles. Since some maps are somewhat a huge pain in the butt to memorize due to their sizes, prepare to be on the lookout everywhere you go, if you don’t want to miss that single candymeat in the total of 23/24 collected. Otherwise, you can complete the ingredients list by playing leisurely, as they are well placed in order not to be missed even when you try to.The first 15 minutes in the starting area and sub-level might not catch much of your attention with its parodic corporate theme and small, long corridors. However, once you unlock the elevators to gain access to the upper environments on the surface (we are in Hell after all), only then will the grand view and pleasing aesthetic of Hell Pie shine the most. This errand trip brings you to locations as low as the repulsive sewers filled with literal turds attacking on anyone on sight, or the morally questionable human meat slaughterhouse with naked people being treated like livestock, and much more for you to find out. Of course, you can’t be expected to play a game that takes place in Hell without going to the high heaven, at least there won’t be aggressively talking poops up there. All of this will be in full display behind a uniquely cute and cartoonish visual style, which strangely enough makes Hell Pie stand out more than most platformers out there.Collecting enough candymeats in your pocket, you can utilize them to enhance Nugget’s abilities like additional swing charges to improve movement range, extra speed boost while swinging, or just a small but very useful height gain to the mid-air attack, etc. Nate is not completely useless by himself though, you can also strengthen him like higher wall climbing, adding damage to his dash, etc. There’s even a level that completely disables Nugget, but that won’t stop the little demon from achieving his goals.Besides candymeats, make sure to look out for the adorable unilambs that are required to be sacrificed, if Nate wants to switch to a different pair of horns. These pointy tusks aren’t just for fashion, they assist him not only with combat, but also greatly with covering large distances, and unlocking hidden areas. The more useful tricks you have at your disposal, the more pathing options you gain to complete the level.Lastly, combat exists, but it’s so simplified that it’s possible to skip most of the enemies encounters on the way. They are just mere annoyances to deal with, and they respawn when you reset at a checkpoint. Except for a few boss fights, you will defeat anything with a single attack. With that being said, there are a few instances where you are given guns with infinite ammo to shoot and destroy obstacles, surprisingly. Hold the trigger and happy hunting.If you can look past the exaggerated violence, blood and unfiltered, dirty sexual jokes, Hell Pie is a fun and solid platformer that brings to the table a decent range of exploration, and a good amount of adequate skills and movesets to traverse from the burning depth of Hell to the gate of the High Heaven.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid collectathon platformer with a focus on aerial mobility. Unlockable skills allow you to stay in the air for an excessively long time, to a point where you can skip most platforming challenges. Overshooting a platform is far more common than undershooting it.Difficulty is low in general. The only way to challenge yourself is to deliberately avoid getting new skills and abilities, but swinging all over the map is more fun. I wish there were more platforming challenge sections similar to the final Lucky Cat room or Light Gate levels.There's combat in the game but it might as well not be there. All common enemies die in one hit and have easily avoidable patterns. There's three boss fights but none of them were particularly difficult. It's very much a casual game. Dying has virtually no consequences. There's no lives system, you just lose a couple coins which you can easily get back by walking a few meters to collect new ones.I spent about 20 hours on this game with 100% collectibles but I spent a lot of time faffing about. I would imagine casual playthroughs would last about half that time. The mobility in the game encourages speedrunning so playtime can be very short if you choose to play that way.Hell Pie takes inspiration from 3D platformers that came before it. You have a skill set based on two conjoined characters, à la Banjo-Kazooie or Yooka-Laylee, a selectable ability wheel similar to A Hat In Time, and the general tone and humor of Conker's Bad Fur Day.Even though Conker is my favorite of the 3D platformers of yore, the humor in Hell Pie is very hit or miss. The game is excessive in its crudeness. It's like someone took a look at the Great Mighty Poo and thought to themselves: "This is good but it needs more poop." The game is filled to the brim with cheeks, genitals, orifices, poop, farts, and gore. There's a couple moments that made me chuckle but with the over-reliance on gross-out visual gags, the humor is a bit lacking, and gets boring fast. I do appreciate how needlessly cruel it is to some characters, though.The game is stable but glitchy. I haven't gotten any crashes but I have experienced a few glitches. I fell through the map once. I got animation glitches where the main character was running backwards until I changed maps. I got glitches where movement directions were locked for a forced camera section but remained locked after leaving that section so pressing W always moved me the same direction instead of forward relative to the camera. -And I had moments where Nugget the angel disappeared or got launched somewhere off screen. None of these had any long lasting negative effects but they were interesting nonetheless. There's also a bunch of spelling errors but that's neither here nor there.I had fun with the game and I'd be interested in a sequel. The one complaint I have that actually matters is that the game is too easy and needs more platforming challenges that actually force you to utilize your entire moveset.

_childDocuments_.review: is an obscene 3D platformer in which the player needs to collect ingredients to make a pie for Satan himself.The story of  is quite simple: Satan’s birthday is around the corner and you are tasked to collect various ingredients, to help out the chef creating the most hellish and most disgusting pie to celebrate Satan’s special day.I’m personally not the biggest fan of platformers but the  demo convinced me to try out the full game whenever it came out.The gameplay itself is very fluent and feels good which helped me to get into the game quite fast.One of the best things in  are the different hub worlds and its levels. Whilst the hub worlds are self-explanatory and offer some exploration, collectibles and enemies to kill, they are just the gateway to the actual smaller levels. Every level’s location feels very unique, mostly because the settings are all different and get a bit more challenging towards the end.Skills that the player can acquire are mostly pretty straight forward but you use the swing ability and its upgrades more than anything else.  offers different upgrades for the horns as well, that help to navigate throughout the world and open passages that would otherwise not be accessible or just too hard to reach. The game is kind of advertised as obscene but besides one or two things it’s really not that obscene as you might expect, so keep that in mind before you buy it – besides that small “issue” it’s a really nice and entertaining 3D platformer. Is  worth your money? If you’re into platforms, I’d say it’s worth your money for sure.If you’re not into platformers that much but still look for a somewhat short game to play here and there, I’d say this game might still be worth to try out, mostly because of its slightly obscene environment and it’s humor.“” - NuggetIf you found this review helpful, feel free to visit my  page.

_childDocuments_.review: Consider this review more of a neutral review than a true negative, but with steam's binary recommendation system, I've gotta pick the one that feels more right.This game's sense of humor just did not work for me at all, which kills a lot of what this game is offering.  It'll no doubt work for some people, but it was just miss after miss for me.  The only reason I kept playing is just because 3D platforming collectathons are one of my favorite types of games, and this was one of the few I had but hadn't beaten yet.  Mechanically it's a pretty solid and fun time.  The movement feels a bit weird at first, it kinda feels like every surface is made of ice and slippery thanks to the momentum, but it's something you get used to after a while.  You have some really solid abilities with the grappling that allow you to do some pretty cool stuff once you get enough upgrades, letting you feel like you're outmaneuvering a level when you find a cool little skip for a section.  There's plenty of stuff to collect, though there's enough in each section to kinda make you wish one of the upgrades you could get pointed out collectibles, since you will almost certainly need to sit through a guide to help you figure out where the 1/20 cans you missed were in a section.  But I don't think the mechanics and satisfying collectibles are enough to save this for me.I'd only really recommend this if you are a big fan of 3D platforming collectathons and are truly desperate for a new one you haven't played yet.  Or if you think the trailer is the funniest thing you've ever seen I suppose.  But otherwise I think you're better off passing.

_childDocuments_.review: is a 3D platformer/Collect-a-Thon game made by the indie developer Sluggerfly and published by Headup Publishing. It was released on Steam on July 21, 2022. To provide some context, I got the game in the Masterful Modern 3D Platformers bundle from Humble Bundle, along with some others. I barely heard of the game before, aside from the fact that it was considered the spiritual child of Conker's Bad Fur Day. How good is it? Let’s find out!In Hell Pie, you play as Nate, known as the 8th sin and the Demon of Bad Taste. Nate is also a small, inconsiderate, goat-shaped demon. While “working” as usual in your office in hell, you get called by no less than Satan himself. The Devil gives you a top-priority mission: go ask Chef about his pie!You won’t make Satan wait for his pie, right?As you take the road toward Chef's Kitchen, you have to walk through a section of the office that will serve as a tutorial and teach you about the controls.Upon your arrival in the kitchen, and after a bootie reveal, Chef asks you to go gather all the ingredients needed for the recipe. And that’s how your journey begins! Time to make the best Hell Pie of all!Well, there's not much of a story here. The plot is just an excuse to give you something to do. You’re a small devilish goat. You travel from level to level to gather stuff and that’s it. Even the backstory behind your character isn’t actually developed. You just know the basics about who you are and what you have to do. The gameplay is very classic for a platformer. You can jump or double jump, throw your lil’ slave angel in the face of your enemies to attack them (or just slam him into a wall because why not), and even use your winged pet as a way to balance yourself through the air and jump from platforms to platforms.However, I must admit that it lacks a bit of precision, and the retro-styled camera doesn’t help much either. I died more times because of a bad jump than being killed by enemies.Hell Pie is a Collect-a-Thon as well. That means you have a lot of items to collect everywhere. That’s even the central point of the game. You’ll mostly collect gems that'll serve as currency to buy new clothes, but there are some other items of higher importance, such as tinned food to feed your angel pet to unlock new skills, lucky cats that'll be used to access the Greed room, lambs that'll be used to get new power-ups, and, of course, the ingredients needed for the pie!As said, in this game, you have a skill tree that will allow you to unlock new skills that’ll be useful and ease your adventure (reaching further platforms, giving you more health, etc.). You can also unlock new power-ups that will allow you to run faster or destroy weak walls, for example.The office serves as a main hub that lets you access through hellevators to other hub levels that all have small sub-levels to explore as well.There are a few puzzles to solve, but nothing really complex. They are easy enough.Regarding the playtime, it took me 19 hours to finish the main story, playing slowly. I still have a few things to collect and some achievements to unlock related to that.Overall, the game isn’t hard to beat, and getting 100% of the achievements shouldn't be much of a problem. However, it may be time-consuming since some of them are about finding all of specific items. Not to help much, some of them are hidden, and nothing will hint you about their locations.Hell pie is really charming. It has nice cartoonish and colorful graphics that weirdly fit the ambiance really well. It allows to hide the true nature of the game (a gross kind of game) behind a seemingly innocent and joyful one. The animations are nice, and there are a good number of elements in the decor that can be interacted with (printers, sinks, the NPCs that react when being hit, etc.). The music here is decent to good. While the songs fit the game, some of them are rather generic. Some others are already much enjoyable, though. I really liked , for example.The sounds part feels quite the same. Nothing exceptional, it’s decent enough, but some can be really annoying. I remember mostly the alert sounds that really got on my nerves in the Flavor Peaks level. Angel gibberish is fun at first, but after a couple of hours, it ends up being redundant.I had so much fun playing this game! I’ve really loved my time since the beginning! Hell Pie has a lot of humor in it! If you're supposed to be the demon of bad taste, the same applies to the game itself as well. From  to , to  or even . The game, while looking cute at first, is just gruesome. It’s a special kind of humor that is not for everyone. I did like it from my end, and I must admit that it had the merit of making me laugh a couple of times! I truly enjoyed the ambiance of the game.- Lots of fun.- The humor.- Nice and cute graphics.- Jumping from platforms to platforms lacks a bit of precision.- The game is quite easy.- Some sounds are annoying.I’d totally recommend the game. It’s a really classic kind of Collect-a-Thon with a gameplay that isn’t innovating, but I still loved my time spent in Hell Pie! It was a pleasant discovery, full of humor that I made here, thanks to that bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW IN PROGRESS: I was looking forward to this after the demo. Possibly one of the my favorite releases this year. It's Conker's Bad Fur Day in essence, and wears influences and references on its sleeve, while providing a fantastic movement system, expansive level design, and a high level of creativity in its content.Movement system is polished and dynamic. You have a ton of options right out of the box, and some early upgrades within the first few hours make it possible to reach more places than you might have thought possible. Platforming is forgiving, but affords many possibilities when you max out your reach. There was even an instance where a level changed and it didn't seem possible to reach a collectible with missing platforms, but I managed to finesse my way up and nab it. Movement becomes intuitive within minutes, and I found myself really enjoying how tight it is. I found myself grinning while playing through levels with absurd story setups. There's a lot of great ideas packed into the first few hours at the very least. There have been a few bugs and QOL stuff I would expect to be fixed soon, like dialogue disappearing too quick or pink bits (collectible currency) getting stuck in the ground, but I also got shot WAY up into the sky after un-pausing/alt-tabbing back into the game. Not a big deal as it let me glide while falling to get past some piranhas. Overall, I would recommend to definitely buy this if you like 3d Mario tier move-set platforming with millennial toilet humor, or if you loved Conker, Banjo, or Crash. It's very creative from what I've seen so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game when I first started playing and was really excited to see how fun the rest of it would be, but just ended up disappointed in the end. BUT; I feel like the devs completely forget how overpowered it is as a movement ability. There are so many levels with platforming spots that seem like they were intended to be difficult, but just get completely obliterated by the fact that you can skip the entire thing just by swinging. Light gates and the tutorial worlds you play in (when unlocking Horns) are no exception at all. The only way I can think of countering this is by limiting your movement at specific spots. I enjoy the game so much till after the end boss, but as an achievement hunter, the game at this moment is a bit rough. It has many collectibles to find, and in the levels themselves it isn't too bad and youtube videos can help you a lot, but in the hub worlds.. those are so big and there are so many collectibles that it is very hard to find the missing ones. The developers are thinking about implementing a system to have an indication of where to find the collectibles you missed and I really hope they will implement that in the future, but that might take a while if they implement it. _childDocuments_.review: Just beat this game and.... its.... something.First off, the game has great mechanics, the abilities are fun, the levels are expansive, massive even, with a huge main map and 3 worlds branching off each map, but its not really a great platforming game.First, the game gives you abilities that allows you to skip most of the platforming early on if you bother to even kind of look for collectables. However the game does eventually take into account your abilities for the last 2 levels, which were nice. I enjoyed them, but it felt strange to make platforming redundant in a platform game to such an extent.Secondly, this game makes one of the worst possible mistakes, and its part of that MASSIVE map design, on top of tons of yellow, orange, red backgrounds, on top of having the smallest possible collectable items they could possibly design. With barely any standout features until you are on top of them. The joy of platforming really comes from the collectathon aspects. I love doing it and this game doesn't seem to be very interested and I say this because there is nothing in the game to guide you to any extent on where any of these collectables are, which is fine initially, stuffs EVERYWHERE so you find things and are exploring. When going back to these worlds however its just a ton of redundant map, with very  very very tiny items hidden in nooks and crannies of which there are potentially thousands and a lot of the map design is redundant design, that is, you can go to wild spots, and there is nothing there. With no design in mind to help you find these to ANY extent, its like they have no idea what game they were designing. I have never played an open world collectathon that has made this mistake to the extent these devs have. Its possibly the worst sin you can ever make when designing a platform game and for that I can't recommend it.Finally, there was generally terrible boss design, in that, there were really only 2 and both felt buggy and half finished. I wouldn't say this is the worst sin, but it definitely dampens the entire platforming concept when you beat a world, get to the end, and are generally greeted with nothing, no boss, nothing cool. Its just kind of bland and for the tons of collectables I did collect beyond the standard requirements, I didn't get anything worthwhile. You can open doors seemingly infinitely as some sort of end game concept, but they never led to anything super cool. I got 1 costume after opening like 12-13? There was one cool thing, I wont ruin it, but overall, it was just rooms full of nothing. Idk.I wish I could recommend this, I really do. Many parts of it were well done, but point number 2 is so bad, that its like going for a haircut and the barber forgetting her scissors. Its such a misstep that its infuriating. Id love to know how that conversation went where they decided to not use the multiple avenues they have already in the game to just not do anything at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Man this game was an absolute blast. If you liked A Hat in Time, this is your next 3D platformer. It looks beautiful with ray tracing on and the gameplay is super tight and smooth. Upgrades are worth acquiring and the levels are great with many secrets and collectibles to find. I wish there were more levels though; there are only three big areas with three sub-areas each, a hub with sub-levels as well and one final area smaller than first three. It may look like a lot but I finished the game in 5 hours, so maybe one or two more big areas would have been very appreciated. Not complaining though, just nitpicking. _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, this just didn't grip me. It tries to be some sort of 3d platformer / collectathon, but mainly you're just collecting gems to unlock new outfits. And on death you lose some, but they keep respawning each time, so ... what's the point? There are some other things to collect, like unlock points, which you already need 5 again for the next level up... and the counter resets after every level. There you will unlock great skills such as more and faster swings ... and health. Mostly. Then you also have your "horn abilities", which you will unlock in the various overworlds, which also have smaller individual levels apparently. The 1st ability is to actually see the entire map in grey scale, complete with quest givers and objectives. The 2nd let's you run a bit faster.Couple that with a rather lacklustre, downright ugly graphics style, a weird story about the devil's birthday cake, and the general lack of ... I don't know, charm? Identity?Controls feel kinda floaty, and the lack of being able to see WHERE you're jumping to is a big no-no for me. It's imperative the players knows where he is relative to the 3d plane at all times. Decades old platformers did that better and they were VERY limited in what they could show on screen. Whether it's BK, Mario, Donkey Kong, Gex, Conker, platformers were a staple back in the 90s, early 2000s. I'd love to see them revived, but this isn't it.The humour if you can call it that ... nah, just nah. I'm not squeamish or anything, but it just wasn't funny. It's like 2020+ era shows for "modern audiences". They think they're funny, because they're gross, but they don't understand how to make gross funny. Or anything really.You can see they're going for the old PS/N64 era of jump n run platformers, but either I just can't get into these anymore, because I'm getting too old, or they just can't capture the essence... Banjo Kazooie for life. I'd still play THAT game any day if they ever bothered to remake/remaster it. That's my bar, sorry. If you can't beat an almost 30 year old game then I can't really be bothered to play this.Yooka Laylee tried it and got almost close. Hat in Time tried it and got even a bit closer, but the story just wasn't my jam. This might be okay for a budget title, but it costs 25 bucks, and it didn't grab me from minute 1 till minute 30, so I'm afraid I got better things to do. Maybe it gets really good later on, but I doubt it, and if so you need to do a better job of grabbing your players' attention.

_childDocuments_.review: As a 3D platformer this is great. Fantastic freeing movement abilities that only get more fun the more you unlock to the point where you can easily and satisfyingly bypass any obstacles. Some of the level design is a bit poo, but at least you can pretty much decide how much you want to engage with it with the traversal options you have. Decent amount of hidden stuff too: some for gameplay upgrades, some for cosmetics, some for nothing. Definitely a better platformer than Conker which it seems heavily inspired by.If you're looking for fun characters/story and are over the age of 12 this might leave you wanting. I GET that it's deliberately bad taste and cringey but that doesn't actually make it more palatable. I will admit a couple of gross jokes got a heh out of me, but it's just never-ending body fluids and orifice honks to the point that it's sort of embarrassing. Also there are some overlong references with nothing added that I doubt the target audience will even get, let alone get a laugh out of. Yes I do recognise this bit from Scarface, now what? Oh it's still going. Doing the whole bit. And now that bit's over and there weren't any jokes. Why. Oh here's that fat guy from Monty Python, I guess he'll subvert expectations and do somethi- oh no he's just done the same gag. Ok. The game is at its best when it forgets it's trying to get you grounded by your fussy mum and just lets you jump around in a colourful silly area.So yeah, a recommend from me. But in the same way I show the Binding of Isaac to my friends and have to look all disappointed and desperate when the first thing they see is an enemy fart a cloud of spunk or whatever "I promise, once you get past that, it is actually fun"Also the devs seem great! Attentive and humble. Already made it so your chubby little companion doesn't talk so much if you get sick of him blocking the screen with speech bubbles.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Less of a thumbs down and more of a sideways hand waving while shrugging. Really wish Steam put a middle-of-the-road option for these.I can't say I didn't have a little bit of fun with this game. The movement system is enjoyable and allows for pretty clever exploration and platforming challenges, though with that said, most of the later levels don't really accommodate for the amount of jumps and swings you get later on, and I had more fun seeing how much I could bypass platforming sections or sequence breaking past places that would need certain powerups. It's probably the best thing about the game if anything, not to say anything about the combat, which is as basic as you can get for a 3D platformer.The visuals are fine, they're rendered well and the optimization is decent, with later updates fixing some of the main issues I'd had with the game.The humor, for me, is very hit-or-miss, usually going on the latter. Vulgar humor can be done very well, but this game sometimes doesn't know how to let off or give it enough nuance to make any impact, it's just gross stuff 90% of the time. There were a couple more subtle lines that got a chuckle from me, and I think there could've been more done with Nate's role in the Underworld, but everything else either fell flat or just repulsed me if anything.The soundtrack is also just fine. I didn't dislike any of the music, but none of it really stuck either, and the only issues I had with audio were Nugget's constant repeating lines before they were patched out.Without wishing to spoil much either, while the bosses were halfway decent for what the combat allowed, and the final boss was probably the best of them, the ending is incredibly abrupt and anti-climactic, feeling less like a joke and more like a middle finger to the player.Overall, I feel as though Hell Pie could've spent more time baking in the oven, though its release was possibly due to time constraints from backer promises, so who knows. There's a lot of areas just barred off completely and a paltry number of levels with the beginning of a movement system that felt genuinely nice to play with, muddled with overall mediocre level design, writing that feels half-assed at times, and an almost desperate notion to cling to its 'edgy, disgusting' sense of humor that doesn't evolve much past what you'd see 14-year olds in 2008 discuss at recess.TL;DR: 5/10, if you really need to scratch that platforming itch buy it when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally like 3D Platformers, but Hell Pie was entertaining enough to keep me playing to the end. However, It's geared towards adults with adult humor, so there is quite a lot of gore and some NSFW jokes. If you don't like that kind of thing, don't play it, but otherwise, you may enjoy it. I personally liked the setting, it's strange, cute, and kinda funny at times. Adult humor can be kind of cheap to me sometimes, like NSFW can only be funny for so long, but thankfully, they don't overdo it to an obnoxious point imo.The gameplay itself was pretty good for the most part. I love the swinging mechanic, and some of the level designs were fun and creative. I mainly liked the Gluttony stage. I found the horns mechanic to be mostly useless (90% of it was using the speed boost horns), the hit boxes seemed off (Nugget sometimes wouldn't hit enemies that were directly in front of him?), and the movement feels strangely slippery; it messed me up a couple times and was a bit annoying. Overall, I didn't  the game -- for a small team, they did good, and I wouldn't discredit the work they put in it -- but there are definitely a lot of issues I've had with it. I wouldn't say you should  play the game; it  fun, you may like it. BUT, in my honest opinion, it's not worth $25 for how long the game is, and for the issues I've had with it.

_childDocuments_.review: It was better than I expected, really liked it! It's definitely not for everybody as it's extremely tasteless and crazy. Here my quick thoughts on it!Story and writing- Totally nuts.- You are a dude from hells office and Satan calls you to make a pie for him.- Then you have to collect disgusting ingredients. They are in different worlds and you have to do insane things to get them.- Satan is hilarious. Especially at the end lol.Gameplay- It's a jump and run game.- Really like the movement options. You get good abilities early on, and can then go for upgrades. Swinging around and boosting is a lot of fun and feels very good.- The great move set allows you to be very mobile and explore the world your way.- Once you get a hang of it, controls are very good and satisfying.- A lot to explore and secrets to find.- You can unlock new horns, that give you new abilities.- The levels are well designed and large, you definitely have to look at the map for navigation from time to time.- Each level has its own theme and all are just.... insane, brutal, while being light hearted, but still dark. It's a weird mix.- You can unlock the most insane costumes for you and your degenerate fat little angel thing.Visuals- Overall pretty good looking.- Textures are lacking.- Art style is great and there are some neat effects like RT reflections.- Some very weird pop in at certain places.- Some levels look great like the first one, later levels like the jungle can look rather bland.- Your fat angel has fat wobble physics.- The game offers DLSS, which is a good way to get good performance with RT and high resolutions.- Game looks clean.VerdictI liked it a lot. The game surprised me at many points, gameplay was a lot of fun, it was a wild ride.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm going to be breaking this down into three categories: Graphics, Gameplay, Story, and giving a rating for each. Five point scale.1 - Terrible2 - Bad3 - Average4 - Good5 - ExcellentCool? Cool.Doesn't blow me away by any means, but the stylized cartoony aesthetic works very well for this. No complaints. I also like the grittily realistic depictions for when you collect the disgusting food items. That's a nice touch.Okay, so I feel like I need to justify this one. The grappling hook mechanic is actually super fun and can be really satisfying to pull off tricks, but it's finnicky. Sometimes it just doesn't do what you want it to do. Sometimes the game decides that you just don't have a double jump. You also need to get used to the fact that when you use the grapple, your character drops slightly. That's lead to me smacking my feet on the very edge of the platform and falling to my death numerous times.Spoiler: Last horns in the game The combat is very one-note. You get a little variety when it comes to attacks, but it's all just melee. No ranged attacks. This doesn't tend to be an issue in the earlier levels as even the floaty-shooty enemies have slow or slowish moving projectiles you can reflect back at the attacker with a well-timed hit. But guess what? In the last world, you have the same types of enemies but this time they have fast-moving projectiles you CAN'T reflect. Not having a ranged attack makes these enemies way more annoying than they have any right to be.Oh yeah, the final boss actually has you using a ranged weapon. At a distance. And I hate aiming with a controller.Let's just touch briefly on the little talent system for Nugget. Mostly okay, not a lot of complaints. Except there's a few that are just traps meant to waste your points, as you'll never use them (To name a few: ground pound, that vertical grapple thing, and then the later version you can use in mid air).Hilarous. Maybe not your thing if you're not into absurdist or gross-out humour.Very much reminds me of something like Conker's Bad Fur Day. Essentially the premise is you're some unwitting intern roped into a plan to make the most disgusting, vile, putrid pie imaginable for Satan's birthday. And you do find a lot of really disgusting stuff. The levels are wacky and sometimes just downright absurd, the various NPCs often have some pretty funny stuff to say, and also  It seems like they try to shoehorn them into every single level too, which I actually found pretty amusing.Disgusting, absurd, absolutely hilarous. And I wouldn't have it any other way.The core movement mechanic is finnicky but can feel great when you do pull it off.

_childDocuments_.review: very underrated game. movement is so fluid I dont actually want to stop moving - the platforming is just so good. level design is also a highlight, as there are many levels that are super creative (inside a whale, slaughterhouse, surgery patient etc). graphics and art style are also great, with lots of graphics customisation options. It runs at mostly solid 40fps medium settings on steam deck. In terms of negatives, it would mainly be that game has some rough edges, especially around the UI, and that its a bit on the short side. Occasional bugs and performance issues tied to number of enemies on screen, but generally stable. The game also doesn't offer that much challenge. Another factor is that it's very very gross/mature. Im personally ok with it, as it allows for some awesome creative level design. But I can see it being too much for some. Definitely recommend. In many ways I prefer Hell Pie to Hat in Time. With more time and money for a sequel, the devs could really create something phenomenal.

_childDocuments_.review: It is very difficult to properly recommend this game because its sense of humor is like Conker's Bad Fur Day cranked up to 500. So if you can deal with overwhelming amounts of raunchy gross-out humor then you should give this a shot.That aside this is one of the most fluid 3D platformers I've ever played. The grappling mechanic opens up so much movement options, especially after it's been upgraded to add additional swings. It's very easy to just swing right over platforming challenges if you're good enough with the grapple, and that's kind of the fun of it. It's designed in a way where it's open-ended enough to allow for that level of experimenting. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - 9.5/10As someone who grew up playing 3D Platformers such as Super Mario 64 and Spyro, this game RESONATED with me on a level no game has hit in a VERY long time... this game has a great sense of humour that doesn't take itself seriously while maintaining an enjoyable story which is funny enough to pay attention to, collecting ingredients for Satan's birthday cake.The themes within this game are some which i enjoy very much in games, the seven deadly sins are a concept which i enjoy very much and this game makes humour with that almost everywhere it can (including a few out of bounds secrets ... looking at you Lust door..) Character Design is also Great and has alot of character, enemy variety is diverse with alot of humorous undertones which i think many will enjoy for varied reasons... Talking about the Movement, Sluggerfly absolutely Nailed the one thing this game pivots on, the swinging system, Using Nugget your Cherub Companion as a Air Anchor to swing is the main focus of aerial movement and there is no clumsiness to this movement AT ALL, Slugger have NAILED every aspect of this traversal system and moving around the levels feels natural and fast paced. The only reason i have deducted .5 points off the 10/10 score from this game is because there was a couple of instances where my game would suffer errors and crash and i'd have to restart (my friend is also playing at the same time as me and he is experiencing this same issue) and also because i have gotten stuck in floors due to hitbox mismatching at times so just minor bugs but other than that this game has been my personal Game of The Year so far. Good Job SluggerFly i hope to see maybe a sequel in the future or even some DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like it was made by christian kids growing up on lolrandom humour and they were trying to make an edgy game. Bad narrative and bad design. They did avoid making the challenge about ridiculous precision and timing, which is a classic pitfall for new developers trying their hands on platformers for the first time. They should give more assistance in grabbing onto the cylinders you can crawl up and down of. I enjoy the fluid movement and the freedom of movement the unlocks grant, but the process of unlocking it didn't feel connected with the platform challenges in the moment. Throughout the narrative we also end up doing good, saving people, getting rid of bad guys, etc. but I guess poopy nazis are too ♥♥♥♥, even for hell.A game full of wasted opportunities and potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy playing Hell Pie, but it's an odd case where I feel the need to first discuss the game's general presentation.The art style is very much not my thing. Nate, Satan, and the snail critters look fine, but generally the creatures inhabiting this world are actively unpleasant to look at. I get the idea that with all the gross-out humor (which struck out a lot more often than it connected for me) it's probably intentional, but I was still wincing at my monitor from start to finish. Not helping matters is that Nugget is one of the ugliest things I've ever seen in my life, and he's on the screen alongside Nate almost 100% of the time. I would actively force him to smash his head into a wall repeatedly purely so I could pretend he could suffer. Do yourself a favor and find a costume that completely replaces his model as soon as you can.It's not helped by the fact Hell Pie's creative staff seemed to be actively thinking of the most revolting things they could throw in the pot. Vomit, gore, feces, drugs, genitalia, anything you can think of is here in spades. There's an enemy class of sentient turds which are being eaten by another race of creatures whose name I forget that usually have dung caked around their mouths and butt cracks. Ingredients (the game's main collectible) are all things like organs, bodily excretions, insects carrying different diseases, each with their own Ren and Stimpy styled high-detail close-up. The fact it's intentional doesn't really stop it from being unpleasant if it's not your bag.Adding to that, there are some technical and design hiccups that make the game seem messier than intended. You can power Nate up with new sets of horns by sacrificing Unilambs (one of the only things that *didn't* make me crave blindness,) but most of those upgrades are either so situational they could easily be context-sensitive prompts, or so base-level they should always be available (looking at you, sprint horns that don't actually move all that fast and horns that highlight main objectives.) The game crashed a few times as I was hunting down collectibles. In the slaughterhouse level, if you hit a human in midair they freeze in place and T-pose, and then any subsequent humans that contact a frozen human will themselves freeze and T-pose. I couldn't tell if the whale in Sashimi Bay saying "[THIS IS A DEBUG MESSAGE]" (or something like it) was a glitch or a joke. Changing to the sprint horns while Nate sinks underwater caused him to continue sinking. The upgrade tree has more than a few options with little use, and I don't mean the intentionally-useless one near the end.The reason I bring all this up at the start is because there was really no escaping it. I do very much enjoy the base gameplay but it does bring things down when I'm constantly looking at an art style I very much dislike.It sucks to say it too, because looking at the actual levels themselves, there are some unique environments in the deck. A restaurant situated inside a whale serving dishes incorporating that same whale's meat. A doctor's office smack in the middle of the jungle. A spire of upscale restaurants with the previously mentioned slaughterhouse built in. There are some cool places to go, they're just populated by some ghoulish creatures.The core gameplay itself (outside the bugs and lackluster horn swapping) feels great. The swinging is smooth and you can get some major height with the boost upgrade. Tracking down collectibles is as satisfying as it always is. For all my umbrage with five of the six horn upgrades the late-game wing horns are fun to use and make exploration even smoother.It's an odd case. You can clearly see I completed my save file and spent upwards of a full day doing so, even getting 10,000 soul shards for a specific, very grind-heavy achievement, but by the same token I'd never have bought it outside of a bundle because of the art direction. I won't say I never laughed, but they were few and far between (though if this kind of humor IS your bag you'll probably love it.) I do recommend it for the gameplay, but by the same token if you just can't stomach the art style or subject matter then yeah it can be safely skipped.

_childDocuments_.review: Way better than you'd expect. Exactly long enough for a fun little platformer and the controls are excellent, movement can be a little frustrating at times but feels great when you master it.The jokes are very crude and over-the-top, going for a "Conker's Bad Fur Day" homage that works surprisingly well, lots of cartoony gore and a generally disgusting vibe really sets this apart from something like "A Hat in Time".All that said, it's an easy game that you can brainlessly waste a couple of days on so get yourself a bottle of whisky or some green and have a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like platformers that much, but even I enjoyed this game. It's entirely based on jumping and timings, but it has just enough combat and story to be engaging and funny without being too over the top or forced.It's not really a metroidvania, even though you can unlock new abilities and expand your current ones to jump farther and higher. There are a few difficult sections, like the boss fights or tighter corridors, but overall the game is well balanced. Exploring and pushing my character to his limits was really fun, the double-triple-quadruple jump abilities add a lot without breaking the game entirely. The controls are excellent and the camera only got stuck in geometry a few times. The gameplay is really well designed, just like the aesthetics. The animations, the creature design and the environments all look really unique and cohesive. Doesn't feel like some asset store game.Now, the game does get a bit repetitive at some point, I feel like the art and puzzle design could have compensated a bit a better in some areas, but the overall level design is near flawless, it's always clear what you have to do and where you have to go. You can even though some unique jumps to skip some areas or to get to locations that seemed inaccessible. That being said, the game got a bit tired after a while, I am roughly half way there, but I don't think I really want to finish it, but I think that's fine.I had fun for a few hours, that's all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really weird.At first I thought everyone who hates this game just has an aversion to Poopy, but it turns out that's not the case.The game is a very good platformer, the moves are good, the level design is decent, and the attention to detail in this game is awesome.But the humor - oh the humor! The humor in this game is todler level humor, there are a few jokes that actually made me smile a bit, but the other 90% of the jokes are just awful, there is no punchline or setup or anything, they just throw ♥♥♥♥ at you and wait for you to laugh.Nothing, NOTHING against toilet humor, but these jokes are too frequent and inserted without context. And it's really weird because I don't understand what audience they were targeting. It's really sad to see the game's potential audience being killed by toilet humor...but i still recommend it because the game itself is really good.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: I received this game for free from the dev/publisher via Keymailer.Hell Pie is just an absolute joy to play but I am getting ahead of myself.Hell Pie caught my eyes first and foremost with its unhinged artstyle, infantile humor (as agiant manbaby, I need this to live) and trailer. My train of thought was: at least I can get a laugh out of it, even if it's poorly made.What I got in the end was something I didn't expect: highly competent collectathon that never outstays its welcome, constantly changes things up and makes them funny/interesting. It's also quite challenging but I am also vertically challenged (not good at platforming) if you ask me. So that is a plus.If I had to criticise one thing, it's the kinda lame boss battles (apart from Gluttony, that one was cool).So yeah, overall, if you are a fan of 3D Platoformers and collectathons, I HIGHLY recommend this one. _childDocuments_.name: Hell Pie

_childDocuments_.review: Not usually the reviewer but I think this game deserves one; I think Hell Pie is at its foremost a really fun platformer. The devs seem to know fully well the freedom and limitations of movement and every level feels very well designed around that. Even when you're zipping around areas, unless you're familiar with it or you've got tons of swinging potential you still have to interact with the area safely, especially ones with unique niches.The game is at it's best however when it's trying things that really push its boundaries! Levels that require you to use certain movement powers, force you to change to a new genre, that have unique gameplay additions that make you interact with things differently. Sadly I find that to be the one thing lacking. Hell Pie isn't a long game if you just go for the finish line, so your time spent relishing in these fun aspects is much shorter, and part of me wishes they just reuse some niches so I could experience them more. But that's not to say this is even a complete negative, this shows the capabilities and I hope to can more of it from the developers!If you want real negatives, I'll say my list is brief. There's some areas that lack polish, there's some bugs, there's some areas that feel a little rushed, and some collectibles were pretty miffing to get. But was the polish really anything that ruined the experience? Not even slightly. Bugs? There have been maybe 2 times in my 20 hours that a bug actually upset me, other than that they've been so negligible that I expect pretty much the same in any big budget game. Rushed areas were a bummer but they're so few and far between. On top of that at worst it only brings a Good game to an Okay game for a moment. As for collectibles... yeah maybe make everything a bit more visible... and maybe something to help understand the hidden candymeats (Seriously I thought I was going crazy till I figured those out).The devs have been wonderful in hearing feedback, so I'd say if I could ask for anything I'd just ask for a time-attack mode or some kinda fast paced collection mode if possible. I'd love to really get the full use of my mobility and tackle older levels with another fun challenge to them. (Also please fix the 100% candymeat achievement, I really wanna rock the perfect achievements with this game :') )With all that said if you enjoy platformers, crude humor, exploration, or just want to experience it's truly amazing mobility controls. Hell Pie's great! I couldn't recommend it more. I hope to see more from this developer and maybe even more of this world if they're interested in it.

It does have some glitches but they aren't game breaking in any way. Some small parts of the game clearly did not get enough development time and it is noticeable but nothing to bad. This is one of the most fun games ive played in a while and one of the only games i think ill ever 100%. Cannot recommend enough.

_childDocuments_.review: So I grew up playing 3D Platformer games. Y'know the classics: Crash Bandicoot, Spyro, Jak and Daxter, Ty the Tasmanian Tiger, Ratchet and Clank, just to name a few as the list is long. I've always loved the colourful charming nature of these games and never get tired of playing them. I love the environment designs, the music, the characters and I especially love that they all have some gimmick that is easy to get to grips with and focuses solely around making gameplay fun. I like playing a variety of genres but 3D Platformers just rest in a special place in my heart. Now with that being said, I can honestly say Hell Pie has satisfied an itch I have long wanted to scratch. Finding 3D Platformers that reward exploration, have imaginative characters/environments, feel smooth and engaging to play whilst consistently providing fun the whole way through? Not as easy as it sounds. In my opinion, the market for quality games in the genre is relatively small so the release of this game immediately caught my eye and I couldn't wait to get stuck in. The movement is the key focus in this game as you use Nugget, your angel companion/prisoner, to swing around from place to place. This pretty much always felt good to use and allowed me to approach platforming segments and exploring every nook and cranny of the map a breeze. It also allowed me to try more daring jumps, saved my ass more times than I can count when I mistimed a jump or attack and actually encouraged me to try to reach places that I probably shouldn't have been able to get to normally. It was the freedom of movement that just made me want to keep going and exhaust the maps because let me tell you the maps are B I G. Usually I'd say big levels could be detrimental to the platforming genre and you can end up feeling like there's just too much space with little substance within it but with Hell Pie I felt like the collectables were really well hidden throughout each area (maybe a little to well hidden in some cases) and they were spread out well enough that the size of the map felt justified. There is a power system too, in the form of Horns you obtain via sacrificing lambs with unicorn horns (no it doesn't feel good to do and I still feel bad). Another part of the power system is the skill tree- albeit short compared to some other games, the skill tree here offers valuable upgrades to your health, movement and combat abilities. These powers allow you to experience the game in even more ways and solve puzzles that you might not have been able to figure out in the earlier stages of the game. Then there are the costumes. The costumes are another thing to collect whilst adding another layer of comedy.Ah yes, the comedy. I'd be amiss to not mention the comedy in this game. It's gross. It's obscene. It is completely juvenile. But that's the point. Think Conker's Bad Fur Day or South Park Stick of Truth, a general dark undertone and you'll get a general idea of what to expect.  Some of it made me cringe and some of it just made me laugh from how silly it all is. In other words if you are at all easily offended don't play it and if you do, don't complain.The music and sound design is great in this game. I was bobbing my head along to a lot of the soundtrack and really loved the detail that went into the noises. I also really like the art style and character designs in this game, it looks great.Now it isn't all great, there are some small things that need to be fixed. There are a few bugs so far in the base build concerning boss levels not progressing, achievements not popping, levels glitching in areas etc. but the good news is the devs are actively responding to the players and assuring us they're addressing any issues that are reported. So even in the bads there's a good. And for the price? I mean come on! It's a steal for how much good outweighs the bad here. I easily got 15 hours out of it (I'd say 10 hours if you collect all of the ingredients and leave it at that, I really went overboard with taking my sweet time exploring absolutely everything).Overall I definitely recommend this game to somebody looking for a 3D Platformer collectathon in the same vein as the PS2 Classics. Also for anyone with a sick sense of humour looking for something new, yeah sure why not give it a go. The devs deserve a lot of praise for making this game come together the way it has and I will always applaud an indie dev team that can produce a high quality game that is crafted with love. I'll be keeping an eye on what they bring out in the future because it'll no doubt be even better than what I've experienced here.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I played this when it was on Steam NextFest and I knew right away it would be good. Yes, the aesthetic is gross, but the design and gameplay is very good. The developers clearly valued giving the player a lot of freedom of movement, which is excellent for a platforming game. _childDocuments_.review: A great little 3D platformer which has some interesting movement mechanics which make traversing the worlds feel very fluid. However that same mechanic (swinging) makes most of the level design pointless as most platforms can be skipped without too much trouble. It's almost as if the whole mechanic was an after thought.Also towards the end it feels like it was either rushed or they lost interest in making the game. As an example the last world has you collect 10 cats where 5 of them are at the exact same spot. But not only that, if you collected everything until the last level there will be no point in collecting anything, as you have pretty much unlocked every upgrade and only the cats have still a minor relevancy. Same for the lambs they were completely useless, just as much as the last horns you get.Another thing is how grindy it becomes if you want 100% including all achievements. You need about 16k gems and the best spot I've found nets you about 250 every 1:45 minutes. Which would add roughly 1 to 1.5 hours of grinding.I personally would make every costume about 100 gems cheaper which would balance the amount of gems you need at the end out and make the swing a little less powerful. Perhaps using the remaining cans to unlock it to be more powerful could be fun.I bought it full price and enjoyed it for the most part, but in retrospect I should've waited for a sale. I still recommend it, however mind that this game isn't without any flaws.In short: The game is fun and the movement feels satisfying, but the end feels rushed & grindy and the level design seems like it was done before implementing the swinging mechanic.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Pie the journey of a diminuitive Imp named Nate and his quest for gag-worthy cuisine, through the bowels of a corporate hell, to the polluted, sadistic earth with its adorable and wretched critters, and finally a heaven that's full of spineless, giant babies and dumb little cherubs who seem to not mind their frequent enslavement.The movement mechanics are freeform but challenging to get the hang of. The level design is also super open to reflect this. Opening up the game as you acquire skills, and seeing pathways and gaps that were previously impossible become reachable is a great feeling.You can see the DNA of a lot of other games in this in the gameplay, and the world is full of direct references to 3D platformers and other media, but its played originally enough to not pull you out of the game.The creature designs are both cute and unsettling, the game worlds are colourful and full of debris, and meticulous details. It's dense, and messy, and the main 3 worlds are a treat to explore.The soundtrack is AMAZING, and as bizarre and eclectic as the rest of the game.Extremely varied and well crafted, with genres from corporate New Wave, Bubbly Pop, Disco, House, French Cabaret, Psy Trance, Industrial, and Metal.Its a little short, I completed it 95% in 13 hours, but a great size for an indie title.The hitbox on the ground attacks are pretty small, so i find myself short-hopping just for the bigger air-attack.Some more ways to use the horns would be nice.A lightning shield while the light horns are active, big punch attacks while the arms are equipped etc.There's a lot of money to pick up, but nothing to spend it on besides costumes.There are guns in several sections of the game, including the final boss, but the mechanic isn't available enough.Hell Pie will definitely put some people off with its extreme comic violence, and grossout humour, but its a point that drew me in personally.If you like 3D Platformers, and can stomach the setting, this is a wonderful gem of a game.A lot of love has gone into this filthfest.Check it out!

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this game for a long while after seeing all the cool movement features they were sharing on Reddit. The movement mechanics are in fact, awesome, but everything else feels a bit unfinished. This is one of those situations where I wish I could give a 'mixed' review.I am not personally a fan of the 'gross out' theming (you'll be swimming through sewers fighting poop monsters and clearing slaughterhouses full of children within the first couple of hours), but since this is, in fact, a 3D platformer, fluid and fun movement options can overcome a lot of that.If you want something rough around the edges with big areas that you can happily jump around in, this is for you. Unfortunately, I don't think I would personally recommend it to anybody because of the theming, short length and rougher elements (one boss fight in particular so far feels like it's still alpha level). For this reason, I am hesitantly making this review negative, but I can totally see a niche of people that would love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Pie is a fun, comical game in an obscene world where you play as Nate, the Demon of Bad Taste along with Nugget, his living grappling hook. The game is filled with hilarious dialogue from various characters, massive levels with incredible detail, and fun platforming with many collectibles to find. Anybody who likes platformers and crude humor will especially appreciate this absolute gem. I have encountered probably one or two bugs, but it was certainly nothing game-breaking.One critique I would give to the game is, it can be pretty frustrating to search big levels to find the last one or two collectibles. It would be neat to see this addressed. For example, one idea might be to introduce some sort of hints system for collectible items that you haven't found. Maybe you could pay for hints like you do costumes... just an idea.Sitting at $25, this game is well worth it at full price and I would recommend it to anybody who is interested in a comical and fun adventure-lite platforming game.
