_childDocuments_.review: I tried 3 or 4 times to come back to this game and enjoy it, but unfortunately each time I ended up putting the game down dissapointed. Im going to break this up into the good, the bad, and the ugly at the bottom.This game advertises itself as a dark humor version of games such as banjo kazooie or a hat and time, however the "humor" in this game (or lack of) is atrocious and just ends up being "gross equals funny, amirite guys??" and doesnt make up for the absolute lack of personality and soul this game suffers from,The Good:this games base gameplay mechanic, swinging from an air hook, your personal enslaved cherub, works well and is fun to use.The Bad:the levels, the enemies, and npc's are incredibly bland and uninspired, and for the most part are just boring or uninteresting to interact with or fight. i made it to the third level (out of a total of 4) and didnt desire to see the rest through. the game for the most part is just flat out boring.A lot of the jokes in this game are also just not funny at all or rely entirely on gross out tactics. you can tell they were supposed to be a joke, but they clearly werent written by someone with a sense of humor. for instance, theres a reoccuring npc who is clearly a body builder. he has an enormous upper body, a shirt that says "never skip leg day," is vaguely "handsome ugly" like handsome squidward, and comes complete with a He-Man haircut. However he has an incredibly tiny lower body and skinny legs and is always seen doing a ballancing one leg squat, implying he only works legs. sure theres a joke there, but its just not a good one.theres also a reoccuring joke where most npc's end up getting killed. again, its supposed to be funny, but it never really is.another bad trait of this game is that your primary attack is rather slow and if you dont time it correctly in some fights, it will end up with you getting hit and you only start the game off with 3 hearts. this can lead to a frustrating experience. especially when some of the boss fights can be frustrating due to this game not having the tightest hitboxes. you will take damage from attacks that arent supposed to be aoe, just by being near them.The Ugly:This games entire schtick is that its obscene and uses mature themes in a genre typically lighthearted and cute. while this is definitely true, its executed terribly. most of the mature themes revolve around gross out humor such as vomit, scat, and food related body horror. its all the incredibly juvenile type of stuff that some edgy sixth grader would probably be proud to be able to tell his friends at the school yard.one of the first gross things you come across is the "♥♥♥♥ (scat) Shtaffel." Sentient Nazi themed logs of poop. and their "holocaust victims" are a race of dung eaters who have poop smeared all over their faces, hands, and rear ends. these enemies are one of the only enemies to reappear throughout the game. there is a frequent reoccurance of poop and toilets all throughout the game to the point that it feels like someone on the dev team must have a scat fetish, theres really no other explanation for it.the devs apparently equated dark with gross because not only is there just an excessive amount of themes revolving around skat, theres constant references to vomit, overeating, rotten food, "used products" etc.it feels at times that this was made by foreigners who thought this is the type of things americans would find funny so they stuffed the entire game full of it.tldr: too much reliance on grossout humor, too much references to somebody's gross fetish, and too much non existant humor, instead of making a game that was actually interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: FINAL SCORE: 3.5/5I recently dived into the chaotic world of Hell Pie, an obscene 3D platformer that proudly takes bad taste to the next level. As the self-proclaimed 'Demon of Bad Taste,' I embarked on a quest to gather the disgustingly unique ingredients for Satan's infamous birthday pie. Here's a breakdown of my experience:Graphics and Art Style:The visual appeal of Hell Pie is undeniable. The graphics and art style are a feast for the eyes, especially with RTX turned on. The lighting adds an immersive touch, creating a devilishly charming atmosphere. However, I did notice that the game is strangely demanding at times.Performance Issues:While the game offers a visual treat, performance issues rear their ugly head. Lag stuttering, particularly during asset loading or shader compilation, is a recurring hiccup. The interruptions last only a few seconds, but it's enough to disrupt the flow. A minor annoyance that requires a pause and patience.Audio Experience:The music, reminiscent of PS2-era 3D platformers, adds a nostalgic layer to the experience. The absence of voice acting is compensated by well-crafted sound effects. It all contributes to the quirky vibe of the game.Level Design:The levels, though linear, make up for it in depth. Numerous little areas offer collectibles, providing an incentive to explore beyond the intended path. Collecting is enjoyable, with most items visible from the main route, sparing players the need to scour every nook and cranny.Character Designs and Content:The character designs are cool and unique, but be warned—Hell Pie doesn't shy away from surprising elements. Unexpected nudity and a generous dose of blood and gore might catch you off guard. While unexpected, I found these elements fitting and well-executed within the game's context.Gameplay:The gameplay is a mixed bag. It's undeniably fun and engaging, but flaws abound. Movement quirks, frustrating climbing sequences, and finicky enemy encounters, especially with the robot eye shooting orbs, are noticeable downsides. Boss battles, however, shine as a highlight. The camera, unfortunately, is the Achilles' heel, requiring constant attention and creating a somewhat frustrating experience.Overall Impression:Hell Pie manages to be both gross and good. I enjoyed the game, despite its flaws. The engaging gameplay, unique design, and standout boss battles overshadow the frustrations. However, it's crucial to note the presence of game-breaking bugs. From progression blockers to getting stuck in walls or falling beneath the map, these issues are a real drawback. Fortunately, most problems can be resolved by a quick exit to the main menu.In conclusion, Hell Pie is an enjoyable romp into the obscene. I'd recommend it to others, but with a cautionary note about the existing bugs. If you can tolerate occasional disruptions and appreciate the bizarre, you're in for a devilishly good time. Grab those horns and embrace the chaos!

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Pie is to A Hat in Time as A Hat in Time is to Super Mario Galaxy.Which is to say, this is okay, but if you like the genre and haven't played A Hat In Time, I'd recommend playing that instead. Or Bang On Balls Chronicles. And if you *have* played both of those, and really want more of the same and are willing to put up with it not being as good, only then you should play Hell Pie.Highlights of things I didn't enjoy about it:* The jumping is relatively clunky, it's hard to tell how far you're going to go* it's often hard to tell whether you're going past or falling short of a platform (something wrong with camera angles or shadows, I guess)* very large areas with often no indication of where you should be going, so there's a lot of uninteresting exploring* collectible gems everywhere, that are pretty much meaningless and respawn so there is no "completion" of them, or sense of progress about them

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of the worst platformers I have ever played, which is really unfortunate considering how much I like everything about it that isn't platforming. People have been comparing this to Conkers bad Fur Day and Spyro, but honesly the gameplay and levels reminds me much more of Psychonauts than anything. The controls for this game are extremely slippery and there are parts of this game where you cannot even see your shadow. In other words, depth perception doesnt exist in this game either. It's like they took all the basic fundamentals of what makes a good platformer and said "we don't need that."The final straw for me was meandering my way through a level about 3/4 way through the game only to find out I don't have a specific upgrade needed to finish a level. Levels don't have shortcuts and are pretty long and tedious in general - so in order to get that upgrade, I would need to go back through the leave the level by going through it backwards, go to an entirely different hubworld (there are 4) find that upgrade (ram horns) and then make my way all the way back to the third hubworld, find my way back to the level entrance, and then do the entire level over again just to beat it. I already wasn't enjoying this game but this was it for me. This progression style is extremely odd and doesn't exist in other platformers to my knowledge. The idea they would even allow you to get into the level at all without that upgrade is incredibly baffling.Regarding depth perception, levels such as the  have platforms where your shadow doesn't even show up. For those who have never played a platformer before, typically to know where you're going to land developers will place something like a shadow below you so you can perceive your depth relative to the ground. This game already has a really weak and barely noticeable shadow, but on certain levels its not there at all. Usually, what makes a good and well received platformer is tight and responsive controls. When controlling mario, for instance, he will move quickly relative to your inputs, and will stop moving quickly when you stop inputting anything. Unfortunately your character in this game will be slip-and-sliding all over the f*cking place. This coupled with the fact you cant see precisely where you're going to land on most of the dark levels (everything but the beach levels) you're going to be dying a lot. Additionally, theres been a bug in this game since launch that prevents you from actually collecting all the items. And of course, me already not loving this game, I encountered it. I thought "well i might as well get my moneys worth by 100%'ing the damn thing" only to find out I cant! how lovely is that. A collecta-thon with a prominent bug preventing you from collecting. (the bug has to do with the radioactive monster in the first major hub world)I can't believe this game has this many positive reviews. Terrible game honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: Double Jump? You bet your sweet ass it does.Hell Pie is a 3D platformer/collecathon-type that also so much freedom its kind of not a challenge really. The main mechanic of this game is you have this lovely little Cherub chained to you. If you hold R, you just swing mid air, and you can get a max of 4, with 1 recharge mid air. This can give you a lot of air time and you don't really have to do a lot of levels. It's satisfying to "break" the levels this way anyways so I don't hate on it for that.The main negative I have for this game is that its goes really ham on gross out humour. I don't really think its a negative, but I think it could be a hard sell on some people with how many nasty poop filled butt cracks you see in this game. The one thing that I really don't wanna see is that you need these cute little unicorn bunny things to sacrifice to altars to get more horns (they are different powers on a quick bar). You have to mash A to pull of its horn, then it shows you doing that for however more you need for that particular altar. _childDocuments_.review: Just watched the Barbie movie and need to wash yourself clean of that pink, glittery nonsense? Hell Pie is the perfect antidote. It's filled to the brim with filthy characters and crude humour, but most importantly, it's a wickedly good platformer. Basic movement is fun and features an awesome upgradable grapple jump (can be extended up to 3 jumps) which is like an unrestricted version of A Hat in Time's hookshot badge. The level design is semi-open worldish and Sluggerly cleverly includes teleporters that cut backtracking in half, unlike Yooka-Laylee which forces you to manually traverse everywhere (massive chore). This is also a true collectathon-you'll never get bored of exploring environments hunting down lucky cats, candymeat and unilambs, although it will feel grindy towards the end. Unilambs and candymeat are the more rewarding collectibles; the former unlocks bonus challenge levels within levels which are more or less on par with the difficulty of the main campaign, save for the light gate near Club Luxuria (Jungle), which was a notably frustrating spike. The latter acts as currency for unlocking new moves, so there's a constant incentive to keep collecting which is evidence the devs took great care to ensure the progression felt worthwhile. There are some minor bugs to be wary of; nothing that will tarnish your enjoyment, but during my playthrough, the levers in Flavor Peaks' restaurant puzzle didn't work, and this could only be rectified by restarting the game. Another problem I encountered was in Joyfruit fields. After completing the incredible 80s dance themed, lizard-blasting hallucinatory 3rd person shootout, the necessary cutscene failed to trigger, forcing a replay of the entire segment and making sure to enter the mansion while blasting the lizards rather than waiting for them to run to the door. Hell Pie's art style feels most reminiscent of Psychonauts or SpongeBob games, and anybody who loved Conker's Bad Fur Day and the bizarre characters in that will feel right at home with the innuendos and obscenities. If you're offended by sacrilegious imagery steer clear, though I'll say the treatment of God is ultimately respectful (and hilarious) despite being cheeky. This is the first game in a while that I didn't want to put down because I was having so much fun. Nice job Sluggerfly! \m/

_childDocuments_.review: Fatal error on exit, that's quite a feat.This game requires V-sync, but the V-sync feels like playing at 20 fps while the fps counter is steadily at 60.It's got RTX support, doesn't change anything though. Probably why enabling RTX on a 3050 doesn't lower the framerate.Why it runs very smoothly, 120+fps. Sometimes, some places create massive performance drop, no idea why. Except for thouse canons in the whale bar whose projectiles explode into shrapnels. Their physics are really hard on the PC. But the lifetime of the shrapnels seems too long anyway and they don't serve any purpose other than FX.Gameplaywise, the movemet is very good. I love that about this game. Checkpoints are very frequent, a bit too frequent until you get to a place especially hard and long to go through and there will be no checkpoint until you made it through.Also if you exit the level, you can't teleport back to those checkpoints when rejoining. A shame, because some bugs sometimes require you to restart the level, going back to the checkpoint doesn't reset the event that you missed. At the end of the whale bar, there's a platform with a limited lifetime for some reason, waste your time or go AFK, and you will have to restart the whole level.IDK if it's by design, and I doubt it. But on death, you don't lose the purple thingies you collect, and when you resurect, they come back so you can just collect them, die, and repeat.The eyes of NPCs track the players, even if the player happens to walk behind them. It's... an interesting feature. That and also, they're barely hidden by eyelids so it looks like 2 white spheres affixed to the face of the model, it's very weird.I feel like some NPC models could use more detail too.Finally, it's only a matter of personal taste, but the humor I expected was dark humor (as advertized), and I mostly just got gross humor with farts and poop. I did like the nazi turds tho. And the only joke I enjoyed so far was pushing that little guy off a building.Also, I don't understand why the overworld is populated by some kind of weird snail people instead of humans.

I find myself playing in bird's eye view and fighting the auto-cam reset most the time because of it.Attack hit-boxes feel way off on some enemies and their attacks. I try to time them for when Nugget should hit them, but it seems to just not connect sometimes. Some projectiles seem to cause damage at a further collision range than others. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for January 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before February 6th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Hell no.Hell Pie has you play the Demon of Bad Taste, and Satan calls you randomly and tells you to go tell the chef, he wants his pie.  That act somehow has you roped into helping get the ingredients for the pie, which also involves you picking up a cherub and platforming through various levels.  The game tries to be humorous while giving players large levels to explore and search out various items that act as the goal for the player. But this humor is so bad, you’ve already seen a demon’s butt, but that’s hardly the worst.  There are so many cringe-worthy and depressing jokes.  This game isn’t funny if you’re older than a teenager and probably not even that funny for them either.  Yet it is the type of humor constantly on display.  The levels too aren’t that exciting and even when they are, it’s just crass humor at best. Pick this up if you want a weaker version of A Hat in Time or Conker’s Bad Fur Day, but let me also say I’ve heard this game compared to both of those, and honestly, I’m offended, this is so much weaker it shouldn't be in the same sentence as those titles.  The gameplay isn’t awful, but the writing and level design make this hard to accept.  All I could think is how Demon Turf has a similar theme with a focus on Hell, but better gameplay and writing. _childDocuments_.review: Overall I had a pretty boring experience and I already anticipated it during the first 10 minutes within the game. I could've refunded it, but I'm stupid and play through every game I begin.Up from the beginning your moveset is pretty strong and only becomes more versatile over the course of the game when you upgrade the skill tree.I see a lot of praise for the game because of its movement mechanics. It controls smooth and you have full aerial control, sounds pretty cool at first glance but it isn't when the game wants to teach you it's main mechanic in the tutorial while you're not even required to use it to move on.So our protagonist Nate is able to swing around the environment, by using his angel sidekick Nugget. There is a certain momentum applied to it which makes up for a high potential of vertical movement. Combined with all the toolsets the game offers you it doesn't matter if an obstacle is vertical or horizontal, you just can bypass any of it without having to put in any critical thoughts.Just to sum it up you have:- a second jump- a dash (can be combined in any order with the jumo)- wall climbing for a certain amount of time (upgradable)- the signature swinging move (which can be triggered at any point in the air)This is the basic moveset, but quickly you find yourself with even more utility by scavenging the games collectibles.At first you can only use your swing move on time until you hit the ground, pretty quickly it can be upgraded to be usable from 2 to 4 times until you hit the ground. But it doesn't end with it, your usage of swing moves can replenish itself while staying a certain amount of time in the air, providing you with even more swings.additionally, you can unlock: - a spin attack that also can be combined with everything else, - a sprint trinket to speed up your horizontal momentum- speeding up your swing movement for further horizontal momentum- ability to swing yourself up in the air by a 90° degree (uses up swing count)- a glide trinket (admittetly pretty late and can't be combined with the speed trinket, so it's doesn't really matter at this point anymore tbh)It's a pure overkill, hardly you will need to combine all of these feats, even with basic movement you can bypass most of the games obstacles.You might be prone to tell me "then just don't upgrade the character", but there are certain single collectibles you can only obtain by upgrading the character, but even if not I don't think it would speak for the game, when you have to ignore the rewarding factor of most of the games collectibles, having to blind out certain sections of a game to maximize their fun, might be a self-serving compromise, but it can be never an excuse for the lack of game-design fidelity, especially because it's not possible to turn off the upgrades once unlocked.So with all this in mind the whole term "level design" practially begins to vanish, there was put a lot of effort in the games environment and it's gauntlets, but what point is there to it, when I never have to play by the rules?Don't misunderstand me, i'm not hostile to sequence breaking, some of the best games allow you for some pretty clever shortcuts like Super Mario 64, but these shortcuts are taken by utilizing the reasonable restrictions of the movement to its fullest degree or exploiting unintended glitches.In Hell Pie on the other hand, swinging above an obstacle course is a "no-brainer" it doesn't require any skill or careful observation, it's basically the most common sense thing you would do when you practicially possess the ability to cross over tremendous weights and heights.But even if you play by the rules, you're never really in danger, cause at every point you could always correct a slip of an edge. A double jump and dash alone suffice to take out large parts of the precision aspect I would've actually expected from an plattformer.Adding to the factor that the game is littered with checkpoints that keep you confidentI mean at this point it's probably for the better cause every throwback would feel like a waste of time anyway, because "challenge" is at no point to be found in this game and so your expectations and main drive ist just progress, the dopamine hit of finding the next collectible until you're done. There is currency in this game you lose on dying, but it's only there to buy cosmetics (which there are a lot of) and the amount is so little, that you already weight out the amount by just collecting the respawned curreny collectibles until you hit the point you died on.There are a few segments where your ability to swing is disabled, these are short glimpses of what could be possible, but it also makes you realize that even without the swings, your basic plattforming movement is already more powerful than in basically every retro collect-a-thon, it's still far from enganging plattforming design.I mean it's ok when you dismiss plattforming and rather focus on exploration, games like Banjo Kazooie are also rather small on plattforming but instead they're encountering you with "problems" be it a minigame, a paperchase, a puzzle, something cryptic where you find the solution by experimenting, cleverbacktracking, stressing your navigational skills, bossfights etc...But Hell Pie doesn't offer any of it. In the second half it almost feels like you're playing minecraft in creative mode and float around the sky searching for macguffins. Even worse if you don't care for 100% which means you could mindlessly skip across almost everything.At it's worst point I would even dare to claim that Hell Pie didn't felt like a videogame but rather as a hunt for eastereggs.That's basically the quintessence of my critique. There is another point to the edgy, cringy humor that doesn't touched me the slightest, neither in a good nor a bad way. ("bad" meant in a offended way) I think a lot of the gags were stale and just overdone for the sake of infantile profanity. It's Ren and Stimpy without the pointe. - "Hahaha nazi poo with guns and high pitched german accent, never seen that coming LMAO XDXDXXDiksdeh"- "LOL there are phallus shaped male genital mushrooms in the jungle OMG they've REALLY DONE THAT!?!? :O:O:O"- "Oh my, these poor innocent children who are processed to meat in a slaughterhouse it breaches all boundaries!!"There was nothing subtle or clever about it, nothing thought-provoking, nothing that resembles the british humor of Rareware. Also there was no coherence, no overarching plot that would somehow glue this mess together, there is basically no narrative besided "just collect these ingredients for the pie" it's a sightseeing of crude situations born from infantile minds who checked all the boxes that obviously are supposed to detonate the boundaries of good taste.So we end up with a pointless narrative and a level-design that doesn't matter, so what remains? Just tons of easy to achieve collectibles that tickle your dopamine addicted minds and a plethora of "cute" outfits... Probably it does its work as an casual game, but if you have some aspirtations or are an veteran to the genre I advise to avoid Hell Pie.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm downright sad that it's getting so little attention, because it bodes ill for the genre, kangaroo kao which is a 2/10 chestnut got so much attention and here nothing?A hell of a game, it has phenomenal movment, it's been a long time since I've played such a pleasantly dynamic jumping game - all credit here to the fawn on the harness which is a kind of static grappling hook, reminding me of the chain from I-ninja. Only unlike the competition, here we put it up ourselves so we have full freedom in overcoming levels. The developers even left us several ways to beat each map without unnecessarily blocking shortcuts.In total we have four large thematically unique HUBs where we can freely move around and explore for finds, in each of them we get three story levels to beat - many times I was surprised how extensive these stages can be, in this respect the game positively surprises! Each has its own unique mechanics and visual variations - cockroaches running a concentration camp, or walking feces dressed in hugo boss uniforms with red banners. The humor may seem toilet-like and unsavory (lol because that's what it is) - However, it's not intrusive it mainly serves as a background that doesn't attack us with stiff ruses and relies on visuals. Including the fetus, which has no narrative impact during the game. It only casts simple sympathetic reactions to what we encounter during exploration.Finds are pleasant to collect, without overdoing the hiding, rewarding exploration and willingness to play rather than tryhardening with tutorials. We have two types of upgrades - the Devil which gives us new mechanics to overcome previously inaccessible places, and for the fawn which affect stats on how many lives, how many extra jumps or attacks. Next are golden cats which only serve us to unlock rooms with easter eggs, which is the best reward in this type of game. The whole game can be completed in 7/8h doing only the story quests, plus two hours to collect all the bonuses - so for me Hell Pie is two leagues above the highly rated yet boring Psychonauts 2 and is a must have in its genre providing a AAA product at an indie price. You can see the passion and creativity of the developers in the game, which gives a product that doesn't get boring at any point, but on the contrary - surprises until the very end. You can feel the vibe of old platformers like Rayman or I-ninja and that's great.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is gory, rauncy, and immature, with frequent use of gross out humor, includng but not limited to poop and vomit.  None of these things are dealbreakers for me. but they're worth pointing out for people that might turn away from this game.This game is fantastic. The music is good, the characters are funny, and the level design is fantastic. There's interesting locations to explore, from a sushi bar inside of a beached whale, to a slaughterhouse mass producing human meat, to a fun dance club, to literal heaven, to....the sewers. This game does feature gore and gross things, as mentioned, but when it's not focusing on that, the visuals and level designs are actually pretty good to look at.There's collectibles, and everything you can collect serves a prupose, though some purposes are more useful than others. Candy meat and unilambs are probably tied for most valuable collecitble, though unilambs are fewer and further between so they probably take the crown. Unilambs let you unlock new horns, granting you new abilities, including sprinting, ramming into destructible objects, and riding demonic rails. Candy meat are your skill points, allowing you to unlock other abilities, mainly for Nugget, like gaining addiitonal midair swings, and, of course, the most crucial ability, letting Nugget fart on cammand. Lucky cats really aren't needed for progression, though they do let you explore Greed's rooms at Sin inc, so they're still worth it for the curious. Crystals are the most numerous collectible, and they're mainly only used to unlock outfits for Nate and Nugget, though they can also be used to simulate the American healthcare system in one particular stage.Collectibles feel rewarding to collect, especially the candy meat, because with a fully maxed out skill tree, you can get a full 5 swings out of Nugget without touching the ground, plus some additional lift from your air attack, allowing you to fully skip entire section of platforming if you so choose. There's also more collectibles than are needed to unlock all abilities, so players don't feel overly punished for not searching absolutely every nook and cranny, and full completion can be left to the true completionists. The game's strongest point is for sure its platforming. Navigating levels with a portable midair grappling hook is way more fun than it has any right to be, and searching somewhere up high or out of the way and finding a secret is always a good feeling. Combat exists, but most enemies die in one hit. Still, the platforming more than makes up for it, and there ARE  few sections where you get to use guns to mow down hordes of enemies, so that's neat. Overall, definitely recommended, as long as you don't mind gore and some gross-out humor.

_childDocuments_.review: I THOROUGHLY recommend Hell Pie because, where it matters most - the mobility gameplay and collect-a-thon adventuring - the game is EXCELLENT.The theme is clearly a bit Marmitey though. It was silly fun that made me giggle plenty of times and was definitely a series of interesting and unique environments to platform around in.If you don't like the sound of that, but DO like very well built platforming and collect-a-thon gameplay then I think you can still enjoy this game, I suppose it depends just how much you are turned off by the idea of the humour/theme.The platforming and abilities you obtain and level up as you find collectibles are honestly some of the best feeling ones I've ever played, absolutely rivaling the juggernauts from the 3D platforming era like Spyro, Banjo and even Mario Sunshine and Odyssey, so again I wholeheartedly recommend it for its platforming experience alone.Honestly I'd give this like a 9 or 9.5/10, it was really, really fun! _childDocuments_.review: very unfortunate it flew under my radar for quite a while. it's better than yooka-laylee, but still has issues, some shared.good:it's an ugly-cute platformer mixed with item collection and crude humor, fun worlds and interesting abilities.it doesn't take itself too seriously and when it decides to do a boss fight or other bigger event it feels satisfying to beat. the movement is quite fun to execute and being able to get everywhere with enough dedication can be fun, but more to that later. you don't have to backtrack too much because puzzles and platforming can usually be solved with the kit you have or acquire when in the levelbad:the bounce talent is made pretty useless being double bound with dash meaning you will have to dash first if you want to use it. the freedom of movement that nugget gives you from a certain point is a shared issue with yooka-laylee. you will not have to plan too much around platforming since once you mastered the movement abilities you can just swing and fly and everything to get almost everywhere. the levels are not quite designed around the freedom, but rather the levels came first and the skills got slapped on top. the levels are a bit tedious to 100% since apart from the first level it doesn't really have areas that make you go "i bet there's something hidden there". past the first level it gets more and more the norm with how things feel randomly placed rather than having levels designed around making you explore. the grind horns are just useless and could've been scrapped.overall it's got the right ideas, but the wrong execution. it's a good timewaster to fire up when you don't have anything better to do and I only spent a few cents on it. it knows where it's coming from with references to banjo-kazooie, yooka-laylee and conker's bad furday, but it fails to do the right thing with those influencespersonal level ranking:

_childDocuments_.review: Navigating the infernal realms of gaming, one often stumbles upon games that are mere imitations of classics. However, every once in a while, a devilishly delightful title like "Hell Pie" emerges to remind us that originality still has a throne in the gaming underworld."Hell Pie" takes the playful spirit and exploration of "Mario 64," throws in the cheeky shenanigans akin to "Conker's Bad Fur Day," and mixes it with the absurdity reminiscent of "Donkey Kong Country 2." These influences are baked together to create a platforming experience that is undeniably quirky and refreshingly engaging.For streamers looking for content that is slightly twisted yet incredibly entertaining, "Hell Pie" offers exactly that—with a cherry on top. The game is designed with two levels of streamer safety, ensuring you can share your gameplay experience to your audience without fearing the omnipresent banhammer.Platformer enthusiasts will appreciate the nod to genre classics, expressed through visually stimulating environments that spark memories of "Ren and Stimpy," speaking to the child in all of us who revels in a bit of animated mischief.The player's path through this wickedly joyous title is paved with forgiveness. The abundance of checkpoints stands testament to the game's dedication to fun over frustration, allowing players to indulge in its humor and devil-may-care attitude without being overly penalized for their missteps.In essence, "Hell Pie" offers a tempting slice of platforming pandemonium that's enriched with humor for those who dare to laugh at the darker side of gaming. It is a sinful treat for content creators and players alike, looking to feast on a game that celebrates the hilarity of high jinks and the thrill of jumping puzzles.Prepare to indulge in an adventure where every checkpoint is a chuckle, and every level a testament to twisted fun. "Hell Pie" is a recommended must-play, especially for those who fancy a walk on the gaming world's wild side. So grab your fork, and dive into this devilishly delicious adventure for a hell of a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great platformer - immediately the feel of the character felt smooth and easy to control. Nate himself is adorable and the use of Nugget the angel as a midair grapple is such a great mechanic. The level design and aesthetic was great and i loved the large and open worlds we seem to see less of nowadays. The humour was really crude and to me sometimes it was overdone, especially in one of the last worlds (if you play you'll know) but it didn't distract enough from the gameplay to stop me from having fun :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hell Pie

_childDocuments_.review: Getting the annoying thing out the way first. The humor of this title is very..."ehhh" as  pointed out by multiple other reviews. The gore is unnecessary at times and the toilet humor gets old extremely fast. If you can ignore that than proceed.It's a really good 3d platformer.  A sort of Super Mario Odyssey meets A Hat in Time meets Conker's Bad Fur Day.  The downside is, it doesn't outshine any of these titles in their strong areas at all. The controls are good, just be aware that bonking into a wall in mid air will probably lead to some weird missed inputs occasionally as you're unsure if Nate will try to climb the wall or bounce off. Visually the game is bright and colorful even in it's darkest moments. Combat is consistent, though (personal gripe) I wish the enemies provided some type of obstacle, but that seems to be more common in modern 3d platformers.My only gameplay complaint is your Cherub doesn't shut up sometimes, and though the devs added some transparency to his chat box it will occasionally obscure what an enemy is doing or what you're trying to see behind it. Overall, if you enjoyed A Hat in Time recently, you'll likely enjoy the gameplay of Hell Pie as well. The visuals of cartoonish gore and toilet humor will be the only deterring factor.
_childDocuments_.name: Hell Pie

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so much fun. It takes basic platformer formula and transforms it into an adult friendly, lewd, satiric comedy game. It has also wonderful gameplay, the game feels like old classics like Spyro or Crash Bandicoot. The game has a lot of easter eggs and jokes that made me giggle few times and even more times laugh out loud as crazy. Pros and Cons:+ Artstyle and overall theme+ Music+ Gameplay+ Everything you collect has it's use+ Humor, although certainly not for everyone+ Story was pretty crazy and the ending was ridiculous+ Difficulty was just right- Few bugs like crystals stuck in the floor (but I ran to a bug only two times)- It certainly can make some people mad by it's natureI had a pretty good time with this game and it took a place among my most favorite platformers. I give Hell Pie 9/10 in the manner of platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Hell Pie

_childDocuments_.review: Hell pie has very quickly found a place in my heart. Whilst it can be sometimes overwhelming in how gross it gets, as a lover of 3D platfomer collect-a-thons I can say this one is good. *really* good. The controls are pretty tight, and the cherub-swing mechanic allowing you to define your own swing point midair is unique and really gives the freedom of movement I seek in games like this.The world design is great. There are nominally 4 hub worlds, each with 3 levels connected to them. Each hub world has its own theme, from the main office building to a sandy island, a nightmare restaurant to a jungle, the locations are lush, filled with characters, things to find, and things to be seen. Exploring feels rewarded, but you never feel lost. The story plot (as far as I am so far), is just enough there to give you a reason to go exploring. It isn't a work of deep storytelling, you are finding things to go in a pie. There are however stories told by the worlds, from trapped whales to horrific meat factories. Yeah, don't play this game if your squeemish.Overall, a solid 9/10, after I complete it I will go on my replay pile.

At first controls felt a little floaty, but once you really figure out how to maneuver, it's so damn fantastic. Felt like Spider-Man swinging around! Levels were interesting, if a bit small. Lots of variety though. 100%ing the game was satisfying, but I'm sad because I forgot I was in offline mode (Deck) and a few achievements didn't pop. :( OH well. _childDocuments_.review: Fun yet disgusting game. This is a 3D platformer/collect-a-thon. The levels are mostly linear with hidden collectibles and side quests, and the hub world is large enough to make exploration feel satisfying, but not too large so that it feels like they're slogs to navigate. The swinging mechanic is one of the best features of the game. It brings a ton of skill expression while also feeling cool as hell. The levels are mostly designed without swinging in mind, making skipping around levels with it to be super fun. Collectibles are overall enjoyable to find and collect, many of them requiring you to use every skill you've picked up while playing. I'd say this is a solid 7/10 game, but beware of the disgusting nature of it. If crude humor, poop, sex jokes, and the like are too much for you, then you should skip it. _childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't recommend this but it isn't bad, I would much rather just give it a meh but here we are. Game starts pretty strong though the humour is crude/gory/gross out but because its the entire game it isn't actually funny at all. There are a lot of minor issues which really drag down the enjoyment, wall run sucks, vertical boost fails randomly if you change the number of inputs (ie if I was holding forward for one then tried another but stopped holding forward it would use the charge but do nothing frequently killing me), double jump gets eaten randomly some times. The boss fight mid game forces a terrible camera angle without drop shadows leading to having no clue where you are. Crashed 7 times, had to reset levels multiple times because of progression items clipping out of the world, etc etc There are three types of collectables, candy meat which is used for upgrades though there are 30 extra and several of the powers are useless so its closer to 60. Golden cats which open rooms that are completely pointless, only containing a couple of costumes and a basic swinging challenge at the very end. The last type is lambs needed to get the powerups, also a bunch extra.The powerups are garbage, one is sprint, one is a ram which is needed to break rocks in places for collectables but is otherwise basically pointless, one is light which unlocks a handful of challenge rooms which do have the best platforming in the game, one is arms that lets you use a couple of zipline esc things but they are largely just used to backtrack pointlessly (there are teleports which are quicker so once again essentially pointless), and the last one is wings which are only needed in the level you get them in for a couple collectables that you probably won't need. Overall boring and unnecessary.Later levels are really uninteresting, where you only really do anything if you want to search for the collectables for the achievements.Speaking of Achievements the last couple require farming to get enough crystals to  buy the rest of the costumes and a 10k shortcut to skip a level.The ending is also literally "haha you were stupid to have done all that" cuts to credits after a boring boss fight. tldr; it had potential but an extremely poor ending half, boring powerups and collectables, a bunch of bugs, glitches, and crashes made it an overall mediocre experience.

The lack of effort of even rationalizing these things pulls me out. I just need a little squirt of effort of acknowledgement with comedic effect. Base price sets expectations so you expect Psychonauts 2 to be better but Psychonauts 2 was cheaper than this game during the Winter sale. This game falls flat in comparison in every way. _childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed my time on Hell Pie. The game understands really well the notion of flow, especially in a platformer context, and never breaks out from it. During the whole experience, you'll be using the mechanics you unlocked throughout the game, jumping and grappling your way through the diverse environments the game has to offer. It's been a while I haven't touched controls with that level of polish and, especially coming from an indie studio, it's always appreciated.Hell Pie markets itself a bit as the next edgy kid in town, and to be fair, it does not do so well in that regard. The written humor usually didn't land so much for me, and if you don't feel like seeing (cartoony) gross stuff regularly, don't play this game. However, one caveat with this edgy and no-filter approach is that the game allows itself to push the boundaries of what can make a level, and thus provides really refreshing and well-designed environments. I bet you haven't yet played a game where you visit a sushi shop taking its meat from the whale in which it is located, a giant doctor's office in the jungle where you have to beat up patients to get their tickets to go in faster, or a giant vertical restaurant in which at the tops are food pipes from which the food is deversed onto customers. What the game lacks in good and funny writing it definitely has in creative and colorful environments, which were all an enjoyment to explore and discover up to the very end. The level of details and care given to the levels is amazing, and it was only way late that I realized I was playing a game from a small indie studio, and not one of the bigger names out there.The movement is fluid, the levels are creative and diverse. The skills get a bit broken later in the game, but only thus allow you to be more creative with how you go through the level instead of trivialising it. If you want a platformer with a fresh movement, and either like or don't mind raunchy humor here and there, I can only vouch for Hell Pie, it really is an underdog and I wish its devs get the chance to double up on such experiences later!

There's tons of little details in each level that you can find on and off the beaten path that I very much enjoyed (for example, a cute little reference to a Studio Ghibli film hidden away on level 2).Would highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: don't take my rating (or any of my high ratings in any medium lol) as a universal recommendation, but its the only appropriate one and my heart knows it. one of the fun things ab liking both retro games and indie games is that we're at the point where just ab every Cool Thing Ur Attached To From The Past is getting some kind of artistic successor, and i dont think i realized just how long i was waiting for someone to do conker's bad fur day already. conker is such formative deeply impactful media for me, and part of why its retained that mystique is that it Shouldn't Have Been formative deeply impactful media...i honestly dont think this would have had the same impact on me had i been able to play it as a young child (not the least of which being that the ending is a Joke rather then a sudden affirmation of the consequences of all the Zany Events...perhaps a missed opportunity but u cant copy the forumla too exactly i supposed), but it is platformers. the game Repeatedly Insists that u break it, and is happy to give u the tools to do so, and smartly keeps the dedicated linear platforming challenges that r potentially trivialized by the _childDocuments_.review: I have over 200 games in my library, and I think I have finished (not 100% completed) maybe half of them. This game was charming and fun enough to make me 100% the game. It's a love letter to collectathons and 3D platformers like Banjo-Kazooie and Conker's Bad Fur Day. I think the most important aspect of 3D platformers is the movement. If the movement doesn't feel right, the game is no good. The movement on this game is near perfect. Controls great, super responsive, and the unique swinging mechanic opens up so many movement possibilities and alternate ways to complete a level or grab an item. The game is FUNNY too. Little nods here and there to other games and media, but the gross out humor and little interactions you have on every level are great and keep things interesting.I think the game is a great length for someone who wants a quick, relaxing 3d platformer that doesn't feel like a chore to get through. _childDocuments_.review: This is a weird game to recommend! I am, always, starved for 3D platformers that transport me back to the halcyon days of collecting ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with goofy mascots on the Nintendo 64. In that way this game delivers, the platforming feels good if a bit too loose (more on that later), there certainly are things to collect, stages to explore and traverse, enough quirk in character and mechanic to propel it forward.But it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥' gross! Clearly and willfully so, I can't knock the game for doing what it promises to, but it's just really....meh about it. The first world introduces literal fascist turds waging a war on fat guys that eat feces. You tear the horns off of baby goat-unicorns to acquire new abilities. Bodily fluids, abrupt violence, and piles of viscera are the go-to for eliciting cheap laughter (or groans). It's almost like it's not gross enough, so banal in the ways it squeezes out ick & squick. Most of it was inoffensive if not quite amusing to me, but the laughs-per-hour ratio felt a little off for something this willfully goofy. (It's also goofy how often attempts at humor come down to "look at this guy! He's fat and naked! Ha-ha!" Maybe once or twice it's funny but then it just feels weirdly mean to fat people and, I guess, nudists.)But it's pleasant enough to play and that was enough to propel me to the end. A big component of that too is that it's relatively frictionless - taking a cue from long forgotten platformer Whiplash, the main mechanic is your demon lad being chained to a cherub lad who you can use to smash & swing. At first you can swing just a couple of times in the air, suitably acrobatic. It evolves into multiple swings, then one that can recharge, then an attack upgrade that gives you a little more distance, on top of the basic double jump, and eventually a glide, and and and long story short you eventually get to a point where touching the ground is more or less optional. I completed one stage without noticing buttons that raise platforms in a way that was unintended but very satisfying. Unfortunately designing against this kind of mobility is difficult when it comes to instituting challenge, and I found no such difficulty self-imposed or otherwise after that point. This is also a game that looks Pretty Good when you're not literally knee deep in ♥♥♥♥. The enormous alpine restaurant hub is exceptional to look at, as is the dense, layered jungle. The main character moves with astounding fluidity such that his wide range of mobility options are functionally seamless. Levels are visually distinct, and collectibles deeply scrutable. It's Good Enough for the platformer-hungry like myself. Anyone else, or folks with an aversion to grossness, probably won't find much to love or even like here.

So if someone had played without looking for collectibles they won't have enough candymeat to do fancy movements but they can still complete the levels. What I'm trying to say is at some point you can clearly see the game has a path to follow yet at that point you could already bypass it. I get why it was made this way, but perhaps it would have been resolved by unlocking skills as you advance and setting the challenges according to the skills you have unlocked, this way you can make the platforming more interesting since you won't risk having players like me who will bypass most of the default platforming. I would be super interested in seeing demanding platforming that is fun and challenging even with four swings, double jump, climb, and all the other movements, gets my imagination flowing thinking of what kind of platforming would get me excited to squeeze every drop of movement the game has. There are unlockable skills to find in each world that will allow you to find more collectibles. There are a total of 4 hub worlds with 3 sub-levels within each to explore. There's some dumb/obscene style comedy that you would actually expect from a game from the 90s. It almost felt like I took a time machine to replay a 3D platformer from my childhood. _childDocuments_.review: GAMEPLAY, CONTROLS & FUN FACTOR: 9/10 - EXTREMELY SATISFYING! Simple but addictive and dynamic movement upgrades. It's not hard but it requires just the right amount of focus to pull off. Nate only has 1 basic attack which is effective but I would've liked to see a larger variety of permanent weapons. During several brief, rare instances you can pick-up weapons like a shotgun and machine gun butNARRATIVE: 8/10 - A very, very simple story is exponentially elevated by CONSTANT humor. You are an employee of Satan and your job is to fetch the nastiest most evil cooking ingredients across the world so Hell's head chef can cook Satan the most devilish birthday cake ever made! That's it. While there's no voice acting in the game, a ton of the dialogue is genuinely laugh-out-loud hilarious (particularly from Nate's Cherub weapon-companion named Nugget.)TECHNICAL FIDELITY: 8/10 - The game looks beautiful and I love all of the designs however there are quite a few grammatical errors in the dialogue and very rare but still frustrating gameplay bugs and glitches.

_childDocuments_.review: A 3D platformer that is as cute as it is grotesque. Gamplay wise, it's pretty slick. Responsive controls, big focus on exploration and, especially with upgrades, tons of ways to wiggle your way around the set out path the game provides. You can essentially create your own path in almost every scenario. Nugget, your angel friend, gives you a great mix of motion and comes with a slight hiccup (he must be tossed for movement) to keep it feeling down to earth. In the end I'd say that while there's combat in this game, the combat is a small part of it. Enemies are weak and usually not numerous enough to be that dangerous, they're obstacles. Hell Pie is thoroughly a platformer, and keeps the platforming challenging and interesting throughout the games length. For criticisms I'd say the camera can be trouble to manage, especially when things get busy with the terrain. Similarily, the shadow that helps you figure out where to land can be hit or miss on when and where it appears, you get a good feel to where you're supposed to land in jumps fast, but starting out it is very rough. Bugs are numerous but fortunately I never found one that hurt my gameplay experience, only one time was I truly stuck and there's a convenient command in the start menu to teleport to your last checkpoint if you're stuck. The bosses however were pretty mixed. Some of them were very good, but others... especially the big hand, was so easy I'm willing to bet it's bugged. The last boss was a blast and definitely the cherry on top of the line of foes.  Levels are varied and have a lot of imagination put into them, platforming remains tight, there's lots of space to explore and find quirky secrets. Even going through the same area multiple times I still found secrets that surprised me. Levels are all designed so that you can finish the game with minimal power ups to your abilities, but it would be very tricky. My recommendation is to go out and find as much as you can for upgrades. If you don't like collectathons then you can ignore a lot of it at the cost of difficulty. Lots of sex and adult humour in the game, if you haven't already seen the trailer, be prepared for it, it's not very subtle but it's not terribly in your face as to be obnoxious if you're worried about it. And what is very direct is 90% of the time optional for continuing the game. Same with the nudity, it's barely visible through the story. Though some of the imagery in Hell Pie can be disturbing, including the use of animal cruelty, so heads up for that. Aesthetically it's very very well done for an indie game. Animation is crisp and smooth, characters are vibrant and colourful, and there's a massive amount of custom models for enemies, objects, and effects. It's a little mind boggling really. Nate and Nugget especially are my favorite, with tons of reactions, animations in special attacks and movements, and of course, their adorable and sexy(?) outfits. It's a big ask but I do wish he had more animations, mostly idle animations which seem to either be him standing  almost still, or panting and standing still.  Misc stuff I enjoyed were the side characters like the chef, barbera and the cowardly office demons, and other critters. Game was never too dark to navigate and the music while it can get repetitive, wasn't offensive and could be quite good, there's even some original tracks I think! Misc stuff I didn't like was that the outfit variety could get pretty slim later in the game, the portal challenges (enter a portal for an extra hard platforming challenge) were in some cases, hard enough to make me wonder how you could beat them without cheesing the movement. Nugget had lots to say which was nice, but sometimes the prompts to talk would happen too often and get in the way when I was doing complex movements or was about to do some. Final thoughts. There's probably 25+ hours of game enjoyment here. Pretty great for an indie game considering the price! A good buy for a person who wants a well made platformer on a budget, worth every penny. The good qualities definitely outweighed the bad and by the end I felt genuine satisfaction and pride in beating it after an arduous quest for pie. 8/10. I hope Nate and Nugget do great things in the future. Or at least get lots of adoring fans outside of hell!

_childDocuments_.review: Cleared a decent bit but its a really decent platformer so far.My only issues are that the dialogue isn't all that funny, especially the start of the game. All the demons in the main Hub have dialogue thats just not what you'd expect when your getting into an "adult themed" game.It makes the first 30 minutes of the game feel like you were tricked and that the game isn't going to be funny.It wasn't until the first world Sashimi Island that you encounter someone who swears. _childDocuments_.name: Hell Pie

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, though honestly I was surprised it's not Early Access. While it has the content, I think it could benefit from more polish. It plays a lot like Hat in Time, but I think my biggest gripe so far (I have almost 100% the first world beyond the starting area) is that the levels are just not very interesting. Visually they are great, there's a lot of charm, and the hub world aspect reminds me a lot of Crash Twinsanity for the PS2. However, I am 4 hours in and there's not much making me want to continue. There's nothing blatantly wrong about the game, but there is very little in the way of interesting things pushing me to keep playing. The collectibles do very little, and unlike in HiT where I was excited to go through each level and see what new hat I would get and how it would be used in the level, there's none of that so far. The first horn you acquire I haven't used it once as a part of the platforming, only as a faster sprint. I think it's the level design and integration of the main horn items into that design that makes me lukewarm on this game.I don't want to give this game a not-recommend, I think these are just my own problems and you may or may not agree. If nothing else, it's a solid platformer and aside from the wonky camera at times and the integration of respawns leaves some to be desired, I haven't noticed any bugs. So for me it's a meh, take it or leave it

name: In Other Waters
detailed_description: a xenobiologist who discovers extraterrestrial life while searching for her missing partner. When Ellery is called to planet Gliese 677Cc by Minae Nomura, only to arrive at an abandoned base, she finds herself adrift in an ocean of secrets, with little more than a malfunctioning diving suit and a strange AI to guide her. You are this AI. Guide Ellery—and keep her safe—as you dive deeper and explore an underwater alien landscape. The planet’s unique life, and its dark history, are yours to uncover and the bond between you and Ellery will be tested by the secrets you learn. Through this shifting narrative, In Other Waters asks questions about the nature of “natural” and “artificial” life, and investigates what it means to be a human in an epoch of extreme environmental destruction. For life to continue, it must change. Freely dive into an expansive section of seafloor, from shimmering reefs to inky depths. Unlock upgrades and make discoveries that allow you to open up new paths, uncovering strange creatures and environments as you do. Navigate an elegant, intuitive UI via gamepad or mouse controls. Interpret signals, set headings, and map the ocean through experimentation and intuition. Discover and catalogue species through observation, scanning, taking samples, and interacting with alien life. Read Ellery’s notes, look at her sketches, and help her classify an entirely new ecosystem. Choose whether to study creatures, investigate secrets or dive new areas, then come back to your base to study samples in the lab, chat to Ellery or read her journals to understand more about this world. Through limited communication learn more about the person whose suit you inhabit, and help guide her towards a terrible truth. What you experience together will bring you closer. ABOUT THE DEVELOPER Jump Over the Age is a one-person game development studio founded by Gareth Damian Martin (they/them). Gareth is the winner of GDCA and Indiecade awards, and has been nominated for a Games Award, multiple IGF Awards, a GDC Award, and four BAFTAs. They have been named both “An accomplished world-builder” (Edge Magazine) and “one of the most exciting indie talents around” (Eurogamer).

_childDocuments_.review: Still in the midst of this one, but having so much fun with it. If you like puzzle, and exploring style games, then give it a try. You may like this if you like Subnautica? Scanning everything, and lots of data collection. Controls are a little bit of a learning curve to start, but once you get the hang of it super easy, especially with a controller. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In Other Waters is essentially a Walking Simulator, with a dose of Interface Puzzler to spice things up. If you aren't interested in either of those, walk away now.If those aren't disqualifying, you will find In Other Waters to be an interesting and fairly chill experience. Well written, great atmosphere, and a decent plot hook.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Would you rather watch than read? Me too. Check out the highlights of the gameplay here:This game uses a really simple idea: Let the player imagine everything that we give them through text so they run wild with the idea. It works pretty dang well, too. Going through the ocean and reading each of the entries for new species, locations and plants is really relaxing. You move at your own pace, just clicking and reading. The game is practically a visual novel. The AI (you) pilots a curious scientist through a vast alien ocean, and it really is that cool.That, however, is really only if you're into really laid back experiences in games. There is no combat or any fighting in this game as far as I am aware. There aren't any lasers or bombs, or killing people. You just click through the ocean and catalog all of the species you can. It's not for everyone. If you don't like reading, don't buy this. If you don't like the ocean, don't buy this. tl;dr - Relaxed heavy reading game for those people who want to chill out and explore.Join the Curator group for more reviews like this:

_childDocuments_.review: I tried playing this game.  It loaded, and instructions for moving my character played on the screen.  The instructions were not very explicit, so I moved hesitantly, and then the robot instructing me got angry with me for being hesitant, which annoyed me.  Don't blame me if you're unable to be clear about what you want me to do!  That was the best part of the experience though!  Within a few minutes from that point I got to an impasse where I seemingly could not do anything to make the game proceed, and no further help or instructions were forthcoming.  So I emailed the game makers.  That was about a month ago, and I've still not received a response from them.  So I'm ranking this as the lowest possible ranking.  Complete waste of money.
