_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Pretty good, but definitely not for everyone. A game that does what it wants to do very well. Maybe not the most enjoyable experience for a lot of people, but maybe a perfect experience for a special niche. I could see this being a sort of therapeutic treatment for people experiencing emotional or psychological distress, especially.As far as game-play goes, the fact that your character is basically on rails is probably the biggest weak point, for me. It's a point and click adventure, albeit a very stylized one. This is a bit jarring since it's an exploration game. Intuitively I'd expect to be able to go wherever I like. The game makes up for this with great storytelling, but to be honest, games that are this close to books I kind of prefer were just actual books. I don't need this stylized interface between me and the story. "click to progress story" is not better, imo, than "turn page."It gets a thumbs up for being well designed. It gets a thumb sideways for interface. It's creative and interesting but also not very enjoyable to navigate once you're learned it.  Also, can I just say, Steam, that your "games like this" box might need to see a doctor. It's listing Halo, for me, when looking at the page for In Other Waters. I'm all for making loose connections between things, but seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: With taking my time and getting lost once on what to do it the full game was just over 4 hours. Sadly it isn't extremely long, but the music and simplicity is quite relaxing. One downside was the dialog- If you happened to not be paying attention then you could miss out on something, but the simple aspect of the game makes it hard to get stuck or lost wondering without really knowing where to go next. Not a multiple play through game. I would say if you are looking for a good story or something to motivate you through the game then I would pick a different game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I had a good experience, but the themes became increasingly heavy-handed and moralistic as we approached the end. There's already a hint of it when , but it gets more overt later. I don't mind artistic works that address climate change and similar issues, but the perspective presented here seemed really flat. Especially when we're ending the game on this note, this really detracted from the overall value of the work.This is also not a game for people who don't like reading. If you can move past that though, the strengths of the game lie in its ability to convey bits and pieces of story in everything from the descriptions of the things you scan to the taxonomic entries. The mix of exploration and horror works, mostly, but some of the writing does get a bit repetitive.I can’t see myself replaying this game, between the moralizing, slightly clunky UI, and writing style, but this was still a better use of my time than not.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A absolutely mesmerizing game and universe; a real treat for any fans of speculative evolution and xenobiology. You can feel the love and careful consideration oozing out of every pore. Fairly quick to complete - I reached 100% on my first playthrough - but definitely worth the price of admission in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In Other Waters is a thrilling, non-violent gem focusing on discovery of life among the stars in a place humanity didn’t think to look. This game proves that sometimes simplicity is best, its minimalist approach to complicated technology an absolute triumph. The immersion is incredible, considering the genre, and the concept is dramatically fresh to the point where I literally feel in awe of how much has been accomplished by so little. Of course, the game is not without its hiccups, and those are slightly more magnified due to the minimalist nature, but all can be forgiven when everything else is taken into account. If you want something vastly different than anything else you’ve experienced with enough familiarity to suck you in from the get-go, you have to dive into In Other Waters.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This game was decidedly odd. I grabbed it after loving Subnautica, and while it's in the same general plot style, the interface is much more menu-based and the movement is limited to pre-generated nodes.The plot is excellent, with a strong element of sadness and regret, mixed in with a solid ever-present confusion about what is actually going on.I thoroughly enjoyed it and would recommend it to other fans of sci-fi mystery games.Only downside I noticed was the shortness of the game. I clocked in at around 7 hours after doing everything, but I enjoyed every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In most games, moving a character somewhere is a single action. You press "W," or click a mouse button, or something similar.In this game, if you would like to move, you must deduce from trial and error that you need to perform all of the following steps:1) Press space.2) Click a solid-coloured yellow triangle in the centre-most circle on the screen, Do not click the much larger yellow triangle just outside the central circle, or either of the two blue triangles nearby. If there is not a yellow triangle located in the central circle, you cannot move. The triangle that will allow you to move will not be labelled.3) Press CTRL.4) Click on a medium-sized yellow circle on the rim of the large central circle. Do not click any of at least sixteen other possible circles of various sizes on the screen, some of which are also yellow and most of which are not labelled. Click and HOLD the mouse button, or you will not be able to do the next step.5) Drag the mouse in an arc until a line between two small circles appears in the largest central circle on the screen.6) Press "W", or click a different circle somewhat to the right of the central one, but only if that circle has changed colour from teal to yellow and a symbol consisting of two more small circles linked by a line has become visible.If this seems intuitive to you, you may enjoy this game. If the prospect of doing this sequence several thousand times sounds fun, you may enjoy this game.Otherwise, you will probably find it as frustrating as I did.It's possible that basic gameplay may be less complex with a console controller or joystick. But on a PC, doing anything becomes a boring grind very quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Like Zephkiel's review, I was hoping to enjoy this game a lot more, as the premise seems great. You're an AI suit helping an explorer on an alien planet. You can't directly "see" anything, only pick stuff up on your sensors. I spent a few sessions playing through the initial steps of this game, and the first thing was, it's very easy to miss the communications from the human inside your suit. They appear in a tiny window amongst all the other stuff on your screen. There's a countdown for the text, so if it passes by, you can easily miss it. I found it very tedious, like a top-down "walking simulator" and the lack of an overhead map (at least in the opening portions of the game after you are free to explore) to consult when you are navigating the waters is noticeable. I got lost and navigating around is slow and tedious.I know they're a small indie team and I applaud them for what they've achieved, but if you want to play a game made by some Indie devs about being an AI and helping a human companion, check out NoCode's Observation.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful little game! With a simple interface, a few simple graphical elements, mechanics that are just as involved that it doesn't take away from the excitement of exploration, and an awesome soundtrack, this game took me to another planet and showed me an entirely alien, different, and amazing biosphere. Plus a story and theme that are certainly nothing new, but always gets to me. I really enjoyed immersing in it, and I wish there was more! The only thing that sometimes bothered me was the moving mechanics, which is a bit more clunkier than ideal, but it never got to the point where I was properly annoyed, luckily.An awesome experience, recommended to everyone who likes these types of "minimalist" interfaces, slow-paced progression, reading, and playing with their own theater of mind. :)
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: There isn't much to this game, logistically. If you're like me and you enjoy chill games that are story line driven, this game is for you. It's more or less a xenobiologist simulator more than anything. While the concept is simplistic, there's a lot to the interface. But, in my opinion, it is very easy to pick up and adjust to. This game relies heavily on theme and variation such as the visual and auditory cues to generate moods and emotions. It's a bit heavy handed on the "humans are trash" troupe, buuuut it isn't anything we aren't used to. There is clearly a lot of love and passion that went into this game - the art aspect of this game is phenomenal.If you're looking for a chill game with some morality woven into the story line, than this is a game for you. Overall - 7/10. I enjoyed it, but I'm not in love with it. I am very glad I experienced the game and played it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: The interface is simple and clean, there is absolutely nothing photo realistic about the game and the interaction with the planet is almost entirely empirical but somehow this still made me think about the movie Solaris. The text based story telling and and scene setting was beautiful and left space for some reflection. Its been months since I finished playing this and I don't often leave reviews but I find myself thinking about In Other Waters quite often. I also played this on a touch screen computer and the controls worked so very immersive, perfect for this as you are basically just interfacing with your little sub thing the whole time.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the games for which I have a hard time putting my feelings into words.Basically try it out no matter how you feel looking at it. If you did not like it for the first hour or two, just drop it. It is not going to ruin your day or something. You will just have tried something you did not like. However, if you liked it, you will most probably be stunned by it and will be a game that you would think about and remember for a long time.I feel saying that the controls are clunky is an overstatement. It definitely controls like no other game but if you are just a tad bit open minded about it, you will adapt in no time. Also, the controls of the hardsuit you are in are part of the exploration the game offers. You need to adapt to your role as a board computer somewhat and explore the world through its lens. I feel that people who criticize it for being on rails (hence not exploratory enough) are missing the point.I feel the main draw of the game is immersion through mechanical means and through immagination. The game offers very little visual information and that opens the door for a lot of guesswork and imagining its world. I value that a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:-Beautiful interface.-Great idea for a game (underwater exploration managed entirely through a simple, stylistic map).-Very interesting biological and ecological descriptions, if you have the patience to read them. In some ways I liked it better than Subnautica, even (though it's a different type of game of course) ... the lack of detailed visuals leaves room for the imagination, and the ecological descriptions are much more involved and interesting here.NEUTRALS:-I found the story serviceable and touching in its way, while also a little simplistic at times (). I felt the ending was alright but didn't do much to develop the already established themes.-In some places, the geographical navigation has several different branches you can follow. On the one hand, this keeps the map from being too linear. On the other hand, it can feel like busy work, retracing your steps to try out another path, going down all the corridors not knowing if you'll find anything there, etc. It didn't get very bad, like some games.CONS:-I found the navigation to be fairly clunky. In a game that's 98% navigation, it's a drawback. You travel between nodes on the map, and to find unexplored nodes, you click a button (or a key on your keyboard) to scan the area. Then you can click on one of the nodes you found (and read it if you want to). Then, to travel to it, you have to exit out of the "scan" function, re-enable the "travel" function, and  THEN travel to the node. You might do this several dozen times, exploring a new area. I think they wanted to avoid making it too fast, didn't want to destroy the ambiance, but it approached drudgery for me.-There was one moment that was possibly a minor plot hole, bothered me a little.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This game might not be for everyone, its a bit slow moving and the movement system takes some getting used to. I loved this game, i had so much fun reading about the different creatures, The story was amazing, and the music and sound design is absolutely beautiful. I would absolutely recommend thisgame to everyone who enjoys something a bit slow paced, with a lot of reading. I enjoyed the game enough to nominate it for the story rich category of the steam awards 2020
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In Other Water is, a lot. I do not feel the desire to spoil the game here, as it is only nine to ten hours in length, but I found the experience moving.The graphics are simplistic, just about as much as the game needs to tell its story and pleasant in a minimalist sort of way. The sound design and music are haunting, the mechanics simplistic but purposeful.What stood out the most to me is the story. The store page itself gives you a tasty little starting point. The world of Gliese 667Cc is wonderful and soothing to immerse yourself in, the story which unfolds across that blue-green ocean is dramatic; it has highs and lows and twists and such vivid scenes. At each precipice I could feel my rapid heartbeat as I braced for the incoming unknown.This is one of few stories to grip me so extremely, and even bring me to tears.Plus it has space lesbians (and I ship them so hard)
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In other waters is a peculiar narrative mystery game where you find yourself working with a Marine xenobiologist by the name of Ellery. You & Ellery work together piloting a dive suit to uncover a mystery pertaining to a previous associate named Minae who has apparently gone missing in the alien waters of Gliese 667c. Along the way you document the alien fauna/flora & utilize it to your advantage in solving small puzzles to aid in your exploration.The story has a strong slow-burn to it, ramping up in intrigue as you progress further with it that I really enjoyed. I felt that the method of control scheme was creative, where you could realistically play this game 100% with a mouse (though there are a couple convenient shortcuts for the keyboard), relying on an interesting interactive UI for tools & navigation. With a blind playthrough & as of writing this, it took me approximately ~8 hours to complete.I've only a couple (minor) gripes for the overall experience, the first being the sample storage you place your samples into after returning from an expedition. Although not very many may have this issue (I'm a bit of a hoarder), if you store too many unique types of samples within it, it will not display all of your items after it has been filled, placing them into a kind of invisible buffer. You can easily get around this by getting rid of or using items you don't need anymore though, so definitely not a game breaking issue, just a mild inconvenience. The latter issue was with the ending area, (BUT) I want to preface that the ending itself was not bad so don't skip this game because of it, seriously. my gripe is Overall, I would absolutely recommend this game if you're into science fiction, mysteries, nature walks or light puzzle solving.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: an amazing story told with minimalistic style, somehow painting beautiful landscapes with simple shapes, with detailed descriptions to give you an idea of what it looks like, almost like a book. The story is compelling and meaningful, and this is easily one of my top favourites of all time, definitely a must play that will change the way you see storytelling in games, as well as games as a whole and the design that goes into them. 11/10, why aren't there more games like this?
