_childDocuments_.review: Dude, this game is seriously well written, one of the best short-story games I have ever played. A lot of people have said that it is "bland" but I disagree. The few characters really grip you and the ending is gut wrenching. My only regret with this game is not spending enough time looking at each little piece of the story as literally every point you can move to in the game has something written about it. Overall, my favorite part was the audio log transcripts at the ending inside the old city, it really gave an atmosphere of death and destruction. Devs, you are artists.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed slowly unwrapping the story, the UI was beautiful and the way the HUD changed as you moved to different areas felt so intuitive. The discovery and exploring was really interesting with fun mechanics and environments. Honestly didn't expect this to take as long as it did, I am a slow gamer but I didn't expect there to be so much to explore. Really satisfying. Will say though reading speed matters in this game, if your a slow reader this game will be somewhat harder, there is some content you may miss out on. However all the major story points you have plenty of time to read, so I wouldn't let that put you off too much! All in all wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This was incredible. If you've ever played Subnautica and loved the discovery aspect of both the world and the mystery of the planet, this is a good game for you. It's not super long, but it involves both scientific discovery (I'm talking taxonomy stuff and collecting multiple samples) as well as figuring out why you're on the planet in the first place. Also, it's anti-capitalist. Go figure! I really loved it and can't recommend it enough. Normally text based games with no images are hard for me, but this really sucked me in!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I want to recommend this game, but I just can't. There's a couple of serious issues that simply make it unplayable. TL;DR: Poor performanceBad input supportTiny text with bad scalingFull review:The first is poor controller support. The controls are needlessly awkward, changing sticks and buttons around for no reason. For example, you're expected to use the left stick *and* dpad simulateously for certain actions. I appreciate there is controller support at all, but it's outright unpleasant to actually use. The game works much better on a mouse, so I thought I'd try it on my surface pro 7 i7 model, and no luck! Even at low resolutions, the game performed surprisingly poorly. Certainly this is a game that doesn't need high performance, but having what little motion there is be stuttery is very unimmersive, which is a big deal for this game's appeal!Speak of low resolution, the game has *tiny* text and even with the UI "zoomed in" it's still very annoying to read many things. This is worsened by the game seemingly using a mix of nearest neighbor and bilinear scaling, which results in elements looking blurry *and* warped even at 1440p!Basically, it seems like the developer expects you to play on a proper gaming computer, on a large 4k screen, with a mouse and keyboard. Anything beyond that is frankly unplayable, which is deeply unfortunate for this very interesting and innovative game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful: the UI makes this game - it's color changing with the areas - the many functions of it just a single button press away and not in your face, the music is great and soothing and picks up and drops when the story does.A story being told with only dots and lines - this game is one of a kind.But it's a game based on anti-humanism - humans are terrible beings and animals (aliens) seem to be perfect. Not all humans are destroyer-of-worlds with a heart of hatred, nor are animals perfect. It's hypocritical to believe animals are better than humans when the human that believes it continues to "invade" nature.There also seems to be subtle LGBT hints from what I've read in the dialogue, or I may be wrong, and I may get hate for it but there are gamers that don't like games because of it and it should be stated. Same could be said about religion in games when people hate anything to do with religion - people need to know so they can be aware of what they are paying for. Wouldn't you want reviews from those that enjoyed it based on actual feedback instead of negative brigading because of political things? But like I said, it's subtle and not forced so you can ignore it and continue playing the game.I put 5 hours into it and finished the story with doing exploration to eventually just wanting to know what the ending was, but if you were curious about playing after the story once you finish it you are sort of given a second task to complete the taxonomy (i.e. finding everything you missed).
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game and thought it looked like a chill time. I didn't expect to enjoy it so much I'd binge it in a day.The UI is really clean and the music and colours work really well to set a mood. The minimalist style works really well here, but the one thing I felt was missing was a map of some sort when I was hunting down the last few samples to research.The gameplay can be a little clunky, with a lot of clicking and dragging a few UI components around. It's pretty novel and fun to begin with, but later on or when you want to move quickly it gets a little old. There are some keyboard shortcuts I found out about halfway through my playthrough that speed things up a bit.The story is pretty interesting, although I think it takes a backseat to exploring the world and all the cool life you find. Usually I'd hit a story point and want to rush through it to explore and find more weird sea life. There are a lot of areas of the game where your air or energy is constantly draining too, which forces you to rush through all the descriptions rather than taking your time to read.Overall I definitely enjoyed the game. I wholeheartedly recommend it if you think you'll enjoy having a (relatively) chill time exploring and reading about an alien ocean.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Very much my preferred game: strong story, beautiful art and music, and unobtrusive gameplay. I would definitely class this as a "walking simulator". I got ten very enjoyable hours out of it and was quite satisfied with the ending. Using exploration of alien flora and fauna into one of the "mystery" aspects of the game was inspired.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: While it's evident that a lot of work and love have gone into the game, I can't find myself playing more than I have. The story didn't catch me right from the start and the slow pace and stylized topological map is nice in the beginning but didn't hold me for long either.I can still give a very honest recommendation for anyone that wants to dive in deep into a non-conventional adventure game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Wish steam had a neutral recommendation option.Mostly well done with a few things that just bugged me to no end. TLDR: time moves too fast (for me supposedly being an AI) in some areas to really enjoy it. Should have access to a static map so you dont get lost.1. Am I an AI or not? while this may seem a straight forward answer, im wondering. I dont have the freedom of time like an AI would unless it didnt have nearly enough ram to run itself. I can understand that while moving resources get used, but when not moving? I should have the relative speed to easily read all the little notes and whatnot that I want without enough time going by to a human to have even taken a breath. 2. As an AI why dont I have access to the overall map when in the diving suite? dont need a real time tracking system (unless it makes sense), but even being able to reference it would have 'made' me spend the time to go hunt down -everything- and get all the taxonomy information, but because I was effectively blind once I left the base... I decided that it was far too much hassle.3. Minor annoyance and what pushed it over the edge. Movement is so slow and clunky.Despite these annoyances I did/do mostly enjoy the gameplay (think im 4/7 the way through at the time of writing this. If her journals are any indication)
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This is a story driven exploration game, with a background of science, space, and exobiology. I loved it. It’s a pretty chill and relaxing game. There are a few spots where there is a little tension but not enough to make you anxious, just to carefully plan your actions.The story is great, and it got better as you went further. It focuses on humanity's relationship with nature. Visually it is pretty, and the music is superb. Being a scientist myself, I think it did a great job with the scientist characters and the way the research is performed (though not entirely realistic of course). I only have a few comments, as constructive criticism. The biggest one is you cannot see the whole map when you’re out and about, only your surroundings. The whole map is available only in the base. I had to take a photo with my phone to use when exploring because I was getting lost in a few spots. It would really be helpful to have a small map on the side telling where you are. The second one is that I think the creature sketches should be shown to the player much earlier. Given the lack of visuals, it would have really enhanced the gameplay having a mental image of the species early on. Maybe you can get a more detailed image if you complete the research on that species. Additionally, a few pics here and there could be inserted in the gameplay as images the biologist takes with the suit of the different environments. Third, the movement is slow. The first time you go through an area it's a perfect pace, but the second or third is a bit tedious. Maybe implement faster movement the second time.The game is short, I completed it in 4.5 hs (steam only recorded <4). I only wish it was longer. I would gladly purchase a follow up game  (sequel or prequel) in the same style.I also purchased the add on PDF that has a short epilogue on the story and pretty art of the creatures. All in all, a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Xenobiology could’ve been more compelling. As stylized as the piloting interface may be, it’s difficult to connect to exploration when there’s a supreme lack of information concerning your supposedly awe-inspiring surroundings. It hurts even more that gameplay fails to facilitate the sensations that the presentation chooses to sidestep. The premise of the game’s underwater investigation desperately needs a primary gameplay loop that complements the curiosity of alien research, the uneasiness of aquatic navigation, and the awe of uncovering new life.None of those feelings necessitate high-resolution on-demand fish pictures, but extensively staring at dots/topography only heightens the thirst for visual feedback. This could’ve been an opportunity to demonstrate how abstract interactivity in games can satisfyingly communicate/approximate larger concepts. Scan the dots, connect the dots, and occasionally drag the dots to a box. It grows old fast, no matter how many times you change the dots’ names. It’s a disservice to merely create a  allegory for the scientific process or marine traversal instead of pursuing the creation of an engrossing one.The focus of  is set on a benign narrative delivered intermittently via a dialogue box. The initial goals felt tangible with some uncertainty and an emotional build-up. Disappointingly, the early intrigue is betrayed by a new  crux that drowned my interest going forward. Frustratingly, the plot lends itself to scenarios where environmental storytelling would’ve been paramount. Narrative retention is a further challenge to maintain when significant moments at the base must play out through scuttling text in a small, uncentered square.The best pieces of  are found in those first few minutes of extraterrestrial curiosity and the game’s aquatic ambiance. The ocean’s soundscape helps to guide the mind’s eye, but the sounds of water are unsurprising and, while pleasant, the reverberating synthesizers mostly reinforce safety, exploration, or tension. Otherwise, the game came across as an unusually dry narrative set in a unique world whose presence is depressingly intangible.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In Other Waters presents a consistent tone across its story, visual style, audio, and game play. This harmony was able to easily draw me into its world. Even the minimalist art became more than moving dots, but a whole ecosystem.Just to be clear, the narrative does the heavy lifting in this game. If you're not looking to read a calm, mysterious novella worth of words, I'd pass on this game until you were in such a mood. The game play is simple, but uses that very quality to support the narrative clandestinely.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks fun and appealing at first, and the music is good: Then you actually start playing the game.- To move you need to press 4 buttons in a certain order. All simple tasks are done in a similar way. (This is the main mechanic in the game)- The visuals are fun at first, until you realise that's what you're stuck with for the rest of the game, albeit a partial colour swap.The story is perhaps fun, but it seems like a hassle to even reach it in the first place. If you are into slow, text based adventures, perhaps its your cup of tea. For anyone else, you won't enjoy much.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game for fans of hard sci fi, alien life, and the beauty of the Earth's oceans. The game takes place on a real planet some four times as massive as the Earth, which orbits a red dwarf star in a triple star system 23 light years away from the Sun. The ecosystem you explore in this game is probably fictional, but it might not be - and that's because this is the most realistic depiction of alien life I've ever seen in fiction, even surpassing Subnautica and the famous works of Wayne Barlowe. The gameplay is simple but thoughtful, clever but not difficult, and mainly serves to create a tranquil atmosphere that encourages discovery. The game also features a strong story wrapped in an unsettling mystery, and to its credit, the story does not overstay its welcome. After finishing the game, I was left hungry for more.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it and bought the soundtrack because I enjoyed that too.I read a lot of sci-fi and so I was pleasantly surprised that the story took a sudden turn I was not expecting. I wish certain aspects of the world were better explored, but that's true of any science fiction setting in the history of literature. This game feels well researched - and while it's not in the realm of "hard sci-fi" it's very much within the realm of "earth's oceans" - which are plenty alien enough.I think this is an important game, made even more relevant by the ongoing damage done to our own oceans. It talks about environmental degradation and how our own oceans might look in the near future without being heavy-handed or preachy about it, and that takes talent as a writer and designer both.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely stunning. it defies succinct description. subnautica has nothing on this; in fact, after taking in the game's message of preservation and study, subnautica is almost a little offensive. i've never been so blown away by an ocean i couldn't directly see. evocative, sad, deeply moving, it's like nothing else i've ever played. my expectations were high and this surpassed them completely. it defies scoring but i'd definitely give it a perfect one. cannot praise it enough

_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a beautiful experience I just can't not take the time to write a review and recommend it. It is closer to a graphic novel than anything else, but with quite an interesting twist in who are you, as a player, in control of: rather than the protagonist biologist, you are the AI in charge of the diving suit, and as such you see the world around you through sensors and an UI.This does not take from immersion though: on the contrary, it enhances it. You perceive the world through the protagonist's commentary, their descriptions of your surroundings and the lifeforms you encounter, their taxonomy notes (which you can help expand by exploring around), the beautiful sountrack and the sounds around you, along with subtle changes in the UI color scheme.In many ways, it is like reading a novel. Your imagination will be the one to carry you to this alien ocean, and the reading and listening will enhance that. While it is not a long game, it is certainly an experience worth having. Go for it!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: If you're up for a sublime and calming yet engaging gaming experience, look no further.Here's why you should join me in unearthing that laid-back explorer in you:- Beautiful prose that challenges you to build not just pictures in your mind, no. Whole mental art galleries.- A graphics style that is almost hypnotic in its functionality. Simple but never boring.- Abstract creature movement has never looked so engrossing and relaxing.- A straightforward gameplay loop, with just the right amount of stuff to do.- You're constantly driven forward to chase after the next revelation. Exploration-fed dopamine hits buttressed by a bittersweet human interest story.- Even though there's urgency in the narrative, there's never a need to rush (for the most part). You're given a lot of space to just drink it all in.It's the abstract, stylized, poetic version of Subnautica, and I highly recommend it.I'm amazed that this is the work of mostly one person. Hats off to you, sir!An extra section just for the music. It's perhaps my favorite part of the game.The soundtrack is otherwordly and has become my album of the year 2020, Spotify-certified.And it makes for the chillest car music.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This was an intriguing little game which I enjoyed very much. The actual gameplay is difficult to describe, imagine visual novel meets walking sim. You see a topographical map, click on highlighted points of interest on a head-up display and read the texts describing the world around you as the story progresses. And this is where the game truly shines - its world building and story. I found it engaging and interesting, although the very end was a little bit flat. Apparently you need to buy a book "DLC" to get the epilogue which is... not very nice.The game's atmosphere is reminiscent of Subnautica, even if the comparison does neither game justice. The same sci-fi ocean world mystery which is revealed through exploring, just a lot less visual and a lot more reading. The audio does its job of describing the aquatic setting and the visuals are pretty to look at while you navigate the world with the HUD and map changing colors depending on your environment and the various blobs representing life moving about. If you're looking for a very relaxing experience with an interesting story and excellent lore to get you hooked, you'll find this game won't disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Yes this is a delightful undersea explore-em-up that manages to capture the wonder and terror of exploring with 3000ft of water on top of you and you worrying about the oxygen and power running out. It manages this with a wonderfully simple AI, some great writing and an amazing soundtrack. It's great :).
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: more of an exercise in interactive fiction and really cool spec-bio than a game in the traditional sense, but that doesn't change the impact it had on me. beautiful, bittersweet, lonely but tinged with hope. made me cry, but in a nice way. strong recommend especially if you are a fan of speculative ecosystems and fictional xenobiology
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I struggled to figure out what to say each time I thought about writing this review. Even though I wanted to write a review for In Other Waters, it's so difficult to put my feelings for this game into words. Not just that, but to try and communicate to other people -- people who haven't played In Other Waters -- the feelings and emotions that this game provided. How do you try to explain to someone, "You essentially play as an AI in charge of an interface, guiding a scientist exploring an alien world that is incredible and teeming with every manner of incredible creature...but you don't get to see any of it. All you get to see is your little navigation interface. And it's amazing."I don't know. It makes perfect sense that imagination is truly the most vivid visual display in existence. Books, after all, have been popular for a very long time. So in that sense, part of what makes In Other Waters special is just having excellent writing. Still, even though your choices are often limited, the interactivity is part of the magic of the experience in a way that a book couldn't emulate. And while the interface isn't "stunning," it's not like the game doesn't have graphics -- it just chooses to present them in a weird way.Perhaps I'm preaching to the choir. Perhaps anyone who would actually enjoy this game has found it already. Perhaps the most this review will do is convince some number of people that won't actually like the game to give it a try, before they walk away frustrated. But if I've convinced even one person who is interested and unsure, someone who tries this game and finds all the beauty and mystery and wonder in it to resonate deeply with them, I'll be happy knowing that the time I spent writing it was worthwhile.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In other waters is a really interesting game. Throughout my play through, I was completely invested in the story. Often I'd get lost in the world, collecting samples and exploring the map, forgetting where I actually was and what I was doing. The controls are a bit counter intuitive, but if you get the shortcuts down it's a lot easier to maneuver. This game was a lot of fun, the only thing I'd note is that it's pretty short. For a game with such a huge world, I hope the developers add more to explore in future updates. It's also hard to progress if you forget what the character says. There's no way to playback what she said, so sometimes you might get stuck in a loop of exploring and sampling without direction.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical about this due to what the gameplay looked like.  It looked like basic UI interfacing. The good reviews drew me in.  The writing initially proposes an intriguing mystery. The minimalist visual style and watery sounds made for an initial good impression.  Quickly I realized how annoying the UI was for me.  Clicking on things while slowly moving around trying to find your way is not fun.  It even feels a bit claustrophobic because of how much wasted space there is on screen vs the actual size of the controlling UI. The game never initially explains what most of the icons on the buttons do in the UI either.  It’s easy enough to figure out, but still.  It also doesn’t explain some of the gameplay mechanics.  The writing never went anywhere for me and I was done interfacing with that UI after wandering around aimlessly.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Masterful narrative/exploration game oozing with atmosphere, but probably not for everyone.Game is mostly focused on linear story which is very well written, thoughtful and immersive, both in terms of character/events and environment of the planet with all it's little details. Little choice you have is mainly relegated to exploration. In terms of gameplay, it is very minimalistic, you basically move on graph of nodes and scan, occasional other activities require max 2-3 mouse clicks. There are few places where you are time/resource pressured, but margin for error is large so it should not pose any challenge. Graphics while very limited do amazing job of environmental story telling and creating atmosphere with simple shapes and colors. Music is phenomenal, greatly adds to the mood of the game.The only negative I could find is that movement is bit clunky, requiring more clicks then it should.In the end all elements of the game fit together very well and create something memorable and unique, well worth the time, as long as you can put up with the simplistic and slow gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A simple game that shows how context is everything. You play an AI that serves a diver on an alien planet. The diver is trying to find someone who has gone missing. As their AI, you manage their oxygen, energy and help them navigate the depths. All of this is done via a stylish and abstract UI with simple dots representing the diver and local wildlife, and guages servicing the gameplay mechanics. Text/audio logs deliver the story. However, the context and central mystery means your brain fills in the gaps and elevates the simplistic UX into a game. Kind of like a 21st century text adventure of sorts. Last about 3-4 hours which feels about right.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10, a touching little narrative with engaging enough character given the limited interactions and simplistic (elegant) design. really enjoyed my time with it!best when you're in the mood for reading, as the snippets of scientific observations of different life forms are really integral to the story unfolding. there's nothing super shocking or terribly difficult as the game goes on, but there's enough variety in the kinds of challenges to navigate that I was never bored or underwhelmed. a great, relaxing and thoughtful little game!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: experiencing the world through an A.Is eyes (HAH), whilst having to take care of a fragile human and discover what has happened to the planet is something that i will never forget. it's chill, it's breathtaking, it's the exploration of a lifetime with insanely immersive music and worldbuilding. highly highly recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This quickly became my favorite game after just 2 sessions of playing it. The concept is simple but puts you right into the immersive world of the alien planet. Collecting information on the life there was my favorite part next to the deep mystery that Ellery is unraveling. Getting to learn all about the creatures AND getting to see scientific sketches really took this game up a notch for me. A beautiful and enchanting experience.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I was never able to get into Subnautica. I loved the concept of alien ocean exploration, but the gameplay wasn't for me. In Other Waters takes the same concept and runs with it—runs in a direction I really love. I found the simple visuals of the game refreshing, and had a lot of fun navigating to new locations, collecting samples, and running analysis at the lab. The incredibly detailed xenobiology was stellar, and a major selling point for me, although I'd probably describe the rest of the story as good-but-unexceptional. If you enjoy the first 20 minutes, it'll be worth playing to the end. If not... maybe go try Subnautica.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Quite different. A point and click biology exploration. It's almost completely descriptive, with minimal imagery of the world you are exploring, but the depth of description meant I barely noticed this since made it easy to imagine the ocean around you. Some leaps in logic, particularly near the end, but I was hooked by this game until the final scene. I really enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: As a aquatic biology nerd I love this game. My best friend and I used to want to be aquatic/marine biologists. Even though we found different paths this game was different are really scratched that scientific exploratory itch. I haven't finished it yet but I'm drawn in by the story and the creatures/places we've found along the way. This is a one player game, but we've been enjoying playing while we hangout. I hope others find the excitement in this game too.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I needed three trys to finish the game, it was worth it. The mechanics are really different, but the music and gameplay are so relaxing. The story was captivating (at least for me) and really touching. In my Opinion it could have even been longer. I enjoyed swimming exploring and learning all about the planet and it's inhabitants. A nice and minimalistig cozy game, just right after a busy working day.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I did not finish this game. I'm a big fan of biology and aliens so I was enticed by the premise, but the gameplay is unacceptably boring, unintuitive and tedious. This was better off being a text RPG or even a book, given the amount of reading you need to do. However, I must give high praise for the designs of the aliens and their ecology - in that sense it's some of the best sci-fi I've ever seen. Subnautica devs ought to be taking notes!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it's slightly more than an interactive novel. Lot's of reading, using your imagination, has some puzzles and resource management elements, but it does more than just give you text to look at. Most of the draw is the story and how it tries to immerse you in itself with it's atmosphere, ambiance, and how it blurs it's simplistic game design with being believable story elements. And for an indie game I'd say it does this pretty well, and even gave me some thoughts afterwards on games as a new and still not fully explored medium for art. 15$ for roughly 8 hours of content may not sound great, but if you're starved for a videogame or book or something with an interesting story and has more interaction and gameplay than a visual novel, it's well worth it as a novel experience.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: if you are having doubts on whether you should play this game or not and looking for a sign, here it is. please give it a chance and buy it right now. the gameplay may be a little repetitive and dull and the visual style may seem too minimalistic but there is one thing that outweighs everything. its the music. no matter how sceptical you are and no matter how predictable do you think the plot is, the music will change your opinion once and for all. it immerses you into the alien ocean and never releases back to reality. if you`ve ever played Subnautica, you`ll know what i mean, because this soundtrack just as much fantastic. with such music, this story is going to blow you away, i promise
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Original gameplay, but a bit tedious even with a gamepad.If you like to read, writing is well done, and artworks of what you can find there are cool.Those artworks you must earn through the game are also the only kind of proper visual content, as the game is otherwise entirely made of top-view schematic screens.More qualitative artworks are available in the book you can buy along.If you crave action and fast-paced games, this game is not for you.Music is soothing and cool. You can find it on Bandcamp as well other artist creations.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: For being a game that takes place exclusively within menus, In Other Waters is extremely atmospheric and well crafted. All the dialogue between you and the diver as well as the intricate notes on the various kinds of evolving sea life are incredibly well thought out. Even though I didn't sit and read through more than probably a third of the notes this game has to offer, it's very clear that it all connects and plays a role in the discovery of the overall story. Really solid experience and definitely worth my time.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a text adventure. Less interesting than reading a plant encyclopedia.There is a story here, somewhere. A scientist, Ellery, who is looking for an old acquaintance landed on this unknown planet and woke you up. As far as he, and you, can tell, you are a consciousness inside an old diving suit. You don't know what you are, how you ended up in a diving suit, or who you are. Are you even a "who"? I guess, you'll find out in the end. I wouldn't know, I stopped playing after 33% of the game. But before that, you do your job, which is to operate the diving suit on the search for Minae, the lost friend.For the majority of the game (at least in the first third of the game), you see and do the exact same thing. There's a small circle of a topographical map. With Space, you scan your immediate surroundings. Triangles show possible next directions. Other symbols denote plants or animals that you can "look" at, i.e. you can read their descriptions. Occasionally, Ellery comments that you could take a sample. With a mouse click, you can read descriptions or pick a new direction. Clicking 'w' twice brings you to this new location. Occasionally, you need to use one of your samples to open up a passage or refuel your diving suit. But it is all clicking the same buttons on the same screen, and reading descriptions.The "pay-off" is that if you found the same plant or animal often enough, Ellery gives it a name. Each region has a "waypoint", a base that you can return to. In that base, you can "analyze" your samples: Drag a symbol from one box into another box. If you took all relevant samples, you can now read even more descriptions of the now fully analyzed plant or whatever.I am very sorry, but I found this game mind-numbingly boring. Maybe there is a nice mystery to solve. I would like to know what happened to Minae. But I just don't see the point of reading  a bunch of minute details about completely imaginary flora and fauna, while getting exactly one data point that is relevant to the story, in what the game tells me is 33% of the content/about 3 hrs of playtime.*All of these are typical descriptions as you'll read them in-game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: There is a part of this game called 'the bloom' that made me stop playing when I bought it: A text-based game should not have moments where you're trying to read while your power and oxygen are breaking down in realtime.This weekend I suffered through it and was rewarded with a fun scifi story and extensive discovery.It's not perfect but it's a great adventure for people who like to take things slow.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Very "theater of the mind," in that you are mainly navigating a map and are given text snippets to describe what you encounter. This is not a bad thing, though - it adds to the feeling of exploring an uncharted, alien territory. Discovering and cataloging new life forms is engaging and satisfying in itself, but the core of this game is a compelling ecological mystery with a unique framing device. I'll remember this one for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Great narrative-driven game with a refreshing and necessary take on the alien-world frame. The collection mechanics are rewarding and creative, the UI succeeds where so many indie games have failed and creates an enjoyable/accessible experience. Those who are disappointed that this is not trying to be Subnautica (or similar) are missing the point.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game a lot. If you like maps, sci-fi and marine animals, you might be the target group.It starts off slow, but gets more intense and starts to unfurl after the first 30 minutes.The descriptions and dialogue were packed with emotion and curiousness.The story and background you learn along the way depends on how much you pay attention to the comments, dialogue and entries, which adds to the immersion of being the AI radar system.The music and soundscape is subtle but effective.This game doesn't have much hints outside the dialogue, so pay attention!One of the best story driven games I've played.Notes: To visually experience the sea creatures you have to buy the DLC art book. To see instructions on how to move and scan, check the pause menu.I tried to first play it on a controller, but found it a lot easier to use the keyboard.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: An interface/UI heavy game about studying an alien planet, felt tedious to play at the start but as the metroidvania mechanics start to reveal themselves, it becomes quite interesting.There is a lot of reading in this game, but reading and learning is part of the game's progression and plenty of people will enjoy reading taxonomy entries.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Received as gift.This is something special; The ambience, the U.I and "feedback" of using it, the plot (as of the little i've played) and how the the communication towards the player engages with you, it's all so engrossing.Really looking forward to putting more time into this experience and finding out the planet we're researching.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: As a biologist, it's clear the amount of love and attention to detail put into this game. It's a beautiful experience that happens just as much in your screens as it does in your mind.I recommend it for people that like simple visuals and a story the lingers for a while.If you can get the DLC, it is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting game! It's definitely going to stick with me for a long time.The UI is intuitive, the visuals are magical, the story is very well written.A thousand times bravo.The game badly needs support for more languages, as the level of English required to get in is really high, especially with all the science analysis litterature. A small thing that could be fixed: the background gradient suffers from heavy banding artefacts on all the monitors I tested the game on :/ I recommend adding a simple shader post process to it, like dithering or blue noise, a lot of solutions are out there to fix it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: The world of this game is so intricately and lovingly crafted, and I really wish the gameplay was more than just mindless clicking.  The game also at times seems weirdly reluctant to allow you to slow down and take in the immersive atmosphere, often forcing you to move too quickly to enjoy anything.  It's still an incredibly unique experience, though, and I'd recommend it to anybody who's willing to slog through long stretches of boring gameplay to learn about a detailed alien ecology.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game! I liked my first couple hours of playing this game! I do find the setting and the story very interesting and the style is gorgeous, but the actual main gameplay loop just wore me down and became really tedious after a while. I got stranded trying to navigate to a new location one too many times and realized I just wasn't having fun.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: What a gem. I have had this game on my wishlist for a while, not really knowing what it was about. Now that is has been released I can already tell from the first minutes that this is a beautifully designed, calming and intriguing experience at the same time. I will update this review further the more I play.So far, the UI is gorgeous, sound design very fitting and the story and text is written in a way that makes me want to find out more. It looks very simplistic at first, but has great depth in story, lore and interactions. The abstraction in terms of visuals fits the overall game and leaves enough room for interpretation of this mysterious world, while being very immersive at the same time.I have finished the game now and I am devastated that the main story is over, which only leaves me with congratulating the makers of the game and a wish for more. It has been a beautiful journey and I have enjoyed the writing immensely, I could feel the amount of love and detail put into this in every step of the way. I will get back to this game to finish the taxonomy, but I am truly hoping for more games of this kind in the future. You have done an amazing job, thank you for this experience.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: -Music and visuals work well together in building a strong atmosphere-Intriguing story-Discovery feels great-Almost complete lack of guidance makes it even more easy to get lost than it already is-Lack of visuals can put some off, same goes for slow game speed-Sampling activity is a chore, movement is unnecessarily clunky-Occasional stutters for seemingly no reasonIn Other Waters is most likely not a game for everyone, it’s speed of gameplay, it’s simplistic graphics or it’s minimalist approach to guidance will definitely turn many away before even giving it a chance. All that being said, For more detail on the above points and a look at gameplay, please join me as I elaborate on my thoughts in this video:.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game, the concept is very cool, I also really liked the topic but that might be because I am a biologist :p . That is crazy how they really create an atmosphere with only orange dots with different size moving around. The music is also very smooth and perfectly adapted for the game. On top of that they are very creative on the species living on the planet, the drawings are amazing and the ecological texts associated to them are really convincing, even to a biologist. Thank you for making this game !
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: If it was possible to leave neutral review, this would have been it. - an intresting idea, - love that all initeractions and view of the surroundungs are through the descriptions or system readings- unintrusive and fitting music and sound effects- nice colors- a lot of small descriptions of envirioment points.- the game itself is so very relaxing borderline with boring. - Some text from the science guy were too excessive, and as such boring. - The message of the game (humans are greedy and bad, corporations are bad, consequences of climate change are bad, and bad humans cause those bad climate change), plus it is delivered in a very direct and annoying way- clunky UX (for example, in order to move to the next point usually you have to click on 4 different buttons/objects in certain order, while you move through the area only by going from point to point).- after finishing the plotline no desire to continue playing, as the only thing left it to collect samples.- extremly limited number of actions - scan, move, collect samples, "study" samples, torch, click yes/no in the dialogues (which seemingly have no consequances), feed samples to your ship(?) to keep it going, and each of these actions seems the same to other.Maybe if not for The Message I would have rated this game positive. Also It would be intresting to see the general idea of the game expanded. Also, if there will be a sequel, expanding the gameplay and adding new staff, I would like to try it
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere of the game is heavenly and intriguing from the get-go. The controls are exciting to explore, and the plot is deliciously sliced as to have you craving more after every bite of lore. The music is stunning and captures you in a bubble of awe, and the color scheme is cool at times and thrilling at others. In its entirety, it is truly a masterpiece, a work of art made entertainment, an achievement of design and story. I would recommend this game to anyone interested in marine astrobiology, or any field even remotely similar.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning in both look and sound, filled with beautiful writing (enough to make me risk the main character's oxigen supply to read more), this game is a unique experience that really makes you feel like you're a exploring an alien planet filled with strange and beautiful life. My biggest recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Great minimalist game. Sure that it doesn't show you the bigger picture through visuals, but it does through dialogue and a beautiful soundtrack. When I saw this game launch I was very curious about it, yet quite scared it wouldn't be that entertaining, which is why I waited for a discount. It's worth the full price. 100% recommend if you are into story based games.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This always sounded interesting until I played it, thought I would love it, but no tutorial and a pretty but confusing and unconventional interface just felt like a lot of hard work just to read a story. Sure it's stylish but it's a bit too minimalist for me.  Figuring out how to play a game without instructions isn't my idea of fun, and it's clearly a design choice rather than an oversight. The game underneath seemed to consist of just finding nodes, going there, and reading a thing, and they've added 'gameplay' by making you figure out the wacky controls for yourself. As long as you're aware of this going in, it's probably as good as everyone says, but personally, it didn't intrigue me enough to make the hard work seem like it would be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Plot and the gameplay seem intriguing at first but the novelty wears off soon. In order to move even a little bit you need to press three or four buttons - not so bad in theory but turns out horrible in the actual gameplay as it is the main thing you will be doing. As for the story - it starts off strong with many mysteries, but quickly boils down to banalities of sci-fi genre with people being agressive expansionists and damaging the worlds they don't understand. The character you search for at first ends up not mattering at all for the story which is a letdown as well. For all intents and purposes this game should've been a 2-hour experience ending with some mysteries unanswered. After the main story you're left to explore the sea and gather samples for different specimens in order to learn more about this alien world. It sounds like fun but then you remember how awful the movement is which adds up with the fact that you can't open the map when you're exploring the seabed - so you're often left wandering around blindly hoping to find the sample you actually need.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the way this game slowly opened up a world.  Starting with no knowledge of who I was, or what I was doing, it was fascinating to gradually learn more about my character, the scientist I was helping, and the world we were exploring.  The only downside was that I still have a million questions at the end of the game.  One character has changed, and we never learn what happened.  I really want to know what happens next.  I also got stuck for a few hours because I thought the map I saw was the whole map.  I finally looked up game play videos, thinking I had missed something important. . . only to find that I could slide the map down to see the newly discovered areas.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly chill game about exploring an alien ecosystem. The ecosystem is the best part -- if you liked something like Subnautica, and don't mind simpler things with less visuals, you should like this one too. The art style (color choices) is great as well.Weaknesses are an awkward movement model (has to press two or three buttons for every move) and overly limited sample storage -- a lot of time spent just managing samples.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, and truly worth the time. It may not be very long. I 100% it in around 8 hours, but I was hooked every single hour. Because the graphics aren't very detailed, it leaves a lot for imagination of how the creatures swim. In the taxonomy you can look at sketches of the creatures that you find, to better understand the creatures in the world. The only thing that is a bit on the negative side is that the game play is slow. This can be pleasant when exploring for the first time, however when you need to go all the way back to a station, it does take its time. With that said, still an amazing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect game if you liked the science-y bits of subnautica. I've never seen or played this type of game style before, but I absolutely love it. Very stress-free and story based, and I cried my eyes out at the end (simply because it was so beautiful, so human). Definitely recommend, especially if you need some hope for humanity.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece of storytelling. At its core it is a story of alien exploration and human hubris, paired with the obvious love for marine biology and taxonomy. The controls and graphics are extremely minimalist and while that made the story the main focus, at time it did make me feel like i was sorting grains of salt with a toothpick. At least until i got really invested in the story, an hour or two  into the gameplay. Once the story kicked off it was virtually impossible to let go. Even the more repetitive elements of the gameplay became enjoyable. Though as a former biologist I think i'm partial to the aloneness, the beauty and simplicity of nature, the meditative repetitiveness of research, and the internal monologue that this game packs.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I've just come back to this game, started back at the beginning and finished it. Honestly, this game deserves something stronger than a thumbs up. It's brilliant. It's a work of powerfully evocative minimalism. It derives a powerful sense of place from topographical maps and text. If you enjoy exploring, I really can't recommend it strongly enough.Original review:I'm still just getting started on this game but so far it's a pleasure. The game seems to deliver on expectations derived from promotional imagery and text. If you like what you're seeing on the Steam page, I'd say it's safe to go ahead and buy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simple and straightforward, very linear, and the story is a little slow. However, I am really enjoying it. The play style seems very unique and the detailed stories behind the world are so interesting I am constantly drawn in. If you don't need action or an open world to keep you interested, give In Other Waters a try!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to write a review after playing so little of a game, but this game was honestly such a snooze fest I could not stay awake long enough to play through much more. I can tell a lot of work went into the game, and it is made well. The idea for the game, however, is just fundamentally completely boring for me. Unless you are a HUGE fan of the point and click adventure genre, I would not recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit slow and tedious; spends too much time walking around. There's a lot of detail in this world and most of it is interesting. Everywhere you go there is a description of the place to help you imagine it, which is cool, but also necessary, as the graphics don't show much of the beautiful world it describes. But all of those descriptions get a bit tedious to read. Especially when you get to the parts where you are time limited and you want to read the interesting descriptions but have trouble separating them from the chaff. And it's tedious when you have to walk the same path three times because you want to get all of the samples but you keep running out of oxygen. If it weren't for the amount of time it takes to walk the same paths, I would have liked this game. But as it is, I'd rather play something a little more active.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and fun game that keeps you on the edge of your seat wanting to know the answers to the dozens of questions it gives you. You get answers for most of them, but not all of them. I won't spoil which ones. The UI and game concept are extremely novel. If you're like me, and game design is a hobby of yours, then you should find it very interesting and stimulating. The playtime is short — about 6 hours, played casually. Probably less than 3 or maybe less than 2 if you speedran it and didn't read anything. You definitely don't get an exhaustive 100% completion in that time, however. There's plenty of exploring, scanning, and gathering to be done, even after the narrative is completed, though there's no real motivation to continue doing so. I recommend buying during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first review ive written in years of being on steam, but this game is so low-key and so amazing that i just had to write one. So i was a backer on kickstarter for this game, and the premise alone sold me on this gem of a game. It's a fascinating experience getting to grips with an entire alien ecosystem, and your human copilot/partner. Especially since most of the time, you don't actually know what your human looks like, or any of the new alien species you're cataloguing, But seeing this little yellow dot zip around, and knowing that it's some sort of animal is... enchanting somehow. As the description says, the UI is great but it doesnt mention the soundtrack is perfect too, it has the right combination of awe and melancholy loneliness. But if you're worried its entirely slow chill, there's quite a few intense moments too. Overall there's just this amazing blend of wonder, isolation, ominous foreboding, and occasionally admiring some cute alien life. Highly recommend, truly a beautiful game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I would recommend giving it a look when you want to *read* through a game and have a relaxing experience that warrants your imagination.The protagonist is a xenobiologist who flew to a watery exoplanet because of a signal from an old friend, tries to uncover why they were called there and during it, researches and categorizes the local flora and fauna. You don't play as the protagonist though but as their diving suit, basically commanding their actions while on a diving trip.The graphics are very minimal, you don't see the world through the protagonists eyes but instead from above via a very basic topographical map on which you can see lifeforms as moving yellow dots. In your real life head though this world becomes more alive since the protagonist talks to you and describes everything they see in various detail. Because of that and since the controls are also very minimal - you click on waypoints, mark your paths, collect samples via a simple interface - I would describe the game as part as a visual novel. There are some puzzles though that demand you to use the samples you collect in various ways or use special functions of the diving suit.You can't die and I found the game to be extremely relaxing. The music is beautiful, with it being calm most of the time but also some more exciting pieces strewn in there if the plot demands it.I 100% it, meaning that I found every lifeform sample on the map and my save file states 9,5 hours. I was really slow though and especially if you only want to go through the main story, the game is beatable in 3-4 hours.The plot is nothing too special but I found it very fitting for the setting/atmosphere and got me quite intrigued in the second half.My sole criticism would be the controls, that can get tedious because it feels a bit more complicated than it needs to be. But if it would be even simpler, it would be even more a visual novel than game.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A very absorbing, engaging narrative point-and-click exploration game. Gameplay simply involves traversing through nodes with some points of interest and you might need to collect samples and use some of those to further proceed to impassable areas. There's a genuine feel of exploration and a sense of depth as you also have oxygen and energy levels to monitor. Don't be wary or distraught with the technical biological vernacular as most of these information are trivial, although you might need some imagination for some visual depiction. Some people might find it slow, but personally it still felt engaging with the pace.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This game is utterly delightful. An engrossing story wrapped in the exploration of an alien ecosystem. There is no combat (although some of the creatures will defend themselves in interesting ways), but you'll have to manage your power and oxygen levels as you explore and discover. The story had me hooked until the very end. If you're a fan of the kind of story Subnautica told, the gradual unveiling of intrigue, In Other Waters is right up your alley. The only criticism I had is that I found the controls to be difficult at first - I had to look up how to move around.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting experimental game that hints at a story that I would like to enjoy.Sadly the story is hidden behind a repetitive point, click, click again in another place, click once more, point and add some clicks because the UI wants them, then click through yet another slow reveal monologue based pointy clicky 'game'.Write the book. I'll read it. Just don't force me to sit through tedium to get to it, as you have here.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Once in a while, there is a game, a different game.Sometimes it has marvelous quests and dialogues.Sometimes it has best graphics you ever seen.And sometimes its something totally different, that catches you in it's grasp and you don't want to stop playing it.This game is In Other Waters, very simple concept of semi text based underwater emotional journey.But really got me is the exploration per se, imagining things you encounter, reading about them, cataloging, watching these points moving around and imagining real, alien life. I wish it was longer, I wish I could never stop playing it.Devs, I salute you, and I hope with enough budget you can make another one of those!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: as a marine biologist, i love this game. you have to use your imagination (if you dont purchase the accompanying sketchbook) but the game play and descriptive text really help build a fantastic world. it is an at-your-own-pace game that is great to play for a few minutes or an hour+. huge thank you to the creators for a lovely game. would be really cool if there was a companion game that you could play as the scientist.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Whatever qualities this game may have are undermined by some of the worst UI work I've experienced. Unresponsive and unexplained buttons and dials litter the screen, only becoming usable in certain situations, with zero feedback when interaction is possible. And even when you know what to do, every task is a laborious chore.Maybe worth it if you have a lot of patience to figure out what the game wants from you, but after about an hour with this I'm done.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: If any of the above: Takeaway from this game: , because you feel like an actual part of this wonderful world.What a damn  of a game. Blinding you with curiosity. I haven't felt this curious since Spore or Elite Dangerous (When i first started exploring...). Even Subnautica's curiosity excitement levels cut close to this! I was not even that interested in biology, (Until now! Crash Course on YouTube, here I come!).I do not think this is for everyone, but if you enjoyed reading explenations/research on "alien species" in any game, or if you have any interest in possible life on other worlds in our universe, this is  for you! The story is fantastic too, even though it's partially predictable! Describes my personally predicted outcome, of what will happen at one point, if/when humans expand into space.I thought this would be a chore, as I very seldomly find text-based games much fun, but this immerses you, and actually gives you that powerful wish to see this world with your own eyes. So, you end up doing the next-best thing. . And it filles you with such sense of awe and wonder.And that in turn, entrenches the story that is told here. It makes you care, because you feel like an actual part of this wonderful world.This is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ work of art like none other, that i have experienced throughout my 15 years of gaming, and arround 500+ games played throughout those years. _childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the aesthetic of this game (and the soundtrack, WOW). Although it does have rather limited actions for the player to take I found that that actually enhances the story aspect. You play as an AI (sort of - spoilers!) piloting a suit and it takes a lot of imagination to let this game take you away into the alien world. I had no problem with this, but I recognise the playstyle isn't for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Before playing, I was worried that the gameplay would be overly simplistic or boring. I was wrong. I got so invested into this world and I legitimately wanted to discover the wonderful life forms on this planet. I had my heart set on finding enough info on each species to unlock the sketch of them (beautifully done by the way!). There's no violent aliens, gameplay is not super intense and is more laidback, and it has a really great story that I loved.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A story game (80% story/atmosphere, 20% game) that give you just enough detail to spark your imagination to fill in the rest. The scene is described to you by your.... copilot... while you see essentially blips on a radar screen moving around. Super creepy/mysterious/evocative... Could have easily gone the route of horror, and I'm glad to say that it didn't. Instead, it embraces a sense of exploration and wonder. Definitely too slow-paced for some, requires a calm, curious mood to fully enjoy, but all in all is a fantastic experience worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautiful and thrilling mystery of a game.  I'm still playing through it but am loving the story and the game-play.  It's a refreshing change from anything else I've ever played and cannot recommend it enough!  Make sure if you play this that you have a quality sound system and you play it in a dark setting so you can truly get immersed into this experience, you'll understand.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I am normally not into these story driven-, text heavy kind of experiences – but In Other Waters really blew me away. The pacing is well done, and the writing breathes live into a simplistic representation of a rich world.The sound design is brilliant, and the game does an amazing job of making you feel the environment through the visuals, story text and sounds. The story is satisfying and rewarding to experience, and I can highly recommend giving it a play-through!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Not for everyone. If you liked reading Subnautica's PDA databank entries, learning about the behavior of animals, and interested in the flora and their biomes, buy this. The story revolves around a xenobiologist discovering and cataloging marine life; uncovering the ecology and history of the planet's ocean. Despite being minimalistic in design, the text beautifully paints the picture of a deep unknown world. Packaged with relaxing music and a story of exploration with well-written worldbuilding.ORIt could be the most boring game you'll refund in 30 mins. Check a gameplay video, you'll immediately know if this is for you or not.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game. I can't describe it any better than a narrative game with a stunning UI. A common technique in horror is to hide the scary thing until the very end since your imagination always makes something scarier than it could possibly actually be. This game does the opposite, it uses text descriptions to evoke a sense of wonder throughout. Somehow this game, with not a single 3D graphic in it's entirety, has evoked a greater sense of wonder about the ocean in me than almost any other. Imaginative, sweet and just gorgeous to look at and play through. I cannot recommend this game highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This game totally bored me. I spent almost half the time I played trying to figure out how to move... then spent the other half realizing that there wasn't anything worth finding. The dialogue was boring, the game is low res and low player control. Maybe this kind of thing might come off as a "relaxing experience" for others, but I need more to hold my interest. More action, more player freedom, or at least more visual impact. I won't be playing it again.

_childDocuments_.review: A deceptively simple looking game with a very simple looking interface and a simple premise. I didn't really bat an eye other than thinking it looked slick; however, very positive reviews are hard to ignore. I bought the game on a whim.6 hours later I had completed it. A relatively short experience. But an extremely rewarding one. What makes the game impressive is the fact that the simplistic interface isn't just a stylistic choice for styles sake, or for cheapness sake; but for storytellings sake.You play as an AI; who sees the world as a bunch of data, a bunch of nodes on a graph, a bunch of dots that occasionally move around. You get exactly the amount of detail your scanners allow you to see with exactly the bare minimum essential knowledge to function. You are accompanied by a human companion who is in the suit you are piloting around. And they can see everything that you cannot, while you can see everything that they cannot. As you play you depend on them to describe and portray the world around you; where you simply see dots they see the raw beauty of life in its finest of forms; and they want to document it.And as you play you become dependent on their descriptions; on their analysis of the life around them. The way they describe everything; it paints a picture. Combined with the music, this game tells an elegant and captivating tale of a mysterious world full of life. You played a game about navigating dots on a graph and managed to gain insight on a deep philosophical perspective in the process; that's no small feat.If the premise of this game sounds interesting; then this game is definitely not something to skip out on. Easily recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game that totally blindsided me. The story is expertly crafted to be both intriguing and impactful and serves as a message to those living now to be mindful of our effect on our environments. Through minimalistic design this game delivers to you a worthwhile experience that'll persist in your mind for many weeks after. The only downside perhaps is that now that it is over, I want more. More from the world, the characters, the story. I'm hoping they have some dlc planned as I would love to continue playing this game for many years to come.Thank you for creating this piece of art.

_childDocuments_.review: In Other Waters would best be described as having the base of a visual novel, but with some added interactivity. The majority of the game is rendered through text. Your interaction is helping a person move through an underwater environment. But you have a simplified interface. You help them move between set locations, and help them complete tasks at appropriate locations. The tasks become a bit more difficult and life threatening as they go on. Moving to a location gives a bit of a description of what is there.The story is interesting, and the interface is well designed, in that it feels like you really are part of the story, and part of the environment, despite not seeing anything. The atmosphere is well done, and I was absorbed in the game and setting.Unfortunately, a bit of the story is apparently in the art book. So it felt a bit incomplete. And the missing bit felt obviously missing, in that I wondered about key information and thought about whether I had missed something during the game, or whether I needed to do something after finishing. Also, despite the fact that every single point you can stop has a description of what is there, as the game goes on you start having to move more quickly and often without much of an opportunity to just sit somewhere forever. This means that the game is simultaneously giving you a reason to move on quickly, and also to stop and read some text. The game doesn't pause to give you a chance to read. And this move quickly imperative generally increases across the game. You don't really need good reflexes to get through anything, but you do have increases in tension and consequences. However, there is no real punishment other than redoing that bit. But the tension does make the ability to focus on descriptions decrease, unfortunately.I recommend In Other Waters. I can honestly say that I was immersed in the game.

And if our oceans die, so will we. We don't have the technology to abandon ship, nor a destination to go. Humanity is facing extinction at its own hands.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it, but I'm leaving a negative review because what started out as a very interesting story ended up as just another generic pessimistic sci-fi plot about humans killing everything. I've read this book before, and IOW doesn't meaningfully add to it. It doesn't even wrap up half the threads it had started before it went off on a galactic parasite tangent, and the final areas hardly even have new creatures for you to find. Scanning and cataloging new life was the entire point of the game before that, and it just forgets about it at the end. Additionally, the games mechanics clash with each other constantly. It wants to be a slow-paced visual novel where you click through an inefficient retro interface and read loads of textual descriptions of the environment, but it also repeatedly puts you in situations where your resources are depleting in real time. If you stop to read the text, you will run out of oxygen and die. If you don't stop to read the text, every part of the game looks the same and there's no atmosphere. I tried to compromise by quickly skimming the text, but it's hard to understand how something so obviously discordant made it into the final game. If you've played Subnautica already and want a very, very similar game in visual novel form, this is worth checking out. Just be prepared for some baffling design and a story that's almost completely predictable from the fact there's a mining corporation involved. Be more original, plot writers.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for a relatively small audience. I found it fun and worthwhile, but my recommendation comes with an asterisk. It is a visual novel with point & click elements and sweet but minimalistic graphics. If you pursue the exploration and discovery aspect of the game, you can unlock some cool sketches of the organisms, though. Science Focused Gameplay:Most of the game is reading about the various alien organisms on this new, strange planet Ellery* has discovered. This is not for everyone, and if you don't want to read about a scientist studying fungi and weird animals, this game is probably not for you. However, if you have an interest in biology, the descriptions are rather fascinating.*Note: You do not play as Ellery. Instead, you are a potentially sentient AI that lives in a diving suit. I think this is neat.Simple but Cute Story:The main story is short. Most of your time in this game is reading about the organisms and clicking around the map to collect samples. While the story is simple and straightforward, I still found it enjoyable. It's about a xenobiologist attempting to find her former colleague and figure out the secrets she had surrounding this planet. However, I do wish the conclusion to the story had a little more. It never really felt "wrapped up." You learn the reasons Ellery's colleague was on this planet, but it doesn't exactly have a resolution. The resolution is simply that you now know the reasons.Patience Is Key:Back to the "point and click" elements I mentioned at the start. While out diving (where you'll be 90% of the time), you are a dot on the screen. You switch between "scanning" which reveals points on the screen and clicking those points you just scanned to move or discovery creatures. It's hardly thrilling, but I don't mind it. It does, however, slow down the game. There is also a power and oxygen meter, but managing those is simple enough. It offers a little bit of tension at a couple moments, but frankly the game would have been the same in their absence.Overall, I give this about 7/10. It was short enough that the elements I didn't like did not overstay their welcome, but entertaining enough to be a satisfying play. If you are a patient biology nerd, then this is a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful digital artwork, and also a game of exploration.  It is not for everyone, and does take patience.  The UI is cryptic and a bit clunky-on-purpose to create a mechanical, dive-suit feel.  The story takes a while to build and becomes more engaging as you go on.  At first finding new lifeforms is a very slow process, but towards the end the descriptions and sketches of new animals and plants start to create a very detailed image of the environment being explored.  The very minimal interface can be hard to figure out and might be too plain for some.  If you enjoy reading and imagining sci-fi environments beyond what is shown on screen you will probably enjoy this.  I liked the story as well, which takes you through numerous types of ocean ecosystems and some remnants of human outposts as well.It can be hard to know quite what to do at times, and it's easy to forget how to use the different abilities if you don't play for a while and come back.  At one point I forgot that one of the icons was a propulsion mechanism and that was how to get to some new places.  Learning how to take samples from your suit inventory and analyze them in the lab is also somewhat cryptic.  For those who don't mind a slow, relaxed game that builds up gradually, there is a lot of reward here.  What you see is what you get graphics-wise, so don't go into this expecting photo-realistic environments or cinematic cutscenes.This will go in my favourites tab, easily.  No achievements but I actually kind of think that suits the meditative and peaceful nature of In Other Waters.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game. Short and bittersweet, with not much to do besides explore, discover, and catalog. It presented itself in a way I have never seen before. The visuals being nothing but topographic maps and various symbols is simple and yet still engaging. I definitely plan on buying the support visuals soon. The overall worldbuilding is fantastic and I cannot wait to learn more about all the organisms in even greater detail.

_childDocuments_.review: Never knew that In Other Water existed, but I'm glad that it's demo appeared on my Store feed when it did. I had been looking forward to it's release, and was quite satisfied with the full release.What I find attractive about the game is how it allows you to play at your own pace. Fully exploring the world isn't mandatory; you're free to focus on the main story and welcome to revisit old areas at your own time. How you wish to navigate yourself is up to you, and that freedom is what goes well with the exploration aspect of the game.The music was one of the highlights of this game, and I sometimes found myself enjoying the game on idle to listen to the soundtrack alone just as much as I was playing it. Mixed in with the ambiance of the ocean made for a relaxing experience.In Other Waters does lack voice acting, so be prepared to read. That may not be to your tastes, but I did find the texts and dialogues helpful in visualizing the alien ocean world of Gliese 667Cc. What the game lacks in "visuals" it make it up for allowing you to imagine yourself how an alien planet would look.I did have a few minor issues with the game. First is that the switch between scanner mode and movement mode can be cumbersome at times. The game requires you to scan new nods first before you can move to them, and that might be a bit frustrating to players who have to navigate through some of the more dangerous areas of the game where you need to keep your fuel and oxygen supply in mind. The second and last issue I had is that distinguishing between different, moving, organisms on your HUD can be difficult when they all appear as the same dots. There is one alien species in the game that moves around and can harm your character called the deep orrery. Though it moves slowly, it had caught me unaware when I mistook it for one of the harmless organisms. Maybe adding some visual difference in the dots would be helpful.All in all, I'm glad that this game popped up on my feed when it did.
