_childDocuments_.review: I didn't back this on Kickstarter.  Heard about it a couple months ago, and decided to buy it after it was released.  I played through it over the course of a week.  It took 8 hours, and I think I 100%ed it.  Anyway, I loved it.  You play as the nameless onboard AI of an advanced diving suit, used to explore an alien ocean.  You and your human "pilot", Ellery, navigate the sea-floor, collecting samples and seeking to understand the world you're on and the creatures that inhabit it.  In some places there are obstructions that rely on your understanding of the world to get past.  Don't expect a grand puzzle in the vein of Outer Wilds, though; for the most part, this is a narrative game, about the wonder of marine biology.  You and Ellery work as a unit, surrounded by bizarre alien fungi and shellfish, many of which have their own symbiotic relations, all part of a broader web.  Graphically, it's minimal; the game gives you lots of written descriptions of creatures, terrain, and phenomena, and expects you to associate them with the slowly undulating dots on-screen.  There are pictures, hand-drawn, of the many forms of life on the planet, but you only unlock them by completing data on a species.  In other words, you need to spend as much time as possible interacting with that species in other ways-- observing its behaviour, collecting samples, reading through your pilot's notes-- and only then do you get an artist's impression to compare with the one in your head.  This has the side-effect of taking the edge off of some of the uglier creatures; your pilot tends to describe them with wonder and admiration, even the ones that are just a mass of tissue and tentacle.  Each of the game's zones has a different look to it; some of these are immediately noticeable, while others are very understated.  The sound design is also quite good, with nearby features (and animals) slowly filtering in as you near them.  The sounds, like the descriptions and the behaviour of the dots, do an excellent job of evoking sea-life without just depicting it directly.  The game uses this point-to-point movement system.  This limits your exploration in a way I think is for the best; it allows for an expansive map, without letting the player waste time in an empty corner (and without encouraging the dev to fill the map up with crap to check off).  It also encourages the player to move slowly when moving into a new area, reading the point descriptions and really looking at the map.  I find that often, in open-world games, I end up just chasing icons on the minimap or compass, not engaging with the map in the way the designers intended.  This system would get tiring in a big game, but for something that goes for 6-8hr it's just perfect.  There's a lot of attention paid to the little details, here.  When characters speak, their text appears in time with the rhythms of actual speech, with pauses at commas and so on.  (To be clear, there's no voiced dialogue-- hey it's a one-man project-- but the textual dialogue is done in the most natural-feeling way possible).  The music is very relaxing, and sombre when it needs to be; sometimes it blends with the conversation, with tones sounding in time with your responses.  The encyclopedia entries for a newly-discovered species can be uncovered in different orders, but are written in such a way that neither one feels like the wrong order.  I found the UI easy to use.  There are a few elements you could call clunky; I would call them "deliberate".  Activating the blow-torch takes two clicks instead of one; this makes it feel like a bigger deal, like you're handling a dangerous tool, which shouldn't be flicked on and off like a lighter.  The movement system forces you to go slowly through new areas, but, well, you SHOULD go slowly through new areas.  (Moving through old areas is a bit clunky until you learn the hotkeys, at which point it gets way easier).  The only element I don't like is the storage bay, which tends to fill up with used-up samples.  I wish it were easier to organise, so that I could separate the useful stuff for long trips.  Anyway, it's great.  Be aware that you've got to read a bunch, and to use your imagination to enhance the graphics.  In another game, that might be a copout, but here it's the whole point of the exercise.  It does exactly what it set out to do, and it's not really like anything else I've played before.  I think it'll stick with me for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game, mostly peaceful exploration using a simple UI and a lot of text that tells an intriguing story without feeling too much like a Text Adventure Dungeon Crawl.  I had some frustrations with the UI.  Mostly the lack of access to the main map when on a dive.  And sometimes I felt like I was missing the text/story because I was rushing to use the UI to avoid more resource depletion.  But those are minor gripes.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful, atmospheric game about soothing oceanic exploration and collecting bio-samples. The game mechanics are innovative and interesting, but might therefore not be for everyone. Over all, it's an enjoyable experience about speculative biology that I recommend to people who aren't adverse to reading.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A very atmospheric exploration game into alien waters. If you love text-based adventures, In Other Waters will sweep you along in its tale of a xenobiologist searching for her missing lover. I loved traversing the ocean, exploring every corner and path I could find. The methodical gameplay is very calming. I had a few nitpicks with the game. I would have liked a map available whilst out in the field and the ability to drop pins on interesting sights. For a game about meticulously recording every detail, you have to do a rather good deal but memory. If you're looking for a hard science fiction game then I wholeheartedly recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it was made specifically for me. A game about marine biology on an alien world. In Other Waters is a perfect game to chill out with and experience its short (took me about 8 and a half hours to 100% it) but beautiful and incredibly well written story. The writing really is the games strongest point. Since you play a suit AI and are unable to see the environment the character is moving in through direct vision, instead relying on a rough topographical map and sonar, the game relies on the descriptions given by the main character to convey what this alien ocean looks like. The descriptions are vividly detailed but not overly long winded, you can really put your imagination to work trying to picture how this world and its organisms might look. What really impressed me was how believable the ecosystems and organisms are. Each one has a fully realised function within its ecosystem, clear evidence of symbiosis, parasitic relationships, and truly wondrous ideas for unique relationships between the organisms and how their bizarre alien biology and functions might affect their environment and the other organisms living around them. In Other Waters is a gem of a game absolutely worth buying for those interested by the concept. It's very niche for sure, but as someone who fits that niche almost too perfectly, I had a brilliant time with it and would recommend it highly.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game.It is a beautiful experience to take part in.Don't be discouraged by the simplicity of the gameplay, that actually frees the player's mind to fully embrace the alien reality they are presented with, and works beautifully to unite the player with the game in a way i've never seen done ever before.It's amazing what this game accomplishes with just yellow lines, dots and some words!A must!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: If you have the patience, this game will totally capture you.The screenshots looked neat and the reviews were good, so I gave it a try. I'm very much glad I did! You need to have a bit of aptience at the start, to really give it a chance. The main gameplay loop might feel tedious at the start, but at some point the game will really capture you through it's atmosphere (set up by some amazing sound design btw) and it's story. Weird to think that all is needed is some music, sound fx, text, and color shifts in a neat AI.If you've told me I would feel about this game as I do now back when I didn't purchase it yet, I'd think you'd be crazy. But this game actually feels really nice and plays quite well. You just need some patience and a little appreciation for the minimalist approach.This game is definitely not for everyone, but if an interesting story and some proper storytelling is also you need, then this will suffice as a neat little experience.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In Other Waters is a fantastic text adventure that really immerses you in its world. The writing, atmospheric soundtrack and "scanner interface" really bring the story to life! You won't get swept away by the visuals (what you see in the preview screenshots is what you get) but don't let that stop you from giving this gem a try. I was so captivated I actually ended up playing it through in one session.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game with an absolutely genius UI. I really loved going on my dives, slowing down and appreciating everything around me. The game graphics is very minimalistic which makes the hyperrealistic drawings stand out even more. As a biologist myself I loved the story, the exploration and the catalogization of the fauna and flora in this game!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant exercise in minimalism to tell a characterful story in a vibrant world you can only visualise through dots and lines on a radar. Told entirely through a UI styled after a small handful of deep sea equipment, it does wonderfully atmospheric work with its evocative use of seabed imaging and ambient sound design. The narrative itself is fairly rote, but told through a lens so new to me I couldn't help but be enthralled to the end.Come the midpoint of the game, I found my play cycle and just coasted to the finale with little to no obstruction. Something about how this and games like Killer7 throw an abstract control scheme onto your lap - then expect you to figure it out on your own, is great to me. When it clicks, it's always pretty special.I dunno, pretty short but really interesting. I enjoyed my time with it, and lament that I don't have much more to spare. I'd love to get all the collectables, would be zen as hell.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautiful game, painting a vivid picture of an alien biosphere concealing a compelling mystery.While the game is largely text-based, I found that the minimalist node-based GUI and light resource management added a LOT to the experience - you'll need to use a bit of imagination, but it's well worth it.I also heavily recommend the artbook DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: The main character is a biologist that thinks fungus needs photosynthesis to grow.  I'm serious.  Most of writing is just as shockingly bad.The game tries to have an environmental message, but ignores the fact we can carve off pieces of wildlife and use them as fuel.  Certain lifeforms can also be used as improvised explosive devices to clear blockages to let us pass.I wish I were joking.Other bad things:  the text auto advances, and there's dialogue choices that also auto advance if not selected quickly enough.  But don't worry, because they don't actually matter or affect anything.  The store description mentions forming a bond with the main character... I don't even know if she has a character, aside from asking us if we know what we're doing when we respond to her SOS at the beginning.  She's unlikable, judgemental, and nags.  She'll start talking to you (remember the timed dialogue?) while you're reading something.  You'll want to drive her into a wall, but there is no death.  You have oxygen and power meters, but if they run out there's an override that brings you back to the last checkpoint...  How do you override an empty battery or oxygen tank again?I liked some things about the game.  Many people complain about the interface and the controls, I thought they were fine.  I liked the aesthetic, and the minimalist look.  The sound design and music were usually good, and occasionally great.  The ideas behind the story are good, I just wish the story (or its implementation) was as good as the ideas themselves.  ...That's it for the good things.  :/Basically, the game looks neat but is so poorly written that I didn't want to explore or read the text.  In a game that is almost completely text!  Save your money.  If you're curious, watch someone else play it.[Edit]  Currently going through again to see how the different dialogue choices play out (they don't really), and encountering some really WEIRD bugs where loading the game simultaneously loads the opening and messes up your save file.  I've had to restart several times.  As long as you don't save during dialogue or the intro section you should be fine.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. I really like the way its played and the story. Its an interesting concept and well executed. If you don't like environmentalism, xenobiology, the ocean, and collection this game may not be for you. My only complaint is the post game is anticlimatic, I found everything and then like. Nothing. No dialogue from the main character or anything. Ik its in the book but I feel like the game needs a bit more closure.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played Subnautica and wondered what it would be like to be the AI thats helping the main character, instead of actually BEING the main character, thats exactly what this game is.  More or less.  Incredibly minimal graphics lead to an added sense of awe and mystery about the ocean and its life on this secret planet you find yourself on.  Lots of exploration and some minimal puzzle solving lead to an incredibly satisfying experience.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing and... different. Enjoying it so far; the music fits it well, and the purposely slow-ish game play works well while relaxing doing other things. That said, I can't help but imagine what this would be like as a VR game where you're in a sub instead of a suit. THAT would have been incredible. Perhaps a sequel? ;)
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Many visual novels suffer from the experience of forcing you to click through trivialities with little more going on than 2D pop-up characters. In contrast, In Other Waters combines a lean, well-written story line focused on dialogue with an exploration game that creates the space to imagine what the protagonists are actually seeing. Once you get the hang of the mechanics, this little gem of a game tells a thought-provoking, brisk story that takes you deep into a mind's-eye view of alien depths teeming with life. Highly recommended as a way to spend 4-6 hours beneath other waters.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I have been absolutely loving this game because it's so peaceful and I love exploring. The story is fun but just the mechanics of exploring a new area and finding all the samples and wildlife is a great premise for a game. The music is also wonderful! If I had to offer a critique it might be that the game is great as is but could use better graphics by the developer to be even more immersive. Maybe pictures of the characters would help. I would love to have some sort of water or plant/animal animations. Still, it's a fun game I will likely replay.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Explore an alien ocean world and search for a missing mentor who is actually so much more. Enjoy narrative games with mystery? The awe of being in wilderness? Learning strange new things about biology*, ecology*, and geology*? Atmospheric synth music? Abstract interfaces in two-toned neon color? It's all waiting for you In Other Waters. It's intriguing, poignant, and teeming with surprises. *The fiction is more science-flavored than anything. The game's xenobiology is very loosely construed with only the stylings of research methods (sample analysis, hypothesized taxonomies). I sometimes get annoyed that samples can be "20% fungus 10% root" etc and many different things are called "spores" that have wildly different relationships to the organisms or colonies that shed them. But its conceptual fumbles and anachronisms are more than worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful unique game with a perfect soundtrack and some of the best use of UI I have seen. Taking the game slow makes it more enjoyable and relaxing, even for someone who hates the ocean... Would recommend to anyone wanting something different in a good way. It took me about 9 hours to complete. The game does not feature any fast pace gameplay or action.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: What is In Other Waters like? It's like reading a relaxing sci-fi book about a marine biologist on an exoplanet. There isn't much gameplay, per se. But the immersive synth soundtrack washes over you and pulls you in. It is a nice world to get lost in for a few hours.Some threads of the story aren't fully explored and left me wanting more. I won't go into them because spoilers. Gameplay-wise too, there was some tedious backtracking required to collect all the samples.But overall, I am glad that this game exists and want there to be more like it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to describe, in the best way.Mechanically, it is very interesting. One of the most minimalist set of controls and graphics that I have ever seen. The premise of being an AI, navigating the water along with your scientist companion, unable to see but vicariously experiencing the native flora and fauna? Fantastic and unique. It is almost closer to a text adventure.To me, the presentation makes for a unique and gripping story, dealing with lost love, mystery, the exploitation of nature by capitalism, and most of all, curiosity and hope. And I found many times that it was easy to slip into the mindset of the AI, following along with the struggles of our scientist. At many times, I found myself in situations where I was nearly out of resources, but there was still much more to explore, yet I held back and got to safety, just because I felt protective of "my human".The mechanic of scientific discovery was fantastic. Being the science nerd that I am, I eagerly gulped up each new entry on the taxonomy of the various species we had encountered. The game did not need to go that hard into biology, but I am exceptionally grateful that it did.Only a few downsides. First, I was able to accidentally sequence break a few times, resulting in getting events and messages out of order. It only happened a few times, however.Second, sometimes it can be a bit tedious tracking down all the samples required to complete entries for certain creatures. Doing so is not required to beat the game, but if you want to see everything, it is a small factor.My 100% playthrough took about 7 hours, which is a sweet spot for this type of game. Able to focus on the core mechanics and themes, while not overstaying its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a really interesting take on underwater settings. While the method of transportation can sometimes feel a bit restrictive, I didn't once miss the first person perspective or fancy graphics of similar games like Subnautica. The text based adventure leaves a lot to your imagination but the vivid descriptions of objects and locations are far above average for the genre. Overall the game played well although it would have been nice to have more hotkeys and settings for things like audio. I would recommend to anyone who enjoys adventure, environmental storytelling, and the underwater environment.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: - Not really much to look at. It kind of looks like a webpage with too much JavaScript or an overdesigned Tableau dashboard- Luckily, the music is very good. Very chill stuff that'll help you relax- I don't really want to spoil too much of the story because it's the biggest thing it's got going for it. Suffice it to say, it's quite an interesting sci-fi narrative with lots of intrigue- Beyond the main plot, the game is very exploration-based, with an impressive amount of imaginative and detailed science fantasy to learn about- The game is incredibly relaxing in spite of the occasionally stressful plot points- Gameplay mostly involves clicking on location dots and reading. Beyond that, you occasionally have to collect samples, run some of your submarine's movement systems, or disperse materials into the water around you- In spite of the amount of time you spend exploring, you'll also find yourself going back to your base to further the story and do science- I really loved the story, the exploratory gameplay, minimalist visual design, and music. Just understand that the pacing may be too slow and the gameplay a little too sparse for some tastes- Given the lack of things happening on your screen, you shouldn't expect much trouble running the game- . If you're looking to just chill out, wander an exoplanet's océan, and read a good story, this game will scratch an itch
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A really unique game. The main mystery is intriguing, but what's most special about it is the details of the multiple different alien ecosystems within the game. They feel so realistic and use fascinating, unexpected mechanisms - I didn't know I would get so interested in this alien biology. The visual style of the game is great and the music complements it really well.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Pictures and reviews of the game will not help you make a decision. This game is far more than what it shows. If you want to have a deep meaningful experience, this game is for you. It will give you a sense of discovery and wonder like no other game (except Outer Wilds). So if swimming in an alien ocean and discovering and working out the behaviours of alien organisms sound in any way interesting to you, do not hesitate to buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Its alot of reading.And not alot of visual excitement.It is just like reading a book, but you (at least I did) feel pressured into rushing through because of the energy and oxygen getting used up. So I end up trying to push through, finding resources and not read alot of the text, resulting in not really getting anything out of the atmosphere that so many people talk about.You can't see the creatures or the environment. It's all just elevation maps and dots (representing vegetation and creatures), while reading what those dots ACTUALLY look like.Not a game for me, but maybe for someone who is a fast reader and enjoys making up the world in their mind, since the dev couldn't be bothered to actually bring it to life.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Very atmospheric game, the music and sounds draw you in as you play and slowly learn about the world. The user interface is unique and seems very simplistic at first but once you are used to it you can easily visualise the alien world and its life around you. More visual novel than  game, but there is enough for the user to do that it's not just a read-a-thon. Recommended if you want a nice game to escape to for a little bit.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This game reawakened the Massive ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Nerd in me, dormant since I stopped playing Subnautica. The artstyle is nice, music and sound design is great, gameplay's pretty good, and I really like the story.One big downside- the bugs. This game is weirdly buggy given how simple it is. Thankfully most of these bugs fall in the buttons-not-working-momentarily category instead of being crashes or softlocks or anything like that.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A bit late, but there are four overall good things that I want to say about this game:- It's enchanting -- despite the simplicity of the UI (or perhaps because of it), you can definitely imagine what's going on.- It's detailed -- the world is interesting, and the species more so.- It's calm -- you need to take your time with it.- It's good.The downside:- I'd tweak the story slightly at the end. Possible spoilers, so I won't say anymore.- - UI is not the optimal, but it works for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In my 8-ish years of buying games from Steam, I've never written a review before. This game resonated with me so strongly that I just had to put in the effort this time. If you are someone like me that has always related more to machines, yearned for an ambiguous form and the opportunity to carry out tasks for someone else, then this game is for you. It scratches that perfect itch for me, that feeling like I'm doing a good job, keeping someone safe and happy. Aside from my deep inner feelings on the matter, the game is gorgeous. The UI is simple but aesthetically pleasing, colors shifting as you move from each area to the next. It really gives the sense that you're an Artificial Intelligence, processing the world in the only way you can. The elaborate descriptions, dialogue, and sound design fills in the details you lack visually. The music is a soothing, flowing ambience, or an eerie buzz depending on the area and the atmosphere of the scene. Amos Roddy did an amazing job on the soundtrack. Without spoiling anything, the story is excellent as well. Its message is important, its theme hopeful, each word carefully picked in a way that clearly shows the developers' love for the world they created. For biologists, AI enthusiasts, or people that just want a beautiful, calming experience, I highly recommend In Other Waters.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This is a VN disguised as a more traditional game. You mostly just click to move along nodes on an invisible web with the occasional requirement to use an item as a key or to refill your (generous) energy/air meters, so the main reason you'll be doing things is for the writing.There are a couple sections where you're forced to move too frequently to be able to read the text, but none of the text in these sections is especially important. There's an optional research mechanic that involves scanning creatures in the world and then gathering items for research samples, which unlocks entries in the taxonomy database including speculation and sketches by the partner character. Considering that as an AI with sonar for eyes you don't actually see anything personally, these flesh out the world nicely, though some of them can be a pain to get.The writing quality is high but the actual story's just OK. I thought I predicted where it was going, then it went in a completely different direction that was still ultimately extremely standard. It's a bit heavy handed with its aesop considering that it's not terribly difficult to come up with alternative interpretations of the evidence that run completely contrary to it, provided you don't take the partner character's interpretations as gospel. Given that the partner character performs an action halfway through the game that would be downright stupid in almost any other sci-fi game (especially in context with recent events IRL) and tries to guilt-trip you if you discourage this, it's not particularly unlikely that you'll start doubting them.Ultimately I'm still recommending it because I don't feel my time was wasted and the moment to moment quality is high even if the ultimate destination is unimpressive, but I also am unlikely to play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In Other Waters is an exploration game set underwater on an alien planet. You control the ship as you work together with a scientists, only 'seen' through text, as you explore the strange world, find new life forms, and find out the mystery of the planet.It is a very slow game with minimalist graphics, which works really well in this case. The majority of the gameplay is slowly moving the ship from waypoint to waypoint, scanning everything in sight in between.I thoroughly enjoyed the about 7 hours I spent on this as the story is well written and the game embraces the minimalist UI and other limitations.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Masterful storytelling via interactive adventure.  This game is for readers and while the UI can become a little cumbersome, I didn't mind because I looked forward to the description of every node and very much appreciated how the story and game progressed to make it even more and more interesting.  The usefulness of the samples in a variety of scenarios added another layer of fun requiring you to plan a small load-out before hitting certain areas on the map.  Don't get this game for a highly graphical experience.  The game interface itself just felt more like a fancy 'turning the pages' interface for the story, with interesting color pallets and beautiful ambient sound and music.  They story was incredibly unique and the illustrations were my favorite things to hunt for and unlock in order to FINALLY get a look at these very simplistic icons on your radar map.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I discovered this after having finished Citizen Sleeper, which is my Game of the Year for 2022. In Other Waters shares a lot in common with Citizen Sleeper, but is a first title and definitely is a more paired down experience. The entire game is played through a futuristic computer UI and involves exploration of this alien sea and talking with your pilot. There is no character art and you never see anyone, it's all just dialogue and subtle environmental storytelling. The excellent writing, sound and music will immerse you in the world, even with the minimal graphics and interaction, telling a poignant and sad, yet hopeful story.You can mainline the story and it will only take you a few hours, or you can spend several more to 100% things if you want. I really enjoyed this and between this and Citizen Sleeper, this developer clearly has some major chops and I look forward to what they release next.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In Other Waters is the horniest game ever and it literally has nothing to do with sex or kink. You play as the AI controlling a scientist's suit on an alien planet. You can only communicate with vague affirmatives or negatives and only when directly addressed and the scientist is just giving you orders to follow the whole time. In between expeditions, there's language about how you (the AI) were offline or upgraded and I just-It's a horny game, is all I'm saying.On the other hand, if you're *not* a degenerate like me, you should probably still play it, because it's legitimately beautiful. The sound design is amazing, which is really good given that as an AI, you can't really *see* the world you're exploringAlthough as you research alien life forms, the scientist in the suit you control documents and describes everything wonderfully, and once your research is complete, you're rewarded with a scientific sketch which is really nice and helps to visualize all the new life you've been learning about.

_childDocuments_.review: even though i give this game a thumbs down that doesnt mean that this game was a bad time for me in fact i thoroughly enjoyed my play through of the game so far even though i have yet to finish it. if the developer is reading this, i want to say good job making this game in particular with the colors used in this game which made it beautiful to look at. _childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite a lovely game. I highly recommend it. It's simple graphics are designed to make you use your imagination as you read the little descriptions of each nook and cranny you can explore. It is a short-ish game I played for 14 hours took my time and am finished with the game but 88% done with the taxa...so some could argue I'm not finished, but the plot of the story has been satisfyingly resolved. For fans of thoughtful peaceful game play. Almost pure exploration. Very entertaining. Really liked the mellow music as well.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so relaxing and fun at the same time. As someone who doesn't like danger elements but still a bit of a challenge, In Other Waters was perfect for me! I also loved how the game is super accessible and easy to navigate for players like myself that are not as familiar with WASD key controls or hand controllers. _childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A game about ecology, symbiosis, what we are, and what we can aspire to.You are a mysterious advanced AI system piloting a robotic dive suit. You are awoken by a biologist exploring a little known planet with the first extraterrestrial life ever found. Together, you explore the ecosystems of the planet and uncover the interrelations of its species by observing their behavior and collecting biological samples. Across about 10 hours, you collect enough data to understand the relationships between the various lifeforms you encounter, as well as the biological history of the planet (including previous encounters with humanity).There isn't all that much "gameplay" to speak of. You move between nodes on a world map, collecting resources which can be used either to refuel or restore O2, or for some light puzzle-solving features. Neither the resource management nor the "puzzles" are particularly complex. The game is mostly a text adventure with a beautiful UI and soundtrack to navigate from point to point, gathering more and more information on the new and wondrous species of the planet.There is also a conventional story undergirding your exploration, with characters, mystery, conflict, and resolution. Its themes reinforce what, to me, is the core draw of the game: Exploring a beautifully rendered portrait of an imagined ecosystem replete with fascinating interrelationships based loosely on analogues found on Earth, with some sci-fi twists. Every new lore dump received by analyzing a sample in your lab is exciting, most of all for the picture of the alien environment as a symbiotic and organic whole that begins to emerge the more mysteries you uncover.Above all, it is a game worth playing because it is a message of environmental hope set against environmental catastrophe. It is the polar opposite of the modern craze of survival games, in which the objective is to transform a hostile environment to suit your needs through domination. In this game, you do not chop down coral reefs to build a new weapon, building an ever greater economy which comes to dominate your map. Instead, you are invited to admire what exists in nature as you study it, and called to protect what is already there, inviting you to come live with it.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: There is no rating high enough to express my satisfaction n joy with this game. The concept is exceptionally well done, the world building is fantastic, the gameplay is thoughtful and pretty easy to grasp. The story is short, but honestly? I think id pay 25 dollars for this game now that I know how good it is. I just finished the main story, but I have so many species to finish researching. I'm looking forward to exploring the world that Jump Over the Age has made. In the hours iv played it, it's become my favorite story game ever. If you love the sea, and are the nerdy sorta person that loves reading about species and environments, or even just love a mystery story, consider getting the game.There ARE a few gripes from other reviews that I can relate with though. For a game based on a cartography presentation, we really dont get enough map tools. I was able to make my way through the game and have fun with what we were given, but more functional features like marking locations, charting long distance paths, etc, would have been nice. Second, while the story (in my opinion, grain of salt here) is good, its cliche. The story is predictable for those who've immersed themselves in these types of story genres. So for those people looking for a very nuanced story, I don't think this is it. Its a good story, dont get me wrong. I loved it to death, but even I as a newly made fanboy can agree it didnt have a ton of depth (feel like theres a pun to be made here somewhere). A lot of the appeal of this game hinges on the player coming into it with a love of marine biology, the ocean, preservation/researching, and other related topics. This game is in some ways more of a loveletter to those ideas than a particularly thrilling story. But, that being said, I still enjoyed it. If you wanna try a fun game with a cool theme n a neat (tho somewhat predictable) story, pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A hauntingly beautiful story about ecology, conservation and queer love. I'm a sucker for excellent worldbuilding, and this game is nothing but worldbuilding, exploring and cataloguing a brand new alien ecosystem - all seen without any actual visuals, only your sensors and the (remarkably detailed) descriptions your pilot narrates. Emotional stories featuring artificial intelligence are very much my jam too, and it's a novel and delightful experience to be playing  an AI, assisting the person who would normally be the protagonist. I think the game gains a lot from it: Ellery isn't just a self-insert for the player, she's a full and complete character in her own right, and you get to uncover her story as you uncover the secrets of the planet.I really can't recommend this game enough, and I wish there were more like it. The closest I can think of is Heaven's Vault, which I'd also recommend to anyone who played and enjoyed this.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly engaging and thought provoking game. Its at its best when making you feel like a engineer as you press buttons and coordinate actions as you explore the map and learn about its secrets. There is some room for improvement here and there, and the amount information can be often overbearing, but definitely a worthwhile experience I recommend giving a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: this game is really good; get it if you are into scifi, if you like reading and imagining things on your own, or if you want to check an incredibly well executed game.Overall, this game is really well made: the story is really well told, the soundtrack is gourgeous, the gameplay was quite nice and the execution was incredibly good, imho.So, the graphics are quite simple in this game, and for me that worked really well. The game uses a top-down eprspective, and you have to scan pretty much everything to get a description; the landscape is quite well drawn (as level curves) in the map, but everything else is dots. Though it might sound strange, that worked really well for me.I really enjoy reading (books and whatnot) and imagine things on my own, so I enjoyed picturing the creatures and the environment details in my head. In fact, this made the process of collecting data about the creatures much more enjoyable, as each scan reveals just a tiny bit about their behavior, and you can picture them better as you advance. After you collect additional samples, you can unlock a hand drawing of the creature in your database -- and it was quite nice to look and admire them.After a few days playing, I found that this "observation practice" translated to my daily life. I often find myself watching more carefully the plants and bugs in my house.As a side note on imagining things, I have played (and loved) Subnautica before, and I guess that made it a lot easier. If you haven't, then I guess watching a few random moments of deep sea documentary or random Subnautica gameplay would be really helpful.The soundtrack is chill, and pretty good. It sets the mood pretty well to all moments in the game.The execution is really good. The time mechanics are very well done. As someone who studied a bit of game dev, it was an amazing example of how things should come together naturally to tell the story to the player in a way that is fun and enjoyable.I am amazed how much fun this game was, it will be among my longstanding favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A deep, mysterious and imaginative story told within a beautiful game. The text-based narrative is paced out expertly by the calm, simple and methodical gameplay, which presents enough 'gentle challenges' to keep you thinking and engaged throughout. Your moment to moment decisions to move and interact with the world in different ways all edge you closer to understanding the strange ecosystems that surround you, and these slowly build towards uncovering the wider secrets of the world's past.If you are curious, dive in without a second thought.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, I loved getting immersed in the beautiful oceanic world. The storytelling was moving and wonderful. Highly recommend to others who love story-based games. The mechanics are smooth, but a little slow paced. Luckily the map isnt huge so you don't feel that frustrated. Lots of reading, especially with the taxonomy. I think it's very interesting though, a nice science lesson. :))
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: The story is interesting enough, but honestly there is very little story compared to how much botanical descriptions of everything. If you want to read an encyclopedia about xenobiology, then this game is for you, if you don't then you are in the wrong place my friend.Worth around $10 if you like this kinda game
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for ALMOST 8 and a half hours straight. As the MC, you are the AI of a marine xenobiologist's divesuit, exploring the waters of an alien world and discovering the secrets there. I was so deeply compelled by this game. It's quite simple, but it's just so beautiful. The themes. the heart of it. It leaves you wanting more. _childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Really lovely game. Mechanically it's fairly simple, I found it quite relaxing. The fun is mostly driven by exploration and discovering new species. The story delivered more than I expected. If you played and enjoyed Tacoma, you'll enjoy this too.The soundtrack and ambiance are gorgeously on point, and the minimalist visual style still serves the story very well.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Really lovely game for a quiet rainy day. Not necessarily for everyone - this is a slow, contemplative experience that lives or dies by your curiosity about the world - but it's really beautiful and atmospheric. I really love the ecosystem that the dev created. Word of advice - I started with a controller (thinking it better for leaning back for a relaxed session) and found the controls a bit awkward and frustrating. I found this game to play much better with a mouse and keyboard.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A very different immersive experience. Requires patience, certainly, but steady progress is made and you are gradually drawn into the story. In fact, you are AI and learn about several different life forms within this fictional world as you proceed. This is for those who want a novel and beautiful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: In Other Waters is a slow but immersive game similar to a walking simulator on rails or an interactive fiction game with minimalist graphics. The game has an impressive 70s sci-fi soundtrack by Amos Roddy and will keep you engaged with an intriguing story that should appeal to environmentalists, biologists and sci-fi fans in general.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim during a Steam sale while looking for some indie games that would be relaxing to play after another terrible day at work. This game checks all the boxes I look for in a game. Gameplay is story driven and relies on scientific curiousity, betrayal, intrigue and beauty to move the plot along. It also made my feel feels at different points throughout the game.On first glimpse, I was underwhelmed by the graphics. Then the more I played, the more I fell in love with the simplicity and the beautiful, mesmerizing colors of the graphics. Different colors alert you to potential dangers to your character. Different regions have their own color scheme, their own unique dangers and creatures to discover. All of these factors combined allowed me to suspend my disbelief throughout the entire game. Also, I still can't figure out what 10% I'm missing from my taxonomy.I would really like to see a Part II of this.  I am hoping the developer opens up another Kickstarter for either a Part II or even to add the nursery upgrade.Great job Gareth Damian Martin! Thank you for giving me 9.3 hours of scientific investigation spurred on by curiosity, a great soundtrack and getting me a little emotional and teary-eyed at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly immersive despite the simplicity of the format, and if you're into taxonomy, this game perfectly captures the experience of classifying species in a team on the field. The writing is impeccable and worked with the soundtrack to create a great atmosphere.The speed of movement could feel slow at times, especially if you lose your way, but since it's more story- than gameplay-heavy, it's a more sit-down type of game. 100%-ing the taxa really rewarded you too, which was great, since more information about the species you classify will be available.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I liked the game, mostly because I found it relaxing. It has an immersive story, a soothing soundtrack, and atmospheric visuals. I would recommend it to anyone who wants to experience a short story about exobiology and humankind. There is not really much replayability, and once you finish the story, the game becomes less engaging. The story itself is short (~5-6 hours of playtime) and not especially deep or complex. The controls could be better, as right now, there is a lot of unnecessary clicking or key pressing just to move forward.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I personally had a wonderful time with this game, however, it is definitely not for everyone. If I had to describe it in the context of other games, it has the character interaction of Firewatch, the gameplay mechanics of a point and click adventure and the setting of Subnautica. If that piques your interest, I would definitely check this game out, if not, I'd give it a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game! Simple, but at the same time interesting gameplay, rich lore and incredibly atmospheric soundtracks accompanied me all the time while I was playing this game. The plot is intriguing and exciting, allowing you to complete the game almost in one go. I really liked all aspects of this game, it's beautiful!I want to say a huge thank you to the authors of the Game, as well as to all the people involved in its birth!
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing text-based walking simulator where you play as a xenobiologist (or rather the AI that controls her diving exosuit) searching an alien ocean planet for her missing friend. The game isn't an ambitious game and never strived to be. It's just a nice contained little narrative experience, nothing more, nothing less. It's really enjoyable in today's age, where every new game wants to be the next breakthrough in the genre and promises hundreds of hours of content. You can finish this game (100%) in around five hours.There's not much to do in the game except go from point A to point B and click on the new organisms that you find in order to learn more about them, and yet the game still remains fun and intriguing. I always went a little bit further to try and discover what is happening to the xenobiologist's friend and what is causing the  .The simple yet polished graphic design really does a heavy lifting for the game's aesthetic and really makes you feel like you're a machine scanning the ocean floor and analyzing samples. This minimalism also forces you to use your head and the light descriptions the game gives you to imagine what the planet and its ecosystem looks like, which I think gives a lot of whimsical wonder to the game and the world it takes place in.Talking about the ecosystem: the setting of the game is also one of its greatest point. Speculative biology and creature design is one of my favourite part of worldbuilding. The creatures are radically different from what we could find on Earth, yet they still feel believable and linked in the environment they live in like a real animal would. It really manages to make you feel like this planet is truly alien even though you only see dots and lines on the screen. My favourite part of the game was discovering those new critters and how they lived in the new biomes that I found. That might just be a biology major alien nerd thing, but I'm so glad to be able to feel true scientific curiosity in a game.The main character feels like a xenobiologist. She's curious, she explores, she wants to know stuff. We understand why she wants to go through so much and go even deeper (literally) to learn what happened to her friend and the planet.The story is pretty straightforward, and while not really being the most original, I think it's rather well-executed. I really enjoy the anti-capitalist and anti-exploitation themes that the developer puts in their games. The sci-fi genre really needs these kind of messages.The music is made by Amos Rody and (as usual) freaking slaps. It's so relaxing and atmospheric, you can put it in your work playlist.I really recommend this game if you don't have a lot of free time to play games or if you really like xenobiology. It's just a nice game, and though it might not blow your mind away, it's just relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: marine biologist on an alien planet simulator. fun concept, really good story and great music. it's fairly short but i think that it works well with the pace of the game and it doesn't overstay where other games would force you to grind for a while. main gripe is that the 100% ending doesn't do too much, but its still a great game nonetheless.

By a not recommended I don't want to discourage anything in the developer who made it, as the premise was really interesting enough to try it.Unfortunately, the game description should have mentioned that all feedack we will have is actually text-based, and even more, should have hinted that we will see the text dialogue of the protagonist mention colors and scenes that we will never even get a glimpse...  or a feeling of.Immersion and the mystery of these discoveries were completely destroyed for me. I don't think it needed anything more than mysterious abstract forms or dynamic additional content of any sort ; but what we get broke and limited the atmosphere a lot, as we read someone's short cues about things and these things are represented almost nowhere; as the other yellow dot is not different from another.For these reasons, I don't recommend this game to the public, as many players will be unaware of all this, and maybe like myself will be disappointed by this.
_childDocuments_.name: In Other Waters

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing this game. I loved the dashboard-like user interface, which was simple and made me feel like I was in a cockpit or control room. I loved the story, which was thought-provoking and unpredictable. I loved the atmospheric music. But more than anything, I ADORED the attention to detail in the design of Gliese 677Cc's ecosystem. The life patterns of the different organisms worked so differently from anything I've seen on Earth, but each species functioned according to consistent logic, and the parts of the life web fit together in a way that was believable and fascinating. Bravo to the creative team on this game; I would play anything else they make in a heartbeat! <3Additional interface notes:The limited field of vision added to the atmosphere of exploring a new place, and the topographic map background made for an aesthetically pleasing and wonderfully navigable map. If I could change one thing about the game, it would be the addition of a portable dive map (even without the teleporting capabilities of the dive map back at the base), so that you didn't have to go back to the base in order to remember where you're trying to get to.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game that really cares about ecology, biology, environmental science... The ecosystem is lovingly crafted and makes sense in ways that sci-fi rarely cares to.
