_childDocuments_.review: I have found it hard to put down this game since I got it. In one day, I put in 10.5 hours because it is easy to lose track of time playing this game. To give a bit of a caveat, I play a lot of town builder games. From the Tropico series, to Cities Skylines, etc. I have also played a few peaceful RPGs, most notably Stardew Valley. I try my best to judge every game for what it is and remove the notions of other similar games. Of course, biases exist, so I am trying to be clear about that.Starting with things I like about the game:1 - The story that is being developed. A hero who defended the world now has to find a new meaning. Your friends as well as others come to you in search of a new place that you build for them to live in. I can't wait for more of this to get fleshed out as the game develops.2 - Love the simplistic pixel based graphics. It does this game really well as it fits the charm this game is striving for.3 - The easy resource gathering that the gameplay gives. It is so much easier to fish and chop wood which makes the part that I like the most, the town-building aspect, more appealing.4 - The music in the background is fitting for the environment so much that I forget it is playing unless I get up to go do something then come back to it playing on. In other words, it really immerses the experience to me.5 - It is a peaceful RPG meaning that you don't have to constantly fight monsters. Littlewood gets this right as there is literally no combat in the gameplay.Now, a few things I think will improve with time:1 - The story is very minimal at the moment. You get quite a bit at the front of the game then start running into a lot of same text or (temporary text) as the develop puts on some text boxes. It would have done the game good to wait a bit to have a little more dialogue finished but it is to come.2 - You cannot rotate furniture inside of structures. You can't have two chairs facing each other around a table which upsets me but that's okay. If this is a function of the game then it is not made readily known which leads to the next point...3 - Upgrading buildings is not made really well known in the gameplay. I figured it out after a few hours of gameplay but these upgrades can sometimes be fairly vital to the game such as the balloon upgrade which unlocks new areas around the world.Finally, things that I don't think will improve with development:1 - The game is locked to a square based grid. This is really upsetting when the villagers are blocking things that you are trying to access like the only road heading to your balloon. This is not to say there are no ways around it but square grid games have always been a major frustration of mine through years of gaming.2 - The game currently has an almost set amount of actions you can take a day before the day ends which is okay. The problem is that there is no way around to negate this. It makes me fairly annoyed when I have 100 carrots and I can't eat 1 to regain an action for the day. I get why the game is like that, I just don't like it.3 - Villagers stay in one spot the whole day, don't move, and don't really seem to do anything. Having them have a routine would be difficult as the player can do what they want with the town, but it is still upsetting that they are just locked in place for the whole day then the next day they are locked in a new place. Overall, this game is early access and has a lot of promise. I don't quite think it is ready for most players to purchase even as an early access. I still recommend it because I think it will be a good game based on how the developer interacts with community members and what has been done up to this point. Honestly, I am excited for what the developer does with this game and I cannot wait for future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is a really interesting case study for minimalist game design. Every task, like fishing, logging, or farming is distilled to a very simple yet engaging mini game. I also enjoyed how Littlewood does not put pressure on you. Time only progresses if you actively work, there are no goals tied to years, and everyone loves you right from the start ;)A true little gem!

_childDocuments_.review: ... Not as good otherwise, but that may change!Littlewood is frustrating because you can see allllll this potential. And really, its a negative review by a thousand paper cuts. The game’s premise is so interesting, but it doesn’t feel like it has much to say about it. You saved the world, now get married and farm. … why? I liked the idea of a game that was about appreciating peace after you’ve completed anything, but I don’t feel like that message is really there in the game. It’s very material orientated in gameplay and mechanics, and that undermines this idea of peaceful retirement. You have to pay the woodcutter to make the area bigger. You have to pay for upgrades. Pay for items. Grind to get the stuff and then make the stuff to upgrade. You go to the library finally and meet characters who want you to… go get them stuff. I feel like achievements help demonstrate where the player focus is supposed to be, and the vast majority of the achievements are grinding oriented. There wasn’t even an achievement for unlocking the third forest and/or cave. One for getting married, but none for a first date or multiple first dates. I’ll keep trying with new builds because of… I’ll update and/or remove this review if anything changes

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely adorable cozy game! The main premise is building your town back up and bringing the community back together after disaster strikes, which you have no memory of. I was drawn to it because of the farming aspect (I'm a huge sucker for a farming sim), but I stayed for the community development, cute characters, decorating the town and villagers homes, and collecting everything possible. One feature that I thought was unique was how time progresses in this game. Instead of your day being set to a timer, which has you trying to use up all of your stamina and be as productive as possible before the clock runs out, the time in this game only progresses as you use up your stamina. I loved that because it allowed me to speak to each villager, do all of my shopping, and explore without worrying that I'm wasting the day away. Also, I'm incredibly indecisive when it comes to picking a love interest but what made this game special to me was once you pick your person, the rest of the town starts to fall in love with the other villagers. It made me feel a lot less guilty about choosing one person! Overall, this game was absolutely adorable and I would 100% recommend to someone who enjoys cozy games with farming, decorating, fishing/bug catching, collecting, and developing relationships!

_childDocuments_.review: i know this is a really small thing in the grand scheme of things, but i really appreciate how this entire game can be played with one hand on the keyboard. i have chronic pain/rsi in my wrists and particularly my right hand, so being able to sit with just one hand on the keyboard and rest my other hand while not feeling like im struggling to play the game properly is amazing. the game itself has a really enjoyable gameplay loop as well, and i love how the stamina/time system works. it means i dont have to rush through the day to do everything i want. i can stop and talk to every npc if i want to without "wasting" time, and i can explore and decorate for as long as i want to, which is something thats not always true with similar games. i played this for the first time several years ago, and since coming back there's a lot more content, and the game feels much more complete and balanced. it previously felt like the content just ran out and all there was left to do was to grind and grind to upgrade buildings while all the stories ended unceremoniously, but that appears to have been fixed in later versions. i have no idea if this game is finished or if its still being updated, but i think it is worth the price as it is now, and any further additions would be welcome bonuses and not sorely needed fixes and patches

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing RPG might be exactly what I need right now. Littlewood has a great premise. After the greatest evil of the world has been destroyed you take the bombed-out ruins of a town and rebuild it. You can name your character and your town, there's nothing like a fresh start. It's perfect because the world has been through hell and now all the monsters are gone. Littlewood is a hyper-casual game, similar to Animal Crossing. My favorite mechanic is how time moves forward. It doesn't. You only have a certain amount of stamina to spend each day.Moving on to what Littlewood is really about. Grinding a million bars to increase the level of everything. Warning, this is not a joke. Everything has a mechanic to level it up. This includes villager relations, their houses, your skills, all the business, and more.However, there's enough progress it doesn't become tiresome but these are chores. This is perhaps the second cutest game ever created to do chores. But when it works it works. I enjoyed leveling up everything and found it easy to focus on one upgrade at a time. When I was spreading my supplies out it was overwhelming. There is one thing that makes it easily digestible. You can go at your own pace, there's zero pressure to upgrade anything. Skipping an upgrade isn't a big deal and the day goes by so fast it's fine. I can't stress enough how low-stress Littlewood is.Now, the game loop consists of harvesting raw materials, then refining those, then spending those on upgrades. You will be doing it a lot. Pretty early on you unlock the ability to travel to locations where you can get the raw stone and wood. So much travel back and forth but the game does give you fast travel options. I really appreciate it.Overall Littlewood is great if you love doing work similar to chores. Getting those bars maxed out and leveling up everything gives a great sense of progression. Also, the game has a strong "just one more day" feeling. There's always a payoff and the game keeps delivering new entertaining things. With so much content the mechanics are distilled into their most basic functions. They simplified as much as they could get away with. But, Littlewood has captured me in the cutest kindness explosion possible. Everyone is so happy and loving how could I not enjoy it. If you're into a calm grind then this game is for you!I create videos, (they're good)
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I did not expect much when I bought this game, but I was pleasantly surprised. The town building mechanics (thus far) are simple, you don't have to drag out an area for a house, just have the materials. However in order to please your NPCs it can get tricky, for example they want to live within x amount of spaces of a shop but not near a foundry, or they want specific furniture that has hard to find blueprints.I wish the initial town map was a little larger, but so far you can farm, raise orchards, have livestock and build all kinds of utility buildings. You can travel to the forest, mines, and a port town. each utility building and even locations can be upgraded. You can cook to make money, and build a market to trade. There are two more destinations that have yet to be finished that you will be eventually able to travel to.The NPCs you recruit teach you new blueprints for buildings, and have a relationship meter. Which is cool keeping everyone happy.Overall the game looks nice, it has a Stardew valley feel, and the music is nice and relaxing. Most early access games disappoint me, but this one is nice, with quick updates and very few bugs. I just hope Sean keeps working on it. I think the game is worth the money as it is, and I am sure that it will only get better.

_childDocuments_.review: It breaks my heart to give this one a bad review because I fell in love with it, but...This game is frontloaded with little to no late game.  Mid to late game is so unpolished and unbalanced that you lose interest in the game entirely.  It starts giving you ridiculous amounts of resources meanwhile the content just stops. It feels like there were meant to be mechanics for those resources to be spent on that were never implemented.  It gives you upgrade options that are pointless by the time they unlock, stores that don't sell anything, npcs that are given half of a storyline and then forgotten about entirely.  It feels so very incomplete.It's so damn lovable and until it isn't.  And that really sucks.  The characters are freaking adorable and memorable, and the early game is just so damn fun! I love this game to death but, it just feels abandoned and incomplete.  Playing this game feels like when your a kid and you preorder your first game from EA, before you know any better.  You get so hyped, and the game arrives and you have a ton of fun for a bit.  Then it all falls apart and this thing that you adored so much just little while ago is sitting there in pieces and you feel like ♥♥♥♥ for letting your self get excited.  I don't know if the guy got overwhelmed or ran out of time and money.  Maybe he's just an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, IDK I hope not though.  Anyway, this game is a punch in the guts, like getting a puppy that goes missing before it's a year old.  What happened to it?

_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I recieved this game as a suprise gift and oh boy, was it the perfect suprise gift.Now this game is exactly as what it presents itself as. It is a little like a simplified Stardew Valley with a city builder aspect.The story or rather backstory and most character interactions are pretty much optional since you can just skip through them if you're not interested in them and just here for the gameplay.Since I play games like this mostly while listening to things on the side, I kept the music and sound effects mostly muted. When I heard them they were ordinary, nothing particularly special, but very fitting for the atmosphere.During the endgame you get the means to pretty much do whatever you want and get easier access to rarer resources.A tip I'd give to new players is to check in on the personal goals, villager requests and the Journal, especially the means how to get specific travellers to show up, to ease through those parts a bit better (I totally wasn't unattentive enough to fully look through the Journal until quite late in the game or anything). Also put the requested funiture into the individual houses soonish as well, it gives you a few neat rewards.Overall I'd definitely recommend Littlewood, especially for more casual players that just want something to do on the side and those who like this type of game to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT AS OF 2023 - I believe the dev has stopped working on the game as there hasn't been anything since 2020. I was hoping there would eventually be some sort of update but alas after waiting three years for anything, I'm gonna go ahead and archive this game. It's a shame because I feel like this could have gone pretty far. Maybe I'll replay it sometime if I run out of games.I loved this game. I got about 50 hours out of it so the price seems worth it. It literally is if Animal Crossing and Stardew Valley had a baby. These kinds of games are my jam and when I found this I was so excited and was not let down. There is plot in this, I guess more of a mysterious backstory type of plot. I loved finding the books to get more lore throughout the game. There are "enemies" in the cave and the forest and you don't have an attack ability but they are very easily avoided. I thought this was a nice touch though. _childDocuments_.review: It's like Stardew Valley but very streamlined. _childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is a good game, but not an exceptional one. My recommendation? Buy on sale.In my playthrough I completed the game after ~30 hours of playtime. Be aware of what you paid for, Littlewood is a game that is centered on unlockables & collectibles. Everything you do in this game is to either unlock more content or collecting collectibles. If you like collect-a-thon games you will surely enjoy this game.First of all, I love how I could design my town and get rewarded for making it look pretty. The soundtrack and sound design also complement the cutesy vibe of the game. It has this rewarding feeling when you collect certain items. I personally feel the most enjoyment when I unlock more content as I collected more items.Unlocking early to mid game items is also fun because the effort you spend to get those items are reasonable, but later when only the difficult ones are left the game gets stupid as the rng is rarely in your favor, leaving your backpack full with mostly collected items that remains useless (yes you could sell those but later in the game the currency doesn't mean anything anymore so it's not rewarding).7/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is an excellent game following the concept of Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon and similar games in this genre.The biggest issue I had with Stardew Valley was constant pressure of time, as you had very limited space for things you could do across the day, which usually resulted in not having enough of that for everything you could've wanted. This could be both an advantage and a disadvantage, personally I was never a huge fan of that system, which is why I personally prefer Littlewood, as it follows on the fixed stamina and therefore actions you can do across the day, and the time passes according to the stamina used.Don't get me wrong however, the stamina is VERY limited and there is still a constant pressure of how many things you can do daily. At the same time I enjoy such system much more as it allows micro-management of what you gonna do in a given day, without a pressure of time if you're currently idling wondering what to focus on next. Therefore, Littlewood is far more relaxing in nature, and personally gives me more fun.As of the rest of the game, it's a masterpiece. There is a significant amount of content, I'd say on-par with Stardew Valley, as with every following day new options open and you can never cover enough of it for all the things you planned on doing anyway. Contrary to Stardew, there is no actual fighting, even though various mobs exist and you have to actively dodge them trying to get to some of the chests and resources.If you asked me which game is better, I'd say they're both equally good. The biggest difference is time management I've mentioned above, therefore Littlewood seems more relaxing and management game, while Stardew, still holding strong on the management side, tries to be a bit more active in micro-managing and min-maxing everything. If you're still unsure, try both, you won't be disappointed with either. If you already played Stardew, you know what to expect, personally I liked Littlewood more due to aspects mentioned above, but both games are masterpiece in my opinion.Of course, I can highly recommend the game, the content is enourmous in size, the price is super cheap in regards to that, and the game is really enjoyable for having a relaxed playing session where you can focus on doing whatever you want to.---If you liked my review, you can find more of them on  and on my .

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, cute, fun, lots of good ideas and fun systems, but the endgame is unpleasantly grindy and the achievements are so grindy as to be not worth even attempting.Pros:-Interesting twist on the standard JRPG premise - the legendary hero won already, but lost their memory and doesn't know how or what happened afterward, and now is mostly just settling down to live the rest of their life-Delightful mix of genuine storytelling on its own terms and parody/satire of other genre staples; story emerges slowly and is only rarely formatted as Big Story Things, preferring generally to give small bits of lore and background here and there as the player experiences the game-Characters are fun, plentiful, and have honestly more personality each than most entire classic JRPG parties (looking at you, Chrono Cross!) despite being shallow enough to fit into three or four sentences each-Cute art, good sprite work, consistent style, and cute designs-Wide variety of systems to engage with ranging from creative base building to relationships to flower breeding to farming to exploration to a pretty decent Yu-Gi-Oh! knockoff-Plenty of content in each system to keep an interested player engaged-Lots of satirical elements make a fun scavenger hunt for references and allusions to older titles to which this plays homageCons:-Progression is based on an unstated assumption that every player will engage with every system consistently and evenly as they play - my experience did not match this assumption-Endgame pacing is very, very weird in that I felt like I was 90% of the way through the game at about 40% of my final playtime-A lot of progression is gated behind random item drops, which for most of the game is very hard to control or mitigate, meaning that often you just can't do whatever you're working on until the game decides you get whatever item you needed-Flower breeding is  - also the only thing in the game I did not complete legitimately, because even after doing just about everything else I had made almost no progress on getting anything but the basic colors and breeds even with following guides and watering daily-The Prodigy achievements are not in any way worth the trouble, and there is not the slightest chance of getting most of them without grinding for literally about as long as the entire main story; I initially was enjoying the game enough that I wanted to 100% it but between the flower breeding nonsense and these painfully grindy achievements I quickly realized it was pointless to waste that many hours for no returnOther notes:-I won't comment on music and sound design as I played the game entirely muted-Obviously this is very subjective but I found a handful of characters very annoying and, due to the nature of gated progression, it is required by the game's systems to engage with those characters regularly-I absolutely loved this game almost the whole way through and by the end was bored and unhappy with it due to the messy grindy endgame stuffIn summary, I would definitely recommend that you play this game, and it's worth finishing - but definitely make sure to engage with every system starting as soon as it's available and don't skip any of it because you'll eventually have to double back. Also avoid selling rare items because you'll definitely end up needing them for something later.

_childDocuments_.review: Very much enjoyed this calming and addictive game. It has vibes from the following games:Harvest moon (stardew may be a more common comparison now though) - farming, lifestock, mining, gathering, friendships and romance with villagers.  Runescape -  leveling system,Dark Chronicle/Dark Cloud - town building with terrain and object requirements, Animal crossing - take your time and design your town. (time only progresses though energy usage)So if you like one or more of those, you will like this one. I've played these 56 hours within just 4 days, was hard to stop. Pretty much done almost everything. Plan to work on my towns design. And a feature I love for this (that you unlock my meeting a certain condition), is to completely destroy everything in the town, being refunded all the materials spent. You can destroy only one category too, say just all the flowers for instance when they've bred out of control. They'll all be in your inventory to replant. This means you can terraform freely without having to move things out of the way. Wish other similar games could implement this where possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely stellar! I'm always a bit nervous about getting EA games, but this one hasn't disappointed me. The developer seems to be really invested in making the game the best it can be. When all of the content comes out, I anticipate preferring Littlewood over Stardew Valley. This game takes so many elements from Animal Crossing and SDV and just,, makes them better. The skill grind doesn't feel unrewarding or boring, and there are so many different things to do! The customizability of the town is amazing. A couple things I wish were implemented:- Longer sunset/better sun positions. As it stands, the night comes in really harshly, like some kind of intense solar eclipse type of thing, and there's no darker day/sunset period that eases the transition. Also, if seasons could kind of bleed over into each other (ie. grass gets progressively more brown around the end of summer, slight bits of snow at the last days of fall) could really make the game feel more realistic and dynamic. - Mod capability. This game is great as-is, but oh man, with mods? a whole 'nother level.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW: GREAT, BUT CAN BE IMPROVEDPositives:This game is fun, the graphics are so cute, there's a lot to doNegatives:There's just a bit of grinding when you have to chop down trees and mine ores all the time, There's also no way to increase your energy No way to see relationships with other villagersWould recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the couple hours I've put in so far. For an early access game there are very little bugs and quite a bit of content to grind through. There are hints at a story line evolving, and I for one look forward to what becomes of it. (I'm watching you Lilith). As for comparisons, I would say it's somewhat of a cross between Harvest Moon and Animal Crossing with a handful of creative aspects to give you hours of torment trying to get your town looking perfect, in between tearing it down and starting again. The UI can be slightly janky at times when it comes to the build menu but nothing that deters me from excessively using it. All in all, a good early access game where you can grind and relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: It's just what I needed right now:Something to soothe my mind, something extremly relaxing, something you can play with no stress at all.But even with those traits this game is far from boring.There are so many things to do and I have the feeling I barely even scratched the surface.Do what you like, when you like.Set your own goals for the day.Just start up Littlewood, chill out and forget the hassle that's waiting for you in reallife.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: So, I don't know if you can tell that I REALLY like this game. This game isn't done, and when I opened it up today I was surprised by a number of changes. If you're not a person that likes change, especially when it was great before, wait until the game releases. Sean is a FANTASTIC game dev, and I really love the weekly updates. Its super exciting, and makes it fun to see whats going to come each week. I will change this again once there's a final release, but all I can say is great things.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, one might think it’s similar to Stardew Valley, and of course, as with all those type of sim games, there are some similarities. But, after having finished it, I have to say, it’s not, not really. The goals are just too different.Most of all, this is not a farming game. It’s a “follow the red line to rebuild a town according to requirements while grinding for money and materials” game.You meet new people, they move into your town when you build their houses, and along the way you unlock new structures you can upgrade. The world is rather small, your town, a few destinations you can travel to, as well as two randomly generated dungeon maps. Mostly you run around, raise skills and gather materials, to build and upgrade and unlock new stuff.imageConsidering that, I did get exactly what I wanted. It took me about 50h to 100% the game (well… I got all the achievements, and leveled all the skills up, but didn’t bother maxing all relationships or dating all villagers or beating them in the mini card game.)Anyway, I’ve already written too much, and if you’re into that kind of games, this is a good one.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: So playing this game for a certain amount of time. I've concluded one thing, addictive. lots of bugs and quarks in it but nothing to bad for a starting up game. a couple bugs/annoyances I've noticed so far.- teleportation your character during build mode is wack- houses needing to be close and far away from certain things really messes up my town look.- when you dismiss a towny infront of an interactable and you're almost about to pass out will cause you to use said interactable and fall asleep.- going to the port after the pig arc casino thing, the guy literally is scooting to the right and falls off the map everytime you go there.- the rewards for the higher leveled things is underwhelming.- placing a pavement under a house is annoying and cant be removed without moving the house, same applys with fences on pastures.- weeds are supreme- THE TOWNIES DON'T MOVE OUT OF YOUR WAY- random pastures start appearing in the port and forest/cave when you have them in your townaside form these bugs and annoyances. I loved the game and plan to keep playing till its bent to my will.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game expecting another Stardew dupe but it was so much more than that. Although there are many similarities this game stands out on its own by having so much more to do. Where many times I felt events depended on time in Stardew, in Littlewood the events are more based on your progression in the game. I never run out of things to do in this game and I feel like I use all my given energy in a day all the time. I've put over 12 active hours in finding collectables, building farms, decorating and terra-forming my town, there's still so much more to do. Although I do feel like I have reached the end game stages, there seems to be more hidden unlockables and so much more room for updates in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, it's cute, gameplay is fun, overwhelming at first, but the progression made it good. Building your own little cute town at whatever pace you choose. There is no time restrictions and your crops grow even during winter. The only problem is late game and certain items you need to craft due to how the rare and miscellaneous item are obtained, making it really grindy and no longer fun. It almost feels like there could have been more content in the end game, would definitely pay at least 20€ for this game if it was the case.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing Littlewood when it was still Early Access and I have had no issues with my experience. Quite the opposite in fact. I love this game and to be honest I find it better than Stardew in a lot of ways. For one: Instead of fighting the daily clock AND your stamina like in Stardew, your stamina bar also acts as the clock. So when it gets low it turns to night time. I think that's one of my favorite features.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Another game where I wish there was a "meh" option. I tend to judge games on whether I can get at least one hour of fun playtime per dollar spent. As you can see, clearly I've gotten that and more. For the price, I definitely recommend this game. It's fun getting to build the town up slowly and meet the new characters. I also really enjoy that each character has their own requirements for their house, since I'm not creative at all about that stuff.  That being said, don't buy it expecting *tons* of fun playtime, cause it gets pretty grindy after a while. Also the NPCs are all very two-dimensional; once you've met them you know pretty much everything there is to know about them, which makes all of the heart events underwhelming. Speaking of which, the game decides what your character says to the NPCs. I haven't seen a single dialogue choice the entire time I've played, which feels weird in this kind of game. It really makes "dating" the NPCs feel gross, since you don't get a choice in how you respond to  them in a conversation. It also adds to the underwhelmingness of the heart events, since the only thing you do is click through them. All in all, there's a lot of potential here, but also a lot of missed marks.tl;dr - Get it, but don't expect the fun to last much beyond 20 hours or so
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: It is a cute game but very short as far as story line gameplay. The only reason I have so many hours in it is because I'm a completionist at heart and the last few achievements are EXTREMELY painfully grindy. Do not play this game if you want to get all the achievements. They're not at all skill or story based. Just mindless, endless, painful grinding. Not worth it imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. There is no combat! (aside from whacking trees with your axe) It's based after a huge battle where all the monsters disappeared and you have to help rebuild the town. I get lost in the game so easily, collecting items for crafting, talking to villagers, exploring the different areas. There is so much to do. Plus you can 100% customize the decor and layout of the town! As well as the interior designs of each house. Also, the pixel art is high quality, super adorable, and the soundtrack for this game is *chef's kiss* :) There is one song that plays at night time that I always have to turn up a little! It's such a vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is a pixel-style game based on the Heroic Adventurer of Solemn. After defeating the 'Dark Wizard', you've retraced yourself to a young woman named Willow, accompanied by a young man called Dalton. The only downside? You have amnesia from your amazing adventures. Both characters will help and guide you through building up your new town, and whatever you wish to do with it is your own imagination! The game features tons of cute characters and things to do as your town grows - you'll very rarely feel boredom.My biggest advice is to save up your Dewdrops (the in-game currency, not a micro-transaction) and materials such as wood, stone, crops, etc. They all come in very handy! Dewdrops will be your main usage throughout the game for a variety of things. One of which counts as donations - which is one of the best things I loved about this game, and what helps keep things going.Although every review should give cons with their pros, and the biggest one would be how repetitive things will get. Now as stated beforehand, this game will rarely come across as 'boring' or 'overwhelming' - but you WILL need to get into a routine of things. You need to continuously stock and sell things from your Marketplace (stock before bed, things sell when you go to sleep), cook food for your Tavern, gather materials, etc. Thankfully, everything is explained within the game and there are new additions, events, and similar every in-game month.Overall, I found this to be the cutest title I've ever played, definitely 10 out of 10 gold stars with a pinch of Unicorn dust. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Good GameLittlewood is simple and a good game to play when you don't want to fight, die (and lose your stuff) and all of the stress you can get. Its very peaceful and the villagers are great. I do wish the villagers have more personality as they usually just say the same stuff over and over again. I enjoy trying to make new recipes at the Tavern, Collecting my dewdrops after selling expensive stuff and exploring all of the new areas. The building in the game is very easy and enjoyable. Overall 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game. Pokemon style graphics with elements of Minecraft and Stardew Valley. I loved SV but Littlewood, albeit similar, is different and interesting and manages to forgo many irritating elements of SV's gameplay. Downside is the mid-game play can become a bit repetitive as the days/energy level is quite short and can't be extended. Can't wait to see more events and such, loving it so far and still feel like I have a lot more to discover!
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun and relaxing game so far. It's arguably even more relaxing than Stardew Valley, as there's never any sort of time crunch or need to min-max - you can sleep early, pull weeds the entire day, or do whatever else you want without the feeling that you're missing out on doing something more important or setting yourself behind. You can also idle, walk around, or work on your town as long as you want without time passing. The gathering mechanics are simple, but still satisfying.There's also a good amount of customization present with the furniture, landscaping, etc. available to you. You can change the entire landscape of the town by raising areas up a level or two or creating rivers and ponds, and you can move every piece of your town wherever you'd like it to be.The game has a very basic farming system in comparison to something like Stardew Valley, and the character depth also heavily pales in comparison. They do have some charm to them and there is a relationship system, but they don't have very in-depth personalities or backstories, so I wouldn't play this if you're looking for immersion. Overall, it's worth the price and a good buy if you're looking for something casual to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: The world has been saved! And now you return "home" to rebuild it. Your "Build Mode" is unlocked the moment you start a new game, giving you the power to place houses where you want, make lakes and/or mountains. It is all up to you! You can give the town any name you want , and you get to write in your own title. So I am "Vorleser, Governor of Edelvale" As you build your town and explore the world, new people will want to move in -- and you build a house for them.There's bug catching, hosting your own marketplace, fishing, cooking, mining, wood refining, ore refining Each townsfolk has their own friendship meter AND you can take them with you to "hang out" so they follow you -- and can provide certain bonuses like finding bonus items or currency. It is a pixel graphic game and has a lot of things to do, it is very relaxing game.It is almost the "Animal Crossing: New Horizons" for PC , since Stardew Valley focuses a lot in the aspect of "your farm" --- this one is more about "Your town" , and for the asking price I'd say its really great value.Nominated this game for "Sit back and relax" category.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically review games in early access, since I don't believe it's fair to the product, but I will make an exception for Littlewood. I backed this game on kickstarter and have thoroughly been impressed by the consistent updates and relaxing gameplay. Sure, it's a bit grindy sometimes, but any game of this nature basically has to be; otherwise people would be complaining it was way too short or it would have to have a ridiculous amount of gameplay for the scope of the project. The characters have been entertaining, the building and rearranging seems really well implemented, and I haven't run into any bugs yet (at 15 hours). Overall, I would absolutely recommend this game for anyone looking for a chill, charming city-building type game.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Was looking for something Stardew-esque, and this definitely has that feel (albeit simplified, and with its own style). I love that you can design every aspect of the town, and that it's as easy as just picking something up and plopping it where you (and/or the townsfolk) want. I love that you can bring your little townie buddies along for adventures. I love how easy it is to play, no burdensome menus to shuffle through or numerous buttons to memorize. Everything is simple, though more depth (and more story) is revealed over time.Everything feels good about it, really. It feels like a game that knew exactly what it wanted to be, and accomplished exactly what it set out to do.

_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is without a doubt, the most charming game in my 200+ library. I am truthfully really impressed with the launch as so very often as a fan you can build up a game to epic proportions in your head and they very rarely live up to expectations.The current content is just so satisfying and the potential for growth is through the roof. From the opening scene, the vibrant colors, adorable pixelart and soothing music... you know you're in for something special. :)I've been following Littlewood's development since the Kickstarter campaign and I can, without a moment's hesitation, wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys simple mechanics, town management and in general, playing in a stress-free setting.There are quite a number of things to dive into with Littlewood, but suffice it to say, it's indeed one of those "just one more day" affairs. I find myself wanting to see how I can encourage new people/shops to join my budding town. I want to know what my past was with these lovely villagers.And I want to collect all the fish... Must. Have. All. The. Fish. ;)My heartfelt thanks to Sean for creating such a lovely game. I look forward to watching Littlewood's development!
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little casual town building game with a simple gameplay loop around grinding resources to rebuild your town and do things for the townsfolk.  There's no real time pressure in the game, as time is fully oriented around your stamina, making it a fun little game to unwind with.I was able to find pretty much everything in a bit over 40 hours.The town can be fully customized, but the townsfolk define what they want in their places. There's a strong random element in the game as many upgrades involve getting rare ingredients which are initially seasonal, so if you miss things, you will have to wait quite a while to see them again, though there are alternate ways to get most things which you can unlock with upgrades.  What you choose to invest in and your luck will determine your progression.There's a fairly interesting deck building mini-game included which is fun, but the game makes it less so by making it unfair by giving your opponents much more health than you get.  While you do have some strategic advantages and can built your desk against your opponent's and get to go first, those factors get outweighed by opponents who can have as much as 60 health to your 10.  You have to both play well and also be lucky to win the end game match ups.The interactions are occasionally funny, but cutscenes are pretty simplistic and just consist of a couple people talking at pre-set locations.  Festivals are also often very similar. Still, it is clear a lot of effort was put into the lore of the game and the dialogue, so it sort of balances out.All in all, it is a fun game but the asking price is a bit much vs the content, especially when compared to games like Stardew Valley.  I'd certainly get it on sale though.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, easy and everything a casual game should be without the waiting to complete times. You can go as hard or as slow as you like and the mini targets are rewarding and worthwhile. There's so much to do and all the time in the world to complete it so very good for young players or older players who want to dip in and out. It has that wonderful simple 8-bit vibe; no trying to impress with graphics, just with that gentle cosy atmosphere. Build everything in an animal crossing way that gets slowly harder... but only if you want it to. I'm currently in love with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: So fun! I think if you enjoyed Animal Crossing and Stardew Valley and you want something in the same vein that isn't those two games (if you're burnt out on them), this one is super fun and calming. The characters are charming. Littlewood definitely has aspects of Stardew, but is different enough in my opinion that it's worth playing even if you've sunk hundreds of hours into Stardew. It's a little less involved, a little more chill. All in all, great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood has its moments of charm and uniqueness. Including a mini TCG within the game is a great touch, and I like the bubbly little character designs and whimsical item names. Chopping trees and smashing rocks in this game is super juicy and fun. I appreciate the total freedom you have in designing and rearranging the town, I’d love to see that in more games. There are a few interviews out there with the game’s creator, Sean Young, and it’s clear that this game is a labor of love, though much of it is derivative of other popular games (as you can tell just by looking at it). I should note that the game isn’t all that buggy and if you’re really itching for a cutesy, grindy, time waster of a game, go right ahead and buy it – you’ll have your work cut out for you.Why I wouldn’t recommend it to most people:The characters are completely one dimensional. This game can’t help but be compared to Stardew Valley, and my god, Stardew does so much more with its love interests, cutscenes, overall plot… The writing here just isn’t up to that level at all. You’ve got a lot of in-game months if not years to get through with these npcs and you’ll run into repeat dialogue after about 10 interactions with any of them. Once you start going down the dating track with one (or in my case all) of them, you’ll quickly realize that they all say roughly the same things and have no depth or much backstory besides what you already know about them… don’t be a completionist about it, just pick one and get it over with. Very disappointing if you’re going into this expecting something heartwarming and character based, which I kinda was.What I find unforgivable is the lack of payoff. I’m never deterred from a game just because it requires some grinding. I say bring it on, I’m into that sh*t… but Jesus, grinding just for the sake of grinding just isn’t fun. The Edge of Solemn is SO hyped by the npcs and when you get there you pick up 2 items and that’s it. After playing this game on and off for a few months, getting to the end and finding nothing there is almost profound. You find yourself looking at this little purple floating rock and think… that’s it? I wasted hours of my time for THIS? It was implied that there’d be some great mystery to untangle but just… nothing. Maybe it’s an avant garde statement on the nature of country-life sims, confronting the player with a hollowed void, revealing to us that all this time and energy spent on romancing fictional characters and planting fictional fruits and vegetables leaves us as sallow and empty as the desolate bit of rock before us…Or it’s an unfinished game. Yeah, it seems to me that this game is basically unfinished. I know it’s now available for Switch and I’m unaware of any updates or changes, so I’m fairly certain this is to remain unfinished forever.Like I said, if you’re looking for a juicy little time waster and don’t care about characters or plot to begin with, by all means go for this one. Otherwise, I’d say skip it.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good, the gameplay is great and adictive, the music is nice and the graphism are also okay. The thing a find a  sad, I can't get attached to any characters, they are all boring and cliché. I honestly think the price is a little too high for what the game have to offer. I recommend buying it when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a longtime fan of "wholesome relaxing" games, and this one has been on my list for ages. Playing it now, it has quickly become a favorite game of mine. _childDocuments_.review: Update as of 2021:There have been no news since end 2020 from the dev, and no signs of further updates or support. A full m+kb control scheme has not been fully implemented contrary to what was stated, and as it stands the game remains in an unpolished state.  Early Access Review:The less stressful, charming little brother of Stardew Valley - no combat, no time management (time only passes when you make an action) and all the pixelart beauty with additional town management mechanisms! I honestly cannot in good conscience not recommend this whimsical time-sinker.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough review for me to write as I've obviously put some time into this game. While I had some enjoyment, I don't think I would generally recommend this game. Others might though, which is why I'd rather give it a mixed review. Unfortunately Steam doesn't allow that so I went with thumbs down as I just finished the goals I wanted in this game and have no plans to ever pick it up again. As a means of comparison (whether fair or not), I'm going to compare it to Stardew Valley which is a similar game that I really enjoyed.What I liked:-I'm a huge fan of games where I upgrade things. This game is pretty much the king of that, with multiple upgrades for each building. With tons of buildings, that was really cool. The thing I didn't love as much was that many of the upgrades were essentially meaningless steps, meant to lock you in to grinding more materials.-No time limit on days made this much more relaxing than Stardew Valley. While you'll still find yourself short on energy, it doesn't feel like you've lost out on anything if you don't use a day efficiently, and you don't have to be watching the clock constantly.-There's a ton of customization of your town and it's much more interesting than Stardew Valley in that regard. I'm not very big into that part of games but I could see how it could be appealing.-There are a few cool secrets, but Stardew takes the cake with that.What I didn't like:-This game is so insanely grindy. I unlocked everything except the last few achievements for gathering materials because it would require me to sit there doing incredibly boring tasks for no tangible reward for probably another 20 hours. The lvl 99 upgrades for each item were super tedious to get to as well, though they were definitely nice.-The random manner in which some items appear can block your progression in one area of the game for a significant portion of time. I spent (in-game) weeks trying to get one type of fish or some black pearls or a specific flower in the forest or other things along those lines. You can generally target items in a way, but that still doesn't guarantee they'll show up. So it's back to grinding...-I get that combat wasn't intended to be a part of the game, but I feel like it could have been a nice addition. The minions in the cave were just plain annoying and I don't see the purpose in including aspects like that.-The card game was a cool idea but I think it was poorly implemented. It was tough to understand at first and when I got it, I found that the best way to play was to just either use 1 cost blockers all the time or a deck full of reflect cards. I used these two decks on every single enemy in the game, even the hardest one with 60 health. Why offer all these cards, when they're not even that helpful? Seems wasted.-While I appreciated removing some of the tedium that Stardew Valley had around farming, other things like fishing were just dull in comparison and lack of automation of some tasks left me getting sick of chopping trees or collecting animal products or watering the flowers for the 100th time.If you like a really laidback game, enjoy chasing upgrades, and love designing aesthetically pleasing towns, this game could be for you. For most people, I would probably just recommend going the Stardew route instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Truly truly love this game. I plan to play for dozens of hours more. This really struck a great balance for me when it comes to farming/dating/collecting games like Stardew Valley, My Time at Portia, and Staxel. I've played all of these games and truly enjoyed all of them, but I'm beginning to realize that I like Littlewood the best. It's so very relaxing in a way that I didn't find the other three games I listed to be as chill and comforting.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This is fun and addictive much like Stardew Valley or Forager. Likes:-I LOVE being able to choose and design the layout of the village and that it MATTERS in terms of meeting villager requests, and more importantly, gameplay efficiency (putting together the most commonly used buildings and buildings that are used together helps a ton)-Game time is limited by "energy" rather than a clock which makes it less stressful, but also feels lower stakes or like how you choose to spend your days does not matter. -Simple, good art style-Sensible upgrades, always something to do-Progression encourages exploring essentially all aspects of the game-Generally charming characters and interacting with them doesn't feel like a chore. Cons:This game felt a LOT like Forager in so many ways that it really bothered me. Overall, this is the better game but having played Forager first ruined it a bit.  The art style is too similar, the upgrades, the lack of consequences/inability for anything truly "bad" to happen, and many many subtle similarities.  -Currently, farming is a bit too weak/uninvolved, and gathering and processing mass lumber and rock is a bit too much of a bottleneck. Not a major problem for a early release game, but hope to see it tuned.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: It's unreasonable to compare every farming sim to Stardew Valley.  It's my humble opinion that anyone who immediately compares these games to SV in their review is potentially cheating you, and maybe even themselves, out of a new and different game experience.  I've read both good and bad reviews and concluded, I really like Littlewood.  There's a lot of potential in this early access game.  A lot of the events aren't ready yet and there are glitches.  It's to be expected of early access, but the good thing is these growing pains, for me, are the only cons so far.   The graphics are charming and the characters are quirky (tough orge chicks, weird miners, a loose cannon witch etc.).  I really like that game play isn't timed.  The day passes according to your energy/tasks completed.  There's really no need to pause the game or rush back home in the middle of a task.  You can project whether you have enough energy to do extra stuff, or not...it's totally up to you.  I like that the game is based around rebuilding after war, the war is a mystery piece together though dialogue with townsfolk, and there may or may not be lesser nature based enemies in the world of Littlewood.  I can't to see what else the developer has up their sleeve.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game while I was searching in the Farming & Crafting store category, and TBH it stayed on my wishlist for a long time. Some things I love about the game is that you don't have to worry about your inventory filling up and having to dump some things to make room for others, and that you don't have to constantly switch between tools. Also, the way that the day progresses by how much stamina you use is actually genius because I don't feel like I wasted any time in my day by walking around, visiting the merchants and talking to people. Games like Stardew (which I LOVE, don't get me wrong) give me anxiety because I struggle to balance the social and work aspects without running out of time. AND, there is a really interesting story happening in the background that flows really well with the gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Super cute and addicting game made by a dev who cares. Slightly buggy because Early Access but less so than some triple A releases.A lot of reviews I've seen are saying "Stardew Valley" this, "Stardew Valley" that, but I think that's a misnomer. This game is different from Stardew, and that's alright. That's good even, it has different content and is executed very well. That being said, if you liked Stardew (lord knows I did) you'll probably enjoy this game.This game has a focus on building up your town that you're the mayor of, and you have damn near full customization of the town. The gameplay is simple and intuitive, which is exactly what you want in a game like this. The townsfolk are charming, the lore of the world is interesting, and the setting itself is wonderful. There are still signs this game is in early access, such as dialogue options not being available, occasional bugs in how villagers move, and some festivals having placeholders but not being available yet. If you're alright with that, I encourage you to get the game. And if you're not alright with that, I encourage you to favorite it and wait for full release. It'll be worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: [summary comparison to stardew/harvest moon with hints of animal crossing]It's Stardew/Harvest Moon:Mine, chop, craft, raise animals, cook, make money, level skills. No "combat" though. Stamina system where performing actions will run out a bar that advances "time" (most of the bar is day, the last about 1/7th or so is the night). Sleep in your bed when it says you're tired or you incur a stamina penalty the next day.It's Animal Crossing:Maybe not THAT many villagers, but you get to customize your town's appearance, landscape and there are quest chains for filling out villager houses. Also no combat.Really easy-going and relaxing game that doesn't antagonize you to get things done at a particular speed. The gameplay loops are fairly basic (wake up, generally dedicate a day to one experience such as mining or woodcutting) but there is just enough going on to allow you to keep changing it up. The closest thing to "combat" is avoiding simple monsters that you can't kill.

_childDocuments_.review: ###Read this first:###To the people saying "this game is another Stardew Valley", you completely missed the point of the game. Littlewood does not have the intention of being a farming game - it has a small farming aspect to it, but it is *not* a farming game, seeing it is a minimal aspect of it. Be very wary about the reviews you either read OR write, especially the negative ones. ########I have been following this game for a while - found it via a Friend a few weeks ago - and it was in my wishlist because its premise seemed interesting.I have to say I am not disappointed; in fact I am rather impressed. The game still has a long way to go but it is very, very promising. It has a lot of potential. So far only played 4h but I am already in Summer day 10 and I am more than willing to dedicate many more hours to this little gem.Littlewood can be somewhat grindy - as many town/city building and RPG games usually are - but it's very rewarding considering all aspects related to said grind. We get access to some boosts as well which help when it comes to leveling skills. The sound effects are fantastic, the music is really good - very relaxing actually - and the overall colours add to its charm. It's neither too flashy nor too boring, it's offers a well-achieved middle-ground.There are a few lacking things that in my opinion could improve the UI:- descriptions for some items and what they can be used for (or if they can / should only be sold), however I am sure these will be introduced later down the line with a new update.- a bit more when it comes to informing the player how they can upgrade their tools (I personally didn't manage to find any information, but on the other hand I am quite glad I don't have all the information just dumped or spoonfed to me);- a bit more clarity when it comes to relationships (I am led to believe it will be possible to have a relationship with some/all of the characters? If not, my town's Fuschia Scarf Enthusiast chef is going to be the reason for my broken hart!);So far I couldn't find any negative aspects that warrant being mentioned. Littlewood isn't too complicated to understand, even for people that don't like "grindy" games or for people with no patience for resource collection / hoarding, but you also won't be spoonfed everything throughout your game either - the game doesn't have a "tutorial" per se, but all the information that's laid out to the player is more than good enough to get one started and acquaintanced with the mechanics.This, in my opinion, could very well be a fantastic multiplayer game - no need for P2P connections, just allow us to have a dedicated server so we can have sessions with friends!I am very excited to see what new content we will be given. Please, do buy this little treasure. It is worth every single penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes but also Meh. The game has Stardey Vallew vibes, so prepare for a lot of gathering, farming, fishing, but this time you  also need to build up an entire village and decorate a lot of homes (which implies a lot of gathering). Oh there is also cooking! So there are a lot of things to do and this will keep you busy for a lot of time!The games gives you different rewards in the form of different kind of decorations. The farming is really easy, you just need to plant a seed and then you can harvest the plant when you want since there are no seasonal or time problems. You can also adjust the terrain at your will (or at the will of the inhabitants if you follow their requests). There are a lot of upgrades! And you can build relationships too. And if you don't like relationships you can just adopt animals yay! All good...but. I was a little skeptical when i bought this game but then i really started to enjoy it. There are a lot of upgrades, a lot of things to do, a lot of things to find, to gather. And not only that. I was really looking forward for the relationships and the story. Yas, this game gave me a lot, A LOT, of expectations for the story. But, simply, at one point, after the game gives you some hint for a potential story, I understood that there was none. The other mega, MEGA, disappointment are the relationships. I was so eager to know the route of each of the character  but...no. A mega giga black hole. They repeat always the three\four default sentences, when you date them they tell you some other sentences. So you actually don't get to "know" them. I had a lot of expectations for this :/Other little things that i didn't like:1) I would have liked more upgrades for the terrain's expansion. 2) The General Store, after Port DeLuca is available, became pretty useless. 3) The farming is too basic 4) There are no cute city events (likes in SV) that makes you build up a sense of community with other villagers. (and i think in this kind of games, that is really important) I really really REALLY hope that the developers will take in consideration some upgrades of this game. _childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is a charming town-building game, but it's sunk by being so shallow that it almost feels like a clicker. You can't be terribly creative about your town construction because all your villagers want a house near specific things and with specific directions, and the deepest any of the resource collection gets is needing to press x again after about a second when fishing. All areas in the game are either a single screen or randomly generated, so there's no point in exploring, and all progress is gated behind getting a crapton of the same item and putting it in a place. The dev did at least lower the amount of each item you need after release and change rewards to be more varied, but that doesn't help much when the rewards are still completely useless except as things to sell. The best way I can describe Littlewood is a cross of Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing without any of the depth of either. I want to like this game, I really do, but I've played for 10 hours and the game has barely advanced at all from what I was doing five minutes in. It's just not very good.

_childDocuments_.review: There are things to like in Littlewood. It is a cute "stardew valley lite" resource management type of game, focused on rebuilding a jrpg kind of town. You have a limited number of actions every day that you spend on farming, gathering, crafting etc. It has it's charm and it has a way of drawing you in. However, it is just such a time sink and a slog, that you will quickly find yourself having been playing this game for several hours to no end - it has this "free mobile game" feel of having to waste frustrating amounts of time doing uninteresting things in order to get a tiny dopamine shot from being rewarded an uninteresting reward. The game has no challenge (unless you'd consider it an endurance challenge) and is more about just moping around and doing chores about your town and it's surrounding world. This would be fine, if you had some interesting things to do - unfortunately, your possibilities are very limited and most of the chores become tiresome very quickly. You have to do everything by hand and most of the time you are not building towards anything except some numbers that help you do the chores in a very insignificant way. Your main incentive to go through the motions is unlocking additional content for the game - mostly blueprints for your town (and furnishing your inhabitants house), a small number of additional locations or snippets of the story (for what it is). Unfortunately, after you get out of early game, getting those becomes significantly more time consuming, to the point that everything you receive feels like a disappointment in contrast to how much effort you had to put into it. The game is very cheap and i wouldn't mind it having little content - it could be fine for what it is, a fun little sandbox to build and decorate your jrpg town. It's colourful, charming, building the town is actually quite a bit of fun - it's starting several hours are rewarding and cool. However, instead of just accepting that this is a cute and small game, the devs decided to pad everything to the moon and back, making the game into an endurance test. One which i eventually failed.
