_childDocuments_.review: This game is Stardew Valley without all of the bells and whistles - for the better.My main points as to why someone would (or would not) enjoy this game are :1. It is not fast-paced, or, does not require a fast reaction time / time management in order to succeed2. Although it may not appear so for the first month or so, it is highly intuitive so long as the player is willing to make self-guided decisions. This means putting up with minor inconveniences for a short time.3. It's cute. It tried to be cute. Nobody is getting decapitated and there are no mature themes to spark philosophical debate.In the first hour that I played, I found myself getting frustrated by a few movement/object placement issues. This is likely going to happen to most players, yes, even you. After a couple more hours of puttering around, the game provided tools to deal with my issues. Problem solved. It's akin to having to wait for your running shoes or bicycle in early Pokemon games. It was frustrating then. It isn't perfect now. But, it provides meaningful progression. The clock in the game is based on actions performed; it is both a clock and a stamina bar. This means that all of my wandering around was not punished and allows exploration to go unfettered (there isn't much exploration to be done, though).The characters are cute and provide gameplay tips (press SHIFT to sprint!), as well as character building anecdotes. My only complaint is that they tend to repeat themselves after a while (and I know I'll be sitting through many more repeated phrases). Considering that talking to townies is a main gameplay loop, I look forward to the devs adding more dialogue and potentially even considering dialogue trees or at least yes-or-no questions with varying responses. If my only complaint is that I want to read more of your writing... Thanks, devs. This game is excellent and worth every dewdrop. It isn't Cyberpunk 2077, and for that, I am glad.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good at what it does at its core, like ... really good. The core gameplay is relaxing and enjoyable, with a larger focus on building, grinding and exploring than anything else. It'll keep you going for a long time, as there are plenty of collections to complete and resources to obtain, furniture to craft, villagers to bring into your town, etc.The only real issues I have with it, is that the story is interesting for what it is, but there's no real ending. There's nothing it culminates to. It just sort of ... ends, and that's it. It's very disappointing considering how integral the story seemed to be from the very beginning. The second issue being the grind gets to become too monotonous and boring at the very end. Breeding flowers for the museum's collection is honestly a headache to get done, to the point it's put me off actually finishing it because of how long and tedious it feels to get done compared to anything else in the game. Getting villager friendship to maximum for everybody doesn't do much, either. There's ultimately very little if nothing to actually do at the end (having max in every skill, every villager in my town, having done everything bar the very last quest and finishing the flower collection), but the journey there is well worth it IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a revision on my last review as whats fair is fair. Although still bare bones there has been a lot of improvement from the devs. The content has expanded since my last play through and I think it is at a stange now where it is playable. Not bad if you wanna waste an hour casually and the characters are quite cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome little pixel farm/crafting game. Cute characters, lovely dialogue, refreshing format. Every task is short and sweet, do whatever you feel like each day and progress the way you want to. Your task is to slowly develop the town of Littlewood. To do this you will grow crops, build homes, decorate the village, complete tasks for villagers, go fishing, collect bugs, play a card mini game, mine, chop trees and cook recipes! Littlewood is most definitely one of my favourite casual games to date ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: A meh-level endorsement, largely because it's not actively irritating in how it falls short of the games that get it recommended to you.  My mom calls the book equivalent of this game a pot-boiler.Don't expect Stardew from it.  It's a much less balanced game - and particularly seems to load a bunch of the fun bits toward the beginning in a way that might lead you to think that there will continue to be little cut scenes and such at a steady pace as time goes by. That doesn't really happen, which is disappointing - especially when you finally unlock things or finish huge projects late in the game and ... absolutely nothing happens.  It's got much shallower events and interactions/character development than SDV.That said, the premise of it being a post-combat game is interesting - even if all the worldbuilding background info doesn't really go anywhere but the increasingly strong suspicion the developer wants to build more games in this setting.Some things are very very reminiscent of Animal Crossing: New Horizons, but again, on a very simplified level.  The flower system - which you would do well to pay more attention to earlier in the game than I did - is one such thing.  And you have to grind grind grind through finding resources to get anything where you want it to go.  That could be good or bad, depending on what you like.  The card game's okay, and I usually kinda hate card mini-games of the same sort.  And it's cute and kind of soothing that, with maybe two exceptions, you can leave your character standing around wherever if you need to go get a drink (or hell, go to sleep or go do something else for a couple days - I did) because you aren't on a running-down clock so much as a limited pool of energy for taking most productive actions. A few late game perks are kinda game-breaking in a non-gradual way.  The game would be better if that weren't so... instantaneous.  Which I am being vague about because, well, spoilers.  All saving is auto, and there's no way to save scum if you realize you proposed to the wrong person, say, so be on your guard.Anyway.  There's something soothing here.  No Moonlight Jellies or lucky shorts moments - it's never going to live up to that kind of competition.  No sense of wanting to inhabit the place so much.  But Toby is pretty hilarious, and it's fine if you don't get your hopes too high.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, Littlewood suffers from being aggressively average. As much as I like life sims like Littlewood, Littlewood is really a life sim taken to the most bare bones a game in the genre could go. The overarching story of an already saved world isn't well expanded upon, the characters aren't very well fleshed out, and the gameplay is pretty much all grind. If you view games as more than just a way to pass the time, skip Littlewood.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is a very cute and cozy farm sim. It is a great game, but I can't recommend it, what is weird, because I will keep playing it for a while until I get bored of it again. The first few hours of the game are great, you have progression and it is fun and really cozy, particularly, I enjoy very much that you don't need to worry about the passing of time, because you use your stamina as the "clock", a downside to it is that you are very limited about what you can do in the game and I couldn't find a way to increase your stamina bar... Another good side of the game is it's lack of combat system, you can get kicked off a dungeon because of a slime... but you can't hurt them, so you have to be creative, the creatures will not follow you, instead they have different speeds and a random walk pattern, but one hit and you are out of the ressource dungeon. The level up system for the skills makes no sense, since (for what I saw) it makes no difference during gathering or stamina consumption or quality of the materials that you got... the only thing it does is the after reaching levels 60 and 99 you can open chests with -spoiler- stuff inside. Oh, also... it's VERY GRINDY. What makes me feels that the devs tried to make a 15/20 hour game last WAY more than what it should.The story is cute, tho :) and very heartwarming. AND YOU CAN DATE THE NPCS!! in a way that feel more organic that just give them gifts and such.The "museum" mechanic is very nice, but it lacks a way for you to understand better the items and how and where to collect them, you really NEED to look trough wikipedia to understand how to get everything. For example, the flower farming system... since you don't get the watering can that easily, you can't water your flowers :V, but when it rains, the flower reproduce themselves and it is a very creative gameplay choice, since the only way to get different "species"/colors/shapes is by putting 2 flowers next to each other and let them do their own thing (it's cute, I made it sound boring, but it feels really organic in the game).TL;DRFun history and gameplay, lot's of positive aspects that become kinda boring on the long run. I'll keep playing it because I already bought it and every now and then it is nice to mindless farm stuff :V.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: i'm only seven hours in at the writing of this review, but I can tell you this game is worth it. While it does have a Stardew Valley/Animal Crossing feel to it, I feel it's different enough to be on its own merits. There is plenty to do, from fishing to mining to gathering items. You can even ask NPCs in your town to follow you as a Hang Out feature! I appreciate that time is based on your energy level in this game. The characters each have their own backstories and reasons for wanting to settle in the town of Littlewood. The lore behind the cuts scenes is interesting enough that I am excited to see the coming updates.I wish there was currently a way to fight off Wompers and Dark Trees, though. At the writing of this review, that's all I can think of as an improvement. Sometime NPCs clip through buildings on different levels, but it's in Beta right now so that's acceptable.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: tldr; I loved this game and if you are a fan of games like Animal Crossing and Harvest Moon it will likely be up your alley! Bigger review here, for those unaware, I pretty much only review games I 100%!  This game was an amazing experience and super fun to integrate into my daily routine. It'd usually play a few days at a time. Though, it can definitely be enjoyable all at once too if you have the time. The characters were very cute, and I though they were well portrayed. Though, I definitely wouldn't complain about having more events with them during the dating part of the game. The customization is surprisingly varied, especially considering how little this game costs. If you are big on collecting items in games, there is a lot here for you too! Over all I'd recommend it, it was a fun and relaxing game. I was able to put a lot of hours into it on my way to 100%!
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I spent a long time playing this, I have enjoyed it a lot! It does suffer from seeming a little grind-y in the end, however if I hadn't rushed through the first bit and kind of did a little of everything throughout I wouldn't have been grinding so much at the end. And by the end I mean after beating the storyline and trying to get all the achievements. I really like how there's no timer and later on you get an item to extend the day. I like that there's no penalty to destroying things and remaking you're whole town - you get all the materials back! Very chill forgiving game.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, chill town-building game. Emphasis on the building, because the core of the game is building your town, upgrading various structures, and filling out the townsfolk's homes. Don't come into this assuming it's like Stardew Valley or Story of Seasons - the townsfolk interaction is pretty barebones, and farming is just a side activity.Despite how simple the core gameplay is, the flow of things will suck you in for hours. There's always something to do, and nothing you do is ever truly a waste of time(or energy, in this case - time passes in this game based on actions you do). The art is simple but effective, and the music lacks variety but doesn't really get old.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Love the premise and design of this game! It looks like a classic rpg game but... the world has already been saved from the big bad evil, there are no monsters around but everything was destroyed and it is your task to rebuild! The environment and characters look fantastic, with great animations despite the minimalist look, it is wonderful pixel art. It also plays great on the steam deck so that is a plus: good controls, no performance issues and long lasting battery life, making it a great 'portable' title.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: The game is overwhelming and underwhelming at the same time. It's both full of stuff to do, but none of that stuff feels very rewarding. There's no timer, but you never feel like you got anything done in a day. You have the freedom to build a town the way you want, but to get rewards from the villagers you need to build it the way  want.I have a hard time recommending this game. It just falls very flat for me. There is a lot of stuff to do- you can garden, fish, catch bugs, talk to your villagers, etc, but none of it is really engrossing. Take gardening for example. I like building up a garden, watering, harvesting, and then either selling or cooking what I've gathered. In this game you can't do that, though. Not really. You're arbitrarily limited in how many garden plants you can plant- not because of space, but because the game says you can only have so many. So, you're forced into other activities that you may not enjoy- and in the process you lose enjoyment out of the thing you did enjoy because you can't do it.The game really focuses on what  wants you to do.  wants you to build a village and make stupid NPCs happy through furnishing their living rooms with specific stuff or putting their houses near specific things. Everything outside of that is just to get supplies, make money, and get the correct plans to  those mindless NPCs happy. And they're so rude! "" Because I didn't want you in my village in the first place, but I didn't have a choice because the game demands I take care of you. Build your own damn house, I'm busy.I was looking for a more laidback version of Stardew Valley, something where I didn't have to plan out crops weeks in advance or be at the mercy of time- what I got was a game that demands me to play it in a very specific way. And I do not like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is relaxing and compromising in a way other sim games aren't. Simple, grindy, and full of character - Littlewood is a very pared-down town builder with very intuitive features and a great atmosphere. If you're easily bored by games like Stardew or Animal Crossing, this game may not be for you, but if you want to listen to a podcast and chop wood with your little pixel boyfriend, this might be your new favorite game.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exceedingly cute in its simplistic graphics. There are a lot of aspects of this game I would describe as simple. The mechanics themselves are so simple as to not really require much forethought; though, this also means that you can't do anything wrong. But the game mechanics are also simple enough to be played entirely with one hand. The incredibly simplistic repetition of the game's day cycles left me in a frequent mind fog.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I first discovered this in my recommendations, as I am a frequent player of Stardew Valley, and decided to check it out. Upon first playing the game, I was struck by how familiar the artstyle was -- only to find out that it was made by the very person who did the art for Kindergarten! If that was not exciting enough, the premise of the game in itself was quite unique. Instead of starting out as a nobody or normal person, you instead start out as a renown hero after an adventure, with absolutely no memory of it, of course. This got me excited, as I was looking forward to learning more about the Hero of Solemn as I played the game. Though I did get bits and pieces about what my character was like beforehand (mainly through dialogue with characters that already knew the protagonist like Willow, Dalton, etc.), I was a bit disappointed that I did not get particular details about the adventures and relationships that I had with my friends, though this could easily be forgiven by one's own interpretation of the events. Additionally, while the plot is interesting, I do wish that some more light was shed on it, as I was left with a lot of unanswered questions. Fortunately from what I heard, the creator is working on a new game that'll tie in with the world of Littlewood.That aside, the overall gameplay was really pleasant for me, and one thing of note that I highly commend is how time and energy work. Instead of being confined to a certain frame of time per day, the in-game time instead proceeded with one's actions; in other words, time and energy were one and the same. This was especially great for someone like me, who gets easily stressed by limited or timed events. I was able to take the time to explore the overall world of the game, all while being able to plan out my daily schedule. Additionally, there is a lot to do in the game -- from doing basic outdoor activities like fishing, farming, etc. to forming romantic relationships with members of the town. Another thing I love is the large pool of eligible bachelors and bachelorettes (literally everyone except one person is a marriage candidate). And while I could describe the other features, I think it would be best for one to experience them for themselves.So would I recommend this game to others? Absolutely. Especially if you enjoy slow-paced rpgs like Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing. It's seriously underrated and I could tell a lot of love and hard work went into this project. I truly hope more people will give it the attention that it deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO cute! I feel like there was another game that came previous to it, because it seems like there's a lot of lore, but I could be wrong. I really enjoy this game! You can build your own town, and make it exactly as you want. You can get married, and have pets! I've already started a game, but it had been a long time so I restarted with a new game to get the hang of it again. It seems short, and there's not a lot other than the achievements but it's definitely a good game and I highly recommend it if you enjoy games like Stardew Valley.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game and was sad when I completed everything there was to do.I've never really played a game quite like this one before, but it generally has been said to be a blend of Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing. There is a lot to do in this game, from gathering materials, crafting items, meeting friends, finding collectables, designing your town, and more.The visual style in this game is bright and colorful, simple yet adorable. The music is fun and soothing. There is no real rush to do things in this game. With only a couple of exceptions, the player can progress in any order and at any pace of their choosing.The only two (very minor) drawbacks to this game are (1) the backstory is pretty simple (I wanted more of this to uncover) and (2) the endgame achievements can be a bit of a grind (which I didn't mind, but other players have been discouraged by this).I played this game for nearly 80 hours unlocking everything and completing all Steam achievements. This game is definitely worth its asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Other reviews compare this game to Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing. I see where that comparison comes from, but I think it does this game a disservice. It's a good game and worth the money, but is not nearly as polished, and that comparison left me disappointed with the game in the first few hours. I'm giving this a thumbs up because I've put a lot of time into it, it was generally relaxing to play, and I'm giving it the benefit of the doubt that it's a very new game, so improvements are likely coming.TL;DR It's a cute little game that's relatively stress free and reminiscent of other games in this genre, but there's lots of room for improvement.Some things I appreciate about the game:- You can navigate menus with just the keyboard- Navigating around the maps is good. Being able to leave the map to go home from the quick menu is a nice shortcut.- In game time ticks away with actions, not a clock constantly moving forward.- There's no tool micromanaging. As long as the tools are in my inventory, my character can seamlessly choose the correct one for the action I'm attempting to take.- There's no concept of storage space. You don't have to manage a bunch of chests of stuff, or drop everything on the floor.- Building isn't stressful because if you demolish something, you get the resources back, so you can endlessly move things around to make the town however you want.- I haven't encountered any bugs or crashes.By less polished, I mean that I'm 16 hours into the game and there's many aspects of the game that seem to serve no purpose or otherwise don't make sense.- After a villager moves in there's almost no point in talking to them unless you want to date them. You only really need to be close to one other villager.- "Rare items": I have 20 or so items in my inventory with no clear purpose. I'm saving them because inventory space isn't an issue, but the game starts giving you these early on and it is still not clear where I'll need them. And assuming I will eventually need them, it's unclear where I'd go to get them aside from continuing to play the game in the hopes I'd find the specific item I need, or it becomes available in a shop. You get rare items by upgrading things, but that just feels messy. It doesn't make sense for the player to put effort into upgrading everything for these rare items that barely matter. Right now I'm just upgrading everything because it feels like that's what the game wants me to do, but I don't really know why.- Upgrading buildings feels like a way to suck resources out of the game with minimal rewards.- The way the early game unfolds leaves the player wondering what they're supposed to be doing. I ended up just continuing to gather resources until nightfall, which threw off the balance of the game because then there was no effort when someone wanted to move to the town -- I already had everything to build their house immediately. Then I was back to not knowing what to do.- There have been a few events which requested things that I hadn't unlocked yet. Not sure if this is because the calendar is randomly generated for each person/save file, or a flaw in the sequence of events in the story. Either way, it left me kind of disgruntled that I couldn't complete these 'special events'.- Filling the villagers houses with requests is an interesting idea, but I'm at the point where villagers want things I can't find. Do I have to be buying out the shop for it to change items? Also I haven't paid enough attention, but will the shop have an item you already own? Do I need to be keeping track of things I've already bought? If it's up to the player to keep track, there should be a way to check what you've bought without leaving the store and going to a villager's home to open the build menu. This one may just be something I'm missing, but contributes to the overall feeling that the pieces of the game don't quite fit together.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is done so well! It's addictive, peaceful, adorable, and just plain fun. The 32 hours I have at the time of this review is from maybe 4 days of playing it... That's how addicted to it I got right away. It's not a "oh no I have to stress to finish this in a 3 day deadline!" kind of game it really is entirely up to you how quickly you want to get things done.One of my favorite aspects is that there isn't day to day time in this game. As in you don't wake up at 6am and only have until 10pm to do what you want in the day. Instead Littlewoods daily time is based entirely on your characters stamina bar, when you've run out of stamina the day is over. However if you choose to stand around and appreciate your town and the people just by walking around, then the day could last as long as you want. That really makes the game not feel stressful or like it's rushing you. This game may not have quite as much content in it as say Stardew Valley, but honestly I think this game is both cuter and more enjoyable if you're looking for a relaxing 'build your own farm/town/relationships' kind of way. I hope theres DLC or a second game that goes into the under world they mention :D
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Stardew Valley or the Harvest Moon games, but want a little more variety in your options, a little more time in your day, and a little more control over the town you live in, this game is what you want. It's a little addictive, it's great for that rush of dopamine you get when completing a task, and offers plenty of cute dialogue from cute characters and what I'm sure is an infinite list of things to do as you work on building a town that suits you and all your NPCs greatest whims. Magnificent, cute, and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: You decide the pace of the game, whether you want to rush things or just take it slow. Remodeling your town has vast possibilities even with what seems like little to work with. The townsfolk have a great variety of personalities,  as you get to know them. Good humor is everywhere in this game. All of the controls are amazingly simple, allowing you to play with only one hand if you like (I'm lazy and have definitely capitalized on this). Interactions and crafting are easy to understand at just a glance, keeping the game simple and casual for those who love that. There is so much to explore even in this unfinished state of the game.Overall, I am in love with it. The 68 hours I've played so far have flown by. There's still so much I haven't unlocked yet, leaving a lot to see even with the time I've already sunk into it. I've found the community for this game to be wonderful as well, full of welcoming, helpful, and good people. Littlewood has been everything I wanted from it and more. I can't wait to see it grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is deceptive, in a good way. The simplistic graphics hide a surprisingly layered interface and system. Characters are charming, mechanics are fun, and play style is entirely up to the gamer. You can be a farmer, a forger, a miner, or all of the above. You unlock different things through tiers with items of varying difficulty to obtain. Or you can stay on the core level and build up something else. There's so much to do and so many ways to play. Highly recommended for casuals and completion freaks alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very addicting, I played nearly 7 hours in my first time opening the game, idk how long it will stay addicting but it's in general very pleasing, most of the characters are interesting enough, i dislike very few of them. Its' definitely a chill game or a game you can play when you don't have much time or that you can sit down and sink quite a few hours in to without any disruptions within the game like time gates, etc. It reminds me a lot of animal crossing meets stardew valley/harvest moon and I'm here for it. I really enjoy the time system and that the days are based off of what you achieve rather than a ticking clock or irl time, I haven't seem much of this kind of time system and I actually really like it for this game. The art is very cute. My only real complaint as of this review is that I can't ask Toad to move in, he's one of my favorites, I would of preferred him over Ash! :pBubsy is love, Bubsy is life. That is all XD

I love the art style and even with seventeen hours of game time I'm not to deep into the story line that I think I'm going to complete it in the next seventeen hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a grind fest. Youll build buildings based off what the towns folk tell you to do. To make money you can farm for items and craft them into dishes for the pub. Your progress (at least early on) is hindered by doing 1 objective per person each day. You may have the energy to do more but the game insists that you do one thing each day. If you want a farming game, get stardew valley. If you want a farminng game and youve finished stardew valley, get a switch and get Rune Factory 4. Perfect for a lazy afternoon.Pros: Really relaxed, doesn't feel grindy so far, cute story premiseCons: The terrain manipulation is a bit painful, occasionally feels a little too chill
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Cutest little game I've come across. I saw someone on Twitch playing and had to have it. It's along the same lines as many other games - Forager, Survivalists, etc. Grind out for the story line, interact with the NPCs, solve quests and get items to sell/upgrade/complete story pieces. I'm near end-game and keep putting off because I enjoy the story and am not quite ready to "finish". Repeatable and very casual. My only complaint is that there are some time-sensitive elements or elements that you can only complete once in a day. Even though you get limited stamina, it does add to the challenge of the game (which is low in general) but can make it a bit frustrating when you need that *one* thing and you have to go through several days to return to a specific location to get it. Doesn't happen often, but happened enough times to mention it. Not off-putting, just a slight bit annoying. Still would recommend as a casual little game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute town rebuilding game. I love that there's no combat and your main focus is building up a town after the climactic battle. Now, this game has a grind. It does take time to acquire rare items and level up hobbies to unlock perks. If you max fishing, your catches are no longer limited by season. You could catch anything, and that's fun. There are some cons to this game. The creator didn't write enough dialogue for villagers. I stopped talking to villagers after a while. Crossbreeding flowers is a painful undertaking. My advice is to start collecting flowers early and make hybrids as soon as possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: if you loved stardew valley and generaly like games like that.. this game is made for you !!onestly, i first "got it illigaly" basicly cracked the game ... after only 2h of gameplay.. just baught it. the money was deserved even tho its a bit on the expensive side for the contents proposed (wen i got it )hope developpement goes well !
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: The most relaxing game on steam by far. Very indepth town customization and house decorating, satisfying gameplay. I was always doing something different each day and never felt bored. The romance options are great, the townspeople are all quirky and unique in their own ways. The soundtrack isn't killer, obviously, but it lends to the atmosphere so well.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This is so cute!! I purchased the game because of the reviews and I ended up playing for 7 hours straight. It took sheer will power to turn off the game and go to bed. If you're a fan of any of the Harvest Moon games or Animal Crossing I think you will enjoy this.  It doesn't have the same depth, detail or complexities of those games, but it was nice to have the same elements and style. Despite it still being early access, there is so much to do to keep you busy. You can see there are areas that are blocked off, or temporary text that actually leaves me excited to see how this game will develop into something more. PROS- I love that you can move things around once it's built. Every new member to the town wants a house that you have to build that you can freely move later and that goes for any of the buildings. I can recreate my town as I see fit. - I absolutely LOVE that your character is genderless. What a change. You don't pick between a male or female character, you are just you. You choose your hair (which can make you look either way) and your clothes and then you're on your way to flirt with whoever you please. - There's no "time" limit. The day shift is based on your energy. Most games you'll see the time ticking away, but with this game you have a certain limit of energy you use for tasks. When you hit about 75% energy, it turns into night. When you max out your bar, it's time for bed and to start a new day or you'll pass out (much similarly to other games). I don't feel that pressure of having to complete tasks before the end of day.- There's no same demand to feel your animals. I have little exposure to them so far, but the sheep I interact with only asks for a certain food every so often. It's not the same thing every single day where you have to feed it something specific and groom it for it to be happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: You can play for 5 minutes at a time, or 5 hours.  The dialogue and characters are cute and funny.  There's not time limits; no ticking clock to keep track of and make sure you get everything done at a certain time *or you might miss it*.  Simple?  Maybe.  But it's a very easy game to pick up and play as long or short as you like.  It's a great breather to enjoy if you feel like getting a little gaming in but don't want to commit to something serious.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed a good 10 hours from this game but after that the game becomes more of a grind, it stopped being fun to run the same path through my town every single day to drop of planks or bricks at every building so the can eventually get upgraded. I'd still recommend the game as it is relaxing and and gave me a good amount of enjoyment at the beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of work has been put into this game and a lot of work still needs to be done. Even so, the game content quality and quantity is impressive for an early access game. Very easy to sink a lot of time into without getting bored of the grind, for there is always something different to do.The main story line is explored by building up relationships with the people around you, and unlocking different areas.With the ability to completely control how your town is built, from houses, to lakes, and hills, no two save files will be the same. NPC's have a wide variety of personality and will comment on a variety of topics; with the personal tasks of furnishing their homes, the player still has complete creative freedom. The more you upgrade your town, the more they have to say!There is heavy inspiration from Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing, all paired with a cute style than reminds me of NDS Pokemon. A beautifully blended game all in all, definitely recommend for anyone who likes easy going games.As more of the game is updated and explored, will edit as necessary.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy Littlewood so much that I looked up the developer and realized, oh, surprise, it's SmashGames, who also made Magicite and Roguelands, both excellent games. I shouid really just follow his releases.Littlewood is not pulse-pounding or quick reaction type gaming, it's a super chill town builder, where you gradually increase your skills, unlock new areas and decorate your village. It's a genre of gaming that I appreciate infinitely more the older and more stressed out I get with work and stuff - playing Littlewood, and games like it, are kind of like meditation rather than frenetic gameplay. Littlewood was suggested to me because I like Stardew Valley, Graveyard Keeper and Forager, so if you're into those games, you'll be into this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I had my eyes on Littlewood for a long time wondering how good it would be and I think it was well worth getting now I've finished it. My hours are mostly from the achievements so just don't think this is representative of anything but that. It's a very relaxed and relaxing game, obviously the core aspects are building your town and gathering resources which are both not demanding in terms of grinding. Don't misunderstand me there is a bit of a grind towards the mid-end game but it's nothing insane. Essentially you will build houses for others and diverse facilities that will let you buy stuff for your town or yourself. Your character doesn't fight but your tools will get some upgrades after doing some favours for your citizens but none of them I'd say will make your life that terribly different. The story is passable, I wish it was more developed it kind of ends abruptly and it feels unsatisfying. Same goes for the events, they are a quite forgettable and underwhelming and there are very few of them. You get 4 seasons but they all blend together I think the only noticeable difference is for some loot with bug catching and fishing the rest stays the same so you will be able to farm and gather all the same all year around. Building is really forgiving which I really like, you can remove stuff and you will get 100% of what you spent back while the menu feels like it was made for a controller it's fairly good to use you just need to get used to basically stop using your mouse altogether in this game. The characters are nice but mostly forgettable, I think it's because all the events or dates you do with them are short and happen at the same exact location. Something I liked in terms of events is when you level characters and it triggers a conversation between them, while they also all happened at the same place it gave a bit more personality since it's the only way you get to see them interact with each others. Overall I know it sounds like I'm complaining more than praising but I really liked the game it's a good purchase for someone who wants to build a little town and relax while gathering resources. If you are looking to buy for those reasons I think you'll like it too just don't expect some good story with well developed characters and crazy events. I know it says "relaxing RPG" in the description but the only thing that is RPG is basically you gaining levels with your citizens and non-combat skills.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: After close to 80 hours, I have 100%ed this game. Its a really neat gem that i did enjoy, not without its drawbacks.It is an addicting game where you are rebuilding the town and collecting as much stuff as you can to unlock upgrades, items and buildings, build relationships with people and unlock a small story underneath it all.You use skills to collect items though mining, farming, woodcutting, fishing being the main ones plus a few extras to add diversity to your game such as crafting and Tarot-Monster.The lore goes flat very fast, the interesting backstory in books you collect and the in game cut scenes show potential for a story, but it is never really shown any further then that. It comes across as there was going to be more but it will never be told. It really does make the story feel half told as there was so much here that could be expanded on so easily, but it wont ever be.You unlock two major places at endgame, one is a forge that you hardly use but for a few upgrades and one is a place where you get a fun item that I used once and it holds no other purpose to ever go back again. Getting the final place was almost like a empty achievement and I felt there could of been more there or even something to do there to add to it.Characters that have major leaps in development tend to have their auto dialogue back to a mood that shows that the cutscene meant nothing at all. So your investment of raising levels in friendship seeing anything further beyond a cutscene or book will be fruitless. Only after you are married you will see a few extra parts of character development, however it is very flat. Levelling everything to level 99 is fruitless as by the point of the game you don't need the upgrades, the only benefit is that if you were to do a second play-through, you would go hard on mining and woodcutting to level 99 as fast as you could as they are the only ones that have any benefit to allow you to go 100% completion easier.The fact the fish spawns are continuously gimped was the major crutch for 100% completion, You are also bound to a RNG that is painful before you hit that level 99 woodcutting/mining trophy. After then as soon as you get them the game is trivialised and your just grinding because achievements. I feel that overall this game had the potential to be more then it was, yes its now considered old in terms of release as I've picked it up and played it now in 2024, but for any one new coming into this today, it's a good game for a sale price and good to pass time, but don't throw yourself deep into the Wikipedia for anything more, because it's not here. There are no new updates, the developer has been working on a new game and has not indicated that he will be back to throw any more updates at this game at all. While that's not a bad thing or should be an expected thing for a game that can be completed with a start and an end, it's clear that there is a lot missing here in terms of story and features that ultimately left a bit of a empty feeling.The fact that things don't need to be fully levelled up because the reward is something you get too little to late to enjoy the benefit really makes it feel like an empty achievement and at the end your just bankrolling the currency because you've bought everything and it's now dead inventory. I feel like I've complained a lot about this game here, but again I did enjoy it and recommend to those who like these nice and chill cosy games. Just don't go in expecting a "stardew" experience here. Still major props to the dev making something that was entertaining and fun and if a sequel or an update comes out to expand on the story of Solemn, I wouldn't turn it down to experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as life sims go, it hits all the regular marks. I feel that storage and simplicity are two of it's strongest points, even going so far as to say this game does better than most. Inventory management is definitely part of life, but I like that this game simplifies that and doesn't punish you for it like some can. Also, the simplicity with crafting and building is refreshing from some games that require a lot of grinding.Otherwise, the game is bound to change from this early stage of development. So I'm excited to see what they will continue to tweak and improve.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is exactly the kind of relaxing, utterly charming game that I needed, right now. If you like games such as Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, or Harvest Moon, you will feel right at home, here. I am having an absolute blast getting to know my new neighbors and building my town. I think the feature that I appreciate the most is the energy system. Instead of having time pass as normal, time only passes when you do something that requires energy, such as harvesting, mining, fishing, etc. So, if I feel like running around and talking to everyone, I don't have that pressure of "oh my gosh! The day is getting away from me!" if there were other things I wanted to do, as well. I simply go talk to all the folks then go do whatever I wanted to do. But, the energy system does mean that I have to choose what I want to do. If I spend a bunch of time crafting, I may not have much time left to go out and harvest. But, again... that's not really an issue. It just means that you do that other stuff on the next day. This really is a no pressure kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with Littlewood although the game has some flaws. Visually it's quite cute and the vast amount of goals keep you moving. I like the lighter tone of the game and the characters are charming.But, this game is incredibly grindy, repetitive and the tasks feel empty sometimes. If you're a completionist, I believe this can be a fun experience. If you just want a rich story, this game probably won't be for you.Either way I can feel this game was created by hard-working devs and I'll be keeping an eye out for their next work!
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: It's really good! Going to compare it to Stardew Valley, but I feel more engaged with the villagers and the main story on this on! Also an option to travel to different islands and stuff. Only thing I would like is diagonal walking movement (this is a big one) and also rotation for more objects in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood has everything that I want for a game. Lovely graphics. relaxing soundtracks, diverse characters with quirky dialogues, and a lot of things to do. The in-game clock only work when you do something (means that if you left your game open for 10 minutes or 1 day, you came back right when you left). You set out at your own pace, there is no rush or any consequences in this game. This game can be a relaxing game, yet it can be stressing too if you choose to. What I like the most is probably how easy it is to decorate/moving objects, it's simple, clean, and fast. So to those of you guys who are indecisive like me, don't worry, you can redecorate your town with no hassle at all. The characters also feel 'real' and unique. There is Bubsy—a green sassy bird, who thinks that he's a fashion icon and keep insulting others in a mean funny way.  Even though the dialogues lines can be repetitive (or probably I just spent a lot of time in this game lol), I genuinely enjoy the NPC's conversations.But seriously guys, what I love the most is you keep finding a new stuffs/things to do. Although the game can be grindy at times, Littlewood is worth it! My favorite game in 2020 so far. Love you Littlewood :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very much like Stardew Valley, except with a little less seriousness and slightly more simplified gameplay. Much of the gameplay is less challenging than Stardew, so if this could make things boring, you might not want this game. However, it does include a mini-game of a trading card game like Magic: The Gathering or Pokemon which does actually require some skill.It's pretty interesting to play a game that starts after the adventure ends...or did it?
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes all you want after a hard day is to sit back, relax, and chill by playing a game, with watching a show, listening to music, or contemplating your entire life. If your looking for that kind of game, Littlewood is here for you. It's one of those games that fun and interesting, but doesn't demand your attention constantly. You can safely go to the bathroom, doze off, or fall of the face of the Earth and Littlewood is right where you left it. You don't have to fear that your not maximizing your time efficiently, just chill slowly build up a town, collect items for the museum, fish, mine, or spend 5 hours painstakingly redesigning your entire town, because one of your villagers is being picky about where they want their house. It's good, it's chill, you'll enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game play feels similar to Stardew Valley, especially with energy depleting rapidly for short days at first, until you build up your in-game stamina. I enjoy getting to plan out the town and to decorate, and things went much faster once I figured out how to delete/move/add the taller elevations or change the layouts of ponds. The story isn't as heavy as Stardew, its a cozier gameplay without fighting (so far), though (SPOILER) there are hints that "the darkness" could return in some form, so things may get heavier story-wise later. Currently just coasting and building up resources to complete town tasks - feels like the story has plateaued a bit, but is still a fun cozy game to play without needing to overthink things!
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Great city builder/rpg. Easy to learn, and very user-friendly. As a parent, it's easy to get distracted and leave the clock running on games like this, but the way that time moves forward is based on your actions--so it's not a problem! Lots of characters, lots of items, lots of building and exploring opportunities. Yet, this game is not overwhelming in the slightest. One of my fave features? The option to teleport back home at the end of the day so you can just rest up and start the next day. Can't wait to see this game evolve even more
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This is sweet, relaxing, wholesome - and addictive. I love that the passage of time is based on you doing energy-consuming actions, and that actions like talking to townspeople, watering flowers, and moving things around as you design your town, don't use up energy. The game looks great too - using a bright palette with simple but well-made pixel graphics. There's a core mystery that helps drive the story, and some cool interactions between NPCs which give them lives beyond their relationships with and utility to the player character. I got this game for Christmas, it's now 27th December, and I've got 25 hours logged already.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: THIS IS MY CRITICAL REVIEW: 6/10 (I may change this in the future)Pros- Addictive gameplay- Simple and charming graphics- Calming music- Very chill compared to other Harvest Moon-esque games!Cons- HEAVY grind- Very repetitive- NPCs need more content-  definitely wasted potentialThis game is super carefree: no consequences to move buildings, you can do whatever you like with your in-game day, there is no rush to finish the game! Time is associated with your energy bar and will only pass with every action you take. I applaud to the devs for creating a game that allows the player to sit back and actually relax and not feel restrained by time, and not feel the need to plan out every passing day. The gameplay really is up to you! BUT...The game is fun but I wouldn't be able to play it for more than a few hours per day just because the grind is so repetitive. The game allows you to explore skills such as woodcutting, bug catching, fishing, mining, farming, gathering, etc... but I've only grazed the bug catching and fishing features because all I do is grind for wood and stone for upgrades on a daily basis.  Within 4 hours of gameplay, I noticed NPCs have repeating and re-occuring dialogue, which makes it harder for myself to get attached to them. Why am I complaining? I feel obligated to continue talking to them everyday in case there's a new blueprint to receive and I keep hoping I'll be charmed by at least one of them. Littlewood emphasizes on its biggest feature: rebuilding your entire town, but there is wasted potential on its mechanics. Moving objects by keyboard is extremely painful if you have like 10 trees from the left side of your town and you want to move them all the way to the right side of your town. You can only make ponds or lakes on the lowest ground level, stairs are only built on the front of the cliff, (it cannot go sideways or on the backside of the cliff) and there could honestly be more outdoor decor. I really wanted picnic tables or swinging benches to put in my little town, but the only options available are a zillion statues or potted plants...IN MY HONEST OPINION, I believe Littlewood was released as a full game too early. You'd be happier waiting for a sale with the lack of balance in gameplay and content in Littlewood. I can't recommend the game in its current state right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

It reminds me of Animal Crossing and Stardew Valley, two games I also love :D (I like laid back games)What I love most about this game is that I'm not 'timed', I don't have to race against the clock to get things done but instead I have an amount of energy every day to do what I need to do.I like to plan my days out, like on Monday I go mining, Tuesday I go gather wood, etc.I also love all the characters and their different personalities, I can't even choose a favorite :CIf you like laid back, colorful and cheery games, I definitely recommend Littlewood!I'm not the best at making reviews but I hope I can be of help to someone who was thinking of getting this game :>P.S when can I date Toad

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood first caught my eye due to my mounting boredom with New Horizons on my switch. Terraforming is so... terrible in that game. Anyway the simplistic but cute pixel graphics, character design, and just the fact that it takes place in a post- RPG plot world had me totally sold. (And the fact I can be gay. Seriously. Automatic interest just from that.)I hardcore binged a solid 20+ hours within 2 weeks of me getting it. I had to force myself to stop playing just so I wouldn't burn out. I'm sure it's a brilliant game, as shown by the reviews on here, but it's just not for me. It's like a simplified Stardew Valley. Requested a refund to see if I can save the £10 I spent on this.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so fun it's dangerous, and the fact that it's that fu n despite still being in development just goes to show how incredible it is! I've sunk 8 hours already, and I'm only a little over 10% "done" with the game (according to the Journal feature). A lot of content is still "coming soon" in-game, but I'm totally fine with that, because it means it's going to take that much longer to get old. The only thing I would change if I could is to make an eating feature to regain some of the energy you lose during everyday activities--the crops you farm and dishes you cook should be edible to you too, not just the townspeople! Other than that, though, this game is one of the best I've played in a very long time, if not EVER. It takes all the best parts of my other favorite games and makes them cuter and more charming. So relaxing. Animal Crossing meets Stardew Valley, for real. I can't wait to see what the devs add next!!! SERIOUSLY, BUY IT NOW, YOU WON'T BE SORRY.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun, Stardew LITE (very lite) style game. You can craft, harvest food, cook, sell, all the standard life sim actions (fishing, mining, etc.) in a cute little world. It's one of those games you can pop on for a little bit and just have a great time. There's no dying, there's no terrible consequences I've found so far. It's also cool to see that I am still unlocking things this far into the game. I will say it's kind of a grind to get the in-game currency and continue to upgrade different buildings, however the upgrades don't always use the in-game currency, sometimes it'll be planks or ore.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I have very mixed feelings about this game as well, and before I go anymore into this review this is NOTHING like Stardew Valley as someone with hundreds of hours sunk into Stardew this is not a carbon copy of Stardew and is completely different.What I like about the game:-It's not like Stardew valley, now what do I mean by this? Well there is farming, wood chopping, fishing,etc but with how these concepts are incoperated in Littlewood is vastly different, faster (due to world/map Size) as well as there isn't a big emphasis on the concept of farming as Stardew Valley and for me I like that because there are times in Stardew where the farming/crops aspect feels more like a chore than it should be at times. This game does well to "copy" Stardew Valley but is different enough to where it isn't just a Carbon Copy where I feel like I am playing Stardew Valley, no instead I feel like I am playing Littlewood a whole different game.-Building(some of the aspect of it}: The aspect of building house for people, store, terraforming to make ponds/lakes, elevated platforms and having to get materials for it makes it feel like I have a goal to achieve by getting that new home built by getting enough materials or having fun tinkering around with revamping my town to where I feel proud of the work I put into the appearance of my town. This is something that for me stands out and I love about this game that I wish more games like this would do, give me the ability to terraform the town in Stardew Valley, build more diverse and it would be phenomenal.-The Air-Balloon aka traveling to different regions: What's one thing that not enough games like this do open you open to a whole new region, or world, and Stardew Valley has that with going to the Desert for the Oasis, Casino, and Skull Cave, and now Ginger Isle but the aspect of going to a different region to mine, a different one to fish, a different one to purchase items from vendors makes me feel like I am not tied to one central location on a map that is static, while it seems tedious to go to different regions to get specific stuff from there and not in a central location makes me feel like I am spending each in game day doing something different, I am not waking up walking into a area of the main town hitting trrees, and rocks but instead am going to a different region, with different layouts, and art themes to them.What I dislike:Now before I post these it is again Subjective what people like and dislike about the game, but the fact the Dev is working on a new game means this game and how it is is set in stone due to the dev working on a new game so I don't expect changes, nor should you but these things make the game feel stagnant at times.-Building mode, now what I mean by this is how building mode works, you want to move a house? The coffee shop? yes you can but it is super slow and tedious to move it tile by tile making it feel like when will this building finally reach it's destination I think a faster way to move buildings, objects, etc would be nice so I don't feel like I have spent all day moving buildings but instead am getting more done.Staying with building mode, how slowly you get outdoor decor for your town, yes fruit trees, flowers, and veggies are nice but for sometime your town will feel SUPER barren even if you have tons of buildings this game gives you a big sense at the start that you are set out to make this town look amazing, and I get it will take time but honestly seeing a town with just buildings and some nature for hours makes you feel like am I making progress at all? When will I finally be getting proper decor for the town.The Energy system: Look I get it energy systems in games like this in Stardew Valley make sense you are spending energy in real life like you would in game chopping down a tree but this is a video game. The last thing I wanna do is chop down a few trees and that games basically telling you get to bed, Stardew Valley you can actually get more done in a day, oh and for those who hate the clock system in Stardew don't worry it's not here but also isn't needed because you run out of energy faster than a 100 meter sprinter at the Olympics. At least let us get more done in a day because I go and chop a few trees and rocks and the game is telling me I need to go to bed to get full energy back is just a bad concept I understand realism in games but this is realism gone too far to where it feels like I spend more time walking to my house, sleeping, and getting up and going outside than I do chopping trees, or anything else.The game is by no means perfect but leaves a bitter taste with issues causing the game too feel too boring at times to play because of the constant down time, and fast energy consumption, if the energy consumption wasn't so bad, and if I could move buildings faster than a turtle than this game would be a 9/10 or a 101/10 for me but with these negatives about the game I am left feeling like it's a 6.5/10 or a 7/10, The game holds up to what people want the game to be like but fast energy consumption and slow moving buildi and objects times make the game sometimes feel like I am not having fun but more or less. If you are looking for a PURE carbon copy of Stardew Valley there isn't one and Stardew Valley and playing it is your best option because Stardew Valley beats out Littlewood or any game like it but Littlewood is a solid enough game for people who like Stardew Valley to play but get used to spending a lot of time in build mode, and none getting materials you need.

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect for fans of Stardew Valley and Graveyard keeper. This game is chilled out, the soundtrack is relaxing and its got enough progression in it to keep it interesting, plus I really enjoy that there's no time limit to your days. I picked it up because it was recommended on sale but I would gladly pay the full price for it, it's definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the chill experience I always want, but never get, from all those "farm sim" type games. The in-game days work more as a stamina bar vs an active timer ticking down, so overly anxious people like me don't need to panic about maximising every second to make the most of every day. Instead, the actions you take use up a small portion of the bar that represents the time of day. Character events and story progression are also tied to your own individual progress, so there's no pressure to get your ducks in a row before XYZ happens.Glad to have finally found a "chill, relaxing" game that actually IS that, for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:A little too slow-paced for me and there isn't really a set goal (at least not one that I can see.) This is literally just a completionist game. If your favourite part of farming games is filling the museum and maxing out your skills, this is the game for you. Pros:The built-in card game is fun. I also enjoy how custom you can make your town. I also like that there isn't really a time limit on anything, but like I said, I wish there was an end goal that I could see. Instead, I'm just wandering aimlessly.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game blends the best aspects of Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, and Animal crossing while still being unique. The art style is adorable and characters are endearing. You can spend hours terraforming, building, and redesigning your very own town to your liking. Go mining, fishing, bug catching, farming, exploring new areas, you name it. I love the idea behind playing a hero character, after the world has been saved. You are just living it up in the quiet valley making it your own paradise. I can't wait to see what else is to come since this is just in early access.

Not to mention how ADORABLE it is! Look at it!(On top of Steam play time, I have a bunch of hours on Nintendo Switch)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm actually not sure what this game is or what the goal is. There is crafting (of course) and you build a village for people. Has a kind of a stardew energy but feels very aimless. Big comfy vibes and a wholesome minimalist style.Stardew and Animal Crossing were never my thing but if it's yours this could be too.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is cute and I like the premise. The thing I hate most about Stardew Valley is the time constraint it places on you, and this game seemed a lite version that uses stamina instead. So I bought it, excited to construct my town and engage in activities ... and I can't. I get told I will get a tool if I talk to an NPC. But when I talk to them, I receive nothing. I get told I can do a certain thing with terrain. But when I try, it does something completely different. The menu is very cumbersome to navigate and it always gets in my way.Seems like lots of people are having positive experiences, so I'm glad for them. But I have requested a refund as I literally cannot do anything besides wander around, pick weeds, and lay down earth (and not in the way I'm trying to). It's very frustrating and not at all fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost forty hours of gameplay, and Littlewood is still able to keep me hooked. Although this game is Early Access and I've unlocked most of the current content, I appreciate how the developer is still able to keep me coming back with weekly updates that provide many new surprises. The music and sprite work are incredibly charming, most of the characters are enjoyable, and I love feeling a sense of accomplishment when I complete a task or discover a rare item. Even though there are occasional bugs and glitches, I'd say the Early Access mode is worth purchasing to even out your playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're familiar with games like Stardew Valley and Harvest Moon (which I feel most people are at this point), then you should already have a general idea as to what this game is about.You play as the hero of Solemn, just after the downfall of the Dark Wizard. The continent, ravaged by the Dark Wizard and his monster minions, can finally begin rebuilding. Unfortunately for you, you seem to have lost your memories, and can't recall much of anything about the events of your previous adventure. Alongside your old friends, you're tasked with building a new home for yourself and other survivors to live and work in.Let's start with the good stuff, shall we? The mechanics used for the construction of your village are interesting, allowing you to raise land to create hills, and lower it to create bodies of water. The various building types are separated into only a handful of types: NPC Housing, Businesses and Crafting Buildings, Important Town Structures, and Town Decor. Each types plays a different role, with Businesses and Crafting buildings allowing you to purchase goods and blueprints, or do things like cook. Some of these buildings supply you with dewdrops (the games version of currency) every day. These buildings can also be upgraded to provide new goods, provide certain bonuses to your town, or even give you some rare items to use. And if you've played games like Dark Cloud, though, then you should feel right at home. You can construct your village any way you see fit, but there are some things that your NPCs will request that, if met, will net you some bonuses and nifty blueprints. This also meant that you can customize the interiors of every NPC's home to meet their needs and requests, adding a bit more life to the world.Every activity you do adds to your "energy" meter, too. If you decide to pick all of your slimeapple trees clean in a day, for example, then you'll have less energy to use for other things like mining or woodcutting. Nearly everything you do will have some sort of energy requirement, though there are ways to give yourself more energy, or even negate energy usage entirely sometimes. That being said, you can still get a decent amount of stuff done with just the base energy bar alone, so don't panic.Which brings me to my next pro: You can take your time doing everything. Unlike Stardew, which has all of your planting, planting and building plotted around the seasons, this game uses the seasons to indicate passage of time, and gives you different events to look forward to. Aside from some things like the kinds of fish and bugs you can catch, hardly anything changes.But now we have to cover the bad.Firstly, the grind can be a bit of a deal-breaker for some. This is especially true for things like orichalcum and goldenwood, which are rare materials that spawn more commonly in higher-level mines and forests, and will be needed for most end-game buildings and upgrades. While you can get upgrades and bonuses that make the grind less annoying, you're still limited by your energy limit.Next, the Endless Forest and Dust Cavern areas are...Well, they're kind of irritating. Presumably since your character has lost their memory, you can't fight back against wompers in the mines, which will knock you out IMMEDIATELY upon contact, thus booting you out of a mine floor and shutting it off for the rest of the day. It doesn't help that wompers tend to spawn in the same square as you do when you enter a floor, either. You have to avoid them, which is difficult when some rooms are densely packed with obstacles. And dark trees in the Endless Forest have no real counter, aside from smacking them with your axe to put them to sleep for a short period of time. This can be annoying if you have to literally harvest, mine, and chop your way to it, only to be smacked by one of its roots and, just like the mines, get booted out and have the floor lock on you.All that being said, I know there are a couple of items which can help you, but those items are late-game, and often completely hidden from you.This leads me to the biggest flaw I've found so far: The game begins to slow to a crawl by the time You meet all of your potential NPC villagers. By this point, you're constantly selling items to make money, spending money to buy blueprints, collecting materials to craft items, using your stockpile of items to build a handful of objects, and then repeating it all at the beginning of the week. While I'm no stranger to grind, it feels as if the game loses a lot of steam after this point. While it can be countered by putting on a podcast or something in the background to help take the edge off, it might be enough to kill some folks' interest in the game.BUT, with all of that, I have to say that I do genuinely enjoy this game. It's charming, simple, and is a nice little distraction after a stressful day at work. Honestly, I spend a lot of my time just deconstructing things and moving them to make the town feel a bit more like a town, and less like a jumble of buildings that have been placed haphazardly around the map.  It's a relaxing little game, and the price is fairly reasonable if you ask me. If you miss spending hours in the Dark Cloud games, building and rebuilding the towns and villages to fit your aesthetic, then this game will hopefully bring some of that nostalgia back to you.

There's lots to do so far from farming to mining, to woodcutting, building your town, fishing, talking to people, exploring the world, achievements, levels, goals, money, market, bar, cooking... the list goes on and on and on, and I think there is more to come.Really looking hopeful for this game, can't wait for more to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is fairly fun and engaging game, providing you don't take it seriously, and I feel that was the intent from the developer. I like to describe it as "Stardew Valley Lite", because it doesn't expect a lot from the player, and that's a good thing in this case. It's simple enough that you can turn your brain off and just have fun, but not so mind numbing that it becomes boring in 3 hours. It's really balanced overall and is best played, in my opinion as something you return to in short bursts daily until you're satisfied.That being said, it's not perfect, both with the game play loop at times and certainly, if you're a completionist. I'd advise you don't worry about precision on events and getting everything super fast. Just play to have fun, then go for achievements if you're that type of person as you'll likely spend half of your playtime having fun, then the other half grinding to get every achievement as I did. It was still somewhat fun though, even then.Overall, it's a game you can learn fast, have fun, and maybe have a few emotionally engaging moments. It can entirely be played with one hand, doesn't have nagging expectations for the player and is overall just a quaint, "return to the simple time of games" kind of game. If you're interested and see it on sale sometime, it's worth checking out if this genre is something you already like.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute and fun little game, with a lot of promise as it gets further developed. So far there has been a fun building aspect, and certainly lends itself to some creative customization. A few points so far;If you are good at colony/farm/city sim games, this may be a bit easier to get to an efficient play through, which can lead to some early on boredom. I personally love games like stardew valley, rimworld, harvest moon, etc, and I found that by the 15 hour of gameplay I had mostly unlocked everything available, minus some timed and money locked items (from merchants, etc). But skill wise I am nearly maxed out, all current locations unlocked, and most farming items available (it's been eluded that there is more, but I have yet to find out where they are). So again, if you are fairly good and efficient, this game in its current early access state can get stale quickly. I'm also not sure how I feel about the energy expended=time passing aspect. It has been nice while talking to villagers, but I feel I am grinding out the rest of the day too quickly. Overall though this has been a fun game, which I will continue playing to unlock what's remaining. And I can't wait for the updates and new content, as it seems some very interesting developments (the dark wizard??) are incoming!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're as stressed as I am and you're bored with your usual destressing games, give Littlewood a shot. This game hits the same peaceful, bright tone as games like Animal Crossing and Stardew Valley, and is perfect for unwinding and enjoying some low stress gameplay. The characters are all unique and adorable. The music is cute and catchy. There are lots of different "hobbies" for you to pursue in-game, and you can build and decorate your entire town. It's plain and simple fun.This game can also be played completely one handed! WASD for movement, E for menus and canceling, Space for activation/confirmation! As you progress and begin completing collections, perfecting your town layout, and making your villagers happy, things get a bit repetitive and grindy if you have a bit of a completionist streak. If you're a level 73/99 Farmer and you've already farmed every available crop, it can be a bit monotonous repeatedly farming just to hit level 99.Also, this game is not yet 100% complete. However, all the core aspects of the game appear to be finished and it's just minor additions, like some (of the many) town events/holidays that aren't finished yet. Don't let this be the deciding factor for you. At $15, this is an incredible value. Treat yourself. Nope! Probably not!
