_childDocuments_.review: Initially fun, addicting, but eventually very grindy game - not in a terrible way, but don't expect this to be another Stardew Valley, even though there is obviously some inspiration. It feels incomplete.At first, the game is super cool, when you're exploring and unlocking things at rapid pace. Later on, it didn't bother me terribly, because there are still things to explore and you're not just amassing "goods", but the game noticeably slows down, and there are no actual story-themed objectives - there is somewhat of a loose storyline that's being told through characters, but it has nowhere near the depth of something like Stardew, and it's not connected with anything you do in the world, it just unlocks through character interactions.Overall, the game is good, if you don't have higher expectations than to have your sandbox building, simple exploration and grinding, which didn't bother me too much here - but I can totally see someone writing this off as lackluster, and frankly, the game has much higher overall rating than it deserves - it's above average. I would love to see the same formula with the game that's a lot more expanded, because there is a ton of potential - it's distinctive in it's own way and very accessible. Specific complaints: I've spend most of the game frustrated that you never have enough energy during a day to do your routines, you always have to sacrifice something - little did I know that there was an item that basically breaks the game, allowing you to have unlimited energy, it's just that the game doesn't tell you about it and hides it underneath an item that I found useless, so I didn't know about it! It only unlocks after another item has been unlocked, without any hints, either in the UI or the game itself.Late game straight up sucks - for example, you get powerful items way, way too late, because of straight up bad design - just like above, you don't know that one item unlocks others, as the game doesn't imply that in any way. Don't bother trying to 100% unless you have some serious issues, it's a waste of life.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great! There's lots of stuff to collect, lots of recipes to unlock, and lots of rewards to strive towards. It gets a bit repetitive towards the "end", when you're trying to wrap up all the achievements, but it's still well worth it. It's similar to other Harvest Moon/Stardew Valley type games, but what I like is that you're not fighting against a real-time clock, and instead your daily limiter is just an energy bar. It feels more relaxing to me. And, unlike some games where you get the same calendar events every year, Littlewood shakes it up, so if you find yourself playing for several in-game years, you could have new events every season that you've never encountered before.All in all, it's worth it if you're into this type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: I would hold Littlewood up as an exemplar of its kind. If you love the simple joy of games such as Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley, this game will stand proudly among the better entries, falling short in depth compared to some but easily making up for it in breadth. It ties your energy bar to the sun, time only moving forward when you exert yourself and taking a lot of pressure off. 14 eligible characters of all types and genders with no restrictions on marriage, skills ranging from the usual fishing and mining to a simplistic deck builder card game. You build this town from the ground up, terraforming and redecorating, moving houses and decorating the interiors to suit the resident's desires. It's a game I spent 65 hours completing all the achievements, and seriously considered immediately diving back in for another (non-100%) run.In short, Littlewood epitomizes the core gameplay of its genre. If that loop is something you enjoy, you will likely love this game. If that alone isn't enough to sate you, I'd suggest waiting for a sale or just not getting it. But I walked away from Littlewood with a warm feeling in my chest, contentment in my heart, and a smile on my face. And right now, few things can accomplish that.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is a bit of a hidden gem, when found you are overwhelmed by it beauty or in this case gameplay. Unlike other fan favourites in this genre, littlewood does not come with timestress attached. You can go about your day without needing to watch that dreaded clock in the upper corner of the map. You can take a toilet break, open the front door, take a phonecall without needing to pause or leave your session. However your char will get tired from activities and the day will eventually turn into night and sleep. You can also save the game at any time during your session, so no need to finish of your day and go to sleep to save. Aside from that, for a game currently in early access there is plenty to go around, from upgrading house interiors, fishing and farming to collecting exotic pets-cats-dogs. You won't get bored easily. I would like to note that the game has no combat, you will instead try to dodge your enemies attacks. The game gets an almost weekly update, so even when you step away from the game a bit you'll come back to plenty new things to discover. If you want a relaxing game with no timepressure but still the farm/townbuilding experience this game will be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was watching my wife play Animal Crossing, I made mental notes of everything that pissed her off about the game; I couldn't help but often say things like "wow, that's some crappy design". And when I got around to playing Littlewood, the biggest surprise was that it seemed like the game's dev was actually hiding in my living room, making notes whenever I chuckled at my wife's fury towards the clunky and uninspired design of Crossing... and just made a game that essentially resolves all of those problems in a simple and elegant way. I'll try to list all of those improvements, as this also doubles as a nice feature list.  - every character ("villager") is completely unique; all of them have unique dialogue and interactions - there's romance and marriage - and friendship and love are separate stats. There are different ways to interact with your townsfolk, indicating your intent. - also, almost all townsfolk are romancible, and there are no gender limitations. The only exception is the old man, you can't date him. - on the topic of gender, your character's gender is effectively "hidden" - there are no indicators whatsoever, and the writing does a good job of not even using any pronouns on you. A clever way to keep everyone satisfied. - levelling, levelling everywhere. You can level pretty much every single thing that you do - from gathering, to woodcutting, to crafting and even character relationships. - there are multiple places to visit, from alternate towns to mini-dungeons which contain rare materials - the museum gives you hints as to where/when to find a given piece - day/night cycle and your energy meter are fused together: it gets dark when you're tired. So you advance time by doing stuff - you can hang out with anyone by just having them follow you and collect pocket money as a bonus - the town construction is incredibly streamlined, you have a pleasant "building" view which is controller-friendly - you can customise the houses of your villagers; in fact, you have to in order to advance their "quests" and receive some unique late game tools, features, or furniture And so on. You get the idea; a lot of things are reevaluated and made fun. That's what happens when people who make games also play games and know what's fun. Because that's what Littlewood is: a fun, well-designed game. Nothing more, nothing less.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game! Definitely a very different feel from games like Story of Seasons and Stardew Valley due to the lack of a timer, with time and energy essentially being merged into one concept. Later on you get incredibly overpowered items like These items are completely broken but also make the game very very fun to 100%! On a more negative note, the dating candidates, despite encompassing the entire town save your old mentor figure, are mostly uninteresting. The dates are basically just fluff that don't really add anything to the characters, and they all take place in the exact same location too. Because of this the characters have to stand almost entirely on their basic premise, which really hurts characters like Willow, Ash, and Mel. Other than that there aren't really any problems! It's just a very sold casual game and I'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing really spectacular, but a pretty addictive albeit casual experience.The city building isn't very expansive, but there's enough to keep you going for a while, and you can do a surprising amount with the tools you have. Just wish the upgrade processes were a little more randomized or expanded, most things in the game require the exact same things to upgrade to a new level with very little variety. Ive still spent a pretty long time just grinding away, because the core gameplay loop is pretty solid, it being using and leveling skills to get more materials for upgrading skills and building, etc. Towards the later stages the game does start to feel much more shallow, and is pretty much my main complaint.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start with the only really negative thing I have to say: the keybindings are not reconfigurable. This is a dealbreaker for many people for accessibility or QOL reasons.Otherwise, I really can't say enough good things about it. It's a calm and relaxing townbuilding game with funny and interesting characters, an adorable sprite art style, and just a really nice vibe. Despite appearances, it is really not much like Stardew or other farming games as there are only light farming elements. The main gameplay loop is about collecting resources to build and decorate your neighbors' homes in order to make your ruined town a nice place to live again. It's simple and satisfying. There are lots of side activities like cooking, flower breeding, and even a Pokemon-style card minigame. There's also a museum collection if you enjoy hunting down rare items. But ultimately the game is about making your neighbors happy--sweet and wholesome.I would add, though, that part of what makes this game so good is that as wholesome as it is, it's never saccharine. Your neighbors include a narcisstic birdman, a widower in mourning, and a fire mage with anger management problems. The game's tone is light and the goal is heartwarming, but there is still *conflict* to keep things interesting. It is rare to see this done well, but Littlewood nails it.I'd also like to note that this game uses a time/energy system that I dearly wish was the standard in games like this. You simply get a daily energy bar for resource collection actions like chopping wood or mining. When it's empty, you can't do any more of those actions, but you can still walk around, talk to people, place or remove decorations, or do other non-collection activities for as long as you wish, as they take no energy. You choose when the day ends by manually going to bed. If you want to spend a real-life hour redecorating your town without any interruptions, you can do that. This is SO much better than making you run around while a daily clock ticks down in real time and you swear every time you hit the wrong key because that's PRECIOUS SECONDS WASTED. Littlewood's system allows you to actually do what you're supposed to be doing in a game like this: relax.

_childDocuments_.review: You are the brave hero of the land....Who just woke up and has no memory.Together with your 'Friend' Willow and sidekick Dalton you start to rebuild a town and by extension the world as a whole.--A Partially Sighted Review--It's very Stardew Valley, you forge relationships explore and open up the world with the exception of no combat, you can be knocked out by wildlife however. Music is good, text is readable, Farming is basically plug and play and you can get buy with one of each crop when you unlock them, setting up the homes of the villagers is actually fun and once you figure out how to make money (Marketplace and Tavern) it's easy enough to have a steady supply, events are fun, Characters feel like people, there is no judgement on who you want to romance.Would highly recommend if your looking for a chill experience to wind down to or to zone out for a few hours being a nice person

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game, but bear in mind it is still in early access, I feel like the mid/late game needs some polishing (putting missing content aside).Things I enjoyed:-Social aspect in this game is shallower than Stardew storywise but feels more fun to engage with, compliment/hangout mechanic is fun! (although I feel their reward when doing actions could be more diversified, as of now it's dewdrop for everyone)-As others have pointed out, since time is attached to action meter, you can always chill and take your time, that doesn't mean it's inherently better, just different.-Customizing your town is hella fun!-Tarott card game is an hidden gem and a great change of pace during the mid/late game.Things I didn't enjoy:Purple chests aren't rewarding at all: you barely get anything for purple chests in your town (either by doing your personal tasks or completing quests on quest board)Need more hints for recipes in the tavern: as of now, it shows recipes you've already learned and it's hella annoying, it'd be nice to show new recipes so you can progress through the tavern when you're stuck.Ways to get some late game corps/trees needs more polishing/other ways to acquire: it sucks that 3 of the most rarest/most valuable tree fruits are ALL from the same vendor in the 60 Woodcutting forest.40 & 60 Mining/Woodcutting areas don't feel like accomplishments: I was really excited to get to 40 and 60 areas, but they're basically the same, it's just one more area to farm in one day, I think it'd be cooler if magic wood was more prominent in the 40 forest and golden wood in the 60 forest so the player can feel a sense of progress.The fishing trips need more fishes: you pay a whole bunch of money for like 5-6 fishes, I get they're rare but it'd be more fun if some fish were added.The evil tree in the forest can be in proximity of your "spawn point" in the forest, and I got bopped 4-5 times during my playthrough because I was checking other stuff after getting there: I think there should be a safe spawn point where no evil trees can be near the player.The passive dewdrop chest in the museum is a joke (the level 10 boost is even worse), come on, 20 dewdrops in the mid game and like 50 dewdrops is literally making fun of us, and even then, 50 dewdrops is better than most purple chests we get. Stamina used for each action should be balanced around your current skill of evel so the player has a sense of progress: for example, after a certain point, it'd be nice if cutting wood would use less stamina than cutting magic wood or golden wood, it really sucks to go out there, have 95 woodcutting skill, cut around 25 normal wood, and bam, you're done with your day.I think tarott card shop is too late (too much of a gem to delay that much) and rescue pet shop is too early (pets are hella expensive). I think it'd be cooler if we got to interact with tarott cards earlier in the game, so we can start building decks, as of now, it feels like once I got to level 6 Deluca town, I just spammed literally all the other zones in the game that I had already access to for the cards, there is no sense of progress in that sense since most cards are already available.  In my opinion the correct order of unlocks for Deluca could be: Tarott Lv.0 - Casino Lv.3 - Rescue Pet Shop Lv.6 - Auction Houde Lv.10.Other ways other than Mayor Office to unlucky new crop space/tree fruit space, also allow the player to plant magic and golden trees in our towns.I love your game Sean, keep up the great work mate, I've had a lot of fun so far!

_childDocuments_.review: My original review was posted when I was freshly diving into the game as it was just gifted to me for my birthday and at 4.8 hours in. This current posted review is at 66 hours in after retrieving all of the steam achievements, and essentially 100%'ing the game as far as I could handle it.If you go at this game, I cannot suggest you seeing it as a wind down and relaxing breath of fresh air. Complete tasks at your own pace, and don't force yourself to achieve something. Treat this like your own little custom village and home to get away from the "magical war" that took place literally in game and metaphorically in life.The first 20 hours of the game are incredibly enjoyable and exciting. You're meeting new townies, finding out about new resources, finding ways to decorate the town, and building the basis of gameplay that's going to stay pretty consistent even up to the end game. The characters are quirky, and their backstories are quite enjoyable (though a bit lacking if you're looking for a dating sim). End game is quite the slog, and I didn't enjoy the mindless grind to "gather 6000 materials" for the sake of achievements. Though, that isn't a requirement to enjoy the game, it does show up in one of the structures you build in a check list. As for getting to all of the places you're able to explore? Not much of an issue as long as you're gathering the correct materials and spending them on the correct structure upgrades. (or selling items to check off flags for a visitor to come bearing gifts)Minus my gripes, I cannot emphasize how much I appreciate this game for the "Animal Crossing aesthetic" that it brings to the table. I loved filling the museum, going on fetch quests to make the townies happy, and eventually even going so far as to marry one of the townsfolk (Lilith if you're wondering) because I was so charmed. I know I can get back into this save and eventually find an item that will allow me to essentially demolish my town from the ground up, and I will most certainly be returning to rebuild a beautiful town that my villagers would be most joyous to live in. HIGHLY recommend this game for anyone to try. The controls are so criminally easy, yet the gameplay is exceptionally vast. 10/10 would suggest it to a friend again.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: An excellent cozy game that revolves around you rebuilding your town after you've already saved the world.Goods:-Lovely, cutesy art-LOTS of stuff to do-Really nice and wholesome when you start discovering the story-Lots and lots of dialogue is in the gameCould-be-betters:-The main gameplay loop could have been made more engaging by including more story elements-Any advice to not approach the game with an optimizing mindset would help to enjoy the game more-Ending is anti-climactic-Could use more secrets (although there are quite a lot!)-Seasons aren't as influential, and rain almost never happens-The game is cute, but could have nailed the "cozy atmosphere and experience" a lot more by focusing on elements of narrative, setting, landscape art, and perhaps even musicFinal verdict:-Really one of the best cozy games on the market right now.-HUGE props to the creator! Will definitely be looking out for what they make next :)Pointers:-Best played by doing a little bit of everything each day.-Don't try to "optimize" too hard or you'll break the fun of the game.-Reason for above: story scenes, dating, card playing, and other fun stuff only unlock if you're taking everything together. If you optimize, you won't have access to the full breadth of experiences this game offers.-Do not sell your important and rare miscellaneous items, and always keep 1 of everything! Pays off a TON later, trust me xD

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended for anyone with spare time, long sessions, and enjoys relaxing sim life and leveling things up.So I guess I have to compare this to Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, and other games. You can instantly jump back home, menus are all quick and snappy, and it all just works quickly.  And I hope you like seeing XP bars increase and getting small rewards as they are everywhere.The possible downsides are having no combat so far 6 hours in, less of an emphasis on exploring as much of your time is spent in your town and small areas, and some repeat dialogue may discourage you talking to NPCs every day to raise their levels.   I feel the repeating dialogue is the only thing that could use some work.Now I have to try really hard not to go back to the game for a while before i stay up all night.

_childDocuments_.review: While it's still in Early Access, Littlewood is a very fun, satisfying game to play. It does have a lot of similarities with other farming / social games, such as Stardew Valley and Harvest Moon, but it has a bit of a different take to it.Instead of moving to a town, you're building the town yourself. You choose the layout, what gets added, how everything looks. There's no strife or actual combat -- this is your life  all the fighting is done. It's a nice, calm, casual play: Your day isn't divided by time, but by your activities draining energy. Even once you're so tired you can't do anything, you can still wander and explore, or do activities that won't gain experience, such as opening chests, making purchases, building things, et cetera. There is no rush, no need to worry if you don't do things by a certain day or a certain time. As long as you have energy, you can do activities. Though there is still quite a bit to be done (there are a lot of placeholders for future content, and a few bugs here and there), it is still absolutely worth picking up and playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to recommend, but it has given me tens of hours of entertainment. It is mind-numbing in the way that handles quests, because they are almost entirely gathering easy to find materials. There is no puzzle nor dexterity challenge. The only challenge is whether the player wants to rush they day timer, or instead spend time talking to every townsperson for gifts. Talking to NPCs should be fun, but their unskipable dialogue is boring and repetitive. There is such a missed opportunity to have some story or character development. There should be a setting option to turn it all off, honestly.If collection games are your thing, you like base-building games with accumulated in-game bonuses, and you are looking for something that you can grind for tens of hours, then you may want to take a look at Littlewood. This does not feel like a made-with-love kind of game, but maybe you are just looking for a dull, chillaxed experience. There's no crime in that, but according to Steam Achievements. only 10% of owners got to the end of the game.My resource gathering experience was done on an Ubuntu Linux desktop, and the game ran flawlessly without any technical issue. I used a gamepad controller, which worked great for all the UI functions.

Once your energy is almost depleted the night time comes and its telling you that you are about to pass out from exhaustion.I passed out in a smelting place and I woke up at the same place just un-rested. I recommend this game definitely. I actually did not want to stop playing but I am tired myself. I am sure I will have plenty of game time hours on this.Definitely Positive game review from others that hold true.

_childDocuments_.review: Well... I got 75 hours in and I am almost done with everything in the game.  Cute design, not overly cartoonish, interesting design of outlandish items. Non invasive sounds that get lost in the background after a while (I've not muted it once). Lots of fun to start with. Perfect for fans of grinding and people who like collecting everything that exists on the map. If you ever went into a dungeon and wanted to smash all the pots and pick up everything, this is the game for you. No real story to speak of.  The romances are equally under developed. It's a collecting game. And that's all. You go around picking everything up. There's no fighting. You can't get killed. Just inconvenienced.To be honest I don't care for the lack of story and the underdeveloped relationships, the last time I really fell for a game character was Neverwinter Nights. What really got on my nerves was the endless grinding towards the end of the game. If you are missing one thing to complete a quest and it never drops (day after day in real time). After a while money means nothing as the item wont drop at shops either.  Also fishing. I hated fishing, until I realized why I lost every single fish. And my greatest  pet hated the  flowers... Absolute nightmare. Lets just say the whole game is a game of dice. Roll, fail. Roll, fail, Roll fail.  tldr; The game is a huge time sink for people who just want to get lost in a game clicking clicking clicking. Tune off the world and look for that sky crystal till your wasd keys wear through. I did not regret buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been with Littlewood for a long time now, as one of the original Kickstarter backers I've gotten to play from it's early conception to now 1.0.I still remember how excited and hopeful I was when I played the original free demo and even now 150+ hours later I still find Littlewood to be extremely relaxing to play.There is rarely ever any time crunch to push you, outside of a few holiday events. Your 'time' is the actions you take. So you are free to get up and answer the door, or plan out your moves in detail without worrying you are missing anything.Building your town is a day one feature, you don't have to unlock the chance to terraform so you can start right away.The characters are all cute and interesting, letting you pick whoever it is (save grandpa Dudley) that you want to romance. I've enjoyed all the little special moments I've gotten to seen between the other characters and hope this is something Sean continues to expand on post 1.0.I love this game, and whole heartedly can recommend it to anyone looking for a relaxed, at your own pace building/life sim game.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Game Release Review:All my early access grinding paid off. Little effort was needed to breeze through the rest of the game. The three pillars in the first room of the Museum magically presented themselves in one of the last early access updates. I have now completed the game 100%. I was a bit taken back that the story ended with minimum engagement. Like, we found out what happened- but that was it. I feel that there could be more at play in the future, maybe. As we did not experience the first world ending -because we begin the game with an utter memory wipe out from our lead character. Maybe we shall see the dark forces escape the Tarot Card spell? Or what's her face, in the purple, shall be overcome like Dark...And we get some Battle play?!? We shall see...Early Access Review:With roughly 99 game play hours- I managed to max the levels within the game. I mean a lot of these levels max at 99, so I was grinding pretty hard. All items for Museum found (except for the three pillars in the first room of Museum) and all recipes cooked. I did have to reference outside sources to figure out what some of the items were and how to get them. EASY game play. Except the Tarot Card Monster Game. Not my strong suit. The story of the characters and the game at current times is very simple. I am sure that once in full access, we will find the rest of the story.Over all, a game with potential. But grinded too hard for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend. Fun game, relaxing, the hours melt away. The characters are all varied and interesting and it's a nifty idea. I like that you can build the village however you feel and the interactions with other characters is fun.  I like how the rest of the world opens up through leveling the air balloon. I like how your energy consumption is also the passage of the day. It is a bit of a drag with how very grindy it can be. I'm currently in hour 9 and just unlocked farming level 25, the use of energy has to be used wisely. I'd like the ability to level your energy consumption to a be a bit more frequent (I came across a wish for it only once so far)Customizing the buildings would be nice (changing roof colors and such) but is not a deal breaker. I'm hoping there comes a time when I can expand the size of the village, the characters pore in rather quickly (not a complaint) and they each have to have their own homes built. Overall its very fun and can't stop playing it, I look forward to what more is to come and will probably be enjoying this game for a couple hundred hours.

_childDocuments_.review: This game beats Stardew Valley and any other farming/town game by a long shot for me.It was amazing during Early Acess already, but with more content being added for Release, so I thought I'd update my review too.Key design choices that make me adore this unique game:- You can terraform the entire town and have tons of options for decoration- You're the hero that saved the world and now you get to rebuild. How cool is that fantasy postgame setting?- Time only progresses when you do work! This is the biggest part. * You can walk around and talk to NPCs 1000 times a day if you wish. * You can decorate all you want. * Terraform your entire city in a day. Without ever feeling the pressure of "Wasting time".Stardew Valley made me stress a lot. Even when I wanted to just play to relax.Cuz "You need to plan out your day if you want to catch X NPC and still get all your bundles done within 2 years."Even standart mechanics are done very well.- You have your skill levels in certain professions and they'll in return unlock chests or new areas / materials. But they never feel grindy. You'll want materials to build houses or upgrade buildings so you'll just naturally level every aspect anyway.- Upgrading houses feels rewarding. Completing the museum feels rewarding. Even your townsfolk wishes feel fun to work towards cuz they give you a reason to rethink your towns layout and they don't simply demmand items.- Days are relatively short so even if you find yourself grinding the same ressource, you will have new dialogue and random events within a couple minutes, preventing it from becoming stale.- The characters are very charming and unique. Funny quirks included.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so impressed with this game! The characters, pacing, controls, and freedom to do whatever I want while still having plenty of tasks is perfect for me. I love, love, love that this is not a combat game. The sound effects are so fun. When I run out of energy and that little sound happens along with my character turning upside down makes it worth it to lose 25% of the next days energy sometimes haha. I am 43 hours in, and I feel like there's so much left to do in a great way! I wish I had known to look at my journal for travelling NPC goals as I'm now having to spend a bunch of time fixing this instead of having it as part of the game play all along. I also wish I had known you can sprint. Those are my only tiny complaints, but stuff I easily could have looked up online if I wanted to earlier. Buy this game. Get two. Give one to a friend because I can't stop talking about it to mine. Thank you for making such a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: The store page makes the game look like a farming sim, almost like Stardew, but the game is so much more than I thought. Playing an hour into the game gives you all these ideas of whats to come if you keep working and leveling up your skills.I was so surprised at the amount of content in this game because like I said, I thought this was a farming sim. Leveling up your relationship with your villagers, leveling up your skills to 99, find out how to get new people to your village, finding books, new items, new CARDS, new tools. There's tons of stuff to do in this game and it had me totally locked on. There were a few days where I just played 8+ hours and I didn't even realize.I highly recommend this game. I have 49 hours on this game with ONE profile. It took me about 30 hours to get through most of the stuff I would consider incredibly fun. I spent another 20 hours trying to get all the achievements. The endgame grinding is very boring but having all the materials to build your town however you want is very nice. But just be aware that grinding everything to 99 isn't hard, but it is time consuming (even with an item that makes it so much easier).I'll say it one more time, I highly recommend this game for people who love leveling skills, love making a town (Animal Crossing vibes), or love farming!
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood developers, you make me feel so seen! This feels like the game I would have created for myself, if I had any of the talent, skill, ambition, etc. required to do such a thing. Relaxing doesn't even begin to describe this gem. It's like Stardew Valley minus the dreaded time pressure plus some shades of Animal Crossing. If Littlewood had Steam achievements, it would be the perfect game. _childDocuments_.review: Anyone looking for a comfort game (if you like building, exploring, and friends) Littlewood is a great comfort game. It’s kind of similar to Stardew valley but without the stressful clock and with a lot more creative control. In Littlewood time passes when you do something, so you can make the most out of everyday. You can fully customise your town, including the landscape for no cost, you only need to gather the materials and for the most part they are easy to find. The characters are all lovable and entertaining, although dialogue can get a little stale/repetitive at times, similar to animal crossing new horizons. A great, relaxing, low stakes game.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little relaxing game to pass the time during these stressful days we live in.This is a very light game, think of it as one step up from a mobile game and many steps down from something like Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon. Everything you do in this game is very basic, you essentially decide each day what you will spend your limited energy on. Harvesting wood, ore, or farming. Everything is sequentially tiered, as in at level 5 you can harvest x, at level 10 y, at level 15 z, etc. The only difference is the higher tiered materials are for higher tier upgrades. This means there is little thought into what you are doing or harvesting.The controls are great for controllers. The graphics look cute. Everything is smooth. The characters are fun although limited in dialogue.Where this game really shines is the town customization. You can totally customize the terrain and layout of your town, and it is free for the most part. You are also responsible for furnishing everyone's houses (not free). There is also motivation to do this as characters each have their own desires for where their house should be and what they want inside.After playing for 12 hours, I unlocked all of the mechanics and was pretty far along the leveling up. At this point I hadn't spent any time on customizing my town layout. I could easily sink many hours into that, but I personally don't get much enjoyment from doing that.If you love spending time making the perfect looking town, this game is definitely for you. You will easily get 30+ hours out of it before running out of things to do.If you're like me and enjoy the farming, crafting, making money, etc. aspect of these types of games, you will likely burnout around 10-15 hours in like me. I'm still glad I purchased the game as I got 12 hours out of it, but by then you are essentially doing the same routine everyday.Tl;dr: Fantastic game if you love customizing town and room layouts. If not, beware you may get bored after 10-15 hours once you've unlocked all of the mechanics and have a steady resource gathering routine.

_childDocuments_.review: Already it's a big yes from me. Stardew Valley without the added time constraint (stamina usage automatically progresses your day, freeing you from feeling as if you have to rush everywhere to get anything done). Animal Crossing without the game playing itself while you're gone. If you're looking for something with a combat aspect, at 3.5 hours in I'll say I've seen basically nothing of that. However, it absolutely satisfies the itch to collect things, and gives you plenty of incentive for doing it, without the restraints of a limited inventory to manage. Between town beautification, a marketplace to sell things (and plenty of items to purchase with the currency), as well a built-in game mechanic (the museum building) that encourages collecting one of everything, I can absolutely see myself striving for 100% completion, and I don't say that about many games. I do think the setup is better played with a controller, but that's more a personal preference. There is also a little dating/friendship mechanic which isn't mentioned anywhere at a glance that I could see initially. This game is exceptionally satisfying to play from everything to the music and sound effects as well as the controls and game play. Neat, tidy, and fun!~

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great game to play. I loved the relaxing farming and cozy feeling, and the added fun of the tarot card dynamic was quite enjoyable!Even after completing the main storyline, there's a wealth of satisfying activities to engage in. From grinding through the game's achievements to the joy of town decoration, there's always a sense of accomplishment waiting for you.Littlewood is a game that truly empowers you. With its vast freedom to choose what to focus on, it caters to everyone's unique gaming preferences. While I yearned for more exploration, the game's relaxing nature still makes it a great choice for unwinding. My ratings for the game:Complexity 7/10: Once you get a handle on the basic gameplay, it will not be very complex and will be pretty straightforward. For some sections, you might have to do some research, such as the flower breeding and cooking recipesCoziness 9/10:It's a very cozy game. There aren't any sections that take away from the cozy small-town feeling. If you like Stardew, then you will also like this game, as they have similar vibes, but Littlewood has a simpler mechanic system.Repeatability 8/10:I actually had to restart since I had a computer issue, and my first save file got wiped. Even having to restart from scratch, I found that this game was still a lot of fun to restart. While choices don't make a big difference, I did find that having gone through the sections before, I was able to better plan out where I spent my dewdrops and placed people's houses more effectively.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game, it is a lot of fun overall despite a couple of minor issues. First of all, the pacing in the beginning of the game works well. You won't be able to do everything you want to in a single day at first, but this is for the best - late in the game, when you gain the ability to do everything every day, the pacing falls apart a little. Until then, though, it is perfectly fine and fits the casual vibe of the game well. Of course your character shouldn't be running themselves ragged chopping every tree on the map on a daily basis in a chill game. The only point at which the pacing becomes a problem is in the endgame when you are trying to get 100% completion - eventually you hit a point where there are only one or two things left you need to do, but they are taking a long time, and it becomes a bit tedious. This is particularly notable with the questing achievements. If you're not going for 100% completion, though, this shouldn't be a problem for you at all. The game focuses a lot more on building up the town than it does on farming, so if you're expecting a Stardew Valley type game, stop expecting that. That's a good thing, though, Littlewood is its own game and plenty of fun on its own merits. I really enjoyed upgrading everything and building new houses, and the town is extremely customizable. You can move everything around - buildings, decorations, trees, the land itself, etc. Each town structure brings new things you can do, I especially enjoyed the tavern, which provides a good source of income and is a lot of fun to discover the recipes for. The events throughout the year are always fun when they occur, too. Overall, I like the characters in this game, but there are a couple of glaring issues with the writing that undermined my enjoyment of them a little bit. I'm going to start out with the good stuff - the variety in the designs is impressive considering the simple style, everyone has their own distinct personality, and I enjoy the cutscenes where townsfolk interact with one another. As an autistic person, I really liked seeing multiple characters (Laura and Terric) who not only read clearly as autistic but are also treated with just as much respect as other characters and remain as romance options - I do not know if it was intentional or not, but it's nice regardless. Dudley was my favorite, though, it was really apparent that a lot of love and care was put into his personality and dialogue as well as other characters' dialogue establishing interactions he'd had with them. I thought he was the most well crafted character despite being the only one who does not have date cutscenes. At the end of the game where it is revealed that The two glaring problems with the character writing are as follows. Since specific game events are discussed here, I will spoiler them. First of all, townsfolk do not develop much over time. This wouldn't inherently be an issue, but because several of the best and most memorable cutscenes in the game are dedicated to moments that really seem like they would have a significant impact on the characters, it becomes one. For example, there is one cutscene where  This isn't the only time that it feels like characters should develop and don't, but I'd certainly consider it the most noticeable simply due to the sheer frequency with which . I would like to see the development of the characters reflected in their regular dialogue, even if just by something as simple as replacing one or two of their regular lines after these cutscenes occur. The other problem with the character writing is less omnipresent and can be avoided by not romancing anybody but, in my opinion, is far more serious - This game has very interesting lore, a lot more of it than I would expect from this type of game. I would love to see more from this universe, either as DLC or as entirely new games. Overall I feel like it is handled very well, my only complaint is that The handling of gender in this game is something I appreciated a lot as a nonbinary person who doesn't use any of the top 3 most popular pronoun sets - namely, that it isn't handled. Usually, even in trans-inclusive games, there is not an option for my pronouns, and so it was refreshing to play a game where the player character just doesn't have any pronouns or gender specified at all. It's an elegant and simple way to make a game truly inclusive of all genders without adding in high levels of customization that could be difficult to code. Sometimes, it is hard to figure out how to get certain items or accomplish certain tasks, but that is standard for the genre and, if anything, less of an issue in Littlewood than in most similar games. The wiki is your friend in these situations, don't be afraid to use it! I also feel I should note that for the entire time I played this game, I only encountered 1 bug, and it was just a minor issue with the characters walking in a way that didn't line up properly with the map which lasted about 5 seconds and then never happened again. It's a very solidly put together game and runs well. To be clear about why it was free, I received the game as a gift from a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't understand, how so many people recommend this game. It's just grind and grind and grind in a not even slightly pc conform environment. There would be serious qol and balancing upgrades needed, to make this game enjoyable.Here just a few examples:Keybinds can not be changed. 'close dialog', 'Open menu' and 'going back in a menu exactly one step' are e and esc, no button for closing a menu completely. 'Use' is space and enter. And you'll be hitting space a lot, as the game does only accept button presses and holds only for the one tree or ore you're doing your three hits on.Some menus can be rolled over, most can't.The very first experience after starting is typing names via an on screen keyboard. This wouldn't be too bad if this theme wouldn't continue through every menu. Harvesting or moving the item you want to build via wasd instead of just using the mouse is just ridiculous. Finding a certain food item to cook for a quest basically requires you to always wasd scroll through all lists of recipes instead of just being able to just type the name in a search bar (or having the quest item highlighted)Everything in this game just makes you feel like the devs just want to torture you and see, when you'll explode.The first hours in Littlewood are really fun (especially after you've realized, that villager affection and therefor talking to them is completely unnecessary. Ignoring them saves A LOT of time.) Meeting new villagers, building your village, exploring the world - all this is super fun and enjoyable. Then the big grind starts. For hours and hours you just do the same daily routine. Going completely braindead and check all merchants for random things you need and collect, catch fish to find the missing rare one, catch bugs to find the missing rare one, sleep until the trades restock and repeat.From the 45 hours I played I regret at least 30 and without my 100% ocd I'd quit way earlier. After completing the main objectives I had collected a bit more than 3500 ores and trees. Checked the achievements and found the ones for collecting 6000 each. ♥♥♥♥ it - I'm done with this ♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is a very sweet game and a nice way to relax and wind down after a busy day. If you like games like Stardew Valley, this one is similar but also a bit different. In Littlewood, you get to slowly rebuild a town, get to know the townsfolk and do quests for them, and more. You get to level up various skills including fishing, farming, cooking, and mining. Do note that this game is a bit buggy, and it won't be updated. However, I wouldn't say it's incredibly buggy, and it's definitely still playable.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: A negative review may be a bit harsh, but... once past half the game, it becomes a relentless grind for very little reward. The very last area of the game, which requires a lot of tedious grind (including the infamous flower breeding) to reach, in particular, is almost empty, and only brings a couple items that aren't much use by that stage of the game.To be fair, the order in which you do things in the late game might ease things a bit (e.g., some villagers give you nice rewards for helping with their house, also there are a few items at Deluca city which can also help with getting the late-game resources), but it still remains a grind.On the plus side, before that middle-to-end-game grind, the game is pretty pleasant, is very well-paced, introducing possibilities in a way that does not feel overwhelming, and always giving you something to do. Unlike Stardew Valley, where each day is time-limited, Littlewood has an energy limit, which is way less stressful and lets you move at your pace.Overall it's a cute little game that starts great but has an awfully grindy late-game with very little end reward. Either skip the end game, or play it in short sessions, and not neglecting the townfolks' houses.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is a super cute and fun game! It is really relaxing and simple. What makes this game even more relaxing than other farming sims is that there is no timer, the day progresses by every action you take! Everything about this smooth pixel game screams adorable. The only downside is that, while the game itself is easy, it can become a little monotonous at times and start to drag. It is extremely grindy and monotonous if you are looking to get all the achievements but you can get all the achievements in less than 50 hours. Super addicting!

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is a game where you build a small town in the peaceful aftermath of your character's journey to save the world. Now that the world is saved, all the tasks left are relaxing and give a real sense of building a community around your little town. It plays similarly to Stardew Valley, but distinguishes itself by eliminating time limitations and allowing you to build and manipulate every aspect of your town. It's a great game for relaxing while being engaging enough to play more attentively as well. If you love peaceful town building sims this is a perfect game for you

_childDocuments_.review: This game tickles both my inner cozy gamer and my ADHD with chill, cute vibes and rewarding gameplay that breaks everything into bite-sized tasks so you always feel like you're making progress. Easy to play in small chunks in your down time, which I appreciate, as most of my other go-to games require a significant time investment. That said, I do still regularly sit down for longer play sessions with this game without getting bored. It's simpler than the big, mainstream cozy games in both art style and gameplay, but not the overly simple bare-bones content that you get from a lot of the low-effort games trying to cash in on the popularity of the genre. I think what you can get out of this game is accurately reflected in the price and I would recommend it to cozy gamers and ADHD dopamine-seekers like myself.

_childDocuments_.review: Having sunk 11 hours into it my take away with this game is that Littlewood isnt' a bad game persay but it is a game with more fat on its bones than meat. About everything you need to do in the game leaves you at the mercy of rng with an energy system that feels stilfing at most times. You'll spend more time grinding out the same resources again and again and again than doing anything else and the town building segment is more or less.. I mean its there, but it never really feels that deep. You get people who want to live in your town, you grind out enough mats to build their house,  you get a blueprint from them that you grind the mats out for and build... eventually like halfway through the game you get the desk blueprint letting you see what they want in their home and then you fight rng both in the marketplace as well in the resource gathering dungeons so that you can finally fill out a page of their requests and get a blueprint for some quality of life ability that feels like should have been gated some other way.  Rinse, repeat, until you get bored.   While its not BAD... when you compare it to other similar titles it feels very light on the content and heavy on the grind (or the fat). It's just hard to recommend it when most the time you will spend with the game is dealing with the arbitrary gating the game puts in front of you to extend its playtime.
_childDocuments_.name: Littlewood

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, this is a good game. I do have some issues, and I honestly think that when you see an overwhelmingly positive rating you expect a masterpiece and that isn't always true. It just means that almost nobody disliked the game overall. It is very much worth the money. I enjoyed the game a lot and got lots of the harder achievements, but it lacks anything that will make me want to replay it.The Good - It's a cute and charming game where you rebuild your town. It's absolutely relaxing and at your own pace. Your days are energy based, not time based. So you don't have to worry about running out of time in a day, just energy. You can place houses, shops, crops, and various other buildings anywhere you would like, and even design the terrain height. Each character has a unique personality anywhere from cute, to goofy, to downright annoying. Lots of different places to explore and for the most part it is reasonably spread out in a way that keeps you engaged, although it gets tedious later game.The Bad - Before I start, I would just like to say I very much enjoyed this game and it is absolutely worth it. Firstly, there really isn't an "end".  The only thing close to an ending is the credits playing after you are married. The scene with Dudley was AMAZING and I loved it, but other than that if you choose not to marry Willow she has no happy ending. Dark never gets any closure either, if you marry him he considers himself forgiven and that's it. After marrying your spouse they also NEVER leave your home ever. Which is really sad. Each character had such a unique personality and the thought of them never leaving the home unless it is by your side is super sad. Lastly, there is no real acknowledgement to any goal. There's some buildup and small goals but you eventually realize that there really isn't a reward for doing  anything. Every few levels in a skill or after you upgrade your townsfolk homes they will send you a generic letter in the mail or have a gift for you. That's it. Before I finished playing I realized I was mostly just tracking steam achievements and the way to get it was to sleep, water flowers, repeat. There was no acknowledgement after spending the time to repair Deluca or fill the museum. In fact, the mayor of Deluca actually continues to ask for donations even after the donations are complete. The only major acknowledgement was collecting all the books from the travelers.

_childDocuments_.review: I ended up kickstarting this game, totally hooked by the concept of an SoL with tie ins to Dark Cloud. Was it worth it?Absolutely. For a game created by a single person, Littlewood is definitely just as up there in quality as Stardew Valley, even if what it offers is a slightly different style of relaxed gameplay. There's more exploration and a decent amount of expansion that comes as you develop your town and relationships. The amount of control you have over your town's design from the very first day is incredibly impressive, and as you go, you'll find yourself quickly beginning to unlock everything you need to design a space that you enjoy. Something that Littlewood adds to this design process in comparison to ACNH, for example, is the villager goals system, accessible through their desks. This is very reminiscent of Dark Cloud's village design, where placement of houses and planning out your town really can pay off. It does add a little bit more into the whole process past "what is aesthetically pleasing to me"?I'm always very impressed with how responsive the game feels in terms of rewards. There's a dozen odd goals that you can work towards at any given time, and everything you do will generally have some kind of payoff at the end. Relationships are easier to maintain and don't come with a negative aspect to them- if you find you want to focus in on grinding out a couple hundred stacks of wood for a week, no worries. Choosing to hang out with a villager also has benefits to it that mean even on days where all you want to do is grind out some crafting, hanging out is worth doing. This simplified relationship building allows you to focus back onto the town with relative ease, though as you get more and more villagers, you might find yourself feeling a bit more stretched out.The music is nothing special, but it's nice enough to listen to for a few hours. Generally speaking it's probably the weakest point of the game for me, but this game works very well as something to plug away at whilst watching things on youtube, so I don't think it really detracts from anything overall.Watching this game develop over the past year has been an absolute joy- I'm really looking forward to seeing it come out on the switch! Also going to be gifting it to more friends going forward, definitely. Great work Sean!

_childDocuments_.review: Where to even start?This game is what far too many games failingly tried to be since Stardew Valley came out. You get the characters whose stories you can actually engage with, you get the building and the homely athmosphere of doing your thing and watching it all grow - paired with a sweet as hell story.I'll be real - I didn't think I'd ever love a game more than SV but here we are. And the reason Littlewood manages to kick even Concerned Ape's genius from its throne for me is that I have never in my life seen someone OWN gameplay loops as much as these devs.Apart from "time passes through doing stuff, not through a timer" being a GENIUS idea for this kind of "play at your own pace"-games, it also tremendously helps with staying engaged. Every little thing becomes its own success - and Littlewood's devs realized something important: If you overdo it with the grind, it becomes tediouos as hell. There's a museum you can donate stuff to - like in Animal Crossing - but it's actually a fully attainable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ goal and I'm only missing a few items here or there at this point. Not even SV made me feel less "well, let's hope the RNG will be nice today".And to stop me from rambling further about how this game deserves more credit, here's a list of all my pros and cons:+ cute, engaging characters+ fun gameplay - esp. in terms of the gameplay loop and in terms of the timing of things - nothing feels tedious, the animations are the perfect length (no eyerolls upon repeating a 2-3 second watering animation over and over again)+ time passes through you DOING things as opposed to seconds being counted down+ you make friends through talking and hanging out, not through buying their affection with gifts+ a great combination of big and small milestones to keep you engaged and not let you fall into a bored grind+ a relaxing soundtrack+ charming graphics+ light terraforming that can affect resource availability (in other words - want more fish, have more water) - offering customization options for your town that other games like this don't+ a plant-breeding mechanic that isn't over the top tedious and needs reading twenty wiki-pages+ SO MANY QUALITY OF LIFE IMPROVEMENTS - if you don't find yourself continuously positively surprised that the game doesn't make you do the annoying bit, you haven't tried filling the hole SV left with the crazy amount of clones out there+ you get to furnish your villagers' houses - according to their wishes, but still. It's fun.- the cutscenes could do with a bit more depth, but they're still charming- Wompers (creatures who live in the mines) can make mining annoying at times- I feel like the characters could've come with specific perks fitting their personalities but I don't know if this really counts as a con - it would've just made it even betterI hope the devs see this review 'cause frankly, this game is made with such love that I just want to pat them on the back for it. It can be hard to find your own vision in this genre and they did a marvellous job.

_childDocuments_.review: I became aware of Littlewood (LW) when checking out possible games to review, but otherwise had never heard of it before. Considering how it had more than 1,000 reviews, many of which were positive, I was quite interested in trying the game out. In case it gets updated, my review is based on the 1.02 version, so certain matters may become obsolete over time. In LW, you'll work on improving the town, by completing tasks such as gathering fruit, farming, fishing, catching bugs, mining, etc. A game like this wouldn't be complete without the opportunity to befriend your fellow townsfolk, and the ability to put a ring on it. Another feature it adds reminds me of a PS2 game, Dark Cloud. While building houses and stores for the townspeople, you have several options on how you set up the landscaping. You can raise and lower the terrain, build waterways and roads, and decide the location of each item, down to the flowers.All of this is more customization then was available in Dark Cloud, but what really reminds me of that game was how each citizen has their own preferences for what goes into their house, and the location they live at, which you'll have to take into account to satisfy them. Even with this influencing how you set up your town, there are numerous ways to customize it, and make it feel like your own creation.You're able to play this game with either a controller or keyboard, with the controls being rather straightforward. Either way, the game simplifies how you control it. Instead of needing to manually select what tool you use, your character will use whatever is contextually appropriate with the item you're in front of. Why shuffle through your tool bar, looking for the right item, when it's obvious based on the item you're facing? This automation really spoils you, and everything else seemed to work fine when I played.Inadvertently, this is an area where LW shoots itself in the foot. The background of the protagonist is that of a legendary, world-saving hero, with a mythical sword, and mastery of many kinds of magic. Unfortunately, after defeating the Dark Wizard, you've lost your memory. My biggest complaint about the story as presented is that what you do in the game doesn't sound nearly as interesting as the stories they'll tell you about yourself, which is exacerbated by how there's no combat. Having to run away from what amounts to a grumpy tree and angry pig is demoralizing, because they should be fodder before such a mighty hero. I'd rather play a game based on what led up to the present situation, than what I'm dealing with here. The visuals are one of the game's charming aspects. By making use of vibrant colors and well-done pixelation, it makes for a relaxing aesthetic. It's never hard to figure out what an item is, although what purpose it serves isn't always so clear. For instance, I have no idea what to do with dark matter, but I easily recognize it when I see it.Much like its graphics, the music of LW is quaint and relaxing. If you can get into a flow with the gameplay, the music will ease you into a calm state easily enough. Sometimes the dark tree sound effect is jarring, but I don't remember hearing any aggravating sounds.🌟 There's no time progression each day, the end of it is centered around your energy bar being depleted. You also can't eat food to replenish it.🌟 You don't have to worry about managing your inventory, as you get infinite inventory space.❌ With all the objectives you can complete dangling in front of you, you're constantly pursuing multiple goals that may not be that interesting. For instance, upgrading buildings require lots of lumber and bricks, so be ready to focus on getting those resources above all else.❌ There's little reason for starting another save file or replaying the game. Even though you could marry someone else, the rest of the gameplay would be nigh identical, except in those areas where you figured out how to be more efficient.❌ Many locations are too small. The Endless Forest makes up an area only a fraction of the size of your town, making it come across like a trip to the park. Port City is supposed to be very busy, but there's barely anyone there.❌ I don't care for a decent number of the characters. Dudley is awesome, but Bubsy is a narcissistic fop, Laura is a nag, and Ash is desperate for a date.🔍 It's worthwhile to add new people to the town, as they will bring with them an addition you'll find useful. To get Mel, keep going back to the Port City after meeting her.🔍 You get more XP harvesting higher level crops and fruit, so when you get the next highest leveled item, plant as many as you can of it.🔍 There's no penalty for rejecting someone's quest if it's too cumbersome to complete.My main complaint with LW is that it gives an impression of freedom and autonomy, yet the game doesn't feel open-ended. While I'm still unable to remember anything, I'm declared the mayor, and have the responsibility of making everyone else happy. Although one could thumb their nose at the townsfolk, with how I'd want to play the character, I'd be a dutiful hero trying their hardest. So, for about the first year, you'll be building new houses, and upgrading the buildings, to the detriment of other activities, such as fishing. I don't have spare money to get furniture and decorations, because I'm paying for everyone else's wishes for the town. Despite having the burden of being mayor, there's no meaningful benefits to speak of.Although I enjoy how the game looks, it takes more than that to make for a compelling title. It held my attention for more than a dozen hours, but I was getting tired of having to cater my time to pleasing everyone else. Plus, once I took a break from the game for a few days, my motivation had tanked to the point I didn't even want to play anymore. The gameplay is very repetitive, with little reward for my efforts, and I don't think I've gotten to the point where the grinding gets especially egregious. With all the cozy games being released lately, you'll certainly find another choice that'd satisfy your farming instincts more than this title.

_childDocuments_.review: With a little under 100 hours in this game, I would highly recommend this as a cozy comfort game. it is something to do when you're too overwhelmed for a complicated game but in the mood to play something easy.LittleWood is a slice of life simulator mixed with a bit of whimsical fantasy. You, the player, were a mighty hero but at the end of your epic story, something happened which gave you amnesia. However, with all the monsters gone in the world, it's not your duty to help build a town and help the folks you meet settle in.  The game has no timers, it's a "do it at your own pace" kinda deal. the UI is simple and easy to use. It's fairly customize-able with player customization, terraforming, and decorating not only your house, but the houses of the townsfolk. If you enjoy 100%-ing everything and collecting items for achievements, this game is the right fit for you with an in-game building which tracks your progress visually with the items you've collected thus far. There is even an achievements tracker item so you do not have to tab in and out of steam just to see the progress you're making on your goals. It does get a little repetitive  but not in a tedious way. For me, it was finding a rhythm with the game as you progress in expanding your space, making your town, and romancing your favorite villager(s). Would highly recommend to anyone and everyone who likes this style of game.

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is overall a wonderful game. It's very laid back with very casual gameplay and it's also just extremely cute. I was amused by much of the dialogue between the various characters and letters received from them.The way the day ends when your energy runs out is pretty unique and I actually found myself liking that feature as it didn't leave me with an entire day and no energy to do anything with it.There is a diverse cast of characters, each with their own unique personality and I liked the majority of them. The music is lovely and peaceful as is the overall feel of the game. There isn't really any plot to speak of--you're given a premise and then just bits and pieces of trivia through dialogue and books that you can use to piece together the events that happened before the game begins as well as things about the world itself. I personally found myself liking the way that was handled.If you're going for all the achievements like I did it gets pretty grindy. _childDocuments_.review: This game was a delight. It scratches the itch of Harvest Moon, but a bit more story which I always wanted. It also obviously has Stardew Valley vibes, which I appreciated. Infinite exploration of dangerous caverns and forests keep you alert, there seems to always be something new to unlock. I distinguishing feature that I liked was the early limitation of the number of crops you could grow and critters you could raise so that you don't spend all day every day maintaining your farm, and it encourages you to work toward multiple goals. Great characters, and an interesting world. I'm honestly suprised this game isn't getting more buzz - it definitely has stuff in common with Animal Crossing, with the freedom of decorations, flower breeding and fun seasonal events. If you like any of those games, this is definitely for you.My only complaint - I wish the sprint speed was faster.

The last few achievements weren't that fun. You have maxed 99 skills well before you complete the last gathering/fishing/mining/crafting/woodcutting/farming achievements. You're just grinding resources for the achievements at that point without using them for anything. Still a good game, just tedious to 100% the achievements.

A great hero has already defeated that menace, and now with no memory of that the hero settles into the role of "mayor" building a small town. With vast amounts of customization, you have a lot of freedom to make the town you want(of course your friends will have some ideas for where their homes should be) and you can easily change the town with a very simple building and moving system. I have plugged hours into this game, and always wish i could go 2 or 3 more game days before I have to stop.

_childDocuments_.review: Littlewood is a relaxing indie simulation game where you rebuild a ruined town and create a lively community. You play as the mayor of Solemn, giving you the freedom to design and organize every part of your town. You can place buildings, decorate with objects, and customize the layout to make the town your own.Farming, fishing, cooking, questing, and even running a shop offer lots of variety. There’s no pressure with time limits, so you can explore and enjoy at your own pace. It’s ideal for a laid-back, casual experience.You'll meet unique characters, each with their own stories. Building relationships with them leads to heartwarming moments. The pixel art is beautiful, filled with vibrant colors and cute details. The soothing soundtrack adds to the calm atmosphere, making it easy to get lost in the world of Solemn.While playing, you might notice some repetitive tasks and occasional pathfinding issues for your townsfolk. The story can also feel a bit short and generic.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore Littlewood! There are so many reasons why, but here are a few.Pros:-I love love love that time is based off of your energy level instead of actual time. I don't feel rushed that time of the day will run out. I can make it my pace. Obviously this also makes you learn how to utilize your energy (Note: not every action you do requires energy)-The characters are so sweet to your character. They also have stories and feelings all their own and all are uniquely different (personality and looks).-I also love how simple and cute everything looks, love the art style!-You get to terraform a bit, move everything around and make it your own!-The story so far I'm also really enjoying and looking forward to seeing where it goes!Cons:-uuuuumm honestly it is difficult to find a con. I guess I could say that sometimes I feel like I'm working too hard/slow to get through it. I try focusing on leveling up my skills so I can unlock the level chests, and I grind to upgrade everything. But I feel like my grinding is too slow. I also have gotten to a point where it is taking forever to find new furniture for the villager's houses. So basically once you get really into it, there is a certain point that it slows down.
