_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of wonderful things about this game, and I've enjoyed it enough to play all the way through the campaign, about 30 hours so far. The mechanics are fairly deep, the art is beautiful, and the little jokes are great. Overall, would recommend it.That said, I think there are some things that could be better, and that I hope the devs will improve.1. The faction communication/quests often require saved up resources, but the player has no way of knowing this except for opening a conversation, reading the greyed out options, mousing over them, then remembering them later. Since conversations are pretty rare actions, and thus a valuable resource, it's punishing to waste them. This mechanic pushes against the overall game flow of spending mana to buy cards as soon as the button lights up. Especially in my first few hours of playing, it felt pretty bad to be penalized for doing the thing the game is telling me to do. And even after playing for a long time, it's annoying that you can't check exactly how much you need to save up for various quests without opening the conversation. The good news is the fix is relatively easy: just let the player view the resource requirements for every conversation event at any time, without spending an action.2. At the beginning of a level, you get to create your Houses before you know what the Curriculum quest is going to be. Just trigger the Curriculum quest at the very beginning instead so the player knows what to build towards.3. There are some UI bugs when the hand gets very full of cards, and also sometimes with placing artifacts in rooms while zoomed out.4. When placing rooms that stick out very far to the side or stick out sideways on very high floors, sometimes no support structure is drawn, and sometimes the support structure art looks kind of janky. Since the overall art quality is one of the strongest aspects of the game, it's a bit immersion breaking.5. UPDATE: Several years later I have to say I am disappointed by the lack of bugfixes to the UI. The game literally doesn't fit inside the window in either windowed or fullscreen. Some bugs on release are okay and to be expected, but customers have a right to expect that bugs will be fixed over time after release, and that hasn't apparently happened.UPDATE 2: The devs have released apparently their final update to the game, which fails to address the UI issue. Based on the poor level of support after release, I can no longer recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I love a lot about this game but I can't give it a positive review in good conscience after the devs have seemingly abandoned it. Last update was almost a year ago with no word since. This game is definitely not finished and as much as I like the gameplay it just doesn't have enough to do at the moment, some mechanics like the dungeons feel incomplete and need a lot more work and like many people pointed out you spend too much time staring at the screen. Would only recommend buying if they come out with another update. Really hoping the devs surprise us so I can change my review to positive.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This game had so much potential to be something more, it's a real wonder why the devs abandoned the game. The UI could use serious improvements - things I'd personally like to see are easily looking at students' progression, their equipment, needs, etc. There's dungeons in this game that utilize the equipment students use, but it's really halfassed content... AFAIK, you only get one attempt at a dungeon in each zone and then it's gone. Anyway, despite me putting some time into this game, I can't recommend it since it's been abandoned. If you decide to play, just know that it's pretty random with what cards you'll get, don't go into a game expecting to create a certain university.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Core mechanics contradict each other - you are on a timer so you need to be effective, but everything you can play is pure RNG. You can't build the deck, you can't focus, you can't strategize - just draw 3 cards out of many and choose which one is best to play and quite often none of them is what you need. There is a good amount of options and even some synergies, but they can materialize only by chance, a rather small one too, and not by conscious effort and when they finally do, it's usually near the end of the round.It's a fun little game for a while, with great art .. just not worth the $20
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good but not great. There is not much feedback how much student can learn, or how long / how teachers teach. How many skills can a pupil learn in 5 years? Also events are a bit too few, so it starts getting repetitive few maps in. Not much feedback how big the classes should be, or how many students can actually sleep in 5 beds.Despite all that, game basis is quite exciting. Pick it up with DLC, if it ever comes out, as events and all other things need bit more flesh on those bones.Solid 7/10, DLC could bring it to 8 or 9.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I'll never understand why someone puts so much time making a unique game and make it... empty. The hard part is done, the game works and works well, it's just boring. There is A LOT going on in the game in spite the simple nature of it. You can make different "Houses" for students, which is neat but pointless (not like a house you physically live in, like House of Slytherin type ♥♥♥♥). It's neat because it lets you give basically buffs to members of said house and each individual student application, which you can accept or reject, comes with different strengths and weaknesses. Each house might give you bonuses for student performances, for example, so you might want your students really good at a trait to be in it, but because of the buffs you also might wanna put students weak in an area to be in that same house. It's so cool, well thought out, but what if I told you that the game is easy to win without this? Every teacher you hire, they have different stats, but they don't really matter. Nothing matters. You spam rooms and you gain more currency and you spam more rooms. You can be very thoughtless, still do well, and move on. There is so much going on, but you are not punished for aimlessly doing nothing. You have no reason to study all the information in the game, it doesn't matter. There's random faction stuff, but it doesn't matter. You have little agency over some things, a lot over others but the choices don't matter much. It's a shame!It is a good game, but not at the price point. You will not likely get your money's worth. It's soul-less, empty. Nothing engaging. It's so close, but without a real challenge and without there being any consequence for spamming rooms to farm a lot of "currency" in various magic types or gold coins, whatever, there's no point. That's how you win, by nothing contemplating consequences for over building your school and watching it accumulate a lot of wealth because it's big. This was on standard difficulty. There are TWO difficulties beneath it that makes the game even easier. How could it possibly get easier is beyond me. A game impossible to lose is somehow capable of being easier. Hah!If you can get it for less than $5, go for it. Don't pay over that though.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game from the Humble Choice monthly bundle. I did not pay for it. Did two and a half runs in less than four hours, and I feel like I've seen pretty much everything the game has to offer mechanics-wise.You get parts to build and tweak your school from various decks rather than building the school yourself. The process of what classes and rooms you add to your school is wholly RNG-based. You might not ever see a certain type of classroom or magical beast that would help you accomplish your three randomly-assigned school goals.It's similar to pulling cards from lootboxes that use a magic-themed metacurrency than anything else. You have little control over what you get aside from cards you receive from events.There are some events which will add a ONE-TIME ACCESS dungeon to the map that you can send students to explore using the skills and spells you've taught them. I would've liked to see more of this. As it stands you probably won't see this side of gameplay more than once per run, if that.There isn't much else to the lather, rinse, repeat gameplay loop and it gets stale fast. I would've liked to see more interaction with the world, the students and the staff.Game has potential if they take the time to add more ways to interact with it. Otherwise it feels like an idle game, and not a very fun one at that.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game and I am glad that I had the chance to get it a bit cheaper through Humble Choice!I generally enjoy deckbuilding/ card games but often struggle with them as I am just not good in creating a good combination in my deck. This game makes it easier and presents you with a fixed deck, which I personally liked a lot.It is your job to build a university for different kinds of magic, to train students for different jobs, keep up with different fractions on the map, etc. The game offers a number of things to do, it never gets boring.For the campain you have to play thorugh a few maps until you unlock the end location and can either win or lose the story. I personally liked that there is an end to the whole thing and you can "complete" it in some way. If you happen to lose you still get the chance to try again, which is very generous and means that you don't have to repeat 10 hours.I got roughly 13 hours out of the campain but I mainly played in double speed, so a normal timed game will probably take a lot longer even. You get a lot of content for the price and I can only recommend you try the game out for yourself :)
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This is Early Access done right. The gameplay loop is already satisfying and creative. It's a unique mix of cards and buildings, and management and strategy. You're basically running hogwarts. You sort students into houses and build rooms to train them. At the end of their school terms they graduate to a career. _childDocuments_.review: Sadly I too think I should not recommend this game.I really would have wanted to like it, since the first few levels sure made a good first impression. The game has cute charm, the humor is delightful and, since I personaly enjoy randomness, I really liked the card-based approach to rooms/items/etc and also enjoy the graduation system.However, I share the opinion that the game has a good foundation but falls short on the long run.At first I too tried to manage smart. I decided which students to take and sometimes didnt accept some into my school, so the rooms wont be exhausted. I was trying to get a feeling for how many students I can host at a given time and tried to do some good managment with the random ressources I get.However, beginning with mission 4 I got that bad feeling that the best approach might be good old "whatever" - "wherever". And much to my (negative) surprise it worked quite well. The thing is: There is little punishment for doing that approach. Students, when their needs arent fulfilled, will just leave the school for a moment, throw a little tantrum and then slink right back in. They wont leave, they wont die, they will just be less efficient. So hey, just spamming (taking in any student and just expand as fast as possible) worked fairly well on the hardest difficulty (Archmage) with the Darkness Challenge enabled ... in the last few missions I only wanted to get the missions done, so I had finished at least one whole campaign playthrough. I knew all the rooms, I knew all the items, and the missions just got a repetitive chore where I would spam most magic disciplines anyways.The only mission that was slightly interesting again was the very last mission which added a bit more of a challenge and was actualy a very close call in my playthrough. But at that point the game had already lost me.So ... if you are looking for a relaxing casual experience with charm and humor you might still enjoy the game. Give it a try, maybe its for you. It does have that good kind of student humor and magical shenanigans. But if you are looking for something where your choices have a deep impact for overcoming challenges... eh, better look somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost didn't buy this game due to the negative reviews, but I gave it a chance on sale and I'm really glad I did. I've had a lot of fun with it, though it did take me a while to get my head around it (the tutorial isn't very helpful, and I had to watch a 'Let's Play' to figure out how everything worked). That being said, the imagination that's gone into customising all the different classrooms is wonderful (I particularly like the Interdimensional room where the students walk up the walls), and it's really fun to watch the students at their lessons. There's a lot to think about based on what traits the students/teachers have, and I really enjoy how the rooms change visibly when you improve them. I definitely find myself thinking up strategies, and wanting to come back to the game and try new things. I also really enjoy the dungeon-crawl system, and wish these events were more frequent.Personally, I would prefer slightly more control over the school, especially when you only get given objectives later in the level. If your first few cards have been Light and Nature focused, and then your student objective comes up (i.e to train a certain number of students in a particular future) and your only choices for that are between Shadow, Arcane and Alchemy it can be tricky to get 3 stars. For the same reason, I wish there was a way to assign particular students to certain classrooms/lessons (something like a timetable) because at the moment even if you assign a particular subject as 'forbidden', students in that House will still study that subject if the classrooms for their permitted subjects are full. This frustrates me, because it can impact what futures the students come out with, so being able to specify in more granular detail what each person could study would be really helpful for attaining higher classes at graduation.I understand that the rooms/futures you get are meant to have an element of chance, but sometimes it's just so difficult as to not be fun/interesting anymore (e.g. if you want to train assassins but every time you pick shadow cards they're all demon/necromancy themed, or else are objects instead of classrooms). Similarly, I've had times where I was desperate for a second dormitory, but had to buy about 10 sets of Gold cards before one came up. I think this could be balanced by a system that allows you to gain a particular card, but with a penalty (for example, if you wanted to specify an Assassin's Chamber, you could pay the normal Shadow fee plus a Gold fee, or loss of prestige).All that being said, neither of those issues are game-breaking for me, they're just things I'd prefer. Oddly, the one thing I don't have a problem with is what's come up frequently in other reviews, and that's room placement. It doesn't bother me at all that you can't move rooms once you've placed them - in fact, I think that makes perfect sense. In a real school, you couldn't just move a classroom whenever you felt like it. Perhaps there could be the option to renovate a room which changes it to something else for a fee, but it's really not something that's bothered me.So, all in all, I had a lot of fun with this game once I got my head round it, and even though there are tweaks that would make it a more interesting game for me personally, I recognise that this won't be true of everyone (and probably would change the game beyond what the developers were aiming to create). If you're on the fence about trying it, I'd say go for it!

Menus have different hunt-and-peck close buttons, with no keyboard or mouse binding such as ESC or right-click.3. Lack of sound and tactile feedback on menu inputs.4. Lack of option to auto-pause on reaching the ability to purchase new cards. There is no decision-making between card selection and play, so this is an unnecessary convenience to the player.5. _childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a glorified mobile app.  Would be worth it for a $10 price tag, not a $25 price tag.  I was pretty addicted about ten hours into the game, on maybe my third school.  However, I quickly soured to the repetitiveness of the game.  The more effort you put into this, the less rewarding it is, which is very counter intuitive.  However, you just don't get enough control over elements of the school that interest you, and I am not sure what is the most efficient way to progress about the halfway point of every level. So the game is played through 6 levels, though each level is basically just a fresh game with minor bonuses and penalties that carry through.  Each level takes around 3-4ish hours to complete, depending on small factors here or there.  Your primary objective (though I didn't know this at first) is to complete the three missions that you select at the beginning of each level.  One mission is likely a faction mission, one is usually an accumulate this much mana of one type, and one is usually graduate students into this job, forcing you to focus on certain classes within your school.  If you do this right, there is pretty solid synergy with the missions, though you are at the mercy of the RNG to try and get the right cards.  And that is one of many frustrating aspects of this game.I loved being able to build up my school with rooms.  You can create some really awesome looking structures as you build.  As you level up rooms (by playing the same card on top of itself) the rooms get some neat graphical improvements which really give character to the game.  However, this is another nitpick I have, as I'm not sure if it is more efficient to level up rooms, or to create new ones, especially with rooms like the bedrooms and dining rooms.  Another really dull aspect that could use improvement is the actual quantity of game here.  If you visit factions, for example, you seem to have access to only a handful of different options.  How many times did I visit the Lord of Evil and just rescue a dragon?  How many times were the orcs having an Olympic games when I visited?  Related: in one dungeon I rescued the same bard looking for the same piano three separate times.  ONE dungeon.My last big complaint about the game is the interface itself.  I have a fairly beastly computer, but I experienced a lot choppy gameplay when trying to zoom in or play a potion component or drag a card to a room somewhere.  Not sure why I would have performance issues on a game like this when I can run high end releases without any issue.  For something that looks like a mobile game, it was annoying and detracted heavily from my enjoyment.I had a lot of fun playing this before the repetitiveness and boredom struck, which means this game will give you about an afternoon of entertainment.  I have played a lot of Steam games that were board games first and then adapted as a video game, but this might be the first one that would be more successful as a board game, and I would love to see some sort of conversion using this theme and several of the same mechanics.I'd pass on this one unless you can get it for under $15 on a Steam sale.  There are far better options at this price tag for this level of enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: Spellcaster University is relaxing and fun once you figure out a few things. Before that it can be a bit frustrating. Don't go into this assuming you'll be in complete control of your school. Luck plays a huge role in the game - the winning strategy is knowing how to make use of the luck you get to build up your school and students, win stars, and use them to finally defeat the Demon Lord. Get an event early on that gives you Nature mana? You might want to decide one of your goals that game is to gain Nature mana, because you've got a head start already. Get Shadow mana instead? Well, guess you might just be more into necromancy and demonology this game. After playing for a while, you begin to have sympathy for Dumbledore and realize that many of the oddities of Hogwarts in fact make perfect sense.  In the meantime, the game throws mild humour at you in the form of cute dragons, unionized, coffee-drinking professors, and the worst parents you can imagine. There's also a bit too many things to keep track of (like which class to sort students into), and lots of details you don't realize are important until later (it took me three schools to figure out that the card icons shown on the top of some cards meant I already had one in my school!). Learning what works in the rare dungeon crawls is also a bit of trial and error. But once you've figured things out, the difficulty of the game ramps down a lot and you're left with random but predictable gameplay.It's the kind of game that's mild fun for hours - not gripping or exciting, but enjoyable when you're tired and just want to relax.

I feel like just running away without a fight while "realistic" just isn't as fun from a gameplay perspective.

Second, it's not a narrative-driven game either: you have cute students and professors coming in and out but they never become "characters" you get attached to. You can't influence the behaviour of a specific person, you mostly look at them walking around and doing the various activities. It's no Academagia (for those who remember that unlucky game).In a sense, the game reminds me of those idle games for mobile phone, where you do something here and there and mostly look passively at what happens in the school while you're waiting for an event to appear or to have enough mana to add a room.Still it's a pleasant enough killing time game, and has nice touches like the cuteish graphics, the occasional adventures in the dungeon and the curiosity to see which job the graduates are going to get. A good game to have some fun without using your brain too much.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a crossover of Project Highrise and Two Point Hospital.I really like the concept and the graphics/animations seem very solid to me. I didn't see notable bugs and the game runs fine. It's poorly optimized though and for me some of the mechanics don't really fit together.There's a few things throwing me off badly and most of them are UI related and easy to improve.1. Since it's not possible to move or remove placed rooms (which is fine), it's really important to plan your future room connections a little in advance. The cards for new rooms have colored doors in different places to give you that information. However you can only spot that briefly when you hover over a card as it is off screen when not hovering and quickly covered with description when hovered. Fix: Either show more of the cards all the time or even better show/hide the description on right click, alt or something similar.Same problem applies to potion brewing. (The recipes show you the items, the cards show you the names)2. It's a real mess to manage your houses. For example when you create a new house and want to move existing students in, it's really tedious to go through their data and sort it out. Also it's hard to find someone you are looking for. Fix: Give me some sorting or filtering options.3. Some rooms have buffs when you reinforce them. You can't check your existing rooms while you get cards to choose from. So you have to recognize what level your rooms are and at what levels they get buffs to make a good decision. Fix:Let me hide/minimize the card overlay and just keep the time at pause until i picked my card.Overall this game wants a few QoL overlays to give you all that information in one go instead of clicking every single room/person every time you forgot. I remember playing "Where is Waldo" whenever i found a trophy room and wanted to move some specific relics/decors there. The problem is they blend in really well, which is actually great, just not when you search for it. I imagine highlighting the outlines of all decor on holding a key just like any point and click adventure.I'd also like to see "+54% chance for new students to get x" instead of "+3% chance for new students to get x, 18"Another thing that i don't feel comfortable with are the game modes.Campaign feels tedious, Endless mode is missing a challenge.It took me about 5h to finish the first of 7 Campaign levels, additionally there are 6 Campaign Challenges requiring you to finish the Campaign once each to unlock more cards. I won't even complete the Campaign once, just because of the time requirement.I really like the idea and i admit that the developers delivered a solidish game, i just don't think it's done yet. More like Early Access...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, for a while. I gave it a thumb down because I expected to manage a magical university, but in truth the mechanics are 98% gameboard. _childDocuments_.review: Spellcaster University is a pretty cool simulator of your very own Hogwarts.  Starting basically with nothing but an empty hall, you play "cards" which further expands your school.  You pay for these cards out of resource pools you earn over time, depending:  gold, shadow magic, arcane, alchemy, nature, and light.  The gist is to have a fully functioning school with various classrooms to meet certain quests, such as having students graduate with one ore more specialties, like having arcane and light magic.  You can even set up specific schools and can tailor what your students will learn while they study, all while trying to make sure they behave, and meeting their needs for boredom, hunger, and sleep by having a student hall, rectory, and dormitory, respectively.  Along the way you have to contend that, soon, "Big Evil" will arrive, and you will be forced from your school to begin a new map.  You can juggle relationships with the major factions and if they like you well enough, you can buy additional cards from them, or even ask them to delay Big Evil before the Dark Lord arrives.It takes awhile to learn how the game works as it seems deceptively simple (and it is!), but it is difficult to master.  You try to meet up to three stars on how well your school is while balancing a budget, monster invasions, and students leaving school to seek fun, sleep, and food elsewhere (which you don't want them to do, but sometimes it's unavoidable).The game is full of quirky good humor.  Is the game in need of improvements?  I'm sure there are, but if you're hesitant to try this game, try looking up "Spellcaster University" (Let's Play!) on Youtube.  You'll find may persons who enjoy the game and discuss game mechanics to your liking.Hope you have fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Really, really enjoyed this game. The different strategies you can use within each campaign makes each experience a bit more interesting than the next. However, I do have one issue with it.Once you reach the final location (won't say it just so I don't spoil anyone), you must find a way to defeat the big boss once and for all. Luckily, you have multiple ways of doing this. My first attempt at this final location, I wasn't able to secure either routes towards victory. However, I was able to secure both at my second attempt. Here is where my issue presents itself. If you try and focus on defeating the boss (especially if it's towards the middle of the timeframe at the top of the screen), you're likely not able to get all 3 stars. If you choose to push towards satisfying your 3 objectives, like I did, the Lord of Chaos will show up and destroy you, even if you've secure both routes towards victory (the 5 cards and the skull's quests). And, when he destroys you, you may get all 3 stars, but it'll still read as you losing the game. That was a huge bummer for me, cause I was really looking forward to bragging to my friend.I'm not sure if this is just an oversight, but I would really recommend for the devs to correct this feature so players aren't stuck between a rock and a hard place. Kind of makes everything feel like it was for nothing, in the end. Overall, I really enjoyed this game. I hope to get 3 stars and an overall victory in my next play through!
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I love the idea of this game.  It has an enjoyable feel.  However, the mechanics are not intuitive at all.  The UI and the tooltips ought to give obvious indications as to what effect your decisions have on your game.  I honestly feel like when I'm playing I'm just picking random choices and there's no sense of what effect my choices have on the outcome of the game.  I don't feel like I'm in control of what happens at all, no do I have any sense of how well I'm doing or how I could improve how I play.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Great game hampered by a tough start for new players. Hear me out.This game suffers from a lack of a tutorial which I find inexcusable for a game not in early access (there is an option in the settings to reset one, but I never saw one). It suffers from a lack of tooltips in some areas. I still have no idea what hunger and sanity does to a character when it gets low for instance. Or what numerous buildings and items do. And I'm 32 hours in and have completed the entire campaign. It is clearly ported from another language and English is someone's second language, making it difficult to understand dialog options. It also has bugs such as being unable to place an item unless you zoom WAY in. Which happens. Every, single, map.All of that is worth slogging through for what is left. Which is an amazingly fun, just one more turn game. Even unpolished like it is I would highly recommend it. Super fun. Tons of replayability. The love poured into the game is apparent and greatly appreciated. I look forward to future patches hopefully addressing my earlier points. Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, especially for the price it's definitely got enough replay-ability IMO. It gives me such a sense of satisfaction completing the goals, discovering new futures for my students, and crushing it in the little dungeons, so 60 hours in and I haven't gotten bored of it. I appreciate the different game options, being able to make it harder or easier for yourself so however proficient you are at these type of sim/resource management type games you can find a level of difficulty that makes it fun. Like I said, I do agree with some of the other criticisms of the game being repetitive and that it does need some tweaks with the teachers having traits that don't matter for the room they're in (like the janitor or the nurse having teaching bonuses), and as an achievement hunter I wish there were more achievements and little secrets to find but but I've still gotten my moneys worth out of it. FYI I bought at full price, after the full release of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I played for 6 hours straight the day I downloaded it, so I must be pretty excited. Still learning, but feels like a management sim such as Two Point Hospital. The card mechanic doesn't really impede the sim overmuch (except when alchemy ingredients pile up and get annoying) although it means you cannot plan from the beginning what you are going to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely worth the purchase. I've put 24 hours into the game so far and that's only been enough time to play through the campaign twice. There is a lot of replayability, although it is a little repetitive and I'm already wanting some DLC. However, I am not usually a fan of the repetition in a rogue-like, so if you enjoy rogue-like games then this one will give you way more than 24 hours. You can complete challenges in the campaign and unlock new cards the appear in your future campaigns as well, so there is already variety added. It's easy to learn and is challenging at times too, you have to think about your moves and try to be strategic. The art is great and there is a quirky appeal to how the characters move and react to things, similar to The Sims games. All in all, great game, totally recommend. Make sure to keep the Orcs happy and feed them waffles.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This a very good game. But whether or not you will enjoy it will depend on your expectations. The game is labeled as a simulation, but I disagree that it is. If you go into this wanting a Hospital Tycoon style sim, you’ll be disappointed. It’s more like a deck-building/engine-building board game. Very RNG heavy. You pay resources to draw from a deck, getting to pick one of three cards. You have to weigh the benefits of taking one over the other. You then place your card, and placing it is permanent, so that adds weight to what you pick. There is a puzzle aspect to placement too - not all rooms connect, and adjacency bonuses are a thing to consider. So is whether you leave room for things like janitors or trophy rooms, both of which can have a huge impact on the efficiency of your school. It’s hugely satisfying when you start to figure out how it all works together and you start to get an efficiently thrumming school. But you don’t have long, there’s a set time (that you can slow or speed up through various actions) until the Dark Lord destroys your school and you have to start over from scratch, keeping some ongoing bonuses from your previous graduates’ outcomes.tl;dr: will I enjoy this game? If you want a deck-builder/engine-builder like Wingspan, then yes. If you want a simulator like Hospital Tycoon, maybe not.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun little simulation of a magic university complete with pets, artifacts, tomes, and a little dungeon crawling mini-game. The gameplay itself gets repetitive quickly but there are many ways to put restrictions on yourself or try new things to keep it interesting. i would try to get it on sale if possible because it will feel like more bang for your buck. other than that i highly recommend this game to fans of easy simulations with some humor and fun twists.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of good ideas in a cool relaxing game. BUT, nope.UI could use improvements (mostly on camera). A few bugs (to be expected in EA) need fixing.But most importantly the game feels like you are not doing anything. You build you university, you have students, they grow, you repeat. What is the game about when this is done?
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like the game since the idea of a wizard academy management sim was very appealing to me, but Spellcaster University leaves so much to be desired. Although genre-wise it's a split between a management sim, RPG and a card game, most of the time you will spend reading and clicking on cards, which honestly pop up way too often, they're almost intrusive and there's not nearly enough of them for you to not receive repeats throughout your playthrough, so eventually you just end up clicking on the same cards over and over again. Also now that I think about it, I doubt I could ever affect the outcome of the game regardless of what card I click. The only thing that seemed to matter, are the occasional story events, I can see those having negative impact, possibly leading to a "game over". That being said, I think you can't really fail since the worst case scenario is your playthrough ending in you not completing objectives in time and the headmaster saying "well because of this or that event, we decided to move the university to a different location" and it starts all over again.The management part of it seems a bit lackluster too. I didn't find a way to cycle between students, the item and card descriptions are very simplistic and so are the ingame statistics - otherwise important for a management sim. Actually the entire UI could've been done way better, clearer. Oh and there's also a combat system, that I got to see once and it was just as bad as the rest of it all, so I won't bother elaborating on it.I think you're meant to play the game multiple times as there're different locations to start your academy in, but honestly I can't be bothered. I just wasn't having fun, due to the inherent repetitiveness and very lacking gameplay mechanics. 3/10
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: It's... a fun enough game. Like a 6/10 game.The restriction on building size and poor AI (or perhaps limitation in how you can limit students into specific areas) makes the mid-late game rather dull and repetitive. However, each run is only a few hours so its bearable. There isn't really enough uniqueness in each map or enough things to do to really justify playing more than 4-5 maps (less than one campaign).
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a net positive. It's not amazing. It's fun for about 10 hours, but after that you really start to notice the bugs (can't place items after dungeons; text randomly goes invisible; characters refuse to go to certain rooms; et cetera). It's an interesting concept and it's certainly very fun at first, but then the game gets a bit repetitive and annoying with the bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun and helps you relax. Although there are few small bugs which can make the game crash but it auto saves, so You wont lose much progress if it may happen.  Also it seems if you play long enough (like 7h+) then small memory leak happens. But that only happened few times. Overall it was great game to be comfy and reduce anxiety.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

YOU CANT demolish any room that been misplaced (your unluck). You got "No control" over any character all you can do is just get new schoolars and teachers you cant even direct them to do something what you need/want neither fire or get rid of someone when they got already in school. With death timer on each level with either forcing you quests that "are cannot be refused" thats demands you a special classes that you didnt even roll basicly screwing you over bad luck. Good for 10 or 20 hours of gameplay but NOT WORTH ITS PRICE.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I am not much of a card based game fan but this one I actually enjoyed.  It has a kind of novel way of playing the cards unlike the standard turn-based designs.  You draw cards and play them to create a university in which to train mages. There's factions and magic types that influence some of the game play plus you draw and pick the cards in a in a manner where the RNG makes each new game completely different.  The key objective:  to build a university that has a spiffing reputation and produces students of an excellent calibre.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: You're in charge of a scuffed Hogwarts, building it from the ground and training Wizards before the LORD OF EVIL overtakes you. That's when you flee to the next map and build another Hogwarts, taking SOME advantages with you, if you performed well.There's six resources (such as light, arcane, ..) that accumulate over time, and grant you a choice of three cards (can be buildings, decorations, studends and more) when you hit a certain treshold.You can also visit the surrounding places from time to time (such as a village, tavern, ...).Sometimes you find a Dungeon and can investigate with a group of your choice.You are NOT directly in charge of the students or teachers. You build the facilities and basically manage the whole thing.All in all a fun and relaxing little indie game that I can definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Even though this game is promissing and interesting, I can't recommand it right now. It's an alpha-like early acces and there is so much to implement, so many bugs to fix and so many details to balance.If you're going for a Hogwarts manager experience, this is the game... But you gotta wait a bit. Devs are working on it, but they obviously need more time on this. Be patient, put this in your wishlist.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: When i saw this game i wondered if it was niche appealing to those who like Harry Potter or similar (while im a huge D&D fan). After a while on my wishlist i decided to buy it.. I'm pretty much impressed, there's a mix of dynamics, RNG, focusing schools for efficiency or trying for a perfect archimage. Maps influence schools too, environmental or locally. I'm at the last hurdle of the campaign but i'm ready for DLC or a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Just a warning, you lose each round. You try to get as far as you can. Your first 'school' is disposable. The students will all go on to be village wizards and minions, but if you keep at that second or third school, you might see significant improvements.Game play works like this:World map, pick a spot.Go to spot, deal with factions, make a school, fall in love with it, run screaming from it as the dark lord comes to burn it down. In this process you get 3 different star missions each on gives you a bonus to the next school. If you can't watch the forces of darkness smash you school, probably not a great game for you. Side note you don't actually see it get destroyed which I think is a sad. In the sims watching your house burn down was some times a healing moment after your main sim died cooking a steak and your kids are trapped inside...
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game.  In the vein of Fallout Shelter or Oxygen Not Included, but with a magical/fantasy theme.  There's enough variety for a lot of playthroughs.  The campaign is fairly long, and it's nice to work towards multiple quests through each phase of the campaign.  There is a bit of a learning curve, and some things aren't the most intuitive, but give it some time, and take advantage of the help pages within the game, and you'll get it.The few negative reviews I've seen so far seem to be from people who didn't fully grasp the mechanics of the game.  If I had one gripe, it's that you can't demolish rooms once they are built, and that sometimes the placement isn't obvious.  Eventually, you memorize how the rooms are laid out so it isn't as annoying, but when you are first beginning there doesn't seem to be clear logic as to why come of the rooms can't be built over.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Glitchy, buggy, laggy, and crash quite often. Refunded. Why do i recommend this then? Well i have faith that one day they will optimize it, i enjoyed the gameplay and love what they attempt to do. Right now this game is only enjoyable if you have NASA computer, maybe one day gamers in third world countries will be able to smoothly play this, i have hope...
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: If you miss click once or your hand gets moved by the cat then that space you wanted for another dormitory or refactory is gone, Or if you have an arcane room and wanted to upgrade it and you miss, now you have two arcane rooms and another teacher to pay for. the most limited resource in the game is space and has no way to reallocate it at all. you mess up once and you are permanently screwed for the rest of the game. hours of work down the drain and you have to start all over. i would rather play elden ring where there is at least a chance for redemption if you mess up, and i suck at elden ring.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Spellcaster University is a fun and challenging game. The random cards that you receive are making every round different and by far not all runs will lead to success. Campaign mode is always winable, due to the fact that the last challenge can always be repeated and the boni will be taken over. Winning the starting challenges will make the last fight easier though.The graphics are cute and the animations are well designed. For me the game has a high chance of being played again, even though right now the content is a little limited. The limitaion in options at that point of time is also the biggest downside. The game has a view flaws which i want to mention as well:- no long time reward in training students or teachers (they do not show up during the next level)- limited amount of variety in cards and options with other factions- few options only for the directors office - no option for an unlimited campaignThese would be the main issues for the time being.Things that I would like to see in the future:- more options to check on student status- more graphs, options and statistics for the directos office- actual fights that matter - option to just develop your school and not end through dark event (possible to get a heavy attack and lose pleanty of things, but continue), therefore implement school defences (magic or assassin traps)- adjacency bonus  and malus for certain rooms- reassignemnt of teachers to different rooms- notification feed of events (gain of reputation, teacher/student lost or gained traits etc)- better overview of student knowledge to use equipment more usefulThese are just some ideas which would improve the game experience in my opinion. But still at that point of time the game is very enjoyable and I am looking forward to what is to come!
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: There is no challenge. You can't lose game. The whole game is RNG based. You can't choose what to build like tropico or city skylines. You spend money or mana which gets progressively more expensive and always get to choose from 1 of 3 cards which can be a room or equipment.Students and teachers have positive and negative traits which in the end don't really matter and you can power through. There is really no difference.Every map I encountered just 1 opportunity to explore a dungeon and it was pretty underwhelming. Game doesn't really explain to you how it works. You either kill everything easily until you don't. I don't understand how damage of students is calculated because there is no explanation anywhere. So for roughly 1 hour of gameplay you get one 2 minute adventure into the dungeon. NiceAfter you kind of finish your university it just gets demolished and you have to build it again with no resources from before aside from yea you guessed it 1 of 3 minor bonuses and 1 of 3 minor penalties. There are some events here and there but all of them as far as I could see were so weak or easy to power through you just forget about them too fast.Game is pretty much scam for this price. Should go for like 5€ max
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah this is gonna be a no for me.The second I started a game the clunky controls on steam deck became apparent.I painstakingly tried to fix some of it in controller settings, which sort of worked, but still not recommendable for the deck.Then when I actually could start playing it stressed me out to no end. You can't change anything once you've confirmed it.Clicked on a creating a house, then realized you might wanna see what kind of students you get first? Nope you can't change it. Build a room that's either in the wrong place due to clunky controls or you feel like it would be better some place else? Too bad, it's stuck.. you can't destroy or move it.I mean come on, it's a magic school.. even non magic themed games allow you to change rooms around. There are no mods to change this either.Some people like the permanence of your choices, I am not one of those people.I like to learn from my mistakes and be able to fix them so I can continue enjoying the game. Especially when everything is still new to me.Shame cause I really liked the premise of this game, but if the stress overrides the fun, it's a no for me
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun, and funny. i was happy with paying full price for it. It does seem like i have reached the end of the content in it already at 30 hours of gameplay but it was super addicting. _childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Not "bad," just boring. At about halfway through my second hour of playing I wasn't even reading any of the cards any longer--just kind of mindlessly point-and-clicking my way through things, and I still 'won' most scenarios. It's not interesting enough to be engaging, not colorful and cute enough to be eye-catching (the graphics are really pretty boring,) and not fun enough to make me want to keep playing past a few hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This is such an addictive game! It's basically as if someone combined Fallout Shelter and the old Majesty games, then cranked up the incremental, progression aspect to where each student, university, or even campaign gives you a boost toward the next effort. There's a bit of a learning curve, particularly for a game where there's no undo button and there are clearly optimal approaches to take, but when you can get everything flowing things quickly become awesome.One of my favorite, unexpected elements is the dungeon mode, which lets you take some of these perfect prodigies you've been cultivating them and go into a dungeon crawl minigame that has an entire parallel combat system based on that magic they've been learning. It really satisfies the desire I got from the Majesty games to be able to control a character within that world.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: So far, it is fun to play. It is interesting to build and manage my own university. But the game lacks a goal. Each game, we have 3 quests, which are all easy to achieve, except the big magician one. So, after finishing the quests, I feel lack of motive to develop my university. Should I focus on quality of education? Or the quantity of students? I don't know. There is no indication of my achievement except for the score board, which I believe no one pays attention to. Therefore, I advise the developer to make the late game more meaningful.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun and probably worth $20, so buy it on sale unless you're really hard up for something to play.  I have some complaints which I'll rattle off, but in general I give it a thumbs up.There are some performance issues (which is strange since the game seems pretty simple graphically) and no real story or interest for anything that's going on.  There doesn't seem to be any way to fire teachers or deconstruct areas you've built, which is a real frustration if you accidentally put down a classroom that you already have (you can upgrade classrooms by dragging another copy of the build card to it...took me a couple rounds to figure that out).  There is some permanent randomness that accrues as you beat campaign levels, special spellbooks and debuffs that you have to pick depending on your performance, but I would like a little bit more freedom in deciding how to proceed.  In some respects, the game feels more like a mobile game than a full-fledged PC game, but it's still fun.The art style is cute and the aesthetic fits the content.  There is a lot of depth in maxing out bonuses for classrooms, but I would have liked to see more evolution or bonuses for building rooms in the same magic school near each other a la Reus.  I would also have liked to be able to set a schedule for the different houses, as you can in Prison Architect.  This is a pretty unique concept, so there's opportunity to expand on it.  The game is otherwise complete from a feature perspective: not early access, which is unusual and refreshing.What I would really like from this game is for the devs to take the resources and capabilities they've gained from making this game and make a sequel that fleshes out the features, makes it feel a little bit more personal and allows you to build some sort of a "community" out of the people you've graduated.  It would be really cool for students to eventually show up as teachers or something like that.  Add more depth, more self-direction, more make-your-own-story and less constraints and I'll buy that too.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Spellcaster University is a fun but relatively simple management game. I would recommend it, but certainly not over the similarly priced Oxygen Not Included or (if you still want the magic flavor) Mind over Magic. There are hints of deep gameplay systems like student equipment and stats, teacher abilities, magic specializations, dungeons, etc.  You are better off accepting every student thrown your way because the only thing that matters is your ability to produce gold and magic. Other reviews mention the RNG aspect of the decks you draw from to get new rooms and items, and there is truth to this, but the solution is the aforementioned "turn your brain off and accept everyone" strategy (more production = more card draws. simple as that). This is still fun though, just don't expect an in-depth management game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: What should be a very solid game gets tripped up by excessive RNG.  4/10 I absolutely do not recommend it at full price, but for $10, it's probably worth it. I've already got 15 hours out of it, so I can't complain too much, but this game should be so much better than it is. There are a lot of promising things going on: building a school, some semi-permanent progression, battles, balancing relationships, creating unique school houses. The game has almost everything I'd want in this sort of experience. Basically every aspect relies on RNG and ends up making the experience more frustrating than rewarding. You can easily get soft-locked out of objectives because the single card you need just doesn't show up, a dungeon run can end in an insane difficult spike that takes you from defeating dragons to having your party wiped by goblins. Not only is the entire game reliant on RNG, but the player rarely has the ability to control their own fate.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I love this silly little game, still learning how everything works but, almost 40 hours in i think I'm finally gettin' the hang of it!Definitely a good time waster, i really have nothing bad to say!You should 100% play if you like a bit of strategy in long form games. Couple tips from what ive learned: if you want any- im not at all a professional hahahvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvMake sure you check the paper on the desk in the headmasters office and adjust the schools settings to how you like, i personally like to keep everything the basic settings except change it to where you get a better chance that higher educated students apply.Play for the long game, try to get as many perma buffs as you can before you get to your last stage. from either finishing as many of the star objectives you choose for the level, or making good students.You wont get to play all the stages that show up, you'll get to pick only a few so make sure to read what the levels do so you know what to focus on as you'll be getting a perma buff and debuff at the end of each level.Try to get a councillor and a janitor up early. Especially the councillor, as they help get your students better jobs at the end of their studies leading to a higher chance of perma buffs for the school.REAAAD everything, the cards tell you what they do, you also don't NEED to play cards some events require you to discard some things.Thats all i think. Have fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: For those concerned about the "doom timer", this game does have endless mode and it's unlocked from the start by choosing "Quick Game" and selecting endless mode.The "resets" in campaign mode is actually a good thing, since buffs that you get from successful graduates are carried over to the next game. You'll build better and better school while learning new mechanics on every iteration.We definitely need "undo", "demolish room" , or "move room" button. Once you misplaced a room, there's nothing you can do to fix that until the next stage.I'd still recommend this game. I got this from humble choice, worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed the game quite a bit, although some of the criticisms listed in other reviews are fair. It's a bit of an "aquarium simulator" in that it's not particularly interactive with the students and settings, although I always found myself busy with building the school and placing upgrades. For the devs: The dungeon crawling addition really added a cool dynamic and allowed you to see your top students in action for the school rather than just at graduation. FLESH THIS OUT MORE and make it a larger/more frequent part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Game crashes out of nowhere. Was streaming and it went down 5x in one evening. Then today when I hit quit to exit the game it stayed up and refused to exit without logging out of windows. When you tab out of the game it just minimizes, which sucks if you are streaming to talk to chat or do anything outside of the game. The game itself is alright but poor contast in the colors of the decks makes it hard to read exactly how much mana you've built up. If the game fixes these issues then I would recommend it but for now, best to find the steam code on another website to play it for the low. 2.5/5 at best
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Spellcaster University is a fairly simple, fun and addictive management game. It does have the marks of an indie title as you will often encounter redundant or wierdly designed systems. Other reviews have already mentioned this, but the dungeon system seems tacked on and it often feels like you have to fight with the game to create the best possible candidates for dungeon-crawls. The quest system also does not really integrate that well into the rest of the game's mechanics. As the classes you can set up are essentially random, it is very possible to get a quest to train a certain type of wizard which you have already specialized your university away from. These are minor nitpicks however. The overall experience remains great and I often have trouble putting the game down once I have started a session. I hope the developers update and polish it in the future, but even if they don't Spellcaster University remains worthy of a purchase.

Take over as the headmaster of a university (while also holding onto the skull of the former headmaster) and create an awesome school … again and again and again ...    • Several levels to a campaign. The player has to rebuild the school each level.    • Player can adjust speed and difficulty at the beginning of campaign.    • Player can create student houses according to traits and/or type of magic proficiency.     • Students consist of: humans, elves, half-orcs, deepfolk, werewolves, and vampires. Non-humans have unique traits.    • There are different factions the school needs to have good reputation with. Each level has a unique character or faction as well. Having good reputation results in a positive effect.    • Types of magic: Shadow, Light, Arcana, Alchemy, and Nature.     • Dungeons involve automated card battles. The player chooses what to use before the start of battle, then clicks “start battle.” If a student dies, they can be revived with a phoenix feather (if the player has one).     • Discworld references.     • Addicting gameplay. I actually like rebuilding the school over and over again, trying different things each time.    • So many different objects and artifacts to decorate and improve the school with.    • There are several pets/familiars that roam around being cute or funny. Of course, my favorite is the cat.     • Students get particular accessories according to what magic they’ve learned. A few examples: angel wings, demon horns, mechanical wings, antlers, etc. There are  of them.     • There are a ton of student futures. Dozens and dozens of “professions” a student can end up being after they’ve graduated. Some of my favorites: guinea pig tamer, grandma eater (werewolf only), hallucinogenic plants gardener, carnivorous plants gardener, sandman, shinobi, archdruid, thaumaturge, plane walker, death master, chimera creator    • Each level is a different setting. Some of them are pretty cool. I liked the clouds, the forest, and, of course, the .     • Can’t organize the cards in hand.    • Sometimes, to place a card, you have to zoom in really closely before the game acknowledges it.    • Clicking on the info question mark during a dungeon sometimes causes the battle to start.    • In-game cursor is really small; it’s difficult to see.     • There could stand to be more random events. I feel like I’ve seen them all and there really aren’t that many overall.I recommend it to those who like building sims and fantasy.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This is a borderline recommendation. Because it's a fairly cheap game and you'll get hours out of it. But it has some issues:1. Meta progression feels weak/RNG heavy. It's even possible to "negatively progress", due to being given trash rewards and only crippling curses after each stage, despite scoring the best possible score. There are some absurdly good rewards, but if you don't get them as an option tough luck.2. Meta progression is self contained in a campaign. You keep the progression for the 7 or so stages you get to play, then it resets back to 0 for your next campaign. The only exception is a handful of artifacts you can unlock by doing challenge runs. 3. Not a lot of events. After 1 or 2 maps you will basically have seen almost everything except the the map unique events. 4. No option to end a mission when you've achieved everything you can. You just have to wait for ages.5. You can't set priorities for certain disciplines under a school. Which means if your objective is to graduate students only knowing, say, enchantment and herbalism, you either only build those facilities (e.g. no druidism/beast tamer if you want herbalism), or just pray your students go to those as much as possible. It would be nice if students prioritized the disciplines needed for your objectives.6. UI is kinda bad. Would be nice if you could display all the slots in your school (e.g. animal slots) even if they are occupied, so you can quickly find the spots you've actually filled as well if you want to replace them. 7. Game will randomly lock out certain areas for building. For example if you build a donut you won't be able to fill in the middle for some reason (and yes I'm aware you got to have exits to the area you want to build, obviously).8. It would be nice if anything besides scoring the stars mattered for meta progression. Like the bonuses your students give you when they graduate. 9. You're unable to fire or hire new teachers after a facility is built, which is kinda dumb.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, quick to grasp yet hard to perfect, and chalked full of humor! Send hamsters instead of owls for diplomatics! invite a TON of magical creatures into your school to mostly just wander around! Has all the stuff you need for a teenage story with no depth (vampires, werewolves, you get the point).Choose longer playtime for those who stress about completing everything, or speed it up to get through it as fast/best you can!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I take it ALL back. I'm leaving my previous review below just so you lot can see precisely how wrong I was, but, sho, yo, pff, damn... yeah, I was wrong. This game is weirdly GRIPPING! I tumbled down the rabbit hole and I got hooked. I don;t know how it happened, I don't know why it happened, but it did. Somewhere along the line I became obsessed with pumping out archmage after archmage and sending my prestige skyrocketing. It doesn't make sense to me, but that's where I am, 25 riveting game hours down in, what? 4 days? I used to have other hobbies!It's as casual as they come but very pleasing. I'm always on the lookout for games I can pick up for half an hour or so in between chores, work, human sacrifices, etc., and I find Spellcaster University ideal in that sense. It takes just a few seconds to pick back up where you left off, and you can drop out again in a few seconds without feeling like everything is going to collapse on you the next time you load up.The aesthetics are basic but bold. I found the bright colours and clean lines to be very pleasing on the eye, and even when your university gets to its maximum size, it's still fairly easy to tell each room and item apart. Having students wander around in their house colours also elicited a sad little squee from me. Turns out Trudi Canavan rubbed off on me a little more than I thought. Oh, and the animals wandering around the school are a nice little touch, both visually, and, well, because. Looking at you, chubby Pegasus. The gameplay is quite bare bones but not unsatisfying. Truth be told, it's a few steps away from being a mobile game in terms of demands on the player. You whack down cards and then wait until you have the resources to whack down a few more. In the meantime, you have a few scripted events to deal with, most of which eventually culminate in slight changes to how quickly you can whack down cards... It's not the most taxing game. Customisation is sufficient to add a little bit of flavour, but could be expanded upon. I imagine I will quickly get bored of seeing the same robe colours, even if I do enjoy giving the houses their own badges. The content is fairly limited. After one playthrough I'd already seen the same events 5-6 times, and I had duplicates of every card available. I'm hoping a little more gets added in the future, but what's there for now is definitely sufficient for half a dozen hours of entertainment. In conclusion, I like the game a lot, but I doubt I will play it beyond my third or fourth university. What's there is nice, but there's just not enough variety in gameplay to make it a marathon time killer.EDIT: My gameplay estimations were WAY off. The dungeon diving is a real draw, and the perks between levels do make a bit of a difference, otherwise, my observations are the same... it's just way more addictive than I anticipated.Hi there! If you like my review, please feel free to check out our curator page! For more full reviews, you can check out my personal page:

_childDocuments_.review: This is a difficult review to write (for several reasons) since I have some mixed feelings about the game. I definitely recommend the game if you like simulation games; this is a decent one and it is fun. It's just not for everyone.Positives:* The game is fun; it allows (at least on normal difficulty) to play around, test combos, and just spend some fun time building up a school, even despite severe restrictions in saving the game* The game is funny; there is an adequate amount of humor, some of it light, some of it quite dark - and it suits the mood just right* There are some interesting worldbuilding tidbits, some serious, some not* The playthroughs are varied; there is an optimal order of maps to follow, but you can play around with it and it is not absolutely necessary* The existence of game-wide bonuses and penalties, choosen after every map, only increases the variety* The faction & reputation system is an interesting mechanics* The messengers; you just have to see themNeutrals, depend on your tastes:* There is just one save slot, so the game is effectively an Iron Man challenge all the way (I'm not calling it roguelike only because it's a sim game); you can manipulate save files but it not exactly convenient* The aestetic is very simple and some people may find it ugly; I find it endearing, cute, and fitting the theme* The plot is very simple - "evil overlord is coming to your lands, you have to train mages and repel the evil" - though in my opinion, it works* You lack control over many things, you only set up the conditions; the amount of micromanagement available is quite limited* Randomness of the game (especially the card choices and teacher choices) can sometimes cause the given map to be suddenly either very easy (if you hit a very fitting card) or horribly hard (if you keep getting useless cards)Negatives:* The game is quite unpolished; there are some bugs that lock the game in an unplayable state (and force a restart with loss of progress) and some that are just annoying* The UI quality is below what one can expect from a game that is out of Early Access - the screen sometimes zooms in unexpectedly, cards get stuck or get in the way, screen moves unexpectedly which causes a misclick, etc.* The UI lacks some functions that would make life easier, like finding a specific room by name/type (you have to remember the appearances or click them all) or knowing the salary of a given teacher; it is not critical, but micromanaging is really difficult* Some expected options are simply missing, like demolishing a room; one misclick (possible because of the UI) and you're stuck with a badly placed room - which can seriously hamper your chances to accomplish the level's goals* The student's behavior is sometimes really erratic and unexpected* Quests descriptions are not always clear, and sometimes you get quest conditions you did not expectIn general, the game is fun, but don't expect it to be flawless.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cute game!Very unique gameplay, easy to grasp (But a bit hard to fully understand), and it was a lot of fun. I feel like there is a lot of potential for things to be added and changed up a bit, but I had a lot of fun, and really enjoyed everything. There are a few bugs here and there (For example, having a controller plugged in messes with your movement), and while some things are explained well, others are not. I also kind of wish there was a mode for just continuously playing, like an endurance mode, where you could have more focus on dungeons and building your university exactly how you want. Also kinda wish there was a way to delete or move rooms, but I suppose that plays into the random aspect.All in all, really good game! A total treat!
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of this game is good.The implementation, optimisation, and everything actually 'live' about the game is is not.I am VERY glad I received a code from a certain other store that meant I only spent $3 instead of the full price here on Steam. I have now uninstalled the game and until there are some significant improvements (and perhaps an explicit promise that eating saves can no longer happen) I will not be playing it again.I spent 2.5 hours playing, and enjoyed it if it was a bit monotonous. Optimising the school layout, upgrading certain rooms to develop highly trained students (my focus was necromancer assassins with a sprinkling of alchemy on the side), selecting the smart and wealthy students to gain prestige, and getting them good items or buffs to get more mana, to then get more rooms and items. It's a 'fine' gameplay loop.Well, the end of my first school arrived, and I'd done pretty well I thought. 2 stars (i.e., 2 of 3 big 'aims' for this school achieved) and lots of prestige ('currency' earned for producing good students). I'd managed to get a lot of campaign based bonuses (some careers give you permanent boosts which will affect your next school in the same campaign). I think I had better Enchantment workshops and more efficient infirmaries (basically, produce more enchantment mana to get more cards and students spend less time in the infirmary), and also more chance for 'worker' student tag and better pedagogy for my teachers.With that first school over, I set up the next one in the forest, saved, and quit the game. I come back to it today, get to the main menu and... 'Continue' is greyed out. ok, I go into 'Load'. Nothing there. I look through all my game files. Can't find my save.So I put in 2.5 hours of quite mediocre gameplay, but honestly still looking forward to slowly improving my schools over the course of the campaign and.. poof. Like a magic trick, the game just deleted my progress. Avada Kedavra on the save. Dead. Gone.For that reason, and the decidedly average gameplay, I cannot recommend this game. If you can get it for $3 like I did, it might be worth a spin, but be warned you might lose all your progress because the game can't save???. Otherwise, don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: I like management sims, and I appreciate how many times SpellcasterU cycles you through a management sim early game. That's the part I enjoy the most anyway, so having it stretched out like this is great. The longer I play the laggier it gets until it eventually locks up entirely, so just be aware and adjust.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could love this game, as it's a good start toward what could be a solid experience. But it becomes monotonous and half-baked really quickly. _childDocuments_.review: It is surprisingly casual and fun to play while also being interesting enough to warrant multiple hours. Like today was my first time playing and I sunk like 6 hours into it. _childDocuments_.review: If Hogwarts and D&D had a lovechild, Spellcaster University would be it. I like playing with the card UI, I always tend to forget that you can keep cards and you don't have to clear the board, regardless, it's definitely a new kind of game play. I love the creativity that went into this. My only recommendation would be to allow a "legacy" style of game play where, throughout the length of the campaign, the children of your initial students come back and enroll in the University. Lots of people don't enjoy building an entire university and then losing it 6-7 times before you get a chance of winning against the bad guy (aka Satan or the Dark Lord), but I think it's refreshing. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Has some promising ideas and aesthetics, but so far the execution has left me disappointed.-There aren't many interesting decisions or tradeoffs. Most of the game is spent waiting passively until I can afford another card, which I then automatically buy because there's nothing else to do with my resources. Then I'm at the mercy of the game as to which 3 cards I receive. It's hard to plan a long-term strategy this way.-None of the characters have personalities. I watch a bunch of random students and teachers walking around the building. This would be a great opportunity to introduce some narratives and relationships, but for now there's nothing to make me care about, or influence the lives of, individual characters.Overall, the game feels less like being Dumbledore and more like watching numbers go up.

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute, as you get further into it you start to realize that you have to be strategic about how you build your school. _childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I was browsing the Store, looking for something of a builder/manager variety, when I stumbled across this game. At first, I thought this looked interesting enough to play, so I bought it and started a new game.Holy fart-bomb-in-an-elevator, Buttman!There's so much detail in the managing that, of course, I bungled my first few games royally, but I kept coming back, because this game really IS interesting. It has combinations of student abilities, intelligence, income, and other factors that will determine their ultimate career once they graduate. That's not even mentioning the teacher abilities, room bonuses, item benefits, and faction bonuses. It's like juggling seventeen pissed-off hedgehogs at the same time!Yes, I am addicted. Yes, the game can be frustrating since you rely on a good roll from an RNG to determine what your next encounter with a faction will be, what your students' full stats will be, and what you get when you draw cards. No, there is no easy way to stack the deck, so to speak, aside from graduating students into the best jobs possible.I fully recommend this game to:- People who enjoy randomization.- Those who enjoy having LOTS of options to balance in order to manage resources/get the best results.- Those who like pina coladas and getting caught in the rain.A few hints that might help starting off:1) Pause immediately upon starting the game, then go into your Headmaster's Office and click on the glowing green item on the desk. You can customize your options for the school there.2) Never choose students with Chatty, or the combination of Dumb and Deaf. Those will guarantee you have Peasants, and nobody wants Peasants.3) Until you get to a certain level in faction popularity, the factions WILL mess with you, which will cost you magic points, gold, or sometimes items. I recommend using banners to raise popularity without costing an arm and a legging.TL:DR - Fun game. Lots of randomness in events. LOTS of aspects to consider when managing school. Addictive. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: It is quite addictive management and optimizing game. However performance gets so abysmal, that there is no way I could recommend it. The game might (or might not) run decently on a fresh map, but after Steam's refund period has passed the game gets somewhat unresponsive and on low fps getting things done might take multiple clicks.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute very sweet makes you feel almost bad about teaching the students assassination techniques (just kidding, the cute atmosphere makes it even more fun!).
