_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun. It's both a mild puzzler and management sim with a LOT of depth. Having specific classrooms only able to be placed in specific parts is really neat and I think that that should be expanded upon, it'd make it more challenging and make the builds a bit more unique. There are a few problems, I have, that I hope get fixed as it moves forward, one being the option to only have 1 of 2 random professors per classroom without the option to fire or rehire. This leads to problems when it comes to needing specific alignments for class/professor cohesion as well as unionized employees. I know this too is a puzzler aspect but it's entirely unavoidable and not having the option to, say, only hire non-union employees when making a classroom is very linear. I'd like to see some cards carry over between zone endings, or the option too in one of the game modes, that'd be cool.

_childDocuments_.review: So I saw this game and really liked the trailer and also the gameplay that I saw, the concept really is great, the problem is that there is no depth for the game. I have done 5 maps in my campaign and have no idea how many more till I finish. The first map was cute, and the novelty of the concept made it fun, but at the second map, I realized I had to repeat the the same process, only a few clicks of difference (choose nature instead of light), by the third map of doing the same, I was starting to get bored. Different maps only have 1 new faction to interact and low challenges (students get more hungry, this does not feel to have any impact). I dont really feel any impact in the game besides creating rooms, over and over again, the students that graduate are only a 1% change in something, its not like you created a famous person that does something to the game. I feel sad because I loved the concept, but it's way too repetetive, I am on the 5th map and dont think I will care to finish

_childDocuments_.review: This game is half way to greatness, but it needs a lot more iteration and love yet. If you play it, don't feel afraid to put the speed slider up to 2x or more. It's easy to think you need to put a lot of attention into each decision you make, but it won't be worth it.My biggest complaint is that the game has a kind of split personality. Sometimes it feels like it's supposed to be a zen gardening game -- where you should just enjoy watching it, but then sometimes it encourages you to do very specific things, where your ability to do those things is almost entirely down to chance, or down to decisions made before you knew what your objectives were. You do have the ability to control the school's direction over a significant time period, but that is problematic since you often cannot know what resources you will need (either mana or types of items in your school).Nothing that's wrong with this game isn't fixable. My concrete suggestions would be:Make dialog events persist longer, and make sure the player has some time to react in game before the opportunities expire.Allow particular applicants to be accepted as "hero students", each of which can have their magical learning monitored more readily in the user interface. Perhaps prestige would determine the number of these students a player could have. These are the students a player would want to name, monitor their educational progression and take on adventures. Find a better way to resolve adventures than having your hero students killed. Maybe they need to recover in the infirmary for a significant amount of time or something. Ensure that the graduation event gives you one last chance to adventure with your students at the moment when their powers are greatest.Permit better design of the flow of traffic through the school. The only tool you have for this right now is where you put your cards when you set them down initially. This often leads to some very inefficient pathing. It's pretty hard to understand when inefficient pathing is really hampering you, and when you do understand it there still may not be anything you can do, unless your hand is full of dormitory, refectory, and staff lounge cards, and you can be sure it isn't. These are some of the hardest cards in the game to come by since they cost gold, which has so many other uses. I'd recommend making gold cards perhaps 50% cheaper but 50% less effective. The user could still choose to always double up the cards, but it would give more opportunities to do layout work and to ensure that it is easier to provide basic services (food, sleep, janitoral services (which should cost gold)) when expanding into new areas. Allow the creation of point to point portals so that you don't get areas of insane traffic right by the front door, which incidentally are detrimental to students trying to study.2/3 refectories on top of each other should become a great hall, obviously.Make a lot of small UI improvements.- When a quest requires multiple prereqs, show me whether I've already met each req.- When looking for a place to drop an accessory card, also show locations that already have accessory cards mounted. It is possible to replace existing accessories, but that requires you to first hunt down where those accessories are.- When looking for a place to drop accessories, make sure they aren't either a) too small to see or target at a wide zoom level and b) make sure they can't be hidden behind walls.- When playing a room card and there is an existing room of the type, make a fixed location on the screen that the card can be dragged to to upgrade the existing room. I can't remember where I put that room, and when I have a big castle I don't really want to go looking for it.Make thoughts more useful. They seem to be random flavor, but sometimes I very much want to know what a particular person is trying to do and why.Make more events! Lots more events!
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing little gem of a game! Your school starts off small and challenging, however as you get better and produce good students, these students go on to give you more bonuses to help with future scenarios in the campaign to help you get better and deal with the harder challenges later on. A great time sink which I loved sculpting my school to create different kinds of necromancers and druids. Do avoid this pitfall I fell into:Don't go heavy into customisation with a school of magic at the expense of other schools! You need a broad range of magics in your school to be the best and to take on the challenges. I focused far too much on shadow magic in the beginning not realising that I needed more than just a school of dark wizardsWould have liked the "wizard houses" to be a bit less RNG based as sometimes when I had planned my foundations of the school, the wizard houses (ie the group of learning you can assign your students to) didn't suit my classrooms and stunted my learning. The flip side was true when I selected the wizard houses first, the cards which were given to me didn't always suit my houses.You also have the chance to send a group of students into a dungeon for some fantastic rewards which were always extremely fun and rewarding. One of the best part of the game! However as they're so lucrative  you can count yourself  lucky if you get 1 per campaign level.All in all an amazing game, albeit a little too reliance on card RNG which could stunt the early start of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I might recommend it, but probably only during sale. The price compared with the playtime is too low in my opinion. I completed in my playtime the campaign twice and basically saw everything there is to see (not interested in sandbox mode). No more replay value.You build your own school for magic under always different circumstances, drawing from random cards of different decks. The impact of the different locations throughout the campaign is merely a visual change but the gameplay is the same every time. You start from zero (with some carryovers from the previous map) and end abruptly when Evil arrives, followed by scoring. Depending on your performance, the final mission is easier or more difficult.It is overwhelming in the beginning. However, when you find your strategy it is basically the same way to play each map. I found only the middle game quite enjoyable. The end gets quite chaotic and I did not feel I want to invest more time in each level when the Evil was close. Also, setting everything up in the beginning is annoying.I still had the urge to complete every level with three stars (not sure why, though. I guess I am a completionist) and I found the special missions and encounters relatively nice. As said above, it has enough content for two playthroughs of the campaign. It is possible to adjust the difficulty and add some extra modifiers to make the game harder. I would not buy it again at full price but at 40 – 50% discount it might be worth getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game that has enough challenge to keep you coming back. I wish some of the game play pieces were more user friendly though. Like the cards for components, rooms, etc. If you have more than like twelve, then it starts this annoying thing where you have to scroll thru all of the cards. Maybe just somehow make a 'x3' over the card so you can see the card but not *every* copy of the card. And maybe making a noise to indicate there is a void or fire might be nice. Those would be nice improvements, but not having them isn't stopping me from playing the game, so yeah.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: 3/10 feels like one of those wait to play building mobile games- its a luck and chance card game.......- drag and dropping everything is annoying- once the game is laggy cause you have 30 rooms/50 people dragging and dropping becomes a nightmare- very few popup events and in one game you run into the same one like 11 times

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun and kind of relaxing game with more depth than immediately meets the eye. Good for chilling out for hours.A bit repetitive once you get to 4th/5th map since you probably have learned all the game mechanics by then, with different objectives giving it slightly more challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and finished it once.  Just beware there are a decent amount of bugs still in this game.  Some of the card text contains strange code tokens in brackets.  What made me stop playing was game breaking pathing bugs where a teacher couldn't figure out how to get to his classroom.  It would have been nice to be able to load a previous save, but this is a rougelike so you can't do that.  I would still recommend, but watch out for these bugs!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun (if a bit repetitive after awhile) card/sim game.  I'm playing on a 2015 macbook pro and the game does hang every so often. (I tend to save after every card draw I'm really happy with just in case). The events are silly and multiple choice, often with choices unlocking only when you meet the requirements.  For me this is a great game to wind down with at the end of a day.Also of note is that the controls seem to be a bit sticky, I'll often have to pull a card toward the game area several times to get it to play. (If you have any trouble figuring out how to zoom in and out, its the scroll wheel or gesture, and arrows/movement keys will move the screen more precisely than moving the mouse to an edge)

_childDocuments_.review: I would give a good review if the price would be like 4 times less. The game looks promising, but it's basically level 1 repeated multiple times over and over again only with the different map which has 1 unique character on each map which really doesn't change anything. It is really boring when u have to basically repeat what you've done on level 1 over and over again to progress with the game. Like don't get me the wrong really nice and cool game, but definitely not worth the price. I was expecting much more from it, and regret I paid that much for such a short game. It would be better of to not try to make it long just for the sake to justify selling it as a more expensive. Feels like a scam a bit in that regard, not sure was it a conscious decision to scam people into a bigger price or did they really try to make a campaign out of it and just failed on executing that. Anyway, I do not recommend even the first 3/4hours were fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cute and fun. The person who says that you can't move the rooms, no, you can't, that's what it said in the tutorial so I'm not sure what they are complaining about? You have to think about the placement of the rooms so you can add add much as possible. You have to think about what your school needs, and yes, it is random because its a card draw game, its not a sim. It takes a while to build your school up, but there's a fast forward button so you can skip the waiting periods. The cards you draw and the choices you make with the encounters make a difference what happens to your school or the community. Yes, it's random, but that's the point. You have to deal with the cards handed to you, literally, or you can just sell the cards. Every student and teacher has positive and negative traits. You can pick up any of the items and animals you place in the rooms, so its not "random" and you can put them in the appropriate room as you add on. You can also send some of your students to fight in a dungeon together, which I think is pretty cool. For brand new game, this one has a lot in it, and I'm sure there will be even more features in the future.Edit: after getting a perfect game, I just want to say, winning difficult mode is the most emotionally challenging thing I have done in a long time. I did not deserve that mistreatment.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, no two games are the same.  Lots of juggling issues, and FUN interesting surprises as well. Only be careful how fast you are clicking on people to put in your schools... I got a bit carried away toward the very end of my first TIER and the character cards got really small and I couldn't read them well enough to figure out where I was placing them.  Glitch I will report, just letting you know.  Otherwise, the game runs great and had no problems or FPS issues, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game the day it released, so bear that in mind while reading.I think it still needs a lot of work but so far I have enjoyed it. Building up your own little Hogwarts is pretty fun. I'll go over a few problems I ran into and then I'll finish on the good points:I did feel like there were a couple of translation issues. It seems like everyone is referred to as a 'he' at the moment. Also when transferring students between 'Houses' the popup windows were in French. There is not a lot to read so I could figure it out but there you go. The tooltips display outside of the page sometimes near the borders of the screen. Which means obviously; you can't read them. This was quite frustrating as I couldn't read any of the info for the heatmaps on the right hand side.I feel like the tutorial needs a bit of work. It is very short.I couldn't find out how to delete rooms I'd already built.Although the card-system is an interesting mechanic, that I did enjoy. I do feel like their should be some basic rooms you can choose from all the time, like corridors, dorms, kitchens, halls... ect.. without having to randomly roll time and time again. Although I do think it works for the more specialised rooms, like classrooms in the different magical disciplines. But that's just my opinion.One of my little dragons got stuck on the right hand side of the playable area and couldn't path his way round. Might be worth implementing a way for him to 'ghost' through a wall if he's stuck for too long.But that's all my complaints so far, onto the good stuff:It is fun if you like builder/tycoon/sim games. The card system kind of forces you to build in a way you wouldn't do normally, which gives a unique feel to each run.You get to name the school and the various houses!! Yay! The art-style is very good and I really enjoyed watching the students and teachers going about their little lives interacting with each-other. I even enjoyed just watching the student and the dragon wandering around at the main menu for a while. The interactions with the other factions and people was interesting, I liked the quests that I was given, I've not progressed far enough to see the final result of my efforts but time will tell. I liked the fact that your students graduating into good jobs gives buffs for the school and I really liked the overall game-play. It was fun!Overall I recommend this game. I feel like after the developer irons out a few of the bugs it's going to get a lot better. I feel like in it's current state it's still worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really fun little simulator. I liked the independence of the style - it's not HP the school-mgmt sim. The UI has some slight odd bits, but generally works quite well.The most annoying part, I would say, is the auto-saving. When you place a building, if there's no Teacher to recruit, it automatically places and saves. There is no "undo". If there IS a teacher to recruit, you automatically get stuck in the recruitment screen, with whatever two choices you randomly drew.Requests/Suggestions:0) DLC1) Please allow disabling auto-save2) Please make recruiting the teacher a second step3) Policies for teachers (like there are for the students) would be nice4) The teach attributes are clearly just a handful of prebuilt cards. It would be interesting if the teacher traits were actually random5) It would be cool if the factions on the map were either: random, selectable, or if they had to be staffed from your teacher pool6) Being able to design logos, names, and schools, ahead of time, and select those when starting, would be cool7) I realize that it reduces the randomness, but it would be convenient to select goals before startingThere seem to be a few "bugs", as well:0) Teachers don't seem to ever die in combat, even at 0 health1) The 'escape' key never closes any dialogues2) The UI makes it extremely unclear what the placement requirements of cards are3) When drawing a card, there is no way to see what slots you have available4) There is no way to see what slots placed buildings have5) Many of the status popups on students and teachers are baffling, and there doesn't seem to be any way to check what the status is. Why do the students sometimes have a "book" thought-bubble above them? What does that mean?
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, a lot. You can tell by how much I have played it. (Although some of that time is me forgetting to shut down the game a few times.) And its really fun and addicting and has a really cool style. But, and I am sure you could feel the but, its not perfect. I feel like the replay mechanic can be a bit tedious and for as much as I have played I have not "beat" the game. Or gotten all the achievements. The end section is just much to hard and almost relies on you getting perfect rounds the whole game. Despite this minor frustration (im sure ill beat it someday) its a lovely game and I like the majority of people who get it will like it. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing really outstanding here but it's a nice calm, relaxing timesink. It's fun to mess around and play with the different magic specialties and see where the RNG takes you. I agree with some of the other reviews that there are definitely some quality of life things needed. Being able to move buildings, furnishings, etc would be a godsend. Also the biggest thing I would love is to see some kind of student and staff chart to track everyone's current condition/traits/etc. Having to click through every one is a bit of a pain.But, overall, I sunk six hours into it over four matches and it was a nice relaxing session. If you can get it for $10 or under, I recommend doing so!

_childDocuments_.review: An easy going game in which you start with a plot of land in various locations, each with their own modifiers and mini-quests. Arrange the rooms of your universities, choose what your houses will specialize in and allocate students to them, and take your star performers on occasional outings to the local dungeons. Not incredibly deep in any of the described mechanics, but a lot of chilled fun to be had here.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This is not merely a casual game, it's the most casual thing since the office didn't bother announcing casual Fridays since no one even bothered to show up on Fridays.You'll sit around and watch your little students wander about. You'll have the opportunity to make a few choices here and there, not often, and mostly small and subtle things. This isn't StarCraft. After an hour or so your school will be attacked by an Evil Dude and the level will end, forcing you to move on to found a new school and start over again. Everything is very small, very slow, and low stakes.You do influence things and shift the school into the direction that you would like, but between extremely random card draws and events it's less like flying a plane and more like steering a glider. Some reviews are complaining about lack of agency, but you'll note most of those people didn't play very long. Understandable, since it's a slow paced game and some won't want to invest to figure it out. When you figure things out you'll start being able to control the game much better.This might not be what you are looking for. Something calm, relaxing, and whimsical. I didn't even know this was what I was looking for. But it was. I'm glad I found it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed this title quite a lot. You'll manage a university for magical education, building out your curriculum by placing rooms one by one, hiring professors, admitting students, managing your relationship with the locals, sending plucky pupils on perilous adventures for plunder, etc. It feels like it's meant to capture the fantasy mood of Harry Potter or the Earthsea books.It's adorably animated, with a distinct cartoon-y style and plenty of clever flourishes. It's definitely worth zooming in to watch individual characters go about their goofy days.The game doesn't feel complete yet - which I think of as a good thing in this case. New content updates sprinkle in now and then, which is lovely. There's a lot of room for the game to grow. For example, there's a "House" mechanic that allows you to control what certain students study, giving them selected bonuses, etc. A clever headmaster can train an elite group of students to be the school's "Mystery Gang" and go raid dungeons. However, I think there is an obvious content gap in intramural competition between the houses - the recent addition of a tournament grounds makes me anticipate a Quidditch analogue forthcoming...Who knows. In any case, it's a great little game and I hope it continues to grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. Build your own university, pick a magic art to specialize in, defeat the evil- but every time you play you can pick a different map to play on with different obstacles for your university to overcome. Plenty of replay opportunities here!  Want to befriend evil? Go for it, see what happens! The art style is good, simple, and goes well with the type of game. Almost like the old 'sim tower' game, but moves quicker and with a magical spin to it. Absolutely recommend this game if you are considering it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game!I've been testing it since I received my key with their Kickstarter. The game has evolved a lot since then and the developers are very attentive to the feedback from the players.It is a management game in which you run a magic school to train students and offer them a job for the future. Unfortunately, the evil lord is chasing us from level to level to destroy the schools of magic. The campaign is very exciting with bonuses and maluses that cumulate over the levels to reach a final level, with a super cool school site ;)The game is original because it is played with playing cards to develop the schools. Mana is needed to draw cards related to different magics and this mana is produced when a student is working. Like any self-respecting management game, there are many ways to manage your school and be specialized. So you can easily redo a game, and play it in a very different way.At first, the game is a little complicated to understand, especially without a tutorial. But you just have to adjust the difficulty to learn all the tricks.There are still some adjustments to be made and bugs to be corrected, but the game has already won me over.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a fun game, still has a lot of potential in it.  7/10 - Worth playing.Things that I think would make it better:  * Actual difficulty (Even on Archmage, Short, Speed Curse - it was basically no struggle to win the campaign)  * Better UI for placement - Highlighting and placing artifacts/animals can be atrocious at times.  It can be incredibly hard to see the white outlines, and sometimes they're blocked by the people in the room so you can't place them very easily.  * What does the number in the shield for the futures even mean!? What are your secrets!?  * (Personal Opinion) - I'd like if the futures that weren't discovered at least hinted at what the prerequisites for them might be.  Discovery is fun, but there's so many permutations of schools + races + traits that trying to randomly come across stuff can be an exercise in frustration instead of fun.  * Less crashes.  I've soft-locked three or four times when I've clicked on the "Incoming Students" notification _just_ as it was expiring.  The window never appears, but the game thinks it's up - so you can't actually do anything else since.  * Ability to demolish (or at least move) rooms.    * Better/more pronounced labeling for rooms in terms of entrances/connections/unable-to-build-overs.

I hope the devs keep adding content sporadically and updating it.Only a few things missing that would make this game perfect:more opportunities to go to dungeons!unlockable card progressionmaybe a game mode that lets you make your own decks from cards you unlock so I don't keep getting the room card six time in a row instead of a cards I need to complete the area quests.room destruction!! or the ability to move rooms at a cost if you place one by mistake.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun. From what I've played, it may as well be a full release (provided there's no nasty surprises at the end). There's some simplicity in combat and there's less freedom because of the card drawing, but it's still a game involving some level of strategy. Figuring out when to use the cards takes a bit, but I've really enjoyed this beyond what I expected to.===Update===I opened the game back up for the update. Honestly, it's a solid game. However, there are a few caveats:-The game sometimes loads unresponsive to the keyboard. It will allow text input, but not recognize other key presses. It is unclear why this happens, but it occurs more often than not.-At least one bug has resurfaced that was previously fixed with this update.-By design, it's not possible to move, remove, or replace rooms once they are placed.-By design, it is sometimes impossible (or close to it) to complete objectives depending on the cards you are dealt.That said, I really love the game overall. I want more. I just finished all the achievements, and I want more. I want more events, more dungeons, more control, more modes. It's a really fun base. If they don't continue updating this game, then I at least want to see a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - It's a fun and good little game - but still missing some functionality and occasionally freezes.  Feels a bit like it's still in early access.  Given this, not sure it's worth the price they're asking for it now.The longer review:Pros:~ Genuinely a fun little game, low learning curve to get the basics but you can go full-on sperg-lord and micro manage LOTS of stuff if you want to (or ignore it if you don't)~ The dungeon mini card game is also fun and feels rewarding~ Some of the little graphical touches they add are hilarious (kids with pumpkin heads, etc.)~ The soundtrack hits that "goldilocks" spot for me - it's fun to listen to if you actually pay attention to it but can fade into the background and not be distracting or annoyingCons:~ You can't delete / destroy rooms once placed.  This will hurt HARD the first map or two you play since you're inevitably going to screw up the placement of a room and block yourself off.~ The tutorial is VERY surface...I had more questions at the end of it then when I started.  It would be nice if they had a tutorial map with simplified goals and room placement so you can get a feel for it before you have to face down the dark lord doom timer.~ There are unrecoverable game freezes.  In the middle of my second map the game froze.   At least there's an auto-save feature now so that you don't lose much progress, but it's still annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This is a prize gem of a game.   Those folks posting negative reviews either gave up too quickly or it didn't fit their preconceived expectations.   After playing several starts and doing a play through I've found this to be an awesome game.Like the description, you're in charge of the development of a Magic school in different settings.   Your choice of which magic lines to follow is critical and you learn which things to buy or to emplace that enhances your magic choices and the strategy side takes off.    You also have to deal with folks like the Orcs or the Inquistion, the king, etc and the choices you make really impacts how the game plays.   Translated that's 'tons of replayability'.  From time to time you can finance a dungeon discovery and the game morphs into a tactical dungeon crawler where you pick 4 students and nursemaid them through it.   The treasures you win as you progress can be used to enhance the school when you decide to leave it and come back.   Translated that's 'a tactical dungeon crawler'.There's a big baddie always closing on your schools location so time pressure is a thing.   You can ask the king and others to attack it to give you more time but it puts an edge on your strategy.  The better your school is developed the higher ranking your students will have at the end.  From placing flying dragons around your school to putting up banners/items here and there to enhance certain rooms everything you do impacts the students progress.   Translated that's 'a strategic view'.I could go on and on, as I said I'm just discovering how great this game is.   Perhaps the best praise I can give it is that it's put my World of Warcraft addiction on hold.   Really can't recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my go-to games to chill out with. You earn cards which let you place new rooms in your school, decorate those rooms with artifacts and trinkets, and buff your students and teachers. As students graduate from your school you are told what their future profession is based on how well you educated them, and you are given rewards based on how impressive they are. It's important to mention the game is a roguelike - after a certain amount of time the armies of the evil lord attack and you have to flee and create a new academy somewhere else with some new buffs and curses. [+] The game is made with lots of love - watching your students run around using facilities is fun. As you place items you can see them hanging on the walls, or pets wandering around the halls. Upgrading a classroom also upgrades how it looks visually.[+] Tonnes of room types, trinkets and artifacts, random events, mini-games like dungeons, alchemy and other factions to improve relations with. Lots of the dialogue is genuinely funny as well.[+] There's no real way to lose the game, but it's genuinely quite challenging to graduate top-level students.[~] It can be a little slow so I when I set up a game I select the Longest game option and play it solely in 3x speed. This ensures events happen quickly and there's not much waiting.[-] There really needs to be some way of moving or deleting rooms you've placed, even if it's just a rare event/card. It's frustrating to make a design mistake or even a misclick and having zero ways of remedying it. [-] It can take ages to find a particular card you need[-] I have no idea why you can build rooms in some places but not others[-] The dungeons are really interesting but also half-baked. Students might know many spells but can only select one and then it can't be changed for the whole dungeon. You might enter a fight with an incredibly powerful enemy you have no way of beating and there's no way to flee.

_childDocuments_.review: Just clocked 14.5 hours this weekend. This game is not as random as some reviewers are making it sound. I'm going to write this review as a spoiler-free walkthrough/guide so you can understand some of the complaints.When you start the game, you begin building immediately with minimal help from the tutorial. My partner is the type of person who plays video games with YouTube guides and gamefaqs-style websites on his lap. He will not play through a game unless he knows everything upfront.  I'm the type of person who tosses guides and manuals away, jumps right in, and figures it out as I go. Once I get a feel for the game, then I go back and look up some guides and tutorials. The game is about how much you can achieve before your school evacuates. When you get evacuated, you unlock new locations. If you complete your goals by end game, you also receive bonuses to use with your next school. Within the first few minutes of game play, you are prompted with questions about what your school is about. Is it Arcane? Light magic? Do you want to heal animals? Perhaps practice necromancy? Will you produce the next "Arcmage"? Your selections determine your three goals to achieve by endgame. They show up as stars on the right hand corner, above your gold and mana. You can hover over them if you forget what they were.  Some are good, some are bad. When you create "houses" for your students, you assign two traits to each other. For example, House 1 can be "beautiful" and "Worker" while House 2 is "Child of Light" and "Steadfast." When you get an application where someone is "Worker" and "Child of Shadow", you might assign them to House 1. I won't spoil much more here. There are events that happen very frequently where you have the opportunity to build relationships with other factions. TAKE TIME TO READ WHAT THEY'RE ABOUT. For example, the Royal King, if you build your relationship with him, will allow you to charge 20 gold for admission for your students. If your RNG for cards is awful and you spent all your gold, you can strategically decide to spend the next several guinea pig events to build your relationship with the Royal King. Read through the other factions as you play to learn how your relationship with them can be beneficial or detrimental. (Sometimes your relationship with one faction will sour your relationship with another).  I'm not 110% sure how these are triggered. I've only had the opportunity to do one dungeon per playthrough. They're brutal and I've killed a lot of my NPC's in them... though in my last playthrough, I got to level 35. I'll leave you with this hint: there are classes you can teach to your students that make them incredible in the dungeon... You don't need your students to be good at everything (if you're going for archmage, you just need them to be good at 4/5 of the types of magic). However, you want to give your students a great learning environment because when they graduate, you get bonuses! Sometimes it's money, prestige, mana, bonuses such as "more applicants," a random dragon pet, etc. If your students keep graduating as peasants, you need to reconsider how you've built your school and what applications you are accepting. (Peasants are normal the first few rounds of graduations but they should phase out by year 5 for sure). You can "reroll" their job ONCE PER STUDENT. Look at the percentages in the corner to see the chances (death is one of them, but usually a low change). . OKAY SO I DIDN'T KNOW THIS GETTING INTO THE GAME - Let's say you already have a Dormitory and you draw another Dormitory. You don't have to place a second dormitory (unless you want to). YOU CAN OVERLAY THE OLD ONE WITH THE NEW ONE AND YOU GET AN UPGRADED DORMITORY. I had no idea I could do this. Anyway, you also get pets, weapons, decor, etc. to outfit each room. The pets move (except obvious ones that can't like a fish in a fishbowl) from their room to other rooms so don't stress about where you place them. I also placed the decor in random places because I'm not trying to manage that hard."You can't move the rooms around!"- You don't have to... It's the least of your worries! Your students will find them, relax."Prestige is too random!"- No, you can earn prestige from your relationships and events (or lose them) but your prestige is mainly based on the jobs your graduates take on. Peasants are -1, while something like Arcmage is 5."It's the same thing over and over."- These people aren't reading any of the text and are just clicking and placing as if they're playing The Sims 3. Of course they're gonna feel it's repetitive. There's several dungeons, different locations to build in after your last school gets evacuated, spellbooks to start new schools with, hexes, even different races of students and combination of courses you'll offer! My first school was a bunch of necromancers. My second was a bunch of nature magicians turned midwives. My last school, I just went nuts and produced a little bit of everything but primarily paladins (per my endgame goal).  I play DnD and Pathfinder 3x a week so I know a thing or two about getting screwed over by RNG. The problem is that the devs do not give you much information about the game going into it. I can compare starting out to Cultist Simulator or Slay the Spire where I'm like "huh... let me just click this and see what happens..." Cultist Simulator players love to tell people, "READ THE DAMN CARD" and I must tell you that this rule applies to Spellcaster University. READ EVERYTHING THAT POPS UP, especially if it "feels random."I play this game as a "palette cleanser" when I'm trying to chill. It's intense enough that I can't watch something in the background as I'm playing but it's chill enough that I don't throw my keyboard.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with enough variety to keep it interesting.  There is a technical issue which needs resolved, where if you do not place a card in the exact location it will get stuck where you left it and the game will appear frozen; grabbing the card again (if you can find it) to place it again resumes the game, however, so it is still playable with this issue.  Overall I love the theme, options for customization, variety of quests and adventures, and many hidden futures to find for students.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an enjoyable game... when it doesn't repeatedly CTD.  I've gotten to the point of my campaign that I can't play for more than four minutes straight before my game crashes.  For the price this game is currently going for, I can't recommend this game just yet.  If you're interested in this game, then I recommend waiting a couple months and revisiting the steam reviews to see if the game has resolved enough bugs to make it less CTD prone.UPDATE (Oct 12, 2019): Update 0.82 was just released  and was supposed to take care of a bug causing teachers to get stuck between rooms, but I still see that problem on my game. More troubling, the game's still crashing after a few minutes. Clearly, the devs need to do more work.UPDATE (November 1, 2019): I downloaded Update 0.83 yesterday, and I was able to play for a couple more hours before I hit another CTD wall.  I probably won't update this review until the game becomes more stable.

_childDocuments_.review: A light base-building/management game with strong rogue-like elements.This is a tough game to rate, because I like the concept but it just didn't feel like it was executed well. Basically you build a school of magic by drawing cards from several decks, in an attempt to train as many students as you can before the generic evil entity destroys your school. The careers (or "futures") your students get imparts bonuses that can be used on the next school you build.I think my big issue with the game is the randomness and lack of stuff to do late game. One round isn't very long, maybe 1-2 hours. After about 30 mins or so I would routinely draw only cards I didn't want, or couldn't use. And the randomness element was so pervasive, it felt like i could only mildly direct the school or students to my required objective and hope they did I wanted. There was a dungeon element that I really enjoyed, but it was rarely useful to actually explore the dungeons and didn't trigger often enough to break up game play. The endgame also tended to have MASSIVE performance issues. I understand tracking 70+ students can be taxing for some computes, but if I can run Cyberpunk just fine, this game shouldn't be struggling to hit 25 FPS
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Go find Mind over Magic. It's everything I wanted Spellcaster University to be.I love this game, I really do, which is why having this opinion of it is so painful.The first two or three runs are great. You're discovering new mechanics, fiddling to make the best university you can, grappling with the objectives and the relation system, and watching your students murder each other. That's kinda where it ends. The game is based on a deck and currency system. Things you do in the game give you currency, currency lets you buy cards at increasingly steep prices, rinse repeat, swish and spit. The problem is that that is where it ends. You pay your money, choose one of three cards, wait for currencies to grow again, and wait to die.You have a hand, full of cards. This is entirely a crutch used by the game to avoid having to put any actual effort into the interface. They could have split the bottom bar up into eight segments: One for each deck's rooms, at quick access, one for all the ornamental items, and a final one for potions (which desperately need the face lift, as I have to scroll through my whole bar to find the last ingredient, and clicking on the recipe in the interface does nothing). Instead, the cards appear in the order you get them, don't stack (despite there being literally no distinction between copies of the same card) and once you fill your bar, start to pile up at either end of the bar and awkwardly interfere with each other when piled up that way. Have a choice between three cards you don't need? Well, you gotta pick one, then either use it anyway, or sacrifice it for a pitiful amount of mana (or gold) in the hopes the next draw will give you literally anything useful. My only positive remark is that you won't get multiple copies of the same card in a draw. In the end, this sings more to artificial rng difficulty than rewarding players for being flexible. Which makes sense, because this game rewards you for being as lazy and straightforward as possible.Onto the deck mechanics. There aren't any. The 'deck' is just a thinly veiled shell for a dice roller that gives you three random cards. In some locations, you get extra cards. If you complete challenges, you gain extra room adornments. I have yet to bother with the latter, for how tedious it seems it'll be.Onto school building. I'm going to start by praising two things: the art style is beautifully immersive for everything that's not alive, and the rooms give you some difficulty in laying them out, since some have only side doors, others have only stairwells, and a scant few don't let you build on the tile immediately above them. This is where my praise ends. There are five (I think) rooms for every discipline. The general education room that teaches all three styles, three style specific rooms, and a single utility room. Outside of those and basic structural stuff like dorms, lunch rooms, so on, you get nothing. The only dynamic you have with rooms is that you can use another card of a room to improve that room. This gives it an extra level, allowing you to spend that point either for a bit of extra efficiency (by default), or in some rooms, reallocating one or more points to produce a special effect. The greenhouse being able to produce either unicorn horns or the mandrake root for one point to each comes to mind. At first I was ecstatic about this mechanic, until I realized that it was the only one to be had. I hope that one day they'll add the ability to combine multiple room types into a single one, but the way the game is gives me no hope.Students. Unless you have a specific objective that you want students to work toward, houses are entirely useless. They're useless most of the time anyway, unless you get lucky with a futures objective that only has a single discipline's magic required. Otherwise, your best use would either be to give students talented in one discipline a focused education in it, or to prevent students with, say, the Goth trait (learns light magic 50% slower) from even bothering to show up to those courses. They have no autonomy, they have barely any initiative. They just do whatever their house says they should and leave it at that. At some point you realize it's also better to just get as many students into your school as possible than to actually give them a quality education. Tying back into the school building thing, I'm 90% sure it's better to make multiple rooms of the same type, than to bother upgrading the same one. Spread them out as much as possible so that your students are always within a few tiles of their needs and next course. Unless you're desperate to save that gold the extra teachers will cost you, there's no reason not to.The only fun part of the game is expeditions, which is dampened slightly by the fact you have almost zero control over them, and they have an even worse card system than the main game, somehow, because it's actually an item system pretending to be cards. There is no penalty to losing all your students (aside from losing your students, which are cheap to replace) so just drive them until they die and reap all those rewards. Basically you set your line up, choose their spells, and throw them at encounters until they either die or you call it off. But there's a good attempt at story in this, so I forgive that. What I don't forgive is that you have to go through the other parts of the game to get a student worth putting in an expedition. And the teaching kinda sucks.Story's alright, thumbs up from me. Pretty bland, plus befriending the dark lord doesn't really stop him from murdering your school every other week. Actually, dark magic is pretty much useless top to bottom. There aren't any objectives that need you to collect enough mana to get that star (as far as I've seen) and the only time it's ever worth building their classrooms is if you either have a specific expedition lineup you want (good luck) or your futures objective gave you no options that don't have dark mana. Basically, avoid whenever possible.What I think would make this game tolerable: Firstly, add actual card mechanics. Have rooms give you access to the decks to stack them in your favor (in various ways, I wouldn't lock the rooms to their specific deck, for example). Cut the 'increasing costs' ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and instead have the cards actually enter and exit the deck through your actions. Make it possible to sacrifice basic room cards to add specialized rooms to the deck. Make it possible to combine room cards in exchange for stronger rooms with unique effects being added to the deck (rather than the hand) at some cost. Make potions more useful than 'gain x of a mana resource (or gold) or get one of four marginally useful concoctions - I can't share any ideas for this. Most importantly, have ways to actually set back the dark lord's progress - if you do anything to slow him down as is, he just speeds up over time and undoes the damage faster and faster. This is good, since it prevents complete slowrolling by abusing the king for infinite time, but also means that these mechanics are lame delay tactics instead of being a proper recurring objective. Above all else, I don't mind that the gameplay loop is 'build school five times, then complete quests to win' but as it stands that exists purely so you can get enough contacts to have access to the alternative options in each step of the victory quests, when in theory you could take the fight to the dark lord with your very first school, and probably win. Having mechanics that actually pit you and your students against the big army that's trying to wreck your ♥♥♥♥ would be nice.tl;dr 4/10 tons of great ideas and creativity, not a single one executed to satisfaction. Barely satisfying altogether. I weep.

_childDocuments_.review: Consider this review 55% positive.This game is light, casual fun and very charming, but it feels incomplete. The game hints at the importance of synergy between teachers, students, and rooms, but the reality is you're going to want to build everything to ensure you're generating resources for each school of magic, as some crucial rooms are school specific, and to placate all factions. The game plays the same every time: you will build absolutely everything, and after a set period of time the game "ends" because an evil overlord automatically destroys your school, and then you do it again with a few more unlocks. The joy of the game consists largely of watching things unfurl around the school, and the animations are delightful. But there's not a lot of GAME here.  Dungeon explorations are few and far between, and not being able to at least TRY and fight the dark lord with your army of students feels like a missed opportunity to evoke some Harry Potter vs Voldemort wish fulfillment. Also, the lack of viable specialist paths reduces some of the appeal for strategy players that like a challenge.Then again, the developer is a five person game studio. Their company web page is static, but they are active on Facebook, so there's a chance more content is coming, if not right away. $24.99 is a steep price for what is presently available, but this game is worth a look at a substantial discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun little strategy base builder. You get stuff by buying one of 6 card packs, giving you a choice of three cards relating to the pack type (generic, nature, light, dark, arcane, alchemy). You build up your university, helping or pissing off the local factions, training gradually better students until, at some point, the university gets destroyed by the Dark Lord (Chris), so you pick up, move on, rinse and repeat - this time with whatever permanent bonuses your alumni gave you, a spell book which gives you a permanent bonus, with power varying on how many objectives you completed (again, a choice of three), and a curse from the DL (which you get to pick, once more from a choice of three, pretty polite of Him if you ask me).That's the basic gist of it, some specific things I liked were:Semi-random card system means you get a game where you experiment instead of just finding one reliable meta-strat and sticking with it, so that in one game your university might churn out a load of nature loving priests, and the next may churn out a load of evil devil worshipping alchemists.The objectives also add into this experimentation, since they're also semi-random you may well end up switching focuses halfway through to make sure you get a truly game-changing spell book. I've had at least two games where my starting cards got me focused on one school of magic, and the objectives caused me to really hone in on one or two others to get those sweet sweet tomes.Rooms have varying sizes and entrance points, and often benefit from adjacency to other rooms (generally not in an "X room makes Y room(s) more efficient" way, but in a "shorter walks between lunch, class, and dormitories means students spend more time learning and less time commuting" way. It means that you may well have a room you want to place now, but decide to hold off for a bit so you can give it a good location. Just a nice bit of weighing up benefits.There are some downsides, though generally not stemming from the basic mechanics.The game is pretty poorly optimised, my PC which can run stuff like Bannerlord, Detroit: Become Human, Cities: Skylines etc. on mid-high graphics at a general 30-60 fps struggles to reach 20 fps after the first 10-30 minutes of each game even with low graphics and lower than 1920x1080 resolution. Even worse on my laptop, where I've had to halve the resolution and keep the graphics low to reach a reliable 20fps.The UI can be a bit clunky, and could do with some more tooltips. When you have more cards than can fit at the base of the screen you have to manually click a small button at the base of the screen to scroll along one card, and moving your cursor there generally pops up a card which gets in the way of the button. Once you activate the screens to accept new students/staff or choose a new card there's no way to cancel out of the screen to check which would be most useful to you,  meaning you have to rely entirely on memory, which isn't impossible but is somewhat inconvenient/annoying.Overall though, I'd say it's a pretty fun game. The shortcomings are mostly annoyances rather than dealbreakers. As it stands I'd probably say to wait for a sale, but if it sounds good to you it's far from the worst thing you could do with the money.

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT THE GAME IS/ISN'TThis is not really a management game as tagged. There are some management aspects but if you are like me, you are probably expecting to build, customize and manage you own little University. That's not going to happen.The game is CARD based. You can only build with the cards that are given to you. But wait, this is NOT a deckbuilder either. You know how you can choose your basic deck in many deckbuilding games and as you progress, you get to pick and choose cards you want to be added / discarded? That's not how it works. As others have brought up, the RNG could get really annoying but it's not "Darkest Dungeon I want to smash my head against the wall" level of RNG.POSITIVESThe game itself is actually pretty good on its own. It's very addictive and charming. I strongly recommend anyone to watch some gameplay first before purchasing because this game is a bit unique. NEGATIVESIt crashes for me. Sometimes I start a new campaign and it loaded to 100% on the loading screen but it won't actually proceed. I can hear my laptop struggling quite a bit and feel the heat. I don't think it's a minimal requirements problem because my machine while not that cutting edge, is way beyond what is recommended. I can deal with restarting the game every now and then when it crashes. So, it doesn't bother me much. You might want to test it out when you buy it.PRICEWorth it when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:- Meh gameplay, play the first run and you've played the game- Houses are cool, if ultimately lackluster- good visuals and animations, very cute- get on a discountHonestly, I got this game and was expecting more. I mean that in terms of gameplay, as most of it is deciding which student go into which houses or which faction(s) you build relationships with. Neither of which will matter later on in your first university as everything gets easier. You draw cards based on mana specific to the magic you want - or money for general rooms and other things - which can give you pets, rooms and items (I think that's all of them) which can also effect things in your university. You also get text based popup events and sometimes your school can be attacked (I played carefully to avoid that, so I don't know much about it). Other than making your School Crest and Student Houses, that's about the extent of the gameplay.I say first university bc there's a timer at the top of the screen, and when times up, the Lord of Evil will come and destroy your school. You don't get a chance to defend yourself, and as I'm aware reading the other reviews, you never do as you build more universities and start over and over again. At the end of my first run, they let me choose a curse and a spell book which effected my states, but so do graduated students who give you a tiny perma buff each.I really wanted more out of the school houses. It's a lot of fun making their crest, deciding their specialties, choosing which students go into what house and watching them graduate. There's too many to get close with any of them, but it was still pretty neat. What I wanted was more gameplay. There's an option in your rules book that lets the houses compete with each other each year, but outside of toggling a checkbox and a change in student behavior you don't see it. If you played the game without making a single custom house, nothing would change.This isn't a bad game, it's just disappointing. Maybe I'll come back to it sometime. It's like magic school fallout shelter, which just means it's a time grinder past the first school. The animations are great, everything's really cute. Music isn't anything to write home about. I got it on a discount and I'd recommend others do as well if they want to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay itself is good and recommendable. There's some polish issues to be addressed, especially when it comes to poorly explained elements, badly structured English, and UI shortcomings, but the gameplay itself is good enough to readily make this a "Recommended" despite those issues.Or it would be, if the game wasn't a complete disaster of terrible optimization, game bugs, and game crashes. Those are all bad enough to make it a Not Recommended- except, thankfully, the game does have auto-saving. Thus far I haven't had any bugs persist through a relaunch and game load, and several even fix just by going into the menu and back into the save, so the existence of auto-saving marginalizes the stresses of the game to the point where it's readily back up to being "Recommended". I do have concern over what'd happen if a save file does ever end up retaining a game-breaking issue, so I can't guarantee the game won't ever lose you hours or tens of hours of effort, but thus far none of the stresses have been persistent enough to fully undermine the recommendability of the game.As far as the gameplay itself, it's pretty much what you'd expect based on the previews. Place rooms, manage students. While woefully incomplete for any specific (eg, event result, confusing card text) clarifications, there's still enough fan information online to help work through general gameplay questions or strategies. With that as a supplement, the gameplay's pretty smooth and relaxing and enjoyable, creating a good "just a bit more" vibe.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! Played it a ton, but there are a lot of factors to consider that may dissuade others from purchasing it today. Pointers I really liked about Spellcaster Uni: 1. The ability to choose the classes, the curriculum, and that almost everything pertaining to your school is customize-able.2. Your choices have consequences. I've always loved choice based games, and better yet their repercussions. Something has to give and nothing's perfect. To support one faction that may anger another is a great way to keep you on your toes and decide your fate carefully. This works especially well with the biome you chose for your school. There may be a certain race that inhabits the area, and a special event or entity that you may choose to either build a relationship with, or be independent.3. Rng items every event or action. Much like a dungeon crawler the game will let you choose 1 of 3 random items to better help you maintain your school. 4. A small turned based dungeon run. I thought this was a fun little quest to do. It's like a small little minigame, and it's endless. Kind of run till you drop, and the rewards are well worth it. However it's sad that you can only do 1 per playthrough. Pointers I didn't like about Spellcaster Uni: 1. A playthrough is way too short! I feel that architect management games shouldn't wipe so quickly. You work so hard to build a school from the ground up and then your progress is lost at the end of the run. 2. Each run is repetitive. Although you may choose a different biome to place your school, the story is linear and really doesn't change. Same old grind, but with 1 variable (the event or entity that inhabits the biome).3. Nothing you do in your playthrough will prepare, or prevent the final outcome of the game. This is an extension of the first pointer of not liking the game, but I feel it was an important one that I should address. I wont go into detail as I dont want to spoil the game for anyone who may want to purchase the game.4. Progress is nonexistent. When your students graduate they usually increase the school's reputation and learning ability, but because the final outcome will never change there's no point or added benefits. 5. The little minigame I talked about earlier is a pretty neat thing. But some of the choices have bs hidden consequences. Like if you decide to do a harmless action, you fight an enemy that is on par with a boss. I still thought it was fun, but I had to scratch my head at some of the choices. 6. The attributes of the teachers and students have no logical synergy. Now I admire the fact that the ai has their own "personalities", but it doesn't really make sense, other than the fact that you're just labeling them, and that slims the chances of the students learning or the teacher's teaching abilities. They don't do anything else. I thought it was pretty stupid that I had a chaotic teacher who teaches more efficiently to chaotic students, but the students I was getting in the rng pool were the polar opposite. It either made most of the students in one subject not really understanding the course, or not enough students in the course. It's just a hurdle that doesn't make sense at all while you're crunching for time. Again, I really enjoyed the game and their polished, simple mechanics. But it gets boring after a while just due to having a small window of time to play in, and it's just the same old story. WIthin that respect, I can't recommend this game. Or at least not at the same price since release! $25 USD is outrageous. I had purchased the game at full price upon release since it had great potential, and I was sad to find out that the devs haven't lowered the price since I think the game still is a unique experience.. If I had to put a price tag on it, I would say the game should be $9 USD.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an ok magical school management sim with some interesting twists.1 campaign complete on all standard settings (~22 hrs)Bad stuff first:- Font size... absolutely tiny. If you have any problem with small fonts do not play this game.- The room tetris mechanic is wholly uninteresting. Is it somewhat important? Sure, but because it is very obscured how the students are affected by it, it more or less doesn't matter.- It is very hard to actually get interested in your students. They don't stay with you long - at most half of a level (End time in a normal game is around year 10-12, and the longest a student stays is 7 for the most part). It's more or less the Tropico character sheet in terms of knowing what is going on in the background with a character, but it's not really interesting, and you have very little you can do to directly impact  a student.- Often the popup interactions will have options that you could have satisfied before clicking on it, or before the timer would have expired if you knew what was coming. That means there is an incentive to store up a buffer of resources, but because it's too random which resource you may need you just go *shrug*.Good:Pacing: Never outstays its welcome, game lengths seem really well tuned on normal settings.Mechanics: - I really like the interactions between house/schools of magic/student perks and flaws etc. This really works well, just wish it was possible to better see what is going on.- Room customization: It has a fairly high randomness, but I quite enjoyed this due to the variety of things that can be added. Again, due to the obscuring of direct effects it is hard to evaluate the effect of any given change, but it was still interesting and probably only gets more interesting with further play.Tone and Writing: Light, somewhat amusing, just chill enough to relax to.Overall game: Seems to have some replayability, and isn't overly taxing.Verdict:Will play a second campaign on a higher difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: has some weird bugs and unfinished parts like UI popups that display off of the screen and incorrect language issues sometimes randomly popping in.Graphics are kind of quaint but pretty amateur. Has that standard assets Unity game engine look to it.Difficult to tell how or why you are succeeding at any given momentThe customization of the houses is kind of fun.Music and sound effects are kind of bland to non-existent.Not clear what you are supposed to be doing with the faction relations.Can't really plan out your school because you just build stuff in the available contiguous spaces as you draw cards for it.No real connection to any characters as they are just randomly generated with some stats effecting how fast they learn.Combat is just watching your units send some little particle effects to the enemy, and the same particle effects get reused a lot. _childDocuments_.review: I had fun with the game, it's one of those "easy to learn, hard to master" games. One of the issues I find is that the dungeon mechanic is very poorly explained and events are not very eventful. The game often says there might be consequences later on but have yet to see that happen. Other than that it's fun for short bursts of play and I recommend it as a side boredom buster.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: You'd think a game like this would require you to carefully plan the layout of your school, but guess again.  That's not really possible since what rooms you are able to build are mostly random.  You draw from several card decks each of which takes a particular resource per draw, and get to keep one of three random cards from that deck, some of which may be rooms.  With the high degree of randomness this enforces, strategic planning is not really a thing you can do.  Furthermore, it seems like just cramming as many students into your school as possible is the way to go.  Even when you don't have nearly enough facilities to handle all of them, more students means more money and resources.  I don't recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice, entertaining game for fans of D&D, J.K. Rowling and other fantasy stuff offering nice humor, easter eggs and a nice to learn but harder to master single-player game. I like the mechanisms of card-draw in the game. The dungeon-crawl aspect could be a bit more fleshed out but devs keep adding stuff as v1.03 came up with new rooms and lots of items for your pupils. Definitively worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the longest reviews I've ever left on a Steam game - so please bear with me. Like a hodgepodge of Harry Potter, The Sims Franchise (i.e. SimCity or SimTown - does anyone remember that game?) and Theme Hospital (Two-Point Hospital for any new to the game), this game is one for the ages. I'm so glad I was introduced to this game. Spellcaster University is a very delightful and engaging game. This game has an incredible art design and is full of adorable details that make it very immersive. It is enjoyable to watch the teachers and students wander around the classrooms and partake in various activities, spells, and teachings. The randomness of the drawing of the cards does leave this game very much up to chance which can be both a plus and a negative. It is a plus because literally no play through will ever be the same, it is a negative because literally no play through will ever be the same. You can't depend on any predictability for the set up of the school. The element of chance does push this game to one more of luck than actual skill. However, it is a fun enough game that the level of chance you are provided is not a serious detriment. There are some features that are lacking such as interaction with teachers and management of the teaching staff and students. There is no way to directly discipline either pupil or staff. And with the randomness between two teachers for each classroom that you can never fire or change, it does leave some room to be desired. It would be incredible to have an ability to train staff or fire staff and re-hire new, better staff. It also would be great to have some edit buttons or the ability to move rooms. (My current first playthrough and I accidentally clicked a Shadow room in one spot and it forever changed the course of my game play) Of course, this adds to the challenge of this game, but sometimes it's a little too challenging, especially when just learning how to navigate the game. (Hello accidentally clicking on a horrible teacher when just trying to attempt to change the name.) Overall, I am really enjoying this highly addicting game. Seriously, I'm playing it for my third night in a row. My husband is lonely and my child feels unloved - send help! :D /s ((It is honestly really addicting though - like seriously!)
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Bad tutorial, too repetitive and incredibly ableist - makes fun of disabled people, stereotyping. Examples - deaf people learn 15% slower. Being deaf has nothing to do with learning speed. Promotes stereotypes about ADHD ( hyperactive student with a description - look a butterfly!). The worst part is that they could have done the game without promoting real-life stereotypes by changing the language and not the gameplay. The tutorial and pacing of the game would have to be reworked, but it is not impossible. It is a shame because I thought this would be a game I would really enjoy. Very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic concept. Great execution. BUGGY. I don't mind lil bugs here and there but It's INFURIATING when I don't hit a goal because of a stupid bug. I recommend it if you just wanna have fun. However, if you are a completionist, forget about it for a year until they fix all the bugs. I'm in love with the game but I hate how buggy it is. _childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive. Entertaining. On the surface (First couple of playthroughs) the strategy portion felt a bit hollow. I thought that they dressed up a game with cute graphics to get you to ignore how shallow the strategy portion was. This isn't true at all. There is quite a bit to do. Much more to consider when playing through an entire campaign. There is a bit of a grindy/samey feel to gameplay at times, but I do often feel the urge to come back to it. Overall, worth 20 bucks to be sure. A great 1st game effort from a small studio. I look forward to seeing what else they come up with in the future. I'm not a Harry Potter fan, but a sim management fan. Take that for what it's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: It's a an alright game. It's fun if you just want to turn your brain off and just look at stuff moving around the screen. While playing I didn't really feel like I was changing much or noticing any tangible impact in what I do. Can't delete rooms so you either save your cards to put them in the way you want or just place them as you go and hope for the best which usually works. The cards themselves don't really have much description to them, there are cards where for whatever reason you can't place them and the game does not tell you how/why you can't. Apparently it has to be on the ground floor so if you want to place a specific room you have to save some space, tough luck if you didn't know this beforehandAlright experience, price is a bit steep for what you get but on sale it's decent enough enjoyment. Just don't expect too much going in.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER:  I don't think this is a terrible game.  I only said I don't recommend because I have to choose "Yes" or "No."  My actual opinion is that this game is on the lower side of "Just Okay."  Criticisms:- The tutorial should actually be interactive.  It looks interactive but it isn't.  I had to Google it to figure out what I was doing wrong/why I couldn't progress in it.  I mean, I guess I could have just done something different, but at this point in gaming I expect in-game tutorials to be interactive.- The UI is bad.  I've played the game 12 hours now and I still don't know, for instance, what all of the info in the statistics book means.  - Maybe I'm just bad at the game, but I think it needs to be tuned.  It's kind of hard to tell, though, because the graphics/game notifications don't make it obvious how boredom, sanity, hunger, etc. are affecting students' studies.  I also have never had a problem with money EVER.  It doesn't seem to really affect anything.  Overall, I wish I had waited for a sale.  I love the theme and concept, but it wasn't executed very well, in my opinion.  This is a great $5-10 game.  It's a mediocre $25 one.

_childDocuments_.review: The premise is really cool. You're basically Dumbledore. You maintain a school for wizards! _childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, but.....INCREDIBLY taxing on any computer for seemingly for no reason.The game is also very very short. Far too short to be worth the price tag.
