_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Love it so much! This game is super fun and low stakes. You draw cards with gold and magic-school specific types of mana, and get random buildings and items to build the school with. There is a 10 in-game year time limit for each map, which can make each session self-contained. The campaign adds interesting, compounding buffs and debuffs for re-playability, as you move the school from one map to another. Very easy to get into, compared to a lot of settlement/building manager games.There's always wacky stuff happening- strategy only matters if you decide to shoot for goals. Setting up rules and being selective with students is deceptively nuanced. The houses can be way more important than you might think, if you set them up like honors student tracks versus the general class. Plus you never know what rooms and items you'll draw, so the plan may go awry or go super well.Since they added dungeons there's a really cool auto-battler mini-game that feeds off of how you set up your school and what skills your students have. The synergies between different abilities feels great if you have talented students, which takes some planning and investing in certain students and classrooms.Highly recommend for a chill time!
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: A really interesting management game. Quite a bit of mechanics in it too, which complement each other nicely.  Many rooms, artifacts, potions, decorations, pets, factions and events to mix up each playthrough. Your students will have varying levels of skill, random traits or alignments that will incline them to specific schools of magic or facilitate a chance in a specific career choice (of which are several) after graduating which will give you some benefits. Each teacher will be randomized as well, with varying levels of expertise and different salary expectation, with maybe some previous affiliation to one of the game’s factions which will improve your school’s relationship with said party, which in turn will give you access to advantages or events you wouldn’t otherwise. You’ll also be able to group students into houses which will randomly have some specific benefits. There’s something of a time limit integrated in the game as well, those I usually hate with a passion but in this case is actually quite welcomed to spice things up. While you play, a meter will fill up, this will cause the evil forces to attack you at full, making you having to “restart” your university in another place. This gives quite a replayability factor, especially because the locations available are random each time. Having to start from zero again also helps you refine your strategies. How many objectives you completed in each stage will give you a permanent buff and debuff, also selected from a random pool with different tiers.Now… let’s go over some things that I Dungeons are fun just once or twice, they feel kind of pointless and even disadvantageous to the pace of gameplay, so I never really went out of my way for them. The gameplay there is quite shallow, to be honest. Let’s be real though, expecting a whole dungeon-crawling RPG implemented into an already expansive management game would be maybe a bit much, I get it. It’s there for whoever would enjoy that kind of  aspect. Just not my cup of tea.What is certainly not much to ask for and mindbogglingly absent from this game seems to be quality of life features. How’s it possible that I can’t delete houses or rooms I don’t want anymore? The point of this type of game, at least for me (someone who plays A LOT of them), is to improve whatever I’m managing to a point where it’s perfectly efficient. A lot of players try to excuse these missing additions by saying they would give an “unfair” advantage, but deleting rooms would slow you down anyway and there’s a time limit to every stage, so min-maxing that way would have a clear disadvantage, so why not add them? Just look at the number of times a wrote “random” or “randomly” in this review. These quality of life features wouldn’t just  they are completely  to avoid frustration and extend gameplay past one or two runs. Quite a fun game with some little but unforgivable missing features that hold it from being truly great.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts with the tutorial that is completely useless. It's just a sequence of pop-ups that describe the UI elements. "This button does this, the options are here..." and... that's it. It reminded me of Silicon Valley episode "your box goes here" data center episode. Nothing is explained about the game and the consequences of your choices.OK, I figured I could learn as I go, how hard could it be? Maybe it's not hard but I can't tell because I just absolutely could not stand the awful UI. It is a card playing game that doesn't involve very complex mechanics but almost every move seems off. To select a card, you need to click off-center. There is no consistent close button. Sometimes the button is drawn but it does nothing and there is a real Close button elsewhere. Sometimes there is no Close/cancel button at all. Esc key does nothing. How am I supposed to just close the huge dialog screen? There is no handy access to Help to read more about the concepts. It feels like an alpha version and I'm really confused by the positive reviews. I don't understand how anyone could spend more than 15 minutes with this game and not go bonkers dealing with terrible UI. Really wanted to like it, neat idea but awful execution.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:If you like the humor and graphic level of West of Loathing or Kingdom of Loathing, you'll like this.On sale? It's different, give it a go.Full price? I wouldn't.Pros and Cons:+Remember this is a card game that brings cards to life as rooms, creatures, items, potions. Its essentially a deckbuilder, keeping that in mind explains so much more and will make you enjoy the game more. It's also a different vibe from most card games you can play, so it will keep things fresher.+For some reason the tutorial doesn't tell you but if you get duplicate room cards you can overlay them with the previous versions to upgrade what's in your school. (But from what I have seen, the same is not true of creatures or items.) This also gives them different looks.+While it can be hard to sus out on your own, the game is good about indicating where things can and cannot be placed, making items and creatures very "plug and play".+No micromanagement. For some that might be a con, but for me its a big bonus. No trying to track down that one specific guy to tell him to do something, he is already doing it.-Very little interaction even at 3x speed and you can't seem to willfully fling students at dungeons to pass the time.-Potion crafting is incredibly situational, as is what the components can be used for outside of potion crafting, and this can make your "hand" of cards very full very awkwardly, don't be afraid to chuck things.-Sometimes a room simply can't be built due to the access points or other pathing issues. It stinks, but you can still sell room cards on the far right with the bucket icon.-The campaign aspect of this is misleading. It's not so much new stages as just different opponents to fight with your cards, which is... odd.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having so much fun pretending to be Dumbledore with this game. Spellcaster University is surprisingly deep, with randomness from card draws causing enough variety to make each game interesting. Though I've seen almost every card with about six hours played, I count that as a positive because it means I can start to strategize which cards to keep and prioritize. I'm discovering more nuances with each game and I'm enjoying the campaign a lot. The game does have some minor quirks, such as occasionally I'm not sure why I can't place a building where I'd like, but nothing that takes away from the delight of building my own little Hogwarts and puzzling out the best way to use my card draws.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and addicting management game with the fattest, cutest little dragons, a guinea pig messenger catapult, and a level where you build a school on the back of a giant turtle. Campaign mode is 7 different locations where you need to use limited, RNG-supplied resources to build a magical school and reach random minigoals before the timer runs out and the evil army of darkness comes to destroy everything you built, then go to a new location and do it all over again. The random card-draw aspect keeps each level fresh and ensure you can't use the same strategy every time, and there are various challenge modes to provide even more chaos. There's also a push-your-luck dungeon crawl offered each level so you can enjoy the fun of watching your precious young charges being murdered by angry trolls because you needed a new wall tapestry. It's pretty well-balanced, and I haven't noticed any serious bugs, though the pathfinding is sometimes a little goofy and people can get stuck in doors (restarting the game fixes it).I would have bought it just for the guinea pigs, but the fact that the game is actually pretty good is a bonus.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, really fun game that accomplishes what it sets out to do. Also, I wish my students could actually die during the school year, but well, those are design decisions.All in all, I am confident about its future.

_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this magical mix of mechanics that is Spellcaster University! It successfully blends deck style gameplay into building management simulator where you train students to be the GREAT wizards of the future! You only have a limited time on each map until the Lord of Evil over runs your school! The good news is, you'll have the option to send your best students to fight in the dungeons!  This'll earn your university more prestige and hold off the invasion of the Lord of Evil a bit longer! Will you successfully beat the map objectives before time runs out?!It's also very replayable! Each time you play feels unique due to the randomness that comes with a deck style draw system, which requires you to have a different approach every time you play the same level!  It also has a neat legacy feature where your past graduates will provide bonuses to your school depending on what their careers are! I truly enjoy this game and am looking forward to mastering the challenges it offers! :DPros:-Fun unique style of gameplay with a lot of replayability -Neat art style-Non-linear campaign that offers challenges for a new feel each play through! Cons:-Limited customization options for making students appear unique.  Can change they names though which is fun, but I wish I could make them look a bit more like people I know too ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet this game is amazing and I highly recommend it!  Without question anyone who is a Harry Potter fan will immediately find a kindred spirit here, but anyone who is into essentially tile placing management games will also enjoy this game.  Without spoilers, mechanically there are two game modes, free play and campaign.  So far I have only played the Campaign but it does have near infinite replayability which is great.  The game's mechanics basically run on a timer, during which your students and teachers work together to generate mana which you use to get more tiles to expand your school or upgrade a currently placed tile.  Once placed tiles cannot be moved and some tiles have fixed interaction points so you have to plan your school accordingly.  As students generate mana they also generate experience which improves their abilities both in generating more mana as well as empowering themselves for the dungeon delve minigames.  The minigames I actually thoroughly enjoy, I just wish there was more than two on average per level (also the ability to intervene during fights would be nice).  There is also a world map in which you interact with other factions, although I found a one-two combo which consistently pushes back the timer which made most other interactions unnecessary unless required for the level's goals.  Each level has its own unique objectives and goals, accomplishing which gives you passive benefits that apply to future levels.As a full game it is exceptionally well made, I am still thoroughly enjoying it, and I commend the developer for their fantastic craftsmanship.  I was a touch sad to hear the developer is now working on new products but wish them best of luck, hopefully their future products replicate this success.  My hope is that this will open the door to the game allowing mods as I feel there is still untapped potential in permitting more dungeon delves per level, more traits for students/professors, more classrooms (perhaps those that mix different schools), and other such additions.But yes, as someone who has played through two campaigns and unlocked two different endings I will continue to play again and see what other endings there are to unlock.  As I stated previously, highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: If I could give neutral rating, I would. The game was ultimately not for me, but I think many people will find it more entertaining. I just don't happen to be in the focus group.Long version: Basically randomness to feedback loops - the game. Player draws from random cards, reacts to random events, sends semi-random emissaries to other factions, gets random students and teachers, and various random things happen at the school too. Feedback loop happens when player gets their foot down on some mana type and starts buying more stuff related to that type, which produces more of that mana and so on.Campaign, the main game type, is the most feedback loopy of them all. Player gets permanent benefits from skilled enough students graduating and from fulfilling missions. These allow player to gain resources faster, train students faster, get better faculties and spend longer in the maps, allowing even more students to graduate with better grades. Good play is rewarded with easier late game, while bad play might lead into spirals of death.The lore of game is tad tropey, but it also leans heavily on standard fantasy setting. There is enough detail and tongue-in-the-cheek to raise it above basic fantasy while still being familiar enough not to distract player from the game. Those seeking deep or original fantasy role will be likely disappointed. Graphics suit the purpose, but interface is glitchy enough to be annoying at times. It is nothing game ruining but definitely hurts flow of the gameplay. Interface could also be much better with small details like cards of same type stacking on top of each other. Alchemy ingredients in particular tended to fill the visible space far too much.

Worth 25 bucks?  Maybe if you're super jazzed about a Hogwarts Management sim, or management sims in general really do it for you.  Otherwise I'd say it's easily worth a buy on sale. _childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a solid management game, with the card deck adding replay-ability / unpredictability, always makes new campaigns different. It has challenging goals and even the standard game options give you a good challenge.There are definitely things that I would like to be added though, such as:- Fire / replace teachers OR more options when picking a teacher. Choosing between two can be hard, especially when both are horrible.- Delete / edit houses (should be able to change the house banner) - I know I've messed up a few times with this and it ultimately can effect the rest of your game.- Move / delete buildings. Can easily add penalties for this such as gold loss.- More selections for your goals. Lots of times I start a campaign with one or two select magics, and half the time the star goals (randomized) do not fit with what I'd like to do. - Better rewards on certain events (20gp to offer services? +5 reputation? +4 prestige? very little gain for using up your communication) Specific reputations can take an entire game to build up, and sometimes other contacts require attention (orcs, ancient orc, minstrel, dwarves, etc)- Would be cool to see more traits for diversity.- Dungeons are cool, but half of the time my students are pretty weak and I have no cards for the venture. Some games I don't even get offered a dungeon which sucks.- Back out of communication options. I've definitely fallen into the habit of quickly picking something and realizing that I wasted my communication.

_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game for what it tries to be. I personally believe that this is NOT a management game. It fits better into the "god game" genre, as player control of any one specific character is minimal. The incremental buffs received as students graduate feels very much like something out of an idle game, and while that genre is certainly not for everyone, it does appeal to me personally.This game is not perfect, but I do enjoy it in its current state, and I hope the dev team continues to iron out the kinks and improve on a sound premise.

_childDocuments_.review: Most of my time was spent staring at the screen watching little cartoon students run around, it gets boring fast. The game's mechanics push you toward specialization, but then punish you if you're not a generalist. It felt like the game offered a variety of strategies, but the only way I could win was to use the most boring one available. Also the building mechanic didn't give me enough freedom to make anything pretty while also not really mattering toward the optimization of my school, it was a good 1/4th of the gameplay that didn't feel like it had any meaning

_childDocuments_.review: So here we have a game that allows you to create a magical school of your liking, complete with establishing houses/classes, keeping relations with world factions and magic hijinks along the way. I started off somewhat skeptical with the card focused gameplay, but as you can see by the hours I played, I liked it. If you like the setting and the idea of managing magical school, give it a shot!For the purposes of this review I want to keep in mind that I am reviewing the early access version as of mid-january to mid-february. Despite starting in a very bug-ridden phase, where save games couldn't load and the campaign couldn't be finished (it has been fixed quickly, so don't worry ;) ), I couldn't stop playing. The gameplay was that captivating for me.Let's start with the presentation and world building. The game is presented with a cute, simple art style and a simple story that doesn't take itself all too seriously. While the evil lord is very clearly a cliche fantasy lord, the other factions are at least a bit more fleshed out. At least I didn't feel like the orcs, inquisition or the peasants were completely one-note. The game very lighthearted and it shows in the presentation and the textboxes. Personally I liked it a lot and it certainly helps to keep the focus on the main class.The main class, of course, being the gameplay. As mentioned I was somewhat skeptical at first, but, to my positive surprise, it turned out to be pretty addicting. It basically works like this: You build rooms and place objects by playing the cards you have "on hand" on the respective spot. The cards are mixed into 6 decks, one for each magical school (arcana, light, shadow, alchemy and nature) and one for general administration and starting classrooms. While the magic related ones require mana, which is produced when students learn the according subject, the general ones require gold. You get basic provision rooms and 600 gold at the start of each level.The cards you draw are randomized, thus making every beginning a bit different. On some occassions it can screw you over, such is the nature of randomized card drawing. Still, in this game it felt more like a challenge than a complete brick. It helps that you will always get prompts by the world factions, that allow you to draw new cards or get gold for them. The principle may be simple, but it turned out to be quite complex, too. A lot of the cards aren't just rooms you can place, but also artefacts and animals that can boost your efficiency. If you ever want one of your students to become an archimage, you will need to adress this. It is here where I realized that this is less of a building game, than a puzzle game. Trying to figure out where to place certain artefacts to ensure the best learning experience for my students was seriously captivating. If you do it correctly and have a bit luck, you can have classrooms that teach up to four or even FIVE different subjects at the same time! Add to this various objects that reduce the speed of needs increasing or help students concentrate more and you will, at some point, reliably have alumni with the best futures.Some rooms can also be upgraded. Okay, technically they all can, which increases efficiency, but some rooms have special upgrades too. The greenhouse has upgrades that generate potion ingredients. The elemantalist dojo has upgrades to increase learning speed (at the cost of health) and gain gold from bets. The jail can be set to rehabilitation to get rid of some negative traits. This adds to the complexity as you will sometimes have to choose between a new room/object or an upgrade you find really useful. Speaking of the futures: Upon graduation a student will have a list of possible futures according to their acquired magical skills and personal traits. Yes, students and faculty have traits, positive and negative ones. They can be affected by objects, too (the armillary sphere can give students that work in a room the ambitious trait for instance, which directly benefits likelhood of good futures). Futures have permanent or immediate effects, so gambling with the fututes can be quite beneficial. Immediate effects usually give mana boosts, gold or relationship boosts, which are especially useful when you started your school. Permanent bonuses stay for the ENTIRE campaign. Make sure you get as many of those as possible when you finished a level! To give concrete examples: Sorcerers apprentice is a future that gives you 50 alchemy mana, no strings attached. This is an immediate bonus and the since the future is possible when a student as 1 enchantment skill (related to alchemy), it's easy to get. Elementalist has a permanent bonus, since it increases the learning speed of elementalism by 1% (can be stacked!) and only requires a student to be good at elemantalism (arcana). Particularly useful ones like time monk (which is a permanent effect that gives you arcana mana for every room card played!) require very good skills. Futures add or detract to school prestige. Prestige dictates how many students you can have and also some in game choices. Most futures do give +1 prestige, but the really good ones may give you two (or five with the minstrel). The best and hardest future to achieve, which can be an optional quest, is getting an archimage. The best of the best. The cremé de la creme of the magical world. Really rare and requires a student to have a magical skill of at least 4 in three subjects. Since they have a looong list of possible futures, it's easy to not get it. It also has a good permanent bonus, so going for archimage can be quite fulfilling. Personally I tend to have a warm feeling whenever a student has a great future, especially if they weren't the best ones or had the stacks against them. The sadder I am when someone who is good ends up as a peasant or even... dead!The management aspect can be a bit lacking though. Sure you can set policies in your office, but I rarely used them. I didn't feel like the patron gave me enough gold, most didn't seem useful and the gender selection is only aesthetic/for atmosphere (in case you want a school solely for witches and whatnot). I also think some characters are underused, which is sad because they can be entertaining. The headmaster of the other magic school only has two events and doesn't appear otherwise, which is a wasted opportunity to show that he is a really condescending jerk, masking behind eloquence. Or the union leader, the angry parents... the events quickly repeat and the characters remain underused as a consequence. I do hope more events get added, especially since some futures actually give you benefits for interacting with them. All in all, despite its flaws and the bugs I encountered, I still can't stop playing this game. The tone is lighthearted and fun, the room management is captivating, getting the students to graduate with bright futures ahead is motivating and the evil forces are approaching with the inquisition hating my guts... sorry that I don't have the truth chamber yet, head inquisitor! I'm not going to pay, you hear?!Anyway, the events repeat a bit too quickly. I do hope more get added later. The management of staff and policy is underwhelming. I couldn't even see how much each staff member takes as wage, despite there being differences (union memebership, greedy trait etc.). So, if you like this sort of gameplay or even just the theme of building a magic school in a fantasy world, give it a try! I certainly like this game a lot and I will definietely continue to play around with classes, room objects and events (of which I want more of).

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this, there's a lot of little details and stuff to manage, but you aren't necessarily punished for overlooking if you don't want to go that deep.  It's very satisfying to have the whole thing laid out and put little plans into action and see them come together.  Finished the campaign and there are still some maps to check out, and it looks like I got the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ending so I suppose I have to go back in anyway.  The one complaint is I think there should be a way to rearrange rooms, even if at a steep resource cost or something.  I don't think there would be any difficulty balance issue to changing your layout and it's unfortunately possible to break your castle by putting dead-end rooms in the wrong place, locking you out.  One fun thing I would add is bridge 'rooms', sort of like the balcony room they have.  There were times I wanted to connect two towers but had to put something pointless in between, like a janitor closet to link them.  It would be fun and lore friendly to have a gothic bridge that gives me a necro bonus or something to that effect.  Your welcome devs you can keep the change on that one8/10 would recommend going back in for more

As it stands it's pretty difficult to get good use out of it, by the time my students are strong enough for a good dungeon run I don't really need much from the dungeon anymore as it's close to the end of the timer for the forces of evil. _childDocuments_.review: This game is hard. There's a lot of meta involved and the online guides don't have all the info, so there's a lot of trial and error to go through. And the RNG can be VERY unforgiving, which is frustrating... but there's something deeply addictive and charming about this game. I keep finding new details. Like for example, today, I realized that your office gains little artifacts for each of the allies you win over, like a lute for the bard and a pet rock for the forest troll. It doesn't do anything but provide flavor text when you mouse over it, but I was so happy when I found it, and so sad that I missed one (the lake monster). I also realized when you zoom in real close, you can hear what's going on in each of the rooms a lot better. Like the guinea pigs chirping in the stable. Adorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun relaxing game. There is a lot of room for strategy and optimization as each student who leaves your school goes on to a "Future" which either provides you instant effects (giving you resources, improving relationships, or giving you items) or permanent effects for the rest of your play through. One could specialized their school to both achieve the maps objectives AND provide a higher chance of achieving certain futures that will help you on the next map. You can build a game plan from your very first map to maximize your power for the last map.However, I don't really feel like doing any of that, so I don't. I mostly play on normal difficulty absentmindedly while watching something else. It is a really great fidget game in that regard. I just make an efficient school and hope my students have a nice future.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: How good are you at managing a school for magic?No, yours truly has no idea, what Harry Potter is about - never watched any full movie or read a book of his adventures. Nevertheless, it was time to prove, that those are not prerequisites to successfully manage a magical school.In this game you are responsible for what is taught and what specialisations are offered, have an influence on how good your students are, recruit teachers and expand your school. And all of this under the pressure of a timeline, because enemies are closing in and you have to change locations and start all over again. For everyone finishing studies, the school gets rewards, so the better the students, the better the result for the whole school.In addition to that, you can send students to dungeons to fight magical creatures and other enemies, and the better they are, the better the reward (if they do not die trying!).Definitely recommended as a management game with magical elements, nice graphics, optional turn-based RPG-like fighting and cute characters of different species.

It took me a whole playthrough (not too long) to see how it works, did a bit of googling and I got it figured out half way through my second play,  I "won" on the second attempt and I will definitely play through again and again! _childDocuments_.review: This is effectively a heavily randomised Sim Tower type game, with a magical school skinning. There is no downplaying how much RNG is involved. You may plan ahead a certain amount but if you don't draw the right items you'll have to change tack. As resource management goes, that's frustrating, but also means you'll never build the exact same school twice.You will have to abandon schools and start over again anew in campaign mode; that's integral to the gameplay loop, but each new school will gain bonuses from previous ones. I found it very addictive, and it's not a difficult game. You can luck into a perfect level, and you can luck out, but it's very hard to lose a level entirely. There are definitely some major UI issues--inability to zoom out using a keyboard, some info windows can't be closed, and I kept hitting bugs where cards would become tiny and unreadable. Sometimes it's hard to tell why you can't place rooms in some locations when identically-shaped rooms can be placed there without issue. And it would be nice to be able to move rooms around, or to get rid of houses (or to pick from more options for traits for them).The minigame dungeon crawls are perfectly okay but not the point of the game--if you love those, there won't be enough of them to keep you satisfied.Anyway, recommended while it's on sale (it's a bit too thin a game for me to recommend buying at full-price) but not if you hate RNG and want to be permitted to build your idealised school every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Like other reviews mentioned, some of the translations for this game are bad.  It's obvious they didn't have the best translator.  Despite that, I became very immersed in this game very quickly.  It's easy to learn and very engaging.  The RNG component of not knowing what cards you're going to draw keeps things interesting and requires you to take a different path for every step of the campaign.All in all, I love this game.  My first day playing it, I quickly spent 5 hours playing without even realizing it.I suspect this game is only going to get better with development.  I'd like to see an option that allows you to examine the rooms in your school while in the card selection screen in order to strategize better but that's my biggest criticism for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Fits into a niche I'm surprised nobody wants to fill in, especially since Harry Potter's been a thing for decades and all we got were the terribly EA games. As enjoyable as it can be and as lovely as the art and soundtrack is, unfortunately it's a very impersonal experience - it's all about building up the school and aiming for quests and certain magic comps with the students and houses, just all about the management really and it's fun, up until you explore the whole map and endings, by which time the repetitiveness starts to show and it becomes a bit of a chore, which is so sad given the potential. There's no real connection to the teachers and students, since each level wipes out your last school and you build anew - all you end up caring about is "is this teacher good enough?" or "does this student fit here or there" etc. and since the "evil" antagonist portion of the game is more theatrical than anything (and you end up siding with them all the time anyway in order to stall the inevitable end) there's nothing to relate to, nothing to make you care about anything other than managing colors and numbers. Biggest pet peeve with it I have is that you can't scale the UI properly, so on any larger resolutions I keep having to "manually zoom in" (aka lean in and squint at the monitor from an inch away) to read the tiny text. Also, no mod support / workshop.Wish we could get something similar but with equal focus on the characters/story and without the hidden roguelike feature, but it's not like we can even properly mod this so *shrugs*. I'm definitely biased, because my craving for a magical school management sim where the students might not be aplenty but customizable and with stakes high enough and gameplay impactful enough for me to care about each and every last one of them (like x-com style), is just way too high.

_childDocuments_.review: For those wondering: no, this is not a Harry Potter pastiche. While it does take place at a magical school with (optional) Houses, the similarities basically end there.Spellcaster University is an interesting management simulator. The results of your students' hard (or not-so-hard) training has impact going forward, both during the same leg of the game and throughout the run. Learning the system is rewarding, because building that skill has clear correlation with how well the next game goes.One thing I find interesting is how the game pace works. While minor problems like aberrations, portals, and fires can interfere with the learning environment, these are treated more like a minor speedbump than an emergency. You can create potions and draw cards that mitigate or remove these problems, but unlike nearly every other management sim, they don't halt the game to shove an alert in your face. This is almost a problem itself, since there's not a notice system that informs you if these problems arise, but I like that not every hitch is a huge, game-stopping issue.The game is an interesting mix of real-time and turn-based. Events pop up in the left sidebar, most with a progress bar that will force you to address them when it runs down,  you are free to click them right away. This means that you don't run the risk of losing 2 in-game years to a bathroom break and forgetting to pause, for example. You can crank the RT parts to 3x speed, as needed (you can adjust game time when starting a campaign, even when doing a Challenge!), and you can take any number of actions while paused. Dealing with events and using cards automatically pauses the game, as well, which I really appreciate.QoL with this game is really strange. It has such fantastic QoL in some places that you won't even initially realize it because the game just takes care of things for you, but also won't, for instance, tell you what students qualify for a piece of equipment without you manually paging through them. It also has some strange choices when it comes to the tutorial - a lot of the gameplay is learned by doing. I only found out students could be transferred between houses at will while checking the forums!There is a certain mix of randomness and repetition to events that can be frustrating if you play too many campaigns in a row, but there are enough events (and good payouts for succeeding) that I mostly don't mind, and it becomes just part of the play structure.For its flaws, Spellcaster University is a very solid management simulator, and if you like management sims, particularly ones with more chill gameplay options, I strongly recommend it. It allows a level of relaxation without undermining your achievements that I'd love to see more games adopt.The one thing I really hope for in the future is modding support, as the game has a lot of modding potential and I'd be delighted should the devs recognize that.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start with my adoration for  I should probably say that I have backed it on the Kickstarter, so I can be somehow biased in my opinion, but I am quite satisfied with the overall results. Also, it’s made by a small indie studio as you can clearly see, but they care for their game very much and put a lot of work into it! Have to say that this is one of the best Kickstarter campaigns I have backed.As the unexpected return of the Lord of Evil (blame the calendar) threatens the peaceful world yet again you are tasked with building a magic Academy from scratch where new prosperous students can become our salvation in the upcoming fight! You have only limited time for maintaining your Academy at each location though, because the evil army seeks your destruction and marches forward slowly, but steadily. When your current Academy is destroyed you get to select benefits and curses (based on your performance) for your next location. Choose wisely, especially the curses can be problematic. Also, in the campaign all of the stats are combined, which gives you a great boost in the long run.In  you are the headmaster and have influence only over what rooms you are gonna build, what magic classrooms are gonna be in your school and who is gonna study in them. And of course we can’t forget about making decisions in the events. Everything else is basically out of your hands, but it’s so much fun and rather addicting!Your goal is to create an effective Academy and for that you have to properly lay out the whole building. Students should have their classes near the bedrooms and dining rooms otherwise they take too long going between them, also you have to mind the numbers of students and their respective rooms - when their capacity is full students would leave to town to satisfy their needs and so they would spent less time on their studies which would generate you less mana which would then hinder your building progress! It's all connected. Also don’t forget about the teachers and their needs, as they will leave for the city too without a proper place to rest and eat and that means no classes for students, and again no mana for you.There are five magic schools to choose from: nature, shadow, light, alchemy and arcana. Each magic school has three specializations which have corresponding classrooms where students learn only that exact specialization, and one classroom that teaches all of it. You are not limited on how many magic schools you can have in the Academy. If you want, you can build all five, just beware that it's pretty challenging to layout the space properly. Also, every location has different advantages (like large buildable area, slower evil progression) and disadvantages (like small buildable area, long distance to town), so you should always adapt your strategy accordingly.Students enroll to the Academy regularly and you can also draw their cards from packages or events. They have traits that can make class selection easier for you. Some are good and some are bad, the bad usually mean that their learning progression will be slowed down and you will get a low amount of mana. Getting rid of those bad traits is always advisable (especially with teachers!). You can order your students which classes they should visit, for good results it’s best to not have more than three magic schools for each hall. Once the students end their studies you will see what their futures are - if they will be Archmages or just simple peasants or even end up dead! You can re-roll the future, but it can be for the worse, so choose carefully. Each graduation has different bonus - some are immediate like cards, some are beneficial in the long run (% raises in learning etc.).To build something in the Academy you have to choose one card from three that you pick from a corresponding package once you have generated enough mana (the required amount raises with each draw). There is also a money package from which you can build basic rooms (dormitory, refectory, staff rooms…), but as the money generation is a bit slower it can take some time before you can start building in a big scale… and usually when you accumulate enough money for picking a card some event happens and robs you of all the money. XD You can level up most of the rooms to raise the efficiency of the room or gain neat bonuses, they also change their appearance a little. You can further decorate the rooms with different items to again gain some bonuses, be it for learning or mana gain or students behavior etc. You can put animals in some of the rooms and some of them would even run around the Academy! There is really a lot to play with!The cards you get to draw are randomly generated so it may happen that you will wait for some specific card for some time (yeah, I have waited almost half of the game), but it doesn't hold you back necessarily. There are other means on how to develop certain class skills even if slowly. Don't forget that you don't have to play the card when you don't wish to. There is no limit to cards on your hand (although it can be rather crowded if you have a lot of them). If you don't have a use for the chosen card you can sell it back for a small amount of mana or money. I should probably mention that you can't rearrange your Academy, no moving with rooms or demolishing them. Once you set it there, it's gonna stay there. Sometimes mistakes can happen and the card can fall from your hand when you are just considering the options (yep, happened to me) - well, you have to improvise then. Actually it’s what I find likeable on the game, how it “forces” me to adapt.Beside many random events you have to develop a connection with neighbors - peasants, King, adventurers… Good relationships are always beneficial to both sides, keep that in mind. In each location you can visit up to two dungeons, it's one of the random events so you never know when they are gonna appear. The good thing about them is that they aren't time limited and you can visit them once you are ready - once you have students with at least some of the magic skills on the highest level. As the dungeons can turn pretty hard it's not advisable to go there early, but as you get pretty good loot from them it's advisable to go there before you develop your Academy to the fullest… yeah, pretty complicated. ;)The graphics are cute, colorful and it's a joy to zoom in on the rooms and look at the running little fellows. You can recognize your students by different cloak colors which you will select when creating their halls, you can also create their coat of arms on your own! Big plus is that during holidays (Christmas and Halloween) there are respective decorations! Music is enjoyable. I have played it from the early access and the game went really far. Back there were stability issues when it crashed on me rather often, but the last 30 hours were without any issue. is a little gem that has a lot to offer. It's a sweet, casual, funny game, where you will easily lose many hours! I can wholeheartedly recommend it! :)

_childDocuments_.review: In a world where AAA Game Companies are determined to send you back to the dullard trenches and tell you that this is the Absolute Heights of Excitement, this is a game that should be tedious because you're in charge of a University. And yet, it's exciting enough I'd recommend it over the latest Ghost Warrior Game.First off; it utilizes Randomness in a way that you can either have trouble getting off the ground, or you'll fly to the moon on gossamer wings of success. Not unlike a D&D game, but one where you're even lonelier than usual. The art style lends itself well to what it wants to portray, which is a University that you're in charge of is in danger of destruction, but it's not too hard to recover from, so no biggie. Also; Gooney Pigs are your blessings.And although you should think that Magic is your only necessary Power, this being a MAGIC UNIVERSITY, Diplomacy's important too. Being able to get the Orcs, the Kingdom, the Peasants, the Inquisition, the Adventurers, and whatever else is on the map on your side is just as important as having the Classrooms, and so is having the Sundries to keep your Teachers and your Students at work, and having an income that will help make more stuff, so think of it like a regular Tycoon Game in that you're in charge of making this University a Success.In the End; you'll only get so much enjoyment from this Game based on how much Busywork you like doing, and if you're a fan of the concept of Magical Education.

The classroom and common areas make sense, and have function that decide the fate of the game, and never feel generic.  Also, I like how buildings can be leveled up.  Overall this game just got many things right.  My only wish is for more room types, so cannot wait to see 1.4+ or even a DLC. _childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to enjoy about this game. As all games, it does have the occasional flaw, but at the time of me writing this, I have 105 hours. I'm going to list a couple pros and a couple cons, but I'll say that it's definitely worth the buy if you want a fun, mindless management game. This is my firs review, so pardon me for doing anything wrong. Here are my pro's and con's: 1. It's easy to pick up. Plays a bit like a rogue like the further you get through it, and the more you play the more you get used to it.2. It's addictive. You can spend hours mindlessly playing it and finding new futures and combinations. 3. Graphics aren't god tier, but the art style is cute, and there are small details everywhere that really add to it. 4. Details to story and quests are good, and the flavor texts on cards is very funny. 5. The difficulty levels are good. You can find good challenges if you want, or just play for fun.1. This is hard, I don't find much wrong with this game. The replay-ability is probably the weakest part. After some point, this game becomes difficult to play if you aren't just playing it for mindless stimulation. There's nothing wrong with that, but it does become repetitive. 2. There's the occasional broken English sprinkled throughout the game, so if that bothers you, that's a con, however it has gotten better and better as the game has added updates. That's all I really have to say. I recommend this game! I'm excited for the bonus content coming soon!

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like a great, early-release game. It shouldn't be the final product. -------------------------------- OVERVIEW --------------------------------It feels like a resource-management, tile-placing, rogue-like kinda game with a magic skin. It does a good job with the theme, though it feels in many ways more like a high school than a university (guidance counselors, misbehaving, teachers' lounge, no inter-dept. politics, etc.). It's clearly inspired by Hogwarts in that sense. Guinea pigs are a really fun addition!You start the game by choosing a region to build your school in. Each region has some unique opportunities and challenges. Eventually, you'll build in each region -- but more on that later. In a given region, you build your university room-by-room based on what cards you're dealt. Some rooms are classrooms where the learning happens. Other rooms are for students: bedrooms, dining halls, common rooms, counselling rooms, rec rooms, etc. Still others are exclusively for teachers, like a teacher lounge. There are yet more rooms that are general: a janitor's closet, a guinea pig tower, an infirmary, etc. You can establish different Houses (think Gryffindor, Syltherin, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw) within your university and set their academic specializations. There's always a "General" house for students with no specialization. You can accept and sort a student into a House, or decline them entrance altogether. You can catapult your excitable guinea pigs (seriously, a fun touch!) to neighboring factions on the map to interact with them. You want to keep your reputation up with them while satisfying their demands. A bit after setting in (I'd like this to happen earlier in a mission!), you get three quests for that mission: things like getting a certain amount of gold, earning a certain amount of mana, or keeping your reputation with everyone else above a certain threshold. If you complete each quest on that mission, you'll earn advantages to the next mission. Meanwhile, each student that graduates can give your university prestige, more mana in the various categories, or certain long-term campaign bonuses. The better educated a student is at their graduation, the better outcomes each student can have. This is pretty fun, though it can be tedious with lots of students. IMPORTANT: the Evil Lord WILL attack your university, and you WILL be forced to abandon it and start over in a new region. This is a core gameplay mechanic: you don't even get to battle the Evil Lord after a mission. -------------------------------- WHAT I LIKE --------------------------------- It is a neat card-playing rogue-like with a combat system for adventures that is a rogue-like within a rogue-like! - I really appreciate the variety of encounters, cards and events in the game! -------------------------------- WHAT NEEDS WORK --------------------------------Highest Priority: - The tutorial is a wall of text all at once, before you even get to start playing. I kept thinking, "Oh, am I supposed to do what it's saying now? I can't...." only to realize that, no, I was supposed to press an X somewhere to get the next instruction. This needs some work. It's hard to learn all at once. Let there be tutorial tips throughout gameplay as new things come up and become relevant to the player. - The UI needs significant work. Let the user press Escape to close a dialogue. Let there be a UI overview that shows the names of each room. Let there be an overview that highlights the artifacts in the various rooms. The stats tab needs work. I know of no way to see the salaries of individual faculty. Unfinished Feel:- It does not distinguish between faculty and staff. This leads to (e.g.) janitors, nurses and guidance counselors being treated as "teachers", which just feels weird. - For example, it sometimes refers to the furry rodent messengers as "Gooney Pigs", but other times it calls them "Guinea Pigs". It's as if the dev(s) didn't proofread or playtest their game. - There are a few spelling/grammar mistakes throughout the game. - It does not seem well-optimized. It makes my laptop fans spin like crazy -- much more than I feel it should.  - There are occasional graphical bugs. - I'd like to be able to zoom out to see my whole university (even in the Forest region), but it does not allow this. I'd like to not be able to zoom in so far that the camera moves behind the university.

_childDocuments_.review: On the one hand, the game has a decent art style, charming writing and there's a decent amount of thought in placing your classrooms and deciding how many refectories, dormitories etc. you need, especially to help keep your upper floors to use.However, there's very little that will actually require you to look at your students. Lower tier futures provide immediate resources to kickstart your early academy while you farm long-term benefits, so even Dumb Deaf bullies will not be a concern for you. For Curriculum, just pick the ones with easy requirements (anything with 12/20 required students) and you barely even need houses anymore - just get one with strong bonuses like Jack-of-all-trades, Athletic or Popular and throw all of your students there.While splitting for different specialties seems appealing, you should at most only focus a house on it if you need a more difficult curriculum. The best future path - Thaumaturge - requires your students to know all schools of magic.I also noticed that needs management is very much not punishing. All that happens is that the affected person will get themselves a break if they're low. One of my teachers went to 0 health and continued to get mauled by orcs yet was completely fine just afterwards.Overall, despite my non-recommendation, it's still a decent game to play casually, it's just not a game for if you really like in-depth management or complex optimizations.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little management game. The campaign gives you missions and a time limit, which does a great job of solving what I think of as "the Dwarf Fortress problem" - namely, what in the heck you're supposed to *do* once you've got a base established and there are no immediate threats remaining. I've never been able to stick with an endless sandbox game for very long for that reason, but in this game you have specific goals in each level, and the Lord of Evil is constantly approaching, which means you gotta hustle.Of course, if you *like* endless sandboxes, you have that option as well, with the single-level "quick play" mode letting you turn off the time limit entirely and build up forever.While the game could certainly use a bit more tweaks and polish, it's absolutely a solid play.

_childDocuments_.review: Harry Potter and why haven't other studios made games like this ????Very cute game, highly addictive and you can come back to it quite easily. There is a lot going on, and whilst it can be very easy to get caught up in the whole constant management and upgrading, it's well worth it to slow down time and watch what they get up to in the classroom. It is very rewarding to see your best students graduate into things like demon hunters or potion makers. The combat missions really demonstrate just how much your students learn in your university. They go from being hopelessly feeble to becoming a mighty team of wizards who can annihilate anything. This lets you feel the teacher-graduate pride that is very unique to this game.I am honestly surprised there are no copies of this game yet !There are defiantly some learning curves, as the early game is very important for each university you set up. My main criticism is that there is a tendency just to create a giant ever expanding upward block of a university, but the structure isn't the main character of the game. Aside from that, like Harry Potter - the culture of magic and the buildings is pure medieval Europe - despite being set in places such as a desert or a floating turtle. It would be nice to see it adapt !Great game and I hope the developer adds DLC to this game. Alternatively makes another great management game like this !

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok as a clicker-like casual game. I didn't feel much control over whatever is happening, both due to a lot of different counteractive elements at play that mostly average out and because of the sheer number of rooms, teachers, students and randomness, that makes going for a specific strategy unreliable. Didn't feel particularly attached to students or the university either since there is a lot of them and not much personality to them. Game also sometimes lags hard when you have a lot of students and zoom out, but a reload helps and it didn't happen too often. Alt+Tab switching broke the game a few times (it didn't want to return as a top window and had to be reloaded with losing progress), but it only happened if I did it for a long time and didn't pause before. Otherwise, it runs ok.While you need to make decisions often, I didn't find most of them particularly important, at least on the default difficulty. There are quite a few positive and negative perks that your university, students and teachers can have, but they are tedious and hard to stack and use to your advantage and can be ignored on average. For example, it rarely matters if your teacher reduces students' boredom or hunger and every positive trait is usually compensated by some negative one. I ended up paying attentions to a handful of perks that I found impactful and largely ignored the rest. Replayability is technically there, but despite there being 5 different types of magic, specializing in a different set doesn't actually matter that much. And you can usually get several types at once. The game is divided into more or less timed levels (you can make the timer go back with certain mechanics, potentially prolonging it indefinitely or at least quite a bunch, but I used it only once during the campaign) with some objectives to complete, bonuses and debuffs carrying over to the next campaign levels and each level restarts with a new university.Overall, a pretty relaxing game with a few bugs, some decision making and some flavor. If you don't expect much from it, you will probably be satisfied. There is some replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really made me feel like I was a headmaster of a magical school whilst fighting off the existential dread of my life's work's inevitable demise. I smiled, I laughed, I stressed, and I played more because it was so addictive and too adorable to ignore. If you love the whimsical, magical feel of Harry Potter's Hogwarts and wouldn't mind running such a magical school yourself, this is the game for you! In-depth game-play that is detailed, addictive, and charming. Build classrooms, fund tuition, and admit students as you see fit between two or more guilds. You can attempt a branching campaign, set your own challenges, or play in an endless mode that allows you to build your school without limit. Each level forces you to start over with a few bonuses and challenges carrying over. There is no way to undo anything that you decide without starting from the beginning. Repetitive level design with only slight variations in theme and challenge.  Is it worth the asking price? I would say it definitely is, and even more so if the game continues to release updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially I enjoyed the game quite a bit. It's open enough that it allows micromanagement for min-max players, but casual enough that you can auto-pilot at standard difficulties and still have a decent run. That said....I only recommend the game if you can get it on sale. I found it fun for the first ~50-75 hours, and then it quickly falls off after the 100 hour mark. (If that's all you're looking for, then great! Buy with confidence.) Typically for these type of games I look for frequent replayability, and ideally shoot for 1000+ hour target.The reason it starts strong, then falls off: in campaign mode you quickly realize that each level doesn't matter. It's an interesting concept... each stage before the final level has essentially two goals: (1) to get as many permanent boosts as possible (through student graduation perks), and (2) to complete the unique level quest to earn your "ally" for the final level. In fact, it's impossible to "lose" these interim stages. You could not do a thing, not even bother to build a single part of the school, and the game will fully complete the level, and allow you to progress. (Of course, since you didn't get permanent boosts or get the stage ally, it will make the last level harder). But once you realize this, it loses all tension for these interim stages. And those interim stages comprise ~90% of your play-time. So once the tension is lost, you quickly figure out the min-max combos (because why not tinker? There's nothing on the line), and once that happens you cake-walk through the game. At higher difficulties the initial levels are challenging, only because you haven't started to accumulate those permanent buffs from student graduations. But by the 2nd or 3rd level, you're back on auto-pilot, frequently with 1000s of spare mana in each school that you don't even bother to spend, since at that stage you just want to rush to the end of the level to finish it, and move on to the next stage.In conclusion: a casual player with no interest in min-maxing could likely get ~100-250 hours of fun out of the game. With even light strategic play the "fun" is exhausted in the 50-100 hour mark. If you're looking for an FTL-style game with thousands of hours of replayability, you will be disappointed.

Decided to go back and spend some time on it to actually try and get good... see if anything changed really.No, probably not worth your time. Price is fine, love the concept, but the execution is dry.Basically, this game is aggressively boring. Every obstacle you face is weak and barely affects you, only adding to an arbitrary idea of efficiency that you'll do your best to care about but have no real way of testing or obtaining data on. UI is garbage, objectives are repetitive and easy after the first few. It's a giant waste of time.Anything cool and magical happens off in the distance while you're busy worrying about taxes and if you're teachers are going to unionize. Dungeons, the only semi-worthwhile idea they had, are also repetitive and only happen once in a blue moon. By the time you have a decent dungeon party, none of the rewards are worth your time anymore.For a management sim, you have control over very little. You can't even destroy and rebuild. I repeat - basically every choice you make is permanent. You can't turn off a classroom or remove a badly placed gazebo. You can tell students to not do certain schools of magic, but can't restrict sub-schools so their learning is still all over the place. You have no control over this simulation beyond surface level concerns and initial setup.I am literally watching the simulation of a game I'd rather be playing while I repeat the same boring process over and over. So no, I don't like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Even though there is no way I would buy Spellcaster University for full price, I really had fun with the game. It's very entertaining for in between. Happy to buy it in the sale for about 5€.In the game you build a university for magicians, accept students (or not), hire teachers, expand the school, make decisions that will affect the course of the game and you will be in constant contact with other schools and populations.The game seems to be relatively simple, but it contains more complexity than one would think.It has a cute art style and is worth giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.  It has a sense of humour and provides good variety in each play through.  There is no guarantee you will do well, but the struggle is always worth it, even when you are cursing the absence of that one card you desperately need to achieve your goals!  The new additions from the April update are welcome, but I was already smitten before that.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: If you ask me, this is a little gem. I really love this game. Most things other people criticized in the Early Access have been worked on (you can now improve teachers for example, although you sometimes have to wait a while). Don't expect the combat to be your gameplay. It isn't. Building, making do with what you got and reading hilarious events is your gameplay. If you ever get bored you can speed up the game. I have not done that so far. Not one single time.And I can't stop playing.The only thing really bad about this game is it's tutorial. Which is basically a manual you have to read with some pointing arrows. And you get all the information dumped on you at once.I recommend watching a tutorial on youtube.This one is a tutorial on the full releaseI really wish I could open up my statistics or look up my teachers when I face a difficult decision. Also you should be able to close all menus with escape.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I think a lot of the negative reviews on this game have very valid points, however they all seem to be annoyed by the lack of 'control' you have within the game. The card based aspect can be frustrating, you don't always pull the card you want, but it IS a card game in that sense that you don't always pull what you want/need but you just have to make do and manage anyway.They put a lot of thought into this game, there are a load of different things to aim for with each build, you need to focus in on certain classes for your students to graduate with the future you want them to. You can adjust what each house focuses on at any time, so once you know what you need to focus on, adjust your houses to suit their chances of getting it.Things don't always go the way you want with this game but I truly enjoyed the 'lack of control' you actually get, and with that came an interesting challenge based on the control that you DO get. You do get to build you school in a way you want, you don't get to manage every little detail like many other sim based games. You have goals set near the start of each build and many are very unique, yes you don't always get them immediately and that can be frustrating but it doesn't take much to adjust as you need to.Overall, for the price (which I consider quite cheap for a game these days) and the fact its an indie company, its a very well put together game. It has its own unique set of challenges, My advice would be to play your first run and then perhaps start over again from the start with the knowledge of how the game works to improve your chances of a better campaign. Good work guys, I look forward to what you do in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Positive:Have you ever wanted to design your own magical school? This is the game for you!This is a really fun way to simulate managing a spellcasting school. Finding all the different careers your students can have, gaming the system to produce ideal students, that's all really fun.The level of depth to the systems are fantastic: levels within levels. Mastering how best to build the school to optimize the rooms, how best to recruit and manage students, how best to manage your teachers, it's all magnificent.Negative:Not as much replay value. Once you've finished a campaign once or twice there's not too much difference in each replay as you've figured it out. There are challenge modes, which might alleviate this somewhat, but has not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: First off - it's not a management game nor sim game or anything along that line. It's a pure 'random draw card ' game - much alike to how one could perceive Solitaire. Do I get the cards, I need to fulfil the objectives or do I not. You don't really have much direct influence on that at all. Even though, I do recommend the game, it's a fun little game although it's riddled with some UI issues. I doubt the longivity and replay-ability though, as the random card draw does limit any sort of strategy or planning.So if the randomness is a large put off, then stay away as it'll be frustrating to draw the same room 5 times when you really needed a specific other room.  But if you can live with the RNG, it can be a fun little distraction for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this was a Harry Potter Themed Fallout Shelter. I was Wrong! This is a Harry Potter Themed Fallout Shelter DONE RIGHT! This is everything you wished Bethesda had done and more, after playing Fallout Shelter.I hope to see Many Expansions here! This game would be wonderful Multiplayer too! What a fun little title!I hope to see more titles like this by these devs. Great Job!What a fun little title! Don't miss out...
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but not exactly what I was expecting. There is some room for improvement but nevertheless I enjoyed playing. I guess I was longing for a bit more personal connection to those going to your university and more storytelling of their lives, but it ends up being rather impersonal. Students don't really interact with each other in significant ways other than giving different buffs when nearby. You will also cycle through so many students and teachers that you won't feel much attachment to them. As far as just being a manager game though, I found it pretty fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: I would easily recommend it for fans of magic, fantasy, Harry Potter, and sim/management games. Plays a lot like a Harry Potter themed Fallout Shelter, which is another game I would recommend, but I enjoyed this one even more. +Art style+Variety of magical schools+Tons of customization+Create your own student 'houses' with different themes/effects+Variety of random events keep things interesting+Good pacing, variety of game/difficulty options-Doom counter-Some rooms are too limited on placement-Creating new houses is unreliable/limited-Some items/bonuses are lackluster or ineffective-Battles/invasions can sometimes go unnoticed
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good and very hard to put down.The main mechanic of having to rebuild, but keeping the benefit from the student you produced works perfectly. At first it looks silly, that something gets 1% better, but after 20 such student are produced it is felt, and at the end of the run, you can have a very strong platform, ...  like education in real life :-)Inside each stage the game is also rewarding in letting you feel the benefits of your decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: The game freezes within serveral minutes of launch. Doesn't matter what you do - start the game, stay in main menu, mess with settings - it just freezes and has to be closed through task manager.Unfortunately, I haven't tried it within the first 2 weeks and cannot refund it despite not being able to actually play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Very good Hogwarts simulator, you get to decide what kind of magics you teach, create and name student houses, delve dungeons with your students, etc. You can set up an endless game and just run your school through the years at a laid back pace. it will lag on the largest maps though, be warned, but you can choose small medium large etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Avoid for now. I will change this review later when the game is "fixed"If it is not a bug, it is definitely not a feature. I would probably tolerate this if the game just came out as early access but it has been in early access for 6 months, these are obvious issues that need to be addressed.I really enjoyed this game and I want to play it more but I could not anymore because of the bugs and the terrible UI. WAY TOO MANY BUGS.1- (Where is my bed?) The cards are random, which is fine but then you run into where is the dorms card this map? Which is fine if the following bug did not exist. Students are running back and fourth on the hallway to the portal outside because there is no vacant bed, oh look there is a bed, oh wait it is gone, oh wait there it is again. Like the AI needs A LOT of work, it is ridiculous. Some students spend 3 years in the university and learn nothing because they can't figure out if they need to go to university's bed or home's bed. You feel stuck whether to charge students for beds to make money to roll (and pray to RNGod) for a dormitory or private room and make the problem worse OR just hold tight and keep it free until the next map or get graduates that give money.2- (It is not my problem) Teachers will not put out fire or close portals, instead will just stand there and teach to no one while his students run away and wait for ANOTHER staff to do the job. I have had issues where staff will run around in circles and not put out fire (or close portal) but a quick save reload fixes the issue once I see it.3- (UI and Tutorial)  Number of total students and staff is missing from the game's UI. Can I see the houses I made along with current students? NO YOU ARE STUCK AT CHOOSING NEW STUDENTS, SO CHOOSE. The stats tab needs a lot of work. The lens on the side do not give clear picture. 12 percent red looks like 0 percent red, also looks like 25 percent red. The campaign is really vague and you don't know what to expect until the third map. Tutorial was fine but a lot of tool-tips are not helpful like "he moves faster" or "you lose prestige but you gain gold". The game is a bit colorless, you have to memorize what things are or just read over and over again. The devs, for example. can just add color red for shadow traits and blue for alch traits when students register. 4- (Strategy) When you hire a teacher, you are given two options. That is it. You cannot fire the one you chose later, you cannot decline both. Did I not say? You cannot fire students either. There is way too many things to consider like good teacher have to go with good student not evil ones. The bully students are not good with sensitive students. Chatty students make other students' study worse. Stupid students are a waste of university resources. Poor students don't give the university much money. ALL OF THIS will be fine if there was a good way to organize it. Alas, with the current AI, it is really hard to make a judgement if this student could be good in one of the houses or not. 5- (What a waste!) Planning stuff at early game is crazy because you go for alchemy house but you don't find an alchemy room. You are kinda forced to play in a specific way which is not fun in this type of games. Potion making is just not worth it at all unless you get all the components required for a good potion, otherwise you just wasted a lot of cards on useless components that make useless potions. Oh wait, I found the components that changes everything but it is too late, the map is about to end.The list goes on and on.Edit: 3 years later, game is released. Some issues are fixed, other were not. No new content was added since. Extremely disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, but no endgame as of now.pros :-build your own academy of wizards-looks cute-individual students developmentcons:-The combat system is a joke for some reason, it's like one of those hands-off tower defense flash games from the 2000s.(except it's all bad without anything good about it)-The years are passing too fast without any option to change it. (5minutes=1year XD) A great game if you want to build your own wizard academy but nothing else.It's in early access and has a lot of potential, I recommend it if you have an itch for a "harry potter tycoon" game.edit : the replay value isn't really there. I don't feel like playing it again, damn it...
_childDocuments_.name: Spellcaster University

_childDocuments_.review: Develop a prestigious university of mages. Build rooms, train your students, fight orcs, slay the bureaucrats, manage your budget... a director's life is not a quiet one.

name: The Survivalists
detailed_description: The island is alive! Your newfound home will change with day/night cycles as you explore and uncover its secrets. Hunt (or be hunted by!) animals for food and an array of mythical enemies, who aren’t necessarily pleased to see you. Get quests from a Mysterious Stranger or find them washed up on the shore. Prepare to trek into a procedurally generated wilderness, with a variety of biomes, for an adventure that’s unique to every player. Finding the perils of island life too much or just looking to share your building expertise with friends? The Survivalists has you covered! Complete joint adventures, gain loot, trade and ultimately survive together and as you and up to three fellow castaways explore fantastical islands. If you’re in need of a builder, a lumberjack or even a soldier, the monkeys on the island can be tamed and trained to help you with everyday tasks or back you up on raids to a fanatic camp! The Mimic System means a wide variety of functions can be performed by your cheeky new friends, with monkey management becoming key to surviving the island’s challenges. The secret to survival is to make the most of the resources around you. Whether that’s piecing together a primitive axe to chop wood or mixing up a refreshing fruit smoothie to keep the hunger at bay, you can discover recipes and expand your options across food, item or structure crafting trees. Looking for an epic sword to hang on your hut wall or want to lay waste to encroaching hostiles? What you seek could be in one of the many temples scattered around the island. However, getting your hands on the loot won’t be easy so any would-be raiders will need to prepare for their treasure hunting escapades.
