Explore, build, craft and even train monkeys with up to three friends in a desperate bid to survive. Have you got what it takes to be a Survivalist?

_childDocuments_.review: Survivalists definitely felt like a survival type genre game IN early access but it is not. I spent my time exploring my very small island and going through tutorial quests to better understand the monkey macro. I was only given one monkey so it almost felt pointless to teach the one for every little task as it was easier for me to do them myself. I filled out my craft tables and their recipes to the point I was able to make the raft and sail. This is where I stopped playing as I really wanted to explore a new island much sooner than this point. I would have kept my joy in playing if the sail was something as easy as the raft to reach. The monkey tutorials were great in explaining and the music was soothing. I may come back to the game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: Got this on sale for me and my buds and it was.... meh, kinda ok tbh, the MONKE gameplay is fun and it's rly funny seeing ur bud running around with 9 monkeys all armed with Spiked Iron Clubs clubbing FILTHY ORC PEASANTS to oblivion, but everything else was pretty boring. The progression and material collecting were both tedious and while you have a ♥♥♥♥ load of crafting options and a few walls and floors to build, they are all so time consuming and material expensive that it's just not worth it.Overall i wouldn't rly recommend it outside of a sale and/or if u have some retarded friends to play with u.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: Unique indie survival game, a bit of Don't Starve Together, a bit of Terraria, graphics reminds me of Ragnarok Online, music is amazing in a loop like Stardew Valley, 1. Great music2. Chill / Casual gameplay3. Basics to a good survival game. hunger, health, healing, simple combat4. Early development so no max upgrading to HP, Stamina, Stamina deduction cost5. Has plenty to explore both in and out6. Plenty to gather & flexibility on building bases7. Realistic, you're a survivor, so there's not much materials to build yourself "armor"     even though there's a material that can create pretty good weapons and armor      in the future. Along with a backpack in someway. Great game overall, 100-120 hours in. ~ sadly game is abandoned.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: I had originally bought this game back when it came out. Pre-ordered it actually.I then completely forgot about it and never played it again. This game sat waiting for me just under two years. With all the updates, changes, and more, this game was nothing like I remembered, and I enjoyed what they started with.Have had nothing but fun playing this game, great experience, I love the soundtrack, actually bought it.Highly Recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: This game does have potential but after about getting in 4 hours in you have kind of seen it all the game feels like it lacks content and some game mechanics can be annoying to deal with especially monkeys the combat can be enjoyable at some points but lame in other aspects like with the bow with mouse and keyboard where you have to make sure your character is facing the right direction then aim and fire makes it kind of slow in my opinion playing the game in the beginning is fun but once you have your base and food is no longer a issue the game kinda halts and at that point you either wanna build a village of your design or you wanna explore and that is really what is left on the table the price I personally feel is way too high for what this game is and I enjoy building but the fact that even simple things like rotating is not in the game makes building very basic plus I was under the impression that in single player you could find other survivors to add to your village but from what I have seen it is only monkeys unless you are playing multiplayer plus looting for legendary gear and weapons do not have much of a purpose in the game give clubs to 4 or 5 monkeys and they will destroy anything. I would say wait to see if the devs figure out how to make the game  a longer experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: The game is funnier than I expected. Explore islands, collect resources, hunt, kill enemies and explore caves and labyrinths as you learn more and more new recipes. The selection of craftable items is quite nice and most items can be learned relatively quickly (except for gold recipes and other small items, which become necessary later in the game).Probably the best thing (and the thing that makes the game unique) is to let the monkeys work for you. They can farm resources, carry resources from crates or create recipes for you. Train them so that they can also fight for you.The pixel art style is well done.A really nice game to play occasionally with a couple of friends.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to playing this game, my friend recommended it to me and I played other games coming from Team17 (Escapists franchise n stuff). If you are planning to buy this game, get it on a sale, otherwise its not worth it. I spent so much time grinding to get a 100% on this game (I'm missing multiplayer achievements and one other really hard achievement), and It feels like its still early access.There are many bugs, minor ones like simple animations and sound bugs, some annoying bugs, like monkeys not following you even though it says they are, and also weird bugs like unbreakable chests that just hang around and furnaces that never run out. The monkey concept is very nice but there should definitely be more features added to them, the combat and AI of the monkeys need to be adjusted. Example: Monkeys that hold weapons just aggro directly onto hostile animals and it can get annoying when you have an 8 man monkey squad and while walking one suddenly aggros on to a pig and gets knocked out and then everyone else follows, its tedious to un-equip every monkey and re-equip them or just fight every single animal you come across. Survivalists is originally an xbox game (If i remember correctly) and you will notice that you can't rotate things in the game which very slightly makes some of the building look triggering. get ready to mash space a lot since you pick up things one at a time and they only stack when you drop them all together since there is no auto stacking mechanic when things are nearby (this is sad most especially for when you make monkeys craft a ton of items). trading and currency system feels lacking, (selling is pretty sad). It is really repetative and is still lacking in content to make the game more interesting (lore is the only story mechanic you have and trying to leave).Now are these things super bad? well not really, honestly I can cope with them they are just really annoying, don't get me wrong I still enjoyed my time playing but for its price I really think there should be more quality of life updates and bug fixing especially since it is out of early access.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game to come out for a while now and finally picked it up today, I find that the Monkey Training is really finicky like selecting a monkey to train and 2 monkey get selected and you need to wait for the timer to run out and start again.  Over all I have put around 4 hours into this game and I am not enjoying myself and I feel no sense of progress.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: Idk, it's a bit boring for a survival. I understand the appeal with all the cute monkeys etc., but the start is very dragging out long for some reason. You grind your recipes to unlock new ones, then you try to collect more monkeys and all. I'm sure there is more to it, but I think it isn't worth my time, when there are more appealing survival games out there for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: If you like survival games to also play with friends, this is a good game I would mainly recommend due to its creativity and survival techniques. You can build and research so many things to help you survive e.g. a forge that also allows you to build many crafting recipes. Things in this game like raids from other goblins, animals to kill for loot to craft and eat, upgrades in weaponry and tools, huge map and mysteries, monkeys to help you with things like crafting, fighting, gathering, mining materials like wood or stone and much more is what makes this game amazing. A recommendation I would give for this game currently is to have the ability to rotate blueprints before placing them for a better experience (at least that i don't know of).
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: It's great for both single-player and multi-player (although I'm heavily biased towards the multi-player function cuz games are more fun with friends). The fact that no game map/world is the same is also pleasant, as you can have a new experience with each map/world.The only minor inconvenience I've found (at least for myself) is that certain treasure maps aren't specific on where treasures might be buried in different parts of the map (i.e. the lightweight pickaxe in a Tanglewood camp, I've been to 2 camps in the wood and still no pickaxe). That's just a personal gripe, though. It is fun just exploring and trying to find treasures.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like the game. A lot of the reviews talk about lack of content. For me, I had no problem with content. After 9 hours in, I still hadn't unlocked a lot of crafting and had only been to 1 other island. So that wasn't really an issue for me, and in fact, I was looking forward to all the other stuff, had it not been for...The mechanics of the game - I like the idea of the monkeys, but it is SO cumbersome the way you have to keep teaching them each time you switch them from another task, for instance, combat to then crafting. But what is worse is that when you have a bunch of monkeys, and only want to train one, it's really hard to click on just one (they all come to you at once, and you have to click quickly otherwise all of them go out of say, combat mode, and go into teaching mode. Then you have to retrain the others again. When playing multiplayer this just got worse with you and your partner's monkeys swarming together. Also, it was difficult to see what weapon or equipment each monkey had. Yes, you can look in a main tab to see the lists of monkeys, but  it's hard to identify which monkey is which (without color coding each one , etc). Lastly, there is a severe lack of inventory space on your character given how much material you had and what was required for crafting. It would be great to have larger inventory space you can work toward or unlock somehow. I found myself constantly moving between different storage chests to get one resource, then having to switch out or drop say my axe, just to make room for the resource I needed. I know you can use monkeys to hold chests for extra inventory, but it's cumbersome. Anyway, it just felt like so much work at the end of the day. It seems like a cool game, and I hope it gets updated! I might then give it another play, but right now, I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: It was pretty fun to play through this game. Setting up all your monkeys to automate all the crafting and building is quite satisfying. Leading an army of monkey warriors is also quite enjoyable (although you do constantly need to replace their weapons, which can be somewhat annoying).The game isn't perfect though. There isn't that much to do. After a handful of hours you'll probably already have unlocked and crafted most of the crafting recipes. It's not particularly challenging either, as having a couple of warrior monkeys following you around trivialises combat. The only exception is one specific room in the labyrinths with a bunch of archers shooting you from across a gap that neither you nor your monkeys can cross without building floors first, which is a massive pain but ultimately still not really difficult if you're carrying around a large stack of meat kebabs like I was.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: The ambiance is very chill and it's a pleasure to play, but the more you play, the more you can feel the lack of content.Many things you can build in the game are useless and you can focus to basic: upgrade weapon & tools => go to next island => clear main dungeon.The endgame is not fun, mostly fetch quests either to farm npc's or to access to the ending.It's very sad to see all of the potential this game have, because even if it's barebones it's really fun.But it will never be completed since the devs dropped it. The end was very disapointing. It was worth playing still, but get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this in co-op had been fun, until the game got out of sync (or something), we had to force-quit it, and then our game/save was corrupted.  Not just back to our previous save, but completely GONE.  I would have decided "♥♥♥♥ this game" and uninstalled, but my co-op friend did a new world and rushed progress and put teleporters up, so it made catching up to where we had been before very easy.   So we gave it another go, with backups of the save data.....but even though we were careful, it never did corrupt a 2nd time.  Corruption aside, it's also not very polished or intuitive or have a good UI.  Another issue with saving: If you exit, it doesn't prompt you to save. If you neglect to explicitly save prior to quitting, all that progress is lost, with no warning.  So as you can see above, you'd better be damn careful with your data, and that's why I've left it as a downvote.  The GAMEPLAY though, is pretty fun.  Start as a bum on a beach, and craft and fight and loot your way up through technology and islands and quests up to repairing a shipwrecked Galleon at the end of the game, to escape to....wherever. I did most of the stuff in the game, and got most of the achievements, didn't care to chase the others down, but none are especially difficult.  TL;DR: be very careful with your save data at all times.  Fun game, but buggy and unfinished feeling in a lot of areas.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: Nice fun game.  Other Devs might learn a thing or two regarding the design of this game.1) Easy game play.  The controls are really simple and easy to master.2) Sounds and graphics are really good.  Very nice art3) Great concept.  There are actual goals to play and follow.  You have the opportunity to host your own survivalist and play with your friends.  There is more to do once you finish the goals.  I had fun.  Certainly worth a second play around.  I like the lores and story.  I highly recommend buying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: So I got my hands on the Experimental branch and I must say the game is a lot better than before, they made it a little bit more grindy but the monkeys solve this.I must say I'm surprised how much things they've actually improved: monkeys, backpack, new structures, raid rework, collect all items around you with space, some new structure mechanics(floor placement), completely new cosmetic structures, weapon repair station, new animals and beastsAnd the best thing is they keep updating the game, the farming update for example. I am glad they help the community and keep improving the game, awesome devs. I give 9/10, it's almost worth the price now.----OLD REVIEW-------------------------------------Overall a good game so far, I was hyped before the release and I loved the demo, however I was disappointed by lack of content. The devs are very active tho, friendly, and they're trying their best to make this game awesome. _childDocuments_.review: While it looks very interesting and the concept does sound fun, unfortunately the content is very much lacking.The first (experimental) patch did fix some bugs and quality of life issues, but there remains far too many issues that ruin the experience.Loading up a save game I found all my monkeys that were trained for attacking had forgotten their role. Later after a raid (which I have no way to possibly get back in time to assist with), I can see that while my defences worked, all my monkeys no longer had any roles assigned.Assigning monkeys to specific roles as well as the user interface is somewhat lacking. It is rather annoying and the button prompts always assume an Xbox controller layout.The first part to the game is very confusing to learn, such as:*where to get more metal*how to find the shop again*how to open chestsThe biggest issue I had was all the objects blocking my path. One must spend time either finding tiny gaps that cannot be seen, or a long time breaking rocks and chopping trees. This is made even worse when you have monkeys carrying chests that count as solid objects.My 2nd biggest issue was monkeys would sometimes wander far from home, after you spend a short time on another part of the map, leaving you to have to fix it for every monkey every time you return. Followers would also forget that they are supposed to follow, after being attacked (which they cannot be told to ignore or run from).It is worth noting that there is a lack of being able to save anywhere. You always have to return to your bed to save, which can take minutes of walking/navigating. This is even worse if you are the middle of something important, such as using a timed buff or inside a temple.You will find yourself running out of things to do fast, while just repeating the same thing over and over for the same reward (with a different name/image).I could easily have overlooked all the issues if the game were in early access, or a beta version.Update: some bugs have been fixed, but content is still quite lacking and repetitive.l

_childDocuments_.review: A C-grade survival game with F-grade implementation. Practically an unfinished beta being sold for $25.To elaborate:-UI is clunky or loves to work only half the time.-Most progression is front-loaded to the first two islands.-The fifth island is literally a combination of the third and fourth island biomes.-Island hazards don't work, making the items to traverse them safely worthless.-Puzzles are really easy, boiling down to "do you have enough monkeys to press these buttons?"-Very few enemies, a good chunk of which are reskins.-"Bosses" are upsized enemies with more HP.-Taskmasters are banal busywork. They shouldn't be relegated to 1 per island, especially because some like the Salesman have tasks designed for early game despite being on the last island. They also unlock the best tools in the game.-Task Tokens are finite, but the Mysterious Stranger can sell already-learned blueprints, wasting tokens and locking you out of other items.-Most pets and trinkets do too little for how much effort it takes to get them, save for ones like Harvest.-Blood moons happen far too often. They renew resources so that's fine, but each one summons a raid on the player that is usually too easy to matter and is just a waste of time.-Monkeys can get stuck out-of-bounds or otherwise stop listening to you, requiring use of a summoning banana to un-bork them.-Monkey work range is annoyingly small, especially for base work. They can be told to chop trees, then stop and say "No more trees!" when there are ten right next to them.-Food system is baffling with how useless most of them are. High-end items are usually overshadowed by cheap food (e.g. meat pasties), especially since you can spam food to heal.-Base building is exceedingly tedious. I spent a lot of time collecting resources for it even during lategame.-Teleporters sometimes refuse to bring your monkeys with you. Get ready to waste charges over this.-Multiplayer progression is tied to the host. You want to bring more monkeys or craft trinkets? Play solo.-YMMV on this, but the ending disappointed me for the effort it took to get there.-The last update was in June 2021, meaning the current broken state of the game is A-OK by the devs nearly 2 years later.Monkey automation is the one neat idea this game has and the artstyle is pretty good, but cool ideas and decent graphics do not a fun game make.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a star rating system instead of a yes or no because I had a lot of trouble deciding whether or not to recommend this game. At a lower price point, I probably would've hit the yes button, but this game is currently priced at $24.99 and I only played for 43 hours before becoming way too frustrated with the tedium. In contrast, I paid ten bucks for Terraria and have hundreds of played hours in that game and continue to play it today.I'll start with the positives. The gameplay is fun, the graphics are cute and it was interesting to unlock each level of crafting. The game world seems vast and is fun to explore. It felt a lot like a cute version of Valheim. Playing with others is easy and fun and I had no issues being able to easily connect with them. This game has a lot of potential and for the first 20 hours or so, I could not stop playing, which is why it was so disappointing that the tedium seemed to increase the further along you get into the game. For instance, once you get to sharpened weapons, you have to craft multiple pieces (3-4), each with their own crafting times before you can even repair your weapon, rather than it using just one raw material to decrease the tedium as a lot of games do. If you lack the necessary resources in your inventory for crafting those pieces, you can easily waste an entire in-game day just repairing your weapon. I appreciate that they tried to decrease the tedium by allowing the monkeys to craft things for you, but that entire process has been implemented poorly and its more of a hassle than it is worth to get them to do anything for you. The food system is tedious and requires way too many ingredients. I get that it is a survival game, but when you add the lengthy crafting time to the fact that each recipe requires 2-3 of multiple ingredients, it's too much. I would have loved to recommend this game and at $5-10 I would have. But for me, a game that only gave me 40 or so hours worth of fun just isn't worth $25.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game.Graphics are cute and welcoming. Sounds and music too.Game mechanics (combat, crafting, exploration, etc...) are simple and easy to pick up.There is automation in this game, done through the monkeys. They can mimic what you do, so after a while you will have a bunch of them doing small, specialized tasks, like harvesting, storing items, and mainly crafting.The (optional) base building is a little resource intensive. _childDocuments_.review: It's a relaxed way to pass the time.You know the drill: hit trees, hit rocks, hit grass, hit animals, and use the resulting harvest to build stuff, which unlocks more stuff to build.Surviving is easy, and death hardly a penalty: you drop you stuff, but that can be retrieved easily, since it isn't hard to escape enemy encounters.Unique selling point is the 'automation' by training monkeys, but that is rather limited. Still, the training itself is easy to do, and it was nice to have one monkey doing all the crafting that I queued up, with another delivering the materials to him and a third storing the resulting crafted item.When I got to the third island I had the feeling that I had seen everything there was to see. I didn't want to build yet another base on a new island, with slightly more powerful enemies, slightly better materials and slightly more uncomfortable surroundings. But up to that moment, I had fun exploring the game world and its mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: The Survivalists is a fun open world adventure game with 5 islands to explore. The artstyle is pleasing to the eyes and the soundtrack fits the relaxing gameplay. Each island has its own monsters, caves and labyrinths. You mainly build a base and gain resources for quests to escape the Sea. The game is unique in that you can command monkeys to do literally ANYTHING for you. The monkeys can fight, craft or even collect resources and mimic your actions. However, the combat movement felt clunky and took me some time to get used to it, although I still did make do with it. This game is still fun and I got addicted to it for awhile. The Survivalists can be quite repetitive and may even feel like a fetch quest simulator at one point, but I still had my fun trying to explore and craft to unlock more items. Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to other top down survival games, such as Don't Starve, in terms of crafting, eating, combat and well... Surviving. It is a much more forgiving, easy to learn experience than many others of the genre. Biggest reason to play is exploration and crafting. For combat enthusiasts, the enemy units so far have the same style of combat. (Almost no damage if hit from the front. Damage needs to be done on the side or rear of the enemy. The enemies tend to charge leaving themselves open... a lot.) In other words it doesn't have a large variety of attacks and you might get bored. Overall the game is more casual than most survival games. So if you are looking for a tough challenge you may want to look somewhere else. If you are looking for a simple base builder for you and your friends, it just might be for you. I'm looking forward to see what the developers could add down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: The game glitched while I was at sea and I couldn't move my boat.  Couldn't sleep to save, so I lost an entire play session worth of progress.Gamebreaking bugs aside, the game is fun-ish, but it requires many, many QOL improvements before it can truly be an immersive experience.  As one example, the act of cooking is an extremely cumbersome mess.  "Choose recipe" and "add ingredients to recipe" are two separate actions.  The game prompts you with "press X to equip cooking tool", but then outright refuses to equip it unless your cursor is over it.  It shouldn't even be necessary to equip it -  having it in your inventory should be sufficient.Speaking of immersion and the inventory, this game is such an inventory management sim that it really takes you out of it.  Each mob / resource on average drops 3 items.  You have 11 slots in your inventory and no way to increase the size.  If you bring a few tools and food items with you, you reach the space limit VERY quickly.As another example where QOL is much needed, unlocking a treasure map puts the map at the bottom of the list of all maps.  So enjoy scrolling past 50 useless maps just to discover, "Oh hey, this one is useless too."  New maps should instantly be placed at the top, and instead of having a popup saying "New map discovered", it should say "New map for XXX item", so you don't have to waste time opening a menu to see what it's about.I want to love this game.  The graphics are extremely cute, and despite the hassle of all the menu and inventory management, despite the hassle of basing a million times per session - this is a fun exploration / building game.  But the game simply wasn't designed well, and there are games out there that do the same thing, but better.Oh yeah, they also ripped off the blood moon mechanic from BOTW.  The game has a "blood moon", and it does the same exact thing as BOTW.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for December 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before January 4th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A Survival game done in The Escapists style. The Survivalists starts like any survival game, you wake up abandoned on an island and start farming minor items to build axes, shovels, and clubs.  This is a common setup but the graphics and style here work well, as does the crafting system.  Players can quickly progress through their recipe chart, always able to see what they need to craft anything, and clear progression is available through the entire chart.  Basically, build the prior item to get to the next.The big addition to The Survivalists is the monkey automation, you heard right.  You use a monkey to automate mundane tasks and that adds just enough to feel fresh early on.  There’s supposed to be a good amount of content here, at least 20 hours, and a mix between standard crafting and farming for loot, as well as exploration and theoretically you should be able to eventually get off the island. Pick this up if you enjoyed the Escapists or want a solid survival game.  I’ll be honest, I didn’t like any of The Escapists, but I still enjoyed this one.   At the same time, this is a very saturated genre, and if you’re not looking for a new survival game, this might not be able to hold your interest. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: #1. High-quality pixel graphics and art style#2. Lots of crafting and gathering (if you like that kind of thing)#3. It's more fun with friends (if you have friends)#4. Emotes, avatar customizations and monkeys!Cons: #1. Obtaining certain materials is a complete RNGfest (this is by far the biggest problem)#2. The combat is painfully flawed (no lock-on, even with bows)#3. Your inventory is extremely small (which severely hampers exploring)#4. Hunger drains way too fast.#5. Some of your inventory just disappears when you die.#6. No tutorial.Overall, it's a passable open-world survival crafting game... but it's not better than ... not even close! Several things can be done to improve the game and perhaps with some time and development, The Survivalists can eventually stand shoulder-to-shoulder with great games Crashlands... but currently it's just not there. _childDocuments_.review: Normally I'm able to say what I don't like about a game with at least some degree of accuracy, but here I honestly can't come up with anything legitimate. It's just... not fun. Everything seems like it should be interesting but it's not. Maybe it's the controls. Normally you can clearly tell which control system - controller or keyboard/mouse - the game was designed for. Here it seems like it was designed for neither, as there is a movable cursor in menus when you're using a controller, but switching items on the keyboard seems to be clearly made with LB/RB in mind. Maybe the primary input device for this game is some futuristic tool that hasn't been invented yet, and the developers are secret time travellers from the future? That's my best guess.Maybe it's the trite setting. Woo, tropical island! "What did you expect, you moron?" I hear you say. Well, let me respond like this: Don't Starve's primary environment is a boring old forest, but there's a dark twist and everything is weird and exciting. Xenoblade Chronicles has you walk around your typical JRPG world, but it's on a corpse of a dead titan. Risk of Rain has a seemingly normal sci-fi alien planet setting but there's always a feeling that something's not how it seems. Point is, it's possible to make a "normal" setting interesting. Apparently here there's some pocket dimension business going on, but it might as well be just a regular boring old island.Or maybe there is this general lack of sense of direction. You can tame monkeys, but why? You can work just as well by yourself. You can make fancy recipes, but why? Normal food is just as nourishing. You can explore, but why? The resources you need are right here. Don't get me wrong, there's nothing wrong with games with no obvious objective - 7 Days to Die and The Long Dark's survival mode just ask you to not die, and Don't Starve's objective is somewhat hidden - but even then, there is some kind of compelling force. Something that makes you create your own objectives. Here I didn't feel anything of the sort - even though the game has a quest log!So there. Doing things seems pointless and unfun. That's my criticism, flimsy as it might be. That said, there's clearly a lot of game in here. Dungeons, quests, multiplayer, many unlockable blueprints... but to me, none of this matters, considering that day-to-day gameplay is just so uninteresting.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game with a friend, and frankly there isn't a ton to praise about it. I kinda like the premise of the game, but it feels like one of those games made entirely from a designer's document without any input from actual playtesting. The main mechanic, the monkeys, feel like an excuse to *not* play the game. They are extremely tedious to control, and somehow you rely on them to do things such as craft for you, because they are simply 10x faster at crafting than you are, leading you into a gameplay loop of having to file your taxes to craft a single pane of glass, every time you want to craft one.Game is rather poor at leading you, and it is very easy to get stuck thinking "what am I supposed to do now?", when the answer is to grab a raft, hope you collide with a lower skull rating island, then start tediously grinding for resources there instead to figure out how to create explosives, with crafting costs (and times) skyrocketing quite fast. Combat is also somewhat unintuitive with enemies enjoying at times full damage immunity if you attack them at certain times that, to us at least, should be just fine.As for multiplayer, it's very unfinished. Crafting recipe tree is not shared, and certain core gameplay mechanics are limited to the host only. This applies to things such as dismantling crafting benches, walls, etc, and also managing monkeys, which leads to a lot of "hey can you come over and destroy this thing I placed in the wrong spot for me?".Overall, cool idea on paper, doesn't work at all in practice. Could've benefitted a ton from playtesting and/or patching, because the core of a fun game is here, but you can't quite play it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does have insane potential. The basic gameplay loop is really engaging and monkey minion mechanic is great. However quickly after starting the game I started to see major flaws that just kept piling onto each other.The game is painfully slow. The run speed is pathetic considering the amount of exploring you have to do. You can go faster by rolling, but that takes stamina, which runs out incredibly fast so you have to wait every 5 seconds to be able to roll again. Crafting of some items takes insane amount of time, even with max level crafting monkeys and that's on top of gathering resources. It took me at least an HOUR to make my first 5x4 tile wooden house with the help of my first monkey.When stamina depletes completely, you get a screen effect that would be fine from time to time, but it gets annoying fast because you see it every 5 seconds if you try to roll to go faster. Even worse, stamina regens SLOWER if you don't use it up completely, so you will be spamming roll till you're out just to roll again faster. This rewards mindlessly roll-spamming and makes you endure the screen effects is you want to any sort of fast.Monkey minions are a great concept, but executed in the most simplistic way it can, which can lead to annoyances. Monkeys choose chests to put things in seemingly at random sometimes, so say bye to neatly organized storage. If there was a solid way to influence where they put things, then it had to be buried in text tutorials because I sure didn't figure it out during gameplay. You can't tell them to craft only a certain amount, so if you make a monkey chain of "bring-craft-take back to chest", they WILL end up wasting resources by crafting too much if you leave them without strict supervision. They will also use tools till they break, wasting MORE resources to craft them new ones instead of repairing, unless you micromanage them like crazy to take tools from them for repairs at the right time. If you tell a monkey to plant seeds, it won't have any consideration for what to plant where either, so no efficient automated farm either.Resources are overabundant to a point of clogging your inventory in seconds, but amount to so little when you'll start crafting. 6 pebbles for a stone chunk, 2 stone chunks and one mud for a stone slab, 3 stone slabs and 3 mud for a stone wall. 36 pebbles and 6 mud for just ONE stone wall. More than one third of a stack for just ONE tile of wall placed.Let's have a list of flaws that don't have whole paragraphs worth of commentary before I get to another big one:-animal taming seems pointless since you can easily just go and kill things for loot without the need to tame, transport and craft breeding feeds;-hunger feels pointless because food is overabundant to a point of meat and fruit items only clogging your inventory and having to be constantly discarded to make space for more important things;-raids are a pointless annoyance. The game advises you to build up defenses, but that only makes the raid bigger, so the best defense against them is just going out of the base so no more than three enemies spawn. With teleporters you can also go to an easier island to oneshot them on top of it in later game;-burning in volcanic biomes and insect swarm in swamp biome debuffs literally don't do anything other than a screen effect and having your character constantly talk in how much pain they are in despite no loss of health nor stamina. Might be a bug, but that's how it was for all of the time of my playthrough, so wasn't patched fast either;-traders and their fetchquests are boring and a pure grind and rng, so is finding the lore entries;-bosses are just normal enemies but slightly bigger with more hp;Now, the last thing that completely ruins this game - progression and balancing. Or rather lack of either. The feel I got was that game expects you to go out and explore islands one by one and move your base from island to island, going up the tiers of buildings and equipment till you reach the finial island and beaten every temple. However that was not my experience at all as the game doesn't do anything to enforce that progression path, and it resulted for balance to completely vanish for me.I stayed on the starting island without venturing out because there was no push for it. I kept (painfully slowly) building up my base till I was stone tier because I liked the looks and the game kept telling me to build up my defenses, so I did. However I wanted to craft things that needed metal that just wasn't on the starting island and that was what finally pushed me to get on a raft and (painfully slowly) start swimming out.First island I landed on was the final, hardest one. I thought that harder island = more resources, so I went out to explore and found out that this island had no iron on it, but gold I couldn't mine. I could kill that sparkly fox though, so I (painfully slowly with my dingy bone clubs) did. It exploded into resources, gold among them. I went around, killed a few more foxes, sailed back home when I had a good chunk of stuff that I couldn't do anything with yet. I found the second island after that and got myself iron, but since I had gold from the foxes at that point, I managed to immediately jump over the tier of metal sword and made the gold one right after unlocking. I've barely explored anything past the first island at that point and I've already had an endgame sword in my hands. Progression went out the window at that point cause combat stopped being any challenge and I killed everything effortlessly even though I didn't even bring monkeys anywhere, leaving them to work at the base. Temples were a joke because I demolished enemies.So after getting the gold sword, the game turned into "run a lot" and "grind resources". Trinkets were useless because I've already beaten everything. Trader quests were a chore since they were either boring fetchquets, or asked me to do redundant things like building a straw house when I had a fully decked stone tier base.All of those flaws are sadly decorated with a bitter cherry on top that is a disappointing lack of content. Every island has only two mini dungeons and after the first island and breaking balance and progression, I didn't even explore them because I had no need for any loot that could've been in them. That made the islands not worth exploring cause there wasn't anything on them save for loot corpses that had useless sellable trinkets that I kept having to throw out (you can make more money and faster by farming resources and selling those). There is an underwhelming amount of enemy types, most of them are reskins with buffed stats, like three types of boar or big cat that are exactly the same same for hp, damage and sprite. Like I said before, there aren't even bosses, just bigger, beefier versions of normal animal enemies with the same behavior. All went down in 10 seconds or less thanks for my gamebreaking sharpened gold sword. There are barely any decorative things to build with so you can't even make anything pretty.Overall, this is a game that managed to keep me engaged, but only because I'm a very specific type of person that found it an interesting experience to analyze and think how it could've been done better. It feels like an early access game, a proof of concept, a foundation upon which a better game should only start being built. It by any means doesn't feel like a full product. If you're like me and can get something out of a game that's such an unrealized potential, then get it when it'll be like 70-80% off, no more. Otherwise it sadly isn't worth price nor time, especially since it's not being updated anymore as devs left it to work on something else instead of expanding and polishing what they have done here.

_childDocuments_.review: #83  The Survivalists1st impressions:  Its a Don't Starve Clone done in the fashion of the Escapists.  At my 1st play, the game seems clunky, almost like the character is being weighed down, and slow.  40 minutes was all i could really play, because it felt really bogged down.  My second session seemed to go a bit better, the controls seemed a bit more intuitive, but still clunky.  It lasted a bit under 2 hours and it gave me the time to explore the island and craft more things.  My major complaint...the crafting is uninspired and it really is bogged down.  Example:  When crafting you can choose to make a lot of one item, or just make one.  The problem, whether you choose a little or a lot, you still have to load the tool after every item you make, but the tool automatically selects the last item you made, making the option to build a lot completely useless.  Another issue, the monkeys.  Neat idea, but they never really tell you how to use them.  When you want a monkey to build something you have to select the monkey, hold the button down for the action you want them use and wait for the circle to expand over you and them.  Its a little thing, but as many developers know, when all the little things add up it can sink a ship.All in all, its not a bad game.  The graphics are sharp, animated in the Escapists method, and very colorful.  The sound is ok, its not grating, but its not spectacular either.  I haven't tried the multiplayer yet, it seems like it could be fun, but i don't know for sure.  A lot of people that have played Don't Starve, and Don't Starve Together are going to find a much better experience there.  But a beginner to the genre could have some fun here.  I'll keep playing, but nowhere near as much DS and DST.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into crafting games and the zen of building up from nothing to something, this will be right up your alley. I think of it as  like a "Stardew Valley", but instead of a homesteading setting, it's a survival-on-a-deserted-island setting.I found it especially interesting that it doesn't use typical RPG elements like leveling up to unlock things. Rather, nothing changes about your character, but the items you craft expand your library of things you can craft, and in turn allow you to get better results to make your character better.The game throws you a bone by allowing you to command monkeys to automate tasks like fending off bad guys or crafting things that take too long on your own while you do other things. It's tricky at first but you get the hang of it as you go.The game was well built, there's a lot of love in it, I have no complaints. The only things I would change are character customizations (Stardew Valley offered a little more, like making your own hats and clothes), expanding the library of crafting recipes (there's only one type of bow for example, maybe a different type could have faster flying arrows), and being a survival-based game, could use a mode where you have more stats to maintain your survival, like getting proper sleep for your stamina, staying hydrated, not getting sick (the game only has you worry about hunger which gets easily solved with the ton of meat you get through the game).

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game is fun, progression system is enjoyable, and has a promising future if devs continue working on it. _childDocuments_.review: I really did want to like this game, but I found the grind to be more of a slog to go through then is even remotely comfortable for me, even after building up to higher value structures and objects it is still a painful slog of a grind, if not worse. The monkeys are horribly inefficient laborers as they only do one action continuously for as long as they have the tool and/or resources required of it, which they will not search for, meaning you practically have to babysit them, with the work stations requiring a minimum of 3 monkeys to operate on its own; one to load ONE of the resources for the station, one to craft the object or structure (while they have a tool on hand), and one to carry the resulting objects to chests for clean storage. If the monkeys could be given more complex instructions, like being able to go search for available tools in the area (on the ground or in chests) after the one they are using breaks, it would be a little more manageable, but as it stands the monkeys are barely helpful outside of combat. Resources, especially wood, can be frighteningly scarce, leading to frustrations as you can't provide for all of the building jobs you have that require said resources when you need them most. Not only are you limited in resources, but you have to constantly have to worry about a hunger and stamina bar, and tools that break far to quickly to be useful in the long run, resulting in you having to make a stockpile of the resources to make a new tool to continue what you were just doing when it broke on you.TLTR; It is far to slow and clunky for me to recommend it as it stands, and sadly looks like it won't change any time soon.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks great with the graphics and musics. However, that's pretty much it.1. Inventory management is a pain: I spent roughly 50% of my play time for managing my inventory. Sure, you could have monkeys to carry however many boxes but that's too tedious. In addition, monkeys constantly drop the boxes and the boxes are getting lost. This is simply not fun.2. The game is way too easy: The title "Survivalists" is almost misleading. I've encountered so far close to zero threats when it comes to survival. Close to zero threats from hunger, climate, biomes. If you have more than 3 monkeys with weapons, combat becomes trivial. The only time I died was when I had to deal with the poor UI and monkey management controls while evading enemy attacks.3. Monkey management is so frustrating: Like others have pointed out, the idea is novel but the execution is, meh. I won't go into details but man, it is not fun. Please fix the inconvenient interface!4. Close-to-zero replayability: this is related to the fact that the game is too easy. Except the base-building (which is a pain because of the monkey management) and end-game (fixing the ship), there are not much to do after.5. Not much incentives for exploring other islands: Since there are only 3 biomes and that there's not much going on in those biomes except that there are a few new resource, monsters, and the dungeons. _childDocuments_.review: I like this game. It's kind of difficult to start off at first and I died many times when starting and learning, but you just got to learn how to play, right, a little difficulty is supposed to be there or it becomes boring. So, what I've noticed about this game, and from some other comments, is that your characters defences are quite weak, so you have to change your gameplay a little than usual rpgs. I played in other games as a pet class, where your character is kinda weak, but our pets are op and do all the fighting, so this game rly reminded me of it, and what can I say, I do quite enjoy this gameplay. And I've got some tips for those frustrated and who keep dieing, employ a ranged weapon, either a bow or a spear, to your character, and employ the monkeys with meelee weapons, and try avoid the enemies, while running around in a way that lets the monkeys stay in the battle, they kind of always follow you, so you can make use of that and lead them to target the enemies that you want. Second advice, keep your tools and food easily reachable and preferably always in the same positions in the quickbar. So when there is a fight or you need to use a tool quickly, you know where they are and can do so quickly or even automatically. Keep your quickbar organised and weapon and food should be 1 mouse scroll away. Also tools should be near the weapon as well, let's say you're mining and suddenly you got an ambush, so that you can quickly switch to your weapon. Third advice: to compensate for a lack of storage when travelling, you can carry a chest (best is large chest), or you can pass it to one of your moneys to carry, also you can place chests on your raft and make it a raft with storage. So convenient that way, and instead of having to make many trips somewhere, one trip is enough. Also, for your base, your starting base can be built in the starting clove, it's usually generated as a pretty safe location, so to not just wander endlessly, just make your first base there, later you can move to other areas or islands. I only explored islands 1 and 2 but yeah, it's a lot of fun. c:

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, but I do feel that the systems are a little clunky. This is one of those games that I enjoy, but am kind of mindless in. I don't really majorly think about any ingame decisions. Kind of like factory games (strange I know) I think about what I do but I'm not actively super hyped about it. The monkey automation system can get really annoying, as monkeys can only perform one task to varying degrees of efficiency. A monkey that grabs items can only hold one item stack at a time, meaning that they're extremely slow. Unless I'm wrong, this doesn't change (if this does change as they level up my bad). Another problem in my opinion is the fact that, automation takes atleast 3 monkeys to be efficient. If I'm trying to mass produce the stone slab like things fully automatically, I need to have a shoveller to gather dirt, then a crafter (the one who holds the multitool), a miner, a supplier, and a gatherer. You also can't set priorities for monkeys, meaning if it's some kind of gatherer, it'll just grab the nearest item, with no preference. The monkeys also don't interact with each other and work together, so they can't coordinate with each other about things. I think it would be cool if a crafter would request for certain resources and then the gatherer grabs them and then (just make the gatherer also a supplier in this case) put it on the table, then the miner mines a stone, and then brings the rocks back so that the crafter can finish the recipe. Monkeys are such a hassle to set up, I kind of wish that they could automatically learn jobs just by watching, and switch their tools. I think monkeys could work like a community that work with you and each other to help out. Of course you could tell them to do certain things, but I think this would cut down heavily on the hassle. Of course that may be unbalanced, but I'm not a professional dev, I'm just giving my input. Compared to my thoughts on the monkeys my next points will be very short. I think the combat system could be changed so it's much more skill based than luck based. I'm not exactly sure how to do this, but I can say that the escapists style combat does not work here. Maybe add a dash ability that could combine with weapons for a fast attack. Armor should be added, and I believe backpacks would also be much appreciated. Now this may sound crazy, but I haven't even said my BIGGEST gripe with this game. Items on the ground don't stack, meaning that you have it spam the space bar (or whatever your pickup key/button is) to pick up items individually. It's so time consuming and obnoxious, that I barely even pick items up because of how much of a hassle it is. With just this change, resource gathering would be 50x more fun, and something I might actually do. They should also balance recipes, as some things (mainly construction) cost way to much, and are such a hassle to get (I'm looking at you stone wall). These are most of my big complaints. All I have to say that's positive is that this game is still enjoyable. I enjoy grinding up to the boats (I barely used my monkeys), I enjoyed grabbing my first rocks, and fighting some later game mobs. This game isn't lacking in content, it's lacking in content that doesn't require a major hassle. I've gotten metals, and the such, and I can say that it's such a drag getting late game items. I feel that the game is lacking in crafting content and am hoping for more in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun monkey management simulator. In all seriousness, it's an interesting survival, crafting, automation sort of game. Well worth a play if you like that sort of thing. Game could use some patches though. Sometimes your monkeys don't come through entrances or portals with you, once I enterred a cave, monkeys stayed outside, I went out and found they had magically spread to the four corners of the island. Sometimes the portals don't register and you need to back out and try again, some of the achievements are a bit finicky... like needing to personally craft items rather than let your monkeys do it, or deliver tamed animals rather than just tame them. The stegosaurus skull is too rare a drop, the lore fragments are fun, but it could use a better system for noting which you have and haven't read, and some of them don't seem to exist on my map. Having the building questgiver be the last you find seems a poor choice given you've already built your house by then, and while it's fun to set up a monkey workshop, some quality of life improvements would be nice. Primarily, a way to tell how much of a particular resource or part you have easily, or simply a way to mark chests for certain products only. You never know where monkeys will put things. Same applies with farm plots, they'll plant whatever when you likely want diversity but can't spare three monkeys for multiple farms Would be nice if you could set up some conditional variables as well, make more of X in condition Y.I could probably go on. Still a good game at its core, but feels a bit simplistic and unrefined.

_childDocuments_.review: Game feels incomplete.  Tons of obvious quality of life improvements aren't present, the pacing is quite bad, and there's basically no end-game.  Sandbox mechanics aren't fun enough to support no end-game, given the lack of quality of life.  For instance:- Manual saves only, with no special warning if you try to exit without having saved recently.  There's a pop-up that's the same whether you saved 10 seconds or 10 hours ago.- Raids spawn a certain radius from you, meaning with a large base they'll just spawn inside your base.  Monster spawns are fixed and unstoppable (e.g. no torches like Minecraft), so there's no sensible way to secure a base besides avoiding building in those spots.- No real use for large bases anyways, as there's not enough that can be automated.  Large scale farming is unnecessary/redundant.- Monkeys put items in random chests, so you either have to do all storage yourself or live with chaotic chest contents.- Monkey management doesn't scale well.  With lots of monkeys, the screen becomes crowded and they often get in the way of performing simple actions, requiring you to time things just right to act during a clear spot.  Swapping items / exchanging chests / picking up items reuse the same key.- Many items that have only one or two uses in the game, making inventory management unnecessarily annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10It's very simple and lacks any depth, but I liked it. To me it feels like a *very light* mix of the main aspects of the games Autonauts and Don't Starve. It does not have much depth and you quickly have crafted all items and seen most of the content, but still it was enjoyable to me and very satisfying at times.Autonauts, in the sense that you instruct hordes of monkeys (instead of robots) to do repetitive tedious tasks and, at least to some degree, automate crafting. Although the few tasks you can "teach" the monkeys are very basic and you have little control to where they do it, I found this much more enjoyable than scripting robots in Autonauts. My only critique is that monkeys immediately forget what they were taught once you tell them to follow you or accidently select them (I played with the controller, all this may be even more accessible with mouse + keys).Don't Starve, in the sense that you explore islands, caves, fight and craft, but with not even a quarter as much depth and complexity to it. It is also not half as hard and doesn't give you ANY penalty for mistakes (e.g. monkeys never die, even if knocked-out in combat, if you starve/die you simply respawn with full stats at the last bed (only hard part is remembering the spot you died at), all resources get replenished every few hour or so (!)). The world is very simple, for example: the "procedural" vaults are just two rooms with usually the same enemies and a monkey at the end, islands are just a random collection of the few "biome" chunks..As this game seems to be mostly aimed for multiplayer, it is very strange that only the host of the game can purchase the most expensive items in the game from the shop, while at the same time money is not shared. The most confusing thing is however, that EVERYONE has to craft and build recipes to unlock the next ones. This added to the feeling of the multiplayer being parallel and just slapped onto the single player experience.Overall the game can feel early-accessy but is still fun with a lot of entertaining features.

_childDocuments_.review: Buggy, shallow, and generally feels unfinished. It's a shame, because there was the core of a really good game here, but it feels like a jam game, or a game still in early access.There's about 15-20 hours of extremely repetitive content that is mostly gated by the amount of time it takes to grind and craft an extremely small variety of extremely minor upgrades. There are effectively about 3 enemies in the game, just with different art and drops. Recipe progression feels good at first but it becomes immediately obvious that you've hit the end of the progression dozens of hours before you would expect to do so.The monkeys are probably this game's selling point, allowing you to automate some of the time consuming crafting but... they essentially just allow you to bypass artificial bloat in crafting times that other games would just skip in the first place. You might as well play V Rising, Core Keeper, or any number of other more interesting survival games, because this doesn't really add anything meaningful to the genre that other games haven't done better, and it seems unlikely that it will ever fulfil its potential given the last update was almost 2 years ago at the time of writing.If this was an early access game that was 25% done, I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it. But it's not. This is what they regard as being complete, with some absolutely insane game breaking bugs. Don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: Being in the mood for a survival game, I installed this one and frankly, I'm not impressed. Maybe I got a bad seed in the starting island, maybe I ran into a series of bugs or maybe these are all just strange design choices.The basic game is nothing out of the ordinary. Easy to pick up if you've played something like Don't Starve before. Pick up items, craft them into other items, learn new recipes, be able to craft higher level stuff so you can learn even more recipes and so on. Hunt, gather, fight, etc.But then the weird things start to show up. Some recipes don't really make much sense, others from the very start seem to require some basic ingredients that are absolutely nowhere to be found. Gathering and crafting is a ridiculous timesink, even for this sort of game. You have the option to train monkeys to do stuff for you, and that's mildly helpful at first until they forget what you taught them and you have to do it again (again, not sure if this is intentional design, because it's no mentioned by the game).Then out of the blue you have a warning that a raid is going to show up and that you have to "prepare your defenses". Oh, was I supposed to care about defenses all this time? Funny that none of the early game tutorials decided to mention it, even when I deliberately went out of my way to find enemies. But now I have less than a day to prepare my defenses, all I have unlocked is a hay wall that takes the whole darn day to build even if only want to put it in a few squares. I don't have enough time to close the wall, so I get raided and killed by enemies I'm woefully underprepared to fight. Reload, try again. I spend the whole day doing nothing but very, very slowly crafting to make this wall. This time instead of locking me behind a square wall, I put it up between two natural stone formations so I only have a few squares of wall which are positioned between me and the top part of the island, where the raiders spawn from. This time they spawn below, so now I'm trapped between the wall and them. I am clearly now locked in an unwinnable save state.I get that this is part of the survival experience and that dying and restarting is part of the experience, but I get the feeling the game is trolling me and not working properly, something that never happened with other survival games I've played, in which I felt that if I lost it was on my own fault.I don't know, I might give it a second try later, but everyone's saying the game is abandoned, which means any of the bugs I've encountered might never be fixed. That doesn't sound promising.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this game up on a whim, thought it looked neat, and fell in love within 14 hours. It's now the only game I really want to play, if it lets me play it. This amazing game got me hooked, three times in a row, because I've had to delete two of my saves in the files themselves in order to start fresh after dumping in at least 20 hours. I had some great worlds too, base all set out, monkeys doing various crafting tasks in order to construct said base and create valuable supplies I'd need later, and had a raft ready to go. I left the island, encountered the Mysterious Shop on another island, or something like that, and everything froze. I couldn't use my crafting menu, raft or anything. I set the game from singleplayer to an online session, and it fixed it for a while before I went back to my base as fast as I could, saved my game and closed it to let it reboot. I never made it past the loading screen again. Fortunately, Team 17 left a comment in the community post I'd gone to for answers, and I was able to give them my save file. They told me I could delete the save and start over fresh after backing it up. R.I.P. 18 hours of work for nothing.But the game was so fun I just couldn't wait to start again! So I did, and as soon as I started exploring another island with the Mysterious Shopkeeper, the game glitches out again. However! I've prepared, see? I've saved my game, I can close the application and reload the save back where I was, right? Not even alt+F4 could save me. Another save for the scrapheap, though this one was only 3-4 hours in. Now I've learned my lesson. I'm copying and pasting the save files in a folder that isn't corrupt in case I run into the bug again. So far it's been working, just avoiding an NPC necessary to finish the game n all, but I like building, programming monkeys to do my will and farming for supplies more than completing the game anyway. Alas, another 14 hour world to wait on, but at least I don't have to delete it. I've found 6 monkeys so far, and I can load into my world, but once I leave my save point past like, 10 feet, the game freezes, and will not respond, forcing me to close the game, and load in again. This bug, I have no idea how to counteract.So please, Team 17, if you see this, fix, the, game. I want to play it so freaking bad right now, even more than Cyberpunk 2077, which is basically going through the same thing. Don't add a bunch of bug fixes into a patch with tons of new content, like the breeding and taming one, please just buckle down your staff working on the game to fix these awful game-ruining bugs and make the game playable for someone that loves to build. This is my only wish for Christmas this year.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed pretty much everything in the game, and my short answer is: Yes, the game is worth it on sale, and you'll most likely have a fun time with it.A more detailed review:The main mechanic, monkey labor, is a somewhat fun, but often frustrating mechanic. You'll likely be spending a lot of time standing around while waiting for your monkeys to finish certain things for you. But, this comes with the benefit that you can use this time to go around and adventure around the several islands. Though, with adventuring comes a rough apple you're going to have to bite through.Combat. I won't sugarcoat it, but the combat in this game is very rough. Not in a, it's very hard kind of way, but in a very buggy kind of way. You'll often find yourself missing hits you definitely were supposed to, and somehow hitting things you definitely missed. Sometimes you'll just get pulled back and hit to a location you were previously. The best way to describe the combat is that it feels like you're playing with heavy latency.Still, despite it's shortcomings, the Survivalist is a somewhat fun experience if you're fan of the survival game genre. It does things a lot of other survival games do, and some it does a little better, some it does a little worse. All in all, I'd rate the game a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon starting a new game, you find yourself face down in the sand besides your broken raft on some unknown island. There are some Coconut trees near by which can help you survive both by eating the Coconuts and by using the Timber and Palm Leaves you gain from cutting down the trees. Searching your broken raft will also contain some resources that can help you survive for a while until you can explore your surroundings and find new resources. Away from the sandy beach coastline you’ll find other regions, lush fields of grass and flowers, swamps and deserts. There are resources everywhere you look that you can gather and then use to craft and build tools, weapons, walls (sausages), doors, windows, food etcetera.  Certain items can be crafted by hand such as Hand Axes, Multitool, Handles, Wooden Rods and a few other basic items to help you on your way. For more complex items like Flimsy Shovels, Axes and Pickaxes, weapons such as Bow and Arrows, Spears, Clubs, Animal Traps, Training Dummy etcetera can be crafted using the Crafting Bench. Crafting as Campfire will allow you to cook Raw Meats and Fish, make Smoothies which will allow you to recover more hunger than trying to survive on Coconuts and Berries alone. Crafting a Forge will also allow you to create new items such as Glass Sheet, Nails, Stone Slabs, Glass Bottles and Bowls. You also have Blueprints where you can build Straw, Wooden and Stone Walls, Tables, Storage Chests, Campfire, Forge, Raft, Fence, Bed etcetera.  Running around the world are Monkey’s, you can tame these monkey’s by giving them something they want and then they’ll trust and follow you. You can then have them Mimic your actions like give them an axe and have them chop down trees and shrubs and they’ll keep going until the axe becomes worn out. You can then assign another monkey to collect the resources and have them drop then somewhere for you. The monkeys can even craft tools and cook food using the crafting bench, campfire etcetera. You can also train them for combat to fight any enemy which raid your base. The more a monkey performs a task the faster and more efficient they’ll become at performing that task. Scattered around the land you’ll find some chests which are locked but smashing them with a club or something will allow you to collect the lovely loot inside. You can also find old ruins, wrecks and skeletons all of which can be searched and you may find some loot. Every now and then a Mysterious Stranger will arrive who will open his doors where you can sell some of your loot you have found and buy some new items. The stranger also has a quest for you which when completed you’ll be able to claim a reward. You may also come across Vaults and Labyrinths, these places are dangerous, have puzzles to complete and treasure. However, if you find the end of the labyrinths you may receive an item that will help you escape the islands.  Crafting a raft and sails will allow you to set sail and explore the seas around your island. However, it will be hit and miss as you search for new lands. To help you try and spot new lands you can use a telescope once you find one. Finding new lands can bring you new resources and treasures, although they can also bring new dangers. You can customise your character, their body colour, hair and clothes and you can also customise the colour of your monkeys so that you can have a certain coloured monkey doing a specific task. The game can be played solo or with up to three friends in co-op. When playing co-op, you can take up to five of your monkeys from your solo game with you. There is also a storage chest which you can fill with items and resources and can take with you from a solo game into a co-op game with friends. In the Options you’ll find the settings Sound Effects and Music Volume, Resolution, Windowed, Constrain Cursor, V-Sync, Region Names, Dyslexia Assist and Background Animations. To begin with I was finding the game a bit frustrating, I was trying to build a base and collecting resources when all of a sudden, I was raided by about seven enemies. It took me totally by surprise so I got my botty handed to me, I died and respawned only to find me still being raided and as I had dropped all my weapons the first time, I died I didn’t have much of a chance of anything other than dying again. This happened four times before the raid was over, my base was ruined as it was only made of straw walls (sausages). So, I decided to try and build multiple walls however, before I managed to complete my walls (sausages), I was having Déjà Vu and got my botty spanked again.  I took me a while before I managed to build stone walls which led me to another problem I was having. When crafting the items for creating the stone walls it kept saying something like “The monkeys should do this job”. It took a while to create the Stone Slabs and then to build the Stone Wall. I tried to have the monkeys mimic me in doing the tasks so I could get on with other things but each time the time limit of the monkeys would run out before they could learn how to create the stone slabs and walls. I have also found it frustrating getting them to craft other items as well.  Although, the game has started to grow on me the more I play the game. The only other problem I had was an item shown in the on-screen inventory even though it wasn’t there. The problem disappeared later on its own. Positives + Nice graphics + Good music + Co-op with friends  + Has achievements + Full controller support Negatives - Can be frustrating - Inventory Bug - No cards currently Train monkeys to help you craft and build as you strive to survive the dangers and perils of island life in The Survivalists 7/10

The amount of positive reviews on this game is baffling, at this point I'm convinced that it's spam or a bunch of 5 year olds with no concept of money or value, because there is no way that the hundreds of positive reviews that just say "nice" or "good game" are genuine and take the massive price tag into account. Just, do NOT buy this game. Please don't make the mistake I did, if you really want to play it because it is a nice game, (had it been sold as a mobile game for $10) then just download the free demo because that's literally the entire game, I was under the impression that there would be more with the full game. _childDocuments_.review: pros of this game:-made me like monkeys more-artstyle is fun-sound design is great-crafting tree reveal based on items made is cool, gives a reason to make each item-monkey helpers/automation is a great conceptcons of this game:-monkey automation is clunky at best. there are no items you need to CONSTANTLY have two monkeys gathering/crafting. At least none that I know of.-Monkey task management is sad. I have to reteach monkeys EVERY time I need them to do something different. And generally? You get so many resources the only things you need them to do are build and fight.-inventory is pathetic and no way to improve it.- Some things you get midway into the crafting tree are useless. not just "oh its decorative" but utterly pointless. No reason to farm really except to get wheat (see further for why wheat is pointless). No reason to tame livestock/store fish because you get so much food passively there is no reason to.-YOU GET SO MUCH FOOD PASSIVELY THERE IS NO POINT TO SPECIFICALLY LOOKING FOR IT/PREPPING FOR IT. Run into a wild boar? meat. run into a male deer? meat. bats? meat. swinging at trees and hit a bush? berries. chopping palms? nuts. -food is barely useful. the hunger meter is one of the few survival mechanics there and half the time i forget to use it except when taking damage. as someone who is a cooking nut in games, i find this sad.it would be better if doing actions made hunger go down faster, or if healing damage would cost hunger, but its kinda just... an extra chore. Or, if the monkeys got hungry so some of it would be used for them too.-wheat is particularly useless. I was excited to get it because it was used to make fishing nets...which is weird because we already get grass/palms right away that make more sense to use for nets... can we even cook with the wheat? idk i got bored shortly after getting it.-health system is poor. You start with a base max, fine. Upgraded beds can increase health! Cool! Oh. I have to... use them regularly in order to get the health? Sleeping? You mean that thing that not doing costs no penalty for? When I could instead be doing other things?-Apparently the answer to combat is have a small army of monkeys at all times and dodge endlessly. Second island fauna take 2-3 hits on you before you're down. Shoulda taken that super health power nap before doing things i guess.- why are windows an option in a top-down roofless game?-why do you have to visit a second island to just make a door?-they REALLY want you to pick up all the sellable items!! maybe I would if the inventory wasn't terrible.-no item almanac. Any game that forces you to google basic items like WHEAT and bamboo??? is an automatic failure.-some resources respawn with the blood moon. EVERY orc outpost respawns fully. perhaps more of a pet peeve- i like defeated areas to at least mostly stay defeated.-cant rotate blueprints. one of the most basic things for a crafting/building game.-pointlessly needed to find a mysterious salesman to make a sail. a thing i clearly should know to make after having made things like rugs. didn't pay attention to the rest of it so i just accumulate money for no reason tbh.-player is just...terrible at crafting things apparently? quit whining i dont want to bother showing a monkey how to do a single task that takes 10 seconds and i wont need to do again for some time.-after reading the ending, the character factor of monkeys is also sad. not just the automation- but the consideration of them as "friends". Would have been neat if you could have a good and bad ending based on a treatment of them mechanic.conclusion:half baked survival crafting tree game with no discernable plot and poor monkey automation.If you really like monkeys or just love restarting games for the grind endlessly? Go for it. Wait for a super cheap sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This could be a fun game, but almost everything you do in it is hampered by the frustratingly small inventory and UI setup.For instance, you can't queue 15 things in a row if you want to make them yourself, you have to click a button every single time. Since a lot of what you work on is mass crafting, this gets tedious quick. In terms of inventory, you have only a handful of slots, and by the time you fill them with the tools you need to efficiently do anything, plus a weapon, you can only carry 3 or so actual raw resources.Speaking of items, there is no clear stats on any tools or weapons, so you don't really *know* what will do more damage to what, so you end up guessing. a lot. In other cases, things just aren't explained. At one point fairly early on, I was attacked by a deer looking creature, that chased me around the map attacking me, yet no weapon I had (gold sword, spear, bow and arrow, club, axe) did any damage to it at all. It just chased me until it killed me with no clear explanation as to how or why.The monkey see monkey do system for setting up crafting changes for quests is a good idea, but also poorly implemented behind confusing UI elements and unclear methodology.I love the art design, the sound design, and the music, but what should be a good game turns into an incredibly frustrating experience because for some reason they wanted the game to be simultaneously compatible with controllers and keyboard/mouse.
