_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: FAIR WARNING: DO NOT ALT TAB FROM THE GAME. BAD SH!T COULD HAPPEN WHEN IN BACKGROUND!Okay, this is one of those "YES, BUT" reviews. I'll try to keep it short.Up until today I'd had undoubtly recommended this, BUT a glaring silly err mishap throw me way off!I had to do something else quick so I left the esc menu pause and alt-tabbed from the game. Did not noticed that the menu options continued to move AND BE PRESSED! no warning, no ask for permission, nada.When I got back I noticed the entire map was new, all my stuff, bases buildings, teleports, etc and all but 5 monkeys were ALL GONE!After a bit of research it seems that the regenerate world or NEW GAME+ or something like that happened, without confirmation, while on background!.At this point I'm not sure I want to continue playing. I'm not sure how close or far I was from the ending but I was so NOT READY nor prepared to start anew..Why do it like this, why!? there are like 12 FAKE save slots which you can't use, ALL saves are not really backups cause all are the same, same time stamps, different name. Trying to manually recover resulted in the game claiming the saves were corrupted and deleting them. ALWAYS shut off the game! treat it like a lobotomized console/handheld port; nothing more.Oh, well now that I've cooled off a bit, realised didn't mention anything else, like at all :PSo, I like the somewhat repetitive music but sure matches the pixel art, reminiscent of the old era..I like the graphics and animations. _childDocuments_.review: After seeing the amount of changes coming to the game based on player feedback, I am happily changing my review. Just one week later, and already most of my biggest issues with the game have been addressed, leaving lack of content as the only real negative. But the quick responses by the developers fixing issues and adding more content post-release, along with their plans for future content lead me to believe this game is worth the purchase.Right now (16 Oct 2020), you'll be lucky to get 8 enjoyable hours out of the game, but I'm sure that will change as the updates continue. So whether you get it now or wait for more content is up to you -- but seeing the commitment to the game's growth leaves me with no other choice but to recommend it.-- Previous Review (thanks for up-voting) --Besides a few irritating control-related things (constantly switching items with following monkeys instead of picking up items on the ground) and some buggy monkey behavior, the game isn't bad. The overall gameplay is very familiar, with a few unique twists that keep it interesting.But as many other reviewers have said, where this game lacks is content. There is hardly anything to do, and definitely feels more like an early-access game. You can easily run through 99% of the game in a just a few hours, which leaves you feeling bored very quickly. By the time you are setting up teleporters, you pretty much have no reason to use them, because there's nothing left to accomplish. Sure you can keep playing to collect all of the legendary items, but for what reason? They won't help you now that you've built and crafted everything.If you're going to buy it, you're going to buy it. But if you're on the fence, all I can say is it's definitely NOT worth $25 in its current state.(Note: Hours on record is not actual hours played -- I tend to leave games running in the background for long periods of time)

_childDocuments_.review: The survivalists is very enjoyable to play alone or with others. If you don't find anyone you can play with, there are also the monkeys in the game who partly replace these players. The monkeys you will meet you must first help to free them or give them food. from then on they belong to your team and you can train them to do certain tasks for you.They can find resources for you, stock them, you can also give them knowledge for the constructive part of the game, so that when things are built you have time to continue doing your thing. the monkeys can also become better at tasks as they do tasks more and as a result, for example, work faster or master several tasks.you will also have to craft extra tools to give to the monkeys so that they can perform the tasks for you. You can also teach them how to fight so that when you explore, you can better defend yourself against wild beasts or native inhabitants. You will also often discover temples where you can find special items, i advice you never to enter such a temple unarmed.when you are dead you drop all your items that you have on you on the spot, these items can be retrieved later at that place.to avoid being killed you also have the option to teach your monkeys how to fight, this will greatly increase your chances of survival. the monkeys are also very useful for holding extra items when your inventory is full.just like you, the monkeys will also lose hp while fighting, your job is to prepare food in time to heal or satisfy hunger. You won't have to drink water to survive but there is an energy meter. While running or taking resources you will have to keep an eye on that, you will get hungry faster if you keep overshooting this energy meter. The game offers you a series of recipes that you can prepare on a campfire. Some recipes only satisfy hunger, others also provide new HP. You can also eat directly from foods that you find in nature, but the prepared recipes will be much more useful and require fewer numbers for a worthy effect. You will also have to hunt for wildlife to make other recipes.To hunt certain animals you will have to craft certain items, for example to catch fish. Or if you want to save yourself the hunting you can also craft traps and wait after you have placed them. you will also find treasure maps, notes, or diaries with useful information that will lead you to useful items or exceptional locations. the game will also offer many interesting quests through bottles washed up on the beach or through a mysterious stranger.Online you have certain options as a host, so you can determine whether players / which players are allowed to build in your world or so you can also determine whether other players can also own monkeys, if not the monkeys that other players find will automatically join the host's team.Tip: when going out for recources you'll have to tap the left mouse button. But when you hold the left mouse button then you will do a more powerfull attack which will be more effective and which will also save you time.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected quite a bit more from Team17 with this one. While it looks charming, and I'm liking the monkey automation system, it leaves so, so much to be desired. If you're a fan of survival games in general, you'll likely find The Survivalists to be far more shallow than your genre favourites.The system works, but it's not at all intuitive. You'll foresee the UI limitations almost immediately, and they've tried to get around them by just creating more and more stations. But while separating recipes across stations gives more space, effectively, it makes finding the recipe you're looking for a pain. Some are obvious where to find them, whereas others you'll find yourself checking 2-3 stations to find it. The lack of any kind of search or sorting (it's a locked, isometric grid UI) makes this a miss for me. It feels like someone  had a clever idea that looked nice with a few recipes in mind, but as the game grew they were too stubborn to give up that restrictive design choice.Building is as basic as it gets. Right now, you can't even rotate blueprints. It's also going to be several hours before you have the resources and labour power to build any substantial infrastructure--and even then it's walls and floors. Tools break way too quickly. Between your monkeys' tools and yours, you'll be repairing items a lot. Which involves more pebble/basalt mining, which means more broken tools, rinse and repeat. It's really unnecessary, and it seems the durability was set this low to hide the fact that the gameplay loop is just a grind.Whatever we're calling them, they're short and they're boring. I've explored about a dozen, and I can't recall any of them taking more than 2-3 minutes in total. Is there a plan to add something more substantial? For a combat system that's fairly decent, compared to most tile-based games like this, they've really failed at showing it off.It's a neat idea, and it's clearly the the "gimmick" they're going to hang this game on. Make it better. Recipes start to require more and more processed parts, rather than raw ingredients, so you're going to want to start training monkeys to build parts. The trouble is, you can only train a monkey to do one single action. For example, if you want to build a stone slab, that's one monkey to feed materials into the crafting table to make stone chunks, then one monkey crafting those stone chunks. Then another monkey digs for dirt. Then another monkey feeds chunks and dirty into the furnace. Then another monkey crafts the slabs. Want to be more self sufficient here? You'll need  another monkey to go mining for rocks, another monkey digging for dirt, and another monkey carting materials home. And you'll need multiple stone slabs for every single wall tile. See the problem?Of course, monkeys set to a command (e.g. feed crafting stations) isn't limited to one station and can feed multiple, you're still going to need many more to fill in other rolls in your base, such as watering crops (1 monkey), harvesting crops (1 monkey), planitng seeds (1 monkey). The list goes on. It would be nice to be able to teach monkeys a few commands, so that while they wait around they can perform other menial duties.Monkeys set to pick up materials off the ground and put them in chests are also a royal pain in the butt. They'll end up just putting things absolutely anywhere, and with zero ability to mark your chests... it gets a bit messy.Lots to improve here, and hopefully that happens. But for the time being, there are far, far better games to scratch your survival/building itch than The Survivalists.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like the game.  It has all the basic components; crafting, building, combat, resource collection, followers, a good art-style, and more.The problem is:* Much of the game is very tedious.  Most of what your monkey-army does, only "require" monkeys, because your character is handicapped.  For example inventory space is expanded by having a monkey following you with a chest.  Crafting speed is needlessly slow for the character.  Monkeys picking up items is only needed because there's no auto-pick-up.* Sorting/finding items is impossible.  Your monkeys just dump stuff in random chests.  If you need to find something like a hinge or food, the easiest way is to initiate a crafting recipe, and see what chests the monkeys drop items off on.* Compared to most similar games, it takes an absurd amount of work to automate anything.  * There isn't much (or any) depth when it comes to weapons, tools, armor, trinkets, materials, etc.The reason I'm giving it a negative review, is because it's been out for quite some time, and plenty of other games in the genre have done much better, like Necesse, Wayward, Forager, and others.

_childDocuments_.review: Exploration/survival/crafting game.  You are an amnesiac survivor of some sort of catastrophe that washes you up on a jungle island.  Establish a shelter that can help protect from periodic raiders.  Teach monkeys to do tasks for you like harvesting, collecting and crafting.  Find food.  Find secrets.  Find vendors.  Don't die (it's really inconvenient).Yet another game where you explore a landscape and learn crafts.  Ordinarily I like this sort of thing, but this particular one doesn't lend too much novelty to the market for me.  It's a step up from Terraria in that it's 3D rather than 2D, but that's not always an improvement when the terrain and vegetation obscure so much that you need to interact with.The presentation is rather low-rez.  Text is tiny, with no way to increase text size, which is bad for people like me with inconsistently-effective aging eyes.  Colors are on occasion awful, with little contrast between text and background (ex. light grey text on medium grey background, dark purple text on practically anything).  Controls are flaky, with descriptions that don't necessarily match the actual keys to be pressed and tricks that have to be learned to do things (ex. space to pick up one thing vs. long space to pick up a bunch of things; quick space to add materials to crafting vs. anything longer which does nothing).Its biggest claim to uniqueness is the ability to train monkeys to do things for you.  Similar to Autonauts, you demonstrate what you're doing for a monkey, give it a tool, and it will then go do what you were doing.  It'll chop down all trees in an area, if the tool holds out.  It'll gather stuff and put it in a specific place or a storage crate.  It'll operate whatever crafting station is ready with materials.  It'll stand in one spot with its arm in the air (this is something you'll need it to do to solve a puzzle).  But there's an emphasis on monkeyS, building supply chains with monkeyS, improving your camp and defending it with monkeyS.  Unlike Autonauts, where you can build multiple automatons at will, I've only seen one monkey so far.There are enemies wandering around that will attack you.  There is wildlife that will attack you.  There's the regularly scheduled raiding party that will attack you.  If you die, you wind up back in your camp in your bed (hint: build a bed, it's needed to save the game).  But all your possessions will be left where you died, a mechanism I've seen in other games and generally loathe.I got this game as part of my Humble Choice monthly subscription, so my monetary investment is pretty low.  Considering the other games of this nature available, I consider the current Steam non-sale price of $25 ridiculous.  Buy Autonauts for less.  Buy Terraria for much less.  Heck, buy Elite Dangerous for only slightly more.  I'll just sit here and bask in smugness for having effectively paid a dollar.

_childDocuments_.review: Was a great survival craft game. The monkey system was a breath of fresh air. Occasionally I was left wondering what the next thing I should do, but before long I was back on track. Haven't finished it yet, but I definitely will. I played it for 12 hours straight, I don't remember the last time I gamed for that long without growing bored. I have an army of monkeys ready to lay their life on the line for me, I have never felt such loyalty, the world better watch out! My raft is a beast, it takes me where I need to go. Had this game in my library for a few months, though with the recent sale, my friend grabbed a copy and I figured it was time for me to finally experience this masterpiece. The online co-op was stable, can't always say that about games in this genre. Probably one of the best games that I've played over the past month. I saw a few negative reviews, I do not agree with much of what they said. I didn't experience the bugs they mentioned, I didn't struggle with learning the controls, though that could be because I play a lot of games like this. I would however recommend playing with a friend, I imagine it would be rather boring on your own.Edit: After playing this game solo while my friend was busy, I came to realise that the host is granted several additional features that should be accessible by their friends whom are playing with them. Only the host can see the monkeys on the map, change their name and view their stats. Only the host is able to use personal storage systems, it would be nice if these purple chests were accessible to all, much like the piggy bank in Terraria. Training your monkeys to automatically do various tasks is nice, but it would be appreciated if we were able to lock certain chests from them having access. These seem like minor issues at first, but it becomes irritating after a while. I can't remember how many times I had to ask my friend to ping where my monkeys were on the map after I died. Still love the game, but would love it more with these minor improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an okay survival game. Good exploration and progression and combat, with some UI and automation problems. What makes this game different is the monkeys, units you can command to repeat your last action. They are both fun and frustrating.Exploring feels rewarding and progression is well defined. It's not too grindy, there's a good balance between needing to farm mats and getting to do other stuff. Combat feels pretty good, it's easy to die if you don't pay attention but it's not very challenging beyond that. It would be nice if enemies had a different health bar color than friendlies.The differing islands are fun but the raft has a weird floaty momentum that makes steering a chore. It is too hard to see objects behind other things especially in dense forests, give me transparency or outlines please. The UI really needs to let you track resource stocks, or all chests need to merge into one display. Hunting for stuff is painful and it's impossible to know when you're running out of something.Multiplayer works well but the non-host cannot get quest rewards, leaving them lacking a few of the trinkets if they don't redo them in their own game.For those standard features nothing stands out as particularly good or bad. It's the monkeys that make this game different from others I've played in the genre.Saving monkeys feels rewarding both roleplay wise and mechanically. Having a pack of minions to help fight or do tasks is a lot of fun, and automating my town was quite satisfying. Unfortunately, as much as I enjoyed the monkeys' basics, I found a lot of frustration in their management.You can't set chest categories so having them automate storage makes inventory even harder to monitor, and I can never tell what area of ground they will decide to cover. Assigning tasks is unnecessarily time consuming. Having to perform the task myself is a fun concept but not fun gameplay. Having to manually swap their gear is tedium that I could live without.Their job AI isn't great, when mining/chopping they'll bounce between nodes on opposite sides of a large area ignoring closer ones, and countless times they've told me "no more rocks/trees" when standing right next to one.The core of the game is solid: combat is ok, exploring is fun, progression is good. Monkeys are a novel and fun concept that sort of work in practice. I listed a lot of complaints but they hold the game back from being really good rather than make it bad. You should watch some videos showing how monkey controls work before you make your purchase decision.

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoying this game so far!Pros:- Love the soundtrack and art style- Survival games are a dime a dozen now - the monkeys add something new.- training monkeys is a nice concept. I like that it isn't just point and click what you want them to do, but that you actually have to act it out for them.- Plenty of customisation for character - I disagree with comments saying it is wrong to charge for additional cosmetics. _childDocuments_.review: In terms of singleplayer, it is well made, but there are a load of bugs with the buildings which take consumables, such as the campfires sometimes not extinguishing. While this is not game breaking, it is clear to see that the same level of detail is not present in this game when compared to another title such as The Escapists.In terms of multiplayer, the game was quite restrictive with permissions. The ones which you can change did work properly, but things such as the session host only being able to purchase labyrinth keys made it somewhat frustrating in that regard. The game is setup as a co-op multiplayer style of game so this sort of mechanic is not required I believe. I understand why it is implemented, in the case of combating speedrunners or griefers in open multiplayer, but perhaps there needs to be a setting added to permissions for this allowing it to be disabled.The art style is fantastic as always. The range of different combat options is broad enough to keep you trying to hone your skills on each weapon type, however the melee combat options being restricted to the cardinal directions only leaves something more to be desired here.Overall, I give this game a 6/10. It was a good time in singleplayer and, for the most part, multiplayer was enjoyable with some friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Take Minecraft and The Escapists, slap them together, and you get something like The Survivalists, the latest offering from Team17, the studio mostly known for the Worms series. It bills itself as an online co-op survival game, and as someone that has played a mountain of those, I had to give it a look.So I feel like something needs to be said about what to expect from this game before people get the wrong impression. The Survivalists is much less a full-on, difficult survival game, and more like a casual adventure game. In all of my hours playing it, I only died once and never had to struggle for food or any other resource I needed to survive. It’s like a much more laidback take on Don’t Starve Together, with simplified survival mechanics, but other cool additions to make up for it.On that front, the game does a great job. The base-building is fun, the crafting system is well-made and doesn’t feel like it was tacked onto the experience, and the added focus on treasure-hunting and tomb-raiding is definitely cool too. Yes, a large chunk of the game is building up your base and setting up crafting systems and whatnot, but the occasional break from that to go explore a tomb on another island, solve a treasure map, or visit the traveling shopkeeper does keep the experience fresh.The monkey mechanic in particular is very cool. With it, you can acquire monkey followers and train them to do a variety of things, including gathering resources, crafting stuff, or even helping you clear tombs of enemies if you give them a weapon to work with. You can even set up entire chains of automation, having one group of monkeys chopping down trees, another group transporting the drops to chests at your base, and then another moving that material to crafting benches for quick and easy crafting. This mechanic may have its faults (which I’ll discuss shortly), but it’s a great addition at its core and definitely added to the experience.And on the topic of adding to the experience, the graphics and music do just that as well. The former is simplistic yet is the perfect match for this style of gameplay and looks great in motion. The lighting system looks great on top of that, and that becomes very apparent when you’re exploring dark caves or tombs with a torch in hand. The music is a bit more mellow – more atmospheric – but does equal work in giving the game its unique aesthetic.So that sounds good and all, but one of the game’s major pitfalls is quality of life features. I’m talking stuff like not being able to pick up more than one item at a time, not being able to easily set monkeys to do certain tasks and instead having to reteach them every single time, and even more minor things like being forced to hold down a button instead of pressing it to acknowledge a popup. The game is rife with such quality of life hiccups, and it can oftentimes make it feel annoying to play.For example: crafting recipes are not shared between players in the same world, so when I was playing with a buddy, we both had to craft each item in the game ourselves despite living in and building the same base. Another prime example being that the button to pick up items is the same button used to give an item to a monkey. This is super annoying when you are spamming spacebar to pick up a bunch of items and accidentally give a random monkey next to you the item in your hand, forcing you to figure out which monkey took it as that is not represented visually without accessing the monkey command menu.And then you got the problems with teaching monkeys and not being able to assign them specifically to certain areas and whatnot. Really, the entire monkey mechanic in general could use a quality of life upgrade, as it just doesn’t feel like it wants to cooperate at times. I would go further and say that the lack of such quality of life features is enough to warrant waiting for patches before considering the game.So, while I did have fun with the game, I would say it’s only worth a light recommendation. The core gameplay is fine, and the multiplayer was a good experience, but the lack of quality of life features really holds it back at times and it’s probably worth waiting for updates before considering the game at full price. If those get patched in and maybe the game receives a few more content updates, it would absolutely be worth a look. In its current state though, I’d advise waiting for a sale first if the updates don’t come anytime soon.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - I really want to give this a positive review, but I just can't at launch. It's well polished and works well in execution, but the content is easily exhausted, and before you hit the ten-hour mark, you've more or less done everything there is to do, by some stretch. As of launch, only buy on sale, 50% off ideally.The Survivalists is a more straightforward approach to the top-down survival genre- think Don't Starve, but the weirdness is just replaced by your typical island survival, plus monkeys. I don't need to give any exposition, the trailers say it all, and the plot, as it relates to gameplay, is fairly barebones. It's a survive-it-up, story optional.Unfortunately, the survival aspects are a bit shallow. While playing, you unlock pieces of a few separate crafting trees, bit by bit, but most of it just feels like fluff, and the mid-tier tools and weapons feel no less effective than end-game gear. The game starts out strong, with you just having a few berries and rocks to start out with, but by the time you transition from a crude hand axe to purpose-built tools... that's it. You're done. You are now doing all you are going to do for the rest of the game. The item progression feels completely meaningless, you could finish this game with a basic spear and a few monkeys.That brings me to the unique aspect of the game: the monkeys. The player finds them scattered about on the various islands- some are in cages for you to break them out of, these chimps will join you as soon as you free them. Others are wandering around with thought bubbles over their heads, the contents of which display what item you need to drop next to them for them to join you. Early game, these items are almost always a low tier food, monkey food, specifically. But at a certain point (I believe it's after you hit a certain population of monkeys), they stop wanting basic items and suddenly want high tier craftables, such as golden statues and power gems. I get that they should be more "expensive" to acquire as the game goes on, but the change was just... jarring. There's no intermediate period, you're either giving them early game stuff or you're giving them costly craftables from the end of the crafting trees. And they're tedious to work with, too. The monkeys learn from "monkey see, monkey do". To tell a monkey to do something, you have to get its attention with a banana (you have an infinite supply of these, they are merely an interaction gimmick), then do the task you want it to do. They can do almost anything the player can do, which is awesome, except... it's a nightmare. Managing multiple monkeys in close quarters is a total clusterf!@#- they'll often stand on top of each other, and move at random when you try to select them. Every time you want to order a chimp to do something, you have to go through monkey-see-monkey-do, and when you're trying to get a dozen monkeys to do a few different jobs, it's just... tedious. So tedious. And I'm not gonna bother getting into the specifics of pathing bugs for the logistics monkeys (they often just stand there, holding an item they're supposed to put on a crafting bench, forever until you retask them).The typical trimmings of survival are there, but lackluster. You and your monkeys can build floors, walls, some crafting benches of different types, spike traps and about a dozen decorations. The construction is serviceable but doesn't really feel rewarding- if you think you're gonna build a unique and awesome base, I've got bad news for you, you simply won't have any toys to get creative with.Hunger and stamina are a thing, and works exactly as it does in other survival titles. Combat feels really clunky, with most attack animations locking you in place. It can be difficult to target a specific enemy. Also, mouse and keyboard controls feel really, really bad, and contextual keys such as "interact", spacebar by default, do everything from open a chest, pick up an item, and unceremoniously give your currently held item to a monkey that just happens to be standing too close to you (this happens WAY too often). I'd be okay with using a controller if the crafting trees didn't require you to use a super slow cursor to select things, a la Destiny or No Man's Sky. You can get used to the controls, but they really are just *bad*.I waited a very long time for Survivalists, and was definitely cautiously hyped. I played the demo early on, impressed by its polish. I thought they would expand more on the crafting tree than what was in the demo, and to be fair, they did. Just not by much. The rest was more or less as I'd expected.I'm hoping that further updates or even some cheap DLC will make this the gem it should be, but until I see that, I'm gonna have to give this game a "no". (Pick it up at 50% off).

_childDocuments_.review: This game was released as a 1.0 version product. This means that it's feature complete (NOT an Alpha) and it's tested (NOT a Beta). As such, as a reviewer, I can only in good faith review it as such. I am aware of future announcements for the game and the promise of more content, but if the developers wanted it reviewed that way, they should have released it as an Alpha (feature incomplete) in Early access. This game DOES have some potential, but I won't review a title based off promises. As it stands, this title feels like a product, not a game. It seems like an idea that was cobbled together to make 30 minutes of playable game so that youtubers and advertisers can exploit children. I'll be happy to be mistaken, but that's the impression I get.As an additional preword, I didn't like The Escapists and think they wouldn't have looked out of place on Kongregate or some other free flash game website.While The Escapists I would describe as ankle deep, this title I would describe as knee deep. What you're doing at one point in the game won't change much to what you're doing 5 hours later. While in other survival titles might see you advance through a dynamic tech tree, figuring things out as you go and gatherering materials, this title sees you follow a linear and static tech tree as you sit around watching monkeys auto gather and your numbers get higher like a mobile game. There is absolutely no "Survival" to speak of. Food is immediately abundant, you don't drink, you don't get cold or hot, sick, poisoned, diseased or anything that might be considered "survival". Survival itself doesn't even seem to be a consideration in this survival game. As a title in the genre, it feels like it was made by lizards who saw the fundamental elements of every successful game, then they proceeded to remove all of the fun and replace it with a sterile version of what a survival title is when written on a piece of paper and read by an executive that's never played a videogame.The monkeys themselves are a core component of the gameplay. Your human character with a fully developed brain can't learn anything, in fact getting WORSE at most tasks as they continue to do it, complaining about how "Bored" they are by having to literally stay alive. Conversely, the monkeys level up and get better at tasks, get more efficient at using tools and are generally just better at everything, tool usage included. Then the monkey training happens and it's counter intuitive. You want to train a monkey to haul things to a workstation. You enter training mode and show him how to do it. But because you didn't access a chest and take an item out during the training, the monkey will only deliver items that are left on the ground. Now okay. This makes sense. "Realism" or whatever. So why can monkeys learn better than a human? The game flip-flops over itself trying to balance "reality" with "fun" and fails at every conceivable junction. Like every single opportunity where the developers thought; "Do we make this realistic or make it enjoyable for the player?", they never chose to make it enjoyable to the player. You're left with an experience that feels like a chore. In many other survival titles, you're doing chores but it's fun. In this title, you're playing a game and it feels like doing chores and I can't descibe why, which is why I'm convinced it was designed by lizards who just don't understand the human brain. All the parts are there and it should be fun, but it isn't.This title is nearly half the price of Cyberpunk 2077. Just let that sink in for a moment before you purchase it and then maybe wait for a sale. Support the developers if you actually believe they're going to improve, but for a general audience, there's absolutely no way that I would suggest someone buy this title. Go play Green Hell or Minecraft or something. At least you'll get a feeling at some point during the game that you need to survive.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER:  75% of the gameplay/game is in the demo. However, this seems like an alpha build just to test all the ideas and implementation of them before the game is even fleshed out. with a $25 price tag.  I was incredibly excited to play the demo of this game, and talked it up for about a month prior to release. Purchased the deluxe version to play a few days early and was severely disappointed. I love crafting games and have played most of them if not on steam, on my consoles. Gameplay; You start out with a simple crafting menu that seems like it will continue to expand, however you are limited to a handful of items and will max out your crafting trees in the first few hours leaving nothing to look forward to. Why not head into a dungeon for some unique items? Nope! You just get a bunch of junk you have to lug back to your base. However, doing the six unique dungeons rewards you with a special weapon or tool that really serve no other purpose than doing a little more damage or lasting longer. Which would make sense if you weren't already on the "end-game." Also, there isn't really a need for the tools as you've more than likely gathered all the available materials in the game within the first few hours.Map: Map is incredibly small, it seems vast and open but in reality there are only a handful of islands that seem pretty empty and void of anything of interest. Yes, you'll find a "treasure map location" which more often than not will be junk you won't use beyond the first few hours of the game. The treasures you find to sell are worthless and cannot be displayed as killing monsters and doing regular dungeons will net you 1000x the amount of gold in the same time.Base building; pretty much non-existant, you get three tiers of walls that you can build almost immediately. No real way to "customize" the base/house and make it yours. Chairs don't even work, even if they did you can't rotate them.Crafting; as stated a few times before, you will unlock all crafting recipes in the first few hours with nothing to look forward to. most games I am excited to craft, in this one it just seems like a chore.Unless they add a ton of content, this game is worth maybe $5-10. only purchase if there is a massive sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to update my review after the recent game update, Sadly, I still can't recommend this game.PROS:- Visually appealing- Controls work fine- Interesting idea for a survival gameCONS:- Nerfing the monkeys would've been fine if they hadn't also powered up the enemies. Even the best weapons in the game seem weak and break in the middle of a dungeon. The balance is way off and now, instead of being too easy, combat feels like a chore.- It takes longer to unlock the crafting tree but doing so is still tedious and boring. If I have 99 grass in my inventory, I should be able to craft 33 ropes without having to do each one individually so I can freshen my drink or take a bathroom break. This one-at-a-time crafting nonsense when I spent hours gathering all of the necessary ingredients is just that, nonsense.- Monkeys now take longer and hesitate for some reason before engaging the enemy. Frustrating when being swarmed in a temple.- Base building is still pointless. Without being able to designate a base zone, all you have to do to avoid raids is place your bed away from the rest of your stuff. Raiders attack the bed, raid ends, you build a new bed.- Still no way to upgrade inventory. Having a monkey carrying a chest around is not a good work around for something which should've been in the game before release: Backpacks and/or pouches.- Still no option for a faster ship. The crazy slow raft is the only way to get around the map until you can place teleporters on all of the islands. I often feel like I'm playing a sailing simulator that was someone's student project as opposed to an island survival game.- Lastly, my biggest gripe, is that monkeys' skills level up but my character never does. It never gets better at crafting, combat, sailing, repairs, or anything. While upgrading the bed and sheets is a novel idea for increasing health and stamina, it makes no sense that my character wouldn't hit harder, craft/build faster, or sail faster through days and weeks of in-game experience.TLDR: Keep an eye on the non-committal road map that Team 17 has laid out for this project. If they actually add the content they're teasing us with, The Survivalists could end up being a great game. As it stands, it should have been early access and it certainly plays like an unfinished game. Buy something else for now or wait for a deep discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Update  2: As of this update I have over 80hrs in game. I have come to the conclusion that while the game has its flaws, it is playable. It still needs some work. There are things that need fixings. There is a bug with the golden statue that sometimes fails to give credit when you create it. Also, when you complete some of the recipes, I have noticed there are some in the recipe tree that are left with no way to access them. I am not sure if this is a mistake carried over from when the devs did their overhaul, or if this is a failure on my part for not completing some part that I am unaware of. Either way, it is frustrating. Over all, I would say I would recommend it as a way to pass time when you have nothing else to do.Update:I have played for about 44hrs at the time of this edit. While I still think the game is unforgiving, I decided to continue to play in the hopes that I might learn to achieve certain tasks in the game. I have begun to understand that they are possible, but it is far easier with help. I have not played with anyone else at the time of this writing, however, I hope to eventually finish this game. There are not a lot of hints that are helpful in game. Most of the "Tips and Tricks" I have read online are outdated as the game has been changed quite a bit, since they have been written.  It took me forever to figure out the islands and map.  Now that I have, it seems simple enough. The map is huge, but the islands are not really very big. Still working on other tasks, trying to understand the steps to completing them. This game is very unforgiving. Early in the game you are required to locate metal veins only they are located on other islands. The problems is, these islands are more dangerous and you don't have the materials to craft better weapons to defend yourself. I have put 25hrs into this game trying to figure out if there are ways around these constraints. There are not. I read some of the walkthroughs that indicated that at one time the dungeons used to be open, on the first island you had a chance of finding metal in the dungeons on the first island, now they are blocked and can only be opened by a bomb, but you need a metal frame to build the bomb. This game has effectively shot it's self in the foot. Way to go devs. I think I'm glad I didn't pay for it. I am sorry to my friend who gifted me the game though.  Also, you cannot get fish without a net? a spear, bow and arrow ( I can't even figure out how that works) or a fish trap?) And you need a metal bucket? to make a cooking pot? What? The metal bucket was something that should have been found on the first island, if memory serves in one of the dungeons. So sad........ This would have been a decent game if the devs hadn't nerf'd it so much.

_childDocuments_.review: Well I was really hoping this game was going to be as fun as the trailers made it look. I even played the demo before it released and was pretty pumped for what was to come. However, what was released is most certainly lacking. This game feels half finished. It feels like they meant to add a lot more into it but then couldn't fit it in. A lot of the mechanics are broken or just shouldn't work the way they do. A prime example of this is, if you play with someone else online, only the host unlocks the recipes that aren't connected to the recipe unlock tree. Your teammates will not be able to unlock the bomb recipe so you will have to craft those for them. Backpacks? They can buy it but won't receive the recipe. It's very frustrating and almost made us quit the game. But we decided to just finish it. Also, I think there needs to be better markers on how to make progress because honestly in the beginning we were just like uhh what now a lot of the time. One of the most frustrating parts of this game was hands down the tools. They break so fast. Like it's actually stupid. You are constantly repairing your tools just for you to maybe get through half a labyrinth and they are already worn down again. And it doesn't get better with the better tools you craft, especially when it comes to your sword. I don't know who thought it was a good idea to barely get any use out of the tools. The raids are pointless, if I'm being perfectly honest. You don't get anything special from them. They are the same enemies that you fought on that island before. They are more an annoyance than anything. Not really any point. Same goes for the treasure, the rewards for tracking it down just aren't worth it unless you're dead set on doing them. We did finish the game and honestly it was just lacking. Like there wasn't any reason to stay and there wasn't any reason to finish. They definitely wanted this game to have replay value but it frankly just doesn't. Just doesn't feel like a complete game. Maybe this will change in the future but we will not be coming back to this game unless major updates are had.

_childDocuments_.review: I really REALLY want to like this game! As kid's we'd use pencil and paper to play the "island game" of living on a deserted island and building huts, growing trees, etc. The Survivalists has charming graphics and good game design that gets overshadowed by the tedium of it. Unless I'm missing a mechanic unlocked later in the game, you need to craft basic items, like vines, individually and then combine them into other crafting before using that item at a specialist building to get upgrades to tools that will break unless you repair them. This is just tedious and worsened by the fact that you need to strip mine / deforest locations to get enough resources for one upgraded tool.This game works well as a skinner box drip feeding progression. With quality of life improvements like instant crafting of basic items (looking at you large rocks and vines), the ability to auto-craft basic items in advanced item crafting menus, and the addition of better automation (not a per monkey affair), I'd be willing to keep going. Maybe it gets better once you're a few hours in, but I'd have more fun in minecraft or don't starve by then.In short, this isn't a bad game at all. It's charming. I'm just not ready to spend multiple hours before it becomes fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't leave reviews because I just cant be bothered sometimes, even for games that aren't great. But this one made me upset.This game is absolutely, 100%, without a doubt, NOT worth the price. I have played games that have cost less and have significantly more content. You could literally play the demo and experience the majority of the game. I see reviews on here about how thats simply not true. That theres more content in the full game than there is in the demo. Yes, that's true. But not that much more. When you play the demo, you can actually see the crafting tree, most of which is locked. That is exactly what is available in the full game. There is no hidden crafts, there is no unlockable crafts. All of those little squares you see in the demo is what you get. Thats it. The monkeys. They're cute and I love them, but they are absolutely useless. They are annoyingly to train and can literally only do one thing at a time. Each time you want it to do something else, you have to retrain it. Even if its learned it before. Combat wise, its fine to have the monkeys around, but you really, really, really don't need them. In fact, my friends and I did a dungeon or whatever and the monkeys got stuck somewhere. We literally just abandoned them there because there was no need for them to help us with combat and it was too annoying to go and find ALL of the monkeys in our monkey hoard before we moved on. There are multiple islands, which you'd think would be great, right? Nope. The islands were very meh. Each new island has one or two new things on it - new ore, new terrain or new beasts. We completed the game without ever going into the swamp (I don't even know what the point of it was). When we finished the game, we realized that you could literally play this game and finish it in a few hours. It only took my group 8 hours because we took forever figuring out what was going on on the starter island. We got to the second island, set up camp then realized there was literally no point to set up camp. We blew through the rest of the islands by just going to them, running to the dungeon thing and then leaving. I will not be buying any more of their games in the future, especially not on release. TL;DR I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone. Everyone one of my friends who played this game ended up disappointed at having spent so much money on a game that wasn't worth it. If you are typically a casual gamer or like games that are simple and cute, maybe get this game on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Right, so, this game is only halfway good.This game is fun for about 10-ish hours if you're into no story, repetitive survival. Even if you're the type of person that's just interested in the monkey mechanic, building a base and collecting stuff etc., this game might be for you. I enjoyed those aspects of it for the 12 hours I played just because I'm the type of person who likes to build bases even if they're kind of pointless.What needs to improve:- Depth. There isn't a large variety of mobs in the game, dungeons are all very similar, basic exploration is very similar. I would literally take more decorations at this point if I could. Just give me something else besides getting a monkey and building a base with little to no furniture. Basically every aspect of this game besides the monkeys (which were frustrating to work with but a cool tool,) needs to be improved.- Goals. To avoid spoilers I'll just say give us side quests, a story, or something greater than just wanting to get off of the island. Make food slightly harder to get or even let us grow our own with the risk of our farms being destroyed via raids (which are very weak by the way if you have ANY amount of food on you.) Give me a reason to hoard, have more than a few monkeys if I'm not a base builder, anything.- Incentive to use important items. I spent 7+ hours on this game today and it crashed. I hadn't saved the game at all since I got on it 7 hours prior, so I lost everything before I could even beat the game which I was basically one step away from doing. Why didn't I save the game? Because there is no incentive to remind me to do so. You can sleep in your bed and skip night time but why? Nothing is harder at night, there is no increased chance of being raided, and it is SO unbelievably easy to make food that the whole "fill your health to max by sleeping," thing is worthless to me. It's not even annoyingly dark at night like other games make us suffer through so why the ♥♥♥♥ would I remember to use a bed?- Clothes. Seriously, making people spend an extra few dollars on a game that wasn't even worth $25 to begin with? I waited for this game for months because it really looked like it would be a game that WAS worth $25. It's the first game that I've ever counted down the days on and while clothes really isn't that big a deal, that combined with the absolute lack of depth was a serious ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ let down.All and all, even though I didn't technically reach the very end and won't be returning to it ever because of the big crash that wiped over half of my gameplay away, I can't recommend it. Sure my dopamine rose a bit here and there at how cute it was from time to time but other than that I have to look back at the 12.6 hours of my life just washed away... and for what... a monkey that kept getting attacked and dropping my box, or the one that wouldn't stop collecting grass when I just needed it to transfer pebbles to my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crafting table... I'm dead inside and it's this games fault. It's not the trauma I suffered through a few times in my life like the rest of us, or my failures as an adult; it's spending $25 on this game that I could have beaten in 5 hours max if I hadn't spent most of my time building a base that meant nothing in the end.

or automatically pick up appropriate tools from the ground or chests? / can't assign a primary job, must teach each time when switching / list goes on).this game is fun, but it's a huge buggy mess. in the end i just wanna complete the achievement and uninstall this game.+ variety of biomes, items, equipment, monsters, and secrets to discover.+ gets repetitive but good amount of quests.--- [hold LMB → run] or [dash → LMB] pretty much sums up the entire combat mechanism.- this game is so fixated on [dash → LMB], enemies are basically invincible if you don't do it.--- can't favorite monkeys on the Q menu, making favoriting monkeys utterly annoying.- storing and dropping shares the same icon.- buggy when entering or exiting instances.- storing or retrieving items from the portable storage is either buggy or broken.- storing is buggy; it often stores items in the nearest chest instead of the one with the same item in it.- buggy when picking up tools from the chest or the ground.- monkeys will stop harvesting even when there are enough resources nearby.- making monkeys follow the player and do their job simultaneously would be a game changing improvement.- need a "primary job" option, so they'll return to their jobs after whatever other tasks are done.--- no fast stocking or restocking option.- pain in the a$$ tracking bought or learned trinkets.- not enough map markers for cleared instances / treasure map POIs / lore finds.- running stops if you input a different direction while looting.- i don't know why but holding RMB never ran for me.- teleportation rarely works on the first try; you must trigger the portal several times for LMB to register at the destination.

_childDocuments_.review: The survivalist is an isometric Game by the Developers of Worms, Team17. You wake up next to your raft to find yourself stranded on an Island and now have to survive.The Audio and graphics are great it looks smooth and the audio fits to what you are doing.The Gameplay itself is quite fun, you have a crafting menu that is always accessible to craft the basic things you need.  Then you have the Blueprint overlay in which you can place certain buildings that you have unlocked and then you can deliver the materials to build them. Through the crafting system you can build things like a bed, a furnace, a table to display some item you found and other things.You also need to craft tools to use the crafting table or the campfire to cook food or to get weapons or better-quality tools which lets you always search for more materials so that you can get the tools you need.You have 3 resources, Health, Hunger and Stamina. Stamina is used whenever you do some action like running, hitting bushes, Trees or Rocks to gather materials but also while fighting and for your Dodge roll. In typical survival fashion you also have a hunger bar. This is a bit confusing because the Hunger and the Health bar are both in the same Icon. Your Hunger is displayed as a slowly emptying Heart while your Health is the red area behind your Heart. There also seems to be some sort of “heat” management in which you need water to keep you cool but I didn’t get to that portion of the game. You recover health and hunger by eating food you create through materials like berries or meat and craft the food item on your fire.Unlike other Survival games in which you are either alone or have other companions, in the Survivalist you either fend for yourself or you “tame” Monkeys and use them to do tasks for you. Yes, that is right, you can have a monkey army. This feature is probably the most interesting but also the most frustrating part of the game. To begin, you need to find a Monkey and if you do, they request and Item you need to give them. That item is a food item specifically for the monkeys, Monkey Meal, you create on your campfire and need a few very early game resources for it like a bowl from Palm leaves, some Berries and Petals. You bring the Monkey that Monkey meal and it will now love you and follow you and basically do whatever you teach him. Unfortunately, there is no variety to that, every monkey you encounter wants the Monkey Meal.As I already mentioned, you can teach the tamed monkeys that they should do certain tasks. That is a very interesting but also lacking feature of the game. Each time you want to give a Monkey a task you need to call them to you, which will call ANY monkey to you in the vicinity even those who you don’t really need, select them, which throws a banana to them and then you have to perform that task they should do like picking up an item and store it in a chest. You can give your monkeys and task you could also do from gathering materials, chopping trees, hacking stones or fighting for you. The longer a monkey does a task the more experienced they will get in doing it and they complete those tasks faster.But that is also what I didn’t like about the Mimic system, it is really just too clunky to handle on the fly. For example, the “teaching” is on a timer which means that you have to select the monkey you want to teach and then do the task or else you will have to do it again. That is problematic if you want to teach monkeys how to fight because YOU are the one getting attacked and you then have to call the monkeys to you, select them (I had to do that for each monkey individually but it seems you can also do that multiple at a time) and then do the task and hope that you don’t trigger a different task like clearing some grass.For the Monkeys to do any of the tasks you taught them you also need to give them the tools to do it. That is a good thing because how should a monkey gather rocks? With its fists? This is not Minecraft. The problem with this approach is that you can’t tell how long the monkeys will still be able to use the tools because they also lose in Durability. That is really problematic if you have some set to Fighting and their weapon breaks and now, they are just standing there and doing nothing.That is also the next problem if the Monkey Mimic system. It is far too easy to take items from monkeys you not really want. I followed a monkey around that was chopping wood to pick up the dropped items. The problem was that you have to pick up ANY item individually with a press of a button. That monkey ran past me and I took the tool away he was carrying and stopped working until I gave it back to him. That happened quite a few times especially in a fight. The monkeys do have an Icon over their heads which describes what they do or what the problem is but those aren’t really that expressive and I could find a description for them either.That brings to the next problem, ammunition. You can craft bows and arrows but without arrows you can’t shoot the bows. I learned that the hard way equipping two of my monkeys with a bow to fight enemies but they did nothing because they didn’t have any arrows and that in the middle of a raid in my base.Another thing I didn’t like was the crafting system itself. You have to craft things to discover other things in the crafting tree. I have to create Nails so that I can create an Iron Sheet to create an Iron Bat and then I can create iron Shovel, Axe and Pickaxe. I also need to have discovered a Hinge to make a pot for my new campfire. You are basically running for materials and wasting them on stuff you don’t really need or want right now. Other things like different walls do make sense in that regard.You can also build your base which I didn’t do because I didn’t feel I needed it. After a few attacks by bats at night, which didn’t go near my campfire, there was nothing attacking me. There was no Rain from which I would need to seek shelter or a roof over my head. The Walls probably could help me with the Raid but it came that early that I was still finding my way around the game to do anything really more efficient.Exploration on the other hand is quite satisfying. The world is quite big and you can discover bottles with treasure maps in it for special items like a Spear you haven’t build yet. You can also discover a goblin Village and as soon as you have the Raft you can explore other Islands. And that you have to do. Your starter Island doesn’t seem to have any Iron resources which you find on another island. The game looks pretty interesting on the first glance but is lacking severely in long term gameplay. You can’t build crops like your own garden for berries or other plants for food production which isn’t much of a problem because you only really need one “medium” food item for a day. The world “restores” itself after a while but you still have to run around, or let your Monkeys run around, and gather those resources.I spent four hours in the game and felt like I have seen everything I wanted to see. There was no real reason for me to go into the vaults because I didn’t feel that I was ready yet but it seem that I was more than ready for them.The last thing that bothered me is the way trees obstruct everything that is behind it. You can see yourself because of a blue-ish outline but I got stuck more than a few times behind a tree and a bush because I couldn't see it. In fact I got stuck a lot moving past obstacles, be that ruins, trees, bushes or whatever. Somehow you are getting caught by something which stops you in its tracks.The Game feels more like a good early access game, good baseline and a lot of room to improve. But seeing that it is a full release at quite a high price for what it offers, I just can’t recommend it. Play the Demo first if you want to check it out and see what you say about it after playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It is a very average game, but I had fun exploring the various islands and the monkeys were fun to work with. Definitely feels like a console port. Would recommend getting it on sale/with a bundle.The game looks gorgeous and I love 2D pixel artstyle so it was a plus for me.The monkeys are implemented properly and can do most things you want them to do. They also get better at the task they are assigned which helps reduce downtime more.  Just remember that each monkey can only one part of a specific task. For example: If you need to collect timber, make one monkey chop down the trees and another monkey pick up the drops and gather them in a chest.There are different biomes to explore, different tools/weapons to craft and use, different materials to gather and craft with, which is good.The game feels like it was make for a controller in mind and keyboard/mouse came as an afterthought. The buttons you have to use seem super random and counterintuitive + lots of actions map to only one button. This is my biggest gripe with the game and might be a turn off for many.I have noticed that some of the artwork (trinkets for example) look really unfinished, so that is something the devs can improve on. From what I understand, these artwork got added with the latest update so it might have been rushed out. Since the base game looks really nice, the drastic change in quality sticks out like a sore thumb.

_childDocuments_.review: It's basicly *Don't Starve together* But not as hard or weird.The controller key mapping is horrible and no way to change it.The default Keyboard & Mouse buttons are a mess, as if the developers has never played a game using mouse and keyboard. BUT you are able to rebind those keys!, altho it might take a while as the game is programmed to only use American? keyboard layout, so if you are from elsewhere like myself, the keybinds might not be what it tells you it is, so you have to go thru and change everything and test your way around until you got it right.The game itself is great fun, very appealing visuals, sound effects, everything.Controller/keyboard mouse - 2 out of 10 (If you somehow have it easy to learn the Controller buttons i guess 9/10?, and if you manage to figure out the keyboard rebinding 9/10?)Everything else about the game 10 out of 10.Edit: Every single time i try to play this with a friend, the connection to steam servers is interrupted, and we loose all progression (Not that easy to save when you are out and about). It's not on our end, I don't think it's the games fault.. We just happen to be THAT unlucky that steam decides to do server maintencence or something whenever we're gonna' play. _childDocuments_.review: The gameplay loop is fine and typical of a survival game but the crafting progression and the game as a whole feels very limited. The survival consists only of hunger (and thirst in some biomes apparently) which is satiated pretty easily and suits the casual atmosphere of the game. The Monkey system is a pretty creative solution to grinding out resources and building/crafting. However, after about 2 hours I had unlocked nearly every crafting blueprint and never had to leave the first island until I needed metal. With everything unlocked and no real need to set up a major main base (nor are there really any buildings that need a ton of resources which would necessitate a main base) I found the repetitive nature pretty underwhelming.Considering how little content there is and how essentially non-existent the "story" is, I feel no need to dive back in despite a pretty satisfying gameplay loop. It seems over priced - more like an Early Access release in terms of content. Maybe the updates they promise will flesh out more of what the game could be.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: The Survivalists is definitely on the more casual side of survival games, there is no degradation of items and resources, so place something on the ground and it will be there forever, but you still run foul of hunger and stamina, but not thirst, so keeping a few meals on you at all times is really called for. Especially since you'll be meeting a variety of enemies on the games many islands.The game is really enjoyable, especially in co-op mode, which lets you get together with 3 other people to explore and complete quests. While the game is limited in the number of resources you can gather, the items you can craft and build, as well as biomes, there is plenty of room for the developers to add extra content and continue to support the game.There are many hours worth of gameplay, the world is large enough that you will spend hours going from island to island on your raft and exploring them to find what treasures they hold. The game never gets too difficult, especially with many armed monkeys by your side, there are no major bosses to defeat so improvements can, and by all accounts, will be made by the developers to increase the content of the game and make exploring and controls better, which is where the game falls down a little.That all being said, The Survivalists is a great game and is definitely worth investing your time into. I enjoyed playing it on my own and with friends and is a much fun as The Escapists 1 and 2.Full review on

_childDocuments_.review: I have 17hs in the game and it's already complete. Played from start to end with my gf.The first i want to say is that user reviews from Steam should be re-designed. There is a lot of people who doesn't understand nothing about videogames; others are tired of every game so they see just bad games, and there is a lot of low IQ "opinologists" and ignorants about gameplay who literally destroyed the entire game in comments.The game is good. It works correctly. _childDocuments_.review: Not a fun experience. I have never once played a game where the automation was this poorly implemented. The lack of ability to queue up multiple orders and the default selection of crafting being infinite means that you have to babysit all your crafting because your monkeys will use all of your resources. Your monkeys will also often lose your resources while you're doing other things.What's worse is this game is painfully boring. There is so much more of it for me to see but I cannot even begin to bring myself to care.  Do not buy this game. I got it at a 90% discount and that's still 10% more than I would recommend for this experience. If you want a cozy farming game play stardew valley. If you want a survival game play rimworld. This game fails to be either.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks good on paper, but it's bogged down by a clunky UI, annoying combat, and an unsatisfying core loop. It shares the problem of a lot of survival-themed games where everything feels like another chore to manage.The core monkey mechanic is the worst offender. The mimicry teaching mechanic is fun thematically, but in practice it's a 5 step process that takes upwards of a minute to get a monkey to do something that it's probably only going to do for a minute or so until it runs out of its tool or resource. If you ever give it any other command you have to go through that whole process again. The idea of exploring other islands is fun, but it's crushed by the raiding system because every 10 minutes or so you have to run back (technically you can build a bed on the new island and set that as home but that doesn't really feel in the spirit of things since you're encouraged to build defenses in your base). If you hand your monkeys weapons to help you fight, you have to individually retrain all of them. Walls are mostly useless because enemies spawn sporadically around your bed anyway.The game would be markedly improved if monkeys remembered prior tasks and you can just set them through a menu. Alternatively, add the ability to equip every monkey with a weapon and a tool and have it automatically fight and then go back to work when there are no threats.As a general rule for these kinds of games, I really think simply removing the item durability mechanic would improve the experience. It would significantly reduce the monkey micro management and reduce the amount of time you spend on the treadmill doing the same thing over and over again. For the record - in real life, I've used the same axe/splitting maul, shovels, and pickaxe for 15+ years. I've chopped down trees, split logs, broken up rocks, and dug holes over this time period. I've had to sharpen the axe once or twice. That's the extent of the maintenance these tools have required and none of them have spontaneously broken.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for about 24 hours, and have escaped. I haven't explored the entire map or gotten all of the achievements (about 4 or 5 missing at the time of this review).Overall I like the game. It can be a little repetitive though there are enough biomes and enemies to keep things interesting. I have unlocked all of the crafting recipes for all of the equipment (cooking, smelting, work bench, etc.) and think there's enough variety of items to keep me interested for further gameplay.This is not your typical survival game; I've played other games on various consoles and this one focuses more on finishing the story rather than exploring. You need to get 4 keys, each at a different labyrinth. Right when you purchase a key (for a hefty price at first) the location of that labyrinth is revealed on your map. I would've preferred it to be given to you in the same manner as the treasure maps; this way you need to work a little more for it.You need to work to finish the game, even once you have all 4 artifacts from the 4 main labyrinths. That being said, the ending is the slapstick humour that you typically get from a Team17 title, so don't go looking for any big answers.Aside from a number of bugs and the lack of an option for new game plus, this is a fun game and I could see myself going back to it to play it all over again and then a few more times with friends. I've continued my game and upgraded my base and will be exploring more to see if there are any more secrets I can find.

_childDocuments_.review: It's absolutely jagging to see so many minor issues in a game this simple, specially after The Escapists. General gameplay, control schemes and UI are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and confusing, combat is eh, simple, there's no interesting story, the progression system is boring and easy to complete, quests are boring, and other mechanics just exist.In part of the issues, I could enjoy a game where I can turn my brain off, relax a bit and probably build some cool bases here and there, but the issues can pester you. Sometimes your character will be stuck in animation, or the game won't let you break constructions despite it giving you the notion it's possible for everything, monkeys seem to function well but it can become too bothersome to deal with, mostly because of the commands and UI being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Speaking of the UI, 90% of it could be done in a way that's not only more intuitive, but also more accessible. At this moment it's horrid with how they organized UI elements and certain mechanics behind multiple button presses, or having you to hold the same button you use to perform other actions, instead of assign it to another button. It's a waste of space AND time to navigate through the menus. A lot of space is wasted in favor of making everything look big, and in result, menus get compact, as if people have presbyopia while making you scroll a lot.Also the keyboard mapping is... outright dumb. How is this a 1-year old 2020 game that not only doesn't have controller mapping, but if you change your keyboard mapping, it doesn't really work? I assigned the Cancel action on my G button, yet the F button still acts as Cancel even if I assigned something else to it.You have a lot of possible keys here and there to use, yet many actions depend in one key, then why have all these actions be separate? I can't even mention anything about controller mapping because it's impossible to change it's mapping, DESPITE the game claiming full controller support.So yeah,  this game is a simple survival game that may initially resemble Stardew Valley, but cannot even achieve the good of Stardew Valley, so you might as well not bother with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: $25 price tag for a gameplay loop that lasts roughly 3-4 hours. If you enjoy doing the same thing over and over for no real reason then this is the game for you. In terms of progression you will easily reach a point with the tech trees and exploring that leaves you questioning why you're doing it in the first place, and that's pretty disappointing.The games premise is establishing a base, growing a small army of monkeys, and above all, exploration and surviving. The problem there, however, is there is no reason to establish a base, exploration is pretty lack luster, and the "tech trees" are tiny. You'll quickly find yourself asking these questions - Why do you need a base in the first place? Well, to store materials of course. Why do you need materials? Well, to make a base of course. Where do I get better materials? Well, exploring of course. Why do I need to explore? To get better materials, of course. Why do I need better materials? To make a better base, of course. The monkeys are arguably the most interesting feature of the game that, while kind of helpful and neat, are only a marginally helpful version of basic automation that still requires player involvement to keep it moving. Need to build a structure? Well, better get ready to manually queue up every material in the process and stand there waiting for 5-10 minutes for the next step _you as the player_ will need to queue up for them. Overall, it's okay. Not worth $25, but okay.

_childDocuments_.review: Survivalists presents a crafting tree progressive survival experience. You'll need to gather resources, process and craft to progress with food being your primary "Survival/Health" mechanic. As the game progresses you'll want to pass of simple tasks to monkeys you find while travelling further out from the starting island to gather more exotic resources and explore simple dungeons.Now I've thumbed this up but I have a list of issues with the game than have forced me to give up playing several times out of temporary frustration.I'm not sure how the third game based on this engine can still have so many flaws with the controls but Survivalists does. Perhaps they're targeting controllers and playtesting KB+M involves pressing space at the title screen. Regardless. Expect unresponsive key presses, dual use key functions based on positional context, combat that seems to aim based on movement, mouse or a combination of both plus a roll of a dice.The UI is similarly awkward, with function like renaming bound to a key rather than simply clicking/selecting the name box. This can also turn into a battle in itself with a totally different monkey renaming because I suppose a mouse hovered over something it shouldn't have.Ultimately these are rookie issues that shouldn't be in the game.This is lacklustre at best and rage inducing at its worst. The aforementioned issues with controls are compounded with scenery occlusion meaning you have no idea what you're hitting, facing or are trapped in until you explode in a shower of your held items as you die. Bring along some monkeys to help you out and you can be sure they'll just add to the mess of sprites piled into a central point like flies piling onto a poop.Raids are also single tone. I'm guessing these are designed to put some pressure on you to seek progression and upgrades. In reality they are telegraphed multiple minutes ahead, meaning you are often left just waiting for them to happen in the middle of a field so as not to encourage the spawn in your base with all its clutter. They're over quickly, rarely a challenge and really just waste your time.Now this is an interesting idea and they mostly work. They take a lot of the basic tasks away from the player so you can focus on other things. Monkeys need to be found or collected as rewards so you're still grinding hours into the game albeit slowly reducing. They're also quite smart in accessing resources, tool broken, they'll go get another from your inventory etc.This does bring problems. Firstly, again back to controls/UI, you'll be doing a Dr Stange level of finger contortions to first open the monkey menu, locate your monkey then select it for training. After this you will need to perform the task you want to train the monkey on. The monkey will then switch to that task type and ask for a tool if necessary. The point here is why can't I just click on a monkey in the menu and select the task? The end result would be the same without the finger-fu, actions, swapping tools etc.Monkeys also appear to have an effective range. This is explained in the game but there is no visual indicator as to where it is other than a monkey not doing a task you think it should be doing. Is it a bug, do I retrain, do I move a crafting station? Who knows. Also good luck managing a bunch of monkeys if you wipe their training.Dungeons form part of the late game progression with specific items and recipes inside which you'll need to complete the game. They are however not that challenging with puzzles being more gatelocked by you having the necessary number of monkeys available to perform tasks to open doors.The upgrade system is a mess of unlocking slots, trinkets, crafting and blueprint buying. None of this is telegraphed well. For example you can buy a backback blueprint to upgrade your inventory space. Even after buying it, you can still buy it again with no benefit. Likewise for crating the abilities, these don't indicate you have already crafted it and activated it. Why, WHY? To top it off, you're talking about using multiple crafting stations and on map characters to progress through this which just smacks of dragging out the playtime by forcing you to travel back and forth.As of writing I'd consider myself into the latter part of the game and have to say it's appeal is now starting to wear thin. Where at the start you're unlocking new items which feel like they're helping you become stronger and progress/survive on new islands. Moving past that you'll find you're doing a lot more "turn in item X" over there type things. A teleporter helps a bit but it's still largely unsatisfying back and forth work to inch ahead in the game and that change of pace is a mood killer.I'd be lying if I didn't say I've enjoyed the game, I've got a lot of good hours in on it and purchased it at a healthy discount which helped. I do however get very annoyed at its failures which hurt more as they seem so simple to resolve. It's a great concept, looks good but is let down with average implementation. How much that impacts your decision to buy I don't know but I hope this review gives you some pause for consideration before doing so.
