_childDocuments_.review: Having really looked forward to this game prior to release, I found myself really disappointed when playing the trial on my Switch. Ordinarily I prefer keyboard and mouse for anything strategic, but was really hopeful for a multiplayer game that worked on the console.  This meant I never purchased it, despite long term intentions to do so. Cue a few days ago, on the hunt for something to play, and I stumbled upon it again and wow am I glad I did. It works so much better for the PC, and yes their is definitely room for improvements, but it has definitely been worth the money paid for it already. I would really recommend this game for players, especially those who enjoy playing with others. Positives+ Great multiplayer option - works seamlessly with no issues and the teleporting purple box is fantastic! + Raids add a continued dimension to the game and keep you on your toes! + The addition of the latest update to allow further explorations has really enhanced the game.+ The monkeys are a well oiled machine that remove the boredom that often comes from crafting multiple copies of the same item - an absolute chore to manage on the switch but so handy now!+ Biomes and elemental impacts are fun to play+ Labyrinths add a good level of challenge, whilst other quests keep the game alive even once the crafting trees have been explored fully. + I love the shift between night and day, and the variance it creates in the world. + Great random creation of the worlds so constantly different every time you restart. + Art Style is quirky and fun, and really suits the gameplay. To Improve/Consider- Why can't multiplayer characters create bombs? It makes no sense :( - The controls - there are far too many tasks allocated to ctrl and space, and why on earth are blueprints not on B?!- Add a build up of difficulty in raids - they were too hard early game but are now far too easy. If not, consider adding further elemental impacts that add challenge to your base/ - Continue to extend the crafting branches - there is metal walls so why no metal doors? - Rotating objects : whilst I appreciate graphically this is a lot more work, it would really appease my aesthetic needs. - Labelling crates so when you walk up to them they are tagged for the items they contain.

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright, 6/10 with my experience as a solo player.  I'd only recommend it,  if you like these sorta survival games and don't mind the monkey management, you HAVE to use the monkeys at least to craft, which makes the game part management sim.  The monkeys make this game a lot more unique compared to other survival games.The fun parts of the game are watching the monkeys getting to work, exploring with them, doing dungeon stuff, sailing and finding new islands.  Unfortunately it's overshadowed by a *lot* of micromanagement and grinding.  The controls are also pretty awful, both on keyboard and mouse and on gamepad.  I frequently found myself swapping between them depending on whether I was managing inventory or not.The crafting and resources required to build are too grindy IMO.  Making a house, or several like you see in the screenshots, takes hours of monkey management, resource collection, resource refinement. The game seriously needs some more quality of life improvements on inventory and monkey management.  I wish I could just have a monkeys remember what they're trained to do at different locations with a button press, instead of manually showing them each time.  It's a lot of little extra steps.You can make your monkeys manage your stuff by just dropping it near chests, but when you need to look through the boxes and find something specific, it's hell.  No way to search, and no smart inventory features.  No auto-sorting.  Even the biggest box is too small, I quickly had 6 big boxes full of junk, and I was making sure there weren't split stacks.Recipes also don't show whether you have an ingredient in storage, so this often happens:  I want to make a sword.  Wait, I'm out of hilts, better make some more.  Wait, I can't make those, I'm out of iron sheets, I gotta make some of those first..  Wait I'm out of iron nails, cancel the recipe, start on these.  Wait, I'm out of iron.. time to figure out which monkey knows how to gather.  Wait, my pickaxes need to be repaired, wait I'm out of tool handles.  This sort of gameplay loop actually IS pretty fun for a while, I love management games, but I think I prefer managing slightly smarter monkeys in games like Rimworld or Oxygen Not Included.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played about 10 hours of this on release day and currently enjoying it reasonably.So initially it might seem like there's limited stuff to do  (like most have pointed out) but once you travel you'll find there's a bit more of a store/end game to try to find. I'm not sure how close I am to the end yet but there's clearly spots for an end game where I guess most people are turtling in their base thinking what they have will suffice. And while 80% of the game is that, there's that little bit extra that you need to do by exploring and fighting/raiding etc.The monkeys are useful and pretty much a requirement however they need some refinement in the future. The teaching aspect when using the monkeys needs some serious refinement. When pressing Q to teach monkeys it brings all the near by monkeys in and clicking on a single monkey can result in somehow throwing the banana to multiple monkeys in turn retraining them from the task you already had them on. Additionally when trying to get the monkeys to get things out of the chest they stand there sometimes despite resources being available and within pretty close proximity (can see both the work bench and chest holding the goods on the one screen - no doors or anything). Also in the game it says the monkeys can do ANYTHING the player can - turns out they cant repair spike traps. I'm enjoying the roaming aspect and have spent quite some time with mates roaming the islands. It was a lot better when I found the spy glass.I've encountered a few bugs so far. First one was when my mate jumped onto my raft and drove at me. This resulted in me being glitched into the adjacent rock formation (mountain not mine-able rock). I then couldnt get out. Luckily we'd just saved so just quit and reverted back. 1 of 2 mates had about 3 or 4 de-sync issues where he's running around doing things yet he's stationary on my screen. This was only 1 of 2 mates hence might be issues on our end. - unsure at this stage.I'd also like to see the ability to not have the monkeys automatically relight the forge and camp fires if the player opts in or out of it. I find my monkeys chewing up a lot of my charcoal to light a forge when I don't even have a need for it to be on. Maybe this could be solved by having the forge have both a charcoal slot and a blueprint slot and if the blueprint slot is not filled then the monkeys wont put stuff in it? Like wise for the campfire (except might need a charcoal slot in case people are trying to farm charcoal for their forges)I'd love to see a better UI for the monkeys. Like in the "tab" screen where you see monkeys I'd love to be able to set tasks for them in that fashion hence to keep a track of the monkeys better. For instance if I have 10+ monkeys in my base and I want to re-task one I could set quick functions eg; chop wood/shrubs, mine, put stuff away (pick up and put away), collect stuff for crafting (pull out of chests and take to relevant stations), build (blueprints), craft (food, craftbench and forge), repair, sentry (stay local and attack when attacked), defend, (follow the player and attack enemies as normal), follow (normal follow function). It might also be good if you could designate an area for the monkeys. EG; set the monkey only to be able to chop wood for a certain area. But overall sometimes it feels like micromanaging the monkeys and fixing up their ways can be more troublesome than doing the tasks yourself.I'm not much of a audio game guy hence haven't paid much attention to the sound track and the graphics are what you'd expect - if you're buying this for high end graphics look else where. The story seems fine, not very linear but that's probably good for an exploratory survival game. The gameplay overall is good. Is it worth $35AUD - jury is out on that one at the moment. If it was half that price I'd say go for it, but I think the mechanics of the monkeys need some attention to make it more enjoyable first. Now forgive me if some of this is already in the game but from my 10hrs game play on release, it doesn't seem too obvious. I look forward to seeing what the devs can to do keep this game interesting. Let me know if you want any questions answered :)

_childDocuments_.review: Having put in enough time to actually get somewhere in game, I have this to say about it.It is definitely a new game.I want to preface the breakdown by saying the game was... somewhat enjoyable, but that it also took WAY too much enjoyment out of kicking me as hard as it could, as often as it could.Pros:Graphics are good, combat (when it doesn't decide to just make you lose) flowed well (I only screamed at my game twice), and the music was top notch.Cons:Oh boy.Combat: The game could very quickly go from an easy fight to an absolute cluster, and there was neither warning nor much I could do once it decided that you needed to lose. The monkeys had a tendency to chase enemies, especially the melee monkeys, and I had one fight where I was clearing a small base (2 opponents) with two monkeys, and then both monkeys pulled at least three enemies each. I was notified when the six enemies (having defeated my monkeys off screen with little to no warning) charged me. I did not win that fight, as they hit locked me to death over the course of about three seconds.Also, enemy damage to items is a little on the silly side, losing a big chest to two shark attacks (I had to just quit for the day when that happened, it was full of all my FOOD!)Raids: This gets its on point simply because this is the game saying 'No, SCREW YOU!' Four or five enemies spawn AT YOUR SAVE POINT and immediately start wrecking things. This can happen at ANY TIME. When you are sleeping, working, rampaging across a dungeon on the far side of your island, who knows, you certainly won't before the game sucker punches you!Crafting: Enjoyable, but quickly gets repetitive, and the amounts are JUST enough to keep you from trying to... say, floor your base to try and keep the re-spawning shrubbery and rocks out. At least not until you get off the first island.Monkeys: The biggest issue I had was figuring out how to make my monkeys fight with me. All you do is give them a weapon and boom, they are ready to go. The issue was that they took so long to 1) notice enemy, 2) start attack or approach and 3) hit enemy, that it took me four hours to get them to hit something, and was finally solved when I was tabbed out too close to a hostile. Most of the time I would kill things before they started their absurdly long attack windups.And lets talk about monkey AI. It is so random I sometimes fully believe I am working with actual freaking monkeys. Put the monkey to do a job, and then activate the conditions to do it, and it will do 1 of 2 things. 1) Start immediately or 2) finish picking its nose and two seconds later actually start its task.And now... The big question: Do I recommend the game?I sit here, staring at the yes/no buttons, and curse Steam once again for a binary choice when it REALLY needs a slightly more nuanced system. As is... I say yes but. Because the premise is enjoyable, the basics WORK, and the nitpicks are just that, nitpicks. As the game stays out, and the devs keep patching things, the game will go from okay to great (hopefully).And now for the 'but.' Wait a bit, until they get some more balance patches out, and hopefully listen to complaints about raids being a total surprise AND starting wherever your save and sleep point is. Sane starting players put it in their base for convenience, until the first raid leads to a quick wiki dive and then it is left in the starting area for a stupidly long trek back to avoid raids. Yes I am bitter!
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: Shallow and unfulfilling, plays more like an early beta or late alpha than a fully released thirty dollar game that's received multiple updates. Which really highlights how awful the initial launch must of been.On the surface level the game looks and feels just fine. Nice graphics, a tangible progression system. But apart from that initial foundation the game offers nothing else, it presents a small spectrum of mechanical systems all of which have zero depth or satisfaction to them.The world is divided into several large islands and there's virtually nothing to interact with between them. At first the ability to build a raft and sail around seems fun, especially with how fast the raft moves, but ultimately it's just an excuse for the developers to waste the player's time. Since there's almost nothing to interact with on the water or between islands at all, the only reason why players sail is just to get to a destination. So while it's interesting at first it quickly becomes a pointless trek players constantly have to make back and forth to different islands with different exclusive resources. The sailing adds nothing to the gameplay experience it's just mandatory idle time waiting to reach the next destination; and the game has been designed around forcing players to do this many times.The islands are populated with a sparse amount of underground labyrinths that add some extra intrigue to the experience beyond just gathering and processing resources. But all the small labyrinths are extremely small, often containing less than three challenge rooms; and the challenge rooms are all mindlessly basic puzzles, are already empty or are just generic unvaried enemy encounters. The single large labyrinth on each island is at least a little more interesting but they never have any puzzles at all, it's just the same enemy encounters over and over; and the boss of each one is just an enlarged surface organism like a big bat or tiger. Straight up copy pasted, just stretch the model and make the health bar yellow. The labyrinths do replenish their resources overtime but the layout never changes so despite how few labyrinths there are in the game there's no intrigue in replaying them as the layout is always the same. The resources players get from the labyrinths aren't even very helpful past the early game. Even the randomly generated surface world loot chests with their copy paste quest descriptions give horrible rewards that seem to be only designed with the early game in mind.The game tries to do something unique with players getting monkeys to do work and tasks for them but it doesn't really matter since they end up being an entirely automatic system. It's interesting at first but quickly becomes forgettable and even tedious what with the monkeys being clumsy, cluttering and disorganized. It'd be more convenient and interactive for players to just make things themselves but the crafting progression is balanced around players using the monkeys to save time. So while the game tries to do something unique there it quickly fades into the background and even becomes a nuisance.In some desperate attempt to waste more time the game features a series of chore-giving characters who reward players with progression elements if they do asinine tasks for them. This chore system constantly requires players to leave the character and the island they're on to go do a chore, then come all the way back once it is done. There's four of these characters and they each have like ten chores; so that's around forty trips the game wants you to make. It's less excruciating after players unlock teleporters and speed boosts but players would need outside knowledge to know not to waste their time on the chores until they get those conveniences.The game is just full of pointless content otherwise. The player's base is periodically attacked by the exact same wave of enemies that do not scale to the player's progression at all. There's an entire system for luring and capturing organisms but there's seemingly no point to it. Small labyrinths and randomly generated chests are so unrewarding it's pointless to bother with. There's a select amount of base defense items but why bother when the periodic non-scaling enemy wave is so easy after progressing at all beyond the difficulty tier of the local island. Numerous food items with no particular advantages to using them. There are several environmental entities such as insects and old bones which serve literally no purpose but to be acquired for doing a single chore. The game is filled with random bones or flying insects, players only need one or two of each to do the chore, then that's it the player has no reason to interact with that aspect of the world ever again. Players also experience some kind of debilitation when in the volcanic and swamp biomes, yet there's no clear tell for what the debilitation even does. Players can craft an item to stave it off; but if the debilitation doesn't even have a clear effect then what's the point.The combat is just broken. Hits on enemies randomly won't register at all, constantly. Players can attack three times in a row and not deal any damage the game just does not register the attack at all; but it sure will register all the enemy attacks. Bats in particular have ridiculous hitboxes that randomly stray meters from where the actual model is. There's no failsafe for stunlocking so players can just get stunlocked for all their health. There's not even much enemy or weapon variety in the game, and the trinket system is so uninspired it doesn't add much to the experience either. This is one of those games that has charge attacks which are almost impossible to use due to players getting staggered out of them most of the time, and if you actually do get the attack off it's barely any different if not worse than a regular attack. The club charge attack actually deals less damage than the regular attack, despite requiring a totally vulnerable charge; and the only difference is it knocks the enemy back a little.Meanwhile the multiplayer is atrociously inconvenient. There's a permission system yet players that aren't the host fundamentally cannot craft multiple crucial items in the game such as trinkets or the bombs needed to open caves. Non-host players also can't break structures. Again the game literally has a system for toggling what joined players can do yet the developers didn't bother to add multiple crucial gameplay elements to that system and just locked non-host players out of that content completely. So you have to constantly ask the host to do things for you. But the developers were fine with players having their own special chests that can only be touched by the player that bought it, so if that chest is in an inconvenient place only the one who bought it can move it out of the way. And multiple basic achievements can't be unlocked by non-host players because it's just not working apparently.Overall this game has a decent foundation but it also has numerous mechanics and features built on that foundation that are just straight up badly designed. Features that literally contribute nothing to the game experience, are so unrewarding there's no point, are designed to just waste the players time or actually have zero point at all to begin with. Yet this game has been updated quite a bit since launch and it's still like this, being sold for thirty dollars no less. This game doesn't feel like it was designed by developers that know what makes survival games remotely enjoyable, and to an extent, what makes games remotely enjoyable in general. It's heavily uninspired, lacks content; and what content it has is either not worth bothering with or only exists to artificially drag the experience out.If you're interested in finding some games that I do positively recommend they can be found on my curator page .

_childDocuments_.review: I run the game on Window's 7, and I suspect that's part of the problem.This is what I've found out.Many things make sense, but it took me a little while to figure out some little things.  When you have a boy in your inventory, highlight your arrows and press space, and your will 'craft' a bow and arrow.  It wasn't the easiest thing to figure out,I like the game, and you can get working alone, or with one monkey.  Of course it was nice to have a monkey fill the fire-pit with ingredients, another to make the food, and a third to collect it and store it in the right small chest.Small chests are great, but since you need two hinges to craft a medium sized chest, and you need to leave your 'starting' Island to get the type of ingots to eventually make a Medium sized chest, I wouldn't worry about it in the beginning.And you'll be crafting a number of small chests for all of the things you'll pick up in your travels.  All of the stuff you'll need to set out your 'homestead'.  My first go-round, I didn't realize the Orcs could get at me from two sides.  I first tried walling and fencing things off at one side and they came at me from another.  Building traps is way better as it takes time to lay down enough traps, but you and your monkey's are immune to your own traps, and the raids now end quickly after they start.  For my second go round, I settled in an area bordered or two sides with large rock formations and the orcs kept coming from the same direction.  I built up my traps and used a few straw walls to 'funnel' the orcs into the traps including bone ones, allowing them to die faster.I managed to get through the crafting trees, and made a sword, but this is the biggest problem.  I'm on Windows 7, and have enough RAM, but the game freezes.  I know it says you can play on Windows &, but I suspect you'll run into problems with freezing later, which is too bad.  I'd figured out a great place to get metal, gold, and ruby(?) Ingots, and was crafting with them. it was on my return trip when I ran into another 'freeze' screen.  If you've got Windows 10 and you also get the game freeze, I'm sorry, but I don't know what else the issue could be.  In discussions someone mentioned the developers suggested  un-clicking the cloud save option, but I wasn't saving via the cloud.I'll see if I can get my save going again and can get the new ingots back, maybe I can finish another crafting tree.  I DO recommend the game, bt be aware of the freeze issue, I'm allowing comments and maybe I'll get a response about freezing with Windows 10.IF you can get the game to play I hope yo enjoy it.  In my second go round, I had p to three monkey's and was looking forward to getting them to work together crafting while I sat on my chair and watched.One thing I would like the developers to consider.  If you are on an island and you have a chest on the island, and you move to another spot on the Island, don't cause the monkey's to forget everything, like picking up things.  I DID like the fact that when a shark damaged my raft, while I was sailing, a monkey, with a tool, repaired the raft.If this continues to develop, I'm sure the issues with the freezing will be worked on.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I thought I would enjoy this so I bought it without just playing the demo first, turns out I don't.I don't want to be negative so quickly so I'll start with what I like:_Graphics_ - Might just be nostalgia, but I'm big on pixelated games, and this is polished and stylized, the game looks beautiful_Map System_ - You use a telescope to scout islands as you travel around, Its kind of awesome to see a survival game that uses these, its not a common gimmick and its one I happen to like._Crafting_ - You unlock crafting recipes as you play, the crafting tree is easy to use and it isn't difficult to figure out what you need to do for the next item_World_ - From the 2 hours of gameplay I got, there seems to be plenty of variety in terms of locations, I like seeing hints to answer certain questions like "where exactly am I?" and "What year is it?" being leads of intrigue instead of immediate answers right away, I'm interested enough I might watch someone else play this just to find out if they answer some of these questions._Environment_ - An extension off of _World_: I like hacking up all the random rocks, trees, etc. Feels satisfying and is most of what I did for these 2 hours, enemies have a healthy variety and have enough difference in combat behavior to keep it fresh enough._Sailing_ - I don't dislike it! Its nice to just go sailing and turn off your brain, though I didn't try to go any further than the second island so idk if you're limited at all, I didn't see any enemies around either._Polished_ - This game is smooth as butter, everything has little animations and effects to pop out just that little bit more, controls feel intuitive for the most part (Keybindings are a little weird, but not a con to me since I can adjust them)I feel this game has a lot going for it, but these next things took it down far enough that I'm not interested in playing, the main thing is I realized a lot of its features are done better in other games I already own:_Gimmicky_ - Some gimmicks I like (ex Telescope) but the rest just get in the way for me, the monkeys being the biggest threat to my enjoyment, the monkeys have to have purpose in this game so certain tasks take extra time (mainly crafting) and you need a lot of resources to get things moving. I was intrigued at first but once I realized the limited scope of what the monkeys can do and what my base will look like in the late game I found it irritating, I like to craft and gather my resources myself, its why I enjoyed Don't Starve so much, the monkeys might be fun if you enjoy seeing an automated base, to be fair, since I don't know about many games that work this way besides Factorio which has a completely different setting that you might not be into, its also way more complex.What sucks about this is this could have been a really fun mechanic, but its not as automatic as it would seem, and its hard to explain why unless I go into massive detail about how they work - so I will, at the very bottomI don't like the teleporters, they are at a weird place where you have to get much further in the game to get them but at the same time there are too many, as I found a pre-built teleport device on the one island I got to which seems to me I might only need to build the first one, while I do like that you have to put in effort on the teleporters I'm generally not a fan of fast-travel mechanics, I want to journeys back-and forth to be fun enough to never want fast-travel, and if there is FT due to huge maps then that's fair if they are reasonably limited._Deterioration_ - Like mentioned under Gimmicks, the monkeys need to have purpose in order to justify their use in this game, so what we have here is weapon deterioration to not only encourage gathering plenty of materials but also to keep the monkeys working on something while you're doing other things, I usually don't like this form of realism in my games, if I want realism I'll go outside. I have heard about games that make clever use of deterioration mechanics in order to add more tension and such, but this feels unecessary in a game with very simple combat and resource gathering - oh yeah......_Combat_ - I did say I like the enemy variety from what I saw, they have different movement and attack patterns but its all very simple, I might be wrong since I didn't get far enough to see any bosses or any more interesting enemies, the second island I wasn't even on long enough to see new enemies it was just more of the same and I had to head back. I also don't like the weapons, there aren't fun options or strategic differences or anything, its either bonk em' or bow em' - now you do have a counter technique if you dodge an enemy attack at the right timing, but besides that its not enjoyable to me. Monster Hunter World gets me there, I have never played a game with better combat mechanics than that, but this is a 2d instead of 3d so for something better how about... Enter the Gungeon, now that game had some fun combat, interesting weapons, on top of varied enemies, and this doesn't have to be a bullet hell to be fun._Survival_ - So this is a SURVIVAL game, right? so there should be things besides enemies to well, SURVIVE! We have hunger and thirst - no wait this game doesn't even have thirst, it has cooking with various ingredients and results but they all do the same thing, restore hunger and health, no buffs or resistances, I didn't see anything that does deals with poison either, if poison is in the game the enemies would probably apply it, for a survival game with environments the islands themselves don't actually do anything, no need to worry about bugs, the sun, rain, disease, nothing at all. Having hunger itself seems entirely unnecessary as you can easily get full hunger on just a stack of berries, so unless you want better healing there is no reason to go beyond that at all._MONKEYS_ - Man, I absolutely hate these things, their entire job is to automate certain tasks so that you can go around and do the things you want to do instead, sure they're cute and yeah it is nice on paper to just give them an axe and let them chop all the trees for you, until you realize that crafting items takes a lot of time simply BECAUSE you're meant to use the monkeys, I wish I had enough space in this review but I'm afraid I don't. If I ever get back into making videos again I'll happily post a link here somewhere.CONCLUSIONI wanted to love this game, I like the style, the polish, certain gimmicks, even the combat isn't that bad, just simple; The fact that the monkeys are essentially required by the way this game is designed is making me hate it instead, they're just too annoying to use and ignoring them isn't really an option either, so I dislike, maybe if mods show up to fix certain things I'll consider rebuying later but for now ta-ta

_childDocuments_.review: Survivalists is a nice looking, casual survival game that I think a decent amount of people will enjoy. When I tried the demo I knew I was going to buy it. And after buying it, I can say that I enjoyed it, and I still enjoy it. But i can't say that I can recommend it because of one main problem. The price. The game is too much money for how much content it in it. I've sunk about 5 1/2 hrs in it and will probably put a decent amount more of hours into it. But there isn't enough content for the 25 dollar asking price. Some games I play and after playing 50 hours I still have a ton of content to do later. But this game after awhile I can see what content is left and It's just not enough. The game mechanics itself are 50/50. The movement feels nice, the UI system is fine. The crafting is fine. But the monkey management system needs a little work. It can get very tedious to have a monkey do a simple task. Maybe I haven't learned all the way how to do it but as of now, I can't say I love it, but I get the idea, and its a good one. The combat isn't the best either. It's neither bad nor good, it's just there. Now I actually enjoy how the building works in it, I like that you can place blueprints to lay out how you want your house to look like, then you gather resources and place them on the blueprint and build. The graphics are pretty good. It's kind of a mix of 2d pixel with some 3d elements. The atmosphere and music are very fitting and flow well with the game. During the day you have this nice calm music and at night you have this slightly eerie music. Or when you go sailing it has this adventure type theme to it. It's all very fitting for each situation.I know this isn't a super in depth review for it, but this is just my reasoning on why I like it but I just can't recommend it at this point. If the game wasn't 25 and maybe was 10 or 15, I would gladly recommend it. But it needs more updates to make it to a 25 dollar price point.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good title for anyone looking to start or get someone started on survival games! It is also a great game for anyone looking for a low-stress survival/building game. I got my 70 year old Dad playing this and he loves it with over 187 hours logged so far and still counting (he took over the entire home island as his base).So here are the good, the bad and the ugly of it The Good:   The monkey automation is fantastic at this stage though it does need some tweaking to perhaps assign single monkeys to a specific workstation IE: this monkey only crafts things at the Forge and ignores other work stations.  The Islands are fairly large and robust with resources and threats. The larger labyrinths while being big are not so large that they are tedious to walk around in special thanks for the teleporter to the exit in the boss rooms. Crafting trees unlock automatically after making the recipe that precedes them. The hunger meter does not deplete so rapidly that you have to eat every 5 seconds.The monkey controls while complex seeming are easily learned even by a 70 year old with bad eye sight (Dad if you're reading this I love you XD ). Defenses are easy to build and easy to maintain if you assign a monkey to be on repair duty. The monkeys are best suited for crafting and base maintenance.  I generally take 6 monkeys with me 5 fighters and 1 to carry a chest.The Bad: The monkeys have hard limits that are either not defined not addressed or not shown. For example monkeys that water your crops will only water so many (no matter how close or far apart the crop plots are to one another) before it will water no more.  Monkeys that are assigned to craft things will leave the bench they are working at to go to another bench. This may not seem like a problem but when you have 2 or more crafting stations and already have a craft monkey and want to assign an extra monkey to help craft you have to be quick or you have to stop the first monkey to add the extra one. The reason for this is that the original craft monkey will run up to the craft station you are assigning the new monkey to and start crafting the item you are trying to get the new monkey to craft effectively blocking your mimic command on that monkey.Sometimes monkeys get blocked behind structures they have built IE: base walls. Monkeys can get "stuck" at sea. When you die the monkeys try to get back to you but end up spread all over the island you died on forcing you to run around and call them back. Cant breakdown rafts.The Ugly: You can't place any decorations or lights on side walls. Base walls even metal ones are easily destroyed by creatures such as orclings, boars, and deer (really deer and boar destroying a metal wall come on Team 17 that makes no sense). Some items after Expeditions update have no purpose (i'm looking at you dried seed pod husk) due to changed recipes, but were still left in the game. The sturdy bow is the only bow worth making the others are so weak it takes half their "arrows" to kill even a small animal.  Giving high tier weapons to monkeys seems to make the weapon weaker IE: monkeys do less damage then the player even with end game weapons.  The game does not give you enough quest tokens to buy all the trinkets but will offer you multiple copies of a trinket to buy from the hot air balloon guy. I found that out the hard way buy buying a trinket that was later given to me as a blueprint. Now there is a trinket blueprint I have to buy from said hot air balloon guy that I can't get because I used the token for it on the blueprint you can find and there are no more vendor quests to do to get more tokens as I have completed them all (i'm screwed lol).There are 4 unlock able trinkets that combine some of the higher tier trinkets into one I've gotten one unlocked and cant figure out how to unlock the other 3.  The one I have is the shield/speed run trinket. There really isn't a lot of info out their from the community like there is for some games (Heroes of Ruin) so a lot of it is trial and error and while that's great sometimes it's frustrating (damn you trinkets)My Last Word: Definitely recommend getting this game on a good sale (thank you summer sale 2021!!)it's a fun light hear-ted survival game. It does feel at times half done but get it at a good price and you wont be disappointed. (oh and if you're stuck on the Beast Master quest to tame two rabbits you need to bring them to the small structure next to him that's a miniature animal pen like the one in your crafting menu).

_childDocuments_.review: PROS- Nice 2d pixel gfx, not too pixelated and still has details in it.- Laid back experience, not stressful at all.- The monkey mechanic is a great addition to survival crafting base building genre, kinda like Ghost in Force of Nature 2. It provides automation to boring tasks.- The monkeys here is really a game changer than most games with the same genre, they provide a lot of help with micromanagements, and they can organize stuffs based on whether an item already in a chest or not. - Storage has a lot of item slots so even after tens of hours of gameplay, only use like less than 10 and categorized well (can be color coded). I use green for plant materials, red for animal product and body parts, black color for materials, yellow for food, etc)- Good item economy, items sink and gathered constantly, takes quite some time to be excessive. CONS - Control is a bit unintuitive, but not a problem after getting used to.- Unpolished. (cant rotate/move object, need to destroy to move item but get 100% mats back)- tedious at first until understanding monkey mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game and idea, bad implementation in my humble opinion. Pros:-Fun gameplay loop to play and chill.-I dig the monkeys, they make it quite enjoyable.-You can have 5 monkeys with weapons around you just killing everything in sight. Watching everything get smacked by a monkey with a metal baseball bat in hand makes for a good time.Now for the cons:-The monkeys get assigned tasks, but you can't specify it more. I can't assign a monkey to craft 5 metal bars while I go scavenging because it just takes every ounce of metal I have and shoves it into the furnace. I have to essentially stand there and wait to stop them.-There is zero way of stopping the crafting process once started. The monkeys just drop everything instantaneously into the crafting bench and quickly start crafting, not allowing me to change the crafting item. Sure I can tell the monkeys to stop, but then I have to start the process of the 'assembly line' over and its tedious.-The targeting system sucks. I can be standing next to a board and my character will just hit a tree. -Speaking of the character, why the heck am I slower to craft, slower while carrying stuff, slower with essentially everything there is to do ingame. Sure the game's main focus is the monkey system but holy heck, I am essentially moving around a useless doll while the monkeys do the work. Might as well make this game into a Sims game with monkeys and I can just control them all like an invisible hand over the sky.-The character is also sooo weak. You get hit by the boar maybe four times and you are dead. While the monkeys just standing around getting hit like seventy times and still standing strong. -The weapons are trash, atleast in the hands of your character. The monkeys can be equipped with a metal bat and use it for hours. You get a metal bat in hand, and maybe 100 hits and it breaks. The weapons need buffs bad because of how trash the system is with durability. I have never once seen a metal pickaxe last about 50 swings before needing a new one, at least until I played this game.- The resource collection is terrible for what you get out of the resources. I can mine for 20 minutes, get what I think is a ton of stuff and wipe out that 20 minutes of collecting for one or two recipes. Sometimes it's not even a full recipe, sometimes it's  20 minutes just to collect a part of a recipe just because of how much stuff you sometimes need per recipe.Now would I recommend playing this game? Yes, I would. All cons aside, it's a pretty fun game.Would I recommend this game for full price? Absolutely zero chance, buy the game at sale time when its 90% off at $2.50. The game is way too lackluster to have that huge price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: The Survivalists is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam to try rake in a bit more money for something designed for iPhones and Nintendo Switches.  This mobile app is a 3D rendered 2.5D retro pixel survival/crafting mobile game.  You wash up on a procedurally generated island (because level and map design is hard, some developers just can't do it, so they use repetitive procgen algorithms instead).  You need to survive, which means eating, bashing up trees with rocks, cutting up wood, building shacks and cooking coconuts or whatever else.  The depth of the game is good, it's a not-so-shallow survival game with decent crafting trees and mechanics.  It's a curious decision that the developers decided to waste all that effort with garbage, trash tier amateur presentation and pixel "a e s t h e t i c".  I know a lot of gamers have given this a positive recommendation, but I find that reasoning flawed.  Imagine how successful this game would have been if they took the same game mechanics and combined them with cutting edge graphics... but if course this is something they can't do, because they designed this game for mobile phones and Nintendos.  Why is that good for PC gamers?  It isn't.  Why does mobile phone pixelcrap belong here on Steam, at higher prices than it is on the app stores?  It doesn't.From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The mobile app features lazy low-polygon "retro" assets with crap 2D retro pixel "art" textures on them, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the early 1990s.  This very poor quality visual style is a method that lazy devs often use to disguise their lack of talent/interest in doing the graphics properly and trying to disguise it under the name of "art", or "We made it look bad on purpose", which really isn't something gamers should have to put up with.  Team 17 are capable of better than this, so it's inexplicable for them to steal the art style of talentless amateur hacks, and also very unfair to those amateur hacks who rely on bad graphics to try appeal to gamers.  It's unclear why the developers weren't willing to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets and high resolution textures for the mobile app.  It looks bad as a result of their decisions, worse, it doesn't authentically recreate the 1990's vibe the developer is hoping people will accept instead of doing their job properly, and that's just another reason to avoid it.Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the mobile app was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The mobile app is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.These technical defects push this mobile app below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is an eye watering $20 USD (for pixelcrap!!!), on app stores, it's still overpriced at $15 USD. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a $5 premium for a cheap mobile game just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  Because this is a mobile app, is priced to insult and gouge PC gamers, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.  Just who do they think we are?Now, I'm going against the grain on this review and I've made it pretty clear why.  If you still really, really want to play this game... don't buy it on PC because it's cheaper on the app stores, where mobile apps like this belong.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not really innovative or anything, but it's a perfectly serviceable survive-'em-up, if that's what you're looking for.The graphics are pretty cute and have a lot of charm, and the soundtrack is okay. Combat is kind of clunky, but it works, I guess? Crafting is grindy and inconveniently repetitive, but you can set up a chain of monkeys to automate things once you get a couple of them, and that makes it a bit less bad. Also your inventory size is way too small, but again, you can make a monkey carry a chest for you to store things in and that sort of helps. I'd rather have a backpack or something to add more hotbars to my own storage, but at least there's something.Progression seems a bit like Valheim-but-2D: use all the resources available to advance through technology tiers, then take a raft to another, higher tier of island to repeat the process and so forth. It's a fun loop, though sometimes figuring out where you're actually supposed to go next can be difficult, and result in a lot of aimless sailing about hoping to end up in the right place. There's also some apparently procgen quests you can find in bottles on the beach; the rewards are not usually worth going out of your way to do, but they exist, I guess. The little dungeon-type places you can find, called 'vaults', are kind of obnoxious, with some obtuse and ill-explained puzzle solving needed to clear them, but you can usually figure it out after a lot of frustration.Overall, it's fun enough to be worth playing around with if you can pick it up on the cheap, but it's not doing anything other games don't already do better. Like nearly all games in this genre, playing with friends definitely makes it a better experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to like this game a lot :(The game really feels lacking. It only took a few hours to get to the end of the crafting/tech tree.That could be ok, if it was not for the fact that construction crafting is a core part of the gameplay loop.That loop also fails in that dealing with the monkeys is really finicky. Some of the status icons are not at all intuitive and don't have any hovertext/tool tips. The conceit is that the monkeys mimick what you do, but it would be easier to just assign a task through some sort of drop down, since there are a limited number of things you can have them do. Then if you get attacked, and a monkey gets knocked out, it resets the monkey's orders.The combat aspect of the gameplay loop is not super satisfying, so that aspect also ends up being lacking.

_childDocuments_.review: The Survivalists is a really charming survival crafting game with some cool adventure mechanics thrown into the mix.So you start off stranded on an island with pretty much no materials and a tutorial kind of walks you through the basics of crafting and picking up materials and eating to restore your health and hunger and by default you have a certain amount of items you can craft yourself.And it is represented in this crafting tree and from the start you only have this hand axe you can craft but as you craft things in the tree you unlock more and more things you can craft.You also have another crafting tree that allows you to craft things like beds and other larger items.And I really liked this concept at first, it gave the crafting a unique spin in that it had a sense of progression to it instead of just having to learn or find new recipes in the world.There are also monkeys you can get as allies and you can have them do honestly anything you can do. So if you go into monkey mode you can tell them to follow you or you can tell them to watch something you do. And so if you fight enemies in that time and they have a weapon you give to them they will fight with you. Same goes with collecting materials, crafting things, chopping down trees, and this seems like it could get really deep really fast. The game is a survival crafting game and with that comes a couple mechanics that annoy me a decent amount. The hunger mechanics got a little annoying, the smaller inventory when needing to collect a ton of different materials is a little annoying, and also the way the crafting trees work can be a little annoying as well.At first, those crafting trees are really awesome. It gives you a sense of progression and everything but then I hit a point where I knew I wanted to go to the island to the west of me but I needed a raft. And I couldn’t craft a raft already so I just had to spend several days crafting completely random items in the crafting tree just to unlock the ability to craft a raft. The crafting tree system really worked for me up until the point of me having to craft completely random things I didn’t want to craft at that moment.The game definitely feels unique and has heart which is definitely what you want in a game and there definitely are adventure mechanics in the game with the dungeons and keys and everything and I know I haven’t even scratched the surface of all that but at its core it is a survival crafting game.So if you are into these types of games I think this will be your game of the year or at the very least a game you can sink hundreds of hours into. It has an immense amount of charm and polish and the crafting mechanics are super deep, the monkey system seems like you could do some crazy stuff with it plus it has online co-op which is huge for these types of games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: Fun interesting game played either on your own or with a couple friends! The monsters are interesting and varied, the monkey management is interesting to learn and perfect and at times hilarious. Adventure feels worth it and not absolutely terrifying, and I absolutely love the music when sailing to new islands! So so worth a purchase and play!

_childDocuments_.review: -- UPDATE --So below is my original review, and I double down on what I said: The first update arrived, and it's much more than I even hoped for. A ton of stupid things fixed, some nice things added, and a promising roadmap for what's to come. Buy this game, it's alot of fun already, and it will be even more fun soon :)----------- Original Review ------------Don't listen to the negative reviews that say the Demo is 80% of the game. Those people don't seem to get off the starting island is my guess. You'll be harvesting alot and putting your monkeys to work most of the time, so that's something to keep in mind. If you like setting up systems and growing a base & stuff, this is definately a game you'll enjoy. There are some bugs and glitches still, and the way you interact with the monkeys feels a bit wonky still at the time of writing. That is really annoying since that's what you'll be doing most of the time, but the next update will already fix some of the most annoying things.Conclusion:It's early, not very polished in some area's, but I see the same kind of potential as I saw at the early days of Terraria. With that I mean that the core gameplay is a great concept with alot of potential, and it's already a ton of fun yet a bit limited. I do have  confidence in the developers as the next update already will touch some really important annoyances. On sale: do it, no doubt. Not on sale: do you like finding out ways to make your systems work and also adventure a little bit (the temples are alot of fun!)? Also go for it, but be patient for the developers to iron out some weird things. If not, keep an eye out for updates, no rush :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: The game does not have a particularly long play through but it was still charming and enjoyable. The length of the game really comes from the time investment involved in getting the ridiculous amounts of materials required to build things and set up a nice base. I suppose that is where the charm lies in getting monkeys to do the bulk of the labor for you while you can still explore or just watch them work diligently. _childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to get this game. Emphasis on the word "was".I was hoping to get a great survival game that can scratch my top down survival itch after burning out on Don't Starve and Don't Starve Together after 600 or so hours of cumulative game time. Sadly this game ain't it chief. The monkey automation is unbelievably janky, combat can be fun but is buggy and some hits just don't register or you do a "phantom" strike that doesn't do damage but still drains stamina, there isn't much enemy variety at all, and there just isn't any content that is fun to repeat.This game is a massive, massive, MASSIVE disappointment and I highly recommend that you stay as far away as possible from this until the devs add more content or put the game out for 70% or more off. _childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: Simply way too many problems for a $29, full release game.  It feels like an Early Access at best.Also, beating 80% of the game with previous demo experience within just 4.2 hours is no excuse for the price tag.When I played the demo a few weeks back, my friends and I were super excited for what's to come.However, the problems existed in the demo persists in the release.  The content is also very shallow and limited.Monkeys being a huge part of the game is very hard to control.  They would instantly forget what you have taught them if you change their job.  Plus it's very easy to make mistakes such as this or swap your item with them due to the clunky control.The monkey selection tool is minimum 1x1 tile, which means if you have multiple monkeys standing in said tile, you will have to select them all and mess up your automation process.  This can be dealt with using hotkeys only, but that's not as intuitive as the built-in GUI.There are also abandoned camps with builds around.  However, there is no way to remove them.  So if your base is built around a rogue campfire, your monkeys will continuously feed the campfire with firewood or get stuck on it, breaking your entire automation pipeline.Monkey names are generated by the local client, always.  Which means their names desync when playing multiplayer and makes the brown fur balls even more confusing to distinguish from one another.Also monkeys are not smart, they will fuel your furnaces till the end of the earth even when there is nothing to be done on it.  Not so much of an issue as your campfire generates more charcoal than it can consume, but a pointless resource sink nevertheless.Collision is also box-shaped and almost as large as the tile.  You have no way to path through a forest with ease unless you chop everything down.And there's also regeneration of the natural resources that spawns in your base which is painfully dumb compared to how Don't Starve does it.I could go on, but there are just so many problems that suggests this game was thrown to the market without any play testing.  And even when demo players saw these problems weeks ago, non have been addressed.I do not recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited to play this game, unfortunately for me, it was a disappointment. Why couldn't I just put some tools in a chest or on the ground and the monkeys will go fetch them on their own? I've played for about 7 hours and most of that was with extreme patience. I know its still in beta so I'll come back in a few months and see if anything has improved.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not about survival. It is the Escapists - Castaway Edition. Your mission is to escape, not survive.I wanted to like this game. The game is beautiful, and the soundtrack is amazing. But at this stage, as I have passed the two-hour mark, I am just playing for the achievements so I can uninstall it.The game itself has promise, but there are just too many things that infuriate me about it. These include:Having your character moan at you because "My monkeys can do this!" while your builder monkey stands and stares at you makes me want to pull my teeth out.Want to build anything above the basic tier? That is fine, if you build something trivial first because if the monkey teach timer runs out before your character can complete it - they do not do it.Getting attacked or starving to death because you started to craft something and are unable to stop. Or my personal favourite - "had your hammer equipped by accident" while attacking an enemy stood over a blueprint.Spending ages setting up the right monkeys so that they follow you, and are set to combat mode, only to have to do it all over again when you reload is incredibly annoying.Playing "Lets guess where the monkey put it!?" because there is absolutely no rationale as to in which chest they put things.Playing "Lets guess where the monkey put it!? - part two!" - retracing your steps because your monkey dropped the chest they were carrying is not fun!

_childDocuments_.review: I played this co-op with my boyfriend for the most part so far, and a bit solo. It has a relaxing atmosphere, the game's not difficult either while fighting (although I'm not a big fan of the stop-motion style of swinging) or managing resources. The game in itself is pretty repetitive in nature, gather resources, fetch monkeys, unlock crafting recipes, do the main dungeons (because the side ones aren't even necessary imo), get to other islands to fetch new resources then build the galleon, which felt more like a resource dump than anything else.Now the worst part is that while playing co-op I didn't get a whole bunch of achievements because only the host would get a solid part of them. I wasn't getting recipe progression or monkeys of my own either... which means that if you want any of that you have to go to your own map where you are the host and progress with your old character from where you left off. Even by getting a small backpack in the early game, the inventory still felt way too small for how many things were dropping around so you're gonna spend a lot of time manually throwing useless things out of your backpack.I would've wished for the NPCs to give us more interesting/different tasks, instead that was mostly just "kill this, fetch that".. and they're not necessary for finishing the game, totally skippable. The lore is found through the journal logs of different adventurers who got lost/ died on the islands in the past. If you played & got sick of the other more popular survival games then maybe. Just wait for a sale or get it in a bundle. Also keep in mind that on one hand people claim this game is abandoned (because it hasn't received updates in a while) while on the other hand I've seen the developers answer to some reviews saying they're working on it. As the game sits when I wrote the review, I still believe it deserves a try keeping in mind what I said before.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING GAME! awesome soundtrack and a lot of love has been put into it however, if your expecting more updates? then im sorry to disappoint. its been a year of radio silence from the devs with no feedback at all, if you really do love survival games. its pretty good all though long term you may feel disappointed. also amazing with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very pretty and cute, it has a lot of concepts I really like and I was very excited when I first heard about this game. However sadly it isn’t what I had hoped. Its by no means a bad game but theres just a lot of things that make me bored after a couple of hours of gameplay.There is very little challenge to this game, all materials are very easy to come by. The combat, whilst annoying are not very difficult bc even if you die you can just go back, pick up your weapon and finish the job. This is even more true for the raids. The monkeys, whilst fun in concept are a big hassle to set up:use. You have to use the monkey screen to assign them anything, however when entering this screen ALL your monkeys show up even if they already have jobs, and often times it’ll select multiple monkeys even if you don’t want it to. When they get “taken out” you have to “reteach” them what they have to do. If you want your monkeys to follow you they loose their task and there is no other way to reassign them. When I have warrior monkeys with me I constantly accidentally give them my tools bc they keep walking through me or stand too close. And overall its just a hassle. I would really preffer it if you could jusy assign them jobs through the screen where you give them hats and change their color and name. Another thing is that there I feel theres little point to going into the vaults and labyrinth (I will admit I haven’t been to the latter one in my gameplay) bc the loot you find there you can fairly easily make yourself. As for the artifacts they can be found all over the land as well. So theres no special reason for going there. The swamp and dry desert area’s are annoying and I just avoid them bc they don’t hold any resources I NEED so I have no reason to actually go there. I’m sure theres much I haven’t mentioned but I cannot currently remember what (gotta love having ADD)I really hope there will be updates to this game to add content and make it more challenging and fun, and also improve on some of the mechanics, specially the monkeys, but as of right now I sadly cant reccomend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: If I could refund I would. I'm so disappointed in myself that I purchased a game on the day of release. I know better than that but I really enjoyed the demo and about 15-20 hours of game play. That's when everything fell apart. My monkeys will no longer take items from chests (or ground) to restock my forge & workbench having to do that manually takes it's toll on my psyche and is not how the game was intended to be played. Two of my monkeys will occasionally return to where I found them (if I don't give them a task at my base). Monkeys do not sort, period. You have to constantly manage your storage chests with no way to label or color code that I could figure out (using a controller). At one point I was just thinking about keeping everything on the ground because it would've been less of a hassle. I've placed chests next to my forge and filled them with all the metal resources but left room for more items. When the item is produced the monkeys will often take it to the chest that is furthest away instead of the one right next to it and no there were not any like items in that chest. My forge and workbench have stopped accepting components from me or my monkeys (when they were working), twice. I had to destroy them and build them again. I feel like I'm beta testing a non-AAA title that I had to pay $25.00 to get into. I did contact support about my issues and they gave me the usual song and dance. I'll keep an eye on it for a little while and see if they actually fix the issues. Buyer beware. If you're interested in the game read the forums and wait until it inevitably goes on sale due to terrible launch reviews.Update: I played on the beta version (experimental branch) after this review and found that they had fixed the issues I was having. Once they pushed the update/patch through I left the beta and all of my saved games seemed to have been corrupted (which I believe I was warned about). That was OK as I wanted to start fresh. I've played for some time now. I have not run into the issues that I had at launch and that's a good thing, kudos. Each recipe requires more components which only makes the progression slower, meh. You run out of items to build so quick for a survival game. Once you figure out the mechanics the replay value is non-existent, imo. I became bored and had no desire to finish my game. I've decided to uninstall it for now and will keep an eye on future content updates and start a fresh game. I still cannot recommend this game at it's existing price point because there is just not enough content. I'll say it again, I feel like I paid $25 to beta test their game. Cheers.

_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in this game feels very... slow. And tedious. I just spent two hours gathering materials to build a wall around my tiny little base because I was randomly attacked with no warning by a horde of goblins which literally destroyed everything I had built.Combat feels slow and clunky.Building things is slow and clunky (why do I have to equip a multi tool EVERY time I want to build something? If it's in my inventory, just let me craft without switching items. Just one more button to press in a long series of buttons that need to be pressed to build even basic things.)The monkeys are a cute idea, but having to "program" them EVERY time I want them to switch a task is .. slow and clunky. Let me teach them a few things, then switch between those things without having to re-program the monkey every time.The graphics are nice, and I like the idea of the game itself, but it's just so frustratingly slow in ways that it doesn't need to be. Hopefully with future updates they'll add more content and more convenient ways to craft (since that is the focus of the game).That said, the "not recommended" rating is more of a.. meh? rating. I don't hate the game. If you really enjoy survival and crafting games, you'll probably enjoy it. Maybe multiplayer is more fun, I haven't tried that yet.  It's just quickly becoming more frustrating than it's worth to me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept and nice graphics but not worth it. Janky across the board from placing things in the world to the crafting system and menu navigation (renaming, selecting items, etc.) Co-op has significant restrictions on non-host players limiting their freedom to play (limited monkeys they control, non-hosts cannot destroy objects). Saving works inconsistently - sometimes the game will not save for whatever reason (my friend and I lost 4 hours of progress despite saving multiple times at the bed in that time frame).Ultimately, the game is interesting and has potential, but with the short length combined with the jankiness and bugs I would not recommend this game at full price. Get it on sale and go in prepared to deal with unrefined systems and hope your game actually saves. I would also recommend playing single player as it seems that was what the game was intended for.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly do not recommend this game, if you expected a game with a decent amount of content and replayability, this isn't the game for you. There is little to no content and you experience most of the content in less then 3hours, its not worth the asking price and If I could I would refund this game.The Tech tree is tiny and what exists is mainly useless.Building in this game is pretty much pointless, you don't need a permanent base as everything is so easily built and there is no indepth tech requirements.Majority of Cooking is next to pointless, since it really only gives you hp and potentially useless buffs. _childDocuments_.name: The Survivalists

_childDocuments_.review: So we have this exploration based game, all about fighting your way through the enemies to release the monkeys. It's just not fun anymore, I've run out of content. Crafting only goes so far, and gets there really quick, I expected another crafting bench for more options and I get an endgame weapons and tool forge. Which you are meant to raid temples for, after grinding a small fortune for each key. Anyways I'm not going to be complaining about that grind because I'm giving up on it early. This game is not based around automation, Its a shallow exploration game with a bit of crafting. Stuff like "gift/fetch quests", "need to eat", and "automation" are tacked on because of how easy they are, yet your character constantly complains about how it would be better to automate this with a monkey, and automating crafting is pretty handy if you have 2 monkeys, and in doing so you are automating all bench jobs and building jobs in an area. But the amounts you need are so low, you might as well help craft or just do it yourself, and after your done you break this automation by assigning your monkeys back to fighters. Because it's time to get back to exploring.. There is no armor equipment or accessories.. In fact the only thing you need to craft would be a club or bow for your monkey guard, and a campfire to cook on, Other than cooking theres not really anything else you need to craft or build aside from the raft which requires you to do enough exploring first.If you wanted to make an automation game, You should have started the logistics chain with something infinite, like a banana tree, make the banana production increase the amount of monkeys that can work etc.. You don't have any infinite ideas that you need to keep running. Just in this exmaple if you needed production or housing in order to "hire" monkey henchmen to fight with you at least you would have a reason to remove them from the hunting party. This game is a very nice starting point to take it in any direction you want by expanding on any of these half assed systems. But unfortunately very little has changed in the 2-3 years since the youtube videos were published that i just watched. Looks like the player inventory has doubled, The raft is harder to build, and monkeys are much rarer. Pretty disappointing to see how much of a game you've worked up to, but in the end did "the bare minimum" with.

_childDocuments_.review: , by the studio behind prison breakout game , has your basic "explore and craft to escape the island" plot.Hoo boy, is there a TON of crafting in this game.  No raw resource that drops is of much use without modification, not even the fruit that you can eat right away.Recipes come in three basic styles.  Items crafted By Hand must have the items in your inventory.  Items made at crafting stations or as blueprints set on the ground do not need you to have all the items in inventory at once.  Instead, you can put just a few at a time until you have all you need.  These latter two styles also require the use of a "multitool," but it looks and sounds like a hammer, unless it's stirring food.By Hand and every crafting station have their own crafting trees.  You unlock recipes by crafting the ones before it, so you cannot skip over all but the final recipe in the branch.  Crafting trees are organized logically, though.  Crafting a core component for the first time might unlock recipes using it, or you go through a series of upgrades, or other items in the category.You'll find extensive crafting trees in another sense.  The more complicated builds require raw materials to be combined into components, and then those components are used in the end build, leading to possibly a couple dozen total steps from raw components to final product.  Crafting also takes time, from a second or two to an entire minute.  A good chuck of game time is waiting for crafting to finish.  (And just you wait until the endgame's build!)Of course, you'll need to collect the raw materials before you start crafting.  Your personal inventory is limited to just 10 slots, but an upcoming update gives you a backpack.  Worse, there's no equipment slots.  You can wield only tools and weapons, no armor or amulets here, and they must be held in inventory.  And those tools and weapons suffer from durability.On the other hand, the game is quite generous with most resources.  The game map itself is , around the size other games might consider for an entire planet.  It even resembles a planet, with "continents" that are actually several procedurally-generated islands, plus sandbars and rock formations.Your midsize starting island has just the first, easy half of the resources with nothing more dangerous than a few aggro animals and enemies.  More dangerous biomes with advanced resources await you on larger islands.  Any one of the large islands contains a bit of everything, but the endgame requires you to visit the other large islands.Another way the game is generous is in respawning treasure chests.  These spawn when you find a message in a bottle that gives you a "treasure map."  Smash the chest open, and you'll find what the map says:  Food, a tool, a weapon, or other items, and gold.Anything in inventory can be dropped and safely left to persist forever.  Excess harvested resources can also be safely left on the ground, or disposed of in an upcoming update's refuse pit.Storage chests are a bit more than their usual godsend.  While you can't color-code or label them, you can pick them up and tote them around, even while full!  This is like an extra or upgraded backpack.Monkey friends are also here to help you.  Scattered on the islands are monkeys either trapped in cages or running wild.  Free a caged monkey or give a wild monkey the gift they desire, and they will become your helpers.This becomes a literal "monkey see, monkey do" situation.  Toss them the right tool or weapon, enter Monkey Mimic Mode, and start the action you want them to do, and they will do it.  Your monkey friends can do any major game task you can do, from harvesting, putting resources in chests, supplying crafting stations, crafting, and combat, with the ability to level up beyond what your poor static avatar can do.  They can also carry chests.The crafting system limits the monkey helper usefulness.  You can't tell Caesar or your own avatar to make axes until you run out of supplies; you have to keep feeding each individual recipe or see that the monkeys do it.  It is possible to set up a whole supply-and-crafting chain, but there's not much room in the safe alcove you start in, and you'll have to keep monitoring it.  The monkeys also have a tendency to lose focus and wander off once they don't have anything to do or once they wake up after getting knocked out.But the monkeys are GREAT for harvesting resources and gathering them, and are a HUGE help in combat.There's both hunger and stamina mechanics here.  Hunger grows with activity.  Get too hungry, and you lose health.  Stamina is of the "lemmee catch my breath a moment" variety, and only becomes a problem in combat.  Naturally, the food you cook act as potions and buffs.  Gathering enough food is a slight struggle until you put together a hunting/bodyguard posse of monkeys and have the metal to build an upgraded cooking station.It seems that every time I draft a review before finishing out a game I have to edit it.  Usually, this is to the negative.  This time around, it's to the positive.I had a description of my annoyances with this game. (You have a surivival game on a bunch of islands, and you have neither farmable crops or effective fishing???  The raids are devastating to your early base!)But, as I was finishing the game, the devs released a beta branch with a ton of features and tweaks, many courtesy of player feedback, that were meant to be eventually folded into the main game.  This branch promises to take care of most of my annoyances.  That patch will likely be in the main game in February or March of 2021.One annoyance I had that might not be in that patch is how the game deals with respawns.  When you die, you lose all that is inventory.  (Not sure if the upcoming backpacks will also lose items on death.)  Sometimes, you respawn right where you died, or at the save point.  But other times, you respawn on a beach elsewhere on the island, forcing you to run to your items through dangerous territory without a weapon.  Fortunately, it's the same spot, so a player can just leave spare weapons nearby.Get past the annoyances and such and you'll find a good endgame, and a cute finale.  A final build to escape the strange islands will take hundreds of raw resources and a multi-step process.  Builder monkeys will help shave down the crafting time here.But even then, you'll still need a few items housed in temple dungeons, and guarded by (disappointing) bosses.  To enter the temples, you'll need to buy keys off the game's lone shop.  In my game, the procedural randomness placed one temple smack in the middle of a dangerous island, but the others were all right off a beach.Those temples hold some interesting and unique puzzles, including  building so you and your monkey pals can pass over gaps.  Another puzzle type involved getting your monkeys to emote (wave, sit, handstand) on a trigger plate.  It was difficult to tell when the emotes were properly registered.The game offers a mulitplayer mode, only of the "come visit and help" sort.  Your friends can take the place of monkeys, including the emote triggers in dungeons and more standard pressure plates.  They can also bring up to five monkeys with them.I struggled with this game at times, but was still going to recommend it because I could finish it and because the devs were listening to the players and tweaking and adding stuff.  The tweaks that might have already come by the time you read this will definitely make it a more enjoyable game.
