_childDocuments_.review: My review tells some spoilers but i personally don't consider them detailed to a point where reading will ruin the experience or storyline. They're just general points in the game e.g. places and progression. HOWEVER the ending is detailed so it'll have major spoiler warnings. With that out of the way! I've broken it into the beginning, middle (The Forest), review, ending Pt 1&2 so skip around to what you want to read. If you want to read my thoughts of the game and its general vibes without spoiling the ending stop reading after the review section. <3 At the beginning of the game you're running! I hate to tell you but that wont stop. But then you arrive at a den, turns out your fox is pregnant! So you have your four beautiful, little cubs and pick what they look like. Lighter, darker, spots, solid, you pick what you'll love. As the game goes on and you grow attached to them you understand that they're the babies you picked, you wanted these cubs, you picked each one individually and now you are the one thing they truly rely on. You form a bond with the babies you're now trying at length to keep safe and fed. But one of your cubs is taken, you don't understand where or why they're taking your cub. So you look for clues, agonising when the trail stops. As your looking for your missing baby keep in mind that you still have three more so keep moving and keep hunting, you have hungry pups to feed!You'll notice the world around you changing as days pass, the season will change. Now the world is covered in snow. Your pups are growing too and your affection for them will only increase. Predators will move, you might lose a pup to an owl or a badger might get mad at you for trying to take its food (definitely not a true story). But you'll face it all, you don't have a choice!Ok, you went through a factory, found some cool locations, and now you've found a new den in the woods. Hooray for you!! But you have a new challenge... The Furrier. (He'll shows up like a pop up book from hell!) Your getting closer to finding your baby though so you press forward, teaching your pups new skills, giving them uniqueness and usefulness for your travels. The world shifts again and now the snow is gone, life is green and absolutely gorgeous! (My absolute favourite den throughout the game).As your learning the trails and paths you might meet some people... some of them will be dangerous but others not so much. You'll find that you really like one of them, they might be kind to you. What you catch will change, berries and fish will swap out for eggs, bunnies, squirrels, etc. But it'll be a bit harder to find food, so don't be afraid to utilise those skills your babies have been learning. Now the world has changed a bit though and the woods are less... woodsy. The paths you favour will change too though and now you've found some chickens. Yay! But with chickens you'll also get the challenge of navigating some areas your pups can't go. Not so yay! Alrightey, the woods are less woodsy, the foods a little worse (both to find and to eat), so with relief you've found a new den to live in. Hopefully this one might be better...I sat crying at my computer for 5 minutes after i had finished this game, i don't think I've ever cried for a game. What i thought would be just a fun game with cute little baby foxes turned out to be an incredible journey on human impact in the world. It was truly beautiful.  I didn't know just how much I had invested into caring about my pups and it was only when i saw them scared or struggling that i truly comprehended the points the game was trying to make. Compassion, empathy, perspective, understanding... connection. This game is an english teachers dream. You could spend forever discussing characters and progression in the game and how it connects to you as the player.Focusing on the design this game is incredible. The art style was gorgeous and somehow made a game with no speech incredibly expressive. The animation of the foxes were perfect and their expressions conveyed exactly what they were experiencing and feeling. The soundtrack was incredible. From my experience i found no bugs. The game truly is one i would recommend to everyone. I promise you will not regret it. It was a 9.9/10 for me (the .1 was for the ending iykyk), progression was good and the game became more difficult as it went on. Overall really good game, one that made me write my first ever review and at 2am!!One thing i hope you take away if you get the game is: exactly as the game tells you...And I hope you can simply comprehend the reality of human impact and its effect on the world.

_childDocuments_.review: I RECOMMEND THIS GAME FOR THOSE WHO ARE STRONG WILLED AND OPEN MINDED.This game will forever be a favorite of mine now, and I will remember it always.Technical peoples:It has amazing animations, music, storytelling, plot, and 3d models. It is highly interactive and fun, and a great joy to explore the map throughout the game as it changes. It is not too difficult, not confusing, but still a challenge and promotes learning the game through creativity and thought. It's various systems are easy to understand and this, alongside the story in it, immerse you in the game in a way no other can.Emotional side:It points out some things that is very prevalent in our society in real life. This fox (you) and her cubs are just trying to peacefully survive, but they are hunted for their pelts and whatever else people want with them. The setting is a dystopian future; yes, I said future, because it isn't a fictional world. This is problems in the real world amplified. This game shows many, many subjects that people need to know, such as these: Sometimes, there's more than one side to an evil act. Pollution is real and is a real problem that will someday NEED to be solved. Greed will lead to destruction. Deforestation is a big issue as well. Don't judge a book by it's cover; there are often deeper things at work.Recommendation note:I do not recommend this game to people younger than 13, and even then I would not recommend it to anyone, adult or otherwise, who are prone to get sad and emotional. This game can be depressing. However, that does not mean it should be disregarded. The messages hidden here are important, and if you are strong willed I think you should buy and play this.Note to Devs:Thank you for making this game. It was an amazing experience, and I love it very much. I feel very connected with this game and all it's contents. The world really needs this, and I hope you have a great life."May God himself, the God of peace, sanctify you through and through. May your whole spirit, soul and body be kept blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ." 1 Thessalonians 5:23

_childDocuments_.review: I feel Endling was very unique compared to anything I've ever played before. It has a nice progression of showing increasing danger and scarcity of resources. The game-play itself is not very difficult, but the story! Oh, I was bawling like a baby towards the end. _childDocuments_.review: This game is an incredible experience,  it won't stay in your mind because of its gameplay (which is good and not janky or frustrating) but because of the story it unfolds. There is no narrator, no text to read, the ever-changing environment and events that happen in front of your fox eyes tell the story. The art style is very cute, full of colors, it's a nice balance to the bleakness of what happens during your journey. The game is divided in nights, during which you have to go out of your lair with your cubs and find food for them while keeping them safe from predators (humans and animals), traps, etc. It's relatively simple yet you have to be careful because a path that was safe before might not stay that way, a danger you haven't seen might threaten you or one of your cubs.I honestly wasn't expecting such a powerful experience from a cute game about foxes to be honest. I'd definitely recommand people who want to be moved by a game to try this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute, sad, and amazing game. The message can be subtle at times, VERY obvious at others, but god does it really hit hard the first time you see some of these in-game nighttime events, and story related developments. Amazing game, highly recommend, tells an incredible story with a lasting message.Edit: If you're in it more for mechanics and gameplay than story, this might not be the game for you. It's mechanically simple and as others have mentioned it can feel very repetitive very fast. Personally for all that the mechanics and gameplay can at times feel slow or tedious, I think the story does very good to make up for that. I personally prefer to play games more for story, emotions, graphics, and soundtracks. For me, this checks all the boxes. If you'd rather play a more mechanically intense game, you're likely to get very bored with this.And also please for the love of god stop saying "The nights are too short and such and such because it really..."It might help you to notice that you're not forced to go back to your lair as soon as the nights over, in fact, you can stay AS LONG AS YOU WANT, on ANY NIGHT YOU WANT. My balls shrivel every time someone complains the nights are short and that you're "forced" to go back home. If you're too worried about dying after making a full nights progress, that's okay. But it's not the length of the night that's the problem. Every night is a balancing act of managing all of  your objectives (Food, moving to different areas, avoiding threats, following scents). If you can't do all that before the night is "technically over" it's your call to play it risky and keep exploring, or play it safe and miss out on potential events, scent trails, food scores, or skills.Five or six very direct spoilers, and the entire next few paragraphs are vague spoilers at the very minimum.

I was often times stretching to follow the story and feed my kits, and then don't forget going out of your way to trick the Furrier once you get to that area. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: maybe buy it on sale if you want an emotional story and you do not care about actual gameplay that much.Sometimes it is really hard to admit certain things are bad. It definitely was with this game. It is a great story but not a great game. Certain narrative moments are a bit cringe but overall the plot is a solid 9/10. The gameplay though is a lot worse.This game relies heavily on exploration and has a decent size map with a lot of places to visit on your journey. The problem is that you won't be able to explore it all as the time limits are really pushing you. With a 2.5D sidescrolling camera you almost have to take it slow in order not to run into trouble. And in most cases running into trouble makes you take it extra slow while you recover so you don't really win much time by going full speed unless you're lucky. Combine it with a few really obscure intersection design choices and you get a world you will consistently fail to explore as you are forced to go back to the shelter before any significant progress can be made. If anything, doubling or tripling the night duration would've turned my opinion about this game 180 degrees.Another big point is the controls. The game is too specific about your positioning when certain events await player input. And again, if time hadn't been such a big concern I would've likely let this slide. But I can't. Because it affected not only the actual game but the ending sequence as well. This one little moment where you know what to do and try to do it but your character is one step away from the zone that accepts the input. I spent like 2 minutes trying to do the thing that should've taken 2 seconds. My main emotion at that point was frustration and it really ruined the experience. Besides, the lack of really different endings is a bummer, I expected my decisions impacting the ending a lot more than what there actually is.And don't even get me started about the price... It's a 3-4 hour game with almost no replayability (I got almost all achievements in the one run I made). The price is ridiculously high and it is not that impressive graphically to forgive it: it's neat and atmospheric but not breathtaking. I've been waiting for a 66% discount before even picking it up in the first place. All in all, considering it's basically an interactive story that drives a point, I'd say it's decent enought to experience. But not as a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Endling is actual the best fox game out there atm - an emotional soft survival adventure with a clear message.Difficulty ★★☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆ (only a few situations in which you get killed instantly and food is not a big deal, there would be space for a hardcore survival mode)* fox sounds are not totally authentic but at least they picked the most comfortable ones (most devs don't dare to use fox sounds, because foxes just do funny noises)* cubs will follow you around no matter how far you are away (only owls and humans must be avoided in a group)* if you drag in food into the den your cubs get feeded after the penalty for going in early is counting (helps to get a good headstart for the next night)* badger den for quicktravel availabe (but they are only two-way connected)* nightly time limit put you under a little pressure, but there is little punishment for stretching your time (some paths get blocked by humans and a hunter is out to catch you, due to necessary detours you have watch your food bar closely though)* less than 10 hours playtime with all achievements is a rather short game* paw spots are not explained (it signals theusage of a cub ability: blue usable, grey not usable yet)* there are missable abilities (though their are plenty of chances to get them)* achievement don't pop up visually* fox can climb up metal pipes like trees (common, be realistic, why not use wooden telegraph poles instead)* hunter w/ rife has serious hitbox issues that should be fixed:  -> sometimes if you sneak out too early while he is still turning away he will spot you out of sight neithertheless and kill you instantly  -> if you make a sharp detour when the hunter spotted you, the shot hits the ground but your fox is dying one meter away of itIn the climate change driven dystopia you actually feel like you really are a fox. You hunt, you collect, you dig, you protect your cubs, you cudle them, you avoid danger, you do whatever necessary to survive. Things that foxes do all the day, I totally loved this. And the story told unfolds without any words but has yet so emotional moments in it that it lets you rethink your personal priorities and place in the world. Way to go to present a gorgeous game with such a grave message behind.

_childDocuments_.review: Endling - extinction is forever took me by suprise with how well it tied everything together into a straight up masterpiece. The gameplay & story are seamlessly intertwined and done in such an elegant way that the message the game tries to deliver doesn't get lost. Instead it's the best depiction of the ecological challenges we face in a game i've seen so far. It shows the worst of the worst of humanity, and the impact it has on the wonderfull lifeforms we share this planet with. But it also shows the good that resides in (hopefully) most of us. It's a game about hope, struggle and love in the hardest of situations and one i couldn't be more happy to have experienced. In fact you should too! I promise it'll be worth it, if not at full price then at a discount. Also if any devs read this, i have a special personal message at the end of my review for you :)Ok so let's start of with the gameplay. The basic premise of endling is surviving. From what you may ask? Well basically almost everything but mostly starvation, traps, humans and predators. Life in endling is harsh but not impossible. You head out at night from your lair and try to find as much food as possible before the day comes, as more threats emerge at this time. Food that's not only for yourself but more importantly for your little kits/cubs. At the start you bring this food back to your lair where they reside but after a few nights one of them has been abducted by a hunter. The main goal of endling then becomes finding back your lost kit/cub while doing your best to keep the other three alive.You see, as the kits/cubs have grown they now follow you around as you head out. Getting into all sorts of precarious situations while still needing as much food as possible to grow. They not only grow in size but also in skills, learning new things such as squeezing into small places to scavenge for food, or hunting on their own. Seeing the cubs grow with unique skillsets makes you attached to each of them and keeping them alive felt more worthwhile than anything else i've ever done in a game. So as you take care of your three little kits/cubs you look for the missing one by scent. This slowly reveals what happened to them as the scent leads you closer and closer to reuniting with your little rascal.Scent is also used to hunt for food which is easy at first, with simple prey that is bountiful and tasty. But as time goes by the impact of the humans gets clearer and clearer. The way the environment changed throughout the game left me speechless and ashamed. This doesn't only influence the visuals of the area but also the abundance of food. Each night finding enough food becomes harder and harder. And managing to keep your kits/cubs fed while making your way back to the lair in time all the while avoiding the traps and predators but still looking for your missing cub made for a super engaging and immersive gameplay loop. It's when all these gameplay aspects work in tandem that the game really shines. The despair i felt as one of them was on the bring of starvation, the sun was rising and i was nowhere near a shelter was immeasurable. The little starving cub started slowing down so i had to pick them up and frantically start looking for food. I picked up the scent of something and rushed my way over only to find it was a thrash bag. These CAN give food but also put a plastic bag over your head which you need to shake off before asphyxiating. By a stroke of miracle there was a morsel of food in that thrashbag, enough to scrape by and save my cub/kit from the brink of death. It gave me enough time to head back to shelter just before sunrise. The relief i felt at that time, it was then that i realized i had my hands on a masterpiece of a game. The next day i stabilized on food and encountered some more events, some harrowing others hardwarming. Little things showing that there's good in some people's hearts and that there is the possiblity of co-existing. I paid extra attention to my surroundings both for my kits/cubs safety and my own as well as to be more perceptive of the heaps of environmental storytelling going on in the background. When i finally reached the ending it resonated with me so much that i reached a state best described as speechless. The ending is worth experiencing yourself, it's one of the greatest finales you could want and once again it's so elegantly done that you can't help but be moved.So the story and gameplay systems all work together to make a fun albeit stressfull experience culliminating in one of the most profound and memorable experiences i've had. What remains are the visuals, audio and technical aspects of the game. I'm happy to say that these are all of the same quality as the rest. The visuals are bloody gorgeous, each vista is worth framing as the colours and shape of the landscape create playable paintings. The score from the very first sequence is enough to give you chills even on a hot summer day and well worth purchasing along with the game in a bundle. On a technical level the game runs flawlessly and i had zero bugs throughout my time. All of this combined makes this game an undeniable masterpiece and it now sits comfortably among my favorite games of all time. Go ahead do yourself a favor and experience this profound and heartfelt game.To the developers, i thank you... I thank you for creating this wonderfull experience that's so much more than a game. I've struggled with depression since i was 16, when it dawned upon me that we are killing the planet. I took it all the worries of the world on me and felt horrible. When i came of age i decided to do something about it by studying environmental chemistry at college. This gave meaning to my life and by now i've graduated with distinction and am looking for a place where i can help make the difference. But i still struggle with the thought of wether or not i can make a difference at all. Your game gave me strenght and hope. Hope that it is possible to change people's minds. I've already convinced most of my friends and family to eat less meat, something i've given up since i was 16. I always try to educate others at the risk of being preachy. People don't like being reminded of the climate problem or polution or deforestation... They point their fingers and refuse to change, waiting for someone else. But we all have a responsibility! You guys delivered this message in such an elegant way that even if you can change just one persons' mind you'll have made the world a better place. You certainly have for me, thank you <3

_childDocuments_.review: It's really pretty and powerful and emotional. Great stuff. But it also manages to be a pretty good game, too!The gameplay is largely comprised of exploration to search for interesting changes to your environment. You'll have to find a balance of exploring/investigating things vs ensuring your cubs are well-fed, else you face the consequence of permanently losing one of them. If all three cubs die, the game is over. But honestly, the game does a great job of making the loss of one cub feel devastating.Surprisingly the game is rather challenging. I had been expecting a linear storypath, but no. For many days you are left on your own to explore and learn about your environments advantages and challenges through gameplay. Occasionally new beats of story will pop up, creating a nice pace of exploration gameplay leeching into story segments. New challenges and the persistent need for food can sometimes make exploring very tough because of how easy it is to starve or get injured.Don't be mistaken; exploring does not consist of purely running around the map. You have puzzles to solve, new threats to navigate, things to climb, and secrets to sniff out. If I did have a complaint, I would reluctantly note there is a vague time-limit to each day that you explore. While it's relatively safe to explore and search for food at night, the day can bring threats in the form of people wandering the map at random. Most of these people are a threat, as all interactions will lead to an injury. As a result, you are motivated to explore by night, then hide by day.I've never been a fan of a "time-limit" in most games, exploration games being my least favorite. This may just be a personal pet peeve of mine, as the game is balanced decently enough (even if day arrives, you can still return to your lair safely, the return route simply becomes more risky). But I didn't really enjoy the feeling of sprinting through the map (and forcing my cubs to sprint after me) just to beat out the clock. Rather than take in the lovely sights, I had to rush through everything due to the anxiety of the day's arrival. Overall, I love this game, and I especially appreciate that it isn't simply a "story-rich experience." it is story-rich, it IS a great experience, and it is beautiful... But it is also simply a fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely good at presenting the player with difficult choices and evocative, near cinematic experiences. It is by no means a casual game. I wouldn't call it difficult, but it isn't a walk in the park either. The world will move on without you, and scents don't last forever. It is absolutely beautiful, I loved the feel of most of the game play, and I only encountered one glitch during my entire play through, that glitch being that when I won a fight against an owl it just... vanished. Like, blinked out of existence kind of vanished. Anyway, I had a wonderful time taking care of my fox pups (I named them Sweet Tart, Smudge, Lil' White, and Mask) and experiencing the world the game has built up. Seriously, great world building! I wish I had more time to experience it, as about 3 hours in the game ended. I'd recommend this game to people who enjoy story driven games with game play that isn't too demanding of the player, but still requires some thinking. Also, it will probably take several play-throughs to see everything.SPOILERS AHEAD FOR THE ENDING!!!I didn't expect a good ending from the game, and I understand why the developers made the choice they did. It continues the hard hitting reality that the game is set in, and what could be ours in the frighteningly near future. Indeed, games like this are essential reminders to that fact of our world. However, every game like this that I have heard of and watched/played has had a very similar ending, so much so that many people like myself have come to assume that this will always be the case. I had a bit of hope that this game would break that trend, give us a little bit of hope that we need to keep going, but it didn't. Personally, I think that it makes a point we already expect it to make, and it would have been nice if it had subverted those expectation just a little bit, to remind us that we can do something, in real life, to prevent the world Endling is set in from coming into existence.

_childDocuments_.review: Endling - Extinction is Forever is a game that's hard to talk about without spoiling anything, so we'll start there.It's a fairly simple game, you're a mother fox, last of your species attempting to survive. At night, you'll hunt and track down family you may or may not have lost during the game. You'll see what the world is around you and what's becoming of it.The entire story is wordless, only through music, sounds and animation does Endling - Extinction is Forever tell its tale. Its one that pulls no punches but I can recommend the playthrough. It'll take about four hours but stick with you for the rest of the day.SPOILERS BELOWSeeing the world decay as corporations and greed become wide spread is hard to see. Watching people forget their humanity towards their own humans in the story is too. Saying all that though the story is damn good, you see survival from all aspects. _childDocuments_.review: OVERALL RATING: 8/10(I want to give it a 9 or 10 out of 10, but as a video game, it's an 8/10. See below.)SUMMARY: "Endling" is just an outright beautiful, thought-provoking game. It's very cinematic. At one point, I thought, "is this the sort of game that would make a better movie?" but no, definitely better as a game. It gets you invested in the premise via the gameplay. I almost consider it a "fox simulator." I will say, apparently I finished it in about 3.5 hours. For a 30$ price tag, I think some people might find that a little steep, but! I'm actually really satisfied with what I got out of it. It's *beautiful* and engaging. I'm going to be playing this game a lot over my life.If you're worried that this game is going to be too depressing for you, I was similarly worried. I would say, yes, the game made me cry, and then it made me cry some more, but ultimately, while the game seems to have a pessimistic outlook, it still cradles and encourages hope. I'm really satisfied with the result of the game, despite the heavy punches.DETAILS: You pretty much *are* the fox. You are the driving force behind every action & every decision. The game dabbles in action, stealth, and puzzle, but never really dives into any of it. It felt decently accurate to what being a wild animal must be like. Besides gameplay, the visuals & music were top notch. It nailed a lower poly aesthetic. Games do not need to look realistic to be beautiful & immersive. The music is REALLY nice and scene setting. The story was minimal.WHY 8/10? (MINOR SPOILERS):"Endling" is an example of what only video games can do as a medium. You really put yourself in the fox's paws through this experience. As I said before, you *are* the driving force behind every action & decision. It's beautiful, thought-provoking, engaging, & replay worthy.However, the game was a lot smaller & less adventurous than I thought it was going to be. It starts and continues to be incredibly strong as you unlock areas and explore them, but after a certain point, you might run out of things to see. By the 70/80% point of the game, I was basically just waiting for the story to come to a conclusion. Perhaps I outpaced it. I think if the game kept a sense of exploration & adventure all throughout, perhaps had more map than gameplay time, it would be *absolutely* 100% stellar. But that, combined with a decently linear gameplay loop, I think an 8/10 is the most fair *as a video game.*As an experience, it was easily 10/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Endling is a powerful emotional journey following the life of a fox raising her cubs in a world destroyed by pollution and corruption. You experience the world first hand as you struggle everyday through a wasteland to feed your cubs and teach them the necessary skills to survive. It's through this intimate fight for survival, and witnessing the harshness and selfishness of others that builds a bond with the characters, and specifically your cubs. While I can't do Endling the justice it deserves in a review, I implore anyone who loves an emotionally involved tale to try Endling. The talented developers at Herobeat crafted a heartbreaking, yet beautiful story here with many layers to it: showing us what may become of our planet if we continue to treat it how we do,  impact of humanity and the beauty and resilience of nature. As well as showing that compassion and caring can still exist in the bleakest moments of life. While a short game, it is a definite must play that was unfortunately overshadowed when it released around the same time as Stray. Both are great games, but I feel much more connected to the message Endling makes.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a lovely story! A wild fox leads, protects, feeds, and tracks her pups. She must survive, and make sure they survive. Bring your tissues, you will cry! Of particular note, I thought the mix of 2D and 3D was interesting. Your travel is only ever along line paths, making it feel like a sidescroller, but when you hit forks in the path or intersections, you can hop onto a different axis path. Then you pop open your map to help you understand how this positions you in the 3D world. Little bit like Kirby 64 or Klonoa.You've got some things to manage:-Hunger. Your pups' hunger meter (they share just one meter) slowly moves throughout the day. Scrounge up enough food to keep it from going bad. On the flip side, if your pups are all the way full, then you may wanna leave food for later so you don't waste it.-Time. Ideally, you should return to your den before the sun comes up. If you run out of time, it's not a huge deal, but I think your hunger meter goes faster, and maybe the world gets a little more dangerous?-Rescue. If you lose a pup, you can track their scent, which is the game's plot progression. These scent trails pop up on certain days.-Exploration. You can find events throughout the world that change each day, and your pups can learn new abilities, some optional.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I have to give Endling - Extinction is Forever a 3.5 out of 5 stars. Having finished this game (except for several achievements I am going back to get), there are some spoilers mentioned later on in this review. This is probably one of the shortest games I've played. It took me 6.6 hours of gameplay to beat the game, and I am confident that when I restart it to unlock the missing achievements, I may only need half that time to beat it again. So, for 30 US dollars, the cost-to-time ratio feels unbalanced. The mechanics are easy enough, but if you miss a skill, it can be challenging (if not impossible) to ever get the chance to teach your fox kit that skill again. Sometimes, the game felt rushed. Between needing to constantly find food in an extremely harsh environment, to finding clues at specific times, and teaching/learning skills at particular times, all while trying to not get killed by humans/predators, it was very challenging to juggle all of that in what often felt like a way too short night. I played this game with my 5-year-old; it gave us a lot of opportunities to talk about death, extinction, deforestation, pollution, poaching, animal welfare, survival, motherly duty, and so many other topics. This game did a fantastic job at sending a message to its audience, but it was ultimately heartbreaking. I can say that my child learned some precious lessons while watching me play this game, but I can't help but hate how sad I was for my child to not have a happy ending, and the game broke my own heart. Sure, we can argue that life does not always have happy endings, and a child needs to learn that sooner or later, and this was my choice to let my five-year-old experience these concepts through this method. (We recently had a death in the family. So naturally, my child has a lot of questions on some of these topics now. Not to mention, I am trying to instill a love for the Earth and to be a better human.)The game left us wanting more and with a sense of dissatisfaction. I couldn't help but echo my child's voice when they asked, "Is this really the end?" It felt a little cruel and harsh for the player to go through the hardships of parenthood, struggling without an end in sight or relief on many occasions, only to have it all ripped away after you finally save your fox kit. I want there to be a sequel or downloadable content to continue the game where Mother Fox left us. Either we get that happy comeback story for Mother Fox, or we have the opportunity to revive a species thanks to her ultimate sacrifice.Overall, I still recommend this game for the lessons you learn, the amazingly beautiful graphic style, the story line, and the music. The only reason I deducted points from this rating is the short game play length, and the tragic ending.

_childDocuments_.review: My summary; Really good! Was worth the money, but maybe wait for a sale if you're seeing this in the far future? The ending got me emotional, and it is 100% possible to keep them all alive! I really recommend. (You should probably practice spamming the space bar btw ;D.)MAJOR SPOILER WARNING! LIKE, IT TELLS THE ENTIRE GAME KINDA SPOILERS. EVEN THE END.So many things to say! To start; the beginning was un-stressful until the brown pup disappears. The rest is mostly easy and mostly fun, until you occasionally run out of nearby food. (Note: Every night the berries replenish, and you are never too good for any kind of food, not even trash.) Night 28, I physically can't return to my regular den, so I have to go back to the first den you stay at (BIG MISTAKE), because the pups come out of the third den (where you were meant to sleep), which means we are all infinitely far from each other, and they almost died of starvation before I reloaded the save and tried again. If this ever happens, make your way to a badger den, it teleports your pups to you. It saved mine. When the girl's sickness got too bad my emotions started acting up, but at least we got our pup back in the end. Returning to the den and sleeping again, I was wondering what'd happen next. The following day was normal, but when we returned to bed to find the flood, and our pups get dragged away by the water as we get knocked out. I was freaking out and telling myself it wasn't the end. "Luckily" though not so luckily, you wake up in a desert, go left and carry your pups out of the, what I can only assume is, mud or tar. Then it's a long walk right. A deceased chicken, the axe man holding some sort of elongated bamboo looking gun. Later on, on the walk, you see him again, and he shoots at you. For me, he missed, but I'm unsure if that's 100% to happen. Then, when you dig under the fence, just before you can get through, he shoots you, and you survive for another minute or two, before slowly falling down, and eventually dying. At the end of the credits your pups start walking away, and looking back, then you get your finishing achievements. This made me just simply cry. 10/10 would cry again, I just wish it could've ended happier, but this is the way life goes.

_childDocuments_.review: Will the last mother fox on Earth be able to save its three little cubs? Experience how life would be in a world ravaged by mankind through the eyes of the last fox on Earth in this eco-conscious adventure. Discover the destructive eect of the human race, which corrupts day after day the most precious and needed resources of the natural environments. Explore Endling's 3D side-scrolling world and defend your cubs, three tiny and defenseless fur balls, feed them, see how they grow up level after level, notice their unique personalities and fears, and most importantly, make them survive. name: Iron Danger
detailed_description: Buzz Featured DLC Join us on Discord About the Game Iron Danger is a tactical combat puzzler with a unique time manipulation mechanic. A never before seen combination that blends the tactical depth of turn-based games with the exciting action of real-time games. Tackle challenging encounters with your party of two characters, using a variety of skills and highly interactive environments. Maybe you will set an enemy on fire and kick them into a grain field for a proper barbeque, or set up a trap and fell a tree on top of them. The options are endless and it is you who will be deciding your own approach! You have control over time The core of Iron Danger is its unique time control mechanic. You can rewind time for up to 5 seconds whenever you want, trying different strategies and combinations of moves until you find the right one for the task at hand. The time manipulation allows us to combine real-time combat gameplay with controls from more traditional, tactical turn-based combat games. This gives tactical combat a puzzle-like element, as you can continuously keep trying new approaches to turn impossible odds to your advantage and synchronize the actions of your characters for the perfect outcome. You will die, but you will not fail! Iron Danger is set in a world of lofty fells, primeval forest, and placid lakes... as well as living gods and monsters of steel. The city of Kalevala, home of the humans who rebelled against the gods and forsook their protection, shines in the middle of this world, surrounded by towns, sea lanes and and woodlands under its protection. But from the frozen north, a witch queen is leading her army on a quest for vengeance against the lords of Kalevala. Ancient ruins from the days when gods dwelled on the earth are opening to unleash forgotten powers, tempting humans and striving to overtake the world. You’ll take on the role of Kipuna, a sharp-witted village girl, who becomes imbued with an ancient power that grants dominion over time and death. You must use your wits to control it as you’re drawn into the midst of a war between the city of Kalevala and the armies of the Northlanders driven by their witch queen Lowhee. Your task is to master the power, in order to use it for mankind’s protection, while your enemies will seek to harness it in the service of total destruction. Use unique time-rewind mechanics and experience a new take on tactical combat combining best aspects of real-time and turn-based combat. Use highly interactive environment for your advantage to succeed against impossible odds. Adventure in a world of steampunk fantasy and meet its unique inhabitants inspired by Finnish folklore. Fight epic boss monsters on the path to fulfill your destiny. No grinding; character progression pace is controlled by the story and every fight matters. 15+ hours of gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this game based on my own preferences and enjoyment. However, there are a couple of things you need to know going in before deciding whether this game is for you.This game is not an RPG. It has no XP or loot. There are no items. You do not make choices that influence the story. It is a completely linear experience. Character progression is based on milestones, which allows you to learn and upgrade skills at the end of a chapter or mission.The game is entirely level based. While they look very pretty there's barely anything to find in them besides consumables and enemies. The reason I consider them levels rather than areas is because you cannot freely travel between levels. Soon as you exit an area you cannot leave until you've completed whatever objective it is you're there to do.The combat is real-time with pause. Everyone acts at the same time but you can pause to assign actions to your characters. Actions are divided into heartbeats similar to rounds in D&D with certain actions taking more heartbeats than others. You can rewind up to a certain point and undo previous actions as you see fit, even when characters die. There is no manual saving and instead the game autosaves between levels. The lack of manual saves means that if you are interrupted you will have to restart the level from the beginning. During missions you can rewind to save a dying character, but you cannot rewind all the way to the beginning, so if you play too recklessly you can still lose the mission.Combat is the meat of the game and quite fun once you get used to it. Don't get frustrated if you die, since you can always rewind. Reacting to audio cues helps in predicting which attacks you have to dodge. Sometimes you have to dodge towards the enemy in order to avoid their strike as well as get within range for a follow up attack. As the game goes on you learn a lot more spells to throw at your enemies and buff allies. The enemies are pretty challenging and you often have to react to their attacks or preemptively prevent them from devastating your party. If you're familiar with Divinity Original Sin then you'll find some similarities in the way certain spells and the environment interact with each other. I actually think the combat is very similar to Divinity with the exception that you don't take turns.I liked the voice actors. Everyone really sinks into their roles. They may be somewhat over the top but I thought it added to the charm. Try to go in with the expectation that this is a fairytale with obvious villains.This is very specific to my background so I don't expect anyone who isn't familiar with Kalevala to get that much out of the setting. Some of it may not translate very well to English. Even the name Iron Danger is drawn from Finnish but it doesn't quite carry the same weight in English.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: is a linear Tactical RPG featuring a unique combat system. The title follows the story of Kipuna, a normal girl living on a coastline village that one day gets attacked by the militarist Northland Empire. Amidst the commotion, the protagonist's fate reveals itself binding her to an ancient artifact. After these events, followed by her trusty friend Topi, she embarks on a quest of knowledge to discover the meaning behind her newfound powers.🟩 🟥 Starting with the good parts, of course the feature that carries Iron Danger all the way into being an original title is the time manipulation system, which divides time into intervals and allows you to rewind up to a limit. This opens up interesting possibilities in combat, not seen in other games. The narrative and writing are very good, as the characters feel coherent with their personality, have an evolution during the quest. The art style is also well-crafted and many locations, some enemies inspire to Finnish folklore. The visuals themselves are more than acceptable for the current times, except for the massive amount of distance blur. The game keeps pumping out new skills and upgraded ones for your characters, along with consumables and throwables, so the variety of approaches increases as you get further, keeping the gameplay fresh.On the bad side there is also much to say. First of all even for a linear RPG style, the lack of side content, quests and optional areas is near absolute here, having only the main quest objectives to clear. The same goes for NPCs which can't be talked with in a deeper way and this may discourage deeper RPG fans. Enemies are pretty unique on their own but get repetitive as the game progresses since only a few new ones get introduced. The lack of a stat / loot / equip system also weighs heavily on replay value and build possibilities.🎮 The gameplay is divided into Exploration, Combat and Character Manegement.Is done mostly on foot and sometimes by remote controlling certain devices. The world is divided in levels set in various places: each of them is usually filled with consumables to gather, devices to activate, dynamic surfaces such as oil or ice, and of course enemies to battle. Keeping an eye out of life-restoring consumables, or useful throwables like grenades and barrels can make the difference in combat, so exploring in this sense is rewarding. There are no side areas or secrets to find though.Is the centerpiece of Iron Danger, and plays out in a unique way. It plays out as a real-time RPG but time is divided in intervals of 0.5 seconds each, and you can rewind it up to a limit, stop it or make it advance. Of course, you will be able to issue orders to your party members simultaneously to coordinate attacks. Trial and error is the keyword here, as your characters will die many times... only to be brought back in time and avoid the fatal mistake, while damaging the enemy. Mastering this mechanic, and uniting it with perfect timing on attacks and skill usage, is the key for success.In combat each character has a variety of skills, having a cooldown but otherwise using no other resource. Kipuna will be able to wield magic while other party members will use other means of offense such as arrows or melee weapons, depending on which one. Consumables, both offensive and defensive, play a major role if used correctly, to lay traps for the enemy or putting foes against each other for example. It takes a while to understand how this system works but once you get the hang of it, it feels very fun and dynamic.Is not very fleshed out. There are no stats to level up or gear to equip, as the only evolution consists in one skill upgrade at the end of each major level. Other than that each character can carry a finite amount of each consumable / throwable so being efficient that is a good idea. There is no leveling system or stat upgrades of any kind outside of temporary buffs in battle.🔩 Optimization needs major improvements, as in some locations noticeable frame drops happen even with a high-end machine, system resource usage is way too high for the graphics complexity delivered (80-90% GPU use on a 2080Ti in 1440p 85Hz and high settings). Character path-finding is prone to glitching and in rare cases can cause gamebreaking bugs. Rarely, triggers for objectives may not work and force a level restart. Hitboxes and reliability of attacks need improvement as well. Movement is very clunky. An innovative Tactical RPG that focuses on a fresh take on combat, but also lacks the roleplaying depth and interaction level some might expect. A good pick for RPG fans that want to try something different.

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Danger is one of those games that makes me wish Steam reviews were less binary than the choices presented to the users. While by no means a bad experience, it was definitely one with several shortcomings that made playing somewhat of a chore. So in short I guess I would rather give Iron Danger a mixed opinion.At it's heart this game is essentially an RPG with it's biggest selling point being a rather unique take on combat. Once in a fight, time stops and is divided into a row of segments at the bottom of the screen. Each character has a large variety of actions they can take which are familiar to the genre in whole. Attack, magic, heal and special abilities can be activated and once done will appear on the timeline and time moves forward. Now the trick in Iron Danger is that if you mess up, like casting a fireball in the wrong location and blowing yourself up, you merely click to a segment on the timeline before said action was taken and everything will reverse back to the chosen point in time.In a way it's almost as if this game has made "save scumming" an actual magic power and at first this is a really fun mechanic to use. You're character will, most likely, die multiple times in a level (or even a single fight) and each time you can rewind and re-do your actions for the best possible outcome until victorious. Like any impressive trick it's entertaining at first but once you've seen it hundreds of times it becomes tedious and routine.One of the problems with the combat is that it doesn't really get much better or advanced as the game progresses. Sure you unlock new abilities for the characters as you finish levels but the tactics for each fight could almost be copied and pasted from start to finish. You only ever get to control a party of two (each with their own timelines you have to manage individually yet keeping the two in tandem) and you never get to choose who to take into the fight. You will always be playing as the mage character (who is the story's main) and one of her three companions (an archer, a warrior and healer) at the behest of the game's choice. The mage then bombards enemies from a distance with magic, while the other characters follow their own set of skills (up close and personal with the warrior or at a distance with the archer).In retrospect it feels as if the game could have been better fine-tuning it's combat to be more like a puzzle than an outright fight. By the time you get into the final third of the game, the main character will have learned so many new and powerful spells that she can almost take on whole armies by herself if you cycle through them in the correct manner. Even the rare boss battles that turn up in this game aren't all that different to regular enemies fought throughout other than the damage they commit, which is undone by reversing time after all.The rest of the game doesn't have much to stand on unfortunately. The music while acceptable isn't memorable. The characters are fine but generic. The art direction is OK but bland. For the one interesting mechanic this game has it's surrounded by an awful lot of mediocrity. I'm probably being too harsh on Iron Danger as in the end after it was all said and done, I was glad I played it and I did have fun to an extent. But there was always a constant nagging boredom building up after finishing a couple of levels (which roughly take 10-30 min to finish with no saving other than autosaves upon completing a level). There's a good idea here that is worth checking out (probably for a discounted price) but it could have been so much more with a little thought and extra creativity.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think people are being objective in the negative reviews.It's true that the time mechanic essentially serves as an undo button, but that's the point!I would sum up the game as a wholesome experience with great voice acting and decent strategic elements. Sometimes it feels like an RPG puzzle game, and I don't think there's anything that fills the niche quite as well as Iron Danger does.A good game to buy on sale if you're looking for something new to fill your time. The character design is interesting, the gameplay is fun, and the story is actually quite engaging.I'm not sure why other reviews say the story isn't good, I'm loving it so far. So much so that I felt compelled to write a review condemning those who felt the need to be so negative. "This game isn't for me." Then why are you reviewing it? Imagine if people who didn't like puzzle games went around reviewing puzzle games? If this isn't the sort of game you'd play, don't burden it with a negative review. For what it is, this game is good. You can feel the passion that went into it and we honestly need more of that.

So, two dark sunglasses up from Jake and Elwood.  Give it a try.  Set the controls for the heart of the sun and just enjoy pure fun gaming goodness.[Update 3/14/2021] I'm getting close to the end of this game, and it is still a blast to play. _childDocuments_.review: Extraordinary game with a wonderful combat system! I would like to call it 'combat choreography' at times, a delight for anyone looking for a casual adventure, because the mechanics ensure that you basically can't loose. This inside a pearl of a story, which isn't always conveyed the best in this game. Kipuna's hometown is under attack, and during her fled out of town, she tumbles through a gap in the pavement to an ancient forgotten temple, right upon a magical shard. The shard is pierced through her heart, and it gives her the power to turn back time 7 seconds, and to conjure firespells. A magical apparition sets Kipuna off on a quest to get the five other shards that form together the Aurolith! The king sets her out on the same quest, he wants to harness the Auroliths power to conjure a shield around the capital. The game is told in small chapters, most of them beatable in half an hour. After each chapter the game autosaves, there is no manual saving. You play realtime, until you encounter combat. The game pauses at that point, and you can execute orders for each character. The orders are per 0,5 second, so you can pinpoint precisely when to move, dodge, attack etcetera. You get hit, or even die? Just rewind a bit and adjust the plan! The description of the game is spot on, . The Steam tags are incorrect, this is not turn-based, and I would not call this RPG (you can select upgrades for spells after chapters, however there is usually only 1 good upgrade). My tagchoices are adventure, time manipulation, tactical, and I added casual. This game is not isometric at all. I don't think the game tells this story the best way possible. To elaborate this I use some spoilers.  I can't believe this story is written like that. Maybe the story had to be shrunk down. There were a lot of dilemmas that were only hinted to, but deserve a bigger story. Understandable that doesn't fit in this game, however the design raises some questions in me. Also because of the jokes which feel unnatural, or the voiceacting, very well performed but feels a bit off. But that's nitpicking, very happy that there is voice acting!! Being a handicapped gamer this was a delight to play! I hope there will be more games with this time manipulation technique! Maybe one with only one character, because that would be quicker in some situations. The other aspects of the game are just solid. Very good level design, good atmospheric music (it really blends in). A very good game to play casually for an hour. 84/100

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing, 6.3 % of people got the achievement for finishing Iron Danger - and now I am one of them. I can only assume that this rather low percentage - for a game that has never been given away for free so far - stems not from the game being overly difficult, but rather being really clunky and unfun to play.Let's start with the positives though. The artstyle of the game is sufficient and clean, it has a very fitting and pleasant soundtrack and the voice acting is decent. The game tries to build up a whole universe in a rather short playtime, and while it doesn't quite succeed, I can applaud the effort. The battle mechanic is, at the very least, creative.The problems start when you look beyond those aspects. Iron Danger is a game that has been completely built on battles. There is nothing else in the game. Almost every mission in every chapter has one or multiple battles, and inbetween battles you spend time walking to the next battle. Aside from a few consumable items and the occasional note, nothing can be found.This would of course be fine if the battles were as fun as they should be, given that they were the focus, but sadly that is not the case. The main gimmick of the game is interesting: due to story reasons, our heroine can reverse time up to a limit, one heartbeat at a time. Each action, like moving around and attacking, costs a certain number of heartbeats. If one of your actions doesn't land or you got hit, you can rewind and try to block or look at a different approach.It's a pretty cool mechanic, but it has two massive problems. First of all, it makes all battles essentially inconsequential. Death doesn't mean anything as you can just rewind, and every enemy action can be countered that way. This also has implications on the story as you can't ever really fail. The second problem is that it makes battles really clunky. You usually fight four, five or even more enemies at a time. They chuck grenades, use skills and ranged attacks and so on. You will constantly get hit, have to rewind to dodge the attack, then get hit again by a different attack, and so on and so forth. Since your two characters can also only take two or three hits max, this quickly becomes frustrating even if you can never really die.Couple that with the dreadful optimization (dropping as low as 25 fps on my pretty good PC, even when not in battles) and the rather slow story and it just isn't fun. I see the approach the developers were going for here - making battles more like puzzles - but it just doesn't work. It's not even really difficult, as you can't fail, it's essentially just a heap of trial & error until you get it right, over and over again.There is a lot of artistry in the style and soundtrack, but sadly I can't recommend it because the only gameplay loop you have isn't very fun. The game does end on a cliffhanger and if a second game ever comes, I hope there will be a bigger focus on making battles fun and maybe giving the game more of an RPG aspect beyond upgrading a skill after every couple missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write many reviews, but I wanted to write one for this game because it's sadly not getting lots of attention (and I know how important reviews are). This game is a LOT of fun. The time rewinding mechanic is addictive, clever and intuitive to use. Even when you lose horribly, it's wonderful to just be able to rewind time and try again. Get killed by an arrow? Rewind a few heartbeats and dodge the arrow just in time. My only wish (and this seems to be a oft-requested feature) would be to be able to see the entire completed fight from beginning to end. Seeing my heroes dodge and weave and strike at just the right moments against impossible odds would be incredibly rewarding. Hopefully they add this feature.The only downside is the story/characters are a touch generic (standard "fantasy heroes against steampunk villains" trope) and ends on a completely unexpected "TO BE CONTINUED" that felt like the game ran out of budget and time. But since the story was probably the weakest part of the game, the lack of resolution didn't bother me so much. Definitely give the demo a try. If you enjoy that, then you will really enjoy the rest of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has gotten so bad, I came back here to edit my review just to make it worse.Pros: --Unique and intriguing time shift mechanic.Cons:--There is nothing "RPG" about this game.--No character customization.--You can't choose who you want as your companion, it just forces one on you.  Which wouldn't be a problem if any of the companions were as good as the one you start your adventure with.--No EXP or level gain--No Shops--No Gear, Weapons, Trinkets to search for or find.--No reason to explore because there is nothing to find.--Every character turns really unlikeable half-way through the game: The main protaganist starts telling people to "shut up" in every other cutscene.  One companion cares more about shards than her life... Another aggressively tells her to kiss him, and then threatens to SLAP her if she doesn't stop talking.--Pointless unmotivating combat.  Enemies don't drop loot, experience, or anything of value.  So there is no point to even fight them... just run through them all, using your dash on cooldown to avoid their attacks and gain distance.--The ONLY merit of the combat is the above mentioned time shifting.  There are no debuffs or status effects to manage, there are no diverse arrays of enemies to plan for.  The time shifting is a fun diversion for the first hour or two of gameplay... but then when you realize that every singe other aspect of this game is bland and boring, it becomes a chore.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr A short game with a unique time bending mechanic that starts to fall off later; recommended when in sale.This is one of the tougher decisions.Firstly, the core mechanic of manipulating time is a really cool idea. Planning combat and luring enemies into traps... it didn't work out? Continue to tweak till perfection. I love that. I often found myself to fiddle around till I got out of a fight without a single bruise (which is not necessary, as there are plenty healing items).Later on however, it started to become tedious. The problem in my opinion was that this gameplay, where you can correct your mistakes at every possible moment, can't really become any harder later on. However in an attempt to give you a feeling of rising stakes, enemies have more and more hit points and many AOE-effects (such as explosive guns). This made my play style impossible.Enemies survived too much punishment to sneak kill them and with many enemies doing AOE, it was impossible to dodge all of it. Their damage wasn't that high and a healing spell reverts that, sure, but it didn't feel right anymore. It didn't feel like you solved these combat puzzles anymore, but it instead you brute-forced your way through. Combine that with more and more fights everywhere, I grew tired of it.At some point even, I just ran past the enemies, because I couldn't be bothered to fight all of them. Maybe that was their intention, to show you the enemy supremacy, but if that was the case, it was poorly communicated.Another little downside is, that you basically play most regions twice, because you need to go to your objective and then go back to your starting point. It feels a bit cheap, though some regions are altered, when you go back.On to other topics:The graphics are quite beautiful, the sound is solid (I do love the voice actor of the main character), and the story is somewhat compelling. It feels like there are some dead end strands, but I think they put a great effort into the development of the main character. She never wanted to be a fighter, much less a sorceress, so we see her struggle with that destiny and these expectations, that come with it.Because of an increasing number of fights, the story parts also become less unfortunately.Concluding, I think this game is worth a try, even if it gets worse at some point. Especially the first few hours were very entertaining. That's why I would recommend this game when it's at sale. If you still don't like it, then use the amazing time-bending ability called refund.Thanks for reading,Have a great day!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting game with a MAJOR flaw. I found that the mechanics of reverse time  allow for some good tactics but the novelty of the system wears out too soon. What's left after that is some generic graphics and a story that is somehow interesting although there is nothing too exciting about it. Nonetheless, the game could have been a fun little time waster and I would definitely recommend it if it wasn't for one major flaw. No manual save. I need to emphasize this, no manual save, no quicksave, no checkpoints, no nothing. The game only saves automatically between chapters, some of which are quite large. There isn't even an autosave half way through the chapters or even before the boss fights.It really defies reasoning for such a feature to be missing, especially on this day and age. No manual save makes playing this game tedious and sucks all fun from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Can you please remove the ads from the menu? i have paid full price for this.EDIT:Well, i didnt wanted to write a full review so it doesnt seem that i want to overkill this game but on popular demand i have to write...The game is really bad. The story is bad and the gameplay is bad.Story------The main character suddenly realize that it is special. She didnt work hard, she didnt learned anything new, she didnt summon a demon on the crossroad, and she didnt find a magic lamp, she have just suddenly became as powerful as a GOD being able to shift time in the past. She is awesome, it is her birth right to be awesome and to win no matter what and to punish everybody that stands in her way and the only punish that everybody deserves is DEATH!!!I mean, i sympathize more with the poor thiefs that try to rob you while they struggle to survive, those people that you kill in cold blood with your super powers leaving their families without any source of income. It is hard for me to sympathize with a immortal overpowered merciless evil witch.Gameplay-----------From a gameplay perspective the time shifting thing seems to be a smart move, fresh, entertaining, intresting and with a lot of potential to be creative. But it is not. In fact this trial and error gameplay element makes this game feel dull. And this is why: - You can not die in this game. The rogue like games are fun because YOU DIE, there is risk, there is something to lose, there are consequences for your action, there is a reason to start over. This is not rogue like, there is no (iron) danger involved, the title is a lie :D- It rely on trial and error. This feels like you save the game every second and then load a older save game if you fail. This "tactics" was used by bad gamers since like forever (who didnt do that on Baldur Gates 2?) but here it is the gameplay.- It is too easy. If it is hard for you than you didnt shift the time in the past enough. Try again, it is the purpose of the game, that how you play it, you try :D- It is not original: remember Matrix? remember Hotline Miami? remember Heroes 3 when that damn necro was killing your good hero? remember when you used to suck at any game with save/load feature? so yea, it is not original. Actuall it competes with most games ever made. And it loses very badly!- No replay value. I mean, you replay the same things over and over again but thats because you have to, not because you want to.- No sense of progression. Indeed u get a new skill from time to time but the number of skills is very limited. And it is very easy to test them, to learn how they work, to experiment with them, all in the same fight. You cant make some sophisticated builds, you just stop the time and test them, thats all the progression of your character, nothing more.- Beside the core time shifting feature there is not much else to do.- Low interaction with the world, exploration is not satisfying at all.- Not a RPG, you cant chose weapons, armors, skill trees, etc. It's more like a adventure game with TBS elements without puzzles.Other things--------------- Some bugs and glitches.Good parts------------- Could be fun for the kids who want something oversimplified and dumbed down at extreme... minimalistic, i mean :D- I like the graphics, a real RPG with this graphics would be awesome. I have to keep searching...

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Danger has an interesting battle mechanic where you can 'Rewind' your battles. In fact it's essential. Unfortunately there is little else of note here. Sorry.If you find the game on sale and the battle mechanic interests you then it may be worth a purchase, but as much as I hate to put down a developers hard work, I recommend you do not pay full price for it.I enjoyed micro-managing and rewinding my two-warrior party during battles, but things rarely get more complex than dodging and counter-attacking or exploding barrels from a distance. I can see why they limited parties to two - it would be too much to micro-manage a larger group of warriors.Skills are the usual fire/ice/heal magic type stuff, the very linear story is mostly uninteresting and the dialogue isn't great. Don't expect to get a choice of responses, there is no branching conversation tree, you're a passenger story-wise and I quite often found myself grinding my teeth at the heroines "Reluctant hero" shtick which went on for too long - I just didn't feel invested in the character at all.The game is largely a series of missions strung together with two to three small maps per mission including a dungeon, there is little variety to the assets so each island/dungeon looks largely the same. There is no loot beyond picking up inflammable things you can throw at enemies.The game saves automatically between each map (There is no manual save here). At the end of each mission you may upgrade one skill for one hero in your party (The game decides who), there are no accumulated "Upgrade points" to spend. Upgrades are pretty much along the lines of 'Small fireball', 'Bigger fireball', 'Biggest fireball'. Fire does spread if you hit something inflammable which is a nice thing to factor into your battle tactics, but it's not a new concept and there is an awful lot of inflammable foliage on an island and some tight enclosed spaces, so you do have to be extremely careful setting light to things.After each mission there might be a little dialogue to progress the story, then it's on to the next mission/set of maps. Do not expect a world map, side quests, things to click on, conversations with NPC's, loot, weapons and armour shops, deep conversation trees or other complex systems. They are not here.I will say that there's the bare bones of something which could have been great given enough time, resource and budget. Unfortunately what we have is merely an OK diversion. Maybe if there's an Iron Danger 2?Pros:* Interesting 'Rewind' battle mechanic* Nice graphics* Nice musicCons:* The 'Rewind' battle mechanic becomes repetitive* Complete absence of many of the systems I consider essential to an RPG/ARPG* No depth to the systems that are there* Uninspired skills and progression of those skills* Uninteresting linear story

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, finished it in two long sittings, because I couldn't resist.That said, it's clear during the game that there were planned more features for the game. The first and second town has shops, with keepers that greet You, but You cant buy anything from them.The current progression system also seems like a rushed thing. And the story ends at a good, point but in a cliff hanger.Nevertheless, upgrading Your skills is very fun. Dialog and story is natural and the music is just SOOO incredibly good! Half of the success of fun battling is because of the music.Definitely worth grabbing in a promotion.

_childDocuments_.review: Adventure game that is heavily inspired by the TRPG and Puzzle genre, with a unique time-manipulation mechanic that is super rewarding and turns more interesting as you progress through the game and gain more levels. Characters seems interesting, though the dialogue is not always respecting me as the player to figure our what's happening as they are stating pretty obvious stuff. Most of the time it's entertaining and giving you some giggles. The combat takes away the "mistake" factor from the game, you can try and optimize your strategy until you find a way to get out of the situation without taking damage. At first it feels weird but you get the hang of it quite quickly and then it becomes super rewarding. You get upgrades to skills and characters after almost every level, so you have something new to bring to battle each level. I understand that this level approach is kinda weird and old-school for a modern game, but it didn't bother me and the lenght of the levels and phasing is good. Enemy variation is good, level design seems interesting and diverse, animations seem good and the game looks awesome in 4k with maxed out graphics.The music in the game is very good and brings a lot of atmosphere / character to the different scenarios of the game. I like that they gave the music a big role in this game to set the mood of an level with a wide variety of songs to listen to while finding solutions for your fights. Some people are complaining about lack of character levels and gear to customize and after 3 hours in the game i don't need it, the game has other systems to reward the player. I don't just expect it to be a full blown trpg, if you look at it as a adventure/puzzle game with rpg elements your expectations will more likely get.Highly recommend this game, first chance in a modern game to get a grasp of finnish folklore and a great job from the studio.Will update when i finnish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Little to no story aside from Mcguffin the quest line, awful optimization in certain parts to the point my PC started chugging along in frames and heat. A completely worthless stealth mechanic that actually hinders the portions of the game you need to play stealthy in, since it makes you move slower while trying to avoid completely invincible automatons. Forgettable and bland enemy designs and environments, with almost no distinction from island to island short of layout. Character dialogue is awkward, poorly delivered, actually recycled when Kipuna calls for the Healer twice (which sounds like she's calling a f*cking dog), and not at all fitting some characters to say. For instance, at one point in the story Kipuna is angry that the bad guys stole a mcguffin stone from her, and weirdly exclaims that she's "going to burn them all." Like, she really hasn't even enjoyed the idea of these stones much from the start to when this happens, and is now planning to exact vengeance on the people who took her favorite toy because, well, plot for a possible sequel. There's a really f*cked up moment where a fellow protagonist (who you actually have to play as at some points to further the game) tries to demand a kiss from Kipuna, even though it doesn't fit either character to want or ask for it. She tells him off, and starts demanding from the Healer and another character Tobi that he should leave, and they tell her don't bother. Then the character in question gets poisoned, and all of a sudden Kipuna is worried sick about him? Like, to the point you race against the clock to find the Healer to help revive him. Who literally says she can't do anything for him, and yet he brushes off the poison on his own. No explanation, no dramatic subversion, he's just fine all of a sudden. Don't worry, it never happened level of forgetfulness on the storyboard artists' parts.This is called an RPG, and should not at all be considered or advertised as one in my opinion. There are no choices you make to advance the plot or develop your character. Your skills, talents, and gameplay are defined by the main story, more akin to a technical metroidvania in that as you progress, new abilities are unlocked as the need for them arises. There is entirely no skill tree, no branching dialogue, not even side quests. There is a singular set of things you can change at the end of levels, being what skills do you know off of a checklist and how effective they are. They did the absolute bare minimum for this to qualify as an RPG and it hurts the game so badly. And because this game is so well balanced, of course there's really only one or two spells you need to win, being Fireball and Heal. Every other skill or spell is largely a waste of time due to them either being weak in damage, or just taking too many frames to be worth it. Tobi gets a skill called "Bull Rush" or something you can unlock at the end of the first or second level, and after the next island, I never found an opportunity to use it because it was so laggy, and he would always take unnecessary damage for using it.The story itself is just laughable. Get 5 shards so you can power a city's defense wall, so said by this world's version of Hercules. What a fun way to get me to play the main story, by telling me to. Not by giving me any kind of stakes, or having any personal involvement. And then your character decides, "f*ck it, I'm just going to go kill the Queen of the bad guys" anyway. Why wasn't this the initial setup? Its just so badly handled, and completely removes any intrigue you have in the story by the Devs basically admitting they phoned it in. After all, why learn from better games like Assassin's Creed 1 about bad story configuration when you can just smash the same quest into a game 5 times over? This does not make an engaging experience.TL;DR- I regret ever paying money for this game. Every aspect of it is just okay at best, and with such an interesting gimmick to help the combat feel weighty and important, the game fails in every respect beyond it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great little indie rpg gem.It has a unique time rewind/stop mechanic, which made me interested in the game in the first place.The game clocks around 10 hours or maybe little less, it's short and sweet.Unfortunately daring devs like these who try something new usually dont get  the attention/fame they deserve so the game probably underperformed. Would love a second game or at least more games from the same dev.Pros:*decent Story*likeable even though few Characters*Voice acting (pretty good voice acting)*Combat system is different and fun/a breath of fresh air Cons:*Don't know why but the game kinda made my cpu and gpu sweat (temp wise).Didn't have performance issues though.*Combat is funa and fresh but i cant put my finger on it it was somehow lacking something for me (maybe more party members or something not sure)Would definately recommend if you like rpgs. It's cheap especially on sale.P.s.: If you like hidden gems like these you should definately try Druidstone and Tower of Time.
