_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed this game. Great artwork, very good voice acting, good (if tropy) characters and an intriguing story (a little more on that below) provide a good setting for the unique take on a turn-based combat system. Here you can rollback time for a certain amount of heartbeats which allows to dodge incoming damage or perfectly time attacks. Especially the final few encounters were very satisfying, in no small part due to one power you get later in the game (no spoilers).As mentioned before I want to finish with a note on the story: I would have liked to stay with the characters longer, know where (or rather how) their journey takes them after the end. This is not necessarily a bad thing, the ending worked well for me. But still, to know how they .... would have been nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Plenty of potential, but missing plenty of accessibility functions.With how small the icons are for the core battle mechanics, it is difficult to read and very easy for it to click through. While rare, this can force a restart as once you get hit, if you don't die, the game will continue on the timeline until you stop being hit. This can result in being stunlocked until you can't undo the action that caused your death. And holding shift the entire time to try to prevent this from happening is not exactly fun.A lot of the shortcuts should have toggle options and the click detection for the actions need to be more solid to reduce click through.Certain areas of the map are just frustrating because it looks like you can pass through, but you can't or if you don't carefully navigate one step at a time, your character might take a much longer path. This gets worse at the end of the game where one area causes your character to spiral into the air (these glitchy areas also make time pass very quickly). That's levitation, Holmes.There are plenty of exploits in this game as well. Probably what annoys me most is the There are also limited ability to jump forward if you just want to pass time during combat because you are doing stunlocks and just to get to your next lock.  There are some exploits if you want to cheese the fights. The last fight can be completely cheesed if you know how.There is also one section where a  activates a barrier and you can get stuck outside the barrier, making the (optional) objective potentially impossible (luckily, that barrier allowed some spells to pass through, unlike one of the later barriers). Fortunately, it seems that if you do end up stuck outside, you do not actually need to kill the enemies inside (except for an achievement, but you can get credit for that achievement elsewhere) as it seems the objective is meant for if you end up being trapped by the trap.Without the glitches and other issues, this game is probably about 12 hours long if you go at a relatively quick pace (even if you collect and kill everything). The issues extend the time it takes to complete missions.Also, be aware to restart the game every 4-8 hours. I experienced some severe system-wide lag/fps drop around the 9 hour mark, which stopped when I restarted the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Price of Persia: Sands of time mixed with an isometric RPG.  It is relatively short and inexpensive.  Buy it on Sale.I find this game frustrating.  There are very good things and things that need work.Like an RPG your characters get better over time and gain new abilities, some of which are useful and others are profoundly useless.  Like the healing ability, which sounds useful until you realize YOU CONTROL TIME.  My characters came out of almost every battle without a scratch, because YOU CONTROL TIME.  Get hit, roll back time, make a mistake, roll back time.  This isn't a bad thing.  It turns every enemy encounter into a neat puzzle game.  Will you step left hit the enemy, back step and shoot an arrow or fall back and knock over a dead tree to fall on the bad guys head.  Possibilities are endless and a wrong choice can lead to certain demise.  However.  Why is there HP? It feels that, like Prince of Persia, hits should be deadlier.  Perhaps a three strikes your out kind of thing, where every time your hit you lose a bar of life and damage persists through the entire mission, so that you have to weigh pulling off an awesome move that costs you a hit or backing up and trying something else.  There is also a plethora of healing items.  Putting aside the question of how someone is caring three barrels of oil in their pockets, I think in a game like this items should be very powerful and you can carry one at a time.  Most of the time you will only have the time to use a single item per combat anyway.The last detractor is the story.  This is someone's D&D Campaign.  The Main characters are a Sorcerer, a Fighter, a Druid, and a Ranger.  That's not a bad thing, but this story feels very trope heavy.  Find all the McGuffins and everybody is lying to you.  I like the idea that each of the companions pulls the main character their own way.  The Druid wants you to find the McGuffins because her totally not evil god told you to, The fighter wants you you follow orders from the totally not evil immortal king, and the Ranger wants you to do whatever you want as long as you don't mind that he does some totally justified and not evil stuff along the way.  I feel there could have been a multiple endings scenario where you choose which companion to side with, however the fact that the protagonist goes her own way is an acceptable outcome as well.  Could have used a little more time to get to know these characters too.  The story is let down by some wonky dialog along the way and by our teen protagonist making some decisions dictated by the plot.  One more pass on the writing front would have done the game some good.Finally the game doesn't end properly.  I was all geared up for the last battle against the evil queen (where we learn she isn't so evil) when the game just ends.  I mean I understand that the creators want to eat something tomorrow too, but this was NOT a good ending.  In my two cents the main character should have returned the Macguffins to the totally not evil king.  That way we get an acceptable ending and the next game could have a similar power progression as you get the MacGuffins back from the totally not evil king when he turns out to be evil.  Well, c'est la vie.  At this point I doubt we are going to get a sequel so be forewarned the game gives story blue balls.Overall Buy it on sale.  It has neat ideas and a passable story.  The short length means that, while combat can get a little tedious, it won't try your patience.  Here's hopping they make some improvements and come out with another one.

_childDocuments_.review: Tried as I may I could not get into it. The game puts the entire focus on it's time manipulation system and it felt cumbersome and boring for me. You are constantly going back and forward, the fight is always on pause, and you never really get to see the entire thing play out. It would have been cool if they allowed you to lay out your actions, see them resolve, and then live with the outcome. Instead every fight felt like a chore for me. There is no loot, no character customization, and very linear gameplay. I did think the voice acting was good and the world map was absolutely beautiful. I think you can get all the achievements in one run so originally I told myself I would bear it for that reason but then I realized it would be silly to waste my time on a game I wasn't having fun with.Some folks might like this sort of thing but I just could not justify putting the time into it. There are things to take into consideration though because it may not be for everyone.- The mechanics heavily revolve around using your ability to go back in time, It may seem hard since you can easily get insta-killed but that is because you are meant to go back and fix your mistakes.-The skill system is akin to something like Divinity Original Sin but it is not open world. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it a lot; I can see some people bouncing off it, but I think it's worth a shot for most people. A few notes and caveats:* It's a pretty tight experience. No open world exploration or complex builds to be found here; just 20-ish hours of gameplay.* There are some rough edges, but nothing that'll force you to restart, or really derail your experience by more than a few seconds. Dialogue might repeat, and some mechanics (looking at you, automatons) don't handle time-warping perfectly.* You might enjoy this more if you like setting your own goals and playing with the system. Merely winning each fight is trivial, but if you're the sort that'll appreciate the satisfaction of orchestrating a pixel-perfect symphony of environmental hazards and explosions, you'll enjoy playing around with this game.* You might enjoy this more if you like experimenting. You'll have a couple dozen abilities and combat options, and you really only need a few to clear the game. If you're the sort to find your favorites early and stick to them, you may end up rather bored.Definitely looking forward to a possible Iron Danger 2!

_childDocuments_.review: After a rocky start, I really grew to enjoy this game. It has some tough parts, there's a LOT of trial and error involved in the encounters, and it can take a bit of time to get a feel for the timing you need. Most of the characters are likable (Lemichen being a notable exception), the artwork is gorgeous, and the music has no right being as good as it is. If you go in expecting to bang your head against some difficulty spikes, and don't need a completely cohesive story or character development, you will find this to be a really fun tactics game.

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Danger has one of those mechanics that FEELS like it should be innovative and interesting. But the pacing of the combat and the sheer confusing nature once you introduce multiple characters makes it a very hard game to play... and not due to difficulty. Its a shame because it looks to be a competently designed RPG then this mechanic has been put in and sort of ruined it.This feels like it may be a marmite mechanic "love it or hate it" but I am definitely in the "hate it" camp. If you like rewinding the combat to perfect the fights you may get a kick out of this but more than likely you'll realise why no other RPGs offer this without calling it "savescumming".

_childDocuments_.review: Isometric action-rpg with a built-in time rewind mechanic. Start out by reacting to what your enemies are about to do and blocking, dodging, moving away or attacking in the perfect way to ruin their ♥♥♥♥. Then throw in fire, poison, cold, ice, area effects, buffs, and a LOT of explosions.The basic gameplay loop is hella fun. You can execute a complex plan with multiple consumables and interlocking elemental effects to take out an entire enemy encounter at once. Or you could lure a troll into an enemy camp and laugh as he wreaks havoc. Or you could rewind face-bash your through the bad guys by simply attacking them to death.It's fairly addictive. 1. The scope of the game is fairly modest. No real skill trees, dialog choices or gear. The story ends as you defeat a mid-boss and decide to take the fight to the enemy. No new game plus or level editor, both of which would be incredible.2. A lot of minor bugs. None of them gamebreaking, but all persistent and annoying.I wrote some more in-depth impressions .Yeah, it's a lot of fun. Just keep in mind it's probably a one-and-done, worth approximately 15-20 hours of gameplay.Hopefully, the sequel is going to be highly expanded.

_childDocuments_.review: If you, like I, find yourself getting lulled into the concept that this game is ANYTHING like Solasta, BG3, Divinity OS2, or Wasteland 2+3; basically ANY tactical RPG games like the steam algorithms claim it to be, then boy will you be pissed off like I just was. This game has no 'tactical' choices in reality. There's this strange 'prince of persia' time rewind trick that happens anytime a combat occurs. You cannot 'lose' a combat- you just rewind and choose the option that makes you win. This is a really REALLY pretty and fancy slide show with some interactivity elements involved.In fairness, I played for an hour and was displeased with the mechanics and gameplay based on my expectation that this game was in fact a tactical RPG. Past that, I will say that what I did look at was gorgeous visually and the voice acting was well implemented without some of the usual hiccups that I encounter. But it's just NOT the game I thought it was going to be, and for that- I requested a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: This game features REALLY unique combat system. What do you get when you mix action and turn-based combat? RTwP is the wrong answer - always has been! THIS game shows the proper way to do it. You can dodge, parry, lunge, attack and counter-attack, use various magic tricks and items to your advantage. It feels a lot like a description of sword combat in books, a blow-by-blow account of fight between two master fencers. This system would fit The Witcher wonderfully, for example.The rest of the game is... Well, less interesting. The world is Viking-themed, the plot is MacGuffin hunt, and the characters attempt a bit of drama, but never succeed. However, it's easy to look beyond all that, and slightly unpolished UI, too, just for the innovative and interesting combat mechanic alone.I wish someone would copy that mechanic in a bigger-budget game - it certainly deserves to take its place among standard approaches to combat in video games.

_childDocuments_.review: The time mechanic is challenging but an enjoyable gameplay experience.The ability to rewind time does, at least for me, bring out ones inner perfectionist, as you won't want to get hit during combat and will try micromanage your moves to avoid taking damage at all. This also shows you how the enemy can adapt to even small changes done by the player during combat. The lack of manual saving does bother at first, but as the levels are designed to be compact enough that you aren't greatly affected by it. The compact levels also make it so that it is easy to enjoy in small chunks. Sometimes you feel like you would want to be able to zoom the camera out just a little bit more than the game lets you.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game with a unique combat system that lets you manipulate a timeline of events. I find this makes combat a bit easy and turns it into more of a puzzle where you're trying to find the right actions to get away without taking damage. Aside from that, the story is interesting enough and I really enjoy the music. Would recommend just to try out the combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10This is a tactical combat game first and foremost and it's a really good one. It also features a good story with good voiceovers. But this is not an RPG, no XP, no leveling, no decisions although you do get to choose a new ability or upgrade an old one for one of your characters after almost every mission.The combat gameplay is reminiscent of Baldur's Gate style RPGs but instead of throwing tons of RNG in your face this one is deterministic in nature and to help you cope with the challenge of facing overwhelming odds, you can turn the time back up to 14 half-second steps. This makes the gameplay an interesting mix of tactical tinkering and trial and error. Positioning, timing, resource management and chosing the right tool at the right time are key to winning. And with over a dozen distinct actions per character, including different moving attacks, dodges, blocks, knockback attacks, position swapping, grenades, explosive barrels and the ever growing magic repertoire of your main character, there is a lot of room for tactical experimentation that always feels satisfying and challenging.The biggest drawbacks are a narrow focus on a set storyline with no sidequests or rewarding optionals, no branching of any kind and some UI issues - like consumables that cannot be picked up. Very much recommended to anyone who likes tactical combat, storytelling games and the rewind mechanics of games like Braid and Life is Strange.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply fantastic.Perhaps you're something like me - you really *want* to be into XCOM, but the perfectionist side of you makes it hard. _childDocuments_.review: It all started with the save scamming. Remember the old school role-playing titles like ? There were powerful spells that had chance to kill any enemy from one hit but the chance for it was pretty small. Now what did people do? Naturally, they used to save before the battle, tried to cast the spell and if it didn't work, they just loaded their save and tried again. Just because it was an easy way to win and... you know how it is. People love the easy ways. Well, as long as those are not the  fans but we're not talking about those masochists today. , later, when playing games in a proper way started to get completely out of fashion, publishers started to add a certain feature to their games. A feature that allowed us to “rewind” things and try again. Without even using an old school save feature. Press one button and pretend that you didn't die a second ago. In a way, it was like watching movies on . You know... ? That bulky thing... with tapes? The one that allowed us, old geezers, to watch movies at home before most of you, youngsters, were even born? OK, OK, I'm shutting up now, don't be mad.One way or another, most of the time it was a way to make the old games easier. Just because the current generation of players don't really understand the fun of dying a lot and developing a skill (again, we're not talking about the  audience today). Which used to make winning a lot more satisfying. Nobody wants to play the same exact game every morning before going to school. Just to become really good at it one day and actually see the ending. Which was usually something like “CONGRATULATION” screen but that... was... not... the... point. Anyway, people want things easier nowadays. So, the big re-releases like   and  () offered the “rewind” feature. Just to make those popular games more accessible for the modern kids. The guys from , though, decided that it'll be fun to add such feature to a modern  title. Like  added time manipulation to their . Not to make things easier this time. But just... for fun. To make their game to stand out. Sounds good, right? Well, unfortunately, the  is far from being good. For many reasons. See, when you see the “rewind” feature in action for the first time, it'll look pretty fun and promising. But the more you'll play this game, the less fun it'll look.First of all, don't expect a proper  experience here.  is just a short (about ten hours on low difficulty) series of missions that take place on tiny little maps. You finish one mission – another one begins. No proper world, no towns, no exploration, no proper interaction with , no complicated dialogues, no choices, nothing like that. Just you and some missions that involve killing monsters. You know, like it was in good ol' , for example (pretty bad comparison, I know, but still). Nothing's wrong with that, though. The formula may totally work. Even today. As long as it's done right? It can totally work. The problem is... it wasn't done right here. See, in this game there are only two types of missions. The ones in which you should open the door to the temple by interacting with magical switches and the ones where you enter the temple and look for shards that'll unlock a new set of skills for your main character (fire, ice, nature, healing... you know the stuff). And all of such missions feel almost identical. As the result, the game beings to feel old pretty fast. Right after the second chapter, actually (there are seven chapters in total). And the fact that the story is barely there and the game even ends with the most poor cliffhanger you can ever imagine (kill a pretty common boss who's pretty much nobody – see the characters sailing away to “the next big thing” because developers got tired of working on their product), there's a big chance you'll uninstall this game long before finishing it. Just because it isn't  enough. The game fails to give you enough motivation to continue and that's it. You install the game, you check the “rewind” feature and then that's it. There's no reason to waste any more time.And it's not like the main selling point of the game works especially well either. Very soon the “rewind” feature stops being fun and starts being annoying. You can't disable it (you meet the enemy – the “rewind” thing turns on and the game begins to feel like a crappy almost-turn-based-something), the characters die a bit too fast, controlling two characters, who often die from one hit, at the same time is really painful (even if one character will get lucky, there's always a chance that another one will die at the same exact time, which means that you'll need to rewind things and try everything all over again), environment adds heck of a lot of problems (yes, characters here can and will stuck in the walls), etc, etc, etc.  looks and feels like yet another cheap  from wannabe developers. Only its main selling point... kind of ruins everything. I mean, we've all played tons of cheap s in . But imagine them being especially slow and requiring you to interact with the annoying  thingy every single time you want to attack somebody? It's just... isn't fun. The magic of the initial “OMG, I love the idea!” disappears very soon and after that? There's only pain.In other words, instead of being “yet another one of those cheap s”,  tries to win by adding the unique feature. Unfortunately, not only that feature fails to save the game from its mediocrity, it also makes it a bit more annoying than needed. Being yet another generic and cheap  is bad as is.  already has tons them. And nobody really needs another one of those games that you forget right after finishing. But ? It adds some really annoying things to the formula. And even though I totally admire it for its attempts of being unique, the game with no face that fails to be fun? It's not something you'll want to waste your time on. Dixi.

_childDocuments_.review: The hybrid between real time and turn based movement respective fighting is a fresh and interesting approach to battle mechanics. I quickly adapted to mostly using kind of hit-and-run combos, because these were clearly superior to a broader approach with using consumables, which also limited the tactical aspect of the game for me. Furthermore, I wish I had more than only two heroes under my control in battle at once, but I guess this would have made the difficulty level trivial, since the time control feature is quite powerful. There are no save points on the maps, therefore you need to finish them in one run, though this is easy doable (in about 30 to 60 minutes), because the time mechanics work as a quick save to not call it save scumming. Although the story is a little cliché, all in all my verdict tends to a positive, since the battle mechanics kept me going until the credits.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool twist on the hybrid realtime/turn-based tactical combat. You have the power to pause and reverse time in combat. The secret sauce is in how you control your party members. You can only control one character at a given moment, or "heartbeat", leaving the other character idle and vulnerable to enemy attacks. After you make your moves with one character you rewind the clock, undoing the seconds the enemy treated them as a punching bag, and play the other. This mechanic really carries the game. I'm still new to the game, but can tell it will take some time to master it although it feels intuitive and easy to grasp. The ideal battle ends without you taking a single hit because you've dodged or blocked every attack and landed every swing. Very difficult had you played it in real-time but do-able with time manipulation. After each stage you're told how many times each character died, which can be fairly high during those punching bag moments.Some negatives. From the first several maps I'm not expecting the environment or ai complexity of Shadow Tactics by a longshot. There are some environmental hazards but the enemies tend to walk right into them like moths to a flame. Also, the ai is dumb. Sneaking exists but it doesn't feel as good as Shadow Tactics. Last thing I'll mention is that it feels a bit difficult to die, at least so far. Given the ability to rewind, you can imagine why. I don't personally see this as a negative since it's part of the unique game mechanics, but worth mentioning. I'm only a couple hours in, so I'll update this review if things change later on.Lastly, I will mention I bought this game on sale for $6.99. So far I'm calling it a steal, but we'll see how much content there is. It would have been nice to see a bit more polish on the stealth mechanics along with better level designs along the lines of Shadow Tactics. But for $20 that is a lot to expect. They did a great job and I would like to see a more fleshed out game with the same mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Danger is a tactical RPG centered around the ability of the main character, Kipuna, to rewind time. The game features semi-real-time combat mechanics and a linear story that narrates the vicissitudes of Kipuna and her friend Topi, while also acting as a glue between fights, which are the main focus of the game.As I've already said in the introduction, Iron Danger lets us control two characters throughout its story: Kipuna, a young girl that, after a unique and strange event acquires the ability to use magic and rewind time, and Topi, an experienced and warm-hearted soldier wielding a big hammer and capable of devastating melee attacks. Fights are centered around these two characters and Kipuna's ability: we can, in fact, speak of semi-real-time combat since everything happens in real-time, but we can stop (and eventually rewind) the game every heartbeat (or 0.5 seconds).During combat, every action is recorder in a timeline that indicates what happens - and when. This gives us the ability to fix our mistakes by rewinding time, cancelling out-of-time attacks and blocking when we know that an enemy will strike. The whole mechanic is quite simple but very effective and well implemented, with the timeline that gives us a clear vision of everything that happens during the fight, even when things get... convoluted. Combat is further improved with the additions of power-ups for the characters' abilities: these effectively improve and/or add additional effects to Kipuna's and Topi's attacks and moves, making more strategies available as the game progresses.One of Iron Danger's most prominent problems is its linearity: the game calls itself an RPG but gives the player no choice on how to advance the story, no choice on how to build or equip the characters and ultimately no choice on what to do outside the main quest... because there's literally nothing outside of it. Locations are divided into watertight departments, one for each level, and generally following the same cycle: loading, initial dialogue with some exploration, one or more fights, some other exploration and then end of the level. Even exploration is itself very limited and only useful to reach the main objective of the level, but nothing more than that, since there are no secret areas or hidden loot (apart from food, which can be found in houses, but I wouldn't categorize that as hidden).This gets particularly obvious during mission 7, when the party reaches Kalevala, a big city filled with NPCs. Here there is no possibility to interact with anyone: you just have to traverse the city, get to a specific point in the map and then return to your ship. You can explore the (little) part of the city you have access to, but that's pretty useless since there are no NPCs to speak with and no loot to acquire. Not even a special scene or dialogues between the members of the party. Nothing.The other problem Iron Danger has is its technical side. There are no ways around it: the game is not optimized at all for what it delivers, and it shows. The medium number of FPS was on 28-29 with an RX580 8GB at 1440p all the time, with some noticeable frame drops in some areas. Also, changing the graphics settings of the game didn't help with the amount of frame. Apart from that, the game has a strong depth of field that cannot be disabled and can make the look of some locations worse.Path-finding, especially during exploration, can be quite clunky, while during combats it can be quite frustrating since it requires you to rewind time, often multiple times in a row until you find the right spot where to move the character.Iron Danger is a fine game during fights, but quite empty outside of them. Luckily, the game is filled with blows and fireball moments, but the asking price of 30€ is a little too high for what the game has to offer right now. Thus, I'll warmly recommend to buy it only on when it's on discount, since a 15-20€ price tag seems more fitting for the current state of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay first review in engelska, so bare with me. After watching the trailers I wasn't expecting too much - the time manipulating mechanic seemed cool and that was it. I've only played for a bit and holy cow this game is fun. I needed to stop playing and come to write this review since I'm afraid that this game ain't getting the attention it deserves.I'm a newbie in games like this and it shows in my gameplay. I get Topi killed like 40-1600 times in a mission but the game won't punish me on that. Just go back a couple heartbeats and you are good to try again. The time manipulation mechanic creates a really fun and addicting aspect that you have to try to get a clean fight without even a one hit taken. In  many fights only one hit will get you actually killed so you're kinda forced to try again. You block, "oh ****, it was too early", you attack, "oh dog, enemy was out of range". Once you manage to win an fight, it feels truly rewarding and satisfying. Like making a pizza dough and it comes out perfect. The graphics are beautiful and the soundtrack so far has been really, really good. I mean amazing. Lots of traditional finnish instruments can be heard which creates really "finnish" atmosphere in a way. If that makes any sense.Only thing that bugs me a bit is that movement animations looks a bit clumsy, but luckily there ain't  much of running in the game, so it isn't much of a problem. You run from a conversation to a fight and so on.Sometimes Iron Danger gets under your skin. Like when Cardi B is playing on the radio while waiting for your food in McDonalds. You're hungry as ♥♥♥♥ but you know after you're done, you are satisfied. Belly full of 20 Chicken McNuggets.. A Big Mac.. A Douple QP.. Half litre of strawberry milkshake.. Your body full of sugars and fat and you feel sad but you want more. Strangely addicting.Buy the game, it's awesome!PS. I'm really missing the sauna in Mörönperse :3

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 gameplay design and strategy when everything falls into place. you can make a good tactic, adjust it on the fly and come out with a great emergent gameplay experience where you have to try and plan in advance and finnaegale everything in place so everything comes out at the right time. Making combos feels fun and intuitive. There are a few cheesy strats, but nothing that's too overpowered or game-ruiningWhen it doesn't work, the game feels very clunky. At it's worst, its a trial and error based game where you just rewind time and make small adjustments to positioning. Game could've used some more polish in a lot of areas, notably AI and enemy design. Towards the end of the game grenadiers were lobbing ♥♥♥♥ from across the map Game is also optimized a bit poorly, I got 40 fps on low and I have a mid-tier PC. Story is also meh, although the MC was pretty cool. The side characters got some neat development but the overall story was incredibly underwhelming with how much time was spent in dialogue. Ending was sequel-bait but that's understandable from a first time dev team. It's a good gameNOTE: GAME IS SHORT, 8 HOURS OF GAMEPLAY, WORTH IT FOR RPG RTT or RTWP PLAYERS AND BELOW 10$

_childDocuments_.review: The time-line mechanic takes a moment to get used to, but once it is in control, it becomes a dance to play. ( , Well crafted set-piece levels with well thought out progression ( just ran for my life down a switchback path with a bear-machine hot on my heels. ) I have a feeling many players may find it a tad fiddly to begin with, as opposed to traditional battle of attrition, This changes it all though, letting you create perfect choreographies of death for your enemies. Peek into the future, see what is going to kill you, adjust. Once you have the hang of it you don't really need to manage every heartbeat anymore, but play creatively and rewind only when really necessary.Top stuff. No saving during levels is a minor negative but realize it, and plan your play session accordingly. The mechanic makes it pretty rare to really wipe out and have to replay a level.Beware, the game does let time suddenly run on uncontrolled sometimes even in the middle of battle. [DEVS PLEASE MAKE THAT NOT HAPPEN] . I assume this is a bug, not a feature.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this one!Not a perfect game by any means, but nothing bothered me enough to not ram through this game in the span of four days. I was already invested in the premise, since modern media inspired by Finnish folklore is scarce, but I ended up really enjoying the game mechanic, too!I don't usually enjoy games where you individually control and nitpick each party members actions, but kudos for the team to limiting it to only 2 characters at a time. I enjoyed fidgeting with different outcomes and more than once encountered some triumphant accidents. I ironically lost my sense of time during combat almost every time and only afterwards realized I had played for hours. Visually and lore wise this game is a delight. The environments are lush, colorful and welcoming, exploring them was fun, though navigating was occasionally difficult. I really enjoyed how Kalevala and Finnish folk lore were adapted in the game and encountering new enemies was always fun. I honestly need more content like this, please and thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little game. It has a very interesting story, the graphics are nice and the soundtrack is very good. The fighting mechanic is quite unique, but can be a bit of a challenge at the beginning. After you get used to it, it's a lot of fun though. The special thing about the combat is that you can rewind the time. So if your strategy doesn`t work, just rewind the time and try something else. Also if you walk into a trap, while not in combat, the game will automatically stop, and put you in rewind mode, so you can just rewind the time, and walk around the trap safely like nothing happend. Because of the rewind mechanic, the combat, which there is a lot of, is a lot try and error, and it can be frustrating for some players.

_childDocuments_.review: No, no, no and once again no.The premise of the fighting is nice, but it is done so horribly it ends up just being frustrating.You control two characters? So why the hell when in trance state you give order to one character it moves time and the other character is idle? This completely ruins the whole premise of tactical combat using two characters. It forces you to move one, look at second character do nothing or fail his action and then turn back time so you can give second one correct action to perform at the same time as the first one. It is a really bad design around interesting mechanic. It ends up in a click fest of turning back time by 1 tile/action every time you want to coordinate movement between both of your characters. What would fix it is actual stop/release time where you can control both characters and then release time. But it would be just an active pause wouldn't it?On the other hand the voice acting and graphics are good. Not much to say about story as I cannot progress with this fight system. Not because it is hard, but because it is tiresome.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and casual game with some pretty neat combat mechanics. It feels like every fight is a dynamic puzzle that you solve by turning back the combat timeline and tweaking actions until you get win the encounter without taking a hit. The story wasn't bad wasn't great.Only downsides are that it's pretty short. There's roughly 9-10 hours of content here, and the ending is basically a abrupt cliffhanger for (maybe?) a second game. _childDocuments_.review: [7.5/10] Got this game as a gift and I absolutely loved it! Admittedly the game is quite short (I 100% the entire game and achievements within 21 hours and 1 main play through), but the gameplay mechanics are super fun. The core mechanic of rewinding time is really fun to dive into, allowing you to craft the perfect strategy where you take out all the enemies in one fell swoop. There definitely are some tedious bits in the campaign which can be irritating to work through (it can feel as if you are just brute forcing it) but overall the time rewind mechanic partnered with environmental tools makes for some really fun game play.The story is pretty short and simple, nothing mind boggling yet, but the enemy design and lore behind them is pretty cool. That said, the story has yet to be fully wrapped up in this game, hopefully implying a sequel is on the way soon. The graphics are gorgeous (it feels as if you are playing with table top figurines), and most devices should be able to handle it. The music is incredible, and with good speakers it is very immersive.Besides that, there are some frustrating design issues such as random locked doors that seem like secrets (but aren't), as well as certain attacks and environmental traps not working as intended. The characters can seem quite selfish or dumb even at some points, which can be quite annoying to deal with, but overall they are okay. I really cannot wait for a sequel where this incredible mechanic is used further, because its really fun to tinker around with it.

_childDocuments_.review: The big draw here is the combat system; it's not the most clearly explained in the marketing materials necessarily, but once you start playing, it clicks into place almost immediately. Being able to rewind in combat and plan our your attacks again and again until it works out in your favour is a great concept, and for the most part it's really well executed. I found the combat was really enjoyable. There are a few cases where it's not clear why you're taking damage or being knocked down, which makes adapting to those fights much more annoying, but for the most part it's pretty fun to tweak and reconfigure your approach, preternaturally dodge arrows and attacks, blast units just as they're emerging from hiding, and so on. Worth playing for the combat system for sure.The story is fine overall. I like that Kipuna seems a bit more hard-headed and self-aware than you'd expect from your average video game protagonists, and I like that there seems to be some greyness to the characters and the setting. Aside from the Finnish touches, though, the world and setting feel very uninspired and typical, like any other random fantasy setting. Unfortunately the game ends on a cliffhanger, setting the stage for a sequel. That's okay, since I do hope they actually get to make an Iron Danger 2 and not just leave it at that, but it felt a bit abrupt.It's a pretty little game, not too long, and given the above, I'd say it's worth checking out if you're interested in these kinds of tactical combat games.

_childDocuments_.review: Only 50% of players make it to the 2nd achievement in the game. It's difficult! Like, after the first couple levels, they make the game very, very, very hard. So the mechanics are a little clunky. I wish I could just use WASD to move the camera around, but the game has a lot of shortcuts for actions tied to that. You operate a two team group a big dude and a little girl. You have to go into combat, get hurt and killed, then reverse time and hopefully kill the enemy with the new knowledge of their attacks. It's like combining turned based RPG mechanics with Braid. I found the controlling of my characters and understanding how to overcome attacks was very hard to manage. It's not like I didn't know what to do, but an attacked would land at this time, my attack would land before that time, I'd still get hit; so I have to go back and try another method.But for me, the big nope was when I met the bandit camp. That's your 4th map into the game. They threw 5 bandits at me at once! I had to initially fight 3 bandits: 2 crossbowmen who can attack every 3 turns and an guy with an axe who can attack every 3 turns. I have my big guy who can attack every 3 turns, but cannot because I have to block every attack. The little girl has a fireball spell that takes 7 to 9 turns to regen, and if it hits correctly, does like 50 damage for guys with 250 health. So I'm blocking with my tank and waiting around for my useless wizard girl to slowly kill these bandits. The fight takes forever and 5 or 6 times I just wanted to give up, but I overcame. Take 3 steps away from that fight and BOOM 5 dudes all agro... Nope! I'm not doing this anymore!

_childDocuments_.review: I mean wow, just by the core mechanics alone, this game is noteworthy enough and should be on any action strategy or tactics' fan's to-play list. If you loved 'Price of Persia: Sands of Time' and Nicholas Cage's 'NEXT' movie, this is a game for you. Ever fantasized of controlling every choice in your life down to the split-seconds so your whole life is lived optimally, without fault, and with grace? This is the game for you. If you love Iron Man's origin story (vaguely), you'd probably relate and love this. You will probably struggle with the character-locked cam as well as the constant reset of character selection every time you go back in time for the first few hours, but it's gonna be fine if you tune yourself alongside the kinda dogsh*t UX configuration that cannot be customized.IRON DANGER has a ton of wasted potential:- The level/session-based environments of each stage (even the ones that are part of the narrative with only talking) are beautifully crafted without more meaning to them. You can't explore and collect lore, collectibles, items and or interact with most NPCs. It feels like there could be so much more to do, especially in town.- Could be expanded into so much more, with RPG leveling/advacement and such.- Why do I craft every move so meticulously in battle such that I don't get a single damage while giving my characters so much chemistry and cooperation completing it with such grace.. just not NOT be able to re-watch it live? It would be so cool to see the perfect battle I have crafted in real-time action. I mean, your system is there. Just save every decision and replay it.! Updated !Cons: Some intense battles have multiple split second tweaks that take FOREVER to rewind redo rewind redo, to realize you can't perfect it and going on to find the next best solution while taking damage, PLUS always fighting with navigating the terrain that blocks input, walking or even skills, till a point I wanna bash the computer screen in. ♥♥♥♥! At the end of it it's so tiring yet you cannot re-watch it live. Serious bummer.

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay idea is interesting... but not great for a game. The problem is it's built around managing time, going backwards and redoing whenever something goes wrong. So you fight enemies that can seriously injur you with a sudden attack, so you roll back time to avoid it before it hit... that's basically just save skumming, saving and loading every few seconds, through a series of some sixteen or so auto saves in your  current timeline. The combat itself is... repetitive fairly quickly, and often annoying and the tougher enemies just take a long time and aren't really satisfying to fight.The core gameplay is, simply, ok... not great or especially enjoyable, and over the coarse of the game it just drags on and on... And now that I hit one area where I had to "find" a character hiding on the map, and I'd run around it three times looking for them... I'm just stopping. I don't even find it fun, I was only trying to play to finish the story but it wasn't even that engaging so I, the type of person that wants to finish all games I play, am just stopping part way through rather unsatisfied, yet happy that I wont have to keep trudging through it after this, so in the end I can't recomend it.

The game was excellent, it just took a little while to learn combat system, which was a unique combat system and different than any I have played.  The story was good to very good, the music was top notch, amazing and the ending was probably one of the best ending games I have seen.  The ending song that plays at the end of the closing scene and during the credits was absolutely wonderful and amazing.  Great Cello, Violin, solo and orchestra.  Beautiful music. _childDocuments_.review: While I will praise them for trying to go with a more unique approach to gameplay, it feels like a clunkier version of real time with pause where all the goods were removed. The entire game will make you feel like you're wrestling with the poor control than fighting the enemies.For example, when you queue order in the timeline, you have to hold shift or else, the action are immediately carried out. Plotting the actions without them being carried out should have been the default, especially when the second major issue presents itself.When stuff are carried out, most of the time, you can't pause it to queue another order or immediately rewind, you have to watch the whole thing happen before you can rewind. If a character is using an attack then get hit, that's 2-3 seconds of gameplay gone that you are going to rewind anyway but cannot because the game doesn't give you the ability to pause and interrupt.And while stuff are fast forwarding or rewinding, you can't buffer a common. When you just want to rewind 1 unit and queue another attack, if you don't wait for the whole action to finish animation when pressing the skills button, nothing is queued. When you left click afterward, the character just run in a straight line and once again, you are stuck watching the thing happen, have to watch the character get hit, the rewind. These are just the most obvious are there are A LOT more stuff that will further hinder your ability to control anything in this game, like how the game is always played with the time manipulation in mind so assigning movement or picking up items comes with a delay by default. I have way easier time giving precise control to a group of 5 or 6 in RTwP than controller just 2 characters in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this game an average review I would. On the plus side the central time rewind mechanic is well done and makes each fight a little puzzle of sorts, how to move and have your attacks connect while avoiding all damage yourself. On the other hand the game has some weird negative quirks. The total lack of loot except the occasional consumable kills any purpose to explore the nicely rendered maps, but they frequently have dead ends to go down and little hidden areas with nothing in them. In general they feel like they were designed for a game that had a lot of features cut. The game would be considerably more fun with equipment to find. The graphics optimization is pretty darn bad. This game will heat up your rig and struggle to maintain FPS all along the way, but the graphics aren't anywhere near good enough for that to be the case. I get a solid 60+ FPS in RDR2 but this game drops to single digits at the same resolution fairly often, which is just unacceptable. Oddly, lowering the detail level doesn't make the performance better. There are no graphical settings other than a single slider for detail, so it's not easy to diagnose that any further. It's just not well designed in that aspect. The levels can drag a bit long given that there's no saving within a level. The lack of quicksave is fine as time rewind makes it largely pointless, but being able to save a session and come back later would have made the game a lot more accessible. Development has ended, so I don't expect any of this will ever be fixed. I liked it well enough that I hope they make a sequel or a similar game that addresses the points above. As is it's a B rating, good one to get on sale if you like semi-turn-based tactical combat similar to Divinity Original Sin, but with a gimmick in place of 99% of the complexity. It's a good gimmick but it shouldn't be trying to carry the game all alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Danger (stupid title) is a tactical (action) combat game with a unique (prince of persia, anyone?) time manipulation mechanic. A never before seen (I got it at 'unique', you special snowflake) combination that blends the tactical depth of turn-based games (who first, and how?) with the exciting action (panic panic panic) of real-time games (and nothing else - no RPG, no stats). A wonderful alternative to the ever present quicksave/quickload/checkpoint mechanics that other games require.Sortof a Sands-of-Time meets ARPG. I really hope that there is more to come. After all there is room for improvement and far more of the world to be told.There could have been non linear progression.There could have been rewards for exploration (right now you can do just the minimal required, no need to kill everyone)There could have been a party and not just Hero+extra (one of three, dictated by the mission)There could have been a less clinffhangy finish (don't read this as an unfinished game)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is rather original in its mechanics, but its very slow, very, very slow. Everything explodes, you can make 1000+ damage combos within a few heart beats, but when game pauses, and you can avoid any attack, enemies just stand and doesn't have a chance, there're thoughts in my head, that some overcaring Dad made a playground for his daughter (Kipuna). Totally no emotions in this game, you can rewind anything, and if there is something stronger, you can ride a very tough automaton. But! This game isn't boring, and even if slow, its not so easy at the beggining. What's more, there're things really shining, like voice acting, like doing some matrix-like scenography sequences, like paradox between medieval and cyberpunk style. There's still some chapters before me, but I can already say, that this game has potential to be real in terms of opponents behaviour. There's really much more place for difficulty, so I don't understand why enemies doesn't go for you, when you're killing 10 metres behind them (or 15). It would be much more fun, if every enemy was alerted by explosion, and every of them came for you. But probably there's no money for testers, so I can understand this. In most games enemies wait patiently for you to come, because it would be impossible to defeat all at once, but here its possible, you can dodge four hits with one move, swap positions with enemies, everything.So to sum it up, someone took some really best, rare ingredients and made a dish, that was probably best possible at that time, but when you get it on an old table with very used cutlery, in a small, sideway pub... Lets say this game is not a must, but I won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like tactical RPGs? Do you  wish save scumming was more convenient? Do you not care for gear treadmills? Are you willing to put up with pretty poorly written dialog? Iron Danger might be for youTactical RPG where the only equipment are consumables, you aren't required to murder absolutely everything to progress at the proper speed, and you can rewind the last few seconds with a flick of the mousewheel rather than spamming F5/F9. The writing isn't great but everything else is (It is 99% voice acted. I found a line missing voice acting but they aren't paying me to point it out.)It's more fun on hard difficulty but some aspects weren't thought out on such. Ex: Cooldowns are increased by 1 including an ability to just wait which can be accomplished by scrolling the mousewheel. The time mechanic looks like video editing software and Excel spreadsheets look more fun than the menus. Dialogue scenes awkwardly freeze time so characters will be facing wrong directions or in awkward positions, making it even harder to actually care about what is going on. There isn't much of an "rpg" element to the game either when you your skill upgrades just lower the cooldown slightly on 'swing sword' and exploring houses and environments only rewards you with things like fish to heal your HP with.It's a shame because the actual dialogue is well-written and the voice acting is good (though the story was hard to discern apart from any other vague "bad guys invade" trope.

_childDocuments_.review: This ended up being one my hardest reviews till day. Why? There are 2. (or 3.) main reasons: I've never been interested in isometric action-rpg games like Dota 2, Diablo etc. but rewind-time function encouraged me to pick up the game.I've never seen game's story end up in such a cliff-hanger since 1979 Revolution: Black Friday game and that game's development was threatened by Iran's government, in this game it just felt like they run out of money and/ or time to finish the campaign with 1 or 2 last levels with a Lowhee or similar boss-battle at Kavelava's northern border.(3.) And this is where giving positive/ negative review for this game gets hard. Heck, I changed my DOOM 2016 review to negative after that cliff-hanger ending. And don't get me wrong, teasing sequel is not a bad thing to do if you ask me. For example HALO 2 ending scene where Master Chief says he's heading to finish the fight felt great ending for me.But this isn't Microsoft funded triple-A game, Iron Danger is an indie-creation with quite a small marketing budget/ ability to draw the big audience aware of itself (as I'm writing this review Iron Danger has less than 150 reviews written). So I'm afraid game will not be commercially successful and thus why we never get to see the sequel I'd wish.But as a customer of this game (and only available to do so in Steam [*looks ostracizing to Epic sh|t store*]) we are able to review our games positive or negative which is shown at the top of game's store page, trying to help other players when deciding whether or not to buy the game.But with careful thinking of rest positives and negatives (right below) I end up giving this game positive review. Mostly in the hope that more people would end up buying this game and fund the sequel. As I'm writing this review, a global pandemic COVID-19 is going through the world and .+ lot of skills/ abilities per character + cool set pieces ( and couple of the bosses you end up fighting during the campaign)+ good tutorials for Kipuna's new shard abilities- only 2 characters at time controllable. Hopefully in sequel(s) we get to command 3 or 4 team-mates at a time.- Lemichen's dialogue is SO CRINGE sometimes () that I wished I could wipe my memory out of them.There's never been better game as a starting experience for isometric action-rpg genre; however suddenly ending story is a big bummer. We must hope that someday we see Iron Danger 2, otherwise a great concept that I wish to see more of will end up disappear like Aino sister of Joukahainen.

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Danger is great fun, if you like tactics and planning turn-based strategy fights down to the last detail. Because of the time travel mechanism, this is also possible for not so experienced tacticians, maybe you have to rewind 2-3 times more, but with a little bit of trial and error, I was able to find a solution in every fight.I really like the story of Iron Danger. It offers some surprises and twists and turns. It has many thrilling, but also some sad and grim moments. The story is easy to follow and the main characters also have some personality. Especially Kipuna has quickly become dear to my heart.(German Voice-over, many subtitles)Since the game has a wide range of functions, the controls are correspondingly complex. But both the skill selection, like the control of the characters in the world and the extensive options of the time travel function are technically well implemented.On the PC, all functions can be clicked with the mouse or directly triggered by hotkeys. All buttons are labeled with their shortcuts, the icons are well-designed, very exemplary. After a short acclimatization, I got along with it very easily. I can’t say anything about the gamepad controls now, but I think it should be easy to handle as well.Depending on how you play, Iron Danger offers 10-20 hours of play, which brings the purchase price in the reasonable to acceptable range. For my taste, the game could offer another game mode or any other features that would provide replay value.I am also a bit disappointed with the role-playing possibilities offered by Iron Danger. Here a lot more would have been possible, a small inventory system, some equipment and maybe a few basic values for level-ups. And the game would have been even more appealing for RPG fans on the one hand and on the other hand, it might have resulted in increased replay value. Chances were missed here, which could have been implemented with relatively little effort.In its present form, you play through the story once, which is also a totally good experience. But then a new run-through isn’t that exciting anymore, because there are only a few decisions, hardly any character-individualization and although the story is exciting and of high quality, it is also very linear. There is a lack of branching and real decisions, that would have been beneficial for the game.The small Finnish studio has delivered very high-quality work with Iron Danger. The game offers a great story, good turn-based strategy, a unique twist through the time travel mechanics, appealing graphics and good dubbing.On the negative side, I noticed that despite having a German publisher only English voice output is available. Additionally, from my point of view, the omitted potential for role-playing and variations in the story should be criticized. Here a solid good game could have been made much better with only little effort.If one compares the offered game fun with the price of the game, I would like to give a basic rating of 90%. But for a lack of replay value due to missed chances in RPG and story decisions, I deduct 5 %. This brings me to a final rating of 85 % for Iron Danger.The developers are talking about updates after release, but I doubt that completely new features will be added to the game. Therefore, I don’t expect that much will change in this evaluation afterward. But I would still like to take a look at the patch notes.

_childDocuments_.review: In short - Rogue-like RPG based on tedious time-rewind mechanic that gets boring soon  score 5/10 – it starts really well, but then only goes downwards, and feels like an USSR lifespan analogy.Only 7.8% of players got past half of the game, only 10.2% got to the half way mark. This is probably more telling than 8/10 or 9/10 reviews that you can see on the game page. This breakdown does reflect my opinion of the game – it starts well, looks interesting and the gameplay mechanic (rogue-like RPG where you can rewind time to align the actions of your characters) appears promising while the visuals are very pleasing with striking that balance between cartoon feel and a good degree of detail. But then you keep playing, and playing, and then you had enough, it is no longer interesting…Even though the game introduces new magic abilities for your main character they fail to inject new life into the game. You basically control only two characters at the time, with Kipuna (the main character who also has magic powers) being one of them for the vast majority of the game and work on micromanaging your team actions in time. Tome is broken down in linear timeslots where some action occupy more than one timeslot and you need to plan around it and also time your opponents movement and by the half way mar this becomes a daunting chore rather than fun gameplay mechanic – position-fireball-block-counter-fireball…rinse and repeat as you are pretty much immortal, because if one of your characters die you can just rewind. The voice acting does not help it as it swings from pathetic to pompous which in turn buries the mediocre story 6ft under with no chance for exhumation… I mean the story is centred around a girl who is collecting six shards of a magic stone to stop great evil of the Northerners invasion and some cliché traitors, the ending should have been her collecting all the shards, snapping her fingers and half of the invading army disappearing….All in all this game is not worth the asking price, and neither is it worth your time as only 1 in 10 gamers will go on to move on past half of it and it is not that long either (4-5 hours to complete half of it)For more review and recommendations follow meas a curator at

_childDocuments_.review: Best tactical combat I've ever experienced. A deadly dance between the heartbeats of time.So... how to define this game?It's like a turn-based combat where you don't wait for enemy turns.It reminds of classic RPG combat, but you don't need to hit pause every second.It's tactical like X-COM, but the save-scam is legit and there's no randomness at all.It feels like younger brother of Divinity: Original Sin in terms of blasting up poison clouds and throwing barrels.It's like Prince of Persia remakes, but it is ARPG and the amount of time rewinds isn't limited.Despite bearing similarity to a lot of games, Iron Danger is truly unique.There's no open world, inventory system or other classic RPG stuff. Iron Danger combat is so awesome that it doesn't need them.Don't get your hopes high, this is not an RPG, there are no dialogue choices. But the main protagonist feels ALIVE, the voice acting is so great, it totally compensates the lack of branching story.EDIT:Chapter VI of the game brought some battles that feel more epic than combat arenas of Doom Eternal. I'm being totally honest, my mind just got blown.

_childDocuments_.review: Intro:Iron Danger, developed by Action Squad Studios and published by Daedalic Entertainment, is a unique blend of tactical RPG and real-time strategy. Set in a steampunk-inspired world, the game introduces a fresh take on combat mechanics with its time-manipulation feature. Pros:- Innovative Time-Manipulation Mechanic: Iron Danger's standout feature is its time-manipulation system, allowing players to rewind and replay combat scenarios. - Visually Striking World: The game's steampunk world is beautifully crafted and a personal favourite setting, with detailed environments, imaginative character designs, and a rich color palette. - Engaging Storyline: Iron Danger offers a compelling narrative with well-developed characters and a plot that intertwines magic and technology. The story is well-paced and keeps players invested in the fate of the protagonist, Kipuna, as she navigates through a world on the brink of war.Cons:- Limited Replayability: Despite its innovative mechanics, Iron Danger's linear storyline and lack of branching paths limit its replay value.- Steep Learning Curve: The time-manipulation mechanic, while innovative, can be challenging for new players to master. - Repetitive Combat: The combat scenarios, though initially engaging, can become repetitive over time. Closing & Rating:Iron Danger is a visually captivating and mechanically innovative game that offers a fresh twist on tactical RPGs. It’s a timely adventure worth experiencing for its originality, but one that might not have you coming back for more.Rating: 7/10 gears in the clock.

_childDocuments_.review: As many have said before, this is not an RPG. It's more puzzle-like, and that's not a bad thing, if you know what you're getting into. _childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite a nice little game. The main selling point is the unusual time manipulation mechanic. It turns the game into something of an ever-evolving puzzle, every move requiring awareness of your surroundings and the potential actions of enemies (which can shift as your own moves shift). It does wear a bit thin late in the game, where one-hit kills abound and ranged attacks come from various directions. However, while failure can come frequently, it's refreshing that it can be reversed with a mere flick of the mouse wheel rather than having to load a save.Beyond the core mechanic, presentation is solid - visuals and voice acting are okay, and the music is distinctive and enjoyable.All up, a solid experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: This turn-based game offers a refreshing twist with its unique ability to maneuver not just across the battlefield, but through time itself. As a player, you're not just strategizing for the present moment, but also considering the past and future, adding layers of depth and complexity to every decision. If you're a fan of tactical games and crave something truly unique, this game will scratch the itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little turn-based (kind of - its done in heartbeats with each action taking a number of beats) strategy game - but it all works with the unique time manipulation system that's lets you rewind and forward time along you heartbeat track so that you can pick that perfect point to dodge the incoming arrows and chuck a fireball at the fuel can they're stood next too whilst your melee guy picks the time to block the swing of his enemy and then thump/stab him one. There's 4 main characters and you play Kipuna - the leading lady who is collecting magic shards that each give new powers along with 1 of the 3 companions Tipo (Blacksmith with a big hammer), Lemichen (Rogue with a Bow) or The healer who has a few spells and basic melee.The story is fairly basic but played nicely with a few Finnish lore bits thrown in for flavour.   Unfortunately the story ends in such a manner it suggests there was a DLC or Sequel planned - but i know the studio hit trouble during its second game which is now in early access with just a few of the staff doing it in there own time now which is a shame as this was a really nice start to a series of games in the same world.   Its not overly long - but will keep you occupied for a few hours and stops to combat going stale with some puzzle based levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: It's clear that this game is premised on the idea of having "perfect knowledge" of the course of a fight thanks to your time manipulation ability. The problem is that for whatever reason, whether its a flaw in the physics or the frame data or the world simulation elements or whatever (it's hard to tell), the results of any given action feel VERY inconsistent. You can be hit by attacks you were nowhere near, knockback direction often has little to do with the direction an attack is coming from, prone chance *seems* random (is it?), attack timing is very hard to read in terms of figuring out which exact beat you should block or dodge on. What should be a Superhot-like flow of combat quickly devolves into micromanaging every step by trial and error for both party members, trying to figure out what exactly even happened.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was an option on steam somewhere between a "yes" or "no" recommendation that was essentially: "would personally wait for a pretty good sale." Because though this game found an AMAZINGLY fun gameplay niche, it really doesn't feel as fleshed out as would be needed to make it something I can't stop playing. There are three main things reeeealllly holding this game back in my opinion. 1) Lack of changeable keybindings which is such a huge modern convenience that can really save frustrating default control schemes. 2) Inconvenient saving mechanics (or lack thereof)3) Such inconsistent hit boxes for attacks. This one is really tough because the core gameplay idea is fine tuning your flow of combat moves, but when maybe 1/5th of the time I'm just watching a replay of my characters weapon swing through an enemy's body without damaging them, it feels less like fighting tough enemies and more like fighting dodgy programming.The other thing I think could go a long way might be more of a me thing, but the team had such a good idea of redoing and fine-tuning combat, I really wish they would make it where the timeline (how far back in combat you could rewind) wasn't so short. I'm sure they had a reason for it's short length, but I would have a ton more fun if I could rewind a lot further back!

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite flawed but i still considered it a good game.It's clunky, badly optimised and not very hard but still quite fun so would like to see a sequel in the same style as the game ends on a cliffhanger, felt it was a few missions short as the big bad is still around.Though if they make a sequel to it, a different engine is a must for sure, it demands a lot of resources for a not overly pretty game (Seems it's made in Unity, would explain performance)You control two different characters, a mage that can throw fireballs and use crowd control spells (freezing, hinder movement, buffs etc) and either a tank or an archer depending on mission (you don't get to choose)It's main mechanic is time control, you take actions with one character then roll back time for the other to do their actions.Can at anytime move it in sections called heartbeats so if you get hurt, miss your attack or die you can undo it by rolling back time (have to on death but is commented on in story so that's nice)This makes combat quite easy but still fun, just wish you could restart combat encounters as sometimes you get stuck and have to restart the whole mission (one mission you can kill 2 trolls needed for an achievement but there's a combat encounter before that slows you down, and the troll you NEED to land the final hit on often dies as it's encounter is triggered at the same time, quite annoying but at the start of the mission so only a few minutes are lost each attempt)had it freeze once during combat, when i killed the enemies and a cutscene started, was fairly early so not much time lost.Quite often the pathing failed, when trying to pick up grenades it often refused to do so running each character to a corner of the box and just standing there.Enemies change their actions based on where your character are so can't really plan ahead as the changes you make often causes attacks to miss as the enemies no longer stand where you expected them to.If you want a better game in the same style, check out Desperados 3, Shadow tactics or Mutant Year Zero, same planning for encounters (no time manipulation except save scumming) but executed better (no performance issues, complete story) or Divinity original sins (or the others like it, but this ones a good recommendation)Time manipulation if you want more of can check out Peaky Blinders, but that is a puzzle game with no real combat.Despite the flaws i would still recommend picking it up as it wasn't game breaking (except that freeze but not much time lost due to it) and fun enough for the few hours it lasted, time a bit bloated as i left i on while doing other stuff, probably closer to 10h.

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said, this isn't so much an RPG as a linear story that's more like a strategic, turn-based, puzzler. The secondary characters generally level up their existing skills.You don't get to choose who goes on each quest, it's the main character and a secondary character that helps the story-line.At no point did I feel under-classed or unable to proceed, but I also felt challenged throughout. Though they threw in one helper in the final battle that made it pretty simple.I definitely enjoyed by 20ish hours, and only encountered one major bug where a character got stuck in a house behind a locked door and I had to restart the level.Definitely a fund game and worth picking up. Just don't think it's open world or that there are any decisions to be made. It's just a fun story with some interesting characters and tricks to figure out how to get through battles.
