_childDocuments_.review: Combat is fun, though easy. Story is flat but not the worst. Controlls are wacky first but once you get accostumed to them they are fine. And a LOT of potential that is unused.I would've liked to replay with other/more characters, Scrub through the levels Desperando-Style afterwards, more story, more insight into mechanicss (how tf does crit/backstab work?), more RPG, ....All in all a decent game. ~13h playtime. Get it on a moderate discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Successfully scratched itch for turned based save scumming. No micromanaging saves as the game eliminates the need. Rewinding time is a core mechanic.Cons and other notes: Its a short game. There isn't much in the way of choice - its a linear story. The rewind time mechanic could use some work - its tedious going back and forth between characters, rewinding to set up actions for the other. Its also annoying how things can intrusively interrupt your planning while time is in trance mode (character dialog, auto shifting in and out of 'combat' mode, etc.). Not something I would recommend to everyone - but maybe check it out if you enjoy reloading in games like Divinity or Baldur's Gate.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. Strips the Action RPG to basics. No open world, no collectables, no side-quests, no classes, no complex advancement trees, no shmup/bullet-hell gameplay, no companion romance system, no loot!?! & NO WEAPONS!!! It's crazy, but this game is so good!Just one clever time-rewind mechanic (think Braid) married to a tactical combat romp. Straightforward, familiar story. Fun, exuberant voice acting. Great art. Doesn't overstay its welcome. Took me 18.5 hrs for a completionist play-through. Easily could have finished in 12-14. One of the few games where I feel I truly underpaid for it. Would gladly have paid $15 and still felt it was a solid value. And right now it's on sale now for a dollar. Crazy. Five of five stars. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: I got this from a humble bundle I think. This is cool and I think worth a go. Story is functional, nothing stand-out. It's pretty clear that this game is a platform for the time manipulation real time tactics thing.I do wonder if it would have worked better on a grid system, both in space and time. When it works, it feels really good, but most of the time it feels a bit finicky and chaotic. I think a lot of it comes down to poor pathfinding and a bit of conflict between the on-grid issuing of commands sometimes conflicting with the smooth movement and smooth flow of time. Not bad enough to break engagement, but I would not mind seeing a more refined version of this mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Danger, developed by Action Squad Studios and released in 2020, is a unique tactical role-playing game that incorporates real-time strategy and an innovative time manipulation mechanic. Although I haven't finished the game, I will discuss some of its notable features, along with certain aspects that could use improvement.1) Unique Time Manipulation Mechanic: The most distinctive feature  its time manipulation mechanic, which allows players to rewind and fast-forward time to test out different strategies and tactics. This feature adds a layer of strategy and depth, making it a refreshing and engaging experience.2) Detailed Environments and Graphics: The game boasts rich and detailed environments that immerse players in the world The developers have done an excellent job in crafting a visually appealing universe that is a pleasure to explore.3) Engaging Storyline: follows the story of Kipuna, a village girl who gains the power to manipulate time after a tragic accident. As players progress through the game, they'll uncover more about Kipuna's past and the mysterious forces at play in the world. ( but sadly, i didn't)1)Flawed Combat Execution: Despite the innovative time manipulation mechanic, the combat execution can be frustrating at times. The AI-controlled enemies tend to run around erratically, making it difficult for the player to perform precise moves. As a result, players may find themselves constantly rewinding time to land successful attacks.2)Steep Learning Curve it can be quite challenging to master. Players may struggle to execute actions effectively, even after rewinding time repeatedly. This steep learning curve might put off some players who are looking for a more straightforward gaming experience ( like me )Iron Danger offers an intriguing concept with its time manipulation mechanic, but it is held back by some frustrating combat execution and a steep learning curve. The game could benefit from refining the AI behavior and making the time manipulation more intuitive for players. However, those who are patient enough to master its mechanics will likely find Iron Danger to be a unique and rewarding tactical RPG experience..
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr If you like small stories and have time to waste on a mediocre game, then I'd recommend. If you're looking for something more than "kinda good", then look elsewhere. The time manipulation mechanic is pretty fun at first, but gets annoying and boring after a while.The story is very barebones, childish and dull.All in all it's alright, but just not quite enough to keep me playing and use time on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say this game is a solid 6/10. I really appreciate what they tried to do with the turn-based, time manupulation element, but for me it just doesn't work. Combat becomes really tedious and repetitive. Once you know how to sequence stuff right, it's just a matter of trial and error with a stun and DOT mechanic. There's no different way to beat different enemies. You keep doing the same stuff, whether it's a soldier or a monster, an archer or a knight. For those looking for a deep and customisable turn-based RPG, look elsewhere. For those looking for a beautiful and expansive world, look elsewhere. For those looking for a story worth your while ... look elsewhere. I really wanted to give the game more credit, but it just doesn't excel in anything. The game did not made me want to play more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Iron DangerReasons to play-Amazing Unique tactical combat. Your characters move in real time, however you can edit their actions with time travel. You manage cool downs, spacing and crowd control, making you feel like a badass of the battlefield. Think of a hybrid between Divinity Original Sin, Super Hot and Into the Breach.The game is not perfect, it does get repetitive towards the end due to being a series of arenas to kill enemies. It lacks polish in some areas, and i wish the story was more fleshed out. That said, if you are looking for amazing combat this is up there.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was skeptical about the game's time travel mechanic: Wouldn't it take out any challenge if you actually could take back ALL your moves? But soon I discovered the chances that this method opened to me. Early on, you can explore your options and multiple different way to defeat enemies. But there are always new twists, always new puzzles, and with several different enemies on-screen and a limited time-frame, every victory soon becomes incredibly challenging. The characters and story are also very compelling, especially Kipuna is a heroine of surprising depth and ambivalence. Unfortunately, the developers decided for an open ending... I still recommend this game because of those former strengths, but I really hope the developers are already working on the sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good steampunk action role-playing strategy game, with an interesting time mechanic, where you can rewind time to make better choices during battle. I did enjoy it so far (im about 80% done). The good: The voice acting is amazing (especially enjoyed Topi). Time manipulation is new and interesting.Lot's of tools at your disposal. Many skills. and you can collect different explosives, and food to heal yourself. Graphics are very nice! Battles are engaging, but getting easier with each new power. The bad: FPS are locked on 30 it seems, because I can see its not smooth and I cannot change that in the settings. Game is very very linear. No exploration.The game states it's RPG, but there is barely any stuff to customize, no weapons, no armors, no levels. You can only choose new skills/spells after you complete a level and that's it.All that being said, I do recommend getting it. Support the devs and they might create a big RPG in the future (Like Torchlight) hehehe who knows ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Basically, a much simpler and shorter Divinity: Original Sin, but combined with time manipulation mechanics. It's definitely not like that of Prince of Persia. Here, you have a 7-second window of opportunity inside of which you can move the slider as you wish and adjust your actions based on enemies'.The only flaw is that enemies are too similar : game would be really boring if not for multiple skills and time reversal.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty sure the game is good; I just could not like it.The whole time gimmick is interesting but it is too much busy work to be honest; the combat and overall movements do not feel fluid so it is more of a turn based experience than a more modern action strategy game. The story is OK, graphics are fine and overall it seems a nice game but I really don't like it overall, and I am glad I just paid 2 dollars for it.You may like it but if you are looking for something like Baldurs Gate or similar games, this game is not like that for sure
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: I love everything about this game, except for its lack of save options. When I can't finish a level, or the game crashes mid way through a level, or - god forbid - after you've finished a level, I lose all that progress. This has happened to me a bunch of times. _childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: You are in search for game that does thing differently? Well, Iron Danger does thing differently.Will you like it?If you like non conventional game yes.If you like game with a simple, smooth, action packed gameplay or complex strategy, then you may not like it.This game is a turn based strategy game disguised as an rts.The main mechanic is a time based one. Not revolutionary but the whole game revolves around it, and it's really polished and enjoiable, once you get the hang of it.The difficulty curve is really smooth and gradual, starting with very few, the game continuosly adds more tools and enemy to play with.I didn't find the game hard. Still there must be some issue if only 50% of the player managed to reach the healer (you can do this in like less than an hour) and only 6% managed to finish the game.The story is simple, and that's perfect for the lenght of the game, and the voiceover is simply gorgeous.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, loved the fighting mechanics. To be fair, it did take a good 3 - 4 hours in order to  use them smoothly - before that I felt clunky as ♥♥♥♥. Excellent music, adept voice acting, okay characters. Frame rate somewhat unstable, especially in larger areas / battles  always dropped below 60, quite often in the 30 - 45 area. Multiple bugs: trying to pick up grenades was a pain in the ass too often (didn't work, same issue many times during different missions with different objects - didn't make the fights too difficult, though) + had to restart a few missions due to a bug preventing me from going forward. Usually would've dropped a game with a problem like this, gameplay was intriguing enough to keep me going.  Linear as it is defined in the dictionary, but there's way too much open world games out there anyway for my taste. Gameplay loop, at least for me, worked. Still, couldn't blame someone for calling this repetitive. The new skills and larger battles kept the experience fresh.Waiting for the obvious sequel ... maybe one day.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting core mechanic: Fighting is in real time but it pauses every time you want to issue an order to a character and you can freely rewind and take back old decisions. Leads to a combination of little dodges and sneaky strikes in the window of opportunity you'd associated with a real time game and the sort of tactical thought you'd get in a turn based game.The difficulty curve is really wonky, it hits its sweet spot right near the start of the game and then gets consistently easier until the closing credits. The enemies get a bit more powerful, but you get a lot more powerful. There's no limit to how often you rewind, only how far, so it's tough for things to have any weight. Early on it felt like there were trade offs along the lines of "Is it worth keeping this outcome where I win getting hit once or should I rewind in case there's a hard fight later and every hp matters?" but as you go through the game you'll get an infinite use healing ability that makes that irrelevant. And learn that there's never a tough fight, even the boss battles aren't really much trouble. Every fight takes place in a massive environment that offers the full range of maneuver so even if you weren't given so many good abilities there's never one off cooldown you can never paint yourself into a corner.Progression works neatly, you pick a new power (on an upgrade to an existing one) at the end of each level. Most of these feel meaty, there's not much "10% more damage" and quite a lot of "Massive improvement." This combination of making level ups feel like they matter and making xp farming unecessary is nice. If there'd been an xp bar I'd probably have felt obliged to hunt down every enemy before ending a level, but I wouldn't have enjoyed it.The environments are beautiful but exploration is pointless. The only things to find are consumable items and none of the fights are hard enough to justify using a consumable item. I stopped bothering to pick them up about a third of the way into the game once I realised I wasn't using them, by halfway I stopped exploring once it became apparent it'd never be rewarded. Some sort of equipment, even if it was a simple each character can equip one charm and they do one thing would've put some mechanical emphasis on exploration.The story is extremely generic and doesn't end in a satisfying way. We're not really here for the story, but there was room to do more with it. The most unique thing they've got to talk about is the subjective experience of dying and seeing friends die over and over while they experience only the timeline in which it all goes great, there are a few neat lines about this but the game doesn't get into it deeply. The voice acting seemed solid enough to me. It's not bad, it's just got nothing to recommend it either.Overall the game is a mix of good and bad points, but if you like games it's worth the price of admission just to get to try out something new :)
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: What I liked about this shorter story, was the atmosphere, polished world building and models, the music / both combat, menu and environmental. Well done on those. The tactics based movement took some time to get used to and sometimes I had to say out loud "why are you moving, please stop!". I liked that the player was given options to choose how they wish to solve the puzzle and all in all a solid experience. A nice puzzle to wonder around.What I wouldve liked to have been worked on, were some of the graphical bugs Ive noticed. At times the water during the sea voyage or on maps was glitching and I saw the patterns. It was not an issue of game enjoyment as a player I have choice. but at times it felt Ive missed something or went ahead of a dialogue by choosing another route. During the death bird level, the player should not see more than once the "What is that thing. Three times was more than enough. Well done all in all. A lovely weekend getaway.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: It's not without its faults but is ultimately a pretty good time. I played 2/3s of the game on hard before bugs halted progress. Checkpoints/saves are ONLY at the start of the level so restart, slog back to where I was, same problem, ♥♥♥♥. Switch to normal and you'll feel like a god even though you'll still die in 1 or 2 hits.Combat is more or less an introduction to tool assisted speedrunning. Once you get the hang of it though, you'll wish every other game had a "please go back 2 seconds k thx" button.Story is fine enough. Protag is and side characters are just short of interesting. Maybe if there was more dialog options or something.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: The principal gimmick of this game is the timeline based combat - you control two characters and can reverse time by up to ten 'time units', allowing you to perfectly rewind time and avoid death and get kills. This is a fun gimmick but ultimately turns into basically turbo-save-scumming your way through every single encounter. The end of level screen shows you how much 'real' time passed versus elapsed non-rewound time as though to challenge you to try to beat the game without rewinding too much, but the encounter difficulty without the timeline is cranked super high, with lots of one hit kill deaths and unpredictable enemy spawns.I'm still recommending it because I had fun playing it, but there's a certain variety of player that enjoys save-scumming their way to 'perfect' play and other players that don't, and this game offers pretty much nothing for the second variety of player, since outside that mechanic there's a lot of clunky hitboxes and annoying enemies. The game's story is alright and teases a sequel, but I'm not sure if that sequel will ever see the light of day.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting, though niche, fantasy combat game, with a unique timeline editor feature where you can move forwards and backwards through time to make your characters efficient - or at least survive many supposedly overwhelming encounters.This game is perfect for people who play XCOM and reload whenever they make any kind of wrong move or an attack unexpectedly misses.And people who play the games where you carefully plan out 5 seconds of game in chunks like Laser SquadConsRuns pretty bad for what it isCamera locked for elevation and zoom. There's some translucency when the camera is behind objects, but things get lost in dense melees or piles of big bodiesIf you're expecting a real time game you're going to be disappointed. This is not a real time strategy. And the people who think they should have dumped their core mechanic in favour of a flavourless RTS completely missed the point of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: This game is inspired quite heavily by Divinity: Original Sin and similar titles, but has enough unique mechanics behind it to become its own thing. The game is well worth a play if you are a fan of the Action-CRPG genre.STORYThe story revolves around a young girl (Kipuna) being granted limited time-travel powers by a mysterious deity. She is soon tasked with gathering the other Shards of power, and meets some interesting characters along the way. Besides the gathering of the shards, the story revolves around Kipuna coming to terms with her power and being torn between what to do with it (if anything) as she is pulled in all directions by her companions. The story is pretty good but lacks polish - it also ends abruptly at the end of Act 2 in the story arc, which is very disappointing. I've seen other reviews say the ending is rushed and comes out of nowhere - but there honestly isn't an ending. The game just stops right when you'd expect Act 3 to begin.GAMEPLAYThe game features a unique timeline mechanic that allows you to go forward and backward along the timeline to perfect your strategy, avoid being hit and guarantee hits against enemies. There is very little RNG in the game which is great for a strategy game like this. The rewind mechanic is basically Savescum: The Game which makes for some very interesting (if a little easy) gameplay. Player characters can generally only take 1-3 hits before dying so it becomes very important to use the timeline to its full extent. The most fun way to play this is to try not to be hit at all!GRAPHICSWhile the graphics aren't the greatest in the genre, the art style is fantastic and will likely hold up for many years to come. When in gameplay, I was always able to tell what was what and some of the fights look pretty flashy. Very nice.MUSICThe music is pretty great, I had my head beating along to some of the action tracks, however they are a little forgettable. The music that plays during the intermissions on the boat in particular is quite moving. General sound effects are very competent but again nothing stands out.BUGSI encountered no bugs while playing the game aside from a small audio error, nothing to stop my enjoyment of the game.OVERALLIron Danger is a great little game that unfortunately lacks the polish to be truly great. I can only assume that they ran out of time and resources near the end. I hope that they are able to take the foundations they built up with this game and make something truly excellent with the sequel. Until then, this game is well worth a look if you are a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Worth $5 on sale, otherwise I wouldn't bother. Mechanics are annoying, you have to micromanage multiple characters and constantly rewind time. I feel like this should have been a turn based game rather than this semi real time mess. The story is a while another issue. The main character is the most whiny, annoying brat I have ever had the displeasure to play with. You don't make any real choices in the game and everything is set on very solid rails, overall its kind of a drag. Divinity original sin has similar mechanics that are thought out 10x better, the story is a few levels above this and it doesn't cost much more.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Well, i really loved playing this game, although it is a bit rough on the edges, but... Let's rewind:Well, I really loved playing this game. The characters are enjoyable and well designed (IMO). The graphics are very nice and the music is great. Also, this game comes with the perfect quicksave/quickload mechanics. This game mechanic is the major selling point of it, and if you don't like it, you should rather stay away.+ Graphics, music, character design+++ Game mechanics are fun. (Be sure to use shift and ctrl hotkeys for Movement and attack timing)+ Characters abilities feel very unique. (Except the Healer, she is very underpowered)+++ Many ways to encounter a fight. use the environment, use different skills,....o The story is interesting but... spoiler ahead: ---- Only two characters will be playable during any specific mission: Kipuna and one of the others. I'd wished to fight with all of them at the same time. Or let me at least choose my companion.-- The healer is to weak and has no unique skills. _childDocuments_.review: Simple enough story to follow, the voice acting is good and the music is well done, but the most interesting part and the biggest selling point of the game is the combat system. Time manipulation is a unique concept and interesting way of fighting, its easy enough to learn yet can be challenging if you don't pay attention to your characters position and the environment.If i had to say anything bad, there were times i couldn't pick up grenades from supply boxes or other items that are scatters around the map for some reason, using melee is punishing for the most part and the game did soft lock me once or twice forcing me to re-play entire areas.over all i would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: My take is that Iron Danger is one of the most honest computer roleplaying games out there. The time rewinding mechanic is more interesting than constantly reloading a difficult fight and the story, such as it is, focuses on the basics. I feel that Iron Danger is worth it, especially discounted.However, the game certainly isn't perfect. The characters feel a bit flat, having very little interaction with each other and the world outside. While the voice actors give a good performance, the writing is lagging behind. For a finn such as myself, the Kalevala-inspired setting is fun to experience, but apart from some references and the song measure there isn't much to grasp. Even without more extensive roleplaying elements I would have preferred to have the world a bit more fleshed out.The game also reeks of strange technical solutions and budgetary issues, as some dialogue-heavy parts are handled with a short level, which introduces a lot of loading. Not a dealbreaker, just very, very weird. The story doesn't also end properly and is lacking the Act III.But all in all, I didn't hate the time with this one. The time rewind mechanic managed to carry it through.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent game, quite generic, lacking interesting findouts and there is nothing that would expand lore. This so called innovative fight system makes the game very easy, I would say it is not very well thought, but at least it makes gameplay very smooth. It's easy to play and forgettable title, not much good content but also doesn't have many flaws or big letdowns.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: ☑️Very unique concept for an RPG.☑️Story is interesting.☑️Characters have personality.☑️Redo your mistakes, as much as you want.☑️Time manipulation puzzles is nice.❌The game can be a little bit laggy / motion blur at times.I went into this game expecting something on the lines of Divinity Original Sin II style of content. It's not what I was expecting. The ability to redo your mistakes and play perfectly, even if you lose all of your characters is refreshing for those that want to simply, play the game without any fear of losing. Some fights can be really challenging but you quickly grasp onto how to fight properly. Puzzles in this game utilize time manipulation, which is really nice to complete. It may be looking into the future or looking into the past to understand them fully, but it just feels good. It's definitely something you need to sit down with for a bit to let it sink in a little, but you get used to this type of game play quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: The big thing I have to say about the game is that it took save scummin to the next level and that's only a compliment from me. Due to the time rewind function, you could essentially try a different action without having to load an autosave. That sht was great and I would love to see more of that!!That said, this game was super slow just due to the nature of how the mechanics work. Chapters really felt like a grind sometimes. Overall tho it was a good time, you could get pretty creative with how you went about the combat and the story was kinda interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Pro-The xp and loot free game makes you act like real heroes. You don't fight everybody, only those you must. This change of attitude was cool because of the variety.-Variety in missions-Nice graphics-MusicCon-Awful controls. Buy it only If you have patience.-Keys cannot be changed to make it more tolerable.-No zoom, fixed camera distance. Sometimes enemies aren't on the screen when a battle begins. It's harder to navigate.-Only ~30% of the grenade boxes work.-No spellbook/help to reread the effects of spells later.-DialogsRating: 75%A little encouragement: the story will be better in mid and late game.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Danger is a very unique game, largely due to the time-manipulating aspect. Missed an attack? Swung your axe too early? Want to complete the stage without taking any damage? Just roll back the timeline to redo that segment - I am sure you can learn from Dr. Strange to find that one perfect timeline that you're happy with.Recommend getting the game if there are discounts (I bought it at 80% off), and I can say that it is worth every dollar! I won't roll back this timeline for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: This game is well done with a unique mechanic of being able to roll back time when you die or really whenever you want.  This is both good and bad.  As they say perfection is the enemy of good and I sometimes found myself rewinding whenever I took any damage but really didn't need to.  This makes all the levels a lot longer than they actually are.  However, you are grossly outnumbered so you really need this mechanic to survive the whole level.  Other than this mechanic, the gameplay isnt particularly exciting.  The game is level based and each level is fairly small.  The story is ok but nothing special and you cant do anything to influence it and ends abruptly before it really should.  Overall the game is somewhat short but I only paid $4 for it so can't complain.  I didn't notice any bugs other than sometimes it just wont let you pick up a consumable even though it is right in front of you.  Other than consumables, there is no loot to find or stuff to upgrade or any crafting at all.  The only character progression is getting to pick a new skill after each level.  I don't feel like it has any replayability.  Overall, I liked it and would probably buy a sequel to it if it ever comes out.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game for "cultural touch", the finnish devs have obviously used some of their cultural heritage to create an interesting background. The game mechanics are appealing, the concept of creating sequences of actions that can be "rewound" if anything drastic happens down the timeline beats having to save and reload often, as in many other games. And I really enjoyed the voice acting, the actors have put a lot of effort into creating interesting characters.On the con side, I find the UI unwieldy. The graphics are, well, o.k., if one likes a bright and colourful cartoon-like design, that, in my opinion, does not fit to the grim background. Some combat skills are rather useless (for instance, the coup-de-grace, that theoretically allows one to finish off a prone enemy, but you never seem to be able to reach him before he gets up again).The maps are mostly rather small and the mission design is quite linear, with little variation possible. I have now finished the game twice in less than 60 hours, once on normal and once on hard (although I'm sure many of the younger gamers can do it in half that time), and now I'm deinstalling it because there is no more replayability value (though the game hints at additional content to be published later . . .).So, I'm giving this game the thumbs-up, but barely.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: A short fun game where you control 2 characters to annihilate well basically an army and some monsters on the way. At first it may feel crazy when you're surrounded and just have to dance around, dodging and blocking all the attacks not having a half-second to hit back but then you begin to grasp it and start to lure single enemies back a little to not fight the full camp at once, use environment and traps to either finish off a group of enemies or some tough one with a lot of hit points. Towards the end of the game your main character is one-man army with all kinds of spells to devastate your enemies. Throw fireball, cast madness, root them in place, refresh cooldowns and do all of that again. After getting fifth shard I only used Kipuna to fight while another character was sitting in nearby bushes sometimes shouting some comments pretending they're doing some job (looking at you Lemichen).The story has a few strange moments that feel like there should've been something else that just didn't make it into the game in the end.Skill system is rather boring and despite having a choice of what skill to improve, I couldn't see a reason to upgrade anything but damage sources. Half of the skills from shards are just there and you try them a few times just to see what they do or try again for fun but never really use in a heat of battle. Wouldn't call it an RPG tho.Overall it's quite fun but I don't see much replayability here.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's a solid game. Not the same tier as games from big publishers, but It has its moments.   The gameplay is the strongest aspect of this game. This game finally gave me the real strategy of fighting that games like Divinity or Pillars failed to deliver. Characters are fragile and can't just stand in one place and DPS. The flow is chaotic and dodging a bullet as one character can lead to a second hero's death. At first, I was annoyed that Kipuna is a backline hero and the other one is actually fighting, but it forces you to take risks which I actually started to enjoy within the story progression. I wish maps could have more interactive elements, and there would be a bigger variety of enemies because we only get a handful of types. The icons are very small, and I was frustrated that the controlled character proceeds to walk into a random spot when I wanted to choose a skill to use. There is a pause and rewind mechanic that lets you redo the choice but it is irritating the chaos that sometimes isn't your fault.   The story is simple and flat, guess it's because of the limited tools the studio had. The protagonist is actually a solid character, a girl that is used by different people that grows from her shyness to being a cold leader that can stand her own is a development done right. We have no control over her decisions and for me it works well because I can witness how she bears with the situation. Lemichen's character is a different case: as the game goes he becomes more and more one dimensional and boring. NPCs are underdeveloped and they leave no impact. There are some story bits here and there, but they build nothing in my opinion. Dialogues on screen are often not visible (they are text only), and there is no indication that some character is currently speaking so you might loose it as there is no dialogue history. As a player, I relied solely on Kipuna's point of view to understand what is going on on the plot because other sources of storytelling are bland and boring. The ending is... mostly okayish? It's a cliffhanger, but we did what we had to do and the protagonist's decision was solid and logical.   Graphics set a cartoonish style that works really well with the overall atmosphere. Sometimes visuals are great (especially ruins), sometimes they look as stereotypical for fantasy as possible. This game didn't try to be innovative in this field but delivered proper material.   Music in this game is wonderful and gives you a vibe of the whimsical feeling of a fairy tale that boosts the current situation.    I got it from sale and I'm not sure if a full price is adequate, but if you grab it at 50-75% discount it's highly recommended just to try the mechanics of fighting.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay - 8.5/10Visuals - 7.5/10Sound/Music - 10/10Voice Acting - 8/10Controls/Responsiveness - 6.5/10Story - 6.5/10Performance/Optimization - 3/10I really enjoyed this game. The controls and combat reminds me of Pillars of Eternity, while the time manipulation mechanic gives the game a prince of persia / XCOM vibe. The game requires pin point strategy to avoid being rekt by unfair enemy encounters. You only have around 5 seconds of rewind time, and this time is split up into half second steps. So walking a few meters might take 3-5 steps to complete, while a powerful spell will take you 2 steps. A whole lot of enemy ambushing will happen in between the steps, as each step is treated like a turn in a turn based strategy game.I like that unlike Pillars of Eternity and many other modern day CRPGs, space is extremely important in combat encounters. The game doesn't use a whole lot of RNG like most CRPGs, but instead uses colliders to implement damage and spell multipliers. So you can easily avoid an attack by simply moving away, or use the handy dodge ability to quickly move out of the way.The game is very linear, so I like to think of this game as a real time strategy game, rather than a CRPG. Although if you played Pillars of Eternity, the controls are very similar. The abilities in this game are vast and can completely change the flow of combat. You'll collect shards to regain power, and gain new abilities, such as damage, healing, and enemy manipulation spells. The ability to turn enemies against each other with the enrage ability is truely amazing and a delight to see in action.I'll also say the soundtrack in this game is incredible. A perfect mix of vocals, strings, electric guitars and drums really sets the mood for this strange blend of medieval fantasy and steam punk hell. The layout for each dungeon you must invade to gain your precious shards gets very predictable after awhile; with a similar go to this dungeon, light up the beacons, kill enemies, get shard, learn new ability, get out of dungeon, escape island, rinse and repeat. Although many of the places are simply beautiful, such as the big harbor town and the gorgeous forest with vegetation almost having a wax painting sort of look.You also gain the ability to use a mech (automation) in this game. You can use the mech to destroy barriers and shoot down a horde of enemies, which never gets old.The controls for this game isn't bad, but sometimes I'll command my character to go somewhere, and they'll run straight into a fire that kills them instantly. So micromanaging my five seconds of control is extremely important, as one wrong series of turns can turn into game over really fast.Only really annoying bug I encountered is a few times, I'll get ready to complete the mission by pressing the sail or exit UI button as the mission slowly fades. Except I had two instances where the UI buttons never popped up after I completed everything in the quest, so I had to restart the level. Oh I forgot to mention there's no saving during levels (you get an autosave once after every level), and level length is highly variable, with some levels lasting less than 30 seconds, while others lasted me over 25 minutes. The major issue with this game is performance. I have an i5 4670k paired with a gtx 1070, and boy does this game chug at a smooth 40 frames per second in scenes with small enemy encounters in a relatively small environment. This game looks pretty, but I'm able to get a smooth 60 fps on very high settings in XCOM 2 and Valkyria Chronicles 4, both of which are leagues better looking than this game. Pillars of Eternity 2 has very similar performance issues on pc.It's worth noting that I discussed the performance issues on the steam forums, and the devs stated they have minimal resources and can't polish the game right now.I got the game on humble choice and thought it was well worth my $$$. But I'd highly recommend to buy this on a very deep sale, don't buy this full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very special one. (Disclaimer: I got the game via Humble Choice)The core of this game is the time rewind mechanic, which basically takes away the first impression of an action rpg and gets more into puzzle territory. Most of the fights you can manipulate the enemies just right to not even get hit once. Though it might be by trial and error most of the time, it still feels like you are a master tactician. But my biggest problem with this game: It really doesn't feel polished. Meaning that there are a few major and a lot of smaller bugs.The most noticeable bug I had was right in the tutorial where the button to end it was missing. Which caused me to wander around wondering what I'm doing wrong, since I didn't even know it was missing. After a short search it seemed like that bug is in there for a while already. After replaying the mission, the button showed up so I could finish it. I didn't have anything quite as gamebreaking after that though.Buuuut, I had quite a handful smaller glitches, like the character being talked to, but instead of stopping, they still walk to the initial destination (like instead of staying in the boat, just walking offscreen on the pier and closing the door behind them). Or the fact that sometimes dialog gets triggered in the middle of combat. Those just look/feel silly, but (as far as I could tell) didn't break anything.Those small little errors certainly made the game feel worse than it actually is.**Kinda Story spoiler (just for the structure near the end):**The voice acting is stellar though, I really liked the whole performance.All in all I would recommend playing the demo first to see if you like the core gameplay. I have enjoyed the whole experience, but with all that jank I don't know if I would pay full price (30€ currently) for it.  -  But the game is worth it for the special twist with the time control function by itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a tactical RTS with pausing and time reversal mechanics. The time reversal essentially means the combat system has incorporated savescumming as a core mechanic, which is truly unique. The closest relative I can think of is Prince of Persia: Sands of Time, but there it was more of a gimmick, while here it's central to the gameplay.To illustrate, in more tactical games you're supposed to carefully position your heroes, prepare defensive abilities and then advance, possibly taking a few hits in the process but tanking them out as planned. If something goes wrong you're supposed to tough it out or start over, and definitely not supposed to load a save from a bit earlier and do things a bit differently.In this game, you'll often get instakilled by a long-range ballista bolt, only to go back a second and step sideways at just the right moment, performing a Matrix-style dodge minus the theatrics. This gets more complex when taking on multiple strong opponents at once, requiring complex combination of preventative knockdowns, dodges and blocks to prevent them from hitting you. And you definitely don't want them to hit you - this is not the kind of game where you can take several hits and tank it out.Game is a bit on the short side and offers no significant replayability but overall it's decent amount of very enjoyable content.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game overall, did not expect to like it as much, but the combat system is very enjoyable. It is true that it feels more like a puzzle than a fighting game, which has its benefits. While there is no manual saving, the levels are conveniently organized and usually take from 15 to 40 minutes to complete. You play two characters at a time, and your second character changes to another from time to time, requiring you to adapt and constantly think of new techniques to use. The main character's features are upgraded in bits, and you get pushed to practice killing foes using only them as soon as you upgrade, which really encouraged me to utilize the majority of my arsenal. The final level was a bit too easy for me, I expected more of a challenge or a further battle after it, but oh well. All in all, this was a nice experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The 11 hours I played were more than sufficient to complete this game, and I doubt it has significant replay value now. If either of those put you off, stop reading.This is a brilliant game. A truly excellent game. It is not a very good RPG, not a good action game, and it is not really a strategy game. This is a Puzzle Game.What I mean by that is that the core gameplay loop is dealing with known information, and experimenting to form a solution. Every single combat is, in at least some way, solveable; it can be "beaten" in an optimal path. The game's engine makes that path fun to engage with and the mechanic is somewhat unique. I've seen people complaining "every battle is easy if you just rewind time in the right way" and that's like complaining that Rubix Cubes are easy if you put all the colours on the same side. The loop is rewarding. At the end, the ability to make foes attack each other and to heal up after combat make the puzzle a little less difficult and a little less rewarding to complete *well* but it's otherwise a really solid experience.I got this game from Humble Choice, but if I saw the sequel I would buy it full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Brief: An entertaining combat system, good music, and a decent ride.  Fairly short (I have 3-4 hours of idling, so beating it in about 12 hours is likely).  A little longer: I liked this one.  The rewind/fast forward mechanic makes it feel more like a puzzle game than a pure strategy RPG, in a good way.  You can also easily experiment without feeling punished for it, which is nice.  Neat ways of setting up combos and controlling the battlefield.  Storyline is adequate.  Characters are fine.  Solid voice acting.Worth a play if you like the concept and fantasy/steampunk settings.Complaints - A lack of mid-mission saving.  The missions aren't very long and I NEVER had to restart one, but some are over half an hour long and you can't save in them.  That's why I had so much idle time, I had some times where I wasn't willing to start over so I left it paused while I got interrupted by other things.  There's some issues in the writing, which is strange for how light the story is, like some throw away lines implying a sub plot that go nowhere.  Enemies and allies clip through each other, and this can cause targeting issues.  The camera angle is too severe and it makes navigating annoying.  Oh, and the game runs quite poorly.  I had low frame rates at times with a 1070 and an i7.  So some serious issues, but they didn't stop me from enjoying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is a neat little gem of a game. I got my copy through Humble Bundle subscription.This game frankly deserves more attention and have enjoyed it thoroughly! It has a unique world and setting that has its own identify and isn't some copy and pasted rehash of another fantasy setting. There aren't a whole lot of exploration elements for you to figure out the way of the game's world, but it does a good job at showing what the game's setting is through its story elements that are intermingled in your story progression. The game play itself is interesting to say the least. Instead of a timing based hack and slash like many games in its genre, it's more of a turn based strategy set up in real time. You manipulate combat with use of the time rewind mechanics by controlling two characters. One is primarily a melee combatant while the other is a mage. The system feels clunky at first, but once you get used to it, it's quite enjoyable. All of your actions occur in "Heartbeats," so you essentially go through combat frame by frame. Movement, attacks, defense, item and environment interactions etc. can all be manipulated with the time rewind mechanics. Your characters are very vulnerable and by no means should take damage if at all possible. One good strike is enough to kill your character(s) you control. If you make a mistake in combat that result in a wound or death, you can rewind those actions up to a certain point and change the outcome of the engagement. Failed to change a combat result? Rewind and have your characters retreat to a better position! Mistimed a block that killed your character? You can fix that! Want to see if an environment interaction changes the outcome of a fight or not? Experiment with it until you've figured it out!This game does not hold your hand despite the chance to "redo" your actions. If you've screwed up to the point your time manipulation can't fix your mistakes, you need to restart the level you're on. You get a bare bones tutorial on how to use the mechanics of the game, then you're fending for yourself. You need to figure out how to use the tools available to you to succeed. It's not a super harsh learning curve, but it's very fair. I highly recommend giving this title a shot!

It plays a lot like Divinity Original Sin, for example, so brain power is your strongest weapon.The voice acting is incredibly good, especially for an indie game of this size. When some building or obstacle is in the way, its solved with a kind of small X-ray bubble that does not make sense in this kind of tactics game- Mediocre cumbersome User Interface- AI that for some reason changes it's action depending on who you currently control (so if you rewind time to the moment of an enemies attack and change your selected character , he will attack him instead)- wastes your time with slow walking in towns where there is nothing to explore, many things that are in the game feel like unfinished stuff that just stayed as is, even without any purpose - Bad annoying dialogue system- Disjointed game, feels like a puzzle of various elements that were put together without any cooperation- Feels unfinished , like they just got it to the minimum playable state- Ad in the main menu that returns even if you close it the next time you open the game - Feels that they tried to do to much in this game and ended up with lots of mediocre or disjointed components + tries to do its own thing so kind of relatively original in its mechanics (but fail at the execution)+ nice that there are voices for the dialogues and the actors feel competent )but the lines themselves feel disjointed from the things that happen in the game)+ fish in game menu react to your clicks+ nice music ( though it also feels sometime disjointed from the game )

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game in Humble Choice and I really enjoyed it. It was not exactly challenging (on normal difficulty) but that rewind time feature and controlling two characters simultaneously was something new for me. It felt incredibly satisfying finishing every fight with full health. I missed the ability to watch the entire fight in one go afterwards like in BSG Deadlock.It took me about 14 hours to complete. If you don't explore all corners of the maps and don't care about how you end your fights as long as you win, you can probably finish it faster. The game is completely linear and there are no choices to make (except one regarding an achievement). Not allowing to make moral choices was a missed opportunity. There are no cutscenes except for the ending (and I would call that one only technically a cutscene). The story is told with text in Kipuna's journal, fully voiced dialogue between the main cast and some text remarks while you travel the individual maps.What left me a confused is the ending. It somehow feels like the ending of Trine 3. It ends but it feels like there should be more. Maybe there will be another game someday to continue the story.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Fun game. I normally play games on easy to normal difficulties, but this one was so perfectly suited to how I like playing games that I was able to set it to hard and still enjoy it. You're able to turn back time up to 12 combat turns, so if you don't feel like getting hit, you can literally just roll back 1-2 moves and make your character sidestep before attacking. My only complaints are that the camera is clunky and I never got used to the controls feeling backwards. (You have to left-click to move, where literally every other top-down RPG in existence uses right-click, for example.) Also, the ending was bad. Baaaad. Like, it wasn't even 'open-ended game left for a sequel' bad, it just ended before the final chapter. Mild spoilers, you have to spend the game collecting crystal shards. then once you collect the last one, there's a dramatic conversation between the protagonists about how they're going in for the final big fight in enemy territory, and as the boat sails towards an ominous looking keep... the credits roll. That's it? That's.... not cool. I HATE bad endings. I'm labelling this as 'yes, I recommend' because it was a fun game and an excellent concept, but my whole 40 hour experience has been tainted by that absolutely trash ending. Ugh.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game, but with its fair share of flaws. The combat is great, graphics & sound are fine too. The story is really shallow (stuff just happens without any exposition; in some games there's too much exposition, but Iron Danger has next to none; ), lack of key RPG elements like meaningful character building or progression (you get to choose an ability to upgrade after some levels, that's it) & no real insentive to replay the game (no side content, linear level-based structure, previously mentioned lack of character building).
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: I love time mechanics as a general and think that they make interesting games every time when done well, fortunately for Iron Danger this is very much one of those times, as time is a major mechanic of the game, rewinding and micro managing each part to optimize. Unlike some RPG where you are the chosen one and the world is your's and nothing else matters, you are still weak, vulnerable, and subordinate to a point. This makes combat to where you need to be careful and optimize taking little or no damage and saving resources. I fell in love when I met the developers and played their demo at PAX and it held up exceedingly well. Great first entry for Action Squad Studios and I look forward to the future that you bring.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let’s talk what this game is not. It’s not an RPG (by my definition), you are neither free nor can you explore, build your own character, choose between discussion option and so on. With that out of the way: let’s talk what this game really is. It is a linear 3D puzzle Adventure. I don’t mean Point & Klick adventure - I mean the kind adventure that an Assassins Creed is. So, you have absolutely no impact on the story (except you die). I like to compare it to the Dwarves which was a great game developed by Kingart games. Its just plain, top down fighting.But what makes it interesting then? Of course, the fights. The unique Time mechanic is very intuitive and after practicing for a bit, it just feels natural. The fact that you are constantly faced with very strong enemies makes it very puzzly because you just have to play the time forwards and backwards all the time to find exactly the right choreography. Unfortunately later in game the enemy got a litte bit repetitive. Also, the hardness of the levels was a little bit too low for me (on normal) but of course normal is not as hard as hard.Generally speaking, it’s a great game and I do not regret having it bought. If roughly 14 hours of play time worth 29.99 €? Meh probably not but this is up to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: The main gameplay mechanic (rewinding your actions) is very enjoyable, as is the art and the music. The story is nothing special, but okay. Characters are endearing.Overall difficulty is okay, a bit on the easy side, but makes the game enjoyable nonetheless. I was only disappointed in the final fight: I found it way too easy, which is kind of a let down. Using the special mechanic provided there (not saying more to avoid spoilers), I did not even have to use any of my abilities, and barely had to rewind time... Added to the fact I found the shortcut in the map right before and had almost no trouble there, it made the end very anticlimactic.Also, maybe I did not get it, but stealth seemed very hard to use and not really useful...Just a detail I enjoyed immensely: Saunas heal you. Just like IRL. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Danger is a tactical combat game with a UNIQUE TIME MANIPULATION MECHANIC(This is pretty much the core mechanic which makes this game so stand out from other turn based game). So Essentially many of you might be wondering If the game worth 10$ price tag. Well it is perspective If you are a pc user and do not own any consoles or you love turn based mechanic games like Divinity Original Sin Series or Tactics Ogre Knights of Lodis and you got nothing else to play during this Quarantine period then yes this game is worth the 10$ price tag. If you like turn based mechanics i suggest you look at some gameplay videos before splurging and if you are new to turn based mechanics this game might not be for you.With that out of the way a bit regarding the game.The game has a unique turn based mechanic(Look up some iron danger gameplay videos). It has a average level design. A slightly likeable protagonist and a average storyline. The level art and background music on the other hand are pretty good for a indie game. The game cannot be termed as a modern RPG due to it lacking many of the modern RPG mechanics. Some of the most basic mechanics like equipment or skill tree are missing. While it does have skill combos the combinations which can be availed with it are limited to 10 or maybe less. The game is capable of keeping you engaged for hours while it is not exceptional when compared to other games it is a decent one for a indie studio. Overall it is a above average game with a very unique core gameplay mechanic. 5.5 - 6 / 10

It feels poorly optimzied and doesn't run well.This is a middle of the road recommendation. The story is alright, the voice acting is of consistent quality (which is good). The gameplay itself works as advertised. This isn't as impressive as Achron, but then, nothing is. _childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:The gameplay is truly exceptional. Having the ability to control time (to a certain extent) reminds me of the days of Prince of Persia and the Sands of Time. Only here, it is not just an "oh ♥♥♥♥" button/resource but an integral part of gameplay.The game truly begins when you start controlling more than 1 character at a time. This leads to a shocking amount of depth as you try to keep your characters alive while maximizing your "heartbeats" to perform the best possible actions at any given time. The game rewards planning ahead while letting you work with a tiny bit of foresight. Push the foresight too far and you lose the ability to wind back to an earlier time.Enemies in this game are unforgivably tough and for good reason. If you are good at it, you could go through the entire game taking no damage yet for every single misstep, you begin to feel as if your chance at victory slowly slips away.The only gripe I have with this game now is that there is no manual save option. The game is saved whenever you complete/start a chapter with no ability to save in between chapters. This has been a problem quite a few times when I had to put the game down for other commitments but either had to leave the game running or just forfeit my current chapter progress as a whole.Characters/Story:The cast of characters are quirky and unique enough that none of them feel too similar to one another. The story and their relationships are abit flimsy and at times feel forced. Voice acting is generally passable with a few exceptional performances while others felt abit flat at delivering certain lines.Visual Design:The visuals are average but work well enough for the game. The game's camera has some issues with certain areas where the player is shown a completely black screen at certain angles but is certainly not game-breaking.A minor nitpick is that certain chapters last mere seconds and would have been better conveyed as cutscenes.Overall Rating:8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun game. The story is compelling, the combat is unique, and the developers leave you to experiment and tinker with finding neat ways to combine skills in order to make lethal combinations or interact with the environment in ways to tip the scales in your favor.Now, with that said I had the wonderful opportunity to alpha, beta, and play test this game before release. i'm extremely proud of what Action Squad have managed to do and I can't wait to see what they come out with next.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! The time rewind mechanics are super fun and make this game truly unique, turning what appears at first glance to be an RPG into a wacky puzzle game of sorts. You can rewind and fast forward to your heart's content and try different solutions in a battle as many times as you wish. Usually the more creative ways offer better results, and I love that in any game. What first feels like a hopeless fight quickly turns around when you figure out (after trial and error) some weird scheme and actually pull it off. Cool game, plus an audiovisual treat. Extra points for the amazing music! Whoever made all this happen must be a talented bunch of people, and probably very handsome.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game and absolutely unique combat system.  With the time rewind mechanism and the many skills, the possibilities are endless.  Its as if save scumming the game and the divinity combat system had a baby.  The graphics are charming, the story is fine - as often in tactics games its there to prop up the fighting system and it gets the job done.  I do like the finnish flavor of the world building.  It will seem confusing at first but once you grasp the flow of battles, you will be hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'm not a big fan of classic RPGs. To me there's no fun in managing an inventory nor grinding enemies by bashing the Attack command. To my fortune, Iron Danger does not have an inventory to care about, no weapons to wield or even any armor to wear. This game is all about the battles, and boy, are they fun!The fights revolve around your ability to rewind time. Got hit by an arrow? No problem, just go back to just before it hit you and dodge. Got ambushed by enemies? Again, just go back in time and take another route. The mechanic is simple and surprisingly rewarding. In some sense, being able to backtrack your choices makes the fights feel more like puzzles than the traditional risk vs reward and roll of dice kinda thing. That doesn't mean you can't die though - you'll mostly likely die all the time, but with the time manipulation mechanic in place you'll always be able to rewind and correct your errors.Overall, Iron Danger is a very good looking game with a nice soundtrack and lively voice acting. The story is based on an actual epic, but it does feel a bit generic and lacks in presentation - as a Finn I mostly just get some chuckles out of the Kalevalan names, but no grander feelings get tickled by the dialog. The controls feel pretty natural, although movement could be a bit smoother outside a fight. Also, with the relatively free 3D camera, you'll have to adjust your view all the time to be able to see what's going on. I can't help thinking if the game would have worked better with a fixed perspective.All in all, Iron Danger is very good indie game and well worth the 30€ it costs at the time of this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Danger

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! The graphics are beautiful and controlling multiple characters is special. You have to plan how to pass the challenges in the game and that makes it more interesting, you can't just run and try to beat everything. A bit difficult for me in the beginning, but then again you can rewind time and try again.

name: Last Epoch
detailed_description: Editions Comparison Join Our Discord Join the Last Epoch Discord server to keep up with the latest updates, recruit some friends, and slay your way across Eterra! About the Game Last Epoch combines time travel, exciting dungeon crawling, engrossing character customization and endless replayability to create an Action RPG for veterans and newcomers alike. Travel through the world of Eterra’s past and face dark empires, wrathful gods and untouched wilds – to find a way to save time itself from The Void. Key Features 15 Mastery Classes Embark on your adventure as one of five powerful classes and, through your journey, ascend into a unique Mastery Class that unlocks more specialized abilities and build-options. 120+ Skill Trees Every skill has its own augment tree that will allow you to control, alter, and empower your playstyle. Transform your skeletons into archers, your lightning blast into chain lightning, or make your serpent strike summon snakes to fight alongside you! Hunt Rare & Powerful Loot Fill your arsenal with magic items that you may craft to perfection, change the rules of your build with powerful unique and set items, and always have that next upgrade just on the horizon with Last Epoch's deep and randomized loot system. Rewarding Crafting System The items you wield are yours to forge! Last Epoch’s community-revered crafting system allows you to control your character's power progression, featuring robust and deterministic upgrade mechanics. Uncover the Past, Reforge the Future Travel to different moments of time where you will discover the many factions and secrets that exist within the world of Eterra and fight to set the timeline onto a new path. Endless replayability With a wealth of classes and skills to customize, deep game systems, randomized loot, and continuing development, Last Epoch is a game that will keep you coming back for years to come. Easy to Learn, Hard to Master We’re committed to making gameplay approachable for new and veteran players alike by allowing you to jump into the fray quickly and providing many in-game resources. Though don’t be fooled, Eterra has many dangers waiting for you that require a mastery of combat and build-crafting. Zero Pay-To-Win Last Epoch will never offer gameplay advantages by being able to spend real money. We believe in creating a fair environment for all players.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game but a bit boring and not nearly as complex as people were making it sound. The story is completely ridiculous even by ARPG standards, the art direction is extremely generic, combat is clunky and the crafting system is a cool idea on paper but a bit too esoteric and grindy in practise. For 44 dollars, I would recommend D4 at this point since both games are very similar but D4 just does everything better.

_childDocuments_.review: I HAVE BEEN LOOKING FOR THIS GAME FOR YEARS!!I didn't know it, but this is what I wanted. I was too late to get into PoE, I dont like joining so late that there are millions of hours of youtube guides/tutorials and layers and layers of things to learn. I wanted a hack-and-slash that was fast paced, where I felt powerful as a character, BUT i want leveling to be custom, and feel the impact of builds.This game NAILS the balance of leveling is cool and your decisions matter vs. being too complicated, too slow. _childDocuments_.review: Last Epoch is not a perfect game but holy f**k it feels really good. - The skills are satisfying right when you unlock them. There's a "crunch" to them. And each skill has its own skill tree so can customize it to suit your play style.- Many of the classes and builds just feels strong, works well, and feels unique. Defensive stats are actually useful. - Crafting is straight forward adding 4 stats to each gear you can craft right away and it feels substantial. There is RNG but from my experience its fair. Also dont worry you'll have plenty of mats so you don't need to worry about saving it for later. Regardless of the item's level, if a piece of gear has nice rolls it will be useful.- Endgame crafting let's you absorb a gear's added stats into Legendary gear. Which means a piece of low level legendary gear can still be useful.- enemies are varied and the bosses are fun and some are challenging- The endgame is good. There is enough content to go on for awhile till new content comes out which seems to be sooner than later.- The QoL is substantial. Storage can be upgraded for some gold. I have like 20 stash tabs. There is a customizable lootfilters built in the game. Craft mats have their own infinite storage that's accessible anywhere meaning you can craft anytime anywhere. Alts can skip the campaign. No WASD yet but controller support works great. Offline mode is available. - There is a leaderboard you can climb by fighting waves after waves of enemies. You'llll have access to your storage in between waves.- Cosmetics are there and would need to be bought through the in game shop. You can get free ones from twitch drops. Skill cosmetics will become available at a later date.The biggest negatives about the game for me have been the connection issues which seem to have been fixed.Overall LE is a great game for bother new players and experienced arpg vets. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Launch and servers is a little rough, especially with the huge growing player base at, but the devs have great communication and are trying their best to resolve the issues. Even now its not perfect but I expected it and somehow managed to play with not too many issues. As a huge diablo and various other ARPG fan, Last Epoch hits that special looter dopamine hit. The skill trees offered allow so much versatility and build diversity, the crafting system is not too complex or difficult but is very engaging especially with uniques being very relevant, echoes (endgame) along with their modifier system gives you options to choose your path towards different loot rewards and mods which keeps the endgame from becoming stale quickly, and boss fights with their mechanics keep you on your toes and are very enjoyable.The merchant faction offers an bustling economy for those who enjoy the trading scene, while the fortune faction gives solo self found players more options and goals to achieve for even more loot. Despite the server issues and a couple bugs, Last Epoch is definitely a great looter ARPG experience made for those who love the genre. It might be best to wait til server issues are resolved, but if you can get past the server issues during peak traffic hours, you'll def find a refreshing and enjoyable looter to scratch that itch.

_childDocuments_.review: No, I'm not recommending this game, but it has nothing to do with the servers. In fact, I'm playing in full offline mode, and haven't had any in-game issues.The reason I don't recommend this game is mostly due to combat. It all feels weightless. Enemies don't react to getting hit. They only react to death. Same with the player character. I'm at level 32 with a sorcerer and I just feel like something is off.Also, although I'm not at endgame, Last Epoch is unfinished with only 9 of 12 acts completed. Which I guess it okay, since the story is awful and just an excuse to travel through time, although I'd argue that's not very fulfilling because we can't truly alter timelines based on our own actions.I don't know. _childDocuments_.review: Im enjoying the game so far. The games still in early access so it has a lot of problems, but overall its a smooth experience thats updated and enhanced regularly. The game is missing multiplayer entirely, but thats the next thing the devs are working on so hopefully thats introduced by the end of this year. Arena doesnt really have a purpose right now other than leaderboard climbing. You'll get better rewards in monoliths Monoliths are fun, not too challenging early on. Ill come in with an edit to talk about endgame once ive hit empowered monoliths on a few different buildsCrafting is fine. Big thing is finding items with stats and modifying, rather than building an item from empty bases due to how the fracturing system works. Its an easy way to patch stat holes. Basic affix shards arent hard to come by, itll be the more usefull skill affixes for builds that youll really need to hunt down. Though you can shatter an item for affixes if you want them on other pieces of gear which is nice. Nowhere near the complexity of PoE but thats to be expected with the crafting not having years worth of evolution. It will be nice to see how this evolves Overall my main issue with the game is lacking a few QoL, which the devs have already discussed so its just an issue of waiting. Not all buffs and debuffs are displayed, or not displayed consistently which can make it difficult to see when you need to reapply a skill. Picking up affix shards is annoying. You always have access to the forge (the main crafting hub) and the forge allows you to store all of your shards so shards dont take up inventory technically. The issue however is that shard will consume inventory space until you manually place them in the forge. This can get annoying when youre picking up a lot of shards and having to constantly empty inventory if you want to pick up other items to either upgrade or strip. I hope they do something about this. Its not game breaking by any means, but given how the forge inventory works shards should not default to player inventory. If they want to make players move shards to the forge manually, make players physically go to the forge and lock crafting to hub world only. Overall my performance has been smooth, though be warned that will not be the case for everyone. The devs are still working on optimization which is to be expected as this stage. Overall I'm having a blast and I cant wait to see this game in a finished state. Its already very polished for an early access game. Be warned, do not buy this game if you are expecting a finished game. The steam page and first screen you see warns that this is early access. They mean it. Many people forget that buying early access is nothing more than investing in a product in order to support it. It does not guarantee in any way a full experience when you pay. My experience may differ from yours because of the state of the game, dont pay for something if you arent pateint enough to wait for the dev time.

_childDocuments_.review: For over a year now, I have looked for an AARPG to fill the void that is left when a current POE season becomes stale, and to play during the off time while I was waiting for the new season.  A game I could pickup and play to scratch that itch.  Other larger companies have taken me for well over double the cost of Last Epoch, and I was always left wanting.I recently picked up LE in Early Access, shortly before 1.0 launch, and I have spent over 100 hundred hours within 2 weeks playing, and I cannot even cover all of the things I love about it.  The campaign is smooth, and gearing and progressing through the campaign is very intuitive.  The skills and passives allow for much customization, and it is possible to do all content on custom or non meta builds. The meta builds merely do things faster, and better, but are not required.Gameplay wise, LE is smooth, and actually performs better on my slightly sub par machine than other games. And there are loads of Quality of Life features that I only wish other AARPG developers would add to their games.  Crafting is actually fun, and viable even from the beginning of the game. I am happy that they are releasing 1.0, and setting the bar for what AARPGs should be.

_childDocuments_.review: After 40 hours of gameplay, I think I have a comprehensive understanding of this game. If you plan to play for less than 50 hours, I would recommend this game. If you're in offline mode, you cannot switch to online mode, so be aware of that. For me, both online and offline modes are the same; it's just solo combat on the map. Offline mode spares you from enduring long loading times of 5 seconds or more, and you can also chat with others.In online mode, you may encounter issues like packet loss, lag, or difficulty connecting to servers. I haven't played with others in online mode, so I can't comment on that experience. However, I don't see anyone else on the map; only the chat window indicates that I'm not alone.Regarding the endgame, the only thing you can do is grind maps repeatedly. When your map level reaches 800, you can fight the boss for boss-specific gear. Assuming I fought the boss 15 times, with each requiring a map level of 800, and each map providing an average of 60 levels, I would need to grind 165 maps. Excluding accidental deaths and the chance for higher levels, that's a minimum of 14 hours to potentially get a single piece of gear for your build, and it may not even meet your requirements.Furthermore, the drop rates for high-quality T6 gear are very low, let alone T7 gear. In over 40 hours of gameplay, I haven't seen a single T7 item. Most of the T6 items with good stats you get may not even be what you're looking for. What can you do? Continue grinding, which seems to be another method to extend gameplay time.Another drawback is the map size, which is excessively large. While en route, you'll encounter groups of ranged enemies that can easily kill you, so much of your time is spent traveling. Even with movement skills for each character, this remains frustrating.I dislike the Arena mode the most because it spawns numerous ranged enemies. As a melee mage, increasing numbers of ranged enemies easily kill me. Plus, you have to wait for 12 waves of enemies to complete the mission. I wish there was a mode for faster enemy spawns to enhance the player experience.So the endgame feels quite boring and repetitive. I wish there were guaranteed rewards instead of relying on extremely low drop rates to extend gameplay time
