_childDocuments_.review: EDITED TO ADD: All you children out there screaming your heads off about not being able to play the game online? Yeah I hope you feel silly now. Took them *maybe* a week to work out the kinks? I played OFFLINE fine for the first week, ever since then I've never had to do that again and I've never had a single problem playing online. Soooo yeah. An ode to Last Epoch: I am one of those folks who hardly ever reviews games. Take that as you will. I'm also from the first crop of millenials to come into this capitalistic h*ellscape, so I absolutely remember the rise of household electronics.  My family got our first home PC around 1992. It was a Tandy HX1000 and it ran on DOS and *hard disks* before the advent of floppies. I cut my gaming teeth on King's Quest and Space Quest, KQIV, Rosella's story, is still my favorite from those days. My cheat codes were in the form of a little booklet you had to buy separate from the game, a little book that fit in your hand on white paper with red ink with a little decoder that you had to slide over the specially hidden writing that would give you the hint on how to move on if you got stuck. I went from that to NES, my little brother and I had the original golden LoZ game, it came with that and the first Mario Bros for a special Christmas price. After the NES came the Sega, and we got Sonic, which was a revolution for us. Streets of Rage 2 was another favorite for the Sega. Somewhere along the line my little brother got a Game Boy that he'd share with me sometimes when a hurricane came through and knocked the power out. Once it got to SNES, though, and the first PlayStation and Xbox, the controllers got too complex and big for my hands, which are still pretty small. So I stopped gaming for a while, but I'd still watch my brother play Quake and Doom when they came out. Didn't get back into it until 2005 when I lived in Tasmania and married a gamer... who almost never let me play ANYTHING. I watched Half-Life, Max Payne, a lot of others that I can't remember now cause I never experienced them personally. None of the newer stuff caught my eye until coming across a little game that my ex jerk was slightly disdainful of, called Diablo 2. Among the ways I'm different is I am aphantasic. I cannot visualize and do not have a "mind's eye". FPS type games were never a pull for me because they make me sick and dizzy, to see from someone else's eyes, and though that has gotten better in the last decade, back THEN... yeah. There was no way to turn it off or modify it or any setting you could play from 3rd with on most of those that I remember. Diablo 2 wasn't like that, and I came back to PC gaming because of it. All of that to tell you where I'm coming from. In the last 24 years it seems the gaming industry has leaned more and more into cash grabbing in every aspect possible. Prime example: Diablo IV, which people waited LITERAL decades for, is really nothing more than a ploy for another big faceless triple A studio to drain you of your last nickel for pretty but useless armor for a horse. Despicable and disgusting, and obviously the focus is on the shareholders and richy rich players who can afford all the finery, and D4 is definitely not alone in this. Last Epoch is for ARPGs what Guild Wars 2 is for MMORPGS. A solid, beautiful, decent game with free updates for life - in the case of GW2, now there are optional expansions that you can pay for, yes, but you get SO MUCH with each of those, and you don't have to have them to enjoy the game. I see what Eleventh Hour is trying to do. I see that this is a labor of love, and guess what? Offline it works perfectly well and I have had not a single issue (that wasn't user error lol). I'm greatly enjoying my new Acolyte, who will def specialize as Necro because that's where I've started since it's been an option, either there or Ranger type, at least, and I'm excited as all get out to try a Primalist next. Down to the designs of the health and mana bowls, so much care and concern and creativity and yes, love, has gone into this game. Everyone spitting hate at these BRAND NEW DEVS for their VERY FIRST RELEASE needs to seriously go touch some grass and/or find another hobby or activity to do for a while, like a regular grown adult-type person. The game hasn't been out for even 48 hours yet, and they did everything they could to prepare, and from what I understand it was an unforeseen circumstance type thing. (And no, dudebros, I really don't need any technical explanation of what went wrong and what mistakes were made, that's okay, please save the effort because I'm happy with the amount of communication the devs themselves are doing on quite a few different platforms.)Last Epoch is gorgeous, fun to play, a really decent challenge, and has a great story. It's definitely worth the money. Eleventh Hour, you have a fan for life. Thank you!

_childDocuments_.review: So loading will get fixed yes, BUT....This game has a bunch of annoying problems: - Inventory & Crafting menus are clunky -> sometimes dialogs open/close at random, you can select items that are located underneath the dialog, hovering on an item grows out of the screen and also prevents from hovering over another. - Combat is clunky -> Mana does not feel great, some skills are too slow/weak even when leveled (probably you need to find the random unique for level 82 to enable them). Some enemy skills land way too fast. - Boss design is horrendous -> all hits are one shots (mostly), all DoTs need to tick you twice (maxed res btw). Basically it is more punishing to play than a souls game, but you also have no dodge and movement skills have infinite cooldown. - Leveling up is slow and boring -> Leveling is slower than PoE for some reason; Monoliths are all the same and there is no variety resulting in you being forced to die of boredom just to quit 2 hours later cause nothing changes. - Gearing up is not exciting-> Suffixes are so useless -> they are mostly resistances (lame) while all character trees already give you more than enough. Items need a revisit. (Add something interesting to suffixes or add a Kitava to lower the character's resistances).Game has potential, ain't a Diablo Killer yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Last Epoch is an excellent game. Whose reputation has been marred by an admittedly shaky first few days of launch.Highlights:___________________________* Combat feels great. Punchy sound effects, good visuals and responsive animations. * Meaningful depth. A lot of character choice and build decisions are provided without sacrificing accessibility. While it's not the staggering depth of Path of Exile, there's far more on offer here than Diablo 4. * Best gamepad support of any ARPG. I frequently swap between using mouse and keyboard and a controller. Thoughtful UX decisions make looting and menu navigation much less tedious.* Crafting is unique, every item has "Forging Potential" which is basically how much you can tinker with it. The game provides a lot of cool ways to tinker.  * Beautiful, varied environments and some really nice music.* Fun campaign. (Personally I liked it more than Path of Exile's campaign but less than Diablo 4s)Critique:____________________________* Player character models are a little lackluster compared to the rest of the games visuals* The actual plot of the story is just okay, it's a bit all over the place* No Cycle Challenge Rewards yet Don't sleep on this one if you're an ARPG fan. With the launch issues now resolved, this is an easy recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun. The systems are very well built. Its still in beta and there are currently a lot of bugs. Enemy variety is lacking. The story is interesting but needs to fleshed out better. Main boss fights are good, smaller bosses are meh. Most of the campaign can be face tanked until you get to Lagon, and even then with a few minor adjustments he can be face tanked to depending on your class. The end game is a bit repetitive. The dungeons are essentially boss rushes, with two levels of mobs to kill before getting to the main boss. Level design is very linear, which is probably my biggest issue with the game. Despite the massive game map, It doesn't feel like a world. It feels like a series of connected way points via large and small tunnel maps with no exploration in between. But despite all that, its fun and after an additional 100+ hours I'm pretty addicted. I cant wait to play 1.0 at launch.

_childDocuments_.review: So, now that loading issues are mostly fixed:This is an AMAZING base for what i bet will be, in a year or two, a truly deep and engaging ARPG with tons of content and challenges.As it stands now, however, it is in the unfortunate position of...going against Path Of Exile. Which is truly an uphill battle given that POE, due to how it's leagues work, is without a doubt to this day the ARPG with the most content that has ever existed. Not even close.It is infact one of the few games where even veteran players often complain that there is too much content; even i myself, after thousands of hours, have yet to truly experience everything (for example i've never reached the final boss of "Delve")I say this simply to point out that, when people complain about Last Epoch not having enough endgame, more often than not it's because they come with the expectation that it should resemble at least vaguely their expectations set by POE...and that is frankly unachievable. POE has a decade of leagues, expansions and refinements implemented at this point.Back to Last Epoch however:to say something that everyone has already said, this is a very good middle ground when it comes to accessibility and depth.I went in without watching a single guide, without knowing anything regarding builds, abilities, masteries and gearing and just came out with a build as i went, and that worked perfectly fine even in endgame.If you love ARPGS, and you want a very good game that it will keep you interested for a couple weeks-a month, this game is in a very good place. However don't go into it expecting a "new hobby" - game that can keep you busy every single day for the next year, because as it stands right now...it simply doesn't have the capability to deliver that for most people..if that's what you're looking for i would suggest waiting a couple new seasons to see how they implement new content.One more thing that gives me hope, however, is that the developers are ABSOLUTELY AMAZING.While the first few days were filled with huge problems of connectivity, meaning that most players found close to impossible playing, they were giving constant updates and being genuinely incredible when it came to comunication, not once giving the appearence that they didn't care.This was double as amazing given how vitriolic, toxic and genuinely awful the response from many players was.It's one thing complaining about a product you paid for not working properly. It's another thing to spend 24/7 making alt accounts to join their discord/social media accounts to constantly spam them with harassment.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The perfect game for people who still want to enjoy ARPGs that dont want to get bogged down by PoE and want something more light-weight.I write this review having had no idea this game even existed before I was told about it just a week ago, I had no intention of even playing it. As it stands I've finished the campaign, regular monoliths, and am starting Endgame content.I haven't really enjoyed an ARPG ever since the days of D2, and you would think PoE would have grabbed me, but ultimately, I felt the main issue with PoE was that it passes the threshold of actually being a video game and is more of an advanced builcraft/theory craft simulator with a game attached to it. The whole appeal of the game seems to be acquiring the knowledge over hundreds, thousands of hours and using your understanding of the game's mechanics to design carefully crafted builds that could never have been organically reached through regularly playing the game.Last Epoch to me, is the inverse design philosophy. It asks: What if we went in the other direction and made a game that was focused on being user-friendly while giving the player a set of horizontal-progression stats/mechanics that allow the player that same freedom and experimentation without the excessive complexity?The skill system is the main highlight in this regard - the skill passives offer you a way to change the way your skills work that isn't just raw flat damage. From changing the damage type, or making the skill move completely differently, to offering synergy with other abilities. What this means is that you're then able to create builds that are centered around certain damage types and synergies, and gear accordingly. When you add in the passives, and the fact you're still able to spec into your non-main mastery to some degree (there are 3 per class), means that there is still room for 2 people who picked the same mastery to still have a large degree of uniqueness to their builds.The gear system is also much more based around finding certain uniques that will provide very signature modifiers to enable certain builds to work. And yeah, you can push those even further if they have legendary potentials, for full min max but LP isn't necessary, you can still run a build, you will just be missing some extra stat bonuses, and you can farm the LP version of that unique later on, very clever idea. It completely manages to escape the "more number betterer" trope and it's clear the designers very much knew what to avoid. Overall, this game has an incredibly solid foundation, it's light-weight, it's fun, and it offers you a *very* competent and enjoyable ARPG while giving the player full freedom of experimentation within this system, another thing I found cumbersome about PoE. Should you buy this game? You probably should. Even if they didn't add more content, there's enough here to justify it's cost and entertain you for at least a few dozen hours, without even touching the Endgame.

_childDocuments_.review: Game play as a someone with many hours in Diablo/grim dawn/path of exile/torchlight/wolcen I can say they got that down pact.  Levelling characters are fun. It's like many of the latter, it's end game that falls into can't be bothered territory. I don't know if its the lag or the bad design in telegraphing which zones are now damage but there is a point where this game made me thing well f' that because every indication I can see says I avoided the zones I needed to avoid I'm dead anyway.The game wasn't engaging enough to find out what the issue was. I've played it a couple times levelling the same sorts of characters (only ones that interested me) and keep getting up to that same point, I got past it one point just upping all my resistances to deal with the inevitable damage despite appearing to avoid it. I figured it would only get worse from there so what's the point. There's a guild where you can sell stuff but requires you to level your reputation to buy things, unless they are newly put up for sale.. You level your rep by selling things (I think, it didn't explain it well).. so why put gold on things you are selling because you need the rep more than gold.. due to lack of functional search/filter you spend most your time scrolling through countless pages of the same item for the same price of nil or some stupid amount of gold looking for one thing you might need..Sure I'd like some more customisation as some of the forced design choices are cringe but overall it was good if you just wanna finish the campaign. I wasn't able to engage with the story, so I skipped it where I could. So maybe if bored and on sale?

_childDocuments_.review: I've been less impacted by the server issues since I'm generally playing at weirder, low volume times. (+) I love diversity of builds at end game. Maybe that collapses onto a handful of builds at the bleeding edge, but for now everything I've played feels viable for a casual in endgame. The loot filter is awesome and if you configure it right every piece of loot you see is meaningful in some way. (-) The story is absolutely forgettable. IDK if others feel this way time travel to me always seems like a cop-out and circumvents world building. Either way, ARPG's aren't story focused and the goal really is endgame gameplay. I rolled merchant's guild. Love the concept and gating actions behind grindable favor means trading is always secondary to the core game and doesn't become its own meta that boxes our casuals. Today the implementation is a bit janky though: 1) the bazaar has different vendors for every gear piece - just inefficient, and 2) prices are all over the place since it's so new. Overall the server issues don't bother me and the core gameplay loops are awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: I want this game to succeed, but I just can't recommend this game in it's current state.This review is from the perspective of a sweaty try hard.The monolith system is very boring and I am constantly be made aware of this repetitive task.I get burnt out very quickly when playing this game. I suspect the fact that this game doesn't have procedural generated maps play a big part in this. At the moment, I pretty much know all the layouts,making the monoliths feel  very 'samey'.The implementation of trading is very bad. Trading doesn't come "online" until you are at least rank 7 (or around level 97-98). Price checking is a chore. You can't sort by rolls. There are a lot more but I don't want this review to be a bug report.Speaking of bugs, this game is very buggy. Over the course of my playtime (~9 days), I encountered 63 bugs, some of which existed for as long as a year ago. I know that you can't expect the devs to fix everything, but the fact is that my experience with the game has been terrible every time I tried it over the years doesn't fill me with confidence.The game has a lot of aspects that don't respect your time (very rich coming from a no life), for example the blessings system. The game is also not alt friendly as your monolith progressions don't carry over. Well since it's such a hassle to level alts, at least you can just try out different skills on your main. NOPE, mastery is locked, gotta level up buddy. Builds balancing? We don't talk about that.The arena ladder is overran by bug abusers.Again, I want this game to succeed. But just can't recommend it in it's current state

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:"We’ve scale tested for months with third parties, consultants, the help of infra providers, and our own backend team. We have the ability to scale servers quickly, have reserved a large amount of bare metal machines, and do not have a maximum spend for cloud overflow- it’s all elastic. From the extensive testing we’ve done, unless we do have a really crazy turnout, we should be stable. It’s not lost on us that many much larger companies than us have had issues at launch though... We’re optimistic and if there are issues it certainly won’t be for lack of effort, spend, or ignorance to the importance of launch day." - Judd (Game Director)So, that was a lie. Four days later, and still massive server problems.Original - STILL STANDS:Not a fan of the direction the game is going at the moment. I'll continue wishing for something more like PoE and less like Diablo.The biggest problem? EVERYTHING is locked down. From animations, to maps (there are no map skips via movement skills), to items, to build interactions.... Items are actually the most egregious problem. I found myself struggling to make endgame builds that actually rely on dynamic use of unique items/skills. Not because they don't exist... but because the items that could be used are far too limited.I'm here to exploit the game for my amusement. I want complex interactions. I want to spend hours building characters before ever playing the game. I can't have that here, and I don't really see it happening until the developers RELAX a little. Make an item that can be exploited. Let people have fun with it, and change it later. Do it. Thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say only good things about this because the ARPG genre needs competition, but I like to keep it real.First, People acting like its far more complex than D3 are being incredibly dramatic because really D3 might be the least complex AAA ARPG ever made. Doesn't make it terrible -- It has its niche which is when you just want to bash and not think too hard. The good:While the story is interesting enough, the time travel gimmick doesn't suspend disbelief for me, as the game has still been incredibly linear despite that. It feels like they just slap the word 'year' over the word 'act'.The crafting system allows for customization rather than making a static item with minor variables, which should be the standard by now. It feels a little convoluted to me starting out, but it is much better than most ARPGs.As far as skills go, its one of the games strongest points. I feel like the devs paid special attention to builds that are almost always neglected in other games, which is actually one of my favorite things so far. I really enjoy that recasting your summon is typically a buff, or a special attack. I enjoy the sentinel's retaliation bubble. If I find a few skills that are modified in how they work by cursor placement, I'll be pretty satisfied overall. Combat feels a little slow, but it seems like a design choice. Its less about swarms and more about avoiding attacks.The bad:The most realistic time travel in the game has to be the graphics, I felt like I was back in 2005. The palette in some areas is incredibly boring, grimdark will do that to a color scheme though. The sound effects are pretty understated, which isn't really a gamebreaker; its just not as 'scream, grunt, scream, monster roar, bubbling potion noise, grunt' as most ARPGs. I don't like my big bashy skills not having big bashy noises though. The music isn't my favorite, and went to mute after a few acts.Verdict:All in all I'd say its worth your time if you like ARPGs at all, especially since the genre needs all the support it can get, having been hamstrung by the success of its two main franchises. I feel like theres plenty of room for growth in the genre, that isn't just adding yet another layer of complexity to the skill or loot systems, and 11th hour seems to understand that.

_childDocuments_.review: So, my review probably ain't going to be worth a damn to many. I have basically 4 hours at this point. But I hope someone at least reads it. I've been in the rut so to speak with ARPGs. First Lost Ark nickle and dimed the hell out of you, then Diablo IV was lackluster, if you can even call it that. But this, this is beautiful. I love the class system, the crafting, the zones, the artwork. It's all just so beautiful. The community isn't complete ass, of course you have your trolls and such, (what game doesn't). But for the most part, people have been willing to help me understand the game. It's best to get it now before it's full release in February, next month. One of the things that really shocked me is how awesome it felt in that level 1-10 phase where you basically start slow, and super weak, and start to really feel that progression around level 5. I really hope that you would give this a chance, and I hope they really carry the torch with this one. To me, it seems like they will! I look forward to leveling to max, and making another character. If you like the game, and my review helped you buy it, please leave a like. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Server issues were temporary, as expected.Last Epoch is perfectly in the middle of the simplicity and ease of access of Diablo 4 and the incredible complexity of balancing 19,000 passives of Path of Exile.Here are my subjective opinions...Positives:+ Classes and sub-classes and customization of builds is extremely fun to theory-craft AND play.+ Items and crafting are actually useful and fun to change and use.+ Skills that can be changed and linked together to feel incredibly useful and satisfying to use.+ A long and enjoyable campaign/story. It was nostalgic to me of some classic console RPGs.+ An engaging and ever-changing end game where you choose what to do and where to go.+ This remote indie company repaired their servers and made a smoother game that costs a fraction of larger companies games AND runs much better. D3 launch was worse, couldn't play online, and took longer to fix.Negatives:- There is no alternative way to level besides the campaign/story.- 0 appearance customization options.- There are a few extremely minor bugs still... but these are a tiny fraction of what exist in Diablo 4 or Path of Exile.- Bazaar (player marketplace) is quite strange... kind of like Path of Exile but with less UI clutter.- You cannot change left/right mouse buttons. Left mouse button is your dedicated click-to-move.

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously with only 5 hours in I can't speak for the game as a whole, but after trying many games of the same type I can tell you this is a great game.So far the experience has been very chill, and within 1 hour of playing I could tell a class wasn't for me (mage) and I chose a different one (paladin) which feels very fun right now.This game is perfectly between Diablo 4 and Path of Exile in terms of complexity. _childDocuments_.review: While it's not as complex in terms of diversity as PoE it does fit that build itch that I enjoy in terms of diversity.  All in all I think the best shining aspect of this game is crafting and skill tree.  Crafting in this game is actually crafting and not just solely based on the use of orbs, while the crafting system is great in PoE this game takes it up a notch and let you pick and chose additions and removals, but in a way that you don't feel to overpowered by easily making best weapons in game.  The skill system is how I envisioned PoE wanted the socket system to be, customizable with effects not just "added melee physical" or "increased spell damage" support.  Your tree effects your skill in LE, so you customize the skill to your liking, while taking away the feeling of "I have to load 4 links of damage".  While PoE fixes these issues by having damage increases in spirit and passives only, this is another look into the idea and it is handled pretty well

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not optimized for mouse and keyboard. At first you can tolerate it. But as you go on, it just become annoying.In many other PC games, you use mouse click to attack and use keyboard for movement. This game is the complete opposite. You use mouse to move and use keyboard for attack. So your mind will be frequently confused with it.It also does not support the latest mouse technology with 5 buttons. For a game released in 2024, it's actually using outdated technology.The game play itself feels interesting at first. But then you'll quickly get bored when you realize how shallow it is. In one screen you'll usually get less than 10 enemies. Click your keyboard many times to hit it and kill it. Then go forward and repeat the same thing over and over again.It lacks variation and content. No story line. Just a simple isometric view of a shooter game with lack of excitement and bad controller for PC.

Following my last login, I did not receive any warning or notification regarding any misconduct, hence I am quite surprised by the account suspension.Here is some additional information that may assist in your investigation:1. My conduct within the game has always aligned with Last Epoch's rules and policies.2. I have not engaged in any illicit trading or deceptive behavior with other players.3. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR  It's even worse than when I downed it the first time, and if the indie dev is sticking microtransactions into their paid game on day one before they fix the server issues, I can't even be respectful anymore.  I can't even recommend waiting to let it cook, this mess went early access in Q2 2019.  So much for all of that "potential".-No rebind controls options.-Gamepad controls don't work for most menus.-Graphics look like a game that's been in early access for 5 years like this one has been.-Mouse controls still don't always act like they should.Previous Review: "Thumbs down with respect.So many of the reviews are on its potential, a potential that might not come.  It's beautiful and engaging, but there are bugs and control idiosyncrasies that everyone seems forgive because it's in beta, but it's been in beta for years now, and it feels like it's never going to move on.If you're looking to scratch an ARPG itch while you wait for something else, this is worth the money.  If you're looking for something more, this could be a long wait for a train that's not coming.There is a lot of production value here.  The devs clearly love their work, but if they love it too much to push it out of the nest, I cannot recommend it.  I do hope that I can edit this review one day."

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me of Diablo 2R I played D1,D2,D3,D2R,PoE, and then just to see the worlds I played immortal and D4. I was sad that the new Diablo's are trash and the games just drive players to the cash shop. Last Epoch feels like a real game and a true spiritual successor of D2. I highly recommend Last Epoch if you were a fan of D2 and PoE. It's a solid middle ground between the two games and it may not have movie quality cinematic's but the story is actually good even though the focus of this game is the ARPG game play. The Dev's for Last Epoch from what I understand is only a 90 man team. They had a vision and they have brought it to life in similar fashion to Baldur's gate 3. I hope people that like ARPG's find this game similar to people that like CRPG's found Baldur's gate 3. I hope this team finds similar success to Larian studio's in this endevor and I look forward to seeing expansion and later new games from Eleventh Hour Games. I hope they make a Last Epoch 2 and Last Epoch 3 etc in the future as technology gets better and Eleventh Hour Games's bank account gets bigger.

_childDocuments_.review: Last epoch is a great middleground between games like Path of Exile which is very complicated, and super simple games like Diablo 3 and Minecraft dungeons. You can create your own build without following a guide and respeccing is pretty accessible and you do not feel like everything is ruined.The crafting system is delightful giving a middleground between deterministic and random crafting, with very exciting with the newly added legendary potential of uniques.I also really like the approach that each skill has its own customizable skill tree, very excited to see where this game goes in the future once it gets leagues and regular resets!

I just want the game to be fluid to play.Again, you allow it with a controller. So what gives? Can't wait for POE 2 is the only take away I get from this issue.

_childDocuments_.review: Current state of the game is catastrophic in every aspect :Server are unstable, it take hours (not kiding) to get to a campaign city, loading screen can take 10-15 min each, door are your most dangerous ennemy and they are everywhere.Game is filled to the brim of various bug, if you try to do a dungeon with friend, you will be with them on the first zone, somehow you can be phased in another dimension on the buffer zone, at the end there is a prompt asking you if you want to start the boss, completly bugged, not taking in account friend vote, so not starting, friend have to abbandon the vote, and if they tp on you, they are stuck out of bound of map, die from enviromental damage, can't loot or acces reward, and need to restart game.But the worst is, even outside of bug : game is just poorly designed:Ui is a calamity, if you want to respec 5 point in your tree, you need to clic on it 5 time then validate it on the "are you sure you want to do that " prompt 5 time. While when you allocate it the first time, there's no prompt, meaning if you missclic, you have to respec the point and relevel it.Worst being respcing your mastery point, let's say you want to change some point at the start of your pathing, you need to unlearn the point at the end, then allocate the one you want, then unlearn the one you really want to unlearn, then realocate the end point. Each point respeced that way open a prompt asking you to validate the operation obviously.Instead we could have a simple planer, where you freely make the modification you want in a preview, the validate and pay ONE TIME and that's it. This is the core concept of the game, tedious useless and ineficient buffer zone, loading screen, validation prompt everywhere. Except where you really want them of course.Party play is useless, 0 incentives to do it, no more reward, content barely get harder, and game is not designed to do it efficiently, it's just not fun do do it, let aside that every time you start a monolith (end game content) while you load into the zone, they reload the zone they are in, then need to take a tp to load to the zone you are. It's really hard to see where your friend are on the map, fun fact, i play a sorcerer, i had a support build to empower my friend with mana regen ward damage and resist, but i had to channel it on them, couldn't aim at their portrait, so had to channel it on their character itself, my friend was a necromancer, 9out of 10 my buff ended in a wandering skeleton that was passing by instead of my friend. Dropped the support build..As for the content itself : monolith : you run as fast as you can to the objective, you can ignore most or every ennemie in the way just to clear the map and get out as fast as possible, reward come from completing the monolith. Feel like a chore.And monster themself are a joke of a design, the biggest monster are trash that are getting oneshoted, while the most dangerous and tanky one are small fast, humanoid ennemies without any distinctive animation, you can only spot them on your minimap they teleport every 5 sec or so, meaning ,every 5 sec you have to play where is charlie to find your ennemied on your screen.Crafting is okay and that the only good thing I can think of.Quite honestly, don't play it in this current state, game is severly unfinished, don't get fooled, that's not a 1.0, that's just a 'that the only moment we can publish it because current Poe league is more or less finished,  next league is coming in a bit more then a month, PoE2 is coming soon, Diablo 4 is attrocious, so we have a very tight spot where arpg player have nothing else to do'

_childDocuments_.review: Re evaluating since launch, the game so far that iv experienced feels great, adaptive and you don't need to meta game to be able to stand your ground. there's no crazy pay to win structure and is generally easy to understand. The end game systems are fun and altered with events in ways that don't make it super repetitive.  At launch the servers were basically unplayable for up to what the first week or two when they finally got some improvements. The improvements were great don't get me wrong, you can play past 2 loading screens and not completely disconnect, now its more like 5-6. I had so much hope and loved theory crafting for this game  but sadly its still not worth it and personally still cant even fully play the realized game. The servers as mentioned, still kinda crap which could be avoidable ya know if there was any type of save system or rejoin forgiveness to major events such as keys which can sometimes take hours just to get the one you wanted. Congrats you got a key, guess what you can go do this major dungeon that's integral to the progression of the game but when your 20 minutes deep into this thing and one loading screen away from fighting the boss, and you just dc instead. Out of 20 keys or so the servers stabilized enough to allow me to complete 3 in total, so lets chalk that up to what 14 wasted hours, resources and piece of mind just for you not to accomplish anything. Then you go over to game play which has awesome theory crafting and plenty of ability's and multi classing opportunities. Sounds awesome right? until you find multiple nodes across multiple classes that just straight up don't work what so ever and you have to get down in the math just to find out, guess what then you have to take a hit and re level again just to get it back, not too bad till your endgame and all of your abilities are capped so the XP bar is huge being at lvl 19 going on 20, but you'v got a mid tier at best system to try and get that singular lvl back to put it into a node that ya know does the only thing its supposed to do. Theres 2 guilds inside the game you can join thing is the Merchants Guild is literally just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You are actively hindering yourself and your character progression with every enemy you defeat while in this guild, but at least these weren't in its 3 year open beta where everything else should have been generally fixed? This game has so much potential but im tired of wasting hours getting so far and getting all the materials to make awesome gear and fulfill power fantasies that on a literal bases, for all intents and purposes are possible. Sadly due to the crappy implementation, somehow being totally unprepared, and lack of consistency I think a lot of players including myself are just going to step away from such an amazing artwork till they can make a consistently working game. Maybe in 1 or 2 cycles, don't even know how long each will be, but in my mind until you can do such basic things and actually participate in endgame material that is the entire point of going past lvl 50 and uniques, Last Epoch will still be labeled as unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I like this game, it's a good ARPG which is fun to play and has some really cool mechanics, I especially love that every skill has its own skilltree, so much customization, so many different possible builds, that's very cool. I also like the crafting, and also the endgame mechanic with the monoliths is pretty cool and motivates me definitely more than most other ARPGs are able to do, with the different echo nodes it feels a little like a roguelike which I like.But sadly there's also some things that bother me: 1. The fact that unique armor pieces look totally different than their respective pictures in your inventory, just bc these items didn't get a unique model and just use the standard models of the base items is lame and lazy and annoys me. This is aggravated by most of the cosmetic armor skins in the shop being (in my opinion) ugly as crap, so you can't even make you character look good by using the transmog feature. That's terrible. In general this is the ARPG with the ugliest looking armor by FAR, which I find really annoying bc I want my characters to look cool too. Some DARK or BLACK armor píeces would be nice, devs!! Not only all these bright-coloured clown costumes!!!!! And having only a handful different chest armor pieces, with most of them only being achievable by buying a full bundle of armor skins, is just miserably bad. Where's the variety??2. Why on earth can you interact with other online players, but you can NOT inspect their gear ingame?? This is, again,  just lazy, this is a feature that imo every online ARPG has to have, period.There's more things like that, what's with the cycle reset for example? Player economy also seems to be totally messed up., not being able to buy something GOOD in the Bazaar for less than like half a billion gold LMAO. No thanks. Merchants Guild seems useless like this, pretty disappointing, then why have this option at all if it's basically unusable? Just make an upper limit for item sales, like 25 million per piece, problem solved.So overall I recommend this game, but it's still far from perfect and I'd give it a 7,5 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic ARPG with a wide variety of build possibilities and a solid endgame already in place.  There are still a few subclasses that still haven't been added and the campaign is missing a few chapters, but what's here is already a blast to play alone or with friends.  It still feels bad to see the same Uniques drop over and over while you  chase others but that's just the nature of the beast.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are good, the game play not as much.  Sure, you hack/slash/zap/fireball, but most of the time you 1 shot enemies and even on hardcore with a glass canon I never really feel at risk even well into the game.  The story wasn't engaging or interesting but maybe I didn't invest enough energy into it, which made levels less interesting because I didn't really think about what my purpose was there in that specific quest.  Loot was plentiful to the point it was annoying, I just waiting a few levels to really start looking at drops each time, vendors never sold anything worth a damn, never used potions because you regen HP so fast, same with mana.  Sure you run out, but then you just run around for 3 seconds or meditate for a beat and your back nearly full.  It made for more action but the game just lacked any sort of strategy like trying to line up hits, be smart about attacks and watching hp/mp, or just need every edge you can get so you are watching drops for something good.   So, I had some enjoyable times but just not the game for me, they got my money either way and I wish the developer luck with the future because they are close to something great.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: The combat feels very fluid and the gameplay in general feels nice, as well as crafting system and more. I can see myself sinking many more hours into this game, even if though I just scratched the surface of the game. The build variety is great in this game, gives a lot of freedom to you, great loot filter, infinite stash stabs etc. The atmosphere in the game is enjoyable too. Coming back from Diablo IV, on which I spent a lot of hours in, I can already feel the contrast that the game is a product made out of passion, and without predetermined mindset of making a business model in shape of an ARPG. Of course there is room for improvement, which I can see that the developers have already addressed (loading times, contact shadows, graphics in general as they can feel quite depthless). One other thing that the team could improve is the cosmetics and how the armor looks like. It really does not make feel you're a killing machine, more like a well-armed peasant. Character customization in general should be developed more. More content could be voice acted as well, but it is understandable why it's not the case yet.Overall, the game is really great and the developer response to the feedback given to the players is very encouraging. If you like ARPG games, make sure to gives this a try and support the company, as they seem like a really dedicated and passionate team. I wish the best of luck to you guys and I'll keep supporting your work. Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game back in 2021 in early access and really enjoyed it from then as a slightly more casual alternative to PoE (which I play every league). There's a small team working on it and there's clearly some issues with scene transitions etc, but considering the number of players, it's not unexpected considering the size of their team.Enjoyable story, great class/mastery system, itemisation is decent and the recent factions are a great addition to the game. Looking forward to some cycle specific content being added in the future, but have really high hopes. Favourite part is the crafting, really easy to get your head around and some really good ideas that differentiate it (LP, forging potential etc). Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: "Just wait until endgame."If you're going to tell me to wait until endgame for the game and loot to be good and fun, then I'm not sticking around.The game should be fun from the start, not after 50 hours.And I'm not messing with a loot filter to get good loot, that should be built into an ARPG automatically.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of ARPGs, I recommend this game to anyone who enjoys the format or is even remotely curious after watching the trailer.This game is very fun and is the most fun I've had in a non-diablo game since Grim Dawn.  The skill system is fantastic. it allows you to level up the 5 primary skills you use and each of the five classes will specialize into 1 of 3 masteries, essentially providing 15 class choices to playersThere is so much loot dropping in this game that you will have to use a loot filter to only show what you need. if you try to pick up and sell everything, you will be teleporting back to town every 5 minutes.Once you find your gear, you have access to a forge to further customize it. you can control the stats on the gear by removing stats from one piece and moving it to another. you can even reroll all the stats or just adding them if there are open slots. I've seen a lot of people claiming it's the best crafting in any ARPG and I am inclined to agree.The game does a good job at making you feel powerful without the game seeming boring or easy.Best thing is I'm not falling asleep while playing like I did with another ARPG that came out last fall.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just janky. It's another prime example why I am disappointed in the gaming industry as of late. Just unimaginative, janky, broken games coming out lately. With this game my friend and I was able to play, but the moment we had to Talk to Balthras, her door never opened. I tried exiting the map and back in I tried having just her go in and nothing changed. The door opened for me every time even if she was the one to walk to it.Now that's just one issue. The game has been in development for so long and I have watched it grow like another in these reviews, I have been so excited for this game to release, but I never expected the janky mess it is now. It should never have left early access. You use a controller and move your character, but if you touch your mouse the character continues running. My mouse happened to be hovering over the chat window and I couldn't attack. I could run but attacking was mute. Loot, there's way too much and not enough influence in your game play. For some reason the portal at one point wouldn't even come up.In all honesty, until this game is more refined I wouldn't touch it.  But of course that's my opinion
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: Last Epoch is a good game with great characters and a good skill and weapon system, but ultimately, I don't really like the gameplay itself.Many maps feel too edgy and lifeless to me, too "artificial" might be a better phrase, and especially the enemies feel - how shall I phrase it - too "artificially placed", coming at you again and again and again from the same places etc.. Somewhat hard to describe.I like Titan Quest / Grim Dawn / Diablo better, at least for the time being, which is somewhat of a shame, as Last Epoch does a lot "right" - but it still can't compete with games appearing more "fleshed-out" to me when it comes to actual gameplay.To put it in a single phrase: The actual "fighting" / "killing", which makes up the core gameplay of such ARPGs, seems like a chore to me in Last Epoch, while it can be "fun" in the mentioned other games. Especially Diablo has become quite good at this (no wonder, given Blizzard North's experience with that).No mixed review button, so I'm still voting for a 'Thumbs Up' for Last Epoch. It's certainly not a 'bad' game - (currently) just not as enjoyable as others in my view.

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok; not great but not particularly bad either. Not worthy of a thumbs up at this point IMO but not entirely deserving of a thumbs down. There are some drags to the gameplay; melee distance feels off (oftentimes enemies that look close enough to be hit are not being hit), leveling feels slow, normal mobs get one shot, elite mobs take 2-5 hits, and then bosses are damage sponges where your build doesn't seem to effect how much damage they take (most of the time you just spend 5 minutes strafing their attacks while you slowly whittle away at their huge hp bar), etc.The character talent tree is setup much like Grim Dawn with you selecting from a few talents which levels up your class unlocking more talents and skills but there are only 2 to 3 options to choose from per 5 levels or so. The skill talent trees are better but leveling is so slow that it feels like it takes forever to reach any sort of solid build. Your skills level up separately from your character level and can't go past your current level so you level up, choose your usually boring 3% stat improvement from the character skill tree, then wait until your skill levels up. Basically the pacing is geared towards late game with the beginning hours on a character being a monotonous grind. If I can force myself to play longer I'll update this review but it's hard to recommend when the beginning is so slow and boring. It seems very likely to be one of those "end game is where it gets good but it kind of sucks before that" games.[Edit] I've put in quite a few more hours now that it's been released. I wouldn't say the my previous review has really changed. It's still a slog to get through the campaign and leveling skills is still way too slow. It does have have some good QOL features but it doesn't change the gameplay overall. The late game 'Monoliths' are boring AF so you're pretty much limited to either doing them or running through the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ campaign on another character where the experience will barely be different then your last run...

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy ARPGs, this game is truly exceptional. The negative reviews mostly stem from individuals who seem inclined to complain about every minor detail, and some who lack a proper understanding of the development process. It's disheartening to witness comparisons between an indie company and industry giants like Activision Blizzard, with comments like "Diablo had a better launch." It's crucial to acknowledge the vast difference in resources and scale between a triple-A company and a smaller team of 80-90 people.The game is already impressive, and with time, I believe it will set new standards in the genre because the developers genuinely care about delivering an outstanding experience. It's unfortunate that, despite the dedication and passion poured into the project by the developers, there are toxic individuals who incessantly complain and cast negativity on their hard work. To the developers, thank you for your tireless efforts, and please continue your fantastic work.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: Far better, and far more satisfying, than Diablo IV. Do not get me wrong - there is a great deal of information a player should pay attention to in order to make the appropriate choices that fits their specific play style. There is nothing dumbed down about this game, however. Just consider Last Epoch the memory foam mattress of this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal contender in the ARPG genre. It is asthetically pleasing, brings a broad build diversity to the table and has an extremely fun and well-designed itemization and crafting system. Contentwise it's not (yet) fleshed out enough to topple the genre titan that is Path Of Exile - but as the 1.0 patch has just had its fresh release, more content is guaranteed to follow up shortly.Still, the endgame content is enough to keep you busy for a good amount of time well worth your money. For me personally, Last Epoch rests at a very comfortable 2nd place being light years ahead of titles like D4 which I wouldn't touch with a 10-ft pole. Also difficulty-wise, as many people have stated before me, it strikes a good balance between D4 (for people that literally possess no more than one singular brain cell) and PoE (which will take you multiple years of getting a grip on, speaking from experience).

_childDocuments_.review: Last Epoch is a wonderful arpg with lots of customization options for your characters. The classes are unique enough feeling to want to play them all, so the amount of replay ability is fantastic. While there are many, many skills to unlock and choose from on your build you use them 5 at a time, so its easy not to get overwhelmed. I re-mapped all of my skills to my mouse buttons and its fine to relax and play with one hand while your fending off parrots with your other hand.The things I wish were different are few, mostly just my laziness i'm sure. You can't fully respec once you start, so when you choose your secondary role, that's it, it can't be changed. So if you want to try all 3 classes for your mage you'll have to make 3 mages. While they are all slightly different in game play, that's still 3 mages you have to make if you want to try them all. With the level cap so high and taking a bit to get to, that can be a headache, but hey replay is replay. The other thing is itemization, specifically the unique ones, with some being so good for your build idea that they can gimp you if you get one at a lower level, because once its really out scaled you have to come up with a totally new build, and that's no fun. But those are really my only to gripes.The great stuff way makes up for that. The storage system is crazy good and customization is easy for it.  I've color coded most everything in mine cause I am just extra like that, but its nice to be able to know where things are quickly when trying new things. I also really love the way you can customize the items you see. at lower levels you won't need it as much, but when you start having loads of drops they can clutter your screen, but you can customize so much. I have a view profile for each character so that only things they can use are visible so i don'[t spend time emptying my bags of stuff i don't need. You won't see as many items highlighted, but the ones you see are the ones you'd keep anyway, more time killin baddies, less time sorting junk. And you can still have all items show up with a button push should you want to sort through junk. Overall I highly recommend it if you like arpgs, it won't let you down.

_childDocuments_.review: A small and rough gem searching for the sweet spot between accessibility and complexity in ARPG.(Edited after 200h) What is last Last Epoch?It's an ARPG without any modern identity crysis that make it transpass into other genre, but giving it’s original take on the formula never the less. What is it’s present state?It’s an early access, right and true. At the moment is a bit unpolished, and incomplete both in story and content.The development is quite slow and the updates are often hot mess in the first weeks after release.Is clearly a passion project from a small and inexperienced but passionate team that is slowly very slowly coming together. However, the it is already fun and can offer a honest amount of content for it’s price.Ok but it’s good?I think, yes. The combat is fun. Loot and skill system that are the core of this kind of games are solid and the game show great potential to be expanded. Settings and story is ok.  And already with it’s present content it can offer quite a bit of hours of gameplay but with a important caveat:the main campaign is short under 20h, but if this is not a dealbreaker for you, it’s a good thing. The main sources of the gameplay hours in this game are two: the end game, and the replayability.Making multiple character, is extremely fun, the build and gameplay diversity is very good in this game and the campaign is exactly of the right size forging and growing you character gliding between all the set pieces and enemy of the game and reaching the end game to put to test your build.A longer campaign could have been tedious ad would have hindered the replay ability . How it compares to Diablo and Path of Exile?It's less complex than PoE, but it’s not a bad thing, as it makes it more accessible and less difficult to return to, after a while. But it’s much more complex that Diablo so while it remains reasonably accessible, it give far more satisfaction customizing skills characters.It try to hit a sweet spot in complexity that is quite appealing to me, as I enjoy both Diablo and PoE but not without complans. It’s not able to stand against those two games on content or presentation however and It will never be, considering the speed of development. The gap will only grow.So to appreciate it, is important to understand what this game is aiming to.As I think it’s doing well what it try to do.For this reason I kept playing after a very rough star (and negative review) till this positive vote 200h of gameplay later.

_childDocuments_.review: Enough is enough. The constant disconnects every 10-15 seconds to 4-5 minutes of gameplay are just too much. This game has had this issue since day one, all through the first season. It got so bad that I gave up halfway through the leveling process.I came back to give this new season a try... and guess what? The same disconnect problem again. In about 5 hours of gameplay, I had more than 50-60 disconnects.And it's not just me. Lots of people have this issue. Just look at the official forums, Reddit, here on Steam, and so on. So many are looking for solutions, and the devs just don't seem to care about this bug. All you'll get from them are some generic tips that don't work, and it's not my job to fix their game.Fix your damn game. Fix your damn network code. Fix your servers. Or whatever is going on. If you can't fix it... then hire some experienced devs that know how to code. It's not my job to find workarounds when Last Epoch is the ONLY game causing issues. I have a way above average setup, the latest drivers installed, and a very stable fiber optic internet connection. I can play much more network-intensive games like PoE with zero disconnects over hundreds of hours of gameplay.So yeah, if you're one of the lucky ones that don't experience the disconnect issue... good for you. But for me (and probably thousands of other players), this is a huge issue and a big NO. Too bad Steam won't let me refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute love letter to ARPG fans. This game has control crispiness and performance optimization of Diablo 3, and meaningful end-game content of Path of Exile without having to alt-tab 12 times per map run and having to use 35 third party programs to make the game playable. I had heard many praises for this game and its systems before trying it out, so I went into it with almost unfair expectations. To my surprise they have all been vastly exceeded. "Quality of life" is an aspect of gaming that has been in consistent decline in the past decade, especially since the rise of the "crafting survival" meta. It seems like the developers purposefully make everything difficult to use and focus on making games as tedious as possible hoping it would result in meaningless supernumerary game time. Here, however, it is quite the opposite. You actually get to spend more time playing the video game than fighting the UI and the inventory system, and this is something I feel is deserving of the highest praise. On a slightly negative note, classes are gender locked. "Agility = girl" philosophy is getting a bit old.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is overall ok though, in hindsight I would not have purchased it. Wanted to play the necromancer but the character is a bit unlikable to me. First I did not know that you cannot customize the characters and they are gender locked. Secondly I figured ok maybe I'll try her out because it will be heavy story oriented. It looked that way but after making it to chapter 2 which is very early in the game the personal story seems to fall a bit flat on me for the necromancer. So I figured I'd give it another chance and try the Primalist as the archetype seemed interesting, and again the story seems fairly flat. Now the excuse for no customization seems to be "well D2 characters were gender locked and had no customization" and "well it would cost too much for an indie company to make 2 character models for each class". Ok, well first it would have been easy to have made a general male and female model with minor customization that could be use for all classes. As an example I would suggest Grim Dawn, you can play any class and combination of classes as either gender. This would allow for also slight customization and easier animation designs as you just need to worry about doing them per ability or model depending on similar casting actions.  As well they have at least 5 different voiced characters for each story, 3 male and 2 female. Well this could be simplified with the above type of customization with starting with just 2 male and 2 female voices and have them voice the character stories. I.E. if you choose Female voice 1 and play as a necro, all the story lines would be voiced in Female voice 1, if you make a new character and choose female voice 2 and play as a necro all the lines would be voiced as female voice 2. Simple customization which allows characters to feel unique, possibly save on design time, and allow for further additions later on in a modular form like adding new voices or models and abilities. Now concerning the story, I expected at least some small cinematic videos voiced by the character like in Diablo 3 between chapters. So far the only voice acting from my characters have been in the very beginning story cinematic and maybe like 2 or 3 lines. If your going to make a game gender locked, no character customization besides your character name, than please provide some decent story. It seemed so bland to me and nothing really stood out. I'm not expecting huge amounts of 3d cinematics with 4k depth that last like 10 minutes, simply some reason to like a character or understand the world. There have also been design decisions made solely via what groups prefer instead of offering simple customization to controls. I.E. the ability to force attack is kinda non existent in the game because your left click is always walk and can only be mapped to an attack already on one of your other 5 slots with the force stand key always being shift. Its not very intuitive compared to other games in the genre and I had to go looking why there was no force stand key mapping and found it wasn't desired by the "discord and reddit" groups. Instead of making something that can be mapped and allow for more versatility the very control structure is decided upon the "community" they decide to appease. I will say the game does seem to run smoothly and has a nice dark theme. Also the skill leveling system does seem interesting and was part of my original intrigue into the game. I do not want to disparage the design team or those that like this game but for me it takes interesting stories or at least letting me make my own like in Grim Dawn's choices. TL;DRGame works and looks good but no customization, bland story, and weird design choices.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The best arpg on the market period, but for some. If to you, D4 or POE are the perfect aprg, then you might not love Last Epoch. However, if D4 feels to shallow, and POE feels toxic in it's game design, then come aboard. Last epoch is already a fantastic game, and it is bound to get even better. Why? Because the developers follow an active strategy of listening to the community through polls, requests, Reddit crawling etc. And then they provide innovative game design ideas that answers the mentioned problems. E.g. The community is split between solo self found and a want for an auction house? They come up with a two faction system, attempting to balance them both for the same content. When do you release the season boss to legacy players? Make a poll, and follow what the majority want. This constant feedback loop coupled to great game design makes for a very promising future. In comparison to the other actors (I have a lot of time on D2, D3, little on D4, and too much on POE), Last epoch shows it wants to learn from the mistakes of the predecessors and deliver. It has the mechanical depth, the power curve, and builds you can explore. It provides both fun skills to play with when you start, and enough complexity you can create some truly insane end game builds with enough commitment. Coming from POE, I love that playing last epoch doesn't feel like being in an abusive relationship. POE players were regularly complaining about carpal tunnel syndrome on the forums, while Chris Wilson answer was that players should "feel the weight" of picking up hundreds of shards. Crafting items was straight up gambling where you could loose your progress, something LE addressed by having rng as a core mechanic while making sure it's hard to brick your item. I think some of the reason for the recent mixed reviews is the popularity of LE. It was iteratively building on a much smaller community the last few years, and it's full of great implementation (crafting, skills, etc). Problem is when your playerbase 7x overnight, and now your old core only represent 13%. And those new players are used to D4, wants free respec, don't like grinding a few hours for an item, etc. And others are used to POE and complain that it's not as complex or deep (ignoring POE has a bajillion seasons behind it, and it's LE first one).  I would strongly encourage people who have enough time to write extensive bad reviews about certain mechanics to go and read the updates and devlog on the reason for that mechanic. I can't believe I see people complaining about the added "shield mechanic making the boss spongy" when the total effective hp of the boss hasn't changed, it was just made more visible. Maybe there was a better way, but people clearly misunderstand and then misrepresent LE designers impact and intent. Same for "global trading limited to faction" completely missing the point of why it was made into a faction in the first place (which was to allow a concurrent playerbase between SSF and traders, even on the same character). Going back to pushing my current build, and then excited for the other ones I still want to try!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun, but there's a single mechanic really holding it back:Adaptive Damage Reduction. What is that? It's a function bosses have in which they just start to resist all your damage when you're doing "too much, too fast."To me, this is the antithesis of these types of games. It completely kills my motivation to grind for better items and builds because, well, the bosses are just going to ignore all of it and take a set amount of damage from you. If this single mechanic was removed, it would be a glowing recommendation from me. Excellent crafting, great build variety, and even decent graphics considering it's an indie ARPG. It's not quite D4 levels but it's more than serviceable.But all of that is squandered by the fact that bosses just don't give a flying ♥♥♥♥ about your stats. It's like an anime character that takes a punch, gets hurt heavily, but then gets back up and takes another without flinching because he gauged your power off of the first hit or something. It's fun as a story, not as a game mechanic. Sorely needs to be changed. Corruption is infinite already, why don't bosses just get harder and harder via that alone? Why do they need the extra help? So I can see the work the animators did or something? I just don't get it.

_childDocuments_.review: The campaign in incredibly fun, and the way Last Epoch has implemented build design and customisation is really well done. Where this game falls flat is the end game. Over time I'm sure they will add more content but for the the cycle becomes grind to find better gear then what do you do with better gear? You use it to grind for even better gear. There is no point in continuing once that becomes the cycle. You need things to test your builds on and currently I haven't found that. Doing Monoliths feels like an empty grind just to find better gear. If each one has a small story to follow I would feel like it was a lot more fun but currently it just feels like a chore to get through each one. Looking forward to seeing how they fix this issue in the future and will come back to Last Epoch when they do but for now I'm going to take a break.

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhere in between Diablo 3 and Path of Exile in terms of depth, pretty close to Grim Dawn. _childDocuments_.review: First time playing a Diablo-like. 2 things made me purchase the game: the adds on Second Wind and the Falconer class. I never tried any Diablo like before mainly because I feared getting addicted to them, just like I did with the grindfest known as Maplestory. The game itself was pretty fun, a lot more than I expected at least, though my view can be a bit skewed because as of now I've played in solo mode exclusively so I can't comment on the multiplayer experience, only on the gameplay and story.The story started kinda mixed for me, I didn't have a full grasp on what was happening, though I think it was kinda by design, giving the player time to focus on the fundamentals of combat. The story really picks up once the main gimmick gets introduced, and it works very well for most of the game. At some point it stopped working fully, but overall it was very much enjoyable.The gameplay followed a similar feel for me. First of all not being able to assign right click as movement huts my MOBA head, so I played with a gamepad. It took me a while to discover how to change my skills, and leveling passives was kinda clunky on controller. Apart from those initial gripes, once you start to specialize the gameplay opens up significantly, and making your own build becomes incredibly fun and engaging. The forge system was confusing at first but once I realized it was similar to VaultHunters it clicked for me, and it became enjoyable too. There still are a couple of things I have yet to fully grasp, but the gameplay in general is accessible enough that I feel like I don't need a guide to make thing work and make me want to try other classes out,So all in all I very much enjoyed this game, it has some things I wished it did better but I'd recommend it if anyone asked. I look forward to playing it with friends to see if my experience gets enhanced.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big PoE head and I have been eager for a second playable ARPG franchise and this is maybe going in that direction but perhaps not there. The levelling takes a lot from Grim Dawn but is much more playable and tactile in practice, gear is often interesting, combat is fairly fluid. Enemies tend to be pretty generic in practice where they get squished and you don't really have to think about them, but it's fun to move through them. It feels like challenge is ramping up as I go, which is welcome. The writing and voice acting are truly dismal unfortunately, and the visuals are pretty generic and feel a bit D3 like in terms of being edgy in that there are lots of spikes and gore on a brightly coloured lump. Overall I think this has managed to be the second best arpg but I don't expect I'll go through more than one run of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I gave this game a lot of my time and effort, so this is not being done out of spite. I had originally played about 300 hours in the Beta, through version 0.9.2, and uninstalled due to a number of unresolved issues, mainly revolving around overpowered Boss fights. So I waited...Now I started again with release 1.0, and was overwhelmingly happy with the progress the game had made. I had (7) viable builds, 2 of which that reached the Empowered Monoliths. I got a character to level 96, and felt that level 100 was actually in the cards.Then the dreaded first major patch came out. While I knew from the postings by EHG that there were some nerfs to builds, I was cautiously optimistic that it would not be as bad as Diablo IV's first major "correction". What an effing disaster. Monsters that used to be afterthoughts were one-shotting high-level characters, formerly "normal" fights were taking 3-4x as long, drop rates for good gear became abysmal.Now, don't get me wrong. There were a lot of positives in the 1.0 and subsequent 1.1 releases, but not enough to overcome the other problems that came with them. Like so many other software updates this massive, they introduced more bugs than they fixed.Maybe I'll try again in a year or two.

This game has memory leak, its unbelievable how bad performance gets just 1-2 hours after playing. You need to restart the game often. Also many classes just LAG. and there is no real fix (Torment warlock for example is insanely laggy)If you thought poe trading is bad, then look no further to last epoch trading, its such a horrendous experience i cant begin to describe, not to mention BILLIONS of gold duped for the second league in a row.gameplay is very shallow, unbalanced, floaty animations, unresponsive (even if you play offline lol)Last epoch's campaign is insanely boring, and you cant really just zoom through it. _childDocuments_.review: What Eleventh Hour Games managed to create for version 1.0 with less than 100 employees compared to Diablo 4's (frankly insane) 9000 people is very impressive indeed.As many people have pointed out, the complexity is a perfect mix of the simplicity of Diablo 4 with the complexity of Path of Exile - both games I've played a lot of. For me personally, the complexity of PoE's many systems oftentimes scares me away from engaging with it, instead opting to sell materials and currency and instead buy my gear. Compare that to  where I have engaged heavily with the crafting system because it is very easy to understand but still has a good amount of depth and room for optimization and chase items. Making your own items instead of buying them is fun!🟢 What I love- Great crafting system that is easy to understand but complex enough to get addicted to- Several fleshed out endgame systems that connect to each other, making all/most of them relevant for all characters- A loot system which manages to make even blues and rares exciting- A built-in loot filter which is easy to set up, modify, and use🔴 What can be improved- More engaging content when running Monoliths (equivalent to maps in PoE)- More endgame challenges such as bosses to really test your builds- Set items seems largely irrelevant at the moment- Graphical fidelity is not as impressive as Diablo 4With a price tag of less than 35€,  is to me a no-brainer for any ARPG fan. I strongly recommend it! 👍

_childDocuments_.review: A fine ARPG and a solid entry into the genre. There are a variety of quality-of-life changes that I really appreciate. Not having to do repeated inventory trips to town, easy respecs, built-in item filters, and stash management are only some.The skill customization is varied enough to support a variety of builds. However, some skills are lacking in cohesion or synergy with their own classes.Item crafting is less of a chore, and really allows you to guide the progression of item rolls without entirely removing the RNG aspect. It's a good balance between binary, flat crafting systems and true RNG rolls.Class balance is a bit weak at the moment, but that will improve over time.The story is a bit below average, which is unfortunate.End game is fine, but doesn't do anything different than other ARPGs of the same type.Overall, I give Last Epoch a 6/10.Below Path of Exile, Grim Dawn, Diablo 2, Inquisitor: Martyr, and Wolcen.Above Diablo 3 and 4, Lost Ark, Torchlight 2, Van Helsing, and Titan Quest.

_childDocuments_.review: As of this 1.1 patch, I cannot continue to play this game.Granted I have only about 140 hours in the game, so there might be mechanics that I do not understand. But I do feel like the game is not as fun as it was in beta patches. I have played through some of the beta patches, autobomber voidknight in 0.8, cold dot werebear in 0.9, both builds were fun with great movement, clear, and damage.I decided to give the developers 1 season to iron things out so I skipped the 1.0 release, but this 1.1 season is lacking the fun that I use to have. Among other minor things, there is one major thing I am failing to comprehend, why giving us 2 dashes but 4-5 bars of health as ward to the bosses? Do the developers expect us, playing a loot-based game, hitting the boss until it goes to ward phase, and just go "Oh, I am going to use my dashes to dodge the attacks while I wait for the ward to go away."? This new ward thing on bosses, and even some rare mobs in monoliths, is making the speedy map clear way less enjoyable that it use to be.This playthrough also reminded me why I stopped playing in the first place. This might be my skill issue, but Lagon and the snake-woman boss in Act 9 of the campaign always give me a hard time. When the snake-woman goes to second phase and just start to charge you right in the face, and if you don't kill her fast enough she can heal back to full health twice? It might just be me but I feel like the difficulty level can be toned down just a tad bit.One more nick-picking thing I have is the game does not encourage me to roll new characters. The game provides 0 incentives, and putting the grind of the entire campaign and normal monoliths on you all over again. Granted it is still faster than POE, as an example, but that is not saying much.Finally, some optimization issues. Server has problems, disconnects happen sometimes. Character animation is weird, if you click to move and wiggle your mouse just bit by bit, you can see your character moon walk, probably fun to some people, bad animation design in my opinion.Anyway, 5.5/10, hope the game gets better, hope the developers realize that keeping players actively playing can sell more cosmetics, instead of pushing them away with frustrating game design.Update: after 40 more hours my opinion about the game is still not changed.Update 2: Making some comments about the endgame gameloop.Gear is easy to farm up to 80-90%, if you want the gg gear it is very hard to get any upgrade. If you are playing MG you can just buy the upgrades but CoF is really a spin on the wheel.Dungeons feel not rewarding, Hellfire dungeon is the worst one, followed by Lightless Arbor, and Temporal Sanctum. Lightless Arbor is not enjoyable if your build has 0 dodge.Mapping feels terrible, there is no target farm, there is no guaranteed drop, CoF prophecies help but mapping 1-2 hours just to be able to afford 20~25 drops of the gear you want? Also some of the maps feels terrible, you want to be blasting and zooming and not be stuck on some ramdom pebbles on the ground.Also heard that there was a money glitch on MG this cycle, who would've thought.I will play again in 1.5
