_childDocuments_.review: Summary first: Yes No Yes No Yes. (Version 1.0)The good: I really love it. Gameplay is smooth, fun and impactful. Skills and Items are complex, but understandable. The story is ok and gives a decent intro to the endgame mechanics. Crafting is a necessity, and gives you great possibilities to modify items. Lots of skills, skill trees, unique items and sets. It´s fun to play into the endgame with any character. I´ve done three classes and specialisations.The Meh: Class balance in the endgame is bad. Some just stomp and have obvious paths to stompiness, others rely on very specific items, skill combinations and stat rolls on specific items. Want to play a Meteor Sorcerer? Well, good luck. Defenses are a bit weird and need to be layered. Some are easy to raise because the specific enchantments are easy to find. Others are more complex and hard to grasp. Damage mitigation to mana after armor, resistance and endurance (three different things).Crafting has a lot of RNG. Items have crafting potential, which an enchantment draws upon. Sometimes upgrading or adding an enchantment uses 1 or 2 potential. Sometimes 20. So with only a little bit of bad luck, you brick an item with perfect stats, except one which you want to remove or change. Well ...Crafting needs Runes and Glyphs. But tbh, most of those are pretty useless. Some are really important. Could be better.The Bad:Dungeons are bad. You die, you reset the dungeon. Which is a PITA with one shot mechanics from bosses which you have to learn first, or watch a couple of hours of YT videos. Also you have to find keys first. Those are not too uncommon though, but still.Unique Items often feel stupid, as some builds require you to wear really low level items with bad implicit stats. Sometimes it feels like a punishment to wear a specific unique.Set items are almost universally useless. They don´t have the legendary mechanic which can make unique items really powerful. They are good to level up with, mostly, but will be replaced soon. They sound fun, but arent.LAG. LAG. Ok, Everyone said it, servers are wonky. But having sudden lag spikes during aforementioned boss fights with one shot mechanics? Ridiculous. No it´s not my ISP. Every other game runs fine. This is a buzzkill, especially when running a dungeon.But I still recommend the game. It´s great fun, just watch a video about which classes are the oldest in the game, and avoid them. They fall off in power compared to the more recent ones. A lot.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has had so many issues.  It's still janky.This has been touted as "between Diablo and PoE", I'd say more between Grim Dawn and PoE, but close enough.  It is fun.  It's great fun.  The endgame difficulty loop is well thought out.  The graphics are great if pretty stereotypical theme wise.  The fact you can see synchronicity in the skill trees without spending an hour in a third party program yet has a much deeper system than say, the Diablo games is awesome.  The deterministic crafting and farming is probably the best idea in the game.  The Lead Dev was in chat the other night answering questions... AMAZING.HOWEVER...  I bought it two years ago.  There's still three masteries that are in the U/I but haven't been implemented, and since they synergize with the other class masteries, those entire classes are essentially unfinished.  The main campaign is still unfinished (No, I don't play PoE for the lore either, but still).  Trade wasn't introduced in multiplayer.  It's still somewhat buggy overall.Making games of this scope (this really has the hallmarks of a AAA arpg, even thought it's a smaller developer) are hard, time consuming, and I imagine bloody expensive.  I'm sympathetic to that.  But rather than introduce the interesting dungeon concept, or as the Lead Dev alluded to new monolith (endgame) features, I'd rather see them polish up and finish the things that were already announced before they move onto the next feature.  Even scrolling down the page, you'll see they did weekly Devcasts (Great!) with charities (Great!) but then the "weekly" became monthly with "weekly" still in the title, which looks kind of sloppy.  I feel they overcommit and hope this is addressed within.I loved D2, I enjoy the mindless couch game of D3, I enjoy the throwback feel and class system of Grim Dawn. PoE is without a doubt my favorite arpg, though I skip a league every once and awhile because of the sheer amount of playtime it requires with all it subsystems.  This game could easily replace all other arpgs combined to fill my arpg itch between PoE playtime IF they are more focused.The game itself could end up being a fantastic arpg for all levels of players, I just feel they need to tighten up, finish up and polish the existing systems before moving onto the next thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of potential but needs some work. This game lands somewhere between Diablo and Path of Exile in complexity, but it is rough around the edges. It has one of the best take on crafting I have seen, but the flip side is getting a great base/unique for SSF in the end game can be a real grind, and unless you join the merchant faction that is the only way to improve. The story is nothing special and just kinda ends but it is more of a game tutorial than anything else. The end game has a pretty cool idea with the 10 monoliths you can use to target farm gear and blessings which help with armor, resistance, etc..., letting you use more offensive minded gear. The problem is each monolith has an independent difficulty scale called corruption so you have grind to a boss and get a drop to add 12 corruption than find another boss in the monolith to add if your lucky another 15 corruption. Now you can stack the 12 corruption drops 4 times so if you are patient you can go up 65 corruptions levels before you reset the monolith to the higher difficulty. Than you have to do the same for the other 9 monoliths with a catch up mechanic that helps a little but its's a grind. Finally the best blessing you can get require a 200 corruption level monolith so you will be just grinding that for a long time. Lastly the monolith boss battles are not pleasant, some of them shrink the arena down and make it hard to maneuver, and most have a one shot kill with a large hit box on your character or do Damage Over Time another death sentence unless you mitigate it. I would not recommend this game at full price but on a sale it is worth it, also if you have burnt out on POE, Diablo or Grim Dawn. I enjoyed on balance the time I put into, and will come back in the next cycle to see what improvements have been made, I wish there was more nuance in the recommendation for choice as I agree with yes but with reservations this is more of a 7/10 game but the potential is there to get it higher.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a few things that still need updating. Monolith echoes that reward gold, for instance, are still very underwhelming. They do not scale with difficulty and the time spent in the echo makes them feel like a waste. One of the dungeons, lightless arbor, allows you to spend accumulated gold to increase loot rewards after completion. This system consumes huge amounts of gold, and the grind to get more is severe. The quest experience and gold rewards are also lackluster and often feel insulting. The developers also show a startling amount of favoritism to the builds they enjoy in their personal play of the game, and that is minion based builds. Perhaps their next big update will address some of these issues. That said, it is a fun game and they have the best loot filter system in any ARPG I've ever played. Their personal stash space, search, and sorting functions are second to none. With some more polish, completion of incomplete features (such as the rune mage mastery for the mage class) and some needed attention to non-minion builds and unique items, this game will really shine. They're a small team, but they do a lot of work and seem receptive to feedback from players.

_childDocuments_.review: Really tried to love this game. Got two characters to 90+ (one pre-launch) and dove into the endgame but it's a poorly balanced, boring, buggy mess. Character progression feels good during the campaign. Your character grows in level and power pretty consistently as the game progresses. Once you reach the endgame, things fall off of a cliff. The endgame systems as they exist today are extremely shallow. Arena is extraordinarily tedious, the dungeons are mostly not worth doing, and empowered monoliths are a complete slog with highly inconsistent difficulty unless you've been blessed with insane RNG or are using a completely broken build. They are an attempt at the mapping system from POE but actually fall closer to the nightmare dungeons that plague D4 to this day.There are a ton of technical issues that are still affecting the game post-launch. Tons of stuttering, ongoing latency issues, and countless skill bugs really drive-home the fact that this game probably needed another year of early access and polish before launching. There is a good game in here somewhere, and with EHG committed to providing free updates for the forseeable future, I hope they're able to turn it around. As it stands though, I can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Great class design and skill trees. Very well done. -Good itemization-Nice crisp graphics-Fun boss fights that aren't too hard or too easyCons: -Gender locking.  Dear GOD I hate gender locking in any RPG game.   Wanna be a female Druid? Too bad.  Wanna be a male Necromancer? NOPE.  Soz. -The world doesn't feel "persistent".  The entire world just feels like a series of instanced dungeons separated by waypoints with the associated load times for each little area you zone to.  It's janky and the zones are so small.  Diablo 2 did better with the world feeling persistent.  AND...-Tying in with the above point: You leave an item on the ground because your bags are full, then go back to town to sell, return back? Yeaaaa that item vanishes.  The world really IS just a series of temporary instances without any persistence.  I absolutely hate that.   -Some of the skill/spell animations are amateur and unsophisticated, needing a good bit of polish and distinction. -When I play offline, I don't want to see chat from other people.  I don't want to have to turn off chat AFTER choosing "Offline play".  It should automatically do that. -The story is a convoluted confusing mess.  The dialogue from NPCs should be presented in bigger windows rather than sentence per sentence per sentence that you have to click through to get where you can accept or turn in a quest.   -Going with the above point, I don't really care what any of the NPCs have to say.   I feel like the writing isn't the most fleshed out aspect of the game. -Leveling feels really, really slow after picking up my Mastery.  -Losing skill points for respeccing is a heinous, stupid thing to do to people especially since leveling builds aren't at all in the same class as endgame builds.  Get rid of that crap.-Gambling and reforging costs too much.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good arpg,I played PoE alot, mostly on console but it took me alot of time to learn everything I know today, this game however is much easier to understand on the surface level while still being complex enough. What I really wanna point out is one of the crafting mechanics called Legendary potential, it basically allows you to slap a rare item onto the Unique item of the same type and Unique will have all the Rare item affixes and suffixes added on top of what it already has. This allows you to pretty much play with any unique you want without worrying that its too weak for endgame etc. At the moment the game lacks end game, if you want to min-max there is alot to do still. _childDocuments_.review: Edit:  Online play at release was not-functional, which relegated it to solo offline only.  This has since been fixed along with the excessive transition times when changing zones.  Originally not recommended.As of 3/14/24:  This is a slight recommendation based upon my experience thus far.Pros:  Decent graphics.  Very good loot filtering system.  Many skills per class which can each be customized using a tree similar to POE passive tree (but smaller and with some more impactful changes), so there feels like there is a decent amount of build variety.  Leveling feels decently fast up through level 50.Cons:  Game feel is a bit off (skill feedback, lackluster death animations).  Most of the game has no challenge, with a huge difficulty spikes on a couple bosses.  Even elites while leveling usually die in a hit or two.  Grim Dawn and some other ARPGs would have some elites which while didn't take forever would at least stick around a bit making dots and other non-direct damage effects a bit more useful.  This may change at high level, but up through 60 this was my experience so far which made it a bit boring.  Just like D4, the camera is super zoomed into your character which renders range less useful (although not as big of a deal here because of the aforementioned super quick kill times in this game).  Also, especially in the beginning there are very small zones with frequent loading transitions which just makes the game feel a bit cheap to me.  Story is servicable but meh...and "choices" mean nothing...you get the same dialogue no matter what you choose which makes the choice stupid and pointless.  Story doesn't finish.  Some classes missing skills.Overall:  A decently fine ARPG but nothing special.  May improve with future updates as apparently it was released incomplete despite being labeled 1.0.  Lukewarm thumbs up for now.

Yeah you can get unique with more LP, but it doesn't fundamentally change the way you play your character or provide a big power spike (think HH or MB in POE). With that said, it is worth the $35, but I dont think the game will last in it's current state.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Games great, multiplayer is getting there, squirrels love nuts.So, Ive owned the game since before the latest multiplayer patch, it was great then and its even better now theres multiplayer.Dont be fooled, there are still bugs and game play issues that are being ironed out with multiplayer however it is still in beta and what they have so far is a really solid base to work off.The devs are actively listening to players and hotfix's are currently coming thick and fast.Gameplay wise:Class builds are amazing, all classes feel completely different to the next and class skills can also massively change the playstyle and feel of your character - best part is you can respec with relative ease.Content is good especially as its still in beta. You have a choice of 10 monolith timelines at end game as well as dungeons/arena's. Loot is as you would expect, EVERYWHERE. Prepare yourself to have a vault rammed with uniques, purples, keys, relics and all sorts of other loot. Nice thing here is that you can buy stash tabs for in game cash that will increase in price with each one.Grouping in multiplayer is fun - albeit there are a number of desync issues affecting some players currently. Multiplayer allows you to gift items to other players that were in the zone when the item dropped, so its not fully free trade which im still deciding if i like or not.As you can see from my gametime, i like the game and would have recommended it before multiplayer went live. With a lot of Arpg's on the market and a big name one on the horizon, Last Epoch is a nicely made balanced game that you cant go wrong with and makes a nice change of pace and  scenery from PoE, Diablo franchise.Oh.....and theres something special about having an army of squirrels doing your bidding! I cant help but find myself constantly shouting: "Go for the nuts..."

_childDocuments_.review: There is a great diversity in this game! For me as someone who likes to experiment with builds, this is a great way to keep your attention. However, this seems to not be the case for Last Epoch, because you have certain goals set even after the campaign ending, which are related to the story itself.Soo, looking forward to see what would be the continuation of it.The only negative is the servers state currently, which probably would be resolved in time.This should not stop you of playing the game at all, because even if you got disconnected while progressing in some dungeon, it does not take that much time to run it again or get a key for it(at least on lower levels).

_childDocuments_.review: Overall an enjoyable experience for anyone with moderate ARPG experience.  System complexity is no where near that of PoE, but more complex than let's say Diablo 3.  Itemization is decent, though exalted items can add a tremendous amount of power (build enabling in some cases), so there is going to be some imbalance there.  End game min maxing requires significant hours of grinding, however thanks to deterministic unique drops, you can ultimately grind to play any build.  Fun overall and worth the price point especially since it seems there will be content updates throughout the life of the game.The biggest issue is with bugs and campaign pacing.  The campaign pacing isn't a huge deal since once you get past it you don't have to touch it again, but the game would benefit with a 30-50% area reduction in some zones.  It can be a slog.  The bugs are pretty bad as well.  If you play a primalist for example, be prepared to have to reset your skill bars multiple times per play session in some instances.  I am sure the devs are working on these issues, but the game has been in EA for a long time now and more polish is expected.**Looks like since writing this they have fixed many bugs which is noticeable**

_childDocuments_.review: Last Epoch is truly setting the new standard of ARPG’s in my opinion in certain fronts. People say this and that about others, Diablo 2, PoE, etc. but LE truly is that “just right” type game for me. I think that EHG is truly just trying to deliver a fun game at a reasonable price point without forced or highly incentivized micro-transactions, something you won’t find in most games today.In addition to that, the game is just straight up fun. There’s RNG elements that feel so rewarding once you get the right roll and a true progression system that you feel as you’re putting together your build. That leads to another point, the resources the game gives you for all of the mechanics in the game is put together so well. Truly I’ve never seen a tool tip as thorough as LE’s. I don’t think I’ve ever left a review on any game before, but I just had to for LE. It’s a great game, I highly encourage you to try it if you’re on the fence!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews. This is probably the first one in the years I've been on Steam. For the past few years the constant AAA money-grab games have really caused me to lose faith in the gaming industries ability to develop and produce games for gamers. Last Epoch has reminded me there ARE developers who want to make good games. Is it a perfect game? No, I don't think those can exist, however the difference in intent between this and other modern games, most closely comparable being Diablo IV, is night and day. This game is fun, unique, and designed to be played, not spend money on micro-transactions. Yes the launch week servers struggled. The devs have been so open and communicative to the point of telling people to wait to buy until the game is in a state to be enjoyed properly. I'd say that those issues have been 80% resolved, and are only improving daily. If you are like me and have lost faith in games being good anymore, give this one a try. To the developers at EHG, thank you for making this. It truly is a pleasure to play. I wish you the best and can't wait to see the success this game becomes, driven solely on its merits of being a fantastic game to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely the most promising casual arpg at the moment. The online functionality needs some work but it is improving every single day. Offline plays absolutely perfectly and I would recommend it if you aren't interested in coop or trading. The amount of build diversity and player choice in this game is amazing and you are not punished for not following a meta build. The game has a reasonably complex crafting system that actually requires you to plan out and put thought into crafting god roll items. The endgame systems are also incredibly solid, however they do get somewhat tedious after a while. The devs are extremely vocal and active and have already outlined their plans over the next few seasons to add various new endgame activities and improvements. This game launched with nearly perfect systems and class design and only really struggles endgame with a minor lack of content. This is not the same as diablo 4, which launched with awful systems and no endgame content. This game will only get better and the devs have already proved themselves to be competent. Definitely recommend if you like arpgs even a little bit, it's one of if not the best I've played in years.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, 10/10 - would recommend to any ARPG fan.This review is from a player that likes necro/minion army builds in arpgs and played a month in early access before the official launch.  #1 a "sick'em" button (A by default as I recall [I've switched it to another key since] to send your army to a spot/enemy), #2 loot filter - for me, arpgs are about loot and searching for those upgrades in certain areas to get stronger over time, so the ability to not see the things that are not relevant to me is very very handy.  I can't believe D4 a) didn't launch with that and b) still hasn't addressed that, #3 great itemization and crafting - as has been said many times elsewhere about crafting here, "easy to learn, hard to master" - want to jack up an existing good item?  can do - use the plentiful runes and glyphs that drop by just regular playing and you can also obtain by breaking down items to upgrade most any gear you want - #4 separate idol inventory on your character for flexible buffs - swap in  resists, damage buffs, etc. as needed for a specific boss fight or whatever without taking up regular inventory space with charms like D2 - #5 seemingly unlimited stash space that is easily organized into categories with labels and so on (I've seen somewhere it is actually limited to 200 tabs or something, but I'm nowhere near that and can keep many things for later crafting or fight needs or whatever. #6 great gameplay - this isn't really last in priority for me because it's really just table stakes to be in the arpg game, but the controls are responsive, the gameplay is crisp, the action is fast, etc.Regarding the launch situation.  I was travelling the week of launch so I naturally didn't play right away and missed a lot of the server issues.  That said, when I returned, I still experienced the disconnects and long queues to reconnect.  I endured them because I already knew what the game was and really enjoyed it having played a month or so in early access.  When I couldn't connect, I just did something else.  It sucked when I was excited to build a new character and check out the new stuff from 0.9x or whatever it was the month before to 1.0, but as I write this a week or whatever later after launch, things seem to be working pretty well and I'm having a lot of fun.  So for me, the server stuff was an expected and annoying blip that didn't change my opinion of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Good ARPG, lots of options but definitely more simplified than Path of Exile. Much easier to get into, great amount of depth and has a lot going for it. I can see this game being an ARPG pillar in the future much like PoE. However, due to this being an indie company and a fairly newer game, there are some issues.Enemy damage: Some mob types have overtuned damage and will delete your character even with proper defenses and tankiness.Endgame: Fairly straightforward and not much to do other than run maps and do dungeons. Looking forward to future iterations of endgame though.Crashing and memory leaks/losing progress. A rare issue that I have not personally experienced, but has been reported on occasion.Jank: The game's animations have been vastly improved from what I have been told, but there is still some jankiness with bugged animations after changing forms.Lag and disconnects: These don't cause a loss in progress but may be inconvenient especially when playing in a dungeon that uses up a key and does not refund it if you get disconnected or crash. The lag will also often get you killed as you rubber-band back into an enemy's attack, so building tank at the moment is a priority for progressing endgame. I expect the server issues to be fixed eventually, and considering this was an indie company that just recently rolled out multiplayer, I would say comparatively that it's been going really well.Overall: 8/10 with lots of future potential. Could eventually be an alternative to PoE and Diablo but at the moment you will have to deal with some jank and bugs/issues. I consider them growing pains, however if you are looking for a polished experience like PoE or D2R/D3 you will not really find any ARPG's that can rival them at the moment.Considering the poor launch of D3, and the early days of PoE, this game is off to a MUCH better start and can become the ARPG that everyone flocks to in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Last Epoch is a diablo-style ARPG that is close to rivaling the scope of the big players in the genre like Diablo 3, Path of Exile, and Grim Dawn. It is content-incomplete (campaign not finished, missing unique items, some missing specializations), feature-incomplete (there is multiplayer now, but no trade yet), and quality-inconsistent. However the upward trajectory of the game is undeniable. The increase in quality of things like voice acting, art, 3D models, enemy design, responsiveness/feel of skills, and class depth has been ramping up in a big way. Most of the game has a new coat of paint and it makes a big difference.  Normally when a project suffers from scope creep the way this one does, the result is a buggy mess that is nothing more than undelivered promises. But I'm here to say that this game is the exception, and good enough to enjoy right now IMO, and there's many reasons to feel optimistic about the game's future.The best aspect of the game, the big reason Diablo fans need to play the game. This game bucks the trend of class-agnostic progression and doubles-down on making players commit to specializing in a unique class, using skills that evolve in more interesting ways than changing skill runes in Diablo 3 or slotting in support gems in POE. Do these restrictions limit the number of possible builds? Technically, but it doesn't feel like it since it allows the design of skill interactions to synergize with each other in more clever and hand-crafted ways. This means whatever build you do develop is NOT going to regress into the infamous 1-button spamathon that is every other class-agnostic ARPG.To accomplish this, the game has a meticulously crafted skill tree for each and ever skill in the game that you will level up separately from your character. The passive nodes in these skill trees often directly relate to other skills available to the class you're playing, and these interactions create meaningful layers of choice both in your build and, . This game wants you to use your whole skill bar all the time and it does a better job than any other ARPG I've played, and I am constantly making new characters. I have played the majority of masteries in the game and I am constantly imagining what each of them would be like if I built differently. Even among every specialization there are many viable ways to play. I am just super impressed overall with the dedication and depth to each playable class, this game will ruin you if you are an altoholic.This didn't used to be pretty game. In fact there used to be two paragraphs here talking about how ugly and slow the game ran. This multiplayer update they release optimized the game more than I've ever seen a game be optimized. The game looks literally twice as good in many places, their new artists are producing significantly better assets, and they've worked a lot of expensive shaders to use deffered rendering. Despite all the visual improvements, the game actually runs 50% faster than it used to on my machine. Auto HDR works now, the new composer is doing a great job with the new music tracks added, and many skills have revamped behavior that feel so much better. This game actually feels good to play now and isn't being carried by it's deep customization alone.Unfortunately, before this update I had said that this game virtually no major bugs. Unfortunately, the switch to server authority has put a dent in that. The past couple days there've been a ton of bugs making the game feel more like a beta than it did back when I first started playing. It's only been a couple days and they've been tracking things well so hopefully they'll be able to deliver fixes for that.The rough edges on the campaign got filed down in a big way this update, and it feels like a more cohesive experience than it used to. There is actually a story here with some voice acting that's been touched up big time. The campaign is also skippable in several places, if your alternate characters are strong enough to beat the dungeons, they can skip large parts of the campaign and get to endgame more quickly.I really like the endgame currently, it offers a lot of ways to target loot and a lot of decisions to make about what zone to run and what nodes to chase, but they're not so complicated that setting it up requires you to stop playing the game to craft maps or something. The monolith system right now is a whole lot better than D3, and a whole lot less complicated than PoE, That doesn't necessarily means it's lacking in depth, although it could still be better. Outside of the monoliths, you have the high tier dungeons that offer unique, bespoke rewards, and an endless arena to push online leaderboards.All of these activities have exclusive uniques to chase, but the chase doesn't stop there. Ultimately the goal is to ascend the best uniques to legendary by actually combining them the best rare items you can muster and get the best of both worlds. This system is, IMO, a big stand out in the genre, and creates a ton of wild possibilities for late-game itemization that is super deep without being an unintuitive cluster ♥♥♥♥ of remote probabalistic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. - controller support is a big plus but you can't aim with the right analog stick and that's a big problem-  In-game UI and documentation are good, but could be better. A lot of subskills and obscure status effects still lack sufficient in-game explanation.- No item linking in chat yet, coming soon in hotfix with other fixes- There is an offline mode you can play if the servers die- Entire game is playable coop, but the coop rules for certain activities like dungeons still feel like a first draft. If you die in a dungeon, you are essentially removed from your team and cannot play with them until they either finish it or die. This is terrible design IMO.- Regular item crafting is useful and accessible at all stages of the game and won't brick your items out of the blue.- I really don't have much bad to say about this game, it's in a damn good spot right now and I believe it's going to be among the cream of the crop by time 1.0 rolls around, even with major AAA competitors around the corner.

_childDocuments_.review: Its okay.  Its short right now but it be expected for early access. I want to see them add something like d3 goblins where they're semi rare, but you feel the dopamine when you see one and kill it.... but when you see a horde of them the adrenaline kicks in. New UI for conversations, animations are a nice add, some new sub classes, overall performance updates but most importantly the introduction of multiplayer.  While I have not had the opportunity to test multiplayer, the option is finally there. I'm also pretty excited about the APM, depending on your build.  I decided to try a druid and I'm switching between different forms, keeping my buffs up and each time I switch theres a new hot bar of new skills and I enjoy how base skills in human form intertwine with the animal forms. I'm pleased with learning my errors as the game is forgiving with correcting them and the game makes you think of your build and actions instead of being mindless by pushing 1 button. I'm excited to see where this brand goes and depending on end game this could be an easy contender for diablo 4.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried this and man, I wanted to like it. My first impression is this thing looks genuinely awful. Diablo Immortal, which can be played on phones, looks better.Than comes their business practices. I'm not one for like, researching developers. But what I noticed is they dropped a huge patch revamping Act 1 the day after I bought this game. What actually occurred is they added the micro transaction shop, and made towns a hub-like area like most games already do. And their inability to do this caused them to softlock literally everyone for hours out of the game until reverting their hub-town experience. New characters were stuck until logging and redoing the tutorial, and old characters were just unable to log in. There is constant rubberbanding every few seconds. Literally constantly. Movement skills are impossible to use and feel janky, and overall the game feels bad. It feels like it's meant to be a phone game with 3.5 stars on Google Play. Not an actual PC game. Can't even make it to endgame at this rate, as it's a true and honest gamble on whether going between zones will send you back to character select. And the worst part is the community seems to be totally okay with this. I can't see how anything will change when nobody is willing to say "Hey, you shouldn't hide behind early access forever as a justification for a bad product." I already know I'm not missing much though, the entirety of Act 1 has been the same temple tileset with purple corrupted roots everywhere. I enjoy lore in games, even PATH OF EXILE lore. I couldn't get into this though.Do NOT even try to play this with someone else. The D/C inbetween zones goes from 25/75 to probably 80/20. Sad part is the combat is ARPG combat, which I enjoy and is hard to get wrong, so I could find myself liking it. But not in this state. You should feel bad for charging people money for this. If that was my livelihood and what I expected to feed my family, I'd be embarrassed and anxious simultaneously.Update: With 1.0 announced I tried this game again. _childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: The Devs have decided to do microtransactions and a cosmetic store for the game, so clearly they've given up. Seriously, don't support this dev...So I've been playing this for a bit and have tried out all of the five classes a bit. Some of them are really weak and some are absurdly powerful. I do think that as a game in a genre full of great games (PoE & Diablo), I expected it to at least have learnt a bit from its predecessors, but it somehow seems to have failed to understand what quality of life features are, since every sort of management is a chore and there's very little customisation, but what to me really makes this a "not recommend" is that, despite having been in early access for 4 years, the game has an incredible amount of bugs and lack of balance (skills / characters). Any skill that involves teleporting seems to come with a high chance of teleporting into the scenery, especially stuff like the Sentinel's skills that allows him to teleport back to a prior location. Some characters, like the Beast dude, have skills that put them in a literal t-pose. Like... seriously?The story is one that quickly lost me, which seems to be a common trend for games in this genre, since the gameplay loop is very antithetical to a standard narrative design from other games. Instead of learning from the passive storytelling of other games in this genre, like PoE which did it really well, it just becomes a side-feature and you stop really caring why you're doing anything.The gameplay loop also quickly becomes quite boring. The main drive of a game like this is gearing up, but after just a few hours, you start to realise that most stuff is basically useless, and your time is better spent killing than looking through loot that 9 times out of 10 is worse than what youve had for the last few hours. I also really couldn't tell if item levels mattered and ended up getting past lvl 50 without changing out of some rare items I found that were like level 10 at most... Honestly a very nonsensical system.There is a bit of intrigue in trying out different skill specialisations, but most are either broken, incredibly weak, or just plain unimaginative. They all generally follow the same trends of "this skill now does x element instead of default element as damage". The most interesting skills were those of the Acolyte / Necromancer, but playing that character quickly becomes the least engaging gameplay possible, as you're incentivised to have minion skills on all available action slots.After playing for about 15 hours I started trying out co-op, and it really doesn't aid the game much, other than giving you someone to make fun of the terrible bugs and design decisions with.All around not a game i'd recommend, even if you're looking for something scratch the itch left by Diablo and PoE, because there are better clones that actually ensured their gameplay loop and core features were well-crafted.I still can't believe how long this game has been in Early Access and yet feels like an early beta. Pretty wild

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a good base but it is full of bugs, GAME BREAKING bugs. Hits don't register on monsters as if code wise they are not located where the model is displayed. It seems to me that sometimes even though I dodge out of the AoE telegraph, the damage still gets me. Monster HP sometimes is not displayed. Sometimes clicking on the quests in the main map does not redirect you to the area where you have to teleport and you have to look for it manually which can be very confusing as the map does not have a clear logic for the level progress. Items inside the inventory have their borders coloured as per rarity but the colours are so dim that it is very hard to distinguish which item is what rarity. _childDocuments_.review: After ~400 hours in the game, I can see some very clear flaws in the design that the devs are unwilling to address and contribute to a toxic community. It heavily favors certain builds, specifically ward/armor/low health endurance builds, and anyone not playing those builds will be trapped in the ~300 corruption area. I'm not saying every build should be viable, but I am saying that every class should be viable. That is just not the case, here, because you are railroaded into one of the aforementioned stat distributions if you ever expect to complete T4 dungeons or press beyond 700ish corruption.There are weird design choices. You have block chance, and block effectiveness, but the same is not true for dodge. Dodge is entirely binary, but block will at a chance reduce damage by a percentage. Why? The binary nature of dodge makes it a secondary defense at best in end game, and completely precludes dodge builds from participating in T4 dungeons. Sure, you CAN beat it, but that assumes you don't get hit by a single attack. This isn't dark souls, it's an ARPG, and it's the same thinking trap that PoE fell into. You have to play the meta builds if you want to go the distance, and the community will take great pleasure in turning up their nose at you as a "skill issue" if you play something other than the half-dozen setups that can complete late-endgame content.It's very clear to me why this happened -- leech. I shouldn't be able to leech 90% of my health back in under a second, but I can, so it makes sense that things can do more than 2800 damage in a single attack. You can stack health in every single available slot and still get one-shotted by T4 bosses or regular mobs in high corruption echoes because there is no in-between from max health and zero health in practice with how overtuned leech is. They could have made it so you take less damage and leech slower so you would have to play defensively for a while, but instead they made the lazy choice of "lol you died try the entire dungeon again" when you got hit by a single attack. It's not that your build was bad. You had full 75% resists, 100% crit avoidance, 71-100% glancing blow, ~30% damage reduction from armor, but that wasn't enough. They failed to account for builds that can generate 5k+ ward easily, or manage 80% damage reduction by armor alone, so unless you play one of those builds? Skill issue. It's a shame that an otherwise very good game would be subjected to such easy to fix issues years after the initial release, and that the fix actions are so blatantly obvious -- and yet the devs are unwilling to make big changes that would make entire *classes* playable.tl;dr skip this one and just play Diablo 4.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE AFTER ALMOST 50 HOURS OF PLAY TIMEThis game is amazing. This is the ARPG you have been waiting for. If you are a fan of D2, this is the game for you. Let me explain why.Flaws (just to get these out of the way, because they are minor)- The game is a little janky and buggy. Nothing major, but it does lack a little bit of polish compared to AAA studios.- The map is fragmented, you don't really get the sense that you are traveling through a persistent world.- The Arena, one of the endgame activities is just okay.- Campaign is okay, but I believe major updates are coming in full release.- Some spell effects are lacking.- Not necessarily a flaw, but early on your character will feel a little clunky before you get more move speed and cast/attack speed.The GOOD stuff, and this is what really matters- Class design feels awesome. Again, much like D2, each class has unique strengths and weaknesses. I also like how classes can't be customized and are gendered-lock. It doesn't affect the game, but yet another nod to D2. Each class has multiple interesting builds and more than that, almost any build you come up with is viable until the very end game. Each class has a huge passive skill tree (that is somewhat linear) but more so each skill has a massive skill tree that allows you to create unique builds. There are so many good passives, and skill upgrades, forcing you to make choices. You can't have it all, so you must decide where you want your character to specialize. This results in rewarding class progression with meaningful choices. - Itemization is top tier. You can see the inspiration taken from D2, and what was built on top of that. Most importantly, there are many interesting stats that are rewarding to gear your character with. More so, you actually have to make interesting choices other than just bigger number = upgrade. Just as an example, defensive and offensive stats require a balance. Offensive has many choices such as flat spell damage (per elemental type), % damage increase (per elemental type), attack/cast speed, on hit DoT ailments, move speed, + to skills, etc. Defensively, there is flat health, % health, armor, resistances, endurance, and more. All of these stats are important, feel good, and require you to actually think about which stats fit your needs at the current time. There are many unique items that are awesome. And to top it off, there is an amazing crafting system that is the best I have seen in an ARPG. In short, nearly every item can be modified to make it fit your build, and some of the best items are made through a combination of uniques combined with "exalted" (basically non-unique rare drops). It's intuitive, and cool. - There are many interesting ways to acquire gear, and many of those ways allow you to pseudo-target the gear you want. - Dungeons are unique, each with a specific purpose. Unlike in D4, dungeons are not just a randomly generated thing you blast through for the same generalized gear drops. In LE, each dungeon has specific and unique purpose, on top of rewarding gear. For example, the Lightless Arbor, upon completion, provides a vault where you can sink an increasing amount of gold for a ton of randomized loot chests. Meanwhile, the Soulfire Bastion allows you to collect a special currency where at the end you can gamble upon specific item types. Each dungeon has a purpose and feels like it has a place in the ecosystem of game progression.- The boss fights are epic and provide a fair challenge. There are some one-shot mechanics, but they are heavily telegraphed and avoidable. The bosses are beefy without feeling like a damage sponge. In short, the bosses feel like just that, bosses. They are challenging without being unfair. And there are some unique mechanics in a few them, requiring you to do more than just dodge and do damage. - The music is REALLY GOOD. I haven't seen anybody talk about this, but this music bangs. It, for like the third time, reminds me a lot of D2. It combines both a fantastical sense of adventure, with a somewhat ominous, even dark tone. Picture act 1 rogue camp theme in terms of feeling. It's really good!- Finally, a smaller detail that I love, there are a few references and homages to other games that clearly provided inspiration. The most obvious is the campaign story, which is of course very similar to Chrono Trigger. I have noticed a few bosses say quotes from bosses in WoW. And even some sound effects sound like they are nodes to other games (the siren enemies do a scream that sounds like the demi-humans in Elden Ring).- Nearly every system in the game is explained by an expanded tutorial, and you can see the love that was put into the game by how thoroughly this tutorial explains things.- I personally like the graphics. They aren't amazing, but they feel stylistic and work for the game despite the limitations. Overall, this game kicks some serious ass, and I am beyond excited for the full release. This shows what happens when a game is made by gamers, people who are passionate about the project. There is so much love and care crafted into nearly every aspect of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of ARPGs. The Butcher from Diablo 1 was my first video game scare, and the adrenaline rush that followed got 10 year old me hooked on aarpgs. Since then I grew up with arpgs and have played Diablo 2 and its expansion extensively, path of exile, diablo 3, and diablo 4. Grim Dawn is next on my list (I have a backlog).  I am more of a casual console player now a days since most of my free time is taken up by life. I heard about this game while playing Diablo 4, and as an avid aarpg fan, I had to try it out!The game overall is great! The standout features are the crafting and character building. The ability to use the forge to customize your affixes and prefixes on your items is well done and give players a lot of freedom to tailor their items to their character build. I LOVE the character growth and building in this game. The game allows you to grow your character through an interesting talent tree that includes specializations that can be unlocked, which is standard for most rpgs and aprgs. What really caught my eye was the ability to level up your skills separate from your character class tree. The amount of customization with just skill growth was impressive. You can change elements of spells, how they function, crit modifiers, etc. all to help play your character the way you want to play it. The only frustrating part regarding character builds and talents was only superficial. You cannot change or edit your avatar, and are stuck with the pregenerated looks of your character, which is pretty staple for aarpgs in my experience. It would be nice to design your toon to look the way you want. Thank goodness for the diversity of builds in this game since it helps offset the inability to customize your toon with being able to have a lot of control with your character build to help make your toon unique with how you want to play the game. What didn't stand out was the more generic storyline, creature / monster design, and atmosphere. The storyline has a lot to do with time travel, and of course the generic corrupting Darkness (in this game Void) as the enemy. The characters are very flat and the voice acting just isn't there. There is potential with seeing how characters play out in different timelines but I won't spoil any of the mainstory. I am not compelled to continue playing this game for the story or the characters and started skipping most of the story beats after act 3. If it wasn't for the character building, item chase, and gameplay I would've put it down. This is more of a testament to how well done the game systems are. You can ignore the story and have a blast! The story isn't bad persay, just very generic. Also I found the atmosphere very conflicting with the game narrative. Colors seem too bright and cheery for how dark the plot is and doesn't mesh well. Music is alright, and very generic as well. This game is not perfect though. Some parts I did not enjoy were annoyances that can be solved with bug fixes. However there is an issue with dungeons I do not enjoy. The most frustrating bugs will crash your game, but one in particular will delete items you leave on the ground out in the field when you return to town. Many arpgers are familiar with returning to town to sell off any extra items when they find their bags are full. When the return back from town the expectation are the items they were not able to pick up before would still be there. In this game they are deleted if you do not pick them up before you head to town, which is frankly very annoying. The other annoyance is regarding dungeons. Dungeons show up in the game after act 2 I believe. In order to access them keys will drop from enemies and chests that will allow you to unlock a dungeon run. What isn't communicated is once you use that key for a dungeon run you cannot leave the dungeon for any reason without it resetting. If you have to portal back to town while you are in the dungeon for any reason, including selling items and making room in your stash, you will lose access to the dungeon and your key will be gone, forcing you to farm for another key and do the dungeon again. If you die while doing the dungeon, same thing. The dying causing dungeons to reset and losing a key I am not so upset about. In fact I do like the mechanic of dying resetting the dungeon, that makes sense, and the dark souls masochist in me loves it, but being penalized cause you needed to portal to use the restroom, or answer a call, or simply sell loot to make room for more is very frustrating, especially in a loot driven game. Why limit our looting in a dungeon in an aarpg? The endgame is a little bare bones but it is expected with a new aarpgs. It is in a much better state than most aarpgs when they are first released though, with clear goals and activities as well as excellent rewards as an incentive. I dont want to spoil the mainstory, but towards the end you will be dealing with timelines. As you complete timelines you will unlock permanent passives that will strengthen your character. There is also the dungeons that I mentioned, an arena mode that reminds me of Horde mode from Gears of War or Firefight from ODST, and farming bosses of course. The gameplay is so much fun its a pleasure to engage in these kinds of endgame activity. I am sure there are more systems on the way and am looking forward to playing them as they are released!With all that said I highly recommend this game. Personally it is a solid 8/10 for me. The gameplay, the character building, and the item crafting are what makes this game stand out. The atmosphere and storytelling are very generic though. The game play will carry you past that. If you are a fan of ARPGs, espcially isometric ones, this is a must buy. I look forward to getting the console release so I can sit back and play on a bigger screen. THANK YOU ELEVENTH HOUR GAMES! THIS GAME IS SO MUCH FUN!!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those ARPG's that will absolutely scratch the itch for an easy access experience.The early levelling isn't grindy, the story isn't overbearing and it lets you just watch big number go up and experiment with your chosen mastery before hitting the endgame.That endgame is probably both the strongest and weakest aspect of the game. It has a lot of endgame content that contains a variety of systems for encouraging you to try different routes and builds. But once you hit that point, the level grind is far, far rougher.I got to level 76 as a Primalist before feeling like I was just stuck and going back through stuff I'd done to level and search for build gear. Fortunately, the positives above mean I felt very comfortable jumping into a new class, and with the Stash available to all characters I was quickly getting back into the grove I enjoyed initially.It's still got some bugs and balance issues, despite the long Early Access period, but it's well priced for the experience and the developers are communicative.All in all, solid 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: BETA RELEASE REVIEWIt's a fun ARPG, in the genre of Diablo mixed with a part of Grim Dawn and a part of Path of Exile.  Currently there are 4 classes, with the Rogue class still in it's initial phase of development without a timeframe for release yet.  You still have the opportunity to play as Acolyte, Primalist, Mage, and Sentinel.  These are the typical base classes you find in these games, with each one having three Mastery choices.Many of the builds currently stress damage mitigation and health, with most of the character builds being fleshed out to their highest efficiency way before you reach cap level.  So basically, between level 50-75 you'll most likely have your skills maxed and already have either bis gear or near it.  That leaves little incentive to continue on to cap level 100 for an occasional passive point to reward your effort.  There isn't an endgame currently either, making it even less desirable to continue on with the character.  You'll probably get more enjoyment by starting a new character with a new build you want to try out.  Hoping to see this being fixed way before full release.For the storyline and quests, it's quite intriguing I have to say.  Not to give too much of it away, but you'll be sort of a time traveler, opening portals to different eras (or epochs as in the game title) from the infancy of humanity to the year 2281, The Ruined Era or Last Epoch.  This is where your story begins.I have had a few bugs so far while playing, nothing too serious, but it could of been.  When breaking tables and furniture with your weapons there's chance that money or even gear will drop.  On a few occasions I've had my drops either floating in the air or outside the play area without any way for me to recover them.  Luckily the weapons and armor were not Unique or Set items, and the amount of gold was negligible.Another issue that has happened twice so far, when entering an area or trying to speak to a npc, the game suddenly would just freeze as the camera view changed.  I was left with no other choice but to alt tab out and do a manual exit of the game.  Nothing too serious so far, and it is still in beta after all.I still only scratched the surface of the game to date, but plan to continue on playing throughout the beta phase and hopefully see a completed released version of the game in the near future.  It's definitely worth buying into if you're a fan of the ARPG genre, and I do have a good feeling about this one.  Same way I felt that Grim Dawn was going to become a great released game when I started playing that game at beta.

_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed my time playing Last Epoch; it has plenty of ways to build and play your character, a meaningful crafting system, and interesting endgame systems.I like that it has enough complexity to be engaging but not so much that it feels like another job.Builds are such that I have two rogues that feel completely different from each other, and my friend has two different Paladin builds that he reports feel completely different as well. I like the ability to target farm gear that you need for your build, as opposed to other games where anything and everything has equal chances of dropping what you want, so you are at the mercy of RNG.I like that the boss fights have actual mechanics and some are quite challenging.If you're a fan of ARPGs and want something that you can play casually or hit hard for many hours, I highly recommend playing Last Epoch; it is more than worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: A Triumphant Recovery: The Ascension of Last EpochAfter surpassing the 100-hour mark in "Last Epoch for 1.0," I feel compelled to share my journey through its evolving landscape, especially considering its initial stumble at the 1.0 launch. It's not uncommon for ambitious titles to face hurdles upon release, and Last Epoch was no exception. The game encountered its share of stability issues early on, which could have easily deterred players seeking a smooth and immersive ARPG experience. However, what sets Eleventh Hour Games apart is their unwavering commitment to their community and game's potential.The developers responded with remarkable speed to feedback, rolling out fixes and patches that not only addressed the critical stability and bug concerns but also refined gameplay mechanics. The transformation was nothing short of remarkable. The game that once struggled with launch woes now stands as a paragon of stability and performance in the ARPG genre. Load times have been significantly reduced, making transitions almost seamless. Online gameplay, a crucial aspect for multiplayer enthusiasts, is now stable, providing a fluid and engaging cooperative experience without the frustration of disconnects or lag.From a personal standpoint, having invested over 100 hours into the world of Eterra, I've witnessed this transformation first-hand. The leveling process in Last Epoch is fast-paced yet rewarding, striking a perfect balance between challenge and progression. Unlike some ARPGs where the journey to endgame can feel like a chore, Last Epoch keeps you engaged with its diverse class system, intricate skill trees, and the thrill of loot hunting. The endgame content is where Last Epoch truly shines, offering a variety of activities that keep the experience fresh and exciting long after the main storyline concludes.Moreover, the game's narrative depth, combined with its unique time-travel mechanic, adds layers to both gameplay and storytelling seldom seen in the genre. Whether you're a veteran ARPG player or new to the scene, Last Epoch offers a rich, dynamic world filled with mysteries to unravel and foes to vanquish.In conclusion, Last Epoch has not only recovered from its rocky start but has soared to new heights, thanks to the dedication and hard work of Eleventh Hour Games. It stands as a testament to what can be achieved when developers listen to their community and strive for excellence. With little to no noticeable bugs or issues to speak of, fast load times, and stable online play, Last Epoch has solidified its place as a must-play title for fans of the genre. Whether solo or with friends, the adventure awaiting in Eterra is one that shouldn't be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game over 2 years ago but hadn't played it until the 1.0 launch. The server issues in the first few days were rough, however the EHG devs (and CEO, no less) have been extremely communicative with the community and provided regular updates on their progress and status on addressing the issues, giving live updates via their discord and forums. As this launch issue was transient (in the grand scheme of things) and has been resolved for a few days in my experience, I won't be holding that against them for the purpose of reviewing the game as it currently stands.The pros: - EXTREMELY communicative dev team. - No pay to win/pay for convenience in-game monetizations. All stash space is purchased with in-game gold you have to farm, and all microtransactions are purely cosmetic and a way to show additional support. You pay $35 for the game, and you get the entire unmolested experience. - Really good feeling gameplay from the get-go. Solid impact on skills and responsive controls. - Excellent itemization and crafting system, with clear gear progression paths that have legs. This includes having extremely interesting and chase unique items that build on top of normal gear. - Well-crafted class fantasies and identities. - Easy to understand builds with very little re-spec cost. - Very interesting skill tree customization system that fundamentally changes how some skills work. - Interesting unique/chase item endgame system for targeting specific items for builds. - Interesting faction choices that determine whether you can sell items to other players or simply find improved personal/untradeable loot.*The cons: - The campaign kind of ends on a cliffhanger.** - Crafting materials feel pretty limited until you're almost done with the campaign around level 50, then you start to have enough resources to buy materials used to acquire upgrade mats. This eventually leads to having a rather excessive surplus once your material intake increases in the endgame, however this fortunately doesn't come at the cost of any sort of storage limits. - The endgame gameplay loop is a bit sparse.*** - Classes do have a somewhat limited kit they're restricted to, with subclass specialization being the only permanent choice you make per character you can't undo. (As of right now there are 5 base classes with 3 subclasses each)*There is a system in place that allows you to gain basically friendship tokens for people you party with, allowing you to apply these friendship tokens to items you find while playing solo to give to said friend. Loot found while playing together with someone in the party can still be freely traded among the party.**The devs have already stated their intention to add additional chapters to the campaign to flesh out the story, but for now it kind of just drops you into the endgame a bit unceremoniously after a particular boss fight, with very loose narrative reasons for doing so.***The devs have already made an announcement regarding their 1.1 patch with their intent to add  endgame/pinnacle content to aspire to, but as of this review it isn't in the game yet.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS IS MY FAVORITE ARPG!. I started playing 20 years ago with diablo 2, and went trough a lot of games of the genre, including the other 3 diablos and Path of exile. this is the game that feel more like D2 than any other. While it doesn't have as much content as PoE, a 10 year old game, it launched as a full fledged game with content for dozens of hours of gameplay. it sure had release problems, but the player count didn't go down because of that. This is not a perfect game, but the devs are very open to listen to community feedback.the graphs are amazing, the skills are very diversified and good looking, and the enemies, the bosses especially are very well designed and good looking.part of the gameplay is still not the best though... the bosses attacks are too easy to dodge. some bosses (mainly the big centaur/moose ) get stuck in walls where you can't hit them. health potions can drop in places where you cannot pick them up and the doors hitbox are so big you can go through them without wanting to, and you get the second class for free, without passing a test or something. there are other bugs/design choices that annoy me a little, but those are the things i dislike the most in the game right now.the fact the game is totally playable offline(offline characters and online characters cannot be played together or be changed from online to offline and vice versa) is also a big plus. if you have a portable like steam deck, you can play it anywhere, and also in the cases of internet going down(a very common thing in my country).conclusion: this is an amazing ARPG for someone who wanna start playing the genre, cause it's not over complicated like the best we have in the market(PoE). This is also a good game for casuals, cause you can achieve significant power early in the game. And also a good game for hardcore gamers, cause the endgame is interesting. it also launched as a complete game, unlike the biggest franchise of the genre that launched a game last year that feels empty after a little time of gameplay. Even with some minor problems in the game now, and the major launch problem(which I avoided by playing offline) this is the best thing that happened to ARPG in the last 10 years, and I really want to see what the devs will come up with in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Last Epoch is a promising action RPG with some innovative mechanics. However, it falls short in a few key areas, significantly impacting the overall experience.One of the most frustrating aspects of Last Epoch is its heavy restrictions on trade, which essentially turn the game into a single-player experience. Another divisive aspect of Last Epoch is its faction system, which has created a noticeable division within the community. This division is particularly pronounced in hardcore mode, where few players are part of the Merchant Guild faction, making the auction house very limited with what items are available. Additionally, the game's infinite mob scaling mechanic can make it feel punishing to play non-meta builds. While challenging content is a staple of the genre, the way Last Epoch implements mob scaling can lead to frustrating gameplay experiences, especially for players who prefer to experiment with off-meta builds or playstyles.Some quick Pros about this game:1. legendary potential (uniques)2. crafting3. character customization TLDR cons:1. trading2. infinite scaling endgame3. overtuned meta charactersThis game has tons of positives going for it, but it just isn't for me.

_childDocuments_.review: 06/06/2023 - Adding a cash shop to an unfinished game. I will say the recent update to the early game is very well done19/12/2022 - Got a new PC. Wanted to give this a go. Fifteen minutes in I crashed.As with all Early Access games you can't go into it with the mindset of playing a finished game so while my review is negative I have a lot of respect for what's been done so far. I'd like to start with the good for this game because there is a lot of good but then there's the bad which really, sadly, killed my passion to keep playing for now. - The community has been nothing but kind and helpful, yes there's toxic elements but nowhere near as bad as some games.- This game loves skill trees so the amount of ways to customise your class is insane. There isn't a ton of skills but almost every single skill has a deep skill tree that can completely change how it's used. Every character can/will pick from 3 specialisations. Your base class has a skill tree and each of the 3 specs have skill trees.- Decent enough voice acting overall though not everyone is good- That main menu theme is fantastic!Sadly there's some really annoying, game breaking, bugs that have apparently been present for a while. - Playing this game actually broke my monitors input timing when I was changing the graphics and I didn't even know what that was until this happened.- Sometimes the gameworld will go pitch black. The UI will still be present and on the minimap I'm moving around the game space but everything is just black. I've tried to look up fixes but to no avail and this feels like one of the bugs that should be addressed sooner rather than later. Teleporting to a new map is a way to fix it but it's annoying.- Loading times are awful and I've crashed so many times between transitions.- Because of the time travel aspect I don't feel connected to this world but I've not played for that long so it could be too soon to comment.For all I know my issues could be hardware based. My PC isn't weak exactly but it's still old. Regardless, I wish the development team nothing but good luck and I can't praise this game enough when it works!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the beta for Last Epoch on and off for over two years now, and the game was worth purchasing even back then. Each class is enjoyable and distinctive, with a multitude of ways to build each of those classes available to you.  They have added a wide variety of fun and interesting unique items that can augment, or even fundamentally define a build. My only complaint about the game is that I would like the development to be a bit faster, but everything they have released has been worth the wait every single time. _childDocuments_.review: The game had a rough launch, and has come out the gate with some visual/gameplay bugs. If we're assuming those bugs are squashed soon, then I'd say the actual  is great and has the potential to be the best arpg of all time, imo.- It sits somewhere between diablo/poe in terms of complexity- combat feels more engaging than poe's hold down one-button & clear an entire map approach- the environmental art of the world is beautiful, the colour palettes used are striking, in a good way- the overall aesthetic of the UI is great- respeccing is relatively low cost/effort, so you're not locked-in if you accidentally created a terrible build- the current endgame systems are a blast (monolith mapping, arena waves, dungeons)- itemization is great, there's no bloat like diablo 4 (ie. extra damage on thursday when it's raining and your pet frog is sick)- loot filters are built into the game and easy to build/import/manage- the crafting system is amazing, and simple to understand- stash management is simplified (no specific currency/item tabs like in POE), but stash space is purchased via in-game gold and abundant- rough launch week- there are quite a few remaining bugs that need to be resolved (shapeshifting classes can sometimes go invisible, porting to party members can desync with the server and put you in two different instances, etc..)- early game visuals are dated and don't give a new player the greatest first impression- the base character models are pretty terrible (the armor looks great though)- the world map is a bit clunky- you need to complete the story on every character (there is no diablo equivalent to adventure mode) but there are dungeons that let you skip certain parts of the campaign if you can find the appropriate keys- controller support is lacking polish (there are no proper controller icons, some buttons can't be rebound, some parts of the ui seem inaccessible via controller)

_childDocuments_.review: You'd think the uninspired choices for base classes and slightly less enthused mastery classes would nail the lid on the proverbial coffin, but giving every single skill its own sphere grid that can drastically change what it does is genius. In Diablo 2 I make the same summon necromancer every time, but in Last Epoch I could easily make 3 distinct summon necromancers with varied playstyles. It's impressive. Other positives include idols, great environments, a transfer materials button, and a fantastic passive skill system.On the downside: multiplayer is a disaster at launch, two particular story bosses are quite overtuned for their multi-phase fights, and story mode isn't finished. You'd figure that 1.0 meant a completed story mode, but instead it means "mostly done with 3 chapters/bosses coming later to finish it up". It's overall a fantastic little ARPG for the $35 price tag. Lots of great ideas and fun things to do for classic players especially from the decades of Diablo 2 play. Just digest the cons before fully deciding.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending with some heavy caveats.  As somebody already quite jaded with looter RPGs, I would not buy this full price.  There are noticeable accessibility issues on Deck, and SIGNIFICANT UI issues for playing this game with a controller.  The equipment menu involves too much dragging the stick around like a mouse, even if you use button shortcuts to switch menu tabs.  Thumbing through equipment is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nightmare when 20 things drop on the floor at once and you can only move the D Pad to scroll through the list.   The game crashed for me several times during tutorial pop-ups in the early game. There are frequent autosaves so I didn't lose progress.  But it's still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dumb for my game to lock up because it's explaining a core mechanic.   Also, there are times where my character would randomly stop attacking until I paused and unpaused the game several times.I emphatically disagree with the decision not to pause the game during level up point allocations in offline mode.  It's a needless annoying, seeing the level up glow and still having to wait until the coast is clear to spend points you already rightfully earned. There are allegedly equipment filters to cut down on the trash drops, but they're needlessly difficulty to figure out. The query menu is about as user-friendly as Microsoft Access.  It shouldn't be rocket science just to delete anything worse than what I already have on.  The Primalist / Beast master class is fun though.  The dual-wielding reminds me of the Barbarian from Dark Alliance 2.  And I like seeing all the different pets run across the screen mauling enemies.I appreciate being able to play the game entirely offline.  This was the deciding factor for buying this over Diablo 4.Edit:  The campaign has an insulting conclusion.  The final boss of chapter 9 has no relation to the entity you were trying to chase down the whole time.  No closure, no end credits, just "there's a brand new villain now on top of the old one, welcome to the postgame where we'll drag you along for eternity."
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying, I am aware this is an early access game.The character models and animations look like they are from 15 years ago. That's not really something I've ever seen change after a game comes out of early access. These are the game assets, I don't think they are going to revamp everything from the ground up moving it 15 years into the future in terms of graphics.I do like the depth of the skill trees, but it didn't seem to matter. For me I could just hold down the Q key and everything would die, so I don't really see the point of upgrading the skills. It seems like these systems were built by ambitious indie devs who are very passionate about making games but lack many years of experience in making games in order to properly balance the game and provide engaging game-play.There also didn't seem to be any aiming involved. As long as your mouse was within 50 yards of the enemy, your character would automatically attack them, provided you held down Q.There didn't seem to be any character customization when creating your character which I think is strange for any RPG not to include. Also, it seems that each class has their own backstory as if they are their own person and you don't really decide their story. I got the impression that I couldn't really imagine a backstory of my own for my character (roleplay) because the game thrusts it's own narrative. I think roleplay is important for any RPG and stifling that is not a good design choice. And I think this problem is coming from ambitions indie game devs who are passionate about their game, but lack the experience required to make sound design choices.Speaking of narrative, I could not get engaged with the story. It's delivered via text boxes like the old games from 20 years ago. It does have voice acting, so that's very nice, but the lines aren't delivered via a character model, it's just a text box and sometimes there is a low res portrait of the character next to the text box. Again, I don't see this changing coming out of early access. These are base systems that they have already built and I've not seen a studio completely replace assets or base systems coming out of early access.Maybe I'm spoiled by all the other games out there, but that's the competition now and if you want to compete you can't really deliver a "blast from the past". Perhaps if this game released 15 years ago, it would be much more exciting.

_childDocuments_.review: Last Epoch is a pretty generic action rpg with many flaws that tries to put personalization and flexibility on builds as its most important feature but fails in every other area when compared to other games of the same genre.Maybe its worst flaw is the story. It is completely forgettable, told in an obtuse way and it becomes uninteresting very fast. I've played 8 hours of the game and I do not know what I'm doing, why I'm changing timelines and even npcs seem to be not bothered to understand. This trails the rest of the experience: npcs became mere quest guivers that are also not interesting and generic. You do not know if you are killing a random elite enemy or a big boss. Areas are mere hallways with enemies that come in different colors but they are not clearly different. Loot is also pretty generic and uninteresting. It is not very noticeable on your character build and it comes in tons of very similar pieces so you need to put a filter on loot very fast and even with that it feels boring.  There is no character customization so if you want to play a Sentinel, everyone gets the same bald dude.Taking all of this into account, you can understand that it becomes boring very fast because, even if there is some customization on classes and its builds, they are surrounded by completely average content, so it is not exciting to level up and do the grind.
