_childDocuments_.review: To preface, this review is not emotionally charged with any of the server related issues, though they were annoying it does not impact my impressions of the actual game. With that out of the way, let me explain my opinions on the game itself. Leveling: Mostly fun, I enjoyed the campaign and felt like the power ramping of your character, as well as the difficulty in relation to balancing your character defensively was well balanced for most builds I tried (3), this is different from other games that feel very slow to level (Diablo) or very punishing if you make a gearing mistake (Path of Exile)Character Diversity: Last Epoch probably has the best diversity of builds in the industry, the ability to truly pick any skill in the game and utilize it to at least reach the end game is unrivaled, and does not leave you feeling incredibly weak or overpowered depending on what you pick. The End Game: This is where Last Epoch really suffers, the game fails to drop gear that feels meaningfully impactful to your character, I get that gear improvements are the point of an ARPG, but Last Epoch almost forces you to gamble away your time to a degree that makes it not even fun to do. Forcing me to randomly roll off an affix to try and craft a perfect item, having that random roll remove the wrong affix, or having the right affix removed but losing 80% of my crafting potential... just feels... really bad. And the only way to mitigate that detrimental gearing impact is to simply just invest more time into running 20 second monoliths on repeat. Yawn. The game lacks diverse difficulty at the end game, and it certainly lacks engaging content to grind out endlessly.

_childDocuments_.review: Game engine felt clunky as hell and it looks like the world and characters were made of Play-Dough. Felt like it lacks a lot of polish. The systems might be decent, I didn't make it past 1 hour because of these issues. I don't require much from my games, but the feel of the gameplay is top priority. Combat had some fluidness to it, sure, but cast animations felt slow, unresponsive and sluggish. Movement abilities that you think might go through walls and ledges go through one but no the other. Map design is very basic modern aRPG (Move through this corridor, enemies spawn, move to next corridor, enemies spawn). Monster design and AI felt like it was lifted without changing one line of code from Diablo 3. All the menus felt awkward and ''lazy''. Picking up items felt like it took ages and required an exact pixel to click on, instead of the whole item label. None of this is meant to offend or devalue people enjoying this game, this is just my personal experience. If you're someone who cares about the issues mentioned, think twice about spending money on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of complaints about adding an in game shop before its release and I want to try to clear the air of this. If the in game shop is what ruins this game for you then you never really should enjoy any in game shop style game. Nothing from the shop is required to win. As some has stated, it's easier to understand over PoE and more complex than D4 currently. It respects your time you put into it and respects the players intelligence. It has a nice in game guide that that you can search for terms to see what exactly it does. Even some terms have the mathematics equation so you can understand how it works. _childDocuments_.review: LE has the worst end-game contents in aRPG, I have ~600h from 0.8x to 0.9 when they started to introduce MP which point the game is not interesting. Devs are busy with rushing 1.0 to cash grab, they priorities MTX than fix and do balancing. What a shame.LE has the most imbalance skill system, lots of nodes are just ridiculous with huge amount of more damage (multiplier), even top T7 affixes don't have such bs stat, once you have the nodes, gears don't matter much.Back to the end-game there are 3 things you can only do:1. Empowered monolith with corruption scaling. This looks promising on paper but once you start pushing it becomes such a chore, boring as hell. Every node takes you not more than 5 mins to do, its basically running from point A to point B, clear the object, loot and repeat. And the loot is aweful though. There are only a few items you could farm from monolith, but the drops are not good to be spending time on. You'll get bore after corruption 800, I guarantee with you so.2. Dungeons: 3 dungeons with lots of keys dropping when you do monoliths. They are one shot dungeons, once you know the mechanics by watching on YT and self trying out, you'll figure it out really easy, nothing is challenging here in those 3 dungons. Only T4 Julra, where you could find some decent stuff and most important thing is to craft Legendaries with LPs Uniques and your T6/T7 gears.T6/7 gears will drop like Diablo 3/4 loots, alot, but meaningful or high-max rolled T6/7 will take you awhile to find then you'll find that your stash are full of bs T6/7, what you actually wanted is not there.3. Ladder and Arena. I pushed to 8-900 waves in 0.9 so I know what I'm talking about here. Once you hit 500+ waves, mobs hit hard, 7-800+ some will one-two shot you with their tiny projectiles, no matter what ward/hp you have. I had some execellent builds just for ladders, but it's so boring and a very long time run, like a few hours if you start pushing from 100. You can "pause" and take a break after every ten waves, but it's in Offline mode, if you do it ONLINE, the bs server will kick you out and waste your progession.Overall, Arena is fun when you have excellent knowledge about the game, know how to build, which build is good and its where to test your build, to push it to the limit. Once you did it, you're done. Its nothing good to waste hours of doing waves after waves because there are no good loots in Arena.So overall, LE's end-game is the worst in aRPG genre. People who just started playing and having fun with the mechanics and crafting, I feel you because you haven't reach the end-game, what I mean is having a good build to be able to farm high contents and competitive in ladder. Once you realize your build is sh1t, sorry, you're in bad luck, you cannot turn around but deleting your char, what a shame.LE is so punishing newbies with its bs mechanics. You can play around anything you want, but if you don't start to do researches and understanding all the tags, % dam, what is your survival capabilities you WILL struggle to push. Then you'll go searching online, following some builds, but you don't have the gear or enough rss to turn around, you'll stuck with a mediocre character. That's what everyone will go through.So do I recommend LE after 6-700h, simply no, Its a blast at first but once you'll realize its end-game has no dopamine to aRPG fans, you'll leave soon like old school people did. Devs they cash grabbed and never fix this game, or do balancing. Those are problems since early stages like 0.8x to 0.9, all are still there.So what do I recommend for your itches of aRPG? Play Grim Dawn, or even Wolcen, they have some unique mechanics.Good luck folks.

_childDocuments_.review: After tackling those pesky server issues, Last Epoch is really making waves in the action RPG scene, like an underdog rising up against the big names.The game's pacing is spot-on. They ditched the whole bullet sponge boss nonsense. It's all about keeping the action flowing and plotting out your character's growth. No tedious trips back to town to sell off junk; if it's not worth it, it stays on the ground. That way, you can stay in the zone, fighting and leveling up.And speaking of depth, Last Epoch falls somewhere between Diablo and Path of Exile. Each skill tree lets you mold your character in loads of different ways. Unlike other ARPGs where you're drowning in pointless gear affixes, Last Epoch keeps it focused. Unique and set items don't have random stats, just a range.The time travel theme adds a nice twist to the story, making the whole experience even cooler.Last Epoch is totally worth getting into, even before you hit the endgame.

_childDocuments_.review: It's sad to see a small indie team work hard to make an amazing game just to get dumped on by players due to server issues. Most of the current negative reviews at release are due to server instabilities that EHG have been working their asses off to address. They've been putting out fixes for an incredibly difficult problem to solve at great speed, but most players wouldn't recognize it. I have confidence that the online issues will eventually be fixed.As for the game itself, it's been one of my favorite, if not my absolute favorite ARPG to be released so far. The builds and customization options are incredibly diverse and the skill upgrade system is uniquely entertaining. Combat is very satisfying, and abilities feel very impactful. The skill tree system is not as overly simplistic as Diablo's but also not as convoluted and punishing as PoE's. The crafting system is amazing, and makes it much easier to get items that you need, yet keeps the feeling of finding upgrades rewarding. The trade system could use some bits of refinement, but is an overall great improvement to that of their competitors'. However, if you are not into trade, there is also an alternative option to not have to deal with it and boost drop rates instead. There's a lot more good that could be said about how this game has taken all the best (and worst) parts of ARPGs and improved upon them. There's also a true offline option where the whole experience is very smooth, which is an absolute rarity in the modern gaming world with every recent release being a "game as a service".I look forward to this game being updated with more content and what future cycles hold. It's absolutely worth the $35 for the offline mode alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, the 1.0 launch was a little rough because of the mind blowing number of people trying to play it. Nearly all connection issues have been ironed out at this point, and if you have spotty internet yourself it has a FULL OFFLINE mode you can play with no internet connection at all. So many builds, so many skills, so much to chose, and yet still very new player friendly and completely fine to go in blind just reading your skills and doing what looks fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sits perfectly between D3's brain dead, shallow, thoughtless gameplay, and PoE. It's the perfect training ground for a slightly more complicated AARPG for D3 enjoyers to move on to. Great build diversity, you don't need a guide to feel strong or make it through the game. It's a solid balanced game. It's beta so animation issues, and bugs are still pretty common. There hasn't been a AAPRG that feels this good to play in a very long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: This game rules. Even years ago while super beta, it was still awesome. I have so much respect for the devs of this game.The game is amazing as-is. They didn't rush it, they listened to community feedback and I feel like the players kind of built the game WITH the devs, rather than the devs building the game for the players.Last Epoch is what Diablo 4 should have been.Yes the game had server-issues when it launched. Can't blame them. This studio is tiny compared to a HUUUGE company like Activision or Ubisoft, but hey, good old offline mode is still available, so you can pause the game if you need to, and you can get to know the game, before playing online too.I feel like this game takes the best parts of Diablo, Torchlight and Path of Exile and mixes them all together into a fantastic game that can be enjoyed by everyone. Not just ARPG experts.

_childDocuments_.review: Gone through the main story and experienced some of the end game. Will update as I progress further.Overall: the game is good. It feels like a mixture of PoE and D3 but different enough from each to stand as it's own experience as opposed to a clone. However, there are improvements that can be made without needing a full overhall to the game. Due to the server issues I chose to play in offline mode not to have my experience spoiled by issues that will soon not exist. I played the vast majority of the campaign on M&K, only playing about 30 mins on my Steam Deck.Pros:- You get a full product for a very low price. You aren't pushed into paying out extra with no underhanded limitations to get your money.- Good variety of builds available with different uniques, sets and ability skill trees- Combat feels nice. Not the best in the genre but still very high quality- Spin to win is a possible build and that's always a pro for me- The way points unlock when you enter certain proximity instead of on click which is far better the way a lot of other titles handle this mechanic- Due to the concept of the game, the areas and enemy types are extremely varied and done beautifully - One of the more vibrant games in the genre which is personally very refreshing- OFFLINE MODE is available. Though it isn't perfect which I will talk about in the cons- Story is decent enough. Again, not the best in the genre but strong enough to make me not just click through to skip the dialogue- Bosses feel great and are varied. Then also seem to scale well in complexity as you progress through the campaign- Monolith feels like better GRs from D3 or perhaps more accurately, simpler Maps from PoE (imo in a good way)Cons- The game needs a bit more optimisation. There are occasional micro stutters when you engage with a new pack of enemies. Also while my machine is perfectly capable of handling the Ultra settings, they seem to tax my PC more than I would expect the game to with the graphics that it has.- OFFLINE MODE doesn't have any appearance customisation. This means even if you pay for Deluxe you will not be able to look how you want and this really makes this mode feel like an inferior experience and that you are being punished for no reason for choosing it- Campaign is quite long with no proper ability to skip it after completion. There are ways that you can skip parts of it but a "Skip Campaign" option would be very much appreciated for alt playthroughs. - The story gives you options for certain dialogues that end up being a loop of "Will you join me to fight?" and response always being "I can't because I have other things to do" which seems kind of pointless to have the option to ask almost every NPC you encounter.- Set items can create a more locked in meta however this is more of a concern than a con because I still need to experience the game more to establish it as such- My gameplay on the Steam Deck with the controller layout, although limited was limited for a reason. It felt far more clunky than other titles in the genre using the controller. I definitely felt disadvantaged switching from M&K far more than I did with other titles in the genre
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually buy early access titles, but I was jonesing for an ARPG and this one looked neat.It's pretty smooth, considering it's still in development.  While there is room for improvement, there is already a lot of fun content here, and the skill customization and passive ability trees mean you can have a different experience with a different character - you're not going to be railroaded into the same character build.I started out a little confused with the time travel early on, which they've just now augmented in an update, to clarify the first few story beats.  That means that getting into it should be easier and make a bit more sense.  I began having fun after a few minutes in.  But the moment I knew the game was a winner, was when I ran into a teleporting 'Jahith Bear' in the wilderness.  Pro move, Last Epoch.  Pro move.A few notes on my experience:I'd say you should give this a try, if you are looking for something a bit more grounded than D3 or Wolcen, but don't want to sink thousands of hours into PoE.  It's fun, accessible, and seems to be headed in the right direction.

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the negative reviews are because of technical issues during the 1.0 launch. While that's obviously not ideal, and negative feedback is fair, these issues were to be expected. The developers have been in constant communication and are clearly working around the clock to get things fixed. Performance has increased dramatically over the last 48 hours or so. I sincerely hope the people leaving the negative reviews will come back to adjust/remove them when the issues are fixed. But given the horribly toxicity of some of these people...I doubt it. Regardless, there's a 100% offline mode that worked perfectly fine throughout this launch, but of course it means giving up on some social online-only features. Now to the actual review. If you're sick of Diablo 4's simple gameplay, lack of endgame, bad and underwhelming seasons, the general disconnect and cluelessness of its devs, and the beyond obnoxious monetization... If you're interested in POE but find the new player experience too overwhelming and confusing... Then Last Epoch is the game for you! LE is perfectly in the middle of D4's simple themepark experience and POE's overwhelming abundance of systems. All of the subclasses (masteries) have their own unique identity and playstyle and they're all viable. While plenty of guides exist you'll be perfectly fine if you just use some common sense and put your build together yourself. Between the monoliths, the 3 dungeons, and the arena there's plenty to do in the endgame. It's obviously not quite as mature as POE yet, but it's a lot better than anything D4 has to offer. There's no 'uber Duriel mats' grind; you can just jump straight in. It has target farming for specific items, it has a robust loot filter, it has plenty of stash space. It's very generous with loot and gold. Because of the loot filter you can actually play the game and don't have to spend half of your playtime painstakingly sorting through an inventory full of items. The elaborate crafting system allows you to adjust your items, or create them from scratch. If you're not interested in the social features like grouping, trading, etc there's the offline mode!Yes there's a MTX shop but it's cosmetics only and it's reasonably priced. If you're into ARPG's you should check this one out, but wait a week so they can iron out the technical growing pains.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR; Cannot recommend game- Gameplay and combat does not feel good, one could argue that it should be expected from an indie company.- Online servers are unplayable, even four days after the release, feels like Wolcen all over again. At least they have offline play, but then you're cut off from trading and so on.- Story is boring, made even worse by the fact that you cannot change your mastery and you'll have to level all over through the boring campaign again (ye i know the game has fast tracks)- Endgame is fairly good however, I do like the crafting system, being able to target specific stats farily easily and the ability to merge unique items with Exalted gear, better than what PoE has imo:But when it comes down to it, I'm not having fun while playing, so what the point?
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Epoch is a really great game, yes it has problems/bugs with it, but it is still really enjoyable. I don't care about a few bugs if the game is fun.If you find the Path of Exile too overwhelming for you, the Last Epoch is the best choice for an isometric arpg. The Harbingers of Ruin cycle was great, the pinnacle boss system and the nemesis system were great, I really enjoyed it. It added a lot more to the game than any Diablo season.Diablo 4 could give you a lot less for twice the price of Last Epoch.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics have very slight glitches for me but barely even noticeable. The game seems to combine the depth of Path of Exile with the more simplistic Diablo 3 game style. The mobs and characters are simple enough as to not cause too much drag on your system resources whilst the world itself is nicely done.I think currently, €29.99 is a little steep for what you get but I do understand that the game is still in development and that the purchase price supports that development. I have not yet found any kind of in game communications such as a global chat to talk to other players in the game other than through a friends menu and would hope to see that kind of thing implemented within the game.So far so good would accurately describe my feelings here and I look forward to seeing the continuing content that Eleventh Hour Games are developing.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: Well this one is a little bit hard to evaluate. From the one hand we have a really good middle-ground arpg between diablo and poe with interesting progression and engaging craft system where you both have to find a good base and finish it yourself. You can easily make a close to perfect gear yourself and it feels incredibly good. Factions allow you to choose between trading or more loot so it doesn't force you to engage with trade if you don't like it unlike poe.From the other hand the game is painfully slow comparing with poe. No zoomy gameplay + they force you to play clunky builds where you have to press extra buttons just to have you damage. Imho they should make more ways to automate such things.But overall i like the direction it's going to. Devs are pretty chill and trying their best to make a good product so a thumb up from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: Awful launch. Tragic. Read on for the game itself.Last Epoch is an aRPG with true game direction. It is built by a team which initially lacked the art muscle and budget for big things, which changed during 2022 & 2023. The production values are there for newer content (e.g animations, character models, skill vfx, combat feel). This shows that they have the capability to deliver something special. The game offers novel and innovative ideas which breathe life into the genre again, and make you want to roll every class & mastery. Lots of these ideas still have jank, bugs or lack of polish. See above comment about EHG capability accelerating.Gamplay loop is great. Difficulty leans towards too easy. Boss encounter design is elementary. Art and vfx are getting there. optimisation needs more work. But the game is really good, worth it right now even for 1.0 to play offline. Nevermind the thousands of hours of replay-ability. We need to support these studios and original games.
_childDocuments_.name: Last Epoch

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has never been able to get into Path of Exile even after trying time and time again (hopefully PoE2 changes that), this game is fantastic. I have played many other ARPGs and this one really just hits the sweet spot with quality of life, satisfying combat, build complexity, and an addicting item grind. I'd love for them to add a dodge mechanic like Lost Ark, Diablo 4, and Path of Exile 2 has/is going to have. The graphical quality is definitely not as good as the new D4 (which I would say I even prefer D2R over D4 aesthetically) but it is good enough to not be distracting and there are still some great set pieces and back drops to be found. For the price, this is worth it. I have faith the developers will successfully continue to build on what is already a fantastic base game with respect to the community that so clearly loves it.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly this game is probably carried by fanboys.Last Epoch was in early access for a very long time and because of that and because so many of my friend who baked it in e.a recommended it as a next Diablo killer (which nowadays isn't a hard goal to achieve)  i purchased it.But why i dislike and refunded it?- Game offers 6 control inputs (QWER+Left@Right mouse) you can only map 5 skills to be an active skill to use. No decent ARPG does that. Diablo2: 15 skills. Grim Dawn 12 skills. Torchlight 10 skills. POE 13skills ect)- Way to close zoom distance. Feels like i'm playing a cheap  asian MMORPG- Dialogues and voice acting and story: Characters are speaking but i have no clue what they want to tell me. Can't recall a single name or event or information. Random jibberish put together by google translate- Network latency: Even teleporting to town with town portal needs 2 sec to start casting the teleport, then the game tells me on screen that is should be prepared for teleportation and then a loading screen appears. If Diablo 2 could instantly open a Town Portal and teleport me into town in the 90's, why does this game require so long to even throw a loading screen to me?- Skill upgrade: Even a failed ARPG like Wolven could manage to do the upgrade of individual skills do well. Here  if you unequip a skill from your active upgrade slots, the entire progress of your skill upgrade gets lost.- And did i tell you that you can have only 2 companions active at a time? You want to play a beastmaster druid (which is a legit subclass with 5 different summons available to choose from) but you can literally summon only 2 at a time?WTF?

_childDocuments_.review: I originally wrote this review on 2/22/24, when Last Epoch was experiencing major issues with its login API. As promised in the original review, I am here to update my review of the game now that the servers have been stabilized. Last Epoch is a game, you can play it and that is kind of cool, but before purchasing it consider the following:It has a highly customizable skill system that allows for unique game-play even among similar buildsIt has a time-travel based story that is sure to leave you wishing you could skip the campaign on your altsIt has dungeons which reward you with the ability to gambleIt's endgame consists of doing the same things repeatedly, but with different modifiers It reinforces your belief in the gamblers fallacy via its crafting systemIt allows for the kind of build crafting that makes your build either completely broken or barely functionalIt has some paid cosmetics which are cool if you like paid cosmeticsIt has two major buff systems which consist of playing tetris and picking which cup the ball is under at a magic showIt has two major factions you can join to help you gear: one is a player driven market and the other is a tarot card readingTLDR: Last Epoch is a game that exists, I really wish I could give it a sideways thumb. It has a lot of promise, but its endgame will put you to sleep and make you wake up with a feeling like you spent a whole lot of time on nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is my first steam review. I think this game is grossly overrated. Look at the female rogue character in the character select screen. It is 2023. This game has been in early access for something like almost 3 years. There's absolutely no excuse for character models that are this bad in 2023. I could draw better with an etchasketch. _childDocuments_.review: For now this game is not recommendable. It has very slow gameplay and the environment is nothing the player gets attached to. There is no excitement due to the slow gameplay and the action is rather lame. It feels like a mixture of Diablo 3 and PoE and that prevents Last Epoch from being a game of its own. Most of the time it´s like ´I´ve seen this in Diablo´ or ´I´ver seen this in PoE.Controls seem to be designed for control pads, since there so little slots to fill. Visually the game is also somewhere between D3 and PoE. It still lacks some basics like comparing item in the inventory and items worn...have to hover between two iems and compare stat by stat. And, one big negative point for me, switching items does not change the visual appearance of your character, except for the weapon. So you won´t look like a badass hero in later game and that leaves out the `visual` progress. Imo that is a big fun killer.Sure, I´ll keep an eye on Last Epoch with the hope that future patches will bring some more quality to the game experience.But for now there are some way better games out there that provide a more complete game experience...After trying Last Epoch several more times trough the last years I thought I should give it another try since it is just before release and it`s talked about a lot recently.I did not manage to play more than 3 minutes this time. Right after starting a new character I was reminded of how bad the controls are and there is no way to change it to your liking. I play keyboard & mouse, this game seems to be made for gamepads in the first place. Last year I foeced myself to play Last Epoch a little longer and got one character to level 51. But I simply did not have enough fun to go any futher.  Imo little to nothing has changed to the better since my first review. The thumb stays down and I will uninstall Last Epoch one last time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has pretty quickly evolved into one of the best ARPGs on the market. Tired of PoE or waiting for  the new league? Want something faster than Grim Dawn? Diablo 2 feels a little bit stale? - This is the game for you. Not to say that it is just the next best thing after those other ARPGs.Combat - it could be better on some classes, Rogue being the smoothest class by far (it really does feel reeally good to play it), but we already know that they are working on overhauling other classes.Skills and Passives - the passive tree is deep enough to have a plethra of choices for builds. The Skill leveling system is amazing, this is what D3 wishes it was - not too complicated, yet you could build each skill 3-5 completely different ways, combine that with multiple skills and sub-classes - you got a ton of variation for each class.Items - more or less the usual ARPG stuff, but the crafting system makes sure that you can get the item that you need, you can just craft the affixes that you need on the base that you want. It is not that simple, as you add instability to your gear that way and can lock up or damage the item in the process, but the system as a whole is great tbh. Uniques, well, they are uniques, they have some modifier that a rare item can't have, more or less specific build enablers and whatnot.Visuals - the game looks great, gives me enough old-school vibes, yet looks fresh and pretty.Sound - leaves a little bit to be desired, could have more impact and weight behind skill sounds, but that also might be fixed in the future.Overall, would say that the game is a good 7.5/10 that also has the potential to become a 9/10 in the nearest future. And I am quite sure that it will.

_childDocuments_.review: Long time ARPG player, this is easily my favorite and by far the most complete-on-release ARPG that has come around. The devs care about the community and communicate better than any other dev team in the space through their community discord. This is not merely a game; it is a dazzling, kaleidoscopic portal to a realm where time itself bends to your will, and where every pixel is infused with the electric thrill of adventure!From the moment you plunge into this exquisite tapestry of fantasy, you are greeted with visuals so lush and vibrant that you’ll swear you’ve been transported to an artist’s dreamscape! The landscapes are painted with an otherworldly brush, teeming with life and dripping with detail. Every tree rustles with purpose, every stone whispers ancient secrets, and every shadow dances with the promise of untold adventures. It’s as if Mother Nature herself teamed up with a team of caffeinated unicorns to bring this world to life!And let’s talk about the classes! Oh, the classes! Each one is a dazzling constellation of abilities, waiting to be unleashed upon your foes. The Sentinel gleams with armored glory, a beacon of might and justice. The Mage weaves spells that shimmer like stardust, blasting enemies into oblivion with the elegance of a cosmic ballet! And don’t even get me started on the Primalist—channeling the raw forces of nature, this class feels like summoning the fury of the earth itself! It’s a smorgasbord of build possibilities that will make your head spin faster than a whirlwind of excitement!Now, let’s delve into the gameplay! The combat is a symphony of chaos and strategy, where every swing of your weapon and cast of your spell resonates like the glorious crescendo of a symphonic masterpiece. You’ll find yourself losing track of time—oh, the delicious irony in a game about time travel—lost in a whirlpool of loot, level-ups, and unparalleled joy! The skill trees are a magnificent maze, offering tantalizing choices that will have you crafting your ultimate hero like a master artisan sculpting a divine masterpiece.And the music! Oh, the music! Each note drips with ethereal beauty, wrapping around you like a warm embrace, urging you onward into the depths of adventure. It’s a soundtrack that could serenade the gods themselves!But wait! There’s more! The developers have crafted a living, breathing ecosystem of quests and lore that will ensnare your imagination like a spider’s web of wonder. It is the glittering crown jewel of action RPGs, a celebration of everything we hold dear about gaming, and a siren call to adventurers everywhere. You stick to 1 role, 1 spec, or simply don't play (because it's pointless).The drop rates are stupid, simply. You get something of value 1/1000000 times, and it feels like no matter the difficulty of the area, whether you are doing a dungeon... The drops just feel stupid. On the gameplay, the skill trees end up being as boring as it can get. I found DIablo IV quite more entertaining, to be fair. In this one you end up just smashing 2 keys. Tried 2 classes and they feel overpowered, no matter what you do. To sum it up, fun, but nothing crazy. . And the support is non-existent. I have reported several in the last 3 days, and I never even got feedback. And some of them are quite discouraging. Here is a brief list:- Long and awkward loading screens. It feels absurd. You click the area threshold and nothing happens for some 5-10 seconds. Then you suddenly get a loading screen. Not that takes 5 min, but well, it feels really absurd. - After transforming back to human form as werebear playing as primalist, I could never see my character until I tp to other area- Had a heroic character (meaning that if he dies, you never get it to be HC again). I advanced to a different area, 0 danger, 0 enemies, and (after one of does stupidly long loading screens) it appeared dead. It wasn't HC anymore :_) - Crazy lag in all EU servers. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game has massive potential, but:1. The game runs like crap. Spezific areas, Mobs and skills dropping your avarage fps from 60 to 5 every few min/sec, even with a very solid hardware.2. Half of the game is based on bugs, from minor to game-breaking bugs, everything included.With half of all skills you usually don't know if it's a wanted feature or a bug. The same applies to the interaction of skills and items (slightly exaggerated). Each patch introduces 20 new or reactivates old bugs.3. The endgame is bare-minimum and even 1.1 doesn't help enough. Their only solution to expand what little content they have is to make farming equipment as tenacious as possible.Do you like RNG? Well, LE has you covered on this part. RNG on top of RNG on top of RNG, sounds fun?To explain: you are exposed to RNG when farming for a unique, these often have RNG-based stats which you try to min-max. After a while, when you have the right unique with reasonably good rolls and legendary potential, you would now like to make a legendary out of it. To do this, you now have to farm an exalted one which has the desired stat as T7. Now you may have to forge this exalted one so that the remaining stats are not total rubbish. If the forging was also successful, you now go to the sanctum to craft a legendary out of the two parts, only for the RNG to decide against you and the unique does not get the relevant stats. Congratulations, you can now start again from the beginning.The RMT is also a joke. According to the saying: "fool me once shame on you fool me twice shame on me". Not even a week into 1.1, there was another big gold dupe that brought the entire market to its knees. Unfortunately, there is little to no improvement in sight from the developers. I would laugh if the same "song" was repeated in 1.2.I tried my best to give the game a chance, and had fun with 1.0, but I see only minimal improvements coupled with dozens of new bugs with 1.1. The game in its current state is anything but a full release and is miles away from it, maybe if the game isn't dead in a year, it could get the title of a full released game with a proper and fun endgame.

_childDocuments_.review: Review: Definitely worth a buy. Enjoyable as either a couple dozen hours if you aren't an ARPG fan, or more than hundreds of hours for those that love the endgame loot grind. Core game: 9.5/10- Mechanics are great, skills feel good, the passive trees and crafting system allows you to be creative in making your own builds. The difficulty of the game is a bit low, and respeccing is forgiving, so you can catch up if you mess up your build. There is trade but if you opt out for it you get bonuses to finding and crafting your items if you prefer that; appears quite balanced. Campaign: 6/10- The story is poorly done and there's no compelling villain unfortunately. Balance is too easy so up until about act 8 out of 9 there's little challenge making it a bit of a slog. Endgame: 8/10- The endgame that exists is excellent but there is a lack things to do in 1.0 as the game just release. However, all the dungeons and timelines have just enough grinding to make you feel progress/accomplishment WITHOUT disrespecting your time (like some other games...).  Technical: 10/10- true offline is a very very good feature. Poorly optimized when I played the beta; at launch it runs better than games from 10 years ago on my (non-gaming) laptop. In-game guide, in-game loot filter, intuitive stash, controls highly mappable.Must play and likely to be the best ARPG on the market with a few more patches.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite good. Firstly, the servers. While personally I have had almost zero issues with them, a lot have. Just luck of the draw I guess. They have gotten better the past couple of days though so there is light at the end of the tunnel for most. Past that, currently lvl 83 Warlock and the game is everything I wanted. Made my own build and had no problem blasting off through content. There were a couple of times that I got "stuck" and noticed that I didn't have enough survivability. 2K gold, one respec later, and it was back to cruising. That's how easy it was. You pair that with a ton of QoL things in the game and it has marked itself as a good ARPG to put into your rotation. Between this and POE (POE 2 when it launches) you should have all you want in between leagues/cycles. I have just about as much time in one character in LE than I did in D4 combined (60ish hours) across all seasons. D4 had a great campaign and looked pretty but past that it was bare bones. This has a pretty enjoyable end game, great itemization, and a crafting system I haven't even interacted with too much yet. I have no doubt that more is coming and heard that they are already adding pinnacle bosses for the first update, which is great. If you are a fan of the genre, want something to play alongside POE, or are just sick that Diablo kind of sucks now, pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Last Epoch is my favorite ARPG, the developers at EHG have found a really good balance of complexity and accessibility that makes the game easy to get into and try out a variety of builds to find something you like but within each build lies a lot of depth to the ways you progress your character and grow in power. It's not a perfect game, and it's not for everyone. If you like tinkering with gear and stats on one character to absolutely conquer the game, this game has a decent amount to conquer, but not a LOT yet. If you just want to go in blind and pick skills and upgrades that sound cool to you - good news, you'll probably do just fine, lots of options are very viable for the vast majority of the game. If you like the idea of crafting gear but found Path of Exile too complicated and the diablo games underwhelming, you'll probably love Last Epoch's simple but deep pseudo-deterministic crafting system that you can start experimenting with even at early levels.And most importantly, if you just want to kill monsters and drop cool loot, Last Epoch has my favorite item design in any game. Whether you choose to play in the trade faction or the magic find faction, Last Epoch has a satisfying sense of gear progression as you consistently attain better and better gear that all feels exciting and rewarding to equip.So... what kind of character will you fight back the void with?

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR; Last Epoch is fantastic. If you've ever loved ARPG, this is a must-play. It's a little rough still, and far from perfect, but it has heart and character, and does right what so many fail at. The pacing, complexity, itemization, combat, and depth are all rock solid. There's excellent quality of life features so it never feels like a hassle to play. Plus, it has some inspiring new ideas in the mechanics, while drawing on the best in class features of the legendary ARPGs of the past. Don't miss out. If they were more established or had a bigger marketing budget, this game would easily sell for $50+.Last Epoch is fun. I mean, legitimately fun. Not fun, except. Not fun, in spite of. It's just a joy to play, like ARPG used to be. If anything, Last Epoch highlights how far the genre has fallen, and how much modern ARPG titles like Path of Exile, Diablo 4, and Lost Ark have failed us. It brings quality of life and good ideas of its own, too. The devs are clearly passionate and understand and enjoy the genre themselves. This is the kind of game that the old guard at Blizzard used to make. Good games, full of exciting ideas and passion, made by fans of the game they're making, for players who share their dreams and want to see them become reality, and (mostly) in defense of that experience.I've played most major ARPG, and have thousands of hours in the genre. Last Epoch is not perfect, but I can safely say that if Eleventh Hour Games made Diablo 4 just like this, but with the IP's graphics, polish, story, and marketing, it would likely exceed Diablo 2 and become the new pinnacle of the genre. Is Last Epoch a perfect game? No, far from it. Some of the systems aren't very impactful. The combat often doesn't feel weighty. It's a little bit too fast and unresponsive. Are the graphics top tier? No, but they're quite good. Does it have live service elements that tarnish the experience a bit? Yes, but they've done so far more ethically than most companies ever have with only cosmetics, no special bundles or sales, and evenly-priced increments on all items that match up to what you pay so it's easy to know exactly how much it costs. And NO PREDATORY LOOT BOXES thank goodness. Is it still sad that it has a cash shop? Yes, absolutely. My character looks like an NPC with mismatched clothes instead of a cool power fantasy hero like they should. But what they've accomplished here is worth far more than $35, and it belays an understanding of the ARPG genre that far exceeds any tepid, risk-averse, shareholder-driven, tone-deaf, investment-bedazzled slop the industry has become used to. Last Epoch has thoughtful mechanics and systems that are complex to increase their value and enjoyment instead of to waste player time or confuse them into spending money to fix their mistakes. It has grind for fun and content, instead of engagement. There's no battle pass. No daily log in. The game, so far, expects you to play because you want to, and none of the events yet are time-limited or constantly flashing at you from a launcher to "play now before it's too late! Special sale in the shop," like some desperate hack trying to peddle what they know is outdated, dusted-off, third-rate junk.I get the impression that they really care about their game, and love it. If that's true, and they avoid the same downfall that other game studios face... if they keep the studio private, always treat their employees and customers right before anything else, and make games they're passionate about and want to play, they'll fast become the industry-leading ARPG studio. It's right in their name. Eleventh Hour Games, presumably based on the religious parable. It speaks to their experience at Blizzard, and I hope the namesake helps them never forget their origins or goals, and leads to more work like this.Last Epoch is already a great game. I am truly excited to see what this company makes next. If they make a Last Epoch 2 or 3, I think it will be their opportunity to really turn the genre upside down and pull a Baldur's Gate 3 or a Final Fantasy 7 on the ARPG genre. If they got someone like Brody on board to do to Hearthstone what they did to Diablo, it might just smash a hype train through this old gamer's jaded heart.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about Last Epoch. It definitely has the potential to become a great ARPG (in a feeew years...), but as for its current state? It's overrated. Generally speaking, as a D2/PoE veteran; it simply .Pros:+ Item crafting is truly EPIC.+ Tons of unique items and skill modifiers.+ Legendary potential is an innovative system.+ There are some unique things that I haven't experienced in any other game, like the druid's swarmblade form - super cool.+ Incredible amount of build customization and the ease of respeccing.Cons:- Performance is bad. Some areas and monster skills are unoptimized af!- The current iteration of the most important endgame system (monoliths) is just so unbearably boring.- Many sounds are misused/outdated. For example, the sound of shooting arrows from a bow is unrealistic and silly. Also, a lot of actions (casting spells or monsters dying etc.) have only one sound associated with them per spell/enemy etc., so combat often feels very repetitive.- The official Feb.2024 release of the game didn't feel a version 1.0. _childDocuments_.review: So far this feels like the perfect middle ground between Diablo 3 and Path of Exile... and i absolutely love it!Graphics are sufficient, gameplay feels smooth and the initial quality of life is amazing (in game wiki with search function, auto sort for inventory and stash, seemingly endless stash space...).If you are a fan of ARPGs and/or disappointed by Diablo 4, this will most likely be a game for you.Edit 100 hrs later:Still having fun, but the game is far from optimized. You will find yourself stuck in a loading screen every now and then, especially if you want to play in a party.Theres a few ways you will get stuck under the map.Tooltips and icons in the skilltree are done in a really lazy way (a lot of art is reused for different skills/effects which makes them unrecognizable).Balancing feels really off (eg the best Beastmaster build does not use beasts).These things can get annoying, but i do believe that the positives still outweigh the negatives and i think these things will be adressed with time.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Game is good played through campaign with 3 characters. most negative reviews are launch server issue problems that have been mostly fixed at this point. Try it if you like ARPGs like Diablo, or Path of Exile its $35 for a feature complete game with cosmetic cash shop that doesnt take away from in game earned cosemetics.I have played this game on and off throughout EA. Now that the game has released I am super happy to see how well it looks and the gameplay has always been as good as it has been. name: ELEX II
detailed_description: ELEX II is the sequel to ELEX , the vintage open-world role-playing experience from the award-winning creators of the Gothic and Risen series, Piranha Bytes. ELEX II returns to the post-apocalyptic Science Fantasy world of Magalan – with massive environments that can be explored with unrivaled freedom via jetpack, you will be able to move through the epic story any way you want. Several years after Jax defeated the Hybrid, a new threat arrives from the sky, unleashing the dangerous powers of dark Elex and endangering all life on the planet. In order to defend the peace on Magalan and the safety of his own family, Jax has to go on a mission to convince the factions to unite against the invaders and find his own son, Dex, who got separated from him … Dive into a huge, hand-crafted, completely unique world with multiple factions and diverse environments set in a post-apocalyptic science fantasy universe. The game allows you to: explore the planet of Magalan with unprecedented freedom, using your trusted jetpack to traverse the map and even fly! interact with a lived-in world, full of unique NPCs, who will remember what you’ve done and react accordingly will join or leave your group depending on how you behave are able to be killed, which will have an effect on the story engage in fluid close and ranged combat with a massively improved control system experience a story where your actions have consequences, immersing you in a world of moral decisions Powered by the Piranha Bytes Engine Genome in its 6th iteration.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s expensive for what you get. The combat is ♥♥♥♥ and the story is a hot mess to the point where I was actually laughing towards the end. Elex has one redeeming factor like most PB games: a satisfying sense of exploration as you roam the open world, but to be honest even this aspect has a short life span, as you quickly reach the cap gear and all exploration is a waste of time. It got the point where I had the best weapon and had spent all skill points where everything RPG related in the game become obsolete. They really needed to expand the faction’s skill set and do something about itemization, as this really killed my enjoyment the most. There’s nothing more boring than having no reason to kill a monster and loot it in an RPG.The dialogue is very entertaining a lot of the time as PB doesn’t shy away from adult themes and language. However, they need to balance the use of such language and themes as having it practically everywhere all the time makes the world feel ridiculous, but I do appreciate a bit of real-world dialogue instead of the usual cringe you get where everyone talks like they’re in a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Harry Potter novel. The final boss encounter is so cooky and nonsensical that I just shook my head as I was kitting the guy around, I won’t spoil it but if you’re into SCI-FI and you ever reach the end of the game—getting there is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ grind and slog—you’ll get what I’m talking about. I mean the story at this point is just getting so ridiculous anyway maybe you might be desensitized, but still it was just the cherry on top.  Overall, I’d probably wait until it’s on sale instead of paying full price. If you a proper RPG enjoyer then you will like this game as long as you figure out how to play. The first thing you want to do with bind dodge to its own key and disable the double tap. Also never make sure of the lock on target function at all. Once you learn to dodge properly the combat works, it’s just very repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: A good entry despite a stale first impression.Once you get used to the changes, the game actually feels like an improvement over its predecessor in many ways.The pros are : Setting is better used and the writing is bleaker (some characters don't look or sound the same but that's no big deal imho), character sheet gives actual info this time, gameplay and combat is faster. It also feels good to go back to a place you know from the first game and see how it changed/remained.There's some cons : like the graphics needing some improvements or the combat feeling less like a souls and easier. But if you get over it you find that the rythme of the game benefits from it and the landscapes can also be stunning at times. All in all, the pace is better but your character feels a little more floaty (same as Gothic 3 was compared to the first two but a lot less).Also, bugs, but nothing really new here, although I seem to be less impacted than some (I use high end GPUs to play games, both NVIDIA (3070) and AMD(6800XT), so maybe there's that Idk).Personnaly, I find myself having more fun with ELEX II than I expected at first.If it could be patched, the game would be more than decent, like the first was.Hope PB give some news at some point about that (a better communication and some transparency would help a lot I guess).Conclusion : If you enjoy PB games, you should like this one also.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand the negative reviews this game received from folks who normally like PiranhaBytes games. For me, this hit the sequel sweet spot by balancing the familiar and the new, with a handful of QoL improvements thrown in. My only significant complaints are the simplification of the combat and crafting systems, but they weren't game-breaking, and there is still a noticeable power curve in character progression. The game also had an unfinished feel to some aspects, as if the Suits demanded release before the developers were ready. All in all, I enjoyed it as much as Elex 1, and I look fwd to re-playing it in another faction.The Good------------ The world: as with previous games, the love and attention to detail of the world is the shining star of the game. I rarely used fast travel because just walking through the countryside was so visually rewarding. And once again exploration of out-of-the-way places almost always yielded some material gain or at least a narrative tableau. Also, they did something clever for a sequel by having half of the map be new territory and the other half being part of the old world, yet changed in interesting ways.- Similar tactic taken with NPCs and factions, where there's a mix of old and new friends.- The jetpack now has a skill tree that allows it to be significantly improved.- Markers can now be added to the map.- Improved graphics, especially running water.- Background music that is evocative without being too invasive.- Map markers to help find corpses yet to be looted.- A convenient headlamp.- Variety in NPC companion quests - not all just fights.- Ability to mark/unmark items as junk, for ease of selling.- Creature sound effects.The Bad---------- Simplified combat and crafting.- Can't combine smaller potions into larger ones.- Limit on the number of markers that can be placed on the map.- False sense of urgency in the plot at times, especially a recurring 'infection.' - Can't remap some frequently-used keys.- A sense that the game was rushed/unfinished. The Ugly---------- The closure of PiranhaBytes Studios, meaning that the significant story setup for Elex III will never be realised.  Here's hoping that the new Pithead Studios can continue to create games of this ilk.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the first Elex. Janky like its predecessor but less boring and definitely less grindy and difficult.- environment graphics are great : vegetation is dense and varied, the buildings, interiors and ruins believable and the lighting is top-tier. Snowy and rocky areas are also well made.- exploration is very pleasant, although almost pointless since most of Points of Interest contain nothing else than scrap and useless items. By the way, even if you discover legendary items there is little to no chance you can use them since the prerequesites are always far too high.- the enhanced jet-pack helps a lot to make the game less boring and slow since it has now an after-burner feature allowing the player to increase horizontal thrust significantly.- the character progression system is sh*tty and old. And yes, you'll still have to find instructors to learn skills.- UI is old and navigating in it is a chore (at least with keyboard/mouse). Especially the inventory in which you'll have to roll down or up to find what you need.- character models are awful (among the worst I've ever seen in the last decade). Moreover, a lot of important npcs are clones. Terrible work.- the music is bland and gets quickly unbearable because it plays continiously, which in a RPG, requiring by definition long game sessions, is always a bad idea. Apparently the OST was made by the game director who is definitely not up to the task. They should really hire a professional composer for their next game.- the quests are tedious, you'll pass a lot of time doing chores and errands for people just to be able to do more chores and errands for other people of higher rank. Lazy as ♥♥♥♥. And a lot of factions quests are mirrored which wouldn't have been a issue if the game didn't encourage you to involve yourself in their problems even if you already have chosen your faction (you can only choose one).- combat system is basic and janky. AI is very bad even in max difficulty (the difficulty only changes life pool of enemies and damage done/received). Ranged weapons are incredibly unbalanced and broken. Coupled with the enhanced jet-pack, they make every encouters, even against the most powerful enemies, trivial.Elex 2 would have been a great achievement for a new studio but for a 20 years old studio like PB which always makes the same game and the same mistakes, it's really infuriating. It's like they lived in a grotto since 2002 and never got out.This could have been a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: What to expect:-beautiful hand-made scenery and meaningful and interconnected quest (as against generic Ubisoft games),-satisfying loot found on the most peculiar places (thorough exploration of the map is highly recommended),-quite conservative approach towards the gameplay (do not expect any help from the game - first creature you encounter will most definitely kill you, no auto-healing (only potions, food and good-night sleep), limited guidance to as how to finish quests - requires some reading),-satisfaction from progressing through the game that you won't get from modern mainstream games.This game is a hidden gem, although a rough one.BTW: Yes, you can change hotkeys according to your needs. The guy that says otherwise and gave the game thumbs down after playing it for 21 minutes is a complete morkon.BTW2: Surprise, surprise: You actually have to talk to NPCs so that they learned that the quest is finished and the game can continue. Just like in the real world. This is not primitive "go to the red marker, kill everything around, go to another one ect., ect., ect..." You have to think. If you are not ready to accept that, if you are not able to put in some effort, choose Ubisoft games. This one is not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: + Good side quests+ Unique and interesting factions+ Cool world with fun exploration+ Jetpack- clunky combat and looting- very repetitive combat- some stale storytelling- bad cutscenesElex II is a game I got into with no prior knowledge of 'AA games'. I had another game by this studio in my library that I had played for a couple of hours several years ago and dropped because I couldn't figure it out. Aside from that brief experience, I didn't really know what a AA game was before I played this one.I went into Elex II expecting it to be just kind of okay, but I got hooked really quickly. The looting is extremely clunky in addition to the melee combat, but for some reason that didn't actually bother me after I figured out how to make it work for me. I was very surprised with how much fun I had playing this.I got massive Fallout: NV or Fallout 3 vibes from this title. It has dialogue options that are based on your skills, factions you can join that alter your abilities and play style, and it has companions that can join you on your adventures and have quests of their own for you to complete. The companions are not equal however, as there are a couple who are just annoying and not really worth helping in anyway (I did anyways because I like to do everything I can in games like this).This game is apparently a direct sequel to the first Elex, but as someone who did not play the first and had no idea what kind of story to expect, I was still able to fully understand the plot and the motivations of the various characters I met. All-in-all, the main story and campaign is just kind of okay, while the side quests are much more interesting.Combat does become quite monotonous after a while and the combat is a major part of the game play. The melee combat is very clunky and not particularly fun, so I played almost my entire game time with ranged weapons. Once I found a particular shotgun, I almost exclusively used it throughout the rest of my play through as it was kind of OP and made combat encounters really easy and basic.In conclusion, I would 100% recommend this game as I had a really good time with it despite the jankiness. I would not recommend buying at full price due to the amount of clunk and high cost, but on sale, this game is a blast.Happy gaming!

_childDocuments_.review: Quick review - all the reasons i will not accept this game in its current state.After closing the game normally it refuses to start again. Only getting a black screen and "App not responding".Performance with an AMD 5950X + 32GB DDR4 3800 C14 + RTX 3080 is really bad @ 2560x1440 with high/max settings. It barely holds 60fps, often enough it dips below 60fps into mid 50s - while doing so, it feels more like 30-40fps. Graphics are as mediocre and dated like in Elex 1. Textures are not bad, not good. Animations are again pretty bad and faces are looking weird depending on lighting sometimes. The childs face... i don't know but i guess this will haunt me in my nightmares. Animations are clunky and even walking / running looks superstiff.Faces / expression are mediocre at best - same as in Elex 1.Very often when running over a small rock or piece of metal or wood, i got pushed away or sometimes bumped into the air - this allready started in the tutorial area. Combat - oh boy, not like this again. As animations are clunky as f_uck, so is the combat. It feels so wrong overall. Feedback is better compared to Elex 1 but overall it is still not really good. It's not fun at all to use melee attacks. Weirdest thing i had - some enemies i did hit with the steel pipe got smashed to the ground or kicked 10 meters away from me like using superpowers. When starting an attack or a fight, it feels like every movement stops to actually use the attack animation. Fluid combat is basically non-existing. The movement keybinds need to be changed as nearly EVERY RPG or Actions game / RPG uses SPACE for jumping and W/A/S/D + SPACE for a role or dodge. But Elex II is different here - W/A/S/D and STRG / CTRL will role / dodge - not very intuitive. It is a basic movement set that is usually on SPACE. I could list more but yeah - it is simply annoying. Enjoy changing your keybinds to what is normal.Cutscenes are triggered with 0 transition. You walk into an area without knowing that it triggers a cutscene and BOOM camera switches and cutscene starts. This is so immersion breaking.World design is ok i guess but the starting area and first camps is not very memorable for me. There is nothing around that makes me think "Wow, this is amazing! I stay here for a second and have to look at this!". I will not rate story or anything like that. I can't play a game longer than 20-30 minutes when performance is so bad, combat is clunky and keybinds/movement destroy any fun.Elex 1 was disappointing and Elex 2 is more of the same. Just wait 1-2 years until it is patched into a enjoyable experience.Right now - can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: is a third-person action role-playing game (ARPG) by Piranha Bytes. The games by this German studio are so unique in terms of atmosphere and playstyle, they might as well be their own subgenre within ARPGs. That's why I'll refer to the collective works of Piranha Bytes as 'PB games' in this review. was definitely the best PB game since Risen, and maybe even since Gothic 2.   continues this trend and manages to top its predecessor. Elex 2 has a true open world with exciting and dangerous places to discover. It has five joinable factions, each having a distinct philosophy and memorable NPCs. It offers choices that matter in the long run, and it has noticeable character progression. But  does have its flaws, as well. The melee combat can feel clunky (yes, again!) and the attribute system is little else than a platform for skill and weapon requirements. If you're into PB games and especially , you'll like or even love . If you're into ARPGs but aren't sure about PB games, first you need to answer two questions. 1. Do you expect games to be perfectly polished? 2. Do you expect to be a god who can kill anything in his way from the very beginning of a game? If you answered 'yes' to either question,  is not for you. If you think you can accept some flaws and a difficulty curve, provided the other aspects of ARPGs are present and excitingly so, you may want to give  a chance. You play Jax, a former Alb commander. In the first Elex game, he saves the world from a threat, only to find out years later that there is another related threat that requires him to take up the role of reluctant saviour of the planet Magalan once again.Gameplay is typical third-person ARPG with three types of combat: melee, ranged and magic.For some reason, melee combat is often the worst part of PB games. In Gothic, Gothic 2 and Risen, melee combat was okay, but in their other games it was pretty bad. In Elex there was some improvement but a ranged build was still superior to a melee build, In Elex 2, the melee combat is a bit better than it was in Elex, but the execution still causes frustration due to the clunky combat.So ranged combat is a lot more enjoyable. There is a wide range of ranged weapons in . Bows and crossbows, as seen in the Gothic series. Guns, as seen in the last two Risen games. And you'll also be able to use flamethrowers, harpoon guns, laser rifles, and so on.Magic is a valid option but not as overpowered as it was in some previous PB games. Both the Berserker and Alb factions have decent magic spells but you will want to invest in another weapon type (melee or ranged) for the times where you’re out of magical power. has classic character development. You gain XP by completing quests and killing opponents. When you level up, you can increase attributes and abilities. You need to increase your attributes to learn better abilities and to equip better weapons. The attribute increase by itself doesn’t make you much stronger. For every 5 points invested in an attribute, you gain 1 point. For example, every 5 points you invest in dexterity will increase your ranged damage by one. When your ranged weapons deal 500+ damage, a +1 bonus means nothing.The factions are satisfyingly different and they each offer strong and weak points. Also, some factions can only be joined after you’ve reached a certain rank in another faction. This adds to replayability. The jetpack from the first game gets a huge upgrade. Again, it adds an additional dimension to the game world, because you can explore the roofs of buildings and towers and such, and often get rewarded for it. But in  you can upgrade the jetpack by adding more fuel so as to be able to stay in the air longer, you can learn how to float in the air while using your weapons to pick off enemies, and so on.PB games never start out easy.  is no exception but to me it felt like the easiest PB game to surmount that initial difficulty curve. The graphics of  aren't triple-A quality. To hide this a bit, PB decided to cover the world in a permanent fog. I think this was a bad choice. I even made a guide that explains how to reduce or remove the fog. And although the graphics still don't look perfect after that little tweak, I think the world of Elex is a lot nicer than its creators gave themselves credit for. The music is atmospheric but not memorable. The quality of the sound effects is okay. The voice acting is decent to good. I have to stress that lip syncing is amazing in this game. I don’t remember a game where the lip sync was so spot on that I took notice of it. Even though the game was originally in German, the English voiceover goes with the most perfect lip sync I ever saw, so  deserves a very special nomination for that.  has 6 Steam Trading Cards. You'll get 3 while running the game.The 50 Steam Achievements are extremely varied. There are some story-related achievements, some faction-related achievements, some achievements that require you to collect a series of items scattered across the game world, some achievements that require you to do menial tasks like killing x opponents by means of y, or collecting x amount of elexit (the currency in the game).

_childDocuments_.review: Elex 2I'll try to keep it short as much as I can, but still cover all of the important aspects of the game.For you who didn't play Elex 1 yet, I recommend you to play it first before this one. Because this is a direct sequel from the first game.This is quite a good game, there are things that really good but some others are really bad so it's kinda a mixed review. The most exciting about this game is the exploring itself, it feels like the environment has its own story,  For example, you see some dead bodies and you read notes or listen to an audio journal near them then you can imagine what was happened there. Or even something simple like you just walking and suddenly you step on a trap mine and you realized there are so many trap mines in the area. at first, you might think that it's just placed randomly, but NO. after I passed the trap mines I saw a tent near them with a couple of rations and potions. Which means? There is someone who lives there and wants to defend themself by planting so many trap mines near their tent. That’s one of the reasons for me wanting to keep exploring Magalan and I've never ever get bored from it.The other thing is the side story, the side story really helps to build the world more immersive and it makes the NPC, world, and everything on it feel alive.Now we talk about the bad things about the game,AnimationThe animation itself is pretty good to be honest, but the transition of each animation is so bad. It makes the combat feel clunky, especially on Melee combat.Cutscenes (In-game scene, not the CG Animation like on the intro)The cutscenes are horrendous, it’s not just it doesn’t feel cinematic at all but the flow of each shot of the cutscenes is just really bad. It feels like different shots crammed into 1 scene and so many cutscenes that feel pointless.StoryAll I can say is that the story itself is pretty good, but the execution not so much. Especially with the cutscenes issue I mentioned above. I really hope that Elex 3 will be much better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: With both eyes closed, i'm giving this game a thumps up.I wouldn't have wanted to pay 50 bucks for it though. Since you can get it for 15 now, i guess it's a good deal and I've spent the whole last 4 days in the game, that should be worth something.Positives: Awesome Map, that isn't too big, even though at first it seems that way, but with your glider you can get from A to B really fast and makes it way more managable.It feels nice to roam around and experience the high amount of detail they put into this world, which definitely received the most attention of the developers.Negatives:Obviously the combat system sucks, I mean i'm used to gothic combat style, but it should be way better by now, it's anything but smooth. The only fun thing in wielding a sword is, the fighting with the glider, which also fails like 50% of the time, but at least feels a little better than the standard fighting.Parrying with the sword or the shield, just feels akward, you constantly are too close to the enemy, so you hit/parry behind/through the enemy which isn't fun and somehow you get damage afterwards anyway, just aweful.On the upside melee weapons are at least balanced, switching to shotgun after 45 hours gameplay was just nuts. 4 shots with the Lead Spreader and you kill behemoths, which is fun at first, but it kinda feels like cheating. Reloading with ranged weapons is also pointless, since unequip/equip saves you half the time.The aiming aid has an options to be turned off, but doesn't quite stop helping me to aim, and since the aidactually makes it harder to aim, that as well quite sucks.It's also annoying that stealth doesn't quite work that well, since people can see you through walls, so not quite the game experience i was looking for. I'm also not sure if it's intentionally that the weapons, enemys drop after being killed, are most of the time gone, or if there's some RNG behind, it's just seems odd. Voluntarily or not I'm not a fan of that.And after discovering the functions of the Sunglasses (highly recommended/game chaning) i've found out, that the weapons are definitely gone, since at first it seemed like they get shot through the map ridiculously far away, after dealing the killing blow.Storywise i'd say it's a matter of taste, so i probably shouldn't rate that.I just didn't like the missing depth in the story of the fractions.It had a great start and suddenly it kind of ended, and it seemed like i spent way more time thinking about which Fraction to join, only to find out that there isn't really a lot to find out, which was kind of a bummer and killed a little bit of the immersion, which i experienced up until that point, at least that's how i felt about it, maybe the other fractions would have had more story idk.Well to summarize I wanna say it's a good game which could have been a great one.PS: Needless to say, this game is still buggy as ♥♥♥♥, i think it crashed at least 15 times on me in almost 60 hours, including two bluescreens which i haven't seen in a long time, so i guess good job on that.(The crashes all seemed related to opening crates and afterwards the map, or generally opening the Inventory or the Menu in general ).Also there where Quests that cannot be solved, since the things you need to find are not even there (known).The night is only dark for like 5 minutes and then everything looks kind of grey (known ).Hope those will be fixed soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: after playing a bit more I decided to change my review to a thumbs down for now. Performance is problematic. Not unplayable if you have above recommended specs but jarring, especially in settlements. However that's not the reason for the thumbs down. The main reason is the story. I think it was a mistake to continue with Jax as main protagonist. To accommodate certain gameplay with the story they had to quite literally wipe the memory of most of the characters in the game. Despite Jax being the big hero who defeated the Hybrid and having only been a few years, most characters you come across have no clue. Jax doesn't bother pointing it out either. It's even worse when you come across characters you had quests with in the first game. You can clearly see how the writing collides with the gameplay leading to serious inconsistencies. And to top it all off, the story has about the same core beats. You get wrecked at the beginning of the game, and need to find your power while uniting the clans against another common threat, minus the revenge sub-plot but with added aliens. It has some twists but it's a lot more predictable than the first one.Original:The game has some performance issues in certain areas but otherwise it's stable. The camera zooming in and out as you sprint is also pretty bad, and some character models are awful. However beyond these issues the game is an improvement over Elex 1 in every aspect. The melee combat in particular is significantly better with a lot of variety to keep it fresh, interesting and fair. If you loved the first one and are willing to put up with some issues getting this one is a no-brainer. Otherwise you may want to wait for a sale, or just try it out and refund if unhappy.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to love Piranha Bytes games since Gothic 1 I played them all, They used to have interesting characters, stories and love for details. Elex 1 was a good game, with characters that had a story to tell, but Elex 2 is sooo boring and disappointing, with incredibly dull characters, the main story is basically the same as in Elex 1... recruit people for your base, deactivate terraformers, fight the evil force. The factions seem half-finished, with empty and bad designed cities (except the berserker base, which is ok). in the Kleriker faction, there is basically no one to talk to. The map is missing interesting hideouts, which piranha bytes games used to have so many of. The overall Quest Design is super annoying because most of the time there is a direct follow-up quest, with the purpose to just send you walking through the map, just to raise playtime it seems.. whyyy?The kid of Jax looks like a shrunken adult, and that entire storyline is sooo ♥♥♥♥♥♥, that I could not care less if he lived or died.I hope for Piranha Bytes to go back to the basics of RPG Design, and design interesting stories and not games that have 100+ hours of playtime. Keep players by engaging them in a story and not by keeping them busy with a thousand follow up quests that seem worthless. It seems like the writing team ran out of ideas for Elex 2 and just recycled Elex1, so when You played Elex1 I recommend skipping this one, you are not missing out on anything!I hate to write a bad review and I really tried to like Elex2, but unfortunately, it is such a waste of time and money, that I can't hide my disappointment.

_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: Overall an improvement over the first game, but still with a lot of jank. For me the most important upgrade they made is to the melee combat, which is now serviceable, it was so bad in the previous title I had to force myself to continue play until the end.The graphics look noticeable better, with really nice looking environments at times, but the character faces look sometimes I think worse than  Elex 1, don't know how they managed that.Sound is mostly the same with good voice acting given the script, except they really can't do dramatic scenes, every single one of them is cringe even if I can tell that the actors did their best, the stiff face animations with dead eyes and awkward choreography is absolutely top Eurojank and I could not stop laughing in the last act where everything should be super serious.Story is ok with lots of big choices that alter the game and small ones that help with the immersion tremendously, a really nice aspect of the game and I wish more developers would do this. Unfortunately the last chapter is the weakest part, they overwhelm you with stuff that made me roll my eyes and because they can't make serious scenes like I previously said, I couldn't take the ending seriously, maybe ditch the In-game cringe Cutscenes with prerendered Cgi next time.
