_childDocuments_.review: I have given this game a chance, but after 40h I am very disappointed. It is like the Elex one, but much worse. -The map is smaller-Many iconic places from the first part are gone. No Alb fortress, now city under dome, no berserk city. And all that for no reason in the story. You just have an invisible wall. Even locations that should be on the map, like Calan launch bay, or shipyard on the south coast, are just erased with no explanation. -Story. It is literally the very same story from the first one. Same plot twists, same characters, same friends, and same enemies. Almost nothing new. -No consequences of choice. If you become alb, you will be forced to kill some albs soldiers and still be alb, no one will notice, no one will be angry at you, nothing. You will have no option not to kill them, no diplomatic solution, nothing.  -No NPC day rutince. All NPCs are just standing still (or moving in circle) 24/7-All main story enemies are just Alb soldiers with different colors of armor. Weapons are similar, AI of units is the same, even lore is the same.-A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of “logic holes” in story and in dialogs. -There are 4 factions but all seem the same. All want to just destroy all others. In first part, such behavior was seen just from desert people, berseks ware eco terrorist, separatists tried to survieve, clerics were religius. Now all of them are just killers for no reason. -You don’t feel your character progress. and all enemies slowly become stronger, on level 40, you do the same damage as on level 25, but to kill an enemy you need ~15 shots on level 40 while on level 25 it was like 4-5 shots. -There are just 3 types of quests. First is to kill X enemies in Y location. Second is to go to Y location with some NPC and kill X enemies. Third is to go to Y location and take/use something there, ow… and to do that you have to kill all enemies first. I mean it. There is NO other quest at all.Only positive thing I see is less bugs in the game. But the whole game looks like one big bug.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is completely directionless, which encourages you to explore the map. That could have been a good thing, but... In fact, you are punished for playing the game at all. I knew it would be like that (because I've played the first one), which is why I used cheats and infinite health right from the beginning (recommended). It's one design aspect of this game that I simply don't understand, and don't like.I have played for more than the registered two hours, at least double that (maybe I was offline the first part of the game). So I've seen a bit of the map.When I see something in the landscape that catches my eye, I tend to become curious and want to explore. Like the ruins of a city... Lesson learned, don't go there. There was nothing interesting there, and nothing interesting along the way. Only overpowered monsters and some loot.And that's my impression of this game. A map with enemies and loot. For hours.I have no idea what the story is like, but if it's like the first game, it will grow on you and become more interesting the more you play. But... It shouldn't be such a pain to get there. A game shouldn't be an effort to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I was going to give this game a solid 6/10 and move on but the more i thought about it the more i realised i would never recommend this game to someone i knew, even if they liked the first game. To keep it short; some pros and cons.Pros: - The combat is better than Elex 1- The buildcraft and faction-specific skills are better than Elex 1- The traversal is better than Elex 1 (jetpack is fun now)- That's it. Cons: - Worse voice acting (quite an impressive feat). I never thought i would actually want the original Jax voice actor back. - Dated, mediocre Eurojank combat. Better than Elex 1 but that's an extremely low bar. - Worse factions. They're watered down and feel like a means to an end instead of the ideological commitment the first game asked of you.- Worse artistic expression. The map, while being easier to traverse, is a whole lot less visually striking and WAY less unique. No more cool biomes. Now you have forest, snow and wasteland city. Even the clearly alien black and neon blue Elex crystals are just regular old stones with some blue in them now. Whole aesthetic of the games feels more generic and less unique.-Locked into a specific world-state you might not have chosen in Elex 1. Including the faction, romance and ending. Spoilers, the forced world-state was far from the one i wanted. - Worse story. It's just so wonky and poorly paced, characters acting weird, decisions being made not because it makes sense for any human to make them but because the plot needs those decisions to happen. The whole thing just feels like wheel-spinning awkwardness. Nothing you do in the story feels urgent or important until the third act and even then, you get one good mission and then the game ends. And the ending fuggin' sucks. - Worse mission structure. Like, so much worse. Although the balance and progression in Elex 1 was terrible and the difficulty spike would sometimes uppercut the mana outta you, those missions were still fun. The game asked you to do cool things and the set pieces were memorable. This game however has so many excruciatingly uninteresting 'kill missions'. You better love the combat because the amount of times the game simply asks you to 'go here, kill 20 enemies' is obscene. Almost felt like Anthem with the egregious main quest padding. - Worse characters. So many returning NPCs barely feel like the previously established people they were and the new characters might as well be a checklist with a few bullet points under them. "Angy, mother, plot device" are just about the only meaningful characteristics of one of the MAIN CHARACTERS in the story. Before i bought Elex 2, i read the reviews online and i saw all these posts saying that Elex 1 was better. I thought those people were insane. There was no way Elex 2 could be worse, the gameplay looks so much better, the progression is more forgiving, some semblance of balance now exists! Surely these people are just 'back in my day' Elex 1 gamer boomers allergic to change. But i was wrong. Truly, this game is just a net negative when compared to its predecessor. You lose out on everything that made the first game unique and the only thing we have to show for it is a jetpack and some still garbage combat. Buy Elex 1 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I played ELEX 1 and liked it but it became a bit of a slog after a while and I couldn't finish it. _childDocuments_.review: Elex 2 is a decent game. Still feels like a Piranha Bytes game, but less cohesive compared to previous titles, exactly how I felt with Elex 1.First time in all Piranha Bytes the music and ambient sounds weren't as epic and sometimes felt out of place. Some tracks reminded me of default music from The Sims... Imagine that. ehh..Movement felt floaty at first but after several hours I adapted to it and it felt good for the rest of the playthrough.They finally fixed accidental "sit on a stool" or "sleep in bed" misclicks. Now you have to hold the button for several seconds to initiate that action. It's a massive Quality of Life improvement. Especially when combing through cities and stealing all the loot from NPC houses ^^Now you can put custom markers on map. You can choose different Icons. Awesome to mark a chest you can't open yet, a difficult monster or a point of interest for later. Too bad that the limit is about 90+ of them. So you can't be too spammy. Combat is a bit different. Melee is definitely improved. More enjoyable than in the previous game. Ranged combat is mediocre. Hitboxes are inaccurate at best.Jet pack is so fun to use now (after upgrading the fuel quite a bit). You can not only go up, but move forward with it. So the pace you can scout an area is incredible. I find the jet pack controls very intuitive for the most part. You can even attack flying monsters in melee with it. Works really well. BUT. I think Jet pack is the main reason why Elex and Elex 2 suffers the most. The exploration, dodging, avoiding damage, dangerous situations (even on max difficulty) is just too easy with it. Even tho most monsters have either ranged or leap ability, it still makes all fights too trivial. Stealing from homes are just too easy with it too. You don't need to find a window or go through the front door. You can just fly on the roof and go from there without anyone noticing. It's too cheesy and too easy. Sadly.Exploration, talking about item discovery, is better than In Elex 1 where most loot was basically useless junk. Now in order to get the best gear - you need to find 3 damaged weapons of that type first, then upgrade it. The next step is to either once again find 3 damaged ones or find another normal weapon of that type, and combine those two to fully max it out. It encourages you to actually explore the areas and buildings. + you can find unique items too. They have lower stat requirements, but can't deal as much damage as a maxed out normal weapon (in most cases). Which is good. BUT! Too bad that the best way to acquire most weapons quite easily is just to pickpocket them from various NPCs. Another thing. Much less visual clutter in Elex 2. Which is a great and bad thing. Great that it's better for the eyes and is easier to spot things, but bad, because the interiors and exteriors feel way too flat sometimes and too clean in some way. Doesn't really suit that apocalyptic world we are playing in.But overall I liked it, felt more in line with what we had in Gothic series.Some dialogues didn't make any sense knowing what actually happened in Elex 1. it's like Jax forgot most about it. Even though Elex 2 plot is like 6 years or so apart from Elex 1. The last chapter is a mess. It's rushed, segmented and disjointed. The way they wanted to make it dramatic felt so amateurish and unbelievable. Like - who cares if this or that happens to that x NPC. The overall presentation just didn't deliver. Elex 1 had much better ending. And that says a lot.Of course, Elex 2, like every PB game, has bugs, enemy/npc pathing issues, but none of them are game breaking. They are more like a feature at this point.Overall, a good game to explore (the map is huge) but not as good if you just want to go from mission to mission. Gets a bit boring at the midpoint and fairly repetitive (hello companion quests...). The story is a mess and has very little intrigue or mystery. Everything felt like you've already seen this in Elex 1 in one way or another.I know that Piranha Bytes are in a difficult situation right now, but I hope they will stay alive as a company and keep delivering us these unique RPGs in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked Elex 1 and I thought it was a great base to build upon for this game, which is why I'm so confused about what happened, because in my opinion Elex 2 is worse than the first in every regard. Even the character models look worse.All the memorable places from the first one are now either random ruins in the middle of a forest or random ruins in the middle of a snowfield, but none of them feel special. There are fun characters with typical PB dialogue, but the new "polished" character models look so uncanny that it just doesn't feel alive.Even though the combat systems in PB games are always clunky/janky, this one feels downright unresponsive at times. It's one of the worst combat systems I've ever had to play. I ended up switching from melee/magic to ranged weapons, because even though they don't feel especially great, at least they work.The story just felt way too big for the world it's set in with the almighty overlords from space who fight like every random bandit in a bar fight. Also the main character having a kid just feels really out of place in these "dirty" PB worlds and the kid being involved in the overarching alien story didn't make it any better to say the least.The one thing that does work and feel fun to use is the jetpack, but that's sadly about it.TLDR: Even if you are a fan of PB games and liked Elex 1, I'd recommend replaying that instead of playing Elex 2.
_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: You've heard of Souls-like now get ready for STOOLS-LIKE!Joking aside I had mixed feelings playing Elex 2. I never played the first one so I didn't have a ton of expectations, but the amount of very negative reviews made me expect something much worse. Is Elex 2 a good game? not really, but it gives you enough systems and freedoms that I can forgive most of the jank. If you play this expecting a modern AAA or even AA title then you will probably be disappointed. BUT, if you are like me and you despise modern gaming as it exists mostly just to sell you junk, then try this out and have a little nostalgia for better times. Every game does NOT need to be some cookie cutter corporate engagement driven live service, and I hope these dudes keep making their weird games.

_childDocuments_.review: More Elex.  I can dig it.  This world feels very immersive.  Everything in Elex has it's place.  Loot and items are placed individually. The people have relationships and purpose.  Helping one npc may anger another.  Completing a quest may block off another quest.  The NPCs have their wants and needs and it's up to you how you approach things.   You start weak in a dangerous world, yet there's a ton of freedom and many ways to solve problems.  The entire world is all there for you to explore how you want from the start.  The game is janky, but it offers an RPG experience you can't get from AAA games.  This game has an identity.  It's telling a story.  It's not jam packed with trendy mechanics and content that exists solely to take up time and space.  Combat has been improved quite a bit and so has voice acting.  Piranha Bytes makes special games.  Elex 2 is no exception.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a pretty fun game, definitely could use some work. The ending was a bit underwhelming though, the hype was built up for the Bastion but nothing became of it. Final fights were bullcrap, the allies were just standing around and I did all the work. Not sure why I spent so much time recruiting them..Pros:- Great scifi fantasy settings, and I love that people are effing a-holes.- Scenery and lighting look gorgeous at times.- Combat is much more fluid than the original.- Entertaining quests and lots of dialogues, getting Witcher 3 vibes. Loving the quests a lot.- Skills and jet pack upgrades are meaningful and make the game so much better to play.- Kiting enemies together and watch them fight is always fun.- The grind is rewarding even just a few hours in.Cons:- Kinda miss that timing for combo, now it's just light/hard attack. - FOV is a bit too close and personal, got used to it after a bit, but it does get a bit nauseous. - Terrible cutscene transitioning..- Characters look worse than the original imo.- Stupid companions. Like bro, don't run in and block my attacks when I'm dueling ffs.- Spells are a bit underwhelming.- Weak quests towards the end.Bugs:- I get black shadows (?) popping up out of nowhere then game crashes.- Jax wouldn't wake up after sleeping - I feel you dude..- Irissa in Ignadon is a b!tch and won't trigger the quest.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game if you are accustomed to Piranha Bites games in general. If you have never played a game from this studio, keep in mind there is a bit of "jank" to some mechanics in the game, such as the combat. Don't go into this expecting AAA Quality gameplay.With that said, the game pretty much takes systems & mechanics from the first Elex and makes improvements/changes to them. The story continues from the first one and from what I have seen, a lot of the same characters from the first game are in this one. Its a fun game for a Piranha Bites fan and I recommend picking this up.
_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: My first impression is very good! The mechanics and movement feels familiar from the first part, but a bit smoother. The character designs are new and the whole textures are looking better. Most surprising are the VERY GOOD looking cutscenes, compared to the Piranha Bytes standard. You shoudln't expect an AAA quality, but a huge jump forward!After a couple hours it feels like a much more beautiful first part with better controls and I'm very ok with that. There are a lot of referals to the first part, in kind of e.g. recurring characters. The game is not like playing 6 hours per session, at least for me, but I'm enjoying to explore the beautiful world and to fill my inventory with tons of discovered items.So if the game will tell a good story too, then I'm pretty satisfied with Priranha Byte's work! :)UPDATE:After playing through the possible fractions I think, that you will have your fun with ELEX 2, but it's not made for everyone - and this is good! The way of "gather your allies and prepare for what's coming" is actually pretty much the same we've known from part one, but with even more decisions, VERY needy comrades, FIVE fractions for the first time and more information about "wtf is happening on that damn planet".
_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: If you were a fan of the first Elex, you kind of know what to expect.If you were a fan of the Risen games, you also kind of know what to expect.If you were a fan of the Gothic series... you understand the god awful humor.I'm 17 hours in and have enjoyed the game as much as I did the first Elex. The graphics are excellent, the dialogue is awful, the story is interesting, and the gameplay is good. Is this the best game ever? Probably not. But it's a solid playthrough and worth your sheckles.
_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game in alot of ways.  The only crafting I could find was upgrading weapons.  I Couldn't craft shotgun ammo either...so most of my money was spent on ammo since all the melee weapons were slow to kill and annoying.  I used the 1 handed lightning sword and it was okay, but  forget about a shield just runs you out of stamina and gets you killed.  I found the hacking fun but the slider chests were annoying and tedious.  I preferred the way it was done on part 1 it seemed less annoying.  The 45 degree angle made it hard to tell if the pin was up or down.   The story was great, but missing details, like I talked to my wife and she didn't talk about her kid or anything like just stupid berserker stuff.  They were terrible parents haha.  The companion quests are a bit boring mostly.  Especially the android.  It was fun to find recordings and notes but would prefer them to have lead to some solvable quest or mystery.  I remember in Fallout there was some pretty fun murder mysteries to solve from clues and recordings.  It would have been nice to be able to dig and do some treasure hunting and grave robbing.  Exploration was great, but kind of annoying with the freezing and poison barriers...Rather just have an invisible wall than to die because you can't get back in time.  The fighting was fair, since there is difficulty settings for when it got impossible.  I liked the shooting, but the electric weapons were lousy not like in Elex 1 where I used those mostly.  All in All I would recommend because it's like Gothic in alot of ways, but not nearly as good.  Hoping part 3 will bring more customization of weapons, armor and character.  I prefer more options for choosing spells etc.  Magic wasn't even worth messing with and I didn't want to join a faction because all of the factions were idiots.  I had no interest in any of their goals or values.  Looking forward to seeing part 3.  Games of this type seem pretty rare.  Loved the graphics, loved the combat, just need more versatility.  It's nice to play a game that I can finish and enjoy.

_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the first one and felt like it had its moments, but was extremely janky and lacked story, enjoyable combat, and graphics. This one has slightly better graphics, though still not good. There is a scene near the beginning where there is a panning, overhead shot that is supposed to show you a glimpse of the world around you. It's a world filled with blocky polygons that look like they are made out of modeling clay. The disparity between the intro cutscene and how things look in the game is laughable. The combat and controls are better than the first game. They are still is not enjoyable, though. Dodging is very hit or miss, attacks take forever to deploy, and the enemy AI is trash. Jumping from a ledge to another ledge is ridiculous. Sometimes your jump doesn't work, but you still clear the gap by somehow horizontally sliding across thin air.The story and dialogue are horrible. It has the hollowness of the Outer Worlds but none of the polish. I had to stop playing because I hated everybody and their stupid words they were saying.This has the feeling of an indie game that should have been 2D but was forced to be 3D, and all the effort that should have gone into making it likable was instead devoted to creating haphazard solutions to solved problems. In a world where the big studios are able to get pretty close to lifelike expression and representation of nature, everything else 3D either pales in comparison, limits scope, or intentionally goes lo-fi and tries to play on nostalgia. This is one of those pales in comparison examples.I'm sure this was a labor of love for some devs and that the budget and timeline were not fair to them. This game is trash tho

_childDocuments_.review: Not your average RPG.If you're a fan of Piranha Bytes and enjoyed the Gothic series / had fun with Elex then this should be an easy purchase. 110% would recommend ON A SALE, full price is not really worth.Elex 2 has some upgrades from it's predecessor, Elex 1, and some nice quality of life features. The upgradable jetpack & turbo boosters which allow you to fly around faster in a straight line or around you is definitely one of the best things, as it makes exploring and just generally getting around, a ton of fun.- Piranha Bytes being Piranha Bytes, means you'll also get rewarded for exploring as they love putting bits and pieces in every nook and cranny.Elex 2 being Elex, and developed by Piranha, you can only fly straight, or using the WASD keys in a direction with turbo but when u need to go one step higher, you can't as you need to let go of said keys and press space to go a little bit higher. My point is, our main character has a problem when it comes to turbo boosters as he'll continue smashing his face into walls, stairs and so on when it's an inclination of any kind, stairs... for example... or EVEN RAMPS...As long as you fly around ground level and around NPCs they can interrupt you to initiate a conversation even mid-flight if u are scared of missing important dialogues by flying. There's Air Combat now, it's there, if u seen the combat in Elex then u know what to expect.One of the things that has seen a downgrade is definitely the combat, it's easier and worse at the same time. Don't bother locking onto enemies as it will put the camera RIGHT BEHIND YOU instead looking over you, meaning you literally can't see the attacks as your character will block the view and it's nauseating. -You can also keep pressing the M2 button to spam the parry button so that when an enemy attacks you, as long as it's not taller than you by 3x times, you will parry, deplete a good chunk of their stamina or even throw them to the ground and initiate a heavy attack for some really high damage. This... makes learning enemy patterns and attacks obsolete. - There's also the kick button... and if your enemy is a human, and u can repeatably kick them in the nuts to drop their stamina, essentially stun-locking them until they fall over, do a heavy attack, then repeat. When it comes to world building, factions and so on, Elex 2 has definitely seen an improvement. With the introduction to Morkons, a new melee based faction and going back to the Albs Faction, it definitely feels like there's more freedom of choice. - The graphics has seen some improvements as well, going around on foot or flying is both enjoyable, as you can see the beautiful landscape from above or admire the beautiful scenery from below. The faces of NPCs have seen some improvement as well as they're more diverse now, same with clothing, wind physics and so on. Definitely a big plus when it comes to graphics & world building. One of the things that game hasn't learned is the high attribute requirements which Piranha thought it could just slap a band-aid fix over and it's done. The band-aid fix in question is the fact that u need to spend 1 Learning Point to reduce the requirements of a certain WEAPON CATEGORY/TYPE by 10%. I will HIGHLY suggest getting the 10% requirement reduction ONLY when u know what faction & class you're going with. Story is... there, that's it. There's a story behind this game. My overall vote would be something around 7.5+/10, perhaps a low 8. The story is meh, the characters, dialogue, world building and so on has seen some improvements but the engine is the same, combat is rather the same, easier and worse at the same time, feels like u can cheese more enemies now, some nice quality of life features and so on. It's a good game, if it baked for a few more months it would've been a solid 9/10. There are some mods to fix a few things here and thereI'm a big fan of Piranha Bytes games and Elex 2 was definitely, an easy purchase for me when it came on sale. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing sequel to the original Elex.  The combat was improved, the magic was improved, the character dialog was improved, the quests were improved, and the jet pack was totally overhauled and is now an amazing feature.  I would highly recommend that you do a  play through of the original Elex just for the story.  Yes, you get a recap at the beginning of this but actually living the events is worth it.  The game does not use your saved data from the 1st so there may be some inconsistencies with your own person experience.  But all in all it's an amazing game IMO and I would highly recommend the game to anyone that enjoys RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game and I enjoy playing it.However, having played the first Elex, there are some things that annoy me.1) How you played and finished Elex 1 doesn't have any influence on this game. I mean, I was a Beserker Paladin, lead the armies of the free people against the Albs and won. And now nearly nobody recognizes me? I am not even admitted entrance to the Berserker's place? Like maybe at most 15 years later, people should recognize Jax more.2) The explanation why Jax has lost all his abilities is crap to non-existent.3) The quests are very similar to Elex 1.  Might be they did that on purpose, because it obviously worked in Elex 1, or perhaps that is what gamers requested according to their marketing people. But I would have liked a bit more originality.I think it would have been better to use a new main character. The ability loss would have been no issue. It would have made sense you needed to gain acceptance anew. It would also have given them the chance to let players customize the main character a bit more (at least the option for a female main character). They could still have had cameos from Elex 1 characters without presuming on how you had played it.P.S. Why do the children look so out of proportion?P.P.S. The late game story writing leaves a lot to be desired. Still, I can't wait for the story to continue.

_childDocuments_.review: After the not so great Risen series the Devs of the legendary Gothic game series returned to form with Elex, and this game continues this trend. A great open world, packed with things to discover, interesting Factions and a great progression system makes this a must buy for RPG fans. Beware though, it is not as polished as other AAA titles, which for me makes it all the more charming though.

_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: First, I'd like to say that if you enjoyed the combat system of Elex, and that's all you cared about then this game is for you. It didn't change, it's still the same clunky system we all know from the first game.Now, despite the combat system, just about everything else did change. You like a certain faction? guess what, they were all completely changed, and for the most part gutted. Want a new faction, lucky you, they added a S&M group just for you. None of the groups available were satisfying. Hell, to join the Clerics you had to become an Alb first. The whole game seems pointed towards you giving up everything you've accomplished and returning to Xacor to resume your life as a Drone. I would say if you want more Elex, play the first game again. The mechanics are the same, but the story and game play offer more variation without making you feel like you swallowed glass simply to progress the game by choosing one of the absolutely miserable classes offered in Elex II.

_childDocuments_.review: It saddens me to give a negative review but I have to, hoping the developers get a grip and improve for their next games. While Elex 2 is better than the 1st in some areas like close and ranged combat, controls, UI, it isn't where it matters the most. The sequel has worse world building, map, environments, customization, quests, factions, story, dialogues, characters.Most of what made Elex a unique and unmissable RPG compared to other games of the same genre from bigger creative studios is worse this time around. The game feels like a downgrade similarly to Risen 2 as it was way worse than Risen 1. Its so bad it doesn't inspire me to finish it even after paying full price on day 1.Come on Piranha Bytes, I know you can do better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: Great example of a middle-thumbs-up type of game. However, with the price tag, I cannot recommend it at full price.  The combat feels inferior to games released fifteen years ago.  The graphics are nice to look at. The dialogue is dreadful.  The chief reason I stopped playing was because the power-curve is not compelling. Early on the combat is super tough (loved it), and fighting was a serious decision. Mid game you have the power to win most fights, but because the parry system is so awful (The worst I have seen) you wind up relying on just dodge-rolling everything and countering once.  You rinse and repeat this until anything dies.  I'd give the game a 7/10 because the exploration and worldcrafting were done really well.
_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: First off I'd like to say I would love to recommend this game but it would be hard to do so in it's current state. Disclaimer: This review is based entirely on a Normal play thru.Pros: The game looks great the lighting and the environments, much better animations than the first game.  Story seems decent enough and the game is full of choices matter situations.  The physics can be pretty cool and even have some hilarious ragdoll moments.  Cons:  The fighting is a bit clunky and the enemies don't respawn frequent enough if at all. The open world feels empty and has few creatures to fight. I feel like the RPG aspect of this game is very lacking most weapons you can't even use for hrs after receiving them.  It takes an extremely long time to get anywhere on the leveling or skills you find from various trainers.  Enemy fights feel excessively long (not unlike this review:) more enemies opposed to long fights would help this game tremendously not to mention with helping balance the leveling.  Grenades:  I'm not sure what the deal is with the grenades you would think it would send the enemies flying a bit?  Maybe I'm asking too much lolHaving said all this I hope the game gets some updates and some serious need of balancing.

_childDocuments_.review: At the first glance of the first hour and half, Elex 2 already looks like the best Gothic made to date in terms of polish and game play mechanics improvements. Also for more casual players or for people not familiar with Piranha Bytes games, this game offers a much more first-time-player-friendly experience than ever, which was usually the biggest complaint with Piranha games; not the case with this game. Will update this later after finishing the game. Good luck and have fun - highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Just to start,  I love PB games.  They may not have the latest and greatest graphics but they can run on older systems so people don't have to go out and buy a whole new rig.  Even AAA companies should take this into account especially with the chip shortages happening.  Also a new rig is really expensive.  I think the stories are well written, though they are very similar in PB games but it is a formula that works. I enjoy the quests and you can easily get drawn into the world. I have put 58 hours into this game so I think the 50 dollars I spent on it is well worth it.  Yes there are minor bugs, but I haven't encountered any game breaking ones. The world is beautiful to explore and each of the factions has their own unique feel.  The combat is still enjoyable, though not perfect and is good for casual gamers. I really like to explore every single corner of the world PB creates for their games.   This is actually one of the more polished ones they have created.  I would strongly recommend Elex 2 and Elex 1 if players want to have a good alternate experience in video games away from the highly intense mainstream games and also if you have an older system.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a hidden gem. Is it janky? Yes. Is it weird in that European CRPG kinda way? Absolutely. But it's also a true living, breathing open world where characters have schedules synchronized to a day / night cycle. It's an RPG where your decisions truly change your story progression. And there's a jetpack :D It also has some of the best lighting I've ever seen, and the combat - while not revolutionary - is actually quite good once you get used to it. Pro tip: don't lock on, just think of all your sword swings as having an area of effect and learn the animation so you know where it lands. I'm having a grand time with this game, probably one of my favorites of 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: To make it short: Mechanically, this game is very much superior to its predecessor. Graphically it is partially old assets partially new ones, and the difference is striking (not so much in quality as glossiness). In regards to worldbuilding, story and style I liked the first one more, but that is a matter of personal preference.THE GOOD:+ Quests are generally solid fare, nothing worldshaking but keeps me entertained throughout.+ Early game is less stressful than in the first game, thanks to the better jetpack and slightly easier enemies.+ Lots of exploring to do and with the new jetpack zipping around is amazing and really fast.+ Reward for collecting the map pieces is really good this time around.+ Attribute and perk systems feel better than before in terms of the general passives.+ More enemy types.+ Dialogues are classic PB, but some quips had me chuckle (like that one time a highwayman used a very odd synonym for "fight" and when I killed him it listed a quest with just that name as completed).+ Upgrading weapons is more expensive now, but does not increase attribute requirements any more. Not being able to use my best weapon after improving it bummed me out in the first game, glad it's gone.THE NEUTRAL:* I miss firemodes on energy weapons. I understand it's for weapon balance to make them all viable, still saddens me slightly.* Companion quests could be spaced out a bit more. I do one and get hit by two more from other people. Maybe partially on me because I decided to "do companion quests now", but since by the end of Passus 2 they are all over and done with, there is enough room left to spread them a bit.* Factions could have done with a few more quests after officially joining. I list this as neutral since they didn't have many in the first game either, so it's not a downgrade.* The reward for the main quest is amazing, but by this point it's not very useful any more.THE WEIRD:# Why do the new textures look like someone freshly spray-painted them and then gave them a good scrub to make them really shine? Contrasts starkly with the older assets. Especially on mutant monsters that look like they come fresh from Monster Wash (TM), where they got sandblasting and a wax coating at a discount.# Some faces, to be fair. Caja stands out as she doesn't really resemble her older model. The old one was a generic Berserker woman, but this change makes it look like she stuck her head into Monster Wash (TM) as well and wasn't well received there on account of not being a monster.# Since I play in German, some items had me scratch my head a bit and ponder the eating habits of whoever was in charge of making up food items in this game (like Mucke♥♥♥♥ instead of plain old coffee).THE BAD:- Factionperks feel lacking. I miss passives and as Alb/Cleric weapons tend to outshine the spells. Same goes for faction equipment. No more singularity-shooting bracers. :(- Berserkers going full idiot mode and replacing metal plate armor with rubber tires because they sniffed glue that day when they decided to redesign their fashion (seriously Rat, stop drugging everyone, it ain't fun!).THE HORRIBLE:-- That main quest where Reinhold tells me to pretty please go kill 150 robots. Even MMOs give lower numbers than that, or if not gives you some doomsday devide to make it very fast and very fun. This here is neither. The enemies are too close to each other to be handily picked off one by one and too far spaced to be easy targets for AoE attacks.

_childDocuments_.review: Once I dialed in my video I could play largely uninterrupted. I'm running an RTX 2080 and fullscreen was problematic, usually I'd see artifacts and then my video card would crash, leaving the system running. Though the error handling was usually elegant, at times the 2080 was simply overcome and became a brick, inert. I had to do a hard reset. However, I have found that I could run a full eight hour session if I used a windowed mode.But once I had that work-around in place I found the game quite interesting, with lots of personality. Well thought-out quests, good progression, ample character building... and could make decisions and choices that seem to matter in the game world. I even like the combat, especially when I've been able to develop my strength, dexterity, and constitution. I badly need to invest points in my intelligence and cunning to open up my crafting, but it won't be long. I am eager about the game now, and it is such a relief from the near despair I felt from my initial technical, hardware challenges. I think the game will find a solid base of fans.

The map is much smaller than the first elex as well.I'm a PB fan, but at this point it's hard to forgive this game's shortcomings. PB have great ideas, quest design, branching narratives etc - but this game feels archaic compared to its contemporaries.

The graphics are SO terrible that it took some time for me to accept this fact. Even melee wasn't to hard, you just couldn't see anything.Now that I have completed this game, I don't know what to say. I like some things and I had some fun. But especially the second half of the main missions were just pure grinding. Nothing changing. Just killing hordes of monsters. And not just one or two, no like at least 15. 15!! And: I did enjoy this game but if ELEX III ever comes out and even looks like this does, I'm not buying. It was a challenge but now that I'm done, I won't think about it any longer.I'll still recommend it. Keep in mind what I said. And if you haven't played Elex I, play that one first. Like, really. _childDocuments_.review: Elex 2 is “We have Elex 1 at home,” inferior in every way: From the awful new Jax with his awful son Dex (Jax and Dex, really) to the visual downgrade to these clay-looking Fortnite models juxtaposed in a world with much higher level of detail, while keeping the same mechanical bugs, weather filters, music, and needlessly-high stat requirements to use any weapon. To create the illusion of new, E2 has made many changes for change’s sake just to say that something is different such as the worse lock-picking interface, the removal of the teleporters-on-map perk, NEW FEATURE #1 of very unwanted escort missions where the dialogue breaks frequently, and NEW FEATURE #2 of auto-grabbing ledges which creates more problems than it intended to solve. E2 is so bad of a sequel that it undoes any enjoyment from the 6 out of 10 E1, and makes it worth not playing the series altogether because of how this sequel ruins the story and the game.Jax now swears all of the time, and is linguistically dumber with an entirely different voice actor because the developers wasted their money on the Screen Actors Guild, which took the vast majority of this game’s budget to produce 25% of the voice actor variety at 1000% of the cost when compared to E1. E2 is littered with “oh hey its you” repetitive dialogue choices from the first game, but now with new voice actors despite being the same character. The new models look nothing like themselves from E1, and not because of story-related age—they appear to be entirely different people with the new different voices, yet with the same name. Flashbacks are also just video files in the old graphics and not truly in-game, showing just how different that the models looked texture-wise.The videos, the models, and the voices for E1 should have either been redone with the new bad design choices from E2 then patched in to E1 to be consistent with E2, or E2 should have kept the same character model graphics and voice actors as E1. I cannot get over how bad that the human skin in E2, especially with the eyes, and at no point did I enjoy any of the new Jax or returning characters voiced by different people. The rest of E2’s budget went to licensing an awful contemporary Billy Idol song along with his likeness and along with this clay puppet man who is supposed to be Steve Stevens, both of who perform in-game on this non-Earth planet to really send home how little that the developers wanted E2 to succeed. Not even anything good by Idol like Cyberpunk or Rebel Yell, just some cheaper off-label licensing which still took too much valuable project funding for E2.There are also new old world ruins which were not in E1 despite the map sharing the overall location with E1 (Tavar is the main point of reference), but none of the new ruins have any significance. The island is no longer an island but instead has cold / toxic zones as barriers. There are now children running around, which are just shrunken adult models with unshrunk adult heads and adult voice actors pretending to be children. The jetpack vehicle improvement is the only reason to play E2, which itself is limited because of fuel and should have been in E1 to begin with.If the developer’s future was staked to this, I can see why the developer shut down because E2 should not have been released as is. I replayed E1 in preparation of E2, but I was only able to endure several hours of E2 before deciding to uninstall it and write off my wasted money. _childDocuments_.review: Exactly what you expect from a Piranha Bytes game, what's not to love?It's like Elex 1, but improved in every aspect. _childDocuments_.review: I give this game a thumbs sideways with a tiny angle towards the bottom. If you are looking for the basic Piranha Bytes (PB) formula you won’t be disappointed. You can spend plenty of time exploring the world of Magalan and get lost in the world. Most of you know the good things the developer gets right so no point iterating through them. After playing approximately 50 hours I can’t help but feel a bitter after taste. I expected a bit more. Here are the main points that bug me. Most of them are about repeated mistakes from the previous Elex. On a side note, I played the German version of the game and these points are spoiler free.: Once again, the first third of the game is a blast (apart from the intro and the inconsistent movie cut scenes). Hooking up with one faction, solving plenty of side quests and seeing your character progress is satisfying as hell. Sadly, once you reach a certain point mid game where you have access to a certain weapon the game becomes too easy because you are able to take care of most of the enemies and experience points come rushing in. Quests become more repetitive, you end up teleporting around like mad and the whole feeling goes awry. Last third of the game was almost insulting with the amount of enemies that were thrown at you. The devs once again failed to balance the game and make the second half as interesting as the first half. : I think the Gothic series created some memorable characters like Diego, Lester, Gorn and Milten because the were naturally woven into the story and helped the player the same way the player helped them. Now in Elex II, which copied the same mechanic as the previous game, you hire these blank characters who completely stop their lives to be your personal body guard. Yes, you do missions with them (quick teleport somewhere to defeat a bunch of grunts) and some of them have nice “twists” but they never feel natural. The annoying prompts “X will remember that” are so inconsistent with what is actually happening it was mind numbing. I’m certain, I’ll forget most of the names of the characters anyway. And don’t get me started on Nasty, which has to be the most annoying character in gaming history.: I don’t need fancy graphics as long as the bigger picture is right. What I mind though are these poorly executed cut scenes. Especially unfortunately when they contain emotional father son talk – it just doesn’t work.: A slight improvement to the previous soundtrack – but god, I miss Kai Rosenkranz.: Piranha Bytes always got the atmosphere right, but never really the story aspect. There is lots of talk but due to the dialogue often being amateurishly written, it never picks up the pace. Please PB, hire a decent author for a change who can write a captivating story. The whole looming threat of alien invaders offered such a nice scenario. There was a forced sense of “PB writes rough dialogue, we give you rough dialogue” in a lot of phrases, featuring a lot of unnecessary bad language that often didn’t fit. Sometimes I had the feeling the script contained narrative talk, that didn’t fit in a face to face conversation. Overall I miss cynical and less self-serious touch the Gothic series had.: There are many different monsters but in the end, you have like 10 who have a unique move set, the rest are just reskins. Here most of it was also recycled. Once you figure out these move sets, fighting them becomes a walk in the park.: Jetpack is a plus, but with 5 years of development in the back I was expecting more. I guess half of this time has already been spent on Elex III.: No point elaborating for that, there a plenty of reviews covering that topic in detail.

_childDocuments_.review: Steams suboptimal interface ate a more lengthy review, so here's a shorter version.Though I put a lot of time into the game, I cannot recommend it.  The early-to-mid game is good and challenging, following the same pattern as the original - going from a chump that could barely armwrestle or outwit a squirrel to an engine of destruction.  There's a lot of great exploration to do, and some interesting bits of story and lore to be found.  Unfortunately the end game was mostly unchallenging, and deeply repetitive - particularly with top tier kit.The scenery is radically improved, but somehow the faces look worse.  Also the game does not know how to do underground lighting at all, which is very immersion breaking.Being able to use a jetpack is still extremely awesome - buy the sprint option for it as soon as possible, and pour all the fuel into upgrading capacity (the latter does not take skill points).Making some of the old factions into mini-factions was a nice innovation - you need to infiltrate one of the bigger factions and advance before you can join the mini-faction.  However one of the new factions was unremittingly badly written, poorly thought out, and frankly deeply unpleseant.  In my saves they are known as 'death w*nkers'.  There is a plot to join them that looks like a redemption arc for the faction, but they seemed so awful I could not face pursuing it.Voice acting was very patchy in places - main character and most of the main npcs were good to bearable, but in some places I was extremely pleased by the presence of a skip dialogue option.Overall it's a bit of a mess boosted with some nostalgia for the old game, but unless you're deeply invested in the first game I'd give it a miss.  I played it as a break from my Blender project I was working on, and I am extremely ready to go back to it now.

_childDocuments_.review: There are technical issues regarding frame timing and overall performance that prevent me from enjoying this game.This could have been a nostalgia trip for long-term fans of games by Piranha Bytes, but the missing quality of life-settings (especially FOV, Zoom slider) and complete lack of optimization is holding the game back. Yes, there are badly animated faces in dialogues and there are clunky mechanics (e.g. stopping and having a short animation for - every - single - item you pick up). In my opinion, this kind of minor issues has always plagued games by Piranha Bytes and did give their games a specific charme.Just for comparison, my system is using a 1080 GTX, i7 9700, 32GB Ram and I am getting the following FPS while standing in the same place.These figures are a small indication of the overall issue, but they are far from scientific.Setup: I am standing near a simple building (a few walls and metal bars, nothing fancy), looking at the same location (controlled by having the red sun / planet in the top right corner) very early in the game.The exact setup can be seen here:  (Please be aware that you need to kill off the game and restart for the resolution change to take effect.)110 FPS @ 720p and everything off / Low80 FPS 	@ 720p and everything high / Ultra / Maximum setting (all the way to the right)65 FPS 	@ 3440x1440 and everything off / Low40 FPS 	@ 3440x1440 and everything high / Ultra / Maximum setting (all the way to the right)Please keep in mind that this is a) early on b) not a crowded area c) very little going on (e.g. NPCs, loading new data, graphical effects) d) completely ignoring frame pacing, so I think these FPS represent a best case scenario.My expectation going in was for the FPS to dip into the 60s or mid 50s in the most demanding scenarios (large fights, center of crowded cities).However, there is one silver lining to the performance issues: Playing on Linux (via Proton GE) feels almost identical to playing on Windows, FPS dips and frame timing issues included.I am torn between asking for a refund right now and waiting / hoping for Piranha Bytes to fix this technical mess.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say yes... but it's A VERY WEAK YES.  (cough, like the ending)It's great for RPG open world players, who what to immerse themselves in a rich landscape with lots of lore, heck load of mutant monster killings tasks and quests with grenade launchers and other weapons types to fire up the testosterone levels to maximum overdrive.[My View of the Story]If Jax wasn't a cool character to play, I'd probably have drop the game early. I couldn't get hooked on the companions. The only ones worth mentioning for me were Caja, Crony U4 and Fox. Caja and Fox seemed to have the better backstories. The other companions I found weird.  I didn't mind that Nasty was something of an anti-hero, but her quest line didn't give enough balance to her character, so she lacked in emotional depth for me. It was the same for the others as well.  Falk almost had the potential with a cool quest line of wanting to be more human, but after all his quest research with Jax he didn't seem to change much in the end.  And don't get me started about Dex's fate... bleh.  As Baxter would put it (in nice terms) it was "weak like a luke-warm **** puddle."Not gonna lie, the ending was just weak. Like, I didn't feel there was enough build up for the main battle. I felt it was largely due to the fact, Jax couldn't build up clout with factions in a satisfactory way that could give a feel of the stakes with each faction for the final battle and after. Like even after saving the Crater or Fort from being run-in by mutants and sabotaged robots,  he gains no clout at all from them. Not even a cut-scene showing their response to his efforts. So the last conversation he has with them is lackluster.   For a novel, that's fine. For a game, what's the point then?To me,  it felt that the Clerics was the canon faction for Jax. Their conversations and quest lines seemed the most smooth progression with the main quest line.[Gameplay]Like first game, farqing hard until you reach level 20.  So the first chapter is really looong to complete. I recommend building up levels and attributes to level 30 - 40 before hitting chapter 2.  Do lots of small quests, go mutant hunting and use feet to explore every inch of world.   The quests get harder later on in chapter 2 and especially in the last two.Overall, the game kept me engaged for 83 hrs and I really liked the mutant fights and likes (when I could fight and not just die all the time), but the story line is MEH.  Could've done a whole lot better.  And I guess it bothered me so much that I had to post a TL:DR review.

_childDocuments_.review: Fellow Gamers,Should you not like this game, I humbly ask that you not leave a negative review.  You're free to write off the money spent or request a refund. _childDocuments_.review: First things first, the game at his release still seems like it's waiting some patches and functionalities, so if some aspects change I will come back to change my review. Now this isn't so much a review as a critique of what could and should be improved or sadly won't be.Interface : The game interface has been heavily downgraded compared to the first game. It is definitely my biggest gripe so far, though also the most likely aspect to receive patches or improvements post-release. It looks quite uglier, shifting from the amazing colorful blue arm implant of the first to an ugly generic looking FPS interface, losing a few practical and difficulty related functionalities in the process.-Instead of being split in different tabs by their functionalities, items are now all in one same vertical tab (still in item type order) but you need to scroll past lenghty undesired categories and search to find what you're looking for, not practical at all when looking for a skill or potion in a hurry, especially since, next point,- The in game menu no longer pauses the game, not even in easy mode, this is an unwelcome change in the classic piranha byte interface (hopefully an option will be added to fix that issue), now I have to worry about finding this or that lifesaving chem or potion in a super long scrolling inventory in a split second, which leads me to the next point,- The item/skill shortcut bar was replaced by a popping circular menu, so you can't see when your item stock is about to be exhausted and what thing is assigned to what shortcut unless you open the popping circular menu, which almost never happens on PC. Whilst it might be more practical for quick selection on a joystick's controller, it is counterintuitive on a keyboard and often leads to repeated accidental wasting of pricy or limited consummable items, also you don't have place for skills in the shorcuts because all of them have to be occupied by essential survival/healing items since going in the menu to select the less often used ones in the middle of action is no longer a viable option-No option to get rid of the endurance gauge, however, the endurance system is way less punitive than in the previous game (at least in easy mode), still, an option to turn it off no matter the difficulty setting would be appreciated for playing in the harder modes. Having no energy limit and stunlocking an enemy is one of the most enjoyable part of the studios's classic gameplay and about the only way to manage against a group of enemies before level 20.- The menu map is zoomed, you can't zoom out to get a better view.Graphics : Many things look uglier than in the first. - The vegetation looks uglier than in the first, no matter the quality settings. I believe it's in part because of the excessive wind physics in some areas, so every tree leaves/bush and even some grass patches shake at least 33% too much to not be bothersome. Also many of the trees have almost no branches or leaves in comparison to the first, looking much smaller too, so they look quite bare and unimpressive.- On a positive note, there are some improvements for some character's looks, with the only clear downgrades so far being the Clerics, who'se red color was given to the Morkons instead, so now they're completely grey and forgettable looking, and Nasty, who's gone from a quirky bratty face with cool expressions to a dead fish one.Story/Factions : Poorly executed, Piranha Bytes games have never done worse.-Berserkers kind of fuse with outlaws and stop being as annoying as they were in the first game, they're clearly the developper's preferred choice in this second game, getting all the love (faction usefulness, 2 companions instead of just 1, center of the world in both gameplay and as the previous game cannon) whilst the other factions are pushed to the sidelines. Outlaws have been nerfed even more than they were in the first game. Clerics, content wise, are basically abandonned, having lost everything that made them appealing in the first game. Morkons are basically a fusion of of Elex 1's Berserkers xenophobia, Outlaw's hardass behaviour and Cleric's faith, which makes them feel like deja vu (and also are the worst part of each factions). Albs are alright, but it feels like the content they have isolates them storywise since no one wants to have anything to do with them, since, you know, they are albs.-I still think the ONE PERK outlaws need desperately and for some reason still don't have is a perk to reduce or nullify the 50% exp loss when using chems, cause let's be honest they don't have anything exclusive and chems aren't very powerful in this sequel. (chems recipe being useless since all chems can be found and bought by players no matter their faction)-The game isn't retro-compatible, which isn't a sin, HOWEVER, they had a lot of choices made cannon, which would have better been left unspecified :     -You joined the berserkers and contributed in their rise to power. (No. I did everything I could against them in both my Outlaw and Cleric games since I found berserkers annoying.)     -You have a child with Caja. Now, it could have worked if they just said "at some point you had a child with Caja", but no, they went for the Elex I cinematic where Jax choses Caja and ditches Nasty, making the inferior choice, and also making it the cannon one. As a quick memo, you could pick either boring superficial Caja (basically equivalent to preston garvey, always whining at you if you didn't act heroic, even with max loyalty) or the witty, fun loving and superior in every way Nasty (which actually opened up and grew to care about Jax much more than Caja did)     -It is made cannon that you were part of the claws, you know, the organisation of cringy, edgy, arrogant and distrustful thieves that apparently you were supposed to like, even though all of them had a thrash DLC tier personality, and if you had joined, had you go on quests to screw over a ton of friendly and innocent npcs, basically for a few shards you no longer needed at that point of the game.MAP-The whole southern beach region is empty, like it isn't finished at all. There are few monsters, almost ZERO item to be looted at or near the shores, (and only empty structures) and even the scrap island has been removed entirely from the second game, including somehow the massive concrete base, so it plain doesn't make sense.-In the same way, the map feels much smaller, and it is. In the first game, there is Tavar, Golieth, Ignadon, Abessa, Xacor and the banished region South of Golieth, that makes 6 regions to explore. In the second game, there is only Ignadon, Tavar, Carakis and the Crater/Cleric ruin, so 4 regions, and many of the ruined buildings are not fully accessible like they were in the first, as if still incomplete. Also, although the map is smaller by a third, it is also much emptier and less concentrated, at least for the moment, with only what feels like half as many nammed characters than in the first and many loot spots being spread around the map in empty spots, with just a bunch of items on the ground, with nothing around.I still have hopes some of those issues will be patched in the next few months, for although the game is relatively enjoyable, it is by no means as much as the previous Elex or even the second or third Risen games in its current state. For now I can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm posting a positive review only because  it was fun to a certain degree to play this game and that's all.Let's focus on the plot- ELEX II tells us the story of Jax six years after the main events of the prequel. As Jax's new journey, filled with obstacles, begins the so called Skyands start their invasion on Magalan.  Our task is to unite the factions again against the Alien race and save the planet once more.Your previous choices do not matter because there is no option to import the save files from the previous game. The devs decided what outcome is canon and based the entire world of ELEX II on it.The Gameplay:There are some changes and improvements in the gameplay which can be instantly noticed, but still, the combat system (especially the hitbox) is sick. Even if you dodge an attack you may get hit and lose your HP. Still sloppy...The graphics:GEEZ! Am I drunk and i'm starting to see ugly things ?  ☣️I mean the planet of Magalan and it's fauna looks pretty decent. When it comes to the character models it kinda reminds me of the "lazy faces" from Mass Effect Andromeda.  People may have great expectations when they see the recommended system requirements and the game's launch date._____________________________________________________If you wanna take part in a boring and repeatable (but still gripping and addicting) adventure then ELEX II is for ya.A word of advice - wait for a sale!

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really, really wanted to like this game. I was looking for ELEX for a very very long time and I consider myself a Gothic/Risen fan, although I'm not very knowledgeagle in those games... but liked them so much to have them on steam and GOG and got Risen back in 2008 or 2009 in a physical edition... But I can't the game is awful, ELEX 2 is a complete failure of a game. It came out on 2022, I'm playing it on 2023 and it feels like playing a game older than Risen, it feels like a 2006 game... Elex is clunky, it's janky, glitchy, buggy, tiresome and incredibly unpolished. It feels like a game in alpha.I'll divide this in two parts, the game technically and the game's plot.Technically speaking, I can't say much more than what I already said. The game feels worst than Risen. Ranged attacks felt more natural and polished in Gothic 2, a game from 2002... Inventory management is counter intuitive, quest logs are stupid because some quests don't progress naturally... You need to talk with someone but the game doesn't tell you... You can sleep but NPCs or events doesn't pass like the time... They literally won't move if you're sleeping... Quests are buggy, the game crashes a lot, is optimized poorly, NPCs dissapear, don't appear, quests doesn't register properly... The ranged attack system sucks, thank god is OP, the melee system is one of the worst I've ever seen and I wasn't interested enough in checking the magic system. Animations feel like if the game is in an Alpha state and 90% of the mods are for QOL improvements and gameplay tweaks. The game is slow, dialogues are slow, animations are slow, facial expresions are dumb... It really feels and runs like an Alpha.With the argument... I... I don't know where to start. Every single character in this game is stupid and just a few of them are actually likeable. Some of the companions you have openly dislike you. Whatever you do... they don't care. There's a bunch of factions that hate each other, sometimes even they hate themselves and sometimes they attack you... but nothing happens. The game gives the impression that it's not really an RPG, what's going to happen is going to happen, no matter what, there's no choice, you, as the main character, are just an anecdote during the game... Nothing that you do really matters... that for an RPG that's really gruesome.Summing up, the story feels like a Gothic 2/3 ripoff and... in a way, it is... it truly is... There's a point in the game, around chapter 2, that if you've played Piranhya Bytes previous games you know what's going to happen.That's the biggest problem... PB is still making the same game they've always did... over and over... with the same mechanics, plots, characters and twists... It's the same over and over... and this time they did it really bad.The game is terrible, it's awful, dull, boring and buggy as hell. Tommy Wiseau woul've done it better. This is trash.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. I've seen many negative reviews that are quite not fair for me, so I will try to make comprehensive review and deal with some myths.First of all, it's BIG upgrade considering first Elex. The evolution and increased budget is clearly visible. It does everything Elex 1 did, just better. Also, it's 6 days after release and I found 0 breaking bugs, where I could not finish quest or anything! Most important improvements:- FIGHTING! Yes, it's just substantially better. I agree Elex 1 had one of worst fight systems I ever seen in a computer game, esp. melee. Fighting in Elex 2 is more like in first Risen than in first Elex, just stamina system is in place, but improved and not as annoying. Yes, there are alot of OP things about fighting, I won't spoil it here (well you will probably find it in internet easily), but finally you can fight since first levels without raising frustration if you don't try to kill troll at level 2.- World is a lot improved, it feels there is more things to find. In Elex 1, I gave up searching as there was nothing really to find besides legendary toilet paper everywhere. In Elex 2 you can find armors, legendary weapons, ammunition, craft ingredients etc. Also world is more interesting.- Jetpack improvements are huge. It's not only to reach mountains and wait 20 seconds to refill, now it gives us bonus movement speed and other stuff. And after finished game, you get jetpack mastery so you can travel very fast to finish achievements, find stuff etc, that's great!- Items - in first Elex, there were very few weapons, and equipment interface was terrible. Now there are alot of weapon types, along with legendary weapons, you can pick what you like best and be strong with every type of weapon. Crafting is also better. Items interface is improved, it could use some tabs but it's ok for me, now I can clearly see what's junk and what I can use.- Cut scenes are finally there, some of them are funny but hey, it's something.- Story feels consistent and continues first Elex plot. I actually kinda like it. It answers many questions araised after first Elex and stands strong to second part events.To not be luscious, there are also alot to improve, like:- camera... It's actually a downgrade from first Elex, but I believe it will be fixed soon.- characters we meet are dull, most of them annoying, couldn't resist if I had a chance I would simply tell them to leave or just kill some (looking at you Nasty). Also, there are alot of characters from first part missing, and instead we have new ones.- animations are still pretty clunky, but well, it's PB- game is shorter than I expected, I've made most of quests and discovered most interesting places, yet it took me 45 hours - like 2x more than first one so it's still improvement, but I expected these 60 hours some revievs pointed.- Since like 3rd chapter this game becomes a slasher, you just go and kill armies of enemies and that's basically all for hours, I was seriously tired of this especially I was so strong at this moment most enemies were 2-3 shots. It was just playing hide and seek with them.Overall I would give this game solid 8/10 (take this with grain of salt as I like all PB games). I can't understand why some people bomb it with negative reviews after few hours of playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a paste of my post. Feelings haven't changed.  tl;dr - This game is early access at best.  I am refunding the game.  Might repurchase if they fix it or when it goes on deep discount and modders at options to the game.I played Elex twice and completed it as a Cleric and an Outlaw. Bought it on GoG originally and bought it on steam to support the devs recently. So make no mistake, I liked Elex. I’m no super fan but I think it’s a super fun game.- Performance is awful. Game crashes if I change view range in the game. I get 45fps whether I raise the settings or lower them. Than sometimes it is just like, lets go for 60 but are you in a building now, well now we are going to set you at 30fps. Why? No idea. Bad optimization. I don't think your graphic card even matters honestly.Interestingly enough, I used blank .bik files to skip the THQ and PB intro logo. So usually, this skips you to the main menu quickly. But those logo's actually hide the fact the game is still loading. So it will show the main menu screen without options and loading text at the bottom. The main menu music is off and wont actually turn on till about 10-15 seconds after you get selectable menu options. Never seen a game that takes so long to get to the main menu. IMO, they hid it on purpose with the dev logo vids.- What is this camera. PB games always had some camera issues that aren't always comfortable but this new dynamic cam is just beyond awful. Why do we have a dead space tight corridor camera in an open world game. Who makes decisions like this. I didn't like it in Elex 1 and you made it worse. Let us zoom in and out, give us fov options. Whether I am running or standing still, stop zooming in and out automatically. How long have you been making games PB, and why do we even have to have a conversation about this. This is like tutorial game dev 101. And the ini change only seems to effect when running. Either way its not a good subsitute for bad game mechanics.- Character Models. Jax and all the characters look awful. Elex 1 looks like a graphics masterpiece compared to this. I accepted Elex 1 models because the game was fun but damn. You outdid yourself. Everyone is so flat, almost as if they were just molded with clay and we haven't got around to the detail texturing yet.- Cutscenes - Whats with them. I totally understand they are going to happen. But literally you are told.. hey go sneak past glow dogs. Cut scene time! Walk within 10 miles of Caja. CUT SCENE TIME BABY.. and a Teleport. Didnt expect that did ya! Go see Adam. THATS RIGHT! CUT SCENE AND TELEPORT ARE BACK BABY!!. Can I at least explore the village before you shove exposition and teleportation up my a-hole?- Voice acting and Audio. Wow.. just wow. When Two Worlds II and Oblivion have better dialogue than your game, you should definitely win a razzie. I feel like I am already taking crazy pills listening to them speak to each other. I feel like it was written by two 6 year olds that sat in different rooms, used 2 Solo Cups connected with string to communicate the story ideas. And I get it, the first game was totally inconsistent and all over the place. I'm not even sure where to start with this game. I'm pretty sure this is a new VA for Jax? I liked the first VA better. But thats just preference. But why does he randomly ramble on like he is talking to someone. He also randomly screams when your jetpack ends and you start falling. Except I fell 1 foot onto a platform.. why is he yelling?! lol. Caja is just unbearable. Honestly some of the cringiest VA I have heard. She is just oh so random. If I had time and it didn't go past my return time, I really wanted to write it down and go through it. Same with Adam. OMG and Dex is just a tiny disaster. But no time as I'm already at 84 minutes.- Seriously.. Caja is canon?!? Nasty was better in just about every way. And can we at least spell it Caya in the english version. Also adding the son Dex felt so cringe. Like the game already jumped the FO4 shark. I'm looking forward to finding out that Dex is the key to everything or that they stole my son at some point. I'm calling it now.- Dialogue inconsistencies and naming. Get to Adam, get exposition about game. He calls them aliens Skyanids.. Jax them calls them Skyands. Than all of a sudden its Skyands. Makes me wonder what other dialogue issues we will get.- Hair - I know the owner or creative director looks like a bald pirate.. but is PB still going with the all character will be bald route. Are you still too lazy to create hair for characters.- Controls - Maybe its just me but on pc/KB/M the controls feel off. Maybe it has to do with the camera or the graphics issues but somethng feels less smooth. I can't quite put my finger on it but Elex 1 felt better combat wise.- Jetpack - Speaking of controls.. the jetpack landing/jumping is so frustratingly annoying. Do we really need to take 3 baby steps when I land. Literally land on small rock to platforming.. oh nm animation decided I am going to walk tiny baby steps and fall off. Jump on truck, ooops, no sir.. you are gonna walk off the edge and back onto the ground.If you love this game and think it has no issues, honestly more power to you, go enjoy it. I just needed to get this out and vent. I haven't been this disappointed with a game purchase in awhile. I want to have some hope that they will improve it but I have this feeling, this is what we get. Almost feels like they hate their fans.
