_childDocuments_.review: Note: I wrote the following several months ago based on time spent in the beta version.It's not easy being a fan of Piranha Bytes. But it's probably even harder to be Piranha Bytes itself when its best, most iconic game was released right from the start. After that, it was sometimes better, sometimes worse, but never as good. The first Elex was a good example of "sometimes better", but to appreciate the new ideas, gameplay finetuning and the dark, original SF plot, it was necessary to spend several hours before one was truly hooked.It is no different with its second part, especially since in terms of the plot it seems to be the "sometimes worse" – there is no earthquake at the beginning, there is no sense of mystery and no need to get even. At the beginning, the player is introduced to the game world and the situation so thoroughly that he has the impression that he knows how it will all end. The above is summed up by an awkward narrative, exposition dialogues, a son's plot that feels forced, and the practical impossibility of plunging into this world if you haven't played the previous part. One has to struggle through the introduction believing that it is worth it.Strangely – this is Piranha Bytes! – there seems to be hardly any bugs, especially serious ones, the game seems stable, there are few glitches and the opponents are demanding, but there will be no, at least at first, no one who kills the player with one bite, so the game is smooth and with time it gets more and more pleasant. The narrative matures, you can start tasting the richness and unconventional nature of adventures and stories, enjoy the freedom of action, which by no means translates to wandering around the empty world, because there is something to discover everywhere, interesting characters are met. You can enjoy the changes that have taken place on the planet Magalan since Jax defeated the Hybrid and realized that real worries would fall from the sky in the near future.And this and that happened in the meantime. The Berserkers took over some terrain of the Outlaws, the Clerics also lost importance, but new religious fanatics appeared: the Morkons. Jax's dramatic attempts to warn the people of Magalan of the looming danger bother most people even less than mankind bothers with the need to vaccinate on the distant planet Earth. Which essentially boils down to the Jax-player again having to save everyone roughly by himself – well, with a handful of friends.As the days grow longer, the storms are stronger – the deeper into Elex II, the more problems, dilemmas, difficult decisions, but also small victories and scraps of satisfaction – the more interesting it gets. After a few hours of play, you want to keep playing. Especially since Piranhas have drawn a number of conclusions from the gameplay shortcomings of the part one and they have addressed them. For example, this time, almost at the very beginning of the game, the player gains access, in fact, control over the Bastion, i.e. the headquarters of his future army, which he can, and even should, successively repair, expand and enlarge its crew; thanks to all above making preparations for the final trial is noticeable and it is hard to doubt what we are here for or what we are striving for.After more than twenty hours spent in Elex II (beta), I became convinced that this is an interesting, solidly made game. As any child of Piranha Bytes it’s not easy to perceive, it punishes carefree, it’s rough here and there, but it’s engaging, giving a sense of mission and curiosity about what will happen next. So far I have the first chapter of the story behind me, with dozens of human stories in which I took a more or less active part, and one attack by an alien race on my Stand, successfully pushed back. Much was happening and, in fact, for the most of time – taking into account the already scolded, not the most intriguing beginning – it was not boring. So I will keep playing until Elex II is finished and probably I will start waiting for the third part.There are still three months to the premiere – this time should allow Piranhas to refine this and that, remove the remaining bugs or certain irritating moments (well, let a long-lost character, encountered in the heat of battle, not rush to tell what happened to him! - also I'm glad to see you, but wait a minute...); maybe even the introduction to the game will be more attractive. Nevertheless, there are not many such problems; the Elex II is smooth, stable and pleasant to play. You can already see that this is a decent game. Unfortunately, although it is a remarkable, valuable production, I am afraid that too much commitment, even dedication, requires from the player, and offers him not enough modern gimmicks to gain good grades and gain new followers. Pity. Well, what are we old fans of Piranha Bytes for ...? (For playing).PS. (To Piranha Bytes, regarding the gimmicks mentioned). You can still create beautiful, probable and inviting worlds, be it fantasy or post-apo, but... Although it is understandable to be attached to your own technology, developed, improved and refined over the years, your well-deserved and well-worn engine unnecessarily pulls this diverse and interesting world down, and with it the whole game; effectively puts a scratch on the first impression. Maybe it's time to say goodbye to it and change to Unreal?PPS. Access to the beta version courtesy of Koch Media Poland.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is alright. I've been playing Pirahna's games since Gothic I. It feels very good to return to a game with the soul of Gothic. It takes you away to another world and makes you feel that you're really a part of it. Nevertheless, I feel that the content is lacking. I have an impression that devs made the final chapters in a rush. They are simply "go there kill that" type of quests with hoards of enemies. Some crucial story moments aren't explained well. It's a real pity since I love this genre mostly for its interesting storylines and twists. Almost none are found in Elex 2, or at least, there were none that I would reminisce. You kinda finish this game and forget it, its characters, and the whole plot. I also had this feeling about Elex I.Magic simply sucks. I played as an Alb but majorly I invested my AP and LP to perfect my shotgun skills. Enemies are dull, especially the bigger non-human ones. Map feels somehow empty. In Gothic you could stumble upon a named character in the most unexpected places (like Diego, for instance). You don't have it here. People are mostly in cities and their stories feel like checkmarks that the devs kinda did it, but you don't really become friends. Also, I didn't feel that my choices had an impact. Maybe they actually did but I haven't felt it.Otherwise, the game is alright. It kept me occupied for a decent number of hours, like 40ish +. But a decent part of it was just roaming around, exploring (Gothic had a lot more rewarding exploration), and killing hoards of monsters.If the last chapters were also filled with content, interesting story twists, and some decent quests, the game would deserve a 4 or 4.5-star rating. Otherwise, it's 3, max 3.5 stars for me. If you're a fan of the Gothic series, it's totally worth buying it. Oh, and it's a decent upgrade if compared to the first installment. I have to mention that my experience was bugfree. It's a great thing, since the majority of modern games require tons of patches to even complete them (!I'm talking to you CD Project Red!). Good job in this regard!P.S. Caja ignores a very important twist in the story. It sunk my immersion to the lowest depths. Pirahnas, I really hope you'll implement some improvements in the game! I'd eagerly replay it.I'm the guy who wrote you many many years ago (Die Nacht Des Raben period) via email and offered you assistance in developing your next game. You even replied me back then :)

_childDocuments_.review: Boy, if you're a fan of ELEX 1 and see all these reviews saying it's terrible (mostly from people with no play time ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about game performance which is actually quite bad to be fair)... even the ones with more play time, I don't understand the hate. ELEX was one of my favorite games at the time of it's release (as every PB game usually is one of the most fun, goofy rpg games of it's era).. and this game does improve on a lot of things, for example I love the jetpack being upgradable and starting out crap but ending up as this awesome mobility tool for more than just upward momentum.The quests, exploration and such are all intact, a bit more freedom though, I've been zipping around the entire centre of the map.Also, exploration is more rewarding with there being stat upgrade potions everywhere, elex potions scattered for xp, AP and skill points with no stupid consequences now, so it's like when you find that stuff it's just a small collectable rather than ELEX being a massive tradeoff and a no-no for good playthroughs. I thought it'd be silly to have these stat point potions and such so easy to get, but it works quite well so far, not too many of them around but a nice treat when you find them.Jet Fuel is my favourite of these collectables, every time I find one I'm excited to be able to fly higher.Will update with more play-time, but for now, 8.5/10 very strongUPDATE, 20 HOURS: Game is still awesome, finished berserker hub mostly and explored a tonne.. the camera became an issue for me, was wildly distacting. BUT the latest update added an alternate camera which is a fixed good fov. No way to tweak it through inis yet, but there will be a mod I'm sure. 8.5/10 still!UDPATE 29 HOURS: Things are flying by like crazy, hours feel like minutes. One of my favorite parts of a PB game, where all the quests and your exploration is starting to all come together, and when a faction is almost entirely explored, you move on to another. Awesome.UPDATE 35 HOURS: Still fun :)

_childDocuments_.review: I finished it. And it finished me.There is no evolution left in PB's games and this newest iteration really shows they are stuck on every level, living off their past glory.The combat: You are a train on rails, so are your enemies, and you slide back and forth against each other until one of you dies. No proper hitboxes, no attack animation windup, no character movement, no attack variation (holding down left click while your enemy moves away 15 meters and you still hit doesn't count). Only rails. End of story.The graphics: Well. Well well. What happened? I don't know. Where their last game was actually quite alright to look at, with this one we got shiny clay faces, disproportioned children and all around ugly character models which are, sadly, being reused for every third non-story npc. Story npcs are unique, but still ugly-unique.The story: Painful to say, but the story-charme that I was hoping for just didn't come through in the slightest. It's bland and uninteresting, there isn't much of a story arch other than "new enemy, must kill". And off you go with your weaponized fighter on rails until enough enemies have died. Choo-choo!The music/sound: To this day I listen to Risen and Gothic playlists on Youtube and it's a delight. I regret to tell you that PB has forgotten or never even realized how awesome and integral the music composition of (some of) their past games has been. Kudos to Kai Rosenkranz. Here the music and sounds don't cause any emotional response in the player at all. Playing it on mute makes almost no difference.The quest design: Initial chapters of the game were fun and quite interesting to play through, well done. As the game went on it deteriorated so much that my mood went down with it up until it really made me agonize over the quest checklists, rather than enjoy the game. All you do with your companion quests and later quests in the game is: kill 50 enemies. then 20, then another 200, then some more. Truly awful.I finished Elex II, I needed to because i wanted to make sure I didn't miss anything.Now all I miss is the time I spent on it.So long, and thanks for all the fun in previous games.

_childDocuments_.review: As a new threat crashes down onto earth, trying to remake the planet into their own home. Our hero, Jax, needs to come out of the shadows and begin his new journey.After getting infected by some sort of poison from the unknown creatures, Jax has been weakened, lost all his strength and skills, and is in need of learning them all again.Explore the world, build up the old bastion, recruit trusted members, join a faction, and stop the incoming threat.Elex II is a sequel to their previous game, Elex, with older and crankier visuals. By the look of Elex II, there have been a lot of improvements since Elex, which can be seen in flashbacks as lore from the first game has grown in the sequel.Elex II is an action role-playing video game similar to Fallout 4 and other similar game. The game starts out with a cutscene of our main character, Jax, carrying a dead creature back to his cabin. Carefully opening the door not to activate his handmade trap/alarm and throwing the creature onto the floor.Walking upstairs to an old, roughed-up room, he picks up a picture of his son, and suddenly a meteor crashes straight through the roof. As it happens, Jax runs down to escape from the house. As he manages to escape, the meteor explodes, turning into a large tower. Bringing with it new dangerous creatures made with Dark Elex running through them. After the cutscene, the player will get to run and loot a bit of items during Jax’s escape from the creatures. A little tutorial for using weapons, walking, looting, and such.After the tutorial, Jax wakes up in a ruined house, with a man taking care of our wounds and giving us a small waist jetpack. But only for us to learn that the man was none other than Doc from the previous game who awoke “The Hybrid.” The player will get to learn more lore during the playthrough by completing the main and side quests. After I woke up as Jax, I looked around my beginnings and looted what I could find. When I first tried the game, I was so unsettled by the movement physics and view of the player character. But with time, I got used to them pretty quickly and learned them.I was having a very enjoyable time during the time I was playing. Finishing one mission after another and exploring my surroundings. The player can choose what to fight with between long-ranged weapons such as bows and guns. Swords and blades with shields and magic.Myself I chose to go with bows, both since they weren’t requiring any high attribute level and to deal a large amount of damage. On the downside, I need to buy more arrows from time to time, but on the upside, it’s a good beginner's weapon of choice. As the game goes on, the player will explore the enormous map and find new towns and points of interest. Each faction has a bit of lore from the previous game, and the player will have the opportunity to decide which faction they want to join.During the main mission, the mission tab can be split into more categories, which can then have their own required side missions.Some side missions are required to further process into a main mission to proceed with the story in the game. Other side missions that aren’t required can be taken on by the player, and in most cases, they will turn out to be something good later on, or they will simply get a bit of currency or an item.Other side missions that aren’t required can be taken on by the player, and in most cases, they will turn out to be something good later on, or they will simply get a bit of currency or an item.The character has six tabs, as follows:Whether tab the player has open, they will see the player level, their amount of currency, AP, and LP (attribute points and skill points)The tab contains:Strength, Constitution, Dexterity, Intelligence, and Cunning.These attribute levels upgrade the player's stats and also give access to better weapons.Abilities can be learned from teachers. It costs currency and skill points to learn a new ability; there are ten ability categories.Combat, Survival, Crafting, Personality, Berserker, Alb, Morkon, Outlaw, Cleric, and Jetpack.The categories: Berserker, Alb, Morkon, Outlaw, and Cleric can only be accessed by joining either of the factions. Meaning that if you join one of the specific factions, you can only learn that category in the abilities.Each one of those categories requires the player to be in their faction to learn their set of abilities.A few NPC's that are traders can teach as well. But there aren’t many of them.Traders will be found inside towns/cities and, on some occasions, outside the town/cities while still remaining on their land. Some traders will have small side quests for the player.Teachers will help the player learn new skills, as the player cannot simply level up and just select a skill. They have to learn it from specialized teachers for a small cost and skill points.The shaders and shadows are truly wonderful, and it all mixes in with the surroundings. Stone walls are lit up by chandeliers hanging from the roofs, blowing tree branches that cover the sun and creating shadows in their design.Everything in this game looks very good and is making me speechless, as it has such a realistic feeling with how the light bounces from objects and how shadows are created from lights either from outside, like the sun, or from a few candles inside.There is a day and night cycle in the game, which makes the sun rise up and go down, so the projectile light moves with the angle of the sun. For the visuals in this game and how detailed, automatic, and simply realistic they are, it’s a show for the eyes.Elex II has changed a lot in its graphical quality since the prequel game. The textures look highly realistic and smooth, reminding me of Fallout 4 graphical textures.All great games have NPCs, and even greater games have voiced all their NPCs with their own voice actors.The recorded voice lines sound just like if the NPCs would have said themselves in-game at the place they are in. Meaning it doesn’t sound like it was made in a studio or poorly made.The music is calm and soothing, with a mix of piano, violin, and drums, along with a light-voiced choir.Depending on the situation, the music can change. When entered into combat, the war drums will start playing. But as soon as the last enemy dies and the battle ends, the music goes back to normal.It's not only the music that makes the time pass by and keeps the mind at ease, it's also all the different sounds that play around the player. Wind blowing in the air, birds chittering, small rocks or boulders rolling down mountains.The time spent reviewing this game took longer than planned, but it was worth the time to make this review.This game is truly amazing and beautiful and has so much to offer. There are so many play styles and items, and I am not even close to finishing this game.Everything is truly amazing, and I want to give it a 10, but with a few minor faults, some of which can be fixed but are not necessary.Rating: 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: The story continues for Jax and with the usual Gothic "baseline", then even after saving the world once, he will start out to be a nobody and be treated like one. Tough world.You're thrown into the story like a bad monday with a quiet hunting turning into a freaking spaceship almost landing on your house. Doubt insurance covers that part.The whole situation ends up with Jax being wounded and infected, causing him to be drained and so results in your hero being "back to square one".The story takes on an approach to a different kind of Elex that's part of the whole chain reaction you learn from the first game. You spend your time building up reputation to make an army to fight the new invaders, learn about the new Elex, stories for new and old companions to ultimately face off those rude beings that destroyed your house.The general atmosphere in Elex 2 feels much like the same in first game to me. There are quite a few different biomes and it's not a bad sight depending on your graphics settings. Running the DX12 version, which is said to be a "beta" client ran perfectly on max settings, albeit a few texture flickering happened here and there.Combat has a bit less "eurojank", but especially the Jetpack combat is versatile and great for both airborne and landbased enemies. It's also a vital tool to upgrade for exploring, which is a large part you'd consider to find great loot.Factions can be joined again and more have been added. They even have a small change, that you can join one faction initially and halfway join a 2nd faction allowing you to keep skills from both factions.Companions bring some chitchat to surroundings, so they don't act like mute followers. Small downside is that some companions feel less useful due to their focus on melee, that cause them to be "stuck" as they try to predict enemy movement. A strong advice is to bring Caja, Crony or Bully.Overall I enjoyed the experience and felt sucked in running around exploring the world, sometimes resulting in quick loads due to a persistence of trying to kill high level enemies. Just because it is possible, but dangerous :PThe biggest downside is that the ending leads up to something interesting, which we may never hear about due to Piranha Bytes being closed down :(

_childDocuments_.review: I think its simple: if you liked Gothic I and II you probably will like Elex II. Does it have a perfect combat system?No and most weapons are underpowered. Shotguns are overpowered in the beginning and kinda balanced later on, while everything else deals not enough damage. This is a common problem of Gothic-like games like Gothic, Risen and Elex I though.Can the Game be unfair to you?Yes, but in my oppinion its part of a Gothic game to find a way to abuse the game to make something work. I remember how back in Gothic you used your temporal companions to fight enemies which were way too strong for you early on. If you stray from the main path in the beginning of the game prepare to be killed by some big enemy. And even the most basic enemies can kill you in the beginning, if you dont pay attention.Does it get worse over time?Sadly yes. Act I is perfect (and the longest) and the game declines after that because the quests tend to be "kill all enemies in a certain area" later on. That is a bit of a let down. Act I has the perfect Gothic feeling though and in my honest opinion that alone is worth the play.I can't say much about the english translation. As far as i know the original is in german and the german version is on point. I finished the game after 52 hours with all achievments completed. You can probably rush the main stroy in about 12 hours but there is much to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: While I recommend Elex 2, it's not a strong recommendation.Elex 2 gives you a large world to explore, relationships to manage, factions to ally with, and monsters to kill.The side-quests, character interactions, and faction quests are interesting and fun.The gameplay is improved from the previous game.There are interesting skill trees to unlock that can greatly modify your experience.Combat certainly feels much better, and the jetpack in particular stands out and feels great to use.However, I think Elex 2 could have been much better had it played to its strengths.The main story is very weak, poorly paced, and feels unengaging. Huge missed potential.The combat, while improved, still feels janky and frustrating to engage with.The choices you make, while impactful, just aren't impactful enough to make you take them seriously.Its trying to cast too wide of a net.I feel like Elex 2 does't do well enough in the combat department to attract new players.By doing this, they removed the focus on story that made the first Elex so charming.I think its a hard game to recommend, but I played the first Elex so I'm used to doing things the hard way.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRElex 2 is a great rpg game with a lot to do but it clearly needs patching. It has graphical bugs, performance issues and various other issues that can effect a players immersion. If you can put up with that great but otherwise wait for a few patches. Personally I'm having a blast even with the bugs.Elex 2 world is both rewarding and fun to explore especially with the jetpack. Combat is a mixed bag you can chain attacks, power attack and parry. There are a range of different ranged weapons from bows, energy weapons and heavy weapons. overall the combat feels a little off, with weapons lacking punch. There are tons of quests in the game, as you would expect some are better than others but the overall standard is good. You can craft, ammo, potions and socket gems into weapons.There is a lot of bugs like graphical flickering scenery and npcs, to the ai getting stuck in the background when you are talking etc.Graphics are a mixed bag the texture range from good to poor, the environmental design is great especially crater town, go there at night very atmospheric.Music is good and fits well with the feel of the game. Some of the background npc dialogue is oblivion level bad, would better to remove them all together.Elex 2 does have graphical bugs, performance issues and various other issues that can effect a players immersion. If you can put up with that great but otherwise wait for a few patches. Personally I'm having a blast even with the bugs, I would highly recommend elex 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Conclusion:  Elex 2 is a good game and worth playing if you're already committed to Piranha Bytes' style of RPG.  It's just not better than Elex 1.Verbose Stuff:I'm a fan of Piranha Bytes.  I've played everything from Gothic through the Risen series and Elex 1.  I won't bother with the comparison of PB games to AAA titles; plenty of other reviews do that.  I finished a mostly completionist playthrough in 65 hours using mostly ranged combat and the Alb faction skills.  What I will try and do is capture my impressions of the improvements and deterioration since Elex 1.Improvements:1. The graphics engine.  The graphics are much improved from Elex 1.  Draw distance, poly count, textures, etc. all look much better this time around.  It does come at a performance cost but frame rates stayed over 60 at max settings on my 2080Ti.2. Terrain and architecture.  Similar to 1 both elements are much improved.  The changes to locations visited in Elex 1 such as the Fort, abandoned Alb converters, etc. are very well done.  It's a pleasure to revisit locations from the first game.3. Flying enemies.  Most of the enemies are a rehash of those from Elex 1 but flying enemies are a new addition.  However, see the comment below on hit boxes.4. Melee combat.  Melee combat is much improved over Elex 1.  Enemy patterns and tells are more predictable making dodging viable and stamina seems to last a bit longer making it possible to use hit and run tactics on tougher enemies.5. Upgradeable jet pack.  Nuff said.  The jetpack was one of the highlights of Elex 1 and making it more versatile in Elex 2 is a great step forward.6. Crafting system.  The crafting system has a bit more depth and is improved over the system in Elex 1.  You can still rely on named weapons but you can likewise craft some really potent versions of regular ones.7. Flashlight.  You now have - wait for it - a flashlight!  No more relying on flares for lighting!  Similarly the extreme gamma from Elex 1 has been toned down a bit.Deterioration:1. Field of view.  Holy ****!  Who thought a narrow FOV which dynamically widens when you move only to contract when you stop was a good idea?  This think is seriously puke inducing if you are prone to motion sickness.  You can change the width of the FOV in the game's XML files but regrettably not the dynamic change.  This needs to be front and center in the settings menu.2. Hit boxes / terrain collision meshes.  Ranged combat is just as viable (and sometimes a necessity) as in Elex 1.  The enemy hit boxes, particularly for flying enemies,  however are a complete disaster.  You will waste countless ammo on shots that should have hit but don't.  Similarly the terrain collision mesh will block countless shots where there is a clear line of sight.3. Magic.  It just feels underpowered.  Scaling is just not sufficient to deal with some of the bullet sponge enemies later in the game.  See below on bullet sponges.4. Enemy lasers.  Thankfully, most enemy ranged attacks (poison, fire, etc.) have been toned down and can be dodged fairly effectively.  Not so with enemy lasers.  These things are unerringly accurate and do massive amounts of damage even in the late game with the best armor and HP upgrades.  These need to be better balanced.5. Bullet sponge enemies.  Elex 2 follows the practice in the Elex 1 of enemies with prefixes - i.e. hunting, weak, old, etc.  However, in the later game some of the prefixed and regular enemies turn into absolute bullet sponges making certain battles a complete laborious slog.6. End game grind.  As you approach the end game, it turns into a serious grind-fest.  Literally, hundreds of enemy troops will encircle faction camps and require elimination before you can progress.  After the first few, I came to dread these missions because of the sheer monotony.7. Unpleasant companions.  Most of your companions are so god****** unpleasant!  I was a big fan of Nasty in Elex 1.  She was admittedly vulgar and abrasive but she did have a certain charm.  And as the story progressed it revealed the reason for her behavior.  Not so in Elex 2.  Nasty, Bully, and Caja in particular are just unbearable and I couldn't finish their loyalty quests fast enough so I could dump them from the party.8. Companion AI.  Companion AI was not great in Elex 1 but I don't remember it being this bad.  Your companions in Elex 2 will be mostly memorable for blocking doorways and getting in the way of ranged fire.9. Bunch of other nits. No meaningful use for the quantities of dark elex you find.  Scrap function in inventory is more hinderance than help.  Jax's disease progression is a complete nuisance and the accompanying sound effect is more akin to serious intestinal distress than an impending mutation.

_childDocuments_.review: As fan of Piranha Bytes (PB) since the first Gothic days I seriously have to ask what happened to them. Elex 2 is by no means an AAA, AA or "good" game for that matter. Following I want to share my thoughts after my full playthrough In short (spoiler free):- The story feels forced, none of the choices the NPCs or the player make have a reasonable argumentation behind them. Main quests contents are mostly that some NPC says "I just got news from an attack there and there, please go and kill the aggressors" be it monsters, story enemies, faction enemies or else. Nothing is really explained. An important NPC dies and no one even mentions it, not even the characters close to them. How? It's just bad writing. - The quests are 80 % "search and kill". If you are into that, have fun. There are two side quests in the whole game that were memorable to me and those were slightly hidden (puppeteer questline and child investigators questline).- The dialogues are absolutely cringeworthy and not funny or logically reasonable in any way. Who approved this? And why do some words in the subtitles have to be in capitals in at least every other line (no joke)? Not even the speakers pronounce them differently.- The graphics are ok, but the game is horribly optimized. With a 1080 GTX at a 1920x1200 resolution I am getting 25 - 40 fps and that with an engine that is used by PB since 2006 (!). Character faces and models lack fine tuning and don't look good at all. A DirectX 12 update was promised but has not arrived for over 5 months now. Update news are non existent since May 2022.To sum it up:Some say Elex 2 is a little bit like Risen 2, being the middle child of the Risen series by the same developer and lacking sensible development choices as well, but with Risen 2 at least the world building and the story choices checked out. Some say with PB games it is always a janky but somehow lovely experience with a believable, detailed world, immersive story and rough humor. Elex 2 is none of that, it just feels like PB had to finish something somehow and with the least effort possible.My feeling with the Elex series is that PB has already signed off from it. Elex 1 was a somehow fresh experience but with Elex 2 it feels like the enthusiasm within the dev studio is already gone. I do not expect Elex 3 to be any better.

_childDocuments_.review: In many aspects the best PB Game ever. Get over the superficial impurities and prepare to be impressed! I have played all PB-Games and I'm glad to find well developed old strengths as well as some new found ones. It will love you back after a while, invest some trust! Its been a long time, since a new game could bring me this much joy.Pros:Great Quest-Design with some of the best Characters since Gothic 2. Very smart decision making. The Setting makes for thought provoking topics, which sometimes do and sometimes dont come across (the technical presentation hinders the atmosphere of otherwise great moments)The dialouge is mixed but has its moments.Incredibly satisfying player-progression thanks to the perfect balance between grind and questing. (playing on normal difficulty)The Jetpack. It just works so well.The combat system is a solid step up from the last game. Works for me. Still not on the level of Risen one (which is gold standard for me), but I fined fighting quite enjoyable, thanks to the Jetpack and the great variety of weapons/spellsCons:What people have issues with are mainly graphics/overall presentation and controls. Both points tested my patients, tooGraphics. I liked the whole Risen series (Just replayed it in parts) better. It's for the most part a pretty ugly game. After some getting used to, I find it works for me more and more, espacially indoors. The outdoors in the bright midday look shockingly bad.Somewhat dissapointed by the open World. Risen one was a master class in how to make good use of limited space, every little place in that game is dear to me as a result. Elex 2 is too big for my liking.The music does its part ok, but in a PB-Game, it can only be compared to Rosenkranz' works, which shine above and beyond Elex one and two.I personally dont like the so called science-fantasy-setting, would much much rather deepdive into a more coherent world than this a-bit-of-everything. In my view, a more focused approach with a smaller world would unleash the unmatched atmosphere of earlier PB-Games. Because I'm overall quite impressed by the improvements since Elex one, just make everything smaller!I dont mind the camera at all, except the stupid enemy-locking system in fights (!)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great fun and hard to put down once started. Its easy to get lost in this beautiful, handcrafted open world where every landmark and every hidden corner has a meaning and holds a little reward for climbing all the way up - and in doing so, feels very much alive. We continue to follow the story of grumpy yet super-cool hero Jax, who's got not only a son (and - highly entertaining - arguments with the mother of said little guy about parenting style) but also  a good measure of dark humor which serves him just great and makes him a lot more human. So, on the pro's we have many hours of fun world exploration, an improved version of the highly motivating character development system of ELEX I, and a pretty cool story with mostly great voice actors (and a bunch of nice little side quests each with their own little side stories that are crafted with love). The con's are just the same issues that plague ELEX I (and before that, every other game of Piranha Bytes Studio): animations and character design are not exactly AAA standard, the fights are simple and a bit clunky, visuals in general a bit flawed. However, for me the pro's are so strong that I can easily tolerate the flaws and still get a great 80 hours of role-play gaming entertainment out of it while feeling pretty heroic and mightly engaged with saving the world for most of the time. Something that I miss in many of the highend blockbusters lately. So, I'd highly recommend this game. However, folks with an AMD graphics board should maybe wait for the next patch until they give it a try as there seem to be issues that need fixing.___Update: I'm close to the final chapter now, and I love the game. Great story, lots of fun, and I absolutely love the open world exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really, really wanted to like this game. I was looking for ELEX for a very very long time and I consider myself a Gothic/Risen fan, although I'm not very knowledgeagle in those games... but liked them so much to have them on steam and GOG and got Risen back in 2008 or 2009 in a physical edition...But I can't the game is awful, ELEX 2 is a complete failure of a game. It came out on 2022, I'm playing it on 2023 and it feels like playing a game older than Risen, it feels like a 2006 game... Elex is clunky, it's janky, glitchy, buggy, tiresome and incredibly unpolished. It feels like a game in alpha.I'll divide this in two parts, the game technically and the game's plot.Technically speaking, I can't say much more than what I already said. The game feels worst than Risen. Ranged attacks felt more natural and polished in Gothic 2, a game from 2002... Inventory management is counter intuitive, quest logs are stupid because some quests don't progress naturally... You need to talk with someone but the game doesn't tell you... You can sleep but NPCs or events doesn't pass like the time... They literally won't move if you're sleeping... Quests are buggy, the game crashes a lot, is optimized poorly, NPCs dissapear, don't appear, quests doesn't register properly... The ranged attack system sucks, thank god is OP, the melee system is one of the worst I've ever seen and I wasn't interested enough in checking the magic system. Animations feel like if the game is in an Alpha state and 90% of the mods are for QOL improvements and gameplay tweaks.The game is slow, dialogues are slow, animations are slow, facial expresions are dumb... It really feels and runs like an Alpha.With the argument... I... I don't know where to start. Every single character in this game is stupid and just a few of them are actually likeable. Some of the companions you have openly dislike you. Whatever you do... they don't care.There's a bunch of factions that hate each other, sometimes even they hate themselves and sometimes they attack you... but nothing happens. The game gives the impression that it's not really an RPG, what's going to happen is going to happen, no matter what, there's no choice, you, as the main character, are just an anecdote during the game... Nothing that you do really matters... that for an RPG that's really gruesome.Summing up, the story feels like a Gothic 2/3 ripoff and... in a way, it is... it truly is... There's a point in the game, around chapter 2, that if you've played Piranhya Bytes previous games you know what's going to happen.That's the biggest problem... PB is still making the same game they've always did... over and over... with the same mechanics, plots, characters and twists... _childDocuments_.review: First impressions with this game are amazing. It plays much better than original Elex (not that it was bad or something, love that game). There are many new little nice things like map markers, grabbing ledges, etc. and overall it feels more polished. Graphics are nice (especially lip sync and face animations), world is beautiful, soundtrack great as always, exploration rewarding. Bonus point for being able to explain blood cult to my young son.Will update as I continue on my journey.Edit 1:Base combat also feels good. Enemy attacks are nicely telegraphed and dodgeable meaning most enemies are defeatable regardless of level or equipment if player is patient and skilled enough. Strong attack feels kind of janky, but it doesn't affect overall experience much.Edit 2:Jetpack upgrades and air combat are fun and enrich combat. Flying seems to fool enemy AI sometimes tho. Monster design is best PB ever had, models are incredibly detailed and beautiful, close look in bestiary is gorgeous. World design, world-building and environmental storytelling is amazing especially changes in world and culture of people of Magalan since events of Elex 1. Edges of map seems to be too empty, at least some loot could have been included. Game also suffer from many little bugs, like occasional funny model behaviour near edges and often dysfunctional quick-scroll trough inventory. Also, for some reason camera has flash-light, like it was a drone following Dex (I choose to imagine that for immersion othewise it's quite annoying).You can pickpocket children. Children interactions are overall very well made and a lot of fun especially one vandalism investigation case.Edit 3:Chloe, Tilas and C.R.O.N.Y.Edit 4:Few things that bother me about the game are that alien energy orbs have no collision or effect on player, it really breaks the immersion. And most NPCs don't seem to have day/night cycles and are just standing at the same place except for specific interactions. This is kind of strange, since NPCs had life cycles back in Gothic 1. It makes it really difficult to steal also. Travelling merchants also steal a ton of EXP from player if they happen to go by, since there is a lot of monsters on roads and merchant guards are extremely strong and kill everything in their way. This is issue only if merchant had spawned (player is close) they wont kill creatures in world without player since they are not physically in world at that point.Stealing (and pick-pocketing) from player perspective is great tho. You can steal weapons from people (it disappears as model) witch is really nice for progression and also money making. I really like lore, society and design of Albs and their technology, also the link to alien invaders. It seems to be inspired by Laconia empire of the Expanse, whole Elex is in many ways.Edit 5:Shotguns feel really nice to use.FINAL EDIT:After long long time I finally finished the game. And it sadly fell apart in story and and quest department in later chapters. I dropped the game for months after unlocking all skills and returned to it, finishing chapter 3,4 and 5 alongside companion story quests in few sittings and it was not a great experience. Quests were really repetitive and uninspired (just killing a ton of stuff basically), all alien constructs the same including FINAL ONE. That being said, game is still great and an improvement in many ways over Elex 1. But in some it feels like few steps backwards. No alternative fire modes for ranged weapons, combo system gone from combat, even more simplistic crafting. Actually I loved the crafting, it allowed me to craft all best weapons just by pickpocketing weapons from NPCs, and yes I looted them all, and forging them together to form ultimate one. But ultimately it was very basic and crafting ammo was more expensive than just buying it. I unlocked that skill just to have it. And the world felt smaller and less interesting even tho it was the most beautiful and detailed in terms of graphical fidelity PB ever made. And the main story is probably the worst I remember from PB. Last half felt really, really underdeveloped, or bloated for no reason. All that story could be told in some more interesting way than just kill X of that Y of that other thing and come back for some exposition. And what was the ending? Caja didn't even have any reaction to her son supposedly dying. She was just really happy I accomplished something big apparently. I don't know all I did was clear the same dungeon for the sixth time. Anyway still recommend the game even if just for initial exploration and first few chapters of the story.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first game, you will most likely enjoy this one as well. If you didn't play  the first game, i'd recommend playing it before this one, since it is cheaper, it will give you an idea of what these games feel like and this is a direct continuation of the first games story. I would say that i did a pretty completionist playthrough, and overall I had a good time with the game. There are a bunch of bugs, most of which are minor but there can be major ones as well. One of my companions died because of one of these bugs, keeping me from finishing her quest. (Her name is Nyra)Overall, movement and combat are all a bit clunky, so saying this game is rough around the edges is pretty accurate. Don't expect a smooth and polished experience. That being said, the game still functions. It's nowhere near to unplayable, just kind of rough at times. Especially the basic magic attacks can be a nightmare to fight with.On the upside, ELEX 2 still has the unique and interesting feel of its predecessor. It's a wild mix of fantasy, science fiction and post apocalyptic themes that all blend together very well. The Art direction for both monsters and environments is genuinely good. New armor sets and weapons look amazing and feel extremely rewarding. Progression overall is one of this series strong points for me, as you literally go from 0 to hero and can really feel it. The game rarely holds your hand and is not afraid to see you killed countless times if you are not careful and do not respect your own weakness in the beginning. The world is pretty big and very diverse, with like 5 or 6 different biomes and different faction bases. You have a jetpack that you can upgrade and use to get to pretty much every peak of every building, where, as in many other locations, you can find hidden loot. Exploring is always rewarding, especially if you have progressed enough to deal with most of the basic threats. In tpyical Piranha Bytes fashion, almost every NPC in the world is either an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or a coward or both and ultimately only out for their own profit. Everyone curses all the time and nobody gives you anything for free. It is a very different experience from pretty much any RPG made by a different developer, and I adore these guys for that. That being said, the story and dialogue, although for the most part entertaining, are rarely truly meaningful or thought invoking. There are some exceptions though. The quests are still fun though, they often have something unique or gripping about them and some of the decisions you make in them can have minor or major consequences. If up-to-date graphics and polish are not your main concerns and you are looking for an open world RPG with a unique setting, you should give this series a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Caja used to love me. Then I became an outlaw. She no longer loves me, but we do still sleep together from time to time.In all seriousness, Elex 2 is a typical modern Piranha Bytes game. If you like their recent games then you will like this.However, what tends to differentiate each of their games for me is the combat, and unfortunately the combat in Elex 2 is still incredibly janky and disappointing. Some of the ideas they implemented aren't bad (such as the finisher move when an enemy is knocked down), and you can actually dodge roll most attacks, which didn't always feel possible in Elex 1, but the real problem is the animations. _childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of PB's games since I first played Gothic 1. If you're not familiar, they all have a similar open world playstyle where you can go pretty much anywhere* (and get your *** beat if you aren't careful) and muck around doing quests and whatever while ignoring the main storyline. Unlike many other open world games, many of your decisions have an impact on future outcomes (though not always a big impact). You also end up having to make irreversible choices (such as to what faction to join) which precludes you from going through the other options in that play through.So is it good? I've enjoyed the game quite a lot. I've got ~26 hours on record up to this point. Overall, I think I am enjoying it more than the first. Most of the mechanics are essentially the same with some improvements here and there; if you hated the systems of the first then you'll probably want to pass on this one since it more of the same. But if you like the play style of Elex 1 or the other PB games, then give this one a go. There's more I could say, but I'd rather be playing :)

_childDocuments_.review: May I present to you Elex II, the latest in a grand line of mostly-fantastic Piranha Bytes games that showed PC gamers the joys of brutally unfair but addictive action/RPG combat years before those games that somehow got an entire genre named for the idea.  Elex I was my game of the year for 2017, so I both was incredibly excited for Elex II and also wondering if they could possibly make the sequel my game of the year for 2022.  Fortunately, my expectations were largely met and in some ways surpassed; unfortunately, Dying Light 2 also came out this year, sooooo not so much able to repeat the best-of-the-year feat.THAT SAID, what exactly do we have here?  An excellently immense (even bigger than the first game I think?) open-world RPG in the beautiful style where everything is mysterious and confusing and you get ABSOLUTELY DESTROYED if you venture even slightly outside where the game expects you to be at low levels, yet can also cheekily grab some powerful loot way ahead of time if you can outrun or at least outmaneuver the terrifying monsters in your path.  Weapons have stat requirements, but armor does not, so with clever hoarding you can get fairly resilient early on, which might help you survive being absolutely annihilated by a pack of raptors.  There are seemingly even more ways to expand your character this time around, with Elex as a character enhancement method no longer having the downside of "COLD" as in the first game, but rather this mechanic is replaced with "destruction" where killing random defenseless creatures for loot and being an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ creep you ever more towards villainy, eventually enabling you to, seemingly anyway, start fights via dialogue with characters who would otherwise live through the game.There are many other changes and enhancements to Elex II compared to its predecessor, and its great and not-so-great things often arise in tandem, such as how interacting with other characters often results in decently-voiced and sometimes quite clever dialogue, yet for whatever reason characters seem to only have about three possible animations, one of which being "basically stand there and sway a little."  This really does bring NPC chatter down a bit in terms of enjoyment.  Fortunately the main storyline is BONKERS DYNAMITE at times, especially if you have been rolling with Jax' adventures in Magalan all the way from the first game, and without any spoilers beyond "I sure do hope they get to make Elex III" I have to say they set up Elex III even more majestically than how they set up Elex II, and the ending of the first game is one of the only times I will tell people "yeah you really should play the first game" when asking if you should get into a series mid-way.  There is so much to love about Elex II that it is incredibly easy to overlook a modest lack of polish, particularly when the lighting effects often look so good (especially sunrise/set and torchlight in darkness) that I find myself taking screenshots despite the fact that the characters are otherwise doing nothing interesting.If you fully commit yourself to investigating the world of Elex, you will find yourself continually rewarded in cameos and callbacks and unexpected moments where things you never even questioned end up having a genuine in-world explanation (ask me about frantically texting my friend at 1 A.M. "THE TOYS!!!  THEY MADE THE TOYS MAKE SENSE!!!").  This is a series where the writers have either known where all (three?) games are going from the beginning or are so good at making it up as they go along that you will never be disappointed by the plot.  I mean, you might be disappointed by some of the general Piranha Bytes jank, but honestly this is about as jank-free as any of their games I have ever played.  Just enough to remind you that you are at the whims of your Eastern European RPG Masters.And when you beat the game, you get to use the jetpack infinitely.  Legitimately one of the best rewards I can think of in gaming history for seeing a title through to the end
_childDocuments_.name: ELEX II

_childDocuments_.review: I love pretty much everything about the PB games and the first installment of Elex in particular, and I really want to love those same things here in Elex 2, but they are just worse compared to the previous games.Combat is substandard - you only have a small number of moves - no special attacks, combos, nothing like that. Hell, Elex wasn't shining at that, but at least it had an organic sequencing of regular/heavy attacks in place! Multiple ranged weapon modes - forget it. A variety of skills (like Suggestion) that you can learn - nope.The story is not bad and it builds up on top of that of Elex pretty decently; there are a few plot twists, even, that are not entirely predictable. But the endgame quests follow the simple go-there-and-kill-40-enemies paradigm. There are a number of other cards that PB had on their hand, but they chose to fold that particular hand.Factions.. PB decided to go the lazy way here. There are 5 factions, but only three have full-scale quest lines. Clerics and Outlaws are just left out. As for the quests themselves, I did an Alb playthrough, and I didn't get the feeling of making an impact on the Alb community, their well-being, infra, anything (unlike in Elex 1). Faction quests are poorly done overall - simply go there do that kind of quest. People who liked Elex will not find satisfaction they want.The game world and locations are nicely done - PB is known for their hand-crafted worlds, and here it doesn't disappoint in the slightest. Exploring this world is less rewarding compared to the predecessor, though. Mainly due to..Crafting. Crafting stat potions is OP and is the easiest way to get the stats you need for better weapons. And as for the better weapons, about the best weapons in the game can be obtained by killing enemies and crafting. Hence, no need to explore.The companions are worse in near every conceivable way. The companions in Elex had interesting stories (for the most part) and character complexities. Remember Ray? The-guy-you-want-at-your-campfire-Ray? Well, forget about chars like that. Here, the companions are simple, far from being interesting. Nyra is OK, so is Fox, but that's about that. Bully is just an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥; Nasty was ruined completely. Caja is just a mean old hag. And guess what - the companions quests and their loyalties don't make any meaningful difference. Wish it was a bit Mass-Effect-2 like.Graphics are better, but that's to be expected. Textures that appear 20m away from you are not.And of course the bugs. Elex wasn't free of those, but those were few and far between. Low impact, too. Here, you sometimes cannot complete quests because of those. Doesn't happen often, thankfully. Here I should also mention that some inconsistencies are present that really get on your nerve (at the beginning, you can go to the Fort with Caja, now a berserker warlord, and guess what - you won't be let in by the guard! With a warlord as your companion!). And things like that areplenty!All in all, it feels like the weakest installment in the whole PB lineup. Gothic 3 wasn't much, but even that was better that Elex 2. Unfortunatelly.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game just like all Piranha Bytes games! Excellent quests and mostly interesting story.Start off as a nobody and slowly build your way up.Awesome character progression with difficult choices until you get your hands on end-game gear.Jetpack with turbo boost is a unique and fun way of getting around the world.Choose one of 5 factions - 3 main / 2 secondary, or no faction at all.Punishing, almost souls-like combat which feels rewarding to learn and execute correctly, especially melee, though it can get repetitive once you learn how to deal with each monster type.What I didn't like:- Legendary Items make the crafting system irrelevant. Most legendaries are too easy to acquire long before you are able to equip them.- Faction progression after joining a faction is shamefully short. You can go from rank 1 to 3 in any faction in under 1 hour (as long as you are lvl 30+). - Many quests in the last 2 chapters are "Go to place X and kill Y number of monsters", which is a big contrast to the engaging and story-driven nature of quests in the rest of the game.- All flying monsters make the 'generic bird sound' before their swoop attack. Yes, even the jetpack mutants. Not to mention the endgame flyers take 10 shots from the best bow in the game to bring down which is a waste of time. The game would have been much better without a single flying monster.- Two handed weapons are only good in the hands of your opponents and companions. Their damage is not enough to warrant being locked into a slow attack and risking death. Some opponents could still 2-shot me with a 2-hander through best armor in the game, with some glitchy out-of-sync 2h attack animations. Your companion Falk uses a 2h, he is the most useful.

_childDocuments_.review: Factions are half-baked. The Berserkers are only ones that got some love - both quest-related achievements come from the Fort, you get some immersion, you get every Berserker NPC commenting on you making Paladin. Even if that community is silly and comical and has its share of flaws - it is the most developed one. Other factions were not so lucky. Albs are sad. Outlaws and Clerics are an afterthought.Story is half-baked. Feels like it was only written up to Act II, it's a dumpster fire from that point onwards.Companions are half-baked. I see some effort made in companions random banter - reacting to the world, to quests, to your decisions and even to each other; yet at the same time I see dozens of copy/paste quests "Scout Ignadon 65535" which are sad and generic filler content.Same could be said for largely everything else. The game is ambitious, it has a soul, but the execution is very shallow.Dear PB, please understand the following:- we don't need 10 different ranged weapon classes, if there's no difference, nuance or balance to them and we'll end up using shotguns for the whole game anyway- we don't need 3 romance options if their models are ugly as sin and their characters are shallow and binary (like every creative choice/dislike every destructive one)- we don't need a dozen companions if their content is soulless copy/paste- we don't need 5 factions if they fail to provide us with unique experience, gameplay and immersion- we don't need a base if it's only good as a static decoration and gives us no way to build, design, manage and customize it- we don't need a huge open world if it's dead, static and boring

_childDocuments_.review: I could play this game forever and ever and ever. The world is so expansive, with so many unique places to visit, characters to interrogate, and things to do. I've been in love with Piranha Bytes' games since Gothic I, and I hope they stick to the successful formula of RPG that they've developed. It works beautifully, and I have yet to be disappointed by a single one of their games. Though I can't lie. The jetpack has spoiled me. Games without it now seem lackluster in comparison. And I LOVE how in Elex II, we now have the option of upgrading our jetpacks. That was a brilliant addition!But what truly separates Elex II from every other RPG is the immersive atmosphere. I can't tell you how often I'm running through a city or whatever and suddenly NPCs start having a unique conversation related to whatever else's been going on in the game. Like the kids, for instance, who are trying to solve a puzzle. Every now and again, I'll run into them huddled up somewhere talking about their latest findings. That sort of immersion makes the game come alive.Here's the catch: The game isn't for those who need their hand held. Like you got really figure things out and grind like crazy to get anywhere. But once you're strong enough to take on Crazy Craig, you feel sooooo good because you earned it through all the hard work.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I'm gonna make this review mostly about ONE particular sidequest because it is that good. I'll do a tl;dr at the end about the rest of the game so let's go.When I got access to The Fort after doing a couple too many fetch quests so that bald bastard of a guard lets me in, I stumbled upon a merchant Morkon in Berserker territory named Ivan. After talking to him, it's easy to notice he isn't like most Morkons I've encountered before -- he's too nice, too polite and doesn't want any trouble but for being a Morkon he is treated like crap by everyone else, within reason mind you given the Morkon's reputation isn't the best in the world of ELEX 2 but Ivan just wants to help with whatever he can, and he supplies the gas masks necessary for the miner's quest I got early from Scrappy.So, why is this guy the main reason of this review? Because his questline is easily on the top 3 of my all-time favourite quests I've EVER done in any videogame ever and I'll explain why.Ivan needs his rations from Chloe, the bar owner in the Fort region, who is currently dealing with some problems of her own so she is in a dire, dire mood. After resolving her issues and getting access to the Upper District, she can get Ivan's rations from an eccentric dude who lives up there. See, Ivan couldn't do anything to get his rations because nobody gave two craps about whether he lived or died just for being a Morkon in an unwanted territory, as his first quest is aptly named "An Unwelcome Morkon". With that done, he is beyond excited he can finally go back home to the Grotto to see his family and here's where I started to get very attached to this character's story.If you're like me and prefer exploring before doing main missions, just wandering around visiting places and talking to every character you find, you will probably find an entrance guarded by two mechanic beasts -- this is the Morkon's place, the Grotto, an old subway station turned into a hub for this particular faction.The Morkons are ruthless, they have their own religion worshipping Raavac (dudes worshipping a battery lmao Rayovac) and there are some 'heretics' who have their own sub-faction who follow Kriiton, a name that most Morkons fear mentioning because the consequences involve torture and more of that good stuff; I won't get too much into their lore because that's a completely different quest to get but basically, followers of Raavac like destruction and followers of Kriiton do not, and Ivan is a guy who talks briefly about the cult of Raavac and even says something along the lines of "If you stand by what's right, the right ones will find you, or you will find them" referencing Kriiton followers who want this unrestrained carnage to stop.Inside of the Grotto, I found PINGAS-- I mean, TENGIS, some self-indulgent prick who wants to know Ivan's whereabouts, and demands that he comes back but here's the thing, Ivan is a merchant, and he has traded with other factions which is strictly forbidden by the law of the Morkons and Tengis knows that, he just wants Ivan to come back so he can have a reason to kill him.When I told Ivan back in the Fort that PINGAS wants him back, he sounded a bit jittery but he packs up and asks me if I want to accompany him to the Grotto. You can choose here and say no and that's that but I said yes, I want to go with Ivan and we begin this little 'escort' mission this game loves throwing at us.Ivan talks about his life, about his old partner Danilo, another Morkan who came with Ivan to... well, not trade. They were sent to pillage and murder people but in one of their misadventures, Danilo got killed which made Ivan rethink his life. He just... isn't made for this. Yes, he killed people before because Morkons don't mourn people, they think death is some kind of privilege and they need to earn their deaths to reach Eternal Oblivion (Tibia reference!) and Ivan attempts to recruit me but, personally, I'm not interested in joining any factions so we keep going. We stopped at a place to rest; Ivan asks me to kill some biters and get their meat so we can cook a meal, then he tells me to get some rest and that he will stay up instead. Here I was sure something bad was gonna happen -- is this happy-go-lucky guy is gonna steal my stuff? Is he gonna try to kill me? Well... nope, when I woke up, Ivan is there by the campfire, excited we are ready to continue the journey to the Grotto.This guy... man, he's such a sweetheart and I am going to protect him with everything I can. We keep walking, he makes jokes, tries to figure out where Jax, the protagonist, is from and such -- all in good fun, until we find some Poachers from the Grotto and Ivan is terrified of them. They haven't seen Ivan in a long time and there's severe punishment for not returning so when they're approached, they seem surprised Ivan is still alive and they ask about Danilo. Ivan explains everything and there we have the option to vouch for him or not, and I vouched for him. They treat Ivan like a vermin but I decided to not get involved, I don't want to complicate things for him, especially now that we are so close to the Grotto. No physicality necessary, just keep going.Ivan talks about how ecstatic he is to see his family again and we finally get to the Grotto, he bids me farewell and hopes to see me again. I go straight to PINGAS to tell him Ivan is here, but this ♥♥♥♥ guy doesn't care, he wants Ivan murdered for 'betraying' the Morkons. At this time I panicked, "NO, I WILL NOT LET IVAN DIE". I ran (jetpacked at full speed inside of the subway station) to Ivan's location, found him and his wife Marika and told him what happened. Ivan was mortified, he begged me to tell PINGAS he fled, escaped somehow and so I did, I ran back to that twit and protected Ivan. PINGAS wasn't happy, blamed on the Poachers but whatever, fk this guy.At this point his questline was over and guess what? Ivan was safe, his wife as well and to my surprise they were back in The Fort so I fast-traveled there to check in on him and here's where my heartstrings were pulled -- Ivan was safe, there's an epilogue to his quest. He asks his DAUGHTER, Tamara to see me but she is scared; she was kept hidden her entire life because the Morkons couldn't find out he had kids. It'll take time for her to adapt to the outside world. Ivan even said "Tamara, please, he's a friend" YES I AM YOUR FRIEND IVAN!!!Marika, his wife, is so happy to see me and beyond thankful I helped them escape. She also had no idea there was a world so big outside the Grotto and wished she got out earlier in her life with her parents.Ivan said everyone is treating him better, it helped he showed up with his family at the gate and even Chloe seems like a different person, doing everything she can to help Ivan stay afloat.This... this side mission in this janky game made me so emotional. A side character whose fate doesn't mean anything to the main plot made me feel things I yearn to feel again. To whoever wrote Ivan's story, if you read this somehow-- thank you, thank you for making such a wonderful character and giving him an actual happy ending because it's stuff like this that makes me happy. ELEX 2 is not a particularly good game but the writing for a couple characters is simply incredible. I love you, Ivan, and I will never forget our adventures together, my friend.Other than Ivan's quest, ELEX 2 is a 6.5/10 game in my opinion. Janky controls, awful combat, terrible story pacing, wonky animations but a vast world to explore, funny easter eggs and many, many quests with interesting characters to talk to and know more about. The upgrades for the jetpack are a must to reduce the slog to the minimum but it's a drag to get there.I only recommend this game because there's a lot of love poured into the writing of minor characters that make the RPG experience all worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Review was previously positive. After spending more time with the game and browsing through the discussions a bit I found this post which stuck with me and eventually convinced me that despite the fun that I am having , the overall title is not to be recommended currently. Not so much because of what the game is and whether you can draw enjoyment from that, but because of how the developer and the series developed.From JeffJ"As a longtime PB fan all the way back from Gothic 1, I have noticed certain trends in their more recent titles.Overall, they seem to have put more focus on stuff like:- Cutscenes, even ones that trigger while exploring and will reposition your player- Immortal NPCs alá Elder Scrolls- Invisible walls- More dumbed down stats / skills systems (for example, attributes do nothing in Elex, only unlock skills, and it's literally impossible to see actual HP numbers, etc.)- More 'accessible' quest design, meaning, waypoint markers. But the inclusion of these also affects writing, since the devs no longer need to make the game the game playable without them through actual dialogue explanations (as in old Gothic for example)All the above are, in my opinion, stark contrasts to their design philosophies of old, which to me always seemed to put strong emphasis on freedom, exploration and immersion. The three main pillars which made me fall in love with their games in the first place, because they offered it to a degree no other developer did. That's what made me live with all the jank.Now, it seems they are trying to move more into some sort of Bethesda / CDPR territory - it seems they believe if they streamline everything enough, dumb down things a tad more, put more emphasis on cutscenes, polish and production (even at the cost of elements that made their fans love them in the first place), they too can make the next actual mainstream success in the veins of Elder Scrolls or Witcher 3. I may be wrong, but that is very much the vibe I have been getting for a while now.Now the real question is - is it actually working? We all know that PB have some very loyal fans, which is one of the reasons they have been able to get away with making the same game for more than 20 years now. We seem to be at a cross-roads here, where they are alienating more and more of their old fans (myself included), but maybe the numbers we don't have access to actually shows them that it's worth it - or maybe, in trying to please the masses (and failing) they will end up with neither mainstream nor old school PB fans. I guess time will tell."

_childDocuments_.review: Elex II revisits the post-apocalyptic, sci-fi fantasy world with vast ambition, but it doesn't always meet the standards set by modern RPGs. While there’s much to appreciate for longtime fans, several aspects hold it back from being a must-play title.Elex II offers a diverse landscape blending nature with futuristic and decaying structures. Each region feels distinct, from lush forests to industrial ruins. The gameplay aims for freedom but feels inconsistent. Combat, especially melee, suffers from sluggish controls and a clunky targeting system. Ranged combat fares slightly better.  However, difficulty spikes can be punishing early on, creating a steep learning curve.One of Elex II's strongest aspects is its open-world design. Exploration is rewarding, with hidden areas, factions to discover, and loot to collect. The world feels alive with faction-based politics affecting gameplay. The narrative builds on the original, offering a world where choices matter. Jax's journey is shaped by player decisions, impacting relationships with factions and characters.  While the overarching story has depth, the writing doesn't always deliver the necessary emotional weight.Elex II is a mixed bag. It delivers a vast, immersive world that rewards exploration and offers player agency through its faction system. Yet, its dated mechanics, uneven combat, and lackluster presentation make it challenging to recommend broadly.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has, like previous PB games, a lot of potential thanks to a large open world and lots of cool high-level features. But it's the basic details that aren't fleshed out well enough. Things like the animation-driven character movement that makes it hard to walk on narrow surfaces (which you do a lot due to the vertical gameplay), the user interface (the inventory is one big list that you need to scroll through - and that doesn't even work smoothly), animation bugs (enemies teleport into your face while they should be stun-locked) and so on. Unfortunately it's these basic elements that you're interacting with permanently throughout the entire game - and if those are annoying, you're annoyed during the whole experience. That's what killed the game for me.I think they should've maybe done a bit of a smaller map, maybe one less faction, a few less items, maybe drop some of the IMO not-so-great lore told through notes and audio logs... and instead put some more resources into developing the key gameplay elements.On top of that, the animations, dialogues, character design, story telling etc. is pretty mediocre at best, but honestly that doesn't bother me much. It's the previous points that bother me.I wish they'd move away from trying to make a hollywood-movie-like experience with emotional story-telling and huge worlds and so on, and instead really concentrate more on fun gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this a thumbs up solely because of the hours I put into it. How bad could it be when that's considered? But it was close to going the other way based on the really poor second half of the game. I loved Elex 1. It was the first PB game since Gothic that actually felt COMPARABLE to Gothic. I called it a "flawed masterpiece." So I had great hopes for this game, fully expecting the "jank" and other traditional PB issues. Oh, we definitely got those in Elex 2, but ... they seem less "endearing" now than they used to. The combat especially ... I mean, if this game had simply GOOD combat, it would be SO much better and more satisfying. It just doesn't. The combat is just bad, particularly the melee side of things. Enemies often just literally stand still waiting for you to pummel them. The shields, something I always enjoy in games like this, are basically useless. The sounds and the FEEL of connecting your blade with an enemy are just crap and wholly unsatisfying. This may have passed the test 15 years ago, but today? There's just no excuse for combat this bad. Even from PB, who has notoriously been subpar in this area (although I loved the combat of the first Gothic games. But that was early 2000s, so ...). The audio is another issue. The sound design is just HORRIBLE. The jet pack sound, the sound when you land hard after a long fall, the sound of a sword fight ... it's just totally offputting and craptacular. The voice acting is actually good, and it's cool that they have the same voice for the nameless hero of Gothic 3 back for this one, but the dialogue itself is at times completely nonsensical and incomprehensible. It often comes across as if it's been translated from Japanese, and there are times when you're just scratching your head as to what you just heard in a conversation. The "Destruction" system or whatever it is is absolutely unnecessary, useless and illogical. I could never get a sense as to what would make an ally "angry" at me or what wouldn't. There was one NPC, Bully, who I hated. I was hoping like hell I'd get the chance to kill him later in the game, so I went along with his quests, but my interactions with him ended up making him "hate" me. What I didn't realize is that, at some point, he hated me so much that he basically told me to ♥♥♥♥ off and left the game, disabling the rest of his quests. I never saw him again. I mean, you could say that's kind of cool for a game to do, and I may agree, but it was just the path of illogic that led to that point that annoyed me. Also, he did it after telling me about another quest, leading me there, getting no negative comments from me  and then, just as the quest was about to begin, deciding that he "hated" me. THis is another thing that bothers me about the game. There are so many NPCs I wanted to kill, but anyone with a name could only be "stunned," unlike other PB games from the past. Made things very unsatisfying. As far as the story ... I don't know what to make of it, to be honest. On one hand, I have to admire its complexity. On the other, I had no idea what was happening a majority of the time. Clearly a ton of effort went into this, and PB is always good at juggling multiple story lines, but ... the story itself was just really hard to follow. Jax is a total douche as well. He looks like a douche. He acts like a douche. He's a horrible father, lol. What's his biggest power? "Willpower." LOL. Yes, that's what it turns out is his biggest asset, his "willpower." Again, that's just an example of how weird this story is and how strange some of the dialogue is. Maybe it's a translation issue, but it's just laughable. So how could I possibly give this a thumbs up after all that? I'm wondering that myself. But I will say, there's just something about these PB games that draws me in. Someone called it their "zen," and that's how I feel about these games at times, too. The exploration is addictive, there are a lot of weapons options (very few armor options this time, though, which sucks), and it IS very satisfying (for awhile) to load up on loot and upgrade your character little by little until he can crush most anything. About halfway through the game, I was really loving it, much like I loved Elex 1. But when it got into the later chapters, where you just had to kill a certain number of aliens on every mission, it really fell apart. Combat is the weakest link in this game, so to suddenly have to rely on that constantly made it very boring. Especially since, at that point, I could rain fire storms from the sky that could kill enemies in one or two hits, even the most powerful ones. That was fun the first few times I did it. After the 20th, not so much. But there were some interesting back stories with some of the NPCs that were fun to uncover, there was a lot of variation in the creature design, some fun puzzles, interesting (at times) secret weapons to discover, etc. It felt like old-school Gothic early on, and that kept me playing. But really, the game was just way too long. It wore out its welcome. I generally love PB, but they simply HAVE to do something about their outdated, broken combat system for the next game. Change up all the audio design, too. There is so much potential here in these games, but it was ultimately squandered here in Elex 2. If you loved the first one, make up your own mind. It's worth it for that. But I was ultimately disappointed. And as I finish the is review, I have decided to change my vote. Yes, it has to be a thumbs down. Sorry, PB, but it's time for some tough love. Do better.
