_childDocuments_.review: I can only recommend this game to people who were already really satisfied with the first game. Whoever thought after the first game "this game has a couple of positive aspects, but also a couple of negative. I hope they really improve this game by the second installment", will be disappointed.Elex II is still as janky as Elex I. PB added new mechanics, which is great, but the base systems are still as janky as they were in the first game. This applies to NPC-behavior as well as to the combat. While the NPC-jank can be annoying and immersion-breaking, the combat-jank is unbearable if you seek a satisfying combat-experience. Enemies bug out on a regular basis, wander off, attack in front of them even if you're not standing in front of them, and their attacks are still poorly animated and boring. Jax still feels floaty, the hits still lack impact, and the combat-sounds are still outright bad. It's great that PB added additional combat-mechanics, but they only improve the combat-experience slightly, because the core combat is still as lacking as in Elex I.If you mainly like Elex for it's world, and simply want to check out a new map and enjoy the quests, the game is good enough. But if you expect your game to have good, solid mechanics to be able to enjoy it, i can't recommend Elex II to you. I played Elex I, and although it was ruff in many aspects, the setting and world was interesting enough to carry me trough the game and make the game enjoyable. The novelty of the setting and the world is now worn off by the second installment, and what is left is simply not good enough to warrant the time and money in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: One of these Open World gems you are striving for, for real. I really enjoyed it so far.I recommend to play the first game, if you want to get the whole story package, it's worth it. And ELEX II is a great update to the first one regarding to many of its core mechanics.-------------PROS:- PB know their audience - an uncomplicated but nice story which doesn't distract too much from the good ol' exploration experience when roaming through Magalan with all its nice spots and easter eggs :D- the new jetpack mechanics are pretty enjoyable- the fighting system has been improved- the soundtrack is as nice as always (congrats to Björn and I love the Cassandra album!)- the graphics are really okay for a 2022 game- pretty immersive atmosphere as you know it from PB - I like the feeling of the endgame, pretty nailed it in my opinion.- very few issues (some clipping enemies in a midgame quest) and bugs, the devs have polished it quite good, I think.-------------CONS:- the companions lining up before you, because each one has a new quest to impose onto you, can be a bit overwhelming at some point and disrupt the immersion but that can be me...- a pain point for me is the poor Skyand loot. The weapons are quite weak compared to others (except the Sphere Splitter) considering that these are the great baddy weaponry. A bit strange in my opinion.- some relations between the factions are a bit confusing. Wasn't sure at first if I really can keep the Alb powers if I decide to switch to the Clerics. Fortunately it worked out well :D- using Dawkins as the mentor early on is a pretty nice idea and constructs an interesting link to the first game but because of his relation to Jax (and well...the rest of the world), it feels a bit strange as a story decision to start with. It's not inherently bad, just a bit...strange. You get Jax's skepticism about it but basically you pretty much do at Dawkins's bidding. But that can be a personal taste thingy.------------RESULT: 9/10If you know and love the former PB games, you will know what you'll get but better. In my opinion the devs put much blood and sweat in this one and it shows. You get a vast, free world to explore and rich, "dense" content within it. The improved mechanics are great and there are just some few points to complain about.Pretty solid and enjoyable game so far with a nice story and a strong link to the narrative of the first part. Many familiar faces and also some new ones which generates a seamless transition in my opinion. Really looking forward to a possible continuation!

_childDocuments_.review: Elex 2 is a very fun third-person action RPG. There are many impactful choices your character can make in dozens of quests. Although the combat can feel low budget at times, the skill tree allows you to make your own character specialized in how you want to play the game. I won’t list plot-specific spoilers in my review, but I will give a brief synopsis of the plots of Elex and Elex 2. I won’t cover past the first hour of plot from either game in case you wanted to play the original game after reading my review.Elex 2 is a direct sequel to 2017’s Elex. You don’t have to play the original game to understand this game, but it would definitely be beneficial because the series has a lot of unique lore to understand and there are plenty of references and returning characters from the original game.If you choose to play the original Elex, note that this sequel will choose certain canon choices even though there are multiple choices to choose from in the original game. For example, even though there were multiple romance choices in the original game, this sequel already chooses who the protagonist had a kid with. The game’s protagonist is Jax, who was previously a commander of a faction named the Albs. Although he had great strides by the end of the original game, he left his old life behind and moved into a secluded hut.In the beginning of Elex 2, Jax’s home is invaded and he is attacked by aliens called the Skyands. Jax gets infected in the attack with Dark Elex and passes out. Adam saves Jax’s life and shows him an area called Bastion, which serves as the player hub. Throughout the game Jax needs to find allies for Bastion so that they are prepared to fight the Skyand invasion. I’m purposely keeping the synopsis simple and spoiler-free, but the game quickly turns into an amazing adventure. Right from the onset, there are five level of difficulties you can choose from, which can also be changed at any time. These difficulties include a story mode where you can enjoy the story without stressing about the gameplay. After going through the game, this title is not as hard to get into compared to the original Elex, and the developers have learned from their missteps.If you weren’t familiar with these kinds of action RPGs from Piranha Bytes, who developed the Risen and Gothic games, they can be challenging in the beginning, and many people can get frustrated and put off by these kinds of games very quickly. In Elex 2, however, the beginning of the game doesn’t have such a bad difficulty spike at all. Your central hub is called Bastion. You can recruit companions throughout the game and send them to Bastion to rest or you can take one with you. You can carry only one companion with you at a time and they will occasionally make a few comments when you visit a city.The playable world only has a few cities, which are essentially faction hubs where leaders and members of each faction congregate together. Each of the faction’s city hubs feels very distinct. For example, the Berserkers are in a hub called The Fort, which looks like a medieval castle with bridges all over.The Elex games are AA games. They’re not indie titles, but they’re also not AAA titles either. They have a budget that is on the lower end, but these games have a lot of charm in them. Just like the original Elex, this game plays “janky” as well.The conversations Jax has with NPCs is similar to that of The Witcher, Mass Effect, or Dragon Age. Jax will generally talk to the NPCs one-on-one, and you’ll be able to choose dialogue options. The game also doesn’t show Jax’s equipped helmet in the cutscenes and you can see his expressions without worrying about awkward looking equipment.If your attributes are high enough, you can even unlock unique conversation options. One event that happened to me was when Jax was mugged by highwaymen. Jax had the option to say, “Are you sure you want to try to rob me?” because his strength was high enough to intimidate his pursuers.The NPCs have a lot of dialogue, and a lot of them feel like actual characters with their own personalities and stories. The amount of quests can feel overwhelming at times, but the developers are masters at their craft. All of the quests had branching options because of the choices you can do. You can almost always choose to help cover for someone or betray them, for example, and your end result will differ depending on your choice. The optional quests are never generic at all, there was only a few of the generic “kill 3 monsters” kind of side-quests out of the hundreds of quests present in this game.The jetpack is a unique mechanic that I don’t see in video games except for maybe Dark Void. You have a jetpack that automatically recharges fuel that can be used anytime. It starts off by letting you fly for roughly 5-10 seconds but can be permanently upgraded to last longer. The game will keep pushing you to join a faction as early as possible, but you don’t have to do it early in the game if you don’t want to. You need to join a faction by the end of chapter 3, otherwise you will be locked out of them. This is more than enough time because chapter 4 consists of mostly endgame missions.The five factions include the Berserkers, Albs, Morkons, Outlaws, and Clerics. Each of these factions have their own different beliefs and civilizations. The Berserkers, for example, prioritize magic and don’t use technology. The Clerics, on the other hand, prefer using technology and use technological weapons in combat. The Morkons focus on melee and believe getting riches from combat (they are like something out of a Mad Max movie). The Outlaws craft chemical drugs to become stronger. The Albs use Elex to become tougher (at the cost of their emotions) and also use technological weapons. All of these factions are at odds with each other and from the premise of the game it looks like there are tensions between them.The game has a morality system called “Destruction”. If you make peaceful or respectful choices your Destruction goes down, but if you make violent or rude decisions your Destruction goes up. It’s important because you can only choose certain factions if your Destruction meets their requirements; for example, joining the Morkons requires a high Destruction. The dialogue is also done well because if you did a questline in a different order, the NPCs will actually acknowledge it. To avoid blackouts, you need to do mental training by talking to one of your companions in Bastion. The thing is, you can’t really do the mental training in advance, you can only do it when Jax feels the onset of a blackout. It’s tricky, I would’ve preferred if they kept Jax being infected as a narrative element, but removed the gameplay element of him being infected and suffering from blackouts. The final 5 or so hours of the game has a lot of amazing twists and the lore as well as all the mysteries get explained and wrapped up succinctly. If you do buy this game and are getting bored, it’s definitely worth it to keep going through it because there’s a big pay-off in the end and the final battles are epic.For the most part, the voice acting is performed well. The main characters and important NPCs do an amazing job. Elex 2 really has a lot of passion put into it. I’ve spent hours just listening to all of the characters and their dialogue. The game is more polished than the original Elex, but this game still does have a few missteps. There’s a lot of small glitches such as characters running into the character you’re talking to. It really isn’t too hard to get into Elex 2 and it really has a beautiful world with many biomes, rich lore, interesting NPCs, and a very engaging story. This is a game that’s easy to get hooked on once you understand its mechanics and I cannot recommend it enough. Just be aware that you do need to overlook some of its shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: Elex 2... Sweet mother of mercy where do I even begin with this mess of a game? This game wants to be so many things and do so many things on such a tiny limited budget but winds up doing a lousy job at anything it attempts. I guess the best way to describe Piranha Bytes studio's vision would be that they have champaign taste and ambitions while working with a Kool-Aid budget. Elex 2 deceives players into the perpetual mind state of "If I just play it a little longer it will get better!" And sadly it doesn't...You never really get stronger in this game and only "less weak". This game can be best described as 3rd person shooter deceptively masquerading around as an RPG game. So let's get into it and breakdown this game's laundry list of issues.Problem #1: UI (User Interface)Wow and I mean wow it is an ugly, clunky and unorganized mess. Normally I don't complain about such things in a game but this one stands out the most in just how awful it is. The inventory screen is just one giant list of items that cannot be sorted in any way possible. Now I know folk are going to immediately try to point out the quick item wheel option, but even that does not compensate for the avalanche of items you have to swim through to find the things you need. And to top off all of that, the game has the nerve to make digging through you inventory a real time event (Yes game world does not pause when you're digging through your items! A flaw which I blame the souls-game for that enraging design mechanic) Wasn't cute when it was first introduced and it's not cute now...Problem #2:Graphics and TexturesThe graphics in this are a 50/50 hit or miss. Some are just very well made and a delight to look at while others look like straight up Playstation 2 game assets. It's like a weird fusion mix between the two all the time. The world is beautiful to look at and fairly large and yet...fairly empty and boring to be honest.Problem #3:AnimationsThe animations in this game are ultra janky and super clunky. It's like they're using the exact same animations from their previous game series Gothic and Risen and HAVE YET to improve upon them. The janky animations in this game are what make melee combat in this game EXTREMELY punishing and unfun. Charge ups for heavy melee attacks are horribly slow, can be seen coming a mile away all while having a questionably small attack range. While on the subject of animations, the NPCs you interact with are terrifying to look at. Apparently nobody in this game has eyelids or facial expressions. I dunno maybe blinking is just something people don't care about in this universe. Because of that everyone you talk to has this disturbing uncanny valley look to them mixed in with the Vietnam veteran 1000 yard stare like they've seen some things...Problem #4The Writing and DialogueWow....ummm...It's...f**king terrible... Who in the world talks like these folk constantly? It's like they got an emo, an edgelord and an angsty teenager in a room together to brainstorm ideas and write this dialogue. 90% of all NPCs in this game swear worse than sailors and machine gun curse words at you every 4 seconds. Holy Christ we get it life is tough on this world of theirs but do they have to sound angry every second of their existence?!? Let me show an example of how 90% of your dialogues with just regular NPCs will go down.Main Character: Excuse me Sir or Madame can you please give me directions to the market place in this area?NPC: Go f**k your mother! What kind of loser a**hole doesn't know where the market place is? What do I look like a f**king tour guide?!?And I'm sitting here reading this edgy dialogue thinking: DAMN DUDE I'M NEW TO THIS S**T TOWN OF YOURS SO CLEARLY I'M A STRANGER! I HAVEN'T EVEN TAKEN 2 STEPS INTO THIS RAGGEDY MF AND YOU'RE ARGUING WITH ME ALREADY!?! CHILL THE F**K OUT! Problem #5FactionsThere is not a single likable faction in this game. Technically you don't have to join a faction but the game is way more difficult and stressful than it already is if you don't join one. So it's kind of a lose/lose scenario there. There are 5 factions in all and they are all terrible in some variation.Faction 1: The Morkons-A bunch of violent religious fanatics who worship a God who loves violence and destruction. Some fanatics even commit suicide to show devotion to this God they worship. This makes absolutely no sense in the overall plot of the game which is to save the world. Which is pretty ironic because the Morkons tell you if they become the dominant faction in the land, first order of business is to murder and genocide all non-believers and non Morkons. Kinda goes against the whole "save the world" plot they want you to follow.Faction 2: The Albs-The Albs is your old tribe from Elex 1 they have no emotions but since you beat the big baddie from the first game, they've considered reintroducing emotions back into society seeing how they helped you realize somethings about the world. Efficiency is either rewarded or punished accordingly and is all that matters in their society which kinda makes them act and speak like Terminators.Faction 3: The Outlaws-See problem #4Faction 4: The Berserkers-See problem #4 Faction 5: The ClericsThis faction curses at you the least but are still pretty bad because they're also passive aggressive, judgmental, self righteous and down right delusional. Their whole religion is based on a lie but no one has yet to tell their followers their "God" is an old broken down rocket ship which is kinda funny...Problem #6CompanionsPiranha Bytes is really REALLY confused about what a companion is because some of your so-called "companions" tell you straight off the bat to your characters face they don't like him, they hate him, they're using him or at the first opportunity they get, they'll try to screw over your character. I'm thinking to myself: This group of idiots, psychos and jacka**es are gonna help me save the planet? Not feeling very confident about this lineup. And also their AI is beyond brain dead I've had multiple instances of companions getting meleed by enemies and doing nothing for several strikes or I'll engage an enemy and my companions are too slow to keep up with the action missing lots of melee swings and gunfire shots.  Problem #7Fun Factor and Game PaceIt's not fun because they level lock all the "fun gear and skills" behind ridiculous stat requirements before anything entertaining pops up. The perks in this game feel redundant because some of the basic skills should just come natural to your character. So for the first 8-10 hours into the game, you'll be rocking starter gear or gear just ever so slightly better than the starter gear. Which also means 95% of the enemies on the world map can flat out kill your character in no more than 3-5 hits which is terrible. The economy is this game is unreal everything is exorbitantly expensive. The only way you'll keep a steady flow of money in your pocket by leveling up the pick pocket skill and even then you don't get that skill for quite sometime. I'm still debating on whether or not I will finish this game especially since I heard the game ends on an intentional cliffhanger so they can make Elex 3 and I'm like Elex 2 was painful enough as it is. I might just scream and run in the opposite direction at the mention of a trailer for Elex 3 at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: What has happened with PB? They used to make games with beautiful, believable worlds in the past. The game has some improvements with some of its aspects, like the combat. I am playing in ultra-difficulty and as far as I can tell, when you understand how the combat works, I dare say it is quite enjoyable and fun. Also, the voice acting for the most characters, especially the protagonist is pretty decent. The exploration has a good pace most of the time but ultimately it is not worth it, because you have thousands of shards and nowhere to spend it, when you are done with gear and training and this is around mid-game. The story is not very interesting this time around and it doesn't make a lot of sense most of the time. But the biggest flaw is the world itself. It is bland and unbelievable. Truly. Sleeping in w/e bed you want, and don't give 2 ♥♥♥♥♥ for the owner, who needs the inn right? Stealing in towns and getting caught (even a freaking apple) leads to your instant death. The factions themselves are a shadow of their former self and not in a good believable way, totally in odds with the seriousness of the situation the world of Magalan is in. The NPCs are lifeless and dump. Many of them stay in one place without moving just to serve as a benchmark to continue the plot, or some quest. They don't have a schedule they don't sleep; they don't eat. They just stay in their freaking place patiently waiting for you to complete the quest. Even if an NPC moves and go to sleep, they don't seem to do anything else that makes sense. They end up as artificial and plastic and the immersion of the world suffer for it. Want to sell some items and it’s the middle of the night? Just wake up the vendor, he will complain “ah why did you wake me up” and sell you staff afterwards. Even Oblivion was WAY more immersive in some aspects, and we are talking about a game that was made 15 years ago. Pickpocket the guard’s weapon with 1 point in pickpocket? Yes, please. I mean common! Let’s be real here. I know it seems cool but it’s not.  Animals that hunt for their food? Nop. They just wander around patiently waiting to fulfill their role, which is giving you some xp and materials to sell. I really don't know how else to describe it, I am certain fans of PB, like me, who have played previous games have already observed these things and many more. They seem like minor details but believe you me, they are not and they add up to a level that they are pretty obnoxious and immersion breakers. Yeah, the world is fake and there is zero chance you'll be immersed in it. A pity. Don't get me started with the companion's bombardment of very tedious go and kill this and that quests. Yeah, it seems PB tried a new formula with the game, which is not a bad thing most of the times, but failed. The strongest aspect of PB's games in the past was a hand-craft believable world, that begs to be explored and I think that that they missed every mark here. if you are a fan of the series, you will find some hours of enjoyment, but I cannot recommend the game to anyone else.

_childDocuments_.review: Piranha Bytes stays true to its ELEX 1 roots, as an INDEPENDENT-MINDED, CHOICES MATTER developer, deep-diving into an evolved RPG faction psychology in ELEX 2. After twenty hours in I still haven't met two of the factions, by choice. To me this is more of an old-school super OPEN-WORLD RPG with a dino. medieval, sci-fi twist formula that WORKS! The beautiful environment, ambient music & multi-level quests chock-full of twists & turns, or unbelievably short and fun quests, where "all is not as it appears", is adventurous & fun.Not your typical triple AAA wave after wave of short-term memory shoot-em-up's with weapon-skin paywalls & withheld DLC content. Here, you'll have a healthy respect for some enemies, unless you can either use the environment or corral up a few followers, who will "sometimes" opt-out of defending you in certain circumstances/challenges. Many quests are so well done, they last for hours, taking you on a Disneyland like tour of certain factions, where NPC's will act appropriately or disproportionately to your choices, which is called being CORRECTLY NON-LINEAR!One glaring problem, as others have pointed out, after hours of game-play, the camera (player movement) becomes either sluggish or hard to control (GTX 1050). Restarting helps but it comes back. Great upgrade from EXEX 1, with trainer-finder locator, as searching for them in ELEX 1 tested my sanity. EXEX 2 says replay-ability & enjoy being  elexit broke, but happy. FUN! :) Thank You for your hard work Piranha Bytes. Bravo!!!

_childDocuments_.review: So, I just sank 50 hours into it and I am delighted.After the first, this one elaborates the story, adds in twist that are not foreseeable (or I did not :D), the characters are great (new faces as well as old ones, nice!). I love have believable the world developed in the years since Elex 1. Revisiting some of the old place, seeing how they have changed, then exploring the vast new areas was amazing!Yes, a few bugs exist still two motnhs after release (I encountered like 2 mobs and a few corpses that did not despawn, but who cares, given the world size and the fact that running away is a core mechanic eitherways), but these bugs are really minor, nothing crashing or breaking or undoable and Elex is great fun. I have a 3 y.o. mid-performance gaming laptop and perfomance was very smooth (even during large battles which it actually has) and the loading times were really brief, given I installed it on a HDD. Go ahead and play it :)

_childDocuments_.review: worst release window in the history of publishers (Elden Ring)even i, as someone who realy liked Elex 1, waited quite a while to finaly play the sequel.but i'm glad i did (buy it that is)yes, it's Elex 2, literaly. most thinks feel the same and work the same.yet, Elex 2 is very pleasant to play. it's hard to describe. the combat hasn't gotten much better (aka euro-jank). it's servicable, but (especialy melee) far from "good". the engine looks pretty with it's own style, but is nothing to write home about. the soundtrack and effects are good.the voice over (english) is pretty good...and there's a lot of dialogue (and it's all fully voiced).but still: it's just very pleasant to play (fun). maybe it's the organic feeling open world design, which feels as far away from an Ubisoft-checkbox-design as possible. maybe it's the fun of seeing what happened after the first game and how the world and it's characters evolved (although it's a pitty they went with just one of the possible routes you could take in the first game; for budget reasons probably).conversations, ingame cutscenes, the general flow are pretty unique; it's just great to play a game where you can be a total a-hole, a do-gooder or anything in between and it all kinda plays out without feeling lesser in any path. when the game tells you: create your own story (which is kinda a buzz-term), it actualy kinda works like that.but don't get me wrong: there's still a lot of euro-jank at every (3rd) corner. the start is pretty rough, the first game had a far better intro into the gameplay and world;about the only real complaint i got is Jax himself. i liked (for story reasons) his very unique acting in the first game, and while i still think he's a good protagonist, some of his uniqueness just isn't here anymore (for story reasons again).if you want to play a kinda kickback and relax open world game, in a living breathing world, where you might encounter a trader-caravan bumping into some critters, or scavangers attacking some monster (to their very own demise); explore a content (so many quests, unique areas, stuff to find and learn) rich world, where npcs actualy walk from A to B and get into bed at night; where you can chose to steal whatever you want, kill pretty much most things or try to play the moral route (which is often quite hard) you should definitly buy Elex 2 (well both games tbh.).the start is rough as it is, but it gets better quick.

_childDocuments_.review: Elex II is everything I had hoped for from a sequel: more Jax, more factions to explore, bigger world, more ♥♥♥♥♥♥ people to interact with, more weapons, more moral choices, enemies that don't level with me, and more jetpack-aided exploration.No, combat doesn't feel as difficult as previous PB games I've played but frankly that's a plus in my book.The only thing I am not enjoying is the game's technical state - it's very much in need of some post-release polish, and thankfully it appears the devs are hard at work to make that happen. While the first patch addressed some issues, there's still a lot more work to be done.I am especially looking forward to a fix for the godawful camera system that zooms in on Jax when he stops moving. And why is he off-centre?? Did QA miss this altogether, or did the devs just ignore them when they raised it? General performance also needs some serious attention, because really, no game that looks like it was made 5 years ago should run this badly.Technical gripes aside, I am happy I bought the game at release. Elex was a pleasant surprise for me, and II offers more of the same (and some) so it's been money well-spent.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so this review will be a bit tough to write, as in general I -did- enjoy the first half or so of the game. Like almost everyone that reviewed the game, I've played all the Piranha Bytes games since the legendary Gothic 1 and I've enjoyed aspects of all of them.The good stuff:Elex 2... huh. Well, the first and second chapter of the game had decent writing, nothing amazing. The companions were enjoyable enough. Combat felt nicer than the first game. I played primarily with strength, dexterity and constitution so I could experience most of the weapon types. Melee fighting was really nice, weapons (especially 2Handed) had weight to them and stunning trolls with a big hammer never got old. Ranged weapons felt a bit lackluster, very static. I didn't try energy weapons at all, so maybe there's something there but I doubt it.The world itself was very nice to return to. The addition of Tomstown was amazing and it's definitely my favourite zone of the game to explore. I did miss the desert of Tavar and I felt that the game could use with some more biome variation here and there, though it wasn't terrible. Guess lore reasons were the primary factor considering the berserkers are spreading their mana juice all over the place.Factions were a mixed bag. Mostly good, but the bad stuff stuck out. I like that the berserkers actually look like they belong in a post apocalyptic setting rather than sticking out artistically like a sore thumb. The addition of Albs is cool and the 2 minor factions, Clerics and Outlaws, was a nice addition. I am not going to write about the Morkons for now. All in all, it's a Piranha Bytes game. It shines with exploration and finding cool stuff here and there, with some really enjoyable quests dotted around the map.Voice acting in German, English and Polish was nice. Bit flat in some areas, but that's okay. I think the protagonist sounding flat is perfectly reasonable, considering his past.The bad stuff:The writing in the second part of the game was so bad. Like the worst I've ever seen. The buildup was really cool, but once the "kill X amount of enemies standing around" popped up, I noticed how lazy the later chapters were. I cannot state enough how bad the writing is later on. Clearly emotional moments were met with eye-rolls, the "BIG REVEAL" at the end was met with a sigh - if you experienced the ending of Elex 1, you'll be met with the same thing here - only done much, much worse. Caja doesn't even comment on something "sad" happening near the end (if you know you know).The Morkons are the worst faction Piranha has done. I just don't get who they're for. BDSM emos LARPing as Vampires. My god I HATE the Morkons.There were some very nice quests, but a lot of the later ones were so boring. ohno suddenly we need to kill X here! UHOH! Kill X that are invading etc etc... Technical difficulties litter the game. It crashed once, which is nice, but the real problems are with framerate drops to the point of having to download a mod from the Nexus to stabilize the game somewhat. If I need external help to fix a game, the game has a problem. Don't know if it was a localization error or whatever, but dialogue frequently felt off, like they used wrong lines occasionally which made some conversations feel so, so off. I'll add this to technical difficulties as I want to give Piranha Bytes the benefit of the doubt that they know how human conversations work.In conclusion, I dunno. 4.5/10. CRONY best companion, game was fun enough. Don't recommend at current price point and polish

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's a Piranha Bytes game, but it is not as good as Elex 1 or previous games. I still recommend it for the things it does well, but just barely. If you haven't played Elex 1, play that one instead.This game is a bit difficult to rate. As someone who played Piranha Bytes Games ever since Gothic 1, their old formula is still quite fascinating: You are a person most people don't recognize and don't really care about, you start off as a weak chump who gets killed easily by just about everything outside a town, and you live in a rough world full of people looking to screw you (and everyone else) over for their own benefit. Over the course of the game, you become much stronger, and enemies who were very deadly at first become cannonfodder while other characters are slowly starting to take you far more seriously. So far, so good. This formula was fun 20 years ago, and it still is.This time, however, the game has quite a few more issues than usual. This is remarkable, because Piranha Bytes games were always famous for being bug-ridden and janky. A new problem is that the writing isn't quite up to par with the usual quality. For some reason, a morality system is introduced that is quite black and white, which is new and completely out of place in these particular games. The "Destruction" meter basically decreases when you're nice, and increases when you're not. Additionally, two factions now require you to either have low or high destruction when you join them. One of these factions is a newly introduced literal death cult whose goal is the destruction of mankind, quite a difference to games where you could usually spend decades arguing which faction is morally correct - when one of the factions is a murder cult, and another faction tells you "You have to be nice to be allowed to join us" that argument becomes uninteresting, and the atmosphere suffers.Additionally, the quest design, especially in the late game, becomes lazy. In one of the main quests, you literally have to kill over 100 robots to advance, which starts feeling like artificially prolonging the "time needed to beat".The story isn't up to par either, especially if you choose some dialogues in the "wrong" order or go to a place at a time when you're not supposed to and everyone suddenly talks in complete non sequiturs or starts babbling.Finally, there is a new "infection" mechanic. Your character is infected at the very beginning of the game, and the infection causes him to start having "Blackouts" during the game, passing a day and teleporting you to a random spot near an enemy hideout. It's cute for the first time, the next twenty times get very annoying.So, if 80% of the review is thrashing the game, why am I giving it thumbs up? Because, despite all these flaws, the basic gameplay is still as fun as it ever was. Slowly growing out of your weakness in a hostile world with the help of your companions is still great. I was disappointed by this game, because it wasn't nearly as good as their previous games - but I still had fun with it (most of the time). If you haven't played Elex 1 though, play that instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Elex 1 and I was looking forward to the second part. I must admit, the first chapter felt like recycling of the story from Elex 1 and I found it a little bit boring. Now, after I finished the game, I can  say, that the real story began in the second chapter and the first chapter was a kind of introduction or prologue.The combat system has been significantly improved compared to the first part. It's fun, but it's not Assassin's creed combat mechanics with beautiful finishing moves: the combat system of Elex is simple.  Elex 1 had a strong auto-corrective camera that I found really awful. In Elex 2 the camera movements are smooth and work well. The spirit of discovering the world is also present in Elex 2. I really loved to find and loot things. The loot is often of no great value, you need time to develop and get stronger. You  are weak and can nothing at the beginning and have rather to avoid enemies than fight them. The developement is hard to get. The mobs don't drop armor or valuable rewards like in other RPG's , so  everythings you find feels of value.  The game flow is slow. I think  you must like this play style in order to enjoy this game. Like in Elex 1 you can mark only one quest at a time, This is part of the game concept  in order to encourage the discovering. The game is very story driven.  The genre is more science fiction than fantasy, so it's no Gothic. -Strong storytelling using cut scenes and deep dialogues. The quality of the story is great. Every quest is either  part of the main  story or a story for it  self. No grind quests. No "go and kill 10 mobs" quests. It's alway intersting.  I completed every main and side quest. -Beautiful grafics. Huge world. -I really loved the new jetpack. You can fight and move in a different way. -I liked the skill system: it's complex and challenging, you always have a goal and can choose what abilities you prefer. -I missed the adaptable quickslots already in Elex 1. I was rather dissapointed that in Elex 2 the quickslots were even removed from the UI. You only have 8 slots what is a pity as there is  a plenty of usable things in the game that you can't use because there is no quick slot for them  available.-I experienced light performance issues in form of lags towards the end game. I didn't annoy me that much that I couldn't continue. - The part with the joining and climbing up in the faction felt too short for me. I wished more quests. Elex 2 is a worthy follow-up of Elex. I really enjoyed playing it and felt pity when the story began to come to the end. Both parts of the game were an enriching game expirience and it's sad that Elex 3 has been canceled. I think this game has its strong sides and weaknesses. If you like sophisticated combat mechanics and fast playing style this game is maybe not for you. If you appriciate a good story with many dialogues and like to discover the open world then this game is great.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't recommend this game on several issues. I have been playing this game for 15 hours and I still seem to be in the starting chapter where the characters or story haven’t hook me in.  You get a virus but there seems to be no impending danger to have it, the game wants you to travel across the map before starting. Every side quest seems like a chore to get to a main quest to move pass the first chapter. I get that this is open world but a better direction in the quest line to have better pacing would have a better playthrough that just randomly hitting quest like Skyrim. The dialog is really basic characters seem bland, and it doesn’t help that the animation is on pair to a decade ago from oblivion standards. The faces barely register emotion to the context of the situation and the dialog is mostly delivered in a flat tone.The rendering of graphics seems rough to say the least, once you are past ten feet of the character but that can be fixed in a patch. Gameplay wise the biggest problem I have is with the combat from the level design. The level is design to be realistic with level having multiple altitude that the lock on doesn’t compensate well for. There are several times where either the monster or the character will miss due to the slightest elevation change. There also a bug where your character will climb on top of the monster while attacking.These seems it should be knock out from the development stage, given this is a third person perspective RPG. These things really matter to hook the player in to wanted to discover more, but all I keep asking why do I care about these characters none of them have made an impression that wants me to have the main character save them from world annihilation.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed Elex prior to Elex II, and I do recommend playing both in order.Elex II Pros:- Open world big time, though there are nudges along the main quest path- Story builds off first Elex well- Had no GPU heating problems; graphics smooth, quick and beautiful (with patches 1,2,3)- Combat is good - pew pew cleric is awesomeCons: - Listen, I'm retired military, and I've said and heard it ALL - but this game embarrassed me with all the gratuitous cussing.  Seriously, not necessary and actually made the horrendous NPC conversations worse.- Many NPC conversations were completely whackadoodle.  It's like the NPC's were in a different game.  I recommend for future endeavors the script developers and voice actors collaborate with capable conversationalist in the games' export language.- Not a lot of replay value unless you just want to try out aligning to a different factionOverall: I'm a long time RPG fan and this game scratches that itch.  I found myself enjoying it much more than being disappointed by it.  It's a good game with typical Piranha Bytes flaws.  If you're a fan of Risen and Gothic series you'll quickly overlook the typical Piranha Bytes querkiness and enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: When I started the game right after finishing Elex 1, I was disappointed. The world looked dull and lifeless and colourless compared to Elex 1. Jax looked at people's neck or their bust when talking (Jax's face during dialogue looks down.. Elex 1, Jax looked at people's face straight up). The Berserkers armour looked like a huge downgrade compared to Elex 1. The World Heart looked like a downgrade from Elex 1. Overall, visually Elex 2 was a downgrade IMHO compared to Elex 1. Even people mannerism looked odd, too much neck and head movement. Some characters' looked like zombies when talking due to their odd neck and head movement.5 hours into the game, I was still disappointed. I couldn't find any teachers, didn't know where to go and what to do (I know, typical PB game, but I felt like it was extreme in E2. E1, Duras takes you to Berserkers and you can spend enough time there. Again, I know, it is my mistake, but just saying). But once I went into the Fort and started taking quests, things became extremely good. The quest design is top notch and it is super engaging and simply one of the best I have played. I think until some good 20 to 25 hours, I didn't learn the JetPack skills. But the game improved 1000% once I learned the JetPack skills.But the best part is the story. The story was actually really very very good. I was curious what is going to happen and how things will fold. After Chapter 3 and 4, I know there is a lot of "go there and kill a million enemies" quests, but in between these crazy quests, there was a story developing. And end of Chapter 3 with "Willpower and Transformation", I was mind-blown. The story and how it all ties together was amazing. So, my recommendation is, play Elex 1 and then play this, but give both the games some time. It may start clueless and hard, but it would get EXPONENTIALLY BETTER.I am huge fan of PB, having played almost all of their games, and some games many many times. And I can say Elex is unique, different, but still has the PB soul intact. I highly recommend this game for any PB fans who are still sceptical and for people who haven't played any PB games too as a start.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings for Elex 2. Although there were some nice additions and new mechanics in this second part, I liked the first part more.GOOD: -The world looks nice, good graphics.-The crafting system of weapons is okay and keeps you interested in doing upgrades.-The money value and economics are okay (you never have too much money)-The new jetpack mechanics are nice.BAD: -The faces of the characters are retardedly ugly. Really, they are unacceptably ugly...-The combat (I enjoyed the combat in ELEX 1 much more). The melee combat is so slow and unresponsive, it is just a headache to use it. The ranged combat is too easy because you can hit very far targets without any additional training and the AI is terribly stupid when you range attack them - all you have to do is to keep going going back while shooting and they never hit you...-The loot is junk. The only interesting stuff to loot are the unique weapons. The chests do not contain interesting stuff, and it really isn't worth playing the unlocking mini-game just to find junk. This makes exploring not rewarding.-The quests are incredibly boring and uninteresting: go there and kill that or fetch some items.-The story is so uninteresting. By the end I stopped caring at all and it felt like a chore to finish it.I think PB are done. They've been redoing the same game over and over again, and they seem to be getting worse with every game.

_childDocuments_.review: *The DX12 beta update is fantastic, I get a 30 to 40% improvement in FPS. Very helpful in the faction areas! Keep up the good work PB!*More enjoyable PB rpg action with Elex 2, here are my super early thoughts 6 hours into the game. Basically most things are slightly improved from Elex, other than performance.Positives:- Improved melee combat- Graphics are ever so slightly improved (most faces other than kid, some of the textures,etc..)- Controls are slightly improved- The opening Cutscene wasn't to bad at all, a nice little surprise, starts you off pretty good - Once again an wonderful game world to explore, already finding tons of items hidden away off the beaten path- Jetpack is improved- Some of the humor is great (The Billy Idol concert lol!, some of the dialogue,etc..)- Voice acting is improved from the last few games (The odd one sucks but most are great)- The Jetpack fully upgraded actually feels REALLY good! I thought this would be jank cityNegatives:- The audio sort of sucks, sound effects are bland and the soundtrack isn't as epic as say Gothic 3 or Risen 1's soundtrack- Performance is slightly lower than Elex 1 (Mainly in the Faction areas)- An FOV option would be nice!More thoughts on the game later, so far performance isn't to bad, I am at about 60 to 65 fps most the time. Not perfect optimization but the game does look better than Elex 1 and it runs slightly worse, so not a big deal. Still early in the game but yes it feels like another PB rpg, if you like there previous games you will like this. If you hated any games you played of theres then you probably won't like this. They make niche type games and I enjoy them, some people won't though. This does everything better than Elex 1 other than performance.So far 6 hours in this is the best PB game for me since Risen 1, combat is improved nicely and most other things have been improved to (minus the performance). For those who care, my favorite PB games over the years have been as follows:1. Gothic 22. Risen 13. Gothic 14. Elex 25. Gothic 36. Elex7. Risen 38. Risen 2Its the best PB game in years.Give the game a fair shot, past the start of the game and check out the map, the different factions, do a ton of quests and its a really fun time.**I ended up beating this game and it was great fun. Sucks to see PB go under, they have made some classic games over the years. While there games are janky, they sure have alot of charm and are really fun to explore there game worlds, you are always rewarded for exploration in PB games. LONG LIVE PB and Euro Jank rpgs!**

_childDocuments_.review: Waited for all the patches to come and I'm glad I did. The performance with my rig (Vega 56, Ryzen 2600X, 16gb ram) is a stable 50fps pretty much all the time with high-medium settings. Changing the resolution scaling to 80 percent helped to get it really nice and smooth. Alternative camera angle is also good. The game is awesome. If you like Piranha Byte games or just Elex 1 I'd highly recommend it. Tons of stuff to do - fun dialogue, interesting quests, good companions, lots of choices, looting, stealing, upgrading all the good stuff. The jetpack is really fun in this one. It brings some depth to the combat and makes moving around the map fun and fast (remember to upgrade it!). The only slight downside for me is the combat. It can get repetitive but mixing in the jetpack, magic and different weapons keeps it still enjoyable. Enemy AI can be pretty stupid at times and the hitboxes for some enemies are really annoying but overall it doesn't ruin the game for me.The story so far has been good, still have some main quests to do. In addition to the main quests I would recommend at least doing the companion quests. They bring a lot to the table as far character development goes. I've also enjoyed most of the basic side quests. Overall a great open world RPG.EDIT: The last main quests were really repetitive, kill X amount of X etc. I would still recommend the game but they really dropped the ball on the last quests. The story itself was fine. If there will be an another sequel I'd hope that the mission structure would be more diverse in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has two points that spoil the game to the point of unplayability for me:1. the technology.It is an outrage how badly this game runs on AMD cards. It looks significantly worse than its predecessor. While Elden Ring and the like run smoothly with medium detail, Elex 2 jerks around with less than 20 frames and hasn't been improved by the past patches. If I had bought the game via Steam, I would have complained about it. 2. the writingI just can't handle it. It really is the worst written video game in a long, long time. It's so bad. The dialogue is all hilarious, the game intro is a disaster. The rendered intro sequence was guaranteed to be outsourced and built by a team that had absolutely no idea of any vision for Elex 2. "Elex 2 is set in green pastures? ♥♥♥♥ it, we'll pack the seamless sequence into the desert and garnish our digital thin with the wildest and most choppy animations imaginable. Traction, physics, atmosphere: Doesn't matters. And then those dialogues. There's your own wife explaining to you for exposition what her profession and position is, and our seven-year-old child asking us if we're "a destructive being or a creative being, and how do you think we'll shape the future of the country."Over all, the urge to want to tell a personal story full of drama with the moral standards of a bioware game, but with the subtlety of an 80's midnight movie. You could call it overambitious, or just, beyond measure, extremely bad :) The villain of the first part shows up after 2 minutes and demands that we trust him and help him build a common ground as a future for humanity. After 2 minutes. Neither does one have a choice, nor sufficient orientation to justify such a choice. Ever heard of game entry, exposition, and slowly building tension?Yes it's charming in principle when a video production is helmed by a small team. But please Piranha Bytes, you urgently need help with technology and story writing. Hire some writers to help you with dialogue and world building.The product here is disastrous and will probably be my last game from the developer unless there is a significant improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: As I loiter and observe the routines of two night watchmen (a narrow window of opportunity is said to exist when their cigarette breaks occasionally overlap), I glance at the moon to get some sense of the passing time. Looming so large as it does in the pale blue sky, it moves at a snail's pace, yet soon I realize that it is also rotating! Indeed, I could sit and count near every crater upon its lustrous surface if this job drags on much longer. But wait, what's this, a SECOND moon? Much smaller though it is, this one also slowly rotates as it follows an orbit 'round the first. Suddenly I no longer yearn to press 'T' to wait, but to press 'T' for telescope, instead...

_childDocuments_.review: All right, first let me tell you this: IF you enjoyed Elex regardless of its flaws, you will enjoy Elex2 as well.i honestly think they did i good job capturing the flair of the first game and continue with it, so its easy to get into it if you liked the first one.Now, to the not so shiny parts of Elex2:People moan and cry about the Camera and i can understand that. The first hour or so i also was put of by it but you get used to it. It's still somewhat annoying if you HAVE to get used to it though.Next i have to fully agree with what people say about face animations... THAT took A LOT of getting used to and PB could have done a better job there, but at least its not as bad as some assasin game from a couple years back.My next point of gripe would be to whoever reworked the inventory screen... c'mon man, at least let us search/sort by slot instead of dumping everything into a single inventory screen, so you have to scroll, like 5minutes, to get to the bottom after a couple of hours of playtime and looting stuff... ESPECIALLY(!!!) those documents... WHY do i need a physical copy in my inventory i cant even stash in my chest, IF you give me an entry of it in my Log anyway? let me store that stuff... its so annoying to have them clutter my inventory screen since there are a lot of them you can pick up.I saw some people complain about the landing after using your jetpack and making a couple babysteps. just dont burn all your jetpack fuel and just tap space to land. Saves the entire babystep thing. Not to mention that you dont really want to run out of fuel while using it.... speed up to travel faster but then run out of fuel and crash into something? hurts a lot, trust me. i literally lost half my health once landing on a flat ground because i was like 3 pixels to high / going to fast. Blocking attacks from humans in Elex was already a pain but i think Elex2 made it even worse... Just dodge everything. 30+ hours and i still  havent figured out the exact timing to block sword blows. Still, this goes with what it was like in Elex, so im just bringing it up for people new to the Elex games.Crashes.... well, gotta say the game is quite stable for a new release. 30+ hours and only 3 crashes. 2 when i was opening safes/chests and 1 at a merchant. could be worse, could be better.Regarding FPS... i use the default settings for my system so far and find my game running at around 70 FPS most of the time, but some areas seem badly optimized and i drop to 40'ish FPS there. Rare instances 30. This is, by the way, regardless of how many objects are present on screen. Heavy foliage? 70fps. building with nothing in it? 30 fps.Final verdict for me is a 7,5/10. could be an 8 if they fix some stuff.If you are new to the Elex games or didnt like the first one that much but want the 2nd game regardless i recommend you wait a couple months until they fixed some stuff up and polished the game a bit more or you might be disappointed. For everyone else who's just curious about the game i'd say wait until you see it for 40-50% off on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the developer and a huge Gothic 1-2 fan and also Elex1 fan. I can say that this game is very good but you gotta be some of the above fan to think like me. It has its flaws and they are quite serious. First moments of playing I was very sceptical and even considered dumping the game. What is terrible about the game: -My biggest flaw is lack of importing the save file from Elex1, I think they said that it would be an option. Small spoiler here I guess, Jax in this game has a kid with Caja whom I did not care about at all in Elex 1, I picked Nasty, this makes me not care about everything around this relationship so bummer. Also the kid's face is an atrocity. -As most of other players note, the camera, at first I was like 'what is going on' but it takes getting used to it, nonetheless its a flaw. -Performance, I understand that my card is not that powerfull to run it in 4k (rtx 3060ti) but I at least want a stable 60 in 2k, game drops from time to time to 50 and there is stuttering. -Wierd anomalies like disappearing assets as you run through the city -The faces of some NPCs are terrifying -Graphics overall take time getting used to as well, at least for me, look at the grass for example its like the wind moves the bottom part and the upper part is solid - looks funny -The inventory, I can't defend it, its terrible, you gotta scroll from bottom to top everytime because there are no categories or something similar -There are small glitches like npcs getting stuck on your character and stepping like madmen but all games have glitches on launch its unavoidable. Whats good about the game: -If you just get used to the above mentioned flaws, because it is possible, the game is amazing overall.-Old, wooden combat, character is a piece of wood as well -Quests are interesting, normally i dont care about what npcs have to say but in this game its actually interesting -I think I heared a sound of a wolf from Gothic 1-2 which an enemy used, also a lot of sounds from Risen games if you can catch it. -Exploring the world - this I think is the biggest and most enjoyable activity in the game. -You dont get a companion early, or I did not, so you can't exploit that To sum upHonestly this is an amazing game, one of those which you just like or not. It has its flaws like all games, it is made for certain part of people, but if you get sucked in the world you will enjoy your time spent. I personally recommend giving the game a try if you are not a fan of Elex, Gothic and Risen games. To all fans of the game I also recommend the game and trying to put the flaws aside. It really is great adventure. 10/10 obviously.

_childDocuments_.review: To clarify, I did not complete the game, but I managed to get to the second half of it. I am a big fan of all Pirahna's games, I even adore Risen 2, but I cannot describe Elex 2 as anything but a total disappointment. I welcome combat changes, although it feels streamlined. Flying is also a nice addition. But that is it, all other aspects of the game are a downgrade compared to the first game. The visuals are mostly the same except for terrible AA and uglier character models. Level design is a big step back. Do you remember fantastic locations such as Hort, Abessa, and Goliath from the first game? Well, there will be nothing as such in Elex 2. Do you remember environmental diversity from the first game? Well, it also disappeared. Faction mixing is an excellent idea which was implemented terribly. The story feels incohesive and full of retcons. The second part of the game is just a bunch of repetitive filler quests. The dialogues were never a strong side of Pirahan, but, oh god, in Elex 2, dialogues and voice acting are pure cringe, even if you already had low expectations. There are some other minor complaints like instead of improving the Emotional/Cold system, they replaced it with something more useless. But I want to emphasise something that is bothering me a lot. The only thing I always expected from Pirahna games is a stable performance and esthetic visuals so I can forget about most of the issues and focus on exploration. Performance is ♥♥♥♥. The lack of proper AA makes my eyes bleed. DX12 branch is better in terms of performance but adds even more visual issues. Guys, you have been doing the same game, gothic in different skins, for the last 20 years. So how the hell you managed to fail so hard?

_childDocuments_.review: Cliche writing, duplicate materials and overused moves make the core of ELEX 2. And the most "I don't give a f**k" to an alien invasion that you ever see. Generous 6/10, there are very little improvements from their first installment, its like they reused the game engine intact. With the exception of jet pack upgrades there is no difference to the lvl-up system. It also introduces new flaws with the targeting and lock-on, which come from the jet pack upgrades., the game overuses the same sprites and animations a lot. Like A LOT. For example there is an animation set used by all the ogres-giants-mutants, exact same attacks and movement, with no variation coming from the fact that one is an oversized ogre and the other is a hulking machine monstrocity. And the same exact weapons for each faction used multiple times with a different name and different stats., it takes place 7-8 years after ELEX 1. Apparently, MC managed to defeat the bad guys at the end of ELEX 1, only to be forgotten by the world and isolate himself because "reasons". Also he gets infected at the start of ELEX 2 , but it just erases the skills you got at the first game and makes you start from scratch. Also-also he is probably the only person who has survived being infected because of plot armor, everyone else infected has died., the game has assumed that MC has taken the Good Guy path at ELEX 1. You don't transfer saves, you don't make choices at start and you don't in any way have a saying in what happened. Now the aliens are attacking and terraforming the planet, but apparently everyone thinks that it's fine and there is no point to panic or actually do something. . If you have played ELEX 1 you know what i mean. If not, expect something that comes out of mobile games. Progression slows down from the 1/3rd of the game, as you need more and more time to grind the skill points to get better weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played a AA game, think AAA (Mass Effect, GTA V, the greats) and take away at least 50% of their funding. This is what you get at the end of the day. A lot of passion but lack of funding makes it a janky but lovable experience just like the first one. Maybe not worth the full price but I've gotten my hours out of it and will get more. If you liked any Piranha Bytes games you'll like this. It's a straight improvement from the first one and it genuinely feels like my choices matter even more this time around. Not just that but the itemization and pure freedom you have with the weapons and building your character in this game is a huge improvement! It used to be locked behind factions but now if you find a shotgun and have the stats? Use it brother it's all yours. The writing can be silly but there's so much heart in this game I can't help but love all of it. Factions are fleshed out, combat is more fleshed out, it truly is just a second ELEX.All in all if you want a good RPG with good quests I really recommend this. This is one of the only situations I've begun replaying to join every faction because of the 5 you can join they all have interesting characters and backgrounds with quests that actually explore their limits and make me want to experience their quests.

_childDocuments_.review: Picking up right a few years after the events of the 1st Elex game, Elex 2 doesn't do a great job of being a successor. The combat in this game is improved in comparison to the first one, but falls flat in many other aspects. They added many annoying elements to the game that robs you of the immersion that Elex 1 had. Some of those things are buggy/backtracking banter dialogue from NPC companions, flying enemies (good luck trying to hit these if you play on controller), too many invisible walls to count, getting endlessly latched on to a ledge that you're trying to let go, and many other inconvenient problems. The addition of new faction options was a plus.I was disappointed that you're unable to revisit the zone of Edan even though the characters you meet talk about it as a past memory. The banter of companion dialogue wasn't as pleasant in this one as the first game. It felt "forced" at many times. Overall, Elex 2 fell short of my expectations after being really pleased from playing the first one. I would only recommend Elex 2 to someone who beat the first Elex game and wants to continue the story (Elex 2 ends on a cliff hanger). To a new player, i'd recommend trying Elex 1 and see if the story pulls you in. If not, look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, another typical Piranha game. Great open world, lots of well-designed quests to do, the quality is just far better than most Ubisoft style of open world trash you can get these days.  But the game has many things that will turn players away: very rough on the edges, animations are wonky, etc,. And the worst of them all, is difficulty. It's almost always like this in the developer's previous titles, player will become the most powerful being in the world by the end, but at the beginning, the game is very, very hard, almost anything can kill the player instantly, and it wont get much better until dozens of hours later. I've played all the developer's previous titles more than once, yet I still get killed almost instantly very often. Not much of a problem for me as I already get used to it, but this can be a critical issue for newcomers.So I can only recommend this game to players who love great open world and have the capacity to endure some suffering. This game is a treasure to some, but poison to many.

_childDocuments_.review: ELEX II is, at least at launch, a bug riddled open world RPG that gives players the freedom to start their adventure the way they want with little to no guidance and minimal hand holding. Sadly, it is being released days within the likes of Elden Ring, Horizon Forbidden West, TW Warhammer III, Lost Ark, Dying Light 2, GT 7, D2 Witch Queen and many others. Steam Curator Page:+Large open world +Definition of freedom +Engaging story and characters +Improved combat +Satisfactory voice acting +Game sometimes recognises your pace +Same world but drastically altered +Companions will be affected by your actions -Audio design (hit markers) -Ranged combat -Mouse smoothing makes aiming a pain -Big cities cause everything to pop in and out -Difficulty levels are not perfectly accurate -AI is easily unintelligent -Quest structure can be tedious -Character models can look SCARY The first impressions I had of the game is the terribly low quality of cinematics, both in their design and fidelity, as well as the audio and video quality. The audio design around the cinematics is done very poorly, a quality standard that sadly carries on in game as well. Poor hitbox effects depending on you weapon, loud, obnoxious water effects that will plague headphone users, as well as ambient noises that are so intrusive, I thought my speakers were starting to fail. Turns out, it was wood creaking. These issues are nothing compared to the festival of bugs that will take place once you enter any large encampment. Describing how severe the issues that plague large encampments does not do it justice. Certain areas of all the settlements cause the game to freak out, popping in and out all elements of the game. Character models such as heads, torsos, hair, or entire people altogether, walls, the floor, trees.Frame render latency is also at an average of 40ms, although I believe (more so hope) that a GPU driver will take care of the issue. The latest Nvidia driver does not mention ELEX 2 amongst the games it is “ready” for. My 3080 TI and R9 5900x struggle to maintain anything over 60 to 70 FPS with the settings maxed out at 1600p ultrawide resolution.Another thing I want to briefly touch on is the AI (Artificial Intelligence) behaviour. The artificial entities in this game are anything but intelligent, especially your companions. This is an issue that has carried over from the previous game. Once hunted by enemies, your companion will be extremely late to respond to the threat, leaving you to fend for yourself early in the battle. This is not at all complimented by the lack of competency fighting said enemies. This is mostly an issue with melee combatants. Alas, the jetpack has been reworked since the last game to give it more functionality through upgrades. You can use it to dash forward fast for a few seconds, increase the fuel capacity to help you climb higher, hover, and use your weapons while doing so and more. Jetpack fuel no longer regenerates while it is not used and there is fall damage in the game this time around. On the other hand, you can now grab onto ledges while using the jetpack which is great.  Combat is also quite coherent for both melee and ranged. There are various weapon types to choose from. Single handed with shield, dual handed, and a variety of long-range weapons such as plasma rifles, crossbows, bows, grenade launchers etc. Ammunition is quite hard to come about so be conservative with it. As mentioned previously, stamina does not drain while in combat and in story mode difficulty. I started the game playing on easy difficulty, but the difficulty levels are quite misleading. Although the quest structure is not perfect, it is damn good. There was an instance where I ignored a certain quest line until 20 hours into the game, where I picked up a quest line that required the previous quests to not have been completed for the new quest to take place. I was quite blown away and started pondering, how many quests have I affected by doing some of the things I had done?What I am certain of however, is one thing. Regardless of all the flaws the game has, deep down in its core, there is a very beautifully crafted adventure to be had. There is true player freedom, real story changes depending on your actions and quests you choose to complete and or ignore. A vast open word to explore and face enemies that are both old and new to the series. Despite all the technical shortcomings, poor performance and bugs, horribly low-quality cinematics, and terribly slow start, immersing yourself in the protagonist’s shoes to unite all the factions in order to face a new enemy that threatens to wipe out all life on earth is very well worth giving this game a try.  Special thanks to Terminals.IO for providing me with the keyFor more, please subscribe#ELEX2#THQ#PiranhaBytes

_childDocuments_.review: A fun RPG with a great sense of progression and exploration.  Exploring the world is fun and rewarding because.- Enemies do not scale with your level. This means that some monsters will simply be too difficult for you to face until you have powered up your character appropriately.- Challenging enemies are not simply located in a designated 'Zone' like many games. Instead they can be found in hand picked locations even close to the start of the game.  This can make for some great opportunities to sneak or simply run past powerful enemies grabbing whatever loot you can.  But it also means that exploring involves learning when to fight, when to run, instead of simply killing everything in an area (at least until your powerful enough).- Important loot is not random, but instead can be found in interesting locations at any time.- In order to acquire skills you need to find someone who can train you in the skill you desire.- The factions are very different from each other and choosing which faction you side with will grant you access to unique and powerful skills.- While difficult at first, it is very satisfying to eventually wade through hordes of enemies that used to kill you in seconds.- Who needs a horse when you have a Jet Pack! (Make sure you upgrade the sprint boosters!)The main thing that my put some people off is that Elex II, like the other Piranha Bytes games, do not have the AAA budget of other titles. Piranha bytes has 33 devs in their studio, so the level of polish, motion capture, graphical details, companion depth, animations etc, can not compare to something like Elden Ring which had approximately 350 devs working for 4 and a half years. However, if you are willing to put in the initial effort to learn the initially challenging combat and happy to overlook aspects of the game like simple cut scenes and animations, then you will find a rich and fun world to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: Had prepurchased this since the various video previews confirmed it implements the same formulae that work and lead to fine ARPG entertainment.A few game design differences compared with the first ELEX game attract a wider target group of players, who appreciate hand-holding. - Story mode difficulty that makes combat easier than Easy mode in case that's yourpreference. - Changes to the combat rules to simplify them more. There's still a stamina threshold, but no longer a requirement to concatenate well-timed normal/power attacks as to increase damage while gaining power for a final special attack. - More map markers, search area indicators, more custom map markers player can add to expand the world overview map, many more teleporters (as the primary fast travelling system). - No strict requirement to join a faction. - Lip-syncing for voice-acting.I've played the English version and really enjoyed all the voice-acting, which contributes a lot to the atmosphere when diving into such a virtual world. Also, there are various ambient sounds, so turning off the background music is highly recommended if you like immersion. Also don't avoid night time activity like the plague.Role-players get choices related to playing a friendly benevolent guy versus an unfriendly malicious to evil brawler - or anything in between. These choices can lead to winning or losing potential allies, also within a faction.There are main factions and sub-factions. For example, one can gain two ranks in one faction and then switch sides and join another faction, gaining access to their extra abilities.The game's virtual world is not the same as in the previous game. The developers have decided to move the story to new areas while keeping some familiar places without copying them directly. As such there is high incentive to explore the world while searching for allies, crafting materials, equipment and places that have not been picked clean.There are flying enemies! And they don't only fly low above the ground as in the Gothic series games, for example. It either needs ranged weapons to hit them or flying with the jetpack and then launching melee attacks against them. Some of the most entertaining battles in this game are against creatures that dig into the ground, crawl out and catapult high into the air while throwing rocks. Quit-in-rage players won't like the "Searchbot" machines that fire three energy beams at once. Even smaller sniper drones can be annoying. Fortunately, there are many weapons and fighting styles to get the job done.Most of the story-telling happens during conversation. The outcome of main missions and related conversation leads to knowledge gain, story progression, events as well as the next chapter of the game. There are some introductory cutscene cinematics and later some brief cutscenes related to missions. It's a game not a movie.The story, the story progression, the factions and interactions with them have kept me interested. Potential companions add their own personal missions for a change. Among the side-quests I particularly enjoyed the longer escorting missions including the reaction from NPCs and companions.

_childDocuments_.review: Update after ~60 hours:I've come to realize that the reason this game is so appealing to me *is* the jank, the weirdness, the polish missing here and there, the quirky dialog, and the fact it is missing so many of the things found in AAA games - but has so many of the desirable things. This game is beautiful. It has heart. It has a group of devs that love it it. It is a dream RPG for me. My initial thoughts after 6 hours (below) apply, but I want to add that I truly love this game. It is a solid RPG with so many high points I'm not going to even list the low points... or any more of them. My recommendation is buy it. Play it. Get over yourself, AAA geek. Learn what heart lends to a game.From when I was younger and more naive:Will revisit and update this later, but getting a solid thumb in now (6 hours playtime).I don't recall all of the details of the first Elex, but read my review recently. This game does not appear to have been made by the same team... almost everything I complained about there has been addressed/fixed/improved. Combat and movement is smooth. Voice acting is pretty darn good. Map is detailed and interesting to explore. Nothing other than minor and infrequent bugs thus far. I'm really enjoying this one for now.One remaining gripe: While I wouldn't characterize the conversation dialog as juvenile here, it is clunky and awkward more often than not. Sometimes I think it is such for the sake of brevity. Other times, I think it is attributable to an odd/bad translation. Sometimes I think the developer might just have hired a budget writer. It is, nevertheless, serviceable and clear in most cases.

If you are a fan of Piranhas’ RPGs, an enthusiast of post-apocalyptic fantasy games or just a casual player looking for quite a long, enjoyable game for a month of regular playing, do not hesitate and get your copy of ELEX II!

_childDocuments_.review: It is what I expected from the second installment of this new PB Franchise.I've played their games since Gothic 1 and I'll admit, their games always follow the same formula. You start as a low level, nonsense character. If its the next game of a series, you have some reason why you are set back to square one. As is the case with Elex II, Jax has pretty much lost all of his powers due to an event which happens right at the beginning. Great... I feel like I'm back in Gothic 2.On the plus side, this game is genuinely the first PB game where I feel like they got the starting experience down. You don't really have the chance to encounter something you won't be able to kill within the first 2 hours, that is, if you're following the story and/or side quests. I got into the game really quickly and sunk straight back into that Gothic Feeling of: DO EVERYTHING POSSIBLE BEFORE JOINING A GUILDThe combat system is massively improved. It is no longer a rythmn game, which is a big plus. However, you cannot cancel animations and because of this, attacking certain creatures at the wrong moment, especially in the early game, just murders you. Due to this: QUICKSAVE OFTEN.Also: Aerial Enemies are a pain in the butt. The best feature imo, is the new and improved Jet Pack. Every point invested in it feels amazing. Having a maxed out jet pack, flying across the world just feels right. It makes me not want to use teleporters often because it is just so much fun.As of writing this, I have sunk 40 hours into it, not completed the game and have enjoyed my experience. If you like the Gothic Series or the Risen Series. You will enjoy this game. Its the classic PB game.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10I love the setting and factions. The blending of tech, fantasy and magic is brilliant. It is what keeps me coming back. Just like with the previous iteration, the combat initially feels like it wants to be a souls-like, but the queued up action animations make it feel more janky/strategic than reflexive. Combine that with the fact that beginning weapons are as effective as pool-noodles and you are forced to learn to run from most fights until mid game. This has the player mostly focusing on completing fetch and story quests to level up, which leads me to my main gripe:The  reasoning of the main characters is just off. I don't know if this is due to translation or writing but I had a hard time NOT scoffing at many interactions. The background characters and factions are pretty good and are the best part of the story IMO, but the more in the forefront the character is, the less sensible they are.Ultimately, it is the Main Characters that hinder the game for me and the setting and factions that carry it.
