_childDocuments_.review: Even Cyberpunk 2077 ran better on my setup on release.I got a lot of graphic glitches. The environment just pops out and fades back in while I walk around. I don't experience heavy framedrops that much, at least it's less concerning than those graphic glitches. Reading the discussions this seems to be a common problem, even with NVIDIA graphic cards which are performing even better than AMD in the game.So absolutely DO NOT BUY at the current state of the game. I will stop playing now, too and wait for some updates - then I'll probably update my review.Beyond the performance issues, I do have some negative points about the game:First of all the controls were never the best in the PB games. But in ELEX II it almost feels like I'm playing Gothic 1 all over again. The controls are so vague and spongy. I almost fell to my death just by trying to pick an item close to an edge, because I just couldn't get the right distance.The main quest line is bad. They tried to explain once again why the hero is a nobody, but it's just ridiculus. Some time has passed and the world forgot about Jax and what he did. That would make sense, but the time that has passed is just a span of maybe a decade. A lot of people Jax knew are still alive and not even aged a lot. A lot of people do actually still remember him. But there starts the next issue with the story: Even though they know who he is and what he did, he still has to do all that "from nobody to faction hero" stuff all over again. This is just a very bad storytelling. Either introduce a new hero or actually let a few hundreds of years pass, with the drawback that most, if not all, other known characters are dead. Another thing that bugs me personally a lot: Your choices in the last game don't matter, the game will just decide for you which faction Jax joined and whom he romanced. Mild spoiler here: He even has a son with Carja. Which is another bad design choice. We are suddenly supposed to care about his family that just appeared out of nowhere. This doesn't work at all.The stories of the side quests on the other hand are good and the world feels alive and worthy of exploration. With the jetpack being available from the very beginning you have even more choices how to advance in the quests and the world.Overall the world does look beautiful. But the character models got even worse compared to Elex 1.Update (28.05.2022): So I just finished the game and I still can't recommend it. The story overall is really bad, the ending is just another major cliffhanger. The last main quest after credits just doesn't make sense and is tedious. And a lot of the late game gameplay is just so annoying. Get to point A, kill x enemies, get to point B and kill x enemies and then get to point C to kill another x enemies. And these are basically are couple of the end game main quests. Also I really hate the fact that you're forced to grind. At a certain point in the game, you can't advance until you reach a certain level. This forces you to do side quests until you reach that level, which sucks incredibly.

_childDocuments_.review: ELEX II is ELEX with somewhat better combat. Animations are smoother and more responsive, but it is now very basic stamina based combat. I do wonder what would happen if they would've combined "rhythm" inputs of first ELEX with better animations and execution of second. But most important part is that it is not frustrating here.What, in my opinion, is completely butchered in this game, compared to first ELEX is the economy. It's too easy to get tons of money, buy everything you need and have enough money to do it twice at the end of the game. This trivializes usual PB dynamic of progression. You no longer really fear getting swindled by NPCs, you don't covet that end-game armor etc.I still would recommend this if you liked first. Especially if you want to continue story. You meet many returning characters with extra janky faces this time, see how the world changed and get some pretty interesting revelations.For newcomers, I recommend, of course playing first part first. As a lure into PB games, If there's one thing I can say about what separates PB RPGs from others is - dialogues. Not the main story ones, they are a bit of a gibberish, that require a bit of a manual untangling. But the ones that happen in side quests, which in these games are almost mandatory to do. There's a lot attention of details in dialogues to what choices you pick, even the smallest, you might think insignificant choices are remembered to you by NPCs at one point or the other. You never know what might happen when you betray or try to swindle someone, it can always come back to you unsuspectingly. But if you judge character you are talking to right and be nice to him, they will also have your back later. Which might be not as simple as it sounds, considering pretty much every other character tries to scam you, it is harsh world there after all. Not every NPC is gonna tell you their life story when you speak to them, they always try to put thought into who that characters is, and base their responses on it, which makes fun talking to them, they are not simply a template with a bit different tone like some RPGs have. There's a lot to this dynamic I can write about, but most importantly, this magic is still present in both of ELEX games.

_childDocuments_.review: ORIGINAL POST - 01-07-2024:ELEX 2...is more ELEX. Not super far into it - around 2.3 hours, according to Steam - but so far, it's good. Differently recommend playing ELEX 1 first, as the game takes place not super-long after the original ELEX and there's already references & character stuff, which it does expect you to remember from the first game. I loved ELEX 1, so I expect I'll also like ELEX 2, in the long-run...provided it doesn't fall apart and all. I'm using mainly the DX12 build here - b/c my God, even on a SSD, DX11 version takes a while just to load. And it both loads & runs quite a bit better on modern hardware, if you're using DX12. Regardless, if you played ELEX, you know what you're walking into: another Piranha Bytes game with some Eurojank & lots of that 3rd-person BTC (behind the character) type of action-RPG goodness. Also, it's nice that I can put it audio-wise in Non-English and use this game's original language here, which sounds much more emotional & passionate; it just works better w/ the game, IMHO.Enjoying this one so far - but yeah, I've got to give it time & it also ain't easy on Default (Normal) difficulty, like many PB games. Just, also note - there is an Easy Mode (right below Normal) & also an even lower-difficulty type of Story Mode, which might help those who have a tough time w/ any sort of PB games, as even PB seems to be trying to get a bit more accessible with their difficult games by adding modes like these - haven't touched those modes yet, BTW. Early on here, but so far - yep, I'm liking it. Hopefully, like most PB games, it's at least good, by the time it's over and I've finished the campaign.ADDENDUM -> 07-25-2024:After having issues w/ the DX12 build in certain areas & with graphical bugs and glitches, causing the game to have all kinds of issues: couldn't get into certain areas, causes the game to freeze, caused the game to crash, and other madness. So, I did have to switch to DX11 build, which runs way worse. DX11 mode's performance is about half as a good as DX12 build & can be downright murderous in areas with lots of NPC's, such as The Grotto and Crater, turning the game's performance into 20-30fps on my laptop loaded with a RTX 3060 6gb VRAM version and my desktop could only pump out 30-45fps with my RTX 3070 8gb VRAM version (desktop GPU). An app called Loseless Scaling is the saving grace here, as I could finally pump out 50-60fps by utilizing Scaling & Frame-Generation type of techniques.After about 85 hours or so according to Steam, ELEX 2 has been finished. No surprise, but it's another really good action-RPG from PB, of course. RIP to Piranha Bytes (PB). It's a shame we'll never really get a real deal ELEX 3 from PB themselves, to wrap stuff up properly, all done their way.Regardless, still one heck of a Swan Song for PB, so....RIP, Piranha Bytes. We'll miss you & your awesome & often very underrated action-RPG's.ADDENDUM - 07-29-2024.Some of this might sound a bit repetitive & redundant, but I'm adding this in anyways. Finished-up ELEX 2 [Steam] last week, after 85 hours. That was pretty good and setting up sadly for an ELEX 2. It's basically more ELEX: so if you liked ELEX 1 and/or any other PB games (Risen series and/or Gothic series) & are fine w/ their typical Eurojank action-RPG's, you'll like this. RIP to Piranha Bytes, since they're now gone - and likely, we'll never see a proper ELEX 3 from PB. I would love to see Tinhead (new studio w/ ex-PB dev's) get the IP and finish the story up with an ELEX 2 expansion or a true ELEX 3 - but, I'm so dreaming here probably; the publisher (ummm, I think that's Embracer?) probably owns the ELEX IP. Again, RIP to Piranha - ELEX 2 was one heck of a swan song, if that's the end of this series as we know it and also the sad ending of PB. RIP, Piranha Bytes; we'll miss you & your underrated action-RPG's.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a reason why I own every single Piranha Bytes game released on Steam: their games never fail to satisfy that itch for an original, imaginative, and highly immersive RPG experience. I've thoroughly enjoyed every game they've ever produced. Admittedly, the original Gothic series remains the unquestionable favorite, but the Elex games are also good. I especially enjoy the jet pack mechanic in the Elex series. In Elex II, I can fly like superman or ironman which isn't something I've ever seen in another RPG. The mixture of futuristic and medieval lore does feel awkward at times, and the choice of objects you can find in the game world can seem very strange, but there's enough to sink your teeth into here that these quirks are easily overlooked. I've played for 150 hours as of the time of this review, and only crashed twice, which is a win in my opinion (especially since the game allows quick saving at any time). There was only one broken side-quest that I wasn't able to complete. The ending was very anticlimactic, and the infinite respawns of monsters leaves any sense of progress from killing them seem pointless once you've achieved a particular level or strength through character progression, but overall I'm happy with my purchase. This is a classic open-world RPG, and Piranha Bytes was among the first developing companies to master the open-world concept of RPGs. Explore, learn, discover, level up, craft, and choose your own path to victory. What's not to love about that? In my opinion, the only other RPG games that rival Piranha Bytes' games are the Elder Scrolls franchise. Nothing else comes close. If you want a true, open-world RPG experience, you cannot go wrong with this one. I'd give it a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Thus far, Elex 2 is a vast improvement over the first entry in the series; however, the voice acting is sub-par at times, and the story is still run-of-the-mill generic. Yet, I love every second of this game, and the world of Magalan. Upon first entering the game one will notice the improvement in graphics, models, and animations (albeit still rough around the edges) when compared to Elex 1. The musical score is still the weird sci-fi fantasy goodness, though I wish it would play different songs more often. Although the graphics have been improved, the combat is still janky, and since one cannot change the FOV in the settings, you will at times be a little bit to up close and personal which can become problematic. Also, the optimization in this game could use work due to it having FPS drops and micro-stuttering at certain times and in certain areas (I have well above the recommended PC specs for this title). Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys some jank with a great big open world to explore and many choices to make, or ultimately not make. One does not need to pick up the original Elex to enjoy Elex 2 but I recommend the first since it is a great experience, even if frustrating during the first 10 hours when leveling up. Pick up in an eventual sale or at full price for a great janky RPG time, 7/10.

Too bad it had a good foundation and much more potential. After this experience I'll scrutinize the next PB game closely before I decide to buy it.

Could have just left vague choices made in previous game but instead you went with canon choices. Either have import, or don't have it at all.Story never got everywhere; it just set up Elex 3, so you better not drop the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ball with it Pyranha Bites.Drinking elex/dark-elex has no consequences unlike Elex 1 which steered your morality according to lore.There are leftover, glaring bugs such as duplicate of dialogue option in the literal first hour of the game, the final 2 chapters of the game seem like they're still in alpha (even tho the game's released for more than 1 year) What did it improve upon?Combat, jet-pack, women no longer have one face. _childDocuments_.review: Piranha Bytes have been making more or less the same game for the last 20 years, aimed at their hardcore fanbase and rarely detracting from the formula. They've changed nothing from Elex 1, only introduced ton of new bugs and removed useful features like respec. You can complete almost all of the side-quest apart from companion-related ones in the very first chapter of the game, get all the best weapons and simply cruise on auto-pilot for the rest of it which gets boring really fast. With a bigger budget and more development time they managed to produce a carbon copy of the first game that feels rushed and unpolished. Studio is obviously stuck and inacapable of evolving or innovating.  That being said, as a long-time fan I still found Elex 2 compelling enough to complete it. Despite janky combat, awful pacing, uninspired quest design (especially in the latter half of the game) I still had fun exploring and slowly building my character from nothing into a over-powered planet-savior. This however does not merit an recommendation. If you can get it on a deep, deep discount and you REALLY liked Elex 1, there's some fun to be had here. Otherwise, avoid

This could have been a DLC of the old game if the story wasnt placed after the first game ending.Also i started the game in story mode just to check it out while getting baked in the process,  and im getting killed everywhere by half the enemies i find. So far anything bigger than a mosquito is potentially deadly, but i managed to clear like 12 bandits with ranged weapons (that i cannot use) at the same time in an encampment i found, which makes zero sense.I recruited a companion that somehow is at the same time powerful and useless, since half the time she misses the spells, but when she hits, she hits. Ive seen her blast away a mob in 2 shots and also miss 100% of the attacks on the next one.Supposedly im a super soldier that beat the old game killing the super hybrid mega boss, but now i start again from level 10? with no abilities even to use any weapon from the start, except a broken metal pipe. _childDocuments_.review: Quite a toss-up if this is a recommend or not-recommend game. I quite enjoyed it at firts, but the end-game dropped a ball hard and took me a lot of effort to make myself finish the game.+ Smaller map. While I could not visit all the places from the first game, the more compact space definietely suits Piranha games more.+ Weeker enemy types. There are areas with weaker enemies at the start of the game (old, young, weak etc...) that you can actually defeat. The part of the game when you avoid most things and hope to get a tiny bit stronger on the weak ones to dare to engage more is a lot smoother then in other Piranha games.+ Combat. They polished what they had in Elex 1, there are a lot less blunders with stuck enemies or elevation issues (when a fight moved to sloped terain in Elex 1, I either had to disengage or load, it was that bad).+ Companion AI. Early on having a sidekick helps a lot. I remeber in Elex 1 they just stood there and waited will I hit the creep or they hit me - and even then it was so cringy to make them engage and save my hide. Here I had no issues, they do engage what they should and do a decent job helping.= Respawning foes. Would not really list this as plus nor minus. For persistent Piranha worlds its an odd one to see re-populated areas you cleaned, but its motly focused on roads and goes for animal creeps from what I feel is a semi-random lists for each areas. - Main story. With a lot of nice side quests, the poor quality of the main sotry get really up there. With the post-apo feel of the first game mostly gone, the story is too sci-fi for me (in a bad sense, too much fiction with too litle to ground it on). Woont say more not to spoil it much for those actually interrested in exploring it themselves.- End game and Companion quests. And this a huge minus. At first when I encountered here quests requiring me to wait a day to continue, I liked it and thought its a nice addition to the game pace. And then every single quest wanted this... The last several hours of the game became just "talk to quest giver, get teleported to a place where they spawned leveled enemies (horrible idea, bandits with more HP then trolls - all just HP pinatas to leghten the engagements), kill them and wait a day to repeat".- Leveling. At first every single point of skill is important and its great to have to decide if you want this or that. But later on, every skill costs goes up and in the end, the levels do nothing for you. I ended running with almost 200 unspent skill points, just because there was no point in them, I did not needed them.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Piranah Bytes!Ok, so after 30 hours of gameplay, I have to leave a review! I don't want to stop playing this game! I was debating if I should even buy the game at launch, since I am still trying to get myself to finish AC:Odyssey. I am compulsive and once I started the first game I wanted to finish the entire series of games. It is exhausting, long and I can only really play it in short bursts. I also didn't want to play it parallel. But in the end, I wanted to support the devs (have been watching many of their videos during the last couple of weeks? months?) and make use of the discount. Thinking about it, that didn't really help the devs as much as buying full price?So now I own the title and I just wanted to quickly check it out ... and there goes my nights sleep :PFrom the first moment I was amazed and thrilled by the fluidity of movement and its speed, that felt (still feels) really nice! I didn't have any stuttering either, it just runs really well!Ok, the fighting is still a bit clunky, but way more enjoyable than in Elex 1 (good job there!). The quick selection works great and is simple to use - would have been nice to even have more slots, since there are so many cool weapons to chose between!What I really enjoy? The freedom to hide the entire HUD! No map! No pointers! No compass! Clean as it should be! I can get lost in the world, travel by sight, orient myself because I am learning the topography and landmarks. The worldbuilding is brilliant! Finding hidden passages, suddenly being overwhelmed by enemies hiding in the dark (yes, I am wearing the wrong set of glasses!), if I need I open the map to check for directions and then I'll fly the rest of the way while smashing flies with my burning axe.Seriously, the jetpack fighting mechanic is so much fun! Though it should maybe have a small tutorial. I only learned by accident, that I could target enemies in air and dash towards them with melee attacks.I really love the freedom of this game! Exploring the map, suddenly stumbeling into Fox and bringing him everywhere I go ever since - I'm playing with German voices (!!Info an die Entwickler!!: Danke für die Stimme! Ich will ihn gar nicht mehr weggeben! danke für das Engagement und seine Freude in den Streams mit euch ist eine Freude, die ansteckt!). Creeping around, knowing that enemies can quickly kill you, but sneaking into the first tower, just out of curiosity and being rewarded with a weapon like that!Did I mention the freedom? Now these developers give us the freedom to save whenever we want! Want to sneak into a house and rob them blind? Just quicksave before entering. Did you get cought? Just reload and try again! Are you going to fight a bunch of enemies? Just quicksave before you descend down onto them. Did you get in a bunch of hits already and stand just out of their reach? Just quicksave again so you don't have to redo the entire fight again, in case you get charged by another hidden creature! - You find this is cheesing the mechanics? Then just don't use it! You have the freedom to play as you please! Fun sidenote - I did this in an arranged duel underground once and upon reloading, my opponent was just walking away from me and telling me that he wasn't done with me just yet and we had to start again, hehe.The athmosphere and lighting is so beautiful! When the godrays from the setting sun shine through the mountains and the fog is making everything golden and hazy, I really enjoy the look of this game!The faces, especially the eyes might be a bit creepy but !!! switching off the torch/light the player has will make faces in dialoges a lot more pleasant! !!! (maybe it could go auto-off once entered into dialoge?)Really, my only real complaint?? Why has Jax lost his slightly angry and pointy eyebrows?? That is the only thing that keeps pulling me out and back into reality.Good night and thank you for this game (and thank you for my love of Gothic 1 that I feel rekindled in this game! If I now just run into Diego, I would not be surprised, nor disappointed!)

_childDocuments_.review: Yes it's bad.Mass Effect Andromeda held me more than Elex 2.In short it's a 2022 game but saying it feels like 2012 is a spit in the face to old games.The UI feels like unreal engine asset for Generic Sci-Fi Game, the world looks like it was slapped together by apprentices or fiverr freelancers. Combat is boring straight away, literally winner is who has faster hit animations and has more HP so if you want to dance around lvl 1 dog for 5 min. be my guest. As soon as I had control of the character i went everywhere i could around the beginning areas, only to find minor healing potions, abundance of food and alcohol. Choices matter my bottom body part, you get a few options, Nice, Sarcastic, Very Sarcastic.There's enough people who explained why this game flopped and there's no reason for me to continue but i felt like these were my major issues with the game. _childDocuments_.review: The enhancements towards character animations is nice to see. Falling animations are actually here this time, If you remember in the first one, when you fell from any decent distance you would go straight into a stickman pose, so its nice to see they took care of that at least. With piranha bytes games you sort of know what you're getting into, for the most part at least. Piranha bytes does an exceptionally great job in making you feel like an absolute god by the end of the game while having the experience towards getting to that a well designed and makes the player feel accomplished by the end of the game and that the case here once again. The world of Magalan looks great, which is another trope of Piranha bytes. The different bioms feel diverse and theirs plenty of lore to discover in the ways of notes and audio files. Characters are also fully voice acted which is nice and all but to be fair, by the end of the the game i had the voice audio turned off and just read through the dialogue.Pretty much everything else. The story this time is a complete snooze fest and the characters have little to no real likeable traits nor do they give you much room to like them due to the horrible voice acting. You would honestly be better off reading everything yourself if you have a single shred of imagination, you can voice act these characters better yourself. The combat was fun enough but the issue was the idiotic AI. I played on the highest difficulty setting and mid way through the game, after finding some items, i was everything in my path. Even the last(and only) boss had zero chance against me. Hopefully next time, if they make another one of course, they should do better than to just slightly increase the health per difficulty level and expect that to suffice because the combination of stupid AI with a high HP count doesn't equate to that much of a challenge, it just sucks away the players time unnecessarily.I would wait for a sale. Assuming you've never played a Piranha Bytes game then i would suggest picking up the first installment first and if you enjoy that one enough then i would say give this one a shot when its on sale. The first installment blows this one out of the water, even with the lack of polish behind it. In conclusion i was pretty disappointed here. I wasn't expecting much better than the first but the features they enhanced are the ones i could careless about in a Piranha Bytes game. I know their games to have poor polish but they always make up for it with the world building, character progression and story. Seem like they focused more on polish this time around, not even really doing that great of a job, in comparison towards their other games then sure but if you compare the polish here with other RPG's you can pick up, its honestly laughable. Hopefully their next project they stick with what they're good at which is world building, character progression and stories which this one severely lacked.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's make one thing clear: you won't be able to run the game at the video quality in the trailers. It's optimised like crap and even setting everything to low causes it to randomly not be able to get past 5 fps.That being said, if you liked gothic 1 & 2, the risen series or the first elex, it's more of the same, but when "the same" is something you enjoy it's not really a negative.Steam really needs more than "yes / no" for recommendations, because there's too many games that fall in that in-between region.If you're capable of potentially playing a game with graphics muddier than an early-to-mid 2000s predecessor, get it. If not, either wait some time or give it a wide berth.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this review is gonna be seen by players who already touched Elex 1 or any other PB game really.Still, I'll try to cater to both players who finished Elex 1 and those who haven't checked out the previous installment.So, once more Jax (that I'll be naming John Elex in further parts of the review) is back and things ain't looking too great for people of Magalan. His best efforts to keep people together went to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - and some shenanigans happened, shifting balance of power around - Clerics and Outlaws become a minor factions (that you can still join, just with "but"), Berserkers expanded, Albs merged with Separatists and new faction - Morkons - appeared from the depths of their basements, ready to be the new local edgy boys.So you still have 3 mayor factions + 2 minor ones to align with... OR you can ignore that and be a true non-aligned hero, which is kinda unheard of in PB games.Now, I want to merge the visual side of review with factions - game looks good. Vistas are nice, locations are interesting - some of them are new, some are very much changed version of Elex 1 locations. Factions have quite nice themes with their gear, some of them evolved - like Bersekers that took on utalitarian approach to their gear since they're now largery merged with Outlaws. Now that void of medieval-ish equipment is filled by Morkons, Albs remain the poster-boys of high-tech aesthetics.Sounds design is fine. Guns and spells maybe aren't outstanding but they do their job fine. Music is mostly imported from Elex 1 with some new pieces, but still it's a nice ambient music. Your ears won't bleed but don't expect to find a new bangers to listed to.Gameplay side... well, it plays mostly like a typical PB game - much improved system from Elex 1, that still takes a lot from Gothic 1 and 2 games - mostly increased cost of learning points when reaching certain breaking points. Why fix something that ain't broken, right?Game allows you to select your build and follow it through, more or less reaching "breaking point" at some moment, where you can pretty much deal with any hostilities on your way. Of course, game at start might be tough but worry not, you'll figure it out without problems.Generally speaking, it plays like a nice action rpg game with a roll and parry mechanics, nothing too out of place.Then, the story. It follows event from Elex 1, assuming it's own cannon version of events - so some characters are well and alive, some things went bad etc. You don't need to know the story of elex 1 since the results are already here and game explains a lot during the story... but well, here it is.Generally speaking, writing isn't the deepest. Some characters have moronic behaviour, some are just silly - and some are decent. Nothing to be replused by, but it's not the game that grabs you with a cast of unforgettable characters.Main story holds the ground and it's decent, but mostly is a motor for you to fight through harder and harder fights.Overall, game is fun. It has a solid rpg skeleton underneath, offers nice combat and character can be build to fit your playstyle. Story is there, world looks nice. I'd say it's a fine game. If unsure, grab it on some sale - or better yet, grab Elex 1 and check out if you gonna like that.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh... where do I begin. It runs worse than ELEX obviously, but it doesnt even look *better* than the first game.The dialogues are messed up, and at parts they were completely non-sensical. And Jax just interjects things from another conversation into it, sometimes the person speaking is the wrong person. _childDocuments_.review: Became absolutely addicted to the Elex story and franchise and have enjoyed the second instalment. Finished my Beserker play through and now to do it all again as the other factions.The game built upon the first and improved in so many areas from the Jet pack to general combat. The world actually feels lived and and the set ups from number 1 coming to reality in 2 is great. Morkons will be my next play through and really enjoyed my time doing quests for them and can't wait to try the quests locked away if your not in the Morkon faction next play through. I like this as gives the game replay potential and different experiences in each play through.Completing the game unlocks you unlimited jet pack fuel and oh my if flying across the map such an amazing feeling and view and the perfect reward for post game.Reading through some reviews i can't understand the complaints of motion sickness etc. i played the game for almost 12 hours a day since launch and not once have i felt motion sickness or had issues with the POV. Also people who complain about running into randoms strong enemies like trolls and dying, you do know you can run away and dodge right? You know you have a jet pack you can use to fly away quickly? I mean they not exactly hard to miss they HUGE. I personalty love the fact i have to be careful and keep an eye on my surrounding for big beasts makes the game feel more like its setting.Highly recommend this instalment and 47 hours on just 1 play through of this game gives plenty to do.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, ♥♥♥♥ Beserker Rat...seriously. I'd pay for a DLC to get rid of his ass and change my review in a heart beat.Most people don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about immersion in games, but some of us do. _childDocuments_.review: Interesting open world (half magic, half robots) with lots of options for questing, exploring, crafting, developing new skills and choosing your friends. Huge amount of small locations with secrets and collectibles (to give you an idea of the amount of content: there are achievements to unlock 32 region teleporters, to complete 300 quests and to gather 10000 items). Flying is fun as well. Overall it's an enjoyable experience so far. The main drawback I can see is on the hardware requirements: there's an issue with GPU optimization (my beefy RTX card is systematically using 90-100% GPU, even when I set every option to the minimum and I limit framerate by adding vsynch), so I highly recommend it but you'll need a computer that is above average.

Lastly, the npcs in the towns seemed more lifeless to me than in Elix I.Refunded for: poor optimization, and not being able to adjust fov/camera angle.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough, having ploughed my way through every Piranha Bytes game so far. Elex 2 is now my new favourite PB game, even though the Steam reviews were less than stellar. I thought the combat was great. Enemies show little intelligence, simply running towards you, then being aggroed by your companion. But using a blaster or the bow lets you stand off nicely, then when they arrive hit them with a couple of blasts of shotgun.For sure, melee was terrible, seemingly borrowed from the souls genre.The magic was disappointing, but I only tried the berserkers. The fireball is way too slow, and the shield confusing to use, and only available when you have the fireball armed. I ended up regretting my investment in magic, and I resorted to the weapons described above.The story was incomprehensible gibberish, with the most catastrophic outcome for one of the characters raising not an eyebrow from the closest character to them (trying to avoid spoilers here). Dialogue got more and more disjointed and bizarre the longer the game went on, with character motivations hidden beneath several layers of jank. What were the motivations of the main protagonist and antagonists? Well, despite the game throwing enormous amounts of speech my way, I have no idea. I mean, I could tell you what I was told, but it makes ZERO sense.There are many times where the game doesn't explain what to do, forcing the player to think things through. Usually the solution is clear enough, but once or twice I resorted to the Steam forums for help.All in all, a AA title bedeviled by jank, but still worth a shot, especially if you can pick it up cheap (which I did).

Since then, lots have changed in my life, but somethings have never changed. I still run errands to join functions, I steal stuff when people are not looking, when they notice,  they chase me (we usually get over it later), I fire hundreds of arrows to the giant creatures from the top of silly rocks where giants can't climb, I listen stupid dad jokes from NPCs. _childDocuments_.review: Considering it's Piranha Bytes' game, it's very good. Overall, fights are more... diversified comparing to Elex I, and it makes it way more entertaining.Some people here complain about quests being too repeatable, that later in the game you must beat lots of enemies in every quest. It can be treated as weak point, but those fights feel... epic, so I actually like it. They are enjoyable for me at least.It can be quite sad, but animations, facial express, gesture of characters look like from games produced 20 years ago. Actually, I laugh at them a lot, so i would say they are so bad that it makes them beautiful xDImo, world is very interesting, and so are stories hidden behind every location. There are so many quests, so many interesting NPCs to meet, You can feel they've put a lot of work to make this aspect of the game awesome.Overall, If you like to discover in-game world, find some easter-eggs, get to know some plot-wise unimportant characters and simply live the life of game character - it's worth giving Elex II a try.Not many people would say that, but actually I think Elex 2 is better version of what we had in Elex 1.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a new game from Piranha Bytes, which already says a lot. Over the decades of their work, a whole complex of those things for which these guys are loved and scolded have already been formed. The good news is that this game has it all, all their good and bad sides. The plot continues the positive version of the ending of the first part of the game; Jax is sitting in retirement in his house, which soon literally sits on an alien hulk, so now he has to travel around his home planet to his heart's content, uniting disparate factions of people to fight the aliens. The plot is quite worthy until the very end credits (with the exception of some things that happen in 3-4 acts, but we will talk about this below), there are unexpected twists and intrigues in it, and the relative branching of decisions. The planet plays a huge role in the attractiveness of the plot, which is still interesting to explore. The ruins of a former civilization rise above everyone here, as if physically pressing on everyone. Learning the secrets of this vast world is incredibly interesting, and with the use of a jetpack, it’s also not so tiring. The simplest example - the whole game you hear the voice of the announcer from the radio, telling you news, advice, and you get used to it almost like your own. And so you explore the planet and in some wild mountain-forest outback you find the booth of this announcer, tell him about everything that is happening in the factions. It's not part of any quest, you might never have found it if you hadn't explored everything so carefully, and you get the biggest buzz from such little things.The first two acts are amazing, but one cannot help saying that the third and fourth acts of the game are very bad in terms of gameplay decisions, because you are constantly destroying a given number of aliens and everything that causes mechanical irritation at some point. The combat system is a perpetual source of controversy in PB games, and this is no exception. On the one hand, combat with melee weapons obviously gives more advantages (due to the use of crafting gems, the ability to choose between one-handed and two-handed weapons, bonuses for parrying, etc.) On the other hand, parrying here seemed to me even more difficult than usual, to guess the moment of hitting the enemy is very difficult, the requirements for melee weapons are very serious. However, firearms have shotguns. That's all. With a starting regular shotgun, you can get to the very end of the game, I'm not joking. The skill system is very flexible, most of them are quite useful during the game, and there are no problems with this. Secondary activities are just a sea, each partner has his own story, each settlement is simply teeming with surprises. A quest with detective children is generally something completely magical. The graphics are quite good, but the facial animation is a lot of fun, especially for the creepiest kid in the world with the face of a 70-year old man. The game gives exactly what you expect from it, it is a step forward in many ways compared to the first part, although there is no need to embellish its shortcomings. I quite liked the game; now let's see what the creators will prepare for us in the third part.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like they didn't put any effort into making it. I'm sure that isn't the case, but it's how the product feels. If you already own the first Elex game, this won't offer you an experience worth the asking price.Game is stable.I've only seen minor glitches so far.You can now purchase small gems, increasing the chance you'll get to use them.The by far worst offender is the quest system. When you get a subquest to one you're doing (or you get a new one), the game doesn't change to that one. This means when you've talked to npc x and the quest now wants you to get to position y, you first have to open the journal, find the correct quest and click to highlight it. This is especially annoying when you're following someone, as the game doesn't pause when you're in the menus. It feels like an alternate version of the first Elex game instead of a sequel. It has the same factions + 1 and uses the same map.The voice acting and dialog is exceptionally disappointing. Especially considering the high caliber voice actors used. I guess sub par writing and poor voice directing is at play.The illusion of choice is quickly shattered as you're repeatedly offered a variety of dialog options that inevitably result in the same outcome.You meet a lot of the same NPCs you did in the first game, and as such its odd that you have to start from scratch with all of them when building relations. The actions of the previous game should've made some impact.You start the game as the same character you played in the first game. In the intro he's bitten by a creature and gets an infection. Somehow that is enough to justify why he's starting again with minimum in all stats and forgot both how to haggle and pick locks. It's just a shame how poor the story is in this story driven game.Mechanics wise I only have two complaints. The options default to an autoaim assist feature that helps you aim. This would've been good if if all opponents would stand still. But they don't, and the auto aim simply makes sure that while you draw your bowstring, your curser has moved to where the opponent was at the start, and when you release your arrow you'll notice the opponent didn't stop and wait, so you're guaranteed to miss. This feature is great once you get your hands on energy weapons - right click, shoot twice, let go of right click and repeat. That means 100% hit rate unless you've got an invisible hitbox between you and your target (such as a tree or geometry from a rock).The second mechanics thing is that enemies are completely clueless. You talk to a guard who forbids you to enter a place. So you just jetpack above him and he keeps standing there. No issue. And if you have issues in combat just turn a corner. The enemies will almost immidiately forget you were there. Not that you'll run into issues in combat, because opponents aren't properly linked. So you can be in a structure with 20 opponents spaced around one big room. You shoot at one and maybe 2-3 of them come running. The rest ignore the shuffle. When they're dead you move a bit closer and shoot the next opponent or pack. They're completely oblivious to the fact that their friends have just been shot in plain sight. Visuals: I've left everything on default except I turned on vsync (remembered screen tear was an issue in the first game). On default settings the game looks very dated on my system. (12 core, 80 GB ram and rtx 1080).I think it's a bug, but it seems some quests get confused sometimes. I've had a couple where it showed an area on the map, but I was actually supposed to go somewhere else and talk to someone.One more slight annoyance I had with the game is that it took almost 5 hours before I got a popup that told me I could turn on a flashlight. That didn't help much because the default brightness is too low for my monitor, but I'd have liked to know earlier.

_childDocuments_.review:
ELEX II is the sequel to ELEX, the vintage open-world role-playing experience from the award-winning creators of the Gothic and Risen series, Piranha Bytes. ELEX II returns to the post-apocalyptic Science Fantasy world of Magalan with massive environments that can be explored with unrivaled freedom via jetpack, you will be able to move through the epic story any way you want.

Several years after Jax defeated the Hybrid, a new threat arrives from the sky, unleashing the dangerous powers of dark Elex and endangering all life on the planet. In order to defend the peace on Magalan and the safety of his own family, Jax has to go on a mission to convince the factions to unite against the invaders.

Dive into a huge, hand-crafted, completely unique world with multiple factions and diverse environments set in a post-apocalyptic science fantasy universe.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; I recommend the game to space and science fiction fans, those that like a deep atmosphere and those that like unusual approaches to gaming.  But buy it on sale.___________Full Review:Almost like an interactive movie, but produced with computer graphics instead of live action actors and full-blown sets (which would probably have been hellishly expensive in this game).  On the subject of graphics, they are very well done.  The game looks and sounds very authentic according to the video footage I've seen from aboard the real life ISS.  Just like the ISS, there are American/European, Russian, and Chinese wings of the station, each with their own distinct styles.The game is also unusual in that you don't control a human character, instead playing the role of the station AI, who is responsible for looking after station functions and ensuring the survival of the station crew.  Unfortunately, without spoiling too much, at the start of the game, you learn that the station has had some kind of accident and most of your functions are offline and your memory corrupted (isn't it always!).  You gradually have to restore your functions and memory of events prior to the incident as the game progresses, working together with one of the crew members.  In function, it reminds me very much of an old game called "Experience 112" or "The Experiment" by French Developer Lexis Numérique (now defunct) which was set aboard an derelict boat after an accident and you played someone sat in a control room somewhere helping the sole survivor navigate the dangerous environment, following her around using video camera feeds and activating certain functions...  Very similar to this.The story is... weird!  I don't think it will get any medals or anything, there are a few clichés, but it works well with the graphics and sound to produce the overall atmosphere, which is important in this genre and I cannot fault it here.I've seen this described as a horror, but maybe that is a little misleading.  There are absolutely no jump scares and I did not feel tense all the time like I do in say, Amnesia.  There is a sense of dread right from the start, due to the situation on board, but I feel this is more of a game of intrigue than horror.  I did feel compelled to try and work out exactly what had occurred. Is it worth full price?  I think nearly £20 is quite steep as it is very short and once you've seen the ending, there is no replay value, so think about picking it up on sale.  Overall though, if you like space, and science fiction that is quite well grounded in reality, I think you would enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I always hate writing negative reviews for things that I can tell have not only obvious effort, but genuine talent behind them.The story felt like meaningless nothing to me, but we can all chalk that up to me being too stupid to get it. I will say that the characters are certainly flat as a pancake, which the decent voice acting can't change.The graphics are nice, though the 90s VHS camera / CRT monitor display style makes everything grainy and hard to see. The gameplay was completely unsatisfying; you switch between camera viewpoints and/or float around in a sluggish robot ball, solving puzzles that you want to ask what in the name of  they're supposed to simulate on a space station. You also pick up audio logs and documents about the boring, boring, boring crew in order to find out how boring they are.Thinking back now, I'm amazed at how much actually happens in this game, how much you do, and how little it all amounts to.So while I see the potential for a good game coming out of these developers in the future, this one, I just couldn't enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game started really interesting but after experiencing two incredibly frustrating bugs within ten minutes of each other I've decided to refund it. The games premise is you playing as an AI on a computer ship, kind of like HAL 9000 as you try to work out what has happened to the missing crew, the character Emma is a survivor and gives context to the events, this premise was really interesting however after about an hour of play i encountered a bug where i could not leave a mini game menu, i had to quit to the main menu and do the whole scene again.It took about ten minutes to replay but was a minor frustration and i decided I would carry on, now if this was the only bug I could've excused it but withing five minutes of me passing that section i encountered another bug where there was a mini game menu stuck on my screen, there was supposed to be a cutscene playing and instead i just had the cutscene in the background and a giant mini game taking up three quarters of the screen.The only way i could seem to get rid of this screen was to quit out to the main menu, after clicking resume game, i was expected to replay the past 15 minutes of gameplay again, if this was engaging gameplay it wouldn't have been so bad but I was literally just floating round in space. I've decided it was not worth the effort and the story was not engaging enough for me to put up with the constant bugs.This game does seem to have an interesting premise however the seemingly constant bugs means i cannot recommend it. Considering the game has been out a year I don't expect this to get patched.

_childDocuments_.review: Want to play "I Spy", "Simon Says" or follow the procedures in space? Want to see mid 2000s animations to relive the Half-Life 2 breakthrough of G-Man's face? Want to experience a story stuck in the 1960s with little understanding of modern science? If you answered yes to all of these, then this game is for you!I played through this in about 6 hours. I think if it was any longer I wouldn't have made it. The game started off pretty well but once you experience the caliber of puzzles, it quickly sours the experience. The developers were obviously influenced by other works (mostly in film), but they fail to do anything meaningful with the subject matter. There is no clear message or philosophical analysis. Just because you shroud something in mystery doesn't mean it is good. Yes, their shrouding methods were decent, but what they were shrouding was sophomoric at best. There are many other better puzzle games that I would recommend over this one. I can see this game being worth ~$5 but nothing more.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Scifi\Thriller-Horror games in recent memory, short but sweet clocking around 4 to 5 hours to complete, it really sells well the idea of being the Hal 9000 of the Observation space station as you try to help the amazingly voiced Dr.Emma Fisher in surviving the huge ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ she finds herself in.A must play for those that wish a narrative driven experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for an evening or two. Got it as part of a Humble Bundle and got nothing to complain about. A rather unusual concept of an adventure game, which felt like a good change from the usual point and click or walk and click type of games.The atmosphere is amazing and you really feel like you're abandoned on a space station. There are also quite a few interesting collectables to gather that shine some light on the story, which ended up to be pretty good (albeit a bit confusing at the very end). Overall a solid buy if you can get it for a few pounds or dollars.Graphics are good, sound is good, characters are very believable and voice acting is top notch (especially Kezia Burrows who voices Emma). A definite 8/10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting indie game with a decently big feel.  I think if the facial person detail was a wee bit better it would put it over the edge.  I'm glad there were other actual characters in the game and it didn't cop out with "oh they all died" so they only had to render one person.(old indie trick)The good: creepy mystery horror stuff that gradually increases, playing the ship instead of the person on the ship is interesting, figuring things out without a time limit(except some annoying puzzles)The bad: While I like figuring some things out, far too many times I didn't know what to do or how to do it, and often the repeated instruction was something vague like "find me".  The map interface doesn't feel very intuitive and was a bit confusing in its simplicity.  I think some tutorial/direction would be welcome.  Some of the mini-puzzles were frustrating when it doesn't tell you anything and you have 5 seconds to do something complex.I still liked this game overall though and it left a good lasting impression on me.  Having to write some things down like symbols or coordinates actually feels a bit astronauty, so I was okay with that.

_childDocuments_.review: Sounded like an interesting concept at first and, as somebody who reads a lot of science fiction, this seemed like something right up my alley. Unfortunately, the controls are terrible. They're slow, stiff, and make it extremely difficult to navigate the ship. Combine this with obtrusive visuals (computer static, low brightness, and very unappealing and same-y design) made the actual gameplay a slog to get through.I dropped the game before the 2 hour mark and refunded it once I realized this was going to be the next 6 hours of my life if I didn't. After watching the rest on youtube (generously skipping through the slow movement and uninteresting puzzles) just to see whether the story was redeeming, I was still disappointed. I'd rather not get into spoiler territory, so I'll just say that the story seemed as if it were designed more to mind♥♥♥♥ the player with weird and cryptic imagery rather than create any real depth or explore any interesting questions. It's all presentation and no substance.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Short game. Great visuals, effects, and especially the soundtrack. Very mysterious. Great Controls and storytelling. Downside is you complete the game in about 6 hours and have no clue what just happened. If you like films like 2001 Space Odyssey, Arrival, Interstellar then this is surely for you. Don't expect an ending you will understand... Also camera sometimes glitched through walls in cutscenes not sure because I am in 2k or 100+ fps but didn't make too much a difference.  Overall 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: 4-6 hours of a cinematic experience intertwined with some easy puzzle solving gameplay pauses. First issue might be a game breaker - controls. This game was designed for gamepad only, and mouse+kb was added as an afterthought. Some puzzles require precise diagonal stick movement, and mouse cursor has the same inertia applied to it as when the controller is used. The first thing I did after launching this game was to alt+f4 because I thought that it launched in wrong resolution but the discussion forum is full of people asking how to fix mouse controls for last five years. Second issue is my personal nitpick - puzzles are just slowing you down and are boring. Save for a simple simon says game, they all simply require you to find (usually next to the terminal) a piece of paper with a password. Or a software update working as a password. So the only puzzle that there is is a pixel hunt, but with terrible controls.You can also spend some additional time traversing the station, collecting some background data, but it's all inconsequential to your understanding of the story - everything you need to piece together is being fed to you as you progress, and all the background fluff has nothing to do with neither the story not even the world building - eg. you can learn that one person you never get to see likes another person that never got mentioned. Wow.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: A well-spent six hours. It's been criticised for being too short, but to my mind it's designed to be like playing a movie, so six hours is a good length for the experience.It does have a few minor technical issues - it wouldn't switch to 1080p on my 1440p monitor no matter what I did, but my GTX970 managed a decent framerate at that res and the game looked fantastic to boot so I wasn't too worried. It also seems to have been designed for gamepad - the keyboard controls are a bit awkward at times, and mouse movement in first-person view is kind of mushy, but those sections are more walking simulator than FPS so again not really that much of an issue.Otherwise a very polished game - great graphics and effects, the story had enough pull to keep me interested, the puzzles were fun if a little easy, and the setting felt authentic enough to carry it all.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Uninstalled without completing.It's simply one of the least fun games I've ever played on PC. The controls are absolutely awful. Forget KB+M, there's no way this is playable without a controller. And even then the controls are just stunningly bad. It's without doubt and by far the worst 6-degrees-of-movement implementation that I've ever seen in a game.The game itself is a walking simulator. I've no issues with that (two of my favourite games from the last three years are walking simulators) but combined with such a diabolical control system this is just boring, dull and frustrating. Other reviews say that story is good so I'll need to take their word for it but the first couple of hours certainly didn't grip me.The puzzles themselves are also fairly simple. The main problem is figuring out which part of the 2D interface the game wants you to press or which trigger/button to hold down. Most puzzles are variants on pressing the buttons in the order that the game tells you to (once you figure out what it wants you to do of course), or remembering a sequence of things or what path you need to follow on a grid. Or they're timed puzzles with an interface that you have to figure out. After 3-4 attempts of watching the timer countdown and repeating your actions you figure it out. They're like the mini-puzzles that you hate in otherwise great games, and that's all that Observation offers. Wholly uninspired.Oh, and the save-points are hopeless. You might think that "after a cut scene" would be a good place to put a save-point but oh no they just appear to be arbitrary. Which means you'll need to repeat the frustrating travelling around bit and the puzzle that you didn't really enjoy in the first place yet again.The graphics and soundtrack are good (the sound is tremendous in fact, great voice acting and environmental sounds), giving the game a good ambience. Beyond that it's been a long time since I had as little good to say about a game as this one. The game play is astonishingly tedious; I'd just rather read a book with this story than be forced to play this. I'm mystified as to the high rating the reviewers are giving it.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend it for being from a different sort what makes it interesting to play, acting sort like HAL and following orders, go here, seek that, activate this one and be obedient, that make fun for a while and keep upright the atmosphere, using the orb is ok as long you stay inside the station, space floating at the other end is complicated and easy to get lost though, the story does along well but only in the first half, than it derails into something what is not expected nor vital nor realistic either but this is point of view of the individuals. I has a bit from 'Deliver us the moon' but it cannot reach this level, however- the exploring of the station and following the story, moving cams, solving puzzles so as being a little helper dd entertain me.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game about controlling an AI on a space station.Looks great and plays great, with a quite intriguing story from a perspective that's quite refreshing!A bit on the short side, clocking in at 4-5 hours unless you go for all achievements.Due to being very story focused, it obviously doesn't have that much replay value.Runs great on Linux using Proton.I wholeheartedly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I love how it visualizes living in a space station. other than that the game was mediocre. story was ok. not mind-blowing nor was it emotionally moving. just ok, mediocre sci-fi. gameplay was cool at first being an AI then becomes tedious and kinda confusing. no music that i remembered. one and done kind of game. i probably wont play it ever again and will forget i played it. it was decent but not memorable. i'd still recommend it for sci-fi/space enthusiasts when it's on sale.3/5
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: No ultrawide support, they even patched out the manual fixes. Mouse controls have an awful filter on them, a max cursor speed too. Ingame camera moves like a snail with time sensitive tasks that you have to look around to do. Got completely stuck 20 minutes in right after the fire when you have to "scan the damage" but not a single thing in the room is interactable, not even the fire damage.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: The story was ok but the gameplay is awful. The controls are frustrating and the "puzzles" are basically just straightforward directions. Feels like being forced to go through a tedious to-do list while using a handicapped robot.  I stuck through it and finished but the pay off was not worth the effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I don't feel like this game's story is very original, often confusing, and generic. The gameplay is neat being in first person and being the ships computer system. Navigating the station and figure out what you need to do is very often confusing and more often frustrating. Nothing is as intuitive as it should be. I was almost at the end of the game, where I needed to contact Earth when I finally called it. I was just not having fun and was not interesting in the story nor did I care how it ended. I can't imagine wanting to play this a 2nd time for achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this one - it's pretty short, but has a great story (lots of 2001 and another space movie vibes) and some unique gameplay, especially being from the AI's point of view.That said - you more or less *must* play this with a controller. There is a puzzle in the intro that's borderline impossible without one, and mouse and keyboard just feel incredibly unnatural for scooting around in your magic spaceball (and I say this as someone who greatly prefers mouse/keyboard).The worst issue, however, was the fact - at least for me - that it refused to stay at the resolution (1920x1080) that I set it to. It changes on it's own all the time. You'll notice things seem fuzzy and it's because it's dropped the resolution for...reasons. Aside from that annoyance, it didn't have any other technical problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never buy games without first checking out reviews on mainstream websites. With Observation though, I saw it pop up in my recommendation feed and took a chance on it - and I'm really glad I did! I found the story to be gripping without getting overly dark or resorting to jump scares. I think I read some user reviews remarking that they found the puzzles too easy. If you consider yourself some Mensa-level logic puzzle solver, then yes, perhaps you won't be challenged by the puzzles. As a person who just likes to enjoy a pleasantly interactive narrative, I found the puzzles just challenging enough to make me feel I'm actively contributing to the action without being so inscrutable that it ground everything to a halt while I beat my head against a wall. I really enjoyed the detail that was put in to every aspect of the station design. It really felt like it could have been a working and lived-in space station. You pick up the odd bit of station drama through a version of audio logs. These aren't too plentiful and it doesn't bog the game down. I went in to the game expecting a short playtime and was not surprised when I finished it in 6 hrs. The story is completely linear, in the style of a walking simulator. Areas are gated and unlocked simply by progressing the story. You could consider this a sort of enhanced walking simulator with 6DOF controls and some light puzzle solving. As such, there is little replay value in the game.All-told, I feel I got my money's worth and would recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Strongly recommend this if you enjoy narrative art.  I've seen elsewhere this game compared to "2001: A Space Odyssey if you played HAL", and I similarly support that comparison.  The symbolic language is very smartly done.  The culmination of the story is trippy in a way that takes a bit of time afterward to process.  I still have a few questions, but I'm satisfied that the game's narrative was adept at provoking such questions.Small technical comment: this plays best with a controller.  Keyboard and mouse are workable, but I found less UI friction with the controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game in around 6 hours in one sitting. Some people claim 4 hours is possible, I can however only see that happening if you're replaying it.Generally speaking, it's a nice idea, but it has a few shortfalls:Pros:- Sci-Fi- Nice Graphics- Good sound design & voice acting- Interesting conceptCons:- Mouse sensitivity is off the charts. Make sure you adjust it.- Basic controls could do with an introduction (or are they meant to be part of the puzzle?) - R for Response is one!- Some puzzles could do with some kind of hint after a certain time- Cut scenes can not be skipped and go on for a bit too long (I know it was done to add more suspense, but it becomes annoying rather fast)- Replayability It can be interesting to try and figure things out by ones self, but at certain points it just became tedious.Replayablility has to be my main gripe: There is no real reason to replay this game. There are no alternative endings, no hidden subplots, no actions that would change the outcome. Not as far as I am aware, that is. Of course I could try and complete SAMs memory, but why should I, if it does not affect anything within the game. Many characters hardly appear at all, and thus there is no interest to find out more about them. Overall I do still recommend this game if you can get it on sale. It's better than average. but because of its potential, I felt let down.I just wish it did more and was more fleshed out. Someone who gets storytelling right: the developer Quantic Dream comes to mind. Unfortunately, this doesn't come close.My Score: 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Strange, Interesting, and had me totally engrossed.The puzzles are simple, the real challenge is learning to navigate the computer system. There's not much "gameplay" in the traditional sense, this is more of an interactive experience.The story is really interesting, weird mind-bending sci-fi stuff with some creepy moments, I'm a sucker for that kind of thing.Played through the whole thing in one sitting without realising, so it's not very long. Left me with some questions but I guess some things are better left a mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Got this on sale for like $7. Well worth it at that price. Neat story and the way you play is pretty cool. My only real gripe is that the puzzles are pretty straight-forward, was hoping for a little more of a challenge there. But the graphics and sound are great, in general the atmosphere of the game will keep most players pretty tense for the hours it takes them to complete. I played through a few times because there are some collectibles you don't have to find to finish, but you do need to get all the back/sidestory. Once you've done that, though, there isn't really any replay-ability. Maybe some minor dialog changes? I tried to do things differently, but it did not seem to affect any outcomes. Maybe I missed a super-secret ending or something? I dunno'...Bottom line: I'd say very worth it for $15 or less; it's an enjoyable interactive sci-fi movie and you get to play as HAL... I mean SAM. If that sounds appealing, you'd probably enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t beat many games but I did beat this one overall the game is short it is up to you but there is no replayability no branching paths, no player choice, this is at best a pilot or a screenplay for a tv or movie that got turned in to “game”. While this is not a bad walking simulator is most certainly is one. I do bet you could write a complicated macro or python script to play this whole “game”. You get the sense that this was a great vertical slice to what could have been a cool game and Sony gave the devs a bucket of money and no direction.Its held back by a host of technical limitation with the port, after beating the game I saw the tag “controller game” and that is so right as a mouse and keyboard player so much is wanting. Overall the game shines in some parts, the design of the space station is good visually, if the functionality of some parts seems odd, you can see they were going for just slightly futuristic and hit that mark several times. Each mission partner who contributed parts to the station have a different flare and feel. Story / Narrative Overall the game is extremely odd, much of the narrative is "hidden" until you reach part of the story where its explained all at once. This game takes itself so seriously like it is being directed by Michael Bay, it starts building this tension which falls flat over and over again as issues in the gameplay wreck the pacing. There are two “attempts” at jump scares that fall to elicit any reaction for the player and kill the tension again. Where the game gets it right however is the voice acting of SAM and Emma Fisher, the interplay between the characters is great, you are immediately are invested in Emma’s goals and feel like you are the only one who can help her. This is nearly on the level of Booker and Elizabeth from BioShock 3 without the odd overtones and is truly remarkable for a game of this size and scope. The rest of the story is lacking and ultimately unfulfilling with twists the player can see from miles away.GameplayYou play as the AI that is supposed to be running the station but something bad happens and you are disconnected. At first, you play through what is on the surface interesting set of tasks but by hour 2 of this you rely upon nothing you do matters there is no time limit, there is no fail state, nothing you do affects other than move the store to its pre-programmed end. The verisimilitude is broken right when you reach a door the devs don’t want you to go through, a laptop that is on but you can't connect to, a peace of the station that is working and you have access to but nothing happens. This is so clearly shown when you try to connect to something when you are in sphere mode but it will not let you, no they want you to go right to the camera and zoom in with it and connect that way. There are many objectives you will have to do that involve, go to compartment X and look for small peace of glowing equipment, do a QTE and click a button, now do that 3 more times. You might get a puzzle but that is it. The quick-time events are the main gameplay mechanic like its on a PS1. Not that this game needs combat but later in the game you get a “boost” for your sphere thing and its so nice, not only can you go places faster but it gives you something to do along the way. THAT IS THE PROGRESSION. Lots of Hidden BS to make you think you will learn stuff, some of the stuff is nice and gives you a though on the daily life of the crew members before but it is not rewarding whatsoever. The worst part is that there is one cutscene where you are going through space and it could have some amount of gameplay, but they make it a cutscene, this happens over and over again. You are a camera all you can do is move around and look at things and the devs take that away for them to give you the next thing in the story. There is just enough useless stuff in the UI when you are looking around that you feel the need to look at everything but can interact with nothing. You can open some doors, you can hack some doors, some you just can't for some reason. Anything that you do that is not on the devs checklist of stuff to do is impossible. There are several times where you can tell the devs were writing something just to be vague, you will ask for the instructions to be repeated but they just say the exact thing again to you no clarification no extra detail. Technical The game struggles to make 60 FPS in cutscenes where are 70% of the game. The number pad does not work for number input. The movement in 3 dimensions is fine but THERE IS NO FOV SLIDER, so you get tuned around supper easily and feel like you’re going to vomit. The articulation of the MC in whatever form you are in is painfully slow, your light is on or off you can’t control it.  Overall this game could have been a game but its not it’s a walking simulator with a cute setting an OK MC and quality voice acting. The writing seems to think we spent 40 hours on backstory and know what is going on, the games last 1/3 is piecemeal at best and the final revival is so any climatic that you will think you are missing something. I looked your not its just a poorly written game with QTEs. Buy better games than this
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game because it offers quite a unique experience. Its big selling points, in my opinion, are:* a captivating sci-fi mystery in the veins of 2001: A Space Odyssey or Interstellar,* suspenseful storytelling that reveals just enough about what's going on to keep you guessing what it all means,* engaging presentation, especially with regards to your interactions with the various ship systems.If you're looking for challenging puzzles or interesting gameplay however, you've come to the wrong place. Some reviews complain that the controls for the various ship systems you have to interact with are awkward. While that is true, I thought that this was done rather purposefully and that the awkward controls actually added to the immersiveness of these parts of the game. On the other hand, the parts of the game where you have to navigate through the ship, I just found plain tedious.Still, it just took me 7-8 hours to finish the game and I thought the story and presentation were well worth the occasionally bad gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I feel stupid, should've dropped this game, watched the ending on YouTube and laughed it off.Instead, I got baited by the intriguing beginning of a story, only to end up spending 5-6 hrs playing one of the most tedious games I've seen in my life. And of course the rest of the story didn't deliver any joy or make much sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: The game is downright beautiful. Respectable voice acting. But, it's pretentious as all hell and not even close to worthy of the praise it's received from major entertainment companies. It's worth it on sale, but that's it. Did I enjoy it? Sort of. The 'puzzles' were not engaging at all. I would call almost all of them memory puzzles, very akin to 'simon says'. I went into this game thinking I would solve the mysteries of what happened to my crew, but that's answered very quickly and the game takes a turn from sci-fi to fantasy nonsense very quickly.The ending went full cop-out mode with "leaving it up to the player's interpretation". And not with any kind of Scorsese flair; it becomes fully obvious they had no real path for the story and want to leave it up to you to fill in the gaps they couldn't have been bothered with.It really reminds me of Interstellar. Starting off as a potentially brilliant sci-fi adventure, only to ham it up at the payload and turn into 4th demension space ghost nonsensse.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Got gifted the game by a Duckling. Had heard good things about it & was already curious.First things first:• Awesome ingenuity of UI, level- & gameplay-design.• Great Voice Acting & Narrative format• Visuals are great (read below, though)• Good value for moneyNow, some pointers to watch for:• The visuals are sadly often obscured too much, to enjoy them. Flimsy grain-stuff (can be turned off), the light from the flashlight is so white, that you cant actually read anything you point at with it. Might be authentic, but it also ads to the visual "pollution" this game suffers from. The graphics are good, but they are often immaterial, because you cant see things properly. Its like having glasses with the wrong perscription-strength. Really exhausted the eyes too. Its NOT a game-breaker at all. But yeah, wish it was better.• The mission-arc & mini-game-focus is the whole idea of the game, I feel. And it works really well. I had a few things I had trouble solving, because its almost 100% intuitive, at times. Which leaves us trying weird things to solve it. Is that a bad thing? Maybe for some. If youre a stickler for easy gameplay & simple minigames, where you dont have to think too much, this game will probably frustrate you.There ARE ways of making it easier (look ofr guides etc.) but yeah, it CAN be a little frustrating, because the game offers very little help. Youre an AI & are supposed to know what to do! ;-)Over-all a great experience for me & the Pond to play through. Loved it & hope there will be more of this design in a future IP.

_childDocuments_.review: Observation is a great thriller science fiction game mixed with puzzle features,here the player control Sam a artificial intelligence who follow the aventure of Emma through cameras or the sphere that we can control. Overall, i think that the story is mysterious, even stresseful somehow because we are lost in space and on this point the atmosphere is efficient. However the control are kinda weird, i recommend to play to game with a controler and sometimes you can get lost which is kinda annoying but the puzzles aspect is enough challenging without being to difficultSo if you like space aventure, with a little bit of horror, and a strong story this game is for you !

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw the trailer I got a really strong 2007 Space Odyssey vibe.And it was not what I expected. It was better.The setting is phenomenal, the graphics are gorgeous and the puzzles are ok (I'm dumb, so it took some time with some of them). The story got me really hooked from start to finish.Can't recommend to buy it full price but you should definitely buy it on promos.10/10 didn't understand the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... Pretty good. Worth playing, certainly, and some of the environments are the most engaging I've ever seen. Mechanically it builds a really nice, slow atmosphere, holding the player back in ways that really make you appreciate what No Code crafted, but this is one of those games that I played a little bit at a time over a long while, and I'm kind-of glad I paced it out that way, otherwise I would probably have gotten annoyed by some of the movement mechanics.Important note if you're playing on mouse and keyboard: Right Click + W/D to go Up/Down in the sphere, respectively. I didn't see that mentioned anywhere in the game.
