_childDocuments_.review: This game is a nod to Stanley Kubrick’s , tribute is clearly paid via both presentation and narrative. While the game stays loyal to the intrinsic nature of the classic, it does bring unique and interesting design as a translation into game media.Compare to the actual film, this game is better described as a thriller rather than a sci-fi. Much of this is due to a more realistic and relatable space setting. If you have watched real life clips of inside the ISS, you can immediately realize how detailed and believable the in-game environment and props are, that alone adds a lot to overall atmosphere and hence immersion.Gameplay blends well with the plot. Playing as an AI provides an unusual perspective with a lot of restrictions: interaction with non-player characters is minimal; movement is often limited; background information and lore are fragmented. Interestingly, such restrictions help to build immersion while playing as an AI. Throughout the game some tasks and puzzles can be quite mechanical. This mechanical feel also greatly contributes to the non-human characteristic of an AI.If you are a fan of , or interested in topics like space and extraterrestrial life, or even remotely intrigued by discussion about AI, evolution and existentialism, you will definitely find this game an enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: While Observation does have some downfalls stemming from obvious budget, teamsize or time constraints, this gem still delivers greatly in atmosphere and storyYou play as SAM, an integrated ai of the observation space station in orbit around earth. As the game begins you have lost all data about the objective of the stations mission, the whereabouts of the crew members and most of the stations systems are shut down or severely damaged. Accompanying on of the crew members, Emma, you try to figure out what exactly happened to you, the station and the crew members, while also trying to stabilize the stations systems. While following Emmas commands, you piece together evidence and resolve the whole mystery, up to the satisfying but somewhat ambigious ending.That is basically all I want to say about the story without spoiling any of the twists and turns the player awaits.I wish the developers would have refrained from spoiling some elements too early, but I guess they were afraid of expecting too much from their audience. Shame really, but still, it works.Just with the last title of No Code (Stories untold) the atmosphere of Observation is amazing, especially considering the small team that developed this title. They used the ressources they had in such clever ways that the whole becomes greater than the sum of it's parts. Your sorroundings feel realistic and claustrophobic while envoirenmental sounds sell the feeling on being on a defunct space station. There are elements of Hard Sci-Fi as well as Cosmic Horror and at certain points the game really dives into the whole horror aspect by limiting your actions while drifting around in small cramped and confusing corridors. It's amazing, how confusing to navigate these samey looking corridors can get, when you can rotate freely in all 3 dimensions and there is no clear indication what is up and what is down. That may sound annoying, but it works wonders for the tension and atmosphere.The Gameplay is limited in a lot of ways, but works for the theme and the story. As the ships AI, Emma will give you clear commands of what to do and you have to basically complete minigames and smaller puzzles to fix systems or switch on modules to further progress in the story. You mostly look and operate from the stations integrated camera network so you'll have to navigate the station by switching from camera to camera and work with their semifixed angles to get a picture of everything there is to interact with. Apart from minigames and a lot of data you can read to gain back your recollection of prior events, you can also communicate with Emma by looking at things that might be of interest to her and telling her about it. At some points you'll also gain control of small drones which you can use to freely roam around the sections and even leave into outer space to check out the outside of the station and assess the damage.While none of this is groundbreaking or even terrifyingly engaging, the menues and sounds are so atmospherically integrated, that I always looked forward to the next system I had to fiddle around with and see, how I am supposed to interact with it. Again there is a downside to all of this in the developers being clearly afraid, that there audience might be too dense and will fail. I found all of the puzzles to be too easy and just on one occasion I was a bit clueless how to solve the task and got the solution just 1 or 2 minutes later on. Still: At every single terminal I opened and every system I interacted with, I giggled like a little child with all those clunky Interfaces that feel like they were ripped straight from the first Alien movie in aesthetics and sounds and I had a lot of fun figuring out what all those beeping buttons do or what sound that chunky switch might produce. If you are a fan of that kind of thing, Observation will be heaven.Eh, the controls are fine, but they could be much better. The fixed camera rotations feel too slow while also being a bit too choppy when trying to hit a very specific detail. The drone movement also feels kinda spongey while also not selling the floating motion of zero gravity as well as I'd liked. I think those issues are fair to critize, but I feel like those shortcomings aren't detrimental to the overall experience of the story.One thing I did like about the controls is they way you interact with the stations subsystems in the minigames. There are some interesting utilization of the same keys with holding down and releasing keys in a specific manner. Again: Nothing groundbreaking, but quite fun.Presentation is a mixed bag. The graphics quality overall is objectively speaking nice, but don't expect AA or even AAA levels of grapical fidelity. Again considering the price tag and the team behind it, I actually am amazed in some scenes and wonder, how they could pull off something so impressive. The lighting in the game is great and helps further the claustrophobic atmosphere and can instill some panic in the player, while the character animations are surprisingly okay. I did spot a lot of clipping issues though: Emma putting her leg partially through a wall in a cutscene or parts of her equipment, while physically animated to behave like they would in zero gravity, floating inside of her body. Again: None of that is all that detrimental to the overall experience, but it shows, that maybe the scope of the game was a bit too much for a small team and they could have used with some more budget/time on those issues.Apart from all my nitpicking, there are some truly spectacular aspects to the presentation: I cannot overstate how amazing the sound design is in this game. Again as with their previous title, the sounds in this game are incredible and most of the thick atmosphere and the effectivity of it's cosmic horror elements can be attributed to just the sound. I cannot go into more detail for spoiler reasons, but there are certain situations in the game, where the sounds transcends the overall experience to feel like a much higher budgeted production.There are also some spectacular camera shots that feel like arthouse cinema at it's best. The direction is truly to be applauded in those instances and there is one shot in the game, that tells so much story without saying a word, just by showing something, that makes the player feel uneasy and give context to everything that has happened.This is the point where a lot of people will decide to not buy the game. As with any storydriven "adventure"-type game, there is not much replay value to be had and the whole thing is over in 4-6 hours. While I can understand the issue some people have in spending 15-20 € for a short game with no replay value, I still think, that a highly engaging and well made story of that length is worth that kind of price. If you like Sci-Fi movies like 2001, Sunshine or maybe Interstellar, you'll definitely enjoy this little gem and I'd recommend it, even at full price.PROSCONS

_childDocuments_.review: An imitative and unfun interactive narrative that barely stretches the boundaries of the science fiction genre, suffering from awkward controls, lousy minigames, irritating puzzles, and ubiquitous tediousness.Positive:- Manipulating various cameras around the station is mostly interesting as events advance, regardless of it not being a novel mechanic. Even if pointing and panning is a slow procedure, exploring the environments in this voyeuristic mode is uncanny and promotes the opportunity of stationary yet gradual visual investigation.- In terms of setting and location, all surroundings look good, while being presented in a purposely austere fashion for establishing an ominous mood. With that said, each and every area appears very similar, generating a semblance of lonely repetitiveness, which is likely to be intentional.- Pervading in all aspects of gameplay is a simulated operating system that is a pleasure to behold and to employ, complete with command line interface loading screens and with a functional graphical user interface needed to fulfill many processes and to achieve technical objectives.Neutral:- Although the game is moderately optimized on "ultra" quality, constantly vacillating in frames per second, it averages about 55, with frequent dips into the 20s. This may or may not be a result of the hardware used for the basis of this review.- The plot is ordinary, coursing through previously explored notions and ideas from decades ago in film and in literature. Unfortunately, there is not enough being presented that is atmospherically fascinating or intellectually profound. As the details of the tale are unraveled and eventually revealed, each intimation is unexceptional and every twist is unoriginal. There is nothing in the story that is clever, imaginative, or innovative.- While rare, crashes do happen. There does not seem to be any way to prevent this. Thankfully, the save file is able to survive the occurrence without corruption.- Albeit serviceable after a period of becoming accustomed with how the physics and interfacing work, the controls remain awkward and unwieldy throughout the whole experience, as they were clearly made for console gamepads instead of mouse and keyboard. Negative:- Activating devices and utilizing them requires one's attention and response by means of minigames and quick time events that feel fake and arbitrary. Such interactions with the environment are a detriment to immersion as the playable character is a sentient artificial intelligence that is capable of interfacing with physical and electronic systems digitally without any corporeal bureaucracy or any external intervention, yet entirely manual actions are demanded of them in order to complete tasks. Accordingly and consequently, all minigames and quick time events are dull and trite, serving as reminders that such activities being performed by the playable artificial intelligence are wholly redundant and absurd within context of the circumstances.- There is no genuine logic for the human non-playable character to completely rely on the assistance of the station's sentient artificial intelligence. The dynamic between the two characters seems nonsensical and unnecessary, creating a prevalent factor of asininity in the conditions of their working relationship.- For being such an advanced artificial intelligence playable character, their navigational capabilities are extremely limited and rudimentary, especially during extravehicular activities. There is absolutely no sensible reason why such basic technology is inaccessible to a system that is so seemingly sophisticated.- Despite not being a traditional point and click adventure game, actuating devices, systems, switches, as well as other mechanical or virtual items necessitates the equivalent of three–dimensional quasi-pixel hunting. The same premise also persists when attempting to locate items scattered throughout the game world.- Saving the game happens strictly on checkpoints established by the developers. This means that if one has to quit the game before a checkpoint is reached, progress will certainly be lost. This is a huge problem that wastes a lot of time. Additionally, previously watched cut scenes cannot be skipped, further wasting one's time unnecessarily due to a poor design choice.- Sleuthing around the station, collecting clues, servicing machineries, administrating systems, and ultimately accomplishing a variety of jobs is almost always unintuitive, making for an utterly annoying, unsatisfying, boring, and extremely frustrating experience.- Subtitles do not always match the spoken lines, even though this occurs relatively rarely. The writing itself is simple and uninspired, with the commentaries and conversations sounding commonplace and conventional. Unfortunately, the text contains many apostrophe errors, indicating that the writing received little to no proofreading and editing. For a game that focuses tremendously on its narrative, this is totally unacceptable.- Too many of the puzzles are unclear in their presentations and ambiguous in their solutions, causing severe confusion and uncertainty. The game world does not provide the player with a suitable amount of information and an accessible set of characteristics of the working particulars for approaching its various conundrums. As the sentient artificial intelligence in charge of assisting in all aspects of running a space station smoothly, there is nearly a complete lack of coherent and realistic connections between possessing an understanding of systems and the competency for resolving dilemmas in a way that makes sense within the framework of the situation.Overall rating: 2.5/5.0

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted a trip to Saturn for £20? Then Observation is for you. Even a space enthusiast like me hasn't played many games set in space, and I've played fewer still which let me take control of the AI in command of the station. Think of all the games which have you avoid or outwit automated security (Thief, System Shock 2, Deus Ex etc) and Observation turns that concept on its head brilliantly well, doing a good job of actually simulating how being the computer would actually feel like. Overall this game really surprised me, even more so for the fact the movement around the station feels suitably awkward and weightless like it would in real life. There's no sci-fi gravity which keeps you on the floor like there is in the spaceships in Tacoma or System Shock. There's a quite jarring disconnect between the sumptuous photorealistic visuals from the view of the camera or command sphere when looking around the station, and the archaic, arcane user interfaces you see when you need to solve puzzles as the AI to operate electronics. That's probably one of the reasons why playing as the computer in this game feels so unique and quite strange. Along the way you can hack into laptops to extract logs and files which fill in some of the backstory, and also obtain crucial schematics and diagrams which help you use stuff like door locks or coolant systems. Before you start, be aware that you need to press R to go into response mode, to answer the crew member's requests. All the effort in getting used to the game's mechanics is worth it just for seeing those magnificent views of the solar system's most awesome planet.

_childDocuments_.review: An atmospheric, oppressive creation that channels 2001:A Space Odyssey , Interstellar, Alien and any other Sci-Fi that leans in that wobbly middle ground between 'Hard Sci-Fi' and 'Science Fantasy', Observation is a great (albeit flawed) experience.This is essentially a walking simulator, or rather a 'floating and rotating' simulator as you play as the station computer rather than a human. This novel twist adds to the claustrophobic nature, and the UI design is brilliantly unique though occasionally obtuse. Visually it's fantastic, and the environments are very detailed and quite authentic seeming. The character models are almost, but not quite, brilliant. Some of the facial animation just seems a little off, and combined with the occasionally awkward vocal delivery it's a bit jarring at times. On a technical level you've got a lot of graphical options, although bizarrely the resolution scale caps off at 2560 x 1440, so if you've got an ultrawide monitor you're SOL. Furthermore, even at that resolution some of the scenes get broken as you can see around the 'edges' of whatever is going on, spoiling some of the effect.If you can keep yourself honed in on the story then you'll be in for a treat, but if you stop to consider it's walking simulator roots then you'll find yourself wondering at the lack of dramatic impetus. It doesn't really *matter* how fast you do anything, regardless of what the game is telling you, and one moment near the end of the game is rendered fairly comical if you stop to think about why no-one is really reacting to anything you do.That said, if you overlook the blemishes there's a great, creative story here that's told well and will send a chill down your spine more than once.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brilliant.The story, the atmosphere, the gameplay, it all fits together to form an amazing experience to play through.Honestly, I wouldn't categorise this as a horror game. It creates a dark atmosphere that grips you by the throat and forces you to watch events unfold, more stressful than scary.The idea of playing the perspective of an AI is executed perfectly, making you do tasks as ordered while also being able to show hints of sentience. Personally the graphics and animation seemed pretty good to me, and honestly this is probably the first game where I turned on post-processing filters like film grain and chromatic aberration, which complement the game really well compared to others that throw them in an attempt to look advanced.If you hate using your brain to play games then you will absolutely hate the game, but unlike others I loved how you would sometimes spend up to 10 minutes to figure out how to do a simple task, it really immersed me in the world of the game as I had to observe every small detail of the station within the restrictions that I had. I doubt this will be the same for others as most probably got extremely frustrated.Only gripe I have is how there's some segments where you have toand it literally gives you zero directions, that was something that I spent so much time on that I ended up having to search it up. Apart from that I experienced zero bugs or glitches during my playthrough.Personally I felt that the ending was great, it didn't completely wrap everything up so that you are left wondering what it means, however it ended in a satisfying enough way that answered all the initial questions posed at the start of the game.That doesn't mean that I don't want a sequel though.Please make a sequel, you will receive all my support and also all of my money.

_childDocuments_.review: On the technical side: The game does not support wide screen resolutions and can only run in 16x9 or 16x10 resolutions. Also, for some reason, the game resets its resolution randomly to minimum (like 1024*768 or similar ancient ones). This is very annoying as texts become hard to read. The game itself doesnt suffer too much from low resolutions as it looks like just another glitch in S.A.M.'s cameras. But still, it's annoying.The gameplay is unique at least. Controlling the game via the station's systems is interesting, and the narrative style very immersive. In the end, there are too many things unclear, and the game feels somewhat unfinished.Many of the puzzles that need to be solved are repetitive and either very easy or have unclear instructions resulting in failures. The puzzles can be repeated until solved, and those that are not repeatable don't seem to alter the course of the story. The controls are obviously made for consoles and don't feel natural on keyboard and mouse.Overall, I enjoyed the story for the first half, then the game kind of lost me

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this is the first game I've seen that models a realistic space station! It's nothing like what you'd see on Star Trek or Star Wars, it's more like the ISS in a few decades. The amount of detail that went into the various station stations just blew my mind. Some have a DOS era interface, one looks like a router from the early 2000s, and overall you get the feeling of multiple systems jammed into one station with laptops and cables stuck to every wall (just like in the ISS).One of the most atmospheric games I've played in a really long time.Story is also great, delivered in a fast pace where if you read some background info you find lying around, it's only a few sentences as opposed to a few pages.Only thing to improve would be the saving mechanism, I'd like to be able to save whenever I want.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Still playing, but overall it is a good, interesting game.  Problem I have is that there is NO Save.  There is a checkpoint saves, but I would like to see at least an option to save to current progress, I don't care to see multiple save options - just the current progress.  Multiple times I didn't notice the checkpoint save icon, and next time I restarted from earlier point.I suspect that some people do "like" that there are no saves, but I think this game does not have reason not to have an option to save the current progress.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Played through in one sitting in 6.5 hours. Story is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Idea, UI, visuals are really great. Scripted scenes are way too long and there are some continuity errors. Character animations are a bit chonky. I really hated that interactable objects were unlocked while you progressed, that way I didn't know I can interact with [OBJECT] and couldn't solve a puzzle. Movement is extremely slow. This and the drawn-out scenes means this game isn't really 6.5 hours long but shorter.Worth the price of 20,99 €? Well, it kept me busy for 6.5 hours. Would I buy it again? Definitely not.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: The game gave me strong Space Odyssey 2001 vibes. The atmosphere is great and there is plenty of attention to detail. From the way interior of module looks to every single VFX sound. Made me feel like I am in space together with all the astronauts. The only thing visually that stood out as not on the same level was when there were scenes with closeup on face. The face animation felt very stiff and I didn't see much expression of Emma Fisher.The story was fantastic. When it comes to puzzles unfortunately I was stuck few times and one time I had to check gameplay video. Turned out there was one important note that I didn't pay attention to because it was too blurred. If I set my gameplay in higher resolution from the beginning it wouldn't be an issue. But despite all those small cons I would still recommend this game to all the space and sci-fi fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this if you're not using a QWERTY keyboard.I'm using an AZERTY keyboard and even after rebinding the keys (A<>Q and W<>Z, so WASD becomes ZQSD) there were too many hardcoded prompts and keys that made the game annoying.What made me eventually refund is the timed minigames where the hardcoded keys just made it so much harder than it needed to be.Why allow for keybinds yet still have a ton of hardcoded keys/prompts ?
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I quick and immersive puzzle game with horror elements where you take the role of a space station AI. It does a good job making you really feel like the AI and feeding breadcrumbs of a larger story over time. The horror elements add atmosphere without taking over the game and rushing the player. Not worth the full price, but a good pick up on sale!TLDR: Scary Myst in space
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: i really really liked this game! it was super fun to have to think outside the box, to really listen to instructions, and maneuver around the ship.  i was able to complete the game without any walkthroughs or tutorials, so dont believe the reviews that say that its impossible without one.  Funnily enough, im a person that gets confused easily, and even i was able to get through it.  The people who complain about the puzzles are people who want instant gratification and are basically looking for something to hold their hand through it.  sure, some of the puzzles can be a bit frustrating, but it makes them all the more rewarding to get through and figure out.  I kinda like how the game doesn't tell us how to do things, it pretty much gives you the controls, gives you a story, and objectives.  plus, its not like you're completely in the dark, you gotta listen to emma's instructions, what shes saying is basically already telling you what to do.  Its a hard game, but its rewarding, i highly recommend this game if you want a challenge with fantastic graphics, and an immersive environment!This game isnt an action game, its a sci-fi puzzle thriller, its exciting in its own way.    yes, the camera is slow, and clunky, youre an ai living in a code.  Youre not no action hero!  No Code makes games that force you to sit and think.  You gotta be okay with being puzzled and confused, be okay with clicking around, be okay with not getting it on the first try, be okay with being frustrated.  isnt that what lifes about anyways? i mean, if life was that easy, we'd all be living the way we wanted to lolAnyways, get this game, its so fun, download it!
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: My god this game is under-recognised as hell. The story is awesome, and there is always something new happening. The graphics are pretty good, but the atmosphere and bgm brings it all together. For something by an indie company, the game is incredibly polished.The game tends to drop you head first into solving puzzles, which I like. It doesn't feel like I'm being instructed step by step.Sometimes it's hard to get around the station, and you'll probably get lost at least once, needing to rely on the waypoints it gives you when you do. The game is also a bit shorter than I would've hoped. But overall, it was an amazing experience for me. If there will be a sequel, I'm getting it for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: With a mix of heart pounding thriller stuff, surreal mind-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and engaging puzzle sequences that will test your gamer-hands, this game is sure to put you on edge.There were several moments where I was literally at the edge of my chair during some sequences, so you can guess how intense the game is at times. Only little nitpick I have is that the story is a bit hard to understand, but it's actually really amazing either way. Character and environment design is also top-notch, so if you're a fan of pretty graphics combined with amazing storytelling then this is a game for you (I'm personally surprised that not much fanart exists of Observation, given how nice the characters and environments look, but that's entirely separate from this review).Also, even though you play as a faceless AI most of the time, you can still feel yourself connecting with Emma as you help her navigate the unnatural situation that you both find yourselves in. And I personally think that's a little bit wholesome (if a game tagged with "Horror" can qualify as having wholesome parts kek).Overall, 9/10 would bond with a qt astronaut again.I'l see you over Saturn, everyone
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I have always loved games with a good narrative and this is one for the books! It is basically an exploration puzzle solver cast in a very suspense fulled setting. I found navigating with the orbs a bit tricky on keyboard but I think this added to the experience when one thinks how disorienting zero gravity can be. If you like sitting on the edge of your seat and straining your brain a little then this is a game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: So far, the auto-save is incredibly frustrating.  You can't manually save, and it only seems to save *before* puzzles, not after them.  Which means if you do a puzzle and then quit, even if you see the saving icon, it'll start you before the last puzzle and you'll have to do it all over again.And I've hit 2 game-breaking glitches after puzzles, too.  Had to just quit the game and start the puzzle over again.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like sci-fi? Did you enjoy the graphics and phase of Alien Isolation? The story of Prey? So try this game.It has a short and interesting story. You can finish the game in 8 hours, it feels like just the right amount of time.The thing that made me buy this game is the fact that you play through the eyes of the ship's IA. The developers did their best to keep it fun and engaging. I am sure it was not an easy task, but they delivered.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Obsessed so much with this game. I could easily vomit in space scenarios. Thanks to non dramatic camera setting, I didn't. I had amazing experience inside/outside a space-station and space walks. Half way of this game, I had a feeling the story had a similar plot as a movie called "Coherence". I hope this is not a spoiler as not much people actually watched this movie. I almost began to take notes. Hopefully, not that insanely complicated, neither are all the puzzles. Thus makes me believe every time Emma walked out of the hatch, it was another Emma. That also explains as boss of Sam, she thought her staff was retarded in the very beginning, but later, she had way gentle voice and appraised Sam as highly capable or even the best. Isn't she different?
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Keep in mind that this is more of a cinematic experience with some puzzles and exploring, than anything else. If you love Lovecraftian horror and science fiction, you'll love this game. Try to go in knowing as little as possible, if you can. Playing as SAM and seeing things through the lens (heh) of an AI is an interesting gameplay system, and it is a nice way for the story to be conveyed while you, as the player, kind of take a back seat and enjoy the experience. The only negative thing I have to say is that the game is a bit unforgiving if you miss any of the optional collectibles. There is a portion of the game that is inaccessible after a certain point, and the game doesn't do a very good job of conveying that. So if you missed any collectibles and trigger the scene change, you have to do a new game and get what you missed the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game but that said I am a massive sci-fi nerd.The atmosphere and story of this game is AMAZING! I was gripping my seat at times playing through this!I loved the 2001: A Space Odyssey feeling of Hal that S.A.M. had (In my mind, SAM doesn't talk much).This game is pretty much a puzzle solving (space) walking sim, it is enjoyable but if you aren't super into sci-fi and are thinking of getting this I would recommend you wait for it to go on sale!or check out my video to see if you might like it yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Story has potential, but lots of it is wasted and has huge logic holes. Graphics are ok, but much worse than the screenshots suggest. Character animation in particular is awful. Controls are probably great for a game pad, but calling mouse and keyboard input an afterthought would be generous. Either way, camera movement is designed to stretch the game. Puzzles are pointless, very easy and just tedious clickwork. Total playtime is five hours and replay value is zero, keep that in mind when looking at the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pure frustration... and a little of enjoyment. But for me, frustration is so much more, you just don't know what the heck devs want you to do. You just float mindlessly clicking everywhere you can to go further.Interesting idea, but clearly bad implementation with no hints of what to do, i had to google so many times, this game is sure the most confusing i've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly sincerely enjoy this game a lot. The gameplay is sort of rough, and I feel like the controls were designed more for console than PC (I've played this on console as well) so use a controller if you can. Personally, I found the puzzles and the overall gameplay, PC controls aside, immersive in a weird way.Also pls play this game in the dark with headphones on if you can, the visuals and the sound design benefit from having a lack of distraction from anything else.The story itself I really really enjoyed, reminding me of one of my favourite movies (2001: A Space Odyssey) which is what I imagine they were going for when making this game. I'm not going to spoil anything, but depending on how open you are with sci-fi you may or may not enjoy the ending of this, with myself enjoying it a lot. Overall, I would recommend this game for any space sci-fi fans!
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Looks good but it's more of an interactive movie. I did not have fun with the gameplay at all BUT there was at least some bit of original story. I am a sucker for sci-fi and that includes the B-tier movies. This could have been one and it would be perfectly fine.What supplements the 'puzzles' is tedious searching for things - ironically at the same time, there is not much to explore, you kind of go over the same things until you find the solution/message/schema/password. Then there is a little bit of Simon Says... Worst one is 'copy these numbers to these fields'. BOO. There seem to be a few throwaway interfaces that you get to use once or twice, forget they exist and then you have to use them randomly again. What I am saying is that it is not designed too well. As is, this is a walking sim with extra steps. I suspect I would have more fun without the 'puzzles'I finished the game and it took me way too long because I got it twice to a halt where I could not progress. Also plan for longer sessions because in the first half, checkpoints are scarce so you might need to replay some of the more tedious bits if you need to quit the game.There are some bigger pacing issues as well - most notably the  But that's just the main example, others are all over the place (first mission already has one of these).I did enjoy the story, graphics, sound, atmosphere and 2 main voices. I did not enjoy controls (tried both controller and KB/m) and overall lack of ... well... gameplay.Overall, if you are really into the genre consider it but if you want it for the puzzle aspect, stay away.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: The station is absolutely amazing! It's just... believable.Story, on other hand, didn't really land with me. Is there such thing as... too cinematic? It's one thing to walk away from 90 minutes movie with some loose ends, it's another to be stuck in a game for 6 hours and it amount to "weird stuff happened".Had no issue with keyboard/mouse controls, it just handles like a small flight sim (because it is), not a shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I feel compelled to review this game, so here you go. I bought this game because it looked interesting and because of the BAFTA award it displays. The price was nice and low so I went for it. But, if I knew then what I know now I would have saved my money. I never really connected with the game or the characters. I found it frustrating from the very beginning and was wishing for it to end by the end of the game. If it had been a long game to play I would have abandoned it but it only took a few hours to get from beginning to end. I immediately deleted the game from my downloads as soon as I finished it and can say with utmost confidence that I will not be playing the game ever again. The one feeling I am left with from this game is frustration... lots and lots of frustration in being told to do something with no clear direction of accomplishing the objective. It's like walking into a new job on your first day and being asked to do a complex task with no instruction, and that is done over and over again in this game. I certainly cannot recommend this torture to any decent human being.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never experienced a story that I liked so much told in a way I hated more than this. Observation features such gripping gameplay as Simon Says, QTEs, and "hunt for the interactable object." Are those three different ways of saying "press the specified button when the game tells you to?" Yes, because this game makes you do exactly that, a lot. This is not a long game, but I would say I spent 25% of my time watching cutscenes (well written and well scripted, again the story is great), and another 25% of my time wandering around, searching for the object I need to interact with. This game really could have made a great walking simulator-style interactive story. Or more interesting puzzles or challenges to solve with the camera system could make this a great adventure game. But as is, it offers the worst of both worlds with the vapid pointless gameplay just serving to diffuse all tension and build frustration. Watch a (condensed) let's play if the story seems interesting, but I do not recommend anyone play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Starts great, falls off a cliff after the midpoint. Puzzles have fantastic visual design, but become frustratingly obtuse and badly designed. Story kept getting deeper, right until it just turned to mediocre 2001-wannabe creepiness with an ending that felt rushed. Saves are strangely rare, and the exit menu doesn't specify how long it's been since the last: Lost 30 minutes of exploration because it didn't save after a story objective! No chapter select either, so you can't check back on any missed collectables.Got it on discount, but still ended up disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Game so far is pretty good. Unique play style and plot is amazing. One major issue though is 1 bug I ran into. I'm unable to finish the game because I am stuck at a part where you have to input EXACT numbers using up/down on a slider, and the numbers randomly skip. So if I had to input 89, you hold W to increase and it will skip from 85 to 88 then 90. There are 6 numbers to input so its relatively impossible to get lucky and have all numbers required accessible.  I feel like I am right at the end so it's pretty frustrating. I would love to give this game a Thumbs Up, but I cant recommend the game because you cant finish it with this bug.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I already finished this in the Xbox App, when it was recommended to me (by some AI / algorithm...).The atmosphere, the story and the main character(s) have impressed me deeply. I am nearing 40 years of age, but I got scared every now and then and it felt like you were really in the ISS. Some technology is not explained well and controls are somewhat bad, especially when you are flying around in that "sphere" thing, but I think that is okay and expectable, while you are using technology from the 1980s, etc.It really felt like controlling "special" high developed computer programs and stuff.There were a few mini games where I could not for the life of me figure out what to do, but the game never made me feel bad about it. Tension was rising while a countdown was active, and happiness was visible on my digital SAM face when I correctly configured the antennas.A game that deserves to be discovered by you. Not perfect, but perfectly memorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend the game? Conditionally yes. The plot is a far more mystery thriller then horror though it does have some horror elements from a conceptional standpoint. From being stuck in space when the events occur, which again from a logical standpoint makes the game terrifying. But...that is about it.The story without going into spoilers is you take on the roll of "S.A.M." or basically the "HAL" of this universe, being the Observation's main AI control system. What this means is you will control cameras to interact with ship systems to overcome puzzles. Which isn't generally complex but does take some moving of the cameras from various angles to get line of sight to objectives. All while being in a two minutes in the future kind of spaceship, or in other words where there is no up and any surface can hold controls.This is actually the worst element, the "realism" aspect of the setting. While it is slightly annoying to track down systems in the camera map your orientation is more or less fixed. So while there is no "up" you still can work with some orientation and spatial awareness. However there are a couple sections where you have to take control of a free floating camera, and combined with the realism of current day space ships you can quickly lose orientation. There were more then a few times I got lost simply trying to navigate the station because or the lack of having any sort of "up" and no quick control to reorientate your camera perspective to any sort of perspective.So in short the story is interesting, the presentation both interesting and not something done for a while. However this is marred by certain gameplay elements that at least in my experience were bad enough to rather jarringly interrupt the story and remind me I was playing a game in the worst possible way. If you love sci-fi and cerebral storylines and have the patience to overlook the issues...I recommend the game. If not I would recommend waiting for a sale if you still are interested.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Take a break from the high pressure shooters and try "Observation", more of a discovery game.  This is the best simulation of being in weightless space that I have seen.  You can't be upside down because there is no upside right.  Besides, you are either a bot or part of the ship's electronic support system, helping out a human character named Emma.  The visuals are great.  When Emma asks you to see what part of the Earth we are above, and you see Saturn, up close, you realize this game has a strange story.  If you liked Portal, you are used to entering  a room and asking yourself, "What am I suppose to do here".  You should like this game too.

_childDocuments_.review: There is nothing I love more than an atmospheric space game. Even though the game had some bad reviews, I knew I had to get it. Sadly, not even my crave for the genre could overlook how lacklustre this game is. The controls are freaking enraging. And don't get me started on the puzzles. Just look up walkthroughs on youtube and what the comments say. The game lets you wander around cluelessly for ages, expecting you to find out stuff you haven't even been introduced to or didnt know was possible. Also you will get stuck numerous times due to bugs. There is no safe function, so the next day I had to start the section from anew, having to watch the unskippable cinematics again.Great idea, abysmal implementation

_childDocuments_.review: I have a soft spot for weird sci-fi, something that mixes very realistic hard science elements with stories about facing something completely beyond human comprehension. So when I stumbled upon Observation, I got highly interested. And now that the game has been made available on more distribution platforms, I couldn’t miss my chance to try it out. It… wasn’t as exciting as I was hoping it would be.Gameplay-wise, Observation can probably be best described as an adventure game as it is mostly based around the same pillars as a lot of adventure titles – exploring locations, solving problems/puzzles, experiencing a story. And given the game’s main gimmick, it’s even more directly comparable to the point & click classics of old due to how you control the game. You see, as the game description says, you don’t play as an astronaut on a space station, you are the space station – the cameras, the drones, the controls to various systems you have access to. And in concept it’s pretty neat and quite unique. It tries to have that feel of the games where you experience the title as if from a perspective of someone looking at a live feed from cameras, but at the same time doesn’t try to go too heavy in the indirect control concept like something you’d find in eXperience 112 or Lifeline for PS2.It’s also very smart about the audio and visual side of things. Everything is trying to simulate a very realistic look with some shots genuinely feeling as if you were looking at a recording of a real space station. And most of the puzzles/problems in the game are based around interactions with different systems. This is also complimented by good voice acting, really strong first half of the game in terms of the story and lots and lots of good narrative moments. It does get you invested in the story, which gets progressively more and more strange, yet still manages to feel real enough to emphasize with the characters.But it eventually does run out of steam. The story never goes bad in any way, but it does end on a somewhat “eh” note. Which is also made worse by the fact that while you have a bonus objective of collecting all background information on the events and characters, that information doesn’t ever reveal anything actually worthwhile. So, you’re left with the ending that’s just “yeah, okay” and when you gather all of the additional info, you’re not given some new context to enhance the story, it’s just there. Which made me remember The Turing Test – another title which had a rather “okay” ending, yet the more information you gathered throughout the game, the more context you’ve gotten by the end, putting the ending choice into a perspective that stays with you after the game ends.The overall “meh”-ness of the ending further complicates the feeling towards the game, because apart from the mood and the story, it’s not a particularly fun game to play. Most of the “puzzles” here are rather primitive and unfun mini-games, including an annoying repeating Simon says mini-game that gets old the first time yet repeats several times later. During multiple occasions it’s also hard to understand what exactly the game expects from you, often because the interaction prompt might not appear where or when you expect it to. The controls are not particularly great with the gamepad for which the game was clearly designed, on keyboard and mouse it’s even worse. And there are countless tiny little bugs which can make the game even more confusing than it already is, including a possibility to trigger certain story events after you’ve completed them once (they thankfully stay completed, yet the comments play twice anyway). And it’s desire to make slow moments where the camera holds for a very long time sometimes make it look as if the game broke – they don’t really nail the technique here.Overall, while playing Observation has been enjoyable in its own way, it’s not a particularly fantastic title. In some ways, I’ve actually found ADR1FT, which is not a very good game, more memorable and fun than this. If it seems intriguing, definitely give it a look, at least at a discount, as it doesn’t overstay the welcome. But don’t expect it to wow you.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun playing this game. Being the surveillance system is super cool. I wish there was more to do, though. The game felt pretty linear to me and only took eight hours. I didn't like being in the sphere at all (clumsy, disorienting, and slow). I think it would be cool if they would slow down time or something when a human's waiting for a response because it just feels weird that she would ask me a simple question and wait ten minutes for me to solve the puzzle and respond. That's just nit-picking, though.Really, I thought the story was basically 2001: A Space Odyssey, only you play the computer, the planet you're going to is Saturn instead of Jupiter, and the monolith is shaped like a hexagon.I wish there was more to do!
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Untold Stories form the same developer i was curious to see what their next game would be like and since it had a space setting i was even more interested in it. So i got it on a sale and i have to say its worth getting on a discount. I dont think its worth getting at full price, let me elaborate.First of all the story, its ok i guess. Interstellar and esspecialy Space odyssey did the same thing,much better too. So the story goes like this you start at a specific location in our solar system and try to figure out how and why you got there while you try to get the station back on track.Now the cast is mediocre and most of it play a small part on the whole thing or none at all, other than a few lines. I with there was more to each character but many stories with similar setting fall flat on that aspect of it.Now the biggest issue here is the gameplay. The gameplay is like they got the worst parts of untold stories and increased them by a tenfold. You jump between 2 modes, camera mode and moving sphere mode. And the sphere mode ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucked, beyond the fact that its there just to prolong the game and offers nothing other than you moving around wasting time searching for little details it feels awful to play. It causes motion sickness easily because the movement and sensitivy feels off, on top of that they added an idiotic mechanic where every time you touch anything the camera breaks up making it even worse.I really dont get why they did that, they could have used it only on the outside of the ship but they decided to use it inside too. Its the worst. The camera part aint bad but it could have been better if they didnt waste time with the ball....Bugs and performance issues, the performance is good but the settings are so werid with no option to lock framerate or tweek the settings. For some reason the fps lock is bound to presets so if i were on high/ultra it locks to my native hz 144, if i go to custom it goes to 72, if i go good or simple it goes to 60. Its so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ weird and to make it even worse the lower the fps the higher the sensitive gets, at 60 fps my mouse was flying like crazy. Also there are a ♥♥♥♥ load of bugs for a 2 year old game. If you launch it from system tray it crashes instantly, you have to launch it from the library....Also i got stuck in a late game encounter because you were supposed to get caught but the npc wasnt anywhere to be seen. Then i quite and play the whole session again ,because there is no save ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, only to get caught but the npc is invisible. _childDocuments_.review: Interesting sci-fi thriller. The story was fairly interesting and the characters didn't feel over the top. Puzzles were fun and a few of them actually took me awhile to figure out. The entire game is just moving around the station and solving puzzles while listening to the story. Which is fine with me, but be aware that this game is basically just walking around and clicking on puzzles. The ending could have been done a little better though. Felt like the writer couldn't figure out how he wanted to end the story so they just made it super vague so that they didn't have to explain anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Decent atmosphere but there is nothing else here. The story is near nonsensical but given the sort of horror its going for thats kinda expected, but it just doesn't have anything interesting in terms of gameplay. There are small "press buttons in the right order" esque tasks that pepper a clearly intentionally obtuse navigation system. The saving grace is that you can get *most* things done with painfully slowly panning camera's (though I understand the decision to make them painfully slow). The way the story unfold's is paced well, if it were not for how much time can be wasted if you accidentally miss something and overshoot the goal. This would be less of an issue if the game was not entirely linear, but there are no side tasks, there is no reason to explore (except for optional message logs), and getting lost means you have that much more time wasted trying to figure your way back.And that's nothing to say for the amount of bugs I encountered during my playthrough. There are serious issues with characters (just the main one for some reason) clipping through walls and just disappearing which left me wondering if I was able to even progress a couple times. Restarting from an earlier checkpoint did help, but it seems random as to how much the character will go off course so sometimes she just clipped a little bit and it was enough to proceed. I can stomach a couple bugs on a game I like, but I did not like this one.I really wanted to like it, it has good qualities, but with the confusing navigation, simplistic and yet a bit too cryptic "puzzles", it being far too linear for how well built out the station is, and characters just clipping into nowhere I cannot recommend it. I honestly would have loved this if it allowed me to skip puzzles, those were the thing that made the rest intolerable, or even if it were just a movie.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: the game has potential but it fails to deliver an overall good gaming experience. it has a stylish look and great concept as well with good voice acting but the technical issues (like missing resolution after every save checkpoint), bad control, and confusing guidance during missions as if the devs intentionally wanted to lengthen gaming time which was very frustrating throughout the game. the ending was stupid and unsatisfying.overall you should avoid this game and waste your time with something else.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: A breathtaking journey across the deep state of mind in an empty(?) space.This game came in a Sale action for something around 10 bucks- was worth every penny.Interesting mechanic, great story and a nice and deep setting.Pro:-Story-Music-GraphicContra:-Movement of the Spheres are a bit blurry.If you are looking for an interesting ~6 hour Trip away from planet earth- here you go.4,5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down, one of the best games I've played. The story is quite catchy and the game puzzles are not that hard which makes this game a real interactive experience. The feeling of playing as a station AI and not the main character was quite a pleasant change. Would definitely recommend, although the price might be a bit steep if not on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: It's essentially Space Odyssey 2001: The Videogame. You play as AI, interacting with world mostly via cameras. The atmosphere is good, despite clear budget constraints which are easily seen in animations.The issue is that gameplay is miserable - it's about following instructions by finding what exactly you are supposed to interact with, maybe even perform small QTE. What makes it really awful are the terrible, sluggish controls. If you are somebody who doesn't mind simplistic gameplay or bad controls, then the game might be for you if you are looking for space horror. But it's not for me and I won't be finishing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR I so want this game to be something I can recommend, but unfortunately it's not. A poor lack of direction, immersion breaking sequences, and a questionable ending made this game something I can't recommend. Is it worth playing? Maybe, but you have to really be into adventure games.When I saw this game listed on Steam, and looked at like 15 seconds of the trailer, I immediately purchased it. I love the space horror genre and there are only a few games that fit that niche. I figured I'd instantly fall in love with this game... Unfortunately from the start I was frustrated with the games design and felt that frustration only build as I pressed further into the story. So Observation takes the player, gives them little to no guidance and dumps them into a situation where you just have to figure it out, or look up a walkthrough. I had to reference a walkthrough 4 times while playing. I also thought I was getting some horror in the title, but it's more of a thriller. You play as an AI who helps the crew try to figure out what's happened. Playing an AI means a new control scheme and way of paying a game; so a little guidance would have went a long way. Certain parts of the game could have been streamlined to make it easier for the player to figure out what to do. They did not do this. Instead the game obfuscates it's objectives and solutions. Plan on getting lost. Not knowing what your objective is. Not knowing where to go. Not knowing what to do next. Not being able to do something you're supposed to do because you missed a thing that's not part of the objective OR the game hasn't decided you CAN do that thing yet; so you move on to other solutions only to find out the actual solution to the puzzle was what you thought in the beginning, but you spent an hour looking at everything else because that solution wasn't unlocked yet. I cannot stress just how rough and unpolished this game is! My rant above only covers the frustration of the lack of guidance in the puzzling. Then there's the controls. The story, which made no honest sense. The fact Amy's face is the one asset that looks like a video game when you're supposed to bond with her (those eyes and teeth!!). The lack of stereo sound; so as I play the game with headphones I had no clue what direction any sounds are coming from. The part where you're killing someone who patiently waits for you to figure out how to actually kill them. The game says you're growing and expanding, but as the player, you never get any new tools or see any expansion of powers. Well I take that back a little. You do get new tools, but they're given to you as part of what you lost in the beginning; so your character sees no growth despite the game constantly telling you just how much more you're expanding.So is the game with $25? Heck no! I paid $12 at launch. There were about 8 times while playing that I thought I was just going to pack it up. I don't feel that the journey and the frustration was worth the time I put in. But I persevered and completed the game. Now that I'm done, I wish I had just refunded it at the 1.5 hr mark when I hit my first, "what the heck does the game even want me to do here," moment.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Continues from the inventive angles that Stories Untold did so well at taking advantage of. Truly, a one of a kind perspective for a game to take. It would fail miserably if the UI didn’t perfectly nail what it was working at, but their artists obviously stared at integrated systems before, because it nails that aesthetic. As far as puzzle design goes too, they do a great job of blending puzzles into this very mechanical feeling interface, with you having to blend together multiple elements together to solve them. As far as story goes, they nail it again. I truly couldn’t have seen where this was going to go from the preview. Can’t recommend it enough and I am glued to the Dev after this.

_childDocuments_.review: There may be a really good sci-fi story here but unfortunately it's buried beneath awfully clunky controls and tedious puzzles. The game also doesn't let you rebind a lot of important buttons and has severe mouse acceleration problems, which makes the experience even worse. I'm usually very forgiving as far as these things go but this is too much even for me. One would think at least  of the technical issues would have been fixed in the last year since the game's release.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the way the graphics are done.I like the way I had to go about solving the puzzles.I like the camera interaction and the way some of the menus where done in the style of Aliens.The story line was interesting although and weird but I did feel for the main character Emma.It isn't a massively long game, so I can't really justify the price. I would wait for a sale, like now.But it's defo worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: this game blew my damn gourd off. in short: incredible visuals, tactile and responsive, drives in the oppressive horror of being stranded in empty space. riffs off of well-known sci-fi while still being bold and refreshing. if you played Tacoma and wished it leaned harder into psychological and cosmic horror a la 2001: A Space Oddysee and Control, play Observation.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Man this is a hard one. Observation is really good story and plot-wise even though it stays pretty mysterious without help from the internet. But damn all the bugs in the game make the experience not that good. Emma teleporting during some scenes (sometimes outside the map and therefore blocking your whole progress), awful lip sync, going through textures even sometimes during cinematics and let's not forget that the handling of high resolution is poor and sometimes switched me back to 1280x720. And don't get me started on the gameplay that can be sometimes awful, especially during space walks. If you don't have a good sense of,orientation, good luck trying to find any objective.It pains me to give this a negative review because you can feel the love from the developers, the design team and the writers. In the end, It's a nice space thriller but it's buggy as hell and space walks are a pain in the buttocks. It seems there was no QC therefore ruining the immersion. What a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: An exceptional and intriguing puzzle game, and a very interesting concept of playing the AI in the spaceship. Great storyline, amazing voice acting and compelling. And the ending ties it all together really well.Been a long time since I've played something this good, just make sure you have a walk through handy - some of the puzzles and particularly the "where am I meant to go now?" are a bit indi

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. First of all, if you've ever wanted to feel like an astronaut on a space station, this game accomplishes that perfectly, even though you don't play as a human person. Second of all, the premise and narrative are brilliant. Imagine playing the role of HAL from 2001 but with a supernatural twist like in Event Horizon or Sunshine. The music and sound effects really sell the premise too. From the beeps and whirring of machinery making you feel like an actual machine to the haunting and chilling noises during certain puzzles, the sound team did a great job creating atmosphere.Speaking of puzzles: The puzzles in this game are top notch and integrate well with the setting. It doesn't actually feel like your completing a puzzle, it feels more like operating laptops and space station equipment. Everything is logical, makes sense, and gives you a great sense of accomplishment. It makes you feel intelligent, again, like you're an actual machine. I highly recommend this game and if you want to play with a friend ....."Bring Them".
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Love the original concept (at least in my experience). Who could imagine playing as an AI could be so much fun? I feel the story carries this game forward as the controls and navigation can be a little frustrating at times. It certainly tests your ability to navigate small encroached spaces - but in many ways this makes you feel that sense of isolation (yes, a shout out to Alien: Isolation) and confinement experienced while living in a space station. Graphically, no complaints there. It captures the void of space beautifully with photo-image like Saturn as its centrepiece. Noticed some small graphical bugs (when the station is pointed directly at the storm) but not much to write home about. One other strange bug I encountered was when I accidentally managed to enter the Russian arm of the station from the space side of the locked depressurised bay. It looks like you can access the internal pressurising controls from outside, which allows you to open the bay door.Puzzles are not overly complicated, which adds a small to medium level of challenge to the game albeit, can sometimes feel like they've as though they've been imported from a memory testing app. In some cases, feel a little confusing and random.I suspect it's not going to be everyone's cup of tea, but if you like a well made psychological horror/puzzle/sci-fi games, this is one for the library.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun adventure/puzzle game.Story was entertaining if you don't think too much about it. I found navigating the station in 3d to be somewhat tedious (and discovered the Waypoint feature much too late).Puzzles break down into:- pixel hunt (fun when clues were cleverly placed and not especially fun when they weren't)- "just click the thing" (amusing)- "click awkward interfaces under a time limit" (super not fun)- find all the collectibles (nope).So uh, don't really expect much from the puzzles.Over-all the voice acting was pretty good and the game did a good job of creeping me out to various degrees for about 5-6 hours.B+. I wouldn't pay the full $24 for it, but $9 wasn't bad for being amused for a whole afternoon.

_childDocuments_.review: That was the first sentence in the game and "What is that mean?".Throughout the gameplay, my head is filled with "What the ♥♥♥♥ is going on?", "What the hell is this/that?", "Something is off". However, I enjoyed this sci-fi interactive game. Players take role as S.A.M.(System Administration & Maintenance), an AI assisting a spaceship crew named Emma Fisher, such as solving puzzles, helping Emma, finding lost crews, and uncover the truth. Solving some of the puzzles in this game were difficult for me, I need to explore the station through CCTV or Sphere, and it was hard to control the sphere honestly, it makes me sick sometimes.What I truly loved the most were the visuals and the sound, it was brilliant. Sci-fi theme, glitchy sounds, voice over, weird stuff - all of those were fantastic. But be cautious for those who has epilepsy flashing light. And one thing that made my mind blew... I consider this game is brilliant from its concept, visual, sound, interpretation. No Code is brilliant. I'm looking forward for upcoming Silent Hill: Townfall.

_childDocuments_.review: Observation is a masterfully crafted experience.The storytelling is top notch and I was kept in suspense for the entire duration of the game. Some have remarked on how this isn't the most profound game, but for something that mixes Sci-Fi and weird fiction, this delivers. Try to be less analytical and more focused on the general emotional feel of the game and you'll have a blast from start to finish. The puzzles and mechanics in it are simple enough for most anyone to figure out. So long as you pause for a second to think and not just rush through everything then you should be fine. There's plenty of lore and story to pick up for those so inclined. At the same time, you can speed through the game without collecting everything.The visuals and audio help deliver the interactive storytelling to great effect as well. I was feeling rather claustrophobic and even on the cusp of motion sickness at times while navigating the space station. I generally don't get motion sick all that easily so this might be something to consider for those more prone to it.I loved the developer's prior offering, Stories Untold, which was also very strong on interactive storytelling and weird happenings. Both of these games are on the shorter side, which is perfect for someone preferring a quality experience which doesn't outstay its welcome. Observation was about 4 1/2 hours to complete for me as I didn't bother seeking out every last bit of lore. All in all, if you like getting caught up in an action-packed short story with quality oozing everywhere and weird things afoot, then Observation is your game. I highly recommend it for the half off price that it's selling for right now.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but only partially.The story is nice, the overall atmosphere is great and the space station is pretty well designed (disclosure: I love space stations ;).BUT what often really sucks are the abundant mini games... searching the earth coordinates on a vast image just containing white dots and grain - seriously?! ;)Additionally mission markers would have been helpful - sometimes I got a little bit stuck.

_childDocuments_.review: ⚠ This game does feature a lot of strong strobing lights that I don't really know how to reduce or turn off. If someone knows they can leave a comment below, but if you are sensitive to strobing (and I don't write these warnings lightly) I'd recommend discretion.Observation (2020) isn't for everyone. It's a fairly slow burning work that is held up by narrative and atmosphere than its gameplay, and does kind of lack a bit of high-level thematic or charcater ambitions, but if there's anything it does well it's selling the atmosphere and tone of the story.A disaster has struck the joint international Low Orbit Space Station (LOSS), maybe a collision with debris or a decompression. Dr Emma Fisher, the medical officer among the crew of six, appears to be only one left as she figures out what has gone wrong and where everyone has went. But you don't play as Emma., or any human character; you play as the Systems Administration & Maintenance operating system, or "SAM", the station's on-board experimental AI that Emma manages to reboot despite loss of system functionality and memory data. As such, everything is only seen through the perspective of onboard cameras and abstract digital interfaces. You "move" by switching cameras from module to module, and only exert action in a room by way of the peripherals and devices you can pair with in them, and scan environmental details like documents and photos as you try to recover mission memory and hopefully piece together what happened.The game's at its strongest when it's letting the atmosphere and mood of its environments speak for themselves. It's mostly just you, a decidedly non-anthropomorphic entity simultaneously flowing through and trapped in your space station body looking at yourself. The cameras have just the right amount of distortion that really mimics the look of the fixed cameras on board a space station, without being TOO noisy to be a farce. The space setting is used appropriately as well: you have the existential dread of being extremely alone surrounded by nothingness, but the space station itself as an interior environment that does also sell this tone. It's claustrophobic, the cameras mimic lost footage horror films, and the lack of a definite "up" in the myriad of modules and their cluttered interiors means it—which, in this case, also means your own body—becomes disorienting to navigate in and around. Observation is really good at letting its tone steep and seep into your veins as you slowly pan cameras looking for clues. I'd like to compare it to games like Outer Wilds where the setting of space is used not for self-fellatio for tech dudebros but to convey mood or broader thematic ideas, and I'd like to play more games like this.Observation does stumble a bit in that some of these puzzle mechanics are a little obtuse and irregular. Sometimes the game throws a deliberately difficult quicktime thing at you, which I guess is tonally appropriate for the situation but still throws you off guard, and might be frustrating for some players in an otherwise contemplative and slow game. And this might be a bit of a nitpick but the lip syncing isn't too great. It's not Life is Strange bad, but in a game that does sell the atmosphere so well otherwise it's a little disappointing to be drawn right out of it when the lacking facial animation department comes into focus.Observation's biggest flaws for me are the fuzzy and unfocused nature of its broader thematic goals. It plays like a video game equivalent of 2001: A Space Odyssey, what with un-anthropomorphic AIs both confined and liberated by this space station body settled alongside a human crew, combined with literal cosmic horror, but it doesn't really seem to comment or explore on, say, Emma's relationship with SAM. That's not to say being an AI in this game is unjustified, since it helps the verisimilitude of why you're following the directions barked at you by the humans, but the nature of SAM as a character and its relationship with Emma could definitely have used some development, and the game's narrative feels a bit hollow because of this.Really it's more in the vein of Alan Wake, in that it's a game that benefits from an existing interest in the subject matter draped in these horror themes that's based on telling this cryptic but not incomprehensible story. But while I disliked Alan Wake for its total reliance on needing to be familiar the things it's referencing (and I really don't like it when games make me do homework) and its insistence on composing itself largely out of dry over-the-shoulder shooter mechanics (as if it feels like its audience would be bored if it didn't cram Gears of War into itself), Observation avoids most of those trappings and I feel is more successful in telling its story and conveying its mood to an audience that is receptive to this type of game, subject matter, and setting.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this but honestly, I love me a good space game. But! Emma is such a hateful person. I really didn't want anything good to happen for her. There were some janky parts that made the game frustrating. Not to mention the long scene being carried by Emma and her walking straight through objects or getting stuck on them. There's no way to skip the long arduous cut scenes that are just self indulgent on the dev's part and don't give them player any information. It's just like "please god hurry up..." Oh and multiple crashes and having to repeat parts... Like good effort but bleh, I wouldn't replay it.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing narrative game with excellent voice acting, a solid atmosphere, and consistently suspenseful and intriguing story. I loved it from start to finish.Unfortunately some technical issues do mar the experience. The camera can sometimes clip through the environment during certain cutscenes. More egregious however was a bug where the game kept lowering its resolution step by step from my native 1440p to, I think, 768p. This could happen within minutes of setting the resolution. _childDocuments_.review: Not that bad of a movie, but a very poor game.The theme is cool, but the player is an spectator for more than half of the experience, and there is little to nothing they can do to alter the outcome, without even a game over or bad end scenarioGaemplay wise there are also many BS moments where one is expected to do things without being explained how and with very little visual feedback. It all amounts to pushing button A when asked to or joining dots, so it's not like there is a puzzle to solve eitherIn the very few moments where there is a bit of suspense it's all broken by knowing it is all going on rails and by not accomplishing the objectives what you're doing is just prolonging the sufferingAll in all, not that bad for the price that I got it for, but I'd suggest passing the experience and using your money for something else
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Very good ambience and feeling of isolation in a space station. I like the story, and the ending is intriguing to say the least.I found the controls and UI a bit frustrating at times. Some good puzzles, some too simple with only looking in the right place to find the right information required.All in all I appreciated it.Got it based on experience from Stories Untold which I actually liked more. It is even smaller, has less polished graphics, but I found it stronger in the puzzles department.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely enjoyed Observation. That said I can see where some people come from as the game can sometimes annoy you to the point of breaking your immersion. Now I never had to look at a walkthrough to progress but there were times where I had to spend a few minutes going back and forth attempting to perform seemingly simple tasks. This really pulls you away from the building tension especially later in the game. That being said the story was very enjoyable albeit short. I finished the entire game in 3 hours and to the best of my knowledge there is only one ending so there is little replay value. I already owned Stories Untold and purchased this game during the summer sale making the full price of the game $9.99 and as far as i'm concerned that's about what I would say this game is worth given its simplicity and length. I would never recommend purchasing this game at full price unless you have money to burn, but if it's on sale and especially if you enjoyed Stories Untold, it's a good buy.
