_childDocuments_.review: NEW REVIEW Nov'23: After initially not being able to get more than 90 minutes of play time into the game before it continuously crashed, I tried again. And what do you know: it worked this time. So here's what I think. (old review below)I love the details of the space station, just looks right and beautiful. I also love the story telling and pace of the game - just right to fully appreciate it. There are for example sequences where almost nothing happens for a whole minute, but it really helps to let the atmosphere sink in! And the biggest difference to games I usually play is the perspective, as you see everything from the limited points of view of an AI that can use cameras and a small sphere - very different and interesting!What I don't like is that some of the laptop pins I had to obtain from guides on the internet, and I have no clue up to this point how to obtain them in-game. That is confusing, as the main "thing" of the game is to explore stuff, so that should not be made unreasonably more difficult for additional content in comparison to the main story line (which is not too hard to follow).I am also a bit disappointed that one of the final cut scenes (to not spoiler anything, let's call it "the walk at the end") was very bugged for me. You cannot control your movement at all, it is pre-arranged. Unfortunately my point of view lead me through the ground a lot and through a wall section at one point, briefly obstructing the scene repeatedly. I wonder how such a grave error could make it into the final game and not get fixed 4.5 years after release, given that the final cut scenes are supposed to reward you for hours of gameplay.Still, my verdict is thumbs-up, as I enjoyed the mystery and twists throughout the game. Just don't expect a lot of action, this one is slow.-- INITIAL REVIEW ~2021/22: Game keeps crashing randomly, support page links to game's landing page without support contact information, developer's contact form is not replied to. So I'm stuck with a broken game along with other players without any way to get this fixed. All in all: will never buy from these guys again.EDIT 1 ~2022: There is a support page now, . Will try again and see if I can continue with help. Will update this review if anything changes.EDIT 2 Nov'23: The game worked by now (either the game or some drivers may have been fixed). Rest of the review see at the top.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game, so consider this less of a review and more of a first impression.Short but sweet. If story based experience’s with minimalistic gameplay is your thing, then this game is for you.Now that that is out of the way.First, know going in that this is not a FNAF style horror game. I can count all the jump scares in it on one hand.The most consistent emotions the game inspired in me were curiosity and dread.After each lore entry I found, or every event in the game, I was left wanting to know more but also dreading what I would find.This continues all the way through the ending, as I still have questions but also don’t want the answers.That said, the story while well written and executed, does little to hide it’s clear inspiration by This is a slight problem, in that once you realize what it was inspired by you can guess fairly accurately where it’s going.However, even though I guessed a rough outline of the ending about halfway through the game, it was still impactful.This is greatly helped by the superb voice acting in the game.No one phoned in their lines in this game, the emotion in the lines of dialogue go a long way to making you care about the characters in way that’s hard to pull off in a game this short.Which brings me to the sound design.Having finished the game about an hour ago as of writing this line, I can say that I don’t remember the music at all.So I suppose that it contributed to the atmosphere of the game without being intrusive, but that is just an inference.The environmental sounds were good, normal things sounded as I expected they should.This contributed to the feeling of dread when you encounter things that shouldn’t be there and the sounds that were produced by them were unnatural and grating.Then there’s the graphics, of which I only have two points to make.1: The textures in the game are gorgeous. They are so good that at times it borders on photorealism.2: The facial animations aren’t great. You’ll see others ragging on the facial animations, and though I do agree with many of the things being said, I also think that their lack of quality has been somewhat exaggerated.To be clear, the facial animations are serviceable but not good.As far as the gameplay is concerned there isn’t much to talk about.It mostly consist of looking for interactable objects in the environment and completing short, simple puzzles to use them.As far as I could tell there are no intentional failure states in the game, i.e. nothing you do will (as far as I could find) get you game over screen.That said, there is one place in the game where I did find a way to “lose”.At one point in the game you have to get past an obstacle without being detected, though the game doesn’t tell you, this section is on a timer.If you don’t do what the game wants you to do before the hidden timer expires, then the obstacle will leave and you’ll be locked in that area with no way of getting out other than reloading.Though I’ve see quite a few people complaining about bugs, the above example is the closest I came to experiencing one myself.Perhaps I’ll see some on repeated playthroughs, or perhaps they’ll be patched out by then.At this point I plan to replay the game at least two more times, one of which will be a 100% playthrough, after that I will post a full review of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing, but the game has soul.It's hard to properly review this game because I'm a little stuck on the potential it had. There were times where you can peek through the door and see the brilliance on the other side. The moments of strength. The game has great atmosphere, does a nice job of simulating that feeling that you're actually in a space station. The building blocks for the story are there, but it really runs into a lot of issues.Some rather blatant clipping issues throughout the game, and even during the final ending scene. Characters floating through walls, or reaching through objects, or your camera going through solid ground.It's probably wrong to fault the game for its story. It's nearly impossible to come up with something new these days. It does an okay job. Probably needed some extra time with character development for the player to really care about the people. Again, it's not really fair to compare this to something like SOMA, but the story just didn't hit as hard, wasn't quite strong enough for me to be impressed by it.The gameplay itself is just a bit too clunky, a bit too slow. I appreciate the intention behind it. The feeling of these cameras being your only attachment to the world hits. Your ability to interact with the world being so limited is something interesting to explore as a concept. The problem is it becomes a slog. It's like playing one of those I SPY find the object books, except you can only look at an eighth of a page at a time, and it takes 3 seconds to look at the next eighth of the page.Most of the puzzles really boil down to matching up a picture with the goal, or following instructions. It was very disappointing to me that the most "plot significant" puzzle was just Simon Says. It wasn't interesting or endearing in any way, and actually took away from the game rather than adding anything to it.Yet after all this negativity I'm spouting about the game, I'm still "recommending" it. I'm glad to have played it, even through the disappointment, and felt strongly enough about the game (Even though mostly it was the missed potential) to write this review.It would have taken quite a bit more work, but there was the possibility of this being something truly special.

_childDocuments_.review: A confusing mess with some brilliant moments======================The positives:======================+Great presentation and photo realistic visuals.+Oppressive atmosphere.+You want to see the story through.+A few WTF moments.+A "One of a kind" king of game, you really have to re-wire your brain to play this one.======================The negatives======================-Frustrating controls and navigation (a minimap would actually be helpful).-Lack of directions and confusing puzzles (I had to use the walkthrough many times)        *"Oh, I have to fly through the vents and break the grates? I had no idea!"        *"Oh, THIS is how you solve this puzzle?"        *"Oh, I have to actually comment on some of the structural damage and the status of the hatches to activate the dialogue that will allow me to proceed further?          I had no idea I could talk in those situations. I thought I could only respond to commands"-Apparently, this used to be an Epic exclusive. Had I known that, I would not have bought the game.-Confusing ending (I now have to go on Youtube and have someone to explain it to me and make me feel like an idiot).=========================I feel like they could have gotten rid of half of the puzzles in this game and just had the AI complete the tasks by itself for the sake of continuity and immersion. I don't mind watching a few cut scenes. When a game stops being fun it becomes tedious and this is one of those games.There are moments of brilliance in this game, but if you want to get frustrated with controls, lack of direction and difficult puzzle, and bang your head against the wall in the process, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a great plot and terrific visuals that are brought down by poor navigation controls and repetitive environmental interactions. The Good:> Great visuals, voice acting, and a terrific sci-fi plot.> The antagonist (of sorts) is enigmatic but develops really well if you pay close attention to your interactions with it> Really good puzzles and interactive 'systems interfaces' that are immersive and interesting to use.The Bad:> When you are moving around the station, you have a very narrow FOV and the rooms are very small which makes it easy to get motion-sick and very difficult to find doors and objects. > For much of the game, the map is 'unavailable', even though the protagonist canonically knows the exact layout of their surroundings. > Interacting with ANY object in the game for the first time requires you to perform a trivially-easy Simon Says task that adds nothing to the game other than padding out the playtime.> The game emphasizes 'collecting' laptop entries and documents, but also hides them and leans into the clunkiness of the navigation system to make them difficult to find.

_childDocuments_.review: very good game if you like weird, experimental stuff. if you have an aversion to looking up guides this may not be the best game for you but if you like figuring things out and are okay with doing a lot of reading & if you have any interest in cosmic horror/near-future sci-fi (or if youre a fan of the movie 2001: A Space Odyssey) i highly recommend it. one of the only games i've seen that lets you play as a robot and doesnt involved gratuitous violence-- wish there were more like it. most of the issues that people tend to complain about (lack of clear direction, difficulty navigating) can be solved with in-game mechanics, but the game doesn't explicitly tell you how to access them, and the lack of hand-holding can put some people off. but for clarity: you can directly check your objectives with the 'O' key, and set waypoints to allow easier navigation by right clicking on destinations. (not sure about controller inputs, but the options for both of these are displayed on screen, so you can figure it out.)also: PLEASE pay attention to the flashing lights warning. its VERY severe and they do not mean it lightly. if you suffer from any kind of epilepsy/seizures triggered by bright, flashing lights do NOT play. for as much as i love it this game was not kind to my chronic migraines.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the developers last game Stories Untold, I was really excited to see what was going to come next from them. This game was such a big leap from their previous title. First off, it it downright gorgeous. The graphical quality of the game is well beyond the price point. The puzzles were fun but could be a bit too easy at times with no real penalty for not figuring out how to do them properly. I see a lot of people complaining about how the games mechanics are something that gets in the way of such a good story, but I only kind of agree. There are some moments in the game where you may get lost trying to figure out what exactly you are supposed to do but I only encountered that maybe twice. The story itself is really entertaining and full of moments of well built suspension and tension. I was glad to see the homages to 2001. The game gives off some really creepy and unsettling atmospheres throughout. There are also a few moments that leave you shocked and confused. Overall, if you like horror games and indie games that take an unusual approach to gameplay, you will probably really enjoy this game even despite some of the mechanical issues everybody is talking about.

_childDocuments_.review: A maintenance simulator that’s set inside a sci-fi thriller that's trying to be more intriguing than it really is. Observation rolls with the slightly formulaic premise of “”, but the scariest part is honestly the close-up face animations. For as much effort that went into the presentation of being in space, it’s a shame the gameplay of being an AI isn’t more inspired. Your interactions with the station/crew largely add up to finding the right terminal, syncing to it, and playing Simon Says with the retro GUI. When not running the cameras, you're navigating the cramped, cluttered station in 6DoF as a clunky sphere, which leads to many very disorienting, drawn-out, and annoyingly nauseating sequences. Observation did really seem promising at the start, but by the end, I was tired of all the copy-pasted mini-games, predictable plot, awkward stop-and-start dialogue, and dramatic sci-fi noises.

_childDocuments_.review: Good Things:-The Plot. The game is very well paced and very well crafted. All the shocking scenes hit with massive impact, the more fantastical elements are introduced quickly enough to peak interest but not so quickly as to be absurd, the few characters that exist are impressively fleshed out and it doesn't turn out to be the guilt-induced psychosis of a drunk driver! I'd honestly recommend it on these grounds alone.-The Innovation. Being an AI is a unique way of doing this kind of story, and it does give an interesting new perspective on things. Being forced to act within your programming is an interesting challenge, and the sense of being a helpful, omnipresent force is a new way of doing this. On a related note, this has a very realistic portrayal of spacetravel (except the AI) and works very well at making what could be boring mundanity interesting and engaging.Atmosphere: the space station is very well designed- it feels like a place people actually live and work, with notes and records providing details on everyone and various personal affects scattered around. The ships slow degeneration also adds to the sense of terror, and the looming void of space is used very effectivelyProblems:-A refusal to commit. For a good half of the game, you're uploaded into essentially a flying roomba, and at that point there's nothing the AI conceit adds to the game- you're basically just playing a clunky astronaut. It's not a deal breaker but it is infuriating next to the more interesting ship AI sections-Slightly infuriating puzzles.: Puzzles are often not so much challenging as dependent finding minor details in an increasingly dark space station (at least twice I was stuck for a good few minutes finding a door on the wall in front of me), and often the plot has to stop for you to scroll through every screen to find the one clickable space. These puzzles aren't the majority but are common enough to be annoyingOverall, I'd give this a 4/5. There are some infuriating and pointless sections, but the story and innovation are enough to sell it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no proper way in which this review can make the game justice. It's an amazingly well crafted experience, intense and executed almost flawless. The stage in which you jump in as the "ghost in the machine" aka SAM is what appears to be a mundane space station where something went wrong and you need to help the only other human, Dr. Fisher discover what happened.I believe one of the strongest points of observation is that it puts the player outside the usual area of "central" character. You are a passive, non emphatic machine that needs to support the crew on their daily tasks and there is never a moment in the game where this immersion is broken. By somehow shifting the focus from the player towards outside events and actors, the amazing voice acting, scenery and characters (with some minor exceptions) get to truly shine.The game looks good and the special visual effects add a certain charm to making the world look and feel convincing.Puzzles are interesting and provide a good challenge without being dismissive. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to give this game a positive review, but even as of version 1.17, almost 3 years after the release date, the game is a buggy mess.  There are so many weird aspect ratio and resolution issues.  The game looks like it was made to work in 16:9 resolutions only.  Playing on a 16:10 ratio 1920x1200 monitor, every time you restart the game or go to the game menu, the resolution would reset to some weird one like 1600:900.  Playing at the native 1920x1200 resolution would result in the game being zoomed-in rather than the extra 120 lines of vertical resolution being drawn.  There would be weird animation glitches where Emma's character model would glitch through the station wall.  The Unity engine even crashed on me when I quit the game after about an hour's playtime.The controls of the game leave much to be desired as well.  The fixed cameras in each room pan at a really slow speed, and when you get in the flying sphere, the controls are so laggy and unresponsive.  In the sphere, it's also easy to get lost in the station and the waypoint system doesn't work very well as a navigational aid.  The waypoint marker would just disappear or get placed over a wall.  It's too easy to get turned around.In spite of all that, the story is a decent deep space sci-fi thriller.  There's always this layer of dread permeating the space station as you try to avert disaster coming around from every corner while trying to solve a mystery of how you wound up in that situation in the first place.  The puzzles are well thought out, but not too obtuse, except for the door/wiring schematic ones.  I hate having to flip back-and-forth between a JPG of the diagram and the actual grid you need to work on.  It would have been better, but probably too easy to just overlay one on top of the other.It's unfortunate that the game is hamstrung by all the Unity engine bugs.  There's a good story buried in there somewhere with half-decent acting.  It has a refreshing "hard sci-fi" setting.  A few more bug fixes and engine updates and it would be a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Observation is a great game for a very specific demographic, an artistic pseudo-Kubrick wannabe for many people, and a walking simulator that somehow has 3D movement for others.  It earned enmity early on by being an exclusive on a different platform (at least for PC) for a while (I'm not whining about it, just stating a fact), but is generally well-rated and has won a 2020 BAFTA. If you're not a completionist it clocks in at around 4 -5 hours or so (at least that's what I did, and I took my time in each room looking at everything).  WASDZC-driven movement (3D), mouse interactions.Pros:-Graphics are fairly polished.  Lighting is usually well done.-Lighting and sound design contribute to a suspenseful atmospheric setting.-Adventure with light puzzles, but with occasional complex pieces.-A space-station scavenger hunt for data to clear the next obstacle.-Voice-acting by people that for the most part seemed to care about their jobs!Kind of both:-You'll love and hate the movement controls when you're in the 3D movement sections.-At least until the ending, the story is trying to lead you into a plot that is trying to be about 8 different scifi movies from the past 45 years, which is both ambitious and derivative at the same time.Cons:-I was both bemused and annoyed by the silly , and that annoyance reached its peak when it .  This (at least in my opinion) kind of pulls a stunt similar to a number of games and some movies lately...a grand story with many mysterious twists that make you want to know how it interconnects, but it doesn't QUITE deliver on the ending, opting for the "make you think" type of ending where you draw your own conclusion in regards to what it all means.  That will work for some people and annoy others.  Ex. Mass Effect 3's ending makes you think Magic Ghost Children are silly.  Well, I now feel the way about .-If you're prone to motion sickness from various FPS titles, this one will do the same thing with quick movements, especially 3D sections. --You'll probably get lost a lot.Bugs encountered during playthrough:-The bugs encountered seemed odd for something that has already been out on PC for a year and the Steam release supposedly has all the fixes/patches released for the game since its initial release.  It does seem however the developer is very willing to watch for errors reported and address them with continued support.-One instance of clipping (see-through wall) during in-station movement-One instance of the wrong schematic coming up at a hatch control (coolant schematic came up instead)-Repeated clipping/camera under "floor" during in-engine cutscene at end of game (terrain elevation changes when other character carrying you), which honestly broke immersion and believability as much as the .Conclusion:  Absolutely worth playing at least once if you're into a story-driven experience, maybe twice for the completionist achievement.  Play in a dark, quiet room.  Headphones will probably enrich the atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW #49Observation----------For full transparency, I've been really conflicted while preparing for this review, even as I type it up now. Observation is a really interesting story told in a very novel and unconventional fashion, but it's a flawed storytelling experience that requires some patience to properly digest and appreciate. Plus, I've admittedly been a fan of No Code since I first played Stories Untold about 4 years ago, and I'm really looking forward to their future projects (including and especially the currently-unreleased Silent Hill: Townfall), so I honestly feel a little bad about metaphorically crapping on and potentially turning people away from what could've been, for all I know, a labor of love for a development team that I eagerly follow. However, Steam simply asks me if I recommend this game to others, and being that I prefer to only recommend things that I'm quite certain others would surely enjoy to some degree, I have to say no.Now that I've gotten that probably unnecessary spiel out of the way....Observation is a problem-solving game wrapped up thickly in an abstract sci-fi thriller tale. There's a few brief moments where quick thinking and reflexes are required, but you mostly have time to complete tasks, explore, and figure out how to solve the issues you and the space station Observation face. You play as SAM, the AI on-board and integrated into the station, and you can switch your perspective between camera views and the interactive menus of your operating system. Those familiar with the movie 2001: A Space Odyssey will see a lot of ideas borrowed from that film, to the point where it feels like the game occasionally struggles to have its own identity apart from being a video game copy of the epic film. Personally, I enjoyed Observation's story, and the cinematic visual direction and camera angles make for some great cutscenes and gameplay moments that are breathtakingly awesome and made me go back to experience them again. It also helps that this title has some of the most convincing voice acting that I've ever heard in a video game, with every line delivered from every character being very well done. Honestly, I had concern that players may not enjoy the abstract storyline much, but after reading other reviews before composing my own, it seems that the tale of the ill-fated space station Observation and its crew has been generally well received.What hasn't been getting positive feedback is the number of glaring technical issues encountered by players, myself included. Ones that I experienced include a resolution setting that sometimes changes itself to seemingly random selections (especially on every startup), character models that suddenly and very obviously snap into another location and animation script, and one specific point in the game that gave me a 50/50 outcome of getting stuck at the end of the related cutscene and halting gameplay without hard locking the program, meaning that I could go to the main menu but couldn't continue play without reloading a save point or restarting completely. These problems I find inexcusable since the developer is still in existence and the game has been available for 3+ years at the time of this review.Even if those technical issues weren't so much a factor, I also feel that the overall gameplay design could've used more polish. Moving cameras is slow, and as you play, you'll progressively be able to access the entirety of the Observation space station, which is a lot of ground to cover and modules to explore. Some points of the game require you to scan a document somewhere in the station with your cameras in order to progress, and while I didn't take issue with the slow camera movement as other players did, slowly combing the entire station over and over again to find one single piece of paper that I kept missing and having no way to narrow down where it could be made the game feel like a slog of unnecessary toil at points. Even after completing the game once before, I found myself checking a guide once or twice during my second playthrough to figure out how to complete a task after spending an ample amount of time and feeling like I was getting nowhere.So, my conclusion is that the technical bugs and the gameplay's inability to keep consistent momentum makes Observation too rough of an experience to fully recommend. I do honestly think that some will still find the game worth their time just as I did, but I can't see everyone having the patience to fully appreciate what Observation is trying and partially failing to do.

_childDocuments_.review: When I found out this was the same developer behind Stories Untold, I had to get this game. Their style of gameplay and story telling is unique to them so I wanted to experience what they crafted in this title.The story is excellent, with a couple of "ohh ♥♥♥♥!!" moments and a solid ending. The graphics are good, although face animations can be improved but do not hinder from the game.The gameplay and controls will be enjoyed or despised on a case by case basis. You play as the AI onboard a spaceship, and the gameplay revolves around connecting to different terminals, cameras, and gadgets and playing mini-puzzles to progress the story. I REALLY recommend using a controller, it was tough to control as it is, I think it would be fairly nightmarish using m&k. At some point you gain access to this robotic sphere that can fly around the space station, and there will be a couple of times that you need to do space walks outside the station. Will little guidance from the in-game character or the game itself, these are by far the most frustrating sections of the game trying to navigate your way around from one objective to another, feeling completely disoriented. A task that can take 3-5 minutes ends up taking a half hour of your time as you whizz about trying to figure out life's most existential question like "why did the developer not add some additional navigational tools?". A robot should know exactly where to go and not bumble about like a drunken human. After the first space walk, I actually used a guide to know exactly where to go on subsequent similar puzzles to keep my hair on my head and the story moving along.Also, the UI/menus are fuzzy and hard to read, trying to read the room labels "UC-3, RU-4, etc" had me squinting and shoving my face into the screen to be able to read them. I'm actually surprised it was like that and wonder if it was just an issue with my game or a purposeful design choice. I'm hoping it's the former.In the end, the developer's passion is clearly on display, the story is excellent, the gameplay is unique when it works, and very frustrating when it doesn't. None the less, I like what this developer is doing and wish them all the success.I recommend this game. If you're particular about your controls, pick it up on discount so you feel like you got your money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I love Devolver Digital as a publisher and I understand why they have decided to release this game: Observation is plenty of good ideas, but unfortunately they are very poorly executed. I impersonate SAM an AI, and the only way to move through space is be via fixed cameras or with special spheres that can physically move without any limitation.  I can only move the camera view with WASD keys, is not possible seeing around by using the mouse, which would be way faster. A cheap solution just to stretch the game. If fixed cameras movements are too slow, the sphere moves too quickly. The field of view is very reduced, there is no way to change it and looking around it is really challenging and not in a fun way. The game is set in a space station where rooms are small and narrow, so you constantly hit walls. All rooms are basically the same, there is nothing that differentiate them, except maybe for the main hub area. So I just wandered around hoping that I'll find the right way. I could not rely on the navigation system as  it is extremely confusing, the UI is just messy, I could not even read the name of the nodes, as the captions are so small. In fact, except for a few of them, most are just random trial and error. Developers should have come up with something a little bit more creative. I understand that creators wanted to amplify the terror feeling by adding film grain, distortions and glitch effects to camera, but the final result is overwhelming. I can understand this choice at the beginning of the game, or during cut scenes, but having this graphic aberrations constantly, completely ruins the terror feeling that we are suppose to feel. Luckily is possible to deactivate all these effects on the setting menu. for sure not very original, but it is enjoyable, and maybe to fully understand what happened I should play more than once.I really like the idea to be an AI and be able just to move within the restraint of a computer, is for sure something different, a fresh idea, compared to a lot of games of the genre. Unfortunately the final result does not meet the expectations. It is an experiment, with room for improvement. I suggest to skip this game, but if you want to play it, wait for a discount, it is not worth almost 21 Euros.

_childDocuments_.review: Nearly finished the game. On the last hurdle, I just lost interest. The gameplay, in the end, is quite monotonous and the control needlessly fiddly. _childDocuments_.review: Observation tells a really interesting story in a very cool way, but the gameplay mechanics can be both unenjoyable and frustrating. I would highly recommend it if you enjoy so-called "walking simulators" and can appreciate a cool experience and look past some flaws. If, on the other hand, your primary concern is with fun gameplay I would probably look elsewhere.None of the story elements feel particularly new (if I were to summarize the plot points they would all feel familiar), but I think the execution is very well done and experiencing the story in the way that Observation allowed me to felt novel and like something I personally hadn't experienced before. I was really invested in what was happening the whole time and wanted to see what happened next. There are some particular moments that I think really stand out, not just in terms of narrative plot points but in how they were presented and in my level of immersion and engagement. I personally feel that narratives like this are best experienced without knowing what to expect and so I don't want to spoil anything, but I guess I can safely say that 1) the story involves space and 2) tonally it introduces a feeling of "something is wrong" and then increasing dread. If that piques your interest then stop reading reviews and play it!Unfortunately, the actual mechanics and gameplay have problems. Judging by other reviews and discussion posts I have read after finishing it seems like my reaction isn't unusual, and so I would probably anticipate that if you play Observation you will encounter some frustrations. It feels like the developers had a goal of making more than a movie and wanted to include actual gameplay elements, but then couldn't quite figure out how to create interactions that were rewarding. One of the most baffling decisions to me was how often the challenge of a sequence was just figuring out what was actually expected of me or what buttons to push; not only did this feel distinctly unenjoyable but it didn't even make sense in the context of the game where my character would have known exactly how to do everything. Another strange decision was the amount of memory challenges, which also didn't make sense to me in the context of the game. I appreciate what I think the developers were trying to accomplish but personally feel like I would have preferred a pure walking simulator to what I actually got. I don't want to give the impression that it was all bad; there were definitely sections where I thought the interactivity enhanced my experience, and there's no question that having this be an interactive experience in general increased my enjoyment over if the same story had been told as a movie. I guess I just want to be very clear for anyone who decides to buy and play this based on my recommendation that there are some gameplay flaws that you should be prepared to power through and overlook :)
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: One piece of advice, do not look at the secret achievements before finishing the game, in this case they are secret for a reason!I slept on this for a while but sorry I did as it was a great experience overall - everything works well together; story, characters, voice acting, environment. A really interesting take on a protagonist, as you felt a lot like a side character. I really liked the environmental storytelling. It did mean that the way to progress was subtle, and sometimes I got lost but everything made sense and I was able to progress by looking around and figuring it out as opposed to looking up a guide.Overall, best to go in without knowing much and enjoy the story unfolding!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the closest to an interactive A24 movie that there is. It's so polished and stylish, even if the story is not so groundbreaking. I really like the voice acting too!As for some negatives... well, the puzzles may be a bit confusing at times, especially if you play in separate sessions while waiting a lot time in between them (like I did).Can't wait for Silent Hill Townfall! They are probably one of the best developers when handling atmosphere and art direction, so I'm sure they'll do a great job.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game, but the game play is atrocious as far as adventure games go. You play as SAM, an AI aboard a space station and are tasked with helping and protecting the main character, Emma as she explores the station. Your job is essentially that of an Alexa with a bit more agency -- executing commands per Emma's request, going around the station to accomplish tasks, etc. It's a really cool idea on paper, and besides a few things here and there the story holds up fantastically -- truly like a science fiction movie -- but the whole game is bogged down by awfully slow camera controls, mind numbingly bad flying controls, and the worst direction I've seen in an adventure game in a hot minute. Too much of the game is trying to interpret what it was Emma said without any way to get better information in order to solve a puzzle, and next steps are never straight forward, which can be very frustrating. And to top it all off, there are far too many visual bugs for this kind of game. More than once did I find the UI failing to communicate what was actually on screen so I may interact with it properly which once again, only proceeded to slow down my gameplay. All this experienced in the two hours I played -- game of which felt more like it should've taken a little closer to 30 minutes.This all sucks because of the game I could tolerate, I was truly enjoying the story. So much so I'd rather watch an LP of the game than waste more time bumbling from puzzle to puzzle with little to no progress. I even like the gameplay/puzzles idea of acting as an AI "whose job is to open doors" as it were, but it just requires so much more refinement that I personally can't be bothered to finish playing as it stands.If you can ignore frustrating controls, janky controls and UI, and obtuse puzzle design, you may enjoy this game yet as there is a decent story here. For me though, because of everything else I can't help regretting my purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Very much on the story-rich side of things. Very atmospheric but definitely falls on the walking simulator side of games. My only complaint is it seems to want you to play again multiple times; you're bound to miss those dang documents more than once and there's no way to go back and get them. Outside of that? Outstanding.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Observation is a thriller with a tinge of horror, so part of the joy stems from racing to unravel the next major plot point. It's expertly paced, for the most part, but there are a few instances where slight treasuress can lead you on a point-and-click-adventure-style. Most of Observation is spent peering through lenses, finding points of interest, and scraping for relevant nuggets of information. It's right there in the name!Even the simple act of responding to Emma's queries – poring through menus right out of a classic sci-fi movie, finding the relevant data for the problem at hand, and mousing over to click it with your communication mode enabled – feels substantial. The AI's vocal performance ties the whole game together. I've never experienced a power fantasy like this before.My favorite part of Observation is that it knows not to overwhelm. In the beginning, S.A.M. the AI protagonist, only has access to a portion of his systems, acting as his guiding force, will still have to poke and prod to learn what he is and isn't capable of.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Controls were certainly a bit strange for mouse and keyboard, so I might recommend using a controller though I have yet to test it myself. Other than that small gripe, I loved this game - engaging storytelling is such a rare thing in titles these days, so its great to see No Code once again delivering an amazing and enthralling world to get involved in.It's a walking sim, yes - though such a simplified analogy of it does it some disservice - so if you want a massive sci-fi epic you'll need a different title. However, if you simply want to experience a narrative adventure that draws series inspiration from the likes of 2001: A Space Odyssey, then jump in - your wild ride awaits.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: This game wears the clothes of a game much smarter than this one is.The story is just a hodgepodge of generic sci-fi horror tropes thrown together without much to link them or anything different to make them interesting, It lacks even much horror or atmosphere really.It has some mechanics which a better game would have made more use of, and could have been interesting if done better: You have all this "control" over this station, but really you can only do "X" thing when you're told to, there's way to accidentally ♥♥♥♥ something up and change the story, you'll have infinite attempts at everything. Not much room for a horror game to be scary when you literally can't lose. There are no meaningful decision to make with these mechanics, its basically a series of quicktime events.Character wise, you're barely around any of them long enough to care, so it feels laughable when one mentions they "feel different", like its supposed to be spooky or unnerving or something. You've barely talked with this person, its hard to even tell a difference between them before and after.TLDR: Looks nice, but there's nothing underneath. These writers wanted to make a movie, but work for a game studio, so they threw in token mechanics and make a mediocre walking sim, but in SPAAAAAAACE.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 The puzzles can be tedious and navigating can be frustrating if you're not using a controller.. But the story telling is great. The ending wasn't amazing, but it wasn't terrible, either. Sort of cliche, but still fun.The cosmic horror aspect is done well, the slow burn of the story unraveling itself into a wild climax was a lot of fun. I also appreciated for a horror game, this is pretty chill, and I especially appreciated the lack of cheap tactics like jump scares. There's lot of small, easy to miss details that really expand on the world building, too, so paying attention to everything helps.My biggest con was the puzzles. None of them were terrible, but a few felt nearly impossible, like a frustrating point and click adventure. I used a guide a few times to gather what I needed, but overall it was fun for the few hours it took me to beat. If you were committed to doing everything, I'd guess your playtime would be around 8-10 hours. I played pretty casually and didn't do everything and finished the game in about 5.5 hrs.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed opinions about Observation, a game in the 'Something Goes Wrong in Space' genre. While I enjoyed the beginning and the role of being the station's AI, the frequent lack of a map and controls (especially mouse acceleration) made navigation and certain tasks difficult, and I would have preferred if the story stayed as realistic as the space disaster at the beginning felt.Spoilers!
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like Observation. The visuals and audio are outstanding. The various interfaces all feel real, and the skudgy/broken/lived-in feel of the environment and interfaces were perfectly done. Two things are keeping me from recommending the game, though.First, I know it's a fine line between leading the player to the solution to puzzles intuitively and holding the player's hand and giving them all the solutions. Observation falls on the wrong side of that line too many times, leaving the player with no clues and no option other than (for example) scrolling an image back and forth until the right location pops up on a monitor, or not realizing the reason nothing is happening is one of the NPCs is waiting for a report, or in the case of the  puzzles being unable to complete the puzzles using a keyboard for reasons that I still cannot explain aside from 'If I had a controller I think this would be much easier.'Second is
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Alien: Isolation and I was suffering from a typical withdrawal syndrome you face every time you complete a great game: you want more of that.I stumbled upon Observation almost accidentally: noticed a banner on the store front page. The way it's built resembles the visual style I was looking for, so I clicked. Trailer talks about some accident on a space station, where a woman has to fight for her life. Sounds familiar? Aesthetics, voice, text fonts, music - everything is so warm and familiar after the Alien game, so I had no other choice, but to buy Observation.After finishing the story I read that some developers worked on Alien: Isolation and you can clearly see where they took inspiration. In a good way. This is not a cheap copy without xenomorphs, but a solid work in a similar genre.Be ready, because your character is not an astronaut. You're an  on-board computer, Harry! Gameplay is built around switching through different station modules to resolve some issues and identify what's going on along the way. In order to enable or disable a station's internal system, you have to play one of mini-games, perfectly stylized and blended with the given setting. It may not sound like a big fun, but it keeps you engaged.Meanwhile, the story unfolds step by step revealing dark secrets, going from adventure to horror. You won't get clear answers on what happened before, what is happening now and what is gonna happen next. By that I don't imply that the ending is anti-climatic, no. Observation is like a well-balanced short-story. It will make you wondering.I enjoyed this game and can definitely recommend it to anyone, who is in fond of mystic stories, horror elements, loves space aesthetics. Observation won't make you sweat in terms of gameplay, but for sure it will stay in your heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Not my cup of tea actually like WTF?I still have no idea what this was about after playing to the end. There was no suspense here because by the time you wait for a scene to happen you are just waiting for ANYTHING else to happen. Why do ppl think it is fun to open/close doors or activate stuff in a space station? There is so much lack of "how to play" in this game, you have to play a puzzle a couple of times until you finally figure out how to get it. Even as I got to about the last hour of the game I finally figured out how to go about and do things AND EVEN THEN the direction of what to do was a tad foggy. I seriously think possibly 2 or 3 hours are just trying to figure out how to do the puzzles, otherwise this would be a short game.Now there were times I had to quit, its a long game and I didn't know where I would be starting back from. Sometimes I was pretty far back and once I got on the mark when I needed to quit the game. And while the story, literally the only thing that I was wanting to keep playing to get, was getting good I have no idea what any of the beg-mid-end means. So if you like technical games where you have to tinker around or figure things out on your own (or have to look at someone else's play through) then by all means this is the game for you. There will be frustration, there will be lack of information and most of all you will be left alone on a space station wondering why this is happening.

_childDocuments_.review: A really tedious experience, non-analogue controller movement, horrible KB/M controls, constant crashing (game even crashed when I turned on my controller). At some point you can see multiple points of interest that should count as progressing the objective, but the game wants you to specifically click on a tiny portion of the whole panel otherwise nothing shows up. Constantly changing resolution and settings. Bad design all around. Would not recommend whatsoever.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: A thought-provoking and tightly-made puzzle game, where the main challenge is working out how to solve the simple puzzles the game gives you. You are the AI helping pilot a space station, and what starts as simply opening doors and flipping switches in response to an emergency becomes a rather baffling journey into weirdness. If you get frustrated with narratives that don't explain everything, this game might annoy you, since it doesn't tie up all the loose ends and leaves a lot of what's going on to conjecture. It's always interesting and well-made and the characters come through well. My playthrough lasted about 5 hours and I found it an interesting narrative and atmospheric experience well worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: pros:-great graphics, sound, authentic feeling space station interiorscons:-aggressively bland gameplay-bad keyboard controls have you constantly reaching over to hit backspace and enter-convoluted storythe game mainly consists of you looking around with painfully slow swiveling cameras reading computer screens and post it notes.  then some spooky stuff happens and you continue to do that.  sometimes you get a little hover orb and you read screens with that.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Okay. This game is fine, the story line is good and very atmospheric. I like the difficulty of the puzzles, they're doable. Of course, I do have my share of disappointment with the game. Navigating where is where is kinda hard, or maybe it's just me having a bad sense of direction. I also have some problems with the controls. Maybe it's my fault for using a keyboard instead of a controller because I think I need to use controller for the game? But holy heck, using keyboard shouldn't be this frustrating. There are some puzzles I couldn't even complete because I couldn't do it quickly enough on keyboard, like the circle puzzle one. I couldn't do the diagonal ones. The sphere is also so hard to control using a mouse, not to mention the amount of motion sickness it gives me, I keep bumping the sphere against the wall. And it's kinda frustrating too how there's no way for me to stop the sphere from swinging too much. There are also times when the visual is a little later than the audio, they don't sync well. In conclusion, good and enjoyable story but painful controls for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I must have misread the game or misunderstood it but i was hoping to play something similar to "Give us the moon" which i loved and want to play many times over. This is not it or even similar in any way. Waste of money. I did not sign up to play a blood AI camera controls, i wanted to play the astronaut. No instructions or hints whatsover. _childDocuments_.review: Decent sci-fi game if on sale.Semi-short with mini-game like puzzles along the way.The atmosphere is great, but just mysterious from beginning to end.Controls are slightly clunky by design, and I have no qualms about it.However I did get lost a few times due to all the locations looking similar aside from the disorientation of space.Not to mention the map is kinda difficult to view due to blurry/small text.Overall felt like watching a 6 or 7/10 movie.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Observation is like if 2001: A Space Odyssey, Oblivion, and Interstellar all wrapped up into one. As some one who loves narrative-drive games this is honestly one of my favorites. It plays and reads like a movie and I had a blast playing it, or well more experiencing it. There are some really cool puzzles in the game and there is not a moment (outside of cutscenes) where you are not trying to solve a puzzle. Time the I have on a record is the rough time to complete the game if you also take your time and look around a little. The zero-g effect can be disorienting at times but that just makes the atmosphere and immersion even better. The replay ability is null and it is really on how often you would want to what a movie again. That is what this is, a cinematic experience that you are a part of and I think it is so cool. For those wondering no this is NOT a walking simulator. I would love to see more games like this. 9/10 from me[EDIT]: I forgot to mention just how good this game looks too! It looks amazing. The main characters face is a little strange but you learn to ignore it. I am running a RTX 2060 and saw no lag (except for when my laptop was unplugged).
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I could describe this game as a mixture of the following titles: Annihilation (film), Gravity (film), Republique (game). The game is simple though some puzzles can be a nuisance...they can't really be called puzzles more like... getting lost in the clutter. Because of this, the end can feel like an unsatisfying edging session. But in general, i love the idea, the artwork is amazing, the concept of the game mechanic is fun, however the challenge is NOT in how big your brain's ♥♥♥♥ is regarding ''puzzles''. If you like puzzle games, you might find this too easy. The actual puzzle (or nuisance...take your pick) is in how "big" your hippocampus is. (Also, if you find that navigation in a game about being in a zero gravity environment is indeed a nuisance, then i am afraid you are criticising a Western for not being Musical enough. )All in all, it is a short lovely game, i recommend it.....to BRING HER!

_childDocuments_.review: I will be honest with you, the current game market, in my opinion, is overly saturated by developers not actually caring for their game except the availability of ingame transactions and all that kinda stuff. Of course there are exceptions but it really is ♥♥♥♥ this isn't it?This game is an absolute gem. I found the story stunning and interesting, not only because it is well written, also because it leaves space (heh) for interpretation. I mean being literally the good Hal 9000 is such an interesting concept because you are actually the space station that you are on. Its so refreshing seeing that, its just something different than being some random grunt or person, trying to fight their way through the end. And I honestly wish that this entire "control ai" thing would be used much more often. Even more now after I have played this game. For the most part the game consists of puzzles that are not overly hard or easy, they are perfect for the game flow, in my opinion. I never actually felt like I am doing a puzzle but more of like fulfilling my duty as an AI.The atmosphere (heh.. okay I stop) is really something, the visuals look stunning even on lower graphical settings and the music is just.. fitting.. like exceptionally well fitting. And this progressive bulid up on a situation sometimes gave me goosebumps. The game is not overly scary its more like.. the game makes you feel uneasy. I mean cope with the fact that around you is nothing but death. Get the game and you will understand what I mean.Regardless of all the epic games stuff whatever.. this game is formidable. For all fans of sci-fi thrillers this is a must buy.Thanks for your attention. have a wonderful day/night- Kapu

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I loved this game. The presentations, the visuals, the dialogue delivery, the exploration. Everything is amazing, but…I found the puzzles to be just an annoyance and waste of time. Really, there were moments in which I was so involved with the story and the exploration just to be distracted from those things because I got very frustrated with an annoying puzzle had no contribution to the narrative at all. Fortunately, the puzzles are only a small part of the game. This is hardly a problem exclusive to this game, but nonetheless, this is the caveat.Nonetheless (again), I still highly recommend this one if you are into narrative-driven games and also if you like space stuff.
