_childDocuments_.review: Avoid. Gameplay is overly complicated and not fun. Nothing is engaging here. Too bad I'm past the refund window.Edit: now that I have finished the game, I have to say that this is the worst game I've ever played in my life. It's like the game was never play tested to check if the game mechanics were fun. The game is loaded of bugs on top. I can't understand the positive reviews, which were what convinced me to get the game. What were you smoking?
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: While not free from some minor frustrations (ISS is unintuitive to navigate in and some puzzle solutions are obscure), this is one of the best games that balances being a video game and an interactive movie, combining both (tense narration and quality writing for the "movie" part & generally fantastic and atmospheric puzzles for the "gaming" part) parts and kind of becoming "the best of two worlds". I wish more games like this were made. Certainly worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty neat game! If we were able to actually give stars, I'd give it 4/5. This is mainly due to a certain type of mini-game (ahem ), during which I was pretty much forced to switch to a controller lest I fail the mission, and I do prefer the keyboard/mouse over controller. Anyways, I do recommend this game with the caveat of using the controller at certain points. Overall, was a new and interesting game that I enjoyed playing. Cheers!  =)
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: this is an amazing piece of sci-fi immersive theatre. Buy if you love ambience, sci-fi and walking simulators. Do not buy if you want: lots of complicated puzzles or horror.Wow. It's rare I get a game and within two minutes I'm hooked, but Observation did that. You wake up as an AI on board a space station, and the story unfolds from there.The design is just sublime. I played for almost 10 hours, which is a lot more than people who complained the game was short. I could have been quicker, but part of that was me just wandering around looking. Looking at everything. Looking out the window. Looking at documents. Looking at... everything.That's immediately one of the great things about this game. While it's scripted and the story points will move you along - there's no choices as such - it doesn't rush you. You can wander at your own rate. You feel in control.There's a really good, solid sci-fi story at the heart of this. I won't say much as it will spoil the story. But as a lifelong sci-fi fan, the story was well crafted and mysterious.The atmosphere and design is where the game excels. The 'sets' are very realistic. The amount of detail in just about everything shows a labour of love. From the fonts, to the interfaces, to even down to something stupid like you're accessing a system where they've gone to the trouble of making it look like a broken 1990s web interface. It's just amazing.These developers know style and mood and context and it shows it.It is a walking simulator. I love them, not everyone does. The puzzles are not really that, they are more interactions to make you feel connected with the story and environment. That's why I describe this more as a piece of immersive theatre. I felt I was there. I felt invested. The characters spoke to me. This was my story. Thankfully it didn't go into horror. Menace yes, and freaky at times. Only one what I would call jump scare. I don't want intense horror - this game kept me on edge, but nicely so. There were a few grumbles. A times it was not clear what I was meant to do and I resorted to some online guides. It could be frustratingly ambiguous at times. But, those were minor - and you can look up online for help. I also wouldn't have objected to the puzzles being more like actual puzzles that require some problem solving. A couple of the 'puzzles' are more like quicktime events which are not my favourite form of gameplay! But again, these were minor annoyances.But in short, I loved this. If you want to feel immersed into a story-based sci-fi experience which is almost a movie, buy now without delay. I feel at a loss now it's ended. I want more.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this, it's not up there with Stories Untold for me unfortunately as I really enjoyed that and Observation definitely has some big negatives as well as positives.Positives:- A lot of free exploration of your environment to find data which adds extra to the story- Fun puzzles where you feel like some kind of coding/engineering genius- Interesting story- Creepy atmosphereNegatives:- Horrible to play on keyboard, I switched to a PS4 controller right at the end because of an issue i'll list below and it was SO much better and smoother!- This is a pretty big issue! If you play on a keyboard then as far as I can tell there is no way to solve the 'thruster' puzzles at the beginning and end of the game which are essential to progress. It's fine on a controller.- The animation of the people is a little 'uncanny valley' especially when you're close up to their face- Sometimes you spend an absolute age trying to figure out what you need to do next as instructions can be incredibly vague and the interface can be confusing.- There is one door you cannot unlock as when you look at the schematic it shows you the one for the coolant system instead of the door lock system! I tried using the usual unlock sequence but it doesn't work (you don't actually NEED to unlock it but I wanted to unlock all doors to see if there was an achievement, I'm guessing this is a 'bug' of sorts?).Overall a fun game and i'd say well worth the sale price but i'm not sure i'd want to pay over £20 for it as it's not really that long.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, interesting game, gameplay is decent, but the graphics are so insane that you might have to look out your real-life windows every so often to remember what world you're actually in. Pick it up on a sale, imo. And don't hesitate to quickly check a guide if you don't really understand what to do next! Sometimes it's really a crapshoot to tell what you need, but the game is worthwhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: CONS: It's not really a game. It's a BARELY interactive movie. And if you're expecting any kind of real payoff, you won't get one.The plot is vague, but far shallower than it thinks it is. It's nothing that hasn't been done before, and better.The controls are truly horrendous. For what is effectively a point-and-click adventure with some puzzles thrown in, it went out of its way to make POINTING and CLICKING as difficult and awkward as possible. Whether it's dragging yourself through a painfully slow camera interface, or piloting a drone in zero-G that can somehow maintain perfect position without input but NOT maintain consistent orientation, everything about the controls are incredibly clunky.The puzzles themselves aren't so much clever or difficult as much as they rely on you having no idea what you're supposed to do. Once you clear that basic step they're about as complex as a 2-piece jigsaw puzzle.The sound design was... I didn't like it. I might have if the constant sense of urgency had been combined with some real sense of AGENCY. The game is over half cutscene. Tension dissipates to nothing when you're forced to sit and wait and watch what happens without ANY control over the situation. ...And I'm sorry, but "Weird black tentacles of corruption" is kind of done to death at this point. They literally added nothing to the story and could have been omitted entirely.Pros: It's pretty. Good graphics, decent design. That's... pretty close to it.All in all, it had some neat ideas (running everything from the perspective of the station A.I. had a LOT of potential), but failed to execute worth a damn. It's all a lot of pretense at profundity without any real substance.Maybe you'll enjoy it more. But I was sorely disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere in this game is just genius!What I love about it is that it's true science fiction, pure unadulterated realistic sci-fi, with that Gravity/space Odyssey/alien interference/rogue AI feel. You play as the station's AI and basically observe the events unfolding by hacking laptops, ship's systems and using camera's and small robots (spheres) to move around and outside of the space station. The station basically uses current ISS like technology in the near future which makes it look so realistic. I won't spoil anything of the story but it's 'Event Horizon' meets 'Space Odyssey' meets 'The Expanse'.Also: It really won't hold your hand. You need to use your brain and 'just do it' and things will become logical. They're all logical systems, push through your uncertainty/ignorance/frustration and you'll figure things out; and the sense of accomplishment is awesome!So much recommended for sci-fi fans!Did you like 'Moon'?Did you like 'Space Odyssey'Did you like 'Event Horizon'Did you like 'Gravity'Did you like the vintage game called 'Descent'Did you own a Commodore C64 or Amiga, or Atari, or ZX etc.. vintage computer and love how those games did not spoon feed you on how to play the game?If you answered 'yes' to any of these questions then just pick up this game and support the developers.It's worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Cool ideas and interesting execution.You can take your time and have many tries with majority of puzzles. There are only a few that do have it timed until you "fail it".  The game itself is rather gorgeous looking. However, there are a few moments when human faces hit the uncanny valley (It hits the uncanny valley when characters mostly try to convey emotions of shock). The game itself is not all that long, I would advise to grab it when it is on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: The controls make me feel like I got really wasted and tried to fly a drone. The camera moves too slow. Sometimes you end up searching around endlessly because there are no waypoints and the ending is a little weak. Despite all of that I absolutely think you should play this game. It's near instantly captivating and as soon as you've hit the first big cutscene you won't want to stop until you've discovered the secrets that exist in this space station for you. Give it a go, it a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Stories Untold developer! In Observation you have control over the AI of a space station. Sounds boring? Not at all! You control the game via cameras and drones, which allows you to explore the station and interact with objects like notes or computer systems.The game also throws you right into the middle of the story. After an unknown incident, you will meet Emma, who may (?) be the only survivor. The space station is heavily damaged, the status of the crew is unknown. Help her to repair systems, prevent catastrophes and find out what happened.Graphics and sound are very good and harmonic, partly creepy. The puzzles range from easy to challenging and are very various. The game does not take you by the hand, you must show initiative. There is a certain help but mostly you have to find out yourself how things works.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game on sale, played it through in one sitting, and oh my F*****G GOD this game is amazing. This was one of the coolest experiences I have had in any video game. The story, voice acting, puzzles, it's all absolutely stellar. There are sometimes little visual bugs (characters phasing into the walls), but to be honest, that didn't really affect my enjoyment of the game. If anything, it made the experience feel so much weirder. TLDR: Best game I've played in a long time. If it's on sale buy it immediately because it's a steal. Well worth full price if you can afford it tho.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to enjoy . The story is compelling, and you'll want to know what happens next... but it's spread too thin, across too much uninteresting gameplay. More often than not, I felt like I was doing chore lists just to be allowed to progress.I hate to say this, because  is a novel experience and I'd like to see developers rewarded for taking chances and not simply churning out another samey, derivative product... but skip buying this one and watch a playthrough on YouTube instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in anticipation of a well polished, well thought out, and cleverly designed story driven game with some kind of arbitrary, but ultimately enjoyable gameplay-loop. What I received instead was a game, which, in favour of the creation of a dark and gloomy atmosphere and an impressive visual experience, seemed to disregard a lot of “best-practice” methods regarding gameplay, level-design and readability that would ensure intuitive understanding and fast, but rewarding execution of tasks at hand. The stark contrast between the almost vast, visually convoluted and difficult to gauge gameplay-area and the very strictly linear and specifically pointed story-progression that disallowed any interaction that wasn’t bound to the given task created not only a disincentive to explore the space-station on  the players terms, thus achieving a sense of wasted time when not trying to progress the main story, but also demanded, for the lack of visual nudging or clever establishment of gameplay features a la 'The Witness', a clear and instructive way of ordering and communicating the tasks the player was to carry out. This was not provided, which effectively took away the astonishment that had set in through the general created sense of immersion and replaced it with slowly building up frustration. More than once I found myself going about scanning rooms for tokens to interact with only to find the majority of these to be unavailable and, after an excruciatingly long time of trying to figure out what exactly to interact with, finding some arbitrary detail on the wall to be what I was looking for. This general missing sense of direction and the game’s unwillingness to provide hints or pointers would become a trope throughout the progression of the game, which led me to learn that the best approach of solving any issue was to mindlessly cycle through every gameplay-mechanic provided to find the eventual fit for the situation in the given room. This became to be a very unrewarding and tedious progression, as the gameplay-loops provided were basic to say the least and more than once relied upon quick-time events to achieve a sense of difficulty. The obviously '2001: A Space Odyssey'-inspired story in itself, though very projected, riddled with cliché and developing some moderately pretentious vibes, did find its place and was assisted nicely by the audiovisual experience, creating an incentive to achieve the tasks given and assisting in the upholding of the general immersion. In conclusion, I can NOT recommend buying this game, unless you’re willing to go to great lengths to enjoy the decent story it has. Observation, though aspiring to greatness, ultimately falls short of achieving something truly commendable in my eyes. If you are looking for a short, immersive, story-driven experience in a space/horror/mystery setting, look no further than The Station, if you want to have fun trying to figure out cleverly thought out puzzles lovingly implemented in a refreshingly open environment, I strongly advise you to take a look at the Witness. Before you buy this game, at least take those into consideration. Anyways, that’s my two cents on the matter. If not for this binary review system, I would give the game a 2.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game if you wait for a sale. The storytelling in this game is effective and unique, but it is very light on gameplay and what is there is often tedious. Controlling the sphere is hell, and I can't believe it made it into the game apart from the fact that it's needed for some cutscenes. This game doesn't really overstay its welcome, but it does start to get a little repetitive towards the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Count this amongst "games I was enthused about but rapidly disappointed by". A fascinating concept completely let down by execution.The objectives are frequently unclear and underwhelming when you get to them. Puzzles aren't explained - you need to figure out how to do the puzzle, and then do it. Which doesn't sound so bad - hey, I like a challenging puzzle - except that you're given no hint to work out, and not much of a challenge. It's less "use the clues to figure out a solution" than "figure out where and what to click, then do it in the correct order/do a QTE". I could live with this, if not for the amount of screen flashing and video popping (for lack of a better term, like an old VHS tape). The screen flashes after every single menu you tab out of, and the screen decides to pop at regular intervals, no matter what you're doing. Between the two, I was left dizzy and with headaches. It ends up looking like a blurry recording of a Rammstein show in the worst way possible. I've been playing all manner of games for over 25 years, and this is the only one to ever give me a headache, and one of only a handful to make me dizzy. To have them together is quite a feat. Combine these with the underwhelming gameplay, and it just wasn't worth my time. I've requested a refund. A shame, because it looks great (aside from the facial animations), and the voice acting is very well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Observation excelled at providing that sci-fi atmosphere, mysterious circumstances and intrigue into what exactly is going on. While not the most straight forward narrative, it's got some interesting ideas, and it's never dull. My two major complaints about the experience was the controls were hard to get used to, even to the end. I tried a controller and mouse and keyboard, and neither felt "right". It always felt like I was fighting against the game to just do what I want in any given situation, and that was immersion breaking.Second, I found some of the puzzles frustrating, especially because I found the story interesting, so being interrupted with very vague and uninteresting puzzles was frustrating at times.The more I think on it after having finished the game, the more the story grows on me, and I think some of my frustrations with the controls and my inability to find my way around the station, or solve some of the puzzles in a timely fashion may have lead to me being in a less than perfect mood, which had an impact on my overall opinion. I think this game would lend itself well to a replay down the road, to rexperience the story, having knowledge of it's systems and puzzles, and being slightly more familiar with the environment.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere of the game is fascinating, I liked it very much. Story is not bad. But the gameplay... It literally drove me crazy at first because the game just tells you what to do but not HOW to do, there is not even a clue. After playing for a while (it gives some clues then) you get used to it and start to figure out how you can complete your tasks. Still, I suggest you take a look at it if you are into sci-fi stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Observation is a great narrative and a very good thriller!This is a great mix of ideas and atmosphere, in my opinion from three great films and books: Knowing (2009 with Nicolas Cage) + Solaris by Stanislav Lem, and 2001: A Space Odyssey by Arthur Clarke and Stanley Kubrick.Many thanks to the developers for such a gift. Although the game is short and rather simple, it leaves behind a pleasant bouquet of emotions, goosebumps, a whole bunch of questions. And yet, you can see how the developers were inspired and successfully convey this feeling further to us.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: If you played Stories Untold you already know what to expect. If not, it's a story-based game with puzzles, horror atmosphere and plot twists. You explore the spaceship using the cameras and sometimes a little robot.I really recommend it to people who like sci-fi/horror stories and puzzles, but the puzzles can become really annoying sometimes. Most of the time you are "bodyless" and cannot explore the environment like in other puzzle/horror games such as Amnesia or Outlast, so if you are not a fan of puzzles the horror/sci-fi element alone may not be enough for you to enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I am too dumb to be able to finish Observation. I don't mostly understand what the game wants me to do (hints are not clear enough, way too abstract). Searching for items (documents, schematics, notes, etc) and solving puzzles is really boring, while the game has such uncomfortable, awkward controls. The levels are quite small, since they are placed on a confined orbital station, but controls make it almost impossible to enjoy exploring. The sci-fi plot is intriguing; main character, Emma Fisher, despite lack of rich facial animations, is quite charismatic; the atmosphere of a loneliness, an extending catastrophe and an escalating despair in the deep space is tense... But the game design, unfortunately, ruins it all.The game also, for whatever reason, from time to time was changing a resolution from Full HD to lower ones, which was quite annoying, but not as much as the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a quick game with interesting puzzles and story, Observation is the game for you. I was able to finish the game in 6 hours, but I loved every second of it. The puzzles were thought provoking and the story kept me guessing what was going to happen next. The premise of playing as the AI on a space station was what we really drew me in, and the experience was so much fun. 10/10 would play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: All in all I had a lot of fun and I would warmly recommend for anyone else looking for eerie sci-fi mysteries. You advance the story in a very natural way and in your own pace (although alarms are sometimes stressing you on). I found the story unpredictable and interesting to follow to start from finish. I was constantly on edge, not knowing what would happen or who to trust. I also generally liked the puzzle mechanics and piecing together information, except for a few puzzles where quick reflexes were required. The biggest downside I would like to mention is the segments where you move freely. Usually you follow what happens via CCTV:s, but there are a few exceptions. Those segments were very disorienting and the constant camera flickering in those can definitely induce headaches. If you're not used to WASD-controls, be prepared for some difficult maneuvering.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really great. I played the whole thing in one sitting cos I couldn't stop playing. The story is thrilling and mysterious. The graphics are super realistic. The atmosphere is so creepy which is exactly what I was hoping for. The thing that impressed me the most was the voice acting, sounds and lighting, all were really good.Some people won't like the ending but if you want a really gripping, immersive and unique experience, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Just give me Observation 2. People keep complaining about disorienting camera but I felt like this is what space stations should feel like. It is very loyal to realism aspect of game play and you can always rest your eyes for a few seconds, game does not rush you into anything unless you start a sequence with very obvious warnings beforehand. There are no fail conditions other than retrying a time attack sequence which is 15 seconds maximum. A very chill, relaxed game which also makes you go "wtf" very often. Keeps you interested through successful storytelling.9/10 would recommend.*-1 for some minor pacing issues on a few chapters of the game*
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting and mind-bending narrative game with puzzle elements, and a story I found both compelling yet also a little too abstract for myself. The puzzles are generally fairly easy (time-based puzzles are a part of this game, though). I had to look up the solution for one or two puzzles, particularly one of the final ones as it's abstract, but also one of the earlier puzzles is prone to bugging out.Overall I'm glad I gave this another chance and I very much enjoyed playing it, but I do feel any meaning to the story went over my head.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Observation is a very strange animal - but in a good way. Consider it more as an interactive movie than a full-fledged game and you won't be disappointed.- Great atmosphere, if you’re a fan of such movies as Contact, Event Horizon, Ad Astra, Gravity and Alien series you’re in for a treat- Surprisingly well written and recorded dialogues- Music emphasizing but not overwhelming the atmosphere-Design with a very authentic feel-Game is not hand-holding the player, you need to connect dots by yourself (true for both gameplay and story)-Not a horror game, but has a lot of suspenseLittle to do gameplay-wise, minigames are nicely done but get tiresome after a while-Nothing can prepare you for the deadliest boss of the game – navigating and controls- Strange story transitions at times- Dialogues feel unnaturally calm at times- Ending leaves a few unsolved story points
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal game.The plot reminds both 2001: A Space Odyssey and Gravity movies stitched together in a game, but from the AI perspective, which is very interesting and fresh gameplay design. Also for me the story was as thrilling and interesting as SOMA's was.Sadly, some actual gameplay moments and puzzles could be made much better and easy to understand, but the story, atmosphere and point of view more than enough make up for it.Another specimen, proving that games are still a piece of art, not a conveyer of identical plastic "AAA" crap.In conclusion this game is a must-have for all gamers with a good taste.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: This product works better as a movie rather than a video game. The story is interesting but the gameplay is too clumsy and slow and completely kills the tension built up by the moments of action, also that the controls seem better adapted to use them on the console than on the PC. Again, it is not a bad game but it would be a better movie since it is simply an interactive cinematic.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Elden Ring was difficult but in a fun way. Observation's difficulty begins with the unintuitive controls and poor communication. The last straw was losing a huge chunk of progress after resetting the game when controls became partially unresponsive.Potentially interesting story marred by ♥♥♥♥ software. Don't buy even when on discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this! Some great and weird sci-fi with some rather disturbing cosmic horror sprinkled in. The story is very engaging, and there's a marriage of narrative and gameplay that is rare to find. It's a simple game to play, it can get disorienting at times but I'm okay with it as it matches the setting. The puzzles are clearly reminiscent of what this team made in 'Stories Untold'. It's kind of an expansion on what that game brought to the table.I'm now unbelievably excited for Silent Hill Townfall.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: The story and atmosphere seemed good, but being scolded for not quickly figuring out what to do under pressure was too annoying. This could have been a great game if the controls weren't so terrible (but I guess that maybe adds realism). And the key rebinding was limited, such as not being able to assign various keys including the keypad keys, which would have been incredibly helpful.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I finally got around to Observation after years of letting it gather dust in my steam backlog, and it is a shame I ignored it until now. Some reviewers have suggested the game is not exactly fun, its mechanics not exactly well communicated. If you are looking for a more conventional type of game experience, this criticism would be true. What Observation delivers to an incredible degree is atmosphere, by way of immersive sound design, UI, screen effects/post processing, and excellent voice acting. The limited pace of fixed camera movement and the disorienting process of navigating a camera sphere are a constant reminder that everything is complicated to do in space. Observation is a game I went to bed thinking about and woke up still thinking about the next day.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on the edge on wheter I wanna recommend this game (if it's on sale) or not. While I did have fun playing it, it definitely has quite a few problems and a lot of wasted potential.Story: the story is based on an interesting premise and had me engaged while playing for the most part. But as the game progresses the story is so "mysterious" that it really leaves out any and all detail, while simultaneously just throwing more and more concepts into the mix to keep things going. In the end it's just another generic and rather incohesive mystery scifi story. (There's a bunch of fully voice acted lore-collectibles to find though which is nice.)Graphics, Audio etc.: aside from some odd animations graphics and audio are generally great. The game manages to create a good, immersive atmosphere.Gameplay: the gameplay is essentially 10 simple minigames in a trenchcoat. There's never any actual weight on what you do and the game is fully railroaded even though it likes to pretend giving you a choice from time to time. As for the minigames themselves: it has everything from "remember these 3 symbols", "enter this 3-digit number that you're looking at right now", "click all the red squares in this image", "hold this button for 5 seconds, then also this one for another 5 seconds, now release them one after another" and more things like that. Most of them aren't repeated *that* often that it becomes super annoying but it's still not great imo.Controls: the game is splits into you either controlling some camera / systems of the station directly and flying around in a robot sphere. The first part is perfectly fine but ♥♥♥♥♥♥ that sphere. The basic controls in the sphere are clunky, but I could see that being a conscious design decision and its manageable and not the end of the world. The thing that really  bothered me however, was that the sphere constantly started spinning on its own and has a nonconfigurable FOV of about 0.5° while having a tendency to shine a super bright light onto reflective surfaces directly in front of your face. Those points combined to make for an *incredibly* motion sickness inducing experience. This was so bad that I had to stop playing and lie down after every longer sphere section.Save-system: the game is entirely checkpoint based while lacking any indication for when you reached a checkpoint. In particular there were no checkpoints at times where I absolutely would've expected one (i.e. after something big had happened in the story). This combined with the lack of save-on-exit and the sphere-sickness problem from above lead to me having to replay some longish sections on multiple occasions.The game also has problems remembering settings apparently, resetting the configured resolution on every restart and on some savegame loads. This seems to be a well known issue that the devs just don't bother fixing.I think to close things off it's worth going into the time of actual gameplay you get:if you cut out all the waiting times etc. from the mini games (like for example having to wait for a random 3-digit combination of 1,2,3,4 to be generated so you can type it back in - which you have to do anytime you interact with some device for the first time which happens a lot), duplicate playtimes caused by having to replay sections due to the bad save system, flying around aimlessly because you don't know what you're supposed to be doing (there's a "repeat last instruction" command but those instructions aren't always helpful) etc. there's maybe 3-ish hours of gameplay left making this game 7€/h. I'm generally okay with shorter games and certainly prefer them to drawn out ones but oof. That's excessive.All in all: like I said there certainly is some fun to be had while playing it - but in the end it felt very unstatisfying to me, especially considering the relatively high price it currently goes for. The story seems interesting but really is rather weak and takes the "ooohhh it's mystery" escape-route way too often imo. The gameplay is pretty weak and there's a number of technical problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this game a sideways thumb.Observation is not a good game. To be fair, it isn't trying to be. What it's trying to be is a movie.It tries really, really hard to be a movie.But it isn't. It's a game. And as such, I find it lacking.The controls are alright. The gameplay is simple. It is perfectly linear. It plays out as a very simple point and click adventure. You play from the perspective of an AI, and it's mostly told entirely from a First person point of view. Unfortunately, since it's trying very, very hard to be a movie, the game loves to take away control from you periodically in order to get big cinematic cutscenes without player interference. It's okay to do this, but really ruins the "first person perspective" running throughout the rest of the game. You can have one or the other, and in trying to do both it just falls flat.But it's okay if the game kinda isn't good, right? Because it's trying to be a movie, to convey a cinematic experience. So surely the story holds up?Well, only if you think "2001, but much worse" is a story worth telling. I fall in the "no" camp on this one.The graphics are great, though the music choice is.... quite bad. Very loud, very unsubtle.In the end, it comes down to how much you want a short, linear, cinematic sci-fi experience. I understand that making a game is much, much cheaper than filming a movie with this same script, and there are things to appreciate here. I just didn't think it was all quite worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Better review Observation is set upon an international space station where a disaster causes damage to the station and for Dr Emma Fisher to lose contact with the crew. Managing to bring online the Systems Administration and Maintenance computer (S.A.M) she uses it to aid her in discovering the crew and what happened.  You play the role of S.A.M accessing cameras around the station and becoming Dr Fisher’s eyes and ears. Later, you will connect to a sphere which can move around the station assisting Emma in running the station and bringing it back to life. I really enjoyed Observation. It is successful in creating an eerie, desperate, claustrophobic and mysterious atmosphere from beginning to end. There are some quiet periods where you have to navigate around the tight corridors and solve some puzzles but it all felt necessary and part of the plan. It is quite easy to get lost in the maze of corridors, especially as the orb can rotate, causing disorientation. There is a map to help you in most circumstances which is vital in gaining your bearings. You will be checking it a lot. I did spend a great deal of time flying around trying to locate the issues reported. Part of the puzzle is finding alternative routes which can be difficult, and due to the station looking so similar you can easily retrace your steps without realizing. It all adds to the confinement and confusion you feel whilst carrying out your tasks. Whilst fixing some of the issues I felt like an astronaut. The puzzles are cleverly designed to fit in with the story and involve schematics, powering on devices and general tasks that felt like you were performing an astronaut’s duties.There is quite a lot of lore introduced to you by exploring the station and finding personal items, documents and hacking laptops. The more you find, the more complete the story feels. A lot of it is trivial but it fills in gaps and reveals the feelings the crew were experiencing at the time.Being the on-board computer felt original and there was a good rapport between S.A.M and Dr Fisher. The computer took on an almost human personality and you felt there was an emotional connection between the two characters, even though one was not alive.The sound and graphics are superb in places with excellent voice acting, even from S.A.M. Although brief, I loved the scenes outside the space station and it was a harsh contrast from the tight corridors and segmented sections to the vast and endless space outside. The story was intriguing and was paced brilliantly up to the exciting ending. I would say I did have a few questions at the end but then again sci-fi does tend to throw up a lot of doubts. You are S.A.M (Systems Administration and Maintenance computer), brought back online to aid Dr Emma Fisher in recovering the broken systems on the space station. Initially, you are able to access cameras in the station and inform Dr Fisher of any faults and to carry out diagnostics on her behalf. There are a number of cameras in each section located in different parts of the area. Switching between these cameras will reveal fresh outlooks and reveal problems some cameras cannot see. Moving the camera around you can highlight these issues and report them to Emma.Sometimes, reporting the issue is not enough and you will need to fix them. There are a variety of different things to fix from opening doors that are locked to powering on systems and dealing with station alerts. I could describe the fixing process as brief mini games. Some are quick time events or similar, but the majority will need documentation found around the station to complete. Dealing with doors requires schematics which are usually pinned to the walls nearby. You have to draw the shape required to unlock, open, close or lock the door causing the obstruction. It isn’t very difficult.Later, you will be able to take control of a sphere and physically fly through the space station between the four segments. The sphere can move in any direction and does feel quite disorientating as you fly past things which are upside down or tilted. The sphere can fly through vents to access areas otherwise obstructed. There is a bit of exploration to enjoy with numerous pieces of documentation, personal items and objects to examine and read. Dotted throughout the station are laptops which can be accessed and their contents inspected. Laptops usually hide voice messages from one crew member to another or detail concerns over procedures and events which happened. Some of these laptops require passwords which you need to find. Items collected all get stored in SAM’s communication core where they can be reviewed and consulted. Certain documents and voice messages can be combined to reveal new clues and revelations. Apart from successfully navigating the station, which can be troublesome, the puzzles are generally manageable without too much effort. There is one puzzle however, that is almost impossible without a walk-through so you may find yourself stuck when trying to find the array co-ordinates. The answer is readily available online however.The game took me around eleven hours to complete.Graphics are beautiful with realistic gravity free animations on characters, and a nice HUD for SAM which flickers when you hit objects. The feeling of weightlessness is evident and impressively showcased.The outside space sequences are stunning also. The station feels tight and restricted and appears realistic. The chambers are similar in appearance which can cause disorientation when navigating.Great sound effects which really ramp up tension and authenticity. It has an awesome sci-fi feel to the game. Characters voice acting is very professional and special effects all sound impressive.Curator Info:

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game.  A unique perspective and set of actions that told a gripping narrative.  But boy was I let down.Firstly some positives:  Sound design is top notch, as is the 3D interior and character.  That's pretty much it.Problems I had:  Zero explanation for anything.  After the first "puzzle" which I had to look up how to solve because the game had not explained the use of the R key very clearly, if at all, you are dumped on with a ton of extra controls.  These are not consistent either.  The puzzle progression is more of a cliff.I got to point where I needed to do a module separation and despite using a keyboard, nothing happened and got shouted at by the main character in the space station.  This annoyed me as the puzzle had a hint, but reading that hint meant I failed the puzzle.  Trying to do what the hint said also fails, meaning it was inevitable for me to fail - if that's by design it's an extremely poor choice given I'm not even 30 minutes into the game.Each puzzle had different keybaord layouts...  One puzzle had me trying to memorise numbers immediately and using WASD to enter them.  Why not the numbers on the keyboard (which I instinctively went for)??? The UI was tonally inconsistent throughout.  I'd be having to navigate a pure 2d schematic, then I'd be trying to traverse a 3D schematic in the next puzzle or action.  Please, please, please, just pick one.  It's visually jarring switching between these different layouts ALL THE TIME.  Personally I'd much rather the old terminal interface like on Duskers, where at least it was visually unified.  Unlike this one which seemed to be incapable of deciding if it wanted to be a retro terminal, modern terminal or flashing HUGE B***** TEXT filling half the screen.Suffice to say, the culmination of all these annoyances made for a horrible time.  I loved the idea, the tension of being limited in vision and scope but this game didn't seem to put it into a cohesive, intuitive whole.  Instead it was a pizza covered in whatever toppings could be found at the back of the cupboard.  Applied for a refund.  A real missed opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliantly atmospheric with a nostalgic sci-fi feel. First things first, it is a walking sim.... or a floating sim. You take control of the AI aboard a space station and you have to respond to the orders of the remaining crew after a sudden event rocks the station to the core. The tasks have mini-game elements, though they are basic. The "meat" of this game is in the exploration of the space station, both aboard and outside, and discovering what you can about the crew and it's mission whilst you perform the necessary maintenance to stop things getting to a catastrophic level. On that last note though, things don't seem to be timed at all which is a hugely welcome positive on the game as you get to explore at your own speed where all to many games in this genre try and force you through at certain points. This game allows you to take a juicy bite out of the narrative and go back for seconds whenever you want. The atmosphere they have created is extremely reminiscent of late 80's/early 90's sci fi movie's as the technology aboard the station is advanced, but also very "normal" too. As you take control of SAM's (the AI's) camera's, they have a distinctly analogue "VHS" feel to them, both with occasional tracking jumps and film grain as well as interference if your camera happens to bump into something. The sound effects they have used are also very "classic sci-fi" in as much as the beeps, whirr's and pulses that you hear are very reminiscent of "MOTHER" from the original alien movie. This is another extremely welcome bonus, as it makes the station feel more alive, albeit with dated technology. I have seen people complain about the lack of direction and map in other reviews, but to be totally honest I don't really understand why those people had trouble as you can always ask your crew to repeat their last order, and the map is a very straight forward list of bullet points connected with lines (almost like a circuit diagram). Obviously as there is not gravity in space, the station uses all dimensions which at first can be jarring, granted, but I found myself getting used to it by the opening credits (which are about 10-15 mins in iirc). I've also seen reviews saying that they kept having to check guides and walkthroughs online to progress, but I didn't really have that problem other than at one point I couldn't find where 'communications' were and I was looking for a physical area where it turned out to be part of your SAM interface instead, and so I had to google how to find it. Even then though, that was because of me mis-understanding something (not paying attention) rather than actually needing to do it. You can easily traverse the game and it's puzzles if you just pay attention and even, at times, take notes. There are points where you definitely have to write down coordinates for example, otherwise you will likely forget them. Really I guess I am saying that if you are relying heavily on a walkthrough when playing, it is really more because of user error than the game itself. I don't want to spoil the story for anyone so I will simply say that I found myself not wanting to log out of the game at all for breaks because it kept me invested and I genuinely wanted to know what was happening next. They really have managed to make a walking sim suspenseful, which also merits extra kudos. If I had to point out any criticism's of the game, the only things I could really say is that sometimes the torch/flashlight on the sphere is too bright (even with gamma turned way down) and so a toggle on/off would have been nice, and the crew's facial features aren't 'perfect' and you will regularly see the eyes looking in weird places and the mouth not being fully synced to the audio during cut scenes. These 'issues' aren't really something you encounter much though, and definitely do NOT spoil the game. Overall I really enjoyed this game and would like to see a sequel at some point in the future, or at least something similar by the developer. They have absolutely nailed the general feeling of this sort of sci-fi story and I think that they could definitely revisit this well if they chose to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first time I took my time to review a game on Steam.I only played this game for 45 minutes and simply cannot recommend it (due to technical reasons).- The resolution setting goes up to 800p. I have to edit the registry to play it at 1440p.- The game runs at 85 FPS (what sort of number is that?)- Any time I pause the game, it resets the resolution (to 600p?). I then have to close the game, edit the registry, then reopen the game.- Any time I alt-tab, the game pauses, triggering the behaviour described above.- A controller is strongly recommended for this game. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! I bought it a second time on Steam (already had it on Epic) to show my support to the developer. I really hope they make a sequel someday!In most space disaster games, you play a survivor and may require the help of a ship's AI system at some point for your continued survival. In Observation, you're the AI system in the ship, and things quite interesting as the story heats up, but I shouldn't say more because the discovery of that story is why the game is so compelling.The game is not very hard--you usually have ample time, or at least ample retries, and the puzzles typically have readily-available solutions, with the area you need to be often indicated in your objectives. Tutorials are somewhat integrated with the gameplay as Emma walks you through what she needs you to do, which is pretty cool.There were a couple of times where I didn't know how to get where I needed to go. The waypoint system is quite good, but sometimes it seems to point at a door that can't open and you need to start the waypoint from somewhere else to get it to calculate a better route. Additionally, there are a couple of sequences outside the space station where it's not always clear where you need to go. But overall, most objectives were obvious and I didn't get frustrated trying to navigate or figure out what to do next.The graphics are good, and combined with the sound and music, there's a great atmosphere and mood throughout the game.If you like story-based sci-fi games and light puzzles, I would highly recommend this!

_childDocuments_.review: Story was slow but ending was good if you're into space mystery.The "puzzle" with the flashing light symbols REALLY hurt my eyes and made me nauseous. Because the pace is slow it gives a lot of time to think about things that could happen and it's a bit disappointing when.. not a lot happens.I missed two memory entries and it would be easy to play again and get them but.. _childDocuments_.review: A fairly short experience that I will most likely be sharing with friends. I was not prepared for what the game actually was and how it played, and by the end of it, I was fairly comfortable with the controls and was comfortable being what I was. It's a sci-fi mystery with a lot of potential for more. I would love a short follow up film or maybe even a sequel, but I don't know how a sequel would work out, especially with how events turn out after you have trained yourself on how to play. The puzzles are not very difficult. It is mainly an interactive movie, but a pretty good one. Expect about 5.5 hours for first run. It will take a little while to catch, but if you liked Stories Untold, you should enjoy this.7/10 Will play again8/10 Recommend to a friend

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this game. Observation is a sci-fi story-driven game set in a space station with a small crew undergoing a serious emergency. The station needs to be stabilized and repaired as best possible, the crew accounted for, and an explanation for the emergency found.The thing that makes this game stand out from the pack is the perspective that you play from--not as a member of the crew, but as the space station's computer network, an AI called SAM. You control cameras to see, obtain information through recordings and document scans, and interact with the world through drones, doors, and environmental controls. Since you're not alive in the first place, you can't really be killed--but you can be shut down, rebooted, and have access to different subsystems revoked, all of which are interesting experiences themselves.The gameplay is straightforward and mostly consists of finding necessary components and information to advance the story through exploration and puzzle-solving. None of the puzzles were difficult enough to be a real source of frustration. I got it on sale and it took me about 10 hours to go through, so I felt like I got a pretty good deal.There is no leaderboard, no chainsaw, and no horde of alien zombies to mow down so if that's how you get your kicks then this isn't the game for you.On the other hand, if you've ever wondered what it's like to be HAL from the film "2001: A Space Odyssey", this is probably about as close as you can get.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game with strong following points: + A good plot I enjoyed following. I loved the AI point of view: instead of being the person unfold the plot, you are the computer helping the protagonist. + The sound design is top tier. You are 100% immerged in this space station and the voice actors are doing a good job+ Nice graphics, nothing too fancy, but the design of the interiors are well made, very credible. I loved the interface for the AI. It reminds of old scifi movies like Alien.But the game is not perfect:- Sometimes, the objectives are not very clear and you can get lost on what to do next. Some UI elements are not very intuitive.- The controls (especially the camera ones) can feel clunky.Overall a good narrative experience that I recommend, but dont expect revolutionary gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game with a couple distinct caveats.Firstly it's a great story, with wonderful visuals and great sound design...but it's a terrible game.It's dreadfully short, and feels like it was made a game to avoid TOO much criticism for being too reminiscent of "2001 A Space Odyssey" which after playing all the way through is a somewhat unfair comparison.I say it's a terrible "Game" because the gameplay is fun for a short time before it crumbles under it's own clunkiness. And remember you can beat this game in less than 5 hours, for gameplay to become that unbearable that fast is a VERY bad sign. My biggest complaint though is what seems to be a lack of quality control. I watched a video of the first hour of a game, and saw two distinct bugs in CUTSCENES. I download the game, and the exact same bugs occur. This should not happen in cutscenes... and it occurs throughout. Character models floating away from their intended position, frozen face animations, desynced lip movements, and cameras going through the environment.That said, if you can land the game on sale, the story carries itself and is worth it. But you might find yourself saying "Get on with it" or "WHERE THE F AM I SUPPOSED TO GO?!" in no less than an hour and a half...

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the slow-burner weird tense atmosphere of 2001: A Space Odysee or Event Horizon, you are going to like this game.The only things I will say is: only play if you have a controller, and if you are OK with 0 hand-holding. If you can do these things, you will get a very weird and enjoyable space mystery out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, but do want to make a few important points before others' dig into it:This is a very different perspective. You are an AI in a computer, and the movement and game play can be a little jarring at first. I think I enjoyed it most because of how different it was. It was difficult to navigate the ship with the little analog and I got lost way more often then I want to admit. That piece probably took the longest for me in the game. Comparatively, the puzzles and story line were wonderful. They really drew me in, the puzzles were reasonably difficult and did take some time to piece together, and there are parts that you could definitely miss if you weren't exploring it. I was a little confused by the ending, but all in all it was a good story with a lot of great details and really hit the thriller piece without being a jump scare frenzy. There were definitely parts where I jumped (a quiet space when suddenly a loud noise or an alarm would go off sort of scares), and the ambiance of the game was wonderful. It was kind of amazing to look out of the window and see the gorgeous planet below and the whirling storm.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Just the kind of space SIM i like with some realism, mystery, claustrophobia and threat - can be a bit frustrating so patience needed - think would be better with save function as if have to leave before its auto saved - can be back to square one or last auto save - but can never be sure exactly how far back and what needs repeating
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying this game. It has a very different and interesting way of interacting with things. The story is good and the space station where everything takes place is amazing. Massive (for a realistic space station a few years into the future)  and really detailed inside and out. You really get a feeling of being there in an actual space station and gradually fixing problems with one of the crew.ETA I've now finished the game and it was fantastic. A brilliant story, superbly told in this format.  Very highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Observation is cinematic science fiction experience with an interesting point of view: Instead of the humans, you are playing as the computer of a space station. This is a fresh idea that allows telling of a story that could not be (interestingly) told in any other media. Going into further story details would be doing the game a disservice -- This is game best experienced raw.Gameplay of Observation could be described as attempting to figure out different systems and interfaces without proper context. In effect, this is a puzzle game where you're trying to find the internal logic of various minigames, which come in the way of various systems on the space station.If you like retro, ASCII-based computer consoles of yore, you are going to love this game. The graphical presentation of the various systems is top notch, rivalling the already excellent ones seen in Alien: Isolation. While the puzzles themselves are never hard, the challenge often lies in coming up with exactly what you're supposed to be doing. Expect a fair bit of frustration and fumbling in the dark, since the game really isn't in the habit of spelling everything out for you. Navigating the station can also get challenging, since losing your bearings in zero-G is easy.Graphics and art are very impressive for what is practically an indie title, with cool static and chromatic aberration effects adding a lot of flavour. Sound design is remarkably successful as well, which is critical in a game that is about atmosphere. You’ll just know whether you like the game or not as the opening credits roll in, as they really hammer in the style Observation is going for.Grand sci-fi concept stories always struggle with their endings, and Observation isn't really an exception in this area. Hard-boiled science fiction aficionados have seen all this before, but not told in this way. And that is what makes Observation stand out in the crowd -- The journey is better than the destination.PS. Play with a gamepad. Keyboard and mouse controls leave a lot to be desired.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: This is in essence a puzzle game with a mystery and no horror.I will not talk about the story and Steam page offers everything you should know as key component for the story is the mystery. However, focus is on the puzzles which player has to solve. Some are easy some are not so obvious. The last puzzle might be the very ending cut scene. The relationship between player and main NPC is really done well and both characters are likable.I did enjoyed this game but I have to point out some major issues I had with:1) This is the port from the console and there are 2 puzzle types which are not well translated for mouse and keyboard. 2) Consistency is lacking with the UI (as example sometimes back will be on BACKSPACE sometimes on SPACE and sometimes on a mouse click but there are more such issues)3) Faces of astronauts are not that good and really pop out in comparison to the rest of the scenery which is quite good and believable4) Game is rather short and has no replay value so it is advisable to buy it on a discount (I got it with a 50% discount). It is sad that there is a only one way to go with the story. Several different outcomes would be quite beneficial for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Being AI on space is pretty interesting idea. See from cameras, moving with sphere, controlling nearly everything. Most of puzzles are pretty nice. But I've gotta admit; I've got bored too much. Controls are terrible. I mean you need to interact something from camera but you need to wait few seconds to rotate camera. Every interactive thing needs at least few seconds. Sometime you don't know what to interact, searching all the room for minutes. And there is worse. The sphere. God, I hate that sphere. It's so hard to control and you're using it too much on the last parts of the game. It was so annoying. After all these experiences I asked myself this: "If I would know all of these experiences before, would I bought it again?". And I answered "No.".
_childDocuments_.name: Observation

_childDocuments_.review: Observation is a sci-fi thriller uncovering what happened to Dr. Emma Fisher, and the crew of her mission, through the lens of the station’s artificial intelligence S.A.M. Players assume the role of S.A.M. by operating the station’s control systems, cameras, and tools to assist Emma in discovering what is happening to the station, the vanished crew, and S.A.M. himself.

name: Stronghold: Warlords
detailed_description: ULTIMATE EDITION Buy Stronghold: Warlords Ultimate Edition and get: Base Game All Special Edition Content 24 DLC Campaign Missions The Art of War (Sun Tzu) The Mongol Empire (Kublai Khan) Rise of the Shogun (Minamoto Yoritomo) The Warrior Queen (Fu Hao) 8 DLC Warlords (Unique Perks & Upgrades) SPECIAL EDITION Buy Stronghold: Warlords Special Edition and get: Base Game Digital Soundtrack Making of Documentary Digital Art Book Stronghold HD POST-LAUNCH CONTENT About the Game The latest chapter in Firefly Studios' real-time strategy series, Stronghold: Warlords is the first game to recreate the castle economies of East Asia. In Warlords players take command of Mongol hordes, imperial warriors and samurai clansmen as they lay siege to Japanese castles and fortified Chinese cities. Besiege historical warlords using new gunpowder-fuelled siege weapons across 31 campaign missions, 45 skirmish trail scenarios, 28 multiplayer maps, skirmish mode and Free Build sandbox with AI invasions. For the first time ever Stronghold: Warlords allows you to recruit, upgrade and command AI lords across the battlefield in the form of in-game ‘Warlords’. Each warlord under your command boosts your strategic prowess with unique perks, characteristics and upgradeable abilities. Put them to work for your industry, fortifying borders, forging weapons or team up for a pincer attack! Each campaign mission, skirmish game and multiplayer battle means a fresh set of warlords to command and a completely new way to play Stronghold. CONQUER AND COMMAND WARLORDS across the battlefield unlocking more powerful castles, armies and abilities. RELIVE HISTORICAL CAMPAIGNS from 3rd century BC China, to the rise of the Tokugawa shogunate and coming of the Mongol Empire. MASTER THE SKIRMISH TRAILS with 45 unique missions challenging your castle building and besieging expertise. RECRUIT NEW UNITS including imperial fire lancers, disciplined samurai, Mongolian horse archers and deadly ninja. RAZE YOUR ENEMIES with the arrival of gunpowder and new siege weapons like the hwacha arrow launcher, siege tower and fire oxen! BECOME THE GREATEST LORD through fear or admiration using a range of medieval entertainment, taxation and torture. VANQUISH FOES IN MULTIPLAYER across 28 maps, mixing and matching 4 human and 4+ AI players for your ideal online battleground.

_childDocuments_.review: Warlords is not the best version of Strong Hold, but if you enjoy playing Strong Hold, Warlords can keep you entertained for hours. _childDocuments_.review: Long time fan... I can play the original and Crusaders titles for hours and hours and thoroughly enjoy every moment.After 10 hours of Warlords I find I have to force myself to go back to it.  I just can't get into it.  I have read other reviews saying this is a regression compared to the others.  I agree.  There is just nothing innovative and there is a lot that is just not necessary.  Like--  Why have multiple housing types?  I mean, yeah, I get it, improved housing gives and improvement to  popularity, but there is no increase in population from one house type to another and there are better ways to improve popularity.  Different cultures, but no unique buildings or unit capabilities?  This was a great add to SH title from 15+ years ago.  The only food production chain is tea, and it is only two layers deep.  Play the others and you will find that bread takes a while to get going, but pays off big later.  Ale is the same way.  Cheese production also has the purpose of providing leather for armor...  With Warlords you just plop down food plots and that's that.  No strategy in placement to ensure the most effect productions; just set them and forget them.  Also do not understand the ability to control rationing of individual foods.  Who cares?   Build enough of one type, work popularity in other ways, and there is no need for this.  I was never a fan of the vassal system-- not useful and generally distract you from other things.  No real advantage to having them.  And why a diplomacy system?  Okay, fine, it is used to upgrade vassals, but again vassals aren't that useful.  Diplomacy distracts from other more important things... and those buildings take up space.  This is the first SH to have roads... why?  The other titles managed just fine without this feature.  Sure they look nice, but that's about it.  Roads along with diplomatic buildings just wasted space.  Troops don't react as crisply as in other SH titles.  They'll go where ever and sometimes not even attack even when troops are approaching. Speaking of troops, I hope this is a bug--  when ranged attack units lock onto a unit, the attacking ranged unit can attack at extremely long range.  From what I have seen, this is an AI thing, not a human player thing.  I have moved troops in range of an AI ranged unit, withdrawn a long way or all the way back to my castle and still had that AI unit pick off my troops even though I had to move into a normal range for them to start attacking and that attacking unit never moved to begin with or followed to keep attacking.  I agree with the folks that say siege weapons attacking walls are nearly useless.  The AI just instantly rebuilds them until a unit is close enough to prevent from being rebuilt.  I am not sure if this is intentional to force a player to immediately take advantage of the situation, but it is infuriating when going for a long haul siege of a superior AI castle.  Why all the separate weapons buildings?  Why can't a bower make one or the other of bows?  Why separate melee weapon buildings?  But, then, there is only ONE armor type?  Gunpowder-- Great idea, but not useful.  Why clothing?  Yep, you can sell it...I might have rambled, but I think what I am getting it is that it appears that the priority of features was mismanaged.  Why go "fix" what wasn't broken?  Why add things that don't provide any value to the game play, or in some cases degrade it?  On my computer this is a beautiful title, but it is more shallow than SH titles I have been playing for 20 years.  Pass on this one.  Go play Crusader 1 and 2, or even the original SH.  You'll have more fun and find them more rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Give this one a pass.I grew up with Stronghold Crusaders, and played it for probably close to 2000 hours- Mainly Multiplayer PVP and CO-OP!This version's netcode is hot garbage, and multiplayer having building, wall and unit limits make next to no sense.When a player is dropped from multiplayer, there is no way for them to rejoin, or even host a save where you left off.The fiefs / warlords system is also a pointless gimmick that detracts more than it adds.Single player campaign was fun-ish, but that was never where the strengths of this series was.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good fun. In my opinion this instalment of the Stronghold series is a solid and enjoyable development. There's the usual mix of fun military campaigns, smart humour, subtle touches that help to bring life to the simulation and decent graphics. Personally I would like to see a deeper and more involved economic campaign but I look forward to seeing what the community comes up with. There's already a decent free build mod which adds attacks on demand and the developers are also promising one of these too. I just love developing my castle and amassing goods to build a huge, thriving economy and so that's why I'd like to see more of this. I've played almost 30 hours on a 4 year old medium spec laptop without a single crash so I suspect those reporting repeated crashes have some other agenda. I've played every game in the Stronghold franchise. It's been a rollercoaster ride as it includes some of my favourite PC games of all time but also some bums. This is a praiseworthy return to form and I have no hesitation in recommending it to fans of the series and newcomers alike. I paid full price for the game and consider it a fair deal.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels extremely good to play. A bit overwhelming at first because there are so many different things you can do and the tutorial is very lackluster in my opinion, but once you got the hang of it it's extremely fun. It requires a lot of thinking when it comes to unit composition. There are also plenty of units to choose from, and it's very close to stronghold crusader: There are unity you need weapons for, so you have to build production buildings to gather those, and there is the military academy which works like the mercenary outpost in stronghold crusader, where you can buy units for gold only, but they are quite expensive. Also, all of those units are useful in their own way, even tho some are obviously better than others.Now, the game features a warlord system. Basically, on every map, there are the players and there are NPCs called warlords. You can conquer those warlords by military occupation (meaning beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of them) or with diplomacy, a resource you can generate with buildings. Once you have their allegiance, you can command them to some extent in exchange for diplomacy. Every warlord has it's own abilites, for example, a pig warlord can be asked to send you food, a tiger warlord has a very powerful "Attack here" ability and a turtle warlord can be upgraded with a massive fortress. So all of those have their unique "playstyle" and they are crucial when it comes to warfare.The game is extremely fun and I can only recommend you playing it. I'm sure every old stronghold fan will be excited when he sees very old concepts brought into the modern times. However, the game definitely suffers from one thing: Lack of content. There are like 8 different skirmish maps and the campaign, that's it. So this game absolutely lives thanks to multiplayer. If you're not a fan of that, I don't think you'll be that much of a fan of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Warlords

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea why this game is mixed reviews, it's everything you'd expect from a stronghold game and then some innovations on top with the warlord system - you can capture, militarily or economically, small AI towns around the map which give you small boosts, giving you a reason to go out on the map and fight. Alternatively, it's possible to turtle up and get those neutral AIs to beat the enemy for you, if that's what you prefer.Skirmish trail and campaign. Multiplayer and skirmishes.City building and castle building. A bit of diplomacy. Some RTS fighting. It's all here, with more modern UI and less bugs than the classic stronghold games.
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Warlords

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to recommend this game, especially as I am a long time RTS fan.  While the game was fun for approx 20 hrs or so, it just doesn't offer that much.  Lots of performance issues once large armies are fighting, even in 1v1.   AI is pretty garbage.  Most of the maps are too small.  Campaign maps are even smaller.  They arbitrarily make half the campaign missions a pain by giving you no room to build anything.  It was challenging the first few times but it quickly got old.  Controlling units is a pain.  I'm surprised this game isn't in early access.Can't recommend at full price $40.  But if you enjoy RTS games and its on sale, it may be worth $20-25 imo.

_childDocuments_.review: So.. the newest Stronghold game: the setting now is different historic periods of eastern and south eastern Asia.It does have issues. I'll say that before everything else. Especially on the technical side (e.g. sometimes performance and pathfinding problems).That being said: it definitely does improve/iterate on the Stronghold brand in meaningful ways too, especially with the unit roster! I would even say, that out of all the other Stronghold titles none has made me feel this much like there was a specific use and/or time for every individual unit like Warlords does now. Of Course: crossbowmen still rain down death like nothing else, it is stronghold after all, and lightly armored troops overall still often feel inferior but more then ever do they have place in the game now anyway!Story mode is nothing to write home about. It's not bad. It does what it's supposed to, but it also cannot compete with the more personal and alive stories and characters of Stronghold 1 & 2.One BIG problem was the unit cap of 400 for all players at launch though. Luckily that has been increased to 600 by now and at least for offline even to 1000 as of the newest update.The Update and DLC policy in general are really quite good and fair this time around.I don't feel scammed out of my money for buying anything I would consider too pricy, and even if I decide not to buy a the new DLC outright, there still comes some free content to enjoy alongside it as well.Overall for people where able find at least some enjoyment within the more recent Stronghold entries: this one might be one of the best ones when it comes to this newer style of Stronghold

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold Warlords - An Epic Castle-Building Adventure!Are you ready to unleash your inner warlord and conquer the world? Well, look no further than Stronghold Warlords! This game takes castle-building to a whole new level, with a hilarious twist that will keep you entertained for hours.First things first, let's talk about the graphics. They are so stunning that you might mistake your screen for a window to the medieval world. From the intricately designed castles to the beautifully rendered landscapes, every detail is a feast for the eyes. Just don't get too distracted by the scenery, or your enemies might take advantage of it!Now, let's move on to the gameplay. As a warlord, you have the power to command your troops, manage resources, and engage in epic battles. But here's the twist - you can also recruit some rather unconventional fighters. Ever seen a ninja fighting alongside a samurai? Well, get ready for some hilarious and unexpected encounters on the battlefield. Who knew that a group of monkeys armed with bananas could be so effective?But the fun doesn't stop there! Stronghold Warlords also introduces a unique diplomacy system. You can forge alliances, negotiate treaties, or simply bribe your enemies with some delicious dumplings. Because let's face it, nothing says "peace" like a plate of freshly steamed dumplings!And if you're feeling a bit mischievous, you can always employ some unconventional tactics. How about launching a cow catapult to surprise your foes? Trust me, it's udderly hilarious! And let's not forget the joy of setting up traps and watching your enemies fall into them. It's like playing a game of mouse and trap, but with a lot more explosions!In conclusion, Stronghold Warlords is a game that combines strategy, humor, and epic castle-building into one unforgettable experience. It will keep you entertained, laughing, and strategizing for hours on end. So grab your sword, rally your troops, and get ready to conquer the world, one hilarious battle at a time!Rating: 5 out of 5 dumplings!
_childDocuments_.name: Stronghold: Warlords

_childDocuments_.review: A solid new entry to the Stronghold series, definitely the best 3D one. Solid gameplay loop, warlords mechanic adds more map control options, torture is an interesting new way for controlling happiness and pumping up your economy (I mean you'd better or you're losing another finger), the setting is nice and different from the usual middle eastern deserts, but unfortunately the visuals are really dated.....like the older stronghold crusade games will age better and they're like 19 years old, but I would stomach that if at least the performance was good, because the gameplay is pretty fun, sadly that also leaves a lot to be desired especially for the visual fidelity on display.
