_childDocuments_.review: Everyone who gives this game a thumbs up has Stockholm Syndrome. This game doesn't meet any standards of a game created for PC in 2021. Whole game feels like you're controlling it with a hotdog on a touchscreen.I've played thousands of hours of SH1/2+Crusader and played through the entire Crusader Extreme campaign and bought ~10 copies of Crusader 2 for friends. Terrible ending for this studio most likely. Really unfortunate as this doesn't hold up in any regard besides making decently pretty castles as long as you don't want a gate on a diagonal wall.Control of units is worst in class.Pathing and fights are laughable at best. 1 unit held back my army of 50 from making it through an area that was 5 times larger than that one unit.Warlords detract from my castle and add a mobile-like feel to the game while blocking the gameplay you want to see. They provide little value and are laughably conquered. I personally hate them as why would I not build my own sustainable castle? I took over warlords with 5 (you could do it with 1) range unit shooting the warlord. He doesn't move or do anything and once his initial 5 troop defense is gone, he's a sitting duck.Got to the third mission and my peasants refused to eat vegetables... which is a pretty gamebreaking bug when the mission wants you to build those farms.Game has no difficulty. Literally auto pilot on fastest speed until someone attacks.Maps are tiny, made smaller by warlord areas.Impossible to micro units and clicking on a single unit near an enemy is impossible as they'll attack. All the units look the same and you can't easily tell if they're ranged/armored or not.Unit colors were atrocious for a color blind person. Lost many units just... everywhere.Had no startup problems myself but between reports of endless load screens and black screens after install, at least wait.There has been no innovation in mechanics or feel since they failed with their first 3d Stronghold.Game is slow and the economy feels disjointed from the castle.I don't like the changes in the popularity system and the addition of luxury housing changing popularity but in a really obscure way that wasn't apparent as just having more than enough housing. The different size housing is great, the luxury part that relates to happiness, not so much.In my short time playing I know it's not the Crusader+ we all wanted and have been asking for.There's already mods to make Warlords better and ways to hack the unit caps.... but why should the community have to do these things when they are INTEGRAL parts of the game.Buy at $10 or if you like playing by yourself because your friends won't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Was so excited for this and followed the Developers throughout there YouTube teaser's. Was really hoping that this game would return the franchise to its former glory of Stronghold-2 (Still the best in the series) but...... I was so disappointed. So... here is whats wrong with the game in my opinion.1. The AI has no intelligence and rely's on numbers to win, no probing tactics at all2. Maps are crazy small and to be able to take advantage of the new diplomacy you need the space3. graphics poor for this day and age, at least with Stronghold-3 they tried4. Diplomacy late game turns into who can click the fastest to own one of the AI army's. Not kidding I played with three of my friends and I literally spent the last 30 minutes betting for favour..It just doesn't work.5. Bugs Bugs & more BugsI hated writing this as the Devs seem to be really nice people, but me and my friends just uninstalled this game and purchased AOE4. If there is ever going to be a stronghold-5 I can only wish they will bring back castle building in (Medieval period) and drop the diplomacy lark.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is OK, not more. Graphics are from last decade at best.Music is ok.The characters, if you want to call them that, are so unimpressive, that I cant remember a single one.Didnt bother playing trough all campaings.Combat is neat, defending a castle can be fun.There is really no significant advancement to the combat. _childDocuments_.review: Easily the best Stronghold of the last 15 years.Warlords does make improvements on Crusader 2.+ The game runs much smoother and better.+ The campagin offers a nice variety of challenges.+ Unit collision prevents the stacking of archers on towers and the merging of melee units to a doom stack. Holding a breach in your wall against superior numbers is quite satisfying. + The Warlords themselfs are powerfull assets. To grab and maintain control over them you are encouraged to leave the safty of your castle. This results in many more frequent skirmishes and sieges.It's not without it's flaws however:-If you where hoping for a complex castle life simulation like Stronghold 2, you won't find it here.-While the AI is the most competent it has ever been, it's still not all that smart.-Only 4 AI lords for skirmish that rarely send you a messge with only a few differnent and mostly dull lines.If you enjoyed Stronghold Legends or Crusader 2, then Warlords is worth checking out. If not, this most likely isn't for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything I wanted Stronghold Crusaders 2 to be years ago.It takes Good and Bad buildings and adds them with various effects back into the game, the Food system works better than ever. Adding spiritual buildings and Diplomacy and roads help boost both effects make the city planning important and keeps it fresh.The units, WOW it feels so good marching large armies across into others, the battles feel so good to fight.AI, Don't get me started on the AI.The AI are COMPLETELY redone from previous entries in this series. Stronghold 2 had maybe the best AI besides this one here, I don't have tons of time against this AI yet, but I am willing to say from the one match I had going...That ended ubruptly...Not the game crashing, but me accidentally hitting the power to my computer:(This game is amazing in every way I wanted and then some I didn't know I wanted that they gave us:)It is a city planning RTS with responsive units and large siege battles that feel like a WAR and not small skirmishes.If you like this series, or RTS games with base building than fighting this game IS a must.

_childDocuments_.review: The latest update made this game better and immediately reverted some features (Like the low unit cap) that were very poorly chosen. Also added in the update was an extreme mode for the AI but over-all it hasn't really made them feel very dynamic or overly challenging.Why my review is staying negative: The game is clunky. The new voice messages they added are constant, annoying, and occur even after the lord is gone. The game has a lot of 'hiccups' where it lags.The AI is 'better' but you're still fairly comfortable. It's hard to find that sweet spot where it's a challenge without being out right crushed by constant swarms of attacks.There are not a lot of maps to choose from.There are still only four lords.I think this game will be better by the end of Summer when their 'road map' of updates is complete. That begs the question why they did not just wait until then to release the game rather than release something that isn't finished.They would have been better off releasing a finished game and getting great reviews out of the gate rather than something that isn't finished getting bad reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Rewrite of my review, some minor opinion changes. Ill reccomend this as a good Stronghold game, but its very rough, especelly for someone who wants to get into the series, at top 20 bucks, but maybe less. Warlords is the latest game in the Stronghold series almost 6 years after Crusader 2 and almost 2 decades since the series started. If you are a newcomer to the series youll have to lower your expectations a bit, both in quality and design. Stronghold is a much more simple game than AOE, it has no Rock Papper Scisors or build times or build orders that you require, with sprinkles of something deeper. For Stronghold fans well there is a bit of a situation. Fans would know that Firefly has had a rocky progress with this series. 1, Crusader and 2 are all beloved games, however rest is either hit or miss, and unfortunately as it is and as it has shown Warlords is very, very, very bouncy. One on hand it improves on from Legends and Crusader 2's strangely balanced economies and some oddities, but the series has only returned to where it was once, without 'annoyances' that were brought to 2. As a Stronghold title it is very good but someone expecting more will be dissappointed. So ill go over some major things gameplay wise and just talk about them. Graphically the game is not good, ill be honest i don't think the series looked good even early 2000's, but eh, its a let down. Soundtrack is fantastic though, there is bit less of it because Warlords doesn't reuse anything and is all newly composed, but its still fantastic the tracks that are there. Economy as said was tweaked, while workshops still cost a lot things like farms and some other general buildings have been made cheaper, somewhat having a balance between old and new. Units have gone trough numerous changes with Firefly's focus on abilities and roles to an extent. At first glance its all same units we always had, but many of them have twists. Pikemen for example have been replaced with guardsmen which has an AOE attack, which simply crushes weaker and grouped units. Samurai the Knight equielent has a devastating Charge that can easily take out Lords without protection. And Waifus... i mean Ninjas, have a minor ranged ability, which makes them even more OP than Stronghold 2 Assassins. The new feature to series, Warlords is... fine. Its a different spin on estates with us being now given bonuses and few neat abilites we can use them for. Some like Tiger and Dragon are great, and someone like Mouse is not great. Id say its more of a different slice of pie rather than a better slice of pie. Now AI has been greatly improved from Crusader 2, ill talk about its state now rather than launch but, AI has seen great economic improvements, being suprisingly good at gathering, everything it needs to, and it DOESN'T CHEAT!... except on Expert. Though AI has lost most of its agression from Crusader 2, so while now AI can properly sustain itself, it having big sieges is rare, but do be afraid from someone like Sun Tzu getting a large army, when they do the pack one of biggest punches in the series. So overall this Stronghold is great... right? Warlords, had the single, third worst launch of Stronghold titles, behind 3 and... okay just behind 3. There were 4 AI lords, i guess they wanted us to use Warlords as suplement, i mean the 4 were good, but there were only 4. There were 8 maps, no kind of Skirmish campaing [there is Standard but both would have been good] And certain lack of options in options and game settings. Performance was terrible, now its just bad but at least you can play it now. And the troop and building cap is, terrible, i will overlook this limit though since it can be changed, in Configuration files, i don't think there is a limit so this does make this extremely good, but on default its terrible, i suggest you don't even look at it, just change it imedietly. Which is a shame, ill be honest Warlords has done almost all i wanted, it improved upon Crusader 2, brough back some things gone for a long while [laddermen] Its polished like, there were few bugs i could note, unlike Crusader 2 and especelly 3. But then Firefly has fallen on basics of every game, it aint Cyberpunk, but its bad. I have noted a bit these 2 months, im not as positive as i was at launch for the game, but at same time i look at this and its, fine. Id say more, but there are limitations for which i cannot express myself fully, but for me, this game is. 7 at its launch state, if it gets more patches and updates down the line, 8, drops down to price, 20, 15, buy it, why not, even if you don't like it at least you didn't buy Stronghold 3.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey everyone, long time RTS player and content creator here. Lets start with the bad:- AI was brain dead in the campaign. Everything felt so dead, and the only difficulty was that the enemy spawns units instead of making their own.  AI didn't manage an economy. AI didn't manage an army. AI didn't manage diplomacy (aside from trying to steal them back via diplomacy point).  Just. A. Lot. of. Unit. Spamming/Spawning. I call this lazy development. It is not fun.  This is coming from playing on Hard on the Mongol Campaign where the enemy spam waves after waves of horse archers.  It would make more sense that the warlords that the enemy AI had at first spawns units because the AI spends diplomacy points on them.- Fighting is extremely clunky. Units have a hard time moving together. They can also go off somewhere else or just abruptly stop. When microing horse archers. I noticed that everytime I get them to move, they stop firing and stagger, allowing other units to catch up really easily.- Attack Move on the GUI doesn't work.  Attack move via keybind (Ctrl + Right Click) does work, but unspammable and is horrible in large scale combat (optimization issue).  Units tend to freeze and just stand there and do nothing or they all actually get in range and start firing.  Sometimes they would just charge into melee range and melee them.  Horse archers specifically will just charge in with attack move (ding ding, just like the previous games). - Skirmish isn't really fun, theres only 3-4 AI lords.  Why is there so little. - And because of so little AI lords, there is no trials. I loved the difficulty of stronghold crusaders trial, but here we have none.- Units can get stuck if you build on top of them AND if they go flying into them after a seige weapon hits them.  Very annoying to deal with.- Why is there no wooden walls still.- Multiplayer has a unit cap because of sync issues.  Even with the unit cap, there are still sync issues.  It was me vs another, both with unit cap 200, we both had around 120-150 troops? The game went at a third of the normal speed. Thats how bad late game multiplayer is.- CRASHES, CRASHES ALL AROUND! CRASHES IN MULTIPLAYER WHICH YOU CANT GET BACK IN. CRASHES IN CAMPAIGN WHICH HAS NO AUTO SAVE. Have fun with crashes :)- This game consumes more CPU than you would expect. Having this game on ultra graphics and streaming to twitch at the same time causes other applications to be locked and show low fps on twitch.The Neutral- Imagine an RTS without being able to change Keybinds.  This is one of them.  It is hardcoded into the game.  Also imagine an RTS that doesn't even allow you to look at the keybinds in game.  They made a separate sheet and posted on their discord/website though, so its not that bad.- Maps are pretty tiny, but this is up to the players. I don't really mind unless it comes to a large lobby of players.- Voice acting was not that bad english wise, literally definition of a white washed asian making fun of their own voice though.- I feel that there should be more ancient eastern type music during battles/non battles.  Some of the music type in the game doesn't really feel eastern-like.- Multiplayer is not designed to be competitive. This is more for having fun with friends and just experience mid-late game sieges and whatnot.  Otherwise, units are extremely unbalanced unless you place a peace treaty timer or limits.- At least the units are kind of new but follow similar concepts compared to previous strongholds.  You got a Military Academy which is the merc camp that you can hire units with only gold.  The Barrack that requires weaponry for all but the spearman and blow pipe.  The siege camp with some new and impressive siege weapons but also oldies like the catapult and trebs.  Suicidal Fire Ox was fun. - Castle building was fun and follows the original concepts, BUT why the hell does towers have the same arrow deflection chance as walls.  Doesn't make sense at all really. They do have range boost however.The Good- Their economy system is fairly new and just fun to manage.  Each consumable resources that affects popularity is separate and macro-able.  Nice little stat page to tell us if we're producing enough vs consumption.  - Some new but comparable chains of goods production. Silk -> threads -> Clothes just like wheat -> flour -> Bread.- Shrines and Roads was a fine addition as a variety for popularity boost.- Diplomacy was fairly unique and utilizing warlords was fun, but could use work.  Higher levels should definitely boost diplomacy options, such as sending larger armies to attack instead of your tiny little regiment, but of course, costs more diplomacy points.- If you like Eastern type RTS, I would highly recommend this to you.- They finally added unit collision! Only during combat.  Otherwise units just run in this big ass line on top of each other.- As a Vietnamese speaker, I loved how some units are speaking in their foreign languages.  A nice touch.Is this a game with high replayability?  - No, unless you want to play with some friends from time to time.  I already got tired of it. I rather play more Stronghold Crusaders to be honest.Is this a game worth 40$ without sales?- No, the amount of hours in this game is roughly 20 with beating the campaign, but the campaign itself is way too generic and AI is dead which showcase how lazy some parts were developed (such as spawning in units for the AI)What are the contents of this game or what you would consider as content:- Generic Campaign, up to 3 Military types and 1 Economic- Sandbox, build your castle the way you want without interference- Skirmish, Fight against other Warlords whether they are players or AI- Finish the achievement section. Theres quite a bit of achievements.KEEP IN MIND THIS GAME JUST RELEASE.  I hope the devs do not abandon the game, because I do believe the game is wonderful in its own touch and continue to develop this game and fix the issues I mentioned above.

_childDocuments_.review: Get the game on sale for max 10e/15e. Firefly simply does not deserve more for this product.When I purchased the “full” game on release, it was no more than an early beta full of game breaking bugs, performance issues and more. They also intentionally hidden these facts in their trailers to the upcoming release. The said issues still exist today, but to a lesser extent so they are no more game breaking issues, but just issues that make the gameplay irritating. And the issues that still persist, the developers do not intend to fix, as they have been present since day one. Simply promising that you are working on fixing them each roadmap video is not enough. I started following the development of the game around 1 year prior to its release, actively following game development on Fire Flies YouTube channel. We were promised very clever AI that would calculate the importance of buildings and then decide whether they are worth spending gold on (to buy resources to build them instantly) or simply waiting for the resources naturally. How they will time their Warlords attacks with their own. Basically, an AI we haven’t seen before in any stronghold series so far. In one of the gameplay videos prior to release me and a couple of people saw units going afk mid fight and pointed that out in the comments. In the next video we got a reply that this is gameplay of a yet released game and it will be all fixed by the time the game is out. They also didn’t accept preorders because they are not “that” type of company. Boy, were we up for a ride.Reality was AI’s sending their whole army through a patch of fire that you or even themselves made, killing their whole army. If you set their buildings on fire, they pretty much got so crippled that they couldn’t recover economically. There were pathfinding issues that made the game so frustrating to play. Multiplayer was unplayable due to permanent freezes and/or permanent resyncing. Troop limit was so small that you can’t, at the same time, have a sizeable attacking and defending army.They kept saying in their videos they are fixing bugs, but they weren’t. Making issues/bugs from game breaking into bugs that make the game playable is not fixing them btw. It’s completely alright for a hotfix patch, but not to just leave it like that. Instead of focusing on fixing the AI’s, bugs and other issues they decided to make more maps and add a new AI (which would be awesome if the game was working in the first place). After that they announced they are making a payable DLC, when their game IS STILL NOT WORKING. This is the point I lost all my hope. Payable DLC wouldn’t even be a problem if your game was working as it should have. AI isn’t completely terrible anymore and is mediocre best. It’s just an average AI, the clever one that syncs attacks with warlords or other AI’s simply does not exists. AI still kills his units with its own fire etc... Multiplayer is playable but you still experience frequent freezes. All game breaking issues at launch are more or less still present but in the form of “makes your gameplay irritating”. Troop limit has been “increased” by a small amount. Still can’t make a decent army, hence issue is still not fixed.Unlike most of the negatived review here, I actually like the Warlords series and am a big fan of the warlords system, however I cannot recommend a 35e game when the same issues from day one still persist 3 months after the release and the developers showing no incentive to fix them. If you fixed all the issues, Stronghold: Warlords would be my favorite game from you. It is just really sad to see the potential this game had to be throw away. When the game launched, you had over thousands of feedback messages on discord regarding bugs each week. If you look at the discord now, you have a message or two in a week at best. Community showed overwhelming support that you decided to ignore, and now in turn the community has also given up on you.

_childDocuments_.review: OK after 18 hours in this game : I really like it.I usually play 1-2 campaign or skirmish each time. Quite a pleasure managing an ancient stronghold in Chinese style, withstand the initial threats, build a large army and crash enemy's castle.If you never tried a Stronghold game, if you like RTS, or if you like Ancient Asian style, go for it.Don't expect an AAA RTS game of the 2020s. This is not one.This is a 2010-ish game, entirely focused on real-time stronghold building, its economics and the attack & defense around them.Don't expect to be impressed the first time launching the game. This is not Hearts of Irons. The ambiance is quite calm for a war game. But once you get used to the pace, it is fun.Talking about ambiance, the dev team should absolutely learn from Koei, the Studios who create strategic games based on Japanese and Chinese history. The graphics & music shows the dev team's desperate attempt to make the game look and sound Asian. You don't need to. Try Koei's Romance of the Three Kingdoms series (9-11). You'll see what I mean.All in all, good game. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all - it is NOT a Stronghold Crusader and don't expect it to be!I've played all SH games, for last 15 years and as far as I can tell - this game feels fresh to me.And no other expansion stick to me like this one. Maybe it is because of moving to some other type of troops and side of history.The gameplay by fundamental means is same - destroy enemy Lord.Game itself feels slower than others, but there is always something to do.I've played whole campaign and it gives a sense of story for historical events. Currently going through skirmish trails - and some are easy some are so so and some are brutal. Even if game itself is more slowish than other SH games, you still need to be fast paced and thinking ahead with warlords - there is not a second where you've got nothing to do.Warlords fell fresh - and game changing mechanic that can turn your games to make it or break it.It doesn't feel repetitive because of mix of warlords and most of time you have to adapt your strategy to that.There are some new troops and buildings that make fighting and positioning different from other games.Graphic wise - personal opinion - I love this type of art, not too realistic, not too cartonish. I was not a fan of 3 or Crusader 2.  In fact, my negative review of Crusader 2 is one of the most viewed on Steam (I don't mean that as some kind of weird brag, just as a note of my passion for this series, for reference).I've followed the development of this game for a long time now, and I can see the effort that went into it.  I also see a lot of room for improvement (mostly visually - the specifics army colors in your units and buildings can make things very convoluted, and the UI could use a bit of polishing - and of course there are bugs that I can promise you the devs are actively working on as I write this).Unlike Crusader 2, my initial reaction to the game is VERY positive.  I instantly felt like I was playing Stronghold 2 again, in a new way.  It felt very intuitive as a veteran player. _childDocuments_.review: This is not my Stronghold.Played all the strongholds and I have to say, and I don't say/review at all really, that this shouldn't be called a Stronghold game, especially from 2021. The Strongholds I know are teaming with character, but this game is very flat. The explosive new visuals, sound and mechanics (warlords) are very welcome additions, but again, falls flat of their real potential.In a world where RTS games are few are far between that satisfy the OG RTS players, this game could have lifted this and pounded traditional RTS back into the scene with the strong foundations of the Stronghold Saga. Who better to make their stamp in history, for the Stronghold Saga and the dying OG RTS scene, in the beginning of 2021. Guess what? Uninspired, seemingly unfinished and so much shorter than its very high potential-ceiling. It makes me want to reinstall the older Strongholds, again, just to override this experience. Massive sigh.It's very easy to take Asian-inspired visuals and run with it as something "different" and rehash the game under a "new" development, but if you are going to run with that then I would have hoped it wouldn't feel as synthetic as these visuals appear. I'm a thorough believer of 'go hard or go home' mentality and they just seem to have slapped quite generic, uninspired Asian visuals on this, but it's nothing on AoE3: Asian Dynasty visuals.I have to touch on the intentionally pixelated cutscenes and just flat out say, this is unacceptable in a 2021-released game. What are the devs playing at?! It's 2021! A first year 3D Modelling student, even a lowkey hobbyist, could make a more appropriate cutscene sequence. This is the same for low definition little character monologues you get through the matches. This really gobsmacked me, I actually think the OG Strongholds had better visuals than this. This is criminal. Total War: Shogun 2 topped those visuals, in 2011. Unacceptable.So far, this is screaming "gutted budget" and "no OG devs". Did another license holding company tragically murder a classic franchise? I'm not sure I'll ever take a different excuse for this.Shall we talk about the uninspired voice overs? Insert "slightly eastern-asian accent that doesn't have much time, so will say the words once and then run away." If I had the budget, I would have thrown in a heavy accented Asian voice actor native to each of the areas. I'm trying not to use the term more, but it just rings true on so much of this game; it just sounds flat and falls flat. I expect the same energy in generic voice overs for online-courses that quickly rile people into hating the droning course. It almost feels unprofessional. I really hope this wasn't a "pull them from their desk and give them a script" scenario, but it begs the question.The final issue I want to touch on is the Warlords mechanics. Conceptually, I think this is great and it's a very welcome concept to the Stronghold saga, as it needed a few little new things, but not game massacring nukes. However, I feel it does just that. This little pick-me-up was actually a soul destroying nuke that takes up half of my game for very mundane reasons. I want to brawl my enemy for the whole game for that key stone deposit, not kill 5 units and get it. It's ultimately quite a small mechanical addition that provides a small inconvenience in order to get map supremacy and/or a blocked resource. This specific addition to the game has embodied the theme of the entire game in that it means well, but falls horrendously...short of its potential.I almost want to round this up with a refund, but as an OG RTS and Stronghold player, I'll keep it for the hope of maybe some updates or something, I don't know. It has Stronghold in the name, I guess. I wanted a Stronghold game that would give me a fresh breath of Stronghold air (fuming medieval Asian cesspits), but it isn't even a breath of old Stronghold guff. This isn't Stronghold. A new RTS player won't enjoy this, an OG RTS player won't enjoy this; do the devs even enjoy this game? I don't know what this point of this game is other than to tick the "Asian rehash" box. It ain't even a rehash, damn it!Absolutely gutted.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was a huge fan of Stronghold and Stronghold 2, I was either lukewarm or disliked all the subsequent entries. I believed the hype from Firefly that Warlords would be a true successor to Stronghold 2, but unfortunately it just isn't the case.Pros:+ The graphics are a nice bump over Stronghold 2 (but so they should be!)+ Combat mechanics are fun and satisfying+ There is a fair variety of unit types including horse archers, crossbowmen, 'Generals' etc.+ Difficulty options (Easy, Medium, Hard) for enemy AI is a very welcome addition+ The game excels when you're playing a siege, either in defense or attack.Cons:- The economic aspects of the game feel hugely dumbed down compared to Stronghold 2. There is no gong, no rats, no crime. The added diplomacy and spirit systems are shallow and uninteresting, it feels like a band-aid solution to try to flesh out the game in the absence of proper game systems. - The warlords system is fundamentally flawed, and in skirmish mode it actively detracts from gameplay when compared with the old estates system. You cannot control the warlords in any sense, can't build on their land, and can only give them orders through extremely restricted 'edicts'. Enemy AI constantly takes over your warlords via diplomacy points, meaning you need to monitor sub-menus within sub-menus every minute in order to keep control of them. Since you can't build on warlords' land, it's no longer possible to build industries away from your castle, and the cart-to-transport-goods-between-estates functionality is completely missing as a consequence.- The honour system is completely absent, meaning no lord's kitchen, no lady's bedchambers, no jousting, no festivals. The Lord does not have feasts or dances, doesn't attend church or jousts, he just stands on the castle unless you use him for combat.- Some basic bugs or design flaws from the original games are still present, such as the fact that the oxen used to transport iron & stone are interchangeable, meaning they will travel across your entire castle to pick up the wrong type of resource. Firefly simply haven't listened to much of the feedback they've had since the days of Stronghold 2 over a 16 years ago.- There are only 4 AI opponents in the whole game.- There is little to no variation between the AI opponents/factions - most units are identical, most buildings are identical, despite the fact that the 4 warlords cover four completely separate cultures (Chinese, Mongol, Japanese and Vietnamese). This makes the game feel very cookie-cutter and unvaried, and really damages the replayability of the game. For an example of just how much of an impact it can have to provide varied unit types per faction, see Lord of the Rings Battle For Middle Earth 1 & 2, which were released over 15 years ago and still hold up today.- The largest map sizes are still very small, adding to the impression that Firefly are not pushing any boundaries when it comes to technical capability or innovation. Yes, they are a small studio, but games like Stardew Valley were developed by one guy in his bedroom and have hundreds of hours more content and more complexity than this game does.Overall, I regret buying the game, and I wouldn't even recommend it at half price. The game can provide 10-15 hours of distraction, for that I'd wait for 75% off at the minimum. Firefly are stuck in the past and haven't listened to feedback. The key selling point of this game - the warlords system - simply doesn't work, and the economic aspects of gameplay which made Stronghold 2 so replayable are dumbed down so much they feel absent.One word to sum up the whole experience: Disappointment.

AI also works surprisingly well in skirmishInterface: 7/10 - Comfort features missing, also easy to missclickContent: 6/10 - Lacking AI opponents and skirmish / MP maps but good groundworkTechnical Stability: 6/10 - Very few bugs but performance issues in grand-scale situations even with the low unit capHere some unsorted thoughts:-From all 3D Strongholds it is the one with the least design issues and best balancing. The gameplay systems work, the AI (in skirmish) as well. -From the visual side it is consistent and sometimes quite beautiful but definitely outdated by at least 10 years. -The soundtrack is epic, the voice-over however might not be for everyone.-Major drawbacks however are the low unit cap (which can be extended in single player by altering a file manually) and the poor performance with many AIs and players.-Also the game as of now lacks content in form of maps and AI opponents which will hopefully added later as DLCs as it happened in Crusader II.-I don't see how Firefly will fix the performance issues, since they are already happening in Stronghold 3 and Crusader II which makes it seem that they cannot handle the engine properly. _childDocuments_.review: I was apprehensive with the mixed scores, but I must say this plays quite well. I have actually run into fewer issues with Warlords than I have with Stronghold 2 (I played both right after each other for a comparison.) I really like the quality of life changes that have been added to Warlords from 2. Namely, stats and bonuses are clearly stated on each unit and building. Towers clearly state for example the number of troops that fit in each, the arrow coverage, and the range increase they receive. Another nice change from previous Strongholds is that military units no longer infinitely stack. They maintain spacing when in a fight which results in more realistic battles where some troops can't fight all at the same time. In battles this means you need to maneuver troops to get encirclements in order to get more soldiers into the fray. This also means bottlenecking enemies works even when you lack area-of-effect attacks. The difficulty is there in singleplayer, with 4 levels which raise the challenge without feeling like its cheating you. There are numerous units to make use of, particularly in the siege and counter-siege area. The economic control is much more accessible and more in-depth in the past. You can easily diversify your food types and set the consumption rates for the peasantry for each individually. Of particular use is the market building that allows you to set auto-sell and auto-buy levels, meaning you don't need to micromanage resource levels such as in the past.Basically I am loving the game as both a long-time Stronghold fan and as someone who enjoys RTSs. To be honest, I much prefer the production-chain approach Stronghold Warlords has over other modern RTS releases such as Age of Empires.In conclusion: an up-to-date Stronghold title that provides substantial improvements over previous releases. Absolutely worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played all previous Stronghold games. Although Warlords cannot compete with the nostalgia fuelled joy that one gets from playing, say, Crusader, it is still a fun game. The main positive about Warlords is the fact that the game overall feels more active than some of its predecessors. The main negatives consist of certain mechanics and a sense of unpolish. I'll take the positive first, and then go to the negatives. Overall, I do think the game is worth playing, but I would maybe wait for a sale.Positives: In older iterations, especially Crusader and Stronghold, you could usually set up your castle and fortifications in a way that sooner or later meant it would be impenetrable (round tower filled 20-ish crossbowmen and a few shields + ballistas or something similar). In Warlords, (at least some of) the enemies actually feel threatening as your castle is harder to defend. So in short: you're forced to pay more attention to your own castle, which makes the game fun. There is also a greater incentive to actually use different troop types. The longer range of archers vs crossbowmen give them a function in defence. The high cost of certain siege defences (like wall mounted ballistae) and the realtive ease with which the yare destroyed, makes you think twice about where and when you want to use them. Etc. Activity is also added from the warlords' perks, which give flavor to the game, and make for more unique playthroughs.Negatives: The use of influence over warlords is a prime example of how a game mechanic in combination with the unpolished state of the game makes for some annoying moments, so I will use that to exemplify. In Warlords, you can either conquer warlords to your side by force or by spending influence points to demand their obedience. Spent influence points decay over time. The influence points you spend on warlords go up to a maximum of 300. If you control a certain warlord, the enemy AI might during the game try to capture it from you. The capture by force method works just fine, nothing much to say about that. But the influence points method is another story. Once you realize the enemy is trying to capture your warlord through influence (by hearing an announcement by the warlord where he says that "a foreign lord is courting us" or something similar), the only way to stop the capture is by spending your own influence to trump out the enemy's. After a while of this back an forth you will reach 300 influence points, and this is where the trouble starts. Once both you and the AI has 300 influence points over the warlord the enemy AI will continuously wait for you your influence to drop by a few points (to 298 or similar) and then try to capture the warlord. Then you have to go into the warlords menu, spend influence to get up to 300 again to deal with this. Less than a minute later, the same process takes place anew, as the enemy AI again has waited for your influence to go down a few points. This spam will go on for a good while, either until you, in the middle of the heat of battle, forget to go in and click on the influence button, or the AI finally stops. There is a way to spend influence points automatically on a warlord, but this mechanic can't be used in this situation, since it is shuts down once you reach 300. So you have to spend the points manually. While I understand that this mechanic is supposed to create some tension for the player, it mostly comes off as annoying. Because you usually have enough influence points to spend, the only reason you might loose one of these spam races, is that you forget to go in and click a button. And this is where the unpolished state of the game comes in. The only way to keep track of these influence takeovers are through audio cues or by manually checking the warlords tab ever so often. While in the warlods tab you cannot do anything else, so the audio cues are your best friend. But should you play a match against multiple enemies, which is often the case, these cues can at times be overridden by the enemies' various threats, boasts etc. Of course, cheesy one-liners from your enemies are part and parcel of a Stronghold game, but in warlords it gets kinda ridiculous. The AI will want to say something (accompanied by a huge drop down image of them that takes up a good portion of the screen, and to my knowledge cannot be turned off) a) when they attack, b) when you attack them, c) when they capture a warlord, d) when their attack fails, e) when your attack fails, f) when they loose a warlord, g) probably something else that I am missing. Add to these the warlords' announcenments and on top of this, the fact that the AI is also set to announce all these things when they are dealing with another AI. So they will for instance announce TO YOU that they are attacking another AI, even if you are not allied with either them or that other AI. (On the skirmish trail there is for instance a mission where it is you against two teams of two.) So it looks like the AI's announcements are just programmed wrong, or are in some form bugged. Summa summarum: If you play against more than one AI you will want to dispatch with them quickly, because otherwise you will slowly go insane by the constant stream of announcements, which inevitably will drown out other information (I have had many situations where one AI is doing an influence takeover of my warlord, while another is planning to attack me, and the only announcement I get, is from the AI attacking me.)There is alot more to say about polish (cannot quickly check keybinds anywhere, cannot turn of the drop down portraits of enemies announcing their intentions, hard to select individual units in a blob, certain warlords build their castles so that some of their perks become unusable etc.). But since this review is already quite long I will skip that for now. In any case, I repeat: I still think the game is worth playing because it is fun. But it would be more fun if the developers would take the time to polish certain things.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold: Warlords is a modern stronghold game. As such, it is utter trash! This game may have had a few nice ideas, but it's still a barebones copy of a franchise that felt outdated a decade ago.Moving the setting might have been a good concept. You can finally choose between different types of houses, unlike the first games, when you could only build improvised shacks, and the later entries, where the quality of house depended on the distance from the central keep (both awful in their own way). Unit tiers was also a good idea on paper. However, this means that you only have three units: one fighter, one archer, one horseman, that's it!On top of that, the graphics are absolutely hideous. The units are all low-quality messes of polygons, the terrain is bland and uninteresting, and every building looks grey and dilapidated. The buildable area is still criminally small ever since Legends divided the map into smaller zones, and the games have yet to compensate by just making the maps bigger.Ugly, buggy, and dated in both graphics and gameplay, Stronghold: Warlords truly has nothing to offer as a game. How this franchise still manages to vomit up new entries baffles me. Just put this aging franchise to rest, and stop ruining your few good games with this low-effort garbage!FINAL SCORE: 2/10

_childDocuments_.review: After being on a Stronghold binge after I caught the big C, I though I'd give this a try when it was on sale. While it's not as bad as SH3 was, it's second to last in the entire series.  It's kind of OK at 50% off, though still a bit expensive. Paying full price for it is not even remotely worth it.Now. Why is it so bad? First off, the easy part. It looks ugly, very ugly. I don't mean that it doesn't look realistic enough or whatever, but it's not a pretty looking game at all. Bland, messy and thrown-together. I might say it's the worst looking out of all the Stronghold games ever made. No scratch that, out of all the games Firefly has ever made. Not the worst flaw as none of the Stronghold games has ever been that good-looking. But this is by far the most bland looking one. At least the old ones looked cleaner and more pleasant. Even SH3 looked better, and that game is fugly.Sound design and audio is uninspiring to say the least. Boring "Asian theme" music. Stronghold 1, 2, Crusader and Legends all had engaging, relaxed or fun music. Especially SH2. The sound of the village seems muted and dead, same goes for the sound of battle. And while Stronghold has never been a industry leader in good voice acting, at least the old games had charm and wit. This is again follows the "Asian theme" which leaves you half asleep. And the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ advisor, is even more annoying that he's EVER been! I'd rather catch herpes than listen to him say "Excellency" again. Gameplay is meh. Only a hair better than SH3. Pacing is slow, population system is very unrewarding and easy to overlook. I like picking rations for different types of food separately, and building different quality homes, but that's about it. Sim mechanics are simple, but not intuitive. Nothing seems rewarding or worth doing.  It's like you bought Age of Empire off of Wish and got some pseudo Stronghold mechanics thrown in together with a slow-paced and boring combat system.I'm gonna play it a bit more, but I know already that this is inferior to anything but SH3 in the series. if it's around $10, it might get you a few hours of fun. But I would rather replay SH1,2, Legends and Crusader.Short story even shorter; skip this unless you really want it and get it cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun at first and brings in unique Stuff never seen before in a Stronghold game, like Cannons, Rockets, even Bombs, but it still manages to bring you that Stronghold feeling you get from the other Stronghold games.The new food mechanics are nice as well, making it a lot more enjoyable since your production doesn't require the enirety of the Arabian Desert just to get enough food for your 50 people and it doesn't collapse completely by just a small touch from the enemy, like it used to in Stronghold Crusader 2.However the enemies are WAY to weak. I don't know if I just broke their AI somehow with my playstyle, but I've tried a 4v1 with every available Lord on the hardest difficulty and all of them were no match. I can't find a real challange in this RTS, so it got very boring pretty quick. Problem with Stronghold games after all is you need to find the Meta Troop (from my experience mainly Troops with high amount of HP), then build like 150 of them 5 Catapults and you win the game, 'cause the AI is too dumb to properly use Traps or other defensive Structures so there is no need for extensive planning.In other RTS games, like Company of Heroes 2, going into a 4v1 without being a mastermind you get f*cked to hell and back by the AI on hardest difficulty - Something I have never experienced in Stronghold games. In CoH2 specifically the AI can actually manage to destroy your base in the late game. In Stronghold you build like 2 walls and 1 tower and the AI NEVER manages to kill you. Sometimes you see a breach in the walls, but thats not too tragic. Just send in your 50 "tanks" and you're fine. In CoH2 you can't just cower in your base and try to build up - sometimes it actually works, but in most of my games, when I get pushed all the way into my home base, I might as well give up. Nearly no resource income is the main problem there. That's what actually balances the "camping" in CoH2, as well as Artillery. You build a massive Army of Anti-Tank Infatry in your base and don't try to push until it's completed? Ain't happening 'cause the Enemy uses Artillery strikes to prevent that - Something that Stronghold doesn't feature.I know that WW2 and the Warlord era are 2 COMPLETELY different things and you can't compare them, but FireFly failed the balancing in ALL of their Stronghold games (that i have played so far).Long story short: It's a great game for beginners in RTS games, but FireFly made the same mistake once again. No real balancing for "base camping". There is no need to push until you finished your ginormous army of "Tanks", because you can do all your stuff in the Stronghold. Resources are not really connected to the "outside world", everything you need is available at spawn. Now I know it's kinda the deal with Strongholds, you sit in there to protect yourself, but if that's what the game is about, than make the enemy stronger. Larger/Smarter attacks, Stronger defense on the AI's Strongholds (3 Archers on the wall during a major attack are you kidding me???) and the game would be playable for longer than 2 maybe 3 hours.In my opinion this game was a great chance that FireFly missed.Feel free to discuss this matter with me in the Comments

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing RTS games and have a fondness of the Stronghold series. I loved the artwork, the goofy CGI, and the economy building. I would spend hours making my own custom maps and just spend hours spawning lions on huge armies to see which side would win. That being said, I have no nostalgia for this game and can only wonder why it came out so poorly.To start, the only real thing to change from the original series and Warlords is the Warlord mechanic and some economy re-skin. The warlord mechanic just from the first 5 missions of the first campaign are clunky and just an overall hassle to work around. I'm spending so much time protecting a warlord that won't respawn its units, defenses, etc. besides that, the enemy economy is limitless and spawns constant units that push at these same pointless and useless warlords. It would be different if I could set up defenses in their area but you cannot do so because it isn't your estate even though you are their 'master'. Now I do understand later in the campaigns different warlords act differently and can make castles, defenses, etc. but why make the first campaign so boring and a tedious without showing off the cool aspects of the warlord mechanic?And the game is made in 2023 and still uses the worst CGI imaginable. Sorry but my nostalgia doesn't translate to ugly CGI. I love Starcraft 1 and love that Starcraft 2 didn't have the same animation, sprites, cut scenes, etc. Onto performance, the best way to win some of the battles early on is to use fire arrow carts. the first time I assemble a group of them and fire it crashes the game and makes me lose progress on the boring mission that I already didn't want to play. There is no save/load mechanic for campaign missions, no hot key customability, etc.Game has like 5 campaign DLC for some reason? The game is only worth buying on an extreme sale, if they had made a better game they would have made their money instead of microing out DLC

And while a lot of reviews like to say 'It's not 2000 anymore, it doesn't work', I can go back to Stronghold HD and have a blast. The game aged like fine wine, while this feels like it needed more time to mature.Yes, it's going back a little to older strongholds for better and worse. It's hard to put my finger on, so here is my attempt:They added a day counter yet there's no 'daily change' stat for resources that would help with the castle sim aspect.Building is back to the original fashion and it works so much better than what Stronghold 3 offered, except placing something on a wall just.. Makes the wall disappear. Gone. No more defense until you break things down and burn more resources if you're building on the edge of your rather limited estate.While I do not enjoy the estate system, the warlords system /is/ an improvement on Stronghold 2, making them more interactive, more useful and more accessible. I just wish I had more room to build my castle on.Speaking of building: I miss more buildings changing art/model to match walls they're put up against.  I wish to site my dang granary, sire! (Disclaimer: My experience so far is just from dipping my toe into the campaign. Skirmish had a puddle of a map pool and I shied away from that for now, I do hope they aren't going to use the modding scene as a crutch. I enjoy having official maps officially balanced made around the ideas they had in mind while making the game).Sure it's 3D, I like sprites but there's nothing wrong with it, except the models become harder to identify when zoomed out. When I think an RTS with 3D graphics that worked I'd think of something like Age of Empires three.. It looks like this game came out years before that game both in terms of options and just graphics while Stronghold HD looks like it could've come out yesterday.The settings are lacking, on that front, too. There is no borderless windowed mode and Every.Single.Time. I tab back in they insist on asking me what UI scaling I want. The UI itself I also have some issue with.. It lacks the personality. It feels like a blank black slate you'd see in a flash game without softened edges or more colour to make it match the graphics before it. If it had a more green and light brown colour palette it'd fit a lot better, but it's lacking art, too. It's lacking a scribe to represent your people. It feels like it has less info to show than prior games yet shows more and floods the screen.As for people objecting to the voices.. Well.. It feels like they held back, too. Like they realized that it wouldn't be as acceptable as it would've been to have fun with it like they did for their own culture and now there's still people objecting. By trying to do both, be gentle/hold back and try to be funny/extravagent, they did neither and it hasn't caught me with anything.. Quotable, I suppose? I might also just be getting older.But there are positives. I tried to balance them with the negatives, but I do not have anything bad to say about the music. They went that extra step since the beta before to add peasants moving about. To give more life to the castle they contemplated not adding because of potential time restraints. They gave them voice lines and went that little extra bit to make it feel like a proper stronghold.The combat, too, feels like an upgrade. The pacing feels just right, it feels familiar, but we also have a bit more control. I do really enjoy those parts.This game gives me some hope for future strongholds in that they're taking design steps back in the right direction. This game dashes some hope for future strongholds in that it's still not quite there yet and I worry they might give up some hope or won't get the budget to keep it going. So, while technically I should give it a thumbs down and I feel a little dirty for not doing so... I want Firefly to know that the chances of a more all out success are still there. I do enjoy my time with this game. It's just that it still misses just a little bit of that soul from the past and basic options from the present.

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit that I was sceptical at first about Stronhold going to Asia, but the theme works really well for the game. The histories of China, Mongolia and Japan make a good source for missions, the asian style castles look nice and the lord and peasant concept of SH works just as well in feudal Asia as in medieval Europe.There are some good advances compared to Crusader2: we now have bannermen and generals in our army. Unit collision works much better now. And most importantly there is the Warlord system of AI controlled vassal estates. Along with castle building you can also do some empire building now. I hope this will be continued and extended in future titles.The engine is still the same old one from Crusader2 - with some improvements, but also limitations. Crashes in multiplayer are currently the biggest problem of this game. It is extremly important that this gets adressed quickly. Multiplayer is what keeps this game alive in the long run.Another area that needs more attention is the map editor. It is a very powerful tool and you can do amazing stuff with it. But it also has a steep learning curve and there are still bugs, which can cause a new map to crash. There are several good maps sitting in the PCs of their authors, who are waiting for the editor to be fixed. Right now map makers should save often and always under a new name (like mymap_01, mymap_02, ...). That way there is always a working version to go back to.One excellent thing was the meta game, that FF had organized on their discord server in the run up to the launch. I never saw another company do such a cool "game around the game" with the fan community. That is a really nice addition to the overall gaming experience and could be lots of fun in the future, if we get the Shogunate, the Dynasty and the Horde to battle it out in new competitions.

_childDocuments_.review: [Stronghold Warlords could be so much better]It breaks my heart to write these lines but I feel like Firefly Studios really needs to reevaluate their ethos regarding the series. Until today, I would have recommended SH Warlods but seeing the new update video, i changed my mind and here's why. ____________________________________________________________________First, what's good?1) The SettingI love the asian setting, the general design of troops and buildings is really nice. The variety is praiseworthy and it seems like Firefly really dug down into asian history to find some cool troops (flame thrower, how cool is that?) to bring new spice to the series. There's more potential here, as FF could add day and nighttime in a future patch, which could lead to more dynamic AI as well as a much more sophisticated experience of playing, both strategically as well as aesthetically. 2) Dynamics of the gameOne of my major issues with SH Crusader 2 was that the units felt slow and kind of unexciting. Fighting in the old games felt quick, challenging and even those old 2D sprites had a stronger feeling of impact to me.Warlords greatly improved on that. Moving my units over the battlefield feels better than in Crusader 2 and is fun. The stronger units are slow, but you know, if they arrive, they are not easily dealt with. Lighter units move fast. This is very subjective and kind of hard to describe, but hopefully people will understand what I mean here. It's fun to tear down defenses with catapults, mortars and rockets, and seeing an ox explode in an army of the oponent gave me more than one big evil grin on my face. :-)3) GraphicsStronghold was never really about the graphics for me and you could criticize the game for definitely not looking as good as a game in 2021 could be. However, FF is still an indie developer and thus credit where credit is due. The units are very well designed and have lots of cool little detail, so do the buildings and the world. The lighting is nice (and could get really cool if there was a night mode), the colours seem livley but not as comic-ish as in the first trailers. 4) Story campaignSo far, I've played the story mode until the last mission of Genghis Khan and there were some cool and creative missions until now. I genuinely enjoyed it, had some very welcome challenges and would recommend anyone who buys the game to try it. It's fun and feels very stronghold, although - on normal difficulty - most of is rather easy. So I'd suggest going hard, if you want the oldschool SH challenge. ____________________________________________________________________Now, what is BAD?1) The game is STILL very buggyUnits get stuck (ninjas when climbing over walls), the game crashed everytime I tried to play it with friends online recently, rockets got stuck mid air, mortars didn't shoot their projectiles, one AI lord just randomly died while being sieged by me. Defense towers didnt function at all because they were kind of in between my lands and the warlord's. and thus just did not react to my orders. There were also graphical bugs like the whole world being flooded (looked hilarious, though).This is happening, even after FF released major improvement updates.2) AI is really uncreative and dullWhile there are multiple warlords with different perks in theory, practically they are kind of useless in most maps. They don't really act individually, they just wait to be conquered by either me or the AI opponents. Of course, each warlord has a different perk, but neither the food or ressource supplies nor the troop attacks are kind of a game changer for me. If i just wait, build up my army and then run each of them over, any castle they build falls easily. I haven't tried this on extreme difficulty but I expected them to be at least some kind of challenge on normal. You really have to play with them to make use of the feature, but the game works exactly the same without them and thus - if you think about it being THE MAJOR USP of this game - it's very disappointing. The AI lords are another thing. I'm giving credit to FF for adding more castle building variety with one of the latest patches, however, all the AI lords are still very boring to fight against. None have special tactics in attacking or defending, you can pretty much run over any AI with any bigger army. With the old games, you really had to think about how to approach the Pig or the Wolf. Even with an extreme advantage of the AI's, it feels like they wait for me to attack them. I never really felt threatened. Occasionaly, they send a small army that you can easily defend with some ranged units on walls. Further, most AI's I played against always attacked the warlords, even with my troops being in close range. Thus, their army just walks past mine, towards a warlord and tries to conqer that one. The AI does not feel well programmed or profound, it feels like one AI with different appearances. Of course, there is some variety, like Genghis mostly using the horse archers, but in the end, all of them just occasionally send small groups of troops and wait for me to conquer them. With the old enemies, you wouldn't just walk into the Wolf's castle as there were traps, fire and worse. Here, you just tear a hole in the wall and send your troups directly towards the lord. Done. Won.3) Firefly Studios seems to ignore feedbackHere's the dealbreaker that changed my mind today.Although FF released a free update with a new AI oponent and some improvement, the game still crashed while playing multiplayer skirmish. However, that would be kind of tolerable with me being a long time fan and WANTING to like the game. However, FF decided to announce a PAID DLC for 2 new warlords and some new maps. For me, this is like a big "F*** you" right to my face. The game is still unpolished, has major stability issues and FF has the guts to announce PAID content updates? I get it, you gotta earn some money and keep the costs under control, but man, this stung as a fan. I bought the game on release, paid the full price for it and what I got was a buggy, unfinished product. And now, instead of fixing things, they decide to release paid updates and add content that's simply not necessary YET.Why add additional maps or warlords before the major flaws have been worked out? Why not finally LISTEN to feedback and improve the engine, the troop limits or the AI? Yes, I probably imagine this to be much easier than it is in real life, but why not just own the issues as a company and give your fans a sign that your GENUINELY care about them and what they have to say?So, to sum it up:Don't buy Stronghold Warlords if you expect a finished and polished game with great AI. The graphics are nice, it's fun to play when it doesn't crash, but currently, things are just not there yet.I truly hope that Firefly Studios realise that there's more to this series than a half-assed new release with bugs that are apparent since the last two games. Maybe they get that, instead of releasing paid DLCs, fixing the major issues of the core game will make so much more fans happy. Maybe, listening to serious and genuine feedback will help make the game a great successor to a series that gave me hours of joy. Otherwise this has been the last Stronghold release I bought and that would really suck. For me and for them.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand how a game can come out in 2021 that uses the same tech as games from 2000. This same is loaded with all the issues you would expect from a RTS that came out back then. This review is for the campaign as I've already beat all but the Japanese one.     Unit movement is horrible. If you set a group to patrol they will but if they get into a fight the ranged units will attack the the first thing they run into then stand there and stop moving. However the melee units will go back to patrolling and charge on ahead which can split your troops. The reason i use the patrol command? Because there isn't a good attack command that wont have your melee troops rush the enemy then stand there and stop moving even when set to aggressive stance and there is an enemy a few steps away.     Then there is the Genghis Khan faction....... A faction that doesn't make castles in a castle building game. A faction that relies on horse troops when they can't go on walls to attack enemy troops or take over warlords as they can't get in his building. Yes they can make the weaker ground troops but they get cut down easily while the horses are useless when attacking a castle. Looks like in multiplayer all factions have access to all the units including the 5 or so unique ones (Maybe not so unique units as they all get them)     Now you would think since there are only a couple factions that they would be have some flavor of the culture to them. NOPE. You have Genghis Khan using Imperial horse units and building Chinese styled building just like every faction in the game. You really can't tell them apart. I have only played the campaign so far so I don't know about multi player but unless you see a unique unit (which there are only a couple) you can't tell the factions apart.     They have added a warlord system to this game to Spice it up! It doesn't. First you cant build defenses around them so you have to just have armies standing around the leader (read capture point) and put some archers in his little tower to give them some range. They don't make new units to defend themselves and they don't really do much besides act as a store to spend your influence points. Honestly they are all pretty horrible but the Tiger which is very powerful for some reason. He will send an army of about 30 mid to elite units for the low low price of 200 influence. This is compared to the horse warlord which will send 3 elite horses for 300 influence....... what. Where did they decide this pricing and the horses don't do anything because there is 3 of them!     This is my first Stronghold game and I was very excited about the castle building aspect. It did not live up to expectations. I should have stuck with the total war series for that. The best tactic is to just rush the walls with archers as the walls provide poor cover and some extra range to the defenders. Its very easy to clean an entire wall with an archer rush and then let your melee characters dig though it. They are just a little slower then a catapult. Its almost not worth bringing siege equipment as they are slow, die easy, and don't do much damage to the walls (with the exception of the gunpowder one shot unit).     The presentation is very dated as is the graphics. This game is on par with a 2000 game with its lifeless level design and bad graphics. Then enemy don't react they send growing waves at you and then have static units in their base that will stand where they are and fight. They wont gather up and try to stop you they just stand there till you get close and attack. Cut scenes remind me of the fist age of empires game in quality and when your warlord addresses you (I thought I was him?) then he will do a preset animation that is the same every time he talks to you and the animation doesn't have anything to do with what hes saying. They couldn't even have them lip sync. Also no tool tips on the enemy units and crappy ones on your own units. Want to see the stats of the enemy units too bad. Want to see the walls hp NOPE.     Overall this looks like a cash grab. The company used the code and mechanics of a much older game and slapped some lipstick on it. This game is beyond dated and it just came out and I don't see a way for them to fix it as the issues are not just with the game itself but in the programming of the game too. I would do a hard pass if i were you.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: This is the successor to Stronghold Crusader 2, and better in every way.  It's 90% the same game but with some nice enhancements.  Graphics are better, AI is better, UI is better, production chain is better, castles are better, new units and ROADS are a welcome addition, combat seems more balanced and engaging (i.e. fun) but it's the same game.  I play SC2 at least once a week with a friend, we play workshop maps and I've even created a few workshop maps myself.  We both bought the game last night, went straight into Skirmish mode and found it all perfectly familiar, but better!  you might say, "The SAME??  but, but I want new and different".   To that i say, "No, you don't".   This developer did not pollute their game with half-baked concepts and over-think every element... instead they left the formula largely alone and just made it better.  The things they did add were useful, and the things they removed were not.The only con is a sore lack of skirmish maps, however the workshop is open and the map editing tool is the same.  TLDR:  If you enjoyed the formula of Stronghold Crusader 2 you will love Warlords, period.

_childDocuments_.review: After nearly 50 hours of gameplay and a few updates later that fixed a few bugs/glitches I am honestly mostly really impressed and happy with the game. I have been playing stronghold games throughout my childhood (mostly on the first Stronghold Crusader) and own and have played every single Stronghold except for Stronghold 3. I am disappointed in there only being 4 different Lords in the game so far, I definitely think that is a very low number of Lords to start out in the base of the game for a Custom Skirmish. The other complaint that I have is the really low number of troops that you can have during a Custom Skirmish and would like to be able to have 2 to 3 thousand military units capable without crashes or instability issues, if that means they dumb down the graphics a bit to do so then I'd rather have that so long as they aren't less than 1080p. Other than those 2 complaints I honestly think that the game is really well designed, the economic system is very well done and nicely complicated without being overly complicated (I'm looking at you Stronghold 2) and the Warlord System really adds to the gameplay of each match. The amount of control that you have over each and every resource that you gather/distribute is very nice. All the unique units in the game is really neat the only thing I wish they had was a healer type unit to heal your troops and a unit count/max number displayed on screen so I could tell where I was at and plan accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: So, are there any serious problems with this game?YES!Does this make this game a disaster as some claim?By the gods NO. So for starters, this is the first Stronghold game I play, so I don't really have an emotional connection like some players. Since I bought the deluxe version, I won the first game of this saga and played a few missions to see why the original was so loved. The reason i bought this game is because i'm a big fan of feudal japan history and i'm frustrated that there is hardly any RTS on the topic and even if some aspects disappointed me, I am very happy to have bought the deluxe version and I am having a lot of fun.I'm going to address the main issue that critics tackle that I think is unfair: The graphics.I think most people don't understand that there is a difference between ugly graphics and simple graphics.One of my favorite shows is called Avadon and it gets a lot of criticism for being very ugly, but I don't agree. It's super simplistic, but its simplicity serves the game and lets us fill in the holes with our imaginations. I can understand that most people don't appreciate this kind of graphics, but I find it cruel just to say that they are bad.Stronghold Warlords has simple graphics compared to today's big RTS. But I find them charming, I love looking at the attention to detail of the buildings and watching the peasants go about their lives. I really feel like the founder of an Asian city. Some people have too high expectations for a small independent studio, by the beards of Zeus I've seen a few reviews that used 3 Kingdoms Total War as the example to follow. TOTAL ♥♥♥♥♥♥ WAR a triple A with a gigantic team and hundreds of developers. C'mom!On the other hand a valid criticism is concerning the UI. She is ... correct in the sense that she is clear and you are never lost ... but she is ugly. I can't understand why such a colorful game has such a dark UI. And we're talking about Asia here, why not take inspiration from Japanese paintings or something like that?Another problem I have (and apparently I'm the only one) is with the Font used, it's so generic and Mobal game like. And it would have been so easy to have just found one that was more oriental. Viner Hand ITC would be my choice, but anyway ...Let's talk about gameplay. There isn't much to say if you've played a Stronghold game before, the formula is the same. But now we have the Warlords system and although I find the concept very fascinating, the realization is ... correct. It's an okay mechanic ... but something more is missing ... for a game that apparently exists thanks to this mechanic I'm amazed at its simplicity. I can understand those who are disappointed, because the developers spent MONTHS telling us how the Warlords system was innovative and blah blah blah.But the most important thing is to build your castle and this part is fun as always. Maybe we could have had a little innovation, but at the same time I'm don't want this aspect of the game to change. If you like the Stronghold formula this game is going to please you in this aspect, but don't have too many expectations for the Warlords.Anyway, this game has some issues and if you are not yet asleep with my gigantic review or you are a game developer, I will come back to the details which I think are really frustrating. But I want to make it very clear that this is I wrote such a long review this is because I LOVED this game, I WANT people to give it an honest chance, I want patches and DLCs (Sengoku Jidai DLC PLEEEEEEEEASE). So if you want the new Age of Empires or Total War you will probably be disappointed, but if you like eastern history, RTS or both, PLEASE don't listen to people who say this one is the worst game ever. It doesn't, there are many flaws, but also charm, heart and passionate developers who WANT to make a good game instead of a cash machine.And if a developer ever reads this mega review, I'd like to thank you and beg you not to be put off by the overly cruel reviews this game is getting. You had managed to make me fall in love with your game, and I don't think I'm the only one.Now let's talk about some issues that can be fixed quite easily, but which for me can make a big difference.1) Why do all factions have the same units and the same visuals? If there is one thing that really, REALLY bothered me in this game is the fact that when I play like a samurai lord I have Mongolian units and others speaking Chinese in my army. This breaks my immersion so much. And I don't even want each people to have their own units with unique stats. But take the basic barracks units and change their visuals a bit according to their culture. For the Japanese, look for Ashigaru on google images and donate a hat for the models. And please ask a Japanese, a Mongolian and a Vietnamese to say generic phrases, so that we can stop having units speaking in Chinese in my samurai army. PLEASE!2) Several people say that Firefly fails to re-capture the magic of classic Strongholds. And I'm afraid the developers haven't quite figured out what this means. Taking over the mechanics and improving them is important, but the magic is in the little details. Why do the peasants not have portraits? Giving a face to your characters is something very important. Why don't we no longer have a crazy guy yelling "SAVING" "LOADING" and saying "hello" and "goodbye" when I enter / exit the game? It's those kinds of details that made people so nostalgic for the original games, so why not use that nostalgia?3) Why don't the Warlords have personalities? What if the crane lord had a super arrogant voice? the dragon that of an old sage? the bull that of an old warrior and each had a unique model? ETC, ETC, ETCThis would have made the game so much more memorable and the system would be more unique and special.4) The maps are WHAAAAAAAAAAAAY to tiny And I think I've already said too much and the Shogunate will not be impose alone, so have a nice day and thank you for your patience ;)"In the midst of chaos, there is also opportunity"Sun Tzu

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself isn't bad. How could it be? It's a lot like the old Stronghold games with the same core mechanics in place. I'd say 20 EUR is a more fitting price for what's currently on the table. embraces all the core mechanics of the old stronghold games, and added a few new ones but nothing groundbreaking.Having played the older stronghold games, I'd think it's safe to say that if you liked these games in general you'll probably enjoy this too. however there are some early day problems we encountered;The game also adds a fear system to shift your peasants towards happiness at the cost of production, vice versa. While I have not used this myself I can see why this could definitely be useful later in the game.Diplomacy was also added to the game, but i think that could be implemented with a little bit more depth to it. right now you just get an x amount of points every in-game day. this can be increased by building an embassy or another building which i cant remember the name of. these buildings have a max amount that can be built and only cost money. their yield can be further increased by connecting them to your Keep with a road. simple enough. That's all. nothing more to it as far as I've seen. It now gets frustrating when playing on the big 8 people map, where the furthest warlords constantly get snagged because they're in firing range of other lords' archers. they suddenly turn towards the other lord while my troops are still standing next to the warlord on top of his keep. I have yet to figure out how this is possible, but it seems that this might be just a bug.what the game does do better compared to the previous game though is give you information about underlying mechanics of buildings. tells you how they work, what they need, what they give. especially so early after the launch, its nice to not have to google for this stuff if it's even on the internet already.
