_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Stronghold titles since I was very young and picked this up a few days ago. I've gotten several games in with my brother and father who are also longtime fans and we have not been disappointed. Warlord system has been a fresh facelift to the estate system of earlier games in the series and allowed a level of gameplay, largely optional if you want to engage in it, that I have found quite enjoyable. This is also a matter of personal preference but I also believe that you should always play with the strong walls feature on.Having read a number of the reviews on this game before writing my own, it seems to me that most of the negative reviews are criticisms of the game not being the same as, at least in its economy and certain city building parts, not as complex as stronghold 2. This criticism is correct, but I believe it is up to the player to decide whether or not they believe that's a bad thing. There is a relatively high barrier-to-entry for new players in this genre so as a matter of personal preference I do not object to the streamlining of the city management aspect of the game. I think this tension is a similar problem had by other complex games like Supreme Commander in which fans are upset by the simplification of the game by later titles but the franchise's ability to produce more titles declined because the game is too complex to bring in a large enough amount of new players to sustain the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Long time ago in the beforefore time, in the midst of Warcraft III and Command & Conquer and gamers relishing in base building and zerging the AI, a little company puts out 'yet another' RTS style but had a uniqueness to it that garnered enough attention to release Stronghold 2 - which is where my tale begins. SH2 is without a doubt - my most favorite game ever. I was in college at the time, and I can remember yearning for classes to finish so I could go home to my castle, where...as a mighty king...I reigned over the peasants, fought off plague, droughts, bandits, and forced them to scoop poop while I dealt with rats in my granary. Hours and hours - the comical nature of your opponents vs. the sometimes hard to obtain goals had me replaying both the path of war and peace countless times. But the shining light of it was was the freebuilding - you could just build and torture (take care) of your public and add events to make the gametime more enjoyable. Sure, there were bugs, errors, crashes, pathing issues, etc. I dealt with them as they came because I loved my castle and the archers on the walls and clicking on a little girl running around the pig farm would greet me with a statement that would make me smile. Then Legends came along - sure, it's fine, but still not SH2. I just didn't get into werewolves and such so I went backwards and tried Crusader - even though it was 2D - still was super fun to play. Then SH3 released and they began taking the things away that made SH2 and the other ones unique and unforgettable. But ask anyone - it's always been 50/50 with one certain title held close to the hearts of SH fans. This title is NO different. The only way to decide if you like it or not is to play it and see for yourself. Anyone (including myself) will always take their favorite title in the series and compare it to that. Trying to view it as neutral as I can - it's a standard run of the mill title that takes all meaning out of the structures and puts emphasis on achieving the goals for each mission.With that being said, the game (to me) is disappointing because it lacks character. For example in SH2 once you set your granary, and peasants start their work - most often than not, one of them will steal food. Therefore, you set a guard post near the granary - as you lack a vast amount of wood - where you placed that post was very important because you couldn't just build ten of them. Not only that - but in order to punish the criminal - you'd have to build a courthouse, a torture building, and set up things like Racks or Stocks. All of that took quite a lot to build and was quite fun following that path to completion while still having to worry about food, soldiers, castle walls, etc. This game lacks ALL of that - not the structures - but the  behind them. Example: In Warlords if you are running low on rice - just spam rice fields or cut the rations and build superior houses with temples - you can literally take away all the food rations and still have people coming to your castle. In SH2 if people start leaving the castle - it was HARD to get them back (most of the time) because you lacked resources and/or gold and usually ended up restarting the mission over again with a new plan. The very first mission in the peace path for this title had me collecting 375 of rice, vegetables, and meat - Rice and vegetables stuck at around 200 even though I had 15 pig stalls the meat stayed at 0. With 2 days left I shut down production of rice and veg, took them to 1/4 rations and got 400 meats in one fell swoop EVEN though my popularity was at -25. I made it to the last mission in the peace campaign - I have to say it hurts to play. It's boring, no castle flow, and the missions are set up to start you at a disadvantage - I honestly hate that. For example in missions you are able to purchase materials, like wood - but in every single mission they take away the option in order to make the game more difficult (I think). This drives me absolutely bananas - I'm all for a challenge, but when I have literally 40 wood shops and 8 pieces and i need one more house to get the pop objective - but I'm not able to purchase wood simply because..and the timer runs out and I have to suffer through the whole thing again...because of 2 pieces of wood....It gets a Thumbs up (Down for real though) from me because - it's better than SH3 and for every negative review there should be a positive one.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I really did. But I can’t. As an age-old fan of the series I get more and more lost on what exactly it is that Firefly wants to deliver with their 3d-games. This game isn’t a (good) castle sim. It also isn’t a modern strategy game. It’s unique selling point, the warlord-mechanic, feels utterly irrelevant and the gameplay soon becomes repetitive. So the game isn’t fun either – In my opinion at least.1.) What I like about the game:To be sure: I really liked some of the little details of the game. For example, I really enjoyed the lighting effects as well as the colors and architectural details of the buildings. Another aspect I was pleasantly surprised about, is that troops can now march in formation – and that looks just cool compared to earlier titles in the series. Combat also feels less clunky than in earlier Strongholds.2.) This game is not about strongholds!My major criticism is that despite those improvements in small details, the overall game experience as a castle sim is very poor: First of all, maps are rather small and the space to build a castle is limited. Furthermore, the game forces you to place a large number of buildings inside that cramped space. The amount of rice fields needed to supply a growing population is, for example, just insane. There always was a moment when I just didn’t know where to place those fields anymore. In combination, these features mean that there is basically no room left to experiment with different castle designs: The best “castle” to build is just a simple, fortified rectangle – that ultimately looks more like a huge city than a castle. In my opinion, this very negatively impacts game experience as every game feels very much the same. Same strategy, same buildings, same “castle”. Where is the flexibility and dynamic of the original Stronghold titles? It all feels so repetitive in Warlords.3.) This game is not about warlords!Thus, with Stronghold we get a worse castle sim than earlier Strongholds that just shines with regard to some little details. What a fan of the series might ask: What is the selling point of Warlords? This obviously is supposed to be the warlord-mechanic. Just what do we, the old stronghold fans, really get? In my opinion, the “warlords” in “Stronghold Warlords” really are no warlords at all, but just some sort of fortified marketplaces that need to be conquered first for players to then spend a strange currency, aka “diplomacy points” (which is simply generated out of nowhere over time), to purchase goods which they don’t really need anyway. As a cynical caricature of capitalism this might have worked – as an honest mechanic in a 2021 RTS-game … I am not sure. Moreover, the AI is so focused on capturing warlord in the early stages of the game that they give up their main advantage against a human player: Being quick in building up an efficient economy and attacking the human player early. In sum: The whole mechanic feels utterly useless and even hampers the AI in playing up to their strength.In short: Although I really enjoyed a lot of small details in “Stronghold Warlords”, the fact that this just isn’t a good castle sim, the fact that gameplay feels repetitive and lastly the mere irrelevance of the “warlords” prevents me from liking this game – as much as I would have liked to.

_childDocuments_.review: In the games' current state I would definitly not recommend buying it.The amount of issues it currently has truely makes for a bad expierence and is generally not fun to play. There are quite a bit of issues, from bugs like men that glitch out on siegetowers to random in game crashes and very low FPS drops. The game is unbalanced (which is actually quite normal for Stronghold games, but this one takes the cake by far). Some units can ruin the entire gameplay expierence like mortarspamm which leaves you unable to do anything but take steps back until the enemy is in your base. The Walls (Can I even call them that?) are extremely useless, with pathetic HP which means 4 enemy infantry units can break down a gate in 15-30 seconds. Even though there is the option of adding dubble the HP to walls, it barely does anything. It also doesn't make sense to be able to put siegecamps into captured Warlords their bases (basically estates for the Legends players ;)) since the maps are so small you are able to rocket spamm into the enemy their base making the game totally un-fun. Stronghold Legends didn't have this issue since the maps had actual breathing room.The feedback from previous games was not added and just plainly ignored. Everyone kept saying and recommending way larger maps, yet we still play in a claustrophobic field which leaves little room for actual combat in between bases. The 'combat' there is, is mostly just sieges which end rather quick since the low HP walls take care of that.There also seems to be a small delay on orders (small but noticable) which can completely mess you up in critical moments. Spamm clicking on the ground won't help since the troops 're-route' their path which sometimes makes them totally stand still and sometimes even bug out and ignore the command entirely. The multiplayer of this game, for being a new game has very very few players currently playing it, making it sometimes even hard to actually fill a lobby, or waiting for a looong time.I do very much like the artsyle, the artists did a very great job, it has a good and well thought out look (coming from a fellow artist). I also really like the economy in this game, it's quite new for Stronghold and I think this adds a new depth to the game, the older games had a more 'plain' way of happiness and income on which they built and expanded.Stronghold Warlords should have had at least another 2 years of development and then be released as an Alpha to be further polished, because now it feels like you are playing a broken unbalanced game. This could have been a Banger if not for the pushed release and very unpolished aspects. The Stronghold games were part of my childhood and early teenage years, I've played them for hundreds upon hundreds of hours.. Yet I unfortunately don't see myself playing this game any longer.I wish the best of luck to the developers, that they can fix this game and actually come to a point where they have a game they hoped they released at the start, but there is still a very long road ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: The latest offering from the Stronghold family is Warlords, set in the intensely conservative and traditional land of Ancient China.Much the same could be said of the game itself, and its developers, Firefly.Remember the old bug where one soldier would emerge from the barracks a second or two after all the others, so he'd be left behind when you clicked the group? That's in. Remember the ludicrously small army sizes? 8 enemies to fight and 66 troops to do it with? That's in. The maximum army size is only 200. Incredible considering I used to design maps way back in Stronghold 2 with up to 16 enemy armies triggering at once.Remember the hopeless pathing where your troops would ignore an open breach in the wall and stand waiting to be slaughtered by the AI? That's in.But wait! I hear you cry, the whole game has been reskinned into an Oriental setting!Bessie the cow is now Bessie the buffalo! Ooh, my lord.Trees are now bamboo! Oooh, my lord.Churches and mosques are now temples, and there's more of them! Ooooh, my lord.And you can paint little roads in your castle! Oooooh, my lord.To be fair, there is one new(ish) thing in Stronghold Warlords. Estates are back, and in some ways they are quite cool. The estates are held by warlords, and you can influence the warlords to improve their own defences or give you resources. Some warlords even provide decent armies that could turn the tide in battle. But what could have been a good idea is ruined by its implementation. Say you conquer an estate in the good old fashion, and the warlord submits to you. You can keep him sweet by adding more influence, up to a maximum of 300. You can even do this automatically. But once you reach 300 influence, the auto-influence is auto-disabled - for the human player. The AI can then pile on its own influence and pilfer your warlord without a fight, quite likely wiping out your defensive contingent as well, since warlords are quite tough in melee. I can see how this mechanic might work in MP, but against the AI it's just pointless makework to have to keep checking your warlords every minute or so to see if the auto-influence has been auto-disabled. Then there are the scenarios. The first few are ok, if uninspired. But so buggy I lost patience with them eventually.   Don't firefly beta-test these things?Stability is ok, I wouldn't put it higher than that. I had crashes on the scenarios but not the skirmish games, though there was a fair bit of frame freeze.The game includes (or claims to include) a sandbox mode. I used to enjoy these particularly in Crusader and Stronghold 2. But it doesn't work, for two reasons. First, it's impossible to initiate invasions, which makes the whole exercise a bit futile. Come on Firefly, it's not as if you're reinventing the wheel! Second, you can't reload a sandbox game (or at least I couldn't). When I tried to reload, it crashed the game, not only for that save but all the others. I had to restart my computer to get Stronghold Warlords to run again in skirmish mode.In summary, I'm giving Stronghold Warlords a thumbs down for now, not because I think there's no hope for it, but frankly because in its present state it reeks of sloppiness in implementation. If like me you are a huge fan of the series, and are thinking of buying the game, hold off for the moment. It's not as if there's any rush to buy it, as in all but the reskin, it's exactly the same game as the ones you have already.Firefly might then actually do something to put the game in order, because my impression so far is that they know they have a more or less captive audience, and are coasting along on the bare minimum of effort.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold veteran review:(note that while i'm 18 hours into the campaign i have not completed the last part set in Japan and the game has not yet introduced Fear factor buildings or religious buildings yet and so i cannot comment on their use)Pros and cons.Pros.- The warlord system is great and to beat the campaign (at least on hard mode) the warlords have to be used and managed well- New units are great additions (mortar, rockets,  etc)- other new units like horse archers and horse cavalry seem balanced and useful in warlords when compared to crusader 2- Roads are a great addition to city planning when thinking of diplomacy point generation- Unit collision makes a huge difference to the game- first time campaign difficulty settings - good for the less experienced players- Music and voice acting is greatCons- Bugs. has crashed maybe 5 times in my 18 hours of play. Wall collision not being removed once the wall had been destroyed etc.- Campaign is short for a AUD $50 game (although delivered well and historically accurate)- Campaign takes too long to provide a challenge. The first campaign is almost useless because of how easy and limited it was and almost put me off the game- Dated game engine- still no moatsconclusion:The game feels like  a stronghold game, the new Warlord mechanic actually works well and adds a new layer onto the strategy. Deciding which warlord to take, when and how(by force or diplomacy bidding) is critical in winning your games. Although the engine is outdated and some of the graphics look dated it is easily the best looking 3D stronghold game to date and the slight stylized look tying the world together works better running on their old game engine than a realistic approach would have - i understand their team is small and this is not AAA game production but i would like to see a more realistic environment in the future.Overall the gameplay feels much more refined than crusader 2 and it is aesthetically pleasing  enough to not throw you out of the world you are in. Unfortunately if you enjoy the challenge of the previous stronghold games you can almost skip half the campaign, but learning of the historic battles is what kept me partially entertained in the more basic missions.For RTS stronghold fans it is a great game but may take some time to adapt to the warlords aspect of the gameplay.I have enjoyed it and would check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold: Warlords is a very interesting twist on the past Stronghold games. While many of the well known elements return (which should be expected) a few new ones show up. This Stronghold game was something I have anticipated for since the announcement. I have been a Stronghold fan ever since my father introduced me to the franchise with Stronghold 2 and I still am years later and for years to come.The main element of this game and what it's basically named after are the Warlords. Similar to the estates in other Stronghold games they can be captured by force or they can be captured diplomatically, this is not done by honour, but with diplomacy points (kind of the same thing just a different name, but there is more to it). It also is not a simple "click once, done", but depending on the warlord you are trying to capture it can take a few or a lot of your points, not to mention that other lords can do the same and take away using both methods too.I have noticed that with this particular game, it is very heavy on economy. With other Stronghold games I usually build a few buildings and that's all I need, but here you need to really watch space and resources. Wood (or bamboo) is not as plentiful or even existant on a few maps, which definitely will be a bind several times.Looking at the units in the game, we can definitely see the typical ones such as bow and crossbow men, catapults, trebuchets, mantlets, horse arches and a few more. There are also many new ones, very interesting are those with explosive capabilities. I won't list them here, but a quick YouTube video will show you everything you need to know.When it comes to the content itself, depending on how you play you should be good for at least 10 hours if not even 20 for the entire campaign, both military and economic. I usually go for building a very strong economy, then castle and only then do I start planning attacks. As they have announced their roadmap, we can expect a entirely new campaign route and campaign trials to appear. Content and updates are looking good and there are always improvements and additions being made.The game runs well on highest graphics options, there are a few visual bugs some of them aren't gamebreaking, few are though. As of now there are some kinds of trees that are missing their textures entirely and in one instance the ground was entirely black. Currently the game is not optimised for 4 (3 AI, 1 Player) skirmishes and will easily lag, especially when everyone starts attacking. Imagine that with 7 AI and 1 player, you won't get anywhere close to 1 FPS, you'd be lucky to even have frames every 1 second.Regardless of the bugs and similarities to the other games, Stronghold: Warlords is definitely worth picking up, sale or not. Yes it is not your typical medieval castle builder, but so isn't all Stronghold: Crusader. Both Crusader and Warlords are well done "expeditions" into another culture and I definitely enjoyed them.Overall I give Stronghold: Warlords a very good:9/10+ New and interesting twist on estates and management+ Complicated / difficult but fun to manage economy+ New and fun unitso Few bugs, which hopefully are fixed for the next patcheso AI are predictable, as all the other Stronghold games, but allow for interesting wall designso/- Towers sadly can't be stuffed with 300 bowmen anymore and have a set limito/- Most likely intentional feature: Units have collision now and can't run through crowds / each other without being slowed down massively- Units can't be "fired" -> with weird troop limits gameplay can become difficult without sacrificing units to the enemy(Oh yeah and multiplayer also works, long gone are the days of multiplayer not being available. Thanks for being available on Steam!!)

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Warlords I now understand why the first Stronghold was so beloved and an instant classic. Even though this game plays and arguably looks well, the problem lies with the execution.For example, the campaign missions are ahistorical. Why do I know? Because the battle of Uji of 1180 was not fought by defending a castle. The Minamoto and its allies were defending a bridge! The next mission? It's next to historical fantasy! There are so many mistakes in the English explanatory trailer for the Genpei war campaign like Minamoto no Yoshitomo being a "king" of the Minamotos (luckily, it's better in the Japanese version). If they can't take history seriously, then it's better if they just make historical fiction like in the first Stronghold.Campaign missions flips between an assault with limited units and turtle up and defend. While the former is fine, the latter is a slow slogfest of endless waves of instantly respawned groups of enemies. This is so artificially hard and unnecessarily long. It's not fun when you know that your opponent is cheating and no matter how much lords you conquer, the enemy will just spawn an another army and retake them.The unit roster is also disappointing. Instead of having each civilization having their own units, they just have the generic units and then tacked on civilization unique units like samurais and ninjas in a separate structure wherein you have to buy them instead of actually gathering and manufacturing their weapons and armor. It's also annoying how slow the armored elite units are. It's understandable in the first game but the elite units here are wearing lighter lamellar armor.The only silver lining about this purchase is that I bought the Ultimate edition on sale and I have a Steam copy of Stronghold HD.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the old stronghold games, that hybrid mix between RTS, city builder and survival sim has had successes and failures across the history of the stronghold series and other competitors either dip their toes poorly into this split or fall down on the side of out and out RTS or city builder and don't bother with the other side.So i'm a fan of the series in all honesty.I've been there for the very first Stronghold as well as all the missteps (The less said about Stronghold 3 the better eh?)So I was hopeful for this latest release.But as you'll see from my review, I've refunded the game after having a very broken experience with it. Key pointers to consider before purchasing: - - The different setting of Asia is a nice touch, but the age old tropes of appallingly bad dialogue and stereotypical 'Asian sounding' advisers is just lazy and poorly executed- The entire campaign acts as more of a tutorial for the MP experience, don't expect any COH2 style deep campaign here at all, its literally all used as a build up to teaching you the fundamentals of being able to play PvP, this feels like a huge missed trick considering the change of setting- In skirmish and MP the significant differences between each army are ignored entirely and you can have a mixture of units from each campaign side, rendering any leader choices entirely pointless, it is literally carbon copy army 1 vs carbon copy army 2 in MP and skirmish, again a huge missed opportunity for strategic play against the AI and real players.- I need to mention the bugs, there are many and this release does not feel like a 'gold' release of the game. Its hugely disappointing but sadly not surprising, the game feels like its been rushed for launch and would have warranted a beta release (With a price to match) before labelling this as a complete game, some of the more significant bugs to be aware of: 1) The MP net-code is very very poor, if you are lucky enough to get into a MP game (More on that below) then expect to be kicked, have sync issues and end up being kicked or get an hour into a game with a friend and then find you are kicked, its frustrating when it happens once, doubly annoying when it happens after an hour of game-play with the time invested but repeat occurrences of it just rapidly reduce your will to keep playing.2) A similar issue occurs in SP and SP offline skirmish against AI players. The game will randomly crash to desktop OR worse crash with nothing short of a hard restart of my PC recovering it, again, annoying when it happens the first time, even more so after 30 minutes or more of build up play in a skirmish or campaign game with the added loss of progress and again it just seeps the will out of wanting to carry on playing the game. What's even more frustrating about this is that numerous players have complained about both this and the MP issues since day 1 of launch, nothing has been done to resolve it, for a game costing £30 that's just not good enough and FireFly do not deserve your custom until they resolve such significant game breaking issues.Other things of note:- The unit cap, lots already mentioned by others about this but a unit cap this small for what appears to be such a grand game is just not sufficient. When games ten years older can manage hundreds or even thousands of units aside in skirmish and mp without having to tell you how to fudge it via a INI file setting, its not good enough and just smells like poor game development effort on the part of the devs. If your engine can't handle that many units, maybe you should invest in a better game engine?- The warlords - feel like a huge missed opportunity, the diplomatic efforts with them feel contrived and poorly executed and nowhere near how they've been described in the blurb for the game, just treat them as extended outposts to your own base and you'll be much closer to the truth.- The 'footprint' for building your base feels extremely small on many of the maps and i've found no way to extend this. You can't build on your warlords footprint either and instruct them via upgrades to build on their own. For a game purported to be a mix of city builder and RTS its incredible that you can't expand out across the map like in previous games in the series. Long gone are the turtling strategies of older games in the series where huge multi-stage castles and defences could be created, instead you'll be lucky to even contain all of your buildings in one walled base here.- MP feels very very quiet for such a recent release. Clearly the game has proven relatively popular (Purely based on the number of discussion threads on Steam) but I fear the game breaking bugs are causing this initial pot of people to rapidly reduce in size. In just the first day or so I struggled to get into a MP game that either didn't break or had enough people, that's not a good sign for having a long term online game to play with others.ConclusionsI really wanted to enjoy the game. Granted the graphics aren't a step change from previous iterations in the series and the gameplay hasn't shifted a great deal despite the change of setting but it had huge potential to be a good follow-up to some pretty shoddy sequels in the stronghold back catalogue, but I fear this launch and the lack of QA on some fairly significant game breaking bugs will leave many people with a real sour taste in their mouths.I have kept coming back to the Steam page since refunding to see how quickly the devs would fix the game crashing bugs but I remain annoyed and deeply disappointed that they've yet to resolve these issues despite repeated tickets from players and a number of refunds. With other strategy games on the release radar coming very soon this feels like a focus on getting the game out quickly at the cost of quality and stability is going to leave an already small MP audience with an even smaller playerbase and an even further damaged reputation for the devs.Very disappointed overall

_childDocuments_.review: While it is generally not known as the best chapter in the series, one of my favourite RTS games is Stronghold: Legends. In my childhood I spent countless hours training frost giants, building impenetrable fortresses and converting weak-minded enemy soldiers using demons. After a decade, I can still remember the different units and their strong and weak points, the different maps for multiplayer games and also the time spent creating custom ones that I then shared with other people through multiplayer lobbies. All this time spent in Stronghold: Legends (and other Stronghold titles, that is) is probably what leaves a bitter taste in my mouth after playing Stronghold: Warlords. But let's proceed with order...Before talking about the weak points of the game, let's talk about the few positives: the game is based on a solid formula and, similarly to the previous titles, creating impenetrable fortresses is still really fun. The possibility of placing walls, towers and anti-siege equipment is the focus of the Stronghold series and this title is no less than its predecessors: manning the wall with archers, crossbowmen and other soldiers is as fun as it was a decade ago. The game has boasts five different campaign, allowing players to have hours upon hours of singleplayer content. The campaigns follow four different lords, plus one campaign defined as "economic", since it more based on production than the actual war. Campaign missions will also be replayable (and replayed) thanks to the high difficulty of some of them, similarly, again, to the previous titles of the Stronghold series.Warlords are marketed as the big new addition of this new title: what they are is basically lonely towers scattered around the map that, once controlled, allow the player to use some special actions called edicts to gain some bonuses. These towers are protected by a warlord: a special unit that, similarly to the one of our faction, can kill many soldiers in battle before falling itself. Controlling a tower, something that can be done either military (by defeating the warlord, that will then join our faction) or diplomatically (by using a special currency), annexes the warlord's territory to our faction's, without however leaving us the possibility of placing buildings on it.During the game, by either controlling warlords or creating embassies, we can earn diplomatic points, which can then be spent to gain control of other warlords, emanate edicts or upgrading warlords that we already control. Edicts are rather basic and are usually of commercial nature: you can request gold, wood, diplomatic points and other resources from your warlords, provided that you can afford the initial cost of the edict. The same is for upgrading the warlord: new levels allow us to use new edicts or to empower the defences in that warlord's territory: the latter is particularly useful because warlords are normally very easy targets, so making them build small fortresses can be beneficial. While the mechanic seems great and is useful in longer games, warlords have one big problem: they get boring after a few hours. This is because our control over them is limited to the pressing of one of five buttons (the edicts) every few minutes, making the incredibly passive throughout a match. They also require attentions that shouldn't be needed: if an attack leaves their castle walls damaged, you will have to emanate an edict telling the warlord to repair them, something that the AI could've done automatically after the attack.Stronghold titles are definitely not known for the incredible strategy of their respective AIs, thus I really was hoping to see some improvements on this aspect in Warlords. And oh boy, was I let down. Stronghold: Warlords has probably the same AI that could be found in Stronghold: Legends 11 years ago. Maybe its code is not the same, but it suffers from the same problems. Storytime: I start a game and find myself against Genghis Khan, the only thing standing between me and him is a lonely Warlord tower, the only one on the map. The AI starts the game very aggressively, trying to capture said tower, but during the fight my soldiers attack: the result is that the AI attackers are wiped away and I get the warlord under my control. The early to mid game proceeds normally, with resource gathering and some skirmishes caused by the AI attacking with a fixed amount of horse archers every time. This is the point when the AI stops playing, basically: I have control over the only choke point that allows the AI soldiers to leave its fortress, so I just spam archers to keep control over the warlord tower. This is until I started producing trebuchets.Trebuchets, like in the previous Strongholds, have a crazy long range, but cannot move, which makes them vulnerable to attacks by the enemy army. Anyway, my trebuchets start raining down boulders on the AI's houses and wood camps, destroying them all. To my great surprise, my enemy keeps using the same strategy of the last 15 minutes: produce 10-15 horse archers and send them my way. Rinse and repeat. Against my army of now 40+ archers. The rest of the game is basically trebuchets raining death from afar, while the only actions the AI takes is instantly rebuilding the destroyed structures, a "strategy" that in around 10 minutes leaves it with no resources, no army and a free coupon for my victory. While rocks fall from the sky, Genghis Khan sends me a message, mocking me about the fact that "apparently I can destroy some buildings". Well, jokes on you, Genghis Khan.While graphics are ok-ish, considering the RTS nature of the game, I was expecting a way more polished experience from the game. The title, like its predecessors, still suffers from pathfinding issues and very often units can get stuck in corners. Other annoying aspects of the game include, but are not limited to, archers getting stuck in towers, making them untargetable (while they can keep shooting arrows), warriors that randomly start chasing the enemy when you told them to target a specific one, a sadistic way of controlling your army that will often make your archers attack in melee the enemy warlord. Plus, the lack of a "move and attack" action is inexcusable in 2021.Another bad title for the series, Stronghold: Warlords fails to innovate, basically resulting in a reskin of the previous games with a bunch of additional features added. The game is so similar to the previous titles in the series that I felt right at home, but having literally the same mechanics of games that are more than a decade old is a clear sign of failure to get the Stronghold brand to new heights. Are the updated graphics and the new warlord mechanic worth the 30€ price point? Absolutely not.

_childDocuments_.review: ▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬FireFly Studios has found its audience throughout its long-running history of the beloved castle-building simulator. Early entries enjoyed both commercial and critical success but in the past decade, they took too many wrong turns.  is no exception. It may hold up better than Stronghold 3 or Crusader II ever could, but in the flesh, there are some caveats that seriously hurt it. This time around,  dumps the European medieval to focus on East Asian civilizations. With around 1800 years of history to cover, choose from the Japanese, Mongol, Chinese, or Vietnamese lords and guide them in their conquests.▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬The choice of setting is a breath of fresh air for the series, as the previous games were mostly focused on medieval European architecture and culture. It is commendable that the developers chose to tackle a less familiar historical area for the series. The campaigns are laid out through a rather long period of Asian history, including the empires mentioned in the beginning. Each has its own respective campaign that progressively familiarizes players with different aspects of ....if it wasn't stifled by most things dated about it. All the flaws I'm about to break down might sound like minute issues that are bordering on nitpicking, but they eventually pile up and dull the whole experience. The bread and butter of the game is about laying siege to opponents while managing your own castle and the general wellbeing of its population. Building and defending castles are still a thrill after years of playing different s.The Chinese invention of gunpowder prepared the grounds for an exciting new era of weaponry in the  series.  Aside from regular troops and siege equipment of the era, players are now able to produce gunpowder-based weaponry to blow enemies sky-high. One look at the new explosive units is all it takes to fall in love with them. On a related note, troops now have body collisions. Players can now use this feature to actually put up a fight on walls or create chokepoints without letting enemies through.Firefly claimed AI has been greatly improved in several videos showcasing the new dynamic systems before release. Now that I've got a good grasp of it, I must say that AI is serviceable, but the improvements are not a big leap forward. It takes into account the map settings and space it is situated in, building based on that. Also, they interact with the new Warlords' system based on their needs. It all sounds fairly exciting; however, the AI still relies on spamming buildings and aggressively marching their troops toward the enemy castles from the get-go (or once the peace treaty is over).Another annoyance is their pathfinding. Units might zigzag through a straight, obstacle-free path for no reason. Or take a few steps back and continue down the way they were already going. This not only slows their movement down but is also troublesome during sensitive battles. Imagine that arrows are raining down on your painfully slow samurai, and they decide to boogie dance meanwhile.Unit formations still serve no purpose, the disband option has been removed, the feature to train units in bulk is taken away, castle building lost some of its elements and is slightly simplified. However, the series isn't making a return empty-handed. The new titular Warlords' system adds depth to just taking over estates. Players can demand a warlord's obedience by force or work out a peaceful solution using diplomacy points earned from consulates or embassies. Each warlord under the player's influence is still controlled by AI yet they offer a unique perk, as well as a set of edicts ready to be issued using the points. They are able to send in resources along with military troops if you invest enough points in upgrading them. Overall, this new system is advantageous to turn the tides of the war in your favor.At a glance, the art direction is befitting the new setting, albeit oversaturated. The castle life is as vibrant and full of energy as ever. Lots of effort is put into making distinct animations for each type of unit and peasant, even though they are as stiff as they were in the previous entries, if not degraded from the modern gaming perspective. It'll probably age even worse than the older titles. Grass pops out when fully zoomed out, textures are flat and look blurry here and there (castle walls and buildings look sharper). For what it's worth, it needs a serious shake-up.Where's that goofy yet delightful voice acting we had the pleasure to hear in early s? Now, it is as stereotypical as it gets. The Asian/English accent feels forced and faked. I'm sure a few natives could've done a better job. On another note, the Asian-tinged musical score is neither awful nor great; it sits right in the middle. I'm no expert in the field, but the fusion of Chinese/Japanese folklore, throat singing, and modern instruments stick out in the mind.▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬All in all,  is a coin toss at best. If you're a build-and-fight strategy enthusiast who doesn't care much about technical quality, the old and simple gameplay loop might entertain you, but not for long. But if you, like me, dislike the poor alterations this franchise had undergone in the past decade, the $30 price tag isn't justified for the content available at launch nor the technical quality it provides.▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: When it comes to RTS games, I prefer to play the skirmish modes over campaign or online multiplayer.Like many fans, I grew up playing and fell in love with the original Stronghold and Stronghold Crusader, but could not stand any of the games that followed because of their 3D graphics and attempts to totally reinvent the wheel. I really wanted a sequel that would simply feel and play like the originals, but add lots of new or fresh content. Stronghold Warlords plays a lot like the originals and adds a lot of new and fresh content -- I was able to jump right in and pick it up. The 3D graphics didn't bother me as much as previous titles. I also give credit to the quality of life improvements (For example: autosell at the market or resource summary in the HUD). However, this game just does not have that "feel" of the originals. It's difficult to find words to describe why...maybe its oversimplified? Or lacking that extra touch?Warlords were cool (reminds me of city-states from CIV 6)...but after 2 straight hours hearing "I serve a new master" every 15-30 seconds I developed mixed feelings about them. I've seen people complaining about the flipping ninjas, but they're actually my favorite unit lolMy laptop runs the game fine with occasional slow-downs on ultra settings (i7-6700HQ @ 2.60GHz, 2601 Mhz, 16.0 GB RAM, GTX 1070, 2TB SSD). I had no major bugs or crashes, but for some reason my ally AI kept sending me messages freaking out about the enemy even though he was the greatest lord and he wasn't even under attack.Overall, this is not a bad game -- nor is it a great game. My first play thru I absolutely hated it. I stopped, waited, then tried again. My second play thru I kind of liked it. I think I'll hold onto this and see what updates/developments/mods come down the pipeline. Honestly, I do not foresee endless addicted hours of replay value like with the originals, but I could see myself spending at least 10-15 hours trying everything out. (Feel free to write off all of my opinions as comparing sequels to originals in reviews is a controversial practice).

_childDocuments_.review: After testing this game for a short while, i can tell you to not get this game for the prize it is placed at(~30$). This game looks a little better than older entries in the Stronghold franchise, while the new setting is a great breath of fresh air, but this game ultimately fails to redeem itself as a new game. It appeals half-baked at many occasions and it lacks in content if you compare it with older Stronghold titles. You can tell that the game was dished out when the game was playable, not when it was done. It is extremely overprized since many of the older Stronghold titles cost 10 bucks in a  hard-copy collection all together, while this one made a step down from their standards in almost every regard except its visuals. It feels this game didn't evolve from what we already had access too, while still demanding a good sum of money for it.Noone can tell me that this is the product of what happened in 6-7 years of silence for this franchise. The developers did not go with current industry standards and left a unit-cap so ridiculous, that you can only recruit 100 units at the same time. Only having a 100-150 Units menas that you can not attack and defend at the same time. Your Enemy will have the same amount of units in a defensive position, while your base is open to any attacks by another person. Your offense has to be an "all in" attack, since otherwise you will be outnumbered and in a bad position, so good luck surviving even the smallest raid at your base. The few maps that are in the game are designed poorly and the NPC-Lords which had so much character in older titles are blank now. There are no quick-communication buttons anymore and all units look and play same-ish. However, it keeps the old castle building fanatsy and with this new "skin" it has some unique aspects. There are positives. I think people who never played Stronghold before might find this charming, this game is not bad at all, it is just not as good as other titles. They added an overview for how much of a resource you produce vs how much you use it and they incresed the complexity of housing/population happiness, It really needs an increased unit cap, more NPC-Lords and bigger maps, everything else can't really be adjusted by now. I don't think that the developers will change productions or the unit design anymore.The new neutral Warlords are especially disturbing. They can be conquered by force or by diplomacy, which is great, but they tend to occupy so much space on the map, that your own castle/town has barely enough place to be built. You can not build on the territory of your Warlords, while they only need a small amount of space for their buildings anyway. In the current state of their implementation i prefer playing maps with none of them. I dislike the system of "hard" borders anyway, why can't we "claim" land to get access to new recources or strategical positions, especially when that worked so well in the past? Warlords are more frustrating than exciting once you get an idea of how they work. I can respect the devs for trying this though. It was an attempt at something new and it just did not work. I must say i enjoy playing this game to a certain degree, but i can not enjoy it for too long, since i always remember i played a better stronghold for years now - for less money.I recommend a few changes to make this game worthwhile:- increase army/population cap, maybe even remove them/make them optional- allow players to build on territory of owned warlords, maybe by having them on rank 6 and purchasing an expensive permanent ownership- add at least 2 NPC/AI lords in the near future, maybe a really defensive one and one that is highly diplomatic and stresses you by using the warlordsWhen giving a review i always hate the fact that i can only select "yes" or "no", since i'd love to give this game a 6/10 which could be easily improved to a 8/10, but Steam asks me if i recommend it....so my answer has to be NO, but....Ultimately it is up to you and how much you are willing to spend on this product. If you care for graphics, then this game is more likely to satisfy your needs, but if you want the better gameplay, then you should probably get one of the older entries in the Stronghold franchise.PS:Okay, i spent another 3 hours to finish the first of 5 campaigns, consisting of 6 missions. Those are the most lifeless singleplayer missions i have encountered in any stronghold game. Roughly 6 lines of story/lore within 3 hours of play, while i got the enemy wiped from the map before the mission even wants me to do that. By now i am convinced that this game can only be described as unfinished, which is sad, because there is something to be made out of this.... We really need to hope for content-updates. I also researched a little more on this game and was surprised to read that only 10 people are developing this game. The game is surprisingly good for a team at that size and they even spoke of increasing the unit-capacity in the future. They want to add maps and improve the AI. Although they did not talk about changes to Warlords or territory/build space yet, this made me believe in the future of the game. I will keep my eyes on the game and might update this review in the future.Update: They actually increased the unit-capacity. By about 10-20%... Not nearly enough. You still cant capitalize on a better economy and you still need to leave your base open for attacks. Maps are still generaly bad and the AI does not deliver any challenge. In a Q&A they also explained that a good amount of missing things are tied to the games engine, making this game not redeemable in my eyes. It hurts to admit it, but i don't think this game can be redeemed anymore. I wish the developer would simply abandon this game and work on a follow-up Stronghold game.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the campaign, I have several mixed thoughts.Did I enjoy playing this game? Sure. Is it a good game? Probably not.As someone who has fond memories of playing stronghold with my uncle when I was 13, I will probably always play any new stronghold game and enjoy it due to the nostalgia. However, despite the excitement of a new stronghold game and an Asian-themed spin on things, this game really failed to take a step forward or develop new features; nothing has changed since Stronghold 2 which came out like fifteen years ago. This literally feels like a game that could have been released in 2005.ProsAsian theme/spin on stronghold is coolBeing able to create paths is cool, and it seems like they're going to further update cosmetic enhancements and customizations for your castle which is coolAlthough it would have been cool to see some change or to see things get bigger and better, the same old stronghold mechanics are goodConsThe UI is outdated and needs a lot of improvementYou can't zoom out very far at all in game, the field of view is extremely limitedThey should have made separate Chinese/Japanese/Mongolian etc. factions instead of having everything and troops be the same for allThe overall scale of the game feels small. They should have gone bigger and better, let you have more troops on the map at once, and had more space for castles.Holy f*** is the game glitchy. They're doing regular patches which are much needed, and if they weren't doing those patches I'd be pissed, but there should have been a lot more testing beforehand. The fact that this game isn't a full $60 title also makes this more acceptable though.Would I recommend this game? For most people, probably not. I enjoyed the game I guess but it's also hard to gauge because like I said, my nostalgia factor. If you've never played stronghold before, don't bother. If you have played before and are thinking about buying this new title, I would wait until it goes on sale because you aren't missing much now and hopefully they'll have a lot of updates to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Dont let the sweats fool you, this is actually a good game and not Stronghold 3 reskinned. It doesn't have the charm that the older strong hold games had with its voice acting and soundtrack, but it is at its core a stronghold game. Currently working my way through the campaigns and the only thing that bugs me is just not knowing what campaigns I have to do in order to unlock the others. Other than that this game is great and introduces other ways to sway public opinion like temples, clothing, and tea of all things. The warlords mechanic is actually very interesting and gives you a reason to go out and control other parts of the map during campaigns instead of just turtling up until you have a huge army then steam rolling the AI. Essentially the warlords are mini keeps that control parts of the map and each type has a different function. Some give you food or resources like the pig, mouse, and ox, others like the tiger give you the ability to launch AI controlled raids on specific estates with reasonably high level units. Other than that they had a champion and need to be defended because the enemy can steal them from you with influence or by beating the warlord. IMO it just makes for a more engaging and dynamic experience, to the point where there are some campaign missions that have your economy completely supported by the warlords you control and you have to spread your army out to control x amount to win the mission. I don't really understand the people saying there aren't that many unit types when there are more than previous Stronghold games, maybe they haven't played around in free build or they did the first campaign which is very limited? Other than that I think they've got a good range that includes early gunpowder units which are interesting. Anyway the game is beautiful, plays well, explores a part of history that hasn't been touched on before by the series, and returns to the roots of the Stronghold experience while introducing new and innovative mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the many bad reviews for this game, I bought it anyway...determined to see for myself if they were true. I must unfortunately report...they are. This is not a game made for 2021. Almost nothing about it lives up to any kind of standard for the age. Be warned if you came here for multiplayer. They did not add any kind of quick-play option, where you just join whatever game that is nearly full. Instead, you must select a single game from the list of available games and then you have to wait  for it to fill up, which could be a long wait since each different game in the lobby is competing for the same pool of noobs. I just checked the multiplayer lobby on a perfectly normal evening...there were a grand total of eight games listed and all of them were locked to outside players. At least two of them were in German.As for the game itself, most fans were not expecting an excellent game...just a decent trip down memory lane. I think the developers had this exact same perspective. This was never some passion project about making a great game with lots of technical advances. I just saw on Steam that one of the old Crusaders games (Crusaders 2 released in 2014) is for sale at the exact same price as Warlords. Let that tell you everything you need to know about the new release. Warlords is a so-so re-skin of the same old same old from a million years ago. If you can handle that, it might offer a few hours of fun.As an example of the bugs and poor design decisions you will encounter: Scenarios where lowlands flood. If you have woodcutters collecting bamboo from the lowlands, they will all keep marching into the flood and drown, only to respawn, and march right back into the flood to drown again.Tigers march straight through the middle of your village...killing no-one. Woodworkers do not attack the tiger. All the tiger does is lower morale.There is almost no difference between the lowliest peasant hovel and the grandest estate in the kingdom...certainly not size. Six different house options from dirt poor to fabulously wealthy...all are exactly the same size, and general look. The models for the rich houses look just awful...barely different from the low-end shack with zero grandeur.Scenarios where they purposely give you almost no military units to defend yourself, depending on warnings from your "squire" to alert you to an impending attack so you can get ready. The only problem...warnings fail  to trigger and you only find out you are being attacked by a massive army when you see it inside your city tearing everything apart. Good luck defending with your 10 whole archers, no walls, and zero ability to respond. How many times in a row can this happen? I quit before I found out.That water is just bad. Worst part...they re-use the image of their bad water to top off your water pots as well...so it's the exact same crappy water material in the rivers and lakes as is in your water pots...waves and all. I guess the screams from guys you burn with fire was just too scary. Now they just turn black, gyrate around silently, and fall over like mimes. Stronghold used to have some guts.The water pots are ridiculous!!! Dudes will stand right next to a burning building doing nothing. Guys from half-way across the map will come over, but the ones right next to the fire will do nothing. Over and over, you'll watch your water pot guys do absolutely nothing while the city burns around them.The Warlord thing is, by no means, some impressive new, game-changing mechanic. It's just some dudes you can kill easily who pay some dumb tribute. Worse yet, it just distracts from the fun of combat when you have to constantly out-diplomacy the other players to control the warlords. More annoying than anything. By the end of the game, you are just spamming diplomacy points while the other player does the same, and control of the warlords flips and flops between you as one gains the upper hand for a few minutes. Another bad idea? The warlords are mandatory. You cannot opt to leave them out and just play Stronghold. You can choose the warlords you have, and you can select to have random warlords, but you cannot select to have no warlords or limited warlords. All warlords all the time...like it or not.What is the point of Skirmish mode? Once you figure out that all you have to do is build a couple of diplomacy buildings at the start of the game...you will then dominate every single match afterward. AI opponents do not build these until later, so you just auto-dominate the entire map and clean house with no effort at all.The number of maps for skirmishes is ridiculously small. These are not works of art here. They are not complicated, with lots of terrain features. Why not give us some more variety? I assume the same holds true for multiplayer. Really disappointing to anyone who came for skirmish/multiplayer rather than the so-so campaign. There is just nothing to get excited about in the handful of rather basic maps we were given in the full release of the game. Really sub-standard for a new release in 2021.The unit caps are absurdly small. I think they used up all their computing power with those dumb warlords...leaving nothing left for the actual players.As many have said before, you would be better off getting one off the better, much older versions of Stronghold. Warlords just ate my money and made me mad.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold: Warlords is a solid entry to the stronghold series. It adds to the game series by including some new things such as gunpowder and Tea to replace pitch and Ale, the former also providing some very interesting units and interactions such as Cannons that are great fun and being able to load bombs into trebuches. It also introduces its namesake, the warlords system. Which feels like a modernisation of the old estate system from Stronghold too and helps add some variety to play and interesting ways to interact with the map.Firefly have nailed the pace and control of castle building, feels more like the older renditions of the game, this is especially in part to using a grid system for the placement of buildings and walls..If you are looking for an update on the older games and the chance to explore a different geography and theater of the middle ages (One that i feel doesn't get enough attention) then this is a good choice. If you are looking for more stronghold crusader, then go play more stronghold crusader, you wont find the exact same game here.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually one of the worst RTS i have ever played.I am a long time fan of the stronghold franchise, but my goodness this is terrible.it's so evident that this game has had VERY little thought into the player experience.  here is some of the reasons why i think this.1.) Very poor AI pathfinding.it's SO frustrating. i have had guys decided to circle the circumference of the enemy's walls rather than cross a courtyard and up some stairs to go up a tower. Or have a melee infantry be told to attack an enemy destroying my walls go out my gates, go halfway to my enemy, then turn back around and go back inside and then stand on the walls and stare at the enemy pick-axing my walls to rubble.2.) Nonsensical number values.for example, a spearman  unit does 1 attack in melee and he has 3000 health! so logically it would take 3000 hits for him to kill another spearman. Or better yet a blowdart infantry has 0 melee attack (fair enough he is a range attacker) and 0 Range attack!wtf? Firefly why would you just pick arbitrary numbers FFS!? 3.) idiotic unit controlsyou can't put any range unit on any other stance other than stand ground. if they are shot at by an enemy that is out of range for them (such as another archer in a tower) they will stand there and die because of this. they wont be able to be in a defensive stance, get shot at, then move closer to shoot back. Not can you do an attack move with any unit. you have an "attack here" button but no "move to this place and attack enemies along the way" button. 4.) TERRIBLE quality artwork. I mean even in the main menu the art is pixely and aliased. it looks like the artwork is 360p, and the textures used for the characters in game are 114p, and my settings are for Ultra. And the 3D mini video portaits that play when an even happens is about the same quality as in 2001. Legit there's better art across the board in the original age of mythology.5.) Laziness over charm.Gone are the days of charming little animations or artwork when you click on a building. Gone is the loveable advisor holding open your log book. _childDocuments_.review: Okay so, I have been a long time fan of Stronghold since Stronghold Crusader. I liked RTS games akin to Red Alert 2 and C&C Generals. My main interest to this genre is the base building aspect of RTS and the Stronghold series is the definition of that. To their credit, this entry might be the best that Firefly can offer in technicality. Graphics looks perfectly fine, great balance of style and quality. So far I've seen a few bugs but nothing game breaking. And the gameplay itself feels smooth, whether it is the performance or the flow of the game, gathering materials, training soldiers, and sieging the enemy feels good. However, there's some problems in the game that I think needs attention in the near future. I will list out all the problems below that in my opinion needs to be addressed soon.1. Warlord Diplomacy SystemThis is a nice change of pace for empty areas in the map. You get the option to capture them by essentially "talking" to them rather than just murdering them repeatedly. They also have great advantages when captured. However, how it stands right now is that you have to essentially monitor them every 10 seconds to make sure they won't leave and betray you, because the enemy can also capture them with diplomacy. And it's a glaring problem for CPU enemies since they can automatically spam capture if their diplomacy points are enough. But don't get me wrong, this concept is great but flawed in execution. I think it lacks on notifications for your warlords. For example, the scribe and the chat box should tell me that one of my captured warlord is being captured by the enemy through diplomacy, so then I can prevent the capture so that the warlord won't be lost. The current state of warlords' notification is that there is a heartbeat sound when some warlord can be captured through diplomacy, while the sentiment of notification is there, the notification itself is not clear enough. One of my other suggestion with capturing is probably we should spend a significant amount of diplomacy points on pressing the capture warlord button, since it feels like capturing warlords have no cost whatsoever especially when we have built our embassies. Speaking of embassies, diplomacy point is useless in the long run, it'll just pile up to ten thousands while I only need hundreds. I guess to counteract this I'm suggesting to have an option for our warlords to make gathering sites so there's a remote industry for needed materials, just like in older titles like I think in Stronghold 2 you can build gathering sites and then send them to our keep. Well, there's already that through the Warlords menu but what I'm saying is to request specific gathering sites to be built and then gathered by them to be sent to our keep.2. Lack of Content (as of now)I personally don't know the roadmap for this game, I'm sure Firefly wants the best of this game and so do I. So let me list out what I mean by "Lack of Content".Lack of Character Based AISo far I think you can classify the enemy AI to Tribal, China, Mongol, and Japan. Only two of them have 2 different leaders and their playstyle isn't very diverse in a way. What I want with this is character within the AI, somewhat like the animal AI in Stronghold Crusader, the Rat, the Snake, the Pig, and the Wolf. These AI are great because the somewhat have their identity in their playstyle, whether the Rat have small castles and their troops are weak, or the Pig that excels in producing leather armor and have troops like maceman and crossbowman. I think you got my point here. The only noticeable difference in Stronghold Warlords is that Hideyoshi utilizes the Military Academy units, the Mongols uses Horses and that's it probably. Maybe add another AI that follows Oda Nobunaga, where he excels at gunpowder arsenal and add a musketeer unit to complement him. Or heck just copying the formula of the Crusader's animal AI in Asian form would be a huge improvement. Imagine fighting Warlords equivalent of the Wolf, the Dragon. That would be sick.Lack of Skirmish TrailI think this is self explanatory, I hope there's more to Skirmish Trails, somewhat like Crusaders 2 where there are multiple "chapters" of the trails. Glad the chicken is back tho.Lack of Skirmish MapsAnd I think this is the reason why the previous problem happens. There's a very small pool of official skirmish maps available. Some standard RTS map designs are missing as well in this game and I think this needs attention real fast, cause this problem makes the game feel very dry. I often find myself confused on picking the maps when trying a custom skirmish and since there's not enough variety I often just stopped playing.Lack of CustomizationI think this is a big problem for someone like me who expects to fully become a Japanese in this game and apparently in I can't be Japanese in Skirmish Trails. I am defaulted to be Chinese with the same skin as always. I hope there's a customization option where I can customize my Lord and my Keep outside of custom skirmish. Speaking of Keeps, keeps should be customizable, and there's no Japan themed Keeps available. The Japanese Keep is defaulted to Chinese Keep which feels lacking. I was hoping for a big option menu in the settings that lets me choose which faction I want to play as. I've played through the Japan campagin as well, their soldiers speak Japanese and this baffles me why is this not a customization option. Cause it wouldn't also work in Custom Skirmish while picking Hideyoshi as my Lord, the soldiers are still Chinese in the Custom Skirmish, they're only Japanese in the Campaign.So yeah all in all, I would still recommend this game for those who wants a great RTS experience. The game runs very well in terms of technicality but is hindered by lack of content and the aforementioned Warlord Diplomacy System for now. I hope Firefly would add new stuffs to the game to make the game as fresh as possible. I wish all the best for this game and your future games as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first real review so I'm just gonna rant with zero direction.Alright, before I say anything, I'll just flat out rate it. Its a solid 6.5/10. I just finished the first campaign and I gotta say, the voice acting is just as good as any other Stronghold game. Spoilers for the first campaign without saying any names: The kingdom loses in the end cutscene after defending a fortress, you can kill ever single enemy without losing a single unit, but you'll still "lose". I don't like this. If the end of the campaign is a lose, choose a different story to tell. The Warlord system thing is kind of cool, but I will say there is hardly any innovation. There is no conscripts that are literally just cannon fodder. There are 2 units called tribesmen and blow-dart tribesmen. This is fine, but the models don't really show much how they are literally just an angry mob. They have shields and spears. This would be fine if they needed equipment to train but they don't. In Stronghold 2 there were literally just a guy with what looked like a farmers trident lookin thing. That's not a big complaint tho. A big one I would have is the lack of innovation in new features. Why didn't they add like a more in-depth happiness system like short term happiness. Balance issues with archers have always been a problem with stronghold games and they added the arrow fire cart to fix it, but damn can that thing still get absolutely shredded by archers on a tower. The graphics are also kind of a downside of the game. They aren't really modern I would say. It looks like it came out two years after Stronghold 3. That's never really a thing I care about, but if a game is coming out in 2021, it should look somewhat better. Like the textures on the ground underneath cut down trees aren't models, its just a flat texture. Another thing that isn't awesome is that you can't zoom really too much. Something I loved from Stronghold 2 is that you could see what the people in workshops were doing. You could literally see the baker take the bread out of the oven. Now you can only guess because there are two zoom settings. This game doesn't truly seem like it is a game out in 2021, more like 2016 or 17. Its not a bad game, just seems really like a reskin. If you like the old stronghold games like I do, go right ahead and play the game, you'll enjoy it, but this won't rekindle any childhood wonder for the Stronghold series.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold: Doesn't Function Properly EditionNormally I wouldn't leave a negative review for something like a technical problem, but anyone who's playing Stronghold in 2021 is probably doing so for nostalgia, so this review is meant for you.. . .Being a Stronghold fan is kindof like thinking about your first serious girlfriend. You still feel the heartache a stupid amount of years later, even though you're both way different people now. The difference is, Stronghold Crusader never gets married to force you to move on, and every Stronghold game after is just a *little* bit more disappointing than the last. The point is, this is were I think I'm fully done with the series. I was on the fence about this game because of the reviews (and lets be honest, because of the newer games in the series), and I now realize it's probably just time to find new RTS series to settle down with. Cons:Wouldn't start properly (in a playable form) for me after the first time it launched. Pros: I'm now irritated enough that I feel like I can move on with closure. I have to spend my gaming time this week waiting for my Steam refund as lesson not to buy games with "mixed" reviews on Steam. Older and wiser.  Conclusion:Buy the game when it's on sale in five years. Nostalgia doesn't make up for a game that doesn't work, and besides the most hardcore of us SH fanboys, I think we can all admit this series has been floundering for over a decade. Whatever this game is- IF you can get it to launch properly- I'd bet forty-one dollars it's not worth forty dollars.Buy a copy of your favorite Stronghold game, bury it outback, and have a shot of whiskey. The series is dead, boys.

_childDocuments_.review: I have bought this game only for campaigns but it's not fun at all. There are two types of campaigns: strategic and economic. Both sucks.In strategic type player has to kill opponent in every single mission. Meanwhile, the game is not focused on strategy aspects; units are clunky, there are like 5 types of units with basic AI and no special abilities. Units like these were ok in the first game, but in the first game building your stronghold was the main goal. Here the main goal is to kill your enemies. Your stronghold is somewhere here... sure, build something, whatever, but now the war is the most important. I cannot understand why developers did that. They want to compete with RTS games? If that's so, it's more fun to play a real RTS like Starcraft or Age of Empires, where units AI and battles works better.When I saw the economic campaign I thought that would be a game I wanted to play. But no, they had to add time limit in every mission, just to ruin the gameplay. So again, you cannot build your stronghold the way you want to. No. You have to hurry up! Missions are designed in a way that is forcing a specific build orders :D If you do not follow it and waste some resources on something - you will probably lose, cause you won't be able to gather some crap on time. Additionally, they added some scripted disasters like swine illness. For example: you are playing mission 3. Suddenly, in the middle of it, the swine illness happens and all your pigs just dies. Because of the time limit you can surrender now, cause there is no chance to recover on time. So now you have to start mission again and remember to not build pig farms. Also I saw some entertainment/scary constructions and decorations but didn't have time to waste resources on these so I didn't use any of it.What's wrong with the classic Stronghold? Why not just reuse gameplay style from the first game and only improve it?

_childDocuments_.review: For those of you who have fond memories of Stronghold 1 and 2 as well as Crusader, you'll most likely be disappointed in this one. Not as much as with Stronghold 3, but still disappointing.Pros -1. Asian setting, which means new things to explore. I always enjoyed watching my filthy peasants working in their station, complaining about taxes. But this is a double edged sword that i'll elaborate down below.2. Team Player VS Comps and etc. Multiplayer is an improved version of what you'd find in stronghold 2. But as of right now, there's some serious lag in multiplayer. Especially when playing big games, which is quite the concern.Neutral - 1. The new 'smaller factions?' thing where on a skirmish map, you have these small factions that dont build anything and you can take control over for benefits such as faster peasant working, or more horses, etc. I honestly found this to be a hindrance/nuisance especially in multiplayer. They border your uh... border, which causes your archers to constantly shoot at the. They also act as good buffers to chease the already incompetent AI (yes i played on hard).2. The new 'influence' system with buildings. Basically you build temples to increase work rate of production buildings, but they have a radius so you have to plan your workstations around them.3. The new 'pleasure and punishment' thing. Back in stronghold 2, you had stockades and such to punish thieves. Now its just a structure that either increases happiness but decreases work speed, or vice versa. Honestly, for me this should go in the cons.Cons -1. No more filthy criminal and punishment. Instead a lame min maxing system with pleasure/punishment buildings.2. Buildings roads to connect castle to embassy/temples to increase spirit or whatever, aside from that roads are useless.3. No wells. Really? I trebuched a fire pot into the enemy's castle where all the production stuff was, the AI was literally on the brink of extinction from the fire damage. You'd think from a game that has flame throwers as units, would have a simple well...4. Troop limit. You can make a small banner formation of men similar to that in cossack. The problem is unlike cossack where you can actually field multiple of those formations to actually look like a real fight, you can only make 2ish with a troop cap limit of 66. So yeah, barely any improvement on that end from previous strongholds.5. No engineers. So instead, go ahead and click the repair button and mass click all your damaged walls for more fun :)6. An asian orgy. So a lot of people have been wondering why, even though they play a Japanese lord, they're troops talk Chinese? You see, all lords are like a panda express big plate. You get some chinese orange chicken, some japanese teriyaki, and Thai? noodles, and Mongolian barbeque, and you get an asian big plate. That's what you're playing. Every lord is a mass combined orgy of all those nations, so basically there's nothing to differentiate them nor make them unique/special. I mean sure, stronghold 2 every lord had the same units. But you know, they were all pretty much the same medieval euro lord! Here you have friggin Ghenghis khan and Tokugawa having little to no difference at all!Honestly i'm at 2 hours on my Stronghold Warlords, and teetering between refunding or waiting it out to see some polish. It is more playable compared to stronghold 3, i'll give em that. But such a wasted oppurtunity to truely make a really damn good Stronghold title. Imagine A stronghold on a scale of like Supreme Commander! But no, we get a 36 buck game that kinda feels like a reskin/mod.
