_childDocuments_.review: Fun for new players. Missing features, dated look and feel, boring mission and map design along with poor optimisation hold it back especially for older fans of the game. Also the roadmap/dlc to me seems more like unfinished or withheld content. Pros - Warlords system is a good idea. Needs more work to make it an enjoyable and worthwhile feature. Especially in multiplayer. - Gunpowder units are very fun to use. - Roads: Small edition but nice for designing your castle. Again this could be improved upon.- Asian setting. It's a good aesthetic but again, can be improved. Separate factions would go a long way. Telling the stories within the missions as well as before and after could really get you into the leaders more.Cons - Campaign: Personally I prefer the older style story driven narratives. They weren't masterpieces but it kept you engaged. The history can still allow for this even if done in a different style but currently it's just not interesting. - Poor optimisation along with basic features any modern game should have. e.g ability to change key bindings. - Lack of game modes upon release. More are coming but I think it should have been there at launch.- No moats or wooden walls amongst many other features from previous titles.- No need for fertile land, it's useful more interesting map designs as resources are mini objectives to fight over.- Map Size, really just needs to be bigger. (heavily requested but still lacking somewhat??) In general maps are bland.- Overall aesthetic: This to me is less down to graphics but more the inconsistencies. The building designs look fairly good, but wall/terrain textures are lacking detail. - Mixing of Cultures: I think an opportunity was missed here to give the lords and warlords more of a unique identity. Unique castle, building and unit designs for each region could really add some diversity without changing the Stronghold formula too much. Also potentially an easy dlc option?Minor Things- Troop Count. This has since been increased but should still be higher and lack of foresight here.- Unit animations, some need more finesse. Improvements/Feedback- Troop slider limit in game. - More maps.- Cooler, unique castle/warlord/lord designs. From buildings to troops, just more diversity would add to the aesthetic.- Build upon the warlords system, Goods can physically travel across map when requested. Mini objective to fight over. The way you acquire control of warlords needs to be changed.- More identity to the lords and where they hail from when building their respective castles. - Add more silly castle defences. (rolling logs, stone tippers, boiling oil) - Terrain interaction. Rock slides, swampy land slowing troops, long grass for hiding light troops. Dynamic weather, seasons. Seasons can change the look of the maps trees, plants, grass, crops matching with the seasons? Weather effects: Rainy weather reduces archer effectiveness? Overall - 6/10 - Best of the "3D" styles. Good foundation and fun to introduce to some friends. BUT basic requests over the years are still lacking. Also just a lack of innovation. Yes the stronghold formula works, but I think the last attempt at changing things up was Legends. (Underrated game) A change of setting is a start but gameplay changes along with modernisation is needed. _childDocuments_.review: THIS IS A COPY OF A PREVIOUS REVIEW, WHICH I AGREE ON!  HOPE THE DEVELOPERS WILL READ AND MAKE AN UPDATE IN ORDER TO MAKE THE GAME PERFECT!As someone who was a huge fan of Stronghold and Stronghold 2, I was either lukewarm or disliked all the subsequent entries. I believed the hype from Firefly that Warlords would be a true successor to Stronghold 2, but unfortunately it just isn't the case.Pros:+ The graphics are a nice bump over Stronghold 2 (but so they should be!)+ Combat mechanics are fun and satisfying+ There is a fair variety of unit types including horse archers, crossbowmen, 'Generals' etc.+ Difficulty options (Easy, Medium, Hard) for enemy AI is a very welcome addition+ The game excels when you're playing a siege, either in defense or attack.Cons:- Limited number of units that you can produce!- The economic aspects of the game feel hugely dumbed down compared to Stronghold 2. There is no gong, no rats, no crime. The added diplomacy and spirit systems are shallow and uninteresting, it feels like a band-aid solution to try to flesh out the game in the absence of proper game systems.- The warlords system is fundamentally flawed, and in skirmish mode it actively detracts from gameplay when compared with the old estates system. You cannot control the warlords in any sense, can't build on their land, and can only give them orders through extremely restricted 'edicts'. Enemy AI constantly takes over your warlords via diplomacy points, meaning you need to monitor sub-menus within sub-menus every minute in order to keep control of them. Since you can't build on warlords' land, it's no longer possible to build industries away from your castle, and the cart-to-transport-goods-between-estates functionality is completely missing as a consequence.- The honour system is completely absent, meaning no lord's kitchen, no lady's bedchambers, no jousting, no festivals. The Lord does not have feasts or dances, doesn't attend church or jousts, he just stands on the castle unless you use him for combat.- Some basic bugs or design flaws from the original games are still present, such as the fact that the oxen used to transport iron & stone are interchangeable, meaning they will travel across your entire castle to pick up the wrong type of resource. Firefly simply haven't listened to much of the feedback they've had since the days of Stronghold 2 over a 16 years ago.- There are only 4 AI opponents in the whole game.- There is little to no variation between the AI opponents/factions - most units are identical, most buildings are identical, despite the fact that the 4 warlords cover four completely separate cultures (Chinese, Mongol, Japanese and Vietnamese). This makes the game feel very cookie-cutter and unvaried, and really damages the replayability of the game. For an example of just how much of an impact it can have to provide varied unit types per faction, see Lord of the Rings Battle For Middle Earth 1 & 2, which were released over 15 years ago and still hold up today.- The largest map sizes are still very small, adding to the impression that Firefly are not pushing any boundaries when it comes to technical capability or innovation. Yes, they are a small studio, but games like Stardew Valley were developed by one guy in his bedroom and have hundreds of hours more content and more complexity than this game does.Overall, I regret buying the game, and I wouldn't even recommend it at half price. The game can provide 10-15 hours of distraction, for that I'd wait for 75% off at the minimum. Firefly are stuck in the past and haven't listened to feedback. The key selling point of this game - the warlords system - simply doesn't work, and the economic aspects of gameplay which made Stronghold 2 so replayable are dumbed down so much they feel absent.

_childDocuments_.review: It is amazing how similar the Stronghold-Series has developed like society in recent years. After centuries of progress we reached the pinnacle in 2005 (with Stronghold 2) and since then things just took the wrong turn. Stronghold 3 was already a failure although it kept some of the things that made the Series so great. You could see your Castle grow, see the vivid daily life of your subjects and then march to war with hundreds of soldiers. Stronghold Warlords manages to put that whole thing onto a new level. A ♥♥♥♥ one though. Just after opening the game you will be immediately greeted with probably one of the worst User Interfaces you will ever see. An almost pitch-black background that spits out bright white rectangels to give you usually irrelevant information. What on earth is wrong with natural colors like brown or whatever? The entire thing is at the bottom, completely overloading that part of your screen with informations. The Voice-Actress that narrates the story tries to imitate a british accent while not beeing able to get rid of her asian accent. (Or the other way around). Her voice doesn´t fit to the setting at all and she is clearly not the best at what she does.The Semi-realistic graphics of Stronghold 2 and 3 have now been exchanged with poorly done cartoon-like designs that are nowhere near what you would expect in 2021. The entire thing is just cheep and lazy. As you can see at the in-game flora. They designed a single! bush, a single! bamboo tree and a single! palm tree which they just spam onto the map. Even though they changed the size of some of them it just looks extremely bad and lazy. The water in the rivers now flows freely over the map, ignoring such out-fashioned constraints as the streambed and solid mountains. The units look even worse than those in the original Stronghold. Or at least you can not be sure, since they changed the zoom-setting so you can no longer look very closely at your units and your town. Obviously to hide their lazy design. The maps probably are the smallest out of all the games in the series. Even though they changed the size of buildings to very small, you still have extremely condensed castles that just look very bad. Overall do  map-size, graphics and UI remind one of a mobile game and definitely not of a RTS-Game for PC. And this is just what is bad about the overall look of the game. The Gameplay itself honestly just feels like clash of clans. (Which you can get for free and not for 30 bucks.)The troop diversity is extremely low. And the amount of viable units is even lower. You can see that very fast in the first campaign, where you conquer Vietnam. This time the "revolution" (your main character keeps mentioning that) starts in South Vietnam leading up to the north. Very soon the Advisor will try to trick you into building modern units like archers and axeman. But you must not be fooled and fall for such imperialist weaponry. You will unleash the power of the Viet Cong and overrun your enemies with blowpipe tribesman, the only units in the game that can walk faster than a turtle. The enemy siege weapons can be easily outmaneuvered and destroyed with these cheap units as can all the other units. Especially the late game "Imperial Swordman" who are expensive as ♥♥♥♥ stand no chance against your pipe-armed rice farmers. The entire castle building aspect of the game was gotten rid of. Most maps are just to small to build a nice looking castle. The buildings are so small that your Small area on the SMALL map will soon like like a slum. Then the new warlord system. GEEZ IT IS SO BADLY DONE. In Stronghold 2 the estates consisted of a nice real looking village that send goods to you on a regular basis. The "Warlords" instead are dudes that sit on weird looking tower-like structures and build neither ressource buildings on the map nor castle walls. Instead they will summon either goods like wood or stone into your stockpile. No cart that goes from their village into your castle, no animation, nothing. That was definitely better in Stronghold 2. The tiger warlord will summon a handfull of troops out of thin air that will perish within seconds after stupidly running into enemy walls and archers. And the mouse warlord will just give you a buff. The entire system is so lazy and cheap, it´s incredible. This is just the pinnacle of what is wrong with the game. You could go on for hours.Buy Stronghold 2. It´s way better in every single regard. Don´t buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: To me, Stronghold Warlords is a decent sequel of the first Stronghold game, but it could have been (much) better. Pros:- The game is set in a new environment (far east Asia), with new buildings and new troops, however it would have been nice to see different castle structures (different walls and towers) for each of the four factions (Chinese, Japanese, Mongolians and Vietnamese), just as each had a different keep. - The Warlords were an interesting addition, but again, there aren't any real differences between them (except for the Turtle having strong walls for protection).- The soundtrack was great. - I loved the addition of gunpowder weapons. Cons:- The game has bugs unfortunately (game crashes, troops remaining stuck on walls), although they are not that often. - Some troops speak in the native language, while the Engineers speak in English. Why is that? - There should have been more food buildings available (not just rice fields, vegetables fields, tea plantations and pork farms). For example, why not fishermen or hunters too? Also, you can do well with only two of them (e.g. rice and tea), without needing to build the others. What I'm trying to say is that this part seems too simplified as compared to Stronghold 1&2. Also, the herbalist workshop doesn't really have a meaningful purpose in the game. Why build it?Overall, although it has its minuses, as a Stronghold fan, I enjoyed playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Needs more polish and maybe a bit more balancing, but all of the features that are new to Stronghold are fun and there's room for improvement and expansion. The warlord system is better implemented than I thought it would be (though only the military lords are worth investing in). Fewer bugs and glitches than Crusader 2 had on its launch.Still some issues with path-finding and clicks not registering. Would like to see more flavor, as having only four AI opponents feels kind of bare compared to earlier Stronghold games. Also, while there is a huge unit roster, the historical campaigns still play anachronistically. And while the new military features are complex and well-executed, the economic ones don't feel that improved. Promotional videos for this game talked about Wusselfaktor, but it feels like the castle-sim aspects take a backseat to the combat. One really easy fix I'd like to see is being able to zoom in more so you can appreciate the details on your buildings and peasants.I have hope that a lot of the problems will be ironed out. _childDocuments_.review: With all the experiences I've had with the game, I think it's really underrated compared to the exciting experiences it offers.As a game I played over 20 years ago, Stronghold Warlord still delivers the enjoyable experience of the series, with strengths in creating a city with various spaces including agriculture, craftsmanship, weapon production, residential areas, recreational areas, military camps, etc.In the comments, I see many complaints about the following issues:The wheat-flour-bread production chain being replaced by rice: I agree with that, but overall, the game compensates for it with other experiences like tea production, strawberry farming, silkworms, and clothing, etc.The meaninglessness of the lord system: Personally, I don't think it really improves the experience (but it doesn't make it worse either). You can choose to ignore it and play the way you have for the past 20 years.The weakness of AI: I completely agree with this opinion. If you can build a castle in the first 10 minutes, you'll definitely win. The AI is fast in sending armies to your castle early on but has no concept of development.You only need 5 samurai to capture a small lord's castle and 20 samurai to win the game. This makes the use of various weapons and unit coordination pointless. You can even play the game for 100 hours without ever producing a mace or a bow because swords and armor are the most powerful weapons in the game. If you evaluate the game solely on the movement and unit coordination mechanisms, the game is worth a 2/10 (if you consider Total War or Company of Heroes a 10).It will be suitable for those who like city-building and simulation games, observing the daily lives of their city's inhabitants from all angles. You will find a woman raising pigs in the fields, a young man drinking under the cherry blossom tree, a herbalist brewing medicine in a small alley, or children playing in the villages and along the walls - all the scenes of an East Asian city are wonderfully displayed (as a Vietnamese, I highly appreciate that).It won't be suitable for those who want an economic and military RTS game like Starcraft or Age of Empires. Honestly, with Starcraft or Age of Empires, we seek ways to optimize the economy, produce military forces as quickly as possible, and throw them into battle with special unit control skills, whereas with Stronghold, these aspects are not emphasized as much as the experiences of construction, architecture, and planning. Stronghold is more of a city-building and defense simulation game than a basic RTS game.Overall point: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a neutral review option. This isn't a terrible game, but 20 years after the release of the original, they still haven't come close to making anything as good as SH1/Crusader, and sadly this one, even though it's a better effort than most of their previous titles, doesn't change that.I really don't care too much about graphics in RTS games. This one looks like a decade old game and that's fine with me, however, it also runs very poorly on a good PC, so when there's not many units on screen and it's not pushing the envelope in terms of graphics, it's a mystery why it runs so incredibly poorly.In terms of gameplay it's fairly similar to the Strongholds before it, but with the introduction of the Warlords mechanic. These are small forts between you and your rival that you can conquer to get aid like extra troops or resource deliveries. It sounds interesting but in practice it kind of ruins what makes Stronghold different from other RTS games. Castle building is an afterthought now. Most of the fighting occurs around the warlord estates, so building armies is far more important than a well built castle.You can also capture them diplomatically, which again is a feature that sounds great, then quickly falls apart in practice. Recruiting warlords just consists of spending more diplomacy points than your rivals, so instead of an interesting mechanic, it's just looking at a window and clicking to make numbers go up. and hoping your opponent does it less.Another weird change in base construction is that you can no longer build anything outside your estate, including resource buildings and farms, so there's no reason to fight over territory, except for the warlord estates. It really removes a lot of what made Crusader fun, fighting over limited farmland. I don't understand the logic behind it at all, other than forcing you to rely on warlords.Finally the campaign. It's there. It's a bunch of random missions with some semblance of a story connecting them. Most of them are pretty forgettable, and some of the sieges are a bit tedious on the highest difficulties where the best strategy is using the fire at area feature of archers and catapults to safely but extremely inaccurately kill your enemies from outside their range of fire. For what it's worth the original Stronghold had the same issue, but it's unfortunate that two decades later they still haven't improved it.Overall it's a decent game plagued by performance issues and some weird game mechanics, but it's also the least focused on castle-building in a series that's defined by it. It's really hard to recommend when the originals are also on Steam if you want a castle building experience, and there are plenty of better options like the Age of Empires series if you want a more straightforward RTS.

_childDocuments_.review: The small team at Firefly have truly done some excellent work, especially considering how difficult the RTS genre is for smaller teams. They know what they are good at, though, and in my opinion they have created something special here. As with all of their titles, there is some genuine clunk, but it doesn't take away from the experience.The movement and unit control is much improved from previous games - although units do occasionally get stuck on things. Nowhere near to the level of something like Stronghold 3, but it happens.The campaigns are enjoyable and do a great job of creating an engaging tutorial for the game, and they actually do something very clever with it. Not only do they show you how to play the game in general, adding mechanics as you go, but they also teach you how the AI enemies play and give you some insight into their strengths and weaknesses. Love this!Many people are upset that there are only 4 AI, but I find this confusing. The first Stronghold only had 4 AI and they were not as different as they are in Warlords. There is no "Rat = Easy, Wolf = Hard" anymore. Now all the AI can be easier or harder depending on your play style and have different challenges in early, middle, and end game. Very smooth. I hope they continue to add AI lords as they have done with previous games, since clearly they have a better idea of how to make them play differently.One thing that is lacking in this installment, is the overacted charm of most of the previous titles. While all of the games have been based in history, this is their first try at going a bit more serious with the setting, and I don't think it served them as well as they hoped. While the gameplay still has the wacky, over the top units that cause all sorts of mayhem (even more so with gunpowder), the voiced lines of units and enemy AI is just not as humorous and fun as previous characters. I don't think they've really had that level of character since the first title, though. That said, none of that really takes away from the actual gameplay too much.I know many people are still nostalgic for the first two games, but seriously folks... those games still exist. Go play them.There's more to say, but I'll come back and add to it when I've played more!

_childDocuments_.review: A few points of criticism beforehand. Besides the rather old-fashioned graphics, there are a few things that annoyed me quite often. These quickly lead to problems in the gameplay, which is often not too easy anyway, and which could actually be avoided.This starts with the fact that some houses have entrances. But you can place them so that they show as green and buildable when you build them, but in doing so, access is not controlled. So if you save resources forever to build the expensive building, and then do not look very closely, it may be that the workers can not enter the house and you may tear it down again. Which then sends half the resources to nirvana.The pathfinding is okay for the most part, but from time to time it seems to drop out completely. Sometimes the enemy puts troops in front of the wall, within range of my archers, and then they gather, patter around, form up, and wait until the slowest troops have all arrived. Before they decide to run, my archers have often already eliminated 30-50% of the enemy. Would it be so hard to put the AI’s rally point outside the shooters’ range? At least that would seem less stupid.Sometimes the troops also run strangely in front of the wall, against rocks, or into the water. These are rather rare problems, but they should simply not appear at all. In multiplayer, there is also a rather low unit limit, which was probably set to cover up performance problems. There is room for improvement here as well.... shortened, read full review for more: Overall, Stronghold Warlords offers a well-rounded package. It comes with a long campaign for single-player, which is also not too easy. And with sandbox, multiplayer, and map editor, there is plenty of long-term motivation and replay value, so you will be able to get the game out again and again later.However, the overall presentation makes it look more like a game from 2010, and with a base price of just under $39 or €35, it’s not exactly a complete bargain either. The graphics, which are no longer quite up to date, and the AI weaknesses then make the game seem a bit lackluster in parts.Considering the fun offered by Warlords, I would like to give the game a base rating of 80%. With a more modern engine and more attention to detail, there would have been possible a much better result here. There is good mid-range gameplay here in a packaging that is getting rather outdated.For small bugs, AI weaknesses, balancing problems, and other rough edges in the game design, I would then like to deduct 4%. And when I look at the price tag, I also have a bit of a stomach ache and think, with this offer, it could have been a tenner less. Which then leads to another 3% devaluation for the pricing.This brings me to a final rating of 73% for Stronghold Warlords. With a few improvements through patches, I see the potential for up to 77%, and if the price drops, it might go even higher, but a real hit won’t come out of it then, unfortunately, even in the sale.EN DE

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to enjoy this game. I really did, and still do, but I cannot. I am surprised it has so many positive reviews as it is too. If you really want to try it out, do not pay $40 for this lump of irritating turd. It's not worth even close to that. I got it on sale, but if I bought it full price, I would have tried to get a refund rather than hope that some of the missions would have had some old Stronghold magic. Long story short. They don't, and this game probably isn't worth even $10. Wait for a sale, just don't pay full price. Also, read some other negative reviews.     A message to at least some of the positive reviews: Please don't dumb down what some negative review people say, like how one compared the intricacies of bread production to this game's food production. There was no complaint of the change, just of the method and simplification. Don't rephrase what someone says without proper context, please. Also, if you have something to say about the game, please say it. Don't just say it was good. If you can't think of anything that supports that claim, then maybe it actually isn't, especially when compared with much older titles.      It is far newer than the classics, but it has so much less to offer, and what it does have to offer has been so dumb downed and simplified that even on brutal, it would be so easy if not for all the bull crap that they throw your way. Take the "peaceful" campaign as an example, there are so many calamities and such that you have to deal with that also cripple your population/economy. It's not that it's hard, but it's a real pain. It's not a challenge- except for your patience. Like, buildings randomly exploding, fire that even several two-team water pots can't put out. It's more effective to just destroy the buildings and rebuild to stop the spread than rely on your water teams. The process that was taking place in the building was completely made void anyway.     Do you remember the old games have amazing music and more than just a few music pieces? Well, this game doesn't even have that. The music is mediocre or only somewhat good, and there are only a few songs. The whole game is just a disappointing piece of pain. The game looks like it wasn't given enough love. I have no idea how it is on the dev side of things. I know that they seemed to want to do well with Stronghold: Definitive edition, but this game seems to have been given up on despite the many glitches it still has. It needed more time in the oven, and it needed more love and attention from the devs. As it is, it's just not good. It's a subpar stronghold game which seems to be in-line in their recent projects. I don't know what happened, but Firefly seems to have lost access to the magic, or they willingly gave it up- in pursuit of other things perhaps.     In the war campaigns, it's the same sort of deal. It's not hard to defend yourself, but if the enemy has fire-carts, then you have to hope that telling your archers and crossbowmen to attack will do the trick because they will focus on the melee troops first- even if there are enemy archers. If there are warlords in the region as well as an enemy castle, then sometimes the only way to take a warlord is by force, and with enough diplomacy points already placed so that you can interrupt the constant diplomatic seizure attempts by the enemy. For a couple minutes at a time, that was how it was in at least one of the missions. More than half of the missions are also DLC, so you really don't get as much with the base version. Your troops may also flat out ignore the enemy. I had a bunch of archers and crossbowmen in a warlord's keep, and they didn't even try to fire at the enemy on his walls unless I told them to.     The game has so many absurd moments to it that it's not fun nor a true challenge. There will be times when you want to place a building because you've been very efficient with something like the farms, but maybe some small bush or rock taking up the place of a single square will ruin it for you. It's almost like some of this stuff was just put there out of spite or to be a fake challenge. "Let's see how the player deals with this! Lots of random rocks!" Something like that. Like... ugh. It's just a pain, not even a challenge.     Not only all of that, but the game is still glitchy/buggy. In the war campaign, every mission that I completed so far had some sort of annoying talking that was repeated, and the after message from the MC was repeated once every time at the end of the mission. One of the missions, the scribe wouldn't stop repeating a "suggestion" as if he was a broken record. Restarting the mission fixed it, but still. That should never happen. The scribe will also give suggestions often like: "You might want to build some houses to have a growing population." You don't say? I would love to do that, except that everything costs so much in wood. Ranged troops will also shoot through, yes through walls- or at least some of them do. If you're assaulting a castle, you cannot count on those nor hills to provide cover. There are still other glitches I'm trying to find, but this game isn't even on par with the classics, but it's also not exactly a new one either. It shouldn't have bugs like these considering when it was released     Now, there are just so many annoying mechanics to this. There is a thing such as house quality. The cheapest building costs 10 wood, and then it goes 20, 40, 80, 120, with the most expensive being 200. Usually I try to go with the second best that is 120 wood because house quality matters in this game. With a "house" costing 80, you break even. More quality than your population gives a bonus while less gives a penalty. Also please note that the woodcutters only give about 12-15 wood with each load, and for some missions the wood and stockpile are set far apart from the beginning to give a sense of challenge, but it's really just a pain and nothing more. Everything costs a lot of wood except for woodcutters, two types of farms, and ox-tethers.    With food production, it's literally just put your granary in a good spot and surround it with the production buildings. There is nothing else needed aside from a single tea-house for tea. That's it. Remember, almost everything was dumb downed and simplified. Nearly everything, and what wasn't or made more complicated is only made more complicated by design of the map, placement of the stockpile, or introduction of something like house-quality. Nothing truly challenging was added. Just rubbish that has to be dealt with patiently.      I know this is a long review, but honestly, there is probably more to say. What I have said is at least the majority of my gripes. I really wanted to like this game, but when I was thinking about playing the last free campaign (I think it's free?), I really hesitated because I realized I have not been having fun. It might take a few tries to get a mission started right, but that's it. Once you get that done, you just put the speed to very fast. There really is a lot missing with Warlords compared with the older titles, like castle-life, diverse unit types, and from each different culture, and different methods of fighting and structures. Almost everything was simplified. I would also recommend reading some more negative reviews because they do put it very nicely.       Again, do not pay full price. You will surely regret it. Get it on sale if you must, and wait for as long as you can if you can. I really wish I could say it was worth more, but it really isn't. If you are looking for some Stronghold magic, this ain't it.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to preface this review, I loved the original Stronghold:Crusaders, and while not as big of a fan, played all the other sequels. However, this game feels like it was an last minute release back in 2001 that was released as a beta for a new landscape setting. Plagued with terrible AI, lots of bugs, frequent crashes, the game is actually less in depth than the original, and for some reason runs considerably worse. Ai players dont seem to have any of the same requirements or restrictions as real players, and get extra bonuses from warlords that real players dont get. Tiny armies that make seiging extremely difficult for players, and insta rebuilds from the AI make the game more a boring war of attrition that goes on for way too long. The AI go from having 0 coins, with their whole economy literally on fire, to hiring 15 250gold Samurai and rebuilt in seconds. Oh, and dont forget about the walls/gates/towers that are rebuilt as soon as they are knocked down, even with my troops right beside them (hopefully you didnt command them to walk on the space first, or else they are stuck there for the rest of the game). The campaign is not much better, where actual game mechanics are replaced with random pillaging armies that appear offscreen from "other castles".  Im really disappointed by this game, I know Firefly isnt a AAA studio, but Ive played single dev Indie games with considerably better coding and AI. I hope that they release some patches, but it will take alot of work to fix this. +1 to the warlords concept though, really like the idea, but poorly executed.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say, I really wanted to like this game because I loved the original in the series all those years ago. The studio seems to misunderstand their own product though. The fans, I believe, want a game that focuses on building a castle and it's economy. The developers seem to want to write AoE.For a castle building game actually building a castle is a painful experience and for most maps pointless. If you don't find the tiny top down view icon getting things aligned is a nightmare and even then it's tricky. It doesn't really matter though as most of the time you're just walling off the one path into your camp until you build up enough forces to make walls pointless.The economy side of the game might as well not be there. It's trivial to create a town that has high or very high taxes and a dozen spare people. There's apparently no limit to the size of army you can create as it doesn't cost anything to have them standing around - apparently you don't feed soldiers. There's no point building any of the weapon production buildings as it's easy to make enough money to just buy weapons (from who?). All the fancy castle defences are pointless as they get destroyed almost immediately if you get attacked and add little to the defence.The "other" lords system is just plain annoying as it's trivial for the computer to keep capturing conquered lords back. There's nothing worse in a game than having to do the same thing over and over again. On top of that you have to keep requesting they send you goods, there's no option to just have them keep sending you wood / stone / whatever.If you loved the original and can pick this up while it's on a deep discount then it's maybe worth it. There's some enjoyment to be had here but it's a poor shadow of what the game could have been.EDIT: I've now completed all but the economic campaign. I saved the economic campaign till last because I thought that would be the one I enjoyed most. Imagine my disappointment when I discover there's (some) fighting in it :-(.I admit I warmed to the game for a while but that faded again as I played more. I dislike timed missions, which are almost all of them. They add stress and I game to escape stress.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently the definition of minimum viable product. It is missing basic features as in keybinds, graphics options, and gameplay/ui options. Issuing commands to units and using hotkeys (that you have to google for, by the way, since they aren't seen or configurable in-game) is unsatisfactory. You cannot orient your troops in a direction like in Total War games. Your units will freeze up and have to be stopped/re-organized/re-ordered frequently. You start getting some serious Warcraft 1 and 2 pathing/AI vibes. Between the Command and Conquer/Warcraft/AOE/Rise of Nations games etc., this game is by far the clunkiest in terms of actually doing what you want to with your units. Your control groups are also invisible and overlapping. The Warlords system is not streamlined enough, and you cannot selectively automate deliveries. The attack range of ranged units seems to vary wildly depending upon which tower type and hill elevation you are dealing with, and building is a nightmare for walls and economy with the current scheme of temporary transparency/grid-highlighting. Due to the game's current state, unfortunately, I'd rather be stuck on an island with the 19-years-old Stronghold: Crusader. I can't think of anything that this newer title does better/cleaner than the older one, besides the strategy element of units having collision. That's quite honestly the only "improvement" that this newer title makes. Even the newer graphics make it harder to see what you're looking at most of the time, regardless of zoom level and the obfuscated mini-map. If this was a Closed Alpha, that was coming out 12 months from now, I wouldn't be too worried. But no, this is the actual release, where they are asking for $36 after the week 1 discount price.

_childDocuments_.review: It is...okay.  I have just under 80hrs on this including DLCs, campaigns and a few of the Skirmish trails.  I am also an avid enjoyer of the other Stronghold titles. I don't like how every armoured melee unit is so tanky, I can just build 30 of these units and walk into almost any lords base and kill them, there's no need for the depth of strategy/ siege equipment that is prevalent in the previous games.  The castle defences such as mangonels don't really do anything either especially for how expensive they are. The Warlord aspect of the game has grown on me over time, if I wrote this review early on I would say it's terrible and needs to be removed; but it must have been tweaked because it actually adds an enjoyable layer to the game.Overall, if you enjoyed the other games and this is on sale, then I would say you may like it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Strongholds franchise since I found Crusader HD for a couple of bucks on GOG I simply had to get this instalment, featuring my favourite period of siege warfare history. With the many creative and often bizarre siege weapons developed across South East Asia, Warlords adds dynamics to the franchise that make it lively and often unpredictable.Carts with enormous arrows driven by rocket engines, huge gunpowder driven ballistic weapons, and even trebuchets that hurl diseased water buffalo, this game has all the toys and the mandate to employ them. Add in the addition of independent warlords peppered between the main players that can be acquired by diplomacy or force, or simply serve as an additional obstacle to conquest, each skirmish match becomes a campaign in and of itself. In addition to the wide range of specialized tools, unique troops like fire lancers and thunder bomb grenadiers, you also have an expanded toolkit to fortify and supply your position. Zen gardens, kung fu arenas, and torture implements creative and cruel, you may rule quietly with a big stick or simply shout a lot while hammering down any and all opposition. Cultivate tea, utilize animal husbandry as both a source of food and ammunition, and treat your workers to some theatre while their kin blanket the fields with honourable dead.Take up the mantle of Sun Tzu, Genghis Khan or a range of other famous warlords, rulers and upstarts and discover that siege warfare isn't all mud and arrows...it can have rockets, too. As Sun Tzu said, it is best to achieve victory without battle, but failing that you've got Strongholds: Warlords.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello,First let me tell you that I recommend this game to any newcomers and veterans of Stronghold franchise. However, I also understand people who did not like the game as it does not have the charm of early entries in the series.To be honest, I am no Stronghold veteran. Heck, Warlords is my third Stronghold game after the original and Crusader (which is basically like an expansion pack for the original). But this lets me compare the first and the last entries and see how the series evolved.I see that the developers tried to innovate without changing the core aspects of the series in this latest game by adding the Warlords system. I can understand people finding the aforementioned system tedious, mainly because of non-optimal AI. However without it, this game would only be a modern 3D version of the same Stronghold formula in another era. Only modernizing and changing the setting may not seem a bad thing for many people but I appreciate the developers going out of their way and inventing new things for a much beloved franchise. Innovation is sorely missed in these times when many studios re-skin and re-release a tried and true game for guaranteed and quick cash.Grab this game if you are a Stronghold fan, especially if it is on sale. This is not a bad game and it has nearly everything the originals did and more, in addition I believe the developers will optimize the AI. If you are a newcomer to the series, Warlords is a good place to get into the genre. However also consider grabbing the original and especially Crusader. I do not know if this is nostalgia speaking or it is because I love 2D animations but those games were much clearer and easier to look at. For people who do not like new things added to their beloved franchise, stick with your favourite entry. Nothing will top the game you love the most anyways.Thank you for reading, have a great day/night!

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely their best title yet. If you liked stronghold 2 but didn't like the others as much, this is the game for you. They've innovated quite a bit considering the studio is literally like 7 people. Some major features that stuck out to me:1) Housing quality is introduced! You can choose what quality of housing you would like your people to have, with higher quality housing costing massively more, but granting bonuses that eventually mean more tax revenue for you $_$2) Religion/Repression system! By using these building chains you can modify your entire population to gain a productivity boost, however major happiness penalties are incurred (repression.) Conversely, you can choose to gain a popularity boost at the cost of productivity (religion.) Really cool element that was around with stronghold 2 that I loved.3) Map size is awesome. Stronghold 3 was really bad for this, but in Warlords it feels like you actually have room to build your perfect fortress, with room for a depth of defences along with a booming economy. This is my favourite feature of the entire game over previous titles.4) Estates system from Stronghold 2 re-visited, optimized and modernized are called Warlords. In Stronghold 2 there was this really fiddly system of carter's workshops and you had to painstakingly design logistics routes which were not efficient. In place of that the resources from your fiefs are put directly into your stockpile, however it costs influence. There is a chain of diplomacy buildings that allow you to court friendly, enemy, and neutral fiefs to your whim. Furthermore you can invest in fiefs in order to improve the quality of what they give you- some of them are fortress bastions with upgradeable and repairable walls and garrisons. Others are production powerhouses which fuel your economy (on a map with no iron, the fight revolves around the iron fief!) 5) Vassal armies. If you upgrade your fiefs (called warlords) they can compose AI armies which you can order to support your assaults on either your opponent's fiefs or their king's citadel. This adds an awesome feudal element to the game that makes everything seem so much richer and more complex.Cons: Stability. Unfortunately the multiplayer crashes if you include too many AI players, however it works fine in 1v1s, and is decidedly stable in a 3 player FFA. I am sure over time these kinks will be worked out.The game has gotten a bad wrap for no reason. Remember this is a very small studio of industry veterans who literally created an entire genre of video games in their twenties. Firefly's most innovative title yet, bar none.

_childDocuments_.review: May update my review/rating as game is updated.Stronghold, the game after my own heart. I have played thru every game Firefly has released since 2001. I love the stronghold games and the unique approach to RTS they took. I will do my best to offer a comprehensive review to give potential new buyers an insight to this game.  4/10 Does not Recommend  7/10	Yes, I know the graphics are not perfect, but all things considered, this is an RTS. The models are decently detailed, and the maps actually seem “alive”.  5/10	Game play is solid. There are aspects of it I would like to change, but the game play is smooth, and I have not ran into very many bugs.  3/10	I love Firefly’s historical approach to the campaigns. I still feel the campaign is a bit stale. The rivalry between you and the Wolf from previous games was such a compelling story, this game seems to fall short at times. 6/10	UI is clear and straight forward. I wish the delete option was a “click and drag” style like previous games. Especially when deleting walls, having to click individual sections to delete is a bit cumbersome. 2/10The warlord system is cool. I think advertising this as a “brand new” system is inaccurate. Its more of an improvement to the estate system from Stronghold 2. 1/10	I would give this a 0, but technically you CAN build a castle so that is not a fair rating. Unfortunately, firefly has not learned the mistakes of their past games and gave its players way too small of an estate to build a castle in. This is supposed to be a castle sim, but to me it just seems like an Age of Empires wannabe that will be lost in the white noise of every other RTS out there. A lot of the castle building seems very watered down compared to their previous games.	-The new era is a fresh approach to the series	-Formation/path finding is really well designed	-Troops destroying walls with pickaxes is very cool, especially the gradual crumbling of the walls!	-Graphically it is quite pretty	-Lacking content	-Your building room is very limited	-Story is a bit stale and I have a hard time caring about the characters I am overall underwhelmed with this title. Part of what made past Stronghold games so appealing was the diverse approach to victory a player could take. This game feels a lot like some of their more recent “spoon fed” titles, essentially forcing you to play the game a certain way. 	The warlord system could be more in depth. It seems like there should be more to it considering how much FFS promoted the new system. The AI is very boring. It seems the game has abandoned the real time castle improvements by enemy AI from previous titles and has instead just created a cookie cutter approach to skirmishes. For the love of God… Give us more building space!!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, it's not a good game, I would give it a 5/10. Pretty mediocre. I've been playing Stronghold since 2003, I'm a longtime fan of the series and have spent many hours with every Stronghold game. This is probably my least favorite game within the series. Let's find out why...1. Sound and music. Voice acting is kind of awful and the music is pretty forgettable. Stronghold 1 and Crusader 1 were filled with a number of catchy and memorable songs. This game? After 90 hours of playtime, I honestly can't recall a single music track. The music is just extremely forgettable and mediocre. There is nothing that even holds a candle to the likes of Castle Jam from the original Stronghold.2. Graphics. Let's just be blunt here, the game is ugly -- It looks like crap. Completely unacceptable for a modern full-price PC game. There are games that were released over ten years ago that look better than this game. Starcraft 2, Halo Wars, and Red Alert 3... just to name a few. 3.  Warlords system. The Warlords system is the big new feature in the game and sadly, it's a hot mess. No one asked for this system and no one wanted this system. Honestly, I hate it. I never want to see this again in another Stronghold game. You spend too much of your time in the Warlords' overlay, managing all your different Warlords. When you have one Warlord under your possession, it's not so bad. But when you're in a game with multiple Warlords on the map and you're going back and forth with other players, trying to control the Warlords, it becomes completely obnoxious and annoying.When another player is going to capture your warlord with diplomacy points, a voice prompt plays "Another lord would have our allegiance." And it's very easy to miss, especially if you're in the middle of combat and juggling a bunch of other things around. I've had my warlords stolen from me without even realizing that they were being captured. There is NO indicator on the mini-map or in the HUD that you're about to lose a Warlord. It's only something that's visible in the Warlord's overlay, which is not something that is opened all the time. Terrible system, poorly designed. 4. Units/balancing. At least half the units/siege equipment in the game are completely useless or super niche. There's a lot of poorly balanced units in this game. And since Firefly has already abandoned this game, I doubt that the balance will ever change. 5. Campaigns. Boring!! I can't even be bothered to finish them all. Firefly's level design would have been acceptable back in 2003. But compared to today's RTS games? The campaigns are awful with horrible presentation and extremely simple level design. Also, we're in 2022 and Firefly still can't sync words to their animated portraits. You'll have a character speaking to you, but its portrait is just grimacing at you like an idiot -- lips not even moving. Come on, Firefly-- we're not in 2001 anymore.  6. Setting. China...   Do I need to say more? I don't think anyone wanted a Stronghold game based on a heavily inaccurate medieval China setting. People like knights in shining armor and European castles. I get that Firefly wanted to try something different, but how tone death must they be to actually think that this was a good idea?6. Is there anything good about this game? Well, it still retains that classic Stronghold gameplay at its very core. That's obviously a good thing but unfortunately, not enough to make this even a semi-decent game. Just a pretty bad game, overall. Firefly just can't get the 3D thing down. The original Stronghold and Crusader were masterpieces for their time. But every game since then has been meh. At the time of writing this review, Firefly has another unannounced Stronghold game in production. Will Stronghold ever return to form? I guess we'll see, but I lose more and more faith in Firefly and Stronghold with every game they put out.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the reviews are pretty long winded so let me sum it up here. Warlords is not like stronghold 2, its more like stronghold crusader. with less focus on economy and more focus on warfare. That being said, the lack of many systems is still concerning. No gong, crime, rats. feasts, honor, or entertainment. Many are disappointed in the fact that this game has much less going on then previous titles. The complaints are all true. In 2021 we expected the game to be more than its predecessors and not less. We expected more units, more buildings, and new ways to run the economy and topple your enemies. more systems in place to drive home the idea that this is a castle sym. But we got far less. It really sucks to boot this game up and see a reskin of crusaders with more limitations than ever before, and not a new game with new concepts. Also side note, the warlords system is very bad. poorly implemented, and a pain to play around. "foreign diplomats have arrived" "foreign diplomats have arrived" "foreign diplomats have arrived" "foreign diplomats have arrived" "foreign diplomats have arrived" "foreign diplomats have arrived" "foreign diplomats have arrived" "a lord is courting us" "foreign diplomats have arrived" every time you hear this you have to stop what you are doing, open a menu, and click a button. Then you have about 10-20 seconds before it happens again. Its just BAD. I can say nothing good about it.Now I'm going to rant. Remember all the old units? what happened to engineers? to being able to throw rocks or burning logs or hot oil down your walls. being able to build spike traps AND oil traps. Being able to put braziers on your walls to have fire arrows. being able to mount your lord on horseback, and being able to mount and unmount troops on horseback. remember when you could dig a moat? or have a second castle entirely with escape paths and secret gates to get you there if your first stronghold failed? Or remember killing a lords castle and economy, driving out all of his people with disease and not having to kill a single troop? remember being able to build a sizable defensive army, AND a sizable attack force without hitting the troop limit? Remember Gong, rats, crime, entertainments, honor, feasts, executions, marriage, churches and candle makers. decorations, flags, statues etc... Wooden walls!?! So much is missing from the new game. along with the sense of life in your little castle. its gone. and replaced with mediocre things at best. Temples do a poor job of replacing churches. and offer nothing to play with. with churches you could have half mass, full mass, double mass like with the rations. you might say that tea replaced that but in the old game you had ale and taverns that worked the same... no, they were much more in depth than tea houses. you had to balance having enough hops farms, breweries, and taverns to cover your peoples thirst and territory. not just a bunch of tea farms and a single tea house. food production was more complex too. you had royal food only for feasts and gaining honor, and food production came in steps. you had to kill pigs from your pig farm to make leather, reducing your food gain from the farm. you had to grow wheat, build a windmill, and employ bakers to make bread. 3 buildings for a single food type. it was more fun and had more to manage and think about. more to do and build, and many more ways to run your economy. there are just only a few ways to play the new game.Okay okay i didn't sum it up. just too many thought the more i think about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Refreshingly different theme for SH. Bad unit AI, annoying UI menus, archaic feel/presentation, strange combination of cultures. Not recommended at +$30 yet.Very interesting change of scenery for the stronghold games. I can say I really appreciate the theme, music, art, setting, stories, etc. I also really like the new mechanics for manipulating warlords on the map to do your bidding, cool new town buildings, and cool new units.But everyone in this game has the same units. The mixing of Japanese styled units and Chinese styled units is ... disappointing. Why not make several unique factions? Some units speak English, some speak Chinese, some speak Japanese (???)... to have all these units bundled together at all times is just so weird.Balancing of resources feels good, I would hope they've mastered the economies of this game by now.The UI seems like it has great potential to make sense (lol), but I found myself getting lost a good number of times. It's also not very intuitive for finding the right menu buttons in some cases. Icing on the cake: some of the help buttons don't work when you click them.The game runs in 32bit, there's no 64bit option (in 2021). Come on guys. On top of that, this game does not ALT + TAB very well and I've lost a session to this, having to force quit the game in task manager. This game could be remade better in Unity, ditch whatever engine you're using - it's old and archaic at this point.I had my first crash, it was right at the end of a long mission, of which I lost all progress for. I've also experienced random jittering and choppy frames for seemingly no reason. I refrained from writing a review until now, that was the final straw.With all that said, this game just boils down to being another stronghold re-skin with really bad unit AI. I think it has potential for improvement and I could see this becoming one of the more fun SH games.I'd recommend this game if the AI and UI were improved. It'll probably be a good purchase if you catch it below $30 in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Stronghold Warlords appears to be a reskinning of previous games from the franchise. While it does introduce some fresh mechanics, such as the Warlords system, it largely retains the core gameplay that defined earlier titles. This commitment to the series’ roots is commendable, as it preserves the essence of what made the original games memorable. However, this adherence to tradition is a double-edged sword, as some game elements feel outdated.Combat in Stronghold Warlords is at its most engaging during sieges, where strategy and planning come to the forefront. Yet, outside these moments, the gameplay is reduced to basic troop movements and confrontations. This is a stark contrast to Stronghold 2, which introduced a wealth of mechanics to building management and boasted a compelling storyline. Similarly, Stronghold Legends significantly enhanced the combat system and wove a captivating narrative from legends around the world.In comparison, Stronghold Warlords seems to add little to the series. It misses opportunities to innovate and expand upon the formula.while I would recommend Stronghold Warlords to the veterans of the series, I would hesitate to suggest it to newcomers looking for a modern RTS experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. It's actually the first new Stronghold game that takes me back to the Crusader days in terms of feel. The NPC system is a little strange and can be both fun and annoying, and a little glitchy, but it does add an interesting "game within a game" kind of vibe. I do like how the NPC system makes turtling more difficult. You actually have to think about defending your protectorates and not just sitting behind a wall. Siege is a lot more difficult in this game than others, but the exploding ox is OP and if you keep sending herds of them to destroy enemy resource buildings the game goes much faster. Overall it feels balanced, and the campaign is good fun for a few hours. My only real complaint is the lack of skirmish maps at launch as I would have preferred to see more than 10 developer maps, but the maps that are there are decent. If you enjoyed playing hours and hours of Crusader or classic, you will enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: All I wanted was a re-flavored Stronghold Crusader, I don't know why FireFly still hasn't managed to pull this off.The mechanics are actually OK, so I don't feel like writing about them, other than they feel *just* OK.My contention is that this game sorely lacks any immersion or investment for the player which, I believe, is what turns a mere point-and-click troop and resource manager into a true experience.GLARING ISSUE: WHERE IS SIX & STONES? This is the single most invigorating and immersing soundtrack in the series; it SCREAMS Stronghold and medieval warfare, and it's GONE. I would love to have been able to hear a new badass orient-themed version of this epic siege score, and it's just missing. As a result, there is no point at which there is a sense of great stakes or grand scale in the game; everything feels small and insignificant.Other problem I think I've noticed even in other stronghold games: Is it just me, or do the maps and expected castle sizes feel smaller with each game? I know that real-life castles are technically pretty small, but this isn't real life. In Crusader I began to approach the scale of a small walled city before the game was halfway through, now in these latest releases I feel relegated to a mere cramped little redoubt, scrounging up square footage for one more building. I look at my lands and am unimpressed each time.I've heard this complaint before, but the voice acting is pretty gross. There's nothing wrong with properly hamming up an accent for your game to emphasize the setting, but I want to fight the voice of Samurai Jack, not the secretary guy from Mulan.All in all, this game fails at every turn to draw me in as a player, I was having an easy time of the campaign, but I stopped wanting to spend any more time in this uninspiring-yet-functional RTS.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I think it's the most entertaining Stronghold game to come out since the original Stronghold Crusader (2D).Positives:- The new setting breathes a lot of life into the game.- It just feels better, more polished, and more fun than Crusader 2 3D.- Actual differences between the lords/factions is nice, like how the Japanese get actual Samurai rather than generic swordsmen, for example.- Campaigns do a fairly nice job of introducing the game mechanics to the player.- Warlord system adds some interesting mechanics and strategic considerations.- Unit formations, while limited in options, are great (I love the banners in the line formation).- It isn't a difficult game for most PCs to run, so you don't need to worry about that much if you have't upgraded in a while.Criticism:- Replayability Issues:        - Skirmish needs an option to remove the "Warlords" system and play normally, as in Castle-vs-Castle.        - Game could use a "Crusader Trail" like the one in Crusader 2D.         - A castle defense "hoard" mode (build a castle, defend from increasingly difficult waves until death)            would be a great addition.        - Somewhat low variety of lords and opponents, especially compared to the original Stronghold            Crusader. - Doesn't always feel like a complete upgrade over the original Stronghold games. There are missing mechanics from the original games which could improve the game a lot, and add variety to play-styles.- The build-able area of your castle could use some tweaking or expanding, it feels a little small at times.- Lack of feed-back for popularity/population drain. It is very easy to just suddenly lose your entire peasant population because you looked away for a moment at the wrong time.- Still doesn't feel like the "definitive" Stronghold experience. I recommend playing the original 2D games before this one.- The presence of this game makes me pine for new 2D Stronghold game even more than before... especially in this setting.Although I had more negatives than positives to share, I do actually recommend the game, and I think that this is a large improvement over Crusader 2 3D. If you've been a Stronghold fan since the original games, and this one looks promising to you, I'd say it could be worth the full price. Especially if you're really hungry for a new Stronghold experience. If not, then wait for a sale, and I think you'll be happy enough with how this one turned out. I also expect many of the games issues, particularly the replayability issues, to be ironed out in potential DLC roll-outs.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this. I haven't played a Stronghold game since the original, but the Asian setting seemed like a fresh take on the formula and a good place to jump in.It's been about 20 years since the original, but it feels like the gameplay hasn't advanced at all. If anything it's a downgrade from the original. It's slow, it's clunky, and it's lacking incredibly basic features, like queued commands and attack move. How do you make an RTS in this decade without a-move?!?The only new feature of any note is the warlord system, in which you conquer neighbouring forts, but while neat in concept, I found it very tiresome after a while. You'll usually have warlords in front of your base that you need to defend, so it almost entirely defeats the purpose of building up your own castle -- which is, you know, the core hook of the franchise -- and maintaining control of your warlords often devolves into an exhausting game of whack-a-mole, especially once enemies start gaining the ability to steal them via diplomacy.

_childDocuments_.review: I was there... 3,000 years ago... Ok enough memes. I've been there since the very beginning. I still own my CD-rom version of Stronghold from 20 years ago. I've loved everything they released except that awkward phase (Kingdoms). I was put off of this newest release by the swath of god-awful reviews until it came on sale... Turns out, it was just the new generation that had NO relationship with this series. So, ofcourse, you wouldn't get it... (look, another meme). Directly compared to S.H.C.2, the diplomacy system was a stroke of genius. It's an awesome feeling to have more control over your A.I allies. It was the greatest hindrance in previous titles that they wouldn't do what was needed when needed. They'd just demand silly amounts of resources for a minor payoff and would act almost entirely randomly often acting only as fodder to give you the time to prepare for the REAL war. The idle lords with pre-set commands when captured is simply brilliant, giving the player tonnes more control than previous titles, also adding additional urgency to any given situation as the player has far more to act on instead of the old formula. "Build walls, make crossbowman on large tower, hoard resources to sell, win". Now the A.I has far more opportunity to surprise you with detrimental map control, snaking victory from beneath you if you aren't careful.I'll admit, the story aspect has really suffered this time around, they've never quite recreated the majesty of the Rat, Snake, Pig and Wolf since the first Stronghold. But! I've thoroughly enjoyed the game none the less. Well worth the £5.99 I picked it up for.I certainly wouldn't have paid the asking price, hence why I waited for the sale. But still, after a few hours I have to say I don't think it deserved the flak it got in the ratings. It's a really good effort with some truly great ideas. I'm yet to buy the DLC as there is so much to do in the base game. But we'll see how we go.One final note. Oh ffs the levels when you have to play the invader! Always hated those levels in every title and they're back again! The game is called "Stronghold" ffs. I wanna base build! Give it a rest Firefly, we don;t like these levels, we tolerate them.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get these reviews - this is the first Stronghold I've had a blast playing since Crusader (1, 2002). It has all the great core gameplay and flow of the original Stronghold and Crusader, but with some cool innovations and a different setting (while some of the sequels got either *way* overcomplicated and clunky, or too oversimplified). I didn't have to convince myself to like it, I just started playing and had fun right away, with familiar and new elements. There's regular campaigns, *four* skirmish trails, free build and all, and everything plays really well.There are a few flaws - first, I think the optimisation could have been better (comparing e.g. to Age of Empires 3 DE, which looks imo slightly better and works much better on my old-ish PC) and I feel the graphics are maybe a little too dark/muted (but I guess they make sense for the grim "warlord" aesthetic). Plus, it feels like the warlord mechanics can get a bit chaotic when there's more of them on the map, but maybe I'll get used to it over time.Basically, this is a great (Crusader-line) Stronghold and a very good RTS. 100% worth trying on sale, and I wouldn't regret it for the regular price either. Will probably play lots of it especially after finally getting a new PC.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like simulation, real time strategy and beautiful zen music then you've came to the right place!Don't come here expecting a completely next-gen experience or mindblowing graphics. Stronghold isn't about that in my opinion. Stronghold is a game about controlling huge armies and defending bustling castles you've created. Paying attention to your castles needs is an important part of stronghold. You can't fight an army without your granary being full with that sweet sweet rice.The gameplay is good in this game. It doesnt quite hold up to Stronghold 2 levels of gameplay in my opinion but this is a huge improvement on the past two games. The warlords is a cool idea which can be used to help win you the match or can just become a nuisance. I'm not a massive fan of having to use a warlord to get wood even though my woodcutters could just get it themselves. It really took the fun out of the game for me when i had to rely on warlords. I think if they were completely optional and less relied upon they would be a more welcome addition to many players. The maps and set-pieces are fantastic. Lush greenery and beautifully crafted soundscapes can take you away if you look hard enough. The sound of war and the beating of the drums gets your heart pumping. The sound designer has done a really good job! The narrator isn't my preferred voice as i wake up nights with the "YOU CAN'T PLACE THAT THERE MA'LORD" voice from Stronghold 2. He is iconic. Bring him back firefly.My biggest gripe with this game involves the timed missions during the campaign. It really really took the fun out of this game for me. I had no joy playing the timed missions and making my castle look beautiful as i know it had to be over within a few minutes. For me stronghold is about creating vast empires and controlling your fierce warriors. Not stressing about getting 20 wood logs within the next 2 minutes. Now i get there are some uses for some of these timed missions and thats cool, but nearly every missions was timed and man, its just not fun. I would love to play the campaign again with an option to turn the timers off. Really really dislike that.There's a few bugs where the game would crash on me or my troops would be stuck in mid air forever and eternity. However i understand that such a large game with such a small team can be quite a task. Firefly have been very generous with their updates they've been handing out. If you're unsure whether to buy then i'd recommend waiting for a sale as the updates should have fixed the minor bugs by then.Overall this game is a fun, 30-40 hour (Or more if you like sandbox playstyles) experience with beautiful imagery, music and sound design. Flawed by a few design choices such as timed missions and unnecessary warlord attributes. However these can be forgiven as the charm of the game and core gameplay are really what drive it home.7/10P.s i wrote this after a bit of a drunk night so forgive my hungover typing.

_childDocuments_.review: Tried playing Skirmish, wound up crashing over 3x on the same mission, on the same map. Its not like its player error. I wasn't intentionally trying to brick the game, instead I was macro-ing up and then BOOM, game crash.Its not like the bad reviews are unwarranted. This was supposed to be a AA game, not AAA but you expect there to be QA and bug fixing. Instead the game crashes during the skirmish trail, as a singleplayer experience. I can't imagine the amount of crashing occuring for multiplayer. In comparison, I never recall crashing in SC1 or SC2, and maybe in WC3 with the occasional return to desktop. But here's the kicker, those game had failsafes like autosaves. It should be an industry practice to trigger autosaves at timestamps. Instead SH warlords decides to decide fk it, and leave it be. I get that this is made by a small team, but then why charge 30 dollars for a game that barely functions. I've crashed to desktop more times than usual, and been wasting HRS of macro time, just doing barebones economy building without getting to the fun part of sieging and attacking. Its ♥♥♥♥♥ infuriating as an RTS player that random crashes can occur this frequently.Also, their point-n-click is horrendous. I cant even select different trebuchets or units when they get stacked on each other. I can't micro-manage low hp units, unit control and some building schemes feel like utter ♥♥♥♥. This is a problem, that in an RTS, I don't feel like playing the "RTS unit control" portion of the game. The stronghold part is fun, but managing and estimating range, figuring out tower and unit range, getting them in formation, sieging and defending accordingly becomes a chore to do. This game covers a weird middle ground between Age of Empire and Total War. Trying to have the best of both worlds just makes me as a player unsure of what to do. I try to focus on battles but the economy sucks and micro-ing isn't very rewarding. I focus on economy but my units become braindead, and you can't really "outmacro" against good opponents.Diplomacy becomes a deciding factor but watch tournaments and custom matches and most players will tell you that you don't win "FK ALL" with diplomacy. So the core mechanics just feels bad. I'm new to the strongholds game but even then, comparing let's plays and stronghold content creator replays, you start to see this game is more eye-candy than game. Like its fun for the first few hours, but its turtle pacing (assuming you go by starcraft/CnC pacing) and lacklustre unit control and gameplay design, just makes you question if you could just speed up the early game.There's probably more that should be said. But the mixed reviews are warranted. On one hand its a good game in theory, but the bad controls, UI and other things just make it apparent the lack of polish it has compared to most other titles. I would recommend but really do your research. I got it off at 50%, but even then I think its too high because of the bugs. For reference you can get plenty of other games for cheaper, with more content, less bugs and less fustration trying to play at times.Only get if you are RTS fan, looking for a base-building defence and attack sim. Its got bugs and issues, mixed ratings are justified. Get only while on BIG discount, and do so AFTER watching replays and let's play to see if this game is for you.
