_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: It's a decent game.Personally I have played every Stronghold game except Kingdoms, and in my opinion Warlords sits among the better half of the series' titles. For context: I've mainly played campaign so far, both military and economy, as well as two skirmishes in singleplayer. First I want to adress the neagative aspects I experienced while playing. And to be honstest, there are pretty few. The game runs well on my 2018 mid-tier PC and I have encountered hardly any bugs, none of which were gamebreaking. I've heard many people complain about the low unit cap in skirmishes, and while I agree that those are a little too strict, I can apprecheate this way the game forces me to actually use my limited troops wisely. Like strategising in a strategy game. MAD. While building 20 trebuchets and mindlessly storming the enemy castle with 500 pikemen is fun, this is actually my prefered way of handling balance. This method also incorporates the Warlord-mechanic pretty well, since a Tiger-warlord for example can add a significant advantage with his 30 unit strong attack army, which he couldn't if the player could just recruit infinite amounts of soldiers. Still, I can see why people think max. 80 unit armies are boring, so I would like to see the cap being raised, too.While at the topic of raising numbers: 4 Skirmish-Lords are way too few. As far as I remember, both Crusader I and II started with 8 and added 8 more eventually. I really hope this will be the case here, too, and at least 4 more should be added for free. I was never really a multiplayer-person and thus I really hope additional Lords are to come. Now let's talk about all the good stuff. Graphics and soundtrack create a really beautiful, immersive atmosphere. This is of course subjective, but in my opinion the new setting is successfully portrayed. Although I would love to see the series return to medieval Europe in the future, Asia works surprisingly well with the good old Stronghold formula. The new economy branches like tea and clothing manufacturers bring a welcome change to the old bread and beer of former games. The military units all have their uses, as far as I experienced it, and I love the improvements to the combat system (collision detection etc.). Sometimes arrows can fly through walls, but that's nothing a little patch can't fix. The campaigns so far (I've finished Economy and am half way through the third Military one) are generally pretty fun. The mission design and objectives are varied, the gameplay is well structured with different sub-objectives, and the hard difficulty offers a decent challenge. The only drawback I see is the presentation of the story. And this is the only aspect I will allow myself to directly compare to the original Stronghold. I will address the reason why I don't want to compare them later. Yes, the main characters talk during the mission, but the overall narrative is just plain text that is not even read aloud. I see that Warlords doesn't tell a character-driven story, rather the story of entire empires, but in my opinion the narration itself could use some more flavor to it than three paragraphs ot text before every misson. The other issue is the storytelling and general atmosphere dunging a mission. Here is where I want to draw comparisions to Stronghold 1. Back then it would go like this: you build your castle when suddenly a message from your enemy arrives, in which he treatens to attack you, and you are being told that an army is approaching. From this moment on the jolly peacetime music stops and you hear nothing but the ambient noises of your settelment. Wind howling across the battlements, some birds in the distance, a tanner sharpening her knife. Suddenly the messanger shouts that the enemy has arrived. Troops are entering the field to the sound of war drums and slowly rally into attack formation. Then you hear the horn of the attackers blown in the distance and the fight begins. The battle music kicks in as the attackers storm towards your walls. The battle rages on and on, but as soon as the last enemy is repelled you hear it again: silence. Only ambient noises of the wind on your battlements and some birds. The same silence that gave you chills minutes ago. And then, it's back to building your castle. I exaggerate this point so much, because I think this masterfully crafted atmosphere was what made Stronghold such an amazing experience. And I think this got lost in later titles, such as Warlords. I believe when people talk about this game having no "soul" too it, they refer to this point I just tried to describe. The game does very much have a soul! Each work process is carefully animated with great detail, your people react to the way you govern your castle, the list goes on. Firefly really put their heart into Worlords, and it shows, if you look closer! But when it comes to the atmospheric storytelling within a mission, the game shows it's weak spot. Your enemies during a campaign are not even given a portrait, no personalities, no character. They are simply NPCs with a Name, sending waves of soldiers towards your castle. No messages, no suspense. They are simply forgettable. I cannot recall a single antagonist form any of the Warlords campaigns I played. But I still know about the Snake, and how he send me reinforcements for the beer I brew, while the Rat's troops were constantly trying to tear down my farms. And then he betrayed me. And then the feared Swordsmen of the Wolf approached my pityful castle. The thing is, if you have played Stronghold 1, you know exactly what I'm talking about, even after 20 years. In Warlords, I don't remember anything after a week has passed. If you have read this far, you might have a pretty negative impression of Warlords, but let me make one thing very clear: I really like the game and would recommend it to everyone, who is somewhat interested in Real Time Strategy Games. This one point I explained (probably way too) extensively is not the focus of the game. I am aware, that Stronghold: Warlords heavily focusses on combat-based, dynamic gameplay. And in this area the game does a very good job. But I think the reason why people play a Stronghold game in particular is also the dynamic atmosphere, and in this department no game in the series comes even close to the original Stronghold. This is also the reason why I didn't want to compare the two games. The basic gameplay may be identical, but the core focus of the game is a completely different one. Many people in the fanbase want a new game like Stronghold 1. Stronghold: Warlords is not like Stronghold 1, but it doesn't want to be. Taking this into perspective, in my opinion Stronghold: Warlords is a really good game.

I really want to like this game, but just like AOE the graphics could be better. The game seems to focus on you controlling other warlords that really are helpless.  During the game the ai literally explodes with resources and builds 2-3 times faster than you at times, it makes for a competitive run for your money defensively but I can say this at times playing older versions I can keep up and even attack first, where this seems like a catch up game version.  My favorite versions are Stronghold crusaders HD and Extreme.  But that's just me. I have over 800 hours combined on those 2 games alone, so I know Stronghold and how the games are supposed to be. As you will notice I barely crested 37 hours on this version. Just doesn't hold my interest.   I really hope that Firefly gets back to its roots, I don't want the old game just improve on what was already great.  Aoe IV has a cool story line but lacks to improve on most aspects of the game.  I am really disappointed with the new strategy games and the pay to play or pay to win or micro transactions, just money hungry now.  Before it was pay for the game then if there were new maps they would would sell a one time fee a map pack that would include hidden gems for you like avatars or pictures or things like that.  Now its all about the money and if you like the game great or try buying this to maybe help you like it better.  If Firefly is going in a new direction I hope the new players really enjoy this version, but for me I will stick to the classics for now.  Warlords is a great concept and a game I really want to enjoy and get into, but I just can't seem to want to lay it that much.  For those new to Stronghold I would say I would recommend it on the fact that you don't have anything to really base your likes and dislikes off of, but overall I can't recommend it, sorry Firefly just not my cup of tea.  Try the classics as well to see what many are trying to explain why they also don't recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: Most of the community is outraged but I love this game....and I'm not a Stronghold fan!Stronghold has always had a deep learning curve, the maps limited you to little to no resources. In fact most times you would be stuck with a poo location with either Iron OR Stone but not really both. That doesn't sound like a problem right?! Wrong. You can't build anywhere you want so getting those resources can be a pain in the ass and meanwhile your enemy is usually slapping you around one way or another for no good reason at all.Warlords fixes that issue giving all players equal resources and the ability to capture a "Gaia" Faction to use for small buildings, siege equipment, and some other things! OH Did I mention that these factions can be FRIGGN' UPGRADED TO HAVE MORE HEALTH?! Or that YOU CAN UPGRADE THEIR CASTLES WITH INFLUENCE?! ORRRRRRRRR That you can USE THEM.AS.A.BAIT.ARMY.TO.DISRUPT OR DEFEAT THE ENEMY. So if you have a few of these bad boys you could take down a whole enemy faction or their sub faction. This is a HUGE deal and completely changes the meta! If you aren't well defended yourself then some dude is going to walk right into your base with an Army he can't control AND.BLOW.UP.YOUR.♥♥♥♥!Ontop of all that it's based on the Eastern Asian side of things so you have: China, Japan, Mongols, and somebody else. There's no horse poo poo as everyone is equal. Now that I've given you a baseline here check this out. This game isn't perfect. The tutorial sucks, the campaign sucks, and most players online have already got this ♥♥♥♥ figured out. The bots aren't very smart and won't utilize the "Warlords" to fight you....It's almost like they recycled the AI from their previous games and just rolled with it.I like at least three of the maps but for the most part there isn't a lot to pick from. The maps feel small, big bases on some aren't really a thing at all and sometimes one dude will have a straight shot to a Warlord from day one. Number three! A common strategy I've seen already is that somebody will WAIT for you to fight off the Warlord AI then come in and swipe the thing from you and upgrade it right away. If you have a decent economy you can always mortar the thing from a distance or launch a rocket at it, it's not like they're invincible but still! If I can't repair the thing on my own accord why should somebody else be able to upgrade it WITH.MY.TROOPS.CONTESTING.THE.DAMN.THING!Regardless of it's faults I still like the game! I love the mix of Eras, I love the somewhat RTS gameplay now, and I love that it so much simpler. If you like the idea of Stronghold, but aren't really a big fan of the previous titles then maybe this one is for you!

_childDocuments_.review: IntroI have played the original Stronghold and Stronghold Crusader (number 1) and really enjoyed the simplistic 2D layout. I will be comparing to those two games heavily as I found those to be the strongest of the Stronghold franchise. Most stronghold 3D games I found to be cringy and awkward to watch and play. The 2D games had a simple and elegant approach that I truly enjoyed.Game Play and StoryThe game play is pretty well done. It took me a day or two of playing to adjust to the tempo of the game. You have to anticipate enemy movement and move your units accordingly since it can take a minute to get your troops into position. The campaign consists of 5 story lines, each with 6 or 7 missions. It took roughly 30 hours to complete the campaign on normal difficulty. My criticism for Warlods is lack of player vs everything (PvE) content. I liked Crusaders because it had an abundance of content. It had a campaign story and two sections that consisted of 80 playable missions (50 in one and 30 in the other) that offered a variety of maps, enemy composition, and challenges. I logged over 200 hours on those 80 missions alone. It had a crazy amount of material that I can replay a mission and it feels new because I had forgotten about it. It offered a "grind" aspect to the game that I enjoyed. I have nearly 34 hours on Warlords and feel done with the game. Once the campaign is completed, you are force fed into Player vs Player (PvP) content and I do not particularly enjoy that for end game content. I need a variety of things. You can solo play an economic game but that gets boring after 20 minutes. I disliked the diplomacy aspect of the game in the beginning but it had grown on me throughout the game. It allows players to get creative with their strategy and can offer an economic boon to the player. I think it can be altered slightly to make it more automatic. You have to keep an eye on them as they may change loyalty and check on them every minute or two to reselect what they should give you (wood, stone, weapons) and think there should be an automated selection for these. I find you have to worry too much about your allies rather than focus on your army and economy. It is a neat idea that requires fine tuning. The game play reminded me a lot of Age of Empires. Some unit control felt a bit clunky where units would stand still when I put them on aggressive stance and want them to charge whomever, and other times on standby I found they would run away and strike things when I want them to standstill. It is a shame that Firefly is only now getting to that type of game (age of empire esque) in 2021, when those titles and type of game play have been around for decades. Visuals and Music/SoundI found their attempt to make 3D version of Stronghold rather cringy but they certainly nailed the visuals for this one. The loading screens are beautiful, the texture and shading are great. The music is by far one of my favourite features that really help a player get into the game. My two criticism for the visuals is the scale of everything and the resemblance and feel to age of empires. Focusing on scale, Stronghold and Crusaders had a larger character models. You could see a woodcutter flex his muscles when he returned to his hut prior to getting back to work, see a baker sit on his stool as he waits for flour, watch the kids run from the stockpile with some wheat and climb into the flour mill to create the flour. You have to scroll in as far as possible to get those little details with Warlords. It is fun to do once to see how everything looks, but is impractical when you are actually playing. Secondly I found there was a lot of similarities to Age of Empire Mythology. When you send your army into battle they will scream and it sounds exactly like that game. Controlling your army and units felt a lot like that game as well.Game SpeedPlayers can alter the speed of the game from slow->normal->fast->very fast. I think the speeds need to be re-calibrated. I found the normal speed is quite slow but the fast speed is too much. If the normal speed was 5-10% faster I think it would have ran much smoother. Its nice when you send your slow marching army across the map at a higher speed, but when it came time for genuine game play I found normal a bit too slow and the fast speed too fast to control my units as I would like.Hot KeysThe system does not allow players to set their own hot keys, which I think is a serious mistake and should be added in the future if they decide to create future Strongholds off this model. There is no link inside the game that shows hotkeys and people have to go into the discussion forum to find the link from Firefly or google it. That type of material should be posted in game and easily accessible. I had difficulty using certain hot keys. I may be unaware of something preventing me from using certain things, example, you can shift from the aerial/birds eye view to normal view by pressing alt+spacebar but it never worked for me and had to manually click between aerial and normal. They allowed players to move the camera with ASWD, which is super nice.ConclusionThe game is certainly a step up from their previous 3D models in terms of visuals and play but the game could offer more. The campaign is rather brief and then you are force fed into online multiplayer skirmishes and Warlords is not on par with other real time strategy games like starcraft. Firefly has taken a step in the right direction but it feels late to the party. As noted above the speed and play feel similar to other titles. I do not think the game is worth the 40$ in its current form. I had hoped for greater content as opposed to a PvP end game. All in all I do think Firefly has done a good job - not a great job, but a good job. I hope they fine tune mechanics to smoothen the game play and offer greater variety in future content.7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure at first about this one. From all the articles and videos I saw, I thought it looked like a mobile game. After watching and reading some positive and negative reviews, I decided to buy it, thinking I could always refund it.The game's graphics are not state of the art. The menus are bare-bones, as are the options. (Most likely have to edit a config file to change more - haven't checked) the in-game GUI is ok, and gets across important information. The game only shipped with nine multiplayer maps, which is not great. The setting is different, and one I was not sure about.But I'm really liking the game. It feels good. The buildings and balancing and industry feels very similar to Crusader 1. The game runs very smoothly for me, and the music and sounds are nice. Some of the voice acting is a bit weird with accents and stuff, but not a huge deal.All in all, this feels like a good return to its roots. Definitely the best since Crusader 1/Stronghold 2. Its not bringing anything mind blowingly different to the genre, but as an original player of stronghold crusader, I appreciate that. I wanted a modernised remake of the older games, and this feels like it.The warlord system makes for some interesting game play. You can capture different outposts around the map, and their lord becomes a vassal, which can either send you tributes in resources, or you can ask them to attack other players, depending on that vassal's capability. They can really help boost your economy, which in turn helps you put out a bigger/better army. Besides the setting, it's really medieval Europe reskinned into an Asian theme. You have all the same weapons and siege weapons. But with rockets and fire arrows thrown in. There's a couple of meme weapons too, with suicidal ox loaded with explosives, and a mortar. You also get your normal trebuchets.Castle building feels good, and it works well. You get all your tower options, and castle defence, including lighting gunpowder on the ground for enemy troops to walk over (similar to pitch in crusader 1), and tiger cages too.The campaign so far is fun, with about 30 missions using different lords.As mentioned, the multiplayer map count is low. (9) I'm hoping more official maps will be added over time. Firefly has also included a map editor, so we should see more maps getting pumped out fairly quickly by the community. I plan on trying it myself as well.Overall, for $40, I'm happy with it. I can see myself putting a good chunk of time into this in the coming weeks/months. Generally, if I can get 2-3 bucks an hour of entertainment out of a game i paid for, I feel like I got my money's worth. (I realise not everyone uses this scale)I feel most of the negativity is overblown, but that is just my opinion - as is this review. Make of it what you will!

_childDocuments_.review: So first of all, the game is really entertaining. I haven't had this much interest in a Stronghold since Crusader and Stronghold 2. Still it's far from perfect. So please read this.I don't have a ton of playing hours, but I wanted to share my first impression. Be it for the developers (hello I hope you read this) or for those who struggle to buy the game. The game is really entertaining (in the first hours), feels good, is oldschool, even if it eats more FPS than expected. If you are a fan of Stronghold 1 you will miss something, but otherwise it has everything you need to PLAY A STRONGHOLD TITLE.But PLAYING A STRONGHOLD TITLE does not mean that it is as good as other parts of the series. That brings us to a point (to you dear developers) that I don't understand. Normally you would think that if you put out a game, get plus points and minus points, then publish another game, another, another and so on, that you would keep the plus points and combine them and also throw out the minus points. Am I wrong about that? For example, why don't you take the combat system from Stronghold 1, the interface and building system from Crusader, the graphics from Crusader 2, the economy mechanics from Stronghold 2 and the atmosphere from Warlords and put it all into one? I don't know anything about development, but I can think logically. Warlords is a good game for Stronghold fans, at least for those who aren't tearfully attached to Stronghold 1 and hate everything else. But it's far from a smash hit. If you're open to new things and want a cool atmosphere, this is the game for you, but you won't find much variety, a great battle system or big graphics. Why is the Warlords system, which you can also find in the game title, so incredibly boring? Why can't you cultivate captured lands like in Stronghold 2? Create effective allies through the warlords to expand your empire? I'm already looking forward to the next Stronghold, where hopefully all of the good features will be combined. You are on a good path. The game is not bad, it becomes just boring after some hours, at least from my perspective. You can do better dear developers. Still.. everyone is really good in crying a river about the things they don't understand. I guess not even 5% of the players are game developers. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Stronghold fan going way back to my childhood and it saddens me to post a negative review for one of my favorite series, but I would not recommend this game to my friends.I bear in mind that this game sold at a low price, and I do not regret my purchase. This game is, by the majority of its features, inferior to Stronghold Crusader 2. The addition of a campaign was initially exciting to me, as that was a feature that was lacking in Crusader 2. However, the campaign is disappointing. The campaigns are based around different culture, (i.e the Huns and the Japanese) but the factions are functionally the same. Why not just have a long campaign with some cultural ambiguity? The campaign primarily features missions relying heavily on the Warlord system. But to me, the warlord system falls flat. Its basically the estates system from Stronghold 2, that has been incorporated in other Stronghold titles, but makes it a bit more impactful and complex, but is not fun or unique enough to base the entire premise of the game around. The Campaign had the typical two Stronghold mission archetypes (attack and turtle to attack), which is were fun, but added a third more annoying archetype in which you are unable to gather resources in your own and have to rely on capturing the warlords while fending off attacks. These missions started out fun, but got tedious and frustrating. Crusader 2 was very challenging, and this game is too, but I found myself to be not having as much of a quality fun/challenging ratio. I understand that they are going to add skirmish trials, something i thought was missing at launch. I'll be redownloading the game to try those out when the time comes. Skirmish is a strong point in the Stronghold series, and I have spent many fun hours playing Crusader 2's multitude of unique maps. Warlords has like 8 maps on launch. Want to play more than tow 2v2 games? You'll have to rely on the community maps, which is a neat feature, but I wish they would have included a few more maps at launch. I'll be coming back to play more official maps as they are released, because I found Skirmish to be the the strong point of the game. I wrote this review before I finished the Mongolia campaign because I may uninstall on a whim. The disappointing campaign makes me yern for a Skirmish Trial series or more skirmish map options. It has turned into a game I play on a friday night after a few beers on easy, which is sad because I really pushed the difficulty of previous Stronghold games that I found were more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: So I played a good bit yesterday and today. I have to say, it’s wonderful! The game exceeded my personal expectations, and is light years better than Stronghold 3. I had a few suggestions that I hope finds the eyes of the devs. If you would like any additional thoughts or clarifications regarding the subsequent suggestions, feel free to let me know. Thanks!Unit Cap - Is it possible to add an option to bump the unit cap for skirmish modes? I believe in the age of 32 gig RAM and 8 gig video cards, having such a low unit cap is a thing of the past. Take a look at Total War, for example.Multiplayer Sieges - I’ve always enjoyed the idea of conducting preset sieges with/against friends. Much like Stronghold 2, where you had the ability to attack or defend a famous castle, but add multiplayer into the mix.Pathing/Crash Issues - I’m having pathing issues with my units when they attempt to walk through spaces between wooden barricades. Also, had a few desync issues occur right before the game crashed entirely during a multiplayer game. Only happened once, so I’m hoping it was an isolated incident. For reference, we have extremely beefy PC’s, so we don’t believe hardware was the issue.Unit Composition Adding some more variety and bonuses to each subsequent faction during multiplayer games would have a huge affect on replayability. FFA Gamemode - I’ve always enjoyed the idea of having a Stronghold game that began with lowly kingdoms that had zero oversight of one another. After some time, they are able to discover other nearby Kingdoms and form “pacts.” Afterwards, maybe they can form an alliance. Once these alliances are formed, the combined kingdoms would play as a shared base coop mode. Mixing A.I. in to the fray, I think it would make for a very fun game mode.Multi-unit build - Fairly simple. Can you add a command in where when we hold down the shift button and click on a unit within a barracks, it builds 4 or 5 of them?Just a few thoughts while playing. I’ve already finished the first two campaigns, and I look forward to the rest. Thanks for all you do, and I look forward to the future of this game - and more importantly RTS’ as a whole!

name: Killsquad
detailed_description: JOIN OUR DISCORD FURTHER NOVARAMA HIGHLIGHTS About the Game Welcome to Killsquad: a co-op action game that blends twin-stick shooter, hack and slash and drops in a dash of character customization & progression. Join us on a journey to five planets full to the brim with enemies for you to annihilate. Choose your hero, select your skills, weapons, gears and talismans, and unleash hell through waves of relentless enemies and fearsome bosses. Killsquad deliveres frantic, direct, skill-oriented control on keyboard or gamepad. Shoot fast, dodge fast, or die even faster. Our core are short, 10-20 minute adrenaline pumping contracts you can enjoy solo or with up to 4 friends in co-op. So it feels a bit like a twin stick shooter. Or a hack and slash. Or a top-down dungeon crawler. Or a sci-fi bullet hell. Well, it feels like Killsquad. And it's a lot of fun to play, solo or with others. Killsquad features five hero classes for you to choose from, each with their own weapons and skills. These combine melee and ranged characters to fit different playstyles. Along your adventures, you'll be able to acquire and equip powerful upgrades for each of your skills, which activate during your contracts. And, if you survive, claim your bounty to spend it on tons of new equipment, such as weapons, power-ups and gear, or cosmetics to show off. Fight your way through +30 contracts in the Campaign Map, visiting five planets along the way. Jump in with your friends or with any other bounty hunter. You can come to the aid of another squad by joining them mid-mission in real time. Cooperate to complete each contract or compete between each other to earn the highest scores. Obtain weapons and gears with unique characteristics that affect the skills of your hero. Earn the trust of the Unseen by finding their Talismans: strong and complex artifacts with exciting passive effects. But be wary, these abilities at first will be detrimental, but through effort and killing lots of monsters can level up to turn into powerful items. Use everything in combination with your skills and upgrades to create game-breaking builds, and make the heroes your own. But this party would not be complete without the main course: the enemies. Hordes and waves of disturbing enemies will make their way to you, clawing and bitting till there's nothing left. But do not worry, you will be fine. It is the bosses which will make you tremble. More than 15 bosses will put you to the test, each with different sets of mechanics and unique ways to be beaten.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game.It has very little depth if any but what is does, it does well.  It is a top down isometric blaster of the old school. No gimmicks. There is no depth to it whatsoever.  I have played a couple of hours now but will probably leave it installed and I can see me coming back to it from time to time.It is not pretending to be more than what it is a fairly shallow yet addictive little arcade game.Its fun.  I would recommend it for what it is.  What it does it does well.  Far from my usual sort of game as I like games with some depth and long term character development and what not but this is one of the best examples of its type.  It took me back to good times hammering games like ''Alien Syndrome'  etc. It looks fine, it has some character development as you grow in power as you progress through the level.  This isnt a persistent increase, you start from scratch each time.  The enemies are varied enough to keep you interested and the difficulty is about right.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, good concept, bad execution.Visually speaking the fidelity is good enough, style is... not my cup of tea, too colorful but I can live with that.Sadly a lot of the boxes of "usual flaws of action rpgs" are ticked. - Camera is too close, to the point that I feel sick after a while.- Enemies attack you from outside view or your range, sometimes even outside the map.- Enemies spawn on top of you, sometimes attacking before the "spawn" animation is even midway so you are basically attacked by an invisible enemy.- Jank. Sometimes that mentioned invisible attacks or outside attacks you cannot defend against took 90% health in a single hit? I doubt that was intentional.- Overcomplicated for the sake of loot. To elaborate more, the whole thing feels shallow that wants to appear deep. Large variety of item types, weapons, consumables, supports, prototypes etc. without any of them really doing much more than a little bit of stat raise here and there while your skills are also limited not to mention the upgrades you equip are only unlocked during the mission. Basically you have to wade through a quagmire of items but get nothing in return really.The missions are pretty much the same, just a linear corridor with a bossroom in the end with enemies spawning on you as you get closer. Darksburg is abandoned and I still feel that game is doing more justice to this concept.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I write this I'd like to say the community of players I've played this game with have been amazing. I don't know if they are devs or randoms but High Five! Secondly, I never write reviews, but this game, this game is a hot mess. Its like they are trying to make an ARPG (Diablo) type game mixed with Destiny and a MOBA. Only it doesn't work! Every new level you need to rebuild your skill powers (MOBA). Your strength comes from gear you buy after the level. Simply run lvl 1 over and over until you are super powerful and can solo any lvl. This is like one of those games you would buy for your phone, play for a few days, forget about and remove.Graphics: The game looks good on high settings. controls: Simple! Seems to be designed for a controller but works well for PC. Id like to be able to move ability's around.Character classes: Horrible! Ranged classes are extremely under powered and basically worthless. Especially in groups (4). hardly no DPS. The Rouge and tank are amazingly over powered while ranged is shooting BBs. Close combat I and was doing 20 times the damage and owning mobs compared to ranged. Loot: There is none. play lvl 1 over and over again to gain credits. why play lvl 15 for 4800 (takes about 30 min.) when ya can play lvl 1 and beat it in 3-5 min.! Sure at the end of the lvl you get a chest with 1 piece of gear. It usually sucks and is broken down for scrap.Fights: The game can be a challenge. Only if you play lvl by lvl as intended and dont farm lvl 1, 1,000,000 times. Lock lvls or make them gear appropriate (easy, normal, expert, extreme, hardcore). Base rewards on completion and difficulty.Map: There is none. There's a compass on the bottom right but its blank. Terrain: Maps are small.Interface: Its a simple point and click meh!mission selection: Its a grid with some cutouts of monsters. its Boxy and lacks depth. Its boring and simple.finding party (multiplayer) : I like how they are doing this. Different but I like it.Overall impression: The game has potential if they stop trying to be a Destiny/Diablo/Moba. the Devs seem to be more worried about how the game looks than how it plays. Personally, id rather have an good looking game with amazing game-play than a amazing looking game with, meh! game-play. work it out.In Closing: The game has potential. Loot drops, skill trees, stop trying to be a mix of Diablo, Destiny and A Moba. Keep the Diablo and Destiny. Drop the Moba!

_childDocuments_.review: is an Early Access co-op Action RPG where you play as bounty hunters and raid planets for glory (and loot). You can play alone or in 2-4 players party.Progression in this game is based on doing contracts-->getting rewards-->upgrading your gear(Vector level)-->doing more contracts (that are partially rectricted based on your currect gear/Vector level).Game starts in a lobby - it takes seconds to choose a contract and launch it. We have 4 heroes to choose from - 2 melee (Tanky dude with a hammer and Assassin with a sword) and 2 ranged (Gunslinger and Medic with lasergun). Each one has 4 skills, 3 from beginning of the mission and 4th (Ultimate) unlocks on level 6. You also choose additional perks/improvements to your skills as your character levels up.:+ The game is almost perfectly polished for a first Early Access build.+ Good skillsets for heroes, every hero feels unique and fun to play.+ Melee characters don't suck compared to ranged ones.+ Good variety of enemies (with more to come)+ You can upgrage every character while playing your favourite one so you can switch between them at any difficulty without problems.+ Nice visuals/sounds. Good technical side, fast loading, smooth controls. I almost forgot to mention all these aspects as I haven't noticed any problems with them.+- Strongly recommended to play in a party. As a singleplayer experience it could become boring rather fast - the game is clearly designed to be played in at least 2 people party. - I didn't like variety of zones/maps so far, mostly in terms of visuals. Honestly, even addition of day cycle or simpliest recolour (blue-ish planet/red-ish planet etc.) would bring more variety to maps compared to what we have now.I can't say anything about lategame content so far, but if there would be enough of it - Killsquad would be a great option to play with friends.  does not offer us anything that we have not seen before, but the existing content is good. This game is entertaining, well-polished and promising in many ways.

The weakest point I saw was the mission based system, where you level up temporarily in the missions, but revert back to level one each time. It reminds me of poorly made MOBAs. So, again.. it's just underwhelming to see so many aspects fall so flat and feel less creative than it could have been.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun. There are bugs, it's early access, it's unbalanced and unfinished, but it's very fun and the devs(granted it's words vs actions this early on) are keen on answering questions and concerns and have already rolled out a great QoL patch 2 days after EA launch.It plays like a wonderful mixture of Darkspore and Helldivers, it even reminds me of Gauntlet Legends, many people seem to think ARPG must mean it's like Diablo/PoE but it's a pretty broad term and if you're refusing to play simply because it isn't a replica of those games, you're missing out but not much is lost. Will say it suffers from a lot of the problems most Arpgs do share though, the ranged vs melee balancing just isn't there but a few simple tweaks and changes can easily remedy most of the huge gaps that are prevalent right now.Some of the bigger problems with the game right now are being acknowledged and the roadmap devs putout look promising, but in it's current state the bigger things are the P2P is pretty wonky on a few levels which can be frustrating if you're in a match with questionable internet, the developers have stated they want to switch to a better system like the one Helldivers uses where host can be changed mid-match to not lose progress/improve gamestate but again just words this early on. Obviously don't know the future of the studio but i've liked what i've seen and while there isn't anything new added to the genre whats there is fun and addicting to play even with the current bugs and hiccups and hope the development cycle gets the funding it needs to keep updating regularly. If you liked Helldivers and/or Darkspore, this game takes good direction from both and improves on it, even at the current price/content I got my moneys worth and then some.

_childDocuments_.review: What an insane time to be alive - we finally have a game that draws inspiration from Diablo, Dota, Overwatch, Destiny, Warframe, L4D2, and HOTS, yet maintains its own identity with extremely satisfying gameplay and great game design.Don't let the videos and reviews fool you - this game is a masterpiece, where each and every skill is choreographed perfectly in sync. Despite my initial doubts about a game that has only four skills, they've applied the HOTS "Talent Tree" to the four current heroes in a way which makes them synergize not only with themselves, but with other players. They've made loot that has modifiers which significantly change up your style of gameplay. We've got a fair and sustainable crafting system that could easily evolve into something far bigger.Play as a gunslinger with a gravity-pulling bomb and follow up with your railgun of doom. A psychic assassin with low health but extremely satisfying combos, chaining every skill together in a requiem of slashes. A brute giant with your standard beyblade and hammer movesets except every hit packs a serious PUNCH.... and a soldier-type class that can be played as both a support or dps - with one of the coolest trap modifier mechanisms I've ever seen conceptualized in a game.Enemies are difficult, with fair use of telegraphing to warn the player of things they should avoid. Normal enemies are not always just punching bags, with many posing a threat to the player when mistakes are made (and deadly when paired with the mini-bosses that spawn often in the game). Fights never feel boring, with action all around the player and things to attack, dodge, kill, and heal.For a game with 4 heroes, that's a lot of good things I have to say. And it will only get better if the pool is even doubled. The contract-based combat system ensures that the developers can easily add new content, maps and bosses without worrying about story flow or lore.I'm glad I looked past the early access tag and small hero pool to find this gem. At its price, its easily worth both the money and time to try it. With this game and risk of rain 2's success, it bodes well for future titles that wish to follow an early access strategy and which are confident that they're entering at the right time to leave the right impressions.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game which I always dreamed of back in the day when I played League of Legends/Heroes of Newerth/Dota actively - a PvE co-op experience with MOBA-style hero progression, cool visuals and plenty of loot. I am not a super-fan of the sci-fi theme in KILLSQUAD though, as I think that it was done pretty generic, without much thought put into it (you are space mercenaries fulfilling contracts for your agency yadda yadda kill this, protect that etc.), and the solo experience is quite unfulfilling. HOWEVER, playing with a friend of two really adds to the fun factor, and I like that the game is tough-as-nails in the upper segments, making you really stick together and prioritize targets and objectives. For the current asking price, I think the game can provide enough fun, but does not put it into "WHOA, AWESOME, WILL PLAY IT FOR 1000 HOURS" territory. Why? Because it lacks CONTENT! The gameplay loop is weak imho, and repeating mission  feels liek a chore - you can't expect KILLSQUAD to compete with the likes of other stellar co-op games like Left 4 Dead, Killing Floor, or Risk of Rain with content that feels like it will become stale after 30 or so hours. Hence, this is more of a 'mixed' recommendation than a straight 'thumbs up' - if the devs decide to really stay true to their word that "reputation is everything to them", then they shall continue to update KILLSQUAD with more content in the coming years and not leave it it this "one and done" state, since the game has enormous (yet untapped) potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m always in the market for a good combat game I can share with friends. The big craze used to be MOBAs, and while I can’t vouch for their elimination entirely just yet, I can say that even some of my MOBA enthusiast friends took a liking to this new action RPG Killsquad. As the name suggests, you squad up in a group of up to four teammates to take on a variety of mercenary missions. These can be anywhere from escort missions to control point missions or just a flat out boss rush. You get to choose which difficulty and which gamemode you want to play while selecting a job from the contract selection board, and if you don’t see one you like, you can just wait a few minutes for them to refresh, though the odds of you getting one you won’t enjoy are very slim. Every mission here follows roughly the same pattern, but with random submissions in the middle. It could just be extra waves of creeps thrown at you, or two bosses at the same time. One game, I was trapped in a small area with two powerful ranged enemies; when I tried to attack one, the other would take aim. In situations like this, cooperation is key. While my teammate (the melee tank) took care of one enemy, I (the ranged healer) was body-blocking the other and spawning med kits as fast as I could. It was as chaotic as it was fun and we made it out with just enough health to spare. Getting so close to death was a rush, and I’m honestly surprised we made it, but it’s that kind of experience that this game has in store for you.For a game with such satisfying and powerful attacks, I was really expecting to spam my kit more than I did, but where we succeeded ultimately came down to precise calculations and strategy. Escorting the payload was much harder than we expected, and we almost died a few times, but we clutched it out in the end with a handful of well-timed ultimates.This game does a really great job of taking that classic head-to-head kit-based team fighting and turning it into a more cooperative game. Rather than two teams fighting against each other, you fight against the AI, and no one gets upset when you win. Playing against another team is necessarily a zero sum game, but I really appreciate this because it’s not as discouraging to lose. You can always battle an easier or more difficult opponent to your liking rather than being matched against people way out of your skill level (higher or lower) and not enjoying yourself. Trying out new characters, of which there are currently four (tank, healer, and two attack) with a few more coming down the line, is completely risk-free since you can always just start a new contract, win or lose. The whole thing is a unique concept applied to an established genre and I love the seamless transition. It almost makes me wonder why I haven’t played something like this before. I have to give major credit where credit is due. Even in early access, this game shows great promise, and I have confidence the devs will stay committed to the roadmap they’ve outlined in their recent news. My only issue with the game right now is that sometimes when playing with friends, I would get randomly disconnected. This happened about 2 in 10 games, which feels like a lot, so I hope moving forward, that gets fixed soon. Otherwise, this is a great game that I would recommend to anyone who loves this kind of action, strategy, or both.Here’s some gameplay from one of my many sessions. This game is great if you just want to jump in and get a contract or two done alone or with some friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Killsquad is an aRPG-meets-MOBA game currently in Early Access, where up to four players can team up and complete different types of missions. There are currently four different heroes, with contracts taking the players to three different planets, each one with its enemies and environments. The game's core features are already implemented solidly, with detailed graphics and an expected Early Access period of six months.Killsquad's gameplay doesn't differ a lot from other games like Helldivers, but also changes based on the hero picked: there are four of them, two ranged and two melees, with at least two new heroes coming before the official release. There's Troy, a famous smuggler, gambler and gunslinger who shoots with his plasma guns and clones himself. There's Zero, a violent medical robot who shoots a giant laser cannon while also leaving medkits for his allies. Then there's Kosmo, once dead cargo technician, now fighting with a giant mallet, his kit being all about AoE damage. Finally, Cass is a monk warrior, fighting with a sword in a flurry of slashed and teleports, becoming invisible when things get tougher. All these heroes fit in a particular playstyle and are balanced in a way that no one is stronger than the other, but unfortunately they also feel uninspired, with none of them having an original design and, while uninspired doesn't mean unfun (and slashing giant monsters with Cass is A LOT of fun), something could have been done to offer a more original gameplay. Each hero offers five different abilities that can be upgraded every two levels during the mission, adding powerful effects to them: Cass' shuriken can bounce between enemies, Kosmo's vortex lasts longer and so on. Unfortunately, the heroes' unoriginal design gets mirrored in these power-ups that do not feel satisfying enough to unlock during the game, mostly because the upgrades are nothing groundbreaking. The fifth ability is the ultimate and can be unlocked once the character reaches level six: this, like in all MOBA games, is the hero's most powerful ability and it's able to deal massive damage or inflict powerful crowd-control effects to the enemies. Combat in Killsquad if fast, flashy and ultimately fun. Whether you're shooting or slashing through masses of enemies, the game feels solid and well constructed, especially when playing in a four-player squad with all different heroes.  The feedback during combat is near perfect and, especially with melee characters, the player is almost able to feel the blows he inflicts on the enemies.With Killsquad being a coop game, some abilities perform better when playing in a group, like Cass' invisibility or Zero's medkits, but combat is enjoyable also when playing solo.The possibility to upgrade the heroes' abilities is very similar to the one that can be found in a lot of different MOBAs, especially Heroes of the Storm. This because both games do not only raise the damage the ability inflicts, but also change the way the ability works, usually by adding secondary effects, like AoE damage, crowd-control abilities or synergies. This, combined with the fact that the progress doesn't get carried over the end of a contract (meaning that the characters start at level 1 at each mission start), make it so that this game is a strange combination of aRPG and MOBA elements.Contracts are the missions players can pick up and play. There are different kinds of contracts as of now, divided into three different tiers, but they all have a similar structure: the player spawns, walks a long way to the objective and then (hopefully) completes it, usually by fighting a big battle or a boss. There are several different goals, like escorting an armored convoy, defending an antenna or killing a powerful enemy, with more to come within the early access period. Contracts unfortunately have two main problems: the first one is the "run to the objective" sections that take up the first half of the mission, which are all very similar, especially when playing on the same planet multiple missions in a row. The second problem is the low variety of enemies that keep showing even on higher-level missions:  this makes contracts very repetitive, even when the objective is different, and some work should be dedicated to diversify environments, mission-flow and the poor creatures that are going to be beaten up by the players.Loot is handled in an atypical way in Killsquad. Unlike most aRPGs, here there are no actual item drops, but only crafting materials and credits. Credits are used to buy items in the shop and materials are necessary for upgrading the equipment pieces.Every character has three slots: weapon, support gear and prototype gear. Every slot can accommodate one item, which in turn has a vector value: the average vector value is also the level of the character.  Items can be acquired in the shop: you choose which category of item you want, spend the amount of credits required, and get a random item from that category with a rarity class based on the level of the character. The item is shipped with a vector value and one or more disabled abilities: these are passive effects that can be installed by spending the requested amount of materials and usually add crowd-control, AoE damage or similar results. Installing passives on items is usually unnecessary on lower vector levels whereas, on higher levels, finding the items with the wanted abilities makes the shop feel like a slot machine.The game delivers exceptionally good graphics for being indie: environments, enemies, abilities and light effects all look beautiful. The design of maps isn't particularly inspired but still good looking, although some repetition can be found, especially in the "Palace of Pain" map where everything looks very similar. Combat, graphically speaking, is very colorful and chaotic, like a good fight should be, but thanks to the precise coloring, identifying the enemies' area of damage it's still easy. Projectiles, instead, are more difficult to locate and dodge, making sure that keeping the attention is vital to stay alive.Killsquad's roadmap details the future updates that the game is going to receive: once every month, content will be added to the game in the form of new factions, enemies, playable heroes and the long waited spec-ops tier contracts. The next update big update is already in a playable beta-state and adds an endgame arena called "Colosseum of the Unseen", which brings destruction and enemy count to the next level.Killsquad is a fun mix of two genres that blend to create a fast-paced, fluid and fun experience. Combats hits the spot when playing on a full team, but to my surprise everything works even when going solo. Outside the combat sphere everything needs adjustments, with loot and contracts being the aspects that need more work.Right now the game has its core done and solidly, too. With more content and the right fixes in the right places, Killsquad could become an exceptional casual aRPG to play with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: well that's weird the store page doesn't show that I made this review, but it exists in my reviews.The game so far is akin to any moba game rather than any proper arpg game, except for the map and pvp, making it more of a rougelite.Leveling system is pretty much the same as any moba game, after every mission you have to relevel yourself from level 1, albeit worse at the moment as you have to open the ingame menu and choose your skill with the analog stick or mouse instead of pushing the attack button or having an option to preselect skill.Then you have Vector level aka gear score/level, but is more akin to Destiny or Skyforge light/power/might level where it affects your overall performance, more on that in the missions.Looting is okayish, as you can find equipable loot, but also can find key shards to unlock chests, or credits to buy ingame random chests of certain item slot type.You only have a weapon(dmg/cooldown etc.), support(extra health/defense etc.) and prototype(exp/credits/reflect dmg etc.) slot. Maybe there was one more slot type, don't remember.Lobby is similar to any moba game, or like in battle royale games, in terms of the waiting lobby where you always are at.You have your hero selection screen with skin selection also info what skills the hero can use and unlock while doing the mission plus inventory and shop.Combat is the best part of the game it's very fluid and impactful.You got your 3 main skills and a basic attack that you can do with a button press or with the right analog stick in any direction, while the A/X button press will try to autotarget the enemy, the rest of attacks you have to target yourself, plus along the way you unlock runes/passive boosts for other skills and at lvl 6 two choices for ultimate skill.Mind that your character does not heal back to full health on it's own, except with certain skills or health drops that only pickup like loot with a push of a button. When soloing you have only one chance at completing missions. Missions also have shops where you can buy a random temp mission item that you use with the dpad on the controller, +max health/shield or heal (also something similar to a moba, rather than arpg).The world is most of the time against you with it's active or passive hazards, but you can use it against the enemies too.Missions are locked away with vector level, at the moment it has 3 ranges, 1-30, 30 to 75 maybe, and 75 maybe to some hundred+. If you have less vector level overall than the mission, then you deal reduced damage and get hit harder against the same level enemies as you are, no idea if you get boosted if you have more gear vector than the mission vector.Graphics and animations look top notch solid.Performance is very smooth at max settings, and had no weird bugs or crashes.Using i7 8700K 3.7-4.7Ghz, RTX 2070 8GB, 16GB DDR4,  Win 7 Ult x64.Anyways the game is not my cup of tea even as I try to own every type arpgs (except mobas) that are out there. Otherwise it's a good solid game, even in it's early access state.

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT RECOMMENDUnfortunately this game is way too far from completion to warrant the price.Pro-A fun Mix of MOBA, Twin Stick Shooter, and Dungeon Looter RPG mechanics-Very satisfying WASD + Mouse for a Twin Stick Shooter Gameplay-One of the best “Early Access” games on the Unreal Engine that I have played in a long time People at Epic should reach out to Team Novarama and encourage other studios to Learn from Novarama- Great Graphics and SoundFun Hero Character Design (reminds me on the Smash Up Card Game)Con-An endless grind of repetitive content with no visible End Game Goal. Just Grind for credits and increase your Vector (aka Character Level)-NO STORY-Core Mechanics are not explained (Seriously, what does increasing your Vector do?; What is the difference between Armor and Shields)-Game is designed for “4-man arty group play” but core group play features are broken (why disband a party after every mission?) or not Explained (Do High Level Vectors get scaled down?)-Game is designed for “4-man group play” BUT the best way to grind credits in SOLOing (or at BEST, DUOing)-Little to no QA Testing or Balancing. The Outdoor Maps are clearly more difficult than the indoor Maps. The attacks of Overseer Boss (and mini-boss) are way too powerful.-Deceptive Marketing Practices. In the US, and item needs to be Sold for 10 days at its base price BEFORE any sales can be offers. Offering a 20% on Day 1 is very misleading (aka deceptive) Yes Steam Seems to allow this practice but it does not make it ethical.ConclusionI played 20 hours of this game and not all was bad. BUT making a person grind 20 hours just to discover there is NO end game is unforgivable. It is still unclear if this game will be going the route of DLCs or Micro-transactions. REGARDLESS, I feel that anyone that have purchased the “Early Access” version of this game deserves a free copy of the first DLC (assuming it is comparable price to the base copy).

_childDocuments_.review: Every negative review I see is posted by someone with less than 5 hours of game-play and has little-to-no idea of how the game really works, i'm going to simplify some things to negate the negative reviews. (I'll update my review as the game progresses or if I see anymore uninformative negative reviews)It's pretty rare you will find Weapons, Support Gear, or Prototype Gear (things used for your character). But, you will find a lot of resources and currency which are used for the shops to buy gear and upgrade that gear. The loot system is fine, eventually they will add more overall gear, resources, etc.I see a lot of people complain that level 10 gear is the same as level 40 gear. Wrong. Base stats of weapons will increase little by little. It's actually hard to notice, but your Vector scales downwards not upwards. As a level 20 vector you will do no damage in a level 60 vector mission but will do the same damage as a level 10 vector in a level 10 vector mission. This is why your gear stats increase very little, by the time you have gear from level 120 you will crush level 10 missions (depending on your gear alone). There are Common, Rare, Epic, and Legendary gear. The higher tier of gear the more upgrades and better stats that gear will have, along with it being more expensive to upgrade. This gear levels your vector up and allows you to progress to more intense and higher level missions.You start as Vector level 5, these levels indicate if you are able to do a contract or not. Contracts vary between level 5-150. Your gear is what levels your vector level. Inside each contract you level up to level 1-10 and select skills (moba style) you don't keep your upgrades or skills after each contract, they reset, but you keep your gear and resources you earned. You use this to buy and upgrade your gear to progress your vector level so you can do more difficult contracts and find better and more loot.People seem to rush quickly to say something negative without understanding how the game really works.I have played many MOBAs and many RPGs. I still play Diablo 2 to this day, these games are my bread and butter and it seems people aren't really giving the game a chance or taking the time to understand it.THIS GAME IS EARLY ACCESS, for the asking price it is 100% worth it, especially with friends. I believe in the developers to add more content. For it being EA, there are little bugs, the graphics and game-play are smooth, and the lighting and difficulty of each contract is nice. You may lag, FPS drop, or other things, but that comes with EA as the game isn't finished being optimized. I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is in general very fun, the graphics are great, the mechanics well thought out. It plays like a mix of diablo, mobas and a bit of dark scifi like warframe. The maps vary between good looking and absolutely stunning. Some are rather flat but others, particularly those set in spaceships, look truly 3D. One problem here is that the resource colleciton points are very hard to spot as they can be obstructed by items on the map. Having gear with loot detection helps but is not ideal.Now for the bad:- Game crashes repeatedly both under Windows and under Linux (emulated on Proton-GE)- Abilities will sometimes not trigger or trigger only partially. Shurikens (Cass) might hit enemies but the teleport will not work.- Nothing is really explained. Some random encounters on the maps like the guy in a manhole really do not make sense without the game telling you what the deal is- Enemy design can be atrocious and frustrating. This is also why I cannot recommend this game until this is fixed. Enemies can and will stunlock you to death and 1-hk you repeatedly. This turns the entire game into a gambling simulator. "Maybe I will not encounter enemy X and live, maybe I will and then I will be forced to restart the map as there is nothing that I can do to not die". If those deaths could be avoided through skill or gear, it would be tolerable, but they cannot. This is really bad game design and simply should never happen. I hope the devs will rethink and fix some enemy designs.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the ARPG genre and this Science Fiction themed dungeon crawler looks to be promising. Cleared two Maps so far and I feel that the combat is fluid and punchy. More than Diablo meets Destiny, I'd like to think that this is an ARPG take on Borderlands due to the quirky cast of classes currently available, and from the looks of it more will be added in as the game get further developed. I liked the fact that there are only a limited number of moves for each character -- think of it as Risk of Rain with an ultimate skill as a cherry on top. I am guessing that level cap will be much higher in the final build because even if the variety is assured on every contract, ten levels might be just a bit too short an experience. Inventory management is on the simple side now, but I'm guessing there's more work to be had in that department. Hope to see more interesting things in terms of gear. Currently armor is purely cosmetic and you only get to equip the character's weapons and accessories. Aside from that hope there will be more mobs and maps to look forward too. Not a bad early access buy.Oh, a map or an improvement on the existing mini map will be plus points too.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get the negative reviews. This is a good ARPG in early access. It's definitely better than Diablo 3 was when it was first released, and this game is still in pretty early access. Are there things to work on? Yes, but the devs are engaged and have a road map published of their current goals. If you aren't willing to play an incomplete game, don't buy early access. Also, very unsure how this game is being compared at all to Destiny except that it is in a sci-fi setting.The good - -Built in easy to find multiplayer. Drop in/out multiplayer is enabled with public match making. -RPG style character progression for each class, as well as multiple types of equipment that can be purchased along the way to increase your players overall power including abilities.-Ability power ups achieved in each mission in the style of Heroes Of the Storm or MOBA style games.-Beautiful sci-fi environments with enemies to match.-Challenging game play that encourages multi-player, though so far it is doable though sometimes difficult in single player.-In game quests that have lore to them (and a TLDR section)-Quick, engaging combat with enemies visibly reacting when attacked. -A clean, good looking UI.-Multiple enemy types in every mission.-Game is played well on M/K or controller.What can be improved - -There is something about the graphics currently that is ever so slightly grainy. This is common in  early access games though, it just needs a bit more polish. -More classes is always a good thing, but they have it published on their road map that a new class is already scheduled to come out.-Unsure how end game is currently. I'm hoping they have end-game content that allows for continued character development and increased replay-ability. A brief discussion of end game content should be noted on the Steam page. Edit: After playing a few more hours, I've found a few tips to make it a better experience. -The game hasn't yet had anisotropic filtering added. I recommend manually adding it via your graphics card profile setting for individual settings (such as NVidia Control Panel). It makes a big difference in the clarity of the images. -The drop/in out for multiplayer is some of the best I've seen. When you join a friends game, you join right besides them and it auto-levels you for that mission to the exact spot they are at, so there is no power gap if you come in late. While I haven't personally tried it, I very much would think this is the same for public match making if you join a match mid-progress.-All loot is able to be picked up by all team members, with the exception of medpacks. The game is a lot of fun, and if you like team based ARPG's this one is good. The balance is good, the dodging, abilities, and basic attacks are smooth and accurate. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've seen quite a few reviews bashing the game and thought I'd give my input.Overall, the game is very well polished for early access, lack of content is there but the early access has been running for 1-2 weeks, there is a road map setup for the games development to show when they are looking to have further content. The gear levels that people say "do nothing" actually mean something, and the actual mechanic of it is great. You have a Vector score which is essentially Gear Score (GS from here after) which when progressing furthers your damage against HIGHER vector contracts/missions. They have a cap on the damage you deal in lower missions to prevent you just going in and carrying everyone, but if you have say 50 GS going into a 90 GS mission, you will do 1-2 damage per hit, so the gear progression IS relevant.There are minor bugs and hitches, which can be expected in an early access game, chat has been introduced and bug fixes are deployed when they are ready.Overall - the game has HUGE potential, taking inspirations from the likes of Destiny/Warframe and Heroes of the Storm.

_childDocuments_.review: [Updated 04/12/21, 1.5 months after Full Release]A sci-fi Gauntlet-style arpg. Sometimes bullet hell, sometimes easy cruising.I bought this as it came to store in 2019 and played for ~50h, reinstalled after 2 years and put in another 50.[+] I can say that some progress has been made. Mission selection is a bit easier. There are some cosmetics you can equip on top of your chosen skin.[~] There are rudimentary quests (kill this enemy x times, finish this contract y times).[~] There is a slot for a new type of item, talisman, which you first need to assemble (rng from many missions) and then 'level up' by having it equipped. At max level, it provides a passive boon. Before you max it out, it actively hurts you.. like a challenge mode? But you cannot reset it, so it will become a buff eventually anyway? Then why.. eh, forget it.[-] There are new enemy types, that range from 'annoying to fight' to 'punch the wall'. Some of them deal insane damage compared to older enemies. One has huge knockback projectile attacks (you will get knocked down, there is no outplaying this). One flies outside your field of view and shoots projectiles. One inflicts 'confusion' (up<->down, left<->right), which is a death sentence. Especially because...[-] Status effects and their duration are unclear. Especially when fighting a large group of enemies. DoTs are easy enough to distinguish, but sometimes I'm unable to dodge for a while? Is it because...[-] Skills straight up do not work sometimes(?). At least partly because...[-] Bugs that have been reported months ago (before 'Full Release') are still there.I want to like this game, but there are more lows than highs. Mostly just 'meh'.

The few times I was able to play with others, the missions were enjoyable and I felt like I was improving my gear (vector level). But I'd say 85% of the time, there is no one else playing the early missions.

_childDocuments_.review: Chasing loot and murdering space bugs are, of course, the best things to do online with your friends. Killsquad has all of that in a kind of sci-fi hack`n`slash package.It's a top down, co-op action RPG where you run missions with your friends as possibly psychotic bounty hunters always on the hunt for bigger and better weapons and gear. It's got a Diablo-style isometric view, but with a colorful sci-fi setting and tons of fast action and dodge-rolling.Unpleasantly, you're always in the employ of some evil space corporation, which hires 'killsquads' to pillage riches and tech from their rivals. But in the process, you'll be finding better guns and materials to make those guns better yet. It's the loot-shooter reward loop, but with a lovely action-RPG presentation. What's not to like?.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty, comfortable, and obviously passionate; a nice lazy co-op action game. But god, god does it ever sorely need gameplay-oriented content, because it suffers in the exact same way its competitor Darksburg does: it needs more abilities and ability customization, more diverse gear and gear effects. It's solid where it is now, but with how little you can really alter any of the few characters' playstyles, and how little you can diversify yourself with say a team of one character, it becomes routine entirely too fast.I love relaxing in this, but it really needs more game to it. You don't even need more characters if you just spread out the idea of that ability tree. Go wild, do some psycho Grim Dawn kind of ability depth. This game desperately needs more complexity to hook for more than just a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a "hold button to press button" game.Every part of the game seems designed to be as clunky as possible and you'll be playing the radar if you play a ranged character. You can't just click something, you need to click and hold buttons that should just be a click.Want to zoom out? Too bad! it just changes the camera angle to cut off more of the screen.Want to equip a weapon from the left side inventory to the right side character? Click and drag right? Wrong.You click the gun, then click the equip button, then click the weapon slot.Want to play the game? Too bad, you get a cutscene of your squad standing around and then standing to attention. Its a second wasted for no gameplay reason. It allows the textures to load (which you can see fade-pop in)after the loading screen which should have just loaded them.Want to finish the mission and move on? Too bad, stand around for 20 seconds. Oh and have another cutscene where you pose dramatically for no reason. Again, another second or 2 that the game wastes.Want to equip the cool stuff you just got? Too bad, you need to watch a little animation where it shows you the item you just got like it was a loot box, but without any useful stats to compare, literally just an image. Want to dodge the enemies attacks? Too bad, they attack from off screen and not all of them have the developers crutch of telegraphing attacks, aka massive red markers. Have some random damage you couldn't dodge or block purely because the camera can't see them. Want to explore a map to find hidden goodies? Goodluck guessing what is a path or not, because the radar isn't a map. There isn't any map.Oh and pray the map doesn't head south. You can't see where you are going. Same with enemies attacking from there.You can't even press escape to back out of the options menu. It just closes the menu and when you open it, it opens to the place you just tried to leave. No. You need to click the back button way at the bottom of the screen.Frankly, it feels like it was made by someone who uses the term "streamlinier" that doesn't know what "streamlined" even means. Its like they thought the word "cool" meant "waiting". Same with suspense. And tension. TLDR.Aiming sucks, enemies suck, menu's suck, many buttons waste your time for no reason and it has some of the weirdest character progression i've seen. Its unfortunate because under all that there is a neat game. Its just interacting with it sucks.The only way the interface could be worse is if in Multiplayer they make the camera shared like Helldivers. Which I haven't tested yet.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun twin stick style RPG shooter. It has good missions and looks good. There are some Quality of Life issues, primarily this is a game where you build a large gear set and swap gear depending on your mission. This mission a fire weapon is better, this one acid, this one kinetic, etc. While you can carry 2 weapons there are 4 types, and your armors and support items ALSO can compound that functionality. SO when you go looking for a mission to play, you see people on a mission you want to join, only to realize you have to now back out of mission search, go into your inventory and entirely re-equip your character. It'd be super nice if you could just select an option to "Auto Equip" the optimum items for a given mission, I can't tell you how annoying it is to join a mission just to realize you're dealing reduced damage to enemies because you didn't take 3 minutes to entirely re-equip before joining a mission. This aside, it's fun to play and the missions are only 10 or so minutes so you can jump in for a few games and then quit without any lost of investment. No long gaming sessions required here.

_childDocuments_.review: The Best way I can describe this game is think of Helldivers meets with Dauntless and you have this game. Just take the best core aspects of both.+ Twin-Stick of Helldivers but more emphasized with ARPG combat style.+ Semi-Generated Linear levels.+ Easy to you MoBA style level progression each mission. Level 1-10. Skills are simple and effective.+ Winning, Rewards, and MVP are much like Dauntless' version.+ Potential for crafting in the future (not currently implemented that I've seen). You will have to grind out certain missions and bosses.+ Loot is simple, 3 pieces to exchange - Weapon, Primary Gear Piece, Secondary Gear Piece. _childDocuments_.review: Good grindy fun!Was looking for something new to play and looked at the recently released "The Ascent" but some of the reviews turned me off of it. The aesthetic looked great, but I was looking for something challenging and a little grindy, with good weapon variety.The amount of builds aren't astounding, there's probably 20 good builds for each of the five characters, and about 20 actually not super different guns that work into those builds. Add random modifiers to those guns, some talismans, support, and prototype gear and you have enough to imagine the build you want and keep rolling to try and find itThe action is good. The character you play's moveset isn't all that crazy, but there's proper ways to play it, and it's satisfying optimizing your aoes.  Speaking of aoes, if you like not standing in the lava this game has plenty of it. In the good fights as much as 90% of the floor may be lava. They saved all the crazy movesets for the bosses. It's not the most original videogame in the world. You'll notice tons of references and homage to other games, most notably overwatch. Some of the UI reminds me of warframe.Speaking of warframe, this game is not nearly as grindy. In fact you can just kinda party up with someone above you, have them drag you through one of their levels, and as long as they get you up to open the chest at the end, you'll jump up about 30 levels. This is a feature of the gameThat leads to this game's biggest problem. It's not popular. I'm not sure why, it's not some mindblowing revelation, but its good honest fun at a reasonable price. Did the dev sacrifice a baby to satan or something im not aware of? Either way, yes, you can play this game solo, but it is much more fun to play with others. It spawns more enemies and more types and you can get so many more numbers up on screen. I really do recommend playing with others. Thankfully, when you're selecting a mission, if there's a poker chip up top, you can just click join and be playing with others as easy as that. All in all, it's good fun

_childDocuments_.review: Killsquad is a good attempt at merging a few ideas from other genres and coming up with an arcade-style isometric shooter with a loot grind. The action loop is solid, and the high enemy count makes for some frantic action that merges quick ability activation with the player’s own skill. It falls short in some elements, such as no end game content and a loot grind that is too focused on the shop rather than rewards through contracts, and could do with a better diverse set of abilities and weapons for each character. Still, this is a game that is easy to jump into, and even if the end game does not exist, taking the game as an experience from the first to the last contract is good enough to recommend, think of it as an isometric shooter rather than an action RPG. One thing though is that make sure you have yourself a friendly bounty hunter or three to come along with you to get the best experience from this entertaining, blaster action game.
