_childDocuments_.review: Update: I think the Core 2 changes to skills are definitely a step in the right direction for build variety, although it makes the early game a lot less fun, something I didn't really think about until playing the new character with no level up options available at all the first mission. I do want to say that the game introduces variety pretty quickly, I'm not at the endgame yet, but once you start getting to the plague missions at vector 50 or so, things heat up really quickly. so don't get too turned off by the initial slowness. There is more enemy variety later on, and rarer items can create a few interesting builds. But overall I think content and build variety is still a weak point, and the game is still smaller in scope than a lot of ARPG's people tend to compare to. With that out of the way, the rest of the review is still pretty relevant.I recommend this game specifically to ARPG fans who are looking for some creativity in a relatively stagnant and niche genre. It really exposes how dated the moment-to-moment gameplay of its older competitors is (like POE and Grim Dawn). It's not going to match the more mature ARPG's on the market in terms of content, and there skill trees are pretty narrow for each of the 4 characters. But it also won't weigh your wallet down as much either at the sale price of $14, and might even delight you with some very different design approaches. So if you're out there looking for the next big ARPG to "fill the void", you need to lower your expectations a bit or you're going to be disappointed. This is a smaller game by an indie studio and is not going to give you a hundred hours of content. But that's why it's also considerably cheaper.Killsquad is a refreshingly different approach to the genre in my opinion, with a higher emphasis on digestible play sessions and fluid gameplay. Your items are persistent but your skill choices reset every mission, allowing you to try a variety of playstyles in bite-sized packages rather than having to slam hours of grind per character to experience what a build is like. You'll lose some of that sense of progression, but you stand to gain more variety and experimentation. It's fast paced but also requires skill and forces you to use all your moves on rotation as opposed to just spamming the lone move that you "invested" in (looking at you path of exile).Itemization right now is a little thin and the early game grind feels more prohibitive than I would like, but the core gameplay is very fun, especially in coop. There is matchmaking, but it's pretty thin in the early levels. New enemies are added to the mix in a trickle but things do heat up later on and the fights become hectic in a way that other arpg's don't match, for a variety of reasons. For one, enemies kill you slower in this game, but enemies die slower as well. The reason this doesn't stop the game from being fast-paced is because the enemies are fast, the screen goes bullet-hell very quickly, and player characters are extremely mobile and often have plenty of i-frames to work with. The game is still pretty thin on the story/lore side of things, but that's usually not a deal breaker for ARPG players. Lastly I'd say the game has felt considerably less buggy since the CORE update.

The medic's beam attack gets blocked by the telegraph indicator of some attacks.All of the bosses have MMO-esque mechanics where you have to avoid telegraphed abilities, sometimes hitting them with those abilities to knock them out of something bigger. As a WoW/FF14 veteran, those were actually kind of fun to learn, and had the proper dopamine hit on a win. The downside to those, though, is that those bosses can be invulnerable during portions of their fight and, if their fight script breaks during that invuln time, you end up with an unkillable enemy that's just sitting there. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for April 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before May 3rd, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A Moba with more RPG elements. Killsquad brings Moba style gameplay to a PVE style game. Players take on short contracts which last about ten minutes. Each contract has players fighting through hordes of monsters with different tasks and a final boss on each level. The levels feel more scripted than the usual style of these games, with a focus on a progression with the players earning loot and leveling up. There are five characters in this game, and I took the melee tank for my hour. While most characters are geared towards range attack, I found the tank to be pretty strong and interesting to control. The action was intense, and the only part I struggled with was when I got distracted from a primary goal, but I also had a great time throughout. Pick this up if you like MOBAs, yes this does have elements of an Action RPG and an inventory system, but this game is unapologetically a MOBA, and it works for it. I enjoyed my time, though I will mention that some people do find this game to get more repetitive as time goes on, but in my first hour, I was engaged, and normally I’m not a huge fan of MOBAs. _childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a ton of the game as of this review (2.1 hrs total). I do however, think that is enough time for me to say whether or not I recommend a game or not. The biggest question you're probably wondering is if this game is fun or not. The answer to that is yes. The game is very fun. The game has a really nice Diablo 3 feel to it that I really enjoy. It's not overly complicated in the beginning like some of these other ARPG's. You dive straight in and begin killing monsters, and I really enjoy that about this game. There's never really a boring moment to the game, as you are constantly in the action. Each character does feel unique, ranging with different abilities and wielding different weapons. I personally prefer melee builds, so I play with the melee characters. The two main melee characters in the game wield different weapons. One holds a sword, the other holds a war-hammer. Then there are two other characters, one wielding dual pistols, and the other holding some sort of grenade launcher, I believe. They all feel unique in their own way. I also really respect that the devs have a road-map of what they plan on doing with the game. This is more of an indie studio, so going into it expecting it to be Diablo 4 isn't really reasonable or logical. However, what these devs have done with this game, is amazing. I think it does compare to Diablo in the ARPG sense, but it is unique enough in it's own way, that it puts me in the mind of Monster Hunter, because of being dropped into a mini area and collecting resources and then of course, Diablo, because it is an ARPG after all. Is the game perfect? No, but for this to be an indie title with devs continuously updating the game, I'm sure it can come close to it in the future. For the price, this game is a steal. Verdict: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Killsquad is an interesting blend of Victor Vran and Helldivers in how it plays moment-to-moment. Structure-wise it also borrows a bit from Warframe, Destiny and Diablo 3's Adventure Mode. There is even a splash of MOBA in there!This game may not provide you that action-RPG fix if you are dead set on getting a traditional, Diablo-esque ARPG experience. It is a lot more focused on the action dimension. The controls are direct input, not click to move or attack. There's also an emphasis on co-op play. Without much in the way of a story campaign or lore, the narrative texture is rather flat at the moment. So the enjoyment comes from grouping up and hitting up series of contracts to grind resources.IF you are down for this kind of gameplay loop, can be patient for more features to get fleshed out and can handle the usual Early Access glitches, then Killsquad can be a hell of a good time. It manages to accommodate both short hits of play and longer grind sessions. However RPG nuts who love to theory craft may not yet have enough meat on the bones. The gear system is paired down from its contemporaries, with not a whole lot to differentiate yourself from other players in terms of build customization.

_childDocuments_.review: My little DreamativityTo join Demanding bloodYou need to killTo pay the billWith targets blood..You've joined !When I first time saw this game, it reminded me of the Master X Master (MxM) project from NC Soft that was closed. I tried to find anything similar, at least one aspect-wise (PvE or PvP). So. I was excited to find Killsquad and immediately added it to my wishlist. WASD movement, skills, action-based gameplay, interesting bosses with cool mechanics akin to MMORPG as FFXiV, for example - that is what I marked for myself from the trailer. To add to that I marked the points from the store page: a rich universe and heroes' customization, so I expected some lore, skills customizations, and skins. Didn't see any info about progression, but I thought that the game would have some sort of it since the devs already wrote this 'Then, on each level up, you get an opportunity to customize your character with new skills to adapt to your play style.'But, when I first watched a stream on the store page, I caught myself with the thought that the game looked empty and too repetitive even if we talk about session-based projects. But, my love for MxM and my desire to find something similar convinced me to try the game, since I always could ask for a refund.So, what the game can offer in my opinion:UPDATE (After the Core update):* Good visuals and nice animations. Killsquad looks good. The first several times, it's cool to watch all those skills' animations or enemies' actions. POSITIVE UPDATE - almost the same, some features were added - cool and nice, but not well optimized.* Combat and gameplay - I liked it a lot. The feeling from MxM indeed. Fast action is where you need to watch your steps, use coordination, and see patterns in boss mechanics. POSITIVE UPDATE - The same as was before if we talk about the basic gameplay. Different tasks are cool as well - defend or escort. But I want to see more of such tasks. More such contracts, while there are most of them, are just to kill, and yet we're killing creeps all the way at any contract anyway.* I want to say a good word about UI as well. It's simple, comfortable to use, and stylish at the same time. POSITIVE UPDATE - The same.* Enemies and tactics: it's interesting to fight. There are cool tactics, especially on bosses, or those chaotic 'environment hazards' such as lasers.. Really cool! Move, move, attack, and move again :D It's not boring when you are in this process. Good action, but not much variety. I counted 22 unique archetypes of mobs in the bestiary. There are more than 22 different creatures but there are just some small variations such as 'Space Worm', 'Toxic Space Worm', and 'Fire Space Worm' (not names from the game just an example). UPDATE - I deleted the writings that are not actual anymore. There is still some problem with variety, but it's not as it was before since mobs are feeling different with unique attacks, aoe, etc. The Bosses are awesomely made! Wanna see more of them. The playthrough is hard for me and my soulmate, and we like it a lot! POSITIVE (Up from mixed)* Progression system. The game offers Vector - the progression well-known as ilvl. And it's used just to get contracts of a higher and more difficult tier. Account heroes' progressions were added with some rewards. Also, factions with levels and rewards as well. It's much better now, though not enough rewards in my opinion. MIXED (Up from negative)UPDATE - I rewrote this almost entirely since new features were added and the old ones were changed.* Customization. You can upgrade skills while you are on a mission. Perks on 2,4,8 and 10 levels and ult to choose from 2 on 6 levels. Similar to Hots or Dota system with ults and talents trees. However, it resets once you complete the contract. So, you need to level up every contract, and you can choose different perks depending on that. I don't have any problems with that, honestly. I wrote above about heroes and account leveling. You can open avatars, badges, and skins. There are not many skins right now and part of them are just re-skin, but, again, much better than it was before. In December, new skins and customization features were promised. Will see about that. MIXED (Up from negative)  UPDATE - I rewrote this almost entirely since new features were added and old ones were changed.* Areas are nice and biomes are different and unique. But, as it was with enemies, it's too repetitive.  MIXED - UPDATE - They changed the system and now zones are not randomly generated but have pre-made maps from the same Biomes as before. I like it more than it was before. Though I would prefer more biomes and zones.* 'A rich universe' - Some lore was added, quests, new descriptions. Not much and only for the novice contracts. The writing isn't good and not to my taste. But at least there is a feeling of some purpose now. MIXED (Up from negative) UPDATE - I rewrote this almost entirely since new features were added and old ones were changed.* Killsquad doesn't have any hub. Just a lobby like Dota or LoL or else. It's not that bad I think but not good for me as well. MxM had a nice hub where people could look at each other and communicate, buy some gear, etc. This game is different, yes. So, I expected something similar to the Helldivers bridge - a hub for you and your teammates. MIXED UPDATE - The same.* Loot. I don't have problems with what I have while on contracts - some mats, and currencies. I didn't expect it akin to arpg that everyone talking about because for me, it was obvious that it's not that type of game. POSITIVE (Up from mixed) UPDATE - There is more variety with the weapons and additional gear. Also, they added consumables with different effects. Weapons now have elemental perks. It's fun, but I want to see different effects, not just elemental damage. Or a better description. But I like it now. Plus, talismans should be added in the December update. * Heroes - 2 ranged and 2 melees. I would say that there is no Mage type. Tank with a hammer, melee DD with a sword, Support with a gun, and dual-pistol range DD. Nothing special. But I liked the skills and the talents tree options. But... The skill and perks system is not deep and kinda dull. MIXED UPDATE - The same. Need more heroes. One new hero in 3 years (should be added the next fall) - it's kinda poor. * Sound - you know, I almost didn't mention it. And, when we're talking about music, it's a not good song for me. I don't mind heroes' voices from the VA library since they almost don't talk. But I like a good soundtrack while fighting and doing missions. MIXED UPDATE - The December update will contain a new soundtrack. Will see. Nothing new for now. * Technical moments. The game does not have good optimization. And some bugs. For example, you can't see your after-run statistics almost every time.  MIXED UPDATE - I rewrote this entirely.* More in comments *

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game with a lot of cool aspects to it. It has unique classes that all play differently, some build diversity for each character (some). As well as a fun gameplay loop. I especially like how you mostly gear up through the store by getting currency through missions to use in the store to up your gear. This really fits the idea that you work as a mercenary to make dough and use that cash to increase your power level. The basic loop of the game is to choose one of the 5 playable characters, and start at low level missions and work your way to higher difficulty missions through progressing your gear. There is a small skill tree, two weapon slots, two gear slots, and two talisman slots, along with 3 item slots for all characters. When you start a new character you will need to start back from low level stuff; the only thing that carries over to different characters are materials, money, and usable items like health kits. This game also heavily reminds me of MasterXMaster, so if you know what that was and enjoyed it, you will like this. I recommend this game, especially for the price it's at currently ($16).Now, for the stuff I don't like so they can be taken into consideration:For some reason, they give you the ability to equip two weapons at once and switch between them. This sounds alright at first, but there is only one weapon type for each character and the only difference between new weapons is the damage and element type. Each mission already has a "best element" for that mission so there is no reason to ever use a secondary weapon.Speaking of missions, there is really not too much variety in the maps themselves. You mainly play in the exact same couple of maps, with different mission objectives for different missions, but the layout is the exact same.Another huge issue I have is the audio; it feels/sounds incredibly flat. when you stand still and no enemies are around the maps are incredibly silent. I believe the fix to this is to add ambiance to the maps like wind and wildlife sounds etc. as well as some better audio balancing all together.Finally, I have issues where i need to close the game after a few hours because of large memory leaks causing the game to stutter and freeze heavily. When I look in task manager i see the memory MB for the game reach upwards of 11,000.00 MBDespite the issues I do still recommend for a fun time for a low price, especially if you have plans to squad up or even play with randoms.Edit: So after some more play time I have noticed a few things: firstly, their is a small amount of ambiance in maps, but it still really doesn't feel like your "there" in the map. There's definitely something missing in the audio department.I have also noticed that unlike the other characters, Zero has a reason to have two weapons because some of his weapon choices have variations such as shorter range and overcharging.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. It certainly looks like it could be a fun game to blast through enemies, complete objectives, and get sweet loot, ala something like Warframe, and it does make good strides to do so with some neat heroes with fun synergistic abilities as well as cool enemies with lots of attacks and good animation telegraphs.But at the moment, I find it only fun in concept, not in execution. The game just feels like it is both significantly lacking polish and lacking good design for a game of its nature:*Levels feel very repetitive and slow due to boring construction and the same vapid, cliche and unfunny story lines being spouted each time you play it: reminds me of Borderlands where it keeps pausing you from having fun to deliver its incredibly stupid jokes. Playing the toxic fog level, for example, was hell in that it forces you to listen to so much dumb dialogue and forces you to go through an incredibly repetitive sequence with the same enemies over and over.*Combat feedback from your attacks feels very dull, muted, and unsatisfying (without the numbers popping up, I seriously wouldn't even believe I'm hitting them), and enemy attacks can be very vague and hard to react/discern despite the (over)use of telegraphs (typically they just add too much visual clutter).*The heroes can get annoying with the way they keep making the same limited number of quips over and over. Also while their abilities can be nice, they just in general feel very uninspired and don't have any level of camaraderie or personality.*The game feels confusing to play with so much being thrown at you with no explanation and levels having unclear directions and objectives that can awkwardly malfunction. For example, there can sometimes be these awkward pauses where a door is blocking your way with no way to open it: you head back, expecting to find another route, but no, you go back to the door again and now suddenly you can open it.*And the game is general just barely seems to be holding itself together with the way it spazzes out sometimes, particularly in the ending screen of a game where the icons and information just keep fading in and out.As said, I want to like it. Despite the incredibly janky feeling of the game, I did somewhat like cutting through enemies and bosses as Cass and Troy and the others. If at the very least the levels didn't feel so repetitive (which is a big killer considering how much the game wants you to grind them over and over) and the combat felt more satisfying with better damage feedback and sounds and so on (seriously, the sound is super lacking), this might've been a win for me. Perhaps they can fix it up with patches.

I think a bit overdone on these ones IMO (achievements);>Not all classes have that "fun" factor attached to it (may vary between players);I'm happy for what is in the game and hopefully they will listen to the community and implement some well desired optimizations.This game is only missing a horde mode of non-stopping enemies where you have to run/retreat/push through/defend until you reach a threshold or a score with increasing difficulties, even create a top score list every week and give away in-game prizes, like a legendary weapon or a slick cosmetic, just something for bragging rights.

_childDocuments_.review: This could be a good game, I like the idea / formula of it and the latest update is good but I'd like to see the devs prioritise the following:1) Sounds designThe sound design for Troy's pistols is like a "pop" "pop" and sounds terrible and doesn't feel impactful at all. I wish it sounded something like similar to other sci fi games (e.g. hawkmoon from Destiny).2) Embrace more RPG elementsYou can't have a MOBA style  game with only 4 classes and you'll never be able to add heaps of classes (MOBA style) and balance them with a small studio.2A) Have some sort of customisation beyond the level up skills. e.g. Some sort of passive tree would be cool which has skills which unlocks every 10 vector level or something. I don't mind selecting the skills based on each mission but some sort of tree for a sense of progression would be good. Passives like +10% standard attack dmg or something along those lines. Doesn't have to be super complex like POE.2b) Have armour as well and not just primary and secondary weapons and the other slots. Make the armour change the characters appearance.3) Focus less on the graphic upgradesIt already looked amazing. I don't care much about the graphics at the moment for where the game is at (early access) - they already looked great before this latest update and now they look even better but still, focus on your core gameplay first before adding all that polish. 4) The pacing of levels is weirdSometimes the enemies jump from level 1 to level 6 right away. I sometimes wonder what I missed and go back and I didn't miss anything it just jumps randomly. I also want early vector levels to be easier so I feel progression. I go back and it's still slow to complete as when I was lower vector.5) Loot is boringFalls into the trap of buying a higher level weapons but with bad stats. I hate that, let me customise / re-roll the stats or something with currency. Why do I have to get bad stats to get to a (required) higher level? Doesn't make sense was a lame thing about Destiny 2. You wanted a higher level but you have to change from a fun weapon / weapon with good stats. No thanks. Frustrating.6) Add a mini map or tab overlay map like in ARPG's I see dot on the map with "220M" but it's weird and I get lost. Just add a mini map please.7) Add AI.There are low player numbers (which is a shame, good game) add some AI at least so solo isn't so painful.Overall love the sci fi setting, you don't see much of that. You've got a winner on your hands if you make it work IMO. There are no other new sci fi ARPGs on the market (well that Warhammer one but they have a weird clunky engine and terrible camera / controls).

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 for an Early access game!This game is awesome, I've enjoyed playing it far more then I expected! The devs are very good at responding to user feedback in the discord channel (highly recommend you join it if you play). The game is updated very often generally at least once a week, there is constant progress towards bigger goals (more content, smoother networking, fixing bugs etc).Now onto the actual gameplay, there are 4 classes and all of them are unique in their gameplay styles (with more to come) if you enjoy a top down shooter, it has 2 characters that scratch that itch (troy and zero) and if you prefer more of the hack and slash style melee then it also has that in Cass and Kosmos (Cass being my favorite) I won't spoil the way each character works but is is very satisfying to master them, and once you start collecting gear with the right passives for your intended play style is blooms into even more awesomeness. It IS early access but to be honest it gets more updates then most ea games I've played and feels like it has a solid direction which it is constantly progressing towards. I'm very glad it exists because I've been wanting a more quick paced top down arpgish style game and this has  filled that role for me. Once the progression system is more fleshed out I can see myself sinking countless hours into this game to de-stress. It's fun to play it as it grows since it has a pretty fast pace considering the team size. There can be some dead time where it's hard to find people but that's the nature of playing a game in such a non-mainstream niche as this is, and I feel like it will only grow as time goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat premise. Could be cool with more characters and better progression.Pros:ARPG top-down gameplay (if you like that sort of thing)Cons:Boring items. Buy new items that give you minor buffs, like +20% experience or +1 second of skill duration.Zero sense of progressionNot an ARPG, at all.Regarding progression: you basically reset level each time you start a contract. As you progress, you pick talents to upgrade your skills, taking a page directly from Heroes of the Storm. This would be an okay mechanic if this were a rogue-like or a competitive multiplayer game. It's not either of those things though. It feels like playing bot matches in LoL or HotS, except with fancier graphics.I've seen a few others compare the game to games like Helldivers; it's nowhere near as good as Helldivers. Helldivers had a decent progression mechanic and your loadout progressively got better.  You weren't reverted to using a pistol at the start of every game.They took the worst aspects of multiplayer MOBAs, combined them with a top down action game (NOT an ARPG) and smashed them together to create Killsquad.Go play bot matches in any MOBA instead. At least that way you'll unlock some skins or something.

_childDocuments_.review: Written based on Early Access version 0.6.2.It's a fun Online Co-op ARPG themed game with a MOBA-like skill tree (Best example is Heroes of the Storm with its level-up skill selection tiers separated by every 4 levels [every 2 levels in this game]) with somewhat linear instances with varying missions. The game is still in Early Access, and the roadmap provided in their Dev Diary does look promising although I'm unsure if it will be based on paid season passes (based on how the roadmap was named, I think there's a possibility of paid seasons later). Killsquad has great potential to be one of the fun ARPG Co-op games you play with a group of friends  the developers provide constant  with added variety in maps/missions/character customization. Currently I cannot really get myself to play the game more than 1-2 hours per day because while it's fun, I still get the feeling that it gets sort of repetitive due to the grinding nature of the game with a rather slow progression system. And with probably a limited selection of mission variations with maps that look almost identical to the previous one you've played, I can imagine it will get old real fast if you don't pace yourself and burn yourself out. I'd imagine once I've encountered all the boss fights more than ten times (if I'm being generous), it'll probably get extremely boring. I can understand the slow grind implementation is necessary since the content is still rudimentary for a mission-based ARPG, but that's essentially how the game feels as of right now (version 0.6.2). What I personally think would make it more fun:- More randomized variables in a mission, such as mobs with affixes similar to Diablo/PoE/Grim's version of Elite/Rare mobs with special buffs/debuffs [ex: Mobs projectile attack bounces off walls, Mobs attack that hit successfully causes player to be slowed, etc]- An expanded skill-tree for current roster as well as future roster as it feels somewhat simplified and feels somewhat flat. (i.e. Since the game is so similar to Heroes of the Storm's talent tree system for level-tiered skills, things like Quest-based skills ). Adding more variety and expanding on early-focused to late-focused skill selections would add more of a spice to the current setup.- Side-quests within a mission. Could be implemented with ideas such as a bounty-board that gets updated globally for the community and parties can strive to complete it, where if a certain number of successful missions is reached by community, the entire community (that participated) gets a small buff and/or items (could be cosmetics too). - Puzzles/Labyrinth - An optional section in a map that has a chance of spawning where players can challenge to solve a puzzle within a set period of time, to doing survival gauntlets, to just dodging all sorts of projectiles/traps to get to an objective that gives you a unique reward either in the form of (limited buff for duration for the day, to some unique item that people can strive for a chance of farming). The list could go on, but hopefully the developers can take the best elements from various genres/games that they took inspiration from to make a fun game that will have a high replay value with frequent updates.I'm skipping listing bugs/issues I've run into since it looks like others have listed it in their reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: I just wanna chime in and say I am glad that after the initial wave of reviews from people who didn't seem to understand what an Early Access game was, the reviews since have been far more positive and understanding. I sat down and played five hours with my friend yesterday, our plan was to only play an hour or two just to give the different heroes a try but we were just having too much fun to stop. That same friend was the one who got me into ARPGs but I have been struggling to find a new ARPG to fill my time with after I exhausted everything Diablo 3 had to offer about eight times over. I have tried out other popular ARPGs like Grim Dawn and PoE but that old school style of ARPG is not for me. I wanted something that has that sense of spectacle, that modern, slick and streamlined feel of Diablo 3 and Killsquad seems to be the answers to my prayers.The game looks, feels and controls fantastically. The controls take a bit of getting used to to begin with, but you'll soon appreciate how tight, streamlined and responsive everything feels. Every one of the awesomely designed heroes is just a simple joy to use, I really like how you pick your skills throughout each mission to keep things mixed up during this time where the game doesn't have a huge wealth of content (yet). This combines the pace, immediacy and urgency of an action game (rather than just point and click with no real dynamic connection to the player) with the joys of loot and it is just a wonderful core loop, that makes you feel like a total badass. The powers are so satisfying to use and feel awesome and just, yeah, this just seems to be the ARPG I have been longing for.  Now for some criticism: Yeah the game has some bugs (most prominent for me was my mouse clicks not registering on menus and one where a certain sound effect would get "stuck" and loop endlessly until I restart the game). I also put the graphics settings up to max and while I don't have a super high end rig, I have a solid rig, so I was disappointed to see some serious frame rate drops. I dunno on whose end that is from or whether it is a server issue or what but it can be a bit annoying during big, chaotic battles, for the frame rate to just drop through the floor essentially locking the game up and usually getting me killed as a result.  It is also worth noting as well that music and sound design is mostly pretty awful, there is this sort of white noise sound that pings to let you know enemies are coming which is very unnecessary, while Troy is a joy to play, like all of the heroes, his guns sound like those automatic airfresheners that pop off once ever half hour and it just takes all the sense of impact away from his shots. Kosmo also has some really rubbish sound effects that don't really fit his moves at all and since you are doing moves dozens of times a Contract, therefore hearing those sounds dozens of times a Contract, it does really become quite irritating over time.  In terms of design decisions I am not a huge fan of, I feel like your health should be way clearer and more prominent on the screen as if you are playing as say... Cass and you're getting stuck in the middle of it all, it is not immediately clear how much danger you are actually in, until you're dead. I am not a huge fan of the map design, too many dead ends and convoluted progression paths and it is far too easy to get separated from the group which can be really frustrating. I also don't like the decision to have enemies spawn from all sides and for them to include environmental hazards because it clashes with the skill system they have in place, on some maps I literally cannot stop for a second to equip any skills and maybe that is designed to add difficulty but it just adds frustration for me. I am also not a hundred percent sure on hero balance, mostly with Zero. Under some missions Zero seems absolutely vital for the mission, especially as you get him up to max level during a Contract. However I feel like he starts much further back than any hero at the start of any Contract, both in terms of damage and support. I have played Contracts where game has backfilled me three Kosmo's and I have basically added nothing to the match at all. Through their overshield and buffs, they can actually do more than I can to maintain their health and I while I may be able to match them for raw damage eventually, I still won't be able to carve through hordes like they can, so I may as well have played as something else. This is a shame as he is actually really fun to play.    Also ignore these points if they intend to be added further on, but having to invite friends after every single contract gets old fast and while I guess it is a time saving feature during the Early Access Phase, the complete lack of balance when it comes to team comps is quite annoying. I kinda wish there was a way the server could say “This team have a Troy and a Zero, so we will only drop in players who have picked Kosmo or Cass to round out the squad”. Right now it can be quite hard to get a real feel of the game as one Contract you are four Kosmo's steamrolling to the end, the next you're three Troys and Cass and you get a Game Over before you even get to the objective. But yeah, those aren't intended as just out and out negativity, I mean every criticism as something constructive and I hope it comes across that way. Overall I highly recommend coming on this journey with the devs here if you are a fan of the Diablo 3 style of ARPG, who perhaps has not enjoyed more old school style ARPGs like Grim Dawn or PoE. Looking at the Road Map this game is starting at a great place and is only going to get better and better over the coming months.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is overall mediocre. It has few things good with it and the bad heavily outweighs it.What's good? -The characters look interesting, and the filler descriptions have potential, and someone on the art team is trying their best so I'll give them credit for that.-Sometimes the action gets intense and fast paced, but it's far too rare for when that happens.What's bad? -Pretty much everything else. -The sound design is atrocious, guns sound like they're shooting nerf darts, you can see one character smacking people around with a hammer bigger than he is and it sounds like flipping pancakes on a pan. A huge boss lunges out of the ground and roars at you and I've met squeaky toys more terrifying than what they sound like. The sound is not satisfying at all, which is going to irritate you because the game gets very, very tedious.-The levels are randomly generated, most of it looks the same, you have to repeat and grind a few of them and they're not interesting at all. Some of them have loot you can explore and collect but it's not worth it and if you do explore it you'll find that some parts of the map are missing and you can see through the floor and into the skybox.-The few good parts I mentioned before? Far and few in between, sometimes the bosses are bullet sponges, and other times they're interesting but you'll have to repeat the bossfights to get anywhere and they lose their charm.-The level design is bad. Not only do they look boring, some of it is confusingly mapped out and none of it is interesting so you don't care about figuring out how to move on, you're just going to get annoyed that you can't drop down a ledge that's a distance smaller than you are and have to go all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ way around. It's just a waste of time, a randomly generated, lengthy waste of time.The priorities of this game is seriously ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and before anyone screams "IT'S IN EARLY ACCESS SO YOU CAN'T JUDGE IT" I can. You know why? Because two big content updates have dropped and none of the base game problems are fixed. It's still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring to play, it sounds boring to play, and boring is being lenient because being bored is slightly better than being frustrated, and you're going to feel both.I could go on and on, there's tons of issues with this game as it is and I don't think they're going to fix it considering how they've been working for the past.. possibly half a year since I bought this game, maybe even longer. Save your money. Go play something else. The Alien Swarm games are free and do a much better intense action gaming experience than this does.Also someone please give the art team a better job because they're clearly stuck in a company that is incompetent otherwise. Seriously, the art design of this game is far better than the sound, programming or any of the other design components of this mess of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a solid isometric looter shooter/slasher. Plays kind of like Diablo or Lost Ark but with WASD movement. Fun core gameplay and meaningful loot that actually gives you abilities and has the capacity to be upgraded for more abilities/passive buffs. Abilities are cool and can be customized with upgrades. Every character actually plays differently, which is nice as that isn't always the case in games like this for some reason. There are a number of issues, though. Sometimes enemies start dealing insane damage out of nowhere and one shot kill you, for one. The fact that you have to level up to 10 every time you start a mission is super annoying because you have to grind and slowly unlock most of your abilities. It doesn't add anything to the game and is just tedious. The game also has handcrafted missions, which is fine, but because of how the difficulty scales, you have to grind missions over and over again to get better gear, which becomes very monotonous. If the missions had some kind of procedural generation a la Path of Exile, this wouldn't be nearly as much of an issue because there would at least be some variety. The game also has that really annoying Destiny UI where even if you're using a controller, you have to slowly move the cursor to select things instead of just moving between them with the analog stick or D-pad.In summary, the game is good, and I recommend it for looter shooter/ARPG fans. However, the frustrating thing is it can be SO much better. Hopefully future updates bring further improvements to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a lot of fun thats for sure, but requires way more content to be feasible, but it is in early access so it means it can grow over time which is good.Gameplay is very basic point and click to shoot or to hit,  while using the WASD keys to move your character. Also, you have access to four different active abilities to use through the dungeon (No. 4 becomes available at lvl 6). It is very fun and even intense at some points, so every time you play the game will always keep you busy and requires very precise timing for dodging.  As you progress you will earn EXP which increase your lvl up to level 10. Every two levels you have to choose one ability from a list  they show to you. Once you choose the ability the others become unavailable for the entire dungeon. So you have to be very careful which ability to use depending in the situation and the party you have. Once you finish the dungeon or contract, the level resets and you start over from level 1 for your next contract. This is similar to how MOBA game works but is not exactly the same.Vector levelYour Vector level is define by your weapons, support gear and prototype gear. As you progress thorugh the game and the contracts, the game will give you higher tier weapons and gear. Note that the Vector lvl does not affect your DMG output or DFS directly but through passive abilities that can increase your character active abilities or offer extra defense against elemental DMG from enemies. But getting the gear or the weapon with High level Vector is not enough, you have to unlock the passive abilities through an upgrade system which requires loot from the 3 differents maps that the game offers right now. Each map offer different type of loot so you need to have a look at your weapon or gear so you can grind for the right type of loot. Unfortunately, The Vector system is not explained and at the beginning it seems it has no impact whatsoever on your character. However, this changes once you try to get to the higher tiers. You are required to equip your character witht the right abilities and Vector level, otherwise you will get pawned very quickly on the levels, specially if you choose melee. For this you require to make multiple runs to get loot to upgrade your weapons or find better weapons or gear to survive the higher tier contracts.I think is pretty much the whole experience, if you like intense isomemetric shooters, give it a try even if the whole Vector level system is not really explained at all. You will get the hang of it very quickly.EDIT:Recently I came back to played the game, and it seems it has change somehow the experience, while the core gameplay still there, now the abilities are purchase in the main character window and you choose which abilities you want to use before starting a mission. To purchase abilities you have to find tokens hidden in missions or by just finishing them. They also add it items, cosmetics, levels for character outside the  missions and ranks for the different factions in the game, in which each give you certain bonuses like credits, quests, cosmetics, or loot for upgrading your gear. You increase the faction levels by doing specific tasks during contracts or finishing a contract assigned by one of the factions.Also they add it a colisseum where you have to defeat wave after wave of enemies giving you a good reward after finishing it. The battles here are pretty intense so you have to be readyThey change the way you get better gear, before you could actually just redo the easy missions and you will always get better gear at the end. Now it depends on the Vector level of the contracts you finished, now is a lot harder and takes longer to get to the higher levels. The Vector level still does not give you specific DMG or DFS bonus, how good the gear is, depends on the bonuses given by the gear. some give you bleed overtime, increase DMG towards a specific type of enemies, or increase LIFE, etc. You choose which kind of gear you want to use for a specific mission, so is always safe to keep different types of gear similar to Destiny or Marvel Avengers.Unfortunately this game suffers the same problems as Marvel Avengers game. Both games dont have a player base. So you mostly you will be playing solo. To be honest I doubt this game can increase is player base. The gameplay loop is too simple and lacks an open world or anything besided doing the same type of missions over and over again. Also, I dont feel like the character actually get stronger and progression is very slow.

_childDocuments_.review: Explore, kill, and loot! Embark on a journey to distant planets alone or with friends, but as with any game in Early Access, its current content is not enough. The lack of a plot, lore, maps that quickly become boring, missions that can only be completed one way, the same enemies and strategies used against them, the lack of competition between players...it's got a good foundation so far, but it also has a long road ahead to fill out its potential, especially at its current price.From what I can see so far the game has 3 modes, 4 maps, and 4 character classes that are completely different from each other; gunner, tank, assassin, and support. The skill tree system is simple and caps out at Level 10 for each mission. It allows you to choose your build to your liking. The overall level of the player, called Vector in this game, develops only with the help of weapons and equipment, which you can get throughout each mission, or buy at the shop using the currency that you get by playing missions and dismantling gear and weapons. At the moment there are no real customization options in the game and cosmetic items for each character are quite low.In reality the exploration is minimal because you choose a contract and each contract takes place in a particular map that belongs to a different planet. Once you're in the map, it's pretty linear with a few short paths that may lead to loot. There is pleasant music, good graphics, and it's fairly optimized so far, but the presence of bugs does hinder it...of course this is Early Access and the developers already fixed a lot of bugs before the release day build went live so there will be many more patches and updates to improve the game. Thankfully the developers are receptive to feedback and take into account what players ask for and suggest.So the game has great potential and if the developers take into account all of the feedback, the game will be great! The question is should you buy it? If you like Action RPGS, HELLDIVERS, MOBA-style games, online co-op multiplayer, Zengeon, or don't mind games that aren't complete yet since they are in Early Access, yes. There are issues with the game but the fact that it's fun is undeniable, especially with a full group where each person plays as a different class and everyone fills out their role. It sometimes feels like a full experience in this way. If you're going to play it alone, you may not have the same experience and it could prove to get repetitive very quickly. Yes, the price is high and I would suggest to the developers to lower it for now and then raise it back to its current price once it leaves Early Access. If you're on the fence, wait for it on sale. In the end, it is a recommendation.Finally the developers themselves have stated that there won't be any microtransactions or lootboxes, thank goodness!

_childDocuments_.review: Killsquad is a twinstick shooter with certain elements from MOBAS such as gaining new and upgrading the base abilitys through leveling up during the course of the mission.What you purchase during Early Access (as of time of this review) is an Alpha build , you purchase to playtest a playable version of the game that is by no means a final product. The content of the game as of writing this review are 3 seperate difficultys that are unlocked upon reaching the prerequisite Vector level , Vector level in simple terms is the powerlevel of your character.Your Character stats are directly influenced by your equipment , the equipment that can be exchanged , enhanced , upgraded , salvaged are your weapon , a utility unit and a defence unit some of which are relative mediocre in comparison to the stats you can roll.You can get gear from reward chests at the end of the game or you can craft RNG based gear for the ingame pseudo currency which you accumulate by simply playing or dismantling the items that you do not desire.The 3 different difficultys that i mentioned earlier are locked behind a fixed "Power" Vector Value which you will need to reach in order to access them in order to reach a higher Vector Value you will need to play the game as the powerlevel of the loot increases gradually.As you climb the difficultys you'll unlock better loot altogether , you will have access to weapons and units which have sockets in which you can craft additional modifiers to the item . These appear to be somewhat random and are not necessarily modifiers to the abilitys of the character that you are currently playing . This statement is solely applicable to the crafted UNITS as the crafted weapons are for each character with the modifiers only applicable to them , the same applies to weapons that drop during missions they will always be for the character that you are playing while the Units can be shared across characters.There are four playable characters for the time being , A Gunslinger that dualwields pistols , an undead space russian with an arsenal of two hand maces , a warrior nun with a variety of one hand swords , and Zero who wields plasma rifles .I will not go into detail of the characters as they are most likely subject to change as the ranged hunters just seem overstat across the board.The Game in itself reminds me of Livelock more than anything and i have absolutely no idea how so many people would compare it to mobas or arpgs , it is a twin stick shooter with gradual progress throughout the mission which is reset everytime you finish a mission.This is not a bad choice as your Ultimates aren't necessarily required at the very beginning of the mission.And i like i said earlier i can't really stress it enough that this is obviously a very early build of the game , it is playable but it is by no means optimised , finished or in a perfect bugless state.There seems to be this trend of people being delusional about what a game is and what state it is in , this game is fun , it has content but it has alot of issues to work out and it really goes to show that this is the first decent PC Game release of the studio as i do not consider "Fallen Lords: Condemnation" a video game.KillSquad is promising , it is not optimised , it is not perfect and it has almost no low lvl api interaction , if they work it out and overhaul half the problems the game currently has then maybe it'll be fun to play but considering all the issues with the Localhost , the audio and the immense strain that the Sectionload of certain mid boss encounters puts on the Disk i just cannot really recommend it. There is alot of promise , there is just an abundance of things that one shouldn't overlook.I feel like i should add that what i put in here as bugs i have in black and white and didn't take me more than 20 minutes to locate and isolate.Feel free to give it a try but do not a expect a perfect game , you pay for alpha testing. that's what you do. overall not a bad game if you enjoyed the likes of Livelock and with some polish probably a decent timekiller.

_childDocuments_.review: I've finally beaten this game and without a doubt, I can say I would NOT recommend this other people. I keep playing hoping for a light at the end of a tunnel with the new legendaries, but the more I play the worse the game gets.The beginning is too easy. I honestly almost fell asleep playing it and would've stopped if my partner didn't insist on continuing. Mid-game has a decent balance of difficulty and it was actually enjoyable. The end game is just terrible. This is problematic, because every lootgame thrives on the end game farm to retain players and give them a chase goal. This is what I find unappealing about the end game:- Enemy attacks are so ridiculously strong. They slow/knock down the player, have large AoEs, are very fast, have insanely good tracking, and can kill a player in a few hits. At times, I can't even use basic skills because I get killed if I'm not moving for more than half a second. I get that it's supposed challenging but the game just feels outright unfair at lot of the time.- The amount of enemies are that spawn to swarm the player is also ridiculous. It gets to the point where there's hardly any space to move between all the bodies and AoE indicators.- After you beat the game you are level 130. The few end game content that does exist is 140. The 10 level difference is huge as enemies are simply capable of killing the player 1-3 hits. Other loot games at least have ways to ease the player into the end game content, but the devs of game seem to just want to throw players right into the fire.- Getting loot to gear up is so slow. Suppose you actually clear the endgame dungeon. You only get 1-2 drops (in all missions, not just the end game actually). Not only that but legendary drops require multiple items to consume and level up. Thus you're repeatedly needing to grind difficult, end game missions that take 10-30 minutes to level up your item once.- Legendaries are just the basic equipment from the game that you now can just control what mods you get on them. They do not have unigue effects of appearances like legendaries from other games.I've played a lot of loot games, but this is the only one that's made me so frustrated and sick of the game by the end of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am always in favour of innovation. People taking risks, trying something new, never seen before. Sometime it works, sometime it doesn't.For the most part Killsquad is trying to innovate with some new mechanism but the result isn't very good ...So what's killsquad? It's a futuristic hack and slash with moba elements (hero selection, level ups) and heavily leaning toward multiplayer (although sp is also a viable option).Yeah it sounds wierd I know. But why not? So as a member of the killing squad you'll take a contract (mission) then join a lobby either sp or mp. While in the lobby you can choose your hero, there's 4 atm (same as at the start of EA btw). They're quite generic to be honest, ranged dps, healer/support, tank, melee dps and I find their design lackluster (matter of taste). Each hero got 3 regular skill and 2 ultimate (you're only available to pick one).If you go for the public lobby option you'll probably have to wait a fair bit of time for people to join. I usually started the contract and player (singular) would join half way through (10min~).Note that I can't speak for higher level or vector level (more on that later) contracts as it's, I suspect, where most player of the game are. Nonetheless at lower level there's not many which means that the game doesn't attract a lots of newcomers. Anyway, contracts are about 15-20 min long, maps variation is okay and you're supposed to ... well fulfill the contract's objective : escorting something, harvesting something, killing something (most of the time). The "thing" is, often, at the end of the map (btw you always navigate maps from left to right, it's quite strait forward, roaming and exploration isn't really a thing).So as it takes the leveling up system from a MOBA, you start level 1 and should reach level 10 by the end. For each even level you get too pick a new "power up" for one of your skill, at level 6 you unlock your ultimate. So that could work out quite well, each mission you pick different power ups, adapting your strategy depending on what you're facing. Well aside from one or two changes every now and then, you find the cookie-cutter build and you stick to it.Combat itself is good I'd say, quite dynamic gotta be careful not to get it and "read" the enemy attacks (basically don't stand in the red areas and move away from projectiles).After your hard fought contract, you'll get some money and go directly to the shop to spend it. The vendor will have a random selection of 4 different type of items : weapons, support, I can't remember the name but also support and consumable (oh yeah five types actually, there's a few cosmetics too).The item selection is adjusted to your hero's vector level. So that's supposed to be a big innovation I guess. It's a kind of item level except higher level item don't necessarily have better stats. Why bother then? Well it's not crystal clear, what I've read is the following :"Vector level defines the bonus percent of certain perks that may influence your health or damage abilities.For example, the base damage on weapons with Vector level and without will be the same, but the weapon with an upgraded Vector level will have a higher percent of bonus damage or any other type of perk, such as venom damage, explosive damage, etc..Another example is the Vitamod support gear, which will not only add extra health to your character with an upgraded Vector level (eg. adds extra 2.500 HP at Vector level 38), but will also increase the healing ability of your medpacks.So if you're wondering whether it's better to get gear or weapons with Vector level, the answer is yes. You should definitely get your gear and weapons with Vector upgrades and increase it gradually."So yeah... even if you don't get it, upgrade your vector level I guess.When you're done that's it! You've seen all the content Killsquad has to offer so yeah contract again then shop then ... yeah you get the idea.Obviously my main complain with the game is the oh-too-repetitive gameplay loop. I guess it could work as a casual game but then the progression is probably too slow...Speaking about progression, well that's another thing that doesn't really work. Since you start from level 1 every missions and higher level gear takes a lots of vector level before showing any meaningful improvements (and even then nothing crazy) you never feel like you're going somewhere. The same kind of missions with the same kind of enemies with the same kind of heroes (only 4).It's still in early access, more heroes are (hopefully) coming, but even then I can't really have faith in this project anymore. The core mechanisms are just not working together.

_childDocuments_.review: Killsquad is a bullet hell hack & slash (later in the game), where half or more of your abilities make you .Almost guaranteed you cast a skill and some AoE marker appears on you that very moment. What do you do? Hope to get the skill out before dodging or cancel out, rinse and repeat. This is the single most annoying thing about this game and it completely ruins the otherwise good flow, turning it into a often frustrating game.It's needlessly complicated in an effort to differentiate itself from similar games and it offers very little in the way of hand holding, expecting you to figure most things out for yourself. It also provides no information on base weapon stats, simply giving you a 'vector rating' without any information on the weapon's basic attack damage.The second worst thing would by far have to be the netcode. It's peer-to-peer and as a client the games feels  laggy. Where other much faster paced games - with more enemies - run with little visible latency, Killsquad will have about an *inch of lag *visually. In other words; enemy projectiles will generally appear about an inch in front of the shooter and will very often collide with you up to around an inch away from your character model.One particular enemy that is very fast compared to the rest in the game cannot be shot by aiming at it's model. You need to aim an inch ahead of it or stun it to be able to land your shots. It almost seems like the game has zero prediction implemented whatsoever.IF you can get past all that, the game isn't all that bad. But the price that is being charged for it is absolutely ridiculous for the quality. It is currently $42.95AUD here and I would not put it above a $10AUD game. There are probably even much better $10 games out there. The price mark is the entire reason behind my negative rating. Just know that you can find this game  cheap and much more reasonably priced if you look around.There's only something like 4 or 5 different mission maps in total that are recycled throughout the game with enemies and loot mixed around.The whole 'do contracts' thing is basically just a regular game where you can pick what stage to do, each with it's own set of rewards in terms of level and upgrade material types. There's no variety in what contracts you are offered as it tries to sound like, since there is usually only 1 worth grinding at whatever stage you are up to and every 'contract' is always available (it's just a regular stage select system).The developers needed to pull out a lot more than just cheesy trailers to make this game worth even 1/3 of the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Killsquad is a co-op centric multiplayer twin stick hero/loot shooter.  Gameplay consists of selecting a character from a smallish list of sci-fi heroes and using their attacks and special abilities to wade through hordes of enemies until you get to a boss and kill it.  Then you repeat this process endlessly, because grind is central to the game.  There's something wrong with the technical implementation here... despite the game having 4K support, everything looks blurry and muddy regardless of the graphics settings.  It's unclear if this is because of a filter of some kind that's forcefully applied, or perhaps the game is rendered at a lower resolution and upscaled... whatever the cause, this looks bad and somewhat spoils the high quality art assets in the game.The chief problem, apart from the blur thing, is the gameplay itself.  You must grind for resource currencies and gear ad nauseum, certainly it's a tough ask if you want someone to come play this with you.  And that's a challenge too, because while the game was initial successful with over 2,000 players, they didn't stick around, there's typically less than 100 per day and declining. While you can play the game single player, it's really not that fun and gets boring before you kill the first boss.  Because the game seems more like a freemium game and it's loot and RNG based progression, you have to redo the same maps over and over again... sigh.  Fun needs to be considered when making games.While this was never released on consoles, it has all the properties of a console game rather than a dedicated PC game.  It's also lined up like a freemium game, but, and this is a real problem, there's a whopping great big AAA $30 for this... it's outperformed by freemium options.  And while it doesn't seem immediately obvious, games like Lost Ark are way better than this, with deeper and richer gameplay, and free.  I just can't recommend this to gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: Just because a game is in early access doesn't mean its flaws should be overlooked, especially if the asking price is 20$, soon to be 25$.Gripes;-The game is bland. As it stands right now, the game doesn't provide much in terms of interesting design or gameplay. Pick character, do mission, kill monsters, get "loot" and repeat. The loot isn't anything special, and although I've been told that there are more interesting loot drops in the mid-to-late game, there just isn't enough substance to keep me interested enough to get there.-The blend of MOBA level-up mechanics with ARPG combat is novel for about an hour. The different choices that you can make in skill builds amount to little more than different damage values and cc capabilities. You pick what's optimal, and there's very little reason to experiment with so few options given.-Matchmaking is just, bad. Probably the most clear comparison between this game and a traditional MOBA is the rampant lag and desync. Any potentially enjoyable experience is marred by this game using a P2P system that, on at least two occasions, caused me to disconnect and lose my mission progress.-No story whatsoever. If there is one, I couldn't find it. No context behind anything, not even an introduction or explanation of what's happening. The game just loads and has you figure it out. This would be fine, better games have explained less, but there's no thematic or mechanical reason behind the lack of story other than there just isn't one.-Lastly, I take issue with this line in the steam description: "a hardcore action RPG done by hardcore RPG fans." What about this game is hardcore? Does hardcore mean difficult? Maybe the game actually get difficult later, but I'm not willing to slog through something that just isn't fun to get to a real challenge. If the game really is "hardcore", then why does everything, from the gameplay to the loot mechanics, seem so shallow, unpolished, and unconducive to something that a hardcore audience could spend hundreds of hours playing?tl;dr - Game isn't worth the money right now. Maybe if I played more it might grow on me, but I'd rather play other ARPGs that have the polish to make the early game at least tolerable.

_childDocuments_.review: The most important thing to understand is that Killsquad is not a traditional ARPG, and comparing it to Diablo or Grim Dawn is like comparing Doom to Tetris.Killsquad is put together like a MOBA, with twin stick controls, permanent skills, and cooldowns that encourage players to use combos for maximum efficiency.  Also like a MOBA, you’ll ‘level up’ during each mission, choosing different enhancements to your skills and giving you the chance to change up your gameplay depending on the environment or party composition. The gear grind takes place between missions, as you spend currency you’ve earned (or found) to gamble up new weapons and components. Missions appear to be randomly generated, with changing goals, enemies, and locations. As I write this review the game is still in early access, which means these random missions appear to be the only content; there will likely be more activities after the official launch, and the devs have pledged to continue introducing new features over time.Killsquad is clearly built for small groups of friends who want to explore a casual PVE version of classic MOBAs like DOTA or League. I enjoy it and therefore I’m recommending it, and if the concept sounds intriguing to you, give it a try – it’s well done.

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay loop is pretty solid.Play a mission.  Level in-mission to unlock skills (MOBA style).  Collect credits, crafting mats, and occasional gear.  After the mission, use currency to purchase new gear and or unlock secondary traits on gear (white = 1, blue =2, purple = 3).  You can equip a total of three gear pieces.There is also some synergy between gear and skill unlock selection (in-mission).  This creates a couple 'builds' per class.If the devs continue to iterate on this and improve the loop, I could see a fun game here.In terms of downsides, there are a bunch.  Although, some are just expected of an EA title.Bugs will have you clipping into and between enemy units (getting stuck until you die), as well as clipping into geometry.  Geometry is not always obvious if it is passable.  Environmental dangers are not scaled evenly.  Some are much more dangerous or annoying than others.  Resource nodes seem underwhelming or borderline pointless.  Map exploration isn't rewarded.  There is no in-mission map. Solo play is MUCH easier on certain classes and near impossible on others.  Balance in terms of damage and durability between classes does not feel even.  But we can assume these bugs and balance problems will be patched.What is more concerning is progression.  Your account 'level' is equal to the average ilvl of what you have equipped.  Upgrades you find/purchase are also based on this average.  So you basically just equip whatever is highest through the entire leveling process -- making upgrading gear semi-pointless.  Right now, there is also a VERY large ilvl cliff around level 50.  This is because missions in the 50-90 range frequently don't guarantee an item drop.  As a result, you have to play to obtain currency and then purchase an item (which equals about 1-1.5 items per mission).  And remember you have three items.  Which means that progression equals about 2-3 missions per 1 average ilvl -- to the tune of 100-150 missions to hit the current 100 cap?  At roughly 30 minutes per mission...  And that isn't even talking about gear optimization.  This is just leveling.  Personally, I doubt most people are going to put up with farming the same two tilesets for 50ish hours to hit that cap, especially if you are encouraged to just toss items in favor of whatever is the highest ilvl.Frankly, this could be intentional -- a way to prolong a small amount of content.  Which is fine.  This is an EA title, after all.  But it gets dull real fast.  IMO, there really isn't a lot more than 10 hours here unless you are just incredibly patient/bored.Another difficulty in terms of endgame gearing is going to be RNG.  You need to find or purchase three items, each of which have a base roll, plus three randomized affixes (with weighting among the types of affixes).  Which means there is a LOT of RNG that goes into finding a piece of gear you want -- much less obtaining the crafting components to upgrade it.  This will likely only get worse if more items and affixes are added to the pool (and they need more already!).  Some sort of crafting or reroll system might improve this a bit, but there's nothing on the current roadmap.One final complaint.  Starting a mission as level 1 just doesn't feel good.  Even with improvements from gear, you start each mission feeling really weak and so I'm personally left feeling like I haven't progressed -- despite the time sink.  Some sort of static out of mission skill tree or level system by hero would help a LOT here. It would make your power level increase more linearly instead of relying entirely on item drops.  Plus, it might make picking up a random new hero feel like more of an investment and differentiate one class from another.  Right now, you can easily just slot high ilvl gear onto another character (gear even rolls with secondary affixes locked to other classes) and there is very little difference in gear between classes (really only the weapon).TLDR:  It's not a bad game and it has promise.  Right now, I suspect the average person will probably get ~10 hours out of it.  However, I'd hold off for a while.  This needs another year or so of additional features and improvements before it's going to feel great.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Game sucks. Money grab by developers. Go play Path of Exile if you're looking for ARPG or League of Legends / DOTA 2 if you want to play a MOBA. Good idea, poor execution.Feels like the sound, music and graphic assets of this whole game was bought off of the Unreal Engine asset store, which isn't too bad considering PUBG did the same thing and made a few billion dollars.Gameplay is very dull. You run around shooting or slashing stuff, with a couple skills on a timer. You levelup just like in any MOBA -- start at lvl 1 and gain 3 skill upgrades and 1 Ultimate skill at lvl 6, as you progress through each mission.There are no item customization. You get 3 item slot for each character that you just buy upgrades for as you get Credits for completing mission. These upgrades increase your "Gear Score" so you can do higher tier contract, that's it. You repeat this until you max you gear score and have nothing else to do.Maps are all the same. There's very little enemies to fight along a linear path leading up to a boss fight (it's just a monster with tons of HP, that's it) that's insanely boring. You run this over and over and over again until you get enough Credits to upgrade your gear so you can do the next tier contract which is on the exact same map and enemies you've been grinding previously, just more HP.Audio glitches, Graphic glitches throughout each mission. Currently can't change resolution and audio slider does not save. Randomly getting kicked from matchmaking games with others, usually when entering the final boss area.There's currently only 700 players online playing this game as of this writing, and it's RELEASE DATE. The ARPG commnunity has a pretty big following and these people will try out every single new ARPG on release date. however this game is completely empty. Give it a week and numbers will most likely drop below 200 players. will the developers continue to work on this game support very low player counts? I think not. Game sucks anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game has been a blast so far.  Sure I’ve only played a couple hours but to the devs, you guys have done an amazing job and should be extremely proud of your work! :) I would love to offer some feedback on what i have personally experienced so far. I’d love to see this game succeed and if I can help by offering feedback then that’s what I’m gonna do ^^.  Pros:  1) Extremely fun combat system through gaining levels during missions to lvl yourself up, gaining new ability’s every 2 levels, up to lvl 10.  At the same time the monsters are getting increasingly more difficult as they lvl up with you. 2) This game is an amazing party game to play with your friends, chaos around every corner and the later you progress the more chaos that ensues! There have been several times my friends and I have screamed due to near death experiences and lots of red circles of doom @.@.  3) Classes feel like they have a purpose and that they are all fun in their own way!  I have put most of my hours into Kosmo and he’s been extremely enjoyable so far!4)  So.....Many....Unlockables and gear upgrades @.@! It feels amazing to have more unlock over time further customizing what your character of choice can do.  From a simple damage increase on a weapon, to spawning a pit of spikes to deal damage to your enemy’s.  My personal favorite is a consumable that freezes everything around your character.  Trust me later on it’s a game changer.Cons: Some of the character abilities don’t seem to synchronize very well with the way the character functions.  For example Troy. His pull and his strong shot feel a little weird on his kit alongside the rest of his abilities.  His strong shot is a line projectile and his pull groups everything up and makes it harder to hit with the strong shot due to it being a line.  Is the pull mainly for it being more of a group ability? His passive ability allows him to ramp in damage the more he kills which is awesome but the rest of the skills he has other than execute actually delay him keeping that passive up.  2) Sometimes when a character dodges or is hit by a trap mid dodge the char will freeze in place or get rooted unable to move or dodge.  3) There are some issues I’ve experienced with cass where her shuriken will fly in the complete opposite direction if activated quickly. Possible tweaks/questions: 1) Do you have a donation page? Again I’d love to watch the game succeed and would be awesome to know I helped with its progression :).  2) Would you accept skill rework ideas or possible future ideas on changes? Example: Reworking troys strong shot to be an attack speed or a conal shape rapid fire attack?  3) Are there any goals we as the community can help you achieve through killsquad? Recently with the pandemic here in the US things have been tough, I just wanted to personally thank each and every person workin on the game for giving us ways to still have fun. _childDocuments_.review: Fun multiplayer, not so much single player, good gameplay with some unfortunate problems.Combat is fun, characters play differently, there are decent build options via the skill tree and gear.Single player gets quite grindy with it being tough to pass mid-tier missions in one go. Playing with friends is much better,  clearing most missions in 1 attempt. Having a healer to support your damage and vice-versa makes a world of difference. It feels like a game that was built for multiplayer not single-player, and it could work really well if the population playing wasn't so small. It's very easy to drop into other players' public games mid mission which is nice.It uses a gearscore system, where your gear level defines how powerful you are, so in order to keep advancing you have to constantly throw out gear you like to slap in whatever new high level thing you find. Unfortunately it means you can't try to assemble gear into some kind of build while leveling. An absolute mistake in a game like this.The end game (gearscore 130+) is extremely repetitive, requiring 10+ runs to farm up decent parts to build just 1 piece of good gear. My crew gave up after we realized how slow progress was. Still, getting to that point was a good time.There is a very serious bug - if you get revived by a partner, there's a split-second window before temp invuln kicks in where you can be killed. After that there is no way to bring you back, even if your team advances to a new wave in a Colosseum. Other than that the game crashes a lot more than it should. Both issues are frustrating but don't happen frequently enough to completely ruin the game.Aside from the various issues listed above, it's a solid twin stick looter-shooter that I recommend if you can get a friend or two to join you.

It's a top-down schmup action RPG with "decent" mechanics BUT it is super grindy, has no matchmaking, has no quick-join or drop-in-drop-out, equipping different weapons does nothing for that character so there is no variety in builds that I can tell - just a generic "power level" that is the average of the players gear level. Looking for top down action RPG that is basically HELLDIVERS without team damage? This is NOT it. It's not a horrible game - it's just not good.

_childDocuments_.review: For EA I think this is worth the purchase. The core is there. The enemies are varied and the classes feel nice depending on your play style. All the hits and shots feel nice and the skills are responsive.This feels like a twin stick shooter with moba aspects and arpg aspects.Each hero levels up mid mission and allows you to enhance how your skills work and choose between two ultimate later mission. I can compare the skill system to how HoTs does theirs. You can build your character to the hazards present.The controls are WSAD similar to Hell Divers shooting or melee with added skills for damage, healing, or taunting and tanking. There are skill radiuses and indicators to know where damage is coming from.This missions seem to be generated and are very skill oriented. You can use credits to buy new gear for characters in the lobby if you dont get gear drops. Gear can have substats and pros/cons. You can have sub gear that affects loot drops, xp gain, or other stats.This game has great potential so give it a follow. If you dont mind an unpolished core with a decent amount of content grab it!
