_childDocuments_.review: KIllsquad, for me, hits all the right notes. Its a EA title and as such is obviously missing quite a bit of content and while a development roadmap is available some may want to wait until launch, or at least until there are enough updates to feel comfortable with your purchase.     The moment to moment combat action is damn near perfect. The polish is evident and the feel is spot on. Telegraphs, red markers that show you a upcoming enemy's attack location, abound with the dodge move being in constant use. The WASD movement makes it a more tactical experience than that of other titles in the genre. Don't like WASD movement? A controller option is available and the buddy I have been playing with says its his preferred way to play.   2 ranged and 2 melee characters make up the 4 currently in game, 2 damage dealers, a healer and a tank. They all feel great to play, fast, fluid, FUN. The MOBA style leveling adds a twist, as well as progression handled via loot instead of via character level. Some may find it too much of a departure from the norm to enjoy, however I found it quite refreshing and look forward to seeing how they build on that.   $25 US feels like a fair price for what is planned, even if it may feel a tad high for what its currently playable. If you are like me and after 1000+ hours in Diablo and Grim Dawn both and are looking for something different, then Killsquad may be just what you've been seeking!

Best played with a friend or two as it is quite difficult at times, and each role shines best paired with another. ie: Kosmo filling the role of Tank, Zero the role of healer/support etc. 7.5 "Do you like my suit?" out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I enjoyed everything about the game except the MOBA leveling aspect. I feel like using MOBA elements in other genres of games is just lazy design. The combat/gameplay is enjoyable, engaging, and challenging. Unfortunately, while the gameplay and ARPG styled graphics are 9/10, that isn't enough. There is a noticeable lack of story, progression, and customization. As for character designs they are meh (i.e. Space Jason, Cayde From Destiny. and Weeb Nun). I would have much rather preferred a Path of Exile/Diablo styled ARPG where players could create their own mercenary, engage in a open world story, undertake contracts, customize abilities/skills and possibly undergo PvP. What's disappointing is that Killsquad is that it's so close to greatness and could possibly reinvent the ARPG genre. Instead, it's struggling with an identity crisis of being a poorly developed Lobby-based PvE MOBA trying to be an ARPG and will probably end up being another casual game that friends with gather to play for a short time. My only hope is that developers become more confident in there skills and go all in to provide their audience with a topnotch game that could last through the ages like the many that came before it. _childDocuments_.review: Killsquad is an ARPG with MOBA elements (PVE only) mixed in. The combat is very fast-paced and well-done, but there is a very small selection of skills (like MOBAs) and only 4 heroes to choose from. As fun as the combat can be, there is little incentive to progress because there's no loot like you'd find in Diablo or PoE. You do get a weapon, and 2 other pieces of gear that have effects like +Armor, +Loot drops, +Health etc. It's very basic and makes virtually no difference in your playstyle. I've also come to realize that there's an optimal build for each class, and you can pretty much just go for the highest damage morphs since you can avoid 99% of the damage in this game.As for how the progression works, you start each mission with your hero at level 1. As you kill enemies you level up (max level 10) and you can morph your abilities and gain an ultimate move. In total, you'll have 4 skills and not too much flexibility in morphs because a lot of them are just plain bad or bugged right now, which is to be expected because it is in EA. At the end of the run, you earn a currency that you can spend on random loot drops and this is how you'll mostly be progressing. You also collect materials to upgrade your gear. They can add a modifier to your weapon, or gears that do things like  add 10% crit. Makes almost no difference in your gameplay. In addition to this, you have vector levels. This is reminiscent of Destiny's light level system. Gear has a vector level assigned to it, and obtaining new gear with higher vector will increase your vector level. This system is worthless because there's no advantage to having a higher vector level really, other than being able to undertake higher level missions. Missions have a recommended vector level, or a minimum vector level requirement. You'll be grinding the same 3-5 missions over and over for very incremental gains. You can solo most of the missions, but be aware that dying will cause you to fail. It's recommended to play in a party because your members can res you. If everyone dies it's a game over.Overall, this game has very fun, responsive combat that's hindered by a lack of variety in skills and very repetitive progression. The missions are fun and adequately challenging the first time around, but not so much after 10+ times. There's a lot of potential here but it's just not worth it in this current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Back at Pax 2019 I tried out a round of killsquad with a friend and found myself pleasantly surprised by the game. I would loosely describe it as a hybrid of Diablo 3 and Warframe. For the price I would recommend picking it up as one can easily get a good 30hrs trying different builds, lvling up characters, and gearing out ideal builds. The average time for a missions is about 20 minutes. A good game to play with a friend or two and knock out a few rounds after work.Gameplay is a fast paced top down "hack/slash" looter with 4 base classes (a 5th is in the works and more to come) and lots of gunplay. Each time at the start of a mission, your character for that mission will start at lvl 1 and progress to lvl 10. As you get levels you get talent points that you use to augment your 3 base abilities, 2 passives, and ultimate skill (you pick 1 of 2 options). This provides various build paths for each character that you can vary on the fly.The actual progress towards endgame takes place outside of missions in the form of equipment upgrades. The gear you purchase gets progressively better and provides more passive ways to augment your characters gameplay (with even more passives to be unlocked with "crafting"). Some of these augments may cause attacks to pierce targets, debuffs to last longer, crits to trigger additional crits. This has kept me interested in getting additional loot.One of the things I enjoy most in the game is the boss fights. There are some intense battles that rely on recognizing attack patterns and reacting quickly to get out of deadly AoEs to survive. The bosses are unique, and well designed.The game definitely has places to improve but they have been providing updates on what they are working on and are regularly creating more content as they develop the game. Things I would like to see more of would include clarity on talents (damage or effect a talent has), balancing on the current traits (some feel notably stronger than others), and additional talents (the gameplay loop if fun and satisfying, but gets repetitive). As it stands, I think there is a fun basic gameplay loop with some really dynamic fights and strong character designs.EDIT @ 15hrs: Typos, Missions duration, character progression, possible improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: Be advised: I do like this game and hope to update my review in the coming months to a recommended buy, but because of where it stands at the moment, I wouldn't necessarily do so. I would like to see that change in the future because there is definitely a solid framework here.What I like:- The Combat / Gameplay is solid and I enjoy that it is a focus over gear and class builds; a nice change of pace for isometric games- The Updates; it's clear that the devs are hard at work here because the updates add visible changes that you can notice immediately upon playing, whether it's added environmental structures and interaction, to new contracts and bosses. And though the changes are welcome, this is already where things start to leave a sour taste in my mouth.What I dislike:- Even with a solid premise, it just feels way too early to have been pulled out of the oven. Even though the game is polished enough to enjoy, there is a clear sense of incompleteness here and it kind of drags the whole experience down.- The graphics and performance aren't bad and yet there's a lack of polish that exposes the rough edges.- Details matter, small ones even, like Troy's guns sounding like the weakest weapons known to man, for instance, leaves a lot to be desired - a minor detail but a very important one to really give the player a more visceral and satisfying feel of impact, purpose and effect within the game world. There are lots of minor irritations like this that just need to be adjusted, like:- Environmental hazards that damage the player while using the kiosk within each contract. Imagine investing at one of these stations to regenerate missing health, only to have a blazing laser from the sky sweep over you while you're in the menu. You rush to escape the menu so you can relocate but by the time you manage to do so, you now have less health than when you made the purchase to heal yourself in the first place. Like, why is that even possible?- So, either from lackluster graphics / fx, performance, features, etc. to gameplay-related issues that cause frustration, it sort of just makes the game as a whole feel...meh. Not bad, just...meh. But "meh" isn't necessarily good, is it?I will definitely boot it up from time to time and hope to see the game improve, but that's about as far as my motivation gets me for now. I would love to say I want to invest time in it, but after only 13.7 hours of playtime, I'm already losing interest.

If late-game is indeed better polished, then progression should be looked at to give players better impressions. The idea seems very cool, combine the MOBA style with some hack & slash and sprinkle some loot. However, the game itself is an exercise in frustration. Backtracking to fully explore maps is slow as ♥♥♥♥, with the minimap being useless (seemingly requiring specific gear to make it useful? I only found something that shows chests). I personally enjoy exploring and finding secrets or random chests, even if it seems less worthwhile than just speedrunning missions. But with large chunks and no terrain , you end up looking at dead ends, and backtracking way too much.The loot is rather convoluted. I can kinda wrap my head around it, but most of the time it seems more useless than anything, and you just get the bigger number. Having played exclusively as Cass, I did not feel the defensive stats being anything useful - I would either get overwhelmed and killed, or mostly manage to go through missions unscathed. It also feels progression is mostly buying higher level weapons in the shop, rather than finding anything useful on the ground. Also gear seems to be a complete credit sink. I'm unsure how progression is meant to work - grind missions? Wait for shop reset, assuming you have enough credits? Why are there multiple resources? Seems like a feature borrowed from freemium games for some reason.The combat feels clunky. One particular mob puts down a white ice field at the same time as having red danger zones, which become nigh invisible because of the white background itself puts on. For some reason, one of the skills on my hero of choice has a follow-up with no duration that teleports me around, meaning that I can't quickly respond to evolving situations, or have to put myself in a poor situation by forcing the teleport. Dashes feel extremely limited as a melee unit, even with some speccing into dashing. Combat feels mostly you either clear everything, or you get overwhelmed and there's nothing to do.Finally, the UI is also frustrating, with long presses, multiple clicks for something as simple as equipping an item in the correct slot, and having to hold down the mouse button for various actions. The UI seems to primarily favour gamepad users, but this is not the kind of game I would choose gamepad over KB+M personally.In the end, trying it with some mates is probably the way to go. I'm unaware of revive mechanics, but there is at least an item I found which allows one to revive nearby allies. At least you're not losing 30 minute worth of mission progress with no rewards if there's someone to revive you. The game takes less investment than something like Warframe or usual MOBAs, so it might be good to pick up for the odd mission here and there, but to seriously play it, at least progress through it, is frustrating more than anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Killsquad is an ARPG where you pick from a selection of heroes, select a contract, queue into a game with three other players and fight through the area until you make it to the primary objective where you complete thing and get loot. Rinse and repeat for better items and progress.If this type of game does not entertain you then do not buy this game as you will find it repetitive and boring.Each hero plays vastly differently and has their own unique set of abilities. As you play through a contract there's a MOBA-like leveling system where you rank up your abilities and stats to become stronger. Early on the game is pretty easy and unchallenging but as you get into the harder contracts things get pretty hectic. Environmental hazards, swarms of enemies, and telegraphed attacked are all things you need to be able to bob and weave around once you get out of new-player territory.The game is solid. At its core, the mechanics and gameplay are satisfying. The foundation of which the developers are building on is solid for an early access title .I'm really picky when it comes to RPG/A-RPG games but this one manages to hit the spot. It has a moba-style system where you level up your skills as you play through a contract (Dungeon) and progression is a lot like a looter shooter where you find items that further a power level (Vector level).However the only problem is content and bugs at the moment Since it's early access it goes without saying that these kind of things are expected. Despite all this, the developers are extremely interactive with the community. They've released a roadmap of whats to come and have been giving the community small little hints of what to expect on their discord. If you don't believe me go onto the Killsquad discord yourself and have your concerns dealt with directly! They're honest and transparent about anything, even if you have negative feedback that they could address in order to move forward.While I don't want to be naive, I have high hopes for this games future. So long as the developers remain as transparent and hard working as they seem I think this game can become something really interesting.I recommend the game and will leave a positive review but I suggest waiting until about August to buy the game when the first big content drop comes out. If you want to support the developers on providing a worthy finished product then by all means go for it.If you want a game that you can play with friends and have a ton of fun, then this is your game.I'll edit this review (if I remember) when the larger content drops release to describe how well things have been holding upIt has a big sledgehammer boi that murders everything in its path so it had me on that.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent game. Very fun to play mechanically, and co-op works great if you have a friend at the ready. I feel that it delivers on the premise pretty well. However, It has one huge flaw which, to me personally, makes me not want to play the game at all: The Vector system.Vector is sort of an overall "gear level" for your character, and is a good estimate of how advanced it is. And just like you have a vector level, each zone in the game has a vector level.As in many games, the further you are "below the recommended level" for a given area, the weaker you'll feel. That's fine. But if you are "overleveled" (i.e. your Vector is way higher than the zone recommendation), you still won't be "too strong". Ever. No matter how much you grind. You can be a "Vector 60" character going into a "Vector 20" zone - and you won't feel overpowered. You'll just feel "fine". Like a "Vector 30" would feel "fine" in that V20 zone, not any different...And I say, where's the fun in that?! Let me grind my way to godhood, dammit. Let me clear whole screens of mobs in 3 clicks like it's a Diablo III Rift level. Let me carry my friends with my overleveled characters. Let me crush my enemies, see them driven before me, and hear the lamentations of the level designers.When I finally understood how this system works, I literally lost all motivation to get stronger in the game and stopped playing.If I could give this a "Neutral" review instead of a Yes/No review, I definitely would. But seeing as this is probably a "hot take" I'll keep this review positive... because honestly it's a pretty sweet game. If the "problem" I described doesn't sound like something you'd care about, give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Killsquad is an unusual surprise. On a surface level this game looks like just another ARPG in the likes of Diablo and Path of Exile. It is a loot-hunt isometric action game with RPG elements.The most notable difference is that this game incorporate some concepts from the MOBA genre, as characters will always start at level 1 in each mission, and level up to 10, unlocking skills on the go. This makes the game more dynamic and helps with powercreep issues, as all players in the match will be more or less with the same firepower.The devs seem to have a solid roadmap in mind since this game is expected to get plenty of updates in the future.✅✅ , even for cosmetics. You buy the game and get the full experience without having to spend a any extra penny.✅ Easy to grasp combat that is very engaging, with a low skill floor but high skill ceiling.✅ Enemy attack patterns are telegraphed, with markers on the screen regarding where and how the attack will land. This makes easier to dodge upcoming attacks while cluttered by other enemies and effects.✅ Small, yet very distinct cast of characters, each with their own role. Tank, DPS, heal, etc.✅ Graphic design, character design and UI are very sleek and clean.✅ Voice-acting is quite funny, with plenty of lines referencing pop culture and memes.✅ The controls are pretty decent whether you're playing with a mouse and keyboard or with a gamepad.✅ Co-op is the juicest part of the game, tons of fun. It also features a dynamic difficulty based on the number of players in the party.✅ Itemization is easy to understand, and the game doesn't shove a bunch of mechanics in your face.✅ Seasonal events with unique cosmetics will make this game's longevity remain strong.✅ Huge plus for adding tons of accessibility and customization, such as tweak of motion blur and colorblind options.❌❌❌ The game suffers from some very serious performance issues, namely a nasty memory leak and obscenely high CPU usage (mine was reaching 95% usage and almost 90C / 194F while playing this game). There is also a lot of stuttering and massive FPS drops while navigating in the menus. I've read that disabling V-sync aids this problem, but I honestly didn't see much of a difference.❌ When playing with a controller, the gamepad navigation in the menus is very wonky, since you move a cursor much like you'd do with a mouse. Not very intuitive.❌ Combat can become a huge clutter with so many particles effects flying all around.❌ Despite my praise of the voice acting, I feel that some of the voices don't really fit the characters. Also, voice lines tend to get a bit repetitive, so it would be nice if there was a larger variation.__________________Overall, this game is a solid experience, with tons of content, a genuine fun and unique gameplay that is ridiculously addicting, and again, . It is clear that the devs have love for the craft and respect their playerbase. I wouldn't even mind if this game was to get paid DLC because these devs deserve the money.Despite the negative points, I feel that these can be solved in the future, and from what I see in the forums the devs interact a lot with the playerbase, showing transparency.If you like nifty ARPGs with strong emphasis on co-op, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a "twin stick shooter" nor is it hack-and-slash.  It's all the worst parts of a MOBA torn out and repurposed into a game with no replayability and very little content.  Combat is slow and cludgy, targetting is awful, movement is bad, visuals are generic, and the progression system is a disaster of random ideas all stacked together in a menu hell from which there is no escape.  This game has none of the gameplay elements that either of the two descriptors-of-choice would imply.  Instead, it's just a dull, generic, unsatisfactory borefest.It's also got some weird visual and design issues.  Text is coarse and blurry and hard to read even on very high-res displays.The HUD also seems designed to ensure you have no idea what's going on at any given time.  Lots of shapes and graphics and very little information.  The gamepad controls (for a game that calls itself a twin-stick-shooter!) are a horrible random mishmash of mouse and gamepad behavior.  Menus are a nightmare.  And why do the damn tutorial popups move around constantly? Who thought that was a good idea?!  On one tutorial page, there are 5 instruction popups in a row, and each one moves to a new location so you have to use the spongy molasses unresponsive floating not-a-mouse-cursor mouse cursor to hit "next" on each one.  Real bad.  Feels like a smartphone game from 5 years ago that got a hacky port where they forgot to swap the touch controls for physical until a day before release.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so, I never write reviews so I apologize in advance if it's not very good but I feel compelled to do my part to write a wrong that has been done to this game by other reviewers. I nearly exclusively play ARPGs so I guess I like to think I have a decent opinion of what makes a good one.The most important thing in an ARPG is the combat and this game has amazing combat. All the moves and movements just flow together so gracefully it really just feels awesome.Other reviewers have seemingly given bad reviews because the game is simplistic in its, uhh character advancement. Well they are wrong. Is this game as in depth as Grim Dawn? Hell no! Nevertheless it has a charm all its own. _childDocuments_.review: The game is fun. Its a select a mission, go and do the mission, collect the loot, and upgrade/progress to harder difficulties type of game, if you are not into grindy games that have repetitive traits then this is not for you, otherwise jump in and experience the fun of early access.The good points, there are few bugs that I have encountered in the 5 hours I have played (which is great for most early access games these days) some being audio resetting every time a mission ends and the very occasional screen freeze when four people are bashing or just finish killing a mini-boss (elites). The loot is satisfactory for early access meaning yes weapon skins are recycled but there a many modifiers on weapons and each weapon randomly generates extra modifiers as the tier of weapon/support items increases. Another bonus is that the four classes currently in the game each feel unique and strong depending on how you take the skills in a mission as well the fact that a tank can deal top damage and take little damage, or a marksman dishing out crazy strong slows for the team. Synergies are balanced and no one class feels like its the end all be all. The bad points, for me specifically are that the current progression system may need to be slowed down a tad because the only true limiting factor for higher tier gear is the class specific weapon (because the other two items are shared between classes) which makes progression for each class quicker. Another issue at the moment that I expect will be added in the future is option to change the mouse targeter different colors or shapes so I do not lose it so easily in a pack of monsters, and hopefully the targeting of monsters when using attacks/abilities gets a bit better. The lack of a chat system is frustrating at times but the game is fully playable even without it. (I believe they have plans to add it in the future.)Overall I think the game is worth picking up if you are into A-RPG's where everything is WASD controlled and you use your mouse to target. The game is fairly casual at the moment and from my experience most people that are fairly high progression will still pop into a lobby and help you out.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a melting pot of ideas that just works! You obviously have the hack in slash classic isometric look which is about all it has in common with games like Diablo but more arcade like as in Gauntlet.Then you have Class/Abilities which is where the MOBA compassion comes in with games like LOL/DOTA2/HOTS where you have access to 3 abilities right from the start with basic attack/dodge being separate.  Like a MOBA you gain levels to unlock perks to your abilities, at level 6 you unlock your Ultimate which will be the 4th button on your ability bar, and every class has some sort of trick shot/skill shot ability using the mouse to aim/right joystick.Next we have the gear which is almost Similar to games like Destiny and, Helldivers, the quality identification is identical. Each piece of gear will always have 1 active affix with 1/2 locked on higher tiers which you will need resources found in missions like Radioactive Fruit and Vibranium. 10 of each plus other components you get breaking down old gear to unlock a better/more powerful affixes that directly affect basic damage and or, abilities.Lastly you have that squad element of synergy. Weather you play 1 of each class for balance, 2/2 of the same class or, 4 Troys. It seems the game will compensate for the group make up. The AI is tough! So communication is key. This is where the Left for Dead and final element brings it all together since you will always be in a 4 player party unless you make a private group, or run solo which again the game compensates.Overall I enjoy this game, for the price it's well worth taking a break from whatever game your grinding in just to play with friends or make new ones in Kill Squad. Thanks to Vulkan and, the devs at Novarama for providing me with a free key and, allowing me to aid in providing feedback. This game is full of all the right elements working together to make a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: As of now I've put about two hours into this, and this'll be pretty gentle given we're still in early access here.That said, my gripes are minor and this is a...pretty dope game! Controls for me were smooth, replay value was great, while the level system threw me a bit at first, I caught on relatively quickly and had a blast learning how the different characters worked!But, like I said, had a few gripes:1. Enemy scaling. Now this could just be me, bumrushing in, but having shot, smashed, slashed or zapped my horde-y nemeses en masse I was a hardly half way to level three when I was encountering level 6 or 7 mobs. That said, they didn't prove much of a challenge, just took more attacks before dissolving into that sweet, sweet DNA.2. Loot drops. While you can use your hard earned credits for random gun or equipment drops, I find the lack of weapon drops in game disturbing. Not a big issue or anything, but I've not gotten a single gun or equip smacking an Alpha down. 3. Experience gain. This ties in with the enemy scaling gripe I started off with, I feel like the experience gain could be better. After schlepping my way through hordes of baddies in dire need of a bullet lobotomy (which I delivered with great gusto), I found that it was a rarity that I hit level 10 before encountering my objective. While this doesn't prove too daunting a task at lower difficulties, once you're dancing through the midrange area, this can prove to be a task best suited for people with more of a taste for grinding. But, again, this can be my own fault what with the said bumrushing.4. Character choice. While the four characters provided ARE distinctly different playstyle wise, I'd like more than just four, personally. (I've dropped into games with 4 Troys, and while that is a hoot and a half, I feel with more diversity comes more eclectic teams) I understand we're still in early access, so not expecting miracles while you wonderful devs are polishing up base game, but this is something I'd like to see later. (Maybe at v1.0, if it's doable!)That said, I'm having an absolute blast wading through enemies in pursuit of sweet, filthy lucre. I've played enough to know that this fits squarely in my wheelhouse and I'm legitimately excited to see what the devs toss in future updates! You guys have made a great game and I dig the level of polish it's already showing. Also, if you guys wanna toss me a couple of free copies, I know two people who'd I'd looooove to drag into the game with me! I kid, of course, but if you're offering...Anyhoo, thanks for the game guys, and I can't wait to see what else you got planned!

_childDocuments_.review: I do NOT at this time recommend this - despite my thumbs up, unless you are interested in supporting a cool idea. Our experience was marred by significant technical issues - where both players at one point or another during the game went into states where they couldn't interact with the game (but were still getting damaged). However, I hate reading a bunch of negative reviews on technical issues which don't matter to me, and think a bunch of thumbs downs doesn't help so I wanted to write something balancing some of the negative >content< reviews that are up.I cannot say what is here is good (since my experience was hindered in a way that shouldn't reflect on content), but I am really pretty excited by the idea - it is really pretty fresh. The negative reviews are often from folk who want an action rpg - grind up levels forever - there are many many of those. This is not that - or if it is, it is a really significant twist on it. Each 'dungeon' you level up from level 1 to 10, choosing your skills fresh along the way - presumably based on your favored play style or the needs of the particular 'dungeon', or the needs of your group. This allows the designers to make an experience where you are constantly going through the fun part of leveling - where every skill is important and you can't wait to get it - and it comes fairly fast - rather than the inevitable long wait for a level with increasingly less impactful decisions. As has been pointed out by other reviewers - it is Dota style leveling. If the developers can make it so each dungeon has strengths and weaknesses that encourage different builds - there will be something really special here.There IS a 'global' level up, called the 'vector'; and equipment varies your player power (and hopefully ideal builds). Obviously, I haven't played enough to comment on the effectiveness of these - but look forward to seeing how much interest and distinct flavor they apply to your character.

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled across Killsquad one day browsing Steam, and thought that it looked like my kind of game.  I was hesitant because the older reviews were mixed, but I took a chance and grabbed it.  I'm glad I did!  It's a fun game with a pretty solid foundation despite being in early access.  The core gameplay loop is action RPG with MOBA style levelling (though the gameplay is nothing like a MOBA).  Each character (class) has several skills which start out at the same base level each mission, and you choose which ones to level up as you gain experience during that mission.  This makes it easy to experiment with builds, as you can choose a different upgrade path each mission if you like, though you'll probably find the skills you prefer pretty quickly and lean on them most of the time.Enemy encounters can be difficult at times, at least for my skill level, but don't feel unfair.  As you would expect, as your gear improves you become stronger, but so far I haven't experienced any huge leaps in power. _childDocuments_.review: After about 4 hours, I am enjoying this game despite some obvious issues of repetitiveness. As the developers have stated, their intention was to first create fun, core game play and to then expand the content afterwards. I believe they have accomplished their goal of creating fun, core game play and they have already started to prove their goal to add variety and expanded content. My #1 complaint is the lack of enemy variety. They've basically created three enemy archetypes that aren't mini-bosses or bosses: A critter enemy that rushes you for close-up damage, a long-range attack enemy, and a charge attack enemy. Those three enemies are re-skinned throughout the four hours I've played, but with slightly more difficult versions of them appearing later in the game. This has caused combat to become too predictable. I hope one of their goals is to create an expanded variety of basic enemy types. It's probably too early for me to know if this next complaint is true, but the loot you get mostly adds bonuses to stats without changing much to the game play. There is one item I've been able to purchase that adds a new cool-down power (a mine) that I love. I hope there will be more items that create new variety of game play. Quality looter games must have those kinds of items in order to be successful. Anthem and Avengers are obvious examples that failed to have items that changed up game play, and they were criticized heavily because of it. To keep this short, I'll list a bunch of things I loved about this game: great pacing, fun combat, interesting hero archetypes, fun bosses, fun environmental effects, well-paced progression, an easy to navigate HUB menu. Last thing, please create a map that actually shows you a map. Right now, it's just a radar that prompts you to move right. The only way you can ever go is right, so why do I need a radar? There is some minor exploration which would be so much less annoying if I could look at a map to see where I haven't or have explored.

_childDocuments_.review: From the 6 hours I have spent on this game, I can say that this game have alot of potential. But overall, yes, I will pay money to buy this game.As for those who have not tried this game, let me tell you a few things. 1. This game is not your usual Looter-ARPG. This game main core combies the common ARPG combat style with WASD movements BUT with MOBA leveling system. As in everybody (including enemy) will start at lvl 1, then as you progress, you will climb lvl and gain access to certain abilities. The skill system is similar like Heroes of The Storm, but with fewer choices. To me this is pretty interesting, as you can build DPS as healer (yes, my fav hero btw).2. This game is pretty straightforward, with latter contracts (mission) becoming harder and harder, and the hordes of enemies are increasing as your hero level (vector) grows.3. The itemization in this game can be cosidered as Gatcha, as the way to obtain the equipments are through Shops or Box from bosses. The item level that you are getting is generated through the highest contract level you have completed with that hero (this is my hypothesis), so wtih this system, your item basically are progressing with the same pace as how you have completed the contracts. The only downside is that you have no idea what affixes / effects you are getting for your next item that you purchase from the shop. So that is why I call it Gatcha. However, for legendary and highest quality item, you will already know the base effects, with 2 unknown random affixes in which must be upgraded (through crafting) to be able to unlock it.4. Death system is like diablo, where if you died, you wil be resurrected in 1 minute. But if you friend can come and rez you (5 seconds channeling), you will live again. I believe that if all member died, the contract will be considered as fail. I have never failed.. Maybe later on I will. hahaOverall this is a good game. _childDocuments_.review: Got it in a bundle, installed and first tried out on a build current to Summer 2022. I had no expectations and was pleasantly surprised to find a game that scratched a lot of itches nothing else has in a few years.The conceit: a slightly randomized instance-based isometric hack-and-slash with wasd movement and support for up to 4 players.Instances seem to take between 12 and 30 minutes.Movement is surprisingly visceral and feels both responsive and interactive up to around 180 ping. Netcode is peer-to-peer and not outstanding, but I have found it perfectly playable minus one crash-to-desktop and a few disconnects from players with ping at or above 300 (2/3 of the way across the globe or more).The game is completely playable solo and scales the difficulty to the number of players you bring. This appears to affect the number of enemies that spawn, and may affect their special abilities or health as well, but I haven't paid close enough attention to say for sure.There are about 30-40h of content if you do every mission once, and very little need to repeat many stages if you do so. You could grind at endgame, but it's not imperative that you do so to continue enjoying the game. Some missions are rehashes of the same map tile sets, but they don't feel too stale, since you're often more busy hitting things than taking in the scenery.Gear does matter. Your damage intake and output are scaled based on your average gear level relative to the recommended gear level of the mission. It's not too severe. Being 10 under the recommendation is enough to contribute. Being more than 10 over does keep scaling, but hits diminishing returns so you don't just one-shot everything with basic attacks.There are five characters (classes) some melee, some operating at various different ranges. I have only played three, and all of them seemed different, useful to a team, and fun. You can customize abilities as well as gear. Many builds are workable, you can lean into bulk, recovery, mobility, CC, or damage for each character I tried, though each has their own distinctive play style which will stick with you whether or not you lean into it. Also worth more: you can freely double up on characters in a party, so don't worry about joining a group and being unable to play your favorite.The player base is trim. Often only 10-50 online at a time, but I have had no trouble finding parties of 2-3 during most of my playtime. I was often invited to join random parties by friendly strangers who graciously helped me through some of the most difficult bosses, and it was generally a good time. You can always buy small gear level upgrades in the shop for credits (the universal currency) so playing with others below your level is relevant, even if it's slightly slower than doing on-level missions.tl;drBite-sized, fun, definitely recommend, probably best to get on-sale.

That being said there's a lot of stuff that I don't like or could be changed.  First, (and I cant believe this has gone on for so long) the co op needs to be changed. Preferably allow us to go from solo to public or public to solo.  Also please let me pause the game in solo.  When I'm in a private match its still "online" and even when you go to settings to change things you can still get hit.  Not sure why it cant just pause, especially when there's nobody else playing with me.  Another point to add when talking about single player/ co op games.  I can't always play with my friends, especially when they don't own the game.  So playing a game solo, and having a harder time, when it could be easier with more people isn't a good selling point.  To try and use the argument, "Guys, the game is... ok but it would be better/easier with more people" thats a terrible argument, not to mention true for basically any co op game.  This game can be played strictly singe player (as far as I have made it) so if you could give some work to the strictly single player experience, that would be great. When theres the green shields and you have to get the green ball, and run over to it to break the shield to keep going.  I 100% hate this "feature/idea".  It slows down the game so much.  Its an absolute dread.  Its not one of those, I dislike it because its hard or something. It doesn't improve the gameplay in the slightest, (the opposite hontestly) it doesn't give you a reward or anything, its just a hindrance.  So please consider changing this, I wouldn't go as far as to say remove, I know you do a lot of work on the game. _childDocuments_.review: Killsquad has all the workings of a game with great potential.YES, it is an Early Access game and thus there are features missing or yet to be implemented. That said, the dev team has been very transparent about the roadmap, and the game director checks in very frequently on the Discord to keep players up-to-date on what is happening with the game, which is IMMENSELY refreshing for a game with this kind of potential.Essentially, Killsquad is an ARPG with MOBA elements. Every time you embark on a mission, you start at level 1 and progress to level 10, selecting talents along the way that you can tailor to the specific needs of the mission you're on. Your skills have internal cooldowns, though you can reduce them with equipment and some talents.The gameplay is fluid and satisfying - big moves like ultimates feel like they have impact and many enemies need to be fought with different strategies.There is a lack of level diversity and build diversity right now, but definitely I feel that Killsquad has all the workings of a game that has huge potential for success. Gameplay that is fun and engaging, attractive graphics, fun combat that doesn't get stale, and a dev team that is transparent and responsive. I'm looking forward to sticking around to see what the future holds, but it looks bright to me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just alright. Nice coat of paint, responsive combat system, depth of a puddle with a carrot-on-a-stick that's got a short stick.It's a decent romp for a group of people for 10-15hrs before it starts feeling really repetitive. Pick it up on a sale if you have friends.The game looks colorful and everything from models to animations look and feel really good. The sound is functional but nothing spectacular. Controls are reponsive and snappy leading to pretty smooth combat on both controller and mouse and keyboard.The skill system makes each character feel very unique and resets every level (contract) for different builds (in theory). Sadly the skill tree is too shallow and simplistic for real build variety and the skill choices end up just being 'x is strictly better than y in most cases' so each character just ends up with a single build outside of very specific cases. Since the skills are the part that changes how a character feels the most, the shallow nature of it really cuts the legs out from underneath the game.Another issue with the skill system is the player has to collect skill points in order to unlock the short little tree but once allocated, there doesn't seem to be a way to respec so a player can get stuck in the early game with some poop skills leading to a less fun experience. Take for example, Troy, dual wielding pew pew robutt with hat. A player who spends most their early skill points unlocking gravity shot and bumping up their dash when compared to one who upgrades the 'high noon' pew pews and 'gunkata whirlwind of pews' would have two very different experiences. (Gravity shot feels like poop in comparison but that's personal opinion). A player who makes a choice and finds it's not for them can't go back and have a do over and if their friends are not on, trying to solo with a sub-par build can get quite difficult early on.The other part of character customization that affects gameplay are the weapons and gadgets. These add very minor changes to the character adding some procs to weapons or increasing damage. For the most part they just feel like stat adjustments and rarely change the feel of a character.Cosmetics earnable in game and look pretty cool. No cash shop for these things is refreshing nowadays. Thumbs up.The game does not have a large enough population to support quick match ups consistently. Yes you can join a Discord server and find like-minded people and organize there but it really feels like a game for a small group of friends to full be enjoyable consistently.If you want a coop game with a small group of up to 4 friends, it's good. Else, it's just okay.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is simply sluggish and slow.  Has some nice character abilities but lacks engagement and basic fun and needs better content and better use of content than it has.Some character abilities are decent and kind of basically enjoyable to set up and use, but too many are not, and everyone readily falls into mechanical, repetitive play.  The worst is the hammer guy, who may have the most boring kit I've ever seen, complete with several slams, the inevitable spin attack, and the requisite taunt-buff even though it makes no sense for the game.  He's an open insult to big hammer guy players.  Shotgun guy is a painfully bad, boring design that feels especially poor on controller.  He's supposed to be about having drones, but all that means is drones deliver your boring abilities.  Nimble DPS guy has low DPS and is pointlessly and obnoxiously rooted by everything he does.  Only the sword character feels like someone kind of tried to be interesting, as her abilities often do two different things and can be situationally useful, so you feel like you occasionally do something as the player.  Sadly, having a sword means you don't aim at enemies and just kind of sweep them about until dead, so even here the bulk of play ends up weak.Game loop is mission based, and there are not very many missions.  Missions have some procedural generation on content (ordering fixed rooms, basically), but lack much actual variety across runs.  Rather than feeling different, the main effect is just to keep you having to look around, as the paths are rife with pointless dead ends to check for possible pickups.  You'll know exactly where something could be, but you have to walk over and look to see if there's actually anything there, room after room after room.Within a mission, you start unleveled and have to gain XP to rank up and unlock some limited ability upgrades (which come based on the build you entered before the mission).  If you fight everything, you usually get to max level (10) by the end (or earlier on longer missions).  There are also extremely simplistic in-mission upgrades (basically, health and faster dodge refresh) you buy with in-mission currency (always starts zeroed).  So, you start every mission weakened from where you ended the last mission, just to try and fabricate the pretense of a power arc, over and over again.  This really does not work.You also have a gear-level (aka "vector"), which gates content and has no effect on your actual stats except for determining affix strength on your very few affixes.  The way you raise gear level is...you buy new slightly higher level gear until you need to grind more currency to buy new slightly higher level gear.  Pretty flat, and involves a  of wishing the shop would offer something decent, because there is almost no selection (almost everything in the shop is lower vector, so the slightly higher items have no options) and you have to wait to see a different option, to drag out the vector process on top of currency.And then, you have ability and upgrade unlocks, a more recent system that takes all the things you  to be able to set for your in-mission build, and locks them, until you jump through hours of mission hoops that are exactly the same for each character.  This gives you something of a longer-term progression arc as you play, but really it takes what was an already dull game and  what you can do that much more, while making you repeat  on every character you want unlocked.  Before, you could vector someone up with credits earned on another character, but now it's several hours on a character just to have a basic build, and way more if you actually want to have options or didn't like something you unlocked.   Each ability feels designed to need upgrades, as though fairly basic abilities were designed and then painfully nerfed to produce upgrades fixing that, but you can slot only a few of your unlocked upgrades.  And let me note again that, after you invest hours in unlocking upgrades to make abilities less bad, you still start every mission with them disabled until you kill enough boring waves to be allowed to have each of them switched on, meaning the very function of your abilities changes over every single mission, and you always start irritatingly limited.It also makes it significantly harder to evaluate the game in Steam's return window, but I suggest you assume the game doesn't have more than it shows you early, because the sad truth is that what's locked doesn't really make the game substantially more fun.  It just makes play a little less bad.Enemies are problematic.  The variety isn't terrible, but they either walk at you and strike (... eventually) or walk away from you and shoot.  They are boring to fight and provide little activity and no real engagement, especially since everything is just so slow.In particular, the game is relentlessly full of basic enemies that slowly drift at you in the hopes of eventually doing a small amount of damage if you graciously let them, or fall asleep.  Most of your time is spent either whittling away these pointless wastes of effort and time, or just slowly walking over empty space (this is probably the bigger one).  If you don't seek out and kill everything you can, you can easily miss getting your last upgrade before the mission ends, too, so you kill them like its your job, but not like that's the fun of the game, which is pretty much exactly how the game throws them at you.The UI outside the mission playing is poor and very clearly designed for mouse with little notion of efficiency or good use cases.  On controller, where you have to do a lot of analog stick mousing, it's terrible.Treasure demons (popup runaway loot enemies) are pure nuisance here, as they always are.  They generally pop up during enemy spawning, so you ignore enemies and run them down because you get nothing unless you kill them, and then go back and deal with whatever mess you made of the enemy wave(s).  The very existence of these is not just annoying, but a sad dev admission about how poor and uninteresting the actual wave battles must be.Graphics look ok, but the sound is poor.  Whoever makes this game clearly has no interest in sound design.  Also still has some weird performance issues that can cause it to hitch at three second intervals, regardless of graphics settings.  That's definitely grating and has been true since early access.If you're a solo player and care about achievements, note that there are a number that require a group, a full squad, or even a full squad with specific compositions.PS: Watch out for middling reviews from before the 40% price hike in March 2022 "because it would be unfair to release on console costing more than PC".

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun. The combat is ARPG like (e.g. Diablo) but mixed with a MOBA elements. You unlock abilities as you beat contracts. In each mission you level up to level 10, with those abilities becoming available as you go through each level. Lots of loot and skill combinations to experiment with. Your items combine to a 'vector' or power level, similar to Destiny.It definitely a focus on playing in a party but the game makes it easy to connect in pub servers. On the mission menu it indicates if a mission already has people playing on it so you don't have to roll the dice or cross your fingers for someone to join your match. Really appreciate that touch.

_childDocuments_.review: There's too much lag to play this game atm. I recommend waiting a week or two if you really want to buy this game.Lag in this game is horrible and cause glitches. I once spent an entire game jumping everywhere; my teammates were moving normally, but my character would use a walking animation and teleport short distances.In terms of the game itself, there are a few issues.1) Height based projectiles. You shoot projectiles straight and if your target is below or above you it might not hit.2) Boss attack tells are worthless. Bosses in this game show how they are going to attack but give no time to avoid it. Sometimes the AOEs are so large that avoiding them is impossible. Perhaps it's a design choice, but it feels bad when you constantly get damaged and you can't do anything about it.3) Sky lasers move extremely fast and deal insane amounts of damage. They are also extremely bright and blind you.These are fixable issues. However the reason I don't recommend this game is due to its core design.- Heroes are limited in variation. Weapon buffs give more incentive towards certain builds and playstyles, but does little to change the actual gameplay. - Mission-based gameplay is extremely repetitive. Unless they plan to pump out missions constantly and create new biomes, this game will get stale very fast.- Hordes of enemies. but no loot. Enemies in this game are not worth killing. Sure you need to kill them to level during a mission, but you have to do that constantly and it gets old. Soon enough it becomes a chore since it's required, but has no incentive beyond that.- Title says loot, but where is it. Some missions give 1 piece of loot. You can buy random loot. But enemies don't drop loot nor do bosses. Loot is scarce and that sucks. This game is not comparable to games such as Diablo, Path of Exile, or Grim Dawn.TLDR; This game isn't like POE or Diablo. It lacks loot and feels more like a higher graphics Helldivers. The core gameplay doesn't seem realistically extendable and becomes stale quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: Please read the update below.Going to keep this review short and simple because at it's core, this is a very simple game. This is an isometric arpg that can be played co-op or solo and has a lot of positives going for it.- The gameplay is mindlessly fun. Very much akin to the usual arpg style, the gameplay is sort of relaxing and simple, where you are doing a lot of non-taxing actions for the most part. Simple fast gameplay, I would relate for to a Diablo 3 style in that its fast moving, can be done on autopilot, and feels kind of like a therapeutic activity. This game will be great for playing while multitasking and watching youtube videos or twitch gameplay.- The gameplay that takes place outside of the action is intriguing to me. I think this is the most important part about an arpg, because an arpg will naturally be grindy and repetitive, so there needs to be a driving force. In Killsquad, gameplay comes by taking contracts. So all the gameplay happens within contained missions. I think this is amazing, because it streamlines the process of playing, especially playing with a group. You can play and join others for specific missions, sort of like in a Division or Anthem style. The devs have said there are 40 contracts available in this early release.- The progression for this game is all about gear. Gear is king. Contracts difficulty is based on your vector, which is more or less your gear score. There is also a leveling progression that happens strictly within the confines of a contract. This is reset for every contract you play, and as you level, you can buff your abilities by picking 1 of 3 available buffs. This is really interesting because you can build differently every game based on your teammates or if you are playing solo.- The art and style is AMAZING. I absolutely love it. The character I'm playing is a gunslinger alien that wears a trucker outfit like he just got out of his trailer. The worlds look beautiful. And most importantly the enemies look like disgusting foul beasts that we need to be rid of ASAP.I don't want to give this game a rating so early on, but this game, at $20, is definitely worthwhile to at least give a 2 hour try to see if you can imagine playing it while watching YouTube or Twitch while keeping yourself stimulated. I think with how slow and uninteresting game releases have been as of late, a good old fashioned well made arpg to drool in is exactly what the doctor ordered.Though the positives of this game are really cool and necessary core aspects of an ARPG game, I think there is a huge reason not to play right now. And that's the seemingly hollow system around the game.- Currently there is only 4 characters who have very strict playstyles associated with them. This mean getting tired of a playstyle and not having anything interesting to try is very possible.- The most important part of an ARPG in my opinion, is the wrapper of the game play that drives the player to keep grind. For example, in Diablo, you might be driven to play to reach the seasons leaderboards, or just to get the best gear possible. In the Division, reaching the highest gear score possible and maximizing your gear and sets is the driving force. However, this games gear system looks very hollow. The loot you get for missions is some unexplained crafting materials that just upgrade the uninteresting loot. - So the driving force is really just to keep playing until you are at a higher gear score where you kill higher leveled enemies, and that's really it. I'm very worried the appeal will wear off in 10 hours or less of gameplay, and for the $20 game tag, I can't be confident in recommending it for everyone. I think the game the way it is would be fine, if it was a F2P game like Warframe or POE, or it was at least substantially less expensive than it currently is.I do still believe the game is worth trying for an hour and half, and then refunding if you can't see yourself getting enough playtime out of it. It really seems like what you see in the first 1.5 hrs is what you'll get through the entire game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I have ever played a worse Action RPG. There are already so few ARPGs with a modern or futuristic aesthetic, and the few that exist are all pretty bland. Sadly, this overshadows the flaws of most other similar games by a large margin of trash. To put very briefly: terrible "progression" system, awful map designs paired with no map to know your location on these insanely samey maps, boring gameplay against boring enemies with patterns devoid of creativity, and worst of all, absolutely NO loot. This game seems to have stripped every good feature of an action role playing game straight out of what makes them fun at its core and then slapped on a soulless shell to make it look like a game. Graphics are the only thing this game has going for it. More detail time. The gameplay is just boring. I haven't played a lot, but it takes almost no time at all to realize how quickly this is going to get stale. I'm going to compare this to Grimdawn and Diablo for the sake of sanity, as most people are familiar with at least one of those. Grimdawn is very repetitive, as is Diablo in terms of combat, yet they both manage to be fun. You have enough diversity in enemies or skills to chain together that combat doesn't grow too stale, at least not for the grind. In this game, however, you have stunningly little skills to use. Combine 4 skills (6 if you want to get incredibly technical) with enemies that either shoot from afar or just walk at you in the exact same patterns and you have an incredibly stale gameplay loop. I've hit two maps so far and that hasn't changed, even with a drastic change in the aesthetic of the enemies. Going from alien creatures to robots, you'd expect more than just extra enemies that shoot. Nope, same patterns. You're just fighting reskined enemies, though at least the reskins look nice. It's hard to explain how a game in this genre is boring, as on the surface, a lot of them seem boring at a glance until you get a feel for it. This game was quite the opposite. It looked fast paced and fun, but ended up being as slow as can be and boring. On top of the enemies being all the same, there are astoundingly few. The maps are just devoid of life, and enemies spawn in from time to time, but that's about it. I'd say maybe 20% of my short time playing was actually filled with fighting enemies. There is so little to do in the way of combat that it's...it's just weird. So, finally getting combat after walking around to explore an unrewarding map is just sad once you're met with mindless combat that isn't even flashy. Let's talk about the maps. Oh BOY the maps are terrible. The first map is an alien planet that looks like every other "dangerous alien planet" design I've seen in my life, and the second map, a rusty mechanical 'city'scape, was just a bunch of rusty walkways. The layouts are dreadfully boring. Normally, in games like this, you'll have SOMETHING to explore, but this is just really poorly designed walkways that lead you in a near straight line to fight what few enemies exist. I think that the biggest affront to the genre is the absolute lack of anything on the maps. I mean this as in: Exploration is unrewarding. You'll find the most meager of things for walking around every last inch of the already dreadfully desolate maps. I spent a solid 5 minutes just walking through an unexplored area, found zero enemies, and a single resource deposit. That meant 5 minutes of walking back with no enemies as I made sure to check EVERYTHING. It constantly felt as though I missed something, as the game had given me near NOTHING for having spent all that time exploring. None of the extraneous paths I found after took quite as long to flesh out, but they all had equally little at the most, and usually nothing at all. If it isn't resource deposits you find, it will probably be a chest that has all of nothing in it. No loot. No weapons. No cosmetics. Just resources or a few credits to buy weapons that will get replaced in probably 1 whole mission. Map exploration is one of my favorite parts of games like this, yet they've decided to punish players for it instead. Literally can't even fathom how they thought that was a good idea. I just can't. It's so far from what is fun to me that, even if you hated map exploration, why would you decide to make it not worth the players time? That would be more reason to make it worth their time, not the opposite! There's zero reason to explore, and it's mind boggling. Now, on top of zero rewards, let us talk about the "grind".Killing enemies amounts to being useless halfway through! Oh joy, another RPG feature that's nullified! Killing enemies suddenly becomes useless, meaning that everything you kill is not only boring, but also a complete and total waste of time! You'll realize instantly that you "level up" your stats veeeery fast, and I instantly knew they were pulling some stupid stuff. Leveling is on a per-mission basis, so they're going for this really stupid rogue-lite thing that in no way adds to the game. I think they did it so they just didn't have to bother with scaling enemies quite as much, but it's still  For what actual purpose? Abilities and skills are also locked behind this. Maybe they thought that it was innovative to lock your ult behind a few kills, but with a 90 second cooldown on the first one I unlocked, I seriously just don't get why. Finishing off this dreadful thing, all experience is just gone when you finish, and if you max your level during a mission, you get nothing for extra kills. The grind of killing droves of enemies is what I crave in a fun game like this, yet they've made it pointless to ever kill anything past a few minutes into a mission. Wonderful. No looting in what is setup as a looter shooter (even heavily draws from several aspects of Destiny 2's systems), unrewarding map exploration that only serves to waste time, no map to help through the maps in which everything looks exactly the same, and some of the most stale gameplay I've felt in a long time. Most people, even those in the in game chat from what I've seen, say that there isn't any end game content. This, I find astounding. I'm unsure how that is their problem with this game, but I can't even fathom playing far enough to get anywhere close to that. This is a glorified walking simulator in which you sometimes kill things. You can't even pause the thing while playing solo in a private lobby. Games from the PS3 era managed to solve that issue, yet here we are. Terrible empty husk of a "game" that's pretending to be a lot of things, but succeeding in only being a time waster.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, Killsquad just ultimately commits the sin of not being very fun to play. It's definitely not absolutely terrible - I could even see how this might be more fun in co-op. I'd been pretty interested in checking it out for a while and found myself with the bandwidth to give it a shot, but I'm pretty disappointed by how my time with it went.I think the biggest problem is bland combat. It's just lacking much of any impact, both whether you play the ranged or melee characters. Most of the attacks just feel kind of limp and weightless with little-to-no feedback or audio, as though you're playing with action figures. The visuals in general are also honestly a bit ugly... especially the environments, which vary in quality from repetitively boring to cluttered eyesores. The music's also just dull, and generally the overall audio balance feels totally out-of-whack.There seems to be a wide, overarching issues that Killsquad suffers from when considering basically the overall creative, design and narrative approaches it takes. The levels are sprawling messes that often feature dead-ends with nothing in them. The art direction is a garish jumble of disparate designs and aesthetics with no real obvious stylistic throughline. And in terms of the plot and lore, basically nothing is explained of justified much - where are we? Who are we? Who are we fighting for? Who are all these random aliens, races and factions? There's a codex of enemies you've fought, but beyond that I wasn't able to gleam much other than we're in some far-future post-apocalyptic wasteland (something something nuclear devastation).It's a shame because there seems to be a good core here, and there does actually seem to be a lot of content to unlock and some depth for potentially serious ARPG buildcrafting. They clearly were considering this game to possess some kind of longevity. Unfortunately, it's basically dead and devoid of any practical, useful matchmaking. Plus there doesn't really seem to be much of any level scaling, which seems kinda par for the course in co-op centric games these days. This also apparently leads to a stale endgame from what I'm seeing posted around here, which doesn't inspire confidence any further.The scaling also feels a bit wonky, with huge difficulty ramps. You can go back to previous missions to grind for gear and currency so you can make sure you're levelled appropriately - but when a game is this boring to play and hasn't earned the right to demand you grind, it just feels like a slog and a chore. Even the promise of the various cool little cosmetic unlocks for each character isn't enough to sway me into repeating content and praying to RNG.I'd imagine you'd be having a better time playing with a friend or two here, since public games are mostly going to be out of the question - in my few hours I saw a couple joinable games that I failed to connect to, and had one person drop in randomly at the end of a mission I was running. But a reliable multiplayer experience requires having friends who also a) have Killsquad and b) want to play it, which I don't have. I played through around a few missions as each character (the gunslinger was about the most fun I could muster), and just couldn't honestly face the prospect of having to play any of them any more whilst largely going it alone.★★✰✰✰

name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw
detailed_description: Out of cash, out of luck, out on the fringe. Juno Markev has a killer to tail, a debt to pay, and more trouble headed her way. Rebel Galaxy Outlaw takes place in a greasy, blue-collar world of outlaws, truckers, cops and thieves. Strap into a variety of spacecraft, settle a score in a filthy space-bar over a game of 8-ball, rock out to over 24 hours of music, and engage in white-knuckle dogfights. In the Dodge Sector it’s hard to get by – and even harder to get even. Rebel Galaxy Outlaw is an open-world space combat adventure game, spread across the nearly 40 systems of the Dodge Sector. Play as a mercenary, a trader, a pirate, or whatever mix of the three you feel fits you best. With an engaging storyline and a full conversation system, you can follow the narrative, or ignore it and forge your own path at any time. Engage in white-knuckle combat, and use the included Autopursuit function to effortlessly fly like an ace, instead of space-jousting for hours. Save up your credits, buy a new ship, kit it out, and then paint it in a fully-fledged 3d-painting application. Make a fortune exploiting lucrative trade routes. Join guilds, help or hunt those in distress, buy and outfit your own space station. Grab a tip in a local bar and hunt hidden treasure. In your down-time, shoot some 8-ball, play some dice-poker, or aim for the high-score in an arcade game in the local seedy watering hole. Flip through the 7 included radio stations and vast music library for just the right track to fit your current mood.

Pro: Concept and SettingInitially its fun to work out how it works, and progress. it feels good to defeat enemies with newly upgraded gunsArtstyle is exaggerated, but stylishCon: Balance and non-PC friendly choices (FOV!!!)-game has a habit of just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you over for no reason  (5 swarm missile spamming enemies spawning right behind you. And whenever you are already damaged, the game seems to throw dozends of randomized enemy encounters at you, that you cant escape out of)-Mission difficult is poorly communicated/ balanced, and like a gamble - you never know if it will be a walk in the park, or if you get recked in seconds - The payout doesnt reflect that. Some missions are not worth it, pay only half or a quarter but are much more difficult or time consuming than others.-you cant save manually , you only save automatically when landing somewhere-There are only 6 ships or so-Ship progress is badly paced - i see no reason to upgrade from starter ship to 2nd tier - they are totally not worth it. Only the top tier ships are worth the upgrade. There is no mid tier.-FOV feels like 40° or something silly low - and of that limited screen space the cockpit takes 50% - even on fighters (esp. the best fighter has the worst cockpit) You can even see that that cockpit in particular was squished so it fits on the screen with that low FOW.-Its a game of mini-cutscenes. Fly from one station to another goes like this: Cutscene for lifting off, cutscene for leaving the planet,  cutscene for entering autopilot, cutscene for landing approach, cutscene for landing. If your flight got interrupted by some random fart again, its another custcene on top.-shop menu has no back button (Esc opens system menu instead)

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is great. I haven't played the first Rebel Galaxy so no "crushed expectations" here. This game is directly inspired/modeled after Wing Commander games from the 90's, specifically Privateer (cockpit aesthetic and npc voice-lines when docking pulled directly from it basically) which I played in the day, so that was a + for me. I read all the negative  reviews and issues people were having but it was 5$. I read some tutorials/hints on how to play and went from there. Let me address some issues I've been hearing in those negative reviews.1) Enemy difficulty:First off, those old WingCommander games were HARD and did not hand hold you, requiring some missions to be attempted several times. You start out in a very modest ship, and some enemies are a 100% no-win situation - but just like those older WC games sometimes you have to run, and avoid certain sectors to escape. And come back with better ship/weaponry another day. The developers have even said, that as you move through the galaxy according to the missions the enemies get harder, so dont jump to the high risk areas too soon. They also said that its not just upgrading, you need skill too! In only my second or third session playing this game those early enemies that smoked me immediately my first time playing, were now easily defeat-able with some careful upgrades and some technique - spamming missiles, dropping ECM than boosting away to avoid their missiles, learning how to get on their 6. which brings us to point 2.2) Flight mechanics:I had to fiddle with the control settings and adjusted the DPI on my gaming mouse a bit before I got used to the flight style. Then it became fun. There is also a "center mouse cursor" button that comes in handy when you want to stop turning and snap onto something. This game never claimed to be Star Citizen or Elite Dangerous so people complaining that it is not a complete space sim and can't use there HOTAS setup sound silly, the devs even say its best with a game controller. You can't down-vote game A because it is not game B3) The developers "abandoned" the game: Well, the game is a complete product, and works fine imo. That's how game development used to work. Having developers continue to release fixes, content and DLC's for a game over many years is a (relatively) new idea in the last 30 years of gaming, and not every small company can have those expectations put on them. And as an old-school gamer it just sounds entitled to me (this company had a tiny handful of developers).
