_childDocuments_.review: Despite liking Rebel Galaxy I slept on this game, thinking that the focus on small fighters instead of huge ships would make the game feel smaller. And it does. That said, it's a fun game with decent progression and combat loop. The biggest weakness is likely that there's still a few hours of story missions to do when you can afford the best ship, equipment and weapons. After that money becomes pointless and all that is left is the story, something that never really goes far enough to be compelling. The stakes feel very low. That said, it's a love letter to wing commander privateer, so if you liked that game way back in the day.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like DDG really dropped the ball on this one. It feels like a generic space shooter and all you do is just fly around in circles just trying to find who's shooting at you. They made a big mistake of switching from flying giant capital ships to these little tiny fighters. The first game is just so much better and you should buy that one instead. The only good thing about is the amazing soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: It's Elite Dangerous Lite. It really is. That being said, the ship options are lacklustre. The game does a poor job of explaining one combat thing:In targeting window, when in big fights, find a target that has a yellow line connected to you - if you're being attacked. Burn that guy, and the damage will stop before he's even finished. Otherwise he'll just pound on you the entire fight, and you'll die. He's not always close at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this! It was light-hearted, and kind to people who try to play space-shooters with a mouse and keyboard. I had no technical or stability issues to speak of, and only one mission in my entire playthrough that didn't fit the (otherwise very smooth) difficulty curve. The story campaign was good, but don't go expecting a mystery - it's more a personal journey for the main character. All up, 7.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: Way too grindy and difficult. AI gangs up on you and destroys you in seconds even on average difficulty missions in the first few systems. Maybe it gets better with a dedicated fighter class ship but I can't be bothered to grind the money for that by doing fetch quests. Side missions are also very very repetitive.The southern country/trucker in space setting is not appealing. It can be done right, like in Firefly, but here it just seems boring and lacks depth.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely in the Maybe to Yes category.  A lot of quality production work has gone into it, but the effort hasn't gone into the places that would help it get close to the age old standard of Freelancer, and it even falls short of Dark Star one in quite a few regards.Graphically it's very nice, and the voice acting is good.  There is welcome streamlining in some places, but that has gone a bit too far and been applied to certain aspects that unfortunately rob you of what should be the full space faring experience.  Docking being a prime example.  Which makes it perplexing that the menu system at space stations is woefully inefficient to navigate despite it being pleasantly simple.The largest disappointment by far though is the dog fighting.  As a proponent of the superior when well implemented relative virtual stick mouse controls, this game mostly leaves me in a frustrated wobble of orientation.  There are a lot of other design decisions that collectively compound to upset the experience.  From the screen real estate of the cockpit, the dated style of radar display, to the mess of confusing target cross hairs, that all seem to have been aesthetically constructed without enough regard to usability during combat.I am sure there are some values that could be tuned to improve the fun factor too - specifically ones that control how the relative distances and positioning between the combatants typically work out.  You may enjoy the game more by giving in to the auto follow/target system, which honestly isn't as bad as it may sound, and does make a certain degree of technical sense.  But again it's just not as fluidly pulled together as you would hope, and it's very likely you will want to remap a few keys to try and improve this.To end on a worthy positive note, the inclusion of the games in the bars are great, specifically the pool table one!
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the trading aspects of this game, mostly, but it is a little flawed in the sense that it is not satisfying being limited in how much cargo you can shift at any given time.  What is the point of having a massive cargo hold if you can't easily buy enough cargo to fill it?  The way the trading is designed is just a damper on the fun factor.Combat is somewhat entertaining and accessible thanks to the auto-tracking feature.  The big issue with this game is that the story / main missions just aren't fun or engaging.  There are other things I could mention such as the lack of ships / ship progression.Overall a pretty disappointing game, though it does somewhat scratch that Freelancer itch I guess.  I don't regret my purchase but I wouldn't really recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that make me wish steam had a neutral option.First of all I recommend messing around with the options menu until you find a control config that works out for you personally.Then Ignore the story and missions and look up a mining guide. Have youtube or podcasts playing in the background as you will probably spend the next few hours mining to amass wealth.I recommend grinding early and getting the best ships/upgrades sooner rather than later since this game throws a lot at you quickly. I can barely fly anywhere without getting interdicted. Sometimes large pirate swarms and even massive freighters at random. I got attacked by large groups of enemies several times in a row just going from station to station. Instead of great, tight dogfights the game just throws large groups of enemies at you.The movement with the mouse feels strange and the crosshair shows your ships profile for some reason making aiming harder than it is.  In addition the control panel used for targeting data, also shows mission updates, and communications (the AI won't shut up). So getting the right information at a glance is difficult.If you can get past all of that then it is a nice little space game. More arcadey than sim. Painting the spaceships gives you full customization in an editor and it is nice to see the damage physically on your ship as modules break.If you can get Freespace 2 on GoG with FSO mods then please check that out. Much better arcade spaceship game and holds up today.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with addicting game play loops, enjoyable art style, interesting story with some decent humor (so far), and an outstanding soundtrack that immerses you in the world. There is a decent selection of ships, meaningful upgrades and the ability to customize your ships appearance through the painting tool. The combat feels solid and while not incredibly difficult you will know when you have tried punching above your weight. Trading isn't my thing but I imagine plenty of people enjoy space trucking around listening to the music. I haven't tried my hand at mining but it is there as an option as well. The mini games (8-ball, arcade, dice, slots) are gimmicky but its nice that they are there. The dice man always beats me so ♥♥♥♥ that guy. This is not a X game, its not elite dangerous, its Rebel Galaxy. It's not trying to be a sim and it creates an enjoyable more laid back experience because of that. Steam gives you two hours to try a game out and still refund it. In that two hours you will have a decent idea if this is for you so for sure try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: Reminiscent of the old Privateer game. I loved every second of the story, the side missions, and exploring the sectors.I gave mining a go, but mostly stuck to the mercenary type work. Always satisfying to overcome the odds.I would say the game lets you get into fights that seem unwinnable, but running is always an option, and you aren't penalized for biting off more than you can chew. Just don't expect to survive every fight.I also had some trouble with the controls, but that was really my own fault. I have a non-DirectInput joystick that I wanted to use, and gave up on trying to map the controls correctly after a few hours.That said, they do recommend you play with a controller, and I even found the mouse and keyboard style easy and intuitive.Highly recommend this game if you have any sort of nostalgia for Privateer or just want to enjoy a fun arcade-style space sim with a great story.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: To fix their terrible flight controls, they added the autopursuit feature. This make fights boil down to 3 things.1.) Press R to lock on to an enemy2.)Hold right mouse to auto-pursuit3.)Hold left mouse to shoot or shift to shoot a missileCongratulations, you are a master at this game. It's a shame, considering how much I liked the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game, with definite potential to be something great. I especially like the mini-game of pool (billiards) in the bars found in every main station. The spacefights are pretty good too, especially after you get a better ship with good shields and more guns. I used a controller, and it was smooth.The story is interesting, and the ability to call in reinforcements for a limited time is very useful.Some kind of ship-builder later on, to create and use custom ships, would increase the rating for this game. The built-in ships are good, but I wanted more variety.Still, it's a fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: REBEL GALAXY OUTLAW is amazing in it's own right, why always compare with the first Rebel Galaxy? This isn't titled Rebel Galaxy 2 for that reason. Still highly recommended and excited where this series goes.I applaud Double Damage for their second entry into the space genre, while Rebel Galaxy has it's own charm (waiting for Rebel Galaxy 2!) While Outlaw certainly isn't perfect, it doesn't have to be, it offers you the same joys as the first, in a different manner of course.Love the whole feel of the series, the look of the ships, the mood, the attention to detail (play several mini games at the space stations) they love what they do and it shows, they take risks and it shows. Dogfights always feel exciting, always at-the-edge-of-your-seat feeling, which is good. And of course there's the option to "paint" your ship using an in-game software, these things certainly add more immersion to an already immersive little world.Double Damage if you can read this thank you for your games, and as a suggestion, in your future game development, a third-person view of the captain that can walk around the ship during space travel, with custom rooms to fill needs (cooking stations, gym, beds, baths, crop plots etc) that would be so amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw is a fast-paced, visually stunning, space combat dog-fighter with one of the best soundtracks in recent gaming. If you're looking for a deep space sim then you'll be better off with Elite Dangerous or Star Citizen. This is for when you wanna get in and out of the action quickly while jamming along with some of the best radio stations in gaming since Three Dog's Galaxy News Radio!After trying to play the game a few times over the years, the poor balancing pushed me away every time. It's just not enjoyable to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Gud game, rough around the edges, I want more content to do because I love the game, and use a controller dipshid.I think this is a great game and I recommend it. Its not perfect by any means. I think my biggest hope for this game is an addon/ free dlc that will add more ships, and more importantly, flesh out the game more. There is a lot of good stuff here but I cant help but want MORE. I wish I could walk around, or see the inside of my ship, or do more at stations and outposts. But before more can be added, that which is already there needs refinement. If you're looking for a AAA title that is perfect in all aspects, good luck. If you want a quirky game with lots of style and a bit of a learning curve, AND IF YOU HAVE A CONTROLLER CUZ FORGET PLAYING THIS ON MOUSE AND KEYBOARD, then this game will be great for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever left a review for a game on steam, and I'm sad that my first review is a negative one, but god, this game just really disappointed me.I will say I do not have a very high bar for games. Brink is hot garbage but I love that game and many other bad games for what they are. I knew going in that this game had mixed reviews, but that didn't bother me. I hadn't played any of the games that influenced this game, and I wasn't looking for a space sim. It looked like at worst it'd be a fun little space western story.And maybe I'd have enjoyed this game if I had a chance to experience said story, but I never had a chance.This game needs a tutorial, and I don't mean tooltips popping up saying use your mouse to aim, I mean an honest to god tutorial. When I took off for the first time, I didn't know what to do. I knew I was trying to deliver some resource to a nearby station, but as soon as I got the controls, I was lost. I've played games like it before, other spaceship controls run off of the same basic principles, but I felt like I had no control over what was happening in this game.I wish I could have played it more, but honestly even at the $7.50 I got it for on sale, it wasn't worth the price.8-ball was fun though.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: I dunno why this game gets so many bad reviews.  Welp, that's actually untrue.  It gets bad reviews because people are either looking for an exact clone of the first or they're looking for an amazing space simulator.  If you're looking for the same attitude and story of the first, but don't mind an updated play-style (you're actually in the cockpit this time and YOU CAN MOVE THREE DIMENSIONAL LOL) then this is your game.  Dogfights are fun, ships are fun, and I really enjoy the mini-games that this game gives you access to such as dice, pool, and slots.  Nice little diversion and more immersion into an actual space station feel.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: A frustrating experience.The game has this "western in space" vibe, not new, but still fun; reminds me of the Killjoys TV show. Cinematics are great, music choices are nice (radio in space, I wish more games had that).When it comes to gameplay, though... The balance is off. Even the first few missions can be frustratingly hard. Mouse and keyboard controls are just terrible. But they warn you that the game was designed for gamepad, so it's fair enough.With a gamepad, aiming and following enemy ships is a lot easier. But scrolling through targets is still a pain, and targeting things like mines that are not considered actual "targets" is more pain.Some basic things are lacking. There seem to be no indicators of enemy health. No fullscreen support for a widescreen monitor. Sound settings don't work, I could not tune down the volume from within the game.Too many bugs to fix before it's worth $10.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I really liked the original Rebel Galaxy, which reminded me very much of playing Freelancer.  This game, however, is more like the old Wing Commander games.  I had to stop playing it because the graphics hurt my eyes because they designed the game to LITERALLY look like Wing Commander.  Also, the field of view seems to be too low.  If you are sensitive to low FOV, just skip this game.  Another thing that I loved about the original Rebel Galaxy was that you used your warp drive to fly quickly through the vastness of space, kind of like using space lanes in Freelancer.  This game, however, you just hit a button and instantly jump to your waypoint.  If you are looking for a Freelancer clone, go buy the original Rebel Galaxy.  But if you are looking for a Wing Commander clone.  Look no further and just hit buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: Elite and X3 didn't start for reasons, so I picked Rebel Galaxy Outlaw. And I think I chose wisely. The X universe bored me and I was a fan of Privateer and Wing Commander. Also, RGO has atmosphere. This universe feels alive to me. Likable characters.Game can be hard, but Privateer was hard, too. So, no problems.I'm surprised this has not so good rating here. Sry for bad english. Lul
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: It saddens me to confirm the mixed reviews are real.  As someone who loved the first game, this one provides frustration and disappointment (and good, although offensively loudly mixed music--fixable in the audio options).The missions are confusing, the 2-D mini map and map system is annoying and boring fasttravel everyhwere (hold E, you are instantly at your destination), and the combat is a bore/chore/hard as ♥♥♥♥ for beginner early missions.  Did a boring cargo mission (straight forward).  Then tried doing some patrol side-missions early on, had no idea what to do (I patrolled/scanned the areas as asked), tried googling, went to a decent dog fight, died, uninstalled and refunded. Flying around in circles while holding right click to lock on and fire was not satisfying at all for me.  Had no interest grinding a downgraded combat and mission system when compared to Rebel Galaxy 1.Make a true Rebel Galaxy 2 sequel please and thanks.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: The overall look is nice, but I dislike the look of the space (e.g. the stars in the background) The story presentation seemed ok. The music was nice, so far. But I really disliked the dogfight/flight mechanics. I know that I didn't even saw 95% the game has to offer, but I didn't like the UI/HUD/Ship interior and the controls... I didn't play many similar games, but I really like the controls and UI/HUD of Elite. Totally differnet games, but for me Elite is much more fun to play/control. I probably could write more of what was missing for me, but long story short - this game is just not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Good music, good combat, good side characters, and a decent story ties it all together. What doesn't work that well is mainly in the technical department.The game only auto-saves when you dock and there is no manual save outside of this. This is usually a non-issue. However, there are times where you will get jumped by pirates or run into a bad encounter that may or may not get you killed early on. You can't easily reload; You have to die first.Additionally, there are some rough edges with in-system travel where it will pilot you into planets or asteroids. Sometimes when you just want to kick back and listen to the amazing sound track, you'll get thrown into a planet or sent right into a rock in your flight path. Couple this issue with auto-save and you get to a point where you'd rather use auto-pilot more frequently just to avoid getting randomly destroyed by the in-system warp.Other issues include balance issues with combat engagements and missing tool tips or explanations on how missile systems work (i.e. - 2 IMREC launchers won't fire two missiles when you hit fire, it will just fire 1 but double your ammo). Finally, there are a bunch of ships but only the ones that can equip max-level equipment are the only viable ones end game. So you only really have 4-5 true end-game ships and everything else are just stepping stones.All that being said -- I enjoyed the game. The combat is fun and is a direct call back to some of the great and hectic battles from some of the best space games in the past. Firing missiles, shunting power to shields, and doing barrel rolls whilst blaring Big Band Swing was not something I expected when I grabbed this game. However, I am not disappointed. It was fun 30 hour romp through space blowing up everything I could get target lock on.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game!I was afraid of buying it after the community bashing everything, but after read some reviews I decided to give it a chance.I didn't regret a single second!Using a hotas, the game is damn fun. It's like being Han Solo or Mando. I'm playing the old school mode (the hardest I think) and the challenge is real. You need to equip your ship to advance and to do it, you will need to get jobs, which range from a simple cargo run or investigation, to patrol and hunt. There is also other activities you can do, like trade, bounty hunt, etc. It's a more fun and dynamic "Elite Dangerous", except that the ships fly more like Star Wars.The dock process is automatic with really well made animations. The interaction inside the bases and outposts are made via menus, while you can see the inside of it, with people and places. Here, I think they missed an oportunnity of a "point and click" feature for navigation, what is sad. The level of care with the details is nice. There is junk flying, little to big meteorites, you can see the damage on the ships, parts flying after being shot, the ship landing is fun to watch, etc. Well, I loved the art.There is a lot of danger in the sectors and you WILL die a lot, until you develop a tactic approach and understand the game "flow", for example "when you need to do jobs to better equip your ship to accomplish that specific mission", and "what build is better for this ship plus my game style".And you can play 8-ball or Asteroid at the bases and outposts bars (and other games).I strongly recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game so far. I have never played any of the other Rebel Galaxies, and that probably helps my enjoyment. It seems a lot of the negative reviews come from people expecting this to be big ship battles and not what is essentially a very true-to-form Privateer remake.This game does a lot of things right.; great atmosphere (think of a mix between Cowboy Bebop and Firefly) , fun flight mechanics and excellent music. Here’s the deal. I’m an ardent fan of the space combat genre and have played most of the popular ones dating back to the hay days of the genre from the early to mid 90’s. This includes the more popular titles like the original Wing Commander and X-Wing/Tie Fighter games as well as the more esoteric releases such as Terminus and Forced Alliance. All this to say that this plays like old school space combat. The enemies don’t do much besides boost away and try for head on attack runs, but, hey, that’s how these games work. Advanced tactical dogfighting is not what this type of game is about. Instead it focuses on simple old school fun and with updated graphics and an entertaining cast of characters. At the end of the day, if you’re an old school space combat fan, you will not be disappointed with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat of a disappointment, their heart is in the right place in many ways, but combat kind of ruins the package.This is clearly trying to be a Privateer Spiritual successor, which is a noble direction. From the ship designs that resemble classic privateer ships (with a more "workmanlike" artsyle) to how you dock at stations, to cockpit designs. This is in many ways similar to that classic.The Art team outdid themselves for the most part (Things kind of blend in with the high saturation killing the otherwise excellent ship/station details, but aside from that the individual pieces are very well done, not to mention some of the best fire/smoke effects I've seen in a game) and they kept the same Music direction from the previous game with a bit more diversity in their music, which I love but if you hate it you can slot your own music in! Also the tools they give you to paint ships are awesome. I'm no artist but the tools feel like something a professional would use.Here's the weird part about combat, The flight model is actually pretty good, kind of a combination of Rouge Squadron and Tachyon the drift. The Weapons also feel pretty good and appropriately weightey but some external factors hurt it. two things kill combat, The first is Autopursuit. For those of you who have played Star Citizen, Remember Autogimbals? For those of you who don't know, Star Citizen has a rather controversial feature where if you have Gimbal mounts, you can turn on a setting that has them lock on to a target and effectively allows you to hit ships without aiming. Well this is like that but worse: Imagine you hold right mouse to not only turn your fixed weapons into autogimbals, BUT it manuvers your ship behind the enemy automatically...generally the best position. This makes combat trivial and boring and makes the only balance lever the devs can throw "How many enemies can we throw at you to overwhelm you?". Personally I'd make the guns gimballed No Man's Sky style (or like in Star citizen, just have a mix of gimbal/Fixed mounts to further differentiate ships), and kill off autopursuit, I think that would be a good medium."Ok Combat becomes utterly trivial and boring with autopursuit,  , but that doesn't ruin an Elite-like" You are correct, becaue its the final problem that made me drop this. You cant dock/Jump if there is combat nearby. Autopilot I get, that makes sense, having to burn away from a fight to not abuse it but you still SHOULD be able to dock/jump if you make it to the respective zones. They even have docking fees as a way to balance abuse of this anyway since its kind of designed for you to have to run a bit tight on cash to progress, assuming you dont grind.So the net result is, lets say you are making a trade run to another system. But  there's a Pirate flotilla on the other side of the gate fighting police....because they are in the general vicinity (despite being out of the way) you cant make a jump out...meaning you have to fight and the only way this game can throw a challenge is by overwhelming firepower, which means you either waste time if you are lucky or limp back to a station where the game ratchets up spawn rates of pirates while you cant run. Yeah this happened to me and caused me to drop it and I can see other similar scenarios play out.In the old rebel galaxy it was often encouraged early game to run, here...not so muchThe general gameplay loops remain the same overall in design from the OG rebel galaxy, Procedural economy (though systems are more handcrafted this time, which is good!) influenced by the state of the system at the time, game opens up quite a bit when you get the jump drive and you can run into distress signals which you can ignore or go to (with a handy setting to straight up ignore them while autopiloting). The Main Difference here is the flight model, instead of broadsides 2D its basically Privateer, which is really a taste thing.Its just too bad the combat design wrecks a promising sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: For those that liked Rebel Galaxy, there is a lot here to like.   For the most part, they haven't changed the formula from Rebel Galaxy all too much:    The ships are smaller (and oddly enough, so are all the bases now to match the ship size) and ship-of-the-line broadside battles have been replaced with 6DOF dogfights.    However, it still all feels part of the same universe.   The attention to detail in the stations are a true high point of the game making it feel that each location is actually different from all the others.  This is a really nice change of pace for most games in this genre.     And of course, it wouldn't be Rebel Galaxy without one of the best soundtracks of any game on the market.  The game has a few UX warts.   Much like in Rebel Galaxy, the game goes out of its way to make finding trade routes a pain, which is strange for a game where trading is a major machanic.    Just having a toggle to switch between  buy rates and sell rates in the sector menu would have been a MAJOR and easy improvement.  Right now you have to wait 3 seconds as it automatically switches back and forth between buy and sell lists.     Also, aiming can be a chore.  It is not so bad in a dogfight, but in the all-too-common "blow up the mines" missions, shooting mines can be a frustrating, unfun chore.  In all, this game feels like the first true spiritual successor to Freelancer and there are LOTS of nods to Freelancer throughout the game, including the use of planetary landing gates and naming every planet after an Earth city (RBO sticks to the American West, while FL used cities around the world).

_childDocuments_.review: Plays like a love letter to the wing commander / privateer games. I picked this up on the EGS when it first came out and I'm having a ton of fun giving it another play-through here.Take your woefully under-armed and fragile garbage truck spaceship and fight, trade, smuggle, and steal your way to the top of the food chain. It's not the longest game, but what's there is stylish as hell and a great deal of fun for anyone looking for more classic space sim action. The cockpits are claustrophobic, each ship has a different layout and you need a few upgrades before your radar feeds you anything useful. But with practice and a little work you'll go from being overwhelmed prey to a god of death, bristling with weapons and taking on whole squadrons without breaking a sweat.It's also got one of the best ship painters in any game ever, if you're willing to put the time in to learn it (or you can just piggy-back on other people's creativity and download some skins).I've been playing with a HOTAS and it plays great, can't speak for mouse/keyboard or controllers.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a lot here. Ship selection is extremely limited, combat leans on the auto-follow function and poor situational awareness essentially requires you to repeatedly pause the game to locate and select targets.The plot's not especially engaging, but even if it were, the protagonist is tiresome and *would* be generic except for how much of a genuine loser she comes off as.The game lifts a lot from Freelancer, except for the gameplay, which is a shame. It also isn't nearly as moddable as the devs seemed to intend, another bummer.With all that said, the music and presentation are excellent and may actually be enough to keep you immersed throughout the game and the gameplay isn't actually bad, it's just that you're likely to master and become bored with it quickly

_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: I regret not playing this game when it was new. It does a whole lot right. It's fast, fun and has a whole lot of style. The menu to navigate stations is elegant and efficient moving you about from scene to scene in a very organic way. If Starfield had the energetic pace of Rebel Galaxy Outlaw space content it would have been a 10/10 game. As for what it is, RGO is a 10/10 in its genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first Rebel Galaxy and want more sea battles in space, lining  up your broadsides then this is problably not for you.If you are an old geezer like me, growing up playing wing commander on your old DOS machine and grinding the hell out of Privateer 1, which was really one of the first "open world" games of the time, then buying this is a no brainer:Phantastic ode to Privateer 1 with a few modern spins on game mechanics and an absolutely stellar soundtrack (if you like Blues and steel guitars). Be warned though, the difficulty curve is quite steep and especially in the lawless systems you may find yourself severely outgunned even on missions that classify as low risk. Plan ahead and prepare your engagements. Make use of the checkpoint mechanic that saves the game when you land at stations. Do it often, especially when your cargo hold is full! Death comes quickly! However, since the game is so fast paced, it usually takes only a few seconds to get back into the action. If you make it through a challenging mission on the third or fouth try, you get a nice sense of accomplishment.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: Soooo... Rebel Galaxy Outlaw wall-of-text initial review::Most of my issues so far are with keyboard mouse controls. This is my own doing as I was too lazy to hook up my Xbox controller. I'll try that down the road. Despite clunky kbm controls the game does have an easy hook into a chill relaxing time delving into a variety of aspects of space. Be it following the main mission, doing side missions, missions for the merchants guild, law missions, and pirate missions or even playing the market buying, transporting and selling goods. I have not quite dealt too deep into pirate missions yet as I'd like to get a better ship first. Not only can you buy better ships but you can outfit them with a variety of improvements. The menu controls are a bit wonky but they do grow on you with use. The game can certainly use some GPU optimization. My 2070 was pegged at 99% most of the time and every now and then on pretty static conversations on a station's bar, my GPU would wind up like it was taking off which this card has never done. Since I have had this GPU I have played plenty of AAA games that this card does not bat an eye at as far as resources needed, yet these seemingly static-ish screens are causing it to kick into overdrive. I hope they optimize this soon. My 3800X CPU barely blipped on usage. The game is single player but is a very relaxing chill experience. Even if you get into a bad situation with enemy ships it is fairly forgiving. This might lend to the difficulty I was playing on as well was Normal. I hardly ever feel the need to burden myself with overly difficult game difficulties. The in-game music is pretty great and the game offers a method to import your own music. It also has an option to select streamer friendly music for those casters that may be concerned about DMCA hits against their profiles. Overall I see myself playing this quite a bit. More so down the road if I see additional GPU optimizations.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: I first want to state that I loved the original Rebel Galaxy and was eagerly awaiting RGO. Sadly I have two issues with the game, the graphics, man these graphics remind me of Wing Commander and maybe that was the point. But only after a few minutes of play I was getting eye strain. Second I was trying to setup the HOTAS, again it was really hard work, (got to think they had game pad in mind) when making this game. It kept wanting to map my throttle to menu selections even after changing them, after about 10 minutes I gave up.  Now the questions of price, is it worth what they are asking? Simple answer NO! I may come back to this title at a later date when it's on sale and I would recommend anyone that uses a HOTAS to do the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs up from me. I see the Privateer/Freelancer/Firefly influences. Definitely on the casual side, and you can stumble onto unwinnable fights from time to time but I've had pretty good success running away - mash the booster, flail around, and get behind something big until you can jump away from the fight. It's not a full on space sim, or a flying spreadsheet with a complex economic system. Travel times are short, and a lot of the side missions are too. Just good causal fun with a catchy soundtrack. I've spent more time and credits than I want to admit on gambling and playing pool at the stations.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: Finally!!  A worthy successor to Wing Commander Privateer. For years I have been searching for a WC Privateer remake which captures the essence of that classic and Double Damage has done the job. Many have come close but they have never really reached the same level. For those who love Privateer this will be a nostalgic trip down memory lane but with really great sound and graphics. It has its issues but overall its pretty good!What I love about it- Easy to get started and get immersed into the universe. Storyline is easy to follow and missions are available right of the bat.  Ship upgrade tree is also very simple and easy to understand. Overall its an easy game to get going. Learning curve is not very steep.- The graphics are a throw back to WC but I love them! I know many will complain about them but I really like the nostalgic feel. The space views are gorgeous and the stations and planets are nicely designed. - Once you get the hang of the controls (which can be tricky), space combat is fun and easy. This is definitely not a sim so don't expect a million options. Its just point, fly and kill. It does have some nice settings like the combat view which allows you to get a feel for the tactical picture. in a nutshell flying and blasting is fun. - Music is awesome with a virtual multiple radio channels to listen to in-flight. Adds a nice new dimension to the game.- Love being in a WC type universe which keeps bringing up nostalgic memories. I think this will be the best feature for old WC fans.What really needs work- The menus are all over the place especially the main menu and the in-game contextual menu. Took me a while to figure it out. They really need to streamline these.- Playing with the mouse-keyboard combination was hell. Took a lot of finessing to get the mouse feel just right. This definitely needs work!- Navigation is really confusing especially in missions with multiple way points. Auto pilot keeps getting interrupted by jump gates, other ships etc and its hard to figure out where you actually have ended up. This could definitely be streamlined- Ships and upgrades are few and expensive in the game which means you really need to spend a lot of time completing missions. It can be a grind sometimes and adds to the overall play time but the variety of mission types can offset the monotony. Maybe they can add a few more intermediate ship types to easy the upgrade ladder a bit.- They have remained true to the WC privateer with the space stations/planets functionality but it is a missed opportunity to do more with them. After a while they all feel the same and one dimensional, which was also the issue with the original WC Privateer. The games in the bar are nice but I would have liked something else connected with the game itself rather then random gambling. A missed chance here.- Would have love a better connection with passing space craft such as in Interstellar Pilot where you can trade even with passing freighters. This is another area where game depth can be added. - Jumping between jump gates can be very tedious and the graphics are repetitive and annoying. There is also a pause as the new location loads up but not a major issue.- It crashes! Although the game play specs are not very high it does crash an awful lot. I think that will improve as the game is updated but yeah, its got to stop crashing.Overall am enjoying this nostalgic journey into the WC privateer type universe. Lots of hours of gameplay ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: Great trading, great dogfights in real 3D (with full 3D trajectories unlike its predecessor), great music, and a variety of ships to optimize, depending on your playing style. There's an autopilot feature built in which you can engage to make it easier to intercept enemy craft during dogfights which makes entry into the gameplay mechanics encouragingly easy, but in the more difficult fights against a capital ship with multiple support fighters, or against a large gang (police fighters or some of the nastier pirates), you'll still get killed quite a bit. As you gain experience, you learn to use the autopilot judiciously, cutting in with manual control of steering and velocity, afterburner, and inertial damper override in order to become a dogfighting expert. This provides a nice balance between gameplay which would otherwise be so hard as to be discouraging in the beginning, vs. gameplay so easy and requiring so little acquired skill as to be boring and lack challenge. For some missions and enemy gangs, optimizing your choice of ship and loadouts can strongly influence your success. In-game main missions are pleasantly deep, but there's no time pressure to complete them and there are also lots of side missions you can pursue instead, including trading, blockade running, assassination, hijack/piracy, and escort missions.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really craving this sort of game and I loved the first, so I figured two years after release it would be fine.  Nope. Playing Outlaw, I see a HUGE assortment of really cool ships in space, but couldn't find almost any to buy.  Upon looking it up, there are only 12 ships you can fly and half of them are duplicates with slightly different specs.  The very first ship you can afford to upgrade to is basically the best and it's a huge letdown.  I'd love to fly some of those awesome ships I see all over the place, but nope.  No fun here.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes it was an epic exclusive, and even though it is full price a year later I feel it was worth it given the time I spent playing it. I was using mouse and keyboard and lining up your shots can be challenging. Often times I was fighting the autoaim for placing shots and the variety of ships seems really limited and there are too many enemy engagements that boil down to enemies magically spawning in a circle around you.What it all breaks down to is that this is NOT a very deep space fighting game. There is no point in trading or mining.Things I did enjoy was the mini games and some of the quests. It would have been really cool to be able to go to some of the events that are advertised on the radio i.e. the Robot Rumble.If you are a fan of simple space fighters that are not too expensive this is a good game and I can recommend it for that. _childDocuments_.review: I’ve been waiting 26 years for Privateer 2!As a kid, I remember spending $75 for the WC: Privateer CD-ROM (with included add-on and speech pack!). We played that game to death. Many years and disappointing non-sequels later (The Darkening SUCKED), we finally have the spiritual and literal successor to Privateer! _childDocuments_.review: Engaging and fun little space shooter - a perfect blend of "Wing Commander Privateer"-ish open world + storyline gameplay and Firefly-like blue collar / Redneck atmosphere, with an impressive soundtrack.Shoot, trade, mine, scout, or pirate your alter ego June through both the storyline and the open world this game has on offer. Hop on one of the side quests to earn yourself a companion for helping out in combat - or to get and to equip your own space station maybe?Gameplay is pretty arcade-y, you basically fly a jet in space, battling small fighters, medium fregattes, and massive destroyers. Apart from a single-button induced "drift" mode (which is quite useful for sniping capital ships' turrets) there's no true free six axis movement. Arcade feeling is augmented by a "auto pursuit" feature which, by pressing+holding a button, controls speed and direction of your ship, helping to get the target you've locked into view. Arguably, this serves its purpose of spending less time overshooting your target and turning, and more time shooting - which helps maintaining gameplay fun even with the massive amount of fights the game throws at you.Arcade shooting aside, space combat is surprisingly tactical  - just storming in guns blazing rarely yields success, even with end-game equipment. Ignoring the freeze-time "targeting mode" which offers a tactical display of your immediate environment will have you explode a lot and will fail most missions fast - no matter if you are trying to protect, or to kill something. But using situational awareness to your advantage will get you a massive bonus and help mastering fights - there's a learning curve here.Each of the "careers" (game loops) have their own little learnings. The game offers specialisation via a variety of ships and equipment - paying attention and mastering each takes little time and feels very satisfying.There are some obvious ship / equipment choices - like a full grade-4 equipped Coyote for hit-and-run / assassinations (make that a Dingo if you really like missiles!) - but all "careers" have their own specific end-game equipment.Running delivery missions may start small in the Platypus, yielding a few thousand bucks per run - but will eventually culminate in a cyclic booster - powered Sequoya, stacking long haul / gauntlet Guild missions for more than 100 times the buck.Mining may feel cumbersome at start - but eventually you'll make it to the Beluga, using its three mining turrets to strip-mine whole asteroid fields at once.Pirating is hard because you either get shot or you don't have the storage for scooping even a single convoy's worth of goods? Stay tuned, and eventually hammer your victims with the heavy Mattock, all while scooping up tons and tons of stuff.Enjoy fighting and bounty hunting, but continually find yourself at the receiving end of pain distribution? Wait 'til you sit in a Foxbat, when you'll be looking for pirate lords just to get these juicy raw weapons, bringing the fight to them.On overall, while both the ship count and the equipment options are quite limited it feels like most options mean something and are in the game for a reason.That said, the game does feel rather small - which is understandable given independent studio Double Damage's size. While the main story is quite long and will keep you engaged for many hours, the specialisations are usually mastered in a few hours. I'm currently on my second playthrough - bought the game for PC after finishing it on Switch - and less than 10 hours into the game I'm in my beloved Foxbat, fully grate-4 equipped. I'd expect to master the other careers in 1-2h each. Maybe the official ModKit (to be released in 2021[??]) will add more options / diversity.Wrapping things up, here's my "getting started" recipe (first 8-10 hours in the game):1. Run local delivery missions until you can afford a tractor beam, mining scanner, and mining laser - optionally a cargo extension (27k - 39k total). Depending on the difficulty you might want to sell equipment to get there faster - like selling your weapons, and switching your radar for a cheaper one.2. Go mining - fly to asteroid fields, scan, fly to asteroids, and shoot glowing spots. This is a great opportunity to play with, and master, the "drifting" mode of flying. Expect to get 20k - 30k per run, so all your expenses above will be compensated after 1-2 mining runs!3. Mine ~200k bucks. Sell your grade-1 cargo extension, mining laser, and scanner, and switch to a Sonora w/ jump drive, cyclic booster, and grade-2 shields, power plant, and cargo extension. Join the Merchant's Guild. Find "Gauntlet", "Guild cargo haul", or "long haul" missions - these pay between 15k and 35k each, so expect 50k-100k per run. Prefer low-cargo missions over highest-paying, pick missions that go into roughly the same direction, stack as many missions as your cargo space allows, and travel the galaxy. Don't pick fights; instead, put your energy into shields and thrusters and just boost off.4. After making ~600k bucks shippping goods, buy a Foxbat, grade-4 equip it, add Autocannons, Photons, and Swarm missiles, then go out and shoot things!

_childDocuments_.review: Both a blast and a bit of a grind. Some reviewers have compared it with Wing Commander. That's true, but if you want to old-school the comparison, it's more like Sid Miers' Pirates! in space. Lots of fun and funny characters. Bartenders with just a drop-down menu system. Lots of buy and sell and like Pirates!, diversions like mini games. I am addicted to it, but not 100% in a good way. More like Evercrack or Mount and Blade. I want to get over hurdles to progress. That said, the combat system is fun (unless you encounter unfair odds). The save system is meh. The building up on your ship is really insightful and a blast once you begin to have a bad-ass machine. Decent main storyline and I really like the tone. Kind of Sergio Leone meets Borderlands. It's less GTA because it feels less sand-boxy and GTA is sometimes ugly in tone. This is just a fun, trippy adventure in space.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit to the review before starting: I flipped my thumb to down because of this statement I put in the initial review about the main quest: but the other the have been, "quick, dodge an oncoming onslaught from multiple ships that can tear through your defenses like butter, but don't attack back because you don't stand a chance."The hijack quest....I kept my distance and fled as fast as possible. Still was torn through. Don't play this unless you want to do all side quests of have a decent pool simulator. The main quest is crap.Well on to the original review:I grew up on games like Space Raiders, Star Wars Arcade, Wing Commander, and X-wing. I picked this up through a bundle for like a couple bucks. I also picked up Rebel Galaxy around the same time.Now, I am recommending this game....but it is a "its decent" recommendation...and not an "OMG YOU GOTTA GET THIS!!!" game.RGO does a lot right in the actual control and combat, to bring me back to those days of playing games like Wing Commander and X-wing. It also retains a lot of the exploration that RG had, except autopilot makes it faster jumps (so you will see less of the universe...which is good and bad at the same time). So you get the exploration still, but you don't.However, the problem is the actual story...or at least how it starts. I've done about 4 primary missions. Two of them have been "fly to a station and dock". That is fine and all, but the other the have been, "quick, dodge an oncoming onslaught from multiple ships that can tear through your defenses like butter, but don't attack back because you don't stand a chance."I like the combat. I like the transport missions. But I am not digging the main mission..and that is a problem. There is only so many "transport from here to there" or "wipe out these ships" side missions that I can do before it gets redundant. If the main mission can't hold my attention...I might not get as much out of the game.Overall, its fun, but might not last. That is fine for me seeing how I got it for a couple bucks. I enjoy playing it, but might not get as much time as I got in RG.Still if you are looking fora good space fighter, this is not bad.

You're either turning at a snail's pace or spinning around at crazy fast speed. Probably better with a controller, not tried it yet, but with mouse + kb it's a mess.Then there's the ever present right-click-to-win mode. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. Rebel Galaxy was one of my favorite space games in years... But I don't plan to keep playing Outlaw. I'm kinda sad that this is the sequel to something so much better.The difficulty is ALL over the place: Every time you upgrade your ships components the enemies seem to become stronger by proportion. The early grind is misery because two different iterations of the same "easy mission" can have VASTLY different challenges. anything from one beginner pirate fighter to an entire wing of gunships that can pub stomp the large NPC ships in seconds.The AI has a 150000% hit rate btw, even with your after burners on and an ecm you get missle spammed to death.  The controls are a mess: You need a second party download to use a controller. And there is this AWFUL dead zone in the actual control of the ships. It's make it feel like the fights are happening in a sea of jello.There's a sticky aim on steroids that lets you auto track targets (because it is literally impossible to hold a target manually) But it just lets everything else on screen put 27 missiles up your thermal exhaust port while you try to figure out were its coming from.  And the Mini games are just a system for punishing the player for their time.Some of the 8-ball players give really good early game gear for beating them but 97% of all the billiard players are clearly just Minnesota Fats in different disguises. I cannot express enough my hate for that mini game in words so ill do it in song: *Ahem* Mimimimi lalala AAAAAAAAARRRRRGGGGGGG!!!!!!Overall I'm just so... Disappointed. This game could have been great. It may STILL be great by the end game. But the problems just don't make it feel like its worth the effort to find out. I play games to de-stress after work. Not to feel like i'm still working. And Rebel Galaxy Outlaw just feel like a chore.
_childDocuments_.name: Rebel Galaxy Outlaw

_childDocuments_.review: Though a departure from the gamelplay of Rebel Galaxy, I personally enjoy the different cockpits and first person gameplay as it ties in much of the simplicity of the first. On the other hand, it can be odd adjusting to a new HUD in each one and being able to discern weapons, shields, etc. Minor inconvenience however. On the other hand, the limited choices of ships and classes (obviously, I'm talking about how much I want another dreadnought) did disappoint me, as it was the primary factor which led me to Rebel Galaxy. It's also unfortunate to lose the use of broadsides entirely. Though I can understand why it didn't work as well in this game, I'd have gladly waited for the devs to find a way to make this work. Of course, these are minor setbacks as I'm thoroughly enjoying the gameplay (when I'm not randomly targeted by space protestants that absolutely obliterate me in the top tier ships) and fully anticipating modders to find a way to work around the details. What I'd really like to see in the future, however, is all of this thought through and implemented, and perhaps even a much more interesting docking gameplay, perhaps even full blown rpg elements of choice and character creation. But I'm getting waaaaay ahead of things and for me, Rebel Galaxy and Outlaw were already groundbreaking in their own way. I've just been playing too much TES, give me a break. Hell, I'm just happy this is a relatively new game that my computer can actually play.Edit: Upon further gameplay, i did notice a few quirks that bother me. 1. Occasionally, I'll make a jump and the entire system will have some graphic problem until I leave to another.2. It constantly switches my primary missions when I'm headed toward another, redirecting me to a mission I did not intend to initiate.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of the original game, Rebel Galaxy. Until yesterday (the release day), I had no idea that this game existed. I was so excited to come home after work and to give it a try.Unfortunately, this instalment feels like a huge step backwards.My only pro is the concept, but it is based on the previous game. Everything else is just absurdly bad.This is an year old game, which feels like it needs a lot of re-work. The problem stems from the fact that it was primarily made for consoles and to play on a TV. FOV is horrible and the graphics feels like it was made for 4:3 800x600. UI is oversimplified and just not user friendly.Graphics is mediocre.There is, apparently, 20 hours of soundtracks, however, I am not big fan of the music genre. And if you mute the music, you may miss on "radio announcement" opportunities. [to be verified]There is a very limited number of flyable ships.Progress is just out of balance. Lots of grinding and lots of luck. For example, taking an average mission to kill pirates may lead you to a swarm of pirates who swarm you with missiles... aaand game over. If you succeed, you get paid only 6k credits.The main mission should give the player some advantage in credits, so the player can move forward. However, to progress, the player needs super ship or huge luck. Grind and luck should not be requirement for progression.After buying a new ship and focusing on ship upgrades (mainly weapons and shields), the missions for the current area disappear, so you have to grind for a jump drive. ..And still had no luck with the main plot.Map is just low-rez really bad. Travel has been oversimplified, you can autopilot jump from A to B in a second (with a beautiful cutscene). I know that no one is forcing me to use this feature, but it is immersion breaking. _childDocuments_.review: Unlike the first Rebel Galaxy, this sequel drops the broadside focus and shifts to a more traditional space-sim with a focus on small fighters rather than large capital ships. The music is still as good as the first game's, that much hasn't changed. Gameplay is similar to the first game, where you do various missions, such as protecting ships, attacking them, hauling cargo, or sourcing cargo. The main downside to the game, IMO, are the controls. It feels like the game was made for consoles, or at least gamepad users, over mouse and keyboard users. Controlling your ship with mouse and keyboard feels sluggish in comparison to using it with a gamepad, which I think the developers should really look into. Also, there aren't as many ships as in the first game, although I can kinda understand that as they have to make interior cockpits for them now, and all ships have different ones (even the HUD is different on them), so I can understand it. Overall I had fun in the short time I've played it so far, but the controls for mouse and keyboard really hurt the experience IMO. _childDocuments_.review: If you want Privateer on a modern engine buy it on GOG and look up Gemini Gold, because while this is blatantly inspired by Privateer it doesn't play like Privateer.Combat deviations from Privateer include:-The AI director is no longer limited to around 3 to 5 actors per Nav point, meaning it can setup scenarios that are more like 12v1.-To partially compensate for that you have buddies you can summon to operate as wingmen.-The AI director has a much more extensive list of ships for opponent factions to draw upon ensuring that combined with sheer quantity and the ability to do waves that it can apply the pressure regardless of what you're fighting.-Associated with that this game neither has a Wing Commander style fixed fuel reservoir for Afterburners or a dedicated recharging reservoir like FreeSpace, instead the afterburner draws from your gun reservoir which in Wing Commander style gets depleted quickly meaning for most of the game Afterburners are only useful for trying to cruise past interdiction encounters.-Along those lines in Privateer you usually could simply burn to a Jump Point or station and AutoDock.  Here you have to clear out the enemies before jumping or docking.-Combat in this game ultimately thus has a lot of pressure to thin out enemies quickly during the more challenging encounters.Mechanical deviations from Privateer include:-The Wing Commander style inertial flight system has been nerfed so activating it drops you out of Afterburner.  This nullifies the main reason you would use it in Privateer or other Wing Commander games as without the afterburner cruise option, this just makes you a target.-This game has a system that will automatically orient your ship to have a target in your front view.  Please see comment above about the games focus being on killing enemies quickly.Trade deviations from Privateer include:-Your cargo holds are significantly smaller than any of the ships in Privateer.-Most places you land with a Commodities market do not have anything for sale, just things they want to purchase.  So the classic Privateer cycle of doing shooty missions while hauling a load of loose cargo largely isn't a thing.-The main use for the Commodities markets thus ends up being a combination of selling off cargo tractored in from people you killed and asteroids you mined.  -There are missions to haul loads of cargo and to source a certain amount of a particular type of cargo which calls upon awareness of what the odd stations are that sell this or that commodity.This game has a lot of character and plays well enough despite a bit of a rough mid-game period during your first run, so I'm giving it a recommend.  Caveat emptor though that the above makes for a bit of a rough mid-game during the initial playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played for 11 minutes and I already feel disappointed. The combat, which is arguably the most important part of the game, is extremely simple. Why?: You do not have to lead targets because of enemy movement or your projectile velocity.  as long as your generously large crosshair is in the general direction of your enemy.: There is a button (right mouse) that makes you automatically look at your currently targeted enemy. To kill the enemy, hold right mouse button for automatic target pursuit and left mouse button to fire guns.Now that's what I call engaging gameplay!EDIT: While you can indeed remove the crutch-heavy gameplay with a higher difficulty setting, the two hardest ones also remove your ability to use third-person view for some reason. I wanted to use that because the cockpit view is claustrophobic, the dashboard looks both terrible and has neon lights all over, so I chose the second difficulty. I unbound the auto-follow key but the auto-leading can never be disabled this way.All reviews that talk about how you can't leave a fight are completely true. _childDocuments_.review: I wish there was an "eh" rating.  Its fine-ish but there is a lack of player ship variety, creating some odd missing roles between the ships that do exist.  There is also a lack of weapon and component variety as compared to Galaxy 1, and entire categories of components missing such as the main ship engines.There are also some confusing decisions between the first Rebel Galaxy and Outlaw that are both minor, and have large negative effects, the best example of this is the new inability to use gates or dock with stations with hostile crafts nearby, meaning that outfitting a reasonable sized cargo ship to be very fast  to run blockades in high danger areas is no longer viable.These are all problems that could be fixed as the core of the gameplay is generally good, but I suspect development on this title is mostly over at this point so I won't be holding my breath. _childDocuments_.review: A generally fun space arcade/sim that worth the price. Once you do get over that curve, thn the game starts feeling a lot more balanced as the devs intended with the occassional challenge.My tip for newbies: if you find yourself struggeling in the beginning because your starting vessel is utter crap, here's what you do: Do a few low-risk missions to get some cash then buy the mining radar and and mining laser. Once you have those, go to any "belt" or "cloud" within your sector and mine the heck out of everything, fly back to the station and sell. Do this enough (maybe an hour or so) in the beginning and you will quickly get the best ship with the best weapons and components

_childDocuments_.review: Double Damage are a five person team and I think this game is an incredible achievement from such a small team. The fact that a five person team, in less than 5 years, can make this game really makes me question what on earth has been happening with Star Citizen.Many butthurt reviewers talk about how unforgiving the games combat is, with many people saying it needs balancing. I feel sorry for these people and the clear lack of attention they've given to the game. When you feel overwhelmed by your opponents, you can literally just radio them and ask them not to attack you. I've noticed that the more overwhelming your opponents, the more likely it is that they will respond back to say they'll let you go. It's a bit like fleeing from wild Pokemon battles in those games. I imagine this is Double Damage's way to keep things balanced while still being able to put you in "oh s****!" situations.After just over 10 hours, this is pretty much "Elite Dangerous Lite" with a heavy Firefly vibe.When I got my jump drive and left the starter star system for the first time (there are forty systems to explore), I got an achievement for leaving the starter system. I found that only 33% of players have this achievement. This suggests that only 33% of players have actually played the game properly enough to get into the actual "meat & potatoes" of it all. With this in mind, I think you should take many of the reviews here with a large grain of salt.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: this review may fluctuate between up and down. I think the game deserves to be bought on discount (they already had discounts on Epic) of if the developers add more features and polish the game.Edit2: Considering that I nominated this game for the best soundtrack (Autumn 2020), I feel I should switch to positive review now /Edit2Negative:- bad structured game menu- ships near jump gates enter the area, approach and bump into it. They never use the jump gate. Not sure if you can track ships to see where they come from and where they go- the controls are almost ok even when playing with mouse and keyboard.The problem I had is that activating tractor beam requires a long press on a button which serves as speed up or warp to a station. So you can actually do stupid things: crashing into asteroids or leaving mission zone by mistake.Edit: this made me switch from positive to negative- mining is the easy way to win the game in a few hoursEdit2: visiting the forum once more I see that there is a targeting mode, which makes missions much easier to play as you gave a good overview about your position related to the enemies. That should have a keybinding too as I didn't used it during fights.Positive:After just 2.5 hours the immersion kept me playing more.I think the game deserves 72% rating for those who want to play the story.I do not own the previous Rebel Galaxy and I cannot compare to that one.This one has that retro feeling of old space sim games.It is achieved by the amazing background music and the way the game is structured.After you loose your ship in the intro sequence, you get a small ship which you have to upgrade or replace with other better ships.To get the money for that you can:- get side missions from a terminal- talk with the bartender to get bounty missions or tips where you can buy cheaper- play some games in the bar (dice, 8-ball) or slot machine- buy products and transport them to sell them in a different place- mine asteroids (not done that yet)You can join mercenaries' or merchant's guild for some benefits and maybe more missions or story. On forum somebody mentioned faction equipment too.These are the game settingsAnd the sector mapI spent half an hour to get familiar with game menu and to customize the controls.This game simply ends when you press ESC in a certain screen instead of showing a game menu :)The difficulty levels are: - Normal (more starting equipment)-Veteran (limited starting equipment)- Sim (no aim assistance, 1st person mode only)- Old School (no flight or aim assistance, 1st person mode only)I chosen the normal start to have no trouble with targeting.There is also a "flight training" which I had no patience to play until the end.The information was presented too fast.But the game can be learned "as you play".While traveling form a place to another, your autopilot can be disengaged by distress signals or enemy ship presence. _childDocuments_.review: For some background, may as well outline what I'm comparing this to. I like flight/space sims a lot, though I'm not someone that ritually picks up flight sims;  is my go-to for mechanic-laden ship flight that just happens to have an FPS MMO attached to it, and I cut my teeth repeatedly on , , a brief stint with  on PS1, and () back in the day.  kind of obtuse and slow for what it is. I wasn't really expecting a ton, but I started playing  after this, which was a game that I played four years ago and dumped on as was warranted at the time. I fired this back up thinking maybe I just needed to give it another shot, but this UI is just... I absolutely loath it. It's long and requires scrolling. It is what I can only describe as "mushy" when using a mouse to navigate. There's no confirmation for things like leaving a station, too, which is pretty damn annoying. The cockpit view is definitely going for that old school feel, but I think that it's too cramped and much too hard to see what you're doing in-game.I think the atmosphere is really cool and I like the ideas, but the combat isn't really doing anything for me in conjunction with the UI problems. Navigating a station is slow despite being menu-driven. There's some cool features to this game for sure, like painting your ship (seriously, well done; probably the best thing about the game to be honest) and even printing a 3D model of it if you have a printer.I also thought the main character was cool, though the animated frameup of how this situation occurs doesn't... make sense to me?  It's admittedly hard to get into  a game where you think your character is an ineffective idiot that is racking up debts due to bad planning in the revenge business, regardless of how "rusty" they are.Pains me to say I'll probably refund due to, in my opinion, a lack of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: A Truly disappointing Sequel with enough shine to make it stand out for itself despite the ever suffocating desire to play something else…Sometime in the last few years, the success of Rebel Galaxy stood out amongst the sea of indie games plaguing the Steam store. Understandably, this success inspired the continuation of this beloved indie franchise to the space reverberating roar of approval from a dedicated and passionate fanbase.Then as years pressed on, the noise of our combined Spotify playlists playing space cowboy music dwindled into the early hours of the morning, and the first footage of the sequel was made public. The reaction could only be described as “denial”.Over the years, many successful games that did so unbelievably well that they warranted a sequel, did so with the hidden threat of failure waiting to strike. Many games did so well they became household names only to inevitably die after they attempted to “modernize” and chase whatever Dragon some overpaid and undereducated focus group deemed appropriate. We have seen this failure with the Command and Conquer, Metal Gear Survive, Dawn of War, Kill Zone - All adjusted on the whims of Fat Rich Corporate asshat who decided they simply knew better,  to target a customer that was either not interested, or didn’t exist…And now we “may” have to heap this into the bargain bin.I purchased this game on sale for $8 - I played this for about 30 minutes, then reviewed about an hour's worth of gameplay footage in hopes that maybe it will get better eventually. I may try to play this again… eventually… maybe… or I may just go back and play the original Rebel Galaxy or even their successful competitors they tried and failed to compete with.Regardless, I’m not going to even ask for a refund - I only hope they put our money into making an actual sequel to Rebel Galaxy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute blast to play.Its basically Privateer 2 done really well (i never played Privateer, sorry).Combat is like Elite FAO but with better controls for faster more fluid drifty fun combat. Gameplay consist of building up your credits to improve your ship by doing jobs or mission or mining. The aim being to make it able to cope with the story mission which sometimes are a little tricky. Once you have a good ship the game does open up but the downside is theres no reason to use the lower ships later into the game. Missions have really good variety considering you are either blowing stuff up, blowing stuff up or scanning stuff!. Ok there is a trading system and trading mission like blockade runs too. But the game leans very heavily into its combat. Which is fine if you want to live a pirate life and just grab tons of loot too sell!As a pirate you can use coms to demand traders drop cargo or blow em up and take it anyway. The downside is you have to sell it at stations with a black market OR become a full pirate and open up the pirate star bases. But its a fun way to play the game.Now replayability. I think there are a few mission where you can make choices but i don't feel the need to go play them again to see the different choices. But outside of the main story campaign what you have is a neat little sandbox that never feels too overwhelming like Elite Dangerous or too vague like No Mans Sky.Its a neat little game that does what it set out to do very well.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I have to state that I'm friends with the devs and received the game as a gift. That said I'll do my best to be as honest and unbiased as I can be. The pro's-If you like Wing Commander:Privateer and have been thirsting for games like it and Freelancer you've found your game. It has just enough story to make it interesting without it getting it in the way and the ship design and combat are well thought out. It's a straight-up dogfighter of old with a few improved bells and whistles. While it's not as grand in scope as Star Wars and not as focused on the minutia of trading and exploring as something like No Man's Sky or Elite:Dangerous it makes up for it in fun and mood. Tons of great music and colorful characters. Cons-It's 3D space combat and not on a 2D plane like the first. If you liked that kind of stuff you won't find it here. If you don't like dark country music, alt hard rock or latin/classical you're not going to like the soundtrack. If you're looking to tailor-make your own character you won't find those options here. The story is about a woman named Juno and serves as a prequel to the first game. If you prefer mouse and keyboard to gamepad you're out of luck. The game was designed around the gamepad. Finally, there aren't a ton of ships to be found. That said as of this review the devs are discussing adding content later. I really like this game. I have about 120 or so hours on it over on Epic and will be playing it more here now that it's on Steam. If it weren't for the fact someone gave it to me before I had a chance to pay for it I would have but it's up to you to decide whether or not to believe me there. All I know is this game is fun and I hope they're interested in maybe fleshing out the universe a bit more and letting us get to know Juno a little better in the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: If you ever wanted to feel like a space truck driver that really pretty much stays a space truck driver for the whole time, this is the game for you.So this game is not for everyone and i think many of the negative reviews come from people who wrongly assumed it was a game that would appeal to them. So I want to try to describe the appeal this game has and why i love it.First of all, i loved Freelancer as a child and Rebel Galaxy Outlaw is in many ways Freelancer's spiritual successor, so if you liked Freelancer, you will love this game. RGO is not Star Wars Battlefront or a generic space shooter. It's more like a simulation of being an everyday person in space, that has been an everyday person for their whole life and after hours of gameplay you will be a slightly richer everyday person. Pirates will gang up on you and blow you to pieces especially in early game, because you are a space trucker with a garbage space truck that transports gold ore to a refinery in Kansas, so it is best to get the hell away from those pirates, because as it turns out, an everyday trucker is no match for 4 guys with guns. This game is hard and can be frustrating but i really enjoy the experience.That being said, it is not hard, like for example souls like games. You do not just die at every corner, but you might die quite some times. The main difference to souls likes is the different feeling of accomplishment. Because in Dark Souls, the bosses are big scary and powerful, and the other lowly beings that will kill you, are still scary and powerful. In RGO, you will regularly be killed by 4 annoying drunk guys with guns.  And so you grind your way up, buying your first slightly better ship, with better weapons and you are suddenly able to effectively shoot back. And that's were the game rewards you. Because it's really nice to finally have the upper hand against someone you have actually grown to hate. You have a sense of bitter sweet accomplishment for running 6 tons of whiskey trough a blockade, because you damn near got killed while trucking 6 tons of whiskey to a casino in Nevada, so that gambling ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ can get drunk. The things you do, to make a few bucks.People complain that your field of view is really bad in your starting ship. Yes, that might be, because it is a garbage truck. All the freighters in the game have cockpits that make fighting harder, because they are not designed to fight. Fighters have better view, but are also limited, because, have you ever seen an actual fighter cockpit? These don't have the best view. You will quite often rely on your radar and i consider it a good thing, as it feels immersive.If you start the game in higher difficulties you might not even have a radar that can descern who is an enemy, which i really don't enjoy, but hey, you are after all piloting a garbage truck and this might be the thing to do if you want even more immersion.The soundtrack is also great, because you have radio stations that play really generic music that you kinda hate, but find yourself singing to at many points, because they are catchy, so basically like real life.The controls are clunky, yes. That being sad, i only play with mouse and keyboard, and I really enjoy myself. I set the controls to the setting I know from Freelancer by heart, primary weapon on the space bar and exclusively steering with the mouse, which i find, make the controls far less frustrating. And again, at the start, you are steering a garbage truck.Another criticism i have is the autopilot, which really can break apart the immersion, because of loading times. This could be fixed, if the sublight speed was not so freaking slow, getting from one point to another in the same system in under a minute flight time without autopilot would be such an improvement and it is something Freelancer actually did better.Overall, don't play this game if you want an action packed hero's journey. But give it a shot if you want the most fun and rewarding everyday-space-person-simulator in existence.
