I guess because it's "the Future" nothing has to make sense. It's like a pulp science fiction book you read where the plot is stupid and you know it's stupid but you keep reading anyway because the writing is decent and there's the occasional interesting idea.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - 5/10 This is a hard one to do, i'd likely give it a neutral rating if I could as its a hard game to quantify in many ways, on one hand you have an amazingly well realised world, that immediately pulls you in, with some fantastic world building, interesting characters and a uniquely portrayed post-apocalyptic world. The writing side I give them absolute full marks on.Same with the companions and characters met, they were always interesting to deal with and talk to and left me wanting more and yet, I got a few hours in and lost my drive to continue. This is due to the gameplay loop / mechanics, now it may just be a case of this type of game not being for me, but it felt I was having to scour every inch of the map to find any potential objects that might assist and move the game forward, worse after a certain point (post warden) the direction really began to feel obscure, which is a real shame as with slightly more direction, it may have completely changed things, but instead it left me feeling forced to wander and without a good log to pursue, it just felt unfocused, I do not doubt there is a good story there and I do wish to see what else the game has to offer, but it felt like it was not respecting my time to experience it. It is rare that I feel that it being a visual novel or a walking simulator would have benefited it far more than what we have, but here we are, it is clear that the developer has a clear vision on what it wants and I wish them all the best as they drip with potential, but they do need to tighten their gameplay up.I will be watching them going forward and encourage the hardcore point and click players to give it a try, otherwise likely stay clear.A very unpolished gem.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: 4.5/10The entire game is a giant fetch quest simulator, go here go there take this item and open that conversation, the game world/stage is big but filled with empty spaces with almost no meaningful exploration, voice acting is pretty avg and your companions do nothing 99.9% of the time, they just follow you around and occasionally give you some dialogues.Only plus for me is the artistic concept of the world and the attempt for replayable narrative story lines tied with moral system. I think the problem is due to budget and time constrains they went too big and too ambitious for this game, if they cut the scale by 1/3 or even half, make it a 2 part/3 part games and focus on deeper game mechanics for each part it would've turned out to be great, I think anyone who have played games like primordia, myst, riven would agree.I finished stasis bone totem before this and can see they are already making adjustments, really hope their next game would be another solid 9/10 like bone totem, sadly, I can't recommend beautiful desolation.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: When I looked at this game and bought it, I thought this is closer to Fallout 1/2, but it is very far from it. There are almost no RPG elements here and it is mostly an isometric point a click adventure game. That does not make it any less of an fantastic game, with beautiful graphics and interesting story. The world is very unique and interesting to explore, lots of "out of this world" type of landscapes, different factions with mixed tribal/sci fi aesthetics. Sound design is also on top and adds to that whole filling of you being surrounded by an unknown. There are some annoying moments however, this being point and click game means a lot of running around like a hobo and picking up everything you can, and there are some moments where you don't know where to go or what to do, though devs added sort of like questmarkers and they partially help. Also despite game trying to tell you that all factions are both good and bad, you clearly can see how some are just a bit nasty and others are absolutely evil. Ending also doesnt make much sense and gives you more questions instead of answering them. None the less, this is one of those games I wish I could forget and replay sometime.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, damn. This game is downright hautingly georgeous. The more you play, the better it gets and story towards the end is downright awesome.If you do not mind older point and click adventure, this is a sure recommend. And as a bonus, there is way less of wierd item combining and random solutions to puzzles. Usually it is fairly logical as long as you pay attention. And hey, if you get yourself stuck, no need to feel bad for looking up a guide. It is worth finishing the journey and one helluva journey it is.This ting is no kak brav, ja? Go and play it.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: Lekker bois!This game is gold.Very high quality in terms of graphics, sound, music, story and world-building,especially considering the size of the team and the price.As a South African myself, I really appreciated all the cultural references and it just reminded me again how culturally rich and diverse our country is.The world of Beautiful Desolation comes across as a very gritty convincing reality wrapped in surrealism, another player described it as a massive acid trip. My only wish was that it didn't have to end so soon, with so many stories still to tell...But alas all things must come to an end eventually...
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Desolation feels like a classic adventure everyone always recommended I play but which I never gave a chance until now. The game is set in a mix of science fiction and Africana, full of beautiful and unusual scenery. I really enjoyed discovering its world through the eyes of two everyman brothers and a talking robot dog who definitely does not sound like you'd guess she would.One weakness, though, is the two minigames the authors must have spent a tremendous amount of time adding but which detract more from the game than they add.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: A very unusual point and click game with a captivating story set in an unique game word. This game caught me off guard in that it was not the game I thought it would be at all. I was surprised that I couldn't predict how the game would unfold that easily. That is a good thing by the way. I am 43h in by now and am halfway through my second playthrough. If it would have been a boring game I would never have let it take so much of my time.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game today. I'm writing this review coming from somebody who has played both STASIS and CAYNE.1. Would I like this game if I enjoyed STASIS and/or CAYNE?- Yes. And if you enjoy the general sense of impending doom of humanity.2. What's improved in Beautiful Desolation (hereon BD)?- More cinematics. - Non-linear exploration.- Implementation of a Map and travel system.- Richer world and setup. More dynamic and interesting characters.- Fully voiced dialogues, beautifully voice-acted on top of that, really provided a diverse cast.- Dialogue choices (which affects your ending outcome and achievements).- The ability to review past dialogues any time you want (without the voice-acting, regrettably).- Icons that help navigate flavor text planted in the world as well as obtainable items on the ground.- Fewer things to read (if you didn't like how text-heavy the previous games were).- Beautiful visuals and different styled towns, locations, etc.- Sketch art available to collect throughout the game.- Humor, great humor.- Soundtrack is amazing. My favorite was the theme of Saxonwold.3. What new risks did they take? What's left to be desired? - Mini-games. Much like the data tag operation sequence in STASIS, we have two new mini games in BD that are required to be complete in order to progress. Failing the mini games does not result in game-overs. However, the Arena Arcade game (a 3v3 action-point based combat game) does get tedious and cumbersome after the first fights. On this front, they could have used better skill designs for the units/combatants.- Puzzle design. If you found STASIS and CAYNE puzzles to be confusing, then I'm afraid it doesn't get better in BD. Besides paying attention to every exchange you have with the NPCs, at times I found myself just having to force the solution by visiting and talking to every possible person, or visit the locations over and over again. WARNING: Always search each new area thoroughly to ensure that you don't miss any crucial pickup items that can stop you from progressing in the game. Some puzzles also require forcing solutions by process of elimination.- World-building and story. BD's world is fascinating and the story engaged me from the get go, however, by the end of the game there are quite a few questions left unanswered, leaving me a little unsatisfied.  4. Last thoughts:- Thematically BD explores what STASIS and CAYNE both did to a degree, which is the contrast between human emotions/virtues and the horrible reality, though I do prefer the visceral setting in STASIS and CAYNE more (BD does have its fair share of fleshy bits). BD also hints and leans into the theme of brotherly/sisterly bonds.- In terms of value, I would say the game is well-worth its buck.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:- Worldbuilding is out of this world amazing (pun fully intended). I generally tend to find postapocalyptic settings boring because they're so grimdark and ugly that it's hard to care about their fate. Not so here, BD strikes a very good balance of the bleak, the bizarre and the, well, beautiful and I found myself fully immersed and very invested in it.- It looks absolutely stunning, and there's a lot of visual storytelling going on adding a great deal to worldbuilding. I particularly liked that the Codex is a collection of drawings rather than a wiki - it both makes a lot of sense in-setting and gives the game a lot of character.- The game is easy, at least for an experienced adventure player, but not very hand-holdy. You have to pay attention to what NPCs say, and the puzzles, while easy, can still give you the satisfaction of a "eureka" moment from time to time.- Non-linearity and "scavenger hunt" plot structure. For all the sparseness of content (see below) the exploration just feels very satisfying - you always have several leads to pursue, there are always new items and maps to experiment with just around the corner. And just learning about the world feels interesting and rewarding.The bad:- Maps do feel a bit empty throughout the game. More frustratingly so given that the game's version of pixel hunt is lawnmowing the map - as hotspots only highlight at proximity, so you need to go through every inch to make sure you didn't miss something.- And you really want to make sure you didn't miss something, because backtracking is very tedious. The worldmap travel looks great the first couple of times, but quickly becomes boring as you can only move between the points of interest. Would be nice if you could find a couple of optional areas just by flying around.- The empty maps are even more frustrating because of how easy it would have been to fill them with environmental puzzles, like in the one in hidden garden. The game being set in the ruins of a few advanced civilizations, it would be really easy to justify. And they would offer a good alternative to lawn-mowing for quest items and gold.- While not very hand-holdy, the game still is a bit too user-friendly for comfort. The separation of hotspots into interactive and read-only and of items into combinable and stand-alone gives away too much information for puzzles. Wouldn't mind an optional difficulty mode that'd turn it off.- The plot structure is a bit formulaic. You arrive at a new map, find two or more opposing factions, one of which is clearly evil and the rest are somewhat less evil, and then you solve their conflict. The factions themselves are very colorful though, I just wish it wouldn't have been so black-and-grey.

_childDocuments_.review: The Brotherhood continues to not let me down.  This team of brothers + more are the definition of world creators.  The worlds are so rich and detailed.  There are elements of this game that blow many AAA titles out of the water (especially cutscenes).  Can you imagine what they could create with a bigger budget than $160k (from the Kickstarter)?While Adventure at the core, this game is hard to describe as it blends a number of classic games together namely: Sanitarium, Fallout 1-2, and Planescape: Torment.  The RPGness and action (except one area) are not here but the exploration and progression is similar.  Just to be clear...this is an Adventure game not Action or RPG although it looks like it!!I love the non-linear exploration.  I loved the fact I had to keep my own notes to figure out the storylines and characters (though it would've been more helpful if there was an easier way to track who was at each location).  Sometimes the waypoints of what to do next can be quite confusing thus you need to rely on your notes.  If I took a break for too long, it would take me 15-30min to figure out what I was doing (I normally solve this by custom naming my save files).  I also wished there was more to do in vehicle mode because I really liked flying around. A-

_childDocuments_.review: What a... Beautiful game.It's an isometric point and click 'style' game with an RPG element to it. It starts off with a cutscene that's a bit fallout / visual novel esque and then throws you right into the game. And it is gorgeous! From the cutscenes to the environment, the details and the portraits, everything is simply beautiful. From there the story beings, putting the protagonist in a different timeline. where the world is more than slightly messed up. There he can team up with a robot dog as well as his brother to tackle on the quirks and puzzles that the game throws at you.The RPG element comes in when you are conversing with people. Think of it like Baldur's Gate 2 or maybe Pillars of Eternity (2). Much of what you say, do or don't do has an impact to the world and the outcome at the end in a very interesting manner. There were several occasions where I simply felt rotten for the action that I had just taken, even choked up at one point.The writing is very good for the most part. There are some typos here and some things that are voiced don't get subtitled correctly. If there is a pet peeve in this, it's that some of the conversations are... Quite annoying, especially if they go on for too long and the voicing is really slow. A good example would be the Nest where I quite literally alt-tabbed to do something else. Which was a shame, as I really quite liked that subplot a lot. On top of that, there's sometimes the case where you have a conversation and halfway through, they just say 'well, gotta go' and the conversation ends. It doesn't happen too often and it's not that annoying, but it's a bit off putting.The voice acting was a hit or miss. Mark and Don were done really darn well, the rest was a bit of a hit and miss. There was one conversation where it sounded like the voice actor kept turning their head. I don't recall which one it was though. Again, minor thing, but off putting. What was off putting was some of the dutch words that were spoken... Please, for the love of ♥♥♥♥, if you use foreign words, try to pronounce them right. It was done fairly well for the most part and most was done right. But there was a conversation with the mongrels where he tried to pronounce 'hondjie' and it sounded like 'ghwohd' or something like that. That was a little disgusting and rather inconsistent, giving that in most other cases, it was done fairly well.The game doesn't hold your hand though. There's no quest log to speak of, nor is there a hint system. You have to figure out everything for yourself. That wasn't a problem for me, but I can understand it if people are put off by it. The only time I found this troublesome was with 'Buddy' in the 'mine'. That puzzle wasn't very great without any sort of hint.So yeah, I'd highly recommend this game. The price is certainly worth it. I've played CAYNE and STASIS as well, from the same developer and supported them by backing this game. If I'd give it a score, it'd be very close to a 9. Go check it out, it's seriously worth it.I've got 19 hours on record, but it's probably closer to 15. I'll most likely play it again in the near future, since it does have some replay value!

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Desolation is a stunningly beautiful adventure game with a great story and well-written characters. It's greatest achievement, however, is its vibrant, weird futuristic version of South Africa, full of strangely beautiful factions and NPCs. I've been a great fan of The Brotherhood ever since Stasis hit Kickstarter. I'm a proud backer of Stasis, Beautiful Desolation and Stasis 2: Bone Totem, always pledging a little bit more than they ask for. Why? Because Chris Bischoff knows how to weave great stories. How to build worlds with unique atmosphere. How to write sparse dialogues that will touch the nerve and chill you to the bone. And each of their games so far has been bolder and better than the previous one. I loved the nihilistic existential horror of Stasis, the slowburn dredge through the endless darkness. But then Cayne came and added some nasty body horror into the formula and voila! More powerful stuff of nightmares! Beautiful Desolation builds on the formula further, offering a branching narrative, side quests and dynamic relationship among the trio of main characters. Moreover, it mixes bleakness with a sense of wonder and wanderlust, prodding you into exploring its picturesque locations. The frustrating elements of pixel hunting are streamlined by adding rippling circles around objects of interest. The desperate attempts to combine everything with everything, just to get further in the story also almost disappeared. What needs to be done usually makes good sense. I never felt hopelessly lost.As for the problems, I could do with less travelling between locations and maps just to get a single item from the other end of the world. Last couple of hours had a wee bit too much of ping-ponging between locations, just to get the things to complete the quest and/or unlock the achievement. Also, I ask myself whether offering four possible ending and asking the players for a fifth playthrough to unlock a bonus ending is not too much. I've played Stasis and Cayne twice - once for the story, the other time for the fun (and achievements). I plan to do the same with Beautiful Desolation. But I do not feel particularly thrilled about the prospect of doing it three times more after that. Nevertheless, Beautiful Desolation is a bomb and I proudly rank among the greats like Planescape: Torment or Fallout 1 & 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start I want to give some warning. If you don't like walking/flying around and visit some of the same locations to solve puzzles this game is not for you. For this adventure game you sometimes have to backtrack already visited locations. As a tip I would write locations of characters and missions down, because there are a fair bit of locations to uncover in there. Now this is out of the way I can say this is a game that brings you into a weird and strange world. The graphics are amazing and really sucking you into this world. The sound and music are really helping you with this and are great in my opinion! The puzzles are never to difficult, however, like I said before it sometimes comes down to searching the right item/device in the world. And this sometimes can be frustrating when you miss this one thing. Sometimes there are indicators showing you where to go, but that is not always the case. But this is not uncommon for adventures. I think this is also one of the few games where you really feel a connection to your party members. The choices in dialogs  are sometimes ehtical and you have to choose between evil, or more evil. There are different endings based on these choices you make within the dialogs. I was sad that the story ended, however I didn't feel the need to replay it. Also a part I didn't like was the part in the arcade hall which is fun the first 3 times. After 5, 6 times you really want it to be over. (But if you win it still gives a great feeling).I am really impressed with this game, the story, music and the universum they created! And also not sure why some characters can speak half dutch :D Are you an adventure fan, and don't mind backtracking. This is a good game!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit clunky at times, but Beautiful Desolation is full of heart and weirdness. It's an isometric point´n´click type game in which you solve riddles, meet a lot of strange lifeforms and decide a lot of fates. It's not too difficult, not too long and the artstyle and weird charm speak for themselves.While I did not like all aspects of the game - the arena side mode, for example, is too clunky, slow and unintuitive to be fun - this was still a treat to play and I wanted to see even more of this strange future world. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Loved it, it's a one of a kind experience. Well worth years of waiting.It's a point & click adventure, has its flaws, definitely not for everyone. But it's the game I really wanted to exist, so I could experience it. And now, here it is. Amazing.Things I loved:- The setting, the lore, the world. It's unique, and well executed.- Protagonist (as a good guy), and companions. Their relationships and small talks. They always felt relatable, grounded in reality, opened characters nicely.- Visual aesthetic. It nailed the nostalgic feel, from the super-detailed, pre-rendered 3D backgrounds, to intentionally 'clunky' interfaces the game uses. Good? Nah, it's GREAT!- CG movies and ink sketches. Did not expect so many of either, enjoyed them all.- Music. Mick Gordon is an ace.- The ending - both the temple and the 'story' parts of it.- Ion cannon. Hell yes!Things I disliked:- Walk-hunting for quest items. It's like pixel hunting, but even slower, as you have to walk to notice items.- Dialogue flow. The game has amazing, unique lore!! But often you can only discuss 1 of 3 options, having to forfeit others. I would love to talk with more NPCs, learn about the world here and there.- Having to leave a location, just to see that a new conversation might have unlocked (or might not).- The idea of replaying multiple times to get all content. Not a fan of this, instead just watched all other endings on YouTube. I had the best ending, anyway!- Too often I felt lost, not sure where to go next. I wouldn't be able to complete the game without an online walkthrough. Hell, I'd never beat those puzzles, or even think of tearing the rift (having to use an item on the worldmap location icon - only once in a game).- Having to tear the rift every time. The errand running between Kettle and Unknown has been a nuisance. - That annoying bone-library Scanner, and being unable to get back at him for all the trash talking.- The disappearance of the dreadlocked robot guy. I was hoping to meet him and hopper again, tbh.- Wasn't there a herd of giraffe-like beasts in early trailers? I didn't encounter those. Miss them.- Some parts felt missing / incomplete. Like, learning about special properties of certain drug, but being unable to share that knowledge to anyone. Or the whole arc about 'scout drones' tribe feeling incomplete - I couldn't help their NPCs, only choices I had were to make things worse for the faction, or much worse.Things I REALLY hated:- Most mini-games (RNG bug fights, the arena fight) - Complex puzzles with obscure hints (garden generators, drone/mine, ion cannon questionnaire etc).So yeah, the game has quite some flaws.But the unique setting and good narrative made up for it.Would love to see more games in the same world.

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals and world building is amazing. The plot is a tapestry of small and big tales and legends from every tribe and character you find.The bigger tale, however, isn't so much about a trio of strangers trying to get home as it is understanding the personal and familial issues of the Leslie brothers and POOCH.As an adventure game, though... slow, kinda clunky, demands pixel hunting and there are many cases where you have no clear indication of where you should go next. (the dev tried to alleviate this by adding green pings in maps with unlockable story events, but even that isn't consistent).The world created for the game is fantastic. Even when things don't make any sense, the visuals and design make most of the intended message pretty clear. (ex: I have no idea how the Chiznyama can use a forcefield or build a space ark, but from the character design to their dialogue, it becomes clear that they aren't spacefaring explorers, they just want to escape a world they don't feel part of anymore)Wish the devs had the means to grow this world beyond the game. Novels or comics, for example, would allow to flesh out much more of the cultures and lives of this crazy retro-futuristic piece of South Africa

_childDocuments_.review: This game is set in a unique world with interesting tasks and interesting characters.  It's pretty and weird and slightly disturbing, all in good ways.The gameplay was the one area that felt somewhat lacking to me, because it required a level of investment from me that I wasn't expecting:  as you explore new areas, your initial quests/puzzles are relatively straightforward, but eventually they get to a point where someone mentions "there used to be a person X who did Y but they're gone now," and you're supposed to remember, "Oh, yeah, I saw someone like that two maps ago," and go talk to them.  As a result, I would highly recommend either playing this all at once, paying close attention to everything to everything stays in your head, or playing while taking careful notes.  Not having done either of those things, I ended up having to resort to walkthroughs partway through, and my experience suffered because of it.The one nice thing is that when you finish talking to someone, the 'talk' icon disappears, and later if there's something new to say to them, the 'talk' icon reappears.  So if you're thorough, you can just wander around everywhere until you see a 'talk' icon again.  This doesn't always work, but it's helpful when it does.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. How to explain this beautiful mind f*** of a game? It is not like anything I have played before. It is a sci-fi post-apocalyptic bizzaro mixed acid trip that takes place in South Africa. If I had to describe the atmosphere I would say it was a mix of the movies mad max, blade runner, District 9, and Stargate. The graphics, voice acting, and story are all superb. And it is a good thing too because this is not a game where you are fighting or solving a lot complex puzzles (typical mechanics that attract gamers to certain genres). It is first and foremost a story-driven game. The mystery, unique characters and universe, as well as the down-right absurd, keep you immersed and chugging along to the end.  If I had to choose a game that it might be similar too then I guess I would say Disco Elysium. I thoroughly enjoyed this game but it's probably not for everyone. If you like story-driven games that break the mold or just want something different, then you will likely this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played both Cayne and Stasis, I was super excited to get this new one!  So far, I'm enjoying it greatly.  I miss the space type theme that the other games had, but this new world is definitely a nice refreshing change of pace compared to the previous titles.  There have been a few times I got confused as to where to go, since there's alot of jumping back and forth between areas.  The graphics are quite lovely and the voice acting is fun to listen to.  Reminds me somewhat of the movie District 9 in a way.  The music is really great too!  I would recommend this game if you are the type that likes point and click games and wants to have some challenges.  I've played over 8 hours and still am not finished since I'm trying my best to get as much as I can so I can earn the achievements.  I do know I'll have to replay to get alternate endings and such, but I very much look forward to it!

_childDocuments_.review: Supported this game through Kickstarter and after playing the 2 games that came with this (Cayne and Stasis), this game plays alot like them, though I was expecting, and got, more.Game looks pretty amazing, especially the cutscenes, and the sound effects are very solid. Game runs amazing smooth as I am playing this on a pretty powered up, though almost 5 year old pc. I had everything cranked to the max and had no glitches at all. Game never froze up or went down, which in todays gaming, seems to be a normal thing anymore. Just ran excellent. Story was wierd, but solid, as were the various races you run into during your adventure.Here are some of the annoying things:The voice acting part was a little off for me. I didn't feel as much a part of the game as I should have as there seemed be alot of "feeling" in the words that were spoken, especially since alot of dialog was regarding their pasts. And was definitely alot of weird dialog as well. And all the back and forth traveling got to be a real pain the Ass. Way too much of that, especially given that you didn't have a "to do" tab like most games. You would have to open PDA and re-read past conversations to see what you missed that might give you a clue where to go next or you just went back and forth to many locations until you found your next step or two.The only other issue I had was for some reason, my graphics kept switching back to the default and I had to switch them back 3 or 4 times within the first 2 hours or so I played, but then stopped after that. Maxing the graphics is a big key to able to see what are doing as the difference can be pretty major and it separates the background and the NPC's.But once you got to figuring things out, you would have these runs where you would make alot of progress quickly. Was a fun game with alot of choices that can really shape what your final ending will be. I can see you having 3 or 4 play throughs of this game to see everything.Pretty fun game for the 15 hours it took to beat.

_childDocuments_.review: ✔️ Wonderful visual design - both environments and characters are original, interesting, and beautifully executed.✔️ The voice acting is nice and gives quite a bit of life to the world.✔️ The choices offered to the player are actually intriguing to explore.✔️ Pretty fun optional tactical combat minigame.✔️ Some investigations require you to wander around quite a bit but I never actually felt the need to check a walkthrough to solve a situation - so that's a good point.❌ Overall the story is a bit bland, with the player character somewhat playing a "white savior" role.❌ The world is somewhat empty in terms of interactions - you spend a lot of time just walking around. Luckily the environments are pretty, but it can still get a bit boring.❌ The user experience is mediocre - the non-interruptible interface animations make the flow clunky, and the interactive objects would have benefited from having a larger interactive area than just a little square.Overall it was a pretty nice game, but it has some downsides that can really make it bothersome to some people, especially if you don't have much time on your hands or aren't patient for any other reason.

_childDocuments_.review: A point and click adventure game set in a post apocalyptic future where you play man trying to find his way back home to the past. The gameplay itself, lots of clicking around and hunting for items and traveling from location to location was so-so for me, but everything else is what sucked me in. The writing was excellent. There's a couple branching decision points in the game where there's no easy right or wrong, moral answer. Some of the decisions I committed to made me feel sick to my stomach afterwards, which is all to the credit of the game's fantastic writing. A truly excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the previous game the Brotherhood have done.  This one started off a bit slow and the interface items were sometimes a little annoying (why have drag-and-drop as well as just drag on inventory?!?).  The story is great though can be a challenge with the sheer number of 'South African derived names" .  Overall the graphs are very good though a little blurry on my 1440p play-through.  Love the ending and how decisions are not as straight forward as one hopes.  Does leave it open for replay which is rare!  What I love about the Brotherhood is that they are keeping Adventure Games and story telling alive and doing this with a stupidly small team!!  Congrats guys, proud of you...especially being fellow South Africans...I wonder how many will catch all the nuances  ;).  The only real detractor was the sound volume inconsistency between vocal lines, which makes them feel like they were 'stuck together' on different takes...a pity.  The choice of voices does seem strange in some areas if one considers the characters and background and the old-school screen presentation of the character discussions seemed a little out of place with the rest of the quality of this game!  Overall I would say a solid 8/10 and you really should place this!  Love the ending...it is...different ;).

_childDocuments_.review: “Beautiful Desolation” is beautiful, hands down. Unfortunately, it’s not an enjoyable experience overall.The game could be a very promising alpha version of a cool story-driven RPG with most of the game mechanics waiting to be implemented: awesome scenery, breathtaking open world map that you traverse on your very own ship, companions with compelling backstories, different factions, and lots of interesting NPCs to interact with.  But “Beautiful Desolation” is the final product and it is marketed as an adventure game, while being riddled with completely unnecessary elements of a different genre: the flights over the map spend your time for no reason, backtracking through the whole world is uncalled for and does no good to the quests, companions are creating noise in the background and the NPCs are just sending you back and forth to bring them yet another key item.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often that game fully captivates my attention from the very first cutscene of the game - however Beautiful Desolation sold me on the intro alone. It's a Point&Click game in very nostalgic, suprisingly beautiful 2D oldschool isometric frame - for example dialogues are represented by Talking Heads, that feel very inspired by classic Fallout ones. Whole setup oozes mystery and setting is filled with bizzarely fascinating concepts resembling some of the best Planescape Torment's weirdness. And when everything starts clicking in your head, all the litle lore pieces perfectly connecting together - that was IMO the best part of the whole game. Second best part would be companions! They don't banter too much, however their dialogue usually is interesting and progresses character development. On the flaws side: there's a lot of flying around and backtracking, as you're trying to find what will progress you further into the story. The path forward isn't always obvious and could require talking to old NPCs with which you already had a full conversation previously. I don't recommend this game to anyone who seeks combat (which though is in the game, it's presented only in form of two mostly optional minigames), dislikes solving puzzles or is easily overwhelmed by 'alien' setting, which don't fully make sense until you put few good hours into the game.And I certainly recommend this game for anyone who seeks a bizzare, interesting adventure within lands of science fiction Africa! Because the Beautiful Desolation is a one of a kind experience.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very unique experience. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have played in recent years. The characters are very well voice acted and interact in meaningful ways that you can actually influence through your choice of words. Something always loved in a good story!  The environment is one of the most beautiful I have seen in an isometric game - I found myself running around in circles thinking "there must be some sort of item I missed here!!" while that may be the case, many zones are filled with pathways and gorgeous scenery just for the sake of beauty and immersion...unless I am missing something(s)?  Couple that with the amazing soundtrack by Mark Morgan, who has worked on several other titles such as Fallout and Planescape: Torment, the game fully comes alive and is a pleasurable experience for both the eyes and the ears.The gameplay is not as challenging when it comes to the puzzles as it was with "Stasis" the first game developed by The Brotherhood.  So, for the most part you will be able to progress without too much strain. You are afforded some flexibility with the progression, although still a linear path is very much so present. You can just simply approach that path a little out of order - in my opinion. The choices you make do have an effect on the world around you, both immediately and for the future. The way this is presented to you at the stories end and how the culture, beliefs and lore all come together for you into a coherent understanding when finally reaching that end... it had me truly in awe.Overall an amazing game, developed by some amazing folks. Can't wait for more!
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting story and presentation, much improvement on the CG scenes compared to their previous games. An intriguing dialogue system with all sort of strange creatures inspired by Fallout. You'll run around a beautiful hand-rendered dystopian future landscape with your brother and robodog, discovering and solving mysteries and siding with several factions over others. The exploration reminded me a lot of various Infinity Engine games like Icewind Dale or Baldur's Gate, but the setting felt more Planescape with a bit of African tribal setting mixed in.STASIS was a great first debut by The Brotherhood, but with Broken Desolation they have come of age. If you love top-down RPGs in a mysterious/strange alien setting like Planescape/Fallout or strange Adventures like Sanitarium, GET IT!

_childDocuments_.review: Now this, this was an adventure, I spent a whole evening awake to see it's twist and turns unfold around me.The beautiful scenery, the great voice acting, the whole world that this team developed is just awe-inspiring, the cultures that were around were a  joy to learn about, my only wish is that there was more 'flavour' dialogue/lore or just unrelated characters to talk to, I leave this game still craving more.If you enjoy point and click adventures (LucasArts style more than Sierra) this is both a loving memory and it's own organism, think Pillars of Exile without the combat and fully voice acted or Grim Fandango but in an isometric view.Sadly it is not without fault, the combat sections were rather awful in honesty, or maybe I just didn't understand them well enough, with a bit more depth it could of been something but in the end I was happy there was an alternative method.Also without going into detail I felt a bit disappointed by the ending, including the entirety of the last 'area' it felt a bit rushed when I'd happily of delved into a couple more hours of story, but I am not deterred by a mediocre ending when the journey was so fantastic9/10 (Disclaimer : A kickstarter backer)

_childDocuments_.review: The general idea of the game, and the story, seem very interesting. However, the pacing is AWFUL. And while I do not need my hand held to progress through a game, this one very much seems directionless by design. Though I read/listened to the dialogue (and thankfully they make it easy to replay past dialogue), the real problem here is that if you do not pass closely enough to some item, it won't show up to be interacted with.  Now, add to that that these items are placed within a map whose boundaries seem capricious at best, and you have a recipe whereby you spend hours traversing a beautiful game looking for something that should take tens of minutes to find, at best, being conservative. This directionless "point-and-click" seems more like a "comb-the-desert" in the hopes of the next plot point.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't call throwing a pack of stinky disgusting cigarettes into your ship "pimping it up". WTF? Now to constructive criticism. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Desolation may not have as gripping a plot as Stasis (in my opinion as sci-fi horror is my favourite genre) but what it does have is a bigger more expansive world to explore and what an imaginative and original world it is! With it's gorgeous graphics and landscapes blending dystopian and sci-fi, with a fusion of African culture, you cannot help but be drawn into this world and it will live long in the memory. However, if i had one criticism is I wanted more of it! Sometimes the plot and the references (from tribes, to forgotten wars and strange technology) it's all pretty vague and left unexplained. The included game codex would have been a great place to talk about some of these areas in more detail or they could have included some written journals or books scattered around the game world to pick up and read to flesh out the plot. Sound wise the game is also great, music is used sparingly but is suitably atmospheric and all dialogue is fully voiced which i personally prefer in a game when done right. For the most part it's of high quality too with the voices adopting the local African accents and alien like tones to those odd ball characters you meet. Gameplay is nothing groundbreaking, this is your standard basic adventure formula of exploring the different maps, interacting with NPC's, occasionally solving inventory or interface like puzzles to progress. An intuitive interface makes for a smooth way forward however as a number of reviewers have already mentioned, the lack of an objectives marker or highlight option for finding what are sometimes well hidden but crucial inventory items does sometime cause you to feel lost and brings the frustration of the inevitable 'i'm stuck what do I do next' scenario. A word on the length, it took be around 15 hours to complete the game and for the price this is fantastic value for money and shows the developers are not greedy despite having a limited budget and resource. Overall I loved Beautiful Desolation, the premise and plot were great and backed with strong writing and cut scenes - it has retro but lush graphics and tried and tested gameplay mechanics. All I would say as room for improvement is better signposting, more in game written lore to digest and perhaps add in some more RPG like elements to expand the gameplay a bit. Overall 9/10 - can't wait to see their next project! Stasis 2 please :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is not Fallout. This is not even an RPG. So don't make the mistake I did in thinking otherwise. It's only an isometric point-and-click adventure game. Exactly like Stasis if you've had the misfortune to have played it, minus the horror element. The "meaningful" choices you make in the story don't really impact your playthrough, merely the ending. Combat is relegated to an optional mini-game halfway through and I question why they bothered to even add it in with how under-used it is. Dialogue is streamlined so no matter your "choice" your character will always get exactly what he (you) need to proceed. The main focus of the game is the story/adventure which already takes a huge hit because the game's ending can be easily predicted within the first hour of the game.Perhaps you might be thinking "but it's the adventure not the destination"? Unfortunately for you you would be mistaken since the adventure also sucks. Most of your time spent in this game won't be talking to people or solving head-scratching puzzles (of which there are remarkably few). No, it'll be you traveling around individual maps scanning for hidden key items to pick up, you running to the next designated NPC the game will let you talk to or you flying around in the overworld to get to said map or NPC so you can progress in the relatively linear order the game has set forth for you.The fact that I managed to put in 6.6 hours amazes even me. I can only attribute it to having a 2nd monitor to distract myself from how tedious the game is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a just a bad game.  REALLY bad.  Stasis ultimately also was a bad game, but I thought it showed enough promise that I was optimistic that The Brotherhood would learn from their mistakes and next time more successfully implement some interest seeming ideas into much better designed gameplay.  Nope!  Beautiful Desolation is worse, much worse.  Everything problematic in Stasis is here again but magnified enormously, and major additional problems are added.Trying to list everything wrong with this game would take forever.  But to hit the major ones, first the world, story, characters, etc. are completely incoherent, ridiculous, and never in any way explained to the player.  At no point in playing through this did I have the slightest idea what was going on.  I'd be surprised if the writers of the game could even give a coherent description of the lore.  It seems like they just threw a bunch of completely ridiculous cartoony characters together and had them babble long, nonsensical monologues at the player.  And your PC character appears to have zero curiousty about any of this!  He walks up to a talking corpse, or something else at that level of silliness, listens to a long nonsensical monologue, and then just acts like he's chit chatting at the office water cooler and nothing odd or unexplained is going on.  Another major problem -- the world is split up into a substantial number of separate maps.  These maps are large and mostly empty of any important items of characters.  The graphics are terrible, so it's very difficult to tell looking from the top down view where you can actually walk to and where you can't (same thing as Stasis but made much worse by the number and size of the areas).  A relatively small number of these numerous mostly empty areas have critical plot items stashed in some random, hard to navigate to spot off in a corner.  These key items will only appear and be interactable with when you get very close to them.  So basically you are forced to run around like an idiot on every single one of the many empty, ugly maps trying to make sure the one item you have to have to progress the plot in some other random region halfway across the world isn't hidden somewhere in a corner that it wasn't clear you could even get to since it looks like any number of other areas nearby you can't walk to because of some kind of invisible wall.  Without the developer walkthrough, you are certain to hit roadblocks where you are hopelessly stuck with no idea what to do to progress the plot other than go back to every map and scour them trying to find the one random, hidden object you missed.  In that regard, the quest journal is 100% totally useless.  It NEVER provides any useful information about what you are supposed to be trying to do.Related to the large number of empty maps with a few hidden key items is the hassle the game makes you go through to get to all these different maps.  There's no fast travel.  You have to get on your ship, travel slowly across an overhead map, often go through a warp device to get to one of the dozen OTHER overhead maps, then slowly travel again to the area you want to get to, then land finally at the new area.  EVERY SINGLE TIME, AND YOU WILL NEED TO DO THIS PROBABLY A HUNDRED TIMES.  It serves no purpose whatsoever other than to waste the player's time.  It's like they wanted to make an open world exploration game, dropped the idea, but didn't drop the pointless overhead map that annoys the F out of the player for no reason in the game they actually made.  You can't find anything by exploring in your ship.  Doesn't matter if you fly right on top of an area that will later be revealed. Locations only ever appear and can be accessed when they are triggered at specific plot points in the pretty much completely linear plot.So after a thumbs down on Stasis and now suffering through the far worse Beautiful Desolation, I'm giving up on The Brotherhood, and am ignore listing anything else I ever see from them.  Two released games, both bad, the second much more so.  Canye, a f2p game related to Stasis isn't any good either, and the demo for Stasis 2 was not at all promising.

_childDocuments_.review: Way too convoluted of a fetch quest. Going back and forth to various areas became rather tedious. _childDocuments_.review: Decent; 4 out of 10. Classic point-and-click game. It’s playable, but it started to drag about 50% of the way through. At that point, I looked up a guide so I could finish up. Even with multiple endings, I won’t go back for another playthrough.IMO, all point-and-click adventure games have similar downsides: too much backtracking, numerously repeated conversations, and item searching. Beautiful Desolation compounds this problem by making many objects in the game flat out invisible until you get near them. You won’t know anything is there until a green circle pops up when you’re close. You’ll be scouring every inch of the environment to make sure you didn’t miss anything. Not very fun. Luckily, outside of 1 or 2 “moon logic” moments, most puzzles are fairly simple once you find the necessary objects.The setting is cool enough: post-apocalyptic South Africa. Unfortunately, the characters, factions, and general story are very difficult to follow. This is because 90% of the NPCs speak like drugged up tribal shamans telling riddles. NPCs could say, “those cyborg guys attacked us and took our resources”. But instead, they say they stuff like, “the demons of silicon poisoned our fertile air with their war smog… the great moon of our ancestors’ weeps upon our guilt tree.” It’s OK when one character does it, but gets old when everyone does.On the positive side, the graphics are way better than what you’d expect from a small developer, especially the cut scenes. There’s nothing *bad* about this game. But with no novel game mechanics, it needs something extra to separate it from the pack. Above average graphics, and a unique setting just wasn’t enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Desolations is like it's name imply, beautiful and desolate...Beautiful in art and sound department, desolate in writing and gameplay...Seriously, this is first game I can recall that I admire for artstyle and sounds and totally despise for writing, which personally, I think is ATROCIOUS! In my opinion everything with writng is horrible, characters feel, well... I can't really put it in any other way than... DUMB, they just feel dumb,  especially fat, bearded brother, younger brother feels like crocodile dundee and pooch is just nonsensical, and I dont even want to write about talking train, for god's sake...Worldbuilding feels rushed like hell, you start not knowing absolutely anything, what was happening with your characters for years after first cutscene, what are his motives? Why he didnt try to find brother earlier for all those years? Nothing like that, you just meet him out of blue and force him to fly with you god only knows why... THIS IS SO DUMB, and one moment later your being introduced to some tribal and mystical stuff by literally FIRST npc you meet in totally new environment before even establishing what hapenned and where are you, I DONT CARE YET ABOUT TRIBAL AND MYSTICAL STUFF, everything is shoved at you too fast... Now dialogs, main characters (brothers) are obviously dumbasses capable of uttering only simpliest sentences, and as for npc's I found most of their dialogs either unbelievably cringe or ridiculous...I really REALLY despise writing of this game...Other thing is voice acting which feels very inconsistent, sometimes just great and sometimes amateurish and totally immersion breaking.Gameplay is also lacking because there's barely any interesting, challenging, ingenious puzzles, you just run between different characters to hand them different items, that's whole ingenuity of developers...Not to mention that you'll spend definitely too much time just flying between locations, it gets tiresome really fast...I feel really sorry that this game turned out failure for me because aesthetically I really like it, but there's simply nothing worthwhile here except visuals and sound, beautiful...desolation.

_childDocuments_.review: As many I appreciated the art style, is beautiful. The soundtrack is great made by Mick Gordon (so ofc I am gonna like it), perfectly enhancing the broken alien like world you find yourself in. Each character has its own VO, and even their personalities is unique. Story and narrative are good, it shows the devs know how to tell a story and I appreciate that, could use more backstory, by the end I hardly knew much of the 3 main characters background.While I do praise the artwork, it also works against the game, there is too much clutter, some areas you cannot even tell which is the path to move on or which is just extra background/foreground fluff; they are not very well defined. This kind of art worked much better in an enclosed environment game like Stasis but for this game, not that much.Up next is too much walking, all quests involve grab X item, talk to X, give item to X and so on, just fetch quests with little and not interesting puzzles sprinkled around. And that is the main problem of the game, it feels too tedious and slow.I was talking about interesting and unique characters, the irony is that the main characters are the most bland ones. You do not learn much about them and even the ending does not help them either, which is pretty much, your choices did not matter and you are in the Matrix, re-try again. So needless to say, I was disappointed in the ending, only to find out later after reading a bit, that I should re-play 4-5 times to get the proper ending… yeah… no thanks, one play and one ending is enough for me. And yes, the game does take note of the choices you make, and gives you a different ending for them, so I do give it a plus for doing an adventure game where choices do matter. I do consider this game decent enough, I would give it 6.5/10 it deserves it, and if you are looking for an old school style, isometric point&click then give it a go. Taken into account the art, sound , uniqueness it really does make it a Beautiful Desolation, too bad is not called Beautiful Gameplay Desolation, cuz it lacking that part…

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Desolation is visually spectacular—really, truly gorgeous, from the world maps to the journal sketches—and this alone makes it worth playing. I do wish there were more (and more nuanced) narrative content and gameplay beyond puzzles, though. The world-building is intriguing, the characters you meet along the way are wonderfully grotesque and charismatic, but there isn't much dialogue through which to interact with your surroundings. Dialogue choices made while interacting with your companions ultimately have an impact, but the choice sets are the same from beginning to end, so there's little sense of growth. As for puzzles—that's more of a personal preference; you might love the gameplay if point-and-click puzzles are your jam, in which case you'll probably love the game as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: A flawed masterpiece of creativity.This is another excellent game from The Brotherhood. What stood our for me in this story is the sheer creativity of the world and the story it tells.This is a game where choices matter.. sort of. The main story remains the same no matter how to role play the main character but a lot of detail has been put into the different endings. I felt a bit angry that the plot railroads you into "choose A or B" options where both have serious consequences. it feels like there were choices to be made but no real reward for playing well.The graphics are generally good, although some animations are definitely B-grade and some of the art direction is questionable.The UI is a bit cumbersome with markers hard to select or hover over. I often found myself pressing the wrong UI button because they just weren't dissimilar enough.The game is fairly short so some of the value will come from playing through again with different endings but there just isn't enough variety to make it worth the time. A smart player will save at critical points and play out both sides of major decisions before reloading and committing to one of them.The sound isn't anything special, although I really liked the voice acting, especially the south african accents and all the little cultural references in the dialog.I would like to see more games in this world but it feels that the plot has covered off major events that would make a sequel difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: For me the best "Fallout"-like-game since the original Fallout (even if it lacks the combat).The story is both challenging and rewarding. Both, visuals and the sound are awesome. Has also a rewarding ending, unlike a lot of other games. The gameplay, as some others also stated, is mostly "point-and-click", but it makes sense, and is fun, and has a lot of surprising elements. (and to be honest: any game is just about point and click ;-))Has very interesting and also sympathic characters, which really matter to you. Only the character you play is a little bit boring.Verdict: this game touched me more than most of the AAA-games in the last decade!

_childDocuments_.review: Groundhog Day! The game was different and weird. I liked the main characters and found them interesting. The NPC's throughout the game were very unusual. _childDocuments_.review: Yes, yes, yes, and hell yes. This is a gorgeous game and I can't stop playing it. Ignore the gameplay for a second and just on the art alone please give this game a go. You will NOT be sad you did! The gameplay though is fantastic, so don't worry - it gets better! In the spirit of the old Fallout style RPG, Beautiful Desolation allows you to take on the future with your brother and a mechanical pooch named, well, pooch. You want to get back to your time, but there's a twist. Will you and your crew be legends for good or selfish? It may be an age old question, but let's face it. We all love a good moral dilemma.  Just please play it. So much to see, do, and experience. I can't say anymore without ruining the game. The imagination the game world took to build reminds me that I'm not alone in my love for the fantastic and that's something every fantasy and scifi lover needs right now.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Stasis and enjoy point-n-click adventure games it's a no-brainer: get this one. There are so many unique things about this game: the art style, the game-world, the characters, the storyline. The gameplay too was at times unique for this genre. You get to make different choices, so there's probably different endings. It took me 29 hours to finish the game, being as thorough as possible. On the negative side; it was unclear on some missions what my task was, what I was supposed to do, and a couple of the later puzzles felt too much like trial and error and had some tediousness to them. Overall though, I enjoyed the different puzzles. The game as a whole is great and feels completely unique.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: Note no spoilers.Beautiful Desolation is a one of a kind experience that is a joy to be a part of. I say “of” because BD is one of THOSE games. The ones that not only pull at your heartstrings but leaves you feeling like you finished a great book. The story is well crafted and is infused with a blend of comedy, tension, and wonderment. BD’s characters are weirdly memorable with frickin fantastic voice acting. The game looks like a modern day Planescape: Torment with crazy and imagination sparking visuals. BD has an artistic style all its own and I found it both creepy and pretty. Gameplay wise, it has an updated point and click adventure feel that I really enjoyed. In BD your choices matter and have an affect on the world. Lastly but not in any way least the music is superb. The composer Mick Gordon is brilliant and he adds so much depth and emotion to the game.If you want to have fun, play Beautiful Desolation.Nitpicks, commentary, and slight spoilers follow.The PDA has a lot of landscape, I wish the buttons were larger.The game does have different outcomes and could warrant some replay.The Arena is a neat idea but not a selling point and thankfully not a requirement to finishing the game.I wish I could have named my save games, it would make keeping track of them better.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning scenes, surprisingly good writing and interesting ideas and concepts make an amazing story to follow. Has a little bit of wonky logic sometimes that's common to all adventure games, and there's ALOT of times you will be running back and forth trying to figure out what you are supposed to do. However, I think its more than worth it. Hell, I really wish there was a first person RPG set in this universe now!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most beautiful and emotional games I've ever played - while short, I have never appreciated my time spent in a game more than in Beautiful Desolation. I would recommend this game to ANYONE who loves story-rich games, beautiful atmospheres, and an absolutely essential for anyone who wants an incredible game experience but doesn't have an enormous amount of time to spend gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: I have actually played about for hours of this game and this is my conclusion:Beatiful Desolation is game that has an awesome setting, awesome cutscenes and a very beautiful, detailed design. _childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique world set in South Africa far in the future. The art is gorgeous and the character designs are all intriguing and unlike most I've seen before. The locations, factions, and dialogue were all easy to get into and I always wanted to learn more. Also the music is excellent (Mick Gordon). The main negative I have is it's not always easy to know what your next task is. I was able to finish it but there were times I felt completely lost. It's a relatively short game with not a ton of replay value, although you can choose different factions to help.Overall, I think it's a good adventure game and an excellent world that Chris Bischoff has made. I look forward to whatever game they make next.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: I thought  was good, but this next title from THE BROTHERHOOD blows it out of the water. The visuals are excellent, some of the high altitude areas have backdrops showing areas below (mountains, ruined cities) that are astounding. The story was surprisingly awesome, and I love that you can make choices that impact the story and world.There is also an optional battle mechanic relating to "tokens" you may be given. While it's not the greatest combat ever designed, the fact that it's so fleshed out is incredibly surprising considering the fact that this is . The story/explanation for the combat is really interesting as well. There's also , a sort of "rock-paper-scissors" game mixed with dice and bug fighting. It's such a unique and awesome idea, but I wish you could play as much as you wanted!There are some puzzles in this game as well. Sometimes they will trick you, make you change the way you think the puzzle is supposed to operate. For example, the Baas reactor puzzle. When I finally figured that one out - all I can say was I became even more impressed with this game. Whatever you do, don't give up and search for the answers online - work it out yourself! It's worth it.This is a really special and excellent game and I hope to see more incredible stuff from this developer!
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: This is a straight-on masterpiece. The visuals, the story, the effects. The gameplay might feel a bit sluggish at times, but after all, you just immerse yourself in it and feel no encumbrance. I loved every bit of it - most of all the deformed, mishappen, but sweet characters. Pooch is a velvet sore of my heart. And so many others. The gray morale, the choices I've made while playing - they made me wonder if I was right or wrong after all. As a game developer myself, I can only applaud the boldness and creativity of the Brotherhood games and wish them to continue. This is just the game I'd like to work on as an artist.

_childDocuments_.review: #Adventure  I've played lots of rpgs. Other reviews mention similarities to well-known rpgs for reference but that is irrelevant. The game creators and their culture are different from most U.S. producers after all, which is refreshing. The ethical issues from this company are present but are more clear so the audience is not confused as to what is a good and bad decision ethically. I found that the game had some redundancy in collecting items. Possibly to reduce main quest completion difficulty. That made achieving 1 side quest pointless. The storyboard contingency could have accounted for that but I'm still happy that the completion rate was high for such a small production team. I hate feeling like I missed something in a game I don't intend to play again and again for lack of time. Try it out yall!
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: There is room for more than a few quality of life improvements, but ultimately I really enjoyed this title.Some things I enjoyed:- Wonderfully fleshed-out world with NPCs you'll actually remember (Sometimes because you screwed them or they screwed you.)- Voice actors that actually sound like real people and not some actor you've heard in every other game- Gorgeous maps. (Although pathing through them was not always completely intuitive)- Arguably, many decisions didn't really create a ton of agency in the story, but they did paint the world in a new way that colored how you were involved. (You could for instance accidentally condemn a whole tribe and then walk through the ashes after they were obliterated.)
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: Every part of this game is pure 90s isometric demented sci-fi goodness. Fortunately/unfortunately, even the glaring flaws triggers deep nostalgia so I’m almost tempted to forgive them. But yes there are flaws. The controls, the ugly hotspots, the arcane plot details that don’t make any sense until you’re halfway in. The puzzle design lacks lateral thinking, it’s mainly fetch quests and choose-your-path. But that said, the art design, the cut scenes, the sci fi sensibilities, just the overall style is unbelievably perfect and brilliant. I want more games just like this but with better puzzles and just more more more. Loved it, looking forward to their next adventure game.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: No one writes sci-fi like this anymore.Beautiful Desolation is a new adventure game from Nic and Chris Bischoff, creators of Stasis and Cayne. They've taken what was great about their earlier games and expanded it vastly.The world of Beautiful Desolation is intricate and full of lore, oozing charm from every crevice. It's designed to have the player lose themselves in the world without any hand holding. It's up to you to pay attention to dialogue and the clues contained within. It took me roughly 11 hours to finish the story and I was fully immersed for all of it.If you are interested in great sci-fi with extensive world building, you should definitely give this a shot.PS: fellow penguins might like to know that the Linux port is flawless.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, this could be an excellent RPG game. But it was made by a very small indie studio, so it's 'only'  (with some RPG elements put in it). A bit rough around the edges or even archaic, yet absolutely worth giving it a try - if not for intriguing story or difficult puzzles, then definitely for it's world. Because Beautiful Desolation is... well, beautiful. . I can't remember the last time I was so absorbed by exploration itself. I just wish the game had more interactive objects and characters in each location. But let us not forget: for a studio as small as The Brotherhood this was an enormous effort, and I believe the final result deserves our praise... and money.

_childDocuments_.review: This is much better than I expected..  Puzzles and where to go next can be a bit vague at times.  Obviously South African in origin and some of the banter can be hard to understand unless you are from that part of the world.  However, all in all a good solid game.  Probably a good 20-25 hour game in length.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: I contributed to The Brotherhood for development of this game after thoroughly enjoying Stasis and Cayne.  Not going to lie, I do miss the space-theme of the 1st two games, but the story and world-building of Beautiful Desolation is fantastic.  This is true creativity and originality.  Love it or hate it, there is no denying that this is a well thought story and a richly designed world.  This is also  a perfect game, most of the gripes and complaints of other reviewers are valid.  There is some debate as to whether this game should be classified as an RPG or Adventure - make no mistake this a traditional point & click adventure game rendered in a beautiful 3D isometric environment.  So everything you love about those games is present, as well as the ones you dread like the obtuse inventory puzzles and pixel-hunting.  If you're on the fence - get it.  Particularly if it goes on sale.  There is nothing really to compare the game to - even the previous Brotherhood games are similar only in mechanics.  I've summarized my own personal thoughts below:All in all - really good game.  I enjoyed it and will definitely back The Brotherhood on their next venture
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: Isometric adventure game with a science fiction setting. Two estranged brothers and a robotic military dog are thrown into a mostly desolate future from the late 80s by an alien device that had been rapidly advance human technology over the last 10 years. Characters and factions also often being estranged family or parts of a whole with you having to help them come together, accept that they are better apart, or to destroy the other while figuring out how to feel about your own brother. Great visuals, well written, and good voice acting and pathfinding. Talking to characters goes into a Fallout 1 and 2 style close up screen that is always a strong fit for the setting and shows off the varied character types well.What few actual puzzles there are are poor, most of the game is going to the right place and remembering the people or spot that makes sense to get an item or to continue the narrative. Near pixel hunting required to find some objects, most not needed luckily.Screenshots:
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: The small amount i looked into or saw of this game prior to release, did not prepare me for the depth and feel of this sci-fi experience. I'm really pleased with the ambience, style of characters, setting and how they mesh together well. A few hits and misses that only slightly detracted from my time so far with the game, such like voice acting feeling out of place or at wrong volume levels and the world being a little tricky to navigate at first.If you want a sci-fi world to get into, this one will do nicely.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the atmosphere in this surreal, post-dystopian world full of strange creatures, even stranger cultures and a whole lot of sadness.From a gameplay perspective, it was a mixed bag for me; at least until the recent patch that added the support for quest markers, a necessity for notoriously impatient players like me, who are interested in the story, but not in running around aimlessly. Still, I had to consult a guide a couple of times due to being stuck (or impatient) to finish the game, although I did it mostly because I wanted to know more about this strange world without having to fight the clunky controls. Yes, the controls were quite annoying at times, especially when the possible paths in the terrain were not transparent or mouse clicks sometimes did not seem to register (or the character plainly ignored the click). Not being able to interfact with things on my screen was infuriating, so having to walk/run anywhere was a chore, especially if I had done so a dozen times before. If there was an option to hold down the left mouse button to have the character continue to run in the direction of the cursor, maybe it would not have been so bad, but the game seemed to try to be as aggravating as possible from the mechanical side of things.However, from a world building perspective, few games are made each year that would top this one, The 2D backgrounds are beautiful and detailed (even if the poor design decision to hide eye icons, until you are basically on top of the icon, made it harder to enjoy the design). The voice acting was solid and had unique features for every character, which made them unique and memorable (I particularly liked "We and us"). The cutscenes were excellent in my opinion, really well done. The game also ran in 21:9 resolution out of the box, which I appreciate since many "AAA" games in 2020 still refuse to do.The small development team deserves high praise for creating this beautiful game world. Maybe a couple more "quality of life" patches would make it even more accessible to the general player and increase its popularity.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful Desolation feels like a true passion project in every way, made with equal focus on the beautiful world that you explore, and the strange, outlandish characters you meet. It is, at its base, an adventure game with several choices to make along the way which shape the story. While hard to describe succinctly, the game feels like equal parts classic RPG (especially Planescape Torment and Fallout), adventure game, puzzle and a dash of Neill Blomkamp cinematography all mixed together in a weird and wondrous story of a world which you never truly get to comprehend fully. It is also rare to have a post-apocalyptic game set in/around the African continent. That alone sets it miles apart from anything else I remember playing.The artwork is excellent, and even the less important locations are beautifully crafted. The music varies from sometimes understated to bombastic and brilliant, and fits the world of DE perfectly. To anyone curious about this game, I would caution that it is above all an adventure game. While there is some combat, most interactions are bloodless. Your choices however can still create massively violent results. If you have played The Brotherhood's other games, CAYNE and STASIS, you probably already know what to expect. If you haven't, I highly recommend them both.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: What a wild and imaginative world. Half the stuff in this game/story is so out there I thought I had already seen it, apparently not. This game is not only interesting and fantastic as far as isometric games go, it really pulls some things from gaming history that worked very well. Such as the world map screen with the Buffalo (your ride). It took me back to FF games where you would fly around on the world map.  Choices in this game actually lead to significant consequences later on in your story with multiple pathways branching off even further.  I found myself saving at points and reloading just to see how far the rabbit hole would go (hint: just play through and don't waste time like I did, you'll understand later.) I really can't think of anything negative to say that's a good thing!

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding old-school adventure with beautiful isometric world graphics, with high quality cut scenes and character interaction overlays. A terrific, satisfying and complex story and a good dash of humour thrown in. I'll be sad when it's over, but there would seem to be significant replay value, given decision branches.
