_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun with the title but there are a few things for others to note before you go and buy it.  The fighting is very little.  It's mostly a Planescape Torment world that is point and click with a tiny portion of fighting.  The biggest problem I had with the game is that while you really get into it for a good ways it starts to become a bit confusing of the various factions and "what" you are doing for "who" and "where".  There is no quest log to the game.  You can look at previous conversations to guide you what you need to do but as so many things pop up I found myself going to a hint guide  to make sure I didn't miss anything.  Second big problem is finding "gold".  They require you to find various gold objects around the maps so you can trade them in for credit to buy items that will be required later.  The really big problem for the gold is there are no indicators where the gold could be.  What they really make you do is walk along every piece of the maps and when you are close an eye icon pops up to let you know there is gold.  The maps are not big at all but seriously taking away time from people to hunt for things like this is a downer.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: A not too difficult point-and-click adventure which might also be the best looking adventure I've ever played. (The not-too-difficult part is not meant as a bad thing; the solutions simply make sense. No nonsensical combining random items with each-other is good.)Voice acting varies from great to pretty bad. Ironically the main character's is probably the worst but after a while I got over it and figured it was just his way of talking I guess.The atmosphere and setting is beautiful, the story is good though I didn't really like the ending; somewhat feels like a lost opportunity because I'm certain there's a better way to end it.Finished it in 14 hours according to steam. Could have done it sooner and quicker but some reloading and afk-time are added to it. It might deserve a second playthrough to witness the results of the other choices, but ultimately in the end it doesn't matter really much so I'm not certain, more about this below. It will be a lot quicker to go through, so I might...Also my completionist OCD made me repeat the pixel-hunting 'gold item finding' more often than required. This is the only part of the game that I didn't really like: You have to really zig-zag across every map, making sure you've checked every possible corner, hoping for an eye icon to pop up so you can find money which helps to buy some items you need to progress. A simple occasional glitter of gold in the sunlight, indicating that there's something to look for, might have been welcome here. This pixel-hunt sadly just distracted me from enjoying the amazing beauty of the place I was exploring, which it bad because the art that each location in this game really is, deserves to be admired without distraction.-- I almost wrote something about wanting more C&C and the lack of meaningful effect my choices had on the ending. But as I wrote it, I realised it's because this game looks so much like an RPG that it's hard to avoid the mistake of comparing it to one.But it is, ultimately, a great point-and-click adventure game and C&C never really is a part of this genre. The fact that there is some C&C is pretty unique for the genre and really adds flavor to the story and setting.
_childDocuments_.name: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION

_childDocuments_.review: BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION is a 2D isometric adventure game set in the distant future. Explore a post-apocalyptic landscape, solve puzzles, meet new friends and make powerful enemies, mediate conflicts and fight for your life as you unravel the secrets of the world around you.

name: Jet Lancer
detailed_description: Jet Lancer is a high-velocity aerial combat shooter where you duel enemy aviators, hunt giant robots, and defy death at supersonic speeds. You are Ash Leguinn: badass pilot, highly paid mercenary, and flight-school drop out. Your day job is fine - the daily grind of dealing with Sky Pirates pays the bills - but nothing compares to the rush of demolishing a ninety-ton mechanical monstrosity at the speed of sound. And you’ll have your chance. As mechanized weapons converge on Root City, you’ll have to be at the top of your game to survive, and you’ll have to surpass your limits if you want to save the world. Be A Badass : Jet Lancer is easy to learn but hard to master. Precise and responsive controls make you feel like an ACE as you dodge and weave through enemy fire without even a scratch in the paint. Surpass your Limits in Ash’s Story : Make your way from rookie aviator to ACE pilot in a story-driven single player campaign containing 30 missions, 11 bosses, and only 1 chance to save the world. Aggressive New Game Plus : Go higher, further, and faster in Jet Lancer’s New Game Plus mode which features more relentless AI, new attack patterns, and some fancy new upgrades for the LANCE to provide a fresh experience. Choose From an Extensive Arsenal : Customizable loadout with 28 different guns, payloads, and flight components to let you dominate the skies in any way you’d like. Customize with Accessibility Options :We think everyone should have the opportunity to feel like an ACE pilot. To that end we’ve included anti-fatigue control toggles, adjustable dodge windows, an invincibility option, and the ability to disable screenshake and screen flashing. Talking Cat : There’s a talking cat! His name is Lem. And if that isn't enough we've got ARCADE MODE , Jet Lancer's take on a wave based score-attack mode! Unique, stacking upgrades : Make each run one-of-a-kind. The longer you survive, the more powerful you become. Multi-boss battles : Fight multiple bosses from the story mode at the same time. New Pilots : Three new pilots with unique jets and handling. Level Up : New Progressions system to unlock additional pilots and their jets New Weapon: Flamethrower : Immense repeatable damage at very close range. New Weapon Railgun : Instantaneous precision shots. New Weapon Coil Gun : Chain lightning between grouped enemies. Vladimir Fedyushkin is the designer of Jet Lancer and is also in charge of art and hacky code solutions. A string of random events in his life led him to game development as a career and he hasn't looked back. You can follow him on Twitter @WhyNotArtDump Nicolai is the code wizard in charge of making things move on the screen. He hits buttons and helps to make the game as fun as we envisioned in our minds. You can follow him on Twitter @NicolaiGD Fat Bard are the guitar-shredders behind Jet Lancer's soundtrack. A composition/sound design duo, they create memorable music and immersive audio for games. Jet Lancer is the debut game from Vladimir Feduyshkin and Nicolai Danielsen.

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually a review written at 20 hours playtime, I just let the game idle by accident. FIRST AND FOREMOST: If you are the kind of user that wants to use the 2 hour window to try the game and refund if you don't like it, then take a pass on the purchase, at least until you've done some of your own research/watching; the early game is the most bland part of the game with easy, unaggressive enemies and not much plot development since it still is laying out what kind of personalities the characters have. It doesn't pick up until about 7 missions in when you finally have some loadout options to try and a boss to fight, along with more advanced units in missions afterwards.PROS:-Excellent control over the Jet-An entire NG+ mode, with new module unlocks-Clean, refined art style; flashy, but still easy to see what's going on-Build diversity is not extremely expansive, but still wide enough that it's interesting, and there are different strategies for the same missions and bosses that work well enough to get highest score.-Varied unit behavior. Compared to LUFTRAUSERS, the enemy AI is more diverse, with some fodder units even becoming crafty every now in then in trying to evade you. Advanced units will be able to nearly match your agility, and some use similar abilities to yours.-Accessibility options. They are limited but include: CAMERA SHAKE SLIDERCAMERA ROTATION SPEED (Loadout menu only)INVINCIBILITY: No damage, half damage takenEVADE WINDOW: By default, there is a split second after getting hit where you can still dodge and stop the damage despite being hit. This can be turned off for HARDER gameplay, and the window can be set HIGHER or to HIGHEST for easier gameplay if your reaction speed is low or little bro wants to play.TOGGLES: various things can be set to toggle on and off instead of held. There are separate options for the Minigun (primary fire), Thrust (forward movement), and Afterburn (boost).FLASHING: On/off. :)UI: You can turn it off here if you want as well.THE "MEH:" -More mission diversity would've been welcome. That said, there are 37.. or are there? ;PIt doesn't wear out its welcome by repeating too much, either.-Soundtrack. This is easily the most subjective part of the review. It is at its lowest at the beginning stages and missions of the game, but do yourself a favor and don't put your playlist on for those last 12 or so missions! That's where the best ones are.-The story. It's just not the focus of the game and it was kinda hard to get attached to it or the characters.CONS:-No colorblind options. The game UI and effects are clean enough that it's mostly fine without them, but they would be extremely welcome regardless.-Score balancing. Some missions are just unreasonably difficult to get a high score on, and boss battles in particular are *extremely* stingy with their time allocation in some cases. Expect to skip acing missions until you have the perfect modules to do it with much later. There will be a patch for swarm mission scoring in particular, at least.-Loadout balance. You have a lot of options and most of it can work, but there are some pretty clear winners that dominate the middling options and losers in the bunch. Worse, Guided Missiles and Swarm Missiles become totally obsolete for two reasons; an enemy unit hard counters them AND they DRAMATICALLY lower your weapon score bonus so they are not viable in most cases for getting ace ranking.-Hidden modifiers, mechanics, etc. A module should tell you exactly what it does. Did you know that the afterburner mod doubles your backdraft damage on top of increasing the max duration you can afterburn? Neither did I. The game also didn't tell me what a backdraft even was, ever, or how to do it. And what about the Ace module? More agility in exchange for all your health as advertised.. but doesn't tell you about the 10% higher minigun damage and 5% higher minigun firerate at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I see everyone noticed the similarity between this game and Luftrausersbut a few actually compared them and pointed out any difference just because it is not a huge deviationaside from the art design which you can see with your own eyes.They're nice people and not nitpickers like me.I have not finished the game yet, but here is my humble insight: This is by far the biggest difference between both games which gave Luftrausers the old "Lunar Lander" feel and which makes Jet Lancer feel more "modern" in a sense. Being able to aim with a mouse instead of arrow keys. Adding the dodge button to that, you don't have to think of positioning that much, and go on with your life acting like an action pilot and focus on killing instead of a poor soldier stuck in a piece of metal junk focusing on surviving which was fun in its own way.  I do not feel like this is such a big deal. It is nice that this game has some character to it. The mission types sometimes freshen the game up, but there are also particularly boring filler missions. In the end you're staying for the combat and the parts where you fight a lot shines the most in this game. I wouldn't recommend it solely for the story. Luftrausers at first looks like it has the upperhand in this because that whole game itself is one good mission, and it's downright challenging combat, not watered down with anything else. On top of that it has literal "challenges" as tiny missions that you have to complete to unlock new stuff when Jet Lancer has a rating system seemingly just for fun. But more missions still mean more variety and I see there is also an arcade mode which is what Luftrausers is, but unfortunately that unlocks later.Your jet is a "prototype" in this game, but it is still a proper jet. It has proper weapons, a machine gun, a secondary weapon like missiles and a special weapon. It is not a crazy German experiment so the options are not as interesting, but it still has enough content to keep you going. Jet Lancer also let's you choose easy or difficult builds without forcing you to play something you don't like to complete challenges.:Luftrausers was a highly unique and compact gem, and this game lacks in that department. But what it does with the combat is fun and i think the game is more complete and accessible as a package and not just a small ware game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like advertised for a while, until you get to late game. Then the poor enemy AI design becomes clear.Last missions require a single specific loadout to be completed on maximum grade, because the rest is balanced to be either less rewarding in points or take longer (and thus reduce your score for that). It still has a freedom of choice, until you are looking for score. Then, that freedom dies. On NG+, not even the freedom of choice you have.Enemy aggression is completely random, meaning you can be swamped by several bullets or missiles, or be left completely alone. When the mission requires fast completion for score, or simply fails when you don't destroy enemy targets fast enough, you can fail because the game decided so.When you get to NG+, this becomes a whole other mess.One particular mission where you have to defend an objective (the whole ground) from being hit by bombs, on the last wave either the 3 bombers can spawn in quick succession, or space themselves a bit. If they spawn too fast, then you can have your mission failed without saving because they can each drop a bomb on each opposite side of the map, and you'll have no chance of getting to both fast enough to destroy them and avoid defeat. And when you are greeted with 3 enemies shooting at you at the same time, missiles to evade, two bombers that spawned in quick succession, the mission is over before it really is. Hours grinding a single mission until the random chance that you won't be screwed over by the game isn't fun.Other type of mission require you to keep destroying enemy targets fast enough. If they don't simply decide to spawn fast enough for it to be a problem, you still have to deal with going from one side of the map to the other, because 4 to 6 enemies will just sit there for no reason. Then, when trying to get there and dealing with them, the travel plus fight time is enough for another 4-6 to spawn on the other side ignoring you.In the end, trying for the best score (or just completing a mission) on the NG+ missions isn't up to you. It isn't up to this promise of "your playstyle". It's about reproducing a single specific loadout that was in mind for that mission, and then grinding until the poor excuse of an AI allows you to be lucky. This kills all the fun.Fighting against an unpredictable enemy can be interesting. When they are unpredictable because they can shift between different strategies, the fun comes from trying to figure out "what are they doing now?". Fighting an enemy that is unpredictable because it is simply flipping coins with no purpose isn't interesting. It's frustrating, because there is no answer to "what are they doing now?". It's frustrating, because the outcome of encounters is a coin flip.Also, the store says "Full Controller Support", but it really isn't. XInput isn't natively supported, and force-feedback/vibration doesn't work properly on XInput too.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who really enjoys progression, missions, and upgrades, this is the game I wanted Luftrausers to be. Don't get me wrong, Vlambeer did a fabulous job making the game they set out to make, but I'm just not a Rogue-like fan. So...this is Luftrausers for people who don't like Rogue-likes. Positives:- impressive fireworks shows- tight controls, generally feels like my fault when something goes wrong- genuinely entertaining writing (love the engineer!)- looks to have a bunch of upgrades (I'm only about an hour in as of writing)- cool boss fights- awesome soundtrack- looks great on an ultrawide monitor(Minor) Negatives: - it can be a little hard to follow at times (it's very fast!)- I haven't quite found a controlling mapping I like, my fingers keep instinctively pressing the wrong button for dodging in particular- the turning seems sluggish, though I suspect that'll upgrade over time Overall super happy I bought it - great job Code Wakers and Armor Games Studios!

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is the game I’ve always wanted. I wrote a long review, but it’s too long for Steam to handle. So here’s what I like about it, in short:• Sweet, vibrant graphics• An excellent (dynamic) soundtrack• A fun anime-inspired story• A variety of missions• A loadout system with plenty of room for customization while keeping things straightforward and simplistic• Mission ranking for your daily ACE needs ;]• Dodge roll and dash mechanic that spices up the action• Two difficulty modes, moderately challenging missions, a bit much at times ;]• Menacing, badass bosses• Responsive controls - you rule the skies!• Accessibility options to help you enjoy the game the way you like• Well-telegraphed attacks and threats, no cheap moments!• High speed explosive arcade action• Appeals to players of all skill levels• An endless Arcade Mode with extremely high replayability

_childDocuments_.review: I was having so much fun with this game until level 22. It is a clear act of idiocy by the devs, as the problem was known back at least as far as 2020. The level is a timed score level, so you have to earn a certain amount of points by x amount of time. This mission is considered "stealth" as the more you fire, the more this laser weapon locks onto you and it makes the level difficult. But even if you go full guns blazing, you do not have nearly enough time. It's not like I'm playing hard or impossible mode, the closest I've gotten is 14000/15000. Planes and weapons simply don't reload or spawn often enough. I have played this level dozens of times by this point and still struggle to get above 12000 points on average before the time runs out, if I'm not shot down by this laser weapon. Seriously, the devs have known this level was stupid as far back as 2020, 3 threes and it's a complete mess. The difficulty had increased in a natural way until this level, it's like there's room for failure to a certain degree, and then all of the sudden, you need perfect luck. Seriously ruined such a good game, still haven't got past this level.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for an hour, I decided I want to keep this game in a drm-free form, so I switched to itch.io instead. Hence the short playtime tracked here.Various modules -- change how the game works slightly -- ensure the game can fit play-style of a player, whatever that could be: people in the official discord were saying their module combination is the best, then realized everyone is insisting the same thing except the combinations they're insisting were all different.If the player still doesn't feel like they're getting comfortable with the game, that's where accessibility options kick in. Damage taken and dodge time window length are adjustable for example, and each fire buttons can be a toggle switch, which would help a lot preventing the hands from getting hurt for playing too much or too hard.The game won't block the player from anything or insult them for using any of the options, as being good at the game will still require efforts. The game shows rank for each cleared stages, and even an invincibility option won't guarantee the best rank. They're there to help the player to enjoy the game, not to just make the game easy.Gameplay depends on a dodge roll mechanic, but besides improbably protecting the player from any threats for a brief time after a button press, the dodge roll in this game even let them deny an already legitimately connected attack if they manage to react shortly after the impact.I am generally not a fan of games depending on it, but while the dodge roll in this game still feels improbable in my opinion, I found that it rather ended up making the game more exciting.The developers said the whole game was tested before this extended evade window is implemented, so a player can completely turn that off in the accessibility menu if they think it's making the game too easy.The difficulty distribution over stages feels little weird, as I found boss stages generally easier than a couple of general stages, that I had to spend multiple hours to just beat once. These general stages are really intense and well made to make the hands all sweaty, so I wonder if boss stages could be more exciting than these -- and probably making me even more nervous about failing them.This game is played following the main story, so every stage is there to progress the story. While I find that grinding for the best rank in stages appeals to many players, I wonder how much replay value this game holds for players who are not interested in it. Some stages can be played as a timed score attack mode so I wonder if these will make up the replay value for them.Still, it's really fun to play the game just to clear, even playing New Game+ -- the second play-through in a harder difficulty -- is fun. So even as a one-time thing like watching a movie, this game is worth to buy. By the way, it took me at least 16 hours to eventually complete the game on New Game+. I think that's longer than a movie.When the game was in development, I asked them if they can make an option to turn off the camera rotation in the hangar screen. I can easily imagine myself not being able to play the game more than an hour at a time due to long-lasting nausea caused every time I want to change my loadout.I waited years for this game, so that could've been a huge disappointment for me. I am deeply grateful as the option was added before the release.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never really been into jet fighter games, however this game absolutely blew me away. The incredible soundtrack, combined with the tight controls, satisfying and intense gameplay, make for an incredible, exciting experience. _childDocuments_.review: I don't know what exactly you classify this genre of shooter as, but this is the new gold standard.  There are other very good games like this, your Luftrausers, your Hyperspace Dogfights, etc, but none of them feel as good as this.  Maybe it's the absolutely spot on soundtrack that is fun while simultaneously building tension constantly or the bright and lovely visual presentation that puts it over the edge, but the thing that will absolutely have you effin glued to this game is the FEEL of these dogfights.  You will absolutely involuntarily wince at close dodges and then be grinning like a maniac at the damage bonus you got for pulling it off.   Even if you suck at it, there'll be at least one moment of every engagement that'll make you feel like an absolute jet-propelled god between dodge rolling through missiles, smashing other planes apart with your jet blast, and the full on Itano Circus missile spam.  You've seen the story missions before, certainly, but the game is essentially perfect.  You can overlook a familiar story when you're completely focused on arcade air combat this good.

The more advanced missions are intense as hell and getting good enough to blaze through them will make you feel like a flying explosion god.This is some peak video game dogfighting right here.

_childDocuments_.review: I think by reading any of the other reviews that you can guess it's a game similar to , though the game was inspired by an Atari game.It's gameplay, feel, and sound design are great. By the time I had finished the game through NG+, I was actually reflexively hitting my dodge button while watching a video on it.The music itself is beautiful, it's an adrenaline rush that gets you into the zone.I think the most important difference between this game and , though, is that  is based off of a hit point system rather than an ambiguous, constantly regenerating health system. Mistakes matter, and that reward for clean dodging is a hefty damage boost to your primary gun.The game also has mouse controls as default, and I cannot stress how much better it is than a purely keyboard-based control system. You really do feel like an ace pilot as you nail a dumbfire rocket right into an enemy.I played through the NG+ (excluding one story-important fight) right near the release of the game in the span of one summer weekend, so I've yet to experience the newly balanced version, but I look forward to the next time I get that urge to play this game once more.

_childDocuments_.review: Will update this later when I have more time but since it's new and relatively under the radar, I wanted to get out a positive review. Been watching and waiting for this game for YEARS and it's finally here! Worth the wait? ABSOLUTELY. I rarely.. RARELY.. double dip on games but for this title I did. I bought it on the Nintendo Switch and here on PC with 0 regrets. It's everything I dreamed of and more! Right away the first thing I fell in love with is the Music! It's really damn good. I want the soundtrack for this game and hope it ends up on Spotify as well. It's some really enjoyable retro 8 bit chiptune that is catchy and really adds some spunk to the gameplay. Very solid if you like this type of music. Gameplay doesn't disappoint either. It's fluid, hard to control and easy to pickup. Lots of missions, upgrades and level variety are all waiting for you. Grabbed it on PC just because 15 USD for this game is criminal and devs deserve an additional kickback in my opinion. Buy this game! No need for sale. _childDocuments_.review: The closest thing you're likely to get to a Luftrausers 2, and Luftrausers was barely a whole game itself so this is very much welcome.Basic gameplay works as such, you use the mouse the turn and aim your jet and W to push it in that direction with most of the fun being how you manage your plane's inertia versus gravity to do cool tricks like like boosting up and then turning down without applying thrust so you can hover and shoot at enemies on the ground. Certain weapons have kick as well adding another layer to it.Your main weapons mostly stays the same the whole game but your secondary and supers have 5 options each. You also have some mods you can install on the plane to further customize it. Overall there's enough options that I fount myself switching between missions to specialize to help me get high scores (scores go from D to A, then the traditional if odd S and S+ with an ACE ranking for getting S+ without taking damage.)Currently the game has a campaign mode, with a fun and challenging New Game + with a setting that remind me of MegaMan Legends or My Time at Portia. Story is decent enough, short and to the point. There's also an Arcade Mode that's a decent if not expansive roguelike take on the game with the game giving a choice of upgrades between certain waves and ever few waves being a boss battle from the campaign.Overall, if this looks like a game you'd enjoy you probably will.Review written after putting over 6 hours into it the day I bought it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a very patient, or a very good, gamer. So a game that can pull me in and make even *me* feel skilled right off the bat, while still challenging me, is quite a nice find for me. Jet Lancer manages to balance a lot of things really well. It has *some* story and dialogue, but not too much; it's difficult, but not punishing; it starts you off with fun weapons, but doesn't make you feel over-powered.The comparisons others have made to Luftrausers are fair.  One thing I find lacking in this game is a lack of sense of momentum. There isn't enough "stuff" in the background to give you some perspective for how fast you're going, or how far you've moved, or where you are in relation to earth and sky. But, for me, the pros outweigh the cons by a good margin.

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is an absolutely phenomenal game and I can’t believe I didn’t know about it sooner. No game has captivated me quite like this has. Since I first picked up the game, I could tell that it was going to be special, and now that I’ve completed it several times, gotten nearly all of the achievements (something I almost never do), and  (something I’ve never done before), I’m pretty comfortable in saying that Jet Lancer has become my favorite game of all time, even dethroning Ace Combat, something I love so much I wrote a 17,000 word article about it. Along the same lines, I made a  too but if you like good, difficult games, you don’t need to read that, just do yourself a favor and buy it.I'll cover a few key things here though.First things first, allow me to say that as easy as it is to look at this and say “Jet Lancer is like Luftrausers but better” (seriously, just look at the Steam reviews and count how many people compare it to that game in their first few sentences,) I think that does a disservice to both games. Luftrausers is a stripped down extremely minimalistic game by design, and that’s all it was ever meant to be. But Jet Lancer is far from minimalistic. Jet Lancer is not just more complex, larger in scale, more polished, more structured, more challenging, and more addicting, but it’s also a lot more ambitious. It feels less like a game developer’s idea for a cool mechanic, and more like someone’s dream brought to life. Maybe it’s not that big a deal for the developers and I’m just projecting, but it sure feels that way. The only thing these games share in common is that you have a jet, you shoot other jets, and you can turn your engine off sometimes. And they’re 2D. They’re both great but they’re not really comparable in my opinion, and I feel quite strongly about that.Part of the reason for that is because while I’m capable of explaining exactly how I feel about Luftrausers and why, down to the details, I can’t do the same for Jet Lancer. The sheer quality of the gameplay has left me blown away, to the point that I can’t effectively analyze it anymore, even after so many playthroughs.The game is not easy, so the journey from rookie to ultra instinct can be grueling if this isn’t the kind of game you’re accustomed to or pick up easily. While I recommend aiming to eventually beat the game with no training modules and on default settings, you can give yourself some breathing room with the accessibility options by increasing the evade window, halving the damage you take, or even becoming invincible entirely. You can also make it harder for yourself if you’re so inclined by removing the evade window entirely and turning off the UI in the same menu. Aside from that, there are other accessibility options there, like changing the minigun and the afterburner to toggles instead of press and hold, and disabling strobe light effects. You can also remap controls and such, or use a controller, but let me just say I have no idea how one could play this game with a controller when the mouse controls are just so, so tight… but I might buy it again on the Switch anyway and find out.A word of warning though, when you beat the game the first time, you might feel a little let down. You might also think it’s a great and fitting ending, I don’t know, but if you do feel let down at all, just trust me on this one: Go beat new game plus, and pay attention to the dialog near the end. If you still aren’t satisfied, well, at least you got good enough to get there at all, and that’s a pretty darn rewarding feeling.Another warning, the final boss is absolutely not the most difficult part of the game, that would be mission 37. I don’t think this is a bad thing at all, and I don’t think you should feel that way either once you see what I mean. If anything, I don’t think adjusting mission 37 would benefit the game at all unless the final boss was then also made much more difficult, because fighting tons of different small targets all over the map at the same time will never be the same as fighting a single particularly dangerous target. Mission 37 is the true final boss, the rest is the victory lap, and that’s okay.All in all, this is a game that I will never forget, and will now always hold a special place in my life. This two man team, Code Wakers, has created an absolute masterwork, a triumph of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so... It's good. Real good.I do have a couple of things I'm not too fan of tho, so I'll start off with that:-Considering how the scoring system works, some missions with a set score to reach will "force" you to use certain loadouts above others. To put a long story short, using unguided weaponry scores you off more points than using the baseline guided missiles, so you're better off using a build containing, say, unguided missiles with the upgrade to make it easier to hit with, otherwise it's going to get REALLY hard to get that score in time.I know it's par for the course to adapt your loadout to the mission, but still, it does cut off some playstyles. I just find the combination of several factors - some of them being spoiler territory - to push you out of the guided missile and Macross Missile Massacre charged weapon quite quickly. Which is a shame, because while they do make things easier, they're fun to use.-The story is more on the predictable side of things, and some characters are really unlikable. Which SEEMS to be the intention for a couple of them, but still, I wanted to punch them in the nose for the entire time.-OP 16. Just... OP 16. You'll know when you see it. On the more neutral side of things, the NG game is quite short - I've beaten it in one evening, in about 4 hours (I haven't ACEd all the missions, quite far from it, you will get more hours out of it going for that). There is, however, a New Game + Mode accessible immediately after that, of which I still have to play through.The last strecth of the game is also significantly harder than the beginning, and some later missions are absolutely brutal.BUT.Don't let all of that deter you.Because this game is great.The gameplay is tight as hell and lets you do all sorts of really stylish aerial maneuvers, that you could only dream of pulling in games like Ace Combat.The music gets you into the mood for high octane action.The upgrade system either lets you get some help with some gameplay aspects you have trouble with, like an anti-crash module and a mercy shield if you get hit, OR you can just throw that away to customize your plane further to your liking once the options are unlocked, and some of them are an absolute blast to play with.The missions, for the most parts, either make you face off against other jets and weapons à la Ace Combat, OR are boss battles, and both are fun in their own right.The game WILL make you feel like a badass. I have been giddy quite a few times during my play time, and I just want more of it... Which I will get thanks to NG+.Don't let the cons at the top or the short playtime deter you. The gameplay more than makes up for it, and getting an ACE rating on all the missions is definitely not going to be easy. And I wouldn't have it any other way.It's good. Real good.

_childDocuments_.review: Few games in recent memory allow the player to take to the skies quite like Jet Lancer. It’s not the most complex twin-stick shooter ever made, but every element was carefully considered to work in service of a larger goal: indulging a glorious ace pilot power fantasy.Set in a tongue-in-cheek airborne dystopia, Jet Lancer tells the story of Ash Leguinn, a brash flight school dropout who scrapes by on contract work. An ancient robotic threat awakens, and it’s up to Ash and her crew of mercenaries (including a talking cat) to save the world. Jet Lancer’s character writing is witty and a bit on the goofy side, giving the player just enough reasons to go kick some ass at the speed of sound.Jet Lancer is a feast for the eyes and ears. Its vibrant color scheme and low poly art is well realized, giving Jet Lancer its own inspired flair. Sounds are both easily distinguishable and crisp, namely the explosions. The soundtrack might be my favorite of 2020 so far, lifting Jet Lancer’s presentation from good to great. While the anime styling might not be a winner for everyone, it serves to supplement the game’s arcade influence and light-hearted tone.Jet Lancer is a frantically fast twin-stick shooter that expects you to learn, and fast. Dodging stray shots, ramming through enemies with a dash, whipping around to break lock-ons and punish the fighter on your tail, all while the booming soundtrack propels you into the fray will leave you with a white-knuckled grip on your controller. It’s a messy, but glorious challenge every time.Jet Lancer uses a unique scoring system based on speed, dodge countering, combos, and accuracy to effectively reward a variety of playstyles. However, the highest ranks will be given to those who can master all of Jet Lancer’s mechanics and skill-checks, which is debatably how it should be.There are plenty of twin-stick shooters on the market that can offer something similar, but what sets Jet Lancer apart is its perfectly struck balance between difficulty and accessibility.Jet Lancer has an intimidatingly high skill floor, but offers just enough difficulty tuning to allow players to cater it to their own tastes. Players can tinker with all sorts of difficulty parameters and even enable invincibility right from the start.The game’s module system allows players to fine-tune the difficulty even further. Training modules that are meant to make flight easier to manage can be swapped out at any time, allowing the player more room to improve their damage output. The freedom this system provides allows players to tailor the game to their specific playstyle while not depriving hardcore players of the hellcrawl they often crave.While I would have liked to see a more creative mission layout than the typical overworld we got, Jet Lancer’s functional, albeit bog-standard level framework offers a respectable amount of gameplay variety. Some missions encourage a sky-high rampage, while others demand precision or multitasking.Jet Lancer’s simplicity is its greatest asset. It doesn’t waste your time with skill trees or padding, and it retains a strong balance between inclusivity and difficulty that I haven’t quite seen elsewhere. Sometimes it’s easy to forget that not everyone on planet Earth has the time or dedication to be good at video games, and there shouldn’t be design gatekeeping in place to keep everyone out. Jet Lancer sells itself as a game to embrace the ace pilot power fantasy, and it succeeds not by raising its skill floor, but by allowing the player to carve it out for themselves. Jet Lancer is punishing, frantic, and absolutely worth its meager price tag. After all, everyone deserves to see that killer view from above the clouds.

_childDocuments_.review: After 24 hours of Luftrausers I've been aching for more, going as far trying to make a Luftrausers-like. _childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is a 2D flight shoot 'em up game similar to LUFTRAUSERS, with the difference of being focused to its story and levels instead of only scoring and gameplay. The story is very simple but engaging enough to give you an idea of what's going on through the game. It has a very polished gameplay, controls are tight and responsive during flight, and it's very satisfying once you get the hang of the game. Graphics are really pretty in a way it imitates 3D pixel graphics similar to PS1/DS games, and sprite animations are just very vivid looking paired with an excellent sound design. It's very hard to come by with bugs, as they only happen through rare scenarios if you push the game hard to them (with most of these already been addressed by the developers which will be fixed in a future patch), so you'll rarely come by with them as you play.However, this game also comes with its fair share of flaws, naturally this game has a very steep learning curve, if you got no experience with the game, you'll possibly have a lot of trouble pulling off some advanced movement in the game without a couple hours of practice, some levels can be downright infuriating with how the scoring can be really tight further in the game (this is true to later levels and in NG+).With all that in mind, it's still an extremely solid game and it's honestly worth the price it offers. The game is intense, visceral, and throws you out of your chair the moment you sit through the game.EDIT:The soundtrack in the game is excellent and it matches the intensity the game offers seamlessly. It's incredibly fast (some songs reaches between 150 up to 220 bpm), and it's really varied yet well contained to suit through the various levels it has.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Really good alternative to Luftrausers for people who are interested in game progression more than they are in scoring.The stylish graphics, satisfying sound design / score and highly adjustable difficulty really make Jet Lancer enjoyable for just about anyone. It took me 7 hours to beat the game with the 1-hit death modifier (you normally have 3 lives per mission), so if you play without it you could probably beat Jet Lancer in under 5 hours. There is a New Game + option however, and it seems to offer a lot of unique content.If you're into scoring, you could still enjoy this game but it might frustrate you: the screen can get hard to read when things get too hectic and dialogue that happens during missions can't always be skipped.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: !DANGER!Missile on your tail.  You cut 2 fighters from the sky in one stroke.  You don't need guns when your jet is a sword.  You twist up to smash a rocket through the drone formation carving apart the clouds.  You race to catch the bomber before it drops its payload.  Kill the engines, pivot, punch the boost and blast it to pieces with the force of your afterburners.Jet Lancer is a fantastic game with beautiful effects, punchy sound and exceptionally tight combat.  If you've ever played Luftrausers, imagine that but with a boost and a parry mechanic (and a less obnoxious combo system).This game is challenging and fast paced, but not unforgiving.  It's more interested in messy, back-and-forth dogfights than perfect execution, letting you dodge through attacks and even shrug off damage if you can find the right timing.However, if you find the game too hard, your can tailor your loadout to be more forgiving and rely on guided rockets to supplement your aim.  Or, if you want more spice, you can trade the safety modules for some juice (my favorite is a module that turns the dodge into a weaponized dash) and chase that S+ rank.  The game also sports rebindable controls and a decent selection of accessibility options, including a toggle for the main gun, more generous dodge timings, and invincibility, should you want it.At this point, the only criticism I have is that the writing is pretty campy and uninspired, but that's not what you're here for.  You're here for crunchy explosions, too many bullets, and jets that handle like a knifefight.  And Jet Lancer delivers.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is a modern shoot-em up with an extremely solid and satisfying core gameplay loop. Played on both a keyboard and mouse and gamepad. Good content here for completionists and shoot-em-up fans. I would recommend this at full-price.+ Cute and diverse characters with nice anime-inspired designs. The background and art direction is pretty great overall and reminiscent of Dragon ball.+ The ship upgrade system is designed in quite a clever way. You pick one charge weapon, one special weapon, and four modules for your ship. The modules you start with are kind of handicaps (eg. autopilot that stops you crashing if you fly too low) then you get access to cooler modules that allow you to do things like dashing through enemies or making your ship faster at expense of shields. You naturally need to remove your handicaps if you want to slot in the more potentially destructive modules, meaning you can tailor the game in a way that matches how confident you are.+ Very good soundtrack.+ High level of replayability, shooting jets into a pile of smoke and then flying through it doesn't get old and is just plain fun, I always find myself coming back to this game at the end of the day. It is easy to pick up but very difficult to master. Achieving the two highest grades for each mission (S+ and ACE) on normal difficulty is quite a task, and I imagine it's even tougher on NG+. I can easily see 30+ hours of content here for completionists, unless you're some kind of shoot-em-up god.+ There is a slider to turn screen-shaking down or off, if you get motion sick easily.+ Doesn't seem to have a way to change the cosmetic look of your ship. To be fair, some of the different weapons and ship modules have nice and meaty effects (especially the dash and laser beam), but it would have been nice to be able to switch up the ship colour, or maybe have different flight trails as a reward for reaching the highest letter grades in missions or something.+ No voice-acting, although this is understandable from an indie team. No voice acting is better than bad voice acting but it would have been nice to see.+ BR Portuguese support would have been nice.

_childDocuments_.review: One in a million chanche huh?I like my odds.Jet Lancer, drawing heavy inspiration from annother game called Luftrausers doesn't make a carbon copy of it but studies what makes it work to take the concept onto new heights improvin on everything, from style to gameplay to story.A sci-fi story that suprisingly doesn't have a grimm and dark look or feel, this may be the most lacking element but it's a needed one and it doesn't lessen the general experience.Style is achieved with very simple sprites, but enhanced by a plethora of effects that keep the screen from being bland but at the same time it's not too busy.This is a dogfighting game believe it or not, and it's achieved by keeping you on your heels with split second decisions but also by making you strategize around enemy and your own position and available resources.It takes a underused concept and makes it even better, greatly reccomanded.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review: Jet Lancer, from Code Wakers Studios and published by Armor Games Studios, is an 2D sidescroller-style arcade shooter, full of action where the player will have to fight his way through waves of enemies and defeating some Bosses along the way.The player controls an experimental fighter jet, which is apparently haunted by a strange AI prototype and spends most of the time inside the flight deck, taking over the controls of the pilot Ashlyn.Ash is part of the group of “misfits” who occupy the main stage of the narrative. They’re trying to understand why so many metal thieves are present in the surrounding areas. But a narrative in a 2D shooter? It is rare for a title with these characteristics to have such a long line of text, but in fact, it is very welcome. The entire dialogue is presented between lines of text without voice acting, between, and during combats.The group thus finds itself in the middle of a mission to save the world. A very old underwater base has been discovered with control properties of giant mechs, which are being controlled by people with bad intentions.However, the main thing about Jet Lancer is its gameplay that makes any player feel like a movie doublet, with all the action, explosions, and stunts that are needed to escape all enemy attacks. It is quite common for the screen to be filled with enemy ships and not even for a second you feel any break in terms of performance.At his disposal, the player has a machine gun that allows you to fire a stream of bullets, a special weapon with several options, from missiles to a line of explosives and the ability to “charge weapon” that has guided missiles, even drones that help to shoot down enemy targets. All of these modules can be picked up during history and make it possible to customize the ship however you want.Already on the ship, it is possible to fly in any direction, rotate on itself to avoid attacks and perform acrobatics, chopped flights, or 180 are on the menu.All the graphics, action, and fights against “Bosses” make Jet Lancer stand out from the rest of the genre titles. In fact, these confrontations are the real highlight of the experience. Although not necessarily difficult, the different attack patterns mean that the player needs to approach them differently. Combat against a giant sphere or a mechanical snake that flies and manages to dive into the ocean requires, of course, different attack strategies that leave any feeling of repetition aside.Between missions, a 3D world is presented, allowing you to control an aircraft carrier and choose the missions available at the moment. In total it is possible to count 40 missions. Although there is nothing but plains and water, the change in perspective is, in fact, a refreshing touch.After the game mechanics are well-tuned, each mission lasts only a few minutes. However, in situations like “score attacks” they can get a little more complicated. There are several factors such as the score that each type of weapon presents, in this situation the skill, the time, and the strategies are hand in hand.All of this together, adding a soundtrack of refinement, perfect for fighting enemies, reveals a vibe of titles from the 80s but with a current and quite successful face. Although a little short it is very desirable for enthusiasts of the genre.Check more recommendations from Exile

_childDocuments_.review: Would you pay a cosplayer to smash your teeth in with a hammer? This is the game for you.-Good Points-The gameplay mechanics are wonderful. There are so few titles these days which give you such tight and satisfying control of your vehicle/character, and I love frenetic shooting games. The music is genuinely great, but those of you who don't listen to a lot of speed metal might want for a more diverse soundtrack. The sound design is also very nice. Each explosion felt satisfying, and the visual aesthetics are very pleasing.-Bad Points-I broke the tutorial level by flying too fast/far or something. To fix it, I had to abandon the level and restart it. The objectives spawned outside of the valid flying area, though this was just a minor issue.There's this odd anime feeling to the whole story. The hot pink jet should've tipped me off, but the narrative is whimsical and a bit childish at some points. There are levels in the game where you are stuck hovering your jet over the water while text rolls across the screen, breaking the frantic action, and the characters' tones of voice just strike me as a little lukewarm. If you really enjoy anime, this may not be a bad point for you.Gameplay gets a little repetitive. The developers do help introduce variety into the game by changing objectives from one level to the next, and adding new enemy types, but the base action is the same. You get bombarded with progressively greater BS toward the end of the game, and the evasion mechanic feels inconsistent - choosing to work when it wants to.-Overall-This game has been on my wish list for a long time and I felt that the components came together a little awkwardly; the game needs a little more refinement. It seems that the difficulty is implemented by throwing more and more enemies at you until you want to rage quit. I suspect that the developers are still young, which can explain some of the qualities of the game, but it is an impressive technical achievement. Jet lancer is a visually appealing, attention-grabbing game with satisfying gameplay; for teenagers.-Final Thoughts-I would enjoy this game better with supplemental game modes such as an aerial obstacle course race, and also a more traditional top-down style shoot-em-up with a more expansive flying area. I just think it would be nice to soar between islands and cities while fighting sky pirates.I think it would be cool, and would add some serious depth and opportunity for narrative, if they had added some levels dedicated to the aircraft carrier. The level select area is fully rendered in 3d, so why not have levels that leverage this aspect of the game? Why not have a few 3-d levels where you have to navigate the captain's boat through a minefield while shooting down planes with an anti-aircraft battery or something like that; or even other boats and submarines (because, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I hate the enemy boats)?Why not have a 2-d rendered level with the aircraft carrier that the player can explore like a "hub world" and use to interact with the other characters and access ancillary features of the game (like changing the color and decals of my jet or, I dunno, like selecting purely aesthetic mods that turn ship explosions into confetti or something; or change the look of contrails and projectiles, or alternative HUD designs)?...and why does everyone call it "dodge rolling"?I like this game, but I wish it were put together differently.

_childDocuments_.review: I have absolutely no idea who or what recommended this game to me, but it definitely had something so I added it to my wishlist.Fast forward to today, I've just finished it and yeah, it's pretty good.Art style is nice, but it really nails the music. It was on point most of the time, giving you that extra shot of adrenaline you need to pass every mission. Maybe a couple more tracks would have been nice though.And speaking of missions, they can get pretty repetitive, but the gameplay is so fluid and addicting that you don't mind at all. Except the "get target score" missions. I hated those from the first one to the very last one.The story is "okay". I'd have liked if it was told with cinematics instead of text boxes. But on the other side there are plenty of boss battles and they are all really exceptional. Big shout out to the developers for this being the first game. I believe you'll do wonderful things in the future with the gameplay, boss battles and music. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun enough premise that's ruined by clunky controls and an exhausting last 25% of the game. Jet Lancer succeeds in levels where you're not fighting things on the ground, don't have gimmick enemy attacks to dodge (like screen-sized railgun-type shots), and have seven to ten enemy fighters to contend with. Otherwise, the awkwardness of controls, the screen filling up with so much visual spam you can't even see what's going on, and the intolerably long length of later levels align to just ruin it.The single best thing in the game, and something I very much appreciate and respect the devs for doing, is the Accessibility menu where you can turn on things like invulnerability, wider dodges, toggles for shoot and thrust, and so on. If that menu wasn't there, I would've refunded it. Fun enough to be had at the $10 mark, so wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It might be an odd way to start a negative review, but I wanted to start by saying a lot of things I liked about the game.  I think the visuals are very good, simple but effective spritework.  I think the plane handles really well, just the way it moves and controls is very fun to play around with, and the weapons are fun and fairly intuitive.  The enemies are actually kinda sophisticated, actively trying to be a little evasive, avoiding when you're on their tail and prioritizing attacking from angles you're not ready.  The bosses that I fought were fun fights.  The plane tuning, while simple, is high-impact, letting you swap out secondary weapons and make tweaks to how the plane fights and handles, which is a good way to add some variety while keeping flying the plane as the focus.So, with all that, why is this a negative review?  At its simplest, it comes down to mission design.  In particular, how so many of the missions seem to be working against the fun parts.  Three stood out, and a section of them in rapid succession is what ultimately made me stop playing.First, hacking missions.  Earlier I mentioned how flying and handling with the plan is fun, here's a mission type that says 'don't do that'.  To the game's credit, you can get the plane to hover with proper movement, but for something designed around speed and agility, finding a mission that goes 'now hold still' never felt fun.  And sure, you can move and break the connection without resetting progress, it just delays things, but the gameplay is so fast it's hard to do that strategically, generally you die before you've figured out whether you can hold ground successfully.Second, is a type of mission where you have to keep enemy presence below a certain level, destroying enemies as fast or faster than the spawn in.  This one works against enemy potential for maneuvers and chances for dogfighting.  Many times, I failed the mission because I would fly aggressively, and the enemy would scatter, essentially waiting out the timer, failing the mission not because I'm being beaten in combat but because I fail on technicality as enemies on the edge of the screen just kinda hover there non-aggressively for a bit.  The other thing is that there's a very similar concept but that works beautifully, in defense missions.  Missions where pushing the enemy away from a defense objective actually helps, as while destroying them is still better at least now aggression can successfully prevent attacks.Finally, score attack.  Something I've not mentioned yet is the scoring system, which includes some time, combo and technique elements.  It's not something I particularly like, I don't enjoy the perceived pressure of being graded and thus criticized for my gameplay at all times, but I respect them as a means to allow people of different skill levels to enjoy the game without compromising gameplay elements.  Someone who's struggling can still potentially muddle through with a low score and have a good time, someone who wants to refine their technique or spend more time with the game can learn the extra score mechanics and spend more time to master.Score attack throws that versatility out the window.  Now, you don't know how or don't enjoy learning the intricacies of semi-arbitrary scoring on top of regular gameplay?  Then you're not allowed to play more of the (otherwise fun) game.For what it's worth, I think some people will greatly enjoy this game.  Some people will enjoy opportunity or even need for greater mastery to make progress.  Certainly, there's an element of, I'm not the best at the game and simply improving my skill and understanding could alleviate these issues.  Some people will enjoy that kind of demand, or have more fun than I do playing around with the score system and other features I found very finicky.  I'm glad those people have fun with the game, but ultimately this review isn't for them.  This is more for people like me, who really like the look of the flying and dogfighting and find those in themselves fun, but have that ultimately frustrated by restrictions and obstacles to that gameplay.I would find it hard to recommend this game unless it was to a very specific sort of person.  Though at the same time, there's enough good here that I'm also very curious what the game might make in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, so, this is a running review. Devs asked for input, and I wanted to get my high HIGH recommendation contributing to this game's score. I presume y'all watched the trailers, so let's break it down based on that:Art: Absolutely beautiful to look at, if you're able to parse what's going on in all the explosions and jets darting about in the game. Vibrant use of colors that sends me straight back into late N64 era games (that overworld reminds me of Mega Man legends in particular, which is NEVER a bad thing). Music: Banger after banger. I'm not a huge music person, so I can't give you a long winded explanation on why I like. But I have the soundtrack on right the heck now, and it carried me through tax filing so 10/10 for your music person, Devs.Accessibility: I'm lucky enough to not need a whole lot of help with playing a game, but I'm extremely happy when I see an abundance of options available. And, well, you got 'em. Big ones, too, that will help all kinds of folk play this RSI inducing masterpiece of a game.Gameplay: Uhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh yes?!?!?! It's very good. Like, I haven't strained my hand like this playing anything in a long long time. Or my eyes, because I forget to blink in all the dog fighting and strafing run action. The base gameplay is solid with the default jet loadout, but the customization options are a big part of what gives the game a great deal of depth. Excuse me while I dash, once again, several meters into the ground.Now, I do have a few quibbles with the game. Clarity is a big issue here, given the speed of the gameplay. I'm not always sure on what killed me, and would definitely love some sort of "KILLED BY: X" notification on death. Maybe even a slow-motion replay option if I wanted to get real needy (it takes work to put this stuff in!). Additionally, there's a couple of enemies I'm not *quite* sure on what they do, exactly. It would be great to have some sort of in-game guide on 'em, once you've encountered a new type? Maybe there is one. Gonna check after posting this.(If you're someone who doesn't do fast games at all, I'd still give this game a look because of all the accessibility options it offers. I'll go into them more deeply on my next pass).TL;DR: Jet Lancer is an incredibly fast paced 2d side-scrolly jet fightin' game with amazing presentation cushioning good heckin' mechanics, and a surprisingly amount of depth and replayability (gotta get that ACE rank, baby).

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer's a pretty awesome 2D dogfighting game in its own right, and everything about it appeals to both a casual and a hardcore audience. The humour is a bit campy, but I like it, and the bossfights always leave in some sort of awe because I've found them pretty creative!The many loadout options means you can really play it your way, and I haven't found anything in the game that felt underpowered to use. Even lobbing a trio of bombs at other aircraft turned out to a pretty legitimate strategy!If you're looking for some difficult, yet accessible (difficulty options!) pick-up-put-down heart-pumping action, and you happen to like planes, you can't go wrong with this little gem!

_childDocuments_.review: (Got this game from exchanging keys with the dev who I met through mutual friends and we got to talking about indie development.)It's just a really solid game at what it is. As someone who isn't a fan of reflex-demanding action, it was satisfying to get into and had surprising depth with all the options you had at once. One big tip I wanna give is if you're like me and not sure about your ability to dodge EVERYTHING BEING SHOT AT YOU ALL THE TIME, just go to the accessability options and turn up the dodge timing a tick. It just allows you to be a *frame* later but it goes a long way into making it a chill but still challenging.As long as you put in a teensy bit of effort, you'll be pulling off pretty badass moves within the hour (I originally typo'd "air" here, how appropriate) - unload your guided missiles towards one target as you kill your engines, turn around and dodge a shot from behind as you annihilate that enemy, boosting past them into the distance as the wreck of the guy you first fired missiles at blazes by.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to feel like a supersonic badass ace pilot, this is the game for you. The gameplay is fast-paced and frantic. Combined with the soundtrack, the feeling of flying at high speed with more explosions on screen than a Michael Bay movie, is easily the best part of the game. Most of the story is okay, with just enough intrigue to keep you playing. The best of the story doesn't come until the . If you intend on getting the full experience, you should play through NG+ as well. In my opinion the normal mode is a little bit easy once you get your bearings. And while most of the game has a good balance of difficulty, there are a select few missions that are just plain frustrating, even more so in NG+. Sea Hunter is easily the worst in my opinion, a long and drawn out mission with tons of enemy spam with tanky boats you have to destroy. In addition, if you intend on going for the ACE achievements, good luck because many ACE requirements are quite tight and leave no room for error. Some of the earlier missions are actually harder to ACE because of the low enemy density depriving you of combo points. But my criticism is little for this game. It's not insane bullet hell, so if you're new to the genre it would be a good start. The gameplay and controls are tight and polished, the story is just a bonus to that. Definitely worth $15, even more so if you catch it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is a very fun, very hard 2D physics driven jet fighting game. It looks great and once you get the hang of it it’s very fun.That being said it’s VERY hard and I suspect a good number of people will bounce off of the title. Also the ranking system for each mission is a mess. Some levels are piss easy to get S+ is and others are nearly impossible to the point where it feels extremely arbitrary. Also the missions where you have to score a certain number of points while also surviving a set amount of time just suck. They’re tedious and the combo system is poorly defined.And this is a very personal preference but I really, really didn’t like the story and by the end just hated the main character. Still, a very fun game overall if you can look past those things.

_childDocuments_.review: Sucked-in and can't stop playing. This is one seriously high-octane, controller-squeezing game. You feel real accomplishment beating each level or boss, but you get to feel it all over again trying to perfect-rank every mission, and then you get it all over again in New Game +, and then you get it AGAIN trying to Ace NG+. If you're exhausted playing all that content, the arcade mode is seriously good fun. Story is seriously good; I cried at both endings. No spoilers but R-TYPE fans will catch a lightbulb early-on.Gameplay is... whew, so good. I am a particularly big fan of the fact that every weapon has a genuine role and there isn't a single choice of weapon that dominates the rest. The loadout screen feels like a "loadout screen" and not a progression tracker.Overall 10/10. Get this in your library; it's one I know I'll be able to pick-up anytime.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. There are really no flaws to the core gameplay that I can speak of; it's just an incredibly tight experience.What this game succeeds at most, in my opinion, is encouraging the player to improve their skill in a very naturalistic way through story-based challenges. For the first ~third of the game, I was getting by on bad habits by constantly firing and tossing out loads of guided missiles. So first the game hit me with a mission where a giant laser will lock onto your heat signature if you don't space out your shots, and didn't let me past until I had gotten that down. A few missions later, it introduced ewar fighters that hack your missile guidance, and I had to switch to more precisely-aimed weapons. And just like that, the game had taught me a more fun and engaging way of playing. If I had a critique to offer, it's that the boss fights can be a little bit lackluster. None are very hard, especially compared to some of the "normal" missions you do leading up to them. The story isn't going to blow your mind, but it has a few fun lines of dialogue.Overall, a very strong recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is a gorgeous shooter with super tight controls that plays like Luftrausers with an actual story mode and progressive gameplay mechanics.Pros:+ Instantly responsive controls.+ Supremely fun flight physics.+ Beautiful 2.5-D graphics.+ Varied stages and gameplay mechanics.+ Tons of unlockable upgrades for your ship.+ Epic boss fights.+ Highly configurable accessibility controls to tweak the game's difficulty.Cons:- Lean on content: NG+ and a few additional upgrades are all that's left after a brisk 5-hour campaign.- Little incentive to pursue S+ rank on stages.- Some tough difficulty spikes, especially in target score stages.All things considered, at $15 Jet Lancer is an easy must-buy for shooter fans. If the dev can smooth out the difficulty spikes and work out some sort of endless horde mode similar to Luftrausers, this game would be a masterpiece.  Try completing the penultimate mission in NG+ a different way...
