_childDocuments_.review: Before playing this game, Vlambeer's Luftrausers would have ranked somewhere in my Top 50 games of all time. The chaotic arcade-y dogfights, plane customization and overall style made it a game I had a hard time pulling away from when it released back in 2014. 2 hours in though, I have no problem saying that Jet Lancer has dethroned the game for me and stolen its spot. Jet Lancer is a fast-paced 2D frenetic dogfighting game in the same vein as Luftrausers. The aesthetics though of seeming like an underrated, sharply polished 90's anime are much more my speed. You play a cocky ace pilot testing out a strange and powerful new jet discovered by your rag-tag group of sky pirate hunting peacekeepers. The bird is ultra fast, sleek, and customizable. You're tasked with using your skills to tackle a bunch of different missions that range from hacking com towers, obliterating sky pirates, and destroying immense and mysterious giant boss robots that might have a considerable connection to your own recently found jet. As you complete a mission you'll be graded on your performance with accuracy, quick completion and perfect dodging enemy fire netting you the higher ranks and the desire to S rank everything is strong. You're also periodically rewarded with new parts that will allow you to change your special attacks or maybe modify your defenses. These new additions might prompt you to return to previous missions to raise your score with the toys at your fingertips that you previously didn't have.  Only critique I'd have at the moment of this review and my time played is the lack of an endless mode (that is of course if such a thing isn't already present and just simply unlocked by some method like beating the game which I've yet to find out). Each mission has a distinct endpoint so far and I'd love to play a mode where escalating hordes of enemies (possibly including difficulty settings that could throw random bosses from the main mode into the fray) attack and you have to survive as long as possible with the loadout you've prepared or maybe even randomized. A mode un-tethered by the mission structures and time limits that appear in the campaign where you are treated to difficult & dazzling dogfights that could last a 1/2 hour or more at S+ rank as your skill gradually increases. Overall, any fans of Luftrausers or anyone else looking for an extremely fun and flashy twitch-based action experience should 100% consider Jet Lancer a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a successor to the excellent action of Luftrausers, you've found it. Beyond that, you're also getting banging BGM, gorgeous visuals, excellent boss fights, a supremely dynamic difficulty system involving the upgrades you select, a suite of accessibility options, an exciting new game plus experience, and a narrative with enough simplicity to let the gameplay do its thing, yet enough charm to get some smiles out of you. By definition, a complete package for a beyond-reasonable price.Also the talking cat. They mention the talking cat in the feature list, and damn if he doesn't deserve to be there.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Fast paced dogfighting action with plenty of over-the-top maneuvers to execute. Be the ace of the skies, assuming the skies are from an anime about superjets. Highly recommended if the trailer/screenshots even vaguely interest you.Positives:+Smooth, exciting gameplay with differing difficulties based on player equipment choice (auto dodge, shield after hit, etc, are optional). Skill expression through a variety of different weapons. Bosses are a cool spectacle, if not a little easy.+Excellent presentation. Simple, but striking visuals and a rocking soundtrack.+New Game Plus for added challenge (they actually change stuff!) and replayability.+Talking catNegatives:-Issues with visibility at times due to screenshake and certain similarly colored enemies. -Relatively simple story, depending on what you enjoy this can be good or bad.-No endless/survival mode! Biggest issue so far. NG+ is fine but I want a sandbox.-Talking catEDIT: They added an endless mode (sort of)! Arcade mode is exactly what I wanted and allows you to go through a ton of waves filled with enemies vying for your death. Random upgrades to choose from and four unique jets/characters mean you'll be entertaining yourself for a while. Doesn't change my final verdict, the game is recommended regardless.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is an incredibly cool game. It can get very intense, but despite its fast pace, it somehow always remains manageable. Feeling like a badass is easily achievable due to the frankly perfect game feel. Most people dismiss the story, but I think it's super intriguing and a perfect fit for the gameplay. Very excited to try out the roguelite arcade mode, as this is some of the most fun I've had in a while!
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: This is as close to perfect as a game can get. Everything from the art style, music, and gameplay is amazing. You can customize the way you fight, and the story keeps you going. The game is challenging, with ways to either increase or decrease the difficulty based on what modules and weapons you bring. Boss fights are interesting and each one is different from the next as to feel like a fresh fight. I'm only halfway through my first playthrough so far but I'll be playing this game for many hours after.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: I had been following this game for a while on twitter, so I had a pretty good idea of how good this game was going to be, but good lord the finished product is so much *more* that I ever could have expected. Every single part of the game (so far at least) is so well made and crafted that it really is a joy to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:This game is a great indie purchase!Great art style, but it was the soundtrack that made me buy it.The combat is a bit tough for me, but I'm rather new to shoot-em-ups so keep that in mind. Good sized campaign, still haven't reached the end at 94 minutes in.Only thing I would tweak: Customizing your aircraft is a nice addition, but the wording/ descriptions seem a bit unclear. If they could be more direct, or highlight which update affects what on your jet may happen clarify it.Go buy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Cool as hell dogfighter with that crucial luftraisers movement dopamine rushThe movement and momentum are fine tuned to allow you to pull off some absolutely nutty stuff, like cutting your engines mid boost just to flip around and blast off in a new direction, or to flip the plane 180 degrees to shoot behind you without changing direction. There’s tons of badass weapons to pick and choose from, but for my money, nothing is as satisfying as barrel rolling through a huge cluster of enemies spraying out homing missles as you go. The sprite work is visceral and striking, with the burning wrecks of enemy planes arcing gracefully out of the sky when you shoot them down. Even the story, while it’s no masterpiece, is still pretty damn good for the kind of arcadey game this is. I do have one complaint, and I have to spoil some of the bosses to talk about it, so heads up. But even with that, I can’t deny that this is the purest, most visceral fun I’ve had with a game since the new Doom came out. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, played Beta and release, if you liked Luftrauser's you won't just like this you will LOVE this.Arcade-y and intense as hell, the gameplay is solid in all regards. The Soundscape is nutty, soundtrack is amazing (made by Fat Bard, who also made the excellent crashlands ost) and dont get me started on the art direction, its all 100%. The perfect mix between a standard shmup and original game play (and i hate shmups normally). Am I really enjoying this game? Hell Yeah. Seriously, this little indie game is solid through and through.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: + Great graphics and music+ Fun and fast-paced gameplay+ Plenty of accessibility options- Lack of mission variety- Boring storylineIt was nearly six years ago that we got LUFTRAUSERS, a cool indie arcade shooter that, while it wasn't without some issues, I did end up giving a positive recommendation to. Now we have Jet Lancer, a game that could prove to be a worthwhile successor.Although it has its issues, Jet Lancer is still a fun enough arcade shooter. The core gameplay is solid, the graphics and music are nice, and the addition of accessibility options was good to see as well. However, the severe lack of mission variety does bring down the experience, along with the lackluster story tacked on top of it. I wouldn't recommend it as an immediate buy, but it's worth a look if you see it on sale. Follow my  for more reviews + videos!
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: You want a Luftrausers clone, but a bigger game with story, characters, missions? I know... but i was disappointed with this one. The controls are overcomplicated & the aircraft feels loose, the visuals are simplistic, too bright & often unpleasant, story's really bland (sky pirates blah blah), boss fights demand hard work - product is at least 3x overpriced.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: I always thought that  looked good ever since I added it to my wish list before it came out. But I never thought it'd be as  as it was! And for such a cheap price, too!I've played other games in this price range; , , and , just to name a few. They were all quite good and definitely worth playing but  blows them all out of the water. It's also surprisingly long for that same price, too; I wasn't expecting to take a bit over seven hours to finish the base game alone, and that's without touching New Game+.The primary gameplay loop of holding W to move forward in the direction of your mouse cursor works brilliantly, especially with your ship's momentum carrying it forward when you let go of W but letting you turn still. This allows for a lot of natural aerial maneuvers that are fantastic to look at but simple to execute yet still difficult to master, much like the combat in the  series.The story's also quite good as well. The characters are fleshed out with good writing and enjoyable dialogue. I think some elements are skipped over a bit too quickly, though; the characterisation of the main villain and the conclusion could've used some more detail. But that's just a bubble in the wall paint of an extremely solid and fantastic game that I cannot recommend enough. It's brilliant and well made.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Please do not purchase this game if you have a sensitivity to strobing lights or sudden bursts of light. There is no option to turn them down, and the latter half of the campaign is an unending parade of them, whether prompted by your dodges, hits to your plane, hits to the enemy, or just your plane abruptly changing direction. The game advertises a 'strobing lights off' option, but in my experience, this does very little to reduce the density of those effects.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: loved luftrausers and always wanted more after finishing it, so when I one day found out somebody was working on something that seemed to basically be a spiritual successor to luftrausers I got excited. now (around 4 years later) jet lancer is finally out. looking through the reviews people throw around luftrausers alot, saying that if you liked it you're going to love this game. for me that was however not the case.enemy bullet hitboxes often seem to be twice as big as their sprite.dodging seems weird. sometimes you have a short period of time to do a dodgeroll AFTER taking damage to negate it while other times this doesn't seem to be an option. I'm not sure if this is a bug or intentional.combat isn't that fun. either you gotta hunt down an enemy for a chance to maybe hit them once or twice then they dodge out of the way, meaning you have to wait for your jet to turn where you now have to shoot just slow enough to be annoying or the enemy is hard to hit because by the time you're able to shoot at it you already gotta change direction and fly away again to avoid taking damage.the upgrades ( or at least the ones I've unlocked so far ) just seem boring and or worse than sutff you have unlocked from the beginning.the UI to indicate wether you're overheating or wether your secondary weapon needs to charge is placed terribly imo. sure it looks fancy but I find myself having to look at my mouse cursor or at the edges of the screen constantly.this often leads to me forgetting I even have a secondary weapon, which usually would be fine because I'd just play without it but every few levels/tries the game has to put the same annoying dialogue to tell you that you're not using your secondary alot.and to top it off some of the missions are just annoying to play. a mission where you have to protect a seeminlgy suicidal AI, a mission where you have to kill more enemies than an AI but it seems to be havily rubber-banded, and missions where everytime you shoot for longer than a second an orbital deathlaser shoots you.maybe I just haven't played the game enough but the first 2 hours certainly seemed more annoying than fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: super hard but still really fun!i love the amazing pixel art and game in general.the ability to choose different powers is cool although i would like to be able to change my ship colour.i love dancing though enemies and dodging and blowing up stuffi highly suggest you buy this game even though at the start it may be hard in the end you feel like a master of the skiesoverall super cool but i would love a multiplayer mode (i know its harder to code but it would be sick)if you are reading this buy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic presentation in service of a game that looks a lot like an update to Time Pilot, but is nowhere near as interesting. I think out of 20 minutes in an arcade style game, about 1 minute of that was spent actually looking at an enemy on screen. The game just doesn't have a good mix of the relative inertia and speed of the player and enemies relative to the size of the maps, and too much of it is spent waiting for a wave to start or navigating to a new mission. Shooting something down or getting hit by something doesn't at all feel like it's related to skilful play or quick inputs, just an MMO style grind of working out whether it's even worth your time to bother dodging before the thinly spread mission content ends.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: I am the bullet hell now!Fun game! Got me considering jet configurations before missions, I do feel somewhat badass. Difficulty is adjustable via configurations.It's not your typical bullet hell but rather a shoot'em up. As in it's not really dodge focused because of the movement style, but it's there a little. Characters interactions are funny it's a cute game.I bought it on sale for 3.69 (nice), and I think it's worth it!Edit : I have now unlocked the NG+ missions. Really ups the pace and I love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is an 'okay' game that I'd rate as a 6 out of 10 - i.e. good but not good enough. Jet Lancer plays 'similar to Luftrausers' - a likeness that is constantly cited throughout the other reviews for this game - but the game fell short comparatively in regards to my overall amount of enjoyment. At the $9.99 USD price I paid for the game (on sale), I'd consider Jet Lancer to be overpriced and would not recommend it to friends unless they saw it on sale for $4 - $5 USD.- The game went in for this 'anime like' style to the character personalities, story telling, and musical score. Done well, this wouldn't normally be an issue but I found myself rolling my eyes and groaning through most of the cutscenes and story segments. The story was like watching a bad 'Americanized' dub to what would otherwise be adequate scripting in the natural language. There's a sassy talking cat, spunky/tomboyish female protagonist, grizzled old-timer with a shady past, a cocky rival that's actually a doofus....the game really wants to throw all these trope-riddled 'anime-like' characters together but fails to do anything compelling with them or the story. - The music repetitive and eventually quite annoying. The 'upbeat' and 'hoppy' nature of the soundtrack does not fit with the overall tone of the story. Imagine playing a game where the fate of humanity was on the line, epic gun fights and explosions were happening all over - people dying......but the sountrack to Super Mario Sunshine was playing in the background....seems like a bad fit, right? Well, that's the auditory experience with Jet Lancer.- You can only get hit 3 times before dying. Your health does not recharge and there are no health pickups during a mission. If you are on a particularly difficult or lengthy mission, this will result in frequent restarts and frustration as you inevitably mistime a dodge-roll or otherwise crash into another jet or stray bullet due to the breakneck speed of your jet. Of course, you can cheat and alter damage settings in the menus but that feels like cheating and cheapens the experience. Jet Lancer would have been infinitely better had it just emulated the damage system used in Luftrausers.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: A nice small game similar to Luftrausers and Hyperspace Dogfights. It is slightly different in that it has a campaign set up where you go from level to level in an overworld a la Broforce. The campaign itself runs for about 3 hours and it overall a pleasant experience that doesn't drag on for too long. There is a ng+ mode as well as an arcade mode. Ng+ seems to be the typical ng+ stuff but I haven't gotten that far in to see if there are any story differences. The arcade mode gives you a more rogue like experience where you pick a ship "class" to start and go from wave to wave/boss to boss getting upgrades in between.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Right now i'm 2 hours into the game and i'm not impressed. Very repetitive missions and enemies. Good music and backgrounds but not enough of either. Bosses share bullet patterns and attacks. Gameplay consists mostly of turbo boosting to an enemy across the stage and immediately killing them. Overall the game is way too easy. Even with upgrades that make it more difficult, most levels can be beaten on a first attempt. Characters and dialogue are bad, and the game has a long ass timer preventing you from skipping it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few games I need a "maybe" recommendation for.Art style and execution is fine, but the game should come with a blatant "challenging" warning like Super Meat Boy. Along with all the judgement and "git gud" comments that comes with.I thought going in it would be similar to Luftrausers, but the changes made to turn it from rougelite into levels with a storyline are cool and make it a different experience (even though the fly and shoot mechanics are super similar).I did not finish the game. The problems for me started at Op 13. Pushed until Op 22 and gave up. Simply not worth the pain.Those aren't even the hardest levels, from discussion threads and vids seen its simply gets more brutal. This is on "normal" difficulty, without even going near NG+.Combat's not even the problem. My issue was constantly finding myself fighting the level design, specifically in minimum score vs time missions. Add to this "stealth" aspect (shoot too much? now dodge beams as well.) and you end up with levels that just aren't fun. I could end up beating them, eventually, but I wouldn't be happy.Caveat: Boss fights were fun, but those are too rare to save me from frustration.Problem is probably me, but I'm guessing others like me may see this and think JL is as light-hearted as its art seems. It isn't.This is a hardcore game that starts easy, but spikes so hard you'll wonder if you accidentally changed the difficulty to "masochistic".If you're up for that, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts really fun, but the game just gets too damn hard. Too many enemies on the screen, Too much going on, I can't even see what's happening sometimes. Occasionally I'll take damage and not even know why? I dodge through one attack and immediately fly into another the second my dodge ends. Feels way to cheap. If there's a way to avoid these situations I never found them.I never feel like I'm getting better. I just feel like I'm beating my head against the wall until I somehow luck out. I know the game has assist modes that go as far as being invincible. But that's just boring. I want a challenge, but I don't want to feel like I'm being punished.I just wish it started this hard so I could've gotten a refund. Oh well, looks pretty anyways.Gamers tend to hate themselves these days and confuse unfair with fun. If you're one of those people, you'll dig this game. Otherwise, skip it. It's over-hyped for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: This is a completely subjective, absolutely petty review.I first played Jet Lancer back in its Beta phase, and followed its development for even longer. Now that I get to play the finished product...I'm happy with what I had already seen in Beta, but unhappy with much of the presentation that has been added since. Hardly any of my complaints are substantial. The game is good. But I don't like it, because of how it's wrapped up. The Good:+ The backgrounds are beautiful. Lots of deep blue sky with interesting architecture and the occasional goings-on to see. Really good. Nice colors!+ The gameplay is generally good.The Bad:- The screen area is too small. I want to see more going on at once - no need to be *that* close to the action. Annoying to have so much off-screen all the time.- The game often freezes briefly, especially when dodging or ramming missiles or other aircraft.- While the game has lots of accessibility options, including autofire, there is no option for having special attacks, which need to be charged, charge in any way other than holding down a key all the time. Tiresome.- OP16, the escort mission, which introduces the character of Peter. Peter is written to be maximally annoying. But to me, the entire cast is that annoying - the only difference is that, with Peter, it's intentional. The writing in the game is that bad. But back to the point - the escort mission is bad. Bad. Bad. And also the point at which I stopped playing.The Ugly:* Core complaint: I was honestly taken aback when I read the dev blog that presented the characters, and I'm not reconciled with them since. I don't like any of the characters in general, nor their personalities in particular, nor the style they're drawn in, nor the dialogues.* The music hurts my ears. Maybe I'm a wuss, maybe I'm insufficiently nostalgic for the Gameboy experience, maybe I should just switch it off. But as it is, it's annoying to painful to listen to.* Why are so many menu transitions keyed to "hold button"? I notice that seems to be the usual for games meant to be played with a controller - do controllers need such a safety feature? KB+M does not. It annoys me.* Forward-swept wings look dumb.* The bullets are too damn big.* The game has such pretty skies, but the camera is tilted far-down in the 3D scenes. What a waste. Sad.* It's evidently made for cat-lovers. Or furries. Too bad. I'm neither.So there we go. Thumbs down, for reasons of differing tastes.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: This game constantly reads false mouse inputs. My mouse does not have any issues with uncommanded inputs in any other game, but in this title the menu is stuck scrolling up constantly and the player vehicle is stuck pointing in one direction. This can't be resolved by unbinding controls to the mouse and I am not willing to unplug my mouse to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game. Upbeat and extremely fun soundtrack. High octane thrill ride and difficult challenge for even elite gamers.A few recommendations for the devs: On normal mode the final boss and penultimate boss need to be a lot tougher. Compared to Empress and the last level before those two they were baby-easy mode.Add an achievement for dunking an enemy in the water when they lock on to you before they charge at you.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful 2D jet fighting game. Very high chaos and rather challenging.There's meaningful modifications to your jet that unlock as you play, and the entire cast of characters if fun and endearing. All in all a very well rounded and enjoyable experience, even if I really struggled with some of the missions so far^^Played through the base game, and New Game + seems to have additional enemy types and everything, in addition to unlocking an arcade mode. If you enjoy the basic principle of what's offered here, this game has such a wealth of quality content.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Feels absolutely phenomenal, if you enjoy arcade-style shoot 'em ups with a bit of bullet hell, like Luftrausers by Vlambeer, then you'll LOVE this!  I had a blast with Luftrausers and this looked like a deeper, more fleshed-out version of that gameplay in every way, and that's exactly what this is.  Haven't even played an hour yet and I know I'll be coming back to this for a long time to come.I'm also super thankful for the difficulty modifications they included in the accessibility menu, it may not look like much but it makes a world of difference.  I highly recommend setting the "invincibility" setting to half damage if you want a more casual experience.  Normally you can take 3 hits before failing a level, having 6 hits instead lets you play recklessly and feel like a badass, which I love for this sort of game!
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: I played with the Invincibility option on, hats off to the developers for including it. I found the game immensely enjoyable. The plane controls weirdly but the dogfights were nonetheless quite satisfying. The story was okay, loved the characters and art style. I read in the Steam Community that the True Ending is achieved in NG+, but the thought of struggling through even more difficult escort / bomber missions feels like a chore, so I'm not going to. OVERALL, fly away!
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD:-Art is very beautiful.-Very fitting music.-The game is easy to read even within the chaos on screen.-Abilities have good variety.-Nostalgia I guess for most people that are going to try it.-Engaging, non-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bossfights. Pretty good.THE BAD:-No options on difficulty/assistence.-Sometimes enemy missiles don't deactivate even when you've dodged them.-I've beaten Resident Evil 4-6 in professional and both Hotline Miamis so I think I have the credentials to say the difficulty is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enough to make me refund it.-Unpredictable enemy attacks that let you with no time window to dodge (mostly with ships).-Sometimes AI kamikazes at you for no reason and you lose the game.-The "Dumb Bomb" weapon is dumb for the wrong reasons, it does like 70% less damage than it should.-The bit of the story i've seen is kinda meh.-The cat is annoying af.-No more planes to play with? Not even a recolor? If it really is like that, that's kinda cheap. Even more considering the base plane colour is a cancerous bright pink.I wanted to like this game. And I think it's the second time maybe in all my life that i've refunded something, but I guess It just didn't rub me the right way. I see a lot of potential and clearly a lot of people liked it, so I'd say give it a try, It might be a blast for you :)
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: This was just really really good. Beautiful pixel art, incredible sense of velocity, good Jet customization, really tight controls and awesome combat.Even the story and characters are nice, feels like a flight anime hehe. Soundtrack is also on point.Overall, one of the best games I've played recently. Great stuff.There's a cat.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer feels like Luftrausers the same way Unreal feels like Quake. It controls very similarly, and is presented very similarly, but once you get past the surface level similarities there's a lot that makes it different (and also really good).You have 3 HP instead of a regenerating pool, you have a dodge that gives you a near-miss weapon boost, and most upgrades are not mutually exclusive. These changes are all balanced very well, and make combat feel more like a sequence of battles with more strategic thought put into loadouts. Appropritately, the campaign is structured by missions (and endless is structured by bosses and waves with rogue-lite upgrades) to complement this.I'm still playing through, so I'll add anything else after finishing the game, but so far it's great! Absolutely worth getting if you had any fun with LuftrausersEdit: Beat the game. Still would recommend, but ♥♥♥♥ mission 26. The game took me ~5 hours to beat, and arcade mode still has at least another 10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game just feels not fun at all, at first its alright but then it just becomes absolute bullethell where you cannot deal any damage to any enemy with abysmal ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dodges that even if you dodged still you get hit and die, the fact that you only get 3 hearts is just bad at that point just make you dont have any hp at all in this game because you cannot regen the hp at all and the upgrades just useless... cause simply because the starting gear is just simply superiour compared to anything else and others just feel downgrade or too useless, expected a lot from this game but got this.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Luftrausers with a light-hearted, ace-combat-y tone to it.Dodges are satisfying to pull off and don't require overly tight timings.If there's anything to criticize, it's that sometimes visual clarity will fail. Some colors match where they shouldn't. And certain cinematic effects for large destructive weapons will turn the screen black and white, meaning you can't see yourself in clouds near the top of the map.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Great, smooth, fast-paced gameplay with beautiful pixel work and an amazing chiptune soundtrack, this game just doesn't miss. There's a fair bit of customization you can get on your ship and it all feels meaningful and fun. The game is also not very long, took me about 6 hours to get through it the first time, but I SUCK at fast games, so better players might get it done in even less than that. Still NG+ has been very fun so far with very powerful unlocks that are exclusive to it. The arcade mode is also just dumb fun to see how long you last before the screen is just bullets.The story is surprisingly fun for a game that really doesn't need it since most people will get it just for the gameplay; it's nothing you haven't seen before, but the characters are cute and have some depth to them.Easy 8/10 game, very much worth the standard price of 8 bucks
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Great experience. Fast-paced action that feels great in hand and made especially gratifying through excellent visual effect work and lots of player agency. Good quantity of content for its price and an insanely rocking soundtrack.Some cons: visual clarity is sometimes poor and the dodge roll feels a bit overpowered as it's highly spammable with next to no risk; it feels like the dash module you get later in the game would be better as the default, since it consumes boost and overall feels more fun to play with. I'll add that the story, while fine and not obstructive to the gameplay, didn't particularly catch my attention.Writing this just after having beaten the main story, so I can't speak for the post-game content, but there seems to be a lot of it with New Game + that I'm looking forward to.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game in my library for YEARS, and in it's first versions i didn't find it really interesting, but i can say with full confidence this is one of the better arcade dogfight titles out there, very replayable, adicting and fun for the price.It has a quick to learn, hard to master control scheme, with a parry system that rewards risky/skillful playstyles, an upgrade/inventory system that makes every engagement approachable for different playstyles, a simple to follow storyline (it's a shoot-em-up arcade style game so it's not it's focus), good music (i've read the best comes in the latter stages, which i haven't gotten to yet...). The only little thing i think could have been done better was the protagonist, as for the time i've played she's not very likable and it's a little too edgy for my taste, but it's just a minor gripe... if you just want to play for the fun: GO FOR THIS GAME.In short: One of the most fun "pickup and play" arcade shooter i've played, it has a LOT more depth to it than you might think at the beggining, please give it a chance and it will not dissapoint. If you played this years ago, it's now a totally different game and a lot of love was put into it, it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game. Story was an entertaining snack.Although the arcade mode unlocks later in the 'base' game, it never really reaches the customisation and handling of Luftrausers, which is what I hold as reference for well handling. Just, the gravity feels off compared to it. And the fact that touching the water is instant death.I would also do away with the roguelike 'rarity' power differences, you're not customising your run when you get offered a basic upgrade vs a 'gold' upgrade where the numbers are just superior. Stacking the same buff, sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Jet lancer is essentially a spiritual successor of games like Luftrausers.The soundracks slaps (even though it doesn't have many tracks), the controls are very responsive and aiming with a mouse is a big upgrade compared to using the keys to aim (like in Luftrausers). The story is nothing special but it's not too bad, and it includes NG+ and new unlockable upgrades to keep the gameplay loop refreshing.11/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a delight to beat in both NG and NG+. Especially the latter because I opted for the perk that reduces you to 1 hit 1 kill with extra mobility. I guess there's always the Arcade mode hahah.Fantastic pixel work, satisfying gameplay and boppin' music!
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 9 hours finishing the campaign on "normal" difficulty and the other 21 on acing every mission including the NG+ mode and it was worth every minute, I never got bored even if simplifying the game it is "just flying around destroying jets" the story it's not that deep but the NG+ mode has a plot twist that I liked a lot, the only thing that i don't know if it's good or bad would be that you don't unlock all the upgrades on the normal mode but in the NG+ mode, "why is it good?" because it motivates you on finishing the NG+ mode. "why is it bad?" because while you're doing a mission in NG+ and unlock a new upgrade you`re like "Oh man, this upgrade would've come perfect for the previous level" and it kinda irritates me a bit since I wanted to Ace the level and then forget about it (trust me some levels are a nightmare that you don't want to repeat), not doing it twice because the upgrade that was better for  that level is unlocked 2 levels later. As I said earlier, the game never got me bored so even if having to complete the level twice it isn't a real problem.But what if you liked the game a lot but you aced every mission? Arcade mode, basically endless mode where you unlock upgrades as you clear the enemy waves, pretty fun and even the arcade mode has some exclusive things  that you can unlock too!The artistic side, I liked it a lot, I'm a pixelart fanboy and the style of this one is really good, the faces already tells you the personality of each character before getting to know them, not to mention the jet sprites animation are very fluid.The technical gameplay side, I think it's very well achieved, like, if you lose it was because you were not good enough, not because the level was bad designed or because of a bug. I was another review saying that "there's no difference between your projectiles and enemy's, so it's harder to avoid things because you don't know if the attack is friendly or not" 1. The projectiles are different. 2. Even if they were the same, how tf is your own bullet supposed to go towards you?, missiles do if they get hacked but the game not only has an icon on screen to tell you that a missile is going to hit you but they're highlighted when they're being hacked and after that, they start to shift colours between red and white like a normal enemy missile. 3. Resuming what I said before, if it's coming towards you, evade it so even if the game was just black and white the experience would be the same.Overall rating of the game: 9.25/10Frantic and challenging, the only bad things about it are the ones I commented at the beginning of the review.Recommended

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun shmup that is very easy to recommend (especially on sale) if you like unique and difficult games. If you've played luftrauser and wanted more I'd totally recommend giving this a go. Some earlier reviews mention the difficulty curve is bumpy but I think that has largely been fixed in patches as it was mostly very solid (except for the last two bosses being much easier than both the bosses and general missions preceding them). It did get pretty difficult towards the end but you can get through it by getting better and tinkering with the equipment you use. The customization is pretty minimal though. I found the challenges a good level and very satisfying. The piloting is fun to learn and get better at. Gameplay felt very tight once you get used to it. I was coming from playing luftrausers which is similar but just different enough that it took some time to adjust. so it took some time to readjust. Early levels we're pretty easy and served as a good tutorial, but it pretty quickly ramped up which forces you to engage in all the systems and is when the game really shines. Really satisfying play. The game looks great the pixel art is very good. Sometimes there is a lot going on on the screen which can be hard to parse but I found that for the most part I was able to get into the flow even when things got crazy.Story and writing both were solid, nothing crazy but also nothing bad, I was happy with it. Nothing cringe, some funny moments, and easy to follow. I was able to beat the standard difficulty campaign in about 10h while not entirely focusing on it. There is a higher difficulty new game plus as well as the option to go for acing all the missions and an arcade mode so there is a good amount of content of you want to dig in deeper and are ok with higher difficulty. EDIT: was able to get 5h more out of new game plus and it wasnt a huge increase in challenge but was fun so would totally recommend it.I played entirely on the steam deck and it was a great experience. Seemed like I was able to get atleast 6h of playtime from fully charged.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Good looking and high octane action fun,Game starts great but later on the missions become enemy spam bullet hell where they spawn faster than you can kill them (See Operation 37 for example, oh and it's a timed score mission - great).Boss battles are rare and far inbetween, you don't really even battle other competent jets in the air besides 2 times.You have to cheese the combat by equiping a dodge on your afterburner and continue endlessly rolling just to survive, that kind of takes out the skill out of the equation, it's just spamming the same two buttons,Was not looking forward to an hour or two of just mindlessly bashing roll.Was unable to finish it, can't refund it, recommend it on sale.

_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: I finished with Jet Lancer the other day, not completed it, but had to mark it "done with" nonetheless.Good game, taking control of a advanced fighter on a 2D plane, armed with various weapons you are given all types of missions to complete, destroy all enemy forces, hack radio towers (i.e. stay in the vicinity of them for a bit), defend something etc, it's all good fun and very much in the template of a similar game called Luftrausers, should you know it.You have the opportunity to load out your fighter how you like, with a range of main weapons, in the form of different types of forward firing guns, explosive weaponry such as homing missiles or dumb fired scatter grenades and also a special attack, like deploying drones that hover in the air attacking enemies on your behalf.The action is fast and fun, and very easy to just pick up and play. Various enemy types have you switching up tactics and approaches to battle, various boss stages present different challenges to overcome, usually focusing on 1 or 2 aspects of the combat (such as dodging at the right time, in the form of a barrel roll that makes you invincible for a few frames) and it all moves a cheesy anime inspired narrative along.The only reason I didn't finish the game was due to getting stuck! I am fairly confident I am in the last few missions of the campaign, however this particular level has you having to hit a certain high score within a time limit, with points awarded for destroying enemies and points multiplied if you can get chains of kills within a certain window.I, however, could not hit the target score, no matter what I did. I even went into the options and activated some of the accessibility options, such as invincibility and longer time windows to successfully dodge attacks,But alas, I couldn't do it. This may be more due to my ineptitude than the game, however after many attempts, I have decided to put this game down and move on.So yeah, recommended arcade shooter, but perhaps a caveat to some potential difficulty spikes.

_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: In short, If you wanted Luftrausers to have a plot, more boss fights, and a different means of customizing your jet, this is a good game to check out. I really liked my time with it, and I'll probably fool around with NG+ pretty soon here. The plot's nothing incredible, but it isn't bad for what it is, and it definitely kept me going. As for the gameplay, it really does feel like Luftrausers. With a few changes. Namely, rather than building a plane from a weapon, a body, and an engine, you pick a sub-weapon, a 'Charge' weapon, and four 'modules'. Your main shooter's a simple machine gun type thing, but upon making a successful dodge roll (A simple dodge in place) it gains a significant damage boost. Sub-weapons have four shots that reload over time and include, thus far, simple seeker missiles (Which can be hacked by late-game enemies) Unguided Rockets (very fast, can't be hacked) Proximity Charges (A shotgun blast of three bombs that go off when they get close to an enemy) and Armor piercing rockets (Unguided, pierce enemies and don't appear to explode. Useful for certain bosses who have multiple 'parts'.) with more seemingly available in NG+.Charge weapons can be fired 'off the cuff' but deal the most damage when you take the time to fully charge them. Fully charging them does mean they take longer to recharge, but it's worth it. They include a seeker barrage (Identical to the sub-weapon seekers, but it fires off something like twelve in a fully charged barrage. Also hackable.) Megabeam (a huge laser with high damage. A bit tricky to use outside of boss fights) A bomb (Just a very large high-damage bomb, good for boats and tanks.) Companion drones (1-3 floating turrets, depending on charge time. They do not move from their initial position, have a moderately short range, and can be killed by enemies. Useful in missions where you're hopelessly outnumbered, or against slow-moving bosses) with more likely available in NG+.Modules make changes to how your jet and weapons act, with small changes like 'increase afterburner time' or 'your charge weapon recharges faster' but some of them really do change up your whole strategy, such as the one that replaces your stationary dodge roll with a short forward dash, capable of slicing through your enemies. You can use four modules at once, and there's too many for me to recount them all, especially since nearly a third are hidden in NG+! As for the boss fights... Well, giant robotic weapons platforms are kind of a shooter stable, but they're mostly well designed, and interesting to fight. I will say they got a little too heavy on the 'Giant death laser beam' attacks towards the end, but still.In summary, it's cheap, it's fun, and I'll probably fool with it again soon.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to try Jet Lancer, but Luftrausers was on sale for $2. They looked similar so I bought the cheaper of the two. I severely disliked LUFTRAUSERS. I played it for like 15 mins, and I hated it. It just felt clunky and hard and bland so Jet Lancer  went on the back burner as both games looked about the same. Well, Jet Lancer finally went on sale for 50% so here I am giving it a try and expecting me to probably not like it, but I had to give it a chance.Good news is I like it.  The plane feels good and has lots of punch with the Afterburners and Barrel Roll for evading. The game is semi-beginner friendly. Gives you a challenge (lest you use equip drones). So I am having fun flying and dodging.I am not a huge fan of is the ugly 3D open world level select. I feel like I'm maneuvering around FFVII world view circa 1997. The story seemed cliche and blah at the start. There is a decent twist at the end if you unlock it. Some voice acting would open it up for sure. The big, long blocks of texts are just that big long blocks of texts. But at the same time... it's an addition to the shmup genre that some may enjoy. I am tired of these bubbly ace pilots in anime, tho after a few scenes that calms down a crumb, and finally, by the end the story is decent.There are various objects over the course of the 40 missions, and some missions even get interrupted so it does help with the story immersion. So Jet Lancer has a nice blend of gameplay, ship customization, story, and strategy.Most of this strategy comes into play if one wants to "ACE" a mission. Meaning take no hits, and often complete the mission in record time or combo & counter the crap out of the enemy (btw you'll need to go back with your weapon unlocks to ACE most missions). Which I just want to say that the requirements for ACE'ing missions can be down right brutal and unfair. I get that it is possible, but I have had some absolute great times or scores but missed the Rank by slivers. ACE'ing seems to also only be possible by using Dash attacks so it really narrows down the creativity, and one has to fly uber, uber aggressive. Hell, even some of the scoring missions require one to be ridiculously aggressive and it can be tedious. Granted, I was playing NG+ with the One Life Module, and I had forgot that I could go back to 3 Lives.... that may have been... my issue at one point lol.Anyways, great game. Hope there's a second one some day with even more oompfh!

_childDocuments_.review: I received Jet Lancer as a gift from a friend, and initially did not really enjoy it. It's a hard game to get into, and although I eventually warmed up to it, I'll say up front that it has a spirit of tryhard-ness not lessened by its variety of accessibility options. They are of course worlds apart in gameplay, but I had a lot more fun playing Project Wingman, as an example.Set above a colorful sci-fi future archipelago, Jet Lancer has you take the role of mercenary fighter pilot Ash Leguinn, armed with a mysterious, AI-driven super-prototype aircraft, the Lancer-01, a chip on her shoulder and a pervasive problem with authority. Her usual routine of fighting sky pirates for money soon gives way to an ongoing struggle that changes not only her world but, certain events permitting, lets Ash achieve an understanding of herself that most never reach.Jet Lancer's basic controls and combat are very similar to that of LUFTRAUSERS, otherwise a much more small-scale arcade survival title. But Jet Lancer's mechanics run deeper, its color palette more vibrant, its health system less forgiving, and most glaringly, it has relationship with its dodge mechanic that I can only describe as unhealthily dependent.Yes, Jet Lancer is one of those "dodge or die" games, to the point where one of the accessibility options allows you to adjust the evasion window, at no penalty to your progression. You can also make yourself flat-out invincible, set your primary machine gun, thrust or afterburner to a toggle instead of a hold, and also more mundane things like turning off screen shake or strobing effects. Jet Lancer is intensive enough to make my worn out milennial trigger-finger tired, and the ordinary evasion window is narrow enough that in the interest of preserving my enjoyment of the game, I eventually dialed that up before things started turning into a Bangai-O sequel in the altered New Game+ campaign.Step one for me to enjoy Jet Lancer was to ignore the ranking system and just focus on finishing levels. I failed step one and proceeded to not touch Jet Lancer for probably close to a year after it was gifted to me,  You don't stand much of a chance at a good rank without access to certain high-end weapons and passives that are only obtained by progressing through the campaign.So why am I recommending it? Well, aesthetically speaking Jet Lancer is really neat. It's got a bright color palette, an interesting blend of voxel and sprite graphics, a decent soundtrack, perhaps most importantly for me, good characters and writing. One reviewer described the plot as having been lifted straight from a 90s anime, which could be high praise or scathing deprecation depending on exactly what anime we're talking about. There's little I can say about it that wouldn't be a massive spoiler, but suffice it to say that in a manner very similar to CrossCode, Jet Lancer's combination of compelling narrative and accessibility options made me stick with it to its conclusion, looking past my issues with its gameplay.Jet Lancer is worth a look if you crave punishing arcade shooter action with screen-filling swarms of projectiles hounding your every move. If you don't, at the very least, you can make the game easier for you without impact to your progression.

_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: An unspoken masterpiece. Some of the most thrilling fun I’ve had in quite some time. The simple yet hard to master gameplay is incredibly satisfying with each enemy you drop and each dodge you nail giving you a rush that just keeps you glued to the screen. The tension is always high and the hectic gameplay always keeps you on your toes. When this is combined with the superb sound design and clear yet vibrant visuals, you start to see the majestic mayhem of metal that the game presents. The absolute banger of a soundtrack is downright phenomenal and can easily stand on its own. The story is nice and doesn't intrude on the gameplay. I adored the presentation and felt that it had that distinct “indie game” charm. I would recommend it with all my heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is everything I've wanted in a 2d shooter since playing Luftrausers. The latter was good, but limited in scale and almost felt like a proof of concept for something larger- Jet Lancer is absolutely "something larger". It really takes that core gameplay style and drives it home, with the weapon, enemy, and mission variety making it much more engaging. It's also very good about maintaining a vibrant and "alive" feeling with the backgrounds; you never feel like you're just in some dismal nothingness fighting an endless series of nobodies. Those regular changes in the scenery keep it from feeling fatiguing- I never had one of those moments of just staring into middle distance, dodging on reflex and sense of smell, that I get in a lot of less visually engaging titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome gameplay, music, effects, a simple but great story and a talking cat! There's plenty of customisation options and unlockable modules that let you play the way you want. Every part of this game reeks quality, exept that levels can feel copy-and-pasty later on. Absolutely give it a shot if you think you'll like it
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible Macross Itano Circus simulator!I absolutely love how chaotic and challenging the dogfights in this get, and the absolute satisfaction you can get from getting in the zone, blasting down planes while weaving through missiles in a trance. Fans of games like Doom Eternal, Hotline Miami, Luftrausers, etc will love getting good at the combat in this and becoming a god of the sky. Beyond the dogfights there are also some great boss fights against huge mecha. Game also has some great feedback with hit-stops/freezes and a revolutionary mechanic where you have a millisecond to dodge after a hit to negate it: very cool and satisfying!Only downsides I can think of is 1) the normal ending is a bit bleh and the good/true ending is locked behind a very difficult NG+ (it's worth it, but it's a lot of commitment and I wouldn't blame people for not realizing it's there in the first place), 2) most of the levels can get a bit repetitive as they usually devolve into just shooting a bunch of planes down over and over with minor differences (and the levels that do differ, like escort missions, can be annoying and down to luck), 3) story is decent but a bit too overly jokey/anime that makes the tone go all over the place.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great game and deserving of the title "hidden gem". I didn't really grow up playing flight shooters, and the few I did play I didn't particularly like. Despite this, when I saw the trailer for this game, it looked really interesting and so I decided to try it out. I am so glad I did because this is a really great game.In this game, you fly around shooting enemies in a limited arena until they die. While there are a variety of missions (e.g. reach a certain score, defeat waves of enemies, clear all enemies, etc…) most of them revolve around killing enemies as fast as possible. You instantly die if you hit the ground, and otherwise you die if you take 3 hits. Now, there are LOT of enemies and bullets in any given mission, so being able to only take 3 hits is a very small margin for error (you can also equip something that grants bonuses but makes it so that you can only take ONE hit before you die). However, the game is able to ask this of its players by giving players a dodge button. You can dodge pretty much any attack in this game using a dodge button that grants fairly generous invisibility frames. Furthermore, if you do get hit, if you press the dodge button in like less than 0.5 seconds afterwards, you won't take any damage. This means that as long as your reflexes are fast enough, you shouldn't take any damage. The game also does a decent job of being fair about this. If an enemy is off-screen, there will be an indicator as to where they are and roughly how far away they are. So you can roughly plan out when you need to dodge at any given time. By having a very generous dodge system in place, the game can be very fast-paced while still being very fair and fun. This is very similar to the game Ruiner where you can die very quickly, but quick execution on your part can allow you to come out on top. Similar to a lot of challenging games, Jet Lancer is fun even if you end up dying in a mission. This is because gratification in this game isn't limited to simply clearing a mission. Playing the game itself is so much fun, and getting better feels great. I particularly really started enjoying this game when I unlocked a module that replaces my roll dodging ability with a damaging dash ability. I had so much fun getting better at sniping enemies as they came anywhere close to me >:DExpertly dodging enemies is fun enough, but attacking them is even more fun! Not only do you have your standard minigun with infinite bullets, but you have 5 different special weapons and 5 different charge weapons you can use. The special weapons do a lot more damage than your regular weapon, and the charge weapons are kind of an "ultimate" ability. Both have relatively short cooldowns (especially the special weapons), so you're expected to use them often in a mission when the situations calls for it. For example, you might want to use your regular weapons for small jets, your special weapon for armored jets, and your ultimate for mini-boss like enemies. I love this type of precision as you're not just spamming your weapons constantly. You have to be careful when you use them, as 2 seconds without your special weapon can mean taking damage because you weren't able to kill an armored jet fast enough. Therefore, it feels rewarding whenever you get kills with your special and charge weapons, as you know you skillfully did it.Most action games simply have a defensive and offensive component to the gameplay, but what's cool about Jet Lancer is that even the movement is fun! Similar to Spider-Man (2018), moving in this game is simply fun to do (though not quite to the extent of Spider-Man :P). The movement is Jet Lancer is so much fun is because it requires an element of skill. You can't just easily go wherever you want because there's turning speed. So, for example, if an enemy is chasing you, it would be a bad idea to keep thrusting and turn around, as the enemy will simply follow you. However, you can stop thrusting and turn around and instantly take out the enemy. It also takes an element of skill to take out enemies close to the ground, as you're at a risk of crashing into the ground. Again, because of these challenges that movement brings, it feels rewarding when you finally master them and can do them without even thinking.So the game has great defensive, offensive, and movement elements in its gameplay. This wouldn't amount to much if the game didn't provide a sufficient challenge. Thankfully, it does through its excellent enemy and boss design. As I alluded to earlier, the enemies can basically be divided into 3 categories: basic jets, armored jets, and mini-bosses. Basic jets are more or less fodder and you simply need to learn their attacks so that you can properly dodge their attacks (within one that shoots 1 bullet, another that shoots 3 bullets, and another that explodes into bullets after dying). Armored jets are more interesting as they often have some type of move that requires you to kill them fast or risk taking damage. For example, there's one that will lock onto your position and rush at you, one that will lock onto your position and shoot very accurate bullets, one that shoot homing missiles, one that snipes at you from far away, and one that constantly chases you shooting fairly accurate bullets. Finally, there's the mini-bosses (around 5 of them. 2 ships, 2 tanks, and 1 floating mech) which often cover the sky with bullets and/or homing rockets and should therefore be prioritized whenever possible. Taking on any one enemy might be easy enough, but the challenge comes in fighting multiple enemies all at once, as you're quite often fighting like 5 or more enemies at any one time. This game is not simply a matter of kiting your enemies as much as you can. You need to learn to attack and dodge all the various enemies as efficiently as you can, and quite often you will fail as mission as you're learning to do this. But once you do and you clear a mission, the feeling of achievement is great :DThe bosses are another highlight of this game. They're all very unique both in terms of looks and in terms of mechanics. You need to learn when to attack and when to defend, and it's not all that easy because the bosses wait like a second between attacks (which is not enough time to get any significant damage in). You want to be able to learn which attacks you can dodge while attacking, and which attacks you want to put your full attention to dodging. One thing I'll add is that the game has a great difficulty curve. I was struggling in the beginning, found a decent challenge later, thought the game was too easy later on, and finally found a decent challenge at the end (i.e. the last few bosses are a treat to fight :D).In regards to negatives, there's just a few:	• Progression system: The progression system is fairly limited. You can equip up to 4 different modules, which are basically passive abilities. The problem is that you'll likely find at least 2 abilities that you really like (for me, it was the dash and autoroll) and so that gives you like 2 other abilities to really play around with. I.e. the progression system could be more in depth because as it stands, you'll very quickly stop caring about the modules you get.	• Game should be zoomed out more: While the game is mostly fair in how much warning it gives you in regards to enemies so that you can plan your dodges, it should probably be zoomed out more. This is because the indicator of where an enemy is works to plan your dodge when the enemy is flying away from you / up or down. However, when the plane is flying directly at you and you're flying directly toward them, you'll like face an attack much faster than you can react to. To be fair, there are very few instances where an enemy flies directly toward you from offscreen.Apart from some small negatives, Jet Lancer was an absolute blast to play. I am so glad that I finally tried it.

_childDocuments_.review: SUCH A BLAST!Pleasant (imo) and very readable artstyle, fun and coherent player tools, challenging dodge mechanic, progressively difficult missions, quite extensive aircraft modification combinations..This game could be compared to Luftrausers. _childDocuments_.review: No more precise way to descrive Jet lancer than anime as ♥♥♥♥. The music is probably the first thing that you’re gonna notice and it’s amazing. In battles it’s dynamic fast and suits the whole undefeatable ace feel perfectly. And on the map and in cutscenes it takes on a contrasting sort of relaxing elevator style. Simply put, it rocks. Reminds me a bit of ZeroRanger’s music, another anime-fighter pilot game of a slightly different genre.Artstyle is gorgeous and unobstructive at the same time. Everything looks juicy and sufficiently explosive without disrupting the gameplay. Enemy aircrafts can be a bit hard to distinguish, but these unclear types mostly fight the same way, just have more health. You probably won’t be looking at them much, but backgrounds are just as good as the action. They represent 3D overworld map locations in a more scenic way with changing time of day and a nice sense of scale.The story is okay, it’s good for what it is. Has some simple twists here and there. Don’t expect to find some sort of narrative revelation here, it’s a game about jet fights and giant mechs.The gameplay might be familiar if you know Luftrausers. You have a jet, a bunch of weapons and you have to either destroy everything on the screen or complete some objective from level to level. I noticed some sudden difficulty spikes on certain levels, but everything is still beatable and the game has a lot of customization that can make it easier(or harder). Just beating levels is good, but your style is also rated. That’s the main incentive to replay them, and it WILL feel good, when you get that perfect score.Speaking of style, you yourself can perform some awesome tricks with the controls given. They work, may take some time to get used to. You’re controlling a jet, so everything depends on thrusting and turning around. I found it a bit hard to dodge sometimes, as if the button doesn’t respond, but perhaps it’s an issue of reaction time or my controller.It’s always a pleasure to launch this game to play or replay a few levels, or even to just hear the music. It’s got an arcade mode too, with a bunch of unique mechanics and pilots.

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly what a shooter game should be—Fluid but weighty action, creative & pretty designs, bright & clear & spacious visuals (especially important for a game about flight), pleasant & exciting music, *seriously crunchy* FX, some earnest focus on story as more than an afterthought with some likable little characters and dialog (obviously it's rather elementary, but it's absolutely vital that a game put some genuine emotional energy into making you believe in & care about what's happening and to whom, and that's dishearteningly rare among arcade action games), and as a treat some direct homages to some of the shooter titans of yore like "Strike Gunner" on the SNES (as if the sleek pink fighter jet wasn't a giveaway).  This game just makes you *feel good* playing it:  Despite seeming to take place in a post-collapse interregnum overrun with deadly sky pirates, the saturated color palate, wide open spaces, brilliant crystal blue skies and seas, retro anime sleekness, and breezy score make it feel like a world that's much brighter and happier than our own, and it's a pleasure to visit, like a little summer getaway that just happens to involve massive air battles.  In between the missions you even putter around a cheerful cartoon archipelago however you please in a cute little hovercarrier—It literally feels like a breath of fresh sea air blowing away the accumulated gray-brown grit from so many other action games.I think it can be summed up perfectly as "exactly halfway between 'Donut County' and 'Ace Combat,'" and if that experience sounds appealing to you, then definitely don't miss out on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: No disrespect to Vlambeer, but Jet Lancers is like if someone saw Luftrausers, and thought "what if this... but BETTER??"To qualify that statement, Luftrausers is a great game. It's a wonderful, frenetic, stylish shootemup with big screen-rattling, juicy explosions, which if you know much about Vlambeer, is pretty much par for the course with them. It plays great, it's good fun, and it FEELS great, but it is absolutely missing something special beyond being a great game for a quick blast now and then.Jet Lancer has a VERY similar style in terms of gameplay; the ability to cut your engines and just let momentum do the work while you turn to fire at something behind you, kickback from the weapon (though not enough to actually fly purely by firing your gun by default, and even then certainly not fly WELL), big super weaponry, huge explosions, high speed aerial acrobatics and all that.What it has IN ADDITION to this however are;1: More upgrades for your sweet as hell looking plane2: an ACTUAL STORY3: your pilot has a helmet with cat ears :D4: CHARACTERS, WITH MOTIVATIONS AND BACKSTORY5: BLAZING FAST 16-BIT COLOUR GRAPHICS MADE POSSIBLE BY BLAST PROC-okay yeah no, it's got pretty colours and vibrant backgrounds and parallax scrolling as opposed to Luftrauser's monochrome, pseudo 1-bit old-timey style, which, credit where credit's do, is absolutely memorable, but it's nice to look at something varied y'know? Especially if you're playing more than a couple minutes here and there.6: A MAP SCREEN with lovely, low-poly 3d-graphics that remind me slightly of Megaman Legends and boy howdy do i love megaman legends.7: A talking cat for an engineer :D8: did i mention BIG FRIGGIN SUPER WEAPONS AND GIANT ROBOTS TO FIGHT AND BLOW APART PIECE BY PIECE!? NO!? WELL IT'S GOT BIG FRIGGIN SUPER WEAPONS AND GIANT ROBOTS TO FIGHT AND BLOW APART PIECE BY PIECE!!9: Sky pirates! Government forces! Conspiracy! A hovercraft aircraft carrier! a GIGANTIC SUBMERSIBLE AIRCRAFT CARRIER! LASERS!! MISSILES!!! EXPLOSIONS!!!! OH MY!!!!!10: also some sweet as hell music that is exceptionally listenable to, which definitely is an area Luftrausers falls down on sad to say.11: accessability options because not everybody is willing or able to "git gud" and we really have ENOUGH issues to worry about in the world without gatekeeping who is a real "gamer(tm)" for needing a little help now and then or not* 12: the ability to redo missions to get higher rankings on. I have no idea what if anything happens if you Ace all the missions, but hey you get a nice shiny gold badge for each mission when you do Ace them!Downsides? I suppose if I had to name one, it's that it doesn't fully capture the mouse during at least non-gameplay sections, and I have a feeling it might cause me to accidentally click off the screen if I'm not careful at some point....also it can sometimes be a little difficult to see where you're meant to go next on the map screen. I mean, yeah, there's a compass point, but it can get hidden behind the cardinal direction markers, aaaaand honestly I just end up looking for the pillar of light and going that way as much as possible most of the time...Finally, if you do use the quick navigation menu to skip back to an earlier stage, then want to go back to the stage you were on, you... gotta drive there. :| It only shows missions you've done in that menu, not ones you NEED to do.These three points are all super minor nitpicks though and honestly, I fully recommend this game. I've been waiting eagerly for this to come out for a while and now that I have it, it was absolutely worth the wait.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Remember those 2d plane pew pew flash games? Well this is that but 2020. Better graphics, better gameplay, an actual story (tho nothing huge here), pretty good music, theres a nice blend between 2d pixel art and nintendo-ish 3d (at times)Some missions can be a little bit tedious, i personally struggled A LOT on 37... literally the only mission i HAD to activate god mode otherwise i could not beat it.Finally the most important part: ARCADE MODE. This is an endless mode and where most of the games value comes from imo. The fact that it doesnt simply end with the story (which already takes a while to complete) is great news and something that we dont always get to see from indie games. I can see myself coming back to the game to chill in arcade mode as ive always wanted to have a game like this in steamOverall a pretty solid game, definetly worth to buy
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: CPU : AMD A8-3800 @2.40GhzGPU : (Inherited) AMD ATI RADEON 6550D 512MB VRAMRAM : 4GB @933MhzController : Keyboard and MouseAverage Frame Rate (AFR) : 30-60 (Normal, both in battle or overworld)Let's make some points before entering the main part of the review, this game is short in Campaing Subject (History Mode) but in fact a good Campaign, the characters are lovely (Mainly Lem) and their Portraits are amazing too, fitting very well with them, the missions and bosses are frenetic and i risk myself to say some are even harder than i expected,.From someone that didn't even got through the 3/4 mission of Sine Mora (another great game, not from the same devs tho) this game is easier than SM, but still a challenge, even the the clunky FR (Frame Rate) caused by my hardware the game was a walk in the park...... A fly in the park? the Ace Module helped a lot on mastering the game (100%), but i don't recommend it on first run.Talking about variety, the game has a set of modules to install on the jet, some of them have their own objective on some mission or even on Campaign Routes (Bad and True Ending), but out of campaign, there's the Arcade Mode, there you see some mods that haven't appeared on the Campaign and this is a nice addition for the mode.For the time i played (20.6h) with some pauses, the game was a great thing to distract me from the world, the Arcade Mode got me with the characters to be unlocked.... (Lem still gives me the creeps tho) and the Achievments were a great challenge, but not impossible, the community got some guides for helping you, the game even support mods (Not heavy modding but still modding).The graphics, this game get some highlights on this part, with some notable effects like Lens Flares and Chromatic Aberration on the right touch, the animations are smooth and easy to read, the 3D part brights as well, the Plane and some other elements on the Map are amazing and well texturized, the Map itself is well translate for the in-battle game section, like the Desert that has some background where there's some kind of Tower at the distance and the City with some kind of Buildings at the foreground.This game is one hell of Master Piece, it has the best mix of 2D/3D i know until now (if i get to know any other i may update this topic), It's a mix of Afterburner, Evangelion... (ok, that giant bot needs to be a reference) and Sine Mora (with less difficulty), i haven't noticed one Glitch/Bug from the start to end (Aside of a keyboard bug that i had but i don't know it's my house eletricity system lacking ground wiring or was some malfuction in the cables, but the game was still at its normal), the game even have some configs to help people with Visual Issues (Like epilepsia and derivatives), this is perfection, if you're looking for a short game about shooting planes and destroying giante machines, well, this one is for you.Thanks for reading and i hope you enjoy the game.Edit: This review has been updated due some typos and other Aesthetic things (like Formatting and Listing).

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game with a massive caveat: later missions become infuriating due to the nature of the gameplay, AI and weapons systems. You're limited to certain loadouts if you want to reach a target score within the time limit, and the AI does everything it can to make it harder for you, but NOT by engaging you. Instead, they will run away, hang out offscreen or fly in circles for no reason. Eventually that same loadout even becomes more difficult to use because enemies can turn your weapons back on you. The fun factor starts to really slip at this point, and I don't know if I'm going to wind up finishing the game. Certain stages become extremely repetitive, and since the gameplay itself isn't that varied, the frustration mounts very quickly. I've gotten my money's worth ($9.89 on sale) but there's a lot about the game that needs work, especially regarding the presentation (why even have an overworld if it's going to be so comically ugly and barren of detail?). The gameplay is a lot of fun, the characters and story are decent but nothing special, the sound design is as good as it needs to be -- if you enjoy this sort of game, you'll probably get something out of Jet Lancer.

_childDocuments_.review: GOTY hands down for me and if Steam would allow me "Best Sound Track" as well. So i caught wind of this from the folks that played Luftrausers calling it its "spiritual successor" and... yeah it is and then someThe game starts out very easy with a lot of mods that put the jet into "binky" mode, mods that keep you from dying too much, but plenty of room to upgrade and change so you can fine tune it to your play style (dummy rockets are the best). The missions are all about killing the things, but the missions vary on objective making it so its not exactly the same every time, sometimes even forcing you to make changes to your jet to better complete the missions. Theres also a nice variety of enemies who all fly slightly different from each other with new attacks so its not the same mindless scrub firing away at you. You always can go back to those missions and retry them as well to get that sweet sweet ACE score. The dodge comes in key to this and is probably my favorite feature in the game. When you dodge you get a bonus to your combo and also faster firing for your gun. At first you'll use it to get out of taking a hit, but when you get more experience you'll be throwing yourself at the enemy looking to get that dodge in. And if you walk out from it thinking you got some moxxi on you then there always "New Game +" to take a chomp atThe art and world in the game very pretty to look at. The backgrounds are vivid and colorful, whether they be in the city, ocean, countryside or desert. The explosions of your foes is also enjoyable as you a satisfying explosion to confirm that, yes, he is for sure dead. The music is top tier in this friking thing! If you like Anamanaguchi or Slime Girl, you'll love the soundtrack to this game. If you have no clue what i'm talking about its essentially a mix of chirp tunes and rock.
