_childDocuments_.review: I meant to review this game sooner, so my apologies for that.This game is honestly great. If you're looking to just complete the game, this game won't run you long, even with New Game+  being required to do to get the good ending. However if you want to go that extra mile and try to ACE all missions, I say that's well worth the time too.If you've played LUFTRAUSERS, you know partially what you're getting into. You are jet. Jet does the shoot at enemies while at the same time controlling the direction you fly in while thrusting. Proper management of stopping your thrusters to shoot people behind you is a common thing. Unlike LUFTRAUSERS however, this game has a few different aspects to it. This is a more story-based game where there are upgrades that you unlock by playing. You aren't affected by gravity while thrusting, and you don't heal by not shooting. This works better for the mission-based story, so it's not a bad thing by any means. You also get a nice dodge roll move where you gain a brief invincibility to avoid any damage. If you successfully avoided taking damage with said roll, you get a score multiplier and a brief increase to your fire rate. Really there's nothing further to say on the matter. There's bosses to fight, missions to do, upgrades to get, scores to perfect, and even an arcade mode if you wish to keep playing after getting ACE on every mission in both NG and NG+ like I have. While I will find myself going to LUFTRAUSERS more for that arcadey experience, I still love the mechanics to this game enough where I'll happily play the arcade mode on this too.The asking price is worth the price of admission, but waiting for a sale if you're unsure won't do you any further damage either. It's a very fun game and definitely deserves more notoriety. Definitely give this game a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: i'm terrible at this game and i absolutely adore it. everything is pitch-perfect, from the aesthetics to the music to the smug interactions. my only gripes are difficulty spikes and a few repetitive objectives, but the game overall more than makes up for those. support the soundtrack over on fat bard's bandcamp! it's one of my most-played albums of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic small-scale game, deeper than a typical arcade shooter and feels mechanically satisfying enough that I want to jump in for a round every once in a while. Looks and sounds great. Lots of accessibility & difficulty options if you just want to get through the main campaign. Definitely worth the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Very tight and fast-paced gameplay. It feels like Luftrausers mixed with a white-knuckled arcade racing game like burnout. The story gets more interesting towards the end, but honestly feels like the weakest part with mostly uninteresting dialogue, and the characters are a little too cookie-cutter (bad guys being overly evil or annoying, side characters being incessantly abrasive with few positive qualities). The lore is interesting, and the alternate ending pathways have some really interesting revelations, however. But the recently added story-free Arcade Mode add a lot of lifespan to this game. I have had so much fun playing it, and would highly recommend. Also, please note that there are alternate endings to be had with the New Game Plus. The art style is fantastic, with lots of bright colors, complimenting the anime-esque opening quite nicely. The overworld is 3D, and reminds me of PS1 era games like Megaman Legends. I wish this part was a little bit more fleshed out, and that there was more to do in the overworld other than drive to the next mission.All in all, it is a fantastic game that doesn't take itself too seriously, but has seriously good and tight gameplay. Would recommend if you want a good intense arcade game that you can pick up and play for short bursts of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: The controls in this game feel fantastic. It's a great flow state game where you can just zone into it and pull off great feeling maneuvers. The scoring system is fair with how you'll feel about finishing a level, so if you pull of an S+ rank, you'll feel like you did an S+ job.It looks great as well. It's solid 2.5d with a consistent pixel art throughout. One thing I don't like is they overuse this effect where the screen goes black and white and silent when some big attack is happening. You can tell the artist thought "this is cool, so I should do it more" but what's going on doesn't read very well and it happens too often to have a lot of impact. It lasts too long, happens to often, and breaks your flow.The difficulty pacing is all over the place. Expect some levels to take a long time with many attempts and then the level immediately following it to be a breeze. An early boss took about 20 attempts, while the boss following it was an easy first try. It's worth sticking with though and nothing every gets too unfair. Plus, going back and doing levels with different builds or for higher scores makes all the levels interesting.The builds are also well thought out. None of the modifiers to your plane really make it strictly "better" and in fact often make the game harder. But the ones that make the game harder almost always feel more rewarding when you pull them off. Pulling off big hits with unguided weapons really puts you in that feeling of pulling off the perfect bombing run. You're constantly managing your cooldowns and the speed of your approach to make sure to optimize your impact. In that sense, the game is precisely turned with the high of doing a perfect sequence of shots with now switching to dodging while you wait for your cooldowns and position for another approach.The arcade mode is also a really good time and does a rouge like version of the game. I'm not sure why they lock it so deep in the story though. I think it's not to spoil the bosses but it does end up cutting off a mode where you can just play the game for getting in a good score building flow and not worrying about the story.Overall, highly recommend. It's a thrilling, well put together piece of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Highly Highly Recommended! Once you get a feel for the controls and your plane, you'll be wasting enemies and feel like a true badass pilot. The story is quite good and kept me invested in finishing story mode. The music is really good, worth seeking out the OST.The comparison to luftrausers is obvious, but this game has an entirely different feel to it. Hitting a plane with an unguided rocket, dodge-rolling through an entire volley of missiles while doing a 180-spin then roasting another plane with your afterburner before blowing another plane away with the amped primary gun is a wonderful feeling.There's barely any handholding at all in this game, you can take the training wheels off right after meeting Lem, pretty early in the story. The game never stops you from going as balls-to-the-wall as you want, it actively encourages you to do so; dodge rolling through projectiles gives you a fire-rate buff so you want to stay near the action, and once you unlock the blink/dash upgrade you can kill things with your "dodge".Oh, and you can fight giant robots, I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. I beat the campaign in just over three hours, but there is NG+ afterwards, which revamps the number and types of enemies for every level as well as adding in some new enemy attacks. Every minute of the three hours I've spent playing have been enjoyable, and it didn't take too long to get a hang of the controls (I now feel like a legend pulling of ludicrous maneuvers whenever I please). Overall, really awesome game, and I can't wait to get wrecked on NG+, which I've found to be considerably more difficult than the regular game after playing through a few missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly high octane game with awesome visuals and soundtrack. The gameplay is extremely reactive, getting better at it feels unbelievably rewarding. There is a reasonable variance in enemies and mission types that keeps the game fresh.My only complain is that some bosses forces you to not move too much which makes the gameplay stall a bit and feel counter-intuitive to the rest of the high pace of the game. (Looking at you, walking armory)Overall for the price this is a must play if you enjoy action packed games.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game.  It feels like the Crazy Taxi of shooters in a sense; it's more arcade-like, great music, bright, fun, yet also very skill-based (like Crazy Taxi).  Don't get me wrong, some of the missions are incredibly frustrating but they always feel doable... in fact, I really appreciated that I had to change my loadout and playstyle in many missions.  If you do feel like the challenge is too high, there are options available for making the game more forgivable (I HIGHLY recommend setting the dodge mechanic window to HIGH). This game is very addicting and really scratched that arcade, level-based itch that many mainstream rougelites and story based games lack.  The action is intense, frantic, and FUN.  If you are watching videos and think this game looks cool, I would say take the leap and check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely incredible so far (2 hours of play time). The soundtrack is phenomenal and the gameplay is extremely tight with a very high skill cap. Easy to learn, but hard to master. With how often the game throws new upgrades for your ship at you, you can try out multiple different set ups that synergize with the other parts and create a unique playstyle with each part. The action is non stop and incredibly fast paced, to the point where, to take a specific mission into this example, your dog-fighting 15 jets all the while dodging missiles being thrown at you from half the map away while still trying not to fire your weapons to much to keep a laser tank 50 miles away from being able to lock onto you and clap your cheeks. I can't really describe how amazing this game is in words alone, you really just have to play it. I hope the developers continue to create more amazing games like this one in the future, and I'm surprised to see that this game hasn't gotten more attention yet. Oh, and the story seems pretty good so far as well. A bit on the simpler side but it doesn't seem to be the main focus. If you have the 15 bucks to spare, then please check this game out. I'm sure you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: its a type of bullet hell i never knew i needed, the game is forgiving without removing the challenge, and while attempting to ace missions has me coming back for more, i do hope some sort of leaderboard is built around the game, to give it the longevity of other bullet hell type games, but as it is its a wonderful game well worth the price

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing bullet hells and shoot'em ups for most of my life I am 29 for reference and I have to say this game is easily in my top 3 of all time! _childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having trouble finding a game that sucked me in. The music and art style of Jet Lancer was really cool, the story was interesting and kept me waiting for more between contracts. The plot took turns I didn't expect and the game play can be set to your style by customizing your jet and changing difficulty. _childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is what would happen if Platinum Games looked at Luftrausers and went "let's do that our way". The controls are excellent and there's a surprising amount of maneuvering tech, including but not limited to perfect dodges, DMC-style stingers and an exhaust dropkick you can trigger by rotating your plane 180° and hammering the afterburners. You know, so that you can cut enemy planes in half with your jet's exhaust flame. So, along with character action levels of combat depth (for an arcade flight game, at least), it's only right that campaign missions come with a style ranking based on time between kills, weapons used (the less guided, the better), time to complete the mission and damage taken during it, with a no-damage run being the only way to get an ACE rank. Because yeah, this game has an actual campaign with like, missions and bosses. It's not just "endless mode until the ♥♥♥♥ you blimp we made to make you stop playing comes". The artstyle is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing, leaning hard into Megaman Legends-style shading for the 3d models and gorgeous spritework for vehicles and backgrounds. There's also character art, since the actual campaign has some ok characters, and it's...clearly not the focus. It's serviceable, but not the artist's specialty and i get that. In terms of music on the other hand, it's not exactly what i was expecting: basically, math rock. Chiptunes in the background, raging guitars as the main instrument. In-game, it does the thing where the better you play the harder the music goes, but that *has* made some people think the music was *just* the background chiptunes for some reason. Wonder why. Discussing the writing last because, all and all, it's kinda just a set of reasons for you to do sick flips in my favourite depiction of the SU-41 berkut in media. Although i gotta say...it actually goes somewhere. If you've been around the shmups block you can see the final twist coming, but i don't mind. They didn't need to put it in there, but they did and it was sick. Overall, a great shmup that I should definitely get back to soon, as they added an endless arcade mode a while back. And no, by endless i don't mean the Luftrausers kinda endless: encounters can be "beaten", there's just an infinite amount of them that get harder and harder. You get to pick an equally infinite amount of powerups inbetween stages though, making some of the crazier encounter later on (such as multiple bosses per battle) actually manageable.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: This a great game with an enjoyable story.  My biggest gripe is that there are some unexplained mechanics and the entire experience feels a bit railroaded if you want to "ACE" every mission, but that's how the developer wanted to design his game.Generally it just takes one bad experience for me to put down a game and not revisit it.  This game delivers!  Super fun, but pretty tense and stressful.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: While I still didn't played the game entirely, I've to say that it's been a while that I didn't have this much fun with a shooter title!The music is fantastic, the artwork and graphics are awesome and the controls are very responsive. On the controls side you may need some fine tuning on the configuration or more time getting to it on the default settings, but when you got used to it and create your own loadout, boy... this game becomes very intense!Aside from some clarity on how the score rating mechanic works, I think this game has a good story (so far) with a great sense of humor and a nice amount of challenge.Awesome job, devs! I hope that you guys keep with the support on this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10Though it is very similar to Luftrausers on the surface level, it is definitely more than just a clone of that game. The gameplay is uniquely high-paced, and the controls make it a smooth experience. It has a good upgrade system, where different modules change gameplay, but don't outclass each other. It also has individual missions, with different goals to complete on each one. This makes gameplay varied and keeps it interesting.The story and characters are interesting enough on their own, and having it mixed in with the stellar gameplay is just perfect for me. The OST is one of the best I've heard in a while, and I won't be forgetting it anytime soon. My only real gripe with this game was its short length, but the individual missions themselves have enough replay value to stay fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: The devs pretty much had the same thoughts as I did after playing Luftrausers, then they went beyond them and made a really good game.  PROS: Responsive controls, fun colourful environments, just enough plot to tie things together, fun unlocks and abilities, and well tuned gameplay. There's a variety of modules and options to customize your difficulty and assist levels. The Soundtrack is consistently very, very good. It also has an adorable cat.CONS: A few accessabilty options are poorly labeled (Screen Flash option does not disable all screen flashes, only strobes, forex, leaving some photosensitve triggers in game), even after changes mission 15 is a bit of an unusual difficulty spike - it's gone from almost nonsense to just noticeably harder.Overall, an extremely solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Just fun. The Luftrauser's comparison is obvious but it's a bit more than just a clone of that, with various subtle differences that do add up to make it feel like it's own game. Especially with a mission structure that manages to be unobtrusive yet offer a lot of content with a decent chunk of variety. Also, anime as ♥♥♥♥ in all the right ways.Just make sure your keyboard doesn't suck. Low key rollover can make the game way less playable.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Game's a lot of fun. Graphics are nice and clean, the effects are super stylish (I first found out about this game because of a twitter video showing off one of the big boss explosions), music is great.  I'm not very good at the game but I'm having a blast.  Hopefully this game gets the attention it deserves.My only two comments would be that turning feels really sluggish (maybe I get an upgrade later that will fix this though, idk) and the dodge is op. It has too many iframes and basically no cooldown which means I can spam the hell out of it and survive a lot of stuff without actually trying
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is to me a pleasant surprise of a game I opted to buy blindly. It's a fast paced highly engaging and addicting game that often leaves you wanting for more after each successful mission you tackle, until inevitably you don't notice how much time has passed. The game accomplishes this by its difficulty of being challenging but fair, missions never really feel overwhelming but they always feel demanding enough for you to keep upping your game and improving. This challenge plays off well with another strength of the game, namely the freshness with each mission as there is a lot of variety to them, and in addition are spaced out enough to keep variety flowing. Add this with the wide range of customization options that you unlock as you play and you quickly find yourself absorbed into the game as you're invited to put these new tools to use to enhance your gameplay experience, and in turn the rank you achieve. The game is very hard to put down as you can imagine at this point as it has so much elements going for it as the game just keeps on giving inviting you to keep going just one more mission till inevitably you finish your first playthrough and proceed with the next, that while familiar still feels different with the surprises that the game continues to offer in newgame +. The game continues to be engaging from one mission to the next, from one playthrough to another its startling how much this game has to offer, especially coming for such a humble price. Definitely one of the best games I've played for the year and I do hope other discover this wonderful gem.*Just a caveat this review is done on a day one release, no patches or any potential future changes. I more or less finished the game twice in just a day more or less, with just a few hours rest. So this review reflects my experience from a day one release and patch. What is impressive here that I didn't note above is how my experience was entirely bug free, the polish of this game is something to take note of.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely. Any time that I find one of these games that make you feel like a god, I have to say something. This game is fun, it's hard, and it's intensely immersive. Once you figure out the crazy stunts you can pull, the game opens up a new chapter in fun.That amount of fun and tension though has me only playing it in short, hyperactive spurts though. But my lack of playtime does not dissuade my +. Get it. There's so much game here for 14.99. :D
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who loves shooters this is a fantastic game, Normal play is pretty fun but the game really takes off in NG+ mode. Having the evade action be super OP means that the game really has to overwhelm your senses so that you'll finally make a mistake. This lends itself to a very frenetic game-play experience.

_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Damn good game on all fronts.Luftrausers but with color and a badass jet! The story is pretty cool overall. _childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that has never played many flight combat games, this one sold me right away from the gameplay trailers alone, and the actual game meets those expectations. Tight controls, a great 3D/2D cartoon style, and a good variety of weapons and upgrades to keep the game from getting repetitive. It feels so satisfying zipping around and destroying enemies, especially in the second half of the game when you get the really good upgrades. It also has good replay value, which is good since the game can be beaten in about 6-7 hours if you know what you're doing.If you're looking for a good arcade-style flight action game to play at a good price, I'd recommend Jet Lancer.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: The closest gameplay comparison would likely be Luftrausers, but it runs circles around Luftrausers. The whole package is phenomenal: gameplay, art, soundtrack -- everything. _childDocuments_.review: The art is fantastic, the soundtrack is great and the controls are satisfying. This game is really fun and, while the levels can feel a bit like boxes full of enemies, the combat feels exciting enough and the enemies have a suprising amount of variety, especially the bosses. Did i mention that this game looks so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good.
_childDocuments_.name: Jet Lancer

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is your classic dogfight game with a moderate amount of customizable options at your disposal, tight controls, hours of missions, and a BUMPPIN' soundtrack. The opening sequence for the game is immersive, immediately throwing you into a narrative you've yet to discover, but when the title music starts playing, it throws you into the clouds and makes you feel like your truly flying. Tight Controls: If you haven't played a 2D dogfight simulator before, you'll come to soon realize how amazingly tight the controls are. You can zoom across the battlefield, cut the engines, fall while firing at a plane chasing you, then blast the afterburners into a dodge roll, narrowly skim the waters, and spin back into the air dodging bullets left and right. Dodging is satisfying. The Explosions are satisfying. The narrow escapes and rapid counterattacks are so, flippin', satisfying.Soundtrack: The music is spot on for this game. The main vibe is chiptune, synchronizing with the pixelated visuals. But then, there's a vibing guitar riff overlay that puts you in the middle of the action. Just check out the soundtrack if you're not interested in buying the game. Fat Bard is an underrated music master!

_childDocuments_.review: Jet Lancer is a high-velocity aerial combat shooter where you duel enemy aviators, hunt giant robots, and defy death at supersonic speeds. You are Ash Leguinn: badass pilot, highly paid mercenary, and flight-school drop out. Your day job is fine - the daily grind of dealing with Sky Pirates pays the bills - but nothing compares to the rush of demolishing a ninety-ton mechanical monstrosity at the speed of sound. And you’ll have your chance. As mechanized weapons converge on Root City, you’ll have to be at the top of your game to survive, and you’ll have to surpass your limits if you want to save the world.

name: WORLD OF HORROR
detailed_description: The Old Gods are reawakening, clawing their way back into a world that’s spiraling into madness. In hospitals, abandoned classrooms, quiet apartments, and dark forests, strange appearances and unexplainable phenomena test the sanity of residents in Shiokawa, Japan. Is it chaotic retribution, or the machinations of beings beyond our comprehension? This is WORLD OF HORROR: The end of the world is nigh, and the only solution is to confront the terror reigning over the apocalypse. Navigate this hellish, roguelite reality through turn-based combat and unforgiving choices in this roguelite-style cosmic horror RPG. Invoke dark rituals, uncover disturbing clues, and solve puzzles across multiple randomized mysteries. Each perplexing case unravels into a series of random encounters with nightmarish figures inspired by the works of horror legends Junji Ito and H.P. Lovecraft. Unveil the fates of 14 unique playable characters, and choose your path through a pool of 20 dreadful investigations. Most mysteries harbor multiple endings - for those that survive long enough. A haunting chiptune soundtrack accentuates the game’s stark 1-bit art style, drawn 100% in MS Paint.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is almost great, mostly because the aesthetic is so incredibly creepy. The interactivity of the different items you can get also seems interesting.The rest of the game needs work. Gameplay is rather repetitive and doesn't require much attention or problem solving. I felt like I was mostly clicking "next" through the stories, while worrying about resource management. Once you figure out how things work, repeating the same resource mgmt problem isn't that fun. The game is very action constrained too, so it's hard to find much satisfaction in leveling up skills, collecting odd items, etc. because it all gets wiped in after an ~hour's worth of actions anyway, after which you have to repeat. Most of the alternate endings don't differ by much more than a different epilogue text, or maybe an item. There are couple cool interactive surprises, and think there ought to be more! Also, the finale was fairly unsatisfying to me.I think perhaps the biggest negative is that it's missing a key feature every horror game should have: jump scares that require a real time reaction. In this game whenever something jumps out at you, you have all the time in the world to react, which makes it a lot less scary to take any action. The lack of immediacy, lowers the stakes greatly. It's an amazing basis, and I think with some improvements it could become a masterpiece. Afaik it's all the work of a random dentist in poland. Right now, it shows; the game feels quite constrained. Maybe with some of the money he's earning he can focus more on development.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute delight for anyone who appreciates asian horror and investigation games. The aesthetics are amazing, the music is moody in an old, chiptuney way that adds a lot to the atmosphere, the characters are all pretty interesting and distinct from one another and the mechanics are generally pretty well done. It is a difficult game, mind you, and dying, going insane or being doomed are common endings for any given playthrough. But I did not feel it was unfair. The mechanics are clear and once you understand them you can plan ahead and make even high difficulty runs succeed reliably. Also, I really liked how the achievements incentivize the player to test different characters and explore. Which is a must because all the mysteries have multiple conclusions, ranging from good, to bad to cosmically horrible. The mysteries themselves are all pretty good and touch upon many classic japanese horror elements and tropes, mixed with Junji Ito's body and existential horror and a sprinkle of lovecraftian cosmic horror. The investigations mostly follow a similar pattern, where you search for clues by exploring different locations in town, which in turn progresses the story and raises your doom meter a little (if the doom meter ever reaches 100% it's game over). You also have the option of doing a side quest related to the case, which generally opens the possibility of a good/better ending. There are a few outliers, like "Spine-Chilling Story of School Scissors", which work a bit differently but, imo, have their own charm and help change the pace a bit.Last, but not least, you can boop the store dog's nose. 11/10 would sacrifice my friends to appease cosmic horrors again.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Very fun emergent storytelling, with some Betrayal at the House on the Hill (great board game) and Eldritch Horror (also a great board game) elements.Cons: Hallmarks of early Access (glitches/bugs, confusing text, balance issues, could use more events as of Feb 27th 2020).I 100% recommend the game, but there are two things I would definitely change. -Getting the two anti-heal god effects (where you can't bathe and also rest for less during investigations) makes the game a sure grind down to death, unless you get specific adventures. With the doom penalty for resting, it feels like on Normal difficulty it should be either/or. -Mysteries that take you out of the regular loop of the game (The tutorial school adventure, the festival, the wake, etc) need to make it more clear that you'll be unable to do regular around-town events. It's ok that they do it, as it makes planning the order of your mysteries necessary, but getting suctioned into a scenario where you die because you chose the wrong mystery doesn't enhance the dread, it just feels bad. A tooltip or an asterisk would fix it entirely.These suggestions aside, this game is awesome, and I can't wait for more! Assuredly one of the most promising early access games I've seen on steam.

_childDocuments_.review: As a mystery solving teenager in 1984 Japan (not 198x, the game's intro lied to me), I must solve mysteries to stop the coming of an eldritch horror. No I won't simply get something that could help me break down the door to the light house.+ Everything is randomized, from the mysteries I do to what events I could get in various places, such as a pickpocket in the crowd of a city, in the middle of the woods for some reason+ Two different timelines. All it does is change up the endings but at the very least, it does give me some boss battles and in one case, a different way of finishing a mystery+ Various characters to play as, with various histories. Makes the game a bit more fresh in how you can play around with the character you have, whether it's a 25 year old burglar who got held back alot in school or an 18 year old idol who has no fear in fighting a lovecraft knockoff using a katana weebs dream of using.- Events can be a pain, especially when they work against you- Sometimes a run will go south and you'll have either lose or restart- Clapping and bowing can be easier in beating a ghost enemy if you get it down right but in my case, I just go with severing the link.- Some characters and a history require a bit of luck, more so with unlocking one character.Overall, I had fun subjecting myself to lovecraftian horrors as I killed off spooky ghost in a manor using nothing but a steak knife.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl:dr} World of Horror is a charming Rouge like RPG that's very inspired by the works of Junji Ito, you should definitely pick up this hidden gem of a gameSo I'm a huge fan of Rouge-likes, and really love the works of Junji Ito, so this game was already pretty high on my list to buy, and I have to say after spending some time with it I have to say, I absolutely adore this charming little abomination, and no please don't take it the wrong way, this game is beautiful in the most disgusting way possible. The art style is very reminiscent of old MSDOS adventures, and a lot of the aesthetic is built around that late 80's early 90's look, meaning 1 or 2 bit color schemes and lot's of pixels, but even with these limitations the game still manages to deliver something super creepy, the music adds to the tension along with the sound effects, all tainted with that glorious 90's crunch that makes it sound like the speakers to my old Dell. The gameplay is also a really cool idea, a majority of your time is spent investigating different locations to advance the plot of a mystery you're currently working on, meaning you'll be going to a wide variety of locations, and after each investigation you'll have an event happen, this can be either a text based encounter where you have to make a decision and depending on what you choose you could walk away with either a nasty new injury, a new ally, or a new item, and then there are the combat encounters. this is the RPG part of the game, as it's turn based combat. now you'll notice I haven't really mentioned the story because that a lot of the fun is experiencing the crazy stories for yourself, no two runs will ever be the same, and honestly this is a shining example of a great indie game on steam, and I hope that the developer continues to make games

_childDocuments_.review: Managing your time, resources, health, and dwindling sanity. Each trip to continue your investigation could be your last. Unique encounters that rely on your level-ups to survive, each choice matters and has lasting effects on if you win, or lose. That battle you ran from? You just lost precious time that allows the lovecraftian horror to come even closer to engulfing the world.Those loss ends in the investigation that weren't covered? Exp lost that could've been used for a much needed level-up to pass a stat check. A variety of characters each with a unique level-up tree to go down gives for different play styles.Want to be the bad-ass syndicate beating ghouls with a baseball bat? We got you!Wanna be the popular e-girl of the class sacrificing your followers to save your own skin? Perfect!How about a mysterious medical student with a cute face and dark past?  It's all up to you!I'm not usually a fan of horror, but this game really does well in representing Junji Ito well. Though many monsters are original, and there's a huge inspiration from Japanese folklore, the game does well for itself in being a quite original piece. I've only read a few of Junji Ito's comics, but from my brief experience with the genre I'd say the eerie atmosphere that those comics give off are reflected perfectly in this game. I'm a huge fan of roguelikes, and WOH really stands out as a unique one in my eyes. The art style adds to the experience, and the approach of 1-bit horror really adds to the style of the game, fitting this "retro" kind of feel.And the modding community helps this game a-lot! Though it's in a fairly primitive state, (which makes sense given this game was released this year). Mods can range from meme-worthy, to so well-aligned with the game that you forget that these creatures, encounters, etc. were even made by a different person.I really don't have any complaints, other than the usual for Roguelikes.RNG is real. Very real. You can go from one investigation away from getting 4 mental cases of paranoia, 2 broken ribs, and third-degree burns in a few encounters. But to me.. that makes it all the more fun!One big thing that I've noticed though, even though this game is difficult. The final push to win, is... lackluster. To say the least. Expecting some huge big fight at the end of the game, I was instead treated to a few skill checks, a sub-par enemy encounter (though the enemy himself is fairly unique), and a single click to lift the fog. Given most of my runs were completed at above 90% doom (Doom is your "time" constraint until the Old-Gods awaken, and thus causes a gameover), it is kind of understandable why this is done. In some ways though, I feel kind of cheated. For an early-access though, it's extremely complete. And the fact that it IS early access gives me hope for some really great content in the future.I honestly look forward to seeing how this game evolves.

_childDocuments_.review: World of Horror is styled to look like a lost Japanese horror adventure from the '80s running on a haunted PC-88. Your enjoyment of World of Horror is likely to be directly proportional to how cool of an idea you think that is.I think it's really cool, myself! Pick a protagonist and start investigating a string of occult mysteries in small-town Japan. Investigation takes the form of semi-randomized incidents and encounters, which force you to make a choice, or use a tool, or grapple with WoH's wonky combat system (easily the weakest part of the game). Over the course of five cases, your protagonist will unlock perks and spells, as well as suffer persistent physical and sanity damage. Then you'll face the cult responsible for the overarching threat from beyond.Junji Ito is the main and primary inspiration, but real heads will pick up references to all sorts of J-horror.WoH has all kinds of promise, and the modular nature of the whole thing seems like it's ideal for mods and DLC. Don't hold your breath for 1.0, though. The development team reportedly consists of one guy with a day job, and he's made a hell of a game, but at this rate it's going to be a while before WoH leaves Early Access. Or maybe he'll make the announcement tomorrow, the hell do I know.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I loaded the game to find the saving/loading is disabled for a future update. I can see how that'd be frustrating, but it's still not a deal breaker IMO as games can typically be completed in one sitting. Anyways, if saving/loading IS a deal breaker for you, go to Properties>Betas and opt in to the older build, it has saving/loading enabled.Felt the need to post a review to counter the small wave of dumb, entitled children screaming "lol lazy dev took money and run 0/10 son".This game hasn't been updated since October 2020, and radio silence from dev since December. If that bothers you, don't buy this game. I can completely understand that mentality and wouldn't fault you for it. I can even understand if you already bought it and were disappointed at the lack of communication and updates after December.But for me personally, I am of the opinion that not every developer needs to inform their audience of every development milestone or roadblock that comes their way. I don't scream foul, demanding... DESERVING to know why a timeline goal wasn't reached. Especially when that developer is one guy. S**t happens, life changes happen, writer's block happens. Hell, maybe guy closes himself off from the world in a fit of depression for a while, I don't know.But I do know I can give some leeway for smaller development teams, and even more leeway if they're creating something exceptional. This falls into both categories.This is an awesome piece of art where it stands, and absolutely worth the asking price. If it never gets another update, I will have gotten my money's worth. If I never play another minute of it (HIGHLY UNLIKELY) I will have gotten my money's worth. The artwork, the soundtrack, the U.I, EVERYTHING about this game oozes style, care and love. SO MUCH so, that I absolutely refuse to believe the developer abandoned this. If it never gets another update ever, the developer died... or just got fed up with the annoying part of the gaming community and switched career paths entirely.Either way, if this game seems interesting to you, you should pick it up. While I wish there were more scenarios, what is here is great. The game itself doesn't just feel like a tech demo, the core game loop is there, and it is enjoyable. A full game can typically last for an hour or so (going from memory, I played it almost to full completion when it came out and shelved it to forget the scenarios for a fresh experience down the line), and you'll have to play a good number of times to be able to see EVERYTHING the game has to offer (I put 21.9 hrs in the original 12 scenarios to see ALMOST everything... not counting achievements, and there were a few added since I played it). I have played literally thousands of games, and still have yet to find a second game that scratches this particular itch of adventuring through a world of Japanese-style horror comics, let alone does so with so much style.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer up front: this game gets more of a neutral opinion than a negative one, the reason I didn't choose to go neutral positive is due to my disappointment after seeing that trailers do not accurately represent actual gameplay. I was very hyped about World of Horror at first glance, the art is beautiful and the Junji Ito/Lovecraft inspirations are very appealing to me, however going into the game after seeing the animated trailers had me expecting an entirely different experience. What I had hoped for and expected was a more classic point and click adventure style game a la Detention, my Halloween purchase from last year, with environments to explore and puzzles to solve. What World of Horror does instead is entirely menu based gameplay where you select different locations in town to roll random encounters on until you reach certain goals within your current mystery, and then after a few mysteries you get to go to the lighthouse and fight a boss. The game isn't bad by any means but I definitely felt heavily mislead and regretted not looking at gameplay on youtube first.As far as what the game does well, the roguelike elements are certainly interesting with a slew of random world effects from different Old Ones, abilities and various debuffs for different characters and events, and a moderate variety of random encounters per location. You might have your character start with a passive ability that encourages collecting npc allies but an old god that reduces your long term DOOM timer so whether or not to spend the extra time to make friends becomes a tough decision. Unfortunately that depth does not extend as much into combat as most encounters I've come across just came down to repeatedly preparing and then launching attacks without much need for any other combat maneuvers. I can't stress enough that the art and just general vibes here are amazing but the gameplay itself really doesn't support it enough for me to recommend despite how much I wanted to like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: -The art aesthetic is awesome.-The writing is solid across the board. The plot is interesting and can vary each time you play.There's a large variety of encounters and plots, all of which cannot be experienced in a single playthrough. -To my surprise, the game has a large amount of customization. You get to chose the color scheme, bit count, etc. Even playthroughs can be customized, as you can select the major antagonizing force, your character, and more. On top of it all, the game even has a modding community.-The mix between a classic RPG and Horror works, although do note that this game requires a fair amount of reading. One thing that I love most about this game is the tone and atmosphere. Starting out each playthrough, things will seem a little unusual or disturbing. As time drags on, and you progress through the plot, the atmosphere gets creepier and the world begins to fall apart around you. Every action you take, from visiting the store to running from a masked mad man has consequences that must be considered when playing. It seems the developer really put in the effort to ensure this game cannot be played mindlessly. -As an avid horror fan who is pretty desensitized to the genre, this game has moments that disturb and frighten even the likes of me. With every playthrough the game continues to do this, which not many other horror titles can boast. I've taken so many screenshots of encounters that creeped me out that I pretty much have an entire folder dedicated to this game. What excites me even more is that it's still an early access game - I hope the developer continues to add in more encounters and mysteries to be solved.TL;DR: This game is like crack but scarier. Highly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: This game wants desperately to be Arkham Horror 2nd edition. You go places, 'draw events' and attempt to ward off a number of not-quite-Lovecraft great old ones. The art is great, the music and atmosphere are good.The game, however, is cripplingly random. Thankfully advancing the plot is not, but you do that by going to a location and having an event, and those events have NOTHING to do with the overall mystery. For example, I spent a whole mystery waiting in line for mysteriously good ramen, and while waiting I was ambushed by cultists (in line?) was chased down an alleyway by a mysterious presence (in line?) and got attacked in my apartment (in line?).You have no way to tell if an event will give you a useful item or kick you in the face. The random run modifiers that show up after every boss range from meh (oh no, I don't get my 1 free point of healing per mystery) to absolutely crippling (the game clock runs faster, all healing is penalized, all spells cost more sanity and you're doing a spellcaster run).Add to that that the ending is mostly an anticlimax and it's a well-made distraction. I hope the designer makes a sequel (if this ever leaves EA) based off of the newer Arkham Horror board game where things are more focused. The mysteries where you leave town and go somewhere new are greatly improved, if only because the smaller event pool makes the game feel more organic and focused.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of roguelikes, but this may just be one of the very best. One thing that I personally adore is that how much it reminds me of the board game Arkham Horror. it scratches that itch wonderfully while also bringing a lot of its own features to the table. I love just how dynamic runs can be from character to character, elder god to elder god, and especially with all of the mysteries and backgrounds, too. Now that the game is fully out, I can confidently say that it's worth your time. The mysteries are each incredible, each character is a blast to play, and the events are very memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: Good, creepy fun.It's a game vaguely in the style of the old "MacVenture" titles like Uninvited, Deja Vu, etc. with music that reminds me of games like Waxworks, in that it manages to be eerie and tense but also quite catchy and melodious too (Waxworks is an old, quite difficult but interesting and also spooky sort of dungeon crawler/adventure hybrid with varied locales and time periods and pretty good horror elements, though good luck with that one without a guide). It plays out like a very light tabletop RPG with stats to manage, skill checks on various random encounters, turn-based combat with a number of bizarre monstrosities from masked killers, mannequins, undead, eldritch horrors and even sometimes a regular street thug who'll throw molotovs at you (inflicting severe burns, one of a number of status effects you can accrue). The art style is great, making the most out of very little. Normal human characters are well-defined, the encounters with people meant to be subtly (or not so much) "off" are very much so, and the out-and-out horror creatures very much radiate as less-than-pleasant things to have to encounter. It definitely wears its influences on its sleeve, as stated so in the store description, Junji Ito and the Cthulhu mythos. The unusual, ghoulish characters and weird, unsettling mysteries you encounter around town in a fictional Japanese setting takes from Ito, and on top all of these events are said to be influenced by whichever elder god you choose to start your game with (or which one the game chooses for you if going for a preset adventure). Each elder god has a certain status effect on the overall game (inability to run from combat, resting raising your doom meter by a good number, doom being a percentage that goes up as you advance the game, fail certain checks, do side events that uses up time, and if it hits 100% it's game over. Considering you need to finish five randomly chosen mysteries and a final trek through a lighthouse per playthrough you need to manage your in-game time carefully, especially on difficulties above "Sceptic." Certain events and completions of mysteries can also lower your doom too though so not all is hopeless).The more you play, the more you unlock, be it game items, characters or even game modes. There are a number of encounters, different endings to mysteries you'll do, enemies to fight, "achievements" and endings in general that you'll find more and more of the more of the game you play. Runs of the game aren't very long, whether you fail or win. Every new game is a pretty quickly paced affair, throwing you right into the heart of the weirdness with events, enemy encounters, and progression of its concisely worded mini-plots for mysteries to resolve. As of this writing, the ability to save mid-game is disabled due to bugginess with its implementation before but anything new encountered or accomplished during playthroughs is saved which is more important in my opinion. Runs of the game are not long enough that you would need mid-game saves. Everything is procedurally generated from a vast pool of different elements, some that you might encounter repeatedly, plenty others brand new. It works fine as it is for me personally.And this is all still in Early Access. The game as it is now is already quite solid, I can't wait to see what new things the devs will bring to the game leading up to its official release.

_childDocuments_.review: A compellingly unique example of a classic genre, a "choose your own adventure" branching narrative with gorgeously stylised pixel and dither artwork. Calling back to the brilliant artists of yesteryear, using only 2 colours to paint convincing worlds, and the brilliant stories that had our imaginations filling in where the visuals of the time couldn't. Think Disco Elysium mixed with a Junji Ito manga on an original Gameboy.The menu and HUD elements are seamlessly incorporated into the overall presentation, giving the whole thing a cohesive and immersive feel. This game doesn't stop when you enter a settings menu, instead the menus for the games settings and the menus for the characters actions all follow the same aesthetic, which really helps maintain the attention, and thus, the tension you feel. The stories are short and sweet, but offer a satisfying degree of variety, and replay value, depending on your choices, as you'd expect from this kind of game, but the artwork and presentation really make the game more than just another CYOA, it doesn't necessarily break the fourth wall, but its knocking on it from the other side, menacingly.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a good "game", but a good immersive story. World of Horror reminds me of a board game. Every game, you solve one of five mysteries. To solve mysteries, you explore various locations, and every time you explore a location you draw a "card" that gives you a random event. Eventually, you will "solve" the mystery and it will either resolve or you will encounter a boss. The gameplay itself is interesting but not exhilarating. It's rolling dice with some extra strategic options; playing it correctly results in saving a couple stamina/reason but for the most part every encounter feels the same, though different characters have slightly different ways to fight. I still find this game has replay value because of the story and because I find rolling dice and drawing cards amusing, but make no mistake that this is essentially want the game boils down to. The game really shines through its atmosphere and pixel art. Each mystery has its own unique pixel artwork along with the various characters in the game, and each mystery is horrifying in an atmospheric eldritch-horror way and stylistically consistent. The music and sound design is excellent. If you would pay $20 for 2-3 Junji Ito horror manga books then I would recommend World of Horror even in its current "pre-1.0" stage.

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere of this game alone is stellar. Drawing heavy inspiration from Junji Ito (to the point that game files are .ito in his honor!) and H.P. Lovecraft (who along with the former, cameos), WoH is pure retro horror-candy. If you've never heard of Junji Ito, he's the mastermind behind Uzumaki and The Enigma of Amigara Fault, to name two of his more famous (in the West) works. You may remember him as being Hideo Kojima's choice, along with Guillermo del Toro, in developing Silent Hills. Seriously, just check out some of the beautiful nightmares he can bring to life sometime. Suffice to say, the setting's foundation is very solid indeed.While the developer can go silent for a few months at a time, it's because he works devotedly on the game. Despite being in early access, it has a vast modding community allowing for custom content, in no small part due to the simple, 1-bit graphics and extremely easy to produce encounter files. How easy? You fill out a list and save it as a .ito. Done.Thus, my verdict is that it draws upon a deep well of eldritch horror, and an equally deep well of readily-available fan contribution. That's a recipe for success.

_childDocuments_.review: World of Horror (WoH) is a very good game with a pretty bad tutorial and doesn't tell you much else. I've beaten the game a few times so far and definitely think it's for a specific crowd.If you want to get into the game:- Do the spine-chilling story of school scissors and run through the combat tutorial, but its not that great in my opinion so you might honestly want to watch a quick video breaking it down. Make sure to go into your storage and read the notes your friend left behind, although to be honest not sure how helpful they are.- After spine-chilling story of school scissors, do extracurricular activity before going into quick play/custom playthrough. Extracurricular has 4 mysteries instead of the 5 in normal quick play so it'll be alot easier. Notes the game does not tell you about but will help you (especially after reading the negative reviews):- Go home and open the cupboards in your room because there's a chance they will contain empty bottles- Take a bath. You usually always want to take a bath between mysteries, whether for health regen or exp boost. You'll want to fill up the empty bottle you found here too, and you can refill it every time you bathe (once between mysteries)- Go to the closest to change your clothes, but the little toy on the top left has 1 fund. Pretty nice.- Pick mysteries that have you start in the city. I know this may not be such a nice tip but after playing the game enough, you'll know what mysteries lead where. My favorite is the eel mystery since you immediately get a follower, Kana, and getting enough followers to do lots of damage via the follower attack is pretty nice when you don't have good weapon or other stats.- Following the previous tip, go to either the store in downtown or the hardware store by the sea to pick up some starting equipment. The store has compass which lets you get alot of free xp and hardware store gets you a good starting weapon. A weapon is better than nothing in my opinion. - The police station also has cuffs in one of the drawers that you can use and the doctor's office has pain killers. - Don't be afraid to run away, better to risk dying later than dying earlier. This game has alot of things it doesn't tell you, but that's also the fun of being rewarded for discovering all sorts of new goodies. I didn't even know that achievements were  thing and that they rewarded you for unlocking them. The devs are working on getting achievements to sync with steam but for now they're in the extra's menu of options. Hope this review helped. I think the fear and hunger and darkest dungeon 1 crowd would appreciate this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Turn up the Judas Priest and sharpen your ritual knives, occultists, it's time to party like it's 198X.Welcome to WORLD OF HORROR! (yes, in all caps, that's how you know it's scary)WORLD OF HORROR is a neoclassical turn-based roguelite/roguelike roleplaying horror game, based on central concepts familiar to the Call of Cthulu folks amongst us; unknowable evil from the dark corners of our universe stir, and it's up to you to put paid to their attempts to awaken and end everything as you know it. In one corner, the legions of eldritch nightmares, abominations, aberrations, urban legends given flesh, and the teeming masses of mortal followers marching headlong into damnation.In the other? A player character with no talents, no equipment, no training, bad cardio, and 10 USD to their name. I can hear the space-faring sorcerous super-lifeform quaking in its metaphorical boots already.So, WORLD OF HORROR has a simple premise : pick a character, pick a backstory, (pick a timeline - don't worry, it doesn't affect much at first), and then pick a rival that will threaten the quiet town of Shiokawa, Japan. Naturally, different characters start with different stats and a random starting gift, bonus, or condition.The elder deity you select changes certain conditions of the run; Ithotu raises damage dealt and received across the board, while Cthac-Atorasu renders you unable to flee an engagement. Each entity also has a group of events specific to them that can trigger, usually to your detriment. From there, you take on WORLD OF HORROR's investigations, any one of 5 given to you per run, attempting to solve it to the best of your abilities, while also accruing the skills, equipment, allies, and assets it will take to survive your how-you-say, eldritch escapade. You juggle your health, your sanity, and the very fate of the human race with the most important resource of all : time. The run is restricted by a DOOM counter; simple premise - actions fill the timer. If the timer reaches 100, you lose. Don't let it do that. Don't die, either, and preferably don't go completely crazy, all while solving each of the 5 cases, and you can take on the final obstacle and  delay the end. Bam, you win! Easy as that.If you're as old as I am, first off, I'm so sorry, and secondly, you might reminisce of the delightful art style; WORLD OF HORROR has a deliberate invoking of 1-bit graphics, supported by some wonderful art direction. Should you not be too fond of the staggering power of the color White and Not-White, you can also apply 2-bit color schemes; "Omen, Neon Slasher," and "Mondo" bring out gorgeous gore, gushing gallons of gore in grandiose (g)red. For best effect, turn on "Jaguar" and some Macintosh Plus for that A E S T H E T I C look.Oh, the many inspirations we show here;  while we're obviously drawing from the haunted mindscape of H.P. Lovecraft and co., much of WORLD OF HORROR also draws from the works of famed mangaka Junji Ito for illustration and mood, alongside a great deal of Japanese urban horror and folklore. The Kuchisake-onna, Aka Manto, and Hanako-san show up alongside more classic examples of folklore, spiced up by the eldritch otherness of it all. It's quite a treat for the shameless eccentrist in all of us; everyone loves a rumor!Of special note is the depiction of your character; you can see them throughout the run, and various status conditions can be seen rendered modeled. Part of the horror charm is seeing your character start out as a fresh-faced, flesh-graced teen and end the journey scarred, mauled, burned, touched by the etheric and otherwise worse for wear.(I like collecting these conditions; it's fun to see the list of disabilities I can accrue before the victory. It's not enough to beat an Old One, you have to do it while looking at least as bad as the things it sent after you.)While, at present, WORLD OF HORROR is early-access, and appears to be as such for the foreseeable future, I still recommend supporting and playing it. If the premise doesn't grab you, at first, allow me to make a more concerted attempt to sway you, the reader?As a closer to this brief summary of WORLD OF HORROR, I'd like to regale you with a list of possibilities you may or may not experience while playing, such as :

_childDocuments_.review: Generally not a fan of games that put your fate heavily into random chance like Roguelikes, and this game absolutely falls into that exact trap as your run might end to misfortune or thrive to fortune. That said, like other RNG heavy games, you're not without options, and learning how to carefully manage your resources can significantly mitigate the impact randomness has on your playthrough.Beyond that, what does the game have to offer? Interesting combat that's just complex enough to supplement the story without being so intricate that it becomes a focus, with the story itself being fairly compelling and interesting, really capturing the Japanese folk horror vibe and mixing it beautifully with Lovecraft-style Eldritch themes. The enemy designs and the mini-stories some of them have are fascinating, and each mystery you can solve has a satisfying conclusion. All of this complemented beautifully by the 1bit/2bit art style that does an excellent job of capturing how to maximize minimalism the way old games tried to do, rather than using the low detail graphics as a crutch to avoid trying on the visuals. All in all, very worth the time of any horror fans, whether it's the atmosphere or the themes that draw you in. Best enjoyed with fresh pizza and a soda.

_childDocuments_.review: Eldritch horror is something that has always intrigued me. Though I find more terror in realistic evil like psychopathic murders, cosmic entities such as Cthulhu and related mythos have a sci-fi element that fascinates me. World of Horror takes plenty of inspiration from Lovecraft's works, but blends it with a healthy dose of the macabre and the disgusting humanoid abominations present in plenty of Japanese artistic mediums. The enemies one encounters through the game range from demonic spirits and disturbed maniacs, to your traditional massive creatures from beyond capable of decimating the world with the blink of an eye.World of Horror is an RPG about a character trying to stop an eldritch entity or deity from destroying a small, seaside town. The player progresses through five mysteries, which randomize every playthrough. As with typical RPG's, you with fight enemies, encounter events, and have the option to visit shops or other places. World of Horror is a short game where you are racing against a "doom" clock, which increases based on time and certain decisions. If you've played titles such as FTL or Darkest Dungeon, you will likely be familiar with this urgency which punishes poor time efficiency. Each playthrough generally lasts around an hour. That said, due to the work-in-progress nature of the game, you should play in one sitting since the save feature is funky.On top of that, World of Horror possesses a solid combat system. This game does not play slow, which is a gripe I have with the few RPG's I have tried in the past. It contains your typical selection of stats (strength, dexterity, etc.) which assist in combat as well as non-combat events. The stat weights also will affect the usefulness of different types of weapons you may use during a playthrough. During combat, you select a series of moves: offensive, defensive, support, and spiritual; each action carries a different "time" cost that you balance with a meter for time each turn. There are no overly drawn out combat animations, just a quick slash or other effect to give a sense of action. This brevity allows the game to move at a much faster pace, leaving little waiting time between moves. Lastly, the artstyle compliments a retro feel without feeling overly gimmicky. Plenty of games have an "8-bit" theme, yet they feel cheap. That style does not do World of Horror a disservice. The animations are fairly simple, but provides enough life to make what you see and interact with feel active. Overall, this game feels fairly polished in it's Early Access state. There are some issues that I expect to be ironed out (namely the save feature along with some grammatical issues.) I much prefer the faster paced turn-based combat of this game compared to other RPG's. One would likely gloss over the text in events on subsequent playthroughs, but this game isn't exactly story focused so I won't really hold that against it. So, if the eldritch and grotesque is your favorite type of horror and you want a game that gives you a quick playthrough for an afternoon or evening, I would definitely recommend picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptional, one-of-a-kind, no need to wait for a sale.Release Update: The game has released a V1.0 and it delivers on the promises of early access.  There's enough variety and content to enjoy multiple runs, lots of unlockables, and customizable difficulty to make a playthrough as challenging as you can stand.  A 1-bit (or 2-bit, if you fancy some shading) point and click roguelike adventure set in a terrifying Japanese seaside town in the late 80s.  The whole game plays like a point-and-click board game (Eldritch Horror is similar) as you attempt to solve 5 mysteries and stop the ritual to summon an old god.  As you solve mysteries, you'll encounter events and battles and choices that will shape the outcome.  Multiple endings to each mystery, lots of varied events, and a quick pace will let you try, fail, and try again many times. _childDocuments_.review: For now I'm going to leave this review as a positive one because based off what I've learned about the dev, I think that the problems this game has will be fixed and probably soon. And once they are, I think it'll be real special.Anyways,World of Horror is equal parts game and love letter to the horror mangaka Junji Ito and H.P Lovecraft. I for one think it's a great idea and really for the most part it doesn't have a lot of ironing out to do at this point as far as basic gameplay is concerned.SETTING AND ATMOSPHEREThe game is set in 1984 Japan in a coastal town called Shiokawa. It's unclear to me if it's in any way related to the real life town of Shiokawa that existed in Fukushima Prefecture up until 2006, but I digress. In what might be intentional irony, this town in 1980s Japan which was a time of extreme wealth, happiness, and optimism has a constant feeling of dread hanging over it. The time period feels right. It's a unique setting, and a game should never let you forget that. This is the 80s in Japan and you know it. And the dread is real. You don't know what's wrong just by looking at the town, but the game is presented in a way that makes you know that something is seriously wrong here. And the pixelated aesthetic feels authentic. The dev didn't emulate a style as much they made a game in that style. It was a primary draw for me to this game, and I have to say I am thoroughly happy with it. This is all combined with a great chiptune soundtrack that complements the whole thing very well. Lovecraft's mythos is the central lore, but with Japanese urban legends and horror elements mixed in. It presents a setting that should feel somewhat familiar to some, but entirely unique as well.GAMEPLAYThe game is an RPG/adventure game through and through, and its mechanics work accordingly. You select from several different characters with varying stats. Then, you choose which Eldritch God you want to fight in this specific playthrough. This effects the narrative, and also adds in a certain debuff like being unable to run from combat depending on which god you choose. This game encourages replaying by making the average playthrough very short, which is typically up to an hour. You're give a choice of seed for the new save, and from there you're given 5 mysteries to solve. All the while, you have to watch the Doom Meter, which rather than telling you when you get the pick up a chainsaw and rip and tear your way through Hell, tells you how much time you have before the Eldritch God you chose awakens from their slumber which when they do of course means you're S.O.L. Almost every action raises the Doom Meter and there isn't much you can do to lower it so you have to be deliberate in your actions. You have to solve the 5 mysteries in order to get access to the Lighthouse which is where you perform a ritual that seals the god away for another 300 years and wins the game.Throughout these mysteries there are random events as well as combat. Your character effectively has two healthbars, Stamina and Reason. When you run out of stamina, you physically die. When you run out of reason, you go insane. Either way it's game over. Certain enemies and actions will drain either of these. If you lift something heavy and pull a muscle, it lowers stamina. If you witness a traumatizing event, it effects reason. As anyone who knows at least a bit about Lovecraftian horror knows, insanity is a central theme in the mythos. The basis of it all is the idea that Cosmic Horrors exist in a way and in a place that is so incomprehensible to the human mind that even looking at them could cause someone to go insane. You have to manage both your physical or mental health, and in this you find the game's greatest flaw.I've heard that the dev wanted to get player feedback on the balancing with early access, but I'm not really sure if balance really exists here. The game relies WAY too much on RNG. It's like the game penalizes you for breathing. You go investigate downtown. RNG says someone's stalking you. You lose reason. Investigate again. Some lunatic without a face attacks you. You lose stamina and reason. You investigate somewhere else. Family friend calls up and asks you to help them move. RNG says you lift something heavy and tear a muscle. You lose stamina. The game gives you very little control over how the game progresses. You're given different choices in many of these random events, but you never know what's going to happen. You don't know if you'll tear a muscle lifting something, or you'll be fine and the friend will give you tea and cookies after. You'll die over and over just because the game decided to throw a bunch of random events at you that sapped your stats so much that once you get to an important fight you're easy pickings. And at the end of every solved mystery, the game also slaps on a new handicap caused by the Old God that lasts for the rest of the playthrough. And you can't just chalk it up to poor planning. There's only so much you can do to recover stamina and reason and the things that do restore them don't add many points. The most reliable way is resting at home but that raises the Doom Meter. In between mysteries you can do stuff at your apartment without raising the Doom Meter including taking a bath which depending on what temperature you set the water to can raise stamina, reason, or give you EXP. But if you get the Old God handicap that contaminates the water you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and can't use the shower anymore. Aside from resting the only other place to really recover is the hospital, but that costs money and the amount of money you get in game means that you'll rarely ever buy more than 3 items in a single playthrough. The fate of a playthrough should lie soley in player error. I should lose a boss fight because I didn't prepare myself, not because I got mauled every time I stepped outside my house. I shouldn't have to totally lose a playthough just because the game decided I should.But as I said, it sounds like the dev is on top of it, and I'm sure they'll listen to feedback. Adjusting the RNG and maybe tweaking how the events and healing works is all I can really see the game needing. From there, I'll look forward to seeing what new content gets rolled out. World of Horror has a place among good horror games and I think it can easily find it.Provided it can get more than three feet out the front door before a masked man beats it to death with a baseball bat.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to write a review with more time under my belt under normal circumstances.But this game isn't exactly "normal".Thematically this game is an absolute triumph, the 1/2bit art used to graphically represent the horror surrounding the player is just as effective as Junji Ito's striking black-ink art style and just as horrifying.I play many horror games and have become somewhat disillusioned to most "scary" events in games, yet this game from the first investigation I played had me legitimately chilled. It felt great to feel like a kid playing a scary game again. The mechanics of the game have what you'd expect from a rouge-like of this era. You unlock goodies and methods of influencing the gameplay experience as you win more and more. There's a standardized playthrough to give you a chance to understand the sorts of items, combat, abilities, and scenarios you'll encounter. A quickplay option that randomizes your playthough settings, and a game mode where YOU PICK all of the settings for your playthough (things like your character, the BBEG, and other tweaks). Multiple endings, characters, and costumes. Trackable achievements and information/lore pages about all the ♥♥♥♥ you find (including items, characters, monsters, elder gods, etc.).I know the graphics wouldn't imply it, but this game is pretty modernized, nothing feels too archaic.It is a point and click rpg. I really don't feel drawn to point and click adventure/rpgs but I really don't care with this game. I completely see past the playstyle in a way.. just because I love the storytelling and imagery so much, I find myself enjoying the pointing and clicking just dandy. Each page turn is exciting the first time, and each mystery is pretty gripping. Every time I encounter something new it's not uncommon for me to audibly say things like "..wow. very cool." I cannot stress the success of the style and storytelling enough.And even when all that wears off, you're left with a fun rpg with lots of options to try and reasons to try them. The campaign has multiple endings like I said, but you have to complete 5 separate "investigations" (which are the equivalent of a "level" or "dungeon" in other games) to complete the campaign, and each of the investigations (save for like one?) have 2-4 multiple endings! I also want to give everyone a tip: there's a timer for your campaign called "Doom %" and if you reach 100% before you die or beat the game you'll get a special ending specific to the BBEG, and there are multiple BBEGs. I cannot stress the amount of content enough. And it costs $15. I've certainly paid more for games I've spent less time with. If you like Edgar Allan Poe, H.P. Lovecraft, and Junji Ito, Get it. If you like Horror Manga, Literature, and games, Get it. If you like point and clicks, get it. If you're looking around thinking of buying a game and you can't quite decide which one, get this one, because at least then you'll have what I consider to be a true hidden gem among games.And I have a near mint copy of Blood Will Tell for the PS2 so I kind of know what I'm talking about.

_childDocuments_.review: While the learning curve is quite rough, that's part of the fun of horror.  What begins as fear of the unknown mechanics and the capabilities of you and the monsters you face, becomes adrenaline as you roll the dice and take calculated risks to secure your own victory.  This shift in tone basically takes the feeling of the game from Lovecraft horror (in which you're pretty doomed) to Buffy the Vampire Slayer (in which things are horrifying but victory is possible).Since it is early access, do expect some bugs.  I haven't personally experienced any crashes, but I did learn to what extent saving and quitting is something you do only when you need to.  Doing so removed all of my allies and perks, I didn't lose my items but they all went to storage, and the extra effects that affected the town were gone too.

_childDocuments_.review: World of Horror had potential to be a great turn-based RPG that dealt with classic takes on local lore and horror and combining it with popular media tropes of horror in a way that made the game's already random story sequencing feel unique a lot of the time compared to other horror games with a "Rogue-like" aspect or element of randomness and repetition. The fanbase however has become quite divided since the radio-silence of the developer, with some declaring the game as Abandonware, and others claiming the former category is toting a sense of entitlement and demand for content that the developer is potentially working on with no visible teases or hints at future content. As the game stands, what I once said was a good game with a good-looking future and more to come has become stagnant save for the community building mods for the game, mostly focused around Vinesauce Vinny though. Players will find a lot of non-action and events that have no bearing on the game as they may not be fully implemented yet, such as the Cthulhu Statuette event, which, has no effect one way or the other. While I hope the developer is alive and well, without any word of development, even a single "Yes. I am working on updates." The game's $15 price tag feels a lot more daunting with a less substantial promise of more in store. Buyer beware, it's fun for a bit of interactive horror with friends or a stream, but you'll find yourself growing weary sooner than later.

The writing and quirky horror narratives which fill this game and a mix of funny parodies of its inspirations, Ito as previously mentioned as well as the works of Lovecraft, and  full on intriguing horror mysteries which reward hesitation and planning. _childDocuments_.review: Currently my new favorite game. The style, music, and writing are wonderfully macabre. The retro aesthetic is executed well and heightens the creepiness of everything. There's just enough detail to ick you out, with room left over to let your imagination run wild.The gameplay itself is highly addictive. I'm not a huge fan of RPGs or roguelikes, but this one strikes a solid balance between thoughtful strategy and pure luck. The randomized elements are well-tuned.  It's unforgiving, the kind of game that lets you screw up big time and pay dearly for it. You get the sense that the game's world is *just* out of your control, but with some intelligent decision-making you can always turn things around. There are some small balance issues—I've found a couple weapons and spells to be basically useless—but overall everything meshes together well.If you're a fan of horror games, definitely check this one out.I'm playing the early access version, and I'm impressed with how smooth everything is running. For all intents and purposes it's a"finished" game, very much worth your money.
