_childDocuments_.review: Because World Of Horror made modding beginner-friendly, I recommend getting the game mostly as a form of creative exercise.I've first heard about this game from a Vinesauce stream from when this was in early access.From my experience, it plays out like a point n' click adventure roguelike where you have to solve five mysteries to save the world from an OLD GOD. Encounters are like shuffled "cards" in a deck, and most outcomes are determined by dice rolls and skill checks, some are combat encounters. You do unlock some some more stuff though the game's achievement system, some being more mysteries.My favourite part of this game, because World Of Horror had made it easy enough for anyone without coding experience to add their own characters, encounters, enemies, and mysteries. The game comes with example templates and instructions for them. I had some fun just making my own custom encounters and characters for the game, it's good for practicing art, writing, and creative ideas in general.-While the game encourages modding, it doesn't have a Steam Workshop at the time this was written. If you want to install mods, you'll need to find them on other websites.-As far as I know, there's no way to make custom OLD GODs, items, curses, injuries, or allies.-Random encounters feel a bit samey, and might need something more dynamic like critical fail/critical success outcomes, or something more interactive like puzzle minigames.-The "save the world" ending feels repetitive, and doesn't fit the themes of most of the OLD GODs at all. I wish that you would go to a more appropriate place to defeat them, like a museum or a spider-infested cave instead of the lighthouse every playthough.I hope my review helps the developer as much as it helps you decide if you want this game or not.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a creepy game that great at establishing an atmosphere of unease and worry. Though the game is in early access, I've enjoyed the soundtrack and visuals immensely and the stories told hit a nice note of scary horror story; but not the jump scare kind: more the slow creeping feeling of some cosmic horror out to get you. If I were to nitpick, I'd say the UI can take getting used to: it isn't immediately clear what does what until you play the game for a while: although, I think that's part of the game design, that you're figuring stuff out in an otherworldly situation. There's a persistent sense that the more times you play it the more you'll get what you're supposed to be doing. With more content down the line planned and more stories added, I cannot recommend this game enough.As of current writing, I only a little over 3 hours clocked, which feels odd to me since I feel like I've played it longer than that. Most years, the sign the game is highly recommended is that I played MANY hours of it: in this case, the horrific unease does make this a hard to play in marathon sessions, I play it from time to time when I need a good chill or feel like getting as far as I can.

_childDocuments_.review: fun rouge-like game with some amazing horror direction. junji ito is written all over this game like it was his own written manfa. but it's more inspired by rather than an imitation of and it works really wellgame-play is a bit rough around the edges and at times a bit TOO unfair. some of the mysteries lose their charm after the first few times you go through them knowing what's about to happen, but the real fun comes from the random events. again they can be a bit too unfair and punishing for no real reason and it can kill runs because you have no control.Some might argue "that's the point" but a game that demoralizes you and is completely hinged on replay-ability can be exhausting and can really kill the mood. but those are my only big complaints, and with that said, everything else about this game is amazing and completely worth your time if you love horror and enjoy rogue-likes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really awesome. It has amazing art direction & writing style (primarily inspired by Junji Ito), but also achieves the rare niche of being a horror game that is actually fun to play. The only criticisms I would have of this game is that characters and stats are not entirely so balanced (i.e. stats like Dex are generally much more useful than others because Dex weapons are the most readily available) and oftentimes you can get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over by RNG - but this is less of an issue because it contributes to the hopeless atmosphere of the game, and good players can win no matter how bad their RNG is (one of the backgrounds in this game literally makes you automatically fail every skill check).Overall: This game will appeal to you if you enjoy Horror or Roguelite games, but for the Niche few that love both this game is tailor-made for youI would also advise largely going into the game blind - as a lot of the fun comes from getting alternatives endings or solutions to each mystery on subsequent playthroughs (Plus alt-tabbing out of the game to check the wiki might invite unwanted attention....)

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Eldritch horror, Japanese spookiness and old school point n' clicks, this manages to keep sucking me in.Great atmosphere, a lot of replay value in the form of unlockables that depend on some RNG, fantastic visuals (even if it's only 8 bit and 2-3 colours) and a great soundtrack make this well worthwhile for any horror fan looking for a quick pick-up-and-play run.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: The most unique horror game you will find on this platform, World of Horror mixes survival horror with solid RPG combat and events that are randomized to keep things fresh. You are a student in a doomed Japanese city, and must investigate 5 events that are given to you at random each playthrough, which have a main plotline and along the way of your investigation you are faced with random events in which you have to manage resources to survive.After you have done all the mysteries, the game keeps fresh by virtue of its randomized nature and the availability of mods, and is a perfect game for short plays as, once you get familiar with it, you will finish runs in 30 minutes or less.A perfect game for anyone wanting a breath of fresh air in the horror genre.

_childDocuments_.review: A must have if you are a fan of horror media, specifically manga, for the homages alone honestly.  I also recommend if you're a Darkest Dungeon fan as well. _childDocuments_.review: Being an early access game, the game has some problems including bugs, missing features, bad UI, and a slight lack of content. But even at the current state the game is worth the price, and I see decent potential to this game as more fixes and additional content are added over time. The game can be frustrating. The game doesn't do a good job at explaining things in certain parts of the game, and some parts of the game are meant to be a learning process from trial and error for beginners. But the atmosphere created by the game's cryptic art and music is just too good to pass up, even if you intend to play this for a short time. It's a great mix of Lovecraft and japanese horror. Don't look at too much spoilers from let's plays and walkthroughs.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: So all the glitches I personally experienced are currently fixed and I have been able to enjoy this game smoothly. The structure of the game play looks great for future add-ons and mods, and I'm pretty excited to see what other ways the stories can play out. There is still that possibility of a newly started game being doomed by a string of events but that also makes it interesting from a story telling point of view. If there was a way to tie previously perished character play throughs into future play throughs that might be an interesting twist to incorporate. But yeah as is the game is great as well as potential replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: World of Horror is a neat game that definitely changes the more you play it, as knowledge is easily the best thing you can have. The first runs are a good spooky time where you really have no idea what any of your selections are going to do, what IS the right option here? As you go on, it changes into more of risk management as you learn the encounters and start to be able to make smarter choices because of what you've learned, but then you'll hit something new and you are back to running blind. If you like horror, especially Junji Ito, World of Horror is worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: Perfectly nails everything it's going for. The vibe, the music, the art, and the tabletop inspired gameplay mesh together to make a totally unique game worth coming back to. Hopefully there will be more officially added mysteries and random events in future updates, but the mod support is so good that there will be plenty of good fan-made content.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: World of Horror is a surprisingly fun and innovative take on the rouge-like/rogue-lite genre!The game's aesthetic of early point-and-click adventure games blends perfectly with the darker, more horrific elements the game! Not to mention, the game is backed by a catchy soundtrack, which somehow works perfectly with the game! As if to top it all off, there are loads and loads of references to horror stories and urban legends sprinkled throughout the game, adding a whole extra depth to it all. The game also feels fairly complete for an early access game (still early access as of writing this review January 25th, at least), and I can't wait to see how it will be developed as time goes on.This game is well worth the money, and I personally found it very easy to get into, once you start to understand the game's combat and stat system. If you have even a passing interest in rogue like games, horror novels, or retro games in general, this is a perfect game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: I really REALLY hope they continue to work on this game. It already has a ton of content which I'm sure I've barely scraped but every addition adds so much more, and with what's there there are some things which would be literal game changers if introduced.I do wish there was a bit more information on the how-to portion of the game. Instead of just "investigate downtown" I would like to see "investigate the street (downtown)" if that's what I'm going to be investigating anyways. With the way it is it makes it feel more railroady. I mean it would just be the illusion of choice but it would be nice, otherwise I feel like I'm just clicking buttons and the game takes me where the story goes and I'm just along for the ride. Still, this is a BIG recommendation for me. The games are short and compact. I haven't quite figured out all the carry-over between games but it's exciting to get the swing of things. Would also love a few more clickables, even if they're red herrings. It would give more of a reason to pay attention to the illustrations and maintain a constant curiosity by the player.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is a fun blend of a lot of different styles of game. If you like games with any of the following, you'll probably have a great time: resource management, accurate difficulty options (easy is a free win if you know the basics, normal a bit harder and hard is a definite challenge), nonlinear puzzle solving (sequence puzzles, memorization, etc), random events, turn-based combat, Japanese horror and a retro art style.The game looks like something that would come out on the original Game Boy, but is clearly very polished in most areas to give it a modern feel. For a game in early access, there is a lot to do, and mod support will expand that even further. The only downsides the game has are the somewhat small pool of "mysteries" (the main objectives of the game, with there only currently being I think 12 though the random encounters total a whopping 115+ as far as I remember reading), the very loud and obnoxious "BEEP" that plays on startup to simulate a genuine DOS program and largest of all the last level of the game, which feels rather anticlimactic after everything you'll struggle through to reach that point.Overall, it's quite fun from what I've played! With 5 being an average game, I would give this a solid 8/10.

I bought this when it was heavily Junji. Its really unfinished but you still have 6+ endings and branching storylines that nod to Ito and Lovecraft. _childDocuments_.review: The TL;DR rundown: 1-bit roguelite point n' click that has elements of old school pen-and-paper tabletop RPG gameplay with a dope af Junji Ito / J-horror x H.P Lovecraft aesthetic that oozes atmosphere to tie everything together nicely. I absolutely dig this game and even in it's current early access state there is a ton of sick content to sink your teeth into. At the time of this review (Dec 2021) the "Ceaseless Curse" patch just dropped which is the largest content update so far. Looking forward to even more future updates (next one tentatively teased for Feb 2022) and custom community content that the fans cook up!If this sounds up your alley, buy this game, join the official community discord  and have fun! If you're still on the fence, check out the demo from 2019  although your mileage may vary as the game has evolved quite substantially since then!

_childDocuments_.review: Discovered WORLD OF HORROR after watching Vinesauce play it. I just had to see it for myself. This game is just... So pleasing to me. I'm too young to be nostalgic towards the early DOS era style, but I really find it quite unique and charming. There's a Ringu vibe to the visuals - correlating vintage media that is roughly familiar to us with unspeakable, unknowable evils. The music also slaps. It strikes the right balance of unsettling with the low, guttural buzzes and drones for the creepier moments and adrenaline pumping beats for combat. Needless to say, also love the yokai and eldritch theme. It's the best of Western and Eastern horror - with the Lovecraftian Gods and the Japanese urban legends comfortably residing together. This game is unsettling, but not startling. If you're looking for jumpscares... This isn't the game for you. It's about creeping dread and despair. Which is why I'm drawn to it. I'm an actual pansy and can't handle most horror games for the life of me. I did jolt in my seat a bit in one mystery. Though I can't quite remember what it was that scared me.The UI is also a bit daunting. I had an advantage because I watched someone else play first, but It only takes some getting used it. In a way... You could argue it helps with the horror by making you feel lost, cramped, and confused lmaoCombat is fine. Unique enough for a turned-based affair. The clapping and bowing system for ghosts still trips me up. Anyways. TLDR; awesome visuals, intriguing concept, awesome music, slightly unintuitive UI, okay combat system. Worth a play! Can't wait for the full release.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: World of Horror is a wonderful exercise in eerie game design. The decision to build the game around early Macintosh-style 1-bit graphics is stylistically perfect, and WoH does really build dread with only that minimalist graphical content. Forget Lovecraft's racist bulldrek - THIS is an eldritch horror setting done correctly. My only complaint is that after a few times through you start to anticipate the events you're going to run into, but the game has a very active modding community that can load you down with hours upon hours of new content, and the game IS still receiving updates. All in all, a very worthy investment for anyone that wants to get freaked out.

_childDocuments_.review: this game looks like trash on the first glance, but is great when given a chance. it takes a hot minute to learn menus and such, but this game is a challenging run-based horror game with resource management to an extent. some of my only gripes with this game is how some perks that help in future situations are very hard to predict for me, making them less of a precaution and more whether they help regardless of any encounters where it would be needed. also, this game is ruthless when it comes to being forgiven for mistakes, even on lower difficulty. it will constantly find unseen ways to catch you offguard and ruin a run, and has 3 different meters that must be monitored, making some runs lacking in stamina or reason, and some way too high in doom to expect a winning scenario. ive had at least 2 runs where ive been about 3-1 encounters to a win, where doom completely ended my run with no real last-minute fix to help me. very rng based, which makes it feel more based on memoery and luck rather than strategic skill. overall, a good purchase, but with flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting little single-player board game that succeeds mostly on its cool aesthetic. Mechanically, there's not a lot going on. A "run" consists of five randomly generated mysteries, each of which behaves like a deck of encounters. To get through them, you have to manage a bunch of resources--two health pools, an inventory, spells, stats, allies, time, money, and the like. Make it through all five, and you win.A run takes about an hour. Content starts to repeat pretty quickly after your first couple of runs, which is a bummer. A lot of my early enjoyment came from just looking at new art and reading new text. The game gets a little extra mileage out of its macroprogression, which encourages you to solve scenarios differently to unlock new content, but the juice isn't really worth the squeeze, I think. Rewards are small and runs are difficult and time-consuming.There appears to be a small but active mod community, and the game openly encourages people to create new content, so this problem is theoretically solvable. But, a quick glance at the community page and sojourn into the discord lead me to believe that it's mostly weeby-anime-boob-monsters and the like. Which is, I guess, a WORLD OF HORROR in its own way.Still, this is worth checking out if the screenshots interest you! A 1-bit mashup of 1980s Japan, Junji Ito, and eldritch horror is a cool concept!

_childDocuments_.review: is a very unique horror game with its style of gameplay, it’s a rogue-like with a choose-your-own-adventure style. The game also takes inspiration from  work and the  as well and blends them together into a very nice horror game with some interesting ideas.I’ll be handling this review in a unique way because the story and the gameplay are tied together. The old gods have reawakened, the world is in a spiraling mess, in hospitals, abandoned classrooms, quiet apartments, and dark forests. Strange events have been occurring and it’s up to you to solve these cases to try and prevent the inevitable.You can play as 14 different characters and each character has a unique story to them and different mysteries for you to solve. Though, the characters themselves don’t have any sort of development to them. Although to be fair, I don’t think that was the intention of the game fully, as I believe they wanted to focus more on the atmosphere of the game.However, to unlock certain characters, you need to get certain achievements in the game to get them. Which may require you to do a few runs on certain things because the game randomly generates what happens for certain events. Although even with all that, it should be possible to get them even with what I just said.Now the game has three specific phases to it, the , and the .  phase will be at your house where you can do things, like take a bath, go to the lighthouse, or choose your next mystery. That’s where the  begins, and you are free to select the location to go to. The game does have a set path that it recommends you go to but you are free to choose wherever you want to go to. The game has these random events that will determine what the player does and what kind of effect they get. Each location you go to has a certain event associated with it and an option for you to choose from. To solve cases you will need to find certain clues and to get these clues, you will need to resolve a certain event that the game gives you.The events as a whole are random and there are certain scenarios where the ending is obvious, it’s still random on what the game gives you. Then there is combat, the game is turned-based, and you have offensive, defensive, support, and spiritual abilities. All of these actions are arranged in a 9x9 grid and some abilities are only available for certain encounters. You will need to prepare a sequence of attacks and click the  button for the game to do the actions that you want.You have at least 200 time units to use on certain actions and each action will use a certain amount. Once your sequence is over, the enemy can then attack you, you can reduce the damage you receive by using defensive actions. You can also cast spells and use throwing items, but they are not tied to the action sequence or the time unit. So you are free to cast as many spells or use as many throwing items as you want.All of these actions have some sort of mathematics to them but that is a whole other thing to explain in this review and would take way too long for it to do that. Once combat is over, you will gain experience points, and some enemies will give you certain items. You can use the experience you get to level up certain stats. Some enemies can also alter certain actions for you, like ghosts for example. Where your attacks won’t be able to hurt them unless you are playing as certain characters as they can or by hurting them in another manner.When leveling up, you can select one perk from three, there are generic perks that are available for all characters in the game. However, there are also character-exclusive perks that you can also select for a certain character. Each character has three or four perks unless you are playing as , who has six unique perks to him.There is a ton that  has to offer but I just can’t explain everything that the game has. Although there are two issues that I do want to address with the game, the game can get quite difficult on its RNG. Now this is a minor issue as some people may enjoy the complete randomness that the game has to offer. Although with that said, there are just some things that the game will throw at you that can completely kill the run so be careful.The UI that the game has is ok, I do think it’s a little cluttered as there is so much on the screen to click and such. This is also another minor issue but just a little something that got to me in some ways.Although the issue I want to talk about mainly is the developer of this game, they have been known to say things and then just disappear. Now you may have known I said there were achievements earlier in the game, well there are no  achievements, but they were promised that they would be in the game. There was supposed to be an update in March for this game, but March has come and gone and we are in the mid to late month of August at the time of this review. _childDocuments_.review: is an early access rogue-like turn-based RPG horror game. As the title suggests, game uses both Ito's and Lovecraft's style of horror so you can be sure to see lot of eldritch enemies as well as Ito's typical bodyhorror. Every single playthrough starts by you choosing an eldritch god, who will negatively modify your experience. Your task is to solve randomly chosen 5 mysteries to get keys to unlock a lighthouse, which serves as a final climb to stop the summoning of the said god. So let's dive into the depths of hell and figure out what the hell is going on here together. has big potential when it comes to its gameplay style. There are two major aspects to the game and that is the combat and the actual story elements driven by decision making. First lets focus on the combat, which is a turn-based RPG with an interesting twist on it. You do not get one action per turn but you get 200 action points (AP), which you can divide into your actions, such as attacks, defense, heal and escape and in case of ethereal enemies, to pray them away. That on its own such amazing, however many times you will find yourself using the same combination of 2 options which you will repeat, successfully vanquishing even tougher opponents. Moreover, I mentioned praying to defeat enemies which do not have physical form. This works in a way that you have to choose a combination of 4 elements, consisting of bowing and clapping. You submit your action and game shows you how many correct positions you got. However, this process is so long and boring that you will find yourself running away from these enemies most of the time.Second thing I mentioned is the story driven by player made decisions. This is done by multiple bottom prompts appearing in a text box which allow to you choose multiple options either decided by a typical Dungeons and Dragons D20 skillcheck modified by your skill stat or by you having the necessary item to open the locked option. The biggest crux of this system comes that it hurts the replayability of the game as the first experience of each text box is unique and even scary, however on your 20th run, you just blast through the options as you care only for the results. With the two bigger aspects out of way, lets focus on the minor details considering gameplay as they aid or hinder the overall experience. Your character has regular RPG stats such as strength, dexterity, charisma, intelligence, luck and unique stat funds. These modify the chances of success rolls, hitting, recruiting allies, strength obviously mostly modifies the damage dealt and funds represent the amount of money you have. On top of that, you have two "health point" stats; reason and stamina. If either of those depletes, it is game over for the said, which adds a bit of challenge managing them to stay at high enough numbers, so your next encounter does not end up your last. Final character stat as well as for the world is DOOM which slowly stacks up with most decisions you make and if it reaches 100%, it is once again, game over. In , player gets to explore their hometown, which is represented by several tiles character can move between, allowing them to explore it, thus finding encounters and new events. Moreover, some of the tiles, such as school or seaside allow the player several new options, such as recruiting allies, getting weapons or spells. However, you will often find yourself not going to the places outside of the mystery required locations, unless you are a completionist and want to experience all the possible events.Final aspect that the game has to offer are items and spells. Items are either instant use or equipable ones. They can be divided into weapons, trinkets and usables. There is a huge amount of items in-game, however you will soon often finding yourself not using the most of them, because either you know how to get much better weapon or in case of spell, I personally did not use them alot as they usually cost reason and I had other means of fighting. It has to be mentioned that not using spells did not make it any harder for me to finish the game even on the hardest difficulty.Save the world from eldritch god invading your hometown. That is the story. However, this game is not focused on its overarching narrative. It is the individual mysteries which are written with care, with reference to japanese urban legends and lovecraftian style of writing. The game offers over ten mysteries, which always get randomly chosen at the start of the run in a group of five. As this is the games biggest aspect, it would be unfair to dive into what these mysteries are and the first time experience for each of them is the best possible one. Only thing I can say is that you should get ready for mermaid making janitors, scissor wielding lady, creepy toilet guy and many others.This game has no concrete main character, has no character developement as everything is event tied. Therefore it would be unwise to judge the game on its characters. However, I can mention that the game offers up to 7 different characters you can unlock and play as, each with distinctive beginning stats and equipment, allowing you to get different experience every single time.Visuals for this game is the first thing that caught everyone's attention. The oldschool MS-DOS looking graphics is what makes this game truly special. Not only it is unique and fresh but also it helps the horror aspect as most people can agree that this artstyle is on its own pretty creepy looking. The game looks old yet everything is detailed to the tiniest pixel. The graphic moments are truly gorey and look real, making more squeamish people look away. On top of that, if you are not fun of the black and white look, you can choose your own colour scheme from barrage of options, which is even increased by the choice of either 1-bit or 2-bit colour scheme. And thus, with these possibilites, even the visuals add to each single run feeling just a little bit different.To be honest, I do not remember much about the music. And I played this recently. However that is mostly because the music is there not to be memorable but to create an atmosphere. The music changes based on the situation and the overall tune is also catchy so you do not get eniterly annoyed by it on your 100th run. The 8-bit style of the OST aids the overall oldschool aesthetic of the game and does not ruin the immersion at any point. The sound design is pretty much the same as music, serving mainly for atmosphere creation, except for combat sounds which are usually dull and placeholders to fill in the silence.If you do not want to be sacrificed to our great god C'thulu then YES but let me still ask you three basic questions:1. Do you enjoy Junji Ito's or H.P. Lovecraft's work?2. Are you looking for a unique take on the whole rogue-like genre?3. Do enjoy being weirded out and scared?If you answered YES to any of these questions, then go away and throw the money at the eldritch gods.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm reviewing this game while it's still in Early Access, which means it's still a little rough around the edges.  I haven't run into any major bugs yet, mostly just fine-tuning issues.  It could use a good proofreading, but that's probably not high on the developer's priority list right now.  As of today, mod support has still not been implemented.In short, this game is fantastic.  I don't think the price would be too high even if mods weren't in the works.  There's a ton of replayability in the base game already, and my impression is that there will be a lot more content added to that as well.The graphical style is based on the low-resolution, black-and-white visuals of 1980s-90s Macintosh games.  It really sets the mood; there's nothing bright and colorful about it, even if you set it to a palette that uses bright colors.  I have a lot of respect for anyone who can create recognizable visuals in this style, let alone something that is actually interesting to look at... which this game definitely is.  Sound and music are atmospheric and pretty simple, which meshes with the graphics perfectly.  There are no cheesy voice samples of an actor screaming in terror; you have to imagine that for yourself.Which is kind of the point.  The source material this game draws on is cosmic horror, a genre that heavily relies on the reader/viewer/player to scare themselves with their own imagination.  Less is more here, and while World of Horror obviously shows you more than, say, a short story would, it doesn't dish out so much visual or auditory horror that you're prevented from giving yourself the creeps.Gameplay is fairly simplistic, which is reminiscent of the old Mac games it pays tribute to.  It's all mouse-clicks.  But there's enough variety in the style of each section of the game, and its systems are sufficiently deep, that it doesn't feel superficial at all.  There's a random element that means every playthrough will be totally different from the last (although you will see the same scenes and items, etc., pop up frequently; you just won't know if or when a particular thing is coming).Once mod support is finished and folks start putting out their own stories, this game will be an absolute steal and an absolute must-play for horror fans.  If you enjoy the works of Junji Ito and/or H.P. Lovecraft, you should already be playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: ++IT'S PERFECTION! PLEASE BUY IT!++One of the most inventive, fun, and distinctly foreign and recognizable horror games I've ever played.-Pros-* A town full of both jokes and seriously dark tones makes World of Horror both instantly familiar to those who have had their stint in horror media before while being just different and unique enough to make the town of Shiokawa instantly recognizable.* The 7 playable characters are currently all very different in terms of stats and general gameplay.  Aiko for instance I won the game with pretty early on when I didn't quite understand what I was doing, while Kirie took far longer requiring me to explore more of the game to unlock more spells, items and A endings to different quests until I won as her, while Haru required me to overcome a nicotine addiction to be helpful [And by that I mean he smoked over 60 cigs by the time the credits rolled]* Visually the game is insanely impressive.  When just starting off I did get pretty damn scared and while I feel somewhat seasoned there is so many new scares and disturbing looks it can be hard for me to really remember to breathe from time to time.* Stunning musical score.* Fun, inventive writing for both main events and supporting events.  * Unique combat mechanics that make each enemy more interesting and hard to beat.  Eldrich for instance can usually attack both your reasoning and stamina, where as humans can only attack you while ghosts can only attack reason.  Further ghosts can be killed by learning the randomized clap - bow ritual or by severing their ties to the world, while eldritch can be used to learn spells you might not know.  Tons of secret mechanics for both combat and investigation keep it all interesting and tied neatly in a bow.* Game about resource management over RNG.  It's really hard to lose if you keep your resources high, but the game will work hard to put you six feet under.-Negatives-* A small image describing complex math would be nice.Now you may notice the lack of negatives?  It's because this game is so simple it's actually very hard to mark it down for anything.  It's simplicity keeps it fresh, scary, enjoyable and enticing even after you've played a deck back to front more than once.  No one run feels the same, no one discovery ever feels final.  Where a lot of rogue likes fail is a hard focus on RNG to keep you coming back until you eventually win once or twice, World of Horror keeps me coming back because I can get close to the end or die suddenly and still fee like I could do better, learn more or try different things to get the results I want.  This game is bad ass honestly and I can't recommend it enough.EDIT: Just got updated again, it's really quite amazing.EDIT 2: It's released, it's perfection

_childDocuments_.review: While there are some petty gripes to be had with this game, I'm honestly surprised that the review aggregate is not "Overwhelmingly positive". This game is absolutely worth your time. While I really enjoyed this game, I was hesitant to post a review because for a period of about 10 months the dev was AWOL. Now that the dev is back and there's an update coming, I'm prepared to say this is an excellent horror game with a satisfying primary gameplay loop. This is probably the most rewarding roguelike I've ever played to discover more about in order to make each run more successful, with each mystery being unique, and there being random events and encounters to learn. The art, narration, and music are all excellent, and absolutely nail the horror atmosphere. My only complaint with this game is that there isn't enough content to make it as replayable as it needs to be, being a rougelike. However, I have faith that with continual updates it will be endlessly replayable by the time it comes out of early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: -Obviously inspired by You Know Who but still extremely impressive.  The art and designs capture the atmosphere very well and the pixel art adds an extra layer of creepiness.-Music does it's job, creates a great atmosphere with the limitations of the "hardware" and so far hasn't gotten old.-Lots of events, items, combinations, and puzzle solving.  The "roguelike" element isn't immediately apparent when you start out but as you progress more stuff unlocks and your mysteries start to become more complex.  It's almost like a Metroidvania where an item you didn't have when you started playing becomes available and allows you to complete certain events that you couldn't before.  The only downside to that is that you'll be grinding a bit playing the same handful of mysteries to unlock them-Combat is turn based with actions taking up Time. You can stack items, actions, prayers, and other actions as long as it fits into your 200 points of Time.  I've had plenty of moments where the game warned me I would die after my turn played out only to use combinations of items and spells to get myself out of that state and win the fight.  It can also be frustrating to know that you're basically softlocked into dying at a certain point but it hasn't been a dealbreaker.Thoughts:-Most times when you're in an event there is an item on the location's art that you can interact with.  They can be big or small but once you memorize where they are you can reliably pick up items like Painkillers and weapons, and also strategize if you want to spend the stamina/reason necessary to do so.--The scariest part of the game is typically the enemies and injuries you can inflict on yourself for various reasons. There's a good amount of self-harm and you can commit suicide through a variety of options very easily as well, so keep that in mind. -Cons:-Can get grindy without mods, you'll be replaying the same mysteries over and over again until you start to unlock more items and spells that will help you.-I got the feeling I was locked into dying or going insane at certain points and it made me want to just restart the game.  Your health will be low, reason is low, no items to help, or you can't do enough damage, all of those things will let you know you won't be surviving more than a handful more turnsThis has been my go-to game to chill out with at the end of the night.  I've gotten my money's worth and I'm excited to see what comes next!

_childDocuments_.review: Review, Now Updated... Again! Ver. 3I've delayed this review a little bit more than I did the last one. Wherein I did the last review immediately after the Something Evil update came out, I waited a few updates, as well as took more to time to dig into the game more. And in all honesty, the way this is going WOH, might just be GOTY. Aside from basically all of the minor kinks that existed when the game was initially getting updated being gone, the new content has really vitalized a lot of the more flavorless portions of WOH. For one, the combat that used to be a bit of a clunk, while still having a certain jank to it, is a whole lot more interesting now, as well as allowing for various playstyles in combat to exist. The new character that has been added is very interesting and really shakes up the standard formula, while the new mystery is a tad too difficult for a new player if anything. Many minor changes and a bunch of new items, a proper modding scene that'll reach the Steam Workshop eventually. Overall WOH is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece, and you would be doing yourself a massive disservice by not at the very least trying it out. It is a little janky here and there, but by god is it incredible through and through.Just play the game already and stop reading reviews. You know it's damn good.

_childDocuments_.review: Updating this review for a second time because, thankfully, the dev did *not* abandon the game. They did go quiet for a while and had some content removed while they were away, which is of course very scary and why I had given it a negative at the time, but they ended up coming back a little over a year after being away and seem to be back in the groove.Yea if you're looking at the screenshots and think you're interested, you'll probably like this game. It's a fun little retro romp through classic horror inspired stories, events, and imagery. OST gets just slightly repetitive as time goes on, but it's not bad in of itself. Base game, there's not *too* much to do here. You'll probably exhaust all content within 20-30 hours, which is pretty low for a roguelite. However, the game hasn't fully released yet, and modding support is widely available and easy to install if you just look for it a bit (the game has a Discord and the modding community takes up a huge chunk of it). From what I played over a year ago, it's actually some high quality enjoyable stuff that fits right in, and of course it's only grown since.I just hope the surprise hiatus the dev took didn't stunt the growth of this game too hard. When it released into early access last year, it generated quite a bit of hype and momentum for what it was. I do think this game deserves attention. I also think it's worth the 15 dollars Panstasz asks for.

_childDocuments_.review: Heavily recommend this game. Dripping with style. Wonderful gameplay loop that keeps me coming back.Mysteries last about half an hour, So it's a great game to pop on for a bit, before doing something else.This is being developed by ONE SINGLE PERSON, so it doesn't update frequently. _childDocuments_.review: World of Horror is a misunderstood game, many people expect a highly cinematic or over the top experience but are then scared by the complexity of the controls or the lack of jump-scares. (a good thing in my opinion.) This is highly inspired by many works such as Junji Ito and Lovecraft as well, and it has pacing much like one of those stories, where it starts out normal before ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan and suddenly there's a mind control ramen monster and a dog that sells you steak knives so you can kill cultists.The gameplay is very reminiscent of older D&D style DOS games and the 2-3 bit pixel art is like that from one too, its a very cool experience, the re-playability is great and the mini-stores are fun. If you want to spend like 30-40 minutes knocking out a couple of short horror stories while passing the time, this game is great for that! A lot of the horror comes from the concepts, stories, and the art which is how psychological horror should work, rather than a lot of games putting you in a chase sequence where the punishment is a jump-scare and restarting the level, World of Horror slowly chips away at your characters and watches them slowly go insane as they investigate case after case of the apocalypse.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: I can understand that the character you are playing as is under the effects of eldritch magic and that unsettling things are magnified and cause damage to your sanity. Two examples.A. I was exploring a mansion when a pickpocket bumped into me and tried to steal something from my purse. when i caught him it said he "dissapeared into the croud" or something like that.What the ♥♥♥♥ are you talking about? A man walked up to me in a mansion and basically manhandled me and then dissapeared in to a crowd? A crowd? In a mansion? Completely absurd.B. I was exploring the forest in a village and my character lost 2 reason because they became stressed out over having to avoid looking at all the mirrors??? In a forest?I can deal with having to play as a character that is effectively a coward that gets scared by someone smiling at them funny. But if I am going to play as someone that is actually weaker then I am in real life, you had better not break my immersion.

_childDocuments_.review: Here are my thoughts on the game so far:1. Though it is in Early Access, it's base game seems fleshed out (in both of the meaning).2. It is been constantly being worked on by the Developers on the game ( and the modding community). So bug fixes and patch are being work on.3. You will die a lot (from being eaten by an ancient Spider, to ending up in the lonney bin), though you may survive and fend off the ancient horrors.4. It's a 2bit game (which make even the most potato computer be able to play it). 5. It capture the feel of Japanese Horror mixed with Lovecraftian horror. Though it feels like there are more callouts to Junji Ito works than other works (that not a bad thing though).6. Each run is different, sometimes it's just brutally hard or overwhelming easy. Though there is a path forward usually forward, getting some lucky break are few if any7.To get the full experience, you have to unlock achivements which range from being killed to just beating a campaign with a character, which in my option worth playing multiple times ( the dog one was by far the best)8. Modders are making new events for the game, though you have to download them and install it into the game file, but it is worth the time and effort, ( it would save time if there was workshop compactity though).In overall option, It's worth the 15 dollars for the base game alone, it will be worth more when new mysteries and events are offically made and modders can put it's events onto the steam workshop

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for everyone. Assuming you think this is the game for you, you may be second guessing your purchase as you start it up and are met with a very simplistic and jarring style of 1-bit graphics and music with text-based style RPG game play. You may think at this point (like I did) that this game looked better on the store page then it does actually playing out in front of you. However when you turn out the lights and play through a few of the creepily disturbing, body horror filled investigations you may realize then what it is that makes this game so interesting. combining disturbing imagery inspired from Junji Ito and eldritch horror of H.P Lovecraft this game will give you the feeling of being a P.I in a Japanese town doomed to tear itself apart unless you can do something about it. The decisions you make along the way can seriously help or hinder your investigation, each having multiple endings for you to discover. You can also rest assured that with a fair amount of encounters that previously completed investigations will maintain their freshness as the game finds more ways to kill, injure, and curse you along the way. I can confidently suggest that if you are interested in the premise of this game that you will like it, but it may take a bit of playing for it to fully immerse you in its game play. When you do though, why dont you go find out why Kana is being such a snoop.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun horror game that doesn't rely on jumpscares to deliver in the horror department. The number of mysteries to solve is not too many, considering it's still in early access, but there is mod support (soon, as of this writing) for custom event triggers that the community will definitely deliver on.The base gameplay is simple, just read and click accordingly. If you delve deep into how the mechanics interact with each other, it can get a bit complicated, but very rewarding when you do so. The musical score is absolutely stellar, it helps immerse you in the atmosphere of the game and also enhances the horror aspect of the game.Replay factor is there, as there are many mysteries to play and many endings for each to find as well as unlockable characters and backstories and achievements to get. At such an affordable price, a highly recommend this game for literally everything it is and will be after early access.

_childDocuments_.review: EARLY ACCESS WARNING: It's still a bit glitchy and unpolished at this point, so hold off if typos and the occasional crash are a dealbreaker for you.It's exactly what I was hoping. It's creepy, unique, and fun, and packed with lots of strange things to see and do. The atmosphere is top notch. The gameplay is fairly simple but the developer has found ways of adding lots of variety and surprises within the framework. It should be noted that this is NOT a roguelite. There are some of the same trappings, permadeath and some randomization, but the main story campaigns are handcrafted and unchanging.Highly recommended if you like spooky mysteries and Junji Ito.

Now I don't need friends around to play it!Jokes aside, pretty cool TTRPG influenced survival horror game. Gameplay consists of choosing the correct location to investigate to solve a mystery, dealing with random events, and occasional turn based combat. Success mostly comes down to luck and classic dungeon crawl resource management / decision making.It's a little unpolished as you'd expect from a one man dev taking on an ambitious concept, but it's unique, charming, and atmospheric enough that I find it hard to mind.I will probably steal a good few ideas from this for the next few TTRPG scenarios I GM.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't do reviews for games often, but World of Horror is one of the best rogue-lites there is. it oozes with style and charm and wears its inspirations on its sleeves. Not to mention the game allows for loads of build possibilities with its characters along with most unlock-able characters having their own mechanics to spice up the game. i'm sitting here at my computer at midnight est on October 19th waiting for the 1.0 update to finally drop and unleash upon this unworthy mind the new mysteries, events, characters and gods. i hope that the success of this game encourages Panstasz to continue making content for the game post this 1.0 update or even work on a sequel as his busy schedule as a dentists allows it.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited after full release*This game is a unique gem for it's unique horror writing, style, and strong replayability.The art and writing carries the experience, character and stat elements fall to the wayside. The way the core gameplay works is not overtly explained but it's intuitive enough to figure out.What I don't like it for is its punishing nature: without mixing words, the game is an RNG fest, creating an issue where most of the time you are only presented with bad and worse options. This adds up quickly and can kill runs slowly, this not always being obvious until a bad roll does you in. With smart play and an overarching plan these issues can be mitigated, but in the end, chance is the antagonist of the game and its enjoyability.The sound matches the style, but it's quite a pain to listen to for a period of time due to the more crunchy, rough, old-school audio. Art's fantastic and haunting, clearly inspired by classics of horror manga and Junji Ito, and I'd say that it's worth playing just to see what surprises it may hold for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Something about the MS DOS 1-bit art really unnerves me. The art and music are fantastic, and there were a couple instances while solving a few of the mysteries that genuinely freaked me out. World of Horror is incredible at building atmosphere and the modular nature of the game means that no two playthroughs will be exactly alike. It's structured like a traditional tabletop boardgame in a way (obviously taking a lot of influence from games like Arkham Horror and Eldritch Horror) in that the random events you encounter are drawn from a deck of "cards" to drive the action, which is important because the main stories of the mystery are kind of vague. The game gives you some flavor text to describe the steps your character is taking to solve the mystery, but encourages you to use your imagination to fill in the blanks. Sometimes my character will stumble onto a terrifying monster and then the game will just tell me that I solved the mystery somehow. Some of the mysteries feel like a Junji Ito story is happening offscreen, and my character is just some shmuck who wandered into the last panel of the manga. I have had a great time with the game so far. That said, now that I've completed a few runs, I feel like I got basically all the game has to offer. I've gotten at least one ending in all the basegame mysteries, and now I am just hungry for more. There are also some very clear optimal strategies to win, and the endgame is very anti-climactic. I'm hoping future updates add more mysteries and fix some of the balance issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Complete rewrite (10/20/2023)It hurts to have to make this update, because I was hoping there'd be some manner of gameplay addition in the full release to make runs less homogeneous, I was hoping it would be finished and be worth the money I paid and the money you, a potential customer, would pay. The gameplay is still a dry, heavily RNG reliant chore which, when the novelty of unlocking exactly one or two new mysteries in an achievement wears off, will amount to endlessly just grinding out runs for diminishing returns. Barely anything other than the few unlockable mysteries and the couple characters you can unlock change anything for further runs, you will still be hoping RNG gives you the events to get top quality equipment, unless you're doing some obtuse secret, your choices in investigations will not matter, and the game will just hand you event after event that boosts doom or lowers your health/sanity without at least doing you the courtesy of throwing an arbitrary stat check.The concept of a Junji Ito inspired title is phenomenal, wasting it on a genre that bloats playtime counts and eschews any form of proper writing in most cases is just bogus.If you must get this, do it at a discount, no less than 75% is my recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the game would've been better off as an episodic point & click puzzle game rather than a rogue-like RPG. The mysteries feel novel at first but given the rogue-like nature the novelty wears off very quickly and what you are left with is a rather poor RPG experience. After a short while, you know pretty much all the stories and you just start to rapidly click your way from event to event.The music and art are superb though and if you play the game at night while the track "Forest Mystery" is playing it can be a thrilling experience for a short while. I am not sure if I can suggest the game based on its gameplay but it is not too expensive for a few hours of entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. The game is about you investigating 5 random mysteries (most of them have multiple endings and this contributes to the replayability) to stop an eldritch god within a time limit (which in the game is presented as "Doom"), The god matters as it will give you gameplay modifiers that will affect your strategy.Throughout the game you can cast spells, talk to people, interact with both the environment and people before you lose your mind (or you die from your injuries which are represented by reason and stamina respectively.  The gameplay is a bit difficult but after some time getting used to you'll get around it. Excels in atmosphere and the art despite being in 2 or 1 bit (depends on your options) is beautiful. Writing is top notch and hits the nail of being Junji Ito esk as well as Lovecaftian at the same time. Finished my first run just now and I would definitely recommend it as long as you know that this game is pretty unforgiving and isn't as straight forward as it implies to be.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: My only real problem i have with this game is that some of the random events can really take you out of the immersion. Such as when i was tasked to break into an abandoned haunted mansion. I had to first figure out its location and the necessary tools to break into the second floor. The atmosphere is tense, the halls are silent as a cold breeze flows from inside the house. Only to have a random stranger pickpocket me and disappear into the "crowd"... Like WHat? my guy is apparently throwing a party and no invites. This game thrives through it's story telling, so it's moments like these that can be somewhat disappointing. This should be an easy fix simply by not allowing certain events to occur at select locations. i say should as i have no idea the actual difficulties of creating a game. This game is in EARLY ACCESS so i know things are bound to change. Otherwise this was a very enjoyable experience with great little call outs to other artists and horror movies like The Autopsy of Jane Doe. Eager to see the future potential of this haunting experience :)

_childDocuments_.review: Play it. It's a fun time.Update: 8/24/2023.I've been playing this game for at lest 2+ years, and have heard about it for longer than that. I can say, beyond a shadow of a doubt, this is the best game in this genre. It perfectly encapsulates a Mid-to-late 80's PC RPG to a T, just with better graphics. Yes, the RNG is not on your side, did you expect to face down Eldritch horrors and win easily? This game is designed to humble you, and it does that exceptionally. Yes, there are bugs, and I would expect that with this being seemingly almost done entirely by one person. I also expect most of those bugs to get ironed out post launch. I honestly thought the game to be dead a while back, but then updates kept coming, and I kept returning.Don't listen to the naysayers, this game is fantastic, and well worth your time and money. Sure, wait for a sale if you want, just like any other game, but don't think you're getting ripped off in any way. You're getting exactly what is advertised, and what you payed for. Nothing less.

_childDocuments_.review: At its core this is a resource-management game, as you've probably noted. The course of play is basically that the player picks a PC with particular stats that determine success at in-game events (including combat), then is presented with five mysteries to solve before running out of HP, Reason ("SAN" for TTHRPG players) or "Doom" (time, progress of the elder god who will devour the world). Generally, progress through the mysteries involves serially visiting various locations throughout the gameworld a certain number of times, while appropriately navigating the random game events (including combat encounters) that pop up with each investigative step.I'm optimistic about how this game will turn out. At present, what it's got going for it is strong atmosphere, good visuals and writing that really carry home the 80s horror manga theme, and engaging play. As it stands (0.9.17, writing on 5 Nov 2020), the inconsistency between some of the mysteries seems to point to some of them being more finished than others. For example, the introductory "Scissors" mystery involves specifically visiting particular locations inside the School, the "Vigil" mystery involves visiting specific rooms in the Mansion, the "Festival" mystery uses a completely different set of investigation locations, and the "Mermaid" mystery involves visiting a separate alternative school location; however, in many mysteries progressing the mystery simply involves resolving a number of random events that are not thematically related to the specific mystery. This tends to make you immediately conscious of the fact that gameplay is fundamentally just learning to navigate the individual random game events.There are a few items that, as of this writing, appear to be sort of unfinished plot threads .Because this game is in beta, and because games like this are all fundamentally just RNG hidden under thematic events, I think it's worth taking a look at. It's retained its replay value for me over dozens of plays (as a roguelike, it tends to kill me about four to six times an hour). It's also a good choice if you have nostalgia for the Apple IIe.

_childDocuments_.review: Turned-based Japanese Lovecraftian adventure-horror rougelike mixed with the works of Junji Ito and Japanese folklore, World of Horror rewards creativity, exploration, and dealing with the unexpected. _childDocuments_.review: As anyone can tell even from a cursory glance at the store page, the vibes on this game are without a doubt its strongest selling point. Art's good, writing's good, and I even feel that all the indie game jank (misspellings, text running slightly off-screen, some events not working exactly as you think they're intended) add to the feel that you're playing some sort of hastily translated Japanese arcade game from another dimension. The only question is, seeing as we're dealing with an early access game here: Does everything else suck? I'd say your mileage may vary.Being a rogue-like shapes World of Horror's story into a chaotic mish-mash of horror vignettes that get stuck together to create a run. These small events are really good the first time through, but of course, the same few will wear out their welcome soon enough. There is a lot of content to unlock which, in my opinion, gives the game just enough mechanical variation and extra events to actually keep it fun even after seeing everything, but the issue here is that the achievements required to access a lot of it is, let's say, esoteric at best. We can all agree it's normally best to experience games like these without knowing much about it beforehand, but there's only so much you can figure out in here without a guide (just like the old games it's styled after, nice?). Sure you might beat the game a couple times and maybe unlock one or two new characters, but you'll also be missing out on a lot of the cool interactions you can find, not just the event and character unlocks. If you're alright with being a wiki gamer for a few hours (which isn't inherently bad) once you feel like you need to unlock the other half of the game, then go for it, especially if this genre of horror is your thing.

I have a few gripes with it:- There doesn't seem to be a way to fast play, which you want when you've read all the endings to a particular mystery- The interface is a bit... obtuse? Like I get what they're going for, that vintage look that Obra Dinn went for the 1/2bit pixel style. _childDocuments_.review: World of Horror is an absolute treat for those even vaguely interested in its namesake genre. It's Ito-Lovecraftian aesthetic is helped greatly along by the fantastic DOS-esque art style and adaptive music. Even with, or especially due to its limited graphics, each encounter brings another unique horror with the player both fearing for their life and dreading what could've caused their fate. Being built for multiple playthroughs, its rather unavoidable that the game becomes less scary with repeat playthroughs. But, in my opinion, that's when the focus shifts. You slowly go from a scared victim of unknowable terrors to a veteran fighting tooth and nail against an evil that dares intrude on your home. As you also unlock more characters, features, and locations while playing, the game manages to keep itself fresh even after hours-long sessions.There are a few criticisms to be had, though, mostly due to its early access nature. While kept intentionally vague at times, the obfuscation of features can prove to be more frustrating than anything at times, such as unclear instructions regarding progression and stats. This even extends to the menus as, while charming, they are easy to get lost in. Two separate toggles for aspect ratio and fullscreen, for example, could be easily merged into one. There's also a very explicit lack of a "go back" or "undo" button, most notably in the scenario selection process. Also, while there is an option to skip the beginning cutscene each playthrough, there doesn't seem to be a corresponding one for game tutorials for things such as map navigation and mystery selection. None of these ruin the game by any means, but would save a lot of time if addressed. Some other more specific issues and suggestions are:-The usage of some items, like the crowbar in the Mermaids case, being unclear or broken-No undo option in the battle screen, so you have to clear the board each time-Unclear previews leave you guessing how much time you have left+Maybe include more failstates or boss powerups, such as eating the ramen without inspecting it or messing up the scissor ritual+Hints on the TV, or a few more uses for radio signal+Gossip that helps with other casesOverall, this is a game I can't wait to see more of, and has the potential to be unforgettable. If my dreams over the past few days have anything to say, it certainly is for me.

_childDocuments_.review: World of Horror is basically the Fantasy Flight board game Arkham Horror but as a point-and-click adventure/turned-based lite-rpg through a 1980s horror manage presentation.The player is assigned a character based on the game mode the pick at the beginning: a one-and-done tutorial-like mission, a more standard 5-mystery game and a more randomized mystery game.  The mysteries themselves once selected involve selecting locations to visit.  And visiting these locations is very much like drawing a random card from a location deck.  Some sort of even occurs sometimes giving options to the players, sometimes a random combat and sometimes just happens.  But the player has to continue going through these events to collect clues and/or unravel the mystery.  To aid the player character, they sometimes gain items or can buy them with any funds they may have at stores at certain locations.  These items include weapons and other equipped gear, clues that offer more information as well as one-time use times to maintain or boost the player characters stats.  In addition, the game also allows the player character to recruit allies.  Which can be used in combat, but not nearly as effectually as most turned-based rpgs.  They are just another type attack, often weaker than what the player character can do themselves.  But they sometimes have skills the player character doesn't and may offer some advice.  If that was not enough, the player can learn and use spells.  Which also tend to one-use and often cost the player character valuable Reason.And maintaining the player character's Stamina and Reason is much of where the game play is found.  Stamina being the hit point/health of the character and when reduced to zero is dead.  While Reason is the character's sanity, and as it drops the screen will often start to glitch out.  If Reason drops to zero, the player character is insane and probably going to the Asylum for as long as the world has left.The mysteries themselves are often about visiting locations enough to trigger the ending.  Though they often contain light puzzle elements.  There's a bit of randomness (like drawing from a card deck in a board game) to going through mystery.  And the game very much plays like a 1980s point-and-click/rpg video game in that respect.  Which isn't a bad thing, just that World of Horror is retro in more than graphics and presentation.Graphically, I greatly enjoy the 1980s horror manga aesthetics.  However, be warned that the trailer has fair more animation than the actual game does most of the time.  Which is fine, since the game is going for a manga and not an anime.  And low bit computer manga at that.  I think the presentation gives World of Horror a lot personality.  It's what drew me in, but I stayed for the retro pseudo-board game player.  The sound is the expected chip tune music that one would expect.  A little limited in scope but serviceable for a small indy game such as this.World of Horror isn't likely to be for everyone.  I'd just suggest watching a video on how the board game of Arkham Horror is played or is being played to get a good understanding of what a player is going to get with World of Horror.  If that board game turned point-and-click adventure/turned-based rpg still sounds fun, I think you will find World of Horror very fun.  But if you are expecting something like 'The Uninvited" but as a Lovecraft manga, you might be disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game on and off pretty much since it began early access.The pace of updates and flow of content was never that great but I have always loved this game. Its rare for me to enjoy a horror game because I'm usually too much of a wuss to get through them, but I World of Horror does two things. First, there's only a handful of jump-scares. World of Horror derives its tense more atmospheric style of horror from the ever ticking DOOM metre, a gauge that slowly fills as your run progresses. Every mystery you solve brings you closer to confronting the forces that seek to invade your world, but it also adds to the DOOM metre. There is no rest, no escape. The only way out is forward.Second, it's a lot better balanced than most rogue likes. I can consistently reach the final stretch of the game just by playing smart, I never had to learn any exploits or busted item/character combinations. Just being good and having basic reading comprehension is enough to win at least on the lower difficulties. It's a nice change from the typical rogue like standard of letting you get right to the end only to drop a bag of anvils on your ♥♥♥♥ and crush your hopes of winning at the eleventh hour. Ultimately, the game play and atmosphere are great. But they're only half the equation in a good horror.  Sound design is where the game falters just a bit, what's here is good but there's not enough music overall. Just a handful of admittedly awesome tracks. But the visuals, my god those visuals.I don't think I've ever felt so much pants pissing terror looking at some monochrome pixels before. I know the art is Junji Ito inspired, and can we just take a second to appreciate that? Someone learned to replicate one of the most detailed manga art styles ever, in MS Paint. There's also a good few things that *aren't* Ito inspired but everything blends together very well. It's the mark of a truly talented artist to both show and hide their inspirations with every piece they do. Overall, one of the best horror games on Steam. If you're at all a fan of tense, slow build eldritch horror you owe it to yourself to try this.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game after a very good friend started talking it up in our Discord server. Can't get enough of it so far! Makes it obvious that World of Horror is built on passion. Of course, with all the impressive graphics having been done more or less by one person in MS Paint, it would have to be. Only major flaw I can think of is that there are a lot of grammar errors in the English text, but it's honestly not that big of a deal. The writing is still clear and easy to understand--not something worth nitpicking over, as it really doesn't detract from the quality of gameplay. The only reason I mention it at all is probably because I edit writing for a living, heheh. TL;DR: Extremely quality and worth your time, especially if you're familiar with Junji Ito's work. Very well done! Super excited for more content!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun horror experience that is simple in its design and big on story! World of Horror uses the trappings of classic horror and Japanese horror (with similar themes to Juni Ito's works) to craft a game that uses old school retro graphics to its advantage. While this game is in Early Access, in its current state, it could be sold as is. The main game-play loop, currently, is solve five mysteries to open a ominous lighthouse and stop an eldritch horror from manifesting. Can your body and mind, or even the world itself, withstand the trials? Those who play point and clicks may be familiar with some of the UI  choices. You investigate locations and a random encounter happens. There's a very board game style feel to things; for example Items are cards that you "flip" to resolve them. As a board game fan I love stuff like this. The custom mode expands on this by letting you unlock card packs to vary up game playing.One thing that might put people off on this game is pretty much all of the item, character, and content unlocks are behind achievements. Most are simple "complete game as X character" "complete game with X background" ect. However some of the more obtuse ones can be frustrating, especially when it's behind a unique combat action during a specific mystery with several specific items equip. For example,  Be prepared to achievement hunt if you want the most out of game play.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely more of a "meh" review than a negative oneIt's a simple, RNG-based RPG built out of modular randomized short stories and events. And the pool of events and stories is much too small for how short playthroughs tend to be even if you win, so there's a lot of redundant clicking through stuff you've seen a dozen times already.I don't remember what I paid for it years ago, but I'd say ~$10 is fair.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Very nice mix of cosmic horrors FEELS from ya boi HP Lovecraft, while being faithful to japanese mythology, urban legends and visual grotesque style of one and only Junji Ito.It's a pretty decent rogue-like detective game, where you have to complete the mystery at hand without losing your mind or health. Multiple endings to each story give you an option to either run through the same route as quickly as possible, or take your chances in exploring different outcomes to your actions. But with the ticking Doom clock above your head at all times you are gently pushed to action. The never-ending balancing act feels pretty great here, and playthrough customizations will either create a smooth sailing or, in my case, an insta death. And it was the most numbingly funny experience i had with the game so far.++++If you're a big fan of body horror and japanese aesthetic - great catchMany things to unlock, it kinda scratches the same itch Binding of Isaac does. To an extent. Options OPTIONS OPTIONS------At the time of the review it's still in early access, so be mindful... don't alt-tab for too long.still no idea how i managed to die 1 second into my custom run.

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who absolutely loves Junji Ito's work, and also enjoys a bit of eldritch horror every now and then, this game is completely worth the 20 USD price.The quick play sessions are great, only taking around 20 to 30 minutes to complete a run. Most achievements are available on all difficulties, meaning you can unlock a lot of content if you're at any skill level. The game isn't the most story driven, mainly relying on telling short stories through the mysteries instead of a major plot line involving the entire game.The RPG mechanics can be a bit overwhelming at first, but it's easy to get used to it once you experiment a bit. The game can be repetitive after a while, but the wide amount of experimentation available can help solve that issue.The horror elements aren't the scariest I've seen, but they do show the strong inspiration towards Junji Ito. The body horror in this game is absolutely amazing, and the art is beautiful. I've been startled a few times while playing, and still am discovering new scares.Overall, I'd give this game a 9/10. There's room for improvement, but seeing how this game is still being updated with new content, I'm sure it'll become even better than it already is.

_childDocuments_.review: I watched the development of this one for about a year on twitter, and this came out being way better than I originally thought it would be.The art is really great, the soundtrack is amazing, and the gameplay is surprisingly deep despite each action having relatively the same results every time.The only problem I've got is a very VERY slight lack of content, which I kind of expected given that it's a small indie game and it's still just Early Access.  The lack of content isn't even that bad, it's just after a few hours you start to see the same mysteries and investigations over and over.  That said, it looks like there's modding support incoming, so that will certainly fix the issue.There's also a handful of bugs in the game.  Sometimes the music will stop and other times multiple background songs play simultaneously.  There's a particularly annoying bug that sometimes skips combat actions, but it only seems to be certain combinations of actions, so when it happens I just switch the order around a little.Also one REALLY minor gripe is that I was kind of ripped out of the game a little bit when I rescued a character clearly inspired by Duane "The Rock" Johnson from a hospital and had him join my team.  I stopped being mad about it though because he led me to my first successful banishment.Definitely pick it up if you're a long time fan of Junji Ito or roguelike games.  Or if you're on the fence, check back once the modding scene kicks in.

_childDocuments_.review: World of Horror is one of the more unique games I've ever played. World of Horror is a rogue-lite horror game focused on turn-based combat, where you'll go on a series of up to five mysteries as you try to solve what's going on in your local Japanese town. You'll encounter some absolutely terrifying creatures and situations as you try to preserve not just your health throughout the mystery, but also your sanity. If you can live long enough to complete five mysteries, then you can ascend the lighthouse in one last-ditch attempt to defeat the eldritch god that's plaguing your town. I like a lot of things about World of Horror. It features some really creepy and well-written story-telling, with multiple endings to each mystery depending on the actions you take to solve it, meaning there's a lot of replay value. The combat system is simple but still pretty fun, and I probably haven't even used all the different features of it. The art style is also really well-done, I'm always impressed by everything I see on my screen. The art features a significant amount of body horror, with inspiration from the works of Junji Ito and H.P. Lovecraft.Honestly my only two cons that I would say are that a) the dev(s) [it might just be one person I don't know for sure] don't update it super often (not too big of a deal, there's enough content already in the game to get your money's worth), and b) because of the 1-bit art style, frequent screen flashes, and bright white color palette (adjustable in the settings), it can be very harsh on the eyes, so I can usually only play one or two runs before I get a little digital eye strain or a headache. That being said, this game's a solid 8/10, pick it up at full price or on sale if you like unique horror games.
