Combines several elements including old-school text and click adventure games, but it's inspired by the work of Junji Ito so its sense of horror is to that level. _childDocuments_.review: The game system itself is a mixture of J-RPG, point-and-click adventure, and turn-based combat system. Each character has two sets of points representing their health and sanity, when either one reaches to zero, it's game over. ( If you have ever played board game like Arkham Horror, you'll understand the concept.)In the beginning of each run of the game you choose your character, and the Elder God that you will be trying to stop for that particular run.Game phase consists of going home, choose from a list of five quests ( In each run you have to solve five randomly chosen quests to get to the final location to stop the Elder God.). In between the quests you can head home to rest and replenish your health and sanity), and finally face the boss of that particular run.The amount of quests available is quite amazing, I have played five different runs so far and haven't seen too many repeated quests. Each quest has its own unique storyline and interactions. While in quest mode it plays like a hybrid of visual novel and point-and-click adventure. Each event happening in the game gives you two to three options to choose from, of which the game then compare you character's stats (strength, dex, per, etc ) and make a roll. If you succeed, you usually get a item or stats boot that will help you in game. If you fail at the roll, the game can take points away from your health/sanity, or destroys your item/penalizes your character stats.During gameplay, you get experiences. You can upgrade your character's stats each time you level up, during level up you can also choose what skill you want to give to the character you are playing.You can also get NPCs to join you to help you with your quests. Each NPC can have different special abilities that help you during the game.The art style is quite similar to the J-horror manga artist Ito Junji's style.Overall,if you like J-Horror, Lovecraftian genre, turn-based combat system, point-and-click adventure, and visual novel, and retro style graphic, you have to give this gem a try.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: In it's early access state, this game is still somewhat buggy, but also entirely playable. Mostly it seems like there are math errors in the code that make certain modifiers do the opposite of what they are supposed to, or not work at all. Some achievements also seem to be bugged.Other than that, the game absolutely delivers on what is promised. It plays like a perfect mix of an rpg, choose your own adventure book, and a horror manga illustrated by Junji Ito. Even though the gameplay is buggy i feel like it barely takes away from the interactive novel type experience that World of Horror aspires to be. If you enjoy any combination of unique indie games, horror, or anime/manga you are probably going to enjoy World of Horror.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a really hard one to judge.I will go straight to the point. The dev is the problem with this one. The game itself is incredibly promising. Some of the best things I have played from early access. Sadly, after a couple of hours and a couple of replays the cracks start to appear. The product is VERY far from being finished. It needs a lot of time in the oven. This would naturally not be a problem for a game in early access... usually. But WOH has a team of a single person and this person is not the most professional. He went completely off the radar for a year, letting the deadline for release come and pass and we are still waiting for any news about a future update.Its a shame, really. Because the game has potential. Probably having a team with a couple more people would have been better.EDIT: One year later. I decided to come back a revisit this review. Sadly everything I wrote on it is still true, or it has gotten worse. The updates are still coming only once a year and every time with less content. Its sad because this game has so much potential.A good example of the problems with this dev is this: When you go to the "Challenges" section on the main menu, there is a BACK icon missing. Is the only screen from which you cant go back to the main menu from. Its a small thing, but it has been like that for more than a year now. An update came and went and it was not solved. Like that there are dozens of thing. Saving for example, has not worked for more than two years now. Its incredible because one would would think that the dev would use this updates to fix all the problems the game has... but nope.Sadly this is still a thumbs down from me.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's spooky and pretty much delivers on everything it promises in the store page.The art style is pretty cool and the amount of care that went into this game is pretty noticeable. There's a pretty decent amount of mysteries to solve and achievements to unlock (the achievements are all in-game at the moment, but there's around 50 or so?) Those achievements unlock more items to mess around with in-game along with other characters, just overall more stuff to improve your overall enjoyment and increase available outcomes from your choices. I'd say it's pretty easy to sink a good amount of hours into trying to unlock everything. The game rewards you for paying attention to your surroundings, which can sometimes give you the upper hand in a lot of cases that really come down to luck.The only real downside I see in this game is its UI, as it takes a bit of getting used to when you first start the game. You'll spend some time getting used to the menus and looking through everything as a majority of your options are very small buttons you have to mouse over to see what you can do. Once you get used to it however, it feels pretty good. Overall, I suggest trying it out as you can get a good grasp on what the game is all about within a few hours and see if it's worth your time.Also, be careful about all of your choices, there is no "are you sure?" option. That goes for the Reset button on the side when you're in a run.

_childDocuments_.review: But very interesting.It's basically (Junji) Ito-Land the Game. If you like RPGs, roguelites, and eldritch horror, this is the place to be. It needs some polish, but other than that, Panstasz has the base experience of the game already done. And what is done, is good. Frankly, I wish I had discovered this project sooner.When you start the game, you'll likely be overwhelmed by the retro aesthetics and huge, obscure arrangement of things to click on. For some reason, the first recommended playthrough, "Spine-Chilling Story of School Scissors" (digging the alliteration by the way), does not contain the basic tutorial for the game, which was provided to me instead in the second "Extracurricular Activity" playthrough. Odd.Despite this, once you get your foot in the door and get things rolling, you'll be subjected to great things.the grammar, writing, and pacing of the game is a bit odd. Although the writing certainly conveys what it is trying to say, it doesn't feel as though it is conveying the kind of emotion that the devs intend. For example, I believe in the toilet stall mystery when you fight the psycho killer, the text says something like:"You need to get away from this psychopathic man!"Which is technically correct, but seems like far too calm of a statement to establish fear. Also, there are some minor grammatical mistakes and weirdness that could be easily fixed with some proofreading. Hit me up panstasz ;)On a similar note, I feel like the 'mysteries' should be called 'legends', 'urban legends', or something else along those lines, instead. Just my opinion.The game does need polish game-play and writing-wise, but I think the developer is well aware of this. So these aren't really criticisms, so much as they are just the state of things. As of right now, if you buy it you'll be subjected to (what appears to be) the base experience that this game was intended to provide, even if things aren't entirely 'smooth'. There is a bit of jankiness to it, especially story-wise, considering the fact that you just jump from situation to situation.The game's still pretty good as-is. But it needs to be finished. I hope the project isn't abandoned like other early access titles.

_childDocuments_.review: World of Horror, as the name suggests, is a retro-style horror RPG. You play as one of 5 characters (more are unlockable) investigating creepy mysteries in your 1980s Japanese town while simultaneously trying to prevent the awakening of a world-destroying elder god. Also, you purchase items from a dog. The game is a tribute to manga artist Junji Ito (who I wasn't really familiar with), but you don't have to understand the references to enjoy them.Despite being in beta, WoH overall runs pretty well and was almost bug free (With the exception of one run where I exited and then re-entered the game to find my character was a completely different person. I initially thought it was part of the game. That's how weird ♥♥♥♥ gets). My primary complaint is with the item equipping system--I wish the items you had equipped stayed equipped from one mystery to another, even after saving/exiting. Because they all go back into storage, I've had more than one instance where I plunged into a new mystery without anything equipped. Not fun for your first enemy encounter.If you haven't played a ton of older RPGs you might have a little trouble at first, but there is a tutorial option you can return to at any time. Even if you are familiar with the genre you will almost certainly die on your first run--but it's part of the fun! WoH is not meant to be an easy game; I spend most of my time on Initiate difficulty and have yet to even try True Believer. To me the difficulty adds to the replay value--you end up wanting to push yourself more, seeing how long you can survive even as the Doom meter gets higher and higher.Overall, WoH is a ton of fun and I am excited for more horror when Scenario Mode is released!

_childDocuments_.review: World of Horror combines simple but effective roguelike mechanics with an evocative world that perfectly balances campy charm with true unsettling dread. While the interface can take a while to get used to, World of Horror generally does a great job of keeping you immersed its world with distinctive art and well-written, approachable text. The game explores the use of randomised narrative in a relatively unique and compelling way. While you may have a fair amount of repetition in the events you see over extended play, there are always multiple ways to solve any given problem, and exploring these options will provide you with new narrative threads that give you more information about the world and the mystery you are trying to solve.World of Horror feels fresh and is full of lovable elements, I highly recommend checking it out!

_childDocuments_.review: **Some minor -to major spoilers will be in my review!!!  Major spoiler will be warned ahead of time**World of Horror is a wonderful throwback to those old DOS or Macintosh adventure games from the 80s.  It has great visuals and some (very light) roguelite elements , and the game promises the players of horrors of Junji ito-style Japanese horror and Lovecraftian Cosmic horror.  But does it deliver on the premises? I'll give you my take on it.Pros:1.  The visuals are very appropriate, appealing, and unique.  It's a great throwback to the 80s adventure games, and I am a big fan.  A few of the sprites look a little derpy, but it looks great for the most part.2.  The music is unsettling and there's a good variety of it.  There are many self-contained mini-mysteries the player can tackle in any order, and each mystery has its own music, and they were all great!Cons:  (Yes, this is early access, but I hope these problems will be addressed in some form b4 full release)1.  The User interface.  I get that old school games used to have cryptic and vague UI, but it's 2020 and I think we can use some tool tips for some of those micro-sized icons!  Pushing the space bar to highlight all the selectable icons was a great addition, but even THAT feature was not explained and took more digging than necessary for me to find out.  Another poor UI example: myself and a few other streamers had trouble figuring out that the big picture panels on the left side of the level-up screens were actually selectable perks, and some of us just went without choosing any.  Even a left-arrow with "select one" would've made it so much clearer.2.  The combat.  For me, most of the battle simply came down to finding the most optimal combination of prep and light weapon attack to maximize damage.  I only used defensive options when I'm at death's door, and I felt that utilizing defensive option more regularly only prolonged the battle but not necessarily ended up in a better outcome.  The spiritual actions were not explained AT ALL (maybe some full-release bosses require it?) so I just did not mess with it at all. even if there is a way to one-shot enemies with the right combination of bows and chants, why would I bother with this hot or cold mini-game when I can simply slash them down with regular attacks in 2-3 turns RELIABLY?   Lastly, the spells could've been powerful special attacks, but instead of feeling powerful, they are always paired with even bigger drawbacks (ex: gain 2 stamina. LOSE 4 reason!) and they always felt awful to use.  Damage spells were equally useless. They would often deal mediocre damage (2-3) but it would cost 2-3 stamina to use, effectively taking DOUBLE DAMAGE to just deal regular dmg to the enemy.  Essentially, what I'm trying to say is there is only one right way to play (as far as I can tell) and it could've been so much more...3.  The dialogue.  While the core mysteries were interesting and I loved exploring different endings, I couldn't help but feel we have a big missed opportunity in regards to developing side characters or the mystery itself.  The game gives you all these options to talk to people (your neighbor, your classmates, your allies, etc) BUT 99% of the time, they are programmed to either say nothing useful, or something terribly generic ("this town doesn't feel safe anymore", etc )  What if these characters had critical rumors or tips that can help our upcoming mysteries or boss battles in some way, more regularly?  I think the Red-paper blue-paper boss (forgot his name) is the ONLY mystery that actually utilizes some dialogue with NPCs in a meaningful way, and even that felt tacked-on (essentially just avoid 5 dmg to either stamina or reason b4 battle)4.  Some story inconsistencies and contrivancesThere is a sense of an overarching story, a story of a shadowy cabal who are orchestrating all these horrible events from the background, but they are never truly explored (in my playthroughs).  Who are these people that are leaving lighthouse keys in your mailbox? Why you?  The final segments of the game was a letdown too. **ENDGAME SPOILERS AHEAD**It was merely a series of stat and health supply checks, a couple of battles, and a cut to "YOU SAVED THE DAY!....For now...".  I was expecting some epic showdown, and maybe I'll get to use some holy artifact that I might've encountered in my run to make the Eldritch god boss fight end quickly... but nope. No real eldrich encounter.  I just dispell the curse from a black rock and I saved the town.  I will try to do 100% doom run and see if that changes the ending.  Also, How did that girl get stuck behind the upper floors when the lighthouse was locked out with 5 padlocks?  I know I'm nitpicking, but all these small inconsistencies and contrivances really took me out of the immersion.4.  The "Horror"The game is unsettling and I like it, but the horror aspect is not well delivered.  The enemies are unsettling at first, but upon second or third encounter, you are easily jaded.  Even the scary mini events are not even remotely creepy on the 2nd encounter.  I know that this is inevitable, but I feel like tension and horror can be built up in other ways. For example, as you are exploring the mansion in the Household Hell mystery, maybe there is an Ao Oni-like monster chasing you and around as you explore room to room and you have to fight it off or run away... All I'm saying is there are ways to scare you other than shocking visual card, and I would love to see this aspect further explored in the full game or even the sequel.  Kudos to the developer for not over-relying on cheap jumpscares like a certain other 5 Nights at a pizza joint game.IN CONCLUSION:By now you may think I hate this game, but that is furthest from the truth.  I love it, and I am actually going to play it as soon as I publish this.  I complain because I care; I care about what this game could be as a full release game.The core concept, the visual aesthetic, the music, the mysteries, there are many things going for it, but there are also many other things that detract from the experience.  Will update when the full game releases I think? Thanks for reading!!!

_childDocuments_.review: A set of horror mysteries played through in a mix of visual novel and RPG styles, with ample references to the works of Junji Ito and Lovecraft. The game thrives when you are first playing it and constantly discovering new things, finding new ways to solve old problems, and getting new characters and tools to use. However, after awhile, that feeling wears off and you will feel like you are retreading a lot of the same steps in the hopes of bungling through RNG to see that one random event you never saw before or to wrap up an annoying achievement chain.---Critically, the game did not launch "feature complete"; the dev pushed it out the door with many promised features still missing with barely any new content added since the last update months ago, leading me to wonder what they were doing with all that time and EA money. All player progress was wiped without warning, Steam achievements and the Workshop are not present at release, some artwork was swapped out under suspicious circumstances, and many core accessibility and UI options are absent.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun RPG that handles horror in a very aesthetically pleasing format. After strange events have been occurring around your hometown, you attempt to find the root of all the strange happenings of your once peaceful seaside town by solving mysteries. Your character will become twisted and warped by the events though injuries, curses and mental illness under the influence of the old god.Despite a full playthrough not lasting much more than thirty minutes, the game has incredible replayability. You'll be unlocking new characters, each of them with their own stories and stats to change how you go about a playthrough, multiple different endings for the mysteries you'll encounter and different old gods whom have different rules which modify the gameplay even further. The game is certainly worth the asking price in my opinion.However, the developer is very inactive, with an update once taking over a year to release, so keep that in mind before purchasing. Despite this, there is an active modding community on their discord server with custom mysteries, characters and events that should keep you occupied. I certainly would say it's worth your time and money if you can overlook the update irregularity.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I've put a lot more hours into this game, and there's certainly more content than I was aware of, and I believe you learn enough, fast enough, to quickly become capable of winning more frequently, I've said this game is heavily reliant on RNG, though there are ways that are more possible, that can reduce bad RNG, or outright allow for good events to occur as you learn what events affect what, and what items you're carrying play a huge roll in your future success. I was a bit too harsh in criticizing this game's systems but I don't feel the need to change it. Leaving it there shows my genuine first impression, this game has more unlockables than I had thought, more events, enemies, content in general. I heavily look forward to its continued production.The Bad: TLDR: It's short so I want more, RNG feels to heavy AKA doom builds too fast, and the strength of the eldritch gods are different and definitely some are stronger than others. Which isn't good.The games events are pretty heavily reliant on RNG. You can honestly lose very quickly from a few missed hits or bad events. Prep prior to attacking is incredibly strong. It's hardly ever worth it to get greedy as hit chances can drop as low as 40%. You could be having a decent run but go and get a couple bad doom%+ events in a row and all of a sudden you feel incredibly behind forcing you to rush when the game rewards you for being prepared with events that only have good outcomes with a very specific item, that is also RNG to get. Each run still feels fresh as the old gods starting ability decides how you approach the game. But certain negative events you get after completing mysteries feel incredibly strong or incredibly underwhelming. You obviously can't do everything, and you obviously must manage 3 different stats that can equate to game over, Standard runs aren't too long and you can always instant restart with Q if you feel like a run is dead on the water either from bad combat or your own personal incompetence. The game also doesn't do a great job explaining things, and I don't mean the eldritch horrors which being vague and eerie is what makes it satisfying to slowly make your way to completion. But I feel like mysteries don't do a good enough job of alluding to the eldritch god and are instead just >Bad thing you either solve or fail to solve gets done>Has nothing to do with the god itself, just more doom and bad effects should you failThe game is rogue like, though I personally think it would highly benefit from having perks to completion that can affect the next run in some way, doesn't need to be positive, just optional.Doom : Always obtained when investigating and from events. Start at 0%, reach 100% and you loseStamina : HPReason : SanityAll 3 can drop either at the same time or one or the other depending on events and enemies. Both of which result in a game over if you reach 0. Or in Doom's case 100Gods: The eldritch gods are not equal, as I stated, doom builds up quickly, and very few things successfully lower doom and typically have strong negative side effects should you fail. But combat is best to end quickly or to avoid completely, the exp you get is laughable VS the stamina and reason loss. One gods starting ability is you're unable to run from combat. Doom increases if you run, you'll probably NEVER run from combat unless doom is low early game and you got hit one too many times without prepping attacks properly. While another god increases the doom you receive from resting at home, which is a great way to recover stamina and reason. The good: TLDR: The aesthetic is obviously incredible, if you're a fan of the eldritch horrors of hopelessness, apathy, and despair. You're in the right place, the plot is simple but the mysteries are satisfying.The aesthetic of this game is obviously amazing, I say obvious because if you're interested in the looks, it delivers exactly as you see, with lots of little things that make this game so creepy for me. I'm not good with horror but I'm willing to put up with it for how good this game is so far. The atmosphere it sets no matter what you do is incredible, whether it's something positive or negative in terms of impact to your current run, it all feels very natural and keeps the hopeless tone strong.While I criticized the lack of connection between the crimes and the summoning of the gods, I do enjoy both individually, the crimes themselves tell interesting stories and are filled with that sweet sweet eldritch horror. The gods themselves look great and the effects they have outside of their base are randomized so you can never predict what you'll get. Which in this case I think is good to keep the replay value high.The Gameplay itself: Turn based combat where you're given 200 action points and each action you make, such as attacking, dodging, or preparing to attack to raise the hit chance, each cost portions of these points. Enemies show you exactly what they do upon attacking, whether they deal Stamina, or Reason, or they raise doom with each combat turn their attack succeeds. Outside of combat, each mystery you're given as long of time as you require so long as you don't investigate the location indicated with a Circle over it. Of course with each investigation, doom raises, chances of negative or positive events may occur, and the chance of being attacked are dependent on RNG and what location you decide to investigate. Certain enemies you fight will be spirits, which cannot be hurt by normal attacks, and you must perform rituals of clapping, bowing, and praying in a correct order to banish it, you're given the notification of (X steps performed are correct, too long, too short) or you can do what's easier, sever it's ties with this earth that deal damage based on the weapon you have, hit chance is high, I think it might even be 100%, and it'll work in like 2 turns usually.To sum it all up: This game lacks content, but it's early access and updates are steady as far as patch notes show. The aesthetic is more than likely what drew you to the game, and it doesn't disappoint there. But there's not enough explanation as to what things do and how things affect you. This game SHOULD be difficult, I'm not saying make it easy, you're a one man army, (though you can recruit allies that offer small buffs, and seem like they'll have more functions in the future) you're up against a being of impossible strength and magnitude, and they KNOW who you are, it should be hard. But I think this game would benefit from a bit more clarification of what things do, items and events, though perhaps showing what events require which skill check to pass may take away from the fear, I'm mixed on that. I want MORE from this game, it's in early access, and hopefully the updates will continue to bring in more mysteries, more events, and especially more god diversity in how you can survive and push it back, and the lore of the gods themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: Ichimura Yumiko, 20 years old.On paper, a baseball player with high strength and low knowledge, searching for her brother who suddenly and mysteriously disappeared.In reality, her strength is lower than that of most characters. Her strength-based baseball bat conflicts with her dexterity-based perk, descriptions suggest she isn't actually great at baseball (or at least pitching).She recently cut her hair, an imperfect job but enough to fool others. It isn't her brother that she's impersonating, though: the person she's masquerading as is a "her", who "they'll" find eventually.She starts with a concussion injury: what injured her, shortly before she fled to Shiokawa?Her name evokes Yumiko from Kawabata Yasunari's the Scarlet Gang of Asakusa, an androgynous heroine who frequently dons the disguise of a fictitious brother while pursuing vengeance for her older sister. Moreover, Kawabata's work is laden with characters who replace others and then totally assume their identities.Is it actually Ichimura Yumiko's brother who's disappeared? Is this really Yumiko? Or could this "sudden disappearance" be that of Yumiko, the actual baseball player, and who we play as is the brother, attempting to become her despite the obvious disparity between the Yumiko of the description and the Yumiko in game?Getting obsessed with a character based on one or two unique events and connections to my favourite work of literature is why I love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always liked horror, the concept of it, but never could get into the first-person jumpscare walking simulators that seem to dominate the genre on Steam. Enter WORLD OF HORROR, a combination Junji-Ito/Lovecraft mix that gets the patient strategy aspect of most good horror fiction exactly right. It's got a nice RPG interface that's a little intimidating on first blush but is really simple once you realize that it's basically just everything you'd get in a regular RPG but without the menu buttons that are usually required to navigate to them. It's got visuals that'll make your heart jump out and just enough lore to keep you entertained searching for alternate endings and difficult achievements. It combines the best aspects of J-horror and western cosmic horror (for horror nerds, it perfectly counteracts the trope in J-horror that the best option is to do nothing by adding a looming Lovecraftian god that you HAVE to stop), and it makes plenty of references to both (mostly J-horror but whatchu gonna do, it's a visual medium and Lovecraft didn't draw).

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely one of the best surprise horror gems I've ever played. Easily top 10 horror games OF ALL TIME material! It's hard to describe what World of Horror actually is, because it's so incredibly unique in the way it seamlessly marries different game styles together in harmony. If I had to try to sum it up in one go, it's a combination rogue-like point-and-click mystery where you are constantly making decisions based on D&D-like stats and planning routes based on outcomes and events. It starts off simple enough, but the game play depth you'll unlock as you pour hours into the game is staggering!Just encountering and doing things in the game unlocks "card packs" that are full of more possible events, weapons, places, and even entire mysteries! Later unlocks on the achievement board are more specific and will require other unlocks to achieve, but they contain special weapons, items, events, places, and even new characters! Some even offer special challenge runs which also includes each characters own challenge run which are all difficult but very fun! Each achievement board square gives a clue on how to unlock it, and they are usually "YOU CAN EVEN DO THAT?!" types of exciting or slyly mysterious!The graphics are a feast for the eyes, and you'll always land up staring at each new scene as it's eerie details work it's way permanently into your brain and psyche. A testament to this is even something as simple as a scene of some creepy dude answering an old rotary phone can absolutely make your skin crawl! The music floats along in tandem to whatever is on screen, and it fits the current atmosphere at any particular moment perfectly.The game play breaks down like this: Each game sets you as a random character from the ones you have unlocked, and each character has strengths and weaknesses to be played/built around. You have to worry about your health, sanity, and doom(doom is essentially time if time was "actions spent" so every action you take matters!) Then there is a randomly chosen evil Eldritch god that curses your run with some special rule like "damage in combat is doubled." There are 5 random mysteries from a pool of ones you have unlocked that need to be solved in the order of your choice. Whenever you solve a mystery a day passes as you get to take a break to reassess your plan, and a new random curse takes over the town which increases the challenge. Once you solve all 5 mysteries you can then ascend the lighthouse to stop the Eldritch god from destroying the world. Beware though the lighthouse will test you based on what you randomly encountered in your current run, so keep that in mind!Each mystery has a brisk and interesting story that is sometimes based on Japanese horror mythology, or is a take on it. One of the mysteries for example is some crazy killer in town is trying to make real mermaids with girls he's snatching, and you have to get to the bottom of it! You'll be guided where to go to further the mystery, but you'll want to think about detouring to recruit allies, shop, learn spells, obtain special items, and much more based on what you think you may encounter in the near future or even late game. There is also optional side quests that are clearly displayed that can help you obtain different paths or endings for each mystery that can leave you better equipped in the end, or more prepared for a specific future mystery. This is all part of the brilliance of the game's design and depth. There are TONS of little things that you can do at any one time that will effect later events, or help you obtain special items, allies, stats, weapons, or something that can allow you to encounter a special epic boss fight which in tandem may then allow you to chain that to another special outcome, or path, etc! Taking advantage of all these little things and planning them all out to your advantage will make you feel like a genius and reward you for all time you've put into the game. It really makes you feel like you're becoming that much better of a player with each and every run!So does the game falter at all? Only a little bit, and it's pretty forgivable considering what a horrifying powerhouse the whole package is. The game tries it's best to introduce new players with a sample mystery, but the intro sample mystery really doesn't explain the games deeper aspects. It sort of just leaves you to discover it all for yourself. Some mysteries are more fun to play through over and over than others. Also combat isn't well explained by the intro, and it is quite simple but also quite complex. Ghost enemies can be very annoying if you're a new player, and I'm not very fond of the system to fight them although once mastered they are no problem for the most part. Normal enemy encounters are simple, but fun! The monsters themselves are absolutely terrifying to look at! You'll want to discover them all! Some even have phases, and you'll want to take note which monsters are weak to which kinds of weapons. The combat also has a lot of options, but really you just want maximize your chance to hit, and make the most out of your swings. You can even cast spells, use allies, throw items, and even use desperation moves!Overall I can't recommend this obscure horror game enough! It's one of my favorite horror games, and there's really nothing else quite like it. I've put in 50 hours and unlocked all the achievement board achievements, but a less die hard player than me would probably take around 80 to 100 hours to unlock all the achievement board items. I still haven't encountered everything yet, but I definitely will try to as I play more! I've shown this game to many friends, and they've all absolutely loved it! This is just one of those games, man!Overall: 9.5 / 10PS: I noticed a lot of comments about "slow updates", but there is a huge fully complete game here well worth the asking price. There is even custom mods, a discord server loaded with content, and more! I think the reason people are so thirsty for "updates" is because the overall game is such a masterpiece, and I too myself despite completing the game would love... just a little more of THE WORLD OF HORROR!!! ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Despite what steam says I've payed closer to 15 hours at this point. Art style and ambiance are great, there's a lot of charm in the visuals and a lot of spooky scenarios to investigate/enemies to fight. I still have a lot of content left to unlock at this point so the game is pretty meaty as well.If I could describe the actual game play I'd say it's risk management. You have to explore certain tiles on a map to advance each "mystery" or story, completing all of the mysteries in a run leads to a win. When exploring these tiles you will either be given a mandatory skill check, a choice of actions followed by a skill check, or a combat encounter. Failing skill checks, receiving status ailments, and racking up the in-game doomsday counter are all inevitable as virtually everything has a catch-22 aspect to it. The player needs to learn the systems in place and try to navigate the world of horror as best they can in their decision making as it's a lot of small decisions that add up along the way vs one big decision that will get a win.  That being said: trying to plan around mysteries to get various items and trying to trigger certain events to uncover a lot of different secrets and endings is fun, and combat is simple yet satisfying enough. If I had one major complaint it's the amount that the rng can punish the player. There are many runs where I will be quickly sabotaged with unavoidable damage as a natural progression of a mystery, sometimes losing as much as 20% or more of my health in the process. Health can be restored by resting , which nets a couple points of health back, but the in-game doomsday counter will increase with every rest, and it adds up quickly considering said counter is constantly filling, little by little, with virtually every action. The player can also heal with certain items and spells but as mentioned earlier almost every action has a consequence. A lot of the time the player will have to suffer debuffs like permanent status ailments or have other stats drop, which in the context of the game is generally fine as it puts more weight behind each choice. However, suffering another debuff because I flipped over the 4th "X happened: -2 stamina" doesn't feel good.  That considered: I still have fun with this game and have plenty of runs where I die to bad decisions that I feel were definitely my fault and not rng assassination. TLDR: Great visuals and ambiance, fun risk management/decision based game play where every action matters, interesting writing & scenarios for the "mysteries" (stories), uncovering the many secrets and endings to mysteries is satisfying, RNG can feel a little unfair at times, but overall the game is enjoyable .

_childDocuments_.review: I saw someone play the demo for this game a while ago, and was intrigued. when I heard that the early access version was out, I had to snap it up and my expectations have so far been surpassed. this game has stunning (and horrifying) visuals, interesting characters with a variety of possible viable builds, and fun mysteries and random events. the junji ito inspirations and references are clear and enjoyable. it's definitely one of the fuller early access titles I've ever played, which just makes me even more excited for the full release. it's definitely a difficult game - getting through five mysteries with enough resources to make it through the lighthouse isn't simple, but every run I learn something new about how to interact with and respond to different events. I suppose it could feel repetitive after a while, but with unlocking new events over time and playing different characters, it's not really something I've had an issue with. a lot of fun, highly recommended, though there are definitely some images that could be triggering (particularly for trypophobia and eye stuff, not to mention blood and descriptions of horror scenes)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really familiar with roguelike games, but being a big fan of Junji Ito, World of Horror is a pretty crazy experience. You fire up one or a series of mysteries where a combination of your choices and random dice rolls determine whether you'll survive them. As you investigate, you face setbacks that nibble away at your stats and slowly make your playthrough more compelling. The two- or three color pixelated art style is a great look for the game's visual style, which is modelled after black & white manga, and funny enough even the occasional grammar mistake seems like it'd be right at home in a fan-translated comic.The game is, I believe, developed by only one person, which is always amazing to see. If I have any criticisms to offer, one would be that the game can feel like the dice rolls determine too much of your fate - a series of inescapable events that knock your stamina or reason down feels like something that can't be guarded against. But, maybe that's a big appeal of roguelikes? Other than that, the game seems ready for simply more content - maybe fan-produced stuff, to further expand the current encounters and monsters. I will add that the developer has recently added a bunch and there's even an option to prioritize seeing new content.edit: I should recommend that after you've played a few rounds, you go through the Extras menu to have a look at the achievements, because those will unlock additional events, enemies and player characters for you - so, the more you play, the more new content you will unlock.World of Horror is one of those brillians mashups - roguelike, horror manga - that just surprises you and completely works.

_childDocuments_.review: You can get an army of dogs to attack and destroy any eldritch creature that stands in your path, but you'll probably still die due to all those holes you've got.And if you feel lonely, remember that there's something truly friendly out there that just cannot sated without your kindness and love! 💓💓Quick summary of the good:* Good art direction - this game takes full advantage of pixel art to create surreal and horrific imagery.* Tons of modes, challenges, and small customizations you can make.* Character builds are flexible, not everything that is "negative" is going to break the current run.* On higher difficulties, it will 100% keep you on your toes.* The music is amazing.* While the story might not be very lore-heavy, it still gives a true sense of Lovecraftian surreal horror.The bad:* While the game itself is excellent, I've grown to dislike the Doom Meter. It's one aspect I wish they could change to make it less static and make survival/impending doom feel a lot more real/threatening. To be fair, no Lovecraftian horror game has managed to get this right.* The game does have some issues with pacing due to the Doom Meter. It makes it so you have to speedrun every run, and yet there are certain items/events you want to get, which might kill the run when you get the same three events at a location ten times in a row. Even if you somehow do get the events/items, there are times when there is still a lot that you could do, but there's no point since it's either the last mystery or the remaining ones aren't open-world.* Certain events feel underwhelming, despite the implied severity of the situation.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to describe how good World of Horror is. The investigation mechanic is amazing and expertly draws you down the rabbit hole. Investigating a location creates encounters for you to resolve with your character's traits and either rewards or punishes you for the result. The scenarios range from terrifying and macabre to classic horror tropes but it never winks at you; this is a genuine horror experience. The aesthetic only serves to enforce the fear through the limits of the graphics palette and user interface. That's not to deride either, they're both amazing (especially the art), but you can feel a sense of confinement through the boundaries imposed on you. Add to all this a massive "deck" of event cards that drive the scene to scene gameplay and there's a TON of replayability; especially when each Mystery you solve has multiple endings. If you like horror, get this. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so oddly fun. The RNG is frustrating as crap, where some runs were just +Doom, +Doom, +Curse, +Curse, +Failed every check, +Bad story, etc. Like one run even people who were familiar with the game and were telling me how bad the seed and my RNG was... ugh. I had over 100% doom by the middle of the third mission. But then on one run, it just all came together (until the end) except for extra luck I ran with the Virtual Boy theme. I ran into one issue at the end when I was trying to equip something else, as I had to throw the mask on to drop below 97% Doom. I put the mask on, and then tried to equip something in B (mask was in C) and the game took the mask off me and dropped all my stats instead of putting the new gear in space B. I was so annoyed. I still managed to win, after putting the mask back on, by getting to the top with 97% Doom. There was an actual feeling of success and relief where I let out an audible exclamation of shock and happiness.So beyond the bad RNG, it was a lot of fun. I really liked the color schemes, I liked the stories and tales, but I wish there was a bit more of a better tutorial. With some help from someone familiar this came together as logical a lot faster and removed trial and error in an RNG/Rogue-ish type game. I am going to replay it more though, because I need to find out what all the blacked out spaces are and what I'm missing to be able to complete things. And since the story can be run through quickly, even bad RNG can be beaten. For instance, I played for 5.3 hours but I ran through several dozen times. For those looking to buy but to save a few dollars, this indie dev IS on one of the other stores, but I feel the Steam experience and keeping things in one place was definitely worth that $5. The game is also worth $20 easily.Summary:Art style is definitely 4/5 after you get into it and start playing. It does not reflect as well in the Steam pictures.Sounds are good.Story is an RNG Choose your own adventure which is great.Replay value is very high as well.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of mystery/point-and-click adventure games, please consider buying this title. The art style is solid and the developers went all in on the Lovecraftian aesthetic. The Good:- Thematic experience is the strong suit of the game.- Randomized upon every play-through, unless you select the 'Custom option'.- Rather simple to play (no need for aim, easily accessible skill-wise.- Mod support- Extras that expand the the theme, story, and the several endings- You can recruit a dog to your team. The Bad- User interface takes time to get used to. It's dynamic, and will change throughout a run.- Not as scary as I first thought. Thematic, yes, but not heavily a horror game (subjective, I know).Should you buy this title? YES. Well worth the price, and even more so if it goes on sale. This is a rougelite that focuses on creating tension between maximizing your stats, while also finishing the story before your DOOM meter rises to 100%. Very solid single player experience.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun premise with a great style for the genre is going for, taking advantage of the old graphics in some few but remarkable aspects. To be fair is more of a board game RPG than a proper roguelike, as most events are roll checks with your character's stats.That's unfortunately the main problem I was starting to notice. The game has indeed a random factor, but is more inbetween small events inside straightline stories with 2-4 endings. Some mysteries work arround a particular gimmick that makes you manage different menus, but overall since death is permanent you'll soon start redoing the same stories with just the tiny events that in sometimes makes no sense (Not in a horror sense) in the context of the current mystery, and simply trying to figure out how to see a new ending. For example the tutorial mystery can show up in normal runs, and with very few factors affecting it will become all about following a pattern and keeping check of your character's stats for the proper roll checks.Since is still in early access I don't wanna bash it too much, as is taking the right path to becoming a very enternaining game if completed and/or with further updates. If anything needs more story branching in the mysteries it offers, not just making the true RNG factor in small events that doesn't affect the whole storyline.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: A gem of a game, though be cautious about the updating frequency (The developer has a habit of disappearing for a year...)The sheer atmosphere, intrigue, story, and mechanics of this game is simply out of this world. I haven't seen a game that evokes cosmic horror so well. The gameplay is also excellent, despite the simplicity of the mechanics (point and click), almost every decision involves some thought and planning.Recommend for any horror fans and adventure game fans, especially those who like watching horror game playthroughs but can't handle the adrenaline of the action-reaction dependent ones.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: This game is still early access, but it has a lot of content for it's current stage of development. The theme/premise is horror/eldritch/Japanese inspired, 1/2 bit graphic and old 8-bit style music. There are many multiple endings to mysteries and different timelines you can choose from (also unlockable acheivements, characters, and outfits) by completing multiple playthroughs and seeing what the game has to offer.The general gameplay is casual with clicking options in response to the situation, and the combat is pretty cool in terms of design. The combat is picking actions that take certain time and sequencing them together, and the actions take more or less time depending on varying factors (your character's stats, augments from spells, weapons equipped, etc). As for picking options, generally they will have a behind the scenes skill check that factors in your character's specific stat, i.e. DEX or STR, etc. Really cool concept of old style RPG mixed with the genre of horror/lovecraft/eldritch stuff.There are also mods you can find on the subreddit that add lots of new content as well, and I really enjoy playing the endless mode to see how far I can get before I lost ( best so far 197 turns! :D ) It's really fun as a sort of rogue-like game experience, it would be cool to see more mods come out, or even more content update with game modes or new mysteries. It would be super cool to see something that helps tamper the Doom progression in endless runs to really see how far you can push a character's attributes/gearset, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: I've played probably dozens of rougelikes in my day- too many to list; but World of Horror is quite possibly the best rougelike I've ever played. Haunting, immersive, engaging, and chilling to the core. With an easy-to-learn hard-to-master gameplay loop, inventive scenarios, and encounters that require you to change your strategy and tactics on the fly, World of Horror will keep you glued to your screen 'til the Old Gods come to devour our planet.9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

_childDocuments_.review: Experience the quiet terror of this 1-bit love letter to Junji Ito and H.P. Lovecraft. Navigate a hellish roguelite reality with turn-based combat and unforgiving choices. Experiment with your deck of event cards to discover new forms of cosmic horror in every playthrough. The inevitable awaits...
_childDocuments_.name: WORLD OF HORROR

name: Bee Simulator
detailed_description: When the first rays of sunlight rise above the horizon, the beehive slowly wakes up. Hierarchy and diligence are vital for the wellbeing of the whole swarm. So you check your wings, measure the antennae degree of deviation, take orders from the Queen, and bee-gin your first independent mission. And that's just the beginning of your adventures. Suddenly, you learn that people want to cut down the tree that holds your hive. Now your fate – and the fate of your whole family – lies in your small, agile legs and fast wings! Take part in a race and show your sisters who has the fastest wings in the swarm! The world of bees is not as carefree as one may think. Wasps and some of the less friendly people will take any chance to ruin your plans. Don't hesitate to use your sting to save your swarm from enemies. You are the master of air acrobatics. Your sisters are eager to mirror your smooth dance moves. So perform your famous waggle dance and show them the way back to the hive. Explore the park thoroughly – visit even the deepest corners to look for rare plants and special flowers in order to collect the best pollen. • A unique chance to see the macro scale world from the micro perspective of a honeybee; • A realistic representation of a place inspired by Central Park; • Three diverse modes enriched with educational elements: - One-player story mode presents you with a family of bees. Will you save the hive from the threat of human beings? - Exploration mode allows you to freely discover a world inspired by Central Park in New York - Split-screen mode can be either used for cooperation or competition. It includes an additional maps that make the game even more fascinating.* • A possibility to interact with the surroundings: people, animals, plants, and other insects; • Lack of violence – it's a perfect choice for parents seeking a game to safely play with their children; • Relaxing music composed by Mikołaj Stroiński, who was responsible for the soundtrack of such games as The Witcher 3 and The Vanishing of Ethan Carter. *Please note a controller is required for local multiplayer

short_description: Live the big adventure of a small bee! Explore a world brimming with life in which you collect pollen, defy dangerous wasps and save your hive. Play with others in three game modes, including co-op and PvP on split screen.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Beekeeper, I saw this game as a humble monthly game and decided that what the heck I'll claim and play it.Unfortunately the "Simulator" is very misleading, as 30 min into the game I had too many "This is not how its supposed to bee (pun intended)". What I saw was cute and all, but really too many misleading aspects of hive infrastructure and bee behavior. 2 of the major things that bothered me was the way the Queen's role has been portrayed, and how the inside of the hive has this "castle with multiple chambers" effect.I did like the facts on the loading screens with how accurate they were though.It can work as a kids game to cultivate an interest in bees and maybe keep them entertained for a while. I've read some of the other reviews and saw similar issues and a lack of more content. I understand that a 1 to 1 ratio of real life to game is impossible, and that in the end to make a game some aspects needs to be changed or ignored.The game was not tagged as "Simulation" , but the "Simulator" in the title gives the wrong impression at face value. Overall beautiful artwork and environment.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Apart from one huge, glaring, and omnipresent error, it's actually a pretty good game. (The error is that they persistently refer to bees gathering pollen to make honey.  Bees gather nectar to make honey, the pollen sticks to them in order to benefit the plants, not the bees.)  I wouldn't really call it a "simulator", though, it's more of a "bee rpg".  There's lots of little side stuff to do if you're into that, so while the story is pretty short you can play it for quite a while if you like.It's extremely family-friendly but the actual game mechanics are well developed so even an adult could enjoy this game if they're in the right mood.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: if youre looking for a scientifically accurate bee sim, this is not the game for you. if youre looking for something mentally stimulating, this is also not the game for you.if youre looking for a fairly chill, mostly entertaining walking/flying sim with some easy tasks and challenges, and where you can make children cry by buzzing around their heads, this is the game for you.its family friendly and i played this game together with my 4 year old brother who probably had a little more fun playing this than i did but it was still entertaining enough for me to not regret the $2 spent. it definitely plays better on controller than mouse and keyboard. i did have to switch to mouse and keyboard for one achievement (hackerman - the drone one) because it was bugged on controller and you were unable to move except for up and down. this is the main negative aspect of this game imo, it is pretty buggy at times and sometimes challenges do reset or you slightly lose some progress if you go back to the main menu. still able to complete it though.now as far as achievements go, if you want to 100% this game and unlock all achievements, the challenges and the achievement where youre required to collect 3k pollen do get very tedious after a while.the whole game can be completed in just a couple of hours if you focus on the main story only. if youre going for achievements, plan on investing a few more hours.overall id probably give this like a 7/10 for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game I really do, but as a hobby entomologist, I just wish it was not based around Honey Bee propaganda, it's exaggerated misinformation :( native pollinators are extremely important, the eu-honeybee is a disaster for the ecosystem and native bees sadly. that aside, great game, really lovely and insightful on the hard work honey bees do and how it goes.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished playing the main story on hard mode all the way through as soon as the game came out and haven't finished collecting everything the game has to offer. First off, I think the game has potential to appeal to more hardcore gamers especially with the different mechanics (fighting is honestly super fun, but gets boring as it becomes repetitive). I can imagine some sort of skill tree or stat progression so you can potentially fight another hornet or another species. There is also room for online multiplayer, but that may be asking too much.Second, I bought the game while it's on sale for $20.99 and I think I had to reach to justify this purchase while it's on sale. I can only imagine how poorly this game would sell when it's not on sale (I've seen it's going to be listed for $40 and I would never buy it for $40).Lastly, if you find yourself justifying this game's purchase, the main story takes 2-4 hours to complete depending on how fast you're trying to complete the game and if you decide to avoid side quests. The skins are super cool (I got the CyBee one) and I'll take time to go back and complete side quests to see if it helps justify the pricing.The game is made for children and if you go in with a childlike mindset, it's enjoyable. However, this is only after you justify the game's price and take a dive into Bee-dom.Overall a solid 6.5/10, I slightly recommend.P.S. I forgot to mention some of the issues with the camera when you fly close to objects (ground, rocks, trees, etc.) so you might have an issue with trying to fly too fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: This game is full of bee misinformation. Everything from the hive structure, to behavior of the bees is incorrect and most of the "facts" presented are inaccurate.Beyond that, the gameplay is cumbersome, boring, and repetitive with far too many notes taken from Superman 64.Beyond being not worth your money, it is not worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game on steam before it was available for purchase, and put it on my wishlist, because it looked amazing. But, after playing through the whole thing, I'm very disappointed, it's not what I thought it would be :( It's ok, but definitely a disappointment, not anywhere near as good as I hoped it would be, it is good enough that I can recommend it, but only really to kids, mainly because of the first con below:Cons - 1. The voiceovers in this game, for the bees and other animals, are very baby-ish; from an adult point-of-view, this is a minus, for kids, though, I think this would be appealing. The voiceover for the bee you play as is pretty good, though, so it's not too bad. But, still, as an adult I'm very disappointed that they brought a baby-ish theme into it, I was expecting better from this game :( 2. Humans sound really weird....there are humans everywhere in this game, in free roam, but they're a disappointment, because: 1. They don't talk, whenever you fly close enough to them, you hear them just making these really weird mumbling noises, it's a really strange thing to listen to....to give you an example, ever watched the old TV show 'Chowder,' about that purple kid that loves eating and cooking? Well, there's a character in there called Schnitzel, and the only way he talks is by making noises like 'Rada rada rada.' Well, that's a lot what people in this game sound like. And 2. Coupled with that first one, they just make robotic hand movements or move in a way that doesn't make them look realistic. I mean, the way they look is good enough, but considering this game came out this year, where game developing in general has come a long way, I really think they could have done a little bit better of a job than this, at least with their movements and sound....3. Story is too short. There's nothing better in a game than having a good long story that keeps you entertained for a long time. The story plot in this game is good and engaging, even teaches you some good life lessons about the bees, and why they are so important, but it's too short, it should have gone on for much longer.4. Steam achievements are totally bugged. I know without a doubt that I've done a lot of things in this game that should have given me the steam achievements, but it says I haven't even completed a single one of them. Not the worst problem out there, but still annoying... Pros - 1. Flight. The flying in this game is just stunning. Panoramic views as you fly up down, forwards and back in all directions (you can even crawl around up walls and upside down on the ceiling, and fly upside down), making it a great little game to come to, for all ages, if you feel you need to de-stress; flying around as a little bee in free roam is very relaxing :) And it's fun, too, you can fly so fast, too, especially when you make sharp turns! ^_^2. You wouldn't think there would actually be the option to customize the look of your character in a game where you play as a bee, but there is ^_^ Not only can you change the look of your bee, you can also choose what pattern trails out behind you when you fly fast (or choose not to have one at all), or give your bee cute little hats (like a little pirate hat, mining hat, or headphones, etc.), it's adorable ^_^3. Good storyline. Even though the story is short, it's, again, good and engaging. It teaches you good life lessons on why bees are so important, and just leaves you with a good feeling inside, by the end of it :) You, as the bee, start out as a pollen gatherer, but when the existence of your home is threatened, you defy orders requiring you to be a pollen gather to go out in search of a new home for your hive, before it's too late.4. Side-quests, discoveries and collectibles to find in free roam. There's exciting things to do in free roam, even when the story ends. From different types of side-quests, like fighting hostiles like wasps and hornets (there's no blood in combat, which is really good), to gathering pollen, and chasing away and even stinging obnoxious bullies that stomp on flowers :D Completing these quests gives you 'knowledge points,' which you can spend in the character customization, to unlock looks for your bee :) There are also lots of animals and plants you can find in free roam, that, when interacted with and discovered, unlocks interesting info about them in a book called the 'Glossary.' And also, free roam is MASSIVE, which is a big bonus :)5. Beautiful soundtrack. The soundtrack when flying around in free roam is just beautiful and very relaxing to listen to. And when you go into 'Beemode' (when you go into this mode, your eyesight changes to a hexagonal view, the way a bee would see things, and all plants that can be gathered are highlighted in a specific colour, depending on their rarity, making it easier for them to spot and identify), the soundtrack becomes more subtle and muffled, making it sound dreamy and beautiful :)Overall, my recommendation for this game is 50-50: I wouldn't really recommend it for adults, due to the majority of voice-overs being very childish, too childish for adult liking, but I would for kids. This game is way too overpriced, though, it shouldn't be the price that it is, around $40. I waited till there was a sale, and got it at half price, around $20, and that's really more like what this game is worth, it's not a terrible game, but not good enough that it should be $40. Just too little content.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Another instance of wishing Steam had a side-ways thumb option. This would be a fine game for young kids, and as a bee keeper myself, I appreciate the devs obvious enthusiasm towards honeybees and attention to detail when it comes to the pleasant art and information during the opening cutscene. The models for assorted insects are also pretty sharp.But as far as a game goes, theres not much here, and its far and away from a simulator. I think the subject at hand would have been better served as a real time strategy game playing as a colony considering hives behave as super-organisms. There would also be a lot more justification for disseminating cool information about bees and their social structure throughout the game instead of just dumping it all in the beginning and opting for an arcade experience for the rest of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, because I can tell a lot of love went into it. However, this game has some faults in game mechanics and the expectations based on the description and game trailer. Firstly, if this game was stated that it was strictly for younger children, I might not have purchased it. I really like cozy and chill games, but there still needs to be something entertaining to do. The story is really boring from an adult perspective and plays like a tale for small children (also this is how the dialogue written). I also finished it rather quickly, even while trying to take my time to do a few "side quests". I didn't really feel like I was doing much of anything except flying around a bit (which was nice) but overall there didn't feel to be too much point to the game for me.Secondly, the flight mechanics were hard to get right. If your whole game is flying, I feel like this should be fine-tuned. It didn't make any of the racing components very enjoyable.Additionally, there seemed to be a lot of places to explore in the photos, but the game doesn't really promote exploration. The main concept is really nice, but this game feels like its not finished in story, especially for the price tag.Perhaps if you have small children, this game is very nice for them, but as an adult (who often plays cozy and child-friendly games), this was a bit too boring, even for me. Really sorry ;_;.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not recommending this for four reasons:1) It's not a simulator. The main task as a honey bee is to find, land on and extract nectar from the flower. This is completely missing. You fly through bubbles representing flowers instead. People and animals are stationary. They don't try to swat you or run away or chickens don't try to eat you. As you're doing your tasks there isn't even the ambiance of other bees collecting honey too. Not a whole lot here made me feel like I was living a bee's life. 2) Not only is it not a simulator, it's an awareness campaign disguised as a game. I'm all for awareness and love honey bees. I want to do more for honey bees based on playing this. Maybe I missed the fine print.3) I bought this on a deep sale for $1.99. Personally I would refund as I'll never play it again. It could be a good educational tool for teachers or parents. I'm not going to refund and consider the $2 a "donation."4) It's more of an interactive documentary about bees than it is a game. The game-play wasn't fun for me. It was very shallow. Fly through this many colored bubbles to fill the honey meter. Get in proximity of a honey comb and all honey is depleted. They could have made a fun game and a documentary at the same time.I would have liked to know these details before buying, so hopefully this helps somebody make an educated decision.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: It's a so-so game but isn't a simulator at all, as virtually nothing in the game provides any realism or education about how bees function as a hive. If they want to help bees survive in the world, maybe the gameplay should help explore some of the actual functions of beehive function and not play up childlike ideas about how bees function. Also the english voice is annoying. Unfortunately I will be asking for a refund. Only good for young children, possibly.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: A busy little bee.Story:You play as Beescuit (although you can pick any name you want). A honeybee that has one simple goal in their life, serve the queen and get pollen for the hive. It's a very simple story and it's made in a way to describe what a bee does and their importance for our own life. The story itself is fine although it falls on a bit too childish at times with some very cringe worthy puns in the dialogue, however it's aimed for a more child friendly crowd and to teach them about the importance of bees and in that department they nail with flying colors. I won't even get into the invasive bee argument cause that's a whole different can of worms, but the fact still stands that we need bees. Graphics:Visually, Bee Simulator looks pretty great. I really like the environments and the world surrounding your hive and the hive itself. Your hive is located in the middle of what seems to be NYC Central Park or heavily inspired by it and it's visually stunning with tons of different areas to explore from a Zoo, to caves and an amusement park to name a few.However the character models that aren't animals or insects look pretty abysmal. Of course the park is filled with tons of people walking around and their models look like they're puppets on string. Their walking animations are incredibly stiff and jerky and just look awful compared to everything else. Audio:I'll begin with the voice acting which is pretty bad. Now it's not the worst thing I've ever heard, but it's pretty bad. A lot of the characters are voiced by the same actress trying to do different voices and it just sounds really weird, not to mention there are instances where you talk with someone and after sometime the actor will switch to deliver another line for the same character.The soundtrack and ambience of the world however are nice and really make for a great atmosphere. It's very relaxing and fun to just fly around and hearing the buzzing is pretty satisfying and the music provides for decent background noise. I wish there were a few more tracks, cause it's generally a few different tracks on rotation and if I played for a 100% I would have definitely lost my mind listening to the same tracks.Gameplay:This is where I'm really mixed about Bee Simulator. Essentially it's an open world game where you have a few different goals you have to do as a worker bee, which ranges from collecting pollen for the hive, doing tasks for other bees and fighting off threats like hornets and wasps. I'll begin with what I like. I think a lot of the activities are fun enough. Flying around collecting pollen is very simple and fun and there's challenges scattered around the world to make the experience slightly challenging, which I found really fun. The other activities like racing where you fly through hoops to catch up to your opponent are also fun, while a bit tedious. The worst activity is hands down the fighting. I played through the story on the hardest difficulty and found myself breezing through all of it, but there are moments where the game ramps up in difficulty and that is the fighting sequences. There are certain fights which are borderline impossible to beat, because a single hit takes off 20% of your help and enemies can chain hits together to just stun lock you and finish you off. It's easy enough once you pick up on it, but still certain enemies pack quite the punch.Story missions themselves are generally fun, but really lack variety as it's basically the same goal over and over you have to do with some new additions to break up the tedium. However the side quests I found to be even more fun than the main story as they had interactions with different insects which really helped going through the main story.Verdict:Overall I feel a bit mixed on Bee Simulator, but in general I did have a good enough time for it to warrant a positive rating. It's a cute game, that's fun to play and teaches you about the importance of bees and it's actually a great game you can play with your kids that will entertain them and will teach them too, so if you ever wanted to experience the life through the eyes of a bee, then check this out.Final Rating:6.5/10Pros:+ The environments look absolutely great+ Some of the side quests are really fun+ Exploration is fun and relaxing + Teaches importance of beesCons:- Voice acting is pretty bad- Not much variety in missions - The fighting mechanic sucks - Human character models look like puppetsIf you liked this review please consider joining
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded it, then re-purchased it because I realized it was 10 dollars  and I felt bad losing the cute game and it's worth the 10. It almost feels like a PS1 game with how everything is done but of course the sandbox is too big for that. It's a very simplistic family friendly game. I'd only recommend grabbing it on sale. You're strictly a honey bee so it should be called Honeybee simulator. It's short and there's not that much to do so again it's not worth 30. If there was a mixed option for steam reviews this would be in here. It has too much charm for me to give it a thumbs down though. A very cute game. It made me feel good.  Expect "Fun" over "realism" I suppose as it felt more like an arcacde-ish game almost than a simulator.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: I am a former beekeeper as well as a big fan/nerd when it comes to bee facts. .If you are like me you will enjoy this game! I love that you can unlock different bee models like orchids and carpenter bees to play.I actually found this game to be frustratingly difficult at times on hard-mode with a controller- especially in chases and fights, but I wasn't too upset with that. I was worried it would be too fast and easy. It was a quick game in terms of the storyline. It took me about two nights to finish. I wouldn't say the storyline flowed the best or always made sense. Sometimes things would happen in the storyline that lead to absolutely nothing but I guess that is pretty realistic. There were some accuracies about bees I really appreciated and some things I wasn't keen on, like stinging people repetitiely and them barely reacting (even if the humans are pretty funny and weird in this game.)I did however like the characters. The graphics and audio are amazing, very engaging, and the flying is very fun. It's a chill game for the most part, and I enjoyed the animals and scenery. Cute game and you can tell it was made by a great team.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: According to all known lawsof aviation, there is no way a beeshould be able to fly. Its wings are too small to getits fat little body off the ground. The bee, of course, flies anyway because bees don't carewhat humans think is impossible. Yellow, black. Yellow, black.Yellow, black. Yellow, black. Ooh, black and yellow!Let's shake it up a little. Barry! Breakfast is ready! Coming! Hang on a second. Hello? - Barry?- Adam? - Can you believe this is happening?- I can't. I'll pick you up. Looking sharp. Use the stairs. Your fatherpaid good money for those. Sorry. I'm excited. Here's the graduate.We're very proud of you, son. A perfect report card, all B's. Very proud. Ma! I got a thing going here. - You got lint on your fuzz.- Ow! That's me! - Wave to us! We'll be in row 118,000.- Bye!
