_childDocuments_.review: The game is mostly minigames. The main story and side quests have variation from the minigames, so it's not just those. But most of your time in the game will be minigames. I gave this a negative review, but it wasn't too bad of a "time waster" game. you fly through blue rings to follow/catch another flying insect. There are speed boost pickups to slightly fill your speed boost gauge, and slowdown pickups to avoid. If you miss a ring you lose a failure token, but you must go through the next ring or lose. There are also obstacles throughout the "courses". The "Easy" difficulty is super easy and short. The "Hard" version is much longer and needs more skill., because bees "dance" to give directions, is where you must press up/down/left/right to repeat the sequence that the other bee does a few times. Do it correctly and you will gain a success mark, fail and you lose a success and have to repeat the last sequence again which the other bee will repeat for you to follow. After you complete all the sequences, you get a nav marker to find a special flower. are completely different minigame between difficulties.Battle on Easy is like a rhythm game where you must press X or Y at the right time as a bar goes along and intersects where it has a blue (defense / X) or red (attack / Y) marker. Battle on Hard it's a real time attack/defend minigame also with directional component to the attack/defense. You have to turn on your "bee sense" where flowers are specific colors based on rarity/tier and collect X before the time runs out. On Easy there is no timer.There's also a rare one where you repeatedly sting (not scientifically accurate) a "bully" child who is stomping flowers to get it to run away. One or two other activities that don't show often.I would have liked there to be a menu option to choose difficulty for each type of minigame. I'd place Battle on "Easy", and everything else on "Hard" since that's my skill level.The gamepad controls are a bit broken. In the Battle minigame, the left stick does not work to change direction of your attack / defense. In the Dancing minigame pressing any direction on the left stick will cause a failure for that attempt. You must use the D-pad for it. There's one side mission where you control a drone. None of the gamepad controls for it work except ascend/descend. KB/M controls work fine for it though.The game could use a minimap. (There are amusment park type "you are here" maps on small walls at set places through the game area you can fly in front of and look at, but meh.)  once you finish the main story and are just going around doing the minigame missions, and side quests to know where they all are.When there's a minigame really nearby, there's a marker symbol on the screen that will lead you to it. IMO this should be much longer range. Again,  once you finish the main story and are just going around doing the minigame missions, and side quests. I've finished MOST of these "missions" and now finding any of them is a huge chore in itself because the range to detect them on your "radar" is so short.Achievements are broken. I have like 4, but I should have more than half of them by now. There's a thread locked by the dev claiming it was fixed. Well... it's not fixed for me. Very frustrating as I'm 100%  going to play through this game again to get them. If the game checks in with steam upon saving what you have done I could get the achievements without needing to play through again.There's a sticky post in the forums from November 2020 noting that achievements are broken, and controller support is too, and that these issues will be "fixed soon". Didn't seem to happen 6 months later. Or if you have some time to kill chillaxing while watching a show on your second monitor and already have it through Humble sub like I did, then maybe.If they fix the controller problem, and make the achievements work in a way I can boot up my game, have it check what I've done (there's an in-game wall of icons in your hive) and give me them on Steam, I'd change my review to positive and put the "lowered expectation kids game" disclaimer at the top.

_childDocuments_.review: Bee Simulator fundamentally fails at everything it's meant to be, yet alone what you'd expect from a game with the word "simulator" in the title.  I can only conclude they stuck simulator in there to cash in on recent popularity in the genre.1: The game heavily pushes the concept that bees are going extinct and we need to take collective action to save them.  It's clearly trying to get people invested in this issue. Unfortunately, the game is priced at £25 and has voice acting and plot seemingly aimed at very young children- what exactly is the target demographic here?  2: I touched on it on 1, but it's bad enough to deserve its own paragraph.  The voice acting is bad.  A lot of the bees are clearly the same voice actor doing a different voice and not quite pulling it off.  The main narrative is incredibly simplistic and read in an almost condescendingly "you're a child" voice.  Note, they knew not to feature any of this in the trailer.  3: The gameplay is not informative.  Why does this matter?  Well, the game is clearly trying to get people interested in bees, never mind the promise of a "simulator" experience.  Landing on flowers to collect pollen?  Nope, fly through yellow spheres.  Pheromones?  Nope, there's 1 setting where you can toggle what amounts to a rarity filter for flowers.  Dealing with predators?  Your first fight (again, bees don't really get in many fights and we all know why) is with a wasp that's portrayed as a school bully.  Instead of letting people putter about seeing from a bee's perspective, it's more a bunch of abstract scripted minigames.4: It's not game-y enough.  I know this directly contradicts my previous complaint, but that's the point.  Bee Simulator is an unsatisfactory hodgepodge of concepts.  If you're going to make it a wacky children's game you should dial back the MUST SAVE BEES message and just run with it being a stupid game.  I kind of ran out of steam at this point, so that's where I'll end the review.  If the devs ever read this (and genuinely gives a hoot about bees) I hope your future endeavours are more successful, and perhaps informative.

_childDocuments_.review: I was close to giving this game a bad review, because I didn’t enjoy playing it… but I need to be honest to myself. I simply am not part of the game’s target group. Let me explain…Bee Simulator is a game for kids. It is much more educational, than it is for fun. There are informative facts about bees on every screen and mid-game. The story itself is very much what you would expect from a bee game (no spoilers) and it is very short (90 minutes – in one play-through). After that, you can fly around and play mini games. These mini games were also the main part of the story. But what are they? Most of the time you will simply fly around the map. The map is open world, quite big and really well designed. It is beautiful. But the gameplay is boring. Fight wasps by clicking X or Y at the right time, follow other insects (flying through rings), collect pollen or do dance battles (4 arrow keys – press them in the right order to copy the opponent’s dance moves). I suppose that you understand by now why this game is for kids. It is impossible to lose any fight or dance battle if you are older than 12.You can also play those mini games in coop multiplayer. There are 3 different maps to choose from and in which you can freely fly around. I think it is nice that they added a coop mode (and 3 unique maps for that game mode).Nevertheless, the hand drawn loading screens, as well as the animated video sequences are really well done. The whole game has quite nice graphics and a solid soundtrack.To sum it up, even if this is a very educational game directed to kids, I must admit, that it suits the target group well. Therefore, I recommend this game (for kids mainly).

_childDocuments_.review: # Steam Deck*IGNORE THE STEAM DECK RATING* - This works flawlessly on steam deck, so long as you're OK with accepting the default name given to you.The reason it fails the steam deck compatibility check is because when the game loses focus it will pause automatically. This means opening the on-screen keyboard will cause it to pause, blocking input. If you really cared enough, you can just plug in a keyboard but I recommend just hitting "A" and accepting the default then moving on.I recommend enabling the gyroscope as this game is a model example of games that work well with gyroscope controls. For extra greatness, I mapped R1 to L3 so that I can boost using R1 or L3. L3 is better, IMO, since R2 is needed for proper flight so your right finger is occupied at times you'd want to boost.> Side-note: After getting my steam deck only about a week ago, I've noticed something peculiar. Every single game I've played on it has worked flawlessly - even the ones listed as "not supported" like this one. As such, I've made it my mission to play every single "not supported" game until I find one that has earned the title. I've yet to find such a game...# GameplayThis game came across as a surprise. I got it with a humble bundle, and just got around to giving it a try. I really like the pacing and story, even though it is as other reviewers have said - very much written for a younger audience.There are things I could nit-pick, but no point in that. The only real issues I see are the flying movement mechanics seem to use a turning based mechanism rather than strafing, so it is a bit hard and unnatural to control. It says I'm already 30% complete so that is a bit alarming especially at this price point.That aside, I applaud the makers for a decently made game that's complete with quality voice acting and reasonable accuracy to the more nuanced things about bees that the average person probably wouldn't know - such as how they use dances to tell each other directions, and don't get along well with wasps (I'd argue the average person doesn't know there's a difference between a bee and a wasp, I went most of my life not knowing).I would absolutely recommend this as a fantastic starter game for a younger kid - the demographic I somewhat expected steam decks to be going to. As for adults who don't mind products targeted at younger audiences (animated movies, etc.), it's probably good as well.Although it's very short, I do think the price is justified with how good the voice acting and overall polish is. I actually love short games that allow me to experience only the best parts of the game without wasting my time with unnecessary fluff just to increase play time. That said, I'd still probably not buy it at full price if I had to do it again unless I was specifically wanting this game. I think $15 would have been a lot easier to swallow. Still, I've paid $20 for games with no voice acting that clearly required much less budget than this game. A DLC with some additional side-quests or maps would be welcomed and would be an easy way to increase the value proposition of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest problem with Bee Simulator may sound like a tiny nitpick: but it is that it has the wrong name.And the reason that's more than a minor problem is because it presents the game as something it is not, creating a gulf of shortcomings where the game falls foul of expectations.To clarify: games following the "X Simulator" trend are not, necessarily, hyper-realistic. They don't need to be absurdly detailed. They are about making a playset; a toy, something in the real world that is being emulated in a virtual space for you to experiment with. Goat Simulator is probably the most tongue-in-cheek instance, but it is still arguably about experimentation and discovery.Bee Simulator, on the other hand, is a linear, narrative-driven arcade game with bees as characters. The driving motivation behind it appears to be spreading awareness about the plight of the honeybee; which is admirable. So too is the intention to actually make a game about something relatively unusual; and I laud both aims. However. All that said, this is not tumblr. Activism games —like educational games— only work when they are enjoyable games *first*, and instructive as a natural byproduct of enjoying them. BS (ha) is unfortunately more anvilicious in its moralising than the closing section of the 80s Inspector Gadget cartoons.Perhaps most importantly, the gameplay itself has really nothing to do with the subject it's exploring. As an example: collecting nectar is done by flying through hoops. It is essentially Pilotwings, with bees. And this is the real trend that needs bucking in the industry: not so much tired, hack subjects of games; but tired, hack designs that take gameplay from elsewhere and put new dressing on it, with no consideration for what makes the source material interesting in the first place.On the pro side, the game does look good and is well voice-acted (if terribly written). If you're in need of an easy, shallow experience with a wholesome subject matter —such as entertaining a small child— there may be a niche for it. And this is why I say its failing is an issue of how it presents itself. If it was pitched on par with the likes of Secret of the Magic Crystal, I may well have given it a recommendation.I look forward to the studio's future efforts. Perhaps it would be called Lobster Fishing Simulator, and you collect lobsters by driving a boat around in circles.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing i did was fly through some rings, the second thing i did was fly through some rings, the third fourth and fifth thing i did was fly through some rings. But then they mixed it up by adding a race, through rings!This is the first 0.3 hrs of the beginning of the game.A bee instructs you to gather pollen. Instead of the developers doing something worth a ♥♥♥♥ like having the player land on a flower and interacting with the stamen to collect pollen as in the real world, instead they added N64 Pilot Wings style game play. Why? Just ... why bother make this game? I thought this was going to be educational...In this reviewers opinion, this concept alone was a complete waste of potential and could easily be expanded on. Everything i have encountered is contrived and baser at best including the dialogue. Worst, it was the entirety of my experience so far.The intro of a game is where developers need to work hardest, if your intro is lackluster and bland then it does not give merit to continue playing. Like a book, the first page needs to grab the reader but if it keeps repeating sentences in the same paragraph then your going to lose them quickly. Like this review intro, im surprised your still reading this.Truth bombing your way through the intro is not going to carry the game by itself.  I get it, were all ♥♥♥♥♥♥, the planets burning and the bees are dying. But Im here to play an interesting Bee Simulator game, hoping to go pollinate flowers and bring some back to the hive, fight in tiny hive battles and become queen bee maybe save the world via honey. I found a bee that needs me to show it the way home through dance, great! Science!  Oh, but that bee is going to teach me the dance on the spot and also show me where it needs to go through a contrived race... ??!! ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wat?The developers could have easily made this work properly, Bee's innately know how to dance and are taught before leaving the hive. _childDocuments_.review: Hello friends,Today i will review the game BEE SIMULATOR. This game can be considered a Edutainment type of game. It teaches you about bee's and the decline of them, which is a real thing happening in the world right now, and how to help the bee population. There are even a glossary dedicated to telling players how to help the current bee population and how to protect them to keep them doing their job pollinating flowers to make delicious fruits. Again, the decline of the bee population is a real life issue, with other things such as viruses, parasites, mold, and even human destruction. As for the gameplay itself, it plays as a rpg where you assume the role of a female worker bee that job is to get pollen from flowers. Note that all bees are born female except one that mates with the queen. After leaving the hive, the world is pretty big for the bee. The player can also do side quests, such as dancing, fighting wasps and other bugs, help other insects to do things, and even help animals find things. The quests in the game are the basic rpg type, either fetch, button pushing, or go here to find X. Some people have reported issues with controllers, but if you have a external program that lets you change buttons, you can rebind the keys. You can also do it in the game, but most people do not like how it is done. Perhaps i am used to doing it as i did it before with other games, but i found no issue with my controller. It functioned exactly fine with this game. I used a ZEN PRO switch controller that is also compatible with PC's. Anyways, here is my PROS and CONS list:PROS:- A game where you play as a female worker bee helping the hive.- Learn about bee's and how to help them in real life.- Side quests to do to help the hive.- Co-Op mode that allows split screen to play with 2 players at once. This can be used on remote play together to play with 2 people.- Collectible items including hats, different bee skins, and different steams that go behind the character when flying as a bee.- A game perfect for young children to teach about ecology and learn about honey bee's and how they interact with the environment.- Works with controllers. I used a ZEN PRO switch controller.- Works with windows 11 OS (Operating System).CONS:- Some player have mentioned issues with controllers and binding keys. I personally had no issues with this.- Loading times when booting up the game may take some time, up to 1 to 2 minutes.- No maps to direct you to different areas of the park. There is a fast travel function though.- Co-Op mode has some collectibles, but you can only get them in Co-Op mode. Be aware when playing remote together, one person will be on the controller, and the other will use the keyboard.Do I recommend the game? Yes, it is fine as it is. It is a great source to learn more about bee's and their functions in ecology. The game play is similar to a RPG where the player can do side quests, fight enemies, and do random stuff to help other insects. The Co-Op mode could be fun, but i personally did not try it, and when i did, i could not really play it. It is not recommended to play Co-Op mode with 1 person.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for July 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before August 3rd, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Something Something Jerry Seinfeld.  I’m sure I’m not the only one who thought of the Bee Movie when they heard about this, right?  Bee Simulator is a story-based open-world game where players explore a large map as a bee.  While it looks like this could be similar to Goat Simulator, it’s more story-based with players being tasked with various jobs from the hive. This is almost edutainment. There’s a heavy focus on bee information, and the game is quite clever.  There are even subtle pieces where they point at the fact the main character is female because she leaves the hive, the queen communicates while releasing odors and pheromones, and bees dance to communicate.  Someone has done their homework. The story and missions are decent, and the gameplay is good.  There’s a lot of discoverability and collecting of different parts of the game if players want to see everything.  The main story is said to be two hours long.   Also, there is the fact that it probably shouldn’t be called a simulator, it’s just a typical game. Pick this up if you want a game where you play as a bee, or want to learn a little more about these tiny animals.  Some of the systems are a bit clunky, and I found myself needing to use the d-pad at times, as well as ending on a rather hard race, but I find myself wanting to return to see more of this world. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: I can't take anymore. Do NOT trust the "Very Positive" rating. I think the nice message about saving bees is influencing the reviews. The game is terrible and the title is misleading—this is not a simulator at all. This is a game for very young children that puts on the facade of being educational.Luckily I didn't pay $29,99 for the game, but I did waste a pick from my Humble Bundle Choice subscription.  This game should be priced under $7. If you purchased this game, I implore you, get a refund before it's too late! The controls are surprisingly good once you get into the first few missions, but you should definitely crank up your mouse sensitivity. _childDocuments_.review: An interesting experience. Loved the art style during the story telling. The story itself is rather short for how large a map this game has. There are large chunks of the map that are never visited or explored unless you just fly out there on your own to explore. There's no quests or tasks or reason to actually explore the full map which, I feel, was a serious mistake on the developer's part. Why bother making such an extensive, open world, map but not have many more things to do in it? While it's a fun game that kept me riveted during the story, it was boring and lackluster with how it never really followed through on all the potential. This needed to be developed further both in content and in overall plot development. I mean, the main character has knowledge about human technology that neither she nor her hive sisters had ever encountered before. Are we really supposed to believe she gained this knowledge from a brief flight across the park? Knowing exactly what the device was called and its purpose? Give me a break. Things like that really broke the immersion and left a lot of questions unanswered. Worth playing but not worth the price for how empty, undeveloped and repetitive the game is.

_childDocuments_.review: Has enough positive reviews that I feel comfortable leaving a thumbs-down.It's not a bad game per se, but it's definitely not a deep, serious or complex bee "simulator". It's casual to the point where it feels like a kid's game, with the intent to garner interest and sympathy for honeybees. It does an okay job, but in doing so completely leaves out the massive positive impact many other less known or liked insects have on the world (including bees native to the US, which honeybees are not) and providing cutesy simplistic minigames and a basic world with basic mechanics to travel around in. I was drawn in by the visuals, and then bounced off the gameplay and the lack of anything else present interactive-wise in the ecosystem that didn't directly affect bees (pesticides were weirdly absent too, but then again I only played a little over an hour). I actually tend to like cute casual games like this, but I was let down by how simple, inaccurate, and clunky a good portion of the game feels. Plus I ran into a couple frustrating bugs (no pun intended).It feels much more designed for controller, but as others did I experienced some issues with actually using one. While many have clearly enjoyed this, I didn't, and want to leave this as both a message about the inaccuracy (and absence) of some important information, as well as letting some people know that this game really won't be their jam despite what's advertised.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off with the positive parts of the game;It's cute sometimes and looks nice and the flying is okay.And now for the negatives;It's pretty bad. From the plot to the narrative to the gameplay to the minigames, it's all subpar or awful. This game is called Bee Simulator yet offers no basic simulation mechanics, it's a really short linear story with some minigames. The story makes no damn sense, and whoever learned their bee facts for this game knew like ten of them and then just guessed everything else it seems like. The Plot: The whole story is you are a newly grown bee that is learning the ropes to become a pollen collector. So one would assume that okay, we gather the pollen and bring it back to the hive to make honey or whatever, maybe help expand the hive by doing this or try and make some sort of quota. Nope, you go and fly through some circles near like ten plants to gather some pollen and then immediately be bombarded by sidequests or other storylines about other bugs and squirrels for some reason? Your characters job is to be a pollen collector yet you only do that for about 3 short missions, collect 30 common pollen, collect 20 rare pollen, collect 10 epic pollen and then boom never bother with that again. Instead your character is constantly trying to do something else, like help some recently grown bees that got lost in a tree somehow? Or investigate a bee drone, or constantly disobeying orders to try and look for new hive spots (even though there should be tons of scouts fully capable of that, she could easily have just told some of them she saw nice spots), or even going off to fight fricken hornets somehow... Yet the game is constantly being peddled as this sort of accurate representation of bees with all this dialogue about bee facts and yet I can take on hornets by the droves as a single honey bee. So little is cohesive about this and it jumps around so much it's rather annoying, and then it all ends so suddenly. The Narrative: Throughout the game there is this 'save the bees' sort of narrative going on, with the narrative telling you all sorts of bee facts. While I suppose there is nothing really wrong inherently with this, combined with the ridiculous nature of the actual gameplay and story I feel like it just fails to really give any sort of meaningful commentary that is backed up by the game itself as many of the things told about bees is almost immediately shown false in the games' world. Born to be a pollen gatherer? Nope, you are an ambitious bee who is also a master warrior capable of taking down swathes of hornets, beat almost every bee and other creatures in races, and also scout more efficiently than entire droves of scout bees. Hornets are a dangerous predator that can easily kill many species of bees, however there are some defensive tactics bees can use (this technique is never mentioned in the game btw, I just like bees) such as luring hornets into their hives and surrounding them, beating their wings to raise the temperature so much that they literally cook the hornet. This however takes many bees to actually perform, so does the game with it's narrative of bee knowledge bother to mention any relevant facts to how a bee might fight back against a hornet? Nah, a hornet busts into the bee hive, two bees (out of the hundreds floating around) notice it (you and some other bee) and the other bee runs to tell the queen to get back up to fight this hornet while you, as a single ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bee, decide to stay and hold off this comically bad supervillain hornet. Not to mention, shouldn't they have just released a ton of warning pheromones? How did a hornet manage to slip into a massive beehive without so much as a single bee death or any warnings from scouts, guards, or pollen collectors on their way in and out of the hive? The world may never know...Gameplay: The only thing that is kind of fun is the flying mechanics. The game insists are starting the sensitivity ridiculously low that I couldn't even imagine how someone could manage to turn their bee around without using a whole table, but once almost maxed out actually offers a decent flight experience. Flying around the park as a bee was just pretty fun and is pretty much the only redeeming quality about this game other than some decent visuals. The gameplay basically just consists of doing the main story quests, three different types of minigames (battle, race, dancing), and dropping off pollen at the hive when you get full. Collecting the same rarity of flower multiple times gives you a speed boost so generally you want to collect some at first when leaving the hive, though when you get further out there is sweets you can eat that more efficiently do this without making you go back the hive. To specify the minigames a bit more in depth; The battle minigame is basically you fighting hornets that are like comical middleschool bullies. It's not awful, and actually has a medium amount of difficulty when fighting bosses, but everything else is crazy easy when you figure out the mechanics. You can attack straight, up, and down and block in the same directions. Most of the enemy AI will act the exact same if you follow through with the same mechanics, such as: Start the fight with a down attack, attack forward twice, followed by an up attack, block, counter, down attack, up attack, forward attack, super special (always forward cause its fastest), forward attack x2, down attack. Sometimes the ai will throw a curveball at you, but mostly this was the ritual I fell into and I could easily kill a first opponent this way. Often the enemies will get confused if you attack from the bottom and will immediately go for a forward block after their bottom block, and if you are aggressive enough you can easily use this to your advantage to attack them the moment they stop shielding. The race minigame is fairly easy most of the time and is quite lenient, so if you fall behind the enemy racer will actually slow down for you or will take wider turns to let you catch up which you can easily use to your advantage to catch them. Basically the racing just consists of not falling behind (or catching the enemy racer) by flying through rings and avoiding wind tunnels and some obstacles. It's pretty basic.The dancing minigame is you just copying the moves of another bee (up, left, down, right) to get directions. I feel like a lot more could have been done with this, but it's literally just a copying minigame. There are no upgrades of any sort, or any purpose other than to do these minigames and story missions other than some trophies you can easily get by just flying around and getting pollen for the tree. My advice? Just get about 2k research (what pollen turns into when delivered to a hive) on the tutorial mission and you won't need any for basically the rest of the game. Setting and Visuals: The whole game takes place in a park with a really sad zoo next to it. There is also a small lake.  The speed of your bee makes the area feel quite large though, especially on you initial foray out of the hive, but it quickly starts to feel small. It all looks rather nice, and there is plenty of activity that does make everything seem lively. When you fly by people and animals they give a little 'bump' interaction. You can interact with some stuff, like popping balloons and stinging random people, but it's pretty shallow. I personally just like bees so I thought a lot of the bee interactions (like picking up mushrooms with your tiny feet) was just really cute. When your pollen level gets full you have big clumps of pollen on your legs which is a nice touch. Overview:The game was meh. The visuals were nice and some parts of the story were cute and the flying mechanics felt good. But ultimately this was almost a flop in every other sector. This wasn't a bee simulator, it's a short linear story. I honestly would have refunded this if I hadn't gotten it off of humble bundle choice. 3.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's an alright game, but I'm recommending not getting this game for a few reasons. There are some things it does well such as the music, but it doesn't make up for what you get.1. When you play it, it's very clearly geared towards kids. While this by itself isn't a problem, it is when the advertising doesn't really hint at it.2. It has a misleading name. It wouldn't be accurate to call this a bee simulator. Instead it's more of a collection of mini-games that won't be that challenging. In addition, there's less than five mini-games as well, despite that being the main core of the game.3. It's not accurate enough. While normally I'd wouldn't care too much how accurate a game is, this game makes it seem like it's going to be teaching you stuff about bees. Despite that, there are lies that are put in to make the game more exciting. They don't make it obvious that these things aren't true. The most obvious is when your character regularly takes out multiple wasps. 4. Despite the fact that this game is 30 dollars, you only get about 2-4 hours of gameplay. Voices are also quite childish which is not for everyone but personally this doesn't bother me in the slightest.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: You'll learn about bees (mainly) and other insects, fly around as a bee in a huge park, explore and collect pollen. A nice, easy and chill game. It's not a totally  simulator game but more light-hearted and cute which I think works well. There's a main story and lots of side quests, like helping some ants cross the water and other activities/challenges, like fighting wasps, racing, collecting pollen from specific flowers and more. A pretty simple game but there's nothing wrong with that. You can also buy skins/hats/trails for your bee - so you can be a bee with a cowboy hat if you want! There's an in-game encyclopedia for the different plants and insects you encounter - like a sticker book - so there's quite a few things to collect and discover as well. I didn't do every little thing in the game but after playing for nearly 13 hours I've had my fill of honey and have learned a little bit more about bees and to appreciate them more. 🌼🐝
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Bad controls. Xbox gamepad won't work properly from the start without loading a fresh default pad profile. Controls on gamepad can't be changed in settings. Flight model is 'hold left stick up to go forward' while the triggers are wasted on ascend/descend. Camera bobs way too hard and the first person camera isn't permitted in the race events. Co-op is a tiresome grind with zero progress/improvement, only cosmetics to tease you along. Seriously, they expect me to do 18 of every activity to unlock a new species of bee? No reason to bring pollen home, it doesn't record or reward anything, it's just an arbitrary gauge to fill and empty. Speaking of empty, the maps are bland and static. Nothing happens in them, the npcs just sit in one place and some respond to being bumped with a sound or a brief disjointed animation. The city has cars driving through it, and nothing of interest besides balloons to pop. Each co-op map is a chore after about twenty minutes. Dancing as a bee is just the game Simon, but you must use the analog sticks (instead of the dpad wtf) and repeat a sequence of directionals. Half of combat is a laggy rhythm game of hitting x or y when told to. The other half is a weird rock-paper-scissor type affair. The 'races' tend to be 'chases' where you try to overtake a bee flying through hoops. Miss three hoops and lose. This is usually just a tense fight with the camera.Feels like this game was made by a 50+ year old hobbyist for their kids/grandkids. Meanwhile the music and art departments had a successful crowd funding or something. I should have loved this game; it's an animal sim, it's a meditative flyer, it's local co-op. Despite ticking all those niches this game is just not fun and doesn't interest me. The animal simulation is puddle-deep. The flying is total garbage. The co-op lacks any progression and gets old real quick. For better bug simulation, try Drunk on Nectar. For better flying try Fugl or anything that doesn't use the sticks for thrust. For the exact same family-friendly local co-op but with cats try Play With Gilbert. Thanks for reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: This was a brilliant game to play.   It's full of heart, with some good voice acting, fun challenges, and loads to do.   Some of the world interactions are fun, and the graphics and sound are good enough to make the world seem vibrant and engaging.The game revolves around a plot where you are a bee (obvs) who has to help the queen to move the hive.  Loads of tasks to locate resources, find locations, solicit help and avoid dangers.    The world is beautifully laid out and there's a lot of diverse environments, most seamlessly connected, such as inside a kitchen, a lake, the inside of a tree and a zoo.It's hard to fault the game really,  my daughter played it through, and now loves bees, and always wants to protect them and find out more about them.  We visited a honey farm and saw lots of bees, and she was fascinated.  Amazingly, the graphics in the game reflected the shapes of the honeycombs in the natural hives too, which she was thrilled at. "Look! That's just like the honeycombs in the roof in Bee Simulator!" she said at one point.The game's really easy to follow, there's not many controls.  There are a few points where you have to follow someone, or get somewhere in a hurry that may tax really young kids, but anyone from the age of 7 with basic keyboard/mouse skills can easily play the game.I didn't know what to expect, but was very pleased with this.  Hope they make a DLC or sequel at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: The concept has great potential. I enjoyed the first 35 minutes. It could have been a better game if the bees had more personality & if it wasn't presented as a simulator. I haven't completed the game and won't. I paid under 4 $ so I can't complain, but according to the achievements, most people don't play for more than 2 hours.Pros : Warm, easy and educative. It raises awareness of an important issue for the future of humanity.Cons : Pollination is too "arcade". You cannot land on flowers. You also can't die or sting anyone. You can fight, which doesn't really make sense to a polenizer bee (+ a bee who would lose their sting if they used it and die). The anatomy of bees is not true to reality. You can dance, but dances are useless since bees are also talking to each other in the game. There's a lack of realism while it's a "simulator" which is intended to be educational... The whole isn't coherent.Probably a good game for kids under 13!ps: Protect the bees IRL, plant flowers and get informed about domestic or urban beekeeping, please. Thanks <3

_childDocuments_.review: 🐝 A small exciting adventure for a couple of hours, which offers you to feel like a real bee, but in a more fabulous & funny way. Just don’t choose the Hard mode, the only difference is that battles aren't qte, but tactical reaction fights (with a choice of shield position and attack angle), as well as more difficult opponents in races – it’s all a waste of time (sometimes with obvious frustration from balance), that won't allow you to really get distracted and relax in the local nature flights. _childDocuments_.review: As proud owner of the Honeycomb Hideout Discord Server and a bee enthusiast, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. I streamed it to all of my friends and we got great joy from it. Not only does this game have Skyrim and possibly an "It" by Stephen King reference, I'm positive that there is more to bee discovered. At this moment, I have played through the main story on Easy. Hard mode is hard. At the very least, not as easy as Easy. Graphics are great, since I cannot actually go to a zoo these days, it is fantastic to see one in game and actually learn about animals. I mean the only thing I have to say about the scientific accuracy of the game, is that as far as bee facts go, it's spot on. Even down to how they deal with wasp intruders. Did anyone else catch that? However, I have a hard time seeing a bearded dragon in a tropical area, and seeing it climb walls? It's hilarious. People are saying oh it's for kids its for kids, well so is Fortnite and Minecraft and I've played both. Speaking of Minecraft, I rebound the controls to have shift = down, spacebar = up, Q = BeeTurbo, E = Confirm/Skip. Improved the whole game for me.How many people buy steam games for wholesale price? Bee simulator will go on sale, put it on your wishlist if you are reading this from the future and wait. Honestly, I do believe it is worth at least $20, if not more. I will pay more money if donations go towards saving bees. That would be really awesome. As far as Steam Achievements and Xbox controller integrations go, to me, it really seems like a Steam problem, not a Bee Simulator problem. I could bee wrong but it's just a feeling I have. If you like simulator games, bees, beeautiful graphics, and just chilling out and not having to worry about everything that is going on in the world right now, walk in the shoes of a bee.

_childDocuments_.review: No, this is terrible. The combat is a complete mess and the gameplay of collecting flowers by rarity is stupidly tacked on. Speaking of tacked on, you can totally tell that they just wanted to make a little bee arcade game and then someone forced them to shoehorn in the whole "Save the Bees!" story elements. Yeah, I love bees, but it's native and bumble bees that are dying out and this game isn't about that. Also this game isn't about saving the bees, it just yells at you occasionally about saving the bees, and excuse me, but I'm not running around tossing insecticides everywhere just for fun. Lecturing me does no good.The actual flying mechanics are mostly good. My only real complaints are with the controls for rising and falling being too slow, and the mouse sensitivity is way, way, way too low (even turned up to max).If this game was open world, or had more things to interact with or see I would have enjoyed it more. _childDocuments_.review: Bee Simulator is a simulation game where you take control of a honey bee and explore an open world while collecting and storing pollen for the upcoming winter season.== Pros ==*Controls are pretty smooth and a hell of a lot smoother than I thought they'd be - even when you're speeding through the open world it was very hard to crash into something.*Several side quests and minigames to complete.*You can customize your bee's skin, headwear, and trail.*Graphics are really nice.*As you're exploring animals and plants get added to an encylopedia which includes 3D models you can view.*The game gives players some real-world advice on how to "help the bees" which I think is pretty unique for a game.*Music is enjoyable and relaxing.== Cons ==*The main story can be completed in 2 hours, but it still leaves you feeling unsatisfied. In addition the story's pacing is off and it seems things randomly happen.*The voice acting seems out of place and the accents chosen for some of the characters is really out of place (why is a wasp talking like a Spanish conquistador)?*The open world, although it looks beautiful and promising, isn't as grandiose as I would like. There's side quests and minigames peppered in and some oddball achievements to complete but you can't interact with any humans or animals unless they're part of a quest, there's very few collectibles to pick up and just wish it was utilized better than it was.All in all, Bee Simulator is a cute little game with a very unique premise. If you're looking for a casual game where you play as a bee - this is for you! I recommend buying it when it's on sale unless it's something you absolutely "gotta have".
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: As I am both passionate and know a lot about bees and slowly becoming a beekeeper myself, I had to get this game! I got it in the sale as I wasn’t sure about it at first but glad I did! It’s actually a really pleasantly relaxing game to play minus the frustrating and pointless “races” you have to do!I think it would have been better to gradually work your way up as a worker honeybee as the second you’re born in the game, you become a worker, which is not accurate at all as honeybees get assigned various roles in the hive such as nurse bee, guard bee and then a worker! I also think it would have been a bit more fun to physically land on flowers to collect the pollen / nectar. Also, when honeybees sting they usually die unless they’re lucky and “unscrew” themselves but again, that probably would have been too much effort and annoying for the game!Shame the game mainly focuses on honeybees although there’s unlockable skins with various solitary bees, which I think are native to the USA such as the blue orchid bee, but I would have also loved to have seen bumblebees cos the game lacks those 🙁The ending is a little big sad *SPOILERS* the humans cut down your tree hive and you then have to rehome in a building roof, which I think was a silly ending cos technically if that was real, you should report a swarm in your house to your local beekeeper, so that isn’t good education! It would have been a lot better if the ending was a beekeeper rescuing you for their hive!Overall, the game is nearly as accurate as it would be to become a real honeybee such as the ultraviolet bee vision as that’s how bees detect flowers (not by their rarity lol). It’s nice it educates you on bee friendly flowers and other little facts on bees.Only downside with the game is the talking, annoying races cos the flying is really tricky to control and the cringy bee puns! Oh, and bees do NOT feed off sweet food - please don't do this!Hopefully I can get all achievements!🐝🐝🐝🐝

_childDocuments_.review: This is neither a bee simulator or anything remotely educational. It's just an arcade flyer that has an insect theme. I mean how dumb can you get when you're assuming that bees want pollen? Bees get nectar from flowers. They only inadvertently spread pollen after drinking nectar. They don't eat or care about pollen at all. Also, bees need to land on flowers to collect food. They don't just fly through it. Change the name to Bee Arcade because this is anything but a Bee Simulator.UPDATE Apparently bees do eat pollen, specifically larvae. I'm still right about nectar being what they actively harvest.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: From a game called "bee simulator" I expected something with a little more substance. This could have been done in a number of ways. Maybe a game where you can actually see some of the struggles of a bee's life. Like their hard work collecting pollen, or how they have to survive humans trying to squash them. If you want to add a story about the invironmental impact on bee's lives that could be done too if taken seriously. There's a number of other ways but Bee Simulator does none of them.The very first thing anyone will hear is the voice of a female voiceactors best impression of a child? Everyone (and I actually think there's only one voice actor doing what sounds like the same voice for different bees) talks in this extremely childish way. Couple that with the constant badly done wordplay ("keeping bee-sy?", nitro is called beetro, you get the idea) and even a young child might feel it's intelligence being insulted.So despite the title "bee simulator", this game is aimed at small children? That title really is so poorly chosen. But why go for the (kinda) realistic aesthetic than? Stylised graphics would have been so much better. This game obviously doesn't have the biggest budget behind it so it would probably have been cheaper to go in that direction anyway.The graphics/animations are a missed opportunity in another way as well. When you polinate a flower that flower opens up. If you've ever played the game "flower" from that game company than you know how beautiful it can be. However because of the camera angle in bee simulator you don't really get to see it and that's a real shame.  For a moment I thought Bee Simulator could actually be a spiritual successor to flower. I think it tries to be but fails. The gameplay, like others have pointed out, consists of minigames. Some have time limits but luckily there's the an easy and a hard option. Anyone should be able to complete the easy option. Controls themselves are quite good and easy enough for most but at the same time if it really is directed at the youngest of children then I doubt they have the necessary coördination to move in 3D as well as up and down. I could be wrong, someone else should test that out. The controls are good though but can feel clunky at times, as does the camera. No big issues, but it could use some polish. The game has been in development for long enough and has already seen many updates so I didn't expect that. Minigames consist of time trial races, battles, pollen collection and dances. All of them are fine. There is a kind of environmental message in here but it's so on the nose and lacks substance. Probably, again, aimed at children. It's not really a bad game, it's just kinda there. It exists. I don't know who it's for or why it was made. I'm really very confused as to who this is supposed to be for. But it definitely exists it's very non-offensive and both it's story and it's gameplay. Again, steam only offers me the option for a thumbs up (recommended) and down (not recommended) rating. Since I can't actually recommend anyone play this, I'll give it a thumbs down. But it's not like I recommend people to not play it either.Oh and I got this in a bundle but that price here on steam is completely ridiculous. The game is like 2 or 3 hours long or something. A few hours more if you squeeze it for all the honey it has, but why would you?

_childDocuments_.review: Review updated to include fixes to the game. (17/05/2021)I first saw Bee Simulator on the Epic Games Store and had intended to buy at some point last year. Lucky for me it later arrived on Steam and I brought it during the autumn sale. I must admit I was taken back on how expansive the game is. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, so controllers don't work on it and that sucks, given it has 'controller support', but the thumb sticks aren't working.  Anyone who is familiar with the concept of simulator games knows what to expect - essentially a fun little sandbox romp of doing the same tasks, over and over, for amusement when you're too tired or stressed for a game with actual challenges and responsibilities.   On that front, the game delivers exactly what you would expect. It is fun. It has the appeal of being able to pick it up, and do not much of anything for a bit to occupy your brain. I like bees, I need simple games on occasion, this meets my needs. I do wish that it was a little longer in terms of story, as the main story itself is only about 2 hours at most if you don't get too sidetracked.By far the best part of this game is the sub-Bethesda level voice acting where you can sometimes hear someone drop out of their American or Spanish accent back into whatever accent it is they have, which seems to be vaguely Scandinavian. Makes it enjoyable to listen to, it is meme-tier gold.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty adorable game! Very cute bees and some luscious art work to boot. A pleasant and relaxing game for older players, and a bright and cute game for younger players, Lots of side quests as well which is a thoroughly fun experience. though I'd recommend easy mode for the kids since the game can be fairly challenging at times in the harder difficulty, even for adults. It defenitely lives up to the name of bee simulator.As for some downs, the graphics can be a little spotty and some vegetation, especially trees, are prone to "pop in" from low resolution to high. And without beetro (speed boost from food and pollen) regular flight can feel painfully slow over long distances, fortunately it's easy to gain though. The main story line as well is fairly short, about 3-4 hours of content in the quests. All in all a good game for adults and a great game for kids! Very recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is amazing! The graphics are beautiful, and it's family friendly. While I do highly recommend this game, I have to also discuss my problem with this game. The European Honeybee, the one we all refer to as the honeybee, is HIGHLY invasive. Wasps actually do more for pollination than the honeybee. These honeybees are awful for the ecosystems they inhabit and make life hell for our native bees that do more of the pollinating work. I love bees, I think they're cute, but as someone who has studied entomology, I also recognize how awful they are for non-native areas. So, while it is a great game, do not listen to the misinformation it feeds you.

_childDocuments_.review: for more reviews.A worker bee lives for around 30-60 days. I'm convinced that's the time frame in which this game was made. It's boring, bland, and should be priced no where near the current $30 price tag. I completed the main story, and spent an additional hour and a half - 2 hours flying around trying to find things to keep me entertained before giving up on the game and uninstalling it, here are my thoughts.Bee Simulator is a game that is made for small children, but due to  the controls being as sensitive as the average Tumblr user, I don't see how even younger children will be able to play this game. I turned the controller sensitivity down as low as it would go and I was still finding myself unable to control my bee at times. Awful controls aside, this game offers nothing to keep you playing. The story is stupidly short and boring. Within 30 minutes of playing this game you'll have seen and done everything this game has to offer and the rest of the game is just repeating the same boring "minigames" over and over again, and there's no way to upgrade your bee or make anything faster which is annoying because everything in this game takes 2-3 times longer than it should. The slow as molasses cut scenes, minigames, and flying speed make a realistically 45 minute story take an hour and a half to get through. The developers made some shocking choices when it came to game mechanics. In order to fly at full speed you need to have energy which you can get by eating sugary treats like cookies or cupcakes. At full energy you get to move at full speed for about 30 seconds. Guess how long it takes to fill up this energy bar. About 30 seconds. THIS IS THE MOST FRUSTRATING THING I'VE EVER DEALT WITH IN A VIDEO GAME. NO ONE WANTS TO FLUTTER AROUND AT THE SPEED OF A 2 LEGGED WART HOG TRAVELING AROUND THIS MASSIVE WORLD WHERE GETTING TO POINT A TO POINT B TAKES 5 MINUTES AT TIMES. HOW THE DEVELOPERS THOUGHT THIS WAS OK BOGGLES MY MIND. This game was genuinely a chore to play through. The developers really padded out this game's playtime as much as they possible could and then have the balls to charge $30 for what is essentially a 25 minute game demo that was thrown together in the Unity engine by an aspiring game developer. Ok I don't wanna end this review on a negative because there is one thing this game does brilliantly. This game teaches you a lot about bees. In fact, the amount of knowledge and education this game has to offer is the only reason I played this game for longer than 30 minutes. There's all kind of facts you learn throughout the story and the game has resources built into the game to where you can learn how to help bees in the wild. Unfortunately copy and pasting a bunch of information from Wikipedia doesn't justify spending $30 on a crappy game. If you really like bees then go watch a National Geographic documentary and eat some honey buns because you'll enjoy that far more than you'll enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: nOt tHe BeEsThis game's title does it a disservice. You'd be forgiven for thinking this is a some kind of meme game like goat simulator or any thing like that. I thought so myself before getting this. This feels much more genuine than that and I think many will be offput by the simulator affix. It's not a simulator at all (not a bad thing in and of itself).As a game, it's a straightforward collection of minigames strung together by a narrative, with a surprisingly good score on top.. There are educational elements here and there and there's definitely an angle of bee-awareness here (There's an entire menu devoted just to real things you can do to help bees). Despite some clunky controls and budget voice acting, i appreciate the thought here and could see it being enjoyable in a classroom setting for instance.My personal opinion,  the game would have been better off leaning more into a less realistic aesthetic and not pretend that it's a simulator. The game Flower for instance managed to convey it's environmental message effectively with no such pretenses and with no dialogue, and there are some similarities between this and Flower. This isn't anywhere near as good as Flower, but it has similarities for sure.Do i like it myself? No not really. Got this as part of a humble bundle that had other things i wanted so my investment is tiny. But i think it's good to leave reviews for honest efforts especially ones that try to be educational/helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an educational game for many preschool children, not a bee life simulator. A real simulator should be more like The Isles, where you actually have to survive as a dinosaur, or The Forest, where you simulate survival as a human in a wild environment. Here we have education for the youngest. It seems like a mockery to me. You could really make a great game with the atmosphere of the forest, meadows, wild animals, and the realities of survival. And not flying around in the park among children, the zoo, flower girls and other things that have nothing to do with the real experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial reaction:"This is barely a game, and if you assume it's aimed at young children even then it's not going to hold their interest."Welcome to Bee Simulator. And by that I mean a couple of uninteresting minigames and then flying through rings with clumsy controls while the game spits bee facts at you with the condescending voice of a kindergarten teacher. It's simple, repetitive gameplay that cycles you through the same 3 minigames over and over (if you bother to do the side content) and it was so tedious I was watching someone streaming the Zelda CDI game at the same time and said to myself "I envy this man".I received this game for free (part of Humble Monthly) and I still want my money back. Normally I try to make it a point to get all the achievements in these short and content-less games but it was difficult even to get myself to finish the story missions in this one. It's probably an hour of gameplay if you do none of the side content and you'd probably get better use out of that hour playing literally any other game because a terrible game is at least something you can laugh about. This was just disappointing on an existential level.The pros: They did a great job at setting up the areas themselves, there was a lot of detail both big and small and I really commend them for that. But I wish they had used that effort to make the game more interesting instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending this game, but only if you want to play a quick fun bee themed game. Playing as a bee is a fun experience, especially since you're pretty free to explore the park and the zoo. The game gives cute extra fun facts about bees, flowers, and wild animals. The main story is pretty short, and afterwards really only achievement hunting and little side quests remain. The achievements are pretty bugged though, so hunting for them is terrrible. Plus the game has trouble starting up sometimes, which at one point even made me lose an almost complete save game. Overall I would still recommend the game, but just know that there are some issues.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute relaxing game. Family friendly and definitely geared towards kids. It teaches a decent amount about bees. It's the the generic simulator style game. The world is vibrant and pretty big in scale to your little bee. The story is linear. The objectives are relatively the same with some mini-games spread around. _childDocuments_.review: This is my first time writing a review for a game and unfortunately it is because the game was rather disappointing, especially in the way how it wraps itself up.  I wasn't sure what to expect from this game so it was quite enjoyable initially. When I was at the end-game phase though, its clunkiness was quite obvious and the technical issues I was experiencing caused more frustration. Some of the issues I had were that:- The game is glitchy, where it does not save properly. I lost my progress several times towards the endgame. This is especially frustrating when you have finished a grindly achievement and to see it disappear (happened twice). - It lacks functionality in its controls. For example, ability to carry more pollen at an end-game phase would be really helpful.- Mini-games within the game itself are varied in its difficulty going from stupidly hard (for no apparent reason) to stupidly easy.- It gets quite repetitive and the pace is rather slow; while this may not be a necessary a bad thing, it has a potential to produce polarising opinions about the game.Overall feel is that this game is unpolished product that began with a grand idea but fails to wrap itself up nicely as a game. I have given up trying to get 100% achievement because it is just too much hassle for its worth and it's not because it requires skill, it's because the technical issues are so apparent. If you were after a relatively straightforward game to kill a few hours, then this game will be entertaining as there definitely is a novelty factor. However, if you are after a well-polished game that considers gamers' experience at a deeper level, this game does not deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very ~  ~ game, you do learn a lot about bees though. I found the ascending and descending controls pretty sensitive when trying to land on the "human" food, Main story was a little short, only took me about 2.5 hours to complete. Extra time on file is just trying to obtain all achievements. If you're going to buy this game make sure you complete the side quests in the first hive before moving to the next hive, otherwise if you want to 100% the game you'll have to do another save file.There's a few reports of people not receiving their achievements however I didn't experience this problem.Overall an enjoyable, educational  game,  not worth the full price through the Steam store but for sure worth grabbing if it's ever on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, and it does have some nice visuals, but I couldn't get past the story's narrative and constant dialogue. Sure, flying around as a bee was fun, but the controls were a little cumbersome and the dialogue was often intrusive when random bees start talking to you just because you fly passed them. The script is very much geared towards a younger audience and, while I don't always mind that, it came off as almost berating for an adult audience.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was thrown off because I could immediately tell it was for kids by the dialog and voice acting. A 4 year old could play this. And I was also not thrilled about the combat system. I thought it would be like other animal sims which let you fight freely but they made a cool little system that kids could grasp easily. The Hard setting does provide a little more fun. But the environments look very pretty. The exploring, collecting pollen, looking for special flowers, buying skins with the pollen I've collected are all pretty fun aspects of the game. It is open world but story driven. After an hour of gameplay so far, I think I will enjoy this game on the days I just want to chill.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Get it -on sale-. The mini-games can be a toss-up depending on your preference (you'll either have fun or be very annoyed/bored) and the story is very short for $20, but movement and exploration as a bee is a very enjoyable experience. It's difficult to do an educational game right, and Bee Simulator leans on the side of done right. If you'd like to get a solid, non-cloying educational game for your child or just want a relaxing experience as an adult, I do recommend this game. But only for a reduced price.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this in Humble Monthly. Thought this game would just be memes. You know collect pollen, sting some folks, and fly around.If you can look past the extremely terrible inputs. Some times it recognized my controller, some times it did not. Usually either a load or entering an options menu fixed this for me. Slightly annoying, but not a stain to ruin the experience. More disappointing seeing this in Unreal Engine after 20+ years.The graphics, story, and controls were just mediocre. A short main story, littered with side quests(There's like 12 throughout the game) and mini games (I.E. the finding the bees in the park, fighting wasps, racing other insects around, stopping the bully kids, etc.) What's going to keep people in the game a long time is the achievements, if not following a guide will just be done through thorough exploration and experimentation. Otherwise you can probably blow through the entire story line in a few hours. I really enjoyed the art style used in the "video" parts of the story. Although I wouldn't necessarily call it animation. It's like 2 FPS as far as animation goes. (Hint for those that know nothing about animation: That's not a lot. That's worse fps animation than 90's anime.) The voice acting was kind of atrocious too. The Queen, and many others sounded very dry and forced. In fact the main character is the only one that showed any sort of consistency. The ability that allows you to fly faster drains a little quickly. You're often going to find yourself full of pollen and very far away from the hive, with little option for stopping to refill it, slowly chugging along until you get to a food item to replenish it or to the hive to continue story line.  Everything is found by markers on the map. It will a giant colored light tunnel (Green, red, white,blue, etc) Everything you need for a quest has this same type of aura also. You can literally be brand new to video games and beat this. The toughest part will be coordination with movement and camera for certain quests. You cannot die, and if you fail something it just restarts you. (These last 2 are not negative, a lot of folks will probably like this since it feels less like failure and more like "Oh I just have to learn this area of the game")Despite all of those things and sounding like a negative time, it really was not. In fact it was very enjoyable. I muted all the sounds in the game, threw on a Spotify playlist and just meandered around. All I really wanted to do was collect some pollen, fly around, and sting some people and other animals. In that respect it fulfilled my expectations and beyond.In all honesty this is probably one of the better games Humble Choice has ever spit at me. It was a meditative experience, just a real chill time. Plus you can unlock cosmetics in game by earning points from literally just playing the game and doing quests. So that was really cool.It wasn't the greatest thing I ever played, but Bee Simulator by far was no where near the worst. I have played some absolutely terrible games, Bee Simulator is holding a solid 6.5/10. If you want a super relaxing and chill game, where you're just exploring, doing quests/side quests, or mini games (None of which are forced upon you. You can literally do what you want in the game) then this is for you. If you're more the action packed, non stop thrills n chills, and surprises around every corner type, turn around, this is not what you seek.

_childDocuments_.review: A enjoyable relaxing simulator that lets you take flight as a bee and see things from a bee's perception. Explore the outside "world" (a large park but it is a bee's perspective), flying around enjoying all that nature offers.While it's mainly educational aimed at children, it does give out facts on bees while also giving an interesting read on different animals and insects once you discover them.The music is relaxing and the environments are a pleasure to encounter and explore. Areas of the map feel like they've been filled in with details so there is stuff to see and no real dead zones.It offers a lot of customisation for your bee, so all the points you acquired from collecting flowers don't necessarily go to waste.However, there are some things that bring down the score:The story / campaign is quite short. Felt like it would only take a few hours to complete.You play as only one bee species. I guess all bees work in a similar method but it could of opened up more depth to the game.It becomes quite repetitive quickly. Essentially all it is, is a collection of mini games and collecting flowers.I doubt it was a subtle intention to simulate what being a bee is really like.Trying to get ALL the achievements / feats is difficult. Trying to track down the last few locations across the whole map while the compass range is short makes it tedious. Ended up search by lines; move in a straight line from one end of the map to the other end, adjust position then head back to the other end. Just repeat and repeat.Having a minimap or overhead map to give a basic position would be helpful.Overall: It's a fun casual flying simulator that offers mini-games and facts. Just flying around as a bee is relaxing in itself. But it would be better to buy at a big discounted price given the short amount of gameplay involved (bought at 75% off which I feel is a reasonable price).

_childDocuments_.review: It's a wuite  fun game once you get past its opening jank, as it has some rather baffling issues at the start. Especially if you're on a controller, which is what the game seems to be designed for. So a few quick tips--You spend knowledge points in the extras menu of your pause screen-Left stick in the overworld is NOT the same as left stick in minigames, that would be your d-pad. This goes for dance and fight minigames.-speaking of fight minigames, "Special dodge" is a counterattack, up or down +attack will take more stamina but lets you dodge incoming attacks and shields.-If you start a race (mainly the first one) and are confused, it likely started you facing the wrong direction. Like back at the hive. look for the glowing trail of rings.-Minigames will endlessly repeat until beaten or you exit from the pause menu DURING the minigame. Option sometimes won't come up during the taunting phase of fights.-Pay attention during cutscenes. Not because the story will be lost, but because it will likely dump you into a minigame immediately with the timer ticking.I know this sounds like a lot of cons, but once you get the hang of that it's a fun little romp.

_childDocuments_.review: Bee Simulator really surprised me. I have played other simulators which were meant not to be taken seriously and I’ve played other simulation-type games which were attempting a level of realism which I really enjoyed. I went into Bee Sim thinking that it would perhaps try and emulate realism (I didn’t look into it too much) and was really surprised to find that it was a story-based game with your own bee character having a voice and personality. You meet your hive’s queen and fellow bees of the hive and help with feeding larvae and collecting pollen. You also meet some villains (flies, hornets, human bullies, wasps, spiders etc.) and you have to defeat those in combat.    Truthfully, although I finished the very short story and did enjoy it, I can’t say it was something I’ll play again. I don’t feel I can 100% the game because it’s also literally buggy as well as thematically, and it will make getting all the achievements more tedious than rewarding. However, if you just want to play through once and quickly it’s still pretty fun to fly around, collect pollen, complete side quests and speed around with your boost. The flying around and exploring is the fun part of the game, the combat is probably my least favourite bit.   I’d recommend getting this on sale if it looks like something you’d enjoy.

It also reminds me a bit of Bee Movie and my guess is the developers used some parts of this movie as inspiration for the game.Some small mistakes are easily forgiven, such as the names for some animals were confused in Dutch language (it said "hippo" when I found some rino's and red macaw while I discovered a green macaw). _childDocuments_.review: 4 DEV8 ART6 FEEL2 PRICE8 SOUND6 WRITING6 STORYLINE7 CHARACTER6 FINAL RATINGTHE GOODThe gameworld and the assets are all wonderful to experience, with the exception of some less than stellar human models. You'll find great joy in flying through the world once you've got a solid handle on the mechanics of moving around as the bee. People used to other flight related games will feel right at home here. The music is amazing, and done by the same person who worked on The Witcher III. The writing is suitable for the type of story they're trying to tell, with a childlike innocence to it, and voice acting that also lends itself well to that tone. The story is simple but suited to the concept at play. The characters are varied and charming, where they could've potentially been very bland and cookie cutter.THE BAD1. There are some bugs (one of which prevented me from completing a quest due to a crash). The game crashed almost every time I played. The game has issues even loading up when you press play. The game stutters often. The devs obviously don't seem to care about these issues, since it's already been a long time since the game has been out now.2. The gameplay is nothing to write home about. QTE's and fetchquests galore. The only thing it serves to do is give you a purpose for being in the charming gameworld. The "combat" encounters were especially grating.THE UGLY1. A reviewer mentioned a price of four hundred dollars? Where? Maybe I was late to the party and missed it, but if it was ever four hundred dollars, I'm sure it was by mistake (unless the devs are genuinely nuts). What I do see, though, is that their current price of thirty dollars is nonsense. Fair price for a game riddled with bugs and issues like this would be ten dollars, with optimal price being five dollars.2. I didn't appreciate the light they painted certain humans in. Sure, pesticides may interfere with bee affairs, but it's also how hardworking farmers produce crops to feed you and every one of us. Did not like how they painted the farmer in the tractor as a villain (even though a bee might see them in such a light). Also, having you sting a child who doesn't know any better, just because they were trampling some flowers? Creepy stuff.TIPS1. You can use the D-Pad to control the bee for dance sequences. This is important, as you'll need to pass certain dance sections in order to progress further into the game, and it's pretty much impossible with the thumbstick (bad input recognition).2. 3. Play on easy mode. This sort of experience is not well suited for frustrating gameplay, and that is what you'll get if you play on hard mode. Also, why is there no middle ground in the form of a normal mode?NOTESA reviewer also mentioned lack of variation in voice acting. I don't think they made it too far into the game, because there are plenty different voices you'll hear throughout.FINAL THOUGHTSWhile this was one of the most charming and unique experiences I've played through in a while, it's not one that I can recommend due to the price and above issues. I do appreciate that it gives you a window into the life of a bee (although cartoonish); one which you would never even consider in your own day to day, and serves to bring to light an important topic of discussion, their receding numbers. I would give this more of a neutral rating if it were possible here on Steam.P.S. If you enjoyed and/or appreciated my review, consider following my curator page. I focus mainly on single player story-driven experiences. Maybe we have similar tastes.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are absolutely gorgeous, the music is sweet and the "save the bees" message is nice (even if it's a bit shoved down your throat).But as an adult who was looking forward to a simulation game, it is NOT a simulation game! This game is probably great for young children who have an interest in bugs and wildlife, but it is mostly a bunch of little minigames and some basic story with really awful cringe voice acting that sounds like they're definitely aiming this at small children.So I'm pretty bummed as I feel like the trailer and advertising is very misleading, not to mention the games title.
_childDocuments_.name: Bee Simulator

_childDocuments_.review: Most probably the best children's game I have played. I was expecting a ridiculous attempt at the now classic clickbait "Simulator" games, but I was pleasantly surprised.The game is basically a documentary about bees and their ecosystem. The story, soundtrack and fully voice-acted dialogs are all charming and cute. The graphics are also pretty good, complemented by simple controls and easy to understand mechanics for fighting or communicating with other bees (dancing). The game constantly aims to educate the player and even has a series of achievements that are based on real bee-related facts.As a kids' game, I can't really think of a downside and I would wholeheartedly recommend it to all parents for their younger kids (age<=12). For an adult, I wouldn't recommend it that easily, because it is quite short if you are not a completionist (probably 3 hours just for the main story, and main an additional 5 for all the achievements).The price is quite steep as a means of entertainment for an adult, but for a kid I think it's pretty fair.On sale, it is definitely worth it.10/10 as a kids' game, 6/10 for adults.
