_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge believer in the moniker that "Games are an Art Form". This game is one of the best contenders for that award from me.The premise is that you're just a barista making drinks for your customers, while listening to them talk to you and to each other. People (I can't even say humans, because most of the characters in this game aren't normal humans) meet each other and make new friends. Paths collide. Epiphanies are made. Sorrows are drowned. And at the end of it all, is there a happy conclusion for everyone?Almost none of the characters in the game are human, but all of them have their own humanly qualities, humanly worries and this makes it so relatable for us, to each of them. Not only that, their own otherworldly traits (being Vampires, Elves or even Aliens) paradoxically add to their relatable-ness to us humans. Every character is so well crafted and well written to have their own humanly traits, and at the end of it all we want to cheer all of them on as they embark on their own journeys to solve their own problems and find meaning in their (sometimes immortal) lives.As you serve the drinks to the customers and watch them talk to each other and to you, gain a further glimpse into their backstories and realities and watch their stories unfold further to their heartwarming conclusions. Decided to try this game on a whim, and within the first few minutes, got hooked. Just like a well-written classic novel, I can't put this game down at all. The fact that it's using a game as the storytelling medium makes it even better.RIP Fahmi, you created a masterpiece before you passed. May the characters that you created last in the dreams of your afterlife, forever.

_childDocuments_.review: "Coffee Talk" is an exceptional gem within the gaming sphere, offering a uniquely captivating experience that truly stands out. This indie title effortlessly blends a cozy, heartwarming atmosphere with an engaging narrative, making it an absolute delight to play.The game's charm lies in its simplicity and relatable storytelling. Through the lens of a cozy coffee shop, players are drawn into the lives of a diverse range of characters, each with their own set of struggles, dreams, and aspirations. The conversations, while seemingly casual, delve into deeper themes such as love, friendship, and personal growth, resonating profoundly with players.Moreover, the pixel art graphics and soothing background music contribute significantly to the game's immersive ambiance. The attention to detail in recreating the warm, inviting setting of a coffee shop creates an atmosphere that feels like a comforting refuge from the outside world.One of the most commendable aspects of "Coffee Talk" is its inclusivity. The game effortlessly represents a diverse cast of characters, showcasing various races, genders, and species, creating a rich tapestry of perspectives and backgrounds that players can easily connect with.Overall, "Coffee Talk" excels in delivering a wholesome, engaging experience that transcends mere gameplay. It's a heartwarming journey that not only entertains but also leaves a lasting impression, making it a standout title worth experiencing for any gaming enthusiast.

_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect game to sit down and play with a cup of coffee and some rain. Coffee talk has much less game play than the games I usually go for, but the development of the characters and story were so enthralling I didn't even care that the only thing you really do is make a few drinks a day. The lo-fi music is stunning and so relaxing and blends well with the whole vibe of the game. The time spent with each of the characters is short, but you learn enough of them to fall in love with their personality and stories. The pacing is wonderful, it's never so fast you can't keep up, but never too slow that you get bored or tired. There is a little bit of replay value to it since there are multiple endings based off the drinks you make for people. Once that's done though, there isn't much more the game has to offer other than straight cozy Seattle vibes. That being said, I will never stop recommending this game to anyone who likes visual novels or wants a quick, cozy game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't really much to write home about. It's a  rip-off that has all the same faults, but with even worse drink mechanics and sophomoric writing. No, you can't pick any dialogue options. There's just about no interactivity in this game other than a mediocre mechanic for making pre-set drinks. It has a nice and cozy atmosphere if you have literally nothing else to do with your day, but for more than a buck or two, it's not worth it.First, let's talk about the poor gameplay mechanics. You don't get to choose anything in this game other than drink ingredients to form existing drinks, which you essentially guess at random. The game seems to know and accept that this is a total guessing game, because it gives you 5 chances to start over. For example, I was told to make a "masala chai", a tea that I grew up drinking in my culture. No brainer, I thought, and picked tea, cinnamon, and milk. That failed. So I tried tea, milk, THEN cinnamon. Also failed. So I substituted cinnamon for ginger in those combinations. Still no dice. The "right answer" which is factually incorrect for anyone who knows the drink, involves no milk at all for some reason. Despite the fact that the real drink always includes milk as a main ingredient, while ginger and cinnamon can be subbed in and out with other spices. The dumbest part of this all? You make a drink for a character later in game with tea, milk, then ginger, and the game actually  call that a ginger chai in its menu description! It made no logical sense and boiled down to luck. Despite this glaring fault, the game limits your ability to re-try drinks to only 5 for some reason, which is unreasonable with the amount of pure guesswork they force you into.And you can't even really customize the appearance of a drink either. All coffee and tea comes in the same, boring cup. There is an option to "make latte art" which is very broken and results in nothing that looks good. They would have been better off just designing a few latte art options to pick from so that your drinks don't look awful.Another mistake I noted: Just prior to learning a character is lactose intolerant, you can serve him a drink with milk. He will accept this drink, and the fact that he was just served milk is never even acknowledged. Considering that the game has such little choice/interactivity in the first place, I don't know how this wasn't part of the focus of the game.Now, the biggest issue: the writing. Every character sounds like they were written by a naive liberal millenial... even the middle-aged cop. An example: one of the characters is worried about their 18 year old daughter being in show-business because he's concerned about her being harassed or using drugs. The cop -- a father of 3 girls -- asks him "aren't you being paranoid"? What???The "alternate fantasy universe" is nothing but window dressing, and all the characters could have just as easily been middle class millenials from any city. Their "racial" issues as merpeople and succubi amount to the exact same problems that regular human races deal with. Merpeople are Mexicans. Elves are Asians. This isn't even thinly veiled, as they make a meta-commentary about it. It's like the writers realized making broad sweeping stereotypes about actual human races would weird and too on-the-nose, so they did it to fake races instead. But it's still weird and on-the-nose because it dumbs down what should be complex historical racial problems to "ah so your culture is just like that, huh?" Very stilted and awkward.The setting is supposed to be Seattle in 2019, but you have people smoking indoors and being in idol groups so that doesn't make sense. I assume this is the game devs just being unfamiliar with American culture. They should've just set the game in Indonesia since everyone seems to be ordering Indonesian specialty drinks anyway.Being unable to interact with the characters also really sucks when they are specifically looking for advice on their problems and come asking for it. All you can do is watch other characters give them advice. I'm left wondering "Why am I watching these people appear, solve their own problems by talking to *other* people, then leave? Why is my character even in this game?" Your most loyal regular -- who you are forced to talk to constantly -- is the second-most annoying character of the lot, and seems to be a Mary Sue type stand-in for the writer. Yes, she's even literally a writer (lol). She behaves like an extremely rude, nosy teenager and isn't very pleasant to deal with. At one point she openly berates a kind old man as a pervert for trying to innocently converse with her. At another, she convinces a man to casually betray his best friend's secret. She's also astonishingly clueless about other species, considering she literally grew up in a world full of them since birth. And as for the writing quality? That same character in-game (again, supposed to be a writer) openly remarks that "conjure" is a complex word....which I think says a lot about the quality of writing you get here. I don't know if maybe the person who wrote this uses English as a second language, but the quality is poor.The worst are the writers' stories you can read on your phone. They are written so poorly that they sound like they were written by a teenager. Also, one is literally about a woman saying that she french kisses cats. Yes, in a sexually thrilling way. Disgusting. And I get everyone is sexually liberated but having some random male strangers you just met bring up porn is uncomfortable and weird in just about any situation.The writing's worst sin is just being....boring. You will find yourself quickly tapping through extremely dull portions of the plot, particularly those that involves the space alien. How did they make a space alien boring, you wonder? By making him some "what is love" clueless fool and spending pages and pages of dialogue explaining to him obvious things about dating which everyone already knows. Absolutely thrilling. The only storyline I found interesting was between Lua and Baileys.The visuals are the best thing about this game and lend to the cozy, familiar atmosphere, but they're very minimal beyond a countertop and some static images. As mentioned prior, the storyline between Lua and Baileys was also fairly interesting. That's really about it.

_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Oh where do I even start with this one,So, coffee talk is an indie VN game about...Scratch that. Writer, Vampire, Werewolf, Succubi, Cop, Orc, Squid, Elf, Alien and Two cats enter the coffee shop. They share their lives as you serve them their drinks. Sound boring? Nothing of a sort.It's hard to say anything about this game without spoilers, but all npcs you meet are quite interesting, they have great dialogues and it pays off to actually listen to them, On side of mechanics of the game it's a VN where you don't make any choices per se aside from brewing a proper drink, and even this aspect is handled pretty nicely - for example, if you make something secondary, not a primary ingredient, a customer will suggest that change. Additionally, few nice touches are decoring the whole experience - npcs are changing their profile picture in an in-game social media app, you can track short stories published in a newspaper by one of the customer etc. Music is on point - lo-fi tunes are really completeing the whole work.The whole gameplay takes anything between 4 and 6 hours and it's very enjoyabe one. I can only recommend it, especially when you need an evening with a hot drink and bitter-sweet stories Or, if you need emotional healing. I know I needed one.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: We all know life and what life can write for stories.Some stories make you laugh, some stories make you sad and then there are stories like Coffee Break that give you the courage & meaning in life and that other people have just as many problems - if not worse - as you and me, and still manage to cope with their lives.I've had this game on my wishlist for quite some time and when the second part came out and I played the demo there I thought, back to the roots and start with the first part before playing the second.I'm currently in a phase in my life where I'm really thinking about what to do with my life. Should I continue to work at location X? Should I finish my studies and enter industry Y? Should I just change jobs and try my luck there? So I decided to buy this game on a Monday when I have free time, to curl up on the couch like on a beautiful autumn day with candles, a cup of coffee and my time. The game captures themes like: - What could happen if I lose my job, but what could also happen if I do my job well or accept a new offer?- Work that sucks but has to be done to make a living- The eternal thought spirals of a writer and the hunt for good stories including the reflection on other individuals and what they have to go through in their lives- Love stories- Daily life struggles etc.Why am I telling you all this? Because you are reading through this review and have come across this game to surely get some - down time.Believe me, just let yourself drift and ideally play through the game in one sitting. It's really balm for the soul, like you're really sitting in a cafe talking to others and making new acquaintancesThe game reminded me again that no matter what comes and you fight and don't lose hope, better days will eventually come. Who knows, maybe I will find my dream job or vocation someday, maybe not. But I know I'm not alone and the stories of us are all worth telling. PS: Download the voice mod It´s really good! (It is in the workshop!)

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk has been on my to play list for a long time, being a fan of visual novel style games it came highly recommended. I first started playing it around last year, and never managed to finish until now. I enjoy the cozy music, graphics and atmosphere of the game, but I felt it lacked a sense of engagement, which is odd considering it actually has more mechanics than the standard visual novel. The game overall felt designed more for a general audience than a gamer one. I thought the characters were charming and well written, and I held interest in their storylines throughout the playtime, but the repetitive nature of the drink making ended up getting old after a while. I also felt that there was little room for error or experimentation for making drinks, which made me anxious to get the right ones in order to progress the story correctly. Overall a pleasant gameplay experience, but it was a bit of a tough one to get through at times. My favorite character was Neil, who sadly was the only character without a proper conclusion unless you play through the game multiple times (which I am not engaged enough to really try). I would maybe check out the DLC if it was on sale, but have little motivation to go back to the same kind of gameplay.Overall 7/10, lacking a progression of features, but plenty of wholesome energy and charm!
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: this game is simple yet very charming, it has a lot of soul, heart, warmth and character development in visual novel, yes there's not much to do but compared to other visual novels this has more in depth characters and it feels so calming and relaxing, its like an ASMR but only a really good ASMR, most will might hate with no heart and prefer the ones with sexual content in it but this game is for people with heart and souls, the sexual content games are like one and done but this game is more forever and is truly what a visual novel should be, when the next one comes out i will buy it and not cause i like visual novels but i want to see more Freya and more Jorji and hopefully more Neil, the other characters might return but i think there story is done and there's more to tell, also if you hate talking too much just get the voice overs in the workshop, this game deserves it overwhelmingly positive rating for being a game that's not all explosions and gunshots but more calm and soothing, also challenge mode can be fun too
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, charming game with its own fun little quirks. Felt very original and the story line is something I will definitely have fond memories of. I think the character development of this game is awesome and I became very attached to the characters the more I played. The progression is very smooth and the game itself is very relaxing if you want to play something more on the casual side.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some pretty clear inspiration from VA-11 Hall-A and other quirky visual novels, but changes up the formula enough that it definitely stands on its own two feet. I really enjoyed the various arcs running the course of the story and the gentle foreshadowing in between nights [like the moon and the articles of that day's newspaper]. The biggest thing I would want out of the sequel is a bit more to explore within the barista, maybe making them an actual character rather than an audience insert, and possibly having the story run a little longer with an additional arc or two. Overall, lovely story, took me about three hours to beat for the first time, and I'm looking forward to the sequel :)
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Very good pixelated art styles that just makes you want to try to make the beverages yourself too. This game is not really for everyone, if you want something calming, in your own pace, no different endings, no dialogue choices, just you being a barista, experimenting different coffees, teas and milk-type beverages, listening to people's problems and stories with calming lo-fi music, this game is definitely for you. Although, you may need some help from the internet if you're stuck in a certain day during the Story mode, or in Endless mode, because the game doesn't immediately show you what beverages you have discovered, since you need to discover it yourself. Overall, great game if you feel mentally tired from action games, and just want to get out of the world for abit

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I had this on my wishlist for so long before finally buying it and giving it a go. I couldn't be happier with this game. _childDocuments_.review: I don't usually end up enjoying visual novels, and even when I do I don't usually finish them. I found this one to be really fun and enjoyable though! the characters are all engaging, and I loved getting to see the growth through each interconnected storyline. the drink making mechanic added a lot for me, it was easy to pick up and satisfying to experiment with. _childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: is a hearty visual novel about the nuance of everyday relationships, it's not a special or particular tale in any way, despite its quirks. But that simple premise is enough to coast through, as you become attached to this little cast of lovable characters from your seat as a barista, becoming a neutral observer of this story. But, as the magic wore off, I grew tired of this game's lack of well, ; Visual novels are not a favourite of mine, and that's fine because I had as much fun as someone like me could with this.I found this game back when I was an Xbox player, as it was included in the now-defunct Games for Gold mere months after release. And something about it made me feel different, it was a cosy and warm experience in a genre I'd never experienced. And three-plus years later, here I am, finally playing it. So, cool I guess. _childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk awoke a strong love for this type of visual novel for me. A visual novel where you get to serve guests (similar to VA-11 Hall-A) and the story unravels from the stories they tell and their interactions with you. After playing Coffee Talk, I was recommended to play VA-11 Hall-A as it's one of the only games in a similar vein, and I absolutely loved that game as well. _childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

But let me be more specific...Pro's- Great characters with a fair variety- An interesting storyline- One of the most laid back games you'll ever play!- Reminds me of something out of 90's TV like Friends or Frasier - Controller support is good!- Steam achievements, point shop item and trading cards all worthwhile!- Easy to drink tea and coffee while playing this game!- A wide variety of hot drinks- Interesting mods added- Great soundtracks/BGM- Official merch!!- Decent character development- **There's comics and even novels they're almost hidden away. _childDocuments_.review: The game is quite disappointing.I cannot even call that a visual novel because there players have options what to answer or what to do. In that game I had to simply click over all dialogues. Story is also not great. It is just okay-ish. Serving incorrect drink doesn't affect almost anything. _childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like it. I was thrilled by the demo and admired the concept. I kept on playing even when it got tedious in hopes of seeing something interesting finally happen and restoring my impression, but... it didn't.You play as a coffee shop barista who chats with customers, observes their conversations, and listens to their stories, occasionally chiming in. Most of the discussions revolve around interpersonal problems and social issues that are pretty clichéd and superficially portrayed, while all the fantasy aspects seem like nothing but a disguise to gloss over otherwise mediocre characters, or make up for a vapid plot.Nevertheless, I totally loved the pixel art visuals, soothing tunes, and the overall cozy atmosphere. I also enjoyed the short satirical stories that can be found in your phone's newspaper app. But there's not much to it besides bland conversations that get old and tiresome over time, thus I cannot recommend it as much as I'd like to.

_childDocuments_.review: These are bits from my full review of Coffee Talk, which you can find here: To vaguely summarise, you play as a late-night coffee shop owner and barista, serving clients mundane and fantastical in a hybrid modern-fantasy setting. The influence from cyberpunk bartending game VA-11 HALL-A is obvious; in many ways Coffee Talk feels like an iteration on the concept laid out so convincingly in that game, recontextualised into the ‘lo-fi beats to relax/study to’ dimension (with orcs). Well-produced and charming, with a sharp aesthetic and an endearing cast, this beverage-slinging confessional nevertheless could have benefited from a little extra time to brew (sorry).While I don’t think that Coffee Talk quite dethrones that game, it’s a thoughtful, strong addition to the burgeoning beverage-based visual novel subgenre. It markets itself as a chill-out game, and it succeeds in this regard with an effective mixture of relaxed aesthetic, warm characters and an unhurried feel. The game’s plotlines are maybe a little too linear for my tastes, and could have done with some interweaving and a little extra substance, but the little stories of these peoples’ lives make for small, effective arcs, wrapped in very pleasing visual presentation.

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is an incredibly cozy game that I think is worth your time.After I played Va-11 Hall-A, I discovered this game. Another VN with a drink creation mini-game to keep the player engaged. But I want to avoid talking about Valhalla because that's unfair to compare this game to that, similar concept different executions and feel.The strongest feature the game has is it's atmosphere. The most comforting thing about playing the game is knowing you come back to a warm coffee shop, that plays lo-fi jazz, in the middle of a rainy Seattle. Where you get to serve cute drinks to a... unique set of characters.The other gimmick of the game is it's world. It takes place in "fantasy" Seattle, so the place is littered with the average bum human, sexually ambiguous vampire, and qt shy squid girl. I will be honest, I'm not crazy about the cast though. They're not bad, I just had no interest in them . However they do begin to grow on you, and I would look forward to their next arrival. Updating me with what was going on with their life.The drink mixing game is simple, choose drink base (coffee, tea, milk, etc.) then a primary ingredient and secondary ingredient (lemon, ginger, honey). However it's intriguing enough to make me go into the game "endless mode" to discover drink recipes so I had everything on hand to serve to customers.My closing thoughts, the game is short. Took me 8 hours to beat and this could've been made shorter as well. I spent prolly an hour afk making tea and another half hour playing in endless mode. I think if you're looking for an enjoyable, snug, and short VN with good art, pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Is goodAlright time edit this review and provide actual thoughts rather than an overly simple expression of enjoyment.Coffee talk has you taking the role of a barista in a urban fantasy setting, you'll get the pleasure of meeting a variety of characters that all have their own goings on, you won't have many customers but you'll have your dedicated regulars. (I have no idea how this coffee shop is still in business) The visuals are absolutely splendid, little animations and great expressive pixel art lets you know what a character is all about just by sitting looking at them for a sec. Soundtrack is absolutely superb and definitely sets in the cafe jazz vibes excellently, the composer has done a lovely job and truly earned getting this put on a vinyl record which I now regret not picking up. On the gameplay side there is a little bit however it is a visual novel, your main goal is to hand over the drink people ask for, there was one nice bit in which a werewolf asks you to help him find a brew that will calm him on a full moon, this helps keep you engaged in the actual gameplay and pay attention to what he says so you can help the guy out. I should also say filling out the entire menu was a nice little treat in my opinion.There is also a mini game where you need to make coffees as fast as possible with varying levels of descriptiveness meaning you need to have the menu downpat if you wanna do well, bit of fun if you wanna sit and chill with the game some more.So on to the big part of this game the story, I'll go into some spoilers here so jump off if you already like the game and wanna try it. Each character has their own lives like I said before and as such you get familiar with a cop who's story is already kinda complete in this game he's just there for everyones support which is nice to see a nice cop, I'm not going there in a review but it's a nice change from what we normally see. In another story we see a father and daughter arguing over the daughters music career, the father is familiar with the industry and doesn't want it to scar his daughter for life like it does in reality and in this game so many other young women. This story is very sweet and one of the ones I personally enjoyed a lot. Another story and one of the more significant of the lot is a couple which is made of an elf and a succubus, this game actually goes into showing a bit of racism in this because of course the elfs family hates the idea of him dating anyone they see as lesser, the succubus actually doesn't want him to fight his family on this either as elf families can banish their own and they lose their immortality (Or was it long life span? I'm writing this from a few months old memory hence why no character names) and she doesn't want him to throw it away for her. It's a love story that actually goes to show quite a bit and the game itself goes into how pissing off people with prejudices can cause them to sink deeper into their hatred for others while countering it with that they still shouldn't control your life because of those prejudices. It's just something to think about at the end of the day but I think the game kinda does a good job of showing the struggles between two lovers when one of them has a racist family effectively, though bare in mind this is fantasy so it really aint that deep. Just typical elf supremacy ♥♥♥♥. And finally the ending of an alien in this game, the game at some point introduces us to a socially inept alien who wants to mate with someone of our planet to complete their mission, it's silly enough and you get to see a nice funny little trope play out with none of the gross ♥♥♥♥ a story like that usually entails. I however have a problem with how this particular story ends as once you clear the game see everyone elses happy or slightly less happy endings is our little ayy lmao coming back to the coffee shop now verbose and smooth talking even looking like an actual human (Is it a skin suit? it's probably a skin suit.) and reveals to the play that he is aware our barista this whole time was an alien too...This sucked as an ending, idk why I don't like it so much but it's such a lame reveal and like honestly I wish they would have left the barista even more vague so you could at least imagine what you'd like them to be in this setting, fortunately it's close enough to the end I can elect to ignore it and it has minimal effect on the plot in this game, obviously the sequel may expand on this. In conclusion it's good, actually it's a really pleasant game with a memorable cast of characters I still find myself thinking of fondly thinking about them drinking my coffees and hoping they're doing okay in the sequel that's yet to arrive. Give it a whirl if this cozy experience sounds good to you if not you probably stopped reading paragraphs ago.

_childDocuments_.review: "Coffee Talk" is an absolute gem that delivers a deeply relaxing and enjoyable experience. As a fan of "Stardew Valley," I stumbled upon this delightful game while discussing calming titles with a friend. Despite initial skepticism about its relaxation factor, the unique concept of working in a world filled with diverse races instantly caught my attention.At the heart of the game lies the life of a barista managing a small coffee shop. Despite the limited number of customers, the true joy comes from listening to the stories of the individuals who frequent your establishment. Each day brings new visitors with their own unique narratives. It's fascinating and amusing to discover that the right cup of coffee can be the remedy to their troubles. Whether it's a werewolf seeking a beverage to control their transformations or a sleep-deprived human in search of a peaceful slumber, your role as the barista grants you the power to assist them by crafting the perfect drink and lending a sympathetic ear.What sets "Coffee Talk" apart is its unflinching exploration of realistic issues and scenarios, even in a world separate from our own. The game fearlessly delves into themes of racism, inter-species love, and the darker aspects of the music industry. The sensitivity with which these themes are handled and seamlessly integrated into the gameplay is truly praiseworthy.With multiple endings for each story, "Coffee Talk" offers remarkable replayability. It entices players to embark on multiple playthroughs, unveiling the true identity of the faceless protagonist. To truly appreciate the impact of this revelation, I highly recommend experiencing it firsthand."Coffee Talk" is an enchanting and immersive experience that provides a much-needed escape from the chaos of everyday life. Its perfect blend of relaxation, storytelling, and thought-provoking themes make it an absolute must-play for those seeking a tranquil and captivating gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a star rating system on Steam instead of this binary recommendation, because this game for me is a solid 3/5. The art and design are beautiful and the game embodies that cosy feeling of being tucked up somewhere warm when it's raining outside well. Unfortunately, though, the gameplay annoyed me.For the most part, this game falls solidly under graphic novel. The story is structured around a month in the Fall of 2020 in a Bright-style take on Seattle, complete with octopus-people (that's not a mermaid), WoW orcs, and succubi. Each evening, people come to your late-night coffee shop and talk at you, and order on average 1.2 drinks each. There are no dialogue actions, you are simply a spectator to the story. There are apparently 5 instances where your choice of drink branches the story - at least two of them are fairly clear - but there is no conscious decision-making in the dialogue. Since the major gameplay is making the drinks, that's what I'll focus on here. When a customer orders a drink, you make it - which I think is pretty well described by other reviewers and in the screenshots of the game itself. What was NOT clear to me on first playthrough however was that you have ~244 permutations of the ingredients and very little help as to how to combine them. The base is always 1 of 5 ingredients (e.g coffee, tea) and then the second and third ingredients can be that same base and/or any of the other six ingredients (ginger, mint, lemon, etc). And the  matters! So a customer may come in asking for 'that special spicy chocolate drink' (fake example) and chocolate+cinnamon+milk will work but chocolate+milk+cinnamon will NOT. You can see how this quickly becomes quite frustrating, particularly since many of the customers are very elusive as to what they actually want.Sometimes they ask for a speciality drink you haven't unlocked yet in your drink menu, and often it has a name that gives no clues, e.g. Bitter Heart, The Grinch. But the game, knowing you haven't unlocked it, doesn't give you any options to figure it out other than brute-forcing on the spot (and you only have 5 tries in which to do this) or playing one of the endless-mode games to unlock the menu item. So, let's talk about the endless modes.Free-play is great for brute-forcing combinations.  The timed endless mode is probably the best if you don't want to brute-force your way through all 244 options (which I ended up doing to figure out the last few drinks). It has increasing levels of difficulty. The first stage of timed mode is essentially a reading comprehension test in which the customer asks for drinks with a specific set of ingredients. Again, important to pay attention to order here, e.g. if they ask for a 'lemon and honey tea' you have to input tea+lemon+honey and not tea+honey+lemon or you won't get the point. In the second stage you have to quickly read menu items off the recipe cards you've unlocked. If a customer asks for one you haven't figured out yet - tough! Unless its name is particularly descriptive you'll have no way of figuring it out and probably time out. The third stage  me. Here customers will ask for drinks with specific attributes, e.g. a COOL and SWEET drink. The problems arise when you get a request such as NOT TOO COOL, BITTER, and VERY WARM. In reading that I would assume that maxing out on an espresso would pass all the criteria (it's both hot and bitter) but they actually want something that has a rating of 2-3 on COOL && BITTER and maxed out on WARM. Confusing, right? And because there's no feedback mechanism other than a character looking grumpy it's hard to know where exactly you've gone wrong when a drink gets returned. The stories are sweet but a little hollow. I'm very amused that many reviewers found them 'too political', if you think in 2020 that segregation is a valid stance in inter-racial relations or mixed-race couples are making a strong political statement... then you're way behind the times anyway to put it lightly. Unless you think werewolves are political? Or indie-game dev? In general I wanted the game to be a little bolder with the story, since that's the bulk of the time you'll spend with it. I found the lead character, the journalist that lies to her boss, to be quite immature and rude at times but an unlikeable protagonist is sometimes more entertaining than not, so I wasn't mad about it. If there was a better feedback system for the drinks other than 'ugh, this isn't what I ordered' and a smarter way to unlock menu items I would have loved this game! As it is, it's too frustrating to play. A good time-killer and beating endless is satisfying if you figure out how to please the customers but ultimately not quite there for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I like Coffee Talk, but some achievements are just convoluted.It has a nice atmosphere, and is particularly relaxing to play in the night time. The music and visuals are the best parts of the game.Sadly, the dialogue is a little clunky. Sometimes it sounds quite natural but other times it feels robotic. Considering the game is heavily focused on conversations, this is a bit of an issue for the story.The characters themselves were okay. I have no strong connection to them, in part because of the dialogue.In terms of making the drinks, you have to guess the exact order because recipes are hidden until you serve them at the right moment. Some drinks can be made correctly with logic - the character will tell you the ingredients or you can make an educated guess with drinks like Masala Chai. But others were a complete mystery.You're likely to give a wrong drink from time to time. There's no harm in that, really. Except if you're going for the achievements.Please, just look at a guide if you want the extra achievements after the main story. I wasted a lot of time thinking that I could just replay days however I wanted, without realising that you had to make specific drinks to unlock things.The game doesn't tell you this clearly.If some things require perfect drinks, then I wish all the recipes were given to you at the start of the game. I'm curious why the developers thought to do it that way. The guessing element doesn't make anything more interesting or fun.It's a good thing that Coffee Talk has a strong art style and musical presence. If it weren't for those things, I would have been more dissatisfied. The endless mode doesn't give much replayability either, so get this on sale if the trailer interests you.

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as i saw the title to this game, I had a good feeling. Then after watching the trailer i knew i was going to love it, and I did.This is simply a huge zen experience, Soothing background music, nice stories with a mixture of relatable and oddball characters, and a no pressure game mechanic.I'm a big fan of Sukeban Games' Va-11 Hall-A, and this matches a lot of the gameplay and art style while swapping cyberpunk for fantasy. While some people may see similarity like that as boring, it shows me that the situation and style works for this kind of narrative game: one where many stories are told and they touch each other ever so slightly.The differences are mainly that the drinks system has it's own complexity in Coffee Talk and it's a LOT easier to screw up. You're given very little basic info in your recipe guide at the start and add to this as you discover named drinks. Adding to this lack of outright information, the order of ingredients seems to matter so swapping the additions may produce different effects on the drink. The factor the drinks has on the story also seems to be rather binary: right or wrong, and if it isn't binary (as is my impression) anything to this effect is rather subtle and isn't explicitly mentioned. (This is all in contrast to Va-11 Hall-A's system where you're given all-bar-one recipes off the bat, ingredient order doesn't matter as it's pure ratios, and the story outcome is based a on a mixture of if the drink is wrong, satisfactory, correct or special, plus the accumulated alcohol value) So I'd argue that if a Coffee Talk sequel is on the cards, i hope that element is given a bit of TLC to eliminate some bugbears and give the player more power over the story.As a minor side-feature, you can do latte art. While I'm no artist, and i found the controls a bit fiddly, i do like the attention to including this feature, even if it's only a bit of vanity as it's rarely asked for by the characters.As for the endless/challenge mode, this is where zen goes out the window in Coffee Talk. Your recipe info (or lack thereof as the case may be) carries over and you're given orders quickfire against the clock trying to earn more time. This is where the recipe collecting falls flat in my opinion, it's a nice idea if the story was longer and there was a bit more nuance to knowing the drinks on a second play through and unlocking other routes with them, but you shouldn't be asked for a drink by name with no hints if you've never made it and have no info.I could talk about the story, but i'm going to say very little other than expand on what I've said before, based on the fact that's what you buy this for: the story, and if i said any much more i feel that would negate some of the discovery. The little i will say it that the setting is "fantasy injected into modern life" and it does a good job with the mix of character races, weaving some of their unique traits into the story, while keeping the feeling that if all were human, they'd have a place in real-life society.If you like short stories, narrative in general, or just want something to zen out to, get this game. It's not perfect, but the bits it trips up on don't detract from the parts you're honestly buying this game for.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this when it first came out a little bit before putting it aside for the reason that I didn't understand the latte art mechanic and worried that it'd be an important part of gameplay to progress the story. With the release of the sequel I thought 'oh I have the first game, I'll give it a try again' and with the help of a non-spoilery guide to tell me the correct drink orders for each person, I learned latte art isn't as important as I thought it was and played through the story and I'm glad I did!The main drive of the story, connecting with your different patrons that you brew drinks for, is its strongest point as each of them feel like actual people that you get invested in the stories they're telling. A couple battling society's pressures on them and a father/daughter who don't see eye to eye anymore are all very real issues some people deal with and the conclusions to their stories could bring a tear to your eye. Same thing with all the other cast having very real problems but those two I mentioned before really stuck out to me.Gameplay is just mixing drinks for people based on what they say they want/have ordered before and you listening to their woes while nice lo-fi beats play in the background. It isn't a terribly long game, maybe about 5 or so hours with a bit more being squeezed out by going back to previous days once you complete the game to get more context for the ending (if you know, you know) and the endless mode where you make all the drinks on the menu for the patrons in increasing difficulty (you can pause during this mode, a big tip from me).Overall the game is short yet satisfying in the vibes it gives you, like a nice warm cup of coffee on a cold day. Onto the sequel!

While I'd have loved for the story to be even longer, I'm still pretty satisfied with how it went!- The pixelated art style is nice to look at, the soundtrack's relaxing to listen to, and the characters all start to grow on you after a while. _childDocuments_.review: What I'd say first is, Don't Judge The Book By Its Cover.Whatever you think you're getting, chances are, this is different from it. I can say I did.Different doesn't mean bad, not at all. If you want to look at it as a "game", then yeah, I guess you can see as trying to make the best drink every time and get it correct for the "high score".But that is not the real premise of this game. Where it really shines is the storytelling. I'll not spoil a crucial part of it in this review, but in the storytelling sense, it's a deep game. I've only played it for a couple of hours now so I don't have any idea how long this is, but treat it as more of a VN(visual novel) than a game. Like reading a book.Of course, don't play this if you are expecting hardcore gameplay. But if you want a light experience where you can just "chill out", yeah - I'll recommend this to you.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay-ish. Nice art and some nice characters and also some nice music I suppose if you're into a whole lot of repetitive Jazz-y tunes calmly splish-splashing around.Far from "overwhelmingly positive" though. Even for a visual novel-esque kind of game your means to influence dialogue and story are extremely limited and obvious. It's also a very short game. My at the time of writing 9 hours in it I was 1-2 or so afk and maybe another one I spent in some grindy, boring "endless" mode to unlock drinks in some mini-encyclopedia of sorts.The drink-based gameplay is barely worth noting either. You choose a mixture of three ingredients, some of which - if you choose the right ingredients in the right order - will be presented as drinks that actually exist in RL (which is sorta nice I guess). Others are just auto-combining the names of the ingredients. A lot of times what the customers request is super easy to do, a few other times they want drinks you cannot possibly know without being a total coffee and tea nerd yourself or by googling them. But that's basically it: Click on three ingredients, press button, wait for comic-like "animations" to finish, click another button to serve. That is the entire gameplay other than just reading. (That "Latte Art" thing is just a glorified MS Paint and serves zero gameplay purpose.)And even if you mess up orders: There is no time limit, there is no money or anything to pay attention to (story-wise you are the owner of this coffee shop and apparently already doing well enough financially, so you basically don't give a f*ck.) At worst you'll be missing out on some slight variations in dialogue and if and how certain customers reappear on certain days. But this game is super short and it saves each day so unlocking the few things you miss in your initial playthrough should be easy enough afterwards by precisely loading into the moments where you messed up. And you don't even serve much per day anyway. Like, only two or three cups at best, if even that much, because sometimes some customers narrative-wise are already sitting there with their coffee when it starts for you (it's a bit messy when you go through the night into the next day) or they don't feel like drinking anything at all. So even what little options there are gameplay-wise are easily thrown out of the window for the sake of narration and to maybe make this game even more relaxing than it already is?There are also odd inconsistencies and missed opportunities in lore/setting/ narrative.The game takes place in 2020 in Seattle in an alternate reality with humans, orcs, elves and a bunch of other fantasy creatures living together. Lore-wise that has always been so; yet when some characters enter your coffee shop you and others are reacting totally surprised - as if they or the writers of this game forgot for a second about this alternate reality and assumed it was our own actual one where the appearance of such entities would probably indeed drive us crazy.Then the game is scraping cringe- and pretentious-territory at times or just has moments of poor writing generally, like with how there is a lot of relationship nonsense going on, a lot of characters being either indie game devs by profession or artsy hipsters (everyone with their cellphones out while sipping their coffees, of course) or how there are short-stories in-game that often make no effort to obscure the names/titles of stuff from our reality being mentioned (like Tinder, Uber or Game of Thrones) while strangely enough turning someone like "Haruki Murakami" into "Maruki Harukami". Like, why? Are you worried he is gonna sue you over this but Tinder, Uber, GoT etc. won't? I don't get it. (Also, of course 90% of those short-stories are only about relationship, love, heartbreak and such as well - is there really nothing else most people care and worry about? Geez...)Missed opportunities being for example some orcish union strike happening. You have orcish customers. But is that ever being brought up by them? No. You only read about some stuff in a static newspaper page shown each day before you go to work. These background things could have been used as dialogue content, even to create conflict beyond the relationship/love stuff that occurs in your shop. But the writers/devs totally dropped the ball there and seemingly preferred to stay on heartbreak and shallow kiss-me-despite-our-oh-so-tragically-inconvenient-circumstances-territory. A real bummer, at least to me.Also, why is it always raining? Is that like a narrative device? You can only feel melancholy and soak in jazzy music properly when it rains outside? God forbid the sun ever shines in this alternate reality 2020 Seattle.TL:DR: Judging by the "overwhelmingly positive" reviews a massively overrated game. If you want some similar but better bartender-esque gameplay (and also better writing) you should get "VA-11 Hall-A" instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I always long for more story-rich relationship-building games, games that feel real. Well, this feels very real, despite the fantasy creatures. I am very happy with the queer representation so far. We need more of that. One major frustration is that your character has no choice of dialogue, and only has the power to make drinks and scroll on your phone. I feel this is a big loss for a game that's person- and emotion-centred. Other characters feel round and real, while I feel like a drink dispenser. On the subject of fantasy races replacing real-life races for social issues, I'm mixed on. On the one hand, it is progressive in that it's not just fantasy races for the sake of it, but to explore relevant real-life social issues. On the other hand, fantasy races being coded for certain real-life races, or the autism coding in the alien and the ocean girl, feels a bit tired and erasing of minority identities in real life. The whole, people of colour face no racism anymore in 2020, but protesting orcs are coded as Black Lives Matter, I don't know... One last note is the animal abuse in a short story on the phone--the narrator graphically describes their fetish for french kissing cats. What the hell was that? Put a trigger warning, maybe? THAT BEING SAID, still, I'm going to recommend  this game for sure. The core of it is right, and it's touching on things we should be talking about more.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: It makes just scrolling through dialogue and listening to people fun. I had more fun in this game then I have in a lot of AAA games. All the characters in this game has realistic personalities and talking to them was just fun and somehow never got boring because I was always asking to myself " I wonder what will happen next"
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This game, while having a calm atmosphere to set the stage and honestly kinda vibe in, gives some great stories dealing with racism in a world unlike ours. The core gameplay of making the coffees is great, and endless mode is a rush, but the characters and atmosphere are what sells the game. All of the characters feel natural, but fully distinct. There were times where one of the main characters would comment on an idea another had, but the other person was too stubborn, even if it was a bad idea. While it's slightly frustrating, it shows a true understanding of how to make characters feel natural. The normal at the restaurant always set the mood for the night, and honestly made me feel a little bit better every time. If you're looking for a game with outstanding gameplay and realistic graphics, this isn't it. It's not Halo. But what it lacks in the gameplay, it more than makes up for in the comforting atmosphere and realistic stories, which I'd argue are more important. The graphics are stylized in pixel art, adding to those waves of comfort. And, even though the gameplay isn't my favorite, Coffee Talk works very well as a game, with its bits of branching narratives and personal interactions.I'm glad this is one of the first games I played this year. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable, meaningful and relaxing. I love that this manages to capture the way that we are limited in our job as a barista but how something as simple as giving someone just the right drink can change their day around. Nice to playthrough. Only downside I could think of is maybe replay-ability enjoyment could be lower if you are the kind of person who wants a lot of new content fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is a beautifully crafted game that offers a relaxing and casual experience perfect for winding down. The game's cute atmosphere, with its soothing lo-fi soundtrack and charming pixel art, makes it easy to lose yourself in the stories of the diverse characters who visit your café. As a barista, you get to mix drinks and engage in meaningful conversations, uncovering the unique backgrounds and emotions of each patron. The game play is simple yet satisfying, focusing more on storytelling and ambiance than on challenges.Coffee Talk is a delightful escape from the hustle and bustle, making it a go-to for anyone looking to relax and unwind.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The art / world is so unique, I really enjoyed the way in which they created a fantasy world that to me, never felt cliche or unrealistic. It's just like our world, with the addition of corporate succubus' and hipster elves. I'll be honest, at first I saw some negative reviews and was like ehh, but I'm happy I didn't listen to them, b/c this is one of my favorite indie games. I like to play it on auto mode so I don't have to constantly click, letting the music and dialogue sink in with a cup o' coffee in hand. Perfect game for the slice of life loving coffee addict.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This talking simulator is set in a fantasty-inspired world in which many different species live together. As you prepare coffee, tea and cocoa-based drinks for your customers, you'll get to listen to everyone's life and problems, helping them by preparing warm drinks.It is a very cute game, with great music and characters : A perfect way to sit down and relax. Coffee Talk is getting a sequel in 2023, titled .The demo is available right now from the game's Steam page.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10A quiet little game where you spend most of your time clicking through other people's conversations with little puzzles in the form of specialty drinks you serve them. As far as visual novels go, this one emulates its setting pretty well: I felt like I was relaxing in a cafe eavesdropping on other customers.  The game is pretty short, about 4 hours for me to get through twice (the second time on fast-forward to skip the bits I had already seen) and a couple of achievements that you can either look up or do a lot of guess-and-checking to discover hidden recipes necessary to the plot.  It was a nice little escape, which is what I needed right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Another soundtrack to add to my chill playlist is always a win. The game itself is easy on the eyes, has a fascinating setting and a knack for attention to detail. I loved the amount of care in the small animations for the character sprites and in the sound design. * Characters not currently speaking would react to others, laughing,  making eye contact, getting angry* The succubus character's horns would glow if she was angry* Customised splashy footstep sounds for the mermaid character* Character profile pictures would change on your phone as the story progressed* Characters' eyes would look to the door if someone entered the cafeLittle things like that were utterly charming. A couple of negatives however:* Drink combination orders weren't always clear, but I guess this can be attributed to being a sort of puzzle?* Some references to pop culture or memes may wear thin on your patienceThoroughly looking forward to the next one. Coffee Talk is a beautiful legacy to leave, thank you Fahmi.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I know very little about this game, but saw the co-creator passed away.  So to help his family as the request went out, we are talking Coffee... Talk!I've played a little and seems to be a chill fun game, where you listen to the stories of Fantasy characters and make them some beverages.  I think this would be great on a night to unwind a bit before bed.Rest in peace, Mohammad Fahmi Hasni.  Thoughts are with your family.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game by accident on Steam a few weeks ago, and it looked somewhat interesting, and it was only $12, so I decided to purchase it over this past weekend, and lemme tell you: I am very glad I purchased this game. I'm not much for games like this, I'm more of a survival or open-world type guy, and this game was a very nice change of pace. It was one of those games that once I was done playing other games for the night, I could unwind for a little bit playing this game along to the chill music that's within the game. all you do in this game is serve people coffee, and listen to their normal, day-to-day problems and give them advice. It's a real world problems type game, and it's so good. It's a shorter game that doesn't take too terribly long to complete, but there's different endings, so now I can go back and see what I can change to make the ending different. It's very interesting to see how these characters' live unfold and come to a closure towards the end of the game, just by serving them coffee and talking to them, then you can go through it all over again for the different endings. I have played a lot of video games in my life and am not really one for games such as this, but I thoroughly enjoyed this game. 10/10: I highly recommend this game for anyone reading this.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: It's amazing how they depicts real life problems in a world where fantastical creatures exist. Every characters in this game is unique and has their own problem. We play as a barista who will listen to their story while serving them a cup of coffee. And don't forget about the music that can bring you chill. Overall 8/10 for character design, storyline, the gameplay, and the music. The only minus is the pixelated graphic which some people might feel uncomfortable with it (but I personally have no problem with it)
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely obsessed with this game!! I haven't finished the whole story yet, but it has me hooked! I definitely recommend it to people who enjoy more lowkey games and listening to others. As someone who doesn't like extremely intense gameplay, routine, and to relax, this game is absolutely perfect for me <3
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game with zero expectations, and it delivered really well. 1. Background Music : absolutely astonishing2. Characters : eventhough they are somewhat set in a fantasy, the characters and their problems are relateable3. Difficulty : just click the game and enjoy the storyi really want to play the sequel of this game, please 2023 come faster !!!
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little collection of personal stories to read and relax.I thought there'd be a little more interactivity, but it's just reading the dialogue between the characters (as in, there's no dialogue choices). _childDocuments_.review: I will give mostly positive comments with this game.  I am a Twitch streamer.  I streamed this game yesterday.  We had fun with the different characters in the game.  It was fun trying out some of my voice acting skills with it.  We also had fun with the whole beverage making part of the game.  It was fun trying out doing the late designs.  I had never done them in real life.  My chat was having fun laughing at my inept skills.The only thing I would say was a downside for me was some of the profanity and crude references.  I purchased this game because it was recommended by the website, "Wholesome Games."  I thought that meant the game would not have those kinds of references.  Looks like I was mistaken.  Something to keep in mind.  For me, this is important because I try to run a strictly family friendly channel.  Unfortunately, that means I will probably not be streaming this game in the future.  As it was, I had to try and skip over or reword quite a bit of the dialogue.  Also, I had to caution my viewers.  Since there are children present at times, I had to let them know I was going to try my best but they might want to be aware.  There is smoking in the game.  Also references to drinking.

_childDocuments_.review: So the art is beautiful and I love the character designs, but the game itself is just really boring.You have to sit through a mound of dialogue before you can make even one cup of coffee and even that part really isn't all that fun. My biggest gripe though is how inconsequential your character is to the whole thing. You really are just meant to sit there and listen to all the other characters talk trough their problems. You don't even get to mediate or give an opinion, nothing. And the one thing, the ONE thing, that should be super important that only your character can do is make the damn coffee. Well, I got a bit spiteful the one boring night and made everyone's coffee wrong and they just don't care? They kind of just go "hey! Oh well, I'm here for vibes" so our character really doesn't matter. I see now I only have one hour playing this game, it felt like ten and honestly I don't know if I'll ever muster up the will to carry on.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

Very sad to hear about Mohammad Fahmi Hasni's passing, the co-creator of the game. If you like visual novels, especially something like VA-11 Hall-A, this game is 100% for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend the game! While the Coffee Talk may be short and a bit lacking in things to do, the art, story, and absolute-♥♥♥♥ tone of love put into the game makes up for any downsides the game may have! It is a beautiful game and Toge Productions clearly went full-out on the art, and it shows! The game also has a great story that really pulls you in! And remember to bring an umbrella as it's always rainy in Seattle.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A short and relaxing visual novel to play before bed -  gives an interesting flavor to mundanity, something that I'd argue it's more appreciated these days considering the wacky times we're living in right now. Regardless, the concept of making drinks is an intricate one albeit limited; there're some attempts into stretching the mechanic but they end up feeling either too shallow, or too stressful to the point of having to make drinks based by "number x of a certain taste or temperature" with a timer. If this sounds like fun to you, then perhaps you might encounter some replay value once you're done with the main story.... which is also short. My biggest frustration is the length, everything feels so shortsighted - it's like you want to surprise someone by making a cosy room spending hours and hours with fragile decoration, just for it to be destroyed minutes after showing. Definitely very nice and I've loved my time with, but unfortunately... could be more memorable.Saddens me to recommend  solely on sale, but I look forward to see what's next for the developer.

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute and cozy game with a lovely cast of characters. It's an absolute joy to get to know them over the course of the game, and see their stories unfold. The drink mixing isn't super complex or anything, but it's quite fun and serves as nice punctuation between bits of story and dialogue, while the atmosphere and ambience is spot on.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: 's alright, but it's not great. Story is simple and not very deep, some characters are charming and well-written, and some have predictable writing. The music is nice, the pixel art is often hit, sometimes miss (e.g. Freya's hand in certain poses looks like it only has 4 fingers). The drink making minigame is a bit finnicky, you can make the same drink but with the order of two secondary items reversed, and this will make for a different drink. This tripped me up in certain situations where the order of ingredients given did not match the actual recipe, and as such, me making the wrong drink. Overall, I did enjoy the game, but I think it needs more polishing before I could recommend it to people.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely urban fantasy slice of life VN. You run a coffee shop, that's only open at night and serve your various customers various hot drinks while they talk about their problems, fears and dreams. Minimal gameplay, it's mostly figuring out what drink to serve each customer and depending if you are correct you will get the good ending for each storyline, other than that your input is 0. The writing is for the most part very solid, fun and heartwarming even if a few lines here and there where a bit on the nose in making sure you don't miss the point (it would have been better if they made it a bit more subtle). There's also a endless mode that's a bit tricky, especially if you aim for a score of 50+ (even if you can cheese it and stop the timer while you think).

_childDocuments_.review: So, I really struggled with whether to give this game a positive or a negative review. I'd give it a middling review if I could - but when the chips are down, I can't say I'd exactly recommend it.Let me preface this by saying I actually like some visual novels and other kinds of dialogue-heavy games. And I really wanted to like Coffe Talk. I like the setting and the sound track and the cozy atmosphere, and the description on steam appealed to me, like the game describing itself as a "talking simulator". The problem is that it's not a talking simulator. It's a listening simulator. This game is barely a game. There is not a single dialogue choice to be made. The only kind of interaction the game offers is serving different drinks to the characters. Most of the time, getting their orders right is absolutely trivial - they straight up tell you the ingredients to use and there is no skill involved in actually making the drinks, you just need to press the correct three buttons. If you get the drink orders wrong a lot of times, some characters will get a bad ending, but I think that for most of them you'd have to be screwing it up on purpose to ever get the bad endings. There are some exceptions to this, but I'll touch on that later.So I thought, alright, let's give this another chance and treat this more like a book. Really focus on the story and the characters, and try not to mind your avatar's insanely bland dialogue too much. The problem is that there's nothing to this game in terms of the plot either. Again, I like the idea of the segmented mini-stories you get to experience each day, but I didn't find myself attached to any of the characters, and their stories all tread extremely familiar ground with obvious conclusions. At times the dialogue tries to be funny, but more often than not it's just contextless references. Sometimes it wants to be thought-provoking, but it's mostly a very middle-school level of thought-provoking. Often it aims to be heartwarming, but it comes off as unearned and saccharine. The game is also extremely light on worldbuilding, even though the setup could be interesting in theory.The ending tries to pull off a funny twist and get you to play a second time. On the second playthrough, only a very small bit of dialogue actually changes, and it takes forever even when using fast-forward. Then, to get the actual true ending, you need to serve two specific drinks on two specific occasions without being pointed to their specific ingredients in any way - it's basically only achievable through trial and error. Definitely not doing that, so I just watched the additional scenes on YouTube, and yeah... they're really not that interesting and they introduce a variety of plotholes. Not worth the additional hours, in my opinion.In the end, all of this just felt pointless. When I play, I want something that's challenging, or that makes me think about its mechanics or its themes, something that inspires me or that makes me feel something. Ideally something that stays with me after completing the game. Coffee Talk does none of those things. There is no substance to this game. But you know what? Maybe that's the point. If you are looking for a game to help you relax, that doesn't pose any risk of failure, make you think, or where you'd even particularly have to pay attention to the plot... if you're really stressed and you just want to turn off your brain, enjoy the cozy atmosphere, and hang out with virtual people while still feeling like you're doing something slightly interactive, Coffee Talk might be just the game for you. It's not particularly expensive and judging by the reviews, it seems to have really struck a chord with a lot of people in that way. I'd definitely recommend it to you in that case. But if you're looking for a game with actual substance, I would advise skipping this one. It will just leave you with a profound feeling of having wasted your money and time.

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is a relaxing visual novel where you play as a barista and serve warm drinks to a host of interesting characters, in a universe where other races of being (werewolves, mermaids, orcs, etc.) exist and live in society with humans. It has quite a charm to it being able to watch the conversations happen before you and the drink-making system is quite easy to use. It's very easy to save-reload if you make mistakes as well and very easy to get to completion.I'd perhaps say the one downside is how short it is and how I wish it was a longer story to enjoy, since it was so endearing to play and enjoy already. I was able to easily complete it in about 5-6 hours, so that's a consideration for your purchase. I'd say it's worth the money, however, if this sounds like an interesting game to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Appearances can be deceptive.  If you haven't already played  and are thinking about trying it, then you need to be aware that at its core it is a linear visual novel with a passive protagonist.  If this concept is one you enjoy and you're happy to follow along to a few story threads whilst intermittently clicking some ingredient icons to create different drinks, then go ahead, this game will suit you.Our (unseen) protagonist is a coffee shop owner/barista who serves drinks and listens to/encourages customers to talk about their lives over the thirteen day period of the game, with a further day two weeks after the final active one providing a rounding-up and epilogues of everything we have seen before.Set in an alternative Seattle where fantasy characters such as orcs and werewolves are integrated into society along with humans, eleven different repeat customers will visit the store and their brief interactions with both the barista and each other serve to narrate their own story arcs.  Each one is interesting and fun in its own way and will (assuming this type of story is your thing) endear each of them to you individually.  It is your job during this process to select the right ingredients in the correct order to supply them the drinks that they ask for during their visits to the shop.  During the story mode of the game, this is pretty easy.Undoubtedly more attention has been paid to graphic presentation than in a more traditional visual novel.  A gentle, pleasing pixel graphic style is used, with large fully animated character sprites and backgrounds (we see silhouettes of both foot and vehicular traffic through the window – along with the persistent rain, an amusing – depending upon your sense of humour – stereotyping of Seattle weather), switching to an ingredients store and drinks machine when making a brew.  The display switches again when you choose to make “latte art”, showing a filled cup from above.  You can pour the milk (which always floats a little towards the bottom as viewed), etch to detail your design, and by clicking the handle and holding the mouse button down, rotate the cup 360 degrees to fine-tune the direction of milk flow.- The game auto-saves at least once a day (it may be more frequent, I am not certain) and you can also overwrite this with a manual save in between times, though there is only the one “floating” save spot.  Once you have played through a full day, you can restart that day at any time using the load option.- Text speed is initially quite slow (or , in keeping with the game's nature, if you prefer).  I was glad to find an “instant” text speed option available.- There is also the option to auto-move the story on if you do not wish to click (or trackpad tap) after reading each entry.  There is no option to go back but there is an easily accessible log which is very good and shows you the most recent caption upon opening.- The “extras” menu features an art gallery, a short “comic strip” mini-story for each character, and a list (with icons) of the game's achievements that you have attained.  I'll return to achievements shortly.- Whilst in the main story mode, you also have access to your mobile phone, within which you will find four features:  a list of all named drinks that you have unlocked so far with their recipes, a social media site which gradually reveals profiles of the regular customers as you get to know them, a music streaming app with a selection of tunes and an online short-story sequence written by the shop's most regular customer.  These stories feel more like incomplete idea propositions than anything, until the final one which runs over three days and has enough detail to hold interest.  None of them in any way affect the main character arcs though, they are purely there for additional entertainment purposes.After completing the visual novel side of the game, there is then also an endless mode.  In one, you can mix and match (any three) ingredients and brew to your heart's content as you go in search of any undiscovered named variations.  This may be fun at first, especially when you get a hit, but it becomes tiring quite quickly.The other is a challenge mode, which is timed, and customers appear with specific requests.  It starts off very easily, with them telling you  what they want, but gets much harder as their combination list extends and becomes less obvious; with requirements like  and  replacing early requests like  with  and .  Extra time is provided each time you serve correctly, and as the timer stops when you put the game into the background, it becomes fairly straightforward to complete and you're able to go and reference a guide without penalty before continuing.  That makes this aspect of the game  more friendly to play than it would have been when first released! is the classic example of a game of two halves.  If you like visual novels, you will almost certainly enjoy that (primary) aspect of this offering.  It has a nice relaxed vibe to it, there are no stressful circumstances to making the wrong difficult decision – the only decisions you have to make are ingredient selections anyway -  and although you have to replay four of the fourteen days to get the full story, the skip function is very efficient; and it's worth doing so for the amusement of Freya's reactions alone.  So for fans of the genre, you have a winner.The endless mode is altogether different though, and for me, it didn't work well.  I am very glad that I didn't get to this game until it had been on release for a long time and various wonderful people have logged and posted guides with all of the details you will need to reach some of the what-would-have-been drudgery-inducing achievements.  The later requirements in the challenge mode are nothing more than a burden: this type of challenge is WAY more fun in a well made time management game; and unless you have a strange fetish for hard-to-control digitised latte art, you're going to have to leave the game on, in the foreground, for a full hour just to get that achievement (meaning that you can't do anything else with your computer while that counts down).  Not fun.Overall though, the game does earn its stripes from its main function as a graphic story and on that basis, it's a comfortable recommendation for fans of the genre,

_childDocuments_.review: Holy hells was this good, thanks to all the people who made this game for this wonderful little experience. I was feeling depressed for a little while and this really helped out, kind of in the same way that a certain cyberpunk bartender game did for me about 6 months ago.To anyone who wants to get this game, do keep in mind it's a nice, mostly serious and sometimes very funny story with a bit of gameplay and decisions mixed in, if that's what you're looking for then I suggest you get this in a heartbeat (along with that certain cyberpunk bartending game), if that's not at all what you're looking for... maybe still get this, when it's on sale, and have it in the background for a rainy day when you might want that kind of story. It luckily doesnt take up much space or much money and I personally think it's a nice experience for anyone having a bit of a rough time in life.
