_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A very cozy and chill game that's rich with fantastical, yet grounded character work. Coffee Talk is a fantastic showcase of empathy through game writing, encouraging you to pay attention to customers and their needs in order to unlock more storytelling. Help a friend write a novel; Develop a friendship between unlikely alliances of werewolves, vampires, mermaids and orcs; Give a friendly alien tips on getting laid. Why not?!I had a great time deducing and delivering the customers' needs, both in terms of beverages and emotional support, and while the experience may be too passive for some players, Coffee Talk is nonetheless a very unique social sim that's quite unlike anything else out there. Godspeed, Neil. May Tinder show you the way!
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Having to essentially guess all of the recipes as you are given no hints after the first four or five basic drinks is honestly quite repetitive and frustrating at points, however, in the long run it makes the feeling of finally figuring them all out and getting the achievement so much more worth it and reassuring.  Watching the characters help each other emotionally makes it feel like you're really there, like you're genuinely helping by simply just listening and always being there for them, its a very humanizing feeling watching them build relationships with one another.  In fact, the entire plot is pretty amazing, I often find myself wanting to replay the entire thing, which ive done ngl, I actually accidentally associated a song with this game, Nobody by Mitski, they have such similar vibes especially when the story mode is coming to an end.

_childDocuments_.review: A Heartfelt Brew of Stories and Serene AtmosphereCoffee Talk is more than just a game—it's an experience that resonates deeply with anyone who enjoys heartfelt storytelling and a cozy ambiance. This visual novel, set in an alternate Seattle where mythical creatures live alongside humans, offers a unique blend of engaging narratives and a soothing environment.Characters and StoriesWhat truly stands out in Coffee Talk is its rich tapestry of characters and their intertwining stories. Each character, from the hardworking succubus to the aspiring elf writer, brings a unique perspective and personal struggle that feels incredibly genuine. The game masterfully provides glimpses into their lives, making every interaction feel deeply human and relatable. The dialogues are beautifully written, filled with warmth, humor, and moments of introspection that make you care about each character's journey.Atmosphere and StyleThe game’s pixel art style is a visual treat, capturing the cozy, late-night coffee shop vibe perfectly. The warm, inviting atmosphere, paired with the sound of rain gently tapping against the windows, creates a serene setting that invites you to relax and immerse yourself in the stories. The design and ambiance of the café make it a perfect haven for late-night conversations and personal reflections.SoundtrackThe soundtrack of Coffee Talk is a highlight, with its soothing lo-fi chillhop tracks that enhance the game’s calming effect. The music perfectly complements the relaxed pace of the game, creating an environment where you can unwind and lose yourself in the narrative. It’s the kind of soundtrack that stays with you long after you’ve finished playing, evoking memories of the time spent in that cozy café.GameplayThe drink-making mechanic adds an interactive layer to the experience, allowing you to craft unique beverages for your customers. This element not only engages you in the daily rhythm of the café but also subtly influences the stories and interactions, making you feel like an integral part of the characters’ lives.ConclusionWords cannot fully express how much I love and care about Coffee Talk. It’s a game that combines beautiful storytelling, memorable characters, and a calming atmosphere into a truly unique experience. Whether you're a fan of visual novels or simply looking for a game that offers a heartfelt escape, Coffee Talk*is a must-play. It’s a serene, soulful journey that leaves a lasting impression on your heart.Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: this is a great game. the graphics, the music, and the ambiences of the cafe are spectacular. the storylines are juicy and very engaging. you really feel like you're behind the counter and listening to each character's story. if you like graphic novels, coffee shops, lo-fi music, and cozy games, then i highly recommend this game to you. i thoroughly enjoyed playing this game and have recommended it to many friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: It's a visual novel without choices, where you get to listen about people's lives and make them warm drinks.After binging a bunch of horror content, I need something wholesome and with good vibes. Coffee Talk fit that bill perfectly. The atmosphere and sounds are similar to one of those relaxing ambience videos, coupled with charming writing and a fun cast of characters (lots of queer ones to my surprise).With the exception of the other races that make up the population, the game is set in "the real world", and so real world problems do get enmeshed with your customer's lives (immigration, overworking, healthcare), but it never gets heavy. You listen to people, watch them build a community and give them a place to find solace.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Well first of all this is a very small game, don't play this expecting it to be an intrigue, mystery and drama sort of thing: there are no great stakes, it's not action packed. It is a game that you play to relax and chill, casually listening to some odd story in the background.The gameplay is, inevitably, repetitive and it is a slow game, but again it's meant to be a "hanging out with friends" experience.There is a challenge mode and an endless mode where you can practice your "brewing skills" but it's very much just clicking on 2 or 3 icons.The music is nice and has a calming groove to it, but i wish there were more tracks and i especially wish the rain in the background would stop from time to time.All things considered a very pleasant experience that i would recommend though.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Is it world-changing? Nah. Does it even have much in the way of “gameplay” or “choices”? Nope.But is it one of my favourite games in recent memory? Flop yeah.Comfy as all heck, charming, witty and all-around so relaxing and wonderful. I quickly found myself looking forward to the next session where I’d get to play this, brewing myself a hot chocolate and getting lost in these characters stories.After a cozy experience to curl up on the couch with after a long day? This is your game.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely fantastic game that does story telling in such a unique way.You are a barista manning a coffee shop and your regular, Freya, decides she is going to write a book about your coffee shop. The story being about the tales told by customers that come in. The world is the same as it is in real life... with the exception of the world having more than humans. Having aquatic people, werewolves, vampires, orcs, cat people.There's quite a few topics that get covered in these stories, some only a passing mention and others more center state. Union strikes, love forbidden by family due to racism and tradition, the corruption of the music industry, the horrible working conditions AAA game devs sometimes experience, learning the importance of disagreements, being a war vet, dealing with guilt, immigration, there's just... there's a lot here and a lot to unpack.The artwork is amazing. The story had me gripped for a lot of the stories. Some I saw how they would go, others I didn't. There's a twist at the end if you played right that will want you to play a second time to get more information. The music is awesome and has been added to the list of game soundtracks I wanna own.I'd say that the game is worth two play throughs, because the twist is pretty good in my opinion.I do have... a SINGLE complaint about the game. That is actually the making of the drinks. The actual mechanic is fine. Nothing wrong with it. If you wanna draw latte art you can and I think it's fairly fun. The problem I have is that the game poses that your character is supposed to basically be able to tell what people need based on how they are acting. Be able to figure out what drink they want/need. Sometimes a customer is straight forward about what they want "I want coffee with lots of mint." Okay. That's clearly one dose of coffee and two doses of mint. Other times a character will just tell you the name of a drink.... that you haven't discovered yet.... and tell you MAYBE one ingredient. You can trash a drink up to 5 times in one day, but there are multiple days where you are guessing the drink you are giving to at least two people. With so many drink combinations... if you don't know ♥♥♥♥ about coffee or tea (like me) then you probably aren't gonna give the right drinks.I feel like the drinks were SUPPOSED to be a puzzle but that they were written by someone who frequents coffee shops. As someone who doesn't, I would have had to play a day over countless times to get some of the drinks right.The first time I played through I only looked up a few drinks. The second play through I just looked up a drink guide. Cause I know I'll never figure out the drinks on my own.I wish that instead of making it a puzzle the characters would just tell you what they want, or tell you the name and you could look up in a recipe book. Having to actually figure out the drink with little clues or looking up a guide both kinda ruined the flow of the game for me.Oh and there's some drinks where you have to put in ingredients in a specific order. Doesn't matter if you have the ingredients right, they need to be in the right order. Which just adds way more complexity to it.Regardless of that it's a fantastic game. Just know that if you don't know jack about coffee and tea to have a guide handy cause you'll probably need it. If that doesn't bother you pick it up. The game has an amazing story, great vibes, great artwork.There's also comics that you unlock that give more stories about the characters which were lovely to read through.

_childDocuments_.review: While the pixel art is very pretty pretty much everything falls flat. In a game driven by little stories the stories (and writing) themselves aren't compelling and are quite cringe. You are a nameless barista living in a Shadowrun-esque world where fantasy races have intermingled with humans where none of that was really explained and only exists as a subtle as a brick jumping off point for stories about racism. The vibes are very 2010s Tumblr with even references to The Omegaverse of all things. Probably one of the worst misfortunes of the game is a background plot about a Zombie virus outbreak and the fact that the game is set in 2020. Gameplay isn't particularly deep but it didn't need to be. The coffee art part could've used a tutorial because its never really explained how to make patterns with the milk.I'm left wondering if the writing improved with the other Coffee Talk games but have no desire to found out after playing through this.

_childDocuments_.review: I had never heard off this game until I randomly saw the Steam post about Fahmi's tragic passing. Even though I knew nothing about him or his games, I felt my heart shatter, and even more so when I read that he died so young, and of an asthma attack. That fact was so scary to me because I have someone very close to me who has asthma, and while I'm sure he and Fahmi's experiences were fairly different, it still impacted me. A few days passed and I saw that it was the last day that the game would be on sale to raise funds for Fahmi's family. I bought it just off of what the steam page said because I thought to myself  "Even if I don't end up enjoying the game, I want to support his family in their time of need." I can safely say that after only a half hour that the game has already hooked me! Rest in peace Fahmi, and if there is an afterlife, I hope you can find peace and happiness there.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This was in my recommendations after playing Valhalla. Similarly, its a Visual Novel / drink-making game with the focus on interesting characters. Though, the topics of discussion always seemed like somewhat stereotypical TV drama and it never really went anywhere surprising. Whether its worth picking up is a bit of a coin-flip. For what it was, it was fine, but the story was too plastic to get my interest.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I'd been thinking of picking this game up for a while before I heard the tragic news of its writer's passing. Once I saw it was on sale, with all of the proceeds directing benefiting Fahmi's family, it made my decision to purchase it that much easier. As someone with a significant other who suffers from asthma, I've seen how scary a disease it can be. I can't imagine how this family must feel right now, but I sincerely hope they're doing all right, all things considered. Maybe my small contribution will help.From what I've played of it so far, the game itself is full of atmosphere with stunning pixel art graphics, lively characters you'll enjoy getting to know, and a fantastic soundtrack. Just buy it, especially if you're reading this while it's still on sale; your money's going to a great cause. Honestly, I would have happily paid full price. To me, it's worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: This visual novel is extremely creative, well-made, and thought provoking. The music creates a calming atmosphere, and I'm a big fan of the pixel art and bright colors.It's set in Seattle 2020, in an alternate reality where humans and different races of monsters co-exist. You play as the owner of a coffee shop that's only open at night, and you get to follow the stories of your customers. Every day starts with a newspaper before you begin your shift. In these articles, the game draws parallels between their societal/cultural issues and ours in the real world. Everyday, a new short story is added to the newspaper app on your in-game phone. I loved this detail!Each character faces a unique conflict that you get to see through until resolution, all while serving them their requested drinks. We also get to see the customers interact with each other up. Everyone in the game is well-rounded, and I'm sure anyone playing will see a little bit of themselves in at least one character. The only thing I'd want to change is for there to be more drink-making and serving. The games does have a challenge mode and freestyle mode where all you do is make drinks. I just wish there was more of that in the main story.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is an enjoyable visual novel with good art and objectively lovable characters. The main story took me about four hours to complete and was decent, though not quite to my taste. The only real criticisms I have are about the lack of any choice (which isn't a bad thing for everyone) and the not-so-subtle discussions about modern problems, such as racism and discrimination. The direct nature of the dialogue could be needed for the people who do their best to ignore these societal issues. I've only completed the storey once as it did not hold enough interest for me to go through a second time. I recommend this title to enjoyers of stories and visual novels with minimal gameplay.

_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly... one of the best games I've ever played. It's very appropriate that the reviews are Overwhelmingly Positive. This is a story-focused game. The actual game-play is minimal, and there aren't any choices besides making drinks (how to make? which to give?). So the core of the game relies on the immersion and characters... and for good reason. The characters are deeply compelling, and I was quickly drawn in by how lifelike and realistic their stories and personalities are. The little expressions and mannerisms each character makes in each conversation and on their own when you or others are not directly interacting with them helps them to feel so alive. I especially loved the lore and world-building that was set up here. It's incredibly creative and different from our own world, yet so similar at the same time. The parallels are very noticeable, especially the game's discourse on current issues and how they would look in this alternate Earth. I thought it was very appropriate. Bringing light to issues that we currently have in our society, in a casual manner that doesn't feel forced or interrupts the story. The newspapers add to it well. And the way the game subtly talked about itself, and some reasons behind it's creation... I can tell a lot of time, work, and love was put into this. So much dedication and care. I love the game it has turned out to be, everyone who worked on it should be very proud. And lastly, one of my favorite parts... The short stories in the Evening Whispers app. I absolutely LOVED them. I almost forgot about them, since there was no notification on the app each day that a new story dropped, but thank god I remembered to check it, because each of those short stories was a ride. Some were weird... (you know exactly which one I'm talking about) but the thing I liked about them is that they were similar to the game itself. The endings weren't one note; they often were very open-ended. They left you thinking about it, and could be interpreted in different ways. The themes and messages in the stories were subtle. To me, they were deep, thoughtful snippets. I felt so moved from most of them, especially "Happily Ever After Ever After Ever After..." which I cried after reading. I honestly think that these should be published in an anthology for romantics like myself, hopefully titled "Evening Whispers" so that they can be shared among a wider audience. I feel they need a much deeper appreciation than I can give. But thank you so much to the Devs. All the love in the world, I am sending through this review. As an aspiring writer and game developer, I am so thankful to have played this, and so inspired by the writing here, thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This is very first game I've won from a giveaway in Toge Productions, you have my whole heart.I can't put in better words on how this game makes me feel.The animation is so smooth that it's very soothing, music is perfect to the touch too.I love the art style, so many artists that work together in this game makes this game more meaningful.I wish there's updated folder for the fan art, I would love to look through all of the fan art.The story, this is where it hits me the most.Seeing the relationships between lovers, between family members & friends or even more than friends;the racial issue stated here was handled so well that it makes me think about how hard it would be in their shoes.I really enjoy that they bought game devs and writers to light, Being able to read Freya's essays while knowing what was going on makes it more enjoyable.How there's appreciation on each game scope makes this game feels very real, it felt like we're talking to the characters ourselves.As a ex-barista trainee; I;d say the making coffee process is pretty spot on!The creative recipes make the game better, it brings out Asian culture and well done on researches.I'd love to make drinks based on Coffee Talk recipes.Coffee Talk is unlike other games, heavily focuses on story telling which is delivered beautifully,not too long and relatable too.It's a plus that you can make choices in the game, watch how other characters live their lives and share about themselves;Thank you Toge Productions for hosting the giveaway 2 years ago.This is my first game I've ever gotten giveaway from and the first game community that I was active in;thank you for giving voices to other indie game devs and for making games that tells stories that hits the feels.Well done, Toge team <3

_childDocuments_.review: I’m kinda attracted to games like this, like visual novels but with interactions that go a little beyond choosing conversation options, and that have a neat relaxed atmosphere. Although I admit that I haven't played many of this style, and the one that has stayed with me the most has been VA-11 Hall-A: Cyberpunk Bartender Action. At the time, Coffee Talk was recommended to me, and just having coffee in the name had me more than interested; however, until now I had not fully taken the bait, but what better time than to try it when the sequel is just around the corner.Coffee Talk is a visual novel with touches of simulation, which focuses on socializing and serving different drinks to a varied and extraordinary clientele. We will assume the role of the "barista" (default name that can be changed, and who I will identify as him for easier reading): owner of the establishment that shares its name with the title, and who lends his ear, and sometimes some help, to those who visit his cozy coffee shop. The  is set in a universe where humans are not the only thinking or predominant race, and many creatures from folklore inhabit the land alongside them. These different lineages abandoned their mysticism to embrace modernization, such as elves who left their forests behind to live in concrete jungles, or dwarves who used their knowledge to open large automotive chains. Orcs, mermaids, even species from beyond the galaxy; all kinds of individuals coexist in this place.More specifically, our story unfolds in Seattle, in the year 2020, and in a corner of this city is where Coffee Talk is located, the aforementioned cafe where the entire game will take place. Said story will be not so much about us as players and barista, but about the varied and unique characters that visit this establishment. Some are already frequent, others are newcomers and strangers to us, but in general very charismatic and individual, and are attracted to this mysterious place because of its somewhat special mode of operation; after all, it opens at night, and focuses on serving those who crave a cup of coffee in the cold hours of the dark.We will gradually become involved in the small, and also big, chats of the visitors, and we will slowly learn about them as people, their motivations, tastes, or even personal problems. For example, we will have Freya, a peculiar writer who one would say pretty much lives in the cafeteria, and works in a renowned newspaper while trying to create and publish her own fictional stories. There are also Hyde and Gala, a vampire and a werewolf, races that have been enemies in the past, but between them they have formed a friendly relationship that overcomes any stereotype of the past. Jorji, a neighborhood policeman, Lua and Baileys, a couple struggling for acceptance from their parents for racial reasons, and several more individuals will be part of this captivating plot; which, I must say, I loved from beginning to end. The narration is very entertaining, the interactions between us and the customers, and themselves with each other, are highly enjoyable and kept me totally hooked with the reading. On more than one occasion I wanted to put myself in the role of another visitor, to sit down and share a coffee and a chat with these charming personalities, and to be able to feel in the flesh the relaxed atmosphere that the game provided. Without a doubt I loved this section, it is very funny and touching at the moments it should be, but it is especially enjoyable from beginning to end.The  is divided into reading and advancing the text, and serving the drinks ordered by our customers. For the latter, we will have a mini-game where we will choose our ingredients and prepare the orders of each visitor separately. From simple and delicious espresso coffee, to more advanced and particular combinations such as “Masla Chai tea”, made with ginger and cinnamon. All these recipes can be unlocked by trial and error, but we will have some already enabled from the beginning, and our lovable clients will usually give us a clue as to how they are prepared.Related to that, we can use our cell phone to see the recipes we have already learned, and we will also have the opportunity to use other applications, such as: the column diary where Freya writes, the music player with which we can change the background song, and "Tomodachil", a social network where we can see information about customers, and that updates as we advance their personal plots. Apart from this, the game has an extras menu where we can see the image gallery, composed from official images to fan-art and some very nice comics, for example.There is not much more to say about it, although I must add that when creating latte we will be able to enter another mini-game (mini-game-ception) where we can create art on top of the drink; yes, just like they do on social media. Although it does not influence much of what we do, it is fun. The truth is that the game handles this section very well, it is simple and very calm, without timers (except in a game mode apart from the story) or pressure, and we have up to five attempts per night to recreate the drink that we are asked for; I think that, in all that I played, I only threw a coffee to redo it, since in general it is all very intuitive. The  section is captured in a beautiful pixel art from the menus and environments to the characters. The character design is beautiful, and I loved how unique and different each Coffee Talk customer is (even though we, as the barista, don't have a face or sprite at any time), ranging from the typical human like Freya, to a girl from Atlantis who has a more triton-like appearance. In addition to the interior of the cafe, we can also see the street in the distance through the shop windows, and glimpse at passersby of varying complexions wandering the streets from one side to the other; this gave me a very atmospheric air of mysticism, making me wonder what kind of races and creatures I must have missed just because they didn't dare to set foot in the shop.The  helps the game's atmosphere a lot, featuring extremely relaxing melodies that generate a very cozy and special vibe. Listening to the sound of the rain (an icon of environmental relax music) and a pleasant song at a slow pace, while paying attention to the characters and their chats, is a very comfortable experience and I enjoyed it to the fullest. The audiovisual section as a whole was splendid to me, I loved every detail in the expressions of the customers, the playlist changes that created an organic and somewhat more realistic scene, and I feel I couldn't ask for more in this aspect. In , Coffee Talk is a game that left me very immersed in its world, practically kidnapping me in that enjoyable and peculiar environment, where it introduced me to precious characters full of individuality, and entertained me with a simple mini-game that appeals to my tastes (I love coffee, what can I say). It's a story that is made up of several narratives, a combination of day-to-day chatter and moments that even though they are happening in a fantasy world, feel extremely real and that one can resonate with; especially seeing the different people of various hierarchies and races share points of view and help each other, it’s just very pleasing.  I've come across these publishers before, when I played “A Space for the Unbound”, and I'm not at all surprised that they have conveyed so many emotions to me; their narratives are completely to my liking, and now I have more than confirmed it. I know that the game has a well-deserved popularity, but I hope that those who are still interested, but have not had the opportunity, give it a chance and try to play it; I invite you to stop by the cafe, and get to know this charming universe, in which I had a beautiful stay.

_childDocuments_.review: Made me want to open a coffee shop ... for like 5 seconds before I realised I absolutely do not want to open a coffee shop. It's an enjoyable premise. I do have to note though that the game lies to you at some points. It presents overpopulation as an actual issue rather than a completely fabricated one. And it presents racism as a natural result of human nature rather than the result of rich psychopaths pitting us against each-other for profit.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: It's VA-11 HALL-A with coffee and urban fantasy instead of cyberpunk. That sounds reductionist, but it's as close to a reskin of that game as you can possibly get. It's a VN in a coffee shop where your only interaction with the game is serving drinks, which influence the story in ways that are not particularly clear. It wasn't a great mechanic in VH, though, and it's not really any better here.So you're here for the story, which is a solid way to spend two hours. It's maybe a bit implausibly dramatic, and the world is so obviously just ours with different names that I don't know why they bothered with the fantasy races, but that doesn't hurt anything. My only complaint is that the end implies there's some metastory going on, but the gameplay is, like VH, so unintuitive that I frankly have no idea what I'd need to do to see it and can't be bothered. Maybe someday later when someone else has figured it out.It isn't going to blow anyone's socks off, but I'm happy with what I got out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: good things: the art stylebad things: no control over the story. its just a visual novel with no gameplay mechanics except finding a combo of three ingredients to make a drink? the characters start out okay but at the end of each day i'm sick of them. they're flat and the dialogue is predictable and the game thinks its better than it is so it just comes across as a snobby hipster art game. the characters are cardboard cutouts and i could go on a much longer rant about the nature of the worldbuilding and the implications of the fantasy racism - which is just cheap. i really wanted to like this, but other games did this bartending simulator concept better.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this isn't exactly a very active game, it's more of a simulation and a nice balance between visual novel and gameplay. The only actual gameplay you get is  That being said, this was an amazing experience, and I absolutely enjoyed every moment of it. If you're someone who really likes well-written stories and want to immerse yourself in one, I recommend Coffee Talk! I'm positive you will find something, or many things, you will enjoy about this game.Without spoiling too much, the characters have a great backstory each, and it's hard not to get invested in every single one of them. I could really relate to some characters, while others reminded me of people I know. Everyone has their own charm and uniqueness, and everyone is so interesting and full of personality. Truly, the writing shines brilliantly in this game, and through it, I could tell how much love and passion the devs of this game had for it.Lastly, this game was a gift from someone who was a friend of the talented and passionate writer, Mohammad Fahmi. I am very grateful to have played this game, and am blessed to have been able to see such a masterpiece in my lifetime.Dear Fahmi, may you rest in peace, kind sir. We shall never forget the legacy you have left behind, and the many hearts you have touched.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so difficult for me to review, because I really want to like it, but I could barely get through the first 2 hours. The main reason I got this game is because it looked a lot like VA11-HALL A (quite a bit of reviews also said it reminded them of VA11-HALL A, too), which really excited me because it's one of my favorite games of all time. However, as I started playing Coffee Talk, I just found myself wanting to be playing VA11-HALL A instead.This might just me being way too picky with visual novels, but in my opinion, if you're making a visual novel, your writing needs to be VERY strong. Coffee Talk's writing is passable, but it's not nearly as good as VA11-HALL A's, which makes it pale in comparison, especially with it's similar art direction and style. The dialogue is stilted and awkward more than charming a lot of the times, and there are multiple grammar and punctuation errors (this might be because the game was originally written in a different language, but I couldn't find any mention of that on the Steam page). Again, this game really feels like it's trying to follow in VA11-HALL A'S footsteps, and there is a genuinely interesting and cozy premise here. From as far as I got, it seemed like it was doing an inverse of VA11-HALL A's setting (mostly interpersonal conflict with a bit of societal conflict interspersed). It's far less "doomer" than VA11-HALL A, but the writing is far too heavy-handed and has not been edited or "tightened up" enough. It's a shame, too, because I can see the inklings of a good game in here, but the writing and characters seem like one-note or combinations of VA11-HALL A characters.One last related note, the fact that you can choose to name your character (presumably to put your name in) at the start really creates a tonal disconnect between you as the player and the character you control. The player character has far too much of a characterization to be that sort of "blank slate" that you want for an audience stand-in. I found myself wondering why my character was being overly sarcastic and almost even mean to Freya at points. In my opinion, the game is much better if you don't name your character after yourself and choose a different name, because if you end up trying to play as yourself, it ruins a lot of the immersion the game tries to create.

_childDocuments_.review: Even without comparing the game to VA-11 HALL-A and judging it by its own merits, it's not good.The world building is awful, most of characters are flat and all talk the same, the use of fantasy elements as a veil to talk about real world issues is tissue thin, it doesn't look that great, the protagonist is a cardboard cutout for Freya (the real main character) to talk to, and the one game mechanic it has is poorly realised.You make drinks by picking from three ingredients, and you can double or triple up on them. But the order you have to put the ingredients in matters. Coffee + Ginger + Milk makes a ginger latte, while Coffee + Milk + Ginger apparently makes rocket fuel. Sometimes when a character gives you the ingredient list, they give it to you in the wrong order.I turned the game off after a character asked for "coffee with a little bit of ginger", so I made a ginger latte (which is only 1 part ginger) and the game gave me a slap on the wrist for getting the order wrong. Not sure I can be bothered to finish it after that. Clearly the game just wants me to shut up and watch its bad story play out like a good sheep.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a tendency to be poignant when we revisit the work of someone who died recently. Good art is one that communicates, and there is undoubtedly sadness when we feel that connection from a person who will no longer be able to give it. As an Indonesian, and a gaming enthusiast, I would certainly prefer that such an inspirational figure as Mohammad Fahmi could have communicated more. Here was a young, Indonesian game dev who could have done more to show his fellow Indonesians great things beyond highly popular online games such as Mobile Legends or PUBG. But there is wisdom in preferring to be grateful for what happened rather than regretful for what could have been. Coffee Talk is nothing short of a lovely experience. You play as a barista of a midnight cafe in an alternate reality Seattle where fantasy races live alongside humans. Through the lives of the cafe regulars, we are told life stories that happen to people of varying generations and races, about complications in relationship and acceptance involving spheres of game dev, fiction writing, pop music, and even extraterrestrial dating. The only twist is that these traditionally monster races couldn't be depicted as more human.The main feature of the game is the second word of the title: the talking. Yes there is coffee-making (and other beverages), even latte art, but there's no vital consequence for failing to fulfill orders. There doesn't need to be. The game is supposed to be played deliberately, while understanding each character as a person with their own feelings, desires, and expectations. Coffee Talk won't amaze you, but it will make you cozy while at times providing conversations that reminds you of very real, very human situations.Fahmi's legacy for myself is this: I don't personally know him, but I will make sure to keep him in my mind every time I think of the game dev scene in Indonesia.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: If you're tired of action games that require intense focus then this may be for you. Coffee Talk provides a calm atmosphere allowing you to relax and just listen to some customers talk about life. The game is good but its not  Other games in a similar category such as  do this genre much better. Coffee Talk is interesting in its own way with cute art, and simple stories. But its not the peak of the genre. It has about 5 hours of game-play (8 hours if you think repeating the main story with near minimal dialogue change counts as continuing the story). But it has its place. The music is very chill and similar to what you may find on YouTube when you look up . And the coffee shop itself and the rain outside makes it feel like a place of warmth and comfort. It certainly helped me relax after a stressful day of classes. In summary, its a  game. But its not great.

_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Welp, seems like I'm in the tiny minority who did not enjoy this game.I saw people praising it and since I was looking for something short and cozy for a change, I got it when it was on sale. However, whatever all the people who have left positive reviews saw in this game was clearly lost on me.First, there were no options to pick when it came to dialogue which frustrated me a lot. I get this is a visual novel but I would've wanted to have at least some sort of options to choose from, now it was simply clicking and clicking and clicking while reading dialogue which I could not take any part of in any meaningful way. There are visual novels that offer you choices and I was expecting that from Coffee Talk as well but was sorely disappointed.Second, the stories to me were simply boring and really did nothing for me so reading through all that stuff was just painful. And here's the thing: I do not not mind reading when it comes to video games. At all. Some of my favourite games ever have massive amounts of reading to be done, so it is not about reading just not being my thing. I probably wouldn't have even minded not having any dialogue options to choose from that much if only the stories were actually interesting enough and written in a way that captivated me, but none of that happened here. I was actually waiting for the game to end because I just wanted it to be over already so I could go and play something else and that tells enough I think.Third, the coffee making itself was too simple. Just mix three ingredients together and that's it. And even if I got an order wrong which happened a few times, there weren't any consequences, as far as I could tell anyway. Granted, I did not go into this game with the coffee making aspect as my main interest anyway, but since the stories weren't engaging to me and the lack of dialogue options bothered me as well, I hoped at least the coffee making would be interesting. You know, because this game is about a coffee shop. But it was not. So, long story short, not a game I can recommend, personally.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A very well crafted game that is both relaxing and intriguing. All of the characters that are introduced to you throughout the story have their place. You want to see where their story ends up, whether that be positive or negative is up to you, fair barista. It is a nice cozy 4+ hour endeavor that will have you brewing different drinks and listening to peoples problems. I love the soundtrack too, I will definitely be picking up the vinyl soundtrack when I can. All in all it is a cozy visual novel that just recently got a sequel that I need to play. Worth every penny
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: The story mode is quick and fun with a few interesting turns. Not necessarily anything new or ground breaking, but incredibly relaxing and fun to play nonetheless. I played it while I was sick and it made me feel better (also made me go get a cup of tea for myself lol). Def going back to get the non-story achievements next time I need to chill a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A visual novel, point and click style game with interesting characters and fun dialogue. There are a few possible endings to get depending on your choices and success at the mini-games (making specific coffee orders). If you're looking for a chill game to relax with after work, or just to take your mind off the current global situation, then this is the one for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts off like waking up on a great day and experiencing various people on the way. But like that only one day, it's very short when eventful and enjoyable. In this game, you starts as a barista owner working leisurely around 9PM to 1AM and you meet various races. Races like dwarves, vampires, werewolves, nekomimis (cat people), aliens, demons, and elves [probably more but the story doesn't cover it]. You make the type of drinks they want and the correct drink will have them talk about their story. There's also a hint about who are you if you made every customer happy at the end.So, I recommend it right now since there's a discount. I just finished it within 3 hours and there is no harm looking up the drinks since some of them are unusual to make without the proper real life ingredients. My gripes...It's short, but I love it since it was talking about these selected stories. I wanted to know more about the lore and more character's stories like it. I did some of the endless mode but....feels missing well, for me. Any bugs? There is one where one of the characters are in a stuck animation and you can't do anything except reload to fix it. I recommend to save every time they want you to make a drink. There's only one save file, BUT you can reload the entire day within the calender if you want re-fix a drink you messed up on that day.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Literally my dream of opening a cozy and small coffee shop with friendly regulars but all in a fantastic game. The story-telling is immaculate and engaging, the coffee making is stress free, and the art style goes perfectly with it. Perfect for a relaxing game session with soft cafe music playing in the background. (The hours I have on this game really shows how much I liked it)
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is fine, good vibe, interesting art and setup, but somehow you feel the game is missing a lot of stuffs, and unfortunately, this game will be compared with another similar game Va-11 Hall-A, especially of what is missing in comparison to that said game.If you are looking for the complexity of the bartender gameplay you have tried on Va-11 Hall-A, like mixing with interesting drinks and ingredients to have secret outcomes and affect the story, you will be somewhat disappointed. A new gameplay mechanic is the latte art editor. While it is fun to fully dive into the editor making some crazy artwork with it, the editor has no impact to the game overall. There is one occasion of one client asking for a latte art, you can spend hours to perfect latte art or just simply one click the pour milk and call it a day, the client will still give you the same response. The editor has a lot of potential, like making a smily face or other art and shapes might change the client mood or conversation, but right now it just serve as an extra add-on. Nothing more nothing less.If you want something to play after finishing Va-11 Hall-A and waiting for N1RV Ann-A to come. This game can be a good middle ground, but if you wanted something more than that, you will not find it here.The ending of the game hints for a potential sequel/DLC to expand on the game world or the story, I will still love to see what they can came up with in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A chill slice of life you can spend the night unwinding to. If you are looking for comparisons with vahalla, I think that coffee talk's tone is decisively more "normal" and its discussions/themes touches a lot more on everyday issues. The tone in vahalla was more quirky and the discussions tended to delve a lot more into the sci-fi/internet sub-culture. In contrast, coffee talk does raise some interesting discussions about the fantasy races which appear in it, but many of them feel like shallow parallels to the real world, rather than trying to build a unique fictional world from it. With that being said, the characters were pretty charming and I enjoyed the interactions between them. The main path definitely felt shorter than vahalla, which is a shame because it would have been nice to have more filler conversations between characters.Gameplay wise, I did appreciate that not all recipes are unlocked at first, and gives you space to experiment with different recipes. You have moments where customers will ask you for a drink you don't even have a recipe to, and it felt a lot more engaging than having every drink recipe from the get-go. Overall, the drink-making mechanics exist as a gateway to the narrative, so similarly to vahalla, if you are looking for a challenging game loop, this genre isn't the place to look.Overall, for its price, it's a welcome addition to the genre that vahalla started. If you like slice of life, I think you will enjoy your time with coffee talk.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: i'm gonna write this review while the memory is still fresh. i'm just gonna say it right off the bat, this game is amazing.lately i've been going through a rough patch but despite that i barely cry at anything, yet for some reason, this game made me bawl my eyes out on multiple occasions even though it's not a very sad game. it just feels so incredibly cozy and friendly and in the  5+/- hours of runtime this game has it get's you so incredibly invested in the main characters that it hurt to see the game end. i honestly hope they add more days or dlc or whatever so we can experience more story. i've been feeling very alone in this world and i guess the feeling that this game gives off is what i am missing in real life.please keep up the great work.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is not interesting.The "It's Seattle but with different species!!!!" concept is pure window dressing. It's all just young metropolitan Americans talking about young metropolitan American issues. It's the sort of thing you've seen a thousand times before as the core plot of some disney channel originals. There's no intrigue and all the characters sound like they've been written by a millenial, even the "old" ones. I don't like the character who regularly comes in to your cafe and orders espresso. Her quips aren't smooth, she's quite annoying, and she'll admonish someone for being too direct with their advice and then do the exact same thing herself the next day. If it's a story about how its hard to be self-aware and internally consistent, that would be fine and maybe even interesting. As it stands, it seems like the plots will eventually resolve themselves without any thing of value being discussed or learned by the characters. You might say that it doesn't matter because its a chill experience, but why bother with reading something trash when you can listen to low-fi hiphop and play a gardening game?One more thing about the setting. It's supposed to be a "diverse" type American city where people care about not offending anyone else. So why is the player character saying lines like "You're a vampire, right? Aren't you guys supposed to be tough?" Imagine mentioning that sort of stereotype about any minority in America. You would at minimum get a stink-eye, and probably be called a racist. But the vampire you're talking to responds to it as if its a perfectly acceptable question, probably because internal consistency in the world is less important than having the vampire explain his backstory. It's lazy writing.The "gameplay" is mediocre, as basically the proper way to do things right is to randomly guess the arrangement of ingredients until the combination leads to an interestingly named drink. I used a guide because I didn't really care by the time I had to figure things out myself. Latte art is unintuitive and doesn't affect anything.(Edit: If you've ever made pour-over coffee or looked into espresso you would know that bean variety and preparation is a big deal. Having espresso triple-shot being made by throwing coffee in the machine three times isn't really pushing the envelope here. Fine, its not a game for coffee makers. But who is it for then? People who want to role-play having friends?)Music is good/fine for the atmosphere, though probably better than an actual Seattle cafe by a couple light-years. The Sprite-work is fine, but your regular's facial expressions get annoying. Of note is the steam/smoke effect coming off of hot drinks and cigarettes. It's clearly not done in a similar way to the other art, and stands out in a less than good way.Wait, it's a cafe in Seattle! Why is everyone allowed to smoke at the counter!?!?!?!To summarize, it's hard to recommend a story game where its clear that I took more care to read it than was taken to write it. It's boring, the character interactions are either dumb or an intentional representation of dumb people, and the "twist" is badly integrated. Go watch a Disney TV movie on your phone while cooking something for dinner. It's a better use of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: The general themes and aesthetics of this game are really nice, I like the premise of making coffee and hearing people's stories. However, the story feels weak at times, boring even. I was rather disappointed in the queer baiting that happened. They include characters with obvious romances but the only love story's that happen are the hetero ones, and the story's revolving around queer relationships are not touched on. They were too afraid it seems to have even mentioned the queer relationships that were alluded to. The only character in the story that was of other gender was made an alien who didn't understand how gender functioned as a role at all, which made it all feel very numb to me. Disappointing to say the least.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is a really interesting game for me. I don't usually play much less have interest in this sort of game but Coffee Talk's aesthetics and character designs caught my eye from the screenshots on the store page. I knew it was a game I wanted to play so I bought it and even though I took my sweet ass time with this game and could've "beaten"it much quicker I had a blast thoroughly playing this game. Getting to meet and talk to all these characters is a joy and the meme "lofi and chill" sums this game up perfectly. Although the music in this game is nice I personally turn it off and rock Boris or something along those lines. If there was any one word I would use to describe this game it would be "peaceful". Even though there's many moments of conflict throughout the game it never really takes away from the peaceful vibes I get from this game. The game (I don't think anyway from the few times I got an order wrong) heavily punishes you in game but if you care about these characters as much as I do you feel bad when you screw up an order and I like that since it's all about me and not the game in an instance like that. There is an endless mode but I didn't try that out and honestly don't really have an interest in that since what drew me into this game to begin with was the aesthetics and character designs and what made me stay until the end was said characters. I'm not sure how replayable this game may or may not end up being for me but I'm glad I got to play this game and if you have any interest in games with great characters/ character writing is important to you than this is your game. R.I.P Mohammad Fahmi Hansi
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a cozy and relaxing game with a fun story narrative. I found this game by accident i was just looking around at the spring sale and this popped up in the recommended area, it looked cute so I said why not. Do i regret it? Not one bit!  The music and the characters are great, i really enjoyed my time playing this game and cant wait for the next one. The story is well written and the fact that you get to make the drinks is a great add to a story game and i enjoyed it alot. Shout out to Myrtle for always ordering drinks we dont know how to make.Also i do always love a good plottwist at the end... Or is it the end?
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: The game has potential but as many indie games it feels like it could have used some more polishing.Also, the replay value is just not there.I did find that the dialogue was fun to read, but that was about it. I think it would benefit from added choices that impact the overall game experience or punishment of some sort for giving characters the wrong coffee... anything to actually make it a GAME. It was rather short, too. Really, please, polish your games, don't just leave things as is just because it kind of works and because the majority of people find this great. I don't know, maybe my standards are just too high but I like it when a project's potential is used to the max. This isn't the case here.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Very Good game but short and weird.  This was a short game that was a pretty cool experience. Its very unique, has interesting characters and it is very compelling. The gameplay is relatively simple, consisting of dialogue and a minigame of making the best drinks by picking the right components. I would not recommend it for everyone but if a chill, short game about people talking in a coffee shop sounds interesting this game might be for you. If game length is an important purchase point for you then this might be important. I beat the game in about 4 hours and have most of the achievements and I believe I have experienced the full story. There is some replayability, you can go back and redo certain days, a challenge/endless mode for the coffee minigame and is some mod support that might help add more length to the game. But for the base game I cant imagine it would take longer then 6-8 hours to 100% the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: If you want good lofi music, characters that you fall in love with and a plot that's heartwarming and blows your mind, Coffee Talk is for you. I absolutely love this game. This was the first game that I played on my stream and I fell in love immediately. The music is soothing to my heart and the characters are just as warm as the drinks! As an ex-barista I enjoyed making coffees and teas and chatting with my customers. The story behind every character and the game itself was definitely worth every hour of my play-through. I would definitely play this game again! I 100% the game on stream and the ending was INCREDIBLE! I love visual novels and this is definitely my top rated one!
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: If you come into this game expecting something like Papers Please from a mechanical-storytelling standpoint, prepare to be disappointed. Coffee Talk isn't bad, it's premise is very interesting, but it's basically a linear visual novel with a gimmick. There are no choices to be made here, and it's main feature (the coffee making mechanic) is inconsequential.The endless mode is also stupidly easy. In it the characters tell you exactly how to make the drinks they want - not fun at all compared to the main campaign where at least you had to think a little to figure out what drink to make for the characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This is the kind of game best for decompressing after a long day. The story session is very much a visual novel, and the lo-fi music makes it get into vibing pretty easy. The challenge mode in endless is entertaining if memory puzzles are your thing. Perfect for super casual gaming but not much more.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying this game. Interesting & thought provoking storyline. Well written overall, though occasionally a little heavy handed with the theme. Deals with relationships, work, and politics from a mildly left leaning perspective.This game is a bit less interactive than I expected at first. I thought there would be more branching conversation options, and it's a bit weird that you never get to choose what your character, the barista, says. The only interactive element is making coffee drinks, otherwise it's just a visual novel. But an engaging one I plan to play through at least once.Update: Finished this game once and had an alright time. There's a second ending if you play it through a second time, and maybe I'll do it someday, but I'm not in a hurry to repeat the story. This is alright if you like visual novel style storytelling and get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Just did the first playthrough of the game ( It's written to be played a few  times over) and I gotta admit, it was better than I expected.  Since this is a VN ( Visual Novel), Writing and visuals are #1 with the barista minigame as a fun distraction and helps add to the story if you're enjoying it. The Writing:The writing is pretty much what you would expect from a indie title about a coffee shop in Seattle, all the characters basically have societal issues that are 1:1 with our own except for the Werewolf so the use of monsters instead of other human races wasn't really needed, or really used to it's full potential. Wasn't blown off my feet but it was acceptable and wasn't a problem, if you're politically progressive you'll definitely vibe with the characters.Audio & Visuals:The visual execution on this is FANTASTIC. Really did a great job on this one, they nailed the vibe of a modern coffee shop alongside a well drawn cast of characters and fantastic background ambiance. The music eventually became a bit of a snore fest as it seemed to repeat the same few tracks and sound too samey after a few hours ( I played the entire game in 1 session), but considering the selection of tracks on offer it seems to be more user error than the game.  Barista "Minigame": I liked the barista minigame,  it's a fun way of spicing up a visual novel that only adds to the story and doesn't penalize you if you don't know the recipes or remember what someone likes. I had the cheat sheet pulled up for most of the game, and other than forgetting the *spoiler alert* It didn't to affect the story all that much other than you potentially losing some more backstory on the characters in one of the apps on your phone. Conclusion:While the game's story may not be winning a Pulitzer prize for originality, Coffee Talk perfectly nails the environment and vibe of a coffee shop in Seattle and does it beautifully. I hope to see more games like this in the genre that can make Visual Novels a bit more stimulating, but relaxing; just like a Masala Chai.  8/10 Would (and will) buy again :)
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface with: I liked this game. But it is probably not for everyone. I will go with the good, the not good and close with good again. Good: This is a nice, slice of life game in a modern fantasy world. Don't expect action or world-crumbling plot twists. There are multiple storylines that you follow or nudge along in the cafe and I found all of them interesting. It really gives you the feel you are in a corner cafe sipping your coffee while listening to the vibe and other people. Also, this will give you major "let's have a coffee while I play" vibes.  The not so good: - The choices matter tag is, in my opinion, a misnomer. The choices you make are mostly how to prepare the drinks. There are two instances I can think of, that what drink you serve probably affects the story in a visible way. Which  in the spirit of the game! You are there listening, offering a word or two and preparing drinks. It is reasonable that you won't be able to significantly alter the life trajectory of someone by serving green tea instead of coffee. - I liked all the stories and all the characters. I doubt everyone will feel the same though. But they are all realistically written characters that act in ways you would expect. - The main sticking point for me is... the length of the game. I am  and it took me just 5 hours to finish the main story and go back to check a few alternate days. I understand that the pricing of the game may be fine for those in high-income countries, but for me, the price of this game was equivalent to the cost of going to a cafe with friends three times. And I got the game . I feel that a game at the price range this one is in, should have at least 15 hours of playtime. That said, I already bought episode 2, for the price of 4 visits to a cafe with friends. Which should tell people that are still reading this review that I either need better friends or that this game was worth that despite the duration. Back to good: - Freya for the win. Loved her. She is the friend material that gives the vibes of the childhood friend even though according to the game you know her for just a few years. - Jorji the policeman. I loved that stoic, low-key guy and I wish he would have a bigger part on the story. His discussions with the Barrista and Freya were the high-points of the game, IMO. His calmness counteracts Freya's turbulence. - I already mentioned that I bought chapter 2. That is because I want to see how the characters are doing 3 years later. I am not prepared to say goodbye to them yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is what would happen if you took the music genre of Lo-Fi and turned it into a game. Nearly every single minute of playing this game is just relaxing yet engaging that is perfect to play when you just want to kick back and enjoy a nice environment. Coffee Talk is a visual novel style game where you, as the barista, engage in conversation with numerous interesting characters found in the fictional world of Seattle. Yes, Seattle, but the twist is that this world is inhabited by fantasy races such as elves and werewolves. Its quite an interesting concept just slapping these type of creatures into the modern world but it works perfectly.The gameplay is nothing special, it is a really linear game where you're mostly reading through dialogues with little to no input outside of making drinks for your customers. The drink making minigame along with the latte art was fun enough but outside of achievements and achieving the true ending for some characters, it won't impact your playthrough too much. Don't go into this game expecting to make much player choices or affecting the story because again, it is extremely linear.The vibes are just simply great. Aesthetically, they went with a anime-inspired pixel art that just pairs wonderful with the aesthetic of a rustic local coffee store. Music is great, complimenting the relaxed cafe vibes that it is going for. Sound design, while not amazing, also contribute greatly to giving you that comforting and relaxing atmosphere. At any given time, you will see the rain hitting the windows, muffled enough to be background noise but present enough to set the mood. The sound of the door ringing as a customer approaches alerts you just enough but not so much that it'll take you out of the current conversation. And the sound of you making drinks, from pouring tea to boiling coffee just ASMR to me. It truly makes me want to visit my locally own cafe just to get this same experience.The meat of the game comes from the writing. As stated in the beginning, I said this is what happen when you turn lo-fi into a game and while that still rings true, this game does not shy away from heavier topics. Each character that comes to your store have their own little baggage. As the game progresses and as they come by more and more to your humble coffee store to relax with a drink, you also begin to dive deeper into each character's personality and stories as they open up to you more. Topics can range from lovers struggling to stay together because of family and racism (As mentioned earlier, racism here is refer to different species rather than different culture/ skin tone), a father struggling to protect his daughter who wants to be an adult, a girl trying to overcome her social anxiety and much more. This add a level of relatability to certain characters depending on the player. And even if they don't provide any sense of relatability, they can at least provide some insight into those topics to other players.Despite all these heavy topics that are prevalent throughout the story, the cozy vibes of the game never goes away. You are simply there to offer people a nice play to relax in and a hot drink. Customers resolve their own issues as you watch as an outsider (sometimes injecting in). You find yourself relating to one character because they are going through what you may have gone through or is going through. People find confidants in you and others who gathered under a cafe for a warm drink. You and your coffee store is simply a vessel for many characters to air out their problems.So kick back and grab a hot drink of your choice because this game is perfect if you just need something to relax to. Give it a chance and you might find yourself feeling like you're running an actual coffee shop and may even grow attached to some of these characters or their stories. Regardless if you're into coffee or social issues that is brought up by this game, one thing that can't be deny and that is the vibes is immaculate.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I tend to write longer reviews for visual novels however I don't really know how to express my love for this game in general. If you played Va-11 Hall-a you'll like this, Red Strings Club, you'll like this, Necrobarista isn't out yet but i assume that's gonna be in the same vein.So instead I'm gonna talk about the Soundtrack, a collection of slow and mellow "coffee shop" music. To me they're all songs you could easily listen to on a rainy but warm day in the middle of summer, under an awning drinking some tea. I don't know if that imagery can be put across through words, but it has a very nostalgic aura. Notable tracks in my opinion include: Gleefully, Way Too Soon, The Last Time, Moon Bright. Cup of Sweetness, Come Closer, It Smells Good, and One More Time. If that sounds like a lot, it's because Andrew Jeremy did an absolutely fantastic job on setting the tone and atmosphere through the music and i can't imagine the game without it, solid 9/10 OST
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I ADORE THIS GAME SO MUCH. I have only played the main game and  although its short its so entertaining. Its the perfect game for wanting to shut off your brain, listening to the woes of different fantasy characters while making tea and coffee. The ending hit me with a jaw drop and I think it'll do the same for most people. It can be played quickly or slowly and doesn't take much brain power. Would genuinely recommend this, especially if you're going through a stressful time, it takes the pressure off with the beautiful comic strip designs and seamless game play, just wish it was longer!
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I had a friend of mine recommend it to me, so I got it. I'm a barista so I think it's pretty funny to play a game as a barista. The story is really interesting and experimenting with the drinks is also a lot of fun. I definitely think that sometimes the story falls off a little and gets boring, but that's because it's a laid back and chill game. Definitely nothing insane happening, just a person writing a book.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Now, before I start it's good to point out I don't usually enjoy visual novels. This game has been one of the few exceptions. Does it have a groundbreaking story? No, but for the price I found it very enjoyable. It has plenty of content to keep you entertained, and I was surprised to find things changed if you went into NG+! There's also an endless mode, if that suits for fancy for serving drinks. I think the only complaint I have is that some characters ask for drinks that you do not know how to make, and they don't tell you how to make them. There are a few ways you can figure them out, but all involve some experimenting. You may like this, but it wasn't my cup of tea (ha). Overall I enjoyed my time with the game, and I can confidently recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I like how immersive the world in the game is, how the newspaper paint a picture of the world outside from what you hear in the coffee shop. The patrons themselves show deep backstories and character, even if they don't seem that important the first time you meet them. This game is filled with personality and is one of my favourites to unwind to. Music is amazing<3
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game to just sit and relax with. I liked the way the story was told, it felt very fitting for the setting. Every character had their own personality and really made this little coffee shop come alive. I especially loved the art, and while the animations slowed the game down a little, I personally thought they were the finishing touches. The music brought it all together and made it a relaxing experience.The only downside was that it was too short. I would have loved more characters, more stories, or just more about the lives of this cast.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is a very laid back visual novel. It expresses themes and conversations that can easily be related to today's world. Though you are in a set location the entire time, I feel like the world building is nicely done by listening to the varying characters that you encounter and reading the quick headlines you read before starting that day's encounter. The different character personalities are very lovable and their designs are all unique. Though the game is only a couple hours long, I felt very connected to them as I played. My only dislike is that there is not a lot of interactivity within the game besides making the customer orders, but I don't entirely mind it, as we are mainly just listening to the lives of our customers and their daily struggles. Though, this fact becomes especially understandable if you do the secret ending as well, which is not difficult to get at all and is accessible after the main story.All in all, if you are looking for a nice and relaxing visual novel, I would highly recommend Coffee Talk.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of my greatest disappointments :(So, you own a coffee shop to talk and make some drinks. But you don't have choices of what you say. You don't have a complex or fun way to make drinks either. You just mix 3 ingredients, do a boring Latte Art and read a lot of text. That's it.Pros:- Stunning Artwork- Amazing soundtrack- Fantasy universe (aliens, vampires, monsters of all kinds)- It's a Barista game - one of my favorite themesCons:- You don't have dialog choices. It is like you are a NPC in your game (This is the major reason for the negative review).- No voice acting- No feeling of immersion- Characters histories are 'cliché':(
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy the atmosphere of the game and the world it presented. The music and the visuals fit the premise well. Beyond that however, the experience didn't feel substantial- the plot felt like it was written for TV but thinned and repackaged for a couple hours of content. Some of the dialogue and character actions seemed unnecessary and mundane when the game should have been keeping the story moving. The sense that one should feel control over the game world through the drink making was awkward and lacking impact and feedback. Having the characters suggest the drinks was too guided, and understanding the impact of certain mixes was overly vague. Perhaps a different view of coffee shops could power this game, but personally I didn't feel that the experience was meaningful enough to warrant recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A solid "Get Va11HallA instead, unless this is on sale. Otherwise, maybe.".Coffee Talk: Fantasy Coffee-brewing Action, is a day-by-day visual novel with slight coffee-brewing mechanics on the side. Its storyline is broken up into several days, of which customers visit your coffee shop and talk. The first few days are rather short: no longer than a few minutes, but as the story advances the days become more packed with story. The game as a whole is rather short, less than 3 hours to complete the main storyline. Overall, generally a well rounded game, but not $15. On the other hand, it compares rather poorly to Va11halla, a game with a nigh identical format, but has more characters, story, and charm. If you liked Va11halla, and really can't wait for N1RVAnnA, then get it on sale. Otherwise, just get Va11halla. But I'm still recommending it because steam doesn't allow maybes, and there's very little competition for this niche of VN.
