_childDocuments_.review: Small note: My objective for my recommendations is not here to be scholarly, but rather to tell you why exactly I liked it. I will try to include some insights as far as the genre of the game -- in this instance visual novels -- even if I'm not particularly savvy with them. But I want to try and give somewhat of a comprehensive but not exhaustive view of the game. 😊The thing that pulled me into this game was after I played it for a little bit. I'm at a point in my life where I really enjoy stories and I enjoy whenever I'm able to get to see character development and development of the environment as it relates to the story. I do enjoy an extensive development on the environment, but here it's rather simple, and it does it well. This game was fun for a run through, and it was a little short, but I definitely think it's worth it. I am not someone who plays visual novels very much, but this was one where I almost felt compelled to review it positively because it was a game where I  want to move forward to the end. But let's dive in and see what it was that compelled me to go forward, and also some of the things that weren't so great. ✅  - This is something that I would think would be somewhat difficult, but here it feels pretty organic. There are these people that come in with their problems they endure during the day, and they rely on you for some enjoyment for their drink. Whether you're giving them their well needed caffeine with a triple espresso, or just a hot chocolate an they feel the warmth of it in from the difficulties they're experiencing, it feels smooth. I enjoyed the almost minigame atmosphere of the coffee making and that it went in tandem with the storytelling and characters. The storytelling was great, and all of it connected. It also gives you endings to all of the stories you encounter, and a dash of replayability! ✅  - It almost seems like they were keenly aware of this from the get-go. There is a little companion app that you have on your mobile device in the game that picks up pieces of information about each one of the characters the more interactions you have with them. It feels good to get to know them more intimately and, even though the interactions are scripted, you can feel your barista character getting to know the characters and having some stake in their interactions. I don't want to go too much into detail about what those interactions are, but there is a richness to it where you can feel like the personalities of the characters remind you of people you've met in real life. This is developed in each conversation you have throughout the game. ✅  - There is a bit of depth to this. You have to remember what your customers ordered previously, you can experiment with drinks as well. There is an encouragement to experiment with different drink conversations, but it's also cool to just be able to remember what someone's drink of choice is. On top of this, you can make latte art, which can be somewhat fun. I don't know how accurate to life it is, but it's a nice touch. It really makes me wonder what it will look like in ! ✅  - There are some familiar tunes in this game as well as just some wonderful coffee house vibes. I just enjoyed having this in the background while I'd be looking at and talking to the characters. On top of this, I  pixel art, so I'm a little biased toward enjoying this game's visual style. I would say if you don't like pixelated anything, then definitely don't look at this. And that's okay if you don't.➖  - I've put this at a neutral point, because when I consider price, I think about a combination of the number of hours that I've played, the memorability of the story, the quality of the writing, and how much I really enjoyed it. All of these things together are partially feelings and partially gauging my experience with writing. Now I'm not necessarily going to measure it academically or something, but there can definitely be things we can understand about maybe what's bad writing and good writing? And how that can affect our enjoyment. Here, we have an example of pretty good writing. The characters feel different and real. The story is good, too. And again, it makes me excited for the next one! ➖  - again I'm putting this as a neutral point because, well, I didn't have a bar for this game or expectations, but I definitely wanted more. I played it for 5 hours and there may be <10h of gameplay--for me--in store. And then I'll max out what I think would be my full experience with this game. I'm anticipating something better for the next game, too. Note: While I didn't think this game is perfect, I don't necessarily think that there was a glaring issue that I could really talk about that's important to point out. Well, do I recommend it? Definitely. And with a 40% off price tag? If you tried your first visual novel and it was $7.79 and you absolutely hated it... Well, I don't think you'd be losing too much. There is a group of different characters whose stories are interwoven here, and it's charming. There is a second one coming out, and it should have promise. I'm looking forward to it. I'm excited for it. For a more mechanical and numerical value, I can definitely give this game a  ✅✅✅

_childDocuments_.review: 8.9h (100% achievement, finished the game) No (you need to AFK for 1h for 1 achievement). Yes (~16 achievements). No. is a visual novel where you play as a barista, talking to your customers and serving drinks daily. It tells stories based on your customer's situation, spreading them into several days to watch how it eventually unfolds.- Multiple endings for the characters- Casual conversations that touch well with reality- You need to find the combination to make most drinks with trial and error: AMD Zen 2 4c/8t 2.4-3.5GHz, 16 GB RAM, 8 AMD RDNA 2 CUsI like the pixelated visuals used in . The environment looks detailed with people walking from time to time in the background. The customers also look lively with their detailed animation; they even give an animation of them doing something when the conversation is focused on another customer. Moreover, the music running in the background matches well with this, making you feel as if you are in the coffee shop.The dialogue might look stiff at first. I thought there was something wrong with the translation, so I tried to switch the language because of it. Well, it turns out that it's just meant that way. The early game used formal words that might seem off given the casual situation. Luckily, the dialogue changed into a more casual tone as you played. This is vital since conversations are done through dialogue bubbles between the customers and you, the bartender. Well, the bartender themselves speak in a formal tone, but it shapes their character, especially compared to others who are more laid back. tells the story of day-to-day situations. Several customers come and go with their troubles. There is a writer who wants to write a story, a couple with their issues -- there are even some that simply come just to have a chat with their friend. Some of the stories might be more than what you see in day-to-day situations, but they touch well on some aspects that might happen in our daily lives. I like how the story was wrapped up. Despite the different stories that each character has, I didn't have trouble following them. The dialogue format works well to make it easy to follow, and the story is paced well. Moreover, despite the conflict of interest that the characters face, it doesn't judge and say which is right and wrong right away - it will try telling both sides of the situation first before reaching a conclusion. The choice and the result presented in the game might be different if it were done in real life, but it's the process that matters - checking both sides of the story and trying to be understanding to find a way out. There are two endings for each character. However, finding the other ending can be too vague and might waste your time, especially since it only differs in a few dialogues in the ending. I still prefer the best ending, of course. I like seeing the characters get what they want after everything they have gone through.  is mainly a visual novel. You need to go through dialogues, divided into several days to proceed with the story. Since it's still a coffee shop, the customers will order drinks from time to time. You start with a small array of ingredients, but it will improve as you progress through the days.Making drinks is simple. You just need to choose 3 ingredients and mix them up. The result is already predetermined, and since there are a lot of ingredients to choose from, you are expected to do trial and error to find the combination that you need. It can be hard to find what the customer wants. You are only given 5 tries every day, and sometimes, your customer will ask for a drink with hardly any clue. Sometimes, they will only tell the name. There is even a case where you are supposed to make a drink that the customers themselves don't know -  It's kinda like a "surprise me" kind of thing. I hate these since I was forced to save scum just to find the correct one, especially since you can only remake the drink for 5 times each day. Even though there is a fast-forward option, the animation when you make a drink and the customer's vague reaction might cause trouble if you choose the save scum option. Moreover, there are just too many combinations to try, and since order matters, you'll end up with more combinations to work with.I finished the game in 5.7h. I continued playing the endless mode after that for some achievements and left the game open for ~1h for the last achievement.Since it's a visual novel, the game won't give you trouble. You might need to do trial and error to get the drink that your customer wants, but you also can look at a guide if you don't want the extra trouble.As for the replayability, you can replay the game to get the other endings, but honestly, I don't think it's worth another replay. Just watch a  video for the other ending instead since it'll be faster.It's hard to know which button was highlighted in the menu.I like . It's a game meant for casual players with a story that is easy to digest. You'll see day-to-day situations in a coffee shop, with some unique stories from the customers. It's a game that can make you chill and relax, especially due to the relaxing music running in the background. If all of these sound interesting to you, you'll definitely enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is a very good game made to be played during fall: the visuals and the music are cozy, the gameplay is simple enough that you could sip coffee yourself during it and the whole game takes place during the season.The latter is something I wish more games did: playing the game in the same days it takes place greatly improves immersion, and it also helps that, despite all the fantasy elements, the story could totally happen in the current times.Many elements of the game are well though out. For starters, the gameplay, while simple and easy, has a bit of depth behind it, as you have to unlock recipes and serve the right drink based on the requests of the customers; for people that are not satisfied with the story, the game even has a challenge mode, which can be pretty difficult. Then, the ability to create your own latte art is a nice time waster where drawing isn't as simple as it would be with a pencil, which can make it rewarding, despite it serves no use.Finally, the game has extras in the form of comics and pictures to unlock, which are a nice way to give even more character to the game.Despite all of this, I'm a bit disappointed by the game, as I didn't feel as immersed as I would have wanted. While the game has a good bit of content, I feel like every day of the story was too short: no day took me more than half an hour to complete and most conversations felt too short, not giving me enough time to get into the characters. I also didn't like how clean slate was the player character: it makes sense, story wise and for immersion, but I wish they were more involved.Other than that, there are more personal reasons, but I still feel the game could have done more.I still recommend the game, despite all: it's a well designed game and, while it missed the mark with me, its story still has a lot going for it. Just try playing it during the right season, it's the best way to enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Super relaxing and fun. Ideally should be played in the evening, preferably with rainy weather. I now understand why my father wanted to open a Cafe.Edit: I feel like my review didn't do this justice. I'm going to start from scratch.At first, I didn't really know what to expect. I must say though, I will never regret buying this game. I'm so glad my friend told me about it. When college started to get stressing for me, I decided to buy it. Seeing how much positive reviews it has, I just had to. More so, I'm very into indie games that have pixel graphics. Honestly, I wasn't really keen of coffee and brewing in particular but, Coffee Talk definitely made me want to get into it. I remember how my mom also took a coffee class too. Anyways, onto the game! I don't know where to start (as always). I do remember my first gameplay though. I was lazily chilling in my chair, feeling dread because my studies have been draining the hell out of me. Introduction pops up with this really relaxing music. At that moment, I just fell in love immediately. I knew I was going to enjoy it so much.And I did. Everything was just beautiful--from the music to the graphics. Seriously, everything just looked so great. I fell in love with the characters. I genuinely just loved listening to them talk about life's shenanigans. I loved how everyone gradually grew closer, how I (MC) connected with every one of them. Needless to say, I got emotionally attached quickly too.I also really, really love the brewing part. I thought I was going to brew only coffee but nope. You get to make drinks that aren't just coffee-based. You get to make tea, green tea, chocolate, and milk drinks too! I had such a blast making them. Experimenting with the ingredients also made me have so much fun also. I literally just find myself vibing with this game (especially with the characters) whenever I do play it. It also helped me relax a lot. It just helped, my dudes. I was having such a tough time in college but whenever I play this game, those feelings of stress and anxiety simply...evaporate. It sounds a bit much but, it's thanks to this that I survived my first sem as a freshman. Okay, enough praise. Playing this game made me realize why my father always wanted to open up a cafe. The vibe, the calming atmosphere, the people....I'm not good at explaining things but I think those are the things that really drove my father to come up with such a dream. In the game, you'll see the characters going through different emotions, you'll get to interact and communicate with them, you'll get to listen to their stories, you'll see their warmed up hearts and smiling faces after making and serving the drink...The idea of it all is just...breathtaking(?). I honestly would want that. Connecting with random strangers and having them become a part of your life just seems so amazing, you know? Plus, you get to serve them with your creations and even touch their hearts. So wholesome. I suppose that's everything from me...for now. I'm a little tipsy and I happened to see this while scrolling through my library.  ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing game. 10000000000000000/10 would recommend. Do play it. Definitely one of the few games I find myself going back to from time to time. Oh and, excuse my grammatical errors. I'm horrible in English lolOH and huge thanks to the devs, I love you all so much.

_childDocuments_.review: Welp, that was underwhelming to say the least. I got this game with perhaps (too) high hopes - ever since playing Strange Horticulture I've been looking for games in a vaguely similar vein and this one got mentioned on the interwebs a lot + has so many positive reviews, so when it was at a half price sale, I thought to myself - I might as well try. Well, reader, I did not think it was worth it. The play time I currently have is ca. 4 hours, at least some of which will have been from trying to gain some achievements outside of the normal gameplay time, which I'd estimate to be maybe 3, 3.5 hours. So it is a short game, a very short game in fact. And not only is it short, I did become bored enough each time that the 4 hours were collated across 3-4 different game play sessions? Having very linear + predictable stories, with very little ability to change anything (as in the only choice you can make is whether to serve someone the drink they requested or something else) and absolutely loveless writing (which honestly, is the thing that could've knocked this out of the park, but instead rammed it further into the ground, because the writing was poor. Short sentences, simple grammar, no differences in character voices, still full of stereotypes, but not in the way they wanted to draw attention to, I don't think..? - if it wasn't written in English, maybe this is at its root a translation issue, rather than the entire writing, but in English the experience remains poor). Coffee making can be frustrating, and it is far less of a puzzle aspect than I would like (or that I guessed it might be, based on what others said). It also seems to have rather less of an effect on story telling, than would make it interesting, because there's barely any narrative... : if you enjoy short, on the nose stories that are cozy and uplifting with at best middling writing and playing around with coffee/tea/flavour combinations, this might be the game for you. If you enjoy more or less mindlessly producing these variations, again very great, chill, game for that. So far, it's really not been the game for me, unfortunately, and that's why it is getting a thumb down for the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk has a great atmosphere, the music and art mesh well, and the soundtrack is great for putting on in the background while doing other tasks. The visual novel aspect of Coffee Talk is strong: the characters are memorable, their personalities and stories are diverse, and all given plenty of screen time, even when you don't get a perfect run. The endings feel satisfying and I felt invested enough to play again and see all their arcs to their conclusion. The cast is more than just their surface-level personalities. What they do for work and any non-human aspect they might have is also taken into consideration, and the writing also feels natural and immersive. I didn't dislike any characters in this game, in comparison to other visual novels I've played before. Coffee Talk's actual drink-making mechanics are great, the drink variety and selection is big, and the game offers an additional Endless game mode, if you like that. It's a short game, I have 12 hours and that's after going for 100% achievements, playing its Endless mode, and just playing the game all over again.Coffee Talk is also is compatible with controller (Xbox, at least), its UI is intuitive and not overly complex or difficult to work with.I highly recommend Coffee Talk to any visual novel player, or people looking to get into visual novels, especially those who're looking for a VN that isn't 20+ hours long, or one that has additional gameplay mechanics.

That may be all the agency you have in this game, but I assure you, that is more than you need to enjoy this game. These drinks will subtly shift the story of your customers, so make sure to prep those with love and care! The characters are pretty unique, the dialogue are fun with several pop culture reference scattered here and there, and there are good music. You can feel yourself just going to this cafe to simply chill, read, chat, whatever you want. There is a hidden narrative in the game that you don't want to miss if you decide to be invested in the game.Lastly, I am not the type to go to cafes to chill, I don't have the budget :_: but I can see the allure of this type of game for cafe lovers. _childDocuments_.review: This was the game that helped me power through a big university assignment in 2023 lol but, putting that aside from an objective standpoint, Coffee Talk is a very relaxing visual novel. You will feel at peace reading through the stories of all the different characters and how everyone who visits bond over a small drink.There are many character arcs and I believe serving the right drinks to everyone will unlock a good ending for each arc you finish while serving the wrong drink could make things go downhill. You're introduced to Lua x Baileys = Young straight couple who struggles to get their parents to approve of their relationship due to race (They are also the poster characters of Coffee Talk, succubi girl and elf boy)Gala x Hyde = Close male friendship, but could potentially end up becoming more than just friends depending on your perspective of their dialogue, I choose to ship them.Myrtle x Aqua = Close female friendship, both are game developers. Aqua is an indie who wants to make it big one day but she isn't sure how.. Myrtle, someone who is highly exprienced in the field decides to give her a hand and they bond over the fact that they both are ambitious, hardworking people who loves gaming and their differences help them both grow into better people. Unlike the Hyde x Gala arc, it is heavily implied that Myrtle and Aqua are just friends Hendry x Rachel = Father and daughter who are both nekomimi (cat people). Rachel is a fresh graduate from college who wants to make it big as a solo artist in performance (singing). Her dad is against  her manager Moris Lester (His name is a pun for the word molester) and wants his daughter to choose him, her dad, to be her manager instead. Rachel refuses because she wants to be more independent and not rely so much on her father and she worries he has gotten"out of touch" with showbiz.Jorji = Police officer. He serves as a bi-character to the Hendry x Rachel story arc, but other than that there is nothing special going on with him. He has no character development nor story of his own which is a shame.. Freya = Journalist who inspires to become a novelist, you can actually read her short stories on the phone app "The Evening Whispers" in the game. Which I found to be a cool feature. Freya's personaly my favorite character because I relate to her the most, being a writer myself it is hard to pull through when you are approaching the deadline. Even though my writing is discriptive whilst Freya's relies solely on narration, it's still difficult to deal with writer's block and pulling through for the days when coffee is one of your superpowers. She does end up becoming successful in the end tho so yay!Neil x The Barista = The two are time travelers from space, they apparently know each other quite well tho Neil drops the costume at the sequel and changes his name to Silver in "Hibiscus & Butterfly" which is cooi. Neil/Silver came to earth to mate with a female in order to produce an offspring that would be the protector of earth. At first Neil's inability to understand the language of the earthlings makes him successful and it also doesn't help that he conceals his appearance through wearing a space suit.. But once he becomes accustomed to life on earth and he drops the costume to reveal his true appearance. The ladies fall for his feet, one by one apparently, judging from a dialogue he has with the barista at the end. The only gameplay element you have is that you mix ingredients to serve hot drinks like coffee, tea and hot chocolate to the customers. You can draw latte art on top and experiment with different combinations. Even if you serve the wrong drinks, sometimes the characters will just choose to drink them anyways. The phone feature allows you to choose the own music you want playing in the background, each character has a social media profile that will tell you who they are and what they want in life, then there is "The Evening Whispers" (my favorite) where you can read Freya's short stories, she publishes one once a day which is cool, and lastly there is a "Brewpad" that you can use to check out drinks you've already made beforeIt's a very relaxing game that I strongly recommend to everyone else who also like cosy games.Definitely will be playing their sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: As you might have already guessed, Coffee Talk is a game about playing as a barista, serving drinks to your loyal customers. You listen to their stories, each character having a unique and interesting one. As the game progresses, you start seeing the characters as friends, rather than just customers.It was way longer than I initially expected it to be. I'm sure it takes about 3 to 5 hours to fully beat the main story if you don't skip the dialogue.  There is also an endless mode where you can mess around with ingredient combinations or go for it's 'challenge mode', where you have to make coffees as quickly as possible.Not sure if it's what you'd call 'AI', but the characters are interesting. Each one has a very unique and bizarre look to them, making each one memorable. Each has their own personality, preference of drink, and species. Yup, species. Vampires, werewolves, catgirls, etc. do exist in this game.I feel like I got my money's worth, even though I thought it was overpriced at first! It really is a fantastic game and I loved playing every second of it. Then again, I am a tea and coffee fanatic so I may be biased just a tiny bit. I felt connected to the characters and felt genuinely happy for them whenever something good happened, and felt genuinely sad whenever something bad happened for them.What you see in the screenshots is what you get. I loved the art style for this game and I thought it fit well for the genre. Facial expressions are very clear and body language is easily readable, which is something I feel is necessary for most games. Each coffee has its different look, which encouraged me to mess around with the ingredients  to see what certain combinations would look like.The characters don't speak out loud, but it doesn't matter that much. If anything, I think it makes the game better. You can imagine how the characters sound like in your head, which made the game more immersive for me. The music in the background is fantastically chosen/composed for the atmosphere for this game. It's one of the few soundtracks I didn't mute in all the video games I've played. Quite an achievement!This game brought back an idea I threw away a long time ago. Maybe I might open my café one day. This game is nothing short of amazing. As for genre, I feel the story plays more like a visual novel. If you want to just serve customers non-stop, then that's what challenge mode is for! As I said before, the game looks overpriced at a first glance but after playing for a bit, you might decide it's pretty well priced. I may buy this again for my Xbox One. As for achievements, they're easy enough. Nothing too hard. Would recommend this to anybody.One thing I found wrong was that in the 'challenge mode', the characters would say "Could I have 'a The Grinch'" and at some points 'a (word starting with a vowel)'. It annoyed me more than it should, but nothing that ruined my gaming experience.I was going to rate this game an 8/10, but it's about coffee. So I have to give it another point!Ran super smooth the whole way through, which isn't that surprising to be fair.Intel Core i5-2500S @2.7GhzNVIDIA GeForce GTX 750 Ti8GB RAMWindows 7 (64 bit) Ultimate N

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is on its surface a simple game about listening in on conversations that happen in a coffee shop. The music is pleasant and relaxing, the pixel graphics are charming, and the characters are relatable. I enjoyed mixing together different drinks to unlock special recipes and of real-world brews from countries around the world. What was most gripping was the stories that occurred in this coffee shop. What appear to be simple, almost cliched tropes are cleverly disguised allegories of mental illness, racism, family politics, and more. The game treats these issues carefully and explores them beautifully, in a way that had me staying up just to find out what would happen. Replaying the game puts things in a different, deeper context, and helped me to fully understand the amount of detail this game has in its fabulous storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: Short review: slice-of-life game with barista simulator.Long review:If you feel deja vu by seeing / playing VA-11 Hall-A, it's not a coincidence. The mixing element is similar, but everything else is different. The cozy feeling is given by the interior of the café, the rainy outside (background) and the fine lo-fi OST. Some exploration work is needed at the mixing to learn new recipes. And the barista is genderless (only the name is asked). So technically YOU are the barista.The comics give some extra context about the characters, which is a nice addition. The OST DLC is also a nice thing.My only negative point is that the story feels a bit short (compared to VA-11 Hall-A). _childDocuments_.review: 2020 was truly a rough year overall. After countless of tries to find a suitable game for late alone still nights, I encountered this gem while reviewing the final 2020 video of the year from the channel "Adam Millard - The Architect of Games". Needless to say how engaging the content was, the stories, the every night routine or just discovering each of the characters little quirks and secrets. For me this game was magical, another reminder of why I love so much this medium and how many strange emotions you are able to feel just by making drinks for this weird humanoids of different races.For the minimal game-play mechanic it serves the purpose and it's very satisfying hitting the right stuff. Also the setting is great, being in a crowded american city while also at peace and at ease in the little safe spot that is the magical coffee bar.Buy it, play it and complete it (and by that i mean it all), support the incredibly talented developers, it is and it will be worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've just played through the story, and I'm going to have to give a very harsh review. I don't intend to be mean, but the story is pretty bad and the gameplay mechanics are very dull.  One of the things that makes the story bad is that, for me at least, not having any interaction of your own to influence outcomes is boring the barista speaks for himself so you're not really playing as the barista. However, what makes the story worse is that it tends to push political agendas that i'm assuming the developers believe in. This is always a bad idea in games we play them for fun not to be preached to. What finally tipped this game into the category of knowing I wanted a refund was when the "alien" brought up a falsehood that 87% of our pollution is straws...anyone even the least educated among us can easily call BS on that one that would mean passing any dumpster, dumps, garbage heaps, or landfills we would be seeing large mounds of straws. So this was simply too much. That the writer "might" believe this makes the political pushes even worse as it is like a flashing neon sign of ignorance "if" they intend this to be a reflection of our own world.So for poor gameplaybad writingandpolitical angling I have to rate this a 1 out of 5 stars. It would be a 0, but I do think the character designs and setting was good.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is not just a game, or actually it's barely a game at all. It's a great read about a rainy day that you can relax to and enjoy at any moment, and it's a piece of art in its own way. It's a bit low on gameplay, but the originality and atmosphere that seeps through its outer shell truly know how to grab you by the shoulders and pull you in for a great experience. Full review at .
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: If you like visual novels, this game is for you. It is very aesthetically pleasing and making the drinks is fun for a bit. It is not much of a game to me, more like an online comic/visual novel. Not many actions for you to take besides making the drinks. And when making the drinks I find myself getting bored very easily. There are only so many combinations you can try with the ingredients given and the only semi interesting part of it is the latte art. Even then, I find the latte art frustrating rather that fun. As a real barista I figured the way the milk moved was to resemble a real latte, but it does not. And if you're just drawing you end up with an ugly lump. I do not find the writing interesting. It does not hold my attention and the conversations crawl by. I would have to say I have not played much of this game because I did not find the story interesting. Maybe it picks up if you play more, but I can only read the dialogue for so long. I continue to find myself putting the dialogue on auto and watching netflix instead of paying attention to the game. And for a game that relies on dialogue as its main pull factor, I found it very weak. I know many people enjoy the story, but it was not for me. Very disappointed because this game was recommended by a friend who typically gives me awesome game recs. She must see something in this game that I cannot. She did bring it up when I asked for a story forward game, which this very much is. It is basically the whole game. I am just not sure the story being delivered is best done through a game. For people who want gameplay and want the story to rely on the player, this game is not for you. Though, this game has an active fanbase and plenty of positive reviews, so this concept could just be missed on me. Still, I would not recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: It is so nice to see how strangers become mutual friends just by sitting at the bar or cafe, talking casually in friendly manners. The story has been told very good and neat, with each character developed really well and they grow up great until the end! Great art and music too! I love the coffee-making puzzle. Since I don't drink coffee, I found it that hard at first to remember how to make one. Thank God, it's in the phone! I don't have any gameplay problem. But I encountered with technical issue, where the app crashed each time the game's been launched. Whenever the problem occurs, I have to uninstall and re-install the game before I can play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing this, the music and art style is nice. It is missing a little something though in terms of depth to the story and game play. In a way the story line just ends abruptly and the game itself too, I guess it's trying to leave it on a bit of a cliff hanger but in a result there's no reason to comeback to the game once that is done...Is it worth recommending, sort of but not really, I think that'll depend on the person playing. I personally enjoyed it but wished for more. If you are after a easy point and click game with a nice story then yes I'd recommend it, maybe get it if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk overall is a cute game, but a bit flawed in some aspect. Since at the beginning it was asking to name the Barista, wich is the main protagonist, I was hoping for some involvement of the player with dialogue, like maybe chosing between options that could lead to different endings, instead it's a pre-setablished linear dialogue with every customer of the cafè that needs one click to progress. Sure, dialogues are well written, but I felt no real conflict when there was one or any real suprising moment, considering how overly-mellow and welcoming the atmoshpere was, to the point of feeling unrealistic despite trying to speak of real life problems with a different cast having their own background.The only gamey part is the coffee making, which unfortunatelly is not very deep. It's just blending 3 ingredients and serve the drink of choise, and if you wanna feel imaginative, you could draw something on it, but it's a mechanic that is just there and doesn't really add anything to the game itself. Even the main drink you serve to the customers, you can make it right or wrong, and as far as I've experienced doesn't do anything to the main storyline.Despite all these negative points, I still recommend it with a discount possibly. It's cozy and in a bad mood surely can lighten up your mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Well coffee talk is... pretty cool actually. It's a drama filled jukebox... I mean barista visual Novel. Don't expect dialog options, life or death situations or a love story with the green haired girl (which is sad), you're here to chill, relax, and follow some drama as if you were sitting in this coffee with the customers. The only difference is that you're the one doing the coffee
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: From the perfect atmosphere, to the characters interests, to the interesting coffee combinations or even to the ability to add small art to your coffees. This game is a perfect mix of story telling to keep the player invested and puzzles to keep the player thinking. Definitely worth the purchase and definitely worth to play all the way through
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Set in an alternate Seattle in which humans, orcs, elves and succubi co-exist,  is a game about listening and making drinks. As the sole barista of the eponymous late-night coffee shop, the player must interact with customers whilst satiating them with a range of warming beverages!Coffee Talk is an interesting and original title, seamlessly combining its narrative and minimal mechanics. Most enjoyable is the way in which the short tales of others are combined with the overarching story of the barista in a subtle, calming yet evocative way. This is further accentuated by the distinctive art and music, both adding to the charming nature of the game and making it even easier to recommend!My full, detailed review of this game is available at .
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as I saw the initial trailer and outline for this game I knew this would be my cup of tea! Perfect relaxing game to play in my downtime after work~ As someone that works in a customer-facing job in real life, it's a really nice filler for those quiet moments where you crave interaction, but already feel socially exhausted. The characters are so in-depth and the exchange in dialogue and story events feel really engaging and well written. I'm only a few hours in and I find myself being really invested in their all their worries and problems, some of which reflect topics of conversation I think we should be encouraged to talk about more in real life --Maybe even over a cup of coffee ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A cute and fairly short game, but despite that there's still a lot of very interesting story lines that get resolved pretty well in my opinion. There were definitely a lot of scenes I either found really compelling, or that stuck with me in some way. Echoing some other reviews, it does play out mostly like watching a movie, + making a drink every once in a while. Long story short, get it if you want to listen to other people talk about their lives while also listening to lofi.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of this kind of game, enjoy the artstyle and vibe. I can't express how much i love the story and characters. It's beautifully written and brings me feels. Its might sound cliche but this game really help me through my bad days. Thanks for making this game and telling these beautiful stories.edit: would like to see more of the world-building story in this semi-fantasy world. It's really interesting where they talk about  would like to read more smtg like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Every character that enters the shop has a different struggle to face, whether they are an artist trying to make ends meet while having a difficult relationship with their parents as they greatly disaprove of their profession and their significant other, or a war veteran trying to heal from the trauma and the disturbing experience that can damage anyone's mental health greatly, by helping others in a hospital, and this is only two of the problems that the diverse cast of characters talks about over a nice cup of coffee in the chill of the night.I know it seems too much and very difficult to understand at first, but the storytelling in this game is very refreshing, bringing new elements to the fantasy genre while adding a turn to it by having tense stories like the ones I briefly talked about; in a simple coffee shop, that isn't very well known, but nonetheless people go there for a warm coffee or a sweet cup of tea to ease their nerves, and in the process end up talking a bit about their problems while connecting to people they would otherwise never meet in their daily life if they have not entered the coffee shop in the first place. I love how they romanticize life and the relationships between the different races in this game, its very soothing, calm and it urges you to take your time to make their drinks, and to listen.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I got this during the memoriam sale after Fahmi's passing in which all proceeds went towards his family. I told myself I'd get around to playing it when the timing felt right and about a year later ended up giving it a go. I put it down until I visited Seattle and was inspired to pick it back up again. As Yahtzee Croshaw (Zero Punctuation / Second Wind) predicted several years ago, the world becoming slightly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ each day has made me turn to cozier comfier games than I probably would have in the past. This game plays out like a visual novel with brief pauses to make someone a coffee as a barista. Occasionally you'll have the opportunity to have events go a slightly different direction, but overall the game is *mostly* a linear story book experience. The dialogue is usually you witnessing a conflict and occasionally intervening. Without going deep into spoiler territory, there is an implication that something else is going on behind the scenes that rewards multiple playthroughs. There is an endless mode where you can make people whatever you want to discover new specialty drinks and a challenge mode linked to a relatively difficult achievement where you have to make 50 correct drinks with a timer. The requests get increasingly complex and occasionally unfair (as in literally impossible to do) which kind of forces you to make people the wrong drink. This is probably the worst part about challenge mode, but the cool thing is that it's totally optional and most people seem to just skip it.Story wise, some of the dialogue did feel a bit unrealistic and very "heartwarming 90s sitcom" which is what I believe the devs were going for, so don't expect anything like bittersweet endings, complex character development or moral ambiguity here. This ain't that kinda game and it would probably ruin the vibes. I do think the lead, Freya, is a bit too stereotypical manic-pixie-dream-girl to be as interesting as they try to make her, but then again she does exist in a world with elves and werewolves so I guess they felt they had to do something with the main human character to make her stand out. But overall, the game is a super relaxing experience and it's nice to get invested in other people's fictional stories for a little while, if only to briefly forget about your own.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is like a cosy, warm drink on a rainy night.I had a tonne of fun with this game. It was lovely to see the Coffee Talk being this place that brought people together, people living very different lives and who would otherwise be strangers, but have found a wordless kind of comfort and understanding in this coffee joint - and the characters are so endearing.The game's atmosphere is very chill, the gameplay is simple but charming. The story is lovely, engaging, and it navigates through important themes in a gentle and loving way (there's also some cheeky humour as garnish). The game makes for great company on a quiet night.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: For a Visual novel-esque type of game this game is good, but can see some improvement. The concept of the story which consist of several small bits of story is great, but the characters personality can be improved to be not too 2 dimensional. The conflict is great but the personality can be improved. Plus maybe some type of economy system can be added, if not for the main story for the additional game mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. I feel like some people need to be aware that at its heart, this is a straight up visual novel. Don't expect any real gameplay. There is the coffee mixing but it's very very simple. It has cozy atmospheric music with some interesting dialogue from all the customers visiting into your coffee shop. For the price, it's a nice experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked it! The script can feel a bit stilted and weird at times, where it feels like responses are too aggressive or too vague, but the conversations themselves are really interesting, and the pacing's super snappy while staying chill, which makes it hard to put down. The mechanics are a bit shallow and rely a bit too much on trial-and-error for me, but they also don't take up much time, so it didn't detract much from the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: i loved this game. it helped me relax, and the slight remarks on todays topics were SO good. i loved it. this is my new favorite game, definitely a worthy purchase.i also loved the art-style, and the conversations between the customers is so funny, especially Freya and the cop LMAO i totally recommend. 1000/10
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I believe that every conversation adds something to your life. Coffee Talk is all about that: conversation. While you don't directly choose what to say or ask your customers, you offer up a drink instead to interact with customers. In my opinion, it's less a game and more a mix of a visual novel with some game elements, but that's okay. The focus of Coffee Talk isn't gameplay, it's dialogue. While Coffee Talk is relatively short, I think it's definitely still worth a purchase because it's more about the experience: dialogue, atmosphere, etc. It's not that replayable in the sense that you get a different story each time because you don't, however, it's replayable in another sense, to remind you of hopes, dreams, and what is means to be human.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Such a charming game! I love a good story game with beautiful art, riveting storylines, and peaceful background music all while still having that interactive element of gaming that makes me feel like I'm part of the story. I'm mad at myself for taking this long to play the game! Truly an underrated masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING GAME!!  So cozy and the story is very intriguing.  Without spoiling anything, I will say you need to replay the game (to some extent) after your first playthrough to experience the entire story and clear your confusion.  This game plays very similarly to VA-11 Hall-A, so if you enjoyed that game you'll enjoy this one as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a wonderful and chill game to play, esp in those times when you dont feel like being an "active" player. I don't care much for reviews but truthfully this game was a one of the only games that I played through a difficult time in my life. I wanna take the time to give my condolences to the team and family of Fahmi who passed away. Rest in peace, mate. The ones who'll remember, will remember.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent VN. It does such a good job at building a cozy, relaxing atmosphere, it tells a fairly good story that tackles various relevant issues in our society without getting too preachy, and though I feel the final few chapters go from 0 to 100 a bit too suddenly, there is at least some buildup to those moments earlier in the game so it isn't completely out of nowhere. The characters are all likeable in their own ways, and their dynamics with each other enrich the experience that much more.Plus you can draw penises in people's lattes. It gets my recommendation for that alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: The demo got me hooked. The full game got me stoked.⠀What attracted me to this game is the combination of elements I love: great pixel art, nice and simple stories, an unusual premise (you play a barista) and great music. While each is very good on their own, it's when they come together that the magic happens. Unlike its title would suggest, Coffee Talk is really a game about listening. Listening to the customers' orders of course, but also to their stories and how they play out almost naturally. I really enjoyed that while you're physically at the centre of everything, you're not the centre of attention. The extra features (latte art and timed challenges) are great to keep it brewing.⠀Nothing, and I'll drink to that!
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I hate drinking coffee, and I love this game. The characters and stories are interesting and relatable. Also I noticed that these are the same developers that made Relic of War and Infectonator. It's nice to see some veteran game devs make another great game, especially one of a different genre as well as coming from Armor Games to Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A quick, cute and relaxing game that focuses on the stories of the customers that visit the nocturnal coffeeshop. Even though you only get a peek of the world setting, it's just enough to get an understanding of what kind of struggles the characters may be dealing with.I especially loved the novel one of the characters was writing about our world -- a world where there would be no other species/races than human, yet society would still be able to find the slightest differences to fault.˖⁺‧₊˚♡˚₊‧⁺˖ Really enjoyed getting to see everything this game had to offer, looking forward to episode two!! ˖⁺‧₊˚♡˚₊‧⁺˖
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Never fails to make me feel at ease. A feel-good game. A calming experience with lovable characters and engaging stories along the way. The rain sounds mixed with the lo-fi soundtrack leaves you feeling cozy. I'm a sucker for pixel graphics, so this appeals to me entirely. If you're someone who likes visual novels, rain, pixel graphics, and lo-fi music...this is for you.(Hyde is best character...>.<)
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk deserves a soft recommendation from me. It has an engaging style that works most of the time, but I cannot help but feel that some of the writing is so "on the nose" that it detracts from the subtle moments that do mostly work. I think when you write social commentary it's always better to have a "show, don't tell" sort of approach. Coffee Talk likes to, well, talk to you about things. Again, as a simple slice-of-life piece that's peppered with a little metacommentary, it sometimes works. However, there were other times where I couldn't help but roll my eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what I assumed it was when I first heard about it a few years ago; a shameless Va11-Halla ripoff.I'd be embarrassed as a developer to release something that so blatantly tries and fails to copy a much better game. Coffee Talk copies everything from the pixel graphics and mechanics down to the fonts used for dialogue and transition screens. The barista being a nameless self insert instead of an actual character isolates the player from the other characters and forces almost all interactions to run through Freya, the main customer. Some of the characters aren't too bad, like Hyde and Rachel, but the majority are forgettable. The dialogue often tries to hard to talk about real world social issues and it ends up coming off as forced and preachy. Social issues were implemented the best when they involved relationships between characters, such as Rachel and her dad as well as the elf/succubus couple. As far as gameplay, it tries to emulate Va11-Halla's style of interpreting customer orders and mixing drinks for them. This would be fine, however instead of having a list of all possible recipes available, you have to unlock most of them for yourself. I'm not sure if this is to encourage the use of the freeplay mode or to just be more time consuming. It's not a bad change but it can make some recipes pretty hard to figure out. The highlight of the system and the entire game was honestly the latte art feature because you could draw whatever you wanted on the drinks.TL;DR just play Va11-Halla ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee talk was the first visual novel game I played, and is an enjoyable intro into the genre, mixing chill gameplay with fun characters and an engaging premise.The pixel art style is a standout, as is the music, which I still listen to on spotifyThe story is simple but very enjoyable, and while short I found it had replay value, having finished the game three times (as well as gaining all the achievements, a simple task to do). All in all in, it's coffee talk's atmosphere that drew me in, and I am looking forward to the sequel coming out for 2023, where hopefully we see a continuation of the characters stories along with some fresh faces.Side note - R.I.P Mohammad Fahmi Hasni
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: It was alright, maybe get it on sale. It's just a nice little game to relax with, the stories are quite light and the characters are likeable enough. The music and vibe are nice. The coffee making mechanics could be improved upon, it's a bit trial and error with only a few tries. I guess you can try and make all the special drinks in free play and refer to the recipes, that makes it easier.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves coffee and drinks in general plus story-rich games, Coffee Talk caught my attention. When I saw the "Overwhelmingly Positive" rating, it was more than enough for me to buy the entire series and I'm so glad I did!Coffee Talk is the type of game I would love to play after a long busy day. It's a feel good game and the stories of each character felt very real and relatable. I enjoyed every single brew I had to create as I learn more about drinks! Even though coffee was the highlight, there was also green tea, chocolate, tea and more! I'm actually curious on how some of the mix tastes like in real life! I also love the pixel art style, the music and the vibe of the whole game! Lastly, this game really shows the significant and importance of being there for someone, even just listening. Definitely a game I would recommend if you wanna take a break from all the action games around. Looking forward to playing episode 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic story game. The atmosphere is incredible, the art is lovely, I love all the characters, and I enjoy making drinks for them. But I REALLY love the little twist at the end. I was sad when the story ended so soon, but that ending made me realize I can play this over and over again to get different results, which I plan to do!I appreciate the feature that lets me just make drinks over and over. It was a little annoying trying to find all the drinks in-game, so that feature is helpful.
_childDocuments_.name: Coffee Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Coffee Talk is a coffee brewing and heart-to-heart talking simulator about listening to fantasy-inspired modern peoples’ problems, and helping them by serving up a warm drink or two. Immerse yourself in the stories of alternative-Seattle inhabitants that modern readers will find strongly echo the world around them.
